These transactions shall be entered on the demarcation records and confirmed by the signature of the judge and the signature of the interested parties present, and if the latter do not know how to sign, mention thereof shall be made in the record. If these operations of transfer of ownership require prior topographical work, the surveying engineer shall undertake it upon instruction from the judge, and the general demarcation plan shall be amended as a result thereof.

Pursuant to the third Article of Decision No. 44/LR dated 20/4/1932, the text of Article 36 was repealed and replaced by the following text:

Neither the Magistrate nor the Single Real Estate Judge shall in any case whatsoever have jurisdiction to adjudicate upon the right of inheritance, nor may he order the partition of any estate unless the claimant party produces in support of his objection or claim the certificates of inheritance or the succession certificates provided for by law.

In all cases where the presumed owner of a partitioned real property claims that he holds his right by way of inheritance, the objection of another heir establishing his right of inheritance shall not be taken into consideration unless he proves that he was omitted when the partition was effected; if he fails to prove this, the objection shall be struck off ipso jure, and in such case he shall retain the right to apply to the ordinary courts under the conditions prescribed by Article 31. Where the matter relates to a real property or immovable property held in undivided co-ownership among the heirs, and the latter do not produce in support of their claim the succession documents provided for by law, the real property or immovable property shall be registered in the name of the heirs of the deceased, and likewise if the heirs or some of them are unknown. However, if an objection or claim relating to the rights of the deceased is lodged in accordance with this Decision, and the heirs are absent, unknown, or fail to prove the validity of their filiation, the Real Estate Judge may admit the heir or heirs designated in the certificate (ilm wa khabar) of the mukhtars, provided that the heirs consent thereto, and if the heirs are unknown, he may appoint a representative for this purpose to represent them. In all cases, hereditary shares as well as the shares of co-owners in undivided ownership shall be expressed as a fraction with a denominator of 2400 shares.

Pursuant to the fourth Article of Decision No. 44/L.R. dated 20/4/1932, the text of Article 37 was repealed and replaced by the following text:

Where the real property or the immovable property is covered by a Tapu deed, or by an entry in the Defterhane registers, or by an entry in the registration ledgers of Old Mount Lebanon, the holder of the right or those to whom the right has devolved from him are the persons in whose name the real property shall be registered as the holders of that right established by the deed or the entry; and if a third party comes forward, having an established right of possession over the real property or over an immovable property, and claims the right of ownership thereof or the right of disposal (tasarruf) thereof, the right claimed shall be registered in the name of the possessor, in the following cases:

1- If he produces instruments or documents entitling him to the right of registration in his name (such as a court judgment or a waqf deed, etc..).

2- In the event of failure to produce any such thing, if the holder of the right established by a deed or by an entry, or the persons to whom this right has devolved from him in the event of the death of the holder of the right, testifies in his favour to his right.

3- If he has been in possession of the real property or the immovable property peaceably, publicly, and uninterruptedly for a period of five years, in person or through the person of his predecessor in title or through another person on his behalf, by virtue of a just title, or for a period of ten years or fifteen years, according to the legal category of the real property or of the immovable property, if he does not hold a just title. By (just title) in this Decision is understood the act or event establishing the acquisition of the real property by one of the following means, such as the occupation of dead land (mawat), or the devolution of property by intestate or testate succession, or a gift inter vivos with or without consideration, or sale or transfer (faragh). If the extinction of heirs or vacancy of the property is established and the current possessor has not fulfilled the conditions mentioned in the third paragraph of this Article, the registration shall be subject to the provisions of the following Article.

Pursuant to the fifth Article of Decision No. 44/L.R. dated 20/4/1932, the text of Article 38 was repealed and replaced by the following text:

Where a real property or an immovable property, of whatever kind, is not originally registered in the Defterhane or in the registration ledgers in Mount Lebanon and is held without a deed, the right of ownership or the right of disposal (tasarruf), as the case may be, shall be registered in the name of the current possessor, if he has occupied it peaceably, publicly, and uninterruptedly, in person or through the person of his predecessor in title or through a third party on his behalf, with a just title or without a just title, for a period of ten years or fifteen years, according to whether the category of the real property or the immovable property is Amiri or pure Mulk; and if the current possessor has not fulfilled these conditions, the right of ownership or the right of disposal (tasarruf), as the case may be, shall be registered in his name if he agrees to pay the equivalent value (badal al-mithl) appraised in accordance with the provisions of Article 42 below, and if he refuses, the real property shall be registered as the property of the State.

The area revealed by measurement and included within the boundaries mentioned in the Tapu deed shall be presumed to be the property of the holder of the deed; provided that if the real property was acquired on the basis of the dhirā', the dunum, or any other unit of area with a statement of the price per unit of area, the excess revealed by measurement shall be subject to the payment of the equivalent value (badal al-mithl), save in the cases provided for in Article 38 above.

If the immovable property adjoins Amiri lands, and the boundaries specified in the Tapu deed are not fixed on the ground by landmarks, marks, or fixed signs, or if the boundaries do not result from an inter partes demarcation carried out in the presence of the representative of the State, the area mentioned in the deed shall be registered in the name of the holder of the deed plus 20 per cent; as for the excess revealed by measurement, it shall be subject to the payment of the equivalent value (badal al-mithl), save in the cases provided for in Article 38 above.

Pursuant to the sixth Article of Decision No. 44/L.R. dated 20/4/1932, the text of Article 41 was repealed and replaced by the following text:

In all the cases mentioned above and in Articles 37 (the third paragraph), 38, 39, and 40, the periods of prescription shall be calculated in accordance with the rules specified in the provisions of Articles 257 and 260 of Decision No. 3339 dated 12 November 1930, and the rules specified in Articles 255, 256, 258, 259, and 261 to 266 inclusive of the same Decision shall apply, save for the exceptions provided for by this Decision.

In the same cases, where the judge has received the testimony of the mukhtars, the members of the council of elders (majlis al-ikhtiyariyya), the property owners, the adjoining owners, and the interveners in the action who have signed the minutes of demarcation of the real property, such testimony shall be deemed sufficient to prove that the possession fulfils the conditions prescribed by Articles 37 (the third paragraph), 38, 39, and 40, unless there is written proof conflicting with the testimony.

The appraisal of the value of the real properties subject to the payment of the equivalent value (badal al-mithl) shall be carried out in each village through the committee in accordance with the provisions specified by law and after taking the opinion of the body of elders (hay'at al-ikhtiyariyya). One tenth of this value shall be deducted for each year elapsed since the date the possessor took disposal of the real property if it appears that the aforementioned person has introduced improvements thereto during this period and has disposed of it peaceably; furthermore, one third of the required value, after its determination in accordance with the aforementioned provisions, shall be deducted if the possessor has, in person or through his relatives or his legal representatives, introduced improvements to the real property.
Pursuant to the first Article of Legislative Decree No. 104 dated 12/6/1959, the text of Article 43 was repealed.

Pursuant to Article 2 of Legislative Decree No. 104 dated 12/6/1959, the text of Article 44 was repealed and replaced by the following text: The equivalent value (badal al-mithl) shall be collected in ten equal annual instalments, and the State shall enjoy, for the settlement of this debt, a privilege exempted from registration.

Pursuant to Article 8 of Decision No. 44/L.R. dated 20/4/1932, the provisions of Article 45 were supplemented and became as follows:

The area shall be expressed in all official documents (minutes of census and demarcation, Land Registers, title deeds, survey plans, judgments, etc..) in hectares, ares, and centiares; provided that the areas may be mentioned in the documents, upon the request of the interested parties, in the old measures in accordance with the official conversion table.

Below is a statement of the equivalence of the old measures to land measures in the metric system.

The square dhirā' or arshin equals 0.758 x 0.758 = 0.574564 square metres.

The square evlek equals 400 square dhirā's or 15.16 * 15.16 = 229.8256 square metres.

The dunum equals 4 evleks or 1600 square dhirā's or 30.32 * 30.32 = 919.30 square metres.

Pursuant to Article 9 of Decision No. 44/L.R. dated 20/4/1932, the text of Article 46 was repealed and became as follows:

In the regions where Decisions No. 186, 188, and 189 issued on 15 March 1926 do not apply, and strictly in respect of immovable properties that are not subject to the provisions of Decision No. 275 issued on 5 May 1926 regarding the sale and administration of the private domain of the State, the Justice of the Peace in the caza shall take the place of the Administrative Councils and shall adjudicate upon the following matters which fall within the competence of the Defterhane: 1- Verification of the extinction of heirs.

2- Granting of land by way of (right of permanence - haqq al-qarar) or against payment of the (equivalent value - badal al-mithl).

3- Rectification of the entries of Tapu deeds if these entries are not in conformity with the entries of the Defterhane registers due to an established material error or omission in accordance with the provisions of the Law of 28 February 1329 regarding disposal (tasarruf).

Pursuant to Article 10 of Decision No. 44/L.R. dated 20/4/1932, the provisions of Article 47 were repealed and became as follows:

In the case provided for in the second paragraph of Article 46 above, the Justice of the Peace shall apply the provisions of Articles 37, 40, and 42 of this Decision.

Pursuant to Article 11 of Decision No. 44/L.R. dated 20/4/1932, the provisions of Article 48 were repealed and became as follows:

When the Magistrate of the Qada adjudicates the matter of verifying the extinction of heirs as well as actions relating to the grant of land by way of the right of settlement (haqq al-qarar) or against payment of the equivalent value (badal al-mithl), he shall apply the rules of procedure designated in Articles 23, 24, 32 and 41 of this Decision. However, he shall in all cases move to the site of the real property in accordance with the provisions of Article 23 to conduct the investigation therein and he shall be assisted, instead of the engineer, by the local official of the Land Registry Departments; and in the actions provided for in the preceding paragraph, the State Domain Administration shall always be joined therein as a third party and the notifications provided for in Articles 23, 24 and 32 of this Decision shall be sent to it, under pain of nullity of the proceeding, through the offices of the Magistrate and under his responsibility.

Where the action relates to the rectification of an entry, as mentioned in the third paragraph of Article 46, the rules of procedure which were previously followed shall be applied to the exclusion of all others, and the interested parties shall have the right to appeal the decisions of the Magistrate rendered in the actions referred to in Article 46 to the competent Court of Appeal.

The appeal must be lodged, under pain of forfeiture, within the fifteen days following the date of the notification effected in accordance with the provisions of Article 32, and the Court of Appeal before which the action is brought shall adjudicate it in the administrative manner; however, if the need arises to conduct an investigation, the Court shall appoint a reporting counsellor to undertake it in accordance with the provisions of Article 23 of this Decision, and where necessary an engineer shall be placed at the disposal of the Court upon a request submitted by the President to the Director of the Land Registry Departments of the State. In all cases, the State Domain Administration must be joined in the action, and the necessary notifications must be sent to it in accordance with the provisions of Articles 23, 24 and 32 of this Decision, and the decision of the Court of Appeal shall be enforceable and not subject to any means of recourse.

As from the date of promulgation of this Decision, the Administrative Council or the State Council is prohibited from entertaining any action or petition relating to the matters designated in the provisions of Article 46 of this Decision.

The files of the proceedings of cases currently pending before the Administrative Councils in respect of which no judgment has been rendered prior to the promulgation of this Decision shall be transferred without delay, by order of the President and through the diligence of the clerk of the said Council, to the Permanent Committee in the Qada or the Governorate (Muhafaza), which shall continue the proceedings previously initiated. As for judgments that have been rendered prior to the promulgation of this Decision, they shall be enforceable within the conditions provided for by law, and recourse in respect of such judgments shall be had to the Administrative Appeal Departments or the State Council in the usual form.

Pursuant to Article 12 of Decision No. 44/L.R. dated 20/4/1932, Article 50 was supplemented and became as follows:

The President of the Committee shall impose, within the limits of the jurisdiction of the Magistrate, the penalties designated by law upon every perpetrator of a contravention during the operations of census and demarcation and upon every person assisting or participating with him therein; and, save for the matters provided for in the following Articles, he shall refer to the ordinary courts the perpetrators of contraventions, misdemeanours or felonies provided for in the provisions of the ordinary penal laws, and those assisting them and participating with them therein.

Judgments rendered in the contraventions provided for in Articles 51 and 52 below shall not be subject to any means of recourse and shall be enforceable without delay, and prosecutions against officials shall be conducted without prior authorisation from the Administration to which they belong.

Pursuant to Article 13 of Decision No. 44/L.R. dated 20/4/1932, the text of Article 51 was repealed and replaced by the following text:

Whoever opposes the carrying out of the operations of demarcation, registration or cadastral survey, or intentionally creates difficulties therein, shall be punished forthwith by a fine of five to fifty Lebanese-Syrian pounds, and in the event of repetition of the act, the maximum penalty shall always be applied against him.

Pursuant to Article 14 of Decision No. 44/L.R. dated 20/4/1932, the text of Article 52 was repealed and replaced by the following text:

Every mukhtar, member of a council of elders (majlis ikhtiyari), surveyor-engineer or official who is negligent in performing the duties incumbent upon him pursuant to the provisions of this Decision shall be punished by a fine of five to fifty Lebanese-Syrian pounds; and if the inhabitants of one of the villages cause damage to the rights of another person by reason of declarations agreed upon amongst themselves and made during the operations of provisional demarcation, the Judge shall, where necessary, order the annulment of the operations of provisional demarcation and their repetition at the expense of the makers of those declarations.

In all the cases provided for in Articles 50 to 52 and Articles 54 and 55 of this Decision, where the matter relates to foreigners, the records drawn up as mentioned above shall be transferred without delay to the Public Prosecutor before the competent Court for Foreign Actions.

Whoever registers or attempts to register the property of another in his own name or in the name of another person by using fraudulent means or by producing under a false name documents or instruments belonging to another shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years and by a fine of twenty-five pounds to five hundred Lebanese-Syrian pounds, without prejudice to the right to claim civil damages.

Whoever gives false testimony for the purpose of facilitating the registration of a real property, without right, in the name of another person shall be punished by the penalties provided for in the preceding Article.

Pursuant to Article 15 of Decision No. 44/L.R. dated 20/4/1932, the text of Article 56 was repealed and replaced by the following text:

In all cases in which the expressions (immovable property or parcel) are used in the text of Decision No. 186 issued on 15 March of the year 1926, they shall be replaced by the expressions (real property or immovable property).
All provisions contrary to this Decision are repealed and shall remain repealed.

The Secretary-General, the Delegate Extraordinary of the High Commissioner to the States of Syria and Jabal al-Druze, and the Delegates to the States are charged, each in so far as he is concerned, with the execution of this Decision.

The Beirut Bar Association shall enjoy internal autonomy and shall exercise its discretionary authority in registering lawyers on its rolls and transferring the names of trainee lawyers to the roll of lawyers without being bound by any registration with any other bar association.

Lawyers registered with the Beirut Bar Association are prohibited from establishing any body, association, league or cooperative for lawyers or for the legal profession other than their Bar Association which has a syndical character and enjoys legal personality, or from joining the same, whether in Lebanon or abroad.

Subject to the provisions of Article 115 of the Law Regulating the Profession, no non-Lebanese shall be entitled to practise law within the jurisdiction of the Beirut Bar Association or to have a consultation office therein, whether individually or in partnership with a lawyer registered with the Beirut Bar Association.

Lawyers registered with the Beirut Bar Association must abide by the provisions of these By-laws, and any violation of the provisions hereof, or of the provisions of the Legal Profession Law, or of the customs, traditions and ethics of the profession, and any act or conduct that undermines its honour and dignity, whether committed during the lawyer's practice of his profession, outside thereof, or in his private life, shall subject the offender to the penalties provided for in Article 99 of the Law Regulating the Legal Profession.

A lawyer registered with the Beirut Bar Association must engage in the actual practice of his profession and have an office within the jurisdiction of the Bar Association, and he may not have an office within the jurisdiction of another bar association.

Only a lawyer registered with the Beirut Bar Association may establish an office within the jurisdiction of this Bar Association.

The Council of the Bar Association shall draw up:

1- A fundamental general roll of the names of all lawyers ordered according to the seniority of their enrollment in the Bar Association, in which the date of enrollment of each of them and any change occurring to such enrollment shall be specified.

2- A general roll of the names of practising lawyers ordered according to the seniority of their enrollment in the Bar Association.

3- A roll of the names of trainee lawyers ordered according to the dates of their enrollment, and in the margin of this roll shall be indicated the date of completion of the training of each of them and the date of his enrollment on the roll of practising lawyers.

4- A roll of the names of temporarily non-practising lawyers and the date of striking the name of each of them off the general roll or the suspension of his enrollment, and in the event of his reinstatement to the general roll, the date of the new enrollment. Each of the aforementioned rolls shall be recorded in a special register.

In addition to the rolls provided for in the preceding Article, the Council of the Bar Association shall draw up during the month of May of each year a special alphabetical roll of the names of the lawyers and trainee lawyers who are entitled to practise law in the judicial year commencing on the aforementioned date.

Lawyers who have not paid the annual subscription and retirement fees prior to the first of May shall not be enrolled on the special roll provided for in the preceding Article. A lawyer who has paid the annual fees after the due time shall be given a certificate proving payment thereof and enabling him to practise law without being entitled to participate in the meetings of the General Assemblies.

The Council of the Bar Association shall strike off its second, third and fourth rolls deceased lawyers and those who permanently cease to practise law due to retirement from practice, placement on retirement, total medical disability, or in execution of a decision issued by the Council of the Bar Association or the Disciplinary Board. This shall be recorded on the first roll. In the fourth register shall be registered the names of those who temporarily cease to practise law or are temporarily prohibited from practising it, whether due to their engaging in activities incompatible with the legal profession, or due to a disciplinary decision imposing a temporary prohibition from practising law, or for any other reason provided for by the Legal Profession Law or its regulations. In the margins of the second or third registers - depending on whether the matter concerns a lawyer or a trainee lawyer - the temporary cessation and its date shall be indicated.

A lawyer who intends to engage in an activity incompatible with the legal profession may declare to the Council of the Bar Association his wish to temporarily cease practising his profession after specifying the activity he wishes to pursue; if the Council of the Bar Association approves his request, he shall be entitled within five years to request the reinstatement of his name on the roll of practising lawyers without being required to pay a new admission fee, and only the additional fee prescribed for each year of cessation in which he has exceeded thirty years of age shall be required. The Council of the Bar Association must reject the request for reinstatement if it appears to it that the applicant engaged during the period of his cessation in activities contrary to the dignity of the profession or lost one of the qualifications required for practising the profession. A lawyer who has ceased to practise his profession shall not be entitled to use the title of lawyer during such cessation nor to benefit from the privileges and rights attached to the status of a practising lawyer.

A trainee lawyer shall be subject to the special provisions provided for in the Legal Profession Law, and training shall be regulated in accordance with the rules provided for in the following Articles:
A lawyer who accepts a trainee lawyer in his office must work to prepare him to become, academically and professionally, a competent lawyer.
The name of a trainee lawyer may not be enrolled in the office of a lawyer unless the latter has an independent office of his own.
No more than two trainee lawyers shall be accepted in a single office except by special permission from the Council of the Bar Association.
Training shall not commence Until after the decision to enroll the trainee lawyer on the roll of trainee lawyers and his taking of the oath provided for in Article 10 of the Legal Profession Law.
A trainee lawyer must introduce himself, prior to the hearing, to the judge before whom he will plead for the first time.

A trainee lawyer must attend to his training without interruption throughout its prescribed period, and if he ceases to pursue it without an acceptable excuse, the lawyer in whose office he is training must notify the Council of the Bar Association of the matter within fifteen days.

Upon notification to the Council of the Bar Association of the trainee lawyer's cessation from pursuing his training, the President of the Bar Association shall address a letter to the latter asking him for the reason for such cessation, and in light of his reply and having regard to the duration of the cessation and its reason, the Council of the Bar Association shall consider whether or not to include this period in the calculation of the period of training.

If the trainee lawyer's cessation from pursuing his training is repeated in such a manner that this training appears not to be serious, the Council of the Bar Association shall decide to extend the period of training as it deems fit. Provided that if five years have elapsed since the enrollment of the trainee lawyer on the roll of trainee lawyers without his being transferred to the roll of lawyers, his name shall, after investigation, be struck off the roll of trainee lawyers, and he may not be re-enrolled again except after paying the enrollment fee anew. All of the foregoing shall apply unless the trainee lawyer submits an excuse accepted by the Council of the Bar Association.

The training lectures which trainee lawyers are required to attend and participate in shall be:

1- Academic and professional lectures.

2- Practical lectures in which trainee lawyers participate by way of exercises in the rules of practising the profession and in the procedures governing the conduct of lawsuits before the courts from the time of their filing until the issuance of the final judgment therein, including the submission of written pleadings and oral arguments.

The training lectures shall be supervised by the President of the Bar Association assisted by a committee of members of the Council of the Bar Association appointed by the President of the Bar Association and called the Training Committee.

The Training Committee shall meet under the chairmanship of the President of the Bar Association or whomever he delegates from among the members of the Council of the Bar Association during the month of June and shall draw up a complete curriculum for all the lectures and a list of lecturers for the following year. The Committee shall have the right to amend the curriculum and the list.
The training lectures shall commence on the first of December of each year, and trainee lawyers shall be required to attend and participate in them.

Trainee lawyers must attend the training lectures in lawyer's attire and sign the attendance register at the beginning and end of the lecture. Each practical lecture shall be deemed equivalent to two academic lectures. For the purpose of applying the second paragraph of Article 26 of the Law Regulating the Profession, the calculation of the number of lectures shall take place year by year.
These lectures shall be announced to the trainee lawyers by a notice posted in the halls of the Bar Association at its headquarters in Beirut and in the annexes.

Trainee lawyers shall be divided, for the purpose of participating in the pupillage lectures, into three categories:

The category of first-year trainees, the category of second-year trainees, and the category of third-year trainees. For the purpose of division into these categories, the date of the first of December of each year shall be taken as a dividing line, such that all those who are registered on the roll of trainees during the period extending between the first of December of each year and the first of December of the following year shall form one category. Before the end of the month of November of each year, a list shall be drawn up with the names of all trainee lawyers who had been registered since the first of December of the preceding year and who form one category, and this matter shall be notified to them.

The Pupillage Committee, when establishing the annual curriculum, must observe the following matters:

1- The academic and professional lectures scheduled to be delivered shall have all trainees from the three categories invited to them together.

2- The practical lectures shall be organised and their topics and dates determined for each category of the three categories independently.

3- If the Committee finds the number of trainees in one of the categories to be large, it may divide them into multiple groups, provided that the curricula of the pupillage lectures in respect of these groups are similar.

4- The topics of the pupillage lectures must be varied so that the trainees are enabled to gain practice in the various activities of the profession.

Practical pupillage lectures shall take place by the lecturer presenting the topic required to be examined, dividing the work in respect thereof among the trainees, calling upon them to perform all the legal acts required by the role of each of them, and listening, at the time of the lecture, to the trainees' discussion of the topic and to their points of view and their pleadings.
After the end of the annual curriculum of lectures, the Pupillage Committee shall set down in writing such observations as it deems fit regarding the trainees.

In the month of December of each year, a competitive examination shall be held for trainee lawyers, and the first three of each of the categories mentioned in Article Twenty-Five of these By-laws who have obtained a mark of 14 out of 20 and above shall be awarded the title of "Secretary of the Pupillage Lectures", whilst the first among them shall be awarded the title of "First Secretary". The Secretaries shall perform the tasks assigned to them by the President of the Bar relating to the affairs of pupillage and trainees, and shall assist the Secretariat of the Al-Adl Journal in its work. The Council of the Bar Association shall organise this competitive examination, which shall revolve around the topics mentioned in Article Nineteen of these By-laws.

Transitional Provisions - In preparation for the full application of the system of lectures after the lapse of three years, and in view of the necessity of commencing the implementation of this system gradually during these three years, the following is required to be done:

1- Immediately upon the adoption of these By-laws, the President of the Bar shall appoint the Pupillage Committee for the current judicial year,

2- Immediately upon the adoption of these By-laws, a list shall be drawn up of the names of the trainee lawyers who were registered on the roll of trainees starting from the first of July 1970 until the first of December 1971, and all of these shall be considered during the current year as the category of first-year trainees.

3- The trainees whose names appear in the preceding paragraph alone shall be obliged during the current year to participate in the practical lectures in accordance with the curriculum established by the Pupillage Committee and under the supervision of this Committee.

4- Starting from the first of December 1972, the trainees set out in the second paragraph shall move to the category of second-year trainees. The category of first-year trainees shall be composed of those registered on the pupillage roll between the first of December 1971 and the first of December 1972.

Starting from the first of December of the year 1973, the three categories of trainees shall be completed, considering that those who will be registered between 1/12/1972 and 1/12/1973 shall form the category of first-year trainees.

5- Trainee lawyers not mentioned above, namely trainee lawyers registered on the roll before the first of July 1970, shall remain subject to the system of lectures that was previously in force.

6- The system of the competitive examination for obtaining the title of Secretary of the Pupillage Lectures shall apply with effect from the month of December 1972.

The special provisions provided for in the Law on the Legal Profession shall apply to the meetings of the General Assembly, and participation in these meetings and voting therein shall be subject to the following rules:

Only lawyers who have paid the subscription fees before the first of May of the year in which the General Assembly is held, and those who were registered on the General Roll after the said date and before the first of October, shall participate in the General Assembly or attend its meetings.

In the meeting of the General Assembly allocated for elections, the Council of the Bar Association shall determine the number of ballot boxes and shall appoint for each box a bureau composed of a chairman and a member to supervise the polling and counting operations. The chairman of each bureau may add to his bureau at most two lawyers to participate in the counting and tallying operations.

Ballot papers that contain a number exceeding the number of members required to be elected shall be counted in respect of the first ones voted for therein, up to the number required to be elected. The results of the boxes shall be totalled and recorded in a general record signed by the boards of the bureaus, and the President of the Bar or whoever acts in his stead shall announce the names of the winners as set forth in the general record.

Subject to the provisions of Article 50 of the Law Regulating the Profession, the principle of secret voting shall be adopted in all meetings of the General Assembly unless this Assembly decides on public voting.

The resolutions adopted by the General Assembly shall be registered in a special register according to the dates of their issuance and shall be given consecutive numbers, and every lawyer may inspect them with the permission of the President of the Bar.

The Council of the Bar Association shall hold an ordinary session every two weeks on the day and at the hour that it appoints, and it shall hold its extraordinary sessions whenever the President of the Bar invites it to meet on his own initiative or upon the request of one-third of the members of the Council. The agenda of each session shall be drawn up three days before it is held and shall be notified to each of the members.
The President of the Bar, and in his absence the Secretary, shall chair the session of the Council of the Bar Association.

In the session held by the Council of the Bar Association to elect the board of its bureau, voting shall take place by secret ballot. In all other sessions, voting shall take place publicly unless the Council decides otherwise.
The members of the Council shall abide by the secrecy of deliberations, and each of them shall, in the first session following his election, take the oath to preserve this secrecy.

The President of the Bar shall adjudicate upon the applications that fall within his competence. He shall refer to the Council of the Bar Association the applications pertaining to it. As for those that require an investigation, it shall be conducted by the President of the Bar or by whomever he assigns thereto from among the members of the Council of the Bar Association. The investigator shall draw up a report in which he includes the result of his investigation and shall submit it to the President of the Bar without delay.

Subject to the provisions of Articles 93 and 115 of the Law Regulating the Profession, the President of the Bar Association, when a foreign lawyer requests from him a licence to plead in a case before the Lebanese courts, must verify the registration of the said lawyer on the roll of practising lawyers in the foreign Bar Association to which he belongs. It is a condition for granting the licence that a Lebanese lawyer be associated in the pleading with the lawyer applying for the licence in the case for which the licence is requested.
The Council of the Bar Association shall have a bureau composed of the Secretariat, the Treasury, and the Commissariat of the Palace of Justice.

In the first session held by the Council of the Bar Association after the general elections, it shall proceed to elect the board of its bureau and to receive the registers and archives from the former President of the Bar, together with a report to the Council on the matters that are still pending, where applicable.
An advocate is prohibited from lending his name or acquiring for himself rights subject to judicial dispute.

An advocate may not accept a mandate in the name of another advocate who works for his account in a case brought before a judge to whom he is related by consanguinity or affinity up to the fourth degree.

With the exception of the word "Advocate" or President of the Bar or Former President of the Bar and the reference to university law degrees, an advocate may not add any title or capacity to the plaque and papers of his office.

An advocate shall refrain from using any expression that reveals contempt or disparagement and infringes upon the dignity or honour of the opponents, within the limits of exercising the right of defence. He shall conduct himself towards the judges in a manner consistent with the dignity of the legal profession and avoid anything that breaches the respect owed to the courts and anything that impedes the course of justice.

An advocate may not produce before the judiciary legal opinions supporting his point of view, with the exception of what is necessary thereof to prove the content of a foreign law or with a view to resolving problems of conflict of laws.

An advocate shall receive his clients in his office and may not travel to meet them except due to their illness or in exceptional circumstances. He shall refrain from communicating with an opponent who has appointed an advocate and from receiving him, except in urgent cases, before informing his colleague who has the right to attend this meeting. However, an advocate who is regularly consulted by a legal person may go in person to its headquarters to attend a meeting or to express his opinion on the matters presented to him.
An advocate shall avoid involving himself in the cases entrusted to him in a manner that exposes his person to discussion.
An advocate shall respect the authorities of the Bar Association and provide all information or clarifications that they request from him, unless he is bound by professional secrecy.
Advocates shall deal with one another with mutual respect, particularly with the Presidents of the Bar and with those who are older than them.

An advocate who pleads in a city other than that in which he practises his profession shall visit the President of the Bar Association if he is resident therein and introduce himself to the judge before whom he will plead.
An advocate has no right to accept a lawsuit against the Bar Association or against any decision of its Council before informing the President of the Bar thereof in writing.
An advocate has no right to wear the advocate's robe when he appears in his personal cases.

If a dispute or difficulty arises between advocates or between them and a judge, the advocate shall not complicate the dispute and shall refer the matter to the President of the Bar or to one of the members of the Bar Council present at the Palace of Justice.

With reference to Article 83 - of the Law Regulating the Legal Profession, the partnership agreement concluded between advocates must specify:

1- The things or rights that belong to the partnership.

2- The rights and obligations of each partner.

3- The headquarters of the partnership.
None of the partners may have an office other than the office of the partnership.
A partner has no right to assign his rights in the partnership because they are personal to him.

Each partner may withdraw from the partnership at any time after notifying his partners of the matter at least three months in advance. In this case, the partners remain bound to follow up on the joint cases unless they agree otherwise with the clients.
A copy of the partnership agreement must be deposited with the Bar Council.

An advocate has no right to belong to more than one of the partnerships provided for in Article 83 of the Law of 11 March 1970, nor does he have the right to remain a member of the partnership if he has retired from the legal profession.
A partner advocate has no right to accept a file or a client if one of the partners objects thereto.

Partner advocates are prohibited from performing any professional act, such as accepting a mandate or giving an opinion, that conflicts with the interest of a client of one of the other partners. An incompatibility arising from the capacity of one of the members of the partnership applies to the rest of the partners.
Partner advocates shall seek to resolve their disputes resulting from the partnership by way of arbitration.
An advocate is prosecuted disciplinarily on the initiative of the President of the Bar or pursuant to a complaint.

The President of the Bar may assign one of the members of the Bar Council to investigate the complaint; the investigator shall acquaint the advocate with what is attributed to him and with all the papers and documents of the file, and shall record his statements. He may question witnesses without administering the oath to them and take any action capable of revealing the truth. Upon completion of the investigation, he shall draw up an objective report in which he does not include his opinion and submit it to the President of the Bar, who decides in light thereof whether or not to prosecute.
An advocate shall answer what is attributed to him and the questions of the investigator with complete frankness, unless he is bound by professional secrecy.

An application by a lawyer to strike his name off the Roll of the Bar Association during disciplinary prosecution against him shall not preclude the continuation of the prosecution and the enforcement of the decision rendered as a result thereof.
The Disciplinary Council may form its conviction by all means of proof.
The Disciplinary Council shall deliberate starting by taking the opinion of the youngest member and ending with the President.

A lawyer suspended from practice is prohibited, during the period of his suspension, from performing, whether by himself or through any other lawyer, any act of the profession, or from participating in the General Assembly of Lawyers, or from wearing the lawyer's robe. The lawyer shall forfeit, during this period, all the rights granted to lawyers, including benefiting from the Cooperative Fund, whilst remaining subject to the duties imposed upon them.
The Internal Regulations issued on 12 April 1962 under number 384 and every prior regulatory text are repealed in all that is contrary to or inconsistent with the provisions of these Regulations.
These Internal Regulations shall enter into force after the lapse of ten days from their posting in the hall of the Bar Association. (End)
Decision No. 527 dated 23/4/958 and Decision 3464/B dated 31/12/64 are hereby repealed, and all previous decisions whose provisions conflict with the provisions of this Decision are likewise repealed

Working hours at construction and public works sites shall be set:

From seven o'clock until nineteen o'clock

The hours for the use of mechanical machinery at construction and public works sites, including: drilling machines, bulldozers, concrete mixers, machines for driving prefabricated piles, artesian well drilling machines, compressor and jackhammer units, tile polishers, machines for demolishing structures (wrecking ball crane) and all other similar noise-causing machinery, shall be set as follows:

A- Starting from the first of the month of May until the end of the month of October:

- From seven o'clock until fourteen o'clock.

- From fifteen thirty o'clock until nineteen o'clock.

B- Starting from the first of the month of November until the end of the month of April .

- From seven o'clock until thirteen o'clock.

- From fifteen o'clock until eighteen o'clock.
Work at construction and public works sites is prohibited on Sundays and official national holidays.
Exceptional cases shall be submitted to the Governor to take the necessary measures regarding them.
This Decision shall be published wherever the need arises.

The closing times for owners of grocer's, provision, dairy, cheese, and cigarette shops in the following streets of Beirut: Al-Zahhar - Adib Ishaq - Sassine - Al-Sioufi and its branches - Al-Ghazaliyeh - Farah - Mar Louis - Mar Nicolas - Mar Mitr - Ishaq Bin Hunayn - Al-Sayyar - Hotel-Dieu - Hawooz Al-Dahdili - Bishop Ghafrail - Bishop Massarra - Sheikh Al-Ghabi - Damascus Road up to Nazareth Street - Nazareth Station - Abdel Wahab Al-Inglizi - Deir Al-Nasirah and its branches - Saif Al-Din Al-Khatib - Zahrat Al-Ihsan - Monot Street - Sodeco Street - Al-Baroudi Street - Lebanon Street - Trabaud Street - Zeidan Street - Furn Al-Hayek, shall be determined as follows: Sundays - the first of May - and the 22nd of November of each year.

These provisions shall not prejudice the right of employees to benefit from a weekly rest for a period of thirty-six hours, which, along with working hours, shall be announced in accordance with the provisions of Articles 35 and 36 of the Labour Law.

No person shall have the right to open the establishment referred to in Article One or to carry on his work therein during the times specified for the closing of such establishments, even if they trade in other articles alongside their principal trade.
Each of the establishments referred to in Article One of this Decision shall post on its outer door a notice of the closing times as specified by this Decision.

Every violation of the provisions of this Decision shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of Article One of the Law of 17 September 1962 amending Articles 107 and 108 of the Labour Law, as amended by Decree No. 9816 dated 4/5/1968.
This Decision shall be published and notified where needed.

Single Article:

The draft law aiming at the organisation of the Lebanese University, as amended by the Finance and Budget Committee pursuant to its report dated 23 November 1967 and the National Education Committee pursuant to its report dated 21 November 1967, has been approved.

This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The Lebanese University is a public institution that performs the tasks of official higher education in its various branches and degrees, and in which there shall be centres for higher scientific and literary research, seeking in all of that to root human values in the souls of citizens.

The following words and expressions, wherever they appear in this Law, shall have the following meanings:

"The University": The Lebanese University.

"The Council": The Council of the Lebanese University.

"The Minister": The Minister of Tutelage.

"The Unit": A faculty or institute.
The Lebanese University shall undertake the holding of examinations that lead to the conferring of Lebanese university degrees and ranks.

The Lebanese University has moral personality. It enjoys academic, administrative, and financial autonomy, and the Minister of Education and Higher Education has the right of tutelage over it, all in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

Arabic is the language of instruction at the Lebanese University, and certain subjects may be taught in a foreign language where necessary, and such subjects shall be determined by a decision of the University Council.

The Lebanese University shall comprise the following faculties and institutes:

1 - The Faculty of Law and Political and Administrative Sciences.

2 - The Faculty of Letters and Human Sciences.

3 - The Faculty of Sciences.

4 - The Faculty of Education.

5 - The Institute of Social Sciences.

6 - The Institute of Information (the designation was amended pursuant to D. 309 d. 4/1/71)

7 - The Institute of Fine Arts.

8 - The Faculty of Business Administration (as amended by Decree No. 14304 dated 20/4/70).

(The following faculties and institutes were added to the Law on the Organisation of the Lebanese University)

9 - The Institute of Applied and Economic Sciences (established pursuant to Decree 10434 / 1968)

10 - The Faculty of Engineering. (established pursuant to Decree 9305 / 1974)

11 - The Faculty of Agriculture. (established pursuant to Decree 9306 / 1974)

12 - The Faculty of Public Health . (established pursuant to Decree 4418 / 1981)

13 - The Faculty of Medical Sciences. (established pursuant to Decree 1118/ 1983)

14 - The Centre for Research and Studies in Legal Informatics. (established pursuant to Decree 3144 / 1986)

15 - The Faculty of Pharmacy . (established pursuant to Decree 4142/ 1993)

16 - The University Institute of Technology. (established pursuant to Decree 8741/ 1996)

17 - The Faculty of Tourism and Hotel Management (established pursuant to Decree 10332/ 1997)

18 - The Faculty of Dental Medicine (established pursuant to Decree 427/ 1999)

19 - Doctoral Schools (Ecoles Doctorales) .(established pursuant to Decree in force ipso jure 74 / 2007)

20 - The establishment of the Faculty of Marine Sciences at the Lebanese University. (established pursuant to Decree 6686/2020)

Faculties and institutes shall be established, abolished, and merged into one another, and branches thereof shall be established where the need arises, and their general regulations shall be laid down and amended by decrees taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Education and Higher Education after consulting the opinion of the University Council or upon its recommendation.

The Lebanese University may establish cultural relations with universities and higher institutes in Lebanon and abroad, provided that in its contacts it observes the provisions of the laws and regulations in force.

a - Members of the teaching staff and employees of the University, both technical and administrative, are employees of the State, and are subject to all laws and regulations relating to other employees, in particular the provisions on step advancement, grade promotion, promotion, dismissal, and retirement, except for the special provisions set forth in this Law and in the regulations relating to the University.

b - Paragraph (c) of Article 4 of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12 June 1959 shall not apply to candidates for appointment to the technical cadre of the University.

The Lebanese University shall be exempted from the provisions of the First Article and from the provisions of Paragraph 2 and Paragraph 3 Section (e) of the Ninth Article, and Paragraph 3 of Article 12 of Legislative Decree No. 114 dated 12/6/1959, and it shall also be exempted from the provisions of Paragraph (c) of Item Third of Article 40 and from the provisions of Article 43 of Decree No. 8337 dated 30 December 1961. It shall likewise be exempted from the provisions of the First Article of Legislative Decree No. 115 dated 12/6/1959, with the exception of the financial field.
The administration of the University shall be undertaken by a President and a Council .

1- The President of the University shall be appointed from among five candidates holding the rank of professor or who have fulfilled the conditions of the rank, nominated by the University Council.

The appointment shall take place by a decree based upon a decision taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister, at least two months prior to the expiry of the term of office of the President of the University.

2- The nomination mechanism shall be determined by a decision taken in the University Council.

3- The term of office of the President shall be fixed at five years, non-renewable except after the expiry of a full term of office.

4- The President shall be exempted from his teaching load.

5- In the event of the absence of the President, the eldest of the Deans shall deputise for him.

6- In the event of a vacancy in the post of the President, a new President shall be appointed by the same mechanism provided for in this Article.
The President of the University is an employee of the First Category.

The President of the University shall secure the administration of the general affairs of the University. He shall have a permanent delegation from the Minister of Education and Higher Education to exercise the administrative and financial powers enjoyed by the Minister in respect of the academic, administrative, and financial affairs of the University, and within the provisions of this Law.

Included among his tasks are:

- Representing the University in legal acts, before the judiciary, and before all official and private administrations and institutions.

- Preparing the work of the University Council, presiding over its meetings, and executing its resolutions.

- Preparing the draft general budget.

- Commissioning lecturers.

- Recommending the appointment of the Secretary-General of the University and its other administrative employees.

- All other powers provided for by the laws and regulations or delegated to him by the University Council.

The President of the University shall submit at the end of each academic year a report to the Minister of Education and Higher Education on the administrative, financial, and academic affairs of the University in accordance with Article 19 of this Law.

- The University Council shall be composed of:

- The President of the University as President

- The Deans of the faculties and the Directors of the institutes affiliated with the University.

- A representative from each of these faculties and institutes elected by the members of the teaching staff who are part of the cadre from among themselves at the beginning of each academic year.

If there is no teaching staff in the cadre in the faculty or institute, the contracted members of the teaching staff shall elect him from among themselves.

- Representatives of the National Union of Students of the Lebanese University at the rate of one representative for each faculty and institute appointed by the Executive Committee of the Union, provided that he is from among the members of this Committee.

- The Secretary-General of the University shall perform the function of Secretary-General of the Council.

The Council shall meet upon the convocation of the President of the University and at the time appointed by him, and whenever one-third of the members submit to him a reasoned written request, or upon the request of the Minister of Education and Higher Education.

Meetings of the University Council shall not be valid unless attended by at least half of the members.

Decisions shall be taken by a majority of votes , and in the event of a tie, the side that includes the President shall prevail .

The functions of the University Council shall encompass:

- Establishing the internal regulations of the University.

- Expressing an opinion on the draft financial regulations of the University.

- Approving the internal regulations of the faculties and institutes.

- Nominating the members of the teaching staff and all other members of the technical cadre.

- Approving the curricula and programmes of study.

- Deciding on contracting with persons nominated by the faculties and institutes to work in the various university activities.

- Accepting participation in scientific and cultural conferences and appointing the person who shall represent the University therein.

- Examining the draft annual budget.

- Supervising the administration of the properties of the University.

- Establishing the regulations of the University Campus.

- Adjudicating on the contracts and transactions concluded by the University, within the limits prescribed by the financial regulations.

- Accepting donations.

- Deciding on the institution and defence of legal proceedings.

- Expressing an opinion on everything relating to the amendment of this Law and the regulations supplementing it.

- All other functions provided for in this Law.

- The University Council shall perform the functions of the Civil Service Board and the Central Inspection Board in respect of the technical and administrative employees of the University.

- The representatives of the National Union of Lebanese University Students shall enjoy all the powers and functions enjoyed by the remaining members and provided for in this Article, except for the powers and functions provided for in the fourth, fifth and sixteenth paragraphs set out above, where they shall have consultative votes only.

- And the representatives of the Union shall not participate in exercising the powers and functions provided for in Article 42 of this Law (No. 75/67 issued on 26 December 1967).

The decision of the Council relating to the internal regulations of the University and the regulations of the University Campus or to the acceptance of donations from Lebanese nationals shall not become effective except after the approval of the Minister of Education and Higher Education.

As for its decision regarding the acceptance of donations from non-Lebanese nationals, it shall not become effective except after approval thereof by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Education and Higher Education.

As for participation in scientific and cultural conferences outside Lebanese territory and the appointment of the person who shall represent the University therein, it shall be subject to the approval of the Council of Ministers.

The Council shall debate in the month of March of each year a general report prepared by the President on the administrative, financial and academic affairs of the University and submitted by him to the Minister of Education and Higher Education.

The University shall administer its funds by itself, and it shall have an independent budget which shall be subject in its preparation, execution and the supervision of its execution to the provisions of special regulations issued by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of National Education and the Minister of Finance after consultation with the Court of Accounts and the recommendation of the University Council.

The budget of the University shall be funded:

A - By the appropriations allocated to it in the general budget.

B - By donations.

C - By registration fees.

D - By the proceeds of the sale of its publications.

E - By the revenues of its properties and all other revenues allocated to the University or obtained by the University, in accordance with the provisions of this Law.
The financial regulations shall determine the rules governing the contracts and transactions concluded by the University.

The Ministry of Finance shall be represented at the University by an employee whom it seconds in the capacity of financial controller, provided that he is of the third category at least.

The salary of the financial controller shall be paid out of the general budget of the State and he shall not be entitled to receive any allowance from the budget of the University, and his powers shall be determined in the financial regulations.
The university unit shall be administered by a dean and a council.

On the appointment of the dean of the unit:

1- The dean shall be appointed for a term of four years, not renewable except after the expiry of a full term, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the supervising Minister.

2- The proposal of the Minister shall be based on a list of nominations bearing three names submitted by the University Council from among five names proposed by the council of the unit concerned.

3- The selection of the candidates referred to in item 2 shall take place from among the professors of the unit included in the cadre of the faculty holding the rank of professor or those who have fulfilled the requirements of the rank, and failing that, the candidates may be selected from among the full-time contracted staff holding the rank of professor or those who have fulfilled the requirements of the rank, provided that the appointed dean is admitted in the very same decree into the cadre of the University if he meets the requirements for admission into the cadre. And failing the availability of persons holding the rank of professor or who have fulfilled the requirements of the rank, they may be selected from among the professors of another unit, subject to homogeneity in specialisation.

4- In the event of the absence of the dean of the unit for more than fifteen days, the highest-ranking or highest-grade director shall deputise for him. And in the event of a vacancy, a new dean shall be appointed to complete the term in accordance with the mechanism provided for in this Article.
The dean of the unit shall be exempted from at most half of his teaching load.

The dean or the director may be relieved of his function by a decree based either on his request or on the proposal of the Minister of Education and Higher Education after seeking the opinion of the University Council, or upon the recommendation of the University Council.

The dean or the director shall preside over the council of the faculty or institute and his functions shall encompass:

- Preparing the business of the council of the faculty or institute and executing its resolutions.

- Ensuring the application of the regulations within the faculty or institute.

- Organising classes and examinations.

- Preparing the draft budget in respect of the faculty or institute for submission to the Council.

- All other functions provided for by the laws and regulations or delegated to him by the President or the University Council or the council of the faculty or institute.

A- The council of the unit shall be composed of:

1- The dean of the unit as president.

2- The directors of the branches of the unit.

3- The representatives of the teaching staff on the councils of the branches.

4- The head of the research centre, where one exists.

5- Two representatives of the students in the unit in accordance with a mechanism established by the University Council.

6- The representative of the professors of the unit on the University Council, without having the right to vote.

B - In the absence of branches, the council of the unit shall be composed of:

1- The dean of the unit as president.

2- The heads of the academic departments, and in the absence of departments, four members elected by the members of the teaching staff from among themselves.

3- An elected representative of the teaching staff.

4- The head of the research centre, where one exists.

5- Two representatives of the students.

6- The representative of the professors of the unit on the University Council shall attend the meetings of the council of the unit without having the right to vote.

- The council of the unit shall meet once every two weeks at least upon convocation by its president, or pursuant to a reasoned written request by one third of the members, or pursuant to a request by the University Council or its President.

- The sittings of the council shall be valid if attended by at least two thirds of the members at the first convocation, and otherwise by an absolute majority at the second convocation.

- Decisions shall be taken by an absolute majority, and in the event of a tie the president shall have a casting vote.

- The secretary of the university unit shall perform the function of secretary of this council, and shall draw up the minutes of the sittings and keep them in due form, after their signature by the president and the members, and in the event of his absence the dean of the unit shall assign a person to perform the functions of secretary of the council.
The provisions applicable to the meetings of the University Council shall apply to the meetings of the council of the unit.

Functions of the Unit Council:

The functions of the Unit Council shall cover the following:

1- Laying down the internal regulations of the unit, provided that they are coupled with the approval of the University Council.

2- Submitting proposals in the various affairs of the unit, especially with regard to curricula, research, research contracts, examination regulations, and the entrance competitive examination.

3- Proposing full-time service contracts and nominations for appointment based on the recommendations of the branch councils, or the departments in faculties that have no branches, in accordance with the mechanism provided for by Decree No. 9084 dated 13/11/2002. And proposing hourly teaching and training contracts pertaining to the unit.

4- Nominating members of the technical and administrative staff for appointment, contracting, and promotion based on the recommendations of the branch councils.

5- Recommending contracting with candidates to work in the various activities of the unit.

6- Proposing the draft budget of the unit based on the proposals of the branch councils.

7- Discussing and approving the annual report prepared by the Dean on the administrative, financial, and academic affairs of the unit, in preparation for submitting it to the University Council before the end of the month of March.

8- Proposing the names of outstanding students nominated to benefit from specialisation scholarships based on the recommendations of the branches, or the departments in faculties that have no branches. This shall be in accordance with the regulations in force and the designation of missions.

9- Proposing candidates from among the members of the teaching staff to benefit from scholarships and pursue further study, based on the recommendations of the branch councils.

10- Deciding on the applications of members of the teaching staff to benefit from the seventh year.

11- Proposing cooperation and exchange projects with public and private institutions at home and abroad, and participation in scientific seminars and specialised conferences.

12- Proposing enrolment fees and fees for the use of the facilities of the unit.

Related text: Amendment of the annual fees collected from students who enrol in the Lebanese University

13- Proposing the approval of grants, donations, contributions, and gifts offered to the unit or to one of its components.

14- Discussing the semi-annual reports and recommendations of the branch directors submitted to the Unit Council

15- Submitting nominations for the position of Dean of the unit and Director of the research centre.

16- Reviewing the results of the examinations and the results of the entrance competitive examination to the unit.

17- Proposing to the University Council the annulment of decisions taken by the Dean of the unit which contravene the adopted regulations and laws, by an absolute majority.

18- Proposing to the University Council the annulment of decisions taken by one of the directors of the branches and centres and heads of departments which contravene the adopted regulations and laws, by an absolute majority. With the reservation of the right of the maker of the contested decision to apply for review before the University Council.

19- All other functions provided for by the laws and regulations in force.

The council of the faculty or institute shall discuss in the month of February of every year a report prepared by the Dean or the Director on the administrative, financial, and academic affairs of the faculty or institute and shall submit it to the President of the University.

The President of the University is the head of the teaching staff in the University.

And the Dean of the faculty or the Director of the institute is the head of the teaching staff in the faculty or institute.

The teaching staff in the University shall consist of:

a - Professors, assistant professors, and lecturers, who are permanent civil servants of the State subject to the General Civil Service Regulations and to the special provisions set forth in this Law.

b - Contracted professors, who are those with whom the University contracts to give hours in the various teaching subjects.

The number of professors, assistant professors, lecturers, and all other staff of the technical cadre shall be determined year by year in the budget of the University.

As for the contracted members of the teaching staff, the University Council shall determine the rank of each of them.

Professors, assistant professors, and lecturers shall be appointed by a decree taken upon the proposal of the Minister of Education and Higher Education.

- The proposal of the Minister shall be based on a list of nominations bearing at least three names for each post, submitted by the University Council on the basis of a reasoned recommendation from the council of the competent faculty or institute.

- Where there is a divergence of opinion between the University Council and the recommendation of the council of the faculty or institute, the University Council may accompany this recommendation with an independent list of nominations.

- Lecturers shall spend two years of probation after which they shall be confirmed in their tenure based on the recommendation of the council of the faculty and the approval of the University Council; if two years pass and they are not confirmed in their tenure, they shall be transferred by operation of law to the secondary education cadre or to another of the cadres of the State.

- Candidates for appointment to the technical cadre of the University shall not be subject to the condition of a competitive examination.

The special regulations of each faculty and institute shall determine the conditions for the appointment of professors, assistant professors, lecturers, and all other staff of the technical cadre, and shall also determine the conditions for contracting.

A professor, an assistant professor, and a lecturer may not be assigned to teach a subject that is not within their specialisation, and the determination of specialisation shall be based on the degrees held by the person concerned or on the subjects of his studies, his authored works, or his previous teaching.

The University Council shall determine the number of weekly teaching hours required of professors, assistant professors, and lecturers. None of these may teach in another institute or perform work outside the University unless he gives the University the full hours required of him under its regulations, and has obtained in advance an authorisation from the President of the University based on the opinion of the competent Dean or Director, after the approval of the council of the faculty or institute.

A professor, an assistant professor, and a lecturer shall be entitled to benefit, at the end of every sixth year of his teaching, from a leave with full salary for a period of one academic year, the regulations of which shall be determined by a decree taken upon the proposal of the Minister of Education and Higher Education and the recommendation of the University Council, provided that the purpose is to further specialisation or to devote oneself to scientific research.

The University Council shall perform the functions of the Disciplinary Board for the members of the teaching staff and all other members of the technical cadre in accordance with the rules that shall be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Education and Higher Education and the recommendation of the University Council.

It shall be permissible to enter into commitments with contracted professors to teach subjects that can be assigned to members of the teaching staff who are part of the cadre.

- Contracted professors shall be chosen from among Lebanese nationals, whether civil servants, retirees, or non-civil servants, and they may be non-Lebanese if it is not possible to find qualified Lebanese professors to teach the subject.

- Where necessary, it shall be permissible to contract with members of the teaching staff who are part of the cadre of the University to teach therein while performing the full hours required of them in accordance with Article 40, provided that the number of contracted hours does not exceed the number of their statutory hours.

- Contracting shall take place year by year, based on the decision of the University Council and the recommendation of the council of the faculty or institute. The President of the University shall sign the contract.

- The teaching hours shall be specified in the contract, provided that they do not exceed the maximum number of hours required of the members of the teaching staff who are part of the cadre.

- No distinction shall be made between contracted professors in remuneration and allowances except with respect to academic standing in accordance with rates set by the University Council.

- Members of the teaching staff who are part of the cadre may be assigned research, inquiries, and investigations in addition to their teaching hours. This shall be in return for an allowance estimated by the council of the faculty and approved by the University Council. The President of the University shall sign the assignment.

The central administrative body of the University shall consist of a General Secretariat which shall be responsible for:

1- The Secretariat of the Presidency

2- The Secretariat of the University, which shall be responsible for:

a - The Secretariat of the University Council

b - Ensuring statistics, information, and publications.

c - Ensuring relations between the University and other universities.

d - Ensuring cultural and university exchange affairs.

e - Ensuring university ceremonies and celebrations.

f - Ensuring conferences.

g - Ensuring the student guide.

h - Supervising the Central Library.

i - Supervising the General Superintendence.

j - Supervising the administration of the University City (for record).

k - All other secretarial works assigned to it by the President of the University.

3- The Joint Administrative Service, which shall be responsible for:

a - Ensuring liaison between the Presidency of the University and its faculties and institutes.

b - Ensuring the correspondence of the University and the affairs of employees and wage earners.

c - Publishing circulars and administrative decisions.

d- Keeping papers and documents received from the faculties and institutes of the University, etc.

e - Keeping the files of the University employees attached to the central administration and keeping copies of the files of permanent and non-permanent employees of the faculties and institutes.

f- Ensuring supplies, materials accounting, and keeping the records thereof in the central administration, and seeing to the coordination and keeping of these records in all faculties and institutes.

g- Seeing to ensuring joint purchases and preparing what is required therefor.

h - Bureau works in general and all other works assigned to it by the President of the University.

i - Supervising the Financial Department, the duties of which are determined in the Financial Regulations.

The administrative and technical body of each faculty and institute shall consist of:

- The Secretariat.

- The Library.

- The Laboratories.

The Secretariat of the faculty or institute shall be responsible for:

- The Secretariat of the Council of the faculty or institute.

- Organising class schedules.

- Ensuring and publishing correspondence, circulars, and notices.

- Registering students and preparing enrollment cards.

- Organising and keeping the files of members of the teaching staff and the files of students.

- Providing information relating to all affairs of the faculty or institute.

- Ensuring the formalities of collecting fees in accordance with the Financial Regulations, ensuring the needs of the faculty or institute for supplies, and keeping the records thereof.

- All other administrative works assigned to it by the Dean or the Director.

- Bureau works in general.

The academic qualification that entitles a student to enroll in the Lebanese University is the Lebanese Baccalaureate certificate (Part Two) or its equivalent. All other conditions shall be determined in the regulations of each faculty and institute.

The enrollment of a student in the faculties and institutes of the University shall be effected after completion of the conditions for his registration in accordance with the regulations of each faculty and institute.

The schedule of fees payable by those enrolled in the University shall be determined by a decree taken upon the proposal of the Minister of Education and Higher Education based on the recommendation of the University Council.

This fee shall be collected in accordance with the regulations of each faculty and institute.

Notwithstanding any other text, "the student's contribution to entrance competitions, enrollment tests, and examinations of all kinds in the various units of the Lebanese University shall be fixed at thirty-five thousand pounds and shall be collected as revenues for the budget of the University".

The University Council shall determine the starting day of the academic year at the University, provided that such day falls within the ten days of the month of October of each year, and it shall also pertain to the said Council to determine the date of termination of classes at the University.
The conditions for student attendance shall be determined in the regulations of each faculty and institute.

University examinations for the academic year shall be held on dates determined by the University Council based on the recommendation of the Council of the faculty or institute, provided that each subject of study shall have two sessions.

Students of private higher institutes may sit for these examinations within the conditions determined by the regulations of each faculty and institute in the University.

In exceptional circumstances, teaching sessions may be opened outside the scope of the academic year provided for in Article 50, by a decision of the President of the University taken based on the recommendation of the University Council.

The Dean or the Director shall manage the examination operations in his faculty or institute, supervise the order thereof, propose the appointment of proctors, and take the necessary measures to prevent and detect cheating.
