a- What is owned by non-Lebanese natural persons and legal persons, or those deemed to be on the same footing as non-Lebanese, after the entry into force of the Law implemented by Decree No. 11614 dated 04/01/1969, across the entirety of Lebanese territory may not exceed three per cent (3%) of its total area, provided that it does not exceed 3% (three per cent) in each district (qada) of its total area and does not exceed in the Governorate of Beirut ten per cent (10%) of its total area. b Account shall be taken in calculating the percentages mentioned above of the ownership of Lebanese companies deemed to be on the same footing as non-Lebanese according to the provisions of the Second Article of the Law implemented by Decree No. 11614 dated 04/01/1969, with the exception of:

1- Partnerships and limited liability companies in which the majority, that is more than fifty per cent of the shares, is owned by natural Lebanese partners or purely Lebanese companies whose articles of association prohibit the assignment of these shares to non-Lebanese, in which case a percentage of fifty per cent (50%) only of the areas that they own shall be counted within the percentages set forth in this Article.

2- Joint-stock companies or partnerships limited by shares in which the majority of the shares, that is more than fifty per cent of the shares, is owned by natural Lebanese persons or purely Lebanese companies whose articles of association prohibit the assignment of these shares to non-Lebanese, in which case a percentage of fifty per cent (50%) only of the areas that they own shall be counted within the percentages set forth in this Article. The attainment of the ownership percentages shall be declared by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance, and the acquisition by non-Lebanese, or those deemed to be on the same footing as non-Lebanese according to the provisions of the Second Article of the Law implemented by Decree No. 11614 dated 04/01/1969, of real property rights shall be suspended unless such acquisition takes place between non-Lebanese persons or those deemed to be on the same footing as non-Lebanese. The Automated Centre in the Ministry of Finance, Directorate of Real Estate Affairs, shall undertake the organisation of the data and statistics necessary to show the said percentages, and upon the attainment of the legal percentages the Directorate of Real Estate Affairs shall take the necessary measures to halt the operations of registering real rights for non-Lebanese, provided that these data are published in the Official Gazette every six months.

- New Article 8: For the purpose of designating the areas that non-Lebanese natural persons may own with or without a licence according to the provisions of this Law, husbands, wives and minor children shall be deemed to be on the same footing as a single person. A child who has not attained eighteen full years of age shall be deemed a minor for the application of this Article.

- New Article 11: Every natural person who has acquired a real property right, in accordance with the provisions of this Law, must complete the erection of a building on the right that is the subject of ownership within a maximum time-limit of five years from the date of registration in the Real Estate Register, extendable once by a decision of the Council of Ministers, and likewise every legal person must allocate the real properties that are the subject of ownership to the purpose for which it acquired ownership or was granted the licence within the said time-limit. All of this shall be under penalty of forfeiture or cancellation of the right and its sale by the Ministry of Finance together with what was erected thereon for the account of the offender and at his expense and responsibility in accordance with the provisions of Legislative Decree No. 147 dated 12/06/1959 "Procedures for the Collection of Direct Taxes and Similar Fees".

And the entire profit resulting from the sale shall be confiscated in favour of the Treasury after the full price and legal expenses have been returned to the holder of the right. And the judicial courts shall have jurisdiction to hear disputes arising from the application of the provisions of this Article. Licence time-limits prior to the entry into force of this Law, both expired and unexpired, shall be deemed extended ipso jure and without the need to issue a special text therefor, provided that the period of extension does not exceed five years from the date of entry into force of this Law.

- New Article 13: Upon the dissolution of companies, establishments and associations licensed or exempted from a licence to own real property rights in Lebanon, it is prohibited to partition these rights and distribute them in kind to non-Lebanese partners except on condition of observing the provisions of this Law.

- New Article 19: For the purpose of calculating the ownership percentages provided for in paragraph "a" of the new Seventh Article, account shall be taken of the areas licensed to be acquired or acquired without a licence after the date of entry into force of the Law implemented by Decree No. 11614 dated 04/01/1969, and those licensed to be acquired or acquired without a licence after the entry into force of this Law, taking into consideration the provisions of the new Seventh Article and the provisions of the last paragraph of the new Article (11).
Articles 6 and 14 of the Law rendered enforceable by Decree No. 11614 dated 04/01/1969 are repealed
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

If the seat of one of the members of the Council falls vacant before the expiration of the term, the vacant seat shall be filled by the candidate who obtained the highest number of votes in the previous elections.

If, however, three or more seats fall vacant before the expiration of two-thirds of the term of office of the Council, the General Assembly shall be convened to fill the vacant seats in an election session.

The Council of the Order shall be deemed dissolved if the number of vacant seats therein exceeds two-thirds of its members, and new elections shall be held within one month from its being deemed dissolved; the President of the Order shall remain in his post until the new elections, and if the post of the President of the Order also falls vacant, the Minister of Health may appoint a provisional committee to manage the affairs of the Order until the elections are held.

The functions of the Council of the Order shall include the following matters:

- Drawing up the internal regulations of the Order and amending them with the approval of the Minister of Public Health Implementing the resolutions of the General Assembly.

- Managing the accounts and collecting the annual fee and the registration fee payable by physiotherapists.

- Supervising the compliance of all physiotherapists with the laws and ethics of the profession and with the duties of their profession.

- Endeavouring to settle disputes between physiotherapists and other members of the health and medical professions, or between physiotherapists and their patients, arising from the practice of the profession.

- Communicating with the authorities or other bodies and persons in respect of the interests of the Order.

- Performing all acts relating to the management of the Order that do not fall within the competence of the General Assembly.

- Expressing an opinion on all drafts and regulations referred to it by the Ministry of Public Health.

Meetings of the Council of the Order shall not be valid unless attended by at least seven members, provided that it holds its meeting on the day fixed by a decision thereof or upon a special invitation addressed by the President of the Order to all the members.

The Council of the Order shall hold its meeting at the headquarters of the Order.
The Council of the Order shall adopt its decisions by a majority of votes, and in the event of a tie, the Chairman shall have a casting vote.

Every person having capacity and interest, as well as the Appellate Public Prosecution, may appeal the decisions of the Council of the Order within a time limit of ten days from the date of notification. The appeal shall be lodged with the Court of Appeal, and the said Court shall rule thereon in camera after adding to its bench two members of the Council of the Order chosen by the said Council, and the Court of Appeal may rule on any dispute even if it is not possible for two members of the Council of the Order to join it due to the dissolution of the Council or their abstention from participating on the bench of the Court.

These decisions of the Court of Appeal shall not be subject to any form of review.

Committees shall be formed, the members of each not exceeding five, to assist in managing the affairs of the Order, and the Council of the Order shall choose their members from within the Council or from outside it, provided that each committee is chaired by a member of the Council of the Order.

These committees shall be constituted as follows:

- The Financial Committee

- The Administrative and Professional Committee

- The Scientific and Educational Committee

- The Social, Public and International Relations, and Media Committee.

The Financial Committee:

This Committee shall be chaired by the Treasurer of the Order and shall be entrusted with the following tasks and powers.

a - Collecting funds against counterfoil receipts signed by the Treasurer and by the President of the Order and recorded in a special register kept for this purpose.

b -Safekeeping the funds of the Order, and no sum may be disbursed except pursuant to a decision of the Council of the Order; however, if the sum to be disbursed does not exceed three times the minimum wage, it may be disbursed upon the request of the President of the Order, provided that such disbursement is justified at the first meeting of the Council of the Order.

c - Preparing the annual financial report, the final accounts and the draft budget for submission to the Council of the Order and to the General Assembly to obtain their approval.

d - Its Chairman, the Treasurer, shall sign with the President of the Order the receipts, vouchers for withdrawal of the funds of the Order from the accredited bank, and all transactions relating to the funds of the Order.

e - In the event that the post of the Chairman of the Committee, the Treasurer, falls vacant, the Council of the Order shall meet immediately to elect a successor to him.

f - Keeping a register in which the revenues and expenditures of the Order are recorded.

g - Carrying out the necessary sales and purchases pursuant to a decision of the Council of the Order.

h - Proposing the pricing of advertisements to the Council of the Order.

The Administrative and Professional Committee:

This Committee shall be chaired by the Secretary of the Order, and this Committee shall assist him in performing the following tasks and powers:

a - Drafting invitations to ordinary and extraordinary meetings of the General Assembly and meetings of the Council of the Order upon the request of the President of the Order, provided that the invitation includes the agenda of the session intended to be held.

b - Receiving all correspondence pertaining to the Order, recording it in the incoming register, and keeping it in files after the President of the Order and the members of the Council of the Order have reviewed it at their first meeting.

c - Keeping a special register of the names of the subscribing members, their addresses and their places of work, and for this purpose a file shall be organised for each affiliated member and kept at the Order.

d - The Secretary, Chairman of the Committee, shall sign with the President of the Order all decisions, correspondence, statements, invitations, membership cards and every transaction issued by the Order, and shall record them in the outgoing register and keep a copy thereof.

e - Engaging the administrative staff of the Order to accomplish the administrative work in the Order after the approval of the Council.

f - The Committee, in cooperation with the President of the Order, shall propose the names of members of the General Assembly from all regions as administrative delegates to facilitate the administrative and syndical communication process between the Council of the Order and the General Assembly.

g - Preparing a report every six months on the activity of the Order to be submitted to the Council of the Order for approval and for submission to the General Assembly.

h - Conducting a comprehensive and continuous survey of physiotherapy across Lebanese territory.

i - Drawing up a health map in the field of physiotherapy in Lebanon.

j - Representing the Order in professional activities by mandate from the Council of the Order.

k - Preparing calls for tenders for insurance with the President of the Order and the Treasurer and submitting them to the Council of the Order to obtain its approval.

The Scientific and Educational Committee:

It shall be entrusted with the following tasks and powers:

a - Representing the Order before universities, institutes and educational institutions by mandate from the Council of the Order.

b - Working on preparing orientation programmes, lectures and seminars for secondary school and university students to be approved by the Council of the Order.

c - Submitting proposals to the Council of the Order aimed at holding continuing education activities and retreats for the members of the Order.

d - Working to obtain scientific studies and research in the field of physiotherapy for distribution to the members or publication in the journal of the Order.

e - Following up on research and studies that may be conducted by a member of the Order and submitting a proposal to the Council of the Order to provide assistance to him where necessary.

f - Proposing to the Council of the Order studies and evaluation questionnaires relating to the needs of the members.

g - Being responsible for the library, archives and documentation in the Order

h - Supervising the scientific and educational section in the journal of the Order.

i - Representing the Order on the Colloquium Examinations Committee upon the proposal of the Council of the Order and by mandate from the Minister of Education and Higher Education.

The Social, Public and International Relations, and Media Committee:

This Committee shall be entrusted with:

A - Participating with the President of the Order in meetings of a decision-making nature regarding the international and local relations of the Order.

B - Following up on files and correspondence with domestic and foreign bodies and twinning projects, and subsequently informing the Council of the Order of the proceedings and results in order to take the appropriate decisions.

C - Establishing programmes for the visits undertaken by the Order.

D - Receiving foreign delegations and organising their residence and visit programmes pursuant to an assignment from the Council of the Order.

E - Contributing to supplying the journal with public and international activities.

F - Fostering social relations with colleagues and representing the Order at social occasions pursuant to an assignment from the Council of the Order.

G - Supervising the social section of the journal of the Order.

H - Dealing with the media and preparing bulletins, statements, and news.

In accordance with the provisions of Article Twenty-Seven of this Law, the Council of the Order shall establish, within the framework of the Bylaws of the Order and with the approval of the Minister of Health, rules governing the operation and powers of the committees, whose members shall be chosen by the Council of the Order from within or outside the Council, provided that each committee is chaired by a member of the Council of the Order.

All physical therapists who are members of the Order, whether Lebanese or non-Lebanese, who violate the duties of their profession and expose their dignity to that which compromises their honour, integrity, or competence, shall be subject to one of the following penalties:

A - Warning.

B - Reprimand.

C - Temporary suspension from work for a period not exceeding six months.

D - Permanent prohibition from practising the profession.

A physical therapist sentenced to temporary suspension shall be prohibited from practising the profession throughout the period to which he is sentenced.

The Disciplinary Board shall be composed of the President of the Order or his Vice-President as Chairman, two members of the Council of the Order elected by the said Council, and two members from outside the Council elected by the General Assembly for a renewable term of one full year; any person nominating himself for membership of the Disciplinary Board from outside the Council of the Order must have practised the profession for a period of at least five years on Lebanese territory.

Professional infractions shall be referred to the Disciplinary Board:

A - Pursuant to an inquiry submitted by the Ministry of Public Health, the Appellate Public Prosecution, or an aggrieved party, whether a physical therapist or not.

B - Pursuant to a request by the President of the Order.

C - Pursuant to a request by a physical therapist who considers himself the subject of an unjust accusation and spontaneously submits his case to the assessment of the Disciplinary Board.

The Disciplinary Board shall follow ordinary, confidential trial procedures, and in determining the liability of a physical therapist, it must take his good faith into consideration; it may resort to all means of proof and summon the prosecuted physical therapist to hear him.

The physical therapist must comply with the summons, answer the questions directed to him, and provide the explanations requested of him, and he may be assisted by one lawyer to defend him.

The Disciplinary Board must issue its decision within two months from the date of the complaint; if it fails to do so, both the President of the Order and the Public Prosecution shall have the right to transfer the case to the Court of Appeal, which shall adjudicate it in the last instance.
Disciplinary decisions shall be subject to opposition and appeal within a period of fifteen days commencing from the date of notification.
Notification shall be effected by registered letter with acknowledgment of receipt. The petition of appeal shall be submitted to the Court of Appeal of Beirut.

The decisions of the Disciplinary Board and the Court of Appeal shall be confidential.

However, if the physical therapist is convicted of an offence that compromises the honour and dignity of the physical therapy profession, or if he is sentenced twice within a period of one year to a penalty more severe than a reprimand, the Council of the Order may decide, by a two-thirds majority of its members, to post the decision at the premises of the Order for one month.
Disciplinary prosecution shall not preclude criminal proceedings if the infraction also constitutes an offence punishable under the Penal Code.

When a complaint is submitted to the President of the Order, he may appoint a rapporteur to conduct a preliminary investigation. The rapporteur member shall hear the statements of the physical therapist concerned after informing him of the substance of the matters attributed to him and acquainting him with the documents in the file; he may hear the statements of witnesses, request documents, and order signature verification. If the rapporteur deems it necessary to inspect the registers, the party concerned must facilitate his task and acquaint him with all that is necessary. Upon the conclusion of the investigation, the rapporteur shall draw up his report without expressing his personal opinion and submit it to the President of the Order, who shall decide whether there are grounds for prosecution or to file the report.

The President of the Order may settle disputes between members of the Order without resorting to disciplinary procedures and, where necessary, may by his own authority issue a fraternal warning which shall not be recorded in the registers of the Order.

A resignation submitted during a disciplinary investigation shall not be accepted, nor shall the resignation of a physical therapist suspended from work be accepted until after the execution of the penalty, and he shall remain throughout this period subject to the authority of the Order.
The physical therapist shall appear before the Disciplinary Board upon a summons from the Chairman of the Board.
The Disciplinary Board shall deliberate, beginning by taking the opinion of the youngest member by age and ending with the Chairman.
A physical therapist suspended from work may not, during the period of his suspension, perform any act of the profession or participate in a General Assembly.

The Secretariat of the Order shall maintain a special register arranged in alphabetical order in which the names of the physical therapists sentenced to disciplinary penalties shall be recorded along with the decisions issued against them; this register may not be inspected by anyone other than physical therapists registered on the roll of the Order pursuant to a written request submitted to the President of the Order.
The retirement fund shall be established by a special law.

A relief fund shall be established to grant financial assistance to physical therapists or their families.

The resources of this fund shall consist of:

1- Contributions provided by the members of the Order.

2- Donations permissible pursuant to the Law on Associations.

The methods of managing this fund shall be determined in the Bylaws.

The Order shall enjoy moral and legal personality; however, it shall not have the right to acquire real property except to the extent necessary for the management of its affairs in accordance with the laws in force.
The Order shall be subject to the supervision of the Minister of Public Health.

Within two months from the date of entry into force of this Law, the General Assembly composed of physical therapists registered with the Ministry of Public Health shall convene upon a convocation by the Minister of Health or his representative to elect the Council of the Order and the President of the Order in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

The Syndicate of Physical Therapists in Lebanon established pursuant to the Decision issued by the Minister of Labour under No. 33/1 dated 24/03/1987 shall be deemed dissolved immediately upon the entry into force of this Law, and its funds, assets, and rights, both movable and immovable, shall be liquidated by being converted and transferred to the Order established pursuant to this Law.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The General Master and Detailed Plan and Regulations for the region of Sidon, comprising the zoning as indicated on Map No. (1) at a scale of 1/2000 and the road setbacks indicated in green on Map No. (2) at a scale of 1/1000 attached to this Decree, are hereby approved. As for the road networks, they shall remain approved in accordance with the aforementioned Decree No. 9016, with the exception of the alignments and setbacks located within the pooling and subdivision zone in the real estate area of Al-Wastani in Sidon and indicated on Map No. (2) at a scale of 1/1000 referred to in Article One of this Decree.

Single Article

The bill aiming at the protection of literary and artistic property, as amended by the Joint Parliamentary Committees and the Chamber of Deputies, has been approved.

This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

For the purpose of applying the provisions of this Law, the words and expressions listed below shall have the following meanings unless the text indicates otherwise, and these definitions shall also apply to the subject of neighbouring rights.

- Performance of a work: is the execution of a work through exhibition, playing of musical instruments, recitation, narration, acting, dancing, or any other manner, whether directly or by means of any device or medium.

- Public performance: a performance shall be deemed public when it takes place in a place or places where persons may be present in a number exceeding the members of a single family or their direct acquaintances.

- Broadcasting: is the transmission of the work to the public by wireless transmission, including transmission via satellite.

- Computer program: is a set of instructions expressed in words, codes, or any other form capable, when incorporated into a medium readable by a computer, of causing the computer to perform or execute a task or give a result.

- Sound recording: is every fixation in any material form consisting of sounds, whether or not such sounds result from the performance of a work, but excluding the sound recording accompanying an audiovisual work.

- Reprographic reproduction: is the making of copies of the original copy of a work by means other than printing, such as copying by means of photocopying machines, and this includes enlarged and reduced copies of the work.

- Neighbouring rights: are the rights enjoyed by performing artists, producers of sound recordings, television and radio broadcasting organisations, stations, companies and bodies, and publishing houses.

- Work: is every work within the meaning of Article /2/ and Article /3/ of this Law.

- Collective work: is a work in which more than one natural person has contributed at the initiative and under the supervision of a natural or legal person who undertakes to publish it under his own name.

- Audiovisual work: is every work consisting of a series of related images, whether or not accompanied by sound, which give an impression of motion when shown, broadcast or transmitted by special devices.

- Joint work: is every work created by more than one author, provided that the said work does not constitute a collective work.

- Producer of a sound recording or audiovisual work:

is the natural or legal person who takes the initiative and responsibility for making the audiovisual work or the sound recording.

- Author: is the natural person who creates a work.

Reproduction: is the making of one or more copies of any work by any manner or in any form whatsoever, including permanent or temporary recording on phonogram records, tapes, discs, or electronic memory. This also includes the making of a two-dimensional copy of a three-dimensional work or a three-dimensional copy of a two-dimensional work.

- Copy: is that which results from any process of reproduction, recording, printing, or reprographic reproduction of the original work.

- Publication: is the making available to the public of copies of the work or of the sound recording with the consent of the author or the producer of the sound recording and in a quantity sufficient to satisfy the reasonable needs of the public through sale, rental, or any other manner that transfers the ownership or possession of the copy of the work or the sound recording or the right to use them, and the word publication also means making copies of the work or the sound recording available to the public by any electronic means.

* The presentation of a final dramatic, dramatico-musical or cinematographic work, the performance of a musical work, the public recitation of a literary work, the transmission or broadcasting of artistic or literary works, the exhibition of a work of art, or the construction of an architectural work shall not be considered publication.

* The making audible of a sound recording by means of any device or medium, or the broadcasting thereof, shall not be considered publication of the sound recording.

- Communication to the public: is the making available of a work to the public by wire or wireless transmission of sound and image, or of either of them alone, in such a way as to enable the public to hear or view it from places distant from the centre of transmission.

This includes making the work available to the public by wire or wireless means (such as the Internet) in such a way that each member of the public may access that work from a place and at a time individually chosen by them.

This Law protects all productions of the human mind, whether written, pictorial, sculptural, graphical, or oral, whatever their value, importance, and purpose, and whatever the manner or form of their expression.

The following works, mentioned by way of example and not limitation, shall be considered covered by protection:

- Books, archives, pamphlets, publications, printed matter, and all other written literary, artistic, and scientific works.

- Lectures, speeches, and other oral works.

- Audiovisual works and photographs.

- Musical works, whether or not accompanied by words.

- Dramatic works and musical plays.

- Choreographic works and pantomimes.

- Works of drawing, sculpture, engraving, ornamentation, weaving, and lithography.

- Drawings and illustrations relating to architecture.

- Computer programs, whatever their languages, including preparatory works.

- Geographical, topographical, architectural, and scientific maps, designs, plans, and three-dimensional models.

- Works of plastic art of any kind whatsoever, whether or not intended for industry.

All of the following derivative works shall also be subject to the provisions of this Law and benefit from the protection granted thereby, provided that the rights of the author of the original work are not prejudiced:

- Translations, adaptations, transformations, and musical arrangements of works.

- Collections of works and collections of data, whether in machine-readable or any other form, authorised by the copyright holder or his universal or particular successors in title, provided that the selection or arrangement of the content is original.

The protection granted under this Law shall not cover:

- Daily news bulletins.

- Laws, legislative decrees, decrees, and decisions issued by all State authorities and bodies, and official translations thereof.

- Judicial decisions of all kinds and official translations thereof.

- Speeches delivered in public assemblies and meetings, provided that speeches and pleadings relating to a single person may only be collected and published by that person.

- Mere ideas, data, and abstract scientific facts.

- All artistic works of traditional folklore; however, works inspired by folklore shall be covered by protection.

The person who creates a literary or artistic work shall, by the mere fact of its creation, have absolute right of ownership over that work, without any need for him to state that he reserves his rights or to carry out any formal procedures.

In the case of joint works in which it is impossible to separate the share of any of the contributors to the creation of the work from the share of the others, all of them shall be considered joint authors and co-owners of the copyright in the work in equal shares; however, if it is possible to separate the share of each of the joint authors from the share of the others, each of the joint authors shall be considered an independent author of the part pertaining to him.

In the case of joint works, none of the authors may individually exercise the copyright without the consent of his co-authors, unless there is a written agreement to the contrary.

In the case of collective works, the natural or legal person who took the initiative to create the work and supervise its execution shall be considered the holder of the copyright, unless there is a written agreement to the contrary.

In the case of works created by natural persons working for a natural or legal person pursuant to an employment contract in the course of performing their functional or professional obligations, the employer or user shall be deemed the copyright holder and shall exercise the rights provided for in Article /15/ of this Law unless there is a written agreement to the contrary.
In the case of audiovisual works, the producer shall be deemed the copyright holder unless there is a written agreement to the contrary.

The natural or legal person who publishes a work that does not bear the name of an author or that bears a pseudonym of an author shall be deemed the author of the work, and if the true author of the work appears, these rights shall revert to him.

Every person whose name appears on a literary or artistic work in the customary manner for mentioning the author's name on such a work shall be deemed the author of the work unless the contrary is proven.

Literary and artistic works created by the following authors shall benefit from the protection granted pursuant to the provisions of this Law:

- Lebanese authors wherever their place of residence may be.

- Non-Lebanese authors, provided that they hold the nationality of one of the countries party to the Berne Convention for the Protection of Literary and Artistic Works or to the Universal Copyright Convention, or are residents therein.

- Authors who are nationals of any Member State of the League of Arab States that is not party to either of the two Conventions mentioned above, subject to reciprocity.

- Producers of audiovisual works who have their headquarters or a place of residence in Lebanon or in one of the States party to the Berne Convention for the Protection of Literary and Artistic Works or to the Universal Copyright Convention.

Literary and artistic works shall also benefit from protection in the following cases:

- If they are published for the first time in Lebanon.

- If they are published for the first time in one of the States party to either of the two Conventions mentioned in the preceding Article.

- If they are published for the first time outside Lebanon and outside the States party to either of the two mentioned Conventions, provided that they are also published in Lebanon or in a country party to either of the two Conventions mentioned above within thirty days from the date of their publication in the other country.
The copyright holder shall enjoy economic rights and moral rights.

The copyright holder alone shall have the right to exploit the work economically and, to that end, shall have the exclusive right to authorise or prohibit the following:

- Copying, printing, recording and reproducing the work by all available means, including photographic or cinematographic reproduction, or on video tapes

and discs, or on tapes, records and discs of whatever kind, or by any other method.

- Translating the work into another language, or adapting, modifying, altering, summarising or adjusting it, or rearranging a musical work.

- Selling, distributing and renting the work.

Importing copies of the work manufactured abroad.

- Performing the work.

- Communicating the work to the public, whether by wire or wireless means, and whether by means of Hertzian waves or the like or by means of coded or uncoded satellites, and this includes receiving normal television and radio broadcasts or those coming via satellite and retransmitting them to the public by any means that allows the transmission of sound and image.
The economic rights of the author shall be deemed a movable right that may be assigned in whole or in part.

Contracts for the exploitation or disposal of economic rights, whatever their subject matter may be, must be drawn up in writing under pain of nullity between the contracting parties, and must state in detail the rights that are the subject of the contract, and be limited in time and place, and mandatorily provide for the author's participation in a percentage of the revenues from exploitation and sale operations; if such contracts do not include a fixed term, they shall be deemed by operation of law to be concluded for a period of ten years only as from the date of signing the contract.
A comprehensive and prior assignment of future works is null and void.
An assignment by the author of any one of his rights must always be restricted to that right alone, and contracts relating to copyright shall be narrowly construed.
The lyricist and the composer of a vocal musical work shall have equal rights in that work unless otherwise agreed.

In addition to the rights provided for in the preceding Article, and even after the disposal thereof, the author shall have the following moral rights:

- The right to disclose the work and to determine the manner and means of its disclosure.

- The right to claim authorship of the work and to have his name mentioned on every copy of the work each time the work is used publicly.

- The right to use a pseudonym or to remain anonymous.

- To prevent any alteration, development, modification or change in the work that might prejudice his honour, reputation, fame, or artistic, literary and scientific standing.

- To resile from contracts for the assignment or disposal of economic rights even after their publication if such resilement is necessary to preserve his personality and reputation due to a change in his convictions or circumstances, provided that third parties are compensated for the damage resulting from such resilement.

The moral rights of the author may not be disposed of, nor may they be attached, provided however that such rights may be transmitted to third parties by way of testamentary disposition or inheritance laws.

Subject to the provisions of Article /24/ of this Law, any natural person may, for his personal and private use, copy, record or reproduce a single copy of any work protected under this Law without the authorisation or consent of the copyright holder and without paying him any compensation, provided that the work has been lawfully published.

The use of the copied or reproduced copy within a company or at any other workplace shall not be deemed personal and private use.

The exception provided for in the preceding Article shall not apply if it results in prejudice to the other rights and interests of the copyright holder, and in particular it shall not be permissible to do the following:

- Executing an architectural work in the form of a complete or partial building.

- Copying, recording or reproducing any work of which a limited number of original copies has been published.

- Reproducing a complete book or a large part thereof.

- Recording or transmitting compilations of data of all kinds.

- Recording or copying a computer program unless this is done by the person authorised by the copyright holder to use the program and is for the purpose of making a single copy for use only in the event of the loss of or damage to the original copy.

It shall be permissible, without the consent of the author and without paying him any compensation, for non-profit educational and university institutions and public libraries to copy or reproduce a limited number of copies of computer programs, provided that they possess at least one original copy of such programs, for the purpose of placing them at the disposal of school and university students by way of free loan, provided that the mechanism for making copies, the categories of programs that may be copied and the number of permitted copies shall be determined by subsequent implementing decisions issued by the Ministries of National Education, Culture and Higher Education, and Vocational and Technical Education; a student shall also be entitled to copy or reproduce a single copy for his personal use.

It shall be permissible, without the consent of the author and without paying him any compensation, to use a limited part of a lawfully published work for the purpose of criticising the work or for the purpose of supporting a point of view or for the purpose of quotation or for an educational purpose, provided that the size of the part used does not exceed what is necessary and customary in such cases; however, the name of the author and the source must always be indicated if the name of the author is included therein.

It shall be permissible, without the consent of the author and without a payer of any compensation to him, to copy or photograph articles published in newspapers and magazines or short parts of a work, provided that this takes place for a purely educational purpose and within the limits necessary for that educational purpose; the name of the author or authors and the name of the publisher must be mentioned upon every use of the copy or photograph of the article or work if these names are mentioned in the original work.

It shall be permissible, without the consent of the author and without payment of any compensation to him, to copy or photograph an additional copy by non-profit public libraries, provided that they have in their possession at least one original copy, for the purpose of retaining that additional copy to use it only in the event of loss of or damage to the original copy.

It shall be permissible, pursuant to a decision of the Minister of Culture and Higher Education and without the consent of the author or payment of any compensation to him, to copy, photograph or record a copy of an audiovisual work of special artistic value for the purpose of retaining it in the archives of the Ministry, where the holder of the copyright unfairly refuses to permit the recording of that copy.

It shall be permissible, without the consent of the author and without payment of any compensation to him, to copy, photograph or record a copy of a work to be used in judicial or administrative proceedings, within the limits necessary for such proceedings.

It shall be permissible for information media, without the consent of the author and without payment of any compensation to him and within the customary informational limits, to use short excerpts of works that were seen or heard during current events and through the description by the information media of those events, provided that the name of the author and the source are mentioned.

It shall be permissible for information media, without the consent of the author and without payment of any compensation to him, to publish images of architectural works, visual artistic works, photographic works or works of applied art, provided that those works are located in public places open to the public.

It shall be permissible, without the consent of the author and without payment of any compensation to him, to display or perform a work publicly during the following occasions:

- At official ceremonies, within the limits required by such occasions.

- Within the scope of the activities of educational institutions if the work is used by teachers or students, provided that the audience is limited to the teachers, the students, their guardians and the persons participating directly in the activity of the educational institution.

It shall be permissible, without the consent of the author and without payment of any compensation to him, to display the artistic work in museums or in exhibitions organised inside museums, provided that the museum owns the tangible medium containing the work and provided that this does not prejudice the legal interests of the author.

It shall be permissible, without the consent of the author and without payment of any compensation to him, to copy or photograph a copy of an artistic work for the purpose of publishing it in catalogues prepared to facilitate the sale of the work, provided that this does not prejudice the legal interests of the author.

Producers of sound recordings, television and radio broadcasting companies and institutions, publishing houses, and performing artists such as actors, musicians, singers, members of musical choirs, dancers, puppet theatre artists and circus artists shall be considered holders of neighbouring rights.

Protection shall be granted to producers of sound recordings in each of the following cases:

أ - If the producer of the sound recording is Lebanese or holds the nationality of a country that is a member of the International Rome Convention for the Protection of Performers signed in Rome on 26/10/1961 .

ب - If the first fixation of the sound took place in a State that is a member of the above-mentioned Convention.

ج - If the sound recording was first published in a State that is a member of the above-mentioned Convention; if the sound recording was first published in a State not party to the said Rome Convention and was then published in a State that is a member of this Convention within a period of thirty days from the date of the first publication, this sound recording shall be deemed as if it had been first published in the member State.

Protection shall be granted to performing artists in each of the following cases:

أ - Where the performance takes place in Lebanon or in a State party to the above-mentioned Rome Convention.

ب - Where the performance is fixed on a sound recording covered by the protection provided for in Article (36) of this Law.

ج - Where the performance not fixed on a sound recording is fixed through a programme covered by the protection provided for in Article (38) of this Law.

Protection shall be granted to radio and television institutions and companies in each of the following two cases:

أ - If the head office of the institution or company is in Lebanon or in a State party to the above-mentioned Rome Convention.

ب - If the programme is broadcast by means of a transmitter located in Lebanon or in the territory of a State party to the above-mentioned Rome Convention.

Subject to the provisions of Article 15 of this Law, performing artists shall have the right to authorise or prohibit the following:

- The broadcasting of their unfixed performance or its communication to the public, unless the broadcasting or communication constitutes a rebroadcast of a performance the broadcasting of which was previously authorised.

- The fixation or recording of their performance that has not yet been fixed on any tangible medium.

- The copying and sale rental of recordings containing an unauthorised fixation of their performance.
Performing artists participating in a joint work or performance shall elect by relative majority one person to represent them in the exercise of their rights mentioned in Article 39 of this Law.

Producers who have been authorised by the performing artists to carry out the first fixation of the audiovisual work on any tangible medium shall have the exclusive right to copy, distribute, sell and rent the audiovisual work that they have produced and to communicate it to the public.

The radio and television companies, institutions and bodies referred to in Article 38 of this Law shall have the right to authorise or prohibit the following:

- The rebroadcasting of their programmes by any means whatsoever.

- The showing of their television programmes in places to which admission is permitted against payment of an admission fee.

- The recording of their programmes on tangible media if the purpose thereof is commercial.

- The reproduction of unauthorised recordings of their television and radio programmes.

Producers of sound recordings shall enjoy the right to authorise or prohibit the direct or indirect reproduction of these sound recordings of theirs and the right to authorise or prohibit the rental thereof for a commercial purpose.

Performing artists shall have, during their lifetime, the right to claim recognition that the performance be attributed to them and the right to prohibit any distortion or modification thereof, and this right shall pass to the heirs of the performing artist after his death.
Publishers of printed or written graphic works shall have the right to authorise or prohibit the copying thereof by way of photography or commercial exploitation.
Agreements relating to neighbouring rights shall not be effective between the contracting parties unless they are in writing.
The exceptions provided for in Articles /23/ to /34/ of this Law shall apply to the rights provided for in Articles /35/ to /45/ of this Law.

The protection granted to neighbouring rights shall not prejudice any of the rights granted to original or derivative works protected by this Law, and none of the rights granted in this Chapter may be interpreted in a manner that prejudices the rights of the original author.

The economic rights of the author shall enjoy the protection provided for in this Law throughout the lifetime of the author plus fifty years running as of the end of the year in which the death of the author occurred.

With respect to joint works, protection shall continue during the lifetime of the joint authors plus fifty years after the death of the last of the joint authors, running as of the end of the year in which the last death occurred.

If one of the joint authors dies without leaving heirs, the other joint authors or their heirs shall benefit from his share, unless there is an agreement to the contrary.

In the case of collective works and audiovisual works, protection shall last for a period of fifty years from the first authorised public publication of the work, running from the end of the year in which the said publication took place, and in the absence of publication, the period of fifty years shall run from the end of the year in which the completion of the work took place.

The economic rights in works published without mentioning the name of the author or under a pseudonym of an author shall enjoy protection for a period of fifty years running from the end of the year in which the first lawful publication of the work took place.

If the pseudonym adopted by the author leaves no room for doubt as to his identity, or if the name of the author appears before the expiry of fifty years from the end of the year in which the first lawful publication took place, the provisions of Article 49 of this Law shall apply.

As for works published in the name of a legal person and works published after the death of their owner, they shall be protected for a period of fifty years from the end of the year in which they were published.

All moral rights of the author or of the performing artist shall enjoy perpetual protection that does not expire by the lapse of any period thereon, and they shall be transmitted to third parties by way of will or the laws of inheritance.
All economic neighbouring rights belonging to performing artists shall enjoy protection for a period of fifty years running from the end of the year in which the performance took place.
Producers of sound recordings shall enjoy protection for a period of fifty years running from the end of the year in which the fixation on the tangible medium took place for the first time.

Television and radio stations, establishments, companies and bodies shall enjoy protection for a period of fifty years running from the end of the year in which the broadcasting of their programmes took place.
Publishing houses shall enjoy protection for a period of fifty years running from the end of the year in which the publication took place.

Authors and holders of neighbouring rights, or their particular or universal successors in title, may entrust the management of their rights and the collection of the royalties due, in whole or in part, to associations or civil companies formed among themselves.

The mandate shall be effected by virtue of a written power of attorney drawn up before a notary public in which all the rights entrusted to the association or company are expressly stated.

The power of attorney shall be for a limited period, and the mandate may include all the present or future works of the author or holder of neighbouring rights, or only some of them, and in case of doubt, all works shall be deemed included in the power of attorney.

Every association or company intending to undertake the collective management of rights shall, prior to undertaking any activity, deposit with the Ministry of Culture and Higher Education the legal acknowledgment receipt of the declaration of establishment of the association provided for in the Law on Associations, or the certificate of registration of the company in the competent register, in addition to a declaration containing the following information:

- A copy of the internal by-laws of the association or the articles of association of the company.

- The name and address of the responsible director.

- The number of authors and holders of neighbouring rights who have entrusted the association or the company with managing their rights and collecting the royalties belonging to them.

- A copy of the powers of attorney drawn up by the authors or holders of neighbouring rights, or their universal or particular successors in title, in favour of the association or company.

- The duration of the powers of attorney drawn up.

- The manner of distributing the collected sums.

- The annual budget of the association or company.

The work of associations or companies for the collective management of rights shall be subject to the supervision and authority of the Ministry of Culture and Higher Education, and these associations or companies shall place at the disposal of the Ministry all their registers and accounting books necessary for exercising ministerial supervision over them.

Every association or company shall appoint a certified public accountant to audit its registers and submit an annual report to the General Assembly, and the association or company shall obtain every year a report from another certified public accountant.

Every association or company shall hold at least one General Assembly per year at which the report of the president of the association or company, the financial report, the balance sheet of the past year and the budget of the coming year are submitted to a vote.
Every association or company shall appoint a lawyer registered with one of the two Bar Associations as a legal adviser, in accordance with the Law Regulating the Legal Profession.

In the event that one of the associations or companies commits any serious violation, or in the event of repetition of legal or regulatory violations, the Minister of Culture and Higher Education may refer the file to the Public Prosecution to take the appropriate measures.

The manner of establishment and operation of the said associations and companies, the manner in which the Ministry of Culture exercises its supervision over them, and the manner of verifying violations shall be regulated by a decree issued in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Culture and Higher Education within three months from the date of publication of this Law in the Official Gazette.

Associations and companies for the collective management of rights shall have the following powers:

- Drawing up contracts with the parties that use the work and determining the royalty due to be collected.

- Distributing the collected royalties among the right holders.

- Taking all administrative, judicial, arbitral and amicable measures in order to protect the legitimate rights of their principals and collect the royalty due.

- Obtaining from users of works all the information necessary in order to calculate, collect and distribute the collected royalties.
Associations and companies may not, without a serious reason, refuse to draw up the contracts referred to in Article 67 of this Law with the users of the works.

The user of the work shall notify the association or company of a list of the acts of exploitation that he has carried out, such as copying, selling, renting, exhibiting, or television or radio broadcasting, mentioning the number of copies, the number of public performances, or the number of times in which the television or radio broadcasting took place.
Associations or companies may not, without a serious reason, refuse to manage the rights of one of the authors and collect the royalties due to him.

Every association or company shall submit an annual report to the authors who have entrusted it with managing their rights and collecting their royalties so that they may express their opinions regarding the sums collected, the method of collection and distribution, and regarding other matters relating to management. The association shall take these opinions into consideration when formulating or amending the methods of management and collection.
Authors, holders of neighbouring rights and their representatives shall have the right to inspect the accounts of the association or company to which they belong whenever they so wish.

Authors and holders of neighbouring rights who have entrusted one of the associations or companies with managing their rights and collecting royalties shall notify the association or company in writing of the works that they have published and those that they publish after the date of mandating the association or company with management and collection.
The distribution of the collected sums among the right holders shall take place at least once a year, in a manner proportionate to the actual use of their works.

The author, the holder of neighbouring rights, or the association or company may revoke the mandate, provided that there is a serious reason and provided that the matter is notified to the other party three months prior to the end of the year, and the revocation shall take effect from the end of the year in which the desire for revocation is notified to the other party.

The deposit of the work, sound recording, performance, or radio or television programme shall be effected with the Intellectual Property Protection Office at the Ministry of Economy and Trade.

The deposit shall constitute a presumption of the depositor's ownership of the work, sound recording, performance, or radio or television programme, and the rebuttal of this presumption may be proved by all means of proof.

Any holder of copyright or holder of related rights, or their particular or universal successors in title, who wishes to effect the formality of deposit must submit to the Intellectual Property Protection Office an application signed by him or by his agent stating the following information:

- The title and nature of the work, sound recording, performance, or radio or television programme.

- The name, capacity and address of the author or the holder of related rights.

If the author or the holder of related rights does not effect the deposit in person, the foregoing information must also be stated in respect of the person making the deposit.

- The nature of the instrument upon which the depositor relies to submit the application for deposit, where the depositor is a person other than the author or the holder of related rights.

- Where applicable, the name and address of the person charged with the material execution of the work (the printer, the caster, etc.) shall be stated, and the application for deposit must be accompanied by:

(a) A copy or an abstract of the instrument pursuant to which the deposit is effected, where the applicant is not the author himself or the holder of the related right himself (the power of attorney, the assignment of right, the contract for work, the agreement...).

(b) Three copies of the work or the subject matter of the related right. However, with respect to photographs, oil paintings, watercolours, statues, architecture and works of which only a single original exists, the copies mentioned above shall be replaced by a photographic or non-photographic reproduction of that work in three dimensions giving the form and appearance of the work as a whole and in detail.

In cases where an imminent infringement of copyright or related rights is feared, the holder of such rights or his universal or particular successors in title, and in particular collective rights management associations or companies, may take all necessary conservatory measures to prevent the occurrence of the infringement of those rights.

To that end, the Judge of Urgent Matters may take all decisions permitted by law, and in particular orders on petitions, for the protection of the right or work targeted by the infringement and of all other works owned by the author or the holder of the related right, and the Judge of Urgent Matters may impose coercive fines in enforcement of his decisions. The competent President of the Court of First Instance or the competent Public Prosecution shall also be entitled to take the conservatory measures referred to above.

The Judge of Urgent Matters, the President of the Court of First Instance or the Public Prosecutor may provisionally seize the materials that constitute evidence of the infringement committed against copyright or related rights, or may order that an inventory be made of such materials and leave them in the custody of the defendant.

Upon the occurrence of any infringement of copyright or related rights, the holders of such rights may apply to the competent courts to obtain a decision ordering the cessation of the infringement and preventing its occurrence in the future.

Every person who infringes any copyright or related right shall pay fair compensation for the material and moral damages sustained by the right holder, to be assessed by the courts on the basis of the commercial value of the work, the damage sustained by the right holder, his loss of profit and the material profit realised by the infringer, and the court may order the seizure of the articles that are the subject of the action and the machinery and implements used in the infringement.

Whether or not the matter relates to works that have fallen into the public domain, there shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to three years and by a pecuniary penalty from five million to fifty million Lebanese pounds, or by either of these two penalties, every person who:

- Fraudulently places, or causes another person to place, a usurped name on a literary or artistic work.

- Fraudulently imitates, with intent to deceive the purchaser, the signature of the author or the sign used by him.

- Knowingly counterfeits a literary or artistic work.

- Knowingly sells, has on deposit with him, offers for sale, or puts into circulation a counterfeited work or a work signed under an assumed name.

The penalty shall be doubled in the event of recidivism.

Every person who, knowingly and for the purpose of profit, infringes or attempts to infringe any of the copyrights or related rights provided for in this Law shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to three years and by a fine from five million to fifty million Lebanese pounds, or by either of these two penalties, and the penalty shall be doubled in the event of recidivism.

The competent court may also order the closure of the premises, commercial establishment, or television or radio station that commits a violation of copyright for a period ranging between one week and one month, and the destruction of all copies of the works made without the authorisation of the right holder and of all equipment and machinery used to manufacture them, and the court may also order the publication of its judgment in two local newspapers at the expense of the defendant.

In the application of this Article, the provisions of Articles 200 et seq. of the Penal Code shall be observed.

Every person who was a Turkish subject residing in the territory of Greater Lebanon on 30 August 1924 is confirmed by operation of law in Lebanese nationality and shall henceforth be deemed to have lost Turkish nationality.

All persons over eighteen years of age who have lost Turkish nationality or acquired by operation of law Lebanese nationality pursuant to the preceding Article shall have the right, within two years commencing on 30 August 1924, to opt for Turkish nationality.

Persons over eighteen years of age who have lost Turkish nationality pursuant to Article 1 and who differ in race from the majority of the population of Greater Lebanon may, within a period of two years commencing on 30 August 1924, opt for the nationality of one of the States to which territory detached from Turkey was transferred under the Treaty of Peace concluded on 24 July 1923, if the majority of the population in that State is of the same race as the person entitled to exercise this option. If that State grants its nationality to the person who exercised the said right of option, his option therefor shall result in the loss of his Lebanese nationality.

Persons who have exercised, in accordance with the provisions of Articles 2 and 3 of this Decision, the right to opt for a nationality other than Syrian nationality must, within the following twelve months, transfer their place of residence to the territory of the State for whose nationality they have opted. However, persons required under the provisions of the preceding paragraph to transfer their place of residence outside the territory of Greater Lebanon shall be entitled to retain their immovable property situated therein, and may take with them their movable property of any kind whatsoever, without any export duty or any minimal other fee being imposed upon them on that account.

Turkish subjects over eighteen years of age who originate from the territory of Greater Lebanon and who on 30 August 1924 were residing outside the said territory or outside the territory of Turkey shall have the right to opt for Syrian nationality if they are of the same race as the majority of the population of Greater Lebanon. This right of option must be exercised within a period of two years commencing on 30 August 1924 before the diplomatic and consular representatives of the Mandatory Government. In territories under French sovereignty, it shall be exercised before the administrative authorities designated for that purpose by the French Government. This option shall result in the acquisition of Lebanese nationality if the said Mandatory Government consents thereto.

In all matters relating to the application of the provisions of this Decision, married women shall follow the status of their husbands, and children under eighteen years of age shall follow the status of their fathers.

The Secretary-General and the Governor of Greater Lebanon shall execute this Decision, each within the scope of his competence.

Annex: Letter of the High Commissioner relating to the interpretation of Decision No. 2825 concerning Lebanese Nationality

From General Weygand, Member of the Supreme War Council and High

Commissioner of the French Republic in Syria and Lebanon.

To General Vandenberg, Governor of Greater Lebanon, through the Assistant Delegate

to the Government of Greater Lebanon - Beirut

I have the honour to draw your attention to Decision 2825 concerning Lebanese nationality, signed on 30 August last, as that date marks the beginning of the legal establishment of this nationality.

Consequently, it has become necessary, starting from the said 30 August, to distinguish between holders of Ottoman nationality residing in Lebanese territory, who become Lebanese subject to the conditions set forth in Article 2, and persons passing through Lebanon who originate from one of the countries that formed part of the Ottoman Empire; the latter shall be deemed foreigners, unlike Syrians who have established their place of residence in Lebanon, who have the right to retain their Syrian nationality without any need to transfer their place of residence outside the State of Greater Lebanon thereafter. This measure shall be reciprocal, as the State of Syria must accept Lebanese persons under the same conditions, the purpose of this measure being to enable holders of Syrian and Lebanese nationality to continue residing in the territory of either of these two States without distinction.

As for Armenian emigrants from Turkey residing in Lebanese territory, they are subject to no exception; they are therefore deemed to be Ottomans who established their place of residence in the territory of Lebanon on 30 August 1924, and they may become Lebanese if, within two years, they do not opt for the nationality of one of the States to which territories detached from Turkey were transferred and do not transfer their place of residence thereto within the twelve months following their option therefor. As for the conditions for the acquisition or loss of Lebanese nationality

and Syrian nationality within the mandated territory, they shall be determined by a Decision to be issued hereafter.

Aley, 19 September 1924

Signed: Weygand
Starting from the first of January of the year 1925, the registration of civil status documents shall become compulsory in all the territories of Greater Lebanon.

The persons required pursuant to the law, to draw up civil status documents are:

- Fathers, testamentary guardians and physicians (midwives)

- for births

- Spouses, or their fathers if they are minors, or legal guardians if the spouses are minors and orphans- for the change of their places of residence.

There must be stated in civil status documents the year, month, day and hour in which the events for which those documents are drawn up took place, and there must be entered the names of all the persons mentioned therein, their surnames (family names), their ages, their occupations and their places of residence. It shall not be permissible at all to make any erasure therein, nor to write any addendum in the margin, nor terse or abbreviated expressions, nor Indian numerals.

The drawers of the documents must sign them in the presence of two witnesses, and the mukhtars must sign them as well.

The age of the witness in a document pertaining to civil status must be eighteen full years.

The testimony of persons sentenced to deprivation of civil rights and the right to give testimony before the judiciary shall not be accepted.

Likewise, a man and his wife may not be witnesses together in a single document.

The persons who have the right to register documents pertaining to civil status and to issue copies thereof or copies of the civil status registers are the head of the Central Registry in Beirut or whomever he delegates, and the civil status officers in the administratively autonomous cities and in the districts.

However, they may not add anything to what has been entered in the documents that they receive.

Civil status officers shall collect, in addition to the stamp duty, and five Lebanese-Syrian piastres for each copy they issue of every document pertaining to a birth, death, change of place of residence, divorce, desertion or marriage.

Whoever is entrusted with the civil status registers shall be civilly liable for any alteration that occurs therein. Where necessary, he shall retain the right to institute an action against the perpetrators of that alteration.

Every alteration or forgery in civil status documents and every registration thereof written on a loose sheet or anything other than the registers prepared for this purpose shall oblige its perpetrator to pay compensation for damages to the injured party, in addition to the penalties provided for in the Penal Code.

The declaration of the occurrence of a birth must be made before the civil status officer within the fifteen days following the birth; as for the birth document, it must be drawn up and signed by the father (in the first degree) or the testamentary guardian or the physician or the midwife before two witnesses, and then signed by the mukhtar.

The perpetrator of the contravention (whether the father, the testamentary guardian, the physician or the midwife who attended the birth) who neglects to submit the birth document within the legal time limit shall be fined a pecuniary penalty of 200 Lebanese-Syrian piastres, and if the contravention is repeated by him, the provisions of the eighth article of the Penal Code shall be applied to him.

If the offender refuses to pay the amount of the pecuniary penalty, this penalty shall be converted into imprisonment, and if the fifteen-day time limit provided for above expires, the civil status officer may not, after its expiration, accept a declaration of any birth.

The birth cannot then be registered except pursuant to a judicial decision requested to be issued by the Public Prosecution after summoning the concerned parties in the legal manner.

There must be stated in the birth document the year, month, day and hour in which the birth took place, the sex of the newborn (whether he is a boy or a girl) and the given name by which he is named, together with the names of the father, the mother and the two witnesses, their surnames, their occupations, their ages and their places of residence.

If twins are born, a birth document must be written for each of them, and there must be stated the hour in which each one of them was born, which child of the two was born before the other and the distinguishing marks on their bodies, and the one born before the other shall be deemed the firstborn child, and there is no need to register children who are stillborn.

If an illegitimate child is born, the name of his father shall not be stated unless he acknowledges him or authorises a special proxy to represent him in acknowledging him.

If this acknowledgment is not effected, the child's name shall be registered in the register as a child whose father is unknown.

As for the mother of the child, the person who draws up his birth document may not disclose her name.

Likewise, the civil status officer may not state her name except on the basis of a declaration by her that she is the mother of the child or on the basis of a judgment from the Court of First Instance.

Paragraph added pursuant to Law 541 dated 24/7/96, Official Gazette 33 dated 29/7/96

"The civil registration and civil status departments that draw up identity cards and individual civil registry extracts may not state in these cards or extracts any phrase indicating that the person to whom the identity card or registry extract pertains is an illegitimate child or that he is of unknown mother and father", provided that the administration concerned may give certificates or statements to this effect to the person concerned or the competent judicial authority only and for legitimate reasons.

Every person who finds a newborn child must hand him over to the mukhtar of the village or quarter together with whatever clothes and other articles he finds on the child, and must state the circumstances of place and time in which he found him, and the mukhtar must thereupon draw up a record in two copies stating therein the apparent age of the child, his sex and the name by which the civil authority to which he is handed over names him, and this record shall take the place of the birth document and must be transcribed in full into the civil status registers, and then one copy thereof shall be sent to the civil status officer to effect the registration and the second copy shall be sent with the child to the civil authority to hand it over to the Public Assistance Administration with the child.
The registration of children who are born in hospitals or in prisons shall be effected in accordance with the written declarations submitted by their directors or their physicians in this regard.

A child who is born in a place other than the place in which the actual place of residence of his father is located, or of his mother in the absence of the father - his registration shall be effected in the place in which the actual place of residence of his parents is located, and a birth document shall be written for him pursuant to the provisions of Articles 14 and 16 and handed over to the civil status registry in the village or quarter to be sent to the civil status officer in the locality in which the original place of the parents is located.

As for the children of Lebanese residing temporarily in the territories of the Syrian Federation, their fathers or their testamentary guardians shall draw up, through the civil status officer in the place of birth, their birth documents and then send to the Government of Greater Lebanon copies thereof containing mention of the original place of the parents.

If a child is born to spouses of Lebanese nationality in a foreign country, the proof of his birth shall be made at the nearest French consulate to their place of residence upon a request by them, and then the consul shall send a copy of the birth document and copies of the identity cards of the parents (civil registration cards) to the Government of Greater Lebanon for the registration of the newborn in the registers of the original place of the parents.

If a child is born during a sea voyage, the parents must draw up for him, through the civil status officer on the vessel, a birth document containing the particulars provided for in Article 16, and its drawing up must be in the presence of two witnesses, and if the parents are travelling to Lebanese territory, they must hand over a copy of that document to the civil status registry in their original place (in Greater Lebanon).

If, however, they are bound for a foreign country, they must hand over the said copy together with copies of their identity cards to the French consulate located in the nearest place to their residence to be sent to the Government of Greater Lebanon.

If a child is born in a village in which there is no civil status officer, the document pertaining to his birth shall be submitted to the mudir of the nahiya, or to the mukhtar in the absence of the mudir, so that he may send it without delay to the civil status registry.

Every application relating to a change of religion shall be submitted to the Administrative Governor, the Mutasarrif, or the Qaimaqam, who shall invite the two spiritual heads (that is, the head of the religion sought to be embraced and the head of the religion sought to be renounced, such as the Bishop, the Rabbi, the Judge of the denomination, or the Mufti) to hold a meeting attended by the applicant, and permission shall then be granted to his spiritual head to confer privately and deliberate with him. If he (that is, the applicant) persists in his desire to embrace the religion to which he is inclined, a record of proceedings shall be drawn up at the same sitting in two copies and signed by each of the two spiritual heads and the applicant, and it shall then be signed by the Administrative Governor, the Mutasarrif, or the Qaimaqam. A copy thereof, together with the identity card of the applicant, shall be sent to the Personal Status Registry located in his place of residence in order to rectify his entry in the census registers and on the identity card, and the personal status officer shall also send an abstract of the record of proceedings of that transaction to the Mukhtar of the village and to the Central Personal Status Registry in order to rectify the entry therein.

Applications relating to the rectification of an entry following a change of place of residence, trade, religion, or denomination shall be accepted by the Personal Status Registries at all times, and the necessary transaction in respect thereof shall be carried out.

Applications relating to the rectification of an entry following a change of place of residence, form, religion, or denomination shall be accepted by the Personal Status Registries at all times, and the necessary transaction in respect thereof shall be carried out.

Personal status officers must carry out the transactions pertaining to the registration of personal status documents within the eight days following their receipt thereof. Abstracts of those transactions must be sent without delay to the Mukhtars concerned and to the Central Registry in order to make the entries and enter the necessary annotations in the following manners:

(a) In entries of births
