Personal status officers must, following the registration of the birth document in the register of births, state in the "Remarks" column of the said register opposite the name of the newborn the form of the census register in which the name of his father is registered and the serial number assigned to the name of the father in this register, and he must also state in the "Remarks" column of the census register and opposite the name of the father the serial number pertaining to the newborn in the register of births.

(b) In entries of marriage and divorce

Personal status officers must state in the "Remarks" column of the register of marriage (or divorce) opposite the names of the married (or divorced or separated) persons the forms and numbers of the census registers in which the names of the spouses were registered prior to their marriage (or their divorce), and he must also state in the "Remarks" column opposite their names in the said census registers a statement of their marriage (or their divorce) and state therewith the numbers of their entries in the register of marriage (or divorce).

(c) In entries of deaths

The personal status officer must state in the "Remarks" column of the register of deaths opposite the name of the deceased person the form and number of the census register in which he was registered (and if the deceased was a newborn, he shall state the number of his entry in the register of births). He must also state in the "Remarks" column of the census register (or register of births) opposite the name of the deceased a statement of his death together with the number of his entry in the register of deaths.

(d) In change of place of residence

The personal status officer must state in the "Remarks" column of the register pertaining to the change of place of residence opposite the name of the person relocating, the form and number of the census register in which he is registered. He must also state in the "Remarks" column of the census register opposite the name of the aforementioned person a statement of the transfer of his place of residence together with the number of his entry in the register pertaining to the change of place of residence, and it shall not suffice in that event to send an abstract of those transactions to the Central Personal Status Registry and to the Mukhtar of the locality to which the person relocated, rather an abstract thereof must also be sent to the Mukhtar and the personal status officer located in the original place of the relocating person in order to rectify the entry in the census registers.

The Head of the Central Census and Personal Status Registry in the central government administration, the Deputy to this Head, and all other personal status officers in the administratively autonomous cities and in the districts, must submit to the Directorate of the Interior within one month from the date of publication of this Decision a financial guarantee in the amount of 150 Lebanese-Syrian pounds (for each of them) and submit therewith proof that they have taken the oath before the Court of First Instance or before the Peace Court. Every officer among them upon whom the said time limit expires without acting in accordance with the provisions of this Article shall ipso facto be deemed to have resigned.

Personal status officers (in the outlying districts) shall draw up every three months a summary statement of all the entries which they have made during the said period and send it to the Central Census and Personal Status Registry on the following dates:

10 January, 10 April, 10 July, and 10 October of each year.

Any negligence in this regard shall subject its perpetrator to summary punishment, and the aforementioned Central Registry shall draw up for the entire State of Greater Lebanon a general schedule based on those statements and then submit it to the Directorate of the Interior in the latter half of each month of the (four) months mencionado above.
All previous provisions contrary to the provisions of this Decision are repealed.
The Secretary-General and the Directors of the Interior and of Justice shall enforce this Decision, each within the scope of his competence.

The married person, or his father (if the married person is a minor), or his guardian if he is a minor and an orphan, shall submit the declarations relating to the marriage to the Civil Status Office within the fifteen days following the date of the marriage, and the married person shall also send to the civil status officer a written declaration regarding his marriage certified by the spiritual head at whose hand the marriage contract was solemnised and signed by the mukhtar in the presence of two witnesses.

The following paragraph was added pursuant to the Law dated 13/5/29

If the husband refrains from giving the declarations, the Census and Civil Status Office may content itself with a written declaration from the spiritual head with whose knowledge the contract took place for the purpose of effecting the registration only, while reserving the right of the injured party to have recourse to the courts.

The marriage certificate shall contain the following:

(1) The name of each of the spouses, his surname, hisoccupation, his religious denomination, his date of birth, the place in which he was born, and his place of residence

(2) The name of each of the father and the mother, his surname, his occupation, and his place of residence

(3) The name of each of the two witnesses, his surname, his age, his occupation, and his place of residence

(4) The date of the marriage (the year, the month, the day, and the hour).

The person obliged pursuant to Article 25 to draw up the certificate relating to the marriage, if he delays in delivering it within the legal time limit to the civil status officer, shall be fined a pecuniary penalty of 200 Lebanese-Syrian piastres, and if this contravention is repeated by him, the provisions of the Eighth Article of the Penal Code shall apply to him. And if he refuses to pay the pecuniary penalty, this penalty shall be converted into imprisonment.

If the marriage is contracted in a locality other than the locality in which the place of residence of the married man is situated, it shall then be incumbent upon the civil status officer in the locality in which the place of residence of the man is situated.

If the marriage is contracted in a foreign country, the husband shall send to the nearest French consulate to his place of residence a marriage certificate drawn up in accordance with the provisions of Article 26 together with a copy of his identity card and a copy of the identity card of his wife. And after the consul certifies the certificate and the two copies, he shall send them to the Government of Greater Lebanon.

The husband shall, upon divorce or desertion, draw up a certificate pursuant to the provisions of Article 26 and in the presence of two witnesses, a delegate on the part of the Sharia judge (if he is of the Muslims), then send it to the civil status officer within the legal time limit, failing which he shall be punished pursuant to Article 27. As for the non-Muslim communities, the husband from among their members shall send with the certificate a copy of the decision issued by the religious authority in this regard, and the mukhtar shall also sign the decision of divorce or desertion.

In the two cases of marriage and divorce (or desertion), the civil status officer who registers the certificate of marriage or divorce or desertion shall send a copy thereof to the Civil Status Office and in the original place of the married woman or the divorced woman (or the deserted woman).

The mukhtars shall draw up the certificates of death in the presence of two witnesses and then send them to the Civil Status Offices within fifteen days commencing from the date of the death. The two witnesses shall be, where possible, from among the nearest relatives or from among the neighbours. And if someone dies outside his place of residence, the person at whose premises the death occurred and a person from among the relatives of the deceased, or another person in the absence of such relative, shall bear witness.

The certificate of death which the mukhtar draws up in the presence of two witnesses shall contain the following:

(1) The name of the deceased, his surname, his age, his occupation, and his place of residence.

(2) If the deceased person is a married man or a widower, the name of his wife and her surname shall be mentioned, and if she is a married woman or a widow, the name of her husband and his surname shall be mentioned.

(3) The names of the two witnesses and the surname of each of them, his age, his occupation, and his place of residence, and if they are from among the relatives of the deceased, the degree of kinship shall be mentioned.

(4) The date of the death (the year, the month, the day, and the hour).

The mukhtar who neglects to submit the certificate of death within the legal time limit shall be fined a pecuniary penalty of 200 Lebanon-Syrian piastres. And if he returns to committing this contravention, the pecuniary penalty shall be doubled.

And if the contravention is repeated by him again, he shall be dismissed and referred to the court.

If the death occurs in a place other than the original place in which the registration of the deceased took place, the mukhtar shall deliver the certificate of death to the local Civil Status Office in order that it may send it without delay to the office of the original place in which the registration of the deceased took place, and this office shall notify the occurrence thereof to the mukhtar of the original place.

If the death occurs in a hospital or a prison, the director of the hospital or the prison shall notify within 24 hours the news of the death to the mukhtar of the locality. And this mukhtar shall go to the place in which the death occurred in order to ascertain it and draw up a certificate therefor, then send it together with the identity card of the deceased to the civil status officer in the locality.

If a sentence of death is executed upon a person, the Public Prosecutor or his deputy shall draw up a record of the death and then send it within 24 hours to the Civil Status Office situated in the locality in which the execution took place, and in all cases in which an unnatural death or a death in prison or an execution occurs, nothing concerning those circumstances may be entered in the civil status register, but rather it shall be confined to drawing up the certificate of death in the ordinary manner.

If a death occurs during a voyage by sea, the captain of the vessel shall draw up a certificate in the presence of two witnesses and send it together with all the papers relating to the identity of the deceased to the French authority present in the first port at which the vessel arrives, and the said authority shall send it together with the identity papers to the Government of Greater Lebanon.

If a death occurs in a foreign country, the family of the deceased shall draw up a certificate and send it together with the identity card of the deceased to the nearest French consulate to their place of residence, and it - that is, the consulate - shall send the said certificate and card to the Government of Greater Lebanon.

Every person whose name is registered in the census registers, if he wishes to transfer his place to a locality other than the locality in which his name was registered with the intention of permanent domicile therein, shall submit a declaration in this regard to the Civil Status Office present in the locality in which he will take up his new residence.

And the submission of this declaration shall be within six months commencing from the date of his arrival therein, and it may be sent directly or through the intermediary of the mukhtar. And every person who does not carry out the formalities relating to the transfer of the place of residence within the said time limit shall be fined by paying a pecuniary penalty of 200 Syrian-Lebanese piastres, and if he refuses to pay, the pecuniary penalty shall be converted into imprisonment.

Nothing shall be paid for certificates of deaths.

As for certificates of birth, divorce, and desertion, and the change of place of residence, a fee of ten Syrian-Lebanese piastres shall be paid to the mukhtar or to the sheikh for drawing up each certificate thereof. And this fee shall be increased to twenty Syrian-Lebanese piastres for a marriage certificate.

The stamps relating to civil status certificates and the registers of these certificates shall be deposited with the mukhtars of the villages, where the persons entrusted pursuant to the law with drawing up the certificates of birth, marriage, divorce, and change of place of residence may obtain, when necessary, what they require of those stamps and registers.

The amounts of the fines provided for in Articles 15, 27, 30, 34 40 of this Decision shall be collected by the Director of Finance on the basis of records drawn up by the civil status officers, and their collection shall be against legal receipts.

The civil status officers in the administratively independent cities and in the districts (cazas) shall have the right to issue identity cards in the names of the newborns signed with their signatures and sealed with the official seal in the manner provided for in the Fifteenth Article of Decision No. 763 dated 10 March of the year 1921

There shall be deemed Lebanese:

(1) Every person born of a Lebanese father.

(2) Every person born in the territory of Greater Lebanon who has not been proved to have acquired by filiation at birth a foreign nationality.

(3) Every person born in the territory of Greater Lebanon of unknown parents or parents of unknown nationality.

An illegitimate child whose filiation is established while a minor shall acquire Lebanese nationality if that one of his parents in respect of whom filiation is first established is Lebanese. Where the proof establishing filiation in respect of both the father and the mother results from a single deed or a single judgment, the child shall acquire the nationality of the father if such father is Lebanese.

A woman married to a foreigner who has acquired Lebanese nationality, and the adult children of a foreigner who has acquired the said nationality, may, upon their application, obtain Lebanese nationality without the requirement of residence, whether by the decision granting such nationality to the husband or to the father or to the mother, or by a special decision.

Likewise, the minor children of a father who has acquired Lebanese nationality or of a mother who has acquired such nationality and survived the death of the father shall become Lebanese, unless within the year following their attainment of majority they decline such nationality.
A foreign woman who marries a Lebanese shall become Lebanese upon the expiration of one year from the date of registration of the marriage at the Civil Status Registry, upon her application.

A Lebanese woman who marries a foreigner shall remain Lebanese until she applies for the striking off of her registration from the census registers by reason of her acquisition of the nationality of her husband.

A woman who has lost her Lebanese nationality following her marriage to a foreigner may recover such nationality after the dissolution of the marriage, upon her application.

Lebanese women who married before the census of the year 1932 and lost their nationality by marriage and had no registration in the registers of that census may, after the dissolution of the marriage, obtain a judicial decision for their registration if their presence on Lebanese territory on 30 August 1924 is established; as for those among them who were outside Lebanese territory on the said date, they may recover their Lebanese nationality pursuant to Article 2 of the Law of 31 January 1946 (1).

There shall lose the status of Lebanese:

(1) A Lebanese who has acquired a foreign nationality, where such acquisition has been previously authorised by a decision of the Head of State.

(2) A Lebanese who accepts a public office conferred upon him by a foreign Government and retains it notwithstanding the issuance of orders to him by the Lebanese Government to relinquish it within a specified period.
The hearing of actions relating to nationality shall appertain exclusively to the civil courts.

Subject to the rights of option provided for in the Treaty of Peace signed at Lausanne on 24 July 1923, every person born in the territory of Greater Lebanon of a father who was also born therein and who on November 1914 possessed Ottoman nationality shall be deemed Lebanese.

Children and married women who shall have acquired a foreign nationality pursuant to Article 36 of the Treaty of Peace concluded at Lausanne may acquire Lebanese nationality by a decision of the Head of State after investigation and provided that they are resident in the territory of Lebanon, by submitting a declaration to that effect within the year following the attainment of majority or the dissolution of the marriage.
All provisions contrary to the provisions of this Decision are hereby repealed.

The Secretary-General and the Governor of Greater Lebanon shall execute, each in so far as concerns him, this Decision, which shall enter into force from the date of its publication in the Official Bulletin of the Acts of the High Commission.

The State or the municipalities may authorise upon their public property, on a temporary and revocable basis and in return for a certain fee, the occupation of a parcel of public property by way of a personal and exclusive occupation, particularly where the matter relates to an undertaking.

The undertaking shall be deemed a concession where it is established as a public utility.

A permit for temporary occupation, however, shall not be for a public utility.

A concession or a permit for temporary occupation upon public property shall be granted subject to the preservation of the rights of third parties.
Concessions shall be granted in accordance with the provisions of Decision No. 2511 issued on 20 March 1924.

- Permits for temporary occupation upon public property belonging to the State shall be granted pursuant to a decision of the Head of State in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter.

- Permits for temporary occupation upon public property belonging to the municipalities shall be granted in accordance with the laws and regulations relating to municipalities.

Permits for temporary occupation shall be granted for a period of one year and may be renewed by tacit consent. The decisions pursuant to which the permits are granted shall specify the fees payable by reason of the temporary occupation; account shall be taken in such fees of the area and the location, and they may by way of exception be substantially reduced and even made a nominal fee of five Syrian piastres,

where the purpose of the temporary occupation may be deemed to be of public benefit.

Fees shall be paid in advance. The holder of the permit shall not be entitled to waive it prior to the expiry of the year that has commenced.

Permits for temporary occupation may be revoked without compensation upon the first request of the Administration, provided that the holder of the permit shall be entitled to claim a portion or the whole of the fees which he has paid. The withdrawal of the permit shall be effected by a decision of the Head of State.

There shall be determined where necessary, by decisions of the Head of State in respect of permits for occupation upon terrestrial, fluvial or maritime public property that are of the same kind, the special conditions whereby such permits may be granted, whether upon the property of the State in certain specified zones or places.

General decisions relating to permits for occupation upon public lands may be revised every five years, in whole or in part, upon the proposal of one of the competent departments.

Such revision may not be invoked against the holders of permits unless it has been notified to them at least three months prior to the expiry of the current five-year period.

Save in the cases mentioned in Article Three, there shall be drawn up prior to the first of January 1927, through the offices of the Department of Public Works, a schedule of all permits granted upon terrestrial or fluvial public property, whether for a consideration or gratuitously, and of all occupied properties for which no authorisation has been issued and which are capable of being recovered; the same procedure shall be carried out through the offices of the Inspector of the Merchant Marine in respect of maritime public property.

These schedules shall be transmitted to the Department of Finance, which shall undertake the review of the permits or the fixing of the fees, whereupon notice shall be given to the holders of the permits

of the obligation to sign an undertaking to pay the new fees, which shall take effect from the first of March 1927; and if the said undertaking is not signed, the permit for occupation shall be withdrawn.

Unauthorised occupations of public property must be regularised in the manner set forth in this Decision; and if the person occupying the premises refuses to submit to the conditions determined by the competent departments, he shall be served notice to vacate the portion of public property occupied without right and to restore it to its former state within a period fixed by the Head of State.

If the occupant of the property fails to comply with the conditions required of him, the Head of State shall order the enforcement of such conditions directly and forthwith by administrative process.
The rules relating to the policing, conservation and use of public property shall be laid down by general regulations enacted by the Head of State in the Council of Directors.

A - In the absence of decrees determining, where necessary, according to the nature of the various contraventions, the officers vested with competence to draw up official reports of offences, contraventions of the regulations relating to the regime of the public domain of the State and to its conservation and use shall be recorded by official reports drawn up, in addition to members of the Internal Security Forces, by the officials appointed for that purpose in each of the Ministries of Public Works and Transport, the Interior, Agriculture and Finance.

B - Such contraventions shall be punishable by an administrative fine the amount of which shall be fixed by decree in respect of each category of public property.

The same decree shall designate the administrative authority charged with imposing the fine. In the event of recidivism, offenders shall be liable, in addition to the administrative fine, to a penalty of imprisonment for a term of not less than 10 days and not more than three months.

This penalty of imprisonment shall be pronounced by the criminal courts. Subsequent decrees may, according to the nature of the contraventions, increase the minimum and reduce the maximum of the penalty of imprisonment provided for in the preceding paragraph.

Administrative and judicial penalties shall be imposed without prejudice to the right of the Administration to claim compensation for damage and to demolish works unlawfully erected upon public property or easement zones, ex officio and without need for any formality.

C - The offender shall be entitled, within a time-limit of 15 days from the date of notification to him of the administrative decision imposing the fine, to lodge an objection against such decision before the court of the district in which the contravention was committed. The objection shall not be admissible unless the objector annexes to his objection a receipt proving that he has paid the fine due. Such objection shall be notified within the time-limit set forth above to the administrative authority which imposed the fine that is the subject of the objection. The administrative decision shall become final if the objection is not lodged in due form. The fine shall be doubled by operation of law in the event that it is upheld by the court, and the fine paid shall be refunded in the event of acquittal.

D - The penalties provided for in the decrees implementing this Law shall be imposed without distinction upon the perpetrator, the employer of the perpetrator, the person for whose account the employer acts, the workmen who participated in the acts constituting the contravention, and the persons who are in charge of the means of transport connected with the contravention or who place others in charge thereof. Where the identity of the employer, the person for whose account the employer acts, the person placed in charge of the means of transport connected with the contravention, or the person who placed him in charge thereof is disclosed in the statement of the offenders recorded in the official report, the said official report shall be referred to the Public Prosecution for completion of the investigation. Materials, equipment, animals and machinery of every kind used by the offender to commit the contravention shall be seized, and may be confiscated by decision of the court for the benefit of the Treasury, either upon the request of the administrative authority charged with imposing the fine or upon the request of the Public Prosecution. The seized items confiscated shall be mentioned in the official report of the offence. The legislative provisions relating to the recording and repression of contraventions contained in this Law may be amended by decrees enacted in the Council of Ministers.

(As amended by Decision 11 dated 13 January 1940):

Where it appears possible to cancel the registration of certain portions of national public property, such cancellation may be effected by a decision of the Head of Government.

The cancellation of the registration of portions of municipal public property shall be effected in accordance with the laws, decrees or decisions governing municipalities.

Portions of national or municipal public property whose registration has been cancelled shall pass into the private property of the State or the municipalities and must be registered in the Land Register in accordance with Chapter Four of Decision 189 issued on 15 March 1926, as amended by Decision No. 46 LR issued on 20 April 1932.
All provisions contrary to the provisions of this Decision are repealed.
The Secretary-General is charged with the execution of this Decision.

The Property Register in each cadastral area shall consist of the aggregate of the real folios pertaining to the immovable properties of the area. These folios shall be collected in the form of a register, and shall be bound therein in a fixed or loose-leaf manner. Each cadastral area shall have one or more registers.

Registers with fixed or loose-leaf folios shall be made according to the model designated by the Administration.

The loose-leaf ones thereof shall have a device ensuring their protection. Where a real folio entered in a loose-leaf register is cancelled, whether its cancellation arises from the striking off of an immovable property by its inclusion in the public domain or from the amalgamation of immovable properties with one another, or from the creation of different rights over storeys or parts of storeys of a building, or from the merger of such rights or from their amalgamation, or from the drawing up of a new folio in which entry is restricted, in compliance with the request of the owner, to mentioning the real rights and real charges encumbering the immovable property, the Registrar shall proceed to close the cancelled folio and withdraw it from the loose-leaf collection in order to annex it to the file of the immovable property. The said file shall be kept in the depository of the cadastral area in which the immovable property is situated. The aforementioned provisions shall also apply to supplementary folios established in accordance with the conditions specified in Article 23 below, when the rights to which such folios are allocated are extinguished, merged or amalgamated. When the cadastral survey map becomes unfit for use, following successive additions supervening thereon, a new map shall be drawn up conforming to the status of the immovable properties according to the entries of the Property Register on the day it is drawn up. The old map shall be kept, after being duly closed, in the depositories of the Cadastral Survey Department.

These provisions shall also apply to new maps that are drawn up to a scale different from the scale of the old maps as a result of the subdivision of immovable properties. In such case, the area of the subdivided immovable properties shall be remeasured and recorded in the Property Register and in the copies of the land folios whenever the holders thereof present them.

The new area may not differ from the old one beyond the tolerated margins specified in the Eighth Article of Decision 188, and the cadastral survey contractor shall certify the accuracy of the new maps drawn up in accordance with the provisions of this paragraph.

The immovable properties of each area shall be registered in the Property Register in accordance with the sequence of their numbers. If an area has several registers, such registers shall be numbered in accordance with the date of their opening. In addition thereto, the number of the first folio and of the last folio therein shall be mentioned on the spine and front of the cover of each register. In each district (qada) or governorate (muhafazah), each cadastral area shall be designated by its name and by a serial number, and these particulars shall be recorded on the spine of the cover of each register of the area and on the front thereof.

Each immovable property shall have a folio composed of four pages, the first of which shall be allocated to the description of the immovable property, to the mention of buildings or plantations encumbered with a surface right, an ijjaratayn right or a muqata'ah right, and to the recording of usufructs and easements.

There shall also be mentioned on this first page the assessed value of the immovable property established for the collection of taxes, and the origin of the land folio. The remaining three pages shall be allocated to the entry of ownership or right of disposal (tasarruf), waqf rights and rights of usufruct, restriction of rights of disposal, mortgages, and contracts of antichresis and lease, and to the recording of the copies of the folio delivered to the owners. As for the different rights provided for in Article 23 below, their registration in the Land Register shall be effected in a supplementary folio opened for this purpose in the Property Register according to the model designated by the Administration, and it shall be placed in the Property Register annexed to the real folio of the immovable property pertaining thereto; the same rules followed in drawing up that folio shall be followed in drawing it up, and the items and index particulars specific to the supplementary folio shall be mentioned in the real folio.

The description of each immovable property shall comprise the following particulars:

1- The name of the cadastral area and its serial number

2 - The number of the immovable property and its legal category

3 - The serial number of the folio (a series of numbers placed for folios drawn up successively for each immovable property when the previous folios are filled)

4 - The cross-reference to the cadastral survey map, with respect to its sections and its number, and the known locality or quarter, and the street and its number

5 - The description of the immovable property:

a - Its location and boundaries on the basis of the cadastral survey map.

b - Its appurtenances and its area.

c - The legal category of the buildings and plantations.

6 - The description of the buildings and plantations encumbered with a surface right, an ijjaratayn right or a muqata'ah right, together with a statement of their state (amiriyyah) sale value

7 - Usufructs and easements

8 - The assessed value of the immovable property taken as a basis for determining proportional fees

9 - The origin of the folio, namely the decision confirming ownership, or the parent immovable property in the case of subdivision

10- The index of the folios pertaining to the immovable property (there shall be mentioned in the index the serial numbers of the folios drawn up successively upon the filling of the previous folios, and the date of their drawing up, together with the signature of the Land Registrar).

Modifications supervening in the state of the immovable property, as a result of partition, amalgamation, boundary rectification, construction of buildings, creation of plantations, or demolition or destruction of buildings, etc., shall be recorded successively in the column allocated to the description of the immovable property upon completion of the topographical operations in accordance with the contracts, agreements and applications that result in a modification in the consistence of the immovable property, in its appurtenances or in its contents.

As for the particulars pertaining to the appurtenances of the immovable property modified by subsequent entries, they shall be cancelled by a horizontal line in red ink bisecting the column across. When a modification supervenes in the contents of the immovable property, the new contents shall be mentioned opposite the transaction from which the modification arose, and the old contents shall be struck out by a line in red ink.

As for the modifications supervening in the buildings and plantations encumbered with surface rights, ijjaratayn rights and muqata'ah rights, and those rights themselves, as well as the modifications supervening in usufructs and easements, and the amount of the assessed value of the immovable property, they shall be recorded in the columns allocated to them in the folio.

The second section of the folio is intended for entering the following entries:

1 - The right of ownership or disposal (tasarruf).

2 - Rights of endowment (waqf) or exploitation (and these rights may be entered in the column of usufruct and easement).

3 - Restriction of the right of disposal, real actions, attachments, etc.

4 - Real estate mortgages, and there shall also be entered in the second section of the folio long-term agricultural lease (daman) or lease contracts, and receipts of advance payment or assignment of an amount equivalent to rent or agricultural lease for more than one year, as well as the copies delivered to owners of the real folios. The registration of ownership on the real estate folio shall be effected by entering the number of the record of the contract, or the agreement, or the Sharia judgment upon which it relies

for registration, the date of entry of these documents in the daily register, a summary of the contract or agreement, and a statement of the name of the owner, and to state the name of the owner there shall be mentioned:

1 - With respect to natural persons:

The first name, surname, nationality, capacity or profession, and where necessary, everything that indicates identity such as date of birth, parentage, etc...

2 - With respect to companies and legal persons:

The trade name or name, nationality, and headquarters, as well as the type of company or legal person, and the amount of the share of each of the partners must be specified when registering a right held in common (undivided ownership), and this share shall be expressed as a number out of a base denominator of 2400, and if the ownership is joint, there must be added to the entries recorded in the column allocated to the type of right and to the summary of contracts a statement of the legal relationship from which the joint ownership arose, and the registration of the restriction of the right of disposal shall be effected in accordance with the rules followed for the registration of ownership, and when registering real estate mortgages, reference must be made to the following particulars:

A - The number of the mortgage contract and the date of its entry in the daily register.

B - The type of mortgage and reference to the supporting documents.

C - The name of the creditor.

D - The name of the debtor.

E - The real property or real properties over which the mortgage runs.

F - The value of the debt and its maturity.

G - The agreed interest and the rank when the contract is a hypothec (ta'min).

Every registration or annotation in the real estate folio shall be effected concisely and necessarily requires specifying the number and date of the entry of the record of the contract or the agreement or the application for registration in the daily register at the auxiliary office.

The date of their registration in the Land Register must be mentioned on the contracts and agreements or applications by means of a dated stamp, and the recording of entries and annotations in the register of ownership shall be effected in indelible black ink, without erasure or addition. Corrections, however, shall be effected in red ink and certified by the Land Registrar.

The Land Registrar shall sign all entries and annotations after verifying and dating them, and then seal them with the special seal of the registry, and the foregoing provisions shall also apply to cancellations (strike-offs) and modifications occurring to the entries, and the cancellation of entries shall be effected by placing a line in red ink underneath them with a reference in that section of the folio to the contract or legal document relied upon in the cancellation.

With respect to real estate mortgages, however, their cancellation shall be effected opposite their entry.

The modification of entries shall be effected in accordance with the rules followed in cancellation. The transfer of debts secured by a real estate mortgage, and in general every annotation relating to the assignment of any debt or its transfer or its reduction, and the changes occurring to a real estate mortgage, shall be registered opposite the mortgage entry in accordance

with the rules prescribed for entries, and if the column does not have enough space, a new column shall be used for them with a cross-reference to the previous column.

The supporting documents shall be inserted into the special file of each real property upon registering the transaction pertaining to them in the register of ownership and shall be kept in that file. This arrangement shall be effected in respect of each transaction according to its chronological order, and a numbered divider sheet shall be placed between the documents pertaining to each transaction and the previous documents, and this number shall be referred to on the cover of the file of the real property with a statement of the type of transaction pertaining to it.

The daily register is allocated to proving the date of deposit of applications for registration in the Land Register.

The Administration shall establish the model of this register.

The daily register shall consist of two hundred pages numbered from one to two hundred, and on its cover shall be mentioned the name of the auxiliary real estate office, the number of the register, and the number of its pages, and the Land Registrar, head of the real estate office, shall sign this annotation.

These same particulars shall be mentioned on the back of the register.

One of the judges of the Courts of First Instance shall initial every page thereof.

The daily register shall be kept in a single copy and shall be closed daily by the head of the auxiliary real estate office, and in each entry there must be mentioned the serial number, the day and hour of submission of the application, the name of the applicant for registration and his place of residence, the type of right requested to be registered, the numbers of the real properties related to the application with a statement of the cadastral area in which they are situated, and an enumeration of the documents produced in support of the application.

The head of the auxiliary office shall close each entry and sign it. The daily register shall be kept without erasure or addition and without leaving any blank space between the lines. Corrections, however, shall be effected by the head of the auxiliary real estate office in red ink and signed by him.

He must always certify marginal notes.

Upon closing the daily register, the head of the auxiliary office shall sign it and transmit it pursuant to a list to the Land Registrar within twenty-four hours to be kept in the repository of the Land Registry office. The Land Registrar must return the said list on the same day to the head of the auxiliary office, with a notice thereon acknowledging receipt of the register.

The daily registers shall be kept at the Land Registry office in cabinets allocated to each auxiliary real estate office and shall be classified according to their chronological order, and on the cover of each daily register and on its back there must be mentioned the date of its opening and its closing.

In addition to the Land Register, there shall be kept in each Land Registry office:

A - For each cadastral area:

First - An alphabetical index of the names of the owners.

Second - An alphabetical index of the names of the holders of real estate mortgages and confirmed attachments.

B - For all areas falling under the Land Registry office:

First - A serial register in which applications for registration transmitted from the auxiliary real estate offices are entered.

Second - A daily register in which objections submitted directly to the Land Registrar are entered.

Third - A ledger in which the decisions of the Land Registrar regarding corrections occurring to the register of ownership and the cadastral survey map and the rejection of applications for registration are entered.

Fourth - A ledger in which notifications of contracts are entered.

Fifth - A ledger for applications pertaining to topographical transactions arising from contracts, agreements, and other matters.

Sixth - A serial register for correspondence.

Seventh - A numbering box for the inventory of archives.

Except for the daily register, there shall be kept in each auxiliary office a register for ordering preliminary transactions for registration, as well as a ledger of records of the model used in the Administration.

Sub-section 1 - When an application is made to register a real property not subject to registration following the creation of real rights over it or its conversion into private property, its entry in the Land Register shall be effected upon the application of the claimant of the right after producing a copy, certified as a true copy of the original by the competent department, of the decision ordering the removal of this real property from the public domain. This copy must be accompanied by the deed of grant of the real property or the deed of its sale from the department that assigned it or sold it. (The State Domain Department or the municipality, according to the circumstances). In this case, the placement of boundary markers shall be initiated through the efforts of the department charged with maintaining the cadastral survey.

If the registration of the real property was omitted due to its having been erroneously placed during demarcation among the public domain or for any other reason, its entry in the Land Register shall be effected upon the application of the claimant of the right in accordance with the following provisions:

The application for registration shall be submitted in writing. And it must contain the particulars specified in the provisions of Article 17 of the Resolution on the Ascertainment and Demarcation of Immovable Properties. It must be certified by the mukhtars and imams of the locality of the adjoining owners.

If these do not attend in person, their signatures must be certified in the form prescribed in Resolution 188 concerning the establishment of the Real Property Register. The Head of the Real Property Office shall, at the expense of the applicant, carry out the demarcation of the immovable property and the drawing of its provisional plan through a sworn engineer from the Topographical Office. This operation shall take place in the presence of the applicant or his proxy. The Head of the Real Property Office shall notify, by means of notices sent to the mukhtars of the locality of the adjoining owners specified in the application as well as the interested parties, of the day and hour at which the demarcation will take place, and this notice shall be sent to the mukhtar eight days prior to the date of the operation ' The demarcation shall take place on the appointed day and hour in accordance with the rules prescribed in Article 11 and the articles following it of the Resolution on the Ascertainment and Demarcation of Immovable Properties. A provisional demarcation plan and proces-verbal shall be drawn up in which shall be stated:

1 - The day and hour of the conduct of the operation.

2 - The names, titles, capacities and places of residence of the persons who attended the operation.

3 - The existing disputes and the claims and objections submitted.

4 - The number of boundary marks and their location.

5 - The documents produced by the two parties .

The proces-verbal shall be closed with the signature of the engineer and the persons who attended as interveners or claimants in respect of any right. If they are unable to sign, it shall be stated in the proces-verbal that they do not know how to sign or that they refuse to do so.

The proces-verbal shall be published and stated at the expense of the applicant through the Head of the Real Property Office in the Official Gazette and in three newspapers in the district, and in addition these documents together with the demarcation plan shall be posted on the door of the Assistant Office. These notices shall be renewed once every 15 days and for a period of two months from the date of filing the application. All objectors shall be required to submit their objections within the two months following the date of this filing. Objections shall be submitted in the form prescribed by the persons specified in Articles 20 and 21 of the Resolution on the Ascertainment and Demarcation of Immovable Properties.

Objections shall be made in writing, signed, and sent to the Head of the Real Property Office either directly or through the mukhtars, justices of the peace, presidents of courts, and judges. The declarations mentioned above must be accompanied by all the deeds or documents upon which the application is based.

Objections submitted during the provisional demarcation or received by the Head of the Real Property Office shall be notified to the applicant. The applicant must rebut the objections within one month from the date of the day of service.

If he fails to do so, the objections shall be referred, after the expiry of the period granted to the applicant, to the Permanent Committee in the district, which shall adjudicate upon them in accordance with the provisions of Article 23 and the articles following it of the Resolution on the Ascertainment and Demarcation of Immovable Properties.
No objection whatsoever shall be accepted after the expiry of the period of two months commencing from the filing of the application.

After the expiry of the period of two months specified in Article 16 mentioned above, and if not the slightest objection has been submitted or if the applicant has rebutted the objections, the Head of the Real Property Office shall, where necessary, proceed with the demarcation and the drawing of the final plan of the immovable property and through a sworn engineer from the Topographical Office, and the immovable property shall be registered in the Real Property Register.

Every immovable property registered in a special folio of the Real Property Register must be in every one of its parts of a single judicial category. Every part of an immovable property whose judicial category differs from the remaining parts must be registered in a special folio.

Every immovable property for which a real property folio is drawn up may only consist of a single parcel or of parcels forming a single block of a single legal category.

By way of exception, land upon which buildings and appurtenances attached thereto (such as canals, gardens, etc.) are erected shall form a single immovable property even if the immovable property and the buildings existing thereon are of different legal categories.

A single principal folio shall only be used for an immovable property belonging to a single person or to several persons all of whom hold undivided rights in all parts of the immovable property without distinction.

If a right of ownership exists or is established over a part that cannot be severed from the immovable property, that shall not require the drawing up of a separate folio, but rather that right shall be stated in the principal folio of the immovable property and the name of its holder shall be recorded in his capacity as a co-owner in the immovable property, subject to the provisions of Article 23.

By way of derogation from the provisions of the preceding article, if different rights exist over the whole of the immovable property, such as ijaratayn, and over the land, such as rights of superficies and muqata'a, or over the storeys of a building or over its rooms, there shall be drawn up, in addition to the principal folio of the immovable property, a supplementary folio for each of these rights. When buildings are erected on contiguous immovable properties in such a manner that their various parts (such as apartments of houses, their storeys, their rooms, etc..) over which different rights of ownership run extend beyond the boundaries of the adjoining immovable properties, a single folio shall be drawn up for the whole of the immovable properties covered by these parts, and supplementary folios for each part of the immovable property or of the buildings over which a right exclusive to it alone runs.

When a real right is established over a specific part of an immovable property, it may only be recorded in the Real Property Register after the partition of the immovable property and after the drawing up of the principal folio for the part of the immovable property over which the recording of the right is requested. Real rights recorded in the folio of subdivided immovable properties or those amalgamated with one another shall be recorded after their subdivision or amalgamation in their respective ranks in the new folios.

If the subdivided immovable property is subject to legally registered mortgage rights or real encumbrances, and the parcels of land created after the subdivision have been assigned to owners who are not jointly and severally liable, the mortgage rights or real encumbrances shall be apportioned by the Registrar and recorded in the new folios in their respective ranks in accordance with the agreement concluded between the interested parties.

In the absence of an agreement, it shall be in proportion to the value of the parcels over which those rights or encumbrances run, as assessed for the imposition of taxes thereon.

If these immovable properties are amalgamated with one another, the mortgage rights and real encumbrances recorded in the principal folios pertaining to the amalgamated immovable properties shall be recorded after the amalgamation in their respective ranks or together in the new folio.

The Head of the Real Property Office may, upon a detailed application by the owner of the property, establish a new folio in which shall be stated only the real property rights in rem and the rights of usufruct and easements actually remaining on the immovable property. The submitted application must state the annotations that are of no avail and that must be deleted in the new folio.

The application shall be submitted to the Head of the Real Property Office, who may accept it in whole or in part or reject it, unless the application is appealed before the Court of the District sitting in council chamber.

In all cases where an entry or endorsement on the folio requires a modification to the cadastral plan, the Registrar, Chief of the Land Registry Office, may not effect the entry until after the completion of this operation.

In such a case, if there is no express provision, the application for entry lodged by the interested parties with the Auxiliary Land Registry Office shall be deemed to include an application for the prior completion of this topographical operation.

Upon receipt of the said application, the Registrar, Chief of the Land Registry Office, shall request the completion of this operation by the sworn surveyor charged with the maintenance of the plan. He shall effect a provisional entry in the Land Register.

The final entry shall be effected immediately upon receipt of the extract copy of the plan and the boundary demarcation record.

If it appears to the surveyor during the carrying out of the prior topographical operation that the boundary markers or demarcation signs have been moved from their places or destroyed, he shall restore them automatically to their places in accordance with the cadastral plan.

However, if the removal of the boundary markers from their places observed by the surveyor results from the encroachment of the public domain upon a portion of private property, the surveyor shall automatically enter the new boundaries on the plan, place the necessary boundary markers, and record this rectification together with the reasons therefor in the boundary demarcation record; and, by way of exception to the first paragraph of this Article, the Registrar shall receive the entry requested to be effected in accordance with provisions notified through the Execution Department, subject to the completion of the topographical operations, the registration of which is required on the parent folio of the real property, and he shall request the cadastral surveyor to complete the topographical operation.

As for the final entry, and where necessary the drawing up or striking out of the folios, this shall be effected in accordance with the boundary demarcation record drawn up by the sworn surveyor attached to the Cadastral Department.

In such a case, the surveyor shall be accompanied by an officer of the Execution Department, who shall attend the operation and sign the boundary demarcation record.

In order to be capable of registration, every right must be acquired directly from the holder of the preceding registration.

Accordingly, in cases where a real right or a right of usufruct and easement has been the subject of successive transfers or contracts, the last transfer or the last contract may not be registered before the registration of all preceding transfers or contracts and before the payment in full of the totality of the fees due in respect of each transfer or contract.

In all cases where the rectification or amendment of a registration is requested and the Chief of the Land Registry Office refuses to effect the same, or the two parties do not accept the rectifications that have been effected, the District Court shall adjudicate the matter by a decision taken in the case without pleading.

Irregular entries and endorsements, and omissions or clerical errors that appear on the folio, may be rectified directly by the Chief of the Land Registry Office if they occurred by reason of the documents, in particular the plans that were used to draw up the folios, or all other subsequent endorsements.
A discrepancy between the endorsements on the folios and the endorsements on the instruments or documents submitted in support of the registration shall be deemed a simple clerical error.

Rectifications shall always be notified to the holder of the copy of the folio, together with a formal notice to him of the requirement to submit the copy in order to bring it into conformity with the folio.

Cancellations, rectifications, annulments, and the striking off of real properties shall be registered on the day on which they occur.

Cancellation shall be effected by placing a line in red ink beneath the text thereof, and at the same time mention shall be made in the same section of the folio of the deed or legal instrument relied upon to effect the cancellation, rectification, annulment, etc...

The copies of the real folios delivered to the owners shall be drawn up on special printed forms the like of which cannot be produced by ordinary printing means. Furthermore, special blue-tinted paper shall be used for their manufacture in such a manner as to reveal any fraud or forgery.

These copies shall be drawn up in accordance with the conditions laid down in Articles 34 and 35 of Decision 188, and shall be signed by the Land Registrar and stamped with the dry seal of the Land Registry; and this official shall affix opposite his signature on every deed, declaration, certificate, or extract issued by him in the course of his office the official seal delivered to him by the State, and the use of signature stamps is prohibited.

Documents containing the creation, transfer, modification, or extinction of real rights or rights of usufruct and easement submitted and lodged for the purpose of being entered in the Land Registers must contain, in addition to the essential clauses of the deeds and contracts relating thereto, the following particulars:

1 - The given name, surname, and family name of the two contracting parties, their capacity, and their personal status.

2 - Where applicable, the name of the spouse, the date of the marriage contract, and the place of residence of the public official who received it.

3 - The place of residence of the contracting parties and the domicile elected by them in the district of the Land Registry Office, where the two parties are not resident in that district.

4 - The names and locations of the real properties to which the said documents relate, as well as the numbers of the land folios.

The signatures of the two parties affixed at the foot of ordinary deeds under private signature must be legalised as prescribed in Decision No. 188 issued concerning the establishment of the Land Register.

As for the identity of the two parties, it is guaranteed in public authentic deeds by the judge or the public official who drew up the deed.

French consuls, vice-consuls, and consular officers charged with representing the interests of the States placed under Mandate abroad shall have the requisite capacity, in accordance with the provisions of Article 12 of the Law on Notaries Public, to receive and draw up all documents and to confer authenticity upon them.

The record of declarations provided for in the provisions of Article 51 of Decision No. 188 concerning the establishment of the Land Register shall be drawn up by the Chief of the Auxiliary Office upon the declaration of the two parties, under the same conditions and according to the same rules observed in authentic instruments.

Records of contracts shall be drawn up on identical forms, and the duplicate copies shall be inserted in a register corresponding to the Daily Journal to which those records pertain; and upon the closing of the Daily Journal, it shall be sent to the Registrar, Chief of the Land Registry Office, to be preserved in the archives of the Registry.

Delivery thereof shall be effected by means of a schedule which shall be returned to the Auxiliary Office concerned as an acknowledgment of receipt.

As for the register of records of contracts, it shall be preserved in the department of the Auxiliary Land Registry Office.

In all cases where the two parties appearing before the Chief of the Auxiliary Office are ignorant of the language used in the country, the Chief of the Auxiliary Office shall request the Notary Public or, in his absence, the President of the Court, to appoint an interpreter.

The expenses of the interpreter's fee or the fee of the interpreter shall be borne by the applicant.

The Chief of the Auxiliary Office may not receive declarations in the following circumstances:

1 - If he does not know the contracting parties and their identity is not attested to him by witnesses known to him, or if one of them is under a state of legal interdiction provided for by law.

2 - If the agent fails to produce a lawful power of attorney.

3 - If the agreement relates to acts contrary to law or morality, or constitutes a transaction of forgery; in the latter case, the Chief of the Auxiliary Office shall seize the forged documents submitted, draw up a record of seizure, and refer the whole to the Public Prosecutor at the District Court.
Every application lodged for the purpose of registration is written to the Land Registry Office in the district and is subject to the payment of the legal costs and fees.

The Chief of the Auxiliary Office shall write in his own hand the record of the declarations of the contracting parties without abbreviation, blank space, erasure, or interlineation; he shall state therein the sums and dates in words in full; every striking out must be certified either in the margin or at the foot of the text. The striking out must be effected by a horizontal pen-stroke beneath which the struck-out text remains visible.

Where the matter relates to a deed between two parties, the acceptance of the two parties must be expressly stated therein; the subject-matter and cause of the agreement must be defined therein with full clarity.

Furthermore, it must contain all the particulars prescribed in Article 51 and the following articles of Decision No. 188 concerning the establishment of the Land Register.

The Secretary-General, the Delegate Extraordinary of the High Commissioner to the State of Syria and the Delegates to the States are charged, each in so far as it appoints him, with the execution of this Decision.

There is hereby put into effect the urgent Bill referred to the Chamber of Deputies pursuant to Decree No. 10845 dated 10/9/1968, concerning the acquisition by non-Lebanese of real rights in immovable property in Lebanon, the text of which follows:

It shall not be permissible for any non-Lebanese person, whether natural or legal, nor shall it be permissible for any Lebanese legal person deemed by this Law to have the status of a foreigner, to acquire, by contract or any other legal act inter vivos, any real right in immovable property in Lebanese territory or any other real right among those specified by this Law save after obtaining a licence granted by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

No exception shall be made to this rule save in the cases expressly provided for in this Law or in a special provision.

It shall not be permissible for any person who does not hold a nationality issued by a recognized State, or for any person where the ownership conflicts with the provisions of the Constitution relating to the rejection of permanent settlement, to own any real right of whatever kind.

For the purpose of applying this Law, the following shall be deemed to have the status of non-Lebanese legal persons:

- Partnerships and limited liability companies in which all shares are not owned by Lebanese natural persons who are prohibited, under their articles of association, from assigning such shares to non-Lebanese or to other than purely Lebanese companies.

- Joint-stock companies and partnerships limited by shares in which all shares are not registered shares owned by Lebanese natural persons or purely Lebanese companies whose articles of association prohibit the assignment of such shares to other than Lebanese natural persons or to other than purely Lebanese companies.

Subject to the provisions of the new Article 1, the following shall be excepted and exempted from the licence:

1- Ownership by non-Lebanese natural persons and legal persons, or those deemed to have the status of non-Lebanese, of built immovable properties or immovable properties designated for building whose area in Lebanese territory does not exceed three thousand square metres.

2- Acquisition of real rights in immovable property pursuant to the provisions of Articles 33 and 40 of Law No. 58 dated 29/5/91, the Expropriation Law.

3- Acquisition of real rights in immovable property in execution of special laws that require their acquisition by way of security or permit it for another reason, and within the limits imposed by those laws and the conditions specified thereby

4- Acquisition of the following real rights:

أ- The right of inheritance for heirs.

ب- The right arising from a bequest or a gift concluded between non-Lebanese who are included among their heirs upon their death, and in particular ascendants, descendants and spouses.

ج- Rights arising from contracts of usufruct, antichresis, sale with a right of redemption or for exploitation, mortgage and lease provided for in Decision No. 12 dated 16/1/1934 (the Musaqat regime) Bail emphyteotique, provided that the provisions of the Fourth and Fifth Articles shall be observed in the acquisition of these rights.

A right of usufruct and an ordinary right of lease the term of each of which exceeds ten years, and the right of lease provided for by Decision No. 12 issued on 16/1/1934 the term of which exceeds twenty years, may not be validly acquired prior to obtaining the licence.

An antichresis or a sale with a right of redemption or for exploitation in which a period of exploitation exceeding ten years is specified shall be subject, as to its acquisition, to the licence. A mortgage or a privilege, however, shall not require a licence.

Nevertheless, a non-Lebanese creditor of a debt arising from an antichresis, a sale with a right of redemption or for exploitation, a mortgage or a privilege shall not be entitled to purchase the real right amicably or by auction through the courts without a prior licence, unless no Lebanese bidder comes forward to purchase it at the reserve price fixed for the first auction or at a price exceeding the secured debt and its accessories.

In such case, the non-Lebanese creditor shall be entitled to purchase that right by auction, provided that his purchase shall be subject to the condition that he sell it to a Lebanese within a period not exceeding two years from the date on which the adjudication decision becomes final, on pain of the sale of this right in accordance with the procedures set forth in the new Article (11); if the creditor is a bank, the provisions of Article 154 of the Code of Money and Credit shall apply to its purchase.

- What is owned by non-Lebanese natural persons and legal persons, or those deemed to have the status of non-Lebanese, after the entry into force of the Law put into effect by Decree 11614 dated 4/1/69, in the entirety of Lebanese territory shall not exceed three per cent (3%) of the total of its area, provided that it does not exceed 3% (three per cent) in each district (caza) of the total of its area and does not exceed in the Governorate of Beirut ten per cent (10%) of the total of its area.

ب- In calculating the percentages mentioned above, account shall be taken of the ownership by Lebanese companies deemed to have the status of non-Lebanese pursuant to the provisions of the Second Article of the Law put into effect by Decree No. 11614 dated 4/1/1969

with the exception of:

ا- Partnerships and limited liability companies in which the majority, namely more than fifty per cent of the shares, is owned by Lebanese natural partners or purely Lebanese companies whose articles of association prohibit the assignment of these shares to non-Lebanese, in which case a proportion of fifty per cent (50%) only of the areas which they own shall be counted within the percentages set forth in this Article.

2- Joint-stock companies or partnerships limited by shares in which the majority of the shares, namely more than fifty per cent of the shares, is owned by Lebanese natural persons or purely Lebanese companies whose articles of association prohibit the assignment of these shares to non-Lebanese, in which case a proportion of fifty per cent (50%) only of the areas which they own shall be counted within the percentages set forth in this Article.

The attainment of the ownership percentages shall be declared by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance, and the acquisition of real rights in immovable property by non-Lebanese, or those deemed to have the status of non-Lebanese pursuant to the provisions of the Second Article of the Law put into effect by Decree No. 11614 dated 4/1/1969, shall be suspended, save where such acquisition takes place between non-Lebanese persons or persons deemed to have the status of non-Lebanese.

The Automated Centre at the Ministry of Finance - Directorate of Real Estate Affairs - shall draw up the statements and statistics necessary to show the aforementioned percentages, and when the legal percentages are reached, the Directorate of Real Estate Affairs shall take the measures necessary to halt the operations of registering real rights for non-Lebanese, provided that these statements are published in the Official Gazette every six months.

For the purpose of determining the areas which non-Lebanese natural persons may own with or without a licence pursuant to the provisions of this Law, husbands, wives and minor children shall be deemed to have the status of a single person. For the application of this Article, a child who has not attained eighteen full years of age shall be deemed a minor.

The application for a licence shall be submitted to the Ministry of Finance, specifying therein the immovable property and the real right sought to be acquired, and shall be referred to the Council of Ministers with a proposal to accept or reject it.

The Council of Ministers shall have absolute discretionary power to grant or refuse the licence, and its decisions of refusal shall not be subject to review by any authority whatsoever.

The effect of the licensing decree shall lapse if it is not acted upon within one year from the date of its publication in the Official Gazette.

Save where the cause of the delay is a judicial dispute between the licensee and the person from whom he derived the right and the action was registered in the Land Register within the said period, or a legal impediment beyond the control of the licensee, in which two cases the running of this period shall be suspended throughout the duration of the proceedings or until the legal impediment ceases.

Every natural person who has acquired a real property right in accordance with the provisions of this Law shall complete the construction of a building on the right that is the subject of ownership within a maximum period of five years from the date of registration in the Real Property Register, renewable once by decision of the Council of Ministers, and every legal person shall likewise allocate the real properties that are the subject of ownership to the purpose for which they were acquired or for which the licence was granted within the said period. All of this shall be under penalty of lapse or revocation of the right and its sale by the Ministry of Finance, together with whatever has been erected thereon, for the account of the offender and at his expense and responsibility, in accordance with the provisions of Legislative Decree No. 147 dated 12/06/1959, "Procedures for the Collection of Direct Taxes and Similar Fees". The entire profit resulting from the sale shall be confiscated for the benefit of the Treasury after the full price and legal expenses have been refunded to the holder of the right.

The judicial courts shall have jurisdiction to hear disputes arising from the application of the provisions of this Article.

The licence periods prior to the entry into force of this Law, whether expired or unexpired, shall be deemed extended by operation of law and without need for the issuance of a special instrument therefor, provided that the period of extension shall not exceed five years from the date of entry into force of this Law.

1- The periods of the licences provided for in Article 11 shall be extended for three years as from the date of entry into force of Law 144/2019 pursuant to a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.

2- In the event that the extended period expires without commencement of the construction of the building, a cumulative annual fine of 2% of the value of the real property shall be imposed on the owner of the real property, to be registered on the real property folio as a privileged debt for the benefit of the Treasury. When the value of the fine reaches 10% of the actual value of the real property, the real property shall be sold at public auction by the Ministry of Finance in accordance with the procedures set forth in the said Article 11. The fines accruing to the Treasury shall be collected.

*The period of the licences provided for in this Article is extended for up to six months from the date of 5/3/2020 (pursuant to Law in Force by Operation of Law No. 6 dated 5/3/2020)

None of the companies specified in the preceding Article and in item 2 of the Third Article that has acquired a real property right in accordance with the provisions of this Law may introduce into its articles of association, other than in the case of the death of one of the partners, any amendment that would reduce the shares or stocks of Lebanese nationals therein, under penalty of nullity and the exposure of the partners who approved the amendment and the managers who executed it to the penalties provided for in Article 16.

Upon the dissolution of companies, establishments and associations licensed or exempted from a licence to own real property rights in Lebanon, it is prohibited to partition these rights and distribute them in kind among non-Lebanese partners except subject to compliance with the provisions of this Law.

An applicant for the registration of a real right governed by the provisions of this Law shall submit official certificates issued by the competent departments specifying the areas that he owns in Lebanese territory, together with a written declaration signed with his signature in which he declares that he owns only those areas. Joint-stock companies and partnerships limited by shares deemed to have the status of non-Lebanese companies may substitute for the aforementioned certificates a statement signed by the chairman of their board of directors and certified as accurate by the auditors, setting out the areas and locations of the real properties that they own on the basis of the entries in their books. Anyone who submits a certificate, statement or declaration contrary to the truth shall be punished with the penalties provided for in Article 16 of this Law, and the real properties acquired on the basis of the false certificate, declaration or statement shall be confiscated without compensation.

Confiscation shall be ordered by the judgment convicting of the said offence, and an annotation shall be placed on the said real properties when a prosecution is brought for this offence.

Every contract or act carried out in contravention of the provisions of this Law and of the texts issued to determine the procedures for its application shall be deemed null and void of absolute nullity and as if non-existent.

Those who committed it, participated in it or intervened in it in any manner whatsoever, and those who authenticated or registered it with knowledge thereof, shall be punished with temporary hard labour and with a fine ranging between the value of the real right and three times its amount.

These provisions shall apply to every legal act concluded through a nominee in order to evade the application of the provisions of this Law.

Every clause aimed at guaranteeing the performance of such a void act or at imposing an obligation to pay compensation in the event of its non-performance shall be deemed null and void.

The provisions of this Law shall not apply to licences to acquire real property rights granted before its entry into force if the licence is used within a period of one year from the date of entry into force of this Law.

For the purpose of calculating the ownership percentages provided for in paragraph "A" of the new Seventh Article, account shall be taken of the areas licensed to be acquired or acquired without a licence after the date of entry into force of the Law promulgated by Decree No. 11614 dated 04/01/1969, and those that are licensed to be acquired or are acquired without a licence after the entry into force of this Law, taking into consideration the provisions of the new Seventh Article and the provisions of the last paragraph of the new Article (11).

Within the limits of the maximum area provided for in this Law, non-Lebanese natural or legal persons may conclude special agreements having as their object the creation of a real right, the effectiveness of which is conditional upon obtaining the required licence.

These agreements shall be deemed null and void by operation of law without need for any formality if the period specified therein for obtaining the licence expires, provided that such period shall not exceed one year. If it exceeds one year or if the contract does not include a period, the period shall be deemed to be one year by operation of law.
The detailed rules for the application of the provisions of this Law shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.
The provisions of Law No. 59/66 issued on 10/9/1966 are repealed, and all texts contrary to or inconsistent with the provisions of the present Law are likewise repealed.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

In this Legislative Decree:

1 - The expression "vehicle" means:

a - Every land vehicle equipped with a motor of any kind and whatever its intended use.

b - Every trailer or semi-trailer whatever its kind or intended use.

c - Every other kind of land vehicle which may be subject to the obligation of insurance provided for in this Legislative Decree.

2 - The expression "bodily harm" means: death and every bodily injury resulting from accidents, fires and explosions caused by the vehicle or its parts or pieces or the tools or materials used in operating or moving it or the things or materials transported therein.

3 - The insurer: the insurance undertaking or the National Institution for Compulsory Insurance.

Every owner of a vehicle in Lebanon shall be bound to conclude an insurance policy with an insurance undertaking licensed to carry on vehicle risks insurance, covering the civil liability which may arise from the bodily harm caused by his vehicle to third parties.

In cases where it is required to obtain a circulation permit, the granting or renewal of circulation permits of all kinds shall be conditional upon proving the existence of the compulsory insurance contract provided for in the second Article.

Determination of the details of application of Legislative Decree No. 105/77 dated 30/06/1977 relating to Compulsory Insurance for Civil Liability for Bodily Harm Caused by Land Vehicles to Third Parties

Owners of vehicles registered outside Lebanon and entering the territory of the Lebanese Republic shall be bound to take out an insurance contract thereon for the duration of their stay in Lebanon or their transit through it.
