Exempted therefrom are vehicles carrying one of the international motor insurance cards in the event that Lebanon joins the international body that grants such cards, and also exempted are vehicles registered and insured in one of the Arab States whose insurance contract covers the duration of their stay in Lebanon. This is subject to reciprocity, and provided that the undertaking which issued the insurance contract has a representative in Lebanon authorised to represent it and to settle and pay the compensation incurred by it in accordance with the provisions of this Legislative Decree. The Arab States covered by this exemption shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Economy and Trade.

The insurance contract shall cover the civil liability arising from any bodily harm caused by the vehicle to third parties whether the vehicle is driven by its owner or driven by another person to whom its custody or driving has been transferred with the consent and knowledge of its owner or without his consent.

Every person who sustains bodily harm caused by the vehicle, whether inside the vehicle or outside it, shall benefit from compensation for the bodily harm sustained by him, with the exception of those excluded by an express provision in the contract. Where applicable, the right to compensation shall pass to the heirs.

None may be excluded in the compulsory insurance contract from the right to benefit from compensation except the persons mentioned below and exclusively:

1 - The owner of the insured vehicle and every person to whom its custody has been transferred.

2 - The driver of the insured vehicle in the event that he sustains bodily harm while driving it.

3 - The spouse, ascendants and descendants of the persons mentioned in the two preceding items in the event that they sustain bodily harm while present in the insured vehicle or boarding it or alighting from it.

4 - The wage-earners and employees of the persons mentioned in the first item of this Article in the event that they sustain bodily harm caused to them by the insured vehicle during the performance of their service.

5 - The partners of the persons mentioned in the first item of this Article in the event that they sustain bodily harm while present in the insured vehicle or boarding it or alighting from it.

6 - The legal representatives of the natural person whose liability is insured in the event that they sustain bodily harm while present in the insured vehicle and boarding it or alighting from it.

A private institution of public utility known as the "National Institution for Compulsory Insurance" shall be established, which shall undertake the tasks specified in this Legislative Decree.

This Institution shall enjoy legal personality and financial and administrative autonomy and shall automatically comprise all insurance undertakings licensed to carry on insurance operations against land vehicle risks, and shall exercise its tasks under the supervision and tutelage of the Minister of Economy and Trade. The Institution shall not be subject to the supervision of the Civil Service Board, the Central Inspection and the Court of Accounts.

The Institution shall undertake in particular:

1 - Determining the standard compulsory insurance contract which all insurance undertakings must adopt.

2 - Determining the tariff of compulsory insurance premiums for each category of land vehicles.

3 - Insuring land vehicles registered abroad in the cases provided for in this Legislative Decree.

4 - Insuring land vehicles which three insurance undertakings refuse to insure.

5 - Paying compensation for bodily harm caused by land vehicles in the following cases:

a - Harm caused by a vehicle insured with it.

b - Harm caused by an uninsured vehicle.

c - Harm caused by a vehicle that remained unidentified,

d - Harm caused by a vehicle where the designated insurance undertaking failed to pay the compensation due by it by reason of its bankruptcy or cessation of payments.

6 - Other tasks which may be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers.

The standard compulsory insurance contract and the tariff shall not become effective until after the approval of the Minister of Economy and Trade, which is given after consulting the opinion of the National Insurance Council.

Implementing decree for this Article

The charges, expenses and obligations of the Institution shall be given as follows:

1 - A percentage of the compulsory insurance premiums for land vehicle risks, determined annually by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Economy and Trade.

2 - The premiums of insurance contracts for land vehicles registered abroad and insured by the Institution and the premiums of insurance contracts for land vehicles insured by the Institution by reason of their refusal by three insurance undertakings,

3 - Fines imposed pursuant to the provisions of this Legislative Decree,

4 - Contributions of insurance undertakings to cover the balance of the charges and obligations of the Institution, the contribution of each undertaking being determined in proportion to the premiums pertaining to the vehicle risks insurance contracts issued by it.

Every insurance undertaking licensed to carry on land vehicle risks shall place at the disposal of the Institution upon commencing the exercise of its tasks and in the first year an amount determined by- the Institution with the approval of the Minister of Economy and Trade on account of the contribution that will be incurred by it- in accordance with the provisions of the preceding Article.

The Minister of Economy and Trade shall be represented at the Institution by the Head of the Department of Insurance Undertakings Affairs at the Ministry of Economy and Trade in the capacity of Government Commissioner, whose mission shall be to watch in general over the application of the laws and regulations relating to the Institution and he shall attend in this capacity the meetings of the Board of Directors of the Institution and shall have therein the right to object to the decisions of the Board.

An objection by the Government Commissioner to any decision of the Board of Directors shall suspend the execution of such decision, and the Government Commissioner must refer the matter to the Minister of Economy and Trade within two days from the date of the objection, and the Minister shall have a time-limit of fifteen days to consult the National Insurance Council on the matter objected to and to rule thereon after such consultation. The decision shall be deemed approved if the said time-limits expire and the Board has not been notified during them of a reasoned decision of refusal. In the event of the absence of the titular Head of the Department of Insurance Undertakings Affairs, the official legally assigned to carry out his duties during his absence shall replace him in the duties of the Government Commissariat at the Institution.

The injured female party and the right holders shall have a right of direct action against the insurer, and the insurer may be sued before the criminal courts, if the action arising from the accident is pending before them.

Subject to the forfeiture time-limits provided for in this Legislative Decree, there shall be barred by a limitation period of two years:

1 - The right of the injured party to bring an action on solidarity in respect of the compensation due to him, as from the date of occurrence of the accident which caused him the damages or from the date of his work of such damages,

2 - The right of the insurer to bring an action against the insured or the person liable for the accident to claim from him payment of the compensations which the insurer has paid, as from the date of payment of such compensations by him.

1 - Any person suffering bodily injuries caused to him by an unidentified vehicle, or his next of kin, shall notify, by means of a written letter and against a receipt, the head office of the Institution or one of its branches of the accident within six days commencing from the day following the day on which the injury occurred, under pain of forfeiture of the right to compensation, unless the failure to declare is due to force majeure; and he, or in the event of his death his heirs, shall submit an application for compensation accompanied by the supporting documents within a time-limit of two months from the date of completion of treatment or of death, likewise under pain of forfeiture of the right.

2 - The Institution shall decide on the application within a time-limit of thirty days at the most, and for that purpose it may carry out such investigations as it deems necessary to verify the accuracy of the facts, information and amounts stated in the notification,

3 - The Institution may refuse payment by a reasoned decision if the inaccuracy of the facts and information submitted or the inaccuracy of the compensations claimed is established to it. Failure by the Institution to reply to the application within the aforementioned time-limit of one month shall be deemed an acceptance.

4 - The injured person or his heirs shall have the right to challenge the express decision of refusal before the Court of Appeal of the Governorate in which the accident was raised, and the said Court shall apply in respect of this action the summary procedure, and its decision shall not be subject to cassation, but shall be open to opposition and third-party opposition in the cases determined by law.

In addition to the cases provided for in the Code of Obligations and Contracts, the Institution and the insurance bodies shall have a right of recourse against the owner of the vehicle or the person liable for the accident - or against both of them jointly - to recover what it has paid to the injured party by way of compensation in the following cases:

1 - If it is established that the driver of the vehicle was, at the time of the accident, in a state of drunkenness or under the influence of narcotics.

2 - If it is established that the vehicle was used for a purpose other than that declared in the registration certificate or for purposes contrary to the laws and regulations in force,

3 - If the driver of the vehicle does not hold a valid legal driving licence applicable to the category of the insured vehicle,

4 - If the vehicle was not presented for mechanical inspection at the time appointed for it, or continued to circulate number the refusal to renew its circulation permit, or if it is established by a final judgment that the accident was the result of negligence in the maintenance of the vehicle,

5 - If it is established that the accident resulted from gross fault committed by the driver of the motor vehicle which was such as to increase the probability of the occurrence of the accident.

6 - If it appears that the insurance contract was concluded on the basis of false statements made by the insured or by his concealment of material facts having an effect on the assessment of the insurance body or the Institution,

7 - If it is established that the bodily injuries resulted from an act committed by the driver wilfully and with premeditation.

Every person who is obliged to conclude a compulsory insurance contract in accordance with the provisions of this Legislative Decree and who neglects this obligation shall be punished by a pecuniary fine of one thousand to two thousand Lebanese pounds and by imprisonment from two months to six months, or by either of these two penalties, and the vehicle shall be impounded until the violation is removed; in the event of recidivism, the said penalty shall be doubled and the offender shall be granted from the right to drive land vehicles for a period of one year.

Every person who drives a land vehicle that is not insured in accordance with the provisions of this Legislative Decree shall be punished by a pecuniary fine of two hundred to five hundred Lebanese pounds and by imprisonment from one month to three months, or by either of these two penalties, and the vehicle shall be impounded until the violation is removed. In the event of recidivism, the two penalties mentioned above shall be doubled and the offender shall be deprived of the right to drive land vehicles for a period of six months.

Shall be punished by imprisonment for a period not exceeding six months and by a fine of not less than one thousand pounds and not more than two thousand pounds, or by either of these two penalties, whoever concludes compulsory insurance transactions contrary to the conditions and models prescribed in accordance with the procedures set forth in this Legislative Decree.

In addition to the implementing decrees and decisions provided for in other articles of this Legislative Decree, there shall be determined.

First - By a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior and the Minister of Economy and Trade, after consulting the opinion of the National Insurance Council:

- The other types of private sector vehicles and the public sector vehicles which may be covered by compulsory insurance, and the procedures and conditions for granting and withdrawing circulation permits of all types in implementation of the provisions of this Legislative Decree and the manner of proving the conclusion of the insurance contracts pertaining thereto, and all administrative and financial regulations relating to the formation of the organs of the National Compulsory Insurance Institution, the powers of such organs, and the methods of financing and operating them.

Second - The details of application of each of the ninth, tenth, eleventh and thirteenth Articles of this Legislative Decree shall be determined by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Economy and Trade and after consulting the opinion of the National Insurance Council.

Third - The details of application of the remaining provisions of this Legislative Decree by joint decisions issued by the Ministers of Economy and Trade and of Interior after consulting the opinion of the National Insurance Council.

Implementing decree for this Article

The date of entry into force of compulsory insurance shall be appointed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Interior and of Economy and Trade, after consulting the opinion of the National Insurance Council

Implementing decree for this Article
Subject to the provisions of the twentieth and twenty-first Articles, this Legislative Decree shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Subject to the reservation of the legal rights belonging to third parties, the immovable private property belonging to the State comprises the built and unbuilt real properties and the immovable real rights which belong to the State pursuant to the laws, decisions and statutes in force, whether they are at its actual disposal or at the disposal of other persons.

The private property belonging to the State comprises in particular the following:

1- Amiri lands (in which the bare ownership belongs to the State).

2 - Metruke lands which are called murfaqa (lands placed at the disposal of communities).

3 - Real properties registered up to this day in the registers of escheats (mahlulat) (vacant properties without an owner or which have no heir).

4 - Properties recorded in the name of the Treasury in the registers of the public administrations.

5 - Transferred (mudawwara) properties (properties attached by the Treasury).

6 - Properties recorded in the registers of the Department of State Property.

7 - Real properties which are proved to belong to the State after carrying out the operations of identification and demarcation the formalities of which are appointed below.

8 - Properties which the State purchases and which do not form part of the public property.

9 - Parcels abandoned from the public property.

10 - Real properties deriving from vacant estates and from estates having no heir, and properties deriving from the neglect of their cultivation and the vacancy or absence of an heir of which is legally established.

11 - Empty lands, woodlands, forests and uncultivated mountains and, in general, all immovable properties which are comprised in the Land Law by the term "dead lands" (aradi mawat), subject to the reservation of the real rights or rights of use which individuals have acquired in accordance with the laws and statutes in force.

The partition of Amiri lands, Metruke lands which are called murfaqa, empty lands and dead (mawat) lands which have not yet been identified and demarcated, and the assignment and sale thereof, shall remain subject to the provisions of the Land Law.

The property of the State shall be subject to the Administration of State Property immediately after its identification, demarcation and registration in the registers of the Department of State Property and in the registers of the Defterhane or the Land Registers.

In the cadastral regions where the operations of census and demarcation are now taking place, the Census and Demarcation Commission shall carry out the works of identifying the property of the State and demarcating it in accordance with the provisions of the Census and Demarcation Decision.
In the remaining regions, the works of identification and demarcation shall be carried out by commissions constituted specially for this purpose.

Each one of the commissions referred to in the sixth Article shall be constituted of the Qaimقام and the locality as president, and an elected member of the Administrative Council, small, medium or large, in every Qada and in every Nahiya having regard to the fertility of the land and its nature in a decision of the Director of Cadastral Services and State Property after taking the opinion of a commission constituted in accordance with the provisions of Article 28 of this Decision.

A decision shall be issued by the Minister or Director of Finance upon the request of the Administration of State Property in which there shall be appointed for each real property the date of the opening of the works.

There shall be mentioned in this decision, by way of instructions only, the name or names by which the real property is known, its situation, its boundaries, the adjoining owners thereto, the lands situated in the middle thereof, and the rights of use or other rights the existence of both of which appears.

Notice of these provisions shall be given to the inhabitants at least one month beforehand by means of their publication in the Official Gazette and in three local newspapers.

The local administrative authority shall summon, through the Mukhtars, the adjoining owners and in general all claimants to any right to attend on the appointed day the demarcation and the placing of boundary marks inter partes.

Starting from this publication and until the date of the issuance of the decision of the Commission, the Land Offices are prohibited from accepting any transaction whatsoever concerning a real property situated in the region subject to demarcation.

If the interested party does not submit a certificate of non-opposition given by the Administration of State Property, every transaction carried out and recorded in the land books in contravention of the provisions mentioned above shall be null by operation of law even as between the two parties.

On the appointed day, the Commission shall proceed with the demarcation of the real property and the placing of its boundary marks (tahrimuhu) inter partes through the surveying engineer in the presence of the Mukhtars, the adjoining owners and the claimants to rights, or in their absence.

Aproces-verbal of all this shall be drawn up, which shall be closed with the signature of the president of the Commission and its members, the engineer, the adjoining owners, the interveners in the matter and the claimants to rights who are present, and if there is any dispute concerning the boundaries or a claim to a right, that shall be mentioned in the proces-verbal; the engineer shall in addition thereto draw up a plan of the real property.

The proces-verbal, after the plan of the real property has been attached thereto, shall be deposited after the termination of the operations upon the termination of the operations with the Qaimقام of the locality.

This deposit shall be announced in the Official Gazette in the State and published in the manner appointed in the ninth Article above.

The proces-verbal shall be placed at the disposal of the interested parties.

Every person claiming any right must, during the two months which follow the date of the publication in the Official Gazette, intervene in the proceedings by way of opposition; the opposition or claim to any right shall be submitted as an official or oral declaration.

There must be mentioned in the declaration the subject-matter of the opposition and the means of proving it; oral declarations shall be accepted in the form of a proces-verbal drawn up by the authority which hears them; the authorities mentioned in Article 21 of the Decision on the Demarcation of Real Properties shall receive declarations and shall forward the declarations or the proces-verbaux drawn up pursuant thereto immediately to the Qaimقام of the locality, and they shall be added to the proces-verbal of the Commission.

If the period appointed in the preceding Article expires and no opposition whatsoever has been submitted, the proces-verbal of the Commission for the Demarcation of State Property shall be homologated in a decision of the Minister of Finance, and there shall be determined therein the physical consistence of the demarcated real property and its legal status; if oppositions are submitted, the Permanent Liberation Commission in the region shall adjudicate thereon within the conditions and according to the rules appointed in the provisions of Articles 24 to Article 34 inclusive of the Decision on the Liberation and Demarcation of Immovable Property.

The real property shall be registered in the administrative registers of State Property and in the Land Register in the cadastral region either in accordance with the instructions of the proces-verbal and the homologation decision in the cases provided for in the first paragraph of Article 14 mentioned above, or in accordance with the decision of execution issued in accordance with the provisions of Articles 24 to 34 inclusive of the Decision on the Liberation and Demarcation of Immovable Property.

The provisions of Articles 37 to 42 inclusive and Article 44 of the Decision on the Liberation and Demarcation of Immovable Property shall apply to the rights of haqq al-qarar, tapu, mithl, etc. - which third parties have acquired in accordance with the legal provisions in force over the real properties of the State prior to the identification of the real property.

No one shall have the right in the future (al-mustaqill) to till, plough or plant land belonging to the State subject to the administration of the Department of State Property without a licence to him therefor.

In the interest of social or public utility, the repurchase of passive rights (servitudes) in force over the real properties of the State may be renewed (effected).

A decision for this purchase shall be issued by the Head of the State, which he shall take upon the proposal of the Director of Cadastral Services and State Property after taking the opinion of the head of the departments concerned (Agriculture - and Public Works - etc.); the valuation of the passive rights shall be carried out by two officials, one of them from the Administration of State Property and the second from the Administration of Agriculture. If the prices which the State offers are accepted, an instrument of mutual undertaking shall be drawn up in the administrative form, and if the rights are recorded in the registers of the Defterhane or in the Land Register, the striking out (amendment) of the entries and deeds shall take place in accordance with the instrument mentioned above.

And if the price offered is refused, the sum shall be deposited in the State Bank in the name of the interested parties; these latter shall be granted, under penalty of forfeiture of their rights, a period of two years to institute an action against the Department of State Property before the ordinary court, which shall adjudicate upon the matter without opposition or recourse.

The supervision and administration of the private immovable property of the State as limited in the First Article of this Decision, with the exception of forests, shall be entrusted to the Administration of Land Registry Services and State Property placed under the authority of the Minister of Finance. Where an immovable property of State property is allocated to a public department, such department shall ensure the administration of that immovable property.

The immovable properties of State property shall be returned to the State Property Department immediately after the revocation of their use for the allocation provided for.

The Director of Land Registry Services and State Property shall represent the private immovable property of the State as defined above in all legal actions in defence thereof before the courts and in all acts of cognizance, purchase, sale, exchange, agreement by mutual consent and other operations designed either to expand or to diminish the rights of the State, as well as in all acts of assignment or allocation to public departments or to collectivities.

The Financial Services shall ensure the collection of the sale price of immovable properties, the differences in shares of exchanges, settlements, leases and, in general, all produce and revenues arising from the properties of the Land Registry Services after examining a copy or duplicate of the collection voucher certified by the Director of Land Registry Services and State Property. Collection shall take place in accordance with the rules prescribed for the collection of the real estate tax.

Deeds relating to State property shall be drawn up in administrative form. Deeds of purchase, sale, exchange and settlement shall be subject to the approval of the Minister of Finance in the State where they involve an amount exceeding one thousand Syrian pounds, as well as a concession granted to collectivities; where the amount exceeds 3000 Syrian pounds, they shall be subject to the approval of the Head of State. Deeds of allocation to a public department shall be drawn up after agreement between the Minister or Director of Finance and the Minister of the department to which the immovable property is allocated.

It shall not be mandatory to appoint attorneys in legal actions relating to State property, and the Administration of Land Registry Services and State Property may be legally and validly represented by one of its officials.

The agricultural lands of State property must be divided and parcelled into lots to serve as a basis for agricultural ownership outside towns. As for the lands that are parcelled into lots, they must be leased with a promise of sale thereof or leased for a long term, and if there is no one to lease them, they may be leased for a term equal to twice the period of agricultural rotation in each region.
Agricultural lands of medium or small cultivation may alone, to the exclusion of others, be leased with a promise of sale thereof.
Leasing with a promise of sale may only be made to farmers.

A farmer who holds an immovable property of the State and who cultivates lands of a village belonging to the State in common cultivation shall enjoy priority over others.

He shall have the right to obtain, by way of lease with a promise of sale, the lands of the village among them in proportion to his rights as determined in accordance with local customs. In this case, the interested parties must, in addition to fulfilling the obligations incumbent upon every purchaser of State lands, parcel and partition among themselves the land cultivated in common within the two months following the date of the lease deed according to the rules prescribed in Decision No. 171 issued on 10 March of the year 1926.

Leases with a promise of sale shall be concluded by mutual consent prior to the opening of the agricultural year in accordance with the provisions of this Decision and pursuant to the general conditions prescribed in the Decision of the Minister of Finance approving the book of conditions drawn up after taking the opinion of the Agricultural Services. The special conditions relating to lease contracts shall be determined for each district by an official from the Department of Agriculture and an official from the Land Registry and State Property Services in the capacity of members.

Lessees must cultivate the lands themselves during the term of the lease, and they may not sublease among themselves or assign their right to the lease without a written authorization from the Administration.

Current lessees of agricultural lands of small cultivation shall enjoy a right of priority over others in cultivating the land which they cultivate with a promise of sale in the following cases:

1 - If they have been lessees for a period exceeding three years.

2 - If they have made improvements to the immovable property.

3 - If they have established plantations or constructions thereon.

4 - If they have conducted new agricultural experiments or used new methods, or perfected agricultural machinery.

The area of lands of cultivation shall be determined. Plots of land of small cultivation shall in all cases be leased by mutual consent and priority shall be given to leasing them to farmers. Plots of land of medium or large cultivation shall be leased by public auction.

The lease rent shall be calculated at the rate of 3 per mille of the sale price. Sale prices shall be fixed as capital and may be divided into fifteen instalments at most. The annual instalments shall be without interest. Each annual instalment shall fall due at the same time as the lease rent falls due.

The sale price for each lot of the agricultural lots shall be fixed by the Minister of Finance upon the proposal of the Director of Land Registry and State Property Services after taking the opinion of the committee provided for in Article 28 of this Decision.

Purchasers shall be granted a discount of 10 per cent on the unmatured annual instalments in the following cases:

1 - If they pay the sale price in cash.

2 - If they pay in a single lump sum the amount of the remaining instalments.

In addition thereto, a discount may be granted by a decision of the Minister of Finance taken upon the proposal of the Director of Land Registry and State Property Services and after taking the opinion of the committee provided for in Article 28 of this Decision, to every purchaser who has fulfilled, prior to the expiry of the period prescribed in the book of conditions, the conditions required of him or who is found to be in one of the cases provided for in paragraphs No. 2, 3 and 4 of Article 3 above, provided there is no provision in the book of conditions regarding the works he has carried out.

It may be stipulated in the lease deed containing the promise of sale that the purchaser is prohibited, after the realization of the promise of sale and for a specified period and under penalty of forfeiture of his right, from making the slightest disposition of the immovable property without authorization from the Director of Land Registry and State Property Services. In this case, and during the period specified in the lease deed, no real estate transaction whatsoever may be carried out in respect of the immovable property unless the notice or application to carry out the transaction includes an authorization from the Director of Land Registry and State Property Services.

Plots of agricultural land leased with a promise of their sale may be declared, in whole or in part, to be unseizable in a special article of the deed.

This shall be recorded in the Land Register at the same time as the right of ownership is registered in the name of the purchaser.
The term of the lease shall be 15 years, provided that it may terminate before its term within the conditions provided for below.
A lease deed concluded with a promise of sale shall terminate if the lessee obtains, prior to the expiry of the term of the lease, the right of ownership or if his rights are forfeited.

The lessee shall become a holder after verification that he has fulfilled the obligations mentioned in the lease deed and in the book of conditions and after he has paid the value of the fixed price in full.

If the lessee fails to fulfil the obligations imposed upon him within the period granted to him, but has begun cultivating his plot and has presented actual reasons that prevented him from cultivating the land in full, the Director of Land Registry and State Property Services may withhold from him a new period equal to the first period; if the matter is otherwise, forfeiture of his rights may be pronounced after three months from serving him with a formal notice notified in administrative form. The rights of a lessee who has assigned his rights to another person without authorization from the Director of Land Registry and State Property Services shall be forfeited by operation of law. The pronouncement of forfeiture of rights shall be issued in a reasoned decision by the Minister or Director of Finance after a formal notice sent to the lessee in administrative form one month prior to the issuance of the pronouncement of issuance. This decision shall not be subject to any recourse whatsoever.

With effect from the date of the decision of forfeiture, the real property shall revert to the State Domain free of any encumbrance, lease, or rights in rem that the lessee may have granted or created.

The value paid of the price shall be refunded to the lessee whose rights have been forfeited, subject to the deduction of the expenses paid and interest at the rate of 5 per cent of the amount of the unpaid annual instalments, and the payments made by the lessee shall be included in this calculation.

If there are plantings or constructions erected by the lessee, the Domain Department shall pay the value thereof.

Leases shall be concluded prior to the opening of the agricultural year and under the conditions specified in a decision approving a book of conditions drawn up through the efforts of the Director of the Land Registry and Domain Services and after taking the opinion of the Agricultural Services. The rental values or the opening bidding price shall be determined by experts from the Administration. Applicants must prove their ability to pay.

If the lease is concluded by mutual agreement and if many acceptable applications are submitted for a single plot of land, priority shall be given to the former lessee if he is among the applicants and if he had exploited the real property.

Otherwise, priority shall be given to applicants residing in the village if they exploit the land themselves, and if competition arises among them, the real properties shall be leased by way of the village and a higher local officer from the Land Registry Services and State Domain as members, and a surveyor engineer attached to the committee shall perform the function of clerk.
Lessees must exploit the land themselves and they may not sublease or assign their rights to other persons without a licence from the Director of the Land Registry and Domain Services.

The rights of the lessee may be forfeited in the following cases:

1 - If he fails to fulfil the clauses and conditions mentioned in the book of conditions.

2 - If he subleases or assigns his right to the lease without a licence from the Director of the Land Registry and Domain Services.

3 - If he fails to pay the specified price at the agreed time. Forfeiture shall be pronounced by a decision of the Minister of Finance in the form specified in Article 41 of this Decision.
Free grazing of livestock is prohibited in all lands subject to the State Domain.

Every lessee shall have the right to graze, in free grazing lands, the animals proven to be necessary for the exploitation of his lands; however, with respect to animals in excess of the livestock of exploitation, fees calculated per head thereof shall be paid thereon.

If the condition of the pastures is favourable and those who raise livestock therein are satisfied, non-lessees may be licensed to graze their herds on the lands designated for this purpose, provided that they submit a declaration to that effect to the Domain Officer and pay the specified fee in advance.
The rate of the fees payable for grazing shall be determined in a decision of the Minister of Finance after taking the opinion of the committee provided for in Article 28 of this Decision.

A licence may be granted, under the conditions provided for in the laws in force and after payment of a fee therefor, for cutting firewood, opening stone and sand quarries and exploiting them, etc., making charcoal kilns and tar factories, and exploiting all kinds of minor produce belonging to the State Domain. The lessee shall have the right of usufruct of such minor produce under the conditions specified in the statutes, decisions, and laws in force.

The rate of the fees payable for licences pursuant to the above Article and the manner of granting licences relating to these various purposes shall be determined by a decision of the Director of the Land Registry and Domain Services.

Works carried out on the State Domain in violation of the provisions of this Decision and of the decisions taken for its implementation shall be subject to the following pecuniary penalties upon the request of the Administration, without prejudice, where necessary, to the application of the penalties provided for in the statutes and laws in force and the imposition of civil damages.

First - If anyone occupies land without a licence, he shall pay the rental value.

Second - If he plants trees without a licence, he shall pay one Syrian pound for each hectare or fraction of a hectare.

Third - If he grazes his livestock without paying the specified fee, he shall pay double this fee.

Fourth - If he builds a dwelling or other unlicensed constructions outside the lots partitioned by the Administration, he shall pay 5 Syrian pounds as a pecuniary penalty.

Fifth - If he damages water control constructions or their channels, he shall pay 5 Syrian pounds as a pecuniary penalty.

Sixth - If he cuts firewood or extracts any minor produce without a licence, he shall pay double the fee specified therefor.

Seventh - If he clandestinely makes charcoal or tar, he shall pay double the fee specified therefor.
If the offence is repeated within a period of one year, the penalty shall be doubled and offenders may be sentenced to imprisonment from one day to five days.

Domain officers, officials, forestry officers, officers of the Land Registry Administrations, police officers, gendarmes, and other officers who have the right to draw up offence reports may investigate contraventions committed on the State Domain, whether they are contraventions relating to this Decision or contraventions provided for in the statutes and decisions relating to the Domain regime.

Contraventions provided for in this Decision shall be established by offence reports and proven by witnesses in the absence of offence reports or in the event of insufficiency of such reports. Offence reports shall constitute probative evidence of the material facts established therein until the contrary is proven. If the offender is not present at the time of writing the report, that shall be mentioned in the report. None of the aforementioned formalities is prescribed on pain of nullity.

The officers of the Domain Department shall serve all documents relating to the prosecution of the offence report by registered letters with request for acknowledgment of receipt, and they are authorised to prosecute actions before the courts. The investigation, whether in first instance or on appeal, shall be conducted orally without the presence of legal counsel. The judgment shall be enforced in the form specified in the law. The sentence of imprisonment shall be enforced in accordance with the provisions of the laws in force.

Actions claiming compensation in contraventions relating to the Domain shall lapse by prescription upon the full expiry of the periods mentioned below:

If an offence report was drawn up, after the lapse of two months from the date of closing the offence report; and if no offence report was drawn up, and save for cases of encroachment upon the State Domain, after the lapse of six months in all other contraventions.

The Domain Administration is authorised to settle matters by compromise in the contraventions provided for in this Decision.

If judgment has been rendered, compromise may only take place with respect to sentences of pecuniary penalties.

The private property of the State may be leased through a public auction organised in accordance with the Public Procurement Law and on the basis of special specifications drawn up by the Minister of Finance and the competent Minister.

Leasing shall take place and for periods not exceeding a maximum of four years, renewable once, in respect of built real properties and unbuilt real properties where the lease contract does not include the erection of constructions thereon and is limited to ordinary maintenance and exploitation, and nine years, renewable once, in respect of unbuilt real properties where the lease contract includes capital maintenance works and exploitation whose value exceeds the rent of two years.

Provided that a feasibility study for the project is submitted and approved by both the Minister of Finance and the competent Minister, and that the Directorate of Roads and Buildings at the Ministry of Public Works and Transport supervises the proper execution.

Ownership of these constructions shall pass to the Lebanese State upon the expiry of the term of the lease or the forfeiture of the lessee's right due to his breach of the conditions of the lease, without any sum or compensation being due from the State in return for its acquisition of ownership of these constructions.

Save in the cases where real properties are leased to a person of public law, leasing shall take place exclusively by public open auction.

If the rent is not paid when it falls due or the other encumbrances and conditions of leasing are not performed, the Minister of Finance may, upon the proposal of the competent Minister, rescind the contract if he does not deem it preferable to pursue the execution of the contract by all legal means.
The places designated in a decision of the Head of State upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance after taking the opinion of the two Departments of Agriculture and Public Works.

If the allotment is carried out on lands belonging to the State situated outside the boundaries of village lands, the lots must be distributed among the nearest neighbouring villages. If the allotment is the establishment of a new village, a special allotment must be carried out for the lands prepared for the construction of dwelling houses.

In these cases, the lots must comprise an agricultural plot situated within the boundaries of the lands of the new village and a plot of land for construction situated within the boundaries of the special allotment.
The engineer of the Land Registry Departments shall carry out the allotment upon taking cognisance of the decision provided for in Article 61.
The sale of the lots must be preceded by a notice in the Official Gazette and in three local newspapers. The sale shall be conducted in accordance with the following manner.

Agricultural lots of small exploitation shall in all cases be sold by mutual agreement at a price designated for each lot by the Minister of Finance after taking the opinion of the committee provided for in Article 28 of this Decision. As for agricultural lots of medium exploitation, they shall be sold by public auction, and if there is no purchaser, they shall be sold by mutual agreement.

The sale prices designated as capital may be divided into ten annual instalments at most. No interest shall be charged on the annual instalments. A deduction of 10 per cent of the value of the unmatured annual instalments shall be granted to the purchaser if he pays the purchase price in cash or pays the total value of the instalments remaining due from him.

The granting of lots of small exploitation shall be made to the persons who submitted their application within the period designated for the sale operations. The committee provided for in Article 28 of this Decision shall examine the applications and rank them in order, after taking the opinion of the local administrative authorities. Preference in the ranking of applications shall be given to farmers, and if numerous persons apply for the same plot and it is established that they have equal rights, the plot shall be granted by way of drawing lots among them.

It may be stated in the contract that the purchaser is prohibited during a limited period from selling, with or without a price, and from mortgaging or encumbering his lot with a security without a licence from the Director of the Land Registry and State Property Departments.

Every instrument concluded contrary to these provisions shall be null and void and shall have no effect. If the real property is registered in the Tapu registers or in the Land Registers, no transaction of sale, mortgage or security may be effected in respect thereof during the period provided for in the contract unless the title deed includes the licence of the Director of the Land Registry and State Property Departments.

In addition to that, it may be stated in the contract that within a designated period there must be either exploitation within the specified conditions if the matter relates to an agricultural plot, or the erection of a building suited to the importance of the location of the real property, the value of which is designated in the instrument of sale, and the fencing of the land within the conditions designated in the said contract if the matter relates to another plot.

The lots which are sold may be declared unseizable pursuant to a clause of the instrument of sale, provided that this clause relating to unseizability shall not prevent the seizure of crops for the payment of sums due to the State, municipalities, public services, financial companies or provident companies and their branches, as well as cooperative associations or agricultural companies of whatever kind that are legally ratified and in which the purchaser is a member.

If the obligations are not fulfilled upon the expiry of the designated period, this period may be extended by the Minister of Finance for a period equal to the period initially designated, if the person who was granted the lot has commenced its exploitation and proves that substantial reasons have prevented him from achieving its exploitation, with the forfeiture of his rights in the form designated in Article 41 of this Decision.

If the real property is registered in registers or in the Land Registers and there are creditors whose names are registered, they shall be notified of the decision of forfeiture in the administrative form at their elected domicile, and the decision of forfeiture shall be entered in the Tapu registers or on the folio of the real property.

From the date of the decision of forfeiture, the State shall recover the land and return to the purchaser the price he has paid after deducting the expenses and the interest due on the annual instalments unpaid when they fell due.

If there are plantations or buildings created by the purchaser, the State Property Department may offer him to pay or sell the plot within the conditions designated below.

Until the expiry of the period during which the purchaser must neither sell, nor mortgage, nor encumber with a security, and no lot of the State property lots may be sold save in the administrative form through the care of the State Property Department and by way of public auction. Only persons possessing the qualifications required of the original purchasers shall be admitted to the auction.

The purchaser whose rights have been forfeited shall not be entitled to participate in the auction.

The auction price which is stated to be payable in cash must be paid within one month to the fund of the accountant designated for this purpose. The price shall be distributed in the following order:

1 - The expenses of the proceedings for forfeiture of rights and offering for sale.

2 - The remaining instalments due to the State, increased by the interest on the overdue instalments.

3 - The debts arising from mortgages registered or of which the Directorate of the Land Registry and State Property Departments has been legally notified.

4 - The instalments which the purchaser has paid, after deducting the rental value calculated in accordance with the instructions above.

5 - The expenses spent out of the purchaser's own funds on the lands.

Neither the creditors nor the purchaser, as regards the expenses he spent out of his own funds, shall have a right in the distribution of the price of the land save in proportion to the value of the real property improvements designated by an administrative inspection committee. Whatever exceeds that of the price shall be taken by the State Property Directorate. The sums accruing to the persons shall be deposited under their responsibility in the State Bank until the settlement of accounts among the interested parties.

If the auction does not succeed, the State shall not be liable to pay the slightest compensation whatsoever by reason of the improvements which the holder of the forfeited lot and his rights may have created in the real property; likewise the creditors shall not be entitled to bring any action whatsoever against the State to obtain recovery of their debts. The instalments which the purchaser has paid shall be returned to him after deducting the overdue interest, and the real property shall revert to the State property free of every encumbrance or real right.

Private State property shall be sold by way of public auction in accordance with the rules provided for in the Public Accounting Law, on the basis of an appraisal established by a committee of experts.

An exchange may be effected in respect of State real properties, provided that the exchange transaction shall be preceded by an inspection by a committee of experts to verify that the State has an interest in effecting the exchange.

The contract of exchange shall not become valid until after its ratification by a decree.

Real properties that are "transferred" (devolved to the State) or attached against guarantees and the like may be returned to their former owners at a price determined by a committee of experts. In the event that they abstain, they shall be sold by way of public auction.

Decommissioned roads and paths or sections thereof, and remnants of real properties that are unfit for use except after being annexed to contiguous real properties, and decommissioned canals and remnants thereof, shall be sold by mutual agreement to the owners of contiguous real properties at the prescribed price, their sale shall take place by way of public auction among the owners of the contiguous real properties, or they shall be assigned by way of exchange to the owners of the real properties in which sections of new roads or paths are opened.

Surface rights belonging to the State shall also be sold by mutual agreement to the owners of the real properties within which such rights are situated, at the price determined by a committee of experts, and in the event that they abstain from purchasing, the said rights shall be sold by way of public auction.

The price of the real properties sold in accordance with the provisions of the preceding Article 79 may be collected in annual instalments, provided that the period of payment by instalments does not exceed ten years, and ten per cent (10%) shall be discounted for purchasers if the price is paid in cash, and ten per cent shall likewise be discounted on each instalment paid within a time limit of at least one year prior to its maturity.

If the purchaser delays in paying the instalments due on their specified maturity dates, the Administration shall have the right either to forfeit his right to registration without his having the right to claim the refund of the amounts paid, subject to serving him with prior formal notice and granting him a time limit of one month to pay what is due, or to pursue the enforcement of the terms of the contract of sale by all means of execution.

Sold properties shall not be registered in the name of the purchaser until after full payment of the price.

In each Governorate, the committees of experts provided for in Articles 77, 78 and 79 shall be constituted as follows:

- The Head of Finance .... Chairman.

- The Head of the Auxiliary Land Registry Office in the cadastral area in which the real property is situated ..... Member.

- A civil engineer appointed by a decision of the Minister of Public Works and Transport, Member.

If the sale concerns a built real property, or an agricultural engineer appointed by a decision of the Minister of Agriculture if the sale concerns an unbuilt real property, Member.
The details for the application of this Decision shall be determined in a special decision.
All provisions contrary to this Decision are repealed and shall remain repealed.
This Decision shall be put into execution in all the territories of the State of Syria.

The Secretary-General and the Delegate Extraordinary of the High Commissioner to the States of Syria and Jabal al-Druze, or the Delegates to the States, are charged, each in so far as he is concerned, with the execution of this Decision.

The General Master Plan in the two areas of Bikfaya-Mhaidseh and Sakiet El Misk-Bhersaf (District of Metn-Governorate of Mount Lebanon) relating to zoning as shown on Map No. 1 drawn at a scale of 1/5000, the detailed alignments coloured in yellow, the setback zones appurtenant thereto coloured in green, and the locations of the gardens as shown on the Maps numbered from (2) to (10) drawn at a scale of 1/5000 and 1/1000 and attached to this Decree, is hereby approved. This Plan shall be subject to the regulations on building, subdivision, land pooling and reparcelling, exploitation, and the general and special conditions annexed to this Decree, which shall be deemed an integral part thereof.

In the event of any ambiguity or discrepancy between the alignments shown on the map drawn at a scale of 1/5000 and the alignments shown on the maps drawn at a scale of 1/1000, the maps of the larger scale shall prevail.
All previous alignments and master and detailed plans contrary to this Plan and all regulations inconsistent with the regulations annexed to this Decree are hereby repealed.
This Decree shall be published and notified wherever needed.

Article 1:

Immovable properties are of three categories:

Immovable properties by nature are corporeal things which by their essence have a fixed and non-movable site, such as lands, mines, plants rooted in the land (so long as they remain fixed therein), and buildings.

The word (buildings) does not mean only constructions known as such (such as dwelling houses, shops, factories, warehouses, granaries....etc.) without also technical constructions of all kinds (such as bridges, wells, ovens, dams, barriers, tunnels...etc.) and, more generally, everything assembled from building materials and fastened together in a fixed manner, whether on the surface of the land or beneath it.

Included among immovable properties by nature are all apparatus, parts... etc. incorporated into the building and intended to complete it, such as balconies, gutters, lightning rods (for preventing lightning strikes) (and water supply pipes).

Immovable properties by destination are things which in themselves are considered movables, yet are appurtenant to the immovable property itself; in all cases, for them to be reckoned among immovable properties, it is required:

1- That they and the immovable property itself belong to a single owner.

2- That they be allocated to the exploitation of the immovable property or, more generally, to the benefit of the immovable property to which these things are appurtenant. Among these things are:

1= With respect to agricultural exploitation:

Animals intended for agriculture, agricultural implements, presses, pipes, and large casks used for placing grapes in wine factories, fish in ponds, beehives, silkworms in spinning sheds, manure and straw intended for fertilising the land, and vine stakes.

2= And with respect to industrial exploitation: Stores, places of entertainment (casinos), bathing establishments, and commercial premises may not be considered as immovable properties; and among the things also considered as immovable properties are movable things permanently attached to the land.
Incorporeal immovable properties are real rights, hypothecs, and servitudes, as well as actions brought before the courts in respect of immovable properties by nature.

Mulk immovable properties are immovable properties situated within the zones of built-up areas as they (that is, the zones) are administratively delimited and which are capable of absolute ownership, with the exception of immovable properties standing on the occupied lands of the former Government of Mount Lebanon, which remain subject to the rules of local custom and usage
Amiri immovable properties = are immovable properties the "bare ownership" of which belongs to the State and over which a right of "tessarouf" may be exercised.

1- Metrouke murfaqa immovable properties are immovable properties which belong to the State and over which a community has a right of use the characteristics and extent of which are defined by local customs by administrative regulations

2- The immovable properties referred to in the preceding paragraph are considered private property of the municipality if they fall within its boundaries.

The municipal authorities may abolish or modify the right of use over some parts of the said immovable properties while preserving the rights of third parties.

Paragraph added pursuant to Law 173 /2000 (Budget)

3- Municipalities are prohibited from selling or disposing of the properties referred to in the second paragraph except after the approval of the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Finance and of Municipal and Rural Affairs.
Metrouke mahmiya immovable properties = are immovable properties which belong to the State or the municipalities and form part of the public domain of the State

Vacant permissible immovable properties or dead (mewat) lands = are Amiri lands which belong to the State, save that they are neither assigned nor delimited, and whoever occupies them first may, by permission from the State, obtain a right of preference within the conditions prescribed in the regulations of the State domain.

The following real rights may subsist over immovable properties:

1- The right of ownership.

2- The right of tessarouf.

3- The right of superficies.

4- The right of usufruct.

5- The right of preference over vacant permissible lands.

6- Real servitudes.

7- Rights of pledge: antichresis and sale with right of redemption (vente à réméré).

8- Privileges and hypothecs.

9- The right of waqf.

10- The right of ijaretein.

11- The right of long lease (ijara tawila).

12- The right of option resulting from a promise of sale.

Immovable ownership is the right to use, enjoy, and dispose of an immovable property within the limits of the laws, decrees, and regulations, and this right applies only to Mulk immovable properties..

Ownership of an immovable property confers upon its holder the right to all that this immovable property produces and to all that unites with it by accession, whether such union is natural or artificial.

Ownership the land comprises ownership of what is above it and what is below it; accordingly, the owner of the land may plant therein whatever plantings he wishes, build whatever buildings he wishes, make excavations therein to whatever depth he wishes, and extract from such excavations all that they may yield, within the restrictions resulting from the laws, decrees, and regulations.

Tessarouf is the right to use, enjoy, and dispose of an immovable property within the conditions prescribed in the provisions of this Decree and within the limits of the laws, decrees, and regulations.

This right applies only to Amiri immovable properties.
Tessarouf over an immovable property confers upon its holder the right to all that this immovable property yields in all that unites with it by accession, whether such union is natural or artificial.

The holder of the right of tessarouf over lands is entitled to plant therein whatever plantings he wishes, build whatever buildings he wishes, make excavations therein to whatever depth he wishes, and extract from such excavations whatever building materials he wishes and dispose of them with full freedom, to the exclusion of all other products, all of this within the restrictions resulting from the laws, decrees, and regulations.
The holder of the right of tessarouf over an immovable property may perform thereon whatever acts of disposition he wishes, except waqf.
Every waqf established after the promulgation of this Decree over Amiri land is considered null and void and as if it had never been.
The right of tessarouf lapses by failure to cultivate the land or by failure to use it for a period of five years.

No co-owner in an immovable property may, without the consent of all the remaining co-owners, exercise his rights over the whole of the immovable property or over a specific part thereof, nor may he exercise any right whatsoever over the share of his co-owner in the immovable property without permission from that co-owner.

The permission of an absent co-owner is always presumed to be obtained in acts relating to the management and administration of the immovable property, unless damage to the absent co-owner results therefrom amounting to at least one-fifth of his right; and this does not prevent the application of the provisions of Decrees Nos. 188 and 189 relating to the establishment of the Land Register.

The co-owners shall determine by agreement among themselves the manner of enjoying the common immovable property, and the division of the yield of the immovable property shall take place in proportion to the common rights unless there is an agreement to the contrary.

Every co-owner in an immovable property is bound to pay his share, in proportion to his quota, of the expenses of administration, repair, and preservation, and his share of the taxes and charges levied upon the common property; and the co-owner who has paid the whole or a part of the aforementioned expenses is entitled to recover them, unless these expenses were incurred solely for the improvement or embellishment of the immovable property, in which case they remain at the expense of the one who incurred them.

Every co-owner in the immovable property disposes with full freedom of his rights in this immovable property, and he may, without permission from his co-owners, assign them to another person or create a hypothec over them, provided that he may not contract an antichresis over his share.
The right of superficies is the right of the owner of buildings, constructions, or plantings standing on land belonging to another person.

The right of superficies may be sold and a hypothec may be created over it. Real servitudes may be established over the property subject to the right of superficies, provided that this is only within the limits compatible with the exercise of the right of superficies.

The right of superficies shall lapse:

1- By its merger with the right of ownership of the land in the same owners and in the same proportions of ownership.

2- By the destruction of the buildings or structures, or by the destruction or disappearance of the plantings, which are the subject-matter of this right. Buildings or structures which have become unfit for the use for which they were intended shall be deemed demolished or destroyed, and their owner shall not be permitted to rebuild them in order to use them anew, or to replant the plantings after their disappearance in order to revive his lapsed right, nor shall the holder of the right of superficies be permitted to add any new constructions thereon. The right of superficies shall remain confined to the buildings, structures or plantings originally covered by this right.

3- Where it is established that the existence of the right of superficies impedes the exploitation or development of the land or that the benefit expected therefrom is of minor importance such that it is disproportionate to the economic damage caused to the land by reason thereof. The Registrar of the Real Property Register shall strike off ex officio the right of superficies in the case set forth in sub-paragraph (1) of this Article. In the other cases, the lapse of the right of superficies shall be established by a judgment having the force of res judicata on the basis of an action brought by the owner of the land before the Single Civil Judge, who shall apply in the proceedings the procedure followed before the Judge of Urgent Matters. The owner of the land shall be bound to pay to the holder of the right of superficies compensation assessed by the competent court not exceeding three times the value of the buildings, constructions or plantings which are the subject-matter of this right as at the date of bringing the action, in the cases set forth in sub-paragraphs (2) and (3) of this Article.
No right of superficies may be created starting from the date of promulgation of this Resolution.

Usufruct is a real right pertaining to the use and enjoyment of a thing belonging to another, and this right shall necessarily lapse upon the death of the usufructuary.

No right of usufruct may be created in favour of juristic persons.
The right of usufruct arises solely by the will of man, and it may be created for a term or subject to a condition.

In real property matters, a right of usufruct may be created over the following rights:

1= Ownership.

1= And tessarouf.

3= And superficies.

4= And ijaretein.

5= And long lease (emphyteusis).

The usufructuary must, before taking possession of the usufruct:

1= Draw up an inventory of the real properties.

2= Provide a solvent surety.

Provided that he may be exempted from these two obligations in the text of the instrument whereby the right of usufruct is created.

The inventory of the real properties must be drawn up in the presence of the owner thereof or after he has been summoned for that purpose in a legal manner, and it must be executed in the form followed before Notaries Public and its expenses shall be paid by the usufructuary, provided that the usufructuary may agree with the bare owner (on condition that both parties are of age and discerning) to draw up the inventory amicably and without expense.

Where the suretyship is provided late, the fruits gathered by the owner of the real property during such delay shall be restored to the usufructuary.

The suretyship may be replaced by a pledge or a mortgage over property deemed sufficient.

Where the usufructuary provides neither suretyship nor other security, the real properties subject to the usufruct shall be leased out or delivered to a judicial receiver, and the remuneration of such receiver shall be taken from the fruits of the real property.

The usufructuary has the right of use consisting in employing the real property for his own enjoyment and for his personal benefit.

This right shall be as comprehensive as the right of the owner of the real property and shall include the exercise of easements as well as the right of hunting and fowling, unless the owner of the real property has leased out these rights prior to the creation of the right of usufruct.

The usufructuary is entitled to the fruits of the real property, namely the natural or pecuniary revenues yielded by the real property at fixed and regular intervals without such fruits diminishing anything of the substance of the real property (and included in these revenues is the rent from leasing out the right of hunting and fowling).

The produce of open-cast mines, worked mines and quarries, where they belong to the owner of the real property (on condition that the mine or quarry was opened prior to the commencement of the usufruct, and trees, where they are exploited at regular intervals (for the consumption of their firewood or for their sale), shall be assimilated to fruits.

At the commencement of the usufruct and at its termination, the fruits which have not yet been gathered, or what remains thereof ungathered, shall be apportioned between the usufructuary and the owner of the real property in proportion to the time during which the right of usufruct was in existence or not in existence, having regard to the annual or non-annual production period corresponding to the fruits.

Neither the owner of the real property against the usufructuary nor the usufructuary against the owner of the real property shall have any claim for reimbursement of any of the expenses of tillage, but account shall be taken in his favour of the price of the fertilizers and seeds which have been used to prepare the standing crops on the land at the commencement or lapse of the usufruct.

The usufructuary must respect the leases concluded by the owner of the real property prior to the commencement of the usufruct; as for the leases concluded by the usufructuary, they shall cease to be enforceable against the owner of the real property after three years from the lapse of the usufruct.

The usufructuary is entitled to assign his right gratuitously or for consideration unless the instrument creating the usufruct contains provisions to the contrary; after the assignment, the right of usufruct shall remain vested in the person of the assignor, and the assignor of the right of usufruct shall therefore not be released from his obligations towards the bare owner, whereas the usufruct shall lapse upon the death of the assignor and not upon the death of the assignee.

The usufructuary must enjoy the real property as a careful and diligent owner of real property; in particular, he must notify the owner of the real property of any encroachments committed by third parties upon his real property (and if he fails to do so, he shall be liable for the damage which attaches to the owner of the real property), and he must also continue performance under the insurance policies (sikorta) previously concluded and pay the premiums due thereunder.

In his use and enjoyment of the real property, the usufructuary must act in accordance with the practice of the former owners of the real property, particularly with regard to the purpose for which the buildings are intended and the manner of cultivating the lands and exploiting the woods and quarries; however, he may cultivate waste lands or, more generally, improve the method of cultivation.

The various real property taxes, as well as the repairs necessary for the preservation of the real property, shall be borne by the holder of the usufruct; otherwise, major repairs, namely repairs which relate to the renewal of an important part of the real property and entail extraordinary expenses, shall be incumbent upon the bare owner.

Neither the bare owner nor the usufructuary shall be compelled to rebuild what has collapsed due to age or by act of God and force majeure; provided that if the collapse occurs following a catastrophe against which the demolished real property was insured in whole or in part, the compensation paid may, upon the request of the owner of the real property or upon the request of the usufructuary, be used for the rebuilding or repair of the real property.

Where it is necessary to discharge a debt the discharge of which entails a reduction of the capital, the usufructuary must contribute to the payment of the debt by a proportionate reduction of his revenues in the following manner:

1- The owner of the real property must pay the required capital, and the usufructuary must account to him for interest to be paid to him for as long as the usufruct subsists.

2- Provided that the usufructuary is entitled to advance the capital, and in this case the owner of the real property must refund it to him (without payment of interest) upon the termination of the usufruct.

The expenses in the payment of which the bare owner and the usufructuary contribute as mentioned in the preceding Article are:

1- The expenses of major repairs.

2- The extraordinary charges imposed upon the real property during the usufruct (such as special war taxes and compensation paid to concessionaires for the draining of marshes by order of the public authority....etc.).

3- The share attaching to the real properties of an inherited debt, where the right of usufruct runs over all the real properties of the deceased; and in order to determine this share, the value of the real properties enjoyed by the usufructuary shall, where necessary, be assessed in proportion to the value of the entire estate.
The usufructuary shall not, in principle, be liable for a debt secured by a mortgage running over the real property which he enjoys.

The right of usufruct is extinguished upon the expiry of its term, or by the death of the usufructuary, or by the total destruction of the thing subject to the usufruct, or by the renunciation thereof by the usufructuary, or by its revocation for abuse of enjoyment, or by the consolidation of rights, that is, by the union of the capacities of usufructuary and owner of the immovable property in one and the same person. This extinction shall have no judicial effect except after the cancellation of the registration entered in the Land Register.

Where applicable, the right of usufruct is transferred to a right in the indemnity paid by the insurance company or in the indemnity paid as compensation for expropriation for public utility.

Upon the expiry of the term of the usufruct, the usufructuary shall be liable towards the owner of the immovable property for the damage caused to the immovable property through his fault, and he shall not be entitled to the slightest indemnity for the improvements which he has made therein without the consent of its owner; provided that if an improvement and damage have occurred at the same time, set-off shall take place between the one and the other. As for the new constructions which the usufructuary may have erected and the plantations which he may have planted, the provisions of Article 218 of this Resolution shall apply thereto.

If the right of usufruct applies only to a building, and that building is destroyed by fire or another accident, or collapses from age, the usufructuary shall have no right to enjoy either the land or the building materials. The contrary shall hold if the usufructuary was in possession of the entirety of the land of which the building forms part, unless in both aforementioned cases the final provisions mentioned in Article 46 above apply.

Moreover, the forfeiture of the usufructuary's right may be declared judicially upon the application of the bare owner grounded on the abuse of enjoyment by the usufructuary, in particular where he commits waste upon the immovable property or allows the immovable property to deteriorate for want of maintenance. In this case, the creditors of the usufructuary may intervene in the action and may offer to repair the waste committed and to furnish guarantees for the future.

The judge may, according to the gravity of the circumstances and conditions, either pronounce the absolute forfeiture of the usufruct, or order that the immovable property shall not be surrendered to the bare owner except on condition, or that he pay annually to the usufructuary, or to the person to whom the usufructuary's right has passed, a fixed sum until the term appointed for the expiry of the right of usufruct.

If the bare owner sells the immovable property encumbered with the right of usufruct, such sale shall not effect the slightest alteration in the right of the usufructuary, and he shall continue to enjoy his usufruct unless he expressly renounces it.
The creditors of the usufructuary are entitled to have the renunciation of the usufruct annulled if such renunciation prejudices their interests.

An easement is a charge imposed upon a determinate immovable property for the benefit of another determinate immovable property belonging to an owner other than the owner of the first immovable property. This charge consists either in conferring upon another person the right to use part of the immovable property encumbered with the easement, or in depriving the owner of the immovable property of the exercise of part of his right in his immovable property.
Easements arise either from the natural situation of the premises, or from obligations imposed by law, or from agreements concluded between the owners of the immovable properties.

Easements arising from the natural situation of the premises and from obligations imposed by law are exempted from publication and advertisement, by way of exception to the principle laid down in Article 10 of the Resolution relating to land registration. However, if the easement relates to a right of way because the dominant land is enclosed on all sides, the exact locus thereof may be precisely determined upon the application of the owner of the servient land.

(By way of derogation from the principle laid down in Article 10 of the Resolution relating to the Land Register, easements resulting from the natural situation of the premises and from obligations imposed by law are exempted from publication and advertisement; however, the easement relating to the right of way by reason of the enclave of one land within another land may be precisely determined, upon the application of the owner of the servient immovable property.

Lower lands are subject, towards the lands which are higher than them, to receiving the waters which flow naturally therefrom onto them without the hand of man having contributed thereto. The owner of the lower lands may in no case erect a dam to prevent this flow.

Nor may the owner of the higher lands do any act calculated to aggravate the easement upon the lower lands.

Every owner of an immovable property has the right to use and dispose of the rainwater falling on his land; however, if the use of such waters or the direction given to them is such as to aggravate the natural easement of flow mentioned in the preceding Article above, compensation shall be due to the owner of the lower land.

These same provisions shall apply to the waters of springs rising on any land.

If the owner of a land brings waters to the surface on his land by boring or by underground works, the owners of the lower lands must receive them, provided that they shall be entitled to indemnity if the flow thereof causes damage to them.

Houses, courtyards, gardens, orchards and enclosed parks adjoining dwellings shall not be subject, in the cases provided for in the preceding paragraphs, to the slightest aggravation whatsoever of the easement of water flow.
