that selected the members whose membership terminated by drawing lots in accordance with the procedures for appointment provided for in the Law

This article was repealed pursuant to Law 242 dated 22 /10/2012 Official Gazette 45)

The members of the Constitutional Council shall take, before assuming their duties, before the President of the Republic, within a time limit not exceeding fifteen days from the date of completion of their appointment, the following oath:

"I swear by Almighty God to perform my work in the Constitutional Council with all honesty, impartiality and devotion, abiding by the provisions of the Constitution, and to preserve the secrecy of deliberations with absolute care."

After taking the oath, the members of the Constitutional Council shall meet upon convocation by the eldest member or at the request of three of them where necessary, and shall elect from among themselves by secret ballot a President of the Council and a Vice-President for a term of three years, renewable, by an absolute majority of the number of members of the Council in the first round and by a relative majority in the second round, and in the event of an equality of votes, the eldest shall be deemed elected.

The following paragraph was added pursuant to Law 650 dated 4/2/2005 Official Gazette 6

As for the members whose remaining term of office is less than three years, the election of one of them to one of the positions mentioned in the first paragraph shall be for a period that ends ipso jure upon the expiry of his term of office.

Membership of the Constitutional Council may not be combined with a ministry, parliamentary office, any other official body or any public office whatsoever. Nor may a member, before the lapse of two years from the end of his membership, stand as a candidate for membership of the Chamber of Deputies, be elected President of the Republic, or be designated President of the Council of Ministers, a minister, or to any public office.

- Members of the Constitutional Council are prohibited, while performing their duties in this Council, from practising any other work, public or private, with the exception of attending international conferences and university teaching.

- Every member who contravenes this shall be deemed to have resigned ipso jure, and the Constitutional Council may declare such resignation by a decision taken by a majority of seven members. In such case, the procedures provided for in the new Article Four of this Law shall apply.

- If the member is a practising lawyer, his membership shall be suspended ipso jure, and he shall cease to practise the profession of law throughout the duration of his membership in the Council.

Members of the Constitutional Council shall not be entitled, during the period of their membership, to express an opinion or counsel or to give consultations or legal opinions on matters that may be brought before them, and they are bound by the duty of reserve and by the secrecy of deliberations in their work.

Members of the Constitutional Council shall wear, during public sittings and on official occasions, a robe the form of which shall be determined in the rules of procedure of the Constitutional Council.

The Constitutional Council shall meet upon convocation by its President, or by its Vice-President in the event of his absence, in the cases provided for in this Law, and notification of the date of the sitting shall be effected through administrative channels.

The Council shall also meet extraordinarily at the request of three of its members.

The Council shall not be deemed validly convened unless eight members at least are present.

The decisions of the Constitutional Council shall be taken by a majority of at least seven members in applications relating to the review of the constitutionality of laws and in disputes and challenges arising from parliamentary elections. Decisions shall be signed by the President and by all the members present, and the dissenting member or members shall record their dissent at the foot of the decision and sign it, and the dissent shall be considered an integral part thereof and shall be published and notified therewith.

Decisions issued by the Constitutional Council shall enjoy the force of res judicata and shall be binding on all public authorities and on judicial and administrative authorities.

The decisions of the Constitutional Council are final and shall not be subject to any ordinary or extraordinary means of recourse.

The decisions of the Constitutional Council and all acts issued by it shall be notified to each of the President of the Republic, the Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies, the President of the Council of Ministers, and to the competent authorities through administrative channels in accordance with the procedures determined by the rules of procedure.

Clerical and administrative tasks in the Constitutional Council shall be performed by judicial assistants or legal assistants seconded for this purpose by the Minister of Justice, from among whom the President of the Council shall choose the Chief Clerk, and their allowances shall be determined by a decree taken upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice.
Applications submitted to the Constitutional Council and all petitions and documents relating thereto shall be exempt from fees, whatsoever they may be.

The Constitutional Council shall prepare its rules of procedure which shall include, in addition to the matters provided for in certain articles of this Law, the rules and procedures to which the conduct of business before it is subject in implementation of the provisions of this Law.

The rules of procedure must be approved by the Council of Ministers and issued by the Chamber of Deputies by virtue of a law.

The Constitutional Council shall exercise review over the constitutionality of laws and all other texts that have the force of law.

Contrary to any text to the contrary, no judicial authority may carry out this review directly by way of challenge or indirectly by way of an plea of unconstitutionality or violation of the principle of the hierarchy of rules and texts.

Each of the President of the Republic, the Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies, the President of the Council of Ministers, and at least ten members of the Chamber of Deputies may apply to the Constitutional Council in relation to the review of the constitutionality of laws.

The heads of the legally recognised confessions shall have the right to apply exclusively in relation to personal status, freedom of belief, the practice of religious rites, and freedom of religious education. The application shall be submitted by the competent authority to the Presidency of the Constitutional Council within a period of fifteen days following the publication of the law in the Official Gazette or in one of the other legally adopted official means of publication, under pain of dismissal of the application in form.

Immediately upon the registration of the application in the registry of the Council, the President, or the Vice-President in his absence, shall immediately convene the Council to examine whether the effect of the text that is the subject of the application should be suspended.

The decision of suspension shall be published in the Official Gazette.

The President shall notify a copy of the application to the members of the Council and shall appoint a rapporteur from among the members.

The rapporteur must prepare his report and submit it to the Council within a maximum period of 10 days from the date of his notification of the decision of his appointment.

Upon the rapporteur finishing the preparation of his report, he shall refer it to the President of the Council, who shall notify copies thereof to the members and convene them within five days to deliberate in a session that shall remain open until the decision is issued.

The decision shall be issued in the council chamber within a maximum period of fifteen days from the date fixed for the session.

If the decision is not issued within the aforementioned period, the text that is the subject of the application shall be deemed accepted.

The Constitutional Council shall declare in its decision that the law is wholly or partially in conformity with or contrary to the Constitution.

If the Constitutional Council decides that the text that is the subject of the application is wholly or partially tainted by a defect of unconstitutionality, it shall rule to annul it wholly or partially by a reasoned decision that defines the limits of the annulment.

A text that has been decided to be annulled shall be considered, within the limits of the decision of the Council, as if it had never been issued, and no person whomsoever may invoke it.

The Constitutional Council shall adjudicate the validity of the elections of the Presidency of the Republic and the Presidency of the Chamber of Deputies and decide on the challenges and disputes arising therefrom, upon a request by at least one third of the members who legally compose the Chamber of Deputies.

The petition of challenge must be signed by them in person and submitted to the Presidency of the Constitutional Council within a period of twenty-four hours following the announcement of the results, under pain of its dismissal in form.

The decision shall be taken in the council chamber in both cases by a majority of at least seven members in the first round, and in the event that such majority cannot be achieved, an absolute majority of the members of the Council shall suffice.

The decision shall be issued within a maximum period of three days from the date of receipt of the application, and the Chamber of Deputies shall remain in session as an electoral college until the issuance of the decision of the Constitutional Council.

The Constitutional Council shall adjudicate the validity of the mandate of an elected deputy and examine the disputes and challenges arising from the elections of the members of the Chamber of Deputies, pursuant to a request submitted by a defeated candidate in the same electoral constituency to the Presidency of the Constitutional Council within a maximum period of thirty days following the date of the due announcement of the election results in his constituency, under pain of dismissal of the request in form.

A challenge to the validity of a parliamentary mandate shall be submitted by a petition registered in the registry of the Constitutional Council, stating the name of the objector, his capacity, the electoral constituency in which he stood as a candidate, the name of the person the validity of whose election is objected to, and the grounds leading to the annulment of the elections, and there shall be attached to the challenge the documents and supporting papers that substantiate the validity of the challenge.

A challenge shall not stay the result of the election, and the elected person shall be considered a deputy and shall exercise all the rights of the parliamentary mandate as from the announcement of the result of the elections.

The objection shall be notified through administrative channels to the Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies and the Ministry of the Interior, and the objection, together with a copy of its supporting documents, shall also be notified to the person the validity of whose parliamentary mandate is challenged, who may, within a period of fifteen days from the date of his notification, submit his observations and his defence together with the documents in his possession.

Each of the challenger and the person whose parliamentary mandate is challenged may be assisted by a single lawyer before the Constitutional Council.

The Ministry of the Interior must and provide the Constitutional Council with all the minutes, documents, and information available to it in order to enable it to conduct the necessary investigations.

The President of the Constitutional Council shall assign one of its members to prepare a report on the submitted challenge and shall delegate to him the conduct of the necessary investigations, and the rapporteur member shall enjoy the widest powers and may in particular request official and other documents, hear witnesses, and summon whomsoever he deems appropriate to interrogate him regarding the circumstances of the challenge.

The rapporteur member must prepare his report within a period of at most three months from his assignment and refer it to the Presidency of the Constitutional Council.

Following the receipt of the report of the rapporteur, the Constitutional Council shall meet immediately and deliberate on the objection that is the subject of the report, and its sessions shall remain open until the issuance of the decision, provided that the period for issuing this decision does not exceed one month.

The Constitutional Council shall declare by its decision the validity or invalidity of the challenged parliamentary mandate, and in this latter case, it shall have the right either to cancel the result in respect of the candidate whose parliamentary mandate is challenged and annul his mandate and consequently rectify this result and declare the victory of the candidate who obtained the majority and meets the conditions that qualify him for the parliamentary mandate, or to annul the mandate of the person the validity of whose parliamentary mandate is challenged and order a re-election for the seat that fell vacant as a result of the annulment. The decision of the Council shall be notified to the Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies, the Ministry of the Interior, and the interested parties.

When the Constitutional Council exercises its powers to decide on a challenge to the validity of parliamentary elections, it shall enjoy, either collectively or through the member whom it delegates, the authority of an investigating judge, with the exception of issuing arrest warrants.
All texts contrary to the provisions of this Law or the content of which conflicts with its provisions are repealed.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.
The Labour Inspection Regulation shall apply to all employers and employees subject to the provisions of the Labour Code.

The Labour Inspection, Prevention and Safety Service at the Ministry of Labour is entrusted with supervising the implementation of all laws, decrees and regulations relating to the circumstances and conditions of work and the protection of employees while carrying out their work, including the provisions of ratified international labour conventions, and in particular:

1) Ensuring the application of the legal provisions relating to the circumstances and conditions of work and the protection of employees while carrying out this work, such as the provisions concerning working hours, rest hours, wages, safety, health, welfare, occupational diseases, industrial accidents, work emergencies, the employment of juveniles, and other matters entrusted to labour inspectors.

2) Providing technical information and advice to the employers and employees concerned in the field of labour legislation and matters relating to health and safety rules in order to adopt the most effective means of complying with the legal provisions.

3) Supervising syndicates and professional federations at their various levels to ascertain that they do not exceed in their activities the limits permitted by the law, their internal regulations, and their bylaws.

4) Supervising prevention and safety measures in family establishments, particularly with regard to work which, by its nature or by the circumstances in which it is carried out, constitutes a danger to the life, health or morals of the persons employed therein.

5) Supervising private employment offices and watching over the progress of work therein, in coordination with the National Employment Institution.

Related text: Determination of occupational diseases

Labour inspectors must collect information on establishments in all matters relating to labour affairs and coordinate it, and notify the competent service at the Ministry of Labour of the shortcomings and gaps not specifically covered by the provisions in force or of the misapplication of these laws.

Labour inspectors must submit annual reports on the outcome of their work and special reports whenever the need arises.

These reports shall be prepared on the subjects and in the manner decided by the Director General of the Ministry of Labour.

Any other duties assigned to labour inspectors may not conflict with their effective performance of their primary duties, or prejudice in any way the authority and impartiality required of inspectors in their relations with employers and employees.

Before commencing their duties, labour inspectors must take the following oath before the President of the Court of First Instance in the governorate: "I swear by Almighty God that I will perform the duty of my office with all honesty and loyalty and that I will not divulge the secrets of manufacture or the methods of exploitation which come to my knowledge by virtue of my office".

Labour inspectors are vested with the following powers:

1 - To enter freely and without prior notice all establishments subject to their supervision during and outside working hours in the establishment, and any workplace therein. Upon carrying out an inspection visit, they must notify the employer or his representative of their presence unless they consider that such notification may prejudice the performance of their duties.

2) To carry out any examination, test or inquiry which they may consider necessary to verify strict compliance with the legal provisions in force. And in particular:

a) To address questions to the employer or to the employees in the establishment, either alone or in the presence of witnesses, on any matter relating to the application of the legal provisions in force.

b) To request to inspect, in the manner prescribed by the laws and regulations, any books, registers or other documents the keeping of which is required by the laws, in order to verify their conformity with the legal provisions, and to take copies or extracts of such documents.

c) To take or remove samples of materials and products for the purposes of analysis, provided that the employer or his representative is notified of the samples or materials taken or removed for these purposes.

d) To take steps aimed at remedying defects observed in installations, layouts or working methods which they have reasonable cause to believe constitute a threat to the health and safety of the employees, and to notify the competent departments in the Ministry to take the necessary measures. In order to enable the labour inspectors to take these steps, and while preserving the right of the employer to seek review before any judicial or administrative body prescribed by law, they must notify the competent authority in the Ministry to issue orders requiring the introduction of modifications to the apparatus or installations within the period of time necessary to ensure compliance with the legal provisions relating to the health and safety of the employees, or to request from this authority the taking of urgent compulsory enforcement measures where there is an imminent danger to their health and safety.

Employers or their representatives must provide labour inspectors with all the information that they request from them and that would facilitate their mission. A labour inspector may summon the employer, his representative, or any employee in the establishment which he is inspecting to his office for the purpose of addressing inquiries, if he finds this necessary for the performance of his duty.

Subject to such exceptions as may be prescribed by the laws, decrees and regulations in force:

1) Labour inspectors are prohibited from having any direct or indirect interest in the establishments under their supervision.

2) Labour inspectors are bound, even after leaving the service, not to disclose any secrets which may have come to their knowledge in the course of performing their duties, failing which they shall be liable to the appropriate disciplinary and legal penalties.

3) Labour inspectors shall treat as absolutely confidential the source of any complaint submitted to them. They must not divulge to the employer or his representative the source of the complaint or the information that led to the carrying out of the inspection.

Whoever violates the legal provisions the enforcement of which is entrusted to labour inspectors or neglects to apply them shall be liable to have an offence report drawn up against him without prior warning, unless the laws and regulations provide for exceptions in cases where a prior warning must be served requiring the implementation of remedial and preventive measures.

The offence report shall be drawn up in three copies, one of which shall be served upon the party concerned, the second sent to the competent judicial authority, and the third kept in the file of the establishment. The reports drawn up shall have probative force until the contrary is proved.

Every violation of the legal provisions entrusted to the Labour Inspection, Prevention and Safety Service, or whoever obstructs the mission of labour inspectors in the performance of their duties, shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of the Law of 17/09/62, the provisions of Article 109 of the Labour Code, and the provisions of the Penal Code.

The competent authority shall make the necessary transport facilities for the performance by labour inspectors of their duties, and shall also make the necessary arrangements to reimburse the inspectors for any travelling and incidental expenses they incur which may be required for the performance of their duties.
Officials of the administration and security personnel must assist labour inspectors in the mission entrusted to them.
Decree No. 14900 dated 2 May 1949 relating to the appointment of labour inspectors and the determination of their jurisdiction is hereby repealed.
This Decree shall be published and notified wherever needed.

The war matériel, weapons, ammunition and explosives provided for by this Legislative Decree are divided into three types:

- The First Type - War matériel, weapons and ammunition intended exclusively for use in land, naval or aerial warfare, which form or will form part of the armament of the armed forces in every State, or the use of which has been discontinued, yet which may be utilized militarily and are not used for any other purpose.

- The Second Type - Non-war weapons and ammunition.

- The Third Type - Explosives, gunpowder and their accessories.

These three types are arranged into nine categories.

The First Type: War weapons, ammunition and matériel.

The First Category - Weapons and ammunition intended for use in land, naval or aerial warfare, namely:

A - Rifles of all sizes and calibres manufactured and intended for war use, and their barrel, stocks, frames, mechanisms and separate parts the manufacture of which has been completed.

B - Machine guns, automatic rifles, submachine guns and machine guns special to aircraft of all calibres and sizes, and the barrels of these weapons, their stocks and all their other separate parts the manufacture of which has been completed.

C - Long and short cannons, heavy cannons and cannons special to aircraft of whatever calibre, and the mounts of these weapons, their muzzles, barrels, stocks, breechblocks, all mechanisms special to them, accessories intended for their assembly, and all other separate parts the manufacture of which has been completed and which are used to repair these weapons or as spare parts therefor.

D - Loaded and unloaded ammunition, projectiles and cartridges special to the weapons mentioned in paragraphs A, B, C, and loaded and unloaded manufactured articles and devices intended for firing, launching or detonating such ammunition, projectiles and cartridges.

E - Bombs of all kinds, water projectiles (torpedoes), fixed or mobile land or sea mines, loaded or unloaded, and atomic, rocket and similar bombs.

And loaded or unloaded manufactured articles and devices or those utilized for launching these bombs and mines or intended for detonating them.

F - All devices and equipment assigned to war operations, such as devices assigned to bombarding aircraft and vessels, range-finding and sighting instruments, rifling mechanisms, distance-control instruments and beams prepared specially for war weapons, devices intended for giving light signals, and devices for detecting aircraft and submarines such as radar and others.

The Second Category - Units equipped with firearms or intended for the use of weapons in war are:

A - Combat vehicles, tanks, armoured cars and flamethrowers.

B - Armoured vessels, destroyers, and naval war vessels and ships of their various kinds, including aircraft carriers and submarines.

C - Periscopes assigned to submarines.

D - Combat aircraft, aerial interceptors, airships and light or heavy aircraft intended for war of all kinds. Appended thereto are the engines, propellers and wings intended for these aircraft, the mounts of their cannons and machine guns, and all their other separate parts.

E - Turrets, mounts and armoured or unarmoured separate parts, the manufacture of which has been completed and which are used to assemble or repair the matériel mentioned in items A, B, D of the Second Category or as spare parts therefor.

The Third Category - Devices intended for protection against combat raids, protective masks and clothing, gear pertaining to these devices, and their separate parts the manufacture of which has been completed.

The Fourth Category - Weapons and ammunition which are not considered war weapons and ammunition, yet are appended to war weapons and ammunition, namely:

A - Revolvers or automatic pistols, their models, their separate parts and the completed devices appertaining thereto which are fired from the shoulder or by hand, of all sizes and whatever their calibre.

B - Loaded or unloaded ammunition intended for these pistols, the magazines, barrels and frames special to these weapons, and all their other completed separate parts intended for assembling or repairing these pistols or which serve as spare parts therefor.

C - Weapons in which the ammunition of the war weapons set forth in the preceding categories can be used, and rifled firearms of all sizes and calibres.

D - All ammunition used in war weapons, including hunting cartridges loaded with a single bullet of calibre 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 20, 24, 28 and 32

E - Bayonets, swords and lances. Excluded therefrom is that which is referred to in the Seventh Category.

The Second Type - Non-war weapons and ammunition

The Fifth Category - Hunting firearms and ammunition of all calibres not mentioned in the preceding categories, and not falling within the weapons or ammunition referred to in items C and D of the Fourth Category. And smooth-bore rifles.

The Sixth Category - Training weapons, namely those fired by means of compression without gunpowder.

The Seventh Category - Antique and commemorative weapons, provided that they are unserviceable and do not fall within the weapons set forth in item (C) of the Fourth Category.

The Eighth Category - Prohibited weapons, namely weapons that do not fall within the categories provided for above, and in particular: daggers, knives, knuckle-dusters, sword-sticks, sticks weighted with lead or tipped at both ends with iron, and in general all concealed weapons.

The Third Type - Explosives, gunpowder and their accessories

The Ninth Category - Varieties of explosives, gunpowder and their accessories, namely:

A - Gunpowder of its various kinds.

B - Explosives - All kinds of dynamite (gelignite or gelatine), explosives compounded of nitrates, blasting gelatine and others.

Ammonium nitrate containing nitrogen in a proportion exceeding 33,5% is considered to be among the accessories intended for the manufacture of explosives.

C - Accessories necessary for explosives - Electric detonators, fuses (wicks), detonating cord, slow match, cord intended for underwater use, and all devices used specially to detonate the substances mentioned in this Category.

No natural or legal person may carry out in Lebanese territory industrial or commercial operations of any kind whatsoever relating to matériel, weapons and ammunition of any category whatsoever before obtaining a legal licence granted by decree upon the proposal of the Ministers of Interior and National Defence.

In order to obtain this licence, the person concerned must submit an application to the Ministry of Interior stating therein:

- First name, surname, date and place of birth, and identity card number.

- Nationality.

- Place of residence.

- Profession (manufacturer or dealer in weapons).

- Registration number in the Chamber of Commerce.

- Address of the premises or factory.

- Manner of operation.

- Through an individual or a company.

And in the latter case, the type of company and the trade name, and the names of the partners, managers, foremen and active agents, and if it is a joint-stock company, the names of the board of directors and its members and their addresses shall be stated.

The application shall be accompanied by a copy of the judicial record for each of the persons mentioned in the preceding paragraph and by a certificate of good conduct issued by the Gendarmerie commander or the Police commissioner in the district in which the person concerned has resided for six months.

The procedures for granting these licences, their models, and the procedures for exportation and importation shall be determined pursuant to a decree adopted upon the proposal of the Ministers of Interior, National Defence and National Economy.

No person shall be licensed to acquire, possess, or transport equipment, weapons, and ammunition falling within the first and second categories, except in the event of a breach of security or in the cases provided for in Chapter Two relating to the manufacture of and trade in such equipment, and subject to the conditions specified therein. The licence shall be granted pursuant to a decision of the Minister of National Defence.

However, members of the Lebanese land, naval, and air armies, the gendarmerie, and the police shall be entitled to transport equipment, weapons, and ammunition of all categories, within the limits of their duties and in accordance with military regulations and laws.

Members of the public forces, forest rangers, watchmen, guards, and all other similar employees are licensed to acquire and carry weapons and ammunition falling within the first category, paragraph (a), and within the fourth category, within the limits of their duties and pursuant to a written permit on special cards issued by the Ministry of the Interior stating the number of the weapon permitted to be carried, and its type.

Employees of the Military Court and all other civilians working for the Ministry of National Defence are licensed to acquire such weapons pursuant to a special permit from the Commander of the Army.

Reserve and retired officers shall be entitled to retain weapons and ammunition of the fourth category which had been delivered to them personally during the performance of their duties and to carry them, subject to the conditions prescribed for the personal arming of officers.

None of the holders of licences to transport or possess weapons and ammunition shall be entitled to sell or dispose of them for consideration or without consideration unless the purchaser holds a licence authorising him to do so. Weapons of the sixth category may be possessed and transported, and identity papers shall stand in place of a licence in respect thereof. As for weapons of the seventh and eighth category, their possession is permitted, provided that carrying them is prohibited. The granting of a licence to carry them is prohibited in all circumstances.

Knives imported specifically for the use of scout troops are exempted therefrom.

A licence shall not be granted to acquire and transport more than two weapons of the fourth category.

As for weapons of the fifth category and their ammunition, they shall not be subject to this limitation.

A hunting licence shall only be granted to one who holds a licence to carry a weapon.

A licence to carry or possess a weapon and ammunition of any category shall only be granted to persons who have attained the age of at least eighteen years; as for hunting weapons, a licence therefor may be granted to one who has completed the sixteenth year of his age under the responsibility of his guardian, provided that the applicant:

1 - Has not been afflicted with a mental illness.

2 - Has not been sentenced to deprivation of civil rights, or for a felony, or for a disgraceful offence.

3 - Has not been sentenced to a prohibition from carrying a weapon or for offences against State security.

4 - If he is a foreigner, has not been the subject of a decision prohibiting residence or ordering expulsion from the country.

5 - Has not been repeatedly convicted of contravening the provisions of this Legislative Decree.
The holder of the licence must produce it upon every request by officers of the public authority.
Every person licensed to carry a weapon who ceases to fulfil one of the conditions required under the provisions of this Legislative Decree shall have the licence withdrawn from him.

The Ministry of National Defence shall be entitled, with the exception of weapons intended for hunting, to withdraw the licence or suspend its effect at any time on the basis of a report from the competent departments or for the requirements of public security.

In the event of the withdrawal or cancellation of the licence, the weapon shall be confiscated and the annual fee shall not be refunded.

The Ministry of National Defence (Army Command) may license the transit of equipment, weapons, and ammunition of the first four categories across Lebanese territory after the approval of the Council of Ministers.

The licence shall only be granted to designated persons belonging to regular armed forces affiliated with one of the recognised powers or officially commissioned by them for this purpose, or to persons holding lawful licences from the competent authorities in the State to which they belong.

As for hunting weapons and their ammunition, and the weapons and materials mentioned from the other five categories, their transit shall be licensed by the Ministry of the Interior.

The General Security departments at border posts shall grant a temporary licence to carry a weapon of war to persons coming to Lebanon on a mission or passing in transit across its territory, provided that they hold a lawful licence from their Government and that the weapons are intended for their personal use and are described in the licence; in the absence of General Security at the border, the Customs shall grant the temporary licence.

The term of the temporary licence may not exceed fifteen days except in exceptional circumstances, and upon the expiry of the period the persons concerned must obtain a licence to carry a weapon from the competent authority.

As for those coming to Lebanon for hunting, they must, in addition to the licence which they hold from their Government, obtain a hunting licence and a hunting weapon licence from the competent Lebanese authorities after paying the annual fee, and a stamp of the value thereof shall be affixed to the licence itself.
In the case specified in the first paragraph of the preceding Article, the quantity of ammunition may not exceed 25 per weapon.

Holders of the licences provided for in Article 33 and the first paragraph of Article 34 must produce them upon every request by officers of the public authorities. If they leave Lebanese territory, they must surrender them to the nearest post of the public forces or of the Customs at the border, which shall return them to the department that issued the licence.

A trader or factory owner is prohibited from selling or giving to any person equipment, weapons, or ammunition of the first four categories before verifying that the person concerned holds a lawful licence authorising him to do so.

For this purpose, the applicant shall be granted a temporary licence stating that he is authorised to obtain materiel or weapons and ammunition and the number of each of them, and he shall produce it to the owner of the factory or shop,

who shall record in the blank space left therein for this purpose the type of weapon intended for sale, its number, and its model, together with the types of ammunition pertaining to it, and shall then sign it and stamp it with the seal of the commercial establishment.

The weapon and ammunition shall not be delivered to the person concerned before obtaining the final licence.
In respect of every licence, the fee prescribed by law shall be levied.

Every person who acquires a weapon or ammunition that is lost from him must give notice thereof to the nearest post of the gendarmerie, the police, or the General Security, stating therein the circumstances of the loss.

He must surrender the licence that he had to the same authorities, which shall give him an acknowledgment of receipt thereof, and if he assigns it to any person he must provide all the information relating to the sale of the weapon and ammunition, stating the name of the assignee, his address, and the number of his licence.

Every person who finds a weapon or ammunition must surrender it immediately to the post of the public forces nearest to the place where it was found; otherwise, he shall be punished for the offence of carrying a weapon.

Every person to whom weapons or ammunition have devolved by inheritance from a legator in a lawful manner must notify the competent authorities thereof within three months and state the number of the legator's licence; if he wishes to retain it, he must submit an application to obtain a lawful licence to possess or carry it, whereas if he does not wish to retain the weapon or ammunition, he may assign them to a third party licensed to acquire them.

If the aforesaid period of three months expires and the formalities provided for in the preceding paragraph have not been carried out, the weapon shall be confiscated from the heir, and if he refuses to surrender it, he shall be prosecuted criminally.

If the legator had acquired the weapon without a licence, the heir must notify the competent authorities within one month from the date of his obtaining the weapon. If he wishes to retain it, he must submit a lawful application to obtain the licence immediately upon the expiry of the month; otherwise, the weapon shall be confiscated from him, and if the heir refuses to surrender it, he shall be prosecuted criminally. In both of the cases mentioned above, the blank space in the temporary licence shall be filled in by the head of the post nearest to the place of residence of the heir.

Persons who possess arms and ammunition without a licence shall obtain one within three months from the date on which this Legislative Decree comes into force or deliver them to the Gendarmerie posts within the jurisdiction of which they reside within the same period, in which case they shall be exempted from the penalty.

The State reserves the right to import, possess, transport and sell types of gunpowder and explosives of whatever kind, and all materials similar thereto, for the account of the State "Ministry of the Interior - Gunpowder Department" and for its benefit.

Installations intended for the manufacture, preparation and sale of gunpowder and explosives, as well as warehouses intended for these materials and the like, shall be subject to the supervision of the technical officers of the Ministry of National Defence.

Whoever introduces or attempts to introduce any gunpowder, any explosives or other materials similar thereto into Lebanon shall be prosecuted, in addition to criminal penalties, in accordance with the laws relating to customs smuggling.
Agencies for the sale of hunting gunpowder may be established to supply retailers with the quantities intended for local consumption.
Retailers shall procure their supplies of hunting gunpowder from the agents of the region to which they belong and from the warehouses.
Sellers are prohibited from selling hunting gunpowder except to a person holding a permit to carry a hunting weapon.
The rules of delivery and sale relating to hunting gunpowder shall be determined by decree.

The sale of explosives and blasting gunpowder without a licence is prohibited.

The Ministry of Public Works and Transport shall specify the quantity to be delivered to each purchaser, public works contractor or quarry operator.
Public warehouses for blasting gunpowder and explosives shall be established and maintained by the Ministry of the Interior - Gunpowder Department.
The types of blasting gunpowder and explosives licensed for sale shall be delivered pursuant to an exit permit granted by the Ministry of the Interior to the purchaser.
Temporary private warehouses for blasting gunpowder and explosives may be established by decision of the Minister of the Interior.

The master of a vessel, whatever the country from which he arrives, shall submit to the Customs before entering the port a special declaration of the gunpowder and explosives carried on his vessel, and of the duration of the vessel's stay in the port, and this declaration must be produced upon the departure of the vessel.

The transport of any quantity of gunpowder exceeding two kilograms is prohibited unless it is sealed with the lead seal of the Gunpowder Department and accompanied by a transit pass endorsed by the Gunpowder Department.

Gunpowder transported in contravention of the provisions of this Article shall be seized and confiscated.
If an establishment for the sale of gunpowder is liquidated, whether amicably or following bankruptcy, the sale may only be made to persons who personally hold a legal licence.

Everyone who consumes explosive materials and their accessories shall keep a legal consumption register in which shall be recorded the quantities of explosives delivered to him by the Gunpowder Department, the quantities consumed thereof and the works in which these quantities were used.

The entries in this register must be made day by day under the responsibility of the contractor or the engineer entrusted with carrying out and supervising the works.
The consumption register must be produced to the Gunpowder Department upon every request by that Department.

The officer of the Gunpowder Department may verify the manner in which the explosives are used by conducting an inspection at the worksites in the presence of the engineer and the representative of the Ministry of Public Works and Transport.
Consumers of explosives shall not be granted a licence to purchase them except after producing their register endorsed by the engineer in charge of the works or by his representative.
Quantities of gunpowder and explosives that have not been used by the completion of the works must be returned to the Gunpowder Department within a period of fifteen days at the most.
Trade in ribbed percussion caps for rifles and percussion caps of all kinds for hunting cartridges shall be restricted to licensed sellers of gunpowder.

The manufacture, import and sale of fireworks and every material similar thereto shall be subject to the technical supervision of the Ministry of the Interior - Gunpowder Department - and such supervision shall cover in particular:

1 - The safety conditions that must be met in factories in which gunpowder, fireworks compounds or materials similar thereto are used, and in warehouses and stores for the sale of fireworks.

2 - The method of operating the factories and the materials used.
The manufacture, import and sale of the fireworks known as firecrackers is prohibited.
The establishment of any factory, warehouse or store for the sale of fireworks is prohibited except after obtaining a licence granted by the Governor.
No premises for the manufacture of fireworks shall be permitted to exist within inhabited places.

Factories and warehouses currently situated within such places must be relocated within a period not exceeding three months, and such premises shall likewise not be permitted to exist except at a distance of at least 100 metres from any warehouse or shop containing inflammable materials such as petroleum, gasoline and the like, and they must be constructed of non-inflammable materials, and there shall not be in the same building any warehouse for rags, paper, wood, cigarettes and the like, nor may any warehouse or factory for alcoholic substances adjoin these factories.

Importers of and dealers in fireworks are prohibited from depositing, in the shops designated for sale, a quantity of the various fireworks exceeding in any event one hundred kilograms, provided that there is in the premises no inflammable substance susceptible of ignition.
The licences provided for in the preceding Articles shall not be granted unless the conditions mentioned above have been fulfilled.

No transaction in fireworks of any kind whatsoever may be concluded, nor may the importation granted therefor take place, except after obtaining an import permit from the Ministry of the Interior, Gunpowder Department. These goods may not be withdrawn from the customs warehouses except after submission of the import permit granted to the importers.

The technical supervision provided for in Article 63 et seq., and the periodic or non-periodic inspection of factories and warehouses, shall be carried out by an official of the Gunpowder Department assisted by technical personnel of the Ministry of National Defence.

The Gunpowder Department may call upon the technical expert to assist it directly in case of necessity.

Any person who, without a licence, undertakes the manufacture of war materiel, weapons or ammunition, or their detached parts, of the first four categories provided for in Article 2 of this Legislative Decree shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years and by a fine from one thousand to five thousand pounds, or by either of these two penalties.

The same penalty shall apply in cases of disposal, purchase, importation or theft of such materiel, weapons and ammunition. Any person who, without a licence, undertakes the transport of weapons of the four categories set out above, or the transport of ammunition or detached parts of weapons where such ammunition and parts are serviceable, shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to two years.

Provided that, in all circumstances, the penalty may be reduced to less than one month of imprisonment, and stay of execution may not be ordered in the case of use of the transported weapon of war. The court may, in addition, order the prohibition from carrying a weapon of war.

Where the act relates to non-war materiel or weapons and ammunition specified in the Fifth Category, the offender shall be punished by imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months and by a fine not exceeding one hundred pounds, or by either of these two penalties.

Save in the case of possession, the same penalty shall apply where the act relates to weapons of the Seventh and Eighth Categories.

In all cases, the materiel, weapons and ammunition referred to in the preceding Articles shall be confiscated, and the machinery, tools and means of transport used for their manufacture and trade therein shall be confiscated.

Any person who discharges a firearm in populated places or in a crowd of people, from a licensed or unlicensed weapon, shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years and by a fine from five hundred pounds to one thousand Lebanese pounds, or by either of these two penalties.

The weapon shall be confiscated in all circumstances.

Any person who buys, sells, transports, possesses or manufactures any gunpowder, explosives or their accessories without a licence shall be punished by imprisonment for up to six months and by a fine of up to five hundred pounds to one thousand Lebanese pounds, or by either of these two penalties.

The materials, tools, goods and means of transport prepared for their manufacture and trade therein shall be confiscated.

Any person who contravenes the provisions of Articles 45, 50, 54, 55 and 62 and Subsections Five and Seven of Chapter Five shall be punished by imprisonment for up to one month and by a fine of up to one hundred pounds, or by either of these two penalties.

The gunpowder and all other explosives and materials which were the cause of the contravention shall be confiscated, and the licence shall be revoked where appropriate.

Every contravention of the provisions of this Legislative Decree for which no penalty is provided shall render its perpetrator liable to the penalty of imprisonment from one month to six months and to a fine of one hundred thousand Lebanese pounds, or to either of these two penalties.

There shall be referred to the Military Court:

First - Any person who commits an offence provided for in Article 72.

Second - Any person who simultaneously commits two offences falling within the ambit of Articles 72 and 73.

Third - Any person who simultaneously commits an offence within the jurisdiction of the Military Courts conjoined with an offence falling within the ambit of Article 73, and in such case a sentence of prohibition from carrying a non-war weapon shall be passed in accordance with the law.

Fourth - All offences provided for in this Legislative Decree and relating to weapons of war.

Where an offence within the jurisdiction of the Criminal Court or the Judicial Council occurs and is connected with one of the offences provided for in Article 72, the Criminal Court or the Judicial Council shall, notwithstanding the provisions of Article 52 of the Military Penal Code, try both offences together.
This Legislative Decree shall be published in the Official Gazette.
