Article Fifth of Decision No. 15 dated 19 January of the year 1925 has been amended in the following manner: The foreign woman who marries a Lebanese becomes Lebanese after the lapse of one year from the date of registration of the marriage in the Civil Status Registry upon her application.

Article Sixth of Decision No. 15 dated 19 January of the year 1925 has been amended in the following manner: The Lebanese woman who marries a foreigner remains Lebanese until she requests the striking off of her registration from the census registers in order to acquire the nationality of her husband.

Article Seventh of Decision No. 15 dated 19 January of the year 1925 has been amended in the following manner: It shall be permissible for the woman who lost her Lebanese nationality following her marriage to a foreigner to recover this nationality after the dissolution of the marriage upon her application. The Lebanese women who married before the census of the year 1932 and lost their nationality by marriage and had no registration in the registers of this census may, after the dissolution of the marriage, obtain a judicial judgment for their registration if their presence on 30 August of the year 1924 on Lebanese territory is proven, whereas those of them who were found outside Lebanese territory on the aforementioned date may recover their Lebanese nationality pursuant to Article Second of the Law of 31 December of the year 1946.
The Lebanese woman who lost her nationality by her marriage to a foreigner before the issuance of this Law may recover this nationality upon her application.

It shall be permissible for the Lebanese woman married to a foreigner to apply separately from her husband for Lebanese nationality, provided that her husband consents thereto and that she proves her residence for a period of five uninterrupted years in Lebanon.
The acquisition of nationality pursuant to this Law shall have no effect on rights accrued and in respect of which lawsuits have been instituted before its entry into force.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

By forest is meant: a thicket comprising various trees intertwined with one another, whether large or small, and a grove comprising trees that are neither large nor entangled with one another. This is of the kind that is generally used only for industry and fuel.

Forests are divided into four categories:

1- Forests that are the property of the State.

2- Forests that are the property of the State and are subject to rights of usufruct for the villages.

3- Forests that are the property of municipalities and villages.

4- Forests owned by individuals

There shall be established in the Ministry of Agriculture a Forest Service which shall secure the enforcement of the provisions of this Law upon the forests of the State and study and enforce measures for the protection and revival of other forests.

This Service shall be composed of technical and administrative officials, officers and guards, whose number shall be determined by decree and who shall be drawn from the current officials of the Ministry of Agriculture.

The officials of the forests, their officers and their guards are officers of the judicial police in respect of what is entrusted to them under the provisions of this Law, and they shall perform their functions in accordance with the Law on Guards.

The officers and guards of the forests shall, before assuming their functions, take the oath that they will perform them faithfully and honestly. The swearing-in procedure shall take place before the Justice of the Peace in the district to which they are appointed.
The forests of the State are the lands included in its private domain comprising forests, woods and scrublands.

In the areas where the operations of cadastral demarcation and census provided for in Decision No. 186 dated 15 March 1926, as amended by Decision No. 44/LR dated 20/4/1932, have not yet been initiated, the demarcation of the forests of the State shall take place either at the request of the Forest Service, or at the request of the Department of State Domain in agreement with the Forest Service, or at the request of the neighbouring landowners.

This operation and, in general, all administrative and judicial proceedings relating thereto shall take place in accordance with the provisions of the land regulations in force, and in particular the regulations governing the demarcation and administration of the private domain of the State.

The demarcation operations mentioned in the two preceding Articles shall be carried out on forests held jointly by the State and others in order to determine finally the ownership rights and usufruct rights thereon belonging to the holders of rights therein.

The Forest Service shall draw up regulations for the exploitation of forests in a manner that guarantees their utilisation, improvement and continuous afforestation at the same time. These regulations shall be approved by the Minister of Agriculture.

No licence shall be granted to fell trees in the forests of the State at ground level unless such measure is required by force majeure. The licence in such a case shall be granted pursuant to a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.

The Forest Service shall give each of its officers and guards a special instrument or hammer to be used to place a mark on trees and timber in order to facilitate the supervision of the legality of felling operations.

The officers and guards may not part with the instrument or hammer or allow it to be used by any person whomsoever. The imprint of the instrument or hammer shall be deposited at the registry of the Peace Court to which the officer and guard are attached.

The produce of the forests of the State shall only be sold by way of public auction, save in the following cases:

1- If the total value of the produce being sold does not exceed five hundred thousand Lebanese pounds.

2- If the matter relates to supplying what the administration needs or executing works on behalf of the State.

3- If the produce could not or cannot be sold by public auction for a reason arising from force majeure.

In no case may the period of exploitation and the terms of payment exceed five years, and at the end of the exploitation works all fixed installations such as roads, canals and buildings constructed for the exploitation or transport of timber and firewood shall remain the property of the State without compensation.

The sale of forest produce by public auction shall be conducted by a committee composed of the Head of the Forest Service or his representative as chairman, and a representative of the Ministry of Finance and a representative of the Governor of the district as two members, assisted by the tax collector of the district, who shall collect the deposit and the price in the absence of a Treasury cash office at the place of sale.

The Forest Service shall draw up for each auction a special book of conditions the main clauses of which shall conform to a general book of conditions drawn up by the aforesaid Service for all auctions. The book of conditions shall include the specification of the nature, location and other descriptions of the produce, the provision of the guarantee or surety, the manner of payment of the price, and other customary auction conditions.

All objections submitted during the auction proceedings regarding the validity of these operations or the financial solvency of the bidders or their sureties shall be adjudicated forthwith by the committee, and the legality of the auction may be challenged after its conclusion before the Council of State in accordance with the procedures set forth in its own regulations.

There may not participate in the purchase of produce by auction or by mutual agreement, whether directly, through an intermediary, or in any capacity whatsoever:

1- Officials of the State and of the municipalities.

2- Relatives of the officials of the central Forest Service and relatives of the local officials in the same district in which the sale takes place, and their relatives by marriage up to the fourth degree.

Every auction conducted in contravention of the provisions of the preceding Article shall be deemed null and void, without prejudice to the imposition on each of the offenders of a fine not exceeding one quarter of the auction price and not less than one tenth thereof.

The auction shall become final as soon as the chairman of the committee announces the award to the highest bidder, unless the auction price exceeds five thousand pounds, in which case the award shall not become definitive until after the approval of the Minister of Agriculture.

In defended forests, that is to say those which suffer no harm from the entry of livestock therein, the gathering of all fruit therein, such as acorns, and the grazing of livestock may be contracted out by way of public auction for a period of three consecutive years at most, and they may also be contracted out by mutual agreement, all in accordance with the procedures set forth in the preceding Chapter.

Whoever has acquired the right of pasture by auction or by mutual agreement may not bring into the forests a number of animals exceeding the number specified in the book of conditions, and he shall be required to place a distinctive mark on all his animals, and he may not leave his animals outside the roads and places designated for them.
Uncultivated lands and vacant plots situated within the forests may be leased for a period not exceeding 15 years by public auction or by mutual agreement pursuant to a book of conditions.

A felling contractor may not, for any reason whatsoever, fell trees except in the places designated for him in the forest, or exceed the number or quantity designated for him. Nor may a lessee of grazing rights or of the gathering of minor produce exploit any produce other than that included in his lease.

The concessionaire or lessee may not commence the felling of trees prior to obtaining an exploitation permit from the Forest Service, and this permit shall only be granted after the payment of the royalties due to the State, and the concessionaire and lessee may not remove the products from the forest except after obtaining a written authorisation from the local forest officer, which he grants on the basis of the exploitation permit.
The concessionaire or lessee shall not touch any tree of the trees exempted from felling situated- in the leased land, nor shall he substitute it for non-exempted trees which he has not felled.

There shall be stated in the auction minutes, the schedule of their general and special conditions, and the decisions of leasing by mutual agreement the following:

1 - The method of felling trees, debarking them, and making charcoal from firewood.

2 - The conditions for the use of stamps and hammers.

3 - The duration of exploitation, clearing, and cleaning.

4 - The method of establishing workshops, shelters, warehouses, and charcoal kilns.

5 - The conditions for the use of fire.

6 - The tracks authorised for use to transport the products.

7 - The daily duration of work in the workshops.

8 - The method of removing the various products, the conditions for the passage of herds, and in general all the conditions relating to the execution of the lease. The Administration shall have a privilege over the products of the felling which are still standing on their stems or deposited in the forest as security for the enforcement of the clauses of the book of conditions, and it may levy the necessary attachment to secure the recovery of the fine and the guarantee allowance accruing to it.

If the exploitation is not completed or the products are not transported from the forest within the periods specified in the concession or lease contract or fixed with the approval of the Administration, the products standing on their stems or remaining at the place of felling shall be attached and ordered to be confiscated in favour of the State. The periods for transporting the products and their renewal may not exceed five years.

If the concessionaire or lessee does not carry out, within the periods specified in the contract, the works stipulated therein to prevent fire, remove and arrange bundles of wormwood, clean the places of felling of boxthorn and harmful shrubs, and repair the ditches, fences, and roads intended for the transport of products, the Forest Service shall carry out these works at the expense of the concessionaire or lessee and draw up a statement of their expenses, which shall be collected in the same manner as State funds.

The concessionaire or lessee shall be criminally liable from the date of his obtaining the exploitation permit until his final discharge from liability for all contraventions of the provisions of this Law committed in the forest included in his concession or lease, and he shall be relieved of liability if he gives written notice of the contravention upon its occurrence before a forest officer inspects it. The concessionaire or lessee shall be pecuniarily liable for the contraventions committed by the persons employed by him in the felling works, including woodcutters, labourers, vehicle drivers, and others.
The concessionaire or lessee may lend himself an agent with the approval of the Forest Service, and the latter shall have the functions of a watchman as defined in this Law.

No product whatsoever of the forest products may be removed from any of the workshops or warehouses accepted by the Administration to be transported outside the place of felling without a transport permit granted by the forest officer authorised to do so. This permit must be produced upon every demand by the forest officers and the members of the security forces, and the latter shall endorse the permit and state the type and quantity of the transported products.

Taking forest products, whatever their type and origin, out of the forests is prohibited between sunset and sunrise; however, the forest officer may grant a night transport permit to the concessionaire or lessee of the felling in a forest that is very far from the ordinary places of sale or warehouses to enable him to transport them in a single day.

If forest products of any type whatsoever are transported without a permit, they shall be attached and seized together with their containers and means of transport, including vehicles and animals, and shall be sold where necessary, all in accordance with the chapter relating to the seizure of contraventions.

The storage of and trading in forest products require obtaining a prior authorisation therefor. The manner of granting this authorisation, its conditions, and the method of supervising its enforcement shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Agriculture.

Traders in forest products may not obstruct the officers of the Forest Service, the representatives of the administrative authorities, and the judicial police officers from entering and inspecting their stores and warehouses.

An inspection of the site of felling shall be carried out within three months from the expiry of the period specified in the concession or lease contract for the transport of the felled trees.

At the end of this period, the concessionaire or lessee shall cease to be liable for the obligations of the exploitation if the Forest Service does not carry out the inspection within the said period; and the concessionaire or lessee may, if he completes the exploitation and clears the place of felling before the end of its period, request the Forest Service, by registered letter with acknowledgment of receipt, to carry out the inspection, whereby his liability shall cease if the aforesaid Service does not carry out the required formality within a period of three months from the date of its receipt of the registered letter.

The concessionaire or lessee must attend the inspection after being notified of its date by a registered letter at least fifteen days prior to the date of the inspection. If he does not attend at the place of inspection or does not send an agent on his behalf, the inspection shall be deemed to have taken place in his presence.

The concessionaire or lessee may request, within a period of thirty days from the date of drawing up the inspection record, its annulment for a defect in its drawing up or for its non-conformity with the facts, by means of an action brought by him before the Council of State. If the record is annulled, the Administration may, within a period of thirty days from the date of the annulment, order that a new record be drawn up in place of the annulled record.

If the Forest Service does not object within the time limit specified in the preceding Article to the inspection record, the concessionaire shall be discharged from liability for the obligations of the exploitation.

State forests over which villages have rights of usufruct shall have these rights recognised upon the optional demarcation of these forests in accordance with the provisions of Articles 7, 8, 9, 10 or on the occasion of a general demarcation. In the demarcation formality, each of the Forest Service and the State Domain Department shall be represented by one of its officers. The rights of usufruct shall be determined pursuant to the decisions of the committee, and a decree shall be issued recognising them. No new rights over State forests may be recognised after the demarcation has been carried out.
The rights of usufruct over State forests which may be recognised shall only be in favour of the municipalities and villages adjacent to the forests or contiguous to the villages adjacent thereto.

The rights of usufruct which may be recognised in accordance with the preceding Article shall only apply to the following matters:

1- Gathering dry firewood and minor products.

2- Providing the firewood necessary for the needs of each house of the houses of the village.

3- Exercising the right of grazing for herds, unless there is a prohibition issued by the Ministry of Agriculture in the interest of afforestation.

4- Providing timber intended for making agricultural implements or for constructing or repairing dwellings. The exercise of these rights shall be suspended when they are detrimental to the methods of exploitation and during the periods specified by the Forest Service; and in any event, and whatever the age or type of the forests, the holders of the right of grazing may only exercise this right in the places declared by the Forest Service to be defensible.

No land may be declared to be defensible before the expiry of a period of ten full years starting from the day on which felling or fire occurred therein, even partially, unless such felling was carried out by the Administration to thin the density of the trees.

: Rights of usufruct shall be established on the basis of official documents or by the means of proof provided for in Articles 37 and 38 of Decision No. 186 issued on 15 March 1926, as amended by Decision No. 44/LR dated 20/4/1932.
The Ministry of Agriculture may specify the type of forest products that may be assigned free of charge.

The delimitation of rights of usufruct subsisting over certain State forests in their capacity as abandoned or encumbered wooded lands, as well as the final recognition of these rights, shall be carried out within the conditions and in accordance with the procedures specified in the preceding Articles 42 and 43.

If a dispute arises regarding the basis of rights of this kind or their substance, the municipality or the village committee concerned with the matter may apply to the Council of State regarding the dispute within a period of one year from the date of publication of the decree.

If the right of usufruct subsisting over the abandoned or encumbered wooded lands is exploited by the municipality or the village for commerce, a fee for the Treasury shall be imposed on the municipality or the village by virtue of a decree.

The Forest Service shall designate the place where the recognised rights of usufruct shall be exercised and the conditions for the use of these rights within the limits of what the forest can bear and the plan established for its exploitation, and this designation shall be carried out as a whole for the entire forest or for a parcel thereof constituting an independent unit of exploitation, and it shall include the allocation in the aggregate to the municipality or the village of what it is entitled to enjoy by way of pasture and the taking of timber and firewood, which shall then be distributed among the individuals in accordance with custom and usage.

With the exception of the gathering of dry firewood lying on the ground or within reach of the hand and gathered without the use of a sickle, saw, hatchet, or other tools, and the gathering of naturally fallen fruits, the right of usufruct shall require obtaining a special licence from the Forest Service

State forests or parts thereof over which rights of usufruct subsist may be freed therefrom by way of consolidating these rights and confining them to a forest or specific parts thereof, and the rights of usufruct may also be purchased either by paying consideration therefor in cash or by exchanging them for another right of usufruct in the same forest or in a second forest. The transactions set out in this Article shall be completed either by mutual agreement or by a decision of the Council of State issued upon the application of the Forest Service

Forests the ownership or rights of usufruct whereof are disputed between the State on the one hand and municipalities, villages, or individuals on the other hand shall be deemed as State forests and shall be subject to the provisions of the two preceding Titles until the dispute is finally adjudicated

Forests that are owned in their entirety by villages shall be administered by the municipalities to which they belong, failing which they shall be administered by the village committees under the supervision of the Forest Service in accordance with special regulations established by a decree. No partition whatsoever of the ownership of these forests may be carried out among the inhabitants of the village itself.

The presidents of municipalities or the village committees shall appoint private guards at their own expense to preserve their forests, and this appointment shall not be effective except after the approval of the Forest Service. The Forest Service may suspend these guards from their duties or dismiss them.
Private guards shall enjoy, with respect to the performance of their duties, all the powers of public guards

Village forests may not be exploited except in accordance with the special regulations governing the methods of their exploitation, and for every exploitation an authorisation must be obtained in advance from the Forest Service, whether it be for felling trees, picking fruit, grazing, or otherwise.

No authorisation shall be granted to fell trees at ground level except where this matter is required by force majeure, and the authorisation shall be by virtue of a decree, and forest produce from the forests of municipalities and villages may not be transported, stored, or traded except in accordance with the provisions of Articles 33, 34, 35, 36, and 37.

The municipal council or the village committee shall undertake the exploitation directly or by way of contracting out after the approval of the Forest Service of this matter and in accordance with the conditions established by it.

The provisions of Articles 19 and 20 shall apply to presidents of municipalities, village committees, and mukhtars

Villages may not clear the forests that belong to them without a special authorisation by a decree taken pursuant to an investigation conducted by the Forest Service. There shall be deemed as clearing of the land any unlawful exploitation or extraction of tree stumps or permanent grazing of new growth in a spot that has been recently felled which takes place contrary to the special regulations governing the same and leads to the disappearance of the forest.

Neither the Forest Service nor its employees shall receive any remuneration whatsoever from municipalities and villages for the prosecutions they undertake regarding their forests and for all other acts relating to supervision, administration, and the establishment of exploitation plans.

One-third of the net income from the sale of the produce of village forests and the leasing of the pastures of these forests shall be compulsorily kept in the reserve funds by the president of the municipality or the president of the village committee, and both shall be personally liable for the execution of this measure. This one-third shall be used under the supervision of the Forest Service in afforestation works carried out on the lands of the village itself in accordance with the provisions of Article 88.

In the event that there are no communal lands suitable for afforestation in the village, the communal body- shall have the right to use this one-third to purchase barren lands in order to afforest them.

The distribution that may take place in kind among the inhabitants of the village of some of the produce of its forests shall be carried out in accordance with custom and usage, unless there is a deed to the contrary.

This distribution shall be carried out by the municipal council or the village committee, and they may decide, instead of distributing the produce among the inhabitants, to sell it for the benefit of the town or the village.

If the village forests are encumbered with rights of usufruct independent of the right of exploitation belonging to the town or the village that holds the bare ownership, the delimitation of these rights and their use shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of Title Two.

The provisions of Articles 38, 39, 40, and 41 relating to the inspection of felling sites shall apply to the forests of municipalities and villages.
Article 64: Individuals shall exercise in their forests all acts of disposition arising from ownership, subject to compliance with the following provisions:

No individual whomsoever may uproot or clear his forest except after submitting a written declaration thereof to the Forest Service through its officer in the district in which the forest is located at least three months in advance, and he must state in the declaration his elected domicile in the said district.

The local forest officer shall conduct an inspection of the forest comprising the location of the forest, its condition, its contents, and his opinion regarding the application, and he shall draw up a record thereof and send the papers to the Forest Service within a period of one month at the most.

The Forest Service shall examine the application and its attachments and shall decide to grant or reject it, and it shall give the applicant the permit in the first case and notify the party concerned of the reasons for rejection in the second case.
The party concerned may refer the matter to the Minister of Agriculture by a petition in which he sets out his objections to the reasons for rejection.

The Minister of Agriculture shall adjudicate the matter, and the party concerned shall be notified of the Minister's decision granting his application for a permit or upholding the reasons for rejection.
An objection against the Minister's decision of rejection may be lodged with the Council of State in accordance with the procedures set out in its special regulations.
If the time limit set out in Article 65 expires and the Administration has not taken any decision regarding the application, the permit shall be deemed to have been granted.

A permit for clearing or uprooting may not be refused except for the following reasons:

1- Preservation of soil on mountains or slopes.

2- Protection of the land from erosion and flooding by large and small rivers and torrents.

3- Preservation of springs or watercourses.

4- Protection of hills on the seashores and interior hills from sand invasion.

5- Maintenance of public health.

6- Preservation of a natural landscape belonging to a classified summer resort.

The prohibition of clearing or uprooting a forest for the preservation of a natural view of a classified summer resort and for public health shall entitle the owner of the forest to a right to compensation for damage if the prohibition is temporary and to compensation for expropriation if the prohibition is final.
Compensation for damage shall be determined administratively and the State Council shall be petitioned in respect thereof upon objection in accordance with the Expropriation Law.

A declaration alone shall suffice when the application for clearing relates:

First - to a forest since the planting of which twenty years have not elapsed unless the density of the trees covers the land. Second - to walled parks and gardens or those adjacent to dwellings. A modern forest established in place of a cleared forest or with the assistance of the State shall be subject to the authorisation procedure.

The exploitation of sloping lands of a forest and grazing therein after exploitation, felling, or fire shall be deemed tantamount to clearing the land if such exploitation or grazing leads to the destruction of the forest in part or in whole or constitutes a danger to the retention of soil on the slopes or to the protection of the land from erosion.

Any private individual who wishes to exploit his forest by way of felling, whatever its type and whatever its products may be, must submit two months in advance a written declaration thereof to the Forest Service through its officer in the district in which the forest is located. He must state in the application his name, the location of the forest, its area, its contents, and the number of trees if they are large trees, and the age and type of the trees, as well as the type and quantity of the products which he wishes to exploit.

The application shall be submitted and examined, and the decision issued in respect thereof shall be objected to, in accordance with the provisions of Articles 65, 66, 67, 68, 69, and 70

If the felling takes place for the restoration of the personal house of the owner in emergency cases, the perpetrator shall not be punished.
The authorisation for clearing and exploitation shall be granted by the Forest Service subject to the reservation of the rights of third parties.

The Forest Service may lay down general conditions for exploitation authorisations, a summary of which shall be inserted into every authorisation together with such special conditions as it may require.
An application for exploitation may not be refused except in the cases set forth in Article 71

The transport of forest products, unless the transport is by a human being or on the backs of animals, from the forests of private individuals, and the storage and trading thereof, shall be subject to the provisions of Articles 33, 34, 35, 36, and 37.

It may be declared by law that certain areas are protection areas if they comprise:

1- forests to which the conditions set forth in Article 71 apply

2- barren lands falling into ruin by reason of the flow of water, whereupon the provisions of Title One shall apply to the forests and barren lands in these areas and no clearing, exploitation, or grazing shall be permitted therein prior to obtaining a licence from the Forest Service.
The Forest Service, with the assistance of the Survey Department, shall demarcate these areas and set boundaries for them.

The Minister of Agriculture shall have the right to decide to prohibit the entry of livestock into afforested or non-afforested lands which are the property of private individuals and villages if their owners request in writing their protection from grazing. The prohibition decision shall be published in the Official Gazette and these lands shall become protected from the date of publication. The protection of these lands from the entry of livestock shall be subject to the provisions of Title One.

Owners may appoint private watchmen with the approval of the Forest Service, which may revoke the decision of approval in accordance with Article 55, and these watchmen shall have the same rights and be subject to the same duties as public watchmen.

It may be declared by law that certain areas are areas for afforestation for the purpose of expropriating them in the future if these areas comprise lands which it is necessary to afforest or restore either for their protection, or for their exploitation, or for stabilising the hills standing upon them, or for regulating the watercourses therein, or for preserving public health, or for improving summer resorts, provided that the expropriation is completed within a period of one year from the date of the expropriation decision. The afforestation shall take place at the expense of the State.

The owners of properties located in afforestation areas shall continue to dispose of them until they are divested of their ownership by expropriation or by way of exchange, and they shall during this period be responsible for the maintenance of the afforestation taking place therein, and in particular for protecting them from grazing.

At the end of every year, municipal councils and village committees must submit to the Forest Service a list of all the sums which they have collected from the revenues of village forests and pastures and which are kept for the execution of works relating to afforestation pursuant to the provisions of Article 61

The Forest Service, upon perusing this list and carrying out a local investigation and as the case may require, shall instruct the municipalities and village committees to use the available sums in the execution of afforestation works under the supervision and technical control of the Forest Service.

Afforestation shall take place in the barren village lands which the Forest Service designates from among the lands of the village. The municipality or the village committee shall be responsible for the maintenance of these works after their completion, in particular for protecting them from grazing.

The available sums which have not been expended on these works shall be kept until they are used thereafter, and their use for other than this purpose shall be prohibited unless authorised by decree. In that case, one quarter of the sum authorised to be used for other than afforestation shall be paid on trust in the name of the Ministry of Agriculture to be expended for the purpose of general afforestation through a committee composed of the Minister of Agriculture as Chairman, and the membership of the Director General of the Ministry of Agriculture and the Head of the Forest Service.

Private individuals, municipalities, and village committees may obtain free of charge from the State through the Forest Service seeds or young saplings for the purpose of afforesting their lands.

The cost of the seeds, planting, and protection of the saplings shall be borne by the interested parties under the control of the Administration, provided that the State may also bear a part of these expenses by way of encouraging afforestation if the intended works are included in a general afforestation programme laid down by the Forest Service.

Forests established on the summits or slopes of mountains or on hills by the act of their owners and which are neither adjacent to their dwellings nor walled shall be exempted from the land tax for a period of thirty years, and forests the establishment of which is renewed after their burning shall also be exempted from the land tax for a period of ten years, provided that their owner is not the one who burned them.

The period of exemption set forth in the preceding paragraph shall commence from the year of the establishment of the forest, and the effect of the exemption shall not run except from the day of the inspection which the Forest Service carries out on the afforestation works upon a written application from the owner.

The Minister of Agriculture may impose compulsory protection from the entry of livestock for grazing upon the areas which he deems necessary to protect for the purpose of their afforestation or the maintenance of their forests, whether they are the property of the State, of municipalities and villages, or of private individuals.

The Minister of Agriculture may decide to remove goats from the lands of villages if this measure is requested by the owners of three quarters of their area, provided that each family of goat owners shall have the right to retain three head tied in a pen, and they may not be brought into State-owned lands, communal lands, or private properties.

The decision of the Minister of Agriculture in this respect shall be published in the Official Gazette and circulated to the villages located within the protected area and in its vicinity, whereupon the provisions of Title One shall apply to the protected areas.

It is prohibited to fell trees of stone pine, Aleppo pine, calabrian pine, cypress, Cedar of Lebanon, fir, and all other resinous forest trees from forests owned by private individuals, communal forests, and State-owned forests except by the method of technical thinning, and an applicant for felling shall not be given a thinning licence unless he holds a certificate from the Forest Service signed by the Minister of Agriculture proving his afforestation of an area of land equivalent to two thousand square metres for every fifty trees of the type requested to be felled.

Forest officers and guards shall investigate contraventions committed against the provisions of this Law in the area to which the said officials are assigned. The guards shall personally draw up the reports, date them and sign them, failing which they shall be null and void, and shall send them forthwith to their immediate superior, who shall refer them to the Summary Court or the Public Prosecution, as the case may be.

The seizure report must state:

1- The nature of the contravention and the place and date of its commission.

2- The name, surname, profession and residence of the offender, and if the offender is a married woman, a minor child or a servant, the name, surname and residence of the husband, natural guardian or master must also be stated.

3- The number of trees upon which the contravention occurred and their age, species and size, and if the trees are small, their weight shall be estimated in accordance with Article 143.

4 - The number and type of seized tools.

5- The number and species of the animals by means of which the contravention was committed or which were found grazing contrary to the law, as well as the age of the forests in which the contravention was committed.

6- And in a contravention of breaking up forest land for the purpose of cultivating it, the ploughed area shall be stated.

Judicial police officials and members of the gendarmerie and police may also record contraventions of the provisions of this Law.

The said officials shall send the original copy of the report to the Summary Court or the Public Prosecution and a copy of the report by way of information to the Forest Service in the district in which the contravention was committed.
Contraventions of the provisions of this Law shall be proved by reports drawn up in accordance with the rules, and in the absence of reports or their insufficiency, by the testimony of witnesses.
At the end of every month, the Summary Court shall send to the Forest Service official attached to it a schedule of the outcome of the judgments rendered in the actions brought before it.

Forest officers and guards shall have the right to seize livestock, implements, vehicles, draught gear, pack animals and all means of transport used by the perpetrators of contraventions, and to place them in the custody of a third party, and to trace the things taken by the offenders to the places to which they were transported or the places in which they are presumed to be, even if outside the area of their office.

Provided that they may not enter houses, courtyards and enclosed places except in the presence of the Summary Judge or whoever he deputises from among the security forces, mayors and mukhtars, or in the presence of one of these directly, and these latter may not refuse to accompany the forest officials forthwith upon their request, and they must sign the reports of the proceedings carried out in their presence.

Officials of the Forest Service may request the assistance of the security forces directly or through their superiors to record contraventions of the provisions of this Law and to search for and seize the forest produce that is the subject of the contravention.

Forest officials may arrest any unknown person whom they surprise in flagrante delicto and hand him over to the security forces.

The third party to whom the seized livestock and produce are delivered must be of good conduct, solvent, and residing in a place near the site of the contravention, and if it is not possible to find such a person, they shall be delivered to the mukhtar of the nearest village to the site of the contravention, and this latter may not refuse to accept the seizure into his custody.

A copy of the seizure report shall be delivered to the third party or the mukhtar, who shall give a receipt for his taking delivery of the seized livestock and things.

If it appears from the contents of the seizure report that the seized produce was taken from State forests, the Forest Service shall order its sale for the account of the State within the three days following the seizure, unless it sees fit to defer the matter.

If the seizure is effected upon livestock, vehicles, draught animals or pack animals, or upon produce not coming from State forests, a copy of the seizure report must, immediately upon its being drawn up, be sent to the registry of a Summary Court within three days. Whoever claims entitlement to the seized things may inspect the said report.

The Summary Judge may, upon the request of the owner of the livestock or things seized in accordance with the preceding Article, lift the seizure provisionally against security and immediate payment of the expenses of the seized property.

If five days elapse from the date of the seizure and no one claims the seized livestock or things, or their owner does not furnish the security and pay the expenses of the seized property within the same period, the Summary Judge shall order their sale by public auction.

This sale shall take place in the nearest market through the clerk of the court and in the presence of an official of the Forest Service.

There shall be recovered from the sale price the expenses of custody, then the expenses of the sale, then the amount of the fine and damages which the judge determines upon a provisional estimate by the official of the Forest Service, and any surplus over that shall be returned to the person entitled thereto.
None of the seized livestock shall be sold, unless its owner is unknown, save such thereof as is necessary to pay the sums set forth in the preceding Article.

If judgment is rendered for acquittal, the owner of the livestock shall be entitled to recover the sale price in full, and the expenses of seizure and sale shall remain borne by the Forest Service, unless the livestock was sold because its owner was unknown or because of his neglect to claim it within the period set forth in Article 124, in which case he shall only be entitled to recover the net proceeds of the sale after deducting all expenses.

Reports of contraventions drawn up and signed by two sworn officers of the Forest Service shall be acted upon until their forgery is proved; as for other reports, they shall be acted upon until the contrary is proved.

Reports drawn up by private guards concerning contraventions committed in forests owned by individuals shall be acted upon until the contrary is proved. These guards shall send the reports of contraventions to the official of the Forest Service in the area to which they are assigned.
Forest officials may request all proceedings required for the trial and the execution of the judgment.

The Forest Service may appeal, through its delegated officials, against judgments in respect of financial penalties and personal damages, and it may not waive its appeal after it has been lodged without the approval of the Minister of Agriculture, and this right of appeal is independent of the right of the Public Prosecution, which may appeal against judgments even if the Forest Service has acquiesced in them.

The Forest Service may compound, subject to the ratification of the Minister of Agriculture, in respect of contraventions before final judgment is rendered thereon, provided that the compounding consideration is not less than the minimum fine and damages prescribed by law therefor if the contravention was committed in the forests of the State, municipalities and villages.

And compounding for less than the said minimum is permissible in respect of a contravention committed in the forests of individuals even after final judgment is rendered thereon, and that is in respect of the fine only.

If during the trial a plea is raised that would strip the act of its criminal character, and this plea rests upon a disputed title deed or upon an official document equivalent to a title deed, the court may grant the defendant a time limit of one month to refer the matter of the dispute over ownership to the competent judicial authority, so that if he fails to do so or neglects to pursue the action before the said authority, the criminal court shall adjudicate upon the contravention.

For contraventions committed by minor children, their natural guardians and testamentary guardians shall be civilly liable for them, just as a master shall be civilly liable for contraventions committed by a person in his service during his work for him. This liability shall include damages, expenses and the restitution of the things taken.
If several persons participate in committing a single contravention or connected contraventions, they shall be sentenced to the fine jointly and severally as well.

Any contravention of the provisions of Articles 19 and 58 relating to the sale of the produce of State, municipal and village forests by public auction resulting from secret participation in the sale or lease effected by auction or by mutual agreement, or from collusion to harm or disrupt the same, or from purchasing the produce at lower than normal prices by means of an agreement to reduce bids, shall be punishable by a fine of five hundred thousand to one million Lebanese pounds and by imprisonment from one month to six months, or by either of these two penalties.

This shall be in addition to the compensation which the Administration may claim for the damage sustained by it, including the cancellation of the auction where necessary.

- Any person who introduces livestock into a forest in which grazing is prohibited, or into cultivated land or land planted with fruit trees and placed under compulsory protection pursuant to a decision of the Minister of Agriculture in accordance with the provisions of Articles 83 and 92 of this Law, shall be punishable by a fine of a minimum of 250.000 L.L. (two hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese pounds.

Any person who contravenes the provisions of Article 23 shall be punishable by the same penalty.

The herdsman may be sentenced to imprisonment from two weeks to three months. If the contravention is repeated or committed at night or in a forest less than ten years old, the maximum fine shall be imposed.

Any contravention of any of the clauses of the auction records, the general and special books of conditions, and the decisions of lease by mutual agreement provided for in Article 28 shall be punishable by a fine of fifty thousand to one million Lebanese pounds.

Any person who contravenes the provisions of Articles 59, 65 and 75 shall be punishable by a fine of ten thousand to two million Lebanese pounds for each hectare cleared, and upon repetition of the contravention by the maximum fine, and in addition thereto a sentence of imprisonment from one month to six months may be imposed.

The same penalty mentioned in this Article shall apply to the contraventions set forth in Article 140 of the Penal Code if the judgment orders the restoration of the cleared lands to their forested state, in which case the convicted person must carry this out within a period of one year at most, failing which the Forest Service shall carry out the afforestation within the specified period at the expense of the convicted person.

If there are multiple convicted persons, the expense of afforestation shall be recovered from them jointly and severally.

The representative of the municipality or village who orders the clearing of the land or tolerates the clearing thereof while having knowledge of the matter shall be punishable by the same penalty.
Any person who clears forest lands that are the property of others or ploughs land therein shall be punishable by the penalties provided for in the preceding Article.

Any person who breaks, destroys, moves or removes boundary markers or signs planted following an official demarcation of forests or places designated for afforestation shall be punishable by a fine of one hundred thousand to one million Lebanese pounds and by imprisonment from ten days to three months, or by either of these two penalties.

The penalty of imprisonment shall compulsorily be imposed if the contravention is repeated or is accompanied by an encroachment upon forest lands by clearing them or by carrying out agricultural works therein.

In all cases, the boundary markers and signs shall be replanted and the places restored to their former state at the expense of the offender.

Any contravention of the provisions of Article 99 shall be punishable by a fine equivalent to ten times the value of the thing taken in accordance with the tariff fixed each year pursuant to a decision of the Minister of Agriculture.

In all cases, the produce that is the subject of the contravention shall be seized.

Any person found between sunrise and sunset in woods and forests that are the property of others outside the normal roads and paths while carrying tools for cutting firewood or for extracting bark, and any person found by night or by day in lands upon which the Administration has commenced works of afforestation or planting or stabilization of hills and has prohibited entry thereto outside the normal roads and paths, shall be punishable by a fine of twenty-five thousand to one hundred thousand pounds, and upon repetition the maximum fine shall be imposed.

Any person who cuts down or uproots, contrary to the provisions of this Law, trees whose circumference exceeds twenty centimetres at a height of one metre above the ground shall be punishable by a fine of ten thousand to five hundred thousand Lebanese pounds for each tree cut down or uprooted according to its size, and the fine shall be calculated in proportion to the weight of the tree cut down or uprooted if its circumference is less than twenty centimetres at the rate of two thousand pounds for each kilogram of firewood and twenty-five thousand for each kilogram of charcoal.

A sentence of imprisonment from ten days to six months may also be imposed.

Any person who contravenes the provisions of Articles 26 and 27 shall be punishable by the same penalty.

The penalty shall be increased twentyfold if the cutting falls upon cedar and juniper trees.

The mutilation of trees by severe mutilation for the purpose of grazing and cutting their tops and branches without distinction between them, and taking fallen branches or firewood and cutting bark contrary to the provisions of this Law, shall be punishable by the penalty prescribed for cutting down trees.

Any person who counterfeits or forges the mark of the State forests hammer mentioned in Article 13, or fraudulently uses the original hammers, shall be punishable by imprisonment from one year to three years and by a fine of one hundred thousand to one million Lebanese pounds.

Any person who destroys one of these hammers shall be punishable by a fine of five hundred thousand to one million pounds and by imprisonment from three months to six months, and upon repetition of the contravention the maximum penalty shall be imposed.

Any contravention of the provisions of Articles 33, 34, 35, 36, 37 and 57 - last paragraph thereof, and Articles 80, 101, 102, 103, 104, 105 and 106, shall be punishable by a fine of five hundred thousand pounds to one million five hundred thousand Lebanese pounds or by imprisonment from one month to six months.

If the contravention causes a fire that reaches the forests, the offender shall be sentenced to imprisonment from from six months to three years.

In all cases, in addition to the penalties specified in this Title, judgment shall be passed for the restitution of the forest materials taken or cut from State forests and for the confiscation of the saws, axes, cleavers, other tools and means of transport used to commit the contravention; as for the forest materials cut or taken from municipal and village forests or from forests owned by individuals, they shall be seized as security for the payment of the fines and compensations awarded.

As for the cutting equipment, judgment shall be passed for its confiscation.

Any contravention of the provisions of Article 109 shall punish its perpetrator by a fine of one hundred thousand to one million Lebanese pounds; if the offender is among those who have a right of usufruct over the forest, he shall be deprived of his right of usufruct for a period ranging between two years and five years by judgment of the court.

Any person who contravenes the provisions of Articles 109 and 110 shall be punishable by a fine of one million to one million five hundred thousand Lebanese pounds, and judgment shall be passed for the demolition of the building at the expense of its owner and under the supervision of the Forest Service.

This Law shall be published in the Official Gazette.

With effect from 01/01/1995, the official minimum monthly wage has been fixed at the amount of two hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese pounds, and it shall be applied in accordance with the provisions of Articles 1 and 2 of Law No. 36/67 dated 16/05/1967

There shall be added to the wages received by wage-earners on 31/12/1994 a cost-of-living increase of twenty per cent of the wage, provided that the increase shall not be less than fifty thousand pounds for the wage-earners covered by the minimum wage in accordance with the provisions of Articles 1 and 2 of Law No. 36/67 and shall not exceed the amount of two hundred and fifty thousand pounds.

For the purpose of calculating the value of the cost-of-living increase, account shall be taken of the basic wage which the wage-earner was receiving prior to his benefiting from any cost-of-living increase granted to him after the enforcement of Decree No. 4631 dated 10/01/1994 and up until the issuance of this Decree.

There shall be deemed a cost-of-living increase, and shall be deducted from the value of the increase provided for in Article 2 above, the increases expressly described in the contract, or in the regulations, or in the administrative records or statements, or in consensual agreements, or those granted by reason of the cost of living after the enforcement of Decree No. 4631 dated 10/01/1994 and up until the issuance of this Decree, and which covered all the wage-earners of the establishment without exception at the same time.

Where the value of this increase exceeds the value of the increase prescribed in Article 2 of this Decree, it may not be reduced. Where, however, it is less than it, the wage-earner shall benefit from the difference only.

In addition to the increase provided for in Article 2 above, the wage-earner shall be granted, for each day of actual attendance at the workplace, a daily transport allowance the value of which is eight thousand Lebanese pounds, for one year pending the activation of the means of public transport, and it may be extended for a second year in the event that that proves impracticable during the first year".

The wage-earner shall benefit from a school grant in respect of his children for the academic year 2010 - 2011, and it may be renewed for a second year in the event that it proves impracticable to activate the public school during the first year. The value of this grant shall be determined as follows:

- Two hundred thousand Lebanese pounds for a student enrolled in public or free schools or institutions specialised for persons with disabilities.

- Five hundred thousand Lebanese pounds for a student enrolled in private schools or universities. - Three hundred thousand Lebanese pounds for a student enrolled in the Lebanese University.

This grant shall be paid in accordance with the following principles:

1 - That the pupil or student has completed the fourth year of his age during the academic year and has not exceeded the twenty-fifth.

2 - That the student is registered in one of the regular schools, and night schools shall not be deemed regular schools.

3 - The grant shall not be due to a female employee in respect of her children unless they are dependent upon her and she receives family allowances in respect of them, or if she is married to a wage-earner who does not receive a school grant in respect of his children.

4 - The wage-earner shall not benefit from the grant unless one year has elapsed since his employment in the establishment prior to the commencement of the academic year.

5 - The number of beneficiary children shall be fixed at three children only, and the value of the grant in respect of them shall not exceed the amount of one million Lebanese pounds.

6 - If the establishment pays to the wage-earner a grant allowance less than what is determined above, the wage-earner shall benefit from the difference; if it pays to him more than that, it shall remain an acquired right for him.

7 - The school grant shall not be deemed an element of the wage, and no fee, tax or contribution to the National Social Security Fund shall be paid in respect of it, and it shall not enter into the calculation of the end-of-service indemnity.

The provisions of this Decree shall apply to all employers and wage-earners subject to the provisions of the Labour Law issued on 23/09/1946 and those contracting on the basis of a percentage, subject to what is stated in paragraph 4 of Article 4 of this Decree.
This Decree shall be published and notified where needed and shall enter into force with effect from 01/01/1995

The mission of the General Security is to collect information on behalf of the Government and in particular political, economic and social information, and the General Security shall contribute to the judicial investigation within the limits of offences committed against the internal and external security of the State and shall likewise contribute with the Security Forces in monitoring the land, air and sea borders and monitoring foreigners on Lebanese territory, and it shall also undertake the granting of laissez-passers.
The General Security is a Directorate General subject to the authority of the Minister of the Interior and directly attached to him.

The training of commissioners, non-commissioned officers and members of the General Security shall take place at the Security Forces Institute, which comprises a special branch organised for this purpose.

The Director shall ensure the command of the General Security and the administration of its affairs and shall attend to the instruction and training of the commissioners, non-commissioned officers and members.

The Director of the General Security shall exercise in respect of his Directorate the same powers and rights as are exercised by the Director General of the Internal Security Forces and unit commanders in respect of the Internal Security Forces, with the exception of the following matters in which the Minister of the Interior decides the penalties that exceed the rights of a unit commander in the Internal Security Forces.

The Director General of the General Security shall in principle be appointed from among the Senior Commissioners of the General Security, provided that he may exceptionally be appointed from among officials of the First Category or from among officers of the Internal Security Forces or the Army or from among non-officials who have held a degree in law or its equivalent for at least twelve years.

The internal organisation of the General Security and the numerical tables relating to equipment shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior

Below is the hierarchy of ranks of non-commissioned officials in the General Security and their equivalence with the ranks of the Internal Security Forces:

Ranks.................... Equivalence

Trainee Constable .......... Trainee Gendarme or Trainee Policeman

Constable .................. Gendarme

Inspector Grade 3 ........ Corporal

Trainee Inspector Grade 2..Trainee Sergeant

Inspector Grade 2 ......... Sergeant

First Inspector.............. First Sergeant

Senior Inspector ........... Sub-Officer

Senior First Inspector ...... First Sub-Officer

Chief Inspector .......... Chief Warrant Officer

First Chief Inspector ..... First Chief Warrant Officer

All inspectors of the General Security shall be considered "non-commissioned officers".

Every non-commissioned officer has the right of command over those below him. If ranks are equal, the right of command shall belong to the more senior in rank, and if seniority in rank is equal, seniority in the preceding rank shall be relied upon, and so on down to the last grade of the hierarchy of ranks in the General Security, and if seniority in the last rank is equal, the right of command shall belong to the more senior in service.

A Constable of the General Security shall be recruited from among:

1- Civilians at a ratio of 60 per cent in accordance with the following conditions:

a- Holding the Lebanese Brevet certificate or a Lebanese certificate officially equivalent thereto.

b - Being a completed 18 years of age on the date of submitting the application for enrolment and not having exceeded 25 years of age.

c - Being at least 168 centimetres in height, while fulfilling the remaining conditions set out in Article 19 of the Legislative Decree relating to the Internal Security Forces.

2- Gendarmes and policemen in the Internal Security Forces at a ratio of 40 per cent in accordance with instructions issued by the Director General of the General Security in agreement with the Director General of the Internal Security Forces.

Inspectors of the General Security of the Second Grade shall be recruited from among:

1- Civilians at a ratio of 60 per cent in accordance with the following conditions:

a - Holding the Lebanese Baccalaureate certificate - Part Two or the Lebanese Technical Baccalaureate certificate - Part Two.

b - Being a completed 18 years of age on the date of submitting the application for enrolment and not having exceeded 28 years of age, while fulfilling the remaining conditions set out in paragraph c of Item One of the preceding Article.

2- Inspectors Grade 3 in the General Security at a ratio of 40 per cent, by virtue of a special competitive examination.
The remaining posts for the other ranks shall be reserved for the promotion of non-commissioned officers and members of the General Security.

The tenant may not assign the leased premises or sublease them in whole or in part except with the written consent of the owner and under the conditions agreed upon. If the original tenant assigns the leased premises and is expressly authorised to do so in the original lease contract or the lease contract extended by operation of law, the assignees shall benefit from the statutory extension and shall replace the original tenant, and their relationship with the owner shall become direct.

In the event of a total or partial sublease with the express consent of the owner in the original or extended contract, the lease relationship shall remain confined between the owner and the original tenant, and the term of the sublease shall expire upon the expiry of the term of the original lease.

The owner must summon the subtenant to the proceedings in every action brought against the original tenant, and the judgment rendered against the original tenant shall have the force of res judicata against the subtenant, provided that the subtenant shall be entitled to claim compensation from the original tenant if bad faith, fault or negligence on the part of the latter is established.

First: As amended pursuant to Law No. 336 dated 24/5/94, Official Gazette 21 dated 26/05/1994

A- The owner may request, for his own residence or the residence of one of his children, the recovery of the residential leased premises, provided that he proves a family necessity compelling him to recover them, and that neither he nor the person for whose benefit the recovery is requested owns another dwelling that is suitable and fit for habitation, unoccupied, and equivalent in standard to the leased premises sought to be recovered within the same municipal area or an adjacent municipal area; and the owner may request the recovery of leased premises contiguous to the dwelling in which he resides if the purpose of the recovery is to annex the recovered leased premises to his residence and make it a dwelling meeting the needs of the family.

B - An owner who is the proprietor of a hospital, or an educational, instructional or charitable institution, or an orphanage, who has leased out for residential purposes a part of his property or of his contiguous properties, may recover this part provided that it is added to the principal property and used for the purposes of the institution.

C - The owner may request the recovery of the leased premises in order to demolish them and erect a new building in their place, and he may, in order to erect new constructions, request the recovery of a structure standing on the roof if such structure occupies less than half of the area permitted by the Building Law or if he wishes to erect two or more new storeys.

It is required that the recovery of the structure be technically necessary for the erection of the new constructions, and an owner who wishes to construct a storey above his leased building may request the recovery of the part that is technically necessary for the erection of the new constructions.

D - The owner requesting recovery pursuant to items A, B and C above must pay the tenant fair compensation assessed by the courts, provided that it shall not be less than 25% twenty-five per cent and shall not exceed 50% fifty per cent of the value of the leased premises.

Second: In all cases of recovery against compensation:

As amended pursuant to Law No. 336 dated 24/5/94, Official Gazette 21 dated 26/5/94.

The amount of compensation shall be determined on the basis of its quantum at the date of issuance of the final judgment in light of the assessment elements available in the action, and in actions in which no final and conclusive decision has been issued, the compensation shall be determined in accordance with the provisions of the law under which the action was brought, provided that the compensation shall not exceed fifty per cent of the value of the leased premises at the date of issuance of the final judgment.

An owner who has recovered his leased premises pursuant to the provisions of this Law shall be liable to pay the tenant additional compensation equivalent to half the value of the awarded compensation without the tenant being obliged to prove the damage

suffered by him, in the two cases set out below.

1- If the leased premises were recovered pursuant to either of the two purposes provided for in paragraphs A and B of item First of Article Eight of this Law and the owner did not use them, without a legitimate justification, in accordance with the required purpose within a period of one year from the date of vacating, or did not continue, without a legitimate justification, to use them in that manner for at least three years.

2- If the leased premises were recovered for the purpose of demolition and reconstruction pursuant to the purpose provided for in paragraph C of item First of Article Eight of this Law and the owner did not commence construction, without a legitimate justification, within a period of one year from the date of vacating by the last tenant, and did not complete it within a period not exceeding five years from the date of commencement of the work without a legitimate justification, or if he used the recovered leased premises for his own residence or for his personal benefit or leased them to a third party during the one-year period set out above.

The tenant's right to extension shall be forfeited and he, or whoever legally succeeds him, shall be ordered to vacate in the following cases:

a - If he fails to pay the rent that has fallen due from him within two months after having been served, either in person or through an adult member of his family residing with him, with a notice addressed to him by means of an unsealed registered postcard with acknowledgment of receipt, or by means of a letter addressed to him through a Notary Public, or by means of a notice issued by the Execution Department in accordance with the provisions of the twenty-second Article of this Law. Where it proves impossible to effect the services of process referred to in the preceding paragraph, service shall be effected by publication in two local daily newspapers designated by the Summary Affairs Judge after he has ascertained the impossibility of effecting service, upon the request of the lessor by way of a petition that is exempt from any fee or stamp of any kind whatsoever. A copy of the notice shall be affixed to the door of the leased premises by a process server, and the two-month period shall run from the date of the last act of publication or affixation. Where it proves impossible to effect service of the notice issued by the Execution Department, service shall be effected by publication, in accordance with the very same procedures, pursuant to a decision rendered by the Head of the Execution Department. The tenant shall bear the expenses of these formalities.

b - If he misuses the leased premises by causing damage therein not resulting from normal use, or uses them in a harmful manner contrary to the terms of the lease without the lessor's written consent. The practice by a tenant who is a liberal professional of his profession in a part of the leased premises designated for his residence, for security reasons that forced him to leave the seat of practice of his profession, shall not be deemed a misuse of the leased premises; in this case, the owner shall not be entitled to claim any compensation from the tenant, nor may the tenant claim any additional compensation therefor from the owner in cases of recovery of possession.

Installations erected by the tenant at his own expense shall not be deemed a misuse of the leased premises, provided that they do not impair the structural soundness of the building; works for the installation of an elevator and a water tank, or the provision of heating, cooling, or hot water, shall be deemed to be of this nature.

"With the exception of simple superficial ornamentation and decoration works, a tenant who wishes to avail himself of the provisions of this Article must summon the lessor before the Summary Affairs Judge to seek permission to carry out the works he wishes to perform, which he must specify, in order to enable the Court to assess their legality and appropriateness."

The tenant or tenants shall bear the costs of an insurance policy against all risks that may arise from the works they perform, the costs of the aforementioned works, and the costs of restoring the parts of the building that may have been damaged by reason of the works to their former condition, without having any right of recourse against the owner to claim the same or any part thereof, whether during their occupancy of the leased premises or on the date of termination of such occupancy.

The value of the improvements resulting from the works mentioned in this item (b) shall not be included in the calculation of the recovery compensation nor in the calculation of the fair rent.

c - If he assigns the leased premises or sublets them in whole or in part without the owner's written consent or in breach of the original or extended lease contract; in this case, the subtenant or assignee must be joined as a party to the proceedings, as amended by Law 336 dated 24/5/94, Official Gazette 21 dated 26/5/1994

d - If the tenant occupies by way of lease, and without family necessity, more than one leased premises designated solely for residential use, separated from one another by no more than seven kilometers in a radial line, he must specify, within a period of six months commencing from the effective date of this amending Law, the leased premises in respect of which he wishes to benefit from the right of extension; if he fails to do so, it shall fall to the Court to specify the dwelling in respect of which the right of extension is forfeited.

e - If the tenant constructs a building for residential use, or if one becomes vacant for him, or if he acquires ownership of a vacant building of which he owns at least three-quarters and which is fit and suitable for his residence and equivalent in standard to the leased premises he occupies in the same city or village, or in a place no more than seven kilometers in a radial line from the leased premises. In these cases, the husband, the wife, the minor children residing with the tenant, as well as the adult children of the tenant who are his dependents, shall be deemed to be a single person for the application of the provisions of items "d" and "e", unless the condition of family necessity provided for in item "a" of the eighth Article of this Law is met in the situation of the children, subject to actual residence within a period not exceeding one year from the date of completion of the building, acquisition of ownership, or vacancy, and continued residence for a period of at least three years.

The following shall be exempted from the provisions of items d and e:

1- The case in which the tenant, or whoever is deemed with him to be a single person, owns an apartment for use as a commercial or tourist office or for the practice of a profession, and actually uses it for this purpose within six months from the date of acquisition of ownership and continues in the same use for a period of at least three years, under pain of forfeiture of the right to extension without any compensation.

2- The case in which the tenant became the owner of a vacant dwelling between 13/4/75 and the date of promulgation of this Law, provided that he sold this dwelling prior to the promulgation of this Law.

f- If he abandons the leased premises for non-security reasons for an uninterrupted period of one year as from the effective date of this Law, notwithstanding his continued payment of the rent.

Lebanese officials and employees serving in official Lebanese missions abroad shall be exempted from the provisions of this item.

g- If he abandons the leased premises for non-security reasons for an uninterrupted period of six months while owing any part of the rent, and has no residence known to the owner at which he may be served with the notice to pay, or has not elected a domicile at which he may be served with such notice, designated by him to the lessor by means of a letter or an unsealed registered postcard with acknowledgment of receipt in accordance with the procedures for service provided for in item a of this Article.

h - If the non-Lebanese tenant abandons the leased premises for an uninterrupted period of 6 months.

- Leases concluded with effect from 1/1/1967 up to 31/12/1972 inclusive 332 three hundred and thirty-two-fold.

- Leases concluded with effect from 1/1/1973 up to 31/12/1978 inclusive 236 two hundred and thirty-six-fold.

- Leases concluded with effect from 1/1/1979 up to 31/12/1982 inclusive 168 one hundred and sixty-eight-fold.

b- With effect from 23/7/1992, the rents concluded with effect from 1/1/1987 or concluded prior to this date and whose first contractual term expired after 31/12/1987 shall be multiplied as follows:

- Leases whose first contractual term expired prior to 1/1/1988 (8) eight-fold.

- Leases whose first contractual term expired between 1/1/1988 inclusive and 19/12/1988 inclusive: (6) six-fold.

- Leases whose first contractual term expired between 20/12/1988 inclusive and 29/6/1989 inclusive (4) four-fold.

- Leases whose first contractual term expired between 30/6/1989 inclusive and 31/12/1990 inclusive (3) three-fold.

- Leases whose first contractual term expired between 1/1/1991 inclusive and 31/12/1991 inclusive (2) two-fold.

2- Floors above and below the ground floor leased for commercial or industrial purposes: the rents of these floors shall be determined at three-quarters of the rents payable on the ground floors.

Second:

Premises leased for non-commercial or non-industrial purposes:

The rents of premises leased for non-commercial or non-industrial purposes shall be determined at three-quarters of the rents of premises leased for a commercial or industrial purpose.

Third:

For the purpose of calculating the multiplication, the rent which was

payable by the lessee on 31/12/1986 shall be adopted in respect of the contracts specified in Item -a- of Article Thirteen of this Law.

The rent which was payable by the lessee on the date of expiry of the first contractual term shall also be adopted in respect of the contracts specified in Item - b - of Article Thirteen, and the consensual increase occurring after the entry into force of amended Law No. 20/82 shall be taken into consideration such that whatever thereof exceeds the statutory increase shall remain a vested right of the lessor and whatever falls short thereof must be paid by the lessee.

Every increase agreed to by the lessee which he is not bound to pay pursuant to the law shall be deemed consensual for the application of the provisions of this Item, and a consensual waiver of previous statutory reductions shall not be deemed to constitute a consensual increase.

Where, however, the fair rent has been determined consensually or judicially, the effective date of this rent shall be adopted as the basis for calculating the multiplications.

Where, however, the rent has been subject to a consensual increase in consideration of additional benefits for the lessee, the rent shall be apportioned into two parts:

The first part represents the basic rent, to which the multiplications pertaining to the date of commencement of the lease shall apply.

The second part represents the increase, to which the multiplications specified for the year in which the said increase occurred shall apply.

When the lease contract covers sections whose leases commenced on different dates or sections covered by several items of this Article, the rent shall be apportioned to determine the multiplication according to the date of commencement of the lease of each of them or according to its location in the building.

Fourth:

Premises leased for the purposes enumerated in Articles 6, 7 and 8 of the Code of Land Commerce shall be deemed commercial or industrial.
