Premises which extend over the ground floor, the floor above it and the floor below it shall be deemed to constitute ground floors if these floors are internally connected to one another within the leased premises in a single building and leased to a single lessee in a single contract.

If a single contract covers sections covered by several items in this Article, it shall be for the court to apportion the rent where necessary in order to determine the rate of the increase.

Fifth:

With effect from 23/7/1992 and after the multiplication mentioned in this Article, the rents shall be linked and successively increased at a rate equal to half the rate of the increase occurring each time on the first bracket of salary, specified in the decrees relating to the cost-of-living increase and the determination of wages of employees and workers, with effect from the date of enforcement of each increase.

- If the lessee vacates the leased premises voluntarily within a period of three months from the effective date of this amending Law or prior to this date, he shall be exempted from paying the previous rents accrued with effect from 23/7/1992, and whatever has been paid thereof may be recovered.

Sixth:

The increases provided for in Article Thirteen of this Law shall fall due from the effective date of Law No. 160/92 dated 22/7/1992 without any retroactive effect, and all agreements executed after Law 160/92 which are contrary to this Item Sixth shall be deemed null and void; furthermore, whatever was previously paid by the lessee on account of the retroactive effect under Article Thirteen of Law 160/92 prior to its amendment shall be deemed payments on account of the rents, and the taxes and fees which the lessor may have paid on the amounts he received on account of the retroactive effect shall be deemed to constitute a payment on account of the taxes and fees that shall accrue upon him in respect of subsequent rents.

Subject to the provisions of Article Twelve of this Law, the lessee's right to extension shall lapse pursuant to the provisions of Items (a), (b), (c), (f) and (g) of Article Ten of this Law. In addition to the grounds for forfeiture set forth in the preceding paragraph, the right to extension of the lessee of premises leased for commercial or industrial purposes shall lapse if he effects a change in the intended use of the leased premises as specified in the lease contract.

The owner of real property leased for non-residential purposes has the right to recover the leased premises pursuant to the provisions of Paragraphs - b - c - of Item First and Item Second of Article Eight of this Law, and the owner shall be liable, in addition to the compensation specified in this Article, for further compensation for the loss sustained by the lessee as a result of the eviction (such as key money, loss of location and clientele, interruption of business, and others).

First:

The following shall be subject to the provisions of the fair rent, provided that this rent does not exceed the rate of one hundred per cent (100%) of the value of the rents after calculating the increase provided for in this amending Law:

A- Premises leased to a natural or legal person who is or becomes the owner of buildings or undivided shares in premises where his share of the total of their actual rents exceeds ten times the rent of the leased premises which he occupies.

For the calculation of these rents, the husband, wife and children residing with the lessee shall be deemed as a single person, and the owner shall not have the right to demand the fair rent from a single lessee or from whoever replaces him by virtue of this Law more than once.

B - Leases deemed to be an element of a commercial establishment and which are subject to a free management contract in accordance with the provisions of Legislative Decree 11/67, throughout the period of the free management.

C - Leases deemed to be an element of a commercial establishment in the event of their assignment or in the event of their sale through the judicial departments.

Second:

The rents of premises leased by the State, public institutions and municipalities shall be subject to the multiples provided for in Article Thirteen of this Law up to 31/12/1993, and shall be increased by a rate of one hundred per cent (100%) starting from 1/1/1994 and onwards on the basis of the rent due on 31/12/1993. For the purpose of applying the provisions of this item, the Government is authorised, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, to open the necessary appropriations, allocate these appropriations and determine the sources of coverage.

Third:

The rents of premises leased by foreign States, international organisations and institutions affiliated therewith, as well as companies of foreign nationality, shall be increased by three times their amount, after calculating the increase provided for in this amending Law.

The fair rent shall be determined at a rate ranging between five and seven per cent of the value of the leased premises. The value of the leased premises shall be assessed by the share pertaining to it of the total cost of the building and of the price of the land. The total cost of the building shall be assessed as at the date of the lawsuit after deducting what may have depreciated from its value due to age. The share pertaining to the leased premises of the price of the land shall be assessed as at the date of filing the lawsuit in accordance with one of the following two cases:

1) If the building has exhausted the entire general exploitation factor permitted in the real property on which it stands, the price of the land shall be distributed over the number of legal storeys of the building.

2) If the building has not exhausted the entire general exploitation referred to above, the area of land necessary for it shall be calculated on the basis of this exploitation factor, and the value of this area shall be assessed and distributed over the number of storeys. In the two aforementioned cases, due regard shall be given to the importance of each of the storeys in view of the other storeys and its condition and special circumstances, without this assessment being affected by improvements of all kinds which the lessee may have carried out at his own expense.

A- The lessee may, after the expiry of the term of the original contract and notwithstanding any agreement to the contrary, pay the rent monthly and in advance if the monthly rent exceeds half the minimum wage as at the due date of this rent.

B - The lessee shall not be adjudged to have forfeited the right of extension:

1- If he sends the rents to the lessor by means of a postal money order in a registered letter with acknowledgement of receipt within the legal time limit to the place of residence of the lessor.

2- If he deposits the rents within the legal time limit with the notary public who operates in the district within the jurisdiction of which the leased premises are located, and the notary public shall notify the lessor of the content of the deposit and invite him to collect them.

Each of the owner and the lessee may execute the judgment ordering recovery, and if the owner fails to pay the amount of compensation due from him at the Execution Department, after being served notice, he shall not be bound to pay an additional compensation of two per cent per month of the value of the compensation, not subject to modification, which shall be calculated, executed and collected directly through the Execution Department.

Services and Maintenance:

1- The expenses of common services mentioned in this Law shall mean the following:

A) Expenses of consumption or generation of electric current pertaining to the janitor's quarters, the lift and the rest of the common parts in a subdivided building and what is deemed as such in an unsubdivided building.

B) Expenses of providing cold water, including that extracted from artesian wells, hot water, heating and cooling, and expenses of maintenance and repairs relating to their apparatus and installations and to the lift, and expenses of insuring it with an insurance company.

C) The doorkeeper's wage equivalent to the minimum wage, in addition to increases including increments, allowances, legal compensations, contributions due to the National Social Security Fund and end-of-service indemnity. The housing allowance shall not be included in the calculation of the wage.

2 - The lessor shall not have the right to refrain from providing the common services which he has customarily provided or which were originally agreed upon in the lease contract. If these services include heating, cooling or hot water, the lessor must provide sufficient heating on a regular basis

from 15 November until 21 March of the following year, and cooling from the first of June until 15 October of the same year; as for hot water, he must provide it throughout the days of the year, all of this unless there is an agreement to the contrary in the contract.

If the owner fails to perform, without lawful justification, all or some all or some of the services agreed upon or required pursuant to this Article, the lessee shall be entitled, after verification thereof by an expert appointed by the Urgent Matters Judge without levying any fee, to a compensation equal to two months' rent, provided that the total compensation awarded in a single lease year does not exceed six months' rent.

3 - If the lease contract does not contain a provision placing the entire common expenses upon the lessee, the owner shall contribute at a rate of 20% of these expenses, provided that his contribution does not exceed 5% of the total rents of the premises that benefit from these services, and the remainder shall be distributed among the units of which the building is composed, whether vacant or occupied by the owner or others.

4 - The lessor must draw up every three months a detailed account of the expenses and a distribution thereof between himself and the lessees showing the share of contribution of each of them in accordance with the rule above and notify them thereof, and each of them shall have the right to inspect the laws proving these expenses and request copies thereof at his own expense when necessary in order to object to their validity if he so wishes.

The area of each leased premises shall be taken into consideration when distributing the shares of contribution among the occupants.

5 - The lessor may request from the lessees an advance on account equivalent to the proportion of what is due from them of the value of the probable service expenses for three months, and in this case the lessees shall have the right to appoint one of their number to supervise the process of spending this advance.

6 - The delay of the lessee in paying his due share in the contribution shall be deemed as a delay in paying the rents and shall produce the same effects provided for in item (A) of Article Ten of this Law.

7 - Contrary to any prior provision contained in the contract, the lessee shall bear all the non-common repairs specific to the leased premises.

8 - Any written agreement concluded between the occupants of three-quarters of the units intended for lease or for occupation by the owner regarding the exemption of the owner from performing all or some of the common services shall be binding upon the owner and upon all the lessees.

The Single Civil Judge shall have jurisdiction to hear and determine all lease actions and all claims and defences connected therewith, whatever the amount of the annual rent may be.

The first hearing in lease actions shall be scheduled without being bound by the time limits for exchanging pleadings, and the judgment of first instance rendered in actions for the lease of built real property subject to this Law shall not be open to any ordinary or extraordinary means of recourse other than opposition within the limits of Article 468 of the Code of Civil Procedure and appeal within a time limit of fifteen days from the date of service thereof, and the appellate judgment shall not be open to any ordinary or extraordinary means of recourse other than opposition within the limits of Article 657 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

However, the appellate judgment shall be open to cassation if there is a contradiction between it and the judgment of first instance in respect of forfeiture of the right of extension only.

This shall apply to appellate judgments rendered as from 1/1/1987, whatever the law relied upon in such judgments.

The summary jurisdiction, within the scope of the provisions of general law, shall remain competent to hear urgent and summary matters the determination of which does not address the merits of the dispute.

The provisions of Article 847 et seq. of the Code of Civil Procedure relating to the enforcement of written instruments and undertakings shall apply to the recovery of rents specified in lease contracts executed between the two parties and extended by operation of law.

The tenancy of lessees who benefited from the provisions of Article Thirty-Five of Law No. 20/82, as amended, and who have not yet returned to the leased premises shall continue, provided that they continue to pay one quarter of the rents due after the application of the provisions of this Law and that they return to the leased premises within a time limit of one year from the date of entry into force of this Law, unless force majeure prevents that.

A Lebanese lessee in undamaged buildings who was deprived of occupying the leased premises by reason of the events occurring as from 9/9/1982 and has not yet returned thereto must return to the leased premises within one year from the date on which this Law comes into operation, and must notify the owner of his wish for the lease contract to continue within a time limit of six months from the date of entry into force of this Law, and in such case he must pay one quarter of the rents in arrears in accordance with the provisions of this Law for the period between the date on which he left the leased premises and the date of his return thereto. Notification to the owner of the lessee's wish to benefit from the continuation of the contract may be effected by all written means of notification, including publication, registered letter, and tender of the rents due. If the said lessee elects to return to the leased premises and is unable to do so for security reasons or by reason of its occupation by a third party without the consent of the owner, the lessee must pay one quarter of the rent in accordance with the provisions of this Law. However, if he is unable to return to the leased premises by reason of its occupation by a third party with the consent of the owner, no rent shall be due from the lessee, and thereupon, if the new lessee's knowledge of the continuation of the prior tenancy is established, the lessee who notified the owner of the continuation of his tenancy may elect either to return to the leased premises or to claim from the owner and the new lessee jointly and severally compensation ranging between (25%) twenty-five per cent and (50%) fifty per cent of the value of the leased premises, if the leased premises are designated for residential use.

If the new lessee's knowledge of the continuation of the prior tenancy is not established, the lessee's right shall be limited to claiming from the owner the compensation mentioned in the preceding paragraph if the leased premises are designated for residential use. If the leased premises are designated for non-residential use, there shall be added to the said compensation an amount equivalent to the loss suffered by the lessee as a result of the act of the owner and the new lessee where the latter's knowledge of the continuation of the prior tenancy is established, and as a result of the act of the owner where such knowledge is not established.

Neither the increase nor the fair rent provided for in this Law shall apply to premises of whose enjoyment their lessees were deprived for security reasons as a result of the events occurring after 13/4/1975 throughout the duration of the deprivation; however, such increase and fair rent shall resume application without retroactive effect after the cessation of the security reasons.

Notwithstanding the legal provisions governing lease contracts, contracts subject to the provisions of this Law and pertaining to buildings damaged by reason of the events occurring as from 9/9/1982 and up to the date on which this amending Law comes into operation shall remain in force with all their effects between lessors and lessees despite the destruction or deterioration of the leased premises or the deprivation of the lessees of the enjoyment of the whole or part thereof, and the provisions of Title One of Legislative Decree No. 7/77 shall apply to these damaged buildings, and the time limits specified in Articles Nine, Ten and Fourteen of the said Legislative Decree shall commence in respect thereof from the date on which this amending Law comes into operation, and in the case of application of paragraph 1 of Article Thirteen of Legislative Decree No. 7/77, the provisions of the fair rent contained in this amending Law shall apply in respect of the fair rent.

Articles Eight and Fifteen of this Law shall also apply in the case of application of item Second of the said Article Thirteen.

In the case of application of Article Four of Legislative Decree No. 7/77, the increases provided for in this amending Law shall be calculated and the sum of five thousand Lebanese pounds shall be replaced by the sum of two million Lebanese pounds. In the case of application of Article Six of Legislative Decree No. 7/77, the rent shall be adopted after calculation of the statutory increase contained in this amending Law.

In all cases of recovery of possession or forfeiture of extension, the court may take into consideration the necessary expenses which the lessee may have incurred to carry out repair works in the recovered leased premises as well as the period that has elapsed since the repair works.
Lease contracts with depreciated rents, concluded or extended prior to the entry into force of this Law, shall be subject to the fair rent provisions provided for in Article Seventeen thereof.

Contracts in which the rent is fixed on a graduated basis shall be performed in accordance with their contents, and the last rent shall be adopted as the contractual rent upon the extension of the lease in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

Subject to the third paragraph of Article Twenty-One of this Law, the provisions of Lease Law No. 20/82 and its amendments, with the exception of Article 12 thereof, are extended until the date of its entry into force, and disputes pending before the courts prior to 23/7/1992 shall remain subject to the exceptional lease laws under which they arose, except for the compensation for recovery of possession, which shall become subject to the assessment of the judge within the limits of item Second of Article Eight of this Law.

The effect of formal notices leading to forfeiture of the right of extension for non-payment of rent served by ordinary or exceptional ways after 15/4/1975 and the date of operation of this Law shall be suspended for a period of two months only running from the entry into force of this Law. A tenant who benefits from this suspension shall, within the two-month time limit provided for in the preceding paragraph, pay in addition to the rent an increase in the amount of 25% of the amount of this rent as it stands at the date of entry into force of this Law, and this increase shall be added to the said rent and become part thereof, and in this case the formal notice shall be deemed null and of no effect, as well as the action for forfeiture of the right of extension that was brought on the basis thereof. If the tenant does not pay spontaneously the arrears of rent and the increase mentioned above within the two-month time limit provided for in this Article, the two parties shall return to the state in which they were prior to the entry into force of this Law, and the time limit of the formal notice shall resume running without the need to address a new formal notice, and the action shall resume its course from the point which it had reached. This Article shall not apply and the tenant shall not benefit from its provisions if a final and conclusive judgment ruling the forfeiture of the right of extension has been rendered.

The time limits specified in the first and fourth paragraphs of this Article shall be extended by a time limit of two months starting from the date of entry into force of this Amending Law.

Notwithstanding any other text, lease contracts relating to premises containing violations of the building or town planning laws shall not be deemed void unless these violations are not capable of settlement pursuant to the laws in force, provided that eviction shall not be executed except concurrently with the removal of the violation.

The increases provided for in the sixth and thirteenth Articles of this Amending Law shall not apply to rents fixed in foreign currency in lease contracts and which are still drawn up in this currency.

The occupied posts in the temporary establishment in the Ministry of Tourism created pursuant to Decree No. 12510 dated 10/04/1963, and amended pursuant to Decree No. 13394 dated 19/07/1963, shall be converted into a permanent establishment.

The temporary employees shall be transferred to the permanent establishment without modification in rank and salary, and they shall retain their right to seniority qualifying for advancement, and their temporary services shall be joined to their subsequent services in the permanent establishment in accordance with the provisions of Article Nine of Law No. 717 dated 05/11/1998.

In order to benefit from the provisions of Article Two of this Law, it shall be required that the temporary employees pass a competitive examination the subject of which relates to the tasks entrusted to them by virtue of their posts.

The temporary employees who do not pass the competitive examination referred to in Article Three of this Law shall constitute from liquidation which terminates upon the termination of their service without the need to issue any text.
All legal and regulatory provisions contrary to the provisions of this Law are repealed.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

With effect from the first of March of the year 1935, the purchase, manufacture, and sale of tobacco, whatever its origin and whatever the form in which it is offered, shall be subject to a single fiscal monopoly in the States under the French Mandate; however, the exportation of leaf tobacco outside these States shall remain free. As for the exploitation of the monopoly, it shall be undertaken by a concessionary administration (Régie) of joint interest in accordance with the provisions of the book of specifications attached to this Decision.
Tombac and other substances capable of replacing tobacco and tombac in the uses to which they are put shall be assimilated to tobacco in the application of the provisions of this Decision.

The heads of the financial departments in each State, government, and territory enjoying financial autonomy shall constitute a commission presided over by the Advisor of the High Commissariat for Financial Affairs, which shall be called "the Permanent Commission for Tobacco and Tombac", while the meetings of this Commission shall be attended by the financial advisors in the States.

A commissioner representing the States, appointed pursuant to a decision of the High Commissioner and subject to the authority of the Advisor of the High Commissariat for Financial Affairs, shall supervise the operations of the Administration (the Régie).

In the event of any dispute arising between the Monopoly Administration and the administrative authority in one or more States, the dispute shall ultimately be referred to the High Commissioner of the French Republic, who shall decide thereon finally and conclusively after taking the opinion of the Permanent Commission.

These provisions shall also apply to every dispute arising between the Permanent Commission and the Monopoly Administration, or to every dispute arising over the manner of interpreting the legal texts or the texts of the agreements relating to the tobacco regime.

(Amended by Decision 100 dated 8 August of the year 1938):

The cultivation of tobacco is permissible in the areas in which planting is beneficial, subject to compliance with the conditions set forth in this Decision.

Planting shall be either for the purpose of delivering the crop to the Monopoly Administration or for the purpose of exporting it. Prior to 14 June of each year, the Monopoly Administration shall send to the Permanent Commission its proposals regarding the extent of the areas that may be planted in the following year, of each category of tobacco or tombac of each variety.

Prior to 25 June, the Permanent Commission shall distribute among the States, governments, and the territory enjoying financial autonomy the areas that may be planted for the purpose of sale to the Monopoly Administration, provided that such areas do not exceed the extent finally decided upon.

This Commission shall also determine the areas that may be planted in each State, government, or territory for the purpose of exportation.

(Amended by Decision 100 dated 8 August of the year 1938):

Prior to 25 July, the Head of State, the Governor, or the highest administrative authority in the territory enjoying financial autonomy shall issue a decree or decision in which he distributes, upon the proposal of the Head of the Finance Department and the Head of the Agriculture Department, the planting areas referred to in the preceding Article among the villages suitable for planting, provided that a distinction is made between the areas allocated for the Monopoly and the areas allocated for exportation. Where necessary, there shall be set forth in this decree or this decision all the measures deemed appropriate to be applied in each area or village.

In addition to the determined areas, it shall be permissible to plant certain lands for the purpose of experimentation, but within the limits laid down by the Permanent Commission in agreement with the Monopoly Administration, the Head of the Finance Department, and the Head of the Agriculture Department in the competent State or government.

It shall thereafter be permissible, subject to compliance with the provisions of the first paragraph, to issue a decree or decision authorising planting in the areas in which the experiments have succeeded.
No person whomsoever may cultivate tobacco unless he submits a declaration to that effect and obtains the licence provided for in the tenth Article.

Amended by Decision 100 dated 8 August of the year 1938):

Persons wishing to engage in the cultivation of tobacco must submit a declaration to that effect, between 25 July and 20 August at the latest, to the Mukhtar of the village in which the land allocated for planting is situated, and this statement must be submitted in the presence of one of the officers of the Monopoly.

The Monopoly Administration must notify the Mukhtar of the passage of this officer through his village at least three days in advance.

As for the cultivators who were unable to submit their declarations as set forth above, they shall have the right to submit them between 20 and 25 August at the latest to the Qaimaqam at the administrative centre of the Qada.

After the legal stamps are affixed to these declarations, they shall be registered in a special register obtained from the Monopoly Administration; then each cultivator shall affix his signature in the register and shall be given a receipt in exchange for his declaration.

There must be stated in the declaration the location of the land prepared for the planting of tobacco, its area, the type of tobacco to be planted therein, the area intended to be planted for the purpose of sale to the Monopoly, and the area intended to be planted for the purpose of exportation.

The Mukhtar, after these declarations have been collected with him, must deliver to the Monopoly officer, prior to his departure from the village, the special register referred to above, which must be delivered to the Qaimaqam on 25 August.

As for the Qaimaqam, he shall undertake the transmission of all the registers of declarations in accordance with the instructions he receives from the central administration.

(Amended by Decision 100 dated 8 August of the year 1938):

If the areas declared in one of the villages are less than the quota allocated to that village, the surplus may be distributed among other villages pursuant to a decree or decision taken prior to 10 September in the same manner in which the decree or decision referred to in the sixth Article is taken.

If the areas declared in one of the villages exceed the quota allocated to that village, that quota shall be distributed among the holders of declarations pursuant to a decree or decision taken upon the proposal of the Head of the Finance Department and the Head of the Agriculture Department.

(Completed by Article 1 of Decision 106 dated 16 July of the year 1937 and amended by Decision 100 dated 8 August of the year 1938):

The Head of the Finance Division shall draw up for each village, prior to the date of 15 October, a list containing the names of the cultivators and the area of the lands they are licensed to plant, whether for the Monopoly Administration or for exportation.

Planting licences shall not be granted to cultivators who deliver two consecutive crops at prices that are at least 25 per cent below the average purchase prices of tobacco of the same types.

This list shall be notified to the interested parties through the offices of the Mukhtar.

A copy thereof, certified as a true copy of the original, shall be sent to the Monopoly Administration on the date of 23 October.

As regards the Governorate of Latakia, the date of publication of the nominal lists of planting licences shall be 25 October, and the date of their notification to the Monopoly Administration shall be 2 November.

In the event of the death of the cultivator, the Mukhtar must notify the Finance Administration thereof within a period of eight days. The Finance Administration shall thereupon proceed to refer the matter to the Monopoly Administration within a period of eight days as well.

If none of the heirs requests in writing from the Mukhtar that he be permitted to continue planting the tobacco under his own responsibility, the heirs or the Monopoly Administration shall be obliged to uproot the seedlings at the expense of those heirs.

Every cultivator who desists from planting must give notice of the matter; the Mukhtar shall notify the Monopoly Administration within a period of eight days, and the Finance Administration shall undertake to notify the Monopoly Administration within a period of eight days as well; the Monopoly Administration shall then delegate an officer who shall first verify that nothing has been picked clandestinely and then supervise the destruction of the seedlings or undertake their destruction himself at the expense of the cultivator in the event of his refusal to do so.

The Monopoly Administration may send to the Mukhtar a list containing the descriptions of each type of tobacco so that he may rely thereon when drawing up the declarations, and it shall also have the right to determine, after its agreement with the Permanent Commission, the methods of cultivation and curing that must be applied to the tobacco which it has undertaken to purchase.

When the crop intended for sale to the Monopoly is delivered to the warehouse at the latest - within a period of five days, the head of the warehouse shall inspect the tobacco in the presence of its producer, verifying its grades, and then these grades and the corresponding prices shall be entered on an inspection sheet given to the owner of the goods.

The officers who receive the crops may make a deduction from their weight if it appears to them that their grade is below the lowest grade, or if their moisture is abnormal.

(Amended by Decision 98 issued on 29 June 1937):

If the grower does not accept the result of the inspection or the decided deduction, the matter shall be finally decided by a committee composed of a delegate of the Finance Administration, a delegate of the party concerned and one of the officers of the Monopoly. The committee shall meet upon the invitation of the Monopoly and at the request of the grower. This request must be submitted before the expiry of a period of six months from the date of carrying out the inspection and must state the price at which the grower requests that the value of his crop be paid and the name of his delegate on the committee. The expenses of the committee shall be borne by the losing party.

If the grower does not submit his request before the expiry of the period provided for above or if his delegate does not answer the invitation of the Monopoly, he shall be deemed in default and shall no longer be entitled to object to the result of the inspection provided for in the preceding Article.

As for tobacco the grades of which are finally found to be very poor, rendering it unfit for use, it shall be rejected and burned under the supervision of the Monopoly Administration.

As for foreign matter that may be found mixed with the tobacco, it shall be deducted therefrom and burned. And the provisions of Article 21 shall apply to the deficit that may result therefrom after comparing the result with the crop declaration.

The Monopoly Administration must pay the grower within fifteen days starting from the receipt at the warehouse or, where applicable, starting from the decision of the committee provided for in Article 27 of Decision No. 16-L.R. issued on 30 January 1935 or from the expiry of the period of six months provided for in the same Article.

The Monopoly Administration shall have the privilege to deduct in advance from the value of the sums due to the grower every sum due to it by way of reimbursement of actual expenses placed at the charge of the grower pursuant to the regulations provided for in Article 4, paragraph 3, of the book of specifications annexed to Decision No. 16 L.R. issued on 30 January 1935.

This privilege is special and ranks immediately before the special privilege belonging to the Treasury.

As regards the recovery of other debts of the Monopoly Administration, the said Administration shall also benefit from a privilege which shall be special where the matter relates to fines imposed on the grower for his contravention of Title II of Decision No. 16 L.R. issued on 30 January 1935 and which shall be exercised over the price of the tobacco produced by the grower, and which shall be general in all other cases.

The special or general privilege of the Monopoly referred to in the preceding subparagraph ranks immediately after the privilege of the Treasury of the same kind.

The price at which the Monopoly must purchase each grade or variety of the varieties of tobacco to be produced by the crop of the coming season shall be fixed by the Permanent Committee before 31 December upon the proposal of the Monopoly Administration.

As for the tariff drawn up by this Committee, it shall be approved by the High Commissioner by way of a decision.

Tobacco delivered to the Monopoly Administration for the purpose of export must be placed in sacks on which shall be clearly stated the mark of the grower, his name, the year of the crop, the serial number, the gross weight, the tare weight, and the gross weight. The arrangement and weight of these packages may not be altered.

There shall be a deduction in weight to be fixed by the special storage regulations against the loss which occurs in stored tobacco (shrinkage).

(Amended by Article 2 of Decision 74 dated 13 April 1945):

Crops stored for the purpose of export may be transferred in whole or in part to the name of a recognised exporting merchant, provided that the grower substantiates to the warehouse a declaration of sale approved by the exporting merchant, and settles all sums due on the goods to the Monopoly Administration.

In the event of a partial transfer of the crop, the quantities transferred shall be stated on the back of the warehouse receipt and on the corresponding counterfoil, which must be signed by the owner of the goods, and in the event of a transfer of the crop in its entirety, the Monopoly Administration shall retain the receipt.

If a portion of the tobacco intended for fumigation is designated, the Monopoly Administration may reserve its right to compel the exporting merchant to pay the sums that may be claimed for it pursuant to the crop storage regulations in respect of the tobacco that has not been moved to the places of fumigation before the expiry of the period provided for in the new Article 40 of this Decision.

In this case, the exporting merchant and the grower shall be jointly and severally liable towards the Monopoly Administration for the payment of all the sums referred to in the preceding paragraph when they fall due.

The Monopoly Administration may at any time whatsoever and in any case whatsoever, before the sale of the goods to the exporting merchant, examine the contents of the bales referred to in the preceding Article in the presence of a sworn officer delegated by the Finance Administration, and the head of the warehouse shall then draw up a record of the examination which he shall send to the Mukhtar for transmission to the owner of the goods.

The owner of the goods shall be entitled to object to the head of the warehouse against the valuation before the expiry of five days from the date on which the record is served upon him and to demand a new valuation to be carried out in accordance with the conditions provided for in Article 27. The provisions of the last paragraph of the said Article shall apply to foreign matter found in the examined bales.

Bales intended for export may be kept in the warehouses of the Monopoly for a period of five years at the latest, and storage shall be free of charge during the first six months beginning from the day the goods enter the warehouse, and the owners of the goods must pay in advance thereafter for every six months a storage fee fixed by the special storage regulations drawn up by the Monopoly Administration and approved by the Permanent Committee. At the end of the fifth year, the Monopoly Administration shall be entitled to sell of its own accord by public auction - in accordance with the provisions of the said regulations - the tobacco left in the warehouse. If the owner of the goods does not attend the auction, the local authorities shall delegate, at the request of the Monopoly, a representative who shall ensure the legality of the auction and sign a record discharging the Monopoly Administration finally towards the owner of the goods. As for the warehouse receipt held by the latter, it shall become valueless thereafter.

The net proceeds of the sale shall be paid. After deduction of all expenses, advances, fines, storage fees and experts' expenses, to the owner of the goods or to his heirs, and if no one comes forward to purchase a quantity of tobacco put up for sale by public auction, such quantity shall be burned after the expiry of a final period of six months.

The Monopoly Administration shall be liable for all damage befalling the tobacco by reason of the poor condition of the premises in which the goods are stored, but it shall not bear the slightest liability for any loss or damage befalling the tobacco by reason of the poor condition in which it was when stored, or befalling it by reason of force majeure, and the owner of the goods shall be obliged to insure, through the intermediary of the Monopoly, the tobacco which he delivers to it against all risks accepted by the insurance policy (sikurtah).

Those who are deemed exporting merchants are the persons who submit to that effect to the Finance Administration a written declaration written on a printed form given to them by the said Administration at their request.

The Finance Administration shall notify the declarants whether they have been accepted or rejected without being obliged to state the reasons for its rejection, and shall then inform the Monopoly Administration of the matter, and if one of the merchants commits two contraventions of the provisions of the Tobacco Regulations, his name shall be struck off the list of recognised exporters.

A seller who wishes to cease operating his shop shall notify the warehouse to which he is affiliated thereof in writing at least 15 days in advance, and regardless of the time at which he ceases selling, he shall not be entitled to claim any part whatsoever of the licence fee, and he shall return the tobacco in his possession, provided that it is in good condition, whereupon the Administration shall refund to him the legal value of such tobacco after deducting therefrom the amount of the discount.

Resident or itinerant sellers must submit to the investigations which the officers of the Monopoly request to conduct, failing which their licence shall be deemed cancelled, and if any shop remains closed for 48 consecutive hours without an acceptable excuse, the Monopoly Administration shall be entitled to deem its licence cancelled as well.

Contraventions committed against Articles 41 and 53 (including this latter Article) with respect to manufactured products to which the marks and stamps of the Monopoly are affixed shall pertain to the officers of the Monopoly to the exclusion of all others.

Leaf tobacco, or tobacco which is still in the course of preparation, or manufactured tobacco, may not be introduced into the States under the French Mandate unless it is imported on behalf of the Monopoly Administration, and the Monopoly Administration shall purchase from local producers what it requires of leaf tobacco in the proportion of 95 per cent of its requirements for domestic consumption. If the local crop is insufficient, it may import from abroad the quantities which it requires; as for the quantities of foreign tumbak which may be imported, they shall be fixed by the Permanent Commission each year upon the proposal of the Monopoly Administration.

The Monopoly Administration may permit individuals to import, by way of exception, certain manufactured products, provided, however, that the quantities which they import do not exceed twenty kilos per person per year, and that they pay a special duty to be added to the customs duties. As for the rate of this duty which the Monopoly Administration collects, it shall be fixed by the Permanent Commission. Ordinary customs duties shall be paid to the customs collectors, but the latter may not deliver the imported quantities of tobacco to their owners until after the banderoles or stamps given by the Monopoly Administration, the affixing of which proves that the special duty referred to above has been collected, have been affixed thereto.

Tobacco in leaf may not be transported within the territories under the French Mandate except under the conditions set forth below:

Every quantity of tobacco must be transported by its owner under the supervision of the Monopoly, and in this case the goods shall be transported to their destination by means of a transport permit issued by the Monopoly Administration. As for transport in other than these two cases, it shall not be permissible except after obtaining a special permit from the Monopoly Administration and under the circumstances which this Administration shall determine.

(Completed by Article 3 of Decision 74 dated 13 April 1935):

The transport permit referred to in Article 57 shall be written on a printed form issued by the head of the warehouse from which the goods are transported, and after the transport is completed, the transport permits shall be returned within the prescribed period to the head of the warehouse who drew them up, bearing an endorsement placed thereon by the Monopoly establishment to which the goods were sent or by the Customs - as the case may be - proving the entry of the tobacco into that establishment or into the customs warehouse. In the event of exportation of the goods, the account of the exporting merchant shall be finally settled upon his production - within a period of three months - of a copy of the customs bond, discharged by the Customs Service, in which a certificate proving the arrival of the tobacco in the country to which it was exported has been specially drawn up.

And a certificate proving - where applicable - the payment of customs duties upon its arrival at the customs warehouse or its admission therein. The Consulate of France must visa these certificates and legalise their signatures if the Monopoly Administration so requests at the time of the transport of the tobacco.

If the tobacco is consigned to a governmental monopoly, the merchant may suffice with producing a certificate from that administration proving the arrival of the tobacco and stating the number of bales received, their types and their weight.

The Monopoly Administration may withhold the issuance of the transport permit referred to in Article 57 until after the payment of all sums claimed on its behalf in respect of the goods on any ground whatsoever.

There shall be deemed contraband:

First: All quantities of tobacco transported or exported for which the relevant documents have not been returned to their positive authority of origin duly certified within the prescribed period.

Second: Any difference between the quantities transported or exported and the quantities for which the relevant documents have been produced within the prescribed period.

The Monopoly Administration may discharge the owners of the goods from liability for quantities of leaf tobacco stored in its warehouses or stores or transported pursuant to a transport permit, if they are destroyed by act of God or by force majeure.

(Amended by Article 4 of Decision 74 dated 13 April 1935):

No person whomsoever may possess leaf tobacco unless he is one of the licensed cultivators or unless he submits a declaration that he engages in the curing of tobacco, provided that the presence of the tobacco on his premises is not established after the latest date fixed for the delivery of the entire crop or for the delivery of the cured tobacco to the Monopoly Administration. It is also required, if the matter relates to one of the curers, that the possession of leaf tobacco not be prohibited pursuant to the new Article 40 of this Decision.

(Completed by Article 2 of Decision 97 dated 29 June 1937):

No person whomsoever may possess tobacco which is still in the course of preparation or manufactured tobacco other than the tobacco which the Monopoly Administration manufactures and to which it affixes its stamps.

No one may possess tobacco in the process of manufacture or manufactured tobacco other than the tobacco of the Monopoly Administration or other than the tobacco to which its marks are affixed. No one may possess zone tobacco in places in which the sale thereof has not been licensed.

Every person in whose possession are found apparatus, machines or mechanical equipment suitable for the manufacture of tobacco shall be deemed to be an unlawful manufacturer and shall be punished in that capacity. As for the importation of the said machines into the territories under the French Mandate, it is prohibited.

Cultivators, exporting merchants or sellers may not place any obstacle whatsoever in the way of the officers of the Monopoly when they are carrying out the verifications required of them. Both the former and the latter must always be in complete readiness to comply with the requests of the Monopoly either in person or through

their agents, in the event of their absence. They must also facilitate for the said officers the means of performing their duties, and place at their disposal the labour which they may require. No opposition may be made to them therein if they wish to take certain samples from their crop.

All schedules, lists and accounting documents provided for in this Decision must be preserved for a period of at least five years by the persons who are required to hold them. A seal may be substituted therein for a signature.

The Monopoly Administration shall be entitled to require the certification of the Mukhtar as to the identity of the person, his seal or his signature. As for the certifications which the Mukhtar issues in accordance with the provisions of this Decision, they shall be exempt from all fees.

Those who are entitled to search for contraventions relating to tobacco, establish them and carry out seizures when necessary are - save in the circumstances provided for in Article 24 - either the officers of the Monopoly assigned thereto and specially sworn for this purpose, or the officers of the judicial police, all sworn officers in the States, and all officers, non-commissioned officers and men of the gendarmerie, and officers and men of the police and customs; and whatever the case may be, it shall not be permissible for the officers of the Monopoly to conduct searches alone.

(Amended by Article 5 of Decision 74 dated 13 April 1935):

Except in relation to growers, smokers, and vendors on whose premises the Monopoly Administration is entitled to conduct its searches permanently, searches may not be conducted in private dwellings, shops, and warehouses except with the assistance of the local authority in accordance with the laws in force.

Searches shall be carried out by one of the officers mentioned in the preceding Article 66, with the exception of the officers of the Monopoly Administration, who may not carry out searches alone. Rather, they must request the assistance of one of the other officers referred to above. Such officer may not refuse to assist them in any case whatsoever.

The provisions of the first paragraph of this Article shall not apply to searches conducted in premises - of whatever kind or whoever their occupant may be - into which smuggled products enter in plain sight of the suppression officers while they are pursuing them closely.

All enforcement officers shall be entitled to subject to search all parcels, bags, and other portable articles.

However, State officers and officers of the Monopoly Administration must, during such searches, observe the duties of propriety towards individuals and avoid violence from which no benefit is to be expected.

If the enforcement officers wish to search certain products intended for sale in markets, such as eggs, hides, fruits, and other products the nature of which permits them to be searched by touch or by probing and which are placed in baskets, sacks, or wrappings that cannot be emptied without causing damage to the goods, those officers may not request to search such products except at the market to which they are consigned, provided that they take along the way all necessary measures for their preservation.

The Governments must assist in surveillance and the suppression of smuggling by all the means at their disposal, and in particular through all members of the public force. Gendarmes, police officers, and customs guards in particular must assist the officers charged with surveillance, the recording of offences, and seizure. They may not refuse to comply with their requests.

The local authorities, and in particular the Mukhtar, the members of the Council of Elders, the Mudir, the Qaimaqam, and the Muhafiz, must assist all the committees formed pursuant to this Decision, and all officers of the public force or of the Monopoly Administration charged with combating smuggling, in carrying out their mission.

These authorities must in particular perform all the duties incumbent upon them in accordance with this Decision, failing which they shall expose themselves to the disciplinary penalties which the Governments must take against negligent or defaulting officials.

The same authorities must take all necessary measures so that proceedings follow their legal course and without being obstructed by acts of violence and intimidation.

Public services, and in particular the Postal Service, concessionary companies, and transport companies, must facilitate for the enforcement officers the means of performing their duties, and inform them of incidents of smuggling of which they may become aware.

Reports recording offences and seizures shall be sent immediately to the Monopoly Administration and shall be relied upon until the contrary is proved.

It is the Monopoly Administration that holds the right to institute judicial prosecutions. The courts competent to hear tobacco cases shall be the courts competent to hear foreign cases.

Every contravention of the provisions of this Decision, all acts of smuggling, and, more generally, all acts and deeds prejudicial to the interests of the Monopoly, shall be deemed misdemeanours and shall be referred as such to the criminal courts.

To these misdemeanours shall apply the rules applicable to ordinary misdemeanours, whether in respect of the rules of procedure or the rules of trial and execution, it being understood that every person caught in flagrante delicto while possessing, transporting, or manufacturing tobacco must be conducted by the drawers of the report to the nearest gendarmerie or police post, and, after being briefly interrogated, shall be referred within 24 hours to the Justice of the Peace". If the offender has no fixed place of residence and is liable to a penalty of imprisonment, the Justice of the Peace shall issue a warrant of arrest against him. However, he may be provisionally released after furnishing cash bail or after producing a personal surety accepted by the competent judicial authority, provided that the one or the other security guarantees the payment in full of the fines due from the offender or other pecuniary awards issued by the administration of the court. The amount of such fines or pecuniary awards shall be assessed by the Monopoly Administration.

Smuggling actions must be heard without delay and given priority over other cases. It is the Court of First Instance that renders final judgments in respect of fines not exceeding 250 Lebanese-Syrian pounds, and in all cases orders the provisional execution of the judgment. However, the convicted person may request a stay of execution pending a ruling by the competent authority as to whether he is not entitled to file an opposition against the judgment, provided that in such cases he furnishes a solvent surety accepted by the court.

In the event of a seizure being levied upon beasts of burden, the court may - upon the request of the Monopoly Administration and after summoning both parties - render a special judgment ordering the sale of those beasts by public auction for their preservation. Their former owner shall have a right of preference over other bidders at the auction in the event that the prices offered are equal.

However, the court must deliver the seized beasts to their former owner if he furnishes, jointly and severally with a third party whose solvency the court determines, a security the amount of which the court itself shall fix. This provisional measure must be observed until the fate of the seized beasts is finally decided.

Persons who participate in committing the contraventions referred to in this Decision shall be liable to the same penalties to which the principal perpetrators thereof are exposed.

Furthermore, the father or - in his absence - the person who has custody of the child shall be civilly liable in all cases for the consequences of all acts that may be committed by the minor child residing with him in violation of the provisions of this Decision.

Masters or principals may be convicted as having participated in the contravention. They must also in all cases be held civilly liable for the contraventions that may be committed by their employees or workmen in the course of performing the duties required of them.

The fines provided for in this Decision shall always have the character of personal damages and shall accrue to the Monopoly Administration.

The fine shall be imposed a number of times equal to the number of distinct contraventions established either in a single report or in several reports.

Every person extraneous to the Monopoly Administration who informs it directly or informs the local authorities of a matter warranting the seizure of a quantity of tobacco or of smuggled articles, or who arrests smugglers, or participates in arresting them, shall be entitled to receive a reward which may not exceed either one-third of the fine or, in the event of failure to recover the fine, one-half of the value of the seized articles, provided that the Monopoly Administration shall undertake the valuation of those articles.

If several persons cooperate in giving this "information" or in arresting the smugglers, the reward shall be divided among them in equal shares, and there shall be another third determined by the Monopoly Administration in the same manner which it shall undertake to distribute among the officers who carry out the seizure.

The Monopoly Administration shall be entitled to enter into a settlement in respect of reports relating to contraventions committed against this Law. In such a case, the offender must pay all judicial costs and the costs of preserving the seized articles.

However, no settlement may be entered into in respect of a penalty of imprisonment imposed by the court.

The court shall be entitled, if it finds that there are mitigating circumstances, to reduce the prescribed fine by half.

The fines shall be doubled in the event of repetition of the contravention or when the contravention and the misdemeanour are committed with the use of violence or the use of forged documents, irrespective of the penalties prescribed by the Penal Code.
Where the offender or smuggler fails to pay the fine imposed upon him, he shall be compelled to pay it by imprisonment for a period determined in accordance with the penal rules in force.

The provisions of (amended) Articles 113 to 115 (inclusive of the last Article) of the Penal Code shall apply to every person who obstructs, insults, strikes, or commits any similar act against the officers of the Monopoly while they are performing the duties of their functions.

The Monopoly Administration shall purchase the quantities of leaf tobacco in the possession of growers within a period that may not exceed three months starting from the date specified in the first Article of this Resolution.

As for the prices at which these quantities must be purchased, they shall be determined by the Permanent Committee upon the proposal of the Monopoly Administration, which in determining them shall rely on the prices at which purchases from the 1934 season were made in each region. As for the 1935 season, the provisions of Articles 5 to 16 (inclusive of this last Article) shall not apply to it. The cultivation of tobacco in the year 1935 shall only be permissible for the growers or their heirs who previously cultivated it for the 1934 season, provided that none of them exceeds the area which he cultivated with tobacco during the said year (1934).

The Monopoly Administration shall proceed to purchase all quantities of leaf tobacco, tobacco still in the course of preparation, or manufactured tobacco, and the equipment allocated to manufacturing, in the following manner:

1- Within a period whose maximum limit may not exceed one month starting from the date specified in the first Article (1), the Monopoly Administration shall, in agreement with the owner of the tobacco, draw up an inventory of the quantities of leaf tobacco held by factory owners and merchants and shall take delivery of them immediately.

As for the prices at which these quantities must be purchased, they shall be determined by the Permanent Committee upon the proposal of the Monopoly Administration, and the purchase prices shall then be paid to the owner of the tobacco within a period of two months from the date of taking delivery thereof.

2- Owners of existing factories must cease manufacturing within a period reaching a maximum limit of three months starting from the date specified in the first Article. As for manufactured and delivered products, they shall be subject to the banderole system.

Upon the termination of manufacturing, factory owners shall return the quantities of banderoles still in their possession to the Banderole Department and shall recover their price.

As for the products that are still in the course of preparation or the manufactured products, and the operating equipment, the Monopoly Administration shall purchase them within the period referred to above, whose maximum limit reaches three months,

after they have been appraised in accordance with the conditions to be laid down by the Permanent Committee, and this Committee shall have the final decision in all difficulties that may arise during the appraisal.

The purchased equipment and products shall be placed at the disposal of the Monopoly Administration immediately upon its purchase thereof. As for their prices, they shall be settled within a period of two months after the date of purchase.

The Permanent Committee shall examine the situation of the factory owners.

The Monopoly Administration must employ nationals of the States placed under the Mandate in a proportion of at least 98 percent of the total number of its employees.

As for the employees of the purchased factories whom the Monopoly Administration will not employ, the Permanent Committee shall examine their situation.

Vendors holding current licences may continue selling until the exhaustion of the products in their possession that are subject to the banderole system. The Monopoly Administration shall have the right to take an inventory of these products starting from the first of July of the year 1935 and to recover them against their cost.

Selling permits and licences currently granted shall remain in force until the expiry of the date on which these permits or licences end, provided that vendors may obtain supplies up to that date from the products of the Monopoly.

Beneficiaries of the provisions of this Title shall have the right to retain the quantities of tobacco in their possession for export. In such a case, they must submit a written declaration of these quantities to the Monopoly Administration and store their tobacco in their warehouses. The Monopoly Administration shall thereupon be released from the obligation to purchase the said tobacco.
All provisions of laws, decrees, resolutions, regulations, and measures prior to this Resolution that are contrary to it are hereby repealed.
The Secretary-General is charged with the execution of this Resolution
The Monopoly Administration may sell cigarette paper in the form of booklets.

No person may possess a quantity exceeding 600 leaves of the cigarette paper of the Monopoly Administration manufactured in the form of booklets unless he holds a licence to sell tobacco and unless he submits a special declaration of his desire to engage in the sale of these booklets

The provisions of Title Three of this Resolution shall apply to cigarette paper manufactured in the form of booklets sold by the Monopoly Administration. Tobacco vendors must comply, with respect to the sale of the said cigarette paper, with the conditions appointed by the Monopoly Administration. Offenders shall be liable to the immediate withdrawal of their licence
The provisions of Titles Five and Six of this Resolution shall apply to acts of fraud concerning the cigarette paper of the Monopoly Administration manufactured in the form of booklets.

The following penalties shall apply to contraventions of the provisions of this Title :

1 - Selling without a licence or without a prior declaration (Article 92): a pecuniary penalty equivalent to three times the annual fee

2 - Selling at prices other than the prescribed price (Article 93): a pecuniary penalty of five to fifty Lebanese-Syrian pounds, and if the contravention is repeated, the licence shall be withdrawn immediately

3 - Fraudulent possession of cigarette paper ( Article 92): a pecuniary penalty of ten Lebanese-Syrian piastres for each leaf, the minimum penalty imposed being ten Lebanese-Syrian pounds, and confiscation of the paper. In addition thereto, vendors who, by reason of their failure to observe the regulations or for any other reason, are accomplices of the principal offenders shall be punished with the principal penalty and their licence shall be withdrawn immediately

4 - Manufacturing counterfeit marks of the marks of the Monopoly Administration, and using and possessing them: imprisonment from one year to three years and confiscation of the articles mentioned above. The judgment rendered in the penal action shall also fix the compensation which the offenders must pay to the Monopoly Administration by reason of the damage and loss caused to it by their acts.

Determination of the budget figures The figures of the General Budget and the Annexed Budgets for the financial year beginning on the first of January 2001 and ending on 31 December 2001 are determined in accordance with the provisions of the Second and Third Articles of this Law.

Appropriations

There are opened in the General Budget and the Annexed Budgets the appropriations set forth as follows:

The General Budget, Parts One and Two: 9.900.000.000.000 Pounds

Budget of Wired and Wireless Telecommunications: 1.038.524.500.000 Pounds

Budget of the Directorate of the National Lottery: 69.500.000.000 Pounds

Budget of the Directorate General of Cereals and Sugar Beet: 94.316.000.000 Pounds

Total: 11.102.340.500.000 Pounds

And that is in accordance with Tables Nos. 1, 2, 3, 4, annexed to this Law.

Revenues

The revenues of the General Budget and the Annexed Budgets are estimated in the following manner:

The General Budget, Part One, Ordinary Revenues: 4.900.000.000.000 Pounds

The General Budget, Part Two, Extraordinary Revenues: 5.000.000.000.000 Pounds

Budget of Wired and Wireless Telecommunications: 1.038.524.500.000 Pounds

- Budget of the Directorate of the National Lottery: 69.500.000.000 Pounds

Budget of the Directorate General of Cereals and Sugar Beet: 94.316.000.000 Pounds

Total: 11.102.340.500.000 Pounds

And that is in accordance with Tables Nos. 5, 6, 7, 8 annexed to this Law.

Authorisation of Collection

Authorisation is granted, in accordance with the provisions of this Law and the provisions of the laws in force, for the collection of the various taxes, fees, proceeds and revenues set forth in Tables Nos. (5 6 7 8) annexed to this Law.

Authorisation to Borrow

1 The Government is authorised, within the limits of an amount equivalent to the needs of the Treasury, to issue Treasury bonds in Lebanese currency for long, medium and short terms, by decisions issued by the Minister of Finance. The Government must notify the Chamber of Deputies of any amounts of the issued Treasury bonds that exceed the limits of the actual deficit realised in the execution of the Budget, including the total appropriations carried over to the year 2001 and the additional appropriations, by virtue of quarterly reports setting out the reasons necessitating such excess.

2 Within the framework of restructuring the public debt, the Government is authorised to issue Treasury bonds in foreign currencies up to a value of two billion US dollars, provided that the funds borrowed pursuant to this authorisation are used to refinance external debt maturities and/or to convert the equivalent of their value of the public debt in Lebanese Pounds into foreign currencies. All of these issued bonds must be finally repaid within a period not exceeding thirty years from the date of commencement of their issuance, and the interest rates on these bonds shall be determined in accordance with the rates prevailing in international markets for similar bonds abroad, and this shall be effected by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

3 When the Government issues Treasury bonds in foreign currency for periods less than the maximum period for their maturities as determined in this Law and previous laws, the Government shall have the right, as from the date their maturity falls due, to issue new Treasury bonds in foreign currency to replace them and in the same value of the matured amounts for additional periods, provided that the value of all Treasury bonds in foreign currency at any time whatsoever does not exceed the volume of the amounts in respect of which the Government is authorised to issue bonds in foreign currencies, and that the total period does not exceed the maximum period determined in this Law and previous laws as from the date of commencement of the first issuance of those bonds, and that the new borrowed funds are allocated for the same purpose determined in paragraph 2.

Loan Accounts

Special Treasury accounts shall be opened for loans, to which shall be credited the value received out of the principal of these loans, and to which shall be debited the values paid in settlement of matured instalments and bonds.

Manner of Repayment of Loans

The Government is authorised, by decrees passed in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance, to open, where necessary, annually appropriations in the General Budget and the Annexed Budgets for the purpose of paying the instalments of loans that fall due (principal, interest and supplementary expenses) and determining the sources for covering them.

Application of the Provisions of External Loan Agreements to the Entirety of Expenditure Pertaining to Externally Financed Projects

There shall apply to the expenditure of external loan and grant agreements in effect with the various public administrations, public institutions and municipalities, the regulatory provisions adopted by the lending party, whether such expenditure is from the local part or from the foreign part, provided that they are subject to the subsequent audit of the Court of Accounts.

Opening of Extraordinary Appropriations

In implementation of the provisions of Article 85 of the Constitution, the President of the Republic may, if emergency circumstances call for urgent expenditures, issue a decree based on a decision issued by the Council of Ministers, opening extraordinary or additional appropriations or transferring appropriations in the General Budget for the year 2001, provided that these appropriations do not exceed thirty-five billion Pounds, and these measures must be submitted for the approval of the Chamber of Deputies at the first session in which it convenes thereafter.

Carry-over of Appropriations and Transfer of Carried-over Appropriations

Authorisation is granted to transfer to the other Chapters of the Budget the appropriations allocated in previous budgets and carried over to the budget of the year 2001 under Chapter 26 (Debts Due for Payment) in the following paragraph:

16 Payment of the increases entailed by the Rent Law. The transfer shall be effected in accordance with the rules provided for in Article 26 of the Public Accounting Law, and authorisation is also granted to carry over the appropriations of Chapter 26 (Debts Due for Payment) before or after their transfer to the other Chapters of the Budget, until the obligations arising out of them are settled, owing to the attachment of the rights of third parties thereto. Authorisation is also granted, where necessary, to carry over the appropriations allocated under Chapter 28 (Budget Reserve), Items (12 and 13 and 14 and 16 and 18),

and authorisation is also granted to transfer within this Chapter from item to item by a decision of the Minister of Finance after the endorsement of the Central Controller of Expenditure Commitment. The carry-over shall be effected in accordance with the rules determined in Article 114 of the Public Accounting Law. Owing to the merger and abolition of certain Ministries pursuant to Law 247 dated 7/8/2000

authorisation is granted, on an exceptional basis, to carry over the appropriations provided for in certain administrations to the new budget lines corresponding to them in the various Chapters of the budget of the year 2001, and the time limit for the carry-over is extended for a period of two months from the date of entry into force of the 2001 Budget Law. All appropriations transferred, committed, reserved or expended under the old budget lines shall be deemed as if they were transferred, committed, reserved or expended under the corresponding new budget lines.

Opening of Appropriations to Subsidise Interest on Development Loans

The Government is authorised annually and as needed to provide in the Budget Reserve for the appropriations required to cover part of the interest on development loans (agricultural, industrial, touristic, technological, and artisanal) in accordance with the special regulations laid down by the Minister of Finance and the Governor of the Bank of Lebanon for this purpose.

Appropriations for Medical Treatment

There shall be distributed by a decree passed in the Council of Ministers, upon the joint proposal of the competent Minister and the Minister of Finance, the appropriations allocated on a lump-sum basis in the various Chapters of the General Budget designated for medical treatment in private institutions and hospitals and contracts with physicians in the private sector.

Authorisation to pay expropriations and contractors' statements of account pertaining to the year 2000 from the balance of Law 95

It is authorised to pay expropriation compensations, contractors' statements of account, medical and hospitalisation expenses, and compensations for martyrs and wounded of the Israeli aggressions that were incurred before 31/12/2000 and for which decisions, statements of account or invoices were issued during the year 2000, by means of special treasury bonds out of the balance of the amount of 1242 billion specified in Law No. 95 dated 18/6/1999.

Deduction of a share from the municipal fee for villages that have no municipalities

The Ministry of Finance shall deduct from the municipal fee on inflammable materials, prior to its distribution to the municipalities, an amount not exceeding eight billion pounds to be allocated for lighting, works and cleaning in villages that have no municipalities (charges for energy, maintenance, equipment and cleaning) through the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities; this amount shall be distributed by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance and the Minister of Interior and Municipalities.

: Permitting the Lebanese University to conclude agreements

The Lebanese University may conclude agreements with persons of public or private law to provide services or prepare studies, consultations or prestations in various fields in return for charges, a percentage of which shall be allocated as fees for members of the teaching staff and for employees who contribute thereto, and another percentage to finance scientific research, its requirements and its equipment, in accordance with the proposal of the University Council and the approval of the Minister of Education and Higher Education and the Minister of Finance, provided that the remaining balance reverts to the University.

Determination of the values of lapsed assessments

Shall be deemed lapsed all assessments, including surcharges and all other additions and fines, the annual total of which does not exceed ten thousand Lebanese pounds from each of the income tax, the built property tax and the transfer duty, and the competent financial departments shall be exempted from issuing assessment rolls and collection orders for these amounts and from collecting them.

Rounding of fractions

A fraction of a thousand pounds shall be rounded up to a thousand pounds in favour of the Treasury in all assessment, collection and expenditure transactions, including allowances, salaries, wages and their accessories.

Deferral of the recovery of treasury advances

The Government is authorised to defer the recovery of treasury advances that were granted to public institutions, funds, councils and all other moral persons of the public and private sectors (in which the State contributes) that were granted treasury advances. The value of these advances may be converted into a contribution to the capital of the institutions concerned in favour of the State, and likewise when these institutions are transformed into joint-stock companies within the framework of privatisation operations pursuant to Law No. 228 dated 31/5/2000 (Regulating Privatisation Operations and Determining their Conditions and Fields of Application).

As for the institutions, councils and funds that do not transform into actual joint-stock companies, they must, as soon as a surplus becomes available to them, transfer this surplus to the Treasury in an amount equivalent to the sums borrowed by each of them, in accordance with the legal rules. Where necessary, the details of application of this Article shall be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

Authorisation to transfer appropriations allocated for publicity and marketing abroad

It is authorised to transfer the appropriations provided for under allocation 1311121249 (other public relations) allocated for publicity and marketing abroad by a decision of the Minister of Finance, after the endorsement of the Central Controller of Expenditure Commitment, to the other chapters of the budget according to need, upon the request of the competent minister and the approval of the President of the Council of Ministers.

Authorisation to execute consensual agreements for the sale of petroleum derivatives

Notwithstanding any other text, the Ministry of Energy and Water may sell petroleum derivatives of all kinds in all public institutions and administrations pursuant to consensual agreements executed for this purpose, in which the administrative and financial conditions are determined, provided that the general and special provisions set forth in the Public Accounting Law are observed in concluding them.

Second: The inheritance and transfer duty departments are granted an additional time limit of two months starting from the date of publication of this Law to complete all transactions the documents of which were submitted up to 30/9/2000 inclusive, and taxpayers are exempted from assessment and collection fines on condition of paying the first instalment or the full duty within a time limit of two months from the expiry of the additional time limit specified above for these departments.

Third: Inheritance and transfer duties due on taxable events the complete documents of which were submitted up to 30/9/2000 inclusive, and the assessments of which were issued and paid or paid by instalments before the publication of this Law, shall be deemed as if they had been paid or paid by instalments within the legal time limits.
