In the event of a contravention of the preceding Articles 76 and 79, every person who carried out or ordered the carrying out of an unlawful clearing on land belonging to him shall be sentenced to a fine of 10 to 50 Lebanese-Syrian pounds for each hectare cleared, and he must in addition restore the cleared lands to their wooded state if so ordered in the judgment upon the request of the Administration within a period not exceeding three years; if the contravention is repeated, the maximum fine shall always be applied and a sentence of imprisonment from two days to thirty days may in addition bepronounced; if the owners do not carry out the afforestation within the prescribed period, the Forest Department shall carry it out at their expense and the recovery of the costs of these works shall be pursued under the conditions provided for in Article 147 of this Resolution

Every individual who wishes to exploit by way of felling his woods, of whatever kind they may be and whatever their produce may be, must submit two months in advance a written declaration thereof to the Forest Administration. In this declaration must be stated the elected domicile in the administrative district in which the woods are situated; during this period, which begins from the day the Administration receives the declaration, the said Administration shall have the right to notify its objection to the exploitation, and the Forest Administration shall then proceed to inspect the state and location of the woods; in the application for exploitation must be stated the name of the applicant, the location of the wood, its area and the number of trees intended to be felled if the wood consists of timber trees, and the age and species of the trees intended to be exploited, as well as the kind and quantity of the produce which he wishes to exploit. The investigation into this application and its result shall not in any manner whatsoever bind the liability of the Administration towards other persons who may have rights over the lands intended to be exploited; upon examining theproces-verbal relating to the inspection of the lands, the Forest Administration shall, if necessary, notify the interested party of its provisional objection to the exploitation, and in this case the proces-verbal shall be notified to the applicant, who may submit his observations regarding this decision, and this proces-verbal, accompanied where appropriate by the observations of the interested parties, shall then be referred to the Head of State, who shall maintain or lift the objection
Objection to exploitation may only be made in the case where the land sought to be exploited falls within one of the conditions provided for in Article 77 of this Resolution
If the Forest Administration deems it necessary to determine the conditions within which the authorisation for exploitation may be granted, it shall do so

Every exploitation commenced before the expiry of the period of two months fixed in Article 82 without the authorisation of the Forest Administration, and every exploitation carried out notwithstanding its objection, and all contraventions of the conditions imposed, shall entail the application of the penalties provided for in Articles 102 and 103 in respect of the exploiter or the persons deriving rights from him

Protection zones may be established by virtue of a law, a resolution or a legislative decree, and these zones may comprise: 1) woods of all categories existing within the conditions provided for in the preceding Article 77 b) barren lands falling into ruin by reason of the runoff of water. The provisions of Title II of this Resolution shall apply to these protection zones, and neither clearing nor exploitation may take place therein without prior authorisation from the Forest Administration. The use of pasture therein shall be subject to the same regime applicable to the forests of the State domain
The Forest Administration shall proceed with the demarcation of these zones and the setting of boundaries for them

The Forest Administration shall have the requisite capacity to decide the prohibition of entry into wooded or unwooded lands belonging to individuals or to communities by a decision published in the Official Gazette if their owners request in writing their protection from pasture; the protection of these lands against the unlawful entry of livestock therein and against all the misdemeanours provided for in this Resolution shall apply forthwith from the date of such publication under the same conditions fixed for forests subject to the forest regime

Owners may appoint private guards approved by the Forest Administration, and the decisions issued approving such guards may be revoked under the conditions provided for in the preceding articles relating to village guards; private guards must wear a badge and may not perform their functions until after they have taken the oath before the magistrate of the locality of the woods

With a view to future expropriation, it may be declared of public utility to establish afforestation zones comprising lands which it is deemed necessary to afforest or restore for the conservation and protection of the soil, or for the needs of land exploitation, or for the fixation of dunes, or for the regulation of watercourses for public health or for the needs of summer resorts. Such afforestation shall be carried out at the expense of the State

Owners whose properties are situated within one of the afforestation zones shall retain the disposal thereof until the purchase of the same by the Administration either by way of expropriation or by way of exchange

At the end of each financial year, municipal councils and village committees must submit to the Forest Administration a statement of all the sums which they have collected from the revenues of village woods and pastures and which are reserved for the works relating to afforestation in application of the provisions of the preceding Article 72

Upon examining this statement and after carrying out a local inquiry, the Forest Administration may request, if it deems it useful, the application of the available sums to the execution of afforestation works through the care of the municipalities or village committees under the supervision and technical control of the Forest Administration. These works shall be carried out on the village lands which are still barren and which the Administration designates for this purpose; the municipality or the village committee shall be responsible for the protection of these works after their completion, in particular their protection against grazing

Extension of the time limit relating to the power of attorney for the transfer of ownership of motor vehicles

By way of exception and on a one-time basis, the power of attorney or powers of attorney relating to the transfer of ownership of motor vehicles shall remain valid for registration with the competent department for a period of two months from the date of execution of the first power of attorney without any surcharge being due thereon. A surcharge of fifty thousand pounds for each month of delay shall be imposed on anyone who delays registration, a fraction of a month being considered a full month, provided that the said surcharge does not exceed one million pounds. Holders of powers of attorney executed prior to the promulgation of this Law shall be granted a time limit ending on 31/12/2001 to complete the registration formalities under the previous provisions, after which the surcharge set forth in the preceding paragraph shall apply.

Exemption of Middle East Airlines from airport fees and charges

Middle East Airlines (MEA) is exempted from the airport fees and charges due by it since the year 1991 and up to the date of publication of this Law.

Amendment of Article 411 of the Customs Code

Article 411 of the Customs Code - Decree No. 4461 dated 15/12/2000 is amended to read as follows: "Imprisonment in customs actions shall be enforced without the need to prove the debtor's solvency, unless he is in a state of bankruptcy and such bankruptcy is not due to a criminal fault on his part; regarding the age of the person whose imprisonment is sought, the general provisions set forth in Article 146 of the Penal Code, read in conjunction with Article 1003 of the Code of Civil Procedure, shall apply." This text shall apply to pending cases.

Organisation and distribution of horse racing revenues

First: The deductions withheld from the gross total of bets at the Beirut Hippodrome shall be determined as follows: (5%) to the Municipality of Beirut, (18%) to the entity with which the Municipality of Beirut contracts to manage, operate and develop the Hippodrome, hereinafter referred to as "the Contractor", and this agreement shall be approved by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers. The value of the amounts resulting from the proceeds of each of the above rates must not exceed maximum limits promulgated by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers.

Second: If the amounts set forth in the last paragraph of Item First above of this Article exceed the maximum limits assigned thereto, the distribution of these amounts shall be carried out by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers as follows: With respect to the amounts exceeding the maximum limit set for the Municipality of Beirut: these amounts shall be distributed between both the Municipality of Beirut and the account allocated for constructions at the Hippodrome. With respect to anything exceeding the maximum limit allocated to the Contractor: the amounts exceeding this limit shall be transferred to the account allocated for constructions referred to above.

Third: With the exception of the deductions withheld pursuant to Item First above of this Article, and notwithstanding any other text, no financial or municipal taxes or fees shall be due on betting slips and admission tickets to the Hippodrome.

Fourth: The agreement between the Municipality of Beirut and the Contractor shall determine the conditions and duration of the contract for the exploitation of the Hippodrome, and the distribution of all other revenues and operating expenses between the Municipality of Beirut and the Contractor, as well as the manner and conditions of use and management of the funds accumulated in the account allocated for constructions, shall be determined pursuant to a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers.

Fifth: The manner of supervision and audit of the management of the Hippodrome, the control and accounting of its operations including bets, other revenues, operating expenses, and the costs of equipment and constructions, as well as the appointment of independent auditors, shall be determined pursuant to a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers, and a committee shall be appointed in the same manner to carry out these tasks.

Sixth: A tax shall be imposed on bets (after deducting the value of the deductions withheld therefrom as provided for in Paragraph First of this Article) on the basis of the winnings rate, that is, the multiple achieved by the betting unit as a result of the bet, one betting unit being equivalent to one Lebanese pound. The tax shall be withheld for the benefit of the Treasury from the betting winnings in accordance with the rates and brackets pertaining thereto as follows: (1%) of the winnings rate exceeding one multiple and not exceeding two multiples of the betting unit. (3%) of the winnings rate exceeding two multiples and not exceeding four multiples of the betting unit. (6%) of the winnings rate exceeding four multiples and not exceeding seven multiples of the betting unit. (10%) of the winnings rate exceeding seven multiples and not exceeding fifteen multiples of the betting unit. (15%) of the winnings rate exceeding fifteen multiples and not exceeding thirty multiples of the betting unit. (20%) of the winnings rate exceeding thirty multiples of the betting unit.

Allocation of pension or dismissal indemnity

The second paragraph of Article 15 of Legislative Decree No. 47 issued on 29/6/1983 is amended to read as follows: The retirement pension or dismissal indemnity shall be allocated by a decision of the Director General of Finance based on the official record of the Retirement Committee.

Expenditures charged to the Independent Municipal Fund

Notwithstanding any other text, the Independent Municipal Fund shall bear the expenditures of sanitation, waste collection, treatment and landfilling, and the cleaning and maintenance of sewers and canals. These expenditures shall be deducted from the share of the municipalities benefiting from these services and which have previously benefited therefrom, in accordance with the proportion of their benefit therefrom. No amount shall be deducted from the share of the municipalities not benefiting from these services.

Liquidation of disability pension or retirement pension for diplomats

There shall be added to the text of the new Article 12 of Legislative Decree No. 47 dated 29/6/1983, amended pursuant to Law No. 717 dated 5/11/98:

6 - Notwithstanding any other text, the salary received by their counterparts in Lebanon shall be adopted in the liquidation of disability pensions, retirement pensions, or dismissal indemnities for foreign service personnel serving abroad.

Dispensing with the easement and planning certificate

The following paragraph shall be added to Article 57 of Decision No. 188 dated 15/3/1926 (Establishment of the Real Estate Register): "In contracts of sale, the easement and planning certificate may be dispensed with if the seller and the buyer agree thereto and each of them undertakes to bear all liability resulting from the non-production of the said certificate".

Granting and manner of repayment of a Treasury advance to the Public Corporation for Housing

The Public Corporation for Housing shall be granted a Treasury advance in the amount of three billion Lebanese pounds, allocated to lending to residents affected by the landslides of the Biakout area, District of Metn, in order to pay the first instalment of the purchase price of new dwellings or to purchase new dwellings, in accordance with the lending regulations in force at the Corporation.

The Treasury advance shall be repaid in whole or in part from the amounts awarded in favour of the residents affected by the landslides of the Biakout area, and the balance shall be repaid through an appropriation provided for in the General Budget.

Authorisation to establish a lottery (TELE-BETTING)

The Government is authorised to establish types of lottery conducted by means of tele-betting (TELE-BETTING) for betting on the results of events, games, sports matches, and others. The rules of operation of these types of lottery and all matters relating to their management, organisation, and supervision shall be determined by decrees adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance. The Government shall award the concession for these types of lottery by way of an invitation to tender.

Application of the amendment of the temporary transport allowance with effect from 1/1/2001.

The amendment of the temporary transport allowance shall apply in accordance with the provisions of Item Third of Article Two of Law No. 717 dated 5/11/1998 (Conversion of the salary scales of the general administrative cadre) with effect from 1/1/2001

Available sums which have not been expended on these works shall be retained to be used later, and it shall be prohibited to use them for other than this purpose except by an authorisation by decree or local decision. The President of the Municipality or the President of the Village Committee is personally responsible for their custody.

Individuals or groups wishing to carry out afforestation works on their lands may obtain free of charge from the State, through the Forests Department, seeds or young saplings, and in such a case the expenses of sowing, planting and protecting the saplings shall be borne by the interested parties under the supervision of the Administration; provided that the State may also bear a part of these expenses by way of encouragement for afforestation if the works carried out in this manner fall within a general programme drawn up by the Forests Department.

The sowing and planting of woods carried out by a person on mountain peaks or their slopes or on hills, and which are neither adjacent to dwellings nor walled, shall be exempted from all tax for a period of thirty years, and likewise woods and forests re-established after a fire shall be exempted from all tax for a period of ten years, provided that their owner has not burned them. The exemption from tax shall not commence except from the day of the inspection of the afforestation works by the Forests Department pursuant to a written petition submitted by the interested owner of the wood. The two periods of thirty years and ten years specified above shall commence from the year of the establishment of the wood.

Whoever breaks, destroys, removes or eliminates boundary markers or flags planted following an official demarcation of forests or places designated for afforestation shall be punished by a fine from one pound to 25 Lebanese-Syrian pounds. If the destruction, removal or uprooting covers several boundary markers or flags, imprisonment from two days to three months may be adjudged, and if following this destruction or removal an encroachment upon forest lands occurs followed by agricultural works or breaking up of the land, the penalty of imprisonment shall always be adjudged. All this shall not preclude claiming damages, and in all cases the boundary markers and flags shall be replanted and the places restored to their former state at the expense of the offender. If the offence is repeated, imprisonment shall be mandatorily adjudged.

Every extraction or removal of stones, sand, mineral, earth, grass, heather (Bruyere), gorse (broom), forage, green or dry leaves, or natural fertilisers found on forest land, or acorns, various seeds or other fruits or forest products designated by the Forests Administration without an authorisation from this Administration or from their owner, as the case may be, must be punished by a fine equivalent to double the value of the thing taken. The value adopted each year as a basis for calculating the fine shall be designated by a decree or local decision, and in all cases the products by means of which the misdemeanour was committed shall be seized.

If building materials are extracted for public works carried out on forest lands, the Public Works Administration shall designate beforehand to the Forests Administration the places of extraction. The forest officers shall determine, in agreement with the public works officers, the conditions and modalities of these extractions, and the Forests Administration shall designate, where necessary, the compensations which must be paid to the State for the occupation of the land and for the value of the extracted materials, as well as the clauses and conditions imposed for the extraction of the materials while preserving the interest of the forest. Every removal of building materials or cutting of trees carried out without the completion of the preceding formalities shall entail the application of the penalties provided for in the preceding Article 98 against the offender.

Whoever ploughs land inside woods and forests which are the property of others must be sentenced, in proportion to the ploughed area, to a fine calculated at the rate of 5 to 25 Lebanese-Syrian pounds for each hectare, provided that this fine may not be less than five pounds. Whoever breaks up forest lands which are the property of others or which are subject to the forest regime must be sentenced, in proportion to the area of the broken-up land, to a fine calculated at the rate of 10 to 50 Lebanese-Syrian pounds for each hectare, provided that this fine may not be less than ten pounds. If the land is ploughed immediately after being broken up, the fine shall be imposed for the breaking up only. If the offence is repeated, imprisonment may be adjudged from eight days to thirty days for ploughing and from eight to sixty days for breaking up. In all cases, damages must be paid as compensation for the harm caused to the afforestation, and in the case of breaking up, the Administration must restore the afforestation at the expense of the offender.

Whoever is found between sunrise and sunset in woods and forests which are the property of others outside the ordinary roads and paths while carrying instruments and tools suitable for cutting firewood or for extracting bark must be punished by a fine from one pound to ten Lebanese-Syrian pounds. Whoever is found by night or by day on lands on which the Administration has commenced works of afforestation, planting or fixation of hills and has prohibited entry thereto outside the ordinary roads and paths must be punished by the same penalties. This shall not preclude, in both cases, the payment of the damages which he caused, and the maximum limit of the fine must always be adjudged in the case of repetition of the offence.

The cutting or uprooting constituting a misdemeanour of trees whose circumference measures, at a height of one metre above the ground, more than two decimetres must be punished by a fine from one pound to five Lebanese-Syrian pounds, according to the size of the tree, for each tree cut or uprooted. As for the cutting and uprooting of trees whose circumference measures two decimetres or less, the fine shall be calculated in proportion to their weight at the rate of one Lebanese-Syrian piastre for each kilogramme of firewood. In addition to that, in all the cases provided for in the preceding paragraph, imprisonment from eight days to two months may be adjudged.

Mutilating trees with a mutilation that leads to decay, topping them, cutting their branches without distinction between them, taking branches thrown down by the wind or firewood constituting a misdemeanour, and cutting bark must be punished as if the tree had been cut from its base.

In all cases, in addition to the fines, the things taken must be seized or restituted and their value taken, and this shall not preclude, where necessary, claiming damages as compensation for the harm caused. In addition to that, the saws, axes, billhooks and other instruments of the same kind found with the offender, as well as the means of transport, must be confiscated.

The owners of animals found by day in the act of committing the misdemeanour of grazing in forests in which grazing is prohibited must be sentenced to a fine of: 5 to 10 Lebanese-Syrian piastres for each head of the species of pig, sheep or horse, and 10 to 20 Lebanese-Syrian piastres for each head of the species of cattle, and 25 to 50 Lebanese-Syrian piastres for each head of goats or camels. In addition to that, the herdsman may be sentenced to imprisonment from two days to thirty days, and if the offence is repeated or if the misdemeanour is committed by night or in woods whose age is under ten years, the maximum limit of the fine must always be applied.

Concessionaires or lessees by mutual agreement of a pasture may not introduce into the forest a number of animals greater than the number specified in the book of conditions or introduce their animals outside the designated places, under pain of the penalties prescribed in the preceding Article 105. They must also, if the book of conditions so imposes, mark the animals with a special mark under pain of the fine specified in the same Article, unless a declaration is made to the officers of the Forests Department that the animals introduced into the forests are unmarked and the officers accept their introduction without a mark.

Whoever counterfeits or falsifies the marks of the State forests hammer mentioned in the preceding Article 18 or fraudulently uses the original hammers shall be punished by a fine of 10 to 100 Lebanese-Syrian pounds and by imprisonment from six months to two years. If the marks of the hammers are intentionally destroyed, the offender shall be punished by a fine of 10 to 100 Lebanese-Syrian pounds and by imprisonment from one month to six months, and if the offence is repeated, the maximum penalty shall always be applied.

An offence shall be deemed repeated when, during the Gregorian year preceding the day on which the misdemeanour was committed, a first judgment has been rendered against the offender and has become final for committing a contravention or a misdemeanour relating to forests.

It is prohibited to carry or light fire outside dwellings and buildings prepared for exploitation within the boundaries of woods and forests, and likewise outside such forests and woods at a distance of less than 200 metres starting from the said boundaries, from the first of July to 31 October. This prohibition applies even to owners of private forests and also includes charcoal making, the distillation of tar and resin, and in general all industries requiring the use of fire, subject to the application of the provisions of the following Articles 110, 111 and 112.

During the period between the first of July and 31 October, dwellings, exploitation buildings and stone-built shelters standing within woods and forests or at a distance of 200 metres therefrom in which a fire is lit either for domestic needs or for industrial needs shall be surrounded by an open space of land 25 metres wide from which all thorns or grass and every resinous tree shall be cleared if the Forest Administration deems it necessary, and this open space shall always be kept in good condition and no combustibles shall be deposited therein.

In shelters, tents, encampments, workshops, factories or temporary structures whatsoever standing in woods and forests or within the two-hundred-metre zone, the use of fire during the same period shall only be authorised for cooking food, and the stoves shall be surrounded by an open space of 25 metres in accordance with the conditions laid down in the preceding Article. During the same period of prohibition, the Forest Administration may exceptionally authorise the use of fire for calcining ores in exploitations situated in woods or within the two-hundred-metre zone starting from such woods, provided that each stove is surrounded by an open space established under the conditions laid down above, the width of which shall be determined in the authorisation decision. The making of charcoal and tar during this same period in State forests and in private forests shall be carried out under the conditions imposed by the Forest Administration, and the said Administration may prohibit it temporarily or permanently if it deems it necessary.

Companies holding a concession for a steam railway or tramway or entrusted with the management thereof, established within forests or within a zone of 200 metres starting from their zone, shall leave no grass or herbaceous plants in the places on which the tracks are laid between the first of June and the first of November. Furthermore, along the sections of railway lines crossing State forests and designated for this purpose by agreement between the Administrations of Public Works and of Forests, trenches shall be established from which all thorns and, where necessary, every resinous tree shall be cleared and which shall always be kept in good condition; the width of these trenches shall be 20 metres on each side of the track, and they shall be established through the diligence of the companies, at their expense and under their responsibility. During this same period, the use of equipment employing fire on roads crossing forests or situated at a distance of less than two hundred metres from their zone shall be subject to obtaining an authorisation from the Forest Administration.

From the first of July to 31 October, no person may burn thorns, grass, straw or other standing plants except by licence from the Forest Administration on lands situated at a distance of less than five hundred metres from woods and forests. From the first of November to 30 June, the zone of this distance shall be reduced to 200 metres unless there is a licence to the contrary.
A person who lights a fire shall in all cases be civilly liable for the damage he causes to third parties, without any liability being incurred by the State as a result thereof.

Whoever burns anything in violation of the preceding Article 113 shall be punished by a fine of 10 to 200 Lebanese-Syrian pounds and by imprisonment from 8 days to two months, or by one of these two penalties only.

In the event of a fire in woods or forests, the representatives of the Forest Administration, as well as officers of the public force and representatives of the administrative authorities, shall have the requisite capacity to requisition all persons, pack or draught animals, means of transport and equipment which they deem necessary. Every person whose assistance is requested by these officers and who refuses it without lawful cause shall be punished by a fine of two to 25 Lebanese-Syrian pounds. Those who use the woods and forests for their needs, if they refuse in these same circumstances to lend their assistance in fighting the fire or prematurely leave the fire-fighting worksites without authorisation from the representative of the Administration, shall furthermore be deprived of their rights of usufruct in these forests and woods for a period ranging between two and five years. This deprivation shall be decided administratively by a decree or a local decision upon the proposal of the Forest Administration, and the deprivation may be collective if the refusal is collective.
Grazing is prohibited for a period of ten years over the entire area of burned woods and forests.

No industrial establishment whatsoever that uses fire or requires the installation of a fuel depot may be established within forests or at less than 500 metres from State forests without a special licence from the Forest Administration, under penalty of a fine of 10 to 200 Lebanese-Syrian pounds, and the establishment shall furthermore be demolished through the diligence of the Forest Administration and at the expense of the parties concerned. The judgment rendered in this regard shall include the requirement to demolish the said establishment within the three months following.

With the exception of inhabited places existing on the date of promulgation of this Resolution, no building whatsoever may be erected and no tent whatsoever covered with or composed of inflammable materials may be pitched within forests or at a distance of less than 200 metres from the boundaries of State forests without a special licence from the Forest Administration, under penalty of a fine of 5 to 100 Lebanese-Syrian pounds. Furthermore, these buildings shall be demolished through the diligence of the Forest Administration and at the expense of the parties concerned within one month starting from the date of the judgment ordering their demolition.
Those who intentionally burn woods or forests, or their accomplices, shall be punished by the penalties provided for in the Penal Code.

Every contravention of the provisions of Articles 109, 110, 111 and 112 of this Resolution shall be punished by a fine of two to 25 Lebanese-Syrian pounds, and imprisonment from two months to three months may furthermore be imposed. If the contravention causes a fire that spreads to woods and forests, the unintentional perpetrator may be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years, without prejudice to a claim for damages. If the lighting of a fire which is legally authorised to be lit or which is lit within the legal conditions causes a fire in neighbouring properties, the person who lit the fire shall be liable for all damages, unless the damage for which compensation is claimed resulted from measures taken to protect a wood from fire.

The State shall bear no financial liability whatsoever on account of the partial or total destruction of a wood belonging to individuals or to communities following the taking of fire protection measures legally ordered by the administrative authority during fire-fighting operations.

Where any misdemeanour among the misdemeanours provided for in Chapter I of this Title is committed and causes damage to a woodland located within natural sites decided to be preserved, the maximum fine must be imposed.

The Forestry Administration is charged, in the interest of the State and in the interest of other owners of woodlands and forests, with ascertaining the misdemeanours and contraventions committed in respect of forests and with the prosecutions relating to compensation therefor. Actions and prosecutions shall be brought before the courts having jurisdiction therefor upon the request of the competent representatives of the Forestry Administration and through the diligence of the Public Prosecution; provided that they may also be brought simultaneously by the officers of the Administration whom the Forestry Administration appoints for this purpose and by the Public Prosecution, which has the right to bring the counterpart of such actions. The representatives of the Forestry Administration have the right to present the action themselves before the court and to have their statements heard in support of the pleadings which they submit.

Forestry guards shall investigate misdemeanours and contraventions and ascertain them throughout the entire district of the court before which they took the oath, and they shall write the reports themselves, sign them and date them under pain of nullity, or send them forthwith to the head of their department, and the said head shall ensure that the necessary action is taken in respect thereof. There must mandatorily be mentioned in the seizure reports the following: - the circumstance of the misdemeanour and the places of its occurrence - the given name, surname, profession, nationality and place of residence of the perpetrator of the misdemeanour, and if it is not possible to mention this information in the seizure report, the reason for not mentioning it must be mentioned - where the person who committed the misdemeanour is a married woman, a young child or a servant, the given name, surname, profession, place of residence and nationality of the husband, the father, the mother or the employer must be mentioned in the seizure report - the age, species, size and number of the trees which are the subject of the misdemeanour, and if the trees are small, their weight shall be estimated as provided for in Article 102 - the type and number of the seized implements - the kind and number of the seized animals - the number and kind of the animals which were found grazing contrary to the law, as well as the age of the woodlands in which the misdemeanour was committed - and in cultivation misdemeanours, the ploughed area shall be mentioned. Judicial police officers, gendarmes, and police commissioners and officers may also carry out all operations of investigating and ascertaining the misdemeanours and contraventions provided for in this Resolution.

Misdemeanours and contraventions relating to forests shall be proved either by seizure reports or by the testimony of witnesses in the absence of seizure reports or where such reports are insufficient.
The Public Prosecution shall inform, by a monthly schedule, the representative of the Forestry Department who referred to it the actions and prosecutions relating to forests of the outcome thereof.

Forestry officers are authorised to seize the livestock by means of which the misdemeanour was committed, and the implements, vehicles, draught gear, pack animals and all means of transport which the perpetrators of the misdemeanours used, and to place them under the hand of a judicial custodian; and they shall follow the things which the perpetrators of the misdemeanours took to the places to which they were transported or the places in which they presume them to be on the basis of reliable information or testimony, and shall also place them under the hand of a judicial custodian; provided that they may not enter houses, thickets and enclosed places except in the presence of the Justice of the Peace or his deputy, or in the presence of the police commissioner, the mayor of the municipality or the mukhtar. These public officers may not refuse to accompany the forestry officers forthwith if the said officers request them to assist them in searches, and they must sign the seizure report of the operations which take place in their presence.

Officers of the Forestry Administration have the right to call directly or in writing upon the public force to assist them in suppressing all contraventions provided for in this Resolution, as well as to search for forest produce taken contrary to the law or sold or transported contrary to the provisions of this Resolution and to seize the same; and they may arrest any unknown person whom they surprise in flagrante delicto and hand him over to the representatives of the public force or to the local administrative authority.

Where livestock found in the commission of a misdemeanour or produce taken fraudulently in a forest is seized, such livestock or produce shall be placed under the custody of a person of good conduct, solvent, and residing as close as possible to the place of the misdemeanour, or if there is no such person, with the mukhtar of the village closest to the place of the misdemeanour, and this latter may not in any case whatsoever refuse responsibility for such custody. If it appears from the contents of the seizure report that the produce placed under custody comes from the State forest domain, the Forestry Administration must order its sale for the benefit of the State within the three days following the seizure, unless the Administration prefers to retain such produce.

Where the seizure is effected upon livestock, vehicles, draught animals or pack animals, or upon produce not coming from the State forest domain, a copy of this report must forthwith after the closing of the seizure report be drawn up and deposited within three days at the registry of the Peace Court. Any person who claims the seized things may inspect this report. Upon the appointment of the judicial custodian, a copy of the custody seizure report shall be delivered to the person charged with carrying it out. The Justice of the Peace may, upon the request of the owner, provisionally lift the seizure subject to payment of the expenses and provision of a security. If not the slightest claim is made in respect of the seized livestock or things within five days starting from the date of the seizure, or if the claimant thereto fails within the same period to provide a security, the Justice of the Peace shall order their sale by public auction and shall fix the expenses of custody and sale. This sale shall take place at the nearest market through the diligence of the clerk of the court registry and in the presence of a representative of the Forestry Department. The proceeds of the sale must be used to cover the expenses of custody and sale first and foremost, as well as the amount of the prescribed penal and civil penalties which the Forestry Department provisionally assesses, and any surplus over that shall be returned to the person entitled thereto. Where the matter relates to livestock, there must not be sold thereof, unless their owner remains unknown, save the number of animals necessary to cover the expenses and penalties mentioned above. Where judgment of acquittal is rendered, the owner of such livestock shall have the right to recover the full sale price, and the expenses fixed for custody and the expenses of sale shall remain chargeable to the Forestry Department. Provided that if the request for recovery of the money is not submitted until after the sale of the seized livestock, their owner, if acquitted, shall only be entitled to recover the net proceeds of the sale after deduction of all expenses.

Seizure reports drawn up and signed by two sworn officers of the Forestry Department shall, until forgery thereof is alleged, constitute conclusive proof of the material facts relating to the misdemeanours and contraventions ascertained therein, whatever the penalties to which such misdemeanours and contraventions lead, and accordingly no proof other than or against them which contradicts the tenor of these reports shall be admitted unless there is a lawful cause for recusing one of their signatories. Where, however, the seizure reports are drawn up and signed by only one officer of the Forestry Department, they shall constitute proof until forgery thereof is alleged, save that this shall only be so where the misdemeanour or contravention does not lead to a penalty exceeding ten Lebanese-Syrian pounds in fines and damages combined. Where different and separate misdemeanours and contraventions against several persons are ascertained in a single report and at the same time, this report shall constitute proof in accordance with the text of this Article in each misdemeanour or contravention which does not lead to a penalty exceeding ten Lebanese-Syrian pounds in fines and damages combined, whatever the value which the total of the penalties adjudged may reach.

There are hereby repealed and shall remain repealed: - The Ottoman Regulation issued on 1 January of the year 1870 concerning the administration of the forests of the Ottoman Empire - The Ottoman Law issued in May of the year 1874 concerning the rate of the fee and the manner of collecting the fees relating to firewood and charcoal - The Ottoman Law issued on 1 April 1877 concerning the fees required to be collected on forest products - The Ottoman Law issued on 20 March 1880 concerning the organisation of the Forests Department The Ottoman Order issued on 29 October of the year 1903 concerning various penalties relating to forests - Decision No. 824 issued on 26 November 1919 by the Chief Administrator of Occupied Enemy Territory - Western Zone concerning the protection of forests and woodlands - Circular of the Administrative Council of Lesser Lebanon No. 447 issued on 27 April of the year 1920 establishing a preliminary general regime in forest affairs - Decision No. 89 issued on 1 November of the year 1920 by Lebanon concerning the protection of the Cedars of Lebanon - Decision No. 1004 issued on 8 December of the year 1921 by Lebanon fixing the amount of forest and mine fees with respect to forests only - The Circular issued on 7 April of the year 1922 concerning the organisation of forests in Lebanon - Decision of the Governor of the State of the Alawites No. 879 issued on 27 October of the year 1923 determining the fees collected on forest products taken from State property - Decision of the Governor of the State of the Alawites No. 960 issued on 5 May 1924 determining the regime applicable to woodlands and forests in the State of the Alawites - Decision of the State of Damascus No. 164 issued on 28 June 1924 - Decision of the Governor of the Alawites No. 995 issued on 5 July 1924 fixing the tariff of fees required to be levied on the exploitation of woodlands and forests of the State of the Alawites - Decision No. 2661 issued on 9 August 1924 concerning the afforestation of Greater Lebanon - Decision of the President of the Syrian Federation No. 187 issued on 15 June of the year 1925 - Decision of the State of Syria No. 685 issued on 29 December of the year 1926 - The Law of the Government of Syria issued on 5 May 1933 Furthermore, as from the date of application of this Decision, the effect of the provisions of the laws, Imperial administrations (Irades), regulations, decisions of the High Commissioner, local decisions and decrees, orders of the occupying authorities, and all circulars which followed them shall cease in the matters that are the subject of this Decision
The application of the provisions of this Decision as from the first of January 1936

The Secretary-General, the Adviser of the High Commission for Economic Affairs, and the Delegates and Assistant Delegates to the local States and Governments are charged, each insofar as it concerns him, with the execution of this Decision

Official reports which are not relied upon as authentic and do not constitute sufficient proof in accordance with the preceding provisions until an allegation of forgery is made against them shall be relied upon as authentic until proof is established to the contrary of what is contained therein.
Actions for forgery shall be instituted in accordance with the rules of procedure in force.

If an official report is drawn up against several accused persons and one or several of them allege the forgery of the report, the report itself shall remain relied upon as authentic as against the others unless the matter in which the forgery is alleged is indivisible and common among the accused.

Misdemeanours and contraventions committed in woods and forests not subject to the forestry regime shall be investigated and ascertained either by sworn officers of the Forestry Department, or by rural watchmen, or private watchmen, or members of the gendarmerie, and in general by all officers of the judicial police. Official reports drawn up by private watchmen shall be relied upon as authentic until proof is established to the contrary of their contents; whereas reports drawn up by officers of the judicial police, members of the gendarmerie, rural watchmen, and village watchmen shall be relied upon as authentic in accordance with the provisions of the laws applicable thereto.

Official reports of misdemeanours drawn up by officers who are not from the Forestry Administration must be sent during the ten days following their drawing up to the officers charged with taking the necessary action in respect thereof.

Forestry officers may, in actions and prosecutions conducted in the name of the Forestry Administration, request every summons before the courts and every service of process, provided that they may not carry out executive attachments. Under pain of nullity, the writ of summons must include a copy of the official report.

The Forestry Administration may, through its representative, appeal against judgments and lodge appeals in cassation against decisions and judgments up to the last instance, but it may not waive its appeal without special authorisation from the Head of State. The right granted to the Forestry Administration to have recourse to the review of judgments and decisions by appealing against them and lodging appeals in cassation against them is independent of this same right which the law confers upon the Public Prosecution, for the said Public Prosecution may always exercise it even if the Administration has accepted the judgments and decisions rendered.

The Forestry Administration is authorised to compound before the rendering of judgment in the misdemeanours and contraventions provided for and punished by this Decision. After the rendering of judgment, compounding may not take place except in respect of pecuniary penalties and civil reparations.

Actions for reparation in misdemeanours and contraventions relating to forests shall lapse by the expiration of six months from the date of the closing of the official report ascertaining them, and after three Gregorian years from the date of the misdemeanour if no official report has been drawn up in respect thereof; all this shall not prevent the application of the special provisions specified in the articles of Section Four of Chapter Three of Title Two of this Decision against lessees by auction and contractors in relation to the obligations imposed upon concessionaires of forestry exploitations. Actions arising from the clearing of woods and thickets contrary to the provisions of Article 76 relating to the clearing of private lands shall lapse by the expiration of two Gregorian years from the date of the carrying out of the clearing.

If the accused in an action for reparation relating to a contravention provided for in this Decision or in the implementing texts issued subsequently raises a right of ownership or another real right, the court before which the complaint is brought shall rule upon the incidental application by following the rules hereinafter: The incidental application shall not be admitted unless it is founded upon a title of ownership or upon an official document equivalent to a title of ownership, and the title or document produced is of such a nature as to remove from the act which is the basis of the prosecution all criminal character. In the event of the adjournment of the action for civil matters, a time limit not exceeding two months shall be fixed in the judgment, during which the party who submitted the incidental application must bring the dispute before the competent judges and prove his diligence in the action; failing which, judgment shall be proceeded with in the contravention. Provided that, in the event of a judgment imposing a penalty, the execution of the judgment of imprisonment must be stayed if imprisonment is adjudged; whereas the amount of the pecuniary penalty and the civil reparations must be deposited in order to be delivered to whomsoever the court which rules upon the merits of the action orders it to be delivered.

The father, the mother, and the guardians are civilly liable for the contraventions committed by their minor children and wards residing with them, and likewise employers and principals are civilly liable for the misdemeanours committed by every person in their service during the work in which they employ them. This liability includes the restitution of the things taken, reparation, and costs.

If several persons are prosecuted in respect of a single misdemeanour and it is proved that they all participated therein, it must be declared that they are jointly and severally liable for the payment of the fines imposed upon them.
The ordinary penal laws must be applied in all cases which are not specially specified in this Decision.

Judgments rendered upon the request of the Forestry Administration or upon the prosecution of the Public Prosecution shall be served by means of a simple extract thereof containing the name and place of residence of the litigants and the substance of the judgment. This service shall be made upon the person himself or at his place of residence. If the place of residence is abroad, the service shall be valid by the mere affixing thereof for a period of fifteen days upon the door of the registry of the court. From the date of this service, the time limits for opposition and appeal shall commence.

The collection of fines relating to forests, costs, and damages arising from judgments rendered in misdemeanours and contraventions shall take place in accordance with the rules applicable to the collection of State funds, provided that contraventors may be permitted to pay the funds due from them in kind or in labour according to a tariff fixed by the Forestry Administration.

Judgments rendered imposing penalties in favour of individuals in reparation for misdemeanours or contraventions committed in their woods shall be served and executed at their diligence in accordance with the same form and means of compulsion as take place in judgments rendered upon the request of the Forestry Administration. The Department of Finance shall secure the collection of the fines within the same conditions.

All the provisions of this Decision relating to the ascertainment of misdemeanours and contraventions, the prosecution thereof, and the reparation therefor committed in the woods and forests of the State shall apply to woods and forests not subject to the forestry regime.

In the application of this Decision, the word Head of State must be understood as a governmental or administrative authority in each of the States, Governments, or Provinces possessing an independent budget.
The details relating to the application of this Decision shall be regulated in local decrees and decisions.
Every person who wishes to recruit foreign female domestic workers to work in private households shall obtain a licence from the Ministry of Labour.

In order to obtain this licence, the following conditions must be met:

- An application to obtain a licence for the recruitment of foreign female domestic workers in accordance with a special form at the Employment Department

- Labour Force Directorate, to which the following documents shall be attached:

- A certificate of deposit from the Housing Bank in the amount of 20.000.000 twenty million Lebanese pounds.

- A registered undertaking certified by a notary public relating to the application of the laws and regulations of the Ministry of Labour and the assumption of liability arising from any violation.

- A copy of the commercial register of the establishment whose object does not conflict with the work of the agency, and which does not contain the phrase of engaging in employment and providing employees.

- A copy of the title deed or lease agreement of the establishment certified by the competent authorities.

- A judicial record for the owner of the establishment and for all partners in the company dating back no more than one month.

- A copy of the identity card of the owner of the establishment and of any partner in the company.
The applicant shall be Lebanese, enjoying full civil rights, and not convicted of a felony or a dishonourable misdemeanour or one contrary to public morals and ethics.

Applications shall be submitted to the Employment Department, Labour Force Directorate, and the time limit for their submission and the procedures for deciding thereon shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister.

No individual, company or establishment shall be entitled to obtain more than one licence or to be a partner in another company engaged in the recruitment of female domestic workers, and this measure shall include family members (husband - wife - children) who live in one household.
Neither the owner of the establishment nor the partners, jointly and severally, shall be entitled to assign, sell or lease the licence of the agency.

Agencies are prohibited from changing their place of business prior to the approval of the Ministry of Labour, and for this purpose they must submit an application to change the place to the Employment Department. Labour Force Directorate.

Each recruitment agency shall be entitled to appoint one representative to represent it before the Ministry, provided that such representative is Lebanese, not convicted of a dishonourable offence, and authorised by the person in charge of the agency pursuant to an official power of attorney registered with a notary public, provided that such authorisation does not include the right to sign on behalf of the owner of the agency or one of the partners duly authorised to sign.

Neither the owner of the agency, nor one of the partners, nor the representative thereof shall be entitled to act as representatives for another agency.
The Ministry of Labour shall provide the representatives of the agencies with a card issued by the Ministry, and the representative shall carry this card visibly while present in the Ministry.

The owner of the agency and the partners in the company shall bear full responsibility for the applications submitted by the agency and for the accuracy of the information contained therein. None of them may sign on behalf of the sponsor on the prior approval application.

Agencies are prohibited from recruiting female domestic workers under the names of fictitious sponsors for the purpose of employing them for a daily or monthly wage in multiple places, or employing them in establishments or companies.

The person in charge of the agency shall bear the expenses of repatriating the foreign woman to her country and securing a replacement for her without charging the employer any additional expenses in the following cases:

If she absconds or it is found that she is pregnant or suffering from a mental illness, a contagious or infectious disease, or a disability that prevents her from working normally, within a period not exceeding three months from the date of entry into Lebanon.

The sponsor, the master of the household, undertakes to provide clothing, food, medicine and an acceptable place for the sleeping and rest of the female domestic worker, to pay the monthly remuneration at the end of each month, and to provide the necessary assistance to transfer her wages abroad upon request, and further undertakes to grant her sufficient periods of rest, and not to ill-treat her or subject her to beating, under penalty of judicial prosecution.

The recruitment agency shall establish a schedule for periodic contact with the sponsors and the female domestic workers working for them, for the purpose of ensuring the proper performance by the female domestic worker of her work on the one hand, and that she is not ill-treated and receives all her rights on the other hand, and it shall notify the Ministry, Labour Force Directorate, of the cases that warrant the filing of a complaint against the female domestic worker or the sponsor.

Persons in charge of, or employees of, recruitment agencies are prohibited from subjecting female domestic workers to beating, and in the event of disputes arising between them and the employers and the female domestic worker, or between the latter two, they shall notify the Ministry of Labour of the matter and file a complaint if necessary.

Each agency shall keep a special register, the pages of which shall be numbered and stamped with the seal of the Labour Force Directorate, in which shall be recorded:

- The name of the foreign woman and her nationality,

- And the name of the employer and his full address,

- And the number and date of the prior approval application and the date of entry into Lebanon,

- And the number of the work permit.

In the event that the female domestic worker does not obtain a work permit within two months from the date of her entry into Lebanon, the person in charge of the agency must contact the sponsor and notify him of the obligation to obtain a work permit, and if the latter abstains from doing so, he must notify the Ministry of Labour, Labour Force Directorate, of the matter upon the expiry of the three-month period specified for obtaining the work permit.
Owners of agencies are prohibited from advertising prices by any means whatsoever, whether directly or indirectly.

The Labour Inspection Department in Beirut and the regional departments in the governorates shall undertake the supervision of the operations of the recruitment agencies, and shall submit a detailed report on the status of each agency once every six months.

A special file for each recruitment agency shall be kept at the registry of the Labour Force Directorate, in which the applications submitted by each agency during a period of one year shall be registered, and the serial number of the file shall be recorded on each applicant.

The Employment Department in the Labour Force Directorate shall be charged with keeping a special file for each agency, containing all the basic documents and information relating to the agency, and the decisions and complaints referred to the Department for preservation shall be attached to the file.

Complaints and representations relating to disputes between employers and female domestic workers, or between either of these two parties and the agencies, shall be submitted to the Employment Department in Beirut and to the regional departments in the governorates, and shall be referred successively to the competent authorities in the Ministry accompanied by the appropriate proposals for taking the necessary decision thereon.
This Decision shall be published and notified where needed, and any text contrary to its content shall be repealed.

The draft law set forth in Decree No. 8343 dated 02/05/1996 aiming at the establishment of the Public Corporation for Housing, as amended by the Joint Parliamentary Committees, has been approved.

This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

A public institution named the "Public Corporation for Housing" is hereby established

It shall enjoy legal personality and financial and administrative autonomy and shall be attached to the Ministry of Housing and Cooperatives, which shall exercise tutorial authority over it.

The headquarters of the Corporation shall be in Beirut, and it shall have the right to establish branches in all Lebanese regions.

The terms and designations set forth below, wherever they occur in this Law, shall be understood as indicated opposite each of them:

The Ministry: The Ministry of Housing and Cooperatives.

The Minister: The Minister of Housing and Cooperatives.

The Corporation: The Public Corporation for Housing.

The Board: The Board of Directors of the Public Corporation for Housing.

The Chairman: The Chairman of the Board of Directors - Director General of the Public Corporation for Housing.

The Beneficiary Entities: The Corporation, entities, associations, and companies

set forth in the new Article Four of the Housing Law No. 58 dated 08/12/1965 and its amendments.

The Beneficiaries: The categories set forth in the new Articles One and Three of the Housing Law No. 58 dated 08/12/1965 and its amendments.

The Corporation shall be subject to the provisions of this Law and to the provisions of the Housing Law that do not conflict with its provisions. The Corporation shall have special administrative and financial regulations drawn up by the Board and approved by decrees passed by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister.

The cadres of the Corporation, the categories of its employees, and their ranks, salaries, and allowances shall be determined pursuant to a decree passed by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister

The Board shall be composed of a full-time Chairman and four part-time members appointed by a decree passed by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister.

The term of office of the Board shall be four years, renewable or extendable.

Each of the Chairman and the members must fulfil the conditions provided for in the General Regulations for Public Institutions, provided that he holds a recognised university degree in law, engineering, business administration, or economics, to the exclusion of others, and that he has practical experience in his field of specialisation.

The Chairman shall be the Director General of the Corporation, and his emoluments and allowances, as well as the allowances of the members, shall be determined by a decree passed by the Council

of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister.

The Director General of Housing shall be the Government Commissioner at the Corporation

and the Minister of Finance shall delegate a Financial Controller to the Corporation.

The allowances of the Government Commissioner shall be determined by a decision of the Minister, and the allowances of the Financial Controller shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Finance, provided that the allowance of either of them does not exceed the allowance determined for a member of the Board. The allowances of each of them shall be paid from the budget of his ministry, and in all cases neither of them shall have the right to receive any allowance or remuneration of any kind whatsoever from the budget of the Corporation.

The powers of the Board, the Chairman - Director General, and the Government Commissioner shall be determined by decrees passed by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister, and the powers of the Financial Controller upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

The Corporation shall conduct housing studies and surveys for all Lebanese regions.

The Directorate General of Urban Planning shall provide the Corporation with a copy of every alignment, expropriation, or easement decree accompanied by the maps annexed thereto immediately upon its publication, as well as with the necessary statistics on building permits granted in the various regions every six months.

The Corporation shall cooperate with the competent administrations regarding housing studies, surveys, and statistics, and it may contract with specialised offices and experts to conduct them, and it may also contract for this purpose with foreign, national, regional, or international bodies, institutions, and funds in accordance with the provisions of the laws in force.

The Corporation shall undertake to facilitate the housing of the Beneficiaries by the following means:

A- Constructing dwellings and their appurtenances directly or through third parties in accordance with programmes, provided that every programme in which the number of residential units exceeds one hundred dwellings shall be subject to the approval of the Council of Ministers.

B- Encouraging saving and credit for housing in accordance with a regulation drawn up by the Board and approved by a decree passed by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister.

C- Granting medium-term and long-term loans to:

1- The Beneficiary Entities to construct dwellings and transfer their ownership to the Beneficiaries who fulfil the required conditions, with the exception of commercial companies.

2- The Beneficiaries to construct dwellings on real properties they own, or to purchase built dwellings or dwellings under construction, or to expand or restore their dwellings.

3- The Beneficiary Entities to construct dwellings in order to lease them to their workers.

(Paragraph D added pursuant to Law 767 dated 11/11/2006 Official Gazette 54

D- Granting medium-term and long-term loans directly or in participation with other financing sources to natural and legal persons and the Beneficiary Entities to construct dwellings with the aim of leasing them to the Beneficiaries by way of lease-to-own.

Lease-to-own means a lease contract that gives the lessee the right to acquire ownership of the leased property in return for a price agreed upon when concluding the lease contract, with the instalments paid by him as rent being calculated towards the principal of the price.

Within three months from the date of entry into force of this Law, the Corporation must draw up a special regulation for lease-to-own to be approved by a decree passed by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister. The said regulation shall determine the conditions and procedures of lease-to-own, including the provisions that the contract must contain, the rights and obligations of each of the owner and the lessee, and the manner of exercising the option to purchase and its effects.

The term of the lease-to-own shall be 30 years as a maximum, and the lessee may not exercise his right to purchase the leased property before the lapse of at least five years of the lease contract.
The Corporation may, with the aim of feeding its resources, sell commercial units and lease constructions and non-residential units in housing projects.

The sale price of the dwelling or the loan in principal, interest, and rent shall be deemed a privileged debt in favour of the Corporation, and it shall also enjoy a general privilege over all the movable and immovable property of the Beneficiary.

The privileged debt shall be registered ipso jure without need for any other formality at the request of the Corporation:

A- On the real folio of the real property if the real property is demarcated or registered.

B- On the record of demarcation and registration if the real property is still under demarcation and registration operations or if the records are still under consideration before the Real Estate Judge.

C- In the special register kept at the Real Estate Registry Offices

pursuant to the provisions of Legislative Decree No. 12 dated 28/02/1930 (concerning the organisation of the Tabu and registration) if the real property is not demarcated and registered.

Notwithstanding any other text:

1- The Land Registry departments shall, at the request of the party concerned, subdivide the building under completion into distinct rights provided that the skeleton of the building (columns and ceilings) has been executed pursuant to a duly issued building permit, and the party concerned must finally complete the constructions and attach a habitation permit for the section pertaining to him within a time limit of three years from the date of the subdivision and he may not carry out any transaction on this section after the lapse of the three years if he does not produce the said

habitation permit.

2- An annotation of a precautionary registration may be placed on the real folio of a property pursuant to ongoing agreements for the purchase of a section not finally subdivided of this property. This annotation shall remain in force for a period of two years from the date of its registration on the real folio and shall lapse ipso jure after the expiry of the period of two years.

3- There shall be deducted from the value of the fiscal stamp duty payable on real estate contracts required to be executed pursuant to the provisions of Legislative Decree No. 67/67 the value of the fiscal stamp duty levied upon the drawing up of agreements and deeds, if the real estate contracts required to be registered came in execution of the content of these agreements and deeds provided that these documents are attached to the contract required to be executed.

Related text: Application of the provisions of paragraph 3 of Article 26 of Law 539 dated 24/7/1996 (Establishment of the Public Corporation for Housing)

The Government is authorised to contract internal or external loans to finance the first phase of the housing projects which the Corporation is entrusted to execute provided that their value does not exceed five hundred billion Lebanese pounds.

1- The Special Fund for Housing established pursuant to the new Article 16 of Law No. 58/65 dated 08/12/1965 (the Housing Law) is abolished and the Corporation shall replace the Fund in all its rights and obligations.

Legislative Decree No. 17/83 dated 16/09/1983 and its amendments relating to the granting of loans for the restoration and reconstruction of buildings intended for habitation that were damaged due to the events is also abolished, and those who benefited from the provisions of this Legislative Decree until the issuance of this Law are exempted from repayment.

The amounts allocated for this purpose in the budget of the year 1996 shall be transferred to the Corporation in accordance with the following appropriation:

Title 21 Part Two A Chapter - 1 Item - 20 Paragraph 2 Economic expenditures and assistance - contribution to the Public Corporation for Housing.

2- The account opened in the name of the Special Fund for Housing in the Directorate of the Treasury and Public Debt at the Ministry of Finance shall be closed and its balances shall be transferred to the Corporation.

3- The Corporation shall continue to accept the applications of owners relating to the increase of the exploitation factor in accordance with the time limits specified in Law No. 370 dated 26/07/1994

Subject to the provisions of the preceding Article, the Autonomous Fund for Housing shall continue to perform its functions pursuant to Law No. 6/80 dated 17/05/1980 and the regulations issued in application thereof, and that on a temporary basis. Until the establishment of the organs of the Corporation and the appointment or attachment of employees thereto and the Minister shall determine the date of commencement of the work of each of them.

The settlement of the status of the employees in the said Fund without modification to their functional status, particularly with respect to category, grade, salary and their right to advancement and the inclusion of their previous services, shall be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister and after the approval of the Civil Service Board, and the settlement shall also include the status of the employees placed outside the schedule of their original cadres for the purpose of attaching them to the Fund.
The details of the application of the provisions of this Law shall be determined, where necessary, by decrees taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The revenues of the Institution shall consist of:

A- Whatever is allocated to it in the General Budget or in the development and reconstruction programmes.

B- The revenues, contributions, allocations, returns, proceeds, fees, taxes, surcharges, interest and fines prescribed for housing or for the Institution pursuant to this Law, the housing laws and regulations, or other laws and regulations.

C- The resources of its investments and the returns from the recovery of the loans that it grants.

D- Loans pursuant to the laws in force.

E- Gifts, donations and bequests following the approval thereof by the Council of Ministers.

F- An additional fee in the amount of two per cent of the value of the fee levied by the municipality on building permits, provided that this fee is paid

pursuant to receipts independent of other building permit fees at

one of the Public Treasury funds.

G- An annual additional fee in the amount of two thousand Lebanese pounds added to the fee due on every horsepower for all private

cars.

H- Any other resources, fees and taxes provided for by special texts.

I- Fees on fuels and their derivatives determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.

The administrations and institutions concerned shall transfer, every six months, whatever has been collected of the revenues, taxes and fees mentioned in this Article to the account of the Institution.

The Institution shall be exempted from the following taxes and fees:

A- Income tax on its revenues, including the profits that it may realise from the sale of real properties and the interest that it charges on the sale price of dwellings, on the loans that it provides to beneficiaries, and on its deposits with banks, and from the tax on interest.

B- All taxes and fees on the bonds, prizes and bonuses that it issues or approves, as well as the instruments signed to its order and the contracts that it concludes.

C- The transfer, mortgage, succession and subdivision fee on the real properties that it purchases or that devolve upon it, and from the mortgage and mortgage discharge tax and the tax on the interest thereof.

D- Stamp duties on all contracts and transactions executed in fulfilment of its purposes.

E- Fees for lawsuits, attachment, execution, sale by public auction, and the transactions and documents completing these operations, including stamp duties.

The benefiting bodies shall enjoy the exemptions set out in the Seventh Article, solely in respect of the revenues, profits, interest, bonds, contracts, transactions and mortgages that they carry out or execute in order to achieve the housing purposes provided for in the new Second Article of the Housing Law.

Savings accounts and their funds allocated to housing credit and the financial bonuses granted to savers shall be exempted from interest tax and stamp

duties.

The value of gifts, donations and bequests made to the Institution shall be deducted from the amounts taken as a basis for determining the income tax due from the donor, contributor or testator.

It shall also be deducted from the amounts taken as a basis for determining the succession duties due on the estate of the testator, and these gifts, donations and bequests shall be exempted from all fees and taxes of whatever kind.

The beneficiary of the provisions of this Law shall be exempted from:

A- The transfer, mortgage and mortgage discharge fees relating to the dwelling from which he benefits.

B- The stamp duty due on the contracts, documents and transactions executed on the occasion of benefiting from the dwelling.

Notwithstanding any other text, the owner of a residential unit who sells it to its tenant shall be exempted from whatever pertains to this unit of:

A- Fees for the rectification of real estate register entries, subdivision and the creation of various rights.

B- The indicated property tax and the sewerage fee for the year in which the sale takes place.

C- The stamp duty on all transactions and contracts that he carries out for this purpose.

These exemptions shall apply once only, provided that:

A- The lease contract is duly registered prior to the date of promulgation of this Law.

B- The area of the residential unit does not exceed two hundred and fifty square metres.

The tenant of the residential unit shall be given priority in obtaining a loan from the Institution to purchase it.

In the event that he obtains a loan to purchase a residential unit other than the unit leased by him, he must produce a deed of waiver of his tenancy in the unit that he occupies by way of lease.

The provisions of this Article shall also apply to whoever benefits at any time from the right of statutory extension of the lease instrument of the residential unit.

Whoever attempts to benefit from the exemptions mentioned in this Law without right, by dissimulation, or by using untrue documents shall be punished for the offence of fraud provided for in the Penal Code, together with the facilitators and accomplices, and shall be fined five times the exemptions he obtained.

The Institution shall be subject to the oversight of the Central Inspection and to the ex post oversight of the Court of Accounts. It shall also be subject to the oversight of the Civil Service Board in accordance with special regulations issued by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Prime Minister and the Minister.

The Minister may request the President of the Central Inspection Board to investigate the Chairman and members of the Board.

The decisions taken by the Board in the following matters and projects shall be subject to the approval of the Minister:

A- Every residential construction programme in which the number of residential units exceeds fifty dwellings.

B- Contracts for supplies, works and services when their value exceeds a certain limit in accordance with the provisions of the Financial Regulations.

C- The book of general conditions for contracts.

D- The staff regulations and the wage-earners regulations

There shall be subject to the approval of the Minister and the Minister of Finance:

A- The annual budget.

B- The final rendering of accounts, the annual general balance sheet, the profit and loss account, the general trial balance of accounts and the annual comprehensive inventory of materials.

C- The use of the reserve and the general reserve.

D- Applications for Treasury advances.

E- Interest rates on loans.

The competent Minister must decide upon the decisions subject to his approval within a period of one month from the date on which they are lodged with the Government Commissioner or the Financial Controller. The period shall be reduced to fifteen days in respect of the approval of contracts. The competent Minister may request a reconsideration of the decision submitted for his approval or request certain documents or clarifications, in which case the period shall be renewed once only for a duration not exceeding ten days for contracts and fifteen days for other decisions from the date on which such documents or clarifications are received by him.
