7- The proportion of the rights of the private lot in each of the common parts Nos. 1, 2 and 3 and its obligations towards each of them, as the case may be, expressed as a number out of one thousand; and each owner of the private lots shall have a number of votes equal to his shares in the common parts, each taken separately, and in the case of co-ownership of a private lot the right to vote shall belong to the holder of the majority of shares in that lot, and if the shares are equal, then to the eldest of them. If the holder of the majority in the lot fails to attend despite having been summoned, the lot may validly be represented by the person who follows him in ownership of the number of shares.

8- Remarks, if any.

B - A plan of the building sought to be registered, showing the location, shape and components of each lot.

C- The provisions relating to the management of the property, provided that there shall be specified in these provisions, without limitation, the following matters:

1- The constitution of the association of owners and the election of a president thereof.

2- Summonses and notifications.

3- The holding of meetings.

4- The drawing up of minutes.

5- Elections of every kind.

6- The adoption and execution of resolutions.

7- Where applicable, the appointment of managers and the board of the management office, and the determination of powers, allowances and wages, the manner of performing the work, and the manner of dismissal, as set forth in Chapter Five of this Legislative Decree.

8- The establishment of administrative councils and the determination of their powers and the manner of their dismissal.

9- The management, maintenance and preservation of the building. Under this last item shall be specified:

- The rights of the owners in their private lots and the common parts, and the manner and extent of the exercise of these rights.

- The internal alterations which each owner may carry out in the lot belonging to him, and the statement of the conditions for carrying out such alterations.

- The conditions for insuring the property against risks, and in particular the risk of fire.

- The works and additions which the association is entitled to carry out on the common parts, and which increase the value of the property in whole or in part, at the expense of all the co-owners, on the basis of such conditions as the association may impose upon them or upon some of them, or for the benefit of some of them over the others.

- The votes pertaining to each of the bare owner and the usufructuary, where both exist. Where the by-laws do not provide for this matter, the provisions of Article 36, item 2, of Legislative Decree No. 146 dated 13/6/1959 shall apply.

- The rules for collecting advances and recovering debts, and for disbursement and receipt.

- The rules for employing salaried staff, employees and workmen and dismissing them from service.

- The manner of settling disputes that may arise between the owners.

- The representation of the association before the courts and public departments and vis-à-vis third parties.

- The rules for amending the by-laws, provided that the amendments shall be authenticated before a Notary Public, attached to the principal by-laws kept in the file of the property, and noted on the first page of the by-laws, on pain of nullity even as between the interested parties.

And everything conducive to the proper management of the property and the optimal enjoyment thereof, within the rules in force. These documents shall be kept in the file of the property and a copy thereof shall be attached to every title deed or certificate of registration of ownership.

The by-laws may not contain any provision that conflicts with the provisions of mandatory laws and regulations, and in particular the provisions of building laws and regulations, and if included, it shall be deemed ineffective even as between the parties.

Where the building has exhausted the general exploitation factor, the applicant for registration may not reserve for himself or for another a private right over the components of the common parts, and in particular the roofs, garages, concierges' rooms and the spaces located between the columns.

Where the building has not exhausted the general exploitation factor, the owner applying for registration is entitled to reserve for his own account what remains of the said exploitation factor, and in that case, the by-laws shall contain a clarification of this right and of the rights in the common parts represented thereby and the obligations arising therefrom, where applicable, in accordance with what is set forth in paragraph A, item 7 of Article 12.

Likewise, the by-laws shall contain the manner of exercising this right and assigning it, and the procedure that must or may be followed in applying for the registration of new constructions and modifying the proportion of rights and obligations and all other matters relating to the common ownership, and this right shall be noted in the real folio of the property and in the supplementary folios pertaining to the lots of which it consists.

Where the owner of the property is a single person at the date of registration, or is deemed to be a single person, he shall be deemed to be the president of the association until the association is established and a president is elected for it. A husband, wife and minor children shall be deemed to be a single person.

The applicant for registration may, if he has not yet completed his project, reserve for himself the presidency of the association by a mere declaration on his part, and he shall remain so until the completion of the project, provided that the period does not exceed five years.

The owners of the property shall, as soon as the number of private lots exceeds three, form by operation of law an association called the general association of owners, which shall undertake the management of the property and the performance of the acts of disposition thereof vested in it in accordance with the provisions specified in this Legislative Decree and in the by-laws for the management of the property.

In the event of a plurality of buildings, a special association may be established for each of them or for each group of them constituting a unit according to the management by-laws, the mission of which shall in principle be the management of what pertains to it, within the conditions specified by those by-laws.

Each of the general association of owners and the special associations of owners shall enjoy legal personality within the scope of its powers, and in the event of a conflict of jurisdiction between them or a contradiction of their resolutions, the Court of First Instance within whose jurisdiction the property is situated shall decide by a final decision taken in council chamber after hearing the representatives of each of them.
The word "association", wherever it appears in this Legislative Decree, means the general association or the special association, according to the context in which it appears.

Subject to what is set forth in Article 17, the general association shall, immediately upon its establishment, elect a president for itself by secret ballot, upon a summons by the person holding the largest number of votes in common part No. 1.

Where the volume of business of the association so requires, an office may be established for it, presided over by the president, the number of whose members, the distribution of work among them, their wages where applicable, and everything relating to them shall be determined in a resolution adopted by the association. As for the summons to elect a president for the special association, it shall be issued by the president of the general association of owners.

The president of the association shall undertake the execution of its resolutions and the taking of all measures and proceedings which the association empowers him to take and execute. In all cases, he shall be responsible for conducting ordinary daily affairs and performing all urgent proceedings and acts required for the safety of the property, and the safety of third parties, against damage that may befall them on account thereof.

The association shall hold a general meeting at least once every year, at the beginning of which the president of the association shall read out a report on the state of the association for deliberation thereon.

Meetings shall be held pursuant to a written summons addressed by the president of the association to each owner or pursuant to a petition signed by the holders of at least one quarter of the votes.

Every owner shall notify his acquisition of ownership to the President of the Association and shall elect domicile within the jurisdiction of the Single Judge Court under which the property falls, failing which he shall be deemed by operation of law to be domiciled in the unit which he owns or in which he owns a share.

If he owns a share in more than one unit, notification shall be served upon him in the unit in which he resides. If he does not reside in the property, notification shall be served upon him in any of the units in which he owns a share.

Notices of meeting shall be served by registered mail if the person to be served has elected domicile within the jurisdiction of the court under which the property falls, failing which by posting at the entrance of the unit, and the occurrence of service by posting shall be recorded in minutes signed by the President of the Association together with two of the owners.

Service may also be effected upon him at his actual place of residence, either in person or through the persons specified in Article 353 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
Service must be effected at least ten days prior to the date fixed for holding the meeting and must include the date of the meeting, the place and the subject-matter.

The meeting may not be held outside the jurisdiction of the court under which the property falls, except for compelling reasons, and with the prior approval of a majority of at least 75% of the votes.

Unless there is a special provision specifying a certain majority for taking a given resolution, the meeting shall not be deemed valid except in the presence of at least an absolute majority of the votes of the owners at the first session, and shall be valid with whoever is present at the subsequent session.

The President of the Association shall preside over the sessions, record the facts and proceedings, and enter the resolutions in minutes drawn up in accordance with due form.

The minutes and the resolutions shall each be numbered consecutively and kept in the files of the Association, after being signed by the owners present, and if one of them refuses to sign, mention thereof shall be made opposite his name.
Only the subjects specified for the session may be discussed therein, unless the Presidency of the Association approves the discussion of subjects raised directly.
The Association shall take its resolutions by majority in accordance with what is provided for, and voting on the subject under consideration shall take place by a show of hands to declare approval.

Acts of disposition, in principle, cannot be the subject of a resolution by the General Association of Owners except by a unanimous vote of the owners, save in the following two cases:

1- The addition of a building or the installation of necessary or useful equipment or machinery.

2- The sale of the property, if the sole building on the property has collapsed or been damaged such that it has become unfit for use, and likewise if the buildings, where there are several, have collapsed or been damaged such that they have become unfit for use, and there is no compensation therefor covering at least sixty per cent of the expenses of reconstructing a similar building, in the event of lack of unanimity among the owners to reconstruct. In these two cases, resolutions may be taken by a majority of not less than 75% of the votes of all the owners in the property.

Where there is a special association, the approval of at least 75% of the votes therein shall also be required for the acts under item 1 of this Article.

The building added pursuant to item 1 of this Article may be registered, according to that for which it is intended, either within the contents of the common part or as a private unit the ownership of which belongs to the Association, and if it is registered as a private unit of the Association, the latter shall have no votes by reason thereof.
Resolutions in matters of an administrative nature shall be taken by an absolute majority of the votes of the owners in the first round, and by a majority of those present in the second round.

The following in particular, without limitation, shall be deemed matters of an administrative nature:

1- The maintenance, repair and replacement of:

- All existing equipment which provides a common service, such as motors, lifts and heating and cooling apparatus, together with the provision of supplies and materials for their operation.

- Common installations of all kinds, such as water, telephone, electricity and other installations.

- Water and fuel tanks together with ensuring the delivery of water or fuel to each of them, where they are common.

- Common sewers intended for the drainage of foul water, bathroom water, and water from gutters and roofs.

- Ventilation ducts and their appliances, light wells and chimneys.

- Sports, recreational and cultural facilities and all necessary tools, supplies and materials rendering them fit for use, where they are intended for common use.

2- The exploitation of certain common parts under contracts the term of which does not exceed one year.

3- The repair of all contingent damage occurring to the common parts or to certain of their elements. In general, everything that does not diminish the rights of the owners in the ownership of the common parts or in their use.

If the building collapses and there is compensation covering at least 60% of the expenses of reconstructing a building similar thereto, the Association may resolve to reconstruct by a majority of at least 75% of the votes of the owners, and the compensation shall be allocated to this purpose.

If one of the owners refuses to comply with the resolution of the Association, he shall be bound to sell his rights to the remaining owners or to some of them, should they agree to purchase, at the price determined by the Court of First Instance in council chamber upon a petition by the President of the Association and after hearing both parties.

Where there are several buildings, and one or some of them suffer total destruction, and the owners of such building abstain from reconstructing it within a period of three years from the date the destruction occurred, and if the majority of those owners as set out in Article 33 agree to sell their rights to the remaining owners in the same property, those owners who formed the majority shall be bound to sell and the remaining owners in the property shall be bound to purchase at the price determined by the Court of First Instance in council chamber after hearing the President of the General Association and the President of the Special Association, if any, failing which the Court shall appoint a special representative for the body of owners of the destroyed building.

Owners who are unable to attend the meetings may appoint proxies to represent them, by virtue of official powers of attorney or before the Mukhtar, authorising them to act in the name of the principal owner.
An owner may not participate in the vote when a resolution is taken by the Association to contract with him.

If one of the owners requests a secret ballot, such ballot shall become mandatory in all matters of a personal nature, such as the dismissal of members of the management or the imputation of liability to them.

If the share of votes belonging to one of the owners exceeds half of the number of votes, and he exercises his right to vote, each of his co-owners may challenge the resolution of the Association within fifteen days from its issuance before the Court of First Instance under which the property falls, as against him and as against the President of the Association, in order to annul it on the ground that it pursued the interest of the said owner at the expense of the interest of his co-owners and was thus contrary to the principles of justice and equity, and the decision of the Court shall be final. The said owner may avoid such a challenge if he declares prior to the vote and the taking of the resolution that he is exercising his right to vote to an extent not exceeding half of the votes of the owners.

In the event of impediments of any kind whatsoever preventing the President of the Association from performing his duties, or in the event of his failure for any reason whatsoever to carry out such duties, any interested party may submit a petition to the President of the Court of First Instance under which the property falls, setting forth the situation and requesting the appointment of a provisional president from among the owners to perform the functions, and the latter shall call a meeting within a period of at most one month to examine the matter and elect a president where necessary.

The Board of Directors shall have broad powers to execute the resolutions of the Association of Owners and to carry out all acts required for the management of the real property in the customary manner and which are not considered part of day-to-day business. These powers shall have no limit or reservations other than what is provided for in the law or in the by-laws. The Chairman of the Board of Directors, and where necessary the Manager or the Managing Director, represents the Association before third parties, executes the resolutions of the Board of Directors, and conducts the day-to-day business as set forth in the by-laws under the supervision and control of the Board of Directors. The Board of Directors may delegate some of its powers to the Chairman or to the Manager for a short and limited period.

The Association shall be bound by what its representatives carry out within the scope of their powers; as for what exceeds this scope, it shall only be bound by the acts that it authorises or ratifies thereafter.

Every agreement concluded between the Board of Directors and one of the members of the Board of Directors shall be subject to the prior authorisation of the Association, whether such agreement is made directly or indirectly, or under the guise of a third party.

Every agreement between the Board of Directors and another enterprise shall likewise be subject to the prior authorisation of the Association if one of the members of the Board of Directors is an owner of such enterprise, a general partner therein, a manager thereof, or a member of its board of directors. The authorisation must be renewed every year if it pertains to contracts of successive, long-term obligations.

The Board of Directors must prepare at the end of the first six months of the financial year a brief statement of the financial position and draw up at the end of the year an inventory and a balance sheet together with the account of expenses and losses or surplus, if any.

The balance sheet must be clear and coordinated, and every change that occurs from one year to another in the manner of its preparation or presentation must be accompanied by explanations in a special report.

It is the Board of Directors that convenes the owners to hold the Assemblies in accordance with the provisions set forth in this Legislative Decree, and they shall also be convened pursuant to a petition signed by the holders of at least one quarter of the votes.

The members of the Board of Directors are liable even towards third parties for their managerial fault, for all acts of fraud, and for every violation of the law or the by-laws. As for the action that the injured party is entitled to bring as an individual action, it may not, even with regard to the owners, be stayed by a proposal from the Association discharging the members of the Board of Directors.

Liability shall be either individual, pertaining to a single member of the Board of Directors, or joint among them all, in which case they shall all be jointly and severally bound to pay compensation, unless a group of them had objected to the resolution taken despite them and their objection was recorded in the minutes. The final apportionment of liability among those responsible shall be according to the share of each of them in the fault committed.
The provisions contained in this Chapter shall not preclude the application of the provisions of the Code of Commerce that are not inconsistent therewith.

Subject to acquired rights prior to the entry into force of this Legislative Decree, the laws relating to pre-emption or the right of preference or any other similar right shall not apply to real properties subject to its provisions; however, every co-owner in a privatelot shall have the right of pre-emption to purchase the undivided share that is intended to be sold by mutual agreement to another person who is not a co-owner, in accordance with the provisions on pre-emption provided for in Resolution No. 3339 dated 12/11/1930.

This right of pre-emption shall not arise in a sale taking place between spouses, ascendants and descendants, or brothers and sisters and their descendants.

Everyone who acquires a right of ownership or a right of usufruct in any of the private lots must notify the person responsible for the management of the real property within thirty days at most and deposit with him all the official documents proving his acquisition of the right; otherwise, the former owner shall remain continuing to represent this lot towards the Association, which may collect all expenses from either one of them, unless the owner had notified the person responsible for the management of the real property of what proves his assignment of this right.

In the event that there exists a built real property owned in undivided co-ownership which is the subject of an action for partition, and partition in kind is not possible in any of the manners specified in the amended Article 942 of the Code of Obligations and Contracts, and it has not become the object of a joint-stock company pursuant to the Law on the Termination of Undivided Co-ownership in Real Properties issued on 16/3/1982, the court must partition it among the co-owners by subjecting it to the regime of co-ownership which is the subject of this Legislative Decree, if the majority of the co-owners in the undivided co-ownership so request and they own more than half of the shares therein.

The court may, where necessary, combine minute shares and join them into one or more lots, as well as adjust the lots in cash up to one fifth of their value, as set forth in items 3 and 4 of the aforementioned Article 942.

In order to carry out the partition in the manner set forth above, the court shall appoint an expert to carry out its distribution into private lots and other common lots and to propose by-laws for the management of the real property supplementing the provisions not provided for in this Legislative Decree, if the existence of the by-laws is required by law.

If the application for registration covers a building duly registered on the real folio or simultaneously covers the registration of the constructions into lots in accordance with the provisions of this Legislative Decree, the fee due shall be (1%) one per cent.
Articles 25, 26, 27, 29, 33, 36, 41, 47, 48, 49 and 73 of this Legislative Decree are among the provisions relating to public policy.
The provisions of Article 72 of Resolution No. 3339 dated 12/11/1930 shall not apply to buildings registered in the Land Register in accordance with the provisions of this Legislative Decree.

A period of six months starting from the date of entry into force of this Legislative Decree is granted to the owners of private lots under the Law of 24/12/1962 to elect a domicile in accordance with what is provided for in Article 25 of this Legislative Decree.

All provisions contrary to this Legislative Decree or inconsistent with its content are repealed, in particular the Law of 24/12/1962 relating to the regulation of the ownership of buildings consisting of several storeys or apartments.
This Legislative Decree shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The Court of Accounts is an administrative court that exercises financial jurisdiction, its mission being to safeguard public funds and funds deposited in the Treasury by:

- Supervising the use of these funds and the extent of conformity of such use with the laws and regulations in force.

- Adjudicating the validity and legality of their transactions and accounts.

- Trying those responsible for violating the laws and regulations relating thereto.

The Court of Accounts is administratively attached to the President of the Council of Ministers, and its seat is in Beirut.

The following shall be subject to the supervision of the Court of Accounts:

1- State administrations.

2- The municipalities of Beirut, Tripoli, El-Mina, Bourj Hammoud, Sidon, and Zahle-Maallaqa, and all other municipalities that have been or shall be subjected to the supervision of the Court of Accounts by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers.

3- Public institutions attached to the State and those attached to the municipalities subject to the supervision of the Court of Accounts.

4- Supervisory bodies representing the State in the institutions which they oversee or in the institutions for which the State guarantees a minimum profit.

5- Institutions, associations, and all other bodies and companies with which the State, the municipalities, or the public institutions attached to the State or the municipalities have a financial relationship by way of contribution, assistance, or lending.

The scope of supervision and its procedures with respect to the institutions, associations, bodies, and companies provided for in paragraphs 4 and 5 of this Article shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the competent Minister, and after consulting the opinion of the Court of Accounts. Until such decree is issued, the provisions of Decree No. 13615 dated 21/8/1963 shall remain in force.
The Court shall be composed of judges, controllers, and auditors, and administrative employees shall be attached thereto, and it shall have an independent Public Prosecution.

The President of the Court shall organise the internal administration and the manner of exercising all tasks entrusted to the Court, and shall correspond directly with all public administrations. The chambers shall be formed and the work of the Court shall be distributed by a decision of the President of the Court after the approval of the Council of the Court, and this distribution may be amended, where necessary, in the same manner. The President of the Court shall have a permanent delegation to exercise, in respect of the Court of Accounts, the financial and administrative powers vested by laws and regulations in the Minister, with the exception of constitutional powers, and he shall undertake the commitment of the expenditures of the Court and the supervision of their commitment and liquidation.

The President of the Court shall prepare the draft expenditures of the Court and send it to the Minister of Finance, and in the event that it is amended, the Council of Ministers shall decide thereon after hearing the President of the Court.

In the event of the absence of the President of the Court, or in the event of a vacancy in the office of the Presidency and the impossibility of his performing his duties, he shall be replaced by the President of the Chamber of the highest grade, and in case of equality, the oldest in age, and in case of equality, the most senior in the judiciary, and in case of equality, the most senior in public service.
The judge shall examine the transactions referred to him and perform the functions of prior and ex-post supervision and render opinions with the bench to which he belongs.

The controller shall assist the judge in his mission. In principle, the accounts of a single public accountant in a single financial year shall be audited by a single controller, and a single controller must not be entrusted with auditing the accounts of a single public accountant for more than two consecutive years. However, it is permissible, where necessary, to depart from the provisions of the preceding paragraph, provided that this is effected by a decision of the President of the Court taken after the approval of the Council of the Court.
The administrative employees shall perform the tasks assigned to them in accordance with internal regulations laid down by the President of the Court after the approval of the Council of the Court.
The acts of the controllers, court clerks, and bailiffs shall be deemed valid within the limits of their functions until proven to be forged.

The Public Prosecutor shall represent the Government before the Court and, in judicial supervision, may attend hearings and be given the floor therein, and may request documents to submit his written submissions and correspond directly with public administrations in all matters relating to the exercise of his mission. The Advocates General shall perform the function of the Public Prosecutor under his supervision. In the event of the absence of the Public Prosecutor and his deputies, the highest-ranking councillor shall carry out the functions of the Public Prosecution.

The competent authorities must notify the Public Prosecutor before the Court of the violations provided for in this Legislative Decree, and the Central Inspection Administration must file with the Public Prosecutor before the Court copies of the financial inspection reports. The Public Prosecutor shall examine these reports and send them with his observations and proposals to the Central Inspection Administration to take the required administrative or judicial measures against the responsible employees.

The Public Prosecutor may request the Public Prosecution before the Court of Cassation to partially prosecute any employee whom he deems to have committed or participated in one of the offences liable to cause damage to the public administration, to public funds, or to funds deposited in the Treasury. He must request such prosecution if the Court so decides. Criminal prosecution shall take place without authorisation from the administrative authority, and the competent administration and the Central Inspection Administration shall be informed of the matter.

The Court or the Public Prosecutor before it may task the Central Inspection Administration with conducting any inspection or investigation required by the public interest. The Central Inspection Administration must give priority to these missions if requested to do so.
The measures taken by the organs of the Central Inspection against offending employees shall not preclude their prosecution before the Court.

The Court of Accounts has two functions: an administrative function, and a judicial function.

It exercises the administrative function through its prior supervision over the execution of the budget, through reports it draws up on the history of its prior and ex-post supervision, and by rendering opinions on financial matters. It exercises the judicial function through its supervision over accounts and over every person who undertakes the use or management of public funds and funds deposited with the Treasury.
Administrative supervision is of two types: prior and ex-post.
The purpose of prior administrative supervision is to verify the validity of the transaction and its conformity with the budget and the provisions of the laws and regulations.

The prior supervision of the Court is an essential formality, and every transaction not subjected to this supervision shall be deemed unenforceable, and the competent employee is prohibited from and putting it into execution under penalty of the sanction provided for in Article 60 of this Legislative Decree.

The following transactions shall be subject to prior administrative supervision with respect to revenues:

1 - Transactions for the contracting out of revenues when the value exceeds /5/ billion Lebanese pounds.

2 - Transactions for the sale of real property when the value exceeds /5/ billion Lebanese pounds".

The following transactions shall be subject to prior administrative supervision with respect to expenditures:

- Supply and works contracts whose value exceeds /15/ billion Lebanese pounds.

- Service contracts whose value exceeds /10/ billion Lebanese pounds.

- Mutual agreements, including lease contracts, whose value exceeds /15/ billion Lebanese pounds.

- Transactions for the purchase of real property whose value exceeds /15/ billion Lebanese pounds.

- Transactions of grants, assistance, and contributions when the value of the grant, assistance, or contribution exceeds /15/ billion Lebanese pounds".

Amicable settlements of lawsuits or disputes shall be subject to prior administrative supervision if the amount in dispute exceeds /5/ billion Lebanese pounds".

"

The transaction, together with its supporting documents, shall be lodged with the Court of Audit, and a copy of the letter of lodgement shall be lodged with the Public Prosecutor by:

1- The competent authority empowered to decide on the transaction, in respect of revenues.

2- The controller of expenditure commitment in public administrations, and the official in charge of controlling expenditure commitment in public institutions and municipalities.

. The President shall refer the transaction to the competent judge in accordance with the work distribution decision, and he may handle it himself where necessary or in the cases specified in the work distribution decision.

Prior control shall be exercised by the competent judge, who shall examine the transaction himself or refer it to one of the controllers working with him to examine it and draw up a report thereon; if the competent judge approves the transaction, it shall be returned bearing his visa, and if he does not approve it, it shall be submitted to a chamber composed of a president and two counsellors, one of whom shall be the competent judge. However, transactions in which the value of the revenue or expenditure exceeds /500/ thousand Lebanese pounds shall be subject to prior control by a chamber composed of a president and two counsellors, one of whom shall be the competent judge. A decision declaring that the Court lacks jurisdiction to exercise prior control shall be issued by the said chamber.

The Court shall issue its decision on the transaction within ten days from the date on which it is lodged. Where it is necessary to request documents or clarifications or, where required, to hear the competent official, the Court shall be granted an additional time limit of five days from the date of obtaining the requested documents or clarifications. Official holidays shall not be counted in the said time limits. If the Court does not issue its decision within these time limits, the administration shall be entitled to retrieve the transaction and disregard the opinion of the Court.

If the decision of the Court grants approval:

- In respect of revenues, contrary to the opinion of the competent authority empowered to decide on the transaction, that authority shall comply with the decision of the Court unless the competent minister agrees to submit the transaction to the Council of Ministers.

- In respect of expenditures, contrary to the opinion of the controller of expenditure commitment, that controller shall comply with the decision of the Court unless the Minister of Finance agrees to submit the transaction to the Council of Ministers.

If the opinion of the Court is contrary to the submitted draft, the competent administration may submit the dispute to the Council of Ministers.

The Council of Ministers shall decide on the transactions submitted to it by reasoned decisions after hearing the President of the Court. Where it departs from the opinion of the Minister of Finance or the decision of the Court, its decision shall take the place of the visa of the Court or the visa of the controller of expenditure commitment. In both cases, reference to the decision of the Council of Ministers shall be made in the transaction.

The decision of the Council of Ministers shall be notified to the Court, which shall retain the right to include the matter in its annual report or in a special report notified to the Chamber of Deputies.

Decisions of the Court within the scope of its prior administrative control may be reconsidered at the request of the competent administration, the President of the Court of Audit, or the Public Prosecution at the Court. The chamber that issued the decision shall examine the request for reconsideration.
The prior approval of the Court shall be deemed lapsed if it is not acted upon during the financial year in which it was granted.

The purpose of subsequent administrative control is to assess financial transactions and their general outcomes from the time they are committed until their execution is completed and they are entered in the accounts.
An annual report and special reports shall be drawn up on the findings of the subsequent administrative control.

At the end of every year, the Court shall draw up a report on the findings of its control and the reforms it proposes to introduce into the various laws and regulations the application of which produces financial consequences. The Court, sitting in plenary assembly, shall adopt this report after hearing the Public Prosecutor.

The annual report shall be notified to the administrations and bodies concerned, and such administrations and bodies shall submit their replies within a time limit of one month, and the Court shall have the right to comment on those replies.

The President of the Court shall submit the annual report to the President of the Republic together with the replies of the administrations and bodies concerned and the comments of the Court thereon. He shall submit copies of this report accompanied by the replies and comments to the Chamber of Deputies for distribution to its members, and shall also submit copies thereof to the Civil Service Board and to the Central Inspection Administration.

The annual report, together with the replies of the administrations and bodies concerned and the comments, shall be published in the Official Gazette and printed in a separate volume for distribution to the administrations and bodies subject to the control of the Court.

The Parliamentary Finance and Budget Committee and the other competent committees shall hear the President of the Court or his delegate and, where necessary, the representatives of the public administrations and competent bodies when examining the report in order to provide the necessary clarifications.

The Court may, whenever it deems necessary, submit to the President of the Republic, the President of the Council of Ministers, or the public administrations and bodies concerned special reports on specific subjects and proposals appropriate thereto.
The Court shall issue each year a declaration of conformity for each of the accounts submitted to it, supported by the evidentiary documents provided for in the laws and regulations.

Declarations of conformity shall be notified:

- To the President of the Council of Ministers for distribution to the members of the Council, and to the Minister of Finance where they relate to the accounts of the general budget, annexed budgets, and other budgets subject to ratification by the legislative authority, and the provisions of Article 51 of this Legislative Decree shall apply thereto.

- To the Minister of Finance, the supervisory minister, the bodies concerned, and the authority competent to ratify the final settlement of their budget accounts, where they relate to the accounts of budgets subject to ratification by an authority other than the legislative authority.
Judicial control is of two kinds: control over accounts and control over officials.

The purpose of control over accounts is to adjudicate upon the accuracy of the accounts of public accountants and of any person who intervenes in the collection or payment of public funds and funds deposited in the Treasury without having legal capacity to do so.

Subject to the final decisions issued by the Court of Audit in respect of the accounts of previous years, the Court of Audit shall exercise its control over accounts starting from the accounts of the year 1991.

Control over accounts shall cover the following transactions:

A- In respect of revenues:

1- The validity of the documents pursuant to which collection was made.

2- The accuracy of the collections and their conformity with the tax collection laws.

3- The remittance of collected amounts to the public coffers.

B - In respect of expenditures:

1- The validity of the documents pursuant to which payment was made and the conformity of the transaction with the laws and regulations in force and with the budget and the appropriations opened pursuant thereto.

2- The existence of the evidentiary documents for the expenditure as defined by law.

C- In respect of Treasury receipts and payments:

The accuracy of collection and payment transactions and their conformity with the orders issued by the competent authority.

D- In respect of supplies: the accuracy of the receipt, safekeeping, and delivery of supplies, and the accuracy of the preparation of inventory statements.

E- In respect of accounts:

1- The accuracy of the accounts and their conformity with the laws and regulations.

2- The conformity of the entries with the submitted evidentiary documents.

The Court of Accounts shall audit and settle the accounts of public accountants, draw them up, and adjudicate thereon by way of provisional decisions or final decisions. The provisional decision shall state the objections attributed to the account and what is required to be submitted in reply thereto. The final decision shall declare the public accountant to be discharged of liability, in advance, or in debit; in the first and second cases, if the public accountant has ceased to hold office, the Court shall order the striking off of the encumbrances placed on his property, if any, and the release of the security furnished by him, and in the third case, the Court shall order the public accountant to pay the balance remaining owed by him within a period which it shall fix for him, and if the liability arose as a result of force majeure, the Court may exempt the public accountant therefrom. Where the public accountant dies, his estate shall not devolve upon his successors before the Court issues a final decision concerning his account. The competent administration shall lodge the account together with its supporting documents with the Court within a period not exceeding three months from the date of death, and the Court shall issue its decision within three months from the date of the lodging of the account with it. In all cases, if six months elapse from the date of lodging the account of the deceased public accountant with the Court without the Court having issued its decision within that period, the said decision shall be dispensed with, and the estate may thereupon devolve upon the successors of the public accountant provided there is no other legal impediment preventing the same.

Supervision over civil servants shall cover the acts of every person who administers or uses public funds and funds deposited in the Treasury, and every person who performs operations of receipt and payment for the account of the Treasury or for its benefit or keeps its accounts, as well as the acts of every person who intervenes in the administration of the aforesaid funds and in performing the aforementioned operations without having the legal capacity to do so, or who participates in the acts and operations referred to, whether by carrying out the preparatory acts therefor, supervising them, or approving them. Every person who is not a civil servant and to whom has been entrusted the assumption of the duties provided for in the first paragraph of this Article, whether by appointment, election, or contract, including members of deliberative bodies on the occasion of their assuming the aforesaid duties, and every person who is not a civil servant who has assumed these duties or intervened or participated therein without legal capacity, shall be deemed to have the status of a civil servant in the application of the provisions of this supervision.

Every civil servant who commits or participates in committing one of the contraventions set forth in this Article shall be punished by a fine from one billion and five hundred million Lebanese pounds to fifteen billion Lebanese pounds, in addition to the civil liabilities and penal and disciplinary penalties that may be imposed by the competent authorities:

1- Committing an expenditure contrary to the provisions of the law or regulations.

2- Committing an expenditure without obtaining the visa of the Controller of Committed Expenditure.

3- Neglecting to submit a transaction to the prior review of the Court, or putting into execution a transaction that was not submitted to such review, or putting into execution a transaction without complying with the conditions set forth in the decision of the Court concerning it.

4- Failing to comply with the refusal of the visa on a transaction by the Court of Accounts or by the Controller of Committed Expenditure.

5- Misallocating an expenditure in order to conceal an excess of appropriations.

6- Executing an order contrary to the law received otherwise than through his hierarchical superior.

7- Procuring or attempting to procure an unlawful profit for persons contracting with the administration.

8- Committing an error, default, or negligence liable to cause material damage to public funds or to funds deposited in the Treasury.

9- Delaying in lodging with the Court of Accounts or the Public Prosecution attached thereto the accounts, supporting documents, and explanations required within the time-limits prescribed in the laws and regulations.

10- Violating the provisions relating to the administration or use of public funds or funds deposited in the Treasury.

Where it appears that the contravention provided for in Article 60 of this Legislative Decree has caused damage or loss to public funds or to funds deposited in the Treasury, the Court shall have the right to punish the offending civil servant, in addition to the fine provided for in Article 60, with a fine calculated in proportion to the gravity of the contravention committed and to the amount of the gross salary received by the offending civil servant where he receives a salary, or to the amount of his allowances or the equivalent thereof in other cases. This additional fine may not be less than the monthly salary of the civil servant or his monthly allowances or the equivalent thereof as at the date of the commission of the contravention, nor may it exceed the total of his annual salary or his annual allowances or the equivalent thereof as at the aforesaid date, and where he performs the work without remuneration, the fine shall be between one thousand pounds and ten thousand Lebanese pounds. A civil servant tried before the Court of Accounts shall be permitted to be assisted by an advocate of his choice.

1- The Court shall assess the causes of the contravention and the extent of liability therefor, and shall sentence the responsible civil servant to a fine within the limits set forth in Articles 60 and 61 of this Legislative Decree.

2- The civil servant shall be exempted from the penalty if the act leading to the contravention is revoked before being put into execution, or if it appears from the investigation that the contravention was committed in execution of a written order received by him from his immediate superior, provided that he had drawn the attention of that superior in writing to the contravention that might result from the execution of his order; in such case, the superior shall take the place of the civil servant in liability and shall be punished within the limits set forth in Articles 60 and 61 of this Legislative Decree. A civil servant directly subordinate to a Minister shall not be exempted from the penalty unless he notifies the Court directly and the Public Prosecutor before the Court, within one week at most, of the written submission which he presented to the Minister prior to executing the order and in which he drew his attention to the contravention that might result from that order.

3- The Court may decide to grant exemption from the penalty if it appears to it that it was impossible for the civil servant to have been aware of the contravention at the time of its commission, or that the civil servant committed the contravention for the sake of the proper functioning of the public services or for the purpose of averting certain damage that might befall them.

4- Where the Court imposes a fine, it may decide to suspend the execution thereof if it is satisfied of the good faith of the convicted person, provided that the latter shall not benefit from a suspension of execution more than once during the single financial year during which the contravention was committed.

Fines imposed by the Court may not be cumulated save within the maximum limit provided for in Articles 60 and 61 of this Legislative Decree. The fines provided for in the two aforesaid Articles shall not be subject to modification by administrative means.
The Court shall inform the Chamber of Deputies of the contraventions committed by Ministers.

1- The termination of the service of a civil servant shall not preclude his prosecution before the Court of Accounts.

2- Prosecution for the contravention shall lapse and be extinguished by the death of the civil servant responsible therefor or by prescription.

3- A contravention shall be barred by prescription upon the expiry of five years from the date of its commission if it was apparent, or from the date of its discovery if it was concealed. The period of prescription shall be calculated from day to corresponding day, and shall only be interrupted by one of the following causes:

أ- A request made to the Court of Accounts to examine the contravention in accordance with the provisions of this Legislative Decree.

ب - The commencement of investigation proceedings into the contravention in accordance with the provisions of this Legislative Decree.

ج- Preparatory decisions taken by the Court of Accounts concerning the contravention.

د- An application to set aside the decision of the Court of Accounts concerning the contravention.

The Court shall exercise its judicial jurisdiction in its capacity as a tribunal composed of a chamber of a President and two Councillors. The provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure shall apply to an application for recusal and withdrawal.

Where it is not possible to constitute the Bench, it shall be completed with judges from the State Council seconded by a decision of the Council of Ministers upon the request of the President of the Court and after the approval of the President of the State Council.

1- The Court shall examine the infraction of its own motion or upon the request of the Public Prosecutor attached to it. For this purpose, the Public Prosecutor may conduct the investigation into the case or expand the ongoing investigation concerning it, and he may hear employees and witnesses, request the competent administration or body to lodge with him the documents, clarifications, and information that he requires, and task the controller assisting him with conducting any local audit relating to the case, provided that the assignment is notified to the immediate superior of the employee prior to commencing the mission. The provisions of Article 80 of this Legislative Decree shall apply to the employees and witnesses, and the provisions of paragraph 2 of this Article shall apply to the request for documents, clarifications, and information. In the event of examination of its own motion, the procedures set out above shall be followed, provided that the competent judge assumes the function of the Public Prosecutor set out therein.

2- The President of the Chamber shall refer the transaction to the competent Advisor, who shall undertake the examination thereof himself or refer it to a controller to assist him in examining it. The Advisor may request from the competent administration the written clarifications and information that he requires, interrogate the employee to whom the infraction is attributed, hear witnesses, and propose to the Bench the appointment of experts, and he may task the controller in writing with conducting any local investigation or audit relating to the transaction referred to him, provided that the written assignment which is to the head of the administration is notified prior to commencing the mission. The competent administration shall reply to the request within the time limit specified therein, provided that such time limit is not less than ten days. This time limit may be extended where necessary, either of its own motion or upon the request of the competent administration. The Court may inspect any file or document, even a confidential one, if it has a connection with the case under examination
As a result of the investigation, the Advisor shall draw up a report containing a summary of the case together with the expression of his opinion thereon.

The reports of the Advisors in which reconsideration, determination of jurisdiction, charging of liability, discharge of liability, or imposition of a fine is requested shall be referred to the Public Prosecutor, together with the supporting documents. As for other reports, they shall be referred to him if he requests them or if the President or the competent Bench so decides. The Public Prosecutor shall return these reports accompanied by his written submissions within a time limit not exceeding ten days.

The provisional decision shall be served upon the public accountant or the employee through process servers in accordance with the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, or by registered mail with acknowledgment of receipt, or through administrative channels, and a copy thereof shall be served upon his immediate superior. The interested party shall submit his defence within the time limit specified in the decision, provided that it is not less than thirty days; if this time limit expires without a reply being submitted, the Court shall examine the case in the state in which it is presented. The interested party shall have the right to inspect the file and to be assisted by a lawyer.
The audit shall be conducted in the deliberation chamber on the basis of the documents produced. Decisions shall be issued in the deliberation chamber by a majority of votes.

The final decision shall be served upon the interested party in accordance with the procedures set out in Article 71 of this Legislative Decree. A copy thereof shall be served upon the Public Prosecutor and upon the competent ministry or administration, and a copy shall be sent to the Ministry of Finance for enforcement in accordance with the Law on the Collection of Direct Taxes.

A compulsory mortgage shall be placed on the immovable properties of the person against whom judgment is rendered. Statutory interest shall run on the liability adjudged as from the date specified in the decision.

The Court may in all cases recommend to the competent Minister that the employee be prosecuted administratively or criminally, provided that it notifies a copy of its recommendation to the Central Inspection Administration.
The final judicial decisions of the Court may be challenged either by way of reconsideration or by way of cassation.

1- Reconsideration of a decision may be sought before the Court:

A- If it appears from the audit of another transaction that there is an error,

omission, forgery, or duplicate entry.

B - If new documents or matters emerge that are bound to alter the outcome of

the decision.

2- Reconsideration shall take place upon the request of the Public Prosecutor, the Minister of Finance in the interest of the Treasury, the public accountant, the competent employee, or the administration or body concerned.

3- The application for reconsideration shall be submitted by the public accountant or the employee within a period of two months from the date of discovery or emergence of the ground justifying it, and the admissibility of the application for reconsideration shall be conditional upon the payment of a deposit in the amount of /10 000/ Pounds

paid against a receipt at the Lebanese Treasury. This deposit shall be forfeited as revenue to the Treasury if the application for reconsideration is dismissed in form or on the merits, and it shall be refunded to the public accountant or the employee in all other cases.

4- An application for reconsideration shall not stay the enforcement of the impugned decision,

provided however that the Court may exceptionally decide to stay the enforcement of the impugned decision upon the request of the competent public accountant or employee if it appears that enforcement would cause him grave harm and that the application for reconsideration is based on a serious ground.

5- The Bench that issued the impugned decision shall examine the application for reconsideration.

Cassation of the decision may be sought before the State Council on the grounds of lack of jurisdiction, breach of trial procedures, or violation of laws and regulations, within a time limit of two months from the date of service of the impugned decision. The application for cassation may be submitted by each of the Public Prosecutor attached to the Court of Accounts, the Minister of Finance in the interest of the Treasury, the competent employee, and the administration or body concerned.
If the decision is quashed, the Court shall be bound to comply with the decision of the State Council.

1- Employees, witnesses, and experts shall be summoned to appear before the Court in prior and ex-post control through the President of the Chamber.

The person summoned before the Court shall comply with the summons, failing which he shall be liable to a fine of 20 000 Lebanese Pounds, which shall be doubled each time he fails to comply with the summons unless he proves that his failure to appear was due to a legitimate excuse.

The Court shall examine the case in accordance with the provisions of Article 68 of this Legislative Decree.

2- Experts at the Court of Accounts shall be appointed from the roster in force before the courts.

The competent Bench at the Court shall, after the approval of the President of the Court, determine the fee of the expert within the limits of the appropriations allocated for this purpose in the budget or out of the deposit that the interested party may advance for this purpose.

The provisions of Legislative Decree No. 65 dated 9/9/1983 shall apply to the determination of the fee.

The procedures for advancing the deposit set out in this item and paying the fee of the expert therefrom shall be regulated by a decision of the President of the Court of Accounts after the approval of its Council.

The competent employees shall send their accounts to the Court of Accounts in accordance with special regulations drawn up by agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Court of Accounts and approved by a joint decision of the Minister of Finance and the President of the Court of Accounts.

The competent employees in municipalities and public institutions that are subject to the Public Accounting Law shall send the accounts, documents, and information in accordance with the regulations provided for in the preceding Article. As for municipalities, public institutions, and other bodies that are not subject to the Public Accounting Law, they shall send their accounts to the Court in accordance with special regulations drawn up by such municipalities, institutions, or bodies in agreement with the Court of Accounts and approved by a decision of the Minister exercising administrative tutelage.
The Court of Accounts may request from the competent administrations all the accounts, clarifications, and documents required for control.

Where an employee delays in submitting the required accounts, information and documents within the fixed time limits, the Court may appoint an expert to collect them and submit them to it at the expense of the said employee, and the Court shall determine the fee of such expert. The rules of procedure provided for in Articles 71 and 80 of this Legislative Decree shall apply to the notification of the decision appointing the expert and determining his fee.

After completing the audit of the accounts and documents sent to it and taking the final decision thereon, the Court of Accounts may retain them in its possession or return them to their source after stamping them with a special stamp. It may also decide to audit the documents locally at the administrations, municipalities, public institutions and all other bodies subject to its supervision, and in such case it shall request the administration, municipality, institution or body concerned not to send the documents to the Court.

Both the Court of Accounts and the Public Prosecutor attached to it shall be notified, immediately upon their issuance, of all instruments containing the appointment of employees or contracted staff at the administrations, institutions and bodies subject to the supervision of the Court. If it appears to the competent chamber that the appointment was made contrary to the provisions of the laws and regulations in force, it must take a judicial decision forbidding the disbursement of the expenditure resulting from this appointment. The competent chamber shall examine the case of its own motion or upon the request of the President of the Court or the Public Prosecutor attached to it, and shall follow in the investigation and trial the rules of procedure provided for in this Legislative Decree in respect of judicial supervision. The decision of the chamber shall be notified to the competent authorities for execution and to the party concerned. This decision shall be subject to the remedies provided for in this Legislative Decree.

Administrations, public institutions, municipalities and all other bodies subject to the supervision of the Court of Accounts may request the opinion of the Court on financial matters. This opinion shall be issued by the competent body in accordance with the decision on the distribution of work, and shall be of an advisory nature.

In the event of divergence of jurisprudence within the Court during the exercise of all types of its supervision, the President of the Court shall refer the matter to the General Assembly of the Court to take a decision unifying the jurisprudence. Decisions unifying the jurisprudence shall be of a binding nature.

Unless the law or regulations provide otherwise, employees required to take the oath before the Court of Accounts shall take the oath worded as follows: "I swear by Almighty God to perform the duty of my office with honesty and faithfulness and to preserve its secrecy forever".

With the exception of the provisions thereof relating to account auditors, Article 90 of the said Legislative Decree, together with the attached schedule provided for in this Article, is repealed, and Article 91 is also repealed.

The documents of the Court of Accounts shall be kept for a period of at least fifteen years, and shall not be destroyed or disposed of after the said period except with the approval of the Council of the Court.

The amount of the fine provided for in Article 60 of Legislative Decree No. 82 dated 16/09/1983 is raised from /500/ L.L. to /150000/ L.L. and from /15000/ L.L. to /1500000/ L.L. (one million five hundred thousand pounds).

- The amount of the fine provided for in the second paragraph of Article 80 of the said Legislative Decree is raised from /200/ L.L. to /20000/ L.L.

- The amount of the security deposit provided for in Article 77 of the above Legislative Decree is raised from one hundred Lebanese pounds to ten thousand Lebanese pounds.
The establishment of the Court of Accounts shall be determined in accordance with Schedule No. 1 attached to this Law.

Military cases shall be heard by: 1- A Permanent Military Court having its seat in Beirut. This Court may, where necessary and pursuant to a decision of the Minister of National Defence, hold its sittings in any other region of the Lebanese regions. 2- Single judges whose number and the territorial jurisdiction of each of whom shall be determined by decree in accordance with the requirements of necessity.

In time of war, military courts attached to the Army may be established by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of National Defence to hear, in accordance with the rules of jurisdiction and procedure provided for in this Law, offences committed in combat zones or zones of occupation carried out by the Lebanese Army to which such courts are attached.

The Military Court shall be composed: 1- For hearing felony cases, of a brigadier general or colonel as president, and of an officer judge of the Military Judiciary, a lieutenant colonel, a captain, and a first lieutenant as members. 2- For hearing misdemeanour cases, of a brigadier general or colonel as president, and of an officer judge of the Military Judiciary, and a lieutenant colonel, or a captain, or a first lieutenant as members.

The Minister of National Defence shall appoint the judges of the Military Court, with the exception of the judges seconded to the military courts. The Minister of National Defence shall draw up in the month of September of every year a roster of the officers of whom the Military Court is composed and of the officers who substitute for them. This roster may be amended where necessary at any time of the year.

If it appears that the case requires multiple sittings, the President of the Court may summon an additional president and additional members of the rank of the President and members of whom the Court is composed, so that they may substitute during the trial for the President or the member who is unable to continue the trial. The additional president and members shall attend all stages of the trial, but they shall not be entitled to participate in the deliberations unless they have substituted for a judge who was unable to continue the trial.

The presidents and members of the military courts, with the exception of the judges attached to the military courts, shall, during their exercise of judicial office, be directly subordinate to the Minister of National Defence, while remaining nevertheless subject to the general military regulations. However, during their exercise of judicial office, they may not be referred before a military court or a board of inquiry, nor may a disciplinary penalty be imposed upon them, except by order of the Minister of National Defence. The Minister of Defence shall appoint these judges for the first time immediately upon the entry into force of this Law.
The seat of the military courts composed of a single judge and their territorial jurisdiction shall be determined by the decree establishing them.
The single judge shall hold his sittings whenever the need arises within the limits of his territorial jurisdiction.

The single judge shall hear: 1- All contraventions, and the contraventions and misdemeanours provided for in the Traffic Law which are committed within his territorial jurisdiction by military personnel, persons assimilated to military personnel, and civilian employees in the Army, unless the military authority sees fit to impose a disciplinary penalty upon them. 2- Other misdemeanours that fall within the jurisdiction of the military courts where the penalty that may be imposed is either a fine without imprisonment, or imprisonment without a fine, or both imprisonment and a fine together, provided that the maximum term of imprisonment does not exceed six months.

With respect to the misdemeanours provided for in the second paragraph of the preceding Article, and until the first sitting is held, the Government Commissioner shall be entitled to request the single judge to divest himself of the action, whereupon he shall refer it to the Military Court hearing misdemeanour cases.

The single judge shall apply, in all contraventions and in the contraventions and misdemeanours provided for in the Traffic Law, the procedures provided for in Decision No. 297 issued on 26 December 1934, and opposition to his judgments shall be lodged in the manner set forth in the said Decision.
Judgments in absentia rendered in the cases provided for in paragraph 2 of Article 9 shall be subject to opposition in accordance with the procedures followed in summary penal trials.
Only judgments imposing imprisonment shall be subject to appeal.
The appeal shall be lodged with the ordinary Military Court composed in accordance with paragraph 2 of Article 3.

The trial procedures before the single judge, the exercise of the right of appeal, and the appellate procedures shall be subject to the rules governing cases within the jurisdiction of the summary judge, insofar as they do not conflict with the provisions of this Law.

There shall be appointed to the Military Court: 1- A Government Commissioner and an Investigating Judge, to each of whom shall be attached, where necessary, one or more assistants. 2- Assistant officers to the Government Commissioner who shall perform the functions of the judicial police.
The functions of the Government Commissioner shall be performed by the Appellate Public Prosecutor and one or more assistants whom he seconds for this purpose at the beginning of each judicial year.
The Government Commissioner and his assistants shall exercise the powers vested in the Public Prosecutor of First Instance pursuant to the regulations and laws in force.
The Government Commissioner may prosecute all offences that fall within the jurisdiction of the Military Court.
The Government Commissioner may institute the public action without its being preceded by an information or a complaint, save in the specific cases exempted by the law by a special provision:

Where the institution of the public action is conditional upon the complainant assuming the capacity of civil party, the Government Commissioner shall be entitled to conduct the prosecution upon the complaint of the injured party.
If it appears to the Government Commissioner that the case does not warrant prosecution for any reason whatsoever, he may decide to close and file it immediately or after conducting an investigation.

If it appears to the Government Commissioner that the case warrants prosecution and the offence is of the nature of a felony, he must refer the case to the Investigating Judge; and if it appears that the offence is of the nature of a misdemeanour, he may either refer the case directly to the Court by way of direct indictment or refer it to the Investigating Judge.
The Government Commissioner shall draw up the bill of indictment.
Save for the special procedures set forth in this Law, the Military Investigator and his assistants shall conduct the investigation in accordance with the procedures provided for in the ordinary law.
The decisions of the Military Investigating Magistrate shall not be subject to any avenue of recourse.

After the submission of the Government Commissioner is obtained, the Military Investigating Magistrate shall issue a decision to bar prosecution or to refer the case before the Military Court, whether in felonies or in misdemeanours. The referral decision shall include an arrest warrant in felony matters.
The provisions of the Law issued on 12 January 1944 concerning the attendance of a lawyer at investigation proceedings shall not apply before the Military Investigating Magistrate.

The functions of the Military Judicial Police shall be exercised by: 1- The Government Commissioner, the Investigating Judge, and their assistants. 2- The officers whom the Supreme Commander of the Army appoints for this purpose

Officers of the Military Judicial Police shall enjoy, with respect to offences falling within the jurisdiction of the Military Courts, the same powers as those enjoyed by the Judicial Police with respect to ordinary offences

Where there are no military judicial officers, ordinary judicial officers shall be entitled, solely in the case of an offence in flagrante delicto, to pursue offences falling within the jurisdiction of the Military Courts, either on their own initiative or at the request of the Government Commissioner, the Investigating Judge, and their assistants

Civilian judges at the Military Court, single judges, and the Investigating Judge shall be drawn from the judicial cadre and shall be appointed by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice.

The appointment of these judges shall be subject to the conditions set forth in the Statute of Civilian Judges, and during their tenure in the military judiciary they shall remain subject to the said Statute and subordinate to the Ministry of Justice in all matters relating to their promotion and discipline, and they may at any time be returned to the civilian judiciary.

Judges seconded to perform the function of a member of the Military Courts shall wear military uniform during their secondment to the military judiciary and shall hold the military rank whose salary is equivalent to the salary of the judicial grade in which they stand, provided that they shall not hold a rank higher than the rank of Colonel, and if the military corps does not contain a grade whose salary is equivalent to the salary they receive in the judicial corps, they shall hold the military rank whose salary is immediately higher than their salary. Upon their appointment, they shall receive a lump-sum allowance for military outfitting determined according to the circumstances by a decision of the Minister of National Defence.
All judges and officers seconded to the Military Courts shall receive an allowance determined by a decree.

Clerical work at the Military Courts shall be performed by a chief clerk with the rank of officer and clerks with the rank of First Adjutant, Adjutant, First Sergeant, or Sergeant. In addition, at each Military Court there shall be: 1- A non-commissioned officer specifically entrusted with watching over the buildings and keeping the papers and criminal exhibits, who is called a custodian. 2- One or several non-commissioned officers to perform the functions of bailiffs, messengers, and assistant custodians.

Judicial assistants at the military judiciary shall be drawn from military personnel and from clerks of the ordinary courts, and they shall be appointed to their functions by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Ministers of Justice and of National Defence, each with respect to the assistants subordinate to his Ministry.

Assistants drawn from the military corps shall remain subject to military regulations- whereas assistants drawn from the corps of judicial assistants shall be subject to the Statute of Judicial Assistants. The number of assistants at the military judiciary shall be determined by a decree, and they shall receive their salaries from the budget of the Ministry of National Defence.
The rules set out in the ordinary law shall apply to the keeping of registers in the Military Courts and to the powers and duties of the assistants of the military judiciary
Every person referred before the ordinary Military Courts must have a lawyer to defend him.
The presence of a lawyer is not mandatory before Military Courts composed of a single judge.
No one shall be entitled to undertake the defence of an absent accused.

The defence of accused persons who do not choose a lawyer shall be entrusted to one of the lawyers or to one of the officers, preference among them being given to one holding a licence in law, provided that the rank of such officers is not lower than the rank of First Lieutenant, appointed by the Supreme Commander of the Army at the beginning of each judicial year.

The Government Commissioner shall verify three days prior to the date of the hearing that the accused has chosen someone to defend him, so that if he has not chosen a lawyer to defend him or if his lawyer is unable to defend him, the Government Commissioner shall appoint a lawyer for him from among the officers provided for in the preceding Article or from among the lawyers whom the President of the Bar Association appoints for this purpose.

In the case of an offence in flagrante delicto, the lawyer shall be appointed at the hearing itself if the accused consents to be tried immediately. If he does not consent to be tried immediately, the case shall be adjourned to the nearest hearing held by the Court after the appointment of the lawyer.

The case file shall be placed at the disposal of the lawyer at least twenty-four hours prior to the date of the hearing, and the lawyer may take copies of all the papers except confidential papers. With respect to these, he may be prohibited from taking copies thereof

If the lawyer commits a grave breach of professional conduct, the Government Commissioner shall be entitled to bar him temporarily for a period not exceeding three months from entering the Military Courts. The Government Commissioner shall notify his decision to the President of the Bar Association within 48 hours in order to consider the matter of taking disciplinary sanctions.
The jurisdiction of the Permanent Military Court organized in accordance with the provisions of this Law shall encompass all Lebanese territory.

If in time of war the Army is stationed in enemy territory, the jurisdiction of the Permanent Military Court shall encompass the occupied territories, except for the areas encompassed by the jurisdiction of the Military Courts attached to the Army

The Military Courts shall have jurisdiction over: 1- Military offences provided for in Title One of Book Two of this Law. 2- Offences provided for in the Penal Code from Article 273 to 280 (Treason), from Article 281 to 284 (Espionage), from Article 285 to 287 (Unlawful Relations with the Enemy), from Article 288 to 294 (Offences Prejudicial to International Law), from Article 299 to Article 300 (Offences of Contractors), and from Article 325 to Article 328 (Carrying Weapons and Ammunition of War). 3- Offences committed in military camps and establishments. 4- And in general, all offences that directly affect the interests of the Army.

There shall be tried before the Military Courts, whatever their nationality: 1- Military personnel, persons assimilated to military personnel, civil employees in the Army, so long as they are in the service of the Army, for felonies, misdemeanours and contraventions which they commit of whatever kind they may be. 2- Prisoners of war 3- Perpetrators of an offence, accomplices and accessories where one of them is among those who must be tried before the Military Courts. 4- Men of the Gendarmerie when they are tried for the offences provided for in Title One of Book Two of this Law.
