No discrimination or imposition of restrictions on the provision of services shall be permitted, nor may such restrictions be imposed on the ownership or operation of the basic infrastructure necessary for the provision of these services.

Compliance with the provisions of this Law and the regulations of the Authority shall be deemed a condition of every licence granted, even if not expressly stated in the licence.

Licensing of Telecommunications Services:

1 - A licence shall be granted by a decree passed by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister, following an international public auction and in accordance with a book of specifications prepared by the Authority, to providers of the following public telecommunications services:

a - Basic telephone services.

b - Cellular telephone services.

c - International telephone services.

d - New categories of licences for the provision of public telecommunications services, including UMTS, on a local or international basis.

2 - The Authority shall grant licences to providers of the following telecommunications services:

a - Private line service.

b - Call offices and public telephones.

c - Leased lines service.

d - Local and international telex and telegraph service.

e - Internet services.

f- DATA services.

g- Any other telecommunications service that the Authority subjects to similar licences.

Licensing Procedures:

1 - Subject to the provisions of Article nineteen of this Law, the Authority shall establish the procedures for submitting and reviewing licence applications. It shall grant the licence to any person or group of persons who meet the required qualifications and specifications.

Where it is not possible to accept all submitted applications, the Authority shall observe the principles of transparency and competitiveness in the method of selection among them, and may select in accordance with criteria that the Authority decides to adopt, provided that such criteria are known to all and that the applications are made available to the public for inspection in accordance with the provisions of Article 12 of this Law.

2 - The Authority may establish, in addition to the qualifications, standards, and requirements specified in this Law, regulations requiring prior approval from the Authority for the installation and operation of equipment, while preserving the rights of licensees to provide services via radio frequencies.

3 - The licence shall include the basic obligations imposed on the licensee in implementation of the provisions of this Law or determined by the Authority in fulfilment of its objectives, including fees, providing the Authority with information, submitting to inspection, the term of the licence, and the conditions for its termination or renewal.

4 - No person may provide or offer any telecommunications service except in accordance with the provisions of this Law and the regulations established by the Authority in implementation of these provisions.

Any violation, including the provision of a service subject to licensing without obtaining a licence, shall subject the offender to the penalties provided for in Article 41 of this Law.

Value-Added Services:

The Authority shall not place any restriction on the provision of value-added services; however, the Authority shall have the right to restrict the right of any service provider having significant market power in the provision of value-added services, by imposing restrictions relating to regulatory, tariff, and accounting rules, or through precautionary measures that the Authority finds consistent with the provisions of this Law.

Provision of Telecommunications Equipment and Subscriber Private Equipment:

The Authority shall not place restrictions on the provision, development, manufacture, sale, lease, installation, and maintenance of telecommunications equipment and subscriber private equipment, except as expressly provided for in this Law or the regulations issued in implementation of its provisions.

However, the Authority shall have the right to restrict the ability of a service provider having significant market power to provide telecommunications equipment and subscriber private equipment, by imposing restrictions relating to regulatory, tariff, and accounting rules and any precautionary measures consistent with the provisions of this Law.

Approval of Equipment - Standards:

1 - The Authority shall determine the standards and technical conditions applicable to telecommunications equipment and subscriber private equipment to ensure that no harm is caused to telecommunications networks or to public health or safety.

Every importer under this Law must comply with all standards and technical conditions established by the Authority, and every licensee must comply with these standards and conditions when connecting telecommunications equipment and subscriber private equipment to public telecommunications networks.

2 - The Authority may determine general or special standards for performance, interoperability, and interconnection for the various categories of equipment, and to ensure that their specifications conform to the provisions of this Law and the rules established by the Authority in implementation of its provisions.

3 - For this purpose, the Authority may seek the assistance of officials responsible for public health or safety, service providers, and manufacturers to determine the conditions for type approval of equipment, and may also resort to industrial advisory groups to test, develop, and update equipment.

Any violation of the provisions of this Article shall subject the offender to the penalties provided for in Article 41 of this Law.

Transfer of Licences:

1 - A licence holder may not assign the licence to any other person, nor may legal or administrative control over the legal person holding the licence be transferred, except after obtaining the prior approval of the Authority and provided that the transfer or assignment is in conformity with the provisions of this Law and the regulations issued in implementation thereof.

2 - The Authority shall have the right to suspend, revoke, or terminate the licence in the event of:

a - Repeated failure to comply with an enforceable order.

b - Deliberate and repeated breach of the conditions of the licence or of the provisions of this Law and the regulations issued in implementation thereof.

c - Death of the licence holder without his heirs, or any one of them, meeting the conditions necessary for the licence.

d - Bankruptcy or liquidation of the company holding the licence.

Competitive Markets:

1 - The Authority may take into consideration, when determining the significance of the market power of a public telecommunications service provider, the extent of its impact on the Lebanese market, and in this case the regulatory consequences resulting therefrom shall be limited to the area of impact.

2 - The Authority may review any existing or proposed agreement or any contractual relationship between a public telecommunications service provider enjoying significant market power and its affiliates or between it and another public telecommunications service provider to verify its compliance with the provisions of this Law and that it does not restrict competition in the concerned markets without being offset by securing the interest of the beneficiaries of the market in general.

The Authority may review all other agreements that may have a non-competitive effect on the Lebanese telecommunications market and it may take the appropriate measures to address the arising situations.

3 - The Authority shall verify that the public telecommunications service provider enjoying significant market power does not abuse its market position and it may prevent it from obtaining additional licences for public telecommunications services or require it to comply with regulatory, tariff, or accounting rules or any other precautionary measures that the Authority deems appropriate to preserve the competitive market.

The Authority may initiate taking the measures it deems necessary before or after the proposal of any agreement or any proposed contractual relationship or the occurrence of any abuse of a significant market position, in order to preserve the development of competitive telecommunications markets.

4 - The Authority may protect competition or impose conditions on a public telecommunications service provider through a number of measures, including:

a - Amending the provisions of the licence conditions.

b - Suspending its approval of any application to transfer control of the licence pursuant to the provisions of Article 24 of this Law.

c - Taking decisions that apply to all public telecommunications service providers.

5 - The Authority may take any measures to secure competition, including, by way of example and not limitation, measures taken to counter:

a - Anti-competitive cross-subsidies.

b - The use of information obtained from competitors which results in anti-competitive outcomes.

c - Failing to enable other telecommunications service providers to obtain on a timely and regular basis technical information about essential facilities and commercial information that they need to provide services.

6 - The Authority may take all possible measures that would increase competition in the Lebanese telecommunications market instead of imposing restrictions on the business or actions of public telecommunications service providers enjoying significant market power.

The Authority shall reconsider these measures immediately and as quickly as possible if it appears that the development of competition in the market requires the cancellation or amendment of these measures.

7- The Authority shall take into consideration, when exercising its duties specified in this Article, the provisions of this Law and the competition principles applicable in countries where a competitive telecommunications market exists.

Numbering Management:

1 - The Authority shall undertake the management of numbering required by subscribers and users to use public telecommunications services.

2 - The Authority shall manage the numbers without any discrimination, and shall make the details of the numbering plan available to the public.

In particular, it shall ensure that all public telecommunications service providers obtain numbers without any unjustified delay, provided that any change in numbering does not cause unusual inconvenience to subscribers and users or to public telecommunications service providers, and provided that the allocation of numbers does not result in any competitive advantage or any impediment to the business of public telecommunications service providers.

Annual or Periodic Reports:

1 - The Authority may require all public telecommunications service providers, or any category thereof, to submit annual or periodic reports when necessary containing the information specified by the Authority and which it deems necessary for the exercise of its duties in regulating the telecommunications sector.

2 - The Authority may require the submission of copies of contracts, agreements, or other arrangements agreed upon by public telecommunications service providers among themselves or with resellers, or any information relating thereto.

3 - All reports and information submitted by public telecommunications service providers shall be confidential and the Authority may not disclose them to third parties.

Obligation to Submit Reports:

The Authority shall submit annual reports to the Council of Ministers showing the revenues collected, explaining how they were used, and including an evaluation of the tenders conducted during the past year.

Protection of the Environment and Classified Sites:

Legal and regulatory provisions relating to the protection of the environment and classified archaeological and tourist sites must be observed in all telecommunications regulations relating to the use of public and private property and in the licences granted to service providers.

Use of Public Property:

1 - Licensed telecommunications service providers shall have the right, in order to provide these services to the public and in accordance with the conditions specified below, to enter any public property, including roads, sidewalks, sewers, and railway lines, and to construct and maintain basic infrastructure for telecommunications services on, above, under, or alongside such public property, and to modify, where necessary and with the approval of the competent administration, the form and specifications of such public property to secure the telecommunications service, provided that this does not prevent the enjoyment or use thereof for the purpose for which it is allocated.

2 - The licensed telecommunications service provider must obtain the approval of the competent administration before entering public property or carrying out works or erecting any installations thereon.

In the event that it is unable to obtain such approval for any reason whatsoever within a period of one month from the date of submitting the application in accordance with terms and conditions it deems acceptable, it must submit a written request to the Authority within a period of another month to mediate between it and the competent administration, and in the event of disagreement between the Authority and the competent administration, the matter shall be referred to the Council of Ministers to take the appropriate final decision.

3 - The conditions for the use of public property, the procedures to which applications for a licence for use are subject, and the determination of the bases for the distribution of burdens, compensations, and fees collected therefor shall be determined by a decree issued by the Council of Ministers, upon the proposal of the Minister based on a study prepared by the Authority, and after consultation with the competent administration.

Penalties:

The Authority may impose one or more of the penalties set out below, according to the gravity of the violation and the circumstances of each case:

1 - Amending the conditions of the licence or imposing new conditions on the licence in a manner that ensures the removal of the violation and the enforcement of the provisions of this Law.

2 - Suspending the licence for a specified period or revoking it permanently, and depriving the violator of obtaining any temporary or permanent licence, upon the repetition of the violation or the commission of a grave violation which shall be within the discretion of the Authority to assess.

3 - Imposing a fine which shall be within the discretion of the Authority to assess in the light of the gravity of the violation or its repetition, provided that upon imposing the fine, consideration is given to the assets of the violating natural or legal person stated in the balance sheet, the value of the equipment and installations used, and the revenues estimated to be realised by reason of the violation, provided that the fine shall not exceed one quarter (1/4) of the total value of the assets of the person stated in his balance sheet. The Authority shall have the right to impose an additional fine for each day of delay in removing a continuing violation.

4 - The Ministry of Finance shall undertake the collection of the amount of the prescribed fines.

Judicial Prosecution:

The measures taken by the Authority shall not preclude criminal prosecution before the competent court if the violation constitutes an offence punishable under the provisions of the laws in force, unless the offence constitutes an infringement upon the right of a third party and a settlement has been reached in respect thereof pursuant to an amicable resolution sponsored by the Authority. If the competent court decides to confiscate the installations or equipment used in the violation, the confiscation shall be deemed to be in favour of the Authority and they shall be sold by public auction for the benefit of the Treasury.

Dispute Resolution:

1 - The Authority shall adjudicate, on the basis of complaints submitted to it, disputes existing between telecommunications service providers, or those existing between them and their subscribers or the beneficiaries of their services, and the provisions of Articles 41 and 42 shall be observed in attempting to reach an amicable resolution and respecting the rights of the defence when adjudicating the dispute.

2 - Decisions of the Authority adjudicating the dispute shall be subject to appeal before the competent Civil Court of Appeal to adjudicate the subject matter of the dispute. Decisions of the Court of Appeal shall not be subject to any ordinary or extraordinary means of recourse.

3 - The Authority shall retain the power to issue a formal notice or an invitation to reach an amicable resolution or to impose the appropriate penalty, in accordance with the provisions of the preceding Articles, if it appears to it during the examination of the complaint that a violation of the conditions of the licence or of the provisions of this Law and the regulations issued in application thereof has occurred.

Incorporation of the Company:

1 - There shall be incorporated by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister, a joint-stock company subject to the provisions of the Code of Commerce with the exception of Article 78 thereof and in all matters not provided for by this Law, named "Liban Telecom", the object of which is to provide telecommunications services in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

2 - The decree shall determine the capital of the Company, which may be in a foreign currency, and shall approve its articles of association, provided that consideration is given to the fact that the ownership of the shares of the Company shall revert in full upon incorporation to the Lebanese State, which shall remain the sole shareholder until the Company is privatised wholly or partially.

3 - The value of the assets, holdings, liabilities and ongoing works the ownership or usufruct of which it is decided to transfer from the Ministry to the Company shall be assessed by a financial firm or an international accounting firm appointed by the Council of Ministers following a call for tenders in accordance with the rules. This procedure shall take the place of the verification procedure provided for in Article 86 of the Code of Commerce.

4 - The shares of the Company must be and shall always remain registered shares. Notwithstanding any other provision, the shares of the Company, including the shares representing contributions in kind, shall be negotiable on the Beirut Stock Exchange immediately.

5 - The board of directors of the Company shall be composed, so long as the shares of the Company are wholly owned by the Lebanese State, of a chairman and members appointed by the Council of Ministers.

Whereas after partial or total privatisation, the members of the board of directors shall be selected by the general assembly without being bound by the nationality requirement provided for in Article 144 of the Code of Commerce, provided that the State shall be represented throughout the duration of its participation in the capital of the Company by a number of members proportional to such participation named by the Council of Ministers, provided that the number shall not be less than three.

6 - Upon its incorporation and prior to offering its shares for privatisation, the Company shall be exempted from notary public fees accruing to the State and registration fees in the Commercial Register, including the fees accruing to the Judges' Mutual Fund and the Bar Association, and the stamp duty on capital, and its contributions in kind shall be exempted from all transfer fees.

7- The Company shall appoint a principal statutory auditor for a period of three years, and shall be exempted from the obligation to appoint an additional statutory auditor.

Granting of the Licence to the Company and the Temporary Exclusive Right

1 - The Company shall be granted a licence for a period of twenty years to provide the following telecommunications services:

a - Basic telephone service.

b - Public international voice service.

c - Local and international telex and telegraph service.

d - Cellular telephone service.

e - Local leased line service.

f- International leased line service.

g- Telecommunications offices and public telephones.

h - Emergency telecommunications service.

i - Directory enquiry and telephone directory service.

j - Any other services that the Authority finds to serve the public interest.

2 - The licence granted to the Company may include an exclusive right to provide any of the services mentioned in items (a), (b) and (c) of the preceding paragraph, for a period not exceeding five years from the date of establishment of the Company.

3 - The Authority may grant a non-exclusive licence to any licence applicant for the purpose of providing a service covered by the exclusive right of the Company, if the Company fails to provide such service in one or more areas, after serving it with a written formal notice of a period of not less than sixty days.

Privatisation Procedures :

The Government may, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers and within a maximum period of two years from the date of establishment of the Company, sell a percentage not exceeding forty per cent (40%) of the shares of the Company to a private sector investor enjoying experience, specialisation and reputation in the field of telecommunications, by way of an international tender and in accordance with tender specifications drawn up by the Higher Council for Privatisation upon the proposal of the Minister and issued by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.

The investor who wins the tender shall be called the Strategic Partner, and this Strategic Partner shall undertake the management of the Company so long as he remains the owner of at least half of the shares which he originally purchased and complies with the obligations specified in the tender specifications, and so long as the Lebanese State remains the owner of the majority of the shares of the Company.

The Council of Ministers shall determine, upon the proposal of the Minister, the dates on which the other shares owned by the Lebanese State are offered to private sector investors, and shall determine on the same occasion the percentage of the shares offered, the price per share and the manner of offering.

National Security for the Council of Ministers:

Upon the occurrence of events likely to affect national security, to request telecommunications service providers to give preference and priority to telecommunications conducted by the security agencies, and the civil agencies placed at their disposal.

Treatment of Valid Licences:

1 - Licences granted prior to the date of issuance of this Law for the provision of telecommunications services shall remain valid ipso jure for a maximum period of one year commencing from the date of its entry into force. The provisions of this paragraph shall not cover the two mobile telephone companies currently operating in Lebanon.

2 - Applications for obtaining licences pending before the Ministry on the date of entry into force of this Law shall be transferred to the Authority immediately upon its formation, and no licence shall be granted in respect thereof except after verifying the fulfilment of the conditions imposed pursuant to the provisions of this Law and after the Authority commences its work in accordance with the provisions of its internal regulations.

3 - Persons who contracted with the Ministry to provide telecommunications services that have become subject to licensing by virtue of this Law may continue to provide the services until the expiry of the term of the contract.

Status of Civil Servants, Wage-Earners, Contracted Personnel and Employees at the Ministry and Ogero:

First: The Transitional Phase:

1 - Within a period of three months from the date of publication of this Law in the Official Gazette, the Ministry shall procure the issuance of the regulatory decrees pertaining to it and determining its cadres, and the civil servants and workers at the Ministry and Ogero whom it needs and who fulfil the statutory conditions shall be attached and transferred to the new cadres in accordance with the provisions stipulated by the said regulatory decrees.

2 - As for the Authority and the Company, within a period of three months from the appointment of their respective boards, the conditions for selecting the needs of each of them for the civil servants of the Ministry and the other workers therein and in Ogero shall be determined in coordination with the Minister of Telecommunications, provided that the status of the concerned parties is settled in accordance with the provisions mentioned in Paragraph - Second - of this Article.

3 - Any of the civil servants and workers in the Ministry and in Ogero may request the termination of his service within a period commencing from the date of publication of this Law in the Official Gazette and ending six months after the date of appointment of the managements of the Authority and the Company, and the civil servant or worker whose resignation is duly accepted in this case shall be granted an additional indemnity equivalent to the total of his salaries and allowances for thirty months, provided that it is not less than thirty million Lebanese Pounds, if more than five years have elapsed in his service.

Whereas if the period of five years has not elapsed for him, he shall be granted an additional indemnity equivalent to the salary of two months for each year of service, provided that it is not less than /30 million L.L./ thirty million Lebanese Pounds and does not exceed /50 million L.L. fifty million Lebanese Pounds.

A request for resignation may not be revoked after its registration with the competent administration.

Second: Settlement of the Status of Civil Servants and Workers:

The status of the civil servants of the Ministry of Telecommunications and the other workers therein and the status of the workers in the Ogero Authority shall be settled in accordance with the following:

A - With respect to the civil servants of the Ministry:

1 - In the event of remaining in the new cadre of the Ministry, their functional status shall remain as it is, particularly with respect to their salaries and their ranks.

2 - In the event of their selection to work in the Authority, they shall be placed outside the cadre and attached to it in accordance with the provisions relating to placement outside the cadre stipulated in the Civil Servants Regulations and without the need for its annual renewal, provided that the value of their allowances is not less than the value of the salaries that they were previously receiving.

3 - In the event that the civil servant chooses to join the Company and the Company approves thereof, his rights shall be liquidated in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

And a contract shall be drawn up for him in accordance with the regulations adopted by the Company.

4 - The provisions mentioned in Item (Second) shall apply to the civil servants and workers in the Directorate General of Posts.

Third: In Other Cases:

A - They shall be transferred to posts in the cadres of the public administrations in accordance with the provisions of the Civil Servants Regulations that govern transfer from one cadre to another.

- As for those whom it is not possible to transfer, they shall be placed at the disposal of the Ministry and shall continue to receive their salaries, their allowances and their step advancement until they reach the statutory age, and it shall be for the Council of Ministers or the competent ministers, at any time, to assign them to any mission in the public administrations or public institutions, and they shall receive their salaries in this case from the entity with which they are assigned to work, provided that the Civil Service Board works during this period to transfer them to vacant posts in the cadres of the public administrations in accordance with the provisions of the Civil Servants Regulations, whenever that is possible.

B - With respect to the wage-earners and contracted personnel in the Ministry and the employees and contracted personnel in Ogero:

1 - In the event that they are selected to work in the Authority and they accept that, their previous services with the National Social Security Fund shall be combined with their subsequent services. Provided that the value of their monthly allowances is not less than the value of the wages and allowances that they were receiving.

2 - Whereas in the event that they are selected by the Company to work for it and they accept that, the provisions of the laws in force shall apply to them.

3 - In other cases, the redundancy provisions in force on the date of issuance of this Law shall apply to them.

Transfer of Functions and Assets of the Ministry and Ogero:

1 - All the functions and powers stipulated in this Law which were assumed by the Ministry or were entrusted to Ogero shall be transferred to each of the management of the Authority after the Authority commences its work in accordance with the provisions of its internal regulations and to the Company after the completion of the operations of its incorporation.

2 - Where necessary, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Telecommunications and Finance, the assets and holdings that are decided to be declassified from the public domain, and all the assets and holdings that are decided to be transferred from the ownership of the Ministry and Ogero to the Authority, shall be determined.

3 - After the completion of the liquidation of the wage-earners and contracted personnel at Ogero and the transfer of the functions and powers that were entrusted to it and the transfer of its assets and holdings, Ogero shall be dissolved pursuant to a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.
All legal and regulatory provisions in force prior to the entry into force of this Law shall remain in effect until the Law is implemented.
The details of the application of the provisions of this Law shall be determined, where necessary, by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the competent Minister.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The following provisions shall apply to the appointment of teachers in the kindergarten and basic education cycles or to contracting with them:

1- Appointment shall be made by decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Education and Higher Education within the jurisdiction of the district in which the candidate chose to work and within the limits of the vacant posts in the schools of the district.

- The procedures and contents of contracting for hourly teaching in the schools of the kindergarten and basic education cycles shall be determined by a decree issued in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Education and Higher Education and after consulting the opinion of the Civil Service Board.

- Contracting for hourly teaching in the schools of the kindergarten and basic education cycles shall take place pursuant to an agreement contract for an academic year with the Ministry of Education and Higher Education.

2- A teacher may be transferred within the jurisdiction of the district by a reasoned decision of the Minister of Education and Higher Education after the lapse of four years from his appointment or contracting with him in the school, and he may also be transferred from the district to another district in the same governorate by a reasoned decision of the Minister of Education and Higher Education after the lapse of at least six years from his appointment or contracting with him in the district from which he is transferred.

Transfer from one governorate to another governorate shall not be permissible except by a reasoned decision of the Minister of Education and Higher Education, provided that the person concerned has spent at least seven years in the schools of the governorate from which he is transferred.

3- Either spouse may, after his appointment to the permanent cadre, request his transfer to the district in which he resides with his spouse within a maximum of three months from the date of marriage.

As for a person who is married upon his appointment to the permanent cadre, the provisions of Clause (2) above shall apply to him regarding transfer.

Either spouse appointed to the permanent cadre before the effective date of this Law may request his transfer to the district in which he resides with his spouse within three months from the effective date of this Law, provided that approval is granted according to need.

4- All other legal provisions relating to the general and special conditions of employment and to the conditions of contracting for the post of teacher in the kindergarten and basic education cycles that do not conflict with or contravene the clauses mentioned above shall remain in force.

Subject to the provisions of this Law, it shall in no case be permissible to appoint or contract for the post of teacher except from among holders of a teaching licence or a recognised university degree.

1- Notwithstanding any other text, the Civil Service Board shall conduct, for one time only, a competitive examination restricted to hourly contracted teachers for teaching in the kindergarten and basic education cycles in public schools in accordance with the number specified in the table annexed to this Law, which shall be deemed an integral part thereof.

2- In order to participate in the competitive examination, the contracted teacher must fulfil the general and special conditions of employment provided for in the laws and regulations in force, except for the age requirement, and the contracted teacher must have been contracted with in accordance with the proper procedures.

3- The announcement of the successful candidates in the competitive examination shall be made on the basis of the district, provided that holders of teaching licences or university degrees undergo preparation courses conducted by the Faculty of Pedagogy at the Lebanese University in accordance with special regulations laid down by the Faculty specifying the programmes of the courses, their subjects, the examination procedures and the passing grades, provided that the duration of each of these courses is not less than one year. These persons shall remain probationary until the end of the courses, and those among them who pass shall be appointed to the permanent cadre in the post of teacher in the kindergarten and basic education cycles, and those among them who fail shall be deemed dismissed from service.

As for the successful candidates who do not hold teaching licences or university degrees, they shall undergo a two-year training course in the Teacher Training Colleges, in accordance with special regulations prepared by the Center for Educational Research and Development specifying the programme of the course, its subjects, the examination procedures and the passing grades; those among them who pass shall be appointed to the permanent cadre in the post of teacher in the kindergarten and basic education cycles, and those among them who fail shall be deemed dismissed from service.

4- Appointment shall be mandatory within the district in whose jurisdiction the candidate chose to work, and due regard shall be given to assigning the teacher to the school in which he was working in the last year of his contract.

5- The successful contracted teachers shall be deemed appointed to the post of probationary teacher at the lowest grade, and upon their confirmation in the permanent cadre they shall benefit from one advancement step for every three years of actual service under contract, and a year of service shall be calculated on the basis that the number of actual teaching hours under contract is not less than fifteen hours per week.

6- The provisions provided for in Clause (2) of Article One above shall apply to the transfer of those appointed pursuant to the provisions of this Article.

Where necessary, the details of application of the provisions of this Law shall be determined by decrees issued in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Education and Higher Education.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Sudden injuries resulting from an external factor, which befall an employee bound by an employment contract within the meaning of Article 624, first paragraph, of the Code of Obligations and Contracts, by reason of the performance of the said contract or on the occasion of the performance of this contract, shall be subject to the provisions of this Legislative Decree.

The employee referred to in the preceding Article shall not be entitled to invoke any legal text other than the provisions of this Legislative Decree by reason of the injury which he sustains during work or on the occasion thereof.

If the accident causes the employee a permanent total incapacity, and his wage does not exceed the official minimum wage, he shall be entitled to receive compensation equivalent to:

/800/ days of his average wage, if his age is less than 35 years.

/700/ days of his average wage, if his age is more than 35 years and less than 50 years.

/600/ days of his average wage, if his age is more than 50 years.

If the wage exceeds the official minimum wage, the employee shall not be entitled to receive, in addition to the compensations provided for in the first paragraph of this Article, more than:

- One quarter of these compensations for the portion of the wage that exceeds the minimum wage up to double this minimum.

- One eighth of these compensations for the portion of the wage that exceeds double the official minimum wage.

If the accident causes a permanent partial incapacity, the injured person shall be entitled to receive compensation proportionate to the loss sustained in his earning capacity. This capacity is represented by the compensation payable when the incapacity is permanent and total.

If the infirmity is mentioned in the schedule annexed to this Legislative Decree (Annex No. 1), the loss sustained by the injured employee in his earning capacity shall be equivalent to the percentage specified in the said schedule. However, if the infirmity is not mentioned in this schedule, the Labour Arbitration Council shall have the right to assess the loss sustained in the earning capacity of the injured employee, after taking into consideration the experience of the employee and his competence in work.

If the accident causes a temporary incapacity for work, the injured person shall be entitled, starting from the first day following the accident and for a maximum period of nine months, to receive without distinction between working days and days of suspension, compensation amounting to three quarters of the last daily wage. By this wage is meant the weekly wage divided by a year if the wage is weekly, the wage of fifteen days divided by twelve if the wage is paid every fifteen days, and the monthly wage divided by twenty-five if the wage is monthly.

The daily compensation shall be paid at the place and time at which payment usually takes place in the establishment, and the period between two consecutive payments may not exceed fifteen days.

If the accident leads to the death of the employee, and his wage does not exceed the official minimum wage, his heirs specified in the Law put into force by virtue of Decree No. /8496/ dated 2/8/1974 shall be entitled to compensation the maximum limit of which is the wage of /500/ days.

If the wage exceeds the official minimum wage, the heirs of the employee shall only be entitled to:

- One quarter of the compensations provided for in the first paragraph of this Article for the portion of the wage that exceeds the official minimum wage up to half of this limit.

- One eighth of the compensations provided for in the first paragraph of this Article for the portion of the wage that exceeds double the official minimum wage.

In addition to the compensation mentioned above, the employer shall bear the funeral expenses up to double the official minimum wage.

The average wage which is taken as a basis for calculating the compensations provided for in Articles 3, 4 and 6 above is the wage which the injured person received in cash or in kind on the date of the accident and in accordance with the bases specified in Article 5 of this Legislative Decree.

In no case may the average wage be less than the official minimum wage. This rule shall also apply to employees who are not subject to this limit.

Where applicable, the compensations due by virtue of this Legislative Decree shall be added to the other compensations due to employees by virtue of the Labour Code, the Social Security Law, or the other laws to which they are subject.

If it is established that the employee intentionally caused the accident which rendered him disabled and a holder of the personal disabled card, he shall not be entitled to any compensations mentioned in this Law and the employer shall be entitled to dismiss him from service in accordance with the provisions in force, provided that he shall benefit from all sickness allowances, consultations and services provided for in this Legislative Decree.

The heirs of a foreign employee shall not be entitled to claim the compensations provided for in this Legislative Decree if they were residing outside Lebanese territory on the date of the occurrence of the accident.

Foreign employees who are nationals of a State that grants Lebanese nationals in this matter the same rights as it grants to its own nationals shall be exempted from the provisions of this Article.

The injured employee or his successors in title after him shall be entitled, in addition to the action brought by them pursuant to the provisions of this Legislative Decree, to sue the persons who caused the accident, other than the employer or his heirs, in accordance with the rules of ordinary law, for compensation for the damage sustained by them as a result of the said accident.

The employer shall also be entitled, on his full responsibility and on behalf of the injured employee or his successors in title after him, to bring this action if those holding the right neglect to bring the aforementioned action. The employer shall be entitled to deduct from the compensation due from him in favour of his employee in accordance with the provisions of this Legislative Decree the compensations awarded in favour of his employee in accordance with the rules of ordinary law.

a - Every employer shall be bound to compulsorily conclude insurance contracts with an insurance company to guarantee the compensations and medical treatment provided for in this Legislative Decree.

b - If the employer does not comply with the obligation specified in the first paragraph of this Article, he shall be bound to pay a fine amounting to double the average value of the insurance premium.

The employee and his successors in title after him shall be entitled to sue the employer and the insurance company together for the compensations due by virtue of the provisions of this Legislative Decree.

The insuring company which has paid the compensation to the employee shall be subrogated to the rights of the employer in the exercise of his rights. In the event of declaration of bankruptcy of the employer, the amounts due from the insuring company shall not be included in the calculation of the assets of the bankruptcy estate.

The debts of the employee injured in a work accident or of his successors in title after him are secured by a special privilege over the totality of the movable property belonging to the employer, and in addition thereto, they are also guaranteed by a compulsory mortgage over the immovable property of the employer.

It shall be for the President of the Labour Arbitration Council to determine the conditions of the nature of the mortgage, its contents and the guaranteed compensations, either ex officio or upon the request of the employee or his successors in title after him.

The effects of the precautionary mortgage referred to above shall remain in force until the issuance of a final decision in the dispute, or until a judicial settlement is reached in respect thereof in accordance with what is provided for in Article 30 of this Legislative Decree.

The provisions of this Article shall not apply to immovable property belonging to the public domain.

Temporary compensation is assignable in favour of third parties. It is also subject to attachment within the rates and conditions applicable to the wages of employees.

Compensation for permanent incapacity or death may not be assigned except within the limit of one quarter of its value, in settlement of debts resulting from foodstuffs. As for debts relating to medical, pharmaceutical, hospitalisation or funeral expenses, they shall not be subject to attachment or assignment.

The general and special measures relating to safety, prevention, health, and first aid that must be applied to the enterprises subject to the provisions of this Legislative Decree shall be determined by decisions issued by the Minister of Labour and Social Affairs, after consulting the Ministry of Public Health, according to the nature, activity, and number of employees working in each of these enterprises.

The employer shall bear, regardless of the duration of the employee's interruption from work due to the accident sustained by reason or on the occasion of work, all medical, surgical, and pharmaceutical expenses, including hospital expenses.

The employer shall also bear the cost of fitting, maintaining, and renewing prosthetic appliances and other medical and surgical appliances necessary for the treatment and recovery of the injured employee.
Physicians, pharmacists, and hospital owners shall have the right to sue the employer directly in respect of the debts owed to them for the costs of the employee's injury.

An employee shall have the right to choose his physician himself. In this case, the employer shall only be liable for the medical and surgical expenses up to the amount determined by the Labour Arbitration Council, in accordance with a tariff established by the Director General of the Ministry of Public Health.

If the injured employee is admitted to a hospital, the expenses to which the employer is bound may not exceed the tariff specified in the agreements concluded by the Ministry of Public Health with such hospitals, plus a maximum addition of 30% thereon.

The Labour Arbitration Council shall determine the cost of the appliances of instruments and medical appliances in the event of a dispute arising between the two parties in respect thereof.

If the employee refuses to submit to the treatment prescribed by the attending physician, he shall forfeit every right to the portion of the damage that may result from the aggravation of his condition due to such refusal.

If the employer has not chosen the attending physician himself, he shall have the right, during the treatment by the latter, to request the President of the Labour Arbitration Council to appoint a physician at his own expense to examine the condition of the employee, and the said physician shall have the right to visit the employee at any time he wishes in the presence of the attending physician, after the latter has been notified of the visit two days prior to its occurrence.

If the employee refuses the visit referred to in this Article, the employer shall have the right, after referring the matter to the President of the Labour Arbitration Council, to suspend the payment of the temporary compensation.

The attending physician must provide the employee with a medical report stating the employee's state of health and the permanent total or partial disability resulting to him from the accident, as well as the appliances that must be used in respect of the damaged limbs.

Each of the two parties shall have the right to object to the contents of the medical report referred to in the preceding Article before the Labour Arbitration Council within five days from the date of being notified of the said report.

Every employer or his representative must declare every work accident that befalls his employee. The declaration shall be submitted to the registry of the competent Labour Arbitration Council in the region in which the accident occurred, within a period of three days from the date of its occurrence, and shall be recorded in a special register prepared for this purpose. The declaration must state:

- The name of the injured employee, his place of residence, his last wage, and his nationality.

- The name of the employer and his place of residence.

- The place where the accident occurred.

- The nature, character, and circumstances of the injury.

A medical certificate shall be attached to the declaration stating the condition of the injured employee, the expected consequences of the injury, and the date on which a final report thereon may be given.

The employee shall be required to inform the registry of the Labour Arbitration Council of the consequences of the injury sustained by him by virtue of a medical report which shall be recorded in the special register referred to in the preceding Article.

The employee or his representative shall also be required to notify the employer of a copy of the said medical report.

If the employer alleges that the employee caused the accident intentionally or that the accident resulted from gross misconduct committed by the employee, or if the employee alleges that the accident resulted from the fault or negligence of the employer or the person in charge of management, the President of the Labour Arbitration Council in the region in which the accident occurred shall conduct an investigation into the said accident at the place of its occurrence and in the presence of the two parties or their representatives.

He shall be required to proceed to the employee if the latter is unable to appear before him due to his state of health.

The President of the Labour Arbitration Council must conclude the investigation within a maximum period of ten days from the date of submission of the allegation referred to in the preceding Article.

The President of the Labour Arbitration Council shall notify the two parties of the decision concluding the investigation within a period of 24 hours from the date of issuance of the decision.

Each of them shall have the right to receive a copy thereof free of any fee.

The Labour Arbitration Council in the region in which the accident occurred shall hear all disputes arising from the application of the provisions of this Legislative Decree.

The said Council must adjudicate upon these disputes within a period not exceeding six months.
The procedures and rules of the means of recourse provided for in the Law promulgated on 21 October 1980 shall apply to work accident disputes.

If a settlement takes place between the parties in a dispute resulting from the application of the provisions of this Legislative Decree and the Labour Arbitration Council is requested to record this settlement by a judicial decision, the Council shall be required to state in its decision, on pain of absolute nullity, the basic wage and the permanent disability resulting to the employee from the accident, and, where applicable, the name of the insurance company guaranteeing the accident, and that the latter was subrogated to the employer in his obligations towards the employee, whereupon the latter shall be barred from making any claim against the employer relating to the said accident.

The action for compensation provided for in this Legislative Decree shall lapse upon the expiration of one year from the date of the occurrence of the accident, or the conclusion of the investigation therein in accordance with the provisions of Articles 26 and 27 above, or the cessation of the payment of the temporary compensation.

Every violation of the contents of the decisions provided for in Article 16 of this Legislative Decree, as well as every violation of the provisions of Article 24 thereof, shall be referred to the competent courts and its perpetrator shall be punished by a fine ranging between /500/ L.L. and /5000/ L.L. and by imprisonment from one month to three months, or by either of these two penalties, and the penalty shall be doubled in the event of recidivism.

Every employer who violates the contents of this Article of this Legislative Decree shall be sentenced by the Labour Arbitration Council to a fine pursuant to an action brought by any employee or any trade union in the company or establishment or any other competent authority. The amount of this fine shall be set at a sum ranging between six (6) and ten (10) times the official minimum wage."

Whoever refuses or delays without a legitimate excuse the execution of a judgment rendered against him in accordance with the provisions of this Legislative Decree shall be subject to the provisions of Article 7 of the Law promulgated on 21 October of the year 1980.

The provisions of Legislative Decree No. 25 ET promulgated on 4 May 1943 are hereby repealed, and all legal or regulatory texts that conflict with the provisions of this Legislative Decree or are inconsistent with its contents are also repealed.
This Legislative Decree shall enter into force ten days after the date of its publication in the Official Gazette.
An association is a legal person founded by at least three persons who permanently pool their knowledge, their activity, or material means for a purpose other than earning or sharing profit.

The formation of associations is one of the constitutional rights of the Lebanese, and the validity of their formation is subject to the provisions of this Legislative Decree and the general laws in force.

The establishment of an association requires the submission of its articles of association signed by the founders, including its name, registered office, objectives, and resources, and specifying the body that manages and represents it, its internal structures, the conditions for selecting its members and bodies, the manner of joining it, the rules followed for amending its articles of association, and the conditions for its dissolution and the liquidation of its assets.

The formation of associations is prohibited in the following cases: 1- If they aim at or lead to violating the Constitution or the laws or regulations in force, or to disrupting constitutional life or public liberties. 2- If they are contrary to public morals or public order, such as aiming at or leading to undermining national unity, disturbing security, or creating division among the elements of the people, religions, or sects. 3- If their activity is contrary to their bylaws. 4- If they are secret. They shall be deemed secret if they are formed in violation of the provisions of Article 337 of the Penal Code or in violation of the provisions of this Legislative Decree. 5- If they bear, whether with respect to their formation, their activity, or the designation of their departments, or with respect to the training of their members, their uniform, their equipment, or their insignia, the character of military or paramilitary formations, whether independent or affiliated with an association. 6- If their founding members or the members of their administrative board, or some of them, or the majority of their members espouse principles that aim at or lead to the matters provided for in items one and two of this Article.
The objective of the association shall be determined on the basis of its bylaws and in the light of the actual activity it carries out.
Non-political associations are those that have no political objectives and do not resort to political means to achieve their objective.
Any person who founds or joins a non-political association must have completed twenty-one years of age, enjoy his civil rights, and not have been convicted of a felony or an infamous misdemeanour.

The formation of non-political associations is subject to a prior licence granted by a decision of the Minister of Interior. If the objective of the association falls within the scope of activity of other ministries, the licence shall not be granted except after the approval of the competent minister. The procedures to be followed for granting the licence shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior.

The competent authority must verify that the formation of the association does not violate the law, particularly with respect to what is stated in the fourth Article of this Legislative Decree. The licence shall be granted within a maximum period of three months from the date of submission of the application, and if this period expires and the licence has not been granted, the silence of the Administration shall be deemed a refusal.

An abstract containing the licence, the name of the association, its objectives, its address or the seat of its management, and its branches shall be published in the Official Gazette at the expense of the founders within one month at most from the date of receipt of the licence.

Every amendment or alteration occurring to the association's articles of association and internal bylaws pursuant to which it obtained the licence, or to its administrative board, the seat of its management, its branches, its works, or the rest of its activities must be notified to the competent authority in order to obtain mandatory approval. The alteration or amendment shall not be deemed effective except from the date of granting the approval or the lapse of two months from its declaration, and the granting of this approval is subject to the procedures set forth in this Legislative Decree.
The establishment of each branch of the association is subject to the conditions and procedures to which the establishment of the association itself is subject.

The association enjoys the right to collect subscriptions and to own and manage immovable property, and it has the right to accept gifts, bequests, and donations provided that they are not coupled with conditions the fulfilment of which leads to violating the bylaws of the association or the laws and regulations.
The association must confine its activity to the works for which it was established, and non-political associations are prohibited from engaging in politics.

The Ministry of Interior has the right of supervision over associations from the financial and administrative aspects; the procedures of such supervision shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior.

An association shall be dissolved if it commits a grave violation of its bylaws or of the laws, or if it disturbs public order or public security, or if it allocates its funds or a part thereof for other than the objective for which it was established. In these cases, dissolution shall be decided by a decree issued in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior. The civil courts shall hear violations arising between the association and one of its members, and they may decide upon dissolution if the reasons so require. The Administration must hear the defence of the association intended to be dissolved before taking any decision of dissolution.

In urgent circumstances, any association whose activity is contrary to the requirements of security may, by a decree issued in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior, be suspended from operating temporarily and for a period not exceeding one year.

The funds belonging to an association that has been dissolved compulsorily or voluntarily shall be distributed in accordance with the provisions of its bylaws, and failing that, by a decision of the Minister of Interior after the approval of the Council of Ministers ordering the distribution of those funds to associations having a similar objective. As for associations that are dissolved for violating the fourth Article, all their funds shall be confiscated and distributed to associations of public utility designated by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior.

A member of an association has the right to withdraw from it at any time whatsoever, provided that he shall be bound to fulfil the annual financial obligation specified in the bylaws of the association which has fallen due. Any provision in the bylaws of the association that restricts the freedom of voluntary withdrawal contrary to the content of this Article shall be rejected.

An association shall be deemed foreign: 1- Every association whose head office is outside Lebanon or which is a branch of a foreign association abroad 2- Every association that is de facto affiliated with an association existing outside Lebanon. 3- Every association that is de facto managed by foreigners or in which at least one quarter of the members of its board of directors are foreigners.

No foreign association may be established or commence its operations in Lebanon except pursuant to a prior licence granted by a decree issued in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior.

A foreign association licensed in accordance with the provisions of the preceding Article may not have any branch or establishment in Lebanon except by a licence granted by a decree issued in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior, nor does it have the right to amend its bylaws or some of the provisions thereof unless it is authorised to do so by a decree issued in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior.
A Lebanese association that transforms into a foreign association must cease operating until the licence for it is issued in accordance with the provisions of this Legislative Decree.
The licence may be granted on a temporary basis and be subject to periodic renewal. A temporary licence may be revoked at any time.

Foreign associations whose licence is refused or revoked are prohibited from carrying out any work or activity, and their funds shall be liquidated in accordance with the provisions of Article 18 of this Legislative Decree.
Foreign associations may acquire immovable property within the regulations and laws in force.

Representatives of the Ministry of the Interior holding a special authorisation shall be entitled to enter the headquarters of foreign associations or their branches or the various institutions affiliated with them. Foreign associations shall annually notify the General Directorate of General Security of a detailed list of the names of their affiliated members.

The Ministry of the Interior shall be entitled to request foreign associations to provide all information capable of ensuring supervision over them, and such associations shall comply with the request within a maximum time limit of one month from their receipt of the request, failing which they shall be served notice and shall respond to the notice within a time limit of fifteen days from the date of their receipt of the notice. Should they fail to comply with the content of the notice, they shall be dissolved by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior.
The liquidation of the property of foreign associations shall take place in accordance with the provisions of Article 18 of this Legislative Decree.
The provisions set forth in this Legislative Decree regarding ordinary associations shall apply to foreign associations in all that does not conflict with this Part.
The Government may, by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers, upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior, regulate the matters relating to the union of associations.
Every association having a political objective shall be considered a political party.
Political parties may not be founded except by a prior licence granted by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior.

Any person who founds one of the political parties shall be required to have completed twenty-five years of age, to enjoy his civil rights, and not to have been convicted of a felony or an infamous misdemeanour. As for those affiliated with them, they must have completed twenty-one years of their age.
Persons convicted of an offence relating to public safety or to the security of the State shall be prohibited from founding political parties, or joining them.

Joining political parties shall be prohibited for judges, military personnel in the Army, the Internal Security Forces and General Security, civil servants, employees, wage-earners and contractors in the administrations of the public sector and municipalities, as well as civilian civil servants, employees, wage-earners and contractors in the Army, the Internal Security Forces and General Security.
Pupils and students shall be prohibited from carrying out any political activity in educational institutions.
Non-Lebanese may not found political parties in Lebanon or join them.

A political party may not be founded with a name denoting a race or a denomination, nor may membership in the party be restricted to a race, a sect, or the inhabitants of a specific region in a manner that practically leads thereto.

A political party proven to have a link with a non-Lebanese party may not be founded. The cases excluded from the prohibition prescribed in the preceding paragraph shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior.
A political party shall deposit its funds in a bank in the name of the party.

All provisions set forth in this Legislative Decree regarding non-political associations shall apply to political parties in all that does not conflict with the provisions of this Part, and the provisions of Articles 16 and 17 of this Legislative Decree shall apply to them in particular.

Founders of associations and their administrative bodies shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to two years and by a fine from one thousand to ten thousand pounds, or by either of these two penalties, in the cases set out in Article Four of this Legislative Decree. As for secret associations, the penalties provided for in the Penal Code shall apply to them.

Subject to the provisions of the draft law put into effect by Decree No. 10830 dated 9/10/1962, any person who works to maintain an association whose dissolution has been decided, or to assist it in continuing its work or holding its meetings, or who makes his premises a centre for the members of a dissolved association, shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to two years and by a fine from one thousand to ten thousand pounds. The courts may, in addition thereto, apply the provisions of the Penal Code.
The penalties set forth in the Penal Code and other laws in force shall apply to every offence for which no special penalty is set forth in this Legislative Decree.

Every violation of the provisions of this Legislative Decree for which no express provision is set forth in this Legislative Decree or in any other legal text shall subject its perpetrator to punishment by imprisonment from one month to six months and by a fine from one thousand to five thousand, or by either of these two penalties.

This Legislative Decree shall not apply to bodies, groupings, syndicates, chambers of commerce and industry, and associations governed by special laws, except within the limits where its provisions do not conflict with such laws.

Non-political associations existing on the date of entry into force of this Legislative Decree shall be granted a time limit of six months, and political parties a time limit of three months, to regularise their status in accordance with its provisions, failing which they shall be considered dissolved ipso jure, and the dissolution shall be declared by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior.

All bodies and political parties governed by this Legislative Decree shall be subject to the permanent supervision of the Ministry of the Interior, and they shall authenticate their books of accounts before the Notary Public. The Ministry of the Interior may inspect these books at any time, and it may, directly or through the Ministry of Finance, inspect the bank accounts of political parties after procuring a decree in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministry itself. The details of the application of the supervision entrusted to the Ministries of the Interior and of Finance shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of the Interior and of Finance.

Associations that carry out activities capable of causing damage to third parties shall conclude insurance against accidents. The cases requiring insurance shall be regulated by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior.

Associations dissolved by a decision of their bodies or due to the cessation of the purpose for which they were formed, and in general every association dissolved at a date prior to the entry into force of this Legislative Decree without its dissolution having the character of a penalty, shall be entitled to request the re-licensing thereof within a time limit of six months from the date of entry into force of this Legislative Decree, and the licence shall be granted in accordance with the provisions thereof.

Associations dissolved at a date prior to the issuance of this Legislative Decree by a judicial or administrative decision and the decision of dissolution of which is characterised as having the character of a penalty, shall be entitled to request the re-licensing thereof after the lapse of ten years from the decision of dissolution, and any administrative act or receipt of notification granted thereto prior to the lapse of this period shall be deemed non-existent. The aforementioned associations shall be granted a period of one month after the expiry of the said ten-year time limit in order to request the re-licensing thereof. The licence shall be granted by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior.
The Code of Obligations and the Penalty shall apply to the activities of associations in all that does not conflict with the provisions of this Legislative Decree.

All provisions contrary to the provisions of this Legislative Decree or inconsistent with its content are hereby repealed, and the details of application of this Legislative Decree shall be determined by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers.
This Legislative Decree shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

1- Whoever intentionally evades, or attempts to evade, and whoever assists another in evading the payment of any tax or duty or any part thereof, by omitting to mention any income of the incomes subject to any of the taxes and duties, or by drawing up, signing, or submitting incomplete or false declarations, or by giving incomplete or false information in response to questions directed to him by the Administration, or by preparing, permitting the preparation of, or concealing forged registers or entries, or by resorting to any means of fraud and deception, shall be punished for each of these offences by a fine ranging between one million pounds and ten million pounds or by imprisonment from six months to one year. In the event of recidivism, both penalties shall be imposed together upon the offender. In all cases, the offender shall be required to pay twenty times the concealed, incomplete, or incorrect tax or duty.

2- Whoever forges or permits the forgery of registers, accounts, or entries in order to evade or assist another in evading the payment of a tax or duty or any part thereof shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years or by a fine ranging between three million pounds and thirty million pounds. In the event of recidivism, both penalties shall be imposed together upon the offender. In all cases, the offender shall be required to pay thirty times the concealed, incomplete, or incorrect tax or duty.

3- The first paragraph shall apply to whoever intentionally commits, attempts to commit, or assists another in committing the acts set forth in the said paragraph

Subject to the time limits specified in special texts, whoever intentionally defaults or delays in paying the full value of the taxes and duties which he withheld from third parties for the account of the Treasury, or delays in paying revenues and profit shares accruing to the State for a period exceeding one month despite being given formal notice, shall be punished by a fine ranging between one million pounds and twenty million pounds

or by imprisonment from three months to one year, and in the event of recidivism, both penalties shall be imposed together.

In all cases, the offender shall be required to pay twenty times the tax or duty that was not paid".

Article 3: Criminal prosecution shall be instituted either ex officio by the Financial Public Prosecution or through it upon the request of the Director General of Finance, and prescription shall be interrupted upon the mere commencement of prosecution.
Article 4: Amended Article 108, and paragraphs 2 and 3 of Article 110 of Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12/6/1959 are hereby repealed.
Article 5: This Legislative Decree shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The Court of Appeal of Bekaa shall hold its sittings in Baalbek to determine actions issuing from the Court of First Instance in the two districts of Baalbek and Hermel. Other Courts of Appeal may be authorised to hold their sittings outside their seat by a decree adopted after consulting the Supreme Judicial Council upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice.

Business shall be distributed among the chambers within a single Court of Appeal by a decision of the Minister of Justice after the approval of the Supreme Judicial Council, upon the proposal of the First President of that court.

The First President of the Court of Appeal shall oversee the proper conduct of business in the departments subordinate to him and the normal dispatch of business.

Where necessary, he shall apprise the President of the Supreme Judicial Council of the difficulties encountered by him in this regard and shall also inform him of

important emergent matters.

Where one of the judges belonging to a single Court of Appeal, whether from among the judges of the Courts of First Instance or of the Court of Appeal itself or from among the judges of the Public Prosecution or the investigating judges, is unable to perform his duties for any reason, the First President of the Court of Appeal may assign a judge from among the judges subordinate to him to carry out the duties of the said judge. The Minister of Justice may decide such delegations as necessity requires after the approval of the Supreme Judicial Council.

Judicial duty rosters during the judicial recess shall be organised by a decision adopted by the First President of the Court of Appeal after seeking the opinion of the Public Prosecutor at that court, in respect of the judges of the Public Prosecution and of the investigation.

At each Court of Appeal there shall be a Public Prosecution presided over by a Public Prosecutor. The Public Prosecutor shall direct the affairs of the Public Prosecution and supervise its staff and the proper conduct of work therein.

At the seat and within the territorial jurisdiction of each Court of Appeal there shall be an Investigation Department composed of a First Investigating Judge and one or more investigating judges. The First Investigating Judge shall supervise the proper conduct of work in his department.
At the head of the judicial courts is a supreme court, which is the Court of Cassation, and its seat is Beirut.

The Court of Cassation shall be composed of chambers the number of which, together with its judges and the judges of the Public Prosecution thereat, shall be fixed in a third schedule annexed to this Legislative Decree. Each chamber shall be composed of a President and two Associate Judges.

The Court of Cassation shall be presided over by a First President appointed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice.

The First President of the Court of Cassation shall exercise, in respect of the Court of Cassation, the financial and administrative powers vested by laws

and regulations in the Minister, with the exception of constitutional powers.

The First President shall distribute the business among the chambers of the Court of Cassation and may, in addition to the chamber over which he presides, preside over any of the civil or criminal chambers.

The First President shall exercise in the departments of the Court of Cassation the powers vested in the First President of the Court of Appeal pursuant to Articles

19, 20 and 21 of this Legislative Decree.

At the beginning of each judicial year, the First President shall draw up an annual report and submit it to the Supreme Judicial Council for discussion and approval, and shall then refer it to the Minister of Justice. This report shall contain an account of the state and business of the judicial courts during the past year, a reference to the important decisions delivered by the Court of Cassation, and the legislative, regulatory and administrative proposals which he deems consonant with the interest of the judiciary.

The Court of Cassation shall sit in its General Assembly in the cases provided for by law. The General Assembly of the Court of Cassation shall be composed of:

- The First President, and where he is unable to act, the Chamber President highest in grade, and where the grade is equal, the longest-serving in the judiciary, and where seniority is equal, the eldest, as President

- The Chamber Presidents as members, and the decisions of the General Assembly may only be delivered by the President and at least four members, and in the event of an equality of votes, the President shall have a casting vote.

The Public Prosecution at the Court of Cassation shall be presided over by a Public Prosecutor appointed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice.

There shall be established at the Public Prosecution of the Court of Cassation a Financial Public Prosecution subject to the authority of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation, the functions and powers of which shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice.

The authority of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation shall extend to all judges of the Public Prosecutions, and he may direct them in the conduct of public prosecution actions and, where necessary, by written instructions. The Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation shall direct the affairs of the Public Prosecution thereat and supervise its staff and the proper conduct of work therein.

The powers vested in the Appellate Public Prosecutor under the Code of Criminal Procedure shall be transferred to the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation.
