In all cases in which criminal prosecution requires an authorisation or approval from any non-judicial authority, and in the event of disagreement

between that authority and the Appellate Public Prosecution or the Government Commissioner at the Military Court, the Public Prosecutor at the Court

of Cassation shall, notwithstanding any special or general provision, have the power to make a final determination on this matter.

The Government Commissioner at the Military Court and his assistants shall be subject to the authority and supervision of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation.

The establishment and number of civilian judges at the military judiciary shall be fixed in a fourth schedule annexed to this Legislative Decree.

The number of judges attached to each of the Director General, the Cases Committee, and the Legislation and Consultations Committee in the Ministry of Justice shall be fixed in a fifth schedule annexed to this Legislative Decree.
An annual appropriation shall be provided for in the budget of the Ministry of Justice under the item of administrative supplies for furniture, printed matter and office supplies.
A judicial department is the court, chamber, section, Public Prosecution or Investigation Department, and the registry attached to each of them.

A judicial department shall be presided over by the President of the court, chamber or section, and where the registry is shared among several chambers or among several sections, the Chamber President highest in grade shall be deemed President of the judicial department, and where the grade is equal, the President or judge longest-serving in the judiciary, and where seniority is equal, the eldest. As for the departments of the Public Prosecutions, each of them shall be presided over by a Public Prosecutor, and the Investigation Departments shall each be presided over by a First Investigating Judge.

The President of the judicial department shall be responsible for the proper conduct of work in his department; he shall be the administrative head of the registry staff working therein and shall have in respect of them the powers conferred upon a Director by the regulations governing administrative staff. The President of the judicial department may assign the staff of his department to work outside official working hours if the court continues to hold its sittings.
The registry of a judicial department shall be composed of judicial assistants and bailiffs.
Judicial assistants and bailiffs shall be attached to the Supreme Judicial Council by a decision of the competent authority upon the recommendation of the President of the Supreme Judicial Council.

The Chief Clerk of the registry shall be responsible for the proper conduct of work before the President of the judicial department and shall have in respect of the registry staff the powers conferred upon a Head of Department by the regulations governing administrative staff.
Work shall be distributed among the staff of a single registry by a decision of the President of the judicial department.
The judicial vacation shall apply to the registries, and a duty roster shall be organised to ensure the continuity of work by a decision of the president of the judicial department.

Judicial judges are the judges included in the establishment of the judicial judiciary in accordance with the table attached to this Legislative Decree, the presidents of the Arbitral Labour Councils, and all other judges belonging to the judicial judiciary appointed to judicial bodies or other posts or seconded thereto, wherein they retain their aforementioned affiliation.

Judges are independent in the exercise of their functions and may not be transferred or dismissed from the judicial corps except in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

Subject to the provisions contained in Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/06/1959 (the Civil Servants Regulations), every collective functional demand must pass through the Supreme Judicial Council.

Notwithstanding any contrary provision, the General Assembly of the Court of Cassation shall hear felonies and misdemeanours attributed to the judges of the Court of Cassation or any of

the members of the Public Prosecution attached thereto, the First Presidents of the Courts of Appeal and the Public Prosecutors attached thereto, the First Presidents of the Courts of Appeal and the Public Prosecutors attached thereto, the heads of bodies at the Ministry of Justice, and the First Investigating Judges, whether arising out of the office or outside thereof; and the Criminal Chamber of the Court of Cassation shall hear felonies and misdemeanours attributed to the remaining judges, whether arising out of the office or outside thereof, and the provisions of Part Three, Title Two of the Code of Criminal Procedure shall be observed, and the First President of the Court of Cassation and the Public Prosecutor attached thereto shall each exercise the powers vested in the First President of the Court of Appeal and the Public Prosecutor attached thereto pursuant to the provisions of the aforementioned Title.

Judges of the Public Prosecutions shall be subject to the direction and supervision of their superiors and shall also be subject to the authority of the Minister of Justice, while retaining freedom of speech during trial hearings.

Upon their appointment and prior to assuming their duties, judges shall take the oath worded as follows:

"I swear by Almighty God that I shall perform my judicial function with the utmost fidelity and impartiality, that I shall be just among people and faithful to their rights, that I shall preserve the secrecy of deliberations, and that I shall conduct myself in all my acts as an honest and honourable judge".

The judicial function may not be combined with public offices. Nor may it be combined with any profession or remunerated work. Excluded therefrom is teaching at universities and institutes of higher education, and the number of teaching hours and the rules for authorising the same shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice. Notwithstanding any contrary provision, a judge shall retain the right to teach following his resignation or his placement on retirement.

Notwithstanding any general or special provision, a judge may be transferred with his consent to the establishment of any of the public administrations or public institutions of

whatever kind by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice and the competent minister following the approval of the

Supreme Judicial Council.

A judge may not be seconded to the establishment of any of the public administrations or public institutions unless a provision in its regulations permits the secondment

of a judge to its establishment. The secondment shall be for a limited or unlimited period.

A seconded judge shall continue to receive his salaries and allowances due in respect of his category and grade from the budget of the Ministry of Justice. A seconded judge shall receive the allowances pertaining to the office to which he is seconded from the budget of the administration to which he is seconded.

Notwithstanding any other provision, a judge who wishes to stand as a candidate for parliamentary or municipal elections shall be required to have resigned from the judiciary and to have effectively ceased exercising his duties at least one year prior to the date of the elections, under pain of rejection of his candidacy application. He may not thereafter be appointed to any judicial office.

Every judge who stands as a candidate for parliamentary or municipal elections shall be separated by operation of law from the judicial corps and may not thereafter be appointed to any judicial office.

A judge may not be assigned a mission in addition to his original office except in the cases provided for by law. "With the exception of committees inherent to the office, the appointment of judges as presidents

and members of standing committees shall be reviewed by operation of law by the Minister of Justice in accordance with the rules, such that a judge shall not be assigned to more than one committee except by a reasoned decision.

It shall be for the Supreme Judicial Council, by a decision issued by it, to define the concept of committees inherent to the office and standing committees.

The provisions of this Article shall apply to the judges of the State Council, provided that the Bureau of the State Council shall replace the Supreme Judicial Council.

Both the Minister of Justice and the Supreme Judicial Council shall permanently oversee the application of the principles set forth in this Article".

The State shall guarantee to judicial and administrative judges, in addition to the guarantees provided for by the laws in force, compensation for any damage sustained by them or by one of their family members or by their property by reason of, during, or on the occasion of the office.

The Institute of Judicial Studies shall ensure:

1- The preparation of trainee judges to assume judicial work.

2- The organisation of training courses for the auxiliary bodies of the judiciary, judicial assistants, notaries public, experts, and others whom the Minister of Justice decides to subject to training courses.

3- The preparation of non-Lebanese judges to assume judicial work in their countries. Judicial preparation shall cover theoretical and practical studies in the science of law and in the sciences useful in forming the culture necessary to qualify the judge intellectually and morally to assume judicial office, and shall also cover training at the various judicial departments where the judge participates in deliberations and abides by their secrecy.

The subject of environmental laws shall be added to the teaching subjects at the Institute of Judicial Studies."

1- The Institute shall be headed and its work supervised by a judge who is required to be of the seventh grade and above and who is seconded for this purpose by a decree adopted

upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice following the approval of the Supreme Judicial Council.

2- Studies at the Institute shall be directed by a judge of the tenth grade and above who is seconded for this purpose by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice

following the approval of the Supreme Judicial Council.

3- A Board of Directors shall be formed at the Institute composed of:

أ- The President of the Supreme Judicial Council as President

ب - The Director General of the Ministry of Justice as Vice-President

ج- The President of the Institute as Member

د- The Director of the Institute as Member

ه- Two judges appointed by a decision of the Minister of Justice following the approval of the Judicial Council for a term of three years, renewable once only.

4- The Board shall lay down the curricula, determine the methods of academic and professional evaluation, organise the study courses, and select the professors and contract

with them through the President of the Institute".

The President of the Institute shall take the decisions necessary to implement the resolutions of the Board, oversee the proper functioning of work at the Institute, and be the direct superior of the employees attached to the Institute. In his absence, the President shall be replaced by the Director of Studies at the Institute.

Outside of any disciplinary prosecution, the President of the Institute may address an observation to the trainee judges.
The administrative staff of the Institute shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice.

The internal regulations of the Institute shall be laid down and amended by a decision of the Minister of Justice adopted upon the proposal of the Board of Directors.

The internal regulations of the Institute shall determine everything relating to the organisation of studies, examinations, traineeship, internal discipline, disciplinary

procedures, and the organisation necessary for the application of the provisions of this Chapter.

Whenever the need arises and after consulting the opinion of the Supreme Judicial Council, the Minister of Justice shall determine the number of trainee judges intended to be appointed and shall request the Supreme Judicial Council to organise a competitive examination for this purpose.

The Supreme Judicial Council shall organise the entrance competitive examination to the Institute, determining the subjects on which it is held and the passing grade average, and shall also appoint the examining committee at the start of each competitive examination from among the judges whom it selects for this purpose.

Every candidate for participation in the competitive examination shall be required:

1- To have been a Lebanese national for at least ten years.

2- To be in enjoyment of his civil rights and not convicted of a felony or a disgraceful misdemeanour.

3- To be free from diseases and infirmities that prevent him from performing his duties.

4- To hold a (Lebanese) Licence in Law.

5- To be proficient in the Arabic language and one of the two languages, French or English.

6- "To be under thirty-five years of age as of the date of commencement of the written competitive examination".

The Supreme Judicial Council shall examine the applications and designate the candidates accepted to participate in the competitive examination, and it may, where necessary, summon whomever of them it deems fit for a prior interview.

The committee shall announce the results of the competitive examination and communicate them immediately to each of the Minister of Justice, the Supreme Judicial Council, and the Board of Directors.

"As for the candidates who were attached to the Institute and whose competence to be trainee judges was declared prior to the issuance of this Legislative Decree, the period of their attachment to the Institute shall be counted towards the period of their training such that they shall be exempted from one academic session".

Successful candidates shall be appointed as trainee judges by a decree adopted upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice and after the approval of the Supreme Judicial Council

and they shall be attached to the Institute of Judicial Studies for a period of three years during which they shall receive the salaries of trainee judges, and if the trainee judge is from among civil servants, he shall be transferred from his cadre to the judicial cadre with the same salary that he was receiving if it was higher than the salary of a trainee judge, and he shall benefit from the promotion specific to trainee judges with effect from the date of his affiliation with the Institute.

Trainee judges shall take, immediately upon their appointment and prior to their commencement of work, before the Court of Appeal of Beirut, the following oath:

"I swear by Almighty God to take care to preserve the secrecy of deliberations and to conduct myself in all my actions as an honest and honourable trainee judge".
A trainee judge shall be promoted by one step at the end of each judicial year.

Authorisation may be granted, by a decree adopted upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice and after the approval of the Board of Directors of the Institute, for the first four of the trainee judges to benefit from specialisation scholarships abroad, provided that the same decree determines the conditions of travel, the place of specialisation, the academic

degree that must be obtained, the certificates that stand in its stead, and the conditions for their equivalence.

Trainee judges may be appointed without a competitive examination from among holders of a State Doctorate in Law, by a decree adopted upon

the proposal of the Minister of Justice and after the approval of the Supreme Judicial Council.

Judicial assistants who succeed in the competitive examination or who apply to benefit from the preceding Article and who have spent five years practising their duties shall be exempted from the age requirement, provided that they do not exceed forty-eight years of age as of the date of submission of the application.

The results of the work of each judge shall be recorded in his personal file kept at the Secretariat of the Institute. At the end of the training period, the Board of Directors of the Institute shall draw up the graduation list and submit it with its proposals to the Supreme Judicial Council, which shall declare the competence of the trainee judge to transfer to the tenured judiciary or his incompetence. The decision of the Judicial Council declaring incompetence shall terminate the service of the judge without the need to issue any other administrative act. The Judicial Council may declare incompetence at the end of each academic year upon the proposal of the Board of the Institute.

Trainee judges whose competence has been declared shall be appointed as tenured judges at the lowest step, or at the step whose salary is equivalent to the salary of the appointed judge, by a decree adopted upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice. Where there is no vacant position in the cadre, the trainee judge shall be attached to the Ministry of Justice pending the issuance of his appointment and attachment upon the vacancy of the first position in accordance with the graduation list at the Institute. During this period, the judge shall receive, in addition to his salary, a monthly allowance equivalent to the difference between his salary and the salary of a tenured judge, together with the allowances incidental to the salary of a tenured judge. The period of his seniority shall commence as though he were a tenured judge after the expiry of three months from the declaration of his competence without the issuance of a decree appointing him as a tenured judge. In the event that trainee judges are appointed as tenured judges, they shall be attached by operation of law to the Ministry of Justice pending their due attachment to the positions specific to judicial judges.

For allowances for teaching, grading, discussions, and research, the rules and limits prescribed at the Lebanese University at the level of postgraduate studies shall be adopted. The allowances of the Board of Directors, the President of the Institute, and the Director of Studies shall be determined by a decree adopted upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice.

The Minister of Justice may admit to the Institute foreign nationals officially delegated by their countries without being bound by the requirements to which Lebanese trainee judges are subject. The administration of the Institute shall organise special sessions for them where necessary.
Trainee judges shall be subject to the disciplinary rules applicable to tenured judges and to the rules of procedure applied to judges in criminal prosecutions.
Auditing students present at the Institute shall be appointed as trainee judges and their training shall take place at the courts during the remaining period of their presence at the Institute.

A Public Law Division shall be established at the Institute of Judicial Studies. The Minister of Justice shall determine, whenever the need arises and after consulting the Bureau of the State Council, the number of trainee judges intended to be appointed to this Division in order for them to become, upon their graduation, assistant councillors at the State Council. In all matters relating to administrative trainee judges, the Bureau of the State Council shall replace the Supreme Judicial Council. In the Board of Directors of the Institute, the President of the State Council shall replace the President of the Supreme Judiciary. And in the State Council in place of the President of the Supreme Judicial Council, and two judges from the State Council in place of the two member judicial judges.

The provisions applicable to judicial trainee judges shall apply to administrative trainee judges.

A Financial Law Division shall be established at the Institute of Judicial Studies.

The President of the Council of Ministers shall determine, after consulting the Bureau of the Court of Audit, the number of financial trainee judges intended to be appointed to the Division in order for them to become, upon their graduation, financial judges at the Court of Audit at the lowest grade.

In all matters relating to financial trainee judges, the Bureau of the Court of Audit shall replace the Supreme Judicial Council, and in the Board of Directors of the Institute, the President of the Court of Audit shall replace the President of the Supreme Judicial Council and two judges from the Court of Audit shall replace the two judicial judges, to be appointed by a decision of the President of the Court of Audit after the approval of the Council of the Court of Audit.

The provisions applicable to judicial trainee judges shall apply to financial trainee judges.

Tenured judges may be appointed by competitive examination. In addition to the requirements provided for in Article 61 of this Legislative Decree, with the exception of the age requirement, the candidate must either have been an advocate for at least six years, including the years of pupillage, or a judicial assistant who has practised his duties for at least six years after obtaining a Licence in Law, or a civil servant in public administrations or public institutions whose post requires a Licence in Law and who has practised such duties throughout the same period after obtaining that Licence. Former trainee judges whom the Supreme Judicial Council decided were incompetent to hold judicial office shall not be admitted to the competitive examination. The provisions of Articles 59, 60, and 62 of this Legislative Decree shall apply to the competitive examination. Appointment shall be made at the lowest step by a decree adopted upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice after the approval of the Supreme Judicial Council.

Subject to the provisions set forth in Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/06/1959 (Civil Servants Regulations) and the provisions of the Bar Association

Retirement Law, for the purpose of calculating the dismissal indemnity or the retirement pension, the period of the judge's practice of the legal profession to the extent that it exceeds seven years, or of any public office, shall be added to his service, provided that he pays the retirement deductions therefor on

the basis of the salary he received in the public office, respectively.

Judicial judges and judges of the State Council and the Court of Accounts currently in service shall benefit from the preceding paragraph, subject to paying the due deductions.

No person may be appointed as a Single Judge unless he is a judge of the second degree or above.

No person may be appointed as a Counsellor at the Court of Appeal, a Chamber President in a Court of First Instance, an Investigating Judge, an Appellate Advocate General, or an Assistant to the Government Commissioner at the Military Court unless he is a judge of the fourth degree or above.

No person may be appointed as a Chamber President at the Court of Appeal, a Public Prosecutor at the Court of Appeal, a Government Commissioner at the Military Court, or a First Investigating Judge unless he is a judge of the sixth degree or above.

No person may be appointed as a Counsellor at the Court of Cassation or an Advocate General at the Court of Cassation unless he is a judge of the eighth degree or above.

No person may be appointed as a Chamber President at the Court of Cassation or a First President at the Courts of Appeal unless he is a judge of the tenth degree or above.

No person may be appointed as a First President at the Court of Cassation or a Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation unless he is a judge of the fourteenth degree or above.

However, the positions set forth in the first five paragraphs of this Article may be assigned in an acting capacity for a period of one year, renewable once or more, to a judge who does not meet the conditions mentioned above, provided that the difference between his degree and the degree qualifying for the position assigned to him does not exceed one degree, and otherwise the general Civil Servants Regulations shall apply. The assignment in an acting capacity shall take place by decree after the approval of the Supreme Judicial Council upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice.

In the event of disagreement, the provisions of paragraph "b" of Article /5/ of this Law shall apply.

Judges shall be granted a specialisation allowance, the rate of which shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice, and this allowance shall not be included in the calculation of the maximum limit of allowances provided for in the Civil Servants Regulations.

Pending the issuance of the decree, judges shall continue to receive the current allowance, and it shall remain deemed not included in the maximum limit of allowances.

Judges shall be granted a salary increment, the value of which shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice at fifteen percent of the basic salary, and judicial judges, judges of the State Council, and judges of the Court of Accounts shall benefit therefrom.

The salary increment determined in Decree No. 3224 dated 29/5/1986 shall be deemed included in the core basic salary of judicial judges, judges of the State Council, and judges of the Court of Accounts, and the conversion of the salary scales of the aforementioned judges in accordance with Tables No. 1, 2, and 3 annexed to this Decree, and each of the indicated judges shall be allocated the new salary corresponding to his old salary without modification in degree, provided that each of them retains the seniority qualifying for advancement.

(Note) With regard to the tables, see Official Gazette No. 51 dated 18/12/86

A new salary scale for judicial judges and judges of the State Council and the Court of Accounts shall be established pursuant to a table issued by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice.

Every breach of the duties of office and every act prejudicial to honour, dignity, or decency constitutes a fault punishable disciplinarily. In particular, failure to attend hearings, delay in deciding cases, failure to fix a specific date for the pronouncement of judgment at the close of deliberations, discrimination between litigants, and disclosure of the secrecy of deliberations shall be deemed a breach of the duties of office.

Outside of any disciplinary prosecution, the President of the Supreme Judicial Council may, where necessary, address an observation to any of the judicial

judges with the exception of the judges of the Body, Council, or Court over which he presides, and each of the Cassation Public Prosecutor, the First President of the Court of Appeal, and the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Appeal may address an observation to the judges subordinate to him with the exception of the sitting judges who compose the chamber of the First President.

The Disciplinary Council for Judges shall be composed of a Chamber President at the Court of Cassation as President and the membership of two Chamber Presidents at the Court of Appeal appointed by the President of the Supreme Judicial Council at the beginning of each judicial year, and he may also appoint a substitute for any of them in the event of absence or impediment.

The President of the Judicial Inspection Body, or whomever he delegates from among the members of the Body, shall perform the function of Government Commissioner before the Council.

The Council shall examine the discipline of judges upon the referral of the Council of the Judicial Inspection Body.

The grounds for recusal and withdrawal provided for in the Code of Civil Procedure shall apply to the President and members of the Council.

The Supreme Judicial Council shall examine the request for withdrawal within a time limit of three days at most.

The President shall prepare a report or assign one of the two members of the Council to do so. The rapporteur shall conduct the necessary investigations, hear the person concerned, receive the testimonies of witnesses under oath, and submit his report to the Council without delay.

The President shall immediately summon the person concerned to examine the file and the rapporteur's report and to appear before the Council at the hearing which he fixes for him.

The trial shall be conducted in camera. The rapporteur's report shall be read out and the person concerned shall be asked to present his defence regarding the matters held against him.

The person concerned shall have the right to be assisted by one lawyer or by one of the judges, and if he fails to appear, the Council shall examine the case in light of the documents alone.

The Council shall issue a reasoned decision on the same day or adjourn it to the following day at the latest.

The decision of the Council shall be open to challenge by the judge concerned or by the President of the Judicial Inspection Body within a time limit of fifteen days from the date of its issuance before the Supreme Judicial Disciplinary Body.

The Supreme Judicial Disciplinary Body shall be composed of the President of the Supreme Judicial Council or his Vice-President as President and four members appointed by the Council at the beginning of each judicial year, and the Council shall also appoint a substitute for any of them in the event of absence or impediment.

The trial procedures in force before the Disciplinary Council shall be followed before the Supreme Judicial Disciplinary Body.

The decision of the Supreme Judicial Disciplinary Body shall not be open to any avenue of recourse, including cassation, and shall be enforceable in itself upon being notified to the person concerned through administrative channels.

This decision shall be notified to the Minister of Justice.

It shall not be permissible to publish or announce any measure of the disciplinary prosecution proceedings except for the final decision if it includes the penalty of dismissal from service or removal from office.

The disciplinary penalties that may be imposed are:

1 - Warning.

2 - Reprimand.

3 - Delay of promotion for a period not exceeding two years.

4 - Reduction in degree.

5 - Suspension from work without salary for a period not exceeding one year.

6 - Dismissal from service.

7 - Removal from office with deprivation of the dismissal indemnity or the retirement pension.

In the event of a reduction in degree, the judge shall retain the period of his seniority for promotion, and in the event of removal from office with deprivation of the dismissal indemnity or the retirement pension, the retirement deductions shall be refunded to him.

The Minister of Justice may suspend from work, upon the proposal of the Council of the Judicial Inspection Body, a judge referred to the Disciplinary Council. A judge suspended from work shall receive half of his salaries and allowances.
The form of the robes of judges shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Justice adopted after consultation with the Supreme Judicial Council and upon the proposal of this Council.

The Special Court for Banks Placed Under Seizure, established pursuant to the Law put into force by Decree No. 1663 dated 17/1/1979, may be abolished by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice, and the manner of liquidating its works shall be determined in the said decree.
All legal provisions contrary to or inconsistent with the provisions of this Legislative Decree are repealed, and Law No. 49/65 dated 6/9/1965 is repealed.
The details of the application of this Legislative Decree shall be determined, where necessary, by decrees taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice.
This Legislative Decree shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The judicial vacation begins on 15 July and ends on 15 September of each year.

The Minister of Justice may, following the approval of the head of the judicial department to which the judge belongs, grant him an administrative leave with full salary not exceeding fifteen days.

The date and duration of the judicial vacation may be amended following the approval of the Supreme Judicial Council by a decree enacted upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice".

Judges who have not incurred during twenty years of exercising their duties any disciplinary penalty other than the penalty of admonition shall be admitted to honorary status, and they shall thereupon enjoy the privileges of judges. Judges shall be admitted to honorary status by a decree enacted upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice following the approval of the Supreme Judicial Council.

Judges who have become entitled to a severance indemnity or a retirement pension shall benefit from the social and health services from which serving judges benefit, subject to paying the fee due therefor.

Apart from any disciplinary prosecution, the Judicial Council may decide at any time the incompetence of a tenured judge by a reasoned decision issued upon the proposal of the Judicial Inspection Board and after hearing the judge concerned, by a majority of eight of its members.

The decisions of the Supreme Judicial Council regarding the competence of a candidate to participate in the competitive examination as a trainee or tenured judge, or regarding the competence of a trainee or tenured judge, taken pursuant to the provisions of this Legislative Decree, shall not be subject to any avenue of review, including an application for annulment on the ground of excess of power.

Tenured judges may be appointed from among the judges of the State Council, provided that each of them is appointed to the grade that corresponds to the salary he receives upon his transfer to the judicial judiciary and with the preservation of his right to seniority for the purpose of advancement.

The jurisdiction of the Judicial Inspection Board, under the supervision of the Minister of Justice, shall cover the judicial and administrative courts and the bodies at the Ministry of Justice, the Court of Audit and the registries attached thereto, and the central departments at the Ministry of Justice.

Within its scope shall fall the works of those performing work of a judicial nature in all councils, bodies, and committees, as well as notaries public, experts, bankruptcy trustees, and supervisors of preventive composition.

The Judicial Inspection Board shall undertake:

1 - To supervise the proper functioning of justice and the works of judges, registry employees, and all other persons subject to it.

2 - To draw the attention of the authorities to any defect it perceives in the works and to submit proposals aimed at rectifying it.

3 - The disciplinary powers provided for in the law in respect of judges and employees of the registries and the central departments at the Ministry of Justice.

4 - To draw the attention of those subject to inspection to any defect that appears in the conduct of their works.

5 - To issue an admonition where necessary to judges and employees.

6 - To propose to the Supreme Judicial Council the taking of the appropriate measure against any judge.

The Judicial Inspection Board shall be composed of a President, four Inspectors General, and six Inspectors. The President and the Inspectors General shall form the Council of the Board. The Board shall have a registry consisting of judicial assistants to whom the regulations of the registries in the judicial departments shall apply.

The President of the Judicial Inspection Board shall be appointed by a decree enacted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice from among the judicial judges of the fourteenth grade and above, or the equivalent of this grade in the cadre of the State Council and the cadre of the Court of Audit.

1 - The Inspector General shall be appointed by a decree enacted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice from among the judicial judges of the

seventh grade and above, or the equivalent of this grade in the cadre of the State Council and the cadre of the Court of Audit.

2 - The Inspector shall be appointed by a decree enacted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice from among the judicial judges of the ninth grade and above, or the equivalent of this grade in the cadre of the State Council and the cadre of the Court of Audit.

3 - The President of the Judicial Inspection Board and the Inspectors General shall be reinstated to their original cadre or transferred to the administration at a rank whose salary is equivalent to their salary upon their written request. They may be reinstated to their original cadre or transferred to another administration by a decree enacted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice and following the approval of a special committee composed of the First President of the Court of Cassation, the President of the State Council, and the President of the Court of Audit.

The Inspectors shall be reinstated to their original cadre or transferred to another administration upon their written request by a decree enacted upon the proposal of

the Minister of Justice and following the approval of the Council of the Judicial Inspection Board.

In the event of the vacancy of the post of President or his absence, the Inspector General highest in grade, and in the event of equality of grade the longest-serving in the judiciary, and in the event of equality of seniority the oldest in age, shall assume his duties ex officio. In the event of the vacancy of the post of an Inspector General or his absence and the loss of quorum, the Inspector who holds priority in accordance with the preceding paragraph shall replace him ex officio and on a temporary basis on the Council of the Board.

The President of the Board is the direct administrative head of the members and the registry employees, and he exercises within the Judicial Inspection the administrative and financial powers vested by the laws and regulations in the Minister, with the exception of constitutional powers.

The Council of the Board shall meet upon the convocation of the President, and its meeting shall not be legal except in the presence of the President and at least two Inspectors General. Decisions shall be taken by a majority of votes; in the event of a tie, the President shall have a casting vote.

The Council of the Board shall establish, prior to the beginning of a judicial year, the annual inspection programme, and a report on the inspection works in the preceding year, which it shall submit to the Minister of Justice with the appropriate proposals.

The Council of the Board shall refer judges and employees of the second category and above who are subject to the supervision of the Board to the Disciplinary Council if it appears to it in the investigations that there are grounds requiring such referral. It may propose to the Minister of Justice the suspension from work of the judge referred to the Disciplinary Council.

The President of the Board shall ensure the implementation of the inspection programme:

1 - He shall issue special inspection assignments.

2 - He shall undertake personally, or through whomever he assigns from among the Inspectors General, the inspection of the Court of Cassation, the State Council, the Court of Audit, and the Directorate General of the Ministry of Justice, and the investigation of judicial judges of the seventh grade and above.

The President of the Board shall immediately undertake personally, or through whomever he assigns from among the Inspectors General or the Inspectors, the investigation of every complaint received by him directly or through the Minister of Justice, and he may close complaints submitted to him directly if he finds them not to be serious.

The person conducting the inspection must be higher in rank than the judge to be inspected.

The President of the Board shall refer employees of the third category and below and all other persons subject to the supervision of the Board to the Disciplinary Council. He shall impose upon them the penalties of the first degree provided for in the General Civil Service Regulations after hearing their defence.

The Inspector General or the Inspector shall perform the duties assigned to him by the inspection programme or entrusted to him by the President. The Inspector General or the Inspector shall submit a report to the President of the Board on every mission he performs, together with the appropriate proposals.

The President and members of the Judicial Inspection Board shall have the right to use all means of investigation to perform their duties, to examine all documents, files, and registers, to hear whomever they deem necessary to hear from among employees and others, and to summon them through the Public Prosecution where necessary.

The Council of the Inspection Board may impose, where necessary, upon employees, in cases of obstruction of inspection works, the penalty of admonition.

Save for the exceptions provided for in this Title, the regulations of judicial judges and their salary scale shall apply to the President and members of the Judicial Inspection Board, and they shall enjoy their rights.

"The regulations of the Central Inspection shall continue to apply in the Judicial Inspection Board in all matters not contrary to the provisions of this Legislative Decree".

The layout shown in yellow on Maps No. (1) and (2) annexed to this Decree, drawn at a scale of 1/2000, and relating to the widening of the seafront corniche in the city of Saida (Governorate of South Lebanon), is hereby approved.

The layout shown in oblique red lines on Map No. (1) mentioned in Article 1 of this Decree is hereby cancelled, and all previous provisions and texts contrary to the content of this Decree are likewise cancelled.
This Decree shall be published and notified where needed.

The President and the members shall be bound by professional secrecy. They shall be referred to the Disciplinary Council by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice and after consulting the Council of the Body. This decree shall appoint the Disciplinary Council that examines each case, provided that it is composed of a President and two members chosen from among the Presidents of the Chambers at the Court of Cassation, and the function of Government Commissioner shall be assumed by the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation and, where this is not possible, by the highest-ranking Advocate General at this Court. The Disciplinary Council shall follow the procedure applicable to judges.

Judicial assistants are the Chief Clerks, Head Clerks, Clerks, Bailiffs, and Typists in the registries of the judicial departments, and their number, categories, scale of grades, and salaries shall be determined in schedules established by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice.

Judicial assistants shall undertake the clerical work provided for by law and all other work required for the functioning of the judicial departments and the central administration at the Ministry of Justice.
The Chief Clerk shall exercise towards the staff of the registry the powers of a Head of Department in the public administrations.
Subject to the provisions of this Legislative Decree, judicial assistants shall remain subject to the Civil Service Board.

Judicial assistants shall be selected as a result of a competitive examination the conditions of which shall be determined by the Minister of Justice after seeking the opinion of the Civil Service Board, provided that the examining committee is chaired by a judicial or administrative judge.

In addition to the general conditions provided for in the Civil Servants Regulations, any person applying for the competitive examination shall meet the special conditions for each post in accordance with the following:

- Typist: The intermediate certificate or a vocational certificate or its equivalent.

- Bailiff: The intermediate certificate or its equivalent.

- Clerk: The Lebanese Baccalaureate certificate - Part One - or five years of actual practice in the post of bailiff.

- Head Clerk: The Baccalaureate certificate - Part Two - or five years of actual practice in the post of clerk.

- Chief Clerk: The Lebanese Bachelor of Laws degree or five years of actual practice in the post of head clerk or ten years of actual practice in the post of clerk. Candidates who pass the competitive examination shall be appointed by a decree adopted upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice after the approval of the Civil Service Board. The Minister of Justice may decide to subject them after their appointment to a training course the conditions of which he shall determine and the conduct of which he shall entrust to the Institute of Judicial Studies.

Judicial assistants in the third category shall be transferred from one post to another by a decision of the Minister of Justice after seeking the opinion of the Judicial Inspection Board. Other judicial assistants and administrative employees in the fourth and fifth categories shall be transferred from one post to another by a decision of the Director General after seeking the opinion of the Judicial Inspection Board.

A Special Disciplinary Council for judicial assistants shall be established, composed as follows:

- A judge of at least the eleventh grade, as President

- An employee of the second or third category in the central administration of the Ministry of Justice, as a member

- A Chief Clerk, as a member. The President and the two members of the Disciplinary Council shall be appointed by a decree adopted upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice and after the approval of the Supreme Judicial Council for a renewable term of three years. An alternate for each of the President and the two members shall be appointed in the same decree. A judicial inspector delegated by the President of the Judicial Inspection Board shall perform his function as Government Commissioner before the Council. The decisions of the Disciplinary Council shall be taken by majority vote and shall be subject to appeal before the State Council.

The Disciplinary Council shall apply the rules of procedure provided for in the regulations of the Disciplinary Council for Civil Servants insofar as they do not conflict with the provisions of this Legislative Decree. The Disciplinary Council shall impose the penalties provided for in the General Civil Servants Regulations.

A judicial assistant shall be referred to the Disciplinary Council by a decision of the Minister of Justice, or by a decision of the President of the Judicial Inspection Board, or by a decision of the First President of the Court of Appeal to which he is attached.
The Disciplinary Council for Civil Servants shall remain competent to examine cases referred to it prior to the issuance of this Legislative Decree.

The General Civil Servants Regulations shall apply to judicial assistants in all matters that do not conflict with the provisions of this Legislative Decree, and they shall be disciplinarily subject to the Judicial Inspection. Notwithstanding any text to the contrary, judicial assistants shall continue to benefit from one grade advancement every two years despite having exceeded the ceiling of their rank and category.

"Every judicial assistant holding a Bachelor of Laws degree shall be granted an exceptional grade advancement".

Bailiffs entrusted with service of process shall be granted a travel allowance the conditions and amount of which shall be determined by a decree adopted upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice. The assignment shall be made by a decision of the Minister of Justice after consulting the head of the judicial department to which the bailiff is attached. In addition to the duties of service of process, bailiffs shall undertake the material tasks required for the functioning of the judicial departments to which they are attached.
The General Civil Servants Regulations shall apply to ushers working in the judicial departments and the central administration of the Ministry of Justice.
The form of the attire of each of the judicial assistant, the court clerk, the bailiff, and the usher shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Justice.

By a decree adopted upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice, notaries public may be appointed from among judicial assistants holding a Bachelor of Laws degree who have practiced their functions for more than ten years after obtaining the degree, without the need for a competitive examination.

The Judicial Assistants Relief Fund shall be replaced by a Cooperative Fund for Judicial Assistants, the purpose of which is to provide social grants and aid, and to which shall be transferred the funds collected pursuant to Article 15 of the 1948 Budget Law as amended pursuant to Article 31 of the 1951 Budget Law and frozen in a special account at the Treasury since the date of entry into force of Decree No. 8914 dated 19/12/1967. This Fund shall be regulated pursuant to a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice. No vested right shall arise for anyone prior to the issuance of this decree.

"A rate of twenty-five percent of the fines collected under judicial judgments shall be deducted to finance this Fund, and five percent of the same fines shall be deducted to finance the Judges' Mutual Fund.

It shall be for the Minister of Justice, by a decision issued by him, to determine the manner of regulating the collection of this percentage and its payment to the relevant fund.

Administrative employees and wage earners working in the Ministry of Justice shall benefit from the Cooperative Fund for Judicial Assistants".
The Civil Servants Regulations shall apply to judges in all matters that do not conflict with the provisions of this Legislative Decree.

The members of the Supreme Judicial Council shall be appointed in application of Article Two of this Legislative Decree within a time limit not exceeding 31 December 1983. The condition of non-renewal shall only apply starting from the end of the term of office of the members of the new Council.

The term of office of the current members of the Supreme Judicial Council shall continue until its expiration. The condition of non-renewal shall only apply starting from the end of the term of office of the members of the new Council.

The schedules provided for in Articles 13, 16, 25, 32, and 33 shall be deemed regulatory matter that may be determined and amended by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice after the approval of the Supreme Judicial Council. In the same manner, and in implementation of the detailed provisions of Law No. 36/75 dated 23/9/1975 (Establishment of the Governorate of Nabatieh in South Lebanon), the judicial bodies in the Governorate of South Lebanon may be separated and amended by way of distribution, addition, and reduction so that each of the two Governorates has an independent and integrated judicial body. The schedules annexed to the Law put into effect by Decree No. 7855 dated 16/10/1961 shall remain in force until the issuance of the implementing decrees provided for in the two preceding paragraphs.
