- Determining the locations of cables, measuring excavations and determining their routes, and recording the information in a special register to be consulted where necessary by the concerned parties.

- Supervising all works of underground networks and keeping registers in respect thereof.

Service of Specifications and Technical Work Methods.

This Service shall consist of:

- Specifications Section.

- Technical Work Methods Section.

Specifications Section:

This Section shall undertake the following primary tasks:

- Following up on technical developments in order to draw up, study and determine the new technical specifications

for the various equipment used by the Establishment:

distribution network equipment, main substation equipment, network protection and monitoring equipment, overhead line and underground cable equipment, tools of various types, production plant equipment and apparatus.

- Following up on the performance of all equipment and apparatus in order to amend or develop their specifications where necessary.

- Coordinating and exchanging opinions with the various operating units in the Establishment regarding the suitability of specifications and the necessities of developing and amending them.

- Acquainting itself with modern technologies and studying the possibility of using them in the Establishment within coordination programmes with electricity establishments outside the country.

- Drawing up technical specifications for office supplies, printed materials and furniture of various types in agreement with the concerned units in the Establishment.

- Drawing up technical specifications for fuels of various types used by the Establishment in agreement with the concerned units in the Establishment.

- Preparing books of conditions relating to all purchases and contracts of the Establishment, including equipment projects, after obtaining the opinion of the Equipment Directorate in agreement with the concerned units in the Establishment.

- Studying and proposing the technical specifications required to be met in electrical equipment and installations inside the buildings of current subscribers.

- Organising a central library for technical references comprising books, magazines, printed materials, publications, regulations and computer software.

- Following up on sources of information, deciding what is suitable and useful for the Establishment, and organising the purchase and receipt thereof.

- Processing the contents of these publications, distributing what is useful thereof to the competent authorities in the Establishment, and communicating the same to whom it may concern among the parties concerned with the matter.

Technical Work Methods Section This Section shall undertake the following primary tasks:

- Preparing methods and rules to facilitate operating works, including transaction workflow methods and shortening their stages in order to achieve the objective as quickly as possible.

- Unifying and developing work methods and coordinating with the various units of the Establishment to this end, and in particular with the Programmes and Guidance Service in the General Inspectorate.

- Determining rules of public safety and worker protection to limit and prevent work accidents, in coordination with the Work Safety and Vocational Training Service

- Issuing periodic bulletins containing technical information and followed rules, and circulating them to all centres of the Establishment

- Drawing up a system of courses and lectures on technical work methods and new technology, in coordination with the Work Safety and Vocational Training Service.

Statistics and Informatics Service This Service shall consist of:

- Statistics Section

- Informatics Section

Statistics Section This Section shall undertake the following primary tasks:

- Collecting of various types from all units of the Establishment and from specialised administrations and establishments

- Recording, classifying and preserving this information

- Studying and analysing the information, drawing conclusions and expressing an opinion

- Drawing up statistical reports and distributing them to the authorities concerned therewith.

Informatics Section

This Section shall undertake the following primary tasks:

- Preparing computer software for the units of the Establishment of various types

- Working on developing this software to keep pace with developments and work requirements in order to save time and improve performance

- Delivering the software to the competent units and training whoever is required on the use thereof.

- Obtaining technical and administrative information from all units of the Establishment and public administrations and establishments in Lebanon, recording it on computer devices, preserving it, and supplying the competent units in the Establishment with what they request thereof

- Keeping pace with the amendments that occur to this information

- Carrying out street numbering, classifying, indexing and setting codes to identify locations and buildings in order to facilitate collection operations, and following up on every amendment occurring thereto

- Coordinating the work and operation of computer devices to ensure the proper performance of systems, in particular those relating:

to Management Information M.I.S

to Customer Information C.I.S

to Geographic Information Systems G.I.S

- Providing all informatics services to the various units of the Establishment in matters relating to the tasks of the Establishment, and in particular those pertaining:

- to issuing invoices

- to issuing salaries, wages and their accessories

- to setting codes for materials, equipment, tariffs and terminology

- to warehouse inventory

- to issuing and preserving the results of the Establishment's accounting works

- to maintaining software for individual devices.

Equipment Directorate This Directorate shall consist of:

- Service of Execution of Works Contracts

- Service of Projects and Classification

Service of Execution of Works Contracts This Service shall consist of:

Execution Follow-up Section

- Contracts Follow-up Section

Execution Follow-up Section This Section shall undertake the following primary tasks:

- Receiving a copy of the contract file

- Handing over work sites

- Following up on the execution of contracts from the operational aspect in accordance with the books of conditions and the order letters pertaining thereto

- Ensuring the completion of works within the schedule specified therefor

- Drawing up statements successively according to the progress of works, and including in these statements the elements of each stage of execution and the deficiencies affecting them where necessary

- Monitoring tests on equipment at the factory and on site

- Informing the Studies Directorate of defects or ambiguities that may arise during execution in order to take them into consideration in the future

Contracts Follow-up Section This Section shall undertake the following primary tasks:

- Following up on problems resulting from the application of contracts of various types and finding solutions for each of them

- Carrying out all correspondence and communications with contractors and suppliers

- Liquidating the contract and preparing all documents necessary therefor, including requesting the reception of completed works, following up on the reception file, and signing the reception minutes

- Following up on the accounting and financial file and applying all clauses of the book of conditions relating to financial matters

Service of Projects and Classification This Service shall consist of:

- New Projects Section

- Contractors Classification Section

Materials Storage Section.

This section shall undertake the following basic duties:

- Supervising the management of warehouses across the various centres of the Establishment, including:

- Receiving goods from suppliers, storing them in the places designated for them, and preserving them.

- Delivering stored materials regularly in accordance with the rules established for them.

- Maintaining the arrangement of materials and the warehouse registers in which every movement therein is recorded.

- Maintaining the conformity of the quantities of stored materials with the contents of the file registers (Kardex).

- Reporting on the movement of materials in relation to the level specified for each type therein.

- Classifying stored materials.

- Taking inventory of non-moving materials.

Collection and Cash Offices Audit Department.

This department shall consist of:

- The Collection Audit Section.

- The Cash Offices and Banks Audit Section.

Collection Audit Section.

This section shall undertake the following basic duties:

- Auditing the accounts of collectors and the time limits for delivering tour vouchers.

- Organising the rules for payment by collectors and auditing payments on account.

- Auditing the time limits for closing tours.

- Conducting spot checks and inventories of overdue invoices and their conformity with the accounting registers.

- Issuing discharges to collectors.

- Performing a similar role in respect of every person who, pursuant to the regulations, carries out collection operations from among non-employees of the Establishment.

Cash Offices and Banks Audit Section.

This section shall undertake the following basic duties:

- Verifying the validity of cash office operations and their registration in accordance with the rules.

- Ensuring the conformity of receipt and payment orders with the daily registers.

- Auditing the balances of the cash offices.

- Ensuring the conformity of cash office balances with the accounting registers.

- Conducting spot checks and surprise inventories.

- Auditing bank accounts and their conformity with the accounting registers.

Directorate of Administrative Affairs.

This directorate shall consist of:

- The Personnel Affairs Department.

- The Litigation and Legal Affairs Department.

- The Occupational Safety and Vocational Training Department.

Personnel Affairs Department.

This department shall consist of:

- The Employment and Personal Files Section.

- The Social and Medical Affairs Section.

Employment and Personal Files Section.

This section shall undertake the following basic duties:

- Studying the needs of the Establishment for human resources.

- Establishing the conditions of employment in coordination with the other directorates.

- Organising and conducting competitive examinations and tests.

- Preparing employment and promotion files and all transactions relating thereto.

- Organising personal files and entering amendments thereto.

- Keeping statistics and preparing transactions for transfer, leave, rewards, discipline, termination of service, and all other transactions relating to the personal status affairs of the employee.

- Studying the conditions of employees and their demands, including those relating to incentive bonuses.

Social and Medical Affairs Section:

This section shall undertake the following basic duties:

- Monitoring the health of the employee throughout the period of his employment.

- Providing first aid inside the buildings of the Establishment.

- Following up on the continuous suitability of workplaces from the health standpoint.

- Following up on the duties of physicians contracted with the Establishment.

- Following up on sick leave, medical reports, and morbidity statistics.

- Social investigations and socio-medical assistance.

- Social security transactions, family allowances, and end-of-service.

- Relations with health insurance companies, including negotiations for the purpose of concluding insurance contracts.

- Addressing problems resulting from the application of insurance contracts and supervising their execution in coordination with the Litigation and Legal Affairs Department.

- Relations with medical institutions and their annexes.

Litigation and Legal Affairs Department

This department shall consist of:

- The Studies and Consultations Section

- The Litigation Section

- The Financial Cases Follow-up Section.

Legal Studies and Consultations Section.

This section shall undertake the following basic duties:

- Preparing legal studies.

- Providing legal consultations to the various directorates and interpreting legal and regulatory texts.

- Preparing draft texts relating to cadres, the scale of ranks and salaries, and all regulations and amendments thereto.

- Notifying the concerned authorities in the Establishment of all laws and decrees issued that concern the Establishment.

The Litigation and Financial Cases Follow-up Sections

A ) The Litigation Section shall undertake the following basic duties:

- Following up on the duties of lawyers contracted with the Establishment.

- Cases of expropriations and real property - and settlements - work emergencies - leases - contracts - books of specifications - discharges of all kinds.

- Preparing the files of lawsuits brought by or against the Establishment.

- Securing information for the lawyers of the Establishment.

- Pursuing lawsuits.

B ) The Financial Cases Follow-up Section shall undertake the following basic duties :

- Cases and lawsuits : networks without balance - thefts of current - operation - subscriptions - billing - collection orders.

Occupational Safety and Vocational Training Department.

This department shall consist of:

- The Occupational Safety and Prevention Section.

- The Vocational Training Section.

Occupational Safety and Prevention Section.

This section shall undertake the following basic duties:

- Following up on the application of public safety rules and worker protection across the various centres of the Establishment in coordination with the Specifications and Technical Work Methods Department (Directorate of Studies) and the Programmes and Guidance Department (General Control).

- Organising courses on the use of protective devices in coordination with the Specifications and Technical Work Methods Department (Directorate of Studies).

- Ensuring the validity and effectiveness of these devices for the purpose of limiting accidents during work.

- Submitting proposals regarding the development of safety rules and their devices on the basis of practice and application.

Vocational Training Section.

This section shall undertake the following basic duties:

- Managing and supervising training centres.

- Preparing new employees in accordance with the general principles determined by the Preparation and Training Administration in the Civil Service Board in light of the duties of the Establishment and the nature of its work, including training in providing first aid.

- Organising training courses for employees working in the Establishment and determining their programmes in coordination with the remaining units and then with the Preparation and Training Administration in the Civil Service Board.

- Securing transactions for training abroad with the competent authorities.

Directorate of Common Affairs.

This directorate shall consist of:

- The Supply and Purchasing Department.

- The Buildings and Vehicles Maintenance Department.

- The Fuels Department.

Supply and Purchasing Department.

This department shall consist of:

- The Supply Section.

- The Orders and Purchasing Section.

Supply Section.

This Section shall undertake the following fundamental functions:

- Monitoring the levels of stored materials of common use so as to initiate purchasing operations in due time.

- Receiving supply requisitions (quantities, specifications and deadlines) received from the various units of the Establishment of all kinds. (Spare parts - equipment - consumable materials - cables - transformers - office equipment...)

- Classifying these requisitions, completing the preliminary information thereon, and coordinating with the Stores Department (Directorate of Financial Affairs) regarding the available quantities thereof.

- Communicating this information to the Directorate of Studies to lay down the specifications therefor and consequently the books of specifications.

- Receiving tenders from the Purchasing Committee, verifying their conformity with the specifications of the books of specifications, comparing prices, and drawing up minutes in this regard jointly with the unit concerned

- Referring the minutes to the competent authority to decide on the contract, and thereafter following up on the procedures for the approval thereof.

- Conducting price inquiries to secure minor purchases necessary for the proper functioning of work and evaluating the tenders pertaining thereto.

Requisitions and Purchases Section.

This Section shall undertake the following fundamental functions:

- Carrying out the necessary formalities to follow up on the order after its approval and until its handover to the Contracts Follow-up Section in the Directorate of Equipment.

- Issuing order vouchers and letters, and sending them to the contractors and suppliers to whom the contract is awarded.

- Following up on the process of purchasing minor purchases from suppliers and contractors, including following up on delivery to the stores.

Buildings and Vehicles Maintenance Department.

This Department shall consist of:

- The Buildings Maintenance Section.

- The Vehicles Maintenance Section.

Buildings Maintenance Section.

This Section shall undertake the following fundamental functions:

- Maintaining the buildings of the Establishment in all its centres and across the various types of equipment pertaining thereto: civil - mechanical - electrical - elevators - generators - sanitary installations - central heating and cooling - furniture and office equipment, guarding and cleaning .... (excluding telecommunications equipment).

- Attending to insurance and maintenance contracts for certain installations and following up on their execution.

- Monitoring the entrances of buildings and entry and exit operations, laying down the necessary foundations therefor, and developing them where necessary.

Vehicles Maintenance Section.

This Section shall undertake the following fundamental functions:

- Laying down foundations for and executing periodic maintenance operations for vehicles of all kinds and carrying out emergency maintenance in the garages of the Establishment or in private garages.

- Issuing monthly and quarterly statistics on the status of vehicles, including fuel consumption.

- Recording and monitoring the movement of withdrawals of fuels and spare parts and drawing conclusions.

- Laying down foundations for monitoring the operation of vehicles and taking the necessary measures to remedy deficiencies.

- Managing the garage and determining the rules of work therein.

- Drawing up insurance contracts pertaining to all vehicles.

- Paying the annual inspection fees (roadworthiness fee).

- Allocating vehicles, ensuring their constant availability, and laying down a programme for their use.

- Studying options and proposing the selection of appropriate methods for the transportation of employees in order to fulfil its functions.

- Laying down replacement and repair standards in respect of vehicles.

- Proposing the purchase of vehicles and determining their types and specifications.

Fuels Department.

This Department shall consist of:

- The Programmes and Supply Follow-up Section.

- The Fuels Purchasing Section.

Programmes and Supply Follow-up Section.

This Section shall undertake the following fundamental functions:

- Following up on the programmes of the Establishment's fuel requirements for thermal generation plants and other equipment.

- Communicating these programmes to the authority concerned with purchasing.

- Following up on obtaining fuels at the appropriate times.

- Following up on the formalities for receiving fuels at the plants, while supervising the delivery process, verifying the delivered quantities, and conducting the necessary tests on the quality of these fuels in agreement with quality control companies, and concluding contracts with them and following up thereon

- Securing operations for the transport of fuels from storage centres by land routes, including the formalities necessary for announcing calls for tenders and relations with transport companies and others.

- Verifying the conformity of the vessel and its cargo with the prescribed specifications and proposing the rejection of the shipment or the fining of the supplier as a result of non-conformity with the book of specifications.

Fuels Purchasing Section.

This Section shall undertake the process of purchasing the necessary fuels according to the prepared programme and from available international or domestic sources, and this process shall include the following functions:

- Continuous knowledge of the global oil market with a view to purchasing the necessary quantities at the economically appropriate time in light of the storage capacities in the plants and terminals, taking into consideration all the interrelated factors in this context.

- The obligation to constantly reconcile needs, capacities, and prevailing and anticipated prices in the near and medium term.

- Following up on orders and correspondence and dealing with contractors.

- Concluding contracts and following up thereon, correspondence, pursuing legal matters, and relations with the ministries and administrations concerned and banks.

Directorate of Generation.

This Directorate shall consist of:

- Jiyeh Plant.

- Zouk Plant.

- Zahrani Plant.

- Deir Ammar Plant.

- Baalbek Plant.

- Tyre Plant.

- Hydroelectric Plants Department.

- A Central Section.

Each of the Jiyeh, Zouk, Deir Ammar, Zahrani, Baalbek and Tyre plants shall undertake the generation of electrical power, the maintenance and operation of the units and various apparatus, and the responsibility therefor up to the power outlets from the plant to the lines.

Each of these plants shall consist of the following sections:

- The Operation Section.

- The Maintenance Section.

- The Performance Follow-up Section.

- The Protection and Prevention Section.

With the exception of the Baalbek and Tyre plants, where a single section shall undertake maintenance works and where the head of the plant shall perform the functions of the Operation Section, the Performance Follow-up Section, and the Protection and Prevention Section.

Operation Section This Section shall undertake the following fundamental functions:

- Operating apparatus of all kinds around the clock.

- Performing all necessary manoeuvres to secure power generation.

- Following up on the operation of apparatus to ensure their continuous proper functioning.

- Recording all necessary readings on the operation of the generation units and all apparatus subordinate thereto in a special register established for this purpose.

- Notifying the competent authorities of breakdowns of whatever kind and immediately upon their occurrence during the operation of the plant in accordance with the prescribed methods.

- Taking the necessary administrative and operational measures to isolate any individual piece of apparatus or any group of apparatus in preparation for carrying out maintenance works and thereafter returning them to service.

- Carrying out the necessary laboratory analyses on the quality of water and steam as well as the oils and fuels used in the plant and monitoring these results.

- Following up on the boiler washing process and restoring the readiness of seawater evaporation machines and water desalination machines and carrying out the necessary laboratory tests.

- Performing simple and necessary mechanical and electrical works to restore the safety factor to the normal level at which it ought to be.

Maintenance Department.

This Department shall undertake the following basic duties:

- Establishing a work schedule to carry out periodic maintenance on the various groups and equipment affiliated thereto.

- Establishing programmes or a workflow plan to carry out emergency maintenance works.

- Compiling a file and establishing slips for the equipment maintenance operation, including, inter alia, descriptions of the task, placing the equipment out of service, and subsequently returning it to service upon completion of the operation.

- Preparing the necessary spare parts and tools, and determining the quality, number, and specialisation of the necessary human staff.

- Following up on the lifespan of each piece of equipment of any kind whatsoever, comparing the results of the maintenance operation with the plan drawn up for this operation, and drawing conclusions to take them into consideration when reviewing the programming and planning operation.

- Taking the necessary measures to order the spare parts, equipment, and tools necessary for maintenance so that they are ready upon request.

- Executing periodic maintenance plans.

- Distributing emergency maintenance work requests to the teams and following up on their execution.

- Keeping the warehouse of spare parts, tools, and consumable materials (receipt and delivery) and preserving the safety of its assets and the level of storage in accordance with the rules established therefor.

Performance Follow-up Department.

This Department shall undertake the following basic duties:

- Following up on technical and economic performance.

- Studying the operating results on a daily basis in order to judge the soundness of the technical performance.

- Studying the operating results from the economic standpoint to show the cost of every operation carried out in the plant of any kind whatsoever and on any of the equipment, along with all requirements of this operation, including spare parts, tools, etc...

- Monitoring the yield of the various machines, equipment, and groups, and consequently the yield of the entire plant.

- Conducting the necessary periodic tests on all this equipment to determine the causes of a decrease in yield, if any, and notifying the concerned authorities thereof in order to remove these causes.

- Taking the necessary readings relating to information of all kinds in order to maintain the yield at its normal level.

- Studying the cost of each kilowatt-hour in terms of consumable materials (fuels - oils - analyses) as well as in terms of the remaining elements of production on the basis of maintenance and operating information and data, analysing this cost, submitting a proposal, and notifying the concerned authorities of the results.

- Preparing the draft budget of the plant, following up on all stages of the draft budget until its ratification, and subsequently following up on the execution of the budget.

Protection and Prevention Department.

This Department shall undertake the following basic duties:

- Following up on the application of the rules and regulations for the protection of installations of all kinds established for this purpose.

As well as the rules for the prevention of risks to workers in the plant. This duty shall include, inter alia:

- Training the workers in the plant, each according to his duties and the nature of his work or post, on how to perform their work in order to protect themselves when operating the equipment or while carrying out maintenance works.

- Conducting periodic inspections and tests on protection installations, and periodic monitoring of workers to ensure their compliance with these rules in terms of wearing the clothing and equipment prepared therefor.

- Ensuring the readiness of protection equipment to operate when necessary.

- Establishing periodic and regular reports on the effectiveness of the established regulations and submitting proposals regarding the necessity of amendments or development when required.

- Investigating accidents that occur, analysing them to ascertain their causes, and submitting proposals regarding their avoidance in the future.

- Monitoring the maintenance of this equipment, proposing alternative equipment and all parts, apparatus, and materials necessary for the application of protection and prevention rules, and following up on all stages until they are obtained.

Hydroelectric Plants Service.

This Service shall undertake:

- The production of electrical energy, the maintenance of units and various equipment, and responsibility therefor from the energy outlets of the hydroelectric plants to the lines.

Central Department.

This Department shall undertake the following basic duties:

- Collecting information of all kinds from all plants.

- Collecting the draft budgets of the plants, studying and analysing them, pursuing ratifications and approvals, and pursuing their execution and disbursement.

- Addressing emergency matters and pursuing the procurement of spare parts and consumable materials, and relations with the concerned directorates and authorities.

- Expressing an opinion on all administrative, technical, and financial matters.

- Establishing periodic maintenance programmes for all plants in coordination with the competent directorates.

- Establishing plans to improve performance and rectify conditions in the various units of the Production Directorate.

Transmission Directorate.

This Directorate shall consist of:

- The Energy Movement Service.

- The High Voltage Networks Service.

- The Main Transformer Substations Service.

- The Protection and Communications Service.

Energy Movement Service.

This Service shall consist of:

- The Coordination Department.

- The Statistics and Analysis Department.

- The Energy Exchange Department.

Coordination Department

This Department shall undertake the following basic duties:

- Establishing and executing plant operation programmes in accordance with daily and annual consumption curves and the requirements of cost and safety elements, and addressing any emergency affecting these programmes.

- Establishing programmes for intervention on the networks and supervising their execution within the technical rules and the rules of safety and security.

- Addressing emergency interventions.

- Establishing periodic repair programmes in the plants and substations in agreement with the competent authorities.

- Recording all information relating to the operation of the network and interventions thereon of whatever kind, and in particular isolation and restoration manoeuvres and all accidents of all kinds, in accordance with a special register established for this purpose.

- Responsibility for the control of the network, along with the powers and duties entailed thereby.

- Proposing partial developments to the elements of the substations and networks in accordance with their absorption capacities and the requirements of operation.

- Operating the informatics equipment pertaining to the control of the network with its various systems, maintaining it along with the programmes pertaining thereto, and introducing amendments to these programmes in accordance with the requirements of operation.

Statistics and Analysis Department:

This Department shall undertake the following basic duties:

- Reviewing the sources of information received by or available in the Energy Movement Service, including registers, audio recordings, and others, and classifying and preserving them.

- Studying and analysing this information, drawing conclusions and solutions, and notifying the concerned authorities in the Establishment thereof within periodic reports.

- Collecting the results of these reports, placing them in statistical bulletins, and distributing them to the concerned authorities.

Energy Exchange Department.

This Department shall undertake the following basic duties:

- Negotiating with the concerned parties to draw up energy exchange contracts (sale and purchase thereof) in accordance with the tariffs proposed by the Accounting Service in the Financial Affairs Directorate.

- Proposing draft contracts and studying them with the Litigation and Legal Affairs Service to place them in their final form, and pursuing their course to obtain the approval of the competent authorities.

- Supervising the execution of these contracts and addressing emergency matters and disputes within the limits of the clauses of these contracts.

- Reading the meters specific to energy exchange, auditing the issuance documents, and approving their contents.

High Voltage Networks Service.

This Service shall consist of:

- The Underground Networks Department.

- The Overhead Networks Department.

Underground Networks Department.

Overhead Networks Department.

Each of the two Departments shall assume the following primary functions:

Operating and maintaining power transmission lines (underground cables and overhead lines) of high voltage of 66 kilovolts and above, starting from the outlets of the generation plants up to the power inlets and outlets at the main transformer substations, and these functions shall include, inter alia, the following:

- Preparing and executing periodic preventive maintenance programmes for these installations in coordination with the concerned authorities in the Transmission Directorate.

- Anticipating the needs for tools and equipment required for periodic and emergency maintenance.

- Ensuring ordinary and emergency maintenance.

- Detecting the causes of recurring faults and submitting the necessary proposals to improve the performance and efficiency of these installations.

- Keeping special registers and maps of the condition of these installations and updating them so that they are ready for inspection at any time whatsoever.

Main Transformer Substations Service.

This Service shall consist of:

- Beirut and Mount Lebanon Substations Department.

- Regional Substations Department.

- Technical Department.

Beirut and Mount Lebanon Substations Department.

- Regional Substations Department.

Each of the two Departments shall assume, within its geographical scope, the following primary functions:

Operating and maintaining high voltage /high voltage/ medium voltage main transformer substations, and these functions shall primarily include the following:

- Ensuring the uninterrupted operation of the main transformer substations around the clock.

- Preparing and executing a preventive maintenance programme in the main transformer substations.

- Ensuring ordinary emergency maintenance and repairs, whereas repairs of an exceptional and joint nature between substations shall be carried out in cooperation with the central intervention teams in the Technical Department. - Keeping a register in the substations in which all events and interventions of all kinds are recorded.

- Anticipating the needs for tools and equipment necessary to carry out maintenance of all kinds.

Technical Department.

This Department shall assume the following primary functions:

- Ensuring maintenance and interventions in all main substations which are characterised by a special nature falling outside the scope of ordinary works, namely, by way of example (oil refining - maintenance of batteries and chargers - intervention on transformers - heavy equipment transport operations - maintenance of air compressors...).

- Assisting local teams in interventions upon their request. - Organising maintenance and operation in all substations. Receiving reports containing all operation events in all sections of the network (lines - cables - communications - power coordination - substations...).

- Studying and analysing these reports and drawing their conclusions and their repercussions on operation.

- Translating these conclusions into recommendations that appear through preventive maintenance programmes and notifying them to the concerned authorities inside and outside the Transmission Directorate.

Protection and Communications Service.

This Service shall consist of:

- Protection Department.

- Communications Department.

- Workshop and Laboratory Section.

Protection Department.

This Department shall assume the following primary functions:

- Putting into execution and operating the schemes of the protection systems on the network laid down by the Studies Directorate.

- Maintaining and operating the equipment pertaining to the protection systems.

- Contributing to the analysis of events on the network in cooperation with the Technical Department in the Main Transformer Substations Service and with the Studies Directorate, and devising solutions.

- Anticipating the needs for tools and equipment for maintenance.

Communications Department.

This Department shall assume the following primary functions:

- Putting into execution and operating the schemes of the communications systems adopted by the Establishment.

- Operating, exploiting and monitoring the communications systems on the network.

- Maintaining and operating the equipment pertaining to wired and wireless communications located in the various centres of the Establishment, including vehicles.

- Contributing to the handling of events on the network in coordination with the concerned Services, especially those relating to joint equipment.

- Anticipating the needs for tools and equipment.

Workshop and Laboratory Section.

This Section shall assume the following primary functions:

- Adjusting and calibrating the equipment pertaining to the Protection and Communications Departments.

- Carrying out the repair of devices and equipment pertaining to the Protection and Communications Departments.

- Providing electrical, mechanical and electronic laboratories for the needs of the various units of the Establishment.

Distribution Directorate in Beirut and Mount Lebanon.

This Directorate shall consist of:

- Distribution Service in Beirut.

- Distribution Service in Mount Lebanon.

- Technical Service.

- Central Department.

This Directorate shall assume the works of distributing electrical power to consumers and shall be responsible for the networks and distribution substations located within its geographical scope, starting from the points of delivery of power to it at the outlets of the medium voltage cells in the high voltage / medium voltage main transformer substations, and up to the points of delivery of power to subscribers.

Distribution Service in Beirut.

This Service shall consist of:

- Beirut Department.

- Antelias Department .

- Chiyah Department.

- Overhead Medium Voltage Networks and Underground Networks Department.

- Operations and Manoeuvres Department.

The Departments of Beirut, Antelias and Chiyah shall, each within its geographic scope, undertake the following basic tasks:

- Receiving customer applications and receiving their follow-ups and complaints, which includes:

= Accepting subscriber follow-ups and examining and processing their complaints.

= Examining applications of all types (new subscription - upgrading an existing subscription, transferring a subscription...) on medium and low voltage.

= Inspecting the site required to be connected to the current and carrying out the measurement operation.

= Studying the quality of subscriber connections and the manner of execution and taking or proposing the appropriate decisions for connection in accordance with the rules and in the light of the type of subscription and the required capacity.

= Executing the subscription with all the stages it requires - preparing equipment - installing branches - installing meters etc..

= Establishing a special box card for each building on which all information regarding this building and the amendments that occur thereto are recorded.

= Keeping a register to follow up on customer applications on which the technical and administrative information relating to the application is recorded from the time of its submission until the time of its fulfilment and all the amendments that occur thereto.

- Responsibility for distribution networks, which includes:

= Carrying out periodic maintenance on the distribution network and on various installations, including repairing connections and replacing meters where necessary.

= Repairing faults on the distribution network.

- Power supply monitoring works, which includes:

= Carrying out periodic inspections of boxes, meter rooms and their contents, subscriber connections, and all metering devices at consumers' premises to verify their safety, proper functioning, and normal operation.

= Detecting violations and drawing up reports against violators.

= Settling these reports in accordance with a special system for suppressing violations of all types.

= Removing violations and encroachments on the distribution network.

- Collection and meter reading works, which includes:

= Reading the meters placed at subscribers' premises, collecting the consumption value, and collecting overdue bills.

= Carrying out transactions for cutting off the current from defaulting payers as well as transactions for restoring it according to the regulations and laws in force.

= Preparing periodic reports on the outcome of the collection of each issue.

- General organisational and technical works, among which:

= Investigating significant outages and faults and their causes, submitting proposals regarding them, and preparing monthly statistics.

= Determining the need for equipment, tools, and devices and taking the necessary measures to secure them in due time.

- Preparing reports on work accidents.

= Keeping the equipment and tools warehouse to execute subscribers' applications and to ensure the maintenance of ordinary and emergency faults.

= Keeping a cash desk for paying transactions and arrears and accounting with collectors

Department of Overhead Medium Voltage Networks and Underground Networks.

This Department shall undertake the following basic tasks:

- Equipping and extending the overhead or underground medium voltage network starting from the main high voltage / medium voltage substations.

- Equipping and extending the underground low voltage networks for the various departments of the Service.

- Equipping overhead substations.

- Executing underground outlets starting from distribution substations up to the buildings.

- Periodic maintenance and repairs on these networks located within the scope of its responsibility.

Department of Operations and Manoeuvres.

This Department shall undertake the following basic tasks:

- Managing an operations room covering the scope of work of the various departments of the Service.

- Receiving notices of current outages and various works and addressing them immediately.

- Round-the-clock shift duty to identify faults and carry out the necessary repairs on the various sections of the networks in order to secure the current and confine the faults to the narrowest possible scope.

- Carrying out manoeuvres and operations of cutting off and restoring the current required by repair operations.

- Preparing periodic reports containing statistics on the types of faults on the distribution network and the extent of effectiveness of the intervention teams, and communicating them to the concerned authorities.

Distribution Service in Mount Lebanon.

This Service shall consist of:

- Department of Jounieh.

- Department of Bikfaya.

- Department of Beiteddine.

- Department of Aley.

- Department of Overhead Medium Voltage Networks and Underground Networks.

These Departments shall, each within its geographic scope (with the exception of the Department of Overhead Medium Voltage Networks and Underground Networks), starting from their centres and from the centres of the sections affiliated to them, undertake the same basic tasks as those undertaken by the distribution departments in the Distribution Service in Beirut, the subject of Article 90 of this Decree, in addition to the tasks of the Department of Operations and Manoeuvres, the subject of Article 92 thereof.

Department of Overhead Medium Voltage Networks and Underground Networks.

This Department shall undertake the basic tasks undertaken by the same Department in the Distribution Service in Beirut, the subject of Article 91 of this Decree.

The Technical Service.

This Service shall consist of:

- Department of Exploitation Studies and Distribution Networks.

- Department of the Public Lighting Network.

- Department of Workshops and Metering, Disconnection and Transformer Devices.

Department of Exploitation Studies and Distribution Networks.

This Department shall undertake the following basic tasks:

- Collecting information about the distribution network, preserving it, and communicating it to the Statistics and Informatics Service in the Directorate of Studies.

- Examining operations for the rehabilitation and renewal of parts of the distribution network.

- Examining the cost of extending the distribution network within subdivision projects.

- Analysing the cost relating to various distribution works and drawing conclusions

- Estimating the materials required for exploitation and maintenance and following up on obtaining them.

- Preparing the draft budget of the Directorate.

- Following up on exploitation safety systems and examining their development and modernisation

- Unifying the means and methods of exploitation and maintenance in the departments of this Directorate.

- Analysing the causes of faults and taking the appropriate measures to reduce them and avoid them where necessary.

- Studying and following up on the state of the distribution network to find appropriate solutions in order to ensure its readiness to distribute the current continuously.

- Improving work methods and execution works on the distribution network.

- Anticipating the evolution of the load, examining how to address it, proposing what is necessary, and taking measures to prevent the waste of energy.

- Monitoring the application of protection rules and the safety of workers and customers.

Department of the Public Lighting Network.

This Department shall undertake the following basic tasks:

- Studying the public lighting network, laying down a plan for its execution, and carrying out contracting transactions.

- Supervising the execution of this network.

- Monitoring equipment, materials, and spare parts.

- Securing communications with the concerned authorities outside the Establishment, such as municipalities, to draw up maintenance contracts for this network.

- Maintaining this network and conducting round-the-clock patrols to monitor the state of lighting therein.

Department of Workshops and Metering, Disconnection and Transformer Devices.

This Department shall undertake the following basic tasks:

- Managing the workshop of transformers and circuit breakers.

- Securing the repair of faulty transformers in the Establishment's workshop or outside it.

- Monitoring the movement and storage of transformers and keeping a register thereof on which all information is recorded (receipt and delivery, dispatch and return)

- Inspecting and refining transformer oils in the workshop continuously and maintaining the refining devices.

- Inspecting and calibrating meters, automatic circuit breakers, and auxiliary equipment (relays, secondary transformers...) and managing the warehouse pertaining to them (receipt and delivery, dispatch and return).

- Installing and maintaining the meters of private substations (medium voltage subscriptions), following up on them, keeping a register thereof on which the information pertaining to them is recorded, detecting violations on these subscriptions, and drawing up reports against violators.

The Central Section.

This section shall undertake the following fundamental duties:

- Providing assistance to the Director in managing the affairs of the Directorate.

- The secretariat of the Directorate.

- Registering outgoing and incoming mail.

- Receiving inquiries and guiding the parties concerned.

- Preparing quarterly and annual reports and submitting them to the competent authorities.

- Ensuring the distribution of information to all services and sections of this Directorate.

The Regional Distribution Directorate.

This Directorate shall consist of:

- The Distribution Service in the North.

- The Distribution Service in the South.

- The Distribution Service in the Bekaa.

- The Technical Service.

- A Central Section.

The Distribution Service in the North.

This service shall consist of:

- The Tripoli Section.

- The Halba Section.

- The Batroun Section.

- The Overhead Medium Voltage Networks and Underground Networks Section.

The Distribution Service in the South.

This service shall consist of:

- The Sidon Section.

- The Nabatieh Section.

- The Tyre Section.

- The Overhead Medium Voltage Networks and Underground Networks Section.

The Distribution Service in the Bekaa.

This service shall consist of:

- The Baalbek Section.

- The Chtaura Section.

- The Joub Jannine Section

- The Overhead Medium Voltage Networks and Underground Networks Section.

These sections, each within its geographic scope, proceeding from their centers and from the centers of the divisions affiliated with them, shall undertake the same fundamental duties undertaken by the distribution sections in the Distribution Service in Mount Lebanon, the subject of Article 94 and Article 95 of this Decree.

The Technical Service.

This service shall consist of:

- The Operation Studies and Distribution Networks Section.

- The Public Lighting Network Section.

- The Workshops, Metering Devices, Disconnection and Transformers Section.

Each of these sections shall undertake the same fundamental duties undertaken by the sections of the Technical Service in the Distribution Directorate in Beirut and Mount Lebanon, the subject of Articles 96, 97, 98 and 99 of this Decree.

The Central Section.

This section shall undertake the fundamental duties undertaken by the Central Section in the Distribution Directorate in Beirut and Mount Lebanon, the subject of Article 100 of this Decree.

Vacancies in the posts of the First Rank of the Second Category shall be filled as follows:

In the posts of the Administrative Corps (2/1 Administrative).

By selection from among the employees of the Establishment:

- Who belong to the Second Rank of the Second Category of the Administrative Corps.

- Who hold a university degree according to the required specialization of a level recognized as equivalent to the level of degrees issued by the Lebanese University in this specialization.

- Who belong to at least the ten highest steps in the aforementioned rank.

In the posts of the Technical Corps (2/1 Technical).

By selection from among the employees of the Establishment:

- Who belong to the Second Rank of the Second Category of the Technical Corps.

- Who hold an engineering degree according to the required specialization.

- Who have obtained a permit to practice the engineering profession in Lebanon.

- Who are affiliated with the Order of Engineers.

- Who belong to at least the ten highest steps in the aforementioned rank.

(Paragraph added pursuant to Decree 967 dated 7/2/2008 O.G. 8)

In the event that there are no employees who meet the selection conditions set forth above, a competitive examination restricted to the employees concerned may be held in accordance with the rules, provided that they are from that corps and hold the academic qualifications required for each of the posts in which employment is proposed.

And where it is not possible to find candidates from among the employees of the Establishment in accordance with the foregoing, a competitive examination may be held in accordance with the rules in which the employees of the Establishment and candidates from outside the Establishment shall be entitled to participate, provided that all candidates, whether from among the employees of the Establishment or from outside it, must possess the academic qualifications prescribed for each of the posts in which employment is required.

The new steps set forth in Tables No. 3, 4, 5, 7, 14, 15, 16 and 18 annexed to Decree No. 2444 dated 11/2/2000 shall be adopted for promotion to the higher categories or ranks specified in Articles 109, 110, 111 and 113 of Decree 13537 dated 19/11/1998 instead of the old steps corresponding to them.

Vacancies in the posts of the Second Rank of the Second Category shall be filled as follows:

In the posts of the Administrative Corps (2/2 Administrative).

By selection from among the employees of the Establishment:

- Who belong to at least the ten highest steps in the First Rank of the Third Category of the Administrative Corps.

- Who hold a university degree according to the required specialization of a level recognized as equivalent to the level of degrees issued by the Lebanese University in this specialization.

- Who have successfully completed a training course at the National Institute of Administration and Development.

In the posts of the Technical Corps (2/2 Technical).

By selection from among the employees of the Establishment:

- Who belong to at least the ten highest steps in the First Rank of the Third Category of the Technical Corps.

- Who hold an engineering degree according to the required specialization.

- Who have obtained a permit to practice the engineering profession in Lebanon.

- Who are affiliated with the Order of Engineers.

- Who have successfully completed a training course at the National Institute of Administration and Development.

(Paragraph added pursuant to Decree 967 dated 7/2/2008 O.G. 8)

In the event that there are no employees who meet the selection conditions set forth above, a competitive examination restricted to the employees concerned may be held in accordance with the rules, provided that they are from that corps and hold the academic qualifications required for each of the posts in which employment is proposed.

And where it is not possible to find candidates from among the employees of the Establishment in accordance with the foregoing, a competitive examination may be held in accordance with the rules in which the employees of the Establishment and candidates from outside the Establishment shall be entitled to participate, provided that all candidates, whether from among the employees of the Establishment or from outside it, must possess the academic qualifications prescribed for each of the posts in which employment is required.

The new steps set forth in Tables No. 3, 4, 5, 7, 14, 15, 16 and 18 annexed to Decree No. 2444 dated 11/2/2000 shall be adopted for promotion to the higher categories or ranks specified in Articles 109, 110, 111 and 113 of Decree 13537 dated 19/11/1998 instead of the old steps corresponding to them.

Vacant positions in the posts of the First Rank of the Third Category shall be filled as follows:

In the posts of the Administrative Cadre (3/1 Administrative).

By selection from among the employees of the Establishment:

- Belonging to at least the nine highest steps in the Second Rank (A) of the Third Category of the Administrative Cadre.

- Holding a university degree according to the required specialisation of a level recognised as equivalent to the level of degrees issued by the Lebanese University in this specialisation.

In the posts of the Technical Cadre (3/1 Technical).

By selection from among the employees of the Establishment:

- Belonging to at least the nine highest steps in the Second Rank (A) of the Third Category of the Technical Cadre.

- Holding an engineering diploma according to the required specialisation.

- Having obtained a permit to practise the profession of engineering in Lebanon.

- Registered with the Order of Engineers.

(Paragraph added pursuant to Decree 967 dated 7/2/2008 O.G. 8)

In the event that there are no employees who meet the conditions for selection set forth above, a restricted competitive examination may be held for the concerned employees in accordance with the rules, provided that they belong to that cadre and hold the academic qualifications required for each of the posts in which employment is proposed.

Where it is not possible to find candidates from among the employees of the Establishment in accordance with the foregoing, a competitive examination may be held in accordance with the rules in which the employees of the Establishment and candidates from outside the Establishment shall be entitled to participate, provided that all candidates, whether from among the employees of the Establishment or from outside it, hold the academic qualifications prescribed for each of the posts in which employment is required.

The new steps set forth in Tables No. 3, 4, 5, 7, 14, 15, 16 and 18 annexed to Decree No. 2444 dated 11/2/2000 shall be adopted for promotion to the higher categories or ranks specified in Articles 109, 110, 111 and 113 of Decree 13537 dated 19/11/1998 in place of the old steps corresponding thereto.

Vacant positions in the posts of the Second Rank (A) of the Third Category in the Administrative and Technical Cadres shall be filled by way of a competitive examination conducted in accordance with the rules in which the employees of the Establishment and candidates from outside the Establishment shall be entitled to participate, provided that all candidates, whether from among the employees of the Establishment or from

outside it, meet the following special conditions:

In the posts of the Administrative Cadre (3/2 (A) Administrative).

- A university degree according to the required specialisation of a level recognised as equivalent to the level of degrees issued by the Lebanese University in this specialisation.

Or

- The Technical Teaching Licence (Licence d'Enseignement Technique) or the Technical Licence (Licence Technique) according to the required specialisation.

Or

- The Technical Superior Diploma (Brevet de Technicien Supérieur) with experience in the specialisation of not less than four years.

In the posts of the Technical Cadre (3/2 (A) Technical).

- A diploma in engineering according to the required specialisation.

- A permit to practise the profession of engineering in Lebanon.

- Registration with the Order of Engineers.

Vacant positions in the posts of the Second Rank (B) of the Third Category in the Administrative and Technical Cadres shall be filled by selection from among the employees of the Establishment belonging to at least one of the four highest steps in the First Rank of the Fourth Category of the concerned cadre. In the event that there are no employees who meet the conditions above, a restricted competitive examination may be held in accordance with the rules in which the employees of the First Rank of the Fourth Category of the concerned cadre shall participate. Where it is not possible to find candidates from among the employees of the Establishment in accordance with the foregoing, a competitive examination may be held in accordance with the rules in which the employees of the Establishment and candidates from outside the Establishment shall be entitled to participate, provided that all candidates, whether from among the employees of the Establishment or from outside it, meet the following special conditions:

In the posts of the Administrative Cadre (3/2 (B) Administrative).

- The Technical Superior Diploma (Brevet de Technicien Supérieur) or at least its equivalent according to the required specialisation.

- Or the Lebanese Baccalaureate certificate

- Or at least its equivalent with 8 years of experience in the required specialisation.

- The Technical Baccalaureate certificate

- Or at least its equivalent according to the required specialisation, or the Higher Vocational Qualification Certificate or at least its equivalent according to the required specialisation with 6 years of experience in the required specialisation.

In the posts of the Technical Cadre (3/2 (B) Technical).

- The Technical Superior Diploma (Brevet de Technicien Supérieur) or at least its equivalent according to the required specialisation.

Or - the Technical Baccalaureate certificate -

or at least its equivalent according to the required specialisation, or the Higher Vocational Qualification Certificate or its equivalent according to the required specialisation with 10 years of experience in the required specialisation.

Or - the Technical Baccalaureate certificate - Part One - or at least its equivalent according to the required specialisation with experience in this specialisation of not less than 10 years in the First Rank of the Fourth Category of the same cadre or 12 years outside the Establishment or outside this category of the same cadre.

(Paragraph added by Decree 967 dated 7/2/2008 O.G. 8)

The new steps set forth in Tables No. 3, 4, 5, 7, 14, 15, 16 and 18 annexed to Decree No. 2444 dated 11/2/2000 shall be adopted for promotion to the higher categories or ranks specified in Articles 109, 110, 111 and 113 of Decree 13537 dated 19/11/1998 in place of the old steps corresponding thereto.

- Schools that teach the curricula of the intermediate and secondary cycles.

- Male and female teacher training colleges

- Male and female teacher training colleges for physical education.

And they shall be classified into three categories:

Shall be classified in the First Category:

1- Secondary education teachers who have entered into the permanent establishment and who hold

the teaching licence degree or its equivalent, provided that they have practised

secondary education for at least three years after obtaining the licence degree.

2- Holders of a State Doctorate in Sciences or in Letters or its

equivalent, preceded by a teaching licence degree or its equivalent.

3- Holders of a Doctorate in Engineering, or a P.H.D. doctorate, provided that

they have practised secondary education for a period of at least one year after

obtaining the degree.

4- Holders of a teaching licence degree or an engineering degree from a recognised higher

institute or a Master's degree (M.A.) or the equivalent of these degrees

or a licence degree in Lebanese Law or a licence degree in Political

and Economic Sciences (to teach the subject of civic education only) or

a licence degree in Social Sciences (to teach the subject of sociology

and civic education only), provided that all holders of these degrees

have practised secondary education for a period of at least three years after

Holders of a Doctorate or a licence degree in the subject of Philosophy

(to teach the subject of philosophy and civilisations only)

- Holders of a diploma in computer engineering or a licence degree

in informatics or the Technical Teaching Licence in

Informatics (LET) (to teach the subject of informatics only)

- Holders of a licence degree in technology or a licence degree

in applied sciences or the Technical Teaching Licence

in industrial specialisations (to teach the subject of technology

only)

- Preference in contracting shall be given to holders of the higher degree

and to the grade stated therein

4- Artists holding a certificate of completion of studies from a recognised higher institute.

The hourly contracting wage for teaching in schools of the intermediate and secondary cycles, male and female teacher training colleges, and male and female teacher training colleges for physical education shall be amended to become as follows:

1 - The First Category 23500 L.L. instead of 16680 L.L.

2 - The Second Category 18500 L.L. instead of 13200 L.L.

3 - The Third Category 15000 L.L. instead of 10560 L.L.

1- Teachers of the First and Second Categories shall work in male and female teacher training colleges, male and female teacher training colleges for physical education, and classes of the secondary cycle.

2- Teachers of the Second and Third Categories shall work in classes of the intermediate cycle.

3- Teachers of the First Category may not work in the classes mentioned in the second paragraph of this Article, nor may teachers of the Third Category work in the classes mentioned in the first paragraph of this Article, except pursuant to a reasoned request submitted by the school principal and approved by the Director or the Head of Service.
Employed teachers shall be treated in the same manner as non-employed teachers in respect of the hourly wage, provided that the employees work outside the official working hours of their workplace.

Shall retain the category in which they were classified: teachers who were classified in either the First or Second Category by the Council of the Lebanese University in accordance with the provisions of Decree No. 2925 dated 7/11/1953

Contracting to provide education in the public secondary and intermediate education cycles and in male and female teacher training colleges shall be prohibited except in exceptional cases the reasons for which are justified by the administration requesting the contracting. And in this exceptional case, preference in contracting shall be given to holders of the teaching licence degree who are not secondary education teachers entered into the permanent establishment of private and public schools, or with employees of public administrations, autonomous agencies, and municipalities (with the exception of teachers of the Ministry of National Education the teaching licence degree), except in the event that there are no contracting applications submitted by the holders of the teaching licence degree mentioned above.
A contracted teacher may not teach anything other than the subject or subjects falling within his specialisation.

An employee may not undertake teaching in one of the schools provided for in the first Article of this Decree except after authorisation is granted to him by a decision from the head of the administration to which he belongs. And the position he occupies and the other duties he performs shall be stated in this decision.

1- The nature of the position he occupies and the other duties he performs.

2- His academic rank and whether he has practised secondary teaching in the past, stating the institutes or schools in which he practised teaching.

3- The subject or subjects he wishes to teach and the school in which he intends to teach.

It is a condition for the granting of the licence provided for in the eleventh Article of this Decree that the total weekly teaching hours for all subjects and in the various schools shall not exceed, the hours prescribed in accordance with the regulations and laws in force.

The Ministry of National Education, Youth and Sports shall announce every year its need for contracted teachers during the period falling between the tenth of the month of April and the tenth of the month of July, provided that the final deadline for submitting applications is fixed on the sixteenth of the month of August.

The duration of the contract shall be fixed for one school year. The Civil Service Board shall be notified, within a time limit not exceeding the end of the month of November of each year, of a list of the names of the old and new contracted teachers whose applications have been accepted and who have actually joined the public secondary schools in need of their services in teaching only, provided that this list includes the basic information contained in the contract of each of them.
All provisions contrary to this Decree or inconsistent with its content are repealed, and in particular the provisions of Decree No. 2925 dated 7/11/1953 and Decree No. 4645 dated 25/3/1954.
This Decree shall enter into force starting from the academic year 1971 - 1972
This Decree shall be published and notified where the need calls.

The provisions of Article 2 of Decree No. 1436 dated 23 March 1950 are repealed and replaced by the following provisions:

"Article 2 (New):

1- The opening of private schools shall be subject to a licence granted by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of National Education, Youth and Sports, provided that teaching in the licensed school shall not commence until after obtaining a permit granted by a decision of the said Minister upon the proposal of the Director General of National Education, in accordance with the provisions of this Decree. A private school means every school for upbringing and education headed or managed by individuals, associations or religious bodies and not governed by special regulations.

2- The granting of a building permit for buildings pertaining to the schools concerned by the provisions of this Decree shall be conditional upon the prior issuance of the decree licensing the opening of the school".

The provisions of Article 6 of Decree No. 1436 dated 23 March 1950, as amended by Decree No. 4030 dated 15/07/1987, are repealed up to item 7 inclusive and replaced by the following provisions: "

Article 6 (New): First: The application to obtain the licence provided for in Article 2 (New) shall be submitted to the Ministry of National Education, Youth and Sports, Private Education Department.

There shall be stated therein:

A- The type of school:

1- In the event that it is for a curricular activity, the stages of education must be specified.

2- In the event that it is for a non-curricular activity, this activity must be specified: religious instruction, language instruction, tutoring lessons in certain subjects,...

3- For day students or for boarders, for boys or for girls, co-educational.

B- The name intended to be adopted for the school.

C- The number of the real property, its location, its area and the name of its owner.

Second:

A- If the applicant for the licence is a natural person, he must fulfil the following conditions:

1- That he has completed the twenty-fifth year of his age.

2- Be of good conduct.

3- Hold at least the Lebanese Baccalaureate Certificate of Secondary Education, or its official equivalent.

4- Enjoy his civil rights.

5- Not have been convicted of a felony or an attempted felony of any kind whatsoever, or of a disgraceful misdemeanour or an attempted disgraceful misdemeanour; the misdemeanours set forth in Article 4 (paragraph E) of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12 June 1959 shall be considered disgraceful.

6- Be authorised to work on Lebanese territory in the field of upbringing or education if he is non-Lebanese.

B- A natural person applying for the licence must attach to his application the following documents:

1- A copy of his identity card.

2- A copy of his judicial record.

3- A certificate of his good conduct issued by the local administrative authority.

4- A certified copy of his academic qualification.

5 - A statement of the places in which he has resided during the last five years and of the professions he has practised during this period.

6- A specimen of his signature.

7- A permit to work on Lebanese territory in the field of upbringing or education if he is non-Lebanese.

C- If there are multiple applicants for the licence, they must declare in the body of the application whom they have chosen from among themselves to represent them before the Ministry of National Education, Youth and Sports in all matters relating to the licence formality.

Third:

If the applicant for the licence is a legal person and not a religious body, it is required that upbringing or education be among its objectives, and that it be authorised to work on Lebanese territory in this field if it is non-Lebanese.

It must attach to its application the following documents:

1- A certified copy of its bylaws.

2- A statement of its official licence (acknowledgement of receipt).

3- A certified copy of its permit to work on Lebanese territory in the field of upbringing or education, if it is non-Lebanese.

4- A specimen of its seal.

5- A statement signed by its representative before the public authorities mentioning his name, his place of residence, his address and the nature of his work.

6- A specimen of the signature of this representative of its.

However, if the applicant for the licence is a religious body, documents Nos. 4, 5 and 6 mentioned in this section shall suffice from it. Fourth: The applicant for the licence, whether a natural or a legal person, must also attach to his application:

1- A real estate certificate on the status of the real property.

2- An approval in principle from the owner of the real property for the use of his real property for the purpose specified in the application.

3- A survey and location map of the real property.

4- An undertaking to effectively supervise the school and watch over its educational, moral and national activities. ' Fifth: The application for a permit to commence teaching shall be submitted to the Ministry of National Education, Youth and Sports - Private Education Department - containing the name of the proposed principal, the name of the assistant principal where applicable, the school schedule (daytime, evening, winter, with the right to teach in summer) and the first foreign language adopted.

The following documents shall be attached to the application:

A- A certified copy of the licensing decree.

B- The papers relating to the proposed principal and to the assistant principal where applicable, which are:

1- A copy of his identity card.

2- A copy of his judicial record.

3- A certificate of his good conduct issued by the local administrative authority.

4- A certified copy of his academic qualification.

5- A certificate of his teaching experience in the event that such experience is required by law.

6- A statement of the places in which he has resided during the last five years and of the professions he has practised during this period.

7- A specimen of his signature.

8- A declaration by him of his acceptance to assume the management, his acquaintance with the laws and regulations governing private schools, his readiness to bear the responsibilities resulting from the performance of his duties, and his undertaking not to combine the management of the school with any work incompatible with this mission.

9- His permit to work in the field of upbringing or education if he is non-Lebanese.

C- The papers specific to the school building (buildings, playgrounds, open spaces and gardens):

1- An architectural plan of the buildings certified by the Order of Engineers and Architects, comprising the dimensions of the classrooms and the halls for various educational activities (libraries, laboratories, sports...) and the open playgrounds and their dimensions and the winter sheds.

2- A statement by a licensed civil engineer of the areas of each of the classrooms, halls, and open and covered playgrounds.

3- A certificate from a licensed civil engineer proving the structural soundness of the building and its suitability for school use.

4- A certificate from the competent health authority (the sanitary engineer in Beirut and the district physician in the governorates) proving that the condition of the building conforms to the health laws. If the school admits boarding students, the certificate must state the number of rooms and halls designated for sleeping and specify the number of students who can be accommodated therein. This certificate shall be certified by the Ministry of Public Health.

5- A title of occupancy (title deed, contract, lease...).

6- An occupancy permit or a certificate of completion of construction.

7- An approval from the Directorate of Civil Defence with respect to securing the requirements of civil defence.

It is required that the specifications legally required in the school building be secured at least at their minimum level.

D- A statement of the fire extinguishers and first-aid kits in each floor or wing.

E- A statement of the school furniture, including benches, tables, blackboards and the like.

F- Detailed statements of the equipment, instruments and supplies intended for practical work required for teaching the official curriculum, covering:

1- Books, publications, dictionaries and the like contained in the school library.

2- Laboratory apparatus, instruments and supplies for each of the curricular subjects that require the same.

3- Visual aids, geographical maps and educational games specific to children.

4- Physical education apparatus, instruments and supplies. (Items 8 to 12 remain without amendment).

Subject to the conditions provided for in First to Fourth of Article Six (new), it is required that the real property which is the subject of the application for the licence to open the school thereon be healthy in location, not exposed to factory smoke and to noise, on the basis of the opinion of the competent Governor, and that the granting of the licence not conflict with the other requirements of public order.

The provisions of Articles Four and Five of Decree No. 1436 dated 23 March 1950 are repealed and replaced by the following provisions:

"Article Four (new)- The provisions of Paragraph (a) of Section Second of Article Six (new) shall apply to the principal and the assistant principal, provided that, with respect to academic qualifications, the provisions of Decree No. 2896 dated 15/10/1992 shall be observed.

"Article Five (new)- The principal shall not be entitled to admit among the teaching staff in his school anyone who has been convicted of a felony or an attempted felony of whatever kind, or of a disgraceful misdemeanour or an attempted disgraceful misdemeanour, and the misdemeanours set forth in Article - 4 - (Paragraph e) of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12 June 1959 shall be deemed disgraceful".

The Director General of National Education shall carry out the following:
