b- Seek the opinion of the Directorate General of General Security and the competent Governor regarding the application for the licence.

c- Seek the opinion of the Directorate General of General Security with respect to the principal and the assistant principal.

a- There shall be specified in the licence decree:

1- The name of the school and its location (the number of the real property and the cadastral area).

2- The name of the licence holder and the date and place of his birth.

3- The type of the school.

b- The decree must include an explicit text that the licence granted lapses automatically if its holder does not obtain, within five years from the granting thereof, the permit to commence teaching provided for in Article Two (new) above, unless the licence is renewed by decree for one time only for reasoned causes. In the event that the said permit is not obtained during the renewal period, the licence lapses finally.

The provisions of Article Seven of Decree No. 1436 dated 23 March 1950 are repealed and replaced by the following provisions: "

Article Seven (new)

First: The Minister of National Education, Youth and Sports shall be entitled, after the approval of the Council of Ministers, to refuse for legitimate reasons to grant a licence to open a new school or schools.

Second:

a- The application for the permit to commence teaching shall be registered at the Ministry of National Education, Youth and Sports - Private Education Service - and the party concerned shall be given a provisional receipt acknowledging receipt of his application and the documents attached thereto in detail.

b- The Private Education Service shall be given a time limit of one month at most to examine the application for the permit; if it appears to it that the application file is complete with the required documents, it shall give the party concerned a final receipt acknowledging its receipt of the application and its documents.

However, if this application is not complete with those documents, the Service shall return the application file to the party concerned with a statement of the missing documents.

c- The permit decision shall be issued by the Minister of National Education, Youth and Sports after verifying the fulfilment of all the required conditions.

d- The Minister of National Education, Youth and Sports may, within a time limit of nine months from the date of delivery of the final receipt, refuse by a reasoned decision to grant the requested permit, and in the event that the said period expires and no reply of refusal, acceptance, or the necessity of completing the conditions has attached to the party concerned, the school shall be deemed permitted automatically and finally.

In the event that the Private Education Service requests the completion of the conditions, the running of the aforementioned time limit shall be suspended starting from the date of notifying the party concerned in writing of the necessity of completing them, until such completion.

a- There shall be specified in the permit decision:

1- The name of the responsible principal and his address, and the name of the assistant principal where applicable.

2- The working hours of the school.

3- The first foreign language adopted.

4- The number of pupils, both day pupils and boarders.

b- The decision must include an explicit text that the permit granted lapses automatically if teaching is not commenced in the school during the two consecutive academic years following the date of the granting thereof.

The provisions of Articles Eight and Nine of Decree No. 1436 dated 23 March 1950 are repealed and replaced by the following provisions:

"Article Eight (new)- Every modification that occurs in the type of the school or affects the provisions of this Decree must first obtain the approval of the Ministry of National Education, Youth and Sports. If a principal is replaced by another, or an assistant principal by another, the licence holder must submit to the Ministry of National Education, Youth and Sports- Private Education Service all the papers and documents relating to the new principal or the new assistant principal and provided for in this Decree".

Article Nine (new)- If the licence holder wishes to transfer the school from one real property to another, he must obtain a new licence and permit in accordance with the conditions and procedures set forth in this Decree".
The applicant for the licence must elect a domicile in Beirut for the service of official correspondence regarding his application.

The provisions of Articles Ten and Eleven of Decree No. 1436 dated 23 March 1950 are repealed and replaced by the following provisions:

" Article Ten (new)- The licence shall be withdrawn by decree in the following cases:

1- If the permit to commence teaching is not issued during the period of validity of the licence.

2- If actual teaching is not commenced in the school during two consecutive academic years following the date of granting the permit.

3- If the school ceases to practise teaching and does not resume its work after the expiry of two consecutive school years therefrom. In the latter two cases, and as a result of the withdrawal of the licence, the permit shall be cancelled by a decision of the Minister of National Education, Youth and Sports".

"Article Eleven (new)- Every private school that practises teaching without a licence or a permit shall be closed administratively".

1- In the event of the death of the holder of a private school licence, the licence shall be transferred by decree to the heirs or some of them upon the fulfilment of the required conditions, and exemption from the two conditions of age and academic degree may be granted by decree upon the proposal of the Minister of National Education, Youth and Sports, if the principal appointed by them holds a recognized university degree, and the fulfilment of 70% of the specifications of the school building shall suffice where it is impossible to satisfy them in full.

2- The heirs must submit to the Ministry of National Education, Youth and Sports -Private Education Service an application in which they declare their wish to have the licence transferred to them or to some of them according to the agreement among them, within a time limit of six months from the date of death, accompanied by the necessary probative documents and the documents specified in Paragraphs (b) and (c) of Section Second of Article Six (new).

3- The compulsory guardian or the testamentary guardian shall replace the minor in all matters relating to the application of the provisions of this Article.

4- The private school shall lose the status of being free of charge as a result of the process of transferring the licence.
The Private Education Service shall undertake the verification of the private school's compliance with the provisions that govern the opening of private schools.
All provisions that explicitly conflict with the provisions of this Decree or are not consistent with the content thereof are repealed.
This Decree shall be published and notified where needed.

The following words and expressions contained in this Decree shall have the meanings set forth below:

1 - The Minister: The Minister of Culture and Higher Education.

2 - The Ministry: The Ministry of Culture and Higher Education.

3 - The Law on Higher Education: The Law issued on 26/12/1961.

4 - The Council: The Council of Higher Education.

5 - The Institution: The private institution of higher education (university - faculty - institute) applying for a licence.

6 - The Technical Committee: The Technical Committee provided for in Article Seven of this Decree.

7 - The Secretary: The Secretary of the Council of Higher Education.

8 - Specialisation Courses: The subjects prescribed in the curricula, the number of teaching hours allocated to each of them, the number of years of study, the system of examinations, and the degrees intended to be awarded.

Every legal person wishing to establish a private institution of higher education or to introduce a faculty, an institute, a new specialisation, a geographical branch, or a new educational level in a legally existing institution must submit an application for a licence in this regard to the Registry of the Directorate General of Higher Education, accompanied by the following documents:

1 - A statement of the institutes and faculties intended to be established, the branches and academic departments, and their geographical location, including the educational specialisations, their curricula and programmes, and the degrees which the licence applicant wishes to award.

2 - A statement of the university qualifications and experience required to be met by the president of the institution, his vice-presidents, the deans, and the directors, and the proposed regulations for their appointment.

3 - The special regulations governing dealings with members of the teaching staff, together with the conditions for hourly contracting, annual contracting, and confirmation in the permanent staff of the institution, and the conditions for dismissal from service and dismissal indemnities, with mention of social benefits.

4 - A statement of the university qualifications and the academic and professional experience required to be met by members of the teaching staff in relation to the specialisations intended to be taught.

5 - The student admission regulations, the teaching and examination regulations, and the graduation conditions that shall be adopted in each specialisation.

6 - A list of the university equipment and facilities, including: laboratories, studios, workshops, libraries, sports grounds, theatre and cinema halls, the cafeteria, the shelter, the car park, and green spaces.

7 - An official deed proving the licence applicant's ownership of the real property upon which the institution is intended to be erected or proving his right to establish it thereon, accompanied by detailed plans of the university buildings and facilities mentioned in item six above, duly certified, provided that these plans include all facilities for access to the buildings and the use of their equipment, in addition to securing all public safety conditions, particularly with respect to providing special emergency exits in accordance with the texts and conditions adopted by the Directorate of Urban Planning.

1 - Subject to the provisions of Article Nine of the Law on Private Higher Education, the licence application shall be submitted to the Registry of the Ministry of Culture and Higher Education, where it shall be duly registered with all its attachments, and the Secretary of the Council of Higher Education shall, upon completion of all the required documents, proceed to submit it to the Minister, who shall convene the Council to meet within a period not exceeding one month from the date of registration.

2 - The Council shall examine the application in accordance with the provisions of the Law Regulating Higher Education, its internal regulations, and the provisions of this Decree, and shall decide on the following procedures:

a - The Council must refer the application with its attachments within two weeks to the Technical Committee provided for in Article Seven of this Decree and assign it to examine the file and draw up a report on its work and its proposals thereon, which it shall submit to the Council within a period of one month from the date it is notified of the assignment.

b - The Council may, within the period specified in Article Twelve of the Law on Higher Education, after reviewing the report of the Technical Committee, take one of the following decisions:

- Either recommend the granting of the licence provided that the licence applicant fulfils what he has undertaken in his application. Or request him to make the necessary amendments before recommending the granting of the licence.

- Or reject the application.

c - In the event of a recommendation to grant the licence, the Minister shall submit the matter to the Council of Ministers to take the appropriate decision. The Decree, upon its issuance, shall be duly notified to the party concerned in order to comply with all legal and regulatory conditions.

d - In the event that the Council of Higher Education recommends the rejection of the application, the said Council shall issue a reasoned decision which shall be duly notified to the party concerned.

e - If the licence applicant does not commence teaching in accordance with the standards and conditions provided for in this Decree, and in accordance with what he has undertaken in his application, within a period of two years from the date of issuance of the licensing Decree, the licence granted to him shall lapse ipso jure without the need for prior formal notice.

On University Buildings:

The buildings of the institution must meet the following conditions:

1 - They shall be independent and unconnected with residential, economic, or non-university educational purposes, or any other purposes that are not for higher education.

2 - They shall be erected on areas proportionate:

a - To the number of institutes and faculties intended to be established and their needs in respect of lecture halls and the number of curriculum years.

b - To the nature of the theoretical and applied specialisations intended to be taught.

c - To the number of students intended to be admitted, provided that the built-up area allocated to a single student shall not be less than four square metres, to which an area of two square metres shall be added in applied specialisations.

3 - Their architecture shall be proportionate to the teaching curricula intended to be followed and to the environmental, economic, and social characteristics of the surroundings in which they are established, in accordance with the construction and urban planning laws.

4 - There shall be annexed to them at least one hall for cultural and recreational activities (cinema or theatre and/or exhibition halls), at least one cafeteria hall, and at least one roofed area, provided that the total area of each single hall and of the roofed areas shall not be less than /280/ square metres in respect of universities.

In respect of a faculty or institute, the conditions regarding the aforementioned areas shall be reduced to one third.

5 - There shall be available to them:

- Green spaces and sports grounds of not less than four square metres per single student.

- Car parks in accordance with the construction laws, provided that they are capable of accommodating the cars of 30% of the total number of personnel working in the institution, both members of the teaching staff and employees, at the same time.

- First aid centres proportionate to the size of the institution and its geographical distribution.

6 - They shall fulfil the necessary technical conditions for sanitary installations, electricity, drinking water, and telephone networks, firefighting means, electric generators, lavatories, and wastewater sewers, in accordance with the construction and urban planning laws.

- The institution must provide the necessary laboratories, studios, and workshops according to the various specialisations intended to be taught, while specifying the capacity of each of them in a manner proportionate to the total number of students in each specialisation.

- The institution of higher education intended to be established must provide a specialised library for each faculty or institute and a central university general library, the specifications of which shall be determined by the Technical Committee provided for in this Decree, and these libraries may be combined into a single central library if the educational units are within a single complex.

- The conditions required for the establishment and equipping of university buildings shall be determined by a schedule issued by the Council of Higher Education in relation to each faculty, institute, and specialisation.

Subject to the provisions of Article 24 of this Law:

1 - The Ministry of the Interior shall determine, in the decision convoking the voters, the number of members to be elected for each municipality, and shall also determine the number of members allotted to each village where a single municipality comprises several villages, in accordance with the proportion of the population of each of them, and nomination for candidacy shall take place on this basis.

2 - The candidate who obtains the greatest number of votes of the voters shall win the election; if the votes are equal, the oldest in age shall win, and if the age is equal, recourse shall be had to drawing lots by the Registration Committee provided for in the Seventh Article of this Law.

3 - If the number of candidates is equal to the number of members required to be elected and the period for candidacy has expired, those candidates shall win unopposed, and this shall be announced by a decision of the Governor (Muhafiz) or the District Commissioner (Qaimaqam); however, if the number of candidates does not reach the number of members required to be elected at the closing of the period for candidacy, or if the withdrawal of candidates from their candidacy leads to that, new candidacies submitted three days prior to the poll may be accepted.

4 - The deposit shall be refunded to the candidate if he wins the elections or obtains at least 25% of the votes of the voters.

If the office of President of the Municipality becomes permanently vacant for any reason whatsoever at least six months prior to the end of the term of office of the Municipal Council, the Municipal Council shall convene upon the convocation of the District Commissioner (Qaimaqam) or the Governor (Muhafiz) to elect a new President from among its members within a time limit not exceeding one month from the date of the vacancy; however, no successor to the President of the Municipality shall be elected if the vacancy occurs within a period of less than six months, and in this case the Vice-President shall assume the affairs of the Presidency for the remaining period of the term of office of the Municipal Council.

The Mukhtar's Council in cities and villages shall be composed of a Mukhtar and three members, whereas in neighbourhoods a Mukhtar shall be elected without Mukhtar's Council members. The Mukhtar shall be elected by direct universal suffrage, as well as the Mukhtar's Council members whose number is determined in the decision convoking the voters in accordance with what is set forth in the Thirty-Fifth Article of this Law.

Elections of Mukhtars and Mukhtar's Councils shall be held in all Lebanese regions in accordance with the rules prescribed in this Law, with the exception of the cities and villages under Israeli occupation, where the Government shall have the right, owing to exceptional circumstances, to appoint Mukhtars and Mukhtar's Councils by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior, and the Government must call for the holding of Mukhtar elections for these towns and villages prior to the date of 30 September of the year 2001.

As for the cities and villages located in the areas of displacement where reconciliation and return thereto have not taken place, they shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of the Interior, of Municipal and Rural Affairs, and of the Affairs of the Displaced, and the Government must call for the holding of elections of Mukhtars and Mukhtar's Councils for these cities and villages whenever that becomes possible by a decision of the Council of Ministers within a period of three months from the date of this decision.
The term of office of Mukhtars and members of the Mukhtar's Councils set forth in Article 15 of the Law on Mukhtars for Mukhtar's Councils is amended so as to become six years.

It shall not be permissible to concurrently hold the office of Mukhtar or membership of the Mukhtar's Council and:

1 - Membership of the Chamber of Deputies or the assumption of a ministerial post.

2 - The presidency, vice-presidency or membership of the Municipal Council.

3 - The judiciary.

4 - Offices of the State, autonomous agencies, public institutions and municipalities.

5 - The presidency or membership of the boards of directors of autonomous agencies and public institutions.

6 - Ownership of a concession or its offices within the scope of the village or neighbourhood.

7 - Membership or offices of bodies or committees entrusted with the management of projects of public utility within the scope of the village or neighbourhood. It shall not be permissible for a Mukhtar to nominate himself as a candidate for parliamentary elections until after the lapse of two years from the end of his term of office or his resignation. This Article shall apply to Mukhtars and members of Mukhtar's Councils who are elected after the entry into force of this Law.

The Minister of the Interior may appoint the date of the Mukhtar elections on a single day for all villages and neighbourhoods, or appoint a special date for each village or neighbourhood or group of villages and neighbourhoods if the safety of the electoral operations so requires, provided that the Mukhtar elections take place in all villages and neighbourhoods within the time limits set forth in the Thirty-Fourth Article of this Law.

1 - Every person who wishes to nominate himself as a candidate for the post of Mukhtar or for membership of the Mukhtar's Body in towns and villages, and for the office of Mukhtar in neighbourhoods, must submit to the Qaimaqamiyya or the Muhafaza in the capitals of the Governorates, at least ten days prior to the date of the election, a declaration registered with the Notary Public containing his name and the name of the village or neighbourhood in which he wishes to nominate himself as a candidate. The Notary Public shall levy a lump-sum fee in the amount of ten thousand Lebanese pounds for each declaration.

2 - An application for candidacy shall not be accepted unless the candidate is a voter whose name is entered on the electoral list specific to the village or city in which he wishes to be a Mukhtar or a member of the Mukhtar's Body, or the neighbourhood in which he wishes to be a Mukhtar, and has deposited a deposit in the amount of 10.000.000 L.L. and satisfies the eligibility for the office of Mukhtar or member of the Mukhtar's Body provided for in the Law on Mukhtars promulgated on 27/11/1947.

3 - The District Commissioner (Qaimaqam) or the Governor (Muhafiz) shall give a receipt proving the submission of the application for candidacy. This latter must, within three days from the submission of the application for candidacy, issue a reasoned decision accepting the application or rejecting it; otherwise, his silence upon the expiry of this period shall be deemed an implicit decision of acceptance. The decision accepting or rejecting the candidacy shall be posted immediately upon its issuance on the door of the seat of the Qaimaqamiyya or the Muhafaza, and a record of this matter shall be drawn up and signed by the competent official.

4 - The candidate shall have the right, within a period of one week from the date of issuance of the decision rejecting his candidacy, to apply to the State Council (Majlis Shura al-Dawla) by a petition exempt from fees or any other formality, and the Council must rule finally on the objection within a time limit of five days from the date of its registration in the registry of the Council.

5 - The names of the candidates whose applications for candidacy have been accepted shall be published without delay in the villages and neighbourhoods in which they are candidates.

6 - The deposit shall be refunded to the party concerned if he withdraws his candidacy by a declaration registered with the Notary Public submitted to the Qaimaqamiyya or the Muhafaza at least five days prior to the date of the election.

The electoral bodies for Mukhtars and Mukhtar's Councils shall be convoked by a decision of the Minister of the Interior within the two months preceding the end of the term of office of the Mukhtars and Mukhtar's Councils. The time limit between the date of publication of the decision and the meeting of the electoral body shall be at least thirty days, and the Mukhtar elections shall be held within the sixty days preceding the date of expiry of the term of office of the Mukhtars and Mukhtar's Councils.

1 - The Ministry of the Interior shall determine, in the decision convening the voters, the number of mukhtars and ikhtiyariyya members to be elected for each village or the number of mukhtars for each neighbourhood, and candidacy shall take place on this basis.

2 - The candidate who obtains the largest number of votes of the voters in the village or neighbourhood shall win the elections, and if the votes are equal, the oldest in age shall win, and if the age is equal, recourse shall be had to drawing lots by the Registration Committee provided for in the seventh Article of this Law.

3 - If the number of candidates is equal to the number of members required to be elected and the candidacy period has expired, those candidates shall win unopposed, and this shall be announced by a decision of the Muhafiz or the Qaimaqam; however, if the number of candidates does not reach the number of members required to be elected upon the closing of the candidacy period, or if the withdrawal of candidates from their candidacy leads thereto, it shall be permissible to accept new candidacies submitted three days prior to the polling.

4 - The deposit shall be returned to the candidate if he wins the elections or obtains 25% of the votes of the voters at least.
Polling operations shall commence at seven o'clock in the morning and end at eighteen o'clock, and shall last for one day.

The validity of the election shall be challenged before the State Council within a period of fifteen days following the announcement of the result, and the said Council must rule on this challenge within a maximum period of six months from the date of its submission.

The Government may, by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior, increase the number of neighbourhoods or the number of mukhtars in the cities and neighbourhoods mentioned in the Law promulgated on 7 May 1949 and in Legislative Decree No. 116 dated 12/06/1959.

With respect to the remaining cities, villages and neighbourhoods, the texts currently in force, which remain effective, shall apply.

Exceptionally, and with respect to cases of death occurring prior to the date of promulgation of this Law, mukhtars shall be granted a period of two months to draw up and submit death certificates of persons registered in their neighbourhoods or villages, whatever the place of death or burial, provided that the death occurred on Lebanese territory, and they shall be exempted for this purpose from the delay fine provided for in Article 33 of the Law promulgated on 7/12/1951 (Registration of Personal Status Documents) and from the fines, penalties and prosecutions provided for in Article 34 thereof.

As from the entry into force of this Law, the direct relatives of the deceased up to the fourth degree shall be required to notify the mukhtar of the village or neighbourhood in writing of the occurrence of the event of death within one month from the date of its occurrence. A financial fine of one hundred thousand pounds shall be imposed on each of the relatives of the deceased or the mukhtar in the event of failure to carry out the procedures required of each of them within the time limits specified above.

Shall lose Lebanese nationality:

1- A Lebanese who acquires a foreign nationality after having obtained authorisation therefor by a decree of the Head of State.

2- A Lebanese who accepts in Lebanon a post conferred upon him by a foreign government or a department dependent on a foreign government without having obtained beforehand

authorisation therefor from the Lebanese Government. And if the Government does not give its answer to the application for authorisation within two months from the date of its submission, its failure to answer shall be deemed a refusal.

3- A Lebanese residing outside Lebanese territory who accepts a public office conferred upon him by a foreign government in a foreign country if he retains such office despite the issuance of an order to him to relinquish it within a specified time limit.

4- A Lebanese currently holding a post conferred upon him by a foreign government if he retains such post despite the issuance of an order to him to relinquish it within a specified time limit.

The loss of nationality provided for in paragraphs 2, 3 and 4 shall take place by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers.

5- The Government may at any time revoke the authorisation referred to above by a decision taken in the Council of Ministers.

6- And shall also lose Lebanese nationality a Lebanese who acquired Lebanese nationality by naturalisation:

a- If he is convicted of one of the offences committed against the security of the State.

b- If he belongs to an association that has carried out a conspiracy or an attack against the security of the State.

c- If he belongs to an association having political objectives that is dissolved or unauthorised, or is convicted of carrying out an activity for the benefit of such association.

The loss of nationality in the cases provided for in this article shall be effected by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior.

Every person of Lebanese origin residing outside Lebanon who has not opted for Lebanese nationality may, if he returns definitively to Lebanon, apply to be considered Lebanese, and a decree shall be issued to that effect taken in the Council of Ministers.
Every foreigner who has been naturalised with Lebanese nationality shall lose this nationality if he is absent from Lebanon for a period of five consecutive years.
The modalities of application of this Law, which repeals all texts contrary to it and which are inconsistent with its content, shall be determined by decree.

The draft law set forth in Decree No. 5745 dated 21 June 2001 relating to Value Added Tax, as amended by the Joint Parliamentary Committees and the Chamber of Deputies, is hereby ratified.

This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Establishment of the Tax:

A tax named "Value Added Tax" is hereby established, which shall be levied, paid and collected in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

- The word "Tax", wherever it appears in this Law, shall mean the Value Added Tax.

- The expression "Lebanese territory" or "Lebanon", wherever it appears in this Law, shall mean the Lebanese land, airspace and territorial waters.

Taxable Transactions:

The following shall be subject to the Tax:

1 - Transactions involving the supply of goods and the rendering of services for consideration carried out within the Lebanese territory by a taxable person.

The transactions provided for in Articles 8 and 11 of this Law shall be deemed to constitute a supply of goods or rendering of services for consideration.

2 - Importation transactions carried out by any person, whether a taxable person or a non-taxable person.

Implementing decree for this Article ---- Another implementing decree No. 2002/7302

1 - Every natural or legal person who, in the independent pursuit of an economic activity, carries out transactions involving the supply of goods or the rendering of services that are subject to the Tax or exempt from the Tax with the right of deduction in accordance with the provisions of this Law, shall be subject to the Tax, provided that the turnover relating to a period ranging between one quarter and four consecutive preceding quarters exceeds the amount of five billion Lebanese pounds.

Subject to Paragraph b of Article 60 of the Law, every natural or legal person who, in the independent pursuit of an economic activity, carries out transactions involving the supply of goods or the rendering of services that are subject to the Tax or exempt from the Tax with the right of deduction in accordance with the provisions of this Law, whose turnover relating to a period ranging between one quarter and four consecutive preceding quarters exceeded the amount of 100 million Lebanese pounds and did not exceed five billion Lebanese pounds during any period of the years 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2023, shall be exempted from the obligation to register for the Value Added Tax and from all other obligations imposed by the Law.

Persons who registered for the Value Added Tax on the basis of their mandatory taxable turnover which did not exceed five billion Lebanese pounds for a period ranging between one quarter and four consecutive preceding quarters during any period of the years 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2023, shall have the right to submit an application for the cancellation of their registration before the Directorate of Value Added Tax.

The detailed rules for the application of this Article shall be determined, where necessary, by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

2 - Every person who independently pursues an economic activity subject to the Tax or exempt from the Tax with the right of deduction in accordance with the provisions of this Law may apply for voluntary registration for the Tax, provided that his turnover exceeds the amount of one billion Lebanese pounds during a period ranging between one quarter and four consecutive preceding quarters.

3 - Persons who do not meet the conditions for liability set forth in Item 2 of this Article and who sign contracts with public administrations, public institutions, municipalities, unions of municipalities or other legal persons under public law relating to transactions subject to or exempt from the Tax with the right of deduction, the value of which, in addition to the value of their turnover, if any, relating to a period ranging between one quarter and four consecutive preceding quarters, exceeds the amount of five billion Lebanese pounds exclusive of the Value Added Tax, may submit an application for their registration before the Directorate of Value Added Tax.

4 - Any exporter and importer who, in the independent pursuit of an economic activity, carries out transactions involving the supply of goods or the rendering of services subject to the Tax or exempt from the Tax with the right of deduction in accordance with the provisions of this Law, shall be subject to the Tax, regardless of the amount of his turnover.

The detailed rules for the application of this Article shall be determined, where necessary, pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

Calculation of Turnover:

The calculation of the turnover referred to in Article 3 of this Law shall include the sum of the following amounts:

- The value of taxable transactions, provided that the amount of Value Added Tax is not included in the calculation of such value.

- The value of transactions provided for in Articles 19, 20 and 21 of this Law.

- The value of transactions provided for in Articles 16 and 17 of this Law The following shall not be included in the calculation of turnover:

- The value of the assignment of the fixed assets of the enterprise.

Implementing decree for this Article

Persons and Transactions Outside the Scope of the Tax:

Transactions involving unbuilt land shall not be subject to the Tax.

Furthermore, the State, municipalities and other persons under public law shall not be subject to the Tax in respect of all transactions they carry out in their capacity as a public authority, even if they collect royalties, fees or subscriptions in consideration thereof, with the exception of transactions involving the following matters, which shall remain subject to the Tax:

- Leasing of private property.

- Telecommunications.

- Water and electricity.

- Audiovisual media.

- Consumer markets, slaughterhouses and warehouses.

- Tobacco and tombac.

- Car parks.

- Ports and airports.

Implementing decree for this Article

Supply of Goods:

"Supply of goods" within the meaning of this Law shall be deemed to be the transfer by a taxable person of the right to dispose, as owner, of tangible movable or immovable property to a third party, such as sale or barter.

Implementing decree No. 2002/7302

Property Deemed to be Tangible Property:

For the application of this Law, the following shall be deemed to be tangible property:

1 - Electric current, gas, heat, refrigeration.

2 - The following real rights provided for in the Real Property Ownership Law: usufruct, emphyteusis (long-term lease), right of disposal (Tassamuf), option resulting from a promise of sale, double lease (Ijaratayn).

Implementing decree No. 2002/7302

Supply of Goods by a Taxable Person to Himself:

The following shall be deemed to constitute a supply of goods for consideration:

1 - The appropriation by a taxable person of goods or assets from his enterprise, in respect of which he had previously deducted, partially or wholly, from the Tax due on his sales, the Tax that was borne by them, for the purpose of:

a ) Allocating them for his private needs or for the needs of his employees and, in general, for purposes other than the needs of his enterprise.

b) Supplying them to a third party without consideration.

2 - The allocation by a taxable person of goods or assets for the purposes of his enterprise, which he manufactured, constructed, acquired or imported in the course of pursuing his activity, where they would not entitle him to the full right of deduction of the Tax borne by them had he acquired them from a taxable third party.

3 - The allocation by a taxable person of goods or assets present in his enterprise for the purpose of pursuing a non-taxable activity, where such goods or fixed assets, or the elements of which they are composed, entitled him to the right to deduct the Tax borne by them upon their acquisition or their allocation in accordance with the provisions of Paragraph (2) above.

4 - The retention by a taxable person or one of his legal successors, after the cessation of the pursuit of the taxable economic activity, of property belonging to the enterprise, where such property had previously granted him, upon its acquisition, the right to full or partial deduction.

2 - With respect to the operations referred to in Article 8 of this Law relating to the supply by a taxable person of property to himself, the taxable base shall be the purchase price of the property or of similar property, and where it is impossible to ascertain the price, the cost price on the date on which such operations are carried out shall be adopted.

3 - With respect to the operations referred to in Article 11 of this Law relating to the rendering by a taxable person of services to himself, the taxable base shall be the total expenditure incurred by the taxable person in order to render such services.

4 - In cases where it is impossible to determine the consideration, the tax shall be levied on the basis of the open market value of the executed operation. Open market value means the price payable in Lebanese territory in return for a similar operation carried out on the date of execution of the taxable operation between a seller and a buyer who are independent of each other and under conditions of full competition.

5 - The taxable base shall include duties and taxes, with the exception of the Value Added Tax, as well as all ancillary expenses such as brokerage, packaging, transport and insurance expenses and the like.

Tax accounting period:

The tax payable by the taxable person shall be calculated at the end of each month of the calendar year.

However, the Minister of Finance may, by a decision issued by him, and for reasons required by the initial phase of adopting this tax or for administrative reasons, modify this period so that the tax is calculated on a quarterly basis.

Implementing Decision for this Article

Right of deduction:

The right of deduction is the right granted to the taxable person to deduct from the principal of the tax payable on a given operation the amount of the tax that has previously burdened the price of that operation or has burdened any of the elements of which the price is composed.

A taxable person shall be entitled to deduct from the principal of the tax that he is obliged to pay for a given accounting period the total amount of the deductible tax for the same period.

The right of deduction shall arise when the deductible tax becomes payable.

Implementing Decree for this Chapter

Deductible tax:

Deductible tax is the tax that has been borne by the property or services obtained by the taxable person from another person

subject to it and the property and services that he has imported, including fixed assets, to carry out, within the framework of exercising his economic activity,

one of the following operations:

1 - The supply of property and the rendering of services subject to the tax.

2 - Operations relating to exportation, similar operations, and international transport operations exempted from the tax pursuant to Articles 19, 20 and 21 of this Law.

Shall be deductible the tax that has been borne by the stock of goods and raw materials held by the taxable person on the effective date

of his registration for the tax and which he acquired on an earlier date, provided that he allocates them to carry out taxable transactions in accordance with the rules and procedures determined by a decision of the Minister of Finance. Shall also be deductible the tax that has been borne by fixed assets acquired by a taxable person on a date prior to his becoming subject to the tax and which he allocates to carry out taxable transactions.

Fixed assets within the meaning of this Article mean tangible property consisting of machinery and equipment allocated for permanent use in the enterprise as a working tool or a means of exploitation.

The rules and procedures for the application of this Article shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

Related texts: Implementing Decree for this Chapter

Determining the application of the provisions of Law No. 379 dated 14/12/2001 (Value Added Tax) relating to the deduction of the tax that has been borne by the stock of goods and raw materials held by the taxable person on the effective date of his registration for the tax and acquired on a date prior to his becoming subject to the tax

Rules governing the right of deduction:

In order to exercise the right of deduction, the taxable person must hold:

- An invoice for the property or services acquired from another taxable person containing the information provided for in Article 38 of this Law, or a document serving in its stead.

- Customs documents issued by the competent authorities proving the validity of the importation and the payment of the tax.

Implementing Decree for this Chapter

Excess of deductible tax:

If the value of the deductible tax, at the end of a given accounting period, exceeds the value of the tax due, the excess shall be carried forward to the subsequent period.

A taxable person shall have the right to submit, after the end of any calendar year and within a period of 20 days, an application for the refund of the balance of the interest of the deductible tax as at that date, provided that the amount claimed for refund is not less than fifty million Lebanese pounds.

Exporters shall have the right to submit, after the end of any tax accounting period and within a period of 20 days, an application for the refund of the excess of the deductible tax calculated for that period, provided that the amount claimed for refund is not less than fifty million Lebanese pounds.

Every person whose application for the cancellation of his registration has been approved by the Administration shall have the right to request the refund of the excess of the deductible tax, within a period of 20 days from the date of the end of the tax accounting period during which he was notified of the approval of the Tax Administration of his application for the cancellation of his registration.

The Administration must decide on the refund application within a maximum period of three months from the date of expiry of the period specified for submitting refund applications.

The period shall be extended for a similar duration and once only if the Tax Administration finds it necessary to expand the examination of the taxpayer or to place the taxpayer's file on the tax audit programme for periods prior to the refund application.

If the Administration approves the refund application, wholly or partially, it must return the amount due to the taxable person, failing which interest shall be payable on the unpaid amount at a rate equal to the average interest rate on one-year category Treasury bills, provided that such rate does not exceed 9% per annum, after the lapse of four months from the submission of the application, or seven months in the event of extension of the period by the Tax Administration.

Implementing decree for this Chapter

Right of partial deduction:

If the taxable person carries out, on the occasion of the supply of goods or the rendering of services, transactions only a part of which confers the right. Of deduction, he shall have the right to deduct a proportion of the tax corresponding to this part.

The details of application of this Article shall be determined by decrees issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

Implementing decree for this Chapter

Adjustment of deduction:

Deduction transactions carried out shall be reviewed for the purpose of adjusting them where the value of the deduction exceeds or falls short of the value that the taxable person was entitled to deduct, as a result of:

1- Material errors.

2- The occurrence of modifications, at a date subsequent to the tax accounting period, to the elements adopted for determining the value of the deduction.

A person who has voluntarily subjected himself to the tax and then requested the cancellation of his registration within a period of two years from the date of registration shall be required to return to the Treasury the difference, if any, between the value of the tax that he recovered and the value of the tax that he collected for the benefit of the Treasury, in respect of the period during which he was voluntarily subject to the tax.

Implementing decree for this Chapter --- Another implementing decree No. 2002/7296

Persons liable for the tax:

1- Within the Lebanese territory:

The tax shall be due from the person subject thereto in accordance with the provisions of this Law and from his legal successors, provided that the transactions of supply of goods and rendering of services that he carries out are subject to the tax.

Pursuant to the provisions of paragraph (1) of Article 40 of this Law, the tax shall be due from the representative of the person not resident in Lebanon appointed in accordance with this Law, or from the person dealing with him in the event that he has not been appointed.

Pursuant to the provisions of paragraph (2) of Article 40 of this Law, the tax shall be due from the person resident in Lebanon who uses therein a service that he acquired from outside the Lebanese territory.

2 - Upon importation:

The tax shall be due from the importer or from his representative in accordance with the provisions of the customs legislation in force.

Exceptionally and notwithstanding any other text, value added tax shall not be due on transactions of leasing built real properties for non-residential purposes on which value added tax was not collected from their lessees or occupants, in the following two cases:

Scope of application of the obligations:

The obligations provided for in this Title shall apply to:

A - A taxable person in accordance with the provisions of Article 3 of this Law.

B - Persons who carry out transactions exempt from tax that entitle them to the right of deduction in accordance with item (2) of the first paragraph of Article 28 of this Law.

Declaration Obligations:

Every taxable person shall submit:

1 - An application for registration with the Value Added Tax Administration within a period of two months commencing from the last day of the quarter during which the conditions for subjection to the tax were fulfilled.

2 - An application for cancellation of registration.

a- Within a period of two months from the date of expiry of the calendar year following the year during which the conditions for subjection to the tax ceased to exist.

b - Within a period of two months from the date of cessation of work.

Implementing decree for items 1 and 2

3 - A notification to the Tax Administration of any change in the nature of his activity, his address, his trade name, his legal personality, or any other information contained in the registration application, within a period of two months from the date the change occurred.

4 - A periodic declaration within a period of twenty days from the expiry of the tax calculation period as defined in Article 26 of this Law, including, where applicable, the amount of the tax requested to be deducted.

Applications and declarations shall be submitted to the competent tax unit and on paper and/or electronic forms prepared for this purpose. Implementing decision for item 4

Another implementing decree No. 2002/7296

Accounting Obligations:

The manner of keeping books and organising the necessary accounting documents which the taxable person is required to adopt and which allow the application and control of the tax shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Finance.

A taxpayer subject to income tax on the basis of lump-sum profit or estimated profit, who is subject to the Value Added Tax, shall be required to keep the books and organise the accounting documents pertaining to taxpayers on the basis of actual profit. Provided that he continues to declare income tax on the basis of lump-sum or estimated profit.

1 - Persons subject to the Value Added Tax whose turnover for four consecutive preceding quarters is less than 300 million Lebanese Pounds, and for as long as their turnover remains at this limit, with the exception of taxable persons who are income tax taxpayers on the basis of actual profit, or who are compulsorily taxed on the basis of lump-sum profit, as well as non-resident persons subject to the Value Added Tax and their agents, shall be required to keep accounting based on the following books and registers:

- A journal in which all transactions that take place are compulsorily recorded.

- An inventory and fixed assets register.

The contents and manner of keeping these books and organising the necessary accounting documents by which the taxable person and beneficiary

of the provisions of this Article is bound shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Finance.

The persons mentioned in this Article shall number and initial the books and registers either at the Commercial Register or before

notaries public, prior to commencing the entry of accounting transactions, provided that this provision shall also apply to income tax taxpayers

concerned by this Article.

2 - The persons mentioned in item 1 of this Article shall benefit from an annual tax deduction of one million five hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds to be deducted from the value of the tax due, for a period of five years commencing from the year in which their registration with the Value Added Tax takes effect.

The details of application of this Article shall be determined by decisions issued by the Minister of Finance.

Implementing decision for item 2

Retention of Books, Invoices and Accounting Documents:

The taxable person shall retain the books, invoices and other accounting documents for a period of four years commencing from the date of expiry of the calendar year during which the tax arose.

Issuance of Invoices:

Every taxable person is required to issue an invoice or any other document serving in its stead upon his delivery of goods or his provision of services to any other person.

The invoice must include at least the following:

- The name, address and registration number at the Ministry of Finance of the supplier of goods or provider of services.

- The name and address of the person in whose favour the invoice is issued.

- The subject of the delivery of the good or the provision of the service.

- The serial number and date of the invoice.

- The amount due for the delivery of goods or the provision of services.

- The amount of the tax due together with the tax rate that was applied.

Implementing decision for this Article ---- Another implementing decree No. 2002/7296

Payment of the Tax:

The tax shall be paid in a single lump sum within the time limit for submitting the periodic declaration, that is within twenty days from the expiry of each tax calculation period, in respect of the taxable transactions that were realised during the said period after deducting the value of the deductible tax.

In the event that the Administration imposes additional or supplementary amounts, the tax shall be paid pursuant to a special notice thereof within one month from the date of notification of the liability for these amounts to the taxpayers liable therefor.

The tax shall be settled at any of the approved private banks or their branches operating in Lebanon in accordance with the rules and procedures determined by the Minister of Finance by a decision issued by him.

Implementing decision for this Article ---- Another implementing decree No. 2002/7296

Non-Resident Persons:

1 - Every person who has no actual or elected domicile in Lebanon, prior to carrying out any transaction of delivery of goods or provision of services on Lebanese territory and whatever the value of the turnover he realises, shall appoint a representative for himself resident in Lebanon, subject to the approval of the Tax Administration as to the fulfilment of the conditions determined by a decision of the Minister of Finance.

Every person resident in Lebanon whose dealing with a non-resident person has given rise to tax liability shall verify that the latter has a representative in Lebanon, and in the event that none has been appointed, he shall be required to pay this tax and the fines due to the Tax Administration, while reserving his right of recourse against the non-resident person. This representative shall be jointly and severally liable with his principal for the payment of the tax and the fines resulting from the transactions subject thereto and shall stand in his stead in respect of all the obligations imposed upon him in accordance with the provisions of this Law and its implementing texts.

2 - Every person resident in Lebanon who uses therein a service that he acquired from an entity resident outside Lebanese territory shall declare the tax due on this service whatever its value and pay it to the Tax Administration, in accordance with rules determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

Implementing decree for this Article

Another implementing decree for this Article

Obligations Imposed Upon Importation:

The same forms and rules provided for in the customs legislation shall apply to the declaration of the tax upon importation.

The tax shall be paid when the goods are released for local consumption, in accordance with the procedures provided for in the customs legislation.

The collection of the tax shall be suspended by operation of law in the event of suspension of customs duties under all customs regimes suspending duties, in accordance with the procedures provided for in the customs legislation.

Travel Agency Transactions:

By travel agencies is meant every natural or legal person who organises and secures, directly or as an intermediary, and for the purpose of profit, travels or stays, and sells travel tickets, hotel stays, and meals, and organises trips and visits to archaeological and other sites, and in general, every person who sells to travellers services connected with the transactions mentioned above or ancillary thereto.

These transactions shall be considered a provision of services within the meaning of this Law.

The bases and rules for imposing the tax and the procedures for its application to the transactions of travel agencies shall be determined pursuant to decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

Inspection Procedures:

1 - The Right of Access:

The employees of the competent tax administration shall have the right to inspect, at the premises of every taxable person or any person related to the tax, the registers, invoices, and all other documents that allow them to verify the proper collection of the tax due from him or from the persons dealing with him.

Subject to the Law issued on 3 September 1956 relating to banking secrecy, no one, including official administrations, may invoke professional secrecy to prevent the employees of the tax administration from reviewing the books, invoices, and other documents that allow the verification of the proper collection of the tax due from those subject to it.

Where the registers and documents are kept or preserved electronically, the employees of the competent tax administration shall have the right to request access to the information recorded on electronic documents and to obtain it in the form of readable digital or paper documents.

2 - Provision of Information:

Subject to the provisions of the Law issued on 3 September 1956 relating to banking secrecy, every natural or legal person in Lebanon shall, upon their written request, grant the employees of the competent tax administration access to the registers, documents, and information in their possession that assist in verifying the proper collection of the tax due from him or from third parties.

3 - Supervision of Import and Export Operations of Goods:

The provisions relating to the powers provided for in the Customs Law shall remain in force, and, with respect to this Article, the legal provisions that do not conflict with this Law regarding the verification, establishment, prosecution, and settlement of offences in all matters relating to the supervision of import and export operations of goods shall also remain in force.

An Implementing Decree for this Article

Professional Secrecy:

Every person whose function, powers, or competence requires him to intervene in the assessment or collection of the tax, or in the examination of objections submitted in respect thereof, shall be bound by professional secrecy and shall be prosecuted in the event of a breach pursuant to the provisions of Article /579/ of the Penal Code.

Professional secrecy may not be invoked in lawsuits affecting the interests of the administration or when the assessment audit or collection departments exercise their administrative functions.

An Implementing Decree for this Article

Cases of Direct Assessment:

In addition to the fines provided for in Article 48 of this Law, the tax administration may undertake the direct assessment of the tax in the following cases:

1 - If the taxable person fails to submit the periodic return relating to the calculation of the tax for a given period within the specified time limits.

2 - If the taxable person fails to comply with the obligations imposed upon him by law or by the regulations relating to the keeping, delivery, and preservation of accounting books and documents, thereby rendering it impossible for the tax administration to perform its duties with respect to inspecting such registers.

3 - If the taxable person fails to issue an invoice in conformity with the provisions of Article 38 of this Law when it is mandatory, or in the event that he issues an invoice containing incorrect information.

4 - If the taxable person submits an incorrect periodic return that does not reflect the reality of his actual economic activity with the aim of evading the payment of the tax or with the aim of unlawfully recovering the tax.

Direct assessment shall be made in the amount of the tax due on the basis of the estimated amounts of the transactions carried out during the relevant tax calculation period.

Collection of the Tax within Lebanese Territory:

1 - Collection Procedures:

The tax unit shall send to the taxable person who has defaulted on paying the tax and the amounts due from him within the legal time limits a letter notifying him of the obligation to pay them within fifteen days from the date on which he is served with the letter.

In the event that the taxable person fails to do so, the tax unit shall send to him, by registered mail, a final personal warning calling upon him to pay the amounts due from him within fifteen days from the date on which he is served with the warning.

If the taxable person does not pay what he owes after the expiry of the time limit of the final warning, this warning shall be affixed to the door of his place of residence or place of business, and the date of execution of this measure shall be deemed the date on which he was served.

The procedures for the collection of direct taxes and similar duties provided for in Legislative Decree No. 147 dated 12/06/1959 and its amendments, the provisions of which do not conflict with the provisions of this Law and its implementing texts, shall apply.

2 - Fine for Late Payment of the Tax:

In the event of failure to pay the tax within the time limit for submitting the periodic return, a fine of three percent (3 %) per month of its amount shall be added thereto.

The late payment fine shall run as from the expiry of the time limit for payment of the tax and this fine shall be calculated on the total of the taxes and assessment fines due, and a fraction of a month shall be deemed a full month.

Where it appears as a result of the examination process or direct assessment that the payment of the tax was made in an amount less than what is due, a fine of three percent (3%) per month of the unpaid amount of the tax legally due and the fines attached thereto shall be imposed ipso jure as from the date of expiry of the time limit for payment of the tax.

3 - Priority Right for Treasury Funds:

With respect to the taxes, fines, and other amounts due to the State pursuant to this Law, the Treasury shall enjoy a general priority right of the first rank over all the property of the persons liable for their payment and a compulsory legal mortgage over all their immovable property.

An Implementing Decree for this Article

Collection of the Tax upon Importation:

With respect to the collection of the tax upon importation, the procedures and rules followed in customs legislation shall apply.

Violations and Fines:

1 - Delay in or failure to submit the application for registration: Every person who meets the conditions of liability to tax in accordance with this Law and who fails to perform or delays in performing the obligations of the taxable person prescribed by law as a result of his failure to submit his application for registration within the legal time limit shall be subject to the following amounts solely:

a - The value of the tax due calculated on the basis of the lump-sum profit margin adopted in the income tax, on the taxable transactions carried out by him from the date of expiry of the time limit for his registration with the Value Added Tax until the effective date of his registration, without being granted the right of deduction provided for in Article 28 of this Law for the said period.

b - A fine equivalent to 10% of the value of the tax due mentioned in Item (a) for each tax period falling within the period mentioned above, provided that the fine pertaining to each tax period shall not be less than the amount of one million Lebanese Pounds. As for the violations committed by the taxable person after the effective date of his registration, they shall be recorded in accordance with the provisions of Items (2) et seq. of this Article.

2 - Delay in submitting the periodic declaration:

In the event of delay in submitting the declaration provided for in Paragraph (4) of Article 35 of this Law, a fine of ten percent (10%) of the amount of the tax due shall be imposed for each month of delay, a fraction of a month being considered a full month, provided that the amount of the fine shall not exceed twice the amount of the tax due, and shall not be less than 500000 Lebanese Pounds for each tax period, in addition to the fine for delay in paying the unpaid tax provided for in Paragraph

(2) of Article 46 of this Law.

3 - Incorrect declaration:

With the exception of material errors, a taxable person who submits an incorrect declaration that does not reflect the reality of his actual economic activity shall be subject to a fine equivalent to twice the undeclared tax.

4 - Unjustified application for refund of the tax:

Every person who submits, with the intent to defraud, an unjustified application for refund of the tax shall be subject to a fine equivalent to twice the amount of the tax requested to be refunded, in addition to the application of the provisions of the Criminal

Code against him.

5 - Violations relating to invoices and documents:

a - Every amount recorded in an invoice or in a similar document as being tax due becomes due for payment within the legal time limits, and in the event of non-payment, the fine for delay in payment specified pursuant to the provisions of this Law shall be imposed thereon, and this fine shall begin to run as of the date on which the tax falls due.

b - Every person who issues an invoice without right shall be subject to a fine equivalent to three times the tax recorded on this invoice.

c - Every person who refrains from issuing an invoice or any similar document, when this is mandatory in accordance with the provisions of Article 38 of this Law, shall be subject to a fine equivalent to twice the tax originally due on the transaction that is the subject of the invoice.

d - Every taxable person who issues an invoice or similar document containing incorrect information regarding the name or address of the parties concerned with the transaction, or the nature or quantity of the goods delivered or services rendered, or the price and its accessories, or the value of the tax, shall be subject to a fine equivalent to twice the tax originally due on the transaction that is the subject of the invoice, or twice the tax recorded on the invoice if it is higher.

6 - Keeping, preserving and producing registers and documents:

Every person who violates the provisions of this Law or its implementing provisions regarding the keeping, delivering, preserving or producing of registers, invoices or any other accounting document shall be punished by a fine equivalent to twice the tax due, provided that it shall not be less than the amount of five hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds.

7 - Intervention by a third party:

Every person who intervenes in any of the violations provided for in the preceding paragraphs of this Article shall be punished by a fine equal to the amount of the said tax, provided that the fine for him shall not be less than five million Lebanese Pounds.

8 - Upon importation and exportation:

In transactions of importation and exportation of goods, violations shall be verified, recorded, collected and settled in accordance with the provisions prescribed in the customs legislation.

9 - Notwithstanding any other text, with respect to violations pertaining to invoices, ledgers and accounting documents that relate to form, namely those that do not affect the substance of the tax due, a fine equivalent to 5% of the tax due shall be imposed, provided that the total fine shall not be less than the amount of 200000 Lebanese Pounds.

10 - The highest fine among the fines imposed pursuant to this Article shall apply to a single violation. The details of application of this Item shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

- The provisions of the amended Article 48 shall apply to all files for which assessments have been issued and have not been paid on the date of entry into force of this Law, as well as to files that have not yet been assessed regardless of the tax period to which they pertain, whether prior or subsequent, noting that even if all assessments that were previously paid are considered a right of the Treasury.

Implementing decision for this Article

Refund:

The taxable person is entitled to recover the full tax paid by him or a part thereof in the event of annulment, cancellation or rescission of the taxable transaction, or in the event of non-payment of the price in whole or in part, or reduction of its value at a date subsequent to the date of carrying out the transaction.

The procedures and rules relating to the refund of the tax whose value exceeds the tax due shall be determined by a decree based on the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

Objection procedures within Lebanese territory:

1 - The objection:

A taxable person shall have the right to object to the amounts assessed against him or the recovery or refund of which has been refused in accordance with the provisions of Article 49 of this Law, by submitting a written petition to the competent tax unit within a period of one month from the date of his notification of the Administration's decision or from the date of his payment of the tax.

The objection must be reasoned, on pain of dismissal.

The competent tax unit must adjudicate upon the objection within a period of six months from the date of its receipt of the petition, and the said unit must notify the objector of its decision within a period of fifteen days following the date on which the decision is taken.

In the event that the six-month period elapses without any decision being issued by the Administration, the silence of the Administration shall then be deemed an implicit decision accepting the objection.

In the event that the objection is accepted expressly or implicitly, its contents shall be given effect within a period of one month from the date of issuance of the decision or from the date on which it is deemed implicitly accepted.

2 - The Objections Committee:

Decisions of the Administration dismissing the objection in whole or in part may be appealed before the Objections Committee, and the appeal must be submitted within a period of one month from the date of notification of the Administration's decision.

One or more committees of first instance shall be formed by decree in each governorate to examine and adjudicate upon objections to the tax, composed of:

- A serving or honorary judge, judicial or administrative, of the fourth grade or above, appointed upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice after the approval of the Supreme Judicial Council or the Bureau of the State Council....as President

- An employee of the Ministry of Finance belonging to at least the third category, selected by the Minister of Finance....as Member-Rapporteur

- A representative of the competent Chamber of Commerce and Industry, selected by the President of the said Chamber .... as Member

This Committee shall apply the rules of procedure followed before summary jurisdiction and shall take its decisions by majority vote.

The Committee must adjudicate upon the objection within a period of six months following its registration with it, and the Rapporteur must notify the decision of the Committee to the competent tax unit and to the taxable person within fifteen days from the date of its issuance.

3 - Appeal before the State Council:

Both the competent tax unit and the taxable person shall have the right to appeal the decisions of the Objections Committee directly before the State Council within a period of 30 days from the date of notification of the Committee's decision.

Summary rules of procedure shall be followed before the State Council. The admissibility of an appeal submitted by the taxable person shall be conditional upon the deposit of a security equivalent to eight percent (8%) of the amount of the contested tax. Any appeal application not accompanied by a receipt proving payment of the security shall be dismissed as to form.

The taxable person shall recover the security in the event that the decision of the State Council is issued wholly in his favour. In the event that the said decision is wholly in favour of the Treasury, the said security shall become the right of the Treasury. However, if the decision is partially in favour of the taxable person, the refundable security shall be in proportion to the tax that the judgment ruled not to be due from him.

Objection procedures:

Upon importation, the rules of procedure followed in customs legislation shall apply to objections to the tax upon importation.

Prescription:

Amounts due to the Treasury shall lapse by prescription after the passage of four years following the end of the calendar year during which such amounts became due.

The prescription period in respect of amounts due to the Treasury shall be interrupted, and extended for four new years, merely by initiating individual enforcement proceedings through the notification of a collection order or the notification of a personal notice of default or the acknowledgment of the debt by the taxable person or any other act interrupting prescription in accordance with the provisions of the Code of Obligations and Contracts.

Notwithstanding any other half, the right of deduction shall lapse by prescription after the passage of four years following the date of the end of the year during which this right arose.

The right to claim a total or partial refund of the tax shall lapse by prescription after the passage of four years following the end of the calendar year during which the tax became due.

Fiscal stamp duty:

Returns, objections, statements and other papers and documents relating to this tax shall be exempt from fiscal stamp duty.

Irrecoverable amounts:

Amounts due from taxable persons, including fines accrued thereon, the value of which does not exceed ten thousand Lebanese pounds, shall be deemed irrecoverable, and the competent financial units shall be exempted from issuing collection orders for these amounts and from collecting them.
