And whereas it appears that the person concerned was appointed in the cadre of the Ministry of Education and Higher Education in accordance with the provisions of paragraph (1) of Article /13/ referred to above on the grounds that she holds an equivalence to the Second Teaching Certificate which is one of the conditions of appointment to the post of teacher and consequently she was not an instructor in primary education prior to this appointment. And whereas the Draft Law put into effect by Decree No. 2270 dated 1979 relating to the settlement of the status of graduates of the Intermediate Teacher Training College established by Decree No. 2294 dated 3/ 12/1971 (Regulations of the Intermediate Teacher Training College) provided in its Article One for the following: "1 - Holders of the Second Teaching Certificate issued by the Intermediate Teacher Training College established pursuant to Decree No. 2294 dated 3/12/1971 shall be appointed without a competitive examination to the post of teacher of the second rank, fifth step (in accordance with the numbering of steps of the old salary scales of members of the teaching staff) as probationers for a period of one year at least and two years at most, at the end of which they shall be confirmed in their posts or dismissed for their professional incompetence. 2 - As for the holders of the aforementioned certificate belonging to the official primary education cadre on the date of issuance of this Law, the following provisions shall apply to them: a - If they had obtained the aforementioned certificate prior to their appointment in the official primary education cadre, they shall be deemed, starting from the date of their assumption of duties, to have been appointed to the post of teacher, second rank, fifth step in accordance with the salary scale that was in force on the aforementioned date, and their advancement shall be reconstituted and the differences in salaries, allowances and increments shall be paid to them on this basis. b -........". And whereas the Ministry of Education and Higher Education, in accordance with what is stated in the letter of its Accounting Department, proceeded after the issuance of the Draft Law put into effect by Decree No. 2270/79 to settle the salaries of the members of the teaching staff who hold the Second Teaching Certificate or its equivalent on the grounds that they were duly appointed to the post of teacher, including the person concerned, and whereas the aforementioned Ministry, after the issuance of Law No. 344/2001, applied its provisions to the beneficiaries thereof among the holders of the Second Teaching Certificate with the exception of those who have an equivalence to the aforementioned certificate, and that the administration concerned did not grant the person concerned the benefit of the provisions of the Law mentioned in this paragraph on the grounds that she holds an equivalence to the Second Teaching Certificate and consequently applied to her the provisions of Article Two of Law No. 344/2001 relating to the exception stated therein. And whereas Article Two of Law No. 344 dated 6/8/ 2001 provided that "None shall benefit from the provisions of the preceding Article except the members of the teaching staff referred to therein who hold one of the two licences mentioned therein, provided that there shall be excluded from among them anyone who had previously obtained an equivalence for his university studies to the Second Teaching Certificate and whose salaries were settled on the basis of the aforementioned equivalence". And whereas it appears that the legal provisions referred to above excluded the members of the teaching staff (that is, those present in the cadre) who obtained an equivalence for their university studies to the Second Teaching Certificate during their performance of the post of instructor or teacher and consequently in the light of this equivalence their salaries were settled in accordance with the provisions of the Draft Law put into effect by Decree No. 2270/79, as evidenced by the fact that this Board received, after the entry into force of the aforementioned Draft Law, a letter from the Ministry of Education and Higher Education requesting the opinion of the Civil Service Board on the settlement of salaries for a female instructor who had obtained an equivalence for her university licence to the Second Teaching Certificate, which indicates that there are equivalences to the aforementioned certificate for some members of the teaching staff appointed to the post of instructor and not to the post of teacher, noting that this Board had considered at the time that these equivalences were not legally valid, however provisions were included in Law No. 344/2001 concerning those concerned with these equivalences. And whereas it appears that the person concerned had obtained an equivalence to the Second Teaching Certificate prior to her appointment to the post of teacher and on the date of entry into force of the Draft Law referred to in the preceding paragraph of this letter she was among the members of the teaching staff who hold the aforementioned certificate, which led to the settlement of her salaries as being one of the members of the teaching staff to whom the provisions of paragraph (1) of Article One of the Draft Law issued by Decree No. 2270/1979 apply on the basis that she holds the Second Teaching Certificate and not on the basis of an equivalence for her university studies, and it is consequently necessary to state that the person concerned is not concerned by this exception on the grounds that she entered the cadre on the basis that she holds the academic qualification required to be available in a candidate for the post of teacher in the teaching cadre and her salaries were settled in accordance with the provisions of the first paragraph of Article One of the Draft Law put into effect by Decree No. 2270/79 and that she did not obtain the equivalence after her appointment in the primary education cadre so that her salaries would be settled in the light thereof. And whereas it appears from the attached certificate of the Accounting Department in the Ministry of Education and Higher Education that the holders of the Second Teaching Certificate among the members of the teaching staff in the primary education cadre and who hold the teaching or university licence have benefited from the provisions of Law No. 344/2001 on the grounds that they are among the members of the teaching staff duly appointed in the primary teaching cadre. And whereas it is necessary that the person concerned have the same rights as those appointed in the primary education cadre among the holders of the Second Teaching Certificate and holding a teaching licence, on the grounds that the equivalence to the Second Teaching Certificate which the person concerned obtained prior to her appointment in the primary education cadre was one of the conditions specified for appointment to the post of teacher. Therefore, the Board of the Civil Service Board considered that the person concerned is not concerned by the exception stated in Article Two thereof and consequently her entitlement to benefit from the provisions of Law No. 344/2001

39 - Exceeding the legal age for appointment - Transfer - Retirement pension: In the matter relating to the extent of the possibility of attaching a civil servant who has exceeded the minimum period for entitlement to the retirement pension to one of the technical institutes or schools and permitting him to commence work, the Civil Service Board replied by its letter No. 3696 dated 3/12/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Education and Higher Education with the following: Whereas the person concerned is an employee at the Electricité du Liban Public Establishment whose name appeared in the third Article of Decree No. 13396/ 2004 (appointment of technical education instructors) along with the civil servants in the public administrations, in the form of transferring him from his current post and appointing him to the post of technical education instructor in the cadre of the Directorate General of Vocational and Technical Education. And whereas the legal texts in force do not permit transfer from a public establishment to a public administration, therefore the transfer mentioned in

the aforementioned Decree is legally unfounded, and consequently the person concerned cannot be considered a former civil servant. And whereas Paragraph (c) of Article /4/ of the Civil Servants Regulations and the amendments thereto stipulated that it is required of every applicant for a public post "that he shall not have exceeded the age of thirty-five if he is applying for a post in either the fifth or fourth category; however, if he is applying for a post in another category, or a technical post of whatever category it may be, the difference between his age and the retirement age fixed for this post must not be less than the minimum period for entitlement to a retirement pension". And whereas the minimum period for entitlement to the retirement pension for civil servants in accordance with what was stipulated in Article /4/ of Legislative Decree No. 47 dated 29/6/1983 and the amendments thereto (Retirement and Dismissal from Service Regulations) is twenty years of actual service. And whereas Paragraph (2) of Article /5/ of the Civil Servants Regulations stipulates that "the minimum and maximum age limits imposed upon appointment shall be calculated from the date of birth until the date fixed for the commencement of the competitive examination or on the first of January of the year in which the appointment took place, with respect to the civil servants whom the law permits to be appointed without a competitive examination". And whereas it appears that the administration concerned relied in proposing the appointment of the person concerned on Paragraph (a(of Item (5) of the second Article of Decree No. 16984 dated 27/7/1964 (determining the conditions of appointment to technical posts in the administrative and educational cadres of the Directorate General of Vocational and Technical Education), which grants a first preference for the appointment of technical education instructors "a - By selection from among holders of the technical teaching licence, in the required specialisation from among graduates of the National Pedagogical Institute for Technical Education who undertook to work with the Ministry of Vocational and Technical Education (formerly) - the Directorate General of Vocational and Technical Education - for a period of ten years at least, and in the event that the number of candidates exceeds the required number, selection shall take place on the basis of the total marks in their certificates". And whereas the second Article referred to above stipulated in its opening part that "In addition to the general conditions for employment, the special conditions for appointment to technical posts in the educational cadre of the Directorate General of Vocational and Technical Education shall be determined as follows:...", a matter which necessitates the fulfilment of the age condition provided for in the Civil Servants Regulations upon appointment in accordance with the provisions of the aforementioned Article. And whereas it appears that on 1/1/2004 the person concerned, who is not a former civil servant, had exceeded the age of forty-four years, meaning that there is no longer the required period provided for in the legal provisions relating to this matter referred to previously, considering that the retirement age for the post to which they are appointed is sixty-four years, a matter from which it is inferred that the appointment of the person concerned was contrary to the provisions of the law, and consequently the administration concerned is required to work towards annulling his appointment in accordance with the rules in force, and consequently there is no longer any need to examine the remaining points raised.

40 - Rescission of contracting - The Higher Disciplinary Board - Deduction of contractual consideration: In the matter relating to the request to state an opinion regarding the re-disbursement of half a monthly allowance to a former contractor, the Civil Service Board replied by its letter No. 614 dated 15/4/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Public Health with the following: Paragraph (First) of Article (13) of Law No. 54/65 dated 2/10/65 and the amendments thereto (Establishment of the Higher Disciplinary Board) stipulated the following: "There shall be established at the Presidency of the Council of Ministers a Higher Disciplinary Board which shall be devoted permanently to examining the infractions on account of which a civil servant, within the meaning defined hereinafter, is referred to it: - The authority of this Board shall cover all workers in the public administrations and in the municipalities, public establishments, and autonomous services affiliated with the State and the municipalities, including permanent and temporary civil servants and employees, contractors of all kinds, wage-earners, and persons dealing with the administration, and the Board shall be entitled to inflict upon them all the penalties set forth in their respective scales of penalties.....". And Paragraph (3) of Item Second of Article (13) of the aforementioned Law stipulated the following: "On the date of the referral of the civil servant or employee to the Higher Disciplinary Board, half of his salary shall be suspended and shall not be returned to him except in the event that he is declared acquitted or sentenced to a penalty of the first-degree penalties at most". And whereas, on the date of the referral of Doctor (- -) before the Higher Disciplinary Board and the deduction of half of the contractual consideration from his monthly allowance, Doctor (- -) was in a contractual relationship with the Ministry of Public Health. And whereas the contractual status of the person concerned did not end until after his referral before the Higher Disciplinary Board, as set forth above. And whereas Article (13) exhaustively determined the cases in which half the salary of the person referred before the Higher Disciplinary Board may be returned.

And whereas the case of a declaration of lack of jurisdiction of the Higher Disciplinary Board to examine the case of the person concerned due to the non-rescission of his contracting does not fall among the cases exhaustively determined in Paragraph (3) of Item Second of Article (13) of Law No. 54/65 which permit, in the event of their fulfilment, the re-payment of the other half of the salary to the person referred before the Higher Disciplinary Board. Therefore, the Board of the Civil Service Board deemed, pursuant to the provisions of Article ( 13) aforementioned, that half of the allowance cannot be returned to the person concerned for the period of his referral before the Higher Disciplinary Board.

41 - Contracting - Reduction of teaching hours - Incorporation of the financial allowance: In the matter concerning the extent to which persons contracted under annual contracts in public agricultural education may benefit from the provisions of the two Laws

No. 250/2000 and No. 551/2003, the Civil Service Board replied by its letter No. 4187 dated 19/2/1004 addressed to the Ministry of Agriculture as follows: It appeared that the Directorate General of Agriculture states that certain members of the teaching staff in the establishment of the Directorate General of Vocational and Technical Education of the Second and Third Categories were granted a monthly financial allowance distributed over three years effective from 1/7/2000, the amount of which was determined for each of them according to his years of actual service as set forth in paragraphs 1 and 2 of the Second Article of Law No. 250 dated 14/8/2000 (amendment of the provisions of the reduction in teaching hours...), and that Law No. 551 dated 20/10/2003 provided for the incorporation of the financial allowance granted pursuant to the two Laws No. 148/99 and No. 250/2000 into the base of the salary. And it appeared that the aforementioned Directorate General requests the rendering of an opinion on the possibility of persons contracted in agricultural education under annual contracts benefiting from the provisions of the two aforementioned Laws in the same manner as their colleagues, the members of the teaching staff in the establishment of public agricultural education who perform teaching functions similar to their functions, particularly since Article 45 of Law No. 173 dated 14/2/2000 (the General Budget and Annexed Budgets for the year 2000) provided for the inadmissibility of the monthly compensations of contracted persons being lower than those of their counterparts in the function. Accordingly, whereas paragraph (b) of Article (9) of Law No. 8/87 dated 2/5/1987 (organisation of public technical and vocational agricultural education) provided for the following: "All laws and regulations relating to salaries, wages, compensations, fees for teaching hours, the number of weekly teaching hours, working hours, and other laws and regulations applicable to principals, members of the teaching staff, and contracted persons in the Directorate General of Vocational and Technical Education shall apply to principals and members of the teaching staff included in the establishment and contracted persons in public agricultural schools". And whereas it is inferred from the text mentioned above that the laws and regulations governing contracted persons in the Directorate General of Vocational and Technical Education apply to contracted persons in public agricultural schools. And whereas the benefits enjoyed by the members of the teaching staff (whether in the establishment of the Directorate General of Vocational and Technical Education or in the establishment of the agricultural schools) pursuant to legal texts do not apply ipso jure to contracted persons working in the Directorate General of Vocational and Technical Education and in public agricultural schools even if their functions are similar, but rather the matter requires the existence of a special text concerning them capable of granting them the benefit of parallel or equivalent benefits to those enjoyed by the members of the teaching staff in the public establishment, and the best example of that is what was provided for by Article (15) of Law No. 8 /87 dated 2/5/1987, which granted persons contracted to teach in public agricultural schools an exceptional increase on their monthly compensations equivalent to the value of the supervening increase on the salaries of the members of the teaching staff in the establishment of public agricultural schools granted pursuant to other legal texts. And whereas Law No. 250/2000 determined the persons benefiting from its provisions, without including contracted persons in the Directorate General of Vocational and Technical Education, and the same applies with respect to Law No. 551/2003 given that the First Article of this Law provided for the incorporation of the financial allowance into the basic salary of the beneficiary of the provisions of Law No. 250/2000 And whereas the Civil Service Board had previously opined by its Decision No. 774 dated 13/7/2001, that the provisions set forth in the two Laws No. 244 dated 7/8/2000 (granting three exceptional steps to members of the teaching staff in the primary and intermediate teaching establishment) and No. 250/2000 include only the members of the teaching staff included in the establishment and contracted persons have no relation thereto. And whereas the provisions of Article 45 of the Budget Law for the year 2000 referred to above cannot be invoked given that this Article aimed at equalising the contracted person with the civil servant who is his counterpart in function and category with respect to the basic salary which was converted in accordance with the schedules annexed to Law No. 717/98 which concern the salaries of administrative functions to the exclusion of the functions of the teaching establishment, and furthermore the provisions of the aforementioned Article (45) do not include the compensations and other benefits that may supervene upon the basic salary of the civil servant pursuant to special legal texts. Therefore, the Board of the Civil Service Board opined the impossibility of persons contracted in agricultural education under annual contracts benefiting from the provisions of the two Laws No. 250/2000 and No. 551/2003

42 - Financial assistance - Deceased contracted person: In the matter concerning the request for the rendering of an opinion on the possibility of the heirs of a former contracted person at the Ain El Delbe Water Authority benefiting from financial assistance equivalent to his compensation for 9 months, the Civil Service Board replied by its letter No. 1976 dated 29/9/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Energy and Water as follows: Whereas paragraph 2 of Article 24 of the Employees' Regulations of the Ain El Delbe Water Authority provides that "if the employee dies of an illness or an accident not related to the function, his family shall be granted assistance equivalent to his basic salary at the date of death for nine months". And whereas the Fourth Article of the contract of agreement of the person concerned exclusively specified the articles of the Employees' Regulations of the Authority applicable to the Second Party with respect to his rights and duties, and the provisions of paragraph 2 of Article 24 mentioned above were not included among them. And whereas the Ain El Delbe Water Authority is one of the investment public institutions subject to the provisions of the General Regulations for Public Institutions. And whereas Article 10 of the General Regulations for Public Institutions provides that the Board of Directors shall oversee the implementation of the policy of the public institution and direct its activity and shall generally take, within the scope of the laws and regulations, the necessary decisions to achieve the purpose for which the public institution was established and to ensure the proper functioning of work therein, and the Board of Directors shall in particular approve the regulations of the institution and its budget and other acts enumerated in the body of this Article, including the provision of contributions and financial assistance to persons other than the employees and wage-earners of the institution. And whereas the contributions and financial assistance that may be decided by the Board of Directors of the public institution concerned in accordance with the aforementioned Article 10 are granted on a personal basis to persons working in the public institution other than employees and wage-earners, and they thereby differ from the death assistance which is granted to the heirs. And whereas the death assistance decided by the State for the heirs of persons working for it is considered one of the benefits that require a special text, due to the financial burdens it imposes upon public funds. And whereas the matter of the non-benefiting of the family of the deceased person concerned from the assistance provided for in paragraph 2 of Article 24 of the Employees' Regulations of the Ain El Delbe Water Authority is legally sound. Therefore, the Board of the Civil Service Board opined that it is not possible to grant the family of the person concerned the benefit of the death assistance under consideration.

43 - Rescission of contract - dismissal deductions: In the case concerning the possibility of paying a dismissal from service indemnity to a contracted engineer who requested the non-renewal of his contract for the year 2004, the Civil Service Board replied by its Letter No. 218 dated 7/4/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities with the following: Whereas paragraph "d" of Article Seven of the contract concluded between the Municipality of Beirut and Mr. (-- --) pertaining to the year 2003 provided as follows: "If the contract is rescinded by the Second Party, he shall not be entitled to claim a dismissal from service indemnity." And whereas the contract is the law of the contracting parties, and whereas the person concerned requested the non-renewal of his contract for the year 2004 and not its rescission, and whereas the non-renewal of the contract differs entirely from the rescission of the contract, given that the non-renewal of the contract means that upon the expiry of the period of validity of the contract in force, the measures leading to its renewal for another period are not taken, whereas the rescission of the contract means terminating its validity before the expiry of its specified term at the request of one of the two parties. And whereas the contract pertaining to Mr. (-- --) for the year 2003 is until 31/12/2003, and Mr. (-- --) executed his contract until the aforementioned date. And whereas Council of Ministers Decision No. 52 dated 20/11/ 2003, which provided for extending the employment of contractors for a maximum period of 31/12/2004 and continuing to disburse their salaries and wages prior to the completion of the transactions relating to the extension, does not mean the automatic renewal of the contract with Mr. (-- --) given that he expressed his wish not to renew the contract with him for the year 2004, therefore the Board of the Civil Service Board considered that the person concerned is entitled to receive the dismissal indemnity for the years of his contractual services that he performed with the Municipality of Beirut, on the grounds that his situation is not covered by the provisions of Article Seven of the aforementioned contract of agreement, and that his request not to renew his contract for the year 2004 does not fall within the concept of rescission set forth in the aforementioned article, given that what was set forth in Article Seven as to granting the right to one of the two parties to the contract to rescind the contract is intended to mean the rescission of the contract before the expiry of its term, and that the condition set forth in the contract as to the non-entitlement to the dismissal indemnity in the event that the contract is rescinded by the Second Party does not apply to the situation of the person concerned.

44 - Aggregation of prior services in a municipality to the administration: In the case concerning the issue of aggregating the prior services of a firefighter in the Municipality of Saida to his subsequent services in the Directorate General of Civil Defense, the Civil Service Board replied by its Letter No. 1045 dated 17/6/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities with the following: Whereas the Ministry of Finance, by its Letter No. 2/S 1 dated 2/1/ 2002, approved the aggregation of the services of the person concerned for the period of his work in the Directorate General of Civil Defense based on the provisions of Article Two of Law No. 371/94 which permits the aggregation of services in Cadre "B", however it did not approve the aggregation of his services during the period in which he worked in the Fire Brigade of the Municipality of Saida, basing its non-approval on Article One of Law No. 383/94 which permits the aggregation of services in public administrations, the Lebanese University, or the Chamber of Deputies. And whereas Law No. 383 dated 4/11/1994 (Aggregation of Temporary Services of Employees Working in Permanent Cadres Subject to the Retirement System) provided in Article One thereof that an employee appointed prior to the entry into force of this Law in the permanent cadres subject to the retirement system shall be entitled to aggregate his services prior to this appointment in public administrations, the Lebanese University, or the Chamber of Deputies, of whatever nature, to his subsequent services in these cadres under the following conditions: 1 - That he was previously duly appointed, prior to the appointment in the permanent cadre, in one of the public administrations, the Lebanese University, or the Chamber of Deputies. 2 - That he submits, within a time limit not exceeding three months from the date of entry into force of this Law, an application to the Ministry of Finance to aggregate his prior services accompanied by the necessary supporting documents. 3 - That he pays to the Treasury Fund the retirement deductions and the dismissal indemnity for those services within a time limit of three months from the date of his notification of the approval of the Ministry of Finance as to the fulfilment of the conditions for aggregating those services and the correctness of the calculation. And whereas it is inferred from the text of Article One of the aforementioned Law No. 383 /94 that the services which the employee is entitled to aggregate to his subsequent services in the permanent cadre are those which he previously performed exclusively in public administrations, the Lebanese University, or the Chamber of Deputies. And whereas the services which Mr. Khadra requested to aggregate and which the Ministry of Finance did not approve are those performed in the Fire Brigade of the Municipality of Saida. Therefore, the Board of the Civil Service Board considered adopting what the Ministry of Finance expressed in this regard due to the absence of a legal text permitting the aggregation of the requested services.

45 - Aggregation of services - transfer from public administrations to municipalities: In the case concerning the rendering of an opinion on the Decision of the Municipal Council of Beirut No. 749/2003 concerning the aggregation of prior services performed by employees who held work in a position provided for in one of the permanent or temporary cadres in the State, or in public institutions, or in a public administration having special administrative and financial powers subject to a tutelage minister, or who held work therein by contract in a position similar to the positions of the municipality, provided that the services were performed continuously and without interruption, the Civil Service Board replied by its Letter No. 4052 dated 1/7/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities with the following: Whereas the municipality enjoys financial and administrative autonomy and the decisions issued by it remain in force within the municipal framework. And whereas there is no text in the laws and regulations in force that permits transfer from the cadres of public administrations or the cadres of public institutions to the cadres of municipalities, or vice versa. And whereas the provisions proposed in the attached Municipal Decision No. 749/ 2003 deal with the services performed by the civil servant in the public administration and the services performed by the employee in public institutions. And whereas the civil servant in the permanent cadre or the employee in a public institution, upon his appointment in the cadre of the municipality, must terminate his relationship with the administration or the public institution for which he worked, and his financial rights resulting from the services he performed in the past must be liquidated, in accordance with the legal rules in force. Therefore, the Board of the Civil Service Board considered that a municipal decision cannot permit the aggregation of the requested prior services to the subsequent services in the municipality, as this conflicts with the obligation to liquidate the prior services

of the civil servant for his services in public administrations and institutions.

47 - Cooperative - Temporary Transportation Allowance - Transportation and Travel Allowance: In the case concerning the entitlement of certain workers in the State Employees' Cooperative to receive a temporary transportation allowance for the days of their attendance at workplaces affiliated with the Cooperative and different from their primary workplaces, the Civil Service Board replied by its Letter No. 2106 dated 21/10/2004 addressed to the State Employees' Cooperative with the following: Whereas Paragraph (a) of the First Article of Law No. 266 dated 23/10/1993 provided for the granting of a temporary transportation allowance paid monthly to all workers in public administrations, including permanent and temporary employees of various positions and cadres, and contractors.... and members of the teaching staff across the various types and stages of public and private education... with the exception of military personnel of all categories, as well as those who benefit from in-kind transportation benefits regardless of their positions and cadres.... And Paragraph (b) of the same Law provided that the aforementioned allowance accrues for each day of actual attendance at a rate of 2% of the minimum wage in force at any time. Whereas Decree No. 5860 dated 10/7/2001 determined the amount of the temporary transportation allowance provided for in Law No. 266/93 at six thousand Lebanese pounds for each day of actual attendance at work, and the aforementioned allowance was also determined pursuant to Decree No. 7723 dated 5/4/2002 at the same value for workers in public institutions for each day of actual attendance at work. Whereas Item (1) of Decision No. 177 /2001 of the Board of Directors of the Cooperative dated 11/7/2001, coupled with the approval of the tutelage authority by its Decision No. 9 dated 31/7/2001, provides as follows: "1 - In the State Employees' Cooperative, as of 1/1/ 2001, the temporary transportation allowance provided for in Law No. 266 dated 23/10/1993 is determined at the amount of six thousand Lebanese pounds for each day of actual attendance at work." Whereas it appears from returning to the basic legal text that introduced the temporary transportation allowance, which is Law No. 67 dated 8/6/1991, that Paragraph (b) of the First Article thereof provides as follows: "b - The allowance mentioned in the preceding paragraph (i.e., the temporary transportation allowance) shall only accrue for actual attendance and shall be determined in proportion to the minimum wage in force at any time in accordance with the following rates for each day of actual attendance: - 1.5% for a person whose place of residence is located in the city, town, or village in which his place of work is located. - 3% for a person whose place of residence is located outside the city, town, or village in which his place of work is located." Whereas it is inferred from the legal texts referred to above that the temporary transportation allowance provided for in Law No. 67/91 and subsequently in Law No. 266/93, the amount of which is determined at six thousand Lebanese pounds pursuant to Decrees No. 5860/ 2001 and No. 7723/2002 and Decision No. 177/2001 of the Board of Directors of the Cooperative mentioned above, accrues to the employee, the salaried employee, the wage earner, and the contractor for each day of actual attendance at his place of work to which he is appointed or to which he is duly transferred. Whereas Paragraph (1) of Article (21) of the Regulations of the State Employees' Cooperative provides as follows: "The employees of the Cooperative may be granted all other allowances and bonuses, including the special allowance, the overtime allowance, the travel allowance and transportation fares, and other various allowances within the scope of the conditions determined for State employees...". Whereas the applicable legal provisions provide that an employee who travels outside his workplace for official duty, and pursuant to a duly issued mission assignment order, shall receive a transportation and travel allowance. Whereas Article (43) of Decree No. 1602 dated 27/ 12/1978 (Provisions Relating to Transportation and Travel Allowance) provides that the transportation and travel allowance shall not be due to an employee who is attached to ensure a specific work or a specific function outside his workplace, if his work or function at the place of his attachment is characterized by practical continuity and he is at the same time exempted from performing his primary work or his primary function. Whereas the temporary transportation allowance - according to the foregoing - accrues to the employee for each day of actual attendance at his primary place of work, whereas the transportation and travel allowance is granted to the employee who duly travels outside his workplace for official duty. Therefore, the Committee of the Civil Service Board deemed that the workers referred to above are not entitled to receive the temporary transportation allowance for the days on which they did not attend their primary workplaces; however, the Cooperative may, in the event that the public interest so requires, resort to assigning persons in its service to travel outside their workplace pursuant to mission orders, such that the assignee in this situation receives transportation fares and a travel allowance pursuant to the provisions of Article 21 of the Cooperative Employees' Regulations and the provisions of the Third Article of Decree No. 1842 dated 6/12/1999 (Raising the Minimum Salaries and Wages in the State Employees' Cooperative...) in addition to the temporary transportation allowance in the event that he attended his workplace prior to travelling to execute the mission assigned to him; whereas in the event that he executed this mission without attending the primary workplace, he shall only receive transportation fares and a travel allowance.

48 - Severance indemnity difference - physicians and pharmacists - Social Security: In the case concerning the possibility of applying the text of Article (7) of Decree No. 1842 dated 6/12/1999 (raising the minimum salaries and wages in the State Employees' Cooperative...) in order to calculate the difference in the severance indemnity from service for full-time physicians and pharmacists in the Cooperative which shall be added to the amount of the indemnity due from the National Social Security Fund, the Civil Service Board answered by its letter No. 3819 dated 14/12/2004 addressed to the State Employees' Cooperative as follows: Whereas Article (7) of the aforementioned Decree No. 1842/99 provides as follows: "Article Seven: - There shall be deducted from the basic salary of the employee: 1 - Half the salary of the first month of the employee's service. 2 - 3% (three percent) of the salary. 3 - The first monthly instalment of every increase occurring to the salary. - These deductions shall be transferred to the end-of-service indemnity reserve in the Cooperative and shall be allocated to pay the end-of-service indemnity to its employees who are mandatorily or optionally affiliated with the end-of-service indemnity branch of the National Social Security Fund, and to cover the end-of-service indemnities for those of them who are not affiliated with this branch". And whereas Article (15) of Decision No. (5) dated 13/5/ 2004 (Regulations on full-time contracting with physicians and pharmacists in the State Employees' Cooperative) provides that "the contracted person shall be granted a severance indemnity from service, calculated in accordance with the bases specified in the regulations of the employees of the Cooperative". And whereas the physicians and pharmacists contracted with the Cooperative receive the severance indemnity from service from the National Social Security Fund. And whereas the Civil Service Board had previously stated in its attached letter No. 3495 dated 21/10/2004, that it is required of the Cooperative, pursuant to the text of the aforementioned Article (15), to grant the full-time physician or pharmacist contracted with it the benefit of the difference - if any - between the amount of the indemnity due to him pursuant to the provisions in force at the National Social Security Fund and the amount resulting from the calculation of the indemnity in accordance with the regulations in force at the Cooperative in this regard. And whereas the Directorate General of the State Employees' Cooperative considers, in its letter No. 4317/S 1/2004, and for the purpose of calculating the difference in the severance indemnity from service for the concerned contracted persons, that the provisions of Article (7) with its three paragraphs of Decree No. 1842/99 should be applied to these indemnities, on the grounds that an additional obligation may be incurred by the finances of the Cooperative as a result of paying the aforementioned severance indemnity in accordance with the bases specified in the regulations of the employees of the Cooperative, after it had been sufficed with the indemnity specified at the National Social Security Fund. Therefore, the Committee of the Civil Service Board decided to adopt the opinion of the Employees' Cooperative in this respect.

49 - Wage earners - engineers - the /13th/ month - calculation of the bonus: In the case concerning the issue of including the rate of the thirteenth month when calculating the bonus allocated to wage earners in the Tripoli Water Authority and fixed at 33% for engineers and 15% of the salary for the remaining wage earners, the Civil Service Board answered by its letter No. 1917 dated 28/8/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Energy and Water as follows: Whereas the Council of Ministers, by its Decision No. 4 dated 8/8/1984, had approved the proposal of the Ministry of Hydraulic and Electric Resources (formerly) comprising the granting to employees and wage earners of a rate not exceeding 33% of the salary for engineers and 15% of the salary for the remaining employees and wage earners who adhered to full-time working hours and performed works worthy of appreciation in the public institutions subject to the tutelage of the aforementioned Ministry, provided that the Directors General and the competent Directors shall have - for reasoned causes - the right to withhold it from those who do not deserve it. And whereas the wage earners in the Water Authorities continued to receive the bonus of 33% or 15% of the salary after the issuance of Decree No. 2448 dated 11/2/2000 (converting the salary scales of employees in the Water Authorities.....) on the grounds that they are not beneficiaries of the provisions of the aforementioned Decree. And whereas the wage earners in the Tripoli Water Authority receive a monthly wage determined in accordance with the laws and regulations in force, and are also entitled to benefit at the end of each year from the salary of the thirteenth month, equally with the employees in the aforementioned Authority (Articles 5 and 26 of the Wage Earners Regulations in the Tripoli Water Authority). And whereas the bonus under consideration was granted to workers in the public institutions subject to the tutelage of the Ministry of Hydraulic and Electric Resources (formerly) in response to their demand for reciprocal treatment following the approval of the annual bonus for engineers working in public administrations pursuant to Article 33 of the 1981 Budget Law, which used to be calculated on the basis of the basic salary only. And whereas the Civil Service Board, by its letter No. 4146 dated 9/ 9/1999, and in the course of examining whether the bonus of 33 % for engineers and 15% for the remaining employees and wage earners in the Water Authorities, is required to be calculated on the basis of the salary and its accessories or on the basis of the basic salary only. Therefore, the Committee considered that the calculation of the annual bonus is calculated on the basic salary only without including in its calculation the production grant or any indemnity, supplement or accessory to the salary whatever its form, designation or nature, and consequently the rate of the 13th month does not enter into the calculation of the bonus allocated to wage earners and fixed at 33% for engineers and 15% for all other wage earners.

50 - Wage earners - Justification of absence - Reinstatement to work - Force majeure: In the case concerning the dismissal of a permanent wage earner from his work effective from 1/4/2004 due to his interruption of work for a period exceeding fifteen days without a justified and legitimate excuse, the Civil Service Board replied by its letter No. 3844 dated 27/11/2004 addressed to the Administrative Committee of the Green Plan Execution Office as follows: Whereas Article One of Decree No. 6024 dated 6/8/2001 (the General Regulations for Wage Earners in Municipalities and in Public Establishments) subjected public establishments and municipalities to the provisions of Decree No. 5883 dated 2/11/1994 (the General Regulations for Wage Earners) and its amendments in all that does not conflict with the Law on Municipalities and the General Regulations for Public Establishments. And whereas Article 32 of Decree No. 5883/94 determined the cases in which the wage earner is dismissed, and among these cases is "if he absents himself from his work without a legitimate excuse for more than fifteen days in a single year or for more than seven consecutive days, provided that an absence lasting a full month without informing the Administration to which the wage earner belongs of its reasons shall be considered without a legitimate excuse, even if he subsequently submits a legitimate excuse for this absence". And whereas the new Special Regulations for the employment of wage earners at the Green Plan Execution Office have not been issued to date. And whereas Article 34 of the aforementioned Decree No. 5883/94 stipulated that "the service of the ordinary wage earner shall be terminated in all the cases indicated in this section (Termination of Service of the Wage Earner) by a decision of the authority having the right of employment upon the proposal of the Director General or the head of the administrative unit directly linked to the Minister". And whereas the competent authority for the employment of wage earners in accordance with the provisions of Article 8 of Decree No. 5883/94 has been determined such that this employment shall be by a decision of the Minister upon the proposal of the Director General or the head of the administrative unit directly linked to the Minister and after the approval of the Civil Service Board, from which it is inferred that it is necessary to submit decisions terminating the service of the wage earner for the approval of the Civil Service Board. And whereas the existing regulations remain in force in all that does not conflict with the General Regulations, and it is therefore required to continue applying the provisions of the Special Regulations for Wage Earners currently in force at the Green Plan Execution Office in matters not provided for by the General Regulations for Wage Earners, which entails that the provisions of the aforementioned Articles 32 and 34 of the General Regulations for Wage Earners apply to the present case. And whereas the dismissal of the person concerned from his work did not observe the provisions of Article 32 as regards the necessity for the Administration to wait for a month to enable the person concerned to justify his absence, given that the decision was issued seventeen days after the date of interruption (the issuance of the decision on 17/4/2003 and the interruption having been effective from 1/4/2003). And whereas it appears that the decision to dismiss the person concerned was not submitted to the Civil Service Board, and consequently the dismissal decision was tainted with a defect rendering it liable to annulment and revocation. And whereas the Administration considers that the failure of the person concerned to report for his work after 31/3/2003 is attributable to causes of force majeure beyond his control. And whereas, following the issuance of Decision No. 4/1 dated 17/4/2003 providing for the dismissal of the person concerned from work, it became impossible for the person concerned to report for his work. Therefore, the Board of the Civil Service Board deemed it necessary to take action to revoke the decision dismissing the person concerned for the reasons set out above, and to enable him to resume his work, provided that the period between 1/4/2003 and the date of his resumption of work anew at the Green Plan Execution Office shall not be considered part of his actual service and that he shall not receive any wage therefor pursuant to the principle of "no wage without work", and consequently the Administration's request, in these circumstances, is approved for the issuance of the attached draft decision reinstating the person concerned to his work.

51 - Wage earners - Daily workers - Benefits and allowances: In the case concerning the extent of the possibility of applying the Wage Earners Regulations in force at the Nabaa Al-Tassa Water Authority and its dependencies to the daily workers benefiting from the provisions of Council of Ministers Decision No. 63 dated 3/12/2003 as regards granting them the benefit of all the benefits and allowances enjoyed by permanent wage earners, the Civil Service Board replied by its letter No. 2845 dated 27/11/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Energy and Water as follows: Whereas the Council of Ministers, by its Decision No. 63 dated 3/12/2003, approved the submission of the Ministry of Energy and Water as regards granting daily workers the benefit of all the benefits and allowances enjoyed by permanent wage earners, the purport of which is that the Council of Ministers did not adopt the proposal to appoint them as permanent wage earners. And whereas it appears from the letter of the Civil Service Board No. 598 dated 26/3/2003 - and in the course of examining the regularisation of the status of invoice workers in the Water Authorities of Nabaa Al-Tassa and its dependencies, Tyre and its annexes, and Jabal Amel, merged into the South Lebanon Water Establishment - that the employment of these workers was dictated by the necessities of the need for manpower, contrary to what exists in public administrations, and that this employment has assumed a character of continuity and permanence in view of the continuing need for it. And whereas Article One of Decree No. 6024 dated 6/8/2001 (the General Regulations for Wage Earners in Municipalities and in Public Establishments) stipulates that the provisions of Decree No. 5883 dated 3/11/1994 and its amendments (the General Regulations for Wage Earners) shall apply to public establishments in all that does not conflict with the General Regulations for Public Establishments. And whereas the General Regulations for Wage Earners determined in Chapter Six thereof (Articles 19 to 22) the allowances and allocations that may be granted to permanent or temporary wage earners (such as overtime pay, financial assistance, transportation allowance, ...), and also determined in a separate chapter, which is Chapter Four (Articles 11 to 16), the leaves enjoyed by wage earners. And whereas it appears that the benefits and allowances enjoyed by wage earners in the Water Authorities - pursuant to the provisions of Decree No. 6024 dated 6/8/2001 and Decree No. 5883 dated 3/11/1994 - are distinguished by their nature from leaves of all kinds, which are considered rights and do not fall within these benefits and allowances. And whereas the rights of wage earners provided for in Decree No. 5883 dated 3/11/1994 (the General Regulations for Wage Earners), and in the legal or regulatory texts governing the status of wage earners in the Water Authorities, apply only to wage earners who have been duly employed in these Authorities. And whereas the benefit enjoyed by invoice and maintenance workers in the Nabaa Al-Tassa Water Authority and its dependencies from the allowances and benefits enjoyed by wage earners in the said Authority must remain within the limits of what the Council of Ministers decided in its aforementioned Decision No. 63/2003. Therefore, the Board of the Civil Service Board deemed that the workers in the Water Authorities concerned by Council of Ministers Decision No. 63 dated 3/12/2003 cannot be granted the benefit of leaves of their various kinds, given that they do not fall among the benefits and allowances from which the said Decision permitted them to benefit.

52 - Associate - Calculation of the Periodic Increment - Calculation of Actual Service: In the case concerning the extent of entitlement to advancement steps for certain associates in the Ministry of Information considered as surplus, who were attached to the National Employment Office, the Civil Service Board replied by its Letter No. 3759 dated 7/4/2004 addressed to the National Employment Office as follows: Whereas Paragraph (2) of Item (Second) of Article 12 of Decree No. 5240/2001 provides that the monthly compensation for each of the persons concerned by the provisions of Item Second of this Article shall be determined in accordance with the provisions of the regulations in force, taking into account the level of the position whose duties are similar to the duties he is assigned to perform, and his previous years of service by granting him the equivalent of one advancement step for every three years prior to his attachment to the new duty station, within the salary scale of the similar position comparable to his new duties. And whereas the decisions issued by the Board of the Civil Service Board concerning the attachment of associates to public administrations, public institutions, and municipalities include a request by this Board from the administration concerned to draw up draft mutual agreement contracts with the concerned parties in accordance with the provisions of Article Twelve of Decree No. 5240/ 2001 And whereas the Ministry of Information, by its Letter No. 786/W dated 28/6/ 2002, had indicated that the certificate of service issued by the National Social Security Fund and attached to the personal file of each of the associates with it includes a specification of the date of commencement of his work with it, as well as periods of interruption if any exist. And whereas it is required, when drawing up the draft mutual agreement contracts, to abide by the provisions of Paragraph (2) of Item (Second) of Article (12) of Decree No. 5240/2001 mentioned above, to determine the monthly compensations of the concerned parties, on the basis of a certificate of service issued by the National Social Security Fund for each of the concerned parties, in addition to a certificate from the Ministry of Information proving that each of them is still persevering in his work at the said Ministry. Therefore, the Board of the Civil Service Board considered that the years of service for which the concerned associate is entitled to the equivalent of one advancement step for every three years of service, are the previous actual services performed by him, the calculation of the duration of which is required to begin as of the date of his commencement of work at the Ministry of Information specified in the certificate issued by the National Social Security Fund attached to his personal file, provided that he continues uninterruptedly in determining the actual, whereas if what is meant is determining the date of entitlement to subsequent periodic increments that are granted to the associates after the commencement of their work in the capacity of contractors, it is required that the calculation of the period necessary for entitlement to these increments begin as of the date of commencement of their work as contractors.

Grade Two Competitive Examination for Admission to the National Institute of Administration: This competitive examination has preoccupied the body of civil servants since its announcement on 31/1/2004, during which time the Civil Service Board answered all questions, petitions, and inquiries submitted to it directly or through the Presidency of the Government, or through the Ministry of Justice, explaining its grounds and legal justifications through the four letters issued by it in this regard: I - Letter to the Presidency of the Council of Ministers No. 426/S dated 29/3/2004 First: The first impression formed from reading the letter of inquiry submitted to the Presidency of the Council of Ministers by persons who did not disclose their names is that they were appalled that a category of Lebanese citizens holding the required university degrees was permitted to participate in the Grade Two competitive examination, and in doing so they deny those persons their right guaranteed to them by the Constitution (Art. 12) to hold public office with no preference of one over another except in terms of merit and competence according to the conditions prescribed by law. As for the second impression, it is the decline in the level of knowledge of administrative and legal texts, and this matter must be heeded in the future by improving selection methods and raising the conditions of appointment currently adopted in the public sector. Second: Article /12/ of Law 222 issued on 29/5/2000 provided as follows: "In addition to the provisions set forth in Article /11/ of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6/1959 (Personnel Regulations) and its amendments, Grade Two posts in the general administrative cadre may be filled from among the graduates of the Preparation Branch in the Higher Special Degree at the Institute. Whereas the provisions set forth in Article /11/ of the Personnel Regulations (to which the text of Article /12/ mentioned above was added) are: Vacant technical posts in Grade Two may be filled by way of a competitive examination in which Grade Three civil servants and candidates from outside the cadre are entitled to participate. Consequently, Law No. 222/2000 is not in conflict with the Personnel Regulations, as it explicitly provided in Article /12/ thereof that what is set forth therein are "additional provisions" (that is, supplementary), given that they did not repeal the possibility of filling Grade Two technical posts (for it to be valid to claim the existence of a contradiction), and all that the matter entails is that the possibility of holding a competitive examination for Grade Two administrative posts was added alongside technical posts. Third: The Civil Service Board, through announcing the competitive examination, applied the relevant legal texts, and consequently the legal justification for the competitive examination is the text of Article /12/ read in conjunction with Article /6/ of Law No. 222/2000 (and its amendments), which provides as follows: "In addition to its primary duties and in cooperation with the Institute, the Personnel Department in the Civil Service Board shall conduct special competitive examinations for preparation at the National Institute of Administration for the posts mentioned in Article Two of this Law. Whereas Article Two of the aforementioned Law No. 222/2000 and its amendments provided as follows: "A public institution known as the 'National Institute of Administration' shall be established and shall be subject to the tutelage of the Civil Service Board and to its law of establishment and its regulations, and shall undertake: 1 - The preparation of civil servants for the administrations at the level of Grades Two, Three, and Four - First Rank - of the general administrative cadre, provided that each grade shall have a special section of its own at the Institute as follows: - The Higher Special Degree for Grade Two posts. - The Higher Degree for Grade Three posts. - The Intermediate Degree for Grade Four - First Rank posts. 2 - The training of civil servants of public administrations, public institutions, and municipalities subject to the powers of the Civil Service Board...". Fourth: 1 - The standard of the administration, and the selection of talented elements distinguished by high competencies, has no relation to the age of the candidate, and the competitive examination remains the best method to reveal the capabilities and faculties possessed by the candidate, noting that years of experience in many administrative positions have not helped to improve the level of performance; strength of character, academic and cultural level, and the capacity for initiative and creativity are the aspects relied upon in many instances. 2 - The persons who will enter the Institute, after succeeding in the competitive examination, will undergo a preparatory course through which they will arm themselves with science, knowledge, and the required administrative and legal information that qualifies them to assume leadership posts. 3 - The competitive examination for admission to the judicial corps and the foreign service corps, all of which are leadership and sensitive posts, permits persons aged between /20/ and /35/ years to participate therein, noting that the Grade Three competitive examination is usually open to all citizens holding university degrees, and it is also considered to be among leadership posts, so why do they deny to others what they permit for themselves? What holds true for Grade Two (leadership) also holds true for Grade Three (leadership); indeed, Grade Three constitutes a larger proportion than Grade Two posts existing in the cadre, and the (practical) duties required of Grade Three are much greater than the duties required of a Head of Service (Grade Two). Fifth: 1 - Appointment to the administrative Grade Two by way of promotion is the common and predominant practice in the administration, and proposing appointment by way of promotion or by way of competitive examination rests with the competent Minister in his capacity as the supreme head of his administration, so why this targeting merely for announcing the first competitive examination for appointment to this grade by way of competitive examination. 2 - Most of the current appointments in Grade Two took place by way of promotion, and not competitive examination, the latest of which (for example) is what took place in the Ministry of Social Affairs, where promotion from within the cadre recently took place to fill four vacant posts of the administrative Grade Two out of five vacant posts, and consequently there is only one post reserved for the upcoming competitive examination in that Ministry. 3 - The logic set forth in the letter allows civil servants of Grade Four to cast doubt on the method of appointment to Grade Three by way of competitive examination, and to demand in their turn the amendment of the law, and that appointment to Grade Three be by way of promotion and not competitive examination; consequently, are they not entitled to demand this when they have spent their lives in the service of the administration, and among them are many who hold university degrees and are experienced in administrative work? Otherwise, how can it be acceptable to enter Grade Three from outside the cadre by way of a competitive examination (for civil servants and non-civil servants) and not be acceptable for Grade Two so long as the law permitted it, and does a restricted competitive examination become acceptable here. - Indeed, more than that, why is appointment to the technical Grade Two from outside the cadre acceptable (and without provoking the outrage of civil servants of the technical Grade Three currently present in the administration) and not acceptable for the administrative Grade Two? Sixth: The competitive examination is the only means that limits automatic discretionary promotion, even if by a small percentage, and instills hope in those who have no political backing to enter public office other than their success in proving their personal capabilities and academic qualifications, strictly within a framework of fair competition, equal opportunity, and equality in rights and duties to hold public office. Seventh: Administrative jurisprudence is settled that a civil servant may not invoke an acquired right in order to maintain an existing regime, as it is subject to amendment or repeal at any time, pursuant to the text of Article Two of the Personnel Regulations issued by Legislative Decree No. 112/1959, which states: "Civil servants are subject to the legal and regulatory provisions relating to public offices, and all subsequent legal and regulatory provisions shall apply to them, without their having any acquired right to benefit from previous provisions". Eighth: Among Grade Three civil servants, and the authors of the letter (of concealed names) may be among them, are those who hold university degrees that have no relation to the science of administration (history - literature - journalism - social sciences), and they entered public office under previous texts that equated a law degree with all other university degrees, and that was pursuant to Council of Ministers Resolution No. /2 dated 9/1/1980, which considered all recognized university degrees, regardless of their specializations, as equivalent to a law degree. This reality has negatively affected, over the past years, the performance of some persons in the departments and services to which they were appointed due to the mismatch between their specializations and the duties entrusted to them, which made the nature of the specialization a misnomer by means of the phrase "or its equivalent". However, the Council of Ministers recently approved by its Resolution No. /43/ dated 13/9/2001 the repeal of its (previous) Resolution No. /2/ dated 9/1/1980 mentioned above, and requested the Civil Service Board to adopt the specialization closest to the posts to which appointment is intended. That is because it is essential that the civil servant possess a specialization that qualifies him to assume the post to which he is appointed, and this matter is among the fundamental and self-evident principles in modern administration, as the requirement of possessing a specialization compatible with the duties of the post must be established as one of the essential conditions for appointment or promotion to vacant posts, particularly leadership ones, and consequently we will have established the rule: "The right person in the right place".

III - Letter of the Ministry of Justice No. 1062/2004 dated 26/3/2004 It appeared that the petitioners (certain employees of the Fourth Category in the General Administrative Cadre) request, through their legal counsel: "First: To take a separate decision to stay the execution of the impugned decision and decree and to suspend the continuation of the entrance competition to the Special Higher Grade appointed pursuant to Decision No. 43/1 pending the determination of the merits of the present petition. Second: a - In form: To admit the petition in form for having been filed within the statutory time-limit and satisfying all its formal conditions. b - And on the merits: 1 - To annul the impugned decision and decree. 2 - To declare the right of the petitioners to participate in the entrance competition to the Special Higher Category of the Preparation Branch for Administrative Positions of the Second Category/Department of Public Administration and Law at the National Institute of Administration. 3 - To order the respondent to pay all fees, expenses, and attorney's fees." It appeared that the request for annulment and stay of execution is based on the plea of ultra vires. And violation of the principle of equality and contravention of numerous statutory texts, and that it caused grave prejudice to the petitioners. Accordingly, and after reviewing the relevant statutory texts, in particular the Personnel Regulations, and Law No. 222 dated 29/5/2000, and the Preparation and Training Regulations promulgated by Decree No. 11044 dated 27/9/2003 and the Statute of the State Council, in particular Article /77/ thereof, we request the dismissal of the petition for lack of a valid legal basis, and because everything advanced in its text does not accord with the provisions and texts governing preparation and training in the public sector, especially since the request for a stay of execution has become moot after the holding of the competition (the subject of Decision No. 43/2) on 6 and 7 March 2004; however, for the benefit of the truth, we deem it appropriate, with respect to certain points set forth in the submitted petition, to express the following observations: First: - Article /77/ of the Statute of the State Council included the following: 1 - "The State Council may decide to stay the execution upon an express request by the petitioner if it appears from the case file that execution may cause the petitioner grave prejudice and that the petition is based on serious and important grounds. However, execution may not be stayed if the petition seeks the annulment of a regulatory decree... The opposing party shall be granted two weeks at most to reply to the request for a stay of execution...". Consequently, we see here the impossibility of requesting the annulment of Decree No. 11044 dated 27/9/2003 and the Preparation and Training Regulations at the National Institute of Administration on the grounds that it is a regulatory decree and does not relate to individual situations, and this is a matter that precludes argument in this regard, and to say otherwise renders the text of Article /77/ without effect. 2 - Legal scholarship and administrative jurisprudence are in agreement that no one has the right to invoke a right to repeal an existing regulation even if it is unlawful, unless he submits a request to that effect within the statutory time-limit. (1) C.E 17 mars 1982, Alexandre et autres, les petites affiches: no.107, 27 sept. 1983, p.5 C.E 30 juin 1982, Assoc-Auto-defense: R.D.P. 1983, p. 518 C.E 9 fevr. 83, Assoc.interprof. des victimes de la maree noire, G.P. 83, 2pan. dr. adm. p. 443. (See to the same effect: Youssef Saadallah Khoury - General Administrative Law - Part One, page 392). 3 - Upon the expiry of the time-limit for judicial review, the administrative decision becomes final whether it is regulatory or individual, and the judge must raise this issue ex officio as it relates to public policy. (French Council of State, 4 December 1960, Louis, Recueil 1960, 705 and Lebanese Council of State, 24 October 1962, Abbas, Recueil 198, and 13 March 1975, Maleh, unpublished, and 12 July 1968, Mouawad, Administrative Collection 1968, p. 168 etc..). Second: With respect to the request for the annulment of Decision No. /174/ on the grounds that it caused grave prejudice to the petitioners: We reply as follows: 1 - Texts issued by the Administration that grant individuals rights in specific matters and places, whether by giving a license, a grant, a real right, or participation in a certain matter and otherwise.., all specify conditions therefor, such that anyone who satisfies the required conditions may benefit from the advantages secured by the text issued by the Administration, and with the exception of these, an ordinary person who does not satisfy the conditions required by the Administration cannot invoke prejudice caused to him, because one of the necessities of granting a right is the satisfaction of the duly specified conditions. 2 - Article /13/ of the Preparation and Training Regulations approved pursuant to Decree No. 11044 dated 27/9/2003 and in force for over six months, provided verbatim as follows: "Article 13: Entrance competition to the Special Higher Grade and the Higher Grade: 1 - The following may participate in the entrance competition to the Special Higher Grade and the Higher Grade: - Non-employee persons who satisfy the general conditions of appointment provided for in the Personnel Regulations, holding a university degree or licence in one of the branches of higher education, provided that this degree is among the degrees mentioned in a schedule drawn up by the Civil Service Board according to each position. - Employees of the Third Category with respect to the Special Higher Grade and employees of the Fourth Category and below with respect to the Higher Grade, holding one of the degrees referred to in the preceding paragraph. 2 - No one may apply for the entrance competition to the Special Higher Grade or the Higher Grade if he has previously failed in three competitions to enter either of these two grades." Accordingly, it appears, in view of the clarity and explicitness of the aforementioned text, that the employees permitted to participate in the competition that is the subject of the annulment action are employees of the Third Category only. Consequently, the request for annulment in this regard is not based on valid legal grounds that justify it, especially when the Administration has observed all the regulatory procedures required for the competition. 3 - The Civil Service Board, by announcing its Decision No. /174/ concerning those admitted to participate in the competition, has applied the text of Article /13/ of the Preparation and Training Regulations, and it does not enjoy any discretionary power in this context in view of the clarity and explicitness of the text, and had it done otherwise, its decision would have been subject to annulment for acting ultra vires. Consequently, everything advanced in this regard is rejected and must be disregarded. Third: With respect to the annulment of Decree No. 11044 dated 27/9/2003, in force since 9/10/2003, that is, for over five months, on the basis of the statement (page /7/ of the petition) that: "the expiry of the statutory time-limit for challenging general regulations opens the way for pleading their illegality in support of a challenge against individual executive decisions executed in application thereof. (See State Council - Decision No. 939 dated 12/7/1968) and that the law and jurisprudence are settled that the time-limit for a petition reopens and runs from the date of execution and, in the alternative, the illegality of the decree may be pleaded during a challenge against subsequent decisions based thereon." - This statement is surprising for several reasons: The first of which: is that a request for the annulment of a regulatory decree does not accord with the rules and procedures followed and in force when submitting a petition challenging enforceable and immune regulatory (non-individual) decrees or their amendments (time-limits - standing), and this matter, if accepted, would overthrow all the foundations and sources that govern the mechanism of administrative action and through which the Administration exercises its powers, and this also means the possibility of challenging at any time all decisions duly issued in the petition, and rendering the power granted to the Administration by a clear and explicit text meaningless; indeed, more than that, it renders the statutory time-limits for challenge, specified in the Statute of the State Council by a clear and explicit text (Article 69 thereof), of no importance when examining the satisfaction of the conditions of an action before the administrative judiciary, so that the rules governing administrative judicial actions become based on unstable, indeed discretionary, formal foundations, knowing that there is no room for interpretation in the presence of an explicit text. The second of which: is how can a precedent that is over /36/ years old (Decision No. 939/68) contravene the explicitness of the text set forth in Articles /69/ and /77/ of the Statute of the State Council promulgated on 14/6/1975 (that is, after the aforementioned precedent and not before it), for there is no room for interpretation in the presence of an explicit text. The third of which: is what was previously referred to above regarding the two administrative precedents relating to the inadmissibility of invoking the right to repeal an existing regulation except within the statutory time-limit. The fourth of which: is because the petitioners are employees in the General Administrative Cadre, subject to the Personnel Regulations which provide in their second Article verbatim as follows: "Employees shall be subject to the legislative and regulatory provisions relating to public positions, and all subsequent legislative and regulatory provisions shall apply to them, without their having any vested right to benefit from previous provisions." When an employee enters the service, a consensual relationship arises between him and the Administration indicative of his consent; however, all his obligations and rights in the position, such as promotion, whether through a competition or without a competition, are subject to the laws and regulations which the State may amend unilaterally without the employee being entitled to invoke vested rights, given that the legal status of the employee towards the Administration is a statutory and regulatory status. This fundamental rule results from the "inequality between reciprocal interests." A public utility requires continuity, authority, and the realization of the public interest. Consequently, an employee can only achieve demands that accord with this interest. Accordingly, the statement at the bottom of page /8/ of the petition that: "The impugned decision and decree have acted ultra vires due to their contravention of the law and regulations, which requires their annulment," is a statement that is rejected and not based on grounds worthy of acceptance. The petitioning party did not specify, according to what was set forth at the bottom of page /8/ of the petition, the statutory provisions contravened by the impugned decree and decision, that is, the provisions that permit employees of the Fourth Category in a clear and explicit manner, and not by way of deduction, the right to participate in the preparation competition for the Special Higher Grade, in order for the annulment petition to be complete in its elements, admissible before the competent judiciary, and supported by arguments rather than mere unclear facts and data. Fourth: With respect to the first ground (page /9/ of the petition): where it was stated: "On the necessity of annulling the impugned decision and decree for acting ultra vires due to their violation of the principle of equality in assuming public positions provided for in the Constitution. And that Article /13/ of Annex E of Decree No. 11044 denied employees of the Fourth Category in the permanent cadre the right to participate in the entrance competition to the Special Higher Grade, thereby contravening the principle of equality provided for in the Constitution." 1 - We reply that the principle of equality is not an absolute principle, but remains governed within the legal frameworks that specify the criteria and conditions on the basis of which equality or inequality between a group of individuals or categories may be established; for example, can an employee who does not hold a university licence plead non-observance of the principle of equality, or must he satisfy the conditions specified by the regulations to participate in the competition.
