Furthermore, Article /5/ of Law No. /717/ permitted only employees of the Third Category of the Fifth Grade at least the right to promotion; can inequality with the rest of the employees of the Third Category of the Fifth Grade and below be pleaded. - Pleading inequality in this manner extends to a large category of texts and provisions in force that do not grant the right to everyone to benefit from a certain matter except under specific conditions, and adopting the logic set forth in the petition exposes all of them to annulment, regardless of time-limits and standing. 2 - Legal scholarship and administrative jurisprudence are settled that: "The principle of equality is not an absolute principle, and it applies among those who are in the same legal situation or position, and it permits the legislator to differentiate in treatment among those who are in different legal situations, just as it allows him to depart from the principle of equality for reasons relating to the public interest." Every person or every case or situation must be treated in an identical manner in accordance with the same rules in force in the same legal system. And whereas the principle of equality applies only among persons or citizens who are in an identical situation, since the principle of equality before the law or regulations or public burdens means equality in law and not equality in fact. - P. Delvolve: Le principe d'egalite devant les charges publiques. in Bibl de Droit Public - Tome 88 - 1969. No 3: Le principe d'egalite s'impose... de maniere generale. Toute personne toute situation doivent etre traitees indentiquement, sous les memes normes, sous le meme regime juridique. No 216:... Le principe d'egalite de traitement ne s'applique qu'entre citoyens places dans une situation identique. No 218: L'egalite devant les charges publiques est une egalite de droit et non une egalite de fait... - B. Jeanneau: Les principes generaux du droit dans la Jurisprudence administrative P 4. a 39. 3 - The acceptance of nomination applications to participate in the competition does not give the applicant any vested right to participate in the competition, otherwise there would have been no need for the issuance of a subsequent decision by the Civil Service Board according to the text of Article /18/ of the Preparation and Training Regulations specifying the persons admitted to participate in the competition. This is in addition to the fact that the Preparation and Training Regulations, including the provisions and conditions for participation in the competition contained therein, are among the regulations published in the Official Gazette, and it is easy for any person, and for the concerned parties, to know whether or not they satisfy the conditions for participation in the competition. 4 - With respect to the second ground set forth on page /11/ of the petition: "On the necessity of annulling the impugned decision and decree for acting ultra vires due to their contravention of the provisions of Article /11/ of Legislative Decree No. 112/59." The Board of the Civil Service Board is surprised here at how the facts were narrated and the statutory provisions presented in a totally erroneous manner contrary to the explicitness of the text set forth in Article /12/ of Law No. 222, where the petitioning party distorted the data and made erroneous deductions far removed from accuracy, objectivity, and the rules of legal analysis and criticism that are supposed to be observed when filing annulment actions, as it was stated in the petition, in a manner totally contrary to reality: "that Article /12/ of Law No. 222 came as absolute without any specification of a certain category, and without any exclusion of another." This statement is purely erroneous, because the aforementioned Article /12/ exclusively specified the persons from among whom positions of the Second Category in the General Administrative Cadre may be filled, namely the graduates of the Preparation Branch for the Special Higher Grade at the Institute. And pursuant to the text of Article /14/ of Law No. 222/2000, which provided for specifying the details of implementation of the aforementioned Law by decrees taken in the Council of Ministers..., Article /13/ of the Preparation and Training Regulations approved pursuant to Decree No. 11044 specified the persons who are graduates of the Preparation Branch for the Special Higher Grade, and they are the persons admitted to participate in the qualifying competition therefor. The implementation of laws takes place in practice by completing the provisions of the law when it is limited to laying down the fundamental principles of matters (the object of legislation), leaving to the executive authority its completion by way of regulation, either by regulatory decrees taken in the Council of Ministers or by ministerial decisions issued by the competent ministers, and in this case the execution of the law remains conditional upon the issuance of the regulatory provisions completing it. Fifth: With respect to the third and fourth grounds (pages /12/, /13/, and /14/ of the petition) for annulment, on the plea: "that the impugned decision and decree acted ultra vires because they were taken for a purpose other than the purpose for which the law vested the competent authority with the right to take them (Detournement de pouvoir)... and because they were based on incorrect grounds." These two grounds are nothing more than superfluous padding and repetition as they carry the same meaning set forth in the two preceding grounds and did not bring any significant new data, and consequently there is no need to repeat our foregoing reply above. For all the foregoing, we request the dismissal of the action on the merits as Decision No. 174 was issued in accordance with the regulatory provisions set forth in the text of Article /13/ of the Preparation and Training Regulations and in observance of all the procedures required for holding the competition.

Article /8/, paragraph - c - of Decree No. 8337 dated 30/12/1961 (Organisation of the Civil Service Board) provides that the Council of Ministers shall hear the President of the Civil Service Board when examining: "Disputes arising between the Civil Service Board and the competent ministries and submitted to the Council of Ministers pursuant to the provisions of Article (97) of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6/1959 (Personnel Regulations) and its amendments. The aforementioned Article (97) provides that "if a dispute arises between the Civil Service Board and the competent ministry... the matter shall be submitted to the Council of Ministers for settlement". - And Article (11) of Decree No. 8337 dated 30/ 12/1961 relating to the organisation of the Civil Service Board requires the President of the Civil Service Board to submit annually to His Excellency the President of the Council of Ministers a report on the works of the Board, the decisions of the Body, the results of its oversight and its proposals of principle, and to send copies thereof to the ministries, public administrations, public institutions and municipalities over which the Civil Service Board exercises its powers, this Article requires among its most important requirements that "the report must include all decisions of the Council of Ministers taken pursuant to the provisions of Article (97) of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6 /1959 and in view of this obligation, the Civil Service Board finds no way other than to include in its annual report the decisions of the Council of Ministers by which it settled contrary to its opinion. We point out in this regard, the following observation: The stripping of the Minister's powers in appointing, promoting and dismissing employees and subjecting them to the provisions of the Personnel Regulations and to the powers of the Civil Service Board, was emptied of its content when the said Regulations included an article subjecting every dispute arising between the Minister and this Board to the will of the Council of Ministers such that the latter settles the dispute, and its opinion is adopted even though it frequently came in violation of the law in an explicit and clear manner. Therefore, this Board, out of its keenness on the reform process, its success and its continued permanence, and out of its belief in the objectives established by the legislator in the year 1959, sees an urgent necessity in repealing the text of Article /97/ to enable it to continue its oversight work in the hoped-for and required manner. This is with the knowledge that the approval of the Civil Service Board constitutes a certain guarantee of the validity of the measures taken by the administration, and that they took place in accordance with the legally applicable rules of procedure, and that the absence of such approval would cast doubt on the validity of the measures taken, and render them subject to accountability, because the approval of this Board is considered one of the substantial rules and formalities Procedure ou Formalite Substantielle which would vitiate the administrative act taken in the event of non-respect of those rules, as it constitutes a fundamental guarantee granted by the legislator to employees and other persons of public law. The purpose of this Decree is to determine the conditions for applying the text of the articles of Law No. 646 issued on 11/12/2004 (the Building Law).

Submission of the declaration - Granting of the receipt of declaration:

1 - The declaration of the works intended to be carried out specified in Item Second - Paragraph (b) of Article Two of this Decree shall be submitted in writing to the competent technical department accompanied by the documents that clarify and specify these works (maps, statements, ...) in addition to the documents specified by the decision of the Minister of Public Works pursuant to the text of Article 3 of the Building Law, where a special register shall be opened for this purpose.

2 - The competent technical department shall grant technical approval or refusal with the justification of the reasons within a period of one month from the date of registration of the declaration with it, and thereafter refer the transaction in the event of approval to the concerned municipality or to the Mohafez or the القائمقام (Qaimaqam) outside the municipal area in order to grant the owner the receipt of declaration within a period of three days at most after collecting the fees due.

3 - In the event that the competent technical administration delays in deciding upon the declaration within the period specified for it, the responsible engineer may: - Appear before the competent department after the expiry of the periods specified above and record in the registers his non-receipt of any reply from the administration, and have the head of the competent technical administration endorse that. He may also address a letter by registered mail to the head of the competent technical administration in which he records the non-receipt of any reply from the administration, and the head of the competent technical administration shall deposit with him a reply by registered mail and deposit a copy thereof with the head of the executive authority in the municipality or the Mohafez or the Qaimaqam within a period of fifteen days from his notification thereof. In this case, the head of the executive authority in the municipality or the Mohafez or the Qaimaqam may grant the declaration based on a certificate from the responsible engineer registered with one of the two Orders of Engineers stating that the declaration application has not been decided upon by approval or refusal within the period stipulated above, accompanied by the documents confirming that. And if the head of the executive authority in the municipality or the Mohafez or the Qaimaqam delays in replying within the three-day period, the applicant for the declaration may address, directly or through a notary public, and contrary to a period of six months at most from the expiry of the periods specified above, a letter in which he considers himself tacitly licensed for the works, accompanied by the amount of the fees due, provided that he undertakes to abide by the contents of the licence file and by the laws and regulations in force.

4 - The receipt of declaration is tantamount to the licence that permits the owner to commence the works after the written approval of the responsible engineer registered with one of the two Orders of Engineers, and it shall remain in force for a period of one year.

5 - The building licence application may include licensing for shoring works (Piling or Shoring up), the construction of enclosure walls and retaining and supporting walls, the reclamation of the land of the real property in its final form, and demolition simultaneously.

Procedures for Granting a Building Permit and Its Effects:

First: The Regulations to Be Observed in Granting a Building Permit:

A - In Granting a Building Permit:

A building permit shall be granted in accordance with the special laws and regulations pertaining to the zones in force on the date of granting the permit, particularly those relating to urban planning, public health, and public safety.

There must be attached to the permit plans and documents a plan of the natural ground levels of the property that is the subject of the permit and of the properties adjacent to it in contact with the boundaries of the property, signed by a surveyor engineer registered with one of the two Orders of Engineers or by a licensed topographer registered with the Syndicate of Topographers, together with photographs of the property and its surroundings prior to commencing excavation works.

Where it appears, after the lapse of more than two months from the date of granting the building permit, that there exist errors in the alignment and easement certificate or a violation of the Building Law or of the zoning regulations (zoning) in the granted permit that necessitate suspending work under the permit until it is amended to rectify it, only that which has been completed of the permitted building shall be deemed a vested right of the concerned party, and the unexecuted constructions shall remain subject to amendment so as to conform to the laws and regulations in force.

The time limits provided for in Item (B) below shall apply to the amendment of the building permit in this case after the submission of the amending plans by the concerned party, and the period of suspension of works shall not be counted as part of the period of the basic building permit, with the exception of the period of amendment of the plans by the concerned party that exceeds two months.

The holder of a valid permit that is unexecuted in whole or in part, granted prior to the issuance of Law 646/2004, shall have the right to choose between:

* Executing the building in accordance with the granted permit.

* Amending the permit in accordance with the provisions in force on the date of granting the basic permit, taking into consideration the zoning regulations (zoning) and easements in force on the date of granting the amendment in accordance with Paragraph "B" below.

* Amending the entire permit in accordance with the provisions of Law 646/2004.

B - Amendment or Addition to a Permitted Building:

In the event of an application to amend a building permit or to add a building, a supplementary amendment permit shall be granted, the validity of which shall expire upon the expiry of the validity of the basic permit, in accordance with the following cases:

1 - If the requested amendment or addition is unexecuted, the building permit shall be amended in accordance with the regulations (zoning) and easements in force on the date of granting the amendment.

In the event that there is an increase in the permitted area or a fundamental amendment to the design of the building, these amending plans shall be registered with one of the two Orders of Engineers in Beirut and Tripoli, and the fee shall be imposed on that which exceeds the basic permitted areas on the basis of the unit fee in accordance with the valuation on the date of granting the basic building permit.

2 - If the requested amendments are executed in whole or in part, the following shall be deemed vested rights:

* The sections executed in accordance with the granted permit.

* The executed sections amended so as to conform to the provisions and regulations in force on the date of granting the amendment to the permit.

* The executed sections amended which do not satisfy the provisions in force on the date of amending the permit, provided that the executed building does not exceed double that which is permitted in respect of the two exploitation ratios and the number of storeys without an increase in the number of permitted blocks.

This shall be subject to compliance with the regulations (zoning) that were in force on the date of granting the basic building permit.

The additions referred to in the two preceding paragraphs shall be subject to the provisions of Article Twenty-Three of Building Law No. 646/2004, and anything exceeding that shall be subject to the provisions of the Law on the Settlement of Building Violations (No. 324/94), or to the provisions on tolerances against payment of a fine (minor violations), in accordance with the legal provisions governing such excess.

Applications for the settlement of building violations in buildings that do not hold an occupancy permit and the fees for which have not been paid shall benefit from the provisions of Item "B" above.

C - Renewal of the Permit:

The renewal of a building permit shall be subject to the provisions of Law No. 646/2004 and to the building regulations and easements in force on the date of granting the renewal of the permit.

As for the permitted sections of the building the load-bearing parts of which (foundations, load-bearing walls, columns, beams, and ceilings) have been executed, the permit therefor must be renewed regardless of any amendment that has occurred to the approved regulations and easements, and the owner shall have the choice between adopting:

* All the provisions of Legislative Decree No. 148/83 and the implementing decrees pertaining thereto, including Article Seventeen.

* Or all the provisions of Building Law No. 646/2004 and this Decree.

D - On Time Limits:

Subject to compliance with the time limits provided for in the second paragraph of Article Four of the Building Law, the mechanism set forth in Article Three of this Decree shall be adopted.

Second - The Alignments to Be Observed in Granting a Building Permit:

In the event of an application for a building permit on a property affected by an approved unexecuted alignment, whether expropriated or unexpropriated, the approved alignment with all its effects shall be adopted when examining the building permit application, particularly in respect of the envelope, the line of sight, and the setback from the alignment:

A - If the unexpropriated approved alignment falls within the municipal boundaries of Beirut or Tripoli, or if the said alignment consists of the widening of an existing public road, no setback of the building from the boundaries of the property on the side of the section thereof affected by the alignment shall be imposed; rather, the setback from the boundaries of the alignment only shall be adopted, including the projections permitted beyond the envelope line on the side of the alignment.

B - Outside the municipal boundaries of Beirut and Tripoli, if the approved alignment does not consist of the widening of an existing public road, the setback from the boundaries of the property on the ground floor and the upper storeys on the side of the section thereof affected by the alignment must not be less than 4.50 m in the event that the building benefits from the line of sight and the envelope on the approved alignment, subject to compliance with the setbacks specified from the alignment for the basement storeys.

(Refer to Drawing No. 19)

In the event that there exist buildings executed on the unexpropriated approved alignment, the Higher Council for Urban Planning may exempt the buildings for the construction of which a permit is requested on the properties located along this alignment from compliance with the content of the preceding paragraph, subject to compliance with the setback imposed from the boundaries of the alignment only.

C - In the event of the absence of an executed public road reaching the property that is the subject of the permit application, the unexecuted approved alignment shall be adopted in respect of determining the manner of entry and exit of vehicles to and from the property, and the owner shall have the choice, upon submitting the building permit application, between:

* Considering the alignment as non-existent in respect of securing access to the garage, and paying the fees in lieu of the car parking spaces that must be provided on the property pursuant to the laws and regulations in force.

* Considering the approved alignment as an executed road, in which case the car parking spaces shall be provided in the building in accordance with the permit plans (in kind), while adopting the longitudinal section of the approved alignment in respect of the relationship of the entrances, exits, and ramps of the garage to the approved alignment and the calculation of the height of the building, provided that the owner shall be exempted from paying the fees in lieu of car parking spaces, on condition of submitting an undertaking drawn up before a notary public waiving the section of the property affected by the alignment in the event of its execution, such that the occupancy permit shall not be granted until after the registration of the undertaking by the owner on the real estate register sheet.

Third - Effects of the Building Permit:

A permit granted pursuant to the provisions of Law 646/2004 shall be valid for a period of six years, renewable once for a period of two years from the date of expiry of the validity of the basic permit, exempted from fees if no increase has occurred in the permitted area, provided that there is no amendment to the alignment, the easement, or the regulations in force that precludes the renewal of the permit.

Renewal applications shall be accepted at the technical departments during the three months preceding the expiry of the validity of the basic permit, and up to a maximum period of six months from the date of expiry of its validity, provided that this period shall be counted as part of the renewal period of the permit.

As for permits granted under Legislative Decree 148/1983, they shall be renewed for a period of four years provided that there is no legal impediment preventing their renewal, and permits that were renewed for a period of two years prior to the issuance of Decree 15874 /2005 shall be extended for two additional years provided that there is no legal impediment precluding their renewal.

Fourth - On the Execution of the Permit:

The owner of the property who holds the permit and his contractors must not commence the execution of the content of the permit prior to obtaining an order to commence execution signed by the responsible engineer and registered with the Order of Engineers.

Where the building permit includes one or more basement storeys, its execution shall be required to take place in two stages:

- A first stage: the execution of the basement storeys and the levelling of the natural ground necessary to secure the legality of the basement storeys and the levelling of the natural ground.

- A second stage: comprising the remaining sections of the permit, which is granted pursuant to the approval of the competent technical administration after verifying the proper execution of the first stage by virtue of a special authorization to proceed.

The works of the second stage may be continued under the responsibility of the responsible engineer, provided that the approval to execute the second stage is granted or refused, with a statement of the reasons for refusal, within a period of one month from the date of its registration with the competent technical administration. In the event that the administration delays in deciding upon the application within the specified period, the engineer may adopt the mechanism provided for in Article Three of this Decree to continue execution in the second stage.

Fifth - Permit to Commence Excavation and Shoring:

A permit to commence excavation and shoring may be granted under the responsibility of the owner prior to obtaining the building permit, in accordance with the following conditions:

- That the total area of the basement storeys subject to fees and for which a permit is requested shall not be less:

* than 2000 m2

* than 2000 m2 for an application for a permit for two or more basements.

- The application for a permit to commence excavation must be accompanied by the plans of the basement storeys (floor plans and sections) signed by the responsible engineer, showing the levels of the property before and after excavation and approximate measurements of the excavation quantities, together with his undertaking to supervise the excavation and execute it in accordance with the submitted plans.

- The application shall be submitted to the competent technical department, which shall refer the permit application, after auditing all the documents referred to above, to the head of the executive authority in the municipality, or the Governor (Mohafez), or the District Commissioner (Qaimقام) outside the municipal boundaries, accompanied by a technical statement of the value of the fees due on the permit for the basement storeys.

- The special permit shall be granted for a period of one year after collecting the value of the technical statement of the permit fee for the entire area of the basement storeys as a deposit to guarantee proper execution, provided that this deposit shall be deducted from the principal of the fees due for the building permit. In the event that the granting of the permit is not completed for any reason whatsoever, the paid deposit shall be allocated to the rehabilitation of the property and compensation for any damages resulting from the excavation, under the supervision of the head of the executive authority in the municipality, or the Governor (Mohafez), or the District Commissioner (Qaimقام) outside the municipal boundaries.

The payment of the value due above may be replaced by a bank guarantee.

If the value of the compensations due and the works for the rehabilitation of the property exceeds the value of the guarantee or the paid deposit, the remainder of the amount shall be registered as a privileged debt on the real estate register sheet pertaining to the property; however, if the value of these works and compensations does not exceed the paid deposit or the amount of the guarantee, what remains of its value after rehabilitation and payment of compensations, if any, shall be refunded to the concerned party, subject to the approval of the competent technical department of the rehabilitation of the property.

Sixth - Use of the Sidewalk:

The owner of the property, upon obtaining a building permit or a declaration receipt and upon commencing work, shall have the right to use the sidewalk in accordance with the following technical conditions:

1 - That the width of the occupied section of the sidewalk shall not exceed two metres as a maximum.

2 - Providing a pedestrian passageway within the sidewalk the width of which shall not be less than eighty centimetres (80 cm) throughout the period of work, covered with protection made of solid materials, without gaps, at an angle ranging between 30 and 45 degrees and the height of which shall not be less than two metres.

3 - That the said passageway be clearly separated from the used section of the sidewalk by means of barriers the height of which shall not be less than two metres, while securing all public safety requirements, particularly in respect of placing illuminated signs at the boundaries of the occupied section.

(Refer to Drawing No. 20).

4 - The owner shall be required to rehabilitate the sidewalk in conformity with what it was or according to other specifications approved by the administration, prior to submitting the application for the occupancy permit.

5 - The period for the use of the sidewalk shall expire upon the cessation of works or their completion within the period of the granted permit.

6 - The boundaries of the area of the sidewalk intended to be occupied must be specified in the building permit application, with a statement of the details of the barriers, the locations of the illuminated signs, and all the measures that will be taken to secure public safety requirements.

Seventh - Uncompleted Buildings:

Upon the expiry of the period of the permit, and in the event that the permit holder has completed the load-bearing parts of the building (foundations, load-bearing walls, all external walls, columns, beams, and ceilings), he may continue the remaining works without new permit fees becoming due from him; however, in the event of completion of the skeleton of the building (load-bearing parts and ceilings), a permit may be granted to complete the external walls of the skeleton of the building executed in accordance with the granted permit, provided that the building permit fees shall be collected for the entirety of the storeys the external walls pertaining to which have not been executed, according to the prevailing valuation.

As for the remaining internal and external works, they shall be deemed complementary works that require obtaining a declaration receipt.

In the event of executing the external walls without completing the external facades of the building, the owner of the property must finish the complementary works of the facades within a period of one year from the date of expiry of the period of the permit after duly obtaining the declaration; otherwise, fines shall be imposed for the unexecuted works of the facades equal to (15%) fifteen percent of the value of the building permit fees for the areas of the permitted building the facades of which have not been completed, according to the prevailing valuation for each year, calculated starting from the lapse of one year after the date of expiry of the period of the building permit.

Buildings existing prior to the entry into force of this Decree, the validity of the permit of which has expired, and the skeleton of which has been completed while their facades have not yet been completed (including the external walls), shall be subject to the provisions of the preceding paragraph in respect of delay fines, and the fees shall be valued and the fines shall take effect after one year from the date of issuance of Law No. 646/2004.

(Drawing No. 116 pursuant to Decree in force 617 /2007 must be inserted.)

The preceding item shall apply to violating buildings that cannot be settled, in respect of removing the violation and completing the facades or demolishing the building in its entirety.

The head of the executive authority in the concerned municipality, or the Governorate, or the District Commissioner (Qaimقام) in areas where there is no municipality, must, during the first month of each year, refer a list of the properties that contain buildings the validity of the permit of which has expired and the skeleton of which has been completed without their facades having been completed, after duly conducting the valuation for these properties, to the competent technical department, which in turn shall calculate the areas and the fines accruing on each property in accordance with the preceding paragraph and lodge the schedule of areas and fines with the concerned municipality within a period of one month from being notified thereof.

The competent technical departments, upon receiving any complaint regarding an uncompleted building outside the time limits provided for above, must refer the file, after duly conducting the valuation for the property that is the subject of the complaint and calculating the areas and the fines accruing for failure to complete the facades, to the concerned municipality within a period of two months at most from the date of submission of the complaint.

The municipality shall collect the fines or register them on the real estate register sheets pertaining to the concerned properties as a privileged debt.

The unexecuted internal works and external complementary works shall be subject to obtaining a declaration receipt or a restoration permit according to the type of unexecuted works, and obtaining the declaration or the restoration permit shall not exempt the owner of the property from the fines imposed pertaining to the unexecuted facades in accordance with the provisions of this paragraph.

Conditions of the Occupancy (Habitation) Permit:

First - Completion of the licensed building

Completion of the licensed building, for the purpose of obtaining the occupancy (habitation) permit within the meaning of Article 6 of the Building Law, shall mean the execution of all the works and conditions imposed in the permit, in particular the following works:

A - External works:

1 - Construction of retaining walls, land reclamation works and demolition works set out in the licensing plans.

2 - The structure of the licensed building in all its storeys, including the basement storeys.

3 - Installation of the electrical and sanitary networks for the common parts so that they become ready for use, and the mailboxes for the autonomous parts.

4 - Completion of all facade works, including balconies and all common parts.

5 - Casting or tiling the floor of the storey erected on pillars (pilotis), if any, the floor of the garage inside the building with its entrances and exits, and demarcating the spaces allocated for the parking of cars. Where the garage is provided for outside the building, the area allocated to it must be arranged by levelling and compacting its ground, including the entrances and exits leading to it, and casting it with concrete, paving it with asphalt, or tiling it.

B - Internal works:

Execution of all internal works that render the building fit for use in accordance with the purpose for which it is intended.

As for apartments the area of which exceeds 300 m2 square, including the parts that are not calculated within the total and surface exploitation ratios, there shall be exempted from such works: + internal whitewashing and painting, internal joinery works, sanitary and electrical fixtures, and kitchen cabinets, provided that the specifications of these works are specified in the body of the contracts of sale of these apartments in the event that they are sold prior to the subdivision of the building.

Second: Types of occupancy permit and the mechanism for granting them:

1 - Final occupancy permit:

Upon completion of the licensed building, including the external facades, the owner shall submit to the competent technical administration an application to obtain the occupancy permit accompanied by the required documents and the as-built plans of the executed works in the event that there are modifications to the licensed building registered with one of the two Orders of Engineers, in addition to a certificate from the concerned engineers, each according to his specialisation, in accordance with the regulations in force and in accordance with the licence or the executed modification and pursuant to the regulations of the two Orders of Engineers.

If it appears that the building conforms to the designs on the basis of which the permit was granted, or differs therefrom yet remained in conformity with the texts in force at the time the licence was granted and with the special provisions specified in the building permit, if any, the occupancy (habitation) permit shall be granted following the approval of the competent technical administrations and after all fees and fines due, where applicable, have been paid in accordance with the prevailing price at the date of granting the original building permit in respect of the additional areas executed without a licence.

In the event that the building or any part thereof does not conform to the texts in force, the owner shall carry out, under the supervision of the responsible engineer who signed the permit application, the works necessary for the building to become conforming, and he shall thereafter notify the administration and submit new plans, where applicable, signed by the responsible engineer and registered with one of the two Orders of Engineers in Beirut and Tripoli.

Where there are several buildings on the same property, a final occupancy (habitation) permit may be granted for each building or block separately (independent staircase and lift), provided that the common parts from which this block benefits, including the entrances, the garage, and the parts of: gardens, boundary walls, grading of the natural ground, basement storeys, public lighting and internal roads appurtenant thereto in accordance with the volumetric plan attached to the licence, are completed in full, and provided that all constructions executed on the property up to its date satisfy the legal conditions.

The right of disposal over the remaining uncompleted part of the building located within the common part shall be restricted to the owner of the original property or his legal successor, whether as regards renewing the licence, modifying it, or obtaining a new licence or an occupancy permit, without prejudice to the acquired rights registered on the real estate folio of the parts that have obtained a final habitation permit, including the subdivided parts, provided that this is registered on the real folio of the property.

If an infringement occurs in any block of the property, work shall be suspended in all the buildings and a notice of infringing building shall be placed on the entire property, with the exception of the parts of the building licensed for habitation and subdivided into autonomous rights.

Where there is a building subdivided pursuant to Article 26 of Law No. 539 dated 24/7/1996, a partial final occupancy permit may be granted for each part separately (autonomous right) if this part and the common parts (including the facades of the building) are completed in full in accordance with the licence, irrespective of the legality of the other autonomous parts.

Upon the granting of the final occupancy permit for a separate building or for all the licensed buildings, the building permit for the parts that have been finally licensed for occupancy shall be deemed terminated ipso jure even if the time limit for working thereunder has not yet expired.

2: Temporary occupancy permit: A temporary occupancy permit shall be granted for a building or for a part of a building, renewable annually until the expiry of the time limit of the building permit, in accordance with the following conditions:

* That all parts of the building executed at the date of the application for the temporary partial occupancy permit are in a legal status.

* That the works have been executed in accordance with Item "First" of Article Five of this Decree which render this part of the building fit for habitation or exploitation, and in particular the structure of the part of the building requested to be occupied, the internal complementary works, the basic sanitary and electrical installations, the septic tank in the absence of a public sewer, and the required garage.

The temporary occupancy (habitation) permit is valid for temporary subscription to water, electricity and telephone and for habitation in the part licensed for temporary occupancy within its validity period, and it is not valid for final subdivision nor for final sale and registration in the Land Registry Offices.

Third - Mandatory requirement to obtain the occupancy permit:

With the exception of the parts subdivided pursuant to the provisions of Law No. 539 dated 24/7/1996, it is prohibited to sell, transfer or assign parts of buildings that do not hold a final occupancy permit in accordance with the rules set forth above, and it is likewise prohibited to occupy the building after the expiry of a time limit not exceeding three years from the date of expiry of the time limit of the building licence unless the final occupancy permit has been obtained.

The occupancy permit shall be replaced by one of the following documents:

1 - A certificate issued by the competent financial departments in the governorates, or a certificate based on official records issued by the head of the executive authority in the municipality or by the Governor (Mohafez) or the District Commissioner (Qaimaqam) in the absence of a municipality, and on their responsibility, proving that the building was completed prior to the date of 13/9/1971.

2 - A certificate from the responsible engineer registered with one of the two Orders of Engineers proving the conformity of the building with the granted permit and the non-receipt of any reply from the administration regarding the application for an occupancy permit despite the expiry of the time limits specified in Article Six of the Building Law, in accordance with the mechanism set out in Article Three of this Decree, while complying with the time limits provided for in the third paragraph of Article Six of the Building Law.

In both of these cases, the building shall be deemed to be a legal building.

Remnants of Public and Private Property:

- The purchase of a remnant of public or private property belonging to the State or to the municipalities resulting from the execution of an alignment (ordinary or within a general master plan) or an expropriation shall only take place after the approval of the entity owning the remnant pursuant to the recommendation of the competent technical administration that prepared the study of the alignment. As for the purchase of remnants of private property, it shall take place in accordance with the provisions of the Urban Planning Law, and is not mandatory for the granting of the permit.

- If the competent technical administration and the entity owning the remnant deem it necessary to annex this remnant to the real property that is the subject of the building permit application, the technical departments concerned with examining the building permit file must include in the technical inspection report the value of the price of the remnant in favour of the entity owning the real property, estimated on the basis of the valuation adopted for the real property for levying the building fee.

The granting of the building permit shall be conditional upon the payment of the aforementioned deposit by the owner or his legal successor, provided that the formalities of declassification, demarcation, and annexation are subsequently carried out at the expense of the purchase applicant.

In this case, the remnant shall be deemed annexed to the real property that is the subject of the building permit application if the conditions for annexation stipulated in the real estate laws are met therein; otherwise, the remnant shall be deemed a single real estate unit with the aforementioned real property.

- The price of the remnant shall be finally determined by the committee specified in Article 80 of Decision No. 275/26 in accordance with the prevailing price on the date of payment of the deposit, and in the event of a dispute over the price, the competent appellate expropriation committees shall adjudicate thereon on the same bases within one year from the date of payment of the deposit. After the lapse of this period, the deposit paid shall be deemed the price for this remnant, and the Land Registry Departments must annex this remnant to the original real property at the request of the purchaser.

- The operation of annexing the remnant to the real property is not mandatory for the administration if it declares its allocation for public use.

II - Letter of the Ministry of Justice - Cases Authority No. 1047/2004 dated 9/3/2004 It appeared that the petitioner and her colleagues request through their legal representative a stay of execution of the effect of Decision No. 43/2 dated 31/1/2004 (organizing the entrance competition to the first session in the Special Higher Degree of the Preparation Branch for administrative Grade Two posts», and the annulment of Decree No. 11654 dated 27/12/2003 (determining the number of positions and titles of the posts envisaged for the first session in the Special Higher Degree of the Preparation Branch at the National Institute of Administration). Accordingly, and after reviewing the relevant legal texts, notably the Personnel Regulations, Law No. 222 dated 29/5/ 2000, the Preparation and Training Regulations issued by Decree No. 11044 dated 27/9/2003 and the Regulations of the State Council, notably Article /77/ thereof, we deem that the petition should be dismissed on the merits, for its lack of a valid legal basis, and because everything advanced in its body does not accord with the provisions and texts governing the public service in Lebanon, and consequently warrants being disregarded, especially since the request for a stay of execution has become moot after the holding of the competition that is the subject of Decision No. 43/2 on 6 and 7 March 2004; however, in the interest of truth and the law, we deem it necessary to point out the following observations: First: - Article /77/ of the Regulations of the State Council included the following: 1 - «The State Council may decide to stay execution upon an explicit request from the petitioner if it appears from the case file that execution may inflict grave harm upon the petitioner and that the petition rests on serious and important grounds. However, execution may not be stayed if the petition aims at annulling a regulatory decree... The opposing party shall be granted two weeks at most to reply to the request for a stay of execution...». Decision No. 43/2 and Decree No. 11654/2003 are two regulatory texts and do not relate to individual situations. 2 - The decision organizing the aforementioned competition was issued on 31/1/2004 whereas the petition was registered with the State Council on 1/3/2004, and was received by the Civil Service Board on 11/3/2004, in addition to the period that separated the issuance of the decision and the holding of the competition during which a petition for a stay of execution could have been submitted (assuming its validity), or whether what is required of the administration is to wait for the employee according to his circumstances and keep administrative situations unstable until he decides to submit an appeal petition, a matter which conflicts with the fundamentals of running the public utility and the higher interests of the administration, in addition to the fact that the referral by the President of the Cases Authority at the Ministry of Justice to this Board came in turn two days after the end of the competition. 3 - Decree No. 11654 determining and reserving the positions did not abolish the possibility of promotion, in addition to the fact that this is not an acquired right for the employee, and that the reserved Grade Two posts are far fewer than the posts currently vacant in the said grade in the general administrative cadre, and consequently promotion under the current legislation remains in force. Second: Administrative jurisprudence is settled that an employee may not invoke an acquired right in order to maintain an existing system, as it is subject to amendment or repeal at any time, pursuant to the text of the second Article of the Personnel Regulations issued by Legislative Decree No. 112/ 1959 which states: «Employees are subject to the legal and regulatory provisions relating to public posts, and all subsequent legal and regulatory provisions shall apply to them, without their having any acquired right to benefit from previous provisions». When an employee enters the service, a relationship of consent arises between him and the administration indicative of his agreement; however, all his obligations and rights in the post are subject to the laws and regulations which the State may amend unilaterally without the employee being entitled to invoke acquired rights, given that the legal status of the employee towards the administration is a statutory status. This basic rule results from «the inequality between mutual interests». A public utility requires continuity, authority, and the realization of the public interest. Consequently, the employee can only achieve demands that accord with this interest. Third: What is striking about the six petitioners or the majority of them (five of them) is that they hold university degrees that have no relation to the science of administration, (history - literature - journalism - social sciences), and they entered the public service under previous texts that equated a law degree with all other university degrees, based on Council of Ministers Decision No. /2/ dated 9/1/1980, which considered all recognized university degrees, regardless of their specializations, equivalent to a law degree. This reality has negatively affected, over the past years, the performance of some persons in the departments and services to which they were appointed due to the lack of proportionality between their specializations and the tasks entrusted to them, which rendered the nature of the specialization a misnomer through the phrase «or its equivalent». However, the Council of Ministers recently approved by its Decision No. /43/ dated 13/9/2001 the repeal of its (previous) Decision No. /2/ dated 9/1/1980 mentioned above, and requested the Civil Service Board to adopt the specialization closest to the posts to which appointment is intended. That is because it is imperative that the employee possess a specialization that qualifies him to assume the post to which he is appointed, and this matter is one of the basic and self-evident principles in modern administration, as the condition of possessing a specialization compatible with the tasks of the post must be set as one of the basic conditions for appointment or promotion to vacant positions, notably leadership ones, and consequently we will have established the rule: «the right person in the right place». Fourth: Regarding the points raised in the brief of the petitioning parties, who were appalled that a category of Lebanese holding the required university degrees was allowed to participate in the Grade Two competition, to the effect that this denies the petitioning party its right guaranteed to it by the Constitution (Art. 12) to assume public posts without preference for one over another except in terms of merit and competence and according to the conditions prescribed by law. We wish - initially - to point out the legal basis that permitted the organization of the competition for entry to the Special Higher Degree of the Preparation Branch for administrative Grade Two posts, namely Law No. 222 dated 29/5/2000 which has become a shielded law (Loi Ecran)

and which the petition under examination failed to mention, where Article /12/ thereof provided as follows: «In addition to the provisions contained in Article /11/ of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6/1959 (Personnel Regulations) and its amendments, Grade Two posts in the general administrative cadre may be filled from among the graduates of the Preparation Branch in the Special Higher Degree at the Institute». Note that the provisions contained in Article /11/ of the Personnel Regulations (to which the text of Article /12/ mentioned above was added) are: «Vacant technical positions in Grade Two may be filled by way of a competition in which Grade Three employees and candidates from outside the cadre are entitled to participate». Consequently, the possibility of filling technical positions in Grade Two was not abolished, and the whole matter is that the possibility of holding a competition for administrative posts in Grade Two was added alongside technical posts. The Civil Service Board, through announcing the competition, applied the relevant legal texts, and consequently the legal justification for the competition is the text of Article /12/ read in conjunction with Article /6/ of Law No. 222/2000 which provides as follows: «In addition to its basic tasks and in cooperation with the Institute, the Personnel Administration in the Civil Service Board shall conduct the special competitions for preparation at the National Institute of Administration for the posts mentioned in the second Article of this Law...». Note that the second Article of the said Law No. 222/2000 and its amendments provided as follows: «A public institution known as the «National Institute of Administration» shall be established and shall be subject to the tutelage of the Civil Service Board and to its law of establishment and its regulations, and shall undertake: 1 - The preparation of employees for the administrations at the level of Grades Two, Three, and Four - Rank One - of the general administrative cadre, provided that each grade has its own section in the Institute in accordance with the following: - The Special Higher Degree for Grade Two posts....». We also add - subsequently - the following: a - Regarding the statement that: «In a course contrary to the provisions of the law, the Civil Service Board proceeded on 15/11/2003 by its letter No. 226/S 1 to propose to the Council of Ministers to delegate to it the determination of the vacant positions in Grade Two in the public administrations and the submission of a draft decree to that effect to reserve these positions for graduates of the National Institute of Administration». - On this point, the petitioning party did not specify the legal provisions violated by the Civil Service Board when it requested the Council of Ministers to delegate to it the determination of the positions, in order for the annulment petition to have complete elements and be admissible before the competent judiciary and supported by legal arguments rather than mere facts and data in general terms devoid of any content, proof, or significant legal basis. Moreover, this delegation is not a delegation of constitutional or regulatory powers, but merely a delegation to determine a number of vacant positions in administrative Grade Two in the public administrations, as a preliminary step to submitting a draft decree in this regard to the Council of Ministers to reserve those positions, considering it the competent authority to reserve them, and subsequently the appointing authority therein in accordance with the provisions of Articles /64/ and /65/ of the Constitution. b - Regarding the statement that: «Without any legal basis, the degree that the candidate was required to hold was in Lebanese law or in public administration or in political or administrative sciences or the equivalent of any of them in terms of specialization». - We wish here that the petitioning party had scrutinized a little the texts governing the issue raised, as it would have become clearly apparent to it the legal basis through which the degrees required to participate in the competition for entry to the National Institute of Administration were determined, and avoided slipping into accusing the Civil Service Board and slandering it regarding «its practice of administrative work without legal bases». Item /1/ of Article /13/ of the Preparation and Training Regulations annexed to Decree No. 11044 provided verbatim: «Article 13: Entrance competition to the Special Higher Degree and the Higher Degree: 1 - The following may participate in the entrance competition to the Special Higher Degree and the Higher Degree: - Non-employee persons who meet the general employment conditions provided for in the Personnel Regulations, holding a university degree or licence in one of the branches of higher education, provided that this degree is among the degrees mentioned in a schedule drawn up by the Civil Service Board according to each post...». Consequently, the appeal - assuming its validity - should have been lodged against Decree No. 11044 within a period of two months from its entry into force, and not against the decision organizing the competition, and this is among the self-evident matters governing the procedure of petitions before the administrative judiciary, bearing in mind that a stay of execution cannot be requested for regulatory texts. c - Regarding the statement that: «This approach resorted to by the Civil Service Board is unique of its kind and it has never before gone so far as to reserve posts in violation of the general conditions of the post». This Board, in reviewing these points upon which the petitioning party relies in requesting a stay of execution, is once again astonished by the lack of familiarity with and follow-up of the texts governing administrative work, notably the text of Article /15/ of the Preparation and Training Regulations referred to above, where it is stated: «Article 15: Number of positions for the filling of which the competition is held: The Civil Service Board, after consulting the opinion of the competent public administrations, shall draw up a statement of the number of positions and the titles of the posts for the filling of which the competition will be held and they shall be reserved for this purpose in accordance with the rules». Is the approach of the Civil Service Board, in light of this Article, contrary to the general conditions of the post, or an application of those conditions governing appointment to public posts? This statement is far from accuracy and objectivity in analysis and in the narration of facts and data that must be adhered to in the field of bringing annulment actions. d - The Civil Service Board is not ignorant of the vacant posts in Grade Two in the cadres of the State (according to what was stated in the second paragraph of page /4/ of the application of the petitioning party); rather, ignorance lies in not knowing what is meant by the request to delegate to it the determination of the vacant positions in place of the Ministers. e - Even if the Minister (according to the petitioning party) had waived essential matters which he is not entitled to delegate to any party, (the fourth paragraph of page /4/), the appeal (assuming its validity and the fulfillment of its conditions) must be against Council of Ministers Decision No. 28 dated 20/11/2003 which delegated the power of designation, and Council of Ministers Decision No. 5 dated 30/1/2004 relating to the approval to hold the competition according to the positions that were determined and reserved in accordance with the rules, and not against the decision organizing the competition No. 43/2 and Decree No. 11654 dated 27/12/2003. f - The statement (on page /6/) that Decision No. 43/2 detracts from the justice that must prevail in the actions of the administration among all employees regarding deprivation from participating in the competition, on the ground that the Civil Service Board has no power to set the conditions for participation in the competition (the third paragraph of page /6/), is also a refuted statement and warrants being disregarded because, further to what we demonstrated previously regarding the power of the Civil Service Board to determine the degrees, Article /17/ of the Preparation and Training Regulations granted the Personnel Administration in the Civil Service Board the power to organize the competition and its subjects and detailed syllabi including the conditions of candidacy. However, in any event, we wish to point out the following here: First: The principle of equality is what governs the administration's relationship with persons, and this principle, according to settled doctrine and administrative and constitutional jurisprudence, is not an absolute principle, as it is for the legislator to depart from it, and to differentiate in treatment for reasons relating to the public interest, provided that this differentiation is compatible with the purpose of the law. g - It appeared that the defects which the petitioning party claimed to set out in the second half of the sixth page of its application and which it indicated involved a transgression of the law, have no basis in truth; rather, all the legally required procedures were observed when organizing the competition. All that was stated in the application is a narration of some facts rather than a presentation of legal data and arguments, which were mostly superficial and not supported by solid essential foundations. Therefore, the Civil Service Board, after scrutinizing the data contained in the petition, requests the dismissal of the case on the merits, on the ground that the conditions for a stay of execution contained in Article /77/ of the Regulations of the State Council are not met in the case, and in any event for the totality of the reasons we have set forth above.

Extent of Line of Sight:

Rooms intended for habitation or for daytime stay or for night and daytime stay must be provided with one extent of line of sight with a length of no less than 4.50 m four metres and a half through openings (windows, glass doors, or glass facades) overlooking open spaces or roads or both.

First - Technical Conditions for Providing the Extent of Line of Sight:

The extent of line of sight is the distance between the vertical line erected tangent to the most prominent point of the facade at the axis of the opening that lights and ventilates the room, and the vertical line erected on the boundary of the property or the boundary of the private or common open space provided for in Item Second of Article Seven of this Decree, or the boundary of the road on the opposite side. This distance is measured within the field of line of sight erected on the axis of the opening.

(Refer to Drawing No. 37)

1 - Measurements of Rooms Provided with an Extent of Line of Sight:

1 - a - An opening shall be deemed to provide the extent of line of sight for the room provided that.

* The depth of the room measured from the outer edge of the opening towards the inside of the room at the axis of the opening does not exceed five times the height of the room under the ceiling.

When the opening of the extent of line of sight overlooks the open air through a veranda or a loggia or under a cantilevered balcony (balcon) or a cornice, the maximum depth of the lit room mentioned in this Article shall be deemed to start from the outer edge of the veranda, loggia, balcony, or cornice, with the exception of the projection pertaining to the tile eaves.

(Refer to Drawing No. 38)

In the event of a difference in the clear height of the sections of the room lit by means of the opening, the minimum clear height of these sections shall be adopted; however, in the event that the ceiling of the room is sloping, the average clear height of the room shall be adopted.

(Refer to Drawing No. 39)

The depth of five times the clear height under the ceiling shall remain applicable so long as there are no other openings providing a legal extent of line of sight and envelope.

* The area of the room does not exceed ten times the area of the opening.

* The distance separating the edge of the opening and the wall of the room erected perpendicular to the wall of the opening does not exceed five times the width of the opening for each of the two sides.

* The room lit by means of the opening is confined within a rectangle perpendicular to the axis of the extent of line of sight, with a width of eleven times the width of the opening and a depth of five times the clear height of the room.

(Refer to Drawings No. 40 and No. 41)

Drawings 42 and 43 and the paragraph preceding them were repealed and replaced by the following paragraph pursuant to Decree in Force 617 /2007 Official Gazette 50

*The section of the room located behind the plane of the opening may benefit from lighting in accordance with the conditions specified in Drawing No. 42

( New Drawing 42 in accordance with Decree 617 /2007 for insertion )

Reception rooms, dining rooms, and the entrance hall shall be deemed a single room so long as they remain connected to each other by an opening whose width is no less than 2.50 m (two metres and a half) and whose height is no less than 2.00 m. (two metres).

1 - b - Rooms resulting from the partitioning of non-residential units with glass partitions shall not be deemed rooms requiring an extent of line of sight, provided that the transparent area of these partitions is less than sixty percent (60%), and voids in the area separating the two rooms shall be deemed part of the transparent area.

2 - Width of the Field of Line of Sight:

2 - a - A room lit onto the legal open space must be provided with a field of line of sight overlooking directly the section of the open space that accommodates the rectangle provided for in Article Seven - Item Second, Paragraph 1, of this Decree.

(Refer to Drawings No. 44 and 31)

2 - b - The width of the field of line of sight must at no point be less than 1/3 (one-third) of the distance separating the start of the vertical line from which the extent of line of sight is taken and this point, provided that it is no less than 2.00 m (two metres) over its entire extent and that this field forms a right angle in relation to the opening. The width of the field of line of sight must extend up to the opening pertaining to the ventilated room.

(Refer to Drawing No. 45)

2 - c - Rooms shall be deemed lit and provided with an extent of line of sight onto the legal open space either directly onto this open space or through the field of line of sight; and in the latter case, the entire field of line of sight erected at a right angle to the facade of the opening must discharge into the rectangle (5.50  4.50) provided for in Article Seven, Item Second, Paragraph 1 of this Decree.

2 - d - The legal open space must be free of any building, constructions, or natural obstacles over the entire area of the legal open space for the line of sight, starting from a height of at most one metre above the floor level of the lowest room in the building that requires an extent of line of sight onto the open space and up to the last floor in the building. It is not permitted in the upper floors to obstruct this vital space for the line of sight even in the event of the non-benefiting of the rooms of all or some of these floors from the line of sight.

(Refer to Drawing No. 28)

Second - The following shall not be deemed rooms requiring an extent of line of sight:

Stairwells - bathrooms - lavatories - entrances of residential apartments provided that their area does not exceed ten percent of the area of the apartment - waiting rooms for commercial offices and for liberal professions provided that their area does not exceed twenty percent of the area of the office with a maximum limit of thirty square metres (30 m2) - corridors - lobbies - pantries (office) - ironing rooms - storage rooms (pantries) - servants' rooms - laundry rooms, and kitchens in apartments whose area does not exceed 80 m2, provided that the area of the kitchen, laundry room, ironing room, storage room, or maid's room does not exceed eight square metres and that the rooms mentioned in this Item are independent of each other - lecture and sports halls - cinema halls - exhibition halls - lobbies of hotels, banks, and private and public institutions - nightclubs, restaurants, and cafes - kitchens designated for food preparation - laboratories - developing, photography, X-ray, operating, and examination rooms - machine rooms - factories (their industrial sections) - hangars - warehouses - buildings of farms for raising poultry and animals - commercial shops - offices pertaining to these halls, auditoriums, and rooms - offices in hotels and hospitals - libraries and video libraries (vidéothèques).

Certain sections of buildings, similar in terms of use to those referred to above, may be exempted from providing an extent of line of sight after the approval of the Higher Council for Urban Planning.

Third - Ventilation of Certain Places Not Required to Be Provided with an Extent of Line of Sight:

a) Small kitchens whose area does not exceed 8.00 m2 (eight square metres), in apartments whose area does not exceed 80 m2 (eighty square metres), and bathrooms and lavatories shall be ventilated individually:

a - 1 - Either directly onto the open air, provided that the width of the open space in front of the opening is no less than .50 m. (fifty centimetres).

a - 2 - Or by means of a lightwell (manwar) enclosed on all its sides, provided that its width is no less than 0.75 m. seventy-five centimetres) and that its area is no less than one and a half square metres clear of any pipes, extensions, or projections.

a - 3 - Or by means of independent individual ventilation flues whose internal diameter or side is no less than 15 cm (fifteen centimetres) connected:

* Either directly to the external open air.

* Or to a main ventilation duct whose diameter is no less than 30 cm (thirty centimetres) or whose internal side is no less than 20 cm twenty centimetres and whose minimum area is no less than 0.09 m2 (nine hundred square centimetres), free of any projection, equipped with an electric exhaust fan and leading to the external open air.

The ventilation flues and ventilation ducts must be tight and sealed.

More than one kitchen, bathroom, or lavatory may be ventilated onto a lightwell whose area is more than 1.50 m2 (one square metre and a half).

b) Rooms of buildings and establishments designated for specific uses, such as classified establishments (factories, cinema houses, theatres, stage theatres, operating rooms in hospitals, and the like...), shall be ventilated in accordance with the technical specifications and standards and the special provisions governing their regulation, if any exist.

c) Sufficient ventilation from the outside must be provided in places where fuel tanks, boilers, burners, and generators erected in the basement floors of buildings are located. The area of the ventilation opening and the power of the exhaust fan, if any exists, shall be calculated by the engineer and under his responsibility, provided that it is no less than 0.25 square metres.

d) Unclassified warehouses and car garages erected in the basement floors of buildings shall be ventilated either mechanically in a direct manner onto the open air, or by means of a shaft or shafts (Gaines) with enclosed sides and an open roof directly onto the open air whose width is no less than thirty centimetres and whose area equals:

Total area of the warehouses and garages in the lower basement floors / m2 Minimum area of the shaft / m2

e) Rooms of buildings and establishments not covered by the three paragraphs mentioned above shall be ventilated in the manner deemed appropriate by the Administration after consulting the opinion of the Higher Council for Urban Planning.

The height of the shaft above the ceiling of the first basement must range between one metre and two metres including the means of protection against rain, and must be no less than one and a half metres in the last floor exposed to the air.

(Refer to Drawing No. 46)

Building height and number of storeys - The independent building - Building above an existing building:

First - Building height and number of storeys:

1 - In the zones where the maximum height of the building and the number of its storeys are determined, the height of the building is measured starting from the level of a horizontal line rising one metre above the lowest point of the adopted ground level in contact with the facade of the building and up to the ceiling level of the highest part of the non-independent buildings.

2 - The pitched tiled roof structure, staircase and lift shafts, water tanks, and parapets erected above the last roof of the building to screen the staircase and lift shafts shall not be included in the calculation of the maximum height.

3 - Where there are several buildings within a single property that do not fulfil the conditions of independent buildings in accordance with the concept of Item Second of this Article, the maximum height specified for the building shall apply to all of these buildings from the level of a horizontal line rising one metre above the lowest point of the natural ground level or the adopted ground level after levelling in contact with the lowest facade of these buildings.

(Refer to Drawing No. 51)

Where the levels of a single building vary, or in non-independent buildings, the number of storeys is calculated starting from the lowest part of the building or buildings, to which is added a storey for every ceiling resulting in a clear height exceeding 5.75 m (five metres and seventy-five centimetres) starting from the floor of the last storey of the lowest part.

(Refer to Drawing No. 52)

Second - The independent building:

Where there are multiple buildings on a single property, any of these buildings shall be considered independent for the application of the envelope and the measurement of the height and number of storeys if the following conditions are met therein:

1 - That the horizontal distance separating the exposed basement storeys and what is above them is not less than twice the largest setback imposed from the boundaries of the neighbouring properties in accordance with the regulations of the zoning area to which the property is subject, with a minimum of four and a half metres.

(Refer to Drawing No. 53)

2 - That there be secured in this independent building the extensions and installations pertaining to the water, electricity, telephone, and sanitary networks and their installations, and all that this building requires to be fit for use independently from others.

3 - The interconnection of basement storeys beneath some or all of the independent buildings on a single property is permitted, provided that the conditions for basement storeys specified in Item 2 - a of the Twelfth Article of this Decree apply to them.

(Refer to Drawing No. 54)

In the event that there are backfilled basement storeys in an independent block, the horizontal distance separating these storeys from the exposed basement storeys and what is above them of the other blocks must not be less than four and a half metres.

(Refer to Drawing No. 55) (New Drawing 55 in accordance with Decree 617 /2007 for insertion)

4 - Where there are separate basement storeys in several buildings within a single property, these basement storeys may be connected to each other by means of passages (tunnels) whose width does not exceed the width of the passages necessary to secure the entry and exit of cars, in addition to the necessary turns and sidewalks, if any, in accordance with the minimum limits provided for in Item Second of the Sixteenth Article of this Decree.

It is also permissible, according to the conditions above, to connect the rear basement storeys to the road through the front ground floor connected to the road.

These passages (tunnels) shall be considered not to conflict with the special conditions that impose the restriction of the basement storeys to the horizontal projection of the building, if any.

Third - Building above an existing building

While complying with the remaining conditions imposed by the regulations to which the property is subject, the building requested to be added above an existing building may be exempted from compliance with the surface exploitation and the setbacks imposed from the neighbouring properties, provided:

1 - That the existing building is legal:

- Standing prior to the date of 13/9/1971 pursuant to a certificate from the competent departments.

- Its violating parts have been settled and the due fees have been paid.

- The demolition of its parts encroaching upon the setback imposed from the boundaries of the road or from the approved road alignment has been postponed.

- Holding a legal building permit or subdivided.

2 - That the building requested to be added, including balconies, is not erected above the parts of the building whose demolition is postponed or which have been settled, located within the setback imposed from the neighbouring properties or from the roads and public domain.

Exempted from the conditions above are pitched tiled roof structures that fulfil the conditions specified in Item 5 of the Twelfth Article of this Decree, with respect to the possibility that the pitched roof structure covers the entire roof of the last storey with the exception of the part located within the road or the alignment.

3 - That the building requested to be added does not impair the legality of the existing old building with respect to the envelopes and the field of view on the basis of which the existing building was licensed.

4 - That the existing building bears the requested addition without any strengthening or shoring within the imposed setback. The engineer signing the permit application shall be considered responsible for the safety and solidity of the existing building and the one intended to be added based on the results of laboratory tests, the necessary studies, and the complete documents registered with one of the two Orders of Engineers, provided that clear photographs showing the actual state of the standing building are attached to the application and coupled with the signature of both the responsible engineer and the head of the technical department concerned with examining the building permit file.

Special easements relating to public safety, public health, and architectural perspectives:

First - The special easements and provisions imposed upon the granting of a building permit may encompass all architectural, structural, and regulatory elements of the building and its surroundings, and the Administration shall have the right to require the owner to provide installations commensurate with the importance of the building, particularly with respect to compliance with the principles of environmental protection and the sustainability of its natural resources (water, air, land and living organisms) as defined by Law No. 444/2002 (Protection of the Environment).

Where the project includes leaving open spaces on the plot at ground level after grading, half the area of such open spaces must be allocated as gardens unless they are maintained in their natural state.

The open spaces left on the plot shall not include:

1 - The designed surface exploitation.

2 - Vehicle entry and exit passages.

3 - Vehicle parking spaces required by law.

Second - The special provisions referred to in Paragraph First above shall include all easements defined by the master plan studies in unzoned areas, particularly with respect to the heights, volumes, areas, and setbacks of buildings, by way of example and not limitation, and these provisions shall become binding upon the authority entrusted with granting the building permit immediately upon the issuance of the decision of the Higher Council for Urban Planning thereon and throughout the period of its discussion with the municipality concerned until the ratification of the regulatory decree in accordance with the rules, provided that this period does not exceed three years.
