In areas zoned by decrees, where the new master plan study for the area provides for a reduction in the maximum limits permitted under the previous ratified regulation or for additional conditions, the authority granting the permit shall be deemed bound to comply with the stricter conditions provided for in the new study prepared for the area, immediately upon its approval by the Higher Council for Urban Planning and throughout the period of its discussion with the municipality concerned until the ratification of the regulatory decree for the area in accordance with the rules, provided that this period does not exceed three years.

In the event that three years elapse from the issuance of the decision of the Higher Council for Urban Planning regarding the master plan study for the area without the ratification of the decree being completed in accordance with the rules, the study shall be re-submitted to the Higher Council for Urban Planning during the last month of the time limit referred to above, and the said Council shall review the study and propose amendments thereto in light of a detailed report setting out the reasons preventing the completion of the ratification of the decree.

Third - The Administration may impose upon the owner, as a condition for granting him an occupancy permit, the planting of trees within his plot.

Fourth - Securing public safety requirements:

a - Starting from the date of issuance of this Decree and until technical control offices are accredited in accordance with the rules set forth in Decree No. 14293 dated 11/3/2005, compliance with the following mechanism shall be required upon submitting a permit application for any building:

1 - Applications for a permit to build, or to modify or add a building to an existing building, or to modify the intended use of the building or a part thereof, even if the modification does not include an increase in areas, must include an undertaking from the engineers who designed the project (each according to his specialization) to comply with the specifications defined pursuant to the said Decree when preparing the execution drawings for the project.

2 - The execution drawings shall be submitted accompanied by all required studies and documents confirming the compliance of the design with the approved specifications for securing public safety upon submitting the application to obtain the order to commence execution, which has become a binding statutory provision within the Building Law.

3 - Upon submitting the application for the habitation permit, a certificate from the engineers who designed the project, signed by them and certified by one of the two Orders of Engineers, shall be attached, containing their assumption of liability and their confirmation that the execution of the building was carried out in accordance with the specifications defined by the said Decree.

b - Buildings intended for use by the public located in basement floors (cinemas, theatres, playhouses, nightclubs, and others...) and the garages pertaining thereto require obtaining the prior approval of the Directorate General of Civil Defense in the event that the buildings are not subject to mandatory technical control.

c - The accuracy of the prepared studies shall remain the responsibility of the engineers who drew up the studies (each according to his specialization), without the registration of such study with the Order of Engineers or with the competent technical departments entailing any liability with respect to the structural soundness of the building and its compliance with the regulations relating to public safety.

Fifth - Airport easements:

The building permit for all buildings shall be granted subject to compliance with all provisions defining the conditions for securing air navigation safety requirements and civil aviation easements.

Sixth - High-rise buildings whose height exceeds 50m (fifty meters)

Where the height of the building exceeds 50 meters from the lowest point of the ground of the plot in contact with any of its facades after grading, excluding the stair penthouse, water tanks, parapets, and technical installations, the building permit must be subject to the approval of the Higher Council for Urban Planning, provided that, in addition to the general and special conditions in force at the location of the plot, the following conditions are met:

1 - Minimum area and dimensions of the plot:

The area of the plot on which the high-rise building stands must not be less than four times the minimum area required for subdivision parcels, and must accommodate a rectangle whose dimensions are not less than twice the length and depth required for parcels resulting from subdivision in accordance with the regulations of the zone within which the plot is located, with a tolerance of 5% at most with respect to the area and dimensions defined above.

2 - Minimum facade width - Podium - Setbacks/Steps - Free open spaces:

The width of any facade of the high-rise building may not be less than eight meters, excluding balconies.

A high-rise building is permitted to be erected above a podium whose horizontal projection area exceeds the projection area of the high-rise building.

The project must include leaving open spaces on the plot at ground level after grading, and allocating half the area of the open spaces as gardens.

The open spaces left on the plot shall not include:

1 - The designed surface exploitation.

2 - Vehicle entry and exit passages.

3 - Vehicle parking spaces required by law.

4 - The projection of the escape staircase or staircases on the ground floor.

3 - Paragraph 3 was repealed pursuant to Decree in force No. 617 dated 8/8/2007, Official Gazette No. 50.

4 - Stairwells, elevator shafts, water tanks, technical installations, parapets, and walls erected above the roof of the top floor:

Stairwells, elevator shafts, water tanks, technical installations, solar collectors and the water tanks pertaining thereto, and ventilation, heating, and cooling machinery erected above the top floor may rise above the level of this roof up to a maximum limit of six meters.

Parapets and walls erected above the roof of the top floor to conceal the installations mentioned above may exceed the building envelope line by the height of these installations. It is also permitted to construct these parapets and walls at the most prominent point of the roof, including projections.

5 - Elevator - Staircase (stairs):

The decrees relating to the conditions for securing public safety requirements with respect to the specifications of staircases and elevators pertaining to high-rise buildings must be complied with.

6 - Exemption from certain imposed conditions:

It shall be for the Higher Council for Urban Planning to exempt certain projects from some of the conditions imposed in Items 2 and 3 above, and it may also impose additional conditions depending on the design and the importance of the project.

Seventh - Minimum width of building facades: The width of any of the facades of the building overlooking roads must not be less than five meters, excluding balconies.

(Refer to Drawings No. 47, 48, and 49)

In certain cases required by the architectural design of the building which conflict with the content of the paragraph above, the prior approval of the Director General of Urban Planning must be obtained.

Eighth - Cooling units (air conditioning):

It is prohibited to install air conditioning units visibly on the facade of the building. Where necessary, these units may be placed on balconies, verandas, and loggias adjacent to the facade wall, provided that they are treated in a technical manner in accordance with the drawing below, and air conditioning units may be placed below the ceiling level of the floor on balconies or within lightwells outside the areas designated for ventilation, provided that they are covered with a screen or a false ceiling.

(Refer to Drawing No. 50)

Structures permitted to be erected within the legally mandated setback First - Within the setback from the boundaries or from the alignment of roads:

1 - Within the mandated setback from the boundaries or from the alignment of the road, official buildings or embassies may be permitted to erect a guard building whose area does not exceed thirty square metres. The clear internal height of this building may be reduced down to 220 cm (two hundred and twenty centimetres). In the event of the existence of other buildings whose importance or intended use necessitates the erection of a guard building within the mandated setback from the boundaries or from the alignment of the road, they shall be submitted for the prior approval of the Directorate General of Urban Planning.

2 - An entrance to the building in the form of: * A slab with a width not exceeding four metres. (Refer to Drawing No. 91)

* An uncovered staircase with a width not exceeding three metres if the building is located below the level of the road. (Refer to Drawing No. 92)

It is required that the owner register a waiver on the real estate folio not to claim any compensation, indemnity or damages in return for the structures that are the subject of Paragraphs - 1 - and - 2 - above in the event of expropriation of the section affected by the mandated setback.

3 - The construction of boundary walls and retaining or breast walls, provided that no compensation shall be due therefor in the event of expropriation of the setback area for the widening of roads.

4 - The installation of advertising poles provided for in the decree regulating and licensing advertisements.

5 - The opening and the tunnel leading to electrical transformer station rooms, subject to compliance with the level of the adjacent road while taking into consideration the external architecture and the existing gardens when creating the tunnel and subject to not obstructing or disrupting the garage and the passages leading to it. It is prohibited to erect any other structures within this setback, such as staircases and ascending or descending ramps to the garage.

Second - Within the setback from the boundaries of neighbouring properties: Subject to the special regulations pertaining to the zones, permission may be granted:

1 - To erect basement floors in accordance with the conditions provided for in Paragraph 2 of Item "Second" of Article 12 of this Decree.

2 - To erect boundary walls in accordance with the provisions of Paragraph - a - of Item Third of the Second Article of this Decree, breast walls whatever their height may reach, and retaining walls whose height does not exceed two metres, and in the event of the existence of a breast wall with a height exceeding two metres within the boundaries of the setback from neighbouring properties, it is prohibited to raise the level of the natural ground adjacent to it.

3 - For the projection of decorative and beautification works, cornices, sunshades and flower boxes, and the protrusion of the pitched tile roof structure provided for in Item - Second of the Eighth Article of this Decree is also permitted.

Large Complexes

First - In addition to what is provided for in Article 16 of the Building Law No. 646 dated 11/12/2004, the permit application file for the construction of any large complex must include the following documents:

1 - A detailed report explaining the objective of the project and showing the architectural specifications by which it is characterised and the benefits that accrue to the area as a result of its execution (development, growth).

2 - A mass plan (Plan masse), preliminary plans (Plans preliminaires), explanatory sketches (Croquis), and a photomontage or photomontages (Photos montage) showing the project with its surroundings within a distance of at least three hundred metres from the boundaries of the plot or plots of the complex on all sides and showing the extent of its harmony with the nature and characteristics of the area surrounding it (Integration dans le site), including maintaining a ratio of not less than 25% of the land area of the plot as gardens.

3 - Topographical maps of contour lines (Courbes de niveau) or of spot levels (Plan cote).

4 - Maps determining the siting of the sections of the buildings, the intended use of each of them, their areas, their volumes, and the distribution of their connection with each other (roads, gardens at ground level with their area in proportion to the number of inhabitants), as well as public services, infrastructure networks in the project, and the organisation of pedestrian traffic and car parking.

5 - Plans and sections (Plans et coupes) of all sections of the complex building at a scale of not less than 1/200.

6 - Maps of the facades and the materials used therein at a scale of not less than 1/100.

7 - A volumetric model (Maquette) at a scale of not less than 1/1000.

8 - The bases adopted to ensure the safety of structures, a study of protection against fire hazards, and resistance to earthquakes in accordance with Paragraph - 1 - of Item Third of Article Ten of this Decree.

Second - All the documents referred to above shall be submitted for the approval of the Higher Council for Urban Planning, which may request the introduction of the necessary amendments to the project or request the attachment of explanatory documents. Any subsequent amendment prior to the building permit or during execution affecting the volumes and siting of the buildings of the complex and the building materials used in the facades must be coupled with the approval of the Higher Council for Urban Planning.

Third - Following the approval by the Higher Council for Urban Planning of the design pertaining to the large complex, the party concerned shall complete the preparation of the building permit files and documents in order to submit the application for this permit to the competent authorities in accordance with the rules.

Fourth - Special conditions

1 - The width of any facade of the buildings of the large complex exempted from height, envelope, and number of storeys may not be less than eight metres, excluding balconies, save in special cases where the design of the building is studied in an unconventional manner.

2 - Outside the scope of Governorate centres, the buildings of the large complex exempted from height, envelope, and number of storeys shall be required to be set back from the boundaries of the plot by a distance of not less than one fifth (1/5) of the height of these buildings.

3 - The building of large complexes shall be required to provide for and be equipped with standby electric generators whose capacity is commensurate with the importance of the project to operate the lifts, the necessary ventilation, and the lighting of vital facilities (corridors, stairwells, basements, emergency exits, etc., ...) in emergency cases.

4 - It shall be required to construct the private garage pertaining to the parking of cars required for large complexes in addition to an additional private garage for the complex to be registered within the common sections of the project accommodating one quarter of the required number of garage parking spaces. It shall be for the Higher Council for Urban Planning to exempt the design of the large complex from the above condition in the light of the nature of the plot and the design of the building. Car garages shall also be required to be equipped with electric signals that facilitate and secure traffic movement inside them, and to secure appropriate connection with the traffic inside them, and to secure appropriate connection with external traffic along with an impact study for traffic movement (Traffic Impact Study).

5- It shall be required to provide for and equip the buildings with the means and equipment necessary for firefighting.

6 - It shall be required to screen the view of laundry drying racks, service-related balconies, and mechanical equipment wherever they are located in the building, as well as the view of all structures erected above roofs (stairwell, lift room, water tanks, cooling towers, etc...) in an artistic and aesthetic manner.

7 - It shall be required to determine in advance the location of cooling units that may be resorted to in the future (in the event that the building is not equipped with central air conditioning), in an artistic manner that does not constitute a disfigurement of the facades and in accordance with the conditions of Item Sixth of Article Ten of this Decree.

8 - A common water tank must be secured for the project, the capacity of which shall be determined at one cubic metre for every one hundred square metres of built-up area, including the area of the basements, excluding the areas pertaining to garages.

9 - In the design of the large complex, it is preferable not to repeat a single design in terms of volumes and masses across all buildings of the complex.

10 - The buildings of large complexes exempted pursuant to the provisions of Article 16 of the Building Law shall not benefit from the provisions of Paragraph 2 - b - 1 of Item Second of Article 12 of this Decree.

Fifth - Residential complexes undertaken by public authorities shall be exempted from some of the provisions of this Article, following the approval of the Higher Council for Urban Planning.

Projection beyond the envelope:

First - Projections beyond the envelope line stipulated on the road side: Projections beyond the envelope line erected on the road side (the calculation of the road width includes the mandatory imposed setback and does not include the optional setback by the owner) are determined as follows:

A: Free unenclosed balconies:

A - 1 - On a road whose width is less than nine metres, any projection is prohibited.

A - 2 - On roads whose width is equal to or exceeds nine metres, a maximum projection of 1.05m. (one metre and five centimetres) is permitted.

B: Canopies on the ground floor:

The maximum projection for canopies on the ground floor is determined at one-eighth (1/8) of the prescribed width of the road including setbacks on both sides with a maximum limit of 3.00m. (three metres) from the setback boundaries, provided that the outer edge of the canopies remains set back 30 cm (thirty centimetres) from the edge of the pavement (kerb) if present, and the canopies on floors located at the level of any of the roads surrounding the property may be at the ceiling level or lower than it, while complying with what is imposed by the minimum clear height from the level of the pavement or the road axis, and these canopies are considered a common part upon the subdivision of the building, and their roof may also be used as flower beds.

C - Sunbreakers (Brise Soleil), cornices, flower beds, means of decoration and beautification, and thermal insulation and damp-proofing works:

Sunbreakers, cornices, flower beds, and means of decoration and beautification are permitted to project 60 cm (sixty centimetres) as a maximum beyond the envelope line erected on the road side and beyond the building facade (without balconies, verandas, and loggias). The projection of thermal insulation and damp-proofing works is permitted, provided that their height does not exceed fifty centimetres /50 cm/ above the roof of the top floor, beyond the envelope line erected on the road side by no more than the thickness of these works. In all cases provided for in the three items A, B, and C above, the height of the lower limit of the projections must not be less than:

1 - 3.00m. (three metres) from the pavement level.

2 - 3.20m. (three metres and twenty centimetres) from the road level in the absence of a pavement.

(See Drawing No. 32)

D - Advertisements: Subject to compliance with the legal and regulatory provisions relating to advertisements, particularly the provisions of Decree No. 8861 dated 25/7/1996 (Regulation and Licensing of Advertisements), the placement and projection of illuminated and non-illuminated advertisements and signboards on building facades may be permitted under the following conditions:

D- 1 - Affixed directly onto the body of the facades of shops, offices, and establishments located on the ground floor of the building, provided that the protrusion of the advertisement beyond the facade erected on the alignment, or the mandatory setback if present, does not exceed sixteen centimetres and does not obstruct the lighting and ventilation of the rooms. Furthermore, in the event that there is a base for the building consisting of a ground floor and at most two upper floors, it is permitted to place advertisements on the edge of the projections of the floors of this base. Provided that the protrusion of the advertisement beyond the facade erected on the alignment, or the mandatory setback if present, does not exceed sixteen centimetres.

D - 2 - Affixed directly or vertically onto the body of the building facades on the upper floors if the building is occupied in all its floors, with the exception of the ground floor and basements, by a single occupant, provided that:

- The total height of the advertisement or signboard does not exceed the height of the building facade.

- The protrusion of the advertisement or signboard beyond the building facade does not exceed the permitted amount in the projection of balconies.

D - 3 - Above the roof of buildings, provided that:

- They do not exceed the boundaries of the alignment and the setback therefrom.

- They do not rise more than four and a half metres above the envelope line and do not protrude more than 1.05 m beyond the body of the building.

E - Awnings of facades in front of which there are pavements: Awnings and their supports are permitted in front of facades in front of which there are pavements, under the following conditions:

E - 1 - That their most projecting parts are at a distance of 0.50m. (fifty centimetres) behind the vertical plane passing through the edge of the pavement, and in the case of trees planted on the pavement, at a distance of 0.50m. (fifty centimetres) from the trunk of the trees.

E - 2 - That the projection does not exceed 3.00m (three metres) from the facade wall erected on the alignment or from the mandatory setback if present, with a maximum limit of three metres from the body of the building.

E - 3 - That the height of these projections is not less than two and a half metres above the pavement level.

(See Drawing No. 33)

F - Stairwells, lift shafts, parapets, and pitched tile roofs: Stairwells, lift shafts, solar collectors and their associated water tanks, ventilation, heating and cooling machinery, parapets, and walls constructed above the roof of the top floor to conceal stairwells, lift shafts, water tanks, and technical installations may exceed the inclined envelope line up to a maximum of four and a half metres for buildings whose height exceeds 15m (fifteen metres).(See Drawing No. 34)

Pitched tile roofs may also exceed the vertical envelope line by 1.05m. (one metre and five centimetres) and the inclined envelope line by 2.50m. (two and a half metres).

(See Drawing No. 35)

Second - Projection beyond the envelope line on the open spaces side:

1 - Projection beyond the envelope line erected on the open spaces side is permitted for sunbreakers, flower beds, cornices, means of decoration and beautification, stairwells, lift shafts, solar collectors and their associated water tanks, ventilation, heating and cooling machinery, and parapets erected above the roof of the top floor to conceal the view of stairwells, lift shafts, water tanks, and technical installations, under the same conditions permitted for them with respect to projections beyond the envelope line erected on the road side. Notwithstanding any special provision, the projection of thermal insulation and damp-proofing works whose height does not exceed fifty centimetres /50 cm/ above the roof of the top floor is permitted beyond the envelope line erected on the open spaces side by no more than the thickness of these works.

2 - A pitched tile roof is permitted to project by: - 2.50m (two and a half metres) beyond the inclined envelope line. - Beyond the vertical envelope line by:

* 105 cm as a maximum if the building setback from the property boundaries, including balconies if any, is equal to or exceeds 4.50m (four and a half metres).

* 60 cm as a maximum if the building setback from the property boundaries ranges between 150 cm (one hundred and fifty centimetres) and 4.50m (four and a half metres).(See Drawing No. 36)

3 - The minimum clear height for cornices, means of decoration and beautification, and sunbreakers must not be less than 2.20m. (two metres and twenty centimetres) from the final ground level after grading.

Third - Exceptional projection:

By virtue of a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport after consulting the Higher Council for Urban Planning, projection beyond the envelope line may be permitted for certain parts of industrial buildings such as chimneys and silos, and certain parts of places of passage [worship] such as minarets in mosques or bell towers in churches when the nature of their structure and designation requires this projection, and provided there are no reasons preventing this projection, such as the safety of air navigation or otherwise.

On the Clear Height Below the Ceiling:

First - The minimum height below the ceiling shall be determined as follows:

1 - For rooms intended for habitation or for daytime or night-time occupancy, or for rooms allocated for special activities:

- 2.80 m. (two metres and eighty centimetres) for rooms with a horizontal ceiling.

- 2.40 m. (two metres and forty centimetres) as an average height for rooms with a non-horizontal ceiling.

- 2.20 m. (two metres and twenty centimetres) for the building caretaker's dwelling.

2 - For buildings and warehouses in basement floors and for the garage.

2.20 m. (two metres and twenty centimetres) below the ceiling and beams.

3 - For the stilt floor (Pilotis):

2.20 m. (two metres and twenty centimetres) as a minimum below the ceiling and beams, including the height of the building caretaker's dwelling constructed within it.

4 - For entrances of apartments and offices and for kitchens where mezzanines exist above them: 2.20 m. (two metres and twenty centimetres).

5 - For laundry rooms, refuse rooms, bathrooms, lavatories, pantries, corridors: 2.00 m. (two metres).

(Refer to Drawings No. 111 and 112)

6 - For the duplex (Duplex): 2.20 m (two metres and twenty centimetres) in the double-level section thereof.

A duplex means a floor consisting of two levels, both of which are included within the two exploitation ratios, and the total clear height of the duplex across both levels together and in the high section thereof shall not exceed five metres and seventy-five centimetres, provided that the area of the upper level does not exceed two-thirds of the area of the lower level, including the internal staircase connecting the two levels. The area of this secondary staircase shall only be counted once in calculating the general exploitation ratio.

Where rooms that legally require a view distance and ventilation are provided within either of the two levels, such rooms must overlook either the open air directly or through the high section of the duplex.

(Refer to Drawings No. 113 and 114)

7 - Constructions pertaining to marine sports (cabins) and winter sports (chalets):

- 2.20 m. (two metres and twenty centimetres) for bedrooms and sitting rooms with a horizontal ceiling.

- 1.90 m. (one metre and ninety centimetres) for bedrooms and sitting rooms with a sloping ceiling, provided that the average height is not less than 2.20 m. (two metres and twenty centimetres) and the slope is not less than ten percent.

It is required that the horizontal projection area of each dwelling unit of the chalet included in the calculation of the exploitation ratios does not exceed 120 m2 (one hundred and twenty square metres) and that the number of floors does not exceed two, excluding the basement floor and the top floor in the form of a pitched roof.

(Refer to Drawing No. 115)

The zones in which the construction of such chalets is permitted shall be determined by a decision of the Higher Council for Urban Planning.

Second - The maximum clear height below the ceiling shall be set at five metres and seventy-five centimetres, with the exception of buildings or parts of buildings which by their nature or according to their intended use require a height greater than that, provided that such exploitation is subject to the prior approval of the Higher Council for Urban Planning.

Clause Third added pursuant to Enforceable Decree 617 dated 8/8/2007 Official Gazette 50

Third - The executed height shall be calculated between the underside of the ceiling and the surface of the tiling, and decoration and ornamental works shall not be included in the calculation of the height.

Rationality of Plans:

The Technical Head of the Administration shall rule on the rationality of the plans and on unusual situations, after they are referred to him by a reasoned report from the competent unit.

a - The holder of a permit granted prior to the issuance of Law No. 646 dated 11/12/2004 shall have the right to choose between executing it in accordance with the laws in force on the date of obtaining the permit, or amending it in accordance with the provisions of Law No. 646 dated 11/12/2004 and this Implementing Decree.

b - Subject to Clause - a - above, Decree No. 2791 dated 15/10/1992 (Application of the Provisions of the Building Law) and Decree No. 9663 dated 30/12/96 (Application of the Provisions of Law No. 523 dated 6/6/96) are hereby repealed, and all texts that conflict with the provisions of this Decree are likewise repealed.

Regarding the amendment of the drawings appearing in the articles, refer to Decree 617 dated 8/8/2007 in the Official Gazette Issue 50 dated 178/2007
This Decree shall be published and notified wherever required.
