1 - Movable and immovable property that meets the following criteria shall be considered cultural property, whoever may own or possess it:

a - That it belongs to one of the categories of objects provided for in Article Two of this Law.

b - That it meets one of the following conditions, whether it is located in Lebanon or outside its territory:

(1) That it was made in Lebanon regardless of the nationality of the person who made it and the historical period to which its making dates back.

(2) That it was found within Lebanese territory or in its subsoil or in Lebanese territorial waters regardless of the method or circumstances of its finding and regardless of the historical period to which it dates back.

(3) That it was made or found outside Lebanon and is located on Lebanese territory pursuant to a non-temporary voluntary exchange or a gift or a purchase transaction and the like, and that all of this took place legally with the approval of the competent authorities in the country of origin of such property.

c - That its preservation constitutes a Lebanese public interest.

2 - Property that belongs to one of the categories of objects provided for in Article Two of this Law and that was made or found outside Lebanon and is legally located on Lebanese territory while it is owned in a legally established manner by a non-Lebanese natural person or a non-Lebanese legal person shall not be included among cultural property.

3 - Property that belongs to one of the categories of objects provided for in Article Two below and that was made or found outside Lebanon and is considered by one of the States with which Lebanon maintains relations to be among its classified cultural property while it is illegally present on Lebanese territory shall be subject to the provisions of Chapter Three of this Law.

Cultural property includes objects that have previously been registered, classified, or recognized, or regarding which this has not yet been done, and which belong, by way of example and not limitation, to the following categories:

a - Immovable property, namely archaeological, historical, or scientific places and sites, and structures, landmarks, monuments, and buildings or parts of buildings of heritage, historical, scientific, aesthetic, architectural, or symbolic value, whether religious or secular, and groups of traditional buildings and historical quarters standing in cities or in the countryside, and natural sites prepared or used by man, and remains of past civilizations of ethnological value, and other such items that have the status of an immovable ancient antiquity within the meaning of the Law of Antiquities and its amendments. All of this applies to ruins standing on the surface of the ground, and to archaeological or historical remains discovered in the subsoil or under territorial waters and not yet discovered, and also applies to a defined geographical extent constituting the protection perimeter of such property.

This is not limited to antiquities and similar objects as defined in the laws and regulations in force relating thereto, in particular the special Law on Antiquities and its amendments.

b - Movable property that is an expression of human creativity or a witness to the evolution of nature, and that has archaeological, historical, artistic, scientific, or technical value or importance, whether religious or secular, for example:

(1) The results of archaeological prospecting and excavation works, both terrestrial and underwater, and in general every movable ancient antiquity within the meaning of the Law of Antiquities and its amendments.

(2) Archaeological and heritage objects of all kinds, such as pottery and metal tools and vessels, inscriptions, coins, seals, jewelry, weapons, and funerary remains.

(3) Objects that formed part of archaeological sites or of structures and monuments that are historical or of heritage or of artistic or architectural value, and that are no longer organically connected to those sites, structures, and monuments.

(4) Objects of scientific importance from an anthropological or ethnological standpoint.

(5) Property relating to history, including the history of science and technology and military and social history, and to the life of peoples and the life of national leaders, thinkers, scientists, and artists, and to important events through which the country has passed.

(6) Property of artistic importance, such as:

- Pictures, paintings, and drawings made entirely by hand, whatever the materials used in making them or the support on which they were executed.

- Works of engraving and prints (estampes), photographs, advertising posters, and the like.

- Works of sculpture, whatever the materials used in making them.

- Artistic assemblages and montages, whatever the materials from which they were made.

- Unique specimens of written or recorded musical compositions.

- Cinematographic films and all other tapes recorded with sound or image, both together.

- Unique specimens of products of traditional arts and crafts made of materials such as glass, ceramics, metals, wood, leather, fabric, and others.

(7) Items of importance to collections of coins, medals, postage and fiscal stamps, and the like.

(8) Items of importance of clothing, furniture, tapestries, rugs, carpets, and musical instruments.

(9) Manuscripts, volumes, handwritten codices, printed books, and all other kinds of publications of special importance from the historical, artistic, scientific, literary, or other standpoints.

(10) Archival documents, including written texts, maps, photographs, cinematographic films, sound recordings, multimedia recordings, and computerized documents, and this is not limited to national archival documents as defined in the laws and regulations in force relating thereto.

(11) Rare geological, botanical, and zoological items, specimens, and collections, or those that express the evolution of the physical environment.

c - Structures and buildings primarily dedicated to exhibiting or preserving movable cultural property as defined in this Article, such as museums, libraries, repositories of artifacts and archives, and the like.

d - All other objects provided for by the decrees and regulations adopted in implementation of this Law.

1 - Cultural property the management of which devolves wholly or partially upon other ministries shall be determined by decrees taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Culture and after consulting the opinion of a specialized committee and the ministers concerned, in particular the Presidency of the Council of Ministers with respect to Paragraph (10) of Item (b) of Article (2) above relating to archival documents, the Ministers of Tourism and of Environment with respect to Paragraph (11) of Item (b) of Article (2) above relating to geological and other items, specimens, and collections, and the Ministers of Tourism and of Interior and Municipalities with respect to Item (a) of Article (2) above relating to immovable cultural property.

2 - As for the immovable cultural property provided for in Item (a) of Article (2) above and the movable property provided for in Paragraphs (1), (2), and (3) of Item (b) of the same Article, their management shall devolve exclusively upon the Ministry of Culture. The Ministry may conclude agreements with municipalities, public institutions, or non-profit associations for the management of such property, provided that such agreements are ratified pursuant to decisions issued by the Council of Ministers.

In addition to the General Inventory List of Antiquities, a List of Recognised Cultural Property and a List of Classified Cultural Property shall be established in the Ministry, each of which shall be subject to the provisions of this Law, and the criteria for inclusion on each of them and the obligations resulting therefrom shall be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Culture.

1 - The competent administrations in the Ministry shall inventory all cultural property that may be included on either of the two lists provided for in the preceding Article.

2 - The Minister may, pursuant to this Law and to the decrees and regulations issued in implementation thereof, include any movable or immovable property subject to his authority the preservation of which constitutes a public interest on the List of Recognised Cultural Property or the List of Classified Cultural Property, upon the proposal of the Director General of Cultural Affairs or the Director General of Antiquities, each within the scope of his competences, and after the approval of the competent committee provided for in Clause (3) below, unless such property is registered on the General Inventory List of Antiquities.

3 - The Minister of Culture shall form a committee of specialists to give an opinion whenever the provisions of this Law so provide.

4 - The registration of cultural property on the General Inventory List of Antiquities shall remain based on the special legal and regulatory provisions in this regard, taking into account the provisions of this Law.

1 - A recognised or classified cultural property shall remain included on the list concerned as long as no decision has been taken to strike it off therefrom or to transfer it from one list to another or to transfer it to the General Inventory List of Antiquities.

2 - Striking off or transfer shall take place in the same manner in which the inclusion took place.

The Ministry shall permanently keep the two Lists of Recognised and Classified Cultural Property mentioned above, provided that each list shall contain at least the following:

The name of the property, its type, a sufficient description thereof to identify it and distinguish it from similar property, specification of its owner and the party entrusted therewith, the parties to which it has passed since its inclusion on either of the two lists, the date of its inclusion on each of the two lists or of its striking off from each of them.

The Minister shall notify the owner of the cultural property and the party in whose possession the property is held of the inclusion decision, and where the property is immovable he shall also notify the competent Real Estate Registry to place an annotation to that effect on the real estate folio.

Cultural property belonging to public administrations and public institutions shall be registered in the name of the Ministry of Culture, which shall be the original custodian thereof, except in the cases determined by the decrees referred to in Article (3) of this Law.

The Minister may, upon the proposal of the competent Director General based on the recommendation of the competent committee, entrust any of the cultural property registered in the name of the Ministry or entrusted to the Ministry to another party, in particular the public institutions subject to its tutelage, to act as custodian of the property concerned and use it for the purposes for which they were established and within the framework of the missions legally assigned to them.

1 - The owner of any recognised or classified cultural property and the party entrusted therewith or the party in whose possession the property is held shall maintain such property in good condition, under penalty of being subject to the measures, penalties and fines referred to in Article (20) of this Law.

2 - The competent administration may at any time inspect any classified cultural property to verify that it is being maintained in good condition pursuant to the regulations in force, and it shall have the right to submit to the Minister any recommendations capable of ensuring the maintenance of the property in the condition in which it must be and to propose any other measures, including the measures, penalties and fines provided for in Article (2) of this Law.

1 - No recognised or classified cultural property may be transferred outside Lebanon except by a special reasoned permit granted by the Minister.

2 - No recognised or classified cultural property may be restored, modified, partially or totally destroyed, assigned, have its ownership transferred, or have the party entrusted therewith changed, and where the cultural property is a building, none of its features or its intended use may be changed, nor may it be totally or partially moved from its place, nor may any part thereof be used for additions thereto, except by a special permit granted by the Minister.

3 - Ownership of any classified cultural property or custody thereof may not be transferred except by a decree taken upon the proposal of the Minister if the party to which ownership or custody is intended to be transferred belongs to one of the following categories:

A - The government of a State other than Lebanon or one of the ministries of such government or one of its institutions.

B - A natural person who does not enjoy Lebanese nationality.

C - A legal person whose principal office is not in Lebanon.

4 - Every application submitted to the Ministry in application of Clauses (1), (2) and (3) of this Article shall state in detail the cultural property concerned, its estimated value, the requested change in its status whatever such change may be, and the date concerned by the change.

5 - The Minister shall decide on the application after seeking a written opinion submitted by the competent Director General and the competent committee within a period of sixty days starting from the date of registration of the application in the Ministry, and the Minister may, if he accepts the application, lay down the conditions he deems appropriate to permit the requested change.

6 - The application shall be deemed accepted in the event that no reply thereto is given within the period provided for in the preceding Clause, except in the cases not permitted by this Law and the decrees and regulations issued in implementation thereof, unless the administration takes a reasoned decision extending the period for a maximum duration of thirty days.

7 - The provisions of the two preceding Clauses shall not apply to the cases provided for in Clause (3) above.

8 - The applicant must in all cases comply with the instructions of the Minister and with the conditions laid down by him, and must also inform him of the occurrence of any change affecting any cultural property within thirty days from the date of occurrence of such change, and no amendment shall be made to the real estate folio except upon a request from the Minister.

1 - The Ministry, in the person of the Minister, shall have the right to exercise over the property the right of pre-emption of ownership if the application provided for in the preceding Article includes a change in the owner of the cultural property or the transfer of the property outside Lebanese territory, after seeking a written opinion submitted by the competent Director General and the competent committee, and in such case it shall decide to pay the price to the original owner.

2 - It shall be for the Minister, if the application provided for in the preceding Article includes a change in the party entrusted with the cultural property, to authorise the requested change, and he may in such case lay down the conditions he deems appropriate in order to preserve the property and use it in the public interest, after seeking a written opinion submitted by the competent Director General and the competent committee.

The Minister may, after seeking a written opinion submitted by the competent Director General and the competent Committee, decide as follows:

(a) - The acquisition by the Ministry, by way of purchase, of any classified or recognized cultural property.

(b) - The expropriation of any immovable cultural property in accordance with the legal provisions in force.

(c) - The exercise of the right of pre-emption over the ownership provided for in paragraph (1) of the preceding Article.

(d) - The acquisition by way of purchase or expropriation of any immovable property the preservation of which is necessary for the protection of a cultural property classified pursuant to paragraph (a) of Article (2) above, or for the proper exploitation or use of such property.

(e) - Special measures for the management of cultural property registered in the name of the Ministry and in its custody, by entrusting the competent administrations in the ministries with doing so, or entrusting the management of all or some of such property to natural or legal persons, and in particular to the public institutions concerned, on the basis of the conditions which he determines.

(f) - Special measures for the preservation of cultural property registered in the name of the Ministry and in its custody, and its use for the public interest, including storing, maintaining, restoring, rehabilitating, transferring it from its original place, modifying it, and displaying it in museums, exhibitions and the like, and making it accessible to citizens and tourists by all available means.

(g) - Contributing to the preservation of classified and recognized cultural property not owned by the Ministry and promoting its use for the public interest, including contributing to works conducive to the objectives envisaged in paragraph (f) of this Article, and determining the rights that accrue to the Ministry in return for such contribution.

(h) - Taking any legal or judicial measure to compel the owner of the classified cultural property or the entity entrusted therewith to carry out the works required to preserve the property in good condition.

(i) - Taking any legal or judicial measure to claim, in the name of the owner of the cultural property and for his account and under his responsibility, the recovery of any cultural property that has been lost, stolen, or unlawfully assigned or sold. In such case, he may exercise the right of pre-emption over the ownership provided for in the first paragraph of Article (13) of this Law.

(j) - Concluding any agreements with natural or legal persons and with municipalities and other concerned bodies for the purpose of implementing the provisions of this Law.

(k) - Proposing such agreements as he deems appropriate with the governments of other States and concerned international organizations for the purpose of implementing the provisions of this Law.

The Minister may, by a decision issued by him, temporarily requisition or confiscate any cultural property that is exposed to any of the dangers entailed against the safeguards secured by this Law, including the likelihood of the property being transferred outside Lebanese territory, or of its features or the purpose of its use being altered without prior authorization, or the exposure of the property to neglect or to the possibility of total or partial damage; and in the event of confiscation, he may determine the compensation arising from such confiscation based on a written opinion submitted by the competent Director General and the competent Committee.

Any immovable cultural property entered on the list of classified cultural property and not used for commercial purposes may be exempted from the built property tax by decrees adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Culture after seeking a written opinion submitted by the competent Director General and the competent Committee.
It is prohibited to import any non-Lebanese cultural property classified in another State with which Lebanon maintains relations without the approval of the government of the State of classification.

Appropriate measures for seizing cultural property classified by other States and imported into Lebanon without the approval of the State of classification, and for returning such property to its owners, shall be determined by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers, provided that the following matters are taken into consideration:

(a) - That such measures are based on the principle of reciprocity.

(b) - That the requesting State pays fair compensation to the bona fide purchaser or to the owner with a valid title.

(c) - That the requesting State furnishes, at its own expense, the documents and other necessary evidence proving the legitimacy of its request for seizure and return.

(d) - That the requesting State bears all expenses incurred from the return, shipping, insurance, and delivery of the cultural property.

1 - Any endowment (waqf) or gift, and any total or partial assignment in any form whatsoever, of any classified or recognized cultural property carried out in violation of the provisions of this Law or the provisions of the decrees issued in implementation thereof shall be deemed null and void.

2 - The competent courts shall rule on such nullity upon the request of the Minister without regard to the prescription periods provided for in any other laws in force.

Every person who violates the obligations provided for in the provisions of this Law or in the regulatory texts issued in implementation thereof shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to three years and by a fine from one million to one hundred million Lebanese pounds, or by either of the two penalties.

The penalty shall be doubled in the event of recidivism.

The competent courts shall hear as a matter of urgency all lawsuits and recourses brought before them by the Minister or by any interested party on the basis of the provisions of this Law and the decrees issued in implementation thereof.

The provisions of the Law promulgated by Decision No. 166/L.R. dated 7 November 1933, entitled the "Regulations on Antiquities", and its amendments, shall remain in force, taking into consideration the provisions of this Law.
Where necessary, the details of implementation of the provisions of this Law shall be determined by decrees adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Culture.
Subject to the provisions of Article 22 above, all provisions contrary to the provisions of this Law or inconsistent with its content are hereby repealed.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Documents required upon the submission of an application for the registration of imported pharmaceutical preparations.

The following documents shall be attached to the application for the registration of imported pharmaceutical preparations, taking into account the special cases mentioned in Articles 11 and 12 of this Decree.

First: Documents relating to the entities concerned with the imported medicinal product, if not previously submitted to the Ministry of Public Health (the form in Annex No. 2 for non-manufacturing entities and the form in Annex No. 3 for manufacturing entities).

1) The profile file of the "Responsible Entity" and a letter issued by it or by the "Parent Company" clarifying the relationship between the entities concerned with the preparation intended to be registered and the role of each of them.

2) The profile file of the Manufacturer of the Pharmaceutical/dosage Form, to which we attach the Good Manufacturing Practice certificate of the manufacturer GMP.

3) The profile file of the manufacturer of the commercial form or the entity responsible for batch release

if different from the entity mentioned in item 2.

The Good Manufacturing Practice certificate of the manufacturer GMP shall be attached.

4) The profile file of the product licence holder/marketing authorisation holder.

If different from the three entities mentioned in items 1, 2, 3.

5) A profile file of all the manufacturers involved in the manufacturing process and not mentioned in items 2 and 3, if any. To each profile file shall be attached the Good Manufacturing Practice certificate pertaining to the concerned manufacturer GMP.

6) A certificate specifying the source of the raw materials and the Good Manufacturing Practice certificate pertaining to the manufacturer of the raw materials GMP.

In the event that the Good Manufacturing Practice certificate GMP is not adopted by one of the countries, the registration applicant must prove that and submit the alternative document to ensure quality.

Second: Documents relating to the medicinal product:

1 - A document identifying the pharmaceutical preparation, provided that it is one of the following two documents:

- Either a "Certificate of a Pharmaceutical Product" COO or CMP.

- Or a "Free Sale Certificate" FSC.

3 - A Technical File for the preparation (Annex No. 6).

4 - Samples and certificate of analysis:

2 original samples of the preparation requested to be registered attached with a Certificate Of Analysis for the submitted samples issued by an analytical laboratory accredited by the manufacturer of the pharmaceutical form or the manufacturer of the commercial form or the entity responsible for batch release (Final Release/Batch Release).

In the event that physical samples according to the required local conditions are not ready, they shall be replaced by Mock ups, provided that the company undertakes to submit the samples according to the applicable conditions before commencing importation.

Third: Documents relating to pricing:

To the application for the registration of imported pharmaceutical preparations shall be attached the documents relating to the pricing of imported medicinal products as determined by the pricing decisions issued by the Minister of Public Health and in force on the date of the registration application.

Documents required upon the submission of an application for the registration of locally manufactured and/or packaged pharmaceutical preparations and those locally manufactured and/or packaged under licence.

To the application for the registration of locally manufactured and/or packaged pharmaceutical preparations and those locally manufactured and/or packaged under licence, the following documents shall be attached, taking into account the special cases mentioned in Articles 11 and 13 of this Decree:

1 - The document pertaining to the factory: the factory profile file Plant profile (the form in Annex No. 3) certified by the Pharmacy Department at the Ministry of Public Health, if this file has not been previously submitted to the Ministry of Public Health.

2 - A Technical File for the locally manufactured preparation (Annex No. 7).

3 - Samples and certificate of analysis:

2 original sale samples of the preparation requested to be registered attached with a Certificate Analysis for the submitted samples issued by the analytical laboratory of the local factory. Non-final samples of the preparation requested to be registered may also be submitted, provided that the local factory undertakes to submit the final samples of the preparation after registration.

4 - Documents relating to the pricing of locally manufactured medicinal products as determined by the pricing decisions issued by the Minister of Public Health and in force on the date of the registration application.

Special cases common to imported preparations and locally manufactured and/or packaged preparations and those locally manufactured and/or packaged under licence:

1 - If the preparation requested to be registered is composed of more than one part, each having a different batch number and expiry date, the applicant must submit a certificate from the "Responsible Entity" or the "Parent Company" clarifying that. In this case, a Combined Batch Number or a separate batch number shall be accepted for the preparation, and the earliest expiry date of the parts shall be adopted as the expiry date of the preparation.

2 - The Technical Committee may, in special exceptional cases not provided for in this Decree, take into account the recommendations of the World Health Organization.

Special cases for imported preparations relating to a difference in the trade name and/or pack size:

1 - If the trade name of the preparation requested to be registered differs from its trade name in one of the "countries of sale" provided for in Article 5 of this Decree, both names must be mentioned in the "Free Sale Certificate" or the "Certificate of a Pharmaceutical Product", or a certificate issued by the "Responsible Entity" or the "Parent Company" and certified by the competent authorities in the concerned "country of sale" stating that the two mentioned names pertain to the same preparation must be submitted.

2 - If the pack of the preparation requested to be registered differs in size from the pack sold in one of the "countries of sale" mandated in Article 5 of this Decree, or in one of the "countries of comparison" or "one of the neighbouring countries", the comparison of the prices mentioned in Decision 306/1 and its amendments shall be carried out according to size and proportionally, i.e. au Pro-Rata.

The difference in the cost of the pack cover Packaging shall be taken into consideration, provided that the mechanism for calculating this cost is determined pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Public Health based on the proposal of the Pricing Committee.

Special cases relating to preparations manufactured and/or packaged locally and those manufactured and/or packaged locally under licence:

1 - Where the preparation sought to be registered by the parent manufacturing company in Lebanon is manufactured by another factory in Lebanon mentioned among the factories listed in the profile of the parent manufacturing company, the applicant shall submit, in addition to the documents required for registering the preparation by the parent manufacturing company in Lebanon, a Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) certificate and a Plant Profile (Annex No. 3 form) for that factory, issued by the Ministry of Public Health, if these two documents have not previously been submitted to the Ministry of Public Health.

2 - Where the preparation sought to be registered is produced under licence by a factory, the following documents shall be added to the documents set forth in Article Eleven:

- A profile of the licensing factory, Plant Profile (Annex No. 3 form), duly certified, if this profile has not previously been submitted to the Ministry of Public Health.

- A certificate from the licensing factory proving its ownership of the preparation.

- A letter issued by the licensing factory confirming that it has granted that licence to the local factory.

3 - Where the preparation sought to be registered is produced under licence by a non-manufacturing company, the following documents shall be added to the documents set forth in Article Eleven:

- A profile of the licensing company, Licensor Profile (Annex No. 2 form).

- A certificate from the licensing company proving its ownership of the preparation.

- A letter issued by the licensing company confirming that it has granted that licence to the local factory.

4 - A Lebanese factory may import proprietary, biological, or generic chemical pharmaceutical preparations packaged in bulk, Bulk, for the purpose of completing their manufacture and/or repackaging them, for retail sale under the generic name or under a proprietary name of the Lebanese factory. Such preparations must be accompanied upon importation by a certificate of analysis, and the Lebanese factory must monitor the quality of such preparations. In this case,

- The name of the local factory, the name of the preparation, the batch number and date, and the expiry date shall be stated on the final packaging of the preparation.

- A Plant profile of the factory producing the preparation packaged in bulk, Bulk, shall be added to the documents set forth in Article Eleven, provided that the local factory undertakes, in the event of a change of the producing factory, to notify the Ministry of Public Health of such change and to submit the profile of the new producing factory.

5 - A Lebanese factory may import proprietary, biological, or generic chemical preparations in their primary packaging, primary packaging, for the purpose of repackaging them and/or completing their packaging locally, for retail sale under the generic name or under a proprietary name of the Lebanese factory. The Lebanese factory must monitor the quality of such preparations, and it shall also be required to:

- Submit a certificate of analysis upon the importation of such preparations.

- State on the final packaging of the preparation the name of the local factory, the name of the preparation, the batch number and date, and the expiry date.

- Add to the documents set forth in Article Eleven a profile of the factory producing the preparation in its primary packaging, primary packaging, provided that the local factory undertakes, in the event of a change of the producing factory, to notify the Ministry of Public Health of such change and to submit the profile of the new producing factory.

6 - A Lebanese factory may contract with foreign pharmaceutical companies holding a product licence/holding a marketing authorisation to execute contracts for the manufacture and/or packaging of pharmaceutical preparations, Contract Manufacturing, for the purpose of export only and not for local distribution, in accordance with the regulations in force in their country. In such case, these preparations shall be registered with the Ministry of Public Health in a special register for "Preparations Manufactured and/or Packaged Locally for Export" in accordance with the principles adopted in Article Eleven of this Decree, with the exception of Paragraph Four relating to pricing documents, and the following special conditions shall apply thereto:

- The local factory shall undertake in writing upon submitting the application not to market these preparations in Lebanon.

- The local factory shall submit a document confirming that the foreign company is the holder of the product licence/holder of the marketing authorisation and that it bears responsibility for the preparation.

- The name of the foreign company and its country shall be stated on the outer and inner packaging, and the name of the Lebanese factory and the country of manufacture shall be stated on the internal package leaflet.

7 - A Lebanese factory shall have the right to import "raw materials" within the meaning defined for such materials in Annex No. 1, in all their forms, under all circumstances, and of any origin whatsoever.

First category variations (Type 1 variations) to registered preparations.

In the event that any variation occurs to registered preparations from among the variations mentioned in Annex No. 8 for imported preparations and Annex No. 9 for locally manufactured preparations, it shall suffice for the concerned party to submit to the Pharmacy Department at the Ministry of Public Health a notice of notification and acknowledgment accompanied by the documents specified in each of the cases mentioned in the same Annex, provided that the concerned party is notified of the acknowledgment of receipt of the notice of the variation within a period of three months from the date of submitting the application.

If the concerned party is not notified of the acknowledgment of receipt of the notice of the variation within this period, he shall be entitled to import the preparations that are the subject of the application.

Second category variations (Type II variations) to registered preparations.

In the event that any variation occurs to imported registered preparations from among the variations mentioned in Annex No. 10 for imported preparations and Annex No. 11 for locally manufactured preparations, they shall be re-registered after submission of the documents specified in all the cases mentioned in the same Annex, provided that the documents relating to the preparations that have undergone the same variation are received in a single batch and are presented to the Technical Committee in a single session.

Importation of a medicinal product from a factory not mentioned in the Certificate of a Pharmaceutical Product.

The provisions of Decision No. 539/1 dated 25/8/1998 and the provisions of Decision No. 96/1 dated 13/2/2002 shall be repealed six months after the publication of this Decree in the Official Gazette, and their provisions shall thereupon be replaced by the following provisions:

After the registration and marketing of the medicinal product for a period of not less than one full year, the pharmaceutical establishment that submitted the registration application, or any other pharmaceutical establishment, shall have the right to import the medicinal product from a factory not mentioned in the Certificate of a Pharmaceutical Product, provided that:

- The "Responsible Entity" or the "Parent Company" does not change.

- This takes place after the approval of the Technical Committee in accordance with the mechanism specified in Articles Fourteen (First category variations) and Fifteen (Second category variations) of this Decree.

- The importation takes place with the approval of the "Responsible Entity" or the "Parent Company",

- And all the conditions specified in this Decree and the pricing conditions specified in the pricing decisions in force are applied thereto.

The "Responsible Party", the "Parent Company" and the agent pharmaceutical establishment shall bear responsibility for the conformity of all batches of the medicinal product placed on the market through them with the technical data of the registration file, particularly those relating to safety.

If any defect is found in any batch, the "Responsible Party" or the "Parent Company" shall, through the agent pharmaceutical establishment, withdraw the medicinal product concerned and imported through it from the markets immediately, refund its price to the wholesale drugstores and pharmacies, and re-export or destroy it in conformity with health and environmental conditions, at its own expense.

The agent pharmaceutical establishment shall also bear responsibility for the proper implementation of this Article with respect to the medicinal products imported through it and for notifying the Ministry of Public Health of any defect in implementation, whether intentional or unintentional.

The registration of preparations shall be cancelled by a decision of the Minister of Public Health upon the recommendation of the Technical Committee in each of the following cases:

1 - Where it appears to the Technical Committee that the preparation has a toxicity that was not known, or where data have become available regarding its inefficacy on the basis of reports from a reliable source such as the World Health Organization.

2 - Where similar measures have been taken by the World Health Organization.

3 - Where the registration took place on the basis of incorrect information or documents.

4 - Where the importer fails to comply with the decisions of the Technical Committee.
The eleven annexes attached to this Decree shall be deemed an integral part hereof.

- All regulatory provisions contrary to this Decree or inconsistent with its content are hereby repealed,

- in particular the provisions of Decision No. 233/1 dated 9/3/1993.

- and the provisions of Decision No. 212/1 dated 5/4/2004.
This Decree shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette, subject to the provisions of Article 16 hereof.

Principals of public schools who assume management duties in accordance with the conditions set forth in the Third Article of this Law shall be granted a management allowance of 15% (fifteen percent) of their salary as of the date of issuance of this Law.

For the purpose of applying the provisions of this Law, the expression "public schools" shall mean:

1 - Kindergartens.

2 - Primary schools.

3 - Intermediate schools.

4 - Secondary schools.

5 - Male and female teacher training colleges.

6 - Vocational and technical schools and institutes.

7 - School complexes.

A person appointed as principal of a public school must meet the following conditions:

First: To be:

a) An employee of the teaching cadres.

b) A holder of a teaching or university degree, or a graduate of male and female teacher training colleges who has practised teaching for a period of at least five years after entering the cadre, or a person who has practised for a period of at least ten years after entering the cadre.

c) Not sentenced during the last five years to any of the second-degree penalties provided for in the Civil Servants Regulations, or to the last two penalties together of the first-degree penalties at their maximum limit, or twice to either of them at its maximum limit.

d) Proficient in the Arabic language and having a good command of one of the two foreign languages, French or English.

Second: To submit his candidacy to assume management within the time limit set for accepting candidacy applications.

Third: To successfully pass an aptitude test the conditions and procedures of which shall be determined by a decision of the Minister.

Fourth: To successfully pass, prior to assuming management duties, a preparatory course in educational administration organised by the Faculty of Pedagogy at the Lebanese University.

Or to be among those who have attended special training courses dealing with administrative and educational matters organised by the Ministry of Education and Higher Education, provided that their duration fell below two months and provided that regulations for the courses to be held in the future are established by a decree issued in implementation of the provisions of this Law.

- The principal shall be appointed by a decision issued by the Minister of Education and Higher Education upon the proposal of the competent Director General, and upon the proposal of the President of the Center for Educational Research and Development in respect of principals of male and female teacher training colleges.

- The candidate who has successfully passed the aptitude test provided for in Clause Third of the Third Article of this Law, and who is selected by the Minister of Education and Higher Education upon the proposal of the competent Director General in respect of general pre-university education and public vocational and technical education, and upon the proposal of the President of the Center for Educational Research and Development in respect of male and female teacher training colleges, shall be attached to the Faculty of Pedagogy at the Lebanese University to attend a preparatory course in educational administration, if he is not a holder of a certificate of competency (Certificat d'Aptitude), Master's degree, or diploma in educational administration awarded by the said Faculty, or equivalent degrees awarded by private universities, and is not among those who attended the special training courses provided for in Clause Fourth of the aforementioned Article (the Third Article), and shall be assigned by virtue of the same decision the management duties for which he stood as a candidate, on a temporary basis until he fulfils the condition of passing the preparatory course to which he was attached at the Faculty of Pedagogy in order to attend.

- In the case set out in the paragraph above, the candidate shall be entitled to a temporary management allowance equal to two-thirds of the allowance provided for in the First Article of this Law, namely 10% of the salary of the person concerned, as of the commencement of his exercise of management duties on a temporary basis.

- The failure of the candidate to join the preparatory course within one month from its commencement, for whatever reason, shall be deemed a forfeiture of his right to attend it, and shall be tantamount to a final dismissal from the management duties temporarily assigned to him.

School principals shall be subject to a performance evaluation system every three years.

Every principal whose performance evaluation reports prove that his performance was average or below during a single academic year shall be relieved of management duties.

Members of the teaching staff shall benefit from the management allowance provided for in the First Article of this Law in the following cases:

- Those who were performing management duties prior to the issuance of Law No. 777 dated 11/11/2006 and continued to perform their duties after its entry into force, as of the date of 11/11/2006, even if their assignment did not fulfil the applicable procedures prior to 1/7/2001, the date of entry into force of Law No. 320 dated 20/04/2001.

- Those originally assigned to management duties in accordance with the procedures as of 1/7/2001, the date of entry into force of the provisions of Law 320 dated 20/04/2001, and who were, at the commencement of its application, in the status of non-beneficiaries of the management allowance because they were transferred to other schools or branches thereof which became their place of work and in which they performed management duties.

- Members of the teaching staff who assumed management duties after 11/11/2006, as of the date of their assignment to those duties, even if the applicable procedures were not observed in their assignment. Those currently performing the duties of managing public schools and assigned thereto before and after 11/11/2006 shall be appointed as principals of these schools by a decision taken by the Minister of Education and Higher Education within one year from the date of issuance of the Law, provided that each of them fulfils the conditions set forth in the First and Fourth Clauses of the Third Article of this Law.

The details of application of the provisions of this Law and the special conditions for appointing principals of vocational institutes and schools shall be determined by decrees taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Education and Higher Education.
Law No. 320 dated 20/4/2001 and its amendments issued by Law No. 777 dated 11/11/2006 are hereby repealed.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Definition of Terms The following expressions, wherever they appear in this Decision, shall have the meanings set out below:

1- The Law: the Tax Procedure Law.

2- The Tax: any tax or duty, with the exception of customs and real estate duties, the assessment and collection of which are undertaken by the Ministry of Finance, including:

a- Income tax.

b - Built property tax c-Transfer duty.

d- Betterment tax.

e - Value added tax.

f- Indirect taxes and similar duties.

g- Taxes and duties that may be introduced Unless the Law provides otherwise, the word "Tax" wherever it appears in this Decision includes the principal of the tax and its accessories, namely fines, interest, and compulsory collection expenses relating to the tax.

3 - The Taxpayer: every person bound by virtue of the tax laws by tax obligations, and the provisions of this Decision applicable to the taxpayer shall also apply to the tax withholder except in cases where the Law provides otherwise.

4 - The Tax Period: the period of time that includes the chargeable event or events giving rise to the tax, upon the expiry of which the tax must be declared or paid within a specified time limit in accordance with the legal provisions for each tax.

5 - The Tax Administration: the competent unit at the Ministry of Finance - Directorate General of Finance - entrusted with the tasks of managing, assessing, auditing, and collecting the tax, in accordance with the powers specified by law.

6 - The Person: the natural and legal person, unless the Law specifies either of them.

7 - The Tax Withholder: the person who is required by law to withhold the tax at source from the amounts due to another person (the primary taxpayer) and pay it to the Treasury.

8 - The Additional Tax: the tax resulting from the recovery of any concealment or shortfall in the tax due.

9 - Joint-Stock Companies: sociétés anonymes and partnerships limited by shares.

10- Lebanese Territory or Lebanon: the Lebanese lands, airspace, and territorial waters.

11- With respect to the articles relating to the use of the electronic tax system, the words and expressions used shall have the following meanings:

-"The Ministry": the Ministry of Finance.

-"The System": the Electronic Tax System, which is the system for managing and transmitting tax declarations and statements to the competent units of the Ministry of Finance via the Internet.

-"The Declaration": the electronic declaration, which consists of all declarations, refund requests, and tax statements that may be transmitted to the Ministry via the System.

-The User": the user of the System, who is the taxpayer (company/sole proprietorship/professional/association/syndicate...) holding the electronic keys to use the System, or the person authorised by the taxpayer to do so.

-"The Electronic Operations": all operations available on the System (for example, declaring periodic and annual taxes or inquiring about previously submitted declarations).

-"The Tax": any tax or duty covered by the System.

-"Undertaking": an undertaking to comply with the rules and conditions for using the System, signed by the user of the System.

Where a transaction is carried out between related persons, the Tax Administration shall have the right to revalue the value of the executed transaction for the purpose of determining the taxable amounts for the tax period to which it relates, and it may for that purpose adopt the fair market value of the transaction.

Fair market value means the value of the transaction as if it had been carried out between persons independent of each other and under conditions of full competition compared with similar transactions taking place on the date of execution of the taxable transaction.

Natural persons shall be deemed to be related where there exists between them a power of supervision and direction or a relationship of subordination, such as where one of them is an employee of the other, or a relationship of guardianship between the guardian and the minor or incapacitated person, or where they are joint and several partners towards a given obligation.

A natural person and a legal person shall be deemed to be related when either of them has the power of supervision and direction over the other.

Legal persons shall be deemed to be related when a legal person has the power of supervision and direction over one or more other legal persons. A person (natural or legal) shall have the power of direction and supervision over a person or enterprises when that person enjoys administrative authority over the others capable of determining the course of action of the other person in financial, economic, and organisational respects.

The following criteria shall be deemed presumptions of the existence of a power of supervision and direction:

a- With respect to capital companies, the holding by a natural or legal person of the majority of the capital of its subsidiary company which enables that person to enjoy the majority of the voting rights therein, or to appoint more than half of the members of its board of directors or its managers. Or where the natural or legal person is authorised by the board of directors of the company with respect to determining the course of action of the company in financial, economic, and organisational respects even if that person does not own the majority of the capital of the company.

b- With respect to partnerships, the ownership by a person of more than 50% of the shares of each partnership or the right to participate in more than 50% of its profits.

c- With respect to natural persons, the ownership by a person of several sole proprietorships or the ownership by several persons of more than one enterprise, provided that the relationship of kinship linking them is limited to the husband or wife or minor or incapacitated children.

For the purpose of calculating the percentage of holding of shares or stakes in companies or the ownership of sole proprietorships, the husband, wife, brothers, sisters, and non-minor children as well as minor or incapacitated children shall be deemed to be a single person.

Where the Tax Administration amends the value and conditions of transactions between related persons, the tax effects relating to the other related party to the transaction may be reconsidered upon the request of this party where it has an interest therein.

Tax obligations shall pass:

-where the taxpayer is deemed missing or absent according to the law, to his legal representative,

-where incapacitated, to his Sharia or legal representative or to the guardian appointed by the court.

The person representing the incapacitated person or the absentee must notify the competent tax unit with which the taxpayer was registered, or was concealed and falls within the scope of its jurisdiction, of his death or of the change in his status, within a time limit of two months from the date of occurrence of the event, and submit a declaration of the tax due by the taxpayer for the period extending from the date of the end of the previous tax period that was declared until the occurrence of the event, and pay this tax.

Every person in respect of whom a judgment of absence or loss of legal capacity has been issued shall be deemed absent or incapacitated.

The notification referred to in Article 7 of this Decision shall include the following information:

- the name of the taxpayer and his personal number at the Ministry of Finance,

- the names of the enterprises and companies in which he owns stakes or shareholdings and their registration numbers at the Ministry of Finance,

- the type of event (absence or lack of legal capacity) and its date,

- the name, address, and capacity of the person representing the taxpayer, and his registration number at the Ministry of Finance, if any,

- the signature and capacity of the person submitting the notification.

The notification submitted to the competent Tax Administration shall be accompanied by the following documents:

a- With respect to absence:

- a copy of the judgment of absence.

b- With respect to loss of legal capacity:

- a copy of the judgment issued declaring the taxpayer's loss of legal capacity.

In the event of the sufficiency of the assets of the absent, missing, or legally incapacitated taxpayer to settle the tax due, his legal or Sharia representative or the appointed guardian may submit a written application to the Tax Administration to write off the portion of the tax due that exceeds the total assets of the taxpayer, subject to submitting the following supporting documents:

- Bank statements and a summary of his credit and debit accounts,

- A certificate from the Land Registry Offices of all real properties that he owns,

- A certificate from the Commercial Register regarding his ownership of establishments, shares, or equity participations in companies,

- A certificate from the Vehicles and Machinery Registration Department and from the Port Administration regarding his ownership of cars and vehicles.

- An undertaking by the signatory of the non-existence of any cash amounts, jewellery, bearer shares, and the like.

The Tax Administration may request the production of any document it deems appropriate to prove the insolvency of the taxpayer.

The writing off of the excess amounts shall be carried out pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Finance upon the proposal of the Director General of Finance and following a recommendation by the Head of the Tax Administration based on a study conducted by this Administration.

The competent tax office shall undertake to notify the representative of the taxpayer of the decision to accept or reject the application.

The write-off decision shall be deemed null and void in the event that:

- The taxpayer recovers his legal capacity or the absent or missing person returns. In such case, the taxpayer or his representative shall be required to notify the Revenue Directorate and the Value Added Tax Directorate, each in so far as it is concerned, thereof in order to revoke the tax write-off decision, without interest and penalty running for the period during which the person lacked legal capacity or was missing, with interest and penalty running from the date of recovery of legal capacity or the return of the missing person.

- It subsequently appears that the tax write-off decision was based on unserious or erroneous grounds as a result of forgery or concealment of information or supporting documents, or as a result of omitting to declare certain information, or as a result of lack of knowledge thereof. Interest and penalty shall run on the tax due from its due date.

The chief clerks of the competent commercial and civil courts, pending the implementation of the electronic interconnection project, shall notify the Revenue Directorate of the registrations recorded in the Commercial Register or the Civil Register and all events relating to natural and legal persons, pursuant to the information statements specified below, in accordance with the following:

- Or upon the request of the Tax Administration in certain cases. These statements must include the following information:

The Personal Status Offices shall notify the Revenue Directorate of the deaths registered with them and of every case of declaration of death of a person who was deemed missing, pursuant to the information statement specified below, as from the effective date of the Law, provided that the notification takes place periodically every three months no later than the fifteenth of the month following the three-month period concerned, or upon its request in certain cases.

The Revenue Directorate shall lodge with each of the administrations, syndicates, and private bodies referred to in this Decision a list of the names of the natural and legal persons regarding whom they have previously notified the Tax Administration of the information relating to them, including their tax identification numbers.

The lodging of the information statements provided for in this Decision with the Tax Administration shall be effected on compact discs (CD), or by granting the Revenue Directorate the right of access to the database belonging to the public administrations, syndicates, and private bodies to extract the required information on the natural and legal persons concerned.

Every natural or legal person, or his legal representative, who wishes to commence a work or a transaction may submit a written request for inquiry to the department or branch competent for taxpayer services, prior to commencing the work intended to be established or prior to executing the transaction, for the purpose of confirming the manner of tax treatment in respect of all taxes and duties assessed by the Directorate of Public Finance.

The request for inquiry provided for in Article 26 of the Law must satisfy the following conditions:

- That it be submitted prior to the completion of the event regarding which the inquiry is sought and that it deal with factual rather than hypothetical matters.

- That it be submitted by the concerned party or his legal representative.

- That the question be asked regarding specific points of law relating to a particular transaction.

- That it include all the necessary elements and facts that enable the Tax Administration to take the appropriate decision regarding the tax treatment.

The request for inquiry must contain the following information:

- The name of the applicant for the inquiry, his address and his elected domicile,

- The tax identification number, if any,

- A clear specification of the subject regarding which the inquiry is sought, that is to say, by way of example and without limitation, the facts, the nature of the transaction, the points of law relating thereto, the date fixed for its execution and its expected cost.

- Specification of the parties concerned in the transaction or contract and their relationship to one another,

And there must be attached thereto all supporting documents relating to it and the legal power of attorney, if any.

A fee shall be imposed on an applicant for an inquiry, the conditions and amount of which shall be determined by virtue of a decree enacted upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance. A request for inquiry shall not be accepted unless it is accompanied by a receipt proving payment of the fee due.

The Tax Administration may, in the course of its examination of the request, request in writing from the concerned party additional information or documents relating to the subject of the inquiry, and he must submit such information and documents within a time limit of ten days from the date on which they are requested of him, failing which the Tax Administration shall proceed to reply to the taxpayer under his own responsibility in accordance with the documents submitted by him, and shall indicate in its reply to him the documents which it requested of him and which he did not produce.

The Tax Administration must decide upon the request and reply to the concerned party by virtue of a written letter addressed to him directly, even if the request for inquiry was submitted by his legal representative, regarding his questions within a time limit not exceeding two months from the date of submission of the information and documents necessary to decide upon the request, and it must notify him of the result in accordance with the rules of service provided for in the Law.

The Tax Administration shall be bound by the reply issued by it if the applicant for the inquiry complies with that reply upon execution and that reply was based on clear and accurate facts submitted by the concerned party.

Where the declarations and operations of the taxpayer are reviewed and audited by the Tax Administration, and it becomes apparent to it that its reply was not applied upon the execution of the transaction that is the subject of the inquiry, it shall have the right to issue the necessary assessments and impose the fines due if the application by the taxpayer was in violation of the statutory provisions.

The taxpayer shall have the right to object to these assessments in accordance with the rules of objection provided for in Chapter 12 of the Tax Procedures Law.

The replies issued by the Tax Administration shall neither apply nor be binding save in respect of the transaction regarding which the inquiry is requested, and these replies shall remain governed by the validity of the laws in the light of which they were issued, such that the Tax Administration shall be released from its reply upon the amendment of the statutory text on the basis of which it founded that reply.

Persons subject to income tax on a basis other than that of actual profit referred to in item 2 of Article 29 of the Law mean taxpayers assessed on the basis of lump-sum profit and taxpayers assessed on the basis of estimated profit.

The accounting registers that must be kept mandatorily are:

أ- In respect of taxpayers assessed on the basis of actual profit:

- The journal, in which transactions relating to the taxpayer's activity are recorded day by day in accordance with their chronological and numerical sequence; a taxpayer whose nature of business prevents that may record those transactions therein in summary form at least once a month, provided that he obtains prior written approval therefor from the competent finance department and preserves all documents that enable the verification of the accuracy of those operations day by day.

- The general ledger for opening and monitoring accounts.

- The inventory register, in which the elements of the inventory, the balance sheet and the income statement are recorded.

- The salaries and wages register, in which are recorded the names of employees, workers, daily workers and other wage-earners, the amount of their salaries and wages, the nature of their work, the date on which they commenced work, and the date on which they left work or were dismissed therefrom.

Joint-stock companies and partnerships limited by shares shall also be bound, in addition to the registers mentioned above, to keep the register of registered shares which includes all information and details relating to these shares since incorporation (purchase, transfer, increase, cancellation.... and all modifications occurring to the registered shares).

ب - In respect of taxpayers assessed on the basis of lump-sum profit:

- The journal, in which revenues and expenditures are entered daily for their chronological and numerical sequence.

- The fixed assets register in accordance with the models set out in Annex No. 6 of Decree No. 4665 dated 26/12/1981 (the General Accounting Plan).

- The salaries and wages register where there are employees.

ج - In respect of taxpayers assessed on the basis of estimated profit.

د- In respect of establishments exempted from income tax. Establishments exempted from income tax that take the form of companies shall be bound to keep the registers required to be kept by taxpayers assessed on the basis of actual profit.

As for establishments exempted from income tax other than companies, they may keep the registers required to be kept by taxpayers assessed on the basis of actual profit, or content themselves with keeping cash-basis accounting consisting mandatorily of the two registers required to be kept by taxpayers assessed on the basis of lump-sum profit in addition to the salaries and wages register.

هـ - In respect of public institutions, municipalities and unions of municipalities:

Public institutions, municipalities and unions of municipalities must keep the salaries and wages register only.
Taxpayers subject to Value Added Tax must keep the journal, inventory register and general ledger.

An establishment may use auxiliary journals and auxiliary general ledgers in accordance with its requirements and needs.

And on a periodic basis, the data recorded in the auxiliary journals shall be consolidated into a central journal and a central general ledger.

Every establishment must conduct an inventory of the elements of its assets and liabilities at least once a year, and close all its accounts for the purpose of determining the result of its operations and drawing up its balance sheet.

Accounting registers and documents may, for the purposes of imposing taxes and duties, be kept without being stamped or initialled, by any appropriate means or method capable of ensuring the accuracy of the entries and meeting the requirements of accounting auditing, including keeping and preserving accounting registers and documents electronically through the taxpayer's adoption of computerised accounting systems that satisfy the conditions secured by the traditional method, particularly in that the machines used by the taxpayer for this purpose are equipped with that which enables the Tax Administration to detect any subsequent entries of additions and to verify the accuracy of the recording and preservation, and the taxpayer must place at the disposal of the Tax Administration the user manual for those systems when needed.

The preservation of accounting records and documents by means of an automated computer or any other modern technology means preserving such records and documents electronically through the taxpayer's adoption of computerised accounting systems that substantiate and process accounting transactions and issue the required documents and statements in paper form upon request by the tax administration.

Taxpayers who make cash sales by means of a cash register (cach register) or who make sales by invoice may preserve the invoices, receipts, and other documents substantiating such sales by electronic means, provided that the machines they use for this purpose are equipped to issue such invoices, receipts, and documents in paper form in more than one copy in chronological and numerical sequence according to their chronological occurrence and in a manner that prevents the addition of any entries by interpolation, the cancellation of any entries, or the making of any subsequent additions, so as to enable the tax administration to verify the validity of the recording and preservation.

Taxpayers who wish to preserve the documents referred to above by electronic means shall obtain prior written approval in this regard from the tax administration.

A taxpayer who replaces the computerised system used by him shall preserve the old records and documents whose destruction is not permitted by law throughout the statutory period, and shall continue to preserve the computerised accounting records and documents even if they have been printed and preserved in paper form.

In all cases, the taxpayer shall retain an additional electronic copy (Backup) of the information preserved in the computerised system and of the user manual.

A taxpayer may contract with a second party for the purpose of keeping and preserving accounting records and documents electronically, provided that they are preserved at his place of business or at his place of residence, and he shall consequently remain liable before the tax administration and his rights and obligations relating to those records and documents shall not be transferred to the second party.
The fine under Article 114 of the Law shall be imposed on a taxpayer who violates the provisions of Articles 29 and 30 of the Law relating to the preservation of accounting records and documents.

Every person who commences a taxable activity or is bound pursuant to the law by tax obligations, including persons exempted from income tax on commercial, industrial, and non-commercial profits, shall notify the competent tax office thereof, by virtue of an application for registration, within a period of two months from the date of commencement of activity, subject to the provisions governing registration with the Directorate of Value Added Tax.

The application for notification referred to above shall be submitted in accordance with one of the following forms:

- A declaration of commencement of activity with respect to income tax.

- An application for registration of an employee/wage earner with respect to the tax on salaries and wages.

- An application for registration with the Directorate of Value Added Tax when such registration is mandatory.

- A declaration of commencement of activity, where required by law, with respect to other specific taxes.

The declaration of commencement of activity shall be required of the taxpayers set out below:

أ- Capital companies: joint-stock companies, limited liability companies, partnerships limited by shares, holding company, offshore companies.

ب - Partnerships: general partnerships, simple limited partnerships and civil companies.

ج - Natural persons:

Every person who carries out, individually or in cooperation with others, the following shall be deemed a natural person:

- Commercial or industrial professions, for example: automotive blacksmithing and mechanics, bookshops, grocery stores, etc...

- Non-commercial or non-industrial activities (liberal professions), for example: lawyer, physician, etc...

- Any activity that generates revenue not subject to another income tax and not classified above.

د - Establishments excluded from the tax on commercial, industrial, and non-commercial profits (Title I), which include, by way of example and without limitation: universities, associations, schools, etc.....

هـ - Establishments temporarily exempted from income tax on profits (Title I): for example, industrial establishments that have been exempted under specific conditions.

All the categories mentioned above shall be deemed responsible with respect to the declaration of the commencement of employment of the persons working for them.

The dates of commencement of activity shall be determined in accordance with the following:

أ - Capital companies: the date of registration of the company in the Commercial Register.

ب - Partnerships: the date of registration in the Commercial Register.

ج - Natural persons: the date of commencement of activity based on one of the following criteria:

1- The date of the first act capable of generating revenue subject to the tax on profits (Title I).

2 - The date of registration in the Commercial Register.

3 - The date of issuance of any document substantiating the occurrence of a commercial transaction, for example: an invoice or a receipt.

4 - The date of hiring a wage earner.

5- The date of leasing or using premises to practise the profession or activity.

6 - The date of the permit to practise the profession or of registration with the professional association for members of the liberal professions, with the exception of:

- Lawyers: as from the date of transfer of their registration to the General Roll.

- Pharmacists: as from the date of registration in the Commercial Register.

Where multiple criteria apply, the date of the criterion that occurs first shall be taken into account.

د - Establishments excluded from the tax on profits:

1- Capital companies.

- Partnerships.

- Sole proprietorships:

According to the dates specified in paragraphs أ-ب-ج of this Article.

2 - Associations-schools-universities-hospitals owned by non-profit associations: the date of the licence or the acknowledgement of receipt of notice (ilm wa khabar).

هـ - Wage earners: as from the date of hiring.

The declaration of commencement of activity shall be submitted to the competent tax unit in accordance with the form prepared by the Ministry of Finance for each of the types mentioned in Article 39 of this Decision.

The declaration of commencement of business shall be accompanied by the following documents:

A- Capital companies:

1- A copy of the company's articles of association registered with the Commercial Register.

2- A copy of the certificate of registration in the Commercial Register.

3 - A copy of the commercial circular.

4 - A copy of the acknowledgment of receipt and notice from the Ministry of Economy and Trade for branches of foreign companies operating in Lebanon.

5 - A copy of the lease contract, the title deed, the exploitation contract, or a statement from the owner that the occupancy is by way of tolerance accompanied by a copy of the title deed (or an acknowledgment and notice for resurveyed properties).

6 - A copy of the identity card or civil status extract for each shareholder or partner not identified in the tax system.

7- A copy of the registration certificate for the corporate shareholder.

8 - Any other document requested by the Tax Administration to verify the accuracy of the information declared by the taxpayer.

B - Partnerships:

1- A certified copy of the partnership agreement.

2- A copy of the certificate of registration in the Commercial Register.

3- A copy of the commercial circular.

4- A copy of the acknowledgment of receipt and notice from the Ministry of Economy and Trade for branches of foreign companies operating in Lebanon.

5- A copy of the identity card, an individual civil status extract for a single person, or a family civil status extract for a married person, for each partner not identified in the tax system.

6- A copy of the lease contract, the title deed, the exploitation contract, or a statement from the owner that the occupancy is by way of tolerance accompanied by a copy of the title deed (or an acknowledgment and notice for resurveyed properties).

7 - Any other document requested by the Tax Administration to verify the accuracy of the information declared by the taxpayer.

C - Individuals, sole proprietorships, and liberal professions:

1- A copy of the certificate of registration in the Commercial Register for those registered.

2- A copy of the identity card, an individual civil status extract for a single person, or a family civil status extract for a married person.

3- A copy of the permit to practice the profession and a copy of the syndicate registration card or a certificate of affiliation, for those required to be affiliated with a syndicate.

4- A copy of the lease contract, the title deed, the exploitation contract, or a statement from the owner that the occupancy is by way of tolerance accompanied by a copy of the title deed (or an acknowledgment and notice for resurveyed properties).

5- Any other document requested by the Tax Administration to verify the accuracy of the information declared by the taxpayer.

D - Persons exempt from the tax on profits:

1- A copy of the bylaws of the establishment or company.

2- A copy of the license issued by the competent authority.

3- A copy of the lease contract, the title deed, the exploitation contract, or a statement from the owner that the occupancy is by way of tolerance accompanied by a copy of the title deed (or an acknowledgment and notice for resurveyed properties).

4- Any other document requested by the Tax Administration to verify the accuracy of the information declared from the accuracy of the information declared by the taxpayer.

5- The wage earner.

1- A copy of a family civil status extract for the married wage earner.

2- A copy of an individual civil status extract or a copy of the identity card for the single wage earner.

3- A copy of the passport for the foreign worker.

As of the date of being notified of his special tax registration number, the taxpayer shall be required to comply with all the obligations imposed on him by the Law and its implementing texts starting from the date of his commencement of business, and all effects of registration shall apply against him and in his favor.

1- Every person who fails to submit his application for registration with the Tax Administration within the legal time limits shall be subject to the fine provided for in Clause 1 of Article 107 of the Law, amounting to:

-2.000.000 L.L. (two million Lebanese pounds) for joint-stock companies,

-1.000.000 L.L. (one million Lebanese pounds) for partnerships, limited liability companies, and institutions excluded from tax,

-300.000 L.L. (three hundred thousand Lebanese pounds) for individuals and other taxpayers.

2- Every employer who fails to register his wage earners with the Tax Administration shall be subject to a flat fine of fifty thousand Lebanese pounds for each employee or wage earner who is not registered within the specified time limits, or for whom false information is provided.

A taxpayer who meets the conditions for the commencement of business and has no intention of actually practicing the business shall be required to submit an application for registration within the specified time limit, accompanied by a declaration of actual non-practice of business.

He must also submit this declaration annually to the competent tax unit within the legal time limit pertaining to the submission of the income tax declaration.

The declaration of non-practice of business shall be submitted to the competent tax unit, in accordance with the form prepared by the Ministry of Finance.

Taxpayers who annually submit a declaration of actual non-practice of business shall be exempted from the obligation to keep statutory records and to submit income tax declarations and the financial statements attached thereto, until the actual practice of business, at which time the procedures specific to the commencement of business shall apply.

Where the declaration of commencement of business includes an activity subject to more than one type of tax, such declaration shall be deemed a declaration for all types of taxes except for the Value Added Tax.
