Where a natural person adds an activity in the same place of business declared to the competent tax department or carries out the same activity in another place of business, he shall be required to amend the information relating to him within the two-month time limit provided for in Clause 2 of Article 32 of the Law in accordance with the form prepared by the Ministry of Finance.

Where a natural person carries out a new activity in another place of business, he shall be required to declare the commencement of a new business within the two-month time limit provided for in Article 38 of this Decision, subject to the provisions of Decision No. 368/1 dated 4 April 2002 relating to persons who simultaneously manage or carry out works or activities or interrelated in multiple establishments with respect to the Value Added Tax.

Where a company commences a new activity or the same activity in another place of business, this shall be deemed a branch of the company and not the commencement of a new business, and it shall be required to submit a declaration of amendment of information.

Subject to the legal provisions that provide for the exemption of certain workers in certain organizations and bodies from the tax on salaries and wages, the obligations of the non-resident employer shall be transferred to the resident employee subject to the tax on salaries and wages with respect to this tax.

A- A taxpayer shall be deemed to have permanently ceased business in the following cases:

- Cessation due to death.

- Cessation which entails the carrying out by the taxpayer, whatever his legal form, of the procedures of voluntary liquidation of his fixed and current assets, the settlement of his obligations, and the completion of the procedures of deregistration from the Commercial Register or the Civil Register for those registered in either of these two registers.

- Cessation which entails the carrying out by the taxpayer who is required to belong to a syndicate in order to practise the profession, of the procedures of striking off his name from the register of the syndicate and the procedures of transferring his name to the roll of retired or non-practising members.

- Cessation resulting from a judicial judgment due to bankruptcy or any other reason which entails the completion by the bankruptcy trustee or the judicial liquidator of the procedures of compulsory liquidation of the fixed and current assets of the taxpayer, the settlement of his obligations, and the completion of the procedures of deregistration from the Commercial Register; and the date of the declaration of bankruptcy shall be deemed the date of the bankrupt's from business.

- A taxpayer shall be deemed to have temporarily ceased business, in the event of interruption of business without such interruption entailing the carrying out of the procedures referred to in Paragraph A of this Article, particularly as regards his retention of his registration number in the Commercial Register, in the Civil Register, or in the register of the syndicate, or the non-transfer of his name to the roll of retired or non-practising members. Consequently, he shall be required to submit a declaration of temporary cessation of business within a time limit of two months from the date of cessation, in accordance with a form prepared by the Ministry of Finance.

C - An employee who leaves his employment shall be deemed to have ceased work in respect of the employer, and the latter shall be required to submit a list of the names of the employees who have left employment with him to the Tax Administration together with the annual declaration specific to the tax on salaries and wages, in accordance with a form prepared by the Ministry of Finance.

The obligations of taxpayers who have permanently ceased business shall be determined in accordance with the following:

1- Partnerships and capital companies, including offshore companies and holding companies:

*Submitting the declaration of cessation of business (Form M6), accompanied by the minutes in which the cessation of business was decided in respect of capital companies, and the deed of dissolution of partnership and winding up of the company in respect of partnerships.

*Submitting all tax declarations for the period from the first of January until the date of cessation of business and paying all taxes due within a time limit of two months from the date of this cessation.

* Submitting the auditor's report within a time limit of 3 months from the date of cessation of business in respect of companies required to submit it, and within a time limit of two months from the date of cessation if the liquidation operations have been completed on the date of cessation.

*If the company that has ceased business is a partnership and one of the partners therein continues in business individually or in another partnership, he shall be required to declare his share of the result of the company that has ceased business within the annual declaration.

*If, after its cessation of business, the company still owns fixed assets or inventory, it shall be converted in the tax system to the status of "company under liquidation", and a special financial year shall be determined for it starting from the date of cessation of business and ending on the corresponding day of the following year.

*If the duration of the liquidation exceeds this special financial year, and the liquidator must draw up the annual balance sheet and pay the taxes due for that year within the legal time limit for declaration (3 months or 5 months according to the legal form of the company) from the date of expiry of the special financial year, and submit the auditor's report within the legal time limit.

*If the liquidation operations are completed, and the general assembly in joint-stock companies and the assembly of quota-holders in limited liability companies and in partnerships approve the result of the liquidation, it shall remain mandatory to submit the declaration of non-exercise of business annually until it is struck off from the Commercial Register.

*Informing the competent financial unit when the company is struck off from the Commercial Register.

2 - Natural persons assessed on the basis of actual or lump-sum profit who own a commercial establishment registered in the Commercial Register:

*Submitting the declaration of cessation of business (Form M6).

*Submitting all tax declarations for the period from the first of January until the date of cessation of business and paying all taxes due within a time limit of two months from the date of this cessation, unless the taxpayer continues in business in an individual capacity or in the capacity of a partner in a partnership, in which case he shall be required to declare his share of the result of the establishment that has ceased business within his annual declaration where he continues to carry on his business.

*It shall remain mandatory to submit the declaration of non-exercise of business annually until the establishment is struck off from the Commercial Register.

*Informing the competent financial unit when the establishment is struck off from the Commercial Register.

3 - Natural persons assessed on the basis of actual or lump-sum profit (practitioners of liberal professions or owners of commercial establishments not registered in the Commercial Register):

*Submit the declaration of cessation of business (Form M6).

*Submitting all tax declarations for the period from the first of January until the date of cessation of business and paying all taxes due within a time limit of two months from the date of this cessation, unless the taxpayer continues in business in an individual capacity or in the capacity of a partner in a partnership, in which case he shall be required to declare his share of the result of the establishment that has ceased business within his annual declaration where he continues to carry on his business.

4-Practitioners of liberal professions required to belong to a syndicate:

- If the cessation of business is due to occupying a post in the public or private sector which prohibits them from practising their activity subject to the tax of Title One, they shall not be required to submit the annual declaration of non-exercise of business after the cessation.

- If the cessation of business is due to travel, they shall be required to submit a declaration of non-exercise of business annually within the legal time limit.

5-Taxpayers assessed on the basis of estimated profit:

*Submitting the declaration of cessation of business (Form M6).

*Paying the taxes due from them.

*Submitting all tax declarations, where applicable.

6-Cessation of business due to the death of a taxpayer who is a partner in a partnership or who was practising business independently:

*Submitting the declaration of cessation of business for the deceased (Form M6) by the heirs, together with the declaration of the deceased's share of the result of the operations of the company, within a time limit of two months from the date of death, as well as submitting all tax declarations for the period extending from the end of the previous tax period that was declared until the date of death if he was assessed on the basis of lump-sum profit or estimated profit.

7-Persons exempt from the tax on profits other than companies:

*Submitting the declaration of cessation of business (Form M6).

*Submitting all tax declarations for the period from the first of January until the date of cessation of business and paying all taxes due within a time limit of two months from the date of this cessation.

The provisions of this Decision shall apply to the heirs, who shall be required to submit the information and statements necessary for the assessment of the tax within a period of two months from the date of death. Furthermore, the provisions of this Decision to judicial liquidators and bankruptcy trustees upon the occurrence of bankruptcy, in which case the time limit shall run from the date of issuance of the decision appointing them.

The declaration of cessation of business shall be accompanied by the information and documents proving its validity and necessary for determining the taxable profit, and in particular the following documents:

- In the event of sale: the contract of sale or assignment of the leased premises.

- In the event of bankruptcy: the bankruptcy judgment.

- Expiry of the term fixed for the company or the will of the partners/shareholders:

- The articles of association of the company indicating the duration of the company where the cessation is due to the expiry of the appointed term of the company.

- The minutes of the partners' resolution to cease business in the case of partnerships.

- The minutes of the extraordinary general assembly to cease business in the case of capital companies.

- In the event of liquidation: - the liquidator's report.

- In the event of death: a death certificate.

- In the event of expropriation of the entire enterprise: the expropriation decision.

- In merger: the merger contract.

- In the case of persons exempt from the tax on profits other than companies:

- The decision withdrawing the notice and acknowledgment.

- The constituent instrument if it includes a specified term, and the cessation is due to the expiry of such term.

- The decision taken to cease business.

The Tax Administration shall complete the audit of the file of the taxpayer who has permanently ceased business within a period of four months from the date of notification of the declaration of cessation of business accompanied by all the documents and information necessary for determining the taxable profit.

A taxpayer who submits a declaration of permanent cessation of business shall be required to continue submitting a declaration of non-exercise of business annually within the time limit for the annual declaration, after the completion of the liquidation process and until striking off from the Trade Register, the Civil Register, or the Syndicate.

He shall also be required, within a time limit of 15 days from his notification of the tax notice resulting from the audit, to deposit his accounting books and documents relating to the years for which retention remains required in accordance with the provisions of the ten-year limitation period with the Tax Administration in paper form or on compact discs, and where the cessation is due to bankruptcy, this obligation shall be transferred to the bankruptcy trustee.

The Tax Administration shall take the necessary measures to preserve those books and documents so as to enable it to inspect them when it needs to respond to requests for information received by it under agreements permitting the exchange of information.

A taxpayer who submits a declaration of temporary cessation of business shall also be required to submit his annual declaration within the legal time limit in respect of the first year in which the interruption of business occurred, provided that he remains obliged to submit a declaration of non-exercise of business annually, within the time limit for the annual declaration, throughout the period of his interruption of business, until the Tax Administration is notified of the resumption of the exercise of business. This taxpayer shall be obliged to retain all accounting books and records that he was using on the date of the temporary cessation of business in order to use them upon the resumption of business. The opening balances upon the resumption of business must be identical to the balances of the accounts on the date of cessation of business.

Subject to the legal provisions providing for joint and several liability, the submission of a declaration of cessation of business shall not cancel the liability of the taxpayer for paying the taxes due from him for the period of his exercise of the taxable activity, whether those taxes were assessed or became due for collection before or after the cessation.

Every person who fails to notify the Tax Administration of his temporary or permanent cessation of business within the legal time limits shall be subject to the fine provided for in Article 108 of the Law.

A taxpayer who is obliged to submit a declaration of non-exercise of business annually shall, in the event of delay in or failure to submit this declaration, be subject to the fine provided for in Article 109 of the Law.

Where the activity that the taxpayer was exercising prior to his cessation of business is subject to more than one type of tax, the declaration of cessation of business shall be deemed to cover the various types of those taxes, and the tax unit to which the declaration of cessation of business was submitted shall be required to inform the other tax units of that declaration.

Consequently, a declaration of permanent cessation of business submitted by the taxpayer to the competent tax unit affiliated with the Revenue Directorate shall be deemed to constitute an application for the cancellation of his registration with the Value Added Tax Directorate.

The Revenue Directorate shall be required to notify the Director of Value Added Tax of this application.

The submission of a declaration of cessation of business shall not exempt the taxpayer from the obligation to submit the periodic declarations and statements relating to the period between the last day of the period covered by the previous declaration of business results and the day on which he ceased business.

Furthermore, the submission of the periodic declarations and statements relating to the period between the last day of the period covered by the previous declaration of business results and the day on which the taxpayer ceased business shall not exempt the taxpayer from submitting the declaration of cessation of business.

With regard to the built property tax, the declaration of permanent cessation of business cannot be considered a declaration of vacancy of the building where the taxpayer occupies real property that he owns in his own name or through his exploitation.

The Tax Administration shall grant the taxpayer, upon his registration with it, a single tax identification number for all types of taxes, including customs and real estate duties, in accordance with the procedures specified in this Decision.

a - The Tax Administration shall grant a single personal tax identification number (TIN):

*To every natural person who submits a transaction to it, commences a business in an individual capacity or in the capacity of a partner in a partnership, or contributes to or owns shares in a capital company.

*To every employee who exercises salaried employment, and the obligation of registration shall lie with the employer if he is a resident and with the employee where his employer is a non-resident.

*The taxpayers mentioned above shall be granted a tax card issued by the Ministry of Finance.

b - The Tax Administration shall grant a personal tax identification number (TIN) to a profession, enterprise, company, or any other person, whether or not enjoying legal personality, when it assumes the status of an independent entity from a tax perspective (joint venture, de facto company....), and they shall be delivered a registration certificate from the Ministry of Finance.

c - The Tax Administration shall grant a personal tax identification number (TIN) to every public administration, public institution, municipality, union of municipalities, and other bodies and associations.

And they shall be delivered a registration certificate from the Ministry of Finance.

d - Every company or owner of a profession or enterprise shall be required to adopt its own personal tax identification number (TIN) when dealing with third parties in that capacity, and every natural person shall be required to produce his own personal tax identification number (TIN) when dealing with official departments.

Public administrations shall be required to provide the Directorate of Public Finance with lists containing the names of their civilian personnel (officials, contractors, daily workers....) and lists containing the appointment of new civilian personnel or the transfer of personnel to another public administration within a maximum time limit of:

- Two months from the date of publication of this Decision in respect of existing personnel registered with them up to 31/12/2008,

- One week from the date of commencement of work in respect of new personnel.

Provided that these lists include:

*The full name (first name, father's name, surname, mother's name),

*Date of birth, place of birth, register number, place of register, identity card number,

*Date of commencement of work,

*Date of transfer,

*Personal address,

*Personal telephone number,

*Capacity of the worker,

*Other information in accordance with the form prepared by the Ministry of Finance.

Public and private institutions, municipalities, unions of municipalities, bodies, associations, and all other natural and legal persons shall notify the Tax Administration of the names of all persons working for them in accordance with the form prepared by the Ministry of Finance, within a period not exceeding:

- Two months from the date of publication of this Decision in respect of all persons working for them prior to the entry into force of this Law.

- Two months from the date of employment of each new employee.

This shall be done in accordance with the form prepared by the Ministry of Finance.

Immediately upon receipt of such information, the Tax Administration shall assign a personal tax identification number to each person, and return to the public administrations, public institutions, and natural and legal persons a list of the names of the employees containing their personal tax identification numbers.

The Tax Administration shall issue a tax card for each of the former and new workers and deposit it with the concerned entities with a view to distributing it to its holders.

All public and private institutions, municipalities, the union of municipalities, bodies, associations, and all other natural and legal persons shall adopt their registration number with the Ministry of Finance on all documents issued by them and shall be bound to use the registration numbers assigned by the Ministry of Finance to their employees and persons dealing with them in all their documents.

Registration Procedure:

1- A taxpayer who wishes to register in the electronic service shall log in through the website of the Ministry of Finance (WWW. Finance.gov.Lb.) to the tax page, click on the electronic tax system service, fill out the approved registration form, and send it electronically.

2- After verifying the accuracy of the entered information, a page shall appear notifying the taxpayer of the receipt by the Ministry of Finance of the registration application, which includes the required documents (list attached hereto) to complete the registration process.

3- The Ministry of Finance shall send an electronic message to the taxpayer's electronic mail address in order to confirm the address.

4- A message shall be sent to the taxpayer's electronic mail containing his registration tracking number, in addition to the follow-up receipt containing the tracking number pertaining to the company and designated for completing the registration procedure in the electronic services.

5- The taxpayer shall receive an electronic notice whereby the Central Taxpayer Database Department sets an appointment to visit it and receive the electronic identification number (e.Pin), and sets out therein a list of the required documents.

6- The taxpayer or the person officially authorised by him shall appear before the Central Taxpayer Database Department at the specified appointment, bringing with him the undertaking (form attached hereto) and the required documents (and the official authorisation granted to him by the taxpayer) to receive the electronic keys, and the Department shall thereupon verify their authenticity before receiving them.

7- The user shall receive, in a special sealed envelope, the personal electronic keys (e-Pin) which authorise him to access the electronic tax system.

1- Within the statutory time limits specified for returns, the user shall fill out the forms required to be submitted that appear on the page designated for periodic or annual returns and statements and refund applications, and send them electronically through the system.

2 - Immediately upon receipt of the return by the system, the return shall be sent to the user's electronic mail indicating thereon the date of receipt.

3 - The user shall print the return and the electronic return receipt and retain them after signing them; the electronic return receipt shall be deemed an official receipt of the return, and the date appearing on the receipt shall be deemed the actual date of the return.

General Provisions:

1- The user shall strictly safeguard the personal electronic keys granted to him and shall not disclose them to any person or allow him, intentionally or negligently, to have access to them. The Ministry shall bear no liability in the event that this system is used by one or more persons who obtained the electronic keys due to the user's negligence or for any other reason relating to the user.

2 - The use of the personal electronic keys shall be deemed the user's signature and shall have the same legal effects resulting from a signature, and he shall not be entitled to object to or challenge the transactions executed by means thereof in the event of any dispute arising in relation thereto.

3 - Transactions carried out through the use of the personal electronic keys shall be deemed final and conclusive proof of the transactions carried out by the user.

4 - The Ministry shall be entitled, in accordance with the requirements of public interest, to revoke the right it granted to the user whenever it sees fit, provided that it notifies him thereof, stating the reasons, within a period of three days from the date of revocation of the right.

5 - The Ministry shall be entitled, in accordance with the requirements of public interest, to change the personal electronic keys whenever it sees fit, provided that it notifies the user thereof and requests him to appear to receive the new keys within a period not exceeding three days from the date of changing the electronic keys.

A taxpayer who is required to calculate the tax due from him in accordance with the self-assessment system shall be responsible for calculating this tax, declaring it, and paying it to the Treasury within the statutory time limits, pursuant to an advance payment notice and without the need for the issuance of a tax notice or an assessment roll by the Tax Administration.

The following categories shall be subject to the self-assessment system:

- Taxpayers subject to income tax on the basis of actual profit and lump-sum profit in respect of the results of their operations and the taxes withheld from the entitlements of third parties and remitted to the Treasury.

- Taxpayers subject to income tax on the basis of estimated profit in respect of the taxes withheld from the entitlements of third parties and remitted to the Treasury.

- Taxpayers who are personally required to declare themselves and pay the tax due from them, namely resident persons who work for a non-resident employer, an employee who works in several establishments at the same time, and an employee who concurrently practises a profession subject to the tax of Title I of the Income Tax Law or who otherwise receives a retirement pension or life annuities.

- Persons subject to Value Added Tax.

- Persons subject to the 5% tax on accommodation, food, and beverage charges.

- Every person resident in Lebanon whose dealings with a non-resident person having no representative in Lebanon have given rise to Value Added Tax becoming due, as well as every person resident in Lebanon who uses therein a service acquired from an entity resident outside Lebanese territory.

- Taxpayers subject to the built property tax whose revenues exceed 20 million L.L. per year for each property and who are required to submit the annual return.

In cases that do not fall within the scope of the preceding Article, the taxpayer shall be responsible for paying the tax within a time limit specified in the law from the date of occurrence of the event (fiscal stamp duty..) or from the date of issuance of the assessment by the Tax Administration (estimated profit taxpayers in respect of their profits, built property tax taxpayers whose revenues do not exceed 20 million L.L. per year for each property, transfer duty taxpayers....).

In cases where the tax laws do not require self-assessment of the tax, the Tax Administration shall issue the assessment by virtue of assessment rolls or payment orders and record them in the taxpayer's account pursuant to the provisions of Paragraph 1 of Article 42 of the Law.

The competent financial department shall undertake the imposition of the tax issued by virtue of payment orders, and the head of the competent financial unit, or the person authorised by him for such purpose, shall approve it.

Where material errors appear in the assessment rolls or collection orders after their entry into the taxpayer's account, relating exclusively to the recording of figures or names, to the performance of arithmetical operations, or to duplicate assessment, the competent department shall undertake the necessary corrections on the computerised systems in coordination with the Electronic Centre, and shall notify the Director of Revenues or the Director of Value Added Tax, each within his competence, and the competent collection department, with copies of the approval of the head of the unit pursuant to which the correction was made.

Where the taxpayer fails to comply with the obligations imposed by the Administration regarding the submission of returns, the keeping of statutory accounting books and documents, or the provision to the Tax Administration of information useful for calculating the tax base, the Administration shall notify him that it will proceed, within a period of one month from the date of his notification of this notice, to determine the tax base in accordance with the provisions of Clause 5 of Article 42 of the Law and such returns and documents as the taxpayer may have submitted during this month.

In this case, and with respect to income tax taxpayers, the Estimated Profit Committee shall, pursuant to a reasoned decision, undertake to determine the tax base upon the proposal of the competent tax unit, and the result shall be either zero or a profit liable to tax assessment in respect of real profit taxpayers, or a profit determined on the basis of the lump-sum profit rates in respect of lump-sum profit taxpayers.
The collection zones defined in the Governorates are repealed and Lebanon is adopted as a single collection zone.

Following the completion of the audit operation provided for in Article 44 et seq. of the Law, the competent Tax Administration shall draw up a report containing the preliminary results of the audit where adjustments to the tax base are required; whereas if it appears to it that there is no need to make any adjustments to the tax base, it shall notify the taxpayer thereof.

The preliminary report of the results must be reasoned such that it includes:

- A detailed breakdown of every adjustment to the tax base or the amounts refused deduction or refund and the reasons therefor, together with their value,

- The legal provisions and facts upon which the assessment is based,

- The contraventions and the rates and values of the fines incurred on each of them.

The competent tax unit shall notify the taxpayer, whether concealed or non-concealed, of the preliminary results of the audit, in the following manner:

- With respect to the non-concealed taxpayer, the procedures provided for in Articles 27 and 28 of the Law relating to notification shall be adopted.

- With respect to the concealed taxpayer, the notice of the preliminary proposals shall be published in two local newspapers and on the website of the Ministry of Finance.

The notice must include:

The tax period, the taxpayer's name and address, a request to the taxpayer to refer to the competent tax unit within a period of thirty days from the date of publication in order to be notified of the preliminary results; and where the said period expires and the taxpayer has not referred to the competent tax department, notification shall be deemed to have been validly effected at the end of the thirty-day period.

In order to avoid theprescription of taxes by the passage of time, the competent tax unit shall:

- With respect to the non-concealed taxpayer, deposit the preliminary results of the audit by registered mail within a maximum period of 31/12 of the fourth year following the year subsequent to the year of the business concerned.

- With respect to the concealed taxpayer, publish the notice summons in two local newspapers and on the website of the Ministry of Finance within a maximum period of 30/11 of the sixth year following the year subsequent to the year of the business concerned.

The taxpayer shall submit his observations on the preliminary results of the audit in writing and send them to the competent tax unit within a period of 30 days from the date of his notification of these results. Where one of the revenue years subject to the audit is a year liable to prescription by the passage of time, the granting of this period shall not lead to the prescription of the taxes subject to these assessments by the passage of time, unless the competent tax unit delays issuing the assessment and depositing it in the mail until after the end of one month from the date of its notification of the taxpayer's observations.

Where the taxpayer agrees, through the submission of his observations, to the assessment contained in the preliminary results notified to him, the competent tax department shall issue the final assessment within a maximum period of one month from the date of its receipt of these observations.

Whereas if the taxpayer does not submit any observations to the competent tax department within the thirty-day period, or sends his observations after the expiry of this period, this is deemed to constitute a tacit acceptance on his part of the preliminary results of the audit, and the competent tax unit shall issue the final assessment within a maximum period of one month from the date of expiry of the period provided for in Article 85 of this Decision.

Where the taxpayer expresses an opinion contrary to the preliminary audit results, he shall state the reasons for his opinion and point out the material and legal errors, if any, and he shall also state the legal points or information upon which he wishes to rely and produce the supporting documents therefor.

The competent tax unit shall examine the points raised by the taxpayer in accordance with the new data submitted by him, and it may request from him, in writing or orally, any clarifications regarding these points, and he shall provide it with the information it requests from him within a period that it specifies for him.

The competent tax unit may withdraw wholly or partially from the preliminary audit results or amend them if it appears to it that the new data justify the same, and it may also disagree with all of the observations of the taxpayer.

The competent tax unit shall issue the final assessment within a period of one month from the date of its receipt of these observations, provided that this assessment includes a reply to the taxpayer's observations.

With respect to the concealed taxpayer, and where he does not refer to the competent tax unit within a period of one month from the date of publication of the notice mentioned in Article 83 of this Decision, the said unit shall proceed to issue the final assessment within a period of one month from the date of expiry of the period for submitting observations on the preliminary results of the audit, and shall proceed to notify the taxpayer by way of publication in two local newspapers and on the website of the Ministry of Finance, and the taxpayer shall be deemed notified as from the first working day following the date of this publication, and he shall consequently be entitled to submit an objection to the assessment within a period of two months from the date of notification.

Where one of the revenue years subject to the audit is a year liable to prescription by the passage of time, the additional one-month period shall not lead to the prescription of the taxes subject to the assessments by the passage of time, unless the competent tax unit delays issuing the assessments and depositing it in the mail until after the end of one month from the date of its notification of the taxpayer's observations.

The final assessment report shall include the following information:

1- The start and end dates of the audit operation.

2 - The periods covered by the audit operation.

3 - The type of audit carried out (comprehensive, targeted,....) and the taxes it covered.

4 - The adjustments made to the taxpayer's return.

5 - The facts and legal points upon which the assessment is based.

6 - The reasons for rejecting the taxpayer's observations on the preliminary results, if any.

7 - The determination of the tax base and the calculation of its amount and the fines due for each period that was audited.

8 - The names and signatures of the employees assigned to the audit operation.

The taxpayer shall be notified of the final results of the audit pursuant to a tax notice. The tax notice shall include the following:

1- The number and date of the notice.

2- The name and address of the taxpayer.

3- His tax identification number.

4- The reasons for the adjustments and the assessment, provided that they are detailed with respect to the violations committed and the legal articles or administrative instructions governing such violations.

5- The taxable amounts, specifying the tax periods to which they pertain.

6- The amount of the tax, interest and fines due.

7- A request to pay the amounts due within the legal time limit and a statement of the payment methods permissible to be adopted.

8- The time limits for objecting to the taxes due.

9- The signature of the competent employee.

10- The signature of the head of the tax administration.

There shall be attached to this notice the collection document that includes the taxes and fines due, if any.
The provisions of the above articles relating to the results of auditing the operations of taxpayers shall apply to taxpayers subject to the tax self-assessment system.

The tax due in accordance with the self-assessment method shall be paid in a single lump sum, whereas the additional tax shall be paid in a single lump sum or by instalments, where the law so permits, subject to the prior approval of the Director General of Finance.
Tax payments shall be settled either in cash, by a banker's cheque drawn in favour of the Central Treasury Cashier, or by bank transfer.

A taxpayer who is required to declare in accordance with the self-assessment method must calculate the tax due from him and shall be responsible for declaring and paying it within the legal time limits pursuant to a payment notice form prepared by the Ministry of Finance.

Periodic and annual taxes and fees subject to the self-assessment method shall be paid exclusively at any of the private banks or their branches operating in Lebanon, or at any of the offices of LibanPost or of any other company with which the Ministry of Finance contracts for this purpose. As for taxes not subject to the self-assessment method and additional taxes, they shall be paid pursuant to a form prepared by the Ministry of Finance at any of the banks or their branches operating in Lebanon, at the competent Treasury cash offices, or at any of the offices of LibanPost or of any other company with which the Ministry of Finance contracts for this purpose.

The tax shall be deemed paid on the day on which its full amount is settled by the taxpayer or the withholding agent, and an approved payment by instalments shall be deemed to constitute payment of the tax.

When the tax is paid by means of a bank transfer, the tax shall be deemed paid on the date of execution of the transfer recorded on the receipt issued by the bank.

First- Taxes and fees that shall be paid exclusively at banks or their branches, or at any of the offices of LibanPost, or at the offices of any other company with which the Ministry of Finance contracts:

- Income tax calculated in accordance with the self-assessment method:

- Income tax on profits.

– Tax on salaries and wages (periodic and annual declaration).

– Tax on movable capital and interest on secured debts.

- Built property tax calculated in accordance with the self-assessment method.

- Value added tax.

Second - Taxes and fees that may be paid at banks or their branches, or at any of the offices of LibanPost, or at the offices of any other company with which the Ministry of Finance contracts, or at the Treasury cash offices:

- Additional tax.

- Taxes and fees imposed pursuant to a collection order.

- Amounts paid on account of taxes due.

- Tax issued pursuant to basic assessment rolls.

In the event that the taxpayer pays the tax at the Treasury cash offices, the cashier shall hand the taxpayer a receipt for the payment of the tax in accordance with a form prepared by the Ministry of Finance.

As for taxes paid at banks or their branches, or at any of the offices of LibanPost, or at the offices of any other company with which the Ministry of Finance contracts, for the account of the Treasury, the mechanism for processing them shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.
Amounts paid by the taxpayer on account of the taxes due from him shall be settled in cash or pursuant to a banker's cheque in favour of the Central Treasury Cashier.

Amounts paid by the taxpayer on account of the taxes due from him shall be paid, in accordance with a form prepared by the Ministry of Finance, at the Treasury cash office, or at any of the banks or their branches, or at any of the offices of LibanPost or of any other company with which the Ministry of Finance contracts for this purpose, and he shall be handed a receipt for the deposit of the amounts.

When the taxpayer makes a payment on account of the taxes due from him that exceeds the amount of the tax pertaining to a single tax period, the payment shall be deemed a settlement of the tax period concerned and the remainder shall be deemed a payment on account of the taxes of other tax periods, pursuant to the provisions of Clause 2 of Article 54 of the Law, provided that the collection fine shall be calculated on the balance due.

When the taxpayer pays any amounts on account of the taxes due from him, and where the value of such amounts is insufficient to settle the full amount of the tax due, the amounts paid by him shall be allocated in accordance with the following rule:

First, the interest, then the late payment fines accrued up to the date of payment, then the assessment fines, if any, and thereafter the tax amounts; and the legal collection procedures shall be pursued with respect to the balance of the amounts remaining owed by the taxpayer after the payment transaction.

Upon settlement of the remaining balance, the late payment fine shall be calculated on the remaining balance as from the date of the last payment transaction.

In the event that there is a reduction of fines decided by the Ministry of Finance, the taxpayer shall benefit from the reduction of fines that is in force on the date of payment of the full tax (the tax + the interest + the fines). However, in the event that the amount paid is less than the tax due, this amount shall be recorded in trust at the Treasury until the payment of the full tax due, provided that the taxpayer shall benefit from the reduction of fines in force on the date of payment of the tax due, if any.

In the event that there is a tax due that is liable to lapse by prescription, the Administration shall be entitled to use the amounts paid on account of the taxes due in order to collect this tax without being bound by the allocation specified by the taxpayer.

Subject to the provisions relating to the payment by instalments of the transfer duty set forth in Legislative Decree No. 146/59, the taxpayer shall be entitled to submit to the tax administration an application for the payment by instalments of the additional tax due from him, whatever its nature, with the exception of taxes withheld at source, value added tax, and indirect taxes, provided that the value of the amount requested to be paid by instalments exceeds 1.000.000 L.L. (one million Lebanese Pounds) for individuals and 3.000.000 L.L. (three million Lebanese Pounds) for companies.

Without prejudice to the authority of the Director General of Finance to issue a decision determining the conditions required for approving applications to pay tax by instalments, the procedures for processing such applications shall be determined as follows:

1- The taxpayer or his representative shall submit a written application to pay the tax by instalments to the competent Collection Department or to the Taxpayer Services Sections in the districts in accordance with a form prepared by the Ministry of Finance indicating the taxpayer's name, his tax identification number, his full address, the total amount requested to be paid by instalments, and the type of tax.

2 - The application to pay the tax by instalments shall be accompanied by. -An undertaking from the concerned party, in accordance with a form prepared by the Ministry of Finance, to report to the competent Collection Department to be notified of the Administration's decision at the end of the prescribed statutory time limit.

- A copy of the legal power of attorney where required.

- A copy of the tax notice.

- Documents proving ownership of movable or immovable property and their value, provided that it is equal to at least twice the value of the tax requested to be paid by instalments, selected by the taxpayer for the purposes of placing an instalment encumbrance entry. -A copy of the commercial circular or the commercial register for companies, if any.

3- The competent Collection Department shall receive the application to pay the tax by instalments accompanied by the documents set out above and shall register it in a special computerised system for instalment applications maintained for this purpose.

4- The concerned party or his representative shall receive a receipt issued by the competent Collection Department indicating the number and date of receipt and the date of the subsequent follow-up fixed at ten working days following the date of submission of the application in order to be notified of the Administration's decision.

5- The competent Collection Department shall examine the application and refer it with its reasoned proposal for approval or rejection to the Head of the Tax Administration through the administrative hierarchy, accompanied by a statement of the types of taxes and fees due from the taxpayer up to the date of the application, stating the type, number and date of the assessment document.

6- The Head of the Tax Administration shall submit the application to the Director General of Finance with his reasoned proposal for approval or rejection.

7- The Director General of Finance shall decide on the instalment application and return it to the competent Collection Department.

8- The competent Collection Department, upon being notified of the approval or rejection of the instalment application, shall undertake the following:

a - In the event of rejection of the application: notifying the taxpayer in person of the rejection decision and the reasons therefor.

b - In the event of approval of the application:

- Notifying the taxpayer in person of the decision approving the instalment application immediately upon receipt of the decision.

- Drawing up the instalment schedule: the value of the first payment, the duration of the instalment plan, the interest rate, the number of instalments and the value of each of them, provided that the duration of the instalment plan does not exceed three years, within a time limit of two working days from the date on which the taxpayer is notified of the approval decision.

- Entering the information contained in the application into the computerised system dedicated to instalment applications in order to manage its operations.

- Issuing an instalment statement, in accordance with a form prepared by the Ministry of Finance, signed by the taxpayer in approval thereof, a payment notice for the first payment, and payment notices for the remaining instalments.

- Placing an instalment encumbrance entry on the taxpayer's movable and immovable property in an amount equal to at least twice the value of the tax paid by instalments.

Obligations of the taxpayer:

1- Receiving the payment notice for the first payment, and paying its value within a time limit of one week from the date on which he is notified of the notice, provided that it does not exceed the end of the month in which the instalment plan was approved, at the Treasury cash desk, or at one of the banks or their branches, or at one of the offices of LibanPost or any other company contracted by the Ministry of Finance for this purpose, and delivering the Administration's copy of the payment notice to the Collection Department, and receiving the instalment statement and the payment notices for the remaining instalments in return for his signature on the copy of the said statement as an acknowledgment of approval and receipt.

2 - Paying the value of the remaining instalments on the dates specified for them in the instalment schedule, under penalty of all instalments falling due.

3 - In cases where a specific reduction of fines applies, the taxpayer shall benefit from the settlement provided that the first payment of the tax paid by instalments is paid within the time limit specified for the reduction of fines.

In the event that the taxpayer defaults on paying any of the instalments together with the interest thereon up to the due date of the instalment on which he defaulted, and a collection fine shall be imposed on the value of the full amounts due together with the interest accrued up to the date of the instalment which the taxpayer refrained from paying, starting from the due date of the instalment on which he defaulted and up to the date of actual payment, while the taxpayer retains his right to the reduction of fines from which he benefited pursuant to the text in force on the date of the instalment plan.

The Collection Departments concerned shall be responsible for:

- Recording the number of the instalment application and the date of its approval on the electronic copies of the assessment documents.

- Deducting the value of the tax paid by instalments from the amounts due from the taxpayer his account.

- Preparing a special statement of status for the amounts paid by instalments for each tax separately, specifying the total of the amounts paid by instalments, the amounts paid of their principal, and the remaining amounts under collection.

Placing the instalment encumbrance entry The competent Collection Department must request the Directorate General of Real Estate Affairs, immediately upon issuing the instalment statement and by virtue of a letter, to place an instalment encumbrance entry in an amount equal to twice the value of the amounts paid by instalments, on specific real properties owned by the taxpayer in accordance with the order of priority specified by him in the application to pay the tax by instalments. The competent Collection Department must also request the Commercial Register, immediately upon issuing the instalment statement, to place an instalment encumbrance entry on the Commercial Register of the taxpayer (if any), in an amount equal to at least twice the value of the amounts paid by instalments.

The Directorate General of Real Estate Affairs and the competent Secretariat of the Commercial Register shall notify the Collection Unit of the placement of the encumbrance entry by virtue of a letter that shall be attached to the instalment file. Upon payment of all due instalments, the Collection Department shall address a letter to lift the instalment encumbrance entry to the Directorate General of Real Estate Affairs or the competent Secretariat of the Commercial Register.

If the taxpayer requests to pay the entire remaining balance in a single lump sum, a collection collection receipt shall be issued in the value of the principal of the amount due plus the interest accrued for the period extending from the date of the last instalment up to the date of actual payment, a fraction of a month being considered a full month.

The competent Collection Department shall place an instalment encumbrance entry on the movable and immovable property in accordance with what is stated above relating to instalment applications approved prior to the date of publication of this Decision.

Upon the occurrence of an infringement involving one or more documents common to several taxes, the highest fine shall be applied to the tax difference. In the event of the occurrence of several infringements relating to a single tax, the fine prescribed for it by law shall be applied to each infringement.

The occurrence of an infringement involving one or more documents common to several taxes means all infringements for which the imposition of a fine is repeated in more than one tax law.

Delay in or failure to submit the required declarations or statements, or to pay the taxes due thereon, shall not be considered an infringement involving one or more common documents, as the fine resulting therefrom shall be due on each infringement.

In the event that the said infringement affects the tax base, the competent finance department that discovered the infringement shall apply the fine prescribed for it by law. This department shall document the said fine on the adopted automated system and archive it, in order to facilitate the possibility of assessing the fine difference when auditing another tax.
All decisions, circulars, memoranda and instructions that are inconsistent with the provisions of this Decision are repealed.
This Decision shall be published in the Official Gazette and on the website of the Ministry of Finance, and shall enter into force on the date of its publication.
Decree No. 82 dated 11/4/1977 concerning the authorisation granted to Mr. Mohammad Moussa Taher Fadlallah, of Lebanese nationality, to acquire Nigerian nationality is hereby repealed.
This Decree shall be published and notified where needed.
The Lebanese University shall adopt the semester system in teaching, and the academic year shall be divided into two semesters, the duration of each of which shall be fifteen weeks.

The teaching system shall adopt the course as a basic educational unit. Each course shall cover a set of lessons and educational activities specialised in a single subject over the span of one academic semester, and shall be equivalent to a number of credits.

A credit shall constitute a unit of measurement for assessing the total effort exerted by the student in his academic attainment, and it is equivalent to:

A - Approximately 10 hours of theoretical lessons in the Licence and 7 hours in the Master's.

B - Between 10 hours and 15 hours for directed work.

C - Between 15 hours and 20 hours for practical work.

D - Between 40 hours and 60 hours for training courses.

Academic advising in each university unit or university branch shall be undertaken by professors assigned by a decision of the Head of the Unit upon the proposal of its council, and they shall be selected every two years from among the members of the teaching staff in the cadre and full-time contractors, and when necessary, recourse may be had to hourly teaching contractors. Academic advising shall cover introducing students to the adopted teaching system and the specialisations of the university unit, and providing advice and guidance in choosing specialised tracks and academic courses.

The Lebanese University shall prepare its students to obtain the following degrees:

1 - The Licence:

The duration of its preparation shall not be less than three years, and shall not exceed five years as a maximum limit. This duration shall be calculated starting from the first administrative registration in the specialisation.

2 - The Master's:

Which is of two types, research and professional; the duration of its preparation shall not be less than two years and shall not exceed four years as a maximum limit, such duration being calculated starting from the first administrative registration in the specialisation.

3 - The Doctorate:

The duration of its preparation shall not be less than three years and shall not exceed five years.

In exceptional cases, following the approval of the President of the University, the student may be permitted to register for one additional year in each of these degrees.

The Licence degree shall consist of one hundred and eighty credits (180) distributed over six (6) academic semesters at an average of thirty credits (30) per single semester, provided that the teaching hours required to obtain the Licence degree shall not be less than one thousand and six hundred hours.

In addition to the general conditions stipulated in Law No. 75/67 dated 26/12/1967 and its amendments, each university unit shall determine the special conditions for the admission of students to prepare for the Licence degree by a decision of the University Council upon the recommendation of the Unit Council.

The courses that constitute the Licence degree shall be classified as follows:

1 - Compulsory courses:

The total of their credits may not be less than one hundred and thirty-five credits, and they are of two types:

A - Specialised compulsory courses: which are the courses that the student must complete as part of the graduation requirements in the required specialisation and are determined in the adopted curriculum schedule.

B - General compulsory courses: which are courses binding on all students of the Lebanese University and are determined by a decision of the University Council, provided that they include the headquarters of "Human Rights" and on condition that the total of their credits does not exceed six.

2 - Elective courses:

The total of their credits ranges between twenty and forty credits, chosen by the student from within a specified list comprising courses in the field of the required specialisation or other specialisations in the same university unit.

3 - Free courses:

The total of their credits ranges between three and ten credits, in which the freedom is left to the student to choose the course from among the courses specified in the units of the Lebanese University.

The Master's degree shall consist of one hundred and twenty credits (120) distributed over four (4) academic semesters at an average of thirty credits (30) per single semester, provided that the teaching hours required to obtain the Master's degree shall not be less than six hundred hours.

Each university unit shall determine the conditions for the admission of students to prepare for the research and professional Master's degree by a decision of the University Council upon the recommendation of the Unit Council.

The curriculum of the research Master's degree shall include a research thesis, and the curriculum of the professional Master's shall include a field study or a training period in the field of specialisation of not less than eight weeks, (250 working hours as a minimum limit) and shall culminate in a thesis prepared by the student.

The number of credits allocated to the thesis shall not exceed thirty credits.
The President of the University, upon the proposal of the Head of the University Unit, shall appoint a committee to examine the Master's thesis.

The student shall undertake two types of registration:

- Administrative registration, which takes place at the beginning of the academic year,

- And academic registration, which takes place at the beginning of each academic semester, whereby the student specifies the courses he wishes to pursue during this semester.

If the student fails in some courses or defaults on them in previous semesters, he must register starting from the third semester in these courses, and complete his registration in the remaining courses according to the sequence of their distribution over the academic semesters, on condition that the total credits registered in the semester do not exceed thirty-six credits.

Each university unit shall determine in its regulations the special conditions for the attendance of students, provided that the percentage of attendance in directed or practical work out of the total hours prescribed for such work shall not be less than 60% in each course separately in the university units that adopt the entrance examination system.

The continuous assessment system and the semester final examinations system shall be adopted in all courses pertaining to each semester, and the duration of the prescribed final examination shall not exceed two hours.

Final examinations for each course shall be held at the end of the semester, provided that students who fail in the first session shall benefit from a second session the date of which shall be determined by a decision of the Unit Council.

Practical courses of a special nature, such as practical work, workshops, practical projects, training..., which are subject to a special assessment system determined in the regulations of each university unit, shall be exempted from the provisions of the two preceding Articles.

The rules for composing the final grade for each course subject to a semester final examination shall be determined in the regulations of each university unit, provided that the percentage allocated to continuous assessment shall not be less than 20% and shall not exceed 40% of the final grade of the course.

A student shall be considered successful in a given course and shall consequently obtain the credits allocated to it if he obtains a final grade equal to at least 50/100, or a grade below 50 and not less than 40 on condition that he has completed his registration in all the courses of the semester and obtained a weighted general average of not less than 55/100.

If a student fails in a given course as a result of the first session examinations, he shall retain the continuous assessment grade for the second session, and the final grade in this case shall consist of the continuous assessment grade and the second session grade of the final examination.

The grading scale according to the credit system shall be used to indicate the hierarchical level of the student in the courses in accordance with the following table:

(See attachment file)

I - Grading scale according to the credit system at the Lebanese University.

II - Percentage of successful students in each grade according to the grading scale adopted at the Lebanese University.

III - Number of points for the grade on the scale of 5 according to the credit system at the Lebanese University.

Each university unit shall determine in its regulations the specialisations specific to its field of knowledge. Each specialisation may branch out into several specialised tracks.

Specialised tracks shall be established, abolished and amended by a decision of the University Council upon the proposal of the Unit Council.

Each university unit shall determine the conditions for recognising credits obtained in other units of the Lebanese University or in other universities by a decision of the Head of the Unit upon the recommendation of its council, provided that they do not conflict with general equivalence regulations laid down by the University Council.

In implementation of the provisions of this Decree and in application of the L.M.D education system, the specialisations, curricula and programmes specific to each university unit shall be established and amended by a decision of the University Council upon the recommendation of the Unit Council.

Where the University Council is unable to convene, the President of the University shall act on its behalf, provided that his decision is coupled with the approval of the Minister of Education and Higher Education.

In addition to the provisions of the fifth Article of this Decree (Scale of Degrees), the units of the Lebanese University may, in accordance with professional necessities and requirements, grant university degrees after the Bachelor's degree or after the Master's degree, each comprising sixty credits. Certain units of the University (Engineering, Medical Sciences, Dentistry, Pharmacy...) may also grant university degrees in a specialisation, provided that these degrees, their conditions and their designations are determined by a decision issued by the University Council.
Every text contrary to the provisions of this Decree or inconsistent with its content is hereby repealed.
This Decree shall be published and notified where needed.

The Comprehensive Master Plan for the Arrangement of the Lebanese Territory (1) constitutes the general guiding framework for urban planning and land uses in Lebanon.

1 - The aforementioned Plan and Maps Nos. 1, 2 and 3 attached thereto are available at the Council for Development and Reconstruction.
Ministries, administrations, public institutions, autonomous services and municipalities are bound to comply with this Plan in every matter of their work relating to land uses and planning.

Decrees and regulations defining land uses, issued prior to the issuance of this Decree, in particular master plans and detailed regulations for cities and villages, shall remain in force so long as they have not been amended. The administration concerned shall, when studying decrees and regulations and submitting proposals relating to land arrangement, observe the provisions of this Decree, and should that prove impossible, by referring the matter to the Minister or the Council of Ministers in accordance with the competencies.

The urban planning policy in Lebanon, within the framework of the Comprehensive Master Plan for Land Arrangement, is based on the use of land in accordance with its nature, its characteristics, and the hazards that may arise from the manner of its use.

The classification of the Lebanese territory in accordance with what is stated in the Plan and in Schedule "A" attached to this Decree is as follows:

U: Urban areas.

R: Rural areas.

A: Areas of national agricultural wealth.

N: Areas of national natural wealth, distributed as follows:

N1: Peak areas.

N2: The Lebanese cedar line and mountain orchards.

N3: Areas of continuity of woodlands, valleys and other natural areas.

The following distinctive sites and areas are indicated as stated in the Plan and in Schedule "B" attached to this Decree as follows:

P: Major natural landscapes.

S: Distinctive archaeological, historical and natural sites and complexes distributed as follows:

S1: Classified archaeological sites and complexes

S2: Classified natural sites and complexes.

Areas exposed to natural hazards are indicated in accordance with what is stated in the Plan and in Schedule "C" attached to this Decree as follows:

F: Areas exposed to floods.

G: Areas exposed to hazards of soil slippage and landslides.

W: Areas exposed to the hazard of groundwater pollution.

The guidelines provided for in the attached Schedules "A" "B" and "C" shall apply to every part of the Lebanese territory within the limits provided for in the third Article of this Decree. In cases where an area is concerned, at the same time, with natural characteristics and hazards, in accordance with Articles 6 and 7, then the strictest guidelines among those stated in Schedules "A" "B" and "C" attached to this Decree shall apply thereto.

The Lebanese Administration shall work, within the framework of the laws and regulations in force, to preserve the natural and heritage landmarks of the sites existing along the Lebanese coast, and to preserve historical sites in accordance with what is stated in the Plan.

An administrative committee shall be formed under the chairmanship of the President of the Higher Council for Urban Planning, comprising representatives from the Directorates General in the Ministries and Institutions listed below, and a member designated by the Director General of each of the following Directorates or the President in respect of Public Institutions shall be appointed:

- Ministry of Public Works and Transport: The Directorate General of Urban Planning, of Roads and Buildings, and of Transport.

- Ministry of Environment: The Directorate General of Environment.

- Ministry of Culture: The Directorate General of Antiquities.

- Ministry of Interior and Municipalities: The Directorate General of Local Administrations and Councils.

As from the date of entry into force of this Decree, the following bases and rules shall apply in respect of the settlement of the hospitalization and treatment expenses of the injured third party:

1 - The insurance shall pay the hospitalization and treatment expenses of the injured third party.

2 - The insurer may only be bound within the limits of the coverage provided for in the compulsory insurance contract.

3 - The insurer shall pay the hospitalization and treatment expenses within a period not exceeding thirty days from the date of issuance of the invoices or in accordance with the agreements signed between the hospital and the insurance company.

In the event of the occurrence of a traffic accident resulting in bodily injury to a third party, the following provisions shall apply:

a - In the event of the involvement of two or more vehicles in the accident, all of which are insured, each insurance company shall undertake the settlement of a proportion of the total hospitalization expenses equivalent to the quotient of this total divided by the number of cars involved in the accident, on a provisional basis, either until the dispute is resolved amicably directly between the insurance companies or, failing an amicable settlement of the dispute, until the issuance of a final judgment by the competent courts determining the liabilities.

b - If the accident resulting from a single insured vehicle leads to the injury of a third-party person, the insurer shall be obliged to pay the full hospitalization expenses to the hospital on a provisional basis until the issuance of a final judgment by the competent courts finally determining the liabilities, and without this settlement being considered an admission of liability by the insurer, so that he remains entitled to his right of recourse against any person against whom he is permitted to have recourse.

c - In the event of the involvement of two or more vehicles in the accident, one or some of which are uninsured, each insurer shall settle a proportion of the value of the hospitalization invoice equal to the quotient of the value of this invoice divided by the number of cars involved in the accident, on a provisional basis until the issuance of a final judgment by the competent courts finally determining the liabilities, while reserving for the insurers the right of recourse against the owner of the uninsured vehicle or vehicles.

The courts shall not be bound by the proportions provided for in the second Article of this Decree, such that these proportions shall be considered provisional and non-final until they are determined pursuant to an irrevocable judicial judgment.

The insuring companies shall, following the amicable resolution of the dispute among themselves, or, in the event of recourse to the courts, following the issuance of the final judgment by the competent courts which determines the liabilities incumbent upon each insurance company, carry out an accounting or set-off among themselves.
The insurers shall have the right of recourse against any natural or legal person against whom recourse is legally permissible.
This Decree shall enter into force as from the date of its publication in the Official Gazette.
