13 - 2 Each board shall be given a number, and if it is double-faced, the face facing

the road shall be designated A and the second face Z.

13 - 3 If there are two boards adjacent to one another, the board adjacent to the road shall be designated A and the inner one B, provided that its back is designated Y.

Removal or Modification of the Installation Site of Advertising Boards

In order to preserve public order, or when executing a building line plan, expropriation, or road widening, the Administration may remove or modify the installation site of advertising boards without the owner of the board having the right to claim any compensation of any kind whatsoever. In the event that the owner of the board refuses to remove it or to carry out the required modification, the board shall be dismantled under the responsibility and at the expense of the owner of the board, provided that the Administration refunds to him the difference in the fee due for the remaining period of the term of the licence after deducting the cost of dismantling the board.

Erection, Maintenance and Dismantling of Advertising Boards

15 - 1 The advertising board must be erected in a technical manner that resists storms and winds in order to preserve public safety, under the responsibility of the owner of the board.

15 - 2 It shall be incumbent upon the owner of the advertising board to ensure its maintenance on a continuous basis. In the event of an infringement, the Administration shall have the right to address a formal notice to the owner of the board requiring its maintenance within a time limit of 10 days if its condition so requires; otherwise, it shall be dismantled at his expense and under his responsibility. The Administration may also compel the owner of the board to dismantle the board immediately at his expense and under his responsibility in the event that its condition is not fit for rehabilitation and maintenance.

15 - 3 The owner of the advertising board is prohibited from throwing remnants of old posters under the boards. In the event of an infringement, a formal notice shall be addressed to him by the Administration, and in the event of repetition of the infringement, the licence shall be cancelled under the responsibility of the owner of the board and the old posters shall be delivered to recycling companies.

15 - 4 The owner of the advertising board is prohibited from throwing leaflets, notices, remnants of advertisements removed from the boards, and the like on public roads and in their vicinity.

15 - 5 The owner of the advertising board must not leave ropes and plastic ties hanging from the advertising boards (unipole) and must not throw them on the ground, and they must be removed.

15 - 6 Upon dismantling the board, its owner must repave the sidewalk or restore the ground to the condition in which it was previously by removing all remnants of the iron base, including bolts and conduits (fourreaux) or the neck of the pole which may cause bodily harm to passers-by; otherwise, all these remnants shall be removed at the expense and under the responsibility of the owner of the board.

Removal of Infringements

16 - 1 The Competent Administration shall address to the owners of boards that are in infringement of the provisions of this Decree a letter requiring the removal of the infringement within a time limit of 10 days, under pain of the Administration removing the infringement under their responsibility and at their expense.

16 - 2 The Competent Administration shall notify the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities in writing of the existence of the infringement simultaneously with its addressing the letter mentioned in Clause /16 - 1/ above, and shall also notify it upon the removal of the infringement.

16 - 3 The costs due for dismantling the infringing boards shall be collected pursuant to collection orders issued by the Administration competent to grant the licences, and the Competent Administration shall also have the right to request the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities for this purpose to liquidate the bank guarantee mentioned in Article Ten of this Decree.

16 - 4 The Competent Administration shall remove unlicensed advertisements at the expense and under the responsibility of their owner without any prior formal notice.
Article 17: Repeal of Contrary Provisions Decree No. /8861/ dated 25/7/1996 is hereby repealed, as are all texts that contravene the provisions of this Decree or are inconsistent with its content.

Transitional Provisions

18 - 1 Owners of advertisements subject to the provisions of this Decree that were licensed prior to its issuance and that remain in force shall regularise their status in accordance with the conditions stipulated in this Decree within a period of three months, without any additional fee being incurred thereby for the remaining period of the licence.

The competent administrations shall not grant any new licence in accordance with the provisions of this Decree within a period of three months from the date of its issuance.

18 - 2 Owners of licensed advertisements that remain in force prior to the issuance of this Decree and whose advertisements are not capable of regularisation shall remove them within a period of 10 days from the date of being notified thereof, failing which they shall be removed at their expense and under their responsibility. The fees collected for the period preceding their removal shall be deemed the right of the administration, and the difference in the fee for the remaining period of the licence shall be refunded to the concerned party. The costs due for the removal of the advertisements shall be collected pursuant to collection orders issued by the administration competent to grant the licences.
This Decree shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The Master Plan and the General Detailed Regulations for the real estate areas of Batroun, Kfar Khollos, Basbina and Kouba (District of Batroun), comprising the division of zones in accordance with the map drawn to a scale of 1/5000 and annexed to this Decree, are hereby approved. This Plan shall be subject to the regulations governing construction, subdivision, land pooling and reparceling, and exploitation, and to the general and special conditions annexed to this Decree, which shall be deemed an integral part thereof.
Every previous plan contrary to the provisions of this Decree is hereby repealed.
This Decree shall be published and notified wherever required.
All drinking water treatment, purification and bottling plants shall be subject to the provisions of this Decision.
It is prohibited to operate any plant prior to obtaining a prior licence in accordance with the conditions set forth in this Decision.

The owner of the plant shall submit an application to the Registry of the Ministry of Public Health according to a specified form, or to the licensing departments in the Central Administration and in the regional departments affiliated with the Ministry of Industry pursuant to Decree No. 8018, together with a copy of the complete file accompanied by the following documents:

. A copy of the applicant's identity card (or a work permit if he is a foreigner),

. A commercial circular and a certificate of registration (if it is a company or an establishment),

. A plan at a scale of 1/100 showing all the arrangements inside the plant, signed by an engineer registered with the Order of Engineers,

. A subdivision plan of the real property within which the plant is located,

. A real estate certificate for the section concerned and the common sections, dated no more than three months earlier,

. A planning and easement certificate, dated no more than three months earlier,

. A certified true copy of the occupancy permit or any document proving the legality of the building,

. A lease agreement certified by the municipality, or a copy of the title deed, or a tolerance agreement before a Notary Public,

. An undertaking before a Notary Public to carry out all the analyses set forth in Law No. 210/2012,

. A copy of the licence to exploit the source of the water supplied to the plant, together with the agreement contract between the owner of the plant and the owner of the water source,

. A list of the equipment and devices specifying their specifications,

. A statement of the manufacturing method and the manner of disposal of liquid and solid waste,

. The scientific prospectus of the containers and caps specifying their sizes,

. A sample of the label intended to be used,

Submitted applications shall be received and the availability of the documents shall be verified in accordance with the powers of the units concerned in each of the Ministries of Public Health and Industry after payment of the verification fee approved at the Ministry of Industry.

A special committee shall be formed to examine drinking water files by a joint decision issued by the Ministers of Public Health and Industry, whose mission shall be to examine the licensing files within a time limit of one and a half months for an establishment licence, two weeks for an exploitation licence, and two months for an establishment and exploitation licence if the establishment is existing and operating prior to the issuance of this Decision, and to submit them through official channels to the Ministers of Public Health and Industry for determination.
The licence shall be granted by a joint decision issued by the Ministers of Public Health and Industry.
Upon exploiting the plant, compliance with the conditions set forth in Annexes 1, 2 and 3 and the Guiding Annex attached to Law No. 210/2012 shall be observed.

Owners of unlicensed plants currently operating shall be granted a time limit of ten days from the date of issuance of this Decision to submit applications to the Ministry of Public Health or Industry to regularise their status.

The plant shall be closed immediately by a joint decision of the Ministers of Public Health and Industry if it becomes apparent to the inspectors of the Ministry of Health that the drinking water bottled therein does not conform to the required characteristics.
Letter No. 528/S2 of the Ministry of Energy and Water dated 11/8/2015 regarding the exploitation of well water, its sale and the monitoring of quantities shall be taken into consideration.
This Decision shall enter into force immediately upon its issuance and until the issuance of the implementing decrees relating to Law No. 210/2012, and shall be communicated wherever needed.

The scope of application of the provisions of this Law shall include:

1 - All types of foodstuffs and beverages in their various types and categories, including water.

2 - All substances used in the operations of manufacturing, transforming,

preparing, packaging, processing and marketing food.

3 - All agricultural products, including those that enter into the preparation or manufacture of food even if they are not considered food in themselves.

There shall be excluded from the scope of application of the provisions of this Law:

1 - Medicines, raw materials used in the manufacture of medicines, and cosmetics, as defined in the Law on the Practice of the Profession of Pharmacy.

2 - Tobacco and tumbak in their various types and the materials manufactured therefor.

3 - Foodstuffs and beverages prepared and stored in homes for personal consumption.

4 - Food supplements and raw materials used in their manufacture.

The Draft Law relating to Food Safety as amended by the Joint Parliamentary Committees has been approved.

This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Definitions and Terms:

For the application of the provisions of this Law, the following definitions and terms shall be adopted:

«Food» (Food): Every product, raw primary material, or partially or wholly processed primary material intended for human consumption, including water, beverages in their various types and categories, chewing gum, and all substances used in manufacturing, preparing, packaging, processing and marketing food.

«Risk» (Risk): The adverse effects on health resulting from food and its products that are likely to occur, and the severity thereof on humans, animals and the environment.

«Hazard» (Hazard): Every biological, chemical, or physical food element or agent capable of causing adverse effects on the health and safety of humans, animals and the environment.

«Label» (Label): Every sticker, mark, picture, or any other information written, printed, drawn, placed, engraved or stamped on food product containers, or attached thereto.

«Animals» (Animals): Animals intended for human consumption.

«Professional» (Professional): Is the natural or legal person, from the private or public sector, who imports, manufactures, transforms, packs, wraps, cans, distributes, transports, stores, refrigerates, preserves, sells or delivers to the consumer food, feed, pesticides, veterinary medicines or fertilisers, whether any of these acts are performed free of charge or for consideration.

«Farmer» (Farmer): Is the natural or legal person, from the private or public sector, who practises a productive agricultural activity in both its plant and animal branches or in either of them.

«Food enterprise» (Food enterprise): Shall include all enterprises, whatever their legal form, including farms, slaughterhouses, hotels, restaurants, factories and shops intended for direct sale to the consumer, which engage in all or some of the following acts: producing, storing, refrigerating, preserving, selling or delivering food directly to the consumer, whether these acts are performed free of charge or for consideration. This expression shall include farms, slaughterhouses, hotels, restaurants, factories and shops intended for direct sale to the consumer. This definition shall also include enterprises for the production of feed, pesticides, veterinary medicines and fertilisers.

«Sale»: The offering or possession of food for the purpose of selling or distributing it, free of charge or for consideration, shall be considered a sale of food within the meaning of this Law.

«Conformity» (Conformity): The fulfilment by food and its products of the requirements of the relevant specifications or technical regulations.

«Pollution» (pollution): The exposure of food to natural, chemical, physical, biological or human factors rendering it unfit for consumption or harmful to human health and life, whether the pollution occurred directly or indirectly.

«The Commission» (FSLC): The «Food Safety Lebanese Commission» (Food Safety Lebanese Commission) established pursuant to Article 22 of this Law.

«Traceability» (Traceability): The monitoring, documenting and tracking of food through all stages of its production or importation, transport, transformation or manufacture, storage and distribution.

«Risk Analysis» (Risk Analysis): A system consisting of three interconnected elements: risk assessment, risk management and risk communication.

«Risk Assessment» (Risk Assessment): A scientifically based process consisting of the following steps: hazard identification, hazard characterisation, and exposure assessment.

«Risk Management» (Risk Management): The process of determining the policies to be followed through consultation among the concerned parties, with respect to the results of risk assessment and other relevant factors, and taking the appropriate measures for prevention and control.

«Risk Communication» (Risk Communication): The exchange and interaction of information and opinions following the risk analysis process, with respect to the source of the hazard and risk-related factors, among risk assessors, risk managers, suppliers of food products, academics and other concerned parties, and subsequently informing the public of those risks.

«Quality» (Quality): The quality of food or food ingredients capable of meeting the needs of the consumer or professional, and which renders the food suitable for consumption, or which meets the conditions and specifications relating to quality issued by the concerned administrations,

«Food Inspector» (Food Inspector): Every person who works on behalf of the Food Safety Lebanese Commission to carry out the inspection tasks provided for in this Law.

Each of the professional, the farmer and the enterprise, each within the scope of their work, shall verify that the produced or imported food which they place at the disposal of the consumer conforms to the adopted specifications, is safe and fit for human consumption, and does not result in any harm to the health of humans, animals or the environment if such consumption takes place properly and appropriately according to the nature of such food.

Food shall be considered safe if its consumption, in a normal and appropriate manner, provides the guarantees of safety and protection expected of it on the basis of:

1 - The ingredients of the food, particularly the substances of which it consists and the procedures of packing, canning, preservation and transport.

2 - The manner of its presentation or display and the information included on the sticker (identification card).

Food shall also be considered safe if it meets the national specifications. In the absence of national specifications, international specifications recognised in Lebanon shall be adopted, particularly those established by the «Codex Alimentarius Commission» in the «Food Code» (Codex Aliment Arius).

Food shall be considered unsafe or harmful to the health of humans and animals, by way of example and not limitation, in the following cases:

1 - If it contains toxic substances or substances harmful to public health.

2 - If one or more of the substances of which it consists constitutes a hazard to public health.

3 - If it does not meet the adopted specifications or was manufactured in violation of the laws and regulations.

4 - If it is prepared wholly or partially from animals that are either diseased or slaughtered in places that do not meet the conditions provided for in the laws and regulations in force.

The local and international laboratories, accreditation agencies, and offices of inspection and pre-inspection whose certificates relating to food safety are recognised in Lebanon shall be determined in accordance with the laws and regulations in force.

* First: The professional or establishment shall, each within the scope of their work:

1 - Refrain from trading in food that does not conform to the approved specifications.

2 - Exercise their activity in places where general safety and hygiene conditions are satisfied.

3 - Take the necessary precautions to prevent food contamination during its importation, manufacturing, processing, packing, canning, wrapping, distribution, transport, storage, sale, display, preparation, serving, or direct delivery to the consumer.

4 - Use suitable and safe materials in packing, wrapping, or canning food that prevent its contamination during its transport, display, refrigeration, or preservation.

5 - Store food in places where the necessary conditions to maintain its safety and quality are satisfied.

6 - Display or serve food to the consumer in a manner that prevents its contamination.

7 - Provide the basic information relating to manufactured or processed food in accordance with the legal procedures and regulations relating to food safety.

8 - Obtain the necessary licences to exercise their activity where the laws and regulations require obtaining such licences.

* Second: The professional and the establishment shall comply with the obligations mentioned above when carrying out any activity involving feed, fertilisers, pesticides, and veterinary medicines.

The farmer shall:

1 - Use pesticides, veterinary medicines, fertilisers, or feed in a manner that does not result in any contamination of food or harm to the health and life of humans or animals or to the environment, and comply with the conditions of their use.

2 - Maintain the safety and quality of plant or animal production and take the necessary measures to prevent its contamination for so long as it remains in his possession.

3 - Provide the Ministry of Agriculture, the professional, and the Authority, upon the request of each of them, with the information relating to the fertilisers, pesticides, veterinary medicines, and feed that he has used during the exercise of his agricultural activity.

4 - Notify the professional with whom he deals, the "Authority", and the concerned administration at the Ministry of Agriculture, within 48 hours at most, of the diseases that have affected agricultural products and/or animals and the manner adopted in treating them.

5 - Obtain the necessary licences to practise his activity where the laws and regulations require obtaining such licences.

Each of the farmer, the professional, or the establishment shall protect food and feed from contamination during transport from one place to another in accordance with the approved conditions for food safety.
Establishments engaged in equipping means intended for the transport of food or feed shall use materials that are non-toxic and easy to clean and maintain.

The conditions that must be satisfied in the means intended for the transport of food and feed, vehicles, and shipping containers, whether with respect to technical conditions or with respect to their maintenance and cleaning to preserve food safety, shall be determined by decisions issued by the "Authority" in coordination with the concerned ministries and administrations.
Each of the professional, the farmer, or the establishment shall comply with the conditions of general safety and hygiene when displaying food for the purpose of selling it directly to the consumer.

The special conditions for displaying a specific food shall be determined by decisions issued by the "Authority" in coordination with the concerned ministries and administrations, in particular, by way of example and not limitation, with respect to the following obligations:

Food products must be displayed or presented to the consumer in accordance with the provisions of the laws relating to labelling, and the promotion and presentation of food products, including the shape, appearance, wrapping, canning, and wrapping materials used, and the manner of their display, provided that the information relating to these food products does not mislead the consumer.

Labels shall be affixed in the appropriate manner to ensure the conformity of the display of the food with its content.

1 - The farmer shall keep registers in which he records the fertilisers, pesticides, veterinary

medicines, and feed that he has used during the exercise of his agricultural activity, their source, and the date of their use.

2 - The farmer shall provide the professional with whom he deals, the "Authority", or the concerned administration at the Ministry of Agriculture, upon the request of each of them, with the information recorded in the registers mentioned above.

1 - The professional or establishment shall keep registers in which they record all information relating to the operations of importing or manufacturing food, its source, and its processing, packing, wrapping, canning, distribution, transport, storage, refrigeration, preservation, display, preparation, serving, or sale to the consumer, as well as all information relating to the materials used during those operations, including additives, in particular preservatives, colourings, and enhancers.

2 - The professional shall provide the person with whom he dealt, the "Authority", or the concerned administrations in the competent ministries, upon the request of each of them, with the information recorded in the registers mentioned above.

Each of the farmer and the professional shall:

1 - Keep a register showing the persons or establishments with whom he deals and detailed

information on the commercial transactions, including the number and date of the production batch and the quantity.

2 - Notify the "Authority" and the concerned ministries and administrations within 48 hours at most of any contamination affecting food or agricultural or animal products and the measures he has taken to address the same.

The "Authority", in coordination with the concerned ministries and administrations, shall determine the registers and documents that the professional, the farmer, or the establishment must keep, the information that they must contain, and the duration of their retention.

The information determined by the competent administration in coordination with the "Authority" shall be included on food labels or packing according to the nature of each food and its characteristics and in accordance with the applicable specifications, and, where applicable, the side effects of the food on one or more categories of consumers.

The provisions of this Article shall not cover unpacked food sold in bulk trade (mal al-qabban), unless a decision issued by the Authority determines the information that must be made available to the consumer.
The Ministry of Agriculture, in coordination with the Authority, shall determine the standards that must be satisfied in genetically modified foods.

The conditions that must be satisfied in vending machines (Distributeur automatique) intended for filling, packing, distributing, and transporting food shall be determined pursuant to decisions issued by the Authority.

Precautionary measures shall be taken in accordance with the following:

1 - Where sufficient and approved scientific bases for risk assessment are not available, the concerned administrations shall in such cases take precautionary measures pending the obtention of further scientific data necessary for taking the decision, with the necessity of announcing the same if confirmed.

2 - Where sufficient scientific bases and the required and approved data for risk assessment are available, the Authority shall issue its decision and inform the competent ministries and concerned administrations of the proposed measures to address the risk under consideration and to take the appropriate measures, including announcement.

3 - In application of the principle of transparency: the concerned administrations shall inform public opinion of the potential risks to which the consumer may be exposed as a result of consuming a specific food product, and specify the nature of such risks, how to prevent them, and the measures that must be taken.

There shall be established pursuant to this Law a commission known as the "Food Safety Lebanese Commission" Food Safety Lebanese Commission (the Commission) (FSLC), enjoying legal personality and financial and administrative autonomy, and the Commission shall be linked to the President of the Council of Ministers, who shall exercise the supervisory authority over it.

The "Commission" shall be subject to the provisions of Decree No. 4517 dated 13/12/1972 and its amendments (the General Regulations of Public Institutions), in all that does not conflict with the provisions of this Law and the provisions of its own regulations. It shall also be subject to the oversight of the Central Inspection and the ex-post audit of the Court of Accounts.

Subject to the provisions of Article 54 of Law No. 583 dated 23/4/2004 (the General Budget and Annexed Budgets for the year 2004), the Commission shall not be subject to the oversight of the Civil Service Board.

The decision-making authority in the Commission shall be vested in a Board of Directors composed of seven members appointed for a term of five years by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers from among persons of competence and expertise in the activities related to food safety.

Diversity of specialisations shall be observed in the formation of the Board of Directors.

There shall be designated in the decree of appointment from among the members a Chairman and a Vice-Chairman, each of whom fulfils the special conditions set forth in Schedule No. (2) annexed to this Law, and who shall work full-time for the business of the "Commission".

Neither the full-time Chairman nor the full-time Vice-Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Commission may combine his office with any parliamentary or municipal membership, or public office, or any activity in any enterprise whatever its nature or legal form, or any professional work, whether such activity is for remuneration or gratuitous. Furthermore, the Chairman, his Vice-Chairman and every member of the Board of Directors of the Commission are prohibited from owning, wholly or partially, enterprises subject to the provisions of this Law or from participating therein.

The service of each of the Chairman, Vice-Chairman and members of the Board of Directors of the "Commission" may be terminated at any time by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, upon a reasoned proposal by the President of the Council of Ministers.

The allowances for attending the meetings of the Board of Directors of the "Commission" shall be determined pursuant to a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers.

The Board of Directors of the "Commission" shall lay down, pursuant to decisions issued by it, the regulations of the "Commission", in particular:

The internal rules of procedure for the work of the Commission,

The organisation of the "Commission" (structure and establishment plan) and the laying down of the schedules and special conditions pertaining thereto.

The staff regulations, the conditions of contracting, and the conduct of competitive examinations to fill the posts specified in the establishment plan of the "Commission".

The financial regulations.

The manner in which the supervisory authority exercises its powers.

These decisions shall enter into force after their approval by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers.

The resources of the "Commission" shall consist of:

1 - The appropriations allocated to it in the General Budget.

2 - The Treasury advances assigned to it.

3 - The revenues and fees resulting from the activities of the Commission.

4 - Grants, bequests and donations.

5 - Any other resources that may be provided for pursuant to special legal texts.

The "Commission" shall undertake the following tasks:

1 - Approving and/or proposing the texts necessary for the implementation of the provisions of this Law.

2 - Determining the conditions and procedures for monitoring the execution of the provisions of this Law and its implementing texts.

3 - Exercising the powers set forth in this Law.

4 - Taking the decisions necessary to put into execution the general policy for food safety approved by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers based on the recommendation of the Commission.

5 - Coordinating among the competent ministries and the administrations concerned for the execution of the provisions of this Law and its implementing texts.

6 - Participating in the preparation of draft standards and technical regulations related to food, pesticides, veterinary medicines, feed and fertilisers, and proposing the issuance or amendment of these standards and technical regulations.

7 - Participating in laying down the criteria related to food safety on the basis

of scientific information and after assessing the risks that may result from the consumption of a certain food or the use of pesticides or feed.

8 - Preparing studies, research and statistics related to food safety.

9 - Holding seminars and issuing bulletins and all other publications dealing with food safety.

10 - Undertaking the operation of traceability (traceability) of the food chain in all its stages in order to be able to analyse the risks of the food safety chain in coordination with the competent administrations to record every violation of the provisions of this Law.

11 - Establishing and managing a rapid alert system for monitoring health and food risks and securing the required informational communication among all those concerned with these risks at the national, regional and international levels.

12 - Analysing the risks that may result from the consumption of a certain food.

13 - Collecting and analysing scientific and technical information related to food safety.

14 - Monitoring the operation of tracing and transforming food, or packing, wrapping, canning, distributing, transporting, storing, refrigerating, preserving, selling, preparing, serving, displaying or delivering it to the consumer in order to record every violation of the provisions of this Law, in accordance with a mechanism determining the health conditions and the monitoring and traceability operations, issued by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the supervisory authority based on the opinion of the Board of Directors of the Commission.

15 - Taking selective samples of food products, whether through the inspectors of the Commission or at the request of private and legally competent administrations, and subjecting them to the appropriate tests and analyses.

16 - Following up on the operations of inspection and examination of all types of food to verify its safety and fitness for human consumption within the concept and principles of precaution, transparency and traceability, and referring this outcome to the competent ministries and administrations to take the necessary measures. The Commission may seek the assistance of any other authority to accomplish these tasks.

17 - Receiving complaints from citizens, verifying them and referring them to the administrations concerned.

18 - Establishing and managing a liaison network through representative offices between the various governorates

and the local, regional and international organisations and bodies operating in the fields of food safety, in coordination with the ministries and administrations concerned.

19 - Laying down a media programme and organising campaigns aimed at raising the awareness of citizens regarding food safety and spreading a food safety culture.

20 - Participating in representing the Lebanese State in international forums in the field of food safety.

21 - The "Commission" may seek the assistance of persons of expertise in any of the matters falling within its competence.

The Chairman of the Board of Directors of the "Commission", or whomever he delegates from among the members of the Board of Directors or from among the employees, shall be deemed a member of the following councils and bodies:

1 - The "Higher Health Council".

2 - The "Higher Agricultural Council".

3 - The "National Council for the Environment".

4 - The "National Council for Consumer Protection".

5 - The Board of Directors of the "Lebanese Accreditation Council".

6 - The Board of Directors of the "Lebanese Standards Institution".

7 - The licensing committees in the Ministry of Industry when examining licensing applications for establishments engaged in an activity dealing with food, feed, fertilisers, pesticides or veterinary medicines.

8 - The Veterinary Medicines Committee.

9 - The Agricultural Medicines Committee.

10 - The Fertilisers Committee.

11 - Councils and bodies in the public sector that carry out an activity dealing with food or when they exercise such an activity.

The "Authority" shall prepare, within the three months following each financial year, an annual report on its activities which shall be submitted to the President of the Council of Ministers, and this report shall be published in the Official Gazette and shall include a summary of the measures it has taken in implementation of the tasks entrusted to it, and the extent of its contribution to achieving the objectives specified in this Law.

The Executive Body shall be composed of a Director General, scientific committees and each of the following units:

The Department of Scientific Studies and Research.

The Department of Risk Analysis, Rapid Alert System and Crisis Management.

The Department of Inspection (Food Inspector).

The Department of Administrative, Financial and Legal Affairs and Public Relations.

The Executive Body shall be headed by a Director General appointed by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers based on the recommendation of the Board of Directors of the Authority, and he shall be responsible for the proper management of the business of the Authority, the preparation of the budget and work plans, and the application of the regulations in force.

The scientific committees shall be established pursuant to decisions issued by the Board of Directors of the "Authority".

The activities of the units of which the Executive Body is composed, the manner of implementing these activities and the formation of the scientific committees shall be determined in the bylaws of the Authority.

The "Authority" shall undertake the analysis and prevention of risks that may befall human or animal health or the environment as a result of the consumption of food or the use of feed, pesticides, veterinary medicines or fertilisers, or the use of water in agricultural activity.

In exercising these tasks, the "Authority" shall enjoy the widest powers, in particular:

1 - Assessing risks, which includes identifying the source of the hazard and its characteristics, studying the probabilities of exposure to this hazard, and estimating the risks that may befall human or animal health or the environment; this assessment shall be carried out on the basis of the available local and international scientific information and standards.

2 - Drawing up a plan to confront these risks, including prevention and inspection measures, in coordination with the competent ministries and administrations to implement the necessary measures.

3 - Informing citizens and the competent administrations of these risks and the measures of

prevention and inspection, while respecting the principle of confidentiality where necessary, in a manner that does not conflict with the health and vital interest of the consumer.

Where information is available regarding the occurrence or probability of occurrence of a serious hazard to human or animal health or agricultural products as a result of the consumption of a specific food or the use of feed, pesticides, veterinary medicines or fertilisers in agricultural activity, which requires taking immediate and urgent measures to address it, the "Authority" shall inform the ministries and administrations concerned so that they may take the measures conducive to preserving public health, covering the food concerned or the feed, pesticides, veterinary medicines or fertilisers, including:

1 - Prohibiting their import or export.

2 Specifying special conditions for their import or export.

3 - Prohibiting their circulation.

4 - Withdrawing them from circulation.

5 - Re-exporting at the expense of the importer.

6 - Destroying them in an environmentally sound manner if this measure constitutes the sole means of preserving public health.

These decisions shall be notified to the Council of Ministers and announced through the media.

The Authority shall establish a rapid alert system which shall serve as a communication network capable of collecting and receiving all necessary data and information and notifying the various parties concerned of the potential risks resulting or that may result from the consumption of a specific food before or after it is placed on the markets.

A state of emergency shall be deemed to exist when it is factually and scientifically proven that food of national origin or imported food constitutes a hazard to the health of the consumer or that it is unsafe and will have significant adverse effects on his life and that it is not possible to control these risks and limit the adverse effects by taking ordinary measures.

The "Authority" shall, after coordination with the administrations concerned, declare the state of emergency and publish it in the various media. It shall submit a written communication to the competent Public Prosecution Office, which shall be empowered to take provisional measures in accordance with the following:

أ - Suspending the production and marketing of the food of national origin, confiscating the quantities present in the markets, sealing the establishment with red wax and closing it temporarily.

ب - Suspending the import of the food and confiscating the quantities previously imported and present in the markets.

ج - Referring the file immediately to the Misdemeanour Court of Appeal hearing fraud cases which, after hearing the professional, shall issue a final decision in which it determines the final measures and the fate of the confiscated quantities.

The Court of Appeal may reconsider its decision upon the request of the owner of the establishment when new circumstances arise.

With due regard to the supervisory tasks entrusted to all other ministries and administrations concerned, the Inspection Unit in the "Authority" shall undertake:

The inspection of all stages of manufacturing, processing, packing, canning, wrapping, distribution, transport, storage, display, preparation, serving and direct sale to the consumer, in order to verify the safety of the food and its compliance with the conditions and specifications provided for in this Law and in the decrees and decisions laid down in implementation thereof.

The food inspector shall have the capacity of judicial police and shall enjoy the widest powers to accomplish his mission, including:

- Entering the premises in which the operations provided for in Article 37 of this Law are carried out.

- Taking samples and specimens and requesting that they be subjected to laboratory examination.

- Drawing up official reports in the event of the existence of violations, with due regard to the provisions of Article /81/ of the Consumer Protection Law.

- Submitting an immediate report to his superior in the event that it becomes apparent to him that a state of emergency exists within the meaning set forth in this Law, in order to take all necessary measures as quickly as possible.

There shall be determined by decisions issued by the Authority, after coordination with the ministries and administrations concerned:

1 - The special conditions relating to the production, manufacturing, import, processing, transport, preservation, refrigeration or trading of foods, pesticides, veterinary medicines, feed or fertilisers.

2 - The hygiene and prevention conditions.

3 - Food safety systems based on Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points.

4 - The academic qualifications required of those in charge of managing the "Establishment", according to its activity and/or size.

The Authority shall determine, by decisions issued by it, in coordination with the ministries and administrations concerned, the conditions for packing, canning and wrapping food, pesticides, veterinary medicines, feed or fertilisers, as well as the conditions required in the materials used for packing, canning or wrapping.

The "Authority" shall determine, by decisions issued by it and in coordination with the ministries and administrations concerned, the conditions required for practising any of the activities of importing, manufacturing, processing, packing, canning, wrapping, distributing, transporting, storing, refrigerating, preserving, selling or delivering directly to the consumer food, pesticides, veterinary medicines, feed or fertilisers.

The professional, the farmer or the establishment shall bear, each within the scope of its work and according to the nature of the offence, the criminal and civil liability provided for in the Criminal Code, the Consumer Protection Law and special texts, for any unsafe food that has been imported and/or manufactured and/or distributed for consumption, and the penalty shall be aggravated where such food causes the death of any person.

All ministries and administrations concerned with food safety must provide the Authority monthly, within ten days of the following month, and whenever the need arises, with reports on violations of the legal and regulatory texts relating to food safety which they have inspected, and the Authority may request a copy of the complete violation file should it deem it necessary.

Within the framework of coordination with the competent ministries and administrations provided for in this Law, the Authority shall refer draft decisions and measures to them in accordance with the administrative procedures in force. If the competent administration does not respond within a period of 30 days from the date of its receipt of the documents, its silence shall be deemed a tacit decision of approval.

In the event of a disagreement between the Authority and any of the ministries and administrations concerned regarding the decisions or measures to be taken relating to the implementation of the provisions of this Law, the matter shall be submitted to the Council of Ministers for final determination. In the event of an emergency in accordance with the provisions of this Law, the period provided for above shall be reduced to three days.
The decisions of the "Authority" shall be published in the Official Gazette and in the media.

In the implementation of this Law, due regard shall be had to the provisions of international treaties relating to food safety, in particular those connected with sanitary and phytosanitary measures and technical barriers to trade.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Sole Article:

A - Every person who meets the following condition shall be entitled to request the recovery of Lebanese nationality if his name, or the name of one of his paternal male ascendants or of his paternal male relatives up to the second degree, is entered on the census registers conducted after the proclamation of the State of Greater Lebanon, namely the 1921 - 1924 registers of residents and emigrants and the 1932 register of emigrants, held at the Personal Status Departments at the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities, and who did not exercise their right to opt for Lebanese nationality. Provided that the person whose name is entered on the registers did not explicitly or implicitly opt for the allegiance of one of the states that separated from the Ottoman Empire, with due observance of and respect for the provisions of the Constitution.

B - The person concerned or his legally authorised representative shall submit the application for the recovery of nationality, and shall produce with his written application the documents and instruments that prove the fulfilment of the condition mentioned in Item (A) above, which are:

1 - The entries in the old personal status registers specified in Item (A) above, pertaining to him or to one of his ascendants or one of his male relatives up to the second degree.

2 - The official documents issued by the Lebanese administration relating to him or to one of his ascendants or his male relatives up to the second degree, as well as the official documents issued by the competent authorities in the foreign country whose nationality he holds, certified by the Lebanese consulate in that country.

C - The person concerned or his legally authorised representative shall submit the application accompanied by the supporting documents referred to in Item (B) of this Law:

1 - Either directly to the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities - Directorate General of Personal Status, provided that this application is signed before the Lebanese notary public by the person concerned directly or by his legally authorised representative.

2 - Or through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants via the Lebanese missions abroad, which shall immediately refer it to the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities - Directorate General of Personal Status, provided that this application is signed by the person concerned directly or by his legally authorised representative before the competent Lebanese or foreign public officer abroad, with a statement of his full identity.

If the person concerned is a minor, the application shall be submitted through his parents or whichever of them survives, failing which by the legal guardian or the testamentary guardian according to the order mentioned.

D - The Directorate General of Personal Status at the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities shall refer the applications received by it within a maximum period of two months from the date of their receipt to the Directorate General of General Security to conduct inquiries and draw up an investigation report on the outcome thereof, showing the status of the applicant, within a period of four months at most from the date of receipt of the applications.

The Directorate General of Personal Status shall, within a period of four months from its receipt of the report of the Directorate General of General Security, draw up a detailed report on the outcome of the investigations conducted regarding the application, which it shall submit to the Minister of Interior and Municipalities, who shall refer it to the Committee provided for in Item (E) of this Law within a period of one month from the date of receipt of the report from the Directorate General of Personal Status.

E - There shall be established at the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities a Committee composed of:

A judicial judge of at least the tenth grade, or an administrative judge of at least the equivalent grade, appointed by the Minister of Justice after the approval of the Supreme Judicial Council or the Bureau of the State Council: as Chairman.

The Director General of Personal Status: as Member.

The Director General of Emigrants: as Member.

The clerical and administrative work at the Committee shall be performed by employees from the Directorate General of Personal Status at the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities, who shall be attached by a decision of the Minister of Interior and Municipalities, provided that their number does not exceed five.

The Chairman and the two members of the Committee and the employees attached to the Committee shall receive allowances to be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Justice, Interior and Municipalities, and Finance.

The Committee shall be formed by a decision of the Minister of Interior and Municipalities within a period of one month from the date of issuance of this Law. An alternate for each of the judge and the two members of the Committee shall be named and appointed in the same manner.

F - The Committee shall examine the files referred to it by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities, and it may for this purpose seek the assistance of the various competent administrations.

It shall take its decisions by a majority of its members and shall consequently issue a reasoned decision as to whether the application must be accepted or rejected, which it shall submit to the Minister of Interior and Municipalities within a period of three months from the referral of the file to it by the Minister of Interior, and shall notify it to the person concerned. If the decision is taken by a majority of the members, the dissenting opinion must be included in the report.

G - Decisions of acceptance or rejection shall be notified both to the Minister of Interior and Municipalities and to the person concerned at the elected domicile specified in the application.

The decisions of the Committee shall remain subject to appeal, within a period of one month from the date of notification, before the Civil Court of Appeal within whose jurisdiction the place specified for the registration of the applicant for the recovery of nationality is located. The appeal shall be lodged by the person concerned or by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities. The decisions of the Court of Appeal shall not be subject to any avenue of recourse except opposition to judgments in absentia.

The opposition to the judgment in absentia shall be lodged by the person concerned within a period of fifteen days from his notification of the decision.

After the issuance of the Committee's decision accepting the application and the expiry of the one-month period for appeal, or after the issuance of the decision of the Court of Appeal accepting the application, a decree shall immediately be issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior and Municipalities deeming the person concerned to be Lebanese.

H - The details of the implementation of the provisions of this Law shall, where necessary, be determined by a decree or decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior and Municipalities, and shall be revised in the same manner.

I - The right to request the recovery of Lebanese nationality provided for in Paragraph (A) of this Law shall lapse if the persons concerned do not submit their applications within a period of ten years from the effective date of this Law.

J - This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The draft law transmitted by Decree No. 8200 dated 24 May 2012 (Amending Law No. 318 dated 20/4/2001, Fighting Money Laundering), as amended by the Subcommittee derived from the Joint Parliamentary Committees and the Chamber of Deputies, has been adopted.

This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

For the purposes of this Law, illicit funds mean tangible or intangible, movable or immovable assets, including legal documents or instruments evidencing title to, or any interest in, such assets, resulting from the commission or punishable attempted commission of, or participation in, any of the following offences, whether committed in Lebanon or abroad.

1 - The cultivation, manufacture, or illicit trafficking of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances in accordance with Lebanese laws.

2 - Participation in unlawful associations with the intention of committing felonies and misdemeanours.

3 - Terrorism in accordance with the provisions of Lebanese laws.

4 - The financing of terrorism or terrorist acts and acts related thereto (travel - organisation - training - recruitment...) or the financing of terrorist individuals or organisations in accordance with the provisions of Lebanese laws.

5 - Illicit trafficking in arms.

6 - Kidnapping by force of arms or by any other means.

7 - Insider trading, breach of confidentiality, hindering the freedom of sale by auction, and unlawful speculation.

8 - Incitement to debauchery and offences against public ethics and morals by way of organised gangs.

9 - Corruption, including bribery, trading in influence, embezzlement, exploitation of office, abuse of authority, and illicit enrichment.

10 - Theft, breach of trust, and embezzlement.

11 - Fraud, including offences of fraudulent bankruptcy.

12 - Forgery of public and private documents and instruments, including cheques and credit cards of all kinds, and counterfeiting of currency, stamps, and stamped papers.

13 - Smuggling in accordance with the provisions of the Customs Law.

14 - Counterfeiting of goods and fraudulent trading therein.

15 - Air and maritime piracy.

16 - Trafficking in human beings and smuggling of migrants.

17 - Sexual exploitation, including the sexual exploitation of children.

18 - Environmental offences.

19 - Extortion.

20 - Murder.

21 - Tax evasion in accordance with Lebanese laws.

Money laundering shall be deemed any act intended to:

1 - Conceal the true source of illicit funds or give a false justification for the said source, by any means whatsoever, in the knowledge that the funds which are the subject of the act are illicit.

2 - Convert or transfer funds, or replace or invest the same to purchase movable or immovable property or to carry out financial operations for the purpose of concealing or disguising their illicit source, or with the intention of assisting any person involved in the commission of any of the offences provided for in Article 1 to evade prosecution, in the knowledge that the funds which are the subject of the act are illicit.

The offence of money laundering is an independent offence and does not require a conviction for a predicate offence, nor does the conviction of the offender for the predicate offence preclude his prosecution for the offence of money laundering where there is a difference in the constituent elements of the offence.

Any person who commits, attempts to commit, incites, facilitates, intervenes in, or participates in:

1 - Money laundering operations shall be punishable by imprisonment from three to seven years and by a fine not exceeding twice the amount that is the subject of the laundering operation.

2 - Operations of financing of terrorism or acts related thereto shall be punishable by the penalties provided for in Article 316 bis and Articles 212 to 222 inclusive of the Penal Code.

Banks, financial institutions, financial leasing companies, institutions issuing and promoting payment or credit cards, institutions engaging in electronic money transfers, exchange institutions, financial intermediation companies, collective investment schemes, and any institutions subject to the licensing or supervision of the Banque du Liban must comply with the obligations enumerated below and with the regulatory texts issued by the Banque du Liban for the purposes of applying the provisions of this Law:

1 - Applying customer due diligence measures to permanent customers (whether natural persons, legal persons, or special legal arrangements) so as to verify their identity on the basis of reliable documents, information, or data.

2 - Applying customer due diligence measures to occasional customers so as to verify their identity where the value of the operation or series of operations executed exceeds the amount determined by the Banque du Liban.

3 - Identifying the beneficial owner and taking the necessary steps to verify his identity on the basis of reliable documents, information, or data.

4 - Retaining copies of documents relating to all operations and information, data, or copies of documents relating to the identity of clients for a period of at least five years after the completion of the operations or the termination of the business relationship, whichever is longer.

5 - Conducting ongoing monitoring and reviewing business relationships.

6 - Applying the measures provided for in clauses 1 to 5 above to permanent and occasional customers when doubts arise as to the veracity or adequacy of previously declared customer identification information, or when a suspicion of money laundering or financing of terrorism arises, regardless of any thresholds or exemptions that limit the application of these measures.

7 - Taking into account indicators denoting the likelihood of the existence of money laundering or financing of terrorism operations and the principles of caution and diligence in order to detect suspicious operations.

Institutions not subject to the Banking Secrecy Law issued on 3/9/1956, in particular insurance companies, casinos, real estate dealers and brokers, and dealers in high-value goods (jewellery, precious stones, gold, works of art, antiquities), must keep records of operations the value of which exceeds an amount determined by the Special Investigation Commission ("the Commission"), established pursuant to Article 6 of this Law, and must comply with the obligations provided for in Article 4 and with the regulatory texts and recommendations issued by "the Commission" for the purposes of applying the provisions of this Law.

Certified public accountants and notaries public must apply these obligations when preparing or carrying out on behalf of their clients any of the following services:

- Buying and selling of real estate.

- Managing of clients' movable and immovable property, in particular asset formation operations and joint investment operations.

- Management of bank accounts and securities accounts.

- Organisation of contributions for the creation or management of companies.

- Creation or management of legal persons or any special legal arrangement, and buying and selling of sole proprietorships or commercial companies.

As for lawyers, the same obligations set out above shall apply to them when they carry out the aforementioned services, provided that the rules for applying these obligations are determined pursuant to a mechanism established by the Beirut and Tripoli Bar Associations taking into consideration the specific nature of the legal profession and its regulations.

An independent commission of a judicial nature, enjoying legal personality, not subject in the exercise of its functions to the authority of the Bank, shall be established at the Banque du Liban and shall hereinafter be referred to as the "Special Investigation Commission" or the "Commission".

1 - The "Special Investigation Commission" shall consist of:

* The Governor of the Banque du Liban and, should he be unable to attend, whoever he delegates from among his Vice-Governors - as Chairman.

* The Judge appointed to the Higher Banking Commission, and, should he be unable to attend, an alternate judge appointed by the Supreme Judicial Council for a term equal to the term of appointment of the original Judge - as a member.

* The Chairman of the Banking Control Commission, and, should he be unable to attend, whoever he delegates from among the members of the said Commission - as a member.

* An original member and an alternate member appointed by the Council of Ministers upon the nomination of the Governor of the Banque du Liban, provided that they possess experience of not less than 15 years in the field of financial or banking law - as a member.

2 - The mission of the "Special Investigation Commission" shall be:

- To receive reports and requests for assistance and to conduct investigations into operations suspected of constituting money laundering offences or terrorism financing offences, and to decide on the seriousness of the evidence and presumptions of the commission of these offences or any of them, and to take the appropriate decision in respect thereof, notably the temporary precautionary freezing of the suspected accounts and/or operations for a maximum period of one year renewable once for six additional months in respect of requests for assistance received from abroad, and for a maximum period of one year months renewable once for three additional months in respect of reports and requests for assistance received from within the country.

- To verify that the concerned parties referred to in Articles Four and Five comply with the obligations provided for in this Law and the regulatory texts issued pursuant thereto, with the exception of lawyers, certified accountants and notaries public, and subject to the provisions of the second paragraph of Article Seventeen of this Law.

- To collect and retain information received from the concerned parties referred to in Articles Four and Five and information received from Lebanese or foreign official authorities and any other gathered information, and to exchange the same with its counterparts in its capacity as the competent authority and the official centre to do so.

- To issue regulatory texts relating to the implementation of the provisions of this Law for the concerned parties referred to in Article Five and to issue recommendations to all concerned entities.

3 - The right shall be restricted to the "Commission", after conducting the necessary audit and analysis, to decide:

. The final freezing of the concerned accounts and/or operations and/or the lifting of banking secrecy in favour of the competent judicial authorities and in favour of the Higher Banking Commission in the person of its Chairman over the accounts or operations suspected of being related to money laundering or terrorism financing.

. Keeping the suspected accounts under monitoring (Traceable) The "Commission" may revoke, finally or totally, any decision it takes in the event that new data becomes available to it in this regard.

4 - The "Commission" shall have the right:

a - To place an encumbrance entry on the records and registers pertaining to movable or immovable property, indicating that such property is the subject of an investigation by the "Commission", and this entry shall remain in place until the causes of suspicion cease to exist or a final decision is issued in respect thereof,

b - To request the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation to take precautionary measures with respect to movable and immovable property for which there are no records or registers, with a view to restricting the disposal thereof until a final judicial decision is issued in respect thereof,

in the event of suspicion that such property is related to money laundering or terrorism financing, and/or throughout the period of the temporary precautionary freezing of the suspected accounts and/or operations as provided for in Clause (2) of this Article and/or throughout the period of the final freezing of such accounts and/or operations as provided for in Clause (3) of the same Article.

5 - The "Commission" may request the concerned official and private persons and entities to take the necessary measures to prevent the disposal of movable or immovable property belonging to the names listed or to be listed on the national lists issued by the competent Lebanese authorities or any other lists circulated by it on the subject of terrorism, terrorism financing and acts associated therewith.

The concerned official and private persons and entities shall respond without any delay to this request.

6 - The "Commission" shall meet, upon the convocation of its Chairman, at least twice a month and whenever the need arises, and its meetings shall not be valid unless attended by at least three members.

7 - The "Commission" shall take its decisions by a majority of the votes of the members present, and in the event of a tie, the Chairman shall have a casting vote.

8 - The Commission" shall appoint a Secretary-General for itself, provided that he works full-time on the tasks assigned to him by it, implements its decisions, and directly supervises its employees, its contractors and the persons delegated by it for a specific mission, without the provisions of the Law issued on 3/9/1956 relating to Banking Secrecy being invoked against any of them.

9 - The members of the "Commission", its personnel, its contractors and those delegated by it shall be subject to the obligation to maintain secrecy.

10 - The "Commission" shall be subject to rules of procedure for the conduct of its work, and regulations for its employees and contractors who are subject to private law.

11 - The Banque du Liban shall bear the expenses of the "Commission" and its affiliated bodies within the budget prepared by it, provided that it obtains the approval of the Central Council of the Banque du Liban.

The concerned parties referred to in Articles Four and Five of this Law, including certified accountants and notaries public, when preparing or executing transactions on behalf of their clients relating to the activities enumerated in Article Five, shall immediately report to the Chairman of the "Commission" the details of the operations executed or attempted to be executed which they suspect are related to money laundering or terrorism financing.

Before lawyers, the obligations set forth in the preceding paragraph shall apply to them in accordance with a mechanism established by the Bar Associations of Beirut and Tripoli which takes into account the specificity of the legal profession and its regulations.

Auditors working at the Banking Control Commission shall report to the Chairman of the "Commission", through the Chairman of the Control Commission, the operations of which they become aware on the occasion of the performance of their duties and which they suspect are related to money laundering or terrorism financing.

External auditors of the parties concerned by Article Four of this Law shall immediately report to the Chairman of the "Commission" the details of the operations of which they become aware on the occasion of the performance of their work and which they suspect conceal money laundering or terrorism financing.

The external auditors of banks, financial institutions and the other companies and institutions provided for in Article Four of this Law shall verify the compliance of all such companies and institutions with the provisions of this Law and with the regulatory texts issued pursuant thereto, and shall notify the Chairman of the "Commission" of any violation in this regard.

The Ministry of Justice, each of the Bar Associations of Beirut and Tripoli, and the Association of Certified Public Accountants shall be entrusted with the task of verifying the compliance of notaries public, lawyers and certified public accountants, each within its respective competence, with the procedures provided for in this Law and in the regulatory texts issued pursuant thereto.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Shall be deemed to be practising medicine and shall bear the responsibility of its practice every person who performs, attempts or undertakes, by himself or through another person or by any means or method whatsoever, upon the person of a human being or his health, one of the following acts:

1- Examination and diagnosis or prognosis.

2- Prescribing or administering a curative, preventive or palliative treatment, whatever its type as a compound or a preparation.

3- Performing or undertaking a medical, surgical or psychiatric act upon a human being.

4- Taking substances from the body of a human being by way of puncture or otherwise for the purpose of examination, with the exception of taking blood for biological analyses.

5- Using laboratory investigations for the purpose of diagnosis or prognosis.

6- Using electrical, X-ray or cauterising rays or radioactive substances for the purpose of diagnosis or treatment.

7- Issuing a medical certificate or report relating to the health of a human being or to his incapacity for work.

8- Blood transfusion acts.

The Government may, by decrees taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Health and after consulting the opinion of the two Orders of Physicians in Lebanon, amend and complete these acts in accordance with the evolution of medical practice and techniques.

The urgent draft law referred to the Chamber of Deputies pursuant to Decree No. 1118 dated 30/3/1978, aiming to regulate the practice of the medical profession, the text of which follows, is hereby put into effect:
This Decree shall be published and notified where needed and shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.
The licence to practise and teach the medical profession shall be granted in accordance with the following provisions:

«A - The licence to practise medicine shall be granted to a Lebanese physician if he holds all the following qualifications and conditions:

1 - That he holds the Lebanese General Secondary Certificate or its official equivalent.

2 - That he holds a medical degree from a state university or from a private university in Lebanon or abroad recognised by the country from which it was issued and which legally qualifies him to practise the profession therein; in both cases, it must be recognised by the Lebanese State and be equated by the Equivalence Committee at the Ministry of Education and Higher Education.

3 - That he has not been convicted of a felony or an attempted felony of any kind whatsoever, or of an infamous misdemeanour; and shall be considered an infamous misdemeanour: theft, fraud, breach of trust, embezzlement, bribery, rape, intimidation, forgery, use of forged documents, false testimony, perjury, offences against morality provided for in Title VII of the Penal Code, and offences relating to the cultivation of and trafficking in narcotic substances.

4 - That he passes the written examination in the basic medical sciences upon completion of their study, followed by the written, oral and clinical examinations conducted by the Ministry of Education and Higher Education in accordance with a system determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Education and Higher Education and of Public Health, which includes the mechanisms and procedures relating to these examinations.

The system of these examinations and the subjects of the basic medical sciences shall be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Public Health and of Education and Higher Education.

B - Physicians holding a licence to practise the medical profession in Lebanon after the issuance of this Law and who do not hold a specialisation certificate may join one of the two Orders of Physicians in the capacity of a non-specialist resident physician (Résident) and they shall have the right to:»

1 - Work in public or private hospitals under the supervision of a specialist physician in a functional capacity as a non-specialist resident physician (Résident) for a period of not less than three years, after which he may continue to practise the profession in his private clinic.

2 - Work in public or private administrative posts that require a licence to practise the medical profession from the Ministry of Public Health.

The licence to practise medicine shall be granted to a physician naturalised with the Lebanese nationality immediately upon his acquisition of this nationality, provided that he fulfils the conditions and qualifications required of a Lebanese physician, set out in Article 3 of this Law.

The licence to practise medicine shall be granted to a non-Lebanese physician who is a national of the Arab States if he fulfils the following conditions and qualifications:

First: The conditions and qualifications required of a Lebanese physician, set out in Article 3 of this Law.

Second: That this physician be a national of a country that permits a Lebanese physician to practise his profession therein, that is, that there be reciprocity, and reciprocity shall be applied according to the inverse numerical ratio of the population in Lebanon and in the country to which the said physician belongs, and reciprocity shall be enshrined in an agreement between the Lebanese State and the State concerned.

As for a foreign physician who is naturalised with the nationality of one of the Arab States, he shall not have the right to practise medicine in Lebanon until five years after his acquisition of this nationality and after he proves that he has resided throughout this period without interruption in the country whose nationality he acquired. He must also fulfil all the conditions and qualifications set out above.

A non-Lebanese physician of other nationalities licensed to practise the medical profession by the Ministry of Public Health before 28 November of the year 1946 shall have the right to continue practising the profession in Lebanon. However, he shall not have the right to be employed in public administrations, public institutions and municipalities.

The licence to practise granted to this physician shall lapse if he absents himself from Lebanon continuously for a period exceeding three years.

The licence to practise medicine shall be granted to a non-Lebanese physician of other nationalities if he fulfils the following conditions:

First: The conditions and qualifications required of a Lebanese physician, set out in Article 3 of this Law.

Second: That he be a national of a country that applies reciprocity in the manner set out in the fifth Article of this Law.

A non-Lebanese physician who is a member of the teaching staffs in the faculties of medicine in Lebanon shall have the right to practise the profession in the following cases and within the following conditions:

First: That he be devoted full-time to teaching in one of the faculties of medicine in Lebanon for a fixed fee, and he shall not have the right to receive any remuneration for his own account for any professional work he performs inside or outside the faculty to which he belongs or in any institution affiliated with this faculty.

Second: That he hold a medical degree and a specialisation certificate officially recognised and which entitle him to the right to practise the medical profession in his country.

Third: That he be contracted in writing with one of the faculties of medicine in Lebanon to practise teaching only, and that the faculty apply to register him with the Ministry of Public Health and with the Order of Physicians. Non-Lebanese physicians who are members of the teaching staffs shall be granted the licence to practise only for the duration of their contract with one of the faculties, and the faculty must notify the competent authorities of the termination of service of every non-Lebanese physician it has.

Fourth: That the percentage of non-Lebanese physicians who are members of the teaching staffs in the faculties of medicine in Lebanon not exceed five per cent, and this percentage may be exceeded up to ten per cent with the approval of the Minister of Public Health.

Fifth: That he not practise the profession outside the faculty to which he belongs or outside the hospital affiliated with the said faculty except as a consulting physician only. In this latter case, he shall not have the right to respond to a request for consultation outside the hospital except upon a written request from the treating physician.

Sixth: That the duration of the contract not exceed three years, renewable pursuant to a decision of the Minister of Public Health, subject to the continued fulfilment of the conditions and qualifications imposed at the commencement of the contract; with the exception of what is stated above, a non-Lebanese physician who is a member of the teaching staffs shall not have the right to perform any other work than the works he is licensed to perform pursuant to this Law.

Non-Lebanese physicians who specialise in Lebanon shall be entitled to carry out all acts required by their specialisation under the supervision and liability of the institution to which they belong during the period of their specialisation.
