The following shall be prohibited from practising medicine in Lebanon, by a decision of the Minister of Public Health, under penalty of prosecution:

1- Anyone who does not hold a licence to practise the profession of medicine from the Ministry of Public Health

2- Anyone who has been convicted of a felony or an attempted felony of any kind whatsoever, or of an infamous misdemeanour or an attempted infamous misdemeanour, and the misdemeanours provided for in paragraph 3 of Article 3 of this Law shall be deemed infamous.

3- Anyone who has been afflicted with insanity or dementia or has become addicted to the use of narcotics or intoxicants, provided that such conditions are established by a final court judgment.

4- Anyone who uses secret medicines and means which he does not disclose to a special medical committee appointed by a decision of the Minister of Public Health.

5- Anyone who engages in commercial or industrial acts requiring continuous personal practice.

6- Anyone whose name has been struck off the roll of the Order of Physicians in which he was registered in accordance with the laws in force.

7- Anyone against whom a decision has been issued by the Disciplinary Council of the Order of Physicians to which he belongs prohibiting him from practising his profession permanently or suspending him from practising it for a specified period, provided that such decision shall not be executed until after it has become final.

General Conditions

A physician holding a licence from the Ministry of Public Health to practise the profession of medicine on Lebanese territory shall not be entitled to bear the title of specialist unless he meets the conditions set out in the following articles:
No specialisation in medicine shall be recognised in Lebanon unless it is listed in the Schedule attached to this Law.

Any person wishing to obtain the title of specialist in one of the branches of medicine set out in the attached Schedule must meet the following conditions:

1- He must be a physician holding a licence to practise the profession from the Ministry of Public Health.

2- He must hold a specialisation certificate from an officially recognised scientific body or university, the years of each specialisation must not be less than the period specified in the Schedule attached to this Law, and such certificate must be the same as that granted to nationals of the country in which the scientific body or university that granted the specialisation certificate is located.

The French specialisation certificate called [blank] shall be exempted from this latter condition

This exemption shall cover all holders of this certificate before and after the issuance of this Law

3- Where a specialisation exists in a given country without being accompanied by a university certificate or a certificate from a scientific body, the Specialisation Committee may examine the case in the light of the criteria which it determines and deems sufficient to decide, provided that the period specified in the aforementioned attached Schedule is adopted.

4- An application for registration of the specialisation shall be submitted to the Ministry of Public Health together with all necessary documents. The application shall be registered and referred to the Specialisation Committee.

1- The list of specialisations recorded in the attached Schedule and the period of specialisation may be amended by a decision of the Minister of Public Health based on a recommendation of the Specialisation Committee.

2- Sub-specialisations linked to the basic specialisations recorded in the attached Schedule may be added, provided that the applicant for the sub-specialisation has completed an additional period of specialisation determined by the Specialisation Committee, provided that this period is not less than one year.

Composition of the Specialisation Committee The Specialisation Committee shall be composed by a decision of the Minister of Public Health as follows:

1- The Director General of the Ministry of Public Health, as Chairman

2- Two physicians proposed by the Council of the Lebanese Order of Physicians and one physician proposed by the Council of the Order of Physicians of the North, from the scientific committees, provided that they hold at least the title of Assistant Professor. Members

3- One Lebanese professor from each officially recognised faculty of medicine in Lebanon, proposed by the Dean of the Faculty- Members.

The bodies mentioned above shall designate for each regular member an alternate member to replace the regular member in his absence.

The functions and powers of the Specialisation Committee, its term of office, its rules of procedure, its meetings, and the allowances of its Chairman and members shall be determined by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Health.

Specialisation Application Fee

The Ministry of Public Health shall levy from every applicant for a specialisation a fiscal stamp to be affixed to the specialisation licence, the value of which shall be determined by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Health.

Decree determining the fiscal stamp fee on the licence to bear a medical specialisation title
The licence to bear a specialisation title shall be granted by the Minister of Public Health based on the opinion and approval of the Specialisation Committee.

Examination Committee

A decree adopted by the Council of Ministers shall determine the manner of composition of the Examination Committee, its functions, its powers, its term of office, its rules of procedure, its meetings, and the conditions for appointing its Chairman and members and their term of office. The decisions of the Examination Committee shall not be subject to any avenue of review, including an application for annulment for excess of power.

On Retaking the Examination

A candidate who fails the examination shall be entitled to apply to retake it after at least six months from the date of announcement of the examination results.

This application shall be submitted to the Ministry of Public Health accompanied by the fee referred to in Article Nineteen of this Law.

The following shall be exempted from the provisions of this Law:

2- Physicians who have been practising their specialisation publicly and continuously for at least ten years prior to the date of entry into force of this Law, provided that they register this acquired specialisation with the Ministry of Public Health and the Order of Physicians after the approval of the Specialisation Committee within a time limit of three months from the date of entry into force of this Law.

There is hereby put into effect the urgent Draft Law referred to the Chamber of Deputies pursuant to Decree No. 1077 dated 18/3/78 aiming to regulate the nursing profession, the text of which follows:
This Decree shall be published and notified where necessary and shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Definition of the Licensed Nurse: The licensed nurse is the person who has completed the study of a basic programme in the field of nursing and has become qualified and licensed to practise the nursing profession on Lebanese territory, in view of his planning and leadership role in the field of nursing in addition to his ability to work as a member of a medical team.

Mission of the Licensed Nurse:

1- Performing nursing acts within the scope of general or specialised nursing study and regulations according to his scientific competencies and qualifications.

2- Teaching nursing to nursing students in the fields of his work and providing health guidance. 3- Contributing to the implementation of public health programmes within the limits of his capabilities, responsibilities and missions, and proposing the necessary nursing services.

4- Participating in nursing research aimed at the development and advancement of these sciences.

No person shall be entitled to assume the title of licensed nurse unless he fulfils the following conditions:

1) He is Lebanese and has attained the age of nineteen.

2) He holds the Lebanese Baccalaureate Certificate - Part Two - or its official equivalent.

3) He holds a university degree in nursing from a university recognised by the Lebanese Government, provided that the duration of university study is not less than three years, or a higher diploma in nursing issued by the Ministry of National Education and Fine Arts - Directorate General of Vocational and Technical Education, the duration of study and curricula of which shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.

4) He possesses the health, mental and moral qualities necessary to practise the nursing profession.

No person shall be entitled to practise the profession of licensed nurse except after obtaining a licence from the Ministry of Public Health after depositing with it the following documents:

1- A certified true copy of the documents proving the fulfilment of the conditions prescribed in Article Three of this Law.

2- A copy of his judicial record proving that such record is free from any conviction for a felony, an attempted felony, or a disgraceful misdemeanour.

3- A certificate proving that he has successfully passed the Colloquium examination conducted by the Ministry of National Education and Fine Arts. Holders of the higher diploma in nursing issued by the Ministry of National Education and Fine Arts shall be exempted from this condition.

Definition of the Nurse: The nurse is the person who has obtained a scientific and technical qualification enabling him to provide uncomplicated general nursing care, and who works under the supervision of the licensed nurse.

Mission of the Nurse:

1- Knowing the basic needs required by the persons entrusted to his care.

2- Contributing to establishing a care programme for such persons together with those working with him.

3- Conveying correct and accurate observations.

4- Executing the instructions of the nurse in charge or the attending physician consciously and attentively.

5- Contributing with the other members of the medical corps to public health care, disease prevention and the rehabilitation of patients.

No person shall be entitled to assume the title of nurse unless he fulfils the following conditions:

1- He is Lebanese and has attained the age of seventeen.

2- He holds the Lebanese Intermediate Studies Certificate (Brevet) or its official equivalent. 3- He has completed nursing studies at an officially recognised nursing school and passed the examinations for the Technical Baccalaureate Certificate - Part Two - Nursing Care.

4- A nurse holding a nursing certificate from outside Lebanon must have his certificate officially equated and pass the Colloquium examination conducted by the Ministry of Education.

5- He enjoys the health, mental and moral qualities necessary to practise the nursing profession.

6- He has not been convicted of a felony, an attempted felony, or a disgraceful misdemeanour, and he must produce a copy of his judicial record proving the same. No person shall be entitled to practise the profession of nurse except after obtaining a licence therefor from the Ministry of Public Health after depositing with it a certified true copy of the documents proving the fulfilment of the conditions prescribed in this Article.

The nurse shall be entitled to pursue university or higher nursing studies to acquire the title of licensed nurse and shall be exempted from the condition of holding the Lebanese Baccalaureate Certificate - Part Two or its official equivalent.
The assistant nurse is the person who has obtained a scientific qualification and vocational training enabling him to assist the nursing team in providing nursing care.

Mission of the Assistant Nurse:

1- Watching over the physical and psychological state of the persons whose care is entrusted to him.

2- Knowing the natural needs of the patient and observing the physiological and psychological changes that may occur in the health of the patient.

3- Conveying his observations orally or in writing to the nurse in charge.

4- Providing the necessary health care under the supervision and responsibility of the licensed nurse or the nurse.

5- Watching over cleanliness and order in the places where he works.

No person shall be entitled to assume the title of assistant nurse unless he fulfils the following conditions:

1- He is Lebanese and has attained the legal working age.

2- He holds the Lebanese Intermediate Studies Certificate (Brevet) or its official equivalent, in addition to one academic year at a nursing school or at a hospital both authorised by the Ministry of National Education and Fine Arts to apply the programme specially prepared by it for this purpose.

3- He has passed the official vocational examinations conducted by the Ministry of National Education and Fine Arts.

4- He enjoys the health, mental and moral qualities necessary to practise his mission.

5- He has not been convicted of a felony, an attempted felony, or a disgraceful misdemeanour, and he must produce a copy of his judicial record proving the same. No person shall be entitled to practise the profession of assistant nurse except after obtaining a licence therefor from the Ministry of Public Health, after depositing with it a certified true copy of the documents proving the fulfilment of the conditions prescribed in this Article.

A non-Lebanese nurse licensed to practise the profession in his country and delegated by an international body, organisation or institution authorised to operate in Lebanon may practise the profession within the scope of the mission entrusted to him.

A non-Lebanese nurse who is a member of the teaching staff at nursing schools in Lebanon may practise the profession of teaching nursing under the following two conditions:

1- He is licensed to practise the nursing profession in his country.

2- He has signed a draft employment contract for a fixed term with one of the nursing schools in Lebanon pursuant to which he devotes himself full-time to teaching nursing therein, and he shall not be entitled to receive, in addition to his salary, any remuneration for his own account for any professional work he performs inside or outside the school.

A non-Lebanese nurse may practise training in the field of nursing in Lebanon under the following- two conditions:

1- He is licensed to practise the nursing profession in his country and passes the Colloquium examination conducted by the Ministry of National Education and Fine Arts.

2- He has signed a draft employment contract for a fixed term with one of the hospitals in Lebanon pursuant- to which he devotes himself full-time to training therein, and he shall not be entitled to receive, in addition to his salary, any remuneration for his own account for any professional work he performs inside or outside the hospital.

An applicant for admission into the Customs Enforcement Corps must satisfy the following conditions:

1 - He must have been a Lebanese national for at least ten years.

2 - He must, on the date of the commencement of the competitive examination, have completed eighteen years of age and not have exceeded twenty-five years of age, with respect to civilians. The age limit may be exceeded for military personnel in active service in the Army, the Internal Security Forces, or the General Security, or for candidates who have served in these forces, by a period equivalent to the duration of their service, provided that their age does not exceed thirty years on the date of the competitive examination.

3 - He must enjoy the physical fitness enabling him to serve in the Customs Enforcement Corps.

4 - He must be the holder of at least the Complementary Certificate (Brevet), or its official equivalent of academic or vocational certificates, or have successfully completed the grade above the Complementary Certificate (Brevet), and with respect to the technical staff, he must be at least at the level of completion of the primary education stage, and the documents submitted to prove the fulfilment of these conditions by the candidate must be certified by the competent authorities at the Ministry of National Education and Fine Arts. With regard to driver guards, they must hold, in addition to the aforementioned conditions, a private motor vehicle driving licence.

5 - His height must be at least:

- 165 centimetres for holders of at least the Lebanese Baccalaureate Certificate, Part One, or its official equivalent of academic or vocational certificates, and for candidates for the post of driver guard, mechanic guard, wireless operator guard, or carpenter guard.

- 167 centimetres for other candidates.

6- He must enjoy his civil rights and not have been convicted of a felony, or twice or more of an ordinary misdemeanour, or once of any of the following misdemeanours: theft - fraud - breach of trust - embezzlement - extortion - intimidation - forgery - cheque without provision - offences relating to weapons of war of all kinds and their transport, manufacture, or trafficking - smuggling offences of all kinds - offences relating to the cultivation, possession, and trafficking of narcotics - offences against public morals provided for in Title Seven of the Penal Code, or of any of the military misdemeanours provided for in Book Two - Title One - of the Military Penal Code. These provisions shall apply to persons who have been rehabilitated or have benefited from an amnesty.

7- He must be of good conduct and morals, not addicted to intoxicants and narcotics, not engage in games of chance, and not be affiliated with a party or cooperating therewith.

8- He must not have practised in his civilian life a disgraceful or dishonourable profession. If he is a former member of the military personnel of the Army, the Internal Security Forces, or the General Security- he must possess a certificate of good conduct if his service exceeded six months.

An appointment file shall be drawn up for each applicant comprising:

1 - Information declared by the person concerned regarding his personal status.

2 - A copy of an individual civil status extract.

3 - A copy of his judicial record and a certificate from the judicial authorities proving whether or not he is subject to judicial prosecution.

4 - A copy of his academic or vocational certificate certified by the Ministry of National Education and Fine Arts.

5 - A statement of the stages of military service, and disciplinary reports, if the applicant is a serving or former member of the military personnel.

A candidate for the post of customs guard must successfully pass a written competitive examination the rules of which shall be determined by a decision of the Higher Council of Customs upon the proposal of the Director General of Customs, and the results thereof shall be entered in the file drawn up in accordance with the provisions of the preceding Article.

Accepted candidates for the various posts shall sign an enlistment contract for a period of five years commencing from the date of their enrolment in the training course provided for in Article 21 of this Law, and they shall be designated as probationary guards. The enlistment contract of probationary guards may be terminated by a decision of the Higher Council of Customs upon the proposal of the Director General of Customs, in the following cases:

1 - For disciplinary reasons.

2 - By reason of the unsatisfactory result of their course from the health, professional, and military standpoints.

3 - If it is established that the person concerned submitted incorrect information in the appointment application file which led to his acceptance.

In all three cases, the persons concerned shall not be entitled to claim any compensation for the period they may have spent in service.

Probationary guards shall, immediately upon their appointment, be enrolled in a military and professional training course at the conclusion of which they shall sit for an examination. As for seaman guards and members of the technical staff, they shall undergo a similar course the curriculum of which shall include, in addition to military and professional subjects, technical subjects relating to the nature of their specialisation.

The Director General of Customs shall, in agreement with the competent authorities, determine the rules of the courses.

Probationers shall be confirmed in the capacity of guard or marine technical guard after the expiry of one year from the date of their appointment, and subject to their passing the examination provided for in Article 21 above.

Pension deductions shall be withheld from the salaries of probationers, in accordance with the law, and shall be entered into a special account, and upon their confirmation the probationary period shall be included in the calculation of active service and the pension deductions from the salaries shall be transferred to the Treasury.

In the event of their discharge, the said deductions shall be refunded to the persons concerned.

The Higher Council of Customs may, upon the proposal of the Director General of Customs, appoint drivers from among the non-specialist guards, provided that they hold a motor vehicle driving licence obtained at least three years prior to the date of appointment, that they declare in writing their desire therefor, and that they undergo a probationary period the duration of which shall be determined by the Higher Council of Customs.

It may also exempt such persons, to the exclusion of others, from the duty of driving vehicles for health reasons, or after the expiry of at least fifteen years of performing service in driving motor vehicles.
Under no circumstances may non-commissioned officers, seaman guards, and all members of the technical staff be transferred from their original post to any other post in the establishment.

Members of the Customs Enforcement Corps shall, after successfully passing the course provided for in Article 21 of this Law, take the following statutory oath before the Single Judge:

"I swear by Almighty God to perform my duties with all loyalty and honesty, to conduct myself in all my acts as a truthful and honourable officer, and not to use the authority vested in me except for the enforcement of the law."

The oath shall be taken once.

Members of the administrative staff shall be selected from among the non-commissioned officers and guards not provided for in Article 24 of this Law, after they successfully pass a professional competitive examination the rules of which shall be determined by a decision of the Higher Council of Customs upon the proposal of the Director General of Customs, and subject to the following conditions:

1 - That no penalties of the third degree have been imposed upon them during the last five years.

2 - That the standard of their professional grades is good.

3 - That they have spent in service:

A - For non-commissioned officers: at least twenty years, including five years in the capacity of non-commissioned officer.

B - For guards: twenty-five years, including at least twenty years in the Customs Administration.

The last two conditions may be waived for members who have suffered, during or by reason of service, an accident resulting in difficulty for such members in performing ordinary duties, pursuant to the decision of the Medical Committee provided for in Article 55 of this Law.

Appointment shall be effected by a decision of the Higher Council of Customs, upon the proposal of the Director General of Customs. Administrative superiors shall exercise, over the members of the administrative staff, the powers dictated by the special nature of their work, without prejudice to the right of their military superiors to exercise all other powers provided for in this Law.

Promotion to a higher rank shall not take place unless the names of the persons concerned are entered on an annual promotion table drawn up by the Higher Council of Customs upon the proposal of the Director General of Customs. The non-commissioned officers and enlisted men whose names are entered on the promotion table shall be promoted successively, in proportion to the vacancy of posts, by an administrative order from the Director General of Customs. In the event that a number of posts become vacant in one of the ranks, and there is not a sufficient number of candidates to fill these posts, a number of non-commissioned officers or enlisted men equal to the number of vacant posts in the said rank may be appointed in the rank that is lower than it.

For the acceptance of candidacy for a higher rank, the candidate must meet, up to 31 December of the year of candidacy, the following seniority requirements:

1 - For the rank of Corporal - two years in the rank of Guard.

2 - For the rank of Sergeant - four years in the rank of Corporal, reduced to three years for holders of at least the Baccalaureate certificate, Part One, or its officially equivalent academic or vocational certificates.

3 - For the rank of Staff Sergeant - three years in the rank of Sergeant.

4 - For the rank of Sub-Officer - four years in the rank of Staff Sergeant.

5 - For the rank of Chief Sub-Officer - three years in the rank of Sub-Officer.

6 - For the rank of Warrant Officer three years in the rank of Chief Sub-Officer.

7 - For the rank of Chief Warrant Officer two years in the rank of Warrant Officer".

The Director General of Customs shall accept the candidacy, on the basis of assessment marks set by the direct superiors, provided that they are at a good level, and that a penalty of the second degree and above has not been imposed against the candidate during the last year preceding the date of candidacy.

1- Promotion to the ranks of Corporal, Sergeant, and Sub-Officer shall only take place after the candidates have been subjected to the following conditions:

a - A competency examination.

b - A military and vocational training course, provided that the candidate passes the end-of-course examination.

c - Successful candidates shall be classified on the basis of the average of the marks of the competency examination and the marks of the training course and its final examination.

2 - Promotion to the rank of Staff Sergeant, Chief Sub-Officer, Warrant Officer, and Chief Warrant Officer shall only take place after the candidates have been subjected to a competency examination.

The names of the successful candidates shall be entered on the promotion table according to their degree of merit.

The Higher Council of Customs shall determine, upon the proposal of the Director General of Customs, the regulations of the competency examination, and the Director General of Customs shall determine, in agreement with the competent authorities, the regulations of the training course, its resources, its programmes, its duration, and the regulations of the final examination.

1 - Upon the expiry of the period of enlistment, non-commissioned officers and guards may renew their enlistment for a period ranging between two and five years, provided that the enlistment contract may not be renewed for a period exceeding the date of reaching the statutory age.

2 - By a decision of the Higher Council of Customs upon the proposal of the Director General of Customs, the discharge of non-commissioned officers and guards who have not reached the statutory age may be refused in time of war, state of emergency, and unrest, and if the person concerned is referred to the Medical Committee or prosecuted before the judiciary or the Disciplinary Council, or is under a professional investigation, until a final decision is taken on his matter. The Director General of Customs shall sign the enlistment renewal contracts.

The Higher Council of Customs may, upon the proposal of the Director General of Customs, refuse to renew the enlistment of non-commissioned officers and guards who have obtained poor assessments based on the average of the professional marks for the last two years.

In addition to what is provided for in Article 20 of this Law, the enlistment contract or its renewal in enlistment or its renewal shall be rescinded in the following cases:

- For disciplinary reasons (expulsion).

- For health reasons.

- For compulsory referral to retirement.

- On the basis of the request of the person concerned for compelling and urgent reasons.

This shall be effected by the Higher Council of Customs upon the proposal of the Director General of Customs.

The hierarchy of officer ranks in the Customs Brigade shall be determined as follows:

1 - Lieutenant.

2 - First Lieutenant.

3 - Captain.

4 - Major.

5 - Lieutenant Colonel.

6 - Colonel.

Where ranks are equal between two officers, command shall belong to the most senior in the rank, and where seniority in the rank is equal, seniority in the previous rank shall be adopted.

If seniority in the previous rank is equal, seniority in the rank preceding it up to the rank of Lieutenant shall be adopted.

Where seniority in the rank of Lieutenant is equal, the order of names in the decree of promotion to this rank shall be adopted.

Where ranks are equal up to the rank of Lieutenant between two officers, one of whom is from the ranks and the other from the graduates of the Military Academy, or between two officers both of whom are from the ranks and each of whom has the same seniority in all ranks, command shall belong to the more senior in service.

Officers of the Customs Brigade shall be recruited in accordance with the conditions determined in this Chapter from among:

- Cadet officers of the Customs Brigade at the Military Academy.

- Non-commissioned officers of the Customs Brigade, other than Corporals, in a proportion not exceeding twenty percent of the total officers of the general establishment.

Cadet officers of the Customs Brigade shall be recruited from civilians and from men of the Customs Brigade in active service who meet the conditions provided for in the regulations for admission to the Military Academy.

Those accepted from among them shall be appointed by a joint decision of the Ministers of National Defence and Finance.

Cadet officers of the Customs Brigade accepted into the Military Academy shall follow the programmes prescribed for Army cadet officers, to which shall be added, where necessary, special professional instruction, in agreement with the military authorities, qualifying them to follow the training course.

Cadet officers of the Customs Brigade shall be subjected, at the conclusion of study at the Military Academy, to the final examinations, and the successful candidates from among them shall be promoted to the rank of Lieutenant.

During their presence at the Military Academy, the regulations that apply to Army cadet officers shall apply to them.

The names of the successful candidates from among them shall be entered in the promotion decree in accordance with the final classification at the Military Academy. As for those who fail the final examinations, the provisions that apply to failing Army cadet officers shall apply to them.

Upon their graduation from the Military Academy, officers shall follow a training course in the Customs Administration interspersed with practical training in the Customs divisions and brigades. The Higher Council of Customs shall determine, after consulting the opinion of the Director General of Customs, the regulations of the course, its duration, its programmes, and the regulations of its end-of-course examination. Officers may be delegated abroad to follow another supplementary course, pursuant to a decision by the Minister of Finance upon the proposal of the Higher Council of Customs and after consulting the opinion of the Director General of Customs.

Lieutenants who fail the end-of-training-course examinations shall be subjected to a second course.
At the end of the training course, the officers shall take, before the President of one of the Courts of Appeal, the statutory oath provided for in Article 25 of this Law.

Non-commissioned officers who are candidates for the rank of Lieutenant must satisfy the following conditions:

1 - They must hold the Complementary Certificate (Brevet) or its official equivalent, or at least the Technical Complementary Certificate.

2 - They must hold at least the rank of Sergeant, and on 31 December of the year of candidacy the following minimum periods must have elapsed since they attained this rank:

- Three years for holders of the Lebanese Licence in Law.

- Seven years for holders of the Lebanese Baccalaureate Certificate, Second Part, or its official equivalent.

- Eight years for holders of the Lebanese Baccalaureate Certificate, First Part, or its official equivalent, or the Technical Baccalaureate Certificate.

- Ten years for holders of the Complementary Certificate (Brevet) or its official equivalent, or the Technical Complementary Certificate.

3 - They must not have exceeded the age of forty-five on 31 December of the year of candidacy.

4 - Their appraisals must be good. The Higher Council of Customs shall rule on candidacy applications upon the proposal of the Director General of Customs.

- Those whose applications are accepted shall be subject to a qualifying competitive examination limited to disciplinary, administrative and judicial matters, in addition to customs subjects, and they shall be granted before placing results increasing as the candidate's rank increases and determined- in the decision provided for in the last paragraph of this Article.

The selection of those accepted shall take place on the basis of the result of the competitive examination and within the limits of the proportion provided for in Article 37 of this Law, by a decision of the Higher Council of Customs upon the proposal of the Director General of Customs.

Those selected by the Higher Council of Customs shall attend a complementary course of a duration of at least six months at the Internal Security Forces Institute or at another institute designated by decree, and the names of those among them who pass the end-of-course examination, and in accordance with their ranking resulting from the examination, shall be entered on the promotion roster for the rank of Lieutenant by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance and the recommendation of the Higher Council of Customs, and they shall be promoted to this rank in the same manner. The rules for applying the provisions of this Article shall be determined by a decision of the Higher Council of Customs, upon the proposal of the Director General of Customs.

An officer shall not be promoted to a higher rank unless his name is entered on the promotion roster, which is issued by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance and the recommendation of the Higher Council of Customs.

There shall be entered on the promotion roster by selection, with due regard to the seniority provided for in Article 36 of this Law, the names of the officers who satisfy the following conditions:

1 - They must have spent at least the following periods in their ranks, up to 31 December of the year of candidacy:

- For the rank of First Lieutenant - three years in the rank of Lieutenant.

- For the rank of Captain - four years in the rank of First Lieutenant.

- For the rank of Major - four years in the rank of Captain.

- For the rank of Lieutenant Colonel - three years in the rank of Major.

- For the rank of Colonel - four years in the rank of Lieutenant Colonel.

2 - The appraisals of them by their superiors must be good, as well as their disciplinary marks.

3 - In addition to the aforementioned conditions, a candidate for promotion from the rank of First Lieutenant to the rank of Captain and from the rank of Major to the rank of Lieutenant Colonel shall be required to pass a professional competitive examination the rules of which shall be laid down by the Higher Council of Customs upon the proposal of the Director General of Customs.
If a Lieutenant is not promoted by selection to the rank of First Lieutenant, he shall be promoted automatically to this rank upon completing four years in his rank.

The promotion of officers shall take place by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance and the recommendation of the Higher Council of Customs, within the limits of vacant positions and according to the order of their names on the promotion roster.

In the event that a number of positions fall vacant in one of the ranks and there is not a sufficient number of candidates to fill these positions, a number of officers equal to the number of vacant positions in the said rank may be appointed to the rank immediately below it.

The provisions of Articles 81 to 90 inclusive and Articles 98 to 101 inclusive of Legislative Decree No. 10 dated 7 July 1967, which determine the status of officers in the Army, shall apply to the officers of the Customs Police.

In this regard, the Minister of Finance shall exercise the powers granted to the Minister of National Defence, and the Higher Council of Customs, the powers granted to the Commander of the Army.

The provisions applicable to the officers of the Internal Security Forces, in respect of the amount of the military equipment allowance, termed prior to the issuance of this Law "official uniform allowance", and the rules for benefiting therefrom, shall apply to customs officers in active service and those who have been or will be placed on retirement.

Specialisation Allowance Personnel of the technical corps shall be entitled to receive a specialisation allowance the rates of which shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance after consulting the opinion of the Higher Council of Customs.

Men of the Customs Police must serve in the posts designated for them and reside therein or in their suburbs. Appointment to these posts or transfer thereto shall take place:

1 - For officers: by a decision of the Higher Council of Customs after consulting the opinion of the Director General of Customs.

2 - For non-commissioned officers and enlisted personnel: by an order of the Director General of Customs. None of the men of the Customs Police shall be entitled to request his transfer until after the expiry of two years of his presence at the post.

Upon the promotion of personnel of the Customs Police from one rank to another, the promoted person shall receive the salary of the new rank that is immediately above his salary prior to promotion, provided that the increase in his salary is not less than the value of one step of his new rank; if this increase is less than the value of two steps, he shall retain the seniority qualifying for step advancement. If this increase is equal to the value of two steps or more, he shall lose the seniority in the step in which he was prior to promotion and his new step advancement shall commence with effect from the date of his promotion.

In case of illness, medical examinations on the basis of which sick leaves are granted shall be conducted by military physicians, in agreement with the military authorities. However, the Minister of Finance may, at the request of the Higher Council of Customs, contract with civilian physicians for the same purpose, should the need arise, within the available appropriations and following the approval of the Council of Ministers.

The Medical Committee referred to in this Law shall be appointed by a decision of the Higher Council of Customs, after consulting the Director General of Customs, in agreement with the military authorities, as follows:

1 - An officer of at least the rank of Captain, as Chairman.

2 - Two physicians from among the physicians mentioned in Article 54 of this Law - as two members.

3 - An officer from the Customs - as Rapporteur.

The duties of the Medical Committee shall be determined as follows:

1 - Examining the health conditions of employees referred to it for the purpose of:

- Determining the duration of medical treatment or deciding on placement in temporary or permanent invalidity.

- Deciding whether or not the illness or accident is attributable to the service.

- Determining the degree of permanent disability in the event of deciding on placement in permanent invalidity.

2 - Examining the files of those who died in service to determine whether or not death was caused by the service.

3 - Summoning the fathers of the deceased to ascertain whether or not they are incapable of working.

4 - Examining all health matters referred by the competent authorities for the application of the provisions of this Law.

5 - Determining the infirmities that render the afflicted person incapable of attending to his own affairs, and establishing cases of insanity and weakness of sight that threatens total blindness.

6 - Invalidity shall be temporary when the infirmity is curable, and it shall be permanent when the infirmity is incurable and may be preceded by temporary invalidity, within the limits of the periods provided for in Article 60 of this Law.

The Higher Council of Customs, after consulting the Director General of Customs, and the men of the Customs Brigade referred to the Medical Committee, shall have the right to object to its decisions within fifteen days from the date of arrival of the file at the Higher Council of Customs, or from the date of its notification to the referred employee, whereupon such decisions shall be referred to a committee appointed and having its duties determined in the same manner as provided for in Articles 55 and 56 of this Law, provided that none of those appointed to the Medical Committee shall be among the members of this committee.

The Medical Committee, and the Medical Objections Committee, may seek the assistance, when necessary, of such specialist physicians as they deem fit, and their decisions shall not become final except after their ratification by the Higher Council of Customs.

All members of the Customs Brigade and members of their families who are in service, as well as those whose service has ended or will end, whether they have become entitled or will become entitled to a retirement pension or a dismissal indemnity, shall benefit from medical treatment, education grants, and all social benefits, from the budget of the Customs Administration and in accordance with what is applied to the personnel of the Internal Security Forces at all times.

1 - If one of the men of the Customs Brigade suffers an illness or an accident not attributable to the service nor aggravated by reason thereof which prevents him from performing it, he shall be entitled to receive medical treatment and to draw a full salary for a maximum period of eighteen consecutive or intermittent months within five years, and in the event that he is not cured after the expiry of this period, his placement in temporary or permanent invalidity shall be decided.

2 - However, if the illness or accident is attributable to the service and aggravated by reason thereof, the period of medical treatment mentioned in item (1) above shall be extended to twenty-four consecutive or intermittent months within five years.

3 - And if the illness or accident occurred in one of the following circumstances:

a - During an armed clash with an enemy, gangs, or groups disturbing security,

b - Following an assault to which he was subjected during the exercise of his duties.

c - Upon performing an act of selflessness to save the life of others.

The period of medical treatment mentioned in item (1) of this Article shall be extended to thirty months.

4 - Invalidity shall be temporary when the infirmity is curable and shall be decided for a period of one year for men of the Customs Brigade of all ranks, renewable for another year for officers. It shall be permanent when the infirmity is incurable and may be preceded by temporary invalidity within the limits of the period set forth above.

5 - In the cases provided for in item (3) of this Article, if the accident results in a permanent infirmity that does not affect the general health condition of the men of the Customs Brigade, but partially limits their physical capabilities, such as the amputation of a limb or the loss of use of one of the eyes, etc., they may be retained in service if they so wish, and employed in fields consistent with their condition.

If it is established before the expiry of the time limits specified in the preceding Article 60 that there is no hope of curing the sick or injured man of the Customs Brigade, he may be placed in temporary or permanent invalidity after receiving medical treatment for a period of not less than nine months if the illness or accident occurred in one of the circumstances specified in item (3) of Article 60, and not less than five months in the remaining circumstances.

The powers to grant sick leaves shall be determined as follows:

1 - Head of a Regional Brigade - ten days and under.

2 - Head of a Region - for a period not exceeding one month.

3 - Director General of Customs - for a period ranging between one month and three months.

4 - Higher Council of Customs - for a period exceeding three months.

The Higher Council of Customs and the Director General of Customs shall grant sick leaves to the personnel directly subordinate to each of them.

The rules for applying this Chapter and the procedures for organizing invalidity and death files shall be determined by a decision of the Higher Council of Customs, upon the proposal of the Director General of Customs.

Leave of absence shall not be considered a right; it is granted for up to 30 days per year, provided that it may be:

- Reduced for those whose services are unsatisfactory.

- Interrupted by recalling those on leave when the exigencies of the service so require.

Leave of absence for cadets of the Military Academy shall be granted in accordance with the internal regulations of the said institution.

In addition to the annual leave of absence, exceptional leaves of absence may be granted for up to seven days in the event of the marriage of the person concerned or the death of his spouse or one of his descendants, brothers, or sisters.

Annual leave of absence shall be granted all at once or in several installments, and may exceptionally be carried over to the following year.

The authority of superiors to grant leaves of absence, within Lebanese territory, shall be determined as follows:

1 - President of the Higher Council of Customs: for personnel directly subordinate to the Council.

2 - Director General of Customs: for the Inspecting Officer, regional officers, and personnel of the divisions directly subordinate to the Directorate General.

3 - Heads of Regions: for other Brigade personnel, within the scope of their work.

The right to grant leaves of absence abroad shall vest in the Higher Council of Customs upon the proposal of the Director General of Customs.

The following rewards shall be granted to the personnel of the Customs Brigade, under conditions determined by a decision of the Higher Council of Customs, upon the proposal of the Director General of Customs:

1 - Encouragement: from one mark to three marks.

2 - Commendation: from one certificate to three certificates.

3 - The Emblem of Honor.

4 - The Customs Medal.

Certificates of commendation granted to an employee who has been penalized by a delay in advancement shall automatically result in the cancellation of a previous penalty at the rate of three months for each certificate, for a period of one year from the date the penalty became final.

The Emblem of Honor granted to an employee who has been penalized by a delay in advancement shall automatically result in the cancellation of a previous penalty at the rate of six months, for a period of two years from the date the penalty became final.

The Emblem of Honor shall be issued in the form of a patent delivered to the person concerned, and certificates of commendation and the Emblem of Honor shall be announced to all units of the Customs Brigade, and kept in the personal files.

The powers of superiors in granting rewards shall be determined as follows:

1 - Marks of encouragement: The Higher Council of Customs, the Director General of Customs, or the regional heads, each in respect of the personnel subordinate to him.

2 - Certificates of appreciation: The Higher Council of Customs or the Director General of Customs, each in both of them in respect of the personnel subordinate to him.

3 - Emblem of Honour: The Higher Council of Customs upon the proposal of the Director General of Customs.

The Customs Administration shall be entitled to grant the Customs Medal provided for in Article 66 of this Law, and in Articles 19 and 20 of Legislative Decree No. 123 dated 12/6/1959, by decision of the Higher Council of General Customs, to an employee who has spent twenty years in the service of the State, including at least fifteen years in the Customs, and has merited appreciation during this period.

Without being bound by the period of service, this medal may be granted exceptionally to personnel of the Customs Brigade for extraordinary acts that required bravery and exposure to danger.

Decisions of the Higher Council of Customs ordering the granting of the Customs Medal shall be subject to the approval of the Decorations Council provided for in Legislative Decree No. 122, dated 12/6/1959.
Other public authorities may grant members of the Customs Brigade military or civil decorations as a reward to them for the services they perform which fall within their competence.

The following penalties shall be imposed on non-commissioned officers and enlisted personnel of the Customs Brigade:

A - First degree penalties:

1 - Reprimand.

2 - Salary deduction for up to five days.

B - Second degree penalties:

1 - Salary deduction for up to ten days.

2 - Deferment of step advancement for a maximum period of six months

3 - Suspension from work without salary for a period not exceeding one month.

C - Third degree penalties:

1 - Suspension from work without salary for a period exceeding one month and not exceeding one year.

2 - Reduction in step.

3 - Deletion from the promotion table.

4 - Reduction in rank.

5 - Dismissal from service.

6 - Discharge.

The following penalties shall be imposed on officers:

A - First degree penalties:

1 - Warning.

2 - Salary deduction for up to five days.

B - Second degree penalties:

1 - Salary deduction for up to ten days.

2 - Deferment of step advancement for a maximum period of one year.

C - Third degree penalties:

1 - Temporary cessation from service.

2 - Permanent cessation from service.

The powers of superiors in imposing penalties shall be determined as follows:

- The Higher Council of Customs: First and second degree penalties on personnel of the Customs Brigade of various ranks, upon the proposal of the Director General of Customs.

- The Director General of Customs: First degree penalties on personnel of the Customs Brigade of various ranks, and second degree penalties on non-commissioned officers and enlisted personnel only.

- The Head of the Region: First degree penalties on non-commissioned officers and enlisted personnel subordinate to him.

- The Controlling Officer: The officer attached to the Control Service: The penalties of reprimand and salary deduction for a period not exceeding three days on non-commissioned officers and guards.

- The Head of the Regional Brigade: The penalties of reprimand and salary deduction for a period not exceeding three days on non-commissioned officers and guards subordinate to him.
The superior who witnesses the offence or verifies it is the one who shall impose the penalty, or propose it if the offender is not subordinate to his unit.

Superiors of the second category in the administrative corps shall be entitled to impose the penalties of reprimand and salary deduction for a period not exceeding three days on personnel of the administrative body subordinate to them, within the scope of the powers provided for in the last paragraph of Article 26 of this Law.

Members of the Customs Brigade shall not be punished except after being interrogated in writing regarding the infraction attributed to them, and the interrogation shall be joined to the penalty file.

Penalties shall not be considered effective except after their ratification by the Higher Council of Customs or the Director General of Customs, each within his powers.
Third degree penalties shall be imposed on personnel of the Customs Brigade by decision of the Disciplinary Council provided for in this Chapter.

Third degree penalties shall not be imposed except in the following cases:

1 - Persistence in misconduct.

2 - Committing a grave offence in the service, or against military discipline, or prejudicial to honour.

Members of the Customs Brigade shall also be referred to the Disciplinary Council if a judicial judgment is rendered against them sentencing them to imprisonment for one month or more for disgraceful misdemeanours, or for three months or more for other offences.

Officers shall be referred to the Disciplinary Council by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance and the recommendation of the Higher Council of Customs. Non-commissioned officers and enlisted personnel shall be referred by a decision of the Higher Council of Customs upon the proposal of the Director General of Customs.

The decree or decision ordering the referral to the Disciplinary Council may provide for the suspension of the employee from work, and the latter shall remain suspended from work until the Disciplinary Council decides on his case or the authority that referred him to the Disciplinary Council revokes the measure of suspension.

The Disciplinary Council shall be composed:

1 - For officers, of:

- A director or head of service in the administrative corps in the Customs - as President.

- A head of service - three officers from the Customs - as members.

- An officer from the Customs - as rapporteur.

It is required that the member officers and the rapporteur be higher in rank or senior in the same rank than the officer referred to the Disciplinary Council, and if the required number of officers is not available, recourse shall be had to chief controllers from the Customs, by decision of the Higher Council of Customs after consulting the opinion of the Director General of Customs.

2 - For non-commissioned officers and enlisted personnel, of:

- A director or head of service from the administrative corps in the Customs. - as President.

- An officer from the Customs - as member

- A non-commissioned officer holding the rank of sergeant at least, provided that his rank is not lower than the rank of the non-commissioned officer referred to the Disciplinary Council, or that he is not junior to him in the rank, and if that occurs, an officer from the Customs shall be appointed - as member.

- An officer from the Customs holding the rank of first lieutenant or lieutenant - as rapporteur.

The referral decree or decision must include the formation of the panel of the Disciplinary Council that will hear the case, and this panel shall be considered dissolved ipso jure immediately upon the issuance of its decision.

If officers, non-commissioned officers, and enlisted personnel are referred to the Disciplinary Council in a single case, a single panel shall be formed to try them all on the basis of the highest in rank among those referred.

If it is decided to refer an employee from the administrative corps and another from the Customs Brigade corps to the Disciplinary Council in a single case, the General Disciplinary Council for State Employees shall hear the case.

The rapporteur must submit his report to the President of the Disciplinary Council within one month from the date the case file is lodged with him, and the Council must decide on the case within at most one month from the date the rapporteur's report is lodged with it.

The Board shall take a reasoned decision by a majority of votes, and such decision shall be subject to objection by the Higher Council of Customs or the referred official, if the latter is an officer, and by the Director General of Customs or the referred official, if the latter is a non-commissioned officer or an individual, within fifteen days from the date the file reaches the two administrative authorities mentioned above, or from the date of its notification to the referred official.

In this case, an appellate panel shall be appointed to examine the case anew, and this panel shall be formed in accordance with what is specified in Article 81 of this Law.

The panel so formed must abide by the time limits provided for in Article 83 of this Law.

The rapporteur before the Disciplinary Board, in both of its panels, shall not participate in the deliberation or in the voting.

Subject to the provisions of the first paragraph of this Article, the following shall not be subject to any form of administrative or judicial review, including an application for annulment for excess of power or a claim for compensation by way of full jurisdiction:

- Decrees and decisions referring officers, non-commissioned officers, and individuals to the Disciplinary Board.

- Decrees and decisions appointing the appellate panel.

- Decisions of the Disciplinary Board and the appellate panel.

- Decrees and decisions relating to the execution of the decisions of the Disciplinary Board and the appellate panel.

The authorities having competence in referring to the Disciplinary Board and in appointing the appellate panel, as well as the president, members, and rapporteur of the Disciplinary Board and the appellate panel, may not be prosecuted before any judicial authority with a claim for compensation on the ground of having committed a fault, whether gross or simple.

An officer, non-commissioned officer, or individual whom the Disciplinary Board rules to dismiss from service may not be reinstated into service in any department of the State, municipalities, or public institutions.

Disciplinary prosecution is independent of the public prosecution action, and the institution of a public prosecution action shall not preclude the institution of disciplinary prosecution and the adjudication thereof.
The regulations of the Disciplinary Board shall be determined by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance after consulting the opinion of the Higher Council of Customs.

Officers shall be mandatorily referred to retirement upon reaching the following age:

- Lieutenant: 52 years.

- First Lieutenant: 52 years.

- Captain: 52 years.

- Major: 53 years.

- Lieutenant Colonel: 54 years.

- Colonel: 56 years.

As for the officers in service upon the issuance of this Law, they shall be referred to retirement upon reaching the following age:

- First Lieutenant and Lieutenant: 56 years.

- Captain: 57 years.

- Major: 58 years.

- Lieutenant Colonel: 59 years.

Non-commissioned officers and guards shall be mandatorily referred to retirement, or discharged from service, in accordance with the following bases:

1 - Upon the expiry of their enlistment contract and non-renewal, with the exception of the cases provided for in the second paragraph of Article 32 of this Law.

2 - Upon reaching the following age:

- 50 years for corporals and guards - including seamen.

- 52 years for non-commissioned officers other than corporals - including seamen.

- 55 years for technical corporals and guards.

- 57 years for technical non-commissioned officers, other than corporals.

- 57 years for members of the administrative corps.

As for those who are in service on the date of issuance of this Law, they shall be referred to retirement upon reaching the following age:

- 54 years for non-commissioned officers and guards.

- 55 years for technical corporals and guards.

- 57 years for technical non-commissioned officers, other than corporals.

- 57 years for non-commissioned officers and guards who are selected to establish the administrative corps in accordance with the provisions of Article 26 of this Law.
The provisions of the Law on Retirement and Discharge from Service applicable to Army military personnel, including war additions, shall apply to the men of the Customs Brigade.

The men of the Customs Brigade shall be subject, by virtue of their capacity, to the general obligations relating to public officials and the men of the General Police, and the penalties and aggravation of penalties provided for in the law for felonies and misdemeanours committed by public officials during the performance of their duties shall apply to them.

The members of the Brigade are bound by professional secrecy, and they are prohibited from disclosing the names of informants to any authority whatsoever, and this prohibition shall not be lifted from them except by a decision of the Director General of Customs in light of the result of the customs investigation, or with the accompaniment of the informant himself.

The men of the Customs Brigade, during the performance of their duty, must be equipped with their service weapons, and they shall have the right to carry these weapons outside of duty in special cases determined by instructions from the monastery of the General of Customs.

The men of the Customs Brigade may not use their weapons except:

1 - In the case of legitimate defence provided for in Article 563 of the Penal Code.

2 - When they are unable, by any means whatsoever, to prevent their disarmament or to defend the place in which they are stationed, or the posts and persons in their custody, or when the resistance against them reaches a degree that they cannot overcome not by the force of arms.

3 - When they are unable, other than by the use of weapons, to stop vehicles, vessels, and other means of transport whose drivers do not comply with the warnings provided for in paragraph (4) of this Article and the signals that must accompany them. The men of the Customs Brigade may also use spikes or other obstacles in order to stop means of transport whose drivers refuse to submit to the warning.

4 - When they warn persons who attempt to flee or escape from them to stop, or repeat within their hearing the warning in a loud voice more than once "Customs, stop", and these persons refuse to comply with the warning, and it is not possible at that time to compel them to stop except by the use of weapons. In this case, it is mandatory that the flight be preceded or accompanied by general or specific evidence proving or making probable their almost certain participation in a felony or in an attempt by them to carry out a smuggling operation.

The men of the Customs Brigade must display calmness, composure, and humanitarian feeling, and they must endeavour to the utmost of their ability to avoid the use of weapons to the maximum extent. The commander of the forces must personally order the opening of fire, and must order a cease-fire after the first shots to ascertain the result, and must not order the resumption of fire if it becomes clear to him that the situation does not require it.
Retired officers shall have the right to retain the pistols that had been delivered to them personally during the performance of their duty, and to carry them.

The provisions of Book Three of the Code of Military Justice shall apply to the men of the Customs Brigade, and the provisions in force in the Internal Security Forces shall apply to them with respect to criminal trials.

The Director General of Customs shall exercise in this regard the powers granted to the Director General of the Internal Security Forces.

When the Military Court examines cases relating to the Customs Brigade, and the Court shall be formed equally of officers of the Army and of the Customs.

The Minister of Finance shall submit to the Minister of National Defence, on the first of each year, a list of the names of the officers whom he has chosen to participate in the composition of the Military Court examining cases of the Customs Brigade during the following year, upon the proposal of the Higher Council of Customs after consulting the opinion of the Director General of Customs.

In the event that the Administration is adjudged to pay damages for an injurious act to a third party committed by a member of the Customs Brigade during the performance of his duty, or by reason of his exercise thereof, it shall have the right of recourse against him if it deems that he committed a gross fault that was easy to avoid.

The authorities alongside which the forces of the Customs Brigade work in the execution of laws and regulations shall not have the right to exercise control over the forces because they are not subject to them in a "hierarchical" subordination, nor shall they have the right to interfere in the details of their special service.

The Customs Guard shall be provided with arms, ammunition, means of wired and wireless communication, surveillance means of all kinds, means of transport with all their equipment, and clothing, in accordance with the rules applied in the Internal Security Forces.

In this regard, the Minister of Finance shall exercise the powers of the Minister of Interior, and the Higher Council of Customs shall exercise the powers of the Director General of the Internal Security Forces.

Other equipment and supplies shall be provided thereto in accordance with the rules applied in the rest of the public administrations.
The forces of the Customs Guard shall render their full assistance to the authorities representing the various ministries, in the cases provided for by their special laws and regulations.

Officers and non-commissioned officers of the Customs Guard, with the exception of corporals, shall be deemed auxiliary judicial police officers to the Public Prosecutor within the scope of their competence within the areas in which they perform their duties, and they shall execute this mission in accordance with the procedures prescribed therefor in the Code of Criminal Procedure.

They shall also be deemed military judicial police officers when they perform, within the scope of their competence, missions involving offences subject to the Military Penal Code.

Notwithstanding the laws in force, expenditures resulting from the following cases shall not be subject to the prior audit of the Court of Accounts:

1 - The recall of former members of the Customs Guard to service in exceptional cases in which the military authorities so request.

2 - Promotions of members of the Customs Guard of all ranks.

3 - Military medals to which financial allowances are allocated.

All these cases shall be subject to the subsequent audit of the Court.

Financial aid and rewards social aid may be granted, by a decision of the Minister of Finance upon the proposal of the Higher Council of Customs, within the limits of the appropriations allocated in the budget for this purpose:

1 - To members of the Customs Guard.

2 - To retirees and to the families of deceased members of the Customs Guard.

3 - To educational institutions and orphanages, in consideration for accommodating and educating the children of members of the Customs Guard, whether retired or deceased.
Members of the Customs Guard who are in service on the date of promulgation of this Law shall retain their current rank and salaries, including their seniority.

Notwithstanding the provisions of Articles 44, 45 and 106 of this Law, and for the purpose of regularising the status of officers currently in service, officers who fulfil, on the date of promulgation of this Law, the following seniority conditions may be promoted by decree:

1 - To the rank of Lieutenant Colonel: Captains who have spent at least fifteen years in this rank.

2 - To the rank of Major: Captains who have spent at least ten years in this rank.

3 - To the rank of Captain: First Lieutenants who have spent at least eight years in this rank.

4 - To the rank of First Lieutenant: Lieutenants who have spent at least four years in this rank.

Notwithstanding the provisions of Articles 28, 29 and 106 of this Law, and for the purpose of regularising the status of sergeants currently in service, those who fulfil, on the date of promulgation of this Law, the following seniority conditions may be promoted:

1 - To the rank of Warrant Officer: Sergeants who have spent at least ten years in this rank.

2 - To the rank of First Sergeant: Sergeants who have spent at least six years in this rank.

Promotion shall be effected by decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance and the recommendation of the Higher Council of Customs.

Notwithstanding the provisions of Articles 28, 29, 30 and 106 of this Law, and for the purpose of regularising the status of garage chiefs currently in service, those who have spent in the actual practice of this function, on the date of promulgation of this Law, the following periods may be promoted:

1 - To the rank of Technical Warrant Officer: Mechanic guards who have been actually practising the function of garage chief for at least thirteen years.

2 - To the rank of Technical Sergeant: Mechanic guards who have been actually practising the function of garage chief for at least six years.

Promotion shall be effected by decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance and the recommendation of the Higher Council of Customs.
The provisions of the Civil Servants Regulations (Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6/1959) shall apply to the members of the Customs Guard in all matters not mentioned in this Law.
The provisions relating to enlistment, provided for in Articles 32, 33 and 34 of this Law, shall not apply to members of the Customs Guard who are in service prior to its promulgation.

The text of Article 24 of Legislative Decree No. 123 dated 12/6/1959 is repealed and replaced by the following text:

Office employees in the Customs, assigned to passenger formalities at land, sea and air border posts, shall be granted an official uniform allowance the amount of which shall be determined by a decision of the Higher Council of Customs upon the proposal of the Director General of Customs and the approval of the Civil Service Board, provided that the rank insignia of this uniform differ from those determined for the members of the Customs Guard.
At the end of the first paragraph of the first Article of Legislative Decree No. 114 dated 12/6/1959, the phrase "and the Customs Guard" is added.

The following are repealed:

1 - From Legislative Decree No. 123 dated 12/6/1959:

A - The texts set forth in Article 17 relating to the conditions of the competitive examination for the post of: guard - mechanic guard - sergeant - and lieutenant.

B - The following Articles: 18 - 21 - 22 - 23 and 25.

2 - From Decree No. 2868 dated 16/12/1959 relating to the organisation of the Ministry of Finance, amended by Decree No. 11801 dated 14/1/1963: the following Articles: 94 - 95 - 96 - 97 - 98 - 100 and 100 bis.

3 - From Legislative Decree No. 10 dated 7/7/1967: the phrase "customs guard" set forth in Article 144, relating to public posts "reserved for members of the Army, the Internal Security Forces and the General Security".

4 - From Decree No. 16292 dated 19/6/1957, and the amendments made thereto: the "Schedule of Ranks and Salaries of Customs Employees".
All provisions contrary to the provisions of this Law or inconsistent with its content are repealed.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.
The regulation of traffic and the use of roads open to public traffic shall be subject to the provisions of this Law and the schedules annexed thereto.

The draft law set forth in Decree No. 16977 dated 24/7/1964 providing for the amendment of Legislative Decree No. 140 (the Traffic Law) and the schedules annexed thereto, as amended by the Administration and Justice Committee and the Joint Committee composed of the Administration and Justice Committee and the Finance Committee on 25 October 1967, is hereby ratified. This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication.

Article 2: The following terms, wherever they appear in this Law, shall have the meanings set forth below 1- "Road" Every way open to the traffic of pedestrians, animals, and means of transport and traction, whether roads, squares, bridges, or the like. 2- "Carriageway" Chaussee The part of the road intended for the traffic of vehicles 3- "Track" Voie A side of the carriageway intended for traffic in one direction 4- "Lane" A part of the track whose width allows the passage of vehicles proceeding in single file and whose sides are clearly defined. 5- "Cycle track" A part of the public road reserved for the traffic of bicycles, raised above the road or separated from it by a "clear" separation. 6- "Built-up area" Every group of contiguous or closely spaced buildings standing on one side of the road or on both sides thereof so as to give it the appearance of a street. 7- "User" A driver of livestock, a driver of draught, pack, or riding animals, a driver of any vehicle not running on rails, and pedestrians. 8- "Vehicle" Every wheeled means of transport or traction propelled by mechanical or physical power (human or animal). 9- "Motor vehicle" Every vehicle propelled by an engine. 10- "Motor car" Every motor vehicle intended for the transport of persons or things, every vehicle intended for the transport of persons if connected to an electric current and not running on rails, and every motor vehicle not intended for the transport of persons or things but equipped with mechanical apparatus for special use. Excluded therefrom are motor vehicles designated for agriculture or public works and motorcycles. 11- "Agricultural vehicle" Every motor vehicle having more than two wheels, designed and manufactured for traction and used specifically in agricultural exploitation. 12- "Public works vehicle" Every motor vehicle having more than two wheels, designed and manufactured to be used specifically in public works projects and not used for the transport of goods and persons on public roads. ' 13- "Trailers": a - "Trailer" Every means of transporting things or persons equipped with two or more axles, designed and manufactured to be drawn by a motor car operating for the same purpose. b - "Agricultural trailer" Every means of transporting things equipped with one or more axles, designed to be drawn by an agricultural vehicle. c - "Public works trailers" Equipment manufactured specifically for the needs of a public works project, not intended for the transport of things or persons, equipped with one or more axles, drawn by a public works vehicle. 14- "Semi-trailers" Every means of transporting things or persons equipped with one or more rear axles and without a front axle, designed and manufactured to be drawn by another vehicle in such a manner that part of its weight rests upon the drawing vehicle. 15- "Motorcycle" Every motor vehicle with two or three wheels equipped with a combustion engine, whose unladen weight does not exceed four hundred kilograms and whose specifications are set out in Title Four of this Law. 16- "Ordinary bicycle" Every vehicle with two, three, or four wheels, not equipped with an engine, but propelled by the power of its rider. 17- "Stopping" Standing for a limited period of time necessitated by the exigencies of traffic or the setting down or taking up of passengers. 18- "Waiting" Stopping for a period of time exceeding the period necessary for taking up or setting down passengers. 19- "Parking" Stationing in a place for a long time. 20- "Competent Department" The Motor Vehicles and Machinery Registration Service in Beirut and its sections in the provinces. 21- "Concessions" Concessions relating to a public service. 1- Notwithstanding the rule set forth in Article (13) of this Law, overtaking on the right of a vehicle is permitted if its driver signals that he intends to turn to the left under the conditions prescribed in Article 25 of this Law. 2- Notwithstanding the rule set forth in Article (13) of this Law, overtaking on the right is permitted on carriageways containing more than two lanes, provided that the driver ensures that his moving from one lane to another does not cause danger or inconvenience to others. 3- Overtaking vehicles running on railway tracks extending along the carriageway must take place on the right side if the space between such vehicles and the edge of the carriageway is sufficient. The aforementioned vehicles may be overtaken on the left side: a - On roads where traffic is one-way. b - On other roads if the overtaking allows meeting an oncoming vehicle in the free part of the carriageway.
A driver is prohibited from overtaking a vehicle running on railway tracks and stopped during the alighting or boarding of passengers, on the side from which the alighting or boarding takes place.

1- If the carriageway is not divided into lanes marked by lines, overtaking is prohibited on curves and at the crests of hills and in general where forward visibility is insufficient, except provided that the left half of the carriageway remains free. 2- And overtaking is prohibited: a - At unguarded railway crossings and on bridges and in tunnels. b - At road intersections, unless the driver is travelling on a section of the road on which he has the right of priority. c - If the vehicle intended to be overtaken is itself overtaking another vehicle. d - In the event that a column of motor vehicles has stopped due to traffic obstruction or due to the presence of a signal requiring it to stop.

If traffic is two-way on a carriageway containing three lanes marked by broken lines, the overtaking driver is prohibited from using the lane situated to his extreme left and is permitted to use the middle lane during the overtaking manoeuvre only.
The overtaking driver shall immediately return to keeping to his right after ensuring that this can be done without any hazard.
Drivers about to be overtaken shall immediately keep to the extreme right of the road without increasing the speed of their vehicles.

1- In cases where the shape of the carriageway, its condition, or the free space of its width does not allow meeting or overtaking with complete ease and safety, drivers of vehicles whose width or the width of whose load exceeds two metres or whose length exceeds eight metres (including their trailers) must reduce their speed and, if necessary, stop or pull aside. "And that is in order to facilitate the passage of smaller vehicles". 2- In the same cases, if a vehicle of the Security Forces, the Fire Brigade, or the Ambulance Service gives warning of its approach by means of the signals set forth in Articles (95) and (219) of this Law, other road users must reduce their speed and, if necessary, stop or pull aside, "and that is in order to facilitate the passage of these vehicles"

Every driver of a vehicle among the vehicles provided for in Article (77) of this Law shall indicate by means of the signal mentioned in Article (92), first paragraph, that he has received the warning of the driver who wishes to overtake him.

The driver of a vehicle or of animals shall ascertain, when approaching a road intersection, that the carriageway he intends to cross is free, and shall proceed at a speed which he reduces in proportion to the worsening of visibility, and he shall give warning, when necessary, of his approach, while observing the traffic measures that may be taken inside built-up areas in application of the provisions of Article (35) of this Law.
