- To cover the budget deficit in accordance with the provisions of Article 196 of this Law.

- To cover additional appropriations (supplementary and extraordinary).

- To finance construction projects.

No amount may be taken from the reserve fund except by law. Every amount decided to be taken from the reserve fund must be recorded immediately in the records of the Central Finance Accountant. The manner of recording these entries shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

Deposits and guarantees shall be delivered to the Treasury, pursuant to an order issued by a competent authority, and the reasons for the deposit shall be recorded on the receipts relating thereto, and they shall not be returned to their owners except pursuant to an order from the competent authority, and after recovering the receipts.

If the receipts for deposits or guarantees are lost, they shall be replaced by an undertaking from their owners to bear all damages and losses that may result from the misuse of the lost receipt throughout five years.

Treasury advances are supplies granted from its assets:

1- To supply the warehouses of public administrations with supplies shared among more than one administration.

2- To purchase storable materials intended for use in a current or subsequent financial year.

3- To fund the funds of public institutions and municipalities as well as independent funds established by law.

The granting of Treasury advances intended to fund one of the funds mentioned in paragraph 3 of the preceding Article shall be conditional:

1- Upon the verification by the Minister of Finance of the ability of the borrowing entity to repay the advance in cash within the time limit set for its settlement.

2- Upon an undertaking by the borrowing entity to mandatorily allocate in its budget the appropriations necessary to settle the advance within the set time limit.

3- Upon the approval of the legislative authority if the time limit for its settlement exceeds twelve months.

- Treasury advances for the purposes specified in Article 203 of this Law shall be granted by decree

upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance and the request of the competent administrations.

- The Government must inform the Chamber of Deputies of the decided advances within one month.

There shall be mentioned in a decree taken in the Council of Ministers:

The custodian of the advance in the cases provided for in the preceding paragraphs 1 and 2 of Article 203, and the borrowing entity in the case provided for in paragraph 3 of the same Article. And the purpose of the advance, its amount, the method of its payment, the conditions of its settlement, and other conditions that the Minister of Finance deems necessary to impose.
Treasury advances shall be paid pursuant to orders issued by the Central Accountant in which reference is made to a decree taken in the Council of Ministers that authorised them.
The advance shall not be used for other than the purpose for which it was granted.

Treasury advances provided for in paragraphs 1 and 2 of Article 203 of this Law shall be settled by virtue of payment orders issued against the budget. And Treasury advances provided for in paragraph 3 of the same Article shall be settled by returning their value in cash to the Treasury within the time limits set therefor.
The accountant must pursue the settlement of Treasury advances in accordance with the conditions under which they were granted and within the set time limits.

The accountant may deduct directly from the salary and allowances of the custodian of the advance the amounts the use of which is not proven, or which he does not settle within the set time limits, and he may also execute automatically against him any other legal measure that secures the recovery of these amounts. The time limit for settlement may be extended in exceptional cases and circumstances by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

If one of the borrowing administrations delays in settling the Treasury advance granted to it, the Central Finance Accountant shall have the right to deduct it directly from whatever funds this administration has with the Treasury.

There shall be annexed to the draft law on the closure of accounts a statement of the Treasury advances granted in accordance with the provisions of Article 203 of this Law and of what was settled thereof during the budget year.
Materials accounting shall include all entries and documents necessary to show the inventory of materials owned by public administrations and to record their movement.
All public administrations must keep materials accounting. And institutions subject to the supervision of the State must keep materials accounting that enables the exercise of this supervision.

Every person entrusted with keeping or using the materials provided for in Article 214 of this Law is financially liable for them.

And the same liability may be incurred by the persons entrusted with keeping the accounts of materials and supervising them.

The application of the provisions of this Chapter shall be limited to materials located within the Lebanese territory and in Lebanese missions abroad.

And they shall not apply to the equipment of armies in active service nor to the equipment used in naval and aerial vessels.
The details of the application of the provisions of this Chapter shall be regulated by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.
The appropriations for salaries and allowances relating to members of the Army and personnel of the Internal Security Forces and General Security shall be recorded in a single item without breakdown.
Contracting shall be undertaken by a special committee formed in accordance with regulations determined by a decree upon the proposal of the competent Minister.

Agreements may be concluded by mutual consent for whatever supplies, works, and services are needed by the Army, the Internal Security Forces, General Security, and Customs detachments in the two cases of war and emergency and exceptional cases that require taking immediate measures, pursuant to a prior decision from the Commander of the Army.

The Ministry of National Defense may, when concluding contracts with foreign governments or institutions supervised or recommended by these governments for the purchase of weapons, ammunition, equipment, and apparatuses, exempt the entity with which it contracts from the conditions relating to domicile, guarantee, and fines, and the requirement of delivery before payment.

The Ministry of National Defence may request, in accordance with the procedures set forth in Article 117 of this Law, the reuse of appropriations corresponding to:

1- The value of supplies furnished for a price by the Army Administration to officers and enlisted personnel in their personal capacity.

2- The value of supplies charged by the Army Administration to the officers and enlisted personnel responsible for the loss or damage thereof.

3- The value of weapons, ammunition, equipment and apparatus sold by the Army Command to a public administration or public institution.

4- The value of used supplies and the consideration for services rendered for the account of public administrations and public institutions or for the benefit of a natural or legal person.
The Ministry of National Defence may deduct from the salary entitlements disbursed out of the appropriations of the current year sums paid in error or without right in previous years.

The value of salaries and their accessories, and of transport and travel advances received by units in any given year in excess of their entitlements and refunded by them to the Treasury before the first of May of the following year, shall be entered on the date of their refund under the revenues of the current year in accordance with the provisions of Article 8 of this Law.

Supplementary appropriations equal to the value of the refunded sums may be opened by decision of the Minister of Finance under the salaries item of the Army budget, provided that they are covered by an equivalent increase in revenues.

With effect from the first of August of each year, the Minister of National Defence may commit, on the account of the following year, equipment expenditures amounting to two thirds of the appropriations allocated for this purpose for the current year in the budgets of the Army, the Internal Security Forces and the General Security, and those earmarked for the Customs detachments in the budget of the Ministry of Finance.

No expenditures to the principle of which the legislative authority has not previously agreed may be committed by this means.

The provisions of Articles 137 and 138 of this Law may be applied to the contracts referred to in this Article even before the commencement of the new year.
Supplies accountants in the Army shall be appointed by decision of its Commander.
Army accountants shall not be subject to the security bond regime to which other accountants are subject.

Neither the Court of Accounts nor the financial inspectors may request to inspect, or inspect, documents and information relating to military secrecy, unless the Army Commander consents thereto. The audit by the Court of Accounts of the supplies accounts pertaining to the Army shall be conducted on site and on the basis of the records kept by the Command and the supporting documents produced by it.

The provisions of Articles 220 to 230 inclusive of this Law shall apply to the Internal Security Forces, such that the Minister of Interior and the Director General of the Internal Security Forces shall each exercise, within his respective competence, the powers vested in the Minister of National Defence and the Army Commander.

As for the General Security and the Customs detachments, the provisions of Articles 220, 222, 228, 229 and 230 of this Law shall apply, subject to the special regulations governing each of these two bodies.
Permanent budgetary advances shall be placed at the disposal of foreign missions, to be used by each mission to pay its expenditures for a maximum of six months.

Contract awarding in foreign missions shall be conducted by a special committee appointed by decision of the head of the mission, whenever possible; otherwise, it shall be conducted in accordance with procedures determined by decision of the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants.
The expenditures of delegations abroad may be substantiated by detailed statements certified by the head of the delegation on his own responsibility.

Representation expenditures abroad may be substantiated by detailed statements drawn up by the head of the foreign mission and certified by the Secretary General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants.

Administrative expenditures incurred by foreign missions shall be substantiated in the same manner where the expenditure does not exceed 500 pounds each time.

Notwithstanding any other text or measure, the financial instructions issued by the joint decision of the Ministers of Finance and of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants dated 29/4/1999 and the amendments thereto shall apply to Lebanese diplomatic and consular missions with respect to the mechanisms for committing and liquidating expenditures, the conditions for committing them, the reservation and annual carry-over of appropriations, and the rules for keeping registers, organising accounting entries, and collecting and disbursing funds.

Allowances, salaries and monthly compensations pertaining to the office or attached to the salary shall be paid on the first of each month.

This measure shall apply to all permanent and temporary employees with the exception of probationers among them, and shall also apply to pensioners and their heirs.

The sum paid in execution of the provisions of the preceding paragraph and of the laws in force shall remain an acquired right for the person who received it, and nothing thereof shall be recovered for the benefit of the Treasury in any case.
The accounting of Posts, Telegraphs and Telephones shall be subject to its own special regulations and to the provisions of this Law in all matters not inconsistent with the said regulations.
The conditions for the application of this Law to municipalities shall be determined by decrees issued upon the proposal of the Ministers of Interior and of Finance.

The conditions for the application of this Law to autonomous agencies and other public institutions shall be determined by decrees issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance and the supervisory minister.

All public funds defined in Article 2 of this Law must be deposited in the account opened at the Bank of Lebanon in the name of the Public Treasury.

The date of application of this Article with respect to municipalities and the public institutions attached thereto shall be determined by a decree taken upon the proposal of the Ministers of Interior and of Finance.

Public administrations, municipalities, public institutions and the legal persons mentioned in the second Article of this Law are prohibited from opening accounts in private banks or opening a special account of their own at the Bank of Lebanon.
A special account shall be opened in the records of the Treasury Department at the Ministry of Finance in the name of each of the entities mentioned in the preceding Article.

- The provisions relating to the maximum sums that each of them is entitled to retain in its own cash offices and the rules for operating the accounts provided for in Article 244 above shall be determined by decision of the Minister of Finance, or by a joint decision of the Minister of Finance and the Minister of Interior with respect to municipalities and municipal public institutions.

- The public administrations, municipalities and public institutions mentioned in this Title shall continue to collect the revenues accruing to them.

As for payment operations, they shall be effected through their cash offices if their value does not exceed a maximum limit fixed by decision of the Minister of Finance, or by a joint decision of the Ministers of Finance and of Interior with respect to municipalities and municipal public institutions; they shall be paid through the Treasury cash office if they exceed this limit.

- Public administrations and public institutions that do not have special cash offices of their own shall continue to carry out all collection and payment operations through the Treasury cash office.
The Treasury Department may not stay any payment operation ordered by one of the entities that has a special account in its records, so long as it has a sufficient credit balance in that account.

The details of the application of Articles 242 to 246 of this Law, and in particular those relating to the keeping of accounts, the organisation of accounting entries, the form of registers and printed forms, the manner in which the Treasury pays the expenditures of the administrations and institutions that have an account in its records, as well as the time limits within which financial transactions must be completed, shall be determined by decision of the Minister of Finance, or by a joint decision of the Ministers of Finance and of Interior with respect to municipalities and municipal public institutions.

The bill transmitted by Decree No. 8176 dated 20/03/1996 relating to narcotics, psychotropic substances and precursors, as amended by the Administration and Justice Committee in the Chamber of Deputies, has been approved. This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication and in the Official Gazette.
Everything relating to narcotics in the broad sense, psychotropic substances and precursors shall be subject to the provisions of this Law.

In this Law, the following terms are adopted:

- The expression "narcotics", by which is meant all plants, natural and synthetic substances, and products placed under control and subject to supervisory measures pursuant to the provisions of this Law.

- The expression "international treaties" includes the Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs of 1961 as amended by the 1972 Protocol, the Convention on Psychotropic Substances of 1971, and the United Nations Convention against Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances of 1988

- The expression "narcotic substances": the lists of natural and synthetic substances included in the four Schedules adopted in the amended Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs of 1961 and the substances added thereto in application of this treaty

- The expression "psychotropic substances": the lists of natural and synthetic substances included in the four Schedules adopted in the Convention on Psychotropic Substances of 1971 and the substances added thereto in application of the said treaty.

- The expression "precursors", that is, all chemical products used in the operations of manufacturing narcotic substances and psychotropic substances.

- The expression "preparation": every solution or mixture, whatever its form, containing one or more substances of narcotics.

- The expression "drug": every preparation for a therapeutic purpose containing one of the substances placed under control.

- The expression "production": the separation of substances placed under control from their plant origin.

- The expression "manufacture": all operations other than production by which the substances mentioned above are obtained, and including purification, extraction, transformation, and the manufacture of preparations other than those compounded by pharmacies pursuant to a medical prescription.

- The expression "importation": the introduction of substances placed under control into Lebanon.

- The expression "exportation": the removal of substances placed under control from Lebanon.

- The expression "transport": the transport of substances placed under control within Lebanese territory from one place to another or by way of transit.

- The expression "licence": the permission in principle to practise one or some of the operations relating to narcotics set forth in Article 13 of this Law.

- The expression "permit" or authorisation: the written approval given to the licensed authority to carry out an individual operation among the operations mentioned in the preceding paragraph.

The expression commercial "carrier": any natural or legal person working in the field of transporting persons or goods for consideration.

- The expression controlled "delivery": the method of allowing illicit consignments of narcotics to continue on their way within the borders of the State or outside it, with the knowledge of its competent authorities and under their supervision, with a view to identifying the persons involved in committing narcotics offences.

- The expression "proceeds": or funds derived or obtained, directly or indirectly, from the commission of a narcotics offence.

- The expression "freezing" and preservation: the temporary prohibition on the transfer, conversion, disposal or conversion of funds, or the temporary taking of possession or attachment thereof, pursuant to an order from the competent authority.

- The expression "funds": assets of whatever kind, whether corporeal or incorporeal, movable or immovable, tangible or intangible, and legal documents or instruments proving title thereto and the rights relating thereto.

- The expression "transit State": a State through the territory of which narcotics are transported and which is neither their place of origin nor their place of final destination.

- The expression Lebanese "territory": the meaning given to it by Articles 15 to 18 inclusive of the General Penal Code.

- The expression "drug abuse" and "illicit use": the personal use of narcotic or controlled drugs without a medical prescription.

- The expression "drug addict": every person in a state of physical or psychological dependence on a controlled narcotic drug.

- The expression "treatment for addiction": treatment aimed at removing the state of dependence on the drug.

- The expression "the Committee": the Committee for Combating Drug Addiction.

- The expression "precursors", that is, all other chemical products used in the operations of manufacturing narcotic substances and psychotropic substances.

- The expression "money laundering", that is, concealing or disguising the illicit origin of movable or immovable funds or resources resulting from offences of narcotics, psychotropic substances and precursors.

This Part deals with:

- The classification of narcotics

- The prohibition of the cultivation of plants from which narcotics result

- The prohibition of the substances and preparations included in Schedule I

- The regulatory provisions applicable to the substances and preparations of Schedules II and III

- The provisions applicable to Schedule IV

The plants, substances and preparations covered by this Law shall be placed under control and classified, according to the supervisory measures to which they are subject, in the four Schedules annexed to this Law.

All plants and substances classified as narcotic substances or psychotropic substances pursuant to or in application of international treaties and their preparations, and all plants and substances dangerous to public health because of the harmful consequences resulting from their abuse, shall be classified in the first three Schedules according to the gravity of their danger and the extent of their medical utility

- Schedule I: Plants and substances of high danger which have no medical utility

- Schedule II: Plants and substances of high danger which have medical utility

- Schedule III: Dangerous plants and substances which have utility in medicine.

All substances used in the manufacture of narcotic substances and psychotropic substances and classified pursuant to or in application of the Convention against Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances of 1988, and all other chemical products used in the operations of manufacturing narcotic substances and psychotropic substances, shall be known as precursors and included in Schedule IV.

The four Schedules annexed to this Law shall be deemed regulatory matter that may be amended by inserting a new entry, by deletion therefrom, or by transfer from one Schedule to another Schedule, by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Health.
Plants and substances shall be included under their common international designations or under their scientific designations in the absence of those former designations.

Solid or liquid mixtures containing one or several controlled substances and psychotropic substances divided into doses shall be deemed preparations and shall be subject to the same regime applicable to the substances they contain, and preparations containing two or more substances governed by different regimes shall be subject to the regime of the substance for which the severest penalty is prescribed.

Preparations containing substances included in Schedules II, III and IV and compounded in such a way as to render the risk of their abuse non-existent or negligible, owing to the impossibility of re-separating their substances in quantities that facilitate abuse and by easily applicable methods, may be exempted from some of the supervisory measures provided for in this Law, and the exemption shall be effected by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Health.

Where the application is submitted for the purpose of commercial activity or in the field of wholesale distribution, the names of the substances and preparations that shall be the subject of such activity shall be specified.

Where the application is submitted for the purpose of exportation and importation, there shall be specified therein the nature of the intended operations, the countries with which such operations shall take place, the names, nature and quantity of the substances and preparations in respect of which the licence is requested, the import or export authorisation granted to the applicant by the Government of the other country, the importer or exporter, the reasons justifying his operation, its approximate date, and all particulars required of him by the Ministry of Public Health.

As amended by Law 193 dated 24/5/2000, Official Gazette 23 dated 1/6/2000

The Minister of Public Health shall have the right to accept or reject the licence application, provided that he decides thereon within ninety days from the date of its submission, and the application shall be deemed rejected in the event of failure to decide thereon within this time limit.

In addition to the provisions of Article 17 of this Law, the period of validity of the licence shall be specified therein, and it shall be deemed cancelled if the operation thereof is not commenced within ninety days from the granting thereof.

The licence shall state the substances and preparations connected with the licensed activity, the quantities that it shall cover, the type of operations that shall be carried out, the accounting that shall be followed, and all other conditions that the licensee must fulfil and the obligations with which he must comply, and the licence shall clarify the permissible operations directly connected with the licensed activity.

No change may be introduced to the status of the establishment, whether in respect of its object, its address, the nature of its activity, the substances covered by such activity, or the procedures of manufacture, extraction or other operations, except after obtaining an amendment to the licence granted under the same conditions required for granting the original licence.

Public and private establishments may not carry out operations relating to the acquisition, sale or distribution of plants, substances or preparations of Schedules II and III unless carried out with natural or legal persons licensed for that purpose.

As amended by Law 193 dated 24/5/2000, Official Gazette 23 dated 1/6/2000

The licence is personal and may not be sold, delivered or assigned except after the approval of the Minister of Public Health and to a natural or legal person licensed for the same activity covering the licensed substances; in such case, the Minister of Public Health shall issue a decision setting out the special conditions and procedures for the delivery and receipt of the narcotic drugs that have been sold or assigned.

In the event of the issuance of a provision prohibiting one or several operations relating to the plants, substances and preparations of Schedules II and III, every prior licence concerning such operation or operations shall be cancelled, and the licensee shall have no right to any compensation as a result thereof.

In the event of the death of the licence holder or the cessation of his activity, the Minister of Public Health may authorise the continuation of the activity for a period not exceeding ninety days under the responsibility of another person who possesses the required qualifications to assume the obligations imposed pursuant to the Law and the licence.

Every licensed premises whose licence is cancelled or not renewed upon the expiry of its term shall have its holdings of narcotic drugs liquidated under the supervision of a committee formed by the Minister of Public Health for this purpose.
The licence may be withdrawn if it is established that the licence application contained incorrect particulars.

The licence shall be cancelled ipso jure after it has been granted if a final judgment is rendered against its holder for one of the offences provided for in this Law, and in the event that the licensee is prosecuted for committing one of these offences, the effect of the licence may be suspended pending the rendering of the judgment.

The licence may be cancelled in the event that contraventions are established during the exercise of the licensed activity, especially where this relates to failure to fulfil the obligations specified in the licence or the loss of one of the conditions required by the licence, and in the event of negligence or a non-serious contravention, the effect of the licence shall be suspended for a period not exceeding six months.

The licence may not be cancelled in accordance with the preceding Article or suspended except after enabling the licensee to submit his explanations regarding the contraventions imputed to him, and the decision must be reasoned. The decision of cancellation or suspension shall not preclude disciplinary or criminal prosecutions.

Where the activity of the establishment ceases, or its licence is cancelled or its term expires, the Minister of Public Health shall recover the order books and registers and shall take the appropriate measures to transfer the possession of the stocks that become unlawfully possessed, subject to what may be provided for by judicial decisions, if any.

It shall not be permitted to carry out the operations provided for in a pharmacy, laboratory, warehouse or pharmaceutical factory that fulfils the conditions determined by the Minister of Public Health.

As amended by Law 193 dated 24/5/2000, Official Gazette 23 dated 1/6/2000

The licence to use installations or premises held by a specifically designated private or public establishment, in whole or by using parts thereof, for the purpose of producing plants, substances or preparations listed in Schedules II and III, or for the purpose of their manufacture, extraction, preparation, transformation, trade, wholesale distribution, international trade, exportation, importation and industrial use, shall be issued; this licence shall be issued by a decision of the Minister of Public Health, and the licence applicant shall be notified of the granting or rejection thereof within ninety days from the date of lodging the application.

No licence may be granted except for installations and premises used by a natural or legal person holding the licence provided for in Article 15 of this Law.

Related text: Conditions and documents required to obtain a licence for the operations and installations provided for in Law No. 673 dated 16/03/1998 and its amendments relating to narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances and precursors

The licence application shall specify the geographical location of each installation or each place that shall be used in whole or in part, with a statement of the legal basis for the establishment's possession thereof. The application shall be accompanied by a description of the designated constructions and premises and an accurate plan thereof. The application shall set out the security measures intended to be taken to facilitate the supervision of the plants, substances and preparations concerned and the manufactured products and to prevent their theft and other operations of diversion thereof. The application shall also specify the name and address of the natural or legal person who shall be specifically entrusted with applying the intended security measures.

The granting of the licence shall be conditional upon verifying that the installations and premises that shall be used in whole or in part meet the security standards determined by a joint decision of the Ministers of Public Health and of the Interior.

Each installation or place shall be required to have its own separate licence; however, authorisation may be granted in a single decision to use several installations or premises, and the decision authorising the exercise of the activities provided for in Section I of this Chapter may at the same time include a licence to use the installations and premises specified in the application.

The licence shall specify the period of its validity and shall state the premises and installations and, where applicable, the parts thereof licensed for use, and the licence shall specify the security measures that must be taken and the natural or legal person who shall be responsible for applying these measures.

No branch may be established, nor may any new installations or premises or new parts thereof be used, nor may any change be introduced to the installations and premises licensed for use or any amendment to the security measures specified in the licence, except after authorisation by virtue of a decree taken in the Council of Ministers. The decision granting or rejecting the authorisation shall be issued within one month from the date of lodging the application.

The licence shall be withdrawn from the installations or premises in their entirety or from parts thereof in the event of non-compliance with the obligations specified in the licence or in the event of the inclusion of incorrect particulars in the application, by virtue of a decree taken in the Council of Ministers.

No decision to refuse, suspend or withdraw the licence may be issued unless the natural or legal person concerned, or the person responsible for the public institution concerned, has been invited to provide all necessary clarifications, and the decision shall be reasoned and the designated person shall be notified thereof, and it shall be served upon the departments competent to establish violations, and there shall also be sent to these departments the complete annual list of the facilities and premises licensed to be used for the private and governmental institutions concerned.
The suspension of the licence to use the facilities and premises shall entail the revocation of the licence to practise the activities for which it was granted.

The Minister of Public Health shall determine each year the maximum quantities of the various substances and preparations that each licensed public or private institution may possess, having regard to the normal course of its business and the state of the market; these quantities may be modified during the year where necessary, and in all cases the total of the quantities determined for the various institutions may not exceed the overall maximum quantity that the National Council for Narcotic Drugs Affairs has approved for export and import, or production, or manufacture, or trading in, or industrial use.

The Minister of Public Health shall determine each year, having regard to the state of the market, the maximum quantities of the various substances and preparations that each private or governmental institution is entitled to manufacture, and this quantity may be modified during the year where necessary, and in pharmaceutical factories licensed in accordance with the provisions of this Law, narcotic drugs may not be used except in the manufacture of special medical preparations.
None other than licensed institutions that use licensed facilities and premises may engage in international trade in the plants, substances and preparations listed in Schedules II and III.

As amended by Law 193 dated 24/5/2000 -

All export and import operations shall be subject to obtaining a prior authorisation from the Minister of Public Health through the Department of Narcotic Drugs at the Ministry, on a form of a model determined by the Ministry of Public Health in accordance with the model established by the Commission on Narcotic Drugs of the Economic and Social Council of the United Nations.

- The application to obtain the authorisation shall include:

The nature of the intended operation

- The name and address of each of the importer and the exporter, and the name and address of the consignee if known

- The international non-proprietary name of each substance, or failing that its name as set out in the international conventions, and its pharmaceutical form, and if the matter relates to a preparation, its name, if any, shall be stated, and the quantity of each substance and preparation covered by the operation, the period it will take, the method of transport or shipping that will be used, and the crossing point on the Lebanese border, and there shall be attached to the application for an export authorisation the import certificate issued by the government of the importing country.

- The export and import authorisation shall contain the same particulars as are required in the application relating to the operation whose procedures the authorisation permits, and the import authorisation shall specify whether such import will be effected in a single consignment or in several consignments, and the export authorisation shall include, in addition thereto, the number and date of the import certificate confirming that the import of the substance or preparation is licensed.
- A certified copy of the export authorisation shall be attached to each consignment, and the Ministry of Public Health shall send a copy thereof to the importing country.

Narcotic drugs may not be imported, exported or transported inside packages containing other substances, and their dispatch - even if by way of a sample - shall be inside insured packages, and the full trade and scientific name of the substance, its nature, its quantity, its concentration, the method of its preservation and use, and the markings prescribed by the World Health Organization shall be indicated on the packages.

If the quantity of plants, substances or preparations actually imported is less than the quantity indicated in the export authorisation, the Minister of Public Health shall state that in the authorisation and in all official copies thereof.

There shall be indicated in commercial documents such as invoices, cargo manifests, customs documents, customs documents, transport documents and other shipping documents the names of the preparations, if they have names, the quantities exported from Lebanon or imported into it, the name and address of each of the exporter and the importer, and the name and address of the consignee if known.

Export operations from Lebanon, as well as import operations into it, in the form of consignments addressed for the account of a person other than the person whose name is in the export authorisation shall be prohibited.

Export operations from Lebanon in the form of consignments addressed to a customs warehouse shall be prohibited unless the government of the importing country states in the import certificate its approval of such consignments, and import operations into Lebanon in the form of consignments addressed to a customs warehouse shall be prohibited unless approval of such consignments is established by the import certificate, and for every withdrawal from the warehouse it shall be required, and the consignments shall be deemed, and for every withdrawal from the customs warehouse the submission of a permit issued by the authorities to which the warehouse is subordinate shall be required, and consignments addressed abroad shall be deemed to be new export operations, and the substances and preparations deposited in the customs warehouse may not be treated in a manner that might alter their nature, nor may their relations be altered without a permit from the authorities responsible for the warehouse.

Upon the arrival of the consignment in Lebanon or the expiry of the period specified in the import permits, the Minister of Public Health shall send to the government of the exporting country the export authorisation with an endorsement indicating the quantity of plants, substances and preparations actually imported.

The competent authorities shall detain any consignment entering Lebanon or leaving it without being accompanied by an official import or export authorisation until the legality of the consignment is established or until a judicial judgment is issued confiscating it.

A consignment arriving at customs may not be delivered except in the presence of a pharmacist inspector and pursuant to a written withdrawal or export permit issued by the Minister of Public Health bearing all the particulars in respect of which a decision is issued by the Ministry of Public Health, and the Customs Administration shall, in both cases of import and export, receive the withdrawal or export permit from the concerned parties and return it to the Ministry of Health and retain a copy of this permit in its possession, and the permit shall be deemed null and void if it is not acted upon within ninety days from the date of its issuance or within a time limit not exceeding the last day of the current year, and the imported or exported substances shall be confiscated and delivered to the Ministry of Health unless the concerned party obtains a renewal of the authorisation and the withdrawal permit.

A consignment may not be withdrawn unless it is registered with the Ministry of Health on the date of issuance of the withdrawal permit and its fitness for use and its conformity with the approved technical specifications and with the particulars set out in the import authorisation are established, and the Minister of Public Health shall regulate the procedures for verifying fitness and conformity by a decision issued by him.
The administrative authority shall determine the customs offices designated in Lebanon for the import and export of the plants, substances or preparations listed in Schedules II and III.

The transit through Lebanese territory and whatever is deemed as such of consignments of the plants, substances or preparations listed in the Second and Third Schedules, whether unloaded or not unloaded from the means of transport thereof, shall be subject to the following provisions:

The transit of the consignment shall be prohibited unless a copy of the export authorisation pertaining thereto is submitted to the competent customs department. Any unauthorised diversion of a consignment transiting Lebanon to a destination other than the destination mentioned in the copy of the export authorisation pertaining to the consignment shall be prohibited.

An application for an authorisation to divert the destination shall be treated as an export operation from Lebanon to the country of the new destination. The processing of the consignment during its transit through Lebanon in a manner that may alter its nature shall be prohibited, and the method of its packaging may not be changed without an authorisation from the department delegated for that purpose by the Minister of Public Health. The preceding provisions shall be without prejudice to the provisions of international conventions signed by Lebanon under which the control operations that it is permitted to impose on the transiting consignment are restricted.

The provisions of the preceding Article shall not apply where the consignment is transported by air, provided that the aircraft does not land in Lebanon, and if it lands, the consignment shall, where necessary, be treated as an export export operation from Lebanon to the country of destination.
Free ports and free zones shall be subject to the same measures of control and supervision to which the remaining parts of the national territory are subject.

Commercial carriers shall take reasonable measures to prevent the use of the means of transport belonging to them in the illicit trafficking of the plants, substances and preparations covered by this Law, and in carrying out their work within the national territory they shall in particular be bound by the following:

- Filing cargo manifests in advance whenever possible

- Placing the said products in locked containers sealed with tamper-proof seals in such a manner that each of them can be inspected separately

- Informing the competent authorities as soon as possible of all circumstances that give rise to suspicion of the existence of illicit trafficking.
The plants, substances and preparations covered by this Law may not be sent by post except in the form of parcels with declared value and accompanied by an acknowledgment of receipt.

The plants, substances and preparations listed in the Second and Third Schedules may not be purchased for the purpose of obtaining professional supplies except through natural and legal persons holding a licence in accordance with Chapter One of this Title.

Only the natural and legal persons holding a licence specified below may purchase or possess the plants, substances and preparations listed in the Second and Third Schedules, within the limits of their professional needs

- Pharmacists working in pharmacies designated for sale to the public

- Pharmacists working in hospital institutions or in public or private therapeutic institutions

- Public or private depots placed under the responsibility of pharmacists and accredited by the Minister of Public Health

- Hospital institutions or therapeutic institutions not managed by pharmacists, in cases of emergency and provided that a physician attached to the institution has accepted to assume responsibility for the depot

- Physicians and veterinarians licensed to practise pharmacy with respect to preparations listed on a list drawn up by the Minister of Public Health

- Physicians and veterinarians within the limits of procuring supplies for the treatment of emergency cases, the types and quantities of which shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Public Health

- Dental surgeons for use in their professional activities, with respect to preparations the types and quantities of which shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Public Health.

1- Every order comprising plants or substances preparations listed in the Second Schedule shall require that the applicant submit two vouchers bearing two consecutive serial numbers extracted from a counterfoil order book in accordance with models prescribed by the Minister of Public Health, and there shall be recorded on the two vouchers the name, address and signature of the purchaser, the designation of the requested plants, substances and preparations, and the date of the order

The seller shall retain one of the two vouchers and shall deliver or send the other to the purchaser after affixing his stamp and signature thereto, while recording the outgoing number of the order, the date of its delivery, and the quantities delivered in his register

No products other than the plants, substances and preparations listed in the Third Schedule may be mentioned on the order vouchers for those plants, substances and preparations, and the persons concerned shall retain these documents for a period of three years for the purpose of presenting them to the competent authorities upon request

2- The provisions of the preceding paragraphs of this Article shall apply to the orders of physicians, dental surgeons and veterinarians for use for professional purposes, and those persons must furthermore submit their orders to a practising pharmacist.

No person whomsoever may deal in narcotic substances and psychotropic substances that a laboratory examination proves to be unfit for use or the expiry date of which has lapsed. These substances shall be destroyed under the supervision of the Ministry of Public Health, and the Minister of Public Health shall issue a decision on the procedures to be followed in this regard.

Individuals may possess the substances and preparations of the Second and Third Schedules for their personal use and for purely health reasons, within the limits of the quantities prescribed for them by physicians licensed to practise the medical profession, and they may not assign these substances to any other person for whatever reasons.

The plants, substances and preparations listed in the Second and Third Schedules may neither be prescribed nor dispensed to individuals except in a form suited to therapeutic purposes (a medication) and pursuant to a prescription from a physician, or a dental surgeon (for prescriptions necessary for the practice of dentistry), or the director of a laboratory for biomedical analyses (for prescriptions directly related to the practice of biological activities), or a veterinarian for veterinary uses).

There shall be stated in the medical prescription:

- The name, capacity and address of the attending physician who prescribed the medication

- The designation of the drug, its dosages and the method of its use

- The quantity prescribed or the duration of the treatment and the number of times it may be renewed where necessary

- The surname and given name of the patient, and the name of the keeper of the animal if the prescription is issued by a veterinarian

- The date of its issuance

- And the prescription must be signed by its author and must be oral in cases of extreme emergency. It shall be prohibited to fill a medical prescription that does not meet these conditions. The Minister of Public Health may issue a decision specifying additional particulars and conditions that must be met in prescriptions, and he may determine the dosages that may not be dispensed to each patient monthly.

The drugs listed in the Second and Third Schedules may not be dispensed except through:

- Pharmacists working in pharmacies designated for sale to the public

- Pharmacists working in hospital institutions or in public or private therapeutic institutions

- Public or private depots placed under the responsibility of pharmacists and accredited by the Minister of Public Health

- Public or private hospital institutions or therapeutic institutions not managed by pharmacists

- Physicians and veterinarians licensed to practise pharmacy and dispense drugs.

It shall be prohibited to direct any advertisement for the substances and preparations or drugs listed in the Second and Third Schedules to the general public, and it shall be prohibited to provide samples of the substances and preparations or drugs listed in the Second Schedule to physicians or individuals. The regulatory rules relating to advertising shall, where necessary, be supplemented by a decision of the Minister of Public Health.

The labels under which drugs are sold shall indicate the designations of the substances listed in Schedules II and III contained therein, in addition to their weight and percentage, and the labels and explanatory leaflets accompanying packages prepared for retail distribution shall indicate the method of use, the precautions to be taken, and the warnings necessary for the safety of the user of the drug.

It is prohibited to transport substances and preparations pertaining to Schedules II and III unless they are wrapped or packed in containers bearing their designations, and it is prohibited to send parcels of substances and preparations pertaining to Schedule II unless they are marked with a broad red line, and it is prohibited to place incorrect marks on dispatched parcels, and the outer wrappings of dispatched parcels may not contain any other indication apart from the names and addresses of the sender and the addressee: provided that they are sealed with the trademark of the sender.

The Minister of Public Health shall regulate, by a decision issued by him, the manner of handling substances and preparations of Schedules II and III in hospitals, sanatoriums, and dispensaries, and the physicians of hospitals, sanatoriums, and dispensaries shall, when dispensing narcotic drugs and using them for patients

- Enter the medical prescription in the patient's record, along with its date and signature, stating the quantity administered, and retain the empty containers and not destroy them except under the supervision of the Ministry of Public Health and in accordance with the rules

- Register the prescription in the register book of dispensed medical prescriptions

and sign it and retain it for a period of ten years from the date of the last entry therein.

As amended by Law 193 dated 24/5/2000, Official Gazette 23 dated 1/6/2000

Medical prescriptions containing drugs of Schedule II shall be drawn up, after examination of the patient, on forms extracted from counterfoil books in accordance with a model determined by a decision of the Minister of Public Health, and the Narcotics Department shall distribute these books.

There shall be stated on these forms, in words in full, the number of prescribed therapeutic units where the matter relates to a proprietary drug, and the doses of the substances listed in Schedule II where the matter relates to an extemporaneous preparation, and the physician shall be bound to retain the counterfoils of the books for a period of three years in order to submit them to the competent authorities upon their request.

It is prohibited to draw up or dispense a medical prescription that does not fulfil the conditions set out in the preceding Article, and it is prohibited to draw up or dispense a medical prescription containing drugs listed in Schedule II for a period exceeding seven days, and it is prohibited to draw up or dispense a medical prescription containing such drugs during a period covered by a previous prescription for drugs listed in the same Schedule unless it contains an explicit reference to the previous prescription by the attending physician, and it is prohibited for any person who already has a medical prescription for one or more of the drugs mentioned in the said prescription to obtain a new medical prescription containing drugs listed in the same Schedule without notifying the physician of the previous prescription, and the attending physician shall be bound to ask the patient about previous medical prescriptions that he may have obtained.

By way of exception to the provisions of the second paragraph of the preceding Article, certain drugs listed in Schedule II and specified by a decision of the Minister of Public Health may be prescribed for a period exceeding seven days and not exceeding sixty days.

If the bearer of the medical prescription is unknown to the person dispensing it, the latter must require him to prove his identity, and it is prohibited to execute a medical prescription where more than seven days have elapsed since it was drawn up, and medical prescriptions shall be classified in their chronological order and retained by the pharmacist for a period of three years, and the pharmacist may deliver to the client, at his request, a copy thereof bearing two transverse lines with an indication that it is a copy.

Persons licensed to dispense drugs of Schedule II shall provide the Minister of Public Health, during the first week of every three months, with a detailed statement signed and stamped with the seal of the pharmacy showing the incoming, the outgoing, and the balance of each substance during the said period, together with a summary statement of the medical prescriptions they have dispensed stating the name of the physician who prescribed the drug and the nature and quantity of the drugs dispensed in respect of each prescription, all in accordance with models prepared by the Ministry of Public Health for this purpose, and this obligation shall apply to private hospitals and dispensaries as well.
The dispensing of drugs listed in Schedule III may be renewed unless the issuer of the prescription indicates otherwise.

The Minister of Public Health may, where necessary, license pharmacists or other approved retail distributors, under the conditions he determines, to dispense to individuals, at their own personal discretion and without a medical prescription, small quantities of substances listed in Schedule III and of preparations containing them, in exceptional cases and for purely medical purposes.
Substances and preparations of Schedules II and III may be dispensed pursuant to a licence card issued by the Minister of Public Health.

The Minister of Public Health shall issue a decision setting out the conditions required to be met for obtaining the licence cards referred to in the preceding Article and the particulars required to be included therein, and this decision shall designate the administrative authority competent to issue them, the quantities beyond which dispensing to the person concerned is not permitted, and the date of expiry of their validity.

A licence card may not be granted except to the following persons:

- Specialist physicians licensed to practise medicine

- Physicians designated by hospitals, sanatoriums, and dispensaries in which there are no pharmacists.

Specialist physicians may possess in their clinics the substances delivered to them pursuant to the licence card for use in cases of extreme necessity, provided that such substances are kept in the form consistent with the medical use for which they are intended without alteration, and they may treat patients with such substances outside their clinics in emergency cases, and a physician is prohibited from dispensing any of these substances to his patients for the purpose of self-administration.

Pharmacists shall indicate on the licence card the quantity they have dispensed and the dates of dispensing, and shall sign these particulars, and the substances indicated on the card shall only be delivered against a receipt from the holder of the card showing in ink the date, the full name of the narcotic substance or psychotropic substance, the quantity in figures and words, and the number and date of the licence card, and the holder of the card shall return it to the competent administrative authority within one week from the date of expiry of its validity.

First-aid kits on means of international transport: The Minister of Public Health may license the possession of small quantities of drugs of Schedules II and III on ships, aircraft, and other means of public transport registered in Lebanon and engaged in international voyages, within the limits of the quantity necessary to provide first aid in cases of urgency. The licence shall be granted at the request of the operator of the means of transport and shall specify the measures to be taken to prevent the use of the drugs for purposes other than those for which they are intended and their diversion to illicit purposes, and the licence shall designate the name of the person in the crew responsible for the drugs, the conditions of their possession, the procedures to be followed to establish the quantities taken therefrom and the quantities that have replaced them, and the report to be prepared and submitted periodically on their use. The administration of these drugs in cases of urgency shall not constitute a violation of the remaining provisions of Section II of this Chapter.

Possession of drugs by patients in transit: Persons undergoing treatment may possess for their personal use while transiting through Lebanon drugs containing psychotropic substances listed in Schedules II and III, in the quantities necessary for their treatment for a period not exceeding seven days in respect of drugs of Schedule II and thirty days in respect of drugs of Schedule III, provided that they have in their possession a copy of the medical prescription certified by the pharmacist who dispensed it. ''

If the owner of the property fails to attend at the place of demarcation, the demarcation shall be carried out on the basis of the information of the mukhtars and the neighbouring owners who are present, and mention thereof shall be made in the minutes of the demarcation of the real properties. In all cases, if a dispute arises over the right of ownership, the person who occupies the real property shall be recorded in the minutes as if he were the presumed owner, and the claimant of a right as an objector. In the aforementioned case, if it is impossible to determine the right of possession, all claimants of the right shall be recorded equally as objectors, and the Single Real Property Judge shall undertake, at the commencement of the action, to determine the rank of each of them in relation to the others. It shall not be permissible for the surveyor to proceed with the provisional demarcation except in the presence of the mukhtar, or in the presence of a delegated member of the council of elders of the locality if the mukhtar is absent, and the Single Real Property Judge, as well as the surveyor, and the supervising authorities shall have jurisdiction to establish the contraventions that occur during the provisional demarcation operations, and the minutes drawn up by these officials shall have probative force until the contrary is proved.

In the cases provided for by the first and second paragraphs of Article 12, the surveyor shall place boundary markers for the limits of the actual possession of the presumed owner, and shall place within these limits boundary markers for the parcels claimed by third parties, but without making them independent real properties, and shall place boundary markers for the parcels in respect of which it is impossible to determine the right of possession, considering them as independent real properties. Provided that, in the aforementioned cases, if the disputed parcels do not permit, due to their narrowness, the placing of boundary markers therefor, the surveyor shall proceed to record the dispute only in the minutes of the demarcation and in the sketch plan (croquis).

The Justice of the Peace or the Single Real Property Judge charged with supervising the legality of the demarcation works and the placing of the provisional boundary markers carried out by the surveyor shall adjudicate immediately upon every dispute that arises between the surveyor and the owners regarding the said works, with the exception of disputes relating to boundaries or to a claimed right, for such disputes shall be decided after the completion of the preliminary works.

The legal penalties shall be imposed forthwith upon the observed contraventions.

The provisional boundaries which are determined in accordance with the provisions of the aforementioned Articles 11, 12 and 13 shall be physically fixed on the ground and, where necessary, their fixing shall be by boundary markers of the regulatory model placed at every deflection in the direction of the boundaries.

Pursuant to the first Article of Decision No. 44/L.R. dated 20/4/1932, Chapter Three (Articles 15 to 21) was repealed and replaced by the following text:

The surveyor shall record the information resulting from the provisional demarcation operations in minutes of census and demarcation drawn up for each real property separately, progressively and as he proceeds with the provisional demarcation, and he shall also record it in a special schedule for the census of real properties. There shall be drawn up, in addition thereto, an alphabetical index of the names of the owners in the real property areas in which the multiplicity of owners resulting from the subdivision of real properties requires that it be drawn up, and each of the minutes of demarcation and census, the schedules of census and the alphabetical indexes of the property owners shall be of the model determined by the administrative authority.

The minutes of census and demarcation drawn up for each real property shall contain the following information:

1- Description of the real property. - Its location, its composition, its legal nature and its declared boundaries.

2- The given name, surname, age, profession and nationality of the declared owners or co-owners of the property, and where necessary, the amount of the undivided share, provided that the undivided shares are expressed in accordance with the rule provided for by the last paragraph of Article 36 mentioned below.

3- The derechos in rem (real rights), in accordance with the provisions of the tenth Article of Decision No. 3339 dated 12 November of the year 1930, and the easements (servitudes) accruing to or encumbering the property, and if the property is subject to a waqf right, mention shall be made in the minutes of the type of waqf (charitable or family), the name of the institution in whose favour the waqf is constituted, the name of the administrator (mutawalli) and the names of the beneficiaries thereof pursuant to the waqf deed. Mention shall also be made of the grounds of possession (such as registration in the Tabu, or acquisition for a price, or gratuitously without a price, or inheritance, or occupation and, in this case, the duration of the occupation).

4- The objections to the boundaries, and to the right of ownership or to the extent of this right, and to all other real rights.

5- Enumeration of the documents and instruments produced by the interested parties.

6- Designation of the elected domicile in the real property area or in the chief town of the Caza or the Mohafazah for the owners of the property, the co-owners, the objectors and the claimants of a right.

The minutes of the provisional demarcation shall be closed with the signature of the surveyor and the presumed owners or the neighbouring presumed co-owners and the objectors who attended the provisional demarcation, and with the signature of the mukhtar of the real property area or his representative.

The surveyor charged with performing the function of clerk of proceedings during the provisional demarcation and census operations shall open the schedule of census of real properties, and shall record therein the result of the adversarial demarcation, and he must also record therein, under the responsibility of the Justice of the Peace or the Single Real Property Judge, the alterations that have occurred in the minutes, and transcribe therein the decisions of the Judge.

After the clearance of the objections or applications and the completion of the works in each real property area, this schedule shall be deposited with the Survey Department to be used in drawing up the survey maps.

The surveyor shall deliver to the Justice of the Peace or the Single Real Property Judge, upon completion of the provisional demarcation in each real property area, minutes on the demarcation of the real properties, the general demarcation plans, the schedules of census of the real properties, and the alphabetical indexes of the names of the owners...

This delivery shall require the drawing up of minutes in two copies signed by the Head of Works and the Justice of the Peace or the Real Property Judge. These minutes shall contain a detailed list of the documents that have been delivered.

In each real property area, as soon as the provisional demarcation works therein are completed, the surveyor shall draw up minutes of the closure of the works, which shall be signed by the Single Real Property Judge, the Head of Works and the mukhtar, and these minutes shall be posted in the office of the Judge's clerk and notified to the Auxiliary Office and the Real Property Office in the area, and these formalities shall be established in the minutes of closure by an annotation recorded at the foot of the draft signed by the clerk, and the inhabitants shall be given notice of the closure of the provisional works through the mukhtars, and the clerk shall undertake, in addition thereto, to receive the declarations and objections from the owners in accordance with the provisions mentioned below and shall record them in the minutes of the real property, and to this end he shall seek the assistance of the mukhtars to notify the owners, the neighbouring owners and the objectors, and in general everyone who claims a right which he did not claim during the adversarial demarcation, to submit their objection or their applications and to produce in support thereof their instruments or their probative documents.

Within a time limit of thirty days commencing from the date of the posting of the minutes of closure of the provisional demarcation operations in the real property area, every person may, if the matter has escaped him previously, intervene:

1- By way of objection, if a dispute has arisen over a right of ownership or over the extent of this right, and over the boundaries.

2- By way of an application for registration, in the event of the existence of claims for the exercise of a real right capable of being recorded in the Real Property Register.

In particular, guardians, legal representatives, relatives or friends, and representatives of the interests of minors, absent persons and missing persons shall have the right to intervene by way of objection or application for registration, in the name of minors and those who have not attained the age of majority, absent persons and missing persons, provided that it shall be incumbent upon the relatives and friends to prove their mandate in order to be entitled to institute an action before the competent judicial authority in the name of the objector or the claimant of the right.

Where necessary and at the request of the Head of the Auxiliary Office, the two parties must clarify, by a written declaration dated and signed by them, their capacity to dispose, their personal status, the nature, subject matter, and cause of the agreement, and the scope, basis, and content of the right sought to be registered. In cases where the two parties do not know how to sign, the Head of the Auxiliary Office shall receive this declaration and draw up a record thereof.

The declarations of the contracting parties may, upon their written request, be received outside the Auxiliary Office at the place of residence of such persons if the matter relates to hearing the declaration of a woman, an infirm person, or any other person who is unable to travel due to illness, imprisonment, or any cause of force majeure. In this case, the applicant must submit in support of his request a certificate from the mukhtar of the locality or its imam.

Declarations shall be received at the place of residence of the concerned parties within the form and conditions prescribed in Articles 36 to 42 mentioned above, provided that the Head of the Auxiliary Office must in all cases be accompanied by the mukhtar of the locality.

Subject to the cases excepted in Article 46, a fixed registration fee and a transfer and transmission fee shall be levied on every entry, annotation, provisional entry, or striking off in the Real Estate Register, the Registration Ledger, or the Tapu Register.

The issuance of title deeds, deeds of various rights, certificates of entry of real rights of all kinds, copies or extracts of real folios or folios of various rights, and copies or extracts of supplementary documents shall not be subject to stamp duties, but fixed fees shall be levied thereon.

The transactions subject to fixed fees and to transfer and transmission fees are detailed in the First and Second Schedules annexed to this Decision.

Entries, annotations, provisional entries, and strikings off carried out ex officio in the Real Estate Register to rectify clerical errors, or which relate to real rights owned or acquired by the State for inclusion in its public or private domain, and to real rights owned or acquired by municipalities for the purpose of including them in their public domain, shall be exempt from fixed fees and transfer and transmission fees.

However, entries, annotations, provisional entries, and strikings off relating to real rights acquired by concessionaires of projects of public utility and intended for inclusion in the public or private domain of the States or municipalities upon their purchase or the expiry of the concession shall remain subject to fixed fees and to transfer and transmission fees, unless the concession contract contains a provision contrary to this rule.

The following shall be exempt from transfer and transmission fees:

1 - The entry of land consolidation transactions, and transactions of partitioning of common property in communal (musha') lands carried out in accordance with the two Decisions of the High Commissioner No. 171 dated 10 March 1926 and No. 37 L.R. dated 5 February 1934.

2 - The entry of the final transfer in the name of lessees of State domain by way of a lease containing a promise of sale.

3 - The return of real properties to their original owner in execution of an express resolutory condition.

Public institutions shall be exempt from the fees on constructions provided for in Item 12 of Schedule No. 2 (amended) of Legislative Decree No. 148 dated 12/06/1959 relating to transfer and transmission fees.

If it is expressly stated in the application for the entry of a real property held in the ownership of a legal person that such real property is intended to be a church, a mosque, a synagogue, a temple, an oratory, a cemetery, or a gratuitous educational or charitable institution recognised by the State, the transfer fees shall be refunded after verifying that the real property is used for that to which it was allocated.
The amount of transfer and transmission fees shall be determined by a legislative decree.

The Administration shall have the right, when fees are assessed on the basis of the value declared by the concerned parties, to investigate, within three years, the concealment of part of the price and then to prove such concealment before the Judge of First Instance in the district by all means of proof.

The Judge of First Instance must rule on the case expeditiously. If concealment is proven, the contracting parties shall be jointly and severally ordered to pay costs, damages, and a fine equivalent to ten times the fees lost by the Treasury. If it is proven that the difference between the true value of the real property and the value on the basis of which the fee was levied exceeds the proportion of twenty-five percent 25%, the contracting parties shall be jointly and severally ordered to pay a fine equal to five times the fees lost by the Treasury.

When agreements relating to the transfer of a right, the assignment of a right, the modification of a right, or other transactions subject to the fees provided for in Article 45 are rescinded or annulled, the courts shall not in any case have the right to order the restitution of an amount exceeding the principal price mentioned in the instruments or declared by the contracting parties in accordance with Article 49.

All fees and expenses due, with the exception of transmission and inheritance fees, shall be paid directly to the Treasury fund by the applicants for registration in accordance with the provisions of Article 68 of Decision No. 188 dated 15 March 1926, completed by Article 18 of Decision No. 45/L.R dated 20 April 1932, and no one may postpone the payment of fees on the grounds of a dispute over the amount of his share thereof or on any other grounds, provided that he has the right to sue for their recovery where necessary.

If it is not possible to assess the fees with precision upon the application for registration, the Head of the Auxiliary Office may determine the amount required to be deposited in the Treasury fund by way of trust. If the amount deposited in trust is less than the total fees due, the difference must be paid to the Treasury fund before the documents are delivered to their owners.

As for any surplus over the deposited amount, the Treasurer shall refund it to the concerned parties upon their presentation of a statement from the Registrar, Head of the Real Estate Office.

Fees that have not been paid in part or in whole due to error, negligence, or any other cause shall be collected in accordance with the Law on the Collection of Public Funds jointly and severally from all those who participated in the contracts, agreements, or declarations, or from those who benefited therefrom.
Every fee or part of a fee legally levied shall not be refunded.
The provisions of prescription that may be invoked regarding debts owed to or by the Treasury shall apply to the collection of fees due or to their refund.
The fee for transmission by inheritance shall be due from each heir in proportion to his share.

Subject to the provisions of the Law of 21 December 1951, upon the registration of rights resulting from an estate opened before the promulgation of this Law, the registration fee shall be levied plus a fine equal thereto. However, if this estate is the subject of a dispute before the courts, the rights resulting therefrom must be registered within six months following the date of issuance of the final judgment without any fine. If the registration of these rights is not completed within the time limit provided for above, the fees shall be collected plus a fine of twenty-five percent for each year of delay in accordance with the Law on the Collection of Direct Taxes, provided that the fine does not exceed the prescribed fees. The delay fine mentioned in the preceding paragraph shall fall due starting from the seventh month following the second day of the issuance of the final judgment. The fine shall accrue year by year, and the beginning of each year shall be counted from the date of issuance of the final judgment.

The fine shall fall due in each year after the lapse of six months from its beginning if the transmission transaction is not completed within these six months.

Contrary to the provisions of the aforementioned Article 54, the period of prescription regarding the collection of fees for transmission by inheritance shall not be calculated except starting from the date of the application for the entry of the hereditary rights. When the fees for transmission by inheritance are distributed over several annual instalments, the Registrar must record the amounts paid by the concerned parties in the field designated for observations in the real folio of the real property, indicating the date of payment of each amount.
Lands gained from the sea, or from lakes and ponds or marshes, without prior authorisation for their discoverer, shall form part of the private lands of the State.

If a large or small river takes a new course and abandons its old bed, the owners of the adjoining properties shall be entitled to acquire the ownership of this old bed, each in the part that lies in front of his land up to an imaginary line in the middle of the river.

The price of the old bed shall be determined by experts appointed by the President of the Court in that place.

The price proceeds from this sale shall be distributed by way of compensation to the owners of the lands occupied by the new course in proportion to its value; however, he shall be entitled, if he so wishes, to leave the yield to this other person in return for the payment of one year's rent.

The owner of the land also becomes the owner by way of accession of the seeds sown by another person, provided that he pays him their value; however, he shall be entitled, if he so wishes, to leave the yield to this other person in return for the payment of one year's rent.

If the time of sowing has not yet passed, the owner of the land shall be entitled to compel the other person who sowed it to remove his seeds without compensating him for the expenses of ploughing the seeds.

Every building or planting and work standing on the land shall be presumed to have been erected by the owner of the land at his own expense and to belong to him, unless proof to the contrary is established.

The owner of the land who builds on his land with building materials belonging to another, or sows it with grain belonging to another, shall not be compelled to return these materials or this grain, but he must pay their value to their owners.

The owner of the land upon which another person has erected buildings or planted plantings with materials or plantings belonging to the owner of the property becomes, by way of accession, the owner of these buildings or plantings under the following conditions:
