If the person who erected the buildings or planted the plantings was in good faith, he shall not be liable towards the owner of the property for the yield which he has obtained, and he shall bear only the liability for the loss or damage which occurred on his account; and if he has built or planted on the land claimed for recovery, he shall not be compelled to remove the buildings which he built nor the plantings which he planted, and he shall be paid compensation for the improvement which accrued to the land by reason of these buildings and plantings; and if the buildings and plantings are of a value exceeding the value of the land, the owner of the plantings and buildings shall have the right to purchase the ownership of the land built upon or planted by paying its owner the value of the bare ownership of the land.

If the person who erected the buildings or planted the plantings was in bad faith, he must return to the owner of the land the value of the yield which he obtained, and although he is not liable for the loss which occurred by reason of the fall in prices, he is liable for the loss or damage even if it did not occur on his account; and if he has built or planted, he shall be compelled to demolish the building and uproot the plantings unless the owner of the land prefers to keep them, provided that he pays to their owner from whom they were taken the value of the building materials and the plantings prior to the building and planting after deducting the expenses which their owner would incur had he been compelled to remove them. These provisions shall apply upon the expiry of the term of the usufruct to the usufructuary who has erected buildings or planted plantings on the land held in usufruct.

If the plantings or buildings were planted or erected by a person with materials not belonging to him, the owner of these materials shall not be entitled to claim them, but he shall have a right to compensation which he shall recover from the said person, and he shall recover what remains to him of the amount of compensation from the owner of the land.

If the plantings or buildings were planted or erected on a common property by one of the co-owners in this property without the permission of his other co-owners, the partition of the property shall, where necessary, be carried out through the judge. Then the provisions of Article two hundred and sixteen shall apply to each of the shares.

A promise of sale is an agreement whereby a person undertakes to sell a certain thing to another person immediately after this other person (who does not undertake to purchase it) declares that he has decided to purchase the thing promised in this manner. No A promise of sale shall not be valid unless the agreement of the two parties takes place at the same time upon the thing, upon the price, and upon the time limit during which the promisee may decide his option.

This time limit may not exceed fifteen years, and if the two parties agree upon a time limit exceeding fifteen years, the promise shall be valid, but it shall only have effect during the fifteen years alone. A promise of sale may be in favour of a specified person, and it may also be (to order), and in this case- it may be transferred by endorsement of the instrument of the promise of sale, and the endorsement shall be null and void if it does not include the date written out in full in words, the signature of the transferor, and the authentication of this signature by the notaries public. The instrument of a promise of sale may not be drawn up "to bearer".

A promise to sell an immovable property gives rise to a real right which, in this capacity, is subject to all the provisions applicable to real rights. (Including the provisions of Resolution No. 188 issued on 15 March 1926, the tenth Article of which applies in particular to transfers of promises of sale, especially to endorsements of promises drawn up "to order", subject to the contrary provisions stipulated in this Resolution.

A promise to sell an immovable property prohibits the promisor from selling the property or from creating a real right over it other than a mortgage during the period of the time limit granted to the promisee to decide his option.

The promisor is entitled to contract a mortgage over the property during this same period, provided that such mortgages contracted in this manner do not prejudice the rights of the promisee. If the promisee decides to exercise his option, the sale price shall be subrogated by real subrogation in place of the mortgaged property, and the rights of the mortgage creditors shall be transferred to this price in accordance with the ranking established pursuant to Articles 16 and 17 of Resolution No. 1329 issued on 20 March 1922.

A promise of sale, and in particular its effects defined in Articles 222 and 223, shall not be enforceable against other persons in good faith except as from their provisional registration in the Land Register in accordance with Article 25 of Resolution No. 188 issued on 15 March 1926 (This provisional registration shall be null and void if there are not mentioned therein the price and the agreed period, as well as the name and address of the promisee and, where applicable, the words "to order".

If the registration of a mortgage takes place during the period between the provisional registration of the promise of sale and the exercise of the option, the purchaser shall not validly pay the price of the property except into the hands of the notary public, who has the competence to distribute this price in accordance with Article 223 and all other legal provisions in force.

If the seller refuses during this time limit to comply with the request of the purchaser to conclude and register the final deed of sale, the buyer must, in order to preserve the effect of the provisional registration beyond the time limit of the option, do the following:

1- Declare in writing prior to the expiry of the said period to the seller and to the Head of the Land Registry Office his desire to decide his option.

2- Bring before the Court, during the fifteen days following the decision of the option, his action requesting judgment for the final transfer.

The action shall be brought against the seller, and the Head of the Land Registry Office must be joined in the action.

The Head of the Land Registry Office shall effect the final transfer upon the request of the purchaser immediately after the judgment ordering the execution of this transfer has acquired the force of a final judgment.

The right of registration in the Land Register is acquired in the ways set forth below:

1- By inheritance.

2- By gifts inter vivos or by will.

3- By occupation of the place.

4- By pre-emption.

5- By prescription.

6- By the effect of contracts.

The right of registration with respect to a gift and a will is acquired by the mere occurrence of the gift and its delivery.

An heir acquires by way of inheritance the immovable properties belonging to the estate; however, he shall not be entitled to dispose of them towards other persons except after their registration in the Land Register.
Estates shall be subject to the provisions of the ordinary laws.

If the interested party objects, the Director of the institute shall be notified thereof, and it shall be incumbent upon him to deposit with the Disciplinary Board all the documents relating to the objector.

The interested party shall have the right to inspect the documents and copy therefrom whatever he deems necessary for his own defence, and to be assisted by an advocate before the Disciplinary Board. If he does not attend the hearing in person, the case shall be adjudicated on the basis of the documents.

The aforementioned Disciplinary Board shall be composed of:

1- A judge seconded by the Ministry of Justice.... President

2- A representative of the Ministry of National Education and from among the civil servants of the second or third category ...Member

3- A representative of the Ministry of Social Affairs from among the civil servants of the second or third category.... Member

The Board shall adopt its decisions by a majority of votes and its decisions shall be final.

Related text: Determination of the allowances of the Disciplinary Board and the Dispute Resolution Committee provided for in the Law Regulating the Teaching Staff in Private Schools

First: The Director of the school shall have the right to dismiss from service any member of the teaching staff, provided that he sends him a registered letter with acknowledgement of receipt to that effect before the fifth of the month of July of every year, failing which he shall be deemed bound to the school for the following school year, and the letter may be served on the interested party directly against his signature of receipt on a certified true copy of this letter in lieu of registered mail.

Second: If the dismissal takes place during the academic year for reasons other than disciplinary or health reasons based on the decision of the Medical Committee competent for civil servants at the Ministry of Health and Social Affairs, the following bases shall be adopted:

1- If the dismissed person is a trainee contractor and is dismissed from service after the fifteenth of the month of February, his salaries must be paid until the end of the school year.

2- If the dismissed person is on the permanent staff or is a contractor, his salaries and the supplements thereto must be paid until the end of the school year, regardless of the time of his dismissal from service.

Third: In cases of non-disciplinary dismissal, the interested party, if he considers his dismissal to constitute an abuse of right, shall have the right to object within a period of two months from the date on which the letter of dismissal was served on him, on pain of forfeiture of the right, before the Judge of Urgent Matters having jurisdiction over the seat of the institution or school.

The Judge of Urgent Matters shall attempt, where appropriate, to settle the dispute by reinstating the dismissed person in his work.

If that proves impossible and it is established to him that the dismissal constitutes an abuse of right, he shall order the institution or school to pay additional compensation to the dismissed person equivalent to one month's salary for each year of service at the institution or school for the first ten years, and ranging between one month and two months for each subsequent year of service, and the decision of the Judge of Urgent Matters shall be final and not subject to any form of recourse.

The dismissal from service of any member of the teaching staff on account of his compliance with the resolutions of his union or his claiming of rights recognized by law shall be deemed to constitute an abuse of right.

The person dismissed from service shall have the right to retain the full amount of the additional compensation awarded to him.

Fourth: The person dismissed from service shall have the right, in all cases, to exercise one of the following two options with respect to the statutory dismissal compensation:

1- To pay the compensation awarded to him into the Compensation Fund if he returns to service in teaching and requests the aggregation of his previous services. In this case, he shall have the right to recover the deductions paid to the said Fund in respect of the service for which he received this compensation.

2- To retain the compensation if he leaves teaching permanently or if he returns thereto and does not aggregate his previous services.

No member of the teaching staff shall have the right to leave work during the school year, failing which he shall be liable for damages equivalent to double his salaries and the supplements thereto for the remaining period of the school year. If he wishes to leave the school in which he works at the end of the year, he must send the Director of the school a registered letter with acknowledgement of receipt to that effect before the fifth of the month of July, failing which he shall be deemed bound for the following school year and shall be liable to be ordered to pay the damages provided for in the preceding paragraph, and the interested party may serve the letter directly against signature of receipt on a certified true copy of this letter in lieu of registered mail.

A- Every member of the teaching staff shall have the right to request his dismissal from service, and the Director of the school shall also have the right to dismiss him in one of the following cases:

1- If he reaches the age at which the service of State civil servants terminates by operation of law.

2- (The text of this paragraph was repealed by Law 53 dated 23/5/1991).

3- If he is afflicted with an illness that incapacitates him for work pursuant to the decision of the Medical Committee competent for civil servants at the Ministry of Public Health.

B - Every person who has practised the teaching profession for at least twenty-five years without interruption shall have the right to request his dismissal from service. In the event that he continues teaching without any interruption and requests to return to the permanent staff, the provisions of paragraph 4 of Article 66 of Legislative Decree 112 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments shall apply to him, provided that the provisions of this Article shall take effect as from the date of entry into force of Law 13/71 dated 4/2/1971 )

C - Female members of the teaching staff shall have the right to request their dismissal from service by reason of their marriage, provided that they submit their applications to the school administration before the fifteenth of July of every year, and their rights shall be liquidated in accordance with the laws and regulations in force.

The following cases shall constitute an interruption of work:

1- Interruption of teaching for a period of at least one year without a legitimate excuse.

2- Practising teaching in an institute outside Lebanese territory.

If a member of the teaching staff travels abroad, with permission from the institute, to complete his studies or is seconded by the institute or institution to teach outside Lebanese territory in a branch affiliated with the institute or institution, he shall not be deemed to have interrupted his work; however, the period that he spends abroad shall not be included in the calculation of the service subject to compensation.

In the cases provided for in Article 31 of this Law and in the case of death, the provisions applicable to members of the teaching staff in public schools shall apply to members of the teaching staff on the permanent staff with respect to the liquidation and calculation of the dismissal from service compensation.

In other cases, the amount of the compensation shall be equal to one month's salary for each year of service, provided that the salary due in the last month of actual service shall be adopted in the calculation of the compensation, and there shall be added to this salary a rate of:

40% for kindergarten teachers, instructors and primary teachers.

60% for secondary education professors.

As for contractors, they shall be granted compensation equivalent to one month's salary for each year in proportion to their particular status in each school, and the wage of the last month of actual service shall be adopted in the calculation of the compensation.

Any service performed before the completion of eighteen years of age and after reaching the legal age at which the service of State civil servants terminates shall not be adopted in the calculation of the dismissal compensation, and no age correction for members of the teaching staff in private schools shall be recognized after the promulgation of the draft law put into effect by Decree No. 17384 dated 02/09/1964.

The Compensation Fund provided for in Chapter Five of this Law shall bear:

1- The full dismissal compensation due to Lebanese members of the teaching staff on the permanent staff or affiliated with free institutes in the cases provided for in Articles 31 and 35 of this Law.

2- Half of the compensation due to Lebanese members of the teaching staff in free institutes in cases other than those mentioned in the preceding paragraph, and the institute shall bear the other half.

The institute shall bear the dismissal from service compensation due to members of the teaching staff:

1- Who are Lebanese, in the cases not set forth in the preceding Article.

2- Who are contractors, in all cases.

3- Who are non-Lebanese, in all cases.

The rules adopted in the valuation of the elements of assets and liabilities in the enterprise have been provided for by Articles 12 to 15 of Decree No. 4665 dated 26/12/1981, and they cover tangible and intangible fixed assets, participating securities, other immobilised securities, investment securities, inventory and work in progress, and accounts receivable and payable.

The application of these rules leads to the determination of the net accounting result of the financial period, which alone is publishable pursuant to the provisions of the Code of Commerce. The transition to the taxable result is effected by making the required adjustments to the accounting result in accordance with the provisions of the tax legislation in force, whereby extraordinary depreciations, the provision constituted to meet a decline in prices, and any other provision the deduction of which from profits is not provided for by the tax law are added back to the taxable profits. Conversely, revenues not subject to the tax on profits are deducted from the profits.

First: Valuation of tangible and intangible fixed assets at the closing of accounts:

1- The appreciation gain resulting from comparing the current value with the book value of the elements of tangible and intangible assets shall not be recorded.

2- The value of the decline in prices resulting from comparing the current value with the book value of the elements of tangible and intangible assets shall be recorded in accordance with the following:

a - With respect to fixed assets whose normal productive capacity continuously decreases due to the factor of the passage of time, or due to use, technical changes, or for any other reason, the enterprise shall establish a depreciation schedule for them in accordance with the provisions of Article 2 of Law No. 27/80. At the closing of accounts at the end of each financial period, the net asset value of the asset shall be determined by its current value unless the latter is lower than it, in which case:

- either an extraordinary depreciation is constituted if this decline has occurred definitively, and the balance of the depreciation schedule is adjusted accordingly,

- or a provision is constituted in the amount of this decline if it is considered to be temporary.

b - With respect to the remaining assets whose current value is less than their book value, the difference shall be recognised by adopting:

- either the extraordinary depreciation method if the decline is definitive,

- or the constitution of a provision if the decline is not definitive.

3- At the end of each financial period, the provisions accounts shall be adjusted either by increasing them or by returning a portion thereof to the financial period result account.

4- The comparison of the current value of fixed assets with their book value shall be carried out, in principle, on the basis of taking each element of the assets separately.

Second: Participating securities:

1- These securities shall be recorded upon their entry into the ownership of the enterprise at their purchase cost or at their value specified in the purchase contract.

2- Whether these securities are quoted on the stock exchange or not, the estimation of their value at a given time must equal the value that a capable and prudent businessman would agree to pay if he wished to acquire them. This value shall be determined by the extent of the benefit that this participation provides to the enterprise.

3- The following elements may be taken into consideration when carrying out the valuation operation referred to in the preceding paragraph: the current or expected yield of these securities, their net position, the possibility of converting them into cash, the economic situation, stock exchange prices, as well as the motives that originally underlay the purchase operation, provided that the subsequent change in the value of these elements is not the result of the occurrence of unforeseen circumstances.

4- If the comparison operation between the book value of the securities and their value at the date of inventory results in showing appreciation gains or a decline in their value, the value of these differences must be determined for each type of securities of the same class that confer equal rights upon their holders. Only the decline in value shall be considered as affecting the result of the financial period and shall be calculated in the form of a provision, and it is prohibited to effect any set-off between the appreciation differences in certain securities and the price decline differences of other securities.

5- When the enterprise sells a portion of a group of securities of the same class that confer equal rights upon their holders, the cost of the sold portion shall be estimated, in principle, in accordance with the weighted average cost price or pursuant to the first-in, first-out method. When the sale of a portion of the securities causes the loss of the majority of votes in the general assemblies, or the loss of the number of votes sufficient to block the taking of decisions in the said assemblies, the current value of the remaining securities must then be adjusted accordingly.

Third: Other immobilised securities and investment securities:

1- These securities shall be recorded upon their entry into the ownership of the enterprise, at their purchase cost or at their value specified in the purchase contract.

2- At inventory, securities quoted on the stock exchange shall be valued in accordance with the average price in the last month, whereas unquoted securities shall be valued at their current value, that is, at their probable selling value.

3- If the comparison between the book value and the current value of securities of the same class that confer equal rights upon their holders results in the appearance of appreciation gains or a decline in their value, a provision shall only be constituted to meet the fall in prices of these securities, and it is prohibited to effect any set-off between the appreciation differences in certain securities and the price decline differences of other securities. However, upon the occurrence of an abnormal temporary decrease in the value of certain quoted securities, the enterprise may, on the responsibility of its directors, refrain from constituting a provision to meet the full value of the decline incurred or a part thereof, within the limits of the value of the normal appreciation appearing on other types of securities.

4- For the purpose of valuing securities quoted on the stock exchange and denominated in foreign currencies, their price in Lebanese currency shall be adopted if these securities are quoted in Lebanon, and the foreign exchange rate shall be adopted if they are quoted only abroad, in which case their value shall be converted into Lebanese currency at the exchange rate on the date of valuation.

Fourth: Inventory and work in progress:

1- Upon its entry into the ownership of the enterprise, inventory and work in progress shall be recorded at the cost of acquiring it plus all the expenses incurred by the enterprise to bring it in its condition to the place where it is located, and only the expenses that normally enter into its constitution shall be included within the cost of inventory and work in progress; accordingly, the loss of goods or their exposure to damage or waste shall not enter into the calculation of this cost. Only fixed production expenses calculated on the basis of the normal productive capacity of the enterprise shall enter into the cost of manufacturing.

As for the portion of fixed expenses that is not charged to the cost of manufacturing due to operation below the level of normal productive capacity, it shall be considered a charge borne by the financial period.

The normal productive capacity shall be determined, in each enterprise, in light of the capabilities in its possession and the production it can yield in accordance with moderate estimates.

Identifiable items shall be valued in accordance with the cost of acquiring them or the cost of producing them, whereas interchangeable items shall have their cost determined as follows:

The cost of opening inventory is added to the cost of purchases of the financial period, and the total is distributed between the consumed items and the remaining items in accordance with the first-in, first-out method or in accordance with the weighted average cost price method, which may be calculated at each purchase operation, or during a period not exceeding, in principle, the average storage period.

2- At inventory, the value of inventory and work in progress shall be estimated at the current price.

3- At the closing of accounts, the current value of inventory and work in progress shall be compared with the book value, and the latter shall be adopted if it is less than the current value.

If, however, the current value is less than the book value, the book value shall continue to be adopted with the constitution of a provision to meet the fall in prices.

This provision shall not be constituted when the inventory and work in progress is the subject of a firm sales contract to be executed subsequently, since the selling price specified in the contract covers at the same time the cost of the goods or raw and consumable materials, the cost of their conversion, and all the remaining expenses incumbent upon the enterprise for the proper execution of the contract.

Fifth: Accounts receivable:

1- A permanent increase in the value of accounts receivable shall be considered as additional accounts receivable matched by revenue for the enterprise.

2- A permanent decline in the value of accounts receivable shall be considered as a decrease in the amount of these receivables matched by a charge borne by the enterprise. If, however, the decline is not definitive, it shall be calculated in the form of a provision.

Sixth: Accounts payable:

1- A permanent increase in the value of accounts payable shall be considered as additional payables matched by a charge borne by the enterprise. If, however, the increase is not definitive, it shall be calculated in the form of a provision.

2- A permanent decline in the value of accounts payable shall be considered as a decrease in the amount of these payables matched by revenue for the enterprise.

Civil Servants and Contracted Workers

1- Civil servants are divided into permanent civil servants and temporary civil servants.

2- A permanent civil servant is one who has been appointed to permanent work in a post provided for in one of the cadres prescribed by the law, whether or not he is subject to the retirement regime.

3- A temporary civil servant is one who has been appointed to a post created for a specified period or for incidental work.

4- Every person in the service of the State who does not belong to either of the two categories set out in the second and third paragraphs of this Article shall be deemed a contracted worker

Legal Status

Civil servants shall be subject to the statutory and regulatory provisions relating to public posts.

All subsequent statutory and regulatory provisions shall apply to them, without their having any acquired right to benefit from the previous provisions

Posts:

1- Permanent posts are divided into categories, categories into ranks, and ranks into grades.

2- Every administration shall have a cadre in which the number of its permanent posts in each category is specified.

This cadre may consist of one or more corps.

General Conditions of Employment:

1- Every applicant for a public post must:

a- have been a Lebanese national for at least ten years

b - have completed twenty years of age

c- not have exceeded thirty-five years of age if he is applying for a post in either the Fifth or Fourth Category.

If, however, he is applying for a post in another category, or a technical post of whatever category, the difference between his age and the retirement age prescribed for such post must not be less than the minimum period required for entitlement to a retirement pension

d- produce a certificate from the official Medical Committee proving that he is free from diseases and infirmities that prevent him from discharging the duties of his post

e- produce a copy of his judicial record proving that he enjoys his civil rights and has not been convicted of a felony or an attempted felony of any kind whatsoever, or of a disgraceful misdemeanour or an attempted disgraceful misdemeanour. The following shall be deemed disgraceful misdemeanours: theft, fraud, breach of trust, issuing a cheque without provision, embezzlement, bribery, rape, intimidation, forgery, use of a forged document, false testimony, perjury, offences against public morals provided for in Title VII of the Penal Code, and offences relating to the cultivation of or trafficking in narcotic substances. These provisions shall apply to persons who have been rehabilitated or who have benefited from an amnesty

f- hold the required academic degrees and qualifications, and successfully pass the competitive examination for appointment in all cases where the law requires passing the competitive examination.

2- The regulations of each Ministry shall specify the special additional conditions that must be met by applicants for its technical posts or certain of its administrative posts.

Age Condition:

1- The age of civil servants and their years of service shall be calculated on the basis of the Gregorian calendar

2- The minimum and maximum age limits prescribed for appointment shall be calculated from the date of birth up to the date fixed for the commencement of the competitive examination, or on the first of January of the year in which the appointment takes place with respect to civil servants whom the law permits to be appointed without a competitive examination

3- The age of the new civil servant shall be stated in the decree or decision providing for his appointment, on the basis of a certified true copy of his entry in the civil status registers, and if the date of the day of birth is unknown, the civil servant shall be deemed to have been born on the first day of the month of July of the year of his birth

If only the month of birth is known, he shall be deemed to have been born on the fifteenth of the month of his birth.

4- No rectification made to the age of a civil servant after the issuance of the instrument of appointment shall be taken into account in determining his age. Likewise, no rectification made to the age of civil servants after the first of March of the year 1943 shall be taken into account, whatever the nature or cause of the rectification, and whether issued through non-contentious jurisdiction or through contentious jurisdiction, with the exception of judicial judgments already executed by the administration.

The provisions of the paragraph shall apply to a civil servant reinstated or who is reinstated into service in public administrations, public institutions, autonomous agencies and municipalities, even if he rectified his age while outside the service. As for a civil servant reappointed or who is reappointed after having left the service, only his age at the date of his first appointment shall be taken into account.

5- Excluded from the provisions set forth above in this Article is any judicial or non-contentious rectification that restores the age of the civil servant to what it originally was in the census conducted pursuant to Decree No. 8837 dated 15/1/1932, in which case the age of the civil servant's entry into office shall be determined in accordance with the said census.

- A civil servant who wishes to benefit from the provisions of this Article must submit an application to that effect to the competent authority.

Paragraph 5 shall be applied within a time limit of three months from the date of entry into force of this Law, under pain of forfeiture of his right.

Conditions of Appointment in the Fifth Category:

The Board of the Civil Service Council shall determine the conditions of appointment in the Fifth Category, provided that the provisions of Article Four of this Legislative Decree are observed therein with the exception of the degree condition, and that the appointment takes place on the basis of an examination organised by the Civil Servants Department in the Civil Service Council

Conditions of Participation for Every Applicant for a Post in Either the Fourth or Third Category:

1- Every applicant for a post in either the Fourth or Third Category must pass the qualifying competitive examination therefor.

2- A special competitive examination shall be held for each of the two ranks of the Fourth Category, and those wishing to participate in the qualifying competitive examination for posts of the Second Rank must hold - the Lebanese Baccalaureate Certificate - Part One, or a certificate equivalent thereto. Exempted from the certificate are stenographers, typists, mail, telegraph and telephone call distributors, and applicants for other posts in which the practical aspect predominates, provided that such posts are specified by a decree after the approval of the Board of the Civil Service Council. "And those wishing to participate in the qualifying competitive examination for posts of the First Rank must hold the Part Two certificate of the Lebanese Baccalaureate, or a certificate equivalent thereto, or Part One of the Lebanese Baccalaureate Certificate if they have spent at least five years in the Second Rank of the Fourth Category, or be among the civil servants of the Second Rank in the Fourth Category who have spent at least ten years in this rank, whatever the certificates they hold.

3- Those wishing to participate in the qualifying competitive examination for posts of the Third Category must hold at least a Licence in Law or a university degree equivalent thereto.

4- These certificates may be replaced for technical posts by special certificates specified in the regulations of each Ministry.

5- A civil servant who has spent ten years in a given category shall have the right to participate in the qualifying competitive examination to occupy a post in the category immediately above it, whatever the certificates he holds, with the exception of technical posts for the occupancy of which the law has required holding a specific specialisation certificate, whether the applicants for such technical posts are civil servants or non-civil servants.

All lease contracts of built real property concluded prior to the promulgation of this Law shall be subject to the provisions hereof, and the expression "lease contracts", wherever it occurs in this Law, shall be understood to mean lease contracts of built real property.

There shall be exempted from the provisions of this Law:

A- Lease contracts of agricultural lands and the buildings appurtenant thereto.

B - Seasonal lease contracts pertaining to summer and winter resorts.

C - Contracts pursuant to which commercial and industrial companies or establishments, building owners, and employers in general provide residential premises for their employees free of charge or for consideration.

D - Lease contracts of villas constructed after 25/3/1974 that meet the following specifications:

- That they consist of one or more storeys, are leased for residential use to a single lessee, and have a garden, a garage, a heating installation, and a special installation providing hot water, even if the lessee bears the expenses of providing the same, provided that these specifications are met on the date of commencement of the original lease.

If the owner does not wish to renew the contract of the exempted villa, he shall notify the lessee thereof at least three months prior to the expiry of the term of the contract, by means of an open registered postal card with acknowledgment of receipt or by means of a written notice through a notary public, and shall pay him a lump-sum compensation equivalent to six times the rent of the last

year, and if the owner fails to give the notification set forth in the second paragraph above, the lease shall be deemed extended for a new year

E - Occupation of the public domain of the State and the municipalities.

F - Lease contracts of furnished premises classified as tourist premises.

Notwithstanding any prior agreement to the contrary, and subject to the exemptions set forth in Article 2 of this Law, there shall be extended until 31/12/ 1995, within the conditions and provisions set forth in this Law,

lease contracts of built real property concluded or extended prior to the promulgation hereof.

The extension shall apply year by year for the benefit of the lessee, and the latter shall be entitled to waive his right thereto provided that he declares his wish not to extend at least two months prior to the expiry of the extended year, by means of an open registered postal card with acknowledgment of receipt addressed to the lessor or by means of a written notice through a notary public. A waiver of the right to extension effected between 1/1/1987 and the date of entry into force of this Law shall remain valid and effective, and a waiver of the right to extension effected under previous laws shall likewise remain valid and effective.
Premises leased under a single contract for both residential and non-residential use shall be deemed residential premises.

In the event of the death of the lessee or his abandonment of the leased premises, there shall be subrogated to him by operation of law in the benefit of the original or extended lease contract, as the case may be, with all its latest conditions or those amended by operation of law:

A - The marriage of the lessee, his ascendants, and his children only who reside with him in the leased premises, with the exception of anyone who has previously left the leased premises and occupied another residence.

B - His relatives who entered the leased premises with him at the commencement of the execution of the lease and have continued to occupy the same without interruption.

For the purpose of calculating the multiplication, the rent that was due by the lessee on 31/12/1986 shall be adopted in respect of the contracts specified in Item A of this Article, and the rent that was due by the lessee on the date of expiry of the initial contractual term shall be adopted

in respect of the contracts specified in Item -B- of this Article, and any consensual increase effected after the entry into force of Law No. 20/82, as amended, shall be taken into account, such that any excess thereof over the statutory increase shall remain an acquired right of the lessor and any shortfall thereof shall be payable by the lessee, and every increase to which the lessee agrees and which he is not bound to pay pursuant to the law shall be deemed consensual for the application of the provisions of this Item, whereas a consensual waiver of previous statutory reductions shall not be deemed a consensual increase, and where the lease contract covers sections whose leases commenced on different dates, the rent shall be apportioned to determine the multiplication according to the date of commencement of the lease of each of them.

C- As of 23/7/1992, and following the multiplication mentioned in Items "A", "B" of this Article, rents shall be indexed and successively increased by a percentage equivalent to half the percentage of the supervening increase each time on the first bracket of salary specified in the decrees relating to the cost-of-living increase and the fixing of wages of employees and workers, as of the date of entry into force of each increase

D- The increases provided for in Items "A" and "B" of this Article shall fall due from the date of entry into force of Law No. 160/92 dated 22/7/1992 without any retroactive effect.

The date of the census and demarcation of real properties and estates in each cadastral area shall be appointed by a decision issued by the Justice of the Peace or the Single Real Property Judge in accordance with the proposal of the Head of Technical Works at the Survey Department. The decision of the Justice of the Peace or the Single Real Property Judge appointing the date of the opening of the operations of census and provisional demarcation in each cadastral area shall be notified to the Head of Technical Works and to the surveyor so that they may, by reason of their mission, notify it to the mukhtars of the cadastral area and the adjoining areas, and this decision shall also be notified to the courts of first instance and of appeal within the jurisdiction of which these areas fall, and the owners and neighbours, and in general every claimant of a right, shall be summoned successively according to the progress of the operations, through the mukhtars, to attend the adversarial demarcation in order to point out the boundaries of their real properties and to establish, where necessary, their claims, and they shall be warned, moreover, that if they do not comply with this summons, their presence shall be dispensed with, and the operation of census and demarcation shall proceed as though they were present, and the Department of Waqfs, with respect to administered waqfs, the State Domain Department, with respect to State domain, and the officer charged with the preservation of terrestrial and maritime public domain shall be subject to the same obligations as those incumbent upon property owners.

Pursuant to the first Article of Decision No. 44/L.R. dated 20/4/1932, Chapter Two (Articles 7 to 14) was repealed and replaced by the following text:

Demarcation and census operations shall, in principle, open every year starting from the first of March, provided that they may be commenced at any time whatsoever. The decision concerning the opening of the operations in each district (qada) or governorate (muhafaza) shall be published at least two months prior to the date of their opening, and there shall be included in an authentic list the villages or localities in which the operations must take place, and reference shall be made therein to the date of their opening, and mention shall be made therein of the obligations incumbent upon the local administrative authorities, and upon the proprietors, as well as mention of the penalties imposed, and this decision shall be notified to the administrative authorities in the governorate (muhafaza), the province (liwa) and the district (qada), and these authorities shall ensure its posting in the real estate areas concerned and in the adjacent areas, and it shall be published in the Official Gazette and in three local newspapers, and all of this shall be carried out through the efforts of the Director of Real Estate Services.

In surveyed areas, the survey shall be conducted on the basis of a grid of primary triangulation points calculated according to perpendicular distances in relation to those points, which must be established in advance prior to commencing the census and provisional demarcation operations.

On the appointed day, the surveyor shall commence the provisional demarcation of the real properties in the presence of the mukhtars, the owners, the interested parties, the adjoining neighbours and the claimants of any right, and shall verify the possession and the existing real property rights in rem, on the basis of the declarations of the interested parties, the adjoining neighbours and the mukhtars.

The declarations must clarify the origin of the claimed rights, and where possession is exercised without title, the cause thereof and the date on which it was established by the current possessor or by his predecessor, and its peaceful, continuous and public character since that date must also be clarified. In the present Decision, the expression (immovable property or estates) shall be understood to mean all rights in rem in immovable property required to be registered in the Land Register, in accordance with the provisions of Decision No. 188 dated 15 March 1926, whereas the word (real properties) means specific parcels of the surface of the land of a single legal category situated within a closed boundary line together with the buildings or plantations thereon deemed to be an integral part thereof, and over which a right of ownership or a right of tessarouf is exercised by a single owner or by several owners in common.

The real property shall constitute the land and cadastral unit, save for the exception provided for in Article 23 of the new text of Decision No. 189 dated 15 March 1926, and upon it shall be founded all the other rights in rem in immovable property subject to registration in the Land Register. The surveyor charged with carrying out the provisional demarcation shall forthwith proceed to record in the minutes referred to in the provisions of Article 15 hereinafter mentioned the declarations of the interested parties, the adjoining neighbours and the mukhtars, and shall also receive and record therein, in accordance with the provisions of Article 21 hereinafter mentioned, the objections and applications put forward by the objectors or claimants of rights during the adversarial demarcation, and shall at the same time receive from them the titles and documents produced in support of the claim, against a receipt issued by him, and the interested parties shall be held responsible for their declarations, which must set out the true state of possession, irrespective of the agreements concluded between the interested parties for the consolidation or partition of lands. Every contract or agreement of this nature shall be received by the Real Property Judge, and confirmed by him where appropriate, upon completion of the provisional demarcation of the real properties and estates in accordance with the provisions of Article 19 et seq. of this Decision.

The Secretary shall oversee the organisation and safekeeping of the registers and files, including:

1- The general foundational register in which all petitions submitted to the President of the Bar or to the Bar Council are registered under serial numbers.

2- A register in which the decisions of the Bar Council are recorded with their consecutive numbers.

3- The registers of the rolls of all lawyers.

4- A register in which the minutes of the pupillage lecture meetings are recorded.

5- A register in which all decisions issued by the Disciplinary Council are recorded with their consecutive numbers.

6- A register in which the correspondence of the Bar Council and the President of the Bar is recorded.

7- A register in which the decisions of the General Assembly are recorded.

8- A file for each lawyer containing all documents and transactions relating to him.

9- A register of the names and salaries of the employees of the Bar.

10- A file for each employee of the Bar containing the documents pertaining to him.

All these registers and others shall be numbered and certified by the President of the Bar and by the Secretary.

No person other than members of the Bar Council may inspect the registers and files set forth in the preceding article or the entries and documents of the Bar except with written permission from the President of the Bar.

The Bar shall have an independent fund called the Bar Council Fund which ensures the collection of the funds of the Bar and the settlement of its financial obligations.

The Treasurer shall undertake the administration of the said Fund and shall be answerable therefor in accordance with the provisions of the Financial Regulations of the Bar.

The resources of this Fund shall consist of:

1- Registration fees on transactions conducted before the Bar.

2- Fees for admission to the Bar.

3- The annual fee on lawyers pertaining to this Fund.

4- Donations and miscellaneous revenues.

The funds pertaining to the said Fund must be collected against receipts from a book with counterfoils and serial numbers. These counterfoils shall be kept at the office of the Bar. Benefits and services shall not be rendered to lawyers who have not paid the Bar fees except by a decision of the Bar Council.

In the real estate areas, the surveyors shall draw up a general demarcation plan progressively as they advance in the operations of survey and provisional demarcation of real properties and estates. The measurement of lands shall be carried out in accordance with the results of the provisional demarcation; however, the final cadastral maps shall only be drawn up after the operations provided for in the provisions of Chapter Four mentioned below are concluded in each real estate area.

These final maps shall be drawn up after verifying their conformity with the texts of the decisions issued by the Justice of the Peace or by the Single Real Estate Judge. If ambiguity arises in the operative part of these decisions, the Technical Cadastral Service shall request their interpretation from the Land Registry Registrar, or by the Adjunct Real Estate Judge appointed for this purpose by the Director of the Real Estate Directorates, or by the Justice of the Peace of the district, as the case may be. If the surveyor entrusted with measuring the land finds that the boundary markers placed as dividers between the real properties have been removed without cause from their locations, he shall automatically proceed to restore them to their former positions, unless they were removed by reason of a topographical operation necessitated by a legal transaction for the transfer of ownership, and this transaction was recorded in the demarcation and survey minutes. After the master map is drawn up in the manner explained above, and its conformity with the decisions of the Single Real Estate Judge is verified, the cadastral contractor shall certify it.

The contractor shall be sworn for this purpose, and upon the publication of this resolution he shall take an oath before the Court of First Instance for Foreign Actions at his place of residence, to perform his function with honesty and proficiency. The certification clause shall be recorded on the map and on the final survey schedule. Thereupon, these documents shall acquire the same conclusive probative force beyond all doubt that attaches to the entries of the Land Register, in accordance with the provisions of Article Eight of Resolution No. 188 dated 15 March 1926, and they shall be deposited with the Land Registry Office as documents pertaining to the Land Register.

The master map shall be preserved without alteration in the archives cabinet of the Office, and shall permanently indicate the status resulting from the decisions issued by the Justice of the Peace or by the Single Real Estate Judge.

As for the modifications that occur to the configuration of the real properties and estates, they shall be recorded on a copy taken from the master map, certified as true by the cadastral contractor.

This copy shall become the authoritative map in the Technical Cadastral Service, and shall be used starting from the date of deposit of the master map. The general demarcation plan, and likewise the cadastral drawing or land measurement, shall be drawn up in accordance with the provisions of the special regulations of the Cadastral Department.

The Treasurer shall:

1- Deposit the funds of the Bar Association in one or more banks selected by the Council of the Bar Association from among the banks approved by the State.

2- Keep and preserve a ledger certified by him and by the President of the Bar Association, in which receipts and disbursements are recorded.

3- Preserve in a special file all supporting documents for the accounting entries.

4- Submit to the Council of the Bar Association, at least once every two months, a statement of the funds received, disbursed and remaining.

5- Prepare, one month prior to the date of the convening of the Ordinary General Assembly, the draft budget for the coming year, which the Council of the Bar Association shall audit and which shall then be submitted to the General Assembly for approval.

6- Abide, with respect to disbursements, by the budget approved by the General Assembly.

All ledgers and documents set forth above shall be preserved at the headquarters of the Bar Association.

The funds of the treasury of the Bar Association shall be allocated to settle the general expenses required of the Bar Association, financial aid to lawyers and to the Retirement and Cooperative Funds, the expenses of the Library of the Bar Association, the purchase of legal books, and every ordinary or extraordinary expense decided upon or approved by the Council of the Bar Association, provided that the budget approved by the General Assembly is abided by.

All transactions pertaining to the treasury of the Bar Association, whether withdrawals or payments, shall only be effected under the joint signature of the President of the Bar Association and the Treasurer, and it is preferable that payment be made by cheques.
The Palace of Justice Commissioners shall attend to the conduct of lawyers in the Palace of Justice and before the courts.

The President of the Bar Association shall supervise the Al-Adl Review issued by the Beirut Bar Association, and the Secretary of the Council of the Bar Association shall be the Responsible Director of this Review.

Notwithstanding the provisions of the Financial Regulations, a special fund outside the annual budget shall be established, in which the collected revenues of the "Al-Adl" Review and its disbursed expenses shall be recorded.

The revenues of the Review shall be collected pursuant to official receipts signed by the Assistant Treasurer, and its expenses shall be paid in accordance with the provisions of Article 55 of the Financial Regulations, and on the basis of payment orders coupled beforehand with the approval of a committee composed of the President of the Bar Association, the Secretary and the Treasurer.

The account of the special fund of the Review shall be closed at the end of each financial year, and this closing of the account shall appear in the general balance sheet of the Bar Association closed at the end of the said year, which is submitted for the approval of the annual Ordinary General Assembly. The surplus resulting from the annual closing of the account shall be carried forward from year to year.

Where it appears during the financial year or at the end thereof that the expenditures of the journal exceed its collected revenues, the difference shall be covered by withdrawals from the surplus realised in previous years, and where that is not possible, such difference shall be covered by withdrawals from the reserve fund of the budget of the Bar Association, provided that such measure is carried out pursuant to a prior decision of the Council and appears in the annual financial statements submitted for the approval of the annual ordinary General Assembly.
The Council of the Bar Association shall elect from among its members a librarian who shall assume the care of the library and the supervision of the work of its employees.

All lawyers registered on the Roll of the Bar Association in Beirut shall have the right to enter the library and consult its books and journals, and no other person may do so without permission from the President of the Bar Association or from the librarian. Any person whomsoever is prohibited from removing from the library room any book, journal or any other item of its contents.
Every lawyer may attach to his service an assistant connected to his office whom he entrusts with pursuing clerical formalities before the courts, enforcement departments and public administrations.

The assistant is required to be Lebanese, not convicted of a felony or a disgraceful misdemeanour, and of good conduct. The offences enumerated in Article 4 of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12 June 1959, as well as acts of incitement thereto and participation and complicity therein, shall be deemed disgraceful.

The lawyer shall submit an application to the President of the Bar Association, who shall order an investigation to be conducted regarding the proposed assistant and shall grant the licence if the result of the investigation is satisfactory; in any event, he exercises absolute discretionary authority in granting or refusing it.

The President of the Bar Association may withdraw this licence after consulting the opinion of the Council of the Bar Association if the assistant ceases to fulfil one of the conditions prescribed for his admission or if he breaches his duties.

The Bar Association shall have employees who ensure the conduct of its affairs and who shall be subject, in respect of appointment, supervision, salaries, promotion and otherwise, to the administrative and financial regulations of the Bar Association.
In addition to the duties provided for in the Law Regulating the Legal Profession, the lawyer shall be subject to the following duties under penalty of disciplinary prosecution.
The lawyer shall accept service of judicial procedure papers when duly presented to him.

The lawyer shall not be entitled to invoke, in the course of examining a dispute, private correspondence or conversations that took place between him and one of his colleagues except with the permission of the latter.
The lawyer may not rely in his pleadings and opinions on texts or case law that he cites contrary to their truth.
The lawyer is prohibited from approaching judges in the absence of his adversary to make statements regarding matters that must be the subject of adversarial discussion.

Article 5 is amended as follows: "In addition to the decisions taken by the Supreme Judicial Council and the opinions it renders in the cases provided for by the law and regulations, the following powers shall be vested in it: a- Preparing the draft of individual or collective judicial transfers, attachments, and secondments and submitting them to the Minister of Justice for approval thereof. b - Approving the drafts of the Minister of Justice to carry out individual or collective transfers and attachments and judicial secondments, unless there is a provision to the contrary. Judicial formations shall not become effective except after the approval of the Minister of Justice and the Supreme Judicial Council, whether the draft originates from the Minister of Justice or from the Council. If the disagreement persists, the matter shall be submitted to the Council of Ministers within a time limit of one month at most to decide thereon. And the Council of Ministers shall decide thereon after hearing the President of the Supreme Judicial Council, who shall present the view of the Council. A ship within the meaning of this Law is every vessel seaworthy for navigation regardless of its tonnage and its designation, whether or not such navigation aims at profit. All accessories necessary for its operation shall be deemed to be part of the ship.

Ships are movable property subject to the general rules of law, subject to the special rules provided for hereinafter.

(As amended by the Laws of 21 December 1954, 30/12/64 and 14/2/66):

And pursuant to Schedule No. 9 of Budget Law No. 280 dated 15/12/93

A ship shall be deemed Lebanese regardless of its tonnage if its port of registry is a Lebanese port and at least half of it is owned by Lebanese persons or by Lebanese joint-stock companies the majority of the members of whose board of directors, including its chairman, are of Lebanese nationality.

All ships intended for long-range navigation, regardless of their net tonnage and regardless of the nationality of their owners, shall also be deemed Lebanese if their port of registry is a Lebanese port, provided that their registration shall be subject to a prior authorisation granted by a decision of the Minister of Public Works.

The paragraphs were added pursuant to Law 280 dated 15/12/93 and amended pursuant to Budget Law 107 dated 23/7/99 :

A - A ship shall also be deemed Lebanese regardless of its tonnage if its port of registry is a Lebanese port and at least half of it is owned by:

- A general partnership in which all the partners are Lebanese.

- A limited partnership in which all the liable partners are Lebanese.

- A limited liability company in which the majority of the partners, including the manager, are Lebanese and the majority of the shares belong to them.

B - The text of Paragraph B was amended pursuant to Schedule No. 9 annexed to Law No. 107 dated 23/7/1999, and then the text of Item B was repealed pursuant to Decree No. 40 dated 22/2/2007 Official Gazette 12 (2007 Budget) (The Treasury shall levy on the gross revenues earned by the two ship pilotage stations in the ports of Beirut and Tripoli a rate of 10% (ten per cent) on these revenues.

This measure shall apply to all other pilotage stations and to licensed pilots in all other ports and terminals.)

C - Previous fees contrary to these fees and every previous reduction or discount granted to Lebanese ships are repealed.

Shall be treated as Lebanese ships.

1) Derelict ships at sea picked up by ships flying the Lebanese flag.

2) Ships confiscated for violating Lebanese laws.

All ships designated in this Article and in the Second Article must fly the Lebanese flag during a voyage, subject to the provisions of the Second Paragraph of Article 16

Lebanese vessels alone shall have the right to fish along the coasts, the right of coastal commercial navigation between Lebanese ports, and the right to tow vessels upon their entry into and exit from these ports.

Lebanese vessels must be marked in Arabic and Latin characters with the following markings:

1) Steamships and motor vessels intended for coastal navigation or navigation on the high seas: the name of the vessel on both sides of its bow. And on its stern, its name and the name of its port of registry.

2) Coastal sailing vessels: on each side of the bow: the distinguishing letters of its port of registry and the number of this registration. On the stern: the name of the vessel and the name of its port of registry.

3) Fishing boats. On each side of the bow: the distinguishing letters of its port of registry and the number of this registration.

4) Launches, quay boats intended for cargo, and all floating hulls therein (such as lighters, dredgers "sand dredgers", barges ...): the markings of fishing boats having the same tonnage.

5) Launches and boats of official departments and concessionary companies. On the bow and on the stern, or on the bow alone: the name of the vessel. In the cabin: the distinguishing letters of its port of registry together with the number of this registration.

6) Pleasure vessels.

These vessels are permitted not to be marked with their registration number on the outside; however, this number must be carved in the cabin.

Shipowners must have officially certified the usable capacity of their vessels (net tonnage) and their entire internal capacity plus the capacity of the structures erected on the deck (gross tonnage). The assessment of the tonnage of vessels, the valuation of their appurtenances, and the specification thereof shall be entrusted to the Port Authority, which shall draw up a certificate for all of the foregoing at the expense of the owner, builder, or trustee thereof, who must provide the necessary means to carry out these procedures
The net tonnage figure of the vessel shall be carved in Arabic and Latin on the aft side of the main deck beam or on the forward side of the main hatchway.

The following paragraph shall be added to Article 31:

"The powers vested in the Appellate Public Prosecutor pursuant to the Code of Criminal Procedure shall be transferred to the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation.

The provisions of Part Three, Title Two of the Code of Criminal Procedure shall be observed, and the First President of the Court of Cassation and the Public Prosecutor thereat shall each exercise the powers vested in the President of the Court of Appeal and the Public Prosecutor thereat pursuant to the provisions of the said Title.
