- A register shall be kept in each of the ports of Tyre, Sidon, Beirut, and Tripoli; every sheet of this register shall be numbered and signed, and its number shall be the registration number of the vessel to which the sheet is exclusively assigned.

All Lebanese vessels shall be entered in this register.

There shall be registered in the port of:

Tyre: Vessels belonging to the ports situated between the Palestinian border and the mouth of the Litani River.

Sidon: Vessels belonging to the ports situated between the mouth of the Litani River and the Damour River.

Beirut: Vessels belonging to the ports situated between the mouth of the Damour River and Ras Al-Barbara.

Tripoli: Vessels belonging to the ports situated between Ras Al-Barbara and the northern border of Lebanon, and these ports shall be indicated by the following distinctive letters:

For Tyre (ص ر) - For Sidon (ص أ) - For Beirut (ب) - For Tripoli (ط).

A vessel is said to belong to a given port when its owner has a real domicile or an elected domicile in that port.

Vessels belonging to official departments (Customs - Police - Quarantine Service and the State, etc.) shall be registered in the port of their habitual anchorage.

Paragraph added pursuant to Table No. 9 of the Budget Law No. 280 dated 15/12/93.

- The ports of Chekka, Byblos, Junieh shall be deemed ports of registration, and the scope of each of them and the letters indicating it shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Transport.

It shall not be permissible in any manner whatsoever to efface, conceal, or cover the legal letters, numbers, or marks. Any violation of these provisions shall subject the owner of the vessel and its master to the penalty of imprisonment from two days to ten days and to a fine ranging between five pounds and one hundred pounds, or to one of these two penalties.

Likewise, the affixing of false marks shall subject the owner of the vessel and its master to the penalties provided for in the second paragraph of Article 19 of this Law.

Vessels belonging to foreign persons residing in Lebanon may be registered in Lebanon by a permit from the Minister of Public Works if such vessels are intended for pleasure or for cruising within a Lebanese port without any other navigation.

This permit may be withdrawn in the event of a violation of these regulations or upon a change of the owner of the vessel, and the permit shall inevitably be withdrawn if the vessel is used for navigation other than that assigned to it in its registration.

Foreign vessels registered in a Lebanese port shall fly the flag of the country of their owner or the flag of the country of one of their owners if owned by several persons.

There must be stated in the registration books for each vessel on its folio:

1) Its name (and if there are several vessels of the same name, a serial number shall be appended to each name).

2) The registration number (to which the distinguishing letters of the port of registration shall be appended).

3) The date of construction of the vessel and the place in which it was constructed.

4) Its type (whether it is a sailing vessel or a steamship, etc..)

5) Its dimensions (in length, breadth and depth).

6) Its net tonnage and its gross tonnage in barrels (tonnages).

7) The type of the propelling engines and their power.

8) The names of the owners, their nationality and their domicile, specifying the number of shares of each of them.

9) The name of the managing ship-operator, his nationality and his place of residence.

10) Any contingent alteration to the vessel such as a change in its port or in its owner, etc..

11) The causes for its striking off, such as loss, destruction or sale.

12) Any attachment or mortgage placed upon it.

Every holder of a registered debt may demand the sale of the vessel by auction or the sale of the mortgaged share thereof by offering an increase over the price amounting to one-tenth and providing security for the payment of the price and the costs.

This demand, signed by the creditor, must be served upon the purchaser within a time limit of ten days after the notification. The demand shall contain a writ of summons before the Court of First Instance having jurisdiction over the place where the vessel is located, or its port of registration if it is at sea, in order to decide on holding the public auction.
The sale by auction shall take place at the diligence of the creditor who demanded it or at the diligence of the purchaser in the forms prescribed in the following Articles.

The sale of a vessel abroad is prohibited if it is mortgaged in Lebanon.

Any sale in violation hereof cannot be recorded in the registration book on account of its being null and void and of no effect. An owner who voluntarily sells abroad a mortgaged vessel shall be deemed guilty of the offence of breach of trust and shall be subject to the penalties provided for in Article 670 of the Penal Code.
An attachment may not be proceeded with until after the expiry of twenty-four hours from the formal notice to pay.

The formal notice must be served upon the person of the owner or at his domicile. If the owner is not present, the formal notice may be served upon the master of the vessel if the debt relates to the vessel or to the cargo.
If ten days and more have elapsed since the formal notice, the creditor must renew it before levying the attachment.

The enforcement officer shall set forth in the seizure report the following:

- The name of the creditor applying for the seizure, his profession, and his domicile

- The instrument pursuant to which execution is pursued

- The amount required to be paid

- The elected domicile of the creditor at the seat of the court before which the sale must be pursued and at the place where the seized ship is moored.

- The name of the owner of the ship and the name of the master

- The name of the vessel, its type, its tonnage, and its nationality.

The submission of a statement and description of the skiffs, boats, gear, tackle, apparatus, provisions, and stores, together with the appointment of a custodian.

The seizing party shall serve upon the owner within a time limit of three days a copy of the seizure report and summon him before the court of the place of the seizure to decide in his presence to proceed with the sale of the seized items.

If the owner is not resident within the jurisdiction of the court, service shall be effected upon him within a time limit of fifteen days in the person of the master of the seized vessel if he is present, and otherwise in the person of the representative of the owner or the representative of the master.

If the owner is a foreigner who has neither a domicile nor a residence in the Lebanese Republic nor anyone representing him, he shall be summoned and served in accordance with Article 362 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

The seizure report shall be registered in the register of the port of registration of the ship or in the register of the port within the jurisdiction of which the ship is being constructed, after its registration if it is under construction.

Following such registration, the debtor subjected to the seizure shall no longer have the right to sell the ship or the right to effect a mortgage thereon. The authority in charge of the registration office shall issue a statement of entries within a time limit of three days starting from the registration (holidays not being included in the calculation thereof), and within a time limit of eight days starting from the issuance of such statement, the party applying for the seizure shall serve upon the registered creditors, at their domicile elected in their registration, the summons set forth in the preceding Article. The creditors shall have a time limit of fifteen days to intervene if they so wish.

If the ship is foreign, service shall be effected within a time limit of eight days after the delivery of the mortgage statement from the consulate to the registered creditors mentioned in the said statement in the manner provided for in the Code of Procedure.

The said creditors shall have a time limit to intervene of fifteen days in addition to the supplementary time limits for distance.

The court of the place of the seizure shall order the sale and the conditions thereof as set forth by the party applying for the seizure and shall fix the date thereof and the upset price.

If no price is offered on the day fixed for the sale, the court shall fix a new upset price lower than the first price and a date for the subsequent auction.

Actions for revendicating ownership and for annulment shall be brought prior to the adjudication. However, if actions for revendicating ownership are brought only after the adjudication, they shall be converted ipso jure into an opposition to the delivery of the sums resulting from the sale.

Actions for revendicating ownership and for annulment shall not be admissible unless they are entered in the register.

The plaintiff or the opposing party shall be granted three days to submit his arguments, and likewise the defendant shall be granted three days to reply thereto. A hearing for the action shall be scheduled upon a mere petition.

The action shall not stay execution unless the court orders its stay for important reasons.

The sale shall take place at a public auction hearing in the Civil Court fifteen days after the posting of the notices prescribed in the following Article and the publication in at least two newspapers, one of which is in Arabic, from among the newspapers designated for the publication of judicial notices at the seat of the court, in addition to the methods of publication authorised by the court.

The notices shall be affixed to the most conspicuous part of the arrested vessel, to the main door of the court before which the sale takes place, on the quay of the port in which the vessel is berthed, and at the Commercial Exchange, if one exists.

The notices affixed or inserted in the newspapers must set forth the following:

- The name, profession, and domicile of the party applying for the arrest

- The documents pursuant to which he is proceeding

- The amount of the sum due to be paid to him

- The domicile he elects at the seat of the court and at the anchorage of the arrested vessel

- The name, profession, and domicile of the owner of the arrested vessel

- The characteristics of the vessel as recorded in the register

- The name of the master

- The place where the vessel is located

- The reserve price and the conditions of sale

- The place, day, and hour of the auction.
An overbid shall not be admissible in the event of a judicial sale.

The purchaser must, within a time-limit of twenty-four hours starting from the adjudication, deposit his purchase price, free of expenses, in one of the banks approved by the Government, on pain of the resale by auction being held at his risk and expense.

In the event of failure to deposit, the vessel shall be put up for sale anew and its adjudication shall be decided three days after the renewal of the publication and notice, as provided for in Article 84, at a resale by auction held at the risk and expense of the purchaser.

The latter shall remain liable for the payment of the deficiency, damages, and expenses.

Sole Article: - The draft law set forth in Decree No. 2695 dated 23 March 2000 relating to the establishment of a compulsory Order of Physiotherapists in Lebanon, as amended by the Administration and Justice Committee, is hereby approved.

- This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Physiotherapists in Lebanon shall have an Order named the "Order of Physiotherapists in Lebanon", whose headquarters shall be in the capital Beirut, and which shall comprise physiotherapists licensed to practise the profession of physiotherapy in the Lebanese Republic.

The mission of the Order of Physiotherapists in Lebanon is a professional, health, scientific and administrative mission, whose purpose is to:

- Unite physiotherapists, safeguard their rights and legitimate interests, raise the standard of their profession, watch over professional ethics, express an opinion on draft laws and regulations relating to the profession of physiotherapy at the request of the competent ministries

- Express an opinion on sending delegations and attending physiotherapy conferences supervised by the Order

- Endeavour with the Government to adopt such resolutions as the Order deems beneficial in matters pertaining to public health, prevention and rehabilitation

- Endeavour to settle disputes arising between physiotherapists, or between them and other members of the health and medical professions, or between physiotherapists and their patients, all arising from the practice of the profession

- Assist needy and disabled physiotherapists or their families, and establish a pension fund to insure against old age and disability.
No physiotherapist shall have the right to practise the profession of physiotherapy in Lebanese territory unless his name is registered on the roll of the Order of Physiotherapists in Lebanon.

Subject to the provisions of Article Two of Law No. 96/99 dated 18/06/1999, any person applying for the registration of his name on the roll of the Order must hold all the qualifications required to practise the profession of physiotherapy in Lebanese territory pursuant to the laws in force, and he must state in his application his first name, surname, nationality, age, the name of the university from which he graduated, the date of obtaining his degree and its number, his academic titles, his place of residence and the place where he intends to practise his profession, together with a certified copy of the supporting documents for the information mentioned above, in addition to a copy of the licence from the Ministry of Health, a recent criminal record extract, and three passport-size photographs, together with the admission fee and the annual fee in full.

The judgment of adjudication shall not be subject to opposition.

However, within five days from the date of its pronouncement, and solely on the ground of a defect in its form, it may be brought before the Court of Appeal pursuant to a writ of summons of three clear days, which shall rule thereon by a decision not subject to opposition.
The judgment of adjudication shall be recorded in the register at the request of the Execution Department after it has acquired the force of res judicata.

Adjudication shall discharge the vessel from all privileges, mortgages, and actions for annulment to which persons who have previously been served pursuant to Article 78 are entitled.

The striking off of the registration of the said privileges, mortgages, and actions shall be effected for the purchaser upon his submission to the registration office of the judgment of adjudication and a certificate from the registry of the court that rendered it proving that the said judgment has acquired the force of res judicata.
The distribution of the moneys resulting from the adjudication shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of Articles 794 to 807 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

Every shipowner shall be personally liable for the obligations arising from the acts performed by the master and the contracts concluded by him in the course of exercising his legal powers, and he shall also be liable for the acts and faults of the master, the seamen, the pilot, and all other servants of the vessel.

The Ordinary General Assembly shall have competence over the following matters:

- Electing the Council of the Order and the President of the Order.

- Approving the resolutions submitted to it by the Council of the Order.

- Approving the financial report after examining and discussing it.

- Determining the general directions for the various activities of the Order.

- Examining the agenda and taking the appropriate decisions thereon.

- Determining the annual fee and the affiliation fee imposed on physical therapists.

- Auditing the accounts of the preceding year and approving them.
The Extraordinary General Assembly shall examine matters related to the profession and set forth in the request for convocation or in the decision of the Council.

The Council of the Order shall be composed of twelve members elected by the General Assembly at its annual general meeting, and it shall elect a President of the Order from among them at the same session.

The members of the Council of the Order and the President of the Order shall be elected by secret ballot for three years, and the term of one-third of the members shall expire each year. Voting shall be by absolute majority in the first round, and by relative majority in the second round, and in the event of a tie of votes, the oldest in age shall prevail.

Members whose term has expired may be re-elected once, and they may not be re-elected for a third time except after the lapse of at least one electoral term. In the first and second years, the one-third of the members whose term expires shall be designated by lot.

Every Lebanese registered with the Order who has practised the profession for at least five years, on Lebanese territory, shall have the right to stand as a candidate for membership of the Council of the Order of Physical Therapists in Lebanon, and a physical therapist who has practised the profession for a period of at least ten years on Lebanese territory shall have the right to stand as a candidate for the post of President of the Order.

The term of office of the President of the Order shall be three years, and he may not be re-elected except after the lapse of three years from the expiry of his term of office.

If it happens that the President of the Order elected for three years is among the members of the Council whose term of office expires in the year following his election, he shall continue in the membership of the Council of the Order until the end of the three years.

The President of the Order shall represent the Order of Physical Therapists and defend its rights, and he is charged with executing the decisions of the Council of the Order, and he has the right to litigate in the name of the Order in accordance with the applicable rules.

The Council of the Order shall examine the application at the first session it holds after the date of its submission or within a maximum period of two months, and shall decide to accept it if it fulfils the legal conditions, and it shall not be entitled to reject any application fulfilling the conditions except with a clear reasoning for such rejection.
The Order shall be composed of all the physical therapists whose names are registered on its roll, and their meeting shall constitute a General Assembly.
The Order shall be represented by a Council elected by the General Assembly in the manner set forth in this Law, presided over by the President of the Order of Physical Therapists in Lebanon.

The Ordinary General Assembly of the Order shall convene once every year during the first half of the month of November, and an Extraordinary General Assembly shall convene pursuant to a decision taken by the Council of the Order by a two-thirds majority or pursuant to a petition submitted to the Council of the Order by one-third of the registered physical therapists.

Only the physical therapists registered on the roll of the Order and who have paid the annual fee shall be entitled to participate in the General Assembly, and only those shall be entitled to vote, provided that they are of Lebanese nationality.

A physical therapist who defaults on paying the annual fee without excuse for a period of two consecutive years shall have his name struck off the roll by a decision of the Council of the Order, and he shall not be entitled to apply for the re-registration of his name until after he pays the overdue fees.

The President of the Order shall preside over the General Assembly, and in the event of his absence or inability to attend, he shall be replaced successively by the Vice-President of the Order, then the Secretary of the Council, then the oldest member.

The convening of the Ordinary General Assembly shall not be deemed legal except in the presence of more than half of the members who have paid their annual subscriptions, whereas the convening of the Extraordinary General Assembly shall not be deemed legal except in the presence of two-thirds of the members; in both cases, if the legal quorum is not met, the invitation of the members shall be repeated a second time, and the convening of the Ordinary or Extraordinary General Assembly shall be deemed legal with whoever attends.

The Ordinary General Assembly shall take its decisions by voting and by the absolute majority of the members present.

Whereas the Extraordinary General Assembly shall take its decisions by voting and by a two-thirds majority of the members present.

The Vice-President shall act in the place of the President in his absence and shall exercise all of his powers while performing this mission.

The functions of the Secretary and the Treasurer shall be determined in the internal regulations.

At the first session held by the Council of the Order following the general elections, the Council shall elect from among its members a Vice-President, a Secretary, and a Treasurer for a term of one year, renewable.

Every member against whom a disciplinary judgment that has become final and conclusive has been issued imposing a penalty other than a warning and a reprimand shall be deemed dismissed from the Council of the Order.

Every member who absents himself from the meetings of the Council three consecutive times without a legitimate excuse after being given written notice shall be deemed to have resigned from the Council of the Order.

The public domain in the State of Greater Lebanon and the State of the Alawites comprises all things intended by reason of their nature for the use of all or for the use of a public service, and they are inalienable and ownership thereof is not acquired by prescription.

The public domain comprises in particular the properties mentioned below, without preventing thereby the application of Article 3 of this Order:

1 - The seashore up to the farthest distance reached by the waves in winter, and beaches of sand and gravel, lagoons and salt lakes connected directly to the sea, watercourses of whatever kind within their limits defined by the line of the height of their running waters in a state of fullness prior to their overflowing, underground running waters and springs of whatever kind, the entire banks of watercourses, that is the parcel of land situated along their courses which enables watching over them, cleaning them and preserving them, lakes, lagoons and ponds within their limits defined in accordance with the highest level which the waters reach prior to their overflowing, and there is added thereto on each bank a zone for passage of ten metres in width starting from these limits, waterfalls suitable for generating motive power.

2 - Navigation canals and their towpaths from which vessels are towed in their course, irrigation, drainage and filtration canals and their entire banks, and aqueducts when the aqueducts are established for the public interest, and likewise the appurtenances of these installations are also included in the public domain, maritime or river dikes, telegraphic wires on the coasts (semaphores), lighting or maritime beaconage installations and their appurtenances, telegraphic and telephonic lines and their appurtenances operated by a public service, fortification installations and war posts or military posts.

3 - Roads, streets, passages, lines and means of communication of whatever kind and their appurtenances, except installations carried out by individuals for their private needs, railways and tramways and their appurtenances, ports, maritime harbours and bays, installations erected for public utility and for the use of hydraulic forces and the transmission of electric power.

The Committee shall first carry out a provisional demarcation; it shall proceed for this purpose to the place of demarcation, receive the observations of the riparian inhabitants, and hear the statements of the persons whom it deems capable of providing explanations to it regarding the material investigations which it is required to conduct; and if the demarcation relates to maritime public domain or to lakes, the Committee shall ascertain the boundaries of the area reached by the highest wave of the year, without confounding these boundaries with the limit reached instead by the highest wave during a storm.

The President of the Committee shall send to the head of the district in which the section of the public domain to be demarcated is situated a notice fixing the date of the meeting of the Committee at the place of demarcation for the commencement of the provisional demarcation operations, and this notice must be widely publicised by being posted in the places where official notices are customarily posted; the President of the Committee shall publish the same notice in the Official Gazette at least 10 days before the date of the commencement of the operations.

After the Committee has ascertained the boundaries of the public domain, it shall place, where necessary, in its presence, boundary markers or stakes along the perimeter of these boundaries and draw up a record in which the position of the boundary markers and stakes is specified as far as possible; there shall be annexed to the record a plan of the premises indicating the proposed boundaries together with the boundary markers, stakes, shores, and the marks by which they are identified; the original copies of the record and of the plan shall be signed by all the members of the Committee.

A copy of the record and of the plan shall be deposited for a period of one month at the office of the head of the district.

This official shall take note during this period of the observations and objections of the riparian inhabitants and other persons in a special register numbered and signed by the President of the Committee; as for the observations and objections sent in writing, they shall be added to the register.

Notice shall be given to the public, in accordance with the conditions specified in Article Nine above, of the date and place of the deposit relating to the inquiries concerning the record and the plan.

The head of the district shall close the register of inquiries upon the expiry of the period of one month and send it forthwith to the President of the Committee.

The Committee shall examine the observations and objections mentioned in the register of inquiry and shall return to the place of demarcation if it deems it useful to inspect the premises and modify, where necessary, the provisional demarcation.

The modifications shall be transferred onto the plans and a new record shall be drawn up containing the new proposals, and if the objections are rejected, that shall be stated in the observations of the Committee.

If the riparian inhabitants accept the demarcation carried out in this manner, the Committee shall annex to its record a written declaration from the interested parties stating that the proposed demarcation does not encroach upon their properties.

Persons who have, over the appurtenances of the public domain as defined in this Decision, rights of ownership, disposal or enjoyment by virtue of established customs or legal and final titles prior to the entry into force of this Decision may not be dispossessed thereof, where public utility so requires, except after payment of fair and prior compensation. The compensation shall be determined, unless the matter is brought before an administrative court in the State, by a commission composed of three members, one of whom shall be appointed by the Head of State, the second by the owner of the property, and the third by the Head of State and the owner of the property by agreement.

If the owner of the property fails to appoint his arbitrator within a period of one month following a request sent to him, and if no agreement is reached on the choice of the third arbitrator, he shall be appointed by the Director of Justice.

The properties mentioned in Article One and Article Two shall be considered as belonging to the national public domain or to the municipal public domain according to their allocation to national utility or to municipal utility.

The distinction between the national public domain and the municipal public domain shall be determined in a decision of the Head of State taken in the Council of Directors.

The boundaries of the public domain as defined in the First and Second Articles of this Decision, with the exception of properties capable of being included in the military public domain, shall be established in accordance with the conditions mentioned in this Decision.

No demarcation operation whatsoever shall be carried out in the public domain except by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister, specifying the district or the section of the district in which the demarcation operation is to take place, and likewise the nature of the public domain required to be demarcated must be stated.

The demarcation operations shall be carried out by a commission composed of three members as follows:

- The Director of Public Works or an engineer delegated by him.

- A chief senior official from the Directorate of Finance.

- A member of the municipality on whose land the demarcation operation is taking place.

If the properties are outside the lands of the municipalities, a representative of the local administration appointed by the Director of the Interior shall be appointed to the commission, and if the demarcation is taking place on maritime public domain, the Inspector of the Merchant Navy or his delegate shall be appointed as the third member.

The minutes, the plan and the entire inquiry shall be signed by all the members of the committee and shall thereafter be transmitted to the Head of State, who shall confirm, pursuant to a decision taken by him, the boundaries of the intended parcel of the public domain and all the rights of other persons reserved to them within the boundaries provided for in this decision.

The roads and narrow passages necessary for passing from one place to another, and which custom has compelled proprietors to accept as a public passage, shall be incorporated into the public domain progressively according to need through the care of a committee constituted as mentioned in the seventh Article above, and this committee shall determine the width and direction of these roads and passages, subject to the approval thereof by the Head of State.

Rights arising from an estate opened prior to the promulgation of this Resolution must be registered within six months from the date of its promulgation. The ordinary fees shall be levied thereon, regardless of the period that may have elapsed since the death of the decedent, and irrespective of the number of subsequent estates, their degrees and their ranks, and these fees shall be liquidated in proportion to the share of each heir; and if these estates are the subject of a dispute pending before the courts, the time limit shall run from the date of the issuance of the final judgment thereon, and if the said time limit expires, the fees shall be levied at double the rate in a single payment.

Heads of Execution Offices must require the interested parties to deposit in advance with the Treasury the registration fees and the transfer and devolution fees pertaining to the rights requested to be entered through them in the Land Register, or in the Registration Book, or in the Tabu registers, and the same obligation is incumbent upon the authorised officials who are requested to make an entry, an annotation, a caveat, or a cancellation of an entry in the Land Register, or in the Registration Book, or in the Tabu registers.

Holders of real rights entered in the Land Register are required to notify the Head of the Auxiliary Land Office of every change that has occurred in the substance and appurtenances of the property as a result of expropriation, or construction of buildings, or demolition, or planting, or subdivision, etc..., within the six months following the occurrence of the event that resulted in the change,

provided that the change did not occur as a result of an official act on the part of the Administration; if they fail to do so, the entry shall be made ex officio at their expense. And the fee shall be levied at double the rate.

Holders of real rights entered in the Land Register who did not notify the Head of the Auxiliary Land Office of the changes that occurred in the substance and appurtenances of their property within the period specified in the above-mentioned Article shall be exempted from the double fee provided for in Article 60 of Resolution No. 189 dated 15/3/1926 (Details relating to the implementation of Resolution No. 188 dated 15/3/1926 concerning the Land Register), if the notification of these changes and the payment of the fee take place within a time limit not exceeding 31/12/2019.

Any changes that have occurred to the physical composition of properties and their appurtenances prior to the promulgation of this Law and that have not been recorded on their real folios must be declared and recorded in the Land Register by the holders of rights in rem within the six months following the promulgation of this Resolution; if they fail to do so, the Registrar of the Land Register in the district shall carry out the registration ex officio on the basis of his personal knowledge or the statement of any person whomsoever, in which case the registration fees shall be doubled, the informant shall be entitled to receive half of the fine collected, and a compulsory mortgage shall be recorded on the real folio of the property until the collection of the fees and the fine.
The tariff of fixed fees and of conveyance and devolution fees, and the manner of collecting these fees, shall be determined in each State by a legislative text.

The registers, namely the record books and the registers of mortgages currently existing and kept at the Defterkhaneh, shall be retained for the registration of real estate disposal and devolution and mortgage agreements in all real estate areas in which there is no Real Estate Register in implementation of Decision No. 188 concerning the establishment of the Real Estate Register.

Whenever these reforms are carried out in full in each district, the permanent record books and the mortgage books in the district shall be closed and sealed by the head of the auxiliary office and sent to the head of the real estate office.

On the same day on which these books are received, the head of the real estate office shall draw up a record of receipt and send a copy thereof to the head of the auxiliary office.
All provisions contrary to this Decision are repealed and shall remain repealed.

Rules for organising competitive examinations for the Fourth and Third Categories:

1- The Board of the Civil Service Council shall lay down the regulations for competitive examinations and their syllabi in agreement with the competent ministries. These regulations may provide for the granting of additional marks not exceeding 15 % of the total marks to candidates holding degrees higher than the required minimum and ten percent to employees who have ten years or more in service, provided that these marks are granted when establishing the order of merit of successful candidates, to those who succeed in the competitive examination.

2- The Personnel Administration at the Civil Service Council shall organise the competitive examinations, with the exception of the entrance competitive examinations to the National Institute of Public Administration, and the competitive examinations and selective examinations aimed at dispatching employees who are in service and persons intended to be prepared for the public service abroad for specialisation, which fall within the sole competence of the Preparation and Training Administration.

Each of the two aforementioned administrations shall, according to its competence, determine the dates and places of these competitive examinations and examinations and the period within which

applications must be submitted, and shall also determine the latest date for announcing the results. It shall announce this on the Lebanese Radio and in at least three local daily

newspapers. The period for submitting applications must not be less than fifteen days starting from the date of the announcement on the radio or in the daily newspapers.

3- The Civil Service Council may organise joint competitive examinations for similar posts within the same category in all administrations, or in some of them,

and it may also organise a special competitive examination for each administration, particularly for technical posts.

4- The Civil Service Council shall appoint the members of the examining committees, provided that some of them are employees and the others are from higher education

bodies or specialists.

5- The Civil Service Council shall draw up, upon the proposal of the Personnel Administration or the Preparation and Training Administration according to the competence of each of them, a list of the candidates who fulfil the conditions for participating in the competitive examination or the examination. Its decision shall not be subject to appeal, including an application for annulment

for excess of power.

6- The competent administration shall seek the assistance, when necessary in conducting the competitive examinations or examinations, of the employees of the competent ministry.

7- The results of the competitive examination or examination shall be announced, immediately upon their issuance, on the door of the Civil Service Council, and the list of successful candidates shall remain valid for a period of two years only from the date of its announcement. This list shall have priority during two years over the list that follows it, and the list of successful candidates shall exhaust its effect upon the expiry of the two-year period.

8- The Civil Service Council may cancel the competitive examination or the examination upon the proposal of the Personnel Administration or the Preparation and Training Administration

according to competence. Provided that the cancellation decision must precede the announcement of the results, and shall be deemed null and void if taken thereafter.

Conditions of Appointment in the Fourth and Third Categories:

1- Employees of the Fourth and Third Categories shall be appointed by decree following the approval of the Board of the Civil Service Council.

2- The order of passing grades in the competitive examination shall be respected in the appointment.

3- The employees referred to in Paragraph (5) of Article (7) shall be appointed to the last step of the category if its salary exceeds their salary, or to the step whose salary is equivalent to their salary. They shall retain the right of qualifying seniority for promotion in the event of equivalence in salary.

Conditions of Probation in the Fourth and Third Categories:

1- Persons appointed to each of the Fourth and Third Categories shall remain on probation for a period of one year in the step to which they were appointed. Exempted from probation shall be

the employees referred to in Paragraph (5) of Article (7) of this Legislative Decree and employees who are graduates of the Preparation Branch at the

National Institute of Public Administration.

2- Each ministry shall undertake the training of the probationers affiliated to it in accordance with the general principles determined by the Preparation and Training Administration at the Civil Service Council.

3- Probationers shall be confirmed by a decision of the Minister following the approval of the Board of the Civil Service Council. The effect of confirmation shall be deemed valid starting from the date of expiry of the probation period referred to in the first paragraph of this Article.

4- The authority vested with the right to appoint them may dismiss probationers before the expiry of the probation period or at its end following the approval of the Central Inspection Administration, and in this case the probationer shall not be entitled to any dismissal indemnity for the period spent in service, and the effect of dismissal shall be deemed valid starting from the date of his notification or from the date of actual cessation of work if that occurred prior to notification.

5- If confirmation or dismissal is not decided upon the end of the probation period, the probationer must request his confirmation within a time limit of one month. The Administration must decide on his request within a period of another month, failing which he shall be deemed confirmed by operation of law since the end of his probation period.

6- The probation period shall be included in the count of years of actual service.

1- Vacant positions in the Second Category shall be filled by selection from among the employees of the first and second grades of the Third Category who have successfully completed a training course at the Institute of Public Administration and whose names have been entered on the promotion roster, and they shall be classified in the last grade of the Category and shall retain their right to the seniority qualifying for advancement if they are classified at a salary equal to their original salary.

The Board of the Civil Service Council may exempt from the requirement of the aforementioned training course the employees who have successfully completed a training course in administrative affairs of a duration of not less than six continuous months at one of the institutes of public administration abroad and who were delegated to these institutes on specialisation scholarships in accordance with the rules, provided that this exemption is coupled with the approval of the Council of Ministers

By way of exception, by a decision issued by the Council of Ministers, graduates of institutes of public administration abroad may be appointed to one of the posts referred to in the preceding Article, provided that they have spent therein a period of at least nine months of continuous study in administrative affairs similar to the study programme adopted at the Institute of Public Administration in Lebanon, which combines theoretical and practical training.

2- Vacant technical positions in the Second Category may be filled by way of a competitive examination in which employees of the Third Category and candidates from

outside the cadre are entitled to participate, provided that the regulations of the Ministry permit this or that the Board of the Civil Service Council decides the matter upon the proposal of the competent Administration, and it is required of all candidates, whether they are employees or from outside the cadre, that they be holders of university degrees and that they be persons of experience in the type of work required in the competent Administration.

3- The provisions of Article (8) of this Legislative Decree shall apply to the organisation of the competitive examination referred to in the preceding paragraph of this Article.

4- Employees of the Second Category shall be appointed by decree after the approval of the Board of the Civil Service Council. The conditions of probation shall not apply to them.

Conditions for Appointment to Category One:

1- Vacant positions in Category One shall be filled by selection from among the employees of the top three grades of Category Two whose names are listed on the promotion roster, and they shall be classified in the last grade of Category One. They shall retain their right to the seniority qualifying for advancement if they are classified at a salary equivalent to their salary.

2- By way of exception, persons from outside the cadre may be appointed to Category One, after seeking the opinion of the Civil Service Board, provided that they hold university degrees, and they shall be deemed confirmed upon their appointment, and this measure shall only apply at a ratio of one-third of the vacant positions in Category One.

3- Category One employees shall be appointed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.

Special Cases:

1- An employee transferred to a position situated outside his place of residence shall be entitled to continue receiving his salaries without interruption, provided that he complies with the written instructions issued by his superiors regarding his travel.

2- An employee shall not receive a salary for the period he spends in prison in execution of a judicial sentence unless he is convicted of an unintentional misdemeanour.

3- If an employee goes missing, news of him ceases, and traces of him disappear during service, his salaries shall be paid to the beneficiaries provided for in the Retirement Law until the earlier of the two dates:

- His reaching the retirement age or the lapse of ten years from his disappearance judicially declared by the competent judiciary with respect to the religious community to which he belongs, and this period during which his salaries are paid shall be deemed included in actual service and the rights of his heirs shall be liquidated provisionally on this basis in accordance with the provisions of the law.

4- If an employee whose service has ended is required to carry out the handover and takeover procedure, he shall receive an allowance equivalent to his salary for the period he spends in carrying out the handover and takeover operation, provided that the allowance does not in any case exceed one month's salary. The value of this allowance shall be determined by a decision of the competent Minister, and shall be disbursed from the salaries item.

Family Allowance:

1- An employee shall be granted a family allowance for his spouse and his children, the value and conditions of which shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Board of the Civil Service Board, provided that his female children benefit from this allowance until their marriage and the males until they reach the age of majority or upon their completing the twenty-fifth year of their age in cases where they are pursuing their studies.

2- Retirees shall receive the family allowance allocated to active employees.

Compensation for overtime work:

1- Employees may be granted compensation for overtime working hours that exceed their official working hours, if the regulations applicable in their department require them to work continuously during and outside working hours.

2- They may also be granted this compensation if the Minister or the Director General assigns them in writing to perform overtime work, provided that the assignment takes place prior to commencing the work and that the overtime work does not fall within the duties entrusted to them by virtue of their position, and the Central Inspection Administration shall be notified with a copy of the assignment and its conditions and explanatory reasons.

However, it is permissible in exceptional cases to derogate from the condition stipulated above (which requires that the overtime work not fall within the duties entrusted to the employees by virtue of their position), when the work is urgent and must be performed outside official working hours by the competent employees themselves, provided that the assignment in this case takes place pursuant to the report of the competent inspector and after consulting the opinion of the Civil Service Board and obtaining the approval of the Council of Ministers.

3- The rate of compensation for each overtime hour shall be determined by a decision of the Minister within the appropriations allocated for this purpose in special items in the budget, in accordance with the instructions laid down by the Presidency of the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Board of the Civil Service Board.

4- Employees may be granted a lump-sum monthly compensation for overtime work assigned to them outside working hours, provided that the execution of such work requires a period of not less than six months, and that the compensation does not exceed half the salary, and that it is decided by a decree upon the proposal of the competent Minister, within the limits of the appropriations allocated in special items of the budget.

Granting or not granting compensation to an employee for overtime hours is left to the discretion of the administration in accordance with its discretionary power (Article 5 of Legislative Decree 7881 /1967).
