5 - A special allowance of 10% (ten per cent) shall be granted to technical employees who do not hold certificates of specialisation or completion of studies and who have been providing for at least five years actual service in one of the branches of aviation attached to the Directorate General of Civil Aviation.

The provisions of this paragraph shall not apply to specialist workers.

6 - The allowance indicated below shall be granted to permanent employees in the Ministry of Agriculture and the public institutions merged therewith, including the Executive Office of the Green Plan, who hold the Technical Agricultural Studies Certificate, the Secondary Agricultural Certificate, or the Forestry Certificate granted by a forestry or secondary school, or the equivalent of one of these certificates, and who are actually exercising their functions in the Ministry of Agriculture on the date of issuance of this Law:

- 20% (twenty per cent) for a person whose service in the permanent cadre has reached eight years or less.

- 30% (thirty per cent) for a person whose service in the permanent cadre has exceeded eight years.

7 - The allowance provided for in the preceding paragraphs shall not be counted as part of the basic salary.

Reorganisation of departments:

1- The Prime Minister shall appoint, upon the proposal of the President of the Civil Service Board, and the President of the Central Inspection Administration, a committee or committees tasked with conducting studies within the administrative unit designated by the competent ministry or the Board of the Civil Service Board or the Board of the Central Inspection Administration or the Council of Ministers, and this study shall cover the tasks entrusted to the administrative unit concerned on the one hand, and the number of employees necessary to perform these tasks and their academic and professional qualifications on the other hand with a view to determining the surplus posts.

2- The committee shall submit its report at the time determined by the Prime Minister. And the competent ministry or administration shall draw up, jointly with the Central Inspection Administration, within a period of one month from the date of its notification of the committee's report, a schedule of the names of a number of the unit's employees equal to the surplus number determined in the committee's report, and if it fails to do so, the President of the Central Inspection Administration shall immediately form a committee of at least three employees to prepare the required schedule within a period of two months at most. And the competent ministry or administration shall have the right to object to the schedule within a period of two weeks, whereupon the matter shall be submitted to the Council of Ministers to take the final decision.

3- If it appears that there are in the administrative unit a number of employees who do not possess the required qualifications to perform their duties, the provisions of Article (71) of this Legislative Decree shall apply to them.

4- The employees whose names are listed in the schedule referred to in paragraph (2) of this Article shall cease to exercise their duties. And they shall continue to receive their full salaries for a period of six months. And if they are not assigned during these six months to a vacant post for which they fulfil the conditions of appointment, with the exception of the two conditions of age and competitive examination, they shall be dismissed ipso jure from the service or referred to retirement at the end of the said period.

Dismissal by way of disciplinary removal:

1- An employee shall be removed by a decision of the Disciplinary Board if he commits a grave breach of one of his professional duties defined in the laws and regulations in force, and in particular in Articles (14) and (15) of this Legislative Decree.

2- The removed employee shall forfeit his right to dismissal compensation and to retirement, and he shall not forfeit his right to recover pension deductions unless the Disciplinary Board so decides in the removal decision.

3- It shall not be permissible under any circumstances to reinstate the removed employee into the service in any permanent or temporary post among the posts of the public administrations or public institutions or municipalities.

Assessment of Needs:

1- Every administration wishing to employ temporary employees shall draw up a statement of the number of temporary positions it needs, the salary of each of these positions, the statement of reasons for establishing them, and the draft regulations to which they must be subject.

2- These documents shall be referred to the Civil Service Board, where the Research and Guidance Administration shall study them and express its opinion thereon, seeking assistance, if necessary, from the Central Inspection Administration to conduct an investigation in the competent administration showing its actual needs for new employees and whether it is possible to meet these needs by transferring employees working in the same administration or in others, or by reorganising the department concerned, or by other means.

3- The Board of the Civil Service Board may take a decision on the request of the competent administration. If it approves it, the file shall be returned to this administration in order to prepare the subsequent legal measures. If it rejects it wholly or partially, its decision must be acted upon.

Request for Appropriations:

The appropriations necessary for the establishment of temporary positions shall not be requested in the annual budget or pursuant to special laws except after completion of the procedures and conditions set out in the preceding Article.

Establishment of Positions:

Temporary positions shall be established by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers within the limits of the appropriations allocated for this purpose, and within the number specified therein, and the regulations governing these positions, as approved by the Board of the Civil Service Board, shall be attached to the decree.

Appointment of Temporary Employees:

The Personnel Administration in the Civil Service Board shall draw up, by way of competition, examination, or other methods provided for in the regulations of temporary positions, a list of persons who fulfil the prescribed conditions of appointment. Those persons shall be appointed by decree.

Cases in Which Service Terminates:

The service of a temporary employee shall terminate in the cases provided for in the regulations to which he is subject and in all of the following cases:

1- Dismissal.

2- Expiry of the term or completion of the work for which he was appointed.

3- Reaching the statutory age.

4- Resignation.

5- Removal from office.

Dismissal:

A temporary employee may be dismissed by decree at any time whatsoever.

Expiry of the Term, or Completion of the Work, or Reaching the Statutory Age:

The service of a temporary employee shall terminate automatically on the day on which the term for which he was appointed expires on the day on which the work for which he was appointed is completed, or on the day on which he reaches the statutory age, and his salaries and allowances shall cease as from that date, even if no decree terminating his service has been issued.

Professional Incompetence

1- The Civil Service Council shall verify the professional competence of civil servants by a decision of its Board or at the request of the competent administrations or the Central Inspection Administration. This shall be done either through collective professional examinations organised by the Civil Servants Administration for civil servants of either the Fourth or Fifth Category who occupy similar posts, or through a personal investigation conducted by a committee composed of a delegate from the Central Inspection Administration, a delegate from the Civil Service Council, and a delegate from the administration to which the civil servant belongs, with a civil servant or a group of civil servants of whatever category they may be, and the committee shall be chaired by its highest-ranking member.

2- Every civil servant whom the examination or the investigation proves not to possess the basic knowledge indispensable for him to perform his post properly shall be dismissed from service or placed on retirement.

3- Dismissal from service or placement on retirement shall be decided by the authority vested with the power of appointment, upon the recommendation of the Civil Service Council, and if two months elapse from the recommendation of the Council and no decree or decision of dismissal or placement on retirement is issued, the Service Council shall have the right to decide that in its Board. Its decisions shall be deemed final in this matter, and the entitlements of the civil servants against whom the Board of the Council has taken a measure of dismissal from service or placement on retirement shall be liquidated in accordance with the laws and regulations in force.

Resignation:

The provisions applicable to a permanent employee shall apply to a temporary employee with respect to the submission of his resignation or the cases in which he is deemed to have resigned.

Dismissal:

A temporary employee shall be dismissed by decree following the approval of the Central Inspection Administration. The decree of dismissal shall not be issued until the temporary employee has been apprised of the charges brought against him and has been enabled to submit his written defence thereon within one week from the date of his being apprised thereof.

A licence to carry out industrial or commercial operations relating to equipment, weapons and ammunition of the first five categories and to explosives shall not be granted except after verification through the Ministry of National Defence that such premises fulfil all the technical conditions for preserving the safety of persons and neighbouring buildings.

The licence shall not be granted except to Lebanese who have attained the age of twenty-one years and after ascertaining their soundness from mental illnesses and that no judgment has been issued prohibiting them from carrying weapons or a judgment for offences affecting State security.

The Ministries of the Interior and of National Defence must be notified of every amendment or alteration occurring during the term of the licence to the articles of association of joint-stock or share-issuing companies or to their boards of directors, as well as upon the closure or transfer of the premises and upon every change in the manufacture of or trade in the equipment mentioned in the licence.

The licence shall be granted for a maximum period of five years, and it may be renewed for the same period at the request of the concerned parties.

Every licence under which the holder thereof has not commenced operations within one year shall become revoked ipso jure.

The licence shall be withdrawn immediately:

1 - From a person who loses one of the conditions provided for in Article 7.

2 - From premises that lose one of the conditions provided for in Article 6.

3 - From premises and persons proved to have lost one of the conditions provided for in Articles 13, 14, 15 and 16.

4 - From premises or persons proved to have contravened the provisions of the decrees taken in implementation of the provisions of this Legislative Decree.

The Ministry of the Interior or of National Defence may decide to withdraw the permit at any time whatsoever due to exceptional circumstances or for the requirements of public safety, and in such case raw materials, manufactured articles and machinery suitable only for the manufacture of weapons and ammunition shall be confiscated for the benefit of the Army in return for fair compensation determined by a committee of technicians appointed by the Ministry of National Defence composed of four members joined by an expert elected by the concerned party.

The decisions of this committee shall be subject to the avenues of recourse before the courts having competence over administrative matters.
By way of exception, foreigners may be granted licences to carry out purely commercial operations relating to equipment and weapons of the fifth, sixth and seventh categories.

The manufacture of equipment, weapons, ammunition and explosives of all categories shall be subject to the technical supervision of the Ministry of National Defence. Administrative supervision, however, shall fall within the competence of the Ministry of the Interior.

The supervision provided for in the preceding Article shall cover technical operations, including the installation, assembly and repair of parts pertaining to equipment, weapons and ammunition, and the verification of the degree of workmanship in manufacturing, and it shall also cover the operations of loading ammunition of all kinds.

This supervision shall be carried out in warehouses, factories and premises, and on every piece of equipment, weapons, ammunition and their separate parts the manufacture of which has been completed, and it shall also cover operations relating to the disposal or storage thereof, and for this purpose, business owners holding licences must keep, in addition to the regular commercial registers, legal registers in which they record the entry and exit of such weapons, the date, the name of the purchaser and the number of his licence.

Owners of industrial establishments dedicated to war equipment, weapons and ammunition must notify the Ministries of Interior and National Defence of the quantities the manufacture of which has been completed, within eight days from the date of completion of the work, and they must record in a special register all the equipment, weapons, ammunition and parts appertaining thereto that have been manufactured.

This register shall be subject to the supervision of the Ministries of Interior and National Defence, and they must also, within the same time limit, notify the two aforementioned Ministries of every invention or patent they have obtained for a new type, and of every improvement occurring to one of the types of their work, and every substantial modification in one of the models.

Every person who, by virtue of his office or mission, becomes acquainted with these inventions must keep their secrets under penalty of criminal prosecution pursuant to Article 579 of the Penal Code, while reserving the right to prosecute him in accordance with the other criminal provisions in force.

The importation, exportation and re-exportation of war equipment, weapons, ammunition and their separate parts, and all materials mentioned in the first four categories, shall be subject to a prior licence from the Ministry of National Economy after the approval of the Ministry of National Defence (Army Command) and the approval of the Council of Ministers.

As for hunting weapons and their ammunition, and the weapons and materials mentioned in the other five categories, they shall be subject to a prior licence from the Ministry of National Economy after the approval of the Ministry of Interior.

However, ammonium nitrate containing nitrogen in a proportion exceeding 33,50 % shall be subject to the prior licence provided for in the first paragraph of this Article.

The prior licence is the licence granted to importers before ordering their goods from abroad, that is, before contracting with the exporter.

The Government may, in time of war or when the outbreak thereof is anticipated, suspend for a specified period or strictly prohibit the granting of certificates for inventions relating to national defence. And which are used for the needs of the Army and defence and the creation, use or exploitation of which may constitute a danger to the safety of the State.

Every person who applies, in time of war or when the outbreak thereof is anticipated, for the registration of an invention of the kind mentioned in the preceding Article shall submit his application in two copies, one of which shall be referred together with the drawings, plans and descriptions of the invention to the Ministry of National Defence, and the said Ministry shall decide within one month from the date of its receipt of these documents whether the invention falls under the provisions of the preceding Article and shall determine the period of suspension of the granting of the certificate.

The inventor and any other person who has become acquainted with the invention in any manner whatsoever is prohibited from disclosing any information relating to the invention, and whoever discloses, communicates or publishes by one of the means mentioned in Article 209 of the Penal Code any information relating to the invention, prior to obtaining permission therefor, shall be prosecuted before the Military Courts pursuant to Article 281 of the General Penal Code.

The prohibition of the disclosure or exploitation of the invention, temporarily or permanently, confers a right to compensation upon the inventor and any other person having an interest. The amount of such compensation shall be determined by the Committee provided for in Article 11 of this Legislative Decree.

The Government shall have the right to exploit the ballot for its own account, and in such case, the inventor or the holder of the right to the invention shall be granted, in addition to the compensation referred to in the preceding Article, shares in the factory established to exploit the invention.

The shares and the amount of compensation for the party concerned shall be determined under the same conditions and circumstances referred to in the preceding Article.

All the provisions of this Chapter shall apply to Lebanese commercial and industrial companies, to their branches and to companies placed under the control of Lebanese nationals wherever they may be within or outside Lebanese territory.

Any person is prohibited from transporting or possessing the arms and ammunition provided for in the Fourth Category within Lebanese territory unless he holds a licence from the Army Command, and the Qaimaqam shall have the right to grant licences relating to hunting arms.

The licence to possess and transport arms of the Fifth Category is personal and is granted once and its validity shall not lapse except by death or by the loss by its holder of the conditions of eligibility provided for in this Legislative Decree.

As for the licence to possess and transport arms and ammunition of the Fourth Category, it shall be granted for one year and may be renewed.

The Forests Department shall issue an afforestation certificate to individuals, municipalities, and villages that have afforested their lands, after verifying such afforestation and its growth for one year by physical inspection.

The afforestation certificate shall include the name of the owner, the location of the land, its boundaries, its area, its contents, and the date of its afforestation.

The holder of an afforestation certificate may sell it to a person who applies for a permit to fell trees of the species specified therein. The afforestation certificate shall be valid for one time only, and its effect shall cease upon the granting of the felling permit requested pursuant thereto.

Any individual who owns barren land or neglected forest land shall commence the afforestation of such land within one year from the date on which the decision of the Minister of Agriculture in this regard is notified to him, and shall complete it within three years.

If the owner fails, within the period specified in the preceding Article, to carry out the required afforestation works, the State shall have the right: either to expropriate such land and sell it by public auction to third parties to afforest it in accordance with the provisions of the preceding Article.

Or to carry out its afforestation at its own expense and recover the expenses of afforestation and other expenses from the revenue of the afforested land by taking possession thereof for the period necessary to recover the value of these expenses.

The value of the expenses shall constitute a privileged debt due to the Treasury and shall be registered in the Land Register as a compulsory mortgage on the land to which it relates. The latter measure may be applied to communal properties.

Fines accruing to the State collected for forest offences, as well as fines collected for violating the provisions of agricultural laws and regulations, shall be paid on trust to the Treasury Fund in the name of the Ministry of Agriculture to be expended for general afforestation through the committee provided for in Article 89

The extraction and removal of stones, sand, mineral, soil, grass, heather, broom (genista), herbage, green or dry leaves, or natural fertilisers from forest land, or acorns, various seeds, other fruits, or forest products designated by the Forests Department, shall require a licence from it or from the owner of the forest.

If public works carried out on forest lands require the extraction of building materials or the felling of trees, the Ministry of Public Works shall designate to the Forests Department the places of extraction and felling prior to commencing the work.

The Forests Department shall, in agreement with the Ministry of Public Works, determine the conditions for extracting materials and felling trees while preserving the forest. The Forests Department shall, where necessary, determine the compensation that must be paid to the State for the occupation of the land and for the value of the extracted materials.

The use of equipment in which fire is used on roads passing through forests or within two hundred metres of their boundaries requires, during the period mentioned in the preceding Article, obtaining an authorization from the Forestry Service.

No one may burn thorns, grass, straw, and other standing vegetation except under a licence from the Forestry Service on lands located less than five hundred metres from forests from the first of July to 31 October, and less than two hundred metres from the first of November to 30 June, unless licensed otherwise.
The person who sets the fire shall in all cases be civilly liable for the damages caused by him to third parties, without any liability arising therefrom on the part of the State.

If a fire occurs in the forests, the representatives of the Forestry Service, security officers, and representatives of the administrative authority shall have the right to employ all persons, pack and draught animals, means of transport, and equipment required by the circumstances.
Grazing is prohibited for a period of ten years over the entire area of burned or felled forests.

In forests that are the property of the State or the property of municipalities and villages, no industrial establishment whatsoever that uses fire or requires the erection of a fuel depot may be established without a licence from the Forestry Service inside the forest or at less than five hundred metres therefrom.

In the forests specified in the preceding Article, no building whatsoever may be constructed, nor may any tent whatsoever covered with or composed of flammable materials be pitched therein, without a licence from the Forestry Service, inside the forest or at the least of two hundred metres from its boundaries.

If the lighting of an authorized fire, or the lighting thereof within the legal conditions, causes a fire in neighbouring properties, the person who set the fire shall be liable for all damages, unless such damages resulted from measures taken to protect a forest from fire.

It is prohibited to light fire and carry it outside dwellings and buildings prepared for exploitation within the boundaries of forests, and likewise outside these forests at less than two hundred metres from the aforementioned boundaries.

This prohibition shall apply from the first of July to 31 October, and it shall also apply to owners of private forests, and it shall also include the making of charcoal and the distillation of tar and resin and, in general, all industries requiring the use of fire, subject to the provisions of the following Articles 102, 103, 104 and 105.

Dwellings, exploitation buildings and stone-built shelters standing within forests or at a distance of two hundred metres therefrom in which fire is lit for family needs or industrial requirements must be, during the period ranging between the first of July and 31 October, surrounded by a clearing of land of a width of 25 metres from which every thorn or grass and every resinous tree shall be removed if the Forests Service deems it necessary, and this clearing must always be kept in good condition and no combustibles may be placed therein.

During the same period, the use of fire shall not be authorised in shelters, tents, encampments, workshops, factories and temporary installations standing in forests, whatever they may be, and in the two-hundred-metre zone except for cooking food, and the hearths must be surrounded by a clearing of 25 metres in accordance with the conditions laid down in the preceding Article.

The Forests Service may exceptionally authorise the use of fire during the aforementioned period for burning minerals in exploitation works located in forests or in the two-hundred-metre zone starting from these forests, provided that each hearth is surrounded by a clearing according to the conditions laid down above and of a width determined by the authorisation decision. The making of charcoal and tar during the same period shall be carried out within the conditions imposed by the Forests Service, and this Service may prohibit this work temporarily or permanently if it deems it necessary.

Concessionary railway or steam tramway companies whose lines cross forests or pass within two hundred metres of their boundaries must not leave in the places of the lines any grass or herbaceous plants between the date of the first of June and the first of November.

They must, moreover, establish along the sections of these lines trenches of a width of 20 metres on each side from which every thorn and, where necessary, every resinous tree shall be removed, and which shall always be kept in good condition, all of this at the expense and under the responsibility of the company.

The State shall bear no financial liability whatsoever on account of the partial or total destruction of a forest owned by individuals, municipalities, or villages following measures ordered to be taken by the administrative authority in the course of fighting a fire in order to guard against it.

The Forestry Service is charged with investigating contraventions committed against the provisions of this Law in forests belonging to the State, municipalities, villages, and individuals, and with instituting actions in respect thereof. Actions shall be instituted before the competent courts at the request of the officials of the Forestry Service, each within his district. The officials of the Forestry Service shall refer the official reports drawn up regarding the contraventions committed to the Justice of the Peace if the action falls within his jurisdiction, and to the Public Prosecution if it falls within the jurisdiction of another court. Duly authorised officials of the Forestry Service shall have the right to attend the trial to support the charge and to request judgment for the penalty and compensation.

The grower must obtain the seeds that he needs from the Monopoly Administration, and the latter is obliged to give him the selected seeds necessary for seedling cultivation at the lowest possible prices.

The Permanent Committee shall approve the tariff of these prices. The nurseries must be destroyed on 15 May at the latest on the coasts and 15 June in the mountains, meaning that the transplanting of seedlings must have been completed on these two dates.

As for the seedlings that remain in the nurseries after these two dates, they shall be deemed an unauthorised crop from the minute in which the length of the leaf reaches 20 centimetres.

The Monopoly Administration shall have the right, immediately upon the growers obtaining the licence, to inspect the cultivated lands, monitor their area, and destroy the nurseries whose owners have not observed the provisions of this Decision.

The growers must, from six o'clock in the morning to six o'clock in the evening during the period ranging between the first of October and 31 March, and from five o'clock in the morning to eight o'clock in the evening during the period ranging between the first of April and 30 September, lead the officials of the Monopoly to their plantations, facilitate for them the means of performing their duties, and allow them to enter upon the slightest request issued by them, whether into the drying sheds of leaf tobacco, its stores, its warehouses, the place of residence, and other parts of their house, or into the drying sheds, stores, and warehouses that belong to their sharecroppers. The latter must not obstruct these investigations, even if the aforementioned buildings are their private property or they are their tenants, the purpose of all that being to enable the officials to carry out the censuses, verifications, and inquiries necessary in the interest of the Monopoly.

The growers must also produce to the officials, upon the slightest request issued by them, concerning their nurseries, their crops, their drying sheds, and their stores, and concerning the names of the sharecroppers who share with them the cultivation of their tobacco, and concerning their surnames and their place of residence.

The grower must also produce to the officials of the Monopoly, upon the slightest request issued by them, the receipts for the declarations that they are obliged to submit in accordance with the provisions of this Decision.

When the seedlings have matured and before starting to harvest them, and in any case before 15 July on the coasts and 15 September in the mountains, every grower must submit a declaration called the "Crop Declaration", in which he estimates the weight of the dry leaves that he expects to obtain from his plantations.

This declaration must be submitted to the Mukhtar after the legal stamps have been affixed to it, in the same form in which the declaration provided for in Article Eight is submitted, with the exception of the third paragraph thereof.

After the submission of the declaration or after the expiry of the two maximum dates referred to in the preceding Article, the Monopoly Administration shall be entitled to undertake the assessment of the crop itself and shall immediately notify these assessments to the grower, so that if he does not accept them, the committee shall assess the crop definitively.

As for the expenses of this committee, they shall be borne by the party whose assessments diverge further than the assessments of the other party, whether by increase or decrease, from the assessments of the committee.

During the weighing, the assessments of the Monopoly - in the case of their acceptance, or the assessments of the committee, shall be taken as a basis for proving the deficit.

It shall be permissible to pick the leaves and transport them from the drying places into the village in which the tobacco was produced without restriction or condition, provided this takes place during the daytime only. Otherwise, transport shall not be permissible except pursuant to a licence from the Monopoly Administration and under the circumstances provided for in this Order.

The grower may not possess more than one drying house for all his plantations located in a single village, in addition to the drying apparatus located in the plantations themselves.

The officers of the Monopoly may enter the drying premises on a permanent basis.
Growers must uproot the seedlings and roots immediately upon picking the leaves, and at the latest immediately upon the expiry of a time limit fixed by the Monopoly Administration for the Mukhtar.

The tobacco must be placed in sacks ready for weighing immediately upon the completion of packing, and at the latest immediately upon the expiry of a time limit fixed by the Monopoly Administration for the Mukhtar.

In no manner whatsoever may the picked tobacco contain pieces of the stalk, flower tops, buds, or foreign substances.

An officer of the Monopoly Administration shall carry out the weighing in the presence of the Mukhtar or, in the event of his absence, in the presence of two members of the Council of Elders.

The cultivators may attend the weighing, but his failure to attend may not prevent the weighing from being deemed valid.

The sacks shall then be sealed with lead and numbered. If the ascertained weights are lower than the weights stated in the crop declaration by more than ten per cent, the cultivator shall send the necessary clarifications in writing to the Monopoly agency to which he belongs. The Monopoly Administration may accept these clarifications and not deem the shortfall a deficit; otherwise, the crop declaration - or where necessary - the result of the verification of this declaration, and the warehouse receipt, or, in the absence thereof, its corresponding counterfoil, shall be taken as the sole legal proof to establish the deficit.

Every unjustified deficit exceeding ten per cent shall be subject to the fines provided for in Chapter Six of this Resolution.

The cultivator shall remain liable for the quantities recorded in his name in the crop declaration or following the verification of the assessment until such quantities are weighed.

After the weighing of the tobacco, the competent officers shall have the right to search, under the conditions set forth in Article 14, the dwellings and premises of the cultivators and the buildings adjacent thereto to ascertain whether there is any concealed tobacco therein. Any tobacco found shall be deemed smuggled tobacco and the penalties provided for in this Resolution shall be imposed thereon.

If the crop is lost in whole or in part, the cultivator must notify the Monopoly agency of the matter within a period of 48 hours, whereupon the said agency shall summon him to attend the investigation conducted by the Mukhtar, a delegate of the Finance Administration, and a delegate of the Monopoly Administration; a record of the investigation shall then be drawn up, and the two delegates shall sign two copies thereof, each keeping one of them. Thereafter, the crop declaration shall be rectified in accordance with the contents of the record.

If it appears that the tobacco is affected by damage rendering it unfit for use, it must be burned, and the burning must be mentioned in the record and on the crop declaration.

If the cultivator claims that he was robbed, his claim may only be taken into consideration if proven by the results of the judicial investigation which the cultivator himself must request immediately upon the discovery of the theft.

No quantity whatsoever of tobacco may be deducted from the cultivator's account if he fails to perform all the formalities provided for in this Article.

The tobacco must be transported to the warehouse of the Monopoly under the supervision of the producers and at their expense immediately upon its weighing and before the expiry of the time limit fixed by the Monopoly Administration in each village.

The Monopoly Administration may itself undertake the transport of the tobacco after its weighing in accordance with a tariff approved by the Permanent Committee, and in such a case it must notify the Mukhtar thereof before the weighing, and the tobacco must be placed at its disposal at any time whatsoever.

The entire crop of the planter must be delivered to the warehouse of the Monopoly.

Upon delivery of the tobacco to the Monopoly Administration, the said Administration shall give to the planter or his representative, if he holds a power of attorney certified by the Mukhtar, a warehouse receipt detached from a counterfoil book. As for the counterfoil, it shall be signed by the planter or his representative.

There shall be stated in the receipt:

First- The quantities intended for sale to the Monopoly and the quantities intended for exportation.

Second - The marks and numbers of the bales.

The tobacco purchased by exporting merchants is intended exclusively for exportation.

Its use for internal consumption is therefore deemed to constitute contraband.

Exporting merchants must keep and submit to the Monopoly Administration at the slightest request made by it an inward and outward account in which shall be debited to them all the quantities which they have purchased and kept in the warehouse, and in which shall be credited to them the exported quantities in accordance with the customs declaration.

This account must be accompanied, where necessary, by all requisite supporting documents.

The quantities of tobacco purchased by exporting merchants must remain stored at their expense in the warehouses of the Monopoly Administration in accordance with the conditions observed under the storage regulations.

The crops intended for exportation must be exported in their entirety.

However, the Monopoly may purchase, by way of exception and after its agreement thereon with the Permanent Committee, a portion of these crops, in the event that the lands cultivated for its account have not produced sufficient quantities.

As for the purchase prices, they shall be the prices set forth in the tariff in force and fixed in accordance with the provisions of Article 29, with the addition thereto of the expenses of storage and insurance (sigorta).

After the drying of the leaves and before the weighing, the "Abou Riha" tobacco shall be transported to the place of fumigation. This transport is free within the village, but if the place of fumigation is situated outside the village, transport shall only be permitted after obtaining a licence from the Monopoly Administration and subject to compliance with the conditions which it shall lay down. Whatever the case may be, transport shall only be permitted during the daytime.

As for the places of fumigation, the officers of the Monopoly may enter them at any time whatsoever, subject to compliance with the conditions stipulated in Article 14.

(As amended by Legislative Decree No. 76 dated 27/6/1977, Official Gazette, Supplement to Issue 19):

Sellers must sell the manufactured products at the fixed prices without any increase or decrease, and a list of the prices must be posted in the shops and places licensed for the sale of tobacco manufactured products.

As for the sellers' commission, it is the discount granted to them out of the principal of their purchases.

The Monopoly Administration shall fix the rate of this discount according to the regions, the circumstances, and the types and varieties of the manufactured products offered for sale, following agreement with the Permanent Committee.

(As amended by Article 1 of Decision 97 dated 29 June 1937):

The Permanent Committee shall determine, upon the proposal of the Monopoly Administration, the types and varieties of the manufactured products offered for sale, and the prices at which they must be sold, and the High Commissioner shall then approve them pursuant to a decision.

The types of products offered for sale, their classification, their selling prices, and the designation of the places of sale with respect to the tobacco known as regional tobacco shall be decided by the Permanent Committee upon the proposal of the Monopoly Administration.

These resolutions shall be approved by a decision of the High Commissioner.

The breaking up of packets or boxes of tobacco or cigarettes for the purpose of retail sale is prohibited, and every tobacco seller is obliged to sell matches; as for the sale of other materials, it is permitted, but it must be ceased upon any request issued by the Monopoly Administration, if it becomes apparent that it prevents the preservation of the tobacco or its sale.

Every individual wishing to engage in the sale of tobacco in a specified shop, or wishing to sell it as an itinerant vendor, shall submit to the Monopoly Administration an application conforming to the model provided thereby. The Monopoly Administration shall not be obliged to state the reasons that may induce it to refuse to grant any of the licences or to refuse the renewal thereof.

An applicant whose application is accepted shall be delivered a sales licence. This licence shall be either annual or semi-annual. It shall be granted for each year or for each six months of the Gregorian year in return for the payment in cash of the amount of the annual fee or half thereof, according to whether the licence is annual or semi-annual.

The licence fee shall be fixed pursuant to a tariff determined in an order issued by the High Commissioner upon the proposal of the Permanent Control Committee.

The classification of sales shops in each State shall be carried out by the Monopoly Administration in agreement with the Head of the Finance Department therein. This classification may be reviewed every year.

Holders of a sales licence or permit must manage their shops in person.

The said licence or permit is a title that may neither be sold nor assigned, and the Monopoly Administration cannot recognise the sale of the licence or the assignment thereof; rather, in such a case, it shall deem it revoked, and reserves to itself the right to institute legal proceedings.

A tobacco sales shop may not be transferred to a place other than the place for which the licence or permit was granted, except after its owner obtains a special authorisation from the Monopoly Administration.

The licence may be immediately withdrawn from vendors who contravene these provisions, and they shall be prosecuted as engaging in the unlawful sale of tobacco.

Vendors may not possess, offer for sale, or sell tobacco except in boxes, wrappers, or packets to which Monopoly stamps are affixed.

Such vendors shall at all times possess sufficient quantities of all kinds and varieties of manufactured products required for local consumption. They shall purchase the manufactured products from the warehouse designated for them by the Monopoly Administration in their region and after paying the value thereof in cash.

Any borrowing or assignment of Monopoly manufactured products between vendors is prohibited.

Upon completion of the fumigation and the preparation works that follow it, and immediately upon the expiry of a time limit not exceeding a maximum of ten months after the date of picking, the "Abou Riha" tobacco shall be placed in sacks and weighed at its place of production by the Monopoly Administration, which the grower shall have notified prior thereto of his wish to weigh, and shall be transported to the warehouse of the Monopoly in accordance with the provisions of Articles 30, 31, 32, 33 and 34, provided that the "Abou Riha" tobacco may be mixed with the stalks in the bales.

The Monopoly Administration must pay the grower within fifteen days starting from the receipt at the warehouse or, where applicable, starting from the decision of the committee provided for in Article 27 of Resolution No. 16-L.R. issued on 30 January of the year 1935, or from the expiry of the period of six months provided for in the same Article.

The Monopoly Administration shall have the privilege to deduct in advance, from the value of the sums due to the grower, every sum due to it by way of reimbursement of actual expenses placed at the charge of the grower pursuant to the regulations provided for in Article 4, paragraph 3, of the book of specifications annexed to Resolution No. 16 L.R. issued on 30 January 1935. This privilege is special and ranks immediately before the special privilege pertaining to the Treasury.

As regards the recovery of the other debts of the Monopoly Administration, this Administration

shall also benefit from a privilege which shall be special if the matter relates to fines imposed upon the grower for his contravention of Title II of Resolution No. 16 L.R. issued on 30 January of the year 1935, and which shall apply to the price of the tobacco produced by the grower, and shall be general in all other cases.

The special or general privilege of the Monopoly referred to in the preceding paragraph shall rank immediately after the privilege of the Treasury of the same kind.
No person whomsoever may sell the products manufactured or imported by the Monopoly Administration unless he holds a licence or permit granted by it.

Every selling licence or permit issued by the Monopoly Administration shall be personal to a specified person whose name is mentioned thereon. It shall be granted for a specified period, and for the purpose of selling in a specified place.

However, the Monopoly Administration may license itinerant vendors to sell tobacco in towns and villages, and to sell it to nomadic tribes during their movement from place to place. As for the licence granted to them, it may be valid either in one region or in several regions, and either in one State or in all the States.

There shall be subject to the forestry regime across all territories of the States of the Levant under French Mandate, and managed in accordance with the provisions of this Decision and the regulatory texts issued hereafter regarding its enforcement, the lands containing forests, woods and thickets mentioned in the following list: 1- Lands in which the bare ownership and right of disposal belong to the State, or in which the State holds rights of co-ownership with legal persons, communities or individuals, as well as lands over which there is a dispute between the State and any of the categories of other owners or beneficiaries of the lands mentioned above 2- Lands in which the bare ownership is presumed to belong to the State pursuant to real property laws or custom and of which possession has been taken by the Administration. These lands shall remain subject to the forestry regime until the date of completion of the settlement of the dispute relating thereto and the demarcation of their boundaries in accordance with the real property laws in force 3- Properties belonging to the category of woods and forests called "Baltalik" (abandoned or communal wooded lands) 4- Lands belonging to public institutions or placed under the supervision of the Administration of Religious Endowments (Awqaf)

There shall also be subject to the forestry regime wooded lands, lands covered with thickets, or barren lands the afforestation or rehabilitation of which is deemed to be of public utility after completion of the legal formalities relating thereto.

Lands containing forests, woods and thickets in which the bare ownership belongs privately to administrative communities, in particular the private village forests situated in the territories of former Mount Lebanon (Petit Liban), shall be managed in accordance with the form prescribed in the special regulations enacted by the Director of Agriculture after hearing the statements of the representatives of those communities, and in the absence of representatives of such communities, after hearing the statements of the village committees

Lands containing woods, forests or thickets in which the bare ownership and right of disposal belong to individuals, and which are not the subject of any claim on the part of the State, shall be managed by their owners, who may freely exercise therein all rights arising from ownership, subject to compliance with the restrictions prescribed in this Decision
No authorisation may be granted to exempt any land of the State domain from being subject to the forestry regime or to sell the same save by virtue of a legislative text

The Forestry Department of the State is charged with ensuring the enforcement of the forestry regime upon the lands subject thereto and with studying and executing works for the protection or rehabilitation of forests in all other lands.

The technical officers of the Forestry Department of the State shall consist of inspectors, technical officers and forest guards who shall be appointed upon the proposal of the Forestry Administration, and whose number shall be sufficient to ensure the enforcement of the orders and regulations relating to forests throughout the lands subject thereto.
The Forestry Department shall be organised by decrees or local decisions.

Forest guards, of whatever grade they may be, are officers of the judicial police, and they shall wear, during the performance of their duties, a distinctive badge whose form shall be determined by the administration to which they belong.

Forest guards, of whatever grade they may be, shall, before assuming their duties, take the oath before the Court of First Instance at their place of residence and register their commission and the instrument of their taking of the oath with the registry of that same court, and if they change their place of residence they shall not be required to renew the taking of the oath.
Forests that belong to the domain of the State include the lands bearing forests, woods and thickets forming part of the private domain of the State.

The establishment of forests that belong to the domain of the State, as well as the purchase, sale or extinction of all real rights subsisting thereon, shall be subject to the provisions of the Real Property Law, in particular the real property texts relating to the private domain of the State.

In localities where the survey and demarcation of real properties provided for in Decision No. 186 of 15 March 1926 have not yet been commenced, the verification and demarcation of lands forming part of the private domain of the State and subject to the forestry regime, and of the adjacent properties, shall be carried out either upon the application of the Forestry Administration, or upon the application of the Domain Administration in agreement with the Forestry Administration, or upon the application of the adjacent owners.

These operations, and in general all administrative and judicial formalities relating thereto, shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of the Real Property Law in force at the time they are carried out, in particular the texts regulating the demarcation and administration of the private domain of the State.

All lands on which there are forests, woods and thickets and in which the State has a right of ownership or use shall be subject to demarcation and to the final determination of the rights provided for in the preceding Articles, and the sectors in which these operations take place shall be designated by decrees or local decisions.

All woods, forests and thickets standing on lands subject to the forestry regime shall be subject to an exploitation regulation the object of which is to ensure their exploitation, improvement and continuous afforestation at the same time.

The Forestry Department shall prepare this regulation and draw up an exploitation plan therefor to be approved by the authority to which this Department is subordinate. The felling of trees at ground level in State forests shall not be authorised except by way of derogation from this rule due to force majeure pursuant to decrees or local decisions.

Forest guards of all grades must each be in possession of a special instrument or hammer given to them by the Department to which they belong and used to place a mark on trees and firewood, and they may not part with it or allow it to be used by any person whomsoever.

The marks of the instruments or hammers, the form of which is determined by the Government, shall be placed by forestry officers on the firewood cut from the place of exploitation as well as on the stumps of the trees from which this firewood was cut, thus enabling by this method the examination of the legality of the felling operations. This mark must be deposited with the registry of the Court of First Instance of the place in which it is used.
Principal forest products or other products of State forests shall not be sold except by way of public auction, unless the exceptional provisions provided for in Article 22 apply.

In no case whatsoever may the periods of exploitation and payment relating to the exploitation of forests exceed five years, and upon the completion of the exploitation works, all fixed installations such as roads, canals and technical buildings erected for the exploitation or transport of firewood shall remain the property of the State without compensation.

However, sales by mutual agreement may be concluded in the cases restricted to the following: 1- If the total value of the products the sale of which is taking place does not exceed 200 Syrian pounds 2- If the matter relates to supplying what the administration needs or executing works for the account of the State 3- If the products could not or cannot be sold by public auction for a reason resulting from force majeure.

All disputes that may arise during the course of the auction proceedings, whether relating to the validity of such proceedings or to the solvency of the persons who submitted bids or of their sureties, shall be decided immediately and without recourse by the officer presiding over the auction session, after taking the opinion of the committee.

The persons mentioned below may not participate in the purchase, neither in person nor through other persons, neither directly nor indirectly, as a principal party, as a partner, or as a surety: 1- Officials and officers of the State, public departments, and municipalities 2- Relatives by blood or marriage up to the fourth degree of the officials and officers of the Forest Department in the district in which the sale takes place Every auction conducted in violation of these provisions shall be deemed null and void, without prejudice to each of the offenders paying an individual fine which may not exceed one quarter of the amount of the bid nor be less than one twelfth thereof.

Every secret partnership and every manoeuvre aimed at harming or disrupting the auction, or purchasing the produce at prices lower than the ordinary prices through an agreement to reduce bids, shall be punishable by a pecuniary penalty from 10 Lebano-Syrian pounds to 500 pounds and by imprisonment from two days to fifteen days, or by one of the two penalties only, without prejudice to an award of damages which the Administration may claim as compensation for the harm suffered by it, and to the mandatory cancellation of the auction therein if such auction has been completed.
The auction shall become final immediately after it is awarded by the president of the auction committee, and no overbid may be made thereafter under any circumstances.

Detailed matters relating to auction formalities, payment of the price and the security deposit or the provision of solvent sureties, performance of the conditions of sale, payment of the value of damages, restitutions, and pecuniary penalties incurred by the bidder, various liabilities, and in general the conditions for the execution and liquidation of exploitation operations, shall be governed by special provisions set forth in the book of conditions drawn up by the Forest Administration.

In State forests declared to be protected (1) free from usufructuary rights, the gathering of acorns, the grazing of swine, pasturage, and the collection of minor produce may be leased out by way of auction for a period of three consecutive years at most. The formalities prescribed in the Second Section of this Chapter for auctions relating to the felling of timber shall be observed in the leasing of such produce. The Administration is also authorised to lease out such produce by mutual agreement under the same conditions.

If the successful bidders or the lessees by mutual agreement fail to carry out, within the prescribed time limits and in accordance with the manner imposed in the book of conditions, the works mentioned therein for protection against fire, removing and arranging bundles of wormwood, clearing the felling sites of thorns, boxthorn and harmful shrubs, repairing the roads designated for unloading the produce, the ditches and the fencing, and enabling the transport of loaded firewood designated for burning, such works shall be carried out at their expense through the care of the Forests Administration, which shall draw up the account of such expenses, whereas the recovery of such expenses shall be pursued in accordance with the provisions of the texts applicable to the collection of public funds.

Successful bidders or lessees by mutual agreement shall be criminally liable, from the day they are granted the exploitation permit until the day of their final discharge, for all misdemeanours provided for in this Resolution that are committed within the boundaries of their concession; provided, however, that they may divest themselves of such liability by giving notice of the occurrence of the misdemeanour before it is inspected by the officers of the Forests Department, and they shall also be liable in all cases for fines, restitutions, civil damages and costs if the perpetrator of such misdemeanours is their woodcutters, their workmen, the drivers of their vehicles and, in general, any person in their service employed in any capacity whatsoever in the felling works.

Successful bidders or lessees by mutual agreement shall not touch any of the reserved trees (RESERVES) situated on the land leased to them, nor substitute them for unreserved trees that they have left uncut. Every contravention of these provisions shall be punishable by a pecuniary penalty equivalent, for each tree felled or mutilated contrary to the law, to exempting the penalties provided for in Title Four, Chapter One of this Decision, all without prejudice to claiming damages calculated on the value of the tree on the date of its felling, to which value shall be added its future value; provided that if it is possible to bring the reserved trees felled contrary to the preceding provisions, these trees shall be restituted in kind if the Administration so requests, and in this case their value shall be deducted from the amount of damages.

There shall be stated in the minutes of auctions, the general and special books of conditions, and the decisions of leasing by mutual agreement the following: 1- The manner of felling trees, barking them, and charring firewood 2- The conditions for using stamps and hammers 3- The time limits for exploitation, clearance, and cleaning 4- The manner of establishing workshops, shelters, warehouses, and charcoal kilns 5- The conditions for using fire 6- The tracks authorised for use to transport produce 7- The daily duration of work in the "workshops" 8- The manner of removing the various produce, the conditions for the passage of herds, and in general all the conditions relating to the execution of the lease. Every contravention of these clauses and conditions shall be punishable by a pecuniary penalty of 5 to 500 L.S.P., and this shall not preclude, where applicable, claiming damages. The preceding provisions shall also apply to bidders and lessees by mutual agreement of various produce. As security for the execution of the clauses and provisions of the book of conditions, the Administration shall have a privilege over the produce of the felling that is still standing on its stems or deposited in the forest, and it may effect such attachments as it deems necessary to secure the payment of the pecuniary penalty and the damages imposed.

If the exploitation is not executed or the produce is not cleared within the time limits set in the legally determined agreement, where applicable, the produce standing on its stems or remaining at the place of felling shall be attached, and the court shall rule to confiscate it in favour of the State; and in any event, the time limits for clearing the produce together with the time limits of renewals may not exceed a period of five years.

Persons to whom the auction is awarded or who lease by mutual agreement may not bring into the places leased to them a number of animals exceeding the number specified for them in the book of conditions, and a distinguishing mark must be placed on all their animals.

If the animals of tenants of this kind are found outside the roads and places designated for them, or if their number is in excess of the specified number, or if they are not bearing their compulsory distinguishing marks, their owners shall be subject to the penalties provided for in Article 105 of this Decision.

The local Government may authorise the leasing of fallow lands and vacant spots located in the forests of State domain for a period not exceeding 15 years, provided that it is renewable, and it may also lease hunting lands under the same conditions. This leasing shall take place either by public auction or by mutual agreement, and in every case a book of conditions shall be drawn up and royalties shall be paid therefor.

After the bidding or the leasing by mutual agreement, no alteration whatsoever may be made to the location of the cutting sections (Coupe), nor may a single tree or a single product of forest products of any kind whatsoever be added to the trees or products covered by the lease; otherwise, a pecuniary penalty equal to double the value of the firewood or forest products not included in the lease which he took in excess shall be imposed upon the successful bidder or the tenant, without prejudice to the restitution of such products or the restitution of their value if they have been removed from their place. Forest officers who authorise or tolerate the addition of anything to the leased property shall be subject to the same pecuniary penalty, without prejudice to the criminal prosecutions that may be brought against them.

Successful bidders or tenants of tree-felling may not begin their exploitation before obtaining in writing from the Forest Administration an exploitation licence, which shall only be granted after payment of the full royalties due to the State, and they may not remove the products of their exploitation except after obtaining a written authorisation from the officer delegated by the said Administration, granted by him pursuant to the exploitation licence. Any exploitation begun in contravention of the provisions of this Decision shall be punishable by the penalties provided for in Title Four, Chapter One, relating to forest misdemeanours.

Special committees shall undertake the assessment of the annual profit subject to tax and shall be composed in each Governorate of:

- The Head of Finance of the Governorate or the Head of the competent tax department or whoever deputises for each of them --- as Chairman.

- A Category Three employee from the competent tax unit --- as Member.

- A delegate from the Ministry of Economy and Trade chosen by the Minister of Economy and Trade --- as Member.

- A delegate from the Chamber of Commerce and Industry in the Governorate proposed by the President of the said Chamber or one of the members of the Governorate Administrative Council where there is no Chamber of Commerce chosen by the Governor --- as Member.

- An employee from the Ministry of Finance, Income Tax Department, or in the competent financial unit or department in the Governorate --- as Member.

- The competent income tax controller --- as Rapporteur.

These committees shall be appointed by a decision of the Minister of Finance upon the proposal of the Director General of Finance, and shall meet upon the convocation of their Chairman and take their decisions by a majority; if the votes are equal, the Chairman shall have a casting vote.

Each of the Chairman and members of the committees for determining the assessed profit shall be granted a lump-sum allowance for each session held by the committee, determined as follows:

For the Chairman: 33,500 L.L. Thirty-three thousand five hundred pounds.

For the Member: 26,750 L.L. Twenty-six thousand seven hundred and fifty pounds.

For the Rapporteur: 13,350 L.L. Thirteen thousand three hundred and fifty pounds.

Provided that this allowance shall not be granted unless the work of the committee is carried out outside official working hours at a rate of eight sessions per month.

In order to assess the net profit, the committee shall avail itself of all information gathered on the taxpayer, and it may rely on the external signs of his standard of living, and hear him if it sees a need to do so.

The committee shall draw up certified nominal lists of the assessed profits which shall be taken as a basis for the imposition of the tax.

The effect of the assessment shall remain in force for a period of three consecutive years. The assessments of the committee may, pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Finance, be reviewed if compelling economic reasons arise.

The taxpayer shall himself calculate the tax assessment on real and lump-sum profits in accordance with the provisions of the laws in force, pay it to the Treasury, and declare it within the legal time limit, without the need to issue basic assessment rolls therefor.

If it appears to it, upon auditing the accuracy of the declaration, that there is reason to amend it, it shall notify the taxpayer of the amount of this amendment and the reasons therefor, together with the notice of additional tax or surcharge, by registered letter with acknowledgment of receipt.

Taxpayers not subject to the method of assessment on the basis of actual profit or on the basis of estimated profit must submit to the financial offices before the first of February of each year a declaration of their total gross receipts realised during the preceding year.

By the gross receipts required to be declared for assessment on the basis of lump-sum profit is meant the receipts of the taxpayer derived from all transactions of various kinds carried out by him effectively and finally during the year preceding the year of assessment, and in particular the total of what the taxpayer collected as the price of goods, commodities, tools or supplies sold by him, and as consideration for what he leased thereof, as well as what he collected in respect of commission, brokerage, royalties, interest resulting directly from commercial transactions, exchange differences, or fees, etc...

As for the revenues originally subject to another schedular income tax (bank interest, loan interest, revenues of built properties.. etc.), they remain subject to their own schedular tax and shall be deducted in full from the gross receipts subject to the tax of Title I together with the corresponding charges directly related to the said revenues.

The total gross receipts to be taken as a basis for determining the lump-sum net profit shall be extracted from the journal provided for in the Code of Commerce, in respect of taxpayers obliged to keep commercial books, or from the register provided for in the following Article 20 in respect of taxpayers practising non-commercial and non-industrial professions.

Every taxpayer practising a non-commercial and non-industrial profession must keep the daily register provided for in the Code of Commerce and record therein his daily gross receipts provided for in the preceding Article 18.

As for members of professions obliged to preserve professional secrecy, they are entitled to content themselves with recording the details of the amounts received and alongside them the date of their receipt without mentioning the names of the payers.

The registries of the competent courts shall initial and number the registers of all taxpayers subject to the tax on commercial and industrial profits regardless of the method of assessment to which they are subject, and the notaries public shall number and initial the registers of the remaining taxpayers.
A committee headquartered at the Ministry of Finance shall determine the rates to be applied to the total gross receipts in order to determine the lump-sum net profit.

The Committee referred to in the preceding Article shall be composed of:

- The Director General of Finance or his representative --- Chairman

- A delegate from the Ministry of National Economy selected by the Minister of National Economy.

- A delegate from the Chamber of Commerce and Industry from among the members of Beirut proposed by the President of the said Chamber.

- An expert representing, as the case may require, traders, industrialists or persons engaged in non-commercial professions, selected by the Minister of Finance.

- An employee of the Ministry of Finance (Income Tax Department) --- Rapporteur

This Committee shall be appointed by a decision of the Minister of Finance and shall meet at the invitation of its Chairman and take its decisions by a majority, and in the event of a tie vote, the Chairman shall have a casting vote.

The Committee shall fix for each type of trade, industry, profession or business an average annual rate. These rates shall be recorded in a general schedule approved by a decision of the Minister of Finance and published in the Official Gazette.

The professions for which the Committee may review the fixed rates shall be designated each year by a decision of the Minister of Finance.

As for the other professions, their rates shall remain in force.

The tax shall be imposed on taxpayers not subject to the actual or lump-sum assessment method on the basis of estimated profit.

Courts and judicial bodies of all kinds shall appoint experts, bankruptcy trustees and preventive composition supervisors from among the persons registered on a special roster drawn up by the Supreme Judicial Council, in which their number is determined, approved by the Minister of Justice and published in the Official Gazette.

When drawing up the roster of experts, the Supreme Judicial Council shall be joined by a representative of the Bureau of the State Council delegated by the President of the Council.

The Military Court may appoint experts from a list drawn up by the Commander of the Army and approved by the Minister of Defense.

An expert is a natural or legal person possessing technical skill and specialization who is commissioned to perform expertise work in accordance with the rules and procedures specified in the Code of Civil Procedure.

Every person applying for registration on the roster of experts must meet the following conditions:

1 - Be a Lebanese national for more than ten years, and have completed the twenty-fifth year of his age.

2 - Enjoy his civil rights and not have been convicted of a felony or of any of the disgraceful misdemeanors provided for in the Civil Servants Law.

3 - Not be a public official or an employee in a public service.

4 - Possess specialization, knowledge, impartiality and integrity.

5 - Be free from diseases and infirmities that prevent him from performing expertise work, and be of good conduct.

The applicant shall attach to his application:

1 - A copy of his judicial record.

2 - A certified copy of the academic or technical certificates proving his qualifications.

In branches that do not necessarily require academic certificates, it may suffice to submit a certificate proving the applicant's registration on the roster of experts for at least ten years, or his practice of work in the required branch for fifteen years.

Where necessary, the academic or technical conditions required for any type of expertise may be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice after consulting the Supreme Judicial Council, constituted in the manner set forth in the first Article of this Legislative Decree.

3 - A copy of an individual civil status extract.

An expert shall be entitled to a fee assessed by the court or judicial body that appointed him on the basis of the work he performed, the difficulty and importance of the mission entrusted to him, the time taken to execute it and the result reached by him. The decision determining the fee must be reasoned.

In addition to his fee, the expert shall be entitled to the necessary expenses required for the execution of the mission.

No account shall be taken of expenses paid to a person who assisted him in performing work that he ought to have performed himself, unless the execution of the mission required technical information not available in the person of the expert, provided that such assistance is preceded by authorization from the court.

If the taxpayer ceases his business, the tax shall be imposed on his industrial, commercial, and non-commercial profits that have not yet been assessed. The assessment shall cover the actual or lump-sum profit realised during the period ranging between the last day of the period covered by the previous assessment and the day on which the taxpayer ceased business.

As for the estimated profit, the tax shall be imposed on the profit calculated in proportion to the period of work of the year during which the cessation occurred. The taxpayer who has discontinued business, subject to the method of actual or lump-sum assessment, must submit a declaration thereof to the financial offices within one month from the date of cessation of business and attach to the declaration all the information and documents necessary to determine the taxable profit.

However, if the taxpayer practices another business, or owns an establishment other than the one he sold or assigned in the course of the year, he must notify the financial offices thereof within one month from the date of branching or sale, and record in his general annual declaration the result of the operations of the establishment in which he ceased business.

In all cases, it shall be incumbent upon all categories of taxpayers to state the buyer's name, surname, and address. The provisions of this Article shall apply to judicial appointees and bankruptcy trustees when bankruptcy occurs. Thereupon, the time limit for the declaration shall commence from the date of issuance of the decision appointing them.

The bankruptcy trustee shall deposit all sums he collects on behalf of the bankruptcy within a period not exceeding three days from the date of their collection in one of the approved banks and in a special account in the name of the bankruptcy.

The withdrawal of any sum from this account shall be effected by the joint, and not separate, signatures of the supervising judge and the bankruptcy trustee.

Any delay in depositing the collected funds exposes the bankruptcy trustee to disciplinary prosecution - and obligates him to pay to the bankruptcy default interest equivalent to the legal interest due for the period of the delay.

The bankruptcy trustee shall have the right to retain from the funds of the bankruptcy in a special cash box held by him a sum not exceeding the sum fixed by the court to cover small daily petty expenses.
All registers specified in Article 17 shall be placed at the disposal of the judge supervising the bankruptcy to enable him to exercise his permanent supervision over them.

Bankruptcy trustees shall submit to the judge supervising the bankruptcy, without any request from him, an annual statement of account at the end of every year regarding its accounts opened with the banks.

Bankruptcy trustees are prohibited from paying the decided distributions, the fees of experts, or any sum due by the bankruptcy prior to obtaining the approval of the supervising judge.

This payment must take place by means of bank cheques drawn on the account of the bankruptcy and signed by the supervising judge and the bankruptcy trustee. Cash payment is permitted only for daily petty disbursements out of the funds of the cash box kept with the bankruptcy trustee in accordance with the text of Article 19 of this Legislative Decree.

The bankruptcy trustee shall submit, in addition to the reports provided for by the Code of Commerce, a comprehensive report on the state of the bankruptcy whenever the President of the court or the supervising judge requests him to do so.

The bankruptcy trustee may, in the state of union, proceed with the sale of the immovable property of the bankrupt by mutual agreement after obtaining the approval of the supervising judge and the court, exceptionally and subject to the fulfilment of the following conditions:

- That attempts to sell by public auction have failed two consecutive times.

- That the body of creditors has an interest therein.

- That the appraisal of the price of the property sold is carried out by at least two experts.
The court shall notify the final decision ordering dismissal to the Supreme Judicial Council, which may take the appropriate measures against the dismissed trustee or supervisor.
Decisions pertaining to the appointment or dismissal of bankruptcy trustees or supervisors shall not be subject to any avenue of recourse.

Experts whose assistance is required by the administration of the bankruptcy or the supervision operations shall be appointed by the supervising judge after obtaining the opinion of the supervisors or the trustees.

Any person applying for registration on the roll of bankruptcy trustees and preventive composition supervisors must meet the following conditions:

1 - Be a Lebanese national for more than ten years and have completed thirty years of age.

2 - Enjoy his civil rights and not have been convicted of a felony or of an infamous misdemeanour provided for in the Civil Servants Law.

3 - Not be a public official or an employee in a public service.

4 - Hold a university degree from a recognised institute or have practised for a period of ten years the profession of bankruptcy trustee or expert in accounting before the courts.

5 - Be free from diseases and infirmities that prevent him from performing expertise work, and be of good conduct.

6 - Provide a financial or bank guarantee determined by a decision issued by the Ministers of Justice and Finance. The applicant shall submit with his petition the documents proving the fulfilment of the preceding conditions.

Every bankruptcy trustee and preventive composition supervisor shall keep:

1 - A daily register in which he records day by day the transactions and operations pertaining to bankruptcies and preventive compositions, receipts and payments, incoming and outgoing commercial papers, and funds deposited or falling due.

2 - A detailed register containing the account of each bankruptcy and each preventive composition separately, to which everything entered in the daily register is transferred day by day. This register and the register mentioned in the preceding paragraph must be initialled by the president of the court that appointed the trustee or the supervisor.

3 - A counterfoil book with serial numbers for receipt vouchers, and the numbers of the said vouchers must be transferred to the daily register alongside the receipts.

4 - A register of commercial instruments in which he enters every day the commercial papers that he finds among the debtor's assets or that are subsequently delivered to him on account of these assets.

The bankruptcy trustee and the supervisor of the preventive composition are two remunerated agents appointed by the judiciary, the first to receive and administer the property of the person whose bankruptcy has been declared, and the second to supervise the administration of the commercial enterprise whose owner has requested a preventive composition, to verify the debts owed to and by it, to conduct an investigation into the manner in which the debtor acts, and to submit a report to the assembly of creditors convened to decide upon the matter of the preventive composition.
