The provisions of this item shall apply to employees of the Foreign Service while exercising their duties in the central administration of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and to those among them seconded to work in the central administration, and to employees of the administrative cadre at the Lebanese University, and to employees of the temporary cadre of the Green Plan Execution Office.

2 - The salary scales of employees of the Foreign Service working abroad shall be converted in accordance with what is shown in Tables Nos. 14, 15 and 16 annexed to this Law, and each of them shall be allocated the new salary corresponding to his old salary and the new step corresponding to his old step, while retaining his right to the seniority qualifying for step advancement, without modification in rank.

The salaries of employees of the Foreign Service determined pursuant to this paragraph shall be subject to multiplication in accordance with the provisions governing the expatriation allowance, and shall not be subject to the provisions relating to the exchange difference. For the calculation of the salaries of employees of the Foreign Service on the date of entry into force of this Law, the following currencies shall be adopted:

- The United States Dollar.

- The Pound Sterling.

- The Deutsche Mark.

- The Swiss Franc.

- The Japanese Yen.

Each currency shall constitute 20% of the value of the converted salary on the date of conversion, and the Euro currency may also be adopted as an alternative index to the currencies that fall under the banner of the Euro currency and at the same weighting rates pertaining thereto.

3 - The salary scale of members of the teaching staff at the Lebanese University shall be converted in accordance with what is shown in Table No. 17 annexed to this Law and each of the members of the teaching staff concerned shall be allocated the new salary corresponding to his old salary and the new step corresponding to his old step, while retaining his right to the seniority qualifying for step advancement, without modification in rank.

Any excess of the current monthly income of each of the employees concerned by this Law over the salary allocated to him pursuant to the First Article shall be deemed a liquidation allowance, the value and conditions of entitlement of which shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance after seeking the opinion of the Civil Service Board.

First - With the exception of allowances for overtime work, bonuses, the family allowance, the temporary transport allowance, the transport and travel allowance, the housing allowance, the acting allowance, the allowances of councils, bodies and committees that meet outside official working hours, the allowances for night hours, the expatriation allowance allocated to employees of the Foreign Service, the allowances of committees and proctors of recruitment competitions and official examinations and the correction of papers pertaining thereto, the allowance in return for carrying out research, inquiries and investigations in accordance with the provisions of Article 43 of Law No. 75/67 dated 26/12/1967 (Organisation of the Lebanese University), productivity bonuses and collection proceeds, shares of fines, and fees for services rendered allocated to employees of the Customs Administration, all allowances, increments, bonuses, and salary accessories and supplements, whatever their type, designation, form or nature, from which the employees concerned by the provisions of this Law benefit, are repealed, as are repealed the exceptional step provided for under Article 18 of Law No. 9/78 dated 21/2/1978 amended by Article 18 of Law No. 21/79 dated 26/12/1979. And all decisions issued by the President of the Lebanese University relating to the creation of allowances or their amendment or the determination of their value or rates, whatever their designation.

New Projects Section This Section shall assume the following primary duties:

- Expressing opinions on terms of reference of all kinds, including equipping projects

- Studying and comparing tenders relating to equipping projects and determining the best tender

- Remaining permanently and continuously informed of the prevailing market prices for various equipment, installations and labour

Contractors Classification Section This Section shall assume the following primary duties:

- Preparing permanent lists of contractors, suppliers and consultants for the various projects and contract awards of the Institution

- Submitting proposals to regulate these lists, including striking off or adding certain names in the light of the contents of the classification files

- Preparing the transactions for qualifying suppliers and contractors for equipping projects, whether prior Pre qualification or subsequent Post qualification

Directorate of Financial Affairs This Directorate shall consist of:

- The Financial Service

- The Accounting Service

- The Stores Service

- The Collection and Cash Offices Audit Service

The Director of Financial Affairs shall assume the duties of Accountant of the Institution

Financial Service This Service shall consist of:

- The Budget and Expenditure Control Section

- The Salaries and Wages Section

- The Procurement, Contracts and Expenditure Liquidation Section

- The Revenue Assessment Section

- The Loans and Treasury Advances Section

Budget and Expenditure Control Department:

This Department shall undertake the following basic duties:

- Receiving statements of projected expenditures and revenues from all units of the Establishment.

- Compiling the elements necessary for drawing up the draft budget.

- Preparing the draft budget in both its first and second parts in a preliminary form in accordance with the Financial Regulations of the Establishment, and studying it with the Directors, the Heads of Units, and the Director General of the Establishment.

- Drawing up the explanatory memorandum of the budget, attaching it to the preliminary draft, referring it to the Directorate General, and following up on the provision of the information requested during its examination by the Board of Directors.

- Making the amendments decided by the Board of Directors, placing the draft budget in final form, and sending it for approval by the competent authorities.

- Following up on its examination with these authorities, providing them with all clarifications, and ensuring the correspondences and follow-ups until the required approvals are obtained.

- Placing the budget in its final form after its adoption and taking the necessary measures to notify it to whom it may concern.

- Closing the budget account and carrying forward unused appropriations.

- The duties of controlling the commitment of expenditures of all kinds, comprising the following:

= Controlling the availability of appropriations for expenditures, the correctness of their imputation, and the conformity of transactions with the laws and regulations in force.

= Controlling transactions relating to salaries, wages, and their accessories.

= Controlling transactions relating to all operating expenditures (Part One of the budget) and all equipment and construction expenditures (Part Two of the budget).

= Recording appropriation reservation transactions and entering all stages, decisions, annotations, and results.

Salaries and Wages Department.

This Department shall undertake the following basic duties:

- Preparing payment documents for salaries, wages, and their accessories of all kinds.

- Preparing collection documents for deductions of all kinds.

- Liquidating end-of-service indemnities in the Establishment and in the Social Security.

- Liquidating family allowances.

- Receiving supporting documents for allowances and indemnities of all kinds together with attendance sheets, auditing them, and sending them to the Informatics Centre for processing and issuing their results.

Section of Liquidation of Transactions, Contracts and Expenditures. This Section shall undertake the following basic duties:

- Receiving copies of order slips and letters and of contracts.

- Receiving the supporting documents for liquidation, such as invoices and delivery minutes.

- Receiving requests for advances pertaining to petty cash expenditures.

- Auditing and liquidating these documents and preparing payment orders, cheques and letters for opening documentary credits.

- Preserving and classifying these documents.

Section of Assessment of Revenues.

This Section shall undertake the following basic duties:

- Receiving the schedules relating to power invoices from the Directorate of Studies (Section of Informatics)

- Issuing accounting documents.

- Receiving daily receipt documents pertaining to power invoices, keeping a register thereof, and showing the balances of uncollected invoices.

- Issuing invoices outside the ordinary issue.

- Issuing works invoices on the basis of statements from the competent Directorates and keeping the accounts thereof.

- Keeping the accounts of municipal revenues and paying the fees to the competent municipalities.

- Issuing receipt orders relating to miscellaneous revenues.

Section of Loans and Treasury Advances.

This Section shall undertake the following basic duties:

- Keeping the accounts of internal and external loans, Treasury advances and bonds.

- Preparing quarterly and annual reports on the status of loans, maturities and repayment.

- Handling correspondence with the sources of loans and advances.

- Following up the application of the conditions mentioned in loans, advances and treaties of a financial nature and ensuring their execution.

Department of Accounting.

This Department shall consist of:

- Section of General Accounting.

- Section of Analytical Accounting.

- Section of Economic Studies and Statistics.

Section of General Accounting.

This Section shall undertake the following basic duties:

- Receiving all receipt and payment orders and accounting documents and auditing them.

- Sending them to the Department of Statistics and Informatics in the Directorate of Studies in order to extract the journal, the ledger and the trial balance.

- Internal auditing of the accounts.

- Preparing the general balance sheet and the income statement.

- Preparing the report of the Accountant of the Establishment in accordance with the regulations in force.

Analytical Accounting Section.

This Section shall undertake the following basic tasks:

- Industrial accounting works, which comprise:

- Analysing expenditure elements in order to ascertain the partial cost at each of the stages of production, transmission and distribution, and the total cost.

- The cost of works for the account of third parties.

- The operating result of the distribution sections.

- Materials accounting, which comprises:

- Receiving entry, exit, return and transfer vouchers (stores movement)

- Auditing them and sending them to the Directorate of Studies (Informatics) in order to extract the results.

- Comparing the accounting results with the stores records (the Kardex) and addressing discrepancies should they exist.

Economic Studies and Statistics Section.

This Section shall undertake the following basic tasks:

- Compiling statistical information from the concerned units in the Establishment, including the elements of analytical accounting.

- Following up on economic data in Lebanon and abroad represented by the evolution of currencies, raw material prices, inflation indicators and others.

- Establishing, amending and developing all tariffs for the sale and purchase of energy at the various voltage levels in light of the available information and data.

- Preparing economic studies on financial investments.

- Preparing periodic reports containing statistics and general economic analyses that may have an impact on the financial position of the Establishment.

Stores Department.

This Department shall consist of:

- Storage Systems Section.

- Materials Storage Section.

Storage Systems Section.

This Section shall undertake the following basic tasks:

- Establishing storage designs and rules for the delivery of goods in all the stores of the Establishment.

- Setting storage levels for the various types of goods and establishing the procedures for notifying when the minimum level is reached in order to initiate purchasing operations.

- Auditing the quantities of unused materials regularly, addressing the accumulation of surplus and scrap materials, and proposing the sale thereof.

- Establishing rules and plans for supplying the regional stores from the main store and among themselves.

The term of office of the municipal councils, mukhtars and ikhtiyariyah councils elected in accordance with the provisions of the two articles referred to above shall expire upon the expiry of the term of office of the general municipal councils, mukhtars and ikhtiyariyah councils elected in the Governorates of South Lebanon and Nabatieh on 7/6/1998.

1 - The members of the Municipal Council shall be elected by direct universal suffrage in accordance with the procedures provided for in the Law on the Election of Members of the Chamber of Deputies and in this Law.

2 - The municipality shall constitute a single electoral constituency.

3 - The Municipal Council shall elect from among its members a President and a Vice-President by secret ballot and by an absolute majority for the term of office of the Municipal Council, at the first sitting it holds at the date and place determined by the Governor or the Qaimaqam within a period of one month from the date of the announcement of the election result. The oldest member by age shall preside over the sitting. In the event of an equality of votes between two members, the older by age shall win, and if they are of the same age, recourse shall be had to drawing lots.

4 - The President and Vice-President of the municipality shall be considered members of the Municipal Council and included within the number specified in each municipality.

5 - The Municipal Council may, after three years from the election of the President and the Vice-President and at the first sitting it holds, withdraw confidence from both or either of them by an absolute majority of the total of its members, pursuant to a petition signed by one quarter of those members. The Municipal Council shall, in this case, immediately hold a sitting to fill the vacant position.

The presidency or membership of the Municipal Council may not be combined with:

1 - Membership of the Chamber of Deputies or the holding of a ministerial post.

2 - The office of Mukhtar or membership of the Ikhtiyari Council.

3 - The judiciary.

4 - Functions of the State, autonomous services, public institutions, and municipalities.

5 - The presidency or membership of the boards of directors of autonomous services and public institutions.

6 - The ownership of a concession or its functions within the jurisdiction of the municipality.

7 - The membership or functions of bodies or committees entrusted with managing projects of public utility within the jurisdiction of the municipality. The President of the municipality and the Vice-President may not stand as candidates for parliamentary elections until two years have elapsed from the end of their term of office or their resignation. This Article shall apply to Municipal Councils elected after the entry into force of this Law.

Each of the officials referred to in Article 60 shall enjoy, in so far as upon establishing infringements of the provisions of this Legislative Decree, the capacity of an officer of the judicial police.

The said officials must establish the infringements committed by means of official reports which they shall sign, and they shall request the person responsible for the infringement or any of his employees with whom the investigation was conducted to sign them without insistence; and if he refuses to sign, that shall be recorded on the report.

The refusal to sign shall have no effect on the probative force of the official report.

The head of the competent finance department shall undertake, after auditing the official report, to impose the fine and notify it to the offender in person or through whichever of his employees acts in his stead at his place of business or at his place of residence, either by registered letter with acknowledgment of receipt or through the collector, the collection enforcement officer, or any other official assigned to this task, against the signature of the offender or of the person acting in his stead, provided that the refusal to sign shall be deemed a legal notification once established by a certificate from the competent official certified by his immediate superior.

Offenders against the provisions of this Legislative Decree shall be subject to financial or administrative penalties imposed upon them by the Administration or to penal sanctions imposed upon them by the courts in accordance with the provisions of the following articles: and the application of one of the types of penalties shall not preclude the application of either of the other two types or both of them.

There shall be imposed upon anyone who neglects to cancel the stamps affixed to instruments and writings, or cancels them in a manner contrary to the provisions of Article 25 of this Legislative Decree, a non-compoundable fine equivalent to twice the value of the stamps that are uncancelled or unlawfully cancelled.

- Fiscal stamp duty fines shall be reduced by 90%; infringements committed prior to the date of issuance of this Law shall benefit from this reduction, provided that they are settled prior to the date of 30/9/2004.

Every person who fails to retain the instruments and writings subject to the duty throughout the retention period provided for in Article 99 of this Legislative Decree shall be subject to a lump-sum fine of five hundred thousand Lebanese pounds, and the competent officials shall then have the right to assess the duty and impose the fine provided for in Article 67 (its first and second paragraphs) on the said instruments and writings on the basis of the offender's registers and records.

The financial penalty (the fine) shall lapse upon the death of the offender unless, at the time of committing the offence, he was acting on behalf of a third party or on behalf of an establishment in which he participates or an association to which he belongs, in which case the fine shall remain payable by the person on whose behalf the offender was acting. If the deceased offender had accomplices in the offence, the fine shall remain in its entirety payable by the survivors among them.

The fines provided for in Articles 67, 68, 69, 70 and 71 shall be doubled upon repetition of the offence within three calendar years. Repetition shall not be deemed to have occurred unless the offender committed his second offence after the date on which the first offence was recorded.

The fines provided for in the preceding Articles shall be imposed by a notice from the head of the competent financial department. Other administrative penalties, such as withdrawal of the licence, cancellation of the permit, closure of the premises and confiscation of the stamps, shall be imposed by a decision of the Minister of Finance.

The fines imposed in accordance with the provisions of the preceding Articles may, upon the request of the concerned parties, be reduced down to one fifth thereof.

The reduction shall be decided upon by the Director General of Finance.

The competent official who draws up an offence report regarding an offence shall be granted a share of the final fine collected as a result of recording the offence amounting to 15% fifteen per cent of its value. A share amounting to 10% shall be granted to the informer who submits to the administration true and factual written information that assists in recording the offence.

In the absence of an informer, his share shall be divided equally between the Treasury and the officials of the financial department in accordance with the following Article 82: An official whose duties require him to work on detecting offences relating to the fiscal stamp duty may not assume the capacity of informer for himself, nor may the spouse of that official or any of his ascendants or descendants assume the said capacity for himself.

10% ten per cent shall be deducted from the total final fines collected resulting from the violations recorded by the competent employees referred to in Article 60 of this Law, and the proceeds shall be distributed in shares among the competent employees at the rate of two shares for the Head of the Revenue Department, two shares for the Head of the competent Finance Section, and one share for each of the indirect taxes controllers attached to the Section and for each of their assistants among drafting clerks, clerks, typists, and ushers.

Any person who delays paying the duty in cash to the Treasury fund, whenever its payment in this form is required pursuant to the law, beyond the specified time limit, shall be subject to a fine equivalent to multiples of the said duty.

Any person who neglects to keep the register provided for in Article 32, as well as the register provided for in Article 52, or delays in keeping either of the two registers or in recording the information that the law requires to be recorded therein, or neglects to submit the notice provided for in Article 54, shall be subject to a flat fine of twenty-five thousand Lebanese pounds.

Any person who sells fiscal stamps at prices exceeding their nominal value inscribed thereon shall be subject to a non-settleable fine of /250000/ two hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese pounds, along with the withdrawal of the sales licence granted to him if he is licensed.

Any person who sells fiscal stamps without a licence shall be subject to a fine of /250000/ two hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese pounds, and the stamps offered for sale shall be confiscated and shall become an acquired right of the Treasury without the concerned party having any right to consideration or compensation.

The Minister of Finance may decide to close the premises, when the violation occurs in unlicensed premises, for a period ranging between three days and one month if the violation is repeated within three years.

Any person who writes on the stamp impression or places thereon any print, writing, drawing or mark of any kind whatsoever that leads to its value being unrecognizable shall be subject to a flat fine of /250000/ two hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese pounds.

Any person who violates the provisions of Article 38 of this Legislative Decree relating to the licensing of the manufacture, importation, sale and trading of stamping machines shall be subject to a non-settleable fine of /250000/ two hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese pounds, and the offending stamping machines shall be confiscated and shall become an acquired right of the Treasury without the concerned party having any right to consideration or compensation.

The licence to use a stamping machine shall be revoked, without the concerned party having any right to compensation, if the licensee misuses the said machine, commits one of the violations or abuses provided for in Article 31, or neglects to comply with the provisions of Articles 32, 34 and 35 of this Legislative Decree.

This Decision determines the details of application of Article 16 of Decree 7336 dated 31/1/2002 relating to the right to deduct Value Added Tax, as amended pursuant to Article One of Decree No. 12910 dated 17/7/2004. The following terms, wherever they appear in this Decision, shall have the meanings set out below:

- "The Law", the Value Added Tax Law.

- "The Tax", the Value Added Tax.

- "The Taxable Person", the person subject to Value Added Tax.

- "The Tax Administration", the Directorate of Value Added Tax.

- "Lebanese Territory" or "Lebanon", the Lebanese territory, airspace and territorial waters.

Pursuant to the provisions of Article 16 of Decree No. 7336/2002 and its amendments, tangible property consisting of machinery and equipment allocated for permanent use in the enterprise as a working tool or a means of exploitation in accordance with International Accounting Standards means that which the Taxable Person allocates for carrying out his economic activity, whether such machinery or equipment is at the core of the production process of the Taxable Person or is used by the Taxable Person to carry out administrative and office work and other work necessary for the Taxable Person to pursue his activity, including, by way of example and without limitation:

- Industrial machinery and equipment.

- Transport vehicles.

- Office and information technology equipment.

- Furniture and furnishings.

With respect to the installations consisting of machinery and equipment mentioned in Articles 3, 4, and 5 of this Decision and acquired by taxable persons after the date on which they became subject to the tax and prior to the effective date of Decree 12910/2004, such persons shall be entitled, pursuant to the provisions of Articles 21, 22, and 23 of Decree 7336/2002, to deduct from the principal of the tax paid upon the acquisition of such installations, the tax pertaining to the remaining period of the five years during which this Decree permitted the adjustment of the deduction to be carried out, provided that the five-year period shall run as of the first of January of the year during which the right to deduct arose, at the rate of one-fifth of the tax originally deducted, and a fraction of a year shall be deemed a full year. Provided that the taxable person declares the result of the adjustment within the periodic return pertaining to the period during which the adjustment took place and deducts it from the tax due from him.

Machinery and equipment deemed to constitute general installations in accordance with the provisions of 16 of Decree No. 7336/2002 and its amendments shall include electrical, mechanical and technical installations, whether fixed in buildings or removable therefrom without damaging the structure of the building, including all extensions and accessories pertaining thereto, such that they are added to the buildings and do not enter into the basis of the construction process, which are the machinery and equipment set forth below:

- Elevators.

- Escalators.

- Moving walkways.

- Central and non-central heating and cooling systems.

- Ventilation systems.

- Fire-fighting systems.

- Lighting systems.

- Security and surveillance systems.

- Control panels.

- Pumps.

- Heaters.

- Valves.

- Electric generators and motors.

- Telephone exchange (central) equipment.

- Computer network systems.

- Lightning protection devices.

- Water treatment plants.

Provided that the tax incurred on the construction process and on the installations that enter into the basis of this process, which is generally based on the following works, shall remain non-deductible:

1 - Excavation, backfilling, levelling, infrastructure works and general site works.

2 - Consulting and engineering works, design, supervision and studies relating to the construction process.

3 - Concrete works, reinforced concrete works and all cement works including masonry, plastering and painting.

4 - Foundation and shoring works.

5 - Doors and windows, works of constructing walls, ceilings and facades (metal - glass...) that cannot be removed without damaging the structure of the building or a part thereof such that it is no longer fit for exploitation, in addition to the painting works pertaining to all that is mentioned in this paragraph.

6 - Tiling, marble and similar works, whether used for the exterior facade of the building or inside it.

Subject to the provisions of Article Three of this Decision, decoration works, including false ceilings, walls (even if they include windows) and false floors, and wallpaper, which can be removed without damaging the structure of the building, in addition to the painting works pertaining thereto, shall be deemed installations for which the tax incurred thereon may be deducted.
With respect to sanitary installations or fixtures, the tax incurred on such installations, including that incurred on their extensions, may be refunded.

With respect to taxable persons who acquired, prior to the date of entry into force of Decree 12910/2004, and prior to the date of their becoming subject to the tax, the installations of machinery and equipment mentioned in Articles 3, 4, and 5 of this Decision, whether they submitted an application for the refund of the tax paid on such installations in accordance with the procedures provided for in Title Five of Decree 7336/2002 and the tax administration refused to allow them to recover this tax or whether they did not submit such an application.

Such persons may submit, within a period of two months from the entry into force of this Decision, an application to the Directorate of Value Added Tax - Tax Compliance Department - in order to determine the value of the tax that was levied on those installations exclusively and which they are entitled to recover, provided that those installations are used to carry out transactions that grant the right of deduction

. Provided that the value of the refundable tax is calculated on the basis of the tax pertaining to the remaining period of the five years during which Articles 21, 22, and 23 of Decree 7336/2002 permitted the adjustment of the deduction to be made, provided that the five-year period runs as of the first of January of the year during which the right of deduction arose, at the rate of one-fifth of the tax originally deducted, and a fraction of a year shall be considered a full year. The application must include the information provided for in Article 19 of Decree 7336/2002, and the tax approved to be refunded shall be deducted from the value of the tax due within the periodic declaration pertaining to the period following the period during which the application was approved, with due regard to all provisions relating to the right of deduction, the adjustment of the deduction, and the right to refund of the tax provided for by the Law and its implementing texts.
This Decision shall enter into force as of the date of its publication in the Official Gazette.

16 - Aggregation of services - Directorate General of General Security: In the matter concerning the aggregation of the services of a former employee in the Directorate General of General Security with the subsequent services in the general administrative cadre, the Civil Service Board replied by its letter No. 4163 dated 22/4/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Finance with the following: Whereas it appears that the person concerned held the post of Inspector Second Grade in the cadre of the Directorate General of General Security and entered the corps on 15/5/2001 and was discharged with effect from 14/9/2003 due to his appointment in the Ministry of Finance pursuant to Decree No. 10819/2003, and whereas the person concerned was subject, in his capacity as one of the non-commissioned officers of General Security, to the legal provisions governing the Directorate General of General Security, which differ from the legal provisions in force in respect of employees in the general administrative cadre, particularly as regards the salary scales applicable to each of them. And whereas the provisions set forth in the Personnel Regulations, including Article 41 which governs transfer from one corps to another corps, do not apply to non-commissioned officers in the aforementioned Directorate General except where a special provision to that effect is contained in the laws and regulations in force therein, which has not been shown to obtain in the present case, and consequently the decree appointing the person concerned No. 10819/2003 is legally sound. However, on the other hand, and with reference to the subject of the request of the person concerned to aggregate his previous services in the Directorate General of General Security with his subsequent services in the Ministry of Finance. And whereas this request has a direct bearing on the calculation of the retirement pension and the severance indemnity. And whereas the seventh Article of Legislative Decree No. 47 dated 29/6/1983 (Retirement and Severance from Service Regulations) determined the services that are counted in the calculation of the retirement pension and the severance indemnity, including the services for which retirement deductions were paid, including the services for which the employee received half salary provided that he pays the retirement deductions for the other half (Item - 1 - of the aforementioned Article), and Article 40 of the aforementioned Legislative Decree provided for the submission of applications for the allocation of pensions and severance indemnities either to the Ministry of Finance or through the administration to which the employee belongs. And whereas it appears that the person concerned remained continuously in his work in the Directorate General of General Security until the date of his appointment in the cadre of the Ministry of Finance pursuant to Decree No. 10819/2003, and that his previous services were not liquidated as a result of the aforementioned appointment, and consequently the functional legal bond between him and the State remained continuous. And whereas the services of an employee who is appointed in one of the administrations of the State subject to the retirement regime, and is thereafter transferred from his cadre to another cadre also subject to the retirement regime, must by operation of law be aggregated with his subsequent services, and that such aggregation must be effected ex officio by the administration. And whereas the previous actual services in the Directorate General of General Security which the person concerned requests to be aggregated with his subsequent services are subject to the retirement and severance indemnity regime pursuant to Item - 1 - of the seventh Article referred to above. Therefore, the Board of the Civil Service Council deems that action should be taken to aggregate the previous services of the person concerned in the Directorate General of General Security with his subsequent services in the Ministry of Finance, together with the financial rights entailed as a result of this aggregation.

17 - Shares of fines - Military service - Actual service: In the case concerning the extent of the entitlement of Mr. (- -) Controller of Expenditure Commitment at the Ministry of Finance - to receive five shares of the fines for the entire period of the last six months of the year 2003, given that he was in actual service for a period of two months and twenty-two days out of the six months, the Civil Service Board replied by its Letter No. 1406 dated 21/10/2004 addressed to the Ministry of Finance as follows: It appears from the letter of the Directorate General of Finance mentioned in the reference above that the concerned party joined military service on 22/9/2003 until 30/12/2003, a matter which led to the withholding of the value of the fines that were due to him for that period, that is, the equivalent of the value of two and a quarter shares out of the five shares that accrued to each Controller of Expenditure Commitment for the period of the last six months of the year 2003, and that the concerned party requests that he be granted five shares, that is, for the entire period, on the grounds that military service is considered part of actual service in the position he occupies, And whereas paragraphs (1 and 2) of Article (117) of Legislative Decree No. 102 dated 16/9/1983 and its amendments (the National Defence Law) stipulated the following: "1 - The salary or wage of an employee or wage-earner who is called up for military service shall cease immediately upon the interruption of his position or work. 2 - The employee or wage-earner shall be reinstated automatically immediately upon his discharge to the position or work to which he was appointed prior to his performance of military service, provided that the period he spent in military service is counted towards advancement in seniority and salary.....". And whereas the final paragraph of Article 121 of the aforementioned Legislative Decree stipulated the following: "If the conscript, prior to being called up for service, was working in the public sector, he shall be reinstated automatically to his work after the expiration of the period of his service in accordance with the provisions of paragraph 2 of Article 117 of this Legislative Decree, and the period of his military service shall be counted as part of the actual services in the position he was occupying when he was called up". And whereas the second paragraph of Article (33) of the General Budget Law for the year 2000 relating to the bases for the distribution of fines, stipulated the following: "A single share shall be determined by dividing the product of the percentage due to employees from the total fines collected on a final basis by the total number of shares due to workers in the Directorate General of Finance and the Government Commissariat at the Bank of Lebanon who were present in service during the period to which the distribution pertains, in proportion to actual service". And whereas it appears from the text of paragraph (1) of the aforementioned Article 117 that calling up an employee for military service leads to the cessation of his salary, a matter which entails, a fortiori, the forfeiture of his right to the allowances and fines that accrue to him as a result of his performance of the duties of his position. And whereas considering the period of military service as part of the actual services of the employee is for the purpose of calculating this period in advancement, without that meaning that the employee benefits from the benefits and fines for the period of his military service, because had the legislator intended for the concerned employee to benefit from those allowances and benefits, it would have stipulated them explicitly just as it did when it considered that the period of military service is part of actual services, given that actual service requires that the employee receive a salary therefor. And whereas it appears from the provisions of the second paragraph of Article 33 of the Budget Law of the year 2000 referred to, that a single share of the collected fines accrues to the workers in the Directorate General of Finance who were present in service during the period to which the distribution pertains, in proportion to actual service, And whereas what is meant by actual service mentioned in the aforementioned paragraph is that the concerned employee be actually performing the duties of his position, and consequently this service is that which is actually performed at the Directorate General of Finance such that the shares are distributed proportionally on the basis of that service, And whereas the action of the administration in withholding the value of the fines that were due to the concerned party for the period of his joining military service, is legally sound. Therefore, the Board of the Civil Service Board deemed that the concerned party is not entitled to claim to be granted five shares of the fines for the entire period of the last six months of the year 2003

Surface Exploitation Rate and General Exploitation Factor:

First: The surface exploitation rate is the ratio between the area of the horizontal projection of the building and the area of the real property. As for the general exploitation factor, it is the ratio between the area of the building across all its floors calculated in the exploitation and the area of the real property. The surface exploitation rate and the general exploitation factor shall be calculated on the basis of the area of the real property after the approved alignment plan and regardless of the existence of easements for the benefit of neighbouring real properties. In the event of the exhaustion of the exploitation factors in a given real property, it shall not be possible to build on any part deducted therefrom, whatever the reasons for this deduction, even if it was in execution of an approved alignment plan.

In the event of the existence of an approved alignment plan on a built real property in which the exploitation factors have not yet been exhausted in full, it shall only be possible to build on the remaining parts thereof within the limits of the remaining exploitation for the real property after the deduction, provided that the part on which the building is to be erected is fit for building as an existing independent real property.

Second - Parts of buildings whose area is not included in the calculation of the general and surface exploitation factors and the number of floors within certain conditions to be determined by a decree:

1 - The area of balconies, verandas, unenclosed loggias, and unenclosed roofed spaces to the extent that the total of

their area in the entire building does not exceed 20% (twenty per cent) of the designed general exploitation area, provided that the area of the balconies on any floor does not exceed 25% (twenty-five per cent) of the area of each floor.

Blinds consisting of movable panels manufactured from transparent uncoloured materials which are placed on balconies shall be considered as traditional blinds that do not require any licence or declaration.

The following shall be calculated within the area of the balconies referred to above:

- Technical areas for the floor.

- Corridors for access to the maid's room, the laundry room, and the pantry room, the area of each of which does not exceed eight square metres.

- Roofed corridors for access between the various buildings in the project, provided that their clear width does not exceed 2.50 m (two and a half metres), their height does not exceed the height of the floor and is not less than 2.20 m (two metres and twenty centimetres), and their number does not exceed two, one of which is on the ground or first floor and the other on one of the upper floors, subject to the approval of the Higher Council of Urban Planning

with respect to the upper corridor.

2 - The area of basement floors the height of the level of the ceiling (concrete) of which does not exceed one metre above:

- Any point above the level of the natural or reclaimed (levelled) ground from all internal sides.

- The level of the line parallel to the road or the pavement, where it exists, which rises above it by one metre, for the front facades.

- As for the side adjacent to real properties in which the number of floors is not specified, the ground level of these neighbouring real properties shall not be taken into consideration, provided that the number of exposed basement floors does not exceed two and that the external height of the exposed part does not exceed /5 m/ (five metres), and provided that the two aforementioned floors are allocated for the service of the building and remain within the common parts upon the subdivision of the building.

The following shall be considered basement floors that are not included in the calculation of the two exploitation factors:

a - In all zones:

Basement floors or parts of basement floors located within the setback from the boundaries of the real property, unless the special regulations stipulate otherwise, whatever their area, if they are allocated for use as car garages or warehouses for the service of the building or for machinery pertaining to the service of the building such as heating and cooling.

Basement floors or parts of basement floors allocated for uses other than the three preceding uses, the total area of which does not exceed fifty per cent (50%) of the general exploitation factor permitted in the zone, and anything in excess thereof shall be included in the general exploitation factor, with the exception of hotels, hospitals, and tourist establishments which by their nature require a basement floor area

greater than that.

b - The exposed basement floor:

- In zones in which the number of floors or the maximum height is specified:

The exposed basement floor erected within the maximum permitted surface exploitation, the height of the ceiling of which does not exceed three and a half metres from the lowest point of the levelled ground and the level of the ceiling (concrete) of which does not exceed one metre in contact with one of the facades, provided that the horizontal area of the natural or levelled ground alongside the facades is not less than two metres.

- In zones in which the number of floors is not specified;

In the event of erecting basement floors backfilled from at least one side and exposed from one or more sides, an area equivalent to a depth of four times its height on each floor for each exposed side shall be included in the calculation of the general exploitation factor.

3 - Projections intended for decoration and crowning, sunshades, cornices, eaves, and the thickness of cladding.

4 - Rooms allocated for electrical power transformer stations: provided that they conform to the plan approved by the competent Electricity Authority, and that they are located outside the boundaries of the setbacks imposed by law with the exception of the access opening to the room, and that they do not obstruct a right of way, car parking spaces, or the line of sight.

5 - Parts of pitched tile roofs and insulation works: Waterproofing and thermal insulation works the height of which does not exceed fifty centimetres /50 cm/, and pitched tile roofs, shall not be included in the calculation of the surface exploitation rate, the general exploitation factor, the maximum height, and the number of floors, provided that their conditions are determined by a decree taken upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport after consulting the opinion of the Higher Council of Urban Planning.

Subdividing the pitched roof into different parts is prohibited; rather, it shall be registered as part of the common parts in the building.

6 - The area of transparent ceilings for spaces: It shall not be calculated within the surface exploitation rate and shall be calculated once in the general exploitation factor regardless of its height.

Transparent ceilings in this case shall not be considered as obstructing the securing of the line of sight, subsequent to the approval of the Higher Council of Urban Planning in accordance with conditions to be determined in the implementing decree.

7 - The area of external walls: In the event of the existence of a double wall for insulation, the area of the external walls (including the thickness of the insulation where it exists), the thickness of which ranges between twenty-two centimetres /22 cm/ and thirty-five centimetres /35 cm/, shall not be calculated within the surface exploitation rate and the general exploitation factor, and anything in excess thereof shall be included in the calculation of the surface and general exploitation factors. The specifications of the double wall shall be determined by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport after consulting the opinion of the Higher Council of Urban Planning.

8 - The staircase and the lift: The area of the main staircase and the lift for each building or block shall not be calculated within the surface exploitation rate and the general exploitation factor, provided that their area does not exceed /20 m2/ twenty square metres, to which /6 m2/ six square metres shall be added for each additional lift, and anything in excess thereof shall be included in the surface exploitation rate and the general exploitation factor; likewise, the area of the emergency staircase, where it exists, shall not be calculated provided that this area does not exceed /15 m2/ fifteen square metres, and anything in excess thereof shall be calculated within the area of the balconies.

Third: Parts of buildings that are not included in the calculation of the general exploitation factor and the number of floors within certain conditions to be determined by a decree:

1 - The area of stairwells, lift shafts, water tanks, technical constructions, and installations pertaining to the service of the building erected above the roof of the top floor.

2 - The area of the caretaker's quarters up to thirty-five square metres /35 m2/ on the ground floor or between the ground and first floors for each block, whatever the nature of the other constructions therein.

3 - The area of mezzanines (lofts): Erected above laundry rooms - ironing rooms - pantry rooms - maids' rooms - bathrooms - lavatories - pantries (office) - internal corridors, apartment entrances - kitchens.

Mezzanines (lofts) erected within shops and showrooms on the floor, provided that their area does not exceed two-thirds of the area of these units and that they do not have any external entrance.

4 - The area of floors and parts of technical constructions which must remain within the common parts in the event of the subdivision of the building, which include the following:

a - The floor or part of the floor that is used as a technical floor, provided that its clear height does not exceed /1.90 m/ one hundred and ninety centimetres. More than one technical floor may be erected in buildings in which the number of floors exceeds twelve upper floors, provided that the technical study justifying that is attached to the building permit application file and the approval of the Higher Council of Urban Planning is obtained.

b - Areas used for technical installations within lightwells. And likewise corridors and stairs within lightwells that contain technical installations, with due regard to public safety conditions.

5 - The area of a stilts (pilotis) floor:

1 - Erected within the horizontal projection of the largest upper floor, in accordance with the following:

a - Erected either above backfilled basement floors or directly on the natural ground, or at the level of the road contiguous or adjacent to the building overlooking it with a maximum tolerance of one metre above or below the level of the road, provided that it is not possible to erect any constructions between the building and the road.

b - Within the stilts (pilotis) and with an area not exceeding 5% (five per cent) of the general exploitation rate, it is permitted to construct a stairwell and lift shaft, an enclosed entrance, the caretaker's quarters, electricity and water meter rooms, a waiting corner, a meeting hall for the occupants of the building, a small warehouse for the service of the building the area of which does not exceed four square metres (4 m2), and everything that is intended for non-exploitation, for each main staircase. Everything in excess thereof shall be calculated in the general exploitation factor without calculating it in the number of floors if the floor does not include any other uses.

Subdividing the contents of these parts of the stilts (pilotis) floor into different private parts is prohibited; rather, it shall be registered as part of the common parts in the building.

c - The height of the stilts (pilotis) floor shall be included in the calculation of the total height of the building, provided that this height does not exceed three and a half metres, and this height may be exceeded up to /4.5 m/ four and a half metres solely in buildings that fulfil the conditions for erecting a technical floor without benefiting from the aforementioned floor, provided that the excess in the height of the stilts (pilotis) floor is allocated for technical extensions.

2 - Erected within the maximum permitted surface exploitation intended for the obligatory garage, provided that its clear height does not exceed two metres and thirty centimetres (2.30 m) and provided that its roof is not used for any purpose.

Fourth - The provisions of the above article shall apply to all new buildings and those not holding an occupancy permit. As for the case of applying for a permit to add an additional building area to an existing building holding an occupancy permit, the provisions of the above article shall apply solely to the added parts.

Works Exempted from the Requirement of a Permit:

Compliance with the regulatory conditions of each zone is required prior to the issuance of the declaration receipt.

First - Works Exempted from Declaration:

Internal works pertaining to ordinary maintenance and beautification works that do not relate to the main structure of the building and do not affect the conformity of the building with the regulations in force shall not be subject to any permit or declaration, such as wallpapering, painting, whitewashing, tiling, cladding, decoration and beautification works, replacing internal joinery, changing the sanitary, electrical, and water network and fixtures, heating and air-conditioning works, and blinds consisting of movable leaves manufactured from uncoloured transparent materials that are placed on balconies.

Second - Works Subject to Declaration:

In buildings that exist legally, or that have been regularised, or that were completed before the date of 13/9/1971, the prior permit application shall be replaced by a written declaration signed by a responsible engineer and certified by one of the two Orders of Engineers, and granted subject to taking all necessary measures to ensure public safety conditions in the vicinity of the building, for the following works:

a - From the Head of the Executive Authority in the municipality concerned:

External construction works pertaining to ordinary maintenance and beautification works that do not relate to the main structure of the building and do not affect the conformity of the building with the regulations in force, such as wallpapering, painting, whitewashing, damp-proofing and external cladding works, installing and changing the external water, sanitary, and electrical network, works of dismantling and installing or changing external joinery of whatever materials. Likewise, the construction of boundary walls that do not require the reclamation of the land of the parcel.

In the event that the building is subdivided, the approval of the owners' association or the approval of 75 percent of the owners must be attached, provided that it is verified that the building which is the subject of the declaration application conforms to the plans pertaining to the occupancy permit or to the certificate of completion of the building.

b - From the Head of the Executive Authority in the municipality concerned after the approval of the competent technical departments:

Restoration and shoring works (Piling or Shoring up), replacing existing roofs, works of levelling the natural ground of the parcel, constructing supporting and retaining walls, demolition works, strengthening works that involve the main structure of the building, modifications, changing and constructing internal walls, and opening or blocking external or internal windows and doors within the different right which do not affect the structural elements and the common parts and do not affect the legality of the unit (the different right), in the light of plans signed by the responsible engineer and registered with one of the two Orders of Engineers.

c - Additional Conditions:

The granting of the declarations referred to in paragraphs (a) and (b) above, or permits comprising similar works, shall be subject to the following additional conditions:

c - 1 - Within the setback from neighbouring parcels

In buildings or parts of buildings located within the setbacks from neighbouring parcels, all works set forth in paragraphs (a) and (b) above shall be permitted therein. As for strengthening works, they shall be permitted on the conditions that the owner registers on the real property folio of the parcel an undertaking drawn up before a notary public to comply with the setbacks imposed according to the regulations of the zone when adding any upper construction, unless the regulations of the zone permit construction above an existing building with the possibility of underpinning.

c - 2 - Within the approved alignment and public domain or within the setbacks therefrom:

When restoring buildings or parts located within the approved alignment and public domain or within the setbacks therefrom, and while complying with the provisions of the Expropriation Law, the owner is required to register on the real property folio of the parcel a waiver drawn up before a notary public not to claim from the Administration any compensation for the betterment resulting from the restoration operation and the replacement of roofs when the Administration expropriates the parts affected by the approved alignment or located within the setbacks therefrom or from the public domain, with the obligation to comply with the setback from the approved alignments and public domain when adding a construction above the existing building.

Third: Technical Conditions for Works Exempted from a Permit:

a - Construction of Boundary Walls

a - 1 - Outside the setback from roads, alignments, or public domain

The construction of boundary walls is permitted provided that the maximum height of the solid part of these boundary walls does not exceed two metres above the level of the natural ground or the levelled ground of the parcel to which the boundary wall belongs. It is also permitted for the solid part of the boundary wall to be topped by a barrier of metal bars, wood, or perforated concrete, provided that the height of the whole (the solid part and the barrier) does not exceed three metres above the level of the natural ground.

(See Drawing No. 1)

a - 2 - On the boundaries of the parcel with the road, alignment, or public domain and within the setbacks therefrom:

The construction of boundary walls is permitted provided that the maximum height of the solid part of these boundary walls does not exceed one metre and twenty cm (1.20 metres) above the level of the road or the natural ground before levelling of the parcel to which the boundary wall belongs. It is also permitted for the solid part of the boundary wall to be topped by a barrier of metal bars, wood, or perforated concrete, provided that the height of the whole (the solid part and the barrier) does not exceed three metres (3.00 m) above the level of the natural ground. This is in the event that the special regulations do not provide otherwise.

(See Drawing No. 2)

It is also permitted to construct boundary walls on the boundaries of the parcel in its part affected by an unexpropriated alignment, subject to submitting an undertaking registered on the real property folio not to claim any compensation therefor when executing the alignment.

a - 3 - When the boundary wall is erected outside the setbacks from roads above a (supporting or retaining) wall pursuant to paragraph (b) below:

If the height of the wall does not exceed two metres: it is permitted to erect a solid part above it with a height not exceeding two metres, provided that the height of the wall with the solid part does not exceed three metres, and it is permitted for the said solid part to be topped by a barrier of metal bars, wood, or perforated concrete, provided that its height with the solid part does not exceed three metres.

(See Drawing No. 3)

If the height of the wall exceeds two metres: it is permitted to erect a solid part above it with a height not exceeding one metre and to erect a barrier of metal bars, wood, or perforated concrete above it, provided that its height with the solid part does not exceed two metres.

(See Drawing No. 4)

b - Works of Levelling the Natural Ground:

Land reclamation works (levelling), including the construction of retaining and supporting walls pertaining to the siting of buildings in the land of sloping parcels, shall be subject to declaration.

The declaration for reclaiming the land of the parcel shall be granted after submitting plans signed by the responsible engineer and registered with one of the two Orders of Engineers, with an undertaking by him showing thereon the level of the natural ground of the parcel prior to commencing the work and the final plans required to be executed. The file shall also be accompanied by a contour map of the natural ground of the parcel linked to the official benchmarks if they exist, signed by a surveyor engineer registered with one of the two Orders of Engineers, or by a topographer registered with the Syndicate of Topographers, and the map must be registered with one of the two Orders of Engineers, or with the Syndicate of Topographers, and accompanied by photographs of the natural ground prior to commencing the works.

The purpose of the reclamation and the intended use shall be stated in the declaration application, and in the event that the area of the parcel exceeds 3000 square metres, the approval shall be granted in stages, provided that the reclaimed area in each stage does not exceed 3000 (three thousand) square metres and that the height of the walls does not exceed three and a half metres. A fraction of less than one thousand square metres shall be rounded.

The provisions of Environment Law No. 444 dated 29/7/2002 shall be observed when granting a declaration for reclaiming the land of parcels whose area exceeds ten thousand square metres.

b - 1: Technical conditions for works of levelling the natural ground outside the limits of setbacks from roads, alignments, and public domain:

b - 1 - 1: Conditions for backfilling and construction of supporting walls:

Supporting walls are walls that contain the backfill necessary to raise the level of the sloping natural ground (murs de soutenement), and consequently the walls or parts of walls located above the level of the natural ground shall be considered supporting walls.

It is permitted to raise the level of any point of the sloping natural ground of the parcel by means of backfilling, provided that the backfills do not exceed the height of the supporting walls necessary for them:

- Three and a half metres outside the setbacks.

- The horizontal distance separating the supporting wall from the wall below it.

- Two metres within the setbacks from the boundaries of neighbouring parcels.

(See Drawing No. 5) (New Drawing 5 in accordance with Decree 617 /2007)

- The level of the natural ground at the boundary of the adjoining parcel which is higher than the level of the ground of the parcel that is the subject of the levelling.

(See Drawing No. 6)

Exceptional cases that require derogation from the conditions above shall be decided upon by the Higher Council for Urban Planning.

b - 1 - 2: Conditions for excavation and construction of retaining walls:

Retaining walls are walls that cover and protect the sloping natural ground (Murs de Protection) in cases imposed by:

- The topography of steeply sloping ground (Falaise).

- The situation resulting from the action of the Administration (cutting a road in the form of a Tranchee) or a subdivision project.

- A land reclamation operation (excavation, hollowing out).

Consequently, the walls or parts of walls located below the level of the natural ground shall be considered retaining walls.

It is permitted to excavate the land of the parcel and erect retaining walls whatever their height may be, in accordance with the following conditions:

* When the height of the retaining walls exceeds 3.50 m (three and a half metres), the erection of any supporting part above any of them is prohibited.

* If the height of the retaining wall is less than 3.5 m, it is permitted to raise the natural ground alongside it, such that the height of the wall (supporting and retaining) becomes 3.5 m as a maximum.

(See Drawing No. 7)

* When the retaining wall is erected to a height exceeding 3.5 m behind buildings to secure the line of sight, the width of the said wall must not exceed the horizontal projection of the building facade from the lower side of the parcel onto the wall, including the passages permitted on both sides of the building whose maximum width does not exceed 4 metres.

* A distance of not less than 80 cm must be allocated alongside the wall for planting trees at a rate of one tree every 3 metres, provided that the natural ground is levelled in terraces on both sides of the building in the form of gardens such that the height of each retaining wall does not exceed the height of the storey with a maximum of 3.5 m.

* In this case, it is permitted to provide at most one passage on each side with a width not exceeding 1.20 m to provide access from the building to the terraced ground, without counting these passages within the two exploitation ratios, with the possibility of allocating the parts of the terraced ground as an exclusive right for the use of the different parts of the building connected to them.

(See Drawings No. 8, 9, 10, and 11)

b - 2: Technical conditions for works of levelling the natural ground within the limits of setbacks from roads, alignments, and public domain

b - 2 - 1: In parcels sloping above the level of the road

The level of the natural ground located within the setback from the road may be raised, provided that the height of the supporting walls does not exceed 1.20 m (one metre and twenty centimetres) as a maximum above the level of the road or the pavement adjacent to the parcel if it exists. It is permitted to erect a parapet of perforated concrete, wrought iron, or wood above the supporting wall, provided that the height of the solid part with the parapet does not exceed three metres, subject to registering a waiver by the owner drawn up before a notary public on the real property folio relinquishing any claim for compensation for the works executed within the setback.

Supporting walls constructed outside the limits of the imposed setback on the side of the road are permitted to rise above the level of the road by three and a half metres, to which is added a height equal to the value of the distance separating them from the imposed setback from the road, provided that they do not in any case exceed three and a half metres above the natural ground.

(See Drawing No. 12) (New Drawing 12 in accordance with Decree in force 617 /2007)

The ground may also be raised in a slope, provided that the slope of the ground after levelling does not exceed 30 degrees and that the height alongside the setback from the road does not exceed three and a half metres, and that the slope is separated from the road by a barrier of not less than thirty centimetres.

In the event of constructing supporting walls, the height of these walls must not exceed the maximum limits specified in the paragraph above regardless of the existence of the slope.

(See Drawing No. 13) (New Drawing 13 in accordance with Decree in force 617 /2007)

The natural ground within the setback from the boundaries of the road may also be excavated to make it at the level of the road.

(See Drawing No. 14)

b - 2 - 2: In parcels sloping below the level of the road

It is prohibited to excavate the part of the parcel located within the imposed setback from the boundaries of the road and from the boundaries of the approved alignment to a level lower than the level of the road and the approved alignment, and it is permitted to backfill the part located within the setback with a slope not exceeding five percent.

(See Drawing No. 15)

b - 3 -: Additional conditions:

* Supporting or retaining walls must be proportionate to the facades of the building and the surroundings.

* It is required to ensure public safety and the safety of structures and buildings erected on parcels adjoining the parcel that is the subject of the excavation, and the engineer who signed the plans shall be held responsible for the stability and strength of the walls, the bearing capacity of the natural ground, and the ensuring of public safety.

b - 4 -: Height of the building

When reclaiming the sloping land of a parcel (levelling) by means of backfilling or excavation, in accordance with the conditions specified above, the level of the ground of the parcel after levelling alongside the body of the building shall be adopted in calculating the height of the building, provided that the horizontal distance alongside the body of the building is not less than two metres.

In parcels sloping above the road, the level of the road adjacent to the parcel shall be adopted as the starting point for the height of the building if the distance separating the building and the limits of the setback from the road does not exceed two metres.

(See Drawing No. 16)

If, however, the distance separating the building and the limits of the setback from the road is equal to or exceeds two metres, the level of the ground after levelling at the lowest point alongside the body of the building shall be adopted.

(See Drawing No. 17)

The total height of the building shall be measured up to the average height of the storeys having a pitched roof, provided that the horizontal parts of the last roof comply with the specified maximum height.

(See Drawing No. 18) (New Drawing 18 in accordance with Decree in force 617 /2007)

b - 5: General provisions

When the nature of the land of the parcel does not allow compliance with the conditions specified under this Article, the permit may be exempted from these conditions after the approval of the Higher Council for Urban Planning.

In approved and unexecuted alignments, the level specified by the authority that established the alignment or that which is adopted by this authority shall be adopted, and in the event of its absence, the level specified by the municipality concerned after the approval of the competent technical department shall be adopted.

It is required to ensure public safety and the safety of structures and buildings erected on parcels adjoining the parcel that is the subject of the excavation, and subject to constructing a retaining wall at the boundaries of the excavation in accordance with the specifications built in item b - 1 - 2.

c - Demolition Works

Works of demolishing buildings and structures shall be subject to declaration on the basis of plans and an undertaking to supervise the demolition works, both signed by an engineer and registered with one of the two Orders of Engineers according to the registration of the engineer.

The plans must show the siting of the building on the parcel and the number of its storeys in the light of two cross-sections in two perpendicular directions, with the shoring of neighbouring buildings and structures, and the placing of barriers around the perimeter of the site, lighting it, and equipping it with the necessary signs to warn pedestrians on the side of the road if necessary.

The declaration must also specify the means and equipment that will be used in the demolition works (blasting, mechanical impact, bulldozers,...), all of this being conditional upon attaching an insurance policy covering all damages that may arise as a result of the demolition works, while adopting the permitted types and means of demolition within the protection, prevention, and public safety measures specified by the regulations and laws.

d - Buildings to which the declaration system for ordinary maintenance, beautification, restoration, and demolition works does not apply

The declaration system that is the subject of this Article shall not apply to ordinary maintenance, beautification, restoration, and demolition works pertaining to classified archaeological buildings and structures and buildings located within a zone whose approved regulations have imposed special conditions thereon; rather, these works shall be subject to the regulations governing these buildings.

Additional and Collective (Public) Garage:

First - Additional Garage:

In the event of providing an additional garage in excess of the garage legally required:

* The area of the additional garage equivalent to an area of twenty-five square metres /25 m2/ for each additional car for which parking is provided therein shall be exempted from the building permit fee, up to a maximum equal to the area of the legally required garage.

* The owner of the real property shall be required to register on the real property register an irrevocable undertaking executed before a notary public that the section of the building designated as an additional garage on the building permit plans shall remain allocated as an additional garage upon the subdivision of the real property into separate shares.

* This paragraph was repealed pursuant to Enforceable Decree 617 dated 8/8/2007 Official Gazette 50

* The additional garage is permitted to be provided in basement floors backfilled on all sides regardless of their number, and within the free spaces of the land of the real property. The owner may, if he wishes, provide the additional garage in exposed basement floors and the piloti floor as well as in the upper floors while benefiting from the exemptions provided for in this Decree, provided that the additional garage in this case does not exceed two floors.

* The area of the additional garage shall not be calculated in the general exploitation factor and the number of floors, subject to compliance with the building envelope line and the height imposed in the zoning regulations.

(Paragraph added pursuant to Enforceable Decree 617 dated 8/8/2007 Official Gazette 50)

*In the event of adding a building or modifying the intended use with the conversion of the additional parking spaces into required parking spaces, the permit for the addition or modification shall not be granted until after payment of the fees due for the area that was exempted for the converted additional garage, in addition to the building permit fees for the required parking spaces in the event that such parking spaces are subject to fees.

Second - Collective Garage for the Public:

1 - A permit may be granted for the construction of a building designated as a collective garage for the public on real properties whose area is not less than one thousand square metres, and a section of the building may be allocated for commercial use provided that the number of car parking spaces allocated to the public is not less than one hundred cars.

2 - The area of the building or section of the building allocated as a collective garage for the public shall not be calculated within the general exploitation factor and the surface exploitation ratio, provided that it complies with the legally imposed setbacks and the building envelope line. The exemptions set forth in the first paragraph of Item First of this Article (Additional Garage) shall apply to the collective garage.

3 - The owner of the real property built as a collective garage for the public is permitted to transfer three-quarters of the balance of the general exploitation factor (not used for a commercial building) to another real property or properties within the same cadastral area and the same zoning area, subject to compliance with the remaining building permit condition on the real property or properties to which the balance of the general exploitation factor was transferred, including the building envelope line.

No more than twenty percent (20%) of the exploitation factor of any real property in the same cadastral area and the same zoning area may be transferred to that real property, and subject to the approval of the Higher Council for Urban Planning on the proposed site for the increase.

Third: Incentives for the Construction of the Additional Garage and the Public Garage:

1 - Occupation of public domain for the construction of public garages:

Notwithstanding any text, a permit may be granted for the occupation of non-maritime public domain belonging to each of the State and the municipalities in order to build garages for the public and exploit them for a specified term, in accordance with the following conditions:

* The proposal to allocate the section of the public domain for a public garage shall be submitted by the owning entity for the approval of the Higher Council for Urban Planning, accompanied by plans showing the location of the real property relative to the main and public roads in the area and its relationship to the residential and commercial clusters in the area, and by a map showing the locations of other public domain properties in the area.

* The Higher Council for Urban Planning shall have the right to propose the allocation of another section of the public domain as a public garage if it appears that the alternative section is more suitable in terms of area or location, or both, than the proposed section.

* In light of the approval of the Higher Council for Urban Planning on the allocation of the public domain or a section thereof as a public garage, the entity owning the real property shall publish a notice to hold a public auction, in accordance with the established procedures, to license the occupation of the public domain to construct a public garage thereon.

* The entity selected as a result of the public auction shall submit to the Higher Council for Urban Planning the plans relating to the proposed parking building while complying with all conditions for the construction of the public garage, particularly with respect to attaching a study of the impact of the building on traffic movement (Traffic Impact Study) and how to address these variables, and submitting a detailed study of the facades of the building.

* In light of the approval of the Higher Council for Urban Planning on the design relating to the project, the occupation of the public domain shall be licensed pursuant to contracts concluded by the competent Minister setting out the duration of the occupation, the fees due therefor, and the rights of the occupant in the event of revocation of the occupation licence, all in light of the result of the public auction, provided that these contract are ratified by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the competent Minister.

2 - Increase of the exploitation factor in the event of providing an additional garage allocated to the municipality.

Buildings whose height exceeds fifty metres (50m) and large complexes that fulfil the conditions of Article Sixteen of No. 646 dated 11/12/2004 shall benefit from an increase in the general exploitation factor in the event that the owner of the building or complex provides an additional garage in accordance with the following conditions:

* The entrance and exit of the additional garage must be independent of the entrances of the building and directly connected to the public road.

* The additional garage must accommodate at least fifty cars in independent parking spaces.

* The provisions relating to the additional garage provided for in Item First of this Article must be complied with.

* The increase in the general exploitation factor shall be set at twelve square metres /12 m2/ for each additional car parking space, provided that the increase does not exceed:

- One thousand five hundred square metres /1500 m2/ as a maximum regardless of the number of parking spaces in the additional garage.

- A rate of ten percent /10%/ of the general exploitation factor.

- At most two floors with a total height of 7m.
