* The owner of the real property who wishes to benefit from the provisions of this paragraph must submit an application to the Higher Council for Urban Planning accompanied by the plans and documents confirming that the application fulfils the conditions referred to above, while complying with all conditions for the construction of the public garage, particularly with respect to attaching a study of the impact of the building on traffic movement (Traffic Impact Study) and how to address these variables and submitting a detailed study of the facades of the building.

* In the event of the approval of the Higher Council for Urban Planning on the increase of the general exploitation factor, the building permit shall be granted in three stages: the basement floors, the public garage, and the upper section of the building including the increase in the general exploitation factor.

* After the completion of the additional garage, an application shall be submitted to obtain a final partial occupancy permit for the garage, on the basis of which the garage shall be subdivided and registered in the name of the municipality concerned, with the registration of the value of the added exploitation on the real property folio of the real property or properties concerned.

* In the final stage, the completion of the building in its upper section, including the increase in exploitation, shall be carried out.

Fourth - General Conditions for Additional and Public Garages:

* The clear height must not exceed two metres and fifty centimetres (2.50m) under the ceiling provided that it is not less than two metres and twenty centimetres (2.20m) under the drop beams, in the event that they are provided for in the ground floor or in the two upper floors referred to in Item "First" of this Article.

* The application for a permit to construct a collective garage for the public must include a study of the impact of its building on traffic movement (Traffic Impact Study) and how to address these variables, and in the case of the collective garage a detailed study of the facades of the building must be submitted.

* In the event of changing the intended use of the additional garage or the collective garage for the public, the constructions licensed for this purpose shall be deemed illegal and the State or the municipalities may demolish or confiscate them.

*The areas allocated for additional parking spaces may not be sold or leased as separate independent units in favour of built units outside or inside the real property within which the additional parking spaces are located unless the following conditions are met therein:

- The number of additional parking spaces provided must not be less than 10 parking spaces.

- Privacy must be ensured for the garage required for the building along with the manner of separating the required garage from the additional garage.

- The conditions for the management of the garage provided for in Items First and Second must be specified within the ownership regulations relating to the building.

(There is an attached drawing annexed to Enforceable Decree 617 /2007 for insertion)

*The additional parking spaces that fulfil the conditions above and the collective garages for the public may be sold or leased without the possibility of changing their intended use.

In the event of changing the intended use of the garage (additional or collective for the public), the constructions licensed for this purpose shall be deemed illegal and the State or the municipalities may demolish or confiscate them.

* The intended use of the additional garage may not be modified unless the building after the modification fulfils the building conditions in the zone, with due regard to the rights of others, provided that double the building permit fees are collected for the areas of the additional garage that are the subject of the modification application, even if the application to modify the intended use is limited to converting from an additional garage to a required garage.

In these Regulations:

The word: "Employee" means the local employee.

The word: "Mission" means the Embassy or the Consulate General.

The words: "Secretary General" mean the Secretary General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants.

The Head of Mission shall establish a cadre of employees therein according to the needs and necessities of work, and it shall not become effective except after the approval of the Secretary General.

The cadre may include, in accordance with the requirements of work, the following categories:

a - Information programmer, and translator.

b - Secretary to the Head of Mission, clerk, assistant accountant.

c - Data entry clerk.

d - Cook, driver.

e - Usher, messenger, servant, guard and gardener.

General conditions of appointment in the Mission:

A candidate for one of the posts of the cadre of local employees in the Mission is required:

1 - To have completed eighteen years of age on the date of his appointment and not to have exceeded fifty years of age as a maximum limit, and the date of birth of the new employee shall be stated in the appointment decision. The cook and the driver are exempted from the maximum limit.

Also exempted from the age requirement is an employee reinstated to service before the expiry of one year from his dismissal (Article 22, paragraph 4).

2 - To enjoy his full mental and physical faculties and be free from infirmities and contagious diseases.

3 - That the candidate submit to the Head of Mission an application containing his curriculum vitae and the places where he previously worked, to which the following documents shall be attached:

a - His civil status extract or his passport.

b - His photograph.

c - Academic certificates and attestations of experience.

d - A medical certificate issued not more than one month earlier proving that he is free from infirmities and contagious diseases.

e - A judicial record or its equivalent in the host country, issued not more than one month earlier, proving that he enjoys his civil rights in accordance with paragraph (e) of Article Four of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6/1959.

f - The documents mentioned above shall be certified by the Head of Mission.

4 - Preference in appointment shall be given to a Lebanese citizen provided that he meets the conditions required for the post for which he is a candidate.

5 - That the candidate fulfil the necessary conditions to obtain a residence and work permit for an employee who does not hold the nationality of the host country.

Special conditions for appointment:

In addition to the general conditions mentioned in Article 3 above, a candidate for the positions of Categories A - B - C (Article 2) must be proficient in one of the French, English or local languages, and in working on the computer, and preference shall be given to one who is proficient in the Arabic language, in addition to the following qualifications and certificates:

For the position of data programmer: to hold a certificate of computer analyst (Informatique de gestion).

For the position of translator: to hold a university degree in translation, or to have practised translation work for a period of not less than three years.

For the position of clerk: to hold a certificate at the level of the Baccalaureate Part II at least or its equivalent, and anyone who has previously practised work for a period of not less than five years in the same position for which he is a candidate shall be exempted from the certificates. Or who has practised work in the same mission in the position of data entry clerk for a period of five years.

For the position of assistant accountant: to hold a certificate in accounting at the level of the Baccalaureate Part II at least or its equivalent, or to have previously practised accounting work for a period of not less than three years.

For the position of secretary: holding a secretarial certificate or a Baccalaureate Part II at least or its equivalent or Head of Mission: experience of not less than three years in secretarial work provided proficiency in the local language in addition to the French or English foreign language. Or practising work in the same mission in the position of data entry clerk for a period of three years.

For the position of data entry clerk: a certificate at the level of the Technical Baccalaureate in Informatics at least or its equivalent, and anyone who has previously practised work for a period of not less than three years in the same position for which he is a candidate shall be exempted from the certificate.

For the position of cook: to hold a vocational certificate or to possess previous experience of not less than two years in accordance with a statement from a reliable authority.

For the position of messenger: to be proficient in the local language.

For the position of servant, usher, guard or gardener: to pass an oral interview conducted by the Head of Mission or whomever he delegates.

For the position of driver: to hold a local driving licence and be proficient in the local language and to undertake to perform the duties required by this position and to work outside the official working hours in force in the mission and in accordance with the requirements of work determined by its head.

Effect and Consequences of Appointment:

1- No one shall be appointed except to a vacant post in the establishment for which an appropriation is allocated in the budget, and in accordance with the procedures prescribed by the Regulations.

2 - Appointment shall be made at the lowest grade of the category.

3 - Any employee who has worked in a foreign mission may be appointed at a grade higher than the lowest grade, provided that his experience therein is calculated at the rate of four full years of experience in exchange for obtaining one grade above the lowest grade.

4 - The appointment shall take effect from the date of assumption of duties, and it shall not have any retroactive effect.

5 - The Head of the Mission shall amend the establishment, should the need arise, by a reasoned decision issued by him, and the amendment shall not enter into force until approved by the Secretary-General.

Appointment of Local Employees:

1 - If it is established to the satisfaction of the Head of the Mission that the applicant for the post is qualified for public service and fulfills the conditions mentioned in the third and fourth Articles of these Regulations, and that the position is vacant and within the limits of the appropriation allocated in the budget, he shall prepare a draft decision of temporary appointment for a period of three months and shall send the complete appointment file in accordance with the third Article within a period not exceeding one month from the date of appointment to the Central Administration for the approval of the Secretary-General thereon. Attached to the decision shall be the employment contract provided for in the thirtieth Article, if adopted. As well as the documents mentioned in the third Article of this decision.

2 - The age of the new employee shall be stated in the appointment decision on the basis of a certified true copy of his registration in the civil status registers or in his passport, and if the date of birth is unknown, the employee shall be deemed to have been born on the first day of the month of July of the year of his birth.

3 - The employee shall be deemed confirmed in the post to which he was appointed after three months if he demonstrates competence at work, and all the rights and duties mentioned in these Regulations shall apply to him from the date of his appointment. It shall not be required to prepare a new decision in this case.

Working Hours:

The working hours observed at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in the host country shall apply, provided that they are not less than six actual working hours per day and thirty hours per week. An attendance register shall be maintained at the Mission, which employees shall sign upon their arrival and departure.

Promotion:

The employee shall be promoted from one category to another, provided that he is transferred to the grade the salary of which equals his salary or is immediately higher than his salary, provided that his next advancement in grade is calculated after the lapse of 24 months from the date of his promotion.

Two separate draft decisions shall be lodged with the Ministry, the first providing for his dismissal from service and the second providing for his reappointment, provided that his financial rights for the period during which he served in the category from which he is transferred are liquidated if he benefits from a dismissal indemnity from the Lebanese Treasury.

Duties of the Employee It shall be incumbent upon the local employee in general:

1 - To respect the working hours specified for him, to obey his superiors and to execute the tasks entrusted to him with all diligence, accuracy and loyalty.

2 - To preserve the property of the mission and to treat persons having business therewith with all courtesy and respect without soliciting or accepting from them any reward or gift.

3 - To inform the head of the mission of every event that would modify the information which he submitted when applying for his appointment.

4 - Not to perform any other remunerated work except after obtaining the permission of the head of the mission, subject to observing the provisions of the tenth Article of these Regulations.

5 - Not to be absent and interrupt work and disturb the working atmosphere, and to abide by the instructions of the head of the mission.

Prohibited Acts The employee is prohibited in particular from the following matters:

1 - Divulging official information of which he became aware during the performance of his function or by reason of this function, or communicating to anyone who ought not to be notified official documents or papers or what is contained in these documents and papers, or letting such documents and papers leak intentionally or through negligence.

2 - Practising work that detracts from the dignity of the function or prevents him from performing his duties in the mission in the fullest manner and with complete independence, or practising work or an activity in an institution the interests of which conflict with the interests of Lebanon, or having a direct relationship or through third parties with interests hostile to Lebanon or incompatible with its interests.

3 - Committing, during the performance of the function or in his private life, an act that would place the mission in an embarrassing position before public opinion or before the local authority.

4 - Soliciting or accepting, directly or through an intermediary, for himself or for third parties, by reason of the function which he occupies, gratuities or donations of whatever kind.

5 - Joining syndicates of whatever kind, with the exception of syndicates of workers in foreign missions organized according to the law of the host country.

Salaries:

1 - The Head of the Mission shall establish a salary scale for each of the positions set forth in the second article of these Regulations, and such scale shall not take effect until after the approval of the Secretary-General, provided that the minimum wage in the country in which the Mission is located is taken into consideration.

The scale shall be amended on the basis of the rise in the cost of living by the percentage by which the host State raises the salaries of public sector employees, pursuant to a decision of the Head of the Mission and the approval of the Secretary-General, provided that the value of the increase does not exceed 30% of the salary in a single year.

2 -

a - The Head of the Mission may grant the local employee an advancement step after the lapse of twenty-four months of continuous actual service, after the approval of the Secretary-General.

b - The steps mentioned above shall not be granted if the Mission pays periodic increases pursuant to local law.

3 - Salaries shall be paid on the basis of twelve months per year, and the number of months may be determined in accordance with local laws, provided that the employees of the Mission are affiliated with the local social security and the labour law in the host States applies to them.

4 - The salary of a new employee shall accrue as of the date on which he commences work, and his salary shall not be entered on the payroll until after notification of the Ministry's approval of the appointment decision.

5 - The new salary of the employee, whether for advancement, a cost-of-living increase, or for any reason whatsoever, shall accrue as of the first of the month following the month in which the increase accrued, provided that in all cases such increase shall not be entered on the payrolls until after notification of the Ministry's approval of the requisite decision. Foreign missions organised according to the law of the host country.

Cases in which the salary is discontinued The salary shall be discontinued:

1 - In respect of an employee who is deemed to have resigned under the provisions of these Regulations, starting from the day on which he ought to have returned to his work.

2 - By operation of law in respect of an employee who has reached the statutory age, as of the day following his reaching such age, even if no decision dismissing him from service has been issued.

3 - In respect of an employee dismissed from service, as of the day following the date on which he is notified of the decision of dismissal from service.

Overtime Work and Bonuses:

Overtime Work:

In cases of necessity, an employee may be required to perform overtime work outside official working hours to complete certain work that cannot be completed during official working hours, pursuant to a reasoned draft decision by the Head of the Mission, which shall only take effect after receiving the approval of the Secretary-General, provided that the draft decision of assignment mentions:

a - The justifying reasons for the overtime work.

b - The name of the assigned employee and his position.

c - The estimated duration of the overtime work in days.

d - The date of commencement of the work and its timing on the day (from hour... to hour..).

e - The local employee shall receive for each overtime hour a compensation equivalent to one 150th of his monthly salary, and these compensations shall be disbursed from the local employees' salaries budget line.

f - The value of overtime hours in a month shall not exceed half the monthly salary of the employee.

Bonuses:

An employee who performs a specific work warranting appreciation may be granted a cash bonus determined by a decision of the Head of the Mission after the approval of the Secretary-General, provided that it does not exceed one month's salary per year, and the justifying reasons for this bonus shall be mentioned in the decision.

The allowance for overtime hours and bonuses shall be disbursed from the local employees' salaries budget line.

Leaves:

Administrative Leaves:

1 - An employee is entitled to an annual administrative leave with full salary for a duration of twenty days on the basis of six actual working days per week. The provisions of the local labour and social security law shall apply to whoever benefits from its benefits in full.

2 - Administrative leaves shall be granted year by year upon a written request submitted by the employee, and in exceptional cases leaves may be accumulated for a duration of two years at most, and no compensation may be given in lieu of leave.

3 - A new employee may not be appointed to perform the duties of an employee who is benefiting from his leave; rather, one of the employees shall be assigned to his work during his absence, and this applies to all types of leaves, including family, administrative, and maternity leaves, except in two exceptional cases:

a - Where there is no other employee in the mission who can perform his work.

b - If the employee is benefiting from leave without pay.

4 - The Head of the Mission shall schedule the leaves of employees in a manner that ensures the continuity of work in the mission, and the leave decision must mention the name of the employee who the leave decision mentions the name of the employee who replaces the described employee on leave throughout the duration of his absence and acts on his behalf in all his powers, and termination of service or retirement shall not take effect until after the expiration of the duration of the administrative leave.

Family leave:

In addition to his annual leave, an employee shall be entitled to be absent with permission and on full pay for a period of three days at most in the event of his marriage or the death of his spouse or any of his ascendants, descendants, siblings, or brothers.

Leave without pay:

An employee may, for private reasons and at his request, be granted leave without pay not exceeding one month within one year.

Assessment documents are divided into:

First- Taxes assessed by way of self-assessment: The return submitted by the taxpayer, in cases where tax laws require self-assessment of the tax, shall be deemed an assessment document.

Second - Taxes issued pursuant to assessment rolls:

-Original:

a- Income tax: These are the rolls comprising the taxes estimated by the tax administration for taxpayers subject to the estimated profit regime in respect of a specific financial year.

b - Built property tax: These are the rolls comprising the taxes due on all real properties in a specified area.

-Supplementary:

These are the rolls issued by the tax administration, which comprise due assessments that the taxpayer has not declared and paid to the Treasury by way of self-assessment, as well as assessments resulting from the amendment of taxpayers' returns following their examination by the tax administration or an amendment to the tax base in respect of taxes issued pursuant to original assessment rolls.

- Abatement rolls: These are the rolls drawn up to rectify assessments issued pursuant to original or supplementary rolls, or paid pursuant to a return according to the self-assessment method, due to the existence of an error in the assessment or upon the taxpayer's objection or a claim for refund.

Third - Taxes issued pursuant to collection orders:

These are the collection orders comprising assessments resulting from the examination of the taxpayer's returns or based on information available to the tax administration in accordance with the provisions of Article 42 of the Law.

- Abatement orders: These are those drawn up to rectify assessments issued pursuant to collection orders, or paid pursuant to a return according to the self-assessment method, due to the existence of an error in the assessment or based on the taxpayer's objection or a claim for refund.

The following rules shall be observed in drawing up assessment rolls and collection orders: - Separate rolls from the assessments of previous years shall be allocated to the assessments of the current year for each assessment district.

- Assessments shall be entered in the rolls according to the sequence of property numbers with respect to the built property tax issued pursuant to basic rolls and the sequence of the dates of collection orders with respect to the transfer duty.

- Additional assessment rolls and abatement rolls for income tax shall be issued for each taxpayer separately, and the roll may include assessments for several tax periods, and it is prohibited to include several taxpayers in a single additional roll or abatement roll.

- Additional assessment rolls and abatement rolls for the built property tax shall be issued for each property separately, and the roll may include assessments for several tax periods and for several taxpayers.

- Collection orders shall be issued for each taxpayer separately and for each tax period separately.

- When drawing up assessment rolls and collection orders, the expiry date of the payment time limit must be indicated in the remarks column, and the collection fine shall run from the day following the expiry of this time limit.

- Additional assessment rolls for income tax on commercial, industrial and non-commercial profits (Title I) for taxpayers who are individuals or partners in partnerships shall be drawn up according to their personal tax numbers and not the number of the sole proprietorship or company.

- Additional assessment rolls for income tax on profits pursuant to the provisions of Articles 41, 42 and 43 of the Income Tax Law with respect to partnerships shall be drawn up in the name of the company, whereas for sole proprietorships the assessment shall be issued in the personal name of the taxpayer, and they must be issued separately from the rolls of commercial profits (Title I).

- Additional assessment rolls for income tax in accordance with the provisions of Article 45 of the Income Tax Law with respect to partnerships shall be drawn up in the name of the company, whereas for sole proprietorships the assessment shall be issued in the personal name of the taxpayer, and they shall be issued separately from the assessment rolls for the tax on commercial, industrial and non-commercial profits.

- Assessment rolls for income tax on salaries and wages shall be drawn up in the name of the company, whatever its legal form, or of the sole proprietorship; however, with respect to the difference in tax on salaries and wages due from taxpayers obliged to submit the personal return (R8) in accordance with the provisions of Article 53 of the Income Tax Law, the additional rolls shall be drawn up according to the name of the taxpayer and his personal tax number.

- Upon drawing up assessment rolls for income tax on salaries and wages, and pursuant to the principle of joint and several liability, the assessment issued in the name of the company or enterprise shall be linked to the tax account of the partners through their personal registration number.

- When drawing up abatement rolls or abatement orders, the number of the assessment roll or collection order from which the abatement is to be made, its type, and the assessment year or tax period in which it was issued shall be recorded in the remarks column.

- The rolls shall be drawn up in two individual copies (an assessment copy and a collection copy) and a summary copy containing the total taxable revenues and the total tax and fines resulting therefrom.

- The assessment and collection copies and the summary roll shall be signed with a live signature by the controller, the chief controller and the head of the unit, and shall be deposited with the head of the tax administration.

- Drawing up collection orders in two individual copies (an assessment copy and a collection copy).

- For every tax imposed pursuant to an additional roll or a collection order, or abated pursuant to an abatement roll or an abatement order, a personal tax notice shall be drawn up in two copies in which all the information entered therein shall be recorded, and these notices shall bear the number of the assessment document and the date of its approval, and one copy of the notice shall be sent to the taxpayer in accordance with the rules and the second shall be kept in the taxpayer's file.

- All assessment and abatement rolls, collection orders and abatement orders which cannot be drawn up on the systems set up by the Electronic Centre shall be drawn up on the computer (Excel program or other) in accordance with the rules set out above.

The assessment rolls and the collection orders shall be sent, after being drawn up in accordance with what is stated above, to the competent authority for their ratification.

The assessment rolls shall be returned, after their ratification, to the competent unit that drew them up in order to be entered into the taxpayer's account by the competent department.

The competent department shall deposit the copies of the assessment rolls signed with a live signature referred to in Article 73 of this Decision in accordance with the following:

- The assessment verification copy and the summary copy: the Directorate of Revenues.

- The collection copy: the competent collection department. The collection department may also obtain electronically ratified collection copies from the automation systems immediately upon their entry into the taxpayer's account.

- Immediately upon entering the roll into the taxpayer's account, the competent department shall print an assessment verification copy together with a summary copy, both electronically ratified, compare them with the copy signed with a live signature, stamp them with the seal of the department, and add them to the documents of the examination file.

- The competent departments shall deposit with the Directorate of Revenues the quarterly statement of the department's verified assessments accompanied by an assessment verification copy and an electronically ratified summary copy for each assessment roll or reduction roll, preparatory to depositing it with the Directorate of Public Accounting in accordance with the procedures established under Decree No. 3373/65.

The competent department shall deposit the copies of the collection orders signed with a live signature referred to in Article 73 of this Decision in accordance with the following:

- The assessment verification copy: kept in the competent department.

- The collection copy: the competent collection department.

The competent departments shall deposit with the Director of Revenues or the Director of Value Added Tax, each within his competence, the quarterly statement of the department's verified assessments accompanied by an electronically ratified assessment verification copy for each collection order,, preparatory to depositing it with the Directorate of Public Apportionment in accordance with the procedures established under Decree No. 3373/65.

Initial Environmental Examination:

(1) Where it appears that the proposed project requires an "Initial Environmental Examination", the project owner shall prepare and submit to the Ministry of Environment the "Initial Environmental Examination" report for his project in accordance with the information set out in Annex No. 6. The Ministry of Environment shall review and evaluate this report within a period of thirty days from the date of registration of the report in its registry and shall express its position:

أ. Either requesting the project owner to prepare an "Environmental Impact Assessment" report if its evaluation of the "Initial Environmental Examination" report shows that the proposed project is likely to have a significant adverse impact on the environment as a result of the construction, operation or decommissioning of the project, and if the project is a private project, a copy of this position shall be notified to the competent official administration;

ب. Or notifying the project owner that his project does not require an "Environmental Impact Assessment" study if its evaluation of the "Initial Environmental Examination" report shows that the project is unlikely to have a significant adverse impact on the environment, provided that the project owner complies with the mechanism of the "Environmental Management Plan" in accordance with Article Eleven of this Decree, and if the project is a private project, a copy of this position shall be notified to the competent official administration;

ت. Or requesting the project owner to correct certain information or complete certain deficiencies; and the Ministry shall issue its position regarding the additional information submitted by the project owner within a period of thirty days from the date of registration of the information in its registry.

ث. In the event that no reply is given by the Ministry of Environment within the time limit specified above, the project owner and the competent official administration shall have the right to consider that the project does not require an "Environmental Impact Assessment" study and to complete the project file.

(2) The review mechanism referred to in paragraph (1) of this Article shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Environment.

(3) The competent official administration shall issue a licence for a private project in light of the Ministry of Environment expressing its position regarding the "Initial Environmental Examination" for this project in accordance with paragraph (1) of this Article, except in the cases referred to in item (ث) of the same paragraph.

(4) Any official administration shall refrain from commencing the construction or operation of its proposed project before the Ministry of Environment expresses its position regarding the "Initial Environmental Examination" for this project in accordance with paragraph (1) of this Article, except in the cases referred to in item (ث) of the same paragraph.

Determining the Scope of the Environmental Impact Assessment:

(1) If it is established that the proposed project requires an "Environmental Impact Assessment" study, the project proponent shall determine, in coordination with the Ministry of Environment, the scope of the "Environmental Impact Assessment" for his project in accordance with the information set out in Annex No. 7.

(2) Upon notifying the project proponent that his project requires an "Environmental Impact Assessment" study, the Ministry of Environment shall request him to notify the stakeholders concerned with the project, whom the Ministry determines from among the list set out in Annex No. 5 in coordination with the project proponent, and the stamp of the concerned official authorities and the date of registration on a special document prepared for this purpose shall be deemed proof that the project proponent has notified them.

(3) The municipality (or the Governor or the District Commissioner in the absence of a municipality) within whose jurisdiction the project is located shall, upon being notified of the project, immediately proceed to announce it for the purpose of informing the public and publish the announcement on the public notice board and at the site of the property where the project will be established for a period of fifteen days, provided that the announcement includes that the proposed project requires an "Environmental Impact Assessment" study, and that it is up to the public to submit their observations. The municipality shall notify the Ministry of Environment of the date on which the publication of the announcement begins; and in the event that the municipality fails to publish the announcement, the right to publish the announcement by posting shall revert to the Ministry of Environment through the Mukhtar or other official employees.

(4) The Ministry of Environment shall allow the stakeholders to submit their written observations on the project at the Ministry of Environment within a period of one month from the date of publishing the announcement locally or notifying the concerned official authority, and the Ministry shall refer all observations to the project proponent

after screening and evaluating them during the review of the Environmental Impact Assessment report and expressing its position in accordance with Article Ten of this Decree.

(5) The project proponent shall submit to the Ministry of Environment the report relating to determining the scope of the "Environmental Impact Assessment" for his project and attach thereto copies of the observations sent to him and the comments received and the original minutes of the public discussion meetings or the original minutes of the bilateral meetings with the stakeholders.

(6) The Ministry of Environment shall, within a time limit of fifteen days from the date of registering the report relating to determining the scope of the "Environmental Impact Assessment" in its registry, express its position and notify it to the project proponent. This position may be to approve the report, or to approve it with specific modifications, or to request additional information. The Ministry shall express its position regarding the additional information submitted by the project proponent within a period of fifteen days from the date of its registration in its registry.

(7) In the event that no reply is given by the Ministry of Environment within the time limit specified above, the project proponent shall have the right to consider the report relating to determining the scope of the "Environmental Impact Assessment" as approved and to adhere to it when preparing the "Environmental Impact Assessment" report.

(8) The Ministry of Environment shall arrange a meeting to discuss its observations and its position, in the event that the project proponent requests so, and it shall have the right to invite any concerned person or institution it deems appropriate.

(9) The report relating to determining the scope of the "Environmental Impact Assessment" approved by the Ministry of Environment is prepared for the perusal of the public and the concerned authorities.

Preparation of the Environmental Impact Assessment Report:

(1) The project proponent shall be responsible for implementing the report relating to the scoping of the "Environmental Impact Assessment", which includes preparing the "Environmental Impact Assessment" report and submitting it to the Ministry of Environment in accordance with the information set out in Annex No. 8.

(2) The project proponent is also responsible for dealing, within the provisions of this Decree, with any environmental impact that was not mentioned in the report relating to the scoping of the "Environmental Impact Assessment" but whose existence became apparent during the stages of studying the project.

Review of the Environmental Impact Assessment Report:

(1) The Ministry of Environment shall review the "Environmental Impact Assessment" report and its conformity with the approved report relating to the scoping of the "Environmental Impact Assessment" within a period of two months from the date of registration of the "Environmental Impact Assessment" report in its registry. If the report is not in conformity with the approved report relating to the scoping of the "Environmental Impact Assessment", or if the project proponent has not carried out the additional studies referred to in paragraph (2) of Article Eight, the project proponent shall be requested to correct the information or complete the deficiencies and resubmit the report. The Ministry must review the additional or corrected information within a maximum period of two months from the date of registration of the information in its registry.

(2) In the event that no reply is issued by the Ministry of Environment within the time limit specified above, the project proponent and the competent official administration shall have the right to consider the "Environmental Impact Assessment" report approved and to complete the project file.

(3) The mechanism for conducting the review referred to in paragraph (1) of this Article shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Environment.

1 - The "Commission" shall convene after receiving the information from the concerned parties referred to in Article Seven above, or after receiving the information from the Lebanese or foreign official authorities.

2 - After evaluating and analysing the available information regarding the submitted case, the "Commission" shall take a decision either to take note or to conduct the necessary investigation thereon, particularly through auditing the accounts or operations or verifying the suspected funds. The "Commission" shall conduct its investigations through whomever it delegates from among its members or its concerned officials, or through its Secretary-General, or whomever it appoints from among the control commissioners, and each of those shall perform his duties subject to observing secrecy and without the provisions of the Law issued on 3/9/1956 relating to banking secrecy being invoked against him.

3 - And after completing the auditing and analysis work, the "Commission" shall take its decisions in accordance with the provisions of Clauses 2, 3 and 4 of Article Six of this Law.

4 - Upon deciding to lift banking secrecy from the concerned accounts and/or to freeze them definitively and/or deciding to request the continuation of the prohibition on disposing of the funds, the "Commission" shall send a certified true copy of its decision to each of the Cassation Public Prosecutor, the Higher Banking Commission in the person of its Chairman, the concerned party, and the parties concerned with this decision, whether local or foreign, either directly or through the authority through which the information was received.

5 - Where the Public Prosecutor before the Court of Cassation decides to close the file in money laundering cases and not to proceed with the public prosecution, the frozen accounts and all other funds shall be deemed released, and the decision to close the file shall be notified to the "Special Investigation Commission", and the "Commission" may not maintain the lifting of banking secrecy, the freezing, and the prohibition on disposing of the funds, and it must immediately notify the banks and the other concerned parties thereof. If it appears to it, before executing the decision, that there is new evidence or presumptions that would justify maintaining the freezing, the prohibition on disposing of the funds, and the lifting of banking secrecy, the "Commission" must send a reasoned report accompanied by the documents containing such evidence or presumptions to the Public Prosecutor before the Court of Cassation, who may decide, where necessary, to expand the investigation in light of these findings.

6 - And where a final decision barring trial is issued by the Investigating Judge or by the Indictment Chamber, as well as where a final judgment or decision dismissing the prosecution or of acquittal is issued in respect of the holders of the frozen accounts and the funds prohibited from being disposed of, the accounts and funds shall become released, and a copy of the issued judgment or decision shall be notified to the "Special Investigation Commission" through the Public Prosecutor before the Court of Cassation, and the "Commission" must notify the judgment or decision to the banks and the other concerned parties thereof, and the "Commission" shall no longer be entitled to lift banking secrecy anew or to reinstate the freezing and the prohibition on disposal in respect of the accounts and funds covered by the decision barring trial except by following the mechanism provided for in Article 127 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

The Chairman of the "Commission" or whoever he delegates may communicate directly with all Lebanese or foreign authorities (judicial - administrative - financial and security) in order to request information or inspect the details of investigations they may have conducted regarding matters related or connected to investigations being conducted by the "Commission". The concerned Lebanese authorities shall respond to the request for information immediately without invoking any obligation of secrecy against the "Commission".

The Chairman of the "Commission" or whoever he delegates may directly request from the concerned parties referred to in Articles Four and Five to provide the "Commission" with all the documents and information necessary to carry out its duties, and these parties shall respond to this request within a reasonable time limit.

Those bound by the reporting obligation and the members of their boards of directors, their officers and their employees are prohibited from disclosing or hinting to anyone about the submission or the intention to submit a report on a suspicious transaction or relevant information to the "Special Investigation Commission", or about the "Commission" making inquiries on clients or auditing their transactions or their accounts.

Each of the Chairman of the "Commission", its members, and the personnel working for it or delegated by it shall enjoy immunity within the scope of their work such that neither they nor any one of them may be sued or prosecuted under any civil or criminal liability relating to the performance by any of them of his duties, including the offences provided for in the Law issued on 3/9/1956 relating to Banking Secrecy, except in the event of disclosure of banking secrecy.

The concerned parties referred to in Articles Four and Five and the personnel working for them, as well as the inspectors working for the Banking Control Commission and the auditors, shall also enjoy the same immunity when performing the obligations incumbent upon them pursuant to this Law or pursuant to the decisions of the "Commission", and in particular when notifying the "Commission" in good faith of the details of transactions that they suspect to be related to money laundering or terror financing.

Any person who violates the provisions of Articles 4, 5, 7, 10 and 11 of this Law shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to one year and by a fine not exceeding one hundred million Lebanese Pounds, or by either of these two penalties.

The "Commission" may address a warning to the entities that violate the provisions of the regulatory texts issued in application of the provisions of this Law, and may request regular reports from them on the measures they take to rectify their situation, and it may also refer these entities to the Higher Banking Commission with respect to those concerned in Article 4 and correspond with the tutelage or supervisory authorities regarding the violators concerned in Article 5.

The Higher Banking Commission may impose a financial fine on those referred to it for failing to comply with the regulatory texts issued in application of the provisions of this Law, provided that it does not exceed two hundred times the official minimum wage, and such fines shall be collected in favour of the Banque du Liban.

The foregoing shall not preclude the application of the administrative sanctions provided for in Article 208 of the Code of Money and Credit with respect to those concerned referred to in Article 4, nor shall it preclude the application of the sanctions provided for in other laws or regulations with respect to those concerned referred to in Article 5.

Movable and immovable property proven by a final judgment to be related to, or derived from, an offence of money laundering or terrorist financing shall be confiscated in favour of the State, unless the owners thereof prove, judicially, their legitimate rights thereto.

Confiscated property may be shared with other States where the confiscation results directly from coordinated investigations or cooperation carried out between the concerned Lebanese authorities and the concerned foreign authority or authorities.

There is hereby put into effect the urgent draft law referred to the Chamber of Deputies pursuant to Decree No. 1184 dated 20/4/1978, aiming at the organisation of the Customs Force, the text of which follows:
This Decree shall be published and notified wherever required, and shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The Customs Force is an armed public force within the Customs Administration; in this capacity, it is subject to the authority of the Minister of Finance, and its duties are defined as follows:

1 - Surveillance of the land, maritime, and air borders and all other places subject to customs control, for the purpose of enforcing customs laws and regulations and the various provisions governing the entry, exportation, and possession of goods.

2 - Investigating and ascertaining smuggling, in accordance with what is provided for in the Customs Code and other regulations, and setting up checkpoints and searching persons.

3 - Assisting the administrative corps in the Customs.

4 - Supporting all armed public forces and official administrations, in accordance with the procedures and cases provided for in the laws in force.

The Customs Force shall be composed of regional commands, branches, detachments, a technical apparatus, and an administrative apparatus, and the designation "Men of the Customs Force" shall be applied to all members of these forces, whether they are officers, non-commissioned officers, or rank-and-file personnel.

The command organs in the Customs Force are:

1 - The Higher Council of Customs.

2 - The Director General of Customs.

3 - The Heads of the Customs Regions.

There shall be attached to the Directorate General of Customs an officer holding at least the rank of lieutenant colonel, designated as the "Inspecting Officer", whose duty shall be to assist the Director General in all matters relating to the Customs Force.

An officer of a lower rank may be assigned to this duty if an officer holding the rank of lieutenant colonel is not available the establishment.

There shall be attached to the Inspection Service at the Higher Council of Customs an officer holding at least the rank of lieutenant colonel, who shall exercise his duties in accordance with the laws and regulations governing this Service with respect to the Customs Force, and an officer of a lower rank may be assigned to this duty if an officer holding the rank of lieutenant colonel is not available in the establishment.

The Regional Commands:

They are the highest echelons in the hierarchy of the Force sectors in the customs regions, and each of them shall be headed by a regional officer holding at least the rank of lieutenant colonel who reports to the Head of the Region. An officer of a lower rank may be assigned to this duty if an officer holding the rank of lieutenant colonel is not available in the establishment.
The Regional Customs Brigade shall comprise a group of sections, each headed by an officer holding the rank of major or below, who shall report directly to the Head of the Regional Customs Brigade.
The section shall comprise a group of detachments, each headed by a non-commissioned officer holding at least the rank of sergeant, who shall report directly to the Head of the Section.

1) - The general establishment of the Customs Brigade, as well as its materiel and equipment, shall be determined by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance after consulting the Higher Council of Customs.

2) - Regional Customs Brigades shall be established and abolished by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance after consulting the Higher Council of Customs.

3) - Sections and detachments shall be established and abolished by a decision of the Higher Council of Customs after consulting the Director General of Customs, within the limits of the establishment.

The uniform regulations of the Customs Brigade shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Finance following the approval of the Council of Ministers and upon the proposal of the Higher Council of Customs after consulting the Director General of Customs.

Members of the Customs Brigade shall remain continuously at the disposal of the service, provided that the Higher Council of Customs, upon the proposal of the Director General of Customs, determines the working regime for such members.

As for the manner of implementation, it shall be determined by instructions from the Director General of Customs.

Evaluations and grades reflecting their disciplinary and professional standing shall be drawn up annually for the members of the Customs Brigade, in accordance with rules laid down by the Higher Council of Customs by a decision issued thereby after consulting the Director General of Customs. Such evaluations and grades shall be taken into consideration in all matters relating to the status of these members.

The Head of the Regional Customs Brigade shall be responsible for the administration and command of the forces placed under his authority, and for the conduct of work in the sections and detachments subordinate to him.

The hierarchy of ranks for non-officers shall be as follows:

- Trainee Guard, Trainee Maritime Guard, Trainee Technical Guard.

- Guard, Maritime Guard, Administrative Guard, Technical Guard.

- Corporal, Maritime Corporal, Administrative Corporal, Technical Corporal.

- Sergeant, Maritime Sergeant, Administrative Sergeant, Technical Sergeant.

- First Sergeant, Maritime First Sergeant, Administrative First Sergeant, Technical First Sergeant.

- Adjutant, Maritime Adjutant, Administrative Adjutant, Technical Adjutant.

- First Adjutant, Maritime First Adjutant, Administrative First Adjutant, Technical First Adjutant.

- Warrant Officer, Maritime Warrant Officer, Administrative Warrant Officer, Technical Warrant Officer.

- First Warrant Officer, Maritime First Warrant Officer, Administrative First Warrant Officer, Technical First Warrant Officer.

Corporals, Sergeants, First Sergeants, Adjutants, First Adjutants, Warrant Officers, and First Warrant Officers shall constitute the category of non-commissioned officers.

Guards shall constitute the category of enlisted personnel.

Administrative non-commissioned officers and guards shall constitute the personnel of the administrative corps.

Non-commissioned officers and guards who are mechanics, drivers, carpenters, and radar and wireless operators shall constitute the personnel of the technical corps.

Every non-commissioned officer shall have the right of command over his subordinates.

However, if ranks are equal, the right of command shall vest in the one with greater seniority in rank; if seniority in rank is equal, seniority in the preceding rank shall be observed, and so on successively down to the lowest rank. If seniority is equal even in the lowest rank, the right of command shall vest in the one with greater seniority in service.

Customs guards shall be recruited from among Lebanese nationals by way of enlistment in accordance with the conditions set forth in the following articles; their appointment shall be decided by a decision of the Higher Council of Customs within the limits of the establishment tables and the value of the appropriations allocated in the budget, and their enlistment contracts shall be signed by the Director General of Customs.
Every vehicle must have a driver.

1- Draught, pack or riding animals and single livestock or herds must have a number of drivers in accordance with the following rate: a - For ten heads of sheep and goats and under or three heads of cattle and others and under: at least one driver b - From eleven up to twenty heads of sheep and goats or from four up to ten heads of cattle and others: at least two drivers c - For every fifty heads of sheep and goats or for every twenty heads of cattle and others exceeding the preceding rates: one additional driver 2- It is prohibited to leave animals straying on the public road, and it is also prohibited for herds of livestock to stand on the public road, and their driving must be organised in a manner that makes crossing or overtaking them possible without obstructing traffic.

The driver of a vehicle or of animals, in the case of normal traffic, must keep to the right side of the carriageway and must keep to the extreme right thereof in the following cases: First: when another user approaches him from the opposite direction. Second: when another user wishes to overtake him, Third: when visibility of the road ahead is insufficient. Fourth: when the speed of his car is below the speed in force on the road, especially on a mountain road.

1- Where the carriageway is divided into two lanes demarcated by continuous lines, it is prohibited for a driver proceeding in either of the two lanes to cross these lines or to drive upon them. 2- Where the carriageway is divided into two lanes demarcated by broken lines, the driver shall, under normal driving conditions, use the right-hand lane, and shall not cross the lines except for the purpose of overtaking in accordance with the provisions of Chapter Three of this Title. 3- Where the lane is demarcated by a broken line adjacent to a continuous line, it is prohibited for the driver to cross this continuous line where it is immediately to his left. However, if the broken line is the one immediately to his left, he may then cross the continuous line. 4- Where a single lane is divided into several sub-lanes, it is strictly prohibited to cross the divider between one lane and another, and the sub-lanes of the other lane shall in all cases be left for traffic moving in the opposite direction. 5- Where a single lane is divided into several sub-lanes, it is permissible to drive abreast in one direction on the sub-lanes of the single lane, provided that slow-moving motor vehicles keep to the sub-lane situated on the far right, except when preparing to leave the road in order to take another road situated to the left, after ensuring that such preparation does not constitute a danger to others and after warning other road users thereof. 6- Where a section of the public road is allocated to a specific category of users, it shall be mandatory for this category to keep to it and for the remaining categories to avoid it. 7- Sidewalks, where they exist, shall be allocated to the following categories: a - Pedestrians b - Hand-pushed carriages for children, the sick, and the disabled, and it is prohibited to place anything on the sidewalks that impedes the movement of users.

A driver who prepares to make a significant change in the speed of his vehicle or animals or in the direction thereof shall ascertain in advance that it is possible to do so without danger and shall warn other road users thereof.

A driver who is preparing to exit a building or a property located alongside the road shall not enter this road until after he has ascertained the possibility of doing so without danger, and he shall also enter it slowly so as to enable him to stop immediately where necessary. b - A driver shall reduce his speed or stop to allow the passage of blind and crippled persons. c - A driver shall not obstruct the movement of other vehicles and the rest of the users of the road and shall not apply the brakes suddenly except on grounds of safety. d - Drivers of motor vehicles whose authorised gross weight exceeds (3000) three thousand kilograms shall leave between themselves and motor vehicles of the same category preceding them while driving outside built-up areas a distance of not less than fifty metres.

It is prohibited: 1- For anyone whomsoever: - To cut through the ranks of military troops, security forces and processions of all kinds while they are in motion. 1- To cling to the exterior parts of a vehicle and to board the vehicle or alight therefrom while it is in motion. 2- For drivers of motorcycles and ordinary bicycles to use other vehicles in order to tow their cycles. 3- For drivers of vehicles: - To stop the engines of their vehicles from running for the purpose of coasting them down slopes by the force of their momentum. - To drive side by side on a single-carriageway road except in the event of overtaking and to perform a turning manoeuvre (U-turn) in the middle of the public road within built-up areas. 4- For drivers of public-hire transport vehicles: - To loiter in their driving in order to solicit passengers. - To demand fares exceeding the prescribed tariff, or to charge any waiting fare for the duration required by the vehicle for repair as a result of a breakdown that occurred to it during its driving. 5- To use wheeled sports skates on the public road 6- To wash vehicles on the public road or repair them thereon except in cases of extreme necessity.

If there stands on a carriageway, a square or a road intersection a building, a monument, a vestige or a roundabout that prevents a vehicle from continuing in a straight line, the driver shall go around it with his vehicle on the right-hand side, unless there are instructions to the contrary.

The driver of a vehicle or of animals shall drive them with full vigilance and shall always remain in control of their speed and shall determine such speed in relation to the difficulties of traffic or probable obstacles, provided that he reduces it in particular: First: When passing through inhabited areas. Second: Outside inhabited areas. - If the road appears to him not to be clear. - If visibility is insufficient - On bends, slopes and congested sections of roads, or those on both sides of which residential houses stand, and at road junctions, and when approaching the crest of a rise. - When meeting a group of pedestrians (civilian or military) in motion, or at a standstill, or when overtaking it, - When meeting draught, pack or riding animals or livestock or when overtaking them

1- The driver shall not exceed the maximum speed or drive below the minimum speed specified in the regulations in force, with the exception of drivers of vehicles of the security forces, the fire brigade and the ambulance service when carrying out a mission requiring rapid intervention, as well as any driver of a motor vehicle transporting an injured person in a state of danger. 2- Drivers of vehicles whose maximum speed is below the speed posted on the roads are prohibited from entering these roads or driving on them.
Passing oncoming traffic shall take place on the right and overtaking on the left
The driver, when passing oncoming traffic, shall keep to the right side of the road insofar as the presence of other road users thereon permits.

1- The driver, before commencing to overtake, shall ascertain that it can be carried out without danger and that he has sufficient space therefor, and that the drivers following him have not yet begun a similar overtaking manoeuvre, and he shall, where necessary - subject to the traffic measures that may be taken within inhabited areas pursuant to the provisions of Article (35) of this Law - warn the road user whom he intends to overtake. 2- The driver may not, when overtaking, use the left half of the carriageway unless that does not impede those travelling in the opposite direction.

1- A vehicle is permitted to tow one trailer or semi-trailer provided that the trailer is of the same category as the towing vehicle. 2- Passenger cars are prohibited from towing trailers for commercial, industrial or agricultural purposes, with the exception of trailers prepared for excursions, tourism, hunting and the like for personal use. 3- Freight vehicles specially designed to tow trailers are permitted to tow only one additional semi-trailer designated for the transport of loads. 4- Buses are prohibited from towing any trailer or semi-trailer whatever the reasons may be. 5- Vehicles are exceptionally permitted to tow behind them, on the responsibility of their owner, another broken-down vehicle, provided that such towing takes place on a single trip, that the towing vehicle has an engine power not less than the engine power of the towed vehicle, that in all cases the towing vehicle and the towed vehicle are completely free of loads and persons except for the driver, and that its maximum speed does not exceed thirty kilometres per hour.

1- Where the need arises to transport or move indivisible pieces, or agricultural or public works equipment, or motor vehicles or trailers designed to transport indivisible pieces, and their dimensions or weights exceed the regulatory limits, the Motor Vehicles and Machinery Registration Service may license their circulation for a single journey or for several journeys according to the requirements. The license shall specify the roads and times to be followed and the measures to be taken to ensure traffic safety and to avoid causing damage to the roads, structures, and appurtenances of the public domain. 2- Agricultural vehicles and equipment not conforming to the provisions of Articles (62), (63), and (64) of this Law are permitted to cross public roads transversely from one side to the other in their operating areas, after ensuring that they do not obstruct traffic and do not pose a danger to the roads or to their users. 3- Public works vehicles and their equipment, and agricultural tractors equipped with a trailer, are prohibited from circulating on international and main roads while loaded. However, they are permitted to cross these roads transversely from one side to the other after ensuring that they do not obstruct traffic and do not pose a danger to the roads or to their users. 4- The Motor Vehicles and Machinery Registration Service is entitled to grant owners of agricultural vehicles with a trailer only an exceptional license authorizing them to circulate on a section of main and international roads while loaded with agricultural crops and materials and equipment necessary for agriculture for a distance not exceeding fifteen kilometers, provided that this license specifies the materials licensed to be transported, the itinerary, the times, the points of departure and arrival, and the validity period of the license, and that such transport takes place in all cases within agricultural areas and does not result in any obstruction of traffic. Such a license may be granted to transport a specific number of agricultural workers, provided that the transport does not take place on international roads and inside cities. The aforementioned agricultural areas shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Ministers of Interior and Agriculture.

Any person is prohibited from: - Throwing or leaving on the public road anything that would impede the movement of traffic or cause hazards, such as waste, dirt, stones, building materials, and others. - Causing damage to the public road by any means whatsoever, or digging a road for any reason without a prior license from the competent authority. - Placing on the public road or casting over it papers or objects by way of publicity and publication.

1- It shall not be permissible to hold any race, of whatever kind, on public roads, except after obtaining a special permit from the Minister of Interior specifying the conditions that must be complied with. 2- It shall be required in all cases, in races of motor cars and motorcycles, to produce an insurance contract against damage to third parties and their property.

1- Subject to the provisions of this Law, a special committee appointed by a decision of the Minister of Interior shall determine: - The authorised gross weight for each motor vehicle designed for carrying loads or for carrying more than eight persons or for drawing a trailer or semi-trailer, in proportion to the strength of the chassis of the vehicle, its tyres, the power of its engine and its mechanical apparatus. - The engine power of the vehicle in proportion to its model, the number of cylinders, their bore, and the stroke of the piston, provided that all of this is determined in accordance with the rules annexed to this Law. 2- The gross weight shall include the weight of the vehicle or combination of vehicles when unladen, and the weight of the load authorised to be carried therein. 3- The vehicle, or combination of vehicles, when unladen, shall consist of: - The chassis - The electric accumulator filled with water - The radiator of the motor car filled with water - One fuel tank fixed to the chassis when full - The bodywork (coachwork) - The complete upholstery of the bodywork if the vehicle is a motor car or an omnibus - One spare wheel - The lifting jack and the necessary tools usually delivered with the motor car placed in a normal moderate box. - A device for towing the motor car the weight of which does not exceed ten kilograms - An ordinary cover if the vehicle is open.
The weight of the vehicle, trailer or semi-trailer, when unladen, shall be the weight resulting from weighing it on a weighbridge, plus sixty-five kilograms as the weight of the driver.
The weighing operation shall be carried out by a committee appointed by a decision of the Minister of Interior, and its mission shall be defined by the said decision.
It shall not be permissible to put into circulation a vehicle the weight of which exceeds the gross weight determined for it and recorded in the circulation permit granted to it.

Subject to the provisions of Article (49) of this Law, the maximum gross weight for each vehicle or combination of vehicles shall be determined as follows: - A vehicle with two axles: 19 tonnes - A vehicle with three or more axles: 26 tonnes - A combination of vehicles consisting of a tractor vehicle and a trailer or semi-trailer: 35 tonnes Vehicles equipped with electric motors deriving their power from electric accumulators mounted thereon shall benefit from an additional weight of up to one tonne at most.
The most heavily loaded axle of a vehicle or of a combination of vehicles may not be loaded with more than fourteen tonnes.
The total weight of a vehicle or of a combination of vehicles may not exceed five tonnes for each metre separating the two extreme axles.

If the vehicle or the combination of vehicles has more than two axles, the load of the more heavily loaded axle of two consecutive axles shall be determined in accordance with the following rule: the distance between the two axles: ninety centimetres - maximum load 7350 kilos - and this - load shall be increased at the rate of - 350 kilos - for every five centimetres of increase in the distance between the two consecutive axles, provided that the load does not exceed the maximum limit specified in the preceding Article.
The wheels of vehicles and of their trailers must be fitted with pneumatic tyres or with other means deemed by the Administration to be of sufficient elasticity.

It is prohibited to fit metallic parts forming a projection on the surface of the tyres that touches the ground, with the exception of metallic chains specially designed for driving on snow-covered roads.

Subject to the provisions of Article (49) of this Law, the dimensions of a vehicle or of a combination of vehicles may not exceed the following limits: - Total width: two and a half metres - Length of a single vehicle with all projections except for the current collector and the rope retriever (trolleybus): eleven metres - Total length of a combination composed of a vehicle and a semi-trailer: fourteen metres - Total length of a combination composed of a drawing vehicle and its trailers with all projections: eighteen metres, provided that the length of the drawing vehicle or of the trailer (except for the drawing equipment) does not exceed eleven metres.

By way of exception to the rules set out in the preceding Article: 1- The length of a vehicle designed for the transport of passengers may exceed eleven metres, without exceeding twelve metres, provided that the length of the rear overhang of the body does not exceed the length of the rear of the frame (chassis) as delivered from its factory, and that it does not exceed six tenths of the distance existing between the two extreme axles, and in any case three and a half metres (the length of the current collector and the rope retriever in the trolleybus shall not be counted in these distances). 2- The Minister of the Interior may, in specific cases, and in order to ensure regular transport services, even in municipal areas, authorise the maximum length of a combination composed of a drawing vehicle and its trailers to be made twenty metres.

The Minister of the Interior shall determine by a decision from him the conditions for applying the provisions of Articles (69) and (70) of this Law and the cases in which a motor vehicle may be administratively stopped from circulation, and he may, where necessary with regard to electrical equipment, make it mandatory to fit an anti-interference device fulfilling specified technical conditions, and a special device on motorcycles that limits their noise.
A motor vehicle must be constructed in a manner that secures for its driver a sufficient field of vision to the front, the right, and the left, such that he is able to drive it in complete safety.

1- All glass, including the windscreen, must be made of a transparent material that does not cause wounds if shattered. 2- And the windscreen must not distort the shape of objects, and must not, in the event of breakage, prevent continuing to see the road clearly.
The windscreen must be equipped with an automatic windscreen wiper the field of operation of which allows the driver to see the road clearly from his seat.
Every motor vehicle whose weight exceeds 350 kilograms must have a reversing device.
A motor vehicle must be equipped with at least one rear-view mirror placed in a manner that allows the driver to see the road at the rear of the vehicle.

The Minister of the Interior shall determine by a decision from him the categories of vehicles that must be fitted, having regard to their weight, their dimensions, or their shape, with a special apparatus of an approved type that enables the driver to hear the warnings of road users who wish to overtake him. And this decision shall determine the conditions for applying the provisions of this Article.

1- A motor vehicle must be fitted with a speed-indicating device, which shall always be in good working order. 2- Motor vehicles designated by the Minister of the Interior must be fitted with a speed-recording device, which shall always be in good working order. - The tapes of this device shall be preserved for a period of at least two months and placed at the disposal of the competent officers where necessary. And the Minister of the Interior shall determine by a decision from him the specifications of the device, the conditions for its installation and inspection, and the maximum time limit necessary for executing the provisions of this paragraph.

A vehicle with three or more axles whose length exceeds eleven metres and which is currently in circulation may continue to circulate until a date determined by the Minister of the Interior by a decision issued by him.

1- All necessary precautions shall be taken to avoid any damage or danger that may result from the load of a motor vehicle or trailer. 2- Every load that exceeds, or may exceed, as a result of jolting, the external perimeter of the vehicle, shall be securely tied down, and its height shall not exceed three metres and eighty centimetres from the carriageway. 3- Every chain, load, cover, or movable or trailing accessory equipment shall be fastened to the vehicle in such a manner that it does not exceed, at any time, the external contour of the load, and does not touch the ground. 4- In all cases, the load shall be arranged in a manner that fully guarantees traffic safety and does not impair the continued stability of the motor vehicle on bends and slopes.

1- Subject to the provisions of Article (49) of this Law, the width of the load of a motor vehicle or trailer, including all its projections in any cross-section, may not exceed the width of the motor vehicle or trailer, and in all cases two and a half metres. 2- Furthermore, the height of the body of the vehicle or its load from the carriageway may not exceed six tenths of the length of its frame (the chassis).

If a vehicle or combination of vehicles is loaded with trees or other pieces of extended length, the length of the load may not, in any case, exceed the front end of the vehicle at the front; at the rear, however, it may exceed the rear end of the vehicle or the rear end of the trailer by up to two metres only, provided that it does not touch the public road.

1- Pieces of extended length shall be securely tied to one another and to the vehicle so that jolting does not cause such load to exceed the limit permitted in the preceding Article. 2- If the load of the motor vehicle consists of items that may fly off or scatter during its movement, it shall be covered with a tightly secured cover.
A motor vehicle may not emit smoke that harms public health or traffic safety or disturbs users of the road.

A motor vehicle may not cause noise that leads to disturbing users of the road or those adjacent to it. Engines shall be fitted with silencers that are always in good condition, provided that this device is manufactured in a manner that does not allow the driver, while the engine is running, to cut off or reduce its effectiveness, and free exhaust of gas is prohibited.

1- Brakes shall be required to have rapid effectiveness and sufficient power to stop and immobilise the vehicle or combination of vehicles even on the steepest gradients. 2- Every motor car and every motor vehicle or combination of vehicles must be equipped with two brakes, each independent of the other, which do not affect, when used, the direction of the vehicle or motor car while it is moving in a straight line, and at least one of which acts on parts technically fixed to the wheels. 3- The main brake shall be required to have its effectiveness in the wheels and to immobilise at least two-thirds of the weight of the motor car or motor vehicle when laden, and its effectiveness on firm or flat ground shall reach at least fifty per cent on each of the wheels. 4- The reserve brake shall be required to have its effectiveness in the wheels or in the drive shaft (transmission) and to remain mechanically engaged during the absence of the driver.
Single trailers shall be exempted from brakes, provided that their authorised total weight does not exceed 750 kilograms and does not exceed half the weight of the towing vehicle when unladen.
The Minister of Interior shall have the right to impose, by a decision issued by him, additional brakes other than those set forth in this Law.

Position lights - A motor car must be equipped at the front with two position lights, emitting forward a white or yellow light, visible at night, in clear weather, at a distance of 150 metres without dazzling the eyes of other drivers.

Driving lights - A motor car must be equipped at the front with two driving lights emitting forward a white or yellow light, illuminating the road at night, in clear weather, for a distance of at least one hundred metres.

Passing lights: 1- A motor car must be equipped at the front with two passing lights, emitting forward a white or yellow light, illuminating the road at night in clear weather, for a distance of at least thirty metres without dazzling the eyes of other drivers. 2- If any point of the projector of the passing light is more than forty centimetres distant from the extremity of the width of the motor car, the position lights must be lit together with the passing lights. 3- The lighting of the passing lights must result in the extinguishing of the driving lights automatically.
