Article 125: A - Buses shall be registered as private in the name of the following departments to meet their needs. 1- State departments, municipalities, and public institutions attached to the State or to municipalities. 2- International organisations. 3- Hospitals and scientific and charitable institutions, provided that each institution restricts the use of the vehicle to transporting the patients, employees, workers, pupils, or teachers who are in its care. 4- Airlines and travel and tourism agencies for the purpose of transporting their passengers with their luggage and their workers and employees from their centres to the airport and to the port and vice versa, and that without consideration. 5- First-class hotels, for their guests, workers, and employees within the areas determined by the Ministry of the Interior. 6- Factories and establishments whose number of employees and workers exceeds fifty, provided that their use is restricted to transporting them only, and that without consideration. 7- Officially licensed travel and tourism agencies that provide tourist services for the purpose of transporting tourists from Beirut or the land and air ports to archaeological and tourist sites in Lebanon and vice versa within conditions determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers, provided that the buses are equipped with air-conditioning units and "Pullman" seats. Provided that the specifications and equipment of the vehicles mentioned in this Article and others shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of the Interior, and the tariffs to be applied by a decision of the Minister of Public Works and Transport. 8- The use of these vehicles for a purpose other than that for which they are licensed is prohibited. B - Private buses shall also be registered in the name of the Lebanese State Railways and Public Transport Authority for Beirut and its Suburbs to provide public transport in return for a consideration. This registration shall not entitle the owners of public vehicles of any category whatsoever to claim any compensation.

The registration of buses as private in the name of establishments engaged in international transport is authorised under the following conditions: 1- That the operation of these vehicles be restricted to transporting passengers across continents or across the desert. 2- That the Ministry of Interior specify the technical features and mechanical equipment that must be available in the vehicle in order to ensure the safety and comfort of travellers. 3- That the routes which the vehicle must follow and the places where it is permitted to stop be specified in the circulation permit. 4- That the name of the relevant establishment be inscribed on the vehicle in large, visible, and clear letters in the Arabic language and in a foreign language (French or English) after the phrase "Prepared for transport across continents and across the desert". 5- That a traveller not be transported except after verifying that he holds a regular entry visa permitting disembarkation in the country of destination or in the place through which the means of transport passes, where applicable. 6- It is prohibited to use these vehicles for any purpose other than the authorised purpose.

Article 127: A goods vehicle shall be registered as private if transport therein takes place without consideration, and if it is allocated to the service of its owner to the exclusion of any other (whether a natural or legal person), provided that it is registered in his name. The following shall benefit from this registration: 1- State departments, municipalities, and public institutions attached to the State and to the municipalities. 2- International organisations and diplomatic and consular missions in Lebanon 3- Owners of industries, manual workshops, agricultural cooperatives, apiaries, and the like. 4- Concession holders, whether companies or individuals, 5- Owners of agricultural tractors, self-propelled agricultural mechanical machinery, and self-propelled and non-self-propelled drilling and excavation machinery, for the transport of the equipment or fuel necessary for their operation. 6- Farm owners and farmers within the conditions set forth in Article (129) of this Law. 7- Owners of animal pens. 8- Contractors with the State, municipalities, or public institutions attached to the State or to the municipalities in their works relating to their contracts, provided that they are registered with the Chambers of Commerce and that their financial qualification is not less than sixty thousand pounds. 9- Hospitals, scientific, charitable, and religious institutions, schools, and airlines, provided that the payload of the vehicle for each branch does not exceed two thousand kilos. 10- Owners of goods vehicles with refrigerated bodies specially prepared for preserving and transporting fruit, meat, fish, and other items. 11- Commercial establishments that distribute their goods to homes, other establishments, restaurants, and hotels, and owners of flower fields, provided that their net payload does not exceed one thousand kilograms and that in no case does their gross weight exceed three thousand kilograms, and provided that the shape of their body is prepared for the type of work to which they will be allocated. 12- Driving instructors licensed to teach driving licence students how to drive goods vehicles and buses, provided that the phrase: "Prepared for teaching the driving of goods vehicles and buses" is written in large letters on both sides of the vehicle's body. These vehicles must be insured against all risks. 13- It is prohibited to use these vehicles for a purpose other than that for which they are licensed.

Article 128: With the exception of private goods vehicles registered in accordance with the provisions of items (1) and (2) of Article (127), the registration of private goods vehicles shall be subject to an additional annual fee specified in the schedule annexed to this Law.

The maximum net payload of the motor vehicle or motor vehicles that may be registered in the name of farm owners and farmers shall be determined as follows: 1- Four tonnes, if the land is planted with fruit trees (even if not yet productive) or vegetables and its area ranges between five and fifteen hectares. 2- From four tonnes up to twelve tonnes, if the land is planted with fruit trees (even if not yet productive) or vegetables, and its area exceeds fifteen hectares. 3- Up to twelve tonnes, if the land is not planted with trees or not planted with vegetables, but is planted with cereals, and its area exceeds fifty hectares, and no motor vehicle or motor vehicles whose net payload exceeds the authorised payload may be registered.

The State, municipalities, public institutions subordinate to the State or to municipalities, concessionaires whether companies or individuals, farm owners, and agricultural cooperatives shall be authorised to transport workers in the beds of goods motor vehicles registered as private in their name, provided that they equip them with the necessary seats in accordance with the conditions determined by the competent department, and concessionaires whether companies or individuals, farm owners, and agricultural cooperatives shall insure the workers required to be transported for an amount of not less than five thousand pounds for each worker.

The registration of all private motor vehicles, with the exception of passenger motor vehicles provided for in the first paragraph of Article (124), shall be subject to prior approval from the competent department, which must verify the need therefor in accordance with the rules and conditions determined by the Administration for this purpose.

Owners of industries, manual workshops, commercial establishments, hotels, restaurants, cafés, owners of flower fields, apiaries, and the like mentioned in paragraphs (3) and (11) of Article (127) shall be authorised to use the private passenger motor vehicles registered in their name to transport their goods, provided that the payload does not exceed eighty kilograms and that it is subject to the authorisation referred to in Articles (131) and (134) of this Law. Owners of private passenger motor vehicles shall also be permitted to transport therein luggage or items belonging to them, provided that such transport does not have a commercial purpose and that visibility to the rear remains clearly unobstructed.
The route that a private bus must follow shall be specified in the circulation permit.
An ordinary bicycle must bear a serial number for the frame stamped by the factory, failing which it shall be stamped by means of cold punching by the competent Administration.
Ordinary bicycles shall be registered at the headquarters of the municipalities where their owners reside

The provisions of Articles 116 to 121 of this Law shall apply to the bicycles mentioned in this Title, provided that the registration application is submitted to the president of the competent municipality.

An ordinary bicycle must bear a serial registration plate affixed to its rear in a manner that renders it constantly visible to the eye and stamped with the official stamp by the municipality to which it belongs.
The provisions of the third paragraph of Article 99 of this Law shall apply to the bicycles mentioned in this Title, and a single registration plate affixed to the rear of the bicycle shall suffice.
The Minister of the Interior shall determine, by a decision issued by him, the model of the registration plates and the conditions for placing them.

Except for the cases set forth in Articles 49 and 246 of this Law, there may not be hitched: 1- To vehicles used for the transport of goods: more than five horses or draught animals if the vehicle is two-wheeled, and more than eight horses or other draught animals if the vehicle is four-wheeled, provided that in the latter case there are no more than five animals in file. 2- To vehicles used for the transport of persons, more than three horses if the vehicle is two-wheeled and more than six if the vehicle is four-wheeled.
If the number of draught animals exceeds six or is more than five animals in file, an assistant must be added to the driver.

The provisions of the first paragraph of Article 243 relating to the limitation of the number of animals shall not apply to sections of roads where the gradient is steep or where the length of the gradient is exceptional.
A single driver may drive a convoy of animal-drawn vehicles, provided that the number of such vehicles does not exceed three.
If the driver is not walking on foot, he must be on the first vehicle.
If the convoy consists of two vehicles only, the number of draught animals may not exceed four for the first vehicle and two for the second vehicle.
If the convoy consists of three vehicles, the first vehicle only may be drawn by two animals, and each of the second and third vehicles must be drawn by a single animal.

The animals drawing the second vehicle and the third vehicle must be tethered to the rear of the preceding vehicle in a manner that keeps the cart they draw from deviating appreciably from the line along which the preceding cart travels.

If the wheels of animal-drawn vehicles are not fitted with rubber tyres, their pressure on the ground must not exceed, at any time, one hundred and fifty kilograms per centimetre of the width of the tyre.

There must not be any protrusion on the surface of metallic tyres in contact with the ground, and it is also prohibited to insert into the flat surfaces of the tyres metallic parts that form a protrusion.

The provisions of the first paragraph of Article 62 of this Law shall apply to animal-drawn vehicles; otherwise, in every animal-drawn vehicle whose body or mudguard does not project beyond the wheel, the most projecting part of the end of its axle, the hub of its wheel, its braking mechanisms, and all its additional parts must not project by more than twenty centimetres beyond the plane passing through the outer rim of its tyre.

Article 257: 1- Animal-drawn vehicles must carry at their rear, under the conditions set out in the first paragraph of Article 256, two devices reflecting or emitting a red light 2- If the length of the vehicle including the load exceeds six metres, or if its width exceeds two metres, these devices must be placed on the outer edges of the vehicle and it must also be equipped at its front with two devices placed at its outer edges and reflecting a white light to the front. 3- Handcarts must carry at their rear a device reflecting or emitting a red light placed on their left at a distance not exceeding forty centimetres from the outer edge of the cart including its load.

Article 258: 1- The lights and devices mentioned in Articles 256 and 257 must be fitted in a manner whereby no part of the vehicle or of its load can cause them to be concealed wholly or partially and consequently limit their effect. 2- Animal-drawn vehicles transporting trees or pieces extending beyond the rear of the vehicle must carry by day at the rear of the load a dark red flag measuring not less than 30x20 centimetres and by night a lamp emitting a non-dazzling red light.
Article 259: Animal-drawn vehicles and handcarts shall be registered at the office of the municipalities where their owners reside.

Article 260: 1- The provisions of Article 99 of this Law shall apply to the vehicles and carts mentioned in this Title. 2- And these vehicles or carts shall carry only one registration plate placed on the right side of their body, which the municipality shall stamp with its official stamp.
Article 261: The Minister of the Interior shall determine, by a decision issued by him, the model of the registration plates and the conditions for placing them.

Article 296: The value of immediate fines or fines paid within ten days from the date of the occurrence of the contravention pursuant to Article 279 shall be determined as follows: - For each contravention of the first category: 15 Lebanese pounds - For each contravention of the second category: 10 Lebanese pounds - For each contravention of the third category: 5 Lebanese pounds The payment of these fines shall result in the abatement of the public prosecution. The payment of fines paid within ten days shall take place at the seat of the court within the jurisdiction of which the contravention occurred, either directly or by virtue of a postal money order sent to the competent Single Judge.
Article 297: If another law punishes one of the acts punishable under this Law, the more severe penalty shall be applied.

The provisions of Articles 65 to 68 of this Law shall apply to animal-drawn vehicles. However, vehicles used for agricultural purposes shall not be subject to the provisions of Article 66 when operating in the transport of crops and straw or fodder between the field and the farm or between the field or the farm and the market of sale or the place of delivery, within a circle having a diameter of twenty-five kilometres.
An animal-drawn vehicle must be equipped with a special device for slowing down and stopping.

1- Animal-drawn vehicles must be equipped at night, and during the day when circumstances so require and especially in time of fog, with the following devices: - at the front, one or two lights emitting a white or yellow light forward. - at the rear, one or two lights emitting a red light to the rear. 2- These lights must be visible at night and in clear weather at a distance of one hundred and fifty metres, without dazzling the sight of other drivers. 3- Where there are two lights with white light or two lights with red light, they must be placed symmetrically in relation to the vehicle, and where there is only one white light, or one red light, it must be placed to the left of the vehicle while in motion, and on the side opposite the pavement or the side of the road when stationary. 4- However, the following vehicles may be signalled by a single light placed on the side opposite the pavement or the side of the road, and emitting a white light forward and a red light to the rear: - hand-drawn carts. - all animal-drawn vehicles having a single axle. - animal-drawn vehicles designated for an agricultural purpose. It must be mounted on the vehicle or carried by hand by an escort positioned immediately to the left of the vehicle. - all other animal-drawn vehicles when stationary, provided that their length does not exceed six metres. - when several animal-drawn vehicles are travelling as a convoy under the conditions specified in Articles 246 to 250, the first vehicle of each group composed of two or three consecutive vehicles without separation must be equipped with one or two lights (white or yellow) and the last vehicle with one red light or the two lights referred to above. As for the vehicle located in the middle, it shall be exempt from all lighting.

The Government may, upon the proposal of the Ministers of Interior and of Public Works and Transport, regulate by decrees enacted in the Council of Ministers the use of public roads inside and outside populated areas according to traffic developments.
The provisions of this Law shall not apply to vehicles operating on a railway line situated within the limits of a road.

1- The provisions of Articles 47 and 49 shall not apply to military convoys and transports subject to their own special regulations. 2- The technical rules provided for in Chapter One of Title Two (Articles 52 to 110) shall not apply to special vehicles and equipment belonging to the Army, the Navy, the Air Force and the Internal Security Forces, unless their technical characteristics relating to their manufacture and use so permit. 3- The administrative rules provided for in Articles (111 to 112) "Acceptance", (114 and 115) "Technical Inspection" and (116 to 121) "Registration" shall not apply to special vehicles and equipment belonging to the Army, the Navy, the Air Force and the Internal Security Forces that are subject to special registration and whose acceptance is carried out by the technical departments subordinate subordinate to National Defence and Internal Security. 4- The provisions of Article 143 (Driving Licences) shall not apply to drivers of military vehicles and Internal Security Forces vehicles holding a permit issued to them for this purpose by their competent authority 5- The provisions of Articles 65 to 68 (Load Measurement) shall not apply to special equipment of fire-fighting services except to the extent that their technical characteristics so permit.

Owners of industrial establishments whose establishments do not meet the conditions set forth in paragraph (6) of Article 125 of this Law are authorised to keep in circulation motor buses registered as private in their name prior to the date of 15 December 1952, provided that their use is restricted to transporting employees and workers to and from the factory and without any consideration of whatever kind. And lorries registered as private prior to 15 December 1952, contrary to the provisions of Article 55 of the Traffic Law issued on 25 June of the year 1949, are authorised to continue operating under the following conditions: - That their operation remain restricted to the purpose for which the private circulation permit was previously granted. - That the private circulation permit be permanently cancelled in the event of the destruction of the vehicle, its sale to a third party, or the cessation of the purpose for which the permit was granted.

1- Every person against whom a report is drawn up for one of the infractions mentioned in this Law and who wishes to object, shall declare so in the report drawn up against him in his presence or shall notify the competent court within ten days of his wish to object if the report was drawn up in his absence, and in all cases he shall not be entitled to exercise this right except after paying the amount of the imposed fine. 2- The person who has declared his wish to object in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph, shall submit, under penalty of forfeiture of his right to object, a petition in which he explains the grounds of his objection to the competent court within ten days from the date of occurrence of the infraction. This objection shall be exempted from every fee except the fiscal stamp duty. It may be sent to the competent court by registered mail. The petition submitted as stated in the preceding paragraph shall be considered as an objection to a judgment rendered according to summary procedures, and the provisions of Article 187 of the Code of Criminal Procedure shall apply thereto.

The court shall adjudge to the objector whose innocence is proven the refund of the value of the fine, and it may request the prosecution of those who drew up the report in the event it is convinced of their abuse of the authority granted to them, or their violation of the law, and this judgment shall not preclude the taking of disciplinary measures against them. As for the members of the Security Forces, the court may request their prosecution before the competent judiciary.

If the owner of a motor vehicle fails to present it for the mechanical inspection provided for in Article 114 in accordance with the decisions that specify the dates for presenting it for this inspection, a delay fine of 25 Lebanese Pounds shall be collected from him for each inspection in addition to the other penalties provided for in this Law unless he proves that the vehicle was attached or impounded or located outside the country.

In the event of the administrative impoundment of a vehicle, the vehicle shall remain detained under the authority of the direct authority of those who drew up the infraction report, and this authority may return the vehicle to circulation after the cessation of the causes that led to the impoundment.

The provisions of this Law shall not limit the authority granted to the Ministers of Public Works and Transport and of the Interior and the presidents of municipalities pursuant to the laws and regulations in force, to impose within their competences and whenever safety and public order require measures other than the measures provided for in this Law. Governors shall have the right to take the same measures within the scope of their governorates.

The Ministry of Public Works and Transport shall have the right to carry out on public roads and on their branches all the works necessary for installing traffic signs and publicity and advertising boards. For the purpose of executing these works on private properties, it shall benefit from the easements established in favour of concessionaires pursuant to Decision No. 145/S dated 11 June 1925 relating to the transmission of high-voltage electric power and pursuant to Decision No. 320 dated 16 May 1926 relating to the use of the waters of the public domain.
A general amnesty is granted for traffic contraventions committed before the twenty-sixth of October of the year 1967.

Legislative Decree No. 140 dated 12 June of the year 1959 is repealed, with the exception of the schedule of fees annexed thereto, which shall remain in force until 31 December of the year 1967 only. Consequently, all provisions contrary to this Law or inconsistent with its content are repealed, with the exception of the additional reconstruction fee, as from the date of publication of this Law in the Official Gazette. This repeal shall not give anyone whomsoever a right to object. The provisions of this Law shall apply to motor cars, motorcycles and motor vehicles registered before its publication.

This Law shall be published in the Official Gazette and its provisions shall apply as from the date of its publication, with the exception of the schedule of fees annexed thereto, which shall apply as from the first of January of the year 1968. And with the exception of the provisions of Article 308.

Operations for committing expenditures for supplies and works shall cease on 30 November of the year; however, they may be committed during the month of December if their execution is possible before the expiry of the year or in urgent emergency cases, the assessment of which shall rest with the competent Minister and the Minister of Finance.

No expenditure shall be committed to the account of a financial year prior to its commencement.

However, as of the first of October of each year, permanent expenditures whose continuation is required by the public interest may be committed to the account of the following year, within the limits of the appropriations allocated thereto in the budget of the current year, and during the period preceding the publication of the budget, such expenditures may also be committed after the commencement of the new year, within the limits of the appropriations allocated thereto in the budget of the preceding year.

Transactions of liquidation, ordering of payment, and payment may also be carried out during the relevant financial year.

1 Provisional twelfth budgets shall be drawn up on the basis of the permanent appropriations allocated in the budget of the preceding year, provided that permanent appropriations added thereto and dropped therefrom are taken into consideration.

(Paragraph added by Law No. 42/88 dated 23/6/88, Official Gazette 26 dated 30/6/88):

As for the appropriations of the budget reserve, the amounts transferred therefrom shall not be considered dropped.

2- The Government shall have the right to distribute, by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the competent Minister and the Minister of Finance, the total appropriations for construction and equipment in each provisional twelfth budget among the various public administrations in accordance with their needs, provided that it abides in this distribution by the appropriations allocated to each public administration in the draft budget of the current year.

3- (Paragraph added pursuant to Article 31 of the 1980 Budget Law):

- Prior to the ratification of the budget, the Government shall have the right, by decrees taken in the Council of Ministers, to transfer appropriations on the basis of the provisional twelfth rule from the budget reserve to fund the various items.

Every transaction leading to the commitment of an expenditure must be accompanied, prior to its signature, by the endorsement of the Controller of Expenditure Commitments.

However, in urgent emergency cases, the competent authority may proceed to commit the expenditure within the scope of the appropriations allocated thereto prior to obtaining the endorsement of the Controller of Expenditure Commitments, provided that it submits the transaction to him for regularisation within a period of one week at most from the date of commitment, with a statement of the reasons that justified its taking this measure, and the party committing the expenditure shall remain liable therefor until its commitment is legally regularised. An application for the reservation of the relevant appropriation (an expenditure commitment application) shall be attached to every transaction leading to the commitment of an expenditure.

The endorsement of the controller on the request for the reservation of an appropriation shall be deemed an endorsement of the transaction in respect of:

1- Expenditure committed by way of a statement or invoice in accordance with the provisions of the first paragraph of Article 151 of this Law.

2- Travel orders of employees.

3- Advancement in step of employees.

4- And in general, expenditure for which a lump-sum appropriation has been reserved in accordance with the provisions of the final paragraph of Article Sixty-Three of this Law.

The endorsement of the controller is of two types:

- Total, encompassing the value of the expenditure requested to be committed in its entirety.

- Partial, limited to a portion of the expenditure requested to be committed.

In the event of granting a partial endorsement, or in the event of refusing the endorsement, the controller must state the grounds for his decision. An endorsement shall not be deemed partial where it results in a reduction of the expenditure requested to be committed by reason of a material or arithmetical error.

1- If the central controller grants a partial endorsement, or refuses the endorsement, he must refer the transaction to the Minister of Finance. If the Minister of Finance concurs with his opinion, the competent Minister shall have the right to refer the matter to the Council of Ministers to decide thereon. If the Minister of Finance does not concur with the opinion of the aforementioned, the central controller must abide by the decision of the Minister, subject to the provisions of the Law of the Court of Accounts.

2- If the controller at one of the ministries grants a partial endorsement or refuses the endorsement, he must refer the transaction to the central controller. If the central controller concurs with his opinion, he shall refer the transaction to the Minister of Finance in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph.

If he does not concur, the controller must abide by the decision of the central controller.
The Council of Ministers may not approve the commitment of an expenditure which the controller refused to endorse due to the absence of a sufficient appropriation therefor.

The competent administration may seek the opinion of the controller assigned to it on its financial matters, and in particular on the draft budget and the requests for additional appropriations which it submits.

The authority competent to commit expenditure may request the increase or reduction of an expenditure previously committed, provided that all necessary documents are attached to the request for modification.

The liquidation of an expenditure is the verification that the debt has accrued against the State, the determination of its amount and its maturity, and that it has not lapsed by prescription or for any other reason.

Liquidation shall be undertaken by the competent accountant or by whomever is delegated to do so with the approval of his hierarchical superior.

The accountant of the Directorate of Public Finance shall undertake the liquidation of expenditures disbursed from the Title of Debts Due for Payment.

The request for reservation of the appropriation necessary for the commitment of expenditure shall be signed by the accountant of the competent administration or by the person whom he delegates for that purpose with the approval of his hierarchical superior.

Requests for reservation of appropriations shall be drawn up:

- For the entire year, if they relate to salaries, and similar staff expenditures.

- For three or six months, if they relate to other permanent expenditures.

- And a separate request shall be drawn up whenever necessary.

A provisional aggregate request may be drawn up for the reservation of the appropriation necessary for permanent expenditures whose nature does not permit a separate request to be drawn up for them each time.

1- The control of the commitment of expenditures shall be undertaken in the name of the Minister of Finance by:

- The Head of the Budget and Expenditure Control Department in the capacity of Central Controller of the Commitment of Expenditures.

- Controllers at the ministries representing the Central Controller.

2- The Central Controller may entrust his representation in certain ministries to employees subordinate to him who shall undertake the auditing of the transactions submitted to him. He may delegate to them some of his powers.

3- The procedures for controlling the commitment of expenditures shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance, and the powers of the controllers at the ministries shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Finance.

4- Controllers shall be distributed among the ministries by a decision of the Minister of Finance upon the proposal of the Director General.

A controller at one of the ministries may not commence his mission before having spent a training period of not less than three months in the Budget and Expenditure Control Department.

The purpose of the controller's audit is to verify the following two matters:

- The availability of the expenditure appropriation and the validity of its imputation.

- The conformity of the transaction with the laws and regulations in force, unless it is subject to the oversight of the Civil Service Board, in which case it shall only be audited from the financial standpoint.

The controller shall endorse the request for reservation of the appropriation and the transaction and return the documents to their source within five days at most from the date of their receipt by him. If this time limit expires without his having decided thereon, the competent administration may retrieve the transaction and execute it on his responsibility. However, if the controller needs to request written clarifications from the competent administration, he shall be granted a time limit of five days commencing from the date of receipt of these clarifications by him. This shall be for one time only. If the transaction is subject to the prior oversight of the Court of Accounts, the controller shall send it to it, prior to endorsement, accompanied by his opinion.

Amounts that have accrued against the State in favour of third parties during a specific financial year and have not been disbursed before the first of February of the following year, for whatever reason, shall be called expenditure of previous years.

A payment order may not be issued except after verifying the following matters:

1- That the expenditure commitment transaction bears the signature of the authority competent for the commitment and the visa of the Controller of Expenditure Commitments.

2- The conformity of the imputation of the expenditure with the commitment transaction.

3- The accuracy of the calculations of the expenditure.

4- The conformity of the liquidation transaction with the financial laws and regulations only.
A payment order shall be drawn up for each right holder when it is disbursed from a single item or a single paragraph.

The payment order shall be drawn up in the name of the creditor, even if he has appointed a proxy or a representative on his behalf to receive payment, and in the name of the heirs in the event of his death.

And it shall be drawn up in the name of the Head of the Treasury Department, if the State is the holder of the debt, and in the name of the competent accountant if the holder of the debt is a municipality or a public institution.

And it shall be drawn up in the name of the competent Governor if it relates to amounts belonging to villages that do not have municipalities, provided that the amount is deposited in trust in the name of the said Governor with the central accountant of the district.

A payment order may be drawn up:

1- In the name of a paymaster appointed by the competent administration, with respect to the salaries and expenses of employees, and retirement pensions.

2- In the name of the employee who paid the amount out of his own funds, with respect to transport fares and certain petty expenses.

3- In the name of the imprest holder, with respect to expenses that he pays out of the principal of the advance.

And, upon the request of the expropriating administration, payment orders relating to expropriation compensation may be drawn up in the name of the accountant of the district in which the expropriated real properties are located, or of the district adjacent thereto, provided that the conditions for paying such compensation are regulated by a decision of the Minister of Finance.

Attachment decisions and deeds of assignment relating to debts accrued against the State shall be notified to the authority competent to issue payment orders. No notification addressed to any other party shall be valid.

The said authority must reply within the legal time limit to the party that notified it of the attachment, and must record the attachment or assignment on the payment order before issuing it.
The authority competent to issue the payment order shall sign it and send it to the competent accountant to secure its payment.

If a payment order is lost, its holder shall be given a copy thereof, upon a request from him stating the reasons for the loss, and upon a written certificate from the central accountant that the payment order has not been paid and that he has taken note of the obligation not to pay it.

Liquidation shall be based on the documents capable of proving the debt.

These documents shall be determined, in respect of each kind of expenditure, by a decision of the Minister of Finance taken after seeking the opinion of the Court of Accounts, and published in the Official Gazette.

A statement certified by the head of the unit that undertook the execution of the expenditure shall suffice if such expenditure does not exceed 50,000 L.L.

The schedules issued by the Electronic Centre at the Directorate of Public Finance, and relating to salaries, wages, retirement pensions and their accessories, and monthly allowances of all kinds, shall be deemed liquidated, and shall not require the signature of the liquidators.

Where necessary, the details of the application of this paragraph shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Finance.

(This Article was amended pursuant to Decree Enforced ipso jure No. 977/2007, Article 35, and the amendment was not adopted)

1- Liquidation shall be carried out automatically, and if that is impossible, then upon the request of the creditor.

2- The liquidator must complete the liquidation within a time limit of five days at most from the date of his receipt of the supporting papers relating thereto.

3- The creditor shall have the right to request from the liquidator a certificate showing the date of submission of his request and a breakdown of the papers produced.
Liquidation shall be effected on the instrument containing the breakdown of the debt.
The ordering of the payment of an expenditure is the issuance of a payment order authorising the payment of its value.

1- The Head of the Expenditure Service at the Ministry of Finance shall undertake the issuance of payment orders, in the name of the Minister of Finance. This official may delegate some of his powers to officials subordinate to his service, provided that they are of the Third Category at least. He may also entrust his representation in certain ministries to officials from his service who shall undertake the local auditing of transactions and the preparation of payment orders.

2- Where necessary, the task of issuing payment orders in public administrations and governorates, with the exception of the Governorate of Beirut, may be entrusted to officials of the Third Category at least belonging to the cadre of the Ministry of Finance, provided that this is effected by a decree.

3- The payment orderer must complete the payment ordering transaction within a time limit of seven days from the date of its receipt by him, and this time limit shall be extended to ten days in respect of salary payment ordering transactions.

However, if the payment orderer needs to request written clarifications from the competent administration, he shall be granted a time limit of five days commencing from the date of his receipt of such clarifications, for one time only.

The ordering of the payment of the expenditures of the financial year may be continued until the date of 31 January of the following year, provided that they are recorded under the date of 31 December of the year to the account of which they were ordered to be paid.

A payment order shall become valid for payment following the endorsement of the Central Accountant, or of the person to whom he delegates the same with the approval of the competent Director General. This official shall:

A- Refuse the endorsement and return the payment order to its source with a statement of the reasons for the refusal in the following cases:

First- If the payment order does not bear at its foot the signature of the authority competent to issue it.

Second- If the supporting documents of the expenditure are not attached to the payment order.

Third- If the name of the creditor, the subject of the expenditure, or its amount does not conform to the supporting documents.

B- Complete the transaction and place the disbursement order pertaining to the payment order at the disposal of the competent administration within a period of three days from the date it is received by him.
The conditions for the payment of payment orders issued in the governorates shall be regulated by a decree enacted upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.
Payment orders shall be paid in cash from the treasury fund designated therein. Payment may also be made by means of a transfer to a bank account.
The salaries of employees for the month of January shall, exceptionally, be paid during the last ten days of the month of December.

Certain expenditures may be discharged without a prior payment order, provided that the payment order is drawn up subsequently by way of regularisation.

The expenditures that may be discharged in the manner set forth above are:

1- Salaries, wages and their ancillaries, retirement pensions, and allowances for holders of military decorations.

2- Ordinary petty expenditures, urgent expenditures, and other expenditures whose nature or the circumstances do not permit their direct payment by the ordinary method.

The conditions for discharging the expenditures set forth in the first paragraph of the preceding Article shall be regulated by decree.

As for the expenditures set forth in the second paragraph, they shall be discharged by means of permanent or contingency advances called budgetary advances, which shall be granted in accordance with the provisions of the following Articles within the appropriations allocated in the budget.

A permanent advance is that which is granted to public administrations to cover their recurring expenditures during the current year.

A contingency advance is that which is granted to public administrations or to a designated person to discharge an expenditure which, in principle, may not be renewed.

The permanent advance shall be managed by a custodian appointed by a decision of the Minister of Finance and the competent Minister.

This decision shall specify:

- The amount of the advance, which must equal in principle three times the anticipated monthly expenditures.

- The nature of the expenditures that may be paid out of the advance.

- The maximum time limit for submitting the supporting documents for the expenditures and for the final settlement of the advance, provided that this does not exceed 31 January of the following year at the latest.

- The name of the custodian of the advance, his duty station, and the nature of the surety that he may be required to provide, and the amount thereof.

The permanent advance shall be granted without prior endorsement from the Controller of Expenditure Commitments.

However, the custodian may not pay out of it any expenditures other than those that have been previously committed and liquidated in accordance with the rules.
The Central Accountant shall pay the permanent advance to the custodian pursuant to the decision providing for the granting thereof.

As amended by Law 193 dated 24/5/2000, Official Gazette 23 dated 1/6/2000

It is prohibited to produce the substances and preparations listed in the Second and Third Schedules, and it is also prohibited to manufacture, extract, prepare, convert, trade in, distribute by wholesale or by international trade, export, import and industrially use them unless such acts are carried out pursuant to a licence in the cases and within the conditions provided for in this Law and the objective thereof is restricted to their use for medical and scientific purposes.

Related texts :- The conditions and documents required to obtain a licence for the operations and establishments provided for in Law No. 673 dated 16/03/1998 and its amendments concerning Narcotic Drugs, Psychotropic Substances and Precursors

- The conditions and documents required to obtain registers for narcotic drugs and synthetic substances

By way of exception, a licence may be granted for the use in industry, and for purposes other than medical or scientific purposes, of the substances for which a licence is required, if the applicant for the licence proves:

- His ability to prevent the abuse thereof or their causing harmful effects.

- The impossibility of easily recovering and separating the controlled substances entering into their composition.

With the exception of those relating to manufacture, the provisions of this Law shall not apply to products manufactured in accordance with the conditions specified in this Article.

As amended by Law 193 dated 24/5/2000, Official Gazette 23 dated 1/6/2000

A licence for the operations provided for in Article 15 of this Law may only be granted pursuant to a decision by the Minister of Public Health. This licence shall be granted for a maximum period of one year, renewable.

As for the substances and preparations registered and circulated under a licence, if the licence holder submits an application for renewal at least sixty days prior to its expiry, the Minister of Health shall decide thereon before the expiry of the time limit, failing which the licence shall be deemed extended until a decision of refusal or acceptance is taken thereon by the Minister.

The licence mentioned in the preceding Article shall only be granted to the following:

- State institutions, scientific institutes and recognised scientific research centres whose specialisation requires the use of narcotic drugs

- Owners of laboratories for chemical, industrial, bacteriological, food or other analyses whose work requires the use of narcotic drugs

- Owners of factories and premises permitted to manufacture medicines into the composition of which narcotic drugs enter.

The cultivation of the opium poppy, the coca plant, the cannabis plant, and, in general, all plants from which narcotics are produced is prohibited, whether as seeds or in all stages of their growth.

The owner of the land, the person exploiting it, or the person occupying it in any capacity whatsoever shall be obliged to destroy the aforementioned plants if they sprout therein and their knowledge of the matter is established, under pain of prosecution.

Village guards and mukhtars shall notify the competent authorities of the presence of plants that have sprouted or been cultivated in their locality immediately upon their knowledge of the matter, under pain of liability.

In the event of the cultivation of these plants, the Public Prosecution shall, without awaiting the issuance of the judgment against the offender, destroy the crops by appropriate technical methods after taking samples and attaching them to the investigation record, and the Ministry of Finance shall collect the expenses of destruction from the offender in accordance with the procedures for the collection of public funds, or they shall be added to the costs of the action in the event of prosecution.

State institutions, scientific institutes, and recognised scientific research centres, to the exclusion of all others, may be licensed to cultivate prohibited plants for medical or scientific purposes, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers and under the conditions it sets, and after the lapse of five years from the issuance of this Law.

The plants, plant seeds, substances, and preparations listed in the First Schedule are prohibited, and it is prohibited to produce, manufacture, extract, prepare, transform, purchase, possess, hold, receive, acquire, own, use, dispense, display, transport, deliver, offer for sale, sell, distribute by wholesale or retail, exchange, assign gratuitously or for consideration, mediate and broker in respect thereof, send, ship, import, export, and traffic in them of whatever kind, and, in general, any act or measure of whatever kind relating thereto

All the acts mentioned above are also prohibited if they relate to equipment, instruments, or other materials, with the perpetrator's knowledge that they will be used or utilised in the production, manufacture, extraction, preparation, or transformation of the substances and preparations of the First Schedule.

The substances and preparations listed in the Second and Third Schedules and their preparations shall be subject to the provisions applicable to all substances and preparations used in human or veterinary medicine if they are consistent with the provisions of this Law.

All natural and legal persons and private and governmental institutions that carry out operations relating to the plants, substances and preparations subject to control measures provided for by this Law shall submit, within the limits of their competence, to the Minister of Public Health.

1- During the first week of each quarter of the year, a quarterly statement for the preceding quarter showing the incoming, the outgoing and the balance

remaining in their possession of the controlled substances and an aggregate statement of the operations they have carried out.

2- During the month of January of each year, a statement relating to the preceding calendar year showing the following:

- The quantities produced or manufactured of each substance and each preparation.

- The quantities used of each substance in the manufacture of other substances

covered by this Law or exempted preparations or substances not covered by this Law.

- The quantities consumed of each substance and each preparation, namely the quantities supplied therefrom for retail distribution or for use for medical purposes or in the field of scientific research.

- The quantities in stock of each substance and each preparation on the last day of the year to which the data relate.

The Minister of Public Health may, during the year, oblige the institutions to submit the data which he requests.

A licence may not be granted except to a pharmacist or to a legal person in the management or administration of which a pharmacist participates, and if the establishment has branches, it is required that a pharmacist undertake the technical management in each of them.

In all cases, the pharmacist shall be personally responsible for applying the measures specified in this Law and in the licence.

The granting of a licence shall be contingent upon verification of the moral and professional qualifications of the licence applicant and of any person responsible for fulfilling the obligations specified in this Law and in the licence, particularly the pharmacist, and in all cases a licence may not be granted to:

- A person sentenced to a felony penalty

- A person convicted of one of the offences provided for in this Law

- A person convicted of one of the infamous offences

- A person who has previously been disciplinarily dismissed from a public office for reasons dishonourable to integrity.

The licence shall be revoked ipso jure after it is granted if a final and binding judgment is issued for one of the offences mentioned above against its holder, and it shall also be revoked in the event that a final judgment is issued against one of the persons responsible with him if he is not replaced by another person approved by the authority that granted the licence. The last clause shall apply especially if the judgment is issued against the pharmacist who undertakes the technical management in the establishment.

An applicant for a licence to practise the operations provided for in Article 15 of this Law must submit an application to that effect to the Ministry of Public Health containing the particulars, papers and documents set out in the following Articles and all other additional documents determined by the Minister of Public Health.

In every licence application, the following shall be set out:

- If the applicant is a natural person: his name, his address, and a certificate proving his registration with the Order of Pharmacists

- If he is a legal person: the name and address of its director or its legal representative, the name and address of the pharmacist person who will undertake responsibility for fulfilling the obligations arising from the licence, and a certificate proving his registration with the Order of Pharmacists

- And in both of the preceding cases, the names and addresses of all persons appointed to carry out the licensed activities.
The following supplementary particulars specific to the nature of the activity for which a licence is requested shall be required in the licence application:

If the application is submitted for the purpose of manufacture or production, there shall be specified therein the location, the designations and quantities of the substances and other raw materials that will be used, as well as the substances, preparations and products that will be manufactured, the extraction and manufacturing procedures that will be followed, and the quantities of the substances, preparations and products intended to be produced, in addition to their composition and the entity to which they will be sent or delivered.

If the application is submitted for the use of the substances in industry for non-medical or non-scientific purposes, there shall be specified therein, in addition to what is set forth in the preceding Article, the operations for altering the natural properties of the substances and the other operations that will be used to prevent the manufactured products from becoming an object of abuse or a cause of producing harmful effects and to prevent it from being practically possible to recover and separate the prohibited substances.

Use of psychotropic substances in the hunting of animals: A list of the psychotropic substances listed in the Second and Third Schedules and their preparations that may be used in the hunting of animals, and the conditions of such use, shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Public Health.

The possession of the plants, substances and preparations listed in the Second and Third Schedules for any purpose whatsoever and in any form whatsoever is prohibited, except in the cases permitted by this Law.

All persons who have in their possession, for professional reasons and in accordance with the law, plants, substances, preparations or drugs listed in the Second Schedule shall be bound to keep them in accordance with the conditions determined by a decision of the Minister of Public Health in order to protect them from theft and all other forms of diversion.

Pharmacies, drug depots and drug factories must keep the substances and preparations of the Second and Third Schedules in special containers to which a label is affixed bearing the name of the substance and an indication that it is a narcotic drug.

These containers shall be kept inside a special, tightly locked cabinet bearing an inscription indicating its contents. The manager responsible for managing the aforementioned premises shall personally keep its key.

All persons who have narcotic drugs in their possession by virtue of the licence granted to them shall be bound to substantiate the quantities thereof that may be lost due to fire, theft or any other incident, while clarifying the circumstances that occur in their special registers, and he must immediately notify the competent authorities of any lost quantity.

A special register for narcotic drugs shall be established at the Ministry of Public Health, in which shall be entered all persons and bodies licensed to import, export, transport, manufacture and produce narcotic drugs and all other operations related thereto. For each natural or legal person holding a licence, a special file shall be organised in which shall be placed all documents, statements and records pertaining to him in respect of the narcotic drug operations that he carries out. The keeping of the register and the files shall be regulated by a decision of the Minister of Public Health.

1- Every person licensed to carry out operations relating to the purchase, dispensing, sale, export, or import of plants, substances, or preparations listed in the Second and Third Schedules shall record each operation upon its execution in a special register with numbered pages and initialled by the employee appointed by the Minister of Public Health; the entry shall include the date of the operation, the name and address of the person with whom it was conducted and his address, its type, the designation or composition and quantity of each product covered by it, the incoming and outgoing of this product, and all other information required by the Ministry of Public Health where necessary.

Leaving blank spaces in the register is prohibited, and scraping, crossing out, alteration, and addition are prohibited, and it must be presented to the inspector of the Ministry of Public Health upon every request.

2- Establishments that manufacture, convert, divide, or use for any purpose whatsoever the substances mentioned in this Article shall also enter in the register upon conducting each operation a statement of the quantity and nature of each substance used and each product obtained, with proof of the quantities lost as a result of the operations

3- There shall also be recorded in the register the quantities lost as a result of a fire, theft, or any other incident, with an explanation of the circumstances in which they occur, and the competent authorities shall be notified of the lost quantities immediately. These statements shall be entered in the register in a manner that allows showing the amount of stored quantities specifically.

4- The special register shall be retained for a period of ten years after the entry of the last relevant operation in order to be presented to the competent authorities upon request.

Upon dispensing drugs of the Second and Third Schedules to an individual by a pharmacist, a physician, or a veterinarian licensed to dispense drugs, it must be recorded immediately in the prescription register without leaving blank spaces or scraping, crossing out, altering, or adding, and it is required to record each drug dispensed under a different serial number, indicating the following:

- The name of the issuer of the medical prescription, his address, and his capacity

- The name of the patient and his address, or the name of the possessor of the animal and his address if the prescription is issued by a veterinarian

- The date of dispensing

- The proprietary name of the drug or the method of its preparation, the quantity dispensed, and if the dispensed drug or preparation belongs to the Second Schedule, the pharmacist must retain the medical prescription, and the name and address of the person presenting the medical prescription shall also be recorded in the register of medical prescriptions if he is not the patient, and if the bearer of the medical prescription is unknown to the pharmacist, the name of the authority that issued the identity card presented by him, the number of this document, and the date of its issuance shall be mentioned.

Every renewal of a medical prescription containing drugs listed in the Second and Third Schedules shall be recorded, and in all cases, a pharmacist shall sign the medical prescription, stamp it with the seal of the pharmacy, take the signature of its recipient thereon and his address, and also note the number and date of its entry in the register, and give its bearer, upon request, a copy thereof if it relates to drugs of the Second Schedule and was retained by the pharmacist, and mention thereon the amount of the quantity dispensed, the date of its dispensing, the signature of the pharmacist, and the seal of the pharmacy.

The registers and records of the pharmacist shall be kept for a period of ten years from the date of the last entry noted therein.

All persons and establishments that have in their possession for professional reasons plants, substances, preparations, or drugs listed in the Second and Third Schedules are obliged to conduct at least an annual inventory of the plants, substances, preparations, or drugs belonging to the Second and Third Schedules that are in their possession, and to prepare summary statements of the incoming quantities and the outgoing quantities.

License holders and pharmacies are obliged, upon selling their establishments or pharmacies, to conduct an inventory in the presence of the buyer of the plants, substances, preparations, or drugs belonging to the Second and Third Schedules, and to prepare a summary statement of the incoming quantities and the outgoing quantities thereof, and both the seller and the buyer shall sign the inventory list and the summary statement

Discrepancies appearing in the enumeration statements or between the results of such statements and the results of the inventory shall be submitted to the pharmacist inspector for ratification upon his first visit following the execution of the enumeration; provided, however, that he must be notified immediately if it appears that the discrepancy may result from theft, diversion or illicit use.

The provisions of Chapters I and II of Title IV of this Law shall apply to the manufacture of substances listed in Schedule IV, to the trading and wholesale distribution thereof, and to the international trading thereof.

Paragraph added pursuant to Law 272 dated 5/1/2001, Official Gazette 3 dated 11/1/2001

The provisions of this Law shall not apply to legally licensed industrial establishments holding an industrial certificate issued by the Ministry of Industry for the production and manufacture of the substances referred to in Schedule IV of this Law which are not used for medical or scientific purposes, provided that the import and export of such substances shall be subject to prior approval issued by the Ministry of Public Health following the approval of the Ministry of Industry in accordance with Articles 57 - 58 - 59 on a form of a model determined by the Ministry of Public Health, and provided that such establishments shall notify the Ministry of Public Health quarterly of their sales in the domestic and foreign markets, indicating the names and addresses of the purchasers in order to enable the Ministry of Public Health to exercise its supervision, and the consignment shall be delivered at Customs after the endorsement of the customs declaration by the Ministry of Public Health.

Export or import authorisations shall be refused if there are reasonable grounds to suspect that the consignment is intended for the illicit manufacture of narcotic drugs or psychotropic substances, and exported or imported consignments shall be required to bear accurate markings.
No person shall disclose economic, industrial or professional secrets or trade practices of which he becomes aware on the occasion of conducting an investigation or by virtue of his office.

Manufacturers, importers, exporters, wholesalers and retailers shall record in a numbered register endorsed by the Ministry of Public Health any purchase or sale of the substances listed in Schedule IV at the time the transaction is carried out, without leaving blank spaces and without erasure or alteration, and the entry shall state the date of the transaction, the designation of the product purchased or sold and its quantity, and the name, address and profession of the purchaser or seller; provided, however, that retailers shall not be bound to record the names of purchasers, and the registers shall be retained for a period of ten years following the entry of the last relevant transaction in order to be produced to the competent authorities upon their request.

Manufacturers, importers, wholesalers and retailers shall notify the competent security authorities of suspicious orders and operations, in particular by reason of the quantity of the substance purchased or ordered and the frequency of such orders and purchases, or by reason of the methods of payment or means of transport used.

If strong indications exist giving rise to suspicion that any of the substances listed in the Fourth Schedule is being prepared for use in the illicit manufacture of a narcotic drug or psychotropic substance, such substance shall be seized immediately until a judicial judgment is rendered in respect thereof.

The Minister of Public Health may, for purposes relating to medical or scientific research or to education, license a natural person to produce, manufacture, acquire, import, use or possess plants, substances or preparations listed in the First, Second and Third Schedules in quantities not exceeding the quantities necessary for the intended purpose, and the beneficiary of the licence shall be obliged to enter in a register kept for a period of ten years the quantities of plants, substances and preparations which he imports, acquires, manufactures, uses or transports, and the beneficiary shall be obliged to record in the register, in addition thereto, the dates of the operations and the names of his suppliers, and to submit to the Minister of Public Health an annual statement of the quantities used or destroyed and the quantities in stock.

All persons, private institutions, governmental institutions, and medical and scientific establishments carrying out activities or operations of any kind relating to the plants, substances, preparations or drugs covered by this Law shall be placed under the control and supervision of the Minister of Public Health, who shall in particular assign pharmacy inspectors to carry out regular inspections of establishments, premises, stocks and records at least once every year, and emergency inspections when necessary.

The boxes in which first-aid equipment is kept in public means of transport designated for international transport shall be subject to the same control and supervision.

Pharmacist inspectors and officers and non-commissioned officers of the Central Directorate for Combating Drugs shall pursue offences and establish them, and they may enter all places in which the operations mentioned in the preceding Article take place or may take place, and effect seizures and take samples of their own accord, and pharmacist inspectors may not enter private places, in particular those owned by persons not holding licences, and carry out the operations mentioned in the preceding paragraph except with the written consent of such persons or pursuant to a decision of the competent judicial authority, and in the event of suspicion of the occurrence of an offence, the file shall be referred to the competent Public Prosecution.

The persons concerned and the establishments and installations concerned shall be bound to provide all necessary facilities to the pharmacist inspectors and to the departments charged with investigations in order to enable them to perform their mission, in particular by facilitating the visitation of the professional premises belonging to them and the inspection of all documents relating to their professional activities.

The provisions of this Part shall apply to all plants and substances placed under control, and a distinction is made between:

- Highly dangerous substances represented by the plants and substances of the First and Second Schedules

- Dangerous substances represented by the plants and substances of the Third Schedule

- Precursors represented by the substances of the Fourth Schedule.

There shall be punished by hard labour for life and by a fine from twenty-five million to one hundred million pounds:

1- Every person who intentionally contravenes the prohibition provided for in the first paragraph of Article 11 (cultivation of prohibited plants which produce highly dangerous substances) and the prohibition provided for in Article 13 of this Law in its various forms and in respect of the substances and preparations of the First Schedule annexed to this Law.

Intent shall be deemed to be established when the perpetrator, accomplice or accessory knows that the substance upon which the act is committed is placed under control.

2- Every person who intentionally contravenes the prohibition provided for in Article 15 of this Law in its various forms set forth in the said Article, or contravenes the licence which authorises him to carry out the acts mentioned in this Article, in respect of the substances and preparations of the Second Schedule annexed to this Law.

The following persons shall be subject to the same penalties set forth in the preceding Article:

1- Whoever sells to another person high-risk drugs or offers them to him for his personal consumption in an unlawful manner

2- Whoever intentionally facilitates for others the use of high-risk substances in an unlawful manner, with or without consideration, and by any means whatsoever

3- Whoever manages, prepares or sets up, in return for consideration, a place for the abuse of high-risk narcotic drugs

4- Whoever owns, manages or, in any capacity, operates a hotel, furnished house, family boarding house, bar, restaurant, club, association, dance hall, cinema or theatre, or premises open to the public or used by the public, if he knowingly and outside the cases authorised by law permits the use of high-risk substances in the aforementioned establishments, in their annexes, or in the said premises

5- Whoever adds high-risk narcotic drugs to food or drink without the knowledge of the consumer thereof

6- Whoever is licensed to possess high-risk substances for use for a specific purpose and disposes of them, with or without consideration and in any capacity whatsoever, for other than that purpose

7- Whoever obtains or attempts to obtain high-risk narcotic drugs by means of fictitious medical prescriptions or those issued out of complaisance

8- Whoever intentionally writes medical prescriptions containing high-risk drugs out of complaisance, and whoever dispenses these drugs without a medical prescription or on the basis of a medical prescription knowing that it is fictitious issued out of complaisance

9- A physician who knowingly delivers to another person a medical prescription for high-risk substances for purposes other than medical treatment

10- Any laboratory director or pharmacist who uses for himself or delivers to another person high-risk substances delivered to him by virtue of his profession, or facilitates for another person the obtaining thereof by means of fictitious medical prescriptions or by any other unlawful means.

Any person who possesses, holds, or purchases a minimal quantity of a highly dangerous substance without a medical prescription and with the intent of use, where its minimal nature allows it to be considered as intended for personal consumption, shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to three years and by a fine from two million to five million pounds, and any person whose addiction to the use of this substance is proven and who does not comply with the treatment procedures provided for in Title Two (Part Two) of this Law shall be subject to the same penalty, and the convicted person may be granted a stay of execution of the imposed penalty or be exempted from its execution if he is a minor, is not a recidivist, or undertakes not to reoffend and submits to the treatment or care measures imposed by the court, and the penalty shall be aggravated if the perpetrator is a professional working in the health sector.

Shall be punished by hard labour for a term not exceeding five years and by a fine ranging between five and ten million pounds:

1- Any person who intentionally violates the prohibition provided for in Article 15 of this Law in its various forms set forth in the said Article, or violates the licence authorising him to perform the acts mentioned in this Article, with respect to the substances and preparations of Schedule Three annexed to this Law.

2- Any person who cultivates any of the plants that produce dangerous substances, or imports or exports them at any stage of their growth, or their seeds, with the intent of trafficking, other than in the cases licensed under this Law.

Any person who commits any of the acts set forth in Article 126 of this Law shall be punished by the same penalty set forth in the preceding Article if the matter relates to dangerous substances and drugs.

Subject to Article 94 of this Law, any person who possesses, holds, or purchases a minimal quantity of dangerous substances without a medical prescription and with the intent of use, where its minimal nature allows it to be considered as intended for personal consumption, shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years and by a fine from one million to three million pounds, and any person whose addiction to the use of this substance is proven shall be subject to the same penalty; the convicted person may be granted a stay of execution of the penalty or be exempted from its execution if he is a minor, is not a recidivist, or undertakes not to reoffend and submits to the treatment or care measures imposed by the court, and the penalty shall be aggravated if the perpetrator is a worker in the health sector.

Shall be punished by hard labour for life and by a fine from twenty-five million to one hundred million pounds whoever produces precursors, equipment or tools, or manufactures, imports, exports, transports, offers, sells, distributes or delivers them for any reason whatsoever, or with the intent of using them or employing them in the cultivation, production or manufacture of highly dangerous or dangerous narcotic drugs by unlawful means, or while knowing that they will be used for these purposes.

Shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year and a fine from two million to five million pounds:

1- The owner of the land, or whoever exploits it or occupies it in any capacity whatsoever, who knows of the existence of prohibited plants and fails to destroy them or report them (Article 11)

2- Village watchmen and mukhtars who know of the existence of prohibited plants that have grown or been cultivated in their locality and fail to report them to the authority (Article 11)

3- The persons named in Article 118 of this Law who fail to notify the competent security authorities of suspicious orders and operations.

Shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years and by a fine from three million to six million whoever submits false statements and information in the licence application that led to the granting of the licence to him, where the disclosure of the truth would have led to the refusal of this licence (Articles 23 to 28 inclusive and Articles 46, 51 and 58).

Shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years and by a fine from three million to six million pounds:

1- The pharmacist responsible for the technical management of the establishment who does not apply the measures provided for in the Law or in the licence (Article 19)

2- The pharmacist who is prohibited from managing the establishment and continues to do so, and the owner of the establishment where a judgment is issued against one of his responsible employees in the establishment that prevents him from working therein and who fails to replace him with a person approved by the authority that granted the licence (Article 21)

3- The licence holder who assigns it in violation of the provisions of Article 34 of this Law

4- The licence holder who violates any of the supervisory measures provided for in this Law for which no harsher penalty is provided.

Where the offence does not carry a more severe qualification, there shall be punished by the same penalty as the preceding Article anyone who, being every person licensed to possess narcotic substances or psychotropic substances, holds them in quantities exceeding those resulting from the multiplicity of required technical weighing operations or transfers from them, if he fails to record them in his ledgers and immediately notify the Ministry of Public Health thereof when the discrepancies exceed the following:

A- Ten per cent in quantities not exceeding one gram

B- Five per cent in quantities exceeding one gram and up to twenty-five grams, provided that the amount of tolerance does not exceed fifty centigrams

C- Two per cent in quantities exceeding twenty-five grams

D- Five per cent in liquid narcotic substances or psychotropic substances whatever their amount, and if it is proven to the court that the increase in discrepancies is intentional, the perpetrator shall be prosecuted for the relevant more severe offence, and every establishment that exceeds the quantity it is licensed to possess or manufacture (Articles 54 and 55) shall be punished by the same penalty as the preceding Article.

There shall be punished by temporary hard labour how much of whoever assaults one of the public officials charged with enforcing this Law or resists him with force or violence during the performance of his duty or by reason thereof, and the penalty shall be hard labour for life if the assault results in a permanent disability or a gross disfigurement that is unlikely to disappear or if the offender is one of the officers of the authority entrusted with maintaining security, and the penalty shall be death if the assault leads to the death of one of the persons, and there shall likewise be punished by death whoever intentionally kills one of the public officials charged with enforcing this Law during the performance of his duty or by reason thereof.

There shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years and by a fine from two million to five million Lebanese pounds anyone who proceeds to resist judicial police officers, pharmacist inspectors and agricultural engineers in any manner whatsoever to prevent them from performing their duties entrusted to them pursuant to this Law, and the employer shall be jointly and severally liable with his employees for the fine adjudicated even if he is not an accomplice with him.

There shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year and by a fine from one million to five million pounds anyone who discloses a secret contrary to what is required by Articles 116 and 203 of this Law.

Shall be punished with imprisonment from one month to one year and with a fine from one million to five million pounds:

1- Anyone who violates Article 85 by failing to include the required particulars on the labels under which the medicinal drugs are sold and on the labels and explanatory leaflets accompanying the packages prepared for retail distribution.

2- Anyone who violates Article 86 regarding the manner of transporting, dispatching and marking the substances and preparations of the Second and Third Schedules.

3- Anyone who violates the provisions of Article 84 regarding advertising the substances, preparations and medicinal drugs of the Second and Third Schedules to the general public and providing samples thereof to physicians or individuals.

4- A commercial carrier who neglects to take the measures provided for in Article 74 of this Law

5- Any owner of a consignment who violates the provisions of Article 71 of this Law.

Shall be punished with imprisonment from two months to two years and with a fine from two million up to six million pounds anyone who:

1- Draws up or dispenses a medical prescription that does not fulfil the legal conditions set forth in Articles 82, 87, 88, 89 and 90 of this Law or contrary thereto

2- Violates the provisions of Articles 76 and 77 of this Law in obtaining professional supplies
