3- Dispenses narcotic medicinal drugs that are unfit or expired (Article 79).

Shall be punished with imprisonment from one month to one year and with a fine from two million to five million pounds anyone who is licensed to practice one of the operations provided for in this Law and is obliged to keep registers and make entries, statements or inventories, or submit periodic or non-periodic declarations to the official authorities, and fails to do so or keeps or performs them contrary to the applicable rules (Articles 92, 99, 108, 109, 111, 112 and 117), and if the offence does not acquire a more severe qualification, the penalty shall be aggravated in the event of intentional manipulation, fraud, concealment, suppression, recidivism and the like.

Any person who drives a motorised land vehicle while under the influence of a high-risk narcotic drug which he has used illicitly shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to two years and by a fine from two million to five million pounds. The penalty shall be doubled if the vehicle is marine or aerial, or if the driver of the vehicle causes material damage; whereas if he causes bodily harm, the aggravating circumstances shall apply to the offence carrying the severest qualification of the criminal act which he has committed. In all the preceding cases, the court may order the withdrawal of the driving licence for a period ranging between three months and three years, and permanently in the event that he causes an accident resulting in mass death.

If security personnel suspect that the driver of a vehicle is under the influence of a high-risk narcotic drug and request him to submit to the detection and examination tests determined by the Minister of Public Health by a decision issued by him, he must comply or refrain from driving, failing which he shall be prosecuted in accordance with the preceding Article.

On Jurisdiction:

Further to the general provisions set forth in Articles 15, 16, 17, 20, 21 and 22 of the Penal Code, the Lebanese courts shall have jurisdiction to hear the offences provided for in this Law in the following cases:

- If the offence was committed within Lebanese territory, or if one of the acts constituting one of the elements of the offence was executed within this territory, even if the remaining acts were carried out in different countries.

- If the perpetrator of the offence is Lebanese or has permanent residence in Lebanese territory.

- If the perpetrator of the offence is present within Lebanese territory and has not been extradited.

- If the offence was committed on board an aircraft registered in Lebanon or a vessel carrying the Lebanese work.

- Subject to international agreements, if the offence was committed on board a vessel whose flag State has authorised the Lebanese authorities to search and inspect it and to take the appropriate measures, in the event of the discovery of evidence of participation in illicit trafficking, with respect to the vessel, the persons on board, and its cargo.

Attempt:

Every attempt to commit one of the felonies provided for in this Law shall render its perpetrator punishable in accordance with Articles 200 and 201, as amended, of the General Penal Code. Every attempt to commit one of the misdemeanours, as well as the disgraceful misdemeanours provided for in this Law, shall render its perpetrator punishable, notwithstanding the provisions of Article 202 of the General Penal Code. An attempt shall be deemed established by the mere carrying out of financial operations in preparation for the commission of the offence.

Material concurrence of offences:

If prosecution proceedings end in the conviction of an accused for committing several offences including one or more of the offences under this Law, or if separate proceedings have ended in one or more of the offences under this Law and the acts that led to the issuance of these two judgments were committed before the other judgment became final, judgment shall be passed for each of the prescribed penalties, and the custodial penalties adjudged shall be accumulated together within the scope of the maximum limit prescribed by law for the most severe offence.

On criminal participation:

The accomplice, the instigator and the accessory shall be punished with the same penalty prescribed for the principal offender in the offences provided for in this Law.

Exemption from and mitigation of penalty:

An accomplice and an accessory who spontaneously takes the initiative to notify the public authorities of the offence before they become aware of it and enables them to prevent its occurrence, identify the other accomplices, and seize the funds and resources that are the subject of the operation, even partially, shall be exempted from penalty

- An accomplice or accessory who provides information on the offence to the authorities after they become aware of it shall benefit from a mitigating excuse if such information leads to the arrest of the offenders or some of them, or to the uncovering of persons who participated in the offence and have ties to local or international criminal gangs.

The court may, if the person convicted of one of the offences of narcotic drugs and the funds and proceeds resulting therefrom is a foreigner, sentence him to permanent expulsion from the Lebanese territory, it is cases of felony and repeated misdemeanour, and deportation for a period ranging between one year and five years in cases of misdemeanour. The person sentenced to deportation shall be escorted to the border after the expiry of the prison penalty.

In addition to the penalties provided for in this Law, a sentence may be passed depriving the convicted person of practising the profession for a period equal to the period of the penalty of deprivation of liberty to which he is sentenced, and any violation of the judgment ordering deprivation of practising the profession shall be punishable by imprisonment for a period not exceeding two years and a fine of one million to five million Lebanese pounds.

1- The provisions of Article 39, paragraph one thereof, relating to the revocation of the licence shall apply to the licence holder in the places licensed pursuant to this Law

2- The licence shall be revoked and the place in which one of the offences provided for in paragraphs (3) and (4) of Article 126 of this Law was committed shall be closed for a period ranging between one month and one year for the first time and permanently in the event of recidivism, provided that it remains possible to exploit the place for another purpose

3- The court may order the closure of any shop or other place in which one of the offences provided for in Articles 125 to 132 inclusive of this Law is committed for a temporary period not exceeding one year.

Ancillary and additional penalties:

In all cases, the court shall order the confiscation of the prohibited plants and substances if they have been seized and have not been destroyed, or order that they be handed over to a body licensed to use them in a lawful manner. The court shall also order the confiscation of the preparations, tools, equipment, apparatus, machines and containers used, the seized means of transport, and other movable property that were used or prepared to be used in the commission of the offence, without prejudice to the rights of bona fide third parties. Natural persons who commit the offences specified in this Law shall be punished by the additional penalties provided for in Article 63 et seq. of the Penal Code. As for legal persons, they shall be deemed criminally liable for these offences and the following penalties shall apply to them:

- The fines provided for in Articles 125, 126, 128, 129 and 130 of this Law

- The penalties provided for in Articles 108 to 111 of the Penal Code.

Grounds for aggravating penalties:

The maximum penalty shall be doubled in the following cases:

- Where the role of the offender is to organise, manage or finance the commission of the offence.

- Where the offender is a repeat offender: foreign judicial judgments of conviction for offences similar to the offences provided for in this Law shall be taken into account in establishing recidivism.

- Where the offender is a participant in an international drug smuggling gang, works for its account or cooperates with it, or where the act committed by him constitutes part of an international operation for smuggling drugs or laundering money, or is concomitant with an international offence of arms smuggling, currency counterfeiting and terrorism, or constitutes part of the work of an international gang engaged in the commission of international offences

- Where the offender belongs to a local organised gang

- Where he participated in other illegal activities facilitated by the offence

- Where he used violence or a weapon

- Where he holds a public office and the offence was committed during his tenure of such office

- Where he is a professional working in the field of health or is charged with combating the abuse of or trafficking in narcotic drugs or supervising their circulation or possession

- Where the narcotic drug was given to a minor, a mentally disabled person or a person undergoing treatment for addiction, or its use was offered to or facilitated for him

- Where a minor or a mentally disabled person participated in the commission of the offence

- Where the delivered narcotic drugs caused the death of one or several persons or exposed the health of one or several persons to serious harm

- Where the offence was committed in a correctional, military or therapeutic institution, or in a social services centre, or in other places frequented by pupils and students to practise educational, sporting or social activities, or in areas immediately adjacent to such institutions and places.

- Where the offender added to the narcotic drugs substances that compounded their danger

- Mitigating circumstances may not be granted in the cases mentioned in these articles.

In the event of the prosecution and conviction of a person addicted to the use of narcotic drugs, the court may oblige him in the judgment, in addition to the penalty, to undergo treatment against addiction or the care measures provided for in this Law.

In the cases mentioned in the preceding Article, the court shall rule for the confiscation of the proceeds presumed to derive from the offence and the movable or immovable property into which such proceeds are presumed to have been converted or for which they are presumed to have been exchanged, and shall also order the confiscation of property acquired by lawful means with which the said proceeds have been intermingled, in an amount equivalent to the value of the latter, as well as the revenues and other benefits derived from these proceeds and from the property into which they have been converted or in which they have been invested or the property with which they have been intermingled; the court shall rule as stated as a result of an investigation which it conducts into the true sources of the proceeds and property, carried out by all means while observing the Banking Secrecy Law, and covering the movable and immovable property of the accused and the property of his spouse and his children or others inside or outside the country, and if it is established to the court that the source of the said property is one of the drug offences, it shall rule for its confiscation.
The costs of confiscations and of the removal and transport of installations and property shall be added to the judicial expenses and collected from the convicted person.

The court may order the publication of a summary of the final judgment imposing hard labour or imprisonment for one of the offences provided for in this Law at the expense of the convicted person in three local newspapers designated by it, and the court may also order the posting of the judgment mentioned in the preceding paragraph in the places designated by it at the expense of the convicted person.

Physical coercion:

In the event of non-payment, a fine shall be substituted by one day of imprisonment for every twenty-five thousand L.L.

On suspension of execution and suspension of judgment:

A judgment suspending the execution of a misdemeanour penalty imposed on a repeat offender in one of the misdemeanours provided for in this Law shall not be permissible.

In the case of the offences provided for in this Law, and in the case of a sentence to a penalty not covered by a suspension of execution whose duration is one year of imprisonment or more, the convicted person may not benefit during the first two-thirds of this penalty from a suspension of execution of the penalty, or from its fragmentation, or from his placement outside prison, or from obtaining leave to exit, or from enjoying restricted liberty, or from early or conditional release.

Judicial Police:

The Director of the Central Directorate for Combating Narcotics and all its personnel shall have the capacity of judicial police officers with respect to the offences provided for in this Law, in addition to the other judicial police officers provided for in the laws in force, and the pharmaceutical inspectors and agricultural engineers employed at the Ministry of Agriculture and their assistants shall have the capacity of judicial police officers with respect to the offences committed in violation of the provisions of this Law.

Custody of Persons:

In the cases referred to in Articles 125, 126 and 131, it shall be permissible, for important and serious reasons relating to the integrity of the investigation, for the officers of the Central Directorate for Combating Narcotics to detain persons during the preliminary investigation, and with the written approval of the competent Public Prosecution, for a period not exceeding three days, and this time limit may be extended once with the approval of the Public Prosecutor of the Court of Cassation if the matter relates to an international gang.

Search Operations:

Operations of inspection, search and seizure may be carried out at any hour of the day or night in the places in which the unlawful manufacture, conversion or storage of highly dangerous or dangerous narcotic substances or precursors, or of equipment or instruments prepared for the unlawful cultivation, production or manufacture of these substances takes place, and raids may likewise be carried out on the places in which persons gather to consume highly dangerous narcotic drugs, and the operation must be preceded by obtaining the approval of the Public Prosecution if it is to take place in a dwelling, and these operations may not be carried out at night except for the purpose of searching and uncovering offences, and every record drawn up for another purpose shall be null and void. Officers of the Central Directorate for Combating Narcotics may accompany the pharmaceutical inspectors and the agricultural engineers employed at the Ministry of Agriculture during their performance of specific tasks in order to seek the assistance of their expertise in this field.

Seizure and Custody of Prohibited Substances:

In the event of the commission of the offence, the incriminating materials, including prohibited substances, preparations, instruments, equipment and other movable property suspected of having been used or of having been prepared for use in the commission of the offence, and the sums and transferable securities suspected of being proceeds of the offence directly or indirectly, shall be seized, and furthermore, without there being any ground to invoke professional secrecy with the exception of banking secrecy, all documents likely to facilitate the establishment of proof of the commission of the offence and the conviction of its perpetrators shall be seized.

Disposal of seized substances:

With the exception of cases in which retaining the seized substances and plants is necessary for the course of the proceedings, the competent judicial authority shall order the execution of the following as soon as possible after the seizure and the taking of samples:

- Delivering the drugs fit for use to a pharmacist in one of the hospital institutions

- Delivering the plants and substances fit for use in the pharmaceutical industry or others, according to the nature of the substance concerned, to a public or private institution licensed to use or export them

- Destroying the other plants and substances completely, provided that this is done immediately and by the most appropriate means possible, and in the presence and under the supervision of the representative of the Public Prosecution

- As for the cases in which retaining the plants and substances is necessary for the course of the proceedings, they shall be delivered or destroyed as soon as the judgment confiscating them becomes final in accordance with its operative part, and the delivery or destruction operations shall be recorded in a report specifying accurately the number of sealed exhibits that were delivered or destroyed, and the labels of the sealed exhibits or the particulars recorded on their wrappers shall be attached to this report, which shall be signed by all the persons who participated in the delivery or destruction operation or were present during its execution.

Technical expertise:

If the need arises to seek the assistance of technical expertise to examine the samples in order to determine the nature of the seized plants and substances, their composition, and their contents, the Public Prosecution or the judicial authority seized of the matter thereafter shall decide to appoint an expert or a committee of experts, and the expertise shall be carried out as quickly as possible after the seizure in order to limit the risks of the occurrence of a physical or chemical change. The expert shall state in his report the number of samples entrusted to him, the nature and weight of the plants and substances contained in each sample thereof, and the number of samples used, and shall mention, where applicable, the number of samples that he reconditioned and the changes that occurred to them.

Monitoring of postal departments:

Those competent to detect or pursue offences may carry out, by night and by day, inspection operations in postal departments for the purpose of detecting illicit consignments of narcotic drugs and precursors, and in the event of the existence of serious indications leading to the presumption of the existence of such consignments, they may open them in the presence of the person concerned and with agreement, and otherwise pursuant to a permission from the Public Prosecution, and draw up a report thereof.

Personal search and search of luggage:

The competent judicial police officers may carry out, at the borders or in public places, personal search operations and searches of luggage in order to detect the offences provided for in this Law.

The seized substances shall be placed in sealed parcels immediately upon their seizure, and these parcels shall be prepared in a manner that prevents the theft of the plants and substances, and each sealed parcel shall be numbered, and a description of the plants and substances contained therein shall be written on its wrapper or on a label integrated with the seal, indicating their nature, their weight, and the number of containers in which they have been placed, where applicable. A record shall be drawn up immediately establishing the date, place, and circumstances of the discovery, and containing a description of the seized plants and substances and a determination of their weight, stating the method of weighing used, the tests conducted thereon, and the results yielded thereby. In addition, the particulars provided for in the preceding paragraph shall be established in the record, and the place where they are to be deposited and all other useful particulars shall be specified in the record. The record and the particulars established on each parcel shall be signed by all persons who participated in preparing the parcels. The sealed parcels shall be kept in appropriate conditions that prevent their exposure to theft and all other forms of diversion. Upon any subsequent handling of the parcels, a record must be drawn up clarifying the matter and the intended purpose thereof, and establishing the integrity of the sealed parcels and their wrappers, or their disappearance or damage, and the changes that have occurred thereto.

If the quantity of seized prohibited substances is so large that it is difficult to attach it to the investigation file, the authority conducting the investigation shall proceed as soon as possible, in the presence of the accused, or in the presence of two witnesses where the presence of the accused is impossible, to take samples in a quantity sufficient for the purposes of the investigation and trial, for ensuring the establishment of evidence, and for conclusively verifying the quality of the seized plants and substances in accordance with international standards. Each sample shall be placed in a sealed parcel, on the wrapper of which, or on a label integrated with the seal, a statement of the nature and weight of its contents shall be established. After the samples have been taken, the seals shall be reapplied, and a record shall be drawn up showing the number of times samples were taken, the nature and weight of the plants and substances taken in each of them, as well as the changes that have occurred to the original sealed parcels. The record, the particulars recorded on each sample, and the resealed parcels shall be signed by all persons who participated in these operations or attended the performance thereof.

Use of medical examination techniques to detect offences:

If there is serious evidence giving rise to the presumption that a person is transporting highly dangerous or dangerous narcotic substances concealed inside his body, he may be subjected to medical examination techniques after the written consent or after obtaining an authorisation from the Public Prosecution, which shall name the assigned physician. The latter shall draw up a detailed report including the results of the medical examination together with an indication of the manner in which it was carried out, and shall submit it without delay to the Public Prosecution. Whoever refuses to comply with the examination to which he has been subjected shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to three years and by a fine from two million to five million pounds.

Controlled delivery:

1- Written permission may be granted for the passage of plants or substances covered by this Law through Lebanese territory if they are dispatched, or suspected of being dispatched, in an illicit manner, for the purpose of identifying the persons involved in these offences and taking prosecution measures against them.

2- The decision to resort to controlled delivery shall be taken by the Head of the Central Directorate for Combating Narcotic Drugs after obtaining the permission of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation and the Director General of Customs, and the decision shall be notified immediately to the competent police authority having jurisdiction at the place where the consignment is presumed to exit from or enter into Lebanese territory, or at the place where the consignment is presumed to be delivered.

3- The Head of the Central Directorate for Combating Narcotic Drugs, or whomever he delegates, shall direct and supervise the operation and shall order such interventions as he deems appropriate. With the consent of other concerned States and pursuant to concluded agreements, where necessary, he may decide to intercept the illicit consignment and allow it to continue on its way with its contents intact or after seizing the plants and substances, and he may also replace them with other products where necessary.

Surveillance and wiretapping of telephone communications:

The competent police authority may, with the approval of the Public Prosecution, place under surveillance or wiretapping the telephone lines used by persons regarding whom there is serious evidence indicating their participation in one of the offences provided for in Articles 125, 126, 131 and 132 of this Law. Calls obtained in this manner may not be considered as a confession, but shall be used only to track the movements of the offenders and to make use thereof in uncovering the offence.

Coordination of Combating Illicit Trafficking:

The Central Drug Enforcement Directorate provided for in Part Three of this Law shall undertake the collection of all information that may facilitate the tracking and prevention of illicit trafficking operations, and shall also coordinate all operations aimed at suppressing such trafficking at the national and international levels.

Expedited Enforcement:

Judgments rendered inter partes imposing a penalty of not less than one year of imprisonment for any of the offences under this Law shall be immediately enforceable despite the filing of an appeal in respect thereof, with the exception of the death penalty.

Full treatment for drug use and addiction shall comprise the following three stages:

1-The stage of detoxification from addictive poisoning and physical dependence on the habit of use, which takes place in specialised sanatoriums accredited by the Ministry of Public Health and subject to the hospitals regime, in which patients are placed under the guard of the public forces.

2- The stage of treatment and elimination of psychological dependence on the habit of use, which takes place in psychosocial clinics accredited by the Ministry of Public Health.

3- A complementary stage aimed at assisting the addict to return to normal life and rehabilitating him to integrate into society, which takes place in care institutions or with natural persons accredited by the Ministry of Social Affairs.

Every drug addict may, before any prosecution is initiated against him, appear spontaneously before the Drug Addiction Control Committee provided for in Article 199 of this Law, requesting to be subjected to physical and psychological treatment measures for the illness of drug use, and sign an undertaking to that effect, whereby he shall have the right in such case to have his identity concealed save from persons bound by professional secrecy, and not to be prosecuted if he pursues the treatment and continues therein until he obtains a certificate proving his complete recovery from addictive poisoning and physical habituation and his elimination of psychological dependence on the habit of use.

The Addiction Control Committee shall refer the addict to one of the designated sanatoriums where he is placed under observation for a period of one month during which he undergoes the necessary examinations, and the Committee shall assign a social worker at the Ministry of Social Affairs to conduct an investigation and study on the addict's personal, family, professional and social life. At the end of the month, both the management of the sanatorium and the social worker shall submit a report on the condition of the addict to the Addiction Control Committee to decide on his matter.

Penetration of information systems:

The competent judicial police may penetrate the information systems used by persons against whom there are serious indications of their participation in one of the offences provided for in Articles 125, 126, 131 and 132, and which are useful in uncovering the offence, after obtaining the permission of the Public Prosecution.

Inspection of financial and commercial records:

The competent judicial police, without professional secrecy being invoked against them, may request to inspect all financial and commercial records, with the exception of banking records, if it is probable that they relate to transactions connected with the offences provided for in Articles 125, 126, 131 and 132 of this Law.

Rewarding informants:

The competent authority may disburse a reward, within the allocated appropriations, to anyone who guides, contributes to, or facilitates the uncovering of the offences provided for in this Law and the seizure of the criminal substances.

Temporary closure of the licence and temporary closure:

1- The provisions of Article 39, paragraph two, of this Law relating to the suspension of the licence shall apply to the licence holder prosecuted for one of the offences provided for in this Law, and in addition to suspending the effect of the licence, the place in which the offence occurred may be closed pending the issuance of the judgment.

2- The competent court and the Public Prosecution, where necessary and in cases of prosecution to which the second and third paragraphs of Article 154 of this Law apply, may order the temporary closure of the place in which the offence occurred for a period not exceeding one month.

Conservatory measures to ensure the payment of fines and the confiscation of the convicted person's property and the proceeds:

1- In the event of prosecution for the commission of the offences provided for in this Law, and for the purpose of ensuring the payment of fines and the execution of confiscation, the court may order, upon the request of the Public Prosecution, the taking of conservatory measures at the expense of the Treasury against the property of the prosecuted person. The conviction of this person shall entail the confirmation of the conservatory attachments and the final registration of the guarantees, whereas non-conviction or discharge from the charge shall entail the lifting of the measures taken at the expense of the Treasury, and this provision shall also apply in the event of the lapse of the public action.

2- In the cases set forth in the preceding Article, the court may order, for the purpose of ensuring confiscation, the taking of conservatory measures against the proceeds presumed to be derived from the aforementioned offences, and against the property into which these proceeds are presumed to have been converted, exchanged, or intermingled, and against the revenues of such property and proceeds.

An addict may directly enter one of the specialized sanatoriums mentioned in the preceding Article, which shall admit him after he signs an undertaking to accept submission to treatment, and it shall immediately notify the matter to the Addiction Control Committee in order to assign a social worker to conduct a study on him, and the addict in the sanatorium shall be subject to the observation and examinations mentioned in the preceding Article.

If it is established that the referred person has no need for the elimination of addictive intoxication and the cessation of his physical habituation, the Committee shall decide to release him from the sanatorium and, depending on the circumstances, oblige him to attend a specialized psychosocial clinic or assign one of the care institutions or natural persons accredited for this purpose to provide assistance to him.

If it is established that the referred person is addicted to use and is in need of treatment for the elimination of addictive intoxication, the Addiction Control Committee shall decide that he remain in the sanatorium for a period not exceeding three months, at the end of which the administration of the sanatorium shall submit a new report on his condition; the Committee may, before taking its final decision, decide to hear the statements of the patient and request the clarifications that it deems appropriate.

If it is established to the Committee that the patient has recovered from addictive intoxication and physical dependence, it shall decide to discharge him, and in the contrary case it shall decide that he remain in the sanatorium for another period or periods, provided that the period of his stay does not exceed six months; the administration of the sanatorium shall notify the patient in writing of the decision issued for his continued retention in the sanatorium within three days from the date of its issuance, and it shall execute the discharge decision within the twenty-four hours following its issuance.

The patient may object to the decision of the aforementioned Committee issued for his continued retention in the sanatorium before the Indictment Chamber within fifteen days from the date of his notification.

The Committee may, upon the release of the patient from the sanatorium, decide to oblige him to attend a psychosocial clinic once or twice a week to assist him in ridding himself of psychological dependence on the habit of use, for a period not exceeding three months, at the end of which the competent physician shall submit a report on his condition, whereupon the Committee shall decide to cease his attendance at the clinic or to continue such attendance for another period or periods until the physician reports the cessation of the state of psychological dependence in the patient. The patient may, where applicable, object to the decisions of the Committee if he deems them unfair to him before the Indictment Chamber within fifteen days from his notification of the decision in accordance with the preceding Article.

An addict who perseveres in pursuing treatment in accordance with what is decided by the Anti-Addiction Committee, and where the management of the sanatorium submits a report confirming his detoxification from addiction and the clinic physician submits a report confirming his recovery from psychological dependence on addiction, shall be granted by the Committee a nominal certificate proving his cure, and in this case he shall be permanently exempted from prosecution and the costs of treatment shall remain borne by the State.

However, if he discontinues treatment and does not persevere in it until obtaining the aforementioned certificate, he shall be prosecuted in accordance with the legal procedures, and the management of the sanatorium and the psychiatrist shall be obliged to notify the Committee upon the discontinuation of treatment.

An addict who has been cured and has obtained the certificate mentioned in the preceding Article may request the Committee, which also has the right to do so of its own motion, to assign one of the care institutions or natural persons accredited by the Ministry of Social Affairs to care for the addict and assist him in returning to normal life, reintegrating into society, finding suitable employment, providing advice and assistance, and managing all his other affairs, and the institutions shall prepare a suitable place in which the persons placed under care meet at least twice a week under the supervision of psychological and social specialists, and this place shall serve as a medical and social forum for them.

The parents, testamentary guardian, legal guardian, and either spouse may request the Addiction Committee to place a minor son or daughter, a person under guardianship, or a spouse whose addiction to the use of narcotics is complained of, in a sanatorium for treatment. The aforementioned Committee shall adjudicate the request after conducting the necessary investigations and hearing the statements of both parties, either by rejecting it or by placing the addict in a sanatorium for treatment.

The Committee may order that the person complained against be placed under observation in a sanatorium for a period not exceeding three weeks to observe him medically before adjudicating the request whenever it finds it necessary to do so.

If the Committee decides to place the addict in the sanatorium, the procedures provided for in Articles 184 to 190 inclusive of this Law shall apply.

The addict shall have the right to object to the Committee's decision within fifteen days from its notification to him before the competent Indictment Chamber.

Anyone who knows of the existence of a person known for his dangerousness to others by reason of his addiction to the use of narcotics may report the matter to the Public Prosecution, which shall conduct an investigation into the matter and shall have the authority to refer the addict to the Addiction Committee to compel him to undergo treatment where necessary before deciding on the matter of prosecution.

The Public Prosecution may, in the event of the arrest of a person for the offence of consuming narcotics, refer him, with his consent, to the Addiction Committee so that he may undergo treatment in accordance with the procedures provided for in Articles 184 to 190 inclusive of this Law.

The addict may, during the investigation and trial, request to be subjected to treatment, whereupon the judicial authority before which the case is pending shall decide to stay the proceedings and refer him before the Anti-Addiction Committee, which shall place him in one of the sanatoriums to proceed with the treatment measures mentioned in Articles 184 to 190 inclusive of this Law.

In the two cases provided for in the two preceding Articles, if the addict perseveres with the treatment until obtaining from the Committee a certificate proving his recovery on the basis of the reports of the management of the sanatorium and the psychiatrist, this shall be notified to the judicial authority seized of the case, which shall decide to stay the prosecutions against him definitively.

However, if the addict discontinues pursuing the treatment or refrains therefrom, the matter shall be notified to the judicial authority to resume his prosecution and trial from the point at which it stopped.

The court before which the addict who refused treatment in the preceding stages is being tried may issue an interim decision obliging him to place himself under treatment for detoxification from addiction and deliverance from psychological dependence in accordance with the procedures set forth in Articles 184 to 188 inclusive and 190 of this Law; if he complies and pursues the treatment until its end and his recovery is proven and the Addiction Committee notifies this matter to the court, the latter shall rule to stay the prosecutions against him definitively.

However, if he refrains from accepting the treatment or does not pursue it until recovery, it shall continue his trial and issue its judgment against him in accordance with the ordinary rules.

If the addict refuses treatment and the offence of consumption is proven against him, the court shall sentence him to the penalties provided for in Articles 127 and 130 of this Law.

The court may, depending on the circumstances of the case, grant the addict a stay of execution if he is not a recidivist, or make the stay of execution of the penalty conditional upon his subsequent acceptance to undergo treatment and proceed with it until recovery, and the execution of the penalty shall not be resumed.

It is the court that issued the judgment that decides to stay the execution of the penalty definitively after the Anti-Addiction Committee notifies it of his complete recovery from the illness of consumption.

In all cases of conviction and sentencing, it shall remain open to the person sentenced for the offence of addiction to request, during the execution of the penalty, to be subjected to treatment, whereupon the duration of the treatment shall be deducted from the original term of his penalty if he pursues it until recovery.

The Drug Addiction Committee shall be composed, by a decision of the Minister of Justice, of:

1- A judge of the eleventh grade and above, as President.

2- A representative of the Ministry of Social Affairs.

3- A physician from the Ministry of Public Health

4- A representative of the Central Directorate for Combating Drugs

5- A person from among those concerned with drug affairs in private institutions:

- Members proposed by the competent administrations.
The Ministry of Public Health shall establish one or more sanatoriums for the treatment of drug addicts from addictive intoxication.
The Ministry of Public Health shall establish or accredit a number of psychosocial clinics for the treatment of addicts from psychological dependence on drug use.

The Ministry of Social Affairs shall establish or accredit one or more institutions and natural persons possessing the competencies to care for addicted persons after their recovery from drug dependence.

Professional secrecy shall be observed with respect to addicts undergoing treatment, and the competent judiciary shall retain, on an exceptional basis, the power to grant exemption from this secrecy for important and serious reasons.

If it appears to the Addiction Committee that the presence of the addict in the sanatorium leaves his family without financial resources, it shall propose to the Minister of Social Affairs to grant this family, by a decision from him, an appropriate monthly allowance within the appropriations allocated for this purpose.

A National Council for Drug Affairs shall be established, composed as follows:

- The President of the Council of Ministers- as President

- The Deputy President of the Council of Ministers- as Vice-President

- The Minister of Justice

- The Minister of the Interior

- The Minister of Public Health

- The Minister of Agriculture

- The Minister of Finance

- The Minister of National Education, Youth and Sports

- The Minister of Social Affairs

- The Minister of Foreign Affairs- as Members

- The Secretary-General of the Council - as Rapporteur

Other ministers may be invited to its meetings as the need arises.

The Head of the Pharmacy Service and the Head of the Narcotics Department at the Ministry of Public Health, the Central Director for Combating Drugs, the two Presidents of the Orders of Physicians and the President of the Order of Pharmacists in Lebanon, and a representative of the recognised national institutions in the field of combating drugs shall also be invited to its meetings.
In the absence of the President of the Council, the Vice-President shall deputise for him, and the remaining ministers may be represented by the competent Directors-General in their ministries.

The National Council for Narcotic Drugs Affairs shall undertake the following:

- Establishing, defining and developing the national plan and the policy of the Government in the field of combating narcotic drugs.

- Preparing the decisions of the Government, whether at the national or international level, in relation to combating the spread of narcotic drugs, their use and addiction thereto.

- Establishing the foundations of coordination and cooperation among the various national administrations concerned with combating narcotic drugs among themselves and with institutions, the Arab Bureau for Narcotic Drugs Affairs, and the competent Arab and international administrations.

- Combating the illicit production, manufacture, trafficking and exportation of narcotic drugs and proposing the determination of the total annual quantity permitted for medical and scientific purposes.

- Combating the cultivation of narcotic drugs and encouraging and revitalising alternative crops.

- Encouraging prevention, medical and social care, and epidemiological and statistical research and studies.

- Encouraging the media and enlightening public opinion against the dangers of use and addiction.

- Supervising the application of international treaties.

- Ensuring the updating and amendment of the texts relating to narcotic drugs.

- Distributing the intervention budget allocated for combating narcotic drugs among the ministries concerned and the subsidies granted to non-governmental organisations that undertake activities in this field.

- Submitting an annual report to the Government presenting the situation at the national level and its development in relation to the supply of and demand for narcotic drugs, and including all proposals that would determine measures for combating narcotic drugs.

The Council shall hold at least two annual meetings in January and July and shall hold other meetings when the need arises.

The President shall determine the dates of the meetings and instruct the Secretary-General to address the invitations.

The Council shall have a Secretary-General with the rank of Director, appointed from among holders of a licence in law, and exceptionally he may be appointed from among officers of the Internal Security Forces with the rank of Colonel at least, by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of its President. Attached to the Secretary-General shall be a staff of employees whose cadre shall be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers, and they may be seconded from other administrations.

The Secretary-General shall prepare the agenda of deliberations of the Council, represent Lebanon before the competent international bodies in combating narcotic drugs, and ensure that the reports and minutes provided for in international conventions are submitted to the competent bodies.

The Secretary-General shall execute the budget of the Council in accordance with the instructions of the President.

Purpose of its establishment and its competencies:

A Central Directorate for Combating Drug Offences shall be established in the Ministry of Interior, which shall undertake the prosecution of the offences provided for in this Law, their suppression, and the pursuit of their perpetrators, and shall be entrusted with:

a- Collecting information that ensures the facilitation of pursuing all offences related to drugs and their abuse.

b- Combating and seizing offences of illicit trafficking in drugs, or the production, possession, holding, manufacturing, exchange, assignment, or use thereof, except in the cases authorised by law.

c- Combating and seizing the cultivation of narcotic plants in all their forms and destroying them in cooperation with the other security agencies.

d- Drawing up the necessary plans and taking the measures capable of achieving this combating locally and internationally.

e- Cooperating with all departments concerned with the matter and similar departments in other countries.

f- Implementing the plans and policies drawn up by the National Council for Drug Affairs.

g- Participating in international, regional, and local conferences concerned with drug affairs and combating them, and implementing the agreements or treaties concluded by them.

This Directorate shall be considered the primary and competent authority for combating all offences related to drugs.

The Director and his competencies:

The management of the Central Directorate shall be undertaken by a senior official with the rank of Director, appointed by decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior. An officer from the Internal Security Forces with the rank of Colonel at least may be appointed to this post, who shall be directly subject to the authority of the Minister of Interior and shall undertake:

- Carrying out the duties of the Directorate, supervising all its personnel, monitoring them, and coordinating their work.

- Receiving information related to drugs from all security agencies and referring it to the units subordinate to him for investigation.

- Ensuring the necessary liaison with all State administrations and other authorities in the various ministries.

- Ensuring the provision of the necessary equipment and monitoring its use by the personnel.

- Training officers, non-commissioned officers, and personnel working in the field of combating at the international and local levels.

- Taking the necessary decision regarding the follow-up of investigations abroad when necessary, and determining the manner in which this shall take place by agreement with the competent authorities in the States concerned and after the approval of the competent Public Prosecution.

Personnel of the Directorate:

The Directorate shall consist of:

- An administrative staff composed of employees seconded or transferred from public administrations, and the administrative work of the Directorate shall be undertaken by a central office in Beirut and branch offices in the governorates which shall undertake suppression and investigation operations, provided that their connection shall be direct with the competent Public Prosecutions.

The personnel of these offices shall be drawn from officers and non-commissioned officers of the security institutions affiliated with the Ministry of the Interior, and they shall be selected from among those attested for their academic and moral qualifications and from elite personnel, and they shall be transferred by a decision

of the Minister of the Interior upon the proposal of the Director of the Central Directorate.

- The organic organisation (cadre of the Directorate) of this Directorate across its various units, the powers and duties of the heads and their responsibilities, and the relations with the military, administrative and judicial authorities shall be determined by regulatory decrees upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior and after consulting the opinion of the Director.

Employees of government administrations and all security agencies to which cases of illicit trafficking in, manufacture of, or cultivation of narcotics are reported, or which seize quantities of narcotics, shall be obliged to proceed forthwith to notify the Central Directorate for Narcotics Suppression thereof directly and at the earliest possible time, and the entire file shall be referred to it after consulting the competent judiciary; and all security agencies shall also be obliged to assist the personnel of the Central Directorate for Narcotics Suppression in its operations, especially the important ones among them, when requested to do so.

The Central Directorate shall submit in the month of January of each year a comprehensive report on the development of illicit trafficking and use operations in the past year, and a copy of this report shall be submitted to the Minister of the Interior and a copy to the Cassation Public Prosecutor.

The Director in the Central Directorate and the rest of his employees and personnel shall have the capacity of assistants to the Public Prosecutor in performing the functions of the judicial police in accordance with Article 12 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

The powers of the Central Directorate shall not preclude the initiation of the investigation and the carrying out of its requirements by the rest of the personnel of the judicial police who are notified of the occurrence of the offence, provided that the ongoing investigations, the seized items and the detained persons are handed over at the earliest time to the personnel of the office present in their areas in order to complete what is required in accordance with the law.

International Cooperation:

1- The Central Directorate shall establish close links with its counterpart offices or agencies in other countries, particularly with respect to:

- The expeditious exchange of information regarding all aspects of illicit trafficking offences and regarding the connection of such trafficking with other criminal activities.

- Extensive cooperation in investigations relating to international trafficking for the purpose of identifying:

- The identity, descriptions, places of residence, movements, and activities of traffickers.

- Ongoing or planned transactions.

- The movements of proceeds and funds derived from international trafficking.

- The movements of controlled substances as well as the equipment, supplies, and instruments used or intended for use in the illicit manufacture of narcotic drugs.

- The establishment of clandestine laboratories for narcotic drugs.

- Expeditiously notifying the competent authorities in the States concerned as soon as there are grounds to believe that a precursor has been imported or exported by way of transit for the illicit manufacture of narcotic drugs, indicating the methods of payment and all other necessary elements justifying such belief.

- Forming joint teams of investigators where appropriate, taking into account the need to protect the security of persons and property and ensuring full respect for the sovereignty of the State over the territory in which the operation is to take place.

- Providing substances for analytical or investigative purposes where appropriate.

- Exchanging personnel and experts and seconding liaison officers.

2- The Central Directorate shall cooperate with counterpart agencies in other countries with a view to planning and implementing training and research programmes that enable the exchange of information regarding illicit trafficking, and, where appropriate, organizing regional and international conferences and seminars to strengthen cooperation and provide an opportunity to study problems of mutual concern, in particular the special problems and needs of transit States.

Relations with International Bodies:

1- The Central Directorate shall submit to the United Nations Organization, in the manner and at the dates determined by this Organization:

- An annual report on the progress of the implementation of international conventions concerning substances placed under control.

- Reports annually on the progress of the implementation of international conventions concerning substances placed under control.

- Detailed reports on illicit trafficking operations of an international character that reveal new trends relating to the presence of large quantities of substances or shed light on the sources that supply traffickers with these substances or on the methods they use - All information requested by the United Nations body

2- The Director in the Central Directorate or his representative shall participate in the meetings organized by the United Nations for the heads of national departments concerned with the suppression of illicit trafficking offences

3- The Central Directorate shall be the correspondent of the International Criminal Police Organization in the field of narcotic drugs.

Controlled Delivery:

The Director, after obtaining permission from the Public Prosecutor of the Court of Cassation and the Director General of Customs, shall take the decision to resort to controlled delivery, provided that in doing so, or with respect to consignments coming from abroad or destined for abroad, the financial arrangements, financial agreements, and agreements concluded with the competent authorities in the States concerned regarding the exercise of jurisdictions are observed, and the Director of the Central Bureau within Lebanese territory shall undertake the management of the operation or its supervision, while ensuring that the Public Prosecutor of the Court of Cassation is kept informed of its course, and he shall take, where necessary, with the approval of the competent authorities in the States concerned, the decision to intercept the illicit consignment and allow it to continue on its way, either without interfering with it or after seizing the narcotic drugs or replacing them wholly or partially with other products where necessary.

The provisions of this Title shall regulate the extradition of offenders and mutual legal assistance in the field of combating illicit acts relating to the plants, substances, and preparations placed under control pursuant to this Law, in the absence of a treaty in this regard, and its provisions shall also apply to matters for which the treaty has not laid down regulatory rules.

The offences provided for in this Law shall not be considered fiscal or political offences their perpetrators or to refuse mutual legal assistance in the field of criminal investigations and prosecutions and the judicial proceedings relating thereto.

The general extradition provisions set forth in Article 30 to 36 inclusive of the General Penal Code shall apply to the offences provided for in this Law, provided that they are consistent with the provisions of this Chapter Extradition Request - Documents Required to Be Submitted.

For the request to be accepted, it shall be required that the act subject of the request be punishable by imprisonment of at least one year in the State requesting extradition and in Lebanese law, and in the case of a penalty, that the judgment be final and the term of imprisonment be at least six months.

The request shall be accompanied by a copy of the legislative and regulatory texts proving that the prosecuted act constitutes an offence in the requesting State punishable by the penalty set forth in the preceding Article.

The request shall be refused if there are substantial grounds for believing that the extradition will facilitate the taking of prosecution measures or the imposition of a penalty against the person sought on account of his race, religion, nationality, or political opinions Mandatory Prosecution:

The request shall be submitted to the competent judicial authority in the event that extradition is refused for the following reasons:

- That the offence was committed within the scope of Lebanese territorial jurisdiction (Articles 15 to 18 inclusive of the General Penal Code).

- That the perpetrator of the offence is Lebanese.

- That the presumed principal of the offence is present within Lebanese territory.

If the request relates to the execution of a sentence handed down and the Lebanese Government refuses it on the ground that the convicted person is Lebanese, and the requesting State asks it to undertake the execution of the sentence or the remaining part thereof, the Lebanese Government shall refer the request to the Minister of Justice, who shall verify that it meets the necessary conditions and conforms with Lebanese law and shall take the appropriate decision regarding it, and if the sentence handed down is more severe in its nature or in its duration than the penalty prescribed by Lebanese law for the same acts, the competent court shall decide, upon the request of the convicted person or the Public Prosecution, to substitute the sentence handed down with a penalty more in conformity with Lebanese law.

Provisional detention:

The competent court may, in cases of urgency and if the circumstances justify it, order the provisional detention of a foreign person whose extradition is sought, upon a request addressed to it directly by any means whatsoever, provided that there is a written instrument or material evidence equivalent thereto showing that the requesting State holds a judicial decision ordering the detention of the person concerned or containing a judgment against him for having committed an offence provided for by this Law in which the conditions for extradition are met, and this person may be released if the Government does not receive, within twenty days from the date of his arrest, a request for his extradition fulfilling the legal conditions.

The Lebanese Government may consent to extradition after examining the request for provisional detention alone if the person whose extradition is sought expressly declares before the judicial authority his consent to his immediate extradition.

A request for or the provision of mutual legal assistance may relate to the following matters:

- Service of judicial documents

- Conducting investigations: receiving testimonies or confessions - search and seizure - examining objects and inspecting sites- identifying or tracing proceeds, property, equipment, instrumentalities and substances for the purpose of gathering evidentiary elements

- Providing information and evidence: providing originals of documents and records or certified copies thereof

- Seizure, freezing and confiscation of proceeds and property derived from the offence

- Producing or bringing forward witnesses, experts or other persons, including prisoners, who consent to assist in the investigation or participate in the proceedings

- Transfer of criminal proceedings where necessary for the proper administration of justice.

Contents of the request:

The request shall include:

- A statement of the purpose of the request for assistance

- Identification of the requesting authority

- The subject matter and nature of the investigation, criminal prosecution proceedings or judicial proceedings to which the request relates, and the name and function of the person supervising them

- A summary of the facts of the case

- A certified copy of the provisions that criminalise it

- A description of the assistance sought and the procedures requested to be executed

- A statement of the identity and nationality of the persons concerned and all other information necessary for the execution of the request

- A translation into the Arabic language of the entire request file, and the requested State may request supplementary information necessary for the execution of the request, and the requesting State may also request additional information where necessary.

Referral of the request:

The request and correspondence relating thereto shall be transmitted through diplomatic channels, and it may be communicated orally in cases of urgency provided that it is subsequently confirmed in writing as soon as possible, and in cases of urgency the request may also be sent through the International Criminal Police Organization or directly between the two judicial authorities in the two States by any means, provided that it constitutes a written instrument or material evidence equivalent thereto; the request shall not be executed unless the requesting Government notifies the Lebanese authorities thereof within twenty days at most.

Assistance may be refused in the following cases:

- If it entails prejudice to Lebanese sovereignty, its security, its public policy or its other essential interests

- If Lebanese legislation prohibits the taking of the requested measures in the case of the offence concerned

- If acceptance of the request is incompatible with Lebanese public policy

- If the requesting State does not grant reciprocity to Lebanon

- If the request is not submitted in accordance with the due procedures

The execution of the request shall be postponed if it is likely to obstruct an ongoing investigation, criminal prosecutions, or judicial proceedings in Lebanon, and this matter shall be notified to the requesting Government.
The decision of refusal or postponement must be reasoned, and the reasons shall be notified to the requesting State.

The Minister of Justice shall forward the requests for assistance addressed to Lebanon, after verifying that they have been duly submitted, to the competent judicial authority, and the request shall be executed in accordance with Lebanese law and the procedures specified in the request, provided that they are consistent with Lebanese legislation.

Limitation of use:

Information and testimonies resulting from the assistance may not be communicated, nor may they be used in Lebanon for purposes relating to investigations, criminal prosecutions, or other judicial proceedings other than those indicated in the request for assistance, unless the State to which the request for assistance was addressed consents thereto in advance.

Preservation of confidentiality:

If the requesting State stipulates that the request and its contents remain confidential except to the extent necessary for their execution, and it is not possible to comply with this request, this shall be notified to it as soon as possible.

Protection of persons:

A witness, expert, or any other person, whether at liberty or detained, who agrees to come to Lebanon to give his statements during specific proceedings or to assist in an investigation, in criminal prosecutions, or in a judicial proceeding, may not be prosecuted, nor may he be detained, punished, or subjected to any restriction of his personal liberty within Lebanon on account of positive or negative acts or convictions prior to his appearance; and this immunity shall cease if the designated person remains within Lebanon or returns thereto of his own free will upon the expiry of a period of fifteen consecutive days after he has been officially notified that his presence is no longer required by the Lebanese authorities; and if the person concerned is detained abroad, he shall be kept in detention within Lebanon and shall be escorted under guard to the State from which he was requested as soon as his presence within Lebanon becomes unnecessary.

If a foreign Government deems it necessary for a person residing in Lebanon to appear, the Lebanese Government, after being notified of a summons for this person to appear, shall obtain an undertaking from him to comply with the request; and the summons to appear shall only be served on the basis of an undertaking that the person concerned will not be prosecuted, detained, punished, or have his liberty restricted on account of facts or convictions prior to his appearance; and unless there are special considerations preventing this, the Lebanese Government shall execute the request to send a person detained within its territory abroad in order to hear his statements or confront him with other persons, subject to an undertaking to return him as soon as possible.

Conservatory measures: The representative of the Public Prosecution to whom a request to take conservatory measures is sent shall submit this request to the competent court, which may order that the requested conservatory measures consistent with this legislation be taken at the expense of the Public Treasury and in accordance with the conditions provided for in Lebanese law. If the requested measure is not provided for in Lebanese law, the court may rule to take measures provided for by this Law whose effects are closest to the effects of the requested measure. The adoption by the judicial authority in the requesting State of a decision to abandon prosecution proceedings or to grant release, or a judgment of acquittal, or the lapse of prosecution proceedings in that State, shall entail the lifting of the measures ordered to be taken by operation of law. Notification to the Lebanese Government of the issuance of a final judgment of conviction shall entail the confirmation of the conservatory measures and the permission for the final registration of the securities provided for by Lebanese law, if the concerned State so requests.

Execution of a confiscation decision issued abroad:

The representative of the Public Prosecution to whom a request to execute a confiscation decision issued abroad is sent shall submit this request to the competent court, which shall ratify, in accordance with the conditions provided for by Lebanese law, the provisions of the decision that are consistent with Lebanese legislation, and shall take a decision regarding its provisions that are not consistent with Lebanese law. The judgment shall be executed upon the request of the Public Prosecution.

Obtaining a confiscation decision:

The representative of the Public Prosecution to whom a request to obtain a confiscation decision is sent shall notify the competent court of this request, and the court may rule for confiscation in accordance with Lebanese legislation. The judgment shall be executed upon a request from the Public Prosecution.

Confiscated funds:

The Lebanese State shall dispose, in accordance with its legislation, of the proceeds and funds referred to in item (1) of Article 244 which it has confiscated in accordance with Articles 246 and 247; however, an agreement concluded in each case of this kind between the Lebanese Government and the requesting Government may provide for the following: - Delivering the value of these proceeds and properties, or the funds derived from their sale, or a large part thereof, to intergovernmental bodies specialised in combating illicit trafficking in narcotics or properties, or sharing the funds derived from their sale.

The Lebanese State shall bear the costs required for the execution of requests for assistance, and if these costs are beyond its capacity to bear or appear to be so, the Lebanese Government and the foreign Government shall consult to determine the conditions in accordance with which the request shall be executed and the manner of bearing the costs.
The implementing provisions of the provisions of this Law shall be issued by virtue of decrees and decisions taken by the competent authorities in accordance with the due procedures.
The Narcotics Law issued on 18 June 1946 is hereby repealed, together with all its amendments and all other provisions contrary to this Law or inconsistent with its content.

Service of documents and records: If a foreign authority, during the investigation of a criminal action before it, sees the necessity of examining incriminating documents or records in the possession of the Lebanese authorities, this request shall be executed unless there are special circumstances preventing that, and subject to the undertaking to return the said documents and records as soon as possible.

Transfer of proceedings:

Where a foreign person is prosecuted in Lebanon for committing an offence provided for by this Law and is imprisoned abroad for committing one of these offences, the Lebanese Government may, in the interest of the proper administration of justice and pursuant to a conforming decision from its competent judicial authorities, authorise the transfer of the proceedings to the foreign Government if this Government submits a request to that effect.

Common provisions

- Every request, whether submitted by Lebanon or addressed to it, for the taking of conservatory measures or for obtaining a judgment of confiscation and for executing a confiscation decision Focusing on:

- proceeds derived from one of the offences of this Law, or movable or immovable property into which the said proceeds have been converted, and property equivalent in value to these proceeds

- or narcotics or psychotropic substances

- or supplies, equipment, instruments or any other things used or intended for use in any manner whatsoever in one of the offences provided for in Articles 125, 126, 128, 129 131 and 132 that are situated within the territory of the requested State

shall be transmitted through diplomatic channels, subject to the provisions of Articles 232-236 inclusive and to the provisions of this Section, provided that the request includes, in addition to the information mentioned in Article 32, a statement of the facts upon which the State relies in its request, a precise specification of the measures requested and a description of the movable or immovable property concerned

Furthermore, if the request relates to the execution of a confiscation decision taken by the requesting State, it must include a legally admissible copy of this decision and a statement of the limits within which its execution is requested.

If the Lebanese Government destroys a request for one of the purposes provided for in Article 244, it shall refer it to the Minister of Justice, who shall verify the fulfilment of its conditions before sending the file to the competent representative of the Public Prosecution.
Allowances of State employees shall be of two kinds: general and special.

General allowances shall include:

- Family allowance

- Transport fares

- Car allowance

- Travel allowance

- Housing allowance

- Representation allowance

- Allowance for overtime work

- Allowance for night hours

- Cash office responsibility allowance

- Sickness grants.

An employee (whether male or female) who receives a monthly salary shall be granted a family allowance in respect of the members of his family set out below:

A - The husband or the wife, or the deserted or divorced wife in whose favour maintenance has been adjudged, provided that in no case shall the allowance be granted in respect of more than one wife.

B - Male children who have not completed the eighteenth year of their age.

C - Male children who have completed the eighteenth year of their age, in the following two cases:

- Where the child is afflicted with an illness or infirmity rendering him incapable of working and requiring his support, provided that this is established by a report issued by the Medical Committee provided for in the Pensions Law, and his case shall be reviewed at most every three years.

- Where the child is pursuing his studies, until he completes the twenty-fifth year of his age.

The rate of the monthly family allowance for a male or female civil servant shall be determined as follows:

A- For a husband or wife: 20% of the minimum wage in public administrations.

B- For each dependent child: 11% of the minimum wage mentioned above, provided that the amount of the allowance for children does not exceed 55% thereof.

C- The family allowance shall cover all full-time contractors in public administrations and the Lebanese University, pensioners, and full-time collaborators with the Ministry of Information.

The family allowance shall accrue with effect from the first day of the month following the date of making the necessary registration in the civil status register, or the date of the occurrence of the event that created a right to the allowance if such event does not require registration in the said register.

"The family allowance shall also accrue starting from the month following the occurrence of an event taking place between 26/2/1975 and 31/3/1978, after its registration is made in the civil status register.

Where it is impossible to make the registration in the civil status register due to force majeure, the family allowance shall not accrue with effect from the first day of the month following the date of the occurrence of the event until after such registration is made and after verification, where necessary, by the Central Inspection of the existence of the elements of force majeure.
The family allowance shall cease with effect from the first day of the month following the date of forfeiture of the right thereto.
The family allowance shall be disbursed pursuant to a written declaration submitted by the civil servant together with all necessary documents to the administration to which he belongs.

Every civil servant who forfeits a right to the family allowance must submit a written declaration to that effect to the administration to which he belongs within one month from the date of forfeiture of the right.

If he delays without excuse in submitting this declaration, or omits to submit it, or submits a false declaration, his matter must be referred to the Central Inspection Board to take the requisite measures against him.
Civilian and military pensioners shall benefit from the family allowance on an equal footing with active civil servants.

In the event of the death of a pensioner, the persons entitled to the pension shall benefit from the full family allowance until an event occurs that causes them to forfeit their right to the pension or the allowance.

Where the number of children exceeds five, the allowance shall be distributed among them in equal shares.

In the event of multiple wives, the wife's allowance shall be distributed among them on the same basis.

Distribution shall be recalculated whenever the number of children or wives decreases.

The State shall provide means of transport to employees or reimburse them for the transport fares they incur in the following cases:

1- If the employee is transferred to a position the duty station of which is in a place other than the duty station of his previous position, unless the transfer is made at his request.

2- If the employee is assigned a mission outside his duty station.

3- If the service of the employee terminates and he requests to return to his original place of residence.

The employee shall be transported:

A- If he is of the First Category: in a whole car or in the first class of other means of transport.

And if he is of the Second Grade: in a whole car, or in the tourist class of air means of transport, or in the first class of other means of transport.

B - If he is of the Third Category: in a single seat - per passenger - in a car or in the second class of other means of transport.

C- If he is of the other categories: in a single seat - per passenger - in a car or in the third class of other means of transport.

D- Assistant inspectors may travel in a whole car.

An employee may travel in a whole car, whatever his category may be:

1- With the approval of the competent Director General, Director, or Head of Service, in the following cases:

A- If there are no shared means of transport along his route of travel.

B - If the mission requires stopping along the way in more than one place.

C- If the mission requires the transport of public funds.

2- With the approval of the Director General in exceptional or urgent cases.

An employee who is entitled to travel in a whole car may use his private car, and the Administration shall not be held liable for any damage that may be caused to his car or to third parties during the execution of the mission, whatever the cause, nature, or source of the damage may be.
An employee who travels continuously within the seat of the Governorate may be granted a lump-sum monthly transport allowance, the amount of which shall be determined by decree.

An employee shall be entitled to transport with him, at the expense of the State, the members of his family in the cases set forth in paragraphs (1 and 3) of Article 14 of this Decree.

Members of the family shall mean the wife and the children for whom the employee receives the family allowance or who are in his custody.

An employee shall be entitled to transport with him, at the expense of the State, his personal luggage and effects in the cases set forth in paragraphs (1 and 2) of Article 14 of this Decree.

Provided that the shipped weight does not exceed ten tons for employees of the upper three categories and five tons for employees of the other categories.

The Real Estate Register is the collection of documents which show the descriptions of each real property, determine its legal status, stipulate the rights accruing to and encumbering it, and show the transactions and modifications relating to it. This Register consists of the Property Ledger and the complementary documents (the Daily Journal, "the demarcation and census minutes", "and the cadastral maps", the photographic drawings by means of aeroplanes, the survey drawings and the supporting papers).
The Real Estate Register shall be kept for each real estate circumscription.
Each village or town shall constitute within its boundaries a real estate circumscription.
The Real Estate Register shall be opened in each real estate circumscription following the completion of the demarcation and census operations in that circumscription.

Every immovable property shall be registered on a special folio of the Property Ledger and a special number shall be assigned to it.

Immovable properties shall be registered in the Property Ledger pertaining to the circumscription to which those properties belong, by extracting the descriptions derived from the final demarcation and census minutes and on the basis of the cadastral map in the circumscriptions in which plotting has taken place, or the photographic drawing or the survey drawing in other circumscriptions.

Public properties shall not be registered unless there are real rights in their favour or encumbering them to be registered, and conversely, the entry of every registered real property shall be struck off the Register if it enters into the public properties.
The rules of the Real Estate Register and the sections of the folio shall be determined by virtue of regulatory provisions.

Immovable real rights the creation of which is authorised by law, real estate registrations, attachments, as well as real estate actions relating to an immovable property or to immovable property in the ownership register.
