And they shall not be deemed to exist vis-à-vis third parties except by their entry in the Real Estate Register and commencing from the date of such entry.

There must also compulsorily be entered on the principal folio of the immovable property all alterations occurring in the boundaries and all easements arising following construction or following the alignment of roads, watercourses, canals, and railways so that they may be invoked against third parties.

There must also be entered the supervening state occurring to the immovable property following the erection of new buildings or following a change in the existing buildings or following a demarcation of boundaries. Owners and the relevant public administrations shall notify the Registrar of the Real Estate Register for this purpose of all changes occurring to the immovable properties.

Every agreement between two parties, whether gratuitous or for consideration, a judgment having acquired final degree, and generally every act aimed at creating a real right or transferring, declaring, modifying, or annulling such right, shall be registered in the Property Ledger.

"And likewise judgments declaring bankruptcy and judgments declaring the opening of judicial liquidation in respect of immovable real rights included in the assets of bankrupts."

Voluntary instruments and agreements relating to the creation of a real right or the transfer, declaration, modification, or annulment thereof shall not be effective, even as between the contracting party, except as from the date of their registration, and this shall not prejudice the mutual right of the contracting parties to bring a claim in respect of the non-performance of their agreement.

These provisions shall apply in particular to real estate instruments and agreements, waqf deeds, and deeds of partition of waqf rights which are drawn up or authenticated by notaries public and the Sharia courts.

Contracts of farm lease and lease, and every quittance or settlement in respect of a sum equivalent to more than one year's unmatured rent or farm lease consideration, may be entered in the Real Estate Register.

Whoever acquires a right in immovable property relying on the entries and statements of the Real Estate Register shall retain such acquired right. The grounds for depriving him of this right arising from lawsuits instituted in accordance with the provisions of Article 31 of Decision No. 186 issued on 15 March 1926 and Article 17 of this Decision cannot be invoked against him, and the judgments relating to these lawsuits cannot decree the annulment of the right acquired and entered in the legal manner.

However, third parties who knew, prior to acquiring the right, of the existence of defects or grounds calling for the annulment of the right or for depriving its acquirer thereof cannot invoke the effect of the entries.

In all cases, the injured party retains the right to institute a personal action for damages against the person who caused the damage.

Registration shall be deemed irregular if effected without right. Anyone who is injured by a registration transaction may directly invoke the illegality of the registration against a third party in bad faith.

Every person whose rights have been injured by reason of an entry, modification, or cancellation effected without lawful cause may obtain the annulment or modification thereof.

No annulment or modification whatsoever may be effected in the entries of the Real Estate Register without a judicial decision, unless the interested parties consent thereto in writing. However, the Registrar, Chief of the Real Estate Office, shall rectify ipso jure simple clerical errors under the conditions provided for in Articles 29, 30, and 31 of Decision No. 189, and if the interested parties object thereto, the Real Estate Registrar shall request the rectification from the judge. In all cases, the old entries must remain as they are. Rectification shall be effected by means of a new entry, an annotation, or a provisional entry - on the date it is effected, without having retroactive effect.

The preceding rules shall apply in the event of the rectification of an error in the cadastral map resulting from an omission or from a discrepancy between the indications mentioned in the map and the documents of the Real Estate Register.

In no case may the annulment or modification be invoked against third parties in good faith, and the decision rendered for annulment or modification cannot decree the annulment of rights acquired and legally entered prior to the disputed entry. In such case, the injured party may invoke the provisions of Article 14 above in the last paragraph.

Leases made public by their entry in the Real Estate Register in accordance with the provisions of Article Eleven shall have effect against rights registered subsequent thereto; however, if they are not registered, they shall have no effect against third parties for any period exceeding a lease of three years.

Whosoever has his name registered in the capacity of owner of any immovable property may not have his rights objected to, and the registration shall acquire conclusive probative force if two years have elapsed since the registration of an immovable property without any objection to the ownership having occurred and been entered in the Property Register, or if objections occurred and were repelled.

The interested parties may, where fraud exists only, institute an action of bequest for damages against the perpetrator of the fraud, in addition to the application of the rules relating to the priority of the State and its officials in accordance with the legal provisions in force.
Prescription may not be invoked to object to the rights registered in the Land Register.

The registration formalities pertaining to any immovable property shall be carried out upon the declarations of the owner of that immovable property; nevertheless, such declarations shall not be necessary where the applicant for registration relies upon the law and upon a judgment having acquired final degree, or upon an instrument by virtue of which registration may be carried out directly or which expressly contains the declaration of the owner of the immovable property, subject to what shall be set forth in the second paragraph of Article 49 below.

The registration of rights pertaining to distrained persons shall be carried out upon the request of their natural guardians and their testamentary guardians, or of such departments as stand in their stead as are charged by virtue of the laws in force with administering the properties of distrained persons and supervising the same, and failing that, upon the request of the denominational judge of the community to which the interdicted person belongs or the consul to whom he pertains.

The formality of registering the rights pertaining to a married woman whose personal status to which that woman is subject requires that she be specifically prohibited from disposition shall be carried out upon the request of the person who represents that woman according to the provisions of personal status.

The rights pertaining to any waqf shall be registered upon the request of its administrator, and failing that, upon the Waqf Administration.

Whosoever disposes without dispute of an unregistered immovable property and in the capacity of owner of the property for a period exceeding the legal period of prescription for a civil action may request the registration of that immovable property in his name in the capacity of his being the owner thereof.

In this case, the formality of registration shall only be carried out pursuant to a legal judgment.

Upon the registration of any right, there must be mentioned, in addition to the holder of that right, the name of the person having the right of disposal thereof, and if it is a waqf, the name of the beneficiaries shall be registered.

Anyone who claims any right in an immovable property registered in the Real Property Register may request the registration of a provisional entry in order to preserve such right provisionally, and the same rule shall apply to anyone whose request was refused in order to seek the fulfilment of the required conditions.

Except for the cases in which the request for the registration of the provisional entry is based upon an official instrument or upon the agreement of the interested parties, no provisional entry may be registered unless it is based upon an order from the President of the Court of First Instance in the place where the immovable property is situated.

The rank of priority pertaining to the registration of the right subsequently shall be determined as from the date of the provisional entry.

When the request for the registration of the provisional entry is based upon an official instrument, its effect shall lapse after the expiry of ten days; if the request for the registration of the provisional entry is based upon the agreement of the two parties, its effect shall lapse upon the expiration of the agreed period.

If the request for the registration of the provisional entry is based upon an authorisation from the President of the Court of First Instance, its effect shall lapse after the expiry of one month if the action in respect thereof has not been brought and this has not been recorded during the said period in the Real Property Register; and in all cases, the effect of the provisional entry shall lapse if the definitive registration is not effected within the six months following the provisional entry.

Registration and provisional entries registered in the Real Property Register may be cancelled pursuant to a deed or a judgment having acquired the force of res judicata establishing, as against all interested parties in a right declared by registration, the non-existence or lapse of the right or the object to which they relate.
They may also be cancelled either by the agreement of the two parties established in the due ways or forthwith under the conditions provided for in the laws in force.
Every provisional entry drawn up in the Real Property Register in respect of which the time-limits provided for in Article 26 of this Resolution have elapsed must be cancelled forthwith.

Conformity must be permanent and complete between the Real Property Register and the cadastral maps with respect to the areas in which mapping has taken place, and between it and the photographic plans or map drawings in the remaining areas.

The Registrar and Chief of the Real Property Office shall notify the departments charged with keeping the cadastral maps, survey drawings and photographic maps, without the slightest delay, of every transaction of registration resulting in the creation of a right of ownership or a modification in the particulars of the aforementioned maps.

The Registrar, Chief of the Real Property Office, shall send in the first month of each year a schedule showing the changes that occurred within the preceding year to the Administration charged with keeping and applying the maps, and the said Administration shall send to the Registrar, Chief of the Real Property Office, a schedule under the same conditions showing therein the material modifications effected in respect of each immovable property.

Every annotation written in the Real Estate Register must be authenticated by the official stamp of the Real Estate Office and by the personal signature of the Chief, failing which it shall be null and void.

The owner of the property alone, to the exclusion of others, shall be entitled to obtain a complete true copy of the folio of the real property, and this copy shall be drawn up in the name of the person and the Registrar, Chief of the Real Estate Office, shall certify its authenticity by signing it with his personal signature and with the official seal of the department; as for other persons, they shall only be entitled to obtain a certificate of the entry of their registered rights.

When the real property is held in common between two or more persons, each of them shall be given a duplicate of its entry, the necessary annotations shall be written on the folio, and the number of duplicates given shall be mentioned on each duplicate.
Every registration or caveat on the folio must be registered at the same time the duplicate.

If he does not produce the duplicate and the application relates to the registration of a right the creation of which requires obtaining the consent of the registered owner of the property, the Registrar must reject this application. In all other cases, the Registrar shall register the requested entry and notify it to the holder of the right registered in the Register, and no registration whatsoever may be requested with the consent of this holder of the right before complete conformity between the folio and the duplicate is renewed.

The Registrar must certify the conformity of the duplicate with the folio whenever requested to do so.

The Real Estate Registrar must give, upon the request of the owner or the holder of any registered right whatsoever, a general or special statement of the annotations mentioned in the Real Estate Register and a copy or abstract of the supplementary documents.
Every modification that alters the status of the real property or its legal nature its recording in the Real Estate Register.

When the registered real property is subdivided by reason of partition or for any other reason, a sworn surveyor shall be entrusted with demarcating each parcel and fixing the dividing boundaries, and this operation shall be transferred onto the illustrated map, the cadastral map, or the survey plan; then a special folio shall be established for each parcel of the real property; provided that, when a parcel of the real property leaves the possession of the owner, he shall be entitled to request the retention of the old folio for the remaining parcel in his possession, and if the Registrar, Chief of the Real Estate Office, deems that the retention of the folio is possible, he shall write the necessary terms therein.

Where several properties are of one legal category and contiguous, yet form a single block registered in different folios and belonging to one owner, they may be combined and registered in a single folio; likewise, any section or several sections of a property or of contiguous properties of one legal category and belonging to one owner may either be consolidated and registered a single folio, or be consolidated with a contiguous property previously registered, and in such case the maps and the folio must be amended as required.

When it is established, the age of the minor or the ground of interdiction must be declared, and when the minor attains his majority or the interdiction ceases, the minor who has attained majority and the interdicted person who has become free to dispose may obtain the declaration of the folio.

When the folio is established or a real right is registered therein in the name of a married woman who does not have unrestricted disposal in the administration of her property having regard to the provisions of her personal status, the requisite annotation thereof shall be drawn up in the folio, and when the woman acquires freedom of disposal in the administration of her property, she may obtain the rectification of the folio.

When the Registrar, Chief of the Land Registry Office, establishes a new folio, he shall cancel the previous folio by placing the cancellation mark and the seal of the Land Registry Office on each of its pages, and he shall cancel in the same manner the duplicate and preserve it among the papers of the Office.

Contracts required to be made public by their registration in the Land Register may be proved by an oral or written declaration before the Assistant Chief of the Office in the district in which the property is situated by an ordinary instrument. Where the instruments are executed in a foreign country, they must be drawn up in authentic form; provided that, in such case, contracts of mortgages, sales with right of redemption, and sales of rent-charge may be drawn up by virtue of ordinary instruments certified by the competent authorities in accordance with the procedures and rules prescribed in the laws in force.

The rules in force concerning the proof of waqf and the rights arising from the partitioning of waqf, as well as the rules relating to inheritance and wills, shall remain as determined in the laws in force.

Notaries public and Sharia courts are prohibited from accepting or certifying any instrument, agreement, waqf deed, or title document relating to the partitioning of a waqf in respect of a property not registered in the Land Register, and no action whatsoever may be heard in respect of an unregistered property before its registration in the Land Register first; furthermore, public officials are bound to request forthwith the registration of every instrument or agreement they receive if it relates to a right subject to registration, and every contravention of the foregoing provisions by public officials shall entail punishment by a pecuniary fine of five or ten Syrian pounds for each unregistered instrument or judgment.

Every applicant or objector who applies for a transaction to be carried out in his name, whether the registration of an entry or the recording of provisional entries in the Real Estate Register, shall elect a domicile within the district of the Real Estate Office if his original domicile is not situated therein.

Whoever applies for the registration of any right shall appear in person or send an agent on his behalf to the Auxiliary Office in the district of the real property, and if the registration is based on a contract between two parties, both of them must appear, another to prove his agency by producing an official power of attorney fulfilling the conditions provided for in the laws in force.

Whoever applies for the registration of a transaction in his capacity as an agent for another shall prove his agency by producing an official power of attorney fulfilling the conditions provided for in the laws in force.

The application for registration shall be submitted to the Head of the Auxiliary Office, and this Head shall receive the declaration in writing or orally from the applicants and record it in a minute containing the following:

1- The designation of the real property sought to be registered by stating the number of the folio in which that real property is registered.

2- The identity of the owner of the property and the identity of the person in whose name the right is to be registered.

3- The nature of the right sought to be registered.

4- The manner of acquisition of the said right and the amount of its price.

5- Stating the special provisions where applicable (the amount of the debt. The amount of the interest and commission, the type of currency stipulated, the manner of payment and before maturity, the restriction imposed on the right of disposal, and the annotations or particulars sought to be registered with the principal right).

The minute shall be drawn up in three copies and signed by the applicant or by the two parties if the registration relates to a contract between two parties, and there shall be attached to the minute the title deed and, where applicable, an original copy or a certified copy of every deed, instrument or notice, whether its production is optional or compulsory according to the provisions in force, and the minute must contain the declarations of the owner of the property or the instrument that dispenses with them. If the application for registration is based on a contract between the two parties, the mutual consent of the two contracting parties must be declared therein, whereas the enforcement notices relied upon in the application for registration must be notified to the Head of the Auxiliary Office through the Enforcement Department.

The Head of the Auxiliary Office shall undertake, on his own responsibility, the verification of the identity of the applicants and their capacity within the provisions provided for in Articles 42, 43, 44, 45, 46 and 47 of the Notaries Public Law dated 15 October of the year 1329, and this verification must be mentioned in the body of the minute, which the Head of the Auxiliary Office shall sign with the witnesses.

If the two parties do not know how to sign, they must acknowledge the authenticity of the contents of the document before one of the following authorities:

1- Notaries public.

2- Presidents of courts or justices of the peace.

3- Consuls with respect to foreigners, and the acknowledgement of the authenticity of the contents of the instrument must take place in the presence of two male witnesses possessing legal capacity.

The aforementioned authorities shall certify that the authenticity of the contents of the instrument was acknowledged, and shall sign it together with the witnesses; and if the names of the witnesses, their personal status and their place of residence are unknown, or if the witnesses are not personally known to the notary public, the president of the court, or the authorities before whom the signature was certified and the acknowledgement took place, they must be identified by two identifying witnesses known to them, possessing the same qualifications provided for above.

The identity of the two parties shall also be deemed verified when the instrument is drawn up in foreign countries, provided that the signatures affixed at the foot of the submitted instruments bear the endorsement and legalisation provided for in the laws in force, without which they are void.

Applications lodged with the head of the auxiliary office by an official department must be signed and certified with the official seal or stamp of that department. The official departments intended by this Decision are the departments of the Government, the provinces (liwas), the districts (qadas), the municipalities, and public institutions.

If one of the formalities provided for in Articles 48, 49, 50, 51, 52 and 53 and Articles 56, 57, 59, 60 and 61 of this Law is incomplete, the head of the auxiliary office must require the applicants to prove their identity and capacity to contract before the Registrar, head of the Land Registry Office, in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

The head of the auxiliary office must nevertheless send the record and the submitted documents to the Registrar, head of the Land Registry Office

and shall state at the foot of the record the nature of the supplementary information required to be requested from the applicants.

The head of the auxiliary office must keep a daily register in which he enters under a serial number the transactions submitted to him and the papers he receives, and he shall enter the date and number of registration in the daily register and on the record sheet, and shall give the applicant a receipt stating the date and number of the daily register in which each application is entered, and shall carry out the transactions in order according to the date of registration of the application in the daily register.
The daily register shall be established in two copies, one of which shall be sent in the month following its closure to the Land Registry Office in the region in order to be preserved therein.

If the two parties do not know how to sign or are unable to sign, they shall acknowledge the authenticity of the contents of the record in the presence of the Head of the Auxiliary Office and in the presence of two male witnesses who know how to sign and who possess the capacity to contract, and the Head of the Office shall then certify that the acknowledgement of the authenticity of the contents of the record took place and shall sign it with his signature together with the witnesses, and if the names of the two parties or their place of residence are unknown to the Head of the Auxiliary Office before whom the acknowledgement of the authenticity of the contents of the record took place, their identity shall be attested by two witnesses known to me and possessing the aforementioned qualifications, and in all cases the Head of the Auxiliary Office shall certify at the foot of the declaration that the two witnesses are personally known to him.

Notwithstanding the provisions of the preceding Article 49, the two parties may apply for registration in the Real Estate Register without appearing in person at the Auxiliary Office to apply for registration in the Real Estate Register without appearing in person at the Auxiliary Office or sending an agent on their behalf, provided that they act in accordance with the following provisions:

The application for registration shall be drawn up in the form of a petition addressed to the Head of the Auxiliary Office located in the district of the real property, provided that such petition contains the following:

1- The number of the folio in which the real property covered by the registration is entered.

2- The identity of the owner of the property and the identity of the person in whose name the right is to be registered.

3- The nature of the right sought to be registered.

4- A statement of the manner in which this right was acquired and the amount of its price.

5- Where applicable, a statement of the special provisions (the amount of the loan . the rate of the interest stipulated, the type of currency in which payment is stipulated to be made, the manner of payment prior to maturity, and the conditions of rescission.

And the restriction imposed on the right of disposal over the real property and the annotations sought to be registered together with the principal right, and in addition to all of that, the name of the identity of the person in whose name the right is to be registered shall be stated.

The application shall be submitted in three copies and shall be subject to stamp duties, and it must be signed by the petitioner with the signature officially legalized, and there shall be attached thereto, where applicable, the original and a certified copy of a deed, instrument, or judgment extract submitted with the petition, and if the application is set forth upon a contract between two parties, the title deed must be attached thereto, whereas enforcement writs submitted with the application must have been served through the Enforcement Department.
The Head of the Auxiliary Office shall, on his own responsibility, undertake the verification of the identity of the two parties and their capacity to contract.

If multiple applications are submitted to the office on a single day in respect of a single real property, the rank of priority of the rights encumbering the said real property shall be determined as from the hour of filing the application; whereas if multiple applications are received in respect of a single real property the filing of which at the office coincided at one and the same time, the necessary annotation regarding this case shall be drawn up in the register and the rights shall be registered concurrently.

When the preliminary formalities are completed, the head of the auxiliary office shall proceed to liquidate the required fees and shall draw up a remittance slip therefor in three copies, the authenticity of which he shall certify by affixing his signature together with the official seal at the foot thereof.

The head of the auxiliary office must also liquidate the amount of the fixed annual rent (muqata'a) and the deferred rent (mu'ajjala) accruing to the pious endowments (awqaf) and draw up for the total thereof a special remittance slip in three copies as well, in the manner set forth above.

A copy of the aforementioned remittance slips shall be delivered or sent in a registered envelope to the applicant, who is required to prove payment of the amount by producing the receipts given to him by the treasurer of the Government or the treasurer of the Administration of Pious Endowments (Awqaf).

The head of the auxiliary office must send, within the twenty-four hours following the production of the receipts referred to in the preceding article, a copy of the record sheet together with the supporting documents and the receipts for the fees or the receipts for the pious endowments (awqaf) revenues referred to, to the Registrar, head of the Land Registry Office, who gave a receipt acknowledging receipt thereof.

A copy of the application and a copy of each of the remittance slips showing the fees or the pious endowments (awqaf) revenues, and the receipt given by the Registrar, shall be kept in the department of the auxiliary office.

The head of the auxiliary office must enter in the daily register the date of dispatch of the record and the documents submitted therewith to the Land Registry Office, on the very same day on which he sends them.

The Registrar, head of the Land Registry Office, must verify in person and on his own responsibility whether the formalities provided for in this Resolution have been duly completed, and shall likewise verify the legality and validity of the documents submitted with the application, both as to their form and as to their substance.

The Registrar, Chief of the Real Estate Office, shall verify that the transaction in respect of which the application is made is not at variance with the wording of the entries of the Real Estate Register nor with the provisions of this Law, and that the documents submitted permit the carrying out of the registration.

If the Registrar, Chief of the Real Estate Office, sees that there is an impediment preventing the carrying out of the registration, he may withhold from the applicant a suitable time limit for the removal of the impediment or reject the transaction; in the first case, the application shall be dismissed upon the expiry of the appointed time limit if the applicant is unable to prove the removal of the impediment within the said time limit.

If a second application is submitted during the time limit granted to the first applicant for the purpose of removing the impediment, the Registrar, Chief of the Real Estate, may immediately draw up provisional precautionary entries in the name of the said first applicant, and if his application is subsequently rejected, these precautionary entries shall also be immediately annulled.

If several applications are received together, or the execution of some of them prevents the execution of the others, the Registrar, Chief of the Real Estate Office, shall notify the applicants thereof and fix for them a time limit for the removal of the impediment; if it cannot be removed within the fixed period, the applications shall be rejected in their entirety.

The provisions of Articles 48 to 61 relating to registration shall also be observed in transactions for the striking out of entries, and in addition thereto, the following matters must be mentioned in the record drawn up by the Chief of the Auxiliary Office, namely:

1- The number of the folio in which the real property to which the striking out relates is registered.

2- The designation of the endorsement or precautionary entry requested to be struck out.

3- The statement of the cause of the striking out and the nature of the instrument or document supporting this cause.

The Registrar, Chief of the Real Estate Office, shall verify on his own responsibility that the documents submitted permit the striking out without contravening the particulars of the entries of the Real Estate Register or the provisions of this Law.

The endorsement of the striking out shall be drawn up on the folio of the real property, and this endorsement shall be dated and signed by the Registrar, Chief of the Real Estate Office, with his signature and the official seal, and the cause which permitted the striking out shall be mentioned; otherwise, the transaction of striking out shall be deemed null and void.
If the Chief of the Real Estate Office rejects an application for registration or striking out, the decision of rejection may be appealed to the local court.

Every opposition to the completion of a real property transaction must be notified through the enforcement officer to the Registrar, Head of the Land Registry Office, who shall register it on the folio of the real property. After such notification, no new transaction may be carried out in respect of that real property. If eight days elapse during which no lawsuit is brought before the court regarding that real property and the lawsuit is not entered on the folio of the real property, the Registrar must cancel the opposition forthwith.

Every real property attachment decision must be notified to the Registrar, Head of the Land Registry Office, through the Enforcement Department, and thereafter no new transaction may be carried out in respect of the said real property during the course of the expropriation transaction.

Whenever the registration of a right agreed upon between two parties is requested after the death of the holder of the right, it may be registered either upon producing a document permitting the registration to be carried out forthwith or upon producing an application signed with the signature of the holder of the right, provided that the signature of the holder of the right is officially authenticated.

If the entry requested to be registered relates to a contract of securities, a sale with right of redemption, or a sale of an annuity, it may be carried out merely by the signature of the acquirer of the right on an ordinary instrument, provided that the signature is officially authenticated in accordance with the provisions of Articles 57, 58 and 59 of this Decision.

Real property rights in rem arising from inheritance may not be registered in the names of their registrants unless the applicants produce, in addition to proof of the death of their legator, where the inheritance is intestate, certificates proving the identity of each of them and his right to the inheritance. The inheritance rights belonging to legal heirs or natural heirs must be proved by virtue of a certificate of inheritance with respect to mulk properties, or by virtue of a certificate issued by the Civil Status Department or by the competent consulate with respect to amiri lands. If the inheritance is designated by virtue of a will, the applicant must produce the instrument of the will or the decision issued on the part of the judicial authority vested with the execution of the will.
Every person is entitled to obtain the information entered in the Land Register in return for payment of the statutory fee for inspection and copying.

In order to obtain this, the interested parties must submit an application to the Registrar, Head of the Real Estate Office, to be given the following documents as required:

- A certificate attesting the conformity of the real estate folio to the copy which is the title deed.

- A copy of the real estate folio and of the annotations contained therein or the annotations requested by the interested party in his petition.

- A certificate of the non-existence of an entry in the Real Estate Register.

- An official copy valid before the courts of a deed or any other document kept among the papers pertaining to a registered real property.

- A copy or abstract of the map pertaining to registered real properties and kept in the Real Estate Office.

If the interested parties do not know how to sign, the applications pertaining to the request for one of the aforementioned documents shall be drawn up and signed with their permission by the Registrar.
The Registrar may give, upon a legal request, all information pertaining to the real properties or to the rights relating thereto, by way of simple information.

The public may inspect the folio of the real property which the interested parties request in writing, provided that they pay the inspection fee and that such inspection takes place in the presence of the Registrar, Head of the Real Estate Office, or one of his employees; provided, however, that they shall not be permitted to copy any entry whatsoever or to take any abstract whatsoever thereof.
If the application for inspection, copies, or documents is submitted by an official administration for a public interest or for the needs of the departments, no fees shall be levied thereon.

If the copy of the folio or the certificate given in respect of an entry is lost, its holder must appear in person before the Registrar, Head of the Real Estate Office, accompanied by the witnesses who have knowledge of the cause of the destruction or loss of the original copy, and his statement shall be taken in the form of a record in which shall be mentioned all the information indicating his identity and relating to the encumbrances and mortgages charging the real property, and the record shall be concluded with his signature and the signatures of the witnesses, those present, and the Registrar, Head of the Real Estate Office; this record shall then be published in the Official Gazette of the Government and in three other local newspapers, and if a period of fifteen days elapses and no objector appears during it, the Registrar may, if he is convinced of the veracity of the declarations of the petitioner, give him a second certified true copy of the folio, provided that the circumstances in which it was given are mentioned therein.

The Registrar must mention in the Ownership Register that a copy of the folio or a provisional certificate of the provisional entry was given, and state the date on which it was given and the circumstances in which it was given. The copy or provisional certificate given in the foregoing manner shall have the force of the original copy itself and shall take its place.

Lebanon is an independent State, of an indivisible unity and complete sovereignty. As for its boundaries

they are those that bound it at present:

In the north: From the mouth of Nahr Al-Kabir along a line accompanying the course of the river to the point of its confluence with Wadi Khaled pouring into it at the height of Jisr Al-Qamar.

In the east: The crest line separating Wadi Khaled and the valley of Nahr Al-Assi

(Orontes) passing by the villages of Muaissra - Harbaana - Hait - Ebbech - Faissan at the height of the two villages of Brina and Matraba, and this line follows the northern boundaries of the district of Baalbek from the north-eastern direction and the south-eastern

direction then the eastern boundaries of the districts of Baalbek, the Bekaa, Hasbaya and Rashaya.

In the south: The present southern boundaries of the two districts of Tyre and Marjayoun.

In the west: The Mediterranean Sea.
No part of the Lebanese territory may be alienated or ceded.
The boundaries of the administrative areas may not be modified except pursuant to a law.
Greater Lebanon is a Republic whose capital is Beirut.

The Lebanese flag is red, white, and red in horizontal stripes, with the cedar in the middle of the white stripe in green.

As for the size of the white stripe, it is equal to the size of the two red stripes together.

As for the cedar, it is in the middle, its top touching the upper red stripe and its base touching the lower red stripe, and the size of the cedar shall be equivalent to one-third of the size of the white stripe.
Lebanese nationality and the manner in which it is acquired, retained and lost shall be determined in accordance with the law.
All Lebanese are equal before the law, and they equally enjoy civil and political rights and bear public burdens and duties without any distinction among them.

Personal liberty is inviolable and under the protection of the law, and no person may be arrested, imprisoned or detained except in accordance with the provisions of the law, and no offence may be defined or penalty prescribed except in accordance with the law.

Any person who commits any of the following acts shall be punished under the offence of forgery and the use of forged documents in accordance with the provisions of the Penal Code:

1- Any person who intentionally and for the purpose of securing an unlawful benefit for any person counterfeits, forges or alters title deeds, documents and certificates issued by the Registrar, Chief of the Real Estate Office, in accordance with the provisions of this Decision, and any person who uses the forged, counterfeited and altered documents.

2- Any person who commits forgery in the documents submitted for registration or for striking off, whether by counterfeiting or altering the writing or signature, or by substituting persons, or by altering the contents of agreements, judgments and discharges, or by inserting them subsequently into the said documents, or by adding or altering conditions, declarations or facts which such documents are intended to record or establish.
The time limits provided for in this Decision shall be calculated in accordance with the rules prescribed in the Code of Civil Procedure.
The tariff of expenses and fees shall temporarily remain as prescribed in the laws in force.
The details and clarifications relating to the implementation of the provisions of this Decision shall be determined by a decision to be issued subsequently.

The provisions of this Decision shall apply in all areas in which demarcation and census operations have been carried out in accordance with the provisions of the Decision on the Demarcation and Census of Immovable Property. All provisions contrary to the content of this Decision are repealed and shall remain repealed.
The Secretary-General is charged with the implementation of this Decision.

If an objection is made to the issuance of the copy, or if the Registrar considers that the application submitted to him ought not to be granted, the applicant shall be entitled to appeal the application to the Court of First Instance in the locality, which shall adjudicate the matter in accordance with the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure.

The Registrar shall be personally liable for damages arising from the following:

1- From his omission to register an entry, a provisional entry, or a striking off in the Register where so requested in a lawful manner.

2- If he omits to record an entry, a provisional entry, or a striking-off entry existing in the Land Register on the copy or abstract issued and signed by him.

3- From the illegality or nullity of provisional entries and striking off in the Land Register. The Head of the Auxiliary Office is personally liable for damages arising from the following:

1- From an error or omission in the daily register.

2- From any omission or illegality in the declarations and minutes which he receives and draws up.

3- From an error in the liquidation of expenses, fees, and Waqf revenues.

4- From delay in forwarding the minutes and documents submitted to him, subject to the provisions of the laws in force concerning the liability of public officials.

In all the foregoing cases, the Government shall be civilly liable in the event of his inability to pay.

The Head of the Auxiliary Office shall not be entitled to refuse to perform the duties of his office when requested to do so, save in the cases expressly provided for by law, nor may he delay the completion of the required transactions or delay forwarding the applications received by him to the Registrar, Head of the Real Estate Office. The Registrar, Head of the Real Estate Office, alone shall have the right to refuse registration, and if this official refuses registration, he must return to the Auxiliary Office the papers and documents deposited with him, accompanied by a written declaration setting forth the reasons for the refusal.

Freedom of conscience is absolute. In rendering homage to God Almighty, the State shall respect all religions and denominations and shall guarantee the freedom to hold religious rites under its protection, provided that public order is not disturbed thereby, and it shall also guarantee for the population, of whatever denomination they may be, respect for the system of personal status and religious interests.

Education is free insofar as it does not disturb public order, run counter to morals, or touch upon the dignity of any of the religions or denominations.

The rights of religious communities to establish their own private schools may not be infringed,

provided that they proceed in this in accordance with the general regulations issued by the State concerning public instruction.

The Arabic language is the official national language.

As for the French language, the cases in which it shall be used shall be determined by a law.

Every Lebanese has the right to hold public office, with no preference for one over another except in terms of merit and competence in accordance with the conditions prescribed by law, and a special statute shall be established guaranteeing the rights of civil servants in the departments to which they belong.
The freedom to express opinion orally and in writing, the freedom of the press, the freedom of assembly, and the freedom to form associations are all guaranteed within the limits of the law.
The dwelling is inviolable and no one is permitted to enter it except in the cases and manners set forth in the law.

Property is under the protection of the law, and no one may be deprived of his property except on grounds of public utility and in the cases provided for by law and after fair compensation has been paid to him therefor.
Legislative power shall be vested in a single body, which is the Chamber of Deputies.

.

Executive power shall be vested in the Council of Ministers. It shall exercise it in accordance with the provisions of this Constitution.
The Chamber of Deputies and the Council of Ministers shall have the right to propose laws. No law shall be promulgated unless it has been adopted by the Chamber of Deputies.

A Constitutional Council shall be established to supervise the constitutionality of laws and to adjudicate disputes and challenges arising from presidential and parliamentary elections.

The right to petition this Council with regard to supervising the constitutionality of laws shall vest in each of the President of the Republic, the Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies, the President of the Council of Ministers, or ten members of the Chamber of Deputies, and in the heads of the legally recognised confessions exclusively in matters relating to personal status, freedom of belief, the practice of religious rites, and freedom of religious education.

The rules governing the organisation of the Council, its procedure, the manner of its formation, and petitioning before it shall be determined by a law.

Judicial power shall be exercised by the courts of various levels and jurisdictions within a system established by law that secures the necessary guarantees for judges and litigants. As for the conditions and limits of judicial guarantees, they shall be determined by law.

Judges are independent in the exercise of their functions, and decisions and judgments shall be issued by all courts and executed in the name of the Lebanese People.
Every Lebanese citizen who has completed twenty-one full years of age shall have the right to be an elector, provided that he fulfils the conditions required pursuant to the election.

Upon the election of the first Chamber of Deputies on a national, non-confessional basis, a Senate shall be established in which all spiritual families shall be represented, and its powers shall be confined to fateful issues.

This article was repealed pursuant to Article 50 of the Constitutional Law dated 17 October 1927).

A member of the Senate is required to be a Lebanese who has attained thirty-five full years of age. It is not required for the validity of his election or appointment as a member of the Senate that he be resident in Greater Lebanon at the time of the elections, and a special law shall be enacted whereby the electoral districts, the eligibility of those elected, and the manner of their election shall be determined.

Until the Chamber of Deputies enacts an electoral law free of confessional restriction, the parliamentary seats shall be distributed in accordance with the following rules:

a - Equally between Christians and Muslims.

b - Proportionally among the confessions of each of the two categories.

c - Proportionally among the regions. Exceptionally, and for one time only, the parliamentary seats vacant at the date of publication of this Law and the seats newly created in the electoral law shall be filled by appointment all at once and by a two-thirds majority by the Government of National Accord, in implementation of parity between Christians and Muslims, in accordance with the Document of National Accord. The electoral law shall determine the detailed rules for the application of this Article.

If the Chamber of Deputies is dissolved, the decision of dissolution must include a call to hold new elections, and such elections shall be held in accordance with Article 24 and shall be concluded within a period not exceeding three months.
Beirut is the seat of the Government and the Chamber of Deputies.
A member of the Chamber of Deputies represents the whole Nation, and his mandate may not be bound by any restriction or condition on the part of his electors.

The office of Deputy and the office of Minister may be combined. As for Ministers, they may be selected from among the members of the Chamber of Deputies, or from among persons outside it, or from both.
The cases in which eligibility for the office of Deputy is lost shall be determined by law.

The Deputies alone shall have the right to decide on the validity of their mandate, and the election of any Deputy may not be invalidated except by a majority of two thirds of the total number of members.

This Article shall be repealed automatically immediately upon the establishment of the Constitutional Council and the entry into force of the law relating thereto.
Every meeting held by the Chamber outside the legal sessions shall be deemed automatically null and void and contrary to the law.

The Chamber shall meet each year in two ordinary sessions; the first session shall begin on the Tuesday following the 15th of the month of March and its sittings shall continue until the end of the month of May, and the second session shall begin on the Tuesday following the 15th of the month of October, and its sittings shall be devoted to the discussion of the budget and voting thereon before any other work, and the duration of this session shall last until the end of the year.

The opening of the ordinary sessions and their closing shall take place automatically at the times specified in Article thirty-two. The President of the Republic, in agreement with the Prime Minister, may convene the Chamber of Deputies to extraordinary sessions by a decree specifying their opening, their closing, and their agenda.

The President of the Republic must convene the Chamber to extraordinary sessions if the absolute majority of the total of its members so requests.

A meeting of the Chamber shall not be legal unless attended by the majority of the members who compose it, and resolutions shall be taken by a majority of votes; if the votes are equal, the proposal under discussion shall fail.

The sittings of the Chamber shall be public; provided, however, that it may meet in a secret sitting upon the request of the Government or five of its members, and it may decide to resume the discussion in a public sitting on the same subject.

Votes shall be given by oral voting or by the method of standing and sitting, except in the case where an election is intended, in which case votes shall be given by the method of secret ballot; however, with respect to laws in general or voting on the question of confidence, votes shall always be given by calling the members by their names and aloud.

The right to request a vote of no confidence is absolute for every Deputy in ordinary sessions and in extraordinary sessions, and discussion of this request shall not take place nor shall a vote be taken thereon except after the expiry of at least five days from its submission before the Secretariat of the Chamber and its communication to the Ministers concerned therewith.
Every proposed law that has not obtained the approval of the Chamber cannot be presented a second time for discussion in the same session.
No criminal action may be brought against any member of the Chamber on account of the opinions and ideas which he expresses during the term of his mandate.

During the session, no criminal proceedings may be taken against any member of the Chamber, nor may he be arrested if he has committed a criminal offence, except with the authorisation of the Chamber, save in the case of flagrante delicto (witnessed offence).

If a seat in the Chamber becomes vacant, the election of a successor must be initiated within two months. The term of office of the new member shall not exceed the term of office of the former member whom he replaces.

However, if the seat in the Chamber becomes vacant less than six months before the expiration of its term of office, no election of a successor shall be conducted.
General elections for the renewal of the body of the Chamber shall be held within the sixty days preceding the expiration of the term of office.
The Chamber may establish its own internal rules of procedure.

Each time the Chamber is newly elected, it shall meet under the presidency of its oldest member, and the two youngest members among them shall serve as secretaries. The Speaker and the Deputy Speaker shall each be elected separately for the duration of the term of the Chamber by secret ballot and by an absolute majority of the votes cast.

In a third round of balloting, the result shall be based on a relative majority, and if the votes are equal, the oldest shall be deemed elected.

Each time the Chamber is newly elected, and at the opening of the October session of each year, the Chamber shall proceed to elect two secretaries by secret ballot in accordance with the majority provided for in the first paragraph of this Article.

The Chamber may, once only, two years after the election of its Speaker and its Deputy Speaker, and in the first sitting it holds, withdraw confidence from its Speaker or its Deputy Speaker by a two-thirds majority of the total of its members pursuant to a petition signed by at least ten Deputies. The Chamber must, in this case, immediately hold a sitting to fill the vacant post.
Members of the Chamber shall not have the right to vote unless they are present at the sitting, and voting by proxy shall not be permitted.
The Chamber alone shall maintain order within itself through its Speaker.
Petitions to the Chamber may only be submitted in writing, and petitions may not be submitted orally or at the bar.
The allowances received by the members of the Chamber shall be determined by a law.

The President of the Republic is the Head of the State and the symbol of the unity of the Homeland. He shall ensure respect for the Constitution and the preservation of the independence of Lebanon, its unity, and the integrity of its territories in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution.

He shall preside over the Supreme Defence Council, and he is the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, which are subject to the authority of the Council of Ministers.

The President of the Republic shall be elected by secret ballot by a two-thirds majority of the Chamber of Deputies in the first round, and an absolute majority shall suffice in the subsequent rounds of balloting.

His presidency shall last six years and he may not be re-elected until six years after the expiry of his term of office.

No one may be elected to the Presidency of the Republic unless he fulfils the conditions qualifying him for the Chamber of Deputies and which do not preclude eligibility for candidacy.

Furthermore, judges and Grade One civil servants, and their equivalents in all public administrations, public institutions, and other legal persons of public law, may not be elected during the tenure of their office and during the two years following the date of their resignation and effective cessation of their functions or the date of their referral to retirement.

For one time and exceptionally, the term of office of the current President of the Republic shall continue for three years ending on the twenty-third of November 1998.

For one time, and exceptionally, the President of the Republic may be elected from among judges or Grade One civil servants, and their equivalents in all public administrations, public institutions, and other legal persons of public law.

For one time and exceptionally, the term of office of the current President of the Republic shall continue for three years ending on the twenty-third of November 2007.

Notwithstanding the provisions of the second and third paragraphs of this Article, the President of the Republic may, for one time, be elected from among judges or Grade One civil servants, and their equivalents in all public administrations, public institutions, and other legal persons of public law.

When the President of the Republic assumes the reins of government, he must swear before Parliament an oath of fidelity to the Nation and the Constitution in the following terms:

"I swear by Almighty God that I shall respect the Constitution of the Lebanese Nation and its laws and preserve the independence of the Lebanese Homeland and the integrity of its territories".

The President of the Republic shall promulgate the laws in accordance with the time limits specified in the Constitution after they have been approved by the Chamber, and shall request their publication, and he may not introduce any amendment thereto or exempt anyone from complying with their provisions.

The President of the Republic may, in the cases provided for in Articles 65 and 77 of this Constitution, request the Council of Ministers to dissolve the Chamber of Deputies before the expiry of the term of mandate.

If the Council of Ministers decides, pursuant thereto, to dissolve the Chamber, the President of the Republic shall issue the decree of dissolution, and in such case the electoral bodies shall meet in accordance with the provisions of the twenty-fifth Article of the Constitution, and the new Chamber shall be convened to meet within the fifteen days following the proclamation of the election.

The Bureau of the Chamber shall continue to conduct business until a new Chamber is elected.

In the event that elections are not held within the time limit provided for in the twenty-fifth Article of the Constitution, the decree of dissolution shall be deemed null and void as if it had never been, and the Chamber of Deputies shall continue to exercise its powers in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution.

The President of the Republic shall promulgate the laws which have been finally approved within one month after their referral to the Government and shall request their publication.

As for the laws with respect to which the Chamber takes a decision that their promulgation must be expedited, he must promulgate them within five days and request their publication. He shall issue decrees and request their publication, and he shall have the right to request the Council of Ministers to reconsider any decision among the decisions taken by the Council within fifteen days from the date of its filing with the Presidency of the Republic.

If the Council of Ministers insists on the decision taken, or if the time limit expires without issuing the decree or returning it, the decision or the decree shall be deemed in force by operation of law and must be published.

The President of the Republic shall have, after informing the Council of Ministers, the right to request the reconsideration of a law once within the time limit specified for its promulgation, and his request may not be refused.

When the President exercises this right of his, he shall be absolved from promulgating the law until the Chamber approves it after another deliberation thereon, and adopts it by an absolute majority of the total members who legally constitute the Chamber.

In the event that the time limit expires without promulgating the law or returning it, the law shall be deemed in force by operation of law and must be published.

Every bill that the Government decides to be urgent with the approval of the Council of Ministers, indicating this in the decree of referral, the President of the Republic may, after the lapse of forty days from its submission to the Chamber, and after its inclusion on the agenda of a plenary session and its reading therein and the lapse of this time limit without a decision being taken thereon, issue a decree putting it into force after the approval of the Council of Ministers.
The President of the Republic may adjourn the session of the Chamber for a period not exceeding one month, and he may not do so twice in the same session.

The President of the Republic shall negotiate the conclusion and ratification of international treaties in agreement with the Prime Minister.

They shall not become ratified except after the approval of the Council of Ministers.

The Government shall inform the Chamber of Deputies thereof whenever the interest of the country and the safety of the State permit.

As for treaties that involve conditions relating to the finances of the State, commercial treaties, and all other treaties that cannot be denounced year by year, they may not be ratified except after the approval of the Chamber of Deputies.

1 - The President of the Republic shall preside over the Council of Ministers whenever he wishes without participating in the vote.

2 - The President of the Republic shall designate the Prime Minister-designate in consultation with the President of the Chamber of Deputies on the basis of binding parliamentary consultations of the results of which he shall officially inform him.

3 - He shall issue the decree naming the President of the Council of Ministers individually.

4 - He shall issue, in agreement with the President of the Council of Ministers, the decree forming the Government and the decrees accepting the resignation of Ministers or dismissing them.

5 - He shall issue individually the decrees accepting the resignation of the Government or considering it as having resigned.

6 - He shall refer bills that are submitted to him by the Council of Ministers to the Chamber of Deputies.

7 - He shall accredit ambassadors and accept their accreditation.

8 - He shall preside over official ceremonies and grant State decorations by decree.

9 - He shall grant special pardon by decree. As for general amnesty, it shall not be granted except by a law.

10 - He shall address messages to the Chamber of Deputies whenever necessity requires.

11 - He shall submit any urgent matter to the Council of Ministers from outside the agenda.

12 - He shall convene the Council of Ministers in extraordinary session whenever he deems it necessary in agreement with the Prime Minister.

The decisions of the President of the Republic must be countersigned with him by the Prime Minister and the competent Minister or Ministers, except the decree naming the Prime Minister and the decree accepting the resignation of the Government or considering it as having resigned.

As for the decree promulgating laws, it shall be countersigned with him by the Prime Minister.

The President of the Republic shall incur no responsibility while performing his office except when he violates the Constitution or in the case of high treason.

As for responsibility in respect of ordinary offences, it shall be subject to the general laws, and he may not be impeached on account of these offences or on the two grounds of violating the Constitution and high treason, except by the Chamber of Deputies pursuant to a decision issued by it by a two-thirds majority of the total of its members, and he shall be tried before the Supreme Council provided for in Article eighty, and the function of the Public Prosecution before the Supreme Council shall be entrusted to a judge appointed by the Supreme Court composed of all its chambers.
The President of the Republic shall cease to perform his duties when he is impeached, and the seat of the Presidency shall remain vacant until the case is decided by the Supreme Council.
In the event that the seat of the Presidency is vacant for any reason whatsoever, the powers of the President of the Republic shall be vested in an acting capacity in the Council of Ministers.
The emoluments of the President of the Republic shall be determined by a law, and they may neither be increased nor reduced throughout the duration of his term of office.

The President of the Council of Ministers is the Head of the Government; he represents it, speaks in its name, and is considered responsible for executing the general policy set by the Council of Ministers.

He shall exercise the following powers:

1 - He chairs the Council of Ministers, and is ex officio Deputy President of the Supreme Defence Council.

2 - He conducts the parliamentary consultations for forming the Government and signs with the President of the Republic the decree of its formation.

The Government must present its ministerial statement to the Chamber of Deputies to gain confidence within a time limit of thirty days from the date of issuance of the decree of its formation. The Government shall not exercise its powers before gaining confidence nor after its resignation or its being considered resigned, except in the narrow sense of conducting caretaker business.

3 - He presents the general policy of the Government before the Chamber of Deputies.

4 - He signs with the President of the Republic all decrees, except the decree designating him Head of the Government and the decree accepting the resignation of the Government or considering it resigned.

5 - He signs the decree calling for the opening of an extraordinary session and the decrees promulgating laws and requesting their reconsideration.

6 - He convenes the Council of Ministers and sets its agenda. He informs the President of the Republic in advance of the subjects included therein and of the urgent subjects that will be discussed.

7- He follows up the work of the public administrations and institutions, coordinates among the Ministers, and gives general directives to ensure the proper conduct of work.

8- He holds working sessions with the concerned authorities in the State in the presence of the competent Minister.

Executive power shall be vested in the Council of Ministers.

It shall be the authority to which the armed forces are subject, and among the powers which it exercises are:

1 - Laying down the general policy of the State in all fields, drafting bills and regulatory decrees, and taking the decisions necessary for their implementation.

2 - Ensuring the execution of laws and regulations and supervising the work of all organs of the State, including civil, military and security administrations and institutions without exception.

3 - Appointing State officials, dismissing them and accepting their resignation in accordance with the law.

4 - Dissolving the Chamber of Deputies at the request of the President of the Republic if the Chamber of Deputies refrains, for reasons other than force majeure, from meeting throughout an ordinary session or throughout two consecutive extraordinary sessions each lasting no less than one month, or in the event that it rejects the budget in its entirety with the intent of paralysing the hand of the Government from acting.

This right may not be exercised a second time for the same reasons that called for the dissolution of the Chamber on the first occasion.

5 - The Council of Ministers shall meet periodically at a special seat, and the President of the Republic shall chair its sittings when he attends.

The legal quorum for its convening shall be a majority of two-thirds of its members, and it shall take its decisions by consensus. If that proves impossible, then by voting, and it shall take its decisions by a majority of those present.

As for fundamental subjects, they shall require the approval of two-thirds of the number of members of the Government specified in the decree of its formation.

The following shall be deemed fundamental subjects:

Amendment of the Constitution, declaration of a state of emergency and its termination, war and peace, general mobilisation, international agreements and treaties, the general budget of the State, comprehensive and long-term development plans, appointment of Category One officials or their equivalent, reconsideration of the administrative division, dissolution of the Chamber of Deputies, the electoral law, the nationality law, personal status laws, dismissal of Ministers.

None but Lebanese may assume the office of Minister, and none may assume the office of Minister unless he fulfils the conditions that qualify him for membership of the Chamber of Deputies.

Ministers shall administer the services of the State and shall be entrusted with the application of regulations and laws, each in so far as concerns the affairs pertaining to his administration and that which is assigned to him. Ministers shall bear collective responsibility before the Chamber of Deputies for the general policy of the Government, and they shall bear individual responsibility for their personal acts.

Ministers may attend the Chamber whenever they wish and shall be heard when they request the floor, and they may be assisted by whomsoever they see fit from among the officials of their administrations.
When the Chamber passes a vote of no confidence in one of the Ministers in accordance with the thirty-seventh Article, that Minister must resign.

1- The Government shall be deemed resigned in the following cases:

(a) - If its President resigns.

(b) - If it loses more than one-third of the number of its members specified in the decree forming it.

(c) - Upon the death of its President.

(d) - At the commencement of the term of office of the President of the Republic.

(e) - At the commencement of the term of office of the Chamber of Deputies.

(f) - When confidence is withdrawn from it by the Chamber of Deputies on its own initiative or pursuant to a question of confidence put by the Government.

2 - The dismissal of a Minister shall be by a decree signed by the President of the Republic and the President of the Government following the approval of two-thirds of the members of the Government.

3 - Upon the resignation of the Government or its being deemed resigned, the Chamber of Deputies shall automatically be in an extraordinary session until a new Government is formed and gains confidence.

The Chamber of Deputies may impeach the President of the Council of Ministers and the Ministers for committing high treason or for breaching the duties incumbent upon them, and the decision of impeachment may only be issued by a majority of two-thirds of the total members of the Chamber.

A special law shall determine the conditions of the civil liability of the President of the Council of Ministers and the Ministers.
The impeached President of the Council of Ministers and Minister shall be tried before the Supreme Council.

The President of the Council of Ministers or the Minister shall cease to exercise his functions immediately upon the issuance of the decision of impeachment against him, and if he resigns, his resignation shall not be a ground for not instituting proceedings against him or for staying the judicial proceedings.

At least one month or at most two months prior to the expiration of the term of office of the President of the Republic, the Chamber shall convene upon the summons of its President to elect the new President.

If the Chamber is not summoned for this purpose, it shall convene automatically on the tenth day preceding the date of expiration of the term of office of the President.

If the Presidency becomes vacant due to the death of the President, his resignation, or any other cause, the Chamber shall convene immediately by operation of law in order to elect a successor, and if the vacancy of the Presidency happens to occur while the Chamber of Deputies is dissolved, the electoral bodies shall be summoned without delay, and the Chamber shall convene by operation of law immediately upon the conclusion of the electoral operations.

The Chamber convened to elect the President of the Republic shall be deemed an electoral body and not a legislative body, and it shall proceed immediately to elect the Head of State without discussion or any other act.
The Constitution may be revised upon the proposal of the President of the Republic, whereupon the Government shall submit the bill to the Chamber of Deputies.

The Constitution may also be revised upon the request of the Chamber of Deputies, in which case the matter shall proceed in the following manner:

The Chamber of Deputies shall have the right, during an ordinary session and upon the proposal of at least ten of its members, to put forward its proposal, by a two-thirds majority of the total members of whom the Chamber is legally composed, to revise the Constitution.

Provided that the articles and issues covered by the proposal must be clearly defined and enumerated; the Speaker of the Chamber shall then communicate that proposal to the Government, requesting it to draft a bill in respect thereof. If the Government agrees with the Chamber on its proposal by a two-thirds majority, it must draft the amendment bill and submit it to the Chamber within four months; if it does not agree, it must return the decision to the Chamber for a second deliberation. If the Chamber insists upon it by a majority of three-quarters of the total members of whom the Chamber is legally composed, the President of the Republic shall then either accede to the Chamber's wish or request the Council of Ministers to dissolve it and hold new elections within three months. If the new Chamber insists upon the necessity of the amendment, the Government must comply and submit the amendment bill within a period of four months.

Where a bill relating to the amendment of the Constitution is submitted to the Chamber, it must persevere in the debate until a vote is taken thereon prior to any other business. Provided that it may neither debate nor vote except upon the articles and issues clearly defined in the bill that has been submitted to it.

When a bill relating to the amendment of the Constitution is submitted to the Chamber, it may neither examine it nor vote thereon unless a majority composed of two-thirds of the members who legally compose the Chamber is assembled, and the vote must be by the same majority.

The President of the Republic must promulgate the law relating to the amendment of the Constitution in the same form and under the same conditions whereby ordinary laws are promulgated and published, and he shall have the right, within the period prescribed for promulgation and after informing the Council of Ministers, to request the Chamber to reconsider the bill once again, the vote thereon also being taken by a two-thirds majority of the votes.

The Supreme Council, whose function is to try Presidents and Ministers, shall be composed of seven Deputies elected by the Chamber of Deputies and eight of the highest-ranking Lebanese judges according to the grades of the judicial hierarchy or, where their grades are equal, on the basis of seniority. They shall convene under the presidency of the highest-ranking of these judges, and decisions of conviction shall be issued by the Supreme Council by a majority of ten votes.

The rules of procedure before it shall be determined pursuant to a special law.

Public taxes shall be imposed, and no tax whatsoever may be instituted and collected in the Lebanese Republic, save pursuant to a comprehensive law the provisions of which apply to all Lebanese territories without exception.
No tax may be amended or abolished save by a law.

Each year, at the beginning of the October session, the Government shall submit to the Chamber of Deputies a budget encompassing the expenditures of the State and its revenues for the coming year, and the budget shall be voted upon item by item.

The Chamber may not, during the deliberation on the budget and on bills for supplementary or extraordinary appropriations, increase the appropriations proposed to it in the draft budget or in the rest of the aforementioned bills, whether in the form of an amendment introduced thereto or by way of proposal. However, upon the conclusion of that deliberation, it may enact, by way of proposal, laws instituting new expenditures.

No extraordinary appropriation may be opened save by a special law. However, if unforeseen circumstances call for urgent expenditures, the President of the Republic shall issue a decree, pursuant to a decision issued by the Council of Ministers, to open extraordinary or supplementary appropriations and to transfer appropriations in the budget, provided that these appropriations in the budget do not exceed provided that these appropriations do not exceed a maximum limit determined in the Budget Law.

These measures must be submitted for the approval of the Chamber at the first session in which it convenes thereafter.

If the Chamber of Deputies has not given a final decision on the draft budget before the end of the session designated for its examination, the President of the Republic, in agreement with the Prime Minister, shall immediately convene the Chamber for an extraordinary session continuing until the end of January to continue examining the budget; and if this extraordinary session elapses and a final decision has not been given on the draft budget, the Council of Ministers may take a decision, pursuant to which a decree is issued by the President of the Republic, whereby the draft, in the form in which it was submitted to the Chamber, is rendered enforceable and operative. The Council of Ministers may not exercise this right unless the draft budget was laid before the Chamber at least fifteen days before the beginning of its session.

However, during the period of the aforementioned extraordinary session, taxes, imposts, duties, excises, and other revenues shall be collected as previously in basis, and there shall be added thereto such permanent appropriations as have been opened therein, and there shall be deducted therefrom such permanent appropriations as have been dropped, and the Government shall draw the expenditures for the month of January of the new year on the provisional twelfth basis.

The municipality is a local administration that exercises, within its territorial jurisdiction, the powers conferred upon it by law. The municipality enjoys legal personality and financial and administrative autonomy within the scope of this Law.

A municipality shall be established in every city or in every village or group of villages mentioned in Schedule No. (1) annexed to Legislative Decree No. (11) dated 29/12/1954 and its amendments, in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

The demarcation of the municipal territorial jurisdiction is an administrative measure unrelated to the entries of the Land Registry. The maps demarcating the municipal territorial jurisdiction shall be joined to the file of the establishment of the municipality, and the topographic operation shall be exempted from fees.
The municipal body shall consist of a deliberative authority and an executive authority.
The deliberative authority shall be exercised by the municipal council.
The term of office of municipal councils shall be six years.
