No one shall take part in the voting except an elector whose name is entered on the electoral roll or who has obtained a decision to have his name entered from the Registration Committee.

The municipal electoral bodies shall be convened by a decision of the Minister of the Interior within the two months preceding the end of the term of office of the municipal councils. The decision shall specify the polling stations, and the period between the date of its publication and the meeting of the electoral body shall be at least thirty days.

The final accounts of the financial administration for every year must be submitted to the Chamber to be approved by it before the promulgation of the budget of the second year that follows that year, and a special law shall be enacted for the formation of the Court of Accounts.
No public loan or undertaking involving expenditure from the funds of the Treasury may be contracted except pursuant to a law.

No concession or privilege for the exploitation of any of the country's natural wealth resources, or a service of public utility, or any monopoly may be granted except pursuant to a law and for a limited period.

The Chamber of Deputies elected on the basis of equality between Muslims and Christians must take the appropriate measures to achieve the abolition of political confessionalism according to a phased plan and the formation of a national body presided over by the President of the Republic, comprising in addition to the President of the Chamber of Deputies and the President of the Council of Ministers political, intellectual and social figures.

The mission of the body is to study and propose the means capable of abolishing confessionalism and to submit them to the Chamber of Deputies and the Council of Ministers and to follow up the implementation of the phased plan. And in the transitional phase:

a - The confessions shall be fairly represented in the formation of the Cabinet.

b - The rule of confessional representation shall be abolished and specialisation and competence shall be adopted in public posts, the judiciary, military and security institutions, and public and mixed institutions in accordance with the requirements of national accord, with the exception of posts of the First Category therein and the equivalent of the First Category therein, and these posts shall be held equally between Christians and Muslims without allocating any post to any confession, while adhering to the two principles of specialisation and competence.
Starting from the first of September of the year 1926, the State of Greater Lebanon shall be called "the Lebanese Republic" without any other alteration or modification.
All legislative provisions contrary to this Constitution are repealed.
The provisions of the Law on the Election of Members of the Chamber of Deputies shall apply to municipal elections in all that does not conflict with the provisions of this Law.
The electoral roll adopted for the election of members of the Chamber of Deputies shall be adopted for the election of municipal councils.

1 - The validity of the election may be challenged before the State Consultative Council within a period of fifteen days following the announcement of the result.

2 - The provisions of Articles 329 to 334 of the Penal Code shall apply to acts committed to corrupt the election.

If at least one-quarter of the seats in a municipal council become vacant, an election of members for the vacant seats shall be held for the remaining period within two months from the date on which the last seat became vacant, provided that a fraction of a number shall be counted as one.

The municipal council may be dissolved by a reasoned decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior if it commits repeated grave violations that have led to certain damage to the interests of the municipality.

The municipal council shall be deemed dissolved by operation of law if it loses at least half of its members or if a judgment is rendered annulling its election. The Minister of Interior must declare the dissolution by a decision issued by him within a period of one week at most from the date on which the Ministry of Interior is notified thereof, failing which his silence shall be deemed an implicit decision declaring the dissolution.

In the event that the council is dissolved or is deemed dissolved, a new council shall be elected within a period of two months from the date of the decree of dissolution or the decision declaring it. The Qaimaqam or the titular head of section in the Qada, and the Governor or the Secretary-General in the centre of the Governorate, shall assume the functions of the municipal council for the remaining period of the term of office of the dissolved municipal council. Until the election of the new council, this shall be by a decision of the Minister of Interior.
The municipal council shall not be renewed in whole or in part during the six months preceding the date of expiry of the term of office of the municipal council.

The following shall not be eligible for membership of municipal councils:

1 - Those who do not know how to read and write.

2 - Persons sentenced to deprivation of civil rights or civil degradation.

3 - Persons convicted of felonies or infamous misdemeanours as defined in paragraph 3 of Article 10 of the Law on the Election of Members of the Chamber of Deputies, or of the misdemeanours provided for in Articles 329 to 334 of the Penal Code.

4 - Persons convicted of offences of belonging to secret societies.

5 - Persons judicially interdicted on the grounds of imbecility and insanity.

6 - Persons declared bankrupt until their rehabilitation.

One person may not be a member of several municipal councils, and likewise, in a single municipality, a father and one of the children, a mother and one of the children, a husband and wife, a father-in-law and a daughter's husband or a son's wife, a mother-in-law and a son's wife or a daughter's husband, brothers and sisters, a paternal uncle and a brother's son, a maternal uncle and a sister's son, a sister's husband, and a brother's husband, indiscriminately, may not be members of a single municipal council. If two of the aforementioned relatives and kin by affinity are elected and neither of them resigns, the Qaimaqam shall dismiss the younger of the two, and if they are of equal age, one of them shall be dismissed by drawing lots at the first meeting held by the municipal council.

If any of the persons mentioned in Article 26 of this Law is elected as a municipal member, he must choose within a period of two weeks between the membership and his office; otherwise, he shall be deemed dismissed ipso jure from the membership of the municipality, and the dismissal shall be declared by a decision of the Governor. If any member of the municipal council is found to be in one of the cases provided for in Article 27 of this Law, he shall be deemed to have resigned ipso jure from the membership of the municipality by a decision of the Governor.

The resignation of the president, the vice-president, or a municipal member shall be submitted to the Governor through the Qaimaqam and shall be deemed final from the date of its acceptance by a decision of the Governor. If no decision is taken regarding the acceptance, the resignation shall be deemed final after the lapse of one month from the date of submitting a second resignation sent by registered letter. After the expiration of fifteen days from the acceptance of the resignation of the president or his vice-president, or from the resignation being deemed final, the municipal council shall meet in accordance with the provisions of Article 71 of this Law. The resignation may be withdrawn before the issuance of the decision accepting it or before it is deemed final.

The vice-president shall preside over the sittings in which the accounts of the administration of the municipality entrusted to the president are discussed, and the eldest of the members shall preside over them if the vice-president has been involved in the financial administration of the municipality. The president of the municipality may attend the discussions of its administrative accounts, provided that he leaves the sitting before the commencement of voting.

The president of the municipality may, of his own accord or upon the request of the Qaimaqam or the Muhafiz, request the municipal council to discuss by way of exception, before all else, a matter that requires urgent study. He may prohibit discussion of a subject outside the agenda.
The municipal council shall exercise its powers pursuant to resolutions it issues in sittings it holds for this purpose.

Voting shall take place by means of open ballot, and voting by proxy shall not be permitted. Recourse shall be had to the method of secret ballot if the president or the majority of the members present so request, or if the voting relates to any election.
The resolutions of the council shall be adopted by a majority of the votes of the members present. In the event of an equality of votes, the president shall have a casting vote.
A member who has a personal interest shall not be permitted to participate in the discussion and the ballot.

The resolutions of the municipal council must be recorded with serial numbers according to their dates in a register the pages of which shall be numbered and signed by the Qaimaqam or whoever he delegates. No blank space must be left in the register, nor shall any striking out or writing in the margin be permitted therein, and where necessary two lines shall be drawn across the blank space and the president and the clerk shall sign against the striking out or the writing in the margin, and every contravention shall be recorded at the foot of the resolution. The omission to record the entry of the resolutions in the special register shall not lead to its annulment and the annulment of the acts executed pursuant thereto, provided that the administrative supervisory authority must draw the attention of the municipal council to this omission and take measures to prevent its recurrence and to record the omitted resolution. The pages of the register of resolutions must comprise a margin and four columns: in the margin opposite the text of the resolution shall be recorded all the particulars relating, where applicable, to its ratification, approval or annulment; in the first column shall be recorded the serial number of the resolution; in the second column, the date of its publication or notification; in the third column, the date of its dispatch to the administrative supervisory authority; and in the fourth column, the text of the resolution itself.
Every elector in the municipal district or interested party may request to be given, at his own expense, a copy of the resolutions of the municipal council certified by the competent employee.

If a member of the municipal council fails to comply with the notice to attend a meeting four consecutive times without a legitimate excuse, the president shall convene the municipal council to a special sitting held for this purpose. The municipal council shall assess the reasons that caused the member to be absent and it may take a decision deeming the member to have resigned. The decision of the municipal council deeming the member to have resigned shall be subject to the approval of the Minister of the Interior. The member deemed to have resigned may contest the decision before the State Consultative Council within ten days from the date it is notified to him.

The municipal council shall meet at least once a month upon a notice from its president and whenever the need arises for its meeting, and the president shall specify in his notice the subjects of the meeting. The president shall be bound to convene the municipal council to a meeting if the Governor, the Qa'im-maqam, or the majority of the members of the council so request, provided that the reasons calling for this meeting and its subjects are mentioned in the request and the notice.

The notice must be in writing, and must be sent at least three days prior to the sitting, to the member's place of residence or his elected domicile, and this time-limit may be shortened if necessity so requires. The municipal council may examine the shortening of the time-limit and decide to continue with the sitting or adjourn it to another date. A member residing outside the municipal area shall elect a domicile within the municipality, failing which he shall be deemed notified at the headquarters of the municipality.

The deliberation of the municipal council shall not be lawful unless attended by more than half of the members of whom the council is composed as of the date of holding the sitting in which the deliberation takes place, and if the said proportion is not met, the meeting shall be adjourned and the members shall be summoned to a new meeting fixed by a notice after twenty-four hours at least, and this sitting shall not be lawful unless attended by at least one-third of the members, and the second notice must contain an explicit summary of the provisions of this article. The second notice shall be dispensed with and the sitting shall be lawful if it is established that the non-attendance arises from the existence of a personal interest for the absent members or for a person whose affairs they manage.

The sittings of the municipal council are confidential. The Governor or the Qa'im-maqam may attend them if they so request, provided that they shall not have the right to vote. The president of the municipality may invite any employee or any other person to attend the sittings of the municipal council in order to be heard.
The president of the municipality shall preside over the sittings of the municipal council, and in the event of his absence, the vice-president, and otherwise the oldest of the members.

The president of the sitting shall be in charge of maintaining order therein, and if a felony or misdemeanour is committed therein, he shall draw up a record of the fact and send it without delay to the competent judiciary and communicate a copy of this record.

Minutes of every sitting of the municipal council shall be drawn up in a special register, the pages of which shall be numbered and initialled by the Qaimaqam or whoever he delegates; they shall be read out at the close thereof and signed at the same sitting by all the members present, and their reservations shall be recorded if they so request. There shall be recorded in the minutes, in particular, the convocation, the agenda, the text of the resolutions adopted by the council, the names of the members present, the names of the persons who took part in the discussion and a summary of their observations, and the names of those who voted in the open ballot with an indication of the way they voted.

Every act of a public character or utility, within the municipal bounds, falls within the competence of the municipal council. The municipal council may express its recommendations and wishes on all other matters of municipal interest and state its observations and proposals regarding public needs within the municipal bounds, and the president of the council, or whoever acts in his stead, shall undertake to communicate the same to the competent authorities in accordance with the prescribed rules.
The regulations issued by the municipal council on matters falling within its competence shall have binding force within the municipal bounds.

The Municipal Council may, within its jurisdiction, establish or manage, directly or indirectly, or contribute to or assist in the execution of the following works and projects:

- Public schools, nurseries, and vocational schools.

- Popular housing, public baths and wash-houses, and swimming pools.

- Public hospitals, sanatoriums, dispensaries, and other health facilities and institutions.

- Museums, public libraries, theatres, cinemas, nightclubs, clubs, playgrounds, and other public and sports venues and social, cultural, and artistic institutions.

- Local means of public transport.

- Public markets for the sale of foodstuffs, cold stores for their preservation, and threshing floors for grain.

The approval of the Municipal Council shall be required in the following matters:

- Changing the name of the town

- Changing the boundaries of the town

- Regulating traffic and public transport

- Projects for the alignment and demarcation of major public roads and general master plans in the municipal area.

- Establishing, transferring, or abolishing public schools and government hospitals and dispensaries.

- Measures relating to public relief.

- Establishing charitable offices and institutions. Applications for licences to operate classified establishments, restaurants, swimming pools, cafés, nightclubs, and hotels. The Municipal Council must take a decision on the aforementioned matters within a period of one month from the date it is notified of the documents relating to these matters, failing which it shall be deemed to have tacitly approved them. In the event that the Municipal Council does not approve and the competent authority insists on taking a contrary measure, the matter shall be submitted to the Council of Ministers through the competent Minister, for a final decision thereon.

The Municipal Council shall supervise the acts of the executive authority, ensure the proper functioning of work in the municipality, and, as a result of the supervision work, draw up reports which it shall submit to the supervisory authority.

The Municipal Council shall elect from among its members at the beginning of each year two principal members and two alternate members who, together with the President of the Municipality and the Vice-President, shall form the body of the Tenders Committee, which undertakes the awarding of municipal contracts and the awarding of fees that the Municipal Council decides to put up for auction. The Municipal Council may also elect committees from among its members to study the matters entrusted to it and may seek the assistance of committees it appoints from outside its members.

The decisions of the Municipal Council are enforceable in themselves, with the exception of the decisions that this Legislative Decree has explicitly subjected to the ratification of the administrative supervisory authority, which shall become enforceable from the date of their ratification.

The municipal council shall undertake, without limitation, the following matters:

- The municipal budget, including the transfer and opening of appropriations.

- The closing of the budget accounts.

- Loans in all their forms for the realization of specific projects the study of which has been completed. The assignment of certain incoming and future municipal revenues to the lender or to the State in consideration of its guarantee of the loan, and the inclusion of the instalments falling due annually in the successive municipal budgets throughout the duration of such loan.

- Fixing the rates of municipal fees within the limits prescribed by law.

- The book of specifications for supply, works, and services contracts.

- The book of specifications for the sale of municipal property.

- Settlements.

- Acceptance and refusal of gifts and bequeathed funds.

- General programmes for works, beautification, cleaning, health affairs, and for water and lighting projects.

- Naming of streets within the municipal area.

- Planning, straightening, and widening of roads, establishment of public gardens and squares, and drawing up designs pertaining to the town and the general master plan in cooperation with the Directorate General of Urban Planning and with due regard to the provisions of the Expropriation Law, provided that the approval of both the Urban Planning authority and the municipality concerned shall be binding for the adoption of the project, and in the event of a difference of opinion between the municipality and the Urban Planning authority, the Council of Ministers shall decide the matter finally.

- Establishment of markets, parks, racecourses, playgrounds, baths, museums, hospitals, dispensaries, shelters, libraries, popular housing, wash-houses, sewers, waste dumps, and the like.

- Contribution to the expenses of public schools in accordance with the special provisions governing such schools.

- Contribution to the expenses of projects of public utility.

- Declassification of municipal public property into municipal private property.

- Regulation of transport of all kinds and fixing its tariffs, where necessary, within the municipal area, and with due regard to the provisions of the laws in force.

- Relief of the needy and the disabled, and assistance to clubs, associations, and all other health, social, sports, and cultural activities, and the like.

- Special regulations for the officials and wage-earners of the municipality and fixing their scale of grades, salaries, and wages.

- The right to contract with municipalities.

- Monitoring educational activities and the progress of work in public and private schools and preparing reports to the competent educational authorities.

- Monitoring the operation of public utilities and preparing reports on the progress of work therein to the administrations concerned.

- Approval to consider roads resulting from a subdivision project and benefiting more than six real properties belonging to different owners as municipal public property upon which the municipality is entitled to carry out works.

- Obliging the beneficiaries of a construction project the study of which has been completed to contribute to the costs of such project in the event of the approval of a majority of at least three-quarters of the beneficiaries thereof.

The following decisions shall be subject to the ratification of the Qaemaqam:

- The municipal budget and the transfer and opening of appropriations.

- The final accounts.

- Fixing the rates of municipal fees within the limits provided for by the Municipal Fees Law.

- Purchasing or selling real properties whose value does not exceed one hundred million pounds and the special specifications relating thereto.

- Lease contracts when their annual rents exceed twenty million pounds in municipalities subject to the prior audit of the Court of Audit and ten million pounds in other municipalities. And in both cases do not exceed forty million pounds.

- Assisting persons with disabilities and aiding clubs, associations, and other cultural, social, sports, health, and similar activities when the total value of the aid per year exceeds ten million pounds.

- Authorising contracts for supplies, works, and services when their value exceeds thirty million pounds and does not exceed eighty million pounds, and ratifying the special specifications relating thereto.

- Authorising works on force account and the purchase of supplies by invoice when their cost exceeds twenty million pounds and does not exceed fifty million pounds.

- Settling disputes and compromises, subject to the provisions of Article 66 of this Legislative Decree.

- Accepting or refusing donations and bequeathed funds encumbered with burdens.

And the following decisions shall be subject to the approval of the Governor:

- Authorising contracts for supplies, works and services when their value exceeds eighty million pounds, and approving the special specifications relating thereto.

- Authorising works by direct execution and the purchase of supplies by invoice when their value exceeds fifty million pounds.

- The purchase or sale of real property the value of which exceeds one hundred million pounds and the special specifications relating thereto.

- Allocating a municipal property to a certain interest, after having been allocated to a public interest.

- Lease contracts the annual rents of which exceed forty million pounds.

- Establishing markets, racecourses, museums, hospitals, public housing, waste disposal facilities and the like.

(Article 4 of the Law dated 25/4/1999 as amended by Law 231 dated 16/7/2021

The president of the municipality shall commit expenditures for supplies and works pursuant to a statement or invoice and shall order their disbursement when their value does not exceed twelve million Lebanese pounds pound.)

(Article 5 of Law 212 dated 26/5/2000 and amended pursuant to Law 231 dated 16/7/2021

Municipalities are authorised by a decision of the municipal council to conclude contracts pursuant to a statement or invoice if their value exceeds twelve million Lebanese pounds and does not exceed fifty million pounds without being bound by any texts contrary to the provisions of this Article.)

The following decisions shall be subject to the approval of the Minister of the Interior:

- Decisions of which general regulations are composed.

- Loans.

- Naming streets, squares and public buildings and erecting monuments and statues.

- Establishing and organising municipal units and determining their cadre, competences and the scale of ranks and salaries of their employees.

- Establishing federations comprising several municipal councils to carry out joint works of public utility.

- Allowances of the president and vice-president of the municipality.

- Declassifying public municipal property into private municipal property, and roads and remnants of land falling within the scope of the municipality, with the exception of international roads, shall be considered public municipal property.

- The general specifications for contracts for supplies, works and services.

- The general specifications for the sale of the property of the municipality.

- Obliging the beneficiaries of a construction project the study of which has been completed to contribute to the costs.

- Waiving some present and future municipal revenues in favour of the lender or the State.

Executory decisions of a general nature taken by the municipal council shall be published on the door of the municipal headquarters, and a record thereof shall be drawn up and signed by the competent employee, whereas other executory decisions shall be notified to their addressees.

1 - Administrative oversight over the decisions of the municipal council shall be exercised by the following authorities:

- The Qaemaqam

- The Governor

- The Minister of Interior

2 - Administrative oversight over the decisions of the Municipal Council of Beirut shall be exercised by the Minister of Interior only.
The Minister of Interior may delegate to the Director General of the Interior the powers vested in him pursuant to the provisions of this Law, in whole or in part.

The president of the municipality shall send the decisions of the municipal council to the competent administrative oversight authority, directly, within eight days from the date of their issuance, provided that a copy thereof is notified to the hierarchical authorities.

The following decisions of the municipal council shall not be subject to the approval of the administrative oversight authority, and they are listed by way of enumeration and example, not limitation:

- Lease contracts whose annual rents do not exceed twenty million pounds in municipalities subject to the prior oversight of the Court of Accounts and ten million pounds in other municipalities.

- Insuring municipal buildings, their equipment and their vehicles with insurance companies, for contracts in which the value of such insurance does not exceed twelve million pounds in municipalities subject to the prior oversight of the Court of Accounts and six million pounds in other municipalities.

- Accepting and refusing donations and bequeathed funds not linked to charges.

- Assisting the disabled and aiding educational, cultural, sporting and social activities when the total aid in the year does not exceed ten million pounds.

- Setting tariffs for transport, carriages and public vehicles of all kinds within the municipal territory.

- Collecting municipal fees and attaching the funds of taxpayers who refrain from paying such fees.

The president and vice-president of the municipality shall be entitled to receive a representation and transport allowance determined by the municipal council, which shall be proportionate to the significance of the effort that each of them expends in conducting the affairs of the municipality.

The decisions set forth in the preceding Articles shall be deemed tacitly ratified if the competent administrative supervisory authority does not take its decision thereon within one month from the date of registration of the decision in the competent unit at the concerned administrative supervisory authority. In such a case, the president of the municipality shall notify the competent administrative supervisory authority that the decision has become ratified. This time limit shall not apply to decisions relating to planning, the budget, the opening and transfer of appropriations, and loans. As for decisions subject to the prior audit of the Court of Accounts, the period in respect thereof shall run from the date of notification of the Court's decision of approval to the administrative supervisory authority.
The ratification of the administrative supervisory authority must be in writing, and it is subject to appeal before the State Council.

The Qaimaqam, the Governor, or the Minister of the Interior may, at any time he sees fit and for reasons relating to security, temporarily postpone the execution of a decision of a municipal council, and this must be effected pursuant to a reasoned decision subject to appeal before the State Council.

Settlements shall be subject to the approval of the Cases Authority at the Ministry of Justice in cases pending before the courts, and to the approval of the Legislation and Consultations Authority at the Ministry of Justice in cases that have not been brought before the courts.

The president of the municipal council shall exercise the executive authority in the municipality, and in the Municipality of Beirut the Governor shall exercise it. The provisions of paragraph (2) of Article 14 of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12 June 1959 shall not apply to the person who exercises the executive authority.

The provisions of Articles 26, 27, 28, and 29 relating to the eligibility of members of the municipal council shall apply to the eligibility of the president of the municipality and the vice-president.

The provisions of Articles 13 - 14 - 15 - 16 - 17 - 18 - 19 - 20 relating to the manner of electing the members of the municipal council shall apply to the manner of electing the president and vice-president of the municipality, provided that a candidate shall only be entitled to submit his candidacy for one position in the municipality, failing which the Qaimaqam shall be entitled to reject all of his candidacy applications.

In the event of the temporary vacancy of the office of presidency of the municipality for seven consecutive working days, the vice-president shall temporarily assume these functions by a decision of the municipal council, and the administrative supervisory authority shall be notified of his assumption of the functions of the presidency.

The head of the executive authority shall undertake, by way of enumeration and not limitation, the following acts:

- Executing the resolutions of the municipal council.

- Drawing up the draft budget of the municipality.

- Managing the departments of the municipality and supervising them.

- Managing the funds of the municipality and its real properties, and consequently performing all acts necessary for safeguarding its rights.

- Managing the revenues of the municipality and supervising its accounts.

- Ordering the disbursement of the municipal budget, incurring expenditures and supervising them, and issuing payment orders for their disbursement.

- Concluding contracts of lease, partition, and exchange, accepting gifts and bequeathed items, and purchasing and concluding settlements, after these acts have been authorised to be performed in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

- Performing, under the same conditions, purchases, agreements, public contracts, and concessions, and supervising the works executed for the account of the municipality and taking delivery thereof.

Committing expenditures that are made by virtue of a statement or invoice.

Committing expenditures that are made by virtue of a statement or invoice.

(Article 4 of Law of 25/4/1999

**The president of the municipality shall commit the expenditures for supplies and works by virtue of a statement or invoice and order their disbursement when their value does not exceed three million pounds.

Article 5 of Law 212 dated 26/5/2000:

**Municipalities are permitted, by a resolution of the municipal council, to conclude public contracts by virtue of a statement or invoice if their value exceeds three million Lebanese pounds and does not exceed twenty million Lebanese pounds, without being bound by any texts contrary to the provisions of this Article)

- Representing the municipality before the courts in accordance with the conditions stipulated in this Law.

- Issuing orders to take local measures in matters entrusted to his care and authority pursuant to the laws and regulations.

- Taking measures regarding the combating of drunkenness, epidemic or contagious diseases, and animal diseases.

- Demolishing dilapidated buildings and repairing them at the expense of their owners in accordance with the provisions of the Building Law.

- Taking delivery of gifts and funds bequeathed to the municipality if they are exposed to perishability or loss, and preserving them until a decision is made regarding them.

- Taking measures related to the suppression of begging.

- Taking the necessary measures regarding insane persons who threaten public morals or the safety of persons and property.

- Taking all necessary measures to forestall and avert accidents that may occur due to the straying of harmful or predatory animals.

- Securing the distribution of necessary aid to relieve victims of calamities and disasters such as fire, flooding of waters, epidemic or contagious diseases, etc...

- Preserving public comfort, safety, and health, provided that he does not encroach upon the powers granted by laws and regulations to the security departments of the State.

- Everything related to securing traffic and facilitating movement in public streets, squares, and roads, and everything related to cleaning, lighting, and removing debris and filth.

Attending to forestalling or preventing anything capable of prejudicing public comfort, safety, and health. Transporting the dead, regulating the procession of funerals, regulating burial and the exhumation of corpses, and maintaining order in cemeteries and their sanctity.

- And everything pertaining to the protection of the health of individuals and public health, such as sanitary supervision over places of assembly, hotels, boarding houses, brothels, cafes, restaurants, bakeries, shops of butchers, grocers, and barbers, etc.., and in general over all places in which the trade or manufacture of foodstuffs or beverages is practised, and sanitary control over persons associated in any capacity whatsoever with these establishments.

- Attending to taking means of prevention against fire, explosion, and flooding of waters, such as organising the fire department, supervising the places in which flammable and explosive materials and fuels are stored, determining the quantities of these materials that such places are permitted to store, and ordering the taking of the means of prevention incumbent upon them.

- Imposing the necessary measures of cleanliness, comfort, health, and safety upon means of public transport.

- Everything pertaining to public morals and decency.

- Attending to taking all necessary means to ensure the purity and wholesomeness of food materials prepared for trade.

- Attending to taking all necessary means to ensure the accuracy of weight, dry measure, and measurement.

- Everything pertaining to the protection of the environment, natural landscapes, and historical monuments, the maintenance of trees and wooded places, and the prevention of pollution.

- Granting building permits, occupancy permits, and certificates of completion of construction for the introduction of water, electricity, and telephone after the approval of the competent technical departments.

- Applying the provisions of the laws related to the settlement of building violations.

-Ordering the suspension of construction at the request of the injured party and against a sufficiency whose value is estimated by the president of the municipality for a maximum period of fifteen days to enable the injured party during that period to saisir the competent court.

- Licensing the excavation of public roads to lay pipes for water, electricity, telephone, sewers, and others against a guarantee ensuring the restoration of the condition to what it was at the expense of the license applicant, and public institutions, autonomous agencies, and State administrations shall not be exempted from this licensing.

- Licensing the connection of sewers within the municipal boundaries after collecting the fees, even if the project was executed by the council of the federation or another body and even if it passes through the boundaries of several municipalities.

- Supervising the trade in foodstuffs and pricing them, provided that this does not conflict with the measures and decisions issued by the Ministry of Economy and Trade.

- Appointing the employees of the municipality in accordance with the regulations and establishment tables of the municipality and terminating their services, and appointing workers and daily wage-earners within the limits of the appropriations allocated to them in the budget. However, it is not permissible for a father and one of the children, a mother and one of the children, a husband and wife, a son's wife, and brothers and sisters to be employees in one municipality; if there is found among the employees anyone who is in these situations, the president of the municipality shall have the right to dismiss one of them from service pursuant to a self-executing administrative decision

- Licensing advertising provided that his indemnities are liquidated in accordance with the provisions of the Civil Servants Law.

- He shall undertake security affairs through the municipal police, which enjoys the capacity of the judicial police, and he may request the assistance of the Internal Security Forces upon the occurrence of any offence or the likelihood of the occurrence of anything that may threaten public safety, and initiate the necessary investigations.

- Taking the administrative and regulatory measures that he deems appropriate for the proper functioning of municipal work and for securing municipal revenues in accordance with the provisions of the Municipal Fees Law.

- Performing certain urgent acts and measures related to public health, public safety, communications, vehicles, protocol, and receptions, provided that they are subsequently submitted to the supervision of the municipal council.

The municipality may establish such administrative, financial and technical units, and conditions, guards, fire brigades and ambulance services as it requires. It shall also be permissible to establish joint units, police, guards, fire brigades and ambulance services between two or more municipalities and to appoint joint employees among them.

1 - The establishment of joint units, police, guards, fire brigades and ambulance services shall be effected by a decision of the Minister of the Interior.

2 - The Minister of the Interior shall lay down unified regulations for the joint employees, while reserving to the municipalities having joint units the laying down of special regulations that take into account their circumstances, provided that these special regulations shall be subject to the approval of the Minister of the Interior.

3 - The expenses of these employees shall be distributed among the municipalities concerned on the basis of percentage rates by a decision of the Minister of the Interior.

4 - The decisions of the Minister of the Interior in this regard shall be issued upon the proposal of the Governor and after seeking the opinion of the municipalities concerned.

Municipal councils in municipalities that are not subject to the supervision of the Civil Service Board may, after obtaining the approval of the Minister of the Interior, contract with persons who fulfil the general conditions for municipal employment to perform some of their functions at specified times and under special conditions defined in the contract. It shall also be permissible, in municipalities whose annual final account is less than five thousand pounds, to assign members of the municipal council, without remuneration, to the duties of clerk, and it shall also be permissible to assign the policeman to the duties of health inspector and collector.

Municipal employees entrusted with the application or supervision of the implementation of the laws and regulations relating to public health, public hygiene, building and the facilitation of traffic in public streets and squares shall have the right to record contraventions of the laws and regulations.

The finances of municipalities shall consist of:

- Fees collected by the municipality directly from taxpayers.

- Fees collected by the State, autonomous agencies or public institutions on behalf of the municipalities and distributed directly to each municipality.

- Fees collected by the State on behalf of all municipalities.

- Grants and loans.

- Proceeds of municipal property, including the entire revenues of the common lands pertaining to it.

- Fines.

- Donations and bequests.
The proceeds of the joint surcharges accruing to all municipalities shall be deposited in trust in an Independent Municipal Fund at the Ministry of the Interior.
The procedures and rules for the distribution of the funds of the Independent Municipal Fund shall be determined by implementing texts after consultation with the State Council.
The rules and procedures of accounting in municipalities shall be determined pursuant to a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior.

The head of the executive authority may license the temporary occupation or the temporary placement of goods in roads and public places or the display thereof along the sides of pavements and public squares, and he may also license the owners of restaurants and cafés to place tables, benches and chairs on the pavements of the said roads and squares.

The head of the executive authority may issue municipal regulations in matters falling within his jurisdiction, and such regulations shall have, within the municipal scope, the binding force pertaining to the laws and regulations of the State. Decisions of a general nature taken by the head of the executive authority shall be posted on the door of the municipal headquarters, and a record thereof shall be drawn up and signed by the competent employee, and other decisions shall be notified to their concerned parties.

1 - The head of the executive authority shall head the municipal units and ensure the proper functioning and coordination of work therein, and he is the highest hierarchical superior of the employees of the municipality.

2 - The head of the executive authority may delegate to the vice-president some of his powers. He may likewise delegate to the heads of the municipal units some of his powers, with the exception of the powers relating to the issuance of texts of a general nature. Delegation shall be effected by a decision notified to the Minister of the Interior and published in the Official Gazette.
A special register shall be kept to record all decisions taken by the head of the executive authority, and it shall be noted on the register whether this decision has been published or notified.

1 - All decisions taken by the head of the executive authority shall be referred for action to the Qaemaqam, and in the Municipality of Beirut to the Minister of the Interior.

2 - The head of the executive authority shall communicate directly with the public administrations in all matters relating to the ordinary affairs of the municipality.

The municipalities of the centres of the Governorates shall be subject to the supervision of the Civil Service Board. Municipalities previously subjected to the supervision of the Civil Service Board by decree shall remain subject thereto. Other municipalities subject to the supervision of the Civil Service Board shall be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior.
Each municipality shall establish regulations for its employees and a cadre for them, as well as regulations for its wage-earners.

The following provisions shall apply in the municipalities subject to the supervision of the Civil Service Board: - Articles 13, 61, 62, 97 and 100 of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12 June 1959 and the amendments thereof. - Articles 40, 41, 42, 43, 44, 45, 46, 47, 48, 59, 60 and 61 of Legislative Decree No. 113 dated 12 June 1959 and the amendments thereof.

The Municipality of Beirut shall be subject to the audit of the Court of Audit, as well as the municipalities currently subject to the same audit. The other municipalities that are subject to the audit of the Court of Audit shall be determined by a decree passed in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior.
The Ministry of Interior shall undertake the preparation of the municipalities to enable them to discharge their duties.

The Minister of Interior shall entrust a number of employees with the task of guiding the municipalities to the means capable of developing them, raising their standard, increasing their effectiveness, improving their organisation, simplifying the methods, procedures and ways of work followed therein, and introducing them to the best ways to achieve their objectives.

The selection of the employees referred to in the preceding article shall be made from among the employees of the State and the municipalities who possess special knowledge and qualifications in the municipal field.

The status and provisions of secondment stipulated in Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12 June 959 shall apply to them, and their number shall be determined, according to need, by a decision of the Minister of Interior.
Training courses shall be prepared for the established municipalities and federations and their bodies in accordance with a programme determined by the Minister of Interior.

Financial acts in the Municipality of Beirut and the other municipalities and federations of municipalities, which are determined by a decree passed in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior, shall be subject to the authority of a financial controller called the Controller General". The authority of the Controller General may cover more than one municipality or federation.

The Controller General shall be appointed by a decree passed in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior, and his services shall be terminated in the same manner. The allowances of the Controller General shall be determined in the decree of his appointment. The Controller General must meet the following requirements:

- He must be an employee of the third category at least, in the cadres of the State or its equivalent in the cadres of the municipalities, holding a university degree or a graduate of the National Institute of Administration and Development, and having undertaken financial acts or financial audit for a period of five years at least. Or he must be an employee of the third category at least, in the cadres of the State or its equivalent in the cadres of the municipalities subject to the procedures and rules of public accounting, and having undertaken financial acts or financial audit for a period of ten years at least.

- The Controller General in the Municipality of Beirut is required to be an employee of the second category at least in the cadres of the State or its equivalent in the cadres of the municipalities subject to the provisions of the Public Accounting Law, and to have undertaken financial acts or financial audit for a period of ten years at least.

The powers of the Controller General and his place of work shall be determined by a decree passed in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior. Save for the powers and allowances prescribed for him, the Controller General in the municipality or the federation may not be entrusted with any mission, nor assigned to perform any work, nor receive any allowance or remuneration.

The Controller General shall benefit from the benefits and services granted to employees in his original cadre, whatever their kind, and they shall be paid to him in addition to his salaries, allowances and allocations from the budget of the municipality or the federation.
The Controller General shall be administratively attached to the Ministry of the Interior throughout the duration of his performance of this function.

The municipal council shall deliberate on lawsuits and judicial proceedings instituted in the name of the municipality, and the decision taken shall authorise the head of the executive authority to pursue remedies at all stages of litigation. The head of the executive authority may undertake urgent matters and conservatory measures prior to the municipal council taking the decision referred to above.

Lawsuits instituted against the municipality before the judicial courts shall be exempted from the submission of the preliminary memorandum. As for the institution of lawsuits against the municipality before the administrative courts, it shall remain subject to the rules of procedure in force before such courts.
The rules of procedure followed in the execution of judgments rendered against the State shall apply against municipalities.

The president of the municipal council, his vice-president, or the member who assumes the acts of the executive authority shall be deemed disciplinarily liable and shall be subject to disciplinary sanctions if he breaches the duties imposed upon him by regulations and laws, despite being warned, and this leads to causing harm to the interests of the municipality. Disciplinary prosecution shall not preclude prosecution, where necessary, before the competent civil and criminal courts.

Disciplinary sanctions are of two categories:

- Category One:

- Warning

- Reprimand

- Category Two:

- Suspension from work for a period not exceeding one year

- Dismissal

Sanctions of the first category shall be imposed by a decision of the Minister of the Interior. Sanctions of the second category shall be imposed by a decision of the Special Disciplinary Board. The Special Disciplinary Board shall have the right to impose any sanction of the first category if it appears to it that the person referred to it does not deserve a more severe sanction.

The Special Disciplinary Board shall be composed as follows:

- The President of the General Disciplinary Council for Civil Servants, as President

- An employee of the Ministry of the Interior of the second category at least, as Member

- A Mayor, as Member

- The function of Government Commissioner shall be performed by the Government Commissioner before the General Disciplinary Council for Civil Servants, and the function of Secretary of the Board by an employee of the fourth category at least in the Department of Municipal and Rural Affairs at the Ministry of the Interior. Neither the Government Commissioner nor the Secretary of the Special Disciplinary Board shall participate in the deliberation and the pronouncement of the judgment.

The Special Disciplinary Board shall be appointed by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior. An alternate president and alternate members shall be appointed in this decree to replace the original President and members in the event of absence, illness, or inability to participate in the work of the Board for a legal reason.

The President of the Municipal Council, his deputy, or the member who assumes the functions of the executive authority shall be referred to the Special Disciplinary Board by a decision of the Minister of the Interior following an investigation conducted by the Ministry of the Interior.
The procedures followed before the General Disciplinary Council for Civil Servants shall be applied before the Special Disciplinary Board.

The decisions of the Special Disciplinary Board shall be subject to appeal for abuse of power before the State Consultative Council in accordance with the procedures followed before it. Recourse to the State Consultative Council shall not stay execution unless the Council decides to stay the execution of the contested decision. The State Consultative Council must rule on the request for stay of execution within three days after the expiry of ten days from the date of notification of the State, failing which the request shall be deemed accepted by operation of law until the date of issuance of the final judgment.
The President, his deputy, or the municipal member may not be prosecuted criminally for an offence related to their duties except upon the written approval of the Governor.

If an indictment order or a judgment of first instance is issued against the President of the Municipality, the Vice-President, or one of the members, he may be suspended from office by a decision of the Governor, until the issuance of the final judgment. If one of these is indicted for a felony or suspected of an infamous misdemeanour, he must be suspended from office by a decision of the Governor until the conclusion of the lawsuit. If an irrevocable judgment for a felony or an infamous misdemeanour is issued against one of these, he shall be considered dismissed ipso jure and the dismissal shall be declared by a decision of the Governor. If an arrest warrant, whether in absentia or adversarial, for a felony or an infamous misdemeanour is issued against these, he shall be considered suspended from office ipso jure as of the date of the warrant. If the arrest warrant is withdrawn or he is released, he shall return ipso jure to the exercise of his duties unless he was arrested for a felony or an infamous offence.

The Public Prosecution shall have the right to characterise the offence for which the President of the Municipality, his deputy, or one of the members is prosecuted, and whether it arises from the functions of the Municipality or does not arise therefrom.
The Union of Municipalities consists of a number of municipalities, enjoys legal personality and financial autonomy, and exercises the powers provided for in this Law.

1 - A Union of Municipalities shall be established by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior, and that - either on his own initiative - or upon the request of the municipalities

2 - Other municipalities may be joined to the Union by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior and on an initiative or upon the request of the municipalities.

3 - A Union of Municipalities shall be dissolved according to the same procedures adopted for its establishment. The decree of dissolution shall determine, subject to the preservation of the rights of third parties, the conditions under which the liquidation of the Union of Municipalities shall take place.
The decree establishing the Union of Municipalities shall determine the name of this Union and its seat.
The term of office of the Council of the Union shall expire upon the expiration of the term of office of the Municipal Councils of which it consists.
The organ of the Union consists of a deliberative authority called the Council of the Union and of an executive authority assumed by the President of the Council of the Union.

The Council of the Union consists of the Presidents of the Municipalities which it comprises for the proposal of the President to be represented by one of its members throughout the duration of the term of office of the Union. In the event of the vacancy of the post of a member of the Union for a permanent reason such as death, resignation, or dismissal from the membership of the Municipal Council, he shall be replaced by the member delegated by the Municipal Council to which he belongs.

The Council of the Union shall convene within a period of two weeks from its formation at the invitation of the Qaimaqam or the Governor in order to elect the President and the Vice-President, and the Qaimaqam or the Governor shall not participate in these elections if he is in charge of the affairs of the municipalities.

The head of the executive authority shall be assisted in managing the affairs of the Union by a staff apparatus headed by a director and consisting of the engineering and health apparatus, of the administrative and financial apparatus and of the police apparatus. The Council of the Union shall undertake to lay down the regulations and cadres of the employees of the Union. The President of the Union shall appoint the employees in accordance with the provisions of the regulations and cadres in force.

The engineering apparatus shall undertake, for the benefit of the member municipalities in the Union, the following affairs:

- Examining applications for building permits, drawing up technical inspection reports and submitting the complete file to the president of the municipality concerned to decide thereon.

- Preparing specifications books for supplies, works and services.

- Preparing the required technical studies and consultations.

- Laying down alignments.

- Preparing expropriation lists and detailed statements for their referral to the competent appraisal committees.

- Examining and giving an opinion on occupancy permits.

- Health supervision.

- Preparing reports to the president of the municipality concerned relating to building violations, health violations and all other violations falling within the competence of this apparatus and occurring within the scope of the municipality, and submitting them through the President of the Council of the Union to the president of the municipality concerned.

- The engineering and health apparatus shall also undertake all other joint technical matters requested of it by the President of the Council of the Union.

The administrative and financial apparatus shall undertake the following matters:

- The administrative and financial affairs of small municipalities whose own budget does not permit the employment of employees to secure these works.

- Assisting the apparatuses of the member municipalities to improve the course of their administrative and financial works. One of the collectors in the Union may be entrusted with supporting the member municipalities in collecting fees from taxpayers.

- The administrative and financial affairs in the Union.

The police force of the Federation shall undertake the following matters:

- Educating citizens to comply with the provisions of the regulations and laws in force.

- Drawing up reports on violations occurring within the jurisdiction of the municipalities affiliated with the Federation and submitting them through the President of the Council of the Federation to the President of the Municipality concerned.

- Conducting preliminary investigations into flagrant offences and offences that affect public safety until the arrival of the judicial police.

- Performing the duties of municipal policemen in municipalities whose budget does not permit the appointment of their own police personnel.

- The policemen of the Federation shall be assigned to these duties pursuant to a decision issued by the President of the Council of the Federation upon the request of the President of the Municipality concerned, and they shall work under the command of the President of the Municipality to which they are seconded.

Member municipalities shall have the right to temporarily detach all or some of their police personnel to work within the jurisdiction of another municipality in the Federation, provided that a number of police personnel from other municipalities are attached to them to work within their jurisdiction. Detachment and attachment shall be effected by a decision of the President of the Municipality after the approval of the President of the Council of the Federation. The policemen shall continue to receive their salaries from the municipalities in which they are appointed and shall receive transport and travel allowances from the municipality to which they are detached.

The Council of the Union shall deliberate and decide upon the following matters:

- Public projects of common benefit from which all or some of the member municipalities benefit, or which encompass the scope of more than one union, whether such projects are existing or prospective, such as roads, sewers, waste, slaughterhouses, firefighting, the organisation of transport, cooperatives, popular markets, and otherwise.

- Alignments, expropriations, books of specifications, and all that is necessary for the execution of the projects.

- Coordination among the member municipalities and the settlement of disputes arising among them.

- Approval of the budget of the Union.

- Approval of the final account. Approval of the regulations and cadres of the employees of the Union.

- Administration of the common lands located within the scope of the municipalities of the Union the administration of which does not revert to a specific municipality and which are currently administered by special common-land committees, and disposal of the entirety of their revenues to realise the projects of the Union, and there shall be transferred to the Council of the Union immediately upon its establishment the funds and assets that are in the possession of the special common-land committees, which shall become dissolved ipso jure.

- Approval of the development plan within the scope of the Union and its competences.

- Obliging the beneficiaries of a construction project the study of which has been completed to contribute to the costs of this project in the event of the approval of a majority of at least three quarters of those benefiting therefrom.

- Loans in all their forms to realise specific projects the study of which has been completed.

- Assignment of some of the current and future municipal revenues to the lender or to the State in the person of the Minister of Finance in return for its guarantee of the loan and the inclusion of the instalments that fall due annually in the successive budgets throughout the duration of this loan.

In the event of a disagreement among the Councils of the Union over one of the joint projects among them, or the refusal of one of them to examine it, the matter shall be referred to the Minister of the Interior, who shall settle the dispute pursuant to a reasoned decision having the character of a legal obligation for the unions concerned.

All decisions taken by the Council of the Union within the scope of its competences shall have the character of a legal obligation for the member municipalities. If one of the member municipalities abstains from executing the decisions of the Council of the Union, the Qa'immaqam or the Governor shall, either proprio motu or at the request of the President of the Council of the Union, address to the competent municipality a written order requiring execution within a time limit of ten days, failing which he shall take the place of the Municipal Council or the President of the Municipality in the decision that ensures the proper execution of the decision of the Council of the Union. The decision of the Qa'immaqam or the Governor shall be recorded in the special register of decisions concerned.

If the municipal council or its president abstains from performing an act which the laws and regulations require to be performed, the Kaymakam may direct a written order to the municipal council or to its president requiring execution within a time limit specified in such written order; and if the time limit expires without execution, the Kaymakam shall be entitled, after the approval of the Governor, to perform the same himself pursuant to a reasoned decision. The decision of the Kaymakam shall be recorded in the register of decisions provided for in Article 44 of this Legislative Decree and shall be subject to the ratification of the administrative supervisory authority where applicable.

Municipalities shall be entitled to use municipal public property to execute their public projects and to carry out excavations and extensions to execute lighting, sewerage, water, and other projects; provided, however, that in no event may any municipality exercise its authority outside its municipal scope, or levy fees from another municipality or from the taxpayers pertaining to that municipality.
Notwithstanding any other text, the acts of the deliberative and executive authorities in the municipalities shall not be subject to the control of the Central Inspection.

With the exception of the Municipality of Beirut, the municipalities of the centres of governorates, and the other federations of municipalities each of which has engineering offices and bodies, all technical and engineering transactions pertaining to municipalities shall be conducted in the technical offices of the branches of Urban Planning in the districts.

As for the technical transactions in respect of which decrees are required to be issued in order for them to become effective, they shall be conducted in the Directorate General of Urban Planning".
The Municipal Act No. 29 dated 29 May 1963 and all provisions contrary to the provisions of this Legislative Decree or inconsistent with its content are hereby repealed.
This Legislative Decree shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.
The council of the union of municipalities shall adopt the same procedures and rules adopted for the conduct of work in municipal councils and provided for in this Law.

The president of the council of the union shall assume the executive authority and shall have, by way of enumeration and not limitation, the following powers:

- Convening the council of the union and setting its agenda.

- Chairing and managing the sessions of the council of the union

- Preparing the draft budget, the final account, and the annual report.

- Supervising the finances of the union and controlling its revenues.

- Committing expenditure and ordering the disbursement of the budget.

- Appointing employees within the provisions of the regulations and the approved cadres.

- Managing the affairs of the union, and he is the highest hierarchical superior of the employees of the union.

- Executing the decisions of the council of the union.

- Representing the union before the judiciary and third parties.

The president and the vice-president of the council of the union shall be entitled to receive from the budget of the union a representation and transport allowance determined by the council, which shall be proportionate to the importance of the effort exerted by each of them in conducting the affairs of the union.

The vice-president shall exercise the powers of the president in the event of his absence or suspension from work or in the event of the vacancy of the office of the presidency for any reason whatsoever, and in the event of the absence of the president and the vice-president or the vacancy of the office of both of them, the oldest member in the council of the union shall temporarily act in the place of the president.

The finances of the union shall consist of:

- Ten percent of the actual revenues of the member municipalities as determined in the final account schedule of the preceding year, and trusts, carried-over cash, loans, and grants shall not be included in the calculation of revenues.

- An additional percentage of the budget of the member municipalities benefiting from a specific project of common utility, determined by the council of the union in light of the costs of the project, provided that this percentage is subject to the approval of the Minister of Interior.

- Grants and loans, and the entire proceeds of the common lands falling within the competence of the council of the union.

- What is allocated to the union from the proceeds of the Independent Municipal Fund.

- The contribution of the State to the budget of the union, provided that the amounts allocated for this purpose are included annually in the general budget. The funds shall be distributed among the unions by a decision of the Minister of Interior and shall be allocated to preparing studies or executing joint projects whose study has been completed and to revitalising the regions, especially the rural ones.

- Donations and bequests.
The decisions of the council of the union shall be subject to the authority of administrative oversight in accordance with the provisions, procedures, and rules applicable to municipalities.

The Law dated 4 August 1954 shall apply in all its articles with respect to all games of chance, and the current prohibition of these games and of the flipper games listed in Tables Nos. 1 and 3 annexed to this Decision shall remain in force, in all public places including cafés, clubs or halls.

The playing of the card games and flipper games set forth in Tables Nos. 2 and 4 annexed to this Decision shall be permitted in the places mentioned in the first Article above, following the issuance of the administrative licence in accordance with the conditions set forth in the subsequent articles.

1- Permissible card games in ordinary cafés and electric amusement games "flippers and the like" shall be licensed by a decision of the Governor. 2- Bingo games and card games in clubs and halls designated for this purpose shall be licensed by a decision of the Minister of Interior.

With the exception of bingo halls, existing amusement game halls shall continue to operate if the conditions provided for in this Decision are met therein, provided that their owners submit applications to obtain the necessary licences.

The opening of licensed halls shall be permitted along main streets and roads, and it grows a warning to open these halls on side roads and alleys and near places of worship and educational institutions. The distance between- the nearest place of worship or the educational institution and the hall must be less than one hundred and fifty metres.
The licensing of amusement game and bingo halls in the upper floors of buildings and in floors located below ground level is prohibited, and licensing shall be restricted to the ground floors.

The minimum area of the licensed hall shall be determined as follows: - Fifty square metres as a minimum for halls designated for ordinary amusement games "flippers"- and the like. Three hundred square metres as a minimum for bingo halls, provided that the area designated for players is not less than two hundred and fifty square metres.

The minimum separating distance between one hall and another (with respect to bingo halls) shall be set at four hundred metres, and existing halls shall be exempted from this condition if they are licensed and fulfil the imposed conditions.
This Decision shall be published and notified where needed.

Owners of restaurants and commercial establishments are prohibited from operating any amusement machine or bingo within the scope of their commercial activity; however, where the conditions provided for in Article Thirteen of this Decision are met, owners of classified restaurants and tourist establishments may be licensed to run the game of bingo for a specified period not exceeding one hour and once per day, without being bound by the mandatory distances provided for in Article Eight of this Decision.

Persons who are under eighteen years of age are forbidden from frequenting the halls specified in items (b) and (c) of Article Three of this Decision, and this prohibition also applies to military personnel regardless of the corps to which they belong unless they are assigned to an official mission.

The decision to close bingo halls shall remain in force until their status is regularised in accordance with the provisions contained in this Decision, and the owners of ordinary amusement halls and electrical games that were in existence prior to the issuance of this Decision are granted a time limit of two months to obtain the necessary licences.

Every violation of the provisions of this Decision shall subject its perpetrator to the following measures: a- Temporary closure for a period of one week in the event of a violation for the first time within a single year b - Temporary closure for a period of one month in the event of a violation for the second time within a single year c Permanent closure and revocation of the licence in the event of a violation for the third time within a single year.
The decision of closure shall be issued by the authority competent to grant the licence.
The prohibited and permitted gambling games and flippers shall be determined in accordance with Schedules 1, 2, 3 and 4 annexed to this Decision.
The Directorate General of the Internal Security Forces is charged with executing the provisions of this Decision.

All texts contrary to the provisions of this Decision are repealed, and all previous licences pertaining to bingo halls are also revoked unless they fulfil the conditions provided for in this Decision.

Working hours in bingo halls shall be fixed between the fourteenth hour and the twenty-fourth hour of every day; whereas in respect of ordinary amusement game halls ("flippers" and the like), working hours therein shall be fixed between the tenth hour in the morning and the tenth at night.

Advertisements, leaflets, banners and posters for the games that are the subject of this Decision, and by any media means, shall be prohibited, with the exception of a signboard on the door of the hall the area of which does not exceed two square metres.
With the exception of cash prizes allocated to players, it shall be prohibited to grant any prizes in kind or additional rewards intended for publicity or to entice, attract or lure the public.

The maximum price of a bingo participation card shall be fixed at 1/10 of the minimum daily wage, and the maximum price of the metal token ("fiche") for ordinary amusement games shall be fixed at the equivalent of 1/50 of the minimum daily wage.

The conditions for licensing shall be fixed in accordance with the following: - That the licence application be in the name of the owner or the operator - That the licence applicant be Lebanese, enjoying all his civil rights, not convicted more than once of an ordinary misdemeanour and not convicted at all of a disgraceful misdemeanour - The licence applicant must attach to his application the following documents: - A certified copy of his identity card or his civil status extract - A copy of his judicial record dated no more than two months earlier - A certified copy of the title deed, lease contract or operating contract - A certificate from the municipality including the location and area of the property and proof of the fulfilment of the following technical conditions: 1- In respect of bingo and video poker halls: a- Washbasins and lavatories b - Air conditioning, ventilation and cooling c- Air extractors d- Fire extinguishers, provided that their number is not less than six, fit for operation at any time e- Sufficient lighting f- Exits, provided that their number is not less than two 2- In respect of ordinary amusement halls ("flipper"), it shall suffice to fulfil the conditions set forth in paragraphs a and c of item 1 above

The maximum number of customers permitted to enter shall be fixed in the licensing decision in the light of the actual area, such that one square metre is adopted for each person, and a notice of this number shall be placed in a conspicuous place in the hall.

Single Article: The Law returned to the Chamber of Deputies pursuant to Decree No. 2416 dated 30/03/1985 relating to the amendment of the Expropriation Law, as amended by the Joint Parliamentary Committees, has been ratified. This Law shall come into force immediately upon its publication.

Real properties or sections thereof shall be expropriated and easements shall be established thereon in the interest of the Administration, and it shall also be permissible to expropriate the rights held by the owner of the real property in the airspace above it and in the subsoil beneath its surface, and real property rights in rem shall also be expropriated, all for the purpose of public utility. No person may be deprived of his ownership except for reasons of public utility and after compensating him therefor with fair compensation in accordance with the provisions of this Law. The word real property in this Law means a real property unit or a group of contiguous real property units owned by a single person or owned by several persons even if the share of each of them differs from one real property to another. However, if the separator is a public road, a railway, a river, a winter watercourse, or a private passage for several real properties owned by numerous persons, the group of real property units shall not be deemed a single real property. A husband, wife, and children shall be deemed as a single person if one of them acquired from the other the real property affected by expropriation during the year preceding the issuance of the decree declaring public utility.

In applying the definition mentioned above, the state in which the group of contiguous real property units stood on the date of issuance of the decree shall be relied upon. The applicant for expropriation is referred to in this Law by the word (the Administration), and the declaration of public utility is referred to by the word (the Decree)."

Public utility shall be decided by a decree upon the proposal of the competent Minister based on the request of the concerned Administration, the municipality, the elective council (ikhtiyariyya) in a village where there is no municipality, the public institution, or the concessionaire, and the public administration and municipalities may expropriate real properties in the interest of persons designated by the law.

The decree shall specify the maximum period within which the expropriation formalities must be commenced, provided that it does not exceed eight years from the date of publication of the decree in the Official Gazette.

As for expropriation decrees relating to antiquities, their maximum period of validity shall not exceed three years from the date of publication of the decree in the Official Gazette, during which the Administration shall have the right to conduct an excavation operation in the property or properties subject to expropriation and extract the antiquities therefrom when necessary.

The Administration may, during the last six months prior to the expiry of the period of validity of the decree, extend it for an additional period not exceeding five years if it appears as a result of the excavation that there are antiquities that could not be extracted during the period of validity of the decree, and it may also extend it, following the approval of the Council of Ministers, for an additional period not exceeding ten years in the event of the presence of antiquities of great archaeological and historical value.
