If the three-year period expires and the concerned Administration has not decided to commence the execution of the expropriation in accordance with the provisions of Article Eight of the Expropriation Law with a view to executing the works, the decree declaring public utility shall be deemed null and void and without any effect, and the competent Administration must request the Registrar of the Real Estate Registry to strike off the entries resulting therefrom, and the concerned party may also do so, and it shall no longer be possible thereafter to expropriate the concerned property or properties for the same purpose before the expiry of ten years.

The following documents shall be attached to the decree:

1- A general plan of the works intended to be carried out

2- A detailed map comprising the properties intended to be expropriated

3- A list of the numbers of these properties, their locations, and the names of the owners and holders of rights registered in the Real Estate Registry. And if the property is not subject to the Real Estate Registry system, its number and the date of its entry in the Mukhtar's register or the Tapu register or in the minutes of demarcation and census before the Real Estate Judge shall suffice. And in the absence of such an entry, the name of its apparent owner shall be mentioned in the list by virtue of a certificate of notice from the Mukhtar showing the boundaries of the property.

4- A detailed statement of the contents of the properties requested to be expropriated and detailed maps of the buildings erected thereon prior to the publication of the decree in the Official Gazette. A copy of the aforementioned documents shall be deposited with the Administration, and every interested party may inspect them and obtain a copy thereof.
A clerk and a sworn process server shall be attached to each First Instance Commission, and a clerk and an usher from the cadre of judicial assistants shall be attached to each Appellate Commission.

The presidents and members of the aforementioned commissions shall be appointed by decree upon the proposal of the competent ministers, and the employees attached to the commissions shall be appointed by a decision of the Minister of Justice.

The Administration shall be represented before the First Instance and Appellate Commissions by an employee of the third category at least holding a degree in law or in civil engineering, seconded by a decision issued by the Director General or the head of the administrative unit directly linked to the Minister if the expropriation is in favour of public administrations.

However, if the expropriation is for the benefit of municipalities, public institutions or any other authority, the appointment of the representative shall take place in accordance with the rules followed by the authority requesting the expropriation.

State administrations may seek the assistance of the Cases Authority at the Ministry of Justice in important cases that raise a legal dispute, in which case they shall be represented by the President of the Cases Authority or by whomever represents him from among the judges, employees or lawyers attached to the Authority. The representative of the Administration shall be authorised by operation of law:

- To be served with all summonses, pleadings, memoranda and decisions pertaining to his administration.

- To submit pleadings and memoranda, pursue avenues of recourse and perform all acts required for the defence of the interests of his administration before the Expropriation Commissions.

The president and members of the Expropriation Commissions, the employees attached thereto and the representatives of the Administration before them shall receive a compensation determined by decree and disbursed from the budget of the administration requesting the expropriation.

The competent administration shall publish the decree in the Official Gazette together with the list provided for in the third paragraph of the preceding Article. A copy thereof and of the list attached thereto shall be posted in the places designated for notices at the seat of the municipality within whose jurisdiction the real properties intended to be expropriated are located, or at the seat of the mukhtar in villages where there is no municipality, and one of the employees of the municipality or the mukhtar shall draw up a record of the completion of the publication formalities, which he shall deposit with the administration requesting the expropriation.

The administration shall serve a copy of the decree upon the interested parties whose names are set out in the list attached thereto at their place of residence through administrative channels or through a sworn officer.

In the event of their absence, they shall be served through one of the adult members of their families residing with them, and if service in this manner proves impossible, or if the interested parties are of unknown residence or deceased with unknown heirs, the mukhtar of the locality shall draw up a record of the fact, which shall be joined to the documents, and service shall be replaced by publication in two local newspapers, copies of which shall be kept in the file pertaining to the decree, and in such case service by publication in two newspapers shall be deemed lawful.

The administration shall send a copy of the decree together with the list attached thereto to the Land Registry Secretariat in order to enter an annotation of this decree forthwith upon the real folios of the real properties. The entry must include the name of the authority requesting the expropriation, the number and date of the decree, the date of its publication in the Official Gazette, and the date of its entry upon the real folio.

When the administration decides to proceed with the execution of the expropriation, it shall refer the decree together with the complete file to the competent First Instance Expropriation Commission. There shall be joined to the file, in addition to the documents set out in Article Four of this Law, complete real property certificates dating back no more than three months.

There shall be appointed by decree for each governorate:

1- One or more First Instance Expropriation Commissions composed of a judge of the tenth grade and above or the equivalent thereof as President. And of two members, one of whom shall be an engineer from among the employees of public administrations, municipalities, or public institutions, and the other an expert in valuation

2- One or more Appellate Expropriation Commissions composed of: a judge of the sixth grade and above or the equivalent thereof as President and of two members, one of whom shall be an engineer from among the employees of public administrations, municipalities, or public institutions, and another an engineer who is an expert in real property affairs and valuation.

An alternate president and two alternate members shall be appointed for each of the First Instance and Appellate Commissions to replace the original president and two original members in the event of absence for any reason or impossibility of participating in the work of the commission.

The procedures to be followed before the Primary Expropriation Commissions shall be determined as follows:

1- Immediately upon taking cognisance of the expropriation file, the Commission shall conduct an inspection of the real properties decided to be expropriated in order to view their location and verify their descriptions, appurtenances, purpose of use, and any rights they may have or encumbrances they may be subject to, and shall draw up an inspection record for each real property.

2- The Commission shall summon the Administration, the owners, and the known right holders to a public hearing, and the writ of summons must include, in prominent letters, a notice to the owner of the obligation to inform it of the right holders such as occupants, tenants, and operators, the date of commencement of their occupancy, and the consideration they pay, and the Commission shall also summon the right holders declared by the owner or the right holders whose occupancy the Expropriation Commission ascertains during the inspection to a similar hearing, provided that the writ of summons includes a notice to them of the necessity to submit whatever instruments and documents they have proving their rights and of the obligation to inform the Commission of the legal right holders, if any. Service shall be effected directly or through the sworn officer attached to the Commission in accordance with the rules provided for in the Code of Civil Procedure. Right holders may appear of their own accord before the Commission to claim their rights even if the owner has not declared them.

3- The Primary Commission shall apply summary procedures.

4- The Commission shall serve its decisions immediately upon their issuance on the representative of the Administration and the interested parties in accordance with the procedures set out in paragraph 2 above.

5- The decisions of the Primary Commission shall be subject to recourse by way of appeal within the time limits and in accordance with the procedures provided for in the Code of Civil Procedure.

1- The value of expropriation compensation for all elements of damage resulting directly from this expropriation shall be determined in accordance with the prevailing prices on the date of issuance of the decision of the First Instance Commission, taking into consideration all elements of assessment and compensation, including location, area, shape, and the subject of exploitation such as loss of clientele, lost profit, difference in rent, and the period of interruption of work with respect to commercial and industrial shops and establishments and liberal professions.

If the decision of the First Instance Expropriation Commission is appealed, or if the case was previously appealed and is still pending before the Appellate Expropriation Commission, and the Administration has obtained a decision to take possession following the deposit of the compensation determined in the first instance, the compensation shall be determined at the prevailing prices on the date of issuance of the first instance decision. However, if more than one year has elapsed between the date of issuance of the first instance decision and the date of the decision to take possession, the compensation shall be determined at the prevailing prices on the date of issuance of the decision to take possession. However, if the deposit has not been made and consequently the decision to take possession has not been issued, the compensation shall be determined at the prevailing prices on the date of issuance of the appellate decision.

- No account shall be taken when appraising the expropriated real property:

- Of the improvement that arose from the issuance of the decree declaring public utility or from the execution of the project for which the expropriation is taking place

- Of the constructions erected after the registration of the annotation of the decree on the real folio of the real property or in the ledgers or the record referred to in item 3 of Article Four of this Law.

- Of the buildings, plantations, lease and exploitation contracts, and all other improvements if the purpose of creating them was to obtain higher compensation. Buildings, plantations, contracts, and improvements made after the registration of the annotation of the decree on the real folio of the real property, and with respect to real properties not subject to the Land Registry system, after the publication of the decree in the Official Gazette, shall be deemed created for the aforementioned purpose without need for proof.

2- If the execution of the expropriation leads to a decrease in the value of the non-expropriated part of the real property, the Commission shall assess the value of the decrease and add it to the prescribed compensation.

The Appellate Committee shall follow the following procedures:

1 - Each of the parties may appeal the decisions of the Primary Committee before the Appellate Committee within whose jurisdiction the real property falls, within a time-limit of thirty days following notification of the decision, provided that the petition is signed by an attorney. Decisions shall be appealed separately and an appeal may not cover more than one primary decision except in the case of connectedness.

2 - The appeal shall be subject to stamp duty, the fixed fee and the appellate deposit, and public administrations, public institutions and municipalities shall be exempted from these two fees and from this deposit.

3- The appeal shall be submitted to the clerk of the Appellate Committee or to the clerk of the Primary Committee that issued the decision, who shall register it in a special register, give a receipt therefor, and send it without delay to the clerk of the Appellate Committee together with the primary file containing all the papers, maps, documents, minutes, decisions and documents of service relating to the decision subject to the appeal, and if the clerk of the Primary Committee fails to send the file within a time-limit of one week from the date of submission of the appeal, he shall be sentenced to a fine assessed by the President of the Appellate Committee, provided that it is not less than five thousand pounds and does not exceed twenty-five thousand Lebanese pounds.

4 - The Appellate Committee shall apply summary procedures and issue its decision within a time-limit that should not exceed three months.

5- An incidental appeal shall be admissible within the conditions provided for in the Code of Civil Procedure.

6 - An appeal shall not stay the progress of the expropriation proceedings, except that the administration, if it brings a principal appeal, may retain ten per cent (10%) of the value of the compensation determined in first instance until the appellate decision is issued.

The sittings of the Primary and Appellate Committees shall not be lawful except in the presence of all the members of the Committee. The expropriation committees shall not be entitled to seek the assistance of an expert except in important matters that require seeking the assistance of persons of expertise, or if the assessment of compensation or the determination of one of the points in dispute requires technical information not available among their members. However, they shall not be entitled to seek the assistance of an expert in ordinary matters limited to the valuation of the land and the constructions and trees thereon.
The expropriation committees shall issue their decisions unanimously or by majority, and they must state the reasons for these decisions and itemise the elements of the compensation that they assess.

If a material error occurs in the final decisions of the expropriation committees, or if their interpretation is ambiguous, or if it appears that the decision covered an area of a property that was previously expropriated or included an error in determining the area or in the appurtenances of the area requested to be expropriated or in the names of the right holders, any of the parties shall have the right to request correction or interpretation by virtue of a petition submitted to the committee that issued the decision, which shall serve a copy thereof upon the other party and invite him to submit his observations within a time limit of eight days, and shall then adjudicate upon the request within a time limit of one week after the expiry of the latter time limit, and the committees may in such cases revoke their decision, amend it or interpret it adversarially vis-à-vis the other party.

Decisions of the appellate expropriation committees shall not be subject to any avenues of recourse other than opposition, third-party opposition and retrial only, within the time limits and on the grounds and in accordance with the procedures provided for in the Code of Civil Procedure.

However, owners and right holders shall have the right to challenge before the State Council the decisions of the appellate expropriation committees if they rule to reduce the value of the compensation awarded in first instance by more than 25%, and the expropriating administration if the appellate expropriation committees rule to increase the value of the compensation by more than 50%.

The recourse in this case shall be subject to the time limits, procedures and grounds to which an appeal before the State Council is subject, which shall adjudicate upon the recourse within a time limit of one month following the date of the conclusion of the exchange of pleadings.

The jurisdiction of the expropriation committees shall include:

1- Determining the amount of all compensations due on account of expropriation.

2- Adjudicating upon requests for total expropriation provided for in Articles 27 and 28 of this Law.

3- Fixing the price of the remnants referred to in Article 40 (forty of this Law).

4- Determining the value of betterment preliminary to imposing the tax thereon.

5 - Adjudicating upon the dispute in the event of the existence of a serious disagreement among the owners, or between them and the right holders, or among the right holders themselves relating to these rights or to the rights over the property; the committee shall assess the amount of compensation and decide to suspend its payment until the termination of the dispute by agreement of the parties or by a final judgment from the competent court.

6- Adjudicating upon disputes concerning the application of the concept of the real estate unit and concerning the amount of successive deductions affecting the property.

7- Everything for which a special provision is made in this Law or another.

After reviewing the certificate of deposit, the Administration shall decide to take possession of the expropriated real property, and the decision shall state the obligation to vacate it within a time limit of not less than 15 days if it is unbuilt, and not less than thirty days if it is built upon, and the Administration may retain one-quarter of the value of the compensation until the execution of the decision to take possession. The decision to take possession shall be notified to the concerned parties and to the Land Registry Departments. If the place of residence of the person required to be notified is unknown or is outside Lebanese territory, the decision to take possession shall be notified by posting it on a conspicuous place of the expropriated real property and a summary thereof shall be published in two local newspapers. The time limit for vacation shall commence as of the date of the last publication. Immediately upon the expiry of the time limits for the obligation to vacate, the Administration shall be able to execute the taking of possession of the real property, and if it includes buildings expropriated in their entirety, the Administration shall demolish them and remove their rubble at its own expense. However, if the buildings are partially expropriated, the owner shall carry out the demolition and the removal of the rubble in return for compensation determined by the valuation decision, the payment of which shall be suspended until the completion of execution, and if he fails to execute the demolition within the time limit fixed for him by the Administration, it may carry out the execution works itself and retain the compensation prescribed therefor.

Immediately upon being notified of the decision to take possession, the Land Registrar shall transfer ipso jure the ownership of the expropriated real properties to the name of the expropriating Administration, free of any right, security or easement, subject to the provisions of Article Thirty-Three of this Law.
Prior to depositing the prescribed compensation, the Administration may at any time revoke the decree declaring public utility.

In the event that a right of usufruct exists on the expropriated real property, the compensation of the holder of the right of usufruct shall be determined in proportion to his age in the following manner: If the age of the holder of the right of usufruct: What accrues to him of the compensation: 30 years and under, six-tenths of the compensation 6/10; more than 30 to 40 years, five-tenths of the compensation 5/10; more than 40 to 50 years, four-tenths of the compensation 4/10; more than 50 to 60 years, three-tenths of the compensation 3/10; more than 60 to 70 years, two-tenths of the compensation 2/10; over 70 years, one-tenth of the compensation 1/10; and the remainder shall accrue to the bare owner. These rules shall apply equally to real properties of both Mulk and Amiri types, without regard to the rights of the State over the bare ownership in the second type.

The Committee shall determine the compensation due to the beneficiaries of easements on the expropriated real property according to the extent of the damage directly sustained by them as a result of their cancellation, and this compensation shall be deducted from the compensation of the owner.

Where the subsoil of the land of a real property is expropriated independently of what is above it, or where a right is created in favour of the Administration over what is above the surface of the land of a real property, the compensation shall be determined according to the extent of the damage sustained by the owner as a result of the restriction of his enjoyment of his property.

No compensation shall be due from the Administration to the holders of rights on the expropriated real property, such as lessees and operators, unless their rights arose prior to the entry of the annotation of the decree on the real folio of the property and are established by a document of a certain date or by documents of an official nature. However, if the real property is not subject to the Land Registry system, compensation shall only be due if the rights arose prior to the date of publication of the decree in the Official Gazette.

Buildings of which a part has been decided to be expropriated shall be taken in their entirety if the remaining part is unfit for exploitation in accordance with the purpose for which it is intended, provided that full expropriation is requested by all the owners of the real property or of the subdivided section of the real property by virtue of one or more petitions submitted to the Primary Expropriation Committee, under penalty of forfeiture of the right after the lapse of one year from the date of the final decision. The same method shall be followed with respect to every plot of land of which there remains, following the subdivision, only an area unfit for enjoyment in accordance with what it was originally intended for, provided that its owner does not have a contiguous plot of land to which it can be annexed.

The Expropriation Commission shall rule on the request for total expropriation and assess the compensation due to the owner and all other right holders in accordance with the provisions of Article Twenty-Two and the articles following it at the prices prevailing on the date of issuance of the Preliminary Expropriation Commission's decision relating to the partial expropriation. The expropriating Administration shall draw up a statement of the properties decided to be expropriated in their entirety in accordance with the preceding procedures and shall notify it to the Land Registry Departments so that ownership of the parts that were not originally affected by the expropriation may be transferred to the private domain of the Administration.

Immediately upon being notified of the Preliminary Commission's decision, the Administration shall deposit the full value of the determined compensation and inform the party entitled to the compensation thereof, and then obtain a decision to take possession of the expropriated property. An appeal shall not stay the other expropriation proceedings. If a period of six months elapses from the date of notification of the Preliminary Commission's decision and the Administration has not deposited the compensation, legal interest shall be due from it by operation of law from the date of expiry of the said period. However, if the delay exceeds two years from the date of notification, the party entitled to the compensation may request the Commission that issued the decision to conduct a reassessment; the Commission shall conduct a reassessment at the prevailing prices in accordance with the bases specified in Article Twenty-Two above. This provision shall apply to prior decisions that were not accompanied by a deposit; the time limits in respect thereof shall run from the date of publication of this Law in the Official Gazette.

The Administration may decide to use the expropriated property in another project declared to be of public utility other than the project for which the expropriation took place, and when it carries out the necessary legal procedures in this regard. However, if the Administration decides to abandon the project, the owner of the property or his universal successors shall have the right to request its recovery within a period of one year from the date of their notification of the abandonment through administrative channels.

If ten years have elapsed from the date of the decision to take possession and the Administration has not commenced the execution of the project for which the expropriation took place, in whole or in part, or the Administration has not decided to allocate it to another project declared to be of public utility, or has decided upon such allocation and has not commenced its execution within a period of ten years, this shall be deemed an abandonment, and the owner of the property or his universal successors shall have the right to request its recovery within a period of one year starting from the date of expiry of the aforementioned ten-year period, provided that they submit a written request to that effect to the expropriating Administration.

In the event a recovery request is submitted, the concerned Administration shall refer the request to the competent expropriation commission, which shall determine the recovery price on the basis of the value of the property requested to be recovered as of the date of the request at the prevailing market price, less 25% (twenty-five percent).

The applicant for recovery must, under penalty of forfeiture of his right, pay in cash to the expropriating Administration on the date of submitting the recovery request the full expropriation compensation paid to him, provided that he pays to the expropriating Administration the difference - if any - between the recovery price as determined by the expropriation commission and the expropriation compensation paid to him, within a period of six months from the date of his notification of the decision of the First Instance Expropriation Commission.

If the property was jointly owned in undivided shares by several owners, each of them shall have the right to recover the undivided share that he owned. If the one-year period provided for in the first and second paragraphs of this Article expires and the owner has not submitted the recovery request in due form, the Administration shall have the right to register the property as its private property.

However, if the expropriating Administration has proceeded to execute the project for which the expropriation took place, it shall have the right, after the expiry of five years from the completion of the project, to use the expropriated property for any other purpose as it deems appropriate.

The establishment, straightening, and widening of public roads and squares shall take place pursuant to an alignment plan approved by a decree that stands in place of a decree declaring public utility.

The decree ratifying the alignment plan shall be published in the Official Gazette and in two local newspapers, and copies thereof shall be affixed at the premises of the municipalities within the jurisdiction of which the alignment plan falls, or at the office of the mukhtar in villages that have no municipality. A copy of the decree and of the alignment plan map shall be deposited with the Land Registry Offices in order to enter a notation thereof on the folios of the real properties affected thereby. The number and date of the decree and the date of its publication in the Official Gazette shall be stated in the entry.

The alignment plan decree shall remain in force as from the date of its publication in the Official Gazette for a period of ten years, renewable once for a maximum period of three years.

If this period expires and the Administration concerned has not decided to commence the execution of the expropriation resulting from the alignment plan in accordance with the provisions of the eighth Article of the Expropriation Law, the decree ratifying the alignment plan shall be deemed null and void and of no effect whatsoever, and the competent Administration shall, on its own initiative or at the request of the interested party, request the Land Registrar to strike off the entries resulting therefrom.

Within a period of five years as from the date of publication of the alignment plan decree, the expropriating Administration shall have the right, where the sections of the real properties affected by the alignment plan are unbuilt lands, to proceed with the execution of the works that are the subject of the alignment plan in return for paying an occupancy allowance to the owner. In such case, the following rules and procedures shall apply:

1 - The Administration must obtain the prior approval of the Council of Ministers.

2 - The Administration shall refer the file to the competent Expropriation Commission and request it to assess the value of the expropriated section of the real property, taking into account the free quarter rule where such rule is applicable. It shall also request the Commission to determine the value of the annual occupancy allowance for the said section.

Decisions of the First Instance Commission shall not be subject to any ordinary means of recourse other than appeal before the Appellate Expropriation Commissions, regardless of the value of the claim, in accordance with the rules set forth in the Code of Civil Procedure.

3 - The Administration shall deposit the value of the annual allowance determined by the Expropriation Commission prior to occupying the said section, and the real property shall remain registered in the name of its owner.

4 - The Administration must execute the expropriation resulting from the alignment plan in accordance with the provisions of the eighth Article of the Expropriation Law prior to the expiry of a time limit not exceeding thirteen years from the date of publication of the alignment plan decree. In such case, the Administration shall deposit the value of the compensation determined by the Expropriation Commission in accordance with paragraph 2 above and shall procure a decision to take possession in accordance with the rules. Amounts paid by way of occupancy allowances shall be deemed a vested right of the owner of the real property.
Every amendment to the alignment decree shall be subject to the formalities provided for in the preceding Articles.

1- Real properties and parts thereof falling within the scope of the alignment for the construction, modification or widening of public roads and squares shall be annexed to the public domain.

2- It is presumed in principle that the remaining parts of the real properties affected by the alignment will accrue an betterment in their value; if the area of the affected part is less than one quarter of the area of the real property, it shall be annexed to the public domain without compensation, with the exception of the compensation due for plantings, buildings and constructions, whereas if it exceeds one quarter of the area of the real property, the value of the excess shall be determined on the basis of the prevailing price on the date of issuance of the decision of the First Instance Valuation Committee.

3 - The acquisition of the one quarter without compensation shall not be permissible in real properties facing closed motorways or bridges and affected by the alignment. The acquisition of the one quarter without compensation shall only be permissible once, regardless of how many times alignments are repeated, and the area of the real property prior to its being affected by the first alignment shall be taken as the basis for calculating the one quarter, even if the alignment leads to splitting the expropriated real property into more than one section and each section acquires a new real property number.

New owners shall benefit from the gratuitous one quarter in the event of repeated deduction, unless more than twenty-five years have elapsed since the first deduction.

4- If it appears, after the execution of the alignment and the placing of the road wholly or partially into use, that the betterment tax that will be imposed on the remaining part of the real property is less than the value of what was annexed therefrom to the public domain without compensation, the owner of the real property may request the Expropriation Committee to determine the difference and compel the expropriating Administration to refund it to him.

Built real properties falling within the alignment plan of public roads and squares shall be condemned to restriction by virtue of the alignment, and no works may be carried out to add a building thereon, and the Administration may remove such works, in the event they take place, by administrative means. However, the owner shall be permitted, after the lapse of five years from the issuance of the decree approving the alignment, to maintain and shore up the buildings standing on his real property in order to keep them fit for use, provided that this is carried out pursuant to a prior permit showing in detail the permitted maintenance and shoring up works, and provided that the competent authority for granting the permit notifies the Administration requesting the expropriation and the Land Registry Secretariat of a certified copy of this permit accompanied by detailed maps showing the condition of the building before and after the permitted works.

An alignment easement and the restriction arising therefrom shall not prevent the owner of the real property from enclosing it and erecting non-permanent structures thereon without giving rise, for his benefit or for the benefit of the operators or occupants of such structures, to any right to compensation upon the execution of the expropriation.

If the execution of an alignment results in a remnant of a public road or square that is not suitable for independent construction, every owner of an adjoining real property shall have the right to purchase the portion of such remnant facing his property by an application submitted to the Expropriation Committee accompanied by the documents relating to the remnant. The Expropriation Committee shall decide upon the application in accordance with the procedures followed in ordinary expropriation and in return for a price determined by the Committee in accordance with the prevailing prices as at the date of issuance of its decision.

If the execution of the project for which the expropriation took place or the execution of other works of a public nature requires the temporary occupation of land, whether to extract or gather materials, or to establish a depot for materials or supplies thereon, or for any other purpose, a prior authorisation for such occupation must be obtained from the Minister of Public Works and Transport or the Minister of the Interior under whose administration or tutelage the administration for whose benefit the project is executed falls, or the Governor. The authorisation decision shall specify the works for the execution of which the temporary occupation will take place, the real properties covered thereby, the road leading thereto, and the nature and duration of the occupation. It is prohibited to occupy courtyards, gardens, and orchards attached to dwelling houses if they are walled.

The authorisation for temporary occupation shall lapse if six months have elapsed since its issuance and its execution has not been commenced, and the duration of the occupation may not exceed three years.

The authority that issued the temporary occupation decision shall determine the compensation due to the owner or occupant and must deposit such compensation prior to the occupation. The party entitled to compensation may collect the amount deposited in his name and may, where necessary, apply to the Expropriation Committee within whose territorial jurisdiction the real property falls to determine the fair compensation. The determination and payment of the compensation shall be subject to the procedures followed in determining expropriation compensation.

The ordinary rules of expropriation shall apply to expropriations decided in the interest of national defence unless the competent authority decides that military necessities require secrecy and speed, in which case the following provisions shall apply:

1- The real properties intended to be expropriated may be mentioned in the decree declaring public utility, rather they shall be designated by virtue of confidential maps deposited at the Ministry of National Defence.

2- Possession of these real properties may be taken immediately by a decision of the Minister of National Defence prior to the determination of the compensation due.

3- Compensation shall be determined by a First Instance Committee appointed by decree and composed of:

- A judge in the cadre of the judicial judiciary of the twelfth grade and above - President.

- An engineer officer from the Ministry of Defence - Member

- An expert in real property affairs and valuation - Member

These persons shall be appointed in accordance with the provisions of Article Twelve of this Law.

4- The procedures followed before the First Instance Expropriation Committee shall apply before the said Committee, and its decisions shall be subject to the avenues of recourse to which the decisions of that Committee are subject

5- Appeals against the decisions of the First Instance Committee shall be heard by the ordinary Appellate Expropriation Committee within whose territorial jurisdiction the real property is located, in accordance with the procedures in force before it.

A betterment tax shall be imposed on the increase in the value of real properties resulting directly from the execution of various public works, with the exception of sewerage and pavement projects. The betterment tax shall give rise to a lien in favour of the Treasury on the improved real property regardless of the person to whom it is transferred, and this lien shall be registered on the real folio of the real property.

Any increase occurring in the value of a real property or part of a real property as a result of the execution of the project from the date it is declared of public utility until the date it is put into use shall be deemed a betterment, and this increase shall be calculated by comparison with the value of real properties not affected by the betterment.

The value of the portion of the betterment that does not exceed five times the minimum wage in force on the date of issuance of the first-instance decision that determined the amount of the betterment shall be exempted from the betterment tax. The tax shall be imposed on the portions that exceed the amount mentioned in the preceding paragraph at the following rates:

- 10% ten per cent on the portion that exceeds five times the minimum wage referred to above and does not surpass twenty-five times.

- 20% on the portion that surpasses twenty-five times the minimum wage and does not exceed fifty times

- 30% on the portion that surpasses fifty times the minimum wage and does not exceed one hundred.

- 40% on the portion that surpasses one hundred times the minimum wage, provided that the value of the betterment tax does not exceed the value of one quarter of the area of the real property on the date of issuance of the valuation decision.

There shall be established in the Ministry of Finance, Revenue Directorate, a special tax department called the "Betterment Tax Department", whose cadre, conditions of appointment to the posts of this cadre, and scale of ranks, grades, and salaries of these posts shall be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

The party that requested the issuance of the decree declaring the utility that requested the issuance of the decree declaring public utility must leave with the Betterment Tax Department, within a time limit of one month from the date of putting the works into execution by way of awarding a tender or otherwise:

- A copy of the decree and the documents attached thereto and set out in Article Four of this Law, with the appropriate amendments where necessary.

- A report on the works the execution of which may have led to a betterment in the value of the real properties affected by the expropriation on the date of completion of the works, within a period of one month from the date of their conclusion and the placing of the project wholly or partly into use or operation, and irrigation projects shall be deemed completed at the beginning of the year following the year of placing the water at the disposal of the beneficiaries thereof.

The Betterment Tax Department shall be entrusted with:

1- Drawing up a reasoned statement of the real properties that it estimates the betterment will cover, which shall be approved by a decision of the Head of the Revenues Service, and a copy thereof shall be notified to the Land Registry Secretariat to register an entry on the folio of each real property indicating that it is subject to the betterment tax, and this entry shall not be struck off except after the issuance of a final and binding decision by the Expropriation Committee ruling that the tax is not due, or after payment of the tax in the event that it is due.

Or after paying a deposit on account of the betterment tax, to be determined upon the proposal of the Head of the Betterment Tax Department and the approval of the Director of Revenues.

2- Verifying the rights in rem and rights not in rem over the aforementioned real properties

3- Investigating the prevailing prices during the stages of study and execution of the project and the probable prices on the date it is put into use, and all other information relating to the betterment of the aforementioned real properties.

4- Notifying the prospective taxpayers and the owners of whom a part of their real properties has been expropriated of the statement mentioned in item (1), requiring them to submit their observations within a time limit of 15 days from the date of notification.

5- Drawing up a detailed report of the information it obtains and of the observations of the concerned parties and their documents.

6- Immediately upon being notified of the notice of completion of the works, referring the aforementioned report together with the complete file to the competent committee to determine the value of the betterment.

Or after paying a deposit on account of the betterment tax, to be determined upon the proposal of the Head of the Betterment Tax Department and the approval of the Director of Revenues.

The Expropriation Committees shall determine the value of the betterment in accordance with the rules and procedures provided for in Articles Fifteen to Twenty-One. of this Law. The committees must commence their work within a time limit of one month at most after receiving the report and the file mentioned in items 5 and 6 of Article Fifty of this Law. And the procedures provided for in this Law shall apply.

The Betterment Tax Department shall be represented before the First Instance and Appellate Expropriation Committees by an employee of the third category at least, assigned by a decision of the Director General of the Ministry of Finance.

The final betterment tax shall be paid in five equal annual instalments, the first of which shall fall due on the first day of the month of July of the second year following the year of notification of the assessment rolls. And the final betterment tax resulting from irrigation projects shall be paid in ten equal annual instalments, the first of which shall fall due on the first day of the month of July of the fourth year following the year of notification of the assessment rolls. Interest shall accrue automatically at the rate of one per cent per month on the value of each instalment that is not paid when it falls due, and the person liable to pay the betterment tax shall have the right to request the extension of one due date one time only for a period of two years at most in return for his payment of interest whose rate is five per cent per annum, and if the taxpayer does not settle the amount due from him on the specified due date, the interest rate shall automatically be raised to one per cent per month, and this tax shall be collected in accordance with the procedures for the collection of direct taxes and similar fees.

The betterment tax on a real property that is the subject of a consolidation and subdivision operation in accordance with the provisions of Decision No. 37/L.R. dated 05/02/1934 (Real Property Improvements in Agricultural Lands) and in respect of which a decision declaring it to be of public utility has been issued by the competent Minister before the First Instance Committee begins conducting the assessment of the betterment shall be reduced by a proportion of 25 per cent.

The proceeds of the betterment tax shall revert to the Treasury or to the fund of the public institution or the municipality for whose account the works were executed, and the Betterment Tax Department shall levy the tax through the financial collection departments, provided that the Treasury credits to the municipality or the public institution that executed the works what has been collected for its account.

The committee shall determine the amount of betterment with respect to each real property in accordance with the bases set forth in Article forty-six of this Law by comparing the prevailing prices as at the date of commencement of carrying out the expropriation formalities and the prevailing prices after completion of the project and placing it wholly or partially into use or exploitation, subject to the following provisions:

1- No account shall be taken in any event of betterment resulting from economic factors and others that cannot properly be considered as resulting from the decree declaring public utility and the execution of the works.

2- Account shall be taken of whatever may have been expropriated from the real property without compensation in application of the text of Article thirty-seven of this Law, the value of which shall be deducted from the value of the betterment tax

3- The decisions of the Expropriation Committee shall be notified within a period of fifteen days from the date of their issuance to the Betterment Tax Department.

The betterment tax shall in principle be imposed on the owner of the improved real property, and where a right of usufruct exists over the real property it shall be apportioned between the bare owner and the holder of the usufruct in accordance with the schedule provided for in Article twenty-three of this Law. Where, however, a right of exploitation or a non-residential lease exists over the real property or over a part thereof, the committee shall determine the share of the resulting betterment that actually accrues to the owner and the holders of the rights.

The Betterment Tax Department shall issue, on the basis of the decisions of the committees determining the value of the betterment, assessment rolls which shall be ratified by the Head of the Revenue Service, and an abstract of each assessment shall be notified to the concerned parties. These rolls shall not be subject to any avenue of review other than an application for correction of a material error. The application shall be submitted to the Head of the Revenue Service for adjudication thereon, and his decisions shall be subject to objection before the First Instance Expropriation Committee.

The provisions of this Law shall apply to expropriations pertaining to all State administrations, public institutions, municipalities, and persons upon whom the law confers the right to request expropriation, and all special legal and regulatory provisions, whether relating to valuation rules, the formation of committees, or the procedures followed in the various stages of expropriation, shall be deemed repealed.

Legislative Decree No. 18 dated 30/03/1983, Decree No. 107 dated 20/06/1977 as amended by Article Three of the said Legislative Decree No. 18, and the provisions of Legislative Decree No. 69/83 dated 09/09/1983 shall be excepted and shall remain in force.

Until the expropriation committees are formed in accordance with the provisions of this Law and the scope of their relative jurisdiction is defined, the abolished expropriation committees shall continue to examine the transactions referred to them and shall apply the provisions of this Law. Transactions that have not been finally decided shall be referred to the expropriation committees provided for in this Law immediately upon their formation, at the stage of proceedings at which they stand.

The State Council shall continue to examine appeals against decisions of the appellate expropriation committees that are pending and have not been finally decided. And the courts before which are pending lawsuits that, pursuant to the provisions of Article Twenty-One of this Law, have fallen within the jurisdiction of the expropriation committees shall continue to examine the said lawsuits up to the final stages of litigation, and the ordinary rules of procedure shall apply thereto.

The provisions of Articles Twenty-Two, Thirty-Seven, and Forty of this Law shall apply to all expropriation transactions that remain pending before primary or appellate expropriation committees and that have not acquired a final, conclusive judgment as of the date of entry into force of this Law.

Legislative Decree No. 4 issued on 30/11/1954 and its amendments are hereby repealed, subject to the provisions of Article Sixty-Two of this Law; the Law put into effect by Decree No. 188 dated 06/06/1977 and its subsequent amendments are hereby repealed with retroactive effect; and Legislative Decree No. 125 dated 07/07/1977 (the Betterment Tax Law) is hereby repealed, as well as all provisions contrary to the provisions of this Law or inconsistent with its content, save for what is excepted pursuant to the provisions of this Law.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication.

Article 58 bis added pursuant to the Law dated 8/12/2006

Upon declaring by a decree issued in the Council of Ministers that the expropriation is granted an urgent character, the expropriation shall be subject to the following rules and procedures:

1 - The detailed map and the list provided for in paragraphs 2 and 3 of Article Four of the Expropriation Law shall be attached to the decree declaring public utility.

2 - The decree declaring public utility or the decree approving the layout shall be notified by way of publication in the Official Gazette and in two local newspapers, and copies thereof shall be posted in the public square of the town and at the entrance of the main municipal headquarters, or at the headquarters of the mukhtar in villages where there is no municipality.

3 - Additional expropriation commissions, of first instance and appellate, may be appointed in accordance with the rules and conditions specified in the Expropriation Law to examine urgent expropriations.

4 - The expropriation commissions of first instance examining urgent expropriations shall follow the following rules:

a - Immediately upon taking cognizance of the expropriation file, the commission shall conduct an inspection of the real properties decided to be expropriated. The commission must describe each real property accurately, encompassing all its contents, take photographs thereof where necessary, and then appraise its value and the value of every right potentially existing for a person other than its owner, and draw up a record of all the foregoing.

b - If the expropriated real property is land clear of constructions, trees, and crops, the president of the commission shall submit the record to the administration requesting the expropriation and to the Minister of Public Works and Transport, who shall take a decision to take possession of the real property immediately after depositing the specified compensation.

c - However, if the real property contains constructions, trees, or crops, and its owners and other right holders were not present when the inspection was conducted, the president of the commission shall summon the known owners and right holders to review the aforementioned record through administrative channels. The summons notice must include, in prominent letters, a warning to the owners of the obligation to inform the commission of the right holders, such as occupants, tenants, and operators, the start date of occupancy, and the rents or fees they pay.

d - The administration, the owners, and the right holders shall have the right to submit their observations on the record within a period of one week from being notified of the summons.

e - After the submission of these observations, the commission may conduct a new inspection where necessary, then rule on these observations and issue its decision; it shall have the right to modify the value of the compensation, by increase or decrease, based on the elements of assessment that it deduces from the inspection record and otherwise.

f - The decisions of the commission of first instance shall be notified in accordance with the rules specified in item (2) above, with the exception of publication in the Official Gazette.

g - The administration shall have the right to deposit the compensation and to obtain a decision to take possession of the real property on the basis of the decision of the commission.

h - Save for the foregoing, the proceedings shall be pursued in accordance with the rules of ordinary expropriation.

Single Article: The draft law set forth in Decree No. 7619 dated 9 December 1995, aiming to regulate the school budget and determine school tuition fees in non-free private schools and miscellaneous provisions, as amended by the Committee of National Education, Culture and Vocational and Technical Education Affairs, is hereby ratified.

This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

A - The school budget in a non-free private school shall be prepared in accordance with the template annexed to this Law, and school tuition fees shall be determined according to the procedures set out in this Law.

For the application of the provisions of this Law, school tuition fee shall be understood as the amounts charged by the school to the pupil, whatever their designation, for a school year in consideration of the instruction, compulsory educational activities, insurance against risks and medical supervision that it provides to him.

B - The annual school tuition fee shall be determined by dividing the total of the expenditures chapter, as determined in the following Article, by the total number of pupils, subject to the provisions of paragraphs <C>, D and E of this Article.

C - There shall be deducted from the total of the expenditures chapter referred to in the preceding paragraph the total amount of the education grants provided for in the last paragraph of Article Six below.

D - There shall be deducted from the total number of pupils referred to in paragraph B above the total number of children of members of the teaching staff who are exempted from the tuition fee pursuant to this Law.

E - The stages of education shall be taken into consideration in determining the tuition fee.

A - Every private school shall submit to the Private Education Department at the Ministry of National Education, Youth and Sports, within a time limit not exceeding the end of the month of January of each academic year, a copy of its annual budget signed by the school principal and the president of the Parents' Committee, or by the delegates of the Committee on the Financial Board in the case provided for in the last paragraph of item 8 of Article Ten, and with respect to the 1995-1996 academic year, the copy of the annual budget shall be submitted within a time limit of one month from the date of entry into force of this Law.

The following documents shall be attached to the copy of the budget:

1 - A certified true copy of the minutes of the Financial Board relating to its position on the draft budget and to the position of the Parents' Committee thereon.

2-An annual financial clearance certificate issued by the administration of the Compensation Fund for Members of the Teaching Staff in Private Schools, proving that the school has paid the deductions and contributions due from it in respect of the members of the teaching staff who have entered into its establishment plan by operation of law, provided that the clearance certificate is accompanied by a copy, certified with the seal of the administration of the Compensation Fund for Members of the Teaching Staff in Private Schools, of the information statement submitted by private educational institutions concerning contracted teachers and those who have entered into the establishment plan, accompanied by a nominal roll of the members of the teaching staff containing the salary and the additional allowances received by each member of the teaching staff as compensation for the collapse of the Lebanese currency, audited in itself and in its content by comparison with the accounting records of the school and the supporting documents and papers thereof by an independent auditor from among the certified public accountants classified in the Lebanese Association of Certified Public Accountants appointed by the school, who shall prepare a reasoned report confirming this information to be attached to the aforementioned nominal roll."

3 - A statement of the names of the children of employees at the school who benefit from an education grant and the value of this grant, and of the names of the children exempted from the school tuition fee pursuant to this Law and their classes, and the value of the education grants declared to the school by members of the teaching staff which are granted to them from a source other than the school.

4 - A copy of the documents proving the payment of settlements relating to the adjustment of the end-of-service indemnity of persons subject to the Labour Law for the preceding year.

"By way of exception, legal persons that have several non-free private schools and wish to alleviate the school tuition fees for the pupils of one or more of these schools by charging the burden thereof to the pupils of their other schools, or some of them, may submit at one time to the Private Education Department, within the time limit legally prescribed, the budgets of the schools concerned, accompanied by a comprehensive budget covering all of these schools signed by the Parents' Committees therein in accordance with the provisions of this Law, and by a detailed letter setting out the situation.

The conditions provided for in the first paragraph of Article Two of this Law shall apply to this comprehensive budget.

B - If new burdens arise as required by newly enacted laws and regulations, the administration of every school must draw up an annex of the total of these burdens and the resulting increase in the tuition fee in proportion to the educational stage as a result of dividing these burdens by the number of pupils adopted for calculating the tuition fee, and send a copy thereof to the Private Education Department, signed by the school principal and the president of the Parents' Committee, or by the delegates of the Committee on the Financial Board in the case provided for in paragraph (A) above, within a time limit not exceeding the end of the academic year.

C - By way of exception, and if it is proven to the Private Education Department that the expenditures and burdens falling within the scope of item (C) of the Chapter of Expenditures exceed thirty-five percent (35%) and are not subject to reduction, the Minister of National Education, Youth and Sports may, upon the request of the school and the proposal of the Head of the Private Education Department, approve the distribution of the percentages among items (A), (B) and (C) in accordance with the actual situation, provided that the increase does not exceed five percent of the total of the three items (A), (B) and (C) and that the Parents' Committee approves this increase.

A - Upon the formation of the Pupils' Guardians Committee (Parents' Committee) and in the determination of its role, in addition to that which is specified in Law No. 11/81 dated 13 May 1981, the following provisions shall be observed:

1- The invitation to the meeting designated for selecting the members of the Parents' Committee shall be addressed in writing in due time during the first term of the school year, provided that it is notified to the pupils' guardians personally and pursuant to a special notification notice to be kept in the invitation file, and provided that a general invitation is also addressed to the pupils' guardians to be posted on the outer door of the school.

It shall be stated in the invitation that if the quorum is not completed at the specified time, the electing General Assembly shall convene on the same day and at the same hour of the following week, and the quorum shall be legal with those present.

2 - The selected member is presumed to be educated and of good conduct, provided that priority shall be given, when naming the delegates of the Parents' Committee to the Financial Board, to those with experience in administrative and financial affairs. The candidacy of anyone working in the school shall not be accepted, and the school shall not have the right to reject any candidacy that fulfils the specified conditions.

3 - The electing General Assembly shall convene, and its legal quorum shall not be completed in the first meeting except in the presence of the absolute majority of its members (i.e. half the number plus one). In the event that the quorum is not completed in the first meeting, the second meeting shall be legal with those present.

4 - The selection process shall take place in the presence of a delegate from the Ministry of National Education, Youth and Sports in the capacity of an observer and a delegate from the federation or grouping of pupils' guardians to which the Parents' Committee in the school is affiliated, provided that the absence of this latter delegate shall not be deemed as obstructing the said selection process. The said Parents' Committee must notify the federation or grouping concerned of the time of the selection.

5 - Anyone who did not participate in the meeting of the General Assembly may not challenge the results of the selection process and the decisions that may have been taken by the Assembly in the same session.

6 - The term of office of the Parents' Committee and the duration of membership therein shall be three years, renewable once only by selection by the pupils' guardians in accordance with the rules so long as the legal conditions for candidacy are met, provided that the duration of membership prior to the date of entry into force of this Law shall be included in the calculation.

7 - The Financial Board is the body empowered to examine financial affairs, approve the budget, determine school tuition fees, and decide on the increase in tuition fees, and it shall complete the examination of the budget within a time limit of ten days from the date the draft is submitted to it. The delegates of the Parents' Committee on the said Board shall not have the right to take any final provisional [stance] within it before referring back to the Parents' Committee, except in the case referred to in Paragraph (8) below.

8 - The Parents' Committee shall take its decision by absolute majority in light of the report of its two delegates on the Financial Board and shall notify it in writing to them both; and if a period of fifteen days elapses and this Committee has not taken any decision or has not notified its decision to the two said delegates, they shall both have the right to take the stance that they deem appropriate.

B - If a judicial dispute arises between the school administration and one of the pupils' guardians therein due to the application of the provisions of this Law, the school administration shall not have the right to take any measure against his children due to the existing dispute.

C - Notwithstanding any text, the term of office of the Parents' Committees established prior to the entry into force of this Law shall terminate ipso jure at the end of September 1996, and the schools concerned therewith must establish Parents' Committees therein during the first term of the 1996 - 1997 school year.

If it appears that the tuition fees paid are below the tuition fees imposed by this Law, the school shall be entitled to collect the difference. However, if they exceed these tuition fees, the difference shall be refunded to the pupils.

The school tuition fee shall be collected in at least three instalments, provided that the first instalment does not exceed thirty per cent (30%) of the annual tuition fee for the preceding academic year, as a payment on account.

If the school imposes a fee for admission to the school or for registration, this fee may not exceed ten per cent of the value of the tuition fee for the preceding year, and in all events it must be considered part of the principal of the annual tuition fee due.

No school tuition fee shall be incurred in respect of the children of members of the teaching staff who have entered into the permanent establishment of the school by operation of law, where they pursue their studies therein.

As for the children of members of the teaching staff who have not entered into its permanent establishment, they shall be subject, with respect to education grants, to the internal regulations in force at the school in the event that such regulations provide for education grants for them.

The guardians of the children exempted from the school tuition fee pursuant to the provisions of this Article, who benefit on their behalf from an education grant from any other source, shall declare to the school the value of this grant and pay it to the school.

Pupils shall not be obliged to use the means of transport belonging to the school, and the school shall subject its means of transport to actual annual mechanical inspection in accordance with the laws in force.

The school may determine the lists of books and the specifications of school supplies. However, a pupil may not be obliged to purchase these books and supplies from the school or from any other authority.

Nor may he be prevented from using used school books that remain fit for use, or be obliged to take meals at the school.

Pupils of kindergarten classes shall be exempted from the provisions of this Article.
Parents' committees shall continue to perform all the functions provided for in Law No. 11/81 dated 13 May 1981, with the exception of that which conflicts with the provisions of this Law.

B - The members of this Council shall be appointed by decree upon the proposal of the Ministers of Justice and of National Education, Youth and Sports, and their appointment shall be subject to the general conditions applicable to the composition of Labour Arbitral Councils.

C - The Government shall be represented before each Council by a Commissioner seconded by the Minister of National Education, Youth and Sports from among the employees of the third category and above working in the Ministry.

D - The Ministry of Justice shall second one of the judicial assistants to perform the duty of clerk before each Council.

E - The President of the Arbitral Council and the two advisers, the Government Commissioner and the clerk shall receive an attendance allowance determined by decree.

B - The right of the parents' committees and of the pupils' guardians to the aforementioned recourse shall lapse after 30 July of the school year.

C - If the party claiming damage from the illegality of the school tuition fee or the increase thereof is a pupil's guardian, he must prove, under pain of inadmissibility of the recourse before the Arbitral Council, that he submitted a request to the parents' committee more than fifteen days earlier which did not lead to the removal of the damage from him or to the taking of any decision by the aforementioned committee.

The Arbitral Councils provided for in this Law shall adopt summary procedure and exceptional methods of service, and they must issue their judgments within a time limit of two months starting from the date of submission of the recourse. These judgments shall be final and shall not be subject to any form of appeal except opposition.
Every legal person licensed to open a fee-charging school shall designate a representative before the State to be responsible before it in the non-educational administrative affairs of the school.

With the exception of forgery in statements and declarations, which remains within the jurisdiction of the ordinary criminal courts, special arbitral councils established at the rate of one council for each educational district shall hear:

- Infringements of the provisions of this Law and disputes arising from its application.

- Appeals of pupils' guardians relating to measures taken by the school administration against their children therein, which are the subject of Paragraph (b) of Article Ten, and the appeal provided for in Article Seven of Law No. 11/81 dated 13 May 1981 in place of the Single Judge, and the provisions provided for in the said Article Seven shall apply to these appeals.

Appeals of school administrations against pupils' guardians who refrain from paying the tuition fee due for their children.

The Private Education Department at the Ministry of National Education, Youth and Sports shall oversee the application of the provisions of the preceding articles of this Law.

If the Private Education Department finds that the tuition fees determined or imposed by the school, or that the increase in tuition fees as adopted by it, are in violation of the provisions of this Law, it shall proceed to call upon the school administration to comply with the provisions of the Law under penalty of judicial prosecution, and in this case the Department shall determine for the school the amount of the tuition fees or the increase that must be adopted; and if the school persists and does not abide by this amount and does not object to it within ten days from its notification thereof, the school shall be referred to the competent arbitral council by a decision of the Minister of National Education, Youth and Sports.

To carry out the oversight, the Private Education Department shall be assisted by a number of employees at the Ministry of National Education, Youth and Sports placed at its disposal for a specified period by a decision of the Minister of National Education, Youth and Sports, and by certified public accountants or auditing and accounting oversight offices registered with the Lebanese Association of Certified Public Accountants.

Where it appears to the Arbitration Council that the increase in tuition fees is unlawful, it shall order the refund of such increase to those entitled thereto. If it appears to it that it was deliberate or in bad faith, it shall impose a financial fine ranging between 10% and 50% of the total value of the increase in tuition fees collected without right.

As for the remaining violations of the provisions of this Law, the following provisions shall apply thereto:

1 - A coercive financial fine for each day of delay and for a period of one month at the rate of one-quarter per thousand of the total annual tuition fees, upon submitting the copy of the budget to the Private Education Department after the expiry of the specified deadline.

2 - A financial fine ranging between 10% and 25% of the total annual tuition fees in the event of failure to submit the copy of the budget after the expiry of one month from the specified deadline.

3 - A financial fine ranging between three and five times the highest annual tuition fee in the school for each of the unmentioned violations. In the event of recurrence of the violation, the fine shall be doubled. The fines shall be collected in favour of the Treasury.

All other provisions that do not conflict with the texts of this Law shall remain in force. Educational Arbitration Councils established prior to its issuance shall continue to have jurisdiction to examine the matters brought before them.

Errors that may occur in the budget template annexed to this Law shall be rectified by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of National Education, Youth and Sports, and the appropriations required for the implementation of the provisions of Articles 13 and 14 hereof shall likewise be opened by a similar decree.

The draft law set forth in Decree No. 1834 dated 3 December 1999 relating to the rights of disabled persons, as amended by the Administration and Justice Committee and the Chamber of Deputies, is hereby ratified.

- This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette

Definition of the Disabled Person. A disabled person is a person whose capacity has diminished or ceased to:

- perform one or more important life activities,

- or secure the necessities of his personal life on his own.

- or participate in social activities on an equal footing with others,

- or ensure a normal personal or social life according to the prevailing standards of his society, due to a total or partial, permanent or temporary, physical, sensory, or mental functional loss or impairment resulting from a congenital or acquired defect or from a pathological condition that has lasted longer than it medically ought to last.

Classification: Proceeding from and inspired by the International Classification of Impairments, Disabilities, and Handicaps issued by the World Health Organization in 1980 and its subsequent amendments, which are in brief the following four types of disabilities:

Motor, visual, auditory, mental, the list of classification of disabilities shall be adopted and amended by a decree issued by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Social Affairs based on the recommendation of the National Committee for the Affairs of the Disabled.

Personal Disabled Card:

a- Every disabled person whose type of disability is included in the list mentioned in Article Three of this Law has the right to obtain a personal card entitling him to exercise the rights and privileges granted by the laws and regulations in force.

b- This card shall be considered the sole adopted means of proving disability.

The following terms, wherever they appear in this Law, shall have the meanings assigned to them below:

(a) "The Ministry": The Ministry of Social Affairs.

(b) "The Minister": The Minister of Social Affairs.

(c) "The National Committee": The "National Committee for the Affairs of Disabled Persons" as defined in Part Two of this Law.

(d) "Disabled Person" or "Disabled Persons": Individuals holding a personal disability card to whom the definition set forth in Article 2 of this Law applies. In the case of a hearing disability, the holder of the disability card may be the disabled person himself or his legal guardian, and in the case of a mental disability, the holder of the card shall be the legal guardian of the owner thereof.

(e) "Associations of Disabled Persons": Legal persons established in accordance with the law for a non-profit purpose (for example: an association) that meet the following conditions:

1- Their by-laws explicitly stipulate that one of their objectives relates to disability and the rights thereof.

2- At least half of the members of their general assembly are themselves "disabled persons" and at least half of the members of their administrative board are themselves "disabled persons" (including associations of legal guardians of "disabled persons" according to the definition of "disabled persons" above).

(f) "Service Associations":

Legal persons established in accordance with the law for a non-profit purpose (for example: an association, a religious community), regardless of the composition of their general and administrative bodies, that meet the following conditions:

1- They have at least one actual, specific, recognised and permanent service programme for disabled persons.

2- They are registered with the Ministry as a service association in accordance with the procedural rules adopted by the Ministry.

(g) "Service Institution": The service programme for disabled persons established for each of the four types of disability within service associations, on the basis of which the latter benefit from a special contract concluded with the Ministry.

For the purposes of applying the provisions of this Law, the number of service institutions in each association may not be less than one (in which case it coincides with the association itself) or more than four, that is, one institution for each type of disability. A service institution does not possess an independent legal personality by law except for the purposes of registration on the electoral rolls in order to benefit from the right to vote and to attend the general meetings provided for in this Law.

(h) "The Four Types of Disability":

They are the following types of disability: motor disability. visual disability. hearing disability. mental disability.

Procedure for issuing the Personal Disabled Person's Card:

A The conditions for obtaining the card shall be determined as follows:

1- Every disabled person must submit an application to obtain the card in person, or exceptionally through his legal guardian, his legal representative, or a member of his family possessing legal capacity.

2 - Applications shall be submitted at the centres accredited and equipped for this purpose by the Ministry.

3 - The Ministry shall issue the Personal Disabled Person's Card immediately if the required conditions and documents are satisfied.

4 - The decision to reject the application is subject to objection before the Ministry, Department of Disabled Persons' Affairs, which shall decide thereon within a maximum period of one month from the date of its submission. Upon the expiry of this period without a decision on the objection, the concerned party shall have the right to apply to the National Committee.

5 - The decision of the National Committee to reject the card application is final.

B - The card shall be issued for a specified period recorded thereon, and this period shall be determined according to the type and circumstances of the disability.

C - The period of the card may be renewed upon its expiry. The application for renewal, the decision thereon, and its rejection shall be subject to the same procedures and means of objection and appeal provided for in the clause of this Article.
