D- The contents of the card, the details of the procedural methods followed to obtain it, the manner of linking services to it, the manner of verifying that these services reach the beneficiary, and all regulatory details shall be determined by a decision of the Minister.

E The cards issued by the Ministry prior to the date of entry into force of this Law shall remain valid throughout the period of their validity.

Definition thereof:

A - The State shall attend to the affairs of disabled persons in all fields, including scientific, vocational, health and social fields, in cooperation between public administrations, the private sector and international institutions.

B - A permanent committee called the National Committee for the Affairs of Disabled Persons shall be established for this purpose, having its seat at the Ministry of Social Affairs.

C - The National Committee shall constitute the decision-making authority that undertakes to approve matters relating to the affairs of disabled persons within the tasks specified in the Seventh Article of this Law.

D - The organs of the Ministry shall constitute the executive body responsible for executing the decisions of the National Committee and putting all matters relating to the affairs of disabled persons into effect across all State organs and the concerned non-governmental and private institutions.

Its functions The National Committee shall perform the following functions:

1 - Preparing the general policy for the affairs of disabled persons in coordination with the competent bodies in the public sector, civil associations and non-governmental bodies.

2 - Contributing to laying down the executive programmes and plans for this policy in coordination with the competent public institutions and administrations.

3 - Preparing draft laws and regulations relating to disability of its own motion or upon the request of the Council of Ministers.

4 - Adopting the specifications and technical conditions that must be met in institutions working for disabled persons and in the field of serving them, in coordination with the competent administrations in the Ministry.

5 - Participating in external communications and in international conferences to develop projects and to organise them and contributing to planning to attract aid. It shall have the right to accept donations connected with disability from States, organisations and bodies in favour of the independent fund of the Ministry. 6 - Bringing an action or intervening in any lawsuit before any ordinary or exceptional judicial body in any matter connected with its functions or assisting in achieving them or defending disabled persons and their rights.

Its membership :

The National Committee shall be composed of eighteen members as follows:

A - Four ex officio members by virtue of their responsibilities and functions in the Ministry, namely: the Minister, the Director General, the Director of Social Services, the Head of the Department of Disabled Persons' Affairs.

B - Four members representing associations of disabled persons, elected by these associations in accordance with the provisions of Article "18" et seq. of this Law, provided that each of them represents one of the four types of disability.

C - Four representatives of service associations, elected by these associations in accordance with the provisions of Article /18/ et seq. of this Law, provided that each of them represents one of the four types of disability.

D - Four representatives of disabled persons themselves, elected by all the disabled persons registered on the special electoral rolls in accordance with the provisions of Article /18/ et seq. of this Law, provided that each of them represents one of the four types of disability.

E - Two members appointed by a decision of the Minister from among persons of expertise that serves the objectives of the National Committee and the success of its work.

The appointment shall take place within a time limit not exceeding fifteen days from the announcement of the election results of all the elected members.
Term of its mandate The term of the mandate of the National Committee shall be three years running from the completion of its composition in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

Its meetings:

A - The National Committee shall hold a regular periodic meeting at a place and date that it determines in the first session it holds after its formation, provided that it holds a meeting at least every two months.

B - The National Committee shall hold extraordinary meetings when need calls for it, upon the invitation of its President or by a written request from five of its members for reasoned causes submitted to the President, whereby he shall be bound to call a meeting within a time limit not exceeding two weeks in accordance with the requested agenda.

C - The sessions of the National Committee shall be convened, discussions shall take place and voting on decisions shall be conducted therein in the presence of the absolute majority of the members, except for the cases in which the law explicitly provides otherwise.

D - The National Committee shall take its decisions by a majority of the votes of the members present, and in the event of an equality in the number of votes, the President shall have a casting vote, except for the cases in which the law explicitly provides otherwise.

E - The National Committee shall lay down the internal regulations for its deliberations and meetings, which shall be issued by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister.

The Bureau of the National Committee:

A- The Bureau of the National Committee shall be composed of the following seven members:

1- The President: the Minister

2- The Vice-President: the Director General of the Ministry

3- The Secretary: the Head of the Department of Disabled Persons' Affairs in the Ministry

4- Member: a representative of the associations of disabled persons

5- Member: a representative of the service associations

6- Member: a representative of the disabled persons themselves

7- Member: a representative of the appointed members

B - The Bureau of the National Committee shall undertake the task of preparing the agenda of the National Committee and following up the implementation of its resolutions.

C - With the exception of the ex officio members of the Bureau of the National Committee (the Minister, the Director and the Head of the Department of Disabled Persons' Affairs), the members of the Bureau shall be elected by the National Committee by secret ballot and by absolute majority in accordance with its own quorum and voting rules, and the term of office of the Bureau shall be one year renewable in accordance with the election procedures specified in this paragraph.

D - The Bureau of the National Committee shall meet periodically in accordance with what it decides, or upon the invitation of the President or at the request of two of its members for reasoned causes submitted to the President, whereby he shall then be bound to call a meeting within a time limit not exceeding one week in accordance with the requested agenda.

E - If one of the positions of the Bureau of the National Committee becomes permanently vacant or unoccupied, an invitation shall be duly issued for a meeting of the National Committee within a time limit not exceeding one month during which the vacancy shall be filled by election.

Determination of the permanent functions at the National Committee:

A - The President: The Minister shall be ex officio President of the National Committee and President of its Bureau, and in this capacity he shall assume the following tasks:

1- He represents the National Committee before all private, political, administrative, judicial and military national and international authorities, and he is responsible for the proper functioning of the work of the National Committee.

2 - He convenes and presides over the sessions of the National Committee, its Bureau, and the annual and extraordinary General Assembly.

3 - He signs, together with the Secretary, the minutes of the meetings of the National Committee, the Bureau, and the annual meetings.

B - The Vice-President: The Director General of the Ministry shall be ex officio Vice-President of the National Committee, and in this capacity he shall assume all the tasks and powers of the President in the event of his absence or by delegation from him.

C - The Secretary: The Head of the Department of the Affairs of Disabled Persons at the Ministry shall be the Secretary, and in this capacity he shall assume the following tasks:

1 - He supervises the keeping and organisation of all legal registers, including the registers of the minutes of the sessions and the decisions of the National Committee, its Bureau and the General Assemblies, and signs them together with the President.

2 - He keeps and organises a general roster of the names of the members of the General Assembly across their various categories.

3 - He receives and keeps correspondence and communications.

4 - He sends out invitations and notifies the resolutions of the Assembly to the concerned parties and official administrations.

Subcommittees:

A - Subcommittees may be established by a decision of the National Committee determining: their name, their tasks, the number of their members, the procedures for admission to membership therein, and their rapporteur, who must be one of the members of the National Committee.

B - The committee is entitled to seek the assistance of whomever it wishes among specialists.

C - Every member of the National Committee has the right to attend the meetings of the committee even if he is not an appointed member thereof, and he may contribute to its work like the rest of its members without having the right to vote.

D - The committee is convened to hold its session by the Minister, President of the National Committee, or by the chairman of the committee or its rapporteur, and it follows in its meetings, mutatis mutandis, all the procedures in force with respect to the National Committee.

E - The committee periodically submits a report on its work to the National Committee. It also submits its proposals to this Committee in the form of drafts for approval, which must include their explanatory memorandums and a summary of the various opinions that were deliberated upon, and a copy of the studies, memorandums and working papers that were discussed must be attached thereto.

Its Convening:

A - The President of the National Committee shall call annually for a general meeting to be held during the first seven months from the beginning of the year, in the presence of the current and former members of the National Committee, a delegated representative of each association of disabled persons and of each service institution, and all disabled persons. If the specified period expires and the President fails to call for the annual general meeting, it shall be convened pursuant to a call by half of the members of the National Committee.

B - The National Committee shall set the date and agendas of the general meetings, and shall address the invitation by means of written letters or an announcement in two local newspapers and an audio medium, at least thirty days prior to the date of the convening of the general meeting.

The Agenda:

The agenda of the general meetings shall include the following matters:

A - Examining and discussing the general annual report of the National Committee and adopting the appropriate recommendations in respect thereof.

B - Examining and discussing all the matters listed on the agenda and adopting the appropriate recommendations in respect thereof.

Its Deliberations:

A - The President of the National Committee shall preside over the sessions of the general meetings.

B - The convening of the sessions of the annual general meetings of disabled persons shall be legal regardless of the number of members present.

C - Any of the invited members present shall have the right to speak on any of the subjects listed on the agenda, and any of them shall also have the right to propose points that he wishes to discuss during the general meetings, provided that he notifies these points to the National Committee at least one week prior to the date of the convening of the meeting.

D - Recommendations shall be adopted by a relative majority of votes (half of the votes plus one) and by a show of hands, and voting by proxy shall not be accepted.

Call for Elections:

The Minister shall issue, at least two months prior to the date of the election, a decision whereby he sets the date of the election and the date of the expiry of the nomination time limits.

The decisions of the Minister relating to the election shall be circulated to all operating associations and institutions by mail and shall be published in the Official Gazette and in three media outlets (at least one of which is audio) at least one month prior to the expiry of the nomination date.

Election of the First National Committee:

The election of the first National Committee shall take place in accordance with the provisions of this Law, within a maximum time limit of three months following its promulgation.

Electoral Bodies and Electoral Lists:

A - The Minister shall issue a decision setting forth the final nominal lists of voters four months prior to the election date, and they shall be of three types:

1 - Four lists specific to associations of disabled persons, classified according to each type of disability, in which registration shall be compulsory and automatic.

2 - Four lists specific to service institutions, classified according to each type of disability and according to the name of the association of which they form part, in which registration shall be compulsory and automatic.

3 - Lists specific to disabled persons, in which registration shall be optional for any disabled person who requests it and agrees to waive his right to confidentiality relating to his disability for the purposes of organising and conducting the elections. Disabled persons who are affiliated and who are not affiliated with any of the associations of disabled persons or service associations shall be registered in these lists.

B - Any candidate, any association concerned with the elections, and any disabled person who requested the inclusion of his name in one of the electoral lists shall have the right to inspect those final nominal lists of the electoral bodies at the Ministry, to copy them, and to request their correction or to challenge them.

Candidacy:

Candidacy for membership of the National Committee shall be submitted to the Ministry, Department of Disabled Persons' Affairs.

The Voting Process:

A - Representatives of the Ministry appointed by a decision of the Minister shall preside over the polling stations, assisted by a clerk appointed in accordance with the same rules. One representative for each candidate shall have the right to enter the polling station and observe the electoral operations.

B - The election of representatives of associations of disabled persons and service associations shall be conducted by secret ballot on a single day and in separate ballot boxes for each of them and for each of the four types of disability that must be represented on the National Committee.

C - The election of representatives of disabled persons themselves shall be conducted by secret ballot on a single day and in separate ballot boxes for each of the four types of disability that must be represented on the National Committee. These elections may be organised in a single place, or decentrally in the regions and centres designated by the Ministry.

Counting of votes, conditions for winning, and results thereof:

A - The head of the polling station and his assistant shall conduct the counting of votes; he shall open the ballot papers, count them, and then read them aloud, whereupon his assistant shall record and tally them. Every candidate or his delegate shall have the right to attend the counting of votes and observe the course thereof. At the conclusion of the counting of votes, the head of the polling station shall draw up a report on the course of the electoral process, the counting of votes, the result thereof, and the objections of the candidates, if any, and shall sign it jointly with the assistant and the candidates or their delegates.

B - Ballot papers that name more than one candidate for a single seat shall be annulled.

C - The candidate who obtains the largest number of votes in the disability category for which he stood as a candidate shall be deemed the winner. If the votes of two or more candidates are equal in any category, the oldest in age shall win. The next candidate shall be deemed the winner as an alternate member, and he shall replace the regular member if the latter resigns or is permanently unable to attend meetings for any reason whatsoever.

D - The member who wins any seat of the National Committee shall be deemed a representative of the entire sector for which he was elected and not solely a representative of the association or institution that nominated him.

E - The regular member shall remain a member of the National Committee until the expiry of the term of office of the latter, even if he leaves the association or institution to which he belongs, for any reason whatsoever.

The Electoral Body:

A - The electoral body for the members of the National Committee representing associations concerned with disabled persons shall be composed of all associations of disabled persons and service institutions whose names appear on the electoral list specific to these two categories.

B - Each association of disabled persons or service institution shall be represented by one of its members holding a special authorisation therefrom to participate in the election process.

Candidacy:

A - The right of candidacy shall be restricted to associations of disabled persons and service associations (excluding service institutions) whose names appear on the special electoral lists.

B - An association shall not have the right to run as a candidate for more than one seat in the National Committee even if it serves more than one category of the four types of disability.

C - The association shall submit its candidacy pursuant to a letter issued by a decision of its administrative board and in accordance therewith, signed by its president or by its representative before the Government (if different from the president), stamped with its official seal, provided that this letter includes the following:

1 - The capacity in which the association is running as a candidate (disabled persons or services).

2 - The type of seat for which the association is running as a candidate for each type of the four types of disability.

3 - Specifying the name of the natural person from among its members who is authorised to carry out the voting process in the name of the association, together with the name of an alternate authorised person from among its members if the authorised person is unable to attend for any reason whatsoever.

4 - Specifying the name of the natural person from among its members who is the candidate to fill the seat in the National Committee.

The Electoral Body:

A - The electoral body for the members of the National Committee representing disabled persons shall be composed of all the disabled persons whose names appear on their special voters' lists.

B - Each member of the electoral body shall vote provided with the disability card.

Candidacy:

The disabled member shall run as a candidate in person pursuant to a letter, provided that it includes specifying the type of disability which he is running as a candidate to represent in the Committee and the name of the association or associations to which he belongs (if he belongs to an association), provided that this shall not be one of the conditions of candidacy.

Scope of rights:

A - Every person with a disability shall have the right to benefit from health services, rehabilitation and support services in their entirety at the expense of the State, represented by the various administrations and bodies that provide such services.

B - These services shall include, by way of enumeration and not limitation:

1 - All surgical operations, whether resulting from the disability or not: including transplantation, treatment of ulcers, orthopaedics of limbs, and hospitalisation in specialised or non-specialised centres for intensive or regular care. This coverage shall include all equipment, instruments, implants and other items necessary for the success of the operation, whether permanent or temporary.

2 - Medical care (general practitioners, specialists, dentists...), medicines, radiology, laboratory analyses and other temporary and permanent treatments and examinations (special analyses for the newborn: including for the thyroid gland, phenylalanine G6PD, psychological assessment, audiometry, ...).

3 - In-patient and out-patient rehabilitative and specialised therapy (physiotherapy, occupational, speech, auditory, psychological therapy...).

4 - Technical aids and equipment, including mobile and fixed prosthetic devices (limbs, hearing aids, artificial eye and others), orthotic braces, mobility aids, wheelchairs (canes and crutches), aids for double incontinence and for the prevention of ulcers, all implants used in surgical operations, and these services shall include maintenance when it arises.

Comprehensive coverage:

A person with a disability shall have the right to benefit from the comprehensive coverage provided by the Ministry of Public Health, whether on the basis of primary coverage if he does not benefit from any other coverage, or on the basis of supplementary coverage added to any other coverage that covers the services only partially, and he shall remain a beneficiary of all other services (family allowances and others) provided by the guaranteeing entity to which he belongs.

Health, Rehabilitation and Support Services Committee:

A - A joint committee representing all administrations and institutions that provide health, rehabilitation and support services shall be formed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, called the Health, Rehabilitation and Support Services Committee for Disabled Persons, and it shall be chaired by the Director General of the Ministry of Social Affairs, and shall include a disabled member from among the members of the National Committee. This Committee shall lay down the internal regulations for its meetings.

B - This Committee shall undertake the following tasks by way of enumeration and not limitation:

1 - Detailing and developing the list of services mentioned in Article 27 of this Law, while specifying the basic specifications that permit the provision thereof, including: description, maximum quantities, age of the beneficiary, validity period of use, and others...

2 - Evaluating and standardising the prices of health services.

3 - Specifying the entities that will provide the services and the conditions required of them, especially those newly established among them.

4 - Standardising the adopted procedural methods.

5 - Laying down measures aimed at:

- Ensuring that the disabled person obtains the service required by his condition.

- Limiting waste and unnecessary expenses.

- Facilitating procedural methods and transactions as much as possible.

- Maintaining all requirements of quality, proper performance, and safety.

C - This Committee shall submit its decisions through the Minister of Social Affairs to the Council of Ministers, to take the appropriate decisions regarding them.

Scope of Rights:

A - Every disabled person has the right to a qualified environment, meaning that every disabled person has the right of access to any place to which a non-disabled person can have access.

B - All public and private buildings, installations and facilities intended for public use must have their engineering specifications in conformity with the standards and in accordance with the conditions and rules stipulated in this Law.

Miscellaneous procedures:

A - No other proof of his disability shall be required from the disabled person save for the Personal Disabled Person's Card.

B - Contrary to the provisions of Article 4 of Legislative Decree No. 72 issued on 19 September 1983 (Care, Treatment and Protection of the Mentally Ill), the hospitalisation of a mentally ill patient at the expense of the Ministry of Health shall not be conditional upon the inability of the mentally ill patient, his relatives or those responsible for him to bear the expenses of his treatment, follow-up or rehabilitation.

C - Where the guaranteeing body is the Ministry of Public Health, this Ministry shall cover all expenses within the hospital even in the event of the exhaustion of the beds allocated to it in accordance with the procedures in force. Provided that a decision shall be issued by the Ministry of Public Health specifying these procedures.

Prevention:

A - With the aim of preventing certain accidents that cause several types of disability, strict standards must be established imposing equipment, continuing training and education programmes, and appropriate methods and technologies in hospitals, maternity homes and other similar institutions.

B - A decision shall be issued by the Ministry of Public Health at the earliest possible opportunity following the issuance of this Law, specifying those specifications and incorporating them into the conditions of the licence granted by the Ministry of Public Health.

C - All concerned institutions shall be granted a time limit of two years after the issuance of the ministerial decision mentioned above to regularise their status, on pain of being subjected, pursuant to a decision issued by the Ministry of Public Health, at least to fines estimated at the value of ten times a delivery operation according to the tariff of the Ministry of Public Health and at most to the cancellation of the maternity department therein, or any offending department.

Awareness-raising:

The Ministries of Public Health and Social Affairs must periodically organise awareness-raising campaigns and publish information relating to the available services, the duties of health bodies, and preventive measures, especially for pregnant women.

Minimum standards and additional standards:

A - The external and internal engineering and technical standards required to be satisfied in all construction, rehabilitation or restoration works for public or private buildings, structures and facilities intended for public or private use shall be adopted; these standards shall be established with the approval of the Ministry of Social Affairs after seeking the opinion of the National Committee for the Affairs of Disabled Persons and shall be added to the Building Law in accordance with the legal procedures in force. These standards shall be referred to as the minimum standards for buildings and installations.

B - There shall also be adopted, in accordance with the procedures set out above, the external and internal engineering and technical standards relating to the additional rehabilitations presumed to be provided in accordance with the special needs of certain disabled persons, which do not automatically fall within the minimum standards for buildings and installations, and which shall be referred to as the additional standards.

C - The minimum standards for buildings and installations shall include in their classification at least four parts:

First: Equipping public buildings and facilities, or those intended for public use, that are to be constructed.

Second: Rehabilitating existing public buildings and facilities, or those intended for public use.

Third: Equipping private buildings that are to be constructed.

Fourth: Encouraging the rehabilitation of existing private buildings.

Related text: Application of the provisions of Law No. 220 dated 29/5/2000 relating to the Rights of Disabled Persons

Permits and certificates of conformity:

A - Starting from the issuance of the minimum standards for buildings and installations, the technical and engineering conditions specified in those standards must be satisfied in applications for permits for construction, rehabilitation, restoration and occupancy, or any administrative permit required for the use or exploitation of any building.

B - A special certificate of conformity regarding the completion of rehabilitation operations, or exemption therefrom where the conditions for such exemption are satisfied, shall be issued by the Ministry of Public Works after consultation with the Ministry of Social Affairs.

Public buildings, facilities and utilities:

A - Official buildings and departments, sidewalks, roads, public gardens, archaeological and tourist sites, and other public buildings, facilities and utilities, including traffic signs, shall be rehabilitated in accordance with the minimum standards for buildings and facilities. Permanent maintenance works shall form an integral part of the works incumbent upon all concerned bodies.

B - All concerned public authorities, whether central (for example: the concerned ministries), deconcentrated (for example: the Qaimaqamiyas and Muhafazas), and decentralised (for example: the municipalities and unions of municipalities), each within the scope of its competence, shall be granted six (6) years to regularise their situation, running from the date of issuance of the minimum standards for buildings and facilities, in accordance with the following programme:

1 - Each concerned authority shall submit to the Ministry of Public Works, during the year following the issuance of the minimum standards for buildings and facilities, a plan to implement all the rehabilitations and modifications provided for therein.

2 - These rehabilitations and modifications shall be implemented in accordance with the plan that has been approved, during the year following the allocation of the necessary appropriations by the competent bodies.

C - Every municipality that completes those rehabilitations, and modifications prior to the statutory time limit specified above, shall be granted an exceptional increase from the Municipal Fund to its budget in the amount of twenty per cent (20%) for the statutory years, provided that ten per cent (10%) thereof is allocated to finance works and projects specific to disabled persons.

D - A specific amount must be provided for in the budgets of municipalities or Qaimaqamiyas or Muhafazas to finance works and projects specific to disabled persons and to secure the rehabilitation works provided for in this Law.

Publication and Teaching of the Minimum Standards:

A - Subjects containing a detailed explanation of all standards relating to the rehabilitation of buildings and all facilities in accordance with the minimum standards for buildings and installations and the additional standards shall be added to the subjects taught at public and private universities and institutes that graduate engineers in all specialisations.

B - The Ministry of Social Affairs shall issue, whenever the need arises, a detailed practical guide on the minimum standards for buildings and installations, the additional standards, and the various legal and technical conditions relating to the implementation thereof, and shall deposit it with the municipalities and other public or private bodies where it shall be distributed free of charge to whoever requests it. It shall also work to provide engineering and technical advice free of charge to anyone who so desires.

Exemptions:

A - All works relating to the subject of rehabilitation mentioned in this Law, including private buildings intended for private use, shall be exempted from municipal fees on rehabilitation permits, if completed within the legal time limit.

B - Every owner who completes such rehabilitations before the expiry of the legal time limit, and before the annual tax on the rental value falls due, shall be granted an exemption of twenty-five per cent (25%) of the value of that tax until the expiry of the six-year period granted by this Law.

C - Every application for a permit to renovate an existing building, with the aim of facilitating the movement of disabled persons in accordance with the standards present in the Building Law and whatever the purpose of use of this building, whether for residence, work, or otherwise, shall be exempted from municipal fees, from building permit fees, and from the obligation to submit a financial or municipal clearance certificate.

Fines:

A - Upon the expiry of the six-year time limit granted by this Law, the buildings and installations covered by Articles /36/ and /37/ of this Law, which do not conform to the required standards and have not obtained the exceptional exemption provided for in Article /38/ of this Law, shall be subject to a fine equal to twice the rental value of the building.

B - Every non-rehabilitated building shall be subject to a doubled annual municipal tax, until it carries out the required modifications.

C - The owner shall pay a fine estimated at the value of the annual tax on the rental value, if he fails to declare the resumption of exploitation within one month thereof in accordance with the provisions of Paragraph (B) of Article /38/ of this Law, and he shall be given a time limit of six months to regularise his status.

D - All fines shall be allocated to the municipalities concerned and shall be used to finance works and projects specific to disabled persons.

Private buildings and facilities intended for public use:

A - Private buildings, facilities, and amenities intended for public use shall be rehabilitated in accordance with the minimum standards for buildings and facilities, and the burden of rehabilitating them shall fall upon the owner or owners in the event that they are occupied or operated by them or upon every new operation following the issuance of this Law.

B - Every three years or whenever necessary, a comprehensive list of all buildings, premises, and amenities intended for public use shall be issued, including, by way of example and not limitation: nurseries, schools, universities and educational institutes. Hospitals and dispensaries, hotels and restaurants, cinemas, sports stadiums, commercial complexes and places of worship, pursuant to a decision issued by the Ministry of Public Works upon the proposal of the Ministry of Social Affairs.

C - The owner or owners of the premises specified above shall be granted a time limit of six years to regularise their status, running from the date of issuance of the minimum standards for buildings and facilities, in accordance with the following programme:

1 - Submitting plans for rehabilitation to the concerned authorities (municipality, Kaymakamlik...).

2 - And two years shall be granted after the approval. thereon to execute them, provided that the time limit for approval does not exceed one month calculated as part of this year.

Exceptional exemptions from the obligation of rehabilitation:

A - Every public or private entity concerned with the provisions of this Law may submit to the competent authorities an application for exemption from the obligations of rehabilitation or from the implementation of all or some of the minimum standards for buildings and facilities, where one of the following reasons is met:

1 - Technical impossibility of carrying out any rehabilitative modification.

2 - A hazard likely to cause harm to the existing building.

3 - If it is impossible for the applicant to operate his property for a period of at least five years.

B - Every exemption granted by reason of the non-operation of the building shall be revoked immediately upon the resumption of operation, and the owner shall declare the resumption of operation or use.

Rehabilitation of private premises intended for the use of disabled persons:

The works relating to the rehabilitation of private premises intended for the use of disabled persons may be financed by loans granted by the Housing Fund, the Public Corporation for Housing, or any other competent public body in accordance with the conditions specified in this Law.

The International Symbol for Disabled Persons:

A - The Lebanese State shall adopt the International Symbol for Disabled Persons and circulate it across all facilities and in all booklets and programmes that include symbols from: the Construction Law, municipal traffic signs, public works, the Security Forces, and others, and the Ministry of Social Affairs shall issue by a special decision, whenever the need arises, a list of all signs and stickers that confer any right or privilege.

B - The Ministry of Social Affairs alone shall have the right to issue or authorise the issuance of any document or sign containing the International Symbol for Disabled Persons that leads to benefiting from public benefits, and a regulatory decision relating to this matter shall be issued by the said Ministry specifying, for example, the party that may obtain it, and how.

C - The municipality or any other competent authority (for example: the Qaemaqam, the Mohafez) shall designate the places allocated for parking for a disabled person by fixing the special sign containing the International Symbol for Disabled Persons, and shall fix it and undertake its maintenance at its own expense.

D - The public authorities shall have the right to remove any sign that was not placed in accordance with the rules specified in this Article, and in the event that the identity of the perpetrator is verified, a fine equal to double the highest fine imposed on unlicensed stickers and signs shall be imposed on him. The Vehicle Registration Department shall remove all stickers containing the International Symbol for Disabled Persons upon the transfer of ownership of the vehicle to a new non-disabled owner.

Public Means of Transport Adapted for Disabled Persons:

A - The Ministry of Transport shall provide buses or other means of transport, adapted and prepared for the use of disabled persons in accordance with international safety standards, and equipped with audio alerts for the blind, with the presence of at least two assistants to the driver, at a rate of at least (15%) fifteen per cent of the total number of each type of means of transport available at the Ministry of Transport, and the said Ministry shall impose the equipping of every new public means of transport in accordance with the standards mentioned in this Article.

B - These means of transport shall be identified by affixing the International Symbol of Access for Disabled Persons on all sides of the means of transport and shall be equipped with a special alarm (horn) which the driver is mandatorily required to sound upon stopping and departing to alert visually disabled persons, and the use of this horn for other than the designated means of transport shall be prohibited.

C - The stations at which the means of transport adapted for disabled persons stop shall be identified by affixing the International Symbol of Access for Disabled Persons in visible places.

D - There shall be formed, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, a joint committee representing the public and private bodies concerned with transport, called the "Mobility Committee for Disabled Persons", whose mission shall be to study and approve everything that facilitates the mobility of a disabled person, and which shall be chaired by the Director General of the Ministry of Transport and include a disabled member from among the members of the National Committee.

This Committee shall submit its decisions through the Minister of Transport to the Council of Ministers to take the appropriate decisions thereon.

Related text: Formation of the Mobility Committee for Disabled Persons

Public Means of Transport Not Adapted for Disabled Persons:

A - Seats near the entrances in public means of transport not specially adapted for disabled persons shall be allocated at a rate of at least one seat in every public means of transport, and the International Symbol of Access for the Disabled Person shall be affixed to the reserved seat. Every holder of a personal card shall have priority to sit on it and the right to claim an adjacent seat for a wheelchair, or for an accompanying person, particularly in aircraft and ships.

B - The driver or the assistant shall ensure that the person provided with the personal disabled person card is allowed to use the door nearest to his seat to exit if he so requests.

Financial Benefits and Discounts:

Every person provided with the personal card and one accompanying person shall benefit from public land means of transport free of charge, and he and one accompanying person shall obtain a discount of fifty per cent on every travel ticket aboard an airline or ships in whose ownership the State participates, whatever the percentage of such participation, provided that the accompanying person is actually travelling with the disabled person.

Violations of Special Parking Rights:

A - Every vehicle parking in places designated for disabled persons must be transporting a person holding the Personal Disabled Card, whether upon parking or upon departure. The Special Parking Card shall be placed on the inside of the front windscreen, where it can be clearly seen.

B - The traffic policeman and the competent authorities must verify that vehicles parked in the designated places comply with the conditions mentioned above; otherwise, they shall be deemed in violation of the Traffic Law in accordance with the applicable article and shall pay the fine relating to parking in prohibited places, at double the fine for parking in a prohibited place.

C - A vehicle parked in a prohibited place and transporting a person holding the Personal Disabled Card and the Special Parking Card shall be exempted from the fines due in the event that no other parking space is available within a maximum distance of one hundred metres (100m) from the intended destination, or if those spaces are occupied, provided that such parking does not harm public safety.

Training:

The Ministry of Social Affairs, in cooperation with the Ministries of the Interior, Transport, and Municipal and Rural Affairs, shall organise training courses directed at traffic and municipal officers and policemen, drivers of public and private buses and public service vehicles (and their assistants), in which it instructs them on all laws and measures in force and on the manner of dealing with disabled persons in terms of the time required for boarding and alighting, assistive devices, accompanying persons, and other useful information.

On the penalty for refusing to transport a disabled person:

Every driver of any means of transport intended for public or shared transport who refuses to transport a disabled person shall be deemed in violation of the Traffic Law. The fine for this violation shall be double the fine for parking in a prohibited place.

Public parking spaces designated for disabled persons:

a - Parking spaces for cars transporting disabled persons shall be designated in the parking lots belonging to every public building or building intended for public use, at a rate of one and a half percent of the capacity of such parking lot in accordance with the standards adopted in the Building Law, and this percentage shall be rounded up to calculate the number of spaces. At least three and a half metres shall be reserved for each car, and they shall be the closest to the entrance of the intended building.

b - In the event of the unavailability of a private or public parking lot for public buildings or buildings intended for public use, parking spaces for cars transporting disabled persons shall be designated on all public roads, provided that this does not compromise public safety, at a maximum distance of fifty metres from the entrance of the intended building.

Private parking spaces for disabled persons:

a - Every person provided with the personal disabled card and the private parking card shall have the right to submit to the municipality (or any competent authority) in his place of residence an application to reserve one private parking space for him in the parking lot designated for his place of residence that is closest to the entrance, or at a maximum distance of fifty metres if a private parking lot is not available, which may be on the public road provided that this does not compromise public safety.

b - The Ministry of Social Affairs shall issue a decision on the specifications and conditions for obtaining that card.

c - Every holder of the personal disabled card shall submit an application to the centres issuing that card to obtain the private parking card, and if his disability corresponds to obtaining this service, he shall be handed the card immediately.

d - The application shall be submitted by the person concerned, his guardian, or one of his family members residing with him in accordance with the certificate of the mukhtar.

e - The municipality shall proceed to reserve this parking space in accordance with the adopted standards, within forty-eight hours from the submission of the application. A notice prohibiting anyone from using this parking space shall be affixed in the entrances of the neighbouring buildings at a distance of fifty metres, or only within the building concerned if the parking space is private.

Driving Licences:

a - Every disabled person shall have the right to submit an application for a circulation licence for a public vehicle of any type or category whatsoever, and it shall be granted to him in accordance with the conditions and procedures in force.

b - The sixth category of the categories specified for circulation licences shall be amended so as to include all adapted and equipped vehicles, from motorcycles to public cars, trucks and others.

c - The phrase printed on driving licences of any category whatsoever indicating any disability shall be amended so that the phrase "A vehicle equipped according to the need of its driver" suffices.

d - Special needs shall be taken into consideration when conducting the written and oral examinations leading to a driving licence, in accordance with a request granted by the Ministry of Social Affairs, and the decisions relating to these examinations shall be reviewed upon a proposal by the Ministry of Health and the Ministry of Social Affairs, at least once every five years or whenever the need requires in view of scientific development relating to dealing with disabilities and illnesses.

e - The ordinary conditions imposed for obtaining a driving licence shall apply to all persons with a hearing disability and persons missing some or all of the toes of both feet without exception.

f - The driving licence shall be renewed for all its holders without exception, in accordance with the applicable medical conditions, once every five years.

g - A category shall be added to the categories mentioned in the circulation licence, specifying the condition of compliance with the fitted aids, namely glasses, prosthetic limb, hearing aid and others.

Insurance of Specially Equipped Cars:

Disability in itself may not constitute a reason for an insurance company to refuse to insure a car specially equipped for the use of disabled persons.

Training Disabled Persons in Driving:

a - Every institution concerned with the affairs of disabled persons shall be given the right to practise the training of disabled persons in driving, in accordance with special conditions issued by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers.

b - The institutions that practise the training operation shall be subject to the supervision of the Ministry of the Interior, and lessons shall be given free of charge, and the disabled person shall only be required to pay the fee for taking the driving examination.

Cost of rehabilitating private dwellings:

A - If the renovated dwelling in accordance with the provisions of Article /55/ of this specification requires additional rehabilitation according to the need of the disabled person who wishes to inhabit it, it shall be provided to him free of any cost in public complexes, and at his own expense in private complexes, in accordance with the standards issued in this regard pursuant to the provisions of Paragraph (B) of Article /34/ of this Law, provided that he submits the following documents: the personal disability card and a prior approval from the Ministry of Social Affairs.

B - A rate of at least two percent (2%) of the budget of the public bodies concerned with housing shall be allocated to disabled persons holding the personal disability card to rehabilitate the dwellings they inhabit or to purchase or rent new dwellings. If the budget decided for this purpose is not disbursed, the remaining value shall be carried over to the amount allocated in the following year, with due regard to the laws and regulations in force in the bylaws of each body.

Facilitation of loans:

A - The procedures and conditions of a loan granted to the holder of the personal disability card shall be facilitated, to the extent possible, in order to assist him in acquiring ownership of a dwelling.

B - These procedures shall be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Housing and Cooperatives after consulting the Ministry of Social Affairs.

Scope of rights:

Every disabled person has the right to education, meaning that the law guarantees equal opportunities for upbringing and education to all disabled persons, both children and adults, within all educational or instructional institutions of whatever kind, in their regular classes and in special classes where necessary.

Allocation of dwellings for disabled persons in public housing projects and private complexes:

A - Qualified dwellings shall be allocated in any popular housing project or residential complexes undertaken by the State or any public entity in accordance with the minimum standards for buildings and facilities in addition to the standards imposed on entrances, parking spaces and other public spaces, for the benefit of disabled persons with limited mobility (for example: those who use wheelchairs), at a rate of no less than five percent (5%) of the total dwellings, the fraction resulting from the mathematical calculation being rounded up to the higher number.

B - Private permanent or seasonal residential complexes must include qualified dwellings in accordance with the minimum standards for buildings and facilities in addition to the standards imposed on entrances, parking spaces and other public spaces, in a manner that they are suitable for the use of disabled persons with limited mobility (for example: those who use wheelchairs), at a rate of two percent (2%) of the total number of dwellings. The fraction resulting from the mathematical calculation shall be rounded up to the higher number.

C - This rate may be increased by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Social Affairs.

D - These dwellings shall be clearly identified on the maps by drawing the International Symbol of the Disabled.

Guarantees in sale and lease:

The State or any public entity concerned with the paragraph of Article /55/ of this Law is prohibited from selling or leasing those clearly identified dwellings to anyone other than holders of the personal disabled card, or one of their children, their parents, their spouse, or their legal guardian, under penalty of annulment of the sale or lease contract, and fining the seller and the buyer in amounts estimated by the competent courts.

Enrolment in Educational Institutions:

A - Disability in itself shall not constitute an impediment to applying for enrolment or admission to any educational or instructional institution, public or private, of any kind whatsoever. Any provision that requires for any application for enrolment or admission to any educational or instructional institution, public or private, of any kind whatsoever, soundness of constitution or body, or the absence of disability, infirmity, illness, or similar expressions and words, shall be deemed repealed.

B - Regular procedures, such as the applicable competency examinations and others adopted for accepting applications for admission or progression from one class to another, shall be deemed sufficient to accept or reject an application for enrolment or admission to any educational or instructional institution, public or private, of any kind whatsoever.

C - Every applicant for enrolment holding a personal disabled card shall be given an opportunity enabling him to pursue studies at the educational or instructional institution of his choice, by securing the optimal conditions that allow him to sit for entrance examinations and all other examinations during the academic year across all school, vocational, and university stages, in accordance with criteria determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers.

D - The committee responsible for granting exemptions regarding the legal age for admitting persons to all educational stages shall examine exemption applications submitted by the concerned parties (parents or administrations of educational institutions) accompanied by the personal disabled card, in accordance with broader criteria and facilities, particularly from a procedural standpoint.

E - All schools, institutes, universities, and educational and tented institutions shall circulate a request to provide the following documents, if available, in addition to the documents required for registration, with the aim of taking the necessary measures during the academic year and in organising official examinations:

1 - A copy of the personal disabled card to be attached to the official file.

2 - A copy of the request for special facilities in accordance with the application issued by the Ministry of Social Affairs in this regard, and the departments tasked with examining school and university scholarships across all fields shall give absolute priority to the applications of persons provided with a personal disabled card who have applied for a scholarship.

Coverage of educational expenses within specialised institutions:

The Ministries of Education, Youth and Sports, and Vocational and Technical Education shall cover the expenses of education and special upbringing or vocational rehabilitation for disabled persons within institutions and service centres specialised in upbringing and education or specialised vocational rehabilitation, for every person provided with the personal disabled card, and upon a special request from the Ministry of Social Affairs, through contracts which they execute with the institutions concerned. This shall include covering the expenses of applying auxiliary educational, athletic, and medico-social curricula. The period of special education within those institutions shall continue up to an age determined by the committee formed in Article /63/ of this Law, provided that it is not less than the age of twenty-one.

Official examinations:

A- The optimal conditions that allow every disabled pupil holding the personal card to participate in all educational classes and in examinations at all school, technical, and university stages shall be secured, in the following respects enumerated by way of example and not limitation:

1 - Rehabilitating entrances and halls

2- Specifying the time allocated for the examination if so required.

3- Securing questions by adapted means (embossed letters, large print, and others)

4- Assistance by third parties or special technology (Braille machines, typewriters, sign language interpreter and others)

B- The decisions issued annually by the Ministries of National Education, Youth and Sports, Vocational and Technical Education, and Culture and Higher Education relating to the timing and organisation of the annual official examinations shall include a special paragraph relating to the procedures to be followed in order to organise all these examinations according to the criteria specified above, and shall also include a paragraph specifying the special subjects that require organising special examinations for certain disabled persons in accordance with their personal files.

C- The personal disabled card shall be considered a sufficient document to exempt disabled persons from the sports examination in the official examinations and to replace it in accordance with the procedures in force in all cases of exemption, except in the event that the disabled person has registered his wish to participate

The Committee Specialised in Education:

a- There shall be formed by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers a joint committee among all private and public administrations, institutions and bodies concerned with upbringing and education affairs, called the "Committee Specialised in the Education of Disabled Persons and Persons with Special Needs", chaired by the Director General of the Ministry of Education and including one disabled member from among the members of the National Committee; this Committee shall lay down the internal regulations for its meetings.

b- This Committee shall undertake the following tasks:

1- Organising all matters relating to the education of disabled persons and persons with special needs, including special units, procedures, technologies and others, and determining the best conditions that allow every disabled pupil holding the Personal Card to participate in all classes and examinations at all school, vocational and university stages; these conditions shall be issued by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of National Education as soon as possible following the entry into force of this Law.

2- Providing consultations and technical, artistic and educational assistance to all educational institutions that wish to receive disabled persons or persons with special needs, and examining funding applications relating to specialised equipment and technologies.

3- Providing the necessary consultations and guidance to disabled persons or persons with special needs in all matters connected with education at all its stages.

4- Preparing for integrated projects to establish a talking national library and a national printing press in raised letters (Braille) and to unify sign language:

c- This Committee shall submit its decisions through the Minister of National Education to the Council of Ministers to take the appropriate decisions thereon.

d- There shall emanate from the Committee formed under this Article a sub-committee for specialised education comprising representatives of the said Committee in addition to four (4) representatives delegated by civil associations, institutions and centres concerned with specialised upbringing at the rate of one person for each of the four types of disability, and three (3) representatives delegated by parents' committees for infants, children and adolescents.

The tasks of this sub-committee shall be to provide the Committee Specialised in the Education of Disabled Persons with all information and expertise relating to the requirements of specialised education and upbringing within specialised centres and institutions.

Related text: Formation of a Committee Specialised in the Education of Disabled Persons

Awareness-raising:

The subject of the rights of the disabled person shall be included at the core of civic education programmes in all schools within the subject of human rights.

Training:

A - The Ministries of National Education, Youth and Sports, Vocational and Technical Education, and Culture and Higher Education shall work to open special branches at the Lebanese University and all public institutes in order to specialise educators in the rehabilitation of disabled persons in regular schools and in special units if necessary.

B - Qualification courses shall be held for coaches, sports physicians, therapists, and other specialists in sports for disabled persons.

Sports for disabled persons:

A - The Ministry of National Education, Youth and Sports shall support the establishment of sports teams specific to disabled persons and shall work to encourage them materially and morally to participate in all local, Arab, and international competitions.

B - The necessary measures shall be taken so that disabled persons enrolled in regular educational and instructional institutions may practise sports exercises suited to them during the periods allocated to sports in these institutions.

C - Sports for disabled persons in both of its specialised branches: sports for mentally disabled persons and sports for motor and sensory disabled persons, shall be incorporated into the core of the educational programmes followed in specialised institutions.

Supporting and organising sports for disabled persons:

A - A joint committee among all private and public administrations, institutions, and bodies concerned with the affairs of sports for disabled persons shall be formed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, called the "Specialised Committee for Sports for Disabled Persons" and chaired by the Director General of Youth and Sports. This Committee shall lay down the internal rules of procedure for its meetings.

B - This Committee shall undertake the following tasks:

1- Examining all standards for all sports games practised by disabled persons.

2 - Providing consultations and assistance in designing and rehabilitating playgrounds specific to sports for disabled persons.

3 - Organising competitions and sports federations specific to disabled persons.

Scope of rights to work and employment:

A - A disabled person, like all other members of society, has the right to work and to employment, which this Law guarantees and puts into effect.

B - The State undertakes to work to assist disabled persons to enter the labour market within the principle of equality and equal opportunities.

Conditions of employment:

A - Disability in itself shall not constitute an impediment to candidacy for any work or post.

B - Every text that stipulates for any work or post soundness of constitution or body, or the absence of affliction with a disability, infirmity, or ailment, or similar expressions and wordings that lead to preventing the acceptance of the disabled person's application, shall be deemed repealed.

C - Examinations relating to competence, and the applicable probationary period, shall be deemed sufficient to accept or reject employment, provided that the special needs of disabled persons are observed in order to enable them to sit the examinations whenever they are applicable.

Guidance to the labour market:

The National Employment Office shall undertake, in cooperation and coordination with the Ministry of Vocational and Technical Education in particular, to rehabilitate disabled persons who have attained eighteen years of age, and to guide them to the regular labour market, or to sheltered workshops, or to work assistance centres, or to operational medico-social institutions, and to follow up on their work, and it shall also undertake the process of permanent follow-up on their work, with the aim of guiding them, if possible, to the regular labour market.

Unemployment benefit:

A - Every person holding a personal disability card who has attained eighteen full years of age shall be deemed unemployed if he meets the conditions, criteria, and procedures issued by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour after consulting the Ministry of Social Affairs. He shall then be entitled to benefit from an unemployment benefit in the amount of seventy-five per cent of the minimum wage, paid by the Ministry of Labour. The obligation to pay the family allowance prescribed in the Social Security Law or by any other official guaranteeing entity shall then cease if its conditions are met.

B - The unemployment benefit shall cease immediately when work becomes available to the disabled person that secures for him a specific monthly income.

C - This Article shall take effect upon the lapse of one year from the date of publication of this Law in the Official Gazette.

Committee for Activating the Rights of Disabled Persons to Work:

A - There shall be formed by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers a joint committee among all administrations, institutions bodies concerned with work and recruitment called the "Committee for Activating the Rights of Disabled Persons to Work", which shall be chaired by the Director General of the Ministry of Labour and shall include a disabled member from among the members of the National Committee. This Committee shall establish the internal rules of procedure for its meetings.

B - This Committee shall undertake the submission of all proposals capable of activating the right to work provided for in this Law, the coordination among all those concerned from public and private administrations and bodies, and the provision of advice to them when needed. It shall also work to establish mechanisms that encourage every disabled person who wishes to establish a liberal profession.

C - This Committee shall submit its decisions through the Minister of Labour to the Council of Ministers, to take the appropriate decisions regarding them.

Allocation of Posts in the Public Sector:

Posts in the public sector shall be allocated to disabled persons at a rate of at least three percent (3%) of the total number of all categories and posts.

Related text: Application of the provisions of Article 73 of Law No. 220 dated 29/5/2000 (Rights of Persons with Additional Needs)

Allocation of Posts in the Private Sector:

A - Employers in the private sector in which the number of employees is not less than thirty (30) and does not exceed sixty (60) shall be obliged to employ one disabled employee who possesses the required qualifications.

B - Where the number of employees in the establishment exceeds sixty employees, the employer or the establishment shall be obliged to employ disabled persons at a rate of at least three percent (3%) of its employees, who possess the required qualifications, and where there is a fraction resulting from calculating the rate, the fraction shall be rounded up.

C - Every employer or establishment that does not fulfil the obligation incumbent upon it within a period of one year from the adoption of this Law shall be obliged to pay an annual amount equal to twice the minimum wage for each unengaged disabled person, to be paid to the Ministry of Labour, until the employer or the establishment regularises their status.

D - The employer shall be exempted from paying the fine if he submits to the Ministry of Social Affairs proof that he submitted a special application to the National Employment Office to recruit a disabled person and the competent administration in the Ministry did not have any person possessing the required specifications after the lapse of three months from the submission of the application.

E The National Social Security Fund must verify the proper application of the obligation of employers to recruit disabled persons, and it must not issue a clearance certificate to a violating employer.

Benefits in the Event of Additional Employment:

Every employer in the private sector who employs disabled persons in a number greater than that which he is obliged to employ shall benefit from a deduction on income tax in the amount of the minimum wage for each disabled person whom he is not obliged to employ, in accordance with a certificate from the Ministry of Social Affairs.

Various Legislative Amendments:

The following paragraph shall be added to Article /15/ of Legislative Decree No. 47 issued on 29 June 1983 (Retirement and Dismissal from Service System): "No employee may be dismissed from service on account of sustaining a disability unless such disability prevents him from performing the function he holds and any other function within the administration".

Work Emergencies:

a - The text of Article 12 of Legislative Decree No. 136 issued on 16 September 1983 (Work Emergencies) is repealed and replaced with the following text: "Every employer shall be obliged to mandatorily conclude insurance contracts with an insurance company to guarantee the compensations and medical treatment provided for in this Legislative Decree".

b - If the employer fails to comply with the obligation specified in the first paragraph of this Article, he shall be obliged to pay a fine equal to twice the average value of the insurance premium.

c - The following paragraph shall be added to Article /32/ (Chapter Six) of Legislative Decree No. 136/83 dated 16 September 1983:

"Every employer who violates the content of this Article of this Legislative Decree shall be sentenced by the Labour Arbitration Council to a fine pursuant to a lawsuit brought by any employee or any syndicate in the company or establishment or any other competent party. The value of this fine shall be fixed at an amount ranging between six (6) and ten (10) times the official minimum wage".

d - The following phrase is repealed from the final passage following Schedule No. (1) of Legislative Decree No. 136/83: "provided that he declared upon entering employment that he is left-handed".

e - An employee who sustains during service a disability that prevents him from performing a function shall have the right to request his dismissal from service.

f - Article 20 of Legislative Decree No. 47 issued on 29 June 1983 (Retirement and Dismissal from Service System) is repealed so that invalidity and retirement pensions may be combined. On the Right of the Disabled Person to Social Benefits
The condition of poverty is repealed wherever it appears in Article 26 of Legislative Decree No. 47/83 issued on 29 June 1983 (Retirement and Dismissal from Service System).

Where the disability of the employee does not result from a work accident or an occupational disease, the medical care provided to him by the Sickness and Maternity Branch shall include prostheses, eyeglasses, medical instruments, and all the rehabilitation and support services provided for in this Law. Disabled persons shall be exempted from the provisions of Article 19 of the Social Security Law.

A - Paragraph (D) of Article 14 of the Social Security Law is repealed and replaced by the following text:

"The legitimate and adopted children of the insured person until they reach the completed age of eighteen years, and if the children are unable to secure their livelihood because they devote their full time to their studies, they shall benefit from the security until the completed age of twenty-five years."

B - However, if the disabled children holding a Personal Disability Card are unable to secure their livelihood due to a disability that prevents them from working, they shall benefit from the security benefits without an age limit.

C - This security shall cease in the event that the disabled person benefits from the unemployment compensation mentioned in this Law.

The following Paragraph "E" is added to the text of Article 14 of the Social Security Law:

"E: The legitimate and adopted children of the insured woman if she bears the burden of supporting them due to the incapacity of the husband, and within the conditions provided for in Paragraph (D) of Article 14 of the Social Security Law.

Article Nine of Legislative Decree 136/83 issued on 16 September 1983 (Work Accidents) is repealed and replaced by the following text:

"New Article 9: If it is established that the employee intentionally caused the accident that rendered him disabled and a holder of a Personal Disabled Card, he shall not be entitled to any compensations mentioned in this Law and the employer shall have the right to dismiss him from service in accordance with the provisions in force, provided that he shall benefit from all sickness assistance, aids, and services provided for in this Legislative Decree."

A - Equipment, educational and medical materials, assistive devices, machines, and tools specific to disabled persons, as well as their parts, shall be exempted from customs duties, all import duties, and any other duties or taxes, provided that the importing party is either the disabled person for his personal use, or an association of disabled persons or a service association, pursuant to a certificate issued by the Ministry of Social Affairs.

B - These devices shall be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Public Health, Social Affairs, and Industry.

National manufacturing of all equipment specific to disabled persons shall be encouraged and measures capable of protecting it shall be taken pursuant to a decree issued by the Council of Ministers, upon the proposal of the Ministers of Industry and Finance after consulting the Ministry of Social Affairs.

Individual and collective means of transport specific to disabled persons shall also be exempted from the fees and taxes referred to above, provided that the importing party is either the disabled person for his personal use, or an association of disabled persons or a service association, provided that five years elapse before purchasing another car, and that is pursuant to a certificate issued by the Ministry of Social Affairs, provided that the fees shall be levied subsequently in the event of transfer of ownership to any non-disabled person, and this clause shall be mentioned on the official papers.

One means of transport for each disabled person holding the personal disabled card shall be exempted from the registration tax in the vehicle registration departments, whether registered in his name or in the name of his father, his mother, one of his children, his spouse, or his wife, jointly or severally.

This application for exemption shall be submitted pursuant to a certificate issued by the Ministry of Social Affairs in accordance with the procedures followed.

One dwelling that serves as a place of residence for a disabled person holding the personal disabled card shall be exempted from the fees on rental value, from guard, sidewalk and sewerage fees, and from the built property tax, whoever the holder of the right of lease or ownership may be among his relatives (for example: ascendants, descendants, spouses, or brothers and sisters).

The decision of exemption shall be taken pursuant to a certificate issued by the Ministry of Social Affairs in accordance with the procedures followed.

The additional exemption provided for in Item (5) of Article 9 of Legislative Decree No. 146 dated 12/06/1959 (Transfer Duty) and its amendments shall include all disabled heirs holding the personal disabled card and mentioned in this Item.

Paragraph (3) of Article 56 of Legislative Decree No. 144/59 dated 12/06/1959 (Income Tax Law) and its amendments shall be amended so as to read as follows:

1- For each person among the taxpayers if he is a holder of the personal disabled card and throughout the period of its validity.

Exemption from Judicial Fees:

Exempted from the judicial fees payable upon filing any lawsuit or complaint or intervening therein before courts of all kinds and degrees, are those brought by disabled persons, their legal representatives, or the National Committee for the Affairs of the Disabled due to a violation of any of the provisions of this Law, or on the basis thereof, or for failure to apply any other legal text that establishes a special right for the disabled. This Article shall apply to all degrees of trial and of all kinds: civil, penal, administrative, military, confessional, personal status, and otherwise.

Special Procedures for Electoral Operations:

The needs of disabled persons shall be taken into consideration when organising all electoral operations, whether parliamentary, municipal, or otherwise, and such measures shall be issued by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministry of the Interior and after consulting the Ministry of Social Affairs.

Lottery Draws:

Lottery draws shall be organised for the benefit of associations of the disabled or service associations after being licensed by the Ministry of Finance, the Directorate General of the National Lottery, after consulting the Ministry of Social Affairs.

Details of Application:

The details of application of this Law shall be determined, where necessary, by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers.

Repeal of Contrary Texts:

All laws and texts that contravene this Law or that are inconsistent with its provisions shall be repealed or amended.

Entry into Force:

This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Article 72 of the Social Security Law put into force by Decree No. 13955 dated 26/09/1963 is amended by adding the following paragraph:

"The amount of the contribution payable by associations of disabled persons and service institutions shall be fixed at a rate of fifteen per cent (15%) of the contribution in force for institutions not subject to the reduced or lump-sum contribution and pertaining to the various branches, with the exception of the end-of-service branch. This application for exemption is submitted pursuant to a certificate issued by the Ministry of Social Affairs in accordance with the applicable procedures.

As for the end-of-service branch, the Board of Directors of the National Social Security Fund shall determine the amount of the contribution payable by this category of institutions or associations.

Associations of disabled persons and service associations shall be exempted from fees on rental value or from the built property tax, and this application for exemption shall be submitted pursuant to a certificate issued by the Ministry of Social Affairs in accordance with the applicable procedures.

The tax payable on a building permit for associations of disabled persons and for service associations that construct buildings, centres or other facilities dedicated to working with disabled persons shall be paid in monthly instalments over a period of five years, without interest and without a down payment, pursuant to a certificate issued by the Ministry of Social Affairs.

One means of transport owned by an association of disabled persons or a service association shall be exempted from the registration fee at the motor vehicle registration departments and from customs duties. This application for exemption shall be submitted pursuant to a certificate issued by the Ministry of Social Affairs in accordance with the applicable procedures.

Associations of disabled persons and service associations shall pay twenty-five per cent of the value of the bills payable by them for water, electricity and telephone, in accordance with an application for exemption pursuant to a certificate issued by the Ministry of Social Affairs in accordance with the applicable procedures.

Additional fines :

There shall be added to every judgment for compensation or fine rendered against any person or institution that caused the disability of others a fine the rate of which shall be determined by analogy with the criteria for determining compensation, and which shall be paid to the Ministry of Social Affairs.

Exemption from postage stamp duty :

All letters and printed matter written in the "Braille" language shall be exempted from postage stamp duty.
