War materiel, arms, ammunition and explosives provided for by this Law shall be divided into three categories: First Category: War materiel, arms and ammunition, and those intended for use exclusively in land, sea or air warfare. Those included or to be included in the armament of the armed forces in every State, or the use of which has been discontinued, yet remain capable of military use and are not used for any other purpose. Second Category: Non-war arms and ammunition Third Category: Explosives, gunpowder and their accessories.

These three types shall be arranged into nine categories: The First Type: War weapons, ammunition and equipment Category One - Weapons and ammunition intended for use in land, sea or air warfare, namely: a - Rifles of all sizes and calibres manufactured and intended for war use, and their barrels, breeches, frames, mechanisms and finished separate parts. b - Machine guns, automatic rifles, submachine guns and aircraft machine guns of all calibres and sizes, and the barrel of these weapons, their breeches and all their other finished separate parts. c - Long and short cannons, heavy cannons and aircraft cannons of whatever calibre, and the mounts of these weapons, their muzzles, barrels, breeches, breechblocks, all mechanisms specific to them, the fittings intended for assembling them, and all other finished separate parts used to repair these weapons or as spare parts for them. d - Ammunition, projectiles and loaded and unloaded cartridges specific to the weapons mentioned in paragraphs a, b, c, and loaded and unloaded manufactures and devices intended for firing, launching or detonating such ammunition, projectiles and cartridges. e - Bombs of all kinds, water projectiles (torpedoes), stationary or mobile, loaded or unloaded land or sea mines, atomic, rocket and similar bombs. And loaded or unloaded manufactures and devices used to launch these bombs and mines or intended to detonate them. f - Devices designated for bombarding aircraft and vessels, including sighting instruments, aiming instruments, screws, range-finding instruments Telemetre, beams particularly intended for war weapons projecteurs, and aircraft and submarine detection devices such as radar and others. ' Category Two: Units equipped with firearms or intended for the use of weapons in war, namely: a - Combat vehicles, tanks, armoured cars and flamethrowers. b - Armoured vessels, torpedo boats, naval warships and vessels of various kinds, including aircraft carriers and submarines. c - Periscopes designated for submarines. d - Combat aircraft, aerial interceptors, airships and light or heavy aircraft of all kinds. Appended thereto are the engines, propellers and wings intended for these aircraft, the mounts of their cannons and machine guns, and all their other separate parts. e - Turrets, mounts and armoured or unarmoured finished separate parts used to assemble or repair the equipment mentioned in sub-paragraphs a - b - d of Category Two or as spare parts for them. Category Three - Devices intended for protection against combat raids, protective masks and clothing, effects pertaining to these devices, and their finished separate parts. Category Four - Weapons and ammunition not considered war weapons but appended to war weapons and ammunition, namely: a - Revolvers or automatic pistols and their finely-crafted models fired from the shoulder or with one hand, of all sizes and of a calibre of 6 millimetres and above. b - Loaded or unloaded ammunition intended for these pistols, and the magazines, barrels and frames specific to these weapons and all their other finished separate parts intended for assembling or repairing these pistols or as spare parts for them. c - Weapons in which the ammunition of war weapons set forth in the preceding categories can be used, and rifled firearms fired from the shoulder whose calibre is equal to 6 millimetres and above, excluding hunting weapons in which the ammunition referred to in the following sub-paragraph (d) is used: d - All ammunition used in war weapons, including hunting cartridges loaded with a single bullet of calibre 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 20, 24, 28 and 32. e - Bayonets, swords and lances. Excluded therefrom are those referred to in Category Seven.

The Second Type - Non-war weapons and ammunition Category Five: a - Revolvers and automatic pistols of a calibre below 6 millimetres, their loaded or unloaded ammunition, and their separate parts and finished mechanisms pertaining to them. b - Other rifled firearms fired from the shoulder of a calibre below 6 millimetres and their ammunition. c Hunting firearms and ammunition of all calibres not mentioned in the preceding categories, and not falling within the weapons or ammunition referred to in sub-paragraphs c and d of Category Four. And smooth-bore rifles. Category Six - Training weapons. Namely smooth-bore firearms whose calibre is equal to nine millimetres or less, and target-shooting weapons fired by compression (- without gunpowder). Category Seven - Antique and commemorative weapons, provided that they are not intended for use and do not fall within the weapons set out in sub-paragraph (c) of Category Four. Category Eight - Prohibited weapons, namely weapons that do not fall within the categories provided for above, and in particular: daggers, knives, brass knuckles, sword-canes, canes weighted with lead or tipped at both ends with iron, and in general all concealed weapons. The Third Type Explosives, gunpowder and their accessories Category Nine - Classes of explosives, gunpowder and their accessories, namely: a - Gunpowder of various kinds b - Explosives - all kinds of dynamite (gelignite or gelatine), nitrate-compound explosives, gum dynamite and others. c - Accessories necessary for explosives - electric blasting caps, fuses (wicks), detonating cord, slow-burning cord, cord intended for underwater use, and all devices particularly used to detonate the materials mentioned in this category.

No person or group may carry out in Lebanese territory industrial or commercial works of any kind whatsoever relating to equipment, arms, and ammunition of any category whatsoever prior to obtaining a legal licence from the Ministry of the Interior after the approval of the Council of Ministers.

To obtain this licence, the concerned party must submit an application to the Ministry of the Interior stating therein: - The first name, surname, date and place of birth, and identity card number - Nationality - Place of residence - Profession (manufacturer or dealer of arms) - Registration number in the Chamber of Commerce - Address of the premises or factory - Method of exploitation - by an individual or a company. In the latter case, the type of company, the trade name, and the names of the partners, directors, foremen, and active agents. If it is a joint-stock company, the names and addresses of the chairman and members of the board of directors shall be stated. The application shall be accompanied by a copy of the judicial record for each of the persons mentioned in the preceding paragraph and by a certificate of good conduct issued by the Gendarmerie commander or the Police commissioner in the district in which the concerned party has resided for six months.

The procedures for granting these licences, their models, and the procedures for export and import shall be determined pursuant to a decree taken upon the proposal of the Ministers of the Interior, Defence, and National Economy.

The licence to carry out industrial or commercial works relating to equipment, arms, and ammunition of the first five categories and to explosives shall not be granted except after verification through the Ministry of Defence that these premises fulfil all technical conditions for preserving the safety of persons and neighbouring buildings.

The licence shall only be granted to Lebanese nationals who have attained the age of twenty-one years and after ascertaining that they are free from mental illnesses and that no judgment has been issued prohibiting them from carrying arms or a judgment for offences affecting State security.

The Ministries of the Interior and National Defence must be notified of every amendment or alteration occurring during the term of the licence to the articles of association of joint-stock or shareholding companies or to their boards of directors, as well as upon the closure or transfer of the premises and upon every change in the manufacture of or trade in the equipment mentioned in the licence.

The licence shall be granted for a maximum period of five years and may be renewed for the same period, upon the request of the concerned parties. Every licence whose holder has not commenced operations thereunder within one year shall become revoked ipso jure.

The licence shall be withdrawn forthwith: 1- from a person who loses one of the conditions provided for in Article 7 2- from premises which lose one of the conditions provided for in Article 6 3- from premises and persons proven to have lost one of the conditions provided for in Articles 13, 14, 15 and 16 4- from premises or persons proven to have contravened the provisions of the decrees issued in implementation of the provisions of this Law.

The Ministry of the Interior or of Defence, after the approval of the Council of Ministers, may decide to withdraw the permit at any time whatsoever due to exceptional circumstances or the requirements of public safety. In such case, the raw materials, manufactured items and machinery which are not suitable for the manufacture of arms and ammunition shall be confiscated for the benefit of the Army against fair compensation determined by a committee of technicians at the Ministry of Defence composed of four members joined by an expert elected by the party concerned. The decisions of this committee shall be subject to the avenues of recourse before the court having jurisdiction over administrative matters.
Foreigners may exceptionally be granted licences to carry on purely commercial activities relating to equipment and arms of the fifth, sixth and seventh categories.

The manufacture of equipment, arms, ammunition and explosives of all categories shall be subject to the technical supervision of the Ministry of Defence. Administrative supervision, however, falls within the competence of the Ministry of the Interior.

The supervision provided for in the preceding Article shall cover technical operations, including the fitting, assembly and repair of parts pertaining to equipment, arms and ammunition, and verification of the degree of workmanship in manufacture, and shall also cover the operations of loading ammunition of all kinds.

This supervision shall be carried out in warehouses, factories and premises and upon every piece of equipment, arms, ammunition and their separate parts the manufacture of which has been completed, and shall also cover operations relating to the disposal or storage thereof. To this end, business owners holding licences must keep, in addition to the regular commercial registers, statutory registers in which they record the incoming and outgoing of such arms, the date, the name of the purchaser and the number of his licence.

The owners of industrial establishments designated for war equipment, weapons, and ammunition must notify the Ministries of Interior and National Defence of the quantities the manufacture of which has been completed, within eight days from the date of completion of the work, and they must register in a special register all equipment, weapons, ammunition, and their component parts that have been manufactured. This register shall be subject to the supervision of the Ministries of Interior and Defence. Within the same time limit, they must also notify the two aforementioned Ministries of every invention or patent of voting they have obtained for a new type, and of every improvement occurring to one of the types of their work. And every substantial modification in one of the models. Everyone who, by virtue of his office or mission, becomes acquainted with these inventions must keep their secrets confidential under penalty of criminal prosecution pursuant to Article 579 of the Penal Code, without prejudice to the right to prosecute him in accordance with the other criminal provisions in force.

The import and export of the war equipment, weapons, ammunition, their separate parts, and the explosive materials mentioned in this Law shall be subject to a licence from the Ministry of National Economy following the approval of the Council of Ministers, and the materiel exported or imported by the Ministry of Defence shall not be subject to this licence.

In time of war or when its outbreak is anticipated, the Government may suspend for a specified period or categorically prohibit the granting of certificates for inventions relating to national defence. Which are used for the needs of the Army and defence and the creation, use, or exploitation of which may constitute a danger to the safety of the State.

Everyone who applies, in time of war or when its outbreak is anticipated, for the registration of an invention of the kind mentioned in the preceding Article must submit his application in two copies, one of which shall be referred together with the drawings, plans, and specifications of the invention to the Ministry of National Defence, and this Ministry must decide within one month from the date of its receipt of these documents whether the invention falls under the provisions of the preceding Article and determine the period of suspension of the granting of the certificate.

It is prohibited for the inventor and any other person who has become acquainted with the invention in any manner whatsoever to disclose any information relating to the invention, and anyone who discloses, communicates, or publishes by one of the means mentioned in Article 209 of the Penal Code any information - relating to the invention, prior to obtaining permission therefor, shall be prosecuted before the Military Courts - in accordance with Article 281 of the General Penal Code.

The prohibition of disclosing or exploiting the invention, whether temporarily or permanently, confers a right to compensation upon the inventor and any other person having an interest. The value of such compensation shall be determined by the committee provided for in Article 11 of this Law.

The Government shall have the right to exploit the invention for its own account, and in such case the inventor or the holder of the right to the invention shall be granted, in addition to the compensation referred to in the preceding Article, shares in the factory established for the exploitation of the invention. The shares and the value of the compensation for the interested party shall be determined under the same conditions and circumstances referred to in the preceding Article.

All the provisions of this Chapter shall apply to Lebanese commercial and industrial companies, to their branches, and to companies placed under the control of Lebanese nationals, wherever located inside or outside Lebanese territory.

No person shall be permitted to carry or possess the arms and ammunition provided for in the fourth and fifth categories in Lebanese territory unless he holds a licence from the Ministry of the Interior, and the Governor (Muhafiz) or the District Commissioner (Qaimaqam) shall have the right to issue licences relating to hunting arms. The licence to possess and carry an arm of the fifth category, paragraph (c), and of the seventh category and the ammunition pertaining thereto, is personal and shall be issued once and shall not cease to have effect except upon death or upon the loss by its holder of the conditions of eligibility provided for in this Law. As for the licence to possess and carry an arm and ammunition of the fourth and seventh categories and the remaining paragraphs of the fifth category, it shall be issued for one year, and it may be renewed.

No one shall be licensed to acquire, possess or carry the equipment, arms and ammunition falling within the first and second categories except in the event of a disturbance of public security or in the cases provided for in Chapter Two relating to the manufacture of and trade in such equipment, and subject to the conditions specified therein. The licence shall be issued pursuant to a decision of the Council of Ministers. Provided that members of the Lebanese land, sea and air armed forces, the gendarmerie and the police shall have the right to carry equipment, arms and ammunition of all categories, within the limits of their functions in accordance with military regulations and laws.

Members of the public forces, forest rangers, watchmen, guards, and all other public servants assimilated to military personnel shall be licensed to acquire and carry arms and ammunition falling under Category 1, Sub-paragraph (a), and Category 4, within the limits of their functions and pursuant to a written authorisation on special cards issued by the Ministry of the Interior. The number and type of the arm authorised to be carried shall be mentioned therein. Employees of the Military Court and all other civilians working for the Ministry of National Defence shall be licensed to acquire such arms pursuant to a special authorisation from the Commander of the Army. Reserve and retired officers shall be entitled to retain the arms and ammunition of Category 4 that had been delivered to them personally during the performance of their duties and to carry them, within the conditions prescribed for the personal arming of officers.

None of the holders of permits to transport or possess arms and ammunition shall be entitled to sell or dispose of them, whether for consideration or without consideration, if the buyer holds a permit authorising him to do so. Arms of Category 6 may be possessed and transported, and identity papers shall stand in place of a permit in respect thereof. As for arms of Category 7 and Category 8, their possession shall be permitted, provided that carrying them is prohibited. It shall be prohibited to grant a licence to carry them under any circumstances whatsoever.

No licence shall be granted to acquire or carry more than two arms of Categories 4 and 5. Hunting arms and their ammunition, however, shall not be subject to this limitation. No hunting licence shall be granted except to a person holding a licence to carry arms.

No permit to carry or possess an arm and ammunition of any category shall be granted except to persons who have attained at least eighteen years of age; as for hunting arms, a licence therefor may be granted to a person who has completed his sixteenth year of age under the responsibility of his guardian, provided that the applicant: 1- Has not been afflicted with a mental illness. 2- Has not been sentenced to deprivation of civil rights, or for a felony, or for a disgraceful offence. 3- Has not been sentenced to prohibition from carrying arms or for offences against State security. 4- If he is a foreigner, has not been the subject of a decision prohibiting residence or ordering expulsion from the country. 5- Has not been repeatedly convicted of an infringement of the provisions of this Law.
The holder of the licence must produce it upon every request from officers of the public authority.
Every person licensed to carry arms who ceases to fulfil any of the conditions required under the provisions of this Law shall have his permit withdrawn.

Save for weapons intended for hunting, the Ministry of the Interior shall have the right to withdraw the licence at any time on the basis of the report of the competent departments or for the exigencies of public security. In the event of the withdrawal or cancellation of the permit, the weapon shall be confiscated and the annual fee shall not be refunded.

The Minister of Defence may, after the approval of the Council of Ministers, license the transit of equipment, weapons or ammunition of the first five categories across Lebanese territory. The licence shall only be granted to designated persons belonging to a regular armed force affiliated to one of the recognised states, provided that they hold an official order from the competent authorities in the state to which they belong.

The departments of General Security at the border posts shall grant a temporary licence to carry weapons to persons arriving in Lebanon on an official mission and holding a lawful licence from their government, provided that the weapons are intended for their personal use and are accurately described in the licence. As for those arriving in Lebanon for hunting, they must, in addition to the licence that they hold from their government, obtain a hunting licence and a hunting weapon licence from the competent Lebanese authorities after payment of the annual fee determined by the Budget Law, for the value of which a stamp shall be affixed to the licence itself.
In the case specified in the first paragraph of the preceding Article, the quantity of ammunition may not exceed 25 for each piece of weaponry.

Holders of the permits provided for in Article 33 and the first paragraph of Article 34 must produce them upon every request by officers of the public authorities. If they leave Lebanese territory, they must surrender them to the nearest post of the public forces or of the customs at the border. It shall return them to the department by which the licence was issued.

A merchant or factory owner is prohibited from selling or giving to anyone equipment, weapons or ammunition of the first four categories and of the fifth category, sub-item (a), before verifying that the person concerned holds a lawful permit authorising him to do so. For this purpose, the applicant shall be granted a temporary permit stating that he is authorised to obtain materiel or weapons and ammunition and the number of each of them, and he shall produce it to the owner of the factory or shop, who shall record in the blank field left therein for this purpose the type of weapon intended for sale, its number and its model, together with the types of ammunition pertaining to it. He shall then sign it and stamp it with the stamp of the commercial establishment. The weapon and ammunition shall not be delivered to the person concerned before obtaining the final permit.
For every permit, the fee determined by law shall be levied.

The State reserves the right to import or possess, transport and sell kinds of gunpowder and explosives of whatever kind they may be, and all substances similar thereto, for the account and benefit of the State "Ministry of the Interior - Gunpowder Department". Facilities prepared for the manufacture, preparation and sale of gunpowder and explosives, as well as warehouses prepared for these substances and the like, shall be subject to the supervision of technicians at the Ministry of National Defence.

Whoever brings in or attempts to bring in any gunpowder or any explosives or other substances similar thereto into Lebanon shall be prosecuted, in addition to criminal penalties, in accordance with the laws relating to customs smuggling.
Agencies for the sale of hunting gunpowder may be established which supply retailers with the quantities prepared for local consumption.
Retailers shall obtain their supplies of hunting gunpowder from the agents of the region to which they belong and from the warehouses.
Sellers are prohibited from selling hunting gunpowder except to a person holding a permit to carry a hunting weapon.
The rules of delivery and sale relating to hunting gunpowder shall be determined by decree.

The sale of explosives and blasting gunpowder without a licence is prohibited. The Ministry of Public Works shall specify the quantity to be delivered to each buyer, public works contractor or quarry operator.
Public warehouses for blasting gunpowder and explosives shall be established and maintained by the Ministry of the Interior - Gunpowder Department.

Every person who possesses a weapon or ammunition that is lost from him shall give notice thereof to the nearest station of the Gendarmerie, the Police, or General Security, stating therein the circumstances of the loss. He shall surrender the permit that he held to the same authorities, which shall give him a receipt of delivery thereof, and if he assigns it to any person, he must give all information relating to the sale of the weapon and ammunition, stating the name of the assignee, his address, and the number of his licence.

Anyone who finds a weapon or ammunition shall immediately surrender it to the station of the public forces nearest to the place where it was found, failing which he shall be punished for the offence of carrying a weapon.

Anyone to whom weapons or ammunition are transferred by inheritance from a decedent who held them lawfully must notify the competent authorities thereof within three months, and state the number of the decedent's permit; if he wishes to retain it, he must submit an application to obtain a lawful licence to hold and carry it. However, if he does not wish to retain the weapon or ammunition, he may assign them to a third party licensed to possess them. If the aforementioned period of three months expires and none of the formalities provided for in the preceding paragraph has been carried out, the weapon shall be confiscated from the heir, and if he refuses to surrender it, he shall be prosecuted criminally.

If the decedent possessed the weapon without a licence, the heir must notify the competent authorities within one month from the date of his acquisition of the weapon. If he wishes to retain it, he must submit a lawful application to obtain the permit immediately upon the expiry of the month, failing which the weapon shall be confiscated from him. If the heir refuses to surrender it, he shall be prosecuted criminally. In the two cases mentioned above, the blank field in the temporary permit shall be filled in by the head of the station nearest to the heir's place of residence.

Persons who possess weapons and ammunition without a licence shall obtain one within three months from the date of publication of this Law, or surrender them to the Gendarmerie stations within the jurisdiction of which they reside within the same period, in which case they shall be exempted from penalty. As for persons who possess weapons or ammunition under lawful permits, they shall replace them with new licences within six months from the date of publication of this Law.
Types of blasting powder and explosives the sale of which is licensed shall be delivered pursuant to a release permit issued by the Ministry of the Interior to the purchaser.
Temporary private depots for blasting powder and explosives may be established by a decision of the Minister of the Interior.

The master of a vessel, whatever the country from which it arrives, shall submit to the Customs, prior to entering the port, a special declaration of the gunpowder and explosives carried on his vessel, and of the duration of the vessel's stay in the port, and this declaration must be produced upon the departure of the vessel.

It is prohibited for any vehicle to transport a quantity of gunpowder exceeding two kilogrammes, unless it is sealed with the lead seal of the Gunpowder Service and pursuant to a transit pass endorsed by the Gunpowder Service. Gunpowder transported in violation of the provisions of this Article shall be seized and confiscated.
If a gunpowder retail establishment is liquidated, amicably or following bankruptcy, the sale may only be made to persons who personally hold a legal licence.

Every person who consumes explosive materials and their accessories shall keep a legal consumption register in which are recorded the quantities of explosives delivered to him by the Gunpowder Department, the quantities consumed thereof, and the works in which these quantities were used. The entries of this register must be drawn up day by day under the responsibility of the contractor or the engineer entrusted with carrying out and supervising the works.
The consumption register must be presented to the Gunpowder Department upon every request by the said Department.

An officer of the Gunpowder Department may verify the manner in which the explosives are used by conducting an inspection at the work sites in the presence of the engineer and the representative of the Ministry of Public Works.
Consumers of explosives shall not be granted a licence to purchase them except after submitting their logbook endorsed by the engineer in charge of the works or by his representative.
Quantities of gunpowder and explosives that have not been used by the conclusion of the works must be returned to the Gunpowder Department within a period of fifteen days at most.
Trade in ribbed percussion caps for rifles and percussion caps of all kinds for hunting cartridges shall be restricted to gunpowder vendors and licensed persons.

The manufacture, importation and sale of fireworks and every similar substance shall be subject to technical supervision in the Ministry of the Interior - Gunpowder Service - and this supervision shall cover in particular: 1- The safety conditions that must be met in factories in which gunpowder, firework compounds or similar substances are used, and in warehouses and stores for the sale of fireworks. 2- The method of operating the factories and the materials used.
The manufacture, importation and sale of fireworks known as firecrackers are prohibited.
It is prohibited to establish any factory, warehouse or store for the sale of fireworks except after obtaining a licence granted by the Ministry of the Interior - Gunpowder Service.
No premises for the manufacture of fireworks shall be permitted to exist within inhabited places.

Factories and warehouses currently located within these places must be relocated within a period not exceeding three months, and such premises shall likewise not be permitted to exist except at a distance of at least 100 metres from any warehouse or shop containing inflammable substances such as petroleum, gasoline and the like. They must be built of non-inflammable materials. There shall not be in the same building any warehouse for rags, paper, wood, cigarettes and the like. No warehouse or factory for alcoholic substances may adjoin these factories.

Importers of and dealers in fireworks are prohibited from depositing, in the stores designated for sale, a quantity of miscellaneous fireworks exceeding in any case whatsoever 100 one hundred kilograms, provided that there is no flammable material in the premises.
The licences provided for in the preceding Article shall not be granted unless the conditions mentioned above have been fulfilled.

No transaction for fireworks of any kind may be concluded, nor may they be imported, except after obtaining an import permit granted by the Ministry of the Interior - Gunpowder Department. Such goods cannot be withdrawn from the customs warehouses except - after submitting the import permit granted to the importers.

Technical supervision over factories and warehouses shall be carried out by inspecting them periodically or non-periodically, conducted by an official of the Gunpowder Department or by a person delegated by this Department. Assistance may be sought from technicians at the Ministry of National Defence.

Any person who, without a licence, manufactures war materiel, weapons or ammunition of the first four categories or their separate parts, or carries, possesses, steals or disposes of them for consideration or without consideration, shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years and by a fine from one thousand to two thousand pounds, or by either of these two penalties.

If the act relates to non-war materiel specified in the fifth category, the offender shall be punished by detention for a period not exceeding six months and by a fine not exceeding one hundred pounds, or by either of these two penalties. With the exception of the case of possession, the same penalty shall apply if the act relates to weapons of the seventh and eighth categories.

In all cases, the materiel, weapons and ammunition referred to in the preceding Articles shall be confiscated, and the machinery, tools and means of transport used for manufacture and trade shall be confiscated.

Whoever holds a licence for a weapon of any category whatsoever and, without cause, discharges a firearm in populated places shall be punished by detention for up to one month. Anyone who commits this offence with weapons of the sixth category shall be subject to the same penalty. If the offence is committed during a gathering or crowd, the penalty shall be detention for up to six months. The weapon shall be confiscated in both cases and the licence shall be revoked.

Whoever buys, sells, transports, acquires or manufactures any gunpowder, explosives or their accessories without a licence shall be punished by imprisonment for up to six months and by a fine of up to five hundred pounds, or by either of these two penalties. The materials, tools, goods and means of transport prepared for manufacture and trade shall be confiscated.

Whoever violates the provisions of Article 45, 50, 54, 55 and 62 and the fifth and seventh sections of the Fifth Chapter shall be punished by imprisonment for up to one month and by a fine of up to one hundred pounds, or by either of these two penalties. The gunpowder and all other explosives and materials that were the cause of the violation shall be confiscated, and the licence shall be revoked where necessary.
Any violation of the provisions of this Law for which no penalty is provided shall subject its perpetrator to a fine ranging between twenty-five and five hundred pounds.
There shall be referred to the Military Court: First: whoever commits an offence provided for in Article 72. Second: whoever simultaneously commits two offences falling under Article 72 and 73.

If an offence falling within the jurisdiction of the Criminal Court or the Judicial Council occurs and is connected with one of the offences provided for in Article 72, the Criminal Court or the Judicial Council, notwithstanding the provisions of Article 52 of the Military Penal Code, shall hear both offences together.
It is prohibited for anyone to hunt if hunting is not open, and if he does not hold a legal licence.
The owner of a property or the person having disposal thereof may prohibit hunting on his real properties by placing notices at the entrance of these real properties indicating the prohibition.

The hunting season shall begin on the first of September of every year and shall end on 31 January. As for waterfowl, hunting them shall remain permissible until the end of February. As for quail, turtle doves and wild pigeons, until the end of May.

The Ministry of Agriculture may temporarily or permanently prohibit the hunting of any bird or animal that appears to be beneficial to agriculture or for the purpose of propagating its species, and it may prohibit the hunting thereof in specific areas for specified periods, and it must issue decisions specifying therein: First: The time during which the hunting of aquatic animals and migratory birds is licensed. Second: The harmful birds and animals that may be hunted at all times. Third: The birds the hunting of which is strictly prohibited. It may also decide to protect game in specific lands at the request of the owners or lessees of these lands, and grant personal licences to property owners and right holders therein to import, in accordance with specified conditions, certain species of game birds to keep them temporarily and subsequently release them therein for the purpose of propagating game of their species.
Hunting is strictly prohibited in cities, villages, picnic areas, public gardens, and in any place located at a distance of less than 200 metres from dwellings.

Hunting is only licensed by means of firearms, dogs, and falcons. It is strictly prohibited by means of birdlime, nets, traps, snares, calling birds, bait, and caged game. It is also strictly prohibited to stalk partridges using a hunting blind and to pursue all kinds of game by car or aeroplane, with the exception of the hunting of aquatic animals. Hunting is completely prohibited on snowy days when snow covers the mountain regions in their entirety.

It is prohibited in all seasons to offer for sale, transport, or knowingly purchase game killed by means of prohibited devices and instruments. Such game shall be confiscated and delivered immediately to the charitable institution nearest to the place of confiscation. No search for or confiscation of game may be carried out in homes, whereas it is permissible in hotels, restaurants, and all other places open to the public.

It is prohibited in every season of the year to remove nests, and to take, destroy, offer for sale, sell, purchase, transport, and export the eggs or chicks of partridges, wild fowl, quails, and all other game birds, and the young of fur-bearing game animals.
It is prohibited to export live game - and to keep partridges in captivity.

If these provisions are violated, the game shall be confiscated and released immediately by the authority that confiscated it. A seizure report shall be drawn up to that effect. As for the eggs and chicks of feathered game, the young of fur-bearing animals, and partridges that have become accustomed to captivity, they shall be delivered to the agriculture department nearest to the place of confiscation to be kept temporarily or raised and then released for the purpose of propagating game, and a seizure report shall be drawn up to that effect.
It is strictly prohibited to sell birdlime and to hunt therewith. Its manufacture shall not be licensed save with a permit from the Ministry of Agriculture and for the purpose of exporting it only.
A hunting licence shall not be granted save to those who fulfil the conditions set forth in Article 29 of this Law.

A hunting licence is personal and annual. It shall be granted in the name of the hunter. There shall be stated thereon the address of its holder and his distinguishing marks. And his signature or his fingerprint and the number and type of weapons licensed to him. This licence shall be granted by the authority provided for in the last paragraph of Article 24 after collection of the fee fixed by the Budget Law. Every person while hunting shall mandatorily carry a licence to carry weapons and to hunt.
At the time when hunting is permitted, the licence entitles its holder to hunt by shooting or by coursing game by means of dogs or by means of falcons.

There shall be punished by a fine from 10 pounds to 50 pounds and by imprisonment from ten days to two months, or by either of these two penalties: 1- Persons who possess game at times during which hunting is prohibited, or display it for sale, buy it or transport it. 2- Persons who hunt on the lands of others without the consent of their owners or the holders of rights therein, or if the hunting takes place on lands containing crops or tree saplings, or on lands whose produce still remains thereon and which adjoin a dwelling house or are surrounded by a closed fence preventing the entry of persons and without any communication with the neighbouring lands. 3- Persons who contravene the provisions of Article 82.

There shall be punished by a fine from 25 to 100 pounds and by imprisonment from 10 days to three months, or by either of these two penalties, and in all cases by confiscation of the weapon used. 1- Persons who hunt without a hunting licence. 2- Persons who hunt at the times and in the places in which hunting is prohibited in accordance with the provisions of Article 85 and the first paragraph of Article 84 of this Law. 3- Persons who hunt by means of prohibited instruments such as nets, snares, pounding, or bait that stupefies birds, or by means of calling or caged birds. 4- Persons who hunt useful birds the hunting of which is prohibited.

A contravention shall be deemed repeated when the offender has been sentenced pursuant to this Law or during the twelve months preceding the last contravention, and in the event of repetition the penalty of the fine shall be doubled without the imprisonment.
The penalties fixed in the preceding Articles shall bepronounced without prejudice to the right to damages that may be claimed by the injured persons.

Every judgment shall specify the method that must be used to confiscate hunting nets, instruments and devices, and the motor vehicles or other vehicles used by the offenders. In addition, the destruction of prohibited hunting instruments shall be ordered.
If the commission of several offences provided for in this Law, in the Penal Code, or in special laws is established, only the most severe penalty shall be imposed.

If a judgment is rendered in respect of a misdemeanour provided for in this Law, the courts shall be entitled to deprive the offender of the right to obtain a hunting licence and a hunting firearm, for a period not exceeding five years.

All security forces, public and private watchmen, and all other sworn officers who are entitled to draw up offence reports shall have the requisite capacity to investigate the offences provided for in this Title and to draw up offence reports thereon.

Offenders may neither be arrested nor disarmed unless they are disguised or masked and refuse to disclose their identity or have no known place of residence, and they shall be brought immediately before the Single Judge, who shall verify their identity and release them.

The fee for a licence to transport and possess a firearm of the fourth category and the ammunition pertaining thereto is fixed at an amount of one hundred and fifty Lebanese pounds per year for each piece of firearm, payable upon taking possession of the licence and upon its renewal every year.

All laws and texts contrary to the provisions of this Law are repealed, in particular: Decision No. 313 dated 25 May 1926 relating to the importation and manufacture of weapons. Decision No. 60/LR dated 3 April 1939 relating to the generalisation of Article 7 of Decision No. 313 issued on 25 May 1926 and to the manufacture, importation, possession and transport of weapons, their ammunition, gunpowder and explosives. Decision No. 736 dated 27 January 1927 concerning the acquisition and carrying of weapons in the territories under the Mandate. Decision No. 1675 dated 22 November 1927 regarding disarmament in places where armed demonstrations take place. Decision No. 2998 dated 3 February 1930 relating to the designation of war weapons. Decision No. 7/LR dated 24 January 1938 relating to regarding the control of the consumption of explosives. Decision No. 63/LR dated 23 June 1938 regarding the trade in percussion caps for hunting rifles. Decision No. 152/LR dated 19 November 1938 regarding the use and possession of gunpowder and explosives by their holders. Decision No. 7 LR dated 23 January 1939 granting the armed force the necessary authority to ensure the enforcement of the regulations on war weapons and to carry out the investigation and inspection of the said regulations. Decision No. 203/LR dated 2 September 1939 prohibiting the sale of gunpowder, weapons and ammunition.

Decision No. 310/LR dated 4 November 1939 regarding the sale of hunting ammunition. Decision No. 382/F.Th. dated 12 November 1941 licensing the sale of types of hunting gunpowder and supplies used in the manufacture of hunting cartridges. Decision No. 240/LR dated 25 September 1941 regarding the importation, manufacture, sale and possession of all types of fireworks. Decision No. 28/LR dated 5 February 1941 regarding the sale of smooth-bore hunting rifles of 6 and 9 millimetre calibre. Decision No. 410/F.L. dated 24 November 1941 relating to fixing the selling prices of hunting gunpowder. Decision No. 165/F.L. dated 17 March 1942 relating to fixing the selling prices of blasting gunpowder, explosives and their accessories. Decision No. 337/F.L. dated 23 August 1943 relating to the stricter suppression of contraventions of the laws relating to weapons, ammunition, gunpowder and explosives. Decision No. 23 dated 24 March 1924 relating to the prohibition of hunting inside towns, hamlets and villages. Decision No. 73 L.R. dated 16 July 1931 relating to establishing a hunting regime in the territories of the Levant under the French Mandate. Decision No. 74 L.L. dated 18 May 1933 concerning the protection of birds useful to agriculture. Decision No. 8282/K dated 3 March 1947 relating to fixing the closing date of hunting throughout the territories of the Lebanese Republic

Articles 324 and 325, as amended by the Law of 9 December 1947, Articles 327 and 328, and the second paragraph of Article 752 of the Penal Code are hereby repealed. Article 120 of the Military Penal Code is hereby repealed and replaced by the following text: "Arms, ammunition, and equipment of the first four categories specified in Article 2 of the 'Law on Arms, Ammunition, and Hunting' shall be deemed war arms, ammunition, and equipment", and the schedule annexed to the Military Penal Code is hereby repealed. The final phrase of paragraph 2 of Article 50 of the Military Penal Code is hereby amended to read as follows: "the transport and possession of war arms and ammunition specified in the 'Law on Arms, Ammunition, and Hunting'."

Single Article: The draft law set forth in Decree No. 9046 dated 30 December 1967 relating to the regulation of the legal profession, as amended by the Administration and Justice Committee, is ratified after replacing the word "institution" with the word "company" and the word "institutions" with the word "companies" in Articles 62, 63 and 64, and this Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.
The legal profession is a profession regulated by this Law and aims to achieve the mission of justice by giving legal opinion and defending rights.

The legal profession contributes to the performance of public service, and therefore grants whoever practises it the rights and immunities provided for by this Law, and binds him to the obligations that it imposes.
A lawyer shall not be bound to abide by the instructions of his client except to the extent of their harmony with conscience and the interest of the client.

Lawyers in Lebanon shall have two Bar Associations: a Bar Association in Beirut, and a Bar Association in Tripoli.

The names of lawyers who establish offices for themselves in all Lebanese governorates except the Governorate of North Lebanon shall be registered in the Beirut Bar Association.

The names of lawyers who establish offices for themselves in the Governorate of North Lebanon shall be registered in the Tripoli Bar Association.

No lawyer is entitled to practise the legal profession in Lebanon if his name is not registered in one of the two Bar Associations. Nor is it permissible one of the two and in a foreign Bar Association. Every lawyer registered on the roll of practising lawyers must have an office within the jurisdiction of the Bar Association to which he belongs.

Any person who intends to practise the legal profession is required to be:

First: Lebanese for at least ten years

Second: Enjoying civil capacity, and having completed /20/ years of age and not having exceeded sixty-five.

Third: Holding the Second Part of the Lebanese Baccalaureate and the Lebanese Law Degree, and the qualifying certificate provided for in the following Article, while preserving the right of whoever benefited from the exemption provided for in paragraph /2/ of Article /20/ of the Higher Education Regulation Law issued on 26 December 1961 regarding equivalence to the Lebanese Baccalaureate certificate, and the right of those who applied as candidates for the examinations of the Lebanese Baccalaureate Second Part and obtained official attestations standing in place of the certificate, and those who obtained the official foreign secondary studies certificate inside and outside the country and obtained an equivalence therefor, for the years from 1987 until 1991.

Fourth: Enjoying a conduct that inspires trust and respect.

Fifth: Not convicted penally or disciplinarily on account of an act prejudicial to honour or dignity.

Sixth: Not dismissed from a public office or a previous profession for a reason prejudicial to honour and dignity.

The subjects of the qualifying diploma shall be distributed over the four years of study prescribed for obtaining a degree in law, and these subjects shall be determined by a decision issued by the Council of the Lebanese University after obtaining the approval of the two Bar Associations in Beirut and Tripoli, and in the event of disagreement regarding the determination of these subjects, the Council of Ministers shall decide the matter by a decree.

Applications for registration in the Bar Association shall be submitted to the competent Council of the Bar Association together with the documents proving the fulfilment of the conditions provided for in the fifth Article. The Council of the Bar Association shall decide by a reasoned decision on the application for registration within a period of two months from the date of its submission, unless it sees the necessity of investigating the conduct of the applicant for registration, in which case the period shall be extended to four months, and if the said period elapses after the submission of the application without a decision thereon of acceptance or rejection, the applicant shall be entitled to petition the Civil Court of Appeal in the governorate in which the seat of the Bar Association to which affiliation is sought is located.

The petition shall be submitted to the Court of Appeal within a period of thirty days from the date on which the applicant for registration is notified of the decision of rejection or from the date of expiry of the four months referred to in the preceding Article. Immediately upon the submission of the petition to the Court of Appeal, the file of the petitioner shall be requested from the Council of the Bar Association, and the Council shall send it within a period of two weeks at the most together with the observations it sees fit to express.

When examining applications for registration, the bench of the Court of Appeal shall be joined by two members of the Council of the Bar Association appointed by the President of the Bar Association, and if one or both of the two representatives of the Bar Association fail to attend, or do not, the Court of Appeal in its ordinary bench may decide on the petition.

Upon the issuance of the decision to register him, whether on the roll of trainee lawyers or of non-trainee lawyers, the lawyer shall take, before the Civil Court of Appeal and in the presence of the President of the Bar Association or whomever is delegated on his behalf, the following oath:

"I swear by Almighty God, and by my honour, to preserve the secrecy of my profession, and to perform its duties with honesty, to preserve its ethics and traditions, and to abide by its laws and regulations, and neither to say nor to publish, whether pleading or acting as counsel, anything contrary to morals and ethics, or anything prejudicial to the security of the State, and to respect the judiciary, and to conduct myself, in all my actions, in a manner that inspires trust and respect".

A lawyer may not commence the practice of the legal profession before taking this oath.

A lawyer who registers his name in either of the two Bar Associations shall be subject to a pupillage for a period of three years in the office of a lawyer at the Court of Appeal.

This provision shall not apply to a judge who has spent in the judicial service a period equivalent to the period of pupillage, nor to professors who have undertaken the teaching of law subjects for a period of not less than three years, nor to lawyers at the Court of Appeal who apply for their re-registration.

A trainee lawyer who applies to register his name in the Bar Association shall designate in his application the name of the lawyer in whose office he wishes to serve his pupillage and shall produce a document proving the consent of that lawyer to accept him as a trainee in his office.

The applicant for pupillage shall attach to his application the items set forth below:

First- The three certificates specified in paragraph 3 of Article Five.

Second- His judicial record

Third- His identity document.

Fourth- The consent of the lawyer in whose office he will serve his pupillage.

Fifth- A receipt proving his payment of the registration fee specified in the internal regulations.

The application for registration in the roll of trainees shall be submitted to the President of the Bar Association, who shall refer it to one of the members of the Bar Council to draw up a report on whether the legal conditions are fulfilled.

The application, together with the report and the documents, shall be referred to the Bar Council for adjudication in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

It is prohibited to combine the legal profession with:

1- Any public office or service, with the exception of membership of the Chamber of Deputies and of municipal and administrative councils and all other offices and services for which the person holding them does not receive a salary.

2- Commercial and industrial activities (except legal or scientific journalism) and in general and all professions aimed at profit.

3- The presidency, vice-presidency, or directorship of companies of various kinds.

4- The work of experts before the courts or other authorities or bodies .

5- Activities that are incompatible with the independence of the lawyer or inconsistent with the dignity of the legal profession.

6- The presidency of the Chamber of Deputies and the ministry during the lawyer's assumption of these functions, and upon commencing to exercise them he shall cease practising the profession and notify the President of the Bar Association thereof.

A lawyer who has held a ministry may not, during one year following his leaving his post, accept a mandate in person or through a lawyer in cases relating to his ministry and brought before the courts or the departments or the administrative councils of autonomous agencies subject to the tutelage of the ministry of which he was in charge.
A lawyer who is a Deputy , may not accept a mandate on behalf of the State in person or through a lawyer in a lawsuit of the State or for one of its institutions or for the autonomous agencies.
A lawyer elected as a member of one of the municipalities may not accept a mandate, in person or through a lawyer, in a lawsuit for or against that municipality.

A government employee who has left the service and practised the legal profession may not accept a mandate, in person or through a lawyer, in lawsuits and against the department in which he served, during the three years following his leaving the service.
A person who was a judge prior to practising the legal profession may not accept a mandate, in person or through a lawyer, in a lawsuit that had been brought before him.
A person who gave his opinion in a case when it was brought before him, in his capacity as an employee, an arbitrator, or an expert, may not accept a mandate in that case.
The trainee is not entitled or to use the title of "Lawyer" without adding to it the title of trainee, nor is he entitled to establish an office in his name prior to the completion of his training.

A trainee lawyer may transfer during the period of his training from the office of another lawyer, provided that he notifies the Bar Council thereof and obtains the approval of the new office and the Bar Council.

The trainee is entitled to plead during the period of his training in the name of the lawyer in whose office he is registered, before the following courts:

1- Courts of First Instance and committees and councils of all kinds.

2- The Court of Appeal for Misdemeanours, on behalf of the defendants only.

3- The Criminal Court, on behalf of the accused.
The trainee lawyer acquires the right to plead in his personal name before all courts upon his registration on the General Roll.

If an advocate is in arrears in the payment of his subscription fees for three consecutive years without a legitimate excuse accepted by the Council of the Bar Association, his name shall be struck off the General Roll after a formal notice, and he shall not be entitled to belong to the Bar Association unless he pays the registration fee anew.
Each of the two Bar Associations in Beirut and Tripoli shall be composed of those belonging to it and registered on its rolls.
Each of the two Bar Associations shall enjoy legal personality and financial and administrative independence.
The organs of each of the two Bar Associations shall consist of the General Assembly, the Council of the Bar Association, and the President of the Bar Association.

The General Assembly is the supreme authority for advocates and shall hold its ordinary meeting every year on the first Sunday of November, and shall hold an extraordinary meeting whenever the Council of the Bar Association deems it necessary or in the event that a request is submitted to it by one-third of the number of advocates who are entitled to participate in this meeting.

The President of the Bar Association shall preside over the General Assembly, and in the event of his absence, the longest-serving of the former Presidents of the Bar Association among those present, then the Secretary, then the oldest by age of the members of the Council of the Bar Association present.

The ordinary General Assembly shall be held at its date specified in Article 35 of this Law.

As for the extraordinary Assembly, it shall be held at the date determined by the Council of the Bar Association, and the practising advocates who are entitled to participate in each of these two Assemblies shall be invited by letters addressed to them or by a notice published in three daily newspapers, a copy of which shall be posted on the door of the headquarters of the Bar Association and of each chamber of the chambers of the Bar Association in the regions affiliated to it.

The meeting of the General Assembly shall be deemed valid if attended by more than half the number of voters who have the right to participate in voting; if this quorum is not reached, the invitation shall be repeated for another meeting to be held within fifteen days, and this meeting shall be valid regardless of the number of those present. Decisions shall be taken by a relative majority, including election results.

The Council of the Bar Association shall undertake the organisation of pupillage lectures for trainee lawyers at times it determines. The President of the Bar Association, or whomever he delegates, shall preside over the pupillage lectures, direct them, and conduct discussions on their subjects, and shall draw up a roll of the names of the trainee lawyers who attend them.

Every trainee lawyer who does not attend at least two-thirds of the pupillage lectures may have the duration of his pupillage extended by a decision of the Council of the Bar Association.

An application for registration on the Roll of Lawyers shall be submitted to the Council of the Bar Association, and every application shall be subject to the special provisions applicable to it as set out in the following two paragraphs:

First: The application submitted by the trainee lawyer:

The application shall be submitted after the expiry of the period of pupillage, accompanied by the following documents:

1- A certificate from the lawyer in whose office he completed his pupillage proving his regular attendance at pupillage for a period of three years.

2- A certificate from the Secretariat of the Council attesting to his attendance at two-thirds of the pupillage lectures.

3- A statement of the lawsuits or cases in the study or pleading of which he participated, signed by him and by the lawyer under whom he completed his pupillage, under the responsibility of each of them.

4- Receipts proving payment of the registration transfer fee, the pension fund fee, and the annual subscription fee due from him as from the date of his registration on the Roll of Lawyers.

Second: The application submitted by the former judge:

The application shall be submitted after leaving the judiciary and the following special provisions shall apply to it:

A former judge shall be exempted from the age requirement set out in the fifth Article of this Law, and the conditions provided for in that Article shall be deemed fulfilled and proven by the certificate issued to the judge by the competent administrative authority stating that he exercised judicial office for a period of at least three years and that his service therein was not terminated for a disciplinary reason incompatible with honour and dignity.

A judge who is exempted from the age requirement or who belongs to the Judges' Mutual Fund and who joins the Bar Association shall not benefit from any of the benefits provided by the Bar Association to its members, including the retirement pension and health and social benefits.
The Council of the Bar Association shall have the discretionary power to register the trainee lawyer on the said Roll or to extend the duration of his pupillage.

If the decision of the Council of the Bar Association rejects the application for completion of pupillage and registration on the Roll of Lawyers, or fails to decide on the application by acceptance or rejection within a period of two months from the date of its submission, the applicant for registration shall have the right, within a period of two months from the date he is notified of the rejection decision or from the date of expiry of the two-month period designated for deciding on the application, to apply to the Civil Court of Appeal in accordance with the provisions of Articles 7, 8 and 9 of the Law Regulating the Legal Profession.
The Council of the Bar Association shall draw up a roll of the names of the lawyers and trainee lawyers in accordance with the provisions of its internal regulations.
Only practising lawyers registered on the roll who have paid the annual fees within their time limits shall participate in the General Assembly or be accepted among the voters or candidates.

The proceedings of the annual Ordinary General Assembly shall cover:

1- Electing the President of the Bar, the members of the Bar Council, and the members of the Retirement Committee mentioned in the third paragraph of Article three of Legislative Decree No. 180 dated 21 May 1942.

2- Auditing and approving the final accounts of the past year and the budget of the following year.

3- Fixing the annual subscription fee due from lawyers to the Bar Fund and the Retirement Fund.
The Extraordinary General Assembly shall examine the matters specified in the requisition for convocation or in the decision of the Bar Council, to the exclusion of any others.

The Council of the Bar Association in Beirut shall consist of twelve members including the President of the Bar, and the Council of the Bar Association of Tripoli shall consist of six members including the President of the Bar.

The Bar Council shall regulate the manner of electing the President of the Bar and the members. Former Presidents of the Bar are permanent members ex officio of the Bar Council, provided however that they shall not participate in the voting.

The Bar Council shall meet upon convocation by the President of the Bar within a time limit of three days from the date of each election, and shall elect by secret ballot the Secretary, the Treasurer, a Commissioner, and the Commissioner of the Palace of Justice.
The term of office of the President of the Bar shall be two years, and it may not be renewed until two years have elapsed after the expiry of his term of office.

The term of office of the members of the Bar Council shall be three years. The term of office of one-third of the members shall expire each year, and no member may be re-elected more than once until two years have elapsed after the expiry of his term of office.

In exceptional cases in which more than one-third of the members are elected at once, lots shall be drawn among the elected members immediately upon the conclusion of the election process and at the first sitting held by the Bar Council in order to ensure the application of the principle of annual rotation of one-third provided for in the first paragraph. The membership of the President of the Bar during his term of office as President of the Bar shall be exempted from the drawing of lots, and the term of office of the member outgoing by lot shall be deemed a full term of office regardless of its duration.

Lots shall be drawn among the members of the Council of the Bar Association of Beirut elected in the year 1981 immediately upon the entry into force of this Law to terminate the membership of two-thirds of its members.

And after the election of the replacement members, another drawing of lots shall take place among them to select four of their members whose term of office shall exceptionally be for two years instead of three.

A lawyer shall not be elected President of the Bar Association unless at least twenty years have elapsed since his registration on the Roll of Practising Lawyers and unless he is a member of the Bar Council. A lawyer shall not be elected a member of the Bar Council unless at least ten years have elapsed since his registration on the aforementioned Roll.

Candidacy for the office of President and membership of the Bar Association shall be submitted to the Bar Council by the candidate himself or by at least fifty lawyers who are entitled to participate in the General Assembly.

A candidacy submitted after the first of October of the year in which the election takes place shall be rejected.

The Bar Council shall verify that the candidacy fulfils the legal requirements and shall issue its decision accepting or rejecting it before the tenth of October, failing which it shall be deemed accepted.

The decision of the Bar Council shall be notified to the candidate by registered letter immediately upon its issuance and a copy thereof shall be posted on the door of the headquarters of the Bar Association.

The decision accepting or rejecting the candidacy shall be subject to appeal by any interested party within a period of three days from the date of lodging the decision with the Registry of the Bar Association.

The Court of Appeal, sitting in chambers, shall rule on the matter within three days
The election shall take place by secret ballot and all other procedural rules for the election shall be determined in the Internal Regulations.

The candidate who obtains a relative majority of the votes cast shall be deemed elected, and in the event of an equality of votes the candidate with greater seniority on the Roll of the Bar Association shall be elected, and in the event of equality the older candidate shall be elected.

If the office of President of the Bar Association becomes vacant for any reason, the General Assembly shall be convened within a period of thirty days from the date of the vacancy of the office to elect a new President if the remaining period of the term of office exceeds six months, and the President elected in this case shall complete the remainder of the term of office of the former President; however, if the remaining period of the term of office is less than six months, the Secretary shall assume the office of President in an acting capacity until the end of the term of office.

If one of the seats of the members of the Bar Council becomes vacant, this seat shall be filled by the alternate who obtained the highest number of votes after the elected candidates in the last election.

In the absence of an alternate and when two or more seats up to half

of the members become vacant, the Bar Council shall continue its work composed of the remaining members until the first General Assembly in which those who fill the vacant seat or seats are elected.

If the seats of more than half of the members become vacant before the first of July, the Extraordinary General Assembly shall be convened within a period of one month, of which the first ten days shall be for candidacy, to elect those who fill these seats.

In all the aforementioned cases, the successor shall replace his predecessor for the remainder of the term of his membership.

The Council of the Bar Association shall be deemed dissolved if the number of vacant seats exceeds two-thirds, and in this case the Extraordinary General Assembly shall be convened for a general election of the members of the Council of the Bar Association, whereas the President of the Bar Association shall remain in his post.
Every member of the Council of the Bar Association who is absent from its meetings three consecutive times without an acceptable excuse shall be deemed to have resigned.
The sessions of the Council shall not be lawful unless they are held at their fixed times or at the times appointed by the President of the Bar Association.
The sessions of the Council shall not be lawful except in the presence of the absolute majority of its members.

The decisions of the Council shall be issued by a majority, and in the event of an equality of votes, the side with which the President of the Bar Association voted shall prevail.

Every interested party shall have the right to obtain from the Secretariat of the Bar Association

a certified true copy of the decisions of the Council.

The Council of the Bar Association shall have competence to administer its affairs, and it shall have in particular:

1- Deciding on applications for affiliation with the Bar Association and applications for appointment to Bar Association posts.

2- Laying down the Internal Regulations of the Bar Association and amending them, and all other regulations relating to the Bar Association.

3- Fixing the registration fee, amending it, and collecting it.

4- Executing the resolutions of the General Assemblies.

5- Preparing the annual budget and executing it.

6- Intervening between lawyers regarding disputes relating to the practice of their profession.

7- Calling General Meetings.

8- Representing the Bar Association at international professional conferences.

9- Corresponding with authorities and persons in matters pertaining to the Bar Association.

10- Endeavouring to secure the admission of trainees into the offices of lawyers.

11- Watching over the conduct of lawyers.

12- Issuing instructions to lawyers relating to the practice of their profession.

13- Supervising the lawyers' rooms and all institutions affiliated with the Bar Association.

14- Granting licences to lawyers' clerks to practise their profession and determining the conditions of those licences.

15- Regulating the traineeship and issuing the decision terminating it or extending its duration.

16- (This paragraph was repealed by Law No. 18/78 dated 18/12/78).

17- Establishing financial prizes disbursed from the fund of the Bar Association for those who author valuable scholarly works.

18- Granting financial aid to lawyers

The President of the Bar Association shall represent the Bar Association and shall have, in particular, the following powers:

1- Supervising its administration and defending its rights.

2- Presiding over the General Assembly and the Council of the Bar Association, executing the decisions of each of them, and signing the contracts which they approve.

3- Litigating in the name of the Bar Association and the right to intervene, in person or through a member of the Council whom he selects, every case that concerns it or concerns one of the lawyers, and assuming the capacity of a civil party in every case relating to acts that affect the dignity of the Bar Association or one of its members.

4- Appointing a representative of the Bar Association at the seat of each judicial district, determining his powers, and dismissing him.

5- Appointing the lawyers who are assigned to defend those who are granted legal aid and the lawyers who are assigned, where necessary, to defend the accused and juveniles.

6- Working to resolve disputes arising in professional matters.

No person other than lawyers may be appointed as legal counsel before the courts, and a lawyer must be appointed where the law so provides and in the following cases:

1- Before the Criminal Court.

2- Before the Court of Cassation and the Administrative Judiciary in all cases.

3- Before the Court of Appeal in all civil, Sharia, and confessional cases.

4- Before the Court of First Instance in unvalued civil cases, with the exception of personal status lawsuits, and in other cases in which the value of the matter in dispute exceeds (three hundred thousand Lebanese pounds).

5- Before the courts of summary jurisdiction, with the exception of ex parte applications.

6- Before the Execution Departments for the purpose of executing judgments, instruments, and all other contracts and deeds that exceed three hundred thousand Lebanese pounds.

7- Before the Appellate Expropriation Committees.

Every joint-stock company and all capital companies, including the limited liability company whose paid-up capital amounts to one million pounds and above, operating in Lebanon, whether its head office is in Lebanese territory or it has a branch therein, is obliged to retain a permanent lawyer from among the practising lawyers registered on the roll of the Bar Association for an annual retainer.

And if the company has a branch in North Lebanon, this branch must have its own lawyer from among the practising lawyers registered on the roll of the Tripoli Bar Association.

And the lawyer must notify the Bar Association of this retainer under penalty of disciplinary prosecution.

No commercial company provided for in this Article shall be registered after the publication of this Law unless it proves its compliance with this obligation.

An attorney shall not be entitled to accept a mandate for an annual fee on behalf of more than five commercial companies from among the companies obliged to appoint an attorney in accordance with Article /62/ of the Law Regulating the Legal Profession.
An attorney shall be entrusted with pleading by virtue of an official power of attorney issued by his client, or by assignment from the President of the Bar Association.

An attorney shall be assigned to plead by the President of the Bar Association in the following cases:

1- The granting of legal aid to one of the litigants

2- The refusal by several attorneys to accept the mandate in a rightful action.

3- A request by the Criminal Court or the Juvenile Court to appoint an attorney to defend an accused or a juvenile who has not appointed an attorney on his behalf.

4- The death of an attorney, the striking off of his name, his suspension, or his interdiction, and the impossibility of his performing a mandate.

In this case, the mission of the assigned attorney is confined to taking provisional measures to preserve the interests of a client until he chooses an attorney.

There shall be allocated to the fund of the Bar Association, in respect of powers of attorney drawn up for them within its jurisdiction, one quarter of the share accruing to Notaries Public from the fees collected on such powers of attorney.

- This share shall be collected by means of a special stamp issued by each of the Bar Associations of Beirut and Tripoli, and the Notary Public must affix this stamp onto the powers of attorney that he draws up.
An attorney has the right to a fee for the acts he performs within the scope of his profession, and to recover the expenses he incurs for the sake of the case in which he was mandated.

The fee shall be determined by an agreement concluded by the lawyer with his client.

If such fee in civil matters exceeds 20 per cent in relation to the value in dispute, the judiciary may reduce it.

In the event that the fee is not determined by a written agreement, it shall rest with the judiciary to determine it after taking the opinion of the Council of the Bar Association, taking into account the importance of the case, the work performed by him, and the condition of the client.

In the event of the existence of a written agreement concluded between the client and the lawyer, the lawyer shall have the right to execute it through the Execution Department after obtaining permission from the President of the Bar Association in due form in accordance with the first paragraph of Article /73/ of this Law.

The Court of Appeal hearing fee cases shall adjudicate objections raised against the execution of the written agreement in accordance with summary procedure, and its decision shall be final and not subject to any means of recourse. Furthermore, the submission of the objection shall not stay execution unless the Court of Appeal rules otherwise.

Upon the termination of any mandate with an annual fee by the client without legitimate cause, or upon the established permanent incapacity of the mandatory to work, or upon his retirement or his death, the client shall be liable for compensation to the mandatory or to his heirs in the amount of one month for each year of mandate on the basis of the last annual fees or compensations he received.

After twenty years of mandate, an annual mandatory who has reached the age of sixty years may request to be relieved from the mandate. The client shall, in this case, be liable for the compensation: set forth in the preceding clause.
If unforeseen actions branch out from the action, the lawyer shall have the right to claim a fee therefor.

If the mandatory recuses himself for reasons justifying such withdrawal, he may claim his fee for the work he has performed, whereas if his client dismisses him without justification, he may claim his fees in full.

The lawyer's fee shall be considered a privileged debt, provided that this privilege does not prejudice rights which the law provides are to be considered privileged and real rights registered prior to the filing of the action or the claim for the fee.

A lawyer shall have the right, in the various actions for fees, to sue for his fees and expenses after obtaining permission from the President of the Bar Association.

The First President of the Court of Appeal shall appoint one of the Presidents of the Chambers of the Court to examine the application, hear both parties, and seek the advisory opinion of the Council of the Bar Association.

The decision issued by the appointed President shall be subject to opposition before the Chamber presided over by the First President. The First President shall also have the right to refer this opposition to a Chamber other than that whose President issued the decision objected to.

The opposition shall be submitted, under penalty of dismissal, within a period of fifteen days commencing from the date of notification of the decision.

The decision issued as a result of the opposition shall not be subject to any form of appeal.

Actions pending before the competent courts in accordance with previous laws shall be adjudicated in accordance with the text of the provisions under which they were brought.

The right of defence is sacred; a lawyer shall not be held liable, nor shall any action for defamation, slander, or contempt arise against him as a result of written or oral pleadings made by him, unless he exceeds the bounds of defence.
