Preventive detention shall not be permissible in an action for defamation, slander, or contempt brought against a lawyer by reason of statements or writings issued by him during the practice of his profession. None of the judges of the court in which the incident occurred may participate in hearing the action.

Any offence committed against a lawyer during the practice of the profession or by reason of such practice shall expose the perpetrator, accomplice, accessory, and instigator to the same penalty by which they would be punished had that offence been committed against a judge, provided that it is subject to the ordinary avenues of recourse.

Any judicial decision ordering the search of a lawyer's office, the attachment of property located therein, or the inventory of its contents shall not be executed until at least 24 hours have elapsed following the deposit of a copy thereof at the headquarters of the Bar Association to which he belongs, accompanied by an invitation addressed to the President of the Bar Association to attend the measures in person or through a member delegated by him for this purpose from among the members of the Council of the Bar Association.

Seals may not be affixed to a lawyer's office on the grounds of collecting a tax or fee until at least ten days have elapsed following a written formal notice to the person concerned and notification of the headquarters of the Bar Association to which he belongs of the matter, all subject to compliance with the provisions of Article 12 of Legislative Decree No. 147 dated 12/6/1959 and Article 13 of Decree No. 2832 dated 14/12/1959, and the drawing up of a record thereof.

With the exception of the case of an offence in flagrante delicto, an attorney shall not be interrogated concerning an offence attributed to him before the matter is notified to the President of the Bar Association, who shall have the right to attend the interrogation in person or through whomever he delegates from among the members of the Bar Council.

- An attorney may not be prosecuted for an act that arose out of the practice of the profession or in the course thereof except by a decision of the Bar Council granting leave to prosecute, and the Bar Council shall assess whether the act arose out of the profession or in the course thereof.

- The decision granting or refusing leave to prosecute must be issued within one month from the date on which the President of the Bar Association is notified in writing of the occurrence of the act; if the one-month time limit expires and the decision has not been issued, leave shall be deemed to have been implicitly granted.

(The last paragraph of this Article was repealed pursuant to Law No. 18/78 dated 18/12/1978 and replaced with the following text):

Decisions of the Bar Council and decisions of the Management Committee of the Retirement Fund shall be subject to appeal before the Court of Appeal within a time limit of ten days following notification, provided that the adjudicating panel is joined by two members of the Bar Council chosen by the said Council from among its members.

The Management Committee of the Retirement Fund shall choose these two members from among its members when the matter pertains to this Fund.

An attorney shall abide in all his acts by the principles of honour rectitude and integrity and shall perform all the duties imposed upon him by this Law and the regulations and traditions of the legal profession.

An attorney is prohibited from contacting the witnesses in the case entrusted to him and hearing their testimonies before they are given, or discussing with them any matter relating to those testimonies.
An attorney is prohibited from purchasing disputed rights.

Professional civil partnerships comprising attorneys at the Court of Appeal in the capacity of partners may be established, and the object of such civil partnerships shall be the practice of law. The partnership instrument must be in writing or registered with the Bar Association, as well as every amendment made thereto, and attorneys who are partners or collaborate in a single office may not plead one against the other, nor represent in transactions and cases two parties with conflicting interests.
An attorney must have an office within the district of the Bar Association to which he is affiliated, and he shall not have the right to maintain more than one office for himself.

An attorney is prohibited from soliciting clients whether by means of publicity or by using intermediaries or brokers or by any other means, and he may not allocate a share of his fees to a person who is not an attorney.
An attorney is prohibited from advertising his office. He shall not have the right to hang at its entrance more than one sign bearing his name.
A lawyer is liable towards his client for the performance of his mission in accordance with the provisions of the law and the terms of his mandate.

A lawyer may withdraw from the mandate after accepting it, provided that he notifies his client and the court of this withdrawal, and that he takes the necessary precautions to prevent harm from befalling his client as a result of his withdrawal.

If the lawyer is unable for any reason whatsoever, especially in the case of the client's place of residence, to notify the latter of the withdrawal from the mandate, he shall refer the matter to the court hearing the dispute, which shall decide conclusively on the validity of the withdrawal after it is proven to it that notifying the client thereof was impossible.

In this case, the court shall exempt the lawyer from representing his client, and the latter shall be notified of the trial proceedings subsequent to the withdrawal in accordance with the legal procedures.

Upon the termination of his mission, the lawyer must return to his client the documents he received from him if requested to do so. The client's right to request the recovery of the documents shall lapse after the passage of five years from the termination of the case.

A lawyer may not accept a mandate on behalf of his client's adversary or render him any assistance, even by way of an opinion, in the action in which he had previously accepted the mandate or in a related action, even after the termination of his mandate.
A lawyer who receives annual or monthly legal fees for actions or consultations may not accept any action or give any consultation to his client's adversary.

A lawyer may not disclose a secret entrusted to him or of which he became aware through his profession, even after the termination of his mandate, nor may he give testimony against his client in the action in which he holds the mandate or in which he was an attorney.

When entrusted with a mandate in an action in which one of his colleagues was an attorney, a lawyer must refuse to accept the mandate unless his colleague permits him to do so, or he obtains the permission of the President of the Bar.

1- A lawyer shall not be entitled to accept a mandate in an action against a colleague of his, or to personally institute an action against him, prior to obtaining permission from the President of the Bar.

2- The application for permission shall be submitted to the President of the Bar, who shall decide thereon if he is unable to conciliate the disputing parties within a period not exceeding thirty days from the date of registration of the application with the registry of the Bar.

In the event that the period expires without a decision on the application, the permission shall be deemed to be granted ipso facto, and each of the parties shall be entitled to file an opposition against the express or implicit decision of the President of the Bar before the Council of the Bar within a period of ten days from the date of notification of the express decision or from the date of issuance of the implicit decision.

The Council of the Bar shall decide on the opposition within a period of thirty days from the date of its receipt; otherwise, the opposition shall be deemed dismissed.

3- The express or implicit decision of the Council of the Bar in this regard shall be subject to appeal in accordance with the rules stipulated in the amended final paragraph of Article /79/

4- Notwithstanding the first paragraph of this Article, a lawyer may, on a wholly exceptional basis, accept a mandate in civil actions to take precautionary measures against property in order to preserve rights at risk of loss prior to obtaining permission from the President of the Bar, provided that he submits an application for permission within a period not exceeding ten days from the date of taking such measures.
A lawyer shall wear the special lawyers' robe when appearing before the courts.

The Disciplinary Board shall be composed of the President of the Bar, or whomever he delegates, as Chairman, and two members chosen by the President of the Bar for a term of one year from the Council of the Bar; and one of the two members may be from among the lawyers registered on the General Roll for at least ten years. The panel of the Disciplinary Board shall wear the special lawyers' robe, as shall the lawyer appearing before it and his counsel.

The members of the Disciplinary Board, or any one of them, may be recused where there exists one of the grounds for the recusal of the judiciary stipulated in the Code of Civil Procedure. The Council of the Bar shall examine the application for recusal and adjudicate thereon in accordance with the rules for the recusal of judges.
The President of the Bar may address a fraternal admonition to a lawyer upon the commission of a minor infraction by him without referring him to the Disciplinary Board.

Every lawyer, whether practising or a trainee, who breaches the duties of his profession defined by this Law, or who, during the practice of that profession or outside it, commits an act that detracts from its standing, or conducts himself in a manner incompatible with its dignity, shall be subject to the following disciplinary penalties:

1- Warning

2- Reprimand

3- Prohibition from practising the legal profession for a period not exceeding three years.

4- Striking off the Roll of the Bar.

The period of temporary prohibition from practising the legal profession shall not be included in the calculation of the period of pupillage, the period of retirement, and all other periods prescribed for assuming Bar functions.

The Disciplinary Council may, when sentencing a lawyer to the penalty of temporary prohibition from practising the profession, order in a special paragraph of its decision the deprivation of that lawyer of the right to be elected as a member of the Bar Council for a period not exceeding ten years.

This supplementary penalty shall be mandatory where a lawyer is sentenced for deliberately breaching a duty imposed upon him by a Bar function assigned to him.

A lawyer shall not be referred before the Disciplinary Council except pursuant to an order issued by the President of the Bar either of his own motion or upon a complaint or report submitted to him.

The referral of a lawyer to the Disciplinary Council shall not be permissible except after he has been heard by the President of the Bar or whomever he delegates, or upon his failure to appear to be heard despite having been summoned. The President of the Bar shall ensure the expeditious determination of the case.
The separation of a lawyer from the legal profession shall not prevent his disciplinary prosecution for acts he committed prior to his separation.
Every court that issues a criminal judgment against a lawyer shall serve a copy of such judgment upon the President of the Bar.

The Disciplinary Council shall adopt the methods of investigation and trial in which it sees a safeguard for the rights of the defence and the proper administration of justice, and the referred lawyer shall have the right to appoint one lawyer.
The trial before the Council shall be conducted in camera, and summonses and judgments shall be served in accordance with the rules of procedure.
The decisions of the Disciplinary Council shall be served upon the President of the Bar and the Appellate Public Prosecution within a time limit of ten days from the date of their issuance.

Disciplinary judgments rendered in absentia shall be subject to opposition by the convicted lawyer within a period of ten days following the judgment in person or by registered letter with acknowledgment of receipt, and the Disciplinary Council shall examine the opposition and issue its decision thereon within a period of fifteen days following the submission of the petition of opposition. Both the lawyer and the Appellate Public Prosecution shall have the right to appeal any decision issued by the Disciplinary Council, and both appeals must be submitted within the ten days following notification.

The appeal against decisions issued by the Disciplinary Council shall be brought before the Court of Appeal, which shall adjudicate thereon in a closed session after adding to its bench two members of the Council of the Bar Association chosen by the said Council from among the members who did not examine the case in the first instance, and the appellant shall have the right to appoint one lawyer to represent him.

A person against whom a disciplinary judgment striking his name off the Roll of the Bar Association has been rendered shall have the right to apply to the Council of the Bar Association, after the lapse of five full years from the issuance of such judgment, for the re-registration of his name on the Roll of Lawyers; if the Council deems that the period which has elapsed is sufficient to remove the effect of what was committed by him, it shall decide to re-register his name, and if the Council rejects the application, it may not be renewed except after the lapse of two years, and the application may not be renewed after being rejected twice.

Every person who usurps the title of lawyer or practises the legal profession without right shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years and by a fine from twenty-five thousand to one hundred thousand Lebanese pounds.

Every lawyer who practises the legal profession after being prohibited from practising it, or during the period of his temporary prohibition from practising it, or after the striking of his name off the Roll of Lawyers pursuant to a final disciplinary decision, shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years and by a fine from twenty-five thousand to one hundred thousand Lebanese pounds.

Every person who gives legal consultations without being a lawyer or a professor at the Law Institute shall be punished by imprisonment for up to one month and by a fine from ten pounds to one hundred pounds.

Every person who solicits clients for a lawyer in return for a commission shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year, and by a fine from fifty pounds to one thousand pounds, or by either of these two penalties. Where such person is a public official, his penalty shall be increased within the limits prescribed by Article 257 of the Penal Code.

Every tout shall be expelled from the Courthouse by the Public Prosecution upon the request of the President of the Bar Association. If he repeatedly enters therein without a legitimate reason, he shall be punished by imprisonment from one week to three months, and by a fine from ten pounds to one hundred pounds, or by either of these two penalties.

Any lawyer who resorts to a broker to acquire clients shall be liable to the penalty specified in the first paragraph of the preceding Article, and he shall be prohibited from practising the legal profession for a period of at least one year, and in the event of a repeat offence he shall be prohibited from practising his profession.
The President of the Bar Association may permit a foreign lawyer to plead before the Lebanese courts in a specific case, subject to reciprocity in the Bar Association to which the lawyer belongs.

The documents and decisions of the Bar Council and the judgments of the Disciplinary Council shall be served in accordance with the procedures provided for in this Law and the procedures determined by the internal regulations of the Bar Association.
The Law Regulating the Legal Profession promulgated on 13 December 1945 and all provisions contrary to this Law or inconsistent with the provisions thereof are hereby repealed.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Permanent employees are divided into two categories:

1- A category subject to the pension system, which includes employees belonging to cadre (A).

2- A category not subject to the pension system, which includes employees belonging to cadre (B).
The provisions of this Title shall apply to the employees specified in item (1) of the first Article of this Legislative Decree.
Severance indemnity shall be due for actual services whose duration is less than twenty years.

A retirement pension shall be due for actual services whose duration is at least twenty years. However, the employee shall be entitled in this case to request, within one month from the date of the termination of his service by operation of law due to reaching the age limit, and from the date he is notified of the decree or decision terminating his service in other cases, the substitution of the severance indemnity for the retirement pension.

His heirs shall also be entitled to request, within three months from the date of his death, to benefit from the same right, and if a dispute arises among the heirs, each of them shall be granted according to his request.

Notwithstanding any other general or special text, it shall not be permissible to combine the retirement pension with any other pension paid from the State Treasury, and in the event that the pensioner or one of the family members of the deceased employee or pensioner to whom the right to the retirement pension passes becomes entitled to another pension or a share of a pension, whatever its nature or designation may be, the higher pension or the more abundant share in amount shall be allocated to the beneficiary.

There shall not be counted in the calculation of the pension or the severance indemnity any service rendered:

1 - Before completing eighteen years of age for whoever entered the service before the date of 13 January of the year 1955.

2 - Before completing twenty years of age, for whoever entered the service after the date of 13 January 1955.

3 - Before completing eighteen years of age, for teachers who entered the service after the date of 13 January 1955.

4 - After reaching the legal age.

5 - After spending the legal period in the service.

Pension deductions shall consist of:

1- Half of the salary of the first month of the employee's service.

2- Six percent of the salary (as amended by Law 5/2025).

3- The first monthly instalment of every increase that occurs to the salary.

The following services shall be relied upon in calculating the retirement pension and the dismissal indemnity:

1- Services for which retirement deductions have been paid, including services for which the employee received half salary, provided that he pays the retirement deductions for the other half.

2- Services rendered to the Government of Greater Lebanon and the Government of the Lebanese Republic, and those previously rendered to the High Commission and the Departments of Common Interests by Lebanese employees subject to Lebanese retirement legislation, as well as services rendered to one of the governments in Syria and Lebanon beginning from the first of October 1918 until the establishment of the Lebanese Republic on 23 May 1926.

3 - Services rendered by Lebanese nationals after 31 October 1918 in the Special Troops of the Levant, and the Lebanese Chasseurs, in the territories of Syria and Lebanon.

4 - Periods of placement on availability with salary for those placed therein pursuant to previous laws.

5 - Services rendered by Lebanese employees in one of the Syrian governments prior to the first of October 1943, provided that they have complied with the provisions of Article 24 of the 1949 Budget Law.

6 - Services rendered in municipal departments in posts similar to State posts for which the law provides a retirement pension, provided that their holders have complied with the terms of Article 54 of the 1951 Budget Law.

For the application of the provisions of items 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6, it is required that the holders of such services pay to the Treasury the full retirement deductions due thereon.

The right to a pension or dismissal indemnity shall arise:

- For the employee, from the day on which his service ends.

- For the members of his family, from the day following his death.

Where the salary or pension has been collected in advance on the first of the month, the pension shall be allocated starting from the first of the following month.

The retirement pension shall be liquidated on the basis of one-fortieth of the last monthly salary, calculated in accordance with the provisions of the new Article 12 of this Legislative Decree, multiplied by the number of years of service up to forty years only, and there shall be added thereto a dismissal indemnity equivalent to three months' salary for each year of service after forty.

Subject to the provisions of the new Article 12 of this Legislative Decree, the dismissal indemnity shall be liquidated on the basis of one month's salary for each year of actual service up to the tenth, two months' salary for each year of actual service after the tenth and up to the thirtieth, and three months' salary for each year of actual service after the thirtieth.
A month shall be calculated as one-twelfth of a year, and a day as one-thirtieth of a month.

1- Notwithstanding any other text, and for the purpose of determining the value of the monthly salary adopted in calculating the retirement pension or the dismissal indemnity, there shall be added to the last basic salary of the employee concerned a proportion of one twenty-fourth of the value of the last step for each month that the employee has spent in actual service after his last advancement in step

2 - Notwithstanding any other text, and for the purpose of calculating the retirement pension or the dismissal indemnity, the product set out in the new Article 12 of Legislative Decree No. 47 dated 29/6/83 and its amendments shall be multiplied by a rate of 85% (eighty-five per cent).

- Notwithstanding any other text, there shall be adopted in the liquidation of invalidity pensions, retirement pensions, or dismissal indemnities for employees of the foreign service working abroad the salary received by their counterparts in Lebanon.

1- Upon the transfer of an employee from a cadre subject to the retirement regime to a cadre not subject thereto, or vice versa, his rights shall be liquidated immediately on the basis of his services in his former cadre, without his being entitled to combine them with his services in his new cadre.

2- However, an employee belonging to a permanent cadre not subject to the retirement regime and transferred to a post belonging to a permanent cadre subject to the retirement regime shall be entitled to request, within one month from the date of his assumption of duties in his new post, that his previous services in the permanent cadre not subject to the retirement regime be combined with his new services; if he does not do so, his rights shall be liquidated in the manner set forth in Clause (1) of this Article.

3- The provisions of Clause (2) of this Article shall not apply to physicians in the Ministry of Public Health belonging to Cadre (B).

Pensions and dismissal from service indemnities shall be liquidated by a committee in the Ministry of Finance called the "Retirement Committee", which shall be appointed by decree and shall be composed of five members of at least the Third Category and a rapporteur. The Committee shall take its decisions by a majority of votes.

The retirement pension or the dismissal indemnity shall be allocated by a decision of the Director General of Finance on the basis of the minutes of the Retirement Committee.

No employee may be dismissed by reason of his having sustained a disability unless such disability prevents him from performing the post which he holds and any other post within the administration.

Every employee discharged:

1- For a disabling infirmity that arose certainly and directly from the performance of his duty and the cause of which is not attributable to his committing a gross fault.

2- For his inability to continue in service as a result of risking his life to save the life of another, or due to a danger to which he was exposed, or an assault or an accident to which he was subjected, during the performance of his duty or by reason thereof.

Shall be granted an invalidity pension in accordance with the following bases:

First: One-third of his last salary if his actual service is less than twenty years and his infirmity does not put him in need of the physical assistance of another, and one-half of this salary if his infirmity puts him in need thereof.

Second: One-half of his last salary if his actual service is twenty years at least and his infirmity does not put him in need of the physical assistance of another, and two-thirds (literally: third) of this salary if his infirmity puts him in need thereof.

In both cases, one-fiftieth of the last salary shall be added for each year of actual service after the tenth, provided that the total pension does not exceed the monthly salary that the employee was receiving upon his discharge by reason of the infirmity.

Every employee discharged for a disabling infirmity, which did not arise from the performance of his duty and puts him in need of the physical assistance of another, shall be granted an invalidity pension equivalent to one-third of his last salary if his actual service exceeded five years.

If an employee dies as a result of wounds, an accident, or an illness that afflicted him in the circumstances specified in Article (16) of this Legislative Decree, there shall be allocated to the Lebanese among the members of his family the pension that he would have been entitled to receive had he been afflicted with an infirmity putting him in need of the physical assistance of another. Provided that this pension does not exceed eighty percent of the last salary received by the employee before his death.

If the infirmity or death that gives rise to a right to the invalidity pension originates from a third party, the Ministry of Finance must have recourse against the third party for what the State may bear as a result thereof.
The invalidity and retirement pensions may be combined.

An employee shall be deemed as disabled and in need of the physical assistance of another, if he is afflicted with insanity, total paralysis, complete blindness, or similar infirmities that render the person afflicted therewith incapable of attending to his personal affairs by himself.

For the purpose of applying the provisions relating to the invalidity pension, the administration to which the employee belonged shall conduct an investigation into the circumstances in which the accident or illness occurred.

The Ministry of Finance shall submit the file of the employee with the result of this investigation to a permanent medical committee appointed by decree upon the recommendation of the President of the Civil Service Board and the proposal of the Ministers of Finance and Public Health, each within his competence, composed of three physicians and a representative from each of the Civil Service Board and the Ministry of Finance, of the third category at least, whose mission is to determine:

1- Whether the infirmity arises from the function.

2- Whether the infirmity is disabling.

3- Whether the infirmity requires the person afflicted with it to have the physical assistance of others.

4- Incapacity to earn a living. The person concerned shall have the right to inspect his file before the meeting of the committee and to request it to hear the physician of his choice. The Ministry of Finance and the employee shall have the right to object to the decision of the medical committee before a second special committee appointed by decree from three specialist physicians and a representative from each of the Civil Service Board and the Ministry of Finance of the third category at least.

This committee must issue its decision within one month from the date of its appointment, and in allocating invalidity pensions, reliance shall be placed solely on the decisions of these two committees.

With the exception of pensions allocated in accordance with the provisions of the Lebanese Military Retirement Law dated March 1320/1904, pensions and dismissal indemnities shall pass to the Lebanese members of the family of employees and pensioners in accordance with the provisions of the following articles:

1- There shall pass to the Lebanese members of the family the pension to which the employee was entitled on the day following the date of his death or which the pensioner was receiving on the day of his death, and the full family allowances.

If the employee dies, and the period of his service does not entitle him to a right to a pension, the Lebanese members of his family shall be granted the full dismissal indemnity to which he was entitled at the date of death. And if his service entitles him to a right to a pension, the Lebanese members of his family shall be granted the full dismissal indemnity if they opt for this indemnity.

The family members of the deceased employee (male or female) or retiree (male or female) who are entitled to the pension or the compensation are exclusively Lebanese nationals from among:

- The wife or the husband, provided that they do not engage in remunerated work.

Where the husband or the wife engages in remunerated work, they shall be entitled only to the difference between the wage or salary received by reason of their work and their share of the retirement pension of their legator

- Male children who have not completed the eighteenth year of their age, children who are pursuing their studies until they complete the twenty-fifth year of their age, and the infirm among them who are incapable of earning a living even if they have exceeded this age, provided that their infirmity is established by a report from the Permanent Medical Committee provided for in Article 22 of this Legislative Decree.

Paragraph added pursuant to Law 40 dated 22/2/2007 Official Gazette 12

The pension shall be discontinued for married male children and sons, regardless of their status, if they have male sons who have completed the eighteenth year of their age, or the twenty-fifth year where they are pursuing their studies, unless the latter are infirm and incapable of earning a living and their infirmity is established by a report from the Permanent Medical Committee provided for in Article 22 of this Legislative Decree, and provided that they have no income or property from the wife or from any other source.

Unmarried daughters, provided that they do not engage in remunerated work, and widowed and divorced daughters, provided that the widow or divorcée has no income or alimony from the property of her husband.

The pension shall be discontinued for divorced or widowed daughters if their male sons have completed the eighteenth year of their age, or the twenty-fifth year where they are pursuing their studies, unless the latter in both cases are infirm and incapable of earning a living and their infirmity is established by a report from the Permanent Medical Committee provided for in Article 22 of this Legislative Decree.

- The father and the mother, where the following conditions are met:

- Incapacity to earn a living, established by official documents

- That the parents have no other source

- That the parents have no other child who has attained the age of majority and is capable of supporting them

- Where any of the aforementioned persons receives a retirement pension in violation of the provisions of this Law, they shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of paragraph (3) of Article 655 of the Penal Code, and they shall be required to refund the amounts unduly received, together with the legal interest.

Persons who submit an application to regularise their status within a period not exceeding six months from the date of publication of this Law shall not be prosecuted and shall also benefit from the payment by instalments of the amounts unduly received.

If it appears upon liquidation that a family member entitled to the pension has been missing for more than two years, the pension shall be distributed among the existing family members only. If he returns, his share shall be allocated to him from the date he claims it.

If, however, he has been missing for a period of less than two years, his share shall be retained until the expiry of the two years, and shall then be distributed among the beneficiaries in equal shares.

As for the missing person's share in the severance compensation, it shall be retained until after the expiry of two years, and the provisions of the preceding paragraph of this Article shall then be applied thereto.

The pension shall be definitively discontinued for male children upon their completion of eighteen years of age, except in the following cases:

1- If they are pursuing studies, in which case their pension shall continue to be granted to them until they complete their studies, provided that it shall be discontinued for them upon their completion of twenty-five years of age at most and that they do not engage in paid work. This rule shall apply to those who have exceeded eighteen years of age at the death of the person from whom their entitlement derives, if they are still pursuing studies.

2- If they are afflicted with an infirmity that incapacitates them from working and their infirmity has been established through the Medical Committee provided for in Article 22 of this Legislative Decree, and their case shall be reviewed every three years at most.

The pension shall be discontinued for legitimate wives, mothers, and daughters upon their marriage or their engagement in paid work, and the pension shall be reallocated in the event of their divorce or their leaving work. The provisions of this paragraph shall apply to cases existing on the date of its entry into force.
The pension shall be definitively discontinued for the father and mother upon the cessation of any of the conditions provided for in item (4) of Article 26 of this Legislative Decree.
The pension shall not be discontinued for a retired female employee upon her marriage. If she dies, her pension shall pass to those entitled thereto.

In the event of the death of one of the family members who receive a retirement pension, or in the event of the discontinuation of the pension for one of them for any reason whatsoever, the remaining family members benefiting from the retirement pension shall receive the entirety of this pension, and it shall be redistributed among them equally.
If two pensions accrue to one of the family members, the pension of the greater amount shall be allocated to him, and the provisions of the preceding Article shall apply to the lesser pension.

Every civil servant against whom it is established by a judicial judgment shall permanently forfeit the right to obtain the retirement pension or the dismissal indemnity, even if they have been liquidated:

1- That he embezzled State funds.

2- That he embezzled private trusts deposited with him, or materials handed over to him, for which he ought to render an account.

3- That he accepted a bribe in matters relating to his function.

4- That he committed forgery in official documents that assisted in the embezzlement of State funds.
Neither a general amnesty nor a special pardon may restore the rights forfeited in application of the provisions of the preceding Article.

The right of the retiree to the pension shall be permanently terminated:

1- Upon the loss or deprivation of Lebanese nationality.

2- Upon the issuance of a judgment imposing a criminal penalty providing for the confiscation of his movable and immovable property. However, upon the issuance of a judgment imposing a criminal penalty other than that mentioned above, the family members of the entitlement holder shall be granted his pension as if he had died.

If he subsequently recovers his rights, his pension shall be disbursed as of the date of cessation of the reasons that led to the suspension of his entitlement, and the allocations of his family shall be cancelled as of the same date.

The right of each family member to obtain the pension shall be permanently terminated:

1- Upon his loss or deprivation of Lebanese nationality.

2- Upon the issuance of a judgment imposing a criminal penalty requiring the confiscation of his movable and immovable property.

However, upon the issuance of a judgment imposing a criminal penalty not mentioned above, the disbursement of the pension shall be suspended throughout the duration of the penalty only, provided that the share is restored to its holder as of the date of cessation of the reason that led to its suspension.

Applications for the allocation of pensions and dismissal from service indemnities shall be submitted exempt from stamp duties, either directly to the Ministry of Finance, or through the administration to which the civil servant belonged, and the date of registration of the application shall be relied upon whether in the Ministry of Finance or in the administration concerned.

The application for the pension and the dismissal indemnity shall be submitted within a time limit of five years from the day on which the service of the civil servant was terminated.

The time limit for those to whom the right of the civil servant was transferred shall begin from the day following his death.

If the holder of the right to the pension does not submit his application within the time limit mentioned in the preceding Article, the pension shall be allocated to him from the date of registration of his application, unless it is conclusively established that force majeure prevented its submission.

An application for a dismissal indemnity that is not submitted within the time limit mentioned in Article 42 of this Legislative Decree shall be rejected unless it is conclusively established that force majeure prevented its submission.

The pension or dismissal indemnity shall be distributed in equal shares among those entitled thereto, and in the event of polygamy, all lawful wives shall be given a single share.

In the event of the death of an employee who is not among those entitled to a pension or dismissal indemnity, the full indemnity due to him shall be paid exclusively to the persons enumerated below, and shall be distributed among them in the following manner:

A- The spouse, children, and direct ascendants:

- Where the spouse or lawful wives and children exist together, the spouse or lawful wives shall receive one-quarter of the basic indemnity due, and the remainder shall be divided equally among the children, and if the deceased was the sole breadwinner in Lebanon for two parents, or for one of them, and their income or the income of the surviving one of them does not equal at least the minimum wage, the two parents together or the surviving one of them shall receive a lump-sum share equal to one-tenth of the basic indemnity.

And if among the children there is anyone who died before the holder of the indemnity, his descendants shall take his place in the share that would have devolved upon him had he been alive. This share shall be distributed equally among the descendants, and in the event of the existence of more than one lawful wife, the share of the spouse shall be distributed equally among the lawful wives.

- In the event of the absence of children, the indemnity shall be distributed with the spouse or lawful wives receiving two-thirds of the indemnity, and the direct ascendants shall receive the remaining one-third equally. In the event of the absence of direct ascendants, the ascendants of the second degree (grandfather or grandmother) shall take the place of the direct ascendants in the share due to them and shall share it equally.

- However, in the event of the existence of a spouse only, or lawful wives, without ascendants of any degree whatsoever, or descendants, or siblings, or descendants of siblings, the spouse or lawful wives shall receive the full indemnity equally.

B - Ascendants and siblings:

- If the deceased has no spouse and children, his indemnity shall devolve upon his direct ascendants and his siblings to the exclusion of others, and the ascendants shall receive half of the indemnity divided equally among them, and in the event of the existence of ascendants without siblings, or siblings without ascendants, the surviving category shall receive the full indemnity and it shall be distributed equally among its members.

Ascendants of the second degree shall take the place of direct ascendants in the share allocated to them, and the indemnity shall be distributed equally among them. And the descendants of the siblings of the deceased shall take their place in the share that would have devolved upon the brother or sister, as if he were alive.
If the employee or pensioner dies leaving a pregnant wife or wives, the pension shall be redistributed upon birth in equal shares among those entitled.

Ministerial services shall not confer a right to a pension or dismissal compensation. However, ministerial services performed by one of the employees may be counted in calculating the pension or dismissal compensation under the following conditions:

1- That the Minister retains his old post in his cadre by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers.

2- That the Minister continues to pay the retirement deductions on the basis of the salary he was receiving in the old post.
It shall be permissible to combine a retirement pension with the allowances of members of the legislative authority and members of the Government.
Pensioners shall be given the family allowance granted to employees.

Pensions or dismissal compensations may not be assigned, nor may they be attached except against a debt to the State, or maintenance for food established by virtue of a judgment, provided that the attachment is exercised only within the limits provided for in the Code of Civil Procedure.

Maintenance for food shall take precedence over a debt to the State.
The beneficiary may object to the pension or to the amount of the dismissal compensation allocated to him within six months from the date of his notification of the text ordering its allocation.

The Ministry of Finance shall have the right at any time whatsoever to reconsider the allocations of compensation for dismissal from service and retirement pensions in the event that a material error or omission in the allocation is proven.

Pensions and dismissal compensations shall be incorporated into the expenditure section of the State budget, and retirement deductions shall be incorporated into the revenue section thereof.

An independent retirement fund may be established by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers, the conditions of financing, rules of management, and investment of the assets of which shall be determined in the decree establishing it.
The provisions of this Title shall cover the employees specified in item (2) of Article One of this Legislative Decree.
The employees specified in the preceding Article shall not pay the deductions provided for in the sixth Article of this Legislative Decree.

Every employee discharged from service shall receive a discharge indemnity equivalent, for each year of actual service, to a rate of 85% (eighty-five per cent) of the last basic monthly salary he received.

- A month shall be calculated as one-twelfth of a year and a day as one-thirtieth of a month.
All other provisions that apply to the discharge indemnity accruing to employees subject to the Retirement Regime shall apply to the discharge indemnity mentioned in the preceding Article.

If the employee is discharged for one of the reasons mentioned in Article 16 of this Legislative Decree, he shall be granted, in addition to the discharge indemnity accruing to him, an additional indemnity equivalent to the salary of fifteen months if the duration of his service is fifteen years or less.

However, if the duration of his service exceeds fifteen years, he shall be granted an additional indemnity equivalent to the salary of one month for each year of actual service, provided that this indemnity does not exceed the amount of the salary of thirty months, whatever the duration of his service may reach.

And if he dies for the same reasons, the Lebanese members of his family provided for in Article 26 of this Legislative Decree shall be granted the value of the indemnities determined for him.

The provisions of Legislative Decree No. 113 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments are hereby repealed,

as well as all legal provisions contrary to the provisions of this Legislative Decree or inconsistent with its content,

and the sixth Article of each of the Laws No. 2/81 dated 20 February of the year 1981.

and No. 1/82 dated 28 January of the year 1982 .

and No. 37/82 dated 15 December of the year 1982, is also repealed,

with effect from the date of entry into force of this Legislative Decree.
This Legislative Decree shall enter into force immediately upon its publication by posting on the premises of the Presidency of the Government.
An application submitted by one of the members of the family within the statutory time limit shall prevent the forfeiture of the rights of the remaining members.
The committee provided for in Article 15 of this Legislative Decree shall rule on cases of force majeure, and a delegate from the Civil Service Board shall join the committee in this case.

A pension may not be combined with any salary, indemnity, or monthly or daily wage paid from the State Treasury, and the disbursement of the pension shall be suspended throughout the period in which its holder remains in office.

If a pensioner is reinstated into service in a post subject to the pension system, his pension shall be liquidated anew upon his retirement a second time on the basis of all his actual services, provided that his new pension shall not be less than the previous pension.

An employee who was dismissed for a non-disciplinary reason and received a dismissal indemnity for his services shall have the right, in the event of his reinstatement to office, to request the inclusion of these services in the calculation of his new pension or indemnity, provided that he submits his application within a time limit of three months from the date of his resumption of service, and that he refunds the indemnity he collected to the Treasury. If the employee does not submit the application within the aforementioned time limit, he shall be granted upon his dismissal a second time a new dismissal indemnity or a retirement pension in the calculation of which only his latest services, to the exclusion of others, shall be relied upon.

If the employee had not collected the dismissal indemnity for his previous services, and was entitled to it at the time, his previous services shall be combined automatically with his subsequent services.

A resigned employee who is reinstated to office shall have the right to combine his previous services with his new services, provided that he requests this within three months from the date of his resumption of service, and that he refunds to the Treasury the pension deductions that he received for his old services.

If he had not recovered these deductions, and was entitled to them at the time, his previous services shall be combined automatically with his subsequent services.

An employee who is deemed to have resigned shall not benefit from the provisions of this Article.

When an employee is required, in accordance with the provisions of this Legislative Decree, to pay pension deductions for previous services, or to refund to the Treasury a dismissal indemnity collected therefor, he shall pay this debt in full in a single lump sum within the period of three months mentioned in the two preceding Articles.

Acts which interrupt prescription with respect to one of the joint and several creditors benefit the others. However, causes which suspend the running of prescription remain personal and specific to each of the creditors.

A compromise concluded between one of the creditors and the debtor benefits the other creditors when it includes the acknowledgment of the right or of the debt. Such compromise shall not be binding upon them when it includes the remission of the debt or prejudices their position, unless they consent thereto.

If one of the joint and several creditors grants the debtor an extension of time, this shall not be binding upon the others unless the contrary is inferred from the instrument creating the obligation, or from the law, or from the nature of the case.

Whatever each one of the joint and several creditors receives, whether by way of payment or by way of compromise, becomes common between him and the other creditors, who shall share therein in proportion to their shares. If one of the creditors obtains a suretyship or an assignment for his share, the other creditors shall have the right to share in what is paid by the surety or the assignee; all of this applies unless the contrary is inferred from the contract, the law, or the nature of the case.
After payment, the total debt shall be divided into equal shares unless the contrary is stipulated.

A joint and several creditor who, after receiving payment, is unable to present the property received for a reason attributable to his fault is liable towards the other creditors to the extent of their shares.

An obligation is joint and several among debtors when several debtors are bound by a single debt and each of them must be considered, in his relations with the creditor, as a debtor for the whole of this debt, in which case it is called "joint and several liability of debtors"; provided that joint and several liability shall not prevent the division of the debt among the heirs of the joint and several debtor.

Joint and several liability among debtors shall not be presumed, but must be expressly derived from the contract creating the obligation, or from the law, or from the nature of the case. However, joint and several liability shall apply as of right in obligations contracted between merchants in commercial matters, unless the contrary results from the contract creating the obligation or from the law.
A single obligation may pertain to several persons who are obligees, or obligors. Obligations in this respect are divided into conjoint obligations and joint and several obligations.

The distribution of benefits and burdens in conjoint obligations shall necessarily be effected on the basis of equality among the creditors and the debtors, unless the contract requires otherwise.

In reality, the number of debts shall equal the number of creditors or the burden of the debtors; this is the matter that must be taken into consideration, particularly in:

(1) that which relates to the right of action, as none of the creditors may exercise this right, nor may it be exercised against any of the debtors, except to the extent of the share belonging to the creditor or the share incumbent upon the debtor under that obligation

2) that which pertains to placing each of the debtors on notice or attributing fault to him, for the notice and the attribution of fault shall be effected in respect of each debtor separately

3) that which relates to assessing the grounds of nullity which may be personal to each party concerned in the obligation

4) that which pertains to the acts that interrupt the operation of prescription and the causes that suspend its running.

Solidarity among creditors exists when two or more persons are the holders of a single debt, each of whom is entitled to demand payment of this debt in its entirety, just as, on the other hand, the debtor is entitled to pay the debt to any one of them; this is what is called solidarity of creditors

However, a joint and several creditor is not entitled to dispose of the totality of the debt, but is deemed to hold a mandate from the rest of the creditors to preserve the portion that exceeds the amount of his share, and to collect it from the debtors.
Solidarity among creditors is not presumed; rather, it must arise from a legal act, from the law, or from the nature of the transaction.

A joint and several obligation is extinguished towards all the creditors by performance, by giving in payment, by deposit of the thing due, by set-off, or by novation made towards one of the creditors

A debtor who pays to one of the joint and several creditors his share in the obligation is discharged towards the others to the extent of this share.

The remission of the debt by one of the joint and several creditors does not bind the others and discharges the debtor only from the share of that creditor

And the merger of the capacities of creditor and debtor in the person of one of the joint and several creditors and in the person of the debtor extinguishes the obligation only with respect to this creditor.

Prescription completed against the right of one of the joint and several creditors does not run against the others, and the fault or delay of one of the joint and several creditors does not prejudice the remaining creditors.
If one of the creditors places the debtor on notice or causes interest to run on the debt, the rest of the creditors benefit from the result of his act.
An obligation is a legal bond which confers upon one or more natural or juristic persons the capacity of debtor towards one or more persons who are described as creditors.

A civil obligation is one the performance of which the creditor can compel from the debtor, and a natural obligation is a legal duty the performance of which cannot be demanded, provided that its voluntary performance shall have the same validity and effects as the performance of a civil obligation.
In the absence of a statutory provision, the judge may decide whether a moral duty constitutes a natural obligation or not, and a natural obligation may not be contrary to a rule of public law.
That which a person knowingly does in performance of a natural obligation may not be recovered and shall not be deemed a gratuitous act, but shall have the effect of payment.
A natural obligation shall not be extinguished by operation of set-off.
The acknowledgment of a natural obligation, even if express, shall not have the effect of converting it into a civil obligation. Such conversion may only arise from a novation of contract.
A natural debt may not be secured by a personal suretyship or by a pledge so long as it remains a natural debt.
Promises made to ensure the performance of a natural obligation shall be subject, as to form and substance, to the provisions governing contracts for valuable consideration.
A creditor who consents to the division of the debt in favour of one of the debtors retains the right to claim the whole debt against the others, unless the contrary is stipulated.

A compromise concluded between the creditor and one of the obligors operates for the benefit of the others if it includes the remission of the debt or another form of release, and it neither binds them nor prejudices their position if they have not consented to it.
The merger of the capacities of creditor and debtor in the person of the creditor and the person of one of the debtors extinguishes the obligation only in respect of the share of that debtor.

A judgment rendered against one of the joint and several debtors does not have the authority of res judicata with regard to the other debtors; whereas a judgment rendered in favour of one of the debtors operates for the benefit of the others unless it is based on a ground personal to the debtor who obtained the judgment. The causes that suspend the running of prescription may remain personal and specific to one of the creditors, whereas the causes that interrupt prescription with regard to one of the joint and several debtors interrupt it also with regard to the others.

Where solidarity exists among the debtors, each of them may discharge all

the others:

1) By paying the debt in full

2) By effecting set-off of a debt owed to him by the creditor against the whole debt

3) By undertaking the obligation alone in place of the remaining debtors

4) By taking the oath, where applicable, as to Whether any debt is due

5) By obtaining from the creditor the remission of the whole debt.
Each of the joint and several debtors is liable only for his own act in the performance of the obligation. Formal notice served upon one of them does not produce its effect against the others.

A joint and several obligation is divided by operation of law with regard to the relations of the debtors

among themselves; as between themselves, each of them is bound only in proportion to his share.

The shares for which the debtors are bound pursuant to the preceding paragraph are equal, except in the following cases:

1) Where the contract expressly provides for the contrary

2) Where the interests of the debtors are unequal.

If the interest in the debt belongs to one of the debtors alone, the others must be considered as sureties in their relation to him.

Where a debtor in a joint and several obligation has paid the whole debt, he has a right of recourse against the other debtors for that which exceeds his share. He may then bring his personal action or the action which the creditor was entitled to bring, together with the securities attached thereto, where applicable. However, whatever the action he brings, he is not entitled to claim from each debtor anything other than the share which that debtor must ultimately bear.

Where there exists a joint and several obligation among the debtors, all of them shall be bound for the same thing, albeit by virtue of distinct and mutually independent bonds, particularly with regard to:

1- The validity of such bonds

2- Their maturity

3- Their extinction
Each of the joint and several debtors shall be entitled to plead the grounds of defence personal to him and those common to all the debtors.

The grounds of defence personal to each of the debtors are those which may be pleaded by one or several of them, and in particular:

1- Grounds giving rise to annulment (duress, fraud, mistake and incapacity), whether personal to one of the debtors or to some of them

2- The modality (term or condition) which does not apply to that to which all have bound themselves.

3- Grounds of extinction of the obligation which have not occurred with respect to all.

The common grounds of defence are those which may be pleaded by all the debtors under the joint and several obligation, and they are in particular:

1- Grounds of nullity (such as an unlawful object or the absence of the formalities required by law, etc.) which apply to that to which all have bound themselves

2- The modality (term or condition) applying to that to which all have bound themselves

3- Grounds of extinction which have resulted in the extinction of the debt with respect to all.
Payment, performance in lieu of payment, deposit of the thing due, or set-off effected between one of the debtors and the creditor, shall all discharge the remaining obligors.
Default of the creditor in respect of one of the obligors shall operate to the benefit of the others as to its effects.

Novation of the obligation between the creditor and one of the obligors shall discharge the others unless the latter consent to be bound by the new obligation. However, where the creditor has stipulated the acceptance of the debtors and the latter refuse, the former obligation shall not be extinguished.

Remission of the debt in favour of one of the joint and several debtors shall operate to the benefit of the remaining obligors, unless the creditor has declared that he intends to remit the debt solely in favour of that debtor and to the extent of his share thereof. In such case, the other debtors shall only benefit to the extent of the share of the discharged debtor.

If there is among the joint and several debtors one or more persons who are absent or insolvent, their shares of the debt shall be borne by the debtors who are present and solvent in proportion to the share of the debt that each of them is bound to bear, all of the foregoing in the absence of a provision to the contrary.
Joint and several liability ceases when the creditor waives it.

The waiver of joint and several liability shall be either general and encompassing all the debtors, or personal to one or more of them. If the waiver encompasses all the debtors, the obligation shall be divided among them in the same manner as a conjunctive obligation is divided; and if the waiver is personal and restricted to one or more of the debtors, the creditor may only claim from those in respect of whom he waived the joint and several liability their respective shares, whereas he shall be entitled to sue the remaining debtors jointly and severally for the entire amount of the debt. And if it happens that one of the debtors not encompassed by the waiver of joint and several liability becomes insolvent, the remaining debtors, including those who benefited from such waiver, shall bear the discharge of the share of the debt due by him.
An obligation is successive if the performance of its object is not effected by a single act all at once, but is effected by abstention, or by a continuous act, or by a series of acts.
A positive obligation is one in which the debtor is bound to give something or to do something.
An obligation to give is one whose object is either the payment of a sum of money or other fungible things, or the creation of a real right.
An obligation to give transfers of right the right of ownership of the thing if it is an ascertained movable corporeal thing.
If the object of the obligation to give is the creation of an immovable real right, its holder shall have the right of registration in the Land Register.
The election shall be effected by merely notifying the other party, and when it is effected, the thing chosen shall be deemed as though it were the object of the obligation originally.

However, where the obligation has alternative objects falling due for performance at periodic terms, the election of one of them at one term shall not prevent the holder of the right from electing another at another term, unless the contrary is inferred from the constituent instrument, established custom, or what is presumed to be the intention of the two parties.

Where the party who has the right of election dies before making the election, his right shall pass to his heirs, and where he is declared insolvent, the right of election shall pass to the body of creditors; and where the heirs or the creditors do not agree, the other party may request that a time-limit be fixed for them so that, if it expires, the right of election shall pass to that party.

The debtor shall be discharged by performing one of the things promised, but he cannot compel the creditor to accept a part of one thing and a part of another; and the creditor is only entitled to demand the performance of one of the things in its entirety, and he cannot compel the debtor to perform by delivering a part of one and a part of another.
Where one of the objects alone is capable of performance, the obligation shall be or shall become a simple obligation.
An alternative obligation shall lapse where all the objects of the obligation become impossible at the same time without fault on the part of the debtor and before his default.

Where all the objects of the obligation become impossible at the same time through the fault of the debtor or after his default, the creditor may claim from him the price of whichever of those objects he elects.

Where the debtor refuses to make the election, or where there are several debtors who have not agreed upon the election, the creditor shall be entitled to request the judge to fix a time-limit for them and to designate the thing that must be performed if they do not make the election within this time-limit.

Where the choice belongs to the creditor and he is in default in making it, the other party shall have the right to request that a sufficient time limit be fixed for the creditor to enable him to decide the matter, and if the time limit expires before his choice is made, this right shall pass to the debtor.

Where, in the case referred to in the preceding Article, the performance of one of the objects of the obligation becomes impossible through the fault of the debtor or after his default, the creditor shall have the right to demand the object which has remained possible or the payment of an indemnity proportionate to the damage resulting from the impossibility of performing that object.

Where the performance of one of the objects of the obligation becomes impossible through the fault of the creditor, he shall be deemed to have chosen that object and may not demand the objects which have remained possible.

An obligation is facultative when one single thing is due to be performed whilst conferring upon the debtor the right to discharge himself by performing another thing. The thing due to be performed is, in the eyes of the law, the object of the obligation by which its nature is determined, and not the other thing by the performance of which the debtor is able to discharge himself.

A facultative obligation shall be extinguished if the thing which constitutes its object perishes without fault on the part of the debtor and before his default, and it shall not be extinguished if the thing the delivery of which was made optional perishes.

An obligation is indivisible:

First- By reason of the nature of the object, when it is a thing or an act that is not susceptible of material or intellectual division

Second- By virtue of the instrument creating the obligation or by virtue of the law, when it is inferred from the instrument or from the law that the performance of the obligation may not be partial.

Where there are several debtors in an indivisible obligation, each of them may be compelled to discharge the whole, provided that he has a right of recourse against the remaining debtors. This rule shall apply to the heirs of the person who contracted such an obligation, as the rule of hereditary division does not hold good therein, contrary to a joint and several debt, and the recourse against the rest of the debtors shall be exercised either by bringing a personal action or by bringing the action which belonged to the creditor together with the securities attached thereto.

Where there are several creditors in an indivisible obligation and there is no joint and several liability among them, the debtor may pay only to all the creditors together. None of those creditors may demand performance save in the name of all and with an authorisation from them; provided that each creditor may, for the account of all, demand the deposit of the thing due, or its delivery to a custodian appointed by the court if that thing is not susceptible of deposit.
The obligation to give also includes the duty to deliver the thing and to preserve it until its delivery if it is a specific thing.
An obligation to do is one in which the debtor is bound to perform an act, and in particular to effect a delivery.
A negative obligation is one the object of which is to abstain from an act.

Personal obligations are those to which the debtor is personally bound and which are consequently secured by the entirety of his patrimony. Real obligations are those in which the debtor is neither personally bound nor answerable for them with the entirety of his patrimony, but is bound in his capacity as the holder of certain things or property and is answerable for the obligation with them alone.
Obligations having multiple objects are conjunctive, alternative, or facultative,
A conjunctive obligation is one the object of which comprises several things due together, such that the debtor is not discharged except by performing all of them.
Conjunctive obligations are subject to the provisions governing simple obligations.

An alternative obligation is one the object of which comprises several things, the performance of one of which wholly discharges the debtor, and the right of election belongs to the debtor alone unless there is a provision to the contrary.

A debtor of an indivisible debt who is sued for the entirety of the obligation may request a time limit to join the remaining debtors in the action in order to prevent judgment being rendered against him alone for the entirety of the debt. However, if the debt can only be recovered from the debtor who is sued, judgment may be rendered against him alone, and he shall then have a right of recourse against the rest of his co-heirs or co-debtors in the obligation in proportion to the share of each of them.

The interruption of prescription by one of the creditors in an indivisible obligation shall benefit the others, just as its interruption against one debtor shall be effective against the rest of the debtors; likewise, the causes suspending prescription shall apply in their effect to all.
All obligations not provided for in the first and second paragraphs of Article seventy are divisible.

A divisible obligation must be performed as between the creditor and the debtor as if it were indivisible, and divisibility shall only be taken into consideration where there are several creditors each of whom can only claim his share of the divisible debt, or where there are several debtors each of whom is only bound for a part of the debt; the same rule shall apply to heirs, who may neither claim nor be sued for other than the share accruing to them or incumbent upon them of the debt of the estate.

A debt that is divisible among the debtors shall not be divided:

First- When the object of the obligation is the delivery of a specific thing identified in itself that is in the possession of one of the debtors

Second- When one of the debtors is solely charged with the performance of the obligation, either pursuant to the instrument creating it or pursuant to a subsequent contract.

In both cases, the debtor in possession of the thing or charged with performance may be sued for the entirety of the debt, and he shall, where applicable, have a right of recourse against his co-debtors.

The interruption of prescription, in the cases set forth in the preceding Article, against the debtor who may be sued for the whole of the debt, shall extend in its effects to the rest of the obligors.

Where two obligations exist, one of them is deemed principal and the other accessory if the first serves as the basis for the second, particularly in the following:

First- When one of the two obligations is a legal consequence of the other, such as the obligation to compensate for damage resulting from the non-performance of a prior obligation

Second- When one of the two obligations is contracted in consideration of the other obligation (such as a penalty clause, a suretyship, or a pledge).

The accessory obligations set forth in the second paragraph of the preceding Article shall lapse with the principal obligation by reason of being linked to it, unless otherwise provided by law or by the agreement of the two parties.

If the party who has reserved to himself the right of rescission becomes insane or loses legal capacity for another reason, the court shall, at the request of the other party or any other interested person, appoint a special guardian for that purpose, who shall decide, with the authorisation of the court, whether there is ground to accept the contract or to rescind it as the interest of the incapacitated person requires; in the case of bankruptcy, however, the guardianship shall be assumed as of right by the bankruptcy trustee or another representative of the body of creditors.

If an obligation is contracted subject to the condition that a certain event occur within a specified time, that condition shall be deemed unfulfilled if that time has elapsed without the event having occurred, and the court may not in any case grant an extension of the time-limit in this event; if no term has been fixed, the fulfilment of the condition may take place at any moment and it shall not be deemed unfulfilled unless it has become certain that the event will not occur.

If a legally permissible obligation is contracted on the condition that a certain event not occur within a specified time, that condition shall be deemed fulfilled if that time has elapsed without the event having occurred, or if before the specified term it has become certain that it will not occur. If there is no specified time, the condition shall only be fulfilled once it has become certain that the event will not occur.

A condition the fulfilment of which depends upon the participation of a third party in the act or upon an act of the creditor shall be deemed unfulfilled if the third party refuses to participate or the creditor fails to perform the specified act, even if the impediment does not depend upon his will.
A condition shall be deemed fulfilled when the debtor bound under a conditional obligation has wrongfully prevented the occurrence of the event or is in default in accomplishing it.
A fulfilled condition shall have no effect if the event was brought about by fraud on the part of the person in whose interest it was that the event should occur.

An obligation contracted under a suspensive condition is not susceptible of compulsory execution or voluntary execution, nor does prescription run against it so long as the condition remains pending; however, the creditor may perform conservatory acts, in particular the registration of the mortgage securing his debt where appropriate, an application for verification of handwriting, the affixing of seals, and the drawing up of records and inventories.
An obligation contracted under a suspensive condition in which the condition remains pending may be assigned by particular title or by universal title.

A condition is a future and uncertain event upon which the creation or extinction of an obligation depends, and it has a retroactive effect unless the contrary results from the intention of the two parties or from the nature of the obligation. In the first case referred to in the preceding paragraph, it is called a suspensive condition, and in the second case it is named a resolutory condition. A past or present event, even if unknown to the two parties, is not deemed a condition within the meaning intended in this article.

The stipulation of an impossible thing or one contrary to good morals or to the law is void and renders void the agreement dependent thereon. The fact that the condition subsequently becomes possible from a material aspect or a legal aspect does not render the agreement valid. However, the matter shall be otherwise, that is, the impossible or illicit condition shall be deemed as if not written, if the two parties did not attribute a decisive importance to it and it did not have in the contracting the status of the motivating cause inducing the creation of the obligation.

Every condition which tends to restrict or prevent the exercise of the rights appertaining to every person, such as the exercise of his rights as to marriage or his civil rights, is void. However, this provision does not apply to the case where one of the two parties restrains himself from exercising a certain industry or profession for a specified time or in a limited place. As for the condition of remaining in widowhood, it is valid if there exist legitimate reasons justifying it. And the right to assess them belongs to the judge.

An obligation is void if its existence is made dependent upon the will of the obligor alone (which is the purely potestative condition). However, the two parties or one of them has the right to reserve to himself the right to declare within a specified period that he wishes to maintain the contract or rescind it, and this reservation may not be stipulated in the acknowledgment of a debt, nor in a gift, nor in the remission of a debt, nor in a forward sale (salam).

If the period is not specified in the case provided for in the preceding article, each party may require the other party to declare his decision within a sufficient period. If the period expires and that party has not declared his wish to rescind the contract, the contract becomes final as from the date of its conclusion. And if he clearly declares to the other party his wish to rescind the contract, the agreement is deemed never to have existed.

If the party who reserved to himself the right of rescission dies before the expiry of the period without having expressed his intention, his heirs shall have the right to maintain the contract or rescind it within the time that remained to their decedent. And if the heirs disagree, those who wish to maintain the contract cannot compel the others to accept it, but they may take the entire contract for their own account.

The period of the term shall commence from the date of the contract if the two parties or the law have not appointed another date. As for obligations arising from a delict or quasi-delict, the period of the term shall commence from the date of the judgment that fixes the compensation due by the debtor.
The day which marks the beginning of the duration of the term shall not be counted, and a term calculated in days shall end upon the expiry of the last day of the duration of the term.
And if it is calculated in weeks, months, or years, maturity shall occur on the day corresponding, by name or by its order in the week, month, or year, to the day on which the contract was concluded.
If maturity falls on a legal holiday, it shall be postponed to the following day that is not a holiday.

A suspensive term is either legal or granted; a legal term is that which is established in the act creating the obligation or in a subsequent act, or derived from the law, and a granted term is that which is granted by the judge.
A legal term is either express or implied: it is express if it is expressly stipulated, and implied if it is inferred from the nature of the obligation.

A suspensive term is not limited to rendering the obligation not due for performance, but also prevents prescription from running against it for as long as the term has not fallen due. However, if the obligation has been performed, there shall be no ground for the restitution of what was not due.
A suspensive term is established in favour of the debtor unless the contrary is inferred from the circumstances, from the text of the contract or its nature, or from the law.

The obligor under a suspensive condition may not, prior to the fulfilment of such condition, perform any act which would prevent the exercise of the creditor's rights or render the same more difficult in the event that the condition is fulfilled, and after the suspensive condition is fulfilled, the acts performed by the obligor in the interim shall be annulled to the extent that they prejudice the creditor, save for rights lawfully acquired by a third party in good faith.
