With respect to goods subject to specific duties, the duty shall be levied on the basis of the quantities, number and units of measurement declared upon removing such goods from the free zone, provided that the provisions referred to in the last paragraph of Article 230 are observed.

Residence, the consumption of goods, and the retail sale thereof shall be prohibited in the free zones except in the following case: All vessels may equip themselves from the free zone with all marine equipment, fixed and movable, that they require. All vessels, whether national or foreign, steam-powered or motor-powered, the net registered tonnage of which exceeds one hundred and fifty marine tons, and which pass through a port having a free zone, may also provision themselves therefrom with the various foodstuffs and consumable materials required for their propelling machinery. The Customs Service shall grant provisioning licences pursuant to a special declaration submitted by the concerned parties.

The body charged with operating the free zone must furnish a guaranteed undertaking to the Customs Administration to abide, insofar as it is concerned, by the obligations set forth in Article 227. The instrument of establishment shall determine the extent of liability incumbent upon this body in the event that its officers become aware of contraventions of the provisions of Article 219 without notifying the Administration thereof.

The manifests or summary documents pertaining to foreign goods entering the free zone are specified in Article 90, whereas national goods or goods having acquired this status entering the free zone shall be subject to the lodging of a customs declaration. There shall be levied on such goods: 1- All duties, customs and otherwise, payable in the event of the return of the goods to the customs territory, 2- The exit duty that may be payable in the event of exportation.

Entry into free zones is prohibited for prohibited or monopolised goods, with the exception of tobacco and tombac in their forms imported by the Regie Administration and remaining in its possession, as well as tombac imported by individuals or companies under the conditions and reservations determined by the Customs Administration. Obtaining the special licence necessary for importing explosive-like materials or hazardous materials into Lebanon and for manufacturing or storing these materials remains mandatory in the free zone. Putrid or inflammable materials may not be introduced into free zones except under the conditions mentioned in the decision establishing the zone fulfilling the requirements of public security and health. The introduction of weapons and ammunition, of whatever kind, into free zones is strictly prohibited.

The legislation in force relating to the protection of commercial, industrial, literary, artistic, and musical property shall apply and remain applicable in free zones. Upon removal, products that have undergone transformation in the free zone must bear, visibly and indelibly, the phrase: "Free Zone of...".

The status of the free zone does not require, in principle, within the boundaries constituting this zone, any action by the Customs Administration, other than actions relating to the inspection for goods prohibited from being introduced therein in accordance with Article 219 and to the compilation of trade statistics. Officials of the Customs Administration are entitled to enter the free zone at any time whatsoever and to move freely therein. If the concerned parties petition the Customs Administration to carry out operations on goods placed in a free zone, the Administration shall carry out the said operations if they are regular, applying its tariffs or requiring the completion of every formality or the provision of guarantees in accordance with its regulations, such as guaranteed bonds of undertaking or guaranteed undertakings, lead-sealing, sealing, escorting the goods, etc...

Goods may not be landed from the sea into the free zone or introduced therein except with an authorisation from the body entrusted with operating this zone and subject to compliance with the provisions of this Decision. Furthermore, imported foreign goods may not be dispatched to a free zone located in an inland city except under the guarantee of guaranteed bonds of undertaking.

Goods coming from the free zone may not be shipped by sea or loaded except with an authorisation from the body entrusted with operating this zone and provided that, where applicable, the formalities referred to in Articles 224 and 225 are completed.

Goods may not be deposited in the free zone except on condition that they are entered in the entry and exit registers, drawn up in accordance with the forms accepted by the Customs Administration, kept by the depositors or owners of the goods, and containing all the particulars of the manifests provided for in Article 90 and all other particulars capable of facilitating the identification of the goods. These registers must always be at the disposal of the officers of the Customs Administration charged with verifying that the free zone is operating within the regulatory conditions. The Customs Administration shall, for its part, by way of supervision and for the purpose of compiling trade statistics, keep entry and exit registers corresponding to the aforementioned registers.

Foreign goods which have acquired national status by their disciplining of the customs duties and which enter the free zone for the operations authorised therein may not benefit, within the conditions referred to in the customs regulations, from the refund of the customs duties levied thereon upon importation, unless the goods are actually re-exported to a foreign country within a period of two years at most.

The penalties applicable with respect to the conduct of operations in the free zones are specified in Article 358. In general, customs offences committed on the occasion of the conduct of operations in the free zones shall be subject to the penalties provided for in Chapter Seven of Title Eight below, subject to observance of the limits imposed by Articles 214 to 229 on the intervention of the Customs Administration.

Foreign products subject to customs duties or to other duties the collection of which is entrusted to the Customs Department, which are intended to be manufactured or to have their work completed in Lebanon by the addition of manual labour thereto, and the owners of which undertake to re-export them or to place them in a bonded warehouse or in a free zone within a specified period of six months in principle, and after fulfilling the formalities and conditions imposed by the Customs Administration, may be temporarily admitted free of duties by virtue of administrative orders from the Higher Council of Customs published in the Official Gazette; by way of derogation from the provisions contained in the preceding paragraph, the Higher Council of Customs may, exceptionally and in the economic interest of the country, grant the status of temporary admission by virtue of special administrative orders published in the Official Gazette, to certain foreign products exempt from customs duties or from other duties the collection of which is entrusted to the Customs Department. The beneficiary of the status of temporary admission must participate in bearing the supervision expenses of the Customs Department by paying a lump sum determined by the Higher Council of Customs upon the proposal of the Director General of Customs, paid in advance and subject to annual revision, which varies in proportion to the importance of the goods accepted under this status and to the general expenses caused to the Customs Department by the operations required of it. The administrative orders taken by the Higher Council of Customs in this respect shall designate the industries benefiting from this status and the nature of their manufactures or the transformations they carry out, and shall determine the royalty payable annually thereon.

However, the Customs Administration may grant authorisations for temporary admission in the following cases: - applications for the admission of supplies for works, trials or tests, - applications for admission of a personal and exceptional nature not susceptible of generalisation, - applications for the admission of sacks and wrappings to be filled.

The importation of products temporarily admitted free of duties requires the signing of guaranteed bonds of undertaking comprising the guarantees determined by the Customs Administration. This importation entails the completion of the same formalities of the detailed declaration, in the form of the aforementioned guaranteed bonds of undertaking, and the inspection formalities provided for in Article 96 and the articles following it and in Article 120 and in the articles following it.
By virtue of an authorisation from the Customs Administration, products temporarily admitted may be placed into home consumption in accordance with the conditions of the tariff.

The offices of entry for products admitted temporarily duty-free, the offices of exit for products re-exported in discharge of temporary admission accounts, the rates of yield of manufactured products and the rates of their waste, the conditions for controlling and supervising operations where necessary, and all special measures relating to the products benefiting from this regime, shall be determined by the Customs Administration.

Any deficiency appearing upon the settlement of temporary admission accounts shall be subject to the payment of import duties. The contraventions committed on the occasion of the application of the temporary admission regime are defined by Article 358.

The Customs Administration shall determine the conditions for the temporary importation of articles of any kind whatsoever belonging to persons coming to Lebanon for temporary residence, provided that these same articles are re-exported within a period fixed, in principle, at one year. Failure to re-export the temporarily imported articles within the prescribed period and conditions shall entail the application of the penalties provided for in Article 358.

Owners of motor vehicles whose principal place of residence is outside Lebanon and who are affiliated to touring associations approved by the Customs Administration may benefit, in respect of their motor vehicles, from the regime of temporary importation free of duties, subject to the following conditions and reservations. Approved touring associations are authorised to substitute their liability for the liability of their members, as security for the payment of the duties payable, where applicable, on motor vehicles that may not be re-exported within the period fixed in Article 237. The undertaking given by these associations shall be guaranteed, vis-a-vis the Customs Administration, by the Automobile and Touring Club of Lebanon by means of a general bond deposited with the Customs Administration.

Motor vehicles shall be imported under this regime by virtue of special documents called "triptyque" or "carnet de passages" issued by the associations concerned. "Triptyques" or "carnets de passages" shall be valid for a period of one year starting from the date of their issue and for an unlimited number of journeys during this period, the "triptyque" regime shall apply to motor vehicles, to motor tricycles, and to motorcycles with or without a sidecar.

Tourists benefiting from the "triptyque" or "carnet de passages" regime shall be required to pay customs duties on liquids intended for generating motive power, with the exception of the remainder of the fuel supply contained in the normal tanks of the vehicles.

Spare rubber tyres, both outer covers and inner tubes, with the exception of two outer covers and two inner tubes for each vehicle, which are admitted under the temporary importation regime free of duties as of right, shall be clearly entered on the "triptychs" or "carnets de passages". Searchlights, lanterns, acetylene generators, and other spare accessories shall also be admitted under this regime. Any of these items that are not re-presented to the Customs Service upon departure from the country shall be subject to the payment of duties.
The conditions for the practical application of the "triptych" or "carnet de passages" regime shall be determined by the Customs Administration.

Foreign motor vehicles that carry out the transport of passengers and goods between foreign countries and Lebanon may be admitted exempt from duties under the temporary admission regime, subject to reciprocity, provided that the reservations determined by the Customs Administration are observed.

The foreign motor vehicles referred to in Article 243 and foreign motor vehicles intended for repair in Lebanon shall be subject, with regard to the payment of duties on fuels and spare parts, to the provisions of Articles 240 and 241. These motor vehicles are prohibited from carrying out any transport whatsoever within Lebanese territory during their stay in that territory, under pain of the penalties provided for in Article 363, No. 3.

Goods returned to the country of origin or of provenance for reasons considered acceptable by the Customs Administration shall benefit from a refund of the duties collected upon entry, under the conditions determined by the said Administration. In principle, the time limit for re-exportation shall be fixed at three months, calculated from the date of lodging the import declaration.

Foreign goods that have not been subjected to the payment of customs duties and that have not been placed under one of the duty-suspension regimes provided for in the preceding Articles may be re-exported directly abroad or transshipped from the vessel on which they were imported to another vessel bound for abroad or for another port in Lebanon, subject to the provision of the special guarantees or undertakings determined by the Customs Administration and provided for in particular in Article 171. The formalities for the declaration and examination of goods re-exported or transshipped from vessel to vessel shall, in principle, be the same formalities provided for in Article 96 et seq. and Article 120 et seq.
Materials and articles imported for the Office of the President of the Republic or in his personal name shall be exempt from customs duties.

1- The United Nations Organization shall be exempted from customs duties imposed on import or export in respect of articles imported or exported by it for its official use, provided that the articles thus exempted shall not be sold in Lebanon except after payment of the duties imposed thereon under the regulatory conditions and after the approval of the competent authority. 2- The representatives of Members to the principal and subsidiary organs of the United Nations and to conferences convened by the United Nations shall, while exercising their functions and during their journey to and from the place of meeting, and in respect of their personal baggage exclusively, enjoy the same immunities and facilities as are accorded to diplomatic envoys. The expression "representatives of Members to the United Nations Organization" shall be understood to mean delegates, deputy delegates, advisers, technical experts and secretaries of delegations. 3- Officials of the United Nations Organization shall have the right to import their furniture free of duty at the time of first taking up their post, provided that they shall be subject to the regulations in force in the event of the disposal of such furniture in whole or in part.

All items imported in accordance with the provisions of Article 263 of this Law in the name of the representatives of foreign States mentioned below and intended strictly for their personal use or for the use of members of their families shall be exempted from customs duties and from the procedures of opening and inspection: a- The head of the diplomatic mission, counsellors, secretaries and attachés who belong to the diplomatic corps. b - Technical attachés nominated by the head of the mission and accepted by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Lebanon. c- Consuls-general, consuls and vice-consuls, provided that the number of those among them who benefit from the exemption shall not exceed two in the capital and one in other cities. Provided that each of the persons mentioned above shall only benefit from the exemption in respect of a single motor vehicle, with the exception of the head of the mission, who may import more than one motor vehicle on condition that they are his private property.

New personal effects, furniture and household appliances arriving for diplomatic and consular officials who do not enjoy customs exemption shall also be exempted from customs duties, in accordance with the following conditions: 1- That the importation has taken place within three months as of the arrival of the exemption applicant in Lebanon, and this period may be extended in certain special circumstances the right to assess which is left to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, provided that the additional period does not exceed six months. 2- That the exemption application is accompanied by the approval and certification of the head of the diplomatic or consular mission.

The following shall be exempted from customs duties in accordance with the first and second paragraphs of Article 263: First- Motor vehicles intended for the official use of legations, the number of which is fixed at two, and this number may be increased by a decision of the Higher Council of Customs taken upon the proposal of the Minister of Foreign Affairs and the approval of the Council of Ministers. Second- Building materials for the construction or restoration of legations, with the exception of materials of a kind produced in the country. Third- Cultural, scientific or social cinematographic films, provided that they are not screened in public or private halls for commercial exploitation, Fourth- Seals, official papers, flags, stationery, supplies and furniture of legations or consulates, and imported medals and insignia, provided that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs determines the scope of application of this Article.

Ammunition, weapons, equipment, means of transport and clothing (with the exception of foodstuffs) imported for the Army, the Gendarmerie, the Police and General Security shall be exempted from customs duties.

Building materials, supplies for fitting out and maintaining buildings, mechanical supplies, engines, machinery, apparatus and tools of all kinds imported by the institutions referred to in Article 253 shall be exempted from customs duties, provided that the reservations, conditions and penalties provided for in Articles 26, 255 to 258, 262 and 263 are observed. The Director General of Customs shall be entrusted with granting the exemption, and the Higher Council of Customs shall have the right to examine objections submitted in this regard.

For the purpose of applying Article 254, applications for exemption shall be submitted to the Director General of Customs, who is charged with conducting the investigation in respect thereof and deciding on the possibility of their acceptance, and such applications must be accompanied by all information, invoices, designs, contracts, plans and measurements deemed necessary.

The duties due on privileged imports must, as a general rule, be secured by deposit in the customs fund. However, the Customs may accept, in lieu of the deposit, a guarantee of a bank approved in advance by the competent Head of Customs Control, whenever the value of the liquidated duties exceeds one thousand Lebanese pounds, or the lodging of an undertaking from the beneficiary foreign institution transmitted to the Customs by the consul of such institution.

The refund of duties deposited by way of security (or, where applicable, the cancellation of the bank guarantee) shall not be effected until after the Ministry of Public Works has supervised the use of the materials and supplies accepted for the benefit of the exemption. Five per cent of the value of the remitted customs duties shall be deducted in favour of the Treasury by way of expenses for this supervision.

(1)- The items, products, materials and supplies enumerated in Articles 253 and 254, which have in the domestic markets similar items or products from local agriculture or industry, may be excluded from the customs exemption by a mere administrative order from the Higher Council of Customs.

Private clinics, even if they are not among the institutions to which the provisions of Articles 253 and 254 apply, may benefit, in respect of the free beds therein, from the exemption provided for in paragraph (e) of Article 253, except with regard to apparatus for projecting fixed illuminated images, cinema apparatus, radio apparatus and their accessories, and cinematographic films.

For the purpose of applying Articles 253 and 259, the Customs Administration shall determine the conditions for drawing up applications for exemption and the undertakings and guarantees which must be submitted by the institutions concerned.

The following shall be admitted to benefit from exemption from customs duties: 1- Stationary pumps used for agriculture and their motors, and stationary motors intended for operating agricultural machinery that benefits from customs exemption, provided that the declaration for release for consumption states the name and address of the actual consignee, the place of installation of the imported apparatus, and the exact purpose of their use. 2- Tools, machinery, apparatus, materials, and products intended for agricultural use which are specified by the orders and decisions adopted by the Higher Council of Customs after taking the opinion of the competent ministry. These exemptions shall only be granted subject to observance of the provisions of Articles 26 and 262 and, where applicable, the special provisions specified by the administrative orders or decisions granting the exemption.

The customs exemptions granted pursuant to: Chapter Two - Section One - Exemptions pertaining to the Army and to the departments of the Gendarmerie, the Police, and General Security. And Chapter Three - Exemptions enjoyed by religious bodies, evangelical missions, educational institutions, and relief societies, and Chapter Four - Exemptions special to agriculture, shall only be granted if the goods subject thereto are imported from countries that benefit from the normal tariff or from countries that benefit from special tariff agreements. As for goods, of whatever kind they may be, imported by the beneficiaries mentioned above, they shall pay the duties of the maximum tariff if their origin is from other countries.

Exemption from customs duties shall be granted within the following general conditions and rules: 1- That the goods have been shipped under bills of lading to the order of the person benefiting from the exemption, or have been purchased in customs warehouses, real warehouses, private real warehouses, fictitious importers' warehouses, or in a free zone. 2- That Lebanese diplomatic representatives and consuls in the State to which the foreign diplomatic representative or consul benefiting from the exemption belongs enjoy the same customs exemption and facilities. 3- That the official who benefits from the customs exemption and facilities is devoted exclusively to his office, does not perform any other work, and does not engage in trade directly or indirectly. 4- Materials that benefit from exemption from customs duties shall be subject to all customs formalities and inspection unless expressly provided otherwise.

Exemption from customs duties shall be granted, within the conditions and subject to the reservations provided for in Articles 258 to 260, 262 and 263, for the goods and products restrictively listed below, which are imported by religious bodies, evangelical missions, educational institutes and relief institutions. A - Objects intended for performing religious rites in churches, temples, mosques, synagogues and other places dedicated to prayer: gifts sent by kings and heads of States, crosses, reliquaries of all kinds, decorated or undecorated, chalices, monstrances, ciboria, basins, ewers, censers, incense boats, wine and water cruets, trays and other vessels made of gold, silver or gilt silver, candlesticks - branched candlesticks - decorated or undecorated vases - artificial flowers - canopies - covers - altar linens - silk or cotton curtains and fabrics for decoration, silk - or silver - ribbons and fringes - pastoral staffs of all kinds - decorated or undecorated paintings. Sacerdotal and other vestments, ready-made or not ready-made, intended solely for religious service, carpets of wool or velvet or embroidered with gold and silver, chandeliers and lamps of silver, gilt silver, metal or crystal - gold and silver leaf - painting colours and pigments intended for decoration - painted or unpainted glass - candles, raw beeswax for making - candles - incense - rosaries - gold and silver icons - pictures - large and small statues, '' organs and harmoniums - liturgical music pieces - religious service books - prayer or hymnal books and, in general, all books intended for performing religious rites. B - Items and products imported by religious bodies and evangelical missions to secure the subsistence of their members: clothing items: ready-made clothes and clothing accessories (excluding furs and other precious trimmings) - headgear - footwear - soles and leather - knitted goods (Bonneterie) of wool or cotton - cotton clothes - kinds of ribbon, braid, threads and woven fabrics of silk, wool and cotton, necessary items and products: bedding supplies - glassware, earthenware, ceramics or enamelled ironware, for the table or for ornament - table knives, forks and spoons of base metal - kitchen supplies - household supplies - gardening tools - pulse and flower seeds - ordinary soap, food items: wheat flour - sugar - rice - coffee - tea, chicory - starch - spices - dried vegetables - potatoes - fats, butter, oils, pastes and preserved foods, cheese and table wine, stationery items: paper - lead pencils - nibs and penholders - ink - ordinary inkwells - paper envelopes. The value of the goods that may be exempted annually must not exceed 7000 L.P. for each person. '' C - Items and products imported by religious educational institutes (clerical schools and others) to secure the subsistence of their boarding students and for their education, or solely for the education of students whose subsistence they do not secure: the clothing items mentioned above in subparagraph B excluding silk ribbons, braid, threads and woven fabrics, the items and products necessary to secure subsistence mentioned above in subparagraph B, excluding table wine, the stationery items mentioned above in subparagraph B, the food products mentioned above in subparagraph B, school supply items: chalk - blackboards - geographical and other maps - books - phonograph records on which language or other lessons are recorded, special items and products: sports supplies - instruments and preparations for physics and chemistry laboratories - apparatuses for projecting fixed illuminated images - cinema apparatuses and their accessories - cinematographic films, provided that the importing institutions undertake in writing not to screen them and not to allow them to be screened in a public cinema hall. '' The value of the goods that may be exempted annually must not exceed 2500 L.P. for each boarding student or 1000 L.P. for each student whose subsistence the institution does not secure. D - Items and products imported by institutions of general, technical or vocational instruction for the education of their students, and institutions for the education and instruction of the blind or the deaf-mute: the stationery items mentioned above in paragraph B, the school supply items mentioned above in paragraph C, to which are added: colours and supplies for artistic painting, and in general all teaching and educational equipment expressly used by scientific institutes for the instruction of their students, including children's classes. The special items and products mentioned above in paragraph C, to which are added: musical instruments - collection objects intended for institutions containing a natural history museum - typewriters and duplicating machines and their accessories intended for institutions that give commercial lessons - wireless telegraphy and radio apparatuses - laboratory instruments and supplies, surgical and medical instruments, dental instruments and pharmaceutical preparations intended for technical education institutions - tableware and kitchen supplies, excluding those made of crystal, porcelain or precious metals, and household supplies intended for hotel vocational instruction and, in general, all special equipment of this kind necessary for such education. Special items, tools and products expressly intended for the education and instruction of the blind. '' Special items, tools and products expressly intended for the education of the deaf and mute. The value of the goods that may be exempted annually must not exceed 1500 L.P. for each student - in primary, secondary or vocational education institutions, 2500 L.P. in university institutions and 5000 L.P. in institutions for the education of the blind or the deaf-mute. E - Items and products imported by hospitals to secure the subsistence and treatment of patients: clothing items: knitted goods (Bonneterie) of wool or cotton, cotton clothes: wool or cotton threads - cotton fabrics, the items and products necessary to secure subsistence mentioned above in paragraph B, the food products mentioned above in paragraph B excluding table wine and with the addition of: cocoa - chocolate - sweets - biscuits - condensed milk, special product items: surgical and medical instruments - dental instruments - laboratory instruments and preparations - drugs - bandages, disinfecting preparations - alcohol -- feeding bottles, teats and rubber stoppers for feeding bottles, intended for maternity homes - apparatuses for projecting fixed illuminated images, cinema apparatuses and radio apparatuses and their accessories - cinematographic films, provided that the importing institutions undertake in writing not to screen them or allow them to be screened in a public cinema hall. The value of the goods that may be exempted annually must not exceed 20000 L.P. for each bed. The following shall benefit from these provisions: - Hospitals that belong to charitable or scientific institutions. - Private hospitals equipped with all modern technical installations and whose number of beds exceeds fifty beds, provided that they place at the disposal of the Ministry of Health and Public Relief, free of charge and on a permanent basis, a proportion of ten per cent of the number of beds. '' F - Items and products imported by dispensaries for the treatment of patients: items and products to secure subsistence: household supplies - ordinary soap, the special items and products mentioned above in paragraph E excluding apparatuses for projecting fixed illuminated images, cinema apparatuses, radio apparatuses and their accessories, and cinematographic films. The value of the goods that may be exempted annually must not exceed 4000 L.P. for each patient. G - Items and products imported by orphanages to secure the subsistence and instruction of the orphans in their care. The clothing items mentioned above in paragraph B excluding leather, soles and kinds of silk ribbon, braid, threads and woven fabrics, the items and products to secure subsistence mentioned above in paragraph B, the food products mentioned above in paragraph E, the stationery items mentioned above in paragraph B, the school supply items mentioned above in paragraph D. The special items and products mentioned above in paragraph C with the addition of: musical instruments - prizes for rewards (decorated books, frames, boxes and children's toys) - fine clothing patterns, samples for tapestry work and sewing supplies, all intended for girls' orphanages - tools and instruments for manual work intended for boys' orphanages. The value of the goods that may be exempted annually must not exceed 2500 L.P. for each orphan

H - Items and products imported by shelters to secure the subsistence of persons taking refuge therein: the clothing items mentioned above in paragraph G, the items and products to secure subsistence mentioned above in paragraph B, the food products mentioned above in paragraph E, the stationery items mentioned above in paragraph B. The value of the goods that may be exempted annually must not exceed 7000 L.P. for each person taking refuge. I - Items and products imported by relief institutions for distribution to those whom they relieve: the items mentioned above in paragraph G, the food products mentioned above in paragraph B excluding table wine and with the addition of condensed milk, special items and products: medicines - dressings - disinfecting preparations, feeding bottles and teats - and rubber stoppers for feeding bottles, intended for "Drop of Milk" (Goutte de Lait) institutions. The value of the goods that may be exempted annually must not exceed 6000 L.P. for each person to whom relief is provided. J - Raw materials imported by asylums for the blind to carry out special work performed by those sheltered therein: items necessary for making carpets and covers: cotton yarn No. 6, No. 6/20 and No. 9/20, items necessary for making furniture and baskets: rattan and cane - "raffia", Chinese grass - wood splints - - straw plait - "Malacca" - "Gorontalos" - wooden boards cut to size for table tops and basket bottoms - nails and screws - metal studs. Items necessary for making brushes and brooms: brush wood cut to size - bristles - fibres - couch grass (chiendent), rice straw and broom corn - (sorghum) - wooden rods for broomsticks - coarse threads. The value of the goods that may be exempted annually must not exceed 5000 L.P. for each blind person.

Shall be exempted from customs duties in the Normal Tariff, subject to observance of the undertakings, guarantees and formalities determined by the Customs Administration: - newsprint, intended for printing daily and weekly newspapers, - thin paper used for wrapping oranges, lemons, apples and pears, - paper called "Kraft paper" intended for making bags used for packing cement, yellow cement, asphalt, salts, fertilisers of animal origin and similar products, - ordinary or decorated paper cut in the shape of lozenges (Losanges) the side length of which does not exceed 100 centimetres and expressly intended for making envelopes. Proofs of use for the regulatory purposes must be submitted within a period not exceeding, in principle, six months as from the date of the guaranteed bond. The Customs Department shall enjoy the absolute right to carry out all verifications, which it deems necessary, in the establishments benefiting from the exemptions in order to ascertain that the paper imported free of duties has not been fraudulently diverted from the purpose for which it is intended.

By way of derogation from the provisions of Article 8, the following shall benefit from customs exemption in the Normal Tariff: A - fire pumps imported by the Government or the municipalities. B - tools and equipment of the N.B.T. (Naqoura - Beirut Tripoli) railway line which - the Government imports for the operation of this line, within the conditions determined by the Customs Administration. C - all motor vehicles, materials, supplies and tools donated to the Government by the various international organisations within the conditions determined by the Customs Administration. Furthermore, and subject to observance of the undertakings, guarantees and formalities determined by the Customs Administration, the scope of this exemption may be extended to include additional tools necessary for firefighting and rescue, and spare parts intended for regularly constituted fire brigades.

Foreign ancient antiquities missions may benefit from exemption, by administrative orders issued by the Director General of Customs, in respect of certain materials consumed in their works (photographic supplies, plaster, etc...).

The following shall be exempted from customs duties in the ordinary tariff: a- Aircraft of officially licensed national air navigation companies and spare parts pertaining to such aircraft. b - Equipment used on the ground of Lebanese airports and special apparatus and technical supplies used for the repair and maintenance of aircraft within the boundaries of such airports, imported by air navigation companies belonging to the States that signed the Convention on International Civil Aviation in Chicago dated 7 December 1944, for the establishment and operation of international air lines.
Where customs exemption is granted in the form of import documents, the Customs Administration shall determine the conditions for issuing and using such documents.

The following shall be admitted exempt from customs duties, within the conditions determined by the Customs Administration: 1- Clothing, articles of undergarments, baggage intended for personal use, wedding trousseaux and students' outfits, household tools, primaries and musical instruments, which are in use and correspond to the status of their owners, imported by nationals returning permanently to Lebanon or by foreigners coming to Lebanon to reside therein. 2- Samples having no commercial value.

The Customs Administration shall determine the conditions within which certain provisions or certain fuels consumed or taken on by warships, new motor vehicles passing in transit, dining coaches arriving from abroad, aircraft of official and regular national companies, and foreign aircraft on the basis of reciprocity may benefit from exemption where necessary.

The Customs Administration shall determine the conditions within which returned goods that are explicitly proven to be of Lebanese origin, and whose prior exportation is regularly proven and the date of which must not, in principle, go back more than two years, may benefit from exemption. This Administration shall also determine the conditions within which the same privilege may be granted, on an exceptional basis, to certain goods or packagings that have acquired national status through the payment of duties and that are re-imported within the same period, after their re-exportation abroad.
Violations of the provisions of Chapters Two, Three, Four, Six, Seven and Eight of this Title shall subject their perpetrators to the penalties provided for in Article 358.

Any goods delivered to the Customs Administration and placed in a warehouse within the customs precinct or in any other place of this precinct, shall be subject to the storage fee if the period of their remaining therein exceeds eight full days.

The tariff of the storage fee, which is collected by the Customs Administration when the concession for operating the customs stores is not granted to a concessionaire company, shall be determined as follows in Lebanese piastres and starting from the ninth day: A- For every one hundred kilograms for each week 25 L.P. 1- Any fraction of 100 kilograms shall pay the fee imposed on the one hundred kilograms, 2- Every week that begins shall incur the full fee, 3- Half of the fee shall be reduced if the storage is on open ground. B - If the period of storage subject to the fee exceeds 30 days, there shall be collected, in addition to the fees set forth above, for every 100 kilograms and for each day, whatever the place of storage may be L.P. 1- For the period of the first thirty days following the expiry of this time-limit 1 2- From the thirty-first day up to the sixtieth day 2 3- From the sixty-first day up to the ninetieth day 3 4- After the ninetieth day 4 As for the goods remaining in the stores and warehouses managed directly by the Customs, pursuant to a judicial receivership or an attachment ordered at the request of any person or administration other than the Customs, the amount of the storage fee in respect thereof shall be determined by the authority that ordered the judicial receivership or the attachment, taking into consideration therein the tariff mentioned above.

The following shall be exempted from the storage fee: 1- Packages in excess of the manifest which are unloaded in error at one of the ports and are intended for re-exportation. 2- Packages remaining as a result of judicial receivership or attachment ordered upon the request of the Customs Administration. 3- Packages unloaded in a condition of apparent damage, duly verified in accordance with the rules, within eight days starting from the date of their unloading. 4- Personal effects and used pieces of furniture belonging to any traveller who does not engage in trade, provided that such effects and furniture do not remain in Customs for more than 60 full days. If this period expires, the fees shall be levied in accordance with the rules starting from the sixty-first day. 5- Goods that were not withdrawn due to force majeure, the assessment of which shall remain the sole right of Customs. 6- Packages requested by their owners which could not be delivered due to congestion in the customs premises or due to an error in classification, solely for the period during which the location of these packages remained unknown. In this case, the owner of the packages shall request the customs officers to verify, on the very day on which the withdrawal request was submitted, that the location of the packages was indeed unknown. If only a part of these packages is missing, their owner must withdraw the existing packages after paying the imposed duties.
The period of eight full days, provided for in Article 273, shall be raised to 30 full days in respect of goods that are in transit and to 15 full days in respect of goods intended for exportation.

Packages left in the customs warehouses due to a dispute that arose between the consignor and the consignee and which are re-exported to the place of origin shall only be subject to the payment of storage fees for a maximum period of 90 full days.
In no case may the total value of the storage fees due exceed half the value of the goods, whether the fees are levied by the Customs Administration or by a concessionary company.

The special provisions, in force on the date of signature of this Decision, governing the rules for levying storage fees in certain customs offices, resulting from agreements concluded with concessionary companies, shall remain in force.

The price of the lead seals and stamps affixed by Customs shall include, in addition to the raw materials supplied, the price of the ropes and thick twine and the expenses of labour and of affixing the lead seals. The price of the lead seals is 20 L.P., whether the packages are sealed with lead package by package or their containers are sealed with lead as a whole.
Internal trade transactions, whether the goods pass through foreign territories or not, are exempted from the lead-sealing fee.
The fee for affixing seals is fixed at 5 L.P. for each seal or stamp.
The fee for animal buttons is fixed at 15 L.P. for each button.
The rate of the royalty for each operation of importing or exporting goods benefiting from a derogation from the provisions prohibiting importation or exportation is fixed in Article 43.
The tariff for every analysis or counter-analysis mentioned in Articles 128 and 131 shall be fixed by a decision of the Higher Council of Customs.
The tariff of sanitary fees applicable to certain live animals and animal products shall be fixed by a decision of the Higher Council of Customs.

There shall be levied, in addition to the customs duty, a specific fee of 30 L.P. for each pack of 32 and 36 cards and 50 L.P. for each pack of 52 cards, on playing cards imported from abroad. Importers are required to state specifically in their declarations the number of packs of each category contained in the packages for which a declaration is submitted. False declarations as to quantity shall be repressed by the application of the penalties prescribed in Article 358.

Internal duties and wharfage fees, established by decisions issued by the Higher Council of Customs or by legislation in force, shall be levied by the Customs Department on behalf of the Treasury or the municipalities to which these duties accrue, upon the importation of foreign goods subject thereto, and under the conditions specified by the decisions or regulations that established them.

Goods subject to the control of the customs zone may not be transported within this area except on condition that they are accompanied by a transport document (a guaranteed bond, a pass for domestic trade, a receipt, a third copy of the customs declaration, etc.) issued by the Customs Service under the conditions determined by it, subject to the provisions of Article 24 where applicable. This document shall specify, in particular, the time required to effect the transport and the route to be followed, and it shall state, where applicable, that it is valid for movement by night. This document must be produced upon every request by customs officers.

The possession of goods subject to the control of the customs zone may be restricted to certain places within this zone designated by administrative orders of the Higher Council of Customs published in the Official Gazette. Outside these places, the existence of any storehouse or warehouse for goods subject to the control of the customs zone is prohibited. Goods of this kind that are in large or small bales or in other packages and for which no valid transport document can be produced, or that are in excess of the normal requirements of trade, shall be deemed as being in a storehouse or warehouse.

When the necessities of supervision so require, an open account may be kept, at the customs offices located within the zone, in which every producer or merchant shall compulsorily register the quantities of grain or live animals that are in his possession, whether resulting from production or breeding, or from imports from abroad or arrivals from within Lebanese territory, provided that the Customs Service retains the right of verification. The Customs Service may carry out sudden inventories at the premises of the persons mentioned in the preceding paragraph. The rules for the practical application of the open account regime shall be determined by the Customs Administration.

Every irregular movement or possession in the customs zone of goods subject to the control of the zone, every movement not in compliance with the provisions of the transport document, and every unjustified surplus or deficit in the open account shall be deemed to constitute importation or exportation by way of smuggling and shall entail the application of the penalties provided for in Article 358.

The application of the regime of the customs zone and the control of the zone shall not introduce any modification to the status of the transit of goods and, in particular, to the special provisions provided for in the agreements concluded with neighbouring countries concerning transit trade with those countries.
The maritime customs zone and the control of the zone at sea are defined in Articles 69 to 74.

The remuneration for work provided by Customs officers on the occasion of their carrying out formalities on behalf of merchants and taxpayers outside the hours, places and conditions specified in the Customs regulations shall be determined by a decision of the Higher Council of Customs.

The remuneration of Customs officers commissioned by the interested parties, in accordance with Article 119, to draw up their declarations in places where there are no officially licensed customs brokers shall be determined as follows: 20 L.P. for each declaration if the value of the goods does not exceed 1000 L.P. 50 L.P. in all other cases.

Goods originating in Lebanon and goods that have acquired national status by payment of duties, dispatched by sea through coasting trade, shall not be subject to any duty upon entry or upon exit, provided that the formalities imposed in respect thereof by the Customs Administration are completed.

When goods are dispatched through coasting trade and are, upon exportation, prohibited or subject to the tariff, the undertakings, guarantees and formalities determined by the Customs Administration must be submitted or completed in respect thereof.

Declarations shall be drawn up in accordance with the rules designated in Article 96 and the articles following it. The inspection, which, in principle, is carried out only at the office of destination, shall be effected in accordance with the provisions of Article 120 and the articles following it.
The Customs Administration may deliver to merchants, at their request, certificates attesting the payment of customs duties or the completion of certain regulatory formalities.

The customs zone is the part of the Lebanese territory situated between the coasts or the land borders, on the one hand, and a line extending behind the first customs posts and offices situated on the coast or on the land borders, on the other hand, and this line shall be determined, in accordance with the requirements of supervision, by administrative orders of the Higher Council of Customs published in the Official Gazette. The Customs Administration shall take, within this zone, special measures to supervise the transport and possession of goods, and shall determine the manner of applying these measures, subject to compliance with the following provisions.
Prohibited goods and heavily taxed goods designated by administrative orders of the Higher Council of Customs published in the Official Gazette shall be subject to the control of the zone.

The contraventions provided for in this Resolution and in the texts relating to Customs may be established and give rise to seizure: 1- With regard to monopolised goods and prohibited goods or goods subject to customs duties or other duties: a- Within the precincts of customs premises and ports, and in general in all stores, warehouses and places, of whatever kind, subject to the supervision of the Customs Department or in which this Department has the right to carry out verifications. b - Throughout the maritime and land customs zone defined in Articles 69 to 74 and 295 to 302. c- Throughout the Lebanese territory when customs officers have pursued the smuggled goods continuously and within their sight, whether after having seen them entering this territory or after having seen them being extracted from the customs zone. d- Outside the coastal waters, when customs officers have pursued the smuggled goods within their sight, whether after having seen them leaving the territory or after having seen them being extracted from the land or maritime zone. 2- With regard to goods prohibited from transit or internal circulation or prohibited from being possessed or sold, or monopolised goods circulating or possessed irregularly: throughout the Lebanese territory. 3- With regard to prohibited goods or goods subject to heavy duties specifically designated by administrative orders of the Higher Council of Customs published in the Official Gazette, the possessors or carriers of which are unable to produce either a receipt proving their regular importation from abroad or an original invoice of purchase or any other proof of origin issued by an establishment regularly established in Lebanon, on the ground that goods in this situation are presumed to have been imported by way of smuggling: throughout the Lebanese territory.

Domiciliary investigations and searches for the purpose of uncovering smuggling may be carried out in Lebanese territory: 1- Throughout the customs zone defined in Articles 295 to 301 inclusive. 2- Throughout Lebanese territory: a- In respect of smuggled goods pursued within sight by customs officers, either after they saw them entering this territory or after they saw them being extracted from the customs zone, and provided they arrived at the time when such goods were brought into the dwellings. b - In respect of the goods referred to in sub-paragraphs 2 and 3 of the preceding Article. Where domiciliary investigations and searches are not based on a warrant of the Investigating Judge, they may only be carried out pursuant to an order of an officer of the higher cadre in the Customs and with the assistance of the Mukhtar or a member of the Police or Gendarmerie. Where the matter relates to an offence in flagrante delicto or to pursuits within sight, domiciliary searches and investigations shall not be subject to these formalities. The provisions laid down in this respect, in the decisions in force, concerning certain goods subject to special prohibitions, shall remain in effect. The right of inspection on board vessels, vested in customs officers, is defined in Articles 69 to 74.

Customs officers are entitled to circulate, when performing assigned service: 1- In public or state domains and village commons, adjacent to the maritime and land borders or situated on river banks at a distance of 500 metres from their mouth. 2- On railway lines situated at a distance from the maritime and land borders not exceeding 1000 metres. 3- On private properties not enclosed by a wall, adjacent to the land borders or situated on the shore bank or the high rocks alongside the sea or river banks up to 500 metres from their mouth. Owners adjacent to rivers and to borders may not erect any barrier preventing the freedom of passage of Customs officers along the land borders and on the sea shore or the high rocks alongside the sea and on river banks up to 500 metres from their mouth. Every resistance or opposition to the freedom of circulation of Customs officers and every infringement of the prohibitions and obligations resulting from this Article, shall be deemed an opposition during duty and prosecuted in accordance with Article 362.

Directors and inspectors of Customs, as well as officers, non-commissioned officers and guards, who are members of the public forces, are authorised to carry regulation weapons to perform the duties of office. Civil and military authorities are required to lend them assistance, and soldiers, the gendarmerie, the police or General Security must provide them with this assistance upon first request.

Customs officers shall receive, upon entering office, a commission of service granted by the Director General of Customs in accordance with a model determined by him. They must always carry this commission during the performance of their duties and produce it upon first request. Every Customs officer who leaves the service for any reason whatsoever (dismissal, placement on reserve, resignation, retirement, etc...) must immediately return to his direct superior his commission and the registers and articles with which he was equipped to perform his duty. If he fails to do so, the Regional Head of Customs is entitled to issue a writ of constraint against him in accordance with the conditions provided for in the third, fourth and sixth paragraphs of Article 156. This order shall be issued with a copy of the administrative order striking the officer off the establishment of the Administration, and in order for it to be served and enforced, it must be endorsed by the Single Judge in the district to the Customs centre of which the officer was attached when struck off the establishment.

Every person apprehended in flagrante delicto of smuggling shall be brought before the local Head of the Customs Service, who shall decide whether or not to place him under arrest. The conditions of such arrest are specified in Article 327. The following shall be deemed an act of smuggling for the implementation of the provisions laid down in this Article: 1- The importation or attempted importation, without a written or oral declaration, of monopolised goods, or goods that are prohibited or subject to restrictions upon importation or circulation, or heavily dutiable goods designated in administrative orders from the Higher Council of Customs published in the Official Gazette. 2- The exportation or attempted exportation, under the same conditions, of goods prohibited from being taken out or goods subject to restrictions upon circulation or exportation. 3- The transport of monopolised goods or goods prohibited from being brought in or taken out, whether or not listed in the manifest, on board vessels, whatever their flag, of a tonnage of less than 150 net register tons, anchored or cruising within the limits of twenty kilometres from the coasts, save in the case resulting from proven force majeure. 4- The stopping or cruising of vessels of a tonnage of less than 150 net register tons carrying heavily dutiable goods, designated in administrative orders from the Higher Council of Customs published in the Official Gazette, within the maritime zone, save in the case resulting from proven force majeure, or the re-exportation of goods of the same kind on board vessels of the same tonnage. 5- The irregular circulation or possession of animals or goods subject to zone policing within the customs zone.

Customs officers of the senior cadre shall have the right to request, at railway stations, to inspect papers and documents of whatever kind (waybills, invoices, loading sheets, ledgers, registers, etc..) relating to the transport and deposit of goods. Any refusal to hand over such documents shall be deemed to constitute obstruction in the performance of duty and shall be prosecuted in accordance with Article 362.

A- Customs officers of all grades shall, upon entering office, take the legal oath before the Single Judge in the district to which they have been appointed. There shall be stated in the commission given to them pursuant to the provisions of Article 309 the date on which they took the oath and the court before which the oath was taken. B - The oath shall remain valid and in force throughout the period during which the officer remains in service. There shall be no need to take a new oath if the officer interrupts service for a legitimate reason and then returns to it, or if he is transferred from one post to another post or from one district to another district.

Abuse, insults, threats and ill-treatment targeting customs officers, and opposition and the creation of disturbances during the performance of their duties, shall render the perpetrators of these acts and their accomplices liable to the penalties provided for in Article 362.
Customs officers shall be prosecuted before the judiciary in accordance with the general procedures in force concerning other State officials.
The Customs Administration shall lend its assistance to other public services or to monopoly companies within the conditions specified therefor in the laws and regulations in force.

The establishment of offences must be carried out by at least two persons. - Either by two customs officers - Or by two other officials or two officers of the public forces (Gendarmerie, Police, General Security, etc...) - Or by a customs officer and another official or another officer of the public forces or a private individual, provided that he is of age. The establishment of offences shall be carried out by means of a seizure report. Officials of the Tobacco and Tombac Monopoly Company shall have the same authority granted to customs officers with regard to establishing customs offences relating to tobacco, tombac and cigarette papers.

Persons who effect seizures shall conduct the smuggled goods, the goods used to conceal the smuggling and the means of transport to a customs office or post which is, as far as circumstances permit, the nearest to the place where the seizure took place.

Where several seizures have taken place against unknown absconding persons and the Service does not deem it necessary to draw up seizure reports in respect thereof, owing to the minor importance of the smuggled goods, and in all cases where there are no prior offences and the value of the goods for each seizure does not exceed 20000 L.P., the Customs Committee provided for in Article 323 may decide to confiscate those goods by a single decision.

The confiscation of the goods seized under the conditions provided for in Article 319 shall be decided by the Customs Committee and executed by the Customs Administration without the intervention of the judiciary after the expiry of eight days from the posting of the decision issued in this regard.

Offences provided for in the decisions and texts relating to Customs may be prosecuted and established by all legal means even if no confiscation has taken place within the Customs zone or outside it.

Except for the cases in which the method of constraint is used, in accordance with Articles 156 and 309, the Regional Head of Customs may issue a writ of constraint against the principal debtor or against his guarantors whenever the Customs Administration holds a debt for duties, whether smuggled or unpaid duties, or duties guaranteed by guaranteed bonds of undertaking, or various undertakings, or judicial undertakings, or settlements, which the debtors refuse or delay to pay. Such writs of constraint shall be issued under the conditions provided for in Article 156. An objection to the constraint shall not stay execution unless the debtor deposits the unpaid duties by way of security.

If the dispute is not settled by way of compromise, the seizure report drawn up in accordance with the provisions of the preceding Articles shall be referred to the Customs Commission, which shall decide on the action to be taken in respect thereof. This Commission is also competent: 1- to examine contraventions prosecuted pursuant to Article 321. 2- to examine any dispute or any litigation or action whatsoever in which the civil interests of the Customs are threatened when the Customs is the plaintiff, in particular for the recovery of customs duties and other duties and the enforcement of undertakings entered into towards the Administration. When cases are duly submitted to the Commission, the courts may not hear them except upon an objection. Customs Commissions may sit only in the centres determined by the Higher Council of Customs. The Customs Commission shall be composed of three members chosen from among the heads of Customs or principal officers, according to the number of officers of the centre in which the Commission sits, assisted by a clerk. If the number of officers of the office is insufficient, one of the members of the Commission shall perform the duties of clerk. Any person who has participated in the investigation of the contravention may not be a member of the Customs Commission.

The Customs Commission shall investigate the cases referred to it. It may also interrogate the seizing officers, the accused and all persons whose testimony it deems useful to hear and shall decide, where applicable, the penalties provided for in this Decree and in the customs texts.
Witnesses summoned to appear before the Customs Commissions must appear and give their testimony under penalty of arrest by virtue of a special decision issued by the said Commissions.
The Customs Commission may issue letters rogatory to any investigating body or adjudicating body and any public department.

Every person arrested under the conditions set forth in Article 305 shall be referred as soon as possible to the Customs Commission, which shall decide on the continuation of the state of remand in custody. If the Commission decides to continue the remand in custody, it shall at the same time fix the amount of the bail that the accused must pay in order to obtain his release. This amount may not exceed the sum that may be awarded according to the assessment of the Commission. The duration of remand in custody may not in general exceed fifteen days. However, this duration may be extended to thirty days when the place of arrest is located within an area situated more than 200 kilometres away from the centre of the competent Customs Commission.

Seizure reports shall state the date of the seizure (the year, month, day and hour), its place and circumstances, the names and capacity of the seizing officers and the office or post to which they belong, the kind, weight, number or quantity of the seized objects, the presence of the second party during the description of the seized objects or the notice addressed to him to attend such description, the place where the report was drawn up and the hour at which it was closed. If the accused is present, the seizure report shall state that it was read to him and that he was invited to sign it. In the event that the accused is absent or refuses to sign, this shall be stated in the report, a copy thereof shall be posted on the door of the Customs office, and this shall also be stated in the report.

Seizure reports drawn up in this form shall be deemed authentic until forgery is alleged against them. The courts may not admit any grounds for the invalidation of such reports other than those resulting from the omission of the formalities prescribed under Articles 314 315 and 316.

An offender who wishes to allege the forgery of a seizure report must submit a written declaration to that effect, at the commencement of the action, at the first sitting held by the Customs Commission, either in person or through a representative holding a special power of attorney in the form of an authentic instrument. Within the three following days, he must file with the registry of the said Commission the evidence of the forgery and the names and capacities of the witnesses whose testimony he wishes to have heard. All of this shall be under penalty of forfeiture of the forgery action. This declaration shall be received and signed by the President of the Customs Commission and its clerk, if the person making it does not know how to write and sign. It shall then be referred to the court charged with hearing the allegation of forgery. If the seizure report is declared forged in whole or in part, the court shall order either its rectification or its annulment. If the plaintiff in the forgery action loses his case, he shall be sentenced to a pecuniary penalty, in favour of the Customs, ranging between 200 and 2000 Lebanese pounds, in addition to the penalties prescribed in respect of the offence itself. The pecuniary penalty of 200 to 2000 Lebanese pounds shall be imposed each time a forgery action is submitted to the registry of the Customs Commission and such action is admitted and the plaintiff subsequently withdraws it, loses it, or has his action dismissed for lack of evidence, insufficiency thereof, or failure to complete the procedural formalities referred to in the first paragraph of this Article.

If the accused does not file an opposition and serve notice of his opposition upon the Customs, under pain of inadmissibility thereof, within a time limit of 15 days commencing from the date of his receipt of the decision of the Customs Commission, the said decision shall become final and shall not be subject to any recourse or any opposition or to a stay of execution.

An opposition against the decisions of the Customs Commission must always be submitted to the Single Civil Judge in Beirut, wherever the place of occurrence of the customs infraction may be and wherever the place of residence of the opposing party may be. The judgment rendered in the opposition submitted in this manner shall always be deemed adversarial, even if the opposing party fails to appear.

The decisions pronounced by the Customs Commissions in all cases falling within their jurisdiction may not be opposed before the Single Civil Judge in Beirut except after depositing with the Customs fund or the Treasury a cash security equivalent to the entirety of the customs duties ordered to be collected, plus, in the event of the application of penalties, an amount equivalent to 25 percent of the value of the penalties imposed in the decision opposed against, and the total value of the security may not exceed the amount of fifteen thousand Lebanese pounds. Under no circumstances may the registry of the court accept the petition of opposition unless it is accompanied by the receipt proving the deposit of the security mentioned above.

Judgments rendered by the Single Civil Judge in Beirut in favour of the Customs shall be final and not subject to appeal when they impose penalties the total of which (the pecuniary penalty and the confiscation of the goods, the means of transport, and the objects used to conceal the fraud) is equal to or less than the amount of 600 Lebanese pounds. Provided that the losing party may file a petition in cassation in the action under the conditions stipulated in Article 337.

The appeal must be submitted within the thirty days following the service of notice of the judgment rendered by the Single Civil Judge in Beirut. The appeal shall not be admitted unless the convicted party has previously deposited, with the Customs fund or the Treasury, a cash security equivalent to the total of the penalties (duties and fines) adjudged by the Customs Commission.

Customs officers shall have the necessary competence to draw up and serve in person writs of summons, citations, and notifications, and in general all documents relating to legal procedure required for the collection of customs duty, the recovery of pecuniary penalties, and the enforcement of confiscations.

The decision of the Customs Commission shall be served upon the party concerned in person, or at his last known place of residence, or at his elected domicile, or at his place of business. If the party concerned is absent, service may be effected upon any person residing with him who is over 15 years of age. Service may be made upon a servant or a commercial employee. In the event of refusal to sign, mention shall be made thereof and the service shall remain valid. If the party concerned changes his declared place of residence or his place of business after the date of the seizure report drawn up against him without notifying the Customs thereof in writing, or if he gives a false address, the formality of service shall be effected by posting on the door of his last, known, or declared place of residence or place of business and on the outer door of the Customhouse. Writs of summons shall be served in accordance with the same rules set forth above relating to the service of the decision of the Customs Commission. If the offence is committed by an unknown person and the total value of the seized articles does not exceed one thousand five hundred Lebanese pounds, service of the writ summoning the offender or of the decision of the Customs Commission shall be effected by posting on the door of the Courthouse and on the outer door of the Customhouse where the Commission holds its sittings. If the total value of the seized articles exceeds one thousand five hundred pounds, service shall be effected by posting on the door of the Courthouse and by publication in two local newspapers. If the offence is committed by a person residing abroad, the writs summoning the offender and the decision of the Customs Commission shall be sent to the Public Prosecution, which shall ensure their service in the manner it deems appropriate.

The Public Prosecution or General Security shall, upon the request of the Customs Administration, prevent any person against whom the Customs has rights from leaving Lebanese territory unless he provides a guarantor whose solvency the Commission recognises.

Decisions rendered by the Customs Commissions shall be final and not subject to appeal when the total of the penalties imposed (the pecuniary part and the confiscation of the goods, the means of transport, and the articles used to conceal the fraud) does not exceed the amount of 300 Lebanese pounds. Provided that the losing party may petition for cassation against these decisions within the conditions referred to in Article 337.

Recourse in cassation is always admissible for violation of the law or for its erroneous application. The petition for cassation must be submitted within the thirty days following the service of the decision of the Customs Commission or the judgment of first instance or of appeal. Recourse in cassation shall not be accepted, if the decision of the Customs Commission or the judgment of the Single Civil Judge in Beirut is not subject to opposition or to appeal, except on condition of depositing the security deposit provided for in Article 334. The registry of the Court of Cassation may not accept the petition for cassation unless it is accompanied by the receipt for the security deposit.

In lawsuits in which the Customs is plaintiff or defendant, the judges must mandatorily issue their judgments as quickly as possible and endeavour to serve upon the litigants the judgments of first instance and of appeal rendered within a period of fifteen days at most from the date of their issuance.

The Customs Administration is exempted from affixing stamps on all documents that it may be requested to submit to the court or that it requests be produced and from paying all judicial expenses incurred in lawsuits that it may bring or that may be brought against it. It is also exempted from all enforcement expenses without the privilege of the Treasury being an impediment to the full exercise of its rights. It shall be incumbent upon the Customs Administration, if it loses the lawsuit, to bear the expenses and costs imposed upon it in favour of the other party. The Customs Administration is also exempted from furnishing a guarantee, security deposit or advance to cover expenses, in all cases in which the law imposes this obligation upon litigants.
A plea of peremption of the lawsuit or prosecution may not be raised against the Customs.
Pecuniary penalties and confiscations provided for in the customs regulations shall be deemed as if they were civil compensation for the Customs Administration.

The courts may not, in applying the penalties provided for in this Resolution and in the customs texts, take into consideration the intention, but only the material facts, for ignorance or good faith are not deemed an excuse. Accordingly, these courts must inflict the penalties built above merely upon the commission of the acts that these penalties repress or merely upon commencing them only.

Pecuniary penalties may be accumulated if the contraventions concur. Duties and pecuniary penalties may be recovered from the heirs of the offenders and from their masters, those commissioning them, their employers and their principals, and from their relatives and their guardians if they are minors or interdicted.

The amounts adjudged (duties, fines, and confiscations) shall be imposed and collected jointly and severally from the principal perpetrators of the offences, the guarantors, the accomplices, the intermediaries, the seamen, the drivers of the means of transport, and all carriers, and from the owners of the offending goods and the persons to whom they are consigned, and from the owners of the means of transport, the owners of the goods used to conceal the fraud, and the owners of the premises in which the smuggled goods were deposited.

The Customs Commissions may order the provisional enforcement of their judgments, whether against the property of the debtor or against his person, notwithstanding any recourse to which he may resort. They may also waive the time limit of the formal notice addressed to the debtor. Thus, the convicted person may be arrested immediately. However, the debtor may apply to the Single Civil Judge in Beirut, who may stay the enforcement of imprisonment provided that the convicted person furnishes a solvent guarantor or pays a sufficient financial security. Where the rules of summary proceedings are resorted to, the application provided for in the preceding paragraph shall be made in accordance with these rules.

For the purpose of enforcing judgments rendered in favour of the Customs, the Administration may, while reserving its right to imprison the debtor, attach and put up for sale simultaneously all of his movable and immovable property.

In all cases where it is impossible to collect in full the pecuniary penalties imposed and the costs, the penalty of imprisonment shall be enforced at the rate of one day for every two Lebanese pounds not collected, provided that the term of imprisonment shall not, under any circumstances, exceed one year.
Imprisonment in customs cases shall be enforced without need to prove the debtor's ability to pay, and even if he is in a state of bankruptcy or is over sixty-five years of age.
The term of imprisonment shall be calculated separately for each judgment.

By way of derogation from the legal provisions in force, if the Customs requests the imprisonment of the same debtor once again, after having consented to or requested his release, its request must be granted.
Warrants to bring in and orders of detention may be executed at the hands of customs officers. All attachments and notifications may be effected through the same officers.

The limitation period for customs actions is: 15 years for the collection of duties the payment of which the taxpayer did not evade except through fraudulent manoeuvres or false or incomplete declarations, and this period shall run from the date of discovery of the fraud. 15 years for the enforcement of any judgment or decision of concern to the Administration, including the collection of duties the payment of which is pursued by writs of constraint issued pursuant to Article 156. 5 years for the collection of duties not paid owing to an error on the part of the Administration, as well as for the collection of pecuniary penalties and confiscations. Apart from the grounds by which limitation is interrupted in ordinary rights, limitation in customs cases shall be interrupted either by a claim made by registered letter or by the opening of an investigation before the Customs Commission.

The Customs Administration shall enjoy, for the collection of all duties, penalties, confiscations and recoveries, a general lien over the movable property of taxpayers. This lien shall operate in all circumstances, even in the event of bankruptcy, and in priority to all debts, save those relating to the preservation of things, judicial costs advanced by a third party, and debts carrying a general lien over movable property. The lien of the Customs Administration shall rank in the first degree over the sums deposited as security by taxpayers prior to an objection or appeal.

A guarantor who pays to the Customs Administration the guaranteed amount shall be subrogated to the Administration in its rights, liens and mortgages. Furthermore, the Customs Administration may, without the consent of the debtor, assign and transfer to any third party, even to joint and several or non-joint and several debtors, and even if its right is the subject of a dispute or a legal action, any debt owed to it in whatever capacity, and subrogate such third party to itself in all its rights, liens and mortgages as against the debtor and his guarantor. Subrogation approved by the Administration shall always operate for the benefit of the subrogee under the same conditions as held by the Administration. In all cases, the rights, liens and mortgages of the Administration shall vest in the subrogee after he has paid the amount of the debt to the Customs treasury.
