The instrument of subrogation shall be constituted, without the need for any other formality, by the receipt issued by the Customs in which the conditions and limits of the subrogation are specified.

The Customs Administration may conclude settlements with offenders, either before or after the issuance of judgment, by replacing the statutory penalties (fixed or variable pecuniary penalties and the confiscation of goods, means of transport, and objects used to conceal the fraud) with a pecuniary penalty that varies according to the circumstances of the seizure and is paid, where applicable, in addition to the amount of duties due on the goods imported or exported by way of fraud. It is authorised, if the circumstances in which the contraventions are established justify it, to waive the contraventions detected by its officers.

A settlement concluded between the Customs Administration, on the one hand, and the perpetrators of the contraventions and their accomplices, on the other hand, shall have the effect of extinguishing both the civil action and the public prosecution together, where the subject-matter of the latter action is fiscal customs contraventions not punishable by corporal penalties.

The right of settlement in cases relating to the contravention of customs decisions and regulations shall vest, depending on the case, either in the Higher Council of Customs, or in the Director General of Customs, or in the Regional Heads. First - Regional Heads shall exercise the right of settlement in the following manner: 1- Regional Heads shall decide finally on contraventions falling under the provisions of Article 362. 2- Regional Heads shall decide, subject to the approval of the Director General, in the following cases: a- On contraventions falling under the provisions of Articles 363 to 367. b - On all other contraventions where the value of the goods does not exceed 2000 Lebanese pounds, and in cases involving evaded duties or duties at risk of being lost, even if the value of the goods exceeds 2000 Lebanese pounds, provided that the amount of such duties does not exceed 600 Lebanese pounds. Second - The Director General of Customs shall decide on the matter if the value of the goods in the contraventions mentioned in category (b) above exceeds 2000 Lebanese pounds and does not exceed 24000 Lebanese pounds, and in cases involving evaded duties or duties at risk of being lost, even if the value of the goods exceeds 24000 Lebanese pounds, provided that the amount of such duties does not exceed 6000 Lebanese pounds. The Higher Council of Customs shall decide in other cases not provided for above, upon the proposal of the Director General of Customs.

In all cases in which the courts order the confiscation of the smuggled goods, they must order at the same time, in addition to the pecuniary penalty provided for in Article 360, the confiscation of the means of transport, the goods and the articles of whatever kind that were used to conceal the fraud (even if a valid declaration had been submitted in respect thereof) and their value shall be added to the amount of the pecuniary penalty.

The amount of the pecuniary penalty provided for in Article 358, irrespective of the regulatory confiscations, shall be determined as follows and may not be less than 50 Lebanese pounds: In the event of the seizure of the goods, the means of transport and the articles that were used to conceal the fraud: A- If the goods and the articles are not prohibited, at an amount equal to their value including customs duties. B- If these goods are prohibited or if they are subject to heavy duties and are subject to the regulations of the customs zone within the conditions provided for in Article 296 and are designated by administrative orders issued by the Higher Council of Customs in accordance with the said Article, at an amount equal to twice the value including customs duties. C- If the goods are designated by a special administrative order of the Higher Council of Customs published in the Official Gazette, at an amount equal to six times the value. If the goods, the means of transport and the articles that were used to conceal the fraud have escaped seizure, the court shall rule, in addition to the pecuniary penalty mentioned above, in compensation for confiscation, for the payment of an amount equal to the value of these goods, means of transport and articles that were used to conceal the fraud (including customs duties), according to the price on the domestic market and on the date of the commission of the fraud. In cases in which the elements sufficient to determine the value of the goods and the articles that have escaped seizure cannot be known, even approximately, a lump-sum fine of 100 to 1000 Lebanese pounds shall be imposed.

The following offences shall be liable to the imposition of a pecuniary penalty equivalent to four times the value of the duty claimed: No. 1- A false declaration aimed at obtaining, without right, by any means whatsoever, an unlawful or irregular refund of the customs duties in whole or in part, even if such duties were deposited as security. No. 2- A false declaration as to kind, type, quality, number, quantity, measurement, volume, weight or origin, aimed at obtaining a drawback of duty exceeding the duty eligible for refund. No. 3- A false declaration as to value, aimed at obtaining a drawback of duty exceeding the duty eligible for refund, where the declared value exceeds by a proportion of 1/20 or more the value determined by the Customs.

The following shall be liable to the imposition of a pecuniary penalty of 50 Lebanese pounds: No. 1- The importation or attempted importation of goods exempt from duties, without a declaration or by way of smuggling. No. 2- The exportation or attempted exportation of goods exempt from duties, without a declaration or by way of smuggling. No. 3- A false declaration as to kind, type, quality, origin, quantity- or value of goods exempt from duties, or which does not expose any duty to loss. No. 4- A false declaration as to type or quality which exposes to loss a duty equivalent to 1000 Lebanese piastres or less. No. 5- The offences set forth in Nos. 10, 11 and 12 of Article 358 whenever the goods dispatched in transit or re-exported are exempt from customs duties. No. 6- The presentation of the goods to the office of exit or to the office of destination after the expiry of the time-limits fixed in the guaranteed bond, and the return of a certificate of discharge for a guaranteed bond after the lapse of one month from the expiry of the time-limit granted under such bond, except in the case of force majeure legally established. No. 7- The breaking of the lead seals or stamps on goods dispatched in transit, without justification and without any shortage or substitution being established. No. 8- The absence of a manifest upon exit or the failure to present the exit manifest to the Customs. No. 9- Insults, affronts, threats and ill-treatment directed against customs officers, and the opposition and disturbance to which they are subjected during the exercise of their functions. This pecuniary penalty shall be adjudged personally against the perpetrators of these acts and their accomplices. In cases of battery or wounding of a customs officer, even if this does not prevent him from performing his work, the penalties provided for in the Penal Code shall, furthermore, remain applicable.

The following offences shall entail the seizure and confiscation of the smuggled goods, subject to observing the provisions of Article 359 and applying the penalty prescribed in Article 360: 1- Provisions common to all goods: No. 1- The importation or attempted importation of prohibited goods or goods subject to customs duties without a customs declaration or by way of smuggling. No. 2- A false declaration as to the kind of goods. Entering prohibited goods on the manifest or the documents replacing it under a designation that does not indicate the truth of their kind, nature and quality shall be deemed to constitute a false declaration as to the kind. No. 3- A false declaration as to the nature or quality which exposes to loss duties the value of which exceeds 1000 L.P. No. 4- A false declaration as to weight, number and measurement (or any other specific unit) which involves an excess exceeding one tenth (1/10) of the declared weight, number or measurement (or any other specific unit), except with respect to heavily taxed products designated by an administrative order from the Supreme Council of Customs published in the Official Gazette, to which the penalties provided for in this Article shall apply if the excess in weight, number or measurement (or any other specific unit) exceeds one twentieth 1/20). No. 5- A false declaration as to value which involves an excess equal to or exceeding one tenth (1/10) of the declared value. No. 6- A false declaration as to provenance or origin intended to obtain the benefit of a tariff lower than the tariff actually applicable. '' No. 7- Drawing up or submitting false or forged documents or documents containing false indications, with the intent to obtain the benefit either of an exemption from duties or of a tariff or duty lower than the tariff or duty actually applicable. No. 8- The ascertainment of false indications as to number, weight, value and nature in the invoices submitted as being original invoices. No. 9- The importation, by letter post, of closed dispatches and packets (ordinary and registered), dispatches with declared value, boxes with declared value, small packets (ordinary and registered), ordinary registered printed matter and ordinary and registered samples, devoid of the regulatory labels and established to contain prohibited goods or goods subject to duties, in accordance with the conditions provided for in the decisions in force. No. 10- The ascertainment, in any case whatsoever, of an unjustified shortage in parcels sent in transit or in goods placed in parcels sent in transit.

11- The substitution of all or part of the goods declared as intended for transit by other goods, ascertained in any case whatsoever, without this preventing, if the substituted goods are prohibited from exportation, the application of the penalties provided for in No. 27 of this Article. No. 12- Failure to prove passage abroad or arrival at destination for goods sent in transit or re-exported. Repetition of this offence and the two preceding offences may, moreover, lead to depriving the perpetrator thereof or his accomplices of the right to engage in transit operations, by a mere simple administrative measure. No. 13- An unjustified shortage in the quantities of goods placed in private actual warehouses or in fictitious warehouses. This offence may lead to depriving the concerned parties of the benefit of the private actual warehouse or the fictitious warehouse by a mere simple administrative measure. No. 14- Failure to return guaranteed bonds relating to the transport of goods from one warehouse to another or their re-exportation from the warehouse, endorsed to certify the arrival of the goods. No. 15- The discovery in the free zone of goods the entry of which into it is prohibited. This offence shall be established against the owners or depositors of the goods or their agents or partners and, in general, against all the persons mentioned in Article 344 or against the body entrusted with operating the free zone and which may be liable under the provisions of Article 226. No. 16- The introduction by way of smuggling into the customs territory of goods placed in the free zone. This offence shall be established against the owners or depositors of the goods or their agents or partners and, in general, against the persons mentioned in Article 344. No. 17- Failure to complete the formalities provided for in Articles 90, 227 and 228 concerning the free zone.

No. 18- Failure to re-present the products temporarily admitted free of duties upon every request by the Customs Service, either in their state or after their transformation within the regulatory time limit for temporary admission. No. 19- Failure to re-export the articles temporarily admitted free of duties or the articles resulting therefrom after their processing, or failure to place them in the warehouse, within the regulatory time limit; this offence and the preceding offence may, moreover, lead to depriving the concerned parties of the benefit of temporary admission, by a mere simple administrative measure. No. 20- The transfer of goods from one means of transport to another means of transport or their re-exportation without a regulatory declaration or authorisation. No. 21- The loading or unloading of vessels, lorries, trucks or other means of transport, or the withdrawal of goods without an authorisation from the Customs or in the absence of its representatives. No. 22- The mention of several closed packages, grouped in any manner whatsoever, on the manifest or on the bills of lading or on the waybills or the detailed declarations as being a single unit. No. 23- Any excess over the manifest or other documents replacing it, ascertained after the unloading of the means of transport whatsoever. This offence shall be established against the person in charge of operating the means of transport or the carrier or the duly appointed representative of either of them and, in general, against all the persons mentioned in Article 344. No. 24- The use of the articles mentioned below outside the places where such use is permitted, or their use in ways other than the specific uses for which they were imported, or their allocation for a purpose other than that for which they are intended, or their substitution, all of that in an irregular manner, or their sale without prior notice to the Customs and before the Customs has secured the collection of the ordinary duties or before the new purchaser has completely replaced the original importer and in all his obligations. These articles are: a- Products admitted, in accordance with the customs tariff, free of duties or subject to reduced duties in view of the specific purpose for which they are intended. '' b - Supplies, materials, tools or products delivered free of customs duties pursuant to Chapters 2, 3, 4, 6, 7 and 8 of Title Four of this Law. c- Motor vehicles temporarily admitted free of duties. These offences shall be recorded against the beneficiaries of the customs exemption or the reduced duties or the temporary admission, or against the customs clearing agents, intermediaries, contractors or concessionaires and, in general, against all the persons mentioned in Article 344. These offences may also lead to the withdrawal of the privileged status from the offenders who benefit therefrom, for a period which may reach five years. No. 25- The movement or possession of goods subject to zone policing, in an irregular manner, within the customs zone, and movement that does not comply with the terms of the transport document. No. 26- An unjustified excess or shortage in the open account prescribed in Article 299. The sale of goods carried out by the Customs Administration shall cover the following categories: 1- Confiscated goods and objects which have become the final property of Customs. 2- Perishable goods referred to in Article 369. 3- Goods abandoned in Customs. 4- Goods which have not been withdrawn from real warehouses, private real warehouses and fictitious warehouses within the regulatory time limits and which are sold under the conditions provided for in Articles 189, 203 and 213. 5- Goods which have become the property of Customs after their owner has relinquished them in writing.

This sale shall take place by public auction, except for monopolised goods. In principle, the goods shall be sold free of all customs duties and expenses that may be chargeable thereon. The price shall be paid in cash.

By way of derogation from the legal provisions in force, customs sales shall be announced to the public, at the discretion of the Customs Administration, by a notice published either in one or several newspapers or posted on the doors of the Customs office. The publication or posting of the notice must precede the sale by at least ten clear days. This time limit may be reduced, and this matter is left to the discretion of the Customs Administration, in the event of the sale of perishable goods. The sale shall take place on the premises and under the conditions specified in the published or posted notice.

The fixing of the reserve price of the goods shall be left to the discretion of the Customs Administration, and in principle this price may not be lower than the amount of the duty if the goods are subject to a specific duty. However, the Customs Administration reserves to itself, when circumstances so require, the right to authorise the sale of the goods even if the price offered does not equal the amount of the duties payable. In this case, the entire proceeds of the sale, after deduction of the privileged expenses, shall be allocated to the collection of the duties. If no purchasers come forward for these goods after two consecutive offerings for sale under the conditions provided for in the two preceding paragraphs, the Administration shall have the right to destroy them of its own motion, and it shall then draw up a formal report of this destruction.
The legal provisions in force relating to the adjournment of sales and to resale upon default of the purchaser shall apply to customs sales.

Shall be liable to the imposition of a pecuniary penalty of 250 Lebanese Pounds: No. 1- A shortage in the packages mentioned in the manifest or the other documents serving in its stead, verified after the unloading of the means of transport, whatever they may be. The pecuniary penalty amounting to 250 Lebanese Pounds shall be due for each missing package. No. 2- The presence of several manifests, or other documents serving in their stead, in the possession of the persons in charge of driving the carriers. This offence, and the preceding offence, shall be booked against the person in charge of driving the carriers and the carrier or the duly authorised representative of both of them, and in general against all the persons mentioned in Article 344. No. 3- The transport of passengers or goods in Lebanese territory by the foreign motor vehicles referred to in Article 344. This offence shall entail the payment of customs duties on such motor vehicles in addition to the pecuniary penalty. No. 4- Failure to submit the original invoice specified in Article 53, without prejudice, where applicable, to the application of the penalties imposed in the event of submitting false declarations or false documents.

When customs officers conduct an inspection on board vessels under the conditions provided for in Articles 69 and 70, and where applicable in Article 72, if the manifest is not produced or if there are goods not mentioned therein, or if discrepancies are found between the goods and the manifest, or if some of the goods mentioned in the manifests are not presented for inspection, the master of the vessel shall be personally ordered to pay an amount equivalent to the value of the goods not mentioned in the manifest, or showing a discrepancy, or not presented for inspection, and a penalty amounting to 250 Lebanese Pounds. The vessel shall be seized and shall remain as security for the payment of the value of these penalties. Furthermore, the prohibited or monopolised goods and various articles that are in excess of the manifest shall be confiscated.

When customs officers search vessels under the conditions provided for in Article 69, if the cargo of these vessels includes goods the entry or exit of which is prohibited, or monopolised goods and materials, whether mentioned in the manifest or not mentioned, these vessels shall be confiscated together with their cargo, and their masters shall be fined a pecuniary penalty of 250 Lebanese Pounds.

During the inspection of vessels provided for in Articles 364 and 365, the resistance of the master to the investigations of the Customs officers, before or after the intervention of the public officer, being the intervention referred to in Article 73, shall render him liable to a monetary penalty of 250 Lebanese pounds, and the vessel and its cargo shall be seized and shall remain as security for the execution of this penalty.

The failure to enter goods that must be entered in the lists provided for in Article 71, and any shortage in these lists ascertained upon the departure of the vessel, shall be recorded against the master undertaking the transport or against his duly authorised representative and shall entail the application of the penalties provided for in Article 365, subject, where applicable, to the application of the penalties provided for in Article 366.

The monetary penalties provided for in respect of Articles 360 and 362 shall be raised to fourfold with regard to importations or exportations (or attempted importation or exportation) without a declaration or by way of smuggling by means of aircraft.

The Customs Administration is permitted to proceed, prior to the judgment of the court, with the sale of perishable goods or means of transport, or goods subject to leakage, or animals, which are kept at the Customs following a dispute, if the Administration is compelled to do so or if doing so is in the interest of the rightful owner. The sale shall take place by public auction after establishing the circumstances justifying it by a seizure report drawn up by the Customs officers. If the court rules after the sale that the sold goods, means of transport or animals be returned to the rightful owner, the proceeds of the sale shall be paid to him in cash after deducting the expenses. Sales carried out under the conditions provided for in this Article may not give rise to the institution of any action for damages against the Customs Administration, except in the case where the Administration has committed an indisputable, established gross fault.

Upon the expiry of a period of six months and one day, the Customs Administration may, of its own accord, sell by public auction the goods abandoned in Customs stores other than real warehouses and private real warehouses.

The proceeds of the sale shall be distributed in accordance with the following order: 1- Expenses of whatever kind incurred by the Administration. 2- Customs duties, and these duties shall be calculated under the conditions mentioned in Article 377. 3- Storage and porterage fees. 4- Freight charges and specified expenses. If the Customs Administration, following a seizure effected outside the customs offices, is unable to reward the informers or the seizing officers satisfactorily out of the proceeds of the pecuniary penalty, it may, in order to achieve this purpose, conduct the sale with exemption from duties, after confiscating the goods, the means of transport, and the objects used to conceal the fraud. The proceeds of this sale shall be distributed pursuant to a special administrative order issued by the competent authority designated in Article 354.

Specific customs duties shall be levied in accordance with the rules of Article 10 to the extent permitted by the proceeds of the sale and subject to compliance with the provisions of Article 23. If the sold goods are subject to an ad valorem duty, this duty shall be levied on the basis of the sale price.

In the third case provided for in Article 371, sales shall be conducted under the supervision of a committee composed of customs officers, which shall also include a representative of the local Chamber of Commerce or, in the absence thereof, a representative of the local authority. If the latter is absent, it shall be stated in the official report of the sale that he was duly invited, and his presence shall be dispensed with. The members of the committee may not participate in the bidding, either in person, or through an intermediary, or in the capacity of proxies, under pain of nullity of the sale, irrespective of the penalties provided for in the legal provisions in force.

In the third case provided for in Article 371, the balance of the sale price, after deduction of the privileged debts mentioned in Article 376, shall be deposited on trust with the customs fund to be subject to the same allocations provided for in Article 189 under the same conditions.

In the third and fourth cases provided for in Article 371, a copy of the notice of sale shall be sent to the owner of the goods if known, and failing that, to the relevant transport company or its commercial or consular agent.

The urgent draft law transmitted by Decree No. 8457 dated 8 January 1962 aiming to regulate the Sunni and Jaafari Sharia Judiciary, as amended by the Administration and Justice Committee, has been ratified.

This Law shall be published and shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.
The Sunni and Jaafari Sharia Judiciary forms part of the judicial organisations of the State.
The Sunni and Jaafari Sharia Judiciary consists of courts of first instance and a Supreme Sharia Court for each of the two denominations.
The court of first instance shall be composed of a single Sharia judge.
The seat of the two Supreme Courts is Beirut. Each court shall be composed of a President and two Associate Judges.
The number of the courts of first instance, their seats, and the territorial jurisdiction of each of them have been designated in Table No. 1 annexed to this Law.

The Sunni courts shall be composed of Sunni Sharia judges and the Jaafari courts of Jaafari Sharia judges.

The jurisdiction of each of them shall be confined to lawsuits and transactions relating to litigants of its denomination, subject to the exceptional cases provided for in this Law.

A judge may not abstain from ruling on the pretext of the ambiguity or deficiency of the law, failing which he shall be deemed in denial of justice. Unlawful delay and rendering judgment may also be deemed a denial of justice.
The judge shall resolve all questions raised by the litigants and shall reason his judgments and decisions by stating the grounds, except in cases exempted by an express provision.
The courts may not adjudge more than what is claimed, except for the application of laws relating to public policy.

Judgments shall be issued by the Supreme Sharia Court constituted in accordance with the provisions of Article Four, and deliberation shall take place in secret, commencing by taking the opinion of the judge lowest in rank, or most junior in the judiciary, or youngest in age. Disclosing the secrecy of deliberation shall constitute the offence provided for in Article 579 of the Penal Code.
The jurisdiction of the courts shall encompass the principal action and the pleas, grounds of defence, and connected incidental claims branching therefrom, unless a contrary provision exists.

Each of the two Supreme Courts shall be presided over by its President; provided that if the President of the Court is absent or unable to attend, its management shall be undertaken by the most senior counsellor therein, and one of the counsellors or a primary judge delegated by its President shall join it. If it is impossible to constitute the Supreme Court in its entirety or by a majority of its original judges to hear a given case, a panel of judges of the judicial courts who belong to the denomination of the Court shall be delegated by decree to hear it.
If one of the Sunni or Jaafari primary judges is unable to exercise his function, a primary judge delegated by the President of the Supreme Court to which he belongs shall act in his stead.

The function of the Public Prosecution before each of the two Supreme Courts shall be performed by a civil or administrative judge of its denomination, who shall be delegated by decree and shall receive an allowance also determined by decree.
Each of the two Supreme Courts shall have a registry comprising a number of judicial assistants as determined in the schedules annexed to this Law.

The Sharia Courts shall be barred from hearing actions and proceedings not mentioned in this Law. They shall also be barred from hearing the aforementioned actions and proceedings against foreigners of their sect who belong to countries in which personal status is subject to civil law, unless one of the spouses is Lebanese, in which case the mentioned actions and proceedings, as well as endowment matters, shall remain subject to the jurisdiction of the Sharia Courts.

In actions of a determinate or determinable value, the Court of First Instance shall render a judgment in the last instance when the subject-matter of the action does not exceed fifty thousand Lebanese pounds, and in applications for the imposition of maintenance the total value of which does not exceed fifty thousand Lebanese pounds per month, and otherwise its judgments shall be subject to appeal.

The judge shall have the right, without addressing the merits of the right, to hear:

1- Applications aimed at taking urgent measures, unless the dispute is before the Supreme Court.

2- Every application aimed at urgently investigating a state of affairs or a fact, either by himself or through a technical expert.

3- An application to hear one of the litigants whose death or absence is feared.

4- An application to hear a witness whose death or absence is feared in a matter not yet brought before the judiciary and likely to be brought before it, upon verifying the necessity of the measure. In the latter case, a copy of the record of investigation shall not be delivered, nor submitted to the judiciary unless the court of the merits deems testimonial evidence admissible.

The judge may, upon application and in chambers, prohibit the defendant from travelling in two cases:

1- In the urgent cases provided for in Article 20 until he is interrogated.

2- In the case of a claim to secure maintenance for the person to whom maintenance is due, and the defendant shall have the right to object to the decision, such that if he is interrogated or his objection is well-founded, the judge shall revoke the decision prohibiting travel, and otherwise he shall uphold it.

In all cases, the decision of the judge issued as a result of the objection shall be subject to appeal within eight days, and it must be adjudicated on appeal within a time-limit of eight days. Upon proof of bad faith, the plaintiff shall be ordered to pay a fine and compensation to the defendant, the assessment of both of which shall rest with the court.

In pecuniary actions falling within the jurisdiction of the Sharia Courts, these courts may levy a precautionary attachment on the movable property of the debtor in his possession or in the hands of a third party, whether in kind or a debt, and they may also, in an action for specific movable property, levy a revendication attachment, and they shall have the right to hear an action to establish the right to the attachment, all of which shall be in accordance with the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure.

The judge shall be entitled during the trial, upon application or in connection with one of the rights of God, or with a minor, an interdicted person, an endowment (waqf), or the public treasury (bayt mal) where its loss is feared, to take any urgent measure he deems necessary in the action in order to avert a grave and imminent damage.

The Supreme Sharia Court shall examine at final instance:

1- Appeals against non-final judgments rendered by the courts of first instance subordinate to it.

2- Applications for judicial liability proceedings (mukhasama) against Sharia judges.

3- Applications for the transfer of an action on grounds of legitimate suspicion or for the preservation of public security.

4- Applications for the recusal and disqualification of Sharia judges.

Every natural or legal person, whether Lebanese or foreign, shall have the right to have recourse to the Sharia judiciary in order to establish and safeguard his rights in matters falling within its jurisdiction.

No claim or defence in which the party raising it has no existing interest recognised by law shall be admissible. Nevertheless, a potential interest shall suffice if the purpose of the application is to take precaution to avert an imminent damage or to establish a right the evidence of which is feared to be lost.

An action brought in bad faith or with the intent to inflict damage shall be dismissed, and the plaintiff shall be ordered to pay compensation to his opponent. Likewise, whoever opposes in bad faith or intends to cause damage in respect of a claim the validity of which has become apparent shall be ordered to pay compensation.

The judge may, of his own motion, sentence the party acting in bad faith to a fine of not less than one hundred thousand pounds and not more than five hundred thousand Lebanese pounds".
A person's capacity to litigate shall be governed by the law of his state. This rule shall apply to guardianship over persons lacking capacity and to the right to represent them.
The court shall, at every stage of the action, verify the capacity to litigate and the validity of the representation of persons lacking capacity or the validity of the guardianship over them.

Where a person lacking capacity is required to obtain a judge's authorisation pursuant to his personal status law, the Sharia court shall grant him such authorisation. Such authorisation shall remain valid throughout all stages of the trial and execution.
The Court of First Instance shall hear all lawsuits falling within the jurisdiction of the Sharia Courts.

Lawsuits and transactions relating to the following matters shall fall within the jurisdiction of the Sharia Courts:

1- Marriage betrothal and its gift.

2- Marriage.

3- Divorce and separation.

4- Dower and trousseau.

5- Maintenance, maternal custody, and the joining of young males and females to their guardians.

6- Lineage.

7- Legal guardianship, testamentary guardianship, and curatorship.

8- Puberty and proof of legal majority.

9- Interdiction.

10- The missing person.

11- Bequest.

12- Proof of death, determination of heirs, and specification of inheritance shares.

13- Inventorying the non-real estate estate, selling it, distributing it, and supervising the administration of orphans' property in accordance with the Orphans' Property Administration Regulations.

14- Waqf, its legal ruling, its binding nature, its validity, its conditions, entitlement to it, its partition, and partition for preservation and development.

15- Appointment of the administrator for a family waqf and the curator for an absent testamentary guardian only. As for the curator for an absent, dismissed, deceased, or resigned administrator, the Waqf Department is the curator pursuant to Article 55 of the Law on the Allocation of Religious Offices.

16- Dismissal of the testamentary guardian and the curator for an absent testamentary guardian and holding both to account, dismissal of the administrator of a waqf, holding to account the administrator of a family waqf or an exempted waqf, and ordering them to pay the funds for which they are liable.

17- Granting permission to the legal guardian, the testamentary guardian, and the administrator of pure family waqfs.

18- Drawing up and registering the deed of bequest and of waqf in due form.

19- Drawing up powers of attorney in lawsuits and matters falling within the jurisdiction of the Sharia Courts

20 -The text of Paragraph (20) of Article 17 of the Law of Sharia Courts issued on 16/7/1962 is repealed, and the times and affairs of the Islamic Shiite confession shall be subject to the provisions of the Law on the Organization of the Affairs of this Confession issued under No. 72/67 dated 19/12/1967 and its amendments, and the Internal Regulations of the Supreme Islamic Shiite Council issued under No. 15 dated 21/8/1969, and these provisions shall apply notwithstanding any other contrary text

21 - With regard to all transactions of charitable waqf, the waqf of mosques and prayer halls, the appointment of the administrator, the drawing up of the waqf deed, and other such matters, submitted by natural and legal persons - individuals or bodies - or associations - or institutions and others within the Sunni Islamic confession, the prior approval of the Supreme Authority for Islamic Waqfs (the Mufti of the Lebanese Republic) shall be required, after notifying him of the application relating to one of the aforementioned subjects.
The principal claim and the incidental claim shall be adjudicated together, unless the proper administration of justice requires adjudicating one of them before the other.
The court shall examine as a matter of urgency every dispute arising over the admissibility of the incidental claim.
Every interested person may intervene in the action to preserve his rights vis-à-vis the litigants or to support the claims of one of them.

Each of the litigants may join a third party to the action in order for judgment to be rendered against him for warranty or to defend him wholly or partially against the harm to which he is exposed by the mere rendering of judgment against him, or to participate in hearing the judgment.

The intervention or joinder of a third party shall be permissible at all stages of the court until the close thereof. An application for intervention shall be submitted by way of a pleading, and an application for joinder by way of a summons.

In respect thereof, the rules governing the summons, the writ of appearance, time limits, and the right of reply shall be observed. Time limits may be shortened, and the summons and the writ of appearance may be sent simultaneously, or the applicant for joinder may be granted a reasonable period to submit his application and have it served in accordance with the rules of procedure.

The court may of its own motion join to the action, with a view to facilitating the right of the dispute or preserving the rights of the litigants:

1- Anyone who was a party to the action at a previous stage.

2- Anyone bound to one of the litigants by a joint and several obligation or an indivisible obligation.

3- Anyone whose interest is threatened by collusion, fraud, or negligence on the part of one of the litigants.

4- Anyone who is an heir or a partner with one of the litigants in disputes relating to an estate or co-ownership.

5- Anyone who may suffer harm from the institution of the action or the judgment therein, or anyone whom the court deems to have an interest in the litigation.

When applying the provisions of the preceding Article, the court shall fix the date for the appearance of the third party, the time limit for the reply, and the party upon whom it is incumbent to serve the papers and the writ of appearance upon him.

If the intervention or joinder involves an intention to delay the adjudication of the action or is devoid of utility, the court may dismiss it and order the applicant therefor to pay compensation to the injured party or the third party

and a fine of one hundred thousand to five hundred thousand Lebanese pounds.

If a person lacking legal capacity has no guardian or tutor when the action is brought against him or when it is pursued, the plaintiff may request the president of the court competent to hear this action to appoint for him a special representative to act temporarily in the place of the legal representative until the latter is appointed. The special representative shall not have the right of discontinuance, waiver, admission, settlement or acquiescence.

The Public Prosecution before the Supreme Sharia Court shall have the right to bring an action directly in the cases provided for by law or relating to public order. It shall have the right to challenge judgments rendered in these cases even if it was not represented therein as a principal party.

Save for the preceding cases, the intervention of the Public Prosecution shall be confined to delivering an opinion before the Supreme Sharia Court in actions concerning marriage, lineage, separation, waqf and the Public Treasury, and in judgments rendered against minors and other interdicted persons, and in maintenance allowances imposed for them in their property, and if the action has a bearing on the regularity of the course of the Supreme such as capacity, and such as a request for the transfer of the action on the ground of kinship or on the ground of suspicion, and such as the designation of jurisdiction, lis pendens, connectedness, retrial, proceedings against judges for liability, and such as recusal and a request for the disqualification of judges. And in actions in which legal aid has been granted, and upon the express request of the court, or if an offence is committed during the trial.

Actions are divided in terms of form into principal claims and incidental claims. A principal claim is that from which the action originates, and an incidental claim is that which arises during the hearing of the action.

An incidental claim is called additional if submitted by the plaintiff, a counterclaim if submitted by the defendant, and an intervention if submitted by a third party. Every claim that arises during the hearing of the action and is not of a nature to broaden or narrow the subject-matter of the principal claim shall be considered an incident of the trial.

For an incidental claim to be admissible, it is required that it be:

1- Connected with the principal claim. This is realised when the solution required by one of them affects the solution required for the other.

2- Not outside the absolute jurisdiction of the court.

The following shall be exempted from the provisions of the preceding Article:

1- Claims aimed at compensation for the litigation in the principal claim.

2- Claims aimed at effecting set-off or at defence in the principal claim.

3- Claims aimed at taking a conservatory or provisional measure.
Litigants must invoke the inadmissibility of hearing the incidental claim for lack of connectedness before arguing on the merits, failing which their right to do so shall lapse.

If no dispute arises regarding the admission of the intervention or the joinder, or if it is decided to admit it, the third party may invoke all effective procedural pleas and request any investigation he deems useful. Either of the two parties may bring a counterclaim against him regarding the rights he alleges.

If one of the litigants is entitled to compel a person to defend him in the trial or to offer him total or partial compensation for the damage to which he is exposed as a result of a judgment being rendered against him, he may join this person in the trial by summoning him thereto for the purpose of warranty.

The warranty claim shall not be admitted before the court hearing the original action in the following cases:

1- If it falls outside its absolute jurisdiction.

2- If there is an agreement between the warrantor and the warranted party placing the right to hear the warranty case within the jurisdiction of another court.

3- If there is an action concerning the warranty itself that is still pending before another court.
The person summoned in warranty may in turn summon in warranty another person who is bound to warrant him. The court may shorten the time limits and compel him to provide security.

The party who summoned a person as his warrantor may withdraw from the trial with the consent of the litigants so that the latter may replace him therein. The judgment shall then be rendered binding on all and on the party who withdrew from the trial.

A substantive defence consists in directly denying the plaintiff's right or in raising a claim capable of extinguishing this right, such as prescription, set-off, res judicata, and a term for payment.

A procedural plea consists in contesting the regularity of the trial or in requesting a time limit, such as an objection to jurisdiction, a request for security, lis pendens, relatedness, nullity of the summons, a request for the transfer of the action for legitimate suspicion or for consanguinity or affinity, and a request for an extension of time and for the service of documents.

Grounds of substantive defence shall be heard at every stage of the trial. As for grounds of procedural plea, they must be raised together at the commencement of the trial prior to arguing the merits, under pain of dismissal, with the exception of those that arise or become apparent thereafter.

In this case, they must be raised prior to resuming the argument on the merits.
An action shall be brought before the court of the defendant's domicile, and if he has an elected domicile, it may be instituted before the court of his elected domicile.
If the defendant has no domicile, the action shall be brought before the court of the plaintiff's domicile.
If there are multiple defendants in the action, it may be instituted against all of them before the court of the domicile of one of them.

An action relating to a will, inheritance, and waqf deed shall be instituted before the court of the defendant's domicile or the court within whose jurisdiction the real property of the estate or of the waqf is located, in whole or for the greater part thereof.

An action concerning marriage and the prompt dower arising therefrom shall be instituted before the court of the defendant's domicile or the court of the place where the contract was concluded, and an action for separation, divorce, and the deferred dower arising therefrom shall be instituted before either of these two courts or before the court of the place where the incident constituting the cause of the action occurred.

An action for custody, maintenance, and remuneration for custody and suckling shall be instituted before the court of the domicile of the plaintiff or of the defendant if the action is brought by the wife and the mother or the female custodian. The same applies to an action for maintenance against an absentee submitted by one of the ascendants or descendants.

The court of the deceased's domicile and the court within whose jurisdiction the real property of the estate is located, in whole or for the greater part thereof, shall have jurisdiction to inventory the estate. However, the outcome of the proceeding must be consolidated in the court of the place of residence.

The court having sole jurisdiction:

1- To grant permission for marriage is the court of either of the applicants for marriage.

2- To appoint the administrator (mutawalli) of a family waqf and to grant the guardian and the administrator of a family waqf permission regarding the administration of the affairs of the minor or the waqf is the court of the domicile of the natural guardian, the appointed guardian, or the administrator, or the court within whose jurisdiction the real property of the minor- or of the founder of the waqf is located, in whole or for the greater part thereof.

3- To issue a certificate of limitation of succession is the court of the deceased's domicile or the court within whose jurisdiction- the real property of the estate is located, in whole or for the greater part thereof.

4- To appoint a guardian is the court of the domicile of the deceased or of the ward.
A lawsuit which multiple courts have jurisdiction to hear, as set forth above, may not, after it has been instituted before one of those courts, be referred to another court in respect thereof.
A change that occurs in the place of residence after the filing of the lawsuit shall not prevent the continuation of the hearing thereof before the court before which it was instituted.

An objection to the jurisdiction referred to in Articles 63, 64, 65, 66, 67 and 68 of this Chapter shall not be admitted unless it is submitted at the outset of the lawsuit and prior to any defence on the merits, and the judge shall not have the right to declare his lack of jurisdiction of his own motion.
The court may decide upon the objection raised to its jurisdiction by a separate decision, or join it to the merits and decide upon both together by a single decision.

If a lawsuit is instituted before a court, and that lawsuit or another lawsuit connected therewith is subsequently instituted before a second Sharia court, the defendant shall have the right to request this court to refer that lawsuit to the first court.

In cases where the hearing of the lawsuit depends upon special leave from the court, the court having jurisdiction to hear it in accordance with the rules mentioned above is the one that shall grant the required leave, and such leave shall be valid for litigation in the lawsuit on appeal.

If a lawsuit is instituted against a minor, an interdicted person, or a waqf that has no natural guardian, testamentary guardian, or mutawalli, or against an estate that has no known heir, the plaintiff shall have the right to request the court having jurisdiction to hear that lawsuit to appoint a temporary guardian, mutawalli, or curator for the litigation until a permanent guardian or mutawalli is appointed or an heir to the estate appears.

If the same lawsuit is brought before two courts of first instance of the same denomination and each of them decides that it has jurisdiction to hear it or, conversely, that it lacks jurisdiction to examine it, and the decision rendered in both of them has become final, this conflict shall be resolved by an application for the designation of the competent court submitted to the Supreme Court concerned.
A plea of absolute lack of jurisdiction shall be admissible at all stages of the trial. The court or the Public Prosecution may raise it of its own motion.
A defendant who invokes any plea capable of resulting in the dismissal of the action or the annulment of the trial shall submit his pleadings and claims on the merits in the alternative.
The court may rule on the pleas separately or join them to the merits.

A court before which a plea of lis pendens or of connectedness with an action brought before another court is submitted shall decline jurisdiction over the action and refer it as a matter of urgency:

1- To the court that has issued, in the action pending before it, a preparatory decision not limited to an administrative measure, unless a third party to the judgment opposes that.

2- To the court hearing the principal action, if the second action is based on an obligation of warranty.

3- To the court before which the dispute was first brought, unless it is established that the plea was intended to vex the adversary.

Any defect in the writ of summons with respect to service, the designation of the court, or the date of the hearing, or for failure to observe the time limit for appearance, shall be cured by the mere appearance of the person to whom it was addressed, without prejudice to his right to request the completion of the time limit.

In matters of inheritance, bequest, and endowment (waqf), if the heirs, the legatees, or the beneficiaries of the endowment belong to two different sects, the court of the sect of the deceased or of the founder of the endowment shall have jurisdiction.

The court of the sect of the husband shall have jurisdiction to grant permission for marriage and to hear actions relating to marriage, separation, and matters connected therewith when one of the spouses is Sunni and the other is Shiite.

If the spouses agree in the body of the marriage contract to designate the sectarian court to which they shall have recourse, that court alone shall have jurisdiction; however, with respect to the inheritance of one of the spouses upon his death, recourse for its division and the settlement of disputes concerning it shall in all cases be had to the court of the deceased husband or the deceased wife.

If the party making an admission claims that he is untruthful in his admission, it shall not be accepted from him and he shall be held to his admission, unless his untruthfulness is established by the judgment of the judge or by the refutation of the opposing party.
An admission made outside the session of the judge must be proved by one of the Sharia evidences.

If one of the parties denies the handwriting, signature, or fingerprint attributed to him in the document produced against him, and such document is material to the lawsuit, a comparison of the handwriting, signature, and fingerprint shall be conducted in accordance with the provisions stipulated in the Code of Civil Procedure.

If one of the parties alleges the forgery of the produced documents, whether official or unofficial, in proof of the lawsuit or in defence against it, and the other party insists on relying thereon, the judge may, if he finds that the alleged forgery has an effect on the outcome of the judgment, stay the proceedings of the lawsuit and grant the party alleging forgery a time limit to institute proceedings in respect thereof before the competent criminal authority.
A lawsuit may be proved by the testimony of witnesses of just character, subject to the following provisions:

In financial matters falling within the jurisdiction of the Sharia courts, if the lawsuit is based on an instrument, no defence against it shall be heard except by way of an instrument, unless there is a commencement of proof in writing, in which case proof of the defence by oral evidence shall be accepted as set forth in the Code of Civil Procedure.

If the plaintiff fails to prove his lawsuit or is deemed unable to do so and requests that the oath be administered to his opponent, and the latter takes the oath or refuses to take it, judgment shall be rendered in accordance with the taking or refusal of the oath. The defendant may refer the oath back to the plaintiff. If the latter refuses to take it, his lawsuit shall be dismissed, and if he takes the oath, judgment shall be rendered in his favour.

The judge may seek the assistance of experts in auditing the accounts of guardians and administrators of family endowments (awqaf dhurriyya), and may conduct an inspection in person or through a person delegated by him in cases where rendering judgment in the lawsuit so requires.

An application for recusal must be submitted prior to any argument on the merits, failing which it shall be liable to dismissal; however, if the ground for recusal did not arise or become known until after the commencement of the arguments, the application shall be admissible within eight days from the date on which the ground arose or became known, and in such case the trial shall be adjourned until the application for recusal is adjudicated.

If the application for recusal is dismissed, its applicant shall be sentenced to a pecuniary fine of one hundred thousand Lebanese pounds to five hundred thousand Lebanese pounds, in addition to the damages that may be awarded to the judge or to the other party to the lawsuit by reason of the unlawful delay of its proceedings.
Recusal for the aforementioned grounds shall apply to experts, arbitrators and the judge of the Public Prosecution before the Supreme Court, unless he is a principal party to the lawsuit.

An application for recusal shall not be admissible in the following cases:

1- If it is directed against the bench of the Supreme Court in its entirety.

2- If it is impossible to constitute the court from appellate or first-instance judges to hear the application for recusal.

3- If it is directed against a number of first-instance judges such that it becomes impossible to delegate one of them to hear the original lawsuit.

4- If it is directed against a number of appellate judges such that it becomes impossible to constitute the bench.
A judge may not hear a lawsuit if the advocate of either party thereto is his relative by consanguinity or affinity up to the third degree, under pain of nullity of the judgment.
Evidence is that which indicates and manifests a right, and it consists of oral and written admission, testimony, oath, presumptions, the report of experts, and inspection by the judge.

For the validity of an admission in matters of marriage, divorce and lineage, it is required that the declarant be of sound mind, of full age, acting of his own free will, and not under interdiction. None of the foregoing is required in respect of the person in whose favour the admission is made. The admission of a person placed under interdiction for prodigality shall be accepted in all matters in which he is not deemed interdicted under Sharia, such as divorce.

An admission made by the defendant in a judicial session shall not be divisible; thus, that which is detrimental to him shall not be taken therefrom while leaving that which is favourable to him, rather it shall be taken as a whole and deemed a denial of the lawsuit, provided that the plaintiff has no evidence for his claim and the defendant has no evidence for his defence.

Where it becomes impossible for a Court of First Instance to perform its functions by reason of force majeure, the plaintiff shall apply to the relevant Supreme Court, and it shall designate another court to act in its stead.

Where there exists legitimate suspicion regarding a judge of first instance, either party may request the competent Supreme Court to transfer the action to another Court of First Instance. Legitimate suspicion exists where the circumstances of fact give rise to doubt as to the impartiality of the judge. If the request for transfer on the ground of legitimate suspicion is dismissed, the petitioner must be sentenced to a pecuniary fine from one hundred thousand Lebanese pounds to five hundred thousand Lebanese pounds."

The judge performing the function of the Public Prosecution shall have the right to request the competent court, pursuant to an order from the authority of the Sharia Courts, to transfer the action from a Court of First Instance to another court for the preservation of public security where the trial in that action is of a nature to cause a disturbance in the district of the court before which it is brought.

A judge shall be subject to recusal:

1- If he, his wife or his fiancée has a direct or indirect interest in the action.

2- If there is between him and one of the litigants kinship by blood or affinity in the direct line or in the collateral line up to the fourth degree.

3- If he has previously been a legal representative of one of the parties by power of attorney, paternal guardianship, testamentary guardianship or trusteeship.

4- If he has previously been a witness in the case.

5- If there exists severe enmity between him and one of the litigants. Contempt directed by one of the litigants at the judge shall not suffice to render him subject to recusal.

6- If a civil or criminal action has been brought between him and one of the litigants or one of his ascendants, descendants or relatives by affinity up to the fourth degree during the preceding five years.

7- If he has expressed his opinion in the action.

A judge of first instance or of appeal must, in the cases set forth in the preceding article, offer his abstention of his own motion, and he may not request abstention in cases other than those mentioned.

A request for recusal or abstention shall be submitted by a written declaration to the Supreme Court to which the judge belongs. The latter shall decide in chambers to accept or reject the request.

Where the request for recusal or abstention relates to an appellate judge, one of the remaining counsellors, and where that is impossible, a judge of first instance designated by its President, shall join the Supreme Court in order to complete its bench.
If the recusal or abstention of the judge of first instance is accepted, the aforementioned court shall delegate another judge of first instance to replace him in hearing the action.

Reference shall be made, with respect to the definition of presumptions, the determination of their probative force, and the instances in which recourse may be had to them, to the Code of Civil Procedure.

Time limits are of two types, namely:

1- Statutory time limits, which are those fixed pursuant to legislative texts. They may not be shortened or extended unless there is a text permitting the same.

2- Judicial time limits, which are those fixed pursuant to a ruling of the judge, who may fix them according to the circumstances of the case after hearing the interested parties.

Trial time limits shall be fixed in hours, days, or months. Time limits fixed by the month shall be calculated from the date of their commencement to the corresponding date in the following months. The duration of a day shall be calculated from midnight to the following midnight.
All trial time limits shall be deemed clear, such that the hour or the day on which the time limit commences and ends shall not be included in their calculation.
If the time limit expires on a holiday, it shall be extended ipso jure to the first working day following it.

If the person to whom the procedural act is directed resides abroad, the additional time limit provided for in the Code of Civil Procedure shall be added to the ordinary time limit:

1- A maximum of thirty days for Syria, Egypt, Iraq, and Jordan.

2- Ninety days for the countries of America, Oceania, Japan, and the Philippine Islands.

3- Sixty days for all the remaining countries. The judge may reduce or extend these time limits according to the circumstances of the case.

No person who is temporarily present in Lebanon and who can be served in person shall benefit therefrom.
The time limit for distance shall be cancelled if the person residing in a foreign country elects a domicile for himself in Lebanon.
Exceeding the time limits appointed for the exercise of a right shall entail the forfeiture of such right.

No trial measure may be carried out, and it shall be deemed null and void if carried out:

1- On official public holidays.

2- Before seven o'clock in the morning and after eight o'clock in the evening, unless the person for whom the measure is intended accepts the same, or the measure is a continuation of what was commenced during the lawful time.

The following shall be exempted from the provision of the preceding Article by order of the President of the Court:

1- Urgent and conservatory measures.

2- Procedures of service, inspection and expertise.

Litigants may appear in person before the Court of First Instance and sign the summons and the pleadings. They may seek the assistance of an advocate registered on the Roll of the Bar Association, or of a relative from among ascendants, descendants, collaterals and spouses with the leave of the Court.

Litigants may not appear or sign any document before the Supreme Court without the assistance of an advocate registered on the Roll of the Bar Association, unless the Court grants him leave to do so upon his request for exceptional reasons.
The appointment of a representative shall be effected by a power of attorney certified before the Notary Public. The appointment of a representative shall also be valid in the Sharia Court.

The representative must prove his power of attorney by producing the original or a copy thereof. The Court may verify the same at any stage of the trial. If the power of attorney is general, the representative may request its registration at the registry of the Court in a special register.
The office of the advocate shall be deemed an elected domicile for the principal at the degree of litigation in which the advocate used his power of attorney.

A power of attorney for litigation vests the representative with the authority to carry out the acts and procedures necessary to file the action, pursue it, defend therein and take conservatory measures until the issuance of the judgment at the degree of litigation for which he was appointed, and to serve notice of this judgment and collect fees and expenses, without prejudice to that for which the law requires a special authorisation.

No contrary restriction may be invoked against the adversary.

Without a special authorisation, the following shall not be valid:

1- Exercising ordinary and extraordinary means of recourse.

2- Admission, waiver, settlement, and arbitration.

3- Directing, accepting, and tendering back an oath.

4- Abandoning the action and waiving the judgment or any means of recourse.

5- Lifting attachment and precautionary entries and abandoning securities.

6- Bringing an action against judges for liability.

7- Making or accepting a real tender, or any other act of disposition for which the law requires a special authorisation.

Everything stated by the litigation representative in the presence of his principal shall be deemed as if it had issued from the latter unless he denies it, objects to it, or disavows it before the adjournment of the hearing.
The litigation representative may not substitute another lawyer in his place unless he is authorised to substitute in the power of attorney.
Where there are multiple representatives, each of them may act individually unless otherwise provided in the power of attorney.

The dismissal of a representative or his resignation from the representation shall not be effective as against the opposing party except from the day it is notified to the latter officially, or to the court by a registered letter, a petition, or a declaration.
A representative may not resign from the representation at an inopportune time.

The mere dismissal from the representation or resignation therefrom shall cancel the election of domicile at the office of the representative, and the principal must elect another domicile within a period of ten days if the law requires him to do so.
The registry of the court shall be composed of clerks and bailiffs subject to special regulations, and the president of the court shall supervise them and distribute the work among them.
The officials of the registry shall perform the duties delegated to them pursuant to this Law and other special laws and regulations.

The Chief Clerk, or the clerk deputising for him, shall receive all petitions, pleadings and documents and register them after collecting the legal fees, and shall arrange for each case a special file to which he shall assign a serial number according to the date of receipt of the action, and shall record on its cover the number, the date, the nature of the case and the identity of the litigants.
The litigants or their attorneys may inspect this file in the registry of the court and obtain copies of the papers and documents after the clerk certifies their conformity with the originals.

The clerks of the courts shall undertake the arrangement and preservation of case files, hearing rolls, trial minutes, and the registers designated for entering actions and recording decisions of whatever kind.
All registers shall be numbered, and their first page and last page shall be initialled by the President of the Court or a judge delegated by him for this purpose.

The Chief Clerk, or the clerk deputising for him, must deliver to the party in whose favour judgment was rendered a copy of the judgment appended with the phrase (A true copy valid for execution), after collecting the fees and verifying the validity of the judgment for execution. He may also deliver, after payment of the expenses and fees due on the action, a true copy to any person whomsoever.

The Sharia courts shall keep the following registers, namely:

1- The general register for entering actions.

2- The general register for deeds and all other Sharia instruments.

3- A register of final judgments.

4- A register for interlocutory decisions, namely those that do not dispose of the action.

5- A register for Sharia deeds that do not contain judgments.

6- A register for marriage contracts.

7- A register for the inventorying of estates.

8- A register for the partition and distribution of estates.

9- A register for powers of attorney.

10- A register for entering instruments and deposits.

11- A register for entering fees.

12- A ledger for permission to conclude a marriage contract.

13- A ledger for incoming correspondence.

14- A ledger for outgoing correspondence.

15- A ledger for the delivery of papers.

The registers set forth in the preceding Article shall be organised in accordance with the instructions established in respect thereof. The pages of these registers shall be numbered in words, and their total shall be recorded at the beginning and the end of the register, and the judge and the clerk shall certify this total.

As for the registers of decisions, judgments and Sharia deeds, the judge shall initial with his signature the top of each leaf thereof.

If an error or omission occurs in the minutes of the trial, judgments, decisions, or registers, it shall not be permissible to correct the error or omission by scraping out the erroneous word and interlining the omitted words; rather, the erroneous word must be struck out with a thin line and the omitted word or words must be written in the margin of the minutes, judgments, and registers, and certified by the judge or the panel of the court and the clerk.

Under no circumstances may the registers of the court be removed from its registry except by a decision of the relevant Supreme Court, and this decision shall be given either directly or upon the request of the party concerned or upon the request of the prosecution judge at the Supreme Court, and the decision shall specify with full clarity the manner of removing the registers from the registry of the court and the manner of returning them to it.
The copy given of deeds, decisions, and judgments shall be certified by the chief clerk as being in conformity with the original and signed by him together with the president of the court.
The president of the court shall supervise the regularity of the registry and the proper conduct of work therein, and he shall be responsible for any negligence in his supervision.

All judicial papers and decisions shall be served upon the party concerned in person wherever he may be found, or upon his representative, or at his domicile, residence, or place of work through the process server.

Service may also be effected within the jurisdiction of the court through the clerk, and where necessary, papers other than judicial decisions may be served through a member of the gendarmerie or the police.

A representative may not refuse service:

1- If he has previously used the power of attorney in the same case and its effect still subsists.

2- If the principal has elected a domicile with him in accordance with the rules governing the election of domicile.

Service in respect of a person who is not found at his place of residence or place of work, or in respect of the State, members of the army, seamen of merchant vessels, legal persons, or others, shall be effected in accordance with the Code of Civil Procedure or special laws.
Service may be effected at the elected domicile just as it is effected at the actual domicile, unless the law provides otherwise.

If the process server does not find anyone at the domicile, residence, or place of work of the person to be served, or if he is prevented from entering therein, or if ordinary service is impossible for any reason, extraordinary service shall be carried out.

The record of service shall include the following particulars:

1- The name and identity of each of the applicant for service, the person to whom service is addressed, and the court that ordered it.

2- The nature of the document served.

3- The place of service and the date of its occurrence.

4- The mention and delivery of the document to the person intended for service or to whoever represents him or acts on his behalf, and the mention of the name and identity of the latter and his relationship to the former.

5- The signature of the person served or his fingerprint, and if he refuses to do so, such refusal shall be indicated by a special endorsement.

6- The signature of the officer who carried out the service.

The process server must deposit the record of service with the court registry within a period not exceeding eight days, otherwise he shall be liable to pay a fine of five pounds pursuant to a final decision issued by the president of the court hearing the case.

Extraordinary service shall be carried out by sending a registered letter with acknowledgment of receipt to the person to be served to attend at the court registry in order to receive the document addressed to him, and this letter shall be sent within an envelope sealed with the seal of the court to the last known domicile or residence or to the elected domicile.

If the addressee refuses to receive the letter, the postman shall then return it without delay to the court registry appended with an indication of his refusal, and it shall be joined to the case file to serve as proof of the occurrence of service. And if the postman does not find the person to whom service is addressed at the indicated domicile, he shall endorse the fact and return the letter without delay to the trial registry.

In this case, as well as in the case where the domicile is unknown, a copy of the document shall be posted on the board designated for notices at the door of the court for a period of twenty days, and a notice informing the person to be served of the existence of a service concerning him at the court shall be published in two daily newspapers of wide local circulation. The record of service shall be replaced by a certificate from the clerk establishing the expiry of twenty days from the posting of the copy and the publication of the notice.

Whenever the service is subject to lapse if it is not completed within a specific time limit, the sending of the registered letter or the posting of the service document shall stay the running of this time limit.

Service in foreign countries shall be effected by a registered letter with acknowledgement of receipt or pursuant to the principles established in the law of those countries, unless there is a treaty stipulating a special method. Service shall be deemed to have been effected from the day the person served signs the acknowledgement of receipt or from the day he refuses to sign or to take delivery. If the letter is returned unserved, or if the legal time limits expire without the return of the letter or the acknowledgement of receipt, the court may deem the person to whom it was addressed to be of unknown domicile.

The president of the court shall examine the matter of proving ignorance of the domicile in light of the inquiry conducted by the clerk or the process server with the relatives and neighbours of the person to be served or the mukhtar of the locality where he used to reside, and the decision issued in this regard shall not be subject to any separate appeal, provided that the court may reconsider it if information comes to its knowledge indicating that the domicile is known.
The clerk of the court may delegate the clerk nearest to the place in which the person required to be served is present.
Where there are multiple attorneys and other representatives of the person required to be served, service may be effected upon one of them.

Service of pleadings and documents directly between lawyers shall be valid, particularly in urgent cases, provided that the attorney of the person intended to be served inserts a statement indicating the same on the original copy submitted to the court after affixing the stamp.

An action shall be instituted before the court of first instance pursuant to a writ of summons or an oral record comprising:

1- The designation of the court to which the action is submitted.

2- The specification of the identity of each of the litigants and his real or elected domicile or his place of residence and, where necessary, the last known domicile of the defendant.

3- A full statement of the subject matter of the action, the documents, the claims and the legal grounds supporting them.

4- A summons to the defendant to submit an answer within the legal time limit and to appear at the date and time appointed by the court for hearing the action.

A plaintiff who has no domicile in the jurisdiction of the court must designate in the writ of summons of his action an elected domicile at the seat of the court or at the office of one of the lawyers in Lebanon.

The defendant must, within fifteen days from the date of service upon him of the writ of summons and the documents:

1- Submit his answer to the action in writing in a full manner and substantiate it with such documents as he possesses.

2- Elect a domicile for himself at the seat of the court or the office of one of the lawyers in Lebanon if he has no domicile in the area falling under the jurisdiction of the court.

The plaintiff must, if he so wishes, submit his reply within ten days after being served with the pleading of the defendant. The latter shall have the right to file a rejoinder thereto within a similar time limit.

If the plaintiff and the defendant fail to declare the election of a domicile for themselves in accordance with the preceding provisions, or if the statements submitted in this regard are incomplete or inaccurate, the court registry shall be deemed as the elected domicile, and it shall then be valid to serve all papers up to the final judgment upon the clerk of the court, who shall be required to immediately post the paper on the notice board designated for announcements at the door of the court throughout the entire time limit granted for answering, appearing, or filing an application, and to draw up a record thereof which he shall attach to the case file.

The clerk shall keep the papers required to be served in this manner in a special file to be delivered to the concerned parties upon request.

Each of the litigants shall be required:

1- To state his claims clearly at the conclusion of the summons or the answering pleading, and if the pleadings are multiple, the last of them must include all the claims, and the judge shall not be bound to adjudicate upon them if they are set forth in a manner contrary to these provisions.

2- To deposit with the court registry a number of copies of the summons, pleadings, or documents produced by him equal to the number of his adversaries having distinct interests, in order to be served upon them.

3- To produce the originals of the documents upon which he relies if the court so orders of its own motion or at the request of the adversary; otherwise, it shall suffice to submit a copy thereof certified as conforming to the original.

The President of the Court or the Single Judge may shorten the time limits provided for in Articles 152 and 154 of this Law down to twenty-four hours whenever necessity so requires on account of urgency, and in particular in urgent matters, and no appeal shall lie against his decision issued in this regard. However, the court may, when hearing the action, modify the prescribed time limit if it sees grounds to do so.

After the expiry of the time limits set forth in the preceding Articles, no new claim, pleading, or document shall be admitted unless the court orders it and fixes a time limit therefor, in the event of an acceptable excuse, the consent of the adversary, or the emergence of new facts such as waiver, settlement, or oath. Nevertheless, if the court deems it in the interest of the realization of justice to admit the claim or the paper, it may sentence the negligent adversary to a fine ranging from ten to fifty pounds. It may also order of its own motion the submission of supplementary memoranda or documents regarding such points of the action as are deemed to require further examination, within time limits that it fixes for this purpose.
