And the party subject to attachment is requested to submit his title deeds relating to ownership relating to the attachment of real property upon a copy of the enforceable instrument, with an election of domicile in the locality where the court of jurisdiction sits - and to specify therein the type of real property parcels sought to be attached, their appurtenances, their area, their boundaries and their numbers - all in accordance with the particulars - entered in the cadastral map and the Land Register and it must also be stated in the formal notice document

The formal notice and the notification provided for in Articles 721, 723, shall have no effect with respect to a third party except from the time of their registration in the real folio of the real property and the Execution Department must request of its own motion and within forty-eight hours at most, that this registration be carried out through the auxiliary Land Registry Office located in the locality of the real property and from the date of this registration the party subject to attachment may not conclude a lease of the real property sought to be attached, nor assign in advance the consideration for finding it to the detriment of the interest of the attaching party

The sending of the formal notice to the party subject to attachment, and the sending of the notification where applicable, must take place at least five days, and at most ten days, before the attachment
Provided that a creditor who holds an enforceable instrument may request the sending of the formal notice and the drawing up of the attachment record at the same time, as stated in Article 665

The third party in whose hands the attachment for recovery of title is levied, and the debtor affected by this attachment, may apply for its lifting by way of summoning the attaching party before the Civil Court. And the prohibition on disposing of the movables shall not cease save pursuant to the judgment that shall be rendered.

After drawing up the record pertaining to the attachment for recovery of title in accordance with the same rules pertaining to executive attachment, the creditor shall apply for the summoning of the debtor or the owner shall apply for the summoning of the holder of the movable property, before the Civil Court within eight days to validate the attachment, and if the time limit of the eight days is not observed, the attachment for recovery of title shall become void.
The judgment validating the attachment shall order that the disputed movable property be restored to the place in which it must be, or that its holder return it to the true owner.

The creditors of a merchant may, upon the conditions set forth in the general law, levy an executive attachment upon the goods and equipment, just as they may attach the debts owed to the merchant on the basis of attachment in the hands of a third party. However, they may not levy attachment upon the other intangible elements of the commercial establishment nor upon the establishment as a whole.
If the standing crop has not been severed from the land, it may not be attached separately from the immovable property, save in the six weeks preceding the time of its maturity.
The standing crop shall be attached against its owner in accordance with the rule of executive attachment.

The aforementioned attachment shall be preceded by a formal notice, and shall be effected by drawing up a record ordering the prohibition on disposing of the crop, and no custodian shall be appointed therefor.

The right to harvest the standing crop shall be sold by auction for the benefit of the attaching party; however, if maturity has reached a degree where it is feared that the fruits may sustain damage, the attaching party may obtain from the Head of the Execution Department a decision authorising him to harvest the standing crop himself, whereupon the harvested fruits shall be sold by auction and the attaching party shall recover first from the price thereof what he expended on harvesting the standing crop.

The enforcement officer or the process server shall proceed to the immovable property intended to be attached and shall levy the attachment, and this record must contain a statement of the enforceable instrument, mention of proceeding to the location of the immovable property, identification of this immovable property in accordance with the provisions of Article 724 - and a general description of the buildings, if any, and the designation of the court that will hear the attachment.

If the attachment covers at the same time several immovable properties located within the jurisdictions of different courts, a separate attachment proceeding must, in principle, be carried out for each of them before the competent court.

However, if the immovable properties intended to be attached are contiguous or form part of a single exploitation project, a single attachment shall be carried out for them before the court of the locality in which the centre of the project is situated or in which the most significant of the immovable properties is situated, and if the immovable properties intended to be attached are not contiguous or do not form part of a single exploitation project, a single attachment may be levied upon them provided that they fall within the jurisdiction of the same court. A single attachment shall be levied if the attaching creditor requests it.

In this case, the enforcement officer may, when he undertakes himself or through the process server the attachment of the immovable properties falling within the jurisdiction of his court, deputise his colleagues at the other courts to levy the attachment upon the immovable properties falling within their jurisdictions, and request them to send the attachment records to be joined to the original attachment record.

If the attachment falls upon several immovable properties all located within the jurisdiction of a single court, they shall be attached on the same day and pursuant to a single record. If attaching them in this manner is not possible, they shall be attached in multiple instalments pursuant to successive records. However, in this case, all the records must be drawn up between the fifth and tenth days following the dispatch of the formal notice, under penalty of nullity.

If the owner of the attached immovable property is not present when the attachment record is drawn up, the Execution Department shall send him a copy thereof between the tenth and fifteenth days following the dispatch of the formal notice.

Within the same time limit, the attachment record itself must be registered in the real folio of the immovable property; otherwise, the registration of the formal notice shall be struck off pursuant to a decision by the Head of the Execution Department establishing the lapse by the expiry of the statutory period.

As of the completion of the aforementioned registration, the debtor subject to attachment may neither sell the immovable property or a part thereof, nor subdivide its ownership, nor mortgage it, and he cannot collect the fruits of the immovable property. The rules of the Civil Law shall apply with respect to the distinction between civil fruits and natural fruits.

Within the twenty-four hours following the seizure report, the enforcement officer shall prohibit the lessee or the sharecropper from paying the rent or the agricultural return to the execution debtor. This prohibition shall be notified by a registered letter accompanied by an acknowledgment of receipt. Any payment made after the receipt of this letter shall be null and void.

If the execution debtor occupies the immovable property and the seizing creditor has not requested the Head of Enforcement to issue an order for eviction, the execution debtor shall remain in enjoyment of the immovable property until the time of sale by auction, and he shall remain entitled to gather and consume the fruits necessary for his livelihood and the livelihood of his family. In this case, the execution debtor must render an account of the surplus fruits and preserve them in kind if their preservation is possible; otherwise, he shall deliver them to the enforcement officer, who shall sell them without delay and keep their price to be added to the price of the immovable property.

The Head of the Enforcement Department may order the execution debtor to vacate if it appears that his remaining in the immovable property causes prejudice to the interests of the creditors. He may also decide this eviction of his own motion if the execution debtor, after being left in the immovable property, has caused damage thereto or abused the enjoyment thereof.
The registration of the seizure report in the Land Register confers upon the seizing creditor a real right over the immovable property.

If a third party wishes to purchase from the execution debtor the ownership rights of the immovable property, he must, in order to be able to register his deed, deposit a sum of money sufficient to satisfy the debt encumbering the immovable property and to pay the amount of the expenses, and the effect of this deposit shall be the lifting of the seizure registered on the folio pertaining to the immovable property, and the right provided for in the first paragraph shall lapse by virtue of the adjudication decision.

If the third party considers that the debt claimed by the seizing creditor, or by another creditor whose name is entered on the list, must be reduced or cancelled, he may, though only after depositing the amount of the apparent debts, obtain a decision reducing them to the true amount and recover from the money which he deposited whatever exceeds this amount.

From the time of the registration of the seizure report in the Land Register, the seizing creditor must be joined as a party in the lawsuits relating to the immovable property brought against the execution debtor or brought by him.

Failure to observe the time limits set forth above, between the formal notice and the seizure report and its registration in the Land Register, entails the annulment of the proceeding, which shall be repeated at the expense of the enforcement officer.
The conditions of sale, whether or not rectified by the enforcement department, shall become unalterable upon the expiry of the time limit of eight days provided for in Article 748.

The enforcement officer shall thereupon extract a summary from the conditions of sale in order to publish it both in the form of notices in the newspapers designated for the publication of judicial notices, and in the form of bills posted on public roads. Publication in both of these manners must take place at most thirty days and at least fifteen days prior to the auction.

Such summary must include the date of the attachment and the date of its registration, the designation of the attaching creditor and the attached debtor, a description of the immovable property as ascertained from the attachment record, the reserve price fixed for the bidding, the date and time of the auction and the place where it is to be held, and a specification of the expenses which the purchaser must pay in addition, after the head of the enforcement department has determined the amount thereof.

It is the head of the enforcement department who determines the number of publications in the newspapers according to the nature and importance of the attached property, as well as the number of bills to be posted on walls.

In all cases, the notices of sale must be posted at the following places at least: 1 The domicile of the attached debtor 2 The doors of the attached immovable properties 3 The municipal hall, and if there is none, on the door of the residence of the mukhtar in the locality of the immovable property 4 The notice board at the department of the court before which the sale proceedings are conducted
The bailiff shall draw up, at the foot of a copy of the notice, a record certifying that the notice was posted in the various places indicated above, without need to itemise them.

The auction shall be held in a special sitting convened by the Civil Court, whereupon the bailiff shall call the sale by repeating the amount of the reserve price, and the bidding shall proceed successively, and the President may fix a minimum increment for each bid.
Adjudication shall be ordered in favour of the last bidder who offered the highest price.

Within the eight days following the registration of the attachment record in the Real Estate Register, the attaching party shall draw up the book of conditions upon which the auction is based, and it must include a mention of the acts preceding the transaction, the designation of the real properties in accordance with what is contained in the attachment record, and the designation of the rights pertaining to them and the encumbrances and easements upon them, as shown in the real folio of the property - and there shall also be stated therein the origin of ownership and the month, day, hour, and place in which the auction will take place, together with the conditions of sale and the fixing of the reserve price.
The day appointed for the auction must be at least forty days and at most fifty-five days after the registration of the attachment record.
The head of the Enforcement Department shall fix the reserve price by making it equivalent to six-tenths of the amount at which the value of the real property is appraised.

If no bidders come forward on the day appointed for the auction, the court shall fix the amount by which it reduces the reserve price and shall then adjourn the date of the sale for at least one month and at most six months. The registration of the attachment record prevents the disposal of the fruits of the attached property and of its revenues, and there shall be distributed - as the price of the real property is distributed - such of them as pertain to the period subsequent to the registration of the said record.

In the period intervening between the eighth day and the fifteenth day from the date of registration of the attachment, the enforcement officer shall send a notice to each of the persons who have a real right over the real property, requiring them thereby to attend at the Enforcement Department to inspect the book of conditions and submit their observations, where necessary, within eight days beginning from the date of the last notice.
As for the observations which the persons notified in this manner deem appropriate to submit, they shall be delivered in error to the enforcement officer.

If the purpose of those observations is to consider what is appropriate to amend of the entries of the book of conditions or to introduce an advisable addition thereto, the head of the Enforcement Department shall consider what he deems appropriate and shall rectify or complete, where necessary, the said book.

If, however, the observations relate to the legality of the book of conditions, the head of the Enforcement Department shall rectify this book or notify the person who submitted them that it is incumbent upon him to request from the Civil Court, prior to the auction, the annulment of that book - and the enforcement officer shall send this notification by registered letter accompanied by an acknowledgment of receipt.
If the annulment of one of the measures is adjudged, its annulment shall result in the nullity of all the measures that succeeded it.
A judgment dismissing an application for annulment shall also order, where appropriate, the continuation of the enforcement, and may order the application of Articles 31, 32.
Every person shall have the right, within the ten days following the adjudication, to submit to the Enforcement Department a declaration offering an outbidding on the price.
The outbidder must undertake in his declaration to purchase the immovable property at a price exceeding the original price fixed in the adjudication by one-sixth thereof.

The enforcement officer shall not accept the offer of outbidding unless the outbidder provides a sufficient guarantee, or deposits in the treasury of one of the banks approved by the Government an amount equivalent to the value of the outbidding. The outbidder must also state in his declaration that he has elected a domicile in the locality where the court sits if he does not reside therein, failing which the registry of this court shall ipso facto be deemed an elected domicile for him.

Within the three days following the declaration of the offer of outbidding, the enforcement officer must serve this declaration upon the purchaser, failing which he shall be liable to a fine of five to twenty-five L.S.P.

Prior to the additional auction, the same publication procedure that took place prior to the first auction must be carried out, provided that the amount of the offered outbidding must be stated in the notices instead of the initial price that was set for the opening of the bidding, and the additional auction shall take place according to the same formalities.
No further outbidding shall be accepted after the adjudication that follows the additional auction.

The adjudication discharges from the real property all registrations of privileges, mortgages, and actions for rescission belonging to the persons who were notified of the obligation to inspect the book of conditions, provided that it preserves the rights divested from the right of ownership, such as the right of usufruct, the right of easement, and others.

The registration of the attachment of real property may be struck off upon the request of the attaching creditor if he agrees on striking it off with the attached debtor, and the attaching creditor shall then bear the expenses that were incurred, and the President of the Execution Department shall determine the amount thereof.

If the writs of notification of the obligation to inspect the book of conditions have been sent, the registration of the attachment may not be struck off except with the consent of the creditors to whom they were sent.

If the applicant for the compulsory sale of the real property has failed, for any reason whatsoever, to perform one of the formalities within the legal time limits, or if this applicant has failed to perform one of the formalities prior to the submission of an application for subrogation, every creditor entered on the list or holder of an enforceable title shall then have the right to request the President of the Execution Department to summon the applicant for the compulsory sale alone and to subrogate him in the place of this applicant in the rights of prosecution. The President of Execution shall adjudicate the case as he adjudicates summary matters.
The applicant may not prevent the subrogation by offering to continue the formalities.
If judgment in the subrogation case is rendered against the applicant, he must deliver all the papers of the formality to the subrogated party, failing which he shall be liable to pay damages.
Raising the nullity of the formality of the attachment of real property remains possible provided that the adjudication is decided.

The action for annulment shall be brought before the Civil Court, and the litigation shall not stay the course of the attachment unless the Court deems it appropriate to order the stay thereof for serious reasons.

Every person who wishes to participate in the auction must, prior to its commencement, prove to the Execution Department either the provision of sufficient security, or the deposit of an amount equivalent to the upset price in one of the banks approved by the Government, whereupon the Execution Department shall give him a certificate which he shall produce before the court in order to be admitted to the auction, and such person must also elect domicile in the locality where the court sits if he does not reside therein, failing which the registry of the court shall ipso jure be deemed his elected domicile.
Every higher bid, even if void, shall extinguish the bid that preceded it.

From the issuance of the judgment ordering the adjudication, the purchaser shall be entitled to have it vacated within forty-eight hours. If he refuses, the Head of the Execution Department may evict him therefrom by means of the public force.

Within twenty days commencing from the date of the adjudication, the purchaser must pay to the Execution Department all the amounts due from him, which shall deposit them in one of the banks approved by the Government, and submit therewith the documents proving his fulfilment of the obligations by submission to the Head of the Execution Department, with the reservation of the right of appeal before the Court of Appeal.
Decisions limited to postponing the sale shall be subject neither to opposition nor to appeal.

The decision of adjudication shall not be subject to opposition; however, within five days from the date of its pronouncement, and solely on the ground of a defect in its form, it may be referred to the Court of Appeal pursuant to a writ of summons for three clear days, which shall rule thereon by a decision not subject to opposition.
The decision of adjudication shall be registered in the Land Register at the request of the Execution Department after it has acquired the force of res judicata.

From the day following the adjudication, the bidders to whom the auction was not awarded shall be entitled to recover the amount of the deposit which they deposited in order to participate in the auction.

The decision ordering adjudication in the supplementary auction shall annul the rights of the purchaser and substitute for him, with retroactive effect, the person who purchased in the supplementary auction, whereas all other effects pertaining to the first adjudication shall remain standing.

If twenty days elapse and the purchaser does not perform his obligations, the auction may be repeated to sell the real property at his responsibility upon the request of the attaching party or of one of the creditors registered in the list, or upon the mere request of the head of the enforcement department.

The head of the enforcement department shall send a notice to the purchaser demanding therein payment of the price and warning him of the resale of the real property at his responsibility by auction if he does not pay within three days.

If the time limit of the days expires to no avail, the enforcement department shall proceed with the formality of publication in the newspapers and on walls as takes place in attachment, and it must be mentioned in the notices that the sale is taking place at the responsibility of the defaulting purchaser, and there must be stated therein the initial price that was set for the opening bid and the price at which the first adjudication concluded.

The defaulting purchaser shall have the right, until the second adjudication, to stay the proceeding conducted at his responsibility, by paying what became due from him in his capacity as a participant in the auction that followed the attachment, together with all the expenses that resulted from his delay.
The auction at the responsibility of the defaulting purchaser shall be conducted in accordance with the forms observed in the attachment auction and on the basis of the same book of conditions.
The auction conducted at the responsibility of the defaulting purchaser shall annul his rights and substitute for him, with retroactive effect, the person to whom that adjudication was made.

If the sale in the auction held at the responsibility of the defaulting purchaser takes place for an amount exceeding the amount at which the first auction concluded, the liability of the defaulting purchaser shall not be discharged unless the new purchaser actually pays the price. The defaulting purchaser shall not benefit from the difference in price; rather, the benefit shall accrue first to the creditors and then to the party subject to attachment.

Where a mortgagee or preferential creditor has the right of priority in the distribution of the price arising from the sale of the property upon which the mortgage was contracted or upon which the preference accrued, such creditor shall retain the right to claim as an ordinary creditor for the satisfaction of the entirety of his debt out of the price realized from the sale of the remainder of the debtor's properties, and the participation of the creditor in the distribution of such price shall be admitted regardless of his right of priority over the other properties subject to the mortgage or preference; however, his share may be reduced so that he does not ultimately receive more than what is due to him.

Where the properties mortgaged to one of the creditors or upon which a preference has accrued to him have not been sold at the time of distributing the remainder of what the debtor owns, the mortgagee or preferential creditor shall be treated, with respect to that remainder, as an ordinary creditor is treated, and if that creditor subsequently recovers, by virtue of the mortgage or preference he holds, an amount equal to the total of his debt, or an amount which, if added to what he received in the first distribution, exceeds such debt, the excess shall be distributed through the agency of the execution officer proportionally among the creditors who participated in the first distribution.

Where several attachments are levied upon several properties of one of the debtors, the amounts arising from the sale of the attached properties shall be combined, so far as possible, into a single pool and distributed in a single distribution.

Where the defendant is adjudged to pay damages for a criminal offence committed by him against the plaintiff, or a civil delict committed by him intentionally, the creditor shall be entitled to invoke a request for his imprisonment in order to obtain the damages and judicial costs, and the Public Prosecution may invoke this same right in order to obtain the fines and judicial costs in criminal actions.

The creditor shall send, through the Execution Department, a formal notice to the debtor upon service of the judgment, or shall give formal notice pursuant to a separate instrument after service of the judgment.

After the expiry of five days, the creditor shall petition the Public Prosecution at the Civil Court to issue an order for the imprisonment of the debtor after proving to it that the formal notice was sent in advance.

The debtor shall be arrested pursuant to the order of the Public Prosecution and by means of the public force, and the regime applicable to the imprisonment of perpetrators of misdemeanours shall be applied to him.

The debtor may, upon his arrest, request to appear before the President of the Court in his capacity as Judge of Urgent Matters. If it appears to the President that the legal conditions required for his imprisonment were not observed, he may issue an order for his release.
If the enforcement officer succeeds in obtaining the consent of all the creditors, he shall request them to sign the distribution schedule, whereupon it shall become final.

And if agreement is reached on only part of the schedule, the enforcement officer shall record this partial agreement by the signing of the signatures of all of them, and shall deliver to the creditors whom all have agreed upon placing in the first rank - warrants drawn on the cash office of the bank to which the deposit was delivered.
And if it appears that any agreement is impossible, the creditors shall be summoned to hold another meeting within five days at most in the presence of the President of the Enforcement Department.

The absence of one of the creditors shall not preclude an amicable settlement, unless such settlement does not include the full satisfaction of his right, and such absence shall entail the imposition of a fine of five pounds to fifty L.S. pounds, ordered by the President of the Enforcement Department, which may be revoked if there is a substantial excuse.

After the President of the Enforcement Department hears the statements of the interested parties and strives to reconcile them, he himself shall draw up a schedule for distribution and serve it upon the attached debtor and the creditors within the five days following the meeting.

Every creditor and the attached debtor shall have the right, within five days commencing from the date the service reaches them, to file an objection to the distribution schedule before the Civil Court, by requesting the summoning of the objector to their debts or to the rank of their priority.

The Court shall join all the objections directed against each distribution, and shall prefer by a single judgment comprising a complete and final settlement that includes the determination of the amount allocated to each creditor.

In execution of the distribution schedule, whether amicable or judicial, the enforcement officer shall deliver to each creditor a warrant equivalent to the amount of his share drawn on the cash office of the bank in which the money was deposited.

If the award is decided at a price lower than the price fixed in the first award, the defaulting purchaser must pay the difference to the Enforcement Department, and this obligation shall be secured either by the suretyship or by the deposit which he deposited prior to the auction, and in the event of insufficiency, it shall be enforced against the value of his wealth.
Bidding at the risk and expense of the defaulting purchaser is permissible after each award.

If it becomes apparent after any attachment, that the money resulting from the sale of the attached property is sufficient to pay the expenses and to satisfy the attaching creditor and the other creditors who have appeared by lodging other attachments, or oppositions, to satisfy the creditors whose names are registered or the preferential creditors if they exist and have declared themselves to the Enforcement Department, the enforcement officer shall send as soon as possible, and within a period not exceeding ten days from the date of the sale, an order to each creditor drawn on the bank in which the deposit provided for in Article 763 was placed, and the value of this order shall be equivalent to what is due to that creditor, and he shall also send to the attached debtor an order for the remainder if there is a remainder, and if the case is contrary to the foregoing, the distribution procedure shall take place.

The enforcement officer shall send of his own motion, or upon the request of one of the creditors, within ten days from the date of the sale which took place pursuant to the executory attachment, or from the date on which the decision awarding the attached immovable property was registered in the Land Register, a registered letter to all the right holders accompanied by an acknowledgment of receipt, whereby he requires them to send to him in the same manner within eight days, a request for payment in which they state their instruments and the amounts of their debts.

Within the ten days following the receipt by the enforcement officer of the last request for payment, the said officer shall summon the right holders by a registered letter accompanied by an acknowledgment of receipt, and the summons must reach them at least five days prior to the day of the meeting at the Enforcement Department, and it must be expressly requested of them in the summons, that they bring the instruments of their debts.

The creditors shall attend in person or through their representatives, and the attached debtor shall also be summoned. Then the enforcement officer shall present to the creditors the draft which he has drawn up for the distribution, granting priority therein to the enforcement expenses, then to the preferential or mortgage creditors according to their ranks, and finally to the holders of ordinary debts who have made their rights known to him by the oppositions they have submitted, allotting to each of these ordinary creditors what is proportional to his right, and the enforcement officer shall receive the observations of the creditors and diligently endeavour to induce them to accept his draft.

Imprisonment for debt shall not apply to persons whose age is less than fifteen years, or exceeds sixty-five years, nor to persons in respect of whom bankruptcy proceedings are still ongoing, and to those who are in the direct line of kinship of the creditor (that is, his direct line of lineage), nor to the spouse of the creditor
If the husband and the wife have children whose age is less than fifteen years, imprisonment for debt may not be inflicted upon them at one time

The period of imprisonment shall be in proportion to the amount of the debt; thus, it is ten days if the amount adjudged does not exceed five Lebanese-Syrian pounds - and one month if the amount varies between five and twenty-five pounds - and two months if it is between five and fifty pounds - and three months if it is between fifty and one hundred pounds - and four months if it is between one hundred and two hundred pounds - and six months for every amount exceeding this limit. The period of imprisonment shall not be calculated with regard to the principal of the debt only, but with regard to the accessories and the expenses also
The subsistence expenses during the period of imprisonment for debt shall be borne by the State, and it shall retain the right of recourse against the judgment debtor after he becomes solvent

Imprisonment for debt shall terminate: 1- If the judgment debtor discharges his debt or another person pays it on his behalf, or the creditor consents to his release, pursuant to a declaration submitted by the creditor to the Execution Department, which sends it without delay to the Public Prosecution 2- If the judgment debtor reaches the age of sixty-five 3- If the judgment debtor furnishes a solvent surety and this surety takes upon himself an undertaking to discharge within - within eight days within eight

A judgment debtor imprisoned upon the request of one of the creditors may be kept in imprisonment upon a request submitted by another creditor to the Public Prosecution in accordance with the provisions of Article 811
A pardon or amnesty that extinguishes penal judgments shall have no effect on imprisonment executed upon the request of one of the creditors

In a civil contract and a commercial contract, the contracting parties may agree among themselves that difficulties arising from the interpretation of the contract or from its performance shall be resolved by arbitrators
They may also agree that those difficulties shall be resolved in accordance with the provisions of a foreign law or a foreign custom.
The validity of the arbitration clause shall be subject to the provisions of the law to which the effects of the contract are subject.
The arbitration clause permits the party who has been wrongfully summoned before one of the courts to invoke the plea known as "plea of lack of jurisdiction".

The arbitration clause permits each party of the contracting parties to serve notice upon the other party of the obligation to conclude an arbitration agreement providing for the submission of any difficulty that has arisen out of the contract to an arbitral tribunal.

If the party served with notice refuses, it shall be for the other party to summon him before the civil court, which shall sentence him to pay damages if the arbitration clause is valid, and in this case the judgment shall fix for the defendant a time limit to accept an arbitration agreement conforming to what the arbitration clause imposed upon him; if the time limit expires and the defendant remains persistent in the refusal, it shall adjudicate upon the claims of the plaintiff on the merits.
If there is no arbitration clause, the contracting parties may agree to establish an arbitration agreement to submit the difficulty on account of which they have differed to an arbitral tribunal.

Provided that the establishment of the arbitration agreement shall only be permissible between contracting parties who have the requisite capacity for compromise and in a dispute capable of compromise on account of which Article 408 or other legal texts do not require the Public Prosecution to submit its opinion.

The arbitration agreement must specify the matter or matters in dispute, and must include the appointment of the arbitrator or arbitrators together with the fixing of their remuneration, and it may provide for the application of a foreign law or a foreign custom. And it may not be proved by witnesses or by presumptions.

The contract may provide for the appointment of a sole arbitrator, or provide that each party may appoint an arbitrator. In this case, the arbitrators of the contracting parties shall appoint an additional arbitrator who shall have the casting vote. If the arbitrators of the contracting parties are unable to agree on the selection of the additional arbitrator, he shall be appointed pursuant to a decision by the President of the Court rendered upon the request of the first to act and of the two parties.

Jurisdiction to issue the aforementioned decision shall vest in the President of the Court that would have had jurisdiction and had the arbitration contract not existed, or in the President of the Court - within whose district is located the Magistrate who would have had jurisdiction had that contract not existed.
The arbitration clause may appoint the arbitrator or arbitrators in advance by designating their capacity. It is not necessary to designate their identity and in another manner.
The arbitration clause may provide for ordinary arbitration or for absolute arbitration, and in case of doubt, ordinary arbitration shall be presumed to be intended.
In ordinary arbitration, the arbitrators shall apply the rules of law and the rules of procedure if they are unable to reconcile the disputing parties.

An arbitral award shall not have enforceable force until after it acquires the enforcement formula. It shall acquire this formula by a decision issued by the President of the Court upon a request in this regard if the arbitration took place in the territory of the Lebanese Republic.
Difficulties arising from the enforcement of the arbitral award shall be adjudicated in the court of the judge who issued the decision granting the enforcement formula.

An arbitral award is not subject to opposition, but it is always subject to appeal, either before the Civil Court if the dispute - had the arbitration contract not existed - fell within the jurisdiction of the Magistrate Court, or before the Court of Appeal and Cassation, provided that the contracting parties have the right to waive appeal, in the arbitration contract, or after the issuance of the arbitrators' award.
A third party may neither applies for intervention nor lodge a "third-party opposition".
A petition for retrial may only be filed in the cases provided for in paragraphs 1, 5, 6 and 7 of Article 537. This petition shall be submitted to the court having jurisdiction to hear the appeal.

An action for the annulment of the arbitral award may be brought before the court whose President issued the enforcement order, in the following cases: 1- If the arbitral award was rendered in the absence of a prior arbitration agreement, or was outside the terms of such agreement, or was based on an arbitration agreement that is null and void or whose term has expired. 2- If the arbitral award deals with matters not requested or grants more than what was requested, except in the case where this is mandatory pursuant to a law relating to public policy. 3- If the umpire took a decision without conferring with the arbitrators appointed by the contracting parties. The action for annulment may only be brought within the fifteen days following the enforcement order.

An arbitration agreement remains possible even if the case is still pending appeal or pending retrial, and it shall be deemed a waiver thereof; the arbitral award to be rendered shall not be subject to any method of recourse, and shall be granted the enforcement order by the First President of the Court of Appeal and Cassation, or a judge thereof delegated by the First President. Execution difficulties, however, shall be referred directly to the aforementioned court.

The arbitrators must render their award within the month following their acceptance of their functions if the arbitration agreement did not fix another time limit for them - if they decide to conduct an investigation, they must adjudicate the case within the fifteen days following the conduct of this investigation.

Every arbitrator who has accepted his function and then refuses to perform it without being exempted by both parties - or fails to adjudicate within the prescribed time limit, may be ordered to pay damages to the claimant.

In order to avoid the aforementioned penalty, the arbitrator shall deposit the arbitral award with the court whose President is entrusted with granting the enforcement order, and a receipt shall be delivered to the arbitrator.
An arbitrator may be dismissed by agreement of both parties.
An action instituted either to establish the validity of the tender or deposit, or to annul them, shall be brought in accordance with the rules prescribed for principal actions.
A judgment ruling that the tender is valid shall decide - if the deposit has not yet been made - that the thing or amount tendered must be deposited if the creditor refuses to receive it.
Execution proceedings concerning real properties to which the Land Registry system has not been applied, shall remain subject to the previous legislation.

The following are repealed and shall remain repealed: - The Ottoman Code of Procedure, and the addendum issued on 30 July of the year 1329 - and the Ottoman Law concerning Peace Courts issued on 11 April of the year 1329 - and the Ottoman Execution Law issued on 28 April of the year 1930, subject to the provisions of the preceding Article - and all other legislative texts that conflict with the provisions of this Law or are inconsistent therewith.
Nothing is amended in the provisions of the Lebanese Law in force issued on 17 February of the year 1928.
This Law shall be put into effect starting from the date on which the "Code of Obligations and Contracts" enters into force.

An arbitrator who ceases to perform his functions for any reason whatsoever shall be replaced by another arbitrator appointed by the party who appointed the first arbitrator. If he is an additional arbitrator, the two parties shall undertake the appointment of his successor. If they do not agree, the President of the Court shall appoint him.
If the arbitration agreement has provided for the appointment of a sole arbitrator, and this arbitrator ceases to perform his functions, each party shall be entitled to withdraw from the arbitration.

If the arbitration agreement requires the appointment of an arbitrator or several arbitrators with absolute powers, they shall rule in equity without being bound by the provisions of the law and the rules of procedure, and their award shall not be subject to appeal; however, it shall remain possible to apply for a retrial and to bring the action for annulment provided for in Article 840.
Arbitral awards rendered in foreign countries shall have the exact same standing as foreign judgments with respect to the authority of res judicata and enforceable force.

A debtor who wishes - in accordance with the provisions of Article 294 of the Code of Obligations and Contracts - to discharge his liability, shall make an actual tender of the thing or sum which he claims to owe. This tender shall be made through the notary public, who shall draw up a record thereof.

This record shall specify the thing tendered and the enumeration of the money, and shall include mention of the acceptance or refusal, and whether the creditor signed, refused to sign, or declared that he is unable to sign.
A copy of this record shall be left for the creditor.
If the creditor refuses to accept the tender, the debtor may, in order to discharge his liability, deposit the sum or thing tendered with a bank or an institution accepted by the Government.

Sunni Muslims are completely independent in their religious affairs and their charitable endowments; they undertake the legislation of the regulations thereof and the administration thereof by themselves in accordance with the provisions of the noble Sharia and the laws and regulations derived therefrom, through representatives from among themselves of competence and sound judgment, in the ways set forth in the following Articles.

The Mufti of the Lebanese Republic is the religious head of the Muslims and their representative in this capacity before the public authorities, and he has the same inviolability, rights and privileges enjoyed by the highest religious heads without specification or exception.

A - Every syndicate, every institution, and every Islamic association shall invite its Sunni Muslim members to elect its representatives to the Islamic Electoral Council pursuant to a written assignment from the Director of Endowments or the person acting in his stead, which he shall send to it at least thirty days prior to the date of the election, and it shall submit to him the names of its delegate within fifteen days from the receipt of the assignment by it; and those entitled from among the members of the syndicates may

- meet of their own accord, elect their delegates, and submit their names directly to the Directorate of Endowments by means of a letter signed by the majority of the members.

B - At the headquarters of each endowment department, the checklist containing the names of those who have the right to vote shall be published at the beginning of every year by the Director General of Endowments and the heads of the regional endowment departments or those acting in their stead.
The Islamic Electoral Council shall convene upon the invitation of the President of the Council of Ministers, and the invitation shall be notified by posting on the door of Dar al-Fatwa.

The highest Islamic authority in the State, or the person acting in his stead, or the person whom he delegates, shall preside over the meeting and shall conduct the election process with the assistance of the Director General of Endowments or the person acting in his stead and two of the voters present whom he chooses to perform the function of two secretaries to record the minutes of the session and announce the result of the election.

Every candidate shall have the right to authorise a delegate on his behalf to attend the voting operations pursuant to a written authorisation which he shall present to the President of the Islamic Electoral Council, certified by the Director General of Endowments or the person acting in his stead.

The President of the Council shall declare the opening of the session and call the members by their names in verification of their attendance and of the completion of the legal quorum among them, and shall distribute to them ballot papers of a single model; then the election process shall commence, whereby each voter shall place his paper in a locked box on the President's table, and his vote shall be noted on the checklist beside his name.

Provided that if there is found among those entitled to the right to vote anyone whose name was not called due to its omission from the list of voters, he shall have the right to submit to the President of the Polling Committee a request enabling him to exercise his right, whereupon the Polling Board shall immediately decide upon the matter, and its decision in this regard shall be final.

Upon the conclusion of the voting process, the ballot box shall be opened in the presence of the voters, and the papers contained therein shall be sorted by matching their number with the number of voting members according to the checklist and by reading aloud the names recorded therein, and the election of the one who obtains the legal majority shall be declared.

The ballot paper may only contain the name of the candidate alone. Every ballot paper bearing a signature, a mark, or an expression shall be considered null and void, even if it does not reveal the identity of its author.

The office of Mufti of the Lebanese Republic shall be assumed by whoever is elected from among the candidates who are Lebanese Sunni Islamic religious scholars of good conduct and righteousness holding a high religious degree or who have practised the judicial office of Sharia judiciary for a period of not less than fifteen years.

It is required that the candidate has completed forty years of age.

The Mufti of the Republic shall be elected for a term that ends upon his reaching the age of seventy-two, provided that in all cases it shall not be less than five years, and he shall not be relieved of his office except for health reasons that prevent him from properly performing his duties, or for grave reasons, and the decision of relief shall be issued by the Islamic Electoral Council upon the invitation of the Supreme Islamic Sharia Council in the event of non-retirement from the office voluntarily

and by choice, and that shall be by a majority of at least three-quarters of the members.

In the event of retirement or relief due to illness, the retiree or the person relieved may be granted sufficient monthly allowances from the Special Ifta Fund if available, and otherwise from the budget of the Islamic Awqaf, provided that he does not personally engage in any public office, profession or work.

These allowances shall be determined by a decision of the Supreme Islamic Sharia Council.

Each member of the Supreme Islamic Sharia Council may nominate in the election session the person who fulfills the conditions stipulated in the fifth Article, and the nomination shall not be accepted unless it is seconded by two other members of the Council.

The Islamic Electoral Council shall be composed of:

1- The serving President of the Council of Ministers and former Presidents of the Council of Ministers.

2- The serving Sunni Muslim Ministers.

3- The serving Sunni Muslim Deputies.

4- The members of the Supreme Islamic Sharia Council.

5- The serving local Muftis.

6 - The scholars who are serving judges of the Noble Sharia.

7- The scholars who are retired judges of the Noble Sharia.

8- The Amin al-Fatwa in each of Beirut and Tripoli.

9- The Director General of the Islamic Awqaf.

Each member of the Council shall have one electoral vote, and he shall not be entitled to represent more than one category or entity of the categories or entities of which the Council is composed. Proxy voting shall not be permissible; rather, the voter must attend in person.

The election shall not be valid unless it is conducted in the presence of two-thirds of the members of the Council the first time and in the presence of half of the members the second time, and the candidate who obtains the absolute majority of the votes of those voting shall be deemed the winner.
The election shall be conducted by secret ballot, and election by acclamation shall be permissible if there is only one candidate who fulfills the qualifying conditions to assume the office.

Amended Article 3:

a- The Mufti of the Republic is the direct head of all Muslim religious scholars and the supreme authority for the Islamic Waqfs and the departments of Ifta

and exercises all the powers vested in him in the Waqf and Sharia laws and regulations.

b - The Mufti of the Republic supervises the affairs of Muslims and their religious and social interests in the various regions of the Lebanese Republic

and meets with the Muftis in the governorates and districts whenever the need arises to study with them the religious and social affairs of Muslims in their regions and the affairs of Ifta, Waqfs, and scholars, and issues the necessary instructions to them.

c- The Mufti of the Republic appoints the administrative employees and the holders of religious offices, including imams, preachers, teachers, reciters, and muezzins, and issues the decisions for their promotion, discipline, and dismissal in accordance with the provisions prescribed in this Legislative Decree and the regulations in force.

d- The Mufti of the Republic exercises his duties and takes his decisions in the various religious and Waqf affairs of Muslims in accordance with the provisions of this Legislative Decree and the regulations in force, and seeks assistance in important matters, when

necessary, from an advisory council which he selects from among men of knowledge and action renowned for integrity, benevolence, and rectitude, who are far removed from personal and partisan objectives, and in selecting them he shall observe the representation of all regions, subject to the fulfilment of the following conditions:

1- That they are not related to him by kinship up to the fourth degree.

2- That they hold high religious or civil degrees or are persons of distinguished social standing, good morals, and commendable conduct.

3- That their age is not less than thirty-five. The members are appointed for a renewable term of one year, and a member may be relieved therefrom by a decision of the Mufti of the Republic in the event of incapacity to work or if he commits a grave matter or

one harmful to the interests of Muslims, and the council shall draw up its internal regulations within one month from the date it commences its work.

e- An independent fund shall be established under the Mufti of the Republic, the administration, resources, and methods of expenditure of which shall be determined by special regulations drawn up by the Supreme Islamic Sharia Council.

The purpose of this fund is to contribute to raising the religious, cultural, social, and health standard of Muslims.

Amended Article 4:

It is not permissible to combine the office of Mufti of the Republic with any function, work, or profession, with the exception of official or honorary offices allocated to religious heads in general, and the mere acceptance of the office of Mufti of the Republic shall be deemed aconstructive and final waiver of any previous function, work, or profession.

A challenge to the validity of the election shall not be admissible except from the losing candidate, and that on the ground of fraud and forgery or on the ground of a violation of the electoral procedures prescribed above being a substantial violation resulting in the loss of the legal quorum for the election.

The challenge shall be submitted within two days of the announcement of the election result to the committee that is elected in the session for the election of the Mufti in accordance with the following Article.

The Islamic Electoral Council shall decide definitively on the validity of the challenge within a period of eight days from the submission of the petition of challenge, and that pursuant to a report prepared by a subcommittee of its members, the number of whom shall not exceed ten and shall not be less than five, whom the Council shall elect by a majority of the votes of its members present; if the Council approves the validity of the challenge, the election shall be repeated in accordance with the provisions mentioned above.

The President of the Council shall announce the result after the completion of the election process and shall state the name of the winning candidate for the post of Mufti of the Republic. On the third day of this announcement, the investiture of the Mufti shall take place at Dar al-Fatwa by the President of the Electoral Council and those present of its members, and the investiture shall be by reading the minutes of the election session in the presence of the Mufti and by proclaiming him Mufti of the Republic in the name of the Muslims.

In the event of winning by acclamation, the investiture of the Mufti shall take place immediately upon the announcement of the result.

However, if there is a challenge, the investiture shall be postponed until after a decision is rendered thereon.

On the day of the investiture, the President of the Council shall officially notify the name of the Mufti of the Republic to the Government to take the necessary legal action.

In the event of a challenge to the validity of the election, the ceremonies set forth in the preceding Article shall take place on the day following the issuance of the Council's decision rejecting the challenge.

Whether the investiture ceremonies take place, are delayed, or are cancelled for any reason whatsoever, the winner of the election shall become Mufti of the Republic by operation of law upon the mere expiry of the period for challenge or the issuance of the decision rejecting the challenge.

If the President of the Council fails to perform the duty of notification or investiture, the Vice-President of the Supreme Islamic Sharia Council shall take his place in these two tasks together with the delegation of the bodies mentioned above.

The Government shall issue, after the election and investiture process, a decree confirming that by considering the winning candidate as Mufti of the Lebanese Republic.

If it is not issued within a time limit of one month at the most, the person elected shall be considered Mufti of the Lebanese Republic by operation of law.

Amended Article 50:

Amended Article 51:

.

Amended Article 44:

The term of the Supreme Sharia Council shall be four years, and it may be dissolved before the completion of its term for grave reasons assessed by the Mufti of the Republic with the approval of at least fifteen members of the Supreme Council, and the dissolution decision shall be issued by

the Mufti of the Republic, and it shall then be mandatory to convene the electoral body to elect a new Council within a period of one month at most from the issuance of the dissolution decision.

The Mufti of the Republic may fill the seats of elected members vacated by reason of resignation, death, or other reasons by appointment if the remaining period for the Council to complete its legal term does not exceed one year, and it shall not be permissible for the Mufti of the Republic to exercise this right if the vacant seats, in their total or successively, exceed one-quarter of the number of the members of the Council, in which case a by-election must be held to fill the vacant seats for the remainder of the legal term of the Council. If the Mufti of the Republic resorts to appointment as mentioned, he must appoint in detail to the vacant membership of the Islamic Sharia Council the person who obtained the majority of votes according to the contents of the election minutes after the member whose seat became vacant.

The proceedings of the sessions shall be recorded pursuant to minutes drawn up for each session, comprising a statement of the matters placed under discussion therein, a summary of the deliberation that took place concerning them, and the resolutions adopted in respect thereof. The draft of the minutes shall be drawn up in the same session, signed by the President of the Council or his deputy and the members present, and transcribed into a special register signed by the aforementioned in the following session.
The Director General of Awqaf in the capital and the Heads of Awqaf in the outlying districts shall be assisted by elected Administrative Councils.

The Administrative Councils shall be entrusted with the following functions:

1- Drawing up the annual budget and supervising the expenditure of the funds appropriated in its items.

2- Constructing and restoring the immovable properties of the Waqf by tender or by direct execution and exploiting them by short-term or long-term contracts, provided that they do not exceed four years.

3- Leasing out the immovable properties of the Waqf by auction or by mutual agreement and deciding upon their eviction in accordance with their regulations.

4- Establishing the cadre of religious and administrative posts, fixing their salaries, and abolishing such of them as exceed the need.

5- Approving the supporting expenditure vouchers other than the monthly salary vouchers of the employees.

6- Auditing and approving the accounts of the administrators (mutawallis) of the annexed charitable Awqaf.

7- Examining applications for the exchange (istibdal) of directly managed (madbuta) and annexed (mulhaqa) Waqf immovable properties, deciding thereon, and determining the conditions for the use of the sums proceeds from the exchange.

8- Examining candidates for religious posts and proposing their appointment in accordance with the provisions of the Regulation on the Conferment of Religious Offices (Tawjih al-Jihat), and proposing the appointment of administrative employees, and promoting the deserving from both categories and disciplining them.

9- Auditing the accounts of the Directorate or Department and inspecting its registers and the assets of its treasury.

10- Considering all matters submitted to the Council by the Director of Awqaf or its local Head or one of the members, and proposing all that leads to improving the condition of the Awqaf, regulating their administration, preserving their corpus, developing their resources, and securing the charitable purposes stipulated or designated for them.

Amended Article 54:

The Council shall itself lay down internal rules to manage its sessions and organise its work, and it shall adopt its resolutions after their subjects have been examined by the competent committee and on the basis of a report drawn up by its rapporteur.

1- The Judicial Committee:

It is composed of nine members and is entrusted with adjudicating

the matters set forth in Parts (a) and (b) of the fourth paragraph and the entirety of the fifth paragraph of Article 39. This committee shall elect its chairman and his deputy from among its members and shall meet at the times determined by its chairman or his deputy whenever the need arises.

2- The Administrative and Financial Committee:

It is composed of seven members who elect the chairman and the rapporteur from among themselves, and the rapporteur shall act in place of the chairman

in his absence, and it is entrusted with studying the general budgets and financial matters and drawing up reports for the Council on what is stated in Part (c) of the fourth paragraph of Article 39, as well as deciding on what is stated in Part (d) of the same paragraph and approving the proposals of the Administrative Councils for the appointment of holders of religious posts in accordance with the rules prescribed in this Decree, or requesting the reconsideration thereof by

the Administrative Council.

3- The Legislative Committee:

It is composed of five members who elect their chairman and their rapporteur from among themselves, and the rapporteur shall act in place of the chairman in

his absence.

It is entrusted with everything relating to the study of legal and legislative matters which it is assigned to study by the Council or by the Mufti of the Republic.

4- The Appeals and Disciplinary Committee:

It is composed of five members who elect from among themselves the chairman and the rapporteur, and the rapporteur shall act in place of the chairman in his absence.

It is entrusted with examining complaints and everything relating to violations by employees and appeals relating to the election of members of the Sharia Council, the Administrative Councils, and the Muftis in the regions. The committees shall be elected for a term of two years at the first session held by the Council.

No single member may be elected to the membership of more than two committees.

The following committees were added pursuant to Decision 39 dated 10/11/2007, Official Gazette 23 dated 5/6/2008

5 - The Waqfs and Waqf Development Committee:

These committees are composed of five members who elect from among themselves a chairman, and a rapporteur who shall act in place of the chairman in his absence.

This committee is entrusted with formulating the general policy for waqf development, laying down a comprehensive strategy for the culture of waqf, formulating a scientific methodology for investing, developing, controlling, and scheduling its movable and immovable property, preparing investment studies, plans, and programmes, and approving development projects decided upon by the Administrative Councils.

6 - The Call (Da'wah), Mosque, and Heritage Protection Committee:

This committee is composed of five members who elect from among themselves a chairman, and a rapporteur who shall act in place of the chairman in his absence.

This committee is entrusted with preparing a study of everything relating to the Call (Da'wah), direction, guidance, and supervision and oversight of mosques and the religious employees therein, and the protection of heritage in coordination with the Ministry of Culture and all competent authorities and international and regional organisations, and it is also entrusted with laying down the foundations of oversight over everything relating to audio, visual, and written religious advertising and media.

7- The Upbringing, Education, and Culture Committee:

This committee is composed of five members who elect from among themselves a chairman and a rapporteur who shall act in place of the chairman in his absence.

This committee is entrusted with the affairs of religious education in educational and pedagogical institutions, laying down comprehensive plans and the mechanism of implementation therefor so as to include the development, supervision, and control of its curricula in a manner that achieves its purpose in education, and proposing appropriate decisions in respect thereof; this committee shall also be concerned with public education curricula so that they do not conflict with our Arab and Islamic culture and the facts of history, and with monitoring everything published that violates or distorts this culture.

These committees shall be elected for a term of two years at the first session held by the Council, and each committee must propose its internal regulations, and no single member may be elected to the membership of more than two committees, and any of the aforementioned committees may hold a joint session with another committee whenever the matter so requires, and the meeting shall be chaired by the chairman of the committee and the rapporteur of the committee shall serve as rapporteur for the session.

.

The Administrative Council in each of Beirut, Tripoli, Sidon, and the Bekaa shall consist of nine elected members.

Two from each of the religious scholars, jurists, and engineers, and one from each of the merchants, landowners, and experts in financial and accounting matters.

The election of the members of these Councils shall take place in accordance with Article 62 of this Decree. The Administrative Council in the Capital shall be chaired by the Secretary of Fatwa, whereas each of the other Administrative Councils shall be chaired by the local Mufti, and in the event of his absence, the Vice-President shall chair the Council, and if the latter is unable to attend, the oldest of the members shall chair it.

The members of the Administrative Councils in the Capital and the seats of the governorates shall be elected by the bodies entrusted with electing the local Muftis in accordance with the procedures laid down in the preceding Articles for this election.

The appointment of the local committees shall be by a decision of the Mufti of the Republic upon the proposal of the Administrative Councils to which they are attached, or of the Director General of Waqfs in the governorate in which there are no Administrative Councils, which he shall submit to him through the Directorate of Waqfs, and the provisions of Article 18 of this Law shall apply with respect to challenging the validity of the election of the members of the Administrative Councils, and the Supreme Sharia Council shall adjudicate the challenges within a period of two weeks at most.

The term of the Administrative Councils shall be three years, and they may be dissolved prior to the expiry of their term by a decision taken by the Mufti of the Republic of his own motion or upon a recommendation from the Supreme Islamic Sharia Council for serious reasons stated in the decision of dissolution, and new Administrative Councils shall be elected within a period of one month from the issuance of the decision dissolving the previous Councils.

The Mufti of the Republic may, in case of necessity, take of his own motion or upon a recommendation from the Supreme Sharia Council a decision extending the mandate of these Councils for a maximum period of one year, or appointing a committee enjoying all the powers of the Administrative Council for the same period.

The provisions of this Article shall apply to the Waqf committees in the regions.

Amended Article 64:

The President of the Administrative Council shall undertake the convocation of the members, the directing of the sessions, and the notification to the Director of Islamic Endowments (Awqaf) or their local head of the decisions of the Council for their execution or their submission to their affirmative authorities.

And the Council shall elect its committees and its Vice-President from among its members.

And the Vice-President shall undertake the aforementioned acts and powers when the President of the Council does not perform them.

Amended Article 65:

The provisions of Articles 45 and 46 shall apply to the Administrative Councils; however, the decision to dismiss a member of the Administrative Councils for the reasons set forth in Article 46 shall be taken by the Administrative Council presided over by the Secretary of Fatwa (Amin al-Fatwa) in the capital and the local Mufti in the regions, and this decision shall not be enforceable unless it is coupled with ratification by the Mufti of the Republic.

The Administrative Council shall meet upon the convocation of its President at least once a month, and it shall draw up the budget of the Directorate or the Department subordinate to it three months prior to the close of the current year and submit it to the Supreme Sharia Council through hierarchical channels for its auditing and approval prior to the commencement of the new year.

Amended Article 67:

The Administrative Council shall not convene except in the presence of at least seven of its members, including the President, and its decisions in this case shall not be taken except by a majority of five members, and its decisions are enforceable in themselves except in matters the enforceability of which is subject to the ratification of the Mufti of the Republic or the Supreme Sharia Council.

The decisions of the Administrative Councils may be appealed to the Supreme Sharia Council for their violation of the laws, regulations, and instructions in force, or for their causing prejudice to the interests of the Islamic Endowments (Awqaf) or to the rights of the interested parties therein.

The Director General of Islamic Endowments (Awqaf), their local heads, and the aggrieved among the interested parties therein shall hold the right of appeal. And the appeal shall be lodged within a period of fifteen days, and this period shall commence in respect of the Director of Islamic Endowments (Awqaf) and their local heads from the date of issuance of the decision in respect of the interested party from the date of his notification thereof or his having binding knowledge thereof.

The Director of Islamic Endowments (Awqaf) shall have the right to appeal any decision taken by one of the Administrative Councils in the outlaying districts contrary to the laws, regulations, and instructions in force, or for its causing prejudice to the interest of the endowment (Waqf), within a period of one month from the date of issuance of the decision if the local Head of Islamic Endowments (Awqaf) does not exercise his right of appeal.

Amended Article 71:

The appeal shall not stay the execution of the decision unless the Supreme Sharia Council orders a stay of its enforcement. However, the appeal of decisions relating to constructions and exchange (Istibdal) and which cause prejudice to the Islamic Endowments (Awqaf) shall

stay the execution as of right.

Amended Article 79:

The Endowments in the regions shall be managed by local Heads appointed by a decision of the Mufti of the Lebanese Republic upon a proposal by the local Mufti or the Director General of Endowments and in accordance with the endorsement of the Supreme Islamic Sharia Council on this proposal, and they shall report directly to the Director General of Endowments in the capital, and each of them shall attend to the affairs of the Endowments located within the region of the Governorate to which he is appointed.

The appointment of each of the Heads of the Endowment Departments of Tripoli and Sidon shall be subject to the same conditions required for the appointment of the Director General.

The local Head of Endowments shall enjoy, within his sphere of competence and in his relation with the Administrative Council in his region, the same powers established for the Director General of Endowments in the preceding Articles.

Elections for the vacant post of Ifta in the Governorate of North Lebanon (the City of Tripoli) and for the elected members of the Supreme Islamic Sharia Council, the Administrative Councils, and the Endowment Committees in the centres of the Districts and villages shall be held within a period not exceeding three months from the date of publication of this Law in the Official Gazette.

From the date of the entry into force of this Law until the completion of the elections provided for in Article 16 and the formation of those Councils and Committees, each of the current Supreme Islamic Sharia Council, its Standing Committee, the Scholarly and Administrative Councils, and the Endowment Committees in the centres of the Districts and villages currently in office shall exercise the rights and powers provided for in this Law, and all previous decisions issued by these Councils and Committees shall remain valid and in force.
The Standing Committee shall adjudicate, in the same previous manner, the appeals and recourses lodged that remain pending before it.
The Standing Committee shall review the cadre of the employees of the Endowment Departments and their classification within a period not exceeding three months from the date of its formation.

The provisions of the laws, regulations, decrees, decisions, and all other legislative - texts that contravene the provisions of this Law or are inconsistent therewith are hereby repealed and shall remain repealed.
This Law shall be published in the Official Gazette and shall enter into force on the day following its publication.

The Director General of Awqaf shall assume the administration of the Awqaf of the capital and the supervision of the administration of the Awqaf in the outlying districts, and shall report directly to the Mufti of the Republic and be responsible for his acts before him and before the Supreme Sharia Council.

The Director of Awqaf shall abide in his actions by the applicable laws, regulations and instructions, and shall ensure the proper functioning of the Awqaf departments and the regularity of the state of their real properties, institutions and charitable entities.

Amended Article 74:

The Director General of Awqaf is the direct superior of the employees of his department and of the Heads of Awqaf in the regions; they shall execute his orders and act in accordance with his instructions in all matters that do not contravene the laws, regulations and budget of the Awqaf.

He shall hold periodic meetings every three months with the Heads of Awqaf in the regions to study the affairs of the Awqaf, the means leading to the increase of revenues and the control of expenditures, and the needs of the Awqaf, and to take the necessary decisions regarding these affairs and submit a report on the results,

resolutions and proposals to the Mufti of the Republic.

The Director General of Awqaf in the capital shall have the authority to take disciplinary measures against religious and administrative employees in the capital and the outlying districts who commit negligence or a breach of the duties of their functions warranting reprimand and deduction of salary for a maximum period of fifteen days. As for other measures, they shall be decided by the Administrative Council to which the responsible employee belongs, based on the investigations conducted against him, provided that it is coupled with the ratification of the Supreme Sharia Council if they provide for demotion in step or rank or for dismissal, and in all cases the decision of the Director General of Awqaf shall be subject to appeal by the penalized employee before the Supreme Sharia Council within a period of ten days from the date of notification.

The Director General of Awqaf in the capital shall have the right to decide the suspension from duty of any religious or administrative employee, with the exception of the local Heads of Awqaf, who has committed a grave breach of the duties of his function, pending the outcome of the investigation and the adjudication thereof. This measure shall not be executed except after its ratification by the Mufti of the Republic, and the payment of half the salary to the suspended employee shall be withheld until the issuance of the requisite decision regarding him.

Amended Article 77:

The Director General of Awqaf may propose the appointment and promotion of the employees of the Awqaf departments, and it shall also pertain to him in the capital and to the Heads of Departments in the regions to appoint ushers, attendants and the like among minor employees after the approval of the Administrative Council, within the appropriations specified in the budget.
The Director of Awqaf shall execute the decisions of the Administrative Council and the decisions of the Supreme Sharia Council that are referred to him for execution.
The property and rights of the deceased shall pass to his heirs designated by law or to the persons specified in the will, in accordance with the following provisions:

Sole Article: The attached Inheritance Law for Non-Mohammedans is hereby ratified, and its provisions shall enter into force as from the tenth day following the date of its publication in the Official Gazette.
The estate shall open and the inheritance shall vest upon the actual death of the decedent or upon his being declared dead by a judicial judgment.

The place of opening of the estate shall be the last domicile of the deceased, wherever his property may be situated. A wife who is not legally separated from her husband shall be deemed domiciled at the domicile of her husband, and minors at the domicile of their compulsory guardian or their tutor. If they have neither a compulsory guardian nor a tutor, it shall be at the place where the whole of the estate or the greater part thereof is situated.

As for a missing person, his domicile shall be deemed to be the last place in which he resided prior to his death.

Entitlement to inheritance requires:

1- The ascertained survival of the heir on the date of the death of the decedent or on the date of his being declared dead by a judicial judgment.

2- The capacity of the heir to succeed to the inheritance.

3- The absence of legal impediments preventing entitlement to the inheritance.

The following shall not have capacity to inherit:

a- A foetus who is not born within three hundred days following the death of the decedent.

b - A child who is not born alive.
