If several persons who inherit from one another perish in a single accident, the court shall determine the successive times of their deaths on the basis of the circumstances of the accident, the age of the deceased persons, their state of health, and other considerations; if it is impossible to determine the times of the deaths, all those who perished in the single accident shall be deemed to have died at the same time, and the inheritance of each of them shall pass to his living heirs.
If a sentence of death is executed on a single day upon several persons each of whom inherits from the other, the rule set forth in the last paragraph of the preceding Article shall apply.

Difference of nationality shall not bar mutual inheritance between Lebanese nationals and foreigners unless the law of the foreigner prohibits the inheritance of Lebanese nationals.

If the law of the foreigner restricts the right of inheritance, the foreigner shall inherit from a Lebanese national only to the extent permitted by the foreign law for Lebanese nationals.
Difference of religion shall not bar inheritance unless the heir is subject to provisions that prohibit inheritance by reason of difference of religion.

Shall be debarred from inheritance:

1- Any person who intentionally, without right or excuse, kills the decedent or any of his descendants, ascendants, or spouse, or acts as an accomplice in the killing.

2- Any person who falsely accuses the decedent of an offence or bears false witness against him in respect of a felony punishable by death, unless the decedent has pardoned the offender by virtue of a written instrument.

The share of the debarred heir shall devolve upon the other heirs entitled concurrently with him.

If there are no heirs entitled concurrently with him, it shall pass to his descendants who would have taken his place had he died before the decedent. Property that devolves in this manner upon the descendants of the debarred person shall not be subject to his legal authority, whether as natural guardian or testamentary guardian over them, nor shall he be entitled to inherit it after their death.

The debarred heir is bound to restore to the estate any property he may have received since the death of the decedent, and he must also restore any revenues and fruits he has derived therefrom since the date of death.

Article 13: There shall be paid out of the estate in the following order: 1- What suffices for preparing the deceased for burial and burying him 2- The debts of the deceased 3- What he has bequeathed within the limit within which the bequest is enforceable. The remainder thereafter shall be distributed among the heirs in accordance with the following rules:

Article 14: Heirs are divided into three classes: - The first class: The children and their descendants - The second class: The father and the mother and their ascendants - The third class: The brothers and sisters and their descendants

Article 15: The children of the deceased and their descendants shall inherit from their parents and their ascendants without distinction between males and females. If the descendants are all of the first degree, they shall divide the estate among themselves equally. If among the children of the decedent there is one who died before him, his descendants shall take his place in the estate of the decedent and the share that would have devolved upon their parent had he been alive shall devolve upon them. They shall divide this share among themselves equally. The right of representation set forth in the preceding paragraph shall apply to the inheritance of descendants however remote.

If the deceased has no descendants, the estate shall devolve upon his parents equally, and if one of them has died, his descendants shall take from the estate the share that would have devolved upon him had he been alive and shall divide it among themselves equally. If he has no descendants, the share that would have devolved upon him had he been alive shall devolve upon the other ascendant or upon his descendants, and if both of them have died before the de cujus, the descendants of each of them shall take the share that would have devolved upon their de cujus had he been alive and shall divide it among themselves in accordance with the provisions of the preceding Article; however, the right of representation shall apply here only for the benefit of the descendants of a brother who died before the de cujus or the descendants of a sister who died before the de cujus when they inherit alongside a surviving brother or sister of the de cujus.

If the deceased has no descendants, or father, or mother, or descendants from either of them, the estate shall be divided among the grandfathers and grandmothers; if one of them has died, his share shall pass to his descendants, who shall divide it among themselves equally, and if he has no descendants, the share that would have devolved upon him shall pass to the grandparent on the same side. If this grandparent has died, then to his descendants, and if the two paternal grandparents of the deceased or his two maternal grandparents have died without descendants, the estate shall be allocated to his two grandparents on the other side, and if they have died, then to their descendants.
Whoever is in the first, second, and third orders of descendants, if he acquires the right of inheritance from different sides, shall take all that accrues to him from those sides.
One-sixth of the estate shall devolve upon the parents of the de cujus, or upon the surviving one of them, if the de cujus has descendants.

One-quarter of the estate shall devolve upon the husband or wife of the de cujus when concurring with heirs of the first order, one-half thereof when concurring with the father, mother, brother, or sister, and five-sixths when concurring with the grandfather or grandmother; if there is no heir from among those mentioned above, the husband or wife of the deceased shall be entitled to the entire estate.
If there is none of the heirs designated in the preceding Articles, the property of the estate shall revert to the State.

An illegitimate child shall inherit from the person who acknowledged him voluntarily or judicially, and his hereditary share shall be determined as follows:

- One-quarter of the share that would have devolved upon him had he been legitimate, if the father or mother left legitimate descendants

- One-half of the share that would have devolved upon him had he been legitimate, if the father or mother did not leave legitimate descendants, but left legitimate ascendants or legitimate brothers or sisters, or legitimate descendants of the said brothers or sisters

- Three-quarters of the estate, if the father or mother left legitimate heirs other than those mentioned above

- The entire estate, if there is no legitimate heir
An adopted child shall be deemed a legitimate child in all matters relating to his rights in the estate of the person who adopted him or in his will.

The filiation of an illegitimate child shall be established by voluntary acknowledgment. The acknowledgment shall be effected by a declaration recorded in the birth certificate in accordance with the rules prescribed for registering personal status documents, or in an official deed drawn up before the notary public. Voluntary acknowledgment of the child may not take place after he reaches the age of majority.
Voluntary acknowledgment shall have effect only with respect to the person from whom it issued.

If either spouse acknowledges during their marriage contract an illegitimate child born to him by a person other than this spouse of his prior to the conclusion of the said contract, this child shall have no effect on the right of the other spouse to inherit from his spouse or the right of their children born after the marriage, and the acknowledgment shall take effect if the marriage is dissolved and the spouses leave no children after the dissolution of their marriage.

An illegitimate child may be attributed to his father before the courts competent to hear this matter:

First- In the case of abduction or rape when the conception took place during the time corresponding to the abduction or rape. Second- In the case of seduction by fraudulent means, such as abuse of authority and promise of marriage.

If there is a commencement of written proof, paternity shall be established in accordance with the provisions of Article 242 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Third- In cases where there are letters or other writings issuing from the alleged father and containing an unequivocal acknowledgment of paternity. An action for acknowledgment of paternity shall not be admissible:

First- If it is proven that during the legal period of conception the mother was notorious for her misconduct or had intercourse at that time with another person.

Second- If during the same period the alleged father was in a situation making it impossible for him to be the father of the child, either by reason of his distance from the place where the mother was present or by reason of an accident having befallen him.

The action shall be admissible only from the child. If the child is a minor, the action shall be admissible from the mother even if she is a minor. In this latter case, and under penalty of forfeiture, the action must be brought within a period of two years starting from the date of delivery. If the action was not brought during the period in which the child was a minor, the latter shall be entitled to bring this action within the year following his attainment of the age of majority. If the mother did not acknowledge the child during the period in which he was a minor, or if she died during this period or was legally incapacitated and absent, the period within which the child may bring the action after reaching the age of majority shall be two years.

The filiation of an illegitimate child to his mother may be proved before the courts having jurisdiction to hear this matter. A child who requests a declaration of his filiation to a mother must prove that the latter gave birth to a child and that he is the child to whom she gave birth. The action shall not be heard unless it is brought before the expiry of two years from the date of attaining the age of majority. Testimonial evidence shall not be admitted unless there is a commencement of proof in writing or serious and existing presumptions.

Every interested party may contest the acknowledgment made by the father or the mother, and may also, within a maximum period of five years from the date of issuance of the final judgment, contest the request of the illegitimate child for his filiation to a father or a mother.

The illegitimate child referred to in the preceding provisions is one born of two persons not bound to one another by a contract of marriage, not related to each other by a relationship constituting an impediment to marriage, and neither of whom is bound by a contract of marriage to a third person. However, if one of the parents is not bound by a contract of marriage to a third person, the child shall inherit from that parent.

Legitimate children or their descendants have the right to exclude illegitimate children from the estate by paying the share accruing to the illegitimate children in cash or in immovable property from the estate after conducting a fair valuation.
A missing person is an absentee whose whereabouts are unknown and who is not known to be alive or dead.

- The death of a missing person shall be adjudged if the disappearance of his traces and the cessation of news of him continue for a period of at least four years since the date of his absence, upon the request of any interested party, and the request shall be decided by the Civil Court of First Instance having jurisdiction over the place of his residence or the last domicile of the person whose death is sought to be judicially declared, and if the disappearance occurred outside Lebanon, the Civil Court of First Instance in Beirut.

The court mentioned in the preceding Article shall examine in chambers the request for the judicial declaration of the death of the missing person, and shall rely, in order to form its conviction, upon various legal means of proof, including publication in local and foreign newspapers where necessary and various means of announcement which the court deems useful, and the reliance on presumptions, particularly in cases and circumstances in which death is probable and the body is not found.

The heirs of the missing person whose death has been judicially declared may enjoy the usufruct of his property, and they shall not have the right to dispose of it by way of transferring ownership or creating real rights over it except after the lapse of six years from the publication of the judgment containing the declaration of death in the local newspapers and the newspapers of the country in which he is presumed to be present, and the expiry of six months from such publication.

The share of a missing person in the inheritance of another and his portion of a bequest, if a bequest has been made to him, shall be suspended until five years have elapsed from the issuance of the judgment declaring his death; upon the expiry of this period, his share in the inheritance shall revert to those who inherit from his decedent at the time of the latter's death, and his portion of the bequest shall revert to the heirs of the testator.

If the missing person appears alive within five years after the judgment declaring his death, he shall take all his property from the hands of the heirs, as well as what was suspended for him from the inheritance of another and from the bequest; and if he appears alive after the lapse of this period, he shall take whatever remains in the hands of the heirs. This shall not preclude the recovery of any of his property that has passed to third parties in bad faith.
It is required that the testator be of sound mind, have capacity to make gratuitous dispositions, and have attained the full age of eighteen years.

A bequest shall be valid in favour of any person, whether an heir or a non-heir, and in favour of an unborn child if born alive, provided that such person is not by operation of law incapable of inheriting or barred therefrom.
A will drawn up in a single instrument by two or more persons shall not be valid, whether the bequest is for the benefit of the testators themselves or of any other person.
The nullity of a will may not be invoked by an heir who has ratified the will or voluntarily executed it with knowledge of the grounds of nullity.

A bequest made by a sick person during his last illness to the physician who treated him during that illness shall not be valid unless such physician is one of the heirs of the testator; however, a bequest drawn up in this case shall be valid if the bequeathed property is in remuneration for services and the wealth of the testator and the services rendered were taken into account in determining its amount.
A bequest to a foreigner shall not be valid unless the law of his country permits a bequest to a Lebanese national, and to the extent that it permits such bequest.
A bequest may be made subject to a charge.

A will shall be executed in Lebanon either in the authentic form or in the handwriting of the testator; as for the will of a Lebanese national executed in a foreign country, it shall be executed and authenticated in accordance with the procedures provided for in this Law or the procedures by which official instruments are authenticated in the foreign country in which it is executed.
An authentic will shall be executed before a notary public.

A will may be executed in the handwriting of the testator, who shall write it in its entirety in his own hand, sign it with his signature, and date it, and in such case it must be deposited by the testator in person or by his special attorney-in-fact with the notary public inside an envelope sealed with red wax, such seal being certified by the notary public. The existence of this will shall be noted in a special register, and if the will is executed in a foreign country, it shall be deposited with the notary public or with the Consul of Lebanon.

With respect to the will of a soldier present on the battlefield, an officer of the rank of lieutenant or above shall act in the place of the notary public. This will shall become null and void upon the expiry of three months following the return of the testator to a place where he is able to make a will by ordinary means.
A will shall be reduced insofar as it exceeds the reserved share of each of the descendants, the parents, and either spouse.

The reserved share of the descendants shall be fixed at fifty per cent of the total movable and immovable property. If all the children are alive, they shall divide this share equally among themselves regardless of their number and without distinction between males and females. If one of them has died, his descendants shall take his place in the share that would have devolved upon him had he been alive, and they shall divide it equally among themselves.
The reserved share of the surviving spouse shall be fixed at thirty per cent.
A bequest in favour of a person deemed by operation of law to lack capacity to inherit or to be excluded from inheritance shall be void, even if such bequest is made in the name of a nominee.

A bequest in favour of places of worship, charitable institutions and other benevolent bodies, and scientific and public institutions enjoying legal capacity, shall be valid, and the bequest shall be valid even if the institutions have not been legally established on the day of death, provided that legal capacity is realised therein within one year beginning from the day on which the legacy becomes due for performance; and if the year expires and the institution has not been established or legal capacity has not been realised therein, the bequeathed thing shall be returned to the heirs of the testator.

So long as the establishment of the institution has not been completed in accordance with the law, no measures other than conservatory measures for the preservation of the bequeathed thing may be taken in the case set forth in the preceding Article.
The legatee must be designated by the testator himself. Every bequest contracted in a manner whereby the legatee cannot be designated at the time of the death of the testator shall be void.

A bequest partitioning the specific assets of the estate among the heirs of the testator whereby the amount of his share is designated for each heir shall be valid; if the value of what is designated for one of them exceeds his entitlement in the estate, the excess shall, by way of bequest, be subject to reduction in the event that it exceeds the disposable portion for bequests.
A bequest of the corpus to one person and of the usufruct to another shall be valid.

A bequest of a usufruct of a nature to tie up property shall not be valid unless it is construed as a family waqf, and in such case it shall not be valid in respect of Amiri real properties. As for owned properties, it shall be valid up to the period for which a waqf is valid, and the rules of family waqf shall apply thereto.

A bequest comprising conditions that are impossible, prohibited, or contrary to public policy and public morals shall be deemed void, provided that if the condition was not the primary motivating cause for the bequest, such condition shall be null and void and the bequest shall be deemed valid.
The reserved share for the parents shall be set at thirty per cent, which they shall divide between themselves equally, and the surviving one of them shall take it in its entirety.

Upon the concurrence of the descendants with one of the spouses and the parents or either of them, the reserved share shall be set for the descendants at thirty per cent, for one of the spouses at ten per cent, and for the parents or either of them at ten per cent.

Upon the concurrence of the descendants with one of the spouses or with the parents or either of them, the reserved share shall be set for the descendants at forty per cent, and for one of the spouses or for the parents or either of them at ten per cent.

If the testator dies without descendants and leaves a spouse with his parents or either of them, the reserved share shall be set for the spouse at twenty per cent, for the father at fifteen per cent, and for the mother at fifteen per cent.

A bequest exceeding the disposable portion shall be reduced to this portion upon the opening of the succession, and the reduction may only be requested by the heirs entitled to a reserved share, or their universal heirs, or their proxies, or their successors.

For the purpose of determining the disposable portion, there shall be added to the net property of the deceased, after deducting his debts therefrom, the value of the property that he gifted during his lifetime, and the price thereof at the time of the gift shall be taken as the basis for the valuation of such property.

If the bequeathed property is a usufruct, or a life annuity, or the bare ownership of immovable property, its value shall be assessed taking into consideration the age of the legatee, his state of health, and other considerations.

If the value of the bequeathed property exceeds the disposable portion that may be disposed of, or the part that remains of this portion after deducting the values of gifts inter vivos, the reduction shall take place without distinction between universal legacies and particular legacies; provided that if the testator has expressed his explicit wish to execute a legacy before others, in such case the preferred legacy shall be executed before the others and shall not be reduced unless the remaining property is insufficient to secure the reserved share.

A bequest shall become binding upon its acceptance by the legatee, expressly or implicitly, after the death of the testator, and if the legatee is a foetus, a minor, or an interdicted person, acceptance shall be made by the person who holds natural or testamentary guardianship over his property.

It shall be permissible to accept part of a bequest and reject the other part, just as it shall be permissible for it to be accepted by some of the legatees and rejected by the others. In such case, it shall be void in respect of the one who rejected it.
The effects of acceptance shall be retroactive to the time of the death of the testator.
Waiver of a bequest prior to the death of the testator shall have no effect.

The testator may appoint one or more executors for his will, and it shall be required that the executor enjoy civil rights and legal capacity, and the testator may stipulate that, in the event of his non-acceptance, he may appoint another or name a specified person to be the executor of his will. In all cases, this right shall not pass to the heirs of the executor.

The testator may define the functions of the executor of his will. If he does not do so, the function of the executor shall be to administer the estate, pay its debts, and distribute its specific assets in the manner appointed by the testator or provided for by the law.

If the testator appoints several executors for his will and they accept the mission, no one of them may act individually unless the testator has authorised them to do so. They shall all be jointly and severally liable for the property of the estate, and if the testator assigns a specific task to each of them, he shall be entitled to act individually in that task.
The expenses incurred by the executor of the will in making an inventory of the estate, affixing the seals, completing the accounting, and others shall be deducted from the property of the estate.
The testator may revoke his will in whole or in part.

Revocation of a will may take place by making a subsequent will, an official deed, or a document in the handwriting of the testator deposited with the notary public in the form set out in Article 55, in which the testator declares that he has revoked his previous will.

A subsequent will that does not contain an express revocation of the previous will tacitly annuls all provisions of the previous will that are contrary to or incompatible with the provisions of the new will. This tacit revocation shall be given effect even if the new will remains unexecuted for a reason beyond the will of the testator.

If the testator sells the bequeathed property in a previous will, the sale shall be deemed a revocation of the will to the extent of the thing sold. This revocation shall be given effect even if the sale is annulled, unless the nullity occurred due to a defect of consent or if the bequeathed property has returned to the ownership of the testator.

Revocation of the will shall be adjudged upon the application of an heir or a legatee in the following cases: 1- If the conditions upon which the will was suspended have not been fulfilled. 2- If the legatee committed one of the crimes that would have rendered him unworthy to inherit from the testator had he been an heir to him.

Actions in all the cases set out in the preceding Article must be brought within one year from the date of death or from the date of the plaintiff's knowledge of the occurrence of the matters calling for the revocation of the will.

A bequest shall be invalidated: 1- By the death of the legatee before the testator. 2- By the death of the legatee before the fulfilment of the condition upon which the execution of the will is suspended, if the intention of the testator was that the will should not take effect unless the condition is fulfilled during the lifetime of the legatee. 3- By the rejection by the legatee of the bequeathed property or by his lack of capacity to receive it. 4- By the total loss of the bequeathed property before the death of the testator.

If the will is not executed in respect of any of the bequeathed things due to the revocation of the bequest of that thing, or the lapse of the bequest thereof, or its nullity, that thing shall revert to the person from whose share it was taken or who was bound to deliver it had the will been executed. The universal legatee, the legatee by general title, or the particular legatee whom the testator intended to benefit thereby shall also benefit from that thing.
The heirs are prohibited from disposing of the specific assets of the estate or administering it in the presence of the executor of the will.
Actions by third parties shall be brought against the executor of the will and the heirs.

The executor of the will must immediately notify the heirs of his acceptance of his mission, deliver to them a statement of the contents of the estate together with the debts owed by it, and notify them of the appointed time for drawing up the inventory of the estate so that they may attend its proceedings if the drawing up of an inventory of the estate is requested.
The executors of the will may seek the assistance of public officials to draw up the inventory of the estate, and the expenses shall be borne by the estate.
The heirs have the right to demand an annual account from the executors of the will if their term is long.

The executor of the will shall be deemed liable for his negligence and for the damages caused to the estate by his act, and the rules of liability for an ordinary agent shall apply to him, and the executor may not be exempted from all liability that may be incurred by him.
If the testator has not fixed a remuneration for the executor of the will, he may claim an ordinary remuneration.
The executor of the will shall be removed upon the request of the heirs if he breaches his duties or becomes unfit to perform his mission, provided that he is heard prior to his removal.

The provisions of the Law on the Sale of Immovable Property shall apply in respect of the sale by auction of immovable properties that are not susceptible of partition, whereas other properties shall be sold by the methods set forth in the Code of Civil Procedure for the sale of attached property, provided that if there is among the assets left an industrial, commercial or agricultural establishment, the Magistrate may decide to sell it with all its elements and without distinction between immovable and movable property. And by the method followed in the sale of immovable property, unless he finds serious reasons that render making a distinction more beneficial.
The decisions of the judge concerning the method of sale are not subject to recourse.

If a person dies and his heirs are not known, the Mukhtar of the locality in which he resides must notify the judge of the matter of his death, whereupon he shall decide in chambers to inventory the estate and appoint a curator over it.

After making the inventory, the judge shall deposit in one of the approved banks the money and valuable objects that he finds among the properties of the deceased and shall deliver the remainder of the properties to the curator for their administration, and the curator may be compelled to furnish a security. And if there is among the properties of the estate that which is feared to perish, the Magistrate may decide to sell it and keep its price in one of the officially approved banks.
After the lapse of five years from the death without an heir appearing, the judge shall take a decision in chambers to deliver the properties of the estate to the State.

The curator shall render to the judge an account of his administration of the properties of the estate, whereupon he shall decide to fix the remuneration of the curator and pay it to him, and the remaining properties shall be delivered to the State.
If the heir appears after the delivery of the properties to the State and proves his right to the inheritance, he shall have recourse against the State for his properties.

If the heir or one of the heirs is absent and has no proxy representing him, the judge may, upon the statement of the Mukhtar of the locality of the deceased or one of the relatives of the absentee, decide in chambers to inventory the estate if he deems inventorying it useful.

Where one of the heirs requests liquidation or partition, the judge shall decide to publish this request in the Official Gazette and in one or more other newspapers which he designates, and shall order that a copy thereof be posted in the vestibule of the court and in a place near the residence of the deceased; and by this notice, anyone who claims a right in the estate and anyone who is owed a debt by it shall be invited to declare the right which he claims and to submit his supporting documents within a time limit of six months from the date of publication of the notice in the Official Gazette.

After the expiry of the period specified for declaring rights and claims, the judge shall draw up a report setting out the claims submitted by the claimants of rights, and shall invite the heirs and the claimants to a hearing at which deliberation shall take place between them regarding an amicable settlement.

If a settlement is reached between the heirs and the claimants, the judge shall ratify it by a decision issued by him in council chamber; otherwise, he shall direct each claimant to bring his action within a time limit which he specifies.

If the claimant brings his action within the specified time limit, the judge shall appoint an urgent hearing at which he shall examine the matter of staying or not staying the liquidation or partition, and in all cases the heirs shall have the right to provide security for the claimed right. In this case, the operations of the inventory of the estate shall be continued.
Where the inventory of the estate is continued, the heirs shall have the right to agree among themselves to divide the property of the estate in the manner which they choose.

If the heirs do not agree on the partition, the judge shall draw up a draft partition and shall seek the assistance of an expert when necessary for this purpose; if the heirs agree to this draft, the judge shall ratify it by a decision issued by him in council chamber.

If one of the heirs objects to the draft partition, the judge shall grant the objector a time limit to submit his objection, and shall rule on the partition by a final judgment not subject to any of the ordinary means of recourse.

If it appears that the property of the estate is not susceptible of partition, it shall be sold by auction through the supervising judge. If it is possible to partition some of the property to the exclusion of the rest, such part thereof as is susceptible of partition shall be partitioned and the remainder shall be sold by auction, unless fragmentation entails grave prejudice.
The settlement of the estate is the determination of the property left by a decedent and, where necessary, its distribution or partition among the heirs and all other holders of rights.

The settlement of the estate shall be permissible in the following cases: 1- If it is requested by one of the heirs, one of the holders of rights in the estate, or the executor of the will. 2- If there is among the heirs or the holders of rights in the estate a fatherless minor, an incapacitated person, or an absentee who has no representative, or if the heirs are unknown.

The application for the settlement of the estate shall be submitted to the Court of First Instance having jurisdiction over the place where the succession opens, and it shall be examined in chambers. Every party aggrieved by the decision ordering the settlement of the estate may file an opposition thereto by way of a summons submitted to the court that issued it, provided that such opposition shall not stay the proceedings for the settlement of the estate if the applicant insists on completing them and furnishes security guaranteeing any damage that may be sustained by the opposing party. In all cases, the court shall retain the power to decide to stay the proceedings for the settlement of the estate where serious grounds exist. In such case, it may require security from the opposing party guaranteeing the damages caused to the applicant for the settlement.
The settlement of the estate shall be carried out through an expert appointed by the judge.

If one of the heirs, the holders of rights in the estate, or the executor of the will requests the settlement of the estate, an inventory showing the property of the estate and the value of each item thereof shall first be drawn up. The judge may order the affixing of seals where necessary.

After the inventory is drawn up and the value of the property left is appraised, the judge shall summon all the heirs as well as all the apparent holders of rights to appear before him at a specified time, submit their documents proving their rights in the estate, and state whether they accept the inheritance, and he shall, where necessary, fix a time limit for the heirs and the legatees to submit this statement.

After those entitled to the estate submit the documents set forth in the preceding Article, and in the event that they declare their acceptance of the inheritance, the judge shall ask them whether they wish to remain in a state of co-ownership of the property or whether they request the liquidation and partition of the estate. If all the heirs and holders of rights declare their wish to remain in a state of co-ownership, the judge shall submit a report stating the same, whereupon the court shall order the delivery of the property of the estate to those entitled thereto against a receipt signed by them. Property specifically bequeathed shall be delivered to those to whom it was bequeathed, and the creditors of the deceased shall have the right to attach the property held in co-ownership, while reserving their right to claim from the heirs and the legatees the portion of the debt incumbent upon each of them in proportion to his share.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

If it appears to the judge that it is in the interest of the minor or the incapacitated person to liquidate the estate and partition it, the rules prescribed in Chapter Two shall apply. The representative of the minor or the incapacitated person shall act on his behalf in the proceedings relating to him, provided that the contracts signed by him shall not be executed prior to the approval thereof by the judge.

If the inventory of the estate concludes with an agreement among the heirs, or between them and the holders of rights in the estate, on the partition of the estate assets, and the partition is executed amicably, such amicable partition, even if approved by the judge, shall not preclude the application of the provisions of Articles 943 and 949 of the Code of Obligations and Contracts.

Actions brought by creditors after a judicial or amicable partition may only be brought against the heirs and beneficiaries of the estate personally, each in proportion to what he received of the estate property. If a claim is made to an immovable property included in the share of one of the heirs and it is evicted from his share, the rules of warranty provided for in Article 948 of the Code of Obligations and Contracts shall thereupon apply among the heirs.
This Law shall not apply, with respect to the designation of heirs and the determination of their shares, to estates opened prior to its entry into force.
Official wills certified by an official authority and drawn up prior to the publication of this Law shall remain in force even if the testator dies after the publication of this Law.
The rules for the inventory of estates shall not apply to estates opened prior to the entry into force of this Law.
This Law shall not apply to the estates of members of the Mohammedan communities.

The following are repealed with respect to estates subject to this Law: 1- The Law of 21 February 1328-1912 relating to the transmission of Amiri and Waqf lands 2- All previous provisions relating to inheritance, wills, and the inventory of estates 3- All texts that conflict with the provisions of this Law or are inconsistent therewith

If there are multiple heirs and some of them are absent, after the inventory is drawn up, the property of the estate shall be delivered to the heirs who are present, after taking security from them guaranteeing the share of the absent heir, and if those heirs refuse to furnish security, the money and valuables, if any, shall be deposited in a bank and the remainder of the property shall be delivered to a judicial receiver who shall manage it on behalf of all the heirs and preserve the absent heir's share thereof and of the fruits thereof, and this latter procedure shall be followed if the sole heir or all the heirs are absent, and the judicial receiver may be required to furnish security.

If the heirs who are present, or any one of them, request the liquidation of the estate and the place of residence of the absent heir can be ascertained, the judge shall notify that heir of the request for liquidation and fix a time limit for him to appear or to appoint an agent to represent him; if he neither appears nor is represented, the liquidation may be carried out in the presence of the judicial receiver; whereas if the absent heir has no known place of residence, he shall be summoned in the manner prescribed in the Code of Civil Procedure for service upon persons of unknown residence, and failing his appearance or the appearance of an agent on his behalf, the judicial receiver shall represent him in the liquidation proceedings.

If none of the heirs requests the liquidation of the estate and the absent heir is not represented, the judge, sitting in chambers, shall order the sale of things liable to perish or deteriorate, the division of their price and of the money, if any, among the heirs, and the preservation of the absent heir's share thereof in a bank, and shall authorise the receiver to participate with the heirs who are present in the management of the remaining common property and to collect the income of the absent heir's share thereof and preserve it in the same bank.
If among the heirs there is a minor orphaned of both parents or a person lacking legal capacity, the judge may order of his own motion or upon information received the inventorying of the estate.
If the minor or the person lacking legal capacity has no legal representative, the judge shall of his own motion order the appointment of a guardian for him.

After the inventory is drawn up, the judge shall order such measures as he deems fit for the preservation of the minor's property, and shall then decide, according to the circumstances of the case, whether or not to carry out the liquidation, unless a request for liquidation is submitted by another heir. In all cases, the judge may order the sale of such property of the estate as he deems necessary to be sold and the preservation of the share of the minor or the person lacking legal capacity in the price thereof in an officially approved bank, or authorise his representative to receive his share of the price or a part thereof.

A non-Lebanese pharmacist of any other nationality shall satisfy the following conditions:

1- He shall fulfil the conditions set forth in Article Three

2- He shall be a national of a country that applies reciprocity in the manner set forth in the second paragraph of Article Five above

3- At least ten years shall have elapsed since he obtained his pharmacy degree

A pharmacy degree granted outside Lebanon shall not be accepted unless the curriculum of study at the university (faculties of pharmacy) that granted it is equivalent to the curriculum of study at the universities of Lebanon and unless it is accepted by the Equivalency Committee

Non-Lebanese pharmacists registered with the Ministry of Public Health prior to the date of entry into force of this Law shall be authorised to practise their profession in Lebanon, and the licence to practise the profession of pharmacy shall be deemed revoked ipso jure if its holder is absent from Lebanon for three consecutive years; the revocation shall be formalised by a decision of the Minister of Public Health

No pharmacy may be established except under a licence from the Minister of Public Health, and such licence shall be granted only to a Lebanese pharmacist holding a licence to practise the profession of pharmacy in Lebanon

First: An application for a licence to establish a pharmacy shall be submitted to the Ministry of Public Health accompanied by the following documents:

1- A certified copy of the licence to practise the profession of pharmacy in Lebanon.

2- A certificate from the Order of Pharmacists proving the registration of the pharmacist with the Order in due form.

3- A copy of a civil registry extract certified in due form.

4- A copy of the judicial record certified in due form and dated no more than three months prior.

5- Four photographs.

6- A plan of the location of the pharmacy and its internal arrangements.

7- The commercial address of the pharmacy.

8- A declaration signed by the applicant stating that the pharmacy is wholly owned by him, that he manages it for his own account and that his name is not used as a front therein.

Second: The Ministry of Public Health shall refer the application to the Order of Pharmacists to give its opinion, and its opinion shall be consultative. The Order shall be granted a period of two weeks only from the date of its receipt to give its opinion.

If the Order does not give its opinion within the aforementioned period, it shall be disregarded and the Minister of Health shall have the right to decide upon the application. In granting the licence, priority in the submission of applications shall be observed, and if the applications are submitted on the same date, seniority of registration with the Order of Pharmacists shall be taken into consideration.

The licence shall be granted as soon as the conditions set out above are fulfilled, and the licensing decision shall be notified to the Order of Pharmacists, and in the event of the assignment of a licensed pharmacy from one pharmacist to another pharmacist who fulfils all the legal conditions, it shall suffice to inform the Ministry of Public Health, which retains the right to verify the fulfilment of these conditions.

Third: A pharmacist licensed to establish a pharmacy must complete

the establishment formalities and actually open the pharmacy within a maximum period of one year from the date of granting the licence, and if this period expires without the pharmacy actually commencing its operations, the licence shall be deemed revoked ipso jure. The revocation shall be confirmed by a decision of the Minister of Public Health.

Single Article: The Law on the Practice of the Profession of Pharmacy, returned to the Chamber of Deputies by Decree No. 3094 dated 2/6/1980, as amended by the Parliamentary Committees and the Chamber of Deputies, is hereby ratified.

This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Shall be deemed a practice of the profession of pharmacy any act leading to the preparation, compounding, manufacturing, dividing, selling, whether by wholesale or retail, distributing, or possessing with intent to sell or distribute any medicine or pharmaceutical substance intended for internal or external use or by way of injection for the protection of humans or animals from diseases or for curing them therefrom, or which is represented as having such properties.

The licence to practise the profession of pharmacy on Lebanese territory shall be granted by a decision of the Minister of Public Health upon the proposal of the Director General of the Ministry. No person may practise the profession of pharmacy or assume the title of pharmacist unless he fulfils the conditions set forth in the following articles:

A Lebanese pharmacist shall be required:

1- To hold a pharmacy degree from a state faculty of pharmacy or from one of the non-state faculties of pharmacy, provided that such degree is completely identical to the degree granted by the said faculties to the nationals of the country enrolled therein without omission or modification, and that it is equally accepted for practice in that country itself, and that such faculties are recognised by the Lebanese Government.

2- To hold the Lebanese Baccalaureate certificate - Second Part - or its equivalent.

3- Not to have been convicted of a felony or attempted felony of any kind whatsoever, or of a disgraceful misdemeanour or attempted disgraceful misdemeanour. The following shall be deemed disgraceful misdemeanours: theft, fraud, breach of trust, cheque without provision, embezzlement, bribery, rape, intimidation, forgery, use of forged documents, false testimony, perjury, offences against public morals provided for in Title VII of the Penal Code, offences relating to the cultivation of narcotic substances, trafficking therein, or the use thereof. 5- To pass successfully the Colloquium examination conducted by the Ministry of Culture and Higher Education.
The provisions of Article Three shall apply to a pharmacist naturalised with Lebanese nationality immediately upon his acquisition of Lebanese nationality.

A non-Lebanese pharmacist who is a national of an Arab State shall be required:

1- To fulfil the conditions set forth in Article Three.

2- To be a national of a country that accords reciprocal treatment to Lebanese pharmacists there in accordance with an agreement in this regard between the two countries.

3- If he is of foreign origin and naturalised with the nationality of one of the Arab States, five years must have elapsed since his acquisition of such nationality.

A pharmacist must manage the business of his pharmacy in person from both the technical and financial standpoints, and he shall have the right to employ a full-time licensed pharmacist in the capacity of a responsible manager after notifying the Ministry of Public Health and the Order of Pharmacists, as well as employees in the preparation of medicines (medicine preparer). The owner or operator of every pharmaceutical establishment in which more than three employees work in the preparation of medicines must employ, for every three of them beyond the first three, a legally qualified pharmacist. The presence of the pharmacist in the pharmaceutical establishment is mandatory throughout working hours, and if he is compelled to be absent from his pharmacy on account of illness or for any other reason for a period not exceeding one month, he may entrust one of his colleagues with supervising the pharmacy. The deputised pharmacist must attend at the pharmacy throughout working hours and shall personally bear the technical responsibility. In the event that the pharmacist who owns the pharmacy is absent for a period exceeding one month, he shall deputise a full-time pharmacist to manage his pharmacy on his behalf, and he must inform the Ministry of Public Health and the Order of Pharmacists of the matter and obtain a special licence from the Minister of Public Health.

Absence may not exceed a period surpassing one year except in exceptional cases (such as study, specialisation, or illness) assessed by the Minister of Public Health, provided that it shall not in any case exceed two years. The provisions of the third paragraph shall apply to the pharmacist who owns a depot, medical laboratory, or factory. Every violation of these provisions shall subject its perpetrator to the penalties provided for in Article Ninety-Two of this Law and to the temporary or permanent closure of the establishment by decision of the Minister of Public Health.
Every pharmacist must inform the Ministry of Public Health and the Order of Pharmacists of his place of residence.

In places where the rotation system operates (the opening of certain pharmacies at night or on Sundays and holidays), the on-duty pharmacist must take all necessary measures to facilitate for the public

consulting him during the period of his duty.

The Order shall draw up each week a schedule of the names of the on-duty pharmacists, and notification shall be given

regarding them and published in the media through the Ministry of Public Health.

As for other places, the pharmacist must take the measures

that ensure that he may be consulted when necessary at the aforementioned times.

"The presence of a licensed legally qualified pharmacist in a pharmacy that opens at night is mandatory, and the duration and hours of opening shall be determined by a decision of the Council of the Order for each region in order to secure medicine for citizens".

With the exception of the cases established in Article Twenty-Three of this Law, every pharmacist who sells directly to the public must be the owner of the pharmacy that he operates and of the equipment and products present therein, and none other than a pharmacist shall have the right to sell directly to the public. Every pharmacist who manages a pharmacy all or part of which is the property of a minor shall be deemed as its owner and shall be subject to the same legal obligations. Every act, whether a contract or otherwise, carried out for the purpose of transferring ownership of a pharmaceutical establishment, in whole or in part, to a person other than licensed pharmacists shall be deemed absolutely null and void and of no effect, and the parties to the contract and anyone who participated directly or indirectly in the transactions of registering, accepting, or authenticating the contract, including employees, brokers, and intermediaries, shall be subject to the penalties provided for in this Law, and the license granted on this basis shall be deemed null and void.

A pharmacist who sells directly to the public may not:

1- Take charge of more than one pharmacy or work in another pharmacy, with the exception of the case of deputization provided for in Article Sixteen of this Law

2- Have an interest in a pharmacy other than his own pharmacy

3- Engage in his pharmacy in anything other than the trade of medicines, drugs, chemical and sanitary products, equipment and articles related to the art of healing and hygiene, and cosmetic products

4- Perform any other work outside his pharmacy other than voluntary supervision of essential medicines in accredited centers for primary health care

5- Perform continuous night service in any pharmacy, subject to the case provided for in Article Sixteen of this Law

6- Operate or manage any other pharmaceutical establishment or perform any remunerated work connected with his profession outside and inside Lebanese territory

A pharmacist licensed to establish a pharmacy shall submit to the competent departments at the Ministry of Public Health the following documents:

1- A certificate of registration of the pharmacy in the special register of commercial establishments at the Court of First Instance

2- A copy of the title deed if its owner is the owner of the premises where the pharmacy is established

3- Or a copy of a lease agreement for the premises in his name or in the name of his partner if he has a pharmacist partner, provided that the designated use of the leased premises includes a pharmacy

4- A notice of the opening of the pharmacy and the actual commencement of work therein. The Ministry of Public Health shall verify the opening of the pharmacy and the actual commencement of work therein within the time limit specified in the last paragraph of the preceding Article by virtue of a report drawn up and signed by the competent official as well as signed by the person concerned

The opening of new pharmacies shall be licensed after they fulfil the prescribed legal conditions, provided that the distance between the pharmacy intended

to be established and the nearest existing pharmacy is observed so as to be as follows:

- Three hundred metres (300m) across all Lebanese territory.

The distance between a licensed pharmacy and another applying for a licence shall be measured:

-A perpendicular line shall be drawn from the middle of the door of each pharmacy up to the point of its intersection with the centreline of the road.

-The distances shall be measured from the middle of the door of each pharmacy up to the points of intersection with the centreline of the road, and then the distance between the points of intersection shall be added thereto, all of this by the shortest route.

The method of measurement set out in this Law shall apply to all pharmacies licensed after the promulgation of Law No. 635 dated 23/4/1997, provided that all pharmacies existing prior to the promulgation of the aforementioned Law No. 635 /1997 shall be exempted from the three hundred metres (300m) condition, on condition that the distance between them and the nearest existing pharmacy is not less than two hundred metres (200 m.) by the shortest route.
Medicines may not be compounded, prepared and sold to the public except at the premises of the pharmacy

A company shall not be licensed to open a pharmacy unless it is composed of licensed Lebanese pharmacists, at least one of whom holds a licence to open a pharmacy, and neither they nor any one of them has a pharmacy or an interest in another pharmacy. Every agreement aimed at giving a person other than the licensed pharmacist a share in a pharmacy or in its profits in whatever form shall be deemed absolutely null and void. Creditors, whatever the nature of the debt, may not participate in the management of the business of their debtor's pharmacy and its operation.
Creditors, whatever the nature of the debt, may not participate in the management of the business of their debtor's pharmacy and its operation.

Consultation of physicians, veterinarians, midwives and dentists, of whatever kind, is prohibited on the premises of pharmacies or in places leading thereto, with the exception of a case requiring haste in treating an injured or sick person. Whoever violates the provisions of the preceding paragraph shall be deemed to be practising the profession of medicine illegally and shall be punished with the penalty prescribed for such offence.
It shall not be permissible for a pharmacist to practise, in addition to his profession, any act of medicine, veterinary medicine, dentistry or midwifery, even if he holds the legal diploma therefor.

The widow and heirs of a pharmacist may operate the pharmacy left by their decedent for a period of five years at most from the date of his death, provided that they entrust its management to a pharmacist for the first six months and for the remaining period to a pharmacist who has no pharmacy, subject to the approval of the Minister of Public Health, and that they assign it to a licensed pharmacist within the said period

failing which the licence to open the pharmacy shall become cancelled.

If the deceased pharmacist has a child who is a student in the pharmacy, the period shall be extended for him by the length of the legal period of study.

The heirs of a pharmacist upon whose death a period of five years has not elapsed from the date of promulgation of this Law shall benefit from the provisions thereof.

There shall be written on the facade of pharmacies, in large, clear and easily readable Arabic letters, the trade name of the pharmacy and the name or surname of its owner, and if the pharmacy is owned by a company, the name of the company and the name of its responsible manager shall be stated.

The name of the pharmacist, his academic title, the number of the licence of the Ministry of Public Health and his serial number in the Order shall be stated on all letters, invoices and cards, and every pharmacy shall have a seal bearing its trade name, its address and the name of the pharmacist who owns it.
The pharmacy must be arranged in a manner that prevents the public from entering the place where medicines are prepared.

Every physician, veterinarian or dentist residing in a place in which there is no pharmacy may obtain from the Ministry of Public Health a licence to possess a medicine cabinet, each according to his speciality, in order to supply the medicines and preparations which he is legally authorised to prescribe to the persons or animals whom he treats, provided that such place is devoid of an existing pharmacy within a distance of five kilometres, and this licence shall not under any circumstances entitle its holder to open a pharmacy or to keep the medicines in a place other than the premises of his clinic, and the medicines which he supplies to his patients must be divided in advance by a pharmacist who is the owner of a pharmacy and who records his name and academic title on these preparations
The physicians licensed pursuant to the preceding Article to possess a medicine cabinet must keep the registers imposed on pharmacists and shall, like them, be subject to inspection

The licence granted in the cases mentioned above shall be deemed revoked ipso jure immediately upon the opening of a legal pharmacy in the same locality or in an area situated five kilometres or less therefrom, and the holder of the revoked licence shall be granted a non-renewable period of six months to liquidate the medicines in his possession
A physician shall be entitled to supply his patients with free medical samples only, and he shall not be entitled to sell medicines even if he holds a degree in pharmacy

A medicine is any simple or compound substance having curative or preventive properties or having a physiological action and used in human or veterinary medicine and surgery. The following shall be deemed medicines or treated as medicines:

1- Proprietary and official pharmaceutical preparations, and as defined in Title Five

2- Sterilised articles having medical properties and specially prepared for dressing wounds, in particular sterilised tissues and pieces of cloth or those impregnated with antiseptic medical products, and other substances determined by a decision of the Minister of Public Health

3- Medicinal mineral waters, namely waters which cannot be used for ordinary drinking in a state of general health and which are determined by a decision of the Minister of Public Health

4- Sera, vaccines and medical substances derived from humans or animals

5- Substances prepared for baths having medical properties

6- Cosmetic substances containing therapeutic medical substances

7- Milk specially prepared for infants under six months in containers not exceeding half a kilogram, and modified milk in accordance with the regulations relating to the classification of milk

1- Owners of pharmacies shall supply their pharmacies with synthetic substances, narcotics, and essential medicines required by a patient in emergency cases, as determined by a decision of the Minister of Public Health.

2- A pharmacy must contain a separate area for preparing, compounding, and fitting out medicines.

3- A pharmacy must be equipped with the following equipment:

- Scales weighing from one centigram to one kilogram

- A set of glass measures graduated in sequence from ten cubic centigrams to one litre

- A refrigerator for preserving all items that are technically required to be kept therein

- The latest edition of the official lists and their supplements published by the Ministry of Public Health containing the names and addresses of physicians, veterinarians, dentists, and midwives

- The official pharmacopoeia of the Lebanese Republic upon its issuance, and until it is issued, the pharmacy shall be supplied with the latest edition of the French, American, or British Pharmacopoeia

In preserving medicines as defined in Article Three, the instructions set forth in the pharmacopoeia shall be observed, and all spoiled and suspect substances shall be destroyed, and substances having a specified period for use shall not be kept after the expiry of such period.

1- All public and private hospitals shall have inside them a pharmacy managed by a full-time pharmacist, provided that it has no access to the public road and that it does not dispense medicines except to patients during their stay therein under treatment.

2- Hospitals existing on the date of entry into force of this Law shall be granted a period of six months to comply with the obligation provided for in the preceding paragraph.

Owners of factories and workshops may acquire a medicine cabinet for first aid, the contents of which shall be determined by the Pharmacy Department at the Ministry of Public Health. Such medicines may not be used except for workers in the factory or workshop, free of charge, and heads of establishments shall be required to obtain a licence from the Minister of Public Health to acquire the medicine cabinet.

The prescribed registers for compounded prescriptions, narcotics, and synthetic substances shall be kept in pharmacies. Pharmacies and medicine cabinets shall be subject to the inspection provided for in this Law.

a- The manufacture, importation, storage, marketing, and dispensing of medicinal herbs and the products derived therefrom that have a therapeutic nature, whether alone or mixed, or that may contain harmful or toxic substances, are all restricted to pharmacists, and shall be subject to registration by the Technical Committee at the Ministry of Public Health.

Likewise restricted to pharmacists are:

1- Every preparation or operation intended to alter the properties of medicinal plants or to extract products therefrom.

2- The sale of products derived from the preparations or operations referred to, whether the sale is by wholesale and by retail.

b - Commercial information and advertising regarding medicinal herbs and other preparations that have a therapeutic nature is prohibited.

Trade in plants and parts of plants not mentioned in the preceding Article shall remain free, provided that they are sold in their natural state and under their scientific or common name, together with the name of their country of production where applicable, without any unusual designation or therapeutic indication

The sale of secret medicines is prohibited, and every medicine whose label does not bear a statement of the substance or substances of which it is composed, the batch number, and the expiry date shall be deemed a secret medicine

A pharmacist is strictly prohibited from carrying out, in person or through another, publicity for his pharmacy among physicians or among others, or from seeking to attract customers to it in a manner detrimental to the interests of other pharmacists in any way whatsoever.

The Minister of Public Health may determine the classes of pharmaceutical preparations (codex) that pharmacists who are owners of pharmacies are licensed to manufacture Every medicine prepared in pharmacies must be placed in a container such as a bottle, box, or vessel, or bearing the name and address of the pharmacy, the method of use of the medicine, and its expiry date, in accordance with what is stated in the medical prescription, the serial batch number, its price, and the name of the patient The adhesive label shall be white in colour if the medicine is intended for internal use, and the adhesive label shall be red in colour if the medicine is intended for external use and there shall be written thereon for external use with the addition of the word poison if the medicine contains toxic or dangerous substances, and the adhesive label shall be green in colour for medicine intended for veterinary use, whether internally or externally, with the phrase for veterinary use, and if the medicine technically requires shaking upon use, that must be explicitly stated on the adhesive label in the Arabic language and in one of the two languages, French or English

It is not permissible to import, possess, sell, or distribute any substance among the substances intended for pharmaceutical use if the conditions required by the official pharmacopoeia in which it is mentioned are not met therein

No pharmacist may dispense any medicine without a medical prescription or with the knowledge of a physician, with the exception of medicines specified by a decision of the Minister of Public Health after obtaining the opinion of the Order of Physicians and the Order of Pharmacists, and pharmaceutical practice shall continue as before until the issuance of the decision of the Minister of Public Health.

A prescription shall be written in an easily legible manner whereby every pharmacy is able to prepare the medicine prescribed therein, and every prescription that does not bear the name and address of its signatory in a legible manner must be refused.

A pharmacist must prepare medicines in accordance with the specified pharmacopoeia, and if no particular pharmacopoeia is mentioned in the prescription, the pharmacist may prepare the medicine in accordance with the pharmacopoeias in force in Lebanon, provided that he states on the medical prescription and in the prescription register the pharmacopoeia pursuant to which the medicine was prepared.

A medical prescription shall be in accordance with the model approved by the Ministry of Public Health and printed in three copies so that each of the physician, the pharmacist and the patient retains a copy thereof.

No pharmacist may, of his own accord or by agreement with the bearer of the prescription, alter the quantities of the substances mentioned therein, or substitute one substance for another. No physician may designate a particular laboratory if the preparation or substance is listed in one of the drug formularies under its scientific name, and no pharmacist may prepare a medical prescription written in terms agreed upon with its writer. If a pharmacist perceives an error in the writing of a medical prescription, he may not, of his own accord or with the consent of its bearer, alter its text or modify the dosages mentioned therein; rather, he must draw the attention of the physician to the matters that attracted his notice therein and request a written confirmation of its contents.

A - A pharmacist shall be entitled, notwithstanding any other provision, to dispense to the bearer of a medical prescription a drug under a generic name - Generique or Brand Generic other than that mentioned therein, subject to the following conditions:

1 - That the substitute drug be included in the list of substitute drugs approved by the Ministry of Public Health in accordance with the standards of the World Health Organization, provided that:

a - The drug dispensed is composed of the same active substances entering into the composition of the drug mentioned in the medical prescription and in the same quantities, and has the same bioequivalence and pharmaceutical form.

b - The public retail price in Lebanon of the drug he dispenses is lower than the public retail price in Lebanon of the drug mentioned in the medical prescription.

2 - That the patient consents to the substitution.

B - The pharmacist shall record, after verifying on his own responsibility that the above conditions are met, the name of the drug he dispensed on the receipt that he delivers to the bearer of the prescription, together with the phrase "Substituted pursuant to the new Article 47 of the Law on the Practice of the Profession of Pharmacy", and the insuring institutions, both public and private, shall be required to accept the substituted drug and reimburse the price in accordance with the rate and principles adopted by each of them, without requiring a medical prescription specifying the substituted drug".

A pharmacist may not compound drugs containing any of the substances listed in Schedules (A) and (B) of the drug regulations approved by the Ministry of Public Health and psychotropic synthetic substances except pursuant to a medical prescription

Every prescription that has been compounded shall be entered in the register of prescriptions, stating the name of its signatory, the substances and quantities of which it is composed, the method of its use, its price, its serial number, and the date of its preparation, and the entry must be in legible handwriting and must not contain any blank spaces or have any erasure or interlineation made therein

The prescription shall be returned to its owner after being stamped with the seal of the pharmacy and having its serial number and its price stated thereon, and if the pharmacist retains the original prescription, whether pursuant to the laws and regulations in force or out of a desire on his part to absolve himself of liability, he shall give the bearer thereof, upon his request, a true copy thereof free of charge, stamped with the seal of the pharmacy and containing its serial number and its price

Pharmacists shall be bound to preserve professional secrecy; they may not disclose to anyone the prescriptions delivered to them, nor give them to anyone other than the physician who prescribed them, the patient, or his messenger

Medicines which have been previously prepared and divided for their sale or display for sale through pharmacies under the responsibility of their producer shall be deemed proprietary or standard pharmaceutical preparations subject to the provisions of this Law, and hair dyes and cosmetic materials containing a dangerous poisonous substance or medical substances having a therapeutic effect shall be deemed proprietary pharmaceutical preparations

Every proprietary or standard pharmaceutical preparation must have the following particulars stated on the container containing it, on the outside of its wrapper, and in the internal medical leaflets:

1- The name and address of the factory or pharmacy where it was produced

2- The name of the preparation and its quantity

3- The names and quantities of all substances entering into its composition, and they must be named by their scientific names or by the names given to them in the pharmacopoeia, while drawing attention to poisonous substances and substances which have side effects or the use of which is prohibited except upon consulting a physician, and all restrictions imposed by the competent departments in the country of origin

4- The pharmacist must send to the Lebanese factory or the importer the preparations which have a specified date for use whose period is nearing expiry, and the Lebanese factory or the importer must replace these preparations and notify the Ministry of Public Health of every preparation in its possession which has a specified date for use whose period is nearing expiry, and the Lebanese factory or the importer must replace these preparations and notify the Ministry of Public Health of every preparation in its possession which has a specified date for use whose period is nearing expiry, and the destruction of these preparations shall be carried out under the supervision of the Ministry of Public Health, and the same method shall apply to every medicine in which an error in manufacturing or any change in its external appearance appears

5- The serial registration number of the licence of the Ministry of Public Health

6- The selling price to the public as determined in the latest tariff of the Ministry of Public Health

7- The batch processing number

8- The date of manufacture

9- The expiry date of efficacy

Proprietary or official pharmaceutical preparations manufactured abroad may not be imported except by a Lebanese pharmacist who is the owner of a pharmacy or the owner of a drug warehouse.

Proprietary or official pharmaceutical preparations may not be imported, sold, or distributed in Lebanon unless they conform to the specifications borne by the preparation as sold in the country of origin.

The applicant for a licence shall submit all documents proving the same within the registration application in accordance with Article fifty-four of this Law.

In all cases, preparations may not be imported unless they are of public utility. An application for a licence to manufacture a proprietary or official pharmaceutical preparation in Lebanon or to import it from abroad shall be accompanied by a receipt from the Ministry of Finance in an amount equivalent to twice the minimum wage, which shall remain an acquired right of the Treasury.

This amount may be amended upwards or downwards by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Health and the Minister of Finance.

"Hospitals classified as university hospitals shall have the right to apply to import the medicines that they need for research and education and that are not available on the local markets, without regard to the provisions of Article five of this Law.

The application shall be referred to the Technical Committee, which shall decide thereon within fifteen days of its submission.

The Committee shall refer its decision of approval to the Import Department for execution.

The hospitals classified as university hospitals that have the right to import medicines shall be determined by decisions of the Minister of Public Health.
The importation, exportation, and re-exportation of medicines, chemical substances, and milk prepared for infant nutrition shall be subject to a permit granted by the Ministry of Public Health.
The sale of medical samples is strictly prohibited, as is carrying out any barter thereof.

Medical samples that are distributed free of charge must satisfy the following conditions:

The particulars set forth in Article fifty-three of this Law.

That the manufacturer print on the inner container and on the outer packaging the phrase: "Free medical sample - not for sale" in the Arabic language and in a foreign language.

All licensed proprietary or official pharmaceutical preparations, whether manufactured in Lebanon or imported from abroad, shall be registered in a special register at the Ministry of Public Health. The approval of the Ministry of Public Health must be obtained upon transferring the ownership of the preparation or changing its origin.

It is prohibited to manufacture any proprietary or official pharmaceutical preparation in Lebanon or to import it from abroad except with a licence from the Ministry of Public Health. The licence application shall be accompanied by six samples of the preparation and, in the event of importation from abroad, by an official certificate issued by the competent authority in the country of origin certifying that the preparation is registered therein and sold on the local market, with the date of its placement into circulation. The licence application shall also be accompanied by the following information:

1- The complete composition of the preparation in terms of the types and quantities of the substances entering into it, its active principles and its side effects.

2- A detailed description of the analytical determination, particularly for the active substances.

3- Detailed information on the designation of the preparation, its pharmacological and clinical effect and the methods of its use. The applications and samples shall be referred to a technical committee composed of:

- The Director General of the Ministry of Public Health - Chairman

- The Head of the Pharmacy Service at the Ministry of Public Health - Member

- The Head of the Inspection Department at the Ministry of Public Health - Member

- The Head of the Importation Department at the Ministry of Public Health - Member and Rapporteur

- Two members delegated by the Order of Physicians, one of whom is a professor of medicine and the second a professor of pharmacology

- Two members delegated by the Order of Pharmacists, one of whom is a professor of pharmaceutical sciences.

* The committee shall decide on every application submitted to it within three months.

In the event of rejection of the preparation, the rejection must be reasoned.

In the event of acceptance of the preparation, the decision of the committee shall be referred to the Pricing Committee provided for in Article Eighty of this Law, together with two samples bearing the registration number and date and the price requested by the importer to be adopted.

The remaining samples shall be referred to the Central Laboratory for analysis.

Decisions in this committee shall be taken by a majority, and in the event of a tie, the Chairman shall have the casting vote.

The Chairman and members of the technical committee shall receive an attendance allowance in return for their work on the committee, the amount of which shall be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Health.

After the registration of the preparation, it shall not be permissible to make any amendment to the particulars set forth in Article Fifty-Three of this Law except after the approval of the Ministry of Public Health, and if the Ministry of Public Health decides to analyse the preparation, the expenses of the analysis shall be borne by its owner.

1- It shall not be permissible to establish a factory for proprietary or pharmacopoeial pharmaceutical preparations except with a licence from the Ministry of Public Health, the conditions of which shall be determined by decree in accordance with the provisions relating to the establishment of medicine factories.

2- The licence to establish and operate the factory shall be granted to a full-time Lebanese pharmacist, and the licence may also be granted to a Lebanese joint-stock company; and if it is not a Lebanese joint-stock company, in these two cases at least one of the partners therein must be a Lebanese pharmacist who shall be responsible towards the Ministry of Public Health in accordance with the provisions of Article Sixty-Three of this Law.
