3- The licensing decision shall be notified to the Order of Pharmacists, and the licensee shall establish the factory and commence production works within a maximum period of two years from the date of issuance of the licensing decision, failing which the licensing decision shall be deemed revoked ipso jure, and this revocation shall be confirmed by a decision of the Minister of Public Health.
The factory must be equipped with an analysis laboratory comprising all the machines, tools and materials necessary for examining the products of the factory and the raw materials received by it.
Every medicine factory shall have a technical director responsible for manufacturing, and the technical director shall be required to be a full-time pharmacist licensed to practise the profession.

In addition to the technical director mentioned in the preceding Article, the work in each of the type of testing, executive compounding and the analysis laboratory mentioned in Article Sixty-Two must be supervised by at least one specialised and full-time pharmacist who shall be responsible with the technical director for the quality of the items that the factory prepares in accordance with the rules of good manufacturing practice.

The conditions of the labels must be specified and the following information must be mentioned on the inner and outer packaging:

The name of the producing factory, the country of origin and the trade name, the scientific name, the storage conditions of the medication, the registration number at the Ministry of Health, the retail price to the public in Lebanon in Lebanese Pounds, the batch number, the manufacturing date, the expiry date, provided that the scientific leaflet includes a warning that medications must not fall within the reach of children. In addition to the imposition of a safety lock by the Ministry of Public Health for medications that require that.

The particulars mentioned on the labels of proprietary and standard pharmaceutical preparations and in the leaflets and advertisements distributed therefrom provided for in Article Forty-One shall conform to the substances that those preparations actually contain, and expressions contrary to public morals or liable to mislead and entice the public must not be mentioned therein.

The approval of the Ministry of Public Health shall be obtained for the texts of those particulars, leaflets or advertisements before using or publishing them.

Owners of pharmaceutical preparation factories or their importer, pharmaceutical owners or their importers, owners of warehouses may not refrain from selling the preparations they manufacture or import to the persons and pharmaceutical establishments licensed therefor against payment of their price, and they may not be sold to the public

1- A special register shall be kept or set aside showing the incoming and outgoing movement and the manner and places of distribution, with the mention of the batch numbers

2- National and foreign medication factories must comply with and fill out the special form for monitoring and recording side effects and contraindications

3- National and foreign medication factories must withdraw samples of marketed medications and conduct the necessary analyses to verify stability, safety, efficacy and quality in accordance with the certification scheme established by the World Health Organization

The pharmacist supervising the analysis laboratory must:

1- Examine with complete accuracy every batch of products, yields, and preparations that have been prepared in the factory prior to commencing the distribution or sale thereof and prior to removing the same from the factory

2- Examine the raw materials to verify that their physical properties or chemical composition conform to the approved official regulations or to what is stated in scientific books or other references, and in the event of non-conformity, he must notify the Primary Ministry so that they may be destroyed by the Ministry of Public Health or returned to the country of origin under the supervision of the Ministry of Public Health

3- Keep a special register in which the results of the analyses of the raw materials and of each manufactured batch are recorded under serial numbers with the date

4- Retain samples from each batch even after the marketing thereof in order to conduct periodic examinations thereon in accordance with the recommendations of the World Health Organization; the results of these analyses shall be recorded in the special register in accordance with the rules specified in the preceding paragraph
It shall not be permissible to use the factory to manufacture substances or preparations other than pharmaceutical preparations

The pharmacist who prepares proprietary or official pharmaceutical preparations in his pharmacy and the technical director of a medicines factory must both keep a ledger or card in which he successively records the amount of the quantity prepared each time of each preparation and the date of preparation, and assign a serial number to each preparation operation, and also record the quantities used therefrom, the date of their disposal, and the parties to whom they were delivered, and the pharmacist responsible for analyses shall sign this ledger

1- It shall not be permissible to remove varieties of potassium chlorate or barium chlorate and picric and nitric acid and their salts from the factory except with a permit from the Ministry of Interior and the Ministry of National Defense and after the approval of the Minister of Public Health

2- The active raw materials used in the manufacture of pharmaceutical preparations must include, as a condition for their importation and use, quality control certificates for each batch separately, in addition to the analyses that must be conducted by the Ministry of Public Health and the quality control department in the factory, and the results shall be recorded and documented in special registers

3- Wrappers must bear clear writings and distinctive marks for medicines intended for external use and those intended for internal use, and antibiotics, narcotic substances, and psychotropic substances must also be distinguished by clear instructions and special signs

The Minister of Public Health may issue a decision, upon the proposal of the Technical Committee, prohibiting the circulation of any pharmaceutical preparation if it becomes evident to him that the use thereof has caused harm to public health, or that it is useless, or if the country of origin has ceased selling it, whilst affirming the implementation of the decisions and recommendations of the World Health Organization in this regard. In such case, the registration of the preparation shall be struck off the registers of the Ministry if it is a proprietary or standard pharmaceutical preparation, and the existing quantities thereof shall be administratively seized wherever found and destroyed, and their owners shall have no right of recourse against the Ministry for any compensation of whatever kind. The Pharmaceutical Inspection Department shall withdraw suspicious samples from pharmacies, depots, or factories and analyse them at the Central Laboratory. In the event that any defect becomes apparent, the Minister of Health shall take a decision to destroy the spoiled medicine, and the person responsible for fraud or negligence shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

1- The trade of representatives of medicine factories who practice their activity prior to the effective date of this Law shall remain free, and they shall not import for their own account, but rather for the account of pharmacists or licensed depot owners, or for their own private depot established or to be established in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

2- The right to represent medicine factories after the issuance of this Law shall be restricted to Lebanese pharmacists or Lebanese companies licensed by the Ministry of Public Health to practice the profession.

A scientific office shall be established for every pharmaceutical factory whose registered preparations imported or manufactured in Lebanon exceed thirty in number, or for several factories not exceeding three in number whose total preparations do not exceed thirty, the management of which shall be entrusted to a full-time legally qualified Lebanese pharmacist, and the activities of this office shall be restricted to the following:

1 - Distributing free medical samples of pharmaceuticals to physicians, dentists, veterinarians, hospitals, dispensaries and scientific research institutions.

2 - Distributing medical information on pharmaceuticals through leaflets, books, journals, scientific and medical publications and scientific motion picture films, and organising scientific seminars and lectures.

3 - The direction and distribution of the aforementioned medical information and samples shall be entrusted to full-time pharmacists, and to full-time physicians not practising the profession of medicine pursuant to a declaration authenticated at the Order of Physicians to which they belong.

4 - The rights of those working in these two fields prior to the promulgation of this Law shall be preserved after they produce documents certified by the Order of Pharmacists and the Ministry of Public Health proving that they have carried out these activities for a period of not less than two years.

5 - Scientific offices and all pharmaceutical establishments shall submit a list of the names of the pharmacists or physicians working for them to the Ministry of Public Health - Department of Pharmacy - under the responsibility of the director of the office or establishment, and any false statement shall subject its perpetrator to the penalties provided for in the ninety-second Article of this Law.

1- No licence for the establishment of a depot shall be granted except to a Lebanese pharmacist or to Lebanese pharmacists, one of whom works exclusively and is licensed to practise the profession of pharmacy in Lebanon. A pharmacist who is the proprietor of a depot may neither be the proprietor of a pharmacy or a laboratory nor a partner in either of them, and he shall personally undertake the management of his depot throughout the official working hours, and the regulations on attendance and working hours and the conditions of absence shall apply to him as they are applied to a pharmacist who is the proprietor of a pharmacy.

2- A depot may not have other branches; however, depots which have branches licensed prior to the date of entry into force of this Law shall be exempted from this matter, provided that the management of each branch is undertaken by a legally qualified pharmacist working exclusively. A licence may be granted to a company one of whose partners is a legally qualified pharmacist authorised to practise the profession in Lebanon. The technical responsibility of the depot shall be vested in a legally qualified pharmacist working exclusively. The licence shall be granted to the company in its style or its trade name.

3- The technical management of the depot shall be vested in one of the pharmacist partners, and the same conditions applied to a pharmacist who is the proprietor of a depot referred to in the first paragraph shall apply to him, and this pharmacist shall be responsible towards the Ministry of Health. A licence may be granted for the establishment of one or more branches for the company, and the licence shall not be granted unless the conditions applied in the paragraph above are fulfilled in the branch, and it shall also be subject to the legal formalities for the establishment of depots.

4- The decision licensing the establishment of the depot shall be notified to each of the Order of Pharmacists and the Syndicate of Importers of Medicinal Products and Proprietors of Depots in Lebanon.

It shall be required in a depot:

1- That it have a private entrance.

2- That it not be on a floor situated at the level of the public highway.

3- That its proprietor engage therein only in the sale of articles and medicinal products which are sold in pharmacies.

The licence stipulated in the seventy-fifth Article shall be granted to the applicant therefor, whether a pharmacist or a company, pursuant to an application containing the address of the depot and a declaration by the applicant that he is the owner or lessee of the depot, accompanied by a copy of the title deed or of the lease contract; and if the application is issued by a company, it must be accompanied by a copy of the company contract and its articles of association.

The provisions of the tenth and eleventh Articles of this Law shall apply to depots, and they may not be transferred from one place to another except by an authorisation from the Ministry of Public Health, and this authorisation shall be granted as of right if the legal conditions are fulfilled in the new place.

Proprietors of depots may not sell or distribute medicinal products to persons other than pharmacists who are proprietors of pharmacies or proprietors of depots or those who have been licensed to sell to the public pursuant to this Law.

Owners of depots shall keep records of the incoming and outgoing products and medications that they possess, and any person who holds narcotic substances or synthetic substances shall keep special additional registers for each of them. In all cases, the entries recorded in the registers shall be substantiated, with respect to the effort of the substances entering the depot, by the invoices pertaining thereto, and with respect to the substances exiting therefrom, by the receipts given by pharmacy owners or licensed persons. These documents shall be preserved for a period of five years. Depots shall be subject to the inspection imposed on pharmacies.

The Minister of Public Health shall establish, by a decision issued by him, a tariff of the selling prices of ready-made pharmaceutical preparations, and the bases for pricing medications shall be established pursuant to a committee formed by a decision of the Minister of Public Health after taking the opinion of the competent ministries, the two syndicates of pharmacists and of medication importers, depot owners, and medication manufacturers. There shall be mentioned on every application referred to the Pricing Committee the number and date of registration with the committee provided for in Article Fifty-Four of this Law, and the Committee shall decide on every application received by it from the Scientific Committee within a time limit not exceeding one month if it is accompanied by all the necessary documents. In this case, if the Committee does not decide on the application within the aforementioned time limit, the Minister shall grant an import, manufacturing, or marketing licence for a period of one year at the price submitted by the concerned party, and then its import shall be suspended or he shall abide by the price set by the Committee. The Ministry of Public Health shall establish a directory of licensed pharmaceutical preparations approved by the Technical Committee and whose prices have been set by the Pricing Committee. No medication may be sold in Lebanon contrary to what is registered in this directory and at the official price set by the Ministry of Public Health.

It is prohibited to combine the practice of the pharmacy profession in a pharmaceutical establishment with:

1- Any official civil or military post

2- Teaching in the capacity of a full-time professor in institutes of medicine or pharmacy and others; however, a pharmacist who holds any official civil or military post or practices teaching in the capacity of a full-time professor may own a pharmaceutical establishment provided that he contracts with a licensed and full-time pharmacist to manage it

In order to ensure the application of the laws and regulations in force relating to the practice of the profession of pharmacy, the combatting of the adulteration of substances with medicinal or health properties, the verification of the quality of products, and the investigation of the manufacture and sale of pharmaceutical preparations or compounds without a legal licence, an inspection of pharmacies, medicine cabinets and, in general, all places in which products with medicinal, health or toxic properties are manufactured, deposited or offered for sale or distribution shall be carried out periodically and whenever the need arises, and pharmacists, owners of medicine depots, physicians authorised pursuant to Article Thirty-Two of this Law, and anyone in possession of products with medicinal, health or toxic properties, whether they are owners of establishments or managers thereof, must allow the pharmacist inspector to examine the products present in their depots, factories or clinic premises and their annexes, and they must show him, upon his request, all the documents relating to the practice of their profession from the technical aspect, enable him to visit all the places and annexes used for their trade and their burning, inspect the entries and registers special to synthetic substances and narcotics, and take samples when necessary for analyses, and this by order of the Head of the Pharmacy Department. Analyses shall be carried out on all standard medicines upon their importation or manufacture before allowing their sale and distribution in the Central Laboratory affiliated to the Ministry of Health, in addition to the results of the analyses issued by the quality control laboratory in the producing factories, and the Ministry of Health may, where necessary, analyse any pharmaceutical preparation by trade name at the expense of the importer or the manufacturer within a period of five days

1- Standard medicines: Analysis is compulsory at every importation operation and for every batch, provided that the result is given within five days from the submission of the substances subject to the analysis, and the Central Laboratory shall be bound to accept the application immediately and give a receipt of delivery, and if the results of the analysis are not given within the five days, the importer or the manufacturer shall be allowed to market or manufacture them under his own responsibility

2- Proprietary medicines: Analysis is when necessary; however, requesting a quality control certificate for every batch of medicine manufactured locally or imported is a compulsory matter

3- Vaccines and blood derivatives: In addition to what is mentioned above, a quality control certificate for every batch from the governmental control laboratory in the country of origin shall be requested

4- With respect to pharmaceutical, medical and cosmetic substances, a certificate of validity from the health authorities in the country of origin shall be requested, and the importation of sterilised substances shall be prohibited if the packages do not include the date of manufacture, the expiry date, the batch number, and the method and type of sterilisation (and this includes the fulfilment of the health conditions for the male barrier preservative and contraceptives)

5- With respect to milk prepared for infants, its importation shall be subject to a certificate of validity from the country of origin (the regulatory authorities), and its importation shall be subject to registration and pricing

Each of the inspectors affiliated with the Pharmaceutical Inspection Department in the Pharmacy Service shall take the following oath before the Court of First Instance (Civil Chamber):

"I swear by God that I shall perform my duties with honesty, loyalty, and honour, that I shall work to apply the laws and regulations with all precision, and that I shall preserve the secrecy and dignity of the profession"

They may request the assistance of members of the public forces when necessary. The inspection of pharmacies and pharmaceutical establishments shall be carried out by an inspector pharmacist, whether alone or accompanied by his superior.

Following each inspection he carries out, the inspector shall draw up a report on the result thereof, including the remarks of the person subjected to the inspection, and shall submit it to his superior. In the event that the inspector ascertains violations in accordance with what is provided for in Title Ten (Penalties), he shall draw up a report of the violations at the site of the violation, and the Order of Pharmacists and the Syndicate of Drug Importers and Warehouse Owners in Lebanon shall be notified of a copy of this report. Where the violation falls under the provisions of Articles Eighty-Nine and Ninety of this Law, the inspector shall carry out the confiscation of the medication after drawing up a detailed inventory of the confiscated quantity and items.

Violations of the legal texts relating to fraud, the Narcotics Law, and the accuracy of measures, weights, and all other instruments of pharmacies shall be recorded, and reports thereon shall be drawn up in accordance with the legal provisions relating thereto. This right shall belong exclusively to the inspectors affiliated with the Pharmacy Service in the Ministry of Public Health, notwithstanding any contrary provision, and without prejudice to the powers vested in members of the judicial police.

Any person who establishes a pharmacy or a pharmaceutical establishment, or manufactures and sells wholesale or retail, or distributes medications, or possesses them for the purpose of sale or distribution without fulfilling the legal conditions and holding the legal licence, shall be punished by a fine of ten million to fifty million Lebanese pounds and by imprisonment from one year to three years, or by either of these two penalties, in addition to the confiscation of the medication or medications for the account of the Ministry of Public Health. In all cases, the penalty of imprisonment may not be less than three months and the fine may not be less than its minimum limit, and in case of recidivism the penalty shall be doubled. The Ministry of Public Health may temporarily close the pharmacy or establishment established in violation of the law until the judiciary issues its final judgment in the case.

Any proprietor of a depot who sells to other than licensed pharmaceutical establishments shall be punished by a fine from six million to twenty million Lebanese Pounds and by imprisonment from two months to six months, or by either of these two penalties, and under no circumstances may the penalty of imprisonment be less than two months and the fine less than its minimum limit, and upon recurrence the penalty shall be doubled in addition to the closure of the depot and the withdrawal of its licence.

Any proprietor of a pharmacy, depot, factory, importer, or agent who refrains from selling medicines or closes his premises without permission from the Ministry of Public Health shall be subject to the same penalty provided for in the eighty-seventh Article. This Ministry may confiscate the medicines that are the subject of the monopoly.

And any pharmacist who enables, by lending his name or by any means whatsoever, persons who are not pharmacists to practise this profession shall be subject to the same penalty provided for in the eighty-seventh Article of this Law and shall be prohibited from practising the profession of pharmacy, and all other persons provided for in the last paragraph of the fourteenth Article of this Law shall also be punished by the same penalty when they violate the provisions of the said paragraph.

Any importer or depot that prices or sells medicine or pharmaceutical preparations contrary to the contents of the decision of the Minister of Public Health determining the pricing shall be punished by a fine from ten million to fifty million Lebanese Pounds, and under no circumstances may the fine be less than its minimum limit, and the Ministry shall also have the right to confiscate the medicine and sell it to pharmacies at the specified price, and the latter must pay the price to the importer, and in the event that the said violation is committed by a pharmacy, the fine may not be less than half of its maximum limit, and in addition to that the medicine shall be confiscated by the Ministry.

The operating licence may be recovered temporarily or permanently pursuant to a decision by the Minister of Public Health issued after hearing the concerned party, in the following cases:

1- The loss by the licence of the concerned party of one of the legal conditions

2- The declaration of bankruptcy of the pharmacist, and the licence shall be returned if the bankruptcy ends with a final composition agreement

3- The issuance of the bankruptcy of the pharmacist, and the licence shall be returned with the health of others as a result of an act of his profession

Whoever commits fraud in pharmaceutical substances, or sells, manufactures, imports, distributes, or in general performs any act involving counterfeit, smuggled, expired, unregistered medicines or medicines the circulation of which is prohibited, shall be punished by imprisonment for at least five years and by a fine of one hundred million to one hundred and fifty million Lebanese pounds, in addition to the destruction of the medicines at his expense. Every pharmacist who is convicted of a felony or who commits fraud in pharmaceutical substances, sells secret medicines or narcotics, or for the illegal practice of the medical profession, shall be deprived for life of the right to practise the profession of pharmacy.

All other contraventions of the provisions of this Law shall subject the perpetrator thereof to punishment by a fine of four million to ten million Lebanese pounds, and under no circumstances may the fine be less than its minimum limit; upon repetition, the fine shall be doubled and imprisonment shall pass from ten days, that is, a month, and upon repetition the two penalties of imprisonment and the fine may not be less than half of the former and the maximum limit of the latter.

The Ministry of Culture and Higher Education shall levy on each candidate for the Colloquium examination required to practise the profession of pharmacy a lump-sum registration fee to be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Culture and Higher Education and the Minister of Finance.

The Ministry of Health shall levy a lump-sum fee on:

a- Every licence to practise the profession of pharmacy on Lebanese territory

b- Every licence to open and operate a pharmacy, warehouse or factory for medicines in Lebanon

c- Every medicinal preparation registered in Lebanon. The value of these fees shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Health and the Minister of Finance

An importer, or his successors in title, who is not a pharmacist and who was licensed by the Ministry of Public Health prior to the date of entry into force of this Law may continue his work, and if he is the owner of a warehouse, he must engage for the technical management a full-time legal pharmacist who attends throughout the working hours of the warehouse and who must be neither the owner of a pharmacy nor a partner therein.
All establishments and persons provided for in this Law must comply with its provisions within a period of six months from the date of its publication in the Official Gazette.

Pharmacies owned by legal pharmacists that were licensed in accordance with the legislative texts in force prior to the date of entry into force of this Law shall remain in existence regardless of their number and the distance separating them from one another, and if they are compelled as a result of force majeure to change their location, they shall be entitled to remain in the vicinity, provided that they observe the same distance that separated them from the nearest pharmacy to them and after the approval of the Ministry of Public Health.

This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

This law defines the municipal fees and surcharges collected directly by municipalities and those collected for their account, as well as the rules and procedures that govern the affairs of their assessment and collection.
The proposed law concerning municipal fees and surcharges, as amended by the Joint Parliamentary Committees, is hereby ratified. This law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication.
Each municipality shall determine and collect within its municipal bounds the fees whose types, bases of assessment, rates, or amounts are specified in this law.

An annual fee on the rental value shall be imposed on the occupants of buildings. The word (buildings) is understood to mean buildings in themselves, their parts, and whatever is deemed as such. The following shall be deemed as buildings or parts of buildings:

- Marine or land vehicles and other installations fixed in a permanent place and used like buildings for residence, trade, industry, or any other purpose, whatever the duration of their manufacture and whatever the place of their presence.

- Vacant lands used for non-agricultural investment purposes, whether annexed to buildings or independent thereof.

The fee shall be imposed on the occupant of the building, whether a tenant or an owner.

Shall be deemed an occupant anyone who exploits a building, whether an owner or a tenant, by way of leasing it as furnished or unfurnished rooms or apartments on a periodic basis (seasonal or monthly...) or by way of placing the building, its apartments, its rooms, or its fittings at the disposal of third parties in return for a specific consideration or a lump-sum subscription (sea baths or others), whatever the duration and form of the disposal.

The concept of rental value includes everything that the lessor receives or obtains from the tenant in cash or in the form of a benefit. It includes in particular, and by way of enumeration not limitation, the following:

1 - The basic rent amounts, including the amounts pertaining to the leasing of the right to use the facades of the building, the roofs, or the installations erected thereon.

2 - The consideration for services provided by the lessor to the tenant, such as heating, cooling, hot water, operation of electric elevators, and others.

3 - The value of the benefits obtained by the lessor from the tenant.

4 - The rental value of furniture and equipment, with the exception of the fittings and machinery of industrial premises.

5 - The value of the burdens that fall upon the lessor and which the tenant takes upon himself, such as the expenses of major repairs, the expenses of supplementary works that render the building more fit for use, and insurance premiums against risks the liability for which falls upon the owner.

Notwithstanding the provisions of the thirty-fourth Article of the Built Property Tax Law issued on 17 September 1962, the owner or the operator must register the lease contracts and their annexes at the municipal department within whose jurisdiction the property is located, or with the Mukhtar in the areas where there is no municipality, within a maximum period ending on 31 December of each year, and each municipality or Mukhtar must keep a special register for this purpose in accordance with the specifications determined in the Built Property Tax Law.

- Public administrations, public institutions, and municipalities shall not be required to register the lease contracts of the buildings that they rent, and an official certificate issued by them which they notify to the competent municipal department at the commencement of the lease and upon every modification occurring to the rent value shall suffice.

- Every violation of the provisions of the first paragraph of this Article exposes its perpetrator to a fine equivalent to the value of twice the due registration fee in addition to the principal of this fee.

- If there is a lease contract registered in a previous year and its effect was renewed or extended implicitly or by operation of law, the owner or the operator or the tenant must deposit with the competent municipality a certified true copy of the previous lease contract having affixed to it the legal stamp that was due on the original contract, and its registration shall be carried out in accordance with the rules.

The rental value shall be determined by the method of direct assessment in the following cases:

- The absence of a registered lease contract in the leased buildings.

- The simulation of the registered contract or for doubt as to its authenticity, whether that is with the intent of evading the fee or under the influence of the factor of kinship, friendship, courtesy, or for any other reason.

- The occupancy of the building by the owner.

- The occupancy of the building by a third party, whom the owner permits to do so by way of tolerance without consideration or for a nominal consideration, whether this third party is from among the members of his family or from among strangers to him.

The assessment of the rental value in the cases provided for in Article Seven of this Law shall be carried out by one or more assessment committees formed by the head of the executive authority in the municipality:

1 - In the municipalities of the capitals of governorates and districts and the municipalities subject to the Public Accounting Law:

- A member of the Municipal Council, as President.

- A salaried engineer representing the technical department in the municipality or the Directorate of Urban Planning, as a member.

- An employee delegated by the Ministry of Finance (Directorate of Public Finance), as a member.

- An employee of the municipality, as rapporteur.

2 - In all other municipalities, of:

- A member of the Municipal Council, as President.

- An employee delegated by the Ministry of Finance (Directorate of Public Finance), as a member.

- A local expert in real estate affairs, as a member.

- An employee of the municipality, as rapporteur

- The assessment committee shall conduct an inspection of the built property, make a comparison with similar buildings leased under similar circumstances, and draw up a report setting forth the bases it adopted in the assessment.

- The assessed rental values shall remain adopted for so long as the reasons for the assessment remain in existence.
The assessment may, upon the request of the taxpayer, be reconsidered if an event occurs to the property that causes it to lose part of its value.

The municipality shall have the right to amend the basic or additional assessments pursuant to a roll of supplementary assessment rolls if it becomes apparent that there is a deficiency or concealment in the rental value on the basis of which the assessment was made.

Every advertisement, wherever found, whatever its type, and whatever its nature, essence, and material, shall be subject to the fee on advertisements.

An advertisement shall mean anything used for publicity, attracting the public, and introducing an establishment, commodity, or service, whatever the methods and means adopted.

The fee on advertisements is of two types:

- A licensing fee.

- And an exploitation fee.

Advertisements subject to the fee are divided into four categories:

1 - Permanent advertisements (whether their base is fixed or mobile).

2 - Temporary advertisements within fixed or mobile boards or frames placed outside the advertising establishments or on their facades or at their entrances.

3 - Advertisements displayed in cinemas and moving illuminated advertisements (screen, ticker...) displayed in any place outside cinemas.

Advertisements displayed by cinemas for publicity for themselves or for cinematographic films prepared for showing on their screen are exempted from the fee.

4 - Advertisements displayed on television or broadcast on the radio.

Advertisements of the first and second categories only shall be subject to a prior licence granted by the competent municipality within the municipal area and by the Qaimaqam or the Governor outside the municipal area.

As for advertisements of the third and fourth categories, they shall not be subject to a prior licence.

5% five per cent thereof for public baths, public gardens and parks.

- In all other municipalities, it shall be expended for the execution of works and projects relating to schools, popular housing, public baths, health installations, museums, libraries, public gardens and other projects and works.

A fee for the construction of sewers and sidewalks shall be imposed on the owner applying for a building permit, set at a rate of half per thousand of the sale price of a square metre of the land of the real property for every square metre of the building intended to be erected, and it shall be collected simultaneously with the building permit.

The fee shall be collected at the same rate in respect of existing buildings, upon the completion of the studies relating to the sewer network for the area to which the real property belongs and with the exception of buildings that have previously been subjected to this fee.

The assessment of the sale price of a square metre of the land of the real property shall be undertaken by the committee provided for in Article 77 of this Law on the basis of the sale price of the land of the real property at the date of completion of the studies.

A fee for the maintenance of sewers and sidewalks shall be imposed on the occupant of the building whatever his capacity (owner, tenant, operator... etc.), collected annually together with the fee on the rental value, at a rate of (1,50) one and a half per cent of the rental value adopted for the imposition of the fee on the rental value.

The United Nations Organization, its branches, and the agencies emanating therefrom shall be exempted from the fees for the construction and maintenance of sewers and sidewalks.

The following shall also be exempted:

1- - Buildings occupied by the State from the date of their occupation until 31/12/2030, and fees previously paid shall not be refunded

2 Buildings occupied by public institutions from the date of their occupation and until 31/12/2022, and fees previously paid shall not be refunded

The municipality shall collect a lump-sum fee of (2000 L.L.) two thousand Lebanese pounds in each of the following cases:

1 - Issuing a statement of an alignment plan for each real property.

2 - Issuing a statement of levels (benchmarks) for each real property.

3 - Issuing a statement of watercourses and easement zones, or either of them, for each real property.

4 - In return for examining each subdivision application.

5 - All other certificates and statements of a technical nature.
The United Nations Organization, its branches, and the agencies emanating therefrom shall be exempted from the fee on technical statements and studies.
The compensation arising from betterment shall be collected in accordance with the Laws on Expropriation and on the Betterment Tax.
The United Nations Organization, its branches, and the agencies emanating therefrom shall be exempted from the compensation arising from betterment.

Mezzanines newly constructed in existing buildings or those intended to be built over part or all of the area of shops, warehouses and offices shall be subject to one quarter of the building permit fee, provided that such mezzanines are within these premises and ancillary thereto and are accessed only from inside them.

Staircases leading to such mezzanines shall be exempted from the said fee.

The following renovation and restoration works shall not be subject to the building permit fee:

- Changing the tiles and the sanitary and electrical installations and fittings.

- Changing the paper, whitewashing, painting and plastering/cladding.

The following shall be subject to a lump-sum permit fee of (10000) ten thousand Lebanese pounds:

- Every restoration or repair that does not result in the erection of an iron structure (load-bearing walls and ceilings or columns and ceiling beams).

- The erection of boundary walls.

Buildings that benefit from exemption from the rental value fee, as well as construction works resulting from alignment pursuant to the provisions of the Expropriation Law, shall be exempted from the fee and from the surcharges attached thereto.

For the purpose of levying the building permit fee, the assessment of the sale price per square metre of the land of the real property on which a building is intended to be erected or added shall be undertaken by a special committee formed by a decision of the head of the executive authority in the municipality, composed of:

- A member of the municipal council, as Chairman.

- An engineer from the municipality or an engineer from the Directorate General of Urban Planning delegated by the Qaemقام (District Commissioner) or the Mohafez (Governor), as a Member.

- An employee from the Ministry of Interior delegated by the Minister of Interior upon a proposal after consulting the Head of the Department of Municipal and Rural Affairs, as a Member.

In areas located outside the municipal boundaries, the committee shall be formed by the Mohafez (Governor) as follows:

- The Qaemقام (District Commissioner) or a Category Three employee in the Qaemقامiya or the Governorate, as Chairman.

- An engineer from the Directorate General of Urban Planning, as a Member.

- An expert in real estate affairs, as a Member.

These committees, each within its respective competence and notwithstanding the provisions of Article 13 of Legislative Decree No. 13/83 dated 25/02/1983 and its amendments, shall undertake the task of assessment when applying the laws on the settlement of building violations, including the assessment of the notional land value.

A special fee of 2% two percent of the assessed rental value of the premises in which the said substances are placed, whatever the purpose of placing them (manufacturing, processing, storage, leasing, and others...), shall be imposed on establishments and individuals engaged in the trade of explosive or inflammable substances. This fee shall be collected annually for the benefit of the competent municipality within the municipal area, and shall be collected for the account of the Independent Municipal Fund outside the municipal area, and if the period of operation is less than one year, it shall be imposed on a monthly basis at a rate of (1/12) one-twelfth of the value of the fee for each month, and a fraction of a month shall be counted as a full month.
The State shall impose and collect for the account of all municipalities the fees and surcharges set forth in the following articles:

A surcharge for the account of the municipality within whose area the buildings are located shall be added to the proportional built property tax at a rate of (3%) three percent of the net revenues subject to the tax.

And a surcharge for the account of all municipalities shall be added to the progressive built property tax at a rate of (10%) ten percent of the principal of the tax. The same surcharges shall be collected outside the municipal area, provided that their proceeds are spent on the development of villages that have no municipalities.
A surcharge for the account of all municipalities at a rate of (15%) fifteen percent of the tax shall be added to the tax on the profits of commercial, industrial, and non-commercial professions.
A surcharge for the account of all municipalities at a rate of (10%) ten percent of the duty shall be added to the transfer duty on estates, wills, and gifts.
A surcharge for the account of all municipalities at a rate of (5%) five percent of the fees shall be added to the real estate registration fees of all kinds.

Notwithstanding any other text, the fees on liquid fuels shall be determined as percentages of the price of the goods delivered ex-refinery or ex-depots, as shown in the official schedule of the composition of liquid fuel prices officially established, as follows:

* Petrol: - A fiscal fee for the State Treasury of 12 per cent.

- A municipal fee for the account of all municipalities of 4 per cent.

- A special fee for the account of the Independent Fuels Fund of 1 per cent.

- A reconstruction fee of 1 per cent.

Total: 18 per cent.

* Kerosene for domestic consumption:

* Aviation kerosene:

* Gasoil (gas oil):

- A fiscal fee for the State Treasury of 6 per cent.

- A municipal fee for the account of all municipalities of 2 per cent.

- A special fee for the account of the Independent Fuels Fund of 0.50 per cent.

- A reconstruction fee of 0.50 per cent.

Total: 9 per cent.

* Fuel oil:

- A fiscal fee for the State Treasury of 2 per cent.

- A municipal fee for the account of all municipalities of 1 per cent.

- A special fee for the account of the Independent Fuels Fund of 0.50 per cent.

- A reconstruction fee of 0.50 per cent.

Total: 4 per cent.

The Customs Administration shall collect, for the account of all municipalities, on goods imported by sea, land and air, a port fee of (3.50%) three and a half per cent of the value of those goods.

Diplomatic and consular missions shall be exempted from the port fee, subject to reciprocity, and goods of Arab origin imported by land shall be exempted from the port fee within the conditions specified in the bilateral and multilateral trade agreements concluded therewith regarding exemption from or reduction of customs duties.

Where necessary, the conditions of the exemption provided for in this Law shall be determined by a joint decision issued by the Ministry of Public Works and Transport, the Ministry of the Interior, and the Ministry of Finance.

There shall be imposed on the premiums of insurance contracts, with the exception of life insurance contracts and reinsurance contracts, a fee collected for the account of all municipalities at the rate of (6%) six per cent of the full value of the premiums of the contract and its addenda.

Insurance companies shall undertake the collection of these fees and shall pay the proceeds thereof at the end of every six months, and within the fifteen days following them, to the State Treasury for the account of the Independent Municipal Fund, accompanied by a detailed statement of the remainder of the premiums, and there shall be imposed on anyone who delays in paying the fee in cash to the Treasury fund beyond the specified time limit a fine equivalent to double the aforementioned fee for each month of delay, a fraction of a month being considered a month, up to tenfold.

A surcharge in the amount of (25%) twenty-five per cent for the account of all municipalities shall be added to the registration fees of cars, motor vehicles and motorcycles of all kinds and of all categories.

The Customs Administration shall levy for the account of all municipalities, in addition to the port fee provided for in Article 92 of this Law, a surcharge at the rate of (1.50%) one and a half per cent of the value of the following goods:

- Beer (ale) of its various kinds and forms.

- Wine of its various kinds and forms.

- Spirits (eaux-de-vie), sweetened and aromatised alcoholic beverages, other spirits.

- Compound alcoholic preparations for the manufacture of spirits, whatever their alcoholic strength.

- Alcohol, whether denatured or undenatured.

- Mineral waters, lemonade, aromatised aerated waters and other non-alcoholic beverages of all kinds.

- Meat and fish in their various forms, whether fresh, salted, smoked or otherwise preserved, including crustaceans, molluscs and others without exception.

With effect from the date of entry into force of this Law, the municipal fees imposed pursuant to Articles 96, 97 and 98 of Law No. 60/88 dated 12/08/1988 on water, electricity and wired and wireless telecommunications services are repealed, and the concerned administrations and institutions shall undertake to impose the tax on the subscribers to these services and collect it in accordance with the rules specified in the Law, for the benefit of the municipality within the scope of which the subscription to these services falls, provided that the proceeds of the tax are remitted once every three months to each concerned municipality, in proportion to its share of the value of the collected subscriptions, or to the Independent Municipal Fund in respect of the services the subscription to which falls outside the municipal scope. These administrations shall be entitled to deduct from the value of the tax due on the water, electricity and wired and wireless telecommunications services that they provide, the value of the tax paid on their purchases which they acquired in order to carry on their activity. With respect to persons who provide telecommunications, water and electricity services to the public pursuant to agreements signed with the State, they shall impose the tax on these services in accordance with the provisions of the Law, and remit it to the administration or department competent for these services after deducting the value of the tax paid on their purchases which they acquired in order to carry on their activity. Each of the persons mentioned in this Article shall submit a special declaration to the tax administration showing therein the value of the tax due for the benefit of the municipality and the value of the tax paid on his purchases for each tax period.

As of the effective date of this Law, the municipal fees imposed pursuant to Articles 96, 97 and 98 of Law No. 60/88 dated 12/08/1988 on water, electricity, and wired and wireless telecommunications services shall be repealed, and the administrations and institutions concerned shall undertake to impose the tax on the subscribers to these services and collect it in accordance with the rules specified in the Law, for the benefit of the municipality within the limits of which the subscription to these services falls, provided that the proceeds of the tax are remitted once every three months to each municipality concerned, in proportion to its share of the value of the collected subscriptions, or to the Independent Municipal Fund in respect of the services the subscription to which falls outside the municipal scope. These administrations shall have the right to deduct from the value of the tax due on the water, electricity, and wired and wireless telecommunications services that they provide, the value of the tax paid on their purchases that they acquired in order to carry out their activity. With respect to persons who provide telecommunications, water and electricity services to the public pursuant to agreements signed with the State, they shall impose the tax on these services in accordance with the provisions of the Law, and remit it to the administration or department competent for these services after deducting the value of the tax paid on their purchases that they acquired in order to carry out their activity. Every person among the persons mentioned in this Article shall submit a special declaration to the tax administration showing therein the value of the tax due for the benefit of the municipality and the value of the tax paid on his purchases for each tax period.

As of the effective date of this Law, the municipal fees imposed pursuant to Articles 96, 97 and 98 of Law No. 60/88 dated 12/08/1988 on water, electricity and wired and wireless telecommunications services are hereby repealed, and the administrations and institutions concerned shall undertake to impose the tax on the subscribers to these services and collect it in accordance with the procedures specified in the Law, for the benefit of the municipality within the framework of which the subscription to these services is located, provided that the proceeds of the tax are remitted once every three months to each municipality concerned, in proportion to its share of the value of the collected subscriptions, or to the Independent Municipal Fund in respect of the services the subscription to which is located outside the municipal scope. These administrations shall have the right to deduct from the value of the tax due on the water, electricity and wired and wireless telecommunications services that they provide, the value of the tax paid on their purchases which they acquired for the purpose of carrying out their activity. With respect to persons who provide telecommunications, water and electricity services to the public pursuant to agreements signed with the State, they shall impose the tax on these services in accordance with the provisions of the Law, and remit it to the administration or department competent for these services after deducting the value of the tax paid on their purchases which they acquired for the purpose of carrying out their activity. Every one of the persons mentioned in this Article shall submit a special declaration to the tax administration showing therein the value of the tax due for the benefit of the municipality and the value of the tax paid on his purchases for each tax period.

There shall be imposed on tobacco, tombac and cigars prepared for domestic consumption, whether manufactured locally or imported, a surtax for the account of all municipalities at the rate of five per cent of the value of each packet of cigarettes or cigars or package of shredded tobacco or tombac.

The Regie Libanaise des Tabacs et Tombacs (Tobacco and Tombac Monopoly Administration) shall undertake to collect the said surtaxes directly and shall remit the proceeds thereof once every three months to the Independent Municipal Fund.

The Municipal Council shall determine the fees the amounts of which have not been determined and for which this Law has prescribed maximum and minimum limits, provided that the Council establishes in advance a regulation containing the concise rules and criteria for that determination.

For the purpose of determining the amounts of the fees on tourism establishments, the Municipal Council shall adopt the bases relied upon by the Ministry of Tourism.

Fees and fines that are collected once shall be imposed pursuant to collection orders issued by the head of the competent unit, and fees that are collected annually shall be imposed pursuant to assessment rolls prepared by the competent unit and approved by the head of the executive authority in the municipality or whomsoever he delegates.
The basic assessment rolls shall be drawn up annually on the basis of the tax base of the fee, its amount, and its nature as they stood on 31 December of the preceding year.

Any omission or deficiency in the assessments may be rectified pursuant to additional or supplementary assessment rolls up to the end of the fourth year following the year in which the assessment should have taken place.

The collection of fees shall take place on the basis of assessment rolls or collection orders. The notice of placing the basic assessment rolls into collection shall be published in the Official Gazette and in at least two daily newspapers, and shall be broadcast by radio twice consecutively, provided that it then includes the date of publication in the Official Gazette. Publication in two daily newspapers and broadcasting may be dispensed with in respect of municipalities not subject to the Public Accounting Law, and replaced by posting a notice on the door of the municipality headquarters and on boards designated for this purpose within the municipal boundaries.

The objection of the taxpayer to the amounts imposed upon him or to the enforcement measures shall not stay the collection, whether the authority to which the objection is submitted is administrative or judicial.

In principle, the fee shall be paid in a single lump sum within two months:

1 - From the date of the notice in the Official Gazette of placing the basic assessment rolls into collection.

2 - From the date of serving the additional or supplementary assessment upon the taxpayer in person.

The two-month time limit fixed for the payment of the fee shall commence on the day following the publication of the notice in the Official Gazette or the date of service of the additional or supplementary assessment, and shall expire upon the end of official working hours on the day whose date corresponds to the date of commencement of the time limit, regardless of the number of days in each month.

If the said time limit expires on a holiday, it shall be extended ipso jure to the first working day following it.

In special cases the assessment of which is left to the head of the executive authority in the municipality, the amounts imposed in accordance with the rules may be paid in instalments, provided that the legal measures are taken that prevent their inclusion, wholly or partially, by the factor of prescription. The amounts paid in instalments shall become due for payment in the following cases:

1 - If the taxpayer delays in paying one of the instalments on its due date.

2 - Upon the compulsory or voluntary sale of the taxpayer's property.

3 - Upon the bankruptcy of the taxpayer or the judicial liquidation of his property.

Amounts that have not been paid by the expiry of the period specified in Article 107 of this Law shall have added to them a fine of two per cent for each month of delay, provided that a fraction of a month shall be deemed a full month. The fine for delay shall accrue on the unpaid value of the fee, and this fine shall not be deemed an accessory of the fee on which a new fine for delay accrues.

Fines for delay accrued pursuant to Article 109 of the Municipal Fees Law No. 60/88 imposed up to 31/12/2003 shall be reduced by a rate of ninety per cent, and unpaid fees pertaining to previous years, including the reduced fines, shall be paid in instalments over a period of three years in equal quarterly instalments. (Pursuant to Law 583 dated 23/4/2004).

Fees shall be collected within the municipal boundary and shall be remitted to the Treasury fund outside the municipal boundary. The collection zones for collectors shall be determined by a decision of the head of the executive authority in the municipality. Municipalities may decide to contract out the collection of the slaughter fee, and the contracting out shall be conducted by way of public auction.

Fees shall be paid either in cash or by postal money order or bank cheque. In determining the date of payment, the date shown on the collector's receipt, the cash office receipt, or the postal money order shall be relied upon.

And if payment is made by way of a bank cheque, or any other banking means of payment, the date of delivery or deposit in registered mail shall be relied upon with respect to the cheque, and the date of notification of the competent accountant with respect to other means of payment.

The competent accountant shall address a general formal notice to the taxpayers who fail to pay the fee imposed pursuant to the basic assessment rolls until after the expiry of the period provided for in Article 107 of this Law.

This formal notice shall be published in two daily newspapers and on the radio twice consecutively within ten days, calling upon those in default of payment to pay what is owed by them within 15 days from the date of publication of the first formal notice.

Publication in two daily newspapers and on the radio may be dispensed with in respect of municipalities not subject to the Public Accounting Law and replaced by posting a notice on the door of the municipal headquarters and on boards designated for this purpose within the municipal area.

Copies of the formal notice shall be affixed, where necessary, in the office of the competent accountant, or on the door of the municipal hall and in places of public gatherings in cities and in public squares in villages.

As for taxpayers pursuant to an additional or supplementary assessment roll who fail to pay the fee until after the expiry of the period provided for in Article 107 of this Law, the accountant shall address to each of them a personal formal notice with an acknowledgment of receipt calling upon him to pay the fee within a period of 15 days from the date of their notification of the formal notice.

The personal formal notice may be replaced by a general formal notice decided by the municipal council stating explicitly that it stands in place of the personal formal notice, and in the event that the taxpayer or his agent refuses to receive the formal notice and in the event of his absence, this formal notice shall be affixed on the door of the taxpayer's place of residence or his place of business and in the offices of the competent accountants, and these measures shall be deemed to constitute legal notification.

If the taxpayer fails to pay, after the expiry of the time limit of the general or personal formal notice, the amounts due, the competent accountant shall proceed:

- Either to attach his movable and immovable property and sell it by public auction.

- Or to close his place of business, if he does not own movable or immovable property which, if attached and sold, could cover the amounts owed by him.

In levying attachment on the property of the taxpayer or the property inherited from him, the following order shall be followed:

1 - Attachment of debts owed to the taxpayer by a third party in the hands of such third party.

2 - Attachment of movable property.

3 - Attachment of immovable property.

If the attachment covers movable property, the accountant or whoever he delegates from among the collectors or pursuing agents subordinate to him shall undertake its execution with the assistance of the competent mukhtar and the security forces where necessary upon assignment by the administrative authority. The attached items shall be kept in the places designated by the accountant.

And if the attachment covers immovable property, the competent accountant shall notify this attachment to the Land Registry Departments in order to place an annotation of the attachment on such property.

In the event of the attachment of monetary funds in the hands of a third party, such as rents of real properties, wages of employees, or other funds due or becoming due to the person whose property is attached, the amounts which the third party claims to have paid prior to the dates appointed therefor shall not be taken into consideration unless the payment is established by an officially authenticated instrument or supported by a certain date.

The competent accountant shall designate the order of sale of the attached property such that the property of which the deprivation is least harmful to the taxpayer shall be sold first. The sale of movable property shall be announced within a period of two weeks starting from the date of levying the attachment.

Movable property, or immovable property, shall be sold by public auction pursuant to a book of conditions approved by the chairman of the sales committee if the property decided to be sold is movable, and by the Qaemaqam or the Governor if it is immovable.

The sale shall be undertaken by a committee appointed the decision by the Qaemaqam or the Governor.

The following information shall be set out in the book of conditions:

- The types of property placed in the auction, their specifications, and their location.

- The appraised value of the said property and the minimum price that must be taken as a basis for the auction, provided that it is equivalent to two thirds of the appraised value.

- The amount of the guarantee that enables participation in the auction and its conditions.

- The conditions of payment.

- Other information the conditions required by the auction.

The auction shall be announced in at least two daily newspapers, at least 15 days prior to the date fixed for the auction, and a copy of the announcement shall be posted on designated boards in the office of the competent accountant and in meeting places and public squares.

The following shall be mentioned in the announcement:

- The subject of the auction.

- The place of conducting the auction and its time.

- The place where the book of conditions may be inspected.

- The appraised value of the property placed in the auction and the minimum price.

- The date of conducting the second auction after the provisional award.

- Other information required by the auction.
The sales committee shall determine the appraised value of the property placed in the auction.

Presidents and members of municipal councils, and employees of the State, municipalities, and public institutions in the capitals of the governorates in which the property put up for auction is originally located, and in the centres in which the auction is conducted, are prohibited from participating therein directly or through an intermediary; the sale shall be deemed null and void in such case, and the offending employee shall be referred to the Disciplinary Council.

The person subject to seizure whose property has been put up for sale shall have the right to request the cancellation of the auction, provided that he pays in full the amounts due from him before the time scheduled for the opening of the auction session.
The auction shall be conducted publicly at the place and time designated therefor.

The auction shall be finally awarded, with respect to movable property, to the person who submits the best prices, following the approval of the Sales Committee. As for immovable property, its sale shall take place in two stages:

- The First Stage: An auction session shall be held therein in which the provisional award is made to the person who submitted the best prices.

- The Second Stage: An auction session shall be held therein ten days after the date of the provisional award session, in which new bids are accepted, and the definitive award shall then be made to the person who submitted the best prices.

The definitive award shall not become final with respect to immovable property except after the endorsement of the minutes of the auction by the Qaimaqam or the Governor.

If the bidder to whom the definitive award was made abstains from fulfilling his undertaking, the guarantee submitted by him shall be confiscated, and another auction shall be conducted. If the best price submitted in the second auction equals or exceeds the price at which the first auction was awarded, the confiscated guarantee shall be recorded as revenue in the budget after the expenses of the second auction are deducted therefrom.

If the best of the prices submitted in the second auction is less than the price at which the first auction was awarded, the guarantee shall be used successively to cover the expenses of the second auction and the difference between the two prices, and if the value of the guarantee exceeds the expenses and the difference, the remainder thereof shall be recorded as revenue for the municipality or for the account of the Independent Municipal Fund outside the municipal perimeter.
The Sales Committee shall continue selling the property of the person subject to seizure until the sale becomes sufficient to settle the amounts payable by him.

If the proceeds of the sale exceed the value of the amounts payable by the taxpayer, the balance shall be placed in trust in his name at the bank, and if the proceeds of the sale fall short of the value of the amounts payable, the taxpayer shall be pursued for the difference.
The taxpayer shall bear all the expenses of seizure, publication, and auction, and these expenses shall be deducted from the proceeds of the sale before the settlement of the amounts due.

If a real property is put up for sale and no bidders come forward at the appraised price, it shall be put up a second time within a period ranging between 30 and 45 days after reducing the appraised price by ten per cent, and if the second auction yields no result, it shall be put up a third time under the same conditions, and if the final auction yields no result, the ownership of the real property shall be transferred to the name of the competent municipality or the Independent Municipal Fund at the price of the final offering, and the Land Registry Departments shall be notified of the matter to take the necessary action within one week at most.

In the event that the ownership of the real property is transferred to the name of the competent municipality or the Independent Municipal Fund, an appropriation in the amount of its price shall be opened in the budget to settle the amounts due, and any surplus over these amounts shall, where applicable, be paid to the owner of the real property.

Real properties the ownership of which has been transferred in the aforementioned manner may not be sold before the lapse of one year from the date of their registration in the Land Register, and in such case the owner of the registered real property shall have the right to redeem it within one year from the date of its registration, provided that:

1 - He pays in full the fees due from him and the surcharges attached thereto, as well as the fines and expenses of all kinds, together with interest calculated at the rate of (9%) nine per cent per annum on the total of these amounts.

2 - He pays the fees accrued on the real property for the period during which it was registered in the name of the municipality or the Independent Municipal Fund.

3 - He also pays the amounts that have been expended on the real property during the aforementioned period for its maintenance and improvement, together with interest calculated at the rate of (9%) nine per cent per annum on the total of these amounts.

The competent municipality or the Independent Municipal Fund shall return to the owner of the real property the yield from which it may have benefited during the period in which it was registered in its name.

The municipality shall enjoy a first-rank privilege, after the State, over all the movable and immovable property of the taxpayer in recovery of the amounts accrued against him, and this privilege shall be exempted from registration in the Land Register with respect to real properties.

The representatives of natural and legal persons subject to the fees shall be liable for the payment thereof in that capacity and for as long as they retain such capacity.

Such persons shall have the right of recourse against the original taxpayer for the amounts they have paid on his behalf and to benefit from the privilege enjoyed by the municipal treasury.
In the event of the death of the taxpayer, his heirs shall be pursued for the fees that were due from him within the limits of the law.

The objection must include:

1 - The given name, surname, address and place of residence of the objector.

2 - The type and amount of the assessment objected to.

3 - The subject-matter of the objection and the grounds thereof.

4 - A statement of the documents and supporting instruments attached to the objection.
The rules provided for in the Code of Civil Procedure shall be applied for the computation of the time limits for objections.

The competent authority to which the objection is submitted shall examine it and may conduct all required investigations, seek clarification regarding anything it deems necessary to be clarified and require the objector to produce such documents and supporting instruments as it deems necessary.

The said authority shall decide upon the objection within a maximum time limit of:

- One month where the objection concerns a material error relating exclusively to the recording of figures or names, the performance of arithmetic operations, a duplicate assessment, or an assessment that is not originally due by reason of cessation, exemption or any other reason.

- Three months in other cases.

The running of the time limits provided for in the preceding Article shall be suspended when the objector is requested to submit clarifications or to produce documents or supporting instruments, until the submission thereof.
Where the time limits provided for in the preceding Articles expire, the objection must be referred without delay to the competent Objections Committee accompanied by a reasoned opinion.

The competent authority to which the objection is submitted shall refer the objection to the competent Objections Committee accompanied by its reasoned opinion if it finds it inadmissible in form or not unfounded on the merits; whereas if it finds it well-founded in whole or in part, it shall grant the objector his rightful claims. In all cases, the said authority shall notify the objector of the outcome of his objection within the fifteen days following the date on which the decision is taken.

An objector whose claims have been granted in part shall be entitled to request, within a time limit of one month from the date on which he is notified of the decision, that the case be referred to the Objections Committee for reconsideration.

In the event of the bankruptcy of the taxpayer and for the purpose of pursuing the collection of the fees due from him, the municipality shall be represented by its accountant, and outside the municipal scope by the head of the competent administrative unit for municipal and rural affairs at the Ministry of the Interior, and documents shall be served upon them directly.

The Independent Municipal Fund shall be represented by the head of the competent administrative unit.

The taxpayer shall not be entitled to request a set-off between the fees due from him and the debts payable to him by the municipality. The competent accountant may request the payment authorising officer to deduct the fees due from the taxpayer from the debts payable to him by the municipality.
In municipalities that do not have the position of accountant, the head of the executive authority or the person delegated by him shall undertake the duties of the accountant.
Every taxpayer shall be entitled to object to any assessment of the fees and surcharges provided for in this Law if he finds therein an error, unfairness, or violation.

The objection shall be submitted within the following time limits:

1 - For fees imposed pursuant to basic assessment rolls: within a time limit of two months from the date of the announcement in the Official Gazette that the rolls have been placed into collection.

2 - Fees imposed pursuant to additional or supplementary assessment rolls, or by collection orders, or by any other means, within a time limit of one month from the date on which the taxpayer is served in person or at his place of residence with the notice relating to the fees.

The time limit for objection shall be extended until 31 December of the third year following the year in which the assessment took place if the objection concerns a material error relating exclusively to the recording of figures or names, the performance of arithmetical operations, double assessment, or an undue assessment. The administration shall be entitled to revoke the said material error within the same time limit without the need to refer to the Objections Committee.

Objections shall be submitted directly or by registered mail to the competent municipality, or to the competent Qaemaqam or Governor if the fee or surcharge is imposed for the account of all municipalities outside the municipal scope.

- The objection shall be deemed submitted:

- On the date of its registration.

- On the date of its deposit with the post if sent by registered mail.
The objection shall be submitted in the form of a petition signed by the concerned taxpayer or by his legal representative.

One or more committees in each governorate, formed by decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice, Finance and the Interior, shall examine and decide upon the objection as follows:

- A judge as chairman.

- A chief tax controller from the Ministry of Finance as member.

- An employee from the Ministry of the Interior of the third category at least as member.

One of the employees of the fourth category at least shall perform the function of rapporteur.

When examining objections in each municipality, an advisory member representing this municipality, delegated by the head of the executive authority therein, shall join the committee. The decree appointing the committee shall include the determination of the allowances due to each of the chairman, the members and the rapporteur, and they shall be disbursed from the budget of the Ministry of the Interior.
The committee shall meet upon the invitation of its chairman, and its sessions shall not be lawful unless attended by the chairman and the members.

The rapporteur must present the file of the objection to the committee accompanied by a report in which he sets out exclusively the facts of the case, the points of dispute and the opinion of the competent authority to which the objection was submitted.

The committee may summon the objector to its sessions, and it may also summon any other person whom it deems necessary to hear and seek clarification from, and the objector may be assisted by a lawyer or a person of expertise.

The objector shall be notified of all summonses, notices, correspondence, decisions and others through administrative channels, and if that is not possible, by sending them to him at his place of residence by registered mail with acknowledgment of receipt.

- However, if the objector has left his place of residence recorded in his objection without informing the authority to which the objection was submitted of his new place of residence, notification shall take place by affixing to the notice board at the headquarters of the said authority and on the door of his previous place of residence mentioned in the objection.

- An objector who has refused notification shall be deemed to have been duly notified.

- The same provisions shall apply to the heirs in the event of the death of the objector.

If the objector fails to attend the sessions of the committee despite being summoned thereto, and if he fails to submit the information he is requested to submit or to produce the documents and instruments he is ordered to produce, the committee shall deem him in default and decide upon the objection in the light of the contents of the file.
The objector may not contest before the committee claims other than those which he set out in his objection.
The committee shall be bound by the secrecy of deliberations.
The Committee may not award amounts exceeding the amounts objected to.

The Committee shall decide upon the objection within a period of six months from the date on which the file is received by it, and it may not exceed this period save by reasoned decisions and for serious causes.

The Committee shall take its decisions unanimously or by majority, without the rapporteur having the right to participate in the deliberations, and its decisions shall be reasoned.

The rapporteur shall notify the decisions of the Committee within a period of fifteen days from the date on which they are taken to the competent authority (municipality, Qa'im Maqam, Governor) through the usual administrative channels and to the objector against a receipt, and if that is not possible, by sending them to him at his place of residence by registered mail with acknowledgment of receipt.

The decisions of the Objection Committees shall not be subject to any avenue of review save recourse before the State Council on the ground of violation of the law. The time limit for filing the recourse shall be fixed at one month starting from the date on which the taxpayer or the municipality is notified of the decision.
