Municipalities shall be entitled to substitute for individuals in carrying out certain works required by municipal regulations or by the exigencies of public health or public safety, if they fail to carry them out despite having been given notice, and they shall thereupon be entitled to collect from them the costs of such works plus an amount equal to (20%) twenty percent thereof, and to pursue the recovery thereof in accordance with the recovery procedures provided for in this Law.

The proceeds of fines imposed by the courts on account of violations of building, traffic, public health, or other municipal regulations shall accrue to the treasury of the municipality within the jurisdiction of which the violation occurs.
Fees which certain municipalities are authorized to collect by virtue of special texts and of which no mention is made in this Law shall remain in force.
Every defaulting or negligent person who delays in remitting the fee or surtax to the municipality concerned or the competent administration shall be prosecuted disciplinarily.

Annual remittances in respect of collected funds shall be granted as follows:

Each municipality shall determine the regulations for granting remittances, which shall be subject to the approval of the Minister of Interior, provided that the bases adopted at the Ministry of Finance are observed therein.

Employees entrusted with assessing the fees for which assessment rolls are drawn up shall be granted a transport allowance determined in accordance with the above-mentioned bases.

Fees, surcharges, and compensations of all kinds shall lapse automatically for taxpayers by operation of prescription on 31 December of the fourth year following the year in which the assessment took place.

Prescription shall be interrupted merely by initiating the individual proceedings provided for in this Law, and a formal notice shall be deemed an initiation of proceedings provided that it is served in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

The five per cent surcharge provided for in paragraph eight of Article three of Law No. 11/64 dated 19/02/1964 (Engineers' Retirement Law) shall not be deducted from the principal of the building permit fee, but shall be calculated on the basis thereof and added thereto.

Legislative Decree No. 68 dated 5 August 1967 (Municipal Fees Law) and its amendments are hereby repealed, as are Legislative Decree No. 28 dated 12/04/1977 and all texts that conflict or are inconsistent with the provisions of this Law. Provided, however, that the rates of fees imposed pursuant to annual assessment rolls, together with their tax bases applied on the basis of these two Legislative Decrees, shall remain in force up to and including the assessments of the year 1988.

The value of the lump-sum fees provided for in the Municipal Fees Law No. 60/88 dated 12/08/1988 and its amendments shall be increased by one fold. (Article 49 of Budget Law No. 107 dated 23/7/1999)
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The Military Court of Cassation shall be constituted:

1- In criminal cases:

Of a judge from the cadre of the judicial judiciary of the seventh grade and above delegated by the First President of the Court of Cassation as President, deputised for where necessary by another judge of the same grade delegated for this purpose by the First President of the Court of Cassation, and of four officer members of the rank of lieutenant colonel and above.

2 - In correctional cases:

Of a judge from the cadre of the judicial judiciary of the seventh grade and above delegated by the First President of the Court of Cassation as President, deputised for where necessary by another judge of the same grade delegated for this purpose by the First President of the Court of Cassation, and of two officer members of the rank of lieutenant colonel and above.

In time of war and on an exceptional basis, the Military Court of Cassation may be presided over in criminal and correctional matters by an officer of the rank of colonel and above, and in this case one of the counsellors therein shall be a judge from the cadre of the judicial judiciary of the seventh grade and above delegated by the First President of the Court of Cassation, deputised for where necessary by another judge of the same grade delegated for this purpose by the First President of the Court of Cassation.

The Military Court shall be composed:

1 - In criminal cases:

Of an officer of the rank of lieutenant colonel and above as President, and of four members, one of whom shall be a judge from the cadre of the judicial judiciary in the thirteenth grade and above and three officers of a rank below the rank of the President.

2 - In correctional cases:

Of an officer whose rank is not less than the rank of lieutenant colonel and above as President, and of two members, one of whom shall be a judge of the thirteenth grade and above, and an officer below the President in rank.

3 - Reserve chambers may, in accordance with the rules set forth above, be constituted from among the judges appointed to the Military Court to hear the cases referred to them.

- The President of the original chamber shall ensure the distribution of cases and business among the various chambers.

The Single Military Judiciary shall be assumed by judges from the cadre of the judicial judiciary.

However, they may be appointed from among officers holding a degree in law of the rank of first lieutenant and above, and if that is not possible, from among those not holding a degree.

The urgent draft law set forth in Decree No. 8682 relating to the Military Judiciary, as amended by the two Committees of Administration and Justice and of National Defence, is hereby ratified.

This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The Military Judiciary shall be composed of:

1- A Military Court of Cassation having its seat in Beirut.

2 - A Permanent Military Court having its seat in Beirut.

3 - Military Single Judges in the governorates, whose seats shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Defence upon the proposal of the Supreme Military Authority.

4 - A Government Commissioner and his assistants.

5 - Investigating Judges.

- The Minister of National Defence shall be vested, in respect of the Military Courts, with all the powers vested in the Minister of Justice in respect of the Judicial Courts in all matters not inconsistent with the provisions of this Law.

The seat of the Military Court of Cassation may be changed by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of National Defence after taking the opinion of the Supreme Military Authority, and the seat of the Permanent Military Court may also be changed by a decision of the Minister of National Defence after taking the opinion of the Supreme Military Authority.

In time of war, temporary military courts special to the Armed Forces may be established by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of National Defence after taking the opinion of the Supreme Military Authority.

This decree shall designate the seat of each of these courts, the scope of its jurisdiction, its composition, and the selection of its judges.
In the provisions of this Law, the term Military Court shall mean the Permanent or Temporary Military Court, unless the text specifically refers to either one of them.

When trying an Army officer, the Military Court of Cassation and the Military Court shall be composed in the manner set forth above, provided that all military judges in each of these two courts are of a higher rank than the defendant officer or at least of his rank.

If it is not possible to compose the court in the manner set forth in the preceding paragraph to try an officer who is still in active service due to the absence of an officer of a higher rank than him or of his rank, or for any other reason, the Minister of Justice, after the approval of the Minister of National Defence and the Supreme Judicial Council, shall have the right to second the necessary number of judges of the ninth grade and above to form the bench of the court.

When trying personnel of the Internal Security Forces or employees of the General Security, the Military Court of Cassation and the Military Court shall be formed in the manner set forth above in equal numbers of Army officers and of officers from the corps of the defendant.

However, if there are several defendants in the case belonging to both of the aforementioned corps together, the two aforementioned courts shall be formed in the manner set forth above, provided that in felony cases each of them shall include an officer from each of the two aforementioned corps and an officer from the Army.

And in misdemeanour cases and other cases, of two officers in the Army including the President, in addition to the seconded judicial judge.
Judicial judges at the military courts shall wear their judicial robes during hearings.

The functions of the Government Commissioner at the Military Court of Cassation shall be performed by the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation or whomever he seconds from among his assistants for this purpose, and he shall have all the powers vested in the Government Commissioner at the Military Court.

The functions of the Government Commissioner at the Military Court shall be performed by a judge of the eleventh grade and above, assisted by one or more judges or one or more officers holding a degree in law, provided that his rank is not lower than the rank of Captain and above; the military personnel among them shall be seconded by the Minister of National Defence for this purpose in accordance with the provisions of Article 14.

The seat of the Office of the Government Commissioner at the military courts shall be at the seats of these courts.

The Government Commissioners at the military courts and their assistants shall be subject to the authority and supervision of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation.

The functions of an Investigating Judge at the Military Court shall be performed by one or more judges of the rank of Investigating Judge in the cadre of the judicial judiciary, or one or more officers holding a degree in law.

The seat of the Military Investigation Department shall be at the seat of the Military Court.

The judicial judges before the military courts shall be appointed from among the judges of the judicial cadre by a decree based upon the proposal of the Ministers of Justice and National Defence and after the accompaniment of the Supreme Judicial Council.

These judges shall remain subject to their regulations and attached to the Ministry of Justice in all that relates to their salaries, their promotion and their discipline, and they may at any time whatsoever be returned to the judicial judiciary in accordance with the rules set forth for their appointment in the preceding paragraph, provided that upon their transfer they must participate in issuing the decision in the actions in which the trial has been closed.

The Minister of National Defence shall appoint at the beginning of each year the officer judges before the Military Judiciary and the officers who substitute for them by a decision based upon the proposal of the Supreme Military Authority in all that relates to the officers belonging to the Army, and upon the proposal of each of the Director General of the Internal Security Forces and the Director General of General Security in all that relates to the officers belonging to the forces of each of them.

This decision may be amended at any time of the year, provided that such may not be done prior to adjudicating the actions in which the trial has been closed. With the exception of the judicial judges attached to the Military Judiciary, the military personnel who are presidents of the military courts and their members shall, during their assumption of the Military Judiciary, be directly subordinate to the Minister of National Defence while remaining subject to the regulations of the corps to which they belong; however, throughout the exercise of their judicial functions and by reason of these functions alone, they may not be referred to an investigation board or to any military court, nor may disciplinary penalties be imposed upon them, save by an order of the Minister of National Defence.

All officers appointed before the Military Judiciary shall take, before the President of the Military Court of Cassation and prior to assuming their duties, the following oath: "I swear by Almighty God to perform my function with all devotion and honesty, to preserve the secrecy of deliberations with absolute care, and to conduct myself in all my acts as an honest and honourable judge."

Clerks of the Military Judiciary shall be appointed:

1- From among the judicial clerks at the Judicial Courts by a decree based on the proposal of the Minister of Justice and the Minister of National Defence after taking the opinion of the Higher Military Authority.

These clerks shall remain subject to their corps and their regulations with respect to their salaries, their promotion and their discipline; however, they shall receive their salaries from the budget of the Ministry of National Defence (the Military Court).

2 - From among Army non-commissioned officers (cadre of Military Judicial Clerks) by a decision of the Higher Military Authority after they have attended training courses and succeeded in the examinations, or from among investigators at the Military Police of the rank of warrant officer and above.

3 - Where it is not possible to appoint non-commissioned officers from the Army to perform these functions, non-commissioned officers from the Internal Security Forces or civilian employees in the Army may be appointed to perform them by a decision of the Minister of National Defence after taking the opinion of the Higher Military Authority with respect to the civilian employees attached to the Army and based on the proposal of the Director General of the Internal Security Forces with respect to the non-commissioned officers of these Forces.

These personnel shall remain subject to the regulations of their corps in everything for which no provision is made in this Law. The cadre of the Military Judicial Clerks and their regulations shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of National Defence based on the proposal of the Higher Military Authority.

4 - All civilian employees at the Military Courts shall be subject to the duties and rights that apply to civilian employees at the Army throughout the period of their presence at the Military Judiciary, provided that they do not conflict with their special regulations.

5 - Subject to the provisions of Article 17, civilian and military employees of the courts shall report:

1 - To the President of the Military Court of Cassation and the Government Commissioner before it, in everything relating to each of them with respect to the employees of this Court and the Public Prosecution attached to it.

2 - To the President of the Permanent Bench of the Military Court with respect to the employees attached to his Court.

3 - To the Government Commissioner before the Military Court with respect to the employees attached to his department and to the investigation departments.

4 - To the Military Single Judges with respect to the employees of the department of each of them; and in addition to what is stated above, and with respect to military discipline, military employees attached to the Military Courts of all grades shall report to the President of the Permanent Bench of the Military Court if their superior is non-military.

Transfers of judicial clerks between the Military Courts shall be effected by a decision of the Minister of National Defence.

Administrative and registry duties at the Military Courts shall be performed by:

1- Before the Military Court of Cassation:

- A Chief Registrar.

2 - Before the Permanent Military Court:

- A Chief Registrar.

Each of them shall be assisted by civilian head clerks and clerks whose number is set out in the schedule annexed to this Law, and they shall also be assisted by military judicial assistants.

3 - Before the Single Judges:

Head clerks and clerks from among the military judicial assistants. Each Military Court shall have:

(a) - A military judicial assistant specifically entrusted with watching over the buildings and keeping the documents and criminal exhibits, who shall be designated as a custodian.

(b) - One or more non-commissioned officers of the Army to perform the function of courier, assistant custodian, bailiff or typist; where necessary, enlisted personnel of the Army or civilian employees may be appointed to these functions, subject to the provisions of paragraph 5 of the preceding Article.

The Chief Registrar of the Military Court of Cassation shall supervise the registry and administrative duties before the said Court and before the Public Prosecution attached thereto, and shall distribute them among his assistants.

The Chief Registrar of the Permanent Military Court shall supervise the registry and administrative duties in all departments of the said Court, including the departments of the Public Prosecution and Investigation, distribute them among his assistants and sign administrative transactions, and he shall also supervise the registries of the Single Military Courts.

Head clerks may be appointed from among military personnel.

In the event that the Chief Registrar of the Military Court of Cassation or the Chief Registrar of the creditor Military Court is appointed from among military personnel, he must hold the rank of officer.

Registry and administrative duties at the Office of the Military Judiciary shall be performed by a Head of Department assisted by a number of military judicial assistants, including a head clerk with the rank of adjutant or chief adjutant, and a number of civilian employees with the Army.
The procedures set forth in the ordinary law regarding the recording of trial proceedings and the keeping of registers shall apply before the Military Courts.

Subject to the provisions of Article 225 of Legislative Decree No. 54 issued on 5 August 1967, the functions of the military judicial police shall be discharged by:

1- The Government Commissioner, his assistants and the investigating judges at the Military Court.

2 - The officers and non-commissioned officers whom the Minister of National Defence appoints for this purpose upon the proposal of the Supreme Military Authority.

3 - The officers of the Army Police, its non-commissioned officers and the heads of its stations.

4 - The Chief Clerk of the Permanent Military Court upon assignment by the Government Commissioner.

- Members of the judicial police, with the exception of the judicial judges among them, shall take the following oath before the Military Court of Cassation:

"I swear by Almighty God that I shall discharge my duty in all honesty and faithfulness and keep the secrecy of the investigation."

All judicial police personnel mentioned above shall be subject to the supervision of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation in accordance with the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

With respect to offences falling within the jurisdiction of the Military Courts, members of the military judicial police shall enjoy the same powers granted to members of the ordinary judicial police.

In the absence of military judicial officers, ordinary judicial officers must pursue flagrant offences only which fall within the jurisdiction of the Military Court.

In all other cases, however, they may not undertake this mission unless requested to do so by the Government Commissioner, the investigating judge, or their assistants.

Members of the military judicial police shall also enjoy the same powers granted to personnel of the Internal Security Forces with regard to drawing up reports of traffic contraventions committed by military personnel, as well as against other persons who are under investigation for other offences falling within the jurisdiction of the military judiciary that are connected to the contravention.

The defence of persons referred before the military judiciary, if they have not chosen an attorney to defend them, shall be entrusted to an attorney or to an officer, and preference among the latter shall be given to whoever holds a degree in law, if the service so permits.

The Supreme Military Authority may enter into agreements with civilian attorneys from the Bar Association to ensure the defence. The officers entrusted with the defence shall be appointed by a decision of the Minister of National Defence upon the proposal of the Supreme Military Authority at the beginning of each year.

This decision may be amended at any time of the year.

If the defendant requests the appointment of one of these officers or attorneys to defend him, his request shall be granted if the requirements of the service do not prevent it.

All judges, officers and lawyers shall receive an allowance for their work before the Military Judiciary.

Where necessary, an allowance may be granted to certain judicial assistants of the Military Judiciary.

The amounts of the aforementioned allowances shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of National Defence upon the proposal of the Supreme Military Authority, and shall be paid from the budget of the Ministry of National Defence (Military Courts).

The jurisdiction of the Permanent Military Court shall extend to all Lebanese territory and foreign territories occupied by the Lebanese Army, with the exception of the areas falling within the jurisdiction of the Provisional Military Courts dedicated to the Armed Forces.

The Military Courts shall have jurisdiction to hear:

1- Offences provided for in Book Three of this Law.

2 - Offences of treason, espionage and unlawful relations with the enemy provided for in Articles 273 to 287 of the Penal Code, in Articles 290 and 291 thereof as well, and in the special laws that punish such offences.

3 - Offences relating to weapons and war ammunition provided for in the Weapons Law, subject to the conditions set forth therein and in this Law.

4 - Offences committed in military camps, establishments and barracks.

5 - Offences committed against the person of a member of the military, with the exception of those committed against the person of a conscript that do not relate to duty

6 - Offences committed against the person of a member of the Internal Security Forces or General Security.

7- Offences committed against civilian employees in the Ministry of National Defence and the Military Courts, or with the Army, the Internal Security Forces and General Security, if such offences are related to duty.

This jurisdiction shall continue after the discharge of the persons mentioned in paragraphs 5-6-7 .

8 - All offences, of whatever kind, that affect the interest of the Army, the Internal Security Forces or General Security.

9 - Offences committed against the person of a member of foreign armies or that affect their interest, unless there is an agreement to the contrary determining jurisdiction between the Lebanese Government and the authority to which such armies belong .

10 - Infractions of the provisions of the Compulsory Military Service Law.

The jurisdiction of the Military Court, of whatever degree, shall be restricted to the public prosecution to the exclusion of the civil claim, and it may decide to return the items seized as corpus delicti to their owners, if the law does not require their confiscation; otherwise, they shall be confiscated for the benefit of the Army.

If the holder of the right to the seized items ordered to be returned to him does not apply for them within a period of five years from the date the final judgment becomes absolute

they shall also be confiscated for the benefit of the Army.

As for trivial items, they shall be destroyed pursuant to a record drawn up through the instrumentality of the Government Commissioner.

The complainant may only be heard by way of information.

The civil claim shall be brought before the competent civil court, and the issuance of judgment therein shall be stayed until the public prosecution is finally decided.

And the injured complainant shall be exempted from the fees of the action.

Where there is a negative or positive conflict of jurisdiction between two military judicial authorities, the competent authority shall be designated by the Military Court of Cassation-its misdemeanour chamber-upon the request of the Government Commissioner.

And if such conflict arises between a military court and an ordinary court, the competent authority shall be designated by the Ordinary Court of Cassation upon the request of the Public Prosecutor before the Court of Cassation.

The rules of procedure set forth in the ordinary law shall apply in the two preceding paragraphs.

There shall be tried before the Military Court, whatever their nationality and whatever the nature of the offence attributed to them:

1 - Military personnel and persons assimilated to military personnel, with the exception of conscripts when they commit offences unrelated to duty.

2 - Personnel of the Internal Security Forces and General Security.

3 - Prisoners of war.

4 - Personnel of the forces of foreign armies and civilian employees therein, unless there is a contrary agreement on jurisdiction in this regard between the Lebanese Government and the authorities to which such foreign armies belong.

5 - Civilian employees of the Ministry of National Defence, the Army, and the Military Courts, or of the Internal Security Forces or General Security, if their offences arise out of duty or fall within the purview of this Law.

6 - Every principal, accomplice, accessory, or instigator in an offence for which one of the persons referred to in the preceding paragraphs is referred before the military judiciary.

Where a person is prosecuted simultaneously for an offence within the jurisdiction of the Military Court and for an offence within the jurisdiction of the ordinary courts, he shall be tried for each offence separately by the competent judiciary.

The court that examines the offence within its jurisdiction after the first court shall decide, where necessary, on the cumulation or merger of sentences.

If the offence is a felony within the jurisdiction of the Military Court, it shall examine, ancillary to the felony, all offences connected therewith.

If the offence is within the jurisdiction of the ordinary judiciary and there is an offence of a weapon of war connected therewith, the ordinary judiciary shall examine both offences together.
The jurisdiction of the Single Judge shall encompass the territory of the governorate to which he is appointed.

Single Judges shall examine the following offences:

1- All contraventions and misdemeanours provided for in the Traffic Law committed within the scope of the governorate by persons whom this Law subjects to the military judiciary.

2 - Other misdemeanours that are within the jurisdiction of the military judiciary, if their penalty does not exceed a fine or imprisonment for up to one year, or both penalties together.

3 - The Supreme Military Authority may, in time of war, refer before the Single Judges:

a - Offences resulting from contraventions of the provisions of civil defence.

b - Misdemeanours and contraventions not covered by the provisions of paragraphs 1 and 2 above, whether having regard to the amount of the penalty or to the identity of the perpetrator, if committed in a territory under a state of emergency or in an area in which martial law has been declared.

In the misdemeanours set forth in paragraph 2 of the preceding Article, the Government Commissioner shall have the right, prior to the convening of the first hearing or at the latest at the commencement of the first hearing, to request by a reasoned decision from the Military Single Judge that he divest himself of the case in order to refer it to another Single Judge or to the Military Court.

The summary procedure set forth in the Code of Criminal Procedure shall apply to all contraventions and to the contraventions and misdemeanours provided for in the Traffic Law, and the ordinary procedure shall apply in cases relating to other offences.

With the exception of contrary provisions contained in this Law, prosecutions, investigations, trials, the rendering of decisions and judgments, and the avenues of recourse against them shall be subject to the Code of Criminal Procedure.

With the exception of the special procedures set forth in this Law, the Government Commissioner and his assistants before the Military Court shall exercise the functions of the Appellate Public Prosecutor, and they shall be charged with prosecuting all offences that are within the jurisdiction of the military judiciary in accordance with the procedures set forth in this Law and in the ordinary law.

Where the institution of a public right action is conditional upon the complainant assuming the capacity of a personal claimant, the Government Commissioner shall have the right to conduct the prosecution on the basis of the complaint of the injured party.

If the injured party is a member of the military or of the personnel of the Internal Security Forces or of General Security, the Higher Army Command or the Directorate General of the Internal Security Forces or the Directorate General of General Security may request the prosecution of the public right action even if the injured party has not submitted a complaint or an information, and it may request the continuation of the prosecution even if the injured party has withdrawn his action.

Actions arising from offences affecting the family shall be exempted from the provisions of the aforementioned paragraph.

The Government Commissioner shall receive complaints and informations relating to offences that fall within the jurisdiction of the military judiciary unless they relate:

1 - To offences committed by a member of the Army against one of its personnel.

2 - To offences relating to a member of the Army without any civilian having any involvement therein.

3 - To offences relating to a member of the Army proposed during service or by reason thereof and in which a civilian had an involvement.

4 - To offences relating to a member of the Army provided for in Title II of Book III of this Law.

5 - With respect to offences that fall within the competence of the military judiciary and are committed by personnel of the Internal Security Forces or General Security, the Government Commissioner shall prosecute the personnel of these forces for these offences after seeking the opinion of the Director General of the Internal Security Forces or the Director General of General Security, and if either of them does not agree, in what concerns him, to the prosecution, the Government Commissioner shall refer the matter to the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation to decide upon ordering the prosecution or not.

In the cases provided for in paragraphs 1, 2, 3 and 4, all papers shall be submitted directly to the Higher Army Command, and this Command must we decide upon the prosecution and send the file to the Government Commissioner. The Government Commissioner must be notified immediately of every offence that occurs in the cases set forth in item 3 of this Article.

Where it appears to the Investigating Judge that the act attributed to the defendant constitutes a misdemeanour or a felony, he shall issue a committal order or an indictment and refer the action to the Government Commissioner together with an arrest warrant against the person accused of the felony.

The Government Commissioner shall refer the action to the authority competent to adjudicate thereon in accordance with the provisions of the following Chapter.

The decision of the Investigating Judge concerning release shall be subject to appeal before the Military Court of Cassation, which shall rule on the matter within twenty-four hours.

The time limit for appeal in this case shall be twenty-four hours for the Government Commissioner and the defendant alike, commencing from the date of notification. The detainee shall remain in detention until the appeal is adjudicated.

The decisions of the Investigating Judge issued pursuant to Article 43 shall be subject to cassation by the Government Commissioners within the time limits and in accordance with the procedures prescribed in the Chapter on Cassation.

The competent military authorities shall be notified of an abstract of all final decisions issued by the Investigating Judges.

Where the defendant is one of the military personnel, persons assimilated to military personnel, or civilian employees subject pursuant to this Law to the military judiciary, and has committed his offence during the performance of duty, on the occasion thereof, or by reason thereof, his superior shall attach to the file:

1 - A detailed report on the circumstances of the incident.

2 - A statement of the services of the defendant and his personal record.

3 - A list of the penal sentences and disciplinary penalties to which he has been sentenced.

The following procedures shall be followed in the two cases of default and desertion:

A - In the case of default:

The report set forth above shall be drawn up by the officer heading the Conscription Department, and he shall attach thereto:

1 - A copy of the conscription order.

2 - A copy of the travel order and of the instrument of notification thereof.

3 - A copy of the documents proving that the defaulting person did not arrive at the appointed time at the place designated for him.

4 - A statement on the circumstances of the incident.

5 - A list of physical descriptions.

B - In the case of desertion:

The report shall be drawn up by the commander of the detachment or unit to which the deserter belongs, and the following documents shall be attached thereto:

1 - A schedule of the weapons, effects, military articles, and animals which are the property of the State and which the deserter took, with an indication, where applicable, of what has been returned thereof.

2 - The investigation records drawn up after the declaration of desertion.

3 - The record proving the return of the deserter or his arrest.

4 - The records of the interrogation of the deserter upon his return or detention, and the statements of the witnesses.

With the exception of the offences mentioned in items 1, 2 and 4 of the preceding Article and in the third item of the preceding Article in the event that they are committed by members of the Army during operations, the Government Commissioner shall have the right, in flagrant offences, to take cognisance of the action directly regardless of who the perpetrators and the victims may be, to prosecute these offences and to refer the case to the competent judiciary without obtaining any prior or subsequent authorisation for prosecution, notifying the authorities to which the prosecuted person belongs as soon as possible of all cases of which he has taken cognisance in this manner, and also serving upon them a copy of all warrants, decisions, final judgments and recourses to avenues of review relating to the persons belonging to them.
The Government Commissioner shall have the right to supervise and inspect the departments of the Military Single Judges.
The provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure shall apply before the Military Investigator.
The Military Investigating Judge may, after seeking the opinion of the Government Commissioner, release the defendant in accordance with the procedures prescribed in the Code of Criminal Procedure.
Upon the conclusion of the investigation, the Investigating Judge shall transmit the action to the Government Commissioner to submit his written submissions within three days.

If the Investigating Judge finds that the military judiciary has no jurisdiction to hear the action, he shall decide to transmit it to the Government Commissioner.

The judicial warrants issued shall be recalled and the defendant shall be placed at the disposal of the Government Commissioner to be sent immediately with the file to the competent authority, unless he sees fit to appeal against the decision of lack of jurisdiction. The acts of prosecution and investigation previously carried out shall be deemed valid and there shall be no need to conduct them anew unless the new authority sees fit to review them.

The Investigating Judge shall issue a decision barring trial:

1 - If he finds that the act attributed to the defendant does not constitute a felony, a misdemeanour or a contravention.

2 - If he does not find sufficient evidence against the defendant for suspicion or indictment.

3 - If the perpetrator of the offence is unknown. In the first and second cases, the Investigating Judge shall be required to release the defendant if he is not detained for another reason. In the third case, he shall send a permanent warrant of inquiry for the perpetrator.

The detained defendant shall remain detained until the expiry of the time limit for cassation prescribed for the Government Commissioner, unless he agrees to the release immediately upon the issuance of the decision.

If the action is of the nature of a felony, the defendant shall be served with the indictment decision and the list of public prosecution witnesses at the request of the Government Commissioner, whereas in all other actions, the writs of summons shall state the legal articles and the names of the public prosecution witnesses and must be served, at the request of the Government Commissioner, upon the defendant at least three days before the hearing is convened.

The defendant must submit to the President of the Court a list of the names of his witnesses, and serve a copy thereof upon the Government Commissioner within three days from being served with the writ of summons. The President of the Court may require him, where necessary, to advance the travel expenses of his witnesses.

In the event that the request is rejected, it may be submitted to the Court during the trial.

All judicial papers and proceedings shall be served through bailiffs or other members of the public forces.

Service shall be effected upon the person required to be served in person or upon someone residing with him in a single dwelling at his actual or elected domicile, provided that it is inferred from his outward appearance that he has completed eighteen years of age, and that his interest does not conflict with the interest of the person required to be served. If no one is found at the actual or elected domicile of the person required to be served, service shall be effected by affixing to the door of the last place of residence.

If no actual or elected domicile is known for the person required to be served, service shall be effected by affixing in the public square in his town or in the neighbourhood in which he used to reside through the Mukhtar, and a copy of the writ shall also be affixed to the door of the Court.

If the town in Lebanon of the person required to be served is not known, service shall be effected through the Mukhtar by affixing in the public square in the town in which or within the jurisdiction of which the offence was committed, and a copy of the writ shall also be affixed to the door of the Court.

The procedures followed in ordinary law shall not apply before the Military Judiciary relating to:

1 - Calling upon the fugitive accused to surrender himself before the date of the hearing.

2 - Interrogating the accused before the date of the hearing.

A released suspect or accused person must surrender himself into custody at the registry of the Military Court before the hour fixed for the opening of the hearing.

The provisions of the preceding paragraph shall not apply before Military Single Judges.
The rules of criminal procedure shall apply to all matters not provided for by a special text in this Law.

If the defendant fails to appoint a lawyer, or if it is impossible for his lawyer to defend him, the President of the Military Court shall appoint for him a lawyer from among the officers or lawyers referred to in Article 21 of this Law, or request the President of the Bar Association to appoint a lawyer to ensure the defence of the defendant.

The President of the Military Court may bar the lawyer from entering the Military Court for a period not exceeding three months if he commits a grave professional fault prior to the trial or during the hearings.

The President of the Military Court shall notify this decision within forty-eight hours through the Government Commissioner to the President of the Bar Association or to the authority to which the lawyer belongs, in order to consider taking disciplinary sanctions against him.

The lawyer may challenge the said decision before the Military Court of Cassation within three days from the reading out of the decision if he was present at the hearing, and otherwise from the date he is notified thereof.

The Government Commissioner before the Military Court may appeal decisions issued by the Military Court relating to release before the Military Court of Cassation within 24 hours from the date of their issuance.

The Military Court of Cassation shall examine this challenge and the appeal of these decisions and shall adjudicate thereon as though it were a court of appeal, and its decisions in these cases shall be final.

It shall decide on the appeal of release decisions within 24 hours from the date the file is received by it, and the detainee shall remain in detention until the appeal is adjudicated.

After questioning the defendant, the President shall order the clerk to read out the indictment sheet, thecommittal order, or the bill of indictment and all other documents that may be the subject of debate.

The defendant, if he wishes to plead lack of jurisdiction, shall raise this plea immediately upon the reading out of the said documents, under penalty of dismissal, and the Court shall immediately adjudicate on his plea of lack of jurisdiction after the reading out of the said documents.

If the defendant, during the trial, commits an act calculated to cause noise or disturbance or any act that disturbs order in the sitting or obstructs the course of justice, the President of the Court may order that he be removed from the courtroom and returned to prison or placed under the guard of the public forces and at the disposal of the Court.

In such case, the trial shall proceed in the absence of the defendant, the judgment shall be rendered as though adversarial, and the Court shall sentence him on account of his aforementioned act to imprisonment for up to one year.

However, the clerk of the Court shall, at the end of each sitting, read out to the defendant the minutes of that sitting, notify him of the submissions of the Government Commissioner and a copy of the judgment, and advise him that he has the right to apply for cassation within the legal time limit.

He shall draw up minutes recording the foregoing, on pain of nullity.

If the defendant appears at the trial and then fails to attend it for any reason whatsoever, or if he absents himself from the trial after having attended one of its sittings, the trial shall be deemed adversarial with respect to him; however, he may file an opposition against the judgment and his opposition shall be admitted if it is established that force majeure prevented his attendance.

When the President declares the trial closed, he shall state the questions that will be put to the judges either of his own motion or at the request of the Public Prosecution or the defence, whether such questions are drawn from what is set forth in the prosecution's claim, in the committal order, or in the indictment decision, or from what transpired during the trial.

The judges shall retire to the deliberation room, and in principle they shall not be entitled thereafter to communicate with anyone or to disperse before rendering the judgment.

The trial shall be held in public before the Military Courts, of their various degrees.

However, they may decide, in accordance with ordinary law, to hold it in camera. Judgments, however, shall always be pronounced in public. The Military Court may prohibit the publication of the proceedings of the hearings or a summary thereof if it sees grounds therefor. It lies within its competence to apply the provisions of paragraphs 1, 2, 3 and 6 of Article 420 and Article 421 of the Penal Code where the matter relates to a military trial or to an offence subject to the military jurisdiction.

The President of the Court shall order that the defendant be brought in, who must appear before it unrestrained and guarded by a sufficient force.

The President of the Court shall maintain order during the hearing.

Every defendant appearing before the Military Court must have a lawyer to defend him, and this lawyer may be appointed during the hearing.

If the power of attorney is in writing, there shall be no need to register it with any authority whatsoever.

The presence of a lawyer before the Military Single Judges shall not be mandatory.

No one shall be entitled to undertake the defence of a defendant who does not appear in person before the judiciary, save in the exceptional cases set forth in ordinary law.

In the case of an offence in flagrante delicto, the lawyer shall be appointed at the same hearing if the defendant consents to be tried forthwith, and if he does not consent thereto, the case shall be adjourned for three days at least and a lawyer shall be appointed for him if he has not himself chosen a lawyer to defend him.

The case file shall be placed at the disposal of the lawyer at least twenty-four hours prior to the scheduled time of the hearing.

The lawyer may take copies of all the documents, with the exception of those among them of a confidential nature, and in this case he shall have the right to inspect them in the presence of the President of the Court or such judge as he may delegate for this purpose.

Judgments rendered by Military Single Judges in misdemeanour cases in adversarial proceedings or proceedings deemed adversarial shall be subject to appeal in accordance with the ordinary procedures prescribed in the Code of Criminal Procedure if they impose a penalty of imprisonment or a fine exceeding one hundred Lebanese pounds or confiscation or other accessory penalties or precautionary measures, or if there is a violation of the law.

The Government Commissioner may appeal all judgments and decisions of release.

Decisions relating to release or to the dismissal thereof shall also be subject to appeal.

The appeal shall be lodged in accordance with the ordinary procedures before the Permanent Military Court.

The Military Court of Cassation shall hear:

1 - Applications for cassation of judgments rendered by the Military Court. It shall also hear applications for appeal against decisions of release rendered by it, filed by the Government Commissioner.

2 - Applications for cassation of decisions rendered by Investigating Judges before the Military Court and appeals against decisions of release.

3 - Applications for rehabilitation concerning judgments rendered by the various military courts.

4 - Applications for the designation of the competent authority where a conflict arises between two military judicial authorities.

5 - Actions against the State on account of the acts of Officer-Judges appointed in accordance with the provisions of Article 14 of this Law and applications for transfer of the case.

6 - Applications for retrial in accordance with the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

Both the Government Commissioner and the convicted person shall have the right to apply for cassation of judgments rendered by the Military Court in the following cases:

1 - With respect to jurisdiction.

2 - In the event of omission of one of the substantive formalities the observance of which is prescribed on pain of nullity.

3 - In the event of an error in the application of the provisions of the law; with the exception of judgments relating to jurisdiction, an application for cassation shall not be admissible until after the final judgment in the case has been rendered.

After answering the required questions, the court shall deliberate on determining the penalty, whereby the President of the Court shall take the opinion of the lowest of them in rank first, then the opinion of the one above him, and so on and so forth, and the President shall express his opinion last.

The penalty shall be determined unanimously or by majority:

Following the determination of the penalty, the court may consider granting the defendant a stay of execution in accordance with the provisions of ordinary law.

Judgments rendered by Military Courts of all degrees shall be deemed equivalent to judgments rendered by Judicial Courts for the purpose of applying the rules of recidivism and material joinder of offences.

The judgment shall include the formalities required by law and the operative part of the judgments rendered regarding jurisdiction, nullity, and all other defences and incidental matters, and neither the answers of the defendant nor the testimonies of the witnesses shall be entered therein.

Under penalty of nullity, the judgment must include:

1 - The names of the judges and the rank of each of the military personnel among them.

2 - The name, surname, nationality, and age of the defendant.

3 - The offence or offences for which the defendant was referred to the Military Court.

4 - The taking of the legal oath by the witnesses and experts, or a statement of the reason for not administering the oath to them.

5 - A summary of the final submissions of the Government Commissioner, a summary of the defence of the defendant's counsel, and the final request of the defendant; it is permissible to suffice with the final request of each of them.

6 - The questions posed and the decisions taken regarding them unanimously or by majority.

7 - The penalties imposed and the legal articles that were applied, without there being a need to record their text.

8 - Whether the hearing was public or in camera, and in the latter case, a reference to the decision taken in this regard.

9 - That the judgment was read out publicly and the date of its issuance.

- The President, the judges, and the clerk shall sign the judgment immediately, and thereafter the bench shall return to the courtroom where the President shall read out the judgment in a public hearing in the presence of the Government Commissioner, the guard under arms, and in the presence of the defendant if the judgment was rendered in presence.

Judgments in absentia rendered by Military Single Judges, or the Military Court, or the Court of Cassation following cassation, shall be subject to opposition in accordance with the ordinary procedures specified in the Code of Criminal Procedure.

Subject to the application of the provisions of Article 62 of this Law and Article 32 relating to the application of summary procedures to traffic offences of any degree whatsoever.

The President shall put the questions relating to the defendant or to each of the defendants in the following manner:

A - With regard to the criminal acts:

- Did the defendant commit the act mentioned below (specifying in the question the act that is the subject of the committal or the prosecution.

And where there is a plurality of acts, a separate question shall be put in respect of each act thereof).

B - With regard to the aggravating circumstances:

- Was the act committed by the defendant accompanied by the circumstance mentioned below (specifying in the question the aggravating circumstance.

And where there is a plurality of aggravating circumstances, a separate question shall be put in respect of each of them, whether those circumstances are material, personal, or mixed).

C - With regard to excuses and mitigating circumstances:

- Was the act of the defendant accompanied by the following circumstance which is considered an absolutory legal excuse (specifying in the question the circumstance that constitutes an absolutory excuse).

- Was the act of the defendant accompanied by the following circumstance which constitutes a mitigating excuse (specifying in the question the circumstance that constitutes a mitigating excuse).

- Are there discretionary mitigating circumstances in the case. (It shall not be required to specify these circumstances unless the defendant is a recidivist).

The President may of his own motion put other subsidiary questions:

1- If it appears from the investigations and the oral proceedings that the act of the defendant may be given a characterization other than the characterization given to it in the prosecution or the committal decision, or that it is among the ordinary offences not subject to the jurisdiction of the Military Judiciary.

2 - If it appears to him that the said act is accompanied by an aggravating circumstance that was not mentioned in the committal decision.

- However, in both of these cases, the President must announce at the hearing in the presence of the defendant and the Government Commissioner, at the close of the oral proceedings, that he will put questions on the aforementioned subject, in order to enable them to submit their observations.

The President must put questions other than the questions specified in the two preceding Articles in order to resolve every issue placed under examination by the defendant or the Government Commissioner.

Every answer to one of the questions that is such as to terminate the case shall leave no necessity thereafter to put the other questions.

Therefore, a start must first be made by putting the questions relating to the matter the upholding of which leads to not examining the merits of the case, then the questions relating to conviction shall be put, and thereafter the questions relating to non-imputability and absolutory excuses shall be put, and after that the questions relating to aggravating circumstances, mitigating excuses, and mitigating circumstances shall be put.

Where material and personal aggravating circumstances, excuses, and mitigating circumstances exist, the provisions of Articles 268 and 269 of the Penal Code shall apply to determine the penalty.

An application for cassation shall be submitted within the following time limits:

1 - Twenty-four hours with respect to decisions issued by the Investigating Judge issued by the Military Investigating Judge, starting from the date of their issuance with respect to the Government Commissioner and from the date of notification thereof with respect to the defendant.

2 - Fifteen days with respect to judgments issued by the Military Courts.

These time limits shall run for the Government Commissioner before the Military Court and for a person sentenced in presence from the date of pronouncement of the judgment, and for a person sentenced in absentia from the date of expiry of the time limit for opposition.

A person sentenced in absentia deemed adversarial, and a person whose opposition was dismissed in form, may appeal the judgment in cassation within the time limit set forth in this Article, and this time limit shall run from the date of notification of the judgment.

3 - Thirty days for the Government Commissioner before the Military Court of Cassation in all cases.

Applications for cassation of decisions issued by Investigating Judges shall be submitted by the defendant to the Military Court of Cassation through the Investigating Judge who issued the decision, in accordance with the procedures set forth in the ordinary law.

An application for cassation from the convicted person shall not be accepted except through an attorney at the Court of Appeal who signs the application or through the military attorney appointed to defend the convicted person. The application for cassation shall be submitted to the registry of the Court of Cassation or to the registry of the court or investigating department that issued the contested judgment or decision. A copy of the judgment sought to be quashed and the attorney's power of attorney shall be attached to the application for cassation.

Upon receipt of the case from its authority, it shall be referred immediately to the Reporting President to draw up a report thereon within forty-eight hours after reviewing the written submission drawn up by the Government Commissioner before the Military Court when raising the case to the Court of Cassation.
Following the report of the Reporting Judge, the case shall be referred to the Government Commissioner before the Military Court of Cassation to submit his opinion.

An application for cassation by the Government Commissioner before the Permanent Military Court or the Military Court of Cassation shall be submitted by a written letter attached to the case upon its referral to the Court of Cassation.

This application for cassation shall be notified to the respondent to reply thereto, if he so wishes, within a time limit of fifteen days.
All applications for cassation shall be registered in a special register in the registry of the court or investigating department through which the application was submitted in a special register.

The Government Commissioner before the Military Court may request, for the grounds set forth in the preceding Article, the cassation of judgments pronouncing acquittal for lack of evidence or for insufficiency thereof, or pronouncing non-liability for lack of a criminal character of the act, or the lapse of the public prosecution for any reason whatsoever.

If the judgment is quashed in this case, the trial shall be conducted anew and the case shall be decided in accordance with the rules of procedure before the Military Court.

If it pronounces conviction and the penalty prescribed by law, this penalty shall be executed in accordance with the rules.

However, notwithstanding the provisions of Article 129 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the accused or the defendant shall be tried without being detained during the trial unless the court orders detention by a reasoned decision.

The Government Commissioner before the Court of Cassation may, either of his own motion or upon the order of the Minister of National Defence, petition in the interest of the law for the cassation of all judgments contrary to the law if they are subject to cassation and no one has submitted a request for their cassation within the legal time limit.

A request for cassation in the interest of the law may be submitted within one year from the date of issuance of the judgment.

If a judgment is quashed, the defendant shall benefit from this cassation and may never be prejudiced thereby.

The cassation of judgments issued on appeal by the Military Court may not be requested except on the condition of the existence of a difference between the Single Judge and the Military Court in the legal characterisation of the act, or in the lapse of the public prosecution by prescription or amnesty, or in the bar to prosecution by reason of res judicata.

Cassation may be requested without the fulfilment of the aforementioned conditions if the offence is a misdemeanour adjudicated concurrently with a felony.

The Government Commissioner before the Military Court may request the cassation of the following decisions issued by the investigating judges:

1 - Decisions barring trial.

2 - Decisions relating to jurisdiction.

3 - All decisions issued contrary to submissions.

As for the defendant, he may only appeal in cassation against the decisions relating to jurisdiction among them.

The Minister of National Defence may, upon the proposal of the Supreme Military Authority, request the Government Commissioner before the Military Court to appeal in cassation against judgments or decisions issued by the Military Court or its investigating judges that are subject to cassation, within the conditions set forth in the preceding Articles. The Supreme Military Authority may, in time of war or in a zone in which military rule has been declared, request cassation directly within the conditions set forth in the preceding Articles.

The procedures prescribed in the ordinary law for the appeal of decisions rendered by investigating judges before the Indictment Chamber shall apply to applications for the cassation of decisions rendered by military investigating judges, and the Court of Cassation, its Misdemeanour Chamber, shall examine the application for cassation.

As for the judgments of the Military Court, the examination of applications for their cassation shall be subject to the provisions prescribed in the following articles.

The Military Court of Cassation shall convene upon the summons of its President, deliberate in the absence of the Government Commissioner attached to it, and render its decisions in council chamber within fifteen days from the date of its receipt of the case file.

The opinions of the members shall be taken starting from the lowest of them in rank and ending with the President.

Decisions shall be taken unanimously or by majority, and the dissenting judge must record his dissent at the foot of the decision.

The Military Court of Cassation shall decide either to uphold the contested judgment or decision or to quash it.

If the judgment is quashed, the Court shall decide to retry the case in a public hearing, provided that it renders its decision within two months from the date of the cassation decision. The ordinary trial procedures shall be followed before the Military Court of Cassation with the exception of the rules provided for in this law.

The Court of Cassation, its Misdemeanour Chamber, shall examine applications for rehabilitation and shall take its decisions in council chamber in accordance with the procedures prescribed for the Indictment Chamber for taking such decisions.
A retrial may be requested before the Military Court of Cassation in felony and misdemeanour cases, whichever Military Court rendered the judgment therein.

Applications for retrial shall be subject to the procedures prescribed in the Code of Criminal Procedure, and the Minister of Defence, upon the request of the Higher Military Authority, may exercise the rights granted by law to the Minister of Justice.

With the exception of a sentence of death, adversarial judgments rendered by the Military Court and by the Military Court of Cassation shall be enforceable immediately.

Cassation against a judgment shall not stay its execution except with respect to the fine and fees, provided that the Court of Cassation may release on bail the applicant for cassation who has been sentenced to a misdemeanour penalty.

Where the judgment imposes the death penalty, the case file shall be submitted, together with the submissions of the Government Commissioner at the Military Court of Cassation, to the Minister of National Defence, who shall transmit the file, accompanied by his observations where necessary, through the Ministry of Justice to the Permanent Pardon Commission. The said Commission shall return the file, after giving its opinion thereon, to the Minister of Justice, who shall in turn submit it to the President of the Republic.

Judgments imposing the death penalty shall be executed by firing squad at the place and in accordance with the procedures prescribed by the decree ordering the execution of the penalty.

The Minister of National Defence shall designate the ordinary or special prison in which the defendant must be detained or in which the penalty imposed upon him by the Military Court must be executed.

The entire period of pre-trial detention shall be included in the calculation of the penalty imposed. The period during which a person was deprived of his liberty shall be deemed pre-trial detention.

There shall also be included in the calculation of pre-trial detention the period during which a person was deprived of his liberty in execution of a disciplinary measure taken against him for the same cause for which he was convicted.

The period to which a convicted person has been sentenced to a penalty depriving of liberty shall not be included in the calculation of the period of his military service.

The Minister of National Defence may, after consulting the Higher Military Authority and with the approval of the Council of Ministers, decide to stay the execution of a judgment for reasons relating to the public interest.

The stay of execution may extend to accessory and additional penalties and precautionary measures, in whole or in part, provided that, in such case, this is expressly stated in the decision staying execution.

The provisions of this Article shall apply only if a person sentenced to a penalty depriving of liberty has served half of its term.

The Minister of National Defence may, with the approval of the Council of Ministers, revoke the decision staying execution at any time, unless one year has elapsed since it was issued in the case of a contravention, five years in the case of a misdemeanour and seven years in the case of a felony.

The Ministry of National Defence shall notify the Judicial Record departments of a copy of all the decisions set forth in this Article.

The revocation of the decision staying execution shall entail the execution of the remainder of the penalty.
In applying the preceding Article, the period spent by the convicted person in military service during general mobilisation shall be deducted from the penalty.

Military courts shall apply, in ordinary felonies and misdemeanours, whoever the perpetrator thereof may be, the principal, additional and accessory penalties provided for in the Penal Code.

They shall, moreover, apply in respect of military personnel the accessory penalties provided for in this Law.

The Military Courts shall apply the penal laws and the procedures provided for in ordinary law or in special laws in all cases that do not conflict with the provisions of this Law.

The procedures provided for in ordinary law concerning actions raising the liability of judges for judicial acts shall be applied before the Military Courts. In such cases, the Military Court of Cassation shall replace the Court of Cassation of the Judicial Courts.

The provisions of ordinary law concerning the transfer of an action shall also be applied, and the Military Court of Cassation shall replace the Judicial Courts competent to examine the request for transfer, and if the transfer is decided, the Military Court shall examine the action with a panel other than the panel that undertook the examination thereof.

When the provisions of ordinary law and special laws are applied pursuant to Articles 98 and 99 of this Law, the officials whose cases fall within the jurisdiction of the Military Court shall be considered as ordinary officials with respect to the offences committed by them or against them during the performance of their duties or on the occasion of their duties.

If the acts provided for in this Law constitute, as a result of the circumstances in which they were committed or the consequences to which they led, an offence carrying a more severe penalty under this Law than under ordinary law, the more severe penalty shall be applied.

In offences designated in this Law exclusively for military personnel and which may be committed by civilians, the provisions of this Law shall apply to such civilians, provided that the penalty may be reduced as follows:

- Instead of the death penalty: Hard labour for life.

- And instead of hard labour for life: Temporary hard labour.

Furthermore, every other penalty may be reduced by up to half.

The word "military person" or "military personnel" for the application of this Law shall mean:

Active-duty military personnel and armed elements attached to the Army.

Military degradation is an accessory felony penalty to the penalties of death, hard labour, and detention imposed on a military person pursuant to the provisions of this Law, and military degradation is an inevitable consequence of civil degradation and entails, in addition to the consequences specified in Article 49 of the Penal Code:

1 - Forfeiture of rank and of the right to wear the uniform and bear the insignia pertaining thereto.

2 - Expulsion from the Army.

3 - Permanent deprivation of every retirement pension or dismissal indemnity and of every gratuity for prior services, and the forfeiture of the right to recover the pension deductions paid throughout those services.

Every judgment imposing military degradation shall be mentioned in the Order of the Day.

Dismissal is a secondary misdemeanour penalty that shall only apply to officers and shall entail the loss of rank and the loss of the right to wear the uniform and bear the insignia appertaining thereto.

A dismissed officer shall lose his rights to any retirement pension or severance indemnity and to any gratuity for previous services, and his right to recover the retirement deductions that were paid during those services shall lapse.

Loss of rank is a secondary misdemeanour penalty to penalties exclusively specified by the law.

This secondary penalty shall have the effects of dismissal, except that it shall not deprive of the right to a retirement pension, nor of a gratuity for previous services, nor of severance indemnity.

The sentencing of any holder of a military rank for a felony or a dishonourable offence shall ipso jure result in the loss of rank, regardless of the court that issued it, whether or not it ordered reduction in rank or dismissal, and whether or not mitigating circumstances were granted. A sentence to a misdemeanour penalty of imprisonment coupled with total or partial deprivation of political and civil rights shall also entail the loss of rank.

The following offences shall be considered dishonourable: theft, fraud, breach of trust, embezzlement, bribery, extortion and blackmail, forgery and the use of forged documents, offences against public morals provided for in Title VII of the General Penal Code, drawing a cheque without funds, false testimony, false oath, offences related to narcotics, and the attempt to commit any of the dishonourable misdemeanours where such attempt is punishable by law.

A sentence of imprisonment exceeding one month for a dishonourable felony shall necessarily entail expulsion from the Army.

The Army High Command may expel from the Army any serviceman sentenced to imprisonment for a term of three months or more pursuant to any judgment whatsoever.

Every person called up for service in the Army or for military training in accordance with the laws and regulations who fails to answer the call "after the expiry of nine days in time of peace and three days in time of war shall be deemed a draft dodger.

A draft dodger shall be punished in time of peace by imprisonment from three months to two years, and in time of war from two years to five years.

Dismissal may be ordered if the draft dodger is an officer, and these penalties shall not preclude the application of the special provisions provided for in the Army Law, the Service in the Army Law, the Military Training Law, and all other military laws.

The penalties set forth in this Article shall apply to any person upon whom military requisitions are imposed and who fails to comply therewith.

In time of peace, the following shall be deemed a deserter within the country:

1- Every serviceman who is absent from his unit or detachment without leave or lawful excuse after the expiry of six days.

2 - Every serviceman who travels from one unit to another or from one post to another, or whose leave has expired, and fails to return to his unit or detachment after the expiry of nine days from the date fixed for his return.

3 - A serviceman who has not been in the service for three months and whose absence has exceeded thirty days. A serviceman who deserts within the country in time of peace shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years.

If the deserter is an officer, he shall also be punished with the penalty of dismissal.

The penalty of imprisonment shall not be less than one year in any of the following circumstances:

a - If the deserter took with him a piece of his weapons or any equipment, effects, clothing, matériel, animals or any item belonging to the Army and failed to return it.

b - If he deserted while on duty or in the presence of rebels.

c - If he has previously deserted.

In time of war, two-thirds of the periods provided for in paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 shall be reduced and the penalty shall be doubled

In time of peace, every serviceman who crosses the Lebanese borders without leave, or leaves his unit and joins a foreign country, after the expiry of three days from his absence without lawful excuse, shall be deemed a deserter abroad.

In time of war, however, he shall be deemed a deserter after an absence of one day.

A serviceman who deserts abroad in time of peace shall be punished by imprisonment from two to five years.

If the deserter is an officer, he shall be punished by temporary detention, and if he is granted mitigating circumstances and punished by imprisonment, he shall also be sentenced to dismissal.

The time limits set forth in Article 108 shall not be taken into account where desertion takes place to the enemy or in the presence of the enemy, or where it takes place by conspiracy.

The penalty of imprisonment shall be increased up to ten years if the serviceman deserts abroad in any of the following circumstances:

1 - If he took with him a piece of his weapons or any equipment, clothing, matériel, animals or any item belonging to the Army

and failed to return it.

2 - If he deserted while on duty or in the presence of rebels.

3 - If he has previously deserted.

4 - If he deserted in time of war or in an area in which a state of emergency has been declared or in a military zone.

If the deserter is an officer, he shall be punished with the maximum penalty of detention, and if he is granted mitigating circumstances and punished by imprisonment, he shall also be sentenced to the penalty of dismissal.

Every member of the military who commits the crime of desertion to the enemy shall be punished by death with military degradation, and if the desertion is to insurgents in the course of pursuing them, the penalty shall be hard labour for life.

If the desertion takes place in the presence of the enemy or in the presence of insurgents, the penalty shall be temporary detention.

If the deserter is an officer, he shall be punished by temporary hard labour and shall also be sentenced to dismissal, even if he is granted mitigating reasons and sentenced to the penalty of imprisonment.

Every desertion committed by two or more members of the military following an agreement among them thereon shall be deemed desertion by conspiracy, even if they surrender or are apprehended before the expiry of the time limit specified in the preceding articles.

The leader of the conspiracy to desert outside the country shall be punished by temporary detention, and if its leader is an officer, by temporary hard labour. The officer shall be sentenced to dismissal even if he benefits from mitigating circumstances and his penalty is reduced to a misdemeanour penalty.

The leader of the conspiracy to desert within the country shall be punished by imprisonment from five to ten years.

The remaining participants in the conspiracy shall be punished by imprisonment from one to five years if the desertion is within the country, and this penalty shall be doubled if the desertion is outside it. The "attempt to commit the misdemeanours" provided for in the preceding paragraph shall also be punished.

If the desertion set forth in the preceding article takes place in time of war, the following shall be punished by death with military degradation:

a - A member of the military who deserts by conspiracy in the presence of the enemy.

b - The leader of the conspiracy if the desertion is abroad.

As for the remaining offenders, they shall be punished by hard labour for life.

If, however, the desertion is within the country, the leader of the conspiracy shall be punished by hard labour for life and the remaining participants by temporary hard labour. If the deserter is an officer, he shall also be sentenced to the penalty of dismissal even if the penalty imposed does not include military degradation.

A member of the military who has engaged the enemy, or who is about to engage it, or who is exposed to its attacks, shall be deemed a deserter in the presence of the enemy.

If a judgment in absentia is rendered against a deserter to the enemy or against a deserter in the presence of the enemy, or against a deserter or a draft evader who has repaired to a foreign country and remained therein during the war, the court shall order the confiscation of all his present or future property.

A copy of the judgment of confiscation shall be sent forthwith to the Ministry of Justice so that it may request the civil court within whose jurisdiction the convicted person was residing to appoint a custodian to administer and invest his property in accordance with the provisions governing the administration of the property of a missing person and Articles 34 et seq. of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
The penalty prescribed for the offence of desertion shall apply to a deserter belonging to an allied army fighting against a common enemy.

Every serviceman who renders himself temporarily or permanently unfit for service in order to evade his military duties or any lawful mission or task assigned to him shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to five years.

If the offence takes place in the presence of the enemy, the penalty shall be death.

If the offence takes place in the presence of insurgents or in a region where a state of emergency or martial law has been declared, the penalty shall be temporary detention.

Military accomplices shall be punished by the same penalty as the perpetrator.

If the accomplices are physicians, pharmacists, or nurses, the penalty of imprisonment or temporary detention shall be doubled, and non-military accomplices and those not assimilated to servicemen shall also be sentenced to a fine from one thousand pounds to three thousand Lebanese pounds, and the convicted person's licence to practise his profession shall be withdrawn for a period ranging between six months and two years.

An officer sentenced to imprisonment solely due to the granting of mitigating circumstances shall also be sentenced to the penalty of dismissal.

Punishment shall extend to anyone who attempts to commit the offence prescribed in this article.

Every person called up for national service who intentionally renders himself temporarily or permanently unfit for service shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years, and accomplices other than ascendants, descendants, spouses, and full brothers and sisters shall be punished by the same penalty as the perpetrator.

If the accomplices are physicians, pharmacists, or nurses, the penalty of imprisonment shall be doubled, and a fine from one thousand to two thousand pounds shall be imposed, and the convicted person's licence to practise his profession shall be withdrawn for a period ranging between six months and two years.
