Every commander of a military region or sector convicted of capitulating to the enemy or of giving the order to cease fighting without having exhausted all the means of defence at his disposal, or without having done everything demanded by honour and duty, shall be punished by death.

If the offence occurs during the pursuit of insurgents, the penalty shall be hard labour for life. The provisions of this article shall apply to commanders of ships, aircraft, and all other means of military transport.

Every commander of a military region or sector, or of a land, naval, or air military unit, who abstains, while capable thereof, from attacking or fighting the enemy, or who delays in assisting any military unit belonging to the Lebanese Army or allied armies, unless prevented by contrary military orders or other grave reasons, shall be punished by temporary hard labour and military degradation, and the same penalty shall be imposed on every commander of an armed unit who surrenders in the open battlefield.

The President of the Civil Court may grant, during the period of receivership, an allowance to the wife or wives of the convicted person, to his children, and to his parents if they are indigent.

If six months elapse from the date of the declaration of the end of the war and the convicted person does not appear, all his property shall be sold in accordance with the procedures prescribed for the sale of State property.

From the price shall be paid the fees, expenses, and genuine debts owed by the convicted person, and the balance shall be deposited in the Treasury fund if the convicted person is unmarried, a widower, or divorced and has no ascendants or descendants; however, if he has a wife, ascendants, or descendants, one-third of the balance shall be given to the State and the remainder shall be distributed among the wife or wives, the ascendants, and the descendants according to the will of the convicted person where it exists, or according to their hereditary shares as they stood at the end of the period of one year following the declaration of the end of the war.

If the person convicted in absentia appears or is arrested after the sale has taken place and the court declares his acquittal, he may sue the State before the State Council for compensation for the material damages he sustained.

The period of limitation shall not be calculated except starting from the deserter reaching the legal age of termination of service set for his rank pursuant to Army regulations.

Neither the public prosecution action nor the sentence imposed shall be subject to limitation in the cases set forth in the first paragraph of Article 113.

Any person who conceals or embezzles the property of the convicted person or participates therein shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to two years and by a fine from 100 to 500 L.L., or by one of these two penalties, and the Military Court shall annul all contracts and acts carried out in violation of this Article, provided that the rights of third parties acting in good faith are preserved.

The penalty shall be doubled if the aforementioned acts are committed by the receiver entrusted with the preservation and administration of the aforementioned property, and he shall be ordered to return what he concealed or embezzled or to pay its value if returning it in kind is impossible.

Any person who incites desertion or failure to report or facilitates either of them by any means whatsoever, whether his incitement produced a result or did not produce a result, shall be subject to the penalty of the principal offender.

Any person who conceals a deserter or performs, with knowledge of the matter, any act calculated to prevent the conduct of legal prosecutions shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years.

The ascendants of the concealed offenders, their descendants, their husbands or wives, or their brothers or sisters of the full blood shall be exempted from punishment.

Any person who conceals a person who has failed to report for military service or performs any act calculated to facilitate his concealment shall be punished by the same penalty, with the exception of ascendants, descendants, husbands, wives, and brothers and sisters of the full blood.
Every Lebanese serviceman or serviceman in the service of Lebanon who bears arms against Lebanon shall be punished by death.

Every serviceman of the land, naval, or air forces shall be punished by death who:

A - Incites to desertion or prevents rallying in the face of the enemy.

B - Proceeds, without an order from his superiors, to incite to the cessation of hostilities, to surrender, or to join the enemy.

C - Intentionally causes the seizure by the enemy of the military units placed under his command.

D - Establishes relations with the enemy with a view to facilitating its operations.

If the offence takes place before rebels or in an area in which martial law has been declared, the penalty shall be temporary detention for five to ten years, and every person who incites servicemen to join the enemy or facilitates the same for them, with knowledge of the matter, or who recruits in the interest of a State that is in a state of war with Lebanon, shall be deemed a recruiter in the interest of the enemy and shall be punished by death. If the offence takes place during the pursuit of rebels or in their interest, the penalty shall be hard labour for life.

If the offender is a serviceman, he shall also be punished by military degradation.

Every person convicted of a conspiracy aimed at undermining the authority of the commander or the discipline or security of the soldiers shall be punished by temporary detention for five to ten years.

The maximum penalty shall apply to the instigators of the conspiracy and to the servicemen of the highest rank.

The penalty shall be death if the conspiracy takes place in time of war, or in areas declared under a state of siege, or in any circumstances that endanger the security of the military unit.
Every serviceman who usurps a command or retains it without lawful cause or contrary to the orders of his superiors shall be punished by detention for five to ten years.

Every Lebanese serviceman or serviceman in the service of Lebanon who falls into the hands of the enemy and undertakes, in order to secure his release, not to bear arms against the enemy shall be punished by imprisonment for one to three years.
Every prisoner of war recaptured after having broken his parole and borne arms against Lebanon shall be punished by death.

The following shall be deemed a spy and punished by death:

1- Every serviceman who enters a war position, a military post, a military establishment, or any other premises of the army in order to obtain documents or information of benefit to the enemy or prejudicial to the safety of such premises.

2 - Every serviceman who gives the enemy documents or information capable of affecting military operations.

3 - Every serviceman who conceals, himself or through another, with knowledge of the matter, enemy spies.

Every member of the military who surrenders to the enemy the troops under his command or the position which he is entrusted to defend, or hands over to him the army's provisions or maps of military positions, factories, ports or docks, or discloses to him the password or any of the secrets of military operations, shall be punished by death.

Members of the military who, acting as a band, proceed to plunder or destroy crops, goods or other items and effects belonging to the army, whether the act takes place with arms, by the use of force, by breaking down or smashing doors or barriers, or by the use of violence against persons, shall be punished by temporary hard labour.

The punishment shall be temporary detention if the collective plunder or destruction takes place in cases other than those mentioned above.

If there are among the perpetrators one or more instigators or members of the military holding rank, they shall be sentenced to hard labour for life in the cases provided for in the first paragraph, and the penalty shall be doubled in the cases of the second paragraph.

An officer who participates in this offence shall be sentenced to the penalty of dismissal, even if he is granted mitigating reasons.

Every person, whether a member of the military or a non-military person, who, in a zone of military operations, proceeds to plunder a wounded, sick, drowning or dead person shall be punished by temporary detention.

The perpetrator shall be punished by death if, in order to facilitate the act of plunder, he inflicts upon the victim acts of violence that worsen his condition.
Every member of the military who intentionally proceeds to destroy or tear up registers or other official papers belonging to the military authority shall be punished by temporary detention.

Every member of the military who, through his negligence, causes the destruction, loss, or permanent or temporary disabling of a building, barricade, fortification, or any land, naval or aerial unit, or any installations or constructions used by the armed forces or contributing to national defence, or official papers belonging to the military authority, shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to five years.

An officer shall be sentenced to dismissal, even if he is granted mitigating reasons.

If the act mentioned in the preceding Article takes place intentionally, the penalty shall be hard labour for life, and if the act results in the death of any person or inflicts grave damage upon national defence, the penalty shall be death.

If the act mentioned in Article 134 takes place upon a weapon of war or any other thing used by the army in military operations, even if such thing or weapon is the property of the perpetrator, the penalty shall be imprisonment from three months to two years.

If the act takes place intentionally, the penalty shall be from one year to three years.

Any person who publicly and without right assumes a military capacity or rank, or wears a decoration, rosette, or badge of the Lebanese military decorations, rosettes, or badges, or wears a uniform or attire of the military uniforms or attires, shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years.

Any military person who wears a decoration or rosette of foreign decorations, rosettes, or badges without having been previously authorised to wear it by the Lebanese authorities shall be punished by the same penalty.

The preceding article shall apply in time of war to any person who publicly and without right uses in combat zones the badge of the Red Cross, its flag, or its emblem, or badges, flags, or emblems similar thereto.
The provisions of this Title shall apply to the Internal Security Forces, General Security, all others of similar status, and soldiers of allied armies.

Military personnel who assemble in a number of four at least and commit one of the following acts shall be considered to be in a state of mutiny:

1- Refusing in agreement to obey the orders of their superiors upon the first warning.

2 - Taking up arms without permission and acting contrary to the orders of their superiors.

3 - Committing acts of violence with the use of arms and failing to answer the call of their superiors to excel and return to order. Mutinous military personnel shall be punished by detention from two to five years in the circumstances set forth in item (1), from three years to five years in the circumstances set forth in item (2), and from five years to ten years in the circumstances set forth in item (3).

As for the mutineers of the highest rank, they shall be punished by temporary hard labour in the first case and by the maximum of temporary hard labour in the last two cases.

These latter penalties shall be inflicted upon the instigators.

The penalty of dismissal shall be pronounced against an officer convicted under this article even if military degradation does not automatically result from the penalty imposed.

If the mutiny or instigation takes place in time of war or in a zone in which military rule has been declared, the maximum of the prescribed penalty must always be pronounced.

If the mutiny takes place before the enemy and in the case set forth in item 3 of Article 148, the penalties provided for in the second and third paragraphs of the following Article 152 of this Law shall be pronounced.

The penalty shall be aggravated in accordance with the provisions of Article 257 of the Penal Code if the offence takes place before mutineers or inside fortified places, a military vessel, or an arms or ammunition depot.

The penalties provided for in this subsection shall be increased in accordance with the provisions of Article 257 of the Penal Code if the act is committed in wartime or in an area in which martial law has been declared.

Any military person entrusted with accounting affairs, whether relating to money or other materials, who commits forgery in the account or uses forged documents while knowing thereof shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to five years.

Shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to five years:

1- Any military person who personally or through third parties adulterates materials entrusted to him for safekeeping or guarding, or distributes them, whether such materials are liquid produce or otherwise.

2 - Any military person who personally or through third parties distributes meat knowing that it is the meat of animals infected with contagious diseases.
The penalty shall be doubled in wartime or in an area in which martial law has been declared.

Any military person or employee of the Army who steals, embezzles, sells, pledges, squanders, or commits breach of trust in respect of funds, equipment, apparatus, clothing, weapons, ammunition, animals, or any item belonging to the Army shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to three years.

Or who fails to return what has been delivered to him of such items.

The perpetrator shall be punished by temporary detention if he was entrusted with the safekeeping or guarding of such items. If the perpetrator is an officer, he shall also be sentenced to the penalty of dismissal or loss of rank.

Any deserting military person who has not been convicted of the offence of desertion or has been acquitted thereof shall be punished by the penalties provided for in the preceding Article if he fails to return the animals, weapons, or any item belonging to the Army that he took upon his desertion, or fails to pay double their value if their restitution in kind is impossible.

Any person, other than the persons mentioned in Article 141, who knowingly steals equipment, apparatus, or clothing of the Army, or its other items, shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years and by a fine from one hundred to one thousand Lebanese pounds, or by either of these two penalties.

Any person who publicly and without right assumes a military capacity or rank, or wears a decoration, rosette, or insignia of the Lebanese military decorations, rosettes, or insignia, or wears a uniform or attire of the military uniforms or attire, shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years.

The provisions of this Article shall apply to any person who knowingly disposes of, possesses, takes in pledge, or transports any item belonging to the Army.

Any attack or resistance with violence or acts of severity committed by a serviceman against members of the armed forces or men of authority shall be deemed rebellion.

Rebellion shall be punishable by imprisonment from two months to one year if the perpetrator is not armed, and by imprisonment from six months to two years if he is armed.

Every serviceman who commits the offence of rebellion while armed, against a sentry, a watchman, or any serviceman delegated to a specific duty with the intent of preventing him from performing the mission entrusted to him, shall be punished by temporary hard labour; if the perpetrator is not armed, the penalty shall be imprisonment from six months to three years; and if the act is committed by two or more persons, even if unarmed, the penalty shall be imprisonment from one year to five years.

The maximum penalty prescribed in each of the three cases set forth above shall be imposed if the violence takes place in time of war or in an area in which martial law has been declared, or if it is in the presence of insurgents, or inside fortified places, an arms or ammunition depot, or a military vessel, or on the flanks of such places.

The penalty shall be doubled if the offence takes place in the presence of the enemy, and if the offender is a civilian, the penalty shall be reduced by up to one half.

The penalty of dismissal shall be imposed if the perpetrator is an officer, even if military degradation does not result ipso jure from the penalty imposed.

The penalty shall be imprisonment from ten days to six months if the sentry or watchman is insulted by words, gestures, or threats.

Every serviceman who refuses to obey his superiors or to execute the orders he receives, unless prevented therefrom by force majeure, shall be punished by imprisonment from six to two years.

Every serviceman who refuses to obey when ordered to attack the enemy or to perform any other act ordered by his superior in the presence of the enemy shall be punished by death with military degradation.

Every serviceman who refuses to obey in the presence of insurgents shall be punished by temporary detention, and if the perpetrator is an officer, the penalty of dismissal shall also be imposed upon him, even if military degradation does not result ipso jure from the penalty imposed.

The penalty shall be aggravated in accordance with the provisions of Article 257 of the Penal Code if the offence takes place inside fortified places, a military vessel, or an arms or ammunition depot.

Any military person who inflicts upon his superior an act of severity for reasons relating to the service shall be punished by temporary detention; if the perpetrator is an officer, he shall be punished by the maximum penalty and shall also be sentenced to dismissal even if military degradation does not automatically result from the penalty imposed. Any military person who commits acts of severity while under arms shall be punished by the maximum penalty of temporary detention.

A military person who commits acts of violence against his superior during the performance of duty or on the occasion thereof for reasons unrelated to the service shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years, and if the defendant is under arms, he shall be punished by the maximum penalty.

However, if the defendant is an officer, he shall be sentenced to the maximum penalty and to dismissal as well.

If the acts of violence are unrelated to the service and occurred outside the performance of duty or not on the occasion thereof, the penalty of imprisonment shall be from three months to two years, provided that it shall not be less than one year if the defendant is under arms or if he is an officer.

The penalty shall be aggravated in accordance with the provisions of Article 257 of the Penal Code if the offence was committed with premeditation or in the presence of insurgents or in the presence of the enemy or in an area in which martial law has been declared or inside fortified places or a military vessel.

Any military or non-military person who inflicts with cruelty acts of violence upon a wounded or sick military person who is unable to defend himself, where that takes place in the area of operations of a combatant military force, shall be punished by temporary hard labour.

Any military person who, during the performance of duty or on the occasion thereof or for reasons relating to the service, insults his superior by words, gestures, writing or threats shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years, and the penalty shall not be less than one year if the perpetrator is an officer. If the insult is not committed under the circumstances set forth above, the penalty shall be from three months to two years.

If it appears that the acts of severity or the insult occurred outside the service and the subordinate did not know the capacity of his superior, he shall be punished by the penalties prescribed in the Penal Code regarding acts of severity and insult occurring between individuals.

Every military person who abuses the authority vested in him for requisitioning in the interest of the Army in accordance with the laws and regulations, or refuses to give a receipt for the quantities he receives, shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years.

Every military person who carries out a requisition without violence when he has no capacity to carry it out shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years, and by temporary detention if the requisition takes place with violence, and he shall also be sentenced to return the requisitioned items in kind if they are found, failing which he shall be liable for double their value.

If the perpetrator is an officer, he shall also be sentenced to the penalty of dismissal if military degradation does not result ipso jure from the penalty imposed.

Every military commander who, without provocation, order, or permission, undertakes an act of hostility in a neutral or allied territory, or continues acts of hostility after officially receiving the declaration of peace, armistice, or cessation of hostilities, shall be punished by temporary detention.

If the officer is punished by imprisonment due to being granted mitigating circumstances, he shall also be sentenced to the penalty of dismissal. Every military person who assumes any command without an order or legitimate cause, or retains command contrary to the orders of his superiors, shall be punished by temporary detention for a period of at least seven years.

However, if the perpetrator is an officer and is sentenced to imprisonment due to being granted mitigating circumstances, he shall also be sentenced to the penalty of dismissal.

Every sentry or lookout who leaves his post before completing the mission entrusted to him shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to one year.

And by temporary detention if in the presence of insurgents, and by death if in the presence of the enemy.

If the offence is committed in an area in which martial law has been declared, but not in the presence of the enemy or in the presence of insurgents, the penalty shall be from two years to five years.

The penalty shall be increased in accordance with the provisions of Article 257 of the Penal Code if the offence takes place inside fortified places or a military vessel.

Every military person who sleeps while performing the duty of sentry or lookout shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to six months. If the offence is committed in the presence of insurgents, the penalty shall be imprisonment from two years to five years.

If the offence is committed in the presence of the enemy, the penalty shall be temporary detention.

If the offence is committed in an area in which martial law has been declared, and not in the presence of the enemy or in the presence of insurgents, the penalty shall be imprisonment from one year to three years.

The penalties shall be increased in accordance with the provisions of Article 257 of the Penal Code if the offence takes place inside fortified places or a military vessel.

Shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to three years any person who commits, by one of the means mentioned in Article 209 of the Penal Code, an act of contempt towards the flag or the army or an infringement upon its dignity, reputation or morale, or who commits an act likely to weaken military discipline in the army or obedience to superiors and the respect due to them.

Shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years anyone who commits in peacetime the publication, communication or disclosure of anything relating to the army or to military incidents inside or outside the barracks, or to the measures which

the military authority takes against one of its members, or the orders or decisions issued by this authority, and everything relating to the movements of units and detachments, promotions and postings, the arrest of suspects, the pursuit of insurgents, or the operations carried out by the State forces, with the exception of notifications and broadcasts the publication of which is permitted by the competent authority.

The maximum penalty shall be imposed if the offence takes place during war.

It shall also apply to allied armies and armies party to the Pact of the States of the Arab League, provided that their laws or the agreement

concluded with them contain similar provisions.

The provisions of this Article shall not apply to the publications designated by Law No. 2/71 issued on 22/1/1971

Shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years any serviceman who strikes his subordinate other than in cases of self-defence or defence of others, rallying fugitives in the face of the enemy or in the face of insurgents, and stopping looting and devastation.

Shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to six months any serviceman who, during service or in the course thereof or by reason thereof, gravely insults his subordinate without provocation, by words, writing, gestures or threats. The offender shall be punished by imprisonment from ten days to two months if the acts provided for in this Article did not take place during service or in the course thereof or by reason thereof.

If the acts provided for in the two preceding Articles took place outside service and the superior did not know of his subordinate's relationship to him, the offender shall be punished by the penalty provided for in the Penal Code for acts of violence or insult committed against individuals.

Any military person who leaves his post of duty shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to six months. If the offence takes place before insurgents, the penalty shall be imprisonment from five to ten years.

If the offence takes place before the enemy, he shall be punished by death.

If the offence takes place in a region in which martial law has been declared, but not before the enemy or before insurgents, the penalty shall be imprisonment from one year to five years.

The maximum penalty shall always be imposed if the offender is the chief of the post.

A post of duty means the place in which the military person is present pursuant to the order of his superiors to perform a specific mission entrusted to him.

Any military person who violates the regulations, orders, or general instructions given to his unit in particular or to military personnel in general, or the instructions the execution of which was entrusted to him personally, or who rebels against the instructions given to another military person, shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years.

The penalty shall be increased to five years if the offence takes place before insurgents, or in a region in which martial law has been declared, or inside fortified places, a military vessel, or an arms or ammunition depot.

If the offence takes place before the enemy, the penalty shall be increased to ten years' imprisonment. An officer convicted pursuant to the last two paragraphs of this Article shall also be sentenced to dismissal.

Every seaman and every other person on board a vessel or naval craft that is military or assigned to military operations who intentionally causes the loss of such vessel or craft or its capture by the enemy shall be punished by death.

If the offence occurs as a result of his negligence, the penalty shall be temporary detention in wartime and imprisonment from six months to three years in peacetime.

The maximum penalty shall always be imposed if the offender is the commander of the force or of the military vessel, and an officer convicted shall also be sentenced to dismissal even if he is punished by detention due to the granting of mitigating circumstances to him. The provisions of this Article shall apply:

1 - To military personnel of the Air Force if the offence relates to aircraft that are military or assigned to military operations.

2 - To civilians:

a - If they are pilots of military vessels

b - If they are pilots of civilian ships escorted by military vessels, or sailors thereof.

c - If they are navigators of civilian aircraft escorted by military aircraft.
Every commander of a military vessel who knows that his vessel is sinking and intentionally abandons it before the last seaman therein shall be punished by death.

Shall be punished by temporary detention every commander of a naval force or military vessel who:

1 - Does not attack the forces of the enemy when his forces are equal or superior thereto, or neglects to assist Lebanese or allied naval forces engaged in combat with the enemy or pursued thereby, or does not destroy an enemy convoy unless prevented therefrom by special orders or grave reasons.

2 - Does not pursue the enemy or its convoys unless prevented therefrom by grave reasons or superiority in the forces of the enemy.

The convicted officer shall also be sentenced to the penalty of dismissal even if granted mitigating circumstances.

The provisions of this article shall apply to military personnel of the Air Force if the offence relates to military aircraft.

Shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to two years every sailor who enables the enemy, through his negligence, to surprise a military vessel or causes the grounding, burning, or severe disablement thereof.

If the offender is the commander of the vessel or a sailor assigned to keep watch, he shall be sentenced to the maximum penalty. The officer convicted under this article shall also be sentenced to dismissal even if granted mitigating circumstances.

The provisions of this article shall apply to military personnel of the Air Force if the offence relates to military aircraft.

Shall be punished by death:

1 - Every commander of a naval force who surrenders before the enemy or orders the cessation of combat without having exhausted all means of combat within his power and fulfilled all that duty and honour dictate to him.

2 - Every sailor who proceeds, by any means whatsoever and without an order from the commander of the vessel, to cause the cessation of combat.

Shall be punished by temporary detention every sailor who proceeds, by any means whatsoever, to incite the cessation of combat without an order from the commander of the vessel if the incitement does not lead to a result, and if the incitement leads to the cessation of combat, it shall be punished by death.

The provisions of this article shall apply to military personnel of the Air Force if the act occurs aboard military aircraft.

The establishment of judicial assistants and civilian employees at the Military Courts is fixed in accordance with the following schedule:

The Military Court of Cassation:

1- Chief Registrar

1 - Head Clerk

1 - Clerk

1 - Typist

1 - Process Server

1- Usher

1 - Attendant.

The Permanent Military Court:

1- Chief Registrar

1 - Head Clerk

3 - Clerk

10- Typist

2 - Process Server

3 - Usher

2 - Attendant.

The cadre of civilian judges in the Military Judiciary shall be determined in accordance with the Judicial Organisation Law.

Where necessary, certain judges may be seconded to the Military Judiciary in addition to their primary duties.

As for the Government Commissioner at the Military Court of Cassation, his assistants and the Single Military Judges, they shall be appointed to their posts at the military courts in addition to their primary duties at the ordinary courts.

Appointments and secondments shall be effected by decrees and decisions taken in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

Military judicial assistants at the military courts shall be seconded in accordance with the requirements of need and pursuant to the laws and regulations in force in the Army and the Internal Security Forces.

Judicial fees at the military courts shall be determined in accordance with the Law on Judicial Fees at the ordinary criminal courts.

However, military personnel and detainees shall be exempted from the registration and stamp fees payable on applications submitted by them.

The chief clerks of the military courts or their deputies shall collect the fines, securities and costs and remit them to the Palace of Justice treasury pursuant to payment orders in accordance with the model followed at the ordinary courts.

Securities shall be returned by them to their owners pursuant to payment orders in accordance with the model followed at the ordinary courts after they have verified that there is no longer any need for them to remain in the said treasury from the legal standpoint.

- The Military Penal Code promulgated on 12 January 1946, together with all its amendments, is hereby repealed.

- And the Law establishing the Military Court of Cassation promulgated on 28 February of the year 1956.

- And all other laws, regulations and provisions contrary to this Law or inconsistent with its provisions.
This Law shall be published in the Official Gazette.

The Ministry of Finance shall deduct from the municipal fee on inflammable materials, prior to its distribution to the municipalities, an amount of six billion pounds to be allocated for lighting and cleaning in villages that do not have municipalities (cost of power, maintenance, equipment and cleaning) through the Ministry of Municipal and Rural Affairs, to be distributed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Finance and of Municipal and Rural Affairs, and the amounts previously deducted for the same purpose shall also be distributed in the same manner.

Notwithstanding any other provision, traffic fines adjudicated by a judgment shall not lapse except after the expiry of three years from the date of due notification of the judgment to the person concerned.

The Lebanese University may conclude agreements with persons of public or private law to provide services, prepare studies or consultations, or make supplies in various fields in return for fees, a percentage of which shall be allocated as remuneration for members of the teaching staff and employees who contribute thereto and another percentage for financing scientific research and its requirements and equipment, in accordance with the proposal of the University Council and the approval of the Minister of Culture and Higher Education and the Minister of Finance, provided that the remaining balance shall revert to the University.

1- The Government is authorised, within the limits of an amount equivalent to the needs of the Treasury, to issue Treasury bonds in Lebanese currency for long, medium and short terms, by decisions issued by the Minister of Finance, provided that the Government notifies the Chamber of Deputies of any amounts of issued Treasury bonds that exceed the limits of the actual deficit realised in the execution of the budget, including the total appropriations carried over to the year 1999 and the additional appropriations, by means of quarterly reports showing the justifying reasons for such excess.

2 - Within the framework of restructuring the public debt, the Government is authorised to issue Treasury bonds in foreign currency within the limits of the value of two billion US dollars, provided that the funds borrowed pursuant to this authorisation are used to convert the equivalent of their value of the public debt in Lebanese pounds into foreign currencies. The entirety of these issued bonds must be finally repaid within a time limit not exceeding thirty years from the date of commencement of their issuance, and the interest rates on these bonds shall be determined in accordance with the rates prevailing in the international market for their equivalents abroad, and this shall be effected by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

All tax assessments, including surcharges and all other additions and fines, the value of which does not exceed five thousand Lebanese pounds in respect of each of the income tax, the built property tax and the succession duty, shall be deemed lapsed, and the competent financial departments shall be exempted from issuing assessment rolls and collection orders for these amounts and from collecting them.

Special Treasury accounts shall be opened for loans, to which the value received from the principal of these loans shall be credited and to which the values paid in repayment of matured instalments and bonds shall be debited.

The Government is authorised, by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance, to open, where necessary, annual appropriations in the General Budget and the annexed budgets for the purpose of repaying loan instalments falling due (principal, interest and supplementary expenses) and to determine the sources for covering them.

A fraction of one thousand pounds shall be rounded to one thousand pounds in favour of the Treasury in all assessment, collection and expenditure transactions, including allowances, salaries, wages and their accessories.

In implementation of the provisions of Article 85 of the Constitution, the President of the Republic may, if emergency circumstances call for urgent expenditures, issue a decree based on a decision issued by the Council of Ministers, to open extraordinary or additional appropriations or to transfer appropriations in the General Budget for the year 1999, provided that these appropriations do not exceed thirty-five billion pounds, and these measures must be submitted for the approval of the Chamber of Deputies at the first session in which it convenes thereafter.

Article Thirty-One of Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12/06/1959 and its amendments (the Income Tax Law) is hereby repealed and replaced by the following text:

The tax shall be imposed on the real profit or the profit determined on a lump-sum basis after deducting therefrom, for each natural person among the taxpayers, an amount of /7 500 000/ L.L., seven million five hundred thousand pounds.

There shall be added to this deduction an amount of /2 500 000/ L.L., two million five hundred thousand pounds, for a married taxpayer, and /500 000/ L.L., five hundred thousand pounds, for each legitimate child still dependent on him, subject to the following conditions:

For males, if they have not exceeded the age of eighteen, or up to twenty-five as a maximum limit for those pursuing university studies. For males afflicted with a disabling infirmity and who do not perform paid work, provided that the disabling infirmity is proven pursuant to a medical certificate issued by the Permanent Medical Committee at the Ministry of Health.

For females prior to their marriage, or if they are widows or divorcees. Provided that the number of benefiting children does not exceed five. If the taxpayer's wife practises a profession or holds an office subject to tax, each spouse shall benefit from the deduction granted to a single person, and if the spouses have children dependent on them, the father shall be granted an additional deduction for the children in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph of this Article. In the event of the father's death or his affliction with a disabling infirmity proven as indicated above and he does not perform any paid work, the mother shall be granted the additional deduction for the children. This deduction shall apply with effect from the operations of the year 1999, and each Lebanese de facto partnership shall benefit from a single deduction. As for the tax on taxpayers subject to estimated profit, it shall be imposed after an annual deduction equivalent to the deduction granted to a married person without children.

The text of the first paragraph of Article 72 of Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12/06/1959 and its amendments (Income Tax) has been repealed and replaced by the following text:

"The rate of tax on the profits of commercial, industrial, and non-commercial professions is set as follows:

"To pay to the Treasury fund the retirement deductions due from him and the dismissal indemnity in respect of such services in a single lump sum within a time limit of three months from the date on which he is notified of the approval by the Ministry of Finance of the fulfilment of the conditions for the aggregation of such services and the accuracy of the calculation, if their value is within the limit of two million pounds. Article (42) (The net taxable amount shall be fixed at fifteen percent (15%) of the gross revenues referred to in the preceding article on a lump-sum basis and at fifty percent (50%) thereof if they have the nature of remuneration for a service, and the tax shall be withheld and levied at the rate of fifteen percent (15%) and no surcharge shall be added to the principal of the tax).

The text of Article 8 of Law No. 282 dated 30/12/1993 amending Article 45 of Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12/06/1959 and its amendments (the Income Tax Law) is repealed and replaced with the following text:

"The income tax rate has been fixed at 10% (ten percent) on the appreciation gain provided for in each of items Second and Third of Article 45 of Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12/06/1959 and its amendments".

Equivalencies of certificates in classes pertaining to all

stages of education, including university education, shall be subject to a stamp duty of:

- /25,000/ L.L. twenty-five thousand pounds for secondary

and lower certificates and classes.

- /50,000/ L.L. fifty thousand pounds for university classes and certificates

granted in Lebanon.

- /125,000/ L.L. one hundred and twenty-five thousand pounds for university certificates granted abroad.

- /10,000/ L.L. ten thousand pounds for each certified true copy

granted for a previous equivalency.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.
The cadre of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants shall consist of a Foreign Service (diplomatic and consular) and an Administrative Service.

The Central Administration shall consist of:

- The Directorate of Political Affairs.

- The Directorate of Protocol.

- The Directorate of Economic Affairs.

- The Directorate of Administrative and Consular Affairs.

- The Directorate of Emigrants.

The powers of the Director General in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants shall be exercised by a Secretary General who belongs to the First Category of the Foreign Service, holds the title of Ambassador, and supervises the Central Administration and the missions.

The Directorate of Political Affairs shall be headed by a civil servant of the Foreign Service from the First Category, and each of the other directorates by a civil servant from the First or Second Category.

An Administrative Committee shall be formed under the chairmanship of the Secretary General and with the membership of the Director of Political Affairs and the Director of Administrative and Consular Affairs, and the Committee shall exercise the competences specified in this Legislative Decree.
Diplomatic and consular missions and honorary consulates shall be established by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers.

Vacant positions in the Third Category in the Foreign Service shall be filled by way of a competitive examination conducted in accordance with the Civil Servants Regulations, and vacant positions in the Second and First Categories shall be filled by way of promotion within the same service.

No candidate shall be entitled to participate in the competitive examination of the Foreign Service except one who satisfies, in addition to the conditions provided for in the general law, the following special conditions:

1- That he has completed the twenty-first year of his age and has not exceeded the thirty-fifth. And if he is from among the civil servants, that he has not exceeded the fortieth.

2- That he is proficient in the Arabic language and one of the two languages, French or English, provided that in the competitive examination regulations additional marks shall be given to whoever is proficient in more than one living language.

3- That he holds a Bachelor's degree in Law, in Arts, in Sciences, or in Social Sciences, or a university degree recognized by the Ministry of National Education as equivalent thereto.

4- That he belongs to one of the Fourth and Third Categories if he is a civil servant in one of the cadres of the State.

5- That he is free from any tie incompatible with the duties of the post, and for that purpose the Civil Service Board shall seek the opinion of the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants regarding the candidates prior to deciding on their admission to the competitive examination. In the event of disagreement, the matter shall be referred to the Council of Ministers.

6- That a female candidate is unmarried.
Vacant
A new official shall remain on probation for a period of two years in the Central Administration and may not be attached to a post abroad until after the expiry of his probationary period.

One of the counsellors of the top three grades may be appointed, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, as head of a diplomatic mission with the title of minister plenipotentiary without modification of salary, provided that he retains this title only for the duration of his performance of the duties of the post to which he is appointed. Save for the case provided for in the first paragraph of this Article, no official may be given a title that is higher than or differs from his actual rank in the Corps.

a- The Government may, exceptionally, appoint abroad, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, ambassadors or ministers plenipotentiary who do not belong to the cadre, within the appropriations entered for this purpose in the budget, and they shall retain this title throughout the performance of their duties, and their services may be terminated at any time.

b- Ambassadors and ministers plenipotentiary appointed in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph shall be deemed to have resigned ipso jure upon the expiry of the term of office of the Head of State who appointed them.

c- The number of ambassadors and ministers plenipotentiary appointed pursuant to this Article may not exceed thirty per cent of the number of regular ambassadors and ministers plenipotentiary in the permanent cadre.

d- The provisions of paragraph (b) shall apply to ambassadors and ministers plenipotentiary from outside the cadre appointed prior to the date of issuance of this Legislative Decree.

They shall be deemed to have resigned ipso jure after the expiry of six months from the date on which this Legislative Decree enters into force, unless the Government reappoints them prior to the expiry of this time limit.

e- The Government may, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, entrust an exceptional diplomatic mission to a personage from outside the cadre who is temporarily granted the title of ambassador or minister plenipotentiary, provided that the duration of this mission does not exceed six months.

f- The services of the ambassadors and ministers plenipotentiary provided for in this Article shall terminate ipso jure upon their completion of the statutory age provided for in the Officials Law.

Lebanese and non-Lebanese honorary consuls may be appointed by decree, receiving the allowance provided for in Article 24. The mission of an honorary consul may be terminated at any time without any compensation.

Honorary consuls shall not be appointed in the areas of consular jurisdiction of diplomatic missions and career consulates.
No honorary diplomatic posts, nor posts for honorary technical attachés at any mission, may be created, nor may honorary diplomatic titles be granted.

Military, economic or cultural attachés, or specialised civil servants holding university degrees from one of the cadres of the State, may be seconded in the capacity of technical attachés to diplomatic missions. The territorial competence of the attaché may cover several missions.

Secondment shall take place for a renewable period of one year by decree adopted upon the proposal of the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants and the approval of the Minister to whose ministry the civil servant belongs.

The seconded civil servant shall in all cases be subject to the authority of the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants and shall receive his instructions from him through the head of mission. However, he shall remain in his original cadre and corps and shall receive his salaries and allowances from the administration to which he belongs. The provisions of Articles 17-18-19-20-30-3840 shall apply to the seconded civil servant.

The military attaché may correspond directly with the Army Command, provided that he submits to the head of mission a copy of such correspondence.

The following provisions shall apply to promotion in rank and advancement in step:

1- The Secretary General shall prepare, with the approval of the Administrative Committee, a schedule of the names of the civil servants whom he proposes for promotion in rank or advancement in step.

These names shall be arranged in order of merit.

2- Merit shall be assessed on the basis of the criteria established by the Civil Service Board.

أ- A diplomatic or consular officer shall not be transferred from his post abroad before the lapse of three years except at his request or that of his superior or of the Central Inspection Administration, or upon the proposal of the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants with respect to heads of missions.

ب - A diplomatic or consular officer may not remain in the same post abroad for more than five years, nor may the period of his consecutive service abroad exceed ten years.

ج- The officers referred to in the two preceding paragraphs of this Article shall return to the Central Administration upon the expiry of the maximum period of their presence abroad. They shall remain therein for a period of at least two years. However, if the number of Category One officers whose presence abroad has reached ten years or more exceeds the number of posts allocated to their category in the Central Administration, they shall be transferred to it successively, taking into account seniority abroad.

د- The periods provided for in the preceding paragraphs shall be calculated from the date on which the officer assumes his duties.

ه- Category One officers shall be transferred from one post within the Central Administration to another post therein by decree, Category Two officers by decision of the Minister, and officers of Category Three and below by decision of the Secretary General.

A diplomatic or consular official shall be granted a regular transfer allowance upon his appointment to the Service, upon his transfer from the Central Administration to abroad and vice versa, upon his transfer from one post to another abroad, and upon the termination of his services for non-disciplinary reasons if he is abroad at that time.
The regular transfer allowance shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.

Foreign Service officials who are assigned to emergency missions pursuant to written instructions from the Minister shall be granted an incidental transfer allowance determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.

a - The expatriation allowance for Foreign Service officials shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers after consulting the opinion of the Administrative Committee and the Civil Service Board, on the basis of the cost of living and social obligations. This allowance shall be increased by twenty-five percent for officials working in the countries mentioned in paragraph (a) of Article (29) of this Legislative Decree.

b - The official's entitlement to the expatriation allowance shall commence as of the date of travel, and shall be discontinued for him upon his transfer to the Central Administration as of the date of his arrival in Lebanon.

c- The expatriation allowance shall be reduced by one quarter during sick leave after the lapse of one month and shall be discontinued in full after the lapse of three months.

d- An official recalled to the Central Administration on an official mission may receive the expatriation allowance in full for a period of one month, as of the date of his departure from his duty station, and in this case no transfer allowance shall be due to him other than travel expenses, and if the period exceeds one month, they may be granted this allowance by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.

e- The expatriation allowance shall be discontinued for an official recalled to the Central Administration in preparation for his transfer to another post as of the date of his arrival in Lebanon.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants shall determine, by a decision adopted after consulting the opinion of the Administrative Committee and the Special Inspector General for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants, the amount of the representation expenses for each diplomatic and consular mission, and the methods of spending them shall be determined by a regulatory decree.

1- The Government shall provide housing for the heads of diplomatic missions abroad.

2- Other diplomatic officials and consular officials serving abroad shall be granted a housing allowance of 25 (twenty-five) per cent of their original basic salary, unless the Government provides them with housing.

3- Heads of diplomatic and consular missions residing in mission residences shall bear a portion of the expenses for lighting, heating, cooling and water, to be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.

4- The housing allowance shall accrue starting from the date of arrival of the official at his duty station. It shall cease upon the date of his final departure from that station.

5- Each head of a diplomatic mission shall have the right to employ a cook and an attendant whose wages shall be paid from the appropriation for local employees.

The head of a diplomatic mission shall receive a lump-sum allowance for a car, the value of which shall be determined by a decree adopted after consulting the opinion of the Administrative Committee and the Inspector General assigned to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants, and this allowance shall accrue starting from the date of arrival of the head of mission at his duty station.

Upon the absence of the titular head of mission for a period exceeding one month, for any reason whatsoever, the Chargé d'Affaires ad interim shall receive half the value of this allowance throughout the period of absence, provided that the other half remains due to the head of mission on condition that no mission is assigned to him for which a car allowance is due to him, and in such case the other half shall revert to the Treasury.

The honorary consul shall receive, in return for the expenses he incurs to ensure the conduct of consular business, including representation expenses, an allowance determined as follows:

A- The entirety of the collected revenues if they do not exceed two thousand Lebanese pounds per year.

B - Ten per cent on whatever exceeds two thousand pounds, provided that the total allowance stipulated in this paragraph and the preceding paragraph does not exceed five thousand Lebanese pounds per year.

The honorary consul shall not have the right to receive any other amount in return for the expenses he incurs for the sake of the consulate.

The honorary consul shall render a monthly account of the revenues of the consulate and shall deposit in the name of the consulate at one of the approved banks the amounts remaining after deducting the allowance referred to in this Article. He shall transfer them on 31 December of each year in the name of the Treasurer of the Treasury through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants shall determine the procedures for rendering account of the expenses and revenues of the missions by financial instructions endorsed by the Minister of Finance and the President of the Court of Accounts.

Counsellors who were appointed before the issuance of this Legislative Decree as heads of missions with the title of Minister Plenipotentiary without the grade requirement provided for in Article ten above being met in them, shall retain the said title until their transfer to another post.
The provisions of Legislative Decree No. 17 issued on 13 January 1955 and all provisions contrary to the provisions of this Legislative Decree or inconsistent with its content are hereby repealed.
This Legislative Decree shall enter into force on the day following its publication in the Official Gazette.

The Financial Affairs Department shall cease sending any amount to every head of mission who is three months late in depositing the revenue accounts or the monthly expenditure accounts, and shall likewise cease disbursing his salaries and allowances. No amount shall be transferred to him except by order of the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants and the Minister of Finance.
The special allowances received by cipher and archives employees in the Central Administration shall be determined by decree.

No one shall be appointed to the administrative corps of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants or transferred to it in the category of clerks and above, except an employee who meets the following additional conditions:

1- That he is proficient in one of the foreign languages mentioned in Article (7).

2- That he holds at least the Second Part of the Lebanese Baccalaureate or its equivalent.

a- The duration of the annual administrative leave shall be determined at two months for employees of missions in the Arabian Peninsula, Pakistan, India, Indonesia, and Africa except North and South Africa, and at one month for employees of all other missions.

b - The duration of travel to Lebanon and return to the duty station by the direct route without stopover, whatever the means of travel, shall not be counted as part of the leave.

c- Leaves may be accumulated over a period not exceeding three years, provided that their total does not exceed four months.

d- If the employee exceeds the duration of the leave due to him, his salary and allowances shall be withheld from him for the period of the excess.

The Government shall cover the round-trip travel expenses to Lebanon for employees on leave and for the members of their families:

a- Once every two years for whoever is entitled to a leave of two months annually.

b - Once every three years for whoever is entitled to a leave of one month annually.

The family shall include the wife and those supported at the expense of the employee among sons who have not exceeded eighteen years of age or who are pursuing their studies at educational institutes up to twenty-five years of age, and among daughters, ascendants, and unmarried sisters who are unable to support themselves.

The inspection of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants shall be conducted by the Central Inspection Administration, provided that its special Inspector General is drawn from the employees of the First Category in the Foreign Service. He may be returned to this Service after the lapse of three years from his undertaking the inspection.
The inspection of each mission shall be conducted once every five years and whenever the need arises to conduct it.

Heads of missions shall have the right to:

أ- Appoint local officials and wage-earners, within the appropriations allocated for this purpose, or dismiss them from service in accordance with the rules in force in the countries to which they are accredited, by decisions subject to the approval of the Secretary-General.

ب - Pay them the remuneration for overtime hours of work, and the additional annual remuneration, in accordance with the rules in force locally.

ج- Increase their monthly wages in accordance with the rules in force locally by decisions subject to the approval of the Secretary-General, within the allocated appropriations.

د- Grant them administrative and sick leave in accordance with the rules in force locally, by decisions notified to the Central Administration.

ه- Grant them severance indemnities immediately in accordance with local laws, provided that they are settled subsequently from the special appropriations in the budget.
Ambassadors and Ministers Plenipotentiary shall place their posts at the disposal of the new Head of State upon his assumption of the duties of the Presidency.

1- An official of the Foreign Service may not marry except with prior permission from the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants, granted after consulting the opinion of the Administrative Committee. Any person who does not comply with the provisions of this Article shall be deemed to have resigned.

2- If a female official in the Foreign Service marries a foreigner, she shall be transferred to the Administrative Corps.

Heads of diplomatic or consular missions and their officials may not leave the country to which they are appointed, whether to spend a leave, for an official mission, or for a private need, except with written permission from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants, failing which their salaries and the allowances supplementary thereto shall be withheld from them as from the date of departure until the date of return, in addition to the disciplinary penalties provided for in the general law.

The Treasury shall bear the travel expenses of officials of the Foreign Service and the members of their families referred to in Article 30.

The Ministry shall transfer to them an amount equivalent to the price of their travel tickets in first class and by direct route by aeroplane in accordance with the international tariff. The official may choose the means of transport that he wishes.
If one of the officials of the Foreign Service or one of the members of his family referred to in Article 30 dies abroad, the Government shall bear the expenses of repatriating the body to Lebanon.
Heads of missions shall be exempted from the financial guarantee in respect of stamp advances granted in their name.
An official of the diplomatic and consular corps abroad may not practise any other work, including teaching. Nor may his wife work in any institution.

A person harmed by an offence may constitute himself as a personal claimant before the First Investigating Judge in a felony or a misdemeanour, or before the Single Judge in a misdemeanour or a contravention.

He may join the public action before the Criminal Court.

The harmed person, by his claim, initiates the public right action if the Public Prosecution has not initiated it.

He may withdraw his personal claim or enter into a settlement in respect thereof without this affecting the public action, except in the cases where the public action lapses consequent upon the lapse of the personal right action.

If the harmed person brings his action before the competent civil judiciary, he shall not be permitted to abandon it and bring it before the criminal judiciary unless the Public Prosecution has initiated the public action on a date subsequent to his claim before the civil judiciary, provided that the civil action has not been decided by a final judgment.

The civil authority must stay its consideration of the civil action until the public right action is decided by an irrevocable judgment, and the judiciary of urgent matters shall remain competent to take urgent measures even if the personal right action has been brought before the criminal judiciary.

The public action shall be brought before the criminal authority within the territorial jurisdiction of which the offence was committed, or to which the place of residence of the defendant or the place of his arrest pertains.

The Law returned pursuant to Decree No. 5328 dated 20/04/2001 relating to the Code of Criminal Procedure has been ratified as amended by the Chamber of Deputies.

This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The Code of Criminal Procedure governs the organisation of the criminal judiciary, the determination of its jurisdiction, the procedures to be followed in investigation and trial before it, and the grounds of appeal against judgments and decisions rendered by it.

It also governs the regulation of the detection of criminal facts and the evidence thereof with a view to the application of criminal laws.

The ordinary criminal courts are divided into:

A- A Single Judge who hears all cases of misdemeanours and contraventions, except those excluded therefrom by a special provision.

The Public Prosecution is not represented before him.

B - A Court of Appeal, each chamber of which is composed of a President and two Associate Judges. The Public Prosecution is represented before it by an Appellate Public Prosecutor or one of the Advocates General before the Court of Appeal, or the Financial Public Prosecutor or one of the Advocates General before the Financial Public Prosecution.

C - A Court of Cassation, each chamber of which is composed of a President and two Associate Judges.

The Public Prosecution is represented before it by the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation or one of the Advocates General before the Court of Cassation.

The investigation department in each governorate is composed of a First Investigative Judge and one or more Investigative Judges in accordance with what is determined by the Judicial Judiciary Law.

One of the chambers of the civil Courts of Appeal undertakes the functions of the Indictment Chamber in each governorate.

The Judicial Judiciary Law determines the manner in which judicial judges are appointed, the number of chambers of the Court of Cassation in the capital, the number of chambers of the Court of Appeal, and the number of Single Judges, Investigative Judges, and Advocates General in each of the capital, the governorates, and the districts.

The public prosecution action, aimed at prosecuting the perpetrators of offences and the participants therein and at applying penalties and measures against them, is vested in the judges of the Public Prosecution designated in this Law.

As for the civil action for compensation for harm resulting from offences, it is a right belonging to every injured party.

Every person against whom a public prosecution action is brought is called a defendant, is called a suspect charged with a misdemeanour if suspected of a misdemeanour, and is called an accused if indicted for a felony.

The Public Prosecution undertakes the functions of exercising the public prosecution action.

It may neither waive it nor settle in respect thereof.

A civil action may be brought ancillary to the public prosecution action before the judicial authority before which that action is brought, and it may also be brought separately before the civil authority.

The public right action shall lapse for one of the following causes:

A - By the death of the defendant.

B - By general amnesty.

C - By the lapse of time for a period of ten years in a felony, three years in a misdemeanour, and one year in a contravention.

D - By the lapse of the personal right action in the cases provided for by law.

The running of the limitation period in instantaneous offences shall commence from the date of their occurrence. As for continuous, continued, or successive offences, it shall only commence from the date of the termination of the criminal state.

Every act of prosecution, investigation, or trial shall interrupt the limitation period of the public action.

The causes that interrupt the limitation period of the public action shall also interrupt it for the personal right action. However, the causes that interrupt it for the personal right action shall not lead to interrupting it for the public action.

The limitation period shall be suspended from running if it becomes impossible, due to force majeure, to carry out any act of prosecution, investigation, or trial, and it shall resume running immediately upon the cessation thereof.

The aforementioned provisions on the limitation period shall not preclude the observance of special provisions governing certain misdemeanours and contraventions.

The criminal court seized of the action shall continue, in the event of the lapse of the public action for one of the first causes mentioned, to hear the personal right action. It must order the confiscation of seized items if they are prohibited by law.

The limitation period of the personal right action shall be subject to the Civil Law.

The provisions of the Penal Code shall apply to the limitation period of imposed penalties.

«The running of the limitation period for the offences provided for in Article 401 shall not commence until after the exit of the victim from prison, detention, or provisional arrest if it is not followed by imprisonment.

On Evidence

«All statements made as a result of any of the acts provided for in Article 401 shall be null and void in any proceedings, except when used against a person accused of committing torture as evidence that such statements were made».

The functions of the Public Prosecution before the Court of Cassation shall be performed by a Public Prosecutor assisted by Advocates General.

The duties of the Financial Public Prosecution before the Cassation Public Prosecution shall be assumed by a Public Prosecutor assisted by Advocates General.

The functions of the Public Prosecution before the Court of Appeal shall be performed by a Public Prosecutor assisted by one or more Advocates General.

The acts of the Public Prosecution before the Military Court shall be performed by a Government Commissioner subject to the authority of the Cassation Public Prosecutor, assisted by one or more Advocates General.

A - Among the Advocates General provided for in the third paragraph of Article 11, there shall be one or more full-time Environmental Advocates General assigned by the Appellate Public Prosecutor to prosecute environmental offences in accordance with the procedures set forth in the laws in force.

B - The Environmental Advocate General shall bring charges for the environmental offence and specify the names of the defendants. He may bring charges against a person unknown before the Investigating Judge, thereby initiating by his charge the public action, or bring charges directly before the competent courts.

C - Environmental offences shall be deemed to be the offences resulting from:

1 - Violation of the laws and regulations relating to the protection of forestry wealth, forests, nature reserves and biological diversity, the protection of air, water and soil from pollution, and those relating to combating harm resulting from sound and noise.

2 - Violation of the laws and regulations relating to quarries, sandpits and crushers.

3 - Violation of the environmental laws and regulations specific to determining the environmental conditions for classified establishments of all kinds.

4 - Violation of the environmental laws and environmental regulations that protect the public and private property of the State and municipalities and territorial waters, and environmental encroachments upon maritime and riverine property and groundwater.

5 - Violation of the laws relating to the disposal of waste of all kinds, in particular medical waste and waste resulting from hospitals, and chemical and nuclear waste.

6 - Violation of the provisions set forth in Law No. 444 dated 29/7/2002 and all other legal provisions relating to the protection of the environment wherever they may be found.

7 - Violation of the laws and regulations that protect antiquities and the cultural and natural heritage.

D - The Environmental Advocate General may seek the assistance of specialists in environmental affairs and in the affairs of antiquities and cultural heritage to carry out the technical and artistic tasks with which he assigns them, after administering the legal oath to them if they are not sworn experts.

E - The Chief Clerks of the competent courts shall notify the Ministry of Environment of every final environmental criminal judgment issued against a natural or legal person in order to record it in the special register referred to in Item (B) of Article (5) of this Law, within three months from the date on which it becomes final.

F - Judgments and decisions issued in environmental cases, including the decision to archive the action, shall be published in two local newspapers.
Each Public Prosecutor shall preside over his department and distribute the business falling within his jurisdiction among the Advocates General who assist him.

The Public Prosecution at the Court of Cassation shall be headed by a Public Prosecutor appointed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice. He shall be assisted by Advocates General.

The authority of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation shall encompass all judges of the Public Prosecution, including the Government Commissioner at the Military Court. He may address to each of them written or oral instructions regarding the conduct of the public action.

However, they shall retain freedom of speech during trial hearings.

He shall refer to each of them, according to his jurisdiction, the reports and minutes that reach him concerning an offence and request him to initiate the public action therein.

Subject to the provisions of Article 79 of the Law Regulating the Legal Profession, and in all cases in which criminal prosecution requires an authorisation or approval from any non-judicial authority, and in the event of disagreement between that authority and the Appellate Public Prosecution, the Financial Public Prosecution, or the Government Commissioner at the Military Court, the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation shall, notwithstanding any general or special provision, have the power to decide finally on this matter.

The Minister of Justice may request the Cassation Public Prosecutor to undertake prosecutions concerning offences of which news comes to his knowledge.

The latter shall, where necessary, have the right to conduct the investigation directly or through his assistants among the judges of the Public Prosecution attached to him or the members of the Judicial Police subordinate to him, without having the right to bring charges.

The Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation may supervise the officers of the Judicial Police within the scope of the acts they perform in their capacity as auxiliaries of the Public Prosecution. He may address to their superiors such observations as he deems fit regarding their aforementioned acts, and may request the Appellate Public Prosecutor, the Financial Public Prosecutor, or the Government Commissioner at the Military Court to bring charges against any of them who commits a criminal offence during the performance of his duties or in the course of performing them, without requesting permission to prosecute him.

The ordinary judiciary shall have jurisdiction to hear this offence notwithstanding any provision to the contrary.

Each of the Appellate Public Prosecutor, the Financial Public Prosecutor, the Government Commissioner before the Military Court, the Director General of the Internal Security Forces, the Director General of General Security, and the Director General of State Security shall notify the Public Prosecutor before the Court of Cassation of the serious offences of which they have become aware and shall abide by his directives in respect thereof.

He may examine the investigation file handled by one of the Investigating Judges and request the competent Public Prosecutor to submit the requisition that accords with his written directives.

He may address a warning to one of the judges of the Public Prosecution by reason of any neglect in his work that he attributes to him, or propose to the Judicial Inspection Authority that he be referred before the Disciplinary Council.

The Public Prosecutor before the Court of Cassation shall undertake the following functions:

a - Requesting the cassation of criminal judgments and decisions in accordance with the procedures specified in this Law.

b - Requesting the determination of jurisdiction and requesting the transfer of an action from one court to another.

c - Prosecuting offences referred to the Judicial Council.

d - Prosecuting offences committed by judges, whether arising out of office or outside thereof.

e - Representing the Public Prosecution before the Court of Cassation and the Judicial Council.

f - Preparing extradition files and referring them to the Minister of Justice accompanied by his reports.

g - Drawing up a detailed report to be attached to the file of a person sentenced to death upon its referral to the Special Pardon Committee.

h - All other duties and powers mentioned in this Law and in others.

The appointment of the Financial Public Prosecutor shall take place by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice.

The Financial Public Prosecutor shall enjoy, within the limits of the duties specified for him in this Law, the powers vested in the Cassation Public Prosecutor.

The Financial Public Prosecutor shall undertake the duties of prosecution in the following offences:

(a) Offences arising from the violation of the provisions of the laws on taxes and duties in the various public utilities, public institutions and municipalities, including state and municipal taxes, customs duties, and wired and wireless telecommunications fees.

(b) Offences arising from the violation of laws on banking, financial institutions and the stock exchange, in particular those provided for in the Code of Money and Credit.

(c) Offences arising from the violation of laws on joint-stock companies and offences of multinational companies.

(d) Offences that undermine the financial standing of the State or Lebanese or foreign banknotes in circulation by law or custom in Lebanon, and offences of counterfeiting, falsifying and uttering currency, public bonds, stamps and stamped papers.

(e) Offences of embezzlement of public funds.

(f) Offences of bankruptcy.

Prosecution shall not take place in banking offences resulting from the violation of the Code of Money and Credit except upon a written request from the Governor of the Bank of Lebanon.

Prosecution shall not take place in violations relating to customs duties except upon a written request from the Director General of Customs.

In cases where the competent administration is entitled to conclude a settlement with the defendant, the public prosecution action shall lapse if the settlement takes place before the judgment is rendered.

The execution of the penalty shall be stayed if the settlement takes place thereafter, unless a contrary legal text provides otherwise.

The Financial Public Prosecutor shall exercise his powers provided for in this Law under the supervision of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation, within the procedures and rules applied by the Appellate Public Prosecutor and defined in this Law and in the financial laws.

These powers shall cover all Lebanese territory.
