The decisions of the judge entrusted with the investigation shall be appealed before the body provided for in Article 350 of this Law in accordance with the procedures followed in appealing the decisions of the investigating judge.

The Judicial Council shall be composed of the First President of the Court of Cassation as President and four judges from the Court of Cassation as members, appointed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice and the approval of the Supreme Judicial Council.

One or more additional judges shall be appointed in the decree to replace a titular member in the event of his death, recusal, disqualification, or termination of service.

The Public Prosecution before the Judicial Council shall be represented by the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation or whomever he delegates from among his assistants.
If the First President of the Court of Cassation is unable to preside over the panel of the Council, the highest-ranking appointed member shall assume its presidency.

The Judicial Council shall convene at the Palace of Justice in Beirut, or at the place where the offence was committed when necessary, or at any other place designated by its President if it is impossible for it to convene at the Palace of Justice in Beirut.

The Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation, or whomever he delegates from among the Advocates General at the Public Prosecution of Cassation, shall assume the duties of initiating and exercising the public action.

The investigation shall be conducted by a judge appointed by the Minister of Justice upon the approval of the Supreme Judicial Council.
The Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation shall bring the charge for the offence before the Judicial Investigator and refer the investigation file to him.

The Judicial Investigator may issue all warrants required by the investigation without a request from the Public Prosecution.

His decisions in this regard shall not be subject to any form of recourse.

He shall be seized of the action in rem.

If the investigation reveals the existence of a participant in the offence, he shall interrogate him as a defendant even if his name was not included among those charged by the Public Prosecution. The Public Prosecution may subsequently bring charges against a person whom it omitted in its original claim, and the Investigator shall interrogate him as a defendant.

Subject to the provisions of the preceding Article, the Judicial Investigator shall apply the procedures followed before the Investigating Judge, with the exception of the period of detention provided for in Article 108 of this Law.

The Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation may inspect the case file and submit whateversubmissions or requests he deems appropriate. The injured party may bring his civil action accessory to the public action.

If any of the President of the Supreme Judicial Council, the President of the State Council, the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation, the President of the Court of Audit, or the President of the Judicial Inspection Board commits an offence of the category of misdemeanour or felony outside his office or during or on the occasion of the performance thereof, he shall be tried before a judicial panel composed of five judges appointed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice.

The members of the panel shall be chosen from among serving judges or retired judges in an honorary position, provided that the grade of none of them is less than the seventeenth.

The Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation shall personally undertake the prosecution unless he is one of those who committed the offence or contributed thereto, in which case a judge whose grade is not less than the seventeenth shall be appointed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers to perform the duties of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation to undertake the prosecution in the offence only.

The Minister of Justice shall, after the approval of the Supreme Judicial Council, appoint the judge who will be entrusted with the investigation into the offence from a grade not less than the grade of the judge referred before him.

The procedures provided for in Articles 345 et seq. shall apply to the prosecution and trial of those aforementioned.

The President of the appointed judicial panel shall undertake the duties of the First President of the Court of Cassation in the matter of approving the detention of the defendant judge.
Actions shall be referred to the Judicial Council pursuant to a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.

The Judicial Council shall hear the following offences:

a - Offences provided for in Articles 270 et seq. up to and including Article 336 of the Penal Code.

b - Offences provided for in the Law of 11/01/1958.

c - All offences resulting from transactions of arms and equipment concluded or to be concluded by the Ministry of National Defence and offences connected therewith or branching therefrom, in particular those provided for in Articles 351 up to and including 366 of the Penal Code, in Articles 376, 377 and 378 thereof, in Articles 453 up to and including 472 thereof, and in Articles 138 and 141 of the Code of Military Justice.

Actions relating to these offences which are pending before the military and ordinary courts shall be referred to the Judicial Council, whose jurisdiction covers civilians and military personnel alike, in execution of the referral decree.

Upon the completion of the investigations, the Cassation Public Prosecution shall submit its submissions on the merits.

The Judicial Investigator shall decide, as a result of his examination of the investigations and the case file, either to bar the trial of the defendant or to indict him and refer him to the Judicial Council. The decision of indictment issued by the Judicial Investigator shall observe the procedures governing the drawing up of the bill of indictment by the Indictment Chamber.

The Judicial Investigator must issue a warrant of arrest against the accused.

If he omits to issue it, he must, at the request of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation, issue it even after he has been divested of the case.

If he has died or it is impossible for him to do so, the President of the Judicial Council must issue a warrant of arrest against the accused upon the commencement of his trial.

The Cassation Public Prosecution shall serve, five days prior to the date of the hearing, upon each of the accused a copy of the decision of indictment and of the list of witnesses for the public prosecution. The accused shall serve upon the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation, five days prior to the date of the hearing, the list of witnesses for the defence.

The civil party may submit within the same period a list of his witnesses, a copy of which shall be served upon each of the Cassation Public Prosecution and the accused five days prior to the date of the hearing.

The trial before the Judicial Council, whether in presence or in absentia, shall be conducted in accordance with the trial procedures before the Criminal Court.

The Council shall issue its judgment in accordance with the same procedures.

The judgments of the Judicial Council shall not be subject to any ordinary or extraordinary means of recourse, with the exception of opposition and retrial.

The Judicial Council is the competent authority to hear an application for retrial in respect of judgments issued by it.

The Judicial Council may, at the request of the Cassation Public Prosecution or of its own motion, conduct a supplementary investigation in the case with its full bench or through one of its members whom it delegates for this purpose.
The competence of the criminal judge seised of the public action shall include deciding upon every plea raised before him, unless it constitutes a prejudicial question or the law provides otherwise.

The following shall be considered prejudicial questions requiring a stay of proceedings:

A - Matters of real property ownership and other real property rights in rem.

B - Matters of nationality.

C - Matters of personal status, with the exception of the determination of age.

D - Administrative matters.

E - Civil matters the determination of which affects the extent to which the elements of the alleged offence are established, provided that they are pending before the civil authority prior to the initiation of the public action.

F - Criminal matters upon the determination of which depends the verification of the extent to which the elements of the offence are met.

The criminal judge shall, when a preliminary question is raised before him, verify, before staying the examination of the action of which he is seised, whether it is serious and whether the determination thereof is necessary and requisite for the determination of the criminal action. If the criminal judge decides to accept the plea of the preliminary question, he shall fix a time-limit for seizing the competent judiciary.

If the party who raised the plea complies with the time-limit fixed for him, the criminal judge shall stay the examination of the action until the determination of the preliminary question.

If he fails to do so, he shall proceed with the action.

Staying the examination of the action shall not prevent the criminal judge from taking necessary or urgent measures and investigations.

The investigating judge may decide to hear the testimony of a person who holds information, in the capacity of a witness, without the record containing the identity of the person heard, where the following two conditions are met:

1 - The offence of trafficking in persons, which is the subject of the investigation, is punishable by felony penalties of not less than detention for a period of five years.

2 - It is feared that giving information regarding the offence would entail a threat to the life or safety of the person heard, his family, or one of his relatives by marriage.

The decision must be reasoned and must contain the factual and material grounds upon which it was based for its issuance.

The identity and address of the person shall be recorded in a special record, which shall not be joined to the case file, and which shall be deposited and kept with the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation.

The defendant may request the judge seised of the case to disclose the identity of the person heard in accordance with the provisions of the preceding Article, where he considers that this measure is essential for the exercise of the rights of the defence.

The judge shall decide, if it appears to him that the conditions of the request are met, either to disclose the identity, subject to the consent of the person concerned thereto, or to annul the record drawn up in accordance with the provisions of Article 370 (2).

The defendant may request a confrontation with the person heard in accordance with the provisions of Article 370 (2), and in such case it shall be for the judge to decide to make use of technical means that render the voice of that person unidentifiable.

The details of the application of the provisions of this Article shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice.

Related text: (Determining the details of the application of the provisions of item 4 of Article 370 of the Code of Criminal Procedure)
Incrimination may not be based solely on the testimony of the person heard in accordance with the provisions of Article 370 (2).

Any person who discloses information concerning the protection measures provided for in this Section shall be punished by imprisonment from two years to three years and by a fine from twenty million to thirty million Lebanese pounds.

When the Public Prosecutor learns of the existence of a document in one of the official departments that is suspected of being forged, he shall proceed in person or delegate one of his assistants to carry out the necessary formalities to inspect it and verify its forgery.

He may also order the transfer of the suspected documents to his department.

The perpetrator of the forgery and his accomplices shall be prosecuted before the Investigating Judge.

When the Investigating Judge is seised of the action, he shall instruct his clerk to draw up a detailed record in which he describes the document suspected of being forged. The Investigating Judge and the clerk shall sign the record and shall also sign the document under the phrase "ne varietur".

The suspected document and the record shall be kept in the investigation department.

If the document alleged to be forged is in one of the official departments, the responsible head of department therein shall sign it before its transfer to the investigation department.

He shall be obliged to hand it over to it immediately upon being notified of the decision of the Investigating Judge.

If he abstains from doing so, the Investigating Judge shall issue a decision to bring him accompanied by the document.

If it appears to the Investigating Judge that there is no legitimate reason for his abstention from handing over the document, he shall sentence him to a fine ranging between two hundred thousand and one million pounds.

The provision of this Article shall apply to an ordinary person who possesses the document suspected of being forged.

When an official document is brought in, a true copy thereof certified by the Investigating Judge and his clerk shall be left with the person with whom it was deposited.

If the document was deposited with a public official, the true copy thereof shall stand in place of the original until it is returned to him.

This official may issue copies of the certified copy, indicating that its original is deposited with the Investigating Judge for the purpose of verifying its forgery.

If the document is a sheet in a register from which it cannot be detached, the Investigating Judge may decide to bring the register into his department.

The forgery of documents may be alleged even if they have been used in judicial, administrative or other transactions.

Any person who invokes a document suspected of being forged shall be obliged to sign it.

This document shall be deposited in the safe of deposits at the court, endorsed with the phrase "ne varietur".

The Investigating Judge may seek the assistance of technical expertise to compare the handwriting and signature appearing in the document suspected of being forged with such authentic signatures or writings as may be available. He may take a handwriting sample from the defendant directly or through experts; if he refuses, that shall be recorded in the record of his interrogation.

Where the original copy of a judgment is stolen, lost or destroyed before its execution, or where the documents of the action or the investigation, in whole or in part, are stolen, lost or destroyed before a decision is rendered therein, the procedures prescribed in the following Articles shall be followed.

Where a duly certified official copy of the judgment or decision is found, it shall take the place of the original copy and be kept in its stead.

Where the certified copy is in the possession of a public official or any other person, the President of the court that rendered the judgment or decision shall decide to compel him to deliver it to the registry of the court.

Should he refuse, the provisions of Article 373 of this Law shall apply to him.

The person from whom the certified copy was taken may request to be delivered a true copy without bearing any expenses.

The loss of the original copy of a judgment or decision shall not entail the conduct of a new trial once the means of recourse against it have been exhausted. An extract of the decision shall suffice where it is not possible to obtain a certified official copy thereof.

Where the documents of the action or the investigation, in whole or in part, are lost before a decision is rendered therein, the investigation shall be repeated wholly or partially.

Where the action is pending before the court, it shall undertake to conduct such investigation therein as it deems fit.

Where the action is lost in its entirety, the file shall be reconstituted in accordance with the rules of procedure.

Where the original of the judgment or decision is lost and neither a certified official copy thereof nor an extract thereof nor a certified copy of such extract is found, but the committal order or bill of indictment is found, a trial shall be conducted and a new judgment shall be rendered.

Where the file of the action does not contain the committal order or bill of indictment and no certified official copy of either of them is found, the proceedings shall be repeated starting from the lost part of the documents.

Where the documents of the action or the investigation, in whole or in part, are lost and the original copy of the contested judgment or decision is available or there exists a certified official copy of either of them, and the action is pending before the Court of Cassation, the procedures shall not be repeated unless the appeal addresses the trial procedures.

In the event that the decision is quashed, the ordinary rules of procedure provided for in the preceding Articles shall apply.

The Supreme Judicial Council shall be vested with the jurisdiction to examine petitions for special pardon submitted by persons sentenced to the death penalty by a final and binding judgment, or referred to it by the competent authorities.

A petition for a special pardon from the death penalty shall be submitted to the President of the Republic directly or through the Minister of Justice by way of an application signed by the convicted person, his counsel or a member of his family.

The application shall be exempt from stamp duty and judicial fees.

Private documents may serve as a basis for collation, matching and comparison if the claimant and the defendant agree upon them. Where the holder thereof is not a public official, the provisions of Article 373 of this Law shall apply to compel him to hand them over.

Investigations in forgery actions shall be conducted in accordance with the procedures followed in respect of all other offences.

Both the Public Prosecutor and the Investigating Judge may enter the residences of persons suspected of counterfeiting the official seals of the State and forging its coins, banknotes and fiscal stamps, or of introducing such counterfeited or forged items into Lebanese territory, or of acting as intermediaries in their circulation, even if the residences of such persons lie outside the territorial jurisdiction of either of them.
The Public Prosecution and all other parties may, at any stage of the proceedings, challenge a document produced in the case on the ground of forgery.

An incidental claim of forgery shall be filed with the registry of the court seized of the action.

The claimant must specify the document alleged to be forged and the evidence thereof.

The court seized of the action shall refer the incidental claim to the Public Prosecution for its submission and may stay the proceedings in the principal action until the competent judicial authority rules upon the incidental forgery action, provided that the determination of the principal action depends upon the outcome of the incidental action.

Where the principal action brought before it is limited to personal damages, it shall adjourn the hearing thereof until judgment is rendered in the forgery action.

Where a final decision is rendered finding that no forgery exists, the court that stayed the proceedings in the principal action by reason of the incidental claim of forgery shall sentence the claimant in the forgery claim to a fine ranging between five hundred thousand and one million pounds, in addition to damages.

Where a private document is adjudged to be forged, the court shall order its annulment and destruction.

Where an official document is adjudged to be wholly or partially forged, the court deciding the forgery action shall order that the effect of the document be annulled or that it be restored to its original state by striking out what was added to it or by reinstating what was deleted from it.

In such case, a summary of the court's judgment shall be appended to the foot of the document.

The documents used as a basis for collation and matching shall be returned to their sources.
The same procedures applicable to a principal forgery action shall apply to an incidental forgery action.
Places of detention and prisons shall be defined and regulated by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.

The Appellate or Financial Public Prosecutor, the Investigating Judge, and the Criminal Single Judge shall each inspect, once a month, the persons held in the places of detention and prisons falling under their respective jurisdictions.

- Each of them may order the officials in charge of the places of detention and prisons falling within the scope of his work to take the measures required by the investigation and trial.

The Appellate or Financial Public Prosecutor and the Criminal Single Judge, each within the limits of his jurisdiction, upon receiving notice of the unlawful detention of any person, shall release him after verifying the unlawfulness of his custody.

If it appears to any of them that there is a lawful cause warranting detention, he shall immediately send the detainee to the competent judicial authority and draw up a record of the facts.

If any of them neglects to act in accordance with the foregoing, he shall be prosecuted disciplinarily.

The execution of final criminal judgments rendered by the Criminal Courts, the Courts of Appeal, and the Court of Cassation shall be carried out by the Public Prosecutor at the court that rendered the judgment. The Criminal Single Judge shall carry out the execution of the judgments rendered by him.

The execution of judgment extracts shall be secured pursuant to a written order to the Internal Security Forces.
The provisions of Articles 53 et seq. up to Article 65 inclusive of the Penal Code, and Articles 112 up to 117 inclusive thereof, shall apply to the execution of criminal judgments.

The day on which execution begins shall be counted as part of the term of the penalty.

The convicted person shall be released on the day on which the term of the penalty expires. - If the term of the sentence of imprisonment imposed is twenty-four hours, its execution shall expire on the day following the commencement of execution.

The execution of the term of a penalty involving deprivation or restriction of liberty shall commence from the day the convicted person is arrested in enforcement of the judgment rendered against him, with the period of his detention being deducted therefrom.

If the accused or the defendant is acquitted of the offence for which he was detained, the period of detention must be deducted from the term to which he is sentenced for any other offence he may have committed prior to or during his detention.

Where there are multiple penalties involving deprivation or restriction of liberty imposed upon the defendant or the accused, the deduction of the period of detention shall be made from the lighter penalty first.

When a death sentence becomes final, the Minister of Justice shall refer the case file, accompanied by the report of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation, to the Supreme Judicial Council, which shall give its opinion on executing the penalty or commuting it to another within ten days at most.

The President of the Supreme Judicial Council, or any member of the Council whom he delegates, shall draw up a brief report on the facts of the case, the evidence upon which the judgment was based, the grounds for the petition for pardon, and his opinion on the petition.

After hearing the statement of its rapporteur and examining the documents, the Supreme Judicial Council shall consider the charge brought against the convicted person, the evidence upon which the judgment rested, and the grounds for the petition for pardon or the requirements of the death penalty or commuting it to another, and shall give its opinion in secret on rejecting the petition or accepting it with a recommendation to commute the death penalty to another, and shall draw up a report which it shall submit to the Minister of Justice.

The Supreme Judicial Council shall form a committee of three of its members to examine all other petitions for special pardon.

The committee may, in accordance with the procedures set forth above, decide on petitions for pardon in respect of judgments imposing felony penalties other than death or misdemeanour penalties.

Upon the submission of a petition for pardon, the execution of a final judgment shall be stayed where it imposes a fine or imprisonment of less than one year, provided that the convicted person is not in custody, pursuant to a notice sent by the chairman of the committee to the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation confirming that the committee has received the petition for pardon.

If the President of the Republic rejects the petition for pardon, a person sentenced to hard labour for life or for a term of at least ten years may not renew his petition before the expiry of three years in the first case, and two years in the second case, from the date on which he is notified of the rejection decision.

He may renew the petition for pardon after the expiry of one year in other cases.

He may not petition for pardon a second time if the judgment imposes a fine or imprisonment for a term of one year or less. However, this shall not preclude the President of the Republic from exercising his right to order that the new petition for pardon be referred to the committee.
If the President of the Republic grants the petition for pardon, he shall issue a decree to that effect.

Decisions ordering remand in custody shall be executed by placing the persons ordered to be remanded in custody in places of detention.

Convicted persons shall be imprisoned and the judgments rendered against them shall be executed by placing them in prisons.
If the convicted woman is pregnant, the execution of her penalty shall be postponed until the expiry of a period of ten weeks from delivery.
If a person sentenced to a penalty depriving or restricting liberty is afflicted with an illness that threatens his life with danger, his penalty may be executed in the prison hospital.

If a person sentenced to a penalty depriving or restricting liberty is afflicted with insanity or a serious mental illness, the Public Prosecution may order that he be placed in one of the hospitals designated for mental illnesses.

The period that he spends in the hospital shall be deducted from the term of the penalty to which he was sentenced.

If his illness continues, the provisions of the law relating to mental patients shall apply to him.

A detainee shall be released upon the issuance of a judgment declaring acquittal, or annulling the prosecutions, or imposing a penalty the execution of which does not require imprisonment, or upon the issuance of a judgment suspending the execution of the penalty, or if the detainee has spent in his preventive detention the term of the penalty to which he was sentenced.

If personal damages, judicial expenses, and a fine are awarded, and the property of the convicted person is not sufficient for all of that, the following priority must be followed in execution.

a - Personal damages.

b - Judicial expenses.

c - The fine.

Personal damages awarded, as well as the legal fees and expenses advanced by him, shall be executed, upon the request of the civil claimant, in accordance with the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure.

A person sentenced to pay judicial expenses must pay them to the State Treasury Fund within a period of ten days from the date of being served notice after the judgment becomes final.

If he fails to pay, the Public Prosecutor shall decide to imprison him for a period of twenty-four hours for each ten thousand pounds.

The period of imprisonment may not exceed six months, nor may the convicted person be imprisoned in lieu of judicial expenses if he was a minor when the offence was committed.

If the period of detention of the defendant exceeds the penalty of imprisonment to which he was sentenced, the equivalent thereof shall be deducted from the fine and the judicial expenses awarded in accordance with the rate of substitution referred to above.
The rule of apportionment set forth in Article 53 of the Penal Code shall apply to judicial expenses.

It is prohibited to publish any statement in the newspapers relating to the execution of the death penalty other than the minutes referred to in the preceding Article.

Every violation of this prohibition shall expose its perpetrator to the penalty provided for in Article 420 of the Penal Code.
The court becomes functus officio in respect of the action when it renders its judgment therein.

Where a purely material error, whether clerical or arithmetical, occurs in the judgment or in the decision issued by one of the judicial authorities, that authority may rectify the error of its own motion or upon the request of one of the parties to the action.

The rectification shall be ordered in the Deliberation Chamber, and the rectification issued shall be entered in the margin of the judgment or decision.

The court that rendered the judgment shall have jurisdiction to examine an application for its interpretation.

It shall rule thereon after seeking the opinion of the Public Prosecution.
The Code of Criminal Procedure promulgated on 18/09/1948 and its amendments are hereby repealed, as are all legislative provisions and texts contrary to or inconsistent with this Law.
This Law shall enter into force upon the expiry of three months from its publication in the Official Gazette.

The urgent draft law referred to the Chamber of Deputies pursuant to Decree No. 5070 dated 8/4/1982 aiming to amend certain provisions of Legislative Decrees No. 111 and 112 dated 12/6/1959 and to authorise the filling of vacant positions in certain posts of the establishments of public administrations from among the permanent, temporary and contracted employees and wage-earners working therein, the text of which follows, is hereby put into effect:
This Decree shall be published and notified where needed, and shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The following shall be added to the text of Paragraph 3 of Article 5 of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6/1959: And if only the month of birth is known, he shall be deemed to have been born on the fifteenth of the month of his birth.

First: The text of the first paragraph of Article 8 of Legislative Decree No. 111 dated 12/6/1959 is hereby repealed and replaced by the following text: The Board of the Civil Service Council shall lay down the regulations and subjects of competitive examinations after consulting the competent ministries. These regulations may provide for the granting of additional marks not exceeding fifteen percent of the total marks to candidates holding degrees higher than the required minimum, and ten percent to employees who have ten years or more in service, provided that these marks are given when ranking the order of success, to those who pass the competitive examination.

Second: The text of Paragraph 7 of Article 8 of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6/1959 is hereby repealed and replaced by the following text: The results of the competitive examination or examination shall be announced, immediately upon their occurrence, on the door of the Civil Service Council, and the list of successful candidates shall remain valid for a period of two years only from the date of its announcement, and this list shall have priority for two years over the list that follows it. The list of successful candidates shall exhaust its effect upon the expiry of the two-year period.
If the convicted person serves the term of imprisonment into which the fine and the judicial costs were commuted, the debt owed to the Treasury shall be extinguished.

If the convicted person is imprisoned in satisfaction of the fine and the judicial costs and expresses his wish while in prison to discharge his debt towards the State, the Public Prosecutor or the person acting in his stead shall order that he be brought out of prison and brought before him to pay the sums due after deducting the amount corresponding to the period he spent in imprisonment.

If, upon his arrest, the convicted person pays the full amount required of him, he shall be released immediately and the decision commuting the fine and the judicial costs into imprisonment shall become null and void.

Upon the death, escape or loss of legal capacity of the convicted person, the judicial costs and the fine shall be recovered through the Ministry of Finance in the same manner as public funds are recovered.

A sentence of death shall not be executed except after seeking the opinion of the Pardon Committee and obtaining the approval of the President of the Republic.

The sentence shall be executed pursuant to a decree specifying the place and means of execution. The execution of a sentence of death is prohibited on Sundays, Fridays, and national and religious holidays.

A sentence of death against a pregnant woman shall not be executed until ten weeks have elapsed after her delivery.

The execution of the sentence of death shall take place in the presence of the persons mentioned below:

a - The President of the chamber that rendered the judgment. Where he is unable to attend, the First President of the Court of Cassation shall designate a judge for this purpose.

b - The Public Prosecutor before the court that rendered the judgment, or one of his deputies.

c - A judge of the civil court of first instance within whose jurisdiction the place of execution falls.

d - The clerk of the court that rendered the judgment.

e The advocate of the convicted person.

f- A clergyman of the religious denomination to which the convicted person belongs.

g- The director of the prison.

h - The Commander of the Judicial Police in Beirut or whomever he delegates, or the commander of the Gendarmerie company within whose jurisdiction the place of execution falls or whomever he delegates.

i - The prison physician or the forensic physician in the district.

The civil judge, referred to in paragraph (c) of the preceding Article, shall ask the convicted person whether he has anything he wishes to say or state before the execution of the sentence against him.

This shall be recorded in a special record which he shall sign together with his clerk.

The clerk of the court that rendered the judgment shall draw up a record of the execution of the death sentence, which shall be signed by those mentioned in paragraphs (a), (b) and (d) of Article 421 of this Law at the place where the execution was carried out.

A copy of this record shall be posted for a period of twenty-four hours at the place of execution of the sentence. The clerk shall transcribe the record of the execution of the sentence at the foot of the original judgment kept with the court.

First: The text of paragraph 3 of Article 10 of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6/1959 is repealed and replaced by the following text: Probationers shall be confirmed in appointment by a decision of the Minister after the approval of the Board of the Civil Service Council. The effect of confirmation shall be deemed valid as from the date of expiry of the probation period referred to in the first paragraph of this Article.

Second: The text of paragraph 4 of Article 10 of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6/1959 is repealed and replaced by the following text: The authority vested with the power to appoint probationers shall dismiss them before the expiry of the probation period or at the end thereof after the approval of the Central Inspection Administration, and in this case the probationer shall not be entitled to any dismissal indemnity for the period spent in service, and the effect of dismissal shall be deemed valid as from the date of notification thereof or from the date of actual cessation of work if that occurred prior to notification.

The following is added to the text of the first paragraph of Article 11 of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6/1959: Exemption from the training course requirement may be granted for exceptional reasons to be assessed jointly by the Boards of the Civil Service Council and the Central Inspection, provided that the exemption is coupled with the approval of the Council of Ministers.

The text of the first paragraph of Article 43 of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6/1959 is repealed and replaced by the following text: Transfer from one post to another, within the same cadre and the same administration, shall take place after consulting the opinion of the Civil Service Council:

A- By a decree for employees of the Second Category

B - By a decision of the Minister for employees of the Third Category.

C- By a decision of the Director General for employees of the Fourth and Fifth Categories.

The transfer of members of the public teaching staff shall be exempted from consulting the opinion of the Civil Service Council.

First: The text of paragraph 6 of Article 44 of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6/1959 is repealed and replaced by the following text:

- An acting official may not be appointed for a period exceeding one year.

- The acting appointment may be renewed in the same manner.

Second: The following two new paragraphs 7 and 8 are added to the text of Article 44 of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6/1959:

7- An employee may not be appointed to more than one post.

8- Where necessary, and by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers, common rules may be established for acting appointments in the various posts of public administrations.

The text of paragraph 2 of Article 47 of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6/1959 is repealed and replaced by the following text: A technical employee may be seconded from one ministry to another ministry, after the approval of the two competent ministries. Secondment shall be decided by the authority which has the right of appointment.

The texts of paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 of Article 50 of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6/1959 are repealed and replaced by the following texts:

1- An employee may be temporarily placed outside the cadre for the purpose of attaching him to one of the public administrations, public institutions, municipalities, Lebanese mixed-economy companies, international organisations or states.

2- An employee temporarily placed outside the cadre shall cease to receive his salaries, and shall retain his right to advancement within his cadre and his right to a pension or dismissal indemnity. Employees placed outside the cadre for the purpose of attaching them to a public administration, public institution, municipality or Lebanese mixed-economy company shall not be entitled to receive, upon the termination of their service therein, any retirement pension or dismissal indemnity from its budget in respect of their services therein.

3- An employee of Category Three and below shall be temporarily placed outside the cadre upon his request by a decision of the Minister after the approval of the Board of the Civil Service Council specifying the duration of placement outside the cadre. The administration shall have the right to revoke this measure at any time in the same manner. As for employees of Categories One and Two, their placement outside the cadre shall be effected by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers after the approval of the Board of the Civil Service Council.

The text of paragraph 51 of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6/1959 is repealed and replaced by the following text: An employee placed outside the cadre shall be reinstated to his original post if it is still vacant by a decision of the authority which has the right of placement outside the cadre, after the approval of the Board of the Civil Service Council, and if such post is not vacant, he shall be assigned by the authority competent for appointment a post equivalent to it in category, or he shall be offered a lower post while retaining his original salary. If he refuses this latter post, he shall be placed on retirement or dismissed from service.

The text of paragraph 2 of Article 52 of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6/1959 is repealed and replaced by the following text: An employee of Category Two and below shall be placed on availability by a decision of the Minister after the approval of the Board of the Civil Service Council. As for employees of Category One, their placement on availability shall be effected by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers after the approval of the Board of the Civil Service Council.

The provisions of the second Clause of Paragraph 2 of Article 50 of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6/1959, added pursuant to the Eighth Article of this Law, shall apply to municipal civil servants and employees of public institutions placed outside the cadre or in any similar status for the purpose of attaching them to a public administration, a public institution, a municipality, or a Lebanese mixed-economy company.

The text of Paragraph 2 of Article 2 of Legislative Decree No. 111 dated 12/6/1959 is repealed and replaced with the following text: Directorates General, Directorates, and Services shall be established, amended, and abolished by a law. Departments and Sections shall be established, amended, and abolished, and the special conditions of appointment to their posts shall be determined, by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers, upon the proposal of the competent Minister, and after the approval of the Civil Service Board and the investigation of the Research and Guidance Administration.

The text of the Third Article of Legislative Decree No. 111 dated 12/6/1959 is repealed and replaced with the following text: The cadres of Directorates General, Directorates, and Services shall be determined, amended, and abolished by a special law. The cadres of Departments and Sections shall be determined, amended, and abolished by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, upon the proposal of the competent Minister and after the approval of the Civil Service Board and the investigation of the Research and Guidance Administration.

The Government may, pursuant to decrees issued upon the proposal of the termination of the Civil Service and the proposal of the competent Minister:

1- Fill the vacant technical positions in the Third Category from among the permanent and temporary civil servants, contracted personnel, and wage earners working in the public administrations on the date of entry into force of this Law and who meet the general and special conditions of appointment with the exception of the age condition, provided that they successfully pass a competition on the basis of qualifications restricted to them, organised by the Civil Service Board for this purpose in accordance with the legal and regulatory provisions in force.

2- Fill up to fifty percent of the vacant positions in the Third Category not mentioned in the first paragraph from among the permanent and temporary civil servants, contracted personnel, and wage earners working in the public administrations on the date of entry into force of this Law and who meet the general and special conditions of appointment with the exception of the age condition, provided that they successfully pass a competition restricted to them, organised by the Civil Service Board for this purpose in accordance with the legal and regulatory provisions in force. The designations of the Third Category positions subject to this competition shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Board of the Civil Service Board.

3- Fill the vacant positions in the Fourth Category from among the permanent and temporary civil servants, contracted personnel, and wage earners working in the public administrations on the date of entry into force of this Law and who meet the general and special conditions of appointment with the exception of the age condition, provided that they successfully pass a competition restricted to them, organised by the Civil Service Board for this purpose in accordance with the legal and regulatory provisions in force.

4- Fill the vacant positions in the Fifth Category from among the temporary civil servants, contracted personnel, and wage earners working in the public administrations on the date of entry into force of this Law and who meet the general and special conditions of appointment with the exception of the age condition, provided that they successfully pass a competition restricted to them, organised by the Civil Service Board for this purpose in accordance with the legal and regulatory provisions in force.

Temporary civil servants, contracted personnel, and wage earners who have spent a period of ten years in service in the public administrations shall have the right to participate in the qualifying competition to occupy the vacant positions in the Fourth and Fifth Categories, whatever the degrees and qualifications required for appointment to these positions may be. The designations of the technical positions covered by the provisions of this Article shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, upon the proposal of the Board of the Civil Service Board.

Article 55 of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6/1959 is amended as follows:

Second Degree: 5- Termination of service. Instead of: 5- Dismissal from service. (The remainder remains unamended).

The following new paragraphs 3, 4 and 5 shall be added to the text of Article 68 of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6/1959:

3- Placement on retirement or dismissal from service shall take place by a decision of the Board of the Civil Service Council, after consulting the opinion of the competent administration and the Ministry of Finance.

4- A civil servant whose service has ended due to reaching the legal age or completing the legal period in service shall cease work by operation of law. If he continues to work, no wage, salary, compensation or fee shall be due to him for the services he performs after reaching the age limit or the limit of the legal period of service, and he shall be subject to penal prosecution.

5- It shall not be permissible to contract with a civil servant placed on retirement or dismissed from service due to reaching the legal age provided for in this Legislative Decree or completing in service the maximum period for the end of service provided for in this Legislative Decree, nor shall it be permissible to employ him to work in any public administration, public institution or municipality.

First: The following shall be added to the text of Article 69 of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6/1959: A civil servant whose actual services in the permanent cadres have reached twenty-five years at least may request his dismissal from service or his placement on retirement, and the Government in the Council of Ministers shall accept or reject this request. The acceptance of the request shall be formalized by a decree.

All provisions contrary to this text or inconsistent with its content are repealed from Article 69. Second: The following shall be added to the text of the fourth Article of the Law put into effect by Decree No. 7881 dated 27/7/1967 (amending certain provisions of Legislative Decrees No. 112, 119 and 134 dated 12/6/1959 and certain other provisions relating to civil servants): A married female civil servant shall have the right to request the termination of her service at any time. Her rights (retirement pension dismissal) shall be liquidated in accordance with the laws and regulations in force.
The phrase "or removal from office" appearing at the end of paragraph 2 of Article 85 of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6/1959 shall be deleted.

Where necessary, the rules and conditions of contracting in public administrations, public institutions and municipalities effected pursuant to Article 87 of the Civil Servants Regulations shall be determined by decrees taken in the Council of Ministers after the approval of the Board of the Civil Service Council.

1- A general statute for hired workers shall be established in all public administrations, public institutions and municipalities.

2- The aforementioned statute shall cover all matters common to hired workers in all public administrations, public institutions and municipalities, in particular:

- The definition of hired workers.

- The types of hired workers.

- The procedures and conditions for employing hired workers.

- The determination of the titles of hired workers, provided that they have no equivalents in the cadres of public administrations, public institutions and municipalities.

- The determination of working duration and hours.

- The determination of leaves of all kinds.

- The determination of wages, allowances and allocations.

- The determination of transfer provisions.

- The determination of disciplinary provisions.

- The determination of provisions for the termination of service of the hired worker.

- And generally all that is required to safeguard the general conditions of hired workers.

3- The general statute shall be approved by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.

4- Each public administration, public institution and municipality shall establish a special statute for hired workers addressing the specific conditions of each of them separately, in addition to the other matters assigned to it by the general statute for hired workers.

The special statute shall be issued by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the competent Minister after the approval of the Board of the Civil Service Council in the light of an investigation conducted by the Research and Guidance Administration for this purpose, and the statute of each public administration, public institution or municipality shall include the determination of the number of hired workers therein.

The employment of hired workers in all public administrations, public institutions and municipalities, whatever the form of employment, including employment by invoice, shall be prohibited except within the limits of the number specified for each administration pursuant to its statute for hired workers.
The details of application of this Law shall be determined, where necessary, by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers.
Subject to the provisions issued by special laws, all provisions contrary to this Law or inconsistent with its content are hereby repealed.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette

Single Article: The proposed law on the organisation of the Internal Security Forces, as amended by the Joint Parliamentary Committees and as amended by the Chamber of Deputies in its Articles: 13 - 18 - 19 - 20 - 21 - 22, is hereby approved. This law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication.

The Internal Security Forces are armed public forces whose jurisdiction extends over all Lebanese territories and the territorial waters and airspace appertaining thereto. Their duties are defined as follows:

1- In the field of the Administrative Police:

a- Maintaining order and consolidating security.

b - Ensuring public tranquility.

c- Protecting persons and property.

d- Protecting liberties within the framework of the law.

e- Ensuring the enforcement of the laws and regulations entrusted to them.

2- In the field of the Judicial Police:

a- Performing the duties of the Judicial Police.

b - Executing judicial mandates and letters rogatory.

c- Executing judicial judgments and warrants.

3- In other fields:

a- Assisting the public authorities in the performance of their functions.

b - Guarding public administrations and institutions as decided by the competent authorities.

c- Guarding prisons and managing them when necessary.

d- Guarding diplomatic missions in Lebanon.

The Internal Security Forces shall be subject to the authority of the Minister of the Interior, and the provisions of military laws and regulations shall apply to them, save for the exceptions specified pursuant to other laws and regulations.

The following expressions, wherever they appear in this Law, shall have the meanings indicated opposite each of them:

- The Director General: The Director General of the Internal Security Forces.

- The Inspector General: The Inspector General of the Internal Security Forces.

- The Institute: The Institute of the Internal Security Forces.

- Men of the Internal Security Forces or members of the Internal Security Forces: All officers, non-commissioned officers, and enlisted men belonging to the corps of the Internal Security Forces, including reservists and conscripts during the performance of their active service in the Internal Security Forces.

- Officers of the Internal Security Forces: All officers belonging to the corps of the Internal Security Forces, including reserve officers during the performance of their active service in the Internal Security Forces.

- Units: The various units and formations in the Internal Security Forces, whatever their strength.

- Army Officers: The officers of the main institutions affiliated with the Ministry of National Defence.

- Army Military Personnel: The military personnel of the main institutions affiliated with the Ministry of National Defence.
In all cases specified for filling vacant posts pursuant to Article Eighteen of this Law, no more than one competitive examination may be held, for any reason whatsoever, for the same purpose.

1- The appointment of a temporary civil servant, a contracted employee, or a wage earner in the Third, Fourth, and Fifth Categories in the permanent establishment in application of the provisions of this Law shall be made at the last step of the Category, and where there is more than one rank in the Category, the appointment shall be made at the last step of the rank in which the appointment is intended to be made.

2- The temporary civil servant, contracted employee, or wage earner shall be granted one advancement step for every three years of actual service spent prior to his appointment to the new post.

3- For the purpose of applying the provisions of the two preceding paragraphs in this Article, the monthly wage of the wage earner shall be calculated on the basis of his daily wage multiplied by thirty working days, provided that a fraction of a pound is rounded up to a pound.

4- Seniority qualifying for acquiring a new advancement step for those concerned by the provisions of this Article shall only be calculated as of the date of commencement of work in the new post.

The rights of the temporary civil servant, contracted employee, or wage earner for his previous services shall be settled upon his appointment to the permanent establishment in application of the provisions of this Law in accordance with the laws and regulations in force.
In appointing a permanent civil servant to vacant posts, in application of the provisions of this Law, the legal provisions provided for in the Civil Servants Regulations shall be applied.

Temporary civil servants, contracted employees, and wage earners who are in excess of the actual need of the public administrations, public institutions, and municipalities in which they work shall be placed at the disposal of the Civil Service Board, where they shall be seconded to various public administrations, public institutions, and municipalities when the need for them arises. If they wish to terminate their service, they shall be entitled to do so and shall receive, in addition to the dismissal indemnity due to them, a bonus equivalent to one month's salary for every three years of actual service, provided that this does not exceed six months' salary. The details of determining the surplus, the rules of secondment, the manner of paying the salaries of the surplus and seconded personnel, their indemnities, their rights, and all other matters branching from their status shall be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers. For the application of the provisions of this Article, the jurisdiction of the Civil Service Board shall cover public administrations, public institutions, and municipalities not originally subject to its authority or supervision.

The Internal Security Forces shall comprise the following forces:

1- The Regional Gendarmerie.

2- The Mobile Forces.

3- The Beirut Police.

4- The Judicial Police.

5- The Internal Security Forces Institute.

6- The Apparatus for the Security of Embassies, Public Administrations and Public Institutions. Each of these forces shall constitute a unit, whereas matters that are common among the units, as well as the means necessary for the execution of these matters, shall be unified and entrusted to a Central Administrative Unit subject to the authority of the Director General. As for the social, cultural and intellectual services rendered to personnel of the Internal Security Forces, including the management of funds of a special nature established for this purpose, they shall be entrusted to a special unit also subject to the authority of the Director General.

The command bodies in the Internal Security Forces shall consist of:

1- The Directorate General of the Internal Security Forces, which includes the Director General, the Staff and the Central Administration.

2- The General Inspectorate of the Internal Security Forces.

3- The Command of the Regional Gendarmerie.

4- The Command of the Mobile Forces.

5- The Command of the Beirut Police.

6- The Command of the Judicial Police.

7- The Command of the Apparatus for the Security of Embassies, Public Administrations and Public Institutions.

8- The Command of the Internal Security Forces Institute.

9- The Presidency of Social Services.

10- The Command Council.

1- The following shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior after consulting the Command Council:

A- The establishment of units and the determination of their designations on the basis of the organic organisation provided for in the preceding Article Seven.

B - The two tables of the strength and equipment of the Internal Security Forces.

2- This decree shall serve as a general plan for the structure of the Internal Security Forces, their strength, and their equipping, and it shall be implemented in stages, whereby the additional appropriations necessary to implement what is decided for a given year shall be allocated in the budget of each year.

The Directorate General of the Internal Security Forces shall be headed by a Director General who reports directly to the Minister of the Interior, and this post shall be assigned either to an officer of the rank of Colonel and above from the Internal Security Forces or to a civil servant of the First Category, and in exceptional cases to an officer from the Army of the rank of Colonel and above.

The Director General of the Internal Security Forces shall be appointed and dismissed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior.

The Director General of the Internal Security Forces shall be subject to the authority of the Minister of the Interior and shall undertake:

1- Discharging the duties of the Directorate General, supervising all personnel of the Internal Security Forces, monitoring them, and coordinating their work.

2- Submitting proposals aimed at determining the establishment of the Forces and taking or requesting the taking of all arrangements necessary to fill this establishment within the limits of the appropriations allocated to it.

3- Issuing instructions, within the limits set forth in this Law and in the laws and regulations in force, in all fields in which unified principles must be laid down, rules of joint action must be determined, or the activities of the various personnel of the Internal Security Forces must be coordinated.

4- Ensuring the necessary liaison with the Directors General and all other authorities in the various ministries and with the Army Command.

5- And in general, ensuring the implementation of all measures vested in him pursuant to the provisions of this Law and all other laws and regulations in force.

The units shall be organised as follows:

1- The Staff:

And it comprises the divisions entrusted with preparing studies and providing consultations to the Director General.

2- The Central Administration:

And it comprises the administrative and technical formations entrusted with managing the funds, equipment and supplies of the Internal Security Forces and the buildings belonging to them or placed at their disposal.

3- The Social Services Administration:

And it comprises the Internal Security Forces magazine, the funds of a special character established by decrees for the benefit of the Internal Security Forces, the institutions affiliated with these funds, the clubs, and all other cultural, intellectual and social services.

4- The Regional Gendarmerie:

And it comprises all sectors operating outside Beirut, with the exception of those that remain wholly or partially attached to one of the other units.

5- The Mobile Forces:

These forces constitute the general reserve in the Internal Security Forces, which must be prepared, in size, organisation, equipment and training, for operations of maintaining order and consolidating security, particularly the important ones among them, throughout all Lebanese regions, and they comprise all mobile formations stationed in Beirut and outside it.

6- The Beirut Police:

Its jurisdiction covers the territorial scope of the City of Beirut, and it comprises the formations operating therein, with the exception of those that remain wholly or partially attached to one of the other units.

7- The Judicial Police:

Its jurisdiction covers all Lebanese territory, and it comprises the formations of the Scientific Police and the Tourist Police, and the formations for combating, investigating and inquiring into crimes.

8- The Security Apparatus for Embassies, Public Administrations and Public Institutions:

Its jurisdiction covers all Lebanese territory, and it comprises all formations entrusted with guarding the premises of diplomatic missions in Lebanon and the institutions affiliated with them, as well as public administrations and public institutions.

9- The Internal Security Forces Institute:

And it comprises all colleges and schools of the Internal Security Forces and the training centres therein.

The organic organisation of the Internal Security Forces in their various units and formations, and the powers, duties and responsibilities of the chiefs, in all that does not conflict with the provisions of this Law, shall be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior after seeking the opinion of the Command Council.

1- The Chief of Staff shall report directly to the Director General, and shall be appointed from among the officers of the Internal Security Forces on active service holding at least the rank of Colonel, by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior after consulting the opinion of the Director General.

2- The duties of the Chief of Staff shall be defined as follows:

a- He shall assist the Director General in his duties and give an advisory opinion on transactions that fall within the competence of the Director General.

b - He shall follow up the execution of the decisions of the Director General and ensure coordination among the various units of the Staff and the uniformity of work therein.

3- He may be delegated to sign on behalf of the Director General in all matters that do not affect the principles of organisation and the professional conditions relating to personnel working in the Internal Security Forces and in all matters that do not lead to the commitment of an expenditure.

4- With respect to the members of the Staff, he shall exercise his powers and rights in his capacity as a unit commander.

The Inspector General shall report directly to the Minister of the Interior, and shall be appointed by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior from among the officers in the Internal Security Forces on active service holding at least the rank of Colonel.

The Inspector General shall be assisted by a number of Inspector Officers. His duties shall be defined as follows:

1- Supervising the service in all its branches across the various units of the Internal Security Forces, provided that supervision in the divisions and units of the Directorate General is carried out with the knowledge of the Director General.

2- Ensuring that the service is organised and executed within the limits of the laws and regulations in force.

3- Ensuring that the personnel of the Internal Security Forces do not interfere in political affairs or local disputes.

4- Ascertaining the morale of the personnel of the Internal Security Forces.

5- Investigating notifications and complaints referred to him by the Minister of the Interior concerning conduct by personnel of the Internal Security Forces that violates the law and regulations.

6- Proposing measures conducive to improving the conditions of the Internal Security Forces and their services.

The Inspector General may directly impose the appropriate penalties, within the powers granted to unit commanders under this law, for general disciplinary offences committed in his presence while exercising his duties.

The Inspector General shall propose to the Director General penalties for the offences and faults which he verifies during his inspections and tours, and the latter shall have the right to ratify them or take the appropriate penalties in respect thereof, provided that the Inspector General is informed of the ratified or taken penalties. The Inspector General shall submit his reports to the Minister of the Interior and the Director General, and shall include therein his observations and proposals regarding the offences which he has verified, and the Minister may request the Director General to take the necessary penalties and measures in respect thereof in accordance with the provisions of the law.
The Inspector General shall exercise, in respect of the personnel of the General Inspectorate, his powers and rights in his capacity as a unit commander.

The commands and presidencies of the units provided for in Article Six of this law shall be entrusted to officers of the Internal Security Forces in active service of the rank of at least Colonel, who shall be appointed by decree upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior after consulting the opinion of the Director General, and each of them shall be considered a "Unit Commander".

Unit commanders shall report directly to the Director General and shall be subject to his authority, and they shall assume the command of their units and ensure their administration in accordance with the laws and regulations in force.

The Commander of the Judicial Police shall be subject to the direct authority of the Director General of the Internal Security Forces and shall be responsible before him for the execution of the attributions entrusted to him from the administrative and disciplinary aspects and the missions related to public security of investigation and surveillance, and those relating to the competence of the Technical Section to assist the rest of the units in the Security Forces.

As for judicial missions, he shall be directly responsible, together with the personnel of his unit, before the Public Prosecutor of the Court of Cassation, without prejudice to his subjection to the authority of the Director General.

1- The Command Council shall report directly to the Minister of the Interior and shall be composed of:

- The Director General.......... President.

- The Inspector General .

- All the unit commanders specified in Article 6 of this law............ Members

2- A member shall ipso jure recuse himself from the session when the deliberation addresses a matter relating to him personally.

1- The Command Council shall hold its sessions upon the convocation of its President or at the request of half of the members of the Command Council.

2- The Council may decide to summon whomever it deems appropriate to attend its sessions.

3- The deliberations of the Council shall be characterised by complete confidentiality.

4- The Head of the Special Affairs Division shall perform the duties of the Secretariat of the Command Council.

The Command Council shall undertake:

1- Proposing the establishment of units and determining their designations.

2- Drawing up draft general tables of strength and equipment.

3- Drawing up draft detailed tables for the distribution of strength and equipment.

4- Appointing trainee gendarmes and trainee non-commissioned officers.

5- Proposing the appointment of cadet officers and specialist officers.

6- Rescinding the enlistment contracts of trainee gendarmes and trainee non-commissioned officers.

7- Refusing to renew the enlistment contracts of enlisted personnel and non-commissioned officers with poor ratings.

8- Accepting the renewal of enlistment contracts of enlisted personnel and non-commissioned officers as a warning for less than two years.

9- Approving the discharge of enlisted personnel and non-commissioned officers for compelling reasons.

10- Reducing the periods of seniority for promotion for enlisted personnel and non-commissioned officers.

11- Proposing the granting of exceptional seniority to officers of the rank of Lieutenant Colonel and below.

12- Promoting martyrs among the enlisted personnel and non-commissioned officers of the Internal Security Forces posthumously.

13- Proposing the promotion of martyrs among the officers of the Internal Security Forces posthumously.

14- Selecting those accepted from among the non-commissioned officers who are candidates for the rank of Lieutenant.

15- Drawing up promotion rosters for officers to the rank of Colonel and below.

16- Designating the transfer posts of officers other than the Inspector General and unit commanders.

17- Imposing penalties of striking off promotion rosters with respect to enlisted personnel and non-commissioned officers.

18- Proposing the imposition of penalties of striking off promotion rosters and reduction in rank therein with respect to officers of the rank of Colonel and below.

19- Designating the posts of officers other than unit commanders upon whom disciplinary transfer penalties have been imposed.

20- Drawing up promotion rosters for enlisted personnel and non-commissioned officers.

21- Drawing up enlistment regulations.

22- Drawing up regulations for competitive examinations and proficiency examinations.

23- Determining the rules for the detachment of members of the Internal Security Forces.

24- Drawing up instructions relating to determining the rules and procedures for promotion, renewal of enlistment, and designation of transfer posts.

25- Reinstating into the corps personnel whose enlistment contracts have been rescinded.

1- The Command Council shall take its decisions unanimously or by a majority of at least eight votes.

2- Anyone who dissents from the opinion of the majority must state the reasons for his position in the minutes of the meeting.

1- Decisions taken by the Command Council unanimously or by a majority of at least eight votes in the matters provided for in items 20 to 25 inclusive of Article 20 of this Law, shall be deemed effective immediately, and a copy thereof shall be sent to the Minister of the Interior for information.

2- Decisions taken by the Council unanimously in the matters provided for in the other items of Article 20 shall be deemed effective immediately and a copy thereof shall be sent to the Minister of the Interior for information. However, if these decisions are taken by a majority of eight votes and above, they shall be sent to the Minister of the Interior, to whom it falls:

A- Either to ratify them within a period of one week from the date of their deposit with him, and they shall become effective immediately.

B - Or not to ratify them and not to return them to the Council within the aforementioned period, whereupon they shall become effective immediately upon the expiry of this period.

C- Or not to ratify them and to return them within the period of one week by a reasoned decision to the Council for reconsideration, whereupon the Council shall examine them anew within a period of one week from the date of their return to it and shall send the decisions it takes as a result of the second examination to the Minister of the Interior, and the Minister may either ratify them within a period of one week from the date of their deposit with him or refer them to the Council of Ministers, which shall take the final decision regarding them.

In addition to the administrations of which the Ministry of the Interior is composed, a Permanent Council for Internal Security shall be established in this Ministry, comprising:

1- A Central Council composed of:

- The Minister of the Interior..... as President.

- The Public Prosecutor before the Court of Cassation.

- The Governor of the City of Beirut.

- The Commander of the Army or whomever he delegates in emergency security cases that prevent him from attending in person.

- The Director General of the Internal Security Forces.

- The Director General of General Security as Members.

- A senior officer of the Internal Security Forces of the rank of Lieutenant Colonel and above, appointed by decree upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior after consulting the opinion of the Director General of the Internal Security Forces..... as Secretary.

2- A Sub-Council in each of the other Governorates composed of:

- The Governor.... as President

- The Appellate Public Prosecutor.

- The Commander of the Military Region.

- The Commander of the Regional Gendarmerie Company, or the Commanders of the Regional Gendarmerie Companies in the Governorate.

- The General Security Officer in charge in the Governorate.... as Members .

- The Secretary General of the Governorate....... as Secretary

A permanent secretariat shall be attached to the Central Council, the presidency of which shall be entrusted to the Secretary of the Council, assisted by a number of employees of the Ministry of the Interior.

1- The Central Council shall undertake:

A- Studying and discussing security affairs.

B - Exchanging information among the agencies represented on the Council.

C- Coordinating work among these agencies.

D- Taking the appropriate decisions and recommendations, where necessary, within the scope of the powers and responsibilities entrusted to each of these agencies pursuant to the laws and regulations in force.

2- The Sub-Councils shall undertake the tasks specified for the Central Council at the level of the Governorates.

Each of the Central Council and the Sub-Councils shall meet upon the convocation of its President at least once a month, and the President of each of these Councils may summon whomever he deems appropriate to attend the meetings of the Council.

The tasks of the Secretariat of the Council shall be determined as follows:

A- Receiving information from the agencies represented on the Council, and analysing, evaluating, classifying and following up on it.

B - Submitting the results of the evaluation of this information to the President of the Council and the competent authorities specified by the latter, including those represented on the Council.

C- Preparing the sessions of the Council, drawing up their minutes, and following up on the implementation of the decisions and recommendations taken therein.
The details of the application of the provisions of this Title shall be determined, where necessary, by a decision of the Minister of the Interior.

The hierarchy of ranks for Enlisted Personnel and Non-Commissioned Officers in the Internal Security Forces is:

- Trainee Gendarme - Policeman for those working in the two units of the Beirut Police and the Embassies, Public Administrations and Public Institutions Security Apparatus,

- Judicial Policeman for those working in the Judicial Police Unit,

- Gendarme for those working in the Directorate General, the Inspectorate General and in all other units.

- Corporal

- Trainee Sergeant

- Sergeant

- First Sergeant

- Adjutant

- First Adjutant

- Warrant Officer

- First Warrant Officer

Trainee Gendarmes, Gendarmes, Judicial Policemen, Policemen and Corporals shall constitute the category of Enlisted Personnel, and Trainee Sergeants, First Sergeants, Adjutants, First Adjutants, Warrant Officers and First Warrant Officers shall constitute the category of Non-Commissioned Officers.

Each of the Enlisted Personnel and Non-Commissioned Officers shall have the right of command over his subordinates. Where ranks are equal, the right of command shall belong to the one who has greater seniority in the rank.

Where seniority in the rank is equal, seniority in the preceding rank shall be taken into account, and so on successively down to the lowest rank on the scale of ranks in the Corps; where seniority in the lowest rank is equal, the right of command shall belong to the one who has greater seniority in the service.

Where rank is equal between reservists and active duty personnel, command shall belong to the one who has greater seniority in active service in the same rank.

An applicant for enlistment must satisfy the following conditions:

1- To have been a Lebanese national for at least ten years.

2- To have completed, on 31 December of the year of commencement of the competitive examination, eighteen years of age and not to have exceeded thirty years of age in respect of civilians and thirty-five years of age in respect of active duty military personnel in the Army

3- To enjoy a physical fitness rendering him fit for service in the Internal Security Forces.

4- To have an educational attainment at the level of the end of the primary education stage.

5- For his height to be at least:

- 164 centimetres if he holds at least the Lebanese Baccalaureate - Part Two or its official equivalent or holds the Technical Baccalaureate, or is among the active duty military personnel in the Army .

- 167 centimetres for the remaining candidates.

6- To enjoy his civil rights and not be convicted of a felony or an attempted felony of any kind whatsoever , or of a disgraceful misdemeanour or an attempted disgraceful misdemeanour, or of imprisonment for a term exceeding six months, and these provisions shall apply to persons who have been rehabilitated and have benefited from a general amnesty or a special amnesty . The following misdemeanours shall be considered disgraceful: theft, fraud, breach of trust, embezzlement , bribery, rape , blackmail,- forgery, use of a forged document, offences offending public morals provided for in- Title Seven of the General Penal Code, drawing a cheque without provision, false testimony, false oath, offences relating to narcotics .
