7- To be of good conduct and morals and not addicted to intoxicants, narcotics, or games of chance, and not affiliated with a party not licensed by law or collaborating therewith.

8- Not to have practised in his civilian life a disgraceful or dishonourable profession.

9- If he is among the military personnel of the Army, conscripts, or former members of the Internal Security Forces, he must possess, in addition to the preceding conditions, a certificate of good conduct if the duration of his service in his former corps entitles him to the right to be granted the said certificate upon his discharge.

All applicants for enlistment shall be subject to an academic competitive examination at the level of the class of the end of the primary education stage, and its results shall be entered into the enlistment file provided for in Article 38 of this Law.

Every competitive examination shall be considered of no effect for those who are not admitted by its result, regardless of the period separating one competitive examination from another.

This principle shall apply to all competitive examinations provided for in this Law which are held for enlisted personnel and non-commissioned officers.

Trainee gendarmes shall be recruited from among Lebanese nationals by way of enlistment in accordance with the conditions specified in the following articles, and they shall be appointed by a decision of the Command Council within the limits of the General Strength Table, and the enlistment contracts shall be signed by the Director General and the persons concerned.

The enlistment of trainee gendarmes shall be conducted from among those wishing to enlist and in accordance with the following priorities:

1- From among active service military personnel in the Army or conscripts, provided that they have spent at least one year in service.

2- From among former members of the Internal Security Forces and Army military personnel who were not discharged for disciplinary reasons. As for those discharged for health reasons, they shall be presented to the Medical Inquiry Committee to verify the cessation of the reasons that had necessitated the discharge.

3- From among the sons and brothers of former members of the Internal Security Forces or the Army who perished or sustained a permanent disability in the line of duty.

4- From among the sons of members of the Internal Security Forces or the Army in active service, or from among the sons of those who perished or sustained a permanent disability during service.

5- From among the sons of former members of the Internal Security Forces or the Army, provided that the father was not discharged for disciplinary reasons.

- From among other civilians.

Each of these priorities shall be granted by awarding additional marks to be added to the marks of the competitive examination provided for in Article 34 of this Law, and which shall be specified in the Enlistment Regulations provided for in Article 46 of this Law.

1- The Director General and the accepted candidates shall sign enlistment contracts for a period of five years commencing from the date they join the Internal Security Forces.

2- Immediately upon signing his enlistment contract, the volunteer shall be deemed a trainee gendarme for a maximum period of one year, during which the laws and regulations in force for all other personnel of the Internal Security Forces shall apply to him, and he shall not be entitled to request the annulment of his enlistment contract after the conclusion of the induction training course except for reasons approved by the Command Council.

A file shall be compiled for each enlistment candidate comprising:

- Information provided by the person concerned.

- A copy of an individual civil status extract. - A copy of his judicial record and a certificate stating whether he is subject to judicial prosecution.

- A statement of the stages of his military service and of the commendations he received, if any.

- A copy of his academic certificates or a school certificate regarding his level of education.

- Any other document capable of demonstrating the merit of the candidate.

Accepted candidates shall be attached to the Institute to attend a military and professional induction training course. Its duration shall not be less than four months, and the military induction training may, upon the request of the Director General and the approval of the Army Command, be conducted at one of the training centres of the Army.

The contracts of trainee gendarmes may be terminated upon the proposal of the Commander of the Institute by a decision of the Command Council in the following cases:

1- For disciplinary or health reasons.

2- By reason of the unsatisfactory result of their course in the Internal Security Forces or in the Army.

3- If it is established that the person concerned submitted incorrect information in the enlistment application that would have led to the rejection of his enlistment.

4- If it is established that the person concerned committed fraud of any kind whatsoever in the enlistment competitive examination.

5- For reasons of force majeure.

In each of the cases referred to above, the persons concerned shall not be entitled to claim any compensation for the period they may have spent in service.

A trainee gendarme shall be confirmed in the capacity of gendarme by a decision of the Director General, either upon the conclusion of the induction training course at the Institute or at the end of the training year provided for in paragraph 2 of Article 36 of this Law.

1- Promotion is the transition of a security member from one rank to a higher rank.

2- The promotion of enlisted personnel and non-commissioned officers to a higher rank shall pass through the following stages:

a- Submission of candidacy applications by the concerned persons.

b - Acceptance or rejection of the candidacy applications by the unit commanders.

c- Circulation of the names of those accepted.

d- The qualifying competitive examination.

e- A study course and end-of-course examinations for certain ranks.

f- Placement on the promotion roster.

g- The promotion decision.

1- A candidate for promotion shall be required to satisfy at least the following seniority conditions:

- For the rank of Corporal: three years in the ranks of Trainee Gendarme and Gendarme, or Policeman, or Judicial Policeman.

- For the rank of Sergeant: three years in the rank of Corporal.

- For the rank of Staff Sergeant: two years in the rank of Sergeant, or three years in the ranks of Trainee Sergeant and Sergeant with respect to those who were not confirmed due to force majeure in the rank of Sergeant at the end of the training year.

- For the rank of Sub-Officer: three years in the rank of Staff Sergeant.

- For the rank of Chief Sub-Officer: two years in the rank of Sub-Officer.

- For the rank of Warrant Officer: three years in the rank of Chief Sub-Officer.

- For the rank of Chief Warrant Officer: two years in the rank of Warrant Officer.

2- Seniority for promotion to attain the rank of Sergeant up to Chief Warrant Officer may be reduced, on a single occasion, by one year for holders of at least the Lebanese Baccalaureate Certificate - Part Two or its official equivalent or the Technical Baccalaureate, and by six months for holders of the Intermediate Certificate or its official equivalent or the Technical Intermediate Certificate.

To reduce seniority by a period of one year, the Lebanese Baccalaureate Certificate - Part One or its official equivalent shall suffice for members of the Internal Security Forces who are in active service prior to the promulgation of this Law.

3- Sergeants who are appointed to the Internal Security Forces in the rank of Trainee Sergeant shall be exempted from the provisions of the preceding paragraph 2.

1 - The Command Council may exceptionally reduce the promotion period by up to half for enlisted personnel and non-commissioned officers on grounds of:

- Their demonstration of extraordinary gallantry in war operations or operations for the maintenance of security and order.

- For having repeatedly distinguished themselves by extraordinary courage or exceptional skill in detecting crimes and arresting persons wanted by justice.

Such persons may be exempted from the qualifying competitive examination, the study course, or the end-of-course examinations, or from all of them.

2- Notwithstanding all conditions of promotion, the Command Council may, with respect to enlisted personnel and non-commissioned officers who are martyred during operations for the maintenance of order and the consolidation of security or during an armed clash, promote them to the rank immediately above their ranks, and each of them shall be deemed martyred at the rank to which he was promoted.

Trainee sergeants may be enlisted, in accordance with the preference specified in Article 32 of this Law, from among civilians and personnel of the Internal Security Forces and the Army who meet the conditions provided for in Article 33 of this Law, provided that they hold at least the Lebanese Baccalaureate Certificate, Part Two, or its official equivalent, or the Technical Baccalaureate Certificate, while the Lebanese Baccalaureate Certificate, Part One, or its official equivalent, shall suffice for personnel of the Internal Security Forces who are in active service prior to the promulgation of this Law.

These cadets shall be subject to a competitive examination at the level of the Lebanese Baccalaureate Certificate - Part Two, and those accepted from among them shall be appointed by a decision of the Command Council within the limits of the establishments; the Director General shall sign their enlistment contracts, and they shall be attached to the Institute to attend a military and professional training course for a period of at least six months.

1- Upon the request of the Director General and the approval of the Army Command, the military training of trainee sergeants may be conducted at one of the training centres of the Army, and the Director General may also reduce the duration of the military training course or dispense with it altogether for cadets accepted from among personnel of the Internal Security Forces and the Army who are in active service or former personnel.

2- The provisions set forth in Articles 36 and 39 of this Law shall apply to trainee sergeants with respect to the durations of their enlistment contracts and the termination thereof.

3- Upon signing his enlistment contract, an enlistee from among these shall immediately be considered a trainee sergeant for a maximum period of one year, during which the laws and regulations applicable to the remaining personnel of the Internal Security Forces shall apply to him.

4- A trainee sergeant shall be confirmed in the capacity of sergeant by a decision of the Director General, either upon the conclusion of the training course at the Institute or at the end of the probationary year provided for in the preceding paragraph 3.

Trainee gendarmes and trainee sergeants who fail the examination at the end of the training course shall be subject to a second course, and the duration of the second course shall not be counted as seniority for promotion.

In the event that trainee gendarmes fail a second time, they shall be discharged ipso jure by a decision of the Director General.

However, in the event that trainee sergeants fail a second time, they shall be given the choice between being appointed at the rank of gendarme or being discharged by a decision of the Director General.

Upon the confirmation of trainee gendarmes and trainee sergeants, they must take the following oath before the Single Judge:

"I swear by my God, my country and my honour that I shall obey my superiors in all that relates to the service to which I am called, that I shall not violate the sanctity of honour, and that I shall not use the authority granted to me except for the purpose of consolidating order and enforcing the law".

1- The system of enlistment for trainee gendarmes and trainee sergeants shall be determined by a decision of the Command Council.

2- The programmes of the training courses and their durations for the personnel mentioned in the preceding clause shall be determined by a decision of the Director General upon the proposal of the Commander of the Institute.

Trainee gendarmes shall be attached, immediately upon the completion of the training course, to the units entrusted with the duties of maintaining order and consolidating security, for a period of at least two years. However, an exception to this rule may be made in respect of specialists and those who have previously served in the Internal Security Forces or the Army and were the subject of commendation, as they may be transferred to any other unit prior to the completion of this period.
Trainee sergeants shall be attached, immediately upon the completion of the training course, to the various units.

Enlisted personnel and non-commissioned officers who have been discharged from service in the Internal Security Forces for non-disciplinary reasons may be reinstated into the service by the Director General, once only, if they meet the following conditions:

1- That they fulfil the conditions provided for in Article 33 of this Law.

2- That they hold a certificate of good conduct.

3- That they have not exceeded 40 years of age, and reliance in this regard shall only be placed on the age recorded in their personal file.

4- That they have served in the Internal Security Forces for at least two years following their confirmation.

5- That no more than five years have elapsed since their discharge at the time of submitting their applications.

6- As for those who were previously discharged for health reasons, the Medical Investigation Committee must, in addition to the aforementioned conditions, approve their admission after ascertaining that the reasons that necessitated the discharge have ceased to exist.

1- Upon the expiry of the period of enlistment, enlisted personnel and non-commissioned officers may request the renewal of their enlistment contracts for a period ranging between two and five years.

However, this period may under no circumstances exceed the date on which they reach the statutory age for compulsory retirement.

2- The Unit Commanders, each within his competence, shall sign the contracts for the renewal of enlistment.

The Command Council may, upon the proposal of the Unit Commanders, each within his competence, refuse to renew the enlistment of enlisted personnel and non-commissioned officers having poor

ratings.

However, the Council may accept the renewal of the enlistment of such personnel for less than two years by way of warning, once only.
The rules for applying the provisions of this Chapter shall be determined by instructions from the Command Council.

The scale of ranks of officers in the Internal Security Forces shall be determined as follows:

A- Junior Officers: - Lieutenant - First Lieutenant - Captain

B - Senior Officers: - Major - Lieutenant Colonel - Colonel

C- General Officers: - Brigadier General - Major General

1- Every officer shall have the right of command over anyone inferior to him in rank.

2- In the event of equality of rank between two officers, command shall belong to the senior in the rank.

3- If seniority in the rank is equal, the order of names on the promotion decree for this rank shall be adopted.

4- If seniority in the rank is equal between two officers, one of whom is a specialist and the other is a non-specialist, command shall belong to the senior in service.

5- In the event of equality of seniority between two Lieutenants, one of whom is from the ranks and the other is a graduate of the Military Academy, command shall belong to the senior in service.

6- In the event of equality of rank between reserve officers and active service officers, the right of command shall belong to the one who has more seniority in active service in the rank.

1- Officers of the Internal Security Forces shall be appointed in accordance with the conditions determined in this Chapter by a decree based on the proposal of the Minister of Interior from among:

A- Officer cadets of the Internal Security Forces after their obtaining the certificate of competency for the rank of Lieutenant.

B - Non-commissioned officers of the Security Forces of the rank of Adjutant at least, and at a rate not exceeding 20 % of the total realised strength of officers.

2- Specialist officers of the Internal Security Forces shall be appointed from among the holders of university degrees in accordance with the provisions of Article 91 of this Law.

Officer cadets shall be recruited from among the personnel of the Internal Security Forces in active service and from among civilians in accordance with the regulations for admission to the Military Academy, and those accepted from among them shall be appointed by a joint decision of the Ministers of National Defence and of Interior based on the proposal of the Command Council.

1- Officer cadets of the Internal Security Forces accepted into the Military Academy shall follow the same programme prescribed for Army officer cadets, to which shall be added, where necessary, special professional instruction qualifying them to follow the professional training course at the Institute.

2- The same regulations that apply to Army officer cadets shall apply to these cadets throughout their presence at the Military Academy.

1- Officer cadets of the Internal Security Forces shall be subject, at the conclusion of study at the Military Academy, to the final examinations, and those among them who pass shall be promoted to the rank of Lieutenant.

2- The names shall be listed in the promotion decree in accordance with the final classification at the Military Academy.

As for those who fail the final examinations, the provisions applicable to those who fail among Army officer cadets shall apply to them.

1- The names of the accepted candidates shall be announced by a decision of the Director General.

2- Those whose candidacy is accepted shall be subject to:

- A competency competitive examination for candidates for the rank of Corporal, Staff Sergeant, Master Sergeant and Chief Warrant Officer.

- A competency competitive examination, a study course and an end-of-course examination for candidates for the rank of Sergeant, Sergeant First Class and Warrant Officer.

3- As a result of the competency competitive examination, the number of accepted candidates for each rank may not exceed the number of vacant positions in this rank or those that will fall vacant over the course of the year.

4- Notwithstanding the provisions of the preceding clause, if the number of candidates for a given rank exceeds the vacancies therein, the accepted candidates for this rank may be set within the limit of the total vacancies in the ranks above it.

1- The names of the successful candidates in the competency competitive examination among the candidates for the rank of Corporal, Staff Sergeant, Master Sergeant and Chief Warrant Officer shall be entered on the promotion roster according to the seniority provided for in Article 31 of this Law.

2- The names of the successful candidates in the end-of-study-course examination among the candidates for the rank of Sergeant, Sergeant First Class and Warrant Officer shall be entered on the promotion roster according to their order of merit resulting from this examination.

3- The names of enlisted personnel and non-commissioned officers shall be entered on the promotion roster by a decision of the Command Council.

Subject to the provisions of the last clause of Article 57 of this Law, enlisted personnel and non-commissioned officers whose names are entered on the promotion roster shall be promoted by a decision of the Director General according to the vacancy of positions in the table of strength.
The rules for applying the provisions provided for in this Chapter shall be determined by instructions from the Command Council.

In addition to the grounds set forth in Article 39 of this Law, the enlistment contract of enlisted personnel and non-commissioned officers shall be terminated in the following cases:

1- By operation of law: upon their reaching the following statutory age:

a - For enlisted personnel: 50 years

b - For non-commissioned officers: 52 years

2 - Optionally: upon their completing a period of 18 years in service.

3 - At their request: upon the expiry of the terms of their enlistment contracts and their unwillingness to renew them.

4 - For health reasons: if their health condition does not permit them to continue service, pursuant to the decision of the Medical Inquiry Committee.

5 - For compelling and unforeseen reasons based on the requests of the concerned parties.

6 - For disciplinary reasons: pursuant to the decision of the Disciplinary Council ordering their expulsion.

1- Enlisted men and non-commissioned officers shall be discharged in the cases provided for in items 1, 2, 3 and 4 of the preceding Article 60 by a decision of the competent unit commander.

Whereas in the case provided for in item 5 of the aforementioned article, the discharge shall take place by a decision of the Director General after the approval of the Command Council.

2- The competent unit commander shall grant certificates of good conduct to discharged personnel whose services are satisfactory.

1- The discharge of enlisted men and non-commissioned officers shall be suspended by operation of law in the following cases, even if they have reached the statutory age limits for referral to retirement:

a- If they are undergoing the execution of a disciplinary penalty with a duration of thirty days of strict arrest or more, or fortress arrest regardless of its duration, until the completion of the execution of the penalty.

b - If a proposal has been submitted to punish them for a serious fault requiring the imposition of one of the penalties provided for in the preceding item a, until the confirmation of the penalty and its execution.

c- If they are under investigation for a serious fault that may lead to punishing them with the penalties mentioned in the preceding (item a), until the completion of the investigation, the taking of a decision thereon, and the execution of this decision.

d- If they are referred before the Disciplinary Council, until the issuance of the final decision concerning them and the execution of this decision.

2- The period that exceeds the statutory age limits for the purpose of executing these measures shall not be counted as active service upon the liquidation of retirement rights.

The liquidation of the retirement rights of discharged enlisted men and non-commissioned officers shall be suspended if they are referred before medical investigation committees, or under judicial prosecution for one of the offences punishable by law by a penalty that leads to depriving them of their retirement rights, until the issuance of the final judgment or the decision to close the case.

1- In a state of war or a state of emergency, or upon the occurrence or anticipation of the occurrence of internal disturbances, the discharge of enlisted men and non-commissioned officers who have not reached the statutory age limits, or some of their categories, or whose services have not reached a certain duration, may be suspended by a decision of the Minister of the Interior upon the proposal of the Director General.

2- In all cases of suspension of discharge provided for in this Chapter, the enlistment contract shall be deemed extended by operation of law until the cessation of the cause for suspending the discharge, subject to the provisions of item 2 of Article 62 of this Law.

1- It shall not be permissible to transfer enlisted men and non-commissioned officers to other administrations during the period of their enlistment in the Internal Security Forces, whatever the reasons may be.

2- The rules for applying the provisions provided for in this Chapter shall be determined by instructions from the Director General.
The rules for applying the provisions of Articles 74, 75 and 76 of this Law shall be determined by a decision of the Command Council.

An officer shall not be promoted to a higher rank unless his name is entered on the promotion roster, which is issued with respect to:

A- The Director General, whatever the rank for which he is nominated:

- By a decree based upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior.

B - Candidates for the ranks of Brigadier General and Major General:

- By a decree based upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior founded upon the proposal of the Director General.

C- Candidates for the remaining ranks:

- By a decree based upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior founded upon the proposal of the Command Council.

1- The names of the officers of each rank shall be entered on the promotion roster by seniority in accordance with the provisions of Article 67 of this Law, and promotion shall take place in accordance with the order of this roster.

2- The promotion of officers shall take place on the first of January and the first of July of each year, with the exception of promotion to the ranks of Second Lieutenant and First Lieutenant, and the promotion of officers who are considered martyrs of duty in accordance with what is specified in Item 2 of Article 85 of this Law.

The number of officers whose names are entered on the promotion roster for each rank may not exceed the number of vacant positions or positions that will become vacant during the year in this rank.

However, if the number of candidates for a given rank exceeds the vacancies therein, a number of candidates for this rank may be promoted within the limits of the total vacancies in the ranks above it.

1- The promotion of a Second Lieutenant to the rank of First Lieutenant shall take place by selection after the candidate has spent at least three years in the rank of Second Lieutenant. However, if his promotion does not take place upon his reaching four years in his rank, he shall be promoted automatically to the rank of First Lieutenant.

2- Promotion by selection to the rank of Captain, Colonel and Major General shall take place after the candidate has spent at least four years in the rank immediately below it.

3- Promotion by selection to the rank of Major, Lieutenant Colonel and Brigadier General shall take place after the candidate has spent at least five years in the rank immediately below it.

1- Lieutenants shall pursue a course of study at the Institute followed by a probationary training course in the units under conditions determined by instructions from the Director General, and they may also be dispatched abroad to pursue another complementary or specialised course.

2- Lieutenants who fail the graduation examinations of the Institute shall undergo a second course at this Institute, and the duration of the second course shall not be counted as seniority for promotion to the rank of First Lieutenant. As for those who fail a second time, they shall be discharged from service by a decree based on the proposal of the Minister of Interior.
Officers shall, upon their graduation from the Institute, take before the President of the Court of Appeal the oath provided for in Article 45 of this Law.

Non-commissioned officers holding at least the rank of Adjutant must meet the following conditions for their candidacy to the rank of Lieutenant to be accepted:

1- That they hold at least the rank of Adjutant, and that at least the following periods have elapsed since they attained this rank:

- One year for holders of the Lebanese Licence in Law.

- Three years for holders of the Lebanese Baccalaureate - Part Two or its official equivalent or the Technical Baccalaureate.

- Four years for holders of the Lebanese Baccalaureate - Part One or its official equivalent for members of the Internal Security Forces who are in active service prior to the issuance of this Law.

- Six years for holders of the Complementary Certificate or its official equivalent or the Technical Complementary Certificate.

- Seven years for all other candidates.

2- That they have not exceeded the age of forty-five on 31 December of the year of candidacy.

- That their evaluations are good.

The Director General shall decide on the applications for candidacy, and those whose applications are accepted shall undergo a qualifying competitive examination limited to professional, administrative, and judicial affairs, and they shall be granted, prior to the establishment of the results of this competitive examination, additional marks that increase progressively with the rise in the candidate's rank and that are determined in the decision provided for in Article 77 of this Law.

1- The selection of those accepted shall take place on the basis of the result of the competitive examination within the limits of the proportion provided for in Article 68 of this Law, by a decision of the Command Council.

2- Those selected by the Command Council shall pursue a course of study at the Institute of a duration of at least six months, and the names of those among them who pass the end-of-course examination shall be entered in accordance with their ranking as a result of this examination on the promotion roster for the rank of Lieutenant by a decree based on the proposal of the Minister of Interior founded on the proposal of the Command Council, and their promotion shall take place by a decree founded on the proposal of the Minister of Interior founded on the proposal of the Director General.

1- Officers may not be promoted after their referral to retirement except where they resume service for a period of at least one year, and perform outstanding acts of bravery, in which case they shall benefit from the statutory age limit prescribed for the new rank.

2- Notwithstanding any other provision, an officer who is martyred during operations to maintain order and consolidate security or during an armed clash shall be promoted to the rank immediately above his rank and shall be deemed to have been martyred at the rank to which he was promoted.

- The promotion of officers shall take place in accordance with the order of their names on the promotion roster and within the limits of vacant positions:

- By decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior, for the Director General

- By decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior based on the proposal of the Director General, for the remaining officers

An officer may be granted exceptional seniority for promotion ranging between three months and two years for displaying supreme gallantry in war operations or in operations to maintain order and consolidate security, and between six months and one year for repeatedly distinguishing himself by supreme bravery or extraordinary skill in detecting crimes and arresting persons wanted by justice.
The conditions for applying the provisions of this Chapter shall be determined by a decision of the Command Council.

Subject to the provisions of Article 91 of this Law, officers shall be mandatorily discharged upon reaching the following statutory age limits:

- Lieutenant - First Lieutenant - Captain : 52 years

- Major : 53 years

- Lieutenant Colonel : 54 years

- Colonel : 56 years

- Brigadier General : 58 years

- Major General : 59 years

An officer who entered the Internal Security Forces before the age of eighteen, or who previously entered one of the offices of the State before this age and was then transferred to the Internal Security Forces, shall be mandatorily discharged regardless of his age when the following years have elapsed since his first entry into service:

- 34 years for a Lieutenant

- 35 years for a First Lieutenant

- 36 years for a Captain

- 37 years for a Major

- 38 years for a Lieutenant Colonel

- 40 years for a Colonel

- 42 years for a Brigadier General

- 43 years for a Major General

1- Medical officers, dental officers, pharmacists, engineers, administrators, musicians, veterinarians, chemists and all other technicians shall be deemed specialist officers in the Internal Security Forces.

2- Non-commissioned officers and enlisted personnel who work in the fields referred to in the preceding paragraph and occupy the posts assigned thereto in the table of establishment provided for in Article 8 of this Law shall also be deemed specialists.

1- Specialist officers holding university degrees in their specialisation that are officially recognised in Lebanon and who are legally permitted to practise their specialisation in Lebanon shall be subject to the same provisions as those applicable to their counterparts in the Army, particularly in respect of appointment, termination of service and recovery of training expenses, and the Minister of the Interior shall exercise in this regard the powers vested by virtue of those provisions in the Minister of National Defence. The Command Council and the Director General shall also exercise, each within his competence, the powers vested in them pursuant to the laws and regulations. As for other matters, the Minister of the Interior, the Command Council and the Director General shall each exercise the powers vested in them by virtue of this Law in respect of regular officers.

2- As for officers, non-commissioned officers and enlisted personnel who are deemed specialists by reason of their practice of work in the field of the aforementioned specialisations, or by reason of their successful completion of study courses in those specialisations, they shall be subject to the same general provisions as those applicable to all other officers, non-commissioned officers and enlisted personnel of the Internal Security Forces, provided that they may be retained in active service for a period of two years at most after reaching the age of mandatory retirement provided for in Articles 60, 88 and 99 of this Law.

3- The rules and conditions for the retention provided for in the preceding Clause 2 shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior based upon the proposal of the Director General.

Subject to the provisions of Clause 1 of Article 60 of this Law, the enlistment contracts of enlisted personnel and non-commissioned officers who successfully attend specialisation courses shall be automatically extended for a period of five years with effect from the date of completion of their specialisation.
The rules for the application of the provisions of this Chapter shall be determined by a decision of the Command Council.

Subject to the provisions of Articles 9, 11, 12 and 16 of this Law, the posts of members of the Internal Security Forces shall be assigned as follows:

1- By a decision of the Command Council for officers.

2- By a decision of the Director General for enlisted personnel and non-commissioned officers upon their first assignment following the completion of the initial training course to the units of the Internal Security Forces and in the event of their transfer from one unit to another unit.

3- By a decision of the unit commanders, each within his competence, in the event of the transfer of enlisted personnel and non-commissioned officers from one detachment to another within the same unit.

With the exception of the Director General and the officers who are unit commanders, no other members of the Internal Security Forces serving in territorial detachments may be transferred before the lapse of two years of their presence in their posts, nor may they be kept in those posts after the lapse of four years therein whether continuously or intermittently.

In addition to the conditions of seniority provided for in Article 81 of this Law, officers nominated for promotion must satisfy the following conditions:

1- Their superiors' evaluations of them must be good.

2- They must attend, where required, a course of study at the Institute.

3- A candidate for promotion to the rank of Major must pass a proficiency examination. In the event that he fails this examination or abstains from participating in it twice consecutively, he shall be deprived of nomination and consequently deprived of participating in the proficiency examination for two consecutive times. However, if he subsequently fails the proficiency examination again or abstains from participating in it, he shall then be mandatorily referred to retirement at the rank of Major and his entitlements shall be settled in his new rank.

4- Specialist Captains provided for in Article 90 of this Law shall be exempted from the examination that is the subject of Clause 3 above.

The procedures for the promotion of officers shall be determined as follows:

1- The nomination of officers for promotion shall take place once a year during the month of November of the year of nomination.

2- Cadets of the Military Academy and of all other schools for specialists and technicians, as well as Lieutenants nominated for promotion to the rank of First Lieutenant, shall be exempted from the provisions of the preceding Clause.

For the promotion of officer cadets to the rank of Lieutenant shall be carried out in accordance with the procedures determined in the regulations of their institutes, and to the rank of First Lieutenant in accordance with the provisions of Clause 1 of Article 81 of this Law; martyred officers referred to in Clause 2 of Article 84 of this Law shall also be exempted from the provisions of the said Clause, as their promotion shall be carried out at any time of the year.

3- During the month of December of the year of nomination, the following measures shall be taken:

a- The Command Council shall hold its sessions in order to:

- Review the results of the proficiency examination for the rank of Major and ratify them.

- Examine the nominations of officers and take a decision thereon.

b - The Directorate General of the Internal Security Forces shall prepare the following draft decrees:

- Inclusion on the promotion roster for the ranks of Brigadier General and Major General.

- Inclusion on the promotion roster for the other ranks.

- Promotion to the ranks of Brigadier General and Major General effective from the first of the following year.

- Promotion to the other ranks effective from the first of the following year.

4- During the month of June, the Directorate General of the Internal Security Forces shall prepare a draft decree for the promotion of officers effective from the first of July.

The same provisions that apply to civilian employees and wage-earners in the Army shall apply to civilian employees and wage-earners in the Internal Security Forces, and the Minister of Interior shall exercise in this regard the powers granted under these provisions to the Minister of National Defence and the Director General the powers granted to the Army Commander.

The establishment of civilian employees in the Internal Security Forces not referred to in the preceding Article 100 shall be determined in the general establishment provided for in Article 8 of this Law.
Where necessary, the rules for implementing the provisions of this Chapter shall be determined by a decision of the Command Council.

Members of the Internal Security Forces shall be entitled to an annual leave of thirty days, which they may enjoy all at once or in several instalments according to their request and the exigencies of the service. This leave may be spent in the place or places chosen by the persons concerned, whether inside or outside the country.

1- If the exigencies of the service prevent a security member from benefiting wholly or partially from the annual leave, he shall receive at the end of the year, for each day he did not enjoy, a financial compensation equal in value to one thirtieth of his basic monthly salary legally determined at the time this compensation is granted to him.

2- In such a case, the security member may waive his right to the compensation and carry over the remainder of his annual leave to the following year; however, if circumstances prevent him from enjoying the carried-over days, he shall be entitled to receive the compensation provided for in the preceding (Item - 1 -).

In addition to the annual leave, a security member shall be granted an exceptional leave of seven days in the event of his marriage or the death of his spouse or one of his ascendants, descendants, brothers or sisters, and up to four days for other family reasons to be determined by instructions from the Director General.

1- The authority of superiors to grant leaves inside the country shall be determined as follows:

A- The holder of a post specified in the table of strength for:

- A subaltern officer: five days

- A senior officer: ten days

- A general officer: fifteen days

B - A unit commander: twenty days

C- The Director General: thirty days.

2- The powers to grant leaves outside the country, whatever their duration, shall vest in the Director General.

3- The power to grant leaves to members of the Internal Security Forces who are outside the country, whatever their duration, and whatever the country in which the leave is intended to be spent, shall vest in the Director General.
The rules for implementing the provisions of this Chapter shall be determined by instructions from the Director General.

Rewards are a means for superiors to express their appreciation for acts of physical and moral courage performed by their subordinates, or to show their satisfaction with their accuracy in work and their mastery thereof.

Rewards are:

- Written congratulation.

- Written commendation.

- Exceptional seniority for promotion.

- Exceptional promotion.

- Decorations.

- Pecuniary reward.

The written congratulation shall be issued by the Minister of Interior, the Director General, unit commanders, or company commanders, and shall be notified to the person concerned and kept in his personal file.

The written commendation shall be issued by the Director General or unit commanders, and shall be circulated to all detachments subordinate to the issuing authority, and a copy thereof shall be kept in the personal file of the person concerned.

Exceptional seniority shall be granted as follows:

A- For enlisted personnel and non-commissioned officers: by a decision of the Command Council upon the proposal of the unit commander.

B - For officers of the rank of Lieutenant Colonel and below: by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior based on the proposal of the Command Council.

C- For officers of the rank of Colonel, Brigadier General, and Major General: by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior based on the proposal of the Director General.

Exceptional promotion shall take place for the reasons set forth in Articles 55, 84, and 86 of this Law and in accordance with the rules specified therein, with the exception of the dates specified for issuing instruments of promotion of officers, as they may be issued at any time of the year.

Decorations shall be granted for the reasons and in accordance with the rules specified in the Decorations Regulations or in the special regulations of certain decorations where applicable. Authorities may grant members of the Internal Security Forces military or civil decorations for outstanding services they perform that fall within the scope of the functions of such authorities.
The rules for applying the provisions of this Chapter shall be determined by instructions from the Director General.

1- An exception may be made to the rule specified in the preceding Article 95 in respect of members of the Internal Security Forces serving at territorial posts with difficult living conditions or arduous service, as the period may be reduced to less than two years. These posts and the periods of service in both of them shall be determined by instructions of the Director General.

2- An exception may also be made to this rule for one of the following reasons, by a decision of the Command Council with regard to officers, and of the Director General upon the proposal of the competent unit commander or after seeking his opinion with regard to enlisted personnel and non-commissioned officers:

a- For disciplinary reasons.

b - For health reasons established by reports from the Medical Inquiry Committee.

c- By reason of the promotion of the person concerned to a rank higher than the rank provided for in the table of strength for the position he occupies.

d- By reason of the success of the person concerned in a specialisation course where the interest of the service requires not postponing his employment in his new field of specialisation.

e- If the status of the person concerned, following his marriage, becomes incompatible with the provisions of Article 98 of this Law.

f- For a personal interest dictated by compelling circumstances.

Members of the Internal Security Forces may, where necessary, be detached from one detachment to another on a temporary basis and in accordance with rules and conditions determined by instructions issued by the Command Council.

1- Members of the Internal Security Forces may not be appointed or employed in territorial detachments within whose territorial jurisdiction their place of origin or the place of origin of their wives falls.

2- Territorial detachments shall be determined by instructions of the Director General.

Members of the Internal Security Forces may be dispatched abroad as follows:

- By a decision of the Minister of Interior upon the proposal of the Director General for members of the Internal Security Forces of various ranks dispatched to carry out official missions, study courses, or training or specialisation courses.

- By a decision of the Director General upon the decision of the Medical Inquiry Committee for the medical treatment of members of the Internal Security Forces of various ranks in health institutions.

Tasks that cannot be performed by personnel of the Internal Security Forces, and those that do not need to be performed by such personnel, shall be undertaken by civilian employees and wage-earners by way of appointment or contracting from among those who meet the conditions required for this purpose. This shall be within the limits of the general cadre provided for in Article 8 of this Law.

The purpose of penalties is to reform conduct, combat negligence, deter faults, and reinforce discipline.

Every superior, whatever his rank or the post he occupies, shall assist in enforcing disciplinary order by disclosing every offence committed by his subordinates or others and by exercising the powers vested in him by law to take the necessary disciplinary measures.

The penalties that may be imposed on members of the Internal Security Forces are determined as follows:

1 - Upon enlisted personnel and non-commissioned officers:

a - Written warning.

b - Written reprimand.

c - Simple arrest.

d - Strict arrest.

e - Fortress arrest.

f- Deduction of salary.

g - Disciplinary transfer.

h - Removal from the promotion roster.

i - Reduction in rank.

j - Dismissal.

2 - Upon officers:

a - Written warning.

b - Written reprimand.

c - Simple arrest.

d - Strict arrest.

e - Fortress arrest.

f- Disciplinary transfer for those other than unit commanders.

g- Removal from the promotion roster or reduction of seniority therein by one degree or more.

h - Temporary suspension from service.

i - Permanent suspension from service.

1- No penalty shall be imposed on a security member except by his hierarchical superiors.

2- The superior who witnesses or ascertains the offence is the one who imposes the penalty if the offender is hierarchically subordinate to him, and proposes his punishment if he is not hierarchically subordinate to him.
Every penalty must be the subject of a written transaction, and must include a written statement from the person concerned regarding the offence attributed to him.

Penalties shall be submitted hierarchically to the competent authority for ratification in accordance with what is specified in Article 122 of this Law, and hierarchical superiors shall have the right to propose increasing or reducing them, provided that they may not withhold them.

1- A penalty shall not become enforceable until after its ratification by the unit commander, the Director General, or the Minister of Interior, each according to the competence defined in Article 125 of this Law.

However, the penalties that shall be referred to the Director General are:

- Penalties of officers, whatever their significance

- Penalties of enlisted personnel and non-commissioned officers where it appears to the competent unit commander:

- That the infraction warrants a penalty that exceeds his competence

- Or that the infraction warrants a penalty that includes measures the ratification of which does not fall within his competence.

- Or that the infraction constitutes at the same time a penal offence of the nature of a misdemeanour or a felony.

- Or that the participants in the commission of the single infraction belong to more than one unit.

- Or that the infraction has resulted in the loss, damage, or disabling of equipment or buildings belonging to the Internal Security Forces or placed at their disposal.

2- The provisions of the preceding clause shall not prevent, exceptionally, the immediate commencement of the execution of the penalty prior to its ratification for certain serious infractions, particularly those likely to prejudice general discipline.

1- The penalty shall be notified after its ratification to the person concerned and recorded in his personal file.

2- Any person against whom a penalty has been ratified shall be entitled to object to it in writing after the commencement of its execution, and it shall rest with the authority that ratified the penalty to decide upon the objection.

If a member of the Internal Security Forces commits a serious infraction while outside his post or area of operation for any reason whatsoever, and the infraction warrants immediate arrest in reinforcement of discipline, the local unit commander or detachment chief, if he is an officer and of a higher rank than the offender, may place him under immediate arrest within the competence defined for him, provided that the direct superior of the person concerned is notified of this measure by the fastest means.

The penalties set forth below shall be executed as follows:

1- Simple detention: The punished person shall continue to perform his ordinary service inside or outside the post. Upon the completion of his service, non-commissioned officers and enlisted personnel shall remain at their posts and officers at their places of residence.

2- Strict detention: The punished person shall be suspended from service, and non-commissioned officers and enlisted personnel shall be isolated in locked premises specially prepared for this purpose and shall be permitted a short daily walk within the walls of the detention post. As for officers, they shall remain at their places of residence and shall be prohibited from leaving them or receiving visitors.

This penalty shall be executed in practice by making the execution of the fourth day after every three days in the manner of simple detention. The authority vested with competence to confirm the penalty may decide to execute all the days of the penalty in the manner of strict detention or simple detention.

3- Fortress detention: The punished person shall be suspended from service and isolated in a solitary room under guard in a barracks designated by the Director General, and he shall be denied the benefit of simple detention on the fourth day.

4- Salary deduction: The penalty of salary deduction shall apply to deduction from the basic salary at the rate of one-thirtieth of the salary for each day of deduction.

The Director General may, upon the proposal of the unit commander, rescind the enlistment contract of anyone who absents himself from his detachment and does not return to it or is not apprehended within at least thirty days, and his entitlements shall not be liquidated until after his apprehension and the issuance of the final judicial decision concerning him. Decisions to rescind enlistment contracts may be revoked pursuant to a decision by the Command Council, provided that the person concerned meets the conditions specified in Article 49 of this Law, with the exception of the condition of holding a certificate of good conduct. As for the period of absence, it shall under no circumstances be counted as actual service.
The rules for applying the provisions of this work shall be determined by instructions from the Director General.

The penalties of placement in temporary or permanent suspension from service for officers, and reduction in rank or expulsion for enlisted personnel and non-commissioned officers, shall only be imposed pursuant to a decision of the Disciplinary Council.

Members of the Internal Security Forces shall only be referred to the Disciplinary Council for one or more of the following reasons:

1- Habitual misconduct.

2- Committing a grave fault in service or against discipline.

3- Committing a fault prejudicial to honour.

4- Where a judicial judgment is issued against them sentencing them to imprisonment for more than one month for the offences provided for in Item 6 of Article 33 of this Law, or for more than three months for other offences.

Officers shall be referred to the Disciplinary Council by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior based on the proposal of the Director General, and privates and non-commissioned officers shall be referred by a decision of the Director General.

A panel of the Disciplinary Council shall be formed for each case in the decree or decision of referral, and this panel shall be deemed dissolved after taking its decision in the case for which it was formed.

In addition to what is set forth in the preceding Articles 131 and 132, the decree or decision of referral must include:

1- The reason that necessitated the referral.

2- The penalties, from among those provided for in Article 125 of this Law, one of which the panel may decide upon, graduated in the form of questions from the most severe to the lightest.

The panel of the Disciplinary Council shall be formed as follows:

1- For officers:

- A senior officer and a general officer.... President.

- Four officers..... Members.

- An officer ...........Rapporteur

The President, the members, and the rapporteur shall be of a higher rank than the referred officer. Where this is not possible, one or more officers from the Army named by the Army Commander at the request of the Director General shall be appointed, and their names shall be included in the decree of referral.

2- For privates and non-commissioned officers:

- A senior officer..... President.

- A junior officer

- A non-commissioned officer of a higher rank than the referred person, and where this is not possible, a junior officer...... Two members.

- A junior officer..... Rapporteur

The panel of the Disciplinary Council may not include among its members:

1- Anyone related to the referred person by consanguinity or affinity in the direct line or in the collateral line up to the fourth degree, even after the dissolution of the marriage from which the affinity resulted.

2- The complainants or the authors of the preliminary reports and anyone who investigated them or expressed an opinion thereon in an official capacity.

3- Anyone who was previously a member of the panel of a military court or a disciplinary council assigned to examine the same case.

If officers, non-commissioned officers, and privates are referred to the Disciplinary Council in a single case, a single panel shall be formed to examine this case on the basis of the highest in rank among those referred.

The Council must adjudicate the case within one month at most from the date the rapporteur's report reaches the President of the Council.

This time limit may be exceptionally extended by a decision of the Director General upon the proposal of the President of the Council for a period of fifteen days, renewable once.

The referred person shall be entitled to choose a lawyer or an officer to defend him before the Council, and he may also undertake this matter himself, provided that his attendance remains mandatory.

The President of the Council may, for compelling and urgent reasons the assessment of which rests with him, adjourn the session to a later date. The trial may also be conducted in the absence of the referred person if he was notified and did not attend, in which case his representative shall be barred from attending the session and defending him.

The session of the Disciplinary Council shall be held in camera, and shall not be deemed lawful unless attended by the President, all members, and the rapporteur, and it shall conclude with deliberations followed by the adoption of a decision by a majority of votes in a secret ballot in which only the President and the members participate.

1- Both the Director General and the person referred to the Disciplinary Council shall be entitled to object to the outcome of the decision before the Minister of the Interior within:

- 20 days from the arrival of the file at the Directorate General with respect to the objection of the Director General.

- 15 days from the date of notification of the decision to the referred person with respect to the objection of the latter.

2- In the event of an objection, a new panel shall be appointed to examine the case anew, and this panel shall be formed in accordance with what is specified in Article 134 of this Law by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior if the referred person is an officer, and by a decision of the Minister of the Interior if the referred person is a non-commissioned officer or an enlisted member, and the formed panel must abide by the time limit provided for in Article 137 of this Law.

The new panel shall abide, in issuing its decisions, by the following rules:

1- If the objection comes from the referred person, it may not decide a measure more severe than the measure objected to.

2- If the objection comes from the Director General, it may not decide a measure more lenient than the measure objected to.

3- If the objection comes from the referred person and the Director General together, it may decide a measure more severe or more lenient than the measure objected to.

4- If the objecting party is one or more of a group of persons referred in a single case, or if the objection of the Director General concerns the measure taken against one or more of a group of persons referred in a single case, it may not reconsider the measures not objected to.

1- Subject to the provisions of Clause 1 of Article 142 of this Law, the following shall not be subject to any avenue of administrative or judicial review, including an application for cassation or annulment for excess of power or an application for compensation by way of full jurisdiction:

A- Decrees and decisions ordering the referral of officers, non-commissioned officers, and enlisted personnel to the Disciplinary Council.

B - Decrees and decisions ordering the appointment of the Body Examining the Objection.

C- Decisions of the Disciplinary Council and the Body Examining the Objection.

D- Decrees and decisions relating to the execution of the decisions of the Disciplinary Council and the Body Examining the Objection.

2- The authorities competent to refer to the Disciplinary Council and to appoint the Body Examining the Objection, as well as the President, members, and rapporteur of the Disciplinary Council and of the Body Examining the Objection, may not be prosecuted before any judicial authority in a claim for compensation on the grounds of having committed a fault, whether gross or minor.

An officer, non-commissioned officer, or enlisted person whom the Disciplinary Council orders to be discharged from service may not be reinstated into service in any department of the State State, municipalities, or public institutions.

The disciplinary action is independent of the public prosecution action; the outcome of either one shall have no effect on the other, and the institution of the public prosecution action shall not preclude the institution of the disciplinary action and adjudication therein.
The regulations governing Disciplinary Councils shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior based upon the proposal of the Director General.

1- Sick or wounded personnel of the Internal Security Forces shall be treated at the expense of the Administration at their posts, at their homes, at healthcare institutions inside the country, or at private healthcare institutions inside or outside the country.

2- Such treatment shall cover all medically approved health matters.

3- The attending physician shall decide the place of treatment, whether at the post, at home, or at one of the public healthcare institutions, and the Director General shall decide the place of treatment at private healthcare institutions inside or outside the country.

The following shall benefit from the medical treatment provided for in the preceding Article:

1- Members of the Internal Security Forces in active service.

2- Members of the Internal Security Forces who are decided to be placed on permanent disability for health reasons attributable to service.

3- Retired members of the Internal Security Forces or those who are entitled to a retirement pension but have received the severance indemnity.

4- The official who has held the post of Director General even after his referral to retirement.

5- Family members of the concerned persons mentioned in items 1 - 2 - 3 - 4 above who remain dependent.

6- Family members of deceased retired members of the Security Forces who remain dependent, including the family members of the official who has held the post of Director General.

7- Family members of members of the Security Forces who were martyred or died while performing service or by reason thereof, whatever their length of service, and who remain dependent.

8- Family members of members of the Internal Security Forces who died following an illness or accident not attributable to service and who remain dependent, provided that the security member has spent at least five years in active service.

9- Each of the family members referred to in the preceding items must fulfil the conditions prescribed by law to benefit from the retirement pension, with the exception of lawful wives who engage in paid work, as they may be granted the benefit of medical care and treatment provided that they do not receive the expenses of medical care and treatment from any other authority.

If the Directorate General of the Internal Security Forces is unable to secure free medical care and treatment through the health institutions affiliated to it or those contracted with it, the entitled persons may be granted sickness allowances in accordance with the same percentage adopted in the Army.

1- A security officer on leave within the country for any reason whatsoever who wishes to extend his leave for health reasons, or wishes to be granted sick rest, must enter the hospital or be examined by a doctor of the Internal Security Forces, by a military doctor, or by a doctor contracted with the Internal Security Forces or the Army.

As for a security officer on leave outside the country, he may not exceed his leave for health reasons nor benefit from sick rest unless he obtains a medical report explicitly indicating the impossibility of his return to the country.

2- Every mode of leave contrary to what is set forth in the preceding clause leads to the deduction of salary for all the days of the extension, and this deduction shall be decided by the Director General without exempting the violator from the criminal or disciplinary penalties required by the offence.

Health investigation committees shall be appointed annually by a decision of the Director General, to which the following tasks shall be entrusted:

1- Examining the health conditions of members of the Internal Security Forces referred before them in order to determine the circumstances of the illness or accident pursuant to Article 149 of this Law, and consequently determining the duration of treatment.

2- Approving, where necessary, placement in temporary or permanent infirmity and determining the degree of disability in both cases as set forth in Article 151 of this Law.

3- Approving the conditions of those referred before them and determining the fields of employment that are commensurate with their physical capabilities.

4- Approving the cases in which the injured person is unable to attend to his personal affairs.

5- Approving the treatment of members of the Internal Security Forces and members of their families outside the country.

6- Examining the files of those deceased in active service in order to determine the circumstances of death and the extent of its connection with the service.

7- Examining the fathers of those deceased in active service in order to ascertain the extent of their ability to work or their total incapacity.

8- Examining the files of medical assistance referred to them and approving what is appropriate regarding them.

A security member who contracts an illness or suffers an accident shall be entitled to receive his full salary throughout the periods specified below, whether such periods are continuous or intermittent within five years from the date of the onset of the illness or the occurrence of the accident:

1- 18 months if the illness or accident is not attributable to service and not aggravated by reason thereof.

2- 24 months if the illness or accident is attributable to service or aggravated by reason thereof.

3- 30 months if the accident occurred in one of the following circumstances:

a- During an armed clash with the enemy or with outlawed groups.

b - During operations to maintain order and consolidate security.

c- By reason of an assault to which he was subjected during the exercise of his function.

d- By reason of a selfless act to save the life or property of others.

1- If the security member does not recover within the periods set forth in the preceding Article 149, his ailment shall be deemed not completely curable, and it shall be decided to place him on temporary invalidity or permanent invalidity with the determination of the degree of disability.

2- Invalidity shall be temporary for a maximum period of two years when the degree of disability is subject to increase or decrease.

3- Invalidity shall be permanent when the degree of disability is finally determined either immediately upon the end of the treatment period or within the two-year time limit prescribed for temporary invalidity.

1 - In the cases provided for in item 3 of the preceding Article 149, if the accident results in a permanent infirmity that does not affect the general health condition of the security member but limits his physical capacities, such as the amputation of limbs or the disablement of one of the eyes, etc...

He may be retained in service, if he so wishes, and employed in fields compatible with his condition.

2- Invalidity shall be temporary for a maximum period of two years when the degree of disability is subject to increase or decrease.

3- Invalidity shall be permanent when the degree of disability is finally determined either immediately upon the end of the treatment period or within the two-year time limit prescribed for temporary invalidity.

If it is established prior to the expiry of the time limits prescribed in the preceding Article 149 that there is no hope for the recovery of the security member, he may be placed on temporary or permanent invalidity after having been treated for a period of not less than nine months if the illness or accident occurred in one of the circumstances prescribed in item 3 of the preceding Article 149, and not less than five months in other circumstances.
Members of the Internal Security Forces shall be granted convalescence leaves for a maximum period of three months with full active service salary.

1- The Medical Investigation Committees shall be appointed, subject to the approval of the Army Command with respect to Army physicians, in accordance with the following:

A- For officers:

A senior officer...... as Chairman

- Two subaltern officers....

- A subaltern officer...... as Secretary

B - Non-commissioned officers and enlisted personnel:

2- One or more physicians from among the physicians of the Internal Security Forces or of the Army or from among the physicians contracted with these two institutions shall be appointed to each of these committees in the capacity of alternate members, so that each of them may replace any absent physician who is a member of the committees.

3- The Command Council may, where necessary, render the work of the members of the Internal Security Forces in each of these committees continuous, and in such case they shall devote themselves full-time to performing the duties entrusted to them pursuant to this Law.

1- The Director General and the person referred before the Medical Investigation Committee shall have the right to object to the decision of the Committee within a period of fifteen days from the date on which he is notified of the decision, whereupon this decision shall be referred to a Medical Objections Committee for officers or a Medical Objections Committee for non-commissioned officers and enlisted personnel appointed by a decision of the Director General along the lines of the committees set forth in the preceding Article 158. Provided that no person who was appointed to the first committee for a category shall participate in the Objections Committee for that same category.

2- The decision of the Medical Objections Committee shall be final and shall not become irrevocable until after its ratification by the Director General.
