The manner of executing the duties of the Medical Investigation Committees and the Medical Objections Committees, the organisation of morbidity and death files, and the rules for the application of the provisions of this Chapter shall be determined by instructions issued by the Director General.

1- Members of the Internal Security Forces may not contract marriage except after obtaining a marriage permit from the competent unit commanders. As for the marriage of unit commanders, it shall be granted to them by the Director General, and in the event of refusal the decision must be reasoned.

2- Notwithstanding the provisions of the preceding paragraph, a permit to marry a foreign woman shall be granted by the Minister of Interior, and in the event of refusal the decision must be reasoned.

3- The procedures for granting marriage permits shall be determined by instructions from the Director General.

Members of the Internal Security Forces in active service, as well as reservists who have resumed service, shall not be entitled, under penalty of disciplinary and penal sanctions, to carry out the following:

1- Engaging in politics and joining political parties, associations, and syndicates after enlisting in the corps of the Internal Security Forces.

2- Attending partisan, political, syndicate, and electoral meetings.

3- Publishing articles, delivering lectures or speeches, or making statements to the media before obtaining prior authorisation issued by the Director General.

4- Practising any liberal profession or remunerated work outside the work of the Internal Security Forces.

5- Striking from service or inciting thereto.

6- Organising or signing collective petitions on any subject whatsoever.

7- Participating in funerals in an official capacity, except in the cases specified in the regulations of the Internal Security Forces.

1- The same provisions applicable to Army officers shall apply to officers of the Internal Security Forces with respect to the statuses in which they are placed, unless a contrary provision in this regard is set forth in this Law.

2- The Minister of Interior and the Director General shall exercise the powers vested in them pursuant to the laws and regulations when applying these provisions to the officers of the Internal Security Forces.

3- The reserve system shall apply to the members of the Internal Security Forces in accordance with the principles and rules determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior.

Officers whose resignations are accepted may be reinstated once only if, in addition to the general conditions, they fulfil the following conditions:

A- That they are of the rank of Lieutenant Colonel or below.

B- That no more than five years have elapsed since their discharge at the time of submitting their applications.

C- That the difference is at least five years between the age of the person concerned upon submitting his application to withdraw his resignation and the age legally prescribed for his referral to retirement.

1- The same provisions applicable to Army military personnel shall apply to members of the Internal Security Forces with respect to salaries, rank scales, and salary advancement, and the same provisions applicable to Army officers shall apply to officers of the Internal Security Forces with respect to the allowances and benefits allocated to them upon their referral to retirement.

2- By a decision of the Ministers of Interior and Finance, the following shall be determined:

A- The remaining net value of the salary.

B- The percentage deducted in advance from the salary for the account of the Treasury in return for pension deductions, income tax, and fiscal stamp duty, calculated on the basis of the net values.

1- The burial expenses of deceased members of the Security Forces of all ranks shall be paid from the budget of the Internal Security Forces.

2- These expenses shall be determined for each rank pursuant to a decree based on the proposal of the Minister of the Interior.
Whoever assumes the Directorate General shall benefit from all the privileges and exemptions enjoyed by the members of the Internal Security Forces in active service, including war increments.
Informants and members of the Internal Security Forces shall have the right to the penalty share prescribed for members of the Customs Police and its informants in the laws in force.
All other allowances and the value of each of them shall be determined pursuant to a decree taken in the Council of Ministers, with the exception of those determined in the law.

Contrary to the laws in force, the expenses resulting from the following shall not be subject to the audit of the Controller of Expenditure Commitments:

1- Enlistment and appointment of members of the Internal Security Forces of various ranks.

2- Recall of former members of the Internal Security Forces to service.

3- Promotions of members of the Internal Security Forces of all ranks.

4- Military medals to which financial proceeds are allocated. All these cases shall be subject to the a posteriori audit of the Court of Accounts.

The provisions of the Retirement Law applicable to Army servicemen shall apply to the members of the Internal Security Forces, with the exception of the number of years of service that entitle non-commissioned officers and enlisted men to the right to obtain a retirement pension, as a retirement pension falls due to non-commissioned officers and enlisted men of the Internal Security Forces after they spend 18 years in service.
Whoever assumes the Directorate General shall benefit, upon his referral to retirement, from the same rights and privileges allocated to a Major General who assumed the Command of the Army.

An officer who assumes the Directorate General in an acting or deputy capacity for a period of thirty consecutive days, or in intermittent periods totalling ninety days, shall benefit upon his referral to retirement from:

A- 75 % of the total of the representation and travel allowances determined for the Director General in active service, provided that their total is not less than the total of the representation and transport allowances determined in the National Defence Law and pertaining to his rank.

B - The other allowances determined in the National Defence Law and pertaining to his rank.

1- Salary shall be withheld from anyone who is unlawfully absent from service starting from the day of his absence, and his right to receive salary shall not be restored to him except from the date he rejoins his unit.

2- If it becomes apparent to the Director General that the absence resulted from a cause beyond the control of the person unlawfully absent from service, he may determine the salary to be allocated to the person concerned or to the rightful beneficiaries, provided that the period of payment does not exceed one full year. After the expiry of the year, the rights shall be determined by a decision taken in the Council of Ministers.

3- Absence accompanied by the withholding of salary shall not be considered active service, nor shall it be considered seniority in rank for promotion to a higher rank.

The same provisions applicable to Army military personnel shall apply to members of the Internal Security Forces regarding salaries allocated in cases of resignation, going missing, temporary and permanent interruption of service, and temporary and permanent disability.

1- The specialists provided for in Articles 90 and 91 of this Law shall receive a monthly specialisation allowance.

2- A special allowance may be granted to certain non-specialist members of the Internal Security Forces upon whom the nature of their service imposes bearing delicate responsibilities, performing strenuous tasks, being exposed to exceptional hazards, or living in difficult living conditions.

The allowances referred to in the preceding Article 166, the categories that benefit therefrom, and the conditions that must be met by the beneficiaries shall be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior.

In the event of the declaration of a state of emergency or war, members of the Internal Security Forces shall be granted the allowance allocated to Army military personnel in accordance with the following:

1- Every time a state of emergency or war is declared, this allowance shall be granted to members of the Internal Security Forces who are in active service within Lebanese territory.

2- Every time a partial state of emergency is declared in a given area, the same allowance shall be granted to members of the Internal Security Forces who are performing active service in that area.

3- The same allowance shall be granted to reserve members of the Internal Security Forces who resume service, after the passage of one month from their resumption of such service.

4- The same allowance shall be granted to civilian employees in the Internal Security Forces, and contractors, wage-earners, and hired staff therein, in the event that they are employed at their posts by virtue of the need for them outside the working hours fixed for them.
A confinement allowance shall be due to members of the Internal Security Forces when they are confined by order of the Director General in exceptional circumstances relating to security.

The retirement pensions and severance indemnities of members of the Internal Security Forces shall be liquidated by a special committee in the Internal Security Forces constituted by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior.

Subject to the powers of the Command Council, the Director General shall manage the materiel, supplies and buildings belonging to the Internal Security Forces or placed at their disposal, and in this domain he shall undertake the duties specified hereinafter in accordance with the provisions of the laws and regulations in force:

- Assessing the needs of whatever kind they may be and submitting them to the Minister of the Interior, particularly upon preparing the draft budget.

- Procuring equipment and supplies, securing services and executing the necessary works within the limits of the appropriations allocated to each of them and in accordance with the legal provisions pertinent thereto.

- Securing the storage, distribution, maintenance and decommissioning of the equipment and supplies belonging to the Internal Security Forces and verifying that the units and their personnel are equipped with all that they need to execute the duties entrusted to them.

- Securing sufficient reserve quantities of equipment and supplies, overseeing their preservation and maintenance, and ensuring that they are ready for use whenever the need arises therefor.

- Issuing the necessary instructions to organise administrative work in all units of the Internal Security Forces in accordance with the laws and regulations.

- Overseeing the proper application of laws, regulations and administrative instructions

- Organising and managing the special institutions provided for in clause 3 of Article 6 of this Law.

- And he shall exercise the administrative and financial powers vested in Directors General in State administrations.

The Directorate General of the Internal Security Forces shall undertake, through its competent organs and in accordance with the laws and regulations in force:

a- Securing all the equipment, supplies and services that it needs.

b - Executing the new constructions necessary for it.

c- Securing the maintenance of the equipment, supplies and buildings belonging to it and those placed in its custody.

The Ministry of Public Works and Transport, the Ministry of Hydraulic and Electric Resources and the Army Command shall provide to the Directorate General of the Internal Security Forces, where necessary, and upon the request of the latter, the equipment, supplies, services or constructions that it needs, within the limits of the appropriations provided for this purpose in its budget. In this case, the transfer of appropriations from the budget of the Internal Security Forces to the budget of the competent administration shall be effected by a decision issued by the Minister of the Interior and the competent Minister after the visa of the Central Controller of Expenditure Commitment.

1- The Directorate General of the Internal Security Forces may request of the public administrations and institutions and of the Army Command, each within its respective competence, the following:

A- To continue executing the contracts that the Directorate General of the Internal Security Forces had previously requested the competent administration to execute before this Directorate General legally assumed the execution of this Directorate General legally the execution of these contracts through its competent bodies.

B - To hand over to it the files of the contracts referred to in the preceding item in order to pursue their execution through its competent bodies.

2- The Directorate General of the Internal Security Forces shall in all cases undertake the commitment and liquidation of expenditures from the appropriations provided for in its budget, in accordance with the established procedures.

The Administration Regulations of the Internal Security Forces and the Uniform Regulations for personnel of the Internal Security Forces shall be determined by decree upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior based on the proposal of the Director General.

1- Both the Minister of the Interior, upon the proposal of the Director General, and the Director General, after consulting the opinion of the competent unit commander, may grant within the limits of their respective financial powers:

1- Financial rewards to personnel of the Internal Security Forces.

2- Financial assistance to personnel of the Internal Security Forces, specialists, and civilian employees working in the Internal Security Forces.

3- Assistance to retirees and to the families of deceased Internal Security Forces personnel.

4- Social assistance to educational institutions and orphanages in return for accommodating and educating the children of retired or deceased Internal Security Forces personnel.

5- Financial rewards to civilian employees, contractors, and wage-earners employed in the Internal Security Forces or working for its benefit.

2- The rules and conditions for applying the provisions of this article shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of the Interior upon the proposal of the Director General.
The Minister of the Interior may decide, when necessary, and upon the proposal of the Director General, to employ Lebanese and foreign experts at the Internal Security Forces.

The Directorate General may provide services to private persons, institutions, and bodies in return for a consideration the value of which shall be determined by decree upon the proposal of the Minister of the Interior, provided that these financial revenues revert to the funds of the social institutions provided for in Item 3 of Article 6 of this Law.

The provisions applicable to military personnel of the Army shall apply to any person discharged from service after attending a study course, and the Minister of the Interior shall exercise in this regard the powers granted under those provisions to the Minister of National Defence, and the Command Council and the Director General shall also exercise, each within his own competence, the powers specified in all that falls within his jurisdiction under the laws in force.

Former members of the Internal Security Forces shall benefit from the same preferences specified for military personnel of the Army relating to the occupancy of positions in State administrations, public institutions, municipalities, and institutions for which the State provides most of their resources. The same conditions specified for military personnel of the Army in this regard shall be imposed upon them.
The Law on State Civil Servants shall apply to members of the Internal Security Forces in all matters not mentioned in this Law.
Members of the Internal Security Forces are prohibited from performing duties outside those provided for in Article One of this Law.

The service of the Internal Security Forces shall be of two types, ordinary and extraordinary. Ordinary service is that performed by the Internal Security Forces on their own initiative and consists of ensuring permanent surveillance aimed at deterring acts disturbing security and order and those generally contrary to the laws and regulations in force, and suppressing such acts in the event that they occur.

As for extraordinary service, it is that performed by the Internal Security Forces upon a request from the competent authorities in accordance with the procedures specified in this Law.

Members of the Internal Security Forces shall perform their functions openly without dissimulation, and shall, while on duty, wear their official uniforms and carry their regulation weapons.

However, members of certain units specified in the regulatory decree provided for in Article 7 of this Law, particularly those whose work is confined to gathering information in the field of administrative and judicial policing, may operate covertly while performing their functions and wear civilian clothes.

Furthermore, the Director General may, in certain exceptional cases, require personnel assigned to specific missions to wear civilian clothes.

Members of the Internal Security Forces, regardless of their ranks, shall perform their functions within the territorial areas assigned to them. However, they may cross the boundaries of those areas whenever the circumstances of the service and the speed of intervention so require, provided that they notify, by the fastest means, the head of the territorial unit responsible for the area of such intervention. Every intervention of this kind must be justified in the report or record drawn up as a result of the execution of the service.

The relations of the Internal Security Forces with the various authorities revolve around the execution of the tasks provided for in Article 1 of this Law, namely ensuring the administrative police and the judicial police, and assisting the public authorities in the performance of their functions. The administrative police consists in the use of the deterrent means permitted by law to maintain order, consolidate security, ensure public tranquillity, protect persons and property, prevent the occurrence of crimes, and enforce the laws and regulations in force. The judicial police consists in investigating crimes, reporting them, seizing their evidence, discovering their perpetrators, pursuing them, arresting them, and entregar/handing them over to the competent judicial authorities, and it executes the requisitions and letters rogatory issued by these authorities and executes judgments and judicial warrants. As for assisting the authorities, it consists in providing them with armed protection when necessary, at their request, to enable them to perform their functions.

The authorities alongside which the Internal Security Forces work in enforcing the laws and regulations shall not have the right to exercise control over these Forces because they are hierarchically subordinate to them, nor shall they have the right to interfere in the details of their special service.

On the other hand, it shall be incumbent upon all members of the Internal Security Forces to maintain their proper standard with the authorities, showing each all due manifestations of regard and courtesy, and assisting them in performing the legal missions with which they charge them.

The Internal Security Forces shall perform their extraordinary service for the benefit of the various authorities, as set forth in Article 191 of this Law, either pursuant to a requisition or pursuant to a request for assistance.

A requisition is an express request to employ the Internal Security Forces in a legal act falling within their competence, the execution of which is, however, contingent upon a request from another authority specified by law.

A requisition must fulfil the following conditions:

1- That it be in writing, signed, dated, and free of expressions of command. In case of urgency, the requisition may be addressed by means of a recorded telephone or wireless message, provided that it is indicated therein that it will be followed by a written requisition in accordance with the due procedures.

2- That it specify the capacity of the person who issued it and the capacity of the person to whom it is issued.

3- That its execution be within the territorial region subject to the authority of the person who issued it and the authority of the person to whom it is issued.

4- That it specify with full precision and clarity the result that must be achieved.

5- It may contain certain recommendations regarding the type and size of the forces that it is advisable to deploy and the arrangements that it is preferable to take, and the person to whom the requisition is issued shall take these recommendations into consideration when making his decision without their being binding upon him, inasmuch as he remains responsible for assessing the means and ways conducive to the proper performance of the required act.

It is not necessary that the execution of the requisition be carried out in the presence of the authority that issued it.

If a requisition addressed to the Internal Security Forces aims at the performance of a lawful act the execution of which does not fall within their competence, the person to whom the requisition is addressed shall refer the matter to the authority that issued it. If the said authority maintains its position, he shall refer by the fastest means to his hierarchical superiors up to the Minister of the Interior where necessary, and shall abide by the orders issued to him.

However, the execution of such a requisition may be deferred if the authority concerned declares in writing and on its own responsibility that it is urgent.

If a requisition addressed to the Internal Security Forces aims at the performance of an inherently unlawful act, or conflicts with a judicial decision, the person who receives it must follow the procedures specified in the first paragraph of the preceding Article 199.

However, under no circumstances may such a requisition be executed, even if the authority that issued the requisition declares in writing that it bears the responsibility therefor.

Members of the Internal Security Forces who refrain from executing lawful requisitions shall be subject to penal prosecution, particularly if harm to public safety results from their refraining.

Members of the Internal Security Forces who execute requisitions that are inherently unlawful or those that conflict with judicial decisions shall also be subject to penal prosecution.

A request for assistance is a request addressed by one of the competent authorities to the Internal Security Forces to secure armed protection for it and for the employees subordinate to it in the execution of measures falling within the jurisdiction of such authority.

Assistance may only take place in the presence of the employee commissioned to execute the measures, and the assisting forces may not intervene in such measures.

Save as aforesaid, a request for assistance shall be subject to the same conditions to which a requisition is subject as set forth in Article 198 of this Law.

Personnel of the Internal Security Forces may not be commissioned to convey correspondence belonging to the various authorities except in circumstances that necessitate the utmost speed in such conveyance, or when the use of ordinary means leads to significant hazards or delay harmful to the conduct of official transactions.
Heads of territorial units shall correspond with the authorities that are of their rank, and vice versa.

Commanders and heads of territorial units shall inform the administrative authorities without delay of information relating to security and of committed felonies and misdemeanours and the outcome of their measures regarding them, and shall execute the requisitions addressed to them by these authorities in accordance with the procedures set forth in Articles 197 et seq. of the preceding Chapter of this Law.

Requisitions shall be mandatory in the following two cases:

- For the purpose of consolidating security.

- For the purpose of using weapons in consolidating security.

The authorities entitled to address these requisitions are:

- The Governors (Muhafizun).

- The District Commissioners (Qaimaqamun).

Each within the territorial scope of his work.

- The Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies: within the building of the Chamber and its perimeter and in the perimeter of his residence.

The Director General of the Internal Security Forces, the officers of the Internal Security Forces, and the non-commissioned officers in the territorial units and in the Judicial Police are auxiliary judicial police officers to the Public Prosecutors and to the Government Commissioner before the Military Court, within the areas of their work, and they shall carry out their measures in the field of the judicial police, and their relations with the aforementioned judicial authorities shall be regulated in accordance with what is set forth in the Code of Criminal Procedure, the Code of Military Justice, and the law that determines jurisdictions in offences relating to personnel of the Internal Security Forces.

The judicial authorities shall address their correspondence to the commanders, commanding officers, and heads of units in the Internal Security Forces, and these latter shall work to execute what is requested therein either in person or through their subordinates according to its importance.

In addition to the duties assigned to the Internal Security Forces in the field of the judicial police, the judiciary may request them to transfer and bring out prisoners and to maintain security during the holding of hearings or on the occasion of their movements on official duty.

The Internal Security Forces may exceptionally be assigned the notifications provided for by the laws in force with regard to civil or criminal procedure, particularly where there is a shortage in the number of process servers or for security considerations. The assessment thereof shall rest with the Minister of the Interior.
Units of the Internal Security Forces shall not be subject to the military authority except upon the declaration of a state of emergency or a military zone.

In ordinary circumstances, the military authorities may assign the Internal Security Forces the following duties in the absence of military police:

A- Ensuring traffic control for convoys of military vehicles or for military units moving on foot.

B - Escorting convicted or judicially detained military personnel and accommodating them overnight, where necessary, at Internal Security Forces posts in preparation for resuming their escort on the following day.

C- Performing the acts of the military judicial police.

The competent authorities in the Internal Security Forces shall inform the corresponding military authorities of:

A- Information and incidents relating to the safety of the Army.

B - Incidents in which members of the Army are involved.

C- Information and incidents relating to public safety.

The rights of members of the Internal Security Forces in the performance of their duties shall be defined as follows:

- The right to ascertain identity

- The right to search persons

- The right to detain persons

- The right to enter dwellings

- The right to seize prohibited items

- The right to set up checkpoints

- The right to use weapons.

The purpose of ascertaining identity is to verify the identity of persons, the legality of their personal status and the lawfulness of the presence of foreigners among them on Lebanese territory, and to detect suspects and persons wanted by justice.

The operation of ascertaining identity shall be carried out by requesting the persons concerned to produce the official document proving their identity, examining that document and completing the operation, where necessary, by way of inquiry, including having them identified by other persons.

The purpose of searching persons is to verify whether they are carrying materials the carriage of which is prohibited by law. The search operation may cover the person's body and the clothing worn by him without exception, the items he is carrying and the vehicle in which he is travelling.

Women may not be searched bodily, nor may the clothing they are wearing be searched, except by women.

Members of the Internal Security Forces shall have the right to enter dwellings in the following cases:

At night:

- In the event of danger such as fire, flood, and the like.

- Upon hearing cries for help or a request for assistance issuing from inside the dwelling.

- Pursuant to a request by the military authority in a state of emergency or in a zone declared military for the purpose of searching dwellings.

By day:

- In the cases in which entry is permitted at night.

- For the purpose of investigating an offence in flagrante delicto that occurred inside a dwelling if it is of the nature of a felony or a misdemeanour.

- For the purpose of searching the dwelling of a suspect in the case of an offence in flagrante delicto if it is of the nature of a felony or a misdemeanour.

- For the purpose of searching any dwelling pursuant to a judicial delegation.

- For the purpose of executing judicial judgments and warrants.

At any time, and for any reason by reason of duty, if the owner of the dwelling permits them to do so.

Members of the Internal Security Forces shall have the right, by reason of duty, to enter premises open to the public during the times at which people are permitted to enter them or during their presence therein.

Members of the Internal Security Forces shall have the right, during their work in the domain of the administrative and judicial police, to set up checkpoints on public roads, for the purpose of searching vehicles and their passengers and ascertaining their identity, and to use physical obstacles at such checkpoints, for the purpose of stopping vehicles whose drivers do not comply with signals of warning and caution.

After having taken all possible precautionary measures and exhausted all other means short of the use of weapons, members of the Internal Security Forces shall have the right to open fire with the weapons with which they are regularly equipped in the following cases:

1- Pursuant to a requisition from the administrative authority (Governorates' Governors and District Commissioners) during operations to consolidate security.

2- In the case of legitimate self-defence provided for in the Penal Code.

3- To prevent their being disarmed of their weapons the seizure of the equipment in their custody.

4- To defend their posts and the places they are entrusted with guarding.

5- To retain the persons placed in their custody or to ensure their safety.

6- Following their clear and repeated warning with the phrase "Security Forces, halt" to persons who attempt to flee from before them and do not comply with the warning, provided that the attempt to flee was preceded or accompanied by general or specific evidence confirming or making probable their commission of a felony.

7- In stopping vehicles that pass through their checkpoints despite clear visual signals and auditory warnings.

Members of the Internal Security Forces shall have the right to arrest persons in the following cases:

1- In execution of a judicial judgment.

2- In execution of a judicial warrant.

3- In execution of a request from the competent judicial authority or from judicial police officers.

4- Of their own accord in the case of a flagrant felony and a flagrant misdemeanour punishable by imprisonment, provided that they immediately inform the competent judicial authority and abide by its instructions.

In the first three cases, they shall conduct the arrested person to one of the places for the execution of judicial judgments, or to the judicial authority that issued the warrant or the request, within a period of 24 hours from the time the arrest takes place.

As for the fourth case, it shall pertain to the competent judicial authority to extend this period exceptionally if the necessities of the investigation so require, provided that this period does not in any event exceed three days.

The arrest operation may take place:

- At any time of day or night outside premises open to the public and outside dwellings.

- In dwellings in accordance with the legal conditions prescribed for entering dwellings.

In addition to the aforementioned cases of arrest, members of the Internal Security Forces may resort to preventive detention of an administrative nature when leaving the person at large constitutes a danger to himself or to others, such as one who is in a state of manifest intoxication or the like, or in order to verify the status of a suspected person or one the validity of whose identity is in doubt, and this detention may not last for more than 24 hours.

Members of the Internal Security Forces shall have the right to seize items the transport or possession of which is prohibited by law and items transported or possessed in violation of the law. They shall also have the right, during the investigation of crimes, to seize items that constitute criminal evidence.

Members of the Internal Security Forces shall be subject to the general obligations relating to civil servants, and the penalties and aggravation of penalties provided for by the laws by reason of offences committed by civil servants in the performance of their duties shall apply to them.

Members of the Internal Security Forces, both on and off duty, shall report offences that they witness themselves or of which they come to have knowledge, shall rescue or work to rescue every person in a state of danger, and shall preserve public and private property, particularly in disasters and grave incidents.
Members of the Internal Security Forces may not, other than in the cases provided for by the law, disturb people in their personal liberty.
Members of the Internal Security Forces, when exercising their coercive powers, shall avoid all violence not required by necessity.

Members of the Internal Security Forces are bound by professional secrecy regarding information that comes to their knowledge by virtue of their work. They may not communicate such information except to the authorities competent to examine it. Nor may they disclose the identity of informants to any authority or any body unless the informant himself releases them from this restriction.

The record is the document in which members of the Internal Security Forces register the contraventions that they detect, the measures that they undertake, the information that they gather, the facts of which they take cognisance, their sensory observations, the statements made before them by the concerned parties, the physical descriptions of arrested persons, and the descriptions of seized items.

Members of the Internal Security Forces shall draw up a record in executing every assignment or request for assistance addressed to them by one of the competent authorities, even if such execution does not lead to the desired result, as proof of their attendance and their attempt to perform the required act.
A single record may be drawn up by one member alone, or several members may participate in drawing it up.
The competent authorities may interrogate the drafter or drafters of the report in order to prove all or part of what is stated therein.
The rules for applying the provisions of this Chapter shall be determined by instructions from the Director General.

In addition to the missions of the Internal Security Forces defined in the first Article of this Law, the Internal Security Forces shall be entrusted with the following:

1- Ensuring traffic policing in the capitals of the governorates and in major cities determined by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior based on the proposal of the Director General.

For this purpose, the Internal Security Forces may seek the assistance of the concerned municipal police, where it exists.

2- Managing prisons until the competent administration in the Ministry of Justice assumes charge thereof.

The settlement of the status of officers who were in active service before the date of establishment of the rank of "Major" and who are still in service on the date of entry into force of this Law shall continue in accordance with the provisions of Decree No. 1458 dated 27/11/1979 and the implementing decisions issued in this regard.

As for the status of officers from the rank of Captain up to the rank of Colonel resulting from the abolition of temporary promotion, the settlement thereof shall continue in accordance with the provisions of the legal texts, decrees and decisions that were in force before the date of 23/3/1985.

1- The age recorded in the first enlistment contract, based on the identity papers presented to the Enlistment Committee which approved their validity, shall be considered the true age for discharge and for the liquidation of the retirement pension.

2- As for members of the Internal Security Forces who were in service on 19/1/1955, their true age shall be considered the age recorded pursuant to the 1932 census, and thereafter, including amendments within a maximum period of one full year from the date of their issuance, and no amendment or correction after this date shall be acted upon, whether issued through non-contentious jurisdiction or through contentious jurisdiction.

3- Age shall be calculated as of the date of the day of birth recorded on the civil identity card, and if the date is unknown, the security member shall be considered born in July.

4- Services rendered by members of the Internal Security Forces currently under arms while under the legal age shall be calculated in the liquidation of the retirement pension and dismissal indemnity if such services were completed before 20 March 1930 or between 2/9/1939 and 31 July 1945.

5- The provisions of this Article shall apply as of 1/8/1945.

Lieutenants or first lieutenants who were previously placed on retirement for having reached the statutory age under the provisions of Legislative Decree No. 54 dated 5/8/1967 shall be reinstated into active service with effect from the date on which they were placed on retirement, provided that their age does not exceed the statutory age specified in Article 88 of this Law.

By way of exception, it shall be permissible to:

1- Promote officers for the years 1990 and 1991 while exempting the candidates among them for promotion to the rank of major from the supplementary course and the proficiency examination provided for in Article 82 of this Law.

2- Promote non-commissioned officers and enlisted personnel for the years 1988 - 1989 - 1990 - 1991, including reservists who continue or resume active service.

1- Non-commissioned officers who fulfilled the conditions provided for in Law No. 5/84 may be promoted to the rank of lieutenant and first lieutenant, provided that:

Non-commissioned officers who were appointed in the Internal Security Forces pursuant to Decisions No. 827 dated 25/6/1983 and No. 93 dated 29/1/1985, and whose confirmation was delayed due to the circumstances prevailing at the time, shall be deemed confirmed by operation of law after the lapse of one year from the date of their appointment.
The provisions of Clause 2 of Article 55 and Clause 2 of Article 84 shall take effect from 23/3/1985.

Officers, non-commissioned officers, and enlisted personnel of the Chamber of Deputies Police and their families shall benefit from the medical treatment provided for in Chapter Seven of this Law (Health Affairs).

The Higher Council for Urban Planning is the competent authority in matters of urban and rural planning and shall undertake, in particular, to express its opinion on the following subjects:

- Plans and regulations of towns and villages and zoning plans.

- Draft decrees aimed at establishing real estate companies, expropriating zones, and carrying out land consolidation and subdivision.

- Appeals against decisions relating to building permits and subdivision.

- Draft amendments to legislation relating to the planning of towns and villages and to the Building Law. The Higher Council for Urban Planning shall express its opinion on the matter submitted to it within one month from the date of its receipt, and if the need arises to request additional information, for one time, it shall run as of the date of obtaining the required clarifications. Official holidays shall not be included within the aforementioned time limits. If the Council does not express its opinion within the specified time limit, it shall be deemed automatically to have approved the matter submitted to it.

The Higher Council for Urban Planning may, when examining matters relating to an administration or a municipality or several administrations, invite to the meeting representatives of the administrations and municipalities concerned with the subjects placed on the agenda.

The establishment of the plans and regulations of towns and villages within the comprehensive plan for territorial planning (Amenagement du territoire) is mandatory:

A - For the capitals of Governorates and Districts.

B - For places classified or to be classified as summer resorts or winter resorts and for archaeological sites.

C - For places designated by decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport after consulting the opinion of the Higher Council for Urban Planning.

Plans and regulations of towns and villages may be established for any case or locality or inhabited agglomeration. Several places may be combined into an urban planning zone provided that such places are the subject of a single plan and regulation.
The plan is the graphic document, whereas the regulation is the text.
The plans and regulations of towns and villages may be divided into master plans and regulations and detailed plans and regulations.

The Master Plan and Regulations shall delineate the general scope of arrangement and determine the fundamental rules and directions for the planning of the area, and in particular the extension of residential zones, taking into consideration the relationship between residential agglomerations and neighbouring areas, and furthermore the balance that must be maintained between the development of zones of urban expansion on the one hand, and the preservation of natural sites, agricultural activities, wooded areas on the other hand.

This Plan shall also determine the general land use in the light of the public interest, the locations of public services and basic infrastructure, the general organisation of transport within the area and between the area and the outside thereof, the locations of productive activities, as well as suitable zones for housing extension and old quarters the surroundings of which must be rectified.

The Master Plan shall guide and coordinate the projects of public administrations, public institutions, and municipalities.

A Higher Council for Urban Planning shall be established, composed of:

- The Director General of Urban Planning - as President.

- The Director General of the Ministry of Justice or such judge as he delegates - as Member.

- The Director General of the Ministry of the Interior or such employee of the Ministry of the Interior as he delegates - as Member.

- The Director General of Roads and Buildings at the Ministry of Public Works and Transport or such employee of the second category at least at the Ministry of Public Works and Transport as he delegates - as Member.

- The Director General of Housing at the Ministry of Housing and Cooperatives or such employee of the second category at least at the Ministry of Housing and Cooperatives as he delegates - as Member.

- The Head of the Programmes Administration at the Council for Development and Reconstruction or such person as he delegates - as Member.

- The President of the Order of Engineers in Beirut or such person as he delegates - as Member.

- A licensed specialist in sociology - as Member.

- A licensed specialist in urban planning engineering conversant with environmental protection - as Member.

- A licensed specialist in architectural engineering - as Member.

The three licensed members shall be appointed by decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport, and an alternate member shall be appointed for each of them to replace the principal member in the event of his absence.

- The Director General of the Ministry of Municipal and Rural Affairs or such employee of the second category at least at the Ministry of Municipal and Rural Affairs as he delegates.

- The Director General of the Ministry of the Environment or such employee of the second category at least at the Ministry of the Environment as he delegates.

- The President of the Order of Engineers in the Governorate of the North or such person as he delegates as Member

A member shall be deemed to have resigned ipso jure if he is absent without excuse, whether in person or through his delegate, from three consecutive meetings, or if he is absent in person without excuse from three consecutive meetings and has not delegated anyone to act in his stead, and the Minister of Public Works and Transport shall assign someone to act in his stead from among the employees of the second category at least in the ministry to which the resigning member belongs and after the approval of the competent minister in respect of the Ministries of the Interior and of Housing and Cooperatives, and from among the engineers registered with the Order in Beirut in respect of the President of the Order of Engineers. And from among the employees of the Council for Development and Reconstruction in respect of the Head of the Programmes Administration.

The meetings of the Council shall be deemed valid if attended by more than half of its members. Decisions shall be taken by a majority of the votes of those present, and in the event of an equality of votes, the President shall have a casting vote.

A permanent secretariat provided by the Directorate General of Urban Planning shall be attached to the Council.

The allowances of the President, members and secretariat of the Council shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Public Works and Transport.

- The Director General of the Ministry of Agriculture or such employee of the second category at least from among the employees of the Ministry of Agriculture - Directorate General of Agriculture as he delegates.

- The Director General of the Ministry of Industry or such employee of the second category at least from among the employees of the Ministry of Industry - Directorate General of Industry as he delegates.

The detailed plan and regulations shall determine, within the framework of the master plan and regulations if any exist, the rules and conditions for the use of land within the zone, including the possibility of prohibiting construction; it shall specify in particular:

1 - The boundaries of the inhabited area, after taking into consideration the agricultural value of the land and the possibility of the existence of important facilities for intensive agriculture or for irrigation.

2 - The primary intended use of the lands or the productive activities in each zone.

3 - The exploitation factors permitted for construction in the light of the public facilities available or intended to be established in the zone.

4 - The built-up zones whose special character must be preserved upon the restoration of buildings and upon the licensing of new construction therein, and the determination of the appropriate conditions therefor.

5 - The boundaries and intended use of the road network that must be maintained, modified or established.

6 - The boundaries of quarters, streets, archaeological buildings or natural sites required to be protected or highlighted for aesthetic, historical or environmental reasons.

7 - The lands that must be preserved for agricultural exploitation.

8 - The boundaries and regulation of public squares and parks, sports fields, gardens and various open spaces, and such wooded places as must be maintained, modified or established.

9 - The zones, and within such zones the parts that must be prepared for a specific type of use or for a special form of housing. As well as the zones in which construction is prohibited temporarily or permanently.

10- The sites that must be reserved for public buildings and services and for installations required by social life.

11- The zones in which it is prohibited or permitted, under certain conditions, to establish industrial, commercial and other establishments and to expand existing establishments.

12- The zones that must be arranged by way of land pooling and subdivision in accordance with the Law on Land Pooling and Subdivision in Inhabited Places, or through real estate companies or by way of zone expropriation or otherwise.

13- The technical conditions relating to the area and dimensions of existing real properties suitable for construction and the conditions of subdivision in each zone. The detailed plan and regulations shall determine the easements in the interest of public safety, health, traffic, beautification and the environment, and they may in particular determine the rules relating to the erection and orientation of buildings or groups of buildings and the distances between them, the creation and preservation of architectural perspectives, the volumes of buildings, their maximum and minimum heights, the number of their storeys, their setbacks, their intended use and the regulation of their surroundings. The detailed plan and regulations may include part of the items mentioned above. A detailed plan and regulations may be drawn up for an inhabited agglomeration or for a zone without its having a master plan and regulations, and the detailed plan and regulations shall in such case stand in the stead of the master plan and regulations.

The provisions of the plans and regulations for the planning of towns and villages shall remain in force so long as they have not been reviewed or have not been repealed, in particular the alignments of roads, streets, and public squares; whereas lands reserved for public buildings and services as well as arrangements of public utility shall revert free if expropriation proceedings have not been initiated within a period of ten years starting from the date of publication of the decree and the regulation which provided for the reservation thereof.

Plans approved in accordance with the provisions of Article 12 of this Legislative Decree shall have the effect of alignment and declaration of public utility, provided that they are drawn up on maps at a scale showing the division into plots, and in such case a list of the real properties wholly or partially affected by the alignment or reserved in whole or in part for public buildings and services and arrangements of public utility shall be attached to the plan.

A copy of this list and of the decree of approval shall immediately be notified to the Land Registry Secretariat in order to place the annotation on the real folio of the real properties. As for prior plans approved the date of entry into force of this Legislative Decree without the list being attached thereto, the decrees of approval thereof shall be deemed valid in their entirety and enforceable notwithstanding the non-notification of the lists of real properties affected by alignment or expropriation to the Land Registry Secretariat and the non-placement of the annotation on the real folios of the real properties.

The Land Registrar is prohibited from registering transactions of transfer of ownership, subdivision, and mortgage for any real property unless they are accompanied by a clearance certificate from the municipality and from the competent financial units, and a certificate of alignment and easement shall be produced for sale transactions only, and these documents shall remain valid until the end of the year during which they were issued.

Plans called "zoning plans" may determine in each locality or group of inhabited places, or area, sectors reserved for specific types of use and determine the permitted exploitation factors. These plans shall be drawn up in accordance with the conditions set forth in Articles 10, 11, and 12 of this Legislative Decree and shall become enforceable by decrees taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport.

Areas for which master and detailed plans and regulations are intended to be established may be placed under study by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport after consulting the opinion of the municipality concerned and the Higher Council of Urban Planning.

This decree shall define the area concerned. As from the date of publication of the decree placing the area under study and throughout a period of one year, renewable once in the same manner for another period of one year, neither a building permit nor a subdivision or pooling and re-subdivision authorisation may be granted in the area concerned, and the cutting of woods and forests and the alteration of the natural conditions of the area shall be prohibited.

However, the Administration may place an area under study, and in the same manner followed above, after the lapse of ten years following the expiry of the period of its placement under study, or upon the occurrence of disasters or exceptional events the assessment of which rests with the Council of Ministers.

By way of exception, permits and authorisations may be granted by the competent authorities after the approval of the Higher Council of Urban Planning, and maintenance and restoration works may be authorised after the approval of the Director General of Urban Planning.

The Directorate General of Urban Planning shall prepare the urban planning plans and regulations for towns and villages. The State shall bear the expenses of studying and establishing the plans and regulations. However, municipalities shall have the right, if funds are available to them, to carry out these works at their own expense in coordination with the Directorate General of Urban Planning.

The plans and regulations for towns and villages shall be submitted to the competent municipal councils to express their opinion thereon in accordance with the Law on Municipalities, and such councils must express their opinion thereon within a period of one month from the date of their submission to them; if this period expires without the municipal councils expressing their opinion, they shall be deemed ipso jure to have approved them. The plans and regulations shall thereafter be submitted to the Higher Council of Urban Planning, which may amend them.

The Governor or Qaimaqam of the district shall take the place of the municipal council in villages that do not have municipalities.

The plans and regulations for towns and villages shall be ratified and become enforceable by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport without submitting them for the opinion of the State Council.
The plans and regulations for towns and villages may be revised, in whole or in part, in accordance with the conditions and forms provided for in Articles 10, 11 and 12 of this Legislative Decree.

Easements imposed pursuant to this Legislative Decree for the protection of public health and safety and the preservation of the beauty of nature or the environment, or which relate to land-use designation, the height of buildings, their forms, their colours, the number of their storeys, the setback from the boundaries of the real property, the surface exploitation ratio, the general exploitation factor, the temporary prohibition of building for a period not exceeding two years, and other easements, with the exception of those that are subject to special laws, shall not give rise to a right to any compensation.

Easements established by virtue of the plans and regulations of towns and villages and by virtue of zoning classification plans shall not establish a right to compensation except where the easement prohibiting building (non aedificaudi) is of a final nature such as to render the parcel of land unsuitable for building.

In such a case, compensation shall be due equal to half the difference between the value of the parcel of land prior to the establishment of the easement and its value after the establishment of the easement as at the date of issuance of the decree set forth in Articles 12 and 16 of this Legislative Decree.

Compensation must be claimed, on pain of forfeiture of this right, within five years from the date of notification of the decree approving the plan or the classification to the concerned party, and this compensation shall be determined in accordance with the provisions of the Expropriation Law.

Payment of the compensation due shall be made in instalments over three years at the most.

An annotation of the easement together with the value of the compensation assessed by reason of the easement prohibiting building shall be registered on the real property folio of the property so that it may be recovered in favour of the administration concerned in the event that the annotation of the easement is subsequently lifted for any reason whatsoever.

Real estate companies may be established by a decree passed in the Council of Ministers for the purpose of an overall development of all or part of a zone for which an urban planning plan and regulations have been or will be laid down. These companies shall comprise the owners as well as, subject to the provisions of Item 6 of this Article, all other holders of rights that enter into the determination of the value of the real property, including tenants and operators, and also the relevant Administration; and the word "Administration" in this text shall be understood to mean the State or the relevant municipalities, whether individually or jointly.

1- The Government may decide, pursuant to the decree set forth above, not to include religious endowment (Waqf) properties within the scope of the company, and it may also decide not to include tenants and operators, provided that they are compensated in accordance with due process.

2 - Upon the formation of the company, an appraisal of the real properties and all other rights shall take place, and the owners and all other holders of rights comprised in the company shall contribute all their rights to the company and obtain shares in consideration of these contributions, subject to the provisions of Item 7 of this Article.

Shares shall also be allocated to the Administration in consideration of its contributions in kind and in consideration of the cash funds it may have paid for the purpose of establishing the company and funding its treasury.

3 - The Administration shall expropriate free of charge, for the creation or widening of streets, gardens, public squares, and all other public facilities and constructions, an area equivalent to twenty-five percent of the entire area of the real properties contributed to the company and situated in the zone that is the subject of the real estate company. Currently existing streets, open spaces, and all other public properties, the ownership of which remains vested in the Administration, shall not enter into the calculation of the said percentage. If it appears from the plan laid down for the zone that is the subject of the real estate company that the area of the public properties provided for therein is less than the total formed by the area of the public properties situated within the perimeter of the zone prior to the laying down of the plan plus the area of the twenty-five percent deducted in accordance with the first paragraph of this Article.

The remaining additional area of the aforementioned total shall be deemed private property of the Administration, and the latter shall have the right of option between contributing this area to the company in consideration of being given shares equal to the value of these contributions, or obtaining in kind plots of land equivalent to the said area upon the development of the zone and the subdivision of the lands.

4 - Immediately upon the publication of the decree licensing the incorporation of the company, the provisions resulting from the effect of an approved alignment plan or a declaration of public utility with respect to the granting of building or restoration permits shall apply to the entire zone that is the subject of the company.

5 - The owners and holders of rights shall continue to dispose of their properties until the convening of the constituent assembly that declares the incorporation of the company in the legal manner. This right shall be transferred to the company as of that date.

6 - The Administration may, by a decree passed in the Council of Ministers, grant holders of rights the value of whose rights does not exceed a certain amount determined by the said decree the option between contributing their rights to the company in return for shares or receiving payment for these rights in cash, in a single lump sum or in instalments. In this case, the Administration shall be subrogated to the holders of rights in all their rights and shall obtain shares in the company in consideration of its contribution of these rights.

7 - Rights of possessory mortgage, non-possessory mortgage, privilege, and attachment on the real property or the commercial establishment situated in the zone that is the subject of the real estate company shall be struck off upon the making of the contributions in kind to the company, and these rights shall be transferred, with the same prior rank that each of them held, to the shares accruing to the owner of such real property or establishment in consideration of his contributions.

8 - Contributions in kind for the formation of the capital of the real estate company shall not be subject to the verification procedure provided for in Article 81 of the Code of Commerce.

9 - The company shall develop the zone in accordance with the provisions of the plan and regulations pertaining to it, and it may sell the developed lands as well as construct buildings thereon and sell, lease, or operate them.

10- Everything relating to the regulation of the said real estate companies, and in particular their mission, the categories of shareholders therein, the rules of their incorporation, their duration, their management, the conduct of their business, their financing, their supervision, and their liquidation, shall be determined by a decree passed in the Council of Ministers.

11- The net funds resulting from such sales, leasing, or operation shall be distributed to the shareholders in proportion to the shares they hold.

The administrations shall be entitled to expropriate the areas indicated on the plan and designated for public interests, such as streets, roads, squares, gardens, public buildings, etc. They shall also be entitled to expropriate the entirety of the areas subject to the plan or those pertaining to a zone thereof, and the properties acquired in this manner may be sold by public auction if necessary after the execution of the works of arrangement, subdivision, or land pooling and reparcelling, and they may also be exploited directly by the administration, or buildings may be constructed thereon and sold or leased permanently, or subsequently resold. The administration or the concerned municipality must expropriate by decree the remaining areas of the real property if they are unfit for construction, for the benefit of the adjoining owners, each opposite the frontage of his real property, and upon their request, each opposite the frontage of his real property.

The owners must, upon the request of the administration, provide the estimated value of this area together with a bank guarantee securing the amounts that may be awarded against the administration as a result of this expropriation.

The administration or the concerned municipality shall take the place of the adjoining owner who refrains from purchasing. The provisions of the preceding paragraph shall also apply to the remaining areas, as stated above, resulting from expropriations effected prior to the entry into force of this Legislative Decree.

The expropriating administration, or any party authorised by law to request expropriation, may settle the rights of the owner by transferring to him the ownership of a real property or shares in a built or unbuilt real property, and may settle the rights of the lessee or operator by delivering to him leased premises equivalent to the leased premises that he occupied and in the nearest possible location thereto.

The expropriation committee in the zone shall determine the value of the real property, the shares in the real property, or the leased premises with which the administration will settle the rights of the right-holders in accordance with the procedures and practices in force for determining expropriation, provided that the right-holder, whether an owner, lessee, or operator, accepts this measure.

The administration shall be entitled, particularly when the parcellation status of the land does not permit reasonable urban planning, to undertake ex officio an operation of land pooling and reparcelling for the entirety of the zone subject to the plan or for a part thereof. Land pooling and reparcelling shall be decided and carried out in accordance with the rules provided for in the Law on Land Pooling and Reparcelling in Populated Areas.

When the urban planning plan and regulations for towns and villages provide for land pooling and reparcelling in a given zone, the administration shall be obliged to carry it out when the total of the applications for land pooling and reparcelling submitted by the owners in the zone reaches at least 20% of the area of the said zone or 20% of the number of plots.

In order to protect woodlands and, in general, natural sites and open spaces located within or near residential settlements, the State or the municipalities may offer the owners of such properties, by way of exchange, building land in return for their relinquishment of their ownership of the land classified as woodland or as a natural site, or of a part thereof. The value of the land offered in return may not exceed or be less than the value of the land relinquished by the owner to the public authority by a proportion exceeding 10%, and the payment or collection of the value of the difference, as the case may be, shall be effected in accordance with the procedures in force.

Furthermore, the owner may be permitted to build on a part of this classified land and at the location that causes the least possible harm to the classified woodland, following the approval of the Higher Council of Urban Planning, and in the event of the exhaustion of the entire exploitation pertaining to the real property or group of real properties, building shall be permanently prohibited in the other parts, and this shall be recorded in the Land Register.

The municipalities or the federation of municipalities concerned may contract with the owners of woodland or natural lands to open these areas to the public for their use as parks in return for an entrance fee collected by the municipality, which shall secure, in particular, the maintenance and guarding expenses of these sites.

The erection of buildings of all types, as well as their conversion, restoration and renovation, shall be subject to the provisions of the Building Law.

A building permit shall only be granted if the works intended to be executed conform to the rules prescribed in the Building Law and the implementing texts pertaining thereto, to the regulations of the zone in which the real property is located, and to the provisions set forth in special texts (aerial easements, classified establishments, protection of the environment and natural sites...) or in the real folio of the real property. The plans and regulations for the urban planning of towns and villages may prescribe, for the zones to which they relate, building rules that differ from those provided for by the Building Law.

In this case, a building permit shall only be granted if the works intended to be executed conform to the building rules prescribed in the plan and in the regulations for the urban planning of towns and villages.

These rules must secure guarantees addressing safety, health, beautification and the environment that are at least equivalent to those prescribed by the provisions of the Building Law.

1- The establishment and exploitation of quarries and crushers in commons, in private properties, and in the public and private domains of the State, public institutions, public administrations, and municipalities, shall be subject to a licence and to conditions and rules determined by the Directorate General of Urban Planning jointly with the competent departments in the Ministries of National Defence, Public Works and Transport, Interior, Public Health, and Finance, to be approved by an implementing decree enacted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport after consulting the Higher Council of Urban Planning. The implementing decree shall also determine the exemptions from the annual exploitation fee that is the subject of item (2) below and the fines and penalties to which an operator who violates the imposed conditions and rules is subject, and it shall also determine, by way of example and not limitation, the administration or administrations that shall undertake technical approval, the granting of licences, the conduct of supervision, and the suppression of violations.

2 - The Minister of Finance shall determine the details of the annual exploitation fee payable by the licence applicant upon being granted the licence to the fund of the competent municipality or to the Treasury fund outside the municipal area, for each square metre of the land area of the quarry or crusher in accordance with the map adopted and approved by the Higher Council of Urban Planning, and the exploitation fee, in addition to the fiscal stamp duty for the expected area and quantity, shall be paid prior to the commencement of work for the remainder of the year upon the granting of the licence and annually in the month of January of each year.

3 - The administration shall be entitled, pursuant to a master or detailed plan, to designate zones allocated for the establishment and exploitation of quarries and crushers which shall have a temporary character that ends upon the end of the exploitation in accordance with the conditions, maps, and final cross-sections established by the administration for this purpose.

4 - Pending the issuance of the implementing decree mentioned in item (1) above, the provisions of Decision No. 253 dated 8/11/1935 (Regulation of Quarries) shall remain in force, with the exception of the provisions of Article 16 thereof, which are repealed and replaced by the text of item (2) above, provided that in this case prior approval is obtained from the Higher Council of Urban Planning. Detailed maps of the site prior to commencing the exploitation of the quarry or crusher or the final maps of the site after the completion of the works must be submitted with the licence application and the documents attached thereto.

The operator or the owner shall be required to rehabilitate the land of the site at his own expense after the completion of the works in accordance with the approved final maps, including the possibility of imposing the rehabilitation and reforestation of the site.

Any operation whose object is the division of a property or several properties into parcels shall constitute a subdivision within the meaning of this Legislative Decree. However, if the purpose of the subdivision is the termination of joint ownership resulting from an inheritance or existing prior to the date of 30/6/1977, the minimum area and dimensions for existing buildable parcels pertaining to the zone in which the property subject to the subdivision is located shall apply, subject to compliance with the remaining regulatory conditions for subdivision in the zone, and the transaction shall be submitted to the competent technical departments to give an opinion before deciding thereon in order to verify the fulfilment of these conditions.

The number of parcels may not exceed the number of heirs in the first case or the number of co-owners in the second case.
Subdivision shall be subject to a prior permit granted pursuant to a decision issued by the competent authority.

An application for the prior permit provided for in Article 28 of this Legislative Decree shall be refused if the subdivision project does not conform to the texts in force relating to urban planning and building applicable in the designated zone, and in particular to the provisions relating to the minimum areas and dimensions of parcels, in inhabited places and groups of places and zones where the provisions in force do not determine such area, the minimum area and dimensions shall be determined by a decision of the Higher Council of Urban Planning.

The application for prior authorisation may be refused, or the authorisation may only be granted subject to compliance with special provisions, if the subdivision is likely to harm public safety and health or natural vistas, or if it refuses to public collectivities the carrying out of new public facilities, or if it is located in an area far from populated areas or in a wooded area or an area of distinctive natural landscapes to which the public authorities do not want construction to extend.

The authorisation decision shall impose upon the subdivider the carrying out of the road network, and it may impose upon the subdivider, according to the importance of the subdivision project and its purpose, the carrying out of certain works, in particular the drinking water network, the wastewater drainage network, the lighting network, the establishment of areas for parking lots, the establishment of open or planted spaces.

It may also impose the contribution of the subdivider, either in cash or by surrendering land free of charge, to carry out the public facilities corresponding to the needs of the subdivision.

The surrender of land free of charge may not exceed one quarter of the total subdivided area except with the consent of the subdivider. Authorisation may be granted to carry out these works in stages.

If the subdivision application aims to divide the property for agricultural purposes and is located in an unzoned area, the contribution by surrendering land free of charge shall not be imposed upon it except for the site of the installations necessary for agricultural exploitation, such as agricultural roads, irrigation canals and drainage ditches, provided that the area of each single plot resulting from the subdivision is not less than /10000/ square metres, even if its purpose is the termination of joint ownership.

It shall be explicitly stated in the authorisation decision that the plots resulting from the subdivision are allocated for agricultural exploitation and that no buildings may be erected therein other than the buildings necessary for agricultural exploitation and for the private residence belonging to the owner of the property and his children, and within a general exploitation ratio not exceeding five percent (5%).

"And upon its rezoning, pursuant to an approved decree, the properties located within the area shall be subject to the new regulations, including the lands that have been divided for agricultural purposes, provided that they are subject to all the conditions of land pooling and subdivision."

The authorisation decision shall become of no effect if the real estate formalities are not commenced within one year from the date of delivery of the authorisation, as well as if the works are not carried out within the period specified in the authorisation decision, which may not exceed ten years. The authorisation decision shall be registered ipso jure in the real folio of the property.

The Government may, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, establish a public institution or institutions of a commercial character for the purpose of rearranging all or part of an area for which an urban planning master plan and regulations have been or will be laid down.

These institutions shall enjoy legal personality and financial and administrative autonomy and shall be subject to the ex post audit of the Court of Accounts to the exclusion of any other control.

The decree establishing these institutions shall determine all provisions relating to their scope and operation, in particular their objectives, powers, management, supervision, methods of financing, and their relations with all other public administrations and institutions and the municipality or municipalities concerned.

First: All or some of the following operations shall be entrusted to the public institution:

1- Temporary acquisition, by way of expropriation, of all real properties located within the scope of its operations, including all rights over such real properties.

2 - Preparing public utilities programmes and executing them directly or through the competent public administrations and bodies and the municipalities.

3 - Consolidating and subdividing the real properties located within its scope for the requirements of the established planning scheme, and redistributing the real properties, after their rearrangement, among the owners in proportion to the rights of each of them.

4 - Preparing the construction programme and securing reconstruction directly or through the owners or through any other agreements it deems appropriate.

5 - Securing the return of tenants and operators to new premises in the constructed buildings, or compensating them.

Second: The institution shall carry out its work as follows:

A- The Administration shall deduct free of charge, for the creation or widening of streets, gardens, public squares, and all other public utilities and installations or otherwise, an area of twenty-five percent of the total area of the real properties located within the perimeter of the area subject to rearrangement.

Streets, squares, and all other public property situated within the perimeter of the area on the date of approval of the planning laid down for the said area, the ownership of which remains vested in the Administration, shall not be included in the calculation of the aforementioned percentage.

If it appears from the master plan laid down for the area that the area of public property provided for therein is less than the total consisting of the area of public property situated within the perimeter of the area prior to the laying down of the master plan plus the twenty-five percent area deducted in accordance with the first paragraph of this Article, the remaining additional area of the aforementioned total shall be deemed private property of the Administration.
