In all these cases, he shall take trade usages into account. He shall decide the dispute as an amiable compositeur if the agreement of the parties defines his mission in that manner. Second: Recognition and enforcement of arbitral awards rendered abroad or in international arbitration

Second - Recognition of arbitral awards rendered

abroad or in international arbitration and enforcement thereof

Arbitral awards shall be recognised and granted leave for enforcement if the person relying on them proves their existence and if they are not manifestly contrary to international public policy. The existence of an arbitral award shall be proved by producing the original thereof accompanied by the arbitration agreement, or certified true copies of these two documents authenticated by the arbitrators or by any competent authority. Where these documents are drawn up in a foreign language, they shall be translated by a sworn translator.

The provisions of Articles 793 to 797 shall apply to the arbitral award. Where the arbitration took place abroad, a certified true copy of the arbitral award may be submitted for the purposes of filing and granting leave for enforcement. Third - Means of recourse against arbitral awards rendered abroad or in international arbitration.

Third - Means of recourse against arbitral awards

rendered abroad or in international arbitration

A decision that refuses recognition or leave for enforcement of an arbitral award rendered abroad or in international arbitration shall be subject to appeal.

An appeal against a decision that grants recognition or leave for enforcement shall be admissible only in the following cases:

1- The award was rendered without an arbitration agreement or pursuant to an arbitration agreement that is null and void or has lapsed by the expiry of the time limit.

2- The award was rendered by arbitrators not appointed in accordance with the law.

3- The award exceeded the mission assigned to the arbitrators.

4- The award was rendered without observing the parties' right of defence.

5- The award violated a rule relating to international public policy.
The appeal provided for in the two preceding Articles shall not be admissible after the expiry of thirty days from the notification of the decision of first instance.

If the parties have waived appeal or have not expressly reserved the right of appeal as set out in the preceding Article, it shall remain possible for them to challenge the award issued by the arbitrators by way of annulment notwithstanding any agreement to the contrary. A challenge by way of annulment shall only be admissible in the following cases:

1- Issuance of the award without an arbitration agreement or pursuant to an arbitration agreement that is null and void or that has lapsed by the expiry of the time-limit.

2- Issuance of the award by arbitrators who were not appointed in accordance with the law.

3- The award exceeding the limits of the mission assigned to the arbitrator or arbitrators.

4- Issuance of the award without observance of the right of defence of the parties.

5- Failure of the award to contain all its mandatory particulars relating to the claims of the parties and the grounds and pleas supporting them, the names of the arbitrators, the grounds of the award and its operative part, its date, and the signature of the arbitrators thereon.

6- Violation by the award of a rule relating to public policy.

If the court before which the challenge by way of annulment is brought annuls the arbitral award, it shall examine the merits within the limits of the mission assigned to the arbitrator, unless the parties agree otherwise.

An appeal and a challenge by way of annulment shall be brought before the Court of Appeal within whose jurisdiction the arbitral award was issued. Both an appeal and a challenge by way of annulment shall be admissible as from the issuance of the contested award. However, it shall not be admitted if brought after the expiry of thirty days from the service of the award granted the enforcement formula.

Unless the arbitral award is subject to expedited enforcement, the time-limit for both an appeal and a challenge by way of annulment shall stay the enforcement of the award, and a challenge brought within the time-limit shall likewise stay its enforcement.

Both an appeal and a challenge by way of annulment shall be brought, and the investigation and adjudication thereof shall be conducted, in accordance with the rules and procedures prescribed for contentious proceedings before the Court of Appeal. The characterization given by the parties to the means of challenge upon its submission may be amended or clarified until the expiry of the time-limit for the challenge.

The decision issued by the Court of Appeal in the cases set out in the first paragraph shall not be subject to challenge by way of opposition and shall be subject to cassation in accordance with the general rules. Subject to the provisions of Article Five of the Code of Civil Procedure, an arbitral award in absolute arbitration shall not be subject to cassation unless the Court of Appeal has annulled the said award. In such case, cassation shall be confined to the grounds of nullity.

An international arbitral award rendered in Lebanon shall be subject to recourse by way of annulment in the cases provided for in Article 817.

The order granting exequatur to such award shall not be subject to any recourse. However, recourse against the latter award by way of annulment shall entail ipso jure, within the limits of the proceedings brought before the Court of Appeal, recourse against the decision granting exequatur or the divestiture of the judge competent to issue such decision.

The recourse shall be submitted to the Court of Appeal within the jurisdiction of which the arbitral award was rendered.

The recourse shall be admissible as from the rendering of the award. However, it shall be inadmissible after the expiry of thirty days from the date of service of the award granted exequatur.
Unless the arbitral award is subject to provisional execution, the time limit for recourse shall stay the execution thereof, as shall recourse lodged within the time limit stay the execution thereof.
The new Article 804 and Article 805 paragraph 2, to the exclusion of all other articles relating to means of recourse in domestic arbitration, shall apply to this Section.

A debtor who wishes to discharge his liability towards his creditor may tender to the latter, through the notary public, the thing or sum which he considers himself, or, indebted for, and deposit it with the same notary public if it is a sum of- money, or deposit it through and in the name of the latter in an approved bank or in the Treasury Fund. If the thing tendered cannot be transported to the office of the notary public, the debtor shall tender to the creditor the taking of delivery thereof at a designated place, and shall give the notary public the necessary authorisation to deliver it. The notary public shall draw up a record establishing the tender and deposit, setting forth the designation of the thing tendered and its location in a manner precluding any ambiguity, and shall serve a copy thereof upon the party to whom the tender is made without delay.

An Execution Department shall be attached to the Court of First Instance and shall be presided over by the Single Judge in the district subordinate to it. Where there are multiple Single Judges, it shall be presided over by the one to whom this task is entrusted. The President of the Execution Department shall be assisted by one or more execution officers from among the judicial assistants. The expression "Execution Office" shall be replaced by the expression "Execution Department" in any text in which it appears.

The Execution Department shall undertake the execution of judgments, decisions, and orders issued by courts of all kinds that contain obligations the execution of which requires taking measures against property or persons, authentic instruments and all other instruments the execution of which is permitted by law, and the ordering of precautionary attachments, subject to the provisions of laws that entrust such tasks to other authorities. With regard to judgments issued by criminal courts, execution shall be limited to civil rights. If the judgment is enforceable upon its original, it may be executed either through the registry of the court that issued it or through the Execution Department.

Save as otherwise provided by a text to the contrary, the President of the Execution Department shall have jurisdiction to issue decisions and orders relating to execution, and shall have exclusive jurisdiction to adjudicate on the merits of disputes relating to execution procedures and shall take his decisions thereon expeditiously. The President of the Execution Department may decide, in accordance with the procedures followed in urgent matters, to stay the execution and direct the party raising a dispute not relating to procedures to apply to the court of the merits within a time limit that he sets for him, under penalty of continuing the execution in the event that the application is not submitted within the time limit. On the basis of an action brought before him by the debtor of a monetary debt against the creditor within the notice period and aimed at granting him grace periods for payment, he may decide, in accordance with the conditions set forth in Articles 538 and 539, to grant the debtor grace periods not exceeding six months, without this preventing the taking of conservatory measures. In all cases, the President of the Execution Department may temporarily stay the execution with or without security, even without summoning the adversary, until his decision is issued.

The creditor shall take a position either accepting or refusing the tender, whether by a declaration recorded on the document of its service or by a declaration submitted by him to the notary public within forty-eight hours at most from the date on which he was served, and acceptance may not be made subject to a condition or reservation. In the event that the tender is refused, the notary public shall serve notice thereof upon the debtor. If the creditor declares acceptance of the tender, the notary public may deliver to him the thing or the sum deposited with him or in his name or located in the place designated in the tender. If he fails to demand delivery thereof, he shall bear the risks of its perishing and the debtor shall be discharged from the debt. If the creditor refuses the tender and the tendered thing is not in the possession of the notary public and is capable of being moved, the debtor may request the judge of urgent matters, within two days from the date on which he was served with notice of the creditor's refusal, for leave to deposit it in the place designated by the judge; whereas if the thing is intended to remain where it is located, the debtor may request the aforementioned judge to place it under receivership.

The debtor shall, under penalty of forfeiture of the effects resulting from the tender and deposit, bring an action within ten days from the date on which he was served with notice of the creditor's refusal to establish the validity of the tender and deposit. The creditor shall have the right, within ten days from the date of issuance of his refusal, to bring an action to establish the nullity of the tender and deposit. An action brought to establish the validity of the tender and deposit or to annul it shall be submitted in accordance with the rules laid down for the institution of actions. This action may be submitted by way of an incidental application in an original action in accordance with the rules relating to incidental applications.

The judgment pronouncing the validity of the tender and deposit shall declare the discharge of the debtor from the date of the tender and deposit. As from the date of the deposit, interest shall cease to run on the amount of the debt, the debtor shall be relieved of liability for delay in performance, and the expenses and risks shall pass to the charge of the creditor.

The debtor may make the tender at the hearing before the court without any other formalities if the person to whom the tender is addressed is present. Upon refusal of the tender, the court shall order the deposit of the tendered sum with the Treasury Fund against a receipt in its name. The notary public shall draw up a record establishing the deposit and what was stated in the minutes of the hearing regarding the tender and its refusal. If what is tendered at the hearing is other than money, the party making the tender shall be bound to request the court to appoint a receiver over it. The judgment issued appointing the receiver shall not be subject to any recourse. The party making the tender may immediately request judgment for the validity of the tender.

Upon the execution of judgments, decisions, and judicial orders, jurisdiction shall vest in the Bureau whose seat is at the centre of the Court of First Instance that heard the action in which judgment was rendered, or whose seat is at the centre of the Court of Appeal where the judgment was issued by that Court or by its President in an action brought directly before either of them. Upon the execution of foreign judgments and Lebanese or foreign arbitral awards, jurisdiction shall vest in the Bureau competent to execute the judgments of the court whose President issued the decision granting the executory formula. Upon the execution of authentic and private written instruments and undertakings and all other documents enforceable directly, jurisdiction shall vest in the Bureau within whose district lies the actual or elected domicile of the party against whom execution is levied, or his place of residence if he has no domicile, or the domicile of one of the several parties against whom execution is levied, or the place designated for the performance of the obligation, unless the execution relates to a movable or immovable specific property, in which case jurisdiction shall vest in the Execution Bureau in the district where that specific property is situated. Where there are several specific properties situated in different places, jurisdiction shall vest in the Bureau in whose district one of those specific properties is situated. The provisions of this Article shall apply to conservatory attachment.

If the property upon which execution is sought to be levied, or part thereof, is situated outside the district of the Bureau to which the request for execution is submitted, it shall commission by letters rogatory the Bureau in whose district the property is situated to carry out the acts of execution and to deposit with it the proceeds collected.

The execution officer shall, under the supervision of the Head of the Bureau, carry out all acts necessary for execution, and in particular the following:

1- Receiving petitions and documents, registering them in the registers under serial numbers, giving the person submitting them a receipt therefor exempt from stamp duty, and preparing a file for each case and a record in which the proceedings and the decisions of the Head issued therein are entered, and signing this record. 2- Receiving the sums paid in discharge of the debt, depositing them in the Treasury chest, and distributing them, and receiving the sums collected from the sale of attached property, depositing them in an approved bank in accordance with the decision of the Head, and distributing them. The execution officer may, when necessary, seek the assistance of the public force directly or through the presidency of the Bureau or the Public Prosecution. He may also affix seals without prior authorization from his superior.
Whoever unlawfully resists the execution officer after the declaration of his official capacity shall be liable to the penalty provided for in Article 379 of the Penal Code.

Officials of the enforcement departments are prohibited, under penalty of the punishment provided for in Article 364 of the Penal Code, from purchasing, by themselves or through interposed persons or on behalf of others, property offered at public auction or attached before the department to which they belong.

Compulsory enforcement may not take place except by virtue of an enforceable title. Enforceable titles are enforceable judgments, judicial decisions and orders, and arbitral awards, official and private instruments, and all other documents that the law considers directly enforceable.
Subject to the provisions on provisional enforcement, a judgment shall not be subject to compulsory enforcement unless it has the status of res judicata as defined by Article 553.

An application for enforcement shall be submitted by way of a petition filed with the enforcement department and shall include the first name, surname, domicile and capacity of the enforcement applicant, and the first name, surname, domicile and capacity of the party against whom enforcement is sought, as well as a statement of the title sought to be enforced, the amount of the debt or the nature of the obligation, and the property requested to be attached. The title requested to be enforced shall be attached to the application.

The petition must also include the designation of an elected domicile for the enforcement applicant within the jurisdiction of the enforcement department if he has a domicile therein.

If the enforcement applicant does not designate an elected domicile for himself in the petition in the aforementioned case, the registry of the enforcement department shall be considered an elected domicile for him, and thereupon the notifications pertaining to him shall be made to the chief clerk of the enforcement department and a copy of the document requested to be served shall be posted on the noticeboard at the door of the department.

Every objection to enforcement must include the designation of an elected domicile for the objecting party within the jurisdiction of the enforcement department if he does not have a domicile therein, failing which the provision of the preceding paragraph must be followed.

A party against whom enforcement is sought who has no domicile within the jurisdiction of the enforcement department must designate an elected domicile for himself within that jurisdiction by a declaration recorded by him on the document of service of the application for enforcement or the procedural formal notice, or submitted by him to the enforcement officer within the time limit of the formal notice, failing which the provisions of the third paragraph of this Article shall apply.

If the enforcement applicant or the party against whom enforcement is sought is represented by an attorney, his office shall be deemed an elected domicile for him and he may be served therein wherever this office is located.

The preceding rules shall apply whether enforcement is requested by the creditor or requested voluntarily by the debtor. ''

The title sought to be enforced must be served upon the party against whom enforcement is sought, in person or at his domicile, together with a formal notice to him to enforce voluntarily within a time limit not exceeding five days. Service of the title shall be dispensed with in the event that it was previously served upon the party against whom enforcement is sought. Enforcement of a judgment enforceable on its original copy shall take place without formal notice.

If the enforcement of a judgment or instrument is conditional upon the performance of an obligation, or upon the provision of a surety, the enforcement applicant shall attach to his petition the documents proving the performance of the obligation or the provision of the suretyship; and, in lieu of the suretyship, it shall be permissible to deposit a sum of money, financial securities, or guarantees accepted by the judge, or for the enforcement applicant to accept the deposit of the proceeds of enforcement with an approved bank or the delivery of the thing adjudicated to a custodian. The adversary may contest before the Enforcement Department, as against the enforcement applicant, the solvency of the surety or the custodian or the sufficiency of the deposited funds and the guarantees provided, and the decision issued in this regard shall not be subject to any recourse.

The creditors of the party against whom enforcement is pursued shall, if their debt satisfies the legal conditions for enforcement, have the right to join in the executory attachment proceedings carried out on movable or immovable property in accordance with the rules provided for in this Law. Whoever is subrogated by law or by agreement to the rights of the creditor shall replace him in the enforcement measures that have been taken.

If the debtor dies, loses his capacity, or the capacity of the person legally representing him ceases prior to the submission of the application for enforcement, enforcement may not be carried out against his heirs or whoever replaces him until five days have elapsed from the date of serving them with the executory instrument. After the submission of the application for enforcement, the provisions of Articles 505 to 508 shall apply.

If the creditor or the debtor dies and a dispute arises as to the capacity of the heirs or it becomes impossible to identify them, the Head of the Enforcement Department may, upon the request of the claimant to the inheritance or an interested party, levy a conservatory attachment and appoint a representative for the heirs.

If a full year elapses and neither the enforcement applicant nor any of the participants in the enforcement proceedings performs an act to pursue them, such proceedings shall lapse by a decision issued by the Head of the Enforcement Department upon the request of one of the parties thereto or of his own motion and after notifying the parties to submit their observations within a time limit of five days, unless a decision staying the enforcement has been issued or a legal impediment has prevented the pursuit of the enforcement proceedings. Such lapse shall entail the nullity of the enforcement petition and the subsequent measures unless they have exhausted their effects. The lapse shall not result in the extinction of the effect resulting from the interruption of prescription.
The provisions of Articles 10 and 11 of this Law shall apply to the enforcement applicant and the party objecting to such enforcement if he is abusive in his application or objection.

The rules of enforcement for a monetary debt shall apply, in principle, to enforcement for an obligation in kind. A judgment ordering the custody, keeping or delivery of a minor to a custodian may be enforced compulsorily, even if this leads to the use of force and entry into the home. It may be re-enforced whenever the circumstances so require.

Litigants in enforcement proceedings must be assisted by a lawyer in cases whose value exceeds

one million Lebanese pounds.

Every creditor holding a personal or real right arising from a contract or undertaking established by an authentic or private instrument may request the enforcement of such instrument directly against his debtor through the competent Enforcement Department. The enforceable authentic instrument is the original instrument or the first copy conforming to the original. In the event of the loss of the first copy, the Judge of Urgent Matters shall rule on the request to issue a second enforceable copy after duly summoning the adversaries.
The application for enforcement shall be submitted to the competent Enforcement Department in accordance with the third paragraph of Article 830.

A copy of the application for enforcement relating to a real property right in rem shall be served upon the Land Registry Secretariat through the auxiliary office for the purpose of registering it in the Land Register. The copy may be delivered to the applicant for enforcement to deposit it with this authority. The Land Registrar must notify the Enforcement Department without delay of the completion of the registration or of the existence of an impediment preventing it.

The Enforcement Department shall serve a copy of the application for enforcement and of the instrument sought to be enforced upon the party against whom enforcement is sought and give him formal notice of the obligation to pay within a time limit of ten days or to submit his opposition to the enforcement within this time limit before the competent court. Upon the expiry of this time limit without the submission of an opposition, the instrument shall become unassailable except on the ground of the total or partial non-existence of the right. This latter challenge shall not stay the enforcement unless it is based on forgery. If forgery of the instrument is alleged before the criminal courts, the Head of the Enforcement Department shall decide to stay the enforcement ipso jure until this allegation is adjudicated by a final and binding decision. However, if forgery is alleged before the civil court, this court shall adjudicate the request to stay the enforcement, and the registry shall serve its decision upon the Enforcement Department for compliance therewith. The first paragraph of this Article shall be inserted into the service document under pain of nullity of such service.

The party against whom enforcement is sought may oppose the enforcement, within the ten-day time limit mentioned in the preceding Article, by a statement of claim submitted to the competent court in the district in which the Enforcement Department is located, and he shall attach to his statement of claim such documents as he has.

The registry of the court shall serve a copy of the summons containing the opposition to execution upon the Execution Department on the day of its submission. The opposition shall not stay the execution of debt instruments; however, the court may stay such execution or make it conditional upon a security if it appears to it that the opposition is based on serious grounds.

If the subject-matter of the execution is not a debt instrument, the opposition thereto shall stay execution by operation of law until the court of first instance renders a judgment dismissing it.

In all cases, neither the opposition nor the stay of execution shall prevent the taking of conservatory measures to preserve the right of the execution applicant.

A judgment dismissing the opposition to execution or determining the right of the execution applicant in a specific manner shall be enforceable immediately and executed upon its original; however, the court may make its execution conditional upon the provision of a security determined by it.

Half of the proportional fee payable upon the execution of judicial judgments and authentic instruments shall be levied on the execution of debt instruments.

The provisions of this Article as amended pursuant to this Law shall apply only to applications for execution submitted after its entry into force, and applications submitted previously shall remain subject to the legal provisions in force at the date of their submission.

If the party against whom execution is sought does not oppose the execution or expressly declares that he does not oppose it, he shall be exempted from the non-advance portion of the judicial fees, and execution shall be carried out without levying that portion from the execution applicant.
If the opposition covers only a part of the right claimed, execution shall be pursued in respect of the other part.

Both the party opposing execution and his adversary, the execution applicant, must be represented by an attorney before the court, unless the subject-matter of the dispute is of a determinate value not exceeding one million Lebanese Pounds.

Judgments rendered in oppositions to execution that are subject to appeal shall be appealed within a period of ten days from the date of their issuance where the parties have been informed of that date, and without the need to submit a copy thereof.

Chapter Four Subject-Matter of Execution and What May Not Be Attached Article 857- The party whose property is attached may, at any stage of the proceedings prior to the occurrence of the sale, deposit a sum of money equal to the debt of the attaching creditors and the participants in the attachment, together with interest and costs, and such deposit shall result in the lifting of the attachment from the attached property and its transfer to the deposited sum, which shall be allocated to the satisfaction of the debt of the attaching creditors and participants to the exclusion of all others.
Article 858- A creditor holding a right of priority, a pledge, or a mortgage over one or some of the properties of his debtor shall not be obliged to execute first against such properties.

Attachment may not be levied upon property the attachment of which is prohibited by law, nor upon the following property:

1- Property of the State and of other legal persons of a public character.

2- Property of foreign States, with the exception of that which is the subject of a transaction governed by the rules of private law.

3- Rights strictly personal to the debtor.

4- Private correspondence.

5- The copyright of an author over his literary and artistic works prior to their publication, and his right to republish them, translate them, or produce them in a new form.

6- Waqf property.

7- Easements and accessory real rights, if their attachment is requested independently of the immovable property to which they relate.

8- Things intended for clothing and bedding necessary for the debtor and his family.

9- Things necessary for the debtor to perform his religious duty.

10- Things intended for consumption, fuel, and forms of income necessary for the subsistence of the debtor and his family for the duration of two months, and the seed grain needed for the farmer's land for the season.

11- Working tools belonging to the debtor, and books necessary for his profession, not exceeding a value of two million Lebanese pounds, leaving to the distrained debtor the right to choose what he retains.

12- Instruments and equipment used for teaching and for the application or practice of sciences and arts, within the limits and conditions specified in the preceding item.

13- One cow, or six head of sheep, or ten goats, and the materials necessary to feed them for a period of two months, in respect of a person who uses them for his craft or work.

14- Things or sums awarded by the judiciary for maintenance or to be expended for a specific purpose.

15- Family allowances, cost-of-living allowances, and sums granted to civil servants, employees, workers, and servants by way of relief.

16- End-of-service indemnities of public sector civil servants and their retirement pensions, provided that it shall not be permissible to attach them up to one half for a debt owed to the State or for an alimony debt for food established by a judgment, with priority given to the alimony debt for food over the debt of the State.

17- Sums or property donated or bequeathed subject to a stipulation of inalienability or unattachability. Provided that the period of prohibition of attachment upon such sums or property shall be limited to ten years from the date the donee or legatee takes possession. Only persons who become creditors after the aforementioned period shall have the right to levy attachment upon the said property or sums.

18- A debt that constitutes the provision for a negotiable instrument in circulation.

19- The text of item 19 of Article 860 was repealed pursuant to Legislative Decree No. 20/1985..

20- The commercial establishment as a whole and the intangible elements thereof, without prejudice to the provisions of bankruptcy and the provisions of Legislative Decree No. 11 issued on 11 July 1967.

As for the tangible elements thereof, they may be attached by way of executive attachment.

The provisions of the Banking Secrecy Law shall be observed.

Article 859 - If the value of the debt for which a conservatory attachment is levied is less than the value of the attached property, the debtor may request the Head of the Execution Department to rule to limit the attachment to part of such property, provided that its value is not less than double the value of the debt for which the attachment is levied, by way of an action brought in accordance with the procedures prescribed for summary actions, in which all the attaching creditors are joined as parties. The attaching creditors prior to the limitation of the attachment shall have priority in satisfying their rights out of the property to which the attachment has been limited. If the attachment relates to immovable property, the decision issued limiting the attachment must be registered in the Land Register in confirmation of the said right of priority.

The creditor may apply to the Head of the Execution Department for authorisation to levy a precautionary attachment upon the property of his debtor as security for his debt.

However, such attachment shall not be permissible as security for a debt that is not due for performance or that is subject to a condition which has not yet been fulfilled, except in the cases specified in Article 111 of the Code of Obligations and Contracts.

If the debt is not established by an instrument, the Head of the Execution Department may decide to levy the precautionary attachment whenever evidence is available to him making the existence of this debt probable.

The application for attachment shall be submitted by way of a petition accompanied by the documents of the debt and the other necessary instruments. If the debt is of an unspecified amount, the Head of the Execution Department must assess it provisionally, provided that there shall be added to the principal of the debt the accrued interest, one year's unaccrued interest, and the expected fees and expenses.

The Head of the Execution Department shall issue a decision ordering the attachment, rejecting it, restricting it by a guarantee, or provisionally assessing the debt, without serving prior formal notice upon the debtor.

The decision rejecting the application for attachment shall be subject to appeal within the time limit and in accordance with the procedure applicable to orders on petitions. As for the decision ordering the attachment and the provisional assessment of the debt, it shall be open to challenge before the judge who issued it within a time limit of five days from the date of its service, and this challenge shall be examined in accordance with the procedure followed in summary matters.

The execution officer shall carry out the acts and measures necessary to levy the attachment upon the property decided to be attached, and to notify the attachment decision to the Land Registry Secretariat through the auxiliary office if it relates to immovable property, or to the competent official departments entrusted with keeping the records of the attached property or with authenticating the transactions conducted in respect thereof, as well as to serve the attachment decision upon the debtor after the levying of the attachment. The rules observed in executive attachment of movable property shall apply to the attachment of movable property, and the rules observed in executive attachment of immovable property shall apply to the attachment of immovable property, with the exception of such rules as are incompatible with the nature and purpose of precautionary attachment.

The attachment shall lapse if the attaching creditor does not submit an application for the enforcement of his enforceable instrument or a claim before the competent court for judgment in his favour for his debt which is the cause of the attachment, within a time limit of five days from the date of the attachment decision, unless he had previously submitted such application or claim. The attaching creditor must prove that he has done so within a time limit of five days from the date of his notification of a notice in this regard from the Enforcement Department, failing which the Head of the Enforcement Department shall declare of his own motion the lapse of the attachment.

However, it shall be valid to submit an application for the enforcement of an unmatured debt instrument in order to prevent the lapse of the attachment, provided that enforcement proceedings are not commenced before maturity.

A copy of the application for the enforcement of the instrument or of the claim provided for in the first paragraph shall be notified to all the departments to which the attachment decision was notified. The notification shall be carried out upon the request of the attaching creditor through the Enforcement Department or the court registry, depending on the assets.

The Enforcement Department shall notify a decision of the lapse of the attachment to all the departments to which the attachment decision was notified in order to strike off its annotation.

The precautionary attachment shall be converted into an executory attachment upon the issuance of an enforceable judgment establishing the creditor's right, and if the attachment was based on an instrument or document that is directly enforceable, its conversion shall not take place until after the expiry of the formal notice time limit without the submission of an objection to the enforcement.

The formalities of the executory attachment shall take their normal course upon the request of the attaching creditor without the need to levy a new attachment, and the Head of the Enforcement Department shall declare the conversion of the precautionary attachment into an executory attachment, and the enforcement officer shall notify this conversion to the Land Registry Secretariat if the attached property is immovable property, or to the competent department if it is a thing the disposal of which is subject to registration with that department.

The attached debtor may request the Head of the Enforcement Department, in the presence of the attaching creditor, to lift the attachment if he furnishes a joint and several guarantee securing the creditor's right in an amount equivalent to the value of the debt which is the cause of the attachment and its accessories. The Head of the Enforcement Department shall assess the nature and amount of this guarantee.
The attachment may be lifted upon the request of the attaching creditor without the need to notify and summon the attached debtor.

The provision of the preceding Article, in relation to paragraphs 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, and 13, shall not apply to the creditor who claims the price of the items referred to in these paragraphs and found in the possession of the person against whom enforcement is carried out or the expenses of their maintenance, nor to the creditor whose debt arose from the supply of foodstuffs.

If, upon levying the attachment, the enforcement officer finds instruments or bills of exchange to the order of the person against whom attachment is levied, he shall take possession of them and collect their value. However, if their maturity date is distant, the Chief of Enforcement shall order their sale by public auction and authorise their purchaser to collect their value.

Subject to the provisions of Article 15 of Legislative Decree No. 25 issued on 4 May 1943 relating to work accidents and Article 57 of the Social Security Law issued on 26 September 1963, attachment may not be levied on the wages and retirement pensions of employees, workers, and domestic servants and on the salaries of public sector officials except in accordance with the following proportions:

1- One-tenth of what does not exceed the official minimum wage.

2- One-fifth of what exceeds this limit and does not exceed three times thereof.

3- One-third of what exceeds three times thereof and does not exceed six times thereof.

4- One-half of what exceeds six times thereof and does not exceed nine times thereof. - The entirety of what exceeds nine times thereof. There shall be added to the original salary, wage, or retirement pension taken into account to determine the attachable value everything that exceeds this salary as a supplement thereto, such as bonuses and other increments. Attachment may not be levied on the end-of-service indemnities belonging to employees, workers, and domestic servants except in accordance with the aforementioned proportions, provided that the official minimum wage is calculated on an annual basis.

Subject to the provisions of item 5 of the preceding Article, the wages of retirement pensions of employees, workers, and domestic servants, their end-of-service indemnities, and the salaries of public sector officials may be attached up to one-half thereof in the following cases:

1- For a debt to the State.

2- For the price of foodstuffs.

3- For an alimony debt.
Assignment may only be made of another portion of the salaries, wages, retirement pensions- and end-of-service indemnities provided for in the two preceding Articles equal to the attachable- portion.

Precautionary attachment on movable property prevents the debtor under attachment from disposing of the property by way of a disposal transferring ownership or from establishing any rights thereon.

If the attached property is immovable or movable property the entries of which are kept and the transactions conducted in respect of which are documented in the official departments, the debtor under attachment may dispose of it, establish any rights thereon, and subdivide it, provided that the new owner or the acquirer of the right bears the results of this attachment and the results of the action on the merits relating to the debt that is the cause of the attachment.

In all cases, the exploitation of the attached property and the enjoyment of its revenue shall remain with the debtor under attachment unless the Head of the Execution Department appoints a judicial receiver over this property.

If the property attached by way of precautionary attachment is in the hands of a third party, the officer who effects the attachment shall deliver to this person a copy of the attachment decision and a copy of the record concerning the attachment of the property in his hands.

Anyone who has a right of priority or a right to follow over movable corporeal property may request from the Head of the Execution Department within the jurisdiction of which the place where such corporeal property is located lies authorization to levy a revendicatory attachment thereon.

In the cases where it is permissible for the true owner pursuant to the law to claim revendication of movable property against the person holding it, that owner may request authorization to levy a revendicatory attachment thereon.
The rules concerning precautionary attachment shall be followed in revendicatory attachment, provided that it may not be lifted against security.
The judgment issued establishing the right implies by operation of law an order returning the attached corporeal property to its true owner or to the place where it must be.

Every creditor may request from the Head of the Execution Department the attachment of what belongs to his debtor in the hands of a third party of the following property:

1- Monetary sums and debts, even if deferred or subject to a condition.

2- Securities quoted or capable of being quoted on the stock exchange and issued in the form of registered or mixed shares or bonds, and revenues and dividend shares in companies.

3- Shares of interest in partnerships even before their dissolution, regardless of the contrary provisions set forth in Article 909 of the Code of Obligations and Contracts and of the pre-emption rights in purchase belonging to the partnership and to the other partners, provided that the provisions of Article 897, paragraph 3, of the present Law are observed.

4- Fungible things and movable corporeal property.

An application for attachment shall be submitted by a petition accompanied by the documents evidencing the debt and the other necessary records. Where the debt as security for which precautionary attachment in the hands of a third party is sought is not established by an instrument, the Head of the Execution Department may decide to levy such attachment whenever evidence is available to him making the existence of the said debt probable. However, such attachment shall not be permissible as security for a debt that is not due for performance or that is subject to a condition not yet fulfilled, except in the cases specified in Article 111 of the Code of Obligations and Contracts.

A creditor who is himself indebted to his debtor may apply for the attachment of that debt in his own hands, unless it has been discharged by way of set-off. This shall be effected by serving notice of the attachment upon the attached debtor. The Head of the Execution Department may, upon an application submitted by the attached debtor or by any interested party against the attaching creditor, order the latter to deposit the funds into the chest of the Department or with an approved bank within a time-limit which he shall fix. In the event that it is not deposited within this time-limit, the attachment shall lapse ipso jure, and its lapse shall be declared by a decision of the Head of the Department upon an application submitted by the party who applied for the deposit against the attaching creditor. The Head of the Execution Department shall examine each of the two aforementioned applications in accordance with the procedure followed in summary matters.

If the debt constituting the ground for the attachment is not of a liquidated amount, the Head of the Execution Department must assess its value provisionally, provided that there shall be added to the principal of the debt the accrued interest, one year's interest not yet accrued, and the expected fees and expenses.

The Head of the Execution Department shall issue a decision granting precautionary attachment in the hands of a third party, rejecting it, making it subject to security, or provisionally assessing the debt, without serving prior formal notice upon the debtor.

A decision rejecting the application for attachment shall be subject to appeal within the time-limit and in accordance with the procedure applicable to orders on petitions. As for a decision levying the attachment and provisionally assessing the debt, it shall be open to challenge before the judge who issued it within a time-limit of five days from the date of its service, and such challenge shall be examined in accordance with the procedure followed in summary matters.

The provisions of Articles 873 and 874 shall apply to attachment in the hands of a third party during its precautionary stage.

The attachment shall cover every debt that has arisen in favour of the debtor as an obligation owed by the garnishee up to the time of the latter's declaration of what he owes, unless the attachment is restricted to a specific debt or to a debt falling due periodically. If the garnishee has several branches, the attachment shall take effect only in respect of the branch designated by the attaching creditor. Where the attaching creditor does not designate a specific branch of the garnishee, the attachment shall take effect ipso jure in respect of the head office located in Lebanon and its branches situated therein, and service in such case shall be effected at the head office.

Subject to the provisions of the Banking Secrecy Law, no single item of a current account may be attached separately, whereas the balance may be attached, and the service of the attachment upon the garnishee shall have the effect of stopping and liquidating the account, for the purpose of executing the attachment, on the basis of previous transactions even if they have not yet been entered therein.

The attachment decision and its supporting documents shall be served without delay upon the garnishee, along with a notice requiring him to declare within five days the property or debt owed by him, by specifying the tangible assets and the amount of the debt or its balance, its cause and conditions, the assignments made in respect thereof, and the attachments levied thereon.

The text of Article 890 shall be included in the service document.

The attachment decision and its supporting documents shall not be served upon the attached debtor until after the service has reached the garnishee. The service must be sent to the attached debtor within a period not exceeding five days from the date of receipt of the document of service upon the garnishee.

In the event that the attached debtor or the garnishee resides outside Lebanon, service upon him shall be effected in accordance with the provisions of Article 413.

The garnishee shall make his declaration in the form of a reply to the attachment decision, which he shall record on the writ of service or on the attachment record, or submit by way of a petition, or send by registered letter with acknowledgment of receipt within a period of five days from the service. The garnishee must submit an additional declaration of any attachment or assignments affecting the debt subsequent to the first declaration and of any loss befalling the property, within five days from the date he is served with the attachment or assignment or from the occurrence of the event of loss. The enforcement officer must serve upon the attaching creditor without delay the content of the declaration submitted by the garnishee in order to enable him to contest it where necessary.

The original declaration and the additional declaration shall be exempt from any fee or fiscal stamp.

If the garnishee fails to send the original declaration within the prescribed period, he shall become liable towards the attaching creditor for the amount that was the cause of the attachment, unless he puts forward an excuse worthy of acceptance as assessed by the court. If the attaching creditor estimates the amount of the debt owed by the garnishee, the latter shall only be liable for what the attaching creditor has specified.

The precautionary attachment in the hands of a third party shall lapse if the attaching party does not submit an application for the enforcement of his enforceable instrument or file a claim before the competent court to obtain judgment in his favour for his debt, the cause of the attachment, within a time limit of five days from the date of his notification by the Enforcement Department, upon the application of the attached debtor, of a notice that the third party garnishee has been served with the attachment decision, unless he has previously submitted such application or claim. The attaching party must prove that he has done so, within five days from the date of his service with a letter in this regard from the Enforcement Department, failing which the Head of the Enforcement Department shall automatically declare the lapse of the attachment.

However, it shall be valid to submit an application for the enforcement of an unmatured debt instrument in order to prevent the lapse of the attachment, provided that enforcement proceedings are not commenced before maturity.

The Enforcement Department shall serve the decision on the lapse of the attachment upon the third party. There shall apply to the attachment in the hands of a third party, with respect to its conversion into an executory attachment, the provisions stipulated in this regard for the precautionary attachment in Articles 871 and 872.

The third party garnishee must, pursuant to an order decided by the Head of the Enforcement Department at the enforcement stage and within a maximum time limit of five days, deliver to the said Department, subject to the provisions of Article 890, what he has acknowledged, or what satisfies the debt of the attaching party and the amount of the expenses if the declared sum exceeds them or if the third party garnishee neglected to make the declaration and did not obtain a decision accepting his excuse, or what the court has adjudicated in the dispute over the declaration. He may deduct the costs he has expended as assessed by the Head of the Enforcement Department.

The third party garnishee must accompany the delivery with a detailed statement of the attachments and assignments affecting the attached property.

The attaching party may, in the event that the third party garnishee fails to make delivery in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph, enforce against the property of the latter in the course of the same enforcement proceeding without the need to obtain an enforceable instrument against him. After the Enforcement Department deducts the expenses of the proceeding, it shall distribute the remainder of the funds it has received from the third party garnishee among the attaching parties appearing up to the date of the order mentioned in the first paragraph, and shall then deliver the balance to the attached debtor if no other attaching parties have appeared after the said date. If the sum is insufficient to satisfy the attaching parties appearing up to the date of the aforementioned order, a proportional distribution shall take place. Priority rights and the provisions of Articles 898 and 899 shall be observed.

If the attachment covers movable tangible property, it must, upon execution of the attaching creditor's instrument, be sold in accordance with the rules prescribed for the sale of movables without the need for a new attachment. If the attached property is a debt not yet due for performance, it may be sold by public auction by order of the Head of the Execution Department and through the execution officer, unless a contrary provision exists. If the attached property is a share in a company, its sale shall be carried out in accordance with the rules provided for in Articles 937 to 944 to the extent that they are consistent with the nature of such property. In cases where a legal text grants the partners the right to approve the purchase, the partners shall have a time limit of ten days from the date of service of the adjudication decision at the company's head office to exercise this right. If they do not declare to the Execution Department within this time limit their approval in accordance with the legal conditions, the purchaser shall have the right to resort to the liquidation of the sold share. The distribution of the price shall take place in accordance with the provisions of Articles 990 et seq.

If the attached debtor assigns the debt on a date prior to the service of the attachment upon the garnishee, the attachment shall have no effect. If the assignment is subsequent to the service of the attachment upon the garnishee and prior to the service of the attachment upon the attached debtor, the assignee shall be deemed to have the status of a second attaching creditor and shall be entitled to share with the attaching creditor in proportion to his share in the debt, unless the attaching creditor has become a holder of a privilege. However, if the assignment takes place on a date subsequent to the service of the attachment upon the garnishee and the attached debtor, it shall not be enforceable against the attaching creditor.

If the assignment of the debt takes place after notification of the attachment to the garnishee and before its notification to the attached debtor, and a second attachment then takes place after the assignment, the distribution shall be effected in the following manner: first, the share of the first attaching creditor shall be determined by making a proportional distribution among the three parties to the relationship, and then the surplus shall be given to the assignee in preference to the second attaching creditor.

Executive Attachment of Movables Section One

- General Provisions on Attachment

Execution against movables takes place in principle by way of attachment and falls upon movable things and tangible property, as well as negotiable instruments made out to bearer or endorsable that are in the possession of the debtor.

Any attaching creditor and the attached debtor may contest the validity of the declaration of the garnishee by summoning him before the competent court in accordance with the general rules.

If it appears that the garnishee all in bad faith, he shall be sentenced to a fine of twenty thousand to two hundred thousand Lebanese pounds, without prejudice to the right of the attaching creditor to compensation for the damage he has suffered by reason of the delay and expenses caused by such conduct.

Where the contested declaration relates to movable tangible property, the enforcement officer may, pursuant to the authorisation of the President, enter the place where such tangible property is located and levy attachment thereon. If the garnishee conceals it or attempts to conceal it in bad faith, he shall be liable to the penalty for embezzlement and destruction of attached property.

Attachment shall entail:

1- Withholding the entirety of the attached property in the hands of the garnishee from the date he is notified of the attachment, and prohibiting the latter from delivering or paying it to his creditor or from effecting a set-off with him against the debt.

2- Prohibiting the attached debtor from taking delivery of the tangible property or collecting the debt, or from waiving it, reducing its value, granting a grace period to his debtor, or disposing of the attached property to the detriment of the attaching creditor.

3- Deeming the garnishee a custodian of the attached tangible property. Attachment shall not suspend the accrual of interest against the garnishee, provided that the running of such interest shall cease upon deposit. Where attachment is levied upon a registered instrument, it shall prohibit the disposal of the principal, the interest and the yields.

The Head of the Enforcement Department may, upon the request of the attached debtor, decide in accordance with the procedure followed in summary matters to restrict the attachment to a portion of the attached property sufficient to satisfy the debt. The attaching creditor shall have a priority right over the portion to which the attachment is restricted, and the attached debtor may recover the other portion from his debtor.

The garnishee may of his own accord deposit the attached property with the fund of the Department or with an approved bank even if a dispute is pending as to the establishment of the debt of the attaching creditor. The attachment shall remain continuing upon the deposited property and sums. The Head of the Enforcement Department may, upon a request submitted by the attaching creditor or the attached debtor against the garnishee, order the latter, in accordance with the manner followed in summary matters, to deposit the attached property with the fund of the Department or with an approved bank within a time limit that he sets. If the garnishee fails to make the deposit within the set time limit, each of the attaching creditor and the attached debtor may, in preservation of his rights, take conservatory measures against the property of the garnishee. The enforcement officer shall inform the attaching creditor and the attached debtor of the occurrence of the deposit within five days.

The attachment record must contain:

1- The identity of the creditor and the debtor and the domicile of each of them.

2- The designation of an elected domicile within the jurisdiction of the Execution Department for the attaching creditor and for the attached debtor if they are present, if they do not have an actual domicile in that area or have not previously elected a domicile therein.

3- The acts performed by the execution officer, the obstacles and objections encountered by him, and what was decided regarding them.

4- A statement of the attached things and property, mentioning their type, descriptions, quantity, weight or measure, and their approximate value.

5- The appointment of a custodian to take delivery of the attached property after hearing and recording the statements of whichever of the two parties is present.
The attached debtor may be appointed as custodian of the attached property unless its dissipation is feared for serious reasons. He has no right to refuse the custodianship.
If no one accepts the custodianship and the attached debtor is not present, the execution officer must take the necessary measures to preserve the attached property by depositing it in a safe place.

The custodian shall sign the attachment record, and if he does not do so, the preventing reasons shall be mentioned, and a copy thereof shall be delivered to him. The execution officer must explain to him the responsibility placed upon him and warn him that any destruction, embezzlement, or concealment of the attached things, or refusal to deliver them, subjects him to criminal and civil liability.

The custodian may not use, exploit, or lend the attached property. However, if the custodian is its owner or the holder of the right of usufruct therein - he may then use it for the purpose to which it is allocated, unless the Head of the Execution Department prohibits him from doing so in the attachment decision or in a subsequent decision. If the attachment falls upon livestock, tools, or machinery for the management or exploitation of land, a factory, a workshop, or an establishment, the Head of the Execution Department may assign the custodian or another person to undertake the management and exploitation.
Property becomes attached merely by drawing up the attachment record, even if it has not been delivered to a custodian.
The Head of the Execution Department may decide a remuneration for the custodianship out of the general expenses if the custodian is someone other than the attached debtor.

Produces attached to the land or to trees, or standing crops, may not be attached separately from the real property except within the six weeks preceding their maturity. This attachment shall be carried out by way of executive attachment. The levying of the attachment is effected by drawing up a record which has the effect of preventing the debtor from disposing of the produce, and its valuation shall be carried out with the assistance of an expert, and the Head of the Execution Department may, where necessary, appoint a custodian therefor.

The attachment shall be null and void if it is not preceded by a formal notice served by the Enforcement Department upon the debtor at least twenty-four hours and at most five days prior to the attachment, unless the Head of the Enforcement Department decides, upon the request of the creditor, to have the formal notice served and the attachment record drawn up simultaneously. In such case, the attaching creditor shall bear the costs of the attachment if the debtor effects payment within a time-limit of two days from the date of the attachment, unless the debtor had been given formal notice to pay the debt prior to the application for enforcement through the notary public or by registered letter and failed to do so.

The attached debtor may object to the formal notice sent to him by the Enforcement Department or to the attachment by summoning his adversary before the Head of the Enforcement Department, who shall examine the objection in accordance with the provisions of Article 829.

The enforcement officer shall proceed, in order to levy the attachment decided by the Head of the Enforcement Department, to the place where the items and property to be attached are located and shall enter the residence of the debtor after declaring his official capacity, and no search shall be conducted in the residence of the debtor except in the presence of the mukhtar of the locality or a member of the judicial police. The attachment record shall be drawn up at the place where the attachment is levied unless necessity requires otherwise. The presence of the attaching creditor at the attachment proceeding may be excluded if the attached debtor so requests.

If the debtor or any member of his family or his employees refuses to allow entry into the residence, place of work, or warehouse, or if he or the members of his family or his employees are called upon and no one answers, or if he refrains from opening closed doors, boxes, safes, or the like, the enforcement officer may force open the doors and locks, provided that this is done in the presence of the mukhtar of the locality or a member of the judicial police. He may temporarily suffice with sealing the doors with red wax and placing thereon a statement prohibiting tampering with the seals without the knowledge of the Enforcement Department under penalty of the law, or appointing a custodian to preserve the property. The enforcement officer may, where necessary, seek the assistance of the public force in order to perform his duty.

The enforcement officer, upon levying an attachment on produce or crops in their condition specified in the preceding Article, shall state in the record the location of the land, its area, the kind of crops, the trees and their number, and what is expected to be harvested, gathered or yielded therefrom.

The right to gather the produce shall be sold by auction; however, the head of the Enforcement Department may authorise a custodian or the attaching creditor himself to gather it if ripeness has reached a point at which it is feared that the fruits or crops may sustain damage, and the gathered fruits or crops shall then be sold in accordance with what the head of the Enforcement Department decides pursuant to the provisions of Article 923. The custodian or the attaching creditor shall recover what he spent on gathering the produce.

If the attachment covers wrought articles or bullion of gold, silver or a precious metal, or jewellery or precious stones, they shall be weighed, their descriptions shall be specified with precision, they shall be appraised by an expert, and they shall be transported in a sealed package.
The Enforcement Department shall deposit money, negotiable instruments, valuable items and wrought articles in its safe or in one of the approved banks.

If the attachment falls upon property kept in a safe-deposit box rented by the debtor from a bank or upon property displayed in a public exhibition, the enforcement officer shall forthwith appoint the manager of the bank or the manager of the exhibition as custodian thereof. In the first case, he shall seal the safe-deposit box with red wax until he is able to open it and make an inventory of its contents in the presence of the attached debtor or in the presence of the mukhtar of the locality or a member of the judicial police. The custodianship shall terminate upon the Enforcement Department taking receipt of the attached property.

The creditors of the attached debtor may not levy a second executory attachment on the attached property, but they may request their participation in the attachment by an application submitted to the Enforcement Department accompanied by the instruments supporting their right, and they shall elect a domicile within the jurisdiction of the Department if they do not have a domicile therein. Unless they are represented by a lawyer, in which case his office shall be deemed an elected domicile for them and they may be served therein wherever such office is located.

The creditors of the attached debtor may apply for the levying of a new attachment on the property excluded from the first attachment. The enforcement officer may, after the issuance of the decision to levy the new attachment, make an inventory of the previously attached property in the presence of the custodian, if any, draw up a record of the attachment of the property excluded therefrom, and deliver such property to the same custodian or to another custodian. The creditors shall bear the expenses if their application does not result in the discovery of new property.

The sale must cease when the value of the property sold reaches an amount sufficient to pay the costs and the debts of the attaching creditor and the participants in the attachment, the proceeds of the sale shall be allocated to satisfy the debts, and the attachment over the property not covered by the sale shall terminate.
Whoever purchases movable property in good faith at an auction and pays the price becomes the final owner thereof, subject to the provisions of Article 306, paragraph 1.

If the attaching creditor refrains from pursuing the enforcement proceedings despite being notified by the Enforcement Department of the receipt of a request from a participant in the attachment to pursue such proceedings and five days have elapsed from his receipt of this notice, such participant may, by a decision of the Head of the Enforcement Department, be subrogated to the attaching creditor in order to pursue the enforcement. This subrogation shall be notified to the attached debtor.

Subject to the special provisions of the regulations of the Beirut Stock Exchange, shares of whatever kind and negotiable bonds shall be sold at public auction through the Beirut Enforcement Department. Other enforcement departments must send to this Department the securities required to be sold by mail in sealed envelopes with their value declared.

The Head of the Enforcement Department may, if the bonds or shares offered for sale are of significance, seek the assistance of a specialist working in the Stock Exchange or banks in certain proceedings threatening the sale, and he must thereupon decide what publication measures must be taken, subject to the legal provisions and regulations relating to sale on the Stock Exchange.

The attaching creditor shall draw up a schedule containing a statement of the identity and domicile of the interested parties, the nature of the right required to be sold, its nominal and real value, the instrument evidencing it, the securities and rights appurtenant to it, the fixing of the reserve price, and the conditions of the auction. The enforcement officer must summon the interested parties to inspect the schedule and state their observations or objections in a petition submitted by them against the attaching creditor to the Head of the Enforcement Department within a period of five days from their notification of the summons, failing which their right to do so shall lapse.
The Head of the Enforcement Department shall adjudicate upon the objections in accordance with the procedures set out in Article 829. He may reconcile the sale for important reasons.

The Head of the Enforcement Department shall fix a date for conducting the sale, which shall be preceded by the formality of publication and posting in the same manner and within the time limits provided for in Articles 924 to 927. If the sale is not completed in accordance with the foregoing conditions, the provisions of Article 931 shall apply.

The enforcement officer shall serve the application for participation in the attachment upon the attaching creditor, the debtor subject to attachment, and the custodian. Service of the participation in the attachment shall be tantamount to an attachment on the proceeds realised from the sale of the attached property, unless the application for participation in the attachment was received after the cessation of the sale. In that case, its effect shall be limited to what remains of the proceeds after satisfying the attaching creditor and those participating in the attachment prior to the cessation of the sale.

The Head of the Enforcement Department may, in respect of the presence of the previously attached property in separate places, decide according to the circumstances of the case to gather all the property in one place and consolidate the sale proceedings.
The Head of the Enforcement Department shall, within five days from the date of drawing up the attachment record, decide to sell the attached property by public auction.
The sale shall take place at the location where the attached property is situated, or at the nearest market, or at any other place designated by the Head of the Enforcement Department.

If the attached property is perishable or subject to price fluctuations, the Head of the Enforcement Department shall, upon the application of the interested parties or the custodian, decide to sell it from hour to hour in such manner as he deems fit and without necessarily being bound by the procedures provided for in this Section.

The enforcement officer shall fix a time for conducting the sale by day and hour and shall announce the sale by publication in the daily newspapers and in the Official Gazette, and by posting on the walls in the square of the city or town, on the notice board designated for announcements at the door of the Enforcement Department, and at the place where the attached property is situated, at least eight days and at most fifteen days prior to the time appointed for the sale.

The Head of the Enforcement Department shall determine the number of publications and announcements in proportion to the value of the attached property and shall designate the daily newspapers, and he may suffice with the posting formality if the value does not exceed one million Lebanese pounds.
The village mukhtars may be entrusted with posting the announcements in the places designated therefor.
Affixing shall be established by a certificate from the enforcement officer, the bailiff, or the mukhtar of the town, and publication shall be established by submitting a copy of the newspaper.

If the enforcement officer estimates that the value of the attached property is one hundred and sixty thousand Lebanese pounds, and the debtor subject to attachment does not contest his estimate, the estimate made shall suffice; otherwise, the President of the Enforcement Department shall appoint an expert to estimate the value of the attached property, and the estimated value shall be indicated in the notices of putting up for sale.

The sale may not be completed unless the price offered reaches sixty per cent of the estimated value.

Gold and silver articles and precious jewellery shall be weighed accurately and their value shall be estimated by an expert, and the value of antiques shall likewise be estimated, and the estimated value shall be indicated in the notices of putting up for sale. Their sale shall not be completed at a price less than nine tenths of this value.

The enforcement officer shall commence the auction proceedings at the appointed time and place and shall award the property to the last bidder who pays the highest price. Recourse may be had to the municipal auctioneer or to another auctioneer chosen by the enforcement officer, whose remuneration shall be fixed from the proceeds of the sale and shall be considered part of the enforcement expenses. The enforcement officer shall record in minutes drawn up by him all the proceedings that took place before him, stating the name of each bidder and the amount reached by the price of each item or each lot.

If no bidders come forward at the time appointed for the auction, the Presidency of the Enforcement Department shall fix the amount by which it reduces the upset price and then adjourn the date of the sale for at least fifteen days and at most thirty days. Prior to the auction on the new date, the publication formality that was followed prior to the first auction shall be followed. The Presidency of the Enforcement Department may expand the formality of publication and affixing, and the reduced price must be mentioned therein. The President of the Enforcement Department must repeat the adjournment and reduction until a prospective purchaser comes forward. The provisions of this Article shall apply immediately upon the publication of this Law.
The sale price shall be paid immediately, and the enforcement officer may not grant the purchaser any time limit.

If the purchaser refuses or fails to pay the price, the attached property shall be put up for sale anew at his responsibility, and the auction shall take place immediately if possible, and the defaulting purchaser shall bear the difference between the price he offered and the price ultimately paid, together with the additional expenses caused by him, and the minutes of the sale shall be considered an enforceable title against him for the difference in price and the aforementioned expenses. The defaulting purchaser shall not benefit from any increase in the price.

The auction shall take place publicly before the Head of the Execution Department, who shall issue a final and irrevocable decision awarding the property sold to the highest bidder. An enforceable copy of the decision shall not be delivered to the purchaser until after the payment of the price and the fulfilment of the conditions of sale.

The Head of the Execution Department may compel the legal person that issued the original instrument to transfer it into the name of the purchaser or to convert it into a bearer instrument according to the wish of the latter, unless the law or the articles governing such instrument prohibit the same.

If the purchaser fails to pay the price within a time-limit of ten days from the issuance of the award decision, the Head of the Execution Department shall, upon the request of the attaching creditor or any interested party, send him a formal notice to do so within a time-limit of three days. If he defaults on payment, the sale shall be repeated on his responsibility, and it shall be mentioned in the notices that the sale is taking place on the responsibility of the defaulting purchaser, and the initial upset price fixed for the auction and the price at which the first award ended shall be stated therein. The final award decision must order the first purchaser to pay the difference in price together with the additional expenses caused by him. The latter shall not benefit from any increase in the price.

Article 945- Any person who claims ownership of the attached movables may file an objection to the attachment before the Head of the Execution Department and request that these movables be excluded from the attachment. He must deposit in advance the publication expenses if publication has taken place, submit the documents in his possession and clarify the evidence proving his right. The execution officer must thereupon summon, by special writs or by registered letters with acknowledgment of receipt, each of the objector, the attaching creditor, the parties participating in the attachment and the attached debtor to a hearing before the Head of the Execution Department. The Head shall examine the objection in accordance with the rules followed in urgent matters. Execution shall be stayed upon the mere filing of the objection and until the issuance of the decision of the Head of the Execution Department thereon.

Immediately upon receiving the creditor's application, the enforcement officer shall send a formal notice to the debtor ordering him:

1- To perform payment within five days.

2- To elect an address for service within the jurisdiction of the Enforcement Department if he has no domicile therein or has not previously elected an address for service therein,

within the time limit referred to in the preceding item, failing which the registry of the Department shall be deemed his elected address for service.

This applies unless he is represented by a lawyer, in which case the lawyer's office shall be deemed his elected address for service and he may be served thereat wherever such office may be located

It shall also include a statement of the nature of the immovable property or the real right sought to be attached, the number of the immovable property, and the area in which it is situated.
