A copy of the instrument sought to be enforced shall be attached to the formal notice, unless it has already been served upon the debtor, in which case it shall suffice to refer to the instrument, the date of its service, and the amount of the debt claimed.
If the owner of the immovable property or the holder of the real right is a person other than the debtor, the enforcement officer shall send him a copy of the formal notice.

Upon the expiry of the time limit of the formal notice without payment of the debt, the President of the Enforcement Department shall, upon the application of the creditor, order the attachment of the immovable properties. He may, upon the application of the latter, order the attachment and the service of the formal notice upon the debtor simultaneously, in which case the provisions of Article 901 shall apply. The enforcement officer shall immediately send a copy of the attachment decision to the Land Registrar through the Auxiliary Office under whose jurisdiction the immovable property falls, and the latter shall enter it in the daily register at the hour of its receipt and then refer it to the Land Registrar for registration on the real folio of the immovable property. If the immovable property is not subject to the Land Register system, the enforcement officer shall send a copy of the attachment decision to the Mukhtar of the locality, who must immediately enter the attachment in the register in his possession or in a register which he establishes for this purpose, and another copy to the competent Land Registrar, who must immediately enter the attachment in a special register kept by him for each village, town, or cadastral area; service upon the Land Registrar and the Mukhtar may be effected through the interested party, and the said authority must return the certificate of service to the Enforcement Department signed by it beside its official seal and stating the date of service. If the immovable property is under demarcation and census, a copy of the attachment decision shall be served upon the Real Estate Judge for the entry of the attachment in the demarcation and census record.

If all concerned parties acknowledge the objector's ownership of the claimed property, such property shall be released from attachment and delivered to the objector. If they disagree, the President of the Execution Department may, where the novelty of the dispute becomes apparent to him, decide to temporarily exclude the property from the sale and deposit it in a place designated by him or deliver it to a custodian until the merits of the dispute are adjudicated. He may require the objector to furnish security guaranteeing the damage that may befall the attaching creditor, the attached debtor, or the participants in the attachment. The objector must bring the action against the attaching creditor, the participants in the attachment, and the attached debtor to prove his right before the competent court within five days starting from the issuance of the decision of the President of the Execution Department; otherwise, execution shall resume and every measure taken to stay it shall lapse. The court registry shall serve a copy of the summons on the day of its filing upon the Execution Department. The stay of execution shall continue until a judgment is rendered dismissing the action wholly or partially, and such judgment shall be enforceable forthwith.
Whoever claims ownership of the attached property may bring his action even after the sale by auction if the purchaser was in bad faith.

An application for execution against immovable property, an undivided share therein, an immovable right in rem, or a floor or apartment registered in the Land Registry pursuant to the Law Regulating Ownership of Buildings Composed of Several Floors or Apartments shall be submitted to the competent Execution Department, or to the Execution Department within whose jurisdiction the immovable property or all the immovable properties against which execution is sought are located, by way of a petition from the creditor accompanied by the enforceable title and by a certificate from the Land Registry Secretariat regarding the immovable property or properties against which execution is sought indicating their ownership and the rights and encumbrances attached thereto, as well as indicating their descriptions and appurtenances. If the immovable property is not subject to the Land Registry system, the certificate shall be issued by the mukhtar of the locality or by the Land Registry Secretariat on the basis of the special register, and if the immovable property is under demarcation and census, the certificate shall be issued by the Real Estate Judge.

If the debtor's immovable properties are located in jurisdictions falling under different Execution Departments, the Execution Department competent for such proceeding must undertake the execution proceeding, provided that its measures with respect to the immovable properties falling under the other Departments are carried out by way of letters rogatory to those Departments, unless the immovable properties are contiguous or fall within the scope of operation of a single enterprise, in which case a single execution shall be conducted before the Department under whose jurisdiction the headquarters of the enterprise or one of the immovable properties falls.

Where there are multiple execution applicants against a single immovable property, the one who was first to register his attachment shall have the right of priority in pursuing execution. Nevertheless, the one who was subsequent in registering his attachment may request the Head of the Execution Department, by a petition submitted to him and for serious reasons, to authorise him to be subrogated to the one who was first in registration in order to proceed with the measures. The decision of the Head shall be subject to appeal by the means by which orders on petitions are appealed.

Every creditor becomes, since the registration of his attachment or his participation in the attachment in the real property folio, or in the mukhtar's register, or in the special register relating to immovable properties not subject to the Land Register system, or in the record of demarcation and census, a party to the transaction, since the service upon him of one of its measures, every holder of a real right or registered creditor.

By the mere registration of the attachment or participation therein in the manner mentioned in the preceding Article, the attaching party or the participant acquires a real right over the attached immovable property.

There shall not be enforceable against the attaching parties and the participants in the attachment, as from the registration of each attachment and participation therein in the manner set forth in Article 957:

1- Dispositions by the party against whom execution is levied that would transfer the ownership of the immovable property, subdivide it, or create a real right over it, unless the concerned parties, prior to the conduct of the sale, deposit an amount to settle the debts of those creditors and their accessories and notify them of the deposit. Such amounts shall be attached and allocated to the satisfaction of their debts to the exclusion of others. The Head of the Execution Department shall, after the lapse of five days from the notification of the deposit to the said creditors and the non-submission of objections by any of them, strike off the attachment, and he may, upon the request of the depositor, reduce the deposited amounts to the actual amount of the debts and return the excess over that to the depositor. The Head of the Execution Department shall examine the objections to the deposit and the request to reduce the deposited amounts in accordance with the procedures followed in urgent matters.

2- Leases concluded by the party against whom execution is levied, unless they do not lead to a right of extension and their term does not exceed one year in buildings and three years in agricultural lands, and they are accompanied by the authorisation of the Head of the Execution Department, who shall take the necessary measures to preserve the rents so that they may be joined to the price upon distribution.

Contracts of lease, quittances for rent, and assignments thereof and of their rents that are free from fraud and authenticated with a certain date prior to the registration of the attachment shall be enforceable against the attaching parties, the participants in the attachment, and the purchasers at public auction, prejudice to the rules pertaining to the Land Register.

The registration of the attachment shall result in the immobilization of the revenues of the immovable property and its fruits subsequent to the registration and rendering them not subject to any non-immovable attachment. Such revenues and fruits shall be appended to the price upon distribution.

The rent or the owner's share in the sharecropping shall be attached in the hands of the lessee or the sharecropper in the capacity of a garnishee without the need for any measure other than notifying the latter not to pay the debtor. The enforcement officer may direct the notice during or immediately upon his conducting the inspection of the immovable property. The President of the Enforcement Department may, upon the request of the creditor or the debtor, order the deposit of the due consideration with an approved bank.

If the immovable property is not leased or delivered to a sharecropper, the debtor shall be deemed a custodian thereof and bound to preserve it and to deliver it to the Enforcement Department for its sale, and liable for its fruits which he harvests except for what is necessary thereof for his livelihood and the livelihood of his family. If the debtor is residing therein, he shall have the right to remain without consideration, and the President of the Enforcement Department may remove the immovable property from the hands of the debtor if its deterioration or misuse is feared, and in such case he may allocate from the yield of the immovable property an amount for the debtor to assist him in his livelihood commensurate with his condition.

The President of the Enforcement Department may authorize, upon the request of the interested parties, the harvesting of the crops and the gathering of the non-civil fruits and their sale in the appropriate manner and the deposit of the price in an approved bank.

The enforcement officer shall draw up, upon the request of the attaching creditor, the schedule of conditions of sale within eight days from the date of registration of the record of description of the immovable property which he drew up, and he shall state therein:

1- A summary of the previous proceedings.

2- A statement of the attached immovable properties, their appurtenances, the rights appertaining to them, and the encumbrances thereon according to the entries of the Land Register or according to the register of the Mukhtar or the register of immovable properties not subject to the Land Register system or the record of demarcation and census held before the Real Estate Judge, the produced documents, and according to the record of description of the immovable property.

3- The conditions of sale and the starting price as determined by the President of the Enforcement Department on the basis of six-tenths of the estimated value of the immovable properties.

The Land Registrar shall send to the Execution Department, within five days from being notified of the attachment, a statement certifying:

1- The date of registration of the attachment in the daily register and in the real folio or in the special register relating to real properties not subject to the Land Register system.

2- A summary of the rights, encumbrances, attachments and precautionary entries burdening the real property. The Mukhtar shall send to the Execution Department within the same time limit a statement certifying the date of registration of the attachment in the register held by him and a summary of the rights, encumbrances, attachments and precautionary entries burdening the real property not subject to the Land Register system. The Real Estate Judge shall also send to the Execution Department within the same time limit a notice containing the particulars set forth in the preceding paragraph and recorded in the minutes of demarcation and census when the attachment falls upon a real property that is under demarcation and census. Where a legal impediment prevents the registration of the attachment, the Land Registrar, the Real Estate Judge and the Mukhtar shall, or return the documents while stating such impediment to the Execution Department, which shall notify the attaching party of the matter without delay, and they shall also enter a precautionary entry of the attachment.

Within five days from the receipt of the reply of the Land Registrar, the Real Estate Judge or the Mukhtar certifying the registration of the attachment, and after the debtor has in any event been served with the formal notice and its time limit has expired, the Head of the Execution Department shall appoint an expert to accompany the execution officer to the site of the real property and conduct an inspection thereof in the presence of the Mukhtar, a member of the council of elders, or two witnesses from among the residents of the locality, in order to verify the description of the real property and determine its boundaries, its contents and its value. If this work takes more than one day, it shall be carried out successively as the circumstances require. The execution officer shall draw up minutes of the description of the real property and serve a copy thereof upon the authorities mentioned in Article 952, which shall enter in the registers, ledgers or minutes held by them and mentioned in that Article an annotation of these minutes and of what they establish contrary to the entries, and the party seeking execution may register the new constructions on behalf of his debtor, and the registration fees shall be added to the execution expenses.

The party seeking execution shall advance, upon submitting his application, a sufficient deposit to cover the expenses of the inspection and the expenses of the expertise as assessed by the Head of the Execution Department.

Article 966- Within three days from the date of drawing up the book of conditions, the enforcement officer shall send a notice to the debtor, to the holder of a right in rem or a creditor registered against the real property, and to every creditor who has become a party to the proceedings, summoning him thereby to appear before the department to inspect the book of conditions, and to state his observations thereon by way of a petition lodged with the enforcement officer, or to challenge it by way of an objection based on a nullity occurring in the enforcement transaction due to a defect in form or in substance, within a time-limit of five days from the date of service in each of the two aforementioned cases.

The provisions of Article 850 shall be observed when the enforcement is shown on an instrument.

Every person who has been served with the notice shall be entitled to inspect at the department the observations submitted and to state his comment thereon before the decision regarding them is issued.

The objection shall be served upon the adversaries and they shall be summoned to a hearing for its examination before the President of the Enforcement Department.

After the expiry of ten days from the date of the last service of the notice effected in accordance with the provisions of the preceding Article, the President of the Enforcement Department shall examine the observations submitted without the need to summon the adversaries.

On the basis thereof, the book of conditions shall, where necessary, be amended, and his decision regarding these observations shall be final without the need for any service.

The President of the Enforcement Department shall examine, after the expiry of the aforementioned time-limit, the objection provided for in the preceding Article in accordance with the procedures prescribed for examining enforcement difficulties.

The Head of the Execution Department shall order the publication of the notice in two daily newspapers designated by him and in the Official Gazette, and its affixation in the following places:

1 - The noticeboard designated for notices at the Execution Department.

2 - The domicile of the party against whom execution is levied.

3 - The doors of the attached real properties or boards fixed thereto and visible from the outside.

4 - The door of the municipal hall and, in the absence thereof, the door of the mukhtar's house in the area where the real property is located.

5 - The city or town square.

The Head of the Execution Department may, where necessary, increase or reduce the number of publications upon the request of the interested parties.

The formality of giving notice by publication and affixation must be completed at least ten days prior to the date of the auction session. Village mukhtars may be entrusted with affixing the notices in the places designated therefor.

Publication shall be proved by producing a copy of the issue of the newspaper containing the notice, and affixation shall be proved by a certificate from the execution officer, the bailiff, or the town mukhtar.

Every person wishing to participate in the auction shall be required:

1 - To deposit in the name of the Head of the Execution Department, prior to the commencement of the auction, with the Treasury fund or one of the approved banks, a sum equal to the reserve price, or to submit a bank guarantee securing this sum.

2 - To elect a domicile within the jurisdiction of the Department if he has no domicile therein or has not previously elected a domicile therein; otherwise, the registry of the Department shall be deemed his elected domicile. This shall apply unless he is represented by a lawyer, in which case the lawyer's office shall be deemed his elected domicile, and service may be effected upon him therein wherever such office is located.

A creditor whose debt is not less in amount than the reserve price shall be exempted from the obligation of deposit or guarantee, and if the value of his debt is less than the said price, he shall be required to deposit the difference or submit a guarantee therefor, all provided that no other privileged creditor ranks ahead of him and no other creditor shares with him.

The auction session shall be held publicly before the Head of the Execution Department in his department or in another place he deems appropriate, and it shall not be commenced except upon the request of one of the attaching creditors, the creditors participating in the attachment, or the registered creditors holding a right of priority whose debt satisfies the legal conditions for execution, or one of the debtors, or a third-party holder to whom the real property was transferred encumbered with a registered mortgage, charge, or privilege, and the bailiff shall call the sale by repeating the value of the reserve price. Every higher bid, even if void, shall extinguish the bid that preceded it.

Article 968: The schedule of conditions shall become final and irrevocable if the time limit specified in Article 966 expires without the submission of observations or an objection thereto, or following the issuance of the decision referred to in the first paragraph of the preceding Article. The right of any person who was served with the notice to lodge any challenge relating to the enforcement proceedings carried out shall thereupon lapse, as shall the right of the seller of the attached real property who was served with the notice to bring any action for the annulment of the sale, and any challenge relating to the right underlying the attachment shall have no effect on those proceedings, subject to the provisions of Article 850.

However, if more than two years have elapsed since the valuation and the auction has not yet taken place, the President of the Enforcement Department, regardless of the judicial authority that ordered the valuation, may decide to have it carried out anew in accordance with prevailing prices, either of his own motion or upon the request of an interested party. Where this is decided, the sale may not take place at a price of less than six tenths of the new appraised value, nor may real property that is impossible to partition in kind be sold at public auction at a price of less than the new appraised value. Where necessary, the President of the Enforcement Department shall amend the schedule of conditions with respect to fixing the reserve price on the aforementioned basis, and such amendment shall not be served upon anyone. Where no bidders come forward, the provisions of Article 976, paragraph 2, shall apply.

The provisions of the second paragraph of this Article shall apply immediately upon the publication of this Law to all enforcement proceedings, including pending proceedings.

The enforcement officer shall draw up an abstract of the schedule of conditions in the form of a notice stating:

1 - The identity of the enforcement creditor and the enforcement debtor, and the domicile of each of them.

2 - The date of the attachment and the date of its registration in the Land Register or the special register relating to real property not subject to the Land Register system, or the mukhtar's register, or the record of demarcation and census before the Real Estate Judge, and the amount of the debt claimed.

3 - A description of the attached real property or properties and the reserve price fixed for each of them.

4 - The date and time of the auction by month, day and hour, and the place where it is to be held, as fixed by a decision of the President of the Enforcement Department.

5 - The expenses payable in addition to the price, as assessed by the President of the Enforcement Department.

The Head of the Enforcement Department shall decide to award the property sold to the final bidder who offered the highest price after the lapse of fifteen minutes, or to the maker of the earliest offer in the event of equal offers. If no one comes forward to purchase, the sale shall be adjourned for a period ranging between two months and the upset price shall be reduced. The advertisement procedure shall then be carried out anew on the basis of the reduced upset price. The Head of the Enforcement Department shall repeat this action until a prospective purchaser comes forward.

Anyone who has participated in the auction and fulfilled the obligation of deposit or guarantee without being the final bidder may withdraw the deposited money or the guarantee immediately upon the conclusion of the auction session.

If the purchaser at the auction fails, within three days from the date of issuance of the award decision, to deposit the full price in the name of the Head of the Enforcement Department with the Treasury Fund or one of the approved banks, the Head of the Enforcement Department shall fix a new session for the sale, and the advertisement and publication procedures shall be repeated, mentioning in particular the real property or properties that were the subject of the first award, the price at which such award took place, and the person to whom it was awarded.

If, at the new session, someone comes forward who accepts to purchase with an increase of one-tenth, accompanied by the full price including the said increase or by an equivalent bank guarantee, the auction shall be repeated on the basis of that price.

If no one comes forward for the one-tenth increase, the first purchaser may, in the same session, deposit the price at which the award was made to him together with the expenses resulting from his delay; otherwise, the auction must immediately be repeated at his responsibility and expense.

No offer not accompanied by its full value or by an equivalent bank guarantee shall be taken into consideration in this session.

The issuance of the award decision in the auction with a one-tenth increase or in the auction conducted at the responsibility and expense of the defaulting purchaser shall entail the cancellation of the rights of the latter and the substitution of the new purchaser in his place with retroactive effect.

The award decision in the auction conducted at the responsibility and expense of the defaulting purchaser must include holding the latter liable for the difference in price together with the additional expenses caused by him, whereas he shall not benefit from the bidding increase in the price.

The Head of the Enforcement Department may, during the auction session and upon the request of the debtor, take into consideration the position of the latter and the economic situation, and adjourn the sale for a period ranging between two months and six months, provided that the debtor advances, for the benefit of all attaching creditors, creditors participating in the attachment, and registered creditors holding a right of priority whose debt meets the legal conditions for enforcement, the interest for the granted period and the expenses paid. This adjournment may not be renewed except with the consent of the said creditors.

The President of the Execution Department shall decide to adjourn the sale for one year upon a petition submitted to him by the debtor at least five days before the date of the sale, in which he proves that the net revenue of his assets for this period is sufficient to pay the amounts due to all the creditors mentioned in the preceding Article. The President of the Execution Department may take the necessary measures to preserve this revenue.

The sale shall be stayed for one of the following reasons:

1 - The issuance of a decision by a competent judicial authority staying execution.

2 - The execution being based on a challenged arbitral award, subject to the provisions of Article 797, or on an instrument criminally alleged to be forged.

3 - Failure by any of the persons mentioned in Article 975 to request the sale at the auction hearing.

4 - The death of the debtor before the auction hearing if such death is notified to the attaching creditors and the participants in the attachment, and the stay of the sale shall continue until the heirs are notified of the new date for the auction.

5 - The bankruptcy of the debtor if there is not among the attaching creditors, the participants in the attachment, or the registered creditors the holder of a special privilege who has insisted on continuing the sale.
Decisions limited to a decision adjourning or staying the sale shall not be subject to any recourse.

The issuance of the adjudication decision shall entail:

1 - The performance by the purchaser of the obligations incumbent upon him, and in particular the payment of the price, fees, and expenses without the need for a formal notice or demand, within twenty days from the date of issuance of the decision, whereupon the Execution Department shall deposit the amounts paid to it with one of the approved banks.

2- The consideration of the purchaser as owner with respect to the party against whom execution is levied and any person who was a party to the proceedings, and enabling him to vacate the real property through the Execution Department voluntarily or compulsorily from the party against whom execution is levied within five days from the date of his being notified of a notice to vacate by the Execution Department; and in the event that the party against whom execution is levied fails to attend or refuses to take delivery of the things and property belonging to him and found in the real property, such things shall be delivered to a judicial custodian. The matter shall be notified to the party against whom execution is levied in order to take those things within a time limit of three days, failing which they shall be sold by public auction and the proceeds of the sale shall be kept in the Treasury fund or an approved bank in trust for their owner after deducting the preservation expenses.

3 - The forfeiture of the right of any person who was notified of the invitation to inspect the conditions of sale to submit any challenge relating to the proceedings subsequent to the said conditions of sale becoming final.

The party against whom execution is levied shall have the right, within ten days from the issuance of the adjudication, to deposit with the Treasury fund or an approved bank an amount sufficient to satisfy all the debts and costs, and such deposit shall entail the lapse of the adjudication decision and the lifting of the attachment.

The Enforcement Department shall, after the expiry of the time limit specified in the preceding Article, the finality of the adjudication decision, and the payment by the purchaser of the price and the fees, request the registration of the adjudication decision in the Land Register, or in the mukhtar's register, or in the special register relating to real property not subject to the Land Register system, or in the minutes of demarcation and census held with the Real Estate Judge.

The registration provided for in the preceding Article shall result in the transfer of ownership with respect to third parties and the purging of the real property from the encumbrances of pledge, mortgage, and privilege held by the persons who were served with the notice to inspect the book of conditions of sale.

The adjudication decision shall not be subject to opposition, but shall be subject to appeal within five days from the date of its issuance, for the following grounds:

1 - A defect in the auction proceedings or in the form of the decision.

2 - Its issuance after the refusal to stay enforcement when it is mandatory.

3 - Violation of the law in an incidental dispute addressed by the adjudication decision if it is capable of affecting the validity of the proceedings. And the adjudication decision shall be subject to annulment during the limitation period of the right upon which the request for annulment is based, provided that it does not exceed five years from the date of its issuance, and that by way of a principal action brought before the competent court by a person who was not a party to the enforcement proceedings.

If the applicant for enforcement neglects, for any reason whatsoever, to carry out the proceedings within the legal time limits or to pursue them, any creditor who has become a party thereto, or another creditor holding an enforceable title and whose debt fulfills the legal conditions for enforcement, may summon him before the Head of the Enforcement Department to hear the judgment subrogating him in his place in the right to pursue the enforcement. The Head shall examine the request in accordance with the rules of procedure followed in urgent matters, and the offer and undertaking of the enforcing creditor to resume the proceedings shall not prevent its granting, and the expenses incurred by the defaulting creditor shall not be refunded to him until after the issuance of the adjudication decision.

If the enforcing creditor waives his right or the enforcement proceedings, any other creditor who was a party to the enforcement and whose debt fulfills the legal conditions for enforcement may pursue the proceedings from the point they have reached without the need for a subrogation decision.

Immediately upon drawing up the draft distribution, the enforcement officer shall summon the interested parties, including the debtor, to appear before him, by virtue of a notification document or a registered letter with acknowledgment of receipt, and such summons must reach them at least three days prior to the appointed date; he shall present his draft to them, and if they agree to it, it shall become final, and if they agree to part of it, the partial agreement shall become final and shall be enforced immediately in favour of the beneficiary thereof. If one of them rejects it, the case shall be referred to the Head of the Enforcement Department to examine it within five days from summoning the party against whom enforcement is pursued and the creditors in the manner and within the time limit specified above.

If the objection is dismissed and the objector was abusive in his objection, he shall be liable to a claim before the competent authority for default interest by way of compensation and for the fine provided for in Article 11 of this Law.

The failure of one of the creditors to appear before the enforcement officer shall not prevent an amicable settlement unless it does not guarantee the full satisfaction of his right. In this case, his failure to appear shall be deemed a rejection and the case shall be referred to the Head of the Enforcement Department, who may sentence the defaulting party to a fine ranging between twenty thousand and two hundred thousand Lebanese pounds unless he presents an acceptable excuse.

After the Head of the Enforcement Department hears the statements of the party against whom enforcement is pursued and the creditors, he shall approve the final schedule and assign to each of them the amount due to him. His decision shall be subject to appeal within a time limit of five days from the date of its issuance; the appellate decision shall not be subject to a petition for cassation, and the distribution decision shall not be enforced until after it becomes final.

The Head of the Enforcement Department may administratively consolidate into a single distribution proceeding the amounts realised from attachments levied upon several real properties of the debtor, with due regard to the rights pertaining to the creditors in respect of each real property.

A creditor may request the imprisonment of his debtor who refuses to pay one of the following debts, subject to the provisions of other laws:

1 - Compensation awarded by judgment on account of a criminal offence or a civil wrong, and the judicial costs relating to the action for such compensation.

2 - Compensation awarded by judgment to a judge and to the State as a result of the dismissal of an action brought against the latter concerning liability arising from the acts of judges.

3 - A maintenance debt awarded by judgment. Each instalment thereof shall be deemed an independent debt.

4 - Dowry and deferred dower awarded by judgment to the wife.
A person ordered by judgment to hand over a minor child may also be imprisoned in the event of refusal to hand over the child.

The decision to imprison the debtor in respect of debts of maintenance, dowry and deferred dower and in respect of the handover of a minor child shall be issued by the Head of the Execution Department, and it shall be issued by the Public Prosecution in respect of all other debts for which imprisonment is permissible under the provisions of this Law or other laws.

The duration of imprisonment in relation to all the debts referred to in the preceding Article shall be at the rate of one day for every twenty thousand Lebanese Pounds of the debt and its accessories, provided that its maximum shall not exceed six months. The duration of imprisonment of a person sentenced to hand over a minor child shall be six months at most.

The application for imprisonment shall be submitted to the Execution Department competent to execute the judgment or to the Appellate Public Prosecution. The Head of the Execution Department or the Public Prosecutor shall issue his decision after verifying the debtor's default in execution through explicit refusal or the expiry of a time limit of five days from placing him on notice, and this time limit may be reduced for a maintenance debt or for the obligation to hand over a minor, provided that it is not less than one day.
The debtor may object to the decision for his imprisonment before the Head of the Department adversely to the creditor if the conditions for imprisonment are not met.

Imprisonment shall not apply to:

1 - A person whose age is less than fifteen years or more than sixty-five years at the time of execution, with the exception of the case of imprisonment for the handover of a minor.

2 - A bankrupt debtor during bankruptcy proceedings or a debtor petitioning for a preventive composition.

3 - The spouse of the creditor or his descendants and ascendants for debts other than those specified in paragraphs 3 and 4 of Article 997 and for obligations other than the handover of a minor child provided for in Article 998.

4 - A pregnant woman until the expiry of two months after delivery and the mother of a newborn until he reaches one year of age.
Imprisonment may not be executed against both spouses together when they have a child whose age is less than fifteen years.

Imprisonment shall be executed through the Public Prosecution, and the prison regime imposed on detainees in a misdemeanour matter shall apply to the debtor, and the subsistence expenses shall be borne by the State, provided that it retains the right of recourse against the debtor for them.
Imprisonment may continue after the expiry of its duration on account of a new debt, upon the application of the same creditor or another creditor.

If the property sold is among the assets in respect of which related rights are registered in a special register, the party seeking enforcement shall be required, following a sale conducted pursuant to an executory attachment of movables and the payment of the price, or following the registration of the adjudication decision provided for in Articles 985 and 986, to produce a certificate from the competent authority showing the status of the property sold and the rights and encumbrances thereon up to the date on which the sale or adjudication took place. Any of the other parties to the enforcement proceedings may produce the certificate referred to in the first paragraph.

If the price realised from the sale of the attached assets is sufficient to discharge the costs and all the debts owed to the attaching creditors, the creditors joining in the attachment, the creditors whose names are registered, and the holders of liens who made themselves known to the Execution Department prior to the sale, the enforcement officer shall pay to each of them his established claim within a period not exceeding ten days from the date of the sale and payment of the price in respect of assets the related rights of which are not registered in a special register, from the date of production of the certificate mentioned in Article 990 in respect of the remaining assets, by delivering to him a payment order drawn on the Treasury fund or the bank where the money was deposited, and shall deliver the remainder to the debtor. Only the creditors mentioned in the preceding paragraph shall participate in the distribution proceedings.

If the price is not sufficient to satisfy the claims in the manner set forth in the preceding Article, the Execution Department shall, within five days from the date of the sale and payment of the price or from the date of production of the certificate mentioned in Article 990, send a notice to the creditors referred to in the first paragraph of the preceding Article requiring them to submit an application for the satisfaction of their debts together with the supporting documents thereof within ten days from their receipt of the notice.

Only those among the said creditors who submit an application for satisfaction within this time limit shall participate in the proceedings for the distribution of the price.

The enforcement officer shall, within ten days from the date of his receipt of the last application for satisfaction, draw up a draft distribution plan adopting the order of priority as follows:

1 - Enforcement costs.

2 - Debts accompanied by a lien, pledge, or mortgage, having regard to their respective ranks.

3 - Pertaining debts in proportion to their amount.

The Lebanese court before which an application for an exequatur is brought may not re-examine the merits of the foreign judgment at the request of the defendant except in one of the following cases:

a - If it is proved that the judgment was rendered on the basis of documents that were deemed or declared to be false on a date subsequent to its issuance.

b - If, after the issuance of the judgment, decisive documents were discovered which one of the parties prevented from being produced.

c - If there is a contradiction in the operative part of the judgment.

d - If it is proved that the laws of the State in whose name the foreign judgment was rendered require a re-examination of the merits of Lebanese judgments before granting them an exequatur.

The Lebanese courts shall refuse the exequatur in the following cases:

a - If a final judgment has been rendered by the Lebanese judiciary between the same parties in the same dispute that led to the issuance of the foreign judgment.

b - If a lawsuit in the same dispute and between the same litigants, filed on a date prior to the lawsuit that resulted in the foreign judgment, remains pending before the Lebanese judiciary.

The party requesting that a foreign judgment be granted an exequatur shall produce:

a - A duly certified copy of the foreign judgment fulfilling the conditions that establish its authenticity in accordance with the law of the country in which the judgment was rendered. b - The documents capable of establishing that this judgment has acquired enforceable force in the country in which it was rendered.

c - A certified copy of the summons addressed to the party who failed to appear at the trial and of the document of service of the trial papers upon him, if the judgment was rendered in absentia.

d - A true translation of the original documents listed above, certified in accordance with the provisions of Lebanese law.

The court may grant the exequatur to the judgment in its entirety or to a partial aspect thereof whenever such aspect is severable from the other aspects, and it may not introduce any modification thereto capable of extending its scope, whether with respect to the subject matter or with respect to the litigants.
During the examination of the application for an exequatur, grounds and means of defence that have arisen after the issuance of the foreign judgment may be raised.

The Lebanese judge, during the examination of a lawsuit brought before him, may give effect to a foreign judgment when it is invoked before him, provided that the conditions stipulated in Articles 1014 and 1015 of this Law are fulfilled. He may also grant this judgment the exequatur if one of the parties expressly requests it. These rules shall apply to foreign judgments relating to capacity and personal status and to foreign judgments rendered by the non-contentious jurisdiction.

An application for an exequatur for a foreign judgment shall be submitted through the non-contentious procedure by means of a petition to the President of the Civil Court of Appeal within the jurisdiction of which the defendant's domicile or residence or the place where the property against which enforcement is sought is located, failing which to the President of the Civil Court of Appeal of Beirut, and the President shall issue an order on the petition accepting or rejecting the application. Where an order is issued accepting the application and granting the exequatur, the aggrieved party shall be entitled to file an opposition against it before the Court of Appeal within a time limit of thirty days from the date of service upon him of this order or of one of the measures for its enforcement. Where the judgment granted the exequatur is contentious and is not subject to provisional enforcement, the time limit for the opponent's recourse shall stay enforcement, as shall a recourse filed within the time limit.

In the event that the application is rejected, the applicant shall be entitled to file an opposition against the rejection order within a time limit of fifteen days from the date of service before the Court of Appeal. The appellate decision shall be subject to the avenues of recourse to which decisions issued by the Courts of Appeal are subject.

An exequatur shall be granted to a foreign judgment if all of the following conditions are met concurrently:

A - That it was issued by competent judges according to the law of the country in which it was issued, provided that their jurisdiction was not established solely on the basis of the nationality of the plaintiff, and in the event that two foreign judgments are issued in the name of two different sovereignties on the same subject matter and between the same litigants, the exequatur shall be granted to the judgment that conforms to the rules of Lebanese law on international jurisdiction.

B - That it has acquired the force of res judicata and enforceable force in the State in whose name it was issued. However, the exequatur may be granted to non-contentious judgments and to provisional judgments that have become enforceable in the State concerned.

C - That the judgment debtor was served with the action that led to the judgment and his rights of defence were secured.

D - That it was issued in the name of a State whose laws permit the enforcement of Lebanese judgments on its territory after examining them or after granting them an exequatur.

E - That it contains nothing contrary to public policy.

Imprisonment shall terminate:

1 - By payment of the debt or at the request of the creditor.

2 - By the debtor presenting a solvent guarantor who guarantees the settlement of the debt within eight days.

3 - By the debtor reaching the age of sixty-five. If the guarantor refuses to pay within the aforementioned time limit, the creditor may execute against him without the need for a judgment or request the imprisonment of the principal debtor anew.
General amnesty shall not preclude the imprisonment of the debtor, nor shall the debt be extinguished by the execution of imprisonment, unless otherwise provided.
Judgments issued in the name of a sovereignty other than the Lebanese sovereignty shall be deemed foreign, within the meaning intended in this Title.

Foreign judgments shall not be executed in Lebanon by means of execution against property or coercion against persons until after they have been granted the executory formula in accordance with the conditions provided for in this Title. However, before the foreign judgment is granted the executory formula, it may be used as a means of proof or as a basis for conservatory measures such as a conservatory real estate registration, judicial receivership, the bankruptcy trustee claiming debts due to the bankruptcy estate or intervening in the bankrupt's lawsuits, conservatory attachment, attachment by way of revendication, and garnishment. The application for the executory formula shall take the place of an action to establish or an action for the validity of the debt.
Foreign judgments issued by the criminal or administrative judiciary shall not be subject to this Law unless they contain obligations of a civil nature and solely with respect to such obligations.

Foreign judgments relating to capacity and personal status and decisions issued by the non-contentious jurisdiction shall produce their effects ipso jure in Lebanon without being granted the executory formula, provided that they are not the subject of a dispute. The making or rectification of entries or the striking off of annotations recorded in the Lebanese personal status registers shall be deemed measures of execution within the meaning intended in Article 1010.

All provisions of international treaties and conventions containing special rules relating to procedure, or to the jurisdiction of courts or judicial authorities, or to enforcement procedures, or to rules of evidence, shall be deemed annexed to this Law.

Subject to the provisions of Articles 761, 931, 968, 1025 and 1026 paragraph 2, this Law shall enter into force as of the first of July 1985, taking into account the period of its application between the first of January 1985 and the date of entry into force of this Legislative Decree.

The provisions of this Title shall apply to actions aimed at declaring the inapplicability of foreign judgments, whether submitted directly or in the course of a pending action before the Lebanese courts.
A foreign judgment vested with an enforcement order shall enjoy the enforceable force enjoyed by Lebanese judgments and shall benefit from the methods of enforcement of such judgments.

With the exception of instruments establishing a personal right or a right in rem, the enforcement of which remains subject to the provisions of Articles 847 to 856, foreign authentic instruments shall not be enforceable in Lebanon except pursuant to a decision issued in accordance with the provisions of Article 1013.

An enforcement order shall not be granted to a foreign authentic instrument unless the following conditions are met cumulatively, namely:

a - Issuance of the instrument by the competent public official according to the provisions of the law that granted him jurisdiction.

b - Drawing up of the said instrument in the form prescribed by the laws of the country in which it was drawn up.

c - The instrument does not contain anything contrary to public policy.

d - Its accompaniment by enforceable force according to the laws of the country in which it was drawn up.

There shall be established at the registry of the Chamber of First Instance hearing civil cases a register of civil companies, the method of keeping which shall be regulated and the effects of the entries of which shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice.

The Commercial Register and the Special Register attached thereto established at the Chamber of First Instance hearing commercial cases shall be regulated by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice.

A Central Commercial Register with a Special Register attached thereto shall be established at the Chamber of First Instance hearing commercial cases in Beirut and shall be regulated by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice.

The provisions of this Article shall apply immediately upon the publication of this Law in the Official Gazette.

All texts of this Law containing a determination of monetary amounts may be amended with respect to such amounts by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice. Furthermore, within a period of eighteen months from the date of publication of this Law, any amendment thereto that does not affect the substance may be introduced by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice.
Courts that have become incompetent pursuant to the provisions of this Law to hear the cases pending before them must refer such cases administratively to the competent courts.

Courts that enshrine recognised principles shall have an interpretative character, and the provisions of Articles 5, item (3), 7, 368, 373, 527 in both of its paragraphs, and 557 in particular shall have this character.
The new rules set forth in the Title on Arbitration shall not apply to arbitration agreements, disputes or proposals prior to the date of entry into force of this Law.

The following laws are repealed:

- The Code of Civil Procedure promulgated by Legislative Decree No. 72 dated 1 February 1933, together with its amendments.

- The Ottoman Law of Execution. - Articles 31 to 98 and 148 of the Judicial Organisation Law promulgated on 16/10/1961, subject to the provisions of Article 30 of the Lease Law promulgated on 9/9/1982.

- The Law relating to the execution of written contracts and undertakings promulgated on 4/5/1968.

- Law No. 73/67 dated 19/12/1967 relating to the enforcement of foreign judgments, arbitral awards and instruments. The texts repealed by the aforementioned laws shall remain repealed. All provisions contrary to this Law or inconsistent with its provisions, as well as other prior provisions the substance of which has been included herein, are also repealed, with the exception of the texts the observance of which has been expressly reserved by the Law and the texts set forth in other laws governing special enforcement procedures for the recovery of specific types of debts or governing procedures for the attachment or sale of special types of property, in particular: - The Code of Land Commerce and Legislative Decree No. 11 dated 11 July 1967 concerning the business concern.

- The Code of Maritime Commerce.

- The Aviation Law.

- The Law promulgated on 20 May 1935 concerning the sale on credit for fixed terms of motor vehicles and agricultural and industrial machinery.

- Law No. 13/78 dated 24 April 1978 concerning the determination of the procedures for the collection of funds of the National Social Security Fund.

- Legislative Decree No. 46 dated 20 October 1932 concerning the contract of pledge of movables. - Decree No. 780 dated 12 March 1971, as amended by Decree No. 8949 dated 25 September 1974, concerning the determination of the conditions for the attachment and impoundment of vehicles. - Decision No. 2385 dated 17 January 1924, as amended by the Law of 31 January 1946, concerning the system of commercial and industrial property rights. The provisions of the Law on the Termination of Co-ownership promulgated on 6 March 1982 shall be observed.

The numbers of the articles of the Code of Civil Procedure mentioned in the texts of other laws shall be deemed replaced ipso jure by the corresponding numbers of the articles of this Law. Furthermore, other legal texts which refer to the texts of laws the rules of which have been incorporated into the articles of this Law shall be deemed ipso jure to refer to these latter articles.

This Law contains, on the one hand, the rules relating to commercial acts performed by any person whatever their legal capacity, and contains, on the other hand, the provisions that apply to persons who have taken up trade as a profession.

Where there is no provision in this Law, the provisions of the general law shall apply to commercial matters, provided that their application shall only be to the extent of their consistency with the principles peculiar to commercial law.
Where there is no legislative provision that can be applied, the judge may be guided by judicial precedents and by the requirements of equity and commercial probity.

In determining the effects of a commercial act, the judge must apply established usage, unless it appears that the contracting parties intended to depart from the provisions of usage or the usage conflicts with mandatory legislative provisions. Special usage and local usage shall prevail over general usage.
Commercial exchanges, fairs, markets, general warehouses, bonded warehouses, and all other establishments intended for trade shall be subject, as needed, to special laws and regulations.

The acts set forth below are, by virtue of their own intrinsic nature, land commercial acts, as are all acts that may be considered analogous to them by reason of the similarity of their characteristics and purposes:

1 - The purchase of goods and other corporeal and incorporeal movables in order to sell them at a profit, whether they are sold in their existing state or after being worked or transformed.

2 - The purchase of those same movable things in order to lease them out, or the leasing of them in order to sublease them.

3 - The sale or leasing or subleasing of the things purchased or leased in the manner set forth above.

4 - Money-changing and banking operations.

5 - A supply enterprise.

6 - A manufacturing enterprise, even if combined with an agricultural exploitation, unless the transformation of materials is effected by simple manual labour.

7 - A transport enterprise by land, by air, or on the surface of the water.

8 - A commission and brokerage enterprise.

9 - A fixed-premium insurance enterprise.

10 - A public entertainment enterprise.

11 - A publishing enterprise.

12 - A general warehouses enterprise.

13 - A mines and petroleum enterprise.

14 - An immovable works enterprise.

15 - An enterprise for the purchase of immovables in order to sell them at a profit.

16 - A business agency enterprise.

The following shall also be deemed maritime commercial acts:

1 - Every enterprise for the construction or purchase of vessels intended for inland or foreign navigation with a view to exploiting them as traders or selling them, and every sale of vessels purchased in this manner.

2 - All maritime expeditions and every operation relating thereto, such as the purchase or sale of their supplies of ropes, sails and provisions.

3 - The licensing of ships or the undertaking of transport thereon, and bottomry loans or borrowings.

4 - And all other contracts pertaining to maritime trade, such as agreements and contracts on the wages of seamen, the remuneration for their service and their engagement to work on commercial vessels.

All acts performed by a merchant for commercial needs shall also be deemed commercial in the eyes of the law.

Where doubt arises, the acts of a merchant shall be deemed to have been issued by him for this purpose unless the contrary is proved.

Merchants are:

First: Persons whose profession is the performance of commercial acts.

Second: Companies whose object is commercial.

As for companies whose object is civil but which have assumed the form of joint-stock companies or partnerships limited by shares, they shall be subject to all the obligations of merchants specified in the following Chapters Two and Three, and to the provisions on preventive composition and bankruptcy laid down in Book Five of this Law.

Individuals who engage in a small trade or a simple craft with modest general expenses, such as an itinerant vendor or a day vendor, or who carry out small transport operations by land or on the surface of the water, shall not be subject to the obligations pertaining to commercial books nor to the rules of publication prescribed by this Law.
A married woman possesses full capacity to carry on commercial acts.
A married woman, in carrying on trade, may perform every act required by the interest of her commercial enterprise.
A married woman shall have the right to enter into a general partnership or to be a general partner in a limited partnership.
The rights of a married woman shall be determined, where necessary, by the provisions of her personal status law and her marriage contract.

Any separation of property between spouses adjudged in a foreign country shall not be enforceable against third parties in Lebanon unless it is registered in the Commercial Register competent for the place where the spouses, or either of them, carry on trade.

Every person, whether natural or legal, having the capacity of a merchant shall keep, manually or by means of a secure digital application whose specifications conform to the standards determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Ministers of Justice and Finance, the following documents:

- The journal, in which financial operations are recorded day by day at a minimum, or in which the results of such operations are recorded monthly if the nature of the business prevents the former, provided that in this case he retains all documents enabling an audit thereof to be conducted day by day.

- The general ledger for opening and monitoring accounts.

He shall also make an annual inventory of all the elements of his enterprise and close all accounts for the purpose of drawing up the balance sheet and drawing up the "profit and loss account", and the documents relating thereto must be drawn up and retained throughout the period provided for in Article 19 of the Code of Commerce.

- The keeping of commercial books by means of the digital application prescribed in this Article shall become mandatory two years after the date of issuance of this Law.
Mandatory commercial books must be kept in chronological order, without blanks, gaps, marginal transfers, interlineations, or erasures.
Books kept manually must be numbered, initialled, and signed by the President of the Court of First Instance in the cities where such court sits.
A merchant must retain the books after their closure for a period of ten years.

The books may be admitted before the courts as means of evidence in favour of the merchant, provided that they are regularly kept, that their contents are invoked against another merchant, and that the dispute relates to a commercial act.

In all cases, they shall constitute evidence against the merchant who kept them, and if this merchant refuses to produce them, the judge may request the other party to take the oath.

The books shall not be delivered in their entirety to the courts except in cases of succession, partition of common property, partnership, preventive composition, and bankruptcy.

Save for these cases, it is always permissible to offer or request the production of the books, or for the judge to order their production of his own motion, in order to extract therefrom what relates to the dispute.

The Commercial Register enables the public to gather complete information on all commercial establishments operating in the country.

It is also an instrument of publicity intended to render its entries enforceable against third parties where an express legal text to that effect exists.
A register shall be maintained at each Court of First Instance by the clerk under the supervision of the President or a judge specially designated by the President each year.

Every merchant must request the clerk of the court within whose jurisdiction his principal establishment is situated to register his name in the commercial register within one month from the date of opening or purchasing the establishment, and the applicant must submit to the clerk a declaration in two copies bearing his signature, stating therein the following:

1 - The merchant's first name and surname.

2 - His trade name under which he carries on his commerce and, where applicable, his nickname and his pseudonym.

3 - The date and place of his birth.

4 - His original nationality. And if he has acquired another nationality, he shall state the manner in which he acquired it, mentioning the date.

5 - And if the matter concerns a married woman who holds a foreign nationality whose applicable personal status law requires that she not engage in commerce except with the express authorisation of her husband, the authorisation granted to her in accordance with the aforementioned law shall be stated.

6 - The matrimonial agreement of the merchant holding a foreign nationality, unless the spouses are subject to the statutory community regime.

7 - The object of the commerce.

8 - The places where the branches or agencies of the commercial establishment are situated in Lebanon or Syria.

9 - The style or trade name of the establishment.

10 - The first names and surnames of the authorised signatories, the date and place of their birth, and their nationality.

11 - The commercial establishments previously operated by the declarant and those which he currently operates within the jurisdictions of other courts.

The clerk shall then transcribe the content of the declaration into the commercial register and deliver to the applicant one of the two copies of the declaration after writing at the end thereof that it is a true copy of the original.

There must also be mentioned in the Commercial Register:

1 - Every amendment or alteration relating to the matters which the preceding Article requires to be entered in the Register.

2 - Letters patent exploited by the merchant and the factory mark or trademark used by him.

3 - Judgments and decisions ordering the appointment of a judicial adviser for the registered merchant, or placing him under interdiction, or lifting the supervision or interdiction from him.

4 - Judgments and decisions declaring bankruptcy, or containing the homologation, rescission, or annulment of a composition, or declaring the excusability of the bankrupt, or ordering the closure of the bankruptcy proceedings for insufficiency of assets, or revoking the closure thereof, or granting rehabilitation.

5 - The assignment of the business concern.

The entry shall be made at the request of the merchant in the cases referred to in paragraphs 1, 2 and 5 of this Article.

It shall be made in the cases referred to in paragraphs 3 and 4 of this Article at the request of the clerk of the court that issued the decisions to be entered.

The clerk shall make the entry directly when the judgment is issued by the court in whose registry a Commercial Register is kept.

Companies that have their principal office in Lebanon must be registered in the Commercial Register having jurisdiction over the district of their office, and the legal representative of the company must apply for registration within the month following its formation:

The applicant for registration shall submit to the court registry a copy of the instrument of formation and an abstract thereof written in two copies, bearing stamps and his signature, and containing in particular the following particulars:

1 - The first name and surname of each of the partners and shareholders, the nationality of each of them, and the date and place of his birth.

2 - The trade name or style of the company.

3 - The object of the company.

4 - The places where the company has branches or agencies, whether in Lebanon or abroad

5 - The names and the partners or other persons authorised to manage the company or sign on its behalf.

6 - The capital of the company and the sums or securities due to be contributed by the shareholders or limited partners, as well as the value of what is contributed to the company, whether in cash or in other property.

7 - The date of commencement of the company and the date of its expiration.

8 - The form of the company.

9 - The minimum capital of the company if it is of variable capital.

10 - The lease contract of the premises in which the company will carry on its business, or a document evidencing its ownership thereof, or a document evidencing its election of domicile with its legal representative, or any legal instrument permitted by the laws in force justifying the occupancy of the company's office.

11 - The identity of the beneficial owner or owners.

There must also be mentioned in the Commercial Register:

1 - Every modification or alteration to the matters required to be registered pursuant to the preceding Article.

2 - The first name, surname, date and place of birth, and nationality of each of the managers of the company's business, the members of its board of directors, and its directors appointed for the duration of its existence.

As for the application for registration, it shall be submitted by the legal representative of the company at the time when registration becomes obligatory.

3 - The exploited patents of invention and the manufacturing (Marque de fabrique) and trade marks used by the company.

4 - The judgments or decisions pronouncing the dissolution of the company or its nullity.

5 - The judgments or decisions declaring the bankruptcy of the company or homologating the preventive composition, and the resolutions pertaining thereto.

Every merchant who has a principal office in a foreign country and branches or an agency in Lebanon must, whatever his nationality may be, register his name within the month following the opening of the agency or branch at the registry of the court within whose jurisdiction the agency was established, and the declaration must include all the particulars mentioned above with the designation of the location of the principal office.

Likewise, there must be mentioned in the Commercial Register all the modifications set forth above together with the judgments and decisions previously mentioned if they are issued in Lebanon or Syria or have acquired an executory formula in their courts.

Every foreign commercial company that has a branch or agency in Lebanon must be registered in the Commercial Register, with the exception of joint-stock companies and partnerships limited by shares subject to the provisions of Decision of the High Commissioner No. 96 dated 30 January 1926.

Before the opening of the branch or agency, the person who assumes its management must deposit at the registry of the court a written declaration in two copies bearing his signature and containing all the particulars mentioned above, and he must add thereto his first name, surname, date and place of birth, with the mention of his nationality.

All changes relating to the matters required to be registered must be registered. Upon the replacement of the manager of the branch, the first name of the new manager, his surname, date and place of birth, and his nationality must be registered in the Commercial Register together with all the required particulars.

If a merchant dies or ceases to carry on his trade without having assigned his business concern to anyone, or if one of the companies is dissolved, the registration pertaining to them in the Commercial Register must be struck off.

This striking off shall be effected ex officio pursuant to a decision issued by the judge entrusted with supervising the Register.

Every entry in the Commercial Register for which no time limit has been fixed in the preceding Articles must be applied for within one month commencing from the date of the instrument or act which it sees fit to enter. As for judgments and decisions, their time limit shall commence from the day of their issuance.
All registrations and entries in the Commercial Register shall be made pursuant to a declaration submitted in accordance with the prescribed forms.

The clerk may not refuse to make the requested entries unless the declarations submitted do not contain all the prescribed particulars.

The clerk must report to the President or to the judge assigned to supervise the Commercial Register the defects he has observed in those declarations.

Every person may request to be given a copy of the entries recorded in the register in consideration of a fee determined by decree. The clerk may, where appropriate, issue a certificate of the absence of entries.

Conformity of the copies with the original shall be certified by the President of the Court or the judge assigned to supervise the Commercial Register.

There may not be mentioned in the copies delivered by the clerk.

1 - Judgments declaring bankruptcy if the bankrupt has been rehabilitated.

2 - Judgments ordering interdiction or the appointment of a judicial adviser if a decision has been issued lifting the interdiction or the advisership.

Every merchant and every company subject to the obligation of registration must mention the place where they are registered and the number of such registration on their correspondence, invoices, order notes (Notes de commande), tariffs, circulars and all other printed matter issued by them.

Every merchant, or agent or manager of a company, who fails to request within the prescribed time limits the making of the compulsory entries, or fails to mention what must be mentioned on the correspondence, invoices and other printed matter issued by his establishment, shall be punished by a fine of fifty to one thousand Lebanese pounds.

This fine shall be imposed by the Court of First Instance upon the request of the President or the judge assigned to supervise the Commercial Register, after hearing the statements of the party concerned or summoning him in due form.

The Court shall order that the entry be made within fifteen days, and if it is not made during this time limit, a fine double that imposed the first time shall be ordered.

Clerks who fail to act in accordance with these regulations shall be referred to the Disciplinary Council.

Every inaccurate statement submitted in bad faith for registration or entry in the Commercial Register shall be punished by a fine of two hundred and fifty Lebanese pounds to five thousand pounds and by imprisonment from one month to six months, or by one of these two penalties alone.

This shall not preclude the application of the provisions on ideal concurrence of offences in order to impose a more severe penalty in accordance with special laws and the Penal Code for offences arising from the inaccurate statement.

The criminal court that renders the judgment may order the rectification of the aforementioned statement in such manner as it shall determine.

The penalties referred to shall be applied without prejudice to the rule of inadmissibility of invoking against third parties the facts and entries whose registration in the Trade Register was prescribed under penalty of nullity.

This article was repealed and replaced by Legislative Decree 11 /1967 The Business Concern

The business concern consists by law of the merchant's premises and of the rights connected therewith.

For the business concern comprises a set of corporeal and incorporeal elements that vary according to the circumstances, and they are in particular the clientele, the goodwill, the name, the emblem, the right to lease, the trademarks, the certificates, the licences, the drawings, the models, the industrial tools, the commercial furniture and the merchandise.

This article was repealed and replaced by Legislative Decree 11 /1967 The Business Concern

The rights of exploitation of the business concern with respect to the various elements set forth in the preceding article shall be determined pursuant to the special laws relating thereto or pursuant to the general principles of law.

The rules provided for by the Code of Obligations and Contracts with respect to the contract of partnership shall apply to commercial companies provided that those rules are not explicitly or implicitly contrary to the rules of this law.

Subject to the preservation of the rights of bona fide third parties, if the number of partners or shareholders in commercial companies of all kinds falls below the number prescribed by law for each of them, the dissolution of the company must be declared by a resolution of the remaining partners within a period of three months from the occurrence of the cause referred to, unless regularisation takes place.

The court must, at the request of any interested party, declare the dissolution of the company after the expiry of the three months granted for regularisation.

All commercial companies except joint ventures must be proven by a written contract; however, third parties may, where necessary, prove by all means the existence of the company or the existence of any provision relating thereto.

All companies incorporated in Lebanon must have a head office therein, and they shall be deemed of Lebanese nationality notwithstanding any provision to the contrary.
The constitutive instruments of all commercial companies - except joint ventures - must be published by carrying out the formalities set forth hereinafter, failing which they shall be null and void.

Failure to deposit the constitutive instrument with the registry of the court or failure to register it in the commercial register shall result in the nullity of the partnership and shall render all the partners jointly and severally liable upon the occurrence of harm to third parties.

Failure to mention a provision of interest to third parties in the partnership's by-laws deposited with the registry of the court or in the extract entered in the commercial register shall render such provision unenforceable against the interested parties, just as failure to publish the amendments introduced to the partnership's instrument shall render such amendments unenforceable against third parties.

Nullity arising from non-publication shall not lapse by prescription, and all interested parties are entitled to invoke it. The partners, however, may not invoke it against third parties.

Nevertheless, if the publication formalities are carried out belatedly, those who contracted with the partnership prior to the rectification shall alone be entitled to invoke the nullity to which the partnership was subject.

Every partner in a general partnership is deemed as though he personally carries on commerce under a partnership name - thus each of them acquires the legal capacity of a merchant. The bankruptcy of the partnership shall result in the personal bankruptcy of each of the partners.

The partnership name shall consist of the names of all the partners or of the names of several of them with the addition of the words "and their partners".

The partnership name must at all times correspond to its current composition.

Every person extraneous to the partnership who knowingly consents to the inclusion of his name in the name of a partnership shall become liable for its debts towards any person who is deceived thereby.

Save for assignments expressly provided for in the constitutive instrument, a partner may not assign to third parties his share in the interests of the partnership except with the consent of all the partners and subject to carrying out the publication formalities; however, one of the partners may transfer to third parties the rights and benefits pertaining to his share in the partnership, as such agreement shall have effect only between the contracting parties.

The right to manage the business shall vest in all the partners, unless the by-laws of the partnership or a subsequent instrument provides that the management be entrusted to a single partner or to several partners or to another person, even if extraneous to the partnership.

The business managers shall be dismissed in the manner in which they were appointed; however, if the dismissal is permissible, it shall give rise to a claim for damages under the conditions set forth in Article 822 of the Code of Obligations.

If a new manager is appointed in place of a statutory manager, such replacement must be published.

The business managers may perform all acts necessary for the regular conduct of the partnership's enterprise.

Unless their authority is limited pursuant to the by-laws of the partnership.

Managers may not enter into any agreement for their own account with the company or any agreement in which they or any one of them has a direct or indirect interest except by virtue of a special authorisation from the partners renewed, as required, each year.

Excepted from this prohibition are ordinary contracts covering transactions carried out by the company with its customers.
Likewise, business managers may not manage an enterprise similar to the company's enterprise except pursuant to a licence renewed each year.

Where there are several business managers, each of them shall have the right to object to transactions which the others intend to conclude.

In such event, the decision shall be taken by a majority of the votes of the said managers, unless the objection is founded on the ground that the act intended to be carried out is of a nature contrary to the company's articles of association.

In the latter case, the assessment of the nature of the act shall lie within the jurisdiction of the court.

The company shall be bound by the acts of the business managers whenever they act within the limits of their authority and sign under the company's trade name, even if their use of such signature is for their personal interest, unless the third party acts in bad faith.
