The creditors of the company shall have the right to sue it, provided, however, that they first serve upon it a formal notice demanding payment. They shall also have the right to sue every partner who was among its partners at the time of contracting.

Such partners shall be jointly and severally liable for payment out of their personal estates.

The general causes of dissolution applicable to all companies are:

(1) The expiry of the term for which the company was formed.

(2) The completion of the enterprise intended to be carried out in the ordinary course.

(3) The extinction of the object of the enterprise itself.

In addition to the foregoing, the court may at any time, upon the application of some of the partners, order either the dissolution of the company for just causes the import of which the court shall assess, or the expulsion of one of the partners for failing to perform his obligations towards the company.

General partnerships shall, in addition to the foregoing, be subject to the following causes of dissolution:

(1) The will of one of the partners where the company is formed for an unlimited term and the withdrawal of such partner does not prejudice the legitimate interests of the company in the circumstances in which it occurs.

(2) Where an event supervenes in respect of the person of one of the partners which deprives him of general capacity.

(3) The bankruptcy of one of the partners.

Provided that the remaining partners may decide by unanimous vote to continue the company among themselves to the exclusion of the partner who resigned, lost capacity or became bankrupt.

They must, however, in such event, carry out the legal formalities of publication.

All commercial companies - with the exception of joint ventures - shall enjoy legal personality.

An amendment to the form of the company shall not result in the creation of a new legal personality for it; rather, the legal personality shall remain in existence and the new company shall continue with the very same legal personality that existed prior to the conversion. This amendment shall not take effect with respect to third parties except as from registration in the Commercial Register and the expiry of a time-limit of one month from the announcement of this amendment in the Official Gazette and in a local daily newspaper designated by the judge supervising the Commercial Register.

Persons who have acted in the name of a company under incorporation before its acquisition of legal personality shall be deemed personally and jointly and severally liable among themselves for the acts executed, unless the company assumes responsibility for such acts after its incorporation, in which case those acts shall be deemed ratified by the company since their occurrence.

A general partnership is a company which operates under a specific business name of its own and is formed between two or more persons who are personally and jointly and severally liable for the debts of the company.

The constitutive instrument may be an authentic instrument, just as it may be an instrument under private signature.

However, in the latter case, as many copies of the instrument must be drawn up as there are partners.

Within the month in which the company is incorporated, an authentic copy or a duplicate of the constitutive instrument must be deposited with the registry of the Court of First Instance in the district of the company's head office.

Within the same time-limit, the company must also be registered in the Commercial Register having jurisdiction over the district of its head office, and this publication shall be concise and shall include all information the knowledge of which is of interest to third parties, and in particular:

(1) The first name, surname, nationality and place of residence of each of the partners, and the business name of the company.

(2) The form of the company.

(3) Its object.

(4) Its principal head office and the offices of its branches and agencies.

(5) The amount of its capital and the value attributed to the partners' contributions in kind,

(6) The names of the partners and the names of the authorised signatories who sign on behalf of the company.

(7) The date of incorporation and the duration of the company.

If an amendment is subsequently made to the constitutive instrument, a new copy thereof must be deposited with the registry of the court.

Registration in the Commercial Register shall also be required if there are entries that are of interest to third parties.

Unless the articles of association of the partnership contain a provision to the contrary, a general partnership shall, if one of its partners dies, continue among the surviving partners unless the deceased leaves a spouse or a descendant to whom his rights devolve; whereas if the case is to the contrary, the partnership shall continue with the partner's spouse or his descendants, and they shall have the capacity of limited partners.

In all cases, the value of the rights of the deceased or excluded partner shall be determined pursuant to a special inventory, unless the articles of association of the partnership provide for another method of valuation.

The dissolution of the partnership:

Save for the case where the dissolution is in accordance with the text of the constitutive instrument.

- Must be published in the same manner as the instrument itself and within the same time limit.

The same shall apply upon the exclusion of one of the partners and the continuation of the partnership after the death of one of them.
After dissolution, the legal personality of commercial companies shall remain as though in existence during the period necessary for liquidation and for the needs of the liquidation only.

If the articles of association of the company do not provide for the appointment of the liquidator or liquidators and the partners do not agree on selecting them, they shall be appointed by the court within the jurisdiction of which the head office of the company is located.
The outcome of the selection or the judicial decision containing the appointment of the liquidators must be published through the diligence of the latter.
The liquidators must, when they assume their functions, draw up the inventory jointly with the managers of the affairs of the company.

The liquidators shall collect the debts owed to the company by third parties or by the partners, pay the debts owed by it, sell its assets, and perform all the acts required by the liquidation; provided that they may neither continue to operate the company's enterprise nor assign the business concern of the company as a whole save pursuant to a special authorisation from the partners.

The liquidators must provide the partners, if they so request, with all information concerning the state of the liquidation. However, no obstacles may be raised in the way of the liquidation on account of unlawful demands.
The partition shall be carried out in accordance with the terms of the company contract, and the provisions of Articles 941 to 949 of the Code of Obligations shall furthermore be observed.

In all commercial companies, and subject to the actions that may be brought against the liquidators in their capacity as liquidators.

- The actions of the company's creditors against the partners or their heirs or their successors in title shall lapse by prescription after the expiry of five years from the dissolution of the company or from the withdrawal of one of the partners with respect to actions directed against that partner.

The period of prescription shall begin to run from the day of completion of publication in all cases where publication is mandatory, and from the closure of the liquidation in actions arising out of the liquidation itself.

The prescription may be suspended or interrupted in accordance with the rules of the general law.

A joint-stock company is a company whose capital is divided into shares, that is, negotiable instruments, which operates under a trade name and is formed among a number of persons not less than three who subscribe for shares, and who are liable for the debts of the company only to the extent of their contributions.

Every joint-stock company, whatever its object may be, shall be subject to the Commercial Code and its usages.

One third of the capital of joint-stock companies whose object is the exploitation of a public utility or a public service must consist of registered shares held by Lebanese natural person shareholders or by companies whose capital consists of registered shares or parts wholly owned by Lebanese persons and whose articles of association prohibit the assignment of parts or shares therein except to Lebanese persons.

Any assignment of such shares in contravention of the provisions of the preceding paragraph shall be absolutely null and void.

The number of founders may not be less than three, and any person shall be prohibited from participating in the incorporation of a joint-stock company if he has been declared bankrupt and has not been rehabilitated for at least ten years, or if he has been convicted in Lebanon or abroad within less than ten years for committing or attempting to commit a felony or a misdemeanour punishable by the penalties for fraud, embezzlement of funds or securities, issuing cheques without provision in bad faith, undermining the financial standing of the State within the meaning of Articles 319 and 320 of the Penal Code, or concealing things obtained by means of these offences.

The same conditions shall apply to the representatives of legal persons participating in the incorporation of the company.

The founders shall be jointly and severally liable for the obligations contracted and the expenses incurred for the incorporation of the company, and they shall have no right of recourse against the subscribers in respect thereof if the company is not incorporated.

Subject to the provisions of the laws and regulations that subject the exercise of certain activities to prior authorisation, the incorporation of joint-stock companies shall not require an authorisation.

The articles of association of the joint-stock company and every subsequent amendment thereto must be deposited and registered with any notary public on Lebanese territory.

If the invitation is addressed to the public to subscribe to the capital of the company, the founders must publish in the Official Gazette and in two newspapers, one a local daily and the second an economic newspaper, a prospectus containing the name, signature and address of each of them and including, in particular, the name of the company, its head office and the offices of its branches, its object, its duration, the amount of its capital, the price of the shares and the amount paid up thereon, the value of the contributions in kind, the fixed interest clause, and, if any, the conditions for the distribution of profits, and the number of members of the Board of Directors, their remuneration stipulated in the company's articles of association, and their powers.

The particulars contained in the prospectus must also be inserted in the personal subscription document, the share certificate, posted notices, broadcasts and circulars, with an indication of the issues of the newspapers in which the prospectus was published.

Every violation of the provisions of the preceding Article shall entail the payment of a fine from two million to ten million Lebanese pounds, and the court may, where necessary, annul the subscriptions concluded.
The capital of a joint-stock company may not be less than thirty million Lebanese pounds and must be subscribed in full.
The minimum price of a single share is one thousand Lebanese pounds, and every subscriber must pay up in advance at least one quarter of the nominal value of each share to which he subscribes.

The founders must deposit the sums paid by the subscribers prior to the final constitution of the company, with one of the banks approved by the Government in an account opened in the name of the company together with a schedule of the subscribers and the sum paid by each of them.

These sums shall be withdrawn after the constitution of the company under the signature of the person or persons appointed in the articles of association of the company, after producing a certified copy of the articles of association, of the decree of authorisation, and of the minutes of the constituent meeting.

If the company is not constituted within a period of six months from the date of the authorisation, every subscriber shall have the right to apply to the judge of urgent matters for the appointment of a provisional administrator entrusted with withdrawing the sums and returning them to the subscribers after deducting the distribution expenses.

The validity of the valuation of contributions in kind shall be subject to the assessment of one or more experts appointed by the President of the Court of the district within which the registered office of the company is situated pursuant to an order issued by him upon the application of the founders.

It is prohibited to grant special advantages to any person in the articles of association of the company.

The report of the experts shall be placed at the disposal of the subscribers for inspection, and the latter may thereupon withdraw from the subscription if the valuation of the founders exceeds by twenty per cent the real value assigned to the contributed property and to the special advantages according to the valuation of the experts.

The founders may then subscribe themselves or procure others to subscribe for the shares of the withdrawing subscribers.
Shares issued for contributions in kind must be paid up in full upon the formation of the company.

And these shares must remain registered and attached to the counterfoil and bearing a stamp indicating their nature and the date of the formation of the company, and they shall not become negotiable until after the general meeting has approved the accounts of the second financial year of the company.

Provided that the aforesaid prohibition of negotiation shall not apply to shares issued for contributions in kind which have been allotted to the shareholders of a merged company whose shares were negotiable prior thereto.

The founders must, within the month following the report of the experts, convene a constituent general meeting of the shareholders, give notice of its meeting ten days prior to the appointed date, and submit to it the report of the experts on the valuation of the contributions in kind.

Resolutions shall be passed in accordance with the rules of quorum and majority applicable to this class of meetings, and holders of contributions in kind shall not take part in the voting even if they are at the same time subscribers for cash shares or proxies for such subscribers.

The carrying out of the aforesaid approval procedure shall not be obligatory in all cases where there are no cash shareholders other than the shareholders making contributions in kind.

The members of the board of directors must, after the incorporation of the company, carry out the initial formalities relating to publication by way of deposit and registration with the competent Commercial Register Secretariat, within the month following the incorporation, on pain of a fine determined by the judge supervising the Commercial Register, imposed on the company and ranging between five hundred thousand and one million Lebanese pounds.

The formalities mentioned in the preceding paragraph may be completed via electronic means specified by the Minister of Justice, provided that they are carried out exclusively by electronic means two years after the entry into force of this Law, and electronic publication on the website of the Commercial Register shall be available for inspection by the public.

Failure to publish entails the same consequences, namely the nullity of the company or the nullity of the omitted clause and the imposition of joint and several liability upon the first members of the board of directors and upon the first supervisory commissioners who are required to supervise the performance of all the formalities.

The company shall, on the other hand, be subject to a form of continuous publication:

The articles of association of the company must be posted in its offices.

Every person shall be entitled to request a certified true copy thereof in return for a moderate fee.

The name of the company must be stated on all its printed, handwritten, and electronic papers, with an indication that it is a joint-stock company and with a specification of the amount of its capital and the portion paid up thereof.

The completion of the aforementioned formalities shall not preclude a subsequent action for liability, which may be brought jointly and severally within five years from the date of incorporation of the company against the founders, the contributors in kind, the first members of the board of directors, and the experts, where a gross overvaluation in the appraisal of the contributions in kind becomes evident.

In all cases, the constituent assembly shall conduct an investigation based on the supporting documents to ascertain whether the conditions required for the incorporation of the company have been duly observed.

The aforementioned assembly shall appoint the first members of the board of directors if they have not been appointed pursuant to the articles of association of the company, and shall also appoint the first supervisory commissioners. The company shall be deemed incorporated as of their acceptance.

Those members and commissioners must verify that the company has been legally incorporated, and they shall be jointly and severally liable therefor.

Where a joint-stock company has been illegally incorporated, any person having standing and interest may, within a period of five years running from the date on which the defect occurred, serve formal notice upon it requiring the completion of the omitted formality.

If the company fails to carry out the rectification formality within one month, any person having standing and interest may apply for a judgment declaring the nullity of the company.

Shareholders may not invoke the nullity of the company against third parties.

A company declared null shall be liquidated as a de facto company.

Where the incorporation of the company is illegal, shareholders and third parties shall be entitled to bring, in addition to the action for nullity, an action for joint and several liability against the founders, the first members of the board of directors, and the first supervisory commissioners, as well as against the contributors in kind and the experts if the verification formalities were not carried out with honesty and good faith.

The establishment of liability requires proof of the existence of a causal link between the defect in incorporation and the damage suffered by the plaintiff. The action for liability shall be brought within the same period prescribed for the action for nullity.

A fine of two million to twenty million Lebanese pounds shall be imposed upon persons who have delivered, even in good faith, to subscribers definitive share certificates of an illegally incorporated joint-stock company, as well as upon persons who have sold or participated in the sale of such shares or have officially published their price. The declaration of liability shall require at least that the defect in incorporation be apparent.
Any fraudulent act intended to induce the public to subscribe or to pay money shall render its perpetrator liable to the penalties for fraud.

The members of the Board of Directors must deposit with the Secretariat of the competent Commercial Register each year, within two months from the date of the General Assembly's approval of the financial statements, and without such deposit exceeding the thirty-first of December of the current year, the following documents:

1 - The report of the auditors accompanied by the individual financial statements for the past year prepared in accordance with the accounting standards in force, in particular the balance sheet, the income statement, the statement of changes in shareholders' equity and the notes to the financial statements.

2 - The report of the auditors accompanied by the consolidated financial statements for the past year prepared in accordance with the accounting standards in force.

3 - The special report of the auditors pursuant to the provisions of Article 158 of this Law.

4 - The report of the Board of Directors on the company's operations for the past year.

5 - The report of the Board of Directors pursuant to the provisions of Article 158 of this Law.

6 - The attendance sheet and the minutes of the General Assembly meeting approving the financial statements for the past year, the report of the Board of Directors for the past year and the special reports relating to the transactions subject to the provisions of Article 158 of this Law, where applicable, provided that the said report includes the following information:

- The result of the past year.

- The accumulated results, especially those requiring the taking of any measure pursuant to Article 216 of this Law.

- The names of the members of the elected Board of Directors whenever its election falls due and any amendment occurring thereto.

- The appointment of the auditors whenever the appointment falls due.

A copy of the documents set forth in this Article may be obtained from the Commercial Register at the applicant's expense.

The formalities mentioned in this Article may be completed through electronic means determined by the Minister of Justice, provided that publication on the website of the Commercial Register after two years from the entry into force of this Law shall be mandatory and accessible to the public.

The judge supervising the Commercial Register shall fine the company an amount of one hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds annually for each document that is not duly deposited.

For the purpose of depositing and registering the documents provided for in Article 101 within the time limits provided for in the Article, the company shall be exempted from a clearance certificate issued by the National Social Security Fund.

In principle, all shareholders in the same company shall have the same rights and shall share in the same benefits.

However, in all cases where the company's articles of association do not contain an express prohibition, preference shares may be created pursuant to a resolution of an extraordinary general meeting deliberating thereon in the manner set forth below.

Such shares confer upon their holders a right of priority either in receiving certain shares of the profits, or in the reimbursement of capital, or in both of these advantages together, or any other pecuniary benefit.

If the general meeting adopts a resolution that would in any manner diminish the rights pertaining to a class of shares, such resolution shall not be effective except after the approval of a special meeting composed of the holders of the shares of the class concerned.

Such meeting shall follow in its deliberations the rules pertaining to quorum and voting in extraordinary general meetings.

When the capital is increased by the creation of new shares to be subscribed for in cash, the shareholders of all existing classes shall, in principle, have a preferential right to subscribe for the total of the new shares in proportion to the old shares which they own and on an irreducible basis.

The extraordinary general meeting which approved the capital increase shall take all measures with respect to the shares remaining after distribution.

However, this meeting may resolve that the right of subscription shall not be reserved to the existing shareholders, or that it shall be reserved to them only in part, or that it shall not be in proportion to the shares previously owned.

In this case, every allotment of the new shares, whether to non-shareholders or to a class of preferred shareholders, shall be subject to the verification to which contributions in kind are subject.

This verification shall cover all the shares allotted to non-shareholders.

As regards shareholders, it shall cover only what exceeds the proportion fixed for the old shares.

If this verification is not carried out, the capital increase shall be null and void.

Every shareholder is entitled, if sufficient assets remain upon the dissolution of the company, to recover the nominal amount of his share, subject to the right of priority granted to priority shares.

As for the surplus, it shall be distributed among all the shareholders in proportion to the number of shares owned.

The company may redeem its capital by appropriating a sum from its profits to a special reserve or to amortisation, both prepared for this purpose.

Redemption shall take place in accordance with the methods provided for in the company's articles of association or the methods approved by the general assembly.

When redemption takes place, the extinguished shares shall be replaced by shares called enjoyment shares (jouissance), and these shares shall grant their holders the privileges of circulating shares except for the interest specified in the company's articles of association and the nominal amount of the shares upon the dissolution of the company.

Every shareholder shall have the right to attend the various assemblies convened to incorporate the company and to conduct its business, and he shall have, in principle, upon voting, a number of votes equal to the number of his shares.

If the company is notified of the existence of a usufruct over specific shares, it shall be obliged to notify the holder of the usufruct of all notices of meetings and matters without exception, including resolutions to distribute any economic benefits.

The holder of the usufruct of the share alone shall have the right to attend ordinary general assemblies and vote therein, and the holder of the bare ownership shall have the right to attend extraordinary general assemblies and vote therein. The holder of the bare ownership shall be deemed the person authorised to be notified of all notices of meetings, papers and all matters without exception, including notification of resolutions to distribute any economic benefits.

The holder of the usufruct and the holder of the bare ownership may agree to depart from the provisions of the preceding paragraph in accordance with the manner they see fit, provided that a contract is signed between them and subject to notifying the company thereof and publishing it and in the commercial register.

In the event of co-ownership of shares, all co-owners must choose one person from among themselves or a third party to attend the ordinary and extraordinary general assemblies and vote therein. Should they fail to agree on appointing one person, the president of the competent court of first instance within whose jurisdiction the company's head office is located shall appoint a representative of the co-owners, upon the request of any of the owners, by virtue of an immediately enforceable decision issued in accordance with summary proceedings and after hearing the remaining owners. The appointed representative shall continue to perform his duties until the convening of the annual general assembly to approve the accounts. The president of the court may renew the appointment in accordance with the same procedures.

Joint-stock companies shall issue shares, and they may issue debentures, and they may also issue debentures convertible into shares.

They may not issue founders' shares, that is, securities granting the founders a right to obtain a share of the company's profits without capital previously contributed.
Shares are equal, indivisible fractions of the company's capital represented by negotiable instruments which shall be registered.

A share confers upon its holder certain rights inherent thereto, namely: the right to dividends, the preferential right of subscription upon an increase of the capital, the right to recover the nominal value of the share, the right to share in the partitioning of the company's assets, the right to vote at the general meeting, and the right to assign his share.

Share dividends must only be drawn from the net profits resulting from a true balance sheet and remaining available after deducting the amount necessary to constitute the legal reserve and the statutory reserve, that is, that provided for in the company's articles of association.

Every distribution of fictitious dividends shall render the members of the board of directors civilly liable towards any person who suffers damage therefrom, and shall also render the auditors liable in the same manner with the members of the board of directors, unless the auditors prove that they committed no fault in supervision.

The members of the board of directors and the auditors shall be criminally liable if dividends are distributed without a balance sheet or pursuant to a fraudulent inventory, balance sheet or financial statements, and they shall be punished with the penalty for fraud or with any other penalty provided for by law.

Shareholders who have received such dividends of profit shall not be bound to return them unless their bad faith or their commission of a gross fault equivalent to fraud is proven.

As for the action for recovery which the company, its creditors or any of the shareholders are entitled to bring against them, it shall bind them to return the amount which they received without right together with interest thereon from the day of payment.

This action shall be barred by prescription after the expiry of five years from the date of distribution.

Amounts distributed pursuant to the provision relating to fixed interest (Interets fixes) paid to the shareholders under any circumstance whatsoever and included among the charges of the company shall not be deemed fictitious profits.

However, such provision shall only be lawful if the following two conditions are met:

- Namely, that the rate of interest does not exceed four per cent.

- And that the period of application of the provision is five years at most.

This provision must be published by depositing it in the company's register at the Commercial Registry, failing which it shall be null and void.

Provided, however, that fully paid-up shares that have remained with a single owner for at least two years prior to the convening of each assembly shall each carry two votes.

With regard to the aforementioned period, the shares shall be deemed as belonging to the same owner when they are acquired by way of inheritance, gift or bequest.

Extraordinary assemblies may, by unanimity of the shareholders, decide to abolish the double vote provided for above.

The text of the first and second paragraphs of this Article shall not apply to companies incorporated after the promulgation of this Law.

Subject to the restrictions relating to shares issued for contributions in kind, every shareholder may freely assign his shares to another person, whereupon such person shall take his place in his rights and obligations in the capacity of a shareholder.

Provided, however, that a provision may be inserted in the articles of association of the company stipulating that pre-emption in purchase shall belong to the shareholders, or to a group of them, or to the company itself, on condition that this right is exercised in accordance with the time-limit and the price determination mechanism provided for in the by-laws of the company. Provided, however, that the exercise of this right may not be abused by rendering the share practically non-negotiable or by inflicting gross prejudice upon the shareholder.

In the event that there is a holder of a right of usufruct and a holder of a right of bare ownership for a single share, the holder of the right of bare ownership alone shall be entitled to exercise the right of pre-emption where applicable.

The company may not exercise the right of pre-emption stipulated in its favour except out of such free reserve funds as it possesses.

Furthermore, a company whose shares are listed on the financial markets may purchase, out of the free reserve funds available to it, shares issued by it, provided that their value does not exceed a percentage of the total of its shares to be determined in accordance with the regulations governing the Financial Markets Law.

The holder of a share who has not paid its full price shall be bound to comply with the call of the board of directors to pay up the remainder of the price or a part thereof, in accordance with the mechanism and conditions provided for in the resolution containing the call for payment.

All those who acquired the share prior to him shall remain jointly and severally liable for the unpaid amount for a period of two years only from the date of assignment.

Every provision in the by-laws of the company or every resolution contrary to the provisions of this Article shall be deemed null and void with absolute nullity.

A former shareholder who has been compelled to pay up the remainder or a part of the price of the share which he assigned shall be subrogated to the rights of the company and to the right of action against all those who acquired the share after him.

In all cases, the former shareholder shall have the right of recourse against the shareholder who acquired the share after him.

The company's articles of association or the resolution of the extraordinary general assembly that decides to issue the preference shares shall determine the privileges, priorities, and other pecuniary rights or benefits enjoyed by these shares, and in particular the share of preferred profit pertaining to them and whether this profit is cumulative or non-cumulative (cumulatif ou non cumulatif).

In the event that profits are available to the company for a given financial year, it must distribute the share of preferred profit pertaining to the preference shares, and if it appears to the company that it has no profits or that its profits are insufficient to pay the whole or part of the share of preferred profit pertaining to the preference shares, the available profits shall be distributed among the holders of the preference shares in proportion to the shares they own, and the recovery of the balance of the accrued preferred profit, where it is cumulative, shall be carried forward to the following financial year and, where necessary, to subsequent financial years.

The distribution of the share of preferred profit shall not take place until after deducting the amounts distributed pursuant to the provision relating to the fixed interest provided for in Article 109 of this Law; as for the remaining balance, the decision on the manner of its distribution shall rest with the ordinary general assembly, provided that such distribution does not conflict with the company's articles of association and with the resolution of the extraordinary general assembly that created the preference shares.

The issuance of new preference shares may not prejudice any of the rights pertaining to the preference shares, or to the priority shares provided for in Article 110 of this Law, or to the bonds convertible into shares, any of which were issued on a date prior to the issuance of the new preference shares, except after obtaining the approval of the special assembly composed for each of the holders of these shares or bonds.

Contrary to the provisions of Article 121 bis, the holders of preferred shares shall acquire a right to vote equal to the right of all other shareholders in proportion to what the shares they own represent in the capital of the company in the following cases:

1 - Where a cumulative or non-cumulative priority share of profits attributable to the preferred shares has been fixed and has not been paid in full or in part, as the case may be, for a single financial year despite the availability of profits in the company for that year.

This right shall remain in force until the expiry of the financial year in which the full priority share of profits due is paid.

2 - Where the company fails to ensure that the preferred shares benefit from all other privileges, priorities or rights prescribed for them.

This right shall remain in force as long as the prescribed privileges, priorities or rights have not been ensured for the beneficiaries.

3 - In general meetings relating to changing the object or form of the company, or to paying up an increase of its capital in kind, or to dissolving it before the term, or to operations of absorption, merger or division to which it is a party.

Notwithstanding any contrary provision, there shall be formed of the holders of preferred shares upon each issue, a special meeting which shall be convened, held and take its resolutions in the manner of the meeting of debenture holders in accordance with Articles 137, 138 and 139 of this Law.

The special meeting of holders of preferred shares may issue one or more advisory opinions on the matters submitted to the general meetings of the company's shareholders or on any matter on which the holders of preferred shares deem it in their interest to express an opinion.

The special meeting of holders of preferred shares shall notify this opinion to the company in order to inform the general meeting thereof and enter it in the minutes of the latter.

This special meeting may also appoint a representative of the holders of preferred shares for the purpose of attending the general meetings of shareholders, and this representative shall have, where necessary, the right to express the opinion of the meeting he represents before the conduct of the vote in which he is not entitled to participate. This opinion shall be recorded in the minutes of the general meeting of the company.

The chairman and members of the board of directors, the general managers and the assistant general managers appointed in accordance with the provisions of Article 153 of this Law, as well as their spouses and minor children, are prohibited from acquiring ownership of preferred shares or having any kind of rights accrue to them over such shares, directly or indirectly, or under the cover of a natural or legal third party, or in any form whatsoever.

If the called amount of the price of a share is not paid, the company shall be entitled, after serving notice of default upon the defaulting shareholder, to sell the share and charge him with the expenses and losses resulting from the sale, and if the price at which the share is sold is less than the amount due, the shareholder shall remain bound to pay the difference, jointly and severally with the shareholders who held the share before him.

All those who held the share before him shall remain jointly and severally liable for the unpaid amount for a period of two years only from the date of transfer.

Where there is a usufructuary and a bare owner of the same share, the bare owner shall be bound to make payment in accordance with Articles 119, 120 and 121 of this Law, unless there is an agreement to the contrary between them duly notified to the board of directors of the company, in accordance with the provisions of Article 116 of this Law.

Articles 121 bis 1 to 121 bis 12 are added to Part One of Chapter Two of Title Three of Book Two of the Code of Land Commerce pursuant to Law 126 dated 29/3/2019.

Without prejudice to the provisions of Law No. 308 dated 3/4/2001 relating to the Issuance and Trading of Bank Shares, any joint-stock company may create registered preferred shares enjoying certain privileges, rights, pecuniary benefits or priorities and benefitting from all the rights provided for in Article 105 of this Law, with the exception of the right to participate in deliberations and voting at general meetings, the right to hold membership on the board of directors, and the right to share in the division of the company's assets.

The management of the company shall make available to the holders of preferred shares the information and documents prepared for the inspection of the other shareholders.

1 - Without prejudice to the application of the provisions of Article 207 of this Law, preferred shares shall be created either upon the incorporation of the company or upon any increase of its capital.

2 - The provisions of Article 8 of Part Three of Chapter Two of Title Three of Book Two and Articles 112 and 113 of this Law shall not apply upon the creation of preferred shares.

3 - Notwithstanding the provisions of item (2) of this Article, the company may grant its shareholders a pre-emptive right to subscribe to the issued preferred shares, provided that the conditions for exercising such right are specified in the articles of association of the company or by virtue of a resolution of the extraordinary general meeting of shareholders that creates the preferred shares.

Preferred shares are prohibited from representing a percentage exceeding thirty percent (30%) of the registered shares representing the capital of the company as at the date of issuance of such shares.

In the event of an increase of the company's capital through the creation of new shares subscribed for in cash, the holders of preferred shares shall not have a pre-emptive right to subscribe for the new shares in accordance with the provisions of Article 112 of this Law; however, it shall be open to the company to grant a pre-emptive right to the holders of preferred shares to subscribe for the newly issued shares and to determine the conditions for the exercise of this right in the articles of association or pursuant to a resolution of the extraordinary general assembly of shareholders, and in this case the provisions of the second paragraph of Article 113 of this Law shall not apply.

If the company increases its capital through the incorporation of reserve funds of whatever kind or retained earnings, or the distribution of new bonus ordinary shares, or an increase in the nominal value of the share, the holders of preferred shares shall not benefit from this distribution or from this increase except where there is a provision to the contrary either in the articles of association of the company or in the resolutions issued by the extraordinary general assembly that created the preferred shares.

The company shall be prohibited, starting from the date of the issuance of the preferred shares and throughout the period of the existence of such shares, from carrying out any redemption of its capital in accordance with Article 115 of this Law.

In the event of a reduction of capital for reasons not resulting from losses, the company must purchase the preferred shares and cancel them before any purchase of ordinary shares or reduction of their nominal value, without prejudice to the application of the provisions of Articles 208 and 209 of this Law, and provided that the full priority dividends due and that shall become due up to the date of payment are paid. In this case, the value of the preferred shares shall be determined on a date prior to or simultaneous with the purchase by agreement between the company and the special assembly of the holders of preferred shares, and in the event of disagreement, the actual value of the share as at the date of the resolution to reduce the capital shall be determined by one or more certified public accountants appointed by the two parties by agreement; in the event that such agreement is not possible, the expert or experts shall be appointed by the President of the Commercial Court within whose jurisdiction the head office of the company is located.

The company shall be entitled to purchase the preferred shares, provided that:

1 - This right and the bases and conditions of its exercise, particularly the timing and price of the purchase, are provided for by an express clause in the articles of association of the company or in the resolution of the extraordinary general assembly which previously resolved to issue the shares sought to be purchased.

2 - This purchase is effected after the full payment of all due and unpaid priority dividend shares pertaining to any issue of preferred shares made by the company, unless the resolution issuing the preferred shares provides otherwise.

Upon the dissolution and liquidation of the company, the nominal value of the preferred shares and the unpaid priority dividend share in its entirety pertaining to those shares shall be paid prior to any payment of the value of the ordinary shares. Furthermore, notwithstanding the provisions of Article 121 bis 1, what pertains to the preferred shares from the liquidation proceeds may be paid in the event that the articles of association of the company provide, or the extraordinary general assembly which created the preferred shares resolved, for their right to benefit from the said proceeds. In the event of not benefiting from the liquidation proceeds, and notwithstanding any other text, the holders of these shares shall be entitled by operation of law to the value of the issue premium paid by them upon subscription to the said shares.

Preferred shares may be converted into ordinary shares pursuant to a resolution of the extraordinary general assembly issued on the basis of a special report by the supervisory commissioners, in accordance with the conditions, bases and time limits provided for in the articles of association of the company or which were decided by the extraordinary general assembly which created the preferred shares.

The company may issue negotiable and indivisible debentures having a single nominal value, given to subscribers in return for the sums which they have advanced.

However, debentures may not be issued until after the capital subscribed by the shareholders has been paid in full.

Members of the board of directors and managers who issue or permit the issue of debentures in contravention of the provisions of the preceding paragraph shall be punished by a fine of one thousand to ten thousand Lebanese pounds, and such debentures shall be null and void.
The holder of the said debentures shall be entitled to receive a fixed interest payable at periodic terms and to recover his capital from the assets of the company. (Patrimoine social.)

Without prejudice to the rules applicable to real estate credit companies, debentures may not be issued for an amount exceeding twice the existing capital of the company according to the financial statement audited by the auditors and approved by the general assembly, provided that its date does not go back more than six months from the date of issue of the debentures.
Even if the articles of association of the company provide for the issue of debentures, they may not be issued except after the approval of the general assembly.

The members of the board of directors of the company must, prior to publishing any advertisement preceding the issue, publish in the Official Gazette and in an economic newspaper and a local daily newspaper a notice containing their signatures and the address of each of them and comprising in particular the date of the resolution of the general assembly which authorised the issue, the number of debentures intended to be issued, their value and the rate of interest, the date of redemption and its conditions and guarantees, the number of debentures previously issued together with their guarantees, the amount of the capital, the value of the contributions in kind, the existence of a fixed-interest clause, and the results of the last certified balance sheet, failing which they shall be liable to a fine of one thousand to five thousand Lebanese pounds.

The subscription document, the debenture certificate, and the advertisements, announcements and circulars must contain the particulars set out in that notice, with a reference to the issues of the newspapers in which it was published.
Those who subscribe for the purchase of debentures may cancel their subscription if the aforementioned formalities are not observed.

Every issue of debentures must, after it takes place, be entered in the Commercial Register through the care of the members of the board of directors.

If they fail to carry out this formality, they shall be liable to a fine of five hundred to two thousand five hundred Lebanese pounds.

If the price of the debentures is not paid in full originally and the calls for payment of the remainder of their price are of no avail, the company shall have the right to resort to the method of sale on the floor of the Stock Exchange.
Mortgage debentures may be issued, provided that their issue shall be in accordance with the provisions of the Decision issued by the High Commissioner No. 77 L.R. dated 26 May 1933.
The representatives of the body of bondholders shall have the right to take all conservatory measures for the preservation of their rights.

However, measures aimed at extending the time limits for redemption, or reducing the interest rate, or the principal of the debt, or the security guarantees therefor, and in general all measures which sacrifice the rights of the bondholders, may only be taken by their general meeting fulfilling the conditions of the legal quorum specified in the first paragraph of Article 193 by a majority of two-thirds of the votes of the bondholders present or represented.

The representatives of the bondholders shall have the right to attend the general meetings of the shareholders after receiving the same notices as are sent to the shareholders.

However, they shall not have the right to vote in the deliberations.

If a company continues to pay interest or dividends on shares, bonds, or other financial instruments whose value is redeemed by way of drawing lots, the company may not recover the aforementioned amounts when the instrument is presented for redemption. Any provision contrary to this rule shall be disregarded.

The management of a joint-stock company shall be carried out by a board of directors composed of three members at least and twelve members at most; subject to what may be provided for by special laws concerning certain joint-stock companies, the number of Lebanese nationals on the board of directors must not be less than one-third.

The board of directors must appoint one of its members to the chairmanship.

The chairman of the board of directors shall not require a work permit if he is a non-Lebanese national not residing in Lebanon.

The members of the board of directors shall receive their remuneration either by the fixing of an annual sum for them, or by the fixing of a lump sum for each meeting they attend, or by the allocation of a proportional percentage of the net profits, or by a method combining these various benefits.

As for the profits from which the proportional percentage allocated to the members of the board of directors is taken, they must in principle only include the net proceeds of the operation that constitutes the object of the company.

Consequently, the income of the portfolio of securities may not be merged therein except by way of exception and pursuant to a special resolution issued by the general meeting and renewed every year.

The ordinary general assembly shall elect the members of the board of directors, provided that the first members may be appointed in the articles of association of the company.

Where there is a usufructuary and a bare owner for the same share, the bare owner alone shall be entitled to be a member of the board of directors, salvo any agreement to the contrary between the bare owner and the usufructuary, in accordance with what is provided for in Article 116 of this Law.

Where there are co-owners in common of the same share, the provisions of Article 116 of this Law shall also apply, and consequently only one person representing the co-owners in common shall be eligible for membership of the board of directors.

During the period falling between two annual assemblies, if the number of acting members falls, owing to death, resignation or other causes, below half of the minimum number fixed in the articles of association or below three, the remaining members shall convene the general assembly within two months at the latest to fill the vacant seats.
The ordinary general assembly shall elect the members of the board of directors from among the shareholders or from among non-shareholders.

No person may be chosen as a member of the board of directors if he has been declared bankrupt and has not been rehabilitated for at least ten years, or if he has been convicted in Lebanon or abroad less than ten years ago for committing or attempting to commit a felony or a misdemeanour, and the same conditions shall apply to the representatives of legal persons on the board of directors.

The members of the board of directors appointed pursuant to the articles of association of the company shall have a term of office of five years at most, whereas those who are appointed by resolution of the assembly of shareholders shall have a term of office of three years at most; they may be re-elected, and the articles of association of the company may include special provisions for the partial renewal of the body of the board of directors.
The members of the board of directors shall be subject to dismissal without any cause. Any provision to the contrary shall be disregarded.

If the general assembly of shareholders resolves upon dismissal and the question of dismissal was not included on its agenda, no effect shall be given to such resolution until after it is confirmed by a new general assembly whose agenda includes that question. And this second assembly shall be convened through the offices of the supervisory commissioners within two months from the date of the holding of the first assembly, and one of them shall preside over it.
Lottery debentures must be authorised by virtue of a governmental licence upon the proposal of the Minister of Economy and Trade.
It shall be permissible to issue debentures allocated a redemption premium payable upon the amortisation of the debenture.
The repayment of the value of the debentures shall take place in accordance with the conditions laid down upon issue, and the company may neither advance nor postpone the due date.

Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary, the debenture holders shall constitute a single body which is formed of its own accord upon each issue, and its resolutions adopted by a majority of votes shall be binding with respect to all.
After the close of subscription, the issuing company shall convene a general meeting of the debenture holders to approve the bylaws of their body and to appoint those who represent it.

Whenever it appears that convening the meeting of debenture holders is of benefit, it shall be called to meet either upon the request of its representatives or the request of a group of debenture holders representing 20/1 of the value of the debentures, or upon the request of the joint-stock company.

The meeting shall be convened by two successive notices in the Official Gazette, in an economic newspaper, and in a local daily newspaper, the interval between them being eight days, and they shall include the subjects listed on the agenda, and the deliberation may not deal with any other subjects.
The rules of legal quorum and voting shall be those specified in Articles 193 and 195 for general meetings of shareholders.

Every change in the composition of the board of directors must be published by depositing the minutes with the competent commercial register through the diligence of the members of the board of directors.

The notice of service whereby the company takes cognisance of the resignation of one of the members of the board of directors shall likewise be registered in the same commercial register.

In both cases, publication or registration shall take place without the need to produce any other document of any kind whatsoever, whether official or unofficial.

The management of the company shall be vested in the chairman of the board of directors-general manager, whom the board of directors elects from among the natural persons of whom the board is composed.

The articles of association of the company may include the possibility of separating the chairmanship of the board of directors on the one hand and the management of the company on the other hand.

The board of directors shall appoint, from among natural persons, a general manager from among the shareholders or from among non-shareholders.

It shall be for the chairman of the board of directors-general manager, or for the general manager exclusively in the event of separation between the two positions, to propose to the board the appointment of one or more assistant general managers, the board of directors appointing the assistant general manager or the assistant general managers from outside the board of directors and from among the shareholders or non-shareholders, provided that they are natural persons.

The assistant general manager shall perform his duties under the personal liability of the authority that proposed his appointment.

Where the chairman is in a state that temporarily prevents him from performing his duties, he may delegate all or part of them to one of the members of the board of directors, provided that this delegation must always be for a fixed period.

If, however, the chairman is in a state in which he is permanently unable to perform his duties, the board of directors may deem him to have resigned and elect another in his stead.

Members of the board of directors may hold managerial positions in the company in return for remuneration determined by the board of directors, save that they shall not benefit from the provisions of the Labour Code unless they have been employees of the company for at least two years upon assuming office.

For the resolutions of the Board to be valid, at least half of the members must attend or be represented at the meeting, and a member may represent only one member.

The company's articles of association may, within the framework of calculating the majority and the quorum in the meetings of the Board, provide for the possibility of considering the members who participate in the meetings of the Board of Directors via remote audio-visual communication technology or other technical means the conditions of which are determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Justice, as present at the meeting, provided that the verification of the identity of the connected member and the security, continuity and reliability of the connection and the effective participation of the connected member in the discussions are ensured, on condition that the company's articles of association provide for the mechanism to be adopted in this framework, and the articles of association may also provide for prohibiting the issuance of certain resolutions by a Board of Directors in which members participate remotely via the aforementioned communication technology.

Recourse to the use of any of these technologies is prohibited in the case of preparing and approving the annual accounts, the annual financial statements and the reports on the past year mentioned in Article 101.

The content of the remote communication in all meetings of the Board of Directors must be recorded, such that the recordings are considered an integral part of the minutes of the meeting and are kept therewith.
