No person may hold the chairmanship of a board of directors in more than six companies in Lebanon, nor may any person be a general manager or an assistant general manager in more than three companies having their head office in Lebanon.

No natural person may be a member of more than eight boards of directors of companies having their head office in Lebanon.

Holding the chairmanship and membership on boards of directors belonging to different insurance companies having one trade name shall be deemed to constitute a single chairmanship or membership.

In the event of a violation of the provisions of this Article, any interested party may serve notice upon the offender and the company requiring compliance therewith. If the offender fails to regularise his position within a period of two months after being notified of the formal notice, he shall be deemed to have resigned ipso jure upon the expiry of this period, and any interested party may, if the violation continues, apply for a judgment declaring the nullity of the resolutions adopted by the board of directors in the presence of the offender.

Neither the offender nor the company may invoke the nullity of such resolutions against third parties.

In all cases, the offender must restitution to the company the salaries and remunerations he has received since the occurrence of the violation.

The chairman of the board of directors and the general manager shall not be deemed merchants except in respect of the following matters:

The competent court may rule against both or either of them for the forfeiture of the rights which the law attaches to bankruptcy if the company becomes bankrupt and its bankruptcy results from fraud or grave faults in the management of the company's business.

If all or part of the functions of the chairman have been delegated to one of the persons referred to in Article 153, the person to whom the functions of the chairman have been delegated shall bear, in proportion to such functions delegated to him, the liabilities specified in this Article in place of the chairman of the board of directors.

The Board of Directors shall have broad powers to execute the resolutions of the General Assembly and to perform all acts required by the normal course of the enterprise which are not deemed to be daily acts. Such powers shall have no limitation or reservation other than what is provided for in the law or in the company's articles of association.

The Board of Directors may delegate some of its powers to the Chairman of the Board of Directors-General Manager in the event that a General Manager is not appointed, or to the General Manager, for a short and fixed period, provided that such delegation is subject to publication in the Commercial Register.

The Chairman of the Board of Directors-General Manager shall have all powers to represent the company before third parties, execute the resolutions of the Board of Directors, and conduct the daily business of the company as set out in the articles of association or custom, under the supervision and control of the Board of Directors.

In the event that a General Manager is appointed in accordance with the provisions of Article 153 of this Law, the Chairman of the Board of Directors shall have the authority of general supervision over the course of business in the company, without interfering in the daily acts, and he shall chair the Board of Directors and address general directives to the General Manager, without their being binding on the latter. In this case, the General Manager shall have all powers to represent the company before third parties, execute the resolutions of the Board of Directors, and conduct the daily business of the company as set out in the articles of association or custom, under the supervision and control of the Board of Directors.

The Chairman and members of the Board of Directors, the General Manager and the Assistant General Manager shall not participate in the management of a company having an object or activity similar to that of their company unless they have obtained prior authorisation from the Ordinary General Assembly, and such authorisation shall be renewed every year.

The Chairman and members of the Board of Directors, the General Manager and the Assistant General Manager shall not have any interest in any company, association, syndicate or other group carrying out operations intended to bring about an effect on stock exchange prices relating to the securities issued by the company, whatever their kind.

The members of the Board of Directors shall, at the end of the first six months of the financial year, prepare the interim financial statements for that period. They shall also draw up at the end of the year the financial statements referred to in Article 101 of this Law.

The financial statements shall be clear. Any change occurring from one year to another in the method of their preparation or presentation shall be disclosed in the complementary notes to the audited financial statements.

In addition to the financial statements referred to in Article 101 of this Law, the Board of Directors shall draw up a report on the situation of the company and its activity during the ended year to be submitted to the shareholders fifteen days prior to the date of the meeting of the General Assembly.

The report of the Board of Directors shall clearly and accurately include the following subjects:

- The situation of the company and its activity during the ended year.

- The results of this activity.

- The progress achieved and the problems encountered.

- The expected development of the situation of the company.

- A statement of the expected risks.

- The important operations that occurred between the date of the end of the year and the date of the meeting of the General Assembly.
The Board of Directors shall convene the shareholders to hold General Assemblies.

The Board of Directors shall form a reserve fund by deducting ten per cent from the net profits after deducting previous losses until the reserve fund becomes equal to one-third of the capital of the company.

The members of the Board of Directors and the General Manager shall be liable, even towards third parties, for all acts of fraud and for every violation of the law and of the articles of association of the company; as for the action which the injured party is entitled to bring, it is an individual action, and it shall not be permissible, even with regard to the shareholders, to stay it by a vote of the General Assembly discharging the members of the Board of Directors and the General Manager.

1 - The members and the Chairman of the Board of Directors, the Assistant General Manager, and every shareholder who directly or indirectly holds voting rights exceeding five percent (5%) in the capital of the company, shall be subject to prior authorisation from the Board of Directors regarding every contract, agreement, or commitment intended to be concluded with the company, whether the said contract, agreement, or commitment is conducted directly, indirectly, or under the cover of a third party.

None of the persons mentioned above shall be entitled to participate in the voting on the resolution granting or refusing the authorisation relating to him, nor shall the votes of the persons mentioned above be counted within the quorum for attendance or voting when discussing the said authorisation.

Contracts, agreements, and commitments the subject matter of which consists of ordinary transactions between the company and its customers shall be exempted from this obligation and from the provisions of authorisation.

2 - Every agreement between the company and another company shall be subject to the prior authorisation of the Board of Directors if any of the persons mentioned in the first paragraph of this Article is:

a - A partner who directly or indirectly holds voting rights exceeding five percent (5%) in the capital of that company.

b - Or a general partner or an authorised partner in that company, regardless of the proportion of his shares in its capital, in the event that it is a general partnership or a limited partnership.

c - Or a manager of that company or a member of its Board of Directors.

This person shall not be entitled to participate in the voting on the resolution granting or refusing the authorisation relating to that company, nor shall his vote be counted within the quorum for attendance or voting when discussing the authorisation.

3 - The person who meets one of the conditions mentioned in the two paragraphs above must inform the Board of Directors thereof immediately, in writing, and in detail.

4 - The Board of Directors must.

a - Examine the authorisations of the contracts, agreements, and commitments mentioned in the first and second paragraphs of this Article, within a reasonable period and prior to the convening of the General Assembly, and in the event of approval of the authorisations, submit a special report thereon to the first General Assembly, whether ordinary or extraordinary, for ratification.

The persons mentioned in the first paragraph of this Article shall not be entitled to participate in the voting on the ratification resolution, nor shall their shares be counted within the quorum.

b - Notify the auditors of the contracts, agreements, and commitments that have been authorised, within a period of fifteen days from the authorisation resolution.

The auditors shall submit to the General Assembly their special report relating to the contracts, agreements, and commitments mentioned in the first and second paragraph of this Article, stating their opinion regarding the impact of those contracts, agreements, and commitments on the financial statements and the supplementary notes thereto, for voting thereon in accordance with the rules.

5 - Subject to the provisions of the laws and regulations specific to banks and financial markets, each of the members and the Chairman of the Board of Directors, the General Manager, the Assistant General Manager, its auditors, and any shareholder who directly or indirectly holds voting rights exceeding five percent (5%) in its capital shall be prohibited from obtaining from the company, in any manner whatsoever, a loan, facilities, a suretyship, or any guarantee towards third parties.

In all cases, the authorisation shall not be deemed effective until after its ratification by the General Assembly.

A shareholder or a group of shareholders, either of which represents at least ten per cent (10%) of the capital of the company, may apply to the President of the Chamber of First Instance within whose jurisdiction the head office of the company is situated in order to appoint an additional auditor chosen from among the accounting experts before the court, who shall have the same authority and whose remuneration shall not exceed the remuneration prescribed for the auditors appointed pursuant to Article 172.

The auditors shall audit the financial statements provided for in Article 101 of this Law prepared by the board of directors in order to express their opinion on the accuracy thereof, provided that their report includes an indication of the cases of non-compliance by the company with its articles of association and the laws and regulations in force.

The board of directors and the general manager shall provide the auditors with all information, documents, papers, instruments and accounting books necessary for them to complete the audit procedures and works at any time of the year.

The board of directors shall provide the auditors with the financial statements provided for in Article 101 of this Law at least sixty days before the convening of the general assembly.

The auditors shall submit to the general assembly their report on the financial statements for approval thereof. If they do not submit this report, the resolution of the general assembly relating to the approval of the statements shall be null and void.

The auditors must convene the general assembly whenever the members of the board of directors fail to convene it in the cases specified in the law or in the company's articles of association.

They shall likewise be entitled to convene it whenever they deem its convening useful.

Moreover, they must convene the general assembly if requested to do so by a group of shareholders representing one-fifth of the company's capital.

And the auditors may not have any direct or indirect interest with a group whose object is to bring about an effect on the prices of any class of the securities of the company.

Nor may the auditors have an interest outside the scope of their mandate, in particular through consultancy contracts of whatever kind, (with the company or with a shareholder that is a legal person or a shareholder or group of shareholders owning ten per cent or more of the company's capital).

The auditors shall be liable, either individually or jointly and severally, even towards third parties, whenever they commit a fault in supervision, subject to the provision on prescription after five years.
The general assemblies of shareholders are the constituent assembly, ordinary assemblies and extraordinary assemblies.

The persons referred to in Article 166 are also liable towards the shareholders for their fault in management.

In general, the members of the board of directors and the general manager shall not be liable for their fault in management towards third parties. However, in the event of the bankruptcy of the company and the appearance of a deficit in the assets, the court may, upon the request of the bankruptcy trustee or the Public Prosecution, or of its own motion, decide that the debts of the company shall be borne by the members of the board of directors and/or the general manager or any other person entrusted with managing or supervising the business of the company, including the supervisory commissioners, and the court shall determine the amounts for which they shall be liable and whether or not they are jointly and severally liable; and in order to be exonerated from such liability, they must furnish proof that they attended to the management and supervision of the business of the company with the care of a diligent and active professional.

In the event of separation between the office of chairman of the board of directors and that of the general manager by the board of directors, the chairman of the board of directors shall not be liable except in the case of violation of the law or of the articles of association of the company.

The right to bring an action against the chairman and members of the board of directors and the general manager pursuant to the first paragraph of the preceding Article belongs to the company, and if it fails to do so, every shareholder shall have the right to bring the action on its behalf to the extent of the interest that he has in the company.

In order for a discharge to be pleaded, it must always be preceded by the rendering of the accounts of the company and the report of the supervisory commissioners. Such discharge shall only cover the matters of which the general assembly was able to have knowledge.

Liability shall be either individual, pertaining to one member of the board of directors or the general manager, or joint among them all. In the latter case, they shall all be jointly and severally bound to pay compensation unless a group of them objected to the resolution passed notwithstanding their opposition and their objection was recorded in the minutes.

The final apportionment of liability among those liable shall be in accordance with the share of each of them in the fault committed.

The action for liability, whether brought by a shareholder or by a third party, shall lapse upon the expiry of five years from the date of the holding of the general assembly at which the members rendered an account of their management.

The constituent assembly, and thereafter the subsequent ordinary assemblies, shall appoint one or more supervisory commissioners, and they may remain in their office for one year only; however, their appointment may be renewed for a period of five consecutive years at most.

The right to convene ordinary and extraordinary assemblies vests primarily in the members of the board of directors. As for the constituent assembly, the right to convene it vests in the founders.

The supervisory commissioners may act in the stead of the members of the board of directors in the cases set forth above.

Shareholders who are unable to attend the assembly may appoint proxies to represent them, provided that such representatives are themselves shareholders, unless the articles of association provide that such representatives may be non-shareholders, with the exception of the legal representatives of incapacitated persons.

The company's articles of association may, within the framework of calculating the majority and the quorum at meetings of the general assembly of shareholders, provide for the possibility of considering shareholders who participate in the meetings of the assembly via remote audio-visual communication technology, or other technical means the conditions of which are determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Justice, as present at the meeting, provided that the verification of the identity of the connecting member is ensured and the security, continuity and reliability of the communication and the effective participation of the connecting member in the discussions are guaranteed, and provided that the company's articles of association set out the mechanism to be adopted in this regard.

The content of the remote communication in all sessions of the general assembly must be recorded, such that the recordings shall be deemed an integral part of the minutes of the assembly and shall be preserved therewith.

An attendance sheet shall be drawn up stating the names of the shareholders who are present, represented, and participating by means of remote communication, where applicable, the number of shares owned by each of them, and the number of votes attached to those shares.

This sheet shall be deposited at the company's registered office and may be inspected by any applicant who proves that he is a shareholder.

A bureau composed of at least a chairman and a secretary shall be established.

The members of the bureau must be present in person.
The assembly may not deliberate on matters other than those listed on the agenda, with the exception of unforeseen and urgent matters that arise during the meeting.
Every shareholder, whatever the class of shares he owns, is entitled to take part in the voting, even if he holds only a provisional certificate.

Subject to the special provisions governing registered shares provided for in Article 117, every shareholder shall have a number of votes equal to the shares he owns or represents, without limitation, unless the company's articles of association expressly provide for a limitation, in which case the limitation must be uniform for all shares whatever their class.

A shareholder may not vote on his own behalf or on behalf of a person whom he represents when the matter relates to a benefit intended to be granted to him or to an existing dispute between him and the company if the meeting adopts a resolution regarding this dispute.
The representatives of bondholders who attend the meeting do not have the right to vote in the deliberations.

If a single shareholder requests a secret ballot, such ballot shall become compulsory in all matters of a personal nature, such as the dismissal of members of the board of directors, for example, or holding them liable.

If the shareholders present find that their information on the matters submitted to them for deliberation is insufficient, the meeting shall be adjourned for eight days at least and fifteen days at most, provided that one-quarter of the members of the meeting request such adjournment.
The members of the bureau must draw up the minutes of the sitting and affix their signatures thereto.

Resolutions that are adopted in accordance with the rules, and in which the conditions of the legal quorum and the majority specific to each general meeting are observed, and in which no fraud or abuse of power occurs, shall bind all shareholders, even those who are absent and those who dissent.

The deliberations of the constituent meeting shall not be valid unless the number of shareholders of which it is composed represents at least two-thirds of the company's capital.

If this quorum is not attained, a new meeting may be held pursuant to a notice published in the Official Gazette, in an economic newspaper, and in a local daily newspaper twice, with one week between one publication and the other.

The notice shall state the agenda of the previous meeting and the results to which it led, and the deliberations of this second meeting shall be valid if the number of shareholders of which it is composed represents at least half of the company's capital.

If this quorum is not attained for it, a third meeting may be held, and it shall only be required at that time to represent at least one-third of the company's capital.

As regards the verification of contributions in kind, the quorum must be calculated on the basis of the number of shares subscribed for or owned by the shareholders, disregarding the shareholders in kind.

With respect to all other permitted amendments, the legal quorum at the three consecutive meetings convened in the manner of the constituent meeting shall represent two-thirds of the capital at the first meeting, half thereof at the second, and one-third thereof at the third.
Resolutions in extraordinary general meetings shall be passed by a two-thirds majority of the votes of the shares of the shareholders present, represented and participating remotely.

The capital of the company may not be increased except after the full payment of the value of the previous capital in accordance with Article 119 of this Law, under pain of nullity of the capital increase.

Where there is a usufructuary and a bare owner of the same share, the bare owner shall have the right to subscribe to the increase of the company's capital, unless the usufructuary and the bare owner have agreed otherwise prior to the resolution to increase the company's capital and have notified their agreement to the company in accordance with the provisions of Article 116 of this Law.

The legal rules relating to the incorporation of joint-stock companies must be observed in respect of the newly issued shares. The same penalties relating to the annulment of the capital increase, to fines, and to the liability of the chairman and members of the board of directors, the general manager or general managers then in office, the shareholders whose contributions were not duly approved, the auditors and the experts shall apply.

If persons other than the existing shareholders subscribe to the new shares notwithstanding the preemptive right granted to the latter, and the company owns a reserve fund, the said shares shall be issued at a price higher than their nominal value, and the excess price shall represent participation in the reserve fund.

A reduction of the capital may not be resolved upon except subject to the reservation of the rights of third parties.

Accordingly, the resolution of the general meeting providing for the reduction may not be executed unless it has been published in the Official Gazette and the creditors have not objected thereto within a period of three months.

If an objection is made, the reduction of the capital shall be postponed until the court decides whether or not such reduction prejudices the rights of third parties.

The members of the board of directors shall be liable for every unlawful reduction of the capital effected by the company purchasing its own shares and paying their price out of funds taken from the capital or from the statutory reserve.

In the assemblies provided for in Articles 193 and 194, resolutions shall be passed by a two-thirds majority of the votes of the shareholders present or represented. Owners of contributions in kind shall not participate in the passing of resolutions in respect of the verification of such contributions.

The ordinary assembly shall be held each year after the end of the financial year to rule on the accounts of the members of the board of directors, distribute dividend shares, appoint new surveillance commissioners, and appoint members of the board of directors upon the expiration of their mandate.

It may also be held during the financial year upon the occurrence of unforeseen circumstances, provided that its purpose is not the amendment of the company's articles of association.

All shareholders and bondholders shall have the right to inspect, at the company's head office or through a special electronic means approved by the company:

- The documents provided for in items 1 to 5 of Article 101 of this Law.

- The list of shareholders.

Interested parties may take or request, at their own expense, copies of all the aforementioned documents.

The company shall not be entitled to charge, in exchange for the delivery of such copies, anything other than the fees fixed by a tariff determined by the Minister of National Economy.

The ordinary general assembly must be composed of shareholders representing at least one-third of the company's capital.

If this quorum is not met, a second assembly shall be held, and its deliberations shall be valid whatever the portion of the company's capital it represents.

In all cases for which no provision to the contrary has been made, resolutions in ordinary general assemblies shall be passed by an absolute majority of the number of votes of the shares of the shareholders present, represented, or participating remotely, of whom the assembly is duly composed.
Extraordinary assemblies shall deliberate on the amendments intended to be introduced into the company's articles of association.

Subject to the provisions of Article 80 and the following rules, extraordinary assemblies may amend the articles of association in all of their provisions, provided that they do not change the nationality of the company, increase the obligations of the shareholders, or prejudice the rights of third parties.
With respect to resolutions providing for a change in the company's object or form, the legal quorum must always represent at least three-quarters of the company's capital.

Pursuant to the legal rules relating to the formal requirements that must be observed in the deliberations of general meetings, every resolution violating such requirements shall be null and void whenever it is proved that such violation actually vitiated the resulting outcome.

Every person having standing and interest shall be entitled to plead such annulment before the competent authority.

The effect of nullity shall lapse by the rectification of the deliberations or by the expiry of one year starting from the day on which the meeting was held with respect to the shareholders, and from the publication of the resolution in the Commercial Register with respect to non-shareholders.

Those who fraudulently fabricate or attempt to fabricate a false majority in a general meeting of shareholders or of bondholders, and in particular those who present themselves in the capacity of holders of securities that are the property of persons who cannot vote, or who induce others to promise them special benefits in order to vote in a certain manner or to abstain from voting, or who use a proxy purchased for money or any unlawful means, shall be liable to the penalties for fraud, without prejudice to the payment of damages.

Accomplices shall be punished with the same penalties.

Joint-stock companies shall be dissolved upon the expiry of the term fixed for them, or upon the completion of the undertaking for which they were formed, or upon the impossibility of completing it.

They shall also be dissolved by the will of the partners expressed in a general meeting under the conditions set forth in Articles 202 and 204, and they shall likewise be dissolved in all the special cases provided for in the articles of association.

If the company loses three-quarters of the capital, the members of the board of directors must convene an extraordinary general meeting to decide whether the situation requires the dissolution of the company before its term, the reduction of the capital, or the taking of other appropriate measures.

In any event, if the members of the board of directors neglect to convene the meeting, or if it cannot be constituted due to the lack of a legal quorum, or if the meeting refuses to dissolve the company, every shareholder shall retain the right to have recourse to the competent court to take the appropriate measure or to dissolve the company.
The resolution adopted must be published, whatever that resolution may be.
Liquidation shall in principle be carried out in accordance with the rules provided for general partnerships.

If the liquidators are not appointed in the company's articles of association, they shall be appointed by a vote of the ordinary general meeting, unless the intention is to dissolve the company before the expiry of its term, in which case the extraordinary general meeting shall appoint them at the same time.

If the general meeting does not appoint the liquidators, the matter of their appointment shall then revert to the competent court upon the request of any interested party.
The auditors, to whom the expert appointed by the court is joined, shall remain in office and shall thereupon supervise the liquidation.

The liquidators shall receive the accounts of the administrative acts performed by the members of the board of directors and the general manager from the approval by the general assembly of the last balance sheet until the opening of the liquidation, and they shall either approve them or submit to the competent court the difficulties that appear to them.
If the duration of the liquidation exceeds one year, the liquidators must draw up the annual balance sheet and publish it.

After the completion of the liquidation operations, the liquidators shall draw up the final balance sheet in which they determine the share of each shareholder in the distribution of the assets of the company.

The auditors shall draw up a report on the accounts submitted by the liquidators; thereafter, the ordinary general assembly shall approve them and decide to discharge the liquidators, or it shall object to the accounts, in which case the dispute shall be referred to the competent court.

A Title Nine shall be added to Book Two of the Code of Commerce as follows:

Articles 210 to 213 of the Code of Commerce are repealed and replaced by the following Title Nine:

Title Nine: On the Merger and Demerger of Companies

Chapter One: General Provisions

Article 210:

The merger of companies is effected by the transfer of the patrimony of one or more companies to an existing company or to a new company created for this purpose.

The demerger of companies is effected by a company transferring its patrimony to several existing or newly created companies.

Companies in liquidation may participate in merger and demerger operations, provided that the implementation of the stage of partitioning the assets among the partners has not begun.

A dissolved company means the company that loses its existence as a result of the merger or demerger.

A beneficiary company means the company to which all, some, or the net assets are transferred as a result of the merger or demerger.

The board of directors may be expanded to include a maximum of twenty members in the event of a merger operation.

These operations shall take place between different types of companies and within the conditions prescribed for amending the articles of association in each of them.

If this entails the creation of a new company or companies, their creation shall be subject to the rules of incorporation of each of them as determined by law.

Chapter Two

Additional Provisions Specific to Joint-Stock Companies

Article 213 bis 3:

The resolution of merger shall be issued by the extraordinary general assembly of each of the companies participating in that operation, on the basis of a written report placed by the board of directors at the disposal of the shareholders, accompanied by the unified and special reports mentioned in Article 213 bis 4

Article 213 bis 4:

The auditors in the companies concerned must draw up a unified report on the merger operation, the valuation of the shares, and the exchange ratio.

The report must also show that the value of the net assets pertaining to the dissolved company is not less than the value of the increase occurring in the capital of the beneficiary company.

The judge supervising the Commercial Register shall appoint one or more special auditors to examine the report mentioned in the preceding paragraph and to submit their observations within a maximum period of three months from the date of being notified of the mission, provided that the report of the auditor appointed by the judge is reasoned.

The unified and special reports shall be placed at the disposal of the shareholders at the head office of each company concerned at least one month prior to the date of the holding of the general assembly before which the adoption of the merger resolution is submitted.

The competent general assemblies in the companies concerned have the final decision in the merger operation.

Each of the unified report and the special report shall be deposited with the secretariat of the Commercial Register.

Article 213 bis 5:

Every merger operation carried out between two companies shall be exempted from the unified and special reports if one of them owns the entirety of the shares of the other between the date of depositing the draft merger with the secretariat of the Commercial Register and the date of the holding of the extraordinary general assembly of the absorbing company.

Article 213 bis 6:

If the merger operation is completed by way of creating a new company, this company may be incorporated with the contributions of the merging companies to the exclusion of any other contributions.

In all cases, the approval of the draft articles of association of the new company shall be effected by the extraordinary general assembly in each of the merging companies, and it shall not be required to obtain the approval of the general assembly of the new company.

- The merger draft shall be submitted to the general assembly of the holders of debt securities in the ceasing companies, which may approve it, whereupon such securities shall be established as liabilities of the merging company. However, its rejection thereof shall not prevent the continuation of the merger operation, which shall then have no effect against those creditors, who shall recover what is owed to them from the assets of the ceasing company without the participation of the creditors of the beneficiary company. This assembly shall also have the right to authorise its representative or representatives to file an objection in accordance with the provisions of Article 213 bis 9 of this Law.

- The submission of the merger set out in the preceding paragraph shall not be mandatory if the repayment of the debt is offered to the holders of debt securities upon their request. In this case, the merging company shall become the debtor for what is owed to them by the ceasing company.

- The offer to repay the debt shall be made by publishing it in the Official Gazette and in a local newspaper and/or by the electronic means referred to in the new Article 101 of this Law, and if the holder of the debt security does not request the repayment of his debt within a period of one month from the date of the last publication operation, he shall remain vested with this capacity in the merging company under the conditions specified in the merger contract.
The merging company shall remain the debtor to the creditors of the merged company other than the holders of debt securities and shall replace it in these debts without novation of the obligation.

The creditors of the companies participating in the merger operation, other than the holders of debt securities, shall have the right to file an objection before the competent Chamber of First Instance against this draft within one month from the date of the last publication operation carried out in accordance with the provisions of Article 213 bis 7 above.

It shall be for this court to dismiss their objection, or order the repayment of their debts, or approve the guarantees offered by the merging company if it finds them sufficient, or impose additional guarantees.

In all cases, the objection shall not prevent the continuation of the merger operation; however, if the debts are not repaid or the prescribed guarantees are not provided, the merger shall have no effect against the objecting creditor.

.

The merger draft shall not be submitted to the assembly of the holders of debt securities in the merging company. However, this assembly may authorise its representative or its equivalents to file an objection against the merger in accordance with the forms and conditions specified in the preceding Article 213 bis 9.
The provisions of Articles 213 bis 7 and 213 bis 8 above shall apply upon demerger.

Merger or division shall result in the dissolution of the disappearing companies without their liquidation and in the transfer of their patrimony to the beneficiary companies in the state in which it stands upon the final completion of the operation, including the lease right.

The partners in the disappearing companies shall acquire the status of partners in the beneficiary companies under the conditions specified in the merger or division agreement, and the old shares and partnership interests shall be exchanged for shares or partnership interests in the beneficiary companies. Those partners may receive a cash payment provided that its rate does not exceed 10% of the nominal value of the partnership interests or shares granted to them.

Such exchange shall not take place if the partnership interests or shares are owned by the beneficiary company or the disappearing company, provided that their value is accounted for when determining the value of the shares or partnership interests in the companies concerned.

The merger or division shall take effect:

1- From the date of registration of the new company in the Commercial Register, and where there are several companies, from the date of the last registration.

2- In other cases, from the date of registration of the minutes of the last general assembly that approved the operation, unless the agreement provides for another date.

Where another date is agreed upon, it must not be subsequent to the closing date of the accounts of the current financial year of the beneficiary company or companies, nor prior to the closing date of the last accounts of the financial year of the disappearing company or companies.
If the merger or division would increase the obligations of the partners or shareholders in the companies concerned, it may only be decided by the unanimous consent of the partners or shareholders.

For Article 213 bis 2:

The companies participating in any of the operations provided for in the first article of the draft merger or division shall draw it up and deposit it with the secretariat of the Commercial Register at their head office, and it shall be registered in their register, and an abstract thereof shall be published at their expense in the Official Gazette and in a local newspaper and/or by the electronic means referred to in Article 101 of this Law within one month from the date of approval by the extraordinary general assembly.

The draft merger or division shall include a statement of the following:

1- The name, form and head office of the contracting company or companies.

2- The purpose and conditions of the merger or division.

3- The determination of the value of the assets and liabilities.

4- The closing date of the accounts of the companies concerned.

5- The amount of the exchange ratio and the cash payment, if any.

6- The amount of the merger or division premium.

When the carrying out of the split-up is based on contributions to newly created joint-stock companies, each of these newly created companies may be incorporated solely with the contributions belonging to the split-up company.

In such a case, and if the shares in the newly created companies are allocated to the shareholders of the split-up company in the same proportion as their rights in the capital of the latter, the two reports mentioned in Article 213 bis 4 above shall not be drawn up.

In all events, the draft articles of association of the new companies shall be approved by the extraordinary general meeting of the split-up company without the need to obtain the approval of the general meetings of any of the new companies.

The provisions of Article 213 bis 11 shall apply to the debenture holders in the split-up companies, and they shall have the same rights belonging to the debenture holders in the dissolved companies, subject to the text of Article 213 bis 19.

The draft split-up shall not be submitted to the meeting of debenture holders in the beneficiary companies; however, this meeting shall be entitled to authorise representatives on its behalf to lodge an objection to the split-up operation in accordance with the provisions and conditions of Article 213 bis 13 above.

The companies benefiting from the contributions resulting from the split-up shall be deemed jointly and severally liable towards the debenture holders and all other creditors of the split-up company.

The beneficiary companies shall take the place of the split-up companies in respect of those debts without such substitution resulting in a novation of the obligation with regard to the debenture holders or the creditors.

A company that contributes a part of its assets to another company may agree with the beneficiary company to subject this operation to the provisions provided for in Articles 213 bis 15 to 213 bis 19.

Chapter Three

Special Provisions Governing Limited Liability Companies

Article 213 bis 17:

The provisions of Articles 213 bis 8, 9, 12, 13, and 19 shall apply to the merger or split-up of limited liability companies for the benefit of companies of the same type.

If the transaction is carried out through contributions in kind to existing limited liability companies, the general provisions relating to and contributions in kind in limited liability companies shall also apply.

Where the merger transaction is carried out through contributions to a new limited liability company, the latter may be formed solely with the contributions of the merged company or companies.

Where the split-up transaction is carried out through contributions to new limited liability companies, the latter may be formed solely with the contributions of the split company. In such a case, and if the shares in each of the new companies are allocated to the partners in the split company in the same proportion as their rights in the capital of this latter company, the two reports provided for in Article 213 bis 4 above shall not be drawn up.

In the two cases mentioned in the two items above, the partners in the dissolved companies may act ipso jure as founders of the new companies in accordance with the provisions in force in limited liability companies.

Article 213 bis 18:

A company that contributes a part of its assets to another company may, in agreement with it, subject that transaction to the provisions governing split-up through contributions to existing limited liability companies.

Chapter Four Miscellaneous Provisions:

Article 213 bis 19:

Where the transactions mentioned in Article One are carried out jointly between joint-stock companies and limited liability companies, the provisions of Articles 213 bis 8, 9, 12, 13, 19, and 21 shall apply in particular.

Article 213 bis 20:

All procedures and formalities required by the merger and split-up transactions mentioned in this Law shall be exempt from the fiscal stamp duty.

Article 213 bis 21:

All procedures and formalities required by the merger transaction carried out between companies shall be exempt from all stamp, conveyance, transfer, notary public, and registration duties before the various official authorities.

Article 213 bis 22:

Merged companies must pay the taxes issued prior to the date of the merger, and all the provisions contained in the Tax Procedures Law regarding liability for the payment of taxes issued subsequently shall be observed. However, these companies shall be exempt from the obligation to submit a clearance certificate from the National Social Security Fund.

(Legislative Decree No. 304 issued on 24 December 1942 and its amendments)

The number of supervisory commissioners must be at least three, including the accounting expert appointed by the President of the Court pursuant to a decision. They may not be chosen from among the managing partners.

They shall meet as a council whenever the supervision and investigations that they must carry out require their meeting.

As for the term of office of the supervisory council, it shall be determined in the articles of association of the company, provided that the first council is appointed for a term of one year only.

All resolutions of the general assemblies, except resolutions relating to the ratification of administrative acts - implicitly entail the personal consent of the managing partners in accordance with the rules determined in the articles of association of the company.

Every company may include in its articles of association a provision stating that its capital is variable, in which case it shall be subject to the provisions of the following articles in addition to the general rules pertaining to it according to its specific form.

Such provision must be published.

When the company is of variable capital, its capital may be increased either by admitting new partners therein or by new sums paid by the partners, and it may also be reduced by the partners recovering all or part of what they have contributed therein.

The increase and reduction of the capital shall take place with complete freedom and shall be exempted from the formality of publication unless the articles of association of the company provide to the contrary.
Article 240 of the Code of Commerce has been repealed.

The articles of association of the company shall determine a sum below which the capital may not be reduced by the recovery of what some partners have contributed or by the withdrawal of some of them.

Such sum may not be less than one-fifth of the capital of the company, and this provision of the articles of association of the company shall be subject to the formality of publication.

A provision may be included in the articles of association of the company stipulating that the general assembly is entitled to resolve, by the majority determined for amending the articles of association of the company, to exclude one or several partners therefrom without depriving them of their vested rights in the reserve fund pertaining to it.

The partner who withdraws from the company, either by his mere will or pursuant to a resolution of the general assembly, shall remain for a period of three years liable towards the partners and towards third parties for all the obligations that existed at the time of his withdrawal.

A limited partnership shall be announced to the Republic under a business name that comprises only the names of the general partners. Where there is only one general partner, the words "and partners" may be added to his name.

Where a limited partner permits the inclusion of his name in the name of the partnership, he shall become like a general partner towards every third party in good faith.

The general partners, whether all of them manage the business of the partnership or one or several of them manage it on behalf of all, shall be subject to the same legal regime to which the members of a general partnership are subject.

A limited partner may not interfere in the management of the business of the partnership towards third parties, even if his interference is based on a power of attorney.

Where he contravenes the provision of this prohibition, he shall become jointly and severally and unlimitedly liable with the general members for the obligations arising from his act of management, and the liability cast upon him shall either be confined to the consequences resulting from the acts in which he interfered or extend to all the debts of the partnership in proportion to the number and gravity of those acts.

However, the supervision of the acts of the business managers, the opinions and advice tendered to them, and the authorisation given to them to perform acts exceeding the limits of their authority shall all not be deemed acts of interference.
A simple limited partnership shall be subject to the rules laid down for the formation and dissolution of general partnerships, even in respect of the limited partners.

As for partnerships limited by shares, their capital shall be divided into shares, and a limited partner therein shall be subject to the legal regime to which a shareholder in joint-stock companies is subject.
Partnerships limited by shares, whatever their object may be, shall be subject to commercial law and custom.
The legal rules pertaining to joint-stock companies shall apply to the formation and operation of partnerships limited by shares.
All the obligations imposed by law upon the members of the board of directors in a joint-stock company shall apply to the business managers of a partnership limited by shares.

Article 213 bis 23:

Merged companies and merging companies shall be subject to the tax provided for in Article 45 of the Income Tax Law at a reduced rate of 5% on the revaluation differences of the fixed assets of any of them.

Profits from the assignment of any of the fixed assets that were previously revalued to complete the merger operation shall be subject to the tax provided for in Article 45 of the Income Tax Law without reduction, in the event that the assignment takes place within two years from the date of completion of the merger operation.

Article 213 bis 24:

All procedures and transactions required for the operation of splitting a company into two or more newly established companies shall be exempted from all stamp, transfer, devolution, notary public, and registration fees before the various official authorities, and such fees shall remain due if the split takes place in favour of an existing company or companies.

Article 213 bis 25:

The split company must pay the taxes issued prior to the date of the split, and all provisions contained in the Tax Procedures Law shall be observed with regard to liability for paying taxes issued subsequently. Provided that such companies shall be exempted from the obligation to submit a clearance certificate from the National Social Security Fund.
