Article 213 bis 26:

Split companies shall be subject to the tax provided for in Article 45 of the Income Tax Law at a reduced rate of 5% on the revaluation differences of their fixed assets in the event that the split takes place into two or more newly established companies.

If, however, the split takes place into two or more existing companies, the revaluation differences shall be subject to the ordinary tax.

If, however, the split takes place into existing and newly established companies, the split into the existing company shall be subject to the tax rate provided for in Article 45 of the Income Tax Law

A limited partnership that carries out its business under a trade name comprises two categories of partners:

The first is the category of general partners, who alone have the right to carry out its management acts and who are personally and jointly and severally liable for the payment of the company's debts.

The second is the category of limited partners, who contribute capital and each of whom is liable only to the extent of his contribution.

Limited partnerships are of two types:

- A simple limited partnership,

- And a partnership limited by shares.

If the company takes the form of a joint-stock company, its shares must remain registered even after the full payment of their price. The articles of association of the company may grant the general assembly or the board of directors the right to object to the transfer of such shares. However, it is stipulated that this right shall not be abused.

Whatever the form of the company, it shall not be dissolved by the withdrawal of one of the partners, or his bankruptcy, insolvency, loss of general capacity, or death, but shall remain in existence by operation of law among the remaining partners.
This law shall apply to agricultural cooperative companies unless the provisions of their special law are contrary thereto.
Joint ventures are distinguished from other commercial companies in that their existence is confined to the contracting parties and that they are not intended to be disclosed to third parties.

The agreements concluded between the concerned parties shall determine with complete freedom the mutual rights and obligations between the partners and the sharing of profits and losses among them, subject to the application of the general principles relating to the company contract.
The existence of the aforementioned agreements may be proven by all means of evidence admissible in commercial matters.
Joint ventures shall not be subject to the publication formalities imposed on other commercial companies.
A joint venture shall not be considered a legal person.

Third parties shall have no legal relationship except with the partner with whom they contracted.

However, a joint venture that makes itself known to third parties in this capacity may be treated in relation to them as a de facto company.
The company may not issue assignable or negotiable shares or securities in favour of the partners.

An Eighth Title is added to the Second Book of the Code of Commerce as follows:

Of Certain Financial Offences

Article 253 bis 1:

Shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to three years and by a fine ranging from twenty-five to one hundred times the official minimum wage, or by either of these two penalties, the chairman and members of the board of directors, the managers and the authorised signatories who, in bad faith, cause harm to the company:

a- By using the company's funds or its credit facilities in a manner harmful to its interests for personal ends.

b- By acting in the interest of another company, enterprise or individual with whom any of them has a direct or indirect interest.

Shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to three years and by a fine ranging from twenty-five to fifty times the official minimum wage, or by either of these two penalties, the chairman and members of the board of directors, the managers and the authorised signatories who intentionally, with the aim of concealing the true position of the company, draw up and publish untruthful financial statements.

Shall be punished by the same penalty the auditors who intentionally conceal these contraventions in their reports.

Article 253 bis 3:

The three-year limitation period for prosecution of the offences provided for in the two preceding articles shall run from the date of their commission if they are apparent and from the date of their discovery if they were concealed.

Proof of commercial contracts is not, in principle, subject to the restrictive rules established for civil contracts; the said contracts may therefore, subject to the exceptions resulting from special legal provisions, be proved by all means of proof which the judge deems ought to be admitted according to custom or circumstance.

In commercial matters, the date of private writings may be proved against third parties by all means of proof.

The date of negotiable instruments and the date of their endorsement shall be deemed true until the contrary is proved.
Co-debtors under a commercial obligation shall be deemed jointly and severally liable in such obligation, and this presumption shall apply to the sureties of a commercial debt.
The legal rate of interest in commercial matters is fixed at nine per cent.
Proof of the fair price and the current price shall be based on stock exchange prices and official price lists, unless otherwise agreed.

No commercial obligation intended for the performance of work or of a service shall be deemed to have been contracted gratuitously. Where the parties have not fixed a remuneration, commission or brokerage fee, the remuneration customary in the profession shall be due.

In commercial matters, the court shall not be entitled to grant time limits for payment save in exceptional circumstances.

A party who has petitioned the court for the annulment of the contract shall not be entitled to demand performance thereafter.

A party who has submitted a demand for performance shall, however, be entitled to substitute therefor a demand for annulment.

Performance of obligations after the institution of an action for annulment shall not be admissible.

Non-performance of one of the obligations in contracts involving successive obligations shall entitle the party who has fulfilled his own obligation to demand the rescission of the contract in respect of all obligations that have not been performed.

This shall not preclude his right to claim damages.

In commercial matters, the right to institute actions shall lapse upon the expiry of ten years where no shorter period is prescribed.

Where a decision containing a judgment has been rendered, the action arising from res judicata shall in all cases lapse upon the expiry of ten years.

Sale, loan, the contract of carriage, the contract of insurance, and all contracts the rules of which are not determined pursuant to this Law shall be subject to the Code of Obligations and to custom.

The special rules relating to public transport undertakings shall also apply to the contract of carriage.

Stock exchange transactions, whether relating to securities or to goods, shall be subject to the rules governing the various types of contracts whose form they borrow or into which they resolve, and to the special regulations of commercial exchanges.

Contracts relating to maritime commerce shall, however, be subject to special rules provided for by the Code of Maritime Commerce.
A commercial pledge subject to the rules set forth hereinafter is that by virtue of which a commercial debt is secured.

Save for the following restrictions, a pledge shall be proved by all means of proof which the court deems must be admitted. The pledge of a registered instrument shall be established by a transfer by way of security recorded in the registers of the establishment which issued the instrument and on the instrument itself.

As for an instrument to order, a pledge thereon shall be established by an endorsement in which is inserted the phrase "value placed as security" or another phrase to the same effect.

As for ordinary debts owed to a designated person, the establishment of a pledge thereon shall require in all cases a written deed of a certain date notified to the debtor upon whose debt the pledge was established.

A contract of pledge shall produce no effect as a pledge if the pledged property remains in the possession of the debtor such that it appears in the estimation of third parties as though it were still part of his unencumbered estate enabling him to obtain new credit for borrowing; rather, the pledged property must be delivered to the creditor and remain in his possession or in the possession of a third party who holds it for his account.

It shall suffice, for the transfer of possession to be deemed complete, that the keys of the premises containing the pledged goods or things be delivered while locked, provided that such premises do not bear a sign in the name of the debtor, or that an instrument representing those things in conformity with commercial usage be delivered.
The pledgee creditor must deliver to the debtor, upon request, a receipt specifying the nature, kind, quantity, weight, and all distinguishing marks of the things delivered in pledge.

If the pledge is established over fungible things or instruments, the contract of pledge shall remain in force even if those things or instruments are replaced by things or instruments of the same kind. If those things or instruments are non-fungible, the debtor shall also be entitled to recover them and replace them with the consent of the creditor, provided that the original contract of pledge stipulated such right.

The creditor must exercise for the account of the debtor all the rights inherent in the things or instruments delivered to him by way of pledge.

If what he has received consists of financial credit instruments conferring a right of option, the debtor who wishes to exercise his right of option must pay to the creditor the necessary funds at least two days before the expiry of the time limit fixed for the option.

If the object placed as security consists of instruments the price of which has not been paid in full, the debtor, if called upon to pay, must pay the funds to the creditor at least two days before maturity, failing which the pledgee creditor may proceed with the sale of the instruments.

In the event of non-payment at maturity, the creditor is entitled - after the expiry of eight days following a simple notification sent by him to the debtor and to the third party who provided the pledged property, if any - to apply to the President of the Execution Department, who shall attend to the sale of the pledged objects by public auction, and the creditor shall recover his debt out of the price by way of priority.

Any clause in the pledge contract authorising the creditor to appropriate the pledged property or to dispose thereof without the formalities set forth above shall be deemed null and void.

A mandate is commercial when it relates to commercial transactions.

In particular, this contract is called a commission contract and is subject to the provisions of the following Chapter when the agent must act in his own name or under a trade name for the account of the person who appointed him.

When the agent must act in the name of his principal, his rights and obligations shall be subject to the provisions of Book Eight of Part Two of the Code of Obligations.

In commercial matters, the agent is entitled to remuneration in all cases, unless there is a provision to the contrary.

If this remuneration is not fixed pursuant to an agreement, it shall be determined according to the tariff of the profession or according to custom or the circumstances.
A commercial mandate, even if it contains an absolute authorisation, does not authorise non-commercial acts except pursuant to an express provision.
An agent who has received instructions in respect of only part of the business shall be deemed to have a free hand in respect of the remaining part.
The agent must pay interest on funds belonging to the principal as from the day on which he was bound to deliver or deposit them in accordance with the order of the principal.

When the contract comprises at the same time the attributes of a mandate and the essential elements of a contract of employment, as usually occurs in contracts concluded between a merchant and his attached agents, the local representative, the travelling representative, the accredited agent, and the manager of a branch or agency, the rules of the contract of employment shall apply with respect to the relations of the merchant with his agent, and the rules of the mandate shall apply with respect to third parties.

Commercial representatives shall be deemed at times as employees and at times as ordinary agents, according to what the contract indicates as to their subordination or independence in the work. However, they are entitled in every case upon termination of the contract, even if such termination is due to a non-abusive cause, to benefit from the period of prior notice established by custom, provided that commercial representation is their sole profession.

If the commercial representative is an agent for several commercial houses and has offices, a staff of employees, management, and general expenses whereby it is permissible to consider him the owner of a genuine enterprise for commercial representation, he himself becomes a merchant.

A commission agent is one who undertakes to conclude in his own name, but for the account of his principal, a sale, purchase, and other commercial operations in return for a commission or a financial fee.

The rules of mandate shall apply to the contract of commission agency, subject to the provisions set forth in this Chapter.

A commission agent who contracts in his own name shall acquire the rights resulting from the contract and shall be directly bound towards the persons with whom he contracted as though the business pertained to him personally, and those persons shall be entitled to raise against him all defences resulting from their personal relationship with him and shall not be entitled to sue the principal directly.

As for the relations of the principal with the commission agent or with his creditor, the rules of mandate shall apply thereto.

The commission agent must personally carry out the orders given to him unless he is authorised by agreement or by custom to substitute a third party for himself or there are circumstances harming him into making such substitution. In such cases, the principal shall be entitled to sue directly the person whom the commission agent substituted for himself.
The commission agent shall not be entitled to set himself up as a counterparty against his principal except with his consent.
Where the commission agent grants credit or makes an advance to a third party without the consent of the principal, he shall bear the risks of his act.

Save in the case of advances made without authorisation, the commission agent shall not be liable for non-payment or for the non-performance of the other obligations incumbent upon those with whom he contracted unless he has commissioned them or the commercial custom in the place where he resides so requires.

A commission agent who guarantees the person with whom he contracts shall be entitled to receive a special commission called a del credere commission, which, failing agreement thereon, shall be determined in accordance with the custom of the locality in which the commission agent contracted.

Subject to the provisions of the preceding article, the commission shall fall due by the mere conclusion of the transaction even if the third party does not perform the obligations which he took upon himself, unless the non-performance thereof results from a fault committed by the commission agent.

The commission shall also fall due where the completion of the operation is prevented by a cause attributable to the principal.

As for operations the completion of which was prevented by other causes, the commission agent shall only be entitled, in return for his efforts, to claim the compensation imposed by the custom of the locality.
The commission shall be calculated on the gross value of the operation, including ancillary expenses, unless there is an agreement to the contrary.

The commission agent shall be entitled to recover all expenses, advances and disbursements which he has made for the benefit of the principal, together with the interest thereon.

He shall also be entitled to include in the account an indemnity in consideration of storage and transport expenses, but he may not claim remuneration for his employees.

Every commission agent shall have a lien on the value of the goods sent to him, stored or deposited, arising by the mere fact of their dispatch, storage or deposit, for the recovery of all loans, advances and payments which he has made, whether prior to his receipt of the goods or during the period in which they are in his possession.

Provided that this lien shall not arise unless the condition laid down in Article 266 of this Law is fulfilled.

The preferred debt of the commission agent shall include the principal amount together with interest, commissions and expenses.

If the goods have been sold and delivered for the account of the principal, the commission agent shall be entitled to recover from their price the amount of his debt in priority to the creditors of the principal.
A principal who revokes the commission or a commission agent who renounces it without legitimate cause shall be liable to pay damages.

A forwarding commission agent who undertakes to dispatch or reship goods for the account of his principal in return for remuneration and in his own name shall be deemed to be a commission agent, but shall be subject, with respect to the transport of the goods, to the provisions to which a carrier is subject.

Brokerage is a contract whereby one party, called the broker, undertakes to direct the other party to an opportunity to conclude an agreement or to act as an intermediary for him in the negotiations for contracting, in return for remuneration.

The rules of mandate shall apply generally to brokerage.

If the broker's remuneration is not fixed by agreement or by an official tariff, it shall be determined in accordance with custom, or the judge shall assess its value according to the circumstances. If it appears that the agreed remuneration is disproportionate to the nature of the transaction and the efforts which it requires, the judge shall be entitled to reduce it so that it becomes a fair remuneration for the service rendered.

The broker shall be entitled to the remuneration when the information which he has given or the negotiation which he has conducted leads to the conclusion of the agreement. If the agreement is concluded subject to a suspensive condition, the remuneration shall not be due until the condition is fulfilled.

If the reimbursement of expenses incurred by the broker has been stipulated, they shall be due to him even if the agreement is not concluded.

The broker shall forfeit all right to remuneration and to the recovery of the expenses which he has incurred if he acts for the benefit of the contracting third party in breach of his obligations, or if he induces such third party to promise him any remuneration under circumstances contrary to the rules of good faith.
A broker shall not be entitled to act as an intermediary for persons who are notoriously insolvent or whose incapacity is known to him.

And he must record all transactions concluded through his intermediary with their provisions and special conditions, preserve all documents relating thereto, and give a certified true copy of all the foregoing to any of the contracting parties who requests it.

In sales concluded according to a sample, he must preserve the sample until the transaction is completed.
Intermediation and brokerage transactions in stock exchanges and in commodity exchanges shall be subject, insofar as necessary, to special legislation.

A current account is formed whenever two persons, whose circumstances require that they mutually deliver funds to one another, agree to convert their respective debts into simple debit and credit items forming a single account, such that the final balance alone, upon the closure of this account, becomes a debt that is due and ready for payment.

The scope of the current account depends on the will of the two parties; they may make it comprehensive of all their transactions or of a specific kind thereof only.

A current account may be overdrawn in respect of both parties or in respect of one party; in this latter case, one of the parties shall not be bound to advance funds to the other unless that party has sufficient provision. And in no event may this account settle on a positive balance in his favour.

The existence of a current account shall not preclude the right to obtain a commission and the reimbursement of expenses for transactions relating to the current account, and these shall be entered in the account unless there is an agreement to the contrary.

Payment by means of a commercial bill shall be deemed to have been made only on condition of collection of its value, unless there is an agreement to the contrary. If the value of the bill is not paid at its maturity date, its recipient shall be entitled, while retaining it by way of security and while exercising the rights attached thereto, to debit its value to the account of the party who delivered it. In the event of the bankruptcy of the party who delivered the bill, the recipient shall not be entitled, notwithstanding any agreement to the contrary, to debit it to the account except after the date of maturity has fallen due and non-payment has been established; and if bills are debited in this manner, their recipient must reduce the amount of his claims in the bankruptcy in proportion to the payments made by the signatories of those bills.
Remittances shall ipso jure bear interest in favour of the party delivering against the recipient, calculated at the statutory rate if it is not determined pursuant to the contract or custom.

Debts due to either of the two parties, if entered into the current account, shall lose their special characteristics and their independent existence, and shall not thereafter be separately capable of payment, set-off, legal action, any method of execution, or lapsing individually by prescription.

Personal or real securities attached to the debts entered into the current account shall be extinguished unless there is a contrary agreement between the two parties.

Neither of the two parties shall be deemed a creditor or a debtor of the other party prior to the closing of the current account; the stopping of this account alone determines the state of the legal relations between them, gives rise inevitably to the aggregate set-off of all items of the account of credit and debit, and designates the creditor and the debtor.

The account shall be stopped and liquidated at the maturity dates fixed pursuant to the contract or according to local custom, and otherwise at the end of every six months.

The remaining balance shall constitute a net debt due and payable, producing, as from the day of liquidation, interest at the rate fixed in the current account if this balance is carried over to a new account, and otherwise at the legal rate.

Actions relating to the rectification of the account on account of error, omission, duplication, or other rectifications must be brought within a period of six months.

The contract shall terminate at the time fixed pursuant to the agreement, and if no term is agreed upon, the contract shall be terminated according to the will of either of the two parties, and it shall also terminate by the death of either of them, by his loss of legal capacity, or by his bankruptcy.

A bank that receives by way of deposit a sum of money shall become the owner thereof and must return it in an equivalent value in a single payment or in several payments upon the first demand of the depositor or according to the conditions of time limits or prior notice fixed in the contract.

Proof of all operations relating to the deposit or to its return must be established by written documents.

Interest shall be due, where applicable, as from the day following each deposit, if it is not a holiday, up to the day preceding the return of each sum, unless there is a contrary agreement.

If what is deposited with the bank consists of financial securities, the ownership of such securities shall remain vested in the depositor unless it is proved that the intention is otherwise.

The existence of such intention shall be presumed if the depositor has granted the bank in writing, without restriction, the right to dispose of those securities or has acknowledged its right to return securities of the same kind.

The rules of mandate shall apply to bank deposits if the bank undertakes the management of the deposited financial securities in return for a commission.

Deposits placed in safe deposit boxes or in compartments thereof shall be governed by the rules relating to the hire of things.

The bank shall be liable for the safety of the leased boxes.

In contracts for the opening of a financial credit, the grantor of credit undertakes to place certain funds at the disposal of the accredited party, who shall be entitled to draw them in a single lump sum or in successive instalments according to his needs within a specified period.

Any amount paid or refunded by the accredited party during the term of the contract shall be added back to the sum placed at his disposal, unless there is an agreement to the contrary.

The grantor of credit may revoke the contract if the accredited party becomes insolvent or was already insolvent at the time of contracting without the knowledge of the grantor of credit.

If a significant diminution occurs in the real or personal securities furnished by the accredited party, the grantor of credit shall be entitled to demand additional security, or to reduce the amount of the credit, or to close it, as the case may require.

Where the security furnished consists of a real property mortgage, the registration of the mortgage effected at the time of the contract shall secure, as from its date, all advances subsequently made pursuant to the contract for the opening of credit.

Where a bank credit is allocated for payment in favour of a third party and the bank confirms such credit to the beneficiary thereof, it may no longer thereafter be revoked or modified without his consent, and the bank becomes directly and irrevocably bound towards him to accept the intended instruments and payments.

The bank shall be entitled to recover the sums it has paid and the expenses it has incurred in executing that with which it was entrusted, together with the agreed interest, or the legal interest in the absence of an agreement, running from the day of payment. It shall also be entitled to charge a commission.

Banking operations not mentioned in this Title shall be subject to the provisions of the Code of Obligations relating to the various contracts arising from the said operations or the contracts under the rules of which such operations fall.

On the creation and form of a bill of exchange:

A bill of exchange contains:

1) The mention of the word "suftaja" or "bill of exchange" in the body of the instrument itself, in the language employed in drawing up this instrument.

2) An unconditional mandate to pay a determinate sum of money.

3) The name of the person who is to pay (the drawee).

4) A statement of the date of maturity.

5) A statement of the place where payment is to be effected.

6) The name of the person to whom or to whose order payment is to be made.

7) A statement of the date and the place where the instrument is created.

8) The signature of the person who creates the instrument (the drawer).

An instrument in which any of the particulars set forth in the preceding Article is lacking shall not be deemed a bill of exchange except in the cases specified in the following paragraphs:

An instrument in which the date of maturity is not indicated shall be deemed payable at sight. In the absence of a special mention of the place of payment, the name of the place mentioned beside the name of the drawee shall be deemed to be the place of payment and, at the same time, the place of domicile of the drawee. A bill of exchange in which the place of its drawing is not mentioned shall be deemed to have been drawn at the place mentioned beside the name of the drawer.

A bill of exchange may be to the order of the drawer himself and it may be drawn on the drawer himself. It may also be drawn for the account of a third party.

It may be payable at the domicile of a third party, whether in the locality in which the drawee resides or in another locality.

In bills payable at sight or at a certain time after sight, the drawer may stipulate that interest shall be payable on the sum, provided that such stipulation shall be deemed null and void in any other bill of exchange.

The rate of interest must be specified in the bill, failing which such stipulation shall be deemed null and void.

Interest shall run from the date of the bill of exchange if no other date is specified.

A bill of exchange in which the sum is written both in words and in figures shall, in the event of a discrepancy between the two amounts, be valid for the sum written in words in full.

As for a bill whose value is written more than once, whether in words in full or in figures, it shall, in the event of a discrepancy between the values, be valid only for the lowest sum.

If a bill bears signatures of persons who are incapable of binding themselves by a bill of exchange, or forged signatures, or signatures of fictitious persons, or signatures which for any other reason cannot bind the persons who signed the bill of exchange or in whose name the bill was signed, the obligations of the other signatories on the bill shall nevertheless remain valid.

Whoever puts his signature on a bill of exchange as an agent for a person whom he had no authority to represent shall himself be bound under the said bill and, if he pays, shall have the same rights as the purported principal would have had.

The same rule shall apply to an agent who has exceeded his authority.

The drawer guarantees both acceptance and payment of the bill. He may release himself from guaranteeing acceptance, whereas every stipulation whereby he releases himself from guaranteeing payment shall be deemed null and void.

Cover shall be provided by the drawer or by the person for whose account the bill is drawn, without prejudice to the drawer for the account of a third party remaining personally liable towards the endorsers and the holder of the bill only.

Cover exists if, at the date of maturity of the bill, the drawee is indebted to the drawer or to the person payment the bill was drawn for his account for an amount at least equal to the value of the bill. Ownership of the cover is transferred by operation of law to the successive holders of the bill.

Acceptance of the bill implies the existence of cover, and such acceptance establishes it with respect to the endorsers. In the case of acceptance or non-acceptance, the drawer alone must, where the existence of cover is denied, prove that the drawee had cover at the date of maturity; failing which, he shall be bound to guarantee it even if the protest was drawn up after the expiry of the prescribed time limits.

Every bill of exchange, even if not expressly drawn "to order", may be transferred by means of endorsement.

Where the drawer has inserted the drawing the words "not to order" or an equivalent expression, the bill may only be transferred in the form and with the effects of an ordinary assignment. An endorsement may be made in favour of the drawee, whether he has accepted the bill or not, or in favour of the drawer, or in favour of any other party liable thereon, and such persons may endorse the bill anew.

An endorsement must be pure and simple. Any condition to which the endorsement is made subject shall be deemed unwritten. A partial endorsement is null and void.

An endorsement "to bearer" is equivalent to an endorsement in blank.

An endorsement must be written on the bill of exchange or on a slip affixed thereto (allonge) and must be signed by the endorser. The endorsement may leave the endorsee unspecified or may consist simply of the signature of the endorser (endorsement in blank).

In the latter case, the endorsement is only valid if it is written on the back of the bill of exchange or on the allonge.

An endorsement transfers all the rights arising out of a bill of exchange.

If the endorsement is in blank, the holder of the bill may:

First - Fill up the blank either with his own name or with the name of some other person.

Second - Endorse the bill again in blank or to some other person.

Third - Deliver the bill to a third person without filling up the blank and without endorsing it.

In the absence of any contrary agreement, the endorser guarantees acceptance and payment. He may prohibit any further endorsement; in which case, he shall not be bound by any guarantee towards the persons to whom the bill is subsequently endorsed.

The drawer may stipulate in any bill of exchange that it shall be presented for acceptance, with or without fixing a time limit. He may prohibit in the bill its presentment for acceptance, unless the bill is payable at the address of a third party or in a locality other than that in which the drawee resides, or is a bill drawn payable at a certain period after sight.

Every endorser of the bill may stipulate that it must be presented for acceptance, with or without fixing a time limit, unless the drawer has expressly prohibited its presentment for acceptance.

Bills drawn payable at a certain period after sight must be presented for acceptance within one year of their date. However, the drawer may fix a shorter or a longer period than this latter period.

Endorsers may abridge the aforementioned periods.

The drawee may demand that the bill be presented to him a second time on the day following the first presentment, and the interested parties may not invoke the failure to comply with this demand unless this demand is mentioned in the protest.

The holder of the bill is not obliged to surrender it to the drawee upon presenting it for acceptance.

An acceptance is written on the bill of exchange and is expressed by the word "accepted" or any other equivalent word, and it is signed by the drawee; his mere signature on the back of the bill constitutes an acceptance.

When the bill is payable at a certain period after sight, or when it must be presented for acceptance within a specified period pursuant to a special stipulation, the acceptance must be dated as of the day on which it was given, unless the holder of the bill requires that it be dated as of the day of presentment. In default of a date, the holder of the bill, in order to preserve his rights of recourse against the endorsers and against the drawer, may establish this omission by a protest drawn up within the legal time.

An acceptance is unconditional, without qualification, but the drawee may restrict it to part of the sum.

Every other modification introduced by the terms of the acceptance to the particulars of the bill of exchange constitutes a refusal. However, the acceptor is bound according to the tenor of his acceptance.

When the drawer has indicated in the bill a place of payment other than the place where the drawee resides, without naming a third party at whose address payment is to be effected, the drawee may name such third party upon his acceptance of the bill; in default of this indication upon acceptance, he is deemed to have undertaken to pay the bill himself at the place of payment.

If a bill is payable at the place of residence of the drawee, he may indicate in the terms of the acceptance an address in the same locality where payment is to be effected.

The possessor of a bill of exchange is deemed to be the lawful holder thereof if he establishes his title through an uninterrupted series of endorsements, even if the last endorsement is in blank. A struck-out endorsement is, in this respect, deemed null and void.

Where an endorsement in blank is followed by another endorsement, the signatory of this last endorsement is deemed to have acquired the bill by the endorsement in blank.

Where a person has been dispossessed of a bill of exchange by any event whatsoever, the holder who establishes his right in the manner set forth in the preceding paragraph is not bound to give up the bill unless he has acquired it in bad faith, or unless in acquiring it he has committed gross negligence.

Persons sued on a bill of exchange are not entitled to set up against the holder defences set forth on their personal relations with the drawer of the bill or with previous holders, unless the holder, in acquiring the bill, has intentionally acted to the detriment of the debtor.

Where an endorsement contains the statement "value for collection" "or for encashment" or "by procuration" or any other statement implying a simple mandate, the holder of the bill is entitled to exercise all the rights arising out of it, but he can only endorse it by way of procuration.

In this case, the parties liable may only set up against the holder of the bill defences which could be set up against the endorser.

The mandate contained in an endorsement by procuration does not terminate in effect by reason of the death of the principal or by his becoming legally incapable.

Where an endorsement contains the statement "value placed in security" or "value placed in pledge" or any other statement implying a security, the holder of the bill is entitled to exercise all the rights arising out of it, but if he endorses the bill, his endorsement is only deemed to be by way of procuration.

The parties liable may not set up against the holder of the bill defences founded on their personal relations with the endorser, unless the holder, in acquiring the bill, has intentionally acted to the detriment of the debtor.

An endorsement subsequent to maturity produces the same effects as an endorsement prior thereto; however, an endorsement subsequent to protest for non-payment, or an endorsement made after the expiration of the time-limit fixed for drawing up the protest, operates only with the effects of an ordinary assignment.

An undated endorsement is deemed to have been made before the expiration of the time-limit fixed for drawing up the protest, unless the contrary is proved.
It is not permissible to antedate orders, failing which such act shall be deemed a forgery.
Until the date of maturity, a bill of exchange may be presented for acceptance to the drawee at his place of residence, whether by the holder of the bill or by any possessor thereof.

The acceptance of the bill by the drawee binds him to make payment at maturity, and in default of payment, the holder of the bill, even if he is the drawer himself, shall have a direct right of action against the acceptor arising out of the bill of exchange, whereby he may claim everything that can be claimed in accordance with the provisions of Articles 370 and 371.

Where the drawee who has put his acceptance on the bill cancels it before returning the bill, acceptance is deemed to be refused, and failing proof to the contrary, the cancellation is deemed to have taken place before the bill was returned.

Nevertheless, if the drawee has notified his acceptance in writing to the holder of the bill or to any signatory whatsoever, he is bound towards them according to the terms of his acceptance.

Payment of the sum of a bill of exchange may be guaranteed as to the whole or part of its amount by an aval.

This guarantee may be given by a third party or by one of the signatories to the bill.

An aval is written either on the bill of exchange or on an allonge, or in a separate instrument indicating the place in which the aval was given.

It is expressed by the words "good as aval" or by any other equivalent formula, and is signed by the aval, literally the guarantee.

An aval is deemed to be constituted by the mere signature of the giver of the aval on the back of the bill of exchange, save where the signatory is the drawee or the drawer.

An aval must specify for whose account it is given. In default of this, it is deemed to be given for the drawer.

The giver of an aval is bound in the same manner as the person for whom he has become guarantor.

His undertaking is valid even when the obligation which he has guaranteed is void for any reason other than defect of form.

When the giver of an aval pays the amount of the bill of exchange, he acquires the rights arising out of the bill of exchange against the person guaranteed and against those who are liable to the latter on the bill of exchange.

A bill may be drawn in the following manners:

- At sight.

- At a fixed period after sight.

- At a fixed period commencing from a certain date.

- At a fixed day.

Bills of exchange at other maturities than those abovementioned or at successive maturities are void.

A bill of exchange at sight is payable on presentment, and it must be presented for payment within one year commencing from its date. The drawer may abridge this period or stipulate a longer period.

These periods may be abridged by the endorsers.

The drawer of a "bill at sight" may prescribe that it may not be presented for payment before a specified date.

In this case, the period for presentment commences from that date.

The holder of a bill of exchange shall not be compelled to accept payment thereof before maturity.

If the drawee pays before maturity, he shall bear the risks of his act.

Whoever pays at maturity shall be legally discharged unless he has committed fraud or gross fault, and he shall verify the regularity of the series of endorsements, though not the authenticity of the signatures of the endorsers.

If a bill of exchange is stipulated to be payable in a currency which is not in circulation at the place of payment, the amount thereof may be paid in the currency of the country according to its rate on the day of maturity; and if the debtor is in default, the holder of the bill may demand, at his option, that the amount of the bill be paid in the currency of the country according either to its rate on the day of maturity or to its rate on the day of payment.

The value of the foreign currency shall be determined according to the usages observed at the place of payment; provided, however, that the drawer may stipulate that the sum payable shall be calculated according to a rate specified in the bill.

Nevertheless, the rules set forth above shall not apply where the drawer has stipulated that payment must be made in a specified currency (stipulation for effective payment in a foreign currency).

If the amount of the bill is specified in a currency having the same denomination in the place of issue of the bill and the place of payment thereof, but a different value in the two places, the currency of the place of payment shall be presumed to have been agreed upon.

If a bill of exchange is not presented for payment on the day of maturity, any debtor shall have the right to deposit the amount in trust with the bank authorised to accept State deposits, at the expense and risk of the holder of the bill.

The debtor shall thereafter only be bound to deliver the receipt of deposit against delivery of the bill of exchange.
Opposition to payment shall not be admitted except in the case of loss of the bill of exchange or the bankruptcy of the holder thereof.
If an unaccepted bill of exchange is lost, the owner thereof shall have the right to verify its collection upon a second, third, fourth, etc. part.
And if the lost bill is coupled with acceptance, payment thereof may not be claimed upon a second, third, fourth, etc. part except by a decision of the court and upon furnishing security.

If the person who has lost the bill, whether accepted or not, is unable to produce the second, third, fourth, etc. part, he shall have the right to request payment of the lost bill and to obtain such payment pursuant to a decision of the court, provided that he proves his ownership by his books and furnishes security.

The maturity date of a bill drawn at a certain period after sight shall be determined either by the date of acceptance or by the date of the protest.

In the absence of a protest, an undated acceptance shall, as regards the acceptor, be deemed to have been given on the last day of the period fixed for presentment of the bill for acceptance.

The maturity date of a bill drawn at one or more months after a fixed date or after sight shall fall on the corresponding date of the month in which payment must be made, and if there is no corresponding date, maturity shall fall on the last day of that month.

Where a bill is drawn at one or more months and a half after a fixed date or after sight, the whole months shall first be reckoned.

Where the maturity date is fixed at the beginning of a month, or in the middle thereof, for instance (middle of January or middle of February, etc...), or at the end of a month, such expression shall be understood to mean the first day, the fifteenth day, and the last day of the month.

The expressions "eight days" and "fifteen days" shall not mean one week or two weeks, but a period of eight days or fifteen days actually elapsed. The expression "half a month" shall signify fifteen days.

Where a bill is payable on a fixed day in a place having a calendar different from that of the place of issue of the bill, the date of maturity shall be deemed to be fixed according to the calendar in force at the place of payment.

Where a bill drawn between two places having different calendars is payable at a certain period after a fixed date, the day corresponding to the day of issue of the bill shall be taken from the calendar of the place of payment, and the maturity date shall then be determined.

The periods relating to the presentment of bills of exchange shall be calculated in accordance with the rules set forth in the preceding paragraph.

However, these rules shall not apply if a stipulation in the bill of exchange, or the terms contained therein, indicate that the intention was to follow different rules.

The holder of a bill of exchange payable on a fixed day, or at a certain period after a fixed date or after sight, must present the bill for payment on the day of its maturity.

Presentment of the bill to a clearing house shall be deemed equivalent to presentment for payment.

The drawee may, upon paying the amount of the bill, require the holder to deliver it up to him with a statement of payment written thereon, and the holder of the bill may not refuse partial payment.

In the case of partial payment, the drawee may require that a note of such payment be entered on the bill and that a receipt be given to him.

Any sum paid out of the original amount of the bill shall discharge the drawer and the endorser to that extent.

The holder of the bill must make protest in respect of the remaining amount.

If the payment requested pursuant to the two preceding Articles is refused, the owner of the lost bill shall be entitled to preserve all his rights by a deed of protest which must be drawn up on the day following the maturity of the lost bill.

As for the notices provided for in Article 367, they must be sent to the drawer and to the endorsers within the time limits specified in the said Article.

In order to obtain the second copy, the owner of the lost bill must address himself to his immediate endorser. This endorser is bound to lend him his name and his assistance towards his own immediate endorser.

And so on from endorser to endorser until it reaches the owner of the bill. As for the expenses, they shall be borne by the owner of the lost bill.

The obligation of the suretyship provided for in Articles 360 and 361 shall lapse after the passage of three years if, during this period, neither a demand nor legal proceedings before the courts have been brought.

The holder of the bill may exercise recourse against the endorsers, the drawer and the other parties liable:

At maturity, if payment has not taken place

And he may exercise such recourse even before maturity:

First - If there has been a refusal of acceptance, whether total or partial.

Second - If the drawee has become bankrupt, whether he has accepted the bill or not, or if he has suspended payment even if such suspension has not been established by a judgment, or if an attachment of his property has been levied and the attachment has remained fruitless.

Third - If the drawer of a bill not acceptable has become bankrupt.

Provided that the guarantors against whom recourse is exercised in the cases set forth in the two preceding last sub-paragraphs may, within three days from the institution of the action, submit to the President of the Commercial Court of their place of residence a petition requesting a time limit; if this request is found to be justified, the order shall fix the date on which the guarantors shall be bound to pay the commercial bills referred to, without the time limits granted in this manner exceeding the date fixed for maturity.

This order shall not be subject to opposition or to appeal.

Refusal of acceptance or of payment must be established by an authentic instrument (protest for non-acceptance or for non-payment).

A "protest for non-acceptance" must be drawn up within the time limits fixed for presentment of the bill for acceptance.

If the bill has been presented for the first time on the last day of the time limit, as in the case provided for in the first paragraph of Article 339, the protest may also be drawn up on the following day.

A protest for non-payment of a bill payable on a fixed day, or at a certain period after date or after sight, must be drawn up on one of the two business days following the day on which the bill is payable.

If the bill is payable at sight, the protest must be drawn up in accordance with the conditions set forth in the preceding paragraph regarding the protest for non-acceptance.

A "protest for non-acceptance" dispenses with presentment of the bill for payment and with protest for non-payment.

If the drawee has suspended payment, whether he has accepted the bill or not, or if an attachment of his property has been levied without result, the holder of the bill may not exercise his right of recourse until after the bill has been presented to the drawee for payment and after a protest has been drawn up.

If the drawee has been declared bankrupt, whether he has accepted the bill or not, or if the drawer of a non-acceptable bill has been declared bankrupt, the production of the judgment declaring the bankruptcy suffices to enable the holder of the bill to exercise his right of recourse.

The holder of the bill must give notice of non-acceptance or non-payment to the person who endorsed the bill to him and to the drawer within the four working days which follow the day of the protest or the day of presentment of the bill where there is a provision permitting return without costs. Every endorser must, within the two working days which follow the day on which the notice reaches him, inform the person who endorsed the bill to him of the notice which he has received, indicating to him the names and addresses of the persons who have sent the previous notices, and so on in turn until reaching the drawer. The time limits specified above run from the date of receipt of the preceding notice.

Where a notice is sent to one of the signatories of the bill in accordance with the preceding paragraph, the same notice must be sent within the same period to the guarantor by aval.

Where one of the endorsers has not specified his address or has specified it in an illegible manner, it is sufficient that the notice be sent to the endorser who precedes him.

A person who is required to send the notice may send it in any form whatsoever, even by simply returning the bill of exchange.

He must prove that the notice was sent within the prescribed time limit. The time limit shall be deemed to have been observed if a letter containing the notice has been placed in the post within the said time limit.

A person who does not send the notice within the time limit specified above does not expose his right to forfeiture, but he shall be liable, where applicable, for the damage which he has caused by his negligence, without the damages exceeding the amount of the bill.

If the drawer, the endorser, or the guarantor by aval places on the bill, together with his signature, the stipulation "return without costs" or "without protest" or any other similar expression, the holder of the bill shall be exempted, if he wishes to exercise judicial recourse, from drawing up a protest for non-acceptance or non-payment.

However, this stipulation does not dispense the holder of the bill from presenting it within the prescribed time limits, nor from sending the requisite notices.

The proof of non-observance of the time limits lies upon the person who invokes it against the holder of the bill.

If that stipulation emanates from the drawer, its effects extend to all the signatories; whereas if its writer is an endorser or a guarantor by aval, its effects do not extend to anyone other than him.

If the holder of the bill draws up a protest despite the presence of this stipulation and the signature of the drawer thereon, the costs shall be borne by him; whereas if the stipulation emanates from an endorser or a guarantor by aval, the costs of the protest, if drawn up, may be recovered from all the signatories of the bill.

All those who have drawn, accepted, endorsed or guaranteed a bill of exchange shall be jointly and severally liable towards the holder of the bill. The holder of the bill may proceed against all of these persons individually or collectively without being bound to observe the order in which they undertook their obligations.

The same right shall belong to every person who has signed a bill and discharged it.

An action brought against one of the parties liable shall not prevent proceeding against the others, even though they may be subsequent to him in order.

The holder of the bill may claim from the person against whom he proceeds:

First - The amount of the unaccepted or unpaid bill of exchange, with interest if stipulated.

Second - Legal interest starting from the date of maturity.

Third - The expenses of protest and of the notices sent, and all other expenses.

If the action is brought before maturity, a discount amount shall be deducted from the value of the bill, calculated at the official discount rate (that is, the rate of the bank authorised to accept State deposits) as such rate stands at the place of residence of the holder of the bill at the date on which the action is brought.

A person who has discharged the amount of the bill may claim from his guarantors:

First - The entire amount he has paid.

Second - Interest on the said amount, calculated at the legal rate, starting from the day on which he paid it.

Third - The expenses he has paid.

Every party liable against whom an action has been brought, or who is exposed to an action, shall be entitled to demand, against his discharge of the bill, that the bill be delivered up to him together with the deed of protest and a receipted account.

Every endorser who has discharged a bill of exchange may strike out his own endorsement and the endorsements of subsequent endorsers.

Where an action is brought following a partial acceptance of the bill, the person who discharges the part for which acceptance was not obtained may demand that such discharge be noted on the bill and that a receipt for the amount be given to him. The holder of the bill must, moreover, deliver to him a certified true copy of the bill together with the deed of protest, to enable him to bring subsequent recourse proceedings.

After the expiry of the time-limits fixed:

1 - For the presentment of a bill payable at sight or at a period after sight.

2 - For drawing up the protest for non-acceptance or non-payment.

3 - For the presentment of the bill for payment where there is a stipulation "return without expenses".

The holder of the bill shall forfeit his rights against the endorsers, against the drawer, and against the other parties liable, with the exception of the acceptor of the bill.

However, such forfeiture shall not take effect in favour of the drawer unless he proves that he had provided cover at the time of maturity. In that case, the holder of the bill shall retain only a right of action against the person on whom the bill was drawn.

If the instrument is not presented for acceptance within the time-limit stipulated by the drawer, the holder's rights of recourse for non-payment or for non-acceptance shall be forfeited within the limits specified in the preceding Article, unless it appears from the terms of the agreement that the drawer only intended to relieve himself of the guarantee of acceptance.

If a time-limit for presenting the instrument is stipulated in one of the endorsements, only the endorser may avail himself thereof.

Should the presentment of the instrument or the drawing up of the protest within the prescribed time-limits be prevented by an insurmountable obstacle (such as a legal provision in any State or other cases of force majeure), these time-limits shall be extended. The holder of the instrument shall be bound to give notice without delay of the case of force majeure to his endorser, and to record this notice, dated and signed by him, on the bill of exchange or on an allonge; as to the rest, the provisions of Article 367 shall apply.

When force majeure has terminated, the holder of the instrument must without delay present it for acceptance or for payment and, if need be, draw up the protest.

If, however, force majeure continues to operate beyond thirty days after maturity, recourse may be exercised without the need for presentment of the instrument or the drawing up of a protest.

In the case of instruments payable at sight or at a fixed period after sight, the time-limit of thirty days shall run from the date on which the holder of the instrument has given notice of the force majeure to his endorser, even before the expiration of the time-limit for presentment of the instrument. In the case of instruments payable at a fixed period after sight, the time-limit ofthirty days shall be increased by the period after sight specified in the instrument.

Facts which are purely personal to the holder of the instrument or to the person whom he has entrusted with the presentment of the instrument or the drawing up of the protest shall not be deemed to constitute cases of force majeure.

Protests for non-acceptance or for non-payment shall be drawn up by the notary public or one of his clerks, and must be addressed:

To the domicile of the person by whom the instrument was payable or to his last known domicile, to the domicile of each of the persons designated in the bill of exchange to pay it in case of need, and to the domicile of the third party who has accepted the instrument by intervention. All of this shall be effected by a single instrument and notifications shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of Article 353 et seq. of the Code of Civil Procedure.

The deed of protest shall contain a literal transcript of the bill of exchange, the text of the acceptance, the endorsements and the instructions indicated therein, and the formal demand to pay the value of the bill. It shall mention whether the person required to pay the bill is present or absent, together with the reasons for the refusal of payment and the inability or refusal to sign.
No act on the part of the holder of the bill may dispense with the drawing up of a protest, except in the case provided for in Article 360 et seq. relating to the loss of the bill.

The notary public must retain an exact copy of the protests and enter their texts in full, day by day and in the order of their dates, in a special register, failing which he shall be liable to pay damages to the interested parties.

Every person having a right of judicial recourse may, in the absence of a stipulation to the contrary, reimburse himself by means of a new bill (redraft) drawn on one of his guarantors and payable at sight at the domicile of that guarantor.

The new bill shall include a brokerage fee and the cost of the stamps required for the bill, in addition to the sums provided for in Articles 370 and 371.

If the holder of the bill is the drawer of the new bill, the value of this bill shall be determined according to the rate for a bill "at sight" drawn from the place where the original bill was payable upon the place where the guarantor is domiciled.

If the holder of the new bill is one of the endorsers, its value shall be determined according to the rate for a bill "at sight" at the place where the drawer of the new bill is domiciled upon the place where the guarantor is domiciled.
Redrafts may not be accumulated; each endorser, as well as the drawer, is liable for only one redraft.

The drawer, an endorser, or a guarantor by aval may specify a person to accept or pay in case of need. A bill of exchange may, under the conditions set forth hereinafter, be accepted or paid by a person intervening for the honour of a debtor subject to recourse.

The intervener may be a third party, even the drawee himself, or a person already liable under the bill of exchange, with the exception of the acceptor of the bill. The intervener must give notice of his intervention within two business days to the person for whose honour he has intervened. If he fails to observe this time limit, he shall be liable, where applicable, for the damage caused by his negligence, without the compensation for such damage exceeding the amount of the bill of exchange.

The Garage

First - Determining the number of required parking spaces:

The designs of buildings of whatever type and whatever their intended use must include one or more garages.

The garage required to be provided in the design of buildings is a place designated for the parking of cars, whether uncovered or roofed, enclosed or not, located at ground level, below it, or above it, to and from which the entry and exit of cars and their circulation inside it is easy.

The garage pertaining to each part or section of the building and the actual possibility of entry, parking, and exit of cars through entry and exit passages and ramps must be provided for on the licensing plans, and this garage shall be considered an integral part of the section of the building to which it pertains (for a residential apartment, a shop, an office, or for the practice of a profession..) upon the leasing, subdivision, or sale of this section.

The number of required parking spaces shall be determined according to the intended use of these sections and their areas, in accordance with the following table:

a) In new buildings:

1 - Residence

One car for every 100m2 of the area of the dwelling that is calculated in the exploitation and for every fraction exceeding 50m2, with a minimum of one car and a maximum of five cars for a single dwelling.

In the event of an application for the amendment or renewal of a building permit granted in the light of the provisions of Legislative Decree No. 148 dated 16/9/1983, the number of required car parking spaces shall be calculated in accordance with the provisions of Decree No. 2791/92 regardless of the provisions of the paragraph above, even if the application for renewal or amendment includes benefiting from the provisions of this Decree.

2 - Furnished apartments or rooms for tourists and students

One car for every two apartments, provided that the area of a single apartment does not exceed 50m2.

3 - Hotels

3 - 1 - In the centres of Governorates and Districts:

One car for every four rooms.

3 - 2 - In the remaining cities and villages:

One car for every two rooms.

To this shall be added the number of cars required for restaurants, cafes, and nightclubs if they exist within the plot of the hotel.

4 - Motels

One car for each unit (room or apartment) .

5 - Restaurants, cafes, nightclubs, and internet cafes:

One car for every 30m2 of the area of the restaurant, cafe, or nightclub, and one car for every fraction exceeding 15m2. The area of roofs, sidewalks, and areas designated for the patrons of the project shall be calculated as part of the area of the restaurant, cafe, or nightclub.

6 - Showrooms, museums, and social and cultural clubs:

One car for each unit, provided that it is not less than one car for every 40m2 and one car for every fraction exceeding 20m2.

7 - Offices or commercial shops

One car for each shop or office, provided that it is not less than one car for every 40m2 and one car for every fraction exceeding 20m2; the area of the mezzanines pertaining to these shops shall be calculated as part of the area to determine the number of required parking spaces.

The number of parking spaces required for offices shall be adopted in determining the parking spaces required for buildings designated for radio and television, medical and veterinary clinics, dispensaries, and municipal halls.

8 - Cinemas and theatres

One car for every ten seats, provided that it is not less than one car for every 15m2 of the area of the hall including the stage.

9 - Amusement game places (amusement park, Amusement Centre...)

One car for every 20m2 and one car for every fraction exceeding 10m2.

10 - Swimming pools and ski centres

10 - 1 - Chalets:

One car for every 40m2 of the area of the chalet and for every fraction exceeding 20m2.

10 - 2 - Cabins:

One car for each cabin.

10 - 3 - Patrons: In addition to the car parking spaces in paragraphs 10 - 1 and 10 - 2 above, an additional area must be provided for parking the cars of patrons (swimmers, skiers,...) who do not own or rent chalets or cabins, determined as follows:

- In private swimming pools.

An additional area shall be designated at a rate of not less than 2% of the total area of the project (private property, maritime property: water and land) to be used as a parking lot for cars.

- In public swimming pools.

Reducing this rate to 1%.

- In ski centres.

An additional area shall be designated at a rate of not less than 1% of the total area of the project (private property, common land,...).

10 - 4:

To the number of parking spaces above shall be added the parking spaces required for restaurants, cafes, and nightclubs if they exist within the swimming pools and ski centres.

11 - Tennis courts, basketball or volleyball courts, and football fields:

Six cars for each court or field, in addition to one car for every 20m2 of the area of the bleachers or the area designated for spectators.

12 - Sports clubs

One car for every 40m2 of the building and one car for every fraction exceeding 20m2.

13 - Schools:

2 cars for each classroom and one large vehicle (bus) for transporting students for every 50 students, in addition to the cars required for the administration.

13 - 1 - Nurseries:

One car for every two classrooms, one car for the administration, two cars for waiting.

14 - Language schools and technical institutes:

One car for each classroom.

15 - Universities

One car for every 75m2 of the area of the building and one car for every fraction exceeding 25m2.

16 - Homes for the elderly

One car for every 100m2 and one car for every fraction exceeding 50m2.

17 - Hospitals:

One car for every 75m2 of the area of the hospital and for every fraction exceeding 25m2.

18 - Orphanages:

One car for every ten beds, to which shall be added the parking spaces required for the administrators.

19 - Factories

One car for every 75m2 of the entire area of the building, one car for every fraction exceeding 25m2.

20 - Farms:

One car for every 200m2 and for every fraction exceeding 100m2, and one truck parking space for every 400m2 and for every fraction exceeding 200m2.

21 - Warehouses

21 - 2 - One car for every 200m2 of the area of the warehouse and for every fraction exceeding 100m2.. The word warehouse is understood to mean everything that is subterranean below ground level in its entirety, including the administrative offices pertaining to it, provided that they do not exceed 10% of its area and that this warehouse is prepared for storage only.

In the event that the basement floor is used for commerce, industry, or other purposes, parking spaces must be provided in accordance with the intended use of the basement floor, and the parking spaces required for warehouses stipulated above shall not be adopted.

21 - 2 - It is permitted to provide the garage within the warehouse when its area exceeds 300m2, provided that the location of the garage is logically determined on the building permit plans.

21 - 3 - It is not required to provide a garage for small warehouses that are not directly connected to different sections of the building, and the area of each of which does not exceed twenty square metres (20m2), provided that each warehouse thereof is designated for the use of the different units in the building; this area shall not be calculated as part of the area of the unit in calculating the required garage (residential apartment, office, store, showroom, etc....), and it shall be attached to it as an integral part thereof when subdividing the building into different rights.

However, if its area exceeds twenty metres, a garage must be provided for it on the basis of the number of cars required for warehouses according to the paragraph above.

As for a warehouse that is directly connected to the unit for which it is designated, its area shall be added to the area of the unit to which it pertains for calculating the cars required to be provided for this unit according to its intended use, whatever the area of the warehouse may be.

22 - Car wash, oil change, and tyre repair centres:

Two cars for each car wash, one car for each oil change centre, and one car for each tyre repair shop.

23 - Places of worship

One car for every 50m2 and one car for every fraction exceeding 25m2.

24 - Other buildings

In the event that permit applications are received for buildings of categories other than those mentioned above, they shall be submitted to the Higher Council for Urban Planning to place them in one of these categories or to determine the number of required cars in the event that it is not possible to place them in one of these categories.

The areas specified above, on the basis of which the number of required cars is determined, do not include the area of external walls, balconies, verandas, loggias, projections prepared for decoration, sunshades, flower boxes, mezzanines not pertaining to commercial shops whose clear height does not exceed 1.90 m, stairwells and elevator shafts, tile attics designated for the service of the building, and external passages connecting stairs and elevators to dwellings, offices, or exploited areas.

b - Changing the intended use of legally existing buildings

Upon applying to change the intended use of all or part of legally existing buildings as permitted by the zoning regulations, or upon amending the number of units of which they are composed, the provision of the garage required pursuant to item (a) above shall be imposed, and in the event of the impossibility of providing the garage, it may be substituted by paying the special fee, for the result of the difference between the two numbers of parking spaces before and after the change in accordance with item "First" of this Article.

c - Adding a building in a built plot:

Upon licensing the addition of a building in a built plot, whether this addition is above the existing building or on an unbuilt area of the land of the plot:

* If the occupancy permit or the building permit for the installations existing in the plot provides for a garage for cars, it is required that the plans attached to the application for the addition of the building provide for the parking spaces or for the total area that was designated as a garage for the existing building, in addition to the parking spaces required for the building requested to be added.

* It is prohibited to license the addition of any installations, such as columns or otherwise, that would negatively affect the garage designated for the existing building in the event that an alternative garage is not provided.

Second - Technical specifications of the garage:

a) In plots whose area exceeds 800m2 (eight hundred square metres):

1 - Regarding the adopted car dimensions

- Length 520 cm (five hundred and twenty centimetres)

- Width 180 cm (one hundred and eighty centimetres)

- Minimum lateral distance between one car and another car or between the car and the walls or column: 40 cm (forty centimetres), and when the cars are parked behind each other in a direction parallel to the clear passage, a distance of not less than 40 cm shall be imposed between one car and another.

- Rear distance between the car and the wall or column 20cm (twenty centimetres).

(See Drawing No. 93)

2 - Regarding the number of cars

In examining the legality of the garage, it shall be adopted that it accommodates the required number of cars, conditional upon securing entry, parking, and exit for each car, without one obstructing the possibility of entry and exit of another.

It may be accepted that a car obstructs the entry or exit of another car if these parking spaces are located in a private garage pertaining to a single different right, provided that the number of cars whose entry or exit is obstructed does not exceed half the number of cars pertaining to this unit.

3 - Regarding entry and exit ramps

3 - 1 - Longitudinal section

The slope of the ramps must not exceed 20% (twenty percent), while connecting them to the internal flat areas and to the external roads by sections whose slope does not exceed 10% (ten percent) and with a length of 5m. (five metres) at least, and provided that the clear height across the entire width of the ramp is not less than 2.20m. (two metres and twenty) at least.

(See Drawing No. 94)

- In ramps whose length is equal to or less than 15 metres, as well as half ramps (Demi rampes) in garages with half levels (Demi niveaux), it is permitted to adopt a continuous (average) slope of 12% including the slope of the sections that connect the ramp to the internal flat areas and to the external roads.

- The slope of the garage space must not exceed 5% (five percent).

In the event of the existence of a slope of 5% in the garage space, a continuous (average) slope of 15% may be adopted, including the slope of the sections that connect the ramp to the internal flat areas.

(See Drawings No. 95 and 96)

3 - 2 - Cross section

The width of the ramp leading to the garage must not be less than:

a - 3.50m. (three and a half metres) for garages in which the number of cars does not exceed 30 cars.

b - 5.25m. (five and a quarter metres) for garages in which the number of cars exceeds 30 cars, and in the event of providing an independent entrance and exit, paragraph - a - above shall apply (3.50 metres for each of them), and they may be provided on the same facade.

Curbs (chasse roues) may be provided for within the width specified above on one side, provided that the height of the curb does not exceed 20 cm and its width does not exceed 30 cm.

(See Drawing No. 97)

3 - 3 - Curves

The inner radius of any curve must not be less than 4.50m. (four and a half metres) and the outer radius not less than 8m. (eight metres).

(See Drawing No. 98)

4 - Regarding internal passages

The slope of the internal passages must not exceed 5% (five percent).

The paragraphs listed below shall apply to them, with the possibility of tolerance in their width up to 2.50m. (two and a half metres) if the length of the passage does not exceed 5.00m. (five metres), for one case only on each floor.

(See Drawing No. 99)

4 - 1 - Passages leading to the spaces prepared for parking cars:

Their clear width between columns or between columns and walls must not be less than 3.50m. (three and a half metres) in the event of the absence of car parking on either side.

4 - 2 - Clear passages for car parking spaces in spaces free of columns and walls (uncovered or roofed spaces):

Their width must not be less than:

- 4.00m. (four metres) when the cars are parked behind each other in a direction parallel to the clear passage in accordance with the conditions of paragraph 1 - 1.

- 5.00m. (five metres) when the cars are parked in a direction forming an angle of 45 degrees with the direction of the clear passage, in accordance with the conditions of paragraph 1 - 1.

- 6.00m. (six metres) when the cars are parked in a direction forming an angle of 90 degrees with the direction of the clear passage, in accordance with the conditions of paragraph 1-1.

(See Drawing No. 100)

4 - 3 - Clear passages for car parking spaces in spaces within which columns and walls exist:

Subject to the provisions of paragraph 1 of item "Second" above, the legality of the garage shall be examined as follows:

- The width of the passages shall be determined in the light of the possibility of cars using them to reach their parking spaces without any obstacle.

- A car that turns must do so within an inner radius of not less than 3.00m. (three metres) and an outer radius of not less than 6.30m. (six metres and thirty centimetres).

- To calculate the width of the passage, the cars must move inside the lines of the inner and outer radius, without this movement being obstructed by the presence of columns, walls, or other cars on both sides of the passage.

- In all cases, the width of the passage must not be less than 3.50m. (three and a half metres).

- To examine the legality of the passage, the model shown in Drawing 101 below shall be adopted

b - In plots whose area is equal to or less than 800m2 (eight hundred square metres) and in existing heritage buildings:

The dimensions and distances specified below shall apply:

1 - Regarding the adopted car dimensions

- Length 480 cm (four hundred and eighty centimetres)

_Width 170cm (one hundred and seventy centimetres)

- Rear distance between the car and the wall or column 20cm (twenty centimetres)

Third - General conditions

1 - Passages whose width is less than six metres and which lead to spaces left behind buildings cannot be considered as a garage for parking cars, and likewise the setback imposed on the facade of the building from the road boundaries cannot be considered as a garage for parking cars for plots whose area exceeds eight hundred square metres, nor shall a space connected to the plot by a passage whose width is less than two and a half metres (2.50m.) be counted as a garage.

2 - A passage on the ground floor with a width of not less than 3.00m. (three metres) must be provided as an entrance to the building where the parking of cars is prohibited, and this width shall be reduced to 2m (two metres) in plots whose area is equal to or less than 800m2, and a separating distance between the car parking spaces and the sections of the building facade facing the roads and occupied for residence or commerce must be provided of not less than 1.20m.
