(one hundred and twenty centimetres), and this distance shall be reduced to 40 centimetres in plots whose area is equal to or less than 800m2. This distance shall be equipped as a sidewalk for pedestrians with the installation of barriers (flower boxes, statues, columns...) on the edge of the sidewalk with a height of not less than 30 cm above the level of the sidewalk to prevent cars from mounting the sidewalk.

3 - It is prohibited to park cars and to construct ascending and descending ramps to the garage within the required setback from the road boundaries or from the alignment boundaries.

(See Drawings No. 109 and 110)

4 - The construction of the required garage in accordance with the building permit is mandatory, and no full or partial, temporary or final occupancy permit may be granted for the building in the event that it is not provided.

5 - It is prohibited to make any amendment to the building during execution or after the occupancy permit in a manner that prevents the use of the garage for cars.

6 - If the garage is provided in floors within the building, at least one staircase must be connected from the ground floor to the various storeys and levels of this garage within the projection of the building. In the event that elevators exist in the building, at least one elevator must be connected to the various storeys and levels of this garage.

7 - When the design of the building, the placement of columns, or the presence of walls in the areas that will be designated for the garage prevents the entry or accommodation of the number or part of the required cars, the competent technical administration is entitled to request a reconsideration of the design of the building or the placement of columns and walls to provide the necessary garage required for the entire exploitation of the plot, even if the subject of the permit covers a part of this exploitation. In this case, the owner of the plot may suffice with providing the garage required for the requested building only, provided that he attaches an irrevocable undertaking registered on the real folio whereby he undertakes not to add any building in the future in the plot except to the extent of what garage is provided for the existing building and the one requested to be added subsequently. This annotation shall not be struck off except with the approval of the competent technical administration.

8 - The application for a permit to construct residential building complexes or buildings of public use (schools, restaurants, theatres) for which more than fifty cars are required must include a study of the impact of the building on traffic movement (Traffic Impact Study) and how to address these variables.

Fourth - Substitution for ramps

Equipping the garage with car entry and exit ramps in accordance with the technical specifications stipulated in item Second of this Article is mandatory, and these ramps may be substituted by car elevators in the following four cases:

1) If the plot, after the mandatory setbacks from the road and public property, does not accommodate a square measuring 16m* 16m.

2) If a single floor of the garage does not accommodate the parking of four cars after installing the necessary ramp.

3) In existing buildings in which it is not possible to provide the necessary ramp for technical or artistic reasons.

4) In certain exceptional cases subject to the approval of the Higher Council for Urban Planning.

These car elevators shall be subject to the following technical and preventive measures and conditions:

- One independent car elevator must be provided up to a garage capacity of twelve cars (12 cars), and two elevators independent of each other must be provided if the number of cars in the garage exceeds 12 cars, and in the event that the number of parking spaces exceeds 50 parking spaces, the provision of a ramp for the entry of cars into the garage shall be imposed.

- A waiting place accommodating the parking of at least two cars must be provided upon entry within the plot (outside the road, public property, setbacks, and open spaces) without obstructing traffic movement to or from the elevator.

- An electric generator must be provided in the building to operate at least one car elevator.

- A maintenance insurance contract for the car elevators must be concluded with a specialised company, as well as an insurance contract against the accidents of their operation with an insurance company, to be attached to the application for the occupancy permit.

- The car elevator must be equipped with an alarm device upon the occurrence of any malfunction or accident and with a fire extinguishing device.

- It is prohibited to use car elevators in public garages unless car entry and exit ramps are provided as a backup.

- In the event of constructing automated parking spaces for cars, the preventive technical conditions must be complied with to secure public safety requirements in accordance with the regulations in force.

Fifth - Substitution for the garage

Certain buildings may be exempted from the condition of providing a garage when there is a compelling technical impossibility preventing the construction of the garage, provided that in these cases a special fee is imposed, to be collected by the authority that grants the building permit.

The required garage fee in lieu shall be determined by a decision issued by the Higher Council for Urban Planning based on the cost of constructing it roofed, equivalent to 25m2 for each car and 50 m2 for each bus or truck, taking into consideration the price of the square metre of the land of the plot and the general exploitation factor in the zone.

1 - The garage shall not be imposed in the following cases and shall be substituted by the special fee stipulated above:

* If what is requested to be erected is an addition of a building in a plot that includes an existing building, with the impossibility of providing a garage for the added building.

* If what is requested is an amendment of the intended use of an existing building that requires providing additional parking spaces beyond what is provided for the existing building, with the impossibility of providing the required parking spaces in the light of the amendment.

* If the plot is located on a road designed as a staircase according to the official maps issued by the Land Registry Offices and executed in reality in the form of a staircase. However, if the road is designed as a staircase and executed in reality as a road whose slope does not exceed 12% and with a width that permits the passage of cars, then the provision of the garage must be imposed in the design of buildings in the plots benefiting from the road.

* If the plot is landlocked (Enclave).

* If the plot is connected to a passage that does not permit the entry of cars.

* If the area of the plot, its shape, or the area of the building intended to be erected does not permit providing entry and exit passages with a slope not exceeding 20% or in which it is not possible to provide curves in accordance with the technical specifications that are the subject of item "Second" above.

It is prohibited to provide for commercial stores or warehouses instead of car parking spaces on the ground floor and basement floors in this case.

* In plots that are connected to the public road by passages whose width is less than 2.50m2.

No building complex comprising more than one building in the plot may be exempted from the condition of providing a car garage, and consequently, in this case, the provision of the garage cannot be substituted by paying the fee.

2 - Substitution for the garage by the special fee:

Upon granting the prior permit, and in the event of the existence of a technical impossibility preventing the construction of the garage and requiring its replacement by a special fee, the building permit shall be granted attached to a request from the authority that granted the permit addressed to the competent Land Registrar to register an entry on the real folio of the plot that the owner has a claim owed by it for the number of cars for which the fee in lieu was paid. This entry shall remain standing until the alternative garage is provided or the annotation is struck off by the owner of the plot benefiting from it in accordance with the provisions of the last paragraph of this item.

A special account for the garage shall be established in the Public Treasury in favour of each municipality, provided that the revenues of this garage are designated exclusively for establishing collective garages or for settling the status of those for whom garages have not been provided, and provided that the expenditures of each municipality do not exceed its revenues from the garage fee or collective garages.

The owner of the plot who has paid the garage replacement fees is entitled, if the competent authorities do not proceed within a maximum period of eight years from the date of collecting the fees to provide a garage, to recover the amounts paid and to strike off the car fee in lieu annotation recorded on the real folio of the plot, provided that he provides the required parking spaces in accordance with the provisions of this Article.

3 - Substitution for the garage by purchasing parking spaces:

Paying the fee in lieu mentioned above may be substituted by purchasing car parking spaces in other plots or buildings that include additional parking spaces or a public collective garage, in accordance with the following conditions:

* The garage pertaining to the building that is the subject of the permit application must not be more than 500m away from the plot concerned, provided that this distance is designated for the public (a road for cars or pedestrians).

* The permit for building, amendment, or occupancy shall not be granted in this case except after registering the contract of purchase of the parking spaces on the folio pertaining to the plot that is the subject of the permit application and to the plot burdened with the easement of providing the parking spaces.

* In the event of erecting a building on the plot burdened with the easement of providing car parking spaces for other plots, the parking spaces that have been sold to other owners must be specified on the building permit plans, provided that the entrances to these parking spaces are separate from the building that will be erected on the plot, while securing ease of access to these parking spaces without any obstacles.

* In the event of an agreement between the owners of the servient and dominant plots to provide an alternative parking space, the alternative parking space must not be more than 500m away from the original dominant plot, and the contract of purchase of the new parking space pertaining to the dominant and servient plots must be registered on the real folio pertaining to the two aforementioned plots, prior to granting the building permit on the plot that was burdened with the easement of providing the garage.

* In the event that it is impossible to provide a legally required garage for a tourist establishment in buildings existing on the date of entry into force of Law 646/2004, the tourist establishment occupying the existing building or any section thereof may pay an annual garage fee in favour of the municipality amounting to a rate of five percent (5%) of the value of the garage fee determined according to the assessments adopted in accordance with the regulations in force.

The provisions of the paragraph above shall apply to tourist establishments that will occupy buildings or sections of buildings existing on the date of entry into force of Law No. 646 dated 11/12/2004, provided that the buildings are legally licensed and not in violation of the building laws in force.

Acceptance by intervention may take place in all cases in which the holder of a bill capable of acceptance has a right of recourse prior to maturity.

Where a person has been designated on the bill to accept it or to pay it in case of need at the place of payment, the holder of the bill shall not be entitled to exercise his rights of recourse prior to maturity against the party who designated such person or against the signatories subsequent to him, unless he has presented the bill to the designated person and the latter has refused acceptance, and such refusal has been established by a deed of protest.

In other cases of intervention, the holder of the bill may refuse acceptance by intervention.

If, however, he admits it, he shall lose his right to institute proceedings prior to maturity against the person in whose favour acceptance was given and against the subsequent signatories of the bill.

Acceptance by intervention shall be noted on the bill of exchange and signed by the intervener, and it shall specify the person for whose account acceptance is given; in default of such specification, the acceptance shall be deemed to have been given in favour of the drawer.

An acceptor by intervention shall be liable to the holder of the bill and to the endorsers subsequent to the person in whose favour he has intervened, in the same manner as such person.

Notwithstanding acceptance by intervention, the person in whose favour such acceptance has been given and his guarantors may require the holder of the bill, against payment of the sum specified in Article 370, to deliver up to them the bill, the deed of protest, and a receipted account if need be.

Payment by intervention may take place in all cases in which the holder of the bill has a right of recourse, whether at maturity or prior thereto. The payment must cover the whole amount payable by the person for whose account it is made.

Such payment must take place at the latest on the day following the last day allowed for drawing up the protest for non-payment.

If the bill has been accepted by interveners who are domiciled at the place of payment, or if persons domiciled at that place have been designated on the bill to pay it in case of need, the holder of the bill must present it to all such persons and, if need be, cause a protest for non-payment to be drawn up on the day following the last day allowed for the protest, which is the latest time limit.

In default of protest within this time limit, the party who designated the person to pay in case of need, or the party in whose favour the bill has been accepted, and the subsequent endorsers shall be discharged from their obligation.
The holder of the bill who refuses payment by intervention shall lose his right of recourse against those persons who would have been discharged thereby.

Payment by intervention must be evidenced by a receipt placed on the bill of exchange specifying the person for whose honour payment is made, and failing such specification, payment shall be deemed to have been made for the honour of the drawer.

The bill of exchange and the deed of protest, if a protest has been made, must be delivered to the person paying by intervention.

A person who pays by intervention acquires the rights arising out of the bill of exchange against the person for whose account payment was made and against those who are liable to the latter under the bill, provided that he may not endorse the bill anew.

Endorsers subsequent to the signatory for whose honour payment was made are discharged.

Where several persons offer to pay by intervention, preference shall be given to the one whose payment effects the widest discharge.

Any person who, with knowledge of the facts, intervenes contrary to this rule loses his right of recourse against those who would have been discharged by the wider payment.

A bill of exchange may be drawn in several identical parts.

These parts must be numbered in the body of the instrument itself, failing which each of them is deemed to be a separate bill of exchange.

Every holder of a bill which does not specify that it has been drawn in a single part may, at his own expense, require the delivery of several parts thereof.

For this purpose, he must address himself to his immediate endorser, who is bound to lend his assistance in proceeding against his own endorser, and so on up to the drawer, and the endorsers are bound to reproduce their endorsements on the new parts.

Payment made on one of the parts operates as a discharge, even though there is no stipulation that such payment annuls the effect of the other parts, provided that the drawee remains liable on each accepted part of which he has not obtained the return.

An endorser who has transferred the parts to different persons, as well as subsequent endorsers, are liable on all the parts bearing their signatures which have not been returned.

A person who has sent one of the parts for acceptance must indicate on the other parts the name of the person in whose hands this part is to be found, and the latter is bound to deliver it up to the lawful holder of another part, and if he refuses to deliver it up, the holder cannot exercise his right of action until he has established by a protest:

First - That the part sent has not been delivered up to him on his demand.

Second - That acceptance or payment could not be obtained on another part.

Every holder of a bill of exchange has the right to make copies thereof.

The copy must reproduce accurately all the entries of the original instrument with the endorsements and all other statements placed thereon, and must specify the limit at which it ends.

The copy may be endorsed and guaranteed in the same manner as the original instrument, and shall have the same effects.

The copy must state the custodian of the original instrument, and the custodian shall be bound to deliver the said instrument to the lawful holder of the copy.

If he refuses, the holder of the copy may not bring an action against its endorsers or guarantors by aval until he has established by a protest that the original instrument was not delivered to him upon his request.

Where the original instrument, after the last endorsement made before the making of the copy, contains the clause "henceforth an endorsement is only valid if made on the copy" or any other equivalent formula, a subsequent endorsement on the original instrument shall be null and void.

In case of alteration of the text of a bill of exchange, the persons who sign subsequent to the alteration shall be bound according to the terms of the altered text, and the persons who signed previously shall be bound according to the terms of the original text.

All rights of action arising out of a bill of exchange against the acceptor shall be barred after three years, reckoned from the date of maturity.

The rights of action of the holder of the instrument against the endorsers and against the drawer shall be barred after one year from the date of the protest drawn up within proper time, or from the date of maturity where there is a stipulation "return without costs".

The rights of action of endorsers against each other and against the drawer shall be barred after six months, reckoned from the day on which the endorser paid the amount of the instrument or from the day on which an action was brought against him.

In the event of an action being brought, the period of limitation shall run only from the day of the last judicial proceeding, and limitation shall not apply if judgment has been pronounced or if the debt has been acknowledged by a separate deed.

Interruption of limitation shall only have effect against the person in respect of whom the interrupting act was performed.

Nevertheless, the alleged debtors shall be bound, if so required, to affirm on oath that they are discharged from the debt, and their heirs or successors in title shall be bound to affirm on oath that they believe in good faith that the debt has been paid in full.

Payment of a bill of exchange of which the maturity falls on a legal holiday cannot be demanded until the first following working day.

Likewise, all proceedings relating to a bill of exchange, and in particular presentment for acceptance and protest, can only be made on working days.

Where any of these proceedings must be carried out within a time limit the last day of which is a legal holiday, the time limit shall be extended until the first following working day.

Intermediate holidays shall be included in the computation of the time limit.
Legal or contractual time limits shall not include the day on which the period begins to run.
Neither legally nor judicially is it permissible to grant a grace period of a single day for payment, except in the cases provided for in Articles 365 and 376.

A promissory note contains:

1 - The order clause or the mention of "promissory note" in the body of the instrument itself in the language used to write it.

2 - An unconditional promise to pay a determinate sum.

3 - The designation of the time of maturity.

4 - The designation of the place where payment must be effected.

5 - The name of the person to whom or to whose order payment must be made.

6 - The designation of the date and the place where the instrument is signed.

7 - The signature of the person issuing the instrument (the maker).

An instrument in which one of the particulars set forth in the preceding Article is lacking shall not be deemed a "promissory note", except in the cases mentioned in the following paragraphs:

- A promissory note in which the date of maturity is not designated shall be deemed payable at sight.

- In the absence of a special designation in the instrument, the place where the instrument is drawn up shall be deemed to be the place of payment and, at the same time, the place of domicile of the maker.

- A promissory note in which the place where it was drawn up is not designated shall be deemed to have been written at the place indicated beside the name of the maker.

The provisions relating to a bill of exchange and concerning the following matters shall apply to a promissory note in so far as they are not inconsistent with its nature:

- Endorsement (Article 325 to 335).

- Maturity (Article 348 to 352).

- Payment (Article 353 to 364).

- Recourse for non-payment (Article 365 to 372 and 374 to 376).

- Protest (Article 377 and 380).

- Re-exchange (Article 381 and 382).

- Payment by intervention (Article 387 to 391).

- Copies (Article 395 and 396).

- Alterations (Article 397).

- Prescription (Article 398 and 399).

- Holidays, computation of time limits and prohibition of days of grace (Article 400 to 402).

There shall also apply to a promissory note the provisions relating to a bill of exchange payable at the address of a third party or in a locality other than that of the domicile of

the drawee (Article 317 and Article 342), the provisions relating to the participation of interest (Article 318) and to discrepancies in the texts concerning

the sum payable (Article 319), the provisions relating to the consequences of affixing a signature in the manner set forth in Article 320, and to the consequences of the signature of a person who acts without authority or who exceeds the limits of his authority (Article 321).

There shall also apply to a promissory note the provisions relating to guarantee by aval (Article 345 and Article 347).

In the case provided for in the last paragraph of Article 346, if the guarantee by aval does not specify on whose behalf it has been given, it shall be deemed to have been given on behalf of the maker of the promissory note.

The maker of a promissory note is bound in the same manner as the acceptor of a bill of exchange.

Promissory notes payable at a certain period after sight must be presented for visa by the maker within the time limits fixed in Article 338.

The period after sight runs from the date of the visa signed by the maker on the note.

If the maker refuses to affix a dated visa, such refusal must be established by a protest (Article 340). The date of the protest shall mark the commencement of the period after sight.

A cheque shall contain:

1 - The term "cheque" inserted in the body of the instrument itself and expressed in the language employed for drawing up the instrument.

2 - An unconditional mandate to pay a determinate sum of money.

3 - The name of the person who is to pay (the drawee).

4 - A statement of the place where payment is to be effected.

5 - A statement of the date and of the place where the cheque is drawn.

6 - The signature of the person who issues the cheque (the drawer).

An instrument in which any of the particulars specified in the preceding Article is wanting is invalid as a cheque, except in the cases specified in the following paragraphs:

In the absence of a special Designation, the place specified beside the name of the drawee is deemed to be the place of payment, and if several places are specified beside the name of the drawee, the cheque is payable at the first place specified.

In the absence of these statements or any other indication, the cheque is payable at the place where the drawee has his principal establishment.

A cheque which does not specify the place at which it was drawn is deemed to have been drawn in the place specified beside the name of the drawer.

A cheque may only be drawn on a banker holding, at the time of the creation of the instrument, funds at the disposal of the drawer and in conformity with an express or implied agreement whereby the drawer has the right to dispose of those funds by cheque.

A cheque cannot be accepted. A statement of acceptance on a cheque shall be deemed unwritten.

Nevertheless, the drawee may certify the cheque, and the effect of such certification shall be to establish the existence of cover at the date of the issue of the cheque.

A cheque may be made payable:

- To a specified person with or without the express clause "to order".

- To a specified person, with the clause "not to order" or an equivalent clause.

- To the bearer of the instrument.

A cheque drawn in favour of a specified person with the words - "or to bearer" or any equivalent term is deemed to be a cheque to bearer.

A cheque which does not specify the name of the payee is deemed to be a cheque to bearer.

An endorsement placed on a cheque to bearer renders the endorser liable in accordance with the provisions governing rights of recourse, and does not have the effect of converting the instrument into a cheque "to order".

Where a cheque "to order" has been dispossessed from the hands of any person by any event whatsoever, the person entitled to this cheque who establishes his right in the manner set forth in Article 421 shall not be bound to give it up unless he has acquired it in bad faith or has committed gross negligence in acquiring it.

An endorsement made after protest or after the expiry of the time-limit for presentment produces only the effects of an ordinary assignment.

An undated endorsement is deemed to have been placed before protest or before the expiry of the time-limit referred to in the preceding paragraph, unless proof to the contrary is adduced.
A cheque is payable at sight. Any stipulation to the contrary is deemed unwritten. A cheque presented for payment before the day stated as the date of issue is payable on the day of presentment.

A cheque which is issued in Lebanon and is payable therein must be presented for payment within a time-limit of eight days.

A cheque which is issued outside Lebanon and is payable therein must be presented within a time-limit of twenty days if the place of its issue is in a country bordering on Lebanon or on Syria, or in Europe, or in a country situated on the shore of the Mediterranean Sea.

The time-limit shall be seventy days if the cheque is issued in any other country.

Where a cheque payable in Lebanon is issued in a country in which a calendar other than the Gregorian calendar is in force, the day of issue shall be reduced to the corresponding day of the Gregorian calendar.

The drawee must pay even after the expiry of the time-limit for presentment.

Opposition to the payment of a cheque by the drawer is not admissible except in the case of its loss or in the case of the bankruptcy of its holder.

If the drawer enters an opposition on other grounds notwithstanding this prohibition, the judge of urgent matters must, upon the application of the holder, order the lifting of this opposition, even if an action has been brought on the merits.
Neither the death of the drawer nor his loss of capacity occurring after the issue of the cheque shall affect its effects.

A cheque may be made to the order of the drawer himself.

A cheque may also be drawn for the benefit of a third party.

A cheque cannot be drawn on the drawer himself except when it is drawn between different establishments of the same drawer and provided that such cheque is not to bearer.
Every stipulation for interest inserted in the cheque is deemed unwritten.
A cheque may be payable at the domicile of a third party, whether in the locality where the drawee has his domicile or in another locality, provided, however, that the third party is a banker.
The drawer is a guarantor of payment; every clause whereby the drawer releases himself from this guarantee is deemed unwritten.

A cheque stipulated to be payable to a named person, with or without an express "to order" clause, is transferable by means of endorsement.

Whereas a cheque stipulated to be payable to a named person with the clause "not to order" or an equivalent clause is transferable only in the form and with the effects of an ordinary assignment.
An endorsement may be made for the benefit of the drawer himself or of any other person bound thereon, and these persons may endorse the cheque anew.

An endorsement must be unconditional. Every condition to which the endorsement is made subject is deemed unwritten.

A partial endorsement is null and void.

An endorsement by the drawee is equally null and void.

An endorsement to bearer is equivalent to an endorsement in blank.

An endorsement to the drawee only avails as a receipt, except in the case where the drawee has several establishments and the endorsement is made for the benefit of an establishment other than that on which the cheque has been drawn.

The possessor of an endorsable cheque is deemed the lawful holder thereof if he establishes his title by an uninterrupted series of endorsements, even if the last endorsement is in blank. Crossed-out endorsements are in this respect deemed unwritten. Where an endorsement in blank is followed by another endorsement, the signatory of this endorsement is deemed to have acquired the cheque by the endorsement in blank.

The drawer and the holder of a cheque may prohibit its payment in cash by writing transversely on the reverse thereof the following words: "for credit in account" or words of similar import.

In this case, the cheque may only be settled by the drawee by means of book-entry (credit in account, transfer or clearing), and settlement by book-entry shall constitute payment. Any striking out of the words "for credit in account" shall be deemed null and void.

A drawee who contravenes the foregoing provisions shall be liable for damages up to the amount of the cheque.

The holder of the instrument may exercise his right of recourse against the endorsers, the drawer and the other liable parties if the cheque, presented in due time, is not paid and if the refusal to pay is evidenced:

1 - either by an authentic instrument (protest).

2 - or by a declaration from the drawee, written and dated on the cheque and specifying the day of presentment.

The protest or equivalent certification must be made before the expiration of the time limit fixed for presentment.

If presentment takes place on the last day of the time limit, the protest or equivalent certification may be made on the first following working day.

The holder of the cheque may claim from the party against whom he exercises his right of recourse:

1 - the amount of the unpaid cheque.

2 - interest as from the day of presentment calculated at the legal rate for cheques issued and payable in Lebanon and at the rate of six per cent for other cheques.

3 - the expenses of the protest or equivalent certification, the expenses of the notices given and the other expenses.

A party who has paid the cheque may claim from his guarantors:

1 - the entire sum which he has paid.

2 - interest on the said sum as from the day on which he paid it, calculated at the legal rate for cheques issued and payable in Lebanon and at the rate of six per cent for other cheques.

3 - the expenses which he has incurred.

The drawee shall be entitled to demand, upon payment of the cheque, that the holder deliver to him a receipted instrument, and the holder may not refuse partial payment.

Where the cover is less than the value of the cheque, the holder shall be entitled to insist upon payment to the extent of the cover. In the case of partial payment, the drawee shall be entitled to demand that such payment be mentioned on the cheque and that a receipt for it be delivered to him.

Partial payments out of the principal value of the cheque shall discharge the drawer and the endorsers. The holder of the cheque must draw up a protest for the balance.

Whoever pays a cheque which is not subject to an objection shall be legally deemed discharged.

The drawee who pays an endorsable cheque shall be bound to verify the regularity of the chain of endorsements, and shall not be bound to verify the signatures of the endorsers.

Where a cheque is stipulated to be payable in a currency which is not in circulation in Lebanon, the sum may be paid, within the time limit for presentment of the cheque, in Lebanese pounds equivalent to its value on the day of payment. Where payment is not effected upon presentment, the holder of the instrument shall have the option to demand payment of the value of the cheque in Lebanese currency according to the rate current on the day of presentment or on the day of payment.

Lebanese custom must be followed in determining the rate of any foreign currency in which the cheque is drawn, for the purpose of fixing its value in Lebanese pounds. However, the drawer may stipulate that the value due to be paid be calculated at a rate specified in the cheque.

The aforementioned rules shall not apply where the drawer stipulates payment in a specified currency (a stipulation of effective payment in foreign currency).

The drawer or the holder of a cheque may cross it, and it shall have the effects set forth in the following Article:

Crossing shall be effected by placing two parallel lines on the back of the cheque, and

the crossing shall be general or special. It is general if there is no designation at all between the two lines, or the word "banker" or an equivalent term. It is special if the name of a banker is written between the two lines.

A general crossing may be converted into a special crossing. However, a special crossing may not be converted into a general crossing. The erasure of the crossing or of the name of the banker shall be deemed null and void.

The drawee may not pay a cheque with a general crossing except to one of his customers or to a banker.

The drawee may not pay a cheque with a special crossing except to the designated banker. Where the designated banker is the drawee, it may not be paid except to one of his customers. However, the designated banker may have recourse to another banker for collection.

A banker may not acquire a crossed cheque except from one of his customers or from another banker, and may not collect it for the account of persons other than these.

The drawee or banker who contravenes the foregoing provisions shall be liable for the damage up to the value of the cheque.

Where the presentment of the cheque or the drawing up of the protest or the equivalent verification within the prescribed time-limits is prevented by an insurmountable obstacle (a legal provision or other case of force majeure), these time-limits shall be extended.

The holder of the instrument is bound to give notice without delay of the case of force majeure to his endorser and to enter this notice, dated and signed by him, on the cheque or on an allonge, and as to the remainder, the provisions of Article 367 shall apply to the remaining formalities.

When force majeure has terminated, the holder of the cheque must without delay present it for payment and, if need be, draw up the protest or the equivalent verification.

If force majeure continues to operate beyond fifteen days from the date on which the holder of the instrument has, even before the expiration of the time-limit for presentment, given notice of force majeure to his endorser, recourse may be exercised without presentment of the instrument or the drawing up of the protest or the equivalent verification being necessary.

Facts which are purely personal to the holder of the cheque or to the person whom he has entrusted with the presentment of the cheque or with the drawing up of the protest or the equivalent verification shall not be deemed to constitute cases of force majeure.

With the exception of bearer cheques, any cheque issued in one country and payable in another country or in a part beyond the seas of the same country and vice versa, or issued and payable in the same part or in different parts beyond the seas of the same country, may be drawn in a set of identical parts.

When a cheque is drawn in a set of parts, the number of each part must be stated in the body of the cheque itself, failing which each part is deemed to be a separate cheque.

The holder of a cheque's right of recourse against the endorsers, the drawer and the other parties liable is barred after six months from the expiration of the time-limit for presentment.

The right of recourse of the different parties liable for the payment of a cheque against one another is barred after six months from the day on which the party liable has paid the amount of the cheque or the day on which he was sued thereon.

However, in the event of forfeiture or limitation, the right of action shall subsist against the drawer who has not provided cover or against the other parties liable who have made an unjust enrichment.

The holder of a cheque's right of action against the drawee is barred after three years from the expiration of the time-limit for presentment.

The presentment of a cheque or the drawing up of a protest may only be effected on a business day.

Where the last day of the time limit granted by the law for performing acts relating to the cheque, in particular for presenting it and drawing up the protest or an equivalent instrument, falls on an official holiday, the time limit shall be extended until the first business day following its expiration; however, holidays occurring during the running of the time limit shall be included in its calculation.

Discharge by delivery of a cheque accepted by the creditor shall not constitute a novation of the debt contract; rather, the original debt shall remain in existence with all the guarantees pertaining thereto until the said cheque has been paid.

Independently of the formalities prescribed for the exercise of the action in warranty, the holder of a cheque in respect of which a protest has been drawn up may, after obtaining leave from the President of the Execution Department, levy a conservatory attachment upon the movable property of the drawer and the endorsers without being required to furnish security.

Whoever issues a cheque without indicating therein the place of issue or the date, or places an untrue date thereon, shall be liable to a fine of six per cent of the amount of the cheque.

Such fine shall not be less than five Lebanese pounds.

The same fine shall be payable without recourse by the first endorser or the holder of the cheque personally if it lacks the indication of the place of issue or of the date, or if it bears a date subsequent to the date of its endorsement or of its presentment; and this fine shall also be payable by anyone who pays or receives by way of set-off a cheque that does not contain the place of issue or the date.

Every banker holding cover who delivers to his creditor blank cheque forms payable at the cashier's desk of the bank shall be bound to mention on each form the name of the person to whom such form has been delivered, failing which he shall be liable to a fine of one Lebanese pound for each contravention.

Every bank must print on the cover of the chequebooks which it delivers to its customers the text of Article 666 of the Penal Code, failing which it shall be liable to a fine of ten pounds for each contravention.
The offence of drawing a cheque without cover is punishable under Article 666 of the Penal Code.
A drawee who knowingly declares the existence of a cover that is less than the existing cover shall be liable to a fine of twenty-five to five hundred Lebanese pounds.

The assignment of a registered security is effected by a declaration of transfer recorded in the registers and signed by the assignor or his proxy.

Prior to registering the assignment, the debtor institution is entitled to require the declarant to prove his identity and capacity. Such assignment confers upon the new owner whose name is registered a personal and direct right.

The debtor institution may not raise against him any defence pertaining to the previous owners of the security.
Registered securities may include detachable coupons conferring upon their bearer the right to collect maturities, distributions and interest (and are called mixed securities).

Transferable securities issued to order are transferred by way of endorsement. Their endorsement is subject to the same rules as those governing the endorsement of bills of exchange, unless there are contrary provisions arising from laws and regulations or from the nature of the security itself.

Global Depositary Receipts

Global depositary receipts are negotiable registered instruments linked to registered shares (the underlying shares) of a Lebanese joint-stock company, issued abroad by an issuer licensed in the country of issue and listed on regulated financial markets.

Furthermore, in addition to the foregoing, the following articles of this Law shall apply to the cheque in so far as their provisions do not conflict with the nature of this instrument:

From Article 319 to 321, from 327 to 329, 331, 332, 335, 345 to 347, the second paragraph of Article 353, 359, 361 to 364, 367 to 369, 372, 377, 393, 397, 399, 401 and 402.

The protest provided for in Article 362 must be drawn up at the latest on the first working day following the expiration of the time limit fixed for the presentment of the cheque.

Every instrument whereby its signatory undertakes to deliver a sum of money or a quantity of fungibles at a specified place and time, may be transferred by way of endorsement if it is expressly drawn up with an order clause.

The endorsement shall be subject to the provisions of Article 325 and following relating to the endorsement of bills of exchange, unless there are contrary provisions in the law or in the instrument itself. The debtor may not set up defences other than those arising from the instrument itself and those which he holds directly against the claimant, unless the claimant is acting in bad faith.

He shall not be compelled to make payment except against delivery of the instrument to order bearing a receipt in due form.

Where a bill of exchange or a promissory note or any other endorsable instrument is delivered by way of payment of a debt, this shall not be deemed a novation of the contract unless the intention of the two parties indicates the contrary.

Shares, debentures, income certificates and other negotiable instruments issued in bulk which confer the right to equal values of money and may be quoted on a financial market, may be registered, to bearer, or to order.

Where the instrument is drawn up to bearer, its transfer is effected by mere delivery. Every holder of such instrument shall be deemed qualified to exercise the rights pertaining thereto, and so long as the debtor has not received a legal opposition, his payment to the bearer of the instrument shall validly discharge him in due form.

The debtor may not set up against the bearer of the instrument any defences other than those based on the nullity of the instrument or arising from the text of the instrument itself.

Where the instrument is registered, the right of its owner shall be established by effecting a registration in his name in the registers of the institution which issued the instrument. Ownership of this instrument arises from such registration.

Subject in full to the regulatory provisions relating to global depositary receipts linked to bank shares, the company shall verify under its responsibility, upon issuing global depositary receipts linked to its shares, that the following conditions are met:

1 - A bank or financial institution abroad issues the global depositary receipts after receiving proof that the underlying shares have been deposited for safekeeping with the Central Depository and Clearing House for Financial Instruments for Lebanon and the Middle East (Midclear) established pursuant to Law No. 139 dated 26/11/1999 .

2 - The approval of the board of directors of the company issuing the underlying shares on the information contained in the subscription prospectus that may be prepared for this issue.

3 - The issuance of global depositary receipts either:

a - Pursuant to the provisions of a contract signed between the bank or financial institution either of which intends to issue global depositary receipts and the company issuing the underlying shares in exchange for shares that it owns of their two shares or in exchange for shares owned by some of the company's shareholders in the issuing company Sponsored DRS.

b - Against a letter of no objection from the company issuing the underlying shares in the absence of a contract in accordance with what is referred to in Paragraph (a) of this Item (3) (Unsponsored DRs ). And the Midclear company shall, in this case, and on the basis of the information that may be available to it, also verify that the conditions of this Article are fulfilled upon the issuance of global depositary receipts.

4 - The permissibility of granting the holders of global depositary receipts the right to exchange them for a number of underlying shares, provided that this does not conflict with legal or regulatory provisions, especially those restricting the ownership of the underlying shares to Lebanese persons.

5 - Keeping the underlying shares in the possession of the Central Depository and Clearing House for Financial Instruments for Lebanon and the Middle East (Midclear) until the value of the global depositary receipts is paid in whole or in part, or until they are exchanged for the corresponding underlying shares in whole or in part, or until the dissolution and liquidation of the company issuing the underlying shares.

6 - The possibility of granting the issuer of global depositary receipts the right to attend the general meetings of the company issuing the underlying shares and the right to participate in voting, provided that:

a - This right does not conflict with legal or regulatory provisions, especially those restricting the ownership of the underlying shares to Lebanese persons.

b - The issuer of the global depositary receipts votes in the sessions of the general meetings in accordance with the instructions of the holders of these receipts, if the contract or the rules of issuance of these receipts permit this and determine the conditions and manner of exercising voting rights; otherwise, the issuer of the global depositary receipts shall vote in accordance with what is required by the interest of the company issuing the underlying shares.

7 - The number of shares represented by global depositary receipts does not exceed 30% of the number of shares constituting the capital of the company issuing the underlying shares and whose price is paid in full.

Upon the dissolution and liquidation of the company issuing the underlying shares, the holders of global depositary receipts shall be entitled to all the rights pertaining to the underlying shares, subject to the provisions of the Law put into force by Decree No. 10845 dated 10/9/1968 relating to the acquisition by non-Lebanese of real property rights in Lebanon.

Every merchant shall be entitled, prior to his cessation of payments or within the ten days following such cessation, to apply to the Court of First Instance sitting in the district in which his principal establishment is located and request it to convene his creditors in order to propose to them a preventive composition.

And the merchant shall submit in support of this application: his mandatory commercial books kept in due form for at least three years, or from the commencement of the period of his practice of commerce if it is less than three years, and he shall also submit a document proving his registration in the Commercial Register, a detailed and estimated statement of his business, and a statement of the names of all his creditors indicating the amount of the debt of each of them and his place of residence. Where the matter concerns a company, the documents proving its incorporation in due form shall be produced.

And the merchant shall explain the reasons that led him to apply for the composition, and shall indicate the rate of distribution which he intends to propose to his creditors or the reasons preventing the immediate disclosure of his proposals, and shall also specify the real or personal guarantees which he offers to his creditors.

In all cases, the proposed rate may not be less than 50 % of the principal of his ordinary debts if the term of payment is one year, nor may it be less than 75 % if the term is eighteen months, nor less than 100 % if the term is three years.

The Court shall, after hearing the Public Prosecution, decide in council chamber to dismiss the application:

First - If the application has not deposited the books and documents set out in the preceding Article.

Second - If he has previously been convicted of fraudulent bankruptcy, forgery, theft, breach of trust, fraud, or embezzlement in the administration of public funds, or if he has failed to perform what he undertook in a previous preventive composition, or if he was previously declared bankrupt and did not pay the debts of all his creditors in full or did not perform the obligations of the composition in their entirety.

Third - If he fails to provide sufficient guarantees to effect the distribution of the proposed rate.

Fourth - If he has absconded after closing all his establishments, or if he has misappropriated or fraudulently diminished a part of his estate. In all such cases, if the merchant has ceased payment of his commercial debts, the Court shall of its own motion decide to declare him bankrupt.

If the court considers that the petition is lawful and admissible, it shall order, pursuant to a decision not subject to appeal, the convocation of the creditors to appear before a delegated judge to discuss and deliberate upon the proposal for preventive composition.

This judge shall appoint the place, date and hour of the meeting within thirty days at the most starting from the date of the court's decision, and shall also appoint the time-limit within which this decision must be published and notified to the creditors.

He shall also appoint a commissioner from outside the creditors whose duty in the meantime shall be to supervise the management of the commercial enterprise, verify the debts owed to it and by it, and conduct an investigation into the manner of the debtor's conduct, and he shall then submit a report to the assembly of creditors in this regard.

He must appoint a time-limit for the petitioner not exceeding five days to complete the nominal statement containing the names of his creditors when the merchant establishes in his petition his inability to submit this statement in full forthwith.

Upon the request of the delegated judge, reference to the court's decision shall be made by an endorsement signed by the judge and the clerk and entered at the end of the entries recorded in the merchant's books, and his books shall then be returned to him.

The court's decision shall be published through the care of the clerk by means of notices affixed to the door of the court, and an abstract of the decision shall then be inserted in one of the newspapers of judicial notices and registered in the Commercial Register, all within a time-limit appointed in the decision itself. If the statement of the creditors' names is incomplete or if it is found necessary to expand the publication, the court shall have the right to designate other newspapers, even if foreign, for the publication of the notices.

The clerk must notify each of the creditors, by means of a registered letter or a telegram, according to the distance, of a notice stating the name of the debtor, the name of the delegated judge, the name of the supervisor, the date of the decision concerning the convocation of the creditors, and the place and date of the meeting, together with a brief statement of the debtor's proposals.

The documents proving that publication and notification to the creditors have taken place must be joined to the file.

From the date of filing the petition until the decision homologating the composition acquires the force of res judicata, no creditor holding a title prior to the date of the decision shall be entitled to initiate or continue enforcement proceedings, or to acquire any right of priority over the debtor's property, or to register a mortgage, and if he does so, his act shall be null and void.

The time limits relating to prescription and to the lapse of actions and rights which had been interrupted as a result of the acts set forth above shall remain suspended.

Ordinary debts which carry no priority shall be deemed due and payable, and their interest shall cease to run as against the creditors only.

However, sums due by way of taxes, even if privileged, shall not be subject to the effects provided for in this Article.

During the preventive composition proceedings, the debtor shall remain in charge of administering his property and shall continue to perform all ordinary acts pertaining to his trade under the supervision of the commissioner and the direction of the delegated judge. Both of these persons shall be entitled to inspect the commercial books at any time.

Gifts and other gratuitous acts or acts of suretyship performed by the debtor during the preventive composition proceedings may not be invoked against the creditors.

The same rule shall apply if the debtor performs acts to borrow money, even if the borrowing is in the form of bills of exchange, or concludes a compromise or arbitration, or effects sales unrelated to the exercise of his trade, or establishes a mortgage or a security without authorisation from the delegated judge. The judge shall not be entitled to authorise them unless their benefit is clear and evident.

If the debtor violates the provisions of the two preceding Articles, or if it is established that he concealed part of his assets or fraudulently omitted to mention certain creditors, or if he generally committed any fraud, the delegated judge shall refer the matter to the council chamber of the court, which shall declare the bankruptcy.

This shall not preclude the criminal penalties to which the merchant has rendered himself liable.

The supervisor, after inspecting the debtor's books and instruments, and on the basis of the information he has been able to gather, shall verify the accuracy of the statement of creditors and debtors, make all necessary amendments thereto, and set out the sums due to or by the debtor. He shall be entitled, where necessary, to request the necessary explanations from the interested parties.

He shall then draw up without delay a detailed report on the debtor's commercial situation and on his conduct, and shall file this report with the court registry at least three days before the date fixed for the composition meeting.

Neither the debts of the spouse of the debtor nor the debts of his relatives by blood and by marriage up to the fourth degree shall be included in the calculation of the majority set forth in the preceding article. Persons who have acquired these debts by way of assignment or auction during the year preceding the application for the composition shall also be deprived of voting.

An assignment of debts, if it occurs after the decision concerning the summoning of the creditors, shall not confer the right to vote in the conclusion of the composition.

The delegated judge must mention in the minutes those who have accepted the composition, and all of them must sign the minutes.

Those who have expressed their acceptance by a letter or telegram to the delegated judge or to the clerk within the five days following the closure of the minutes of the meeting shall be included in the calculation of the majority.

The clerk shall record this acceptance in the margin of the minutes and annex it thereto.

Before the affixing of the signatures, the delegated judge shall take a decision which he shall insert in the minutes, whereby he summons the interested parties to attend a specified hearing before the court for the homologation of the composition within a time limit not exceeding twenty days.

The supervisor must lodge with the court registry, three days before the hearing appointed for the homologation, his reasoned submissions regarding the possibility of admitting the composition.

At the hearing, the delegated judge shall submit a report, and the debtor and the creditors shall have the right to intervene in the deliberation.

The court may summon the supervisor to the deliberation chamber for clarification after sending notice to the debtor, the creditors and the interveners.

In the decision of homologation, the court shall have the right to assess provisionally and on the basis of presumptions the importance of the declared debts and their amounts in order to ascertain the existence of the required majority, subject to any final judgments that may subsequently be rendered.

If the court considers that the debtor deserves to benefit from the composition, that the objections set forth in the preceding articles do not eliminate the required majority, and that the proposals for the composition are not less than the legal minimum, and that they are lawful and their performance is guaranteed, it shall decide to homologate the requested composition.

In the same decision, the court shall order the deposit of the distribution dividends pertaining to the declared debts. However, if the homologation of the composition is refused, the court shall declare the bankruptcy of its own motion.

The delegated judge shall preside over the meeting of creditors.

Every creditor is entitled to appoint on his behalf a special proxy bearing a written power of attorney, and this power of attorney may be written without any formality on the letter of invitation or the telegram.

The debtor or his legal representative must attend in person, and representation through a special proxy shall not be accepted unless the attendance of the debtor is absolutely impossible and the delegated judge has verified that.

After the reading of the supervisor's report, the debtor shall submit his final proposals.

If it is not possible to complete all the proceedings on the appointed day, their continuation shall be deemed adjourned ipso jure to the nearest following working day, without the need to notify the creditors anew, even those absent among them.

The matter shall proceed in this manner until the proceedings are completed.

Each of the creditors may set forth the reasons for which he believes that this or that debt is doubtful, or that the debtor is not worthy of the indulgence which he solicits, or that his proposals are not worthy of acceptance.

And the creditor may give his answer, and he must provide all the explanations that are requested of him.

Then a summary of all these matters shall be recorded in the minutes and all the documents shall be annexed thereto.

The preventive composition must be approved by a majority of the creditors who participated in the voting, and this majority must represent at least three-quarters of the debts that are neither privileged nor secured by a movable or immovable pledge.

However, creditors holding a privilege or real or non-real pledges may participate in forming this majority, provided that they waive their right to exercise the security granted to them.

This waiver may be limited to a portion of the debt and its accessories, provided that the waived portion is specified and is not less than one-third of the total debt.

However, participation in the voting without a declaration of partial waiver, and subsequent acceptance of the composition which will be discussed hereinafter, necessarily entails the waiver of the security of the entire debt.

The court shall, in the decision of homologation, calculate the increase that may occur in the debtor's assets following this voting and this acceptance.

The effects of the waiver of a privilege or of a real or non-real pledge, even if such waiver is partial, shall necessarily lapse if the composition is not concluded or if its annulment is decided.

In the absence of an agreement to the contrary included in the composition deed or in another resolution adopted in accordance with the conditions set forth above and confirmed by the court, the debtor shall not be entitled, before performing all the obligations he undertook in the composition deed, to sell or mortgage his immovable properties or to establish security rights, and in general he shall not be entitled to dispose of a part of his assets in a manner other than that required by the nature of his trade or industry.

Every act he performs in violation of this prohibition shall be without effect towards the creditors prior to the confirmation of the composition.
Judgments granting or refusing the confirmation of the composition must be published in accordance with the rules that shall be determined hereinafter for the judgment declaring bankruptcy.

Dissenting creditors shall be entitled to file an opposition against the confirmation of the composition within five days from the date of the closing of the final minutes, and such opposition must contain the grounds and be served upon the debtor and the supervisor.

An appeal shall only be admissible from the debtor himself or from the opposing creditors.

The time limit for appeal shall be fifteen days.

When the decision confirming the composition becomes final, the function of the supervisor shall ipso facto cease, unless there is an express provision in the composition deed entrusting him with supervising its execution. The expenses and sums due to the supervisor shall be determined by the delegated judge. Every agreement to the contrary shall be null and void.

The confirmation of the preventive composition shall render it binding upon all creditors.

The creditors, even those among them who voluntarily agreed to the composition deed, shall retain in full all their rights against the debtor's co-debtors, his guarantors, and those to whom the debtor has assigned. However, the latter shall be entitled to intervene in the deliberation to submit their observations regarding the composition.
A composition granted to a company shall benefit the partners who are personally liable for the debts of the company, unless there is a provision to the contrary.

In every commercial company that has issued debentures the value of which exceeds twenty per cent of the total debts owed by it, a composition may not be granted unless the general meeting of debenture holders approves the proposals by a resolution adopted in accordance with the conditions of quorum and majority prescribed in the Title on joint-stock companies.

The approval of the general meeting of debenture holders shall be mandatory whatever the ratio between the amount of the debt arising from the debentures and the total general debt if the composition deed contains special conditions inconsistent with the conditions fixed upon the issue of the debentures with respect to their holders.
Whenever there is an interest in convening the general meeting of debenture holders, the time limit previously fixed for summoning the creditors may be extended to sixty days.

Holders of bonds for which the payment of a premium upon redemption is stipulated shall not be limited to claiming the issue price, but shall add thereto the portion of the premium to which they have become entitled for the elapsed period.

Upon the application of any creditor whomsoever within three years starting from the date of publication of the homologation decision, the court shall be entitled to annul the composition and to declare the bankruptcy of the debtor if it is established that he fraudulently exaggerated in determining the debts owed by him or concealed a substantial portion of his assets.

No other action for the annulment of the composition shall be entertained after its homologation.

If the annulment of the composition is decided, the guarantors who did not participate in the fraud shall be discharged from the obligations which they undertook in the composition agreement, and the real estate mortgages and other securities established in the same instrument shall lapse ipso jure.

If the debtor fails to perform all the obligations provided for in the composition agreement, every creditor shall be entitled, after pursuing the guarantors and invoking the rights granted by way of security, to request the rescission of the composition and the declaration of bankruptcy of the debtor.

It may be stipulated in the composition agreement that the merchant shall not be finally discharged from the remitted portion of his debt pursuant to this agreement unless he remains insolvent. However, the period of application of this condition must be fixed at five years, and it is also required that the value of the debtor's assets exceed the debts owed by him at a rate of at least twenty-five per cent.

Subject to the application of the provisions of the preceding Title, every merchant who ceases payment of his commercial debts, and every merchant who sustains financial confidence in himself only by means that clearly appear to be unlawful, shall be deemed to be in a state of bankruptcy.

Bankruptcy shall be declared pursuant to a judgment of the Court of First Instance in whose district the principal commercial establishment is located. This judgment shall be provisionally enforceable.

If several courts simultaneously rule to declare the bankruptcy of the same merchant, there shall be a stream for the designation of the competent authority.

The court referred to above shall be competent to hear all actions that may arise and whose origin lies in the rules pertaining to bankruptcy.

The case may be brought before the court by a declaration from the merchant himself, and he must make this declaration within twenty days from the date of his cessation of payments, failing which he shall be exposed to committing the misdemeanour of negligent bankruptcy, and he must deposit at the same time a detailed balance sheet certified as conforming to the state of his assets and the debts payable by him.

The case may also be brought before the court by a three-day summons lodged by one or more creditors.

In urgent cases, such as where the merchant closes his stores and absconds or conceals a significant portion of his assets, creditors shall be entitled to apply by way of petition without a summons, in which case the court shall decide the case in council chamber.

The court may order that the necessary conservatory measures be taken to safeguard the rights of the creditors upon the request of the Public Prosecution or of its own motion.

The court may, where necessary, also declare bankruptcy of its own motion.

A merchant who has retired from trade or died may be judicially declared bankrupt within a period of one year running from the date of his retirement from trade or from the date of his death if his cessation of payments preceded the retirement or the death.

However, the heirs of the deceased merchant may not request his bankruptcy.

The judgment declaring bankruptcy shall specify the time of cessation of payments.

The court may carry back the time of cessation of payments to an earlier date by virtue of a judgment amending the date or several judgments subsequently rendered by it on the basis of the report of the judge-commissary, or of its own motion, or upon the request of any interested party, in particular the request of the creditors, each of whom shall be entitled to apply separately.

This request may not be admitted after the expiry of the time limit provided for in Article 551, after the expiry of which the schedule of debts is finally closed. Upon the expiry of this time limit, the time appointed for the cessation of payments shall become irrevocably fixed with respect to the creditors.

The time of cessation of payments may not be carried back to more than eighteen months prior to the judgment declaring bankruptcy.

The judgment declaring bankruptcy and the judgments amending the date of cessation of payments must be posted within five days through the diligence of the trustees in bankruptcy in the hall of the court that rendered them and at the nearest stock exchange premises, and an extract thereof must also be published within the same time limit in a newspaper designated for legal notices.

This publication must take place in the locality where the bankruptcy was declared and in all other places where the bankrupt has commercial establishments.

At the same time, these judgments must be registered in the Commercial Register and notified to the Public Prosecution through the diligence of the clerk.

These judgments are subject to opposition and appeal, as well as all judgments issued in bankruptcy matters, unless there is a provision to the contrary in this Law.

The time limits for opposition shall equally be eight days and the time limits for appeal fifteen days commencing from the date of the judgments, provided that the time limits pertaining to judgments subject to the formalities of posting and publication of the extract in the newspapers shall commence from the day of completion of these formalities.

The Court of Appeal adjudicates submitted by the bankrupts, neither of which shall in any case have a suspensive effect.

If it appears incidentally to the court in the course of a civil, commercial, or criminal trial that the merchant is in a state of apparent bankruptcy, it shall be entitled, even if the bankruptcy has not been declared, to apply the fundamental provisions of bankruptcy as defined in this Book.

The names of merchants declared bankrupt who have not been rehabilitated shall be entered in a schedule posted on the door of every court and in the public hall of all stock exchanges.

The name of the merchant shall not be entered in the schedule if he was deceased at the time of the declaration of his bankruptcy; in all other cases, the name of the bankrupt merchant shall be struck off six months after his death.
Furthermore, the political rights of the bankrupt shall be forfeited. He may neither be an elector nor be elected to political or professional councils, nor may he perform a public office or mission.

A judgment declaring bankruptcy entails ipso jure, from the day of its issuance, the divestment of the bankrupt in favour of the bankruptcy trustees of the administration of all his property, including the property which he may acquire during the period of bankruptcy.

In particular, the bankrupt may not sell any of his property, nor is he entitled to make any payment or receive any payment unless the payment is made in good faith for a commercial bill, and he cannot contract or litigate before the courts except as an intervening party in actions pursued by the bankruptcy trustees.

However, he may perform all conservatory acts to preserve his rights.

However, this divestment does not include rights that pertain exclusively to the person of the bankrupt or to his capacity as head of a family, or rights that concern a purely moral interest.

Nevertheless, the intervention of the bankruptcy trustees in the case shall be admitted if it leads to a judgment for a sum of money.

Likewise, the divestment does not include property that the law has rendered unseizable, nor the profits that the bankrupt may earn through his activity or industry, to the extent considered by the bankruptcy judge to be proportionate to the needs of the bankrupt to support himself and his family.

The judgment declaring bankruptcy entails stopping ordinary creditors or those holding a general privilege from individual litigation, which, after the issuance of this judgment, shall be confined to the bankruptcy trustees without distinction between commercial debts and civil debts.

The judgment declaring bankruptcy stops, with regard to the body of creditors only, the running of interest on debts not secured by a privilege or by a real estate or non-real estate mortgage.

As for the interest on secured debts, it may only be claimed out of the principal of the funds resulting from the sale of the properties placed as security.

The judgment declaring bankruptcy causes the forfeiture of the term with regard to the bankrupt alone, excluding his co-obligors, even if that is in the interest of his creditors who have obtained security.

Holders of bonds coupled with a premium upon payment may produce them immediately in the bankruptcy, as provided in the chapter on preventive composition.

If the bankrupt is the owner of real estate properties or real rights in immovable property, the judgment declaring bankruptcy shall be subject to the rules of publication pertaining to real estate mortgages, and it shall be registered through the care of the bankruptcy trustees, giving rise, from the date of its registration, to a compulsory mortgage in favour of the body of creditors.

The following acts shall be void by operation of law with regard to the body of creditors if the debtor has performed them after the date of his cessation of payment as determined by the court or within the twenty days preceding this date:

First - Gratuitous acts and alienations, except for customary small gifts or the creation of a waqf.

Second - Payments prior to maturity, whatever their form.

Third - Payment of matured pecuniary debts otherwise than in cash, bills of exchange, promissory notes "to order" or assignments, and in general any payment by delivery of an equivalent.

Fourth - The establishment of a contractual or judicial real estate mortgage, a pledge of movables, or an antichresis over the debtor's property to secure a pre-existing debt.

If the payment by delivery of an equivalent takes place in the form of the alienation of real estate, the nullity shall have effect only towards the creditor who contracted with the bankrupt.

It shall not prejudice the rights of those who acquired ownership from this creditor for consideration, provided that they are in good faith.

Any other payment of matured debts performed by the debtor and any act carried out by him for consideration after his cessation of payment and before the judgment declaring bankruptcy may be annulled if the persons who received payment from the debtor or contracted with him had knowledge of his cessation of payment.

The annulment of the aforementioned acts shall, where necessary, give rise to an action for restitution.

Where that which was paid was a bill of exchange or a cheque, the said action may only be brought against the person for whose account the bill or the cheque was given; whereas if it was a promissory note "to order", the action may only be brought against the first endorser.

In both cases, proof must be established that the person from whom restitution is demanded had knowledge, at the time of the issuance of the instrument, of the debtor's cessation of payments.

The registration of a mortgage or pledge after the recording of the judgment declaring bankruptcy shall be void as against the body of creditors.

Registrations effected after the cessation of payments, or within the twenty days preceding it, shall be voidable if more than fifteen days have elapsed between the date of creation of the security and the date of registration, and if the delay has prejudiced the creditors.
The actions for annulment provided for in Articles 507, 508 and 510 shall be barred by prescription after eighteen months from the day of the declaration of bankruptcy.

The administration of the bankrupt's property shall be entrusted to a salaried agent called the bankruptcy trustee. The judgment declaring bankruptcy shall appoint one or more trustees for the bankruptcy.

The number of trustees may at any time be increased to three. Their expenses and remuneration shall be determined by a decision of the supervising judge in accordance with the tariff annexed to Legislative Decree No. 79/L dated 13 March 1933, and the debtor and the creditors shall be entitled to object to the decision on expenses within eight days, and the court shall adjudicate upon the objection in council chamber.
One or two controllers from among the creditors who nominate themselves for this function may at any time be appointed by a decision of the supervising judge.
No relative by blood or marriage of the bankrupt up to the fourth degree inclusive may be appointed as a bankruptcy trustee.
Where it becomes necessary to add or replace one or more bankruptcy trustees, the supervising judge shall refer the matter to the court, and the court shall undertake the appointment.

Where several bankruptcy trustees are appointed, they may only act jointly; provided, however, that the supervising judge shall be entitled to grant one or more of them special authorisation to perform certain administrative acts individually, and in such case the authorised trustees shall be solely liable.

Where an objection is raised against certain acts of the trustees, the delegated judge shall adjudicate thereon within three days. The decision of the delegated judge shall be provisionally enforceable.

The delegated judge shall have the right, upon complaints submitted to him by the bankrupt or by the creditors, or of his own motion, to propose the dismissal of one or more trustees.

Where the delegated judge does not examine such complaints within eight days, they may be referred to the court. The court shall then hear, in the deliberation room, the report of the delegated judge and the explanations of the trustees, and shall rule on the dismissal in a public sitting.
Decisions relating to the appointment or dismissal of the bankruptcy trustees shall not be subject to any avenue of recourse.
In its judgment declaring bankruptcy, the court shall appoint one of its members as delegated judge.

The delegated judge is specifically charged with expediting and supervising the operations and administration of the bankruptcy. He shall submit to the court a report on all disputes arising from the bankruptcy that fall within the jurisdiction of the court.

The decisions of the delegated judge shall be deposited forthwith at the court registry and the court may. They shall in all cases be subject to objection by any interested party before the court also to examine them of its own motion.
