The objection shall be submitted in the form of a simple declaration to the court registry within five days from the date of the decision, and the court shall adjudicate thereon within eight days by a decision not subject to recourse.

The court may at any time replace the delegated judge of the bankruptcy with another of its members, and neither this decision nor the decision appointing the delegated judge shall be subject to the avenues of recourse.

In its judgment declaring bankruptcy, the court shall order the affixing of seals, and it shall have the right at any stage of the case to order that the bankrupt be compelled to appear and be detained, and in all cases the bankrupt may not absent himself from his place of residence without the permission of the delegated judge.

Where the delegated judge considers that the assets of the bankrupt can be inventoried in a single day, the seals shall not be affixed, but the drawing up of the inventory list shall be commenced forthwith.

The clerk of the court shall immediately send notice to the justice of the peace of the paragraph of the judgment ordering the affixing of seals.

The justice of the peace shall have the right to affix the seals even prior to the issuance of this judgment, either of his own motion or upon the request of one or several creditors, and he shall possess this right only in the event of the absconding of the debtor or the smuggling of all or part of his assets.

The seals shall be affixed upon the warehouses, offices, safes, files, books, papers, and the movable property and effects of the bankrupt.

In the event of the bankruptcy of a general partnership, it shall not suffice to affix the seals upon the principal office of the partnership, but they must be affixed at the place of residence of each of the general partners separately.

In all cases, the justice of the peace shall send without delay notice of the affixing of the seals to the president of the court.
And if the affixing of the seals did not take place prior to the appointment of the bankruptcy trustees, the latter must request the justice of the peace to affix them.

The judge-commissary shall order, upon the request of the bankruptcy trustees, that the seals not be affixed upon the following items or shall authorise their extraction: the clothes, garments, furniture, and effects necessary for the bankrupt or for his family.

Delivery of what the judge-commissary has permitted shall take place in accordance with the statement submitted to him by the bankruptcy trustees. He shall also have the right to authorise that the seals not be affixed:

1) Upon items subject to imminent perishability or to rapid depreciation in their value.

2) Upon items suitable for the operation of the commercial establishment if such operation cannot be suspended without damage befalling the creditors.

The items referred to in the two preceding paragraphs shall be recorded immediately, together with a statement of their value, in an inventory list drawn up by the bankruptcy trustees in the presence of the justice of the peace, who must sign the record.

The sale of items subject to perishability or to rapid depreciation in their value or the maintenance of which entails heavy expense shall be carried out through the care of the trustees and by authorisation of the judge-commissary.

The operation of the commercial establishment through the care of the bankruptcy trustees may not be permitted by the court upon the report of the judge-commissary unless the public interest or the interest of the creditors requires it by necessity.

The magistrate shall extract the commercial books from among the sealed items and deliver them to the trustees in bankruptcy after marking the end of their entries, and shall then briefly record in his minutes the condition in which those books were found.

The file of negotiable instruments of near maturity, or prepared for acceptance, or requiring conservatory formalities, shall also be extracted by the magistrate from among the sealed items and delivered, after a description thereof, to the trustees in bankruptcy for the collection of their value, and the list of these instruments shall then be delivered to the judge-commissary.

Other debts shall be collected by the trustees in bankruptcy against a receipt issued by them. Letters addressed to the bankrupt shall be delivered to the trustees, who shall open them, and the bankrupt, if present, shall have the right to attend their opening.
The bankrupt and his family may receive from the assets of the bankruptcy a maintenance allowance to be determined by the judge-commissary upon the proposal of the trustees.

The trustees shall summon the bankrupt to close the books and strike a balance of their accounts in his presence. If he fails to answer the summons, a formal notice shall be sent to him requiring him to appear within forty-eight hours at the most.

He may appoint an authorised representative on his behalf, provided that he shows grounds for his failure to appear which the judge-commissary deems worthy of acceptance.

If the bankrupt has not submitted the balance sheet, the trustees must draw it up without delay on the basis of the bankrupt's books and papers and the information which they obtain, and then deposit the balance sheet with the court registry.

The judge-commissary may hear the statements of the bankrupt, his clerks, his employees, and any other person, whether with regard to the drawing up of the balance sheet or the causes and circumstances of the bankruptcy.

If a merchant is declared bankrupt after his death, or if the merchant dies after the declaration of his bankruptcy, his widow, his children, and his heirs shall have the right to appear in person or to appoint someone to represent them to act in place of the bankrupt in the drawing up of the balance sheet and in all other bankruptcy proceedings.

Within three days from the date of the affixing of the seals, or from the date of the rendering of the judgment declaring the bankruptcy if such measure took place prior to the rendering thereof, the trustees shall request the removal of the seals in order to proceed with the inventory of the bankrupt's property in his presence or after he has been duly summoned.

The trustees shall draw up the inventory in the presence of the Justice of the Peace in two original copies in proportion as the seals are removed, and the said judge shall affix his signature to the inventory at the conclusion of each session of work, and one of these two copies shall be deposited with the registry of the court within twenty-four hours while the other copy shall remain in the hands of the trustees.

The trustees may seek the assistance of whomever they wish in drawing up the inventory and in appraising the items.

A verification shall be carried out of the items that were exempted from the affixing of seals or that were extracted from among the sealed items and for which an inventory was drawn up and their value appraised as set forth above.

If bankruptcy is declared after the death of the bankrupt and the inventory had not been drawn up prior to its declaration, the drawing up thereof shall be commenced immediately in accordance with the forms set forth in the preceding Article in the presence of the heirs or after summoning them in due form, and the same procedure shall be followed if the bankrupt dies prior to the opening of the inventory.

The trustees in every bankruptcy must submit to the judge-commissaire, within fifteen days from the date of assuming the duties of their office, a report or a summary account of the apparent state of the bankruptcy and of its circumstances, its principal causes, and the characteristics that it appears to bear.

The judge-commissaire must refer that report without delay to the Public Prosecution together with his observations.

If the report is not submitted to him within the appointed time limit, he must notify the Public Prosecution, stating the reasons for the delay.

The officers of the Public Prosecution shall have the right to attend at the domicile of the bankrupt to observe the drawing up of the inventory, and they may at any time request that all records, books, and papers relating to the bankruptcy be communicated to them.

Upon completion of the inventory, the goods, cash, debt instruments owed to the bankrupt, books, papers, and the furniture and effects of the debtor shall be handed over to the bankruptcy trustees, who shall sign in acknowledgment of their receipt thereof at the foot of the inventory.

The trustees must, from the time they assume the duties of their office, perform all acts necessary for the preservation of the rights of the bankrupt against his debtors.

They must also request the registration of mortgages on the immovable properties of the debtors of the bankrupt if the bankrupt had not requested it.

The trustees shall effect the registration in the name of the body of creditors and shall attach to their schedules a certificate proving their appointment.

Finally, they must also effect the registration of the compulsory mortgage pertaining to the body of creditors as set forth above.
And the trustees shall continue, under the supervision of the judge-commissaire, the collection of debts owed to the bankrupt.

The delegated judge may, after hearing the statements of the bankrupt or after summoning him in due form, authorise the trustees to sell the movable objects and goods. He shall decide that this sale be carried out either amicably or by public auction through the Execution Department.

Pursuant to the same authorisation, and after hearing the bankrupt and seeking the opinion of the supervisors, if any exist, the trustees may exceptionally proceed with the sale of immovable properties, particularly the immovable properties that are not necessary for the operation of the commercial establishment, in accordance with the forms specified hereinafter for sales of immovable property following the establishment of the union of creditors.

The funds resulting from the sales and from the collections shall be handed over immediately to the bank authorised to accept State deposits, after deducting the sums determined by the delegated judge for costs and expenses.

Proof of this deposit must be furnished to the delegated judge within three days from the date of receipt. If the trustees delay, they shall be liable for interest on the sums which they have not deposited.

All sums deposited by the trustees or other sums deposited by other persons for the account of the bankruptcy cannot be withdrawn except by a decision of the delegated judge. If there is an attachment, the trustees must obtain beforehand a decision lifting it.

The delegated judge may order that payment be made by the bank directly into the hands of the creditors of the bankruptcy in accordance with a distribution schedule drawn up by the trustees and ordered to be executed by the delegated judge.

The trustees may, after obtaining the authorisation of the delegated judge and after summoning the bankrupt in due form, enter into a compromise in any dispute relating to the body of creditors, even that which pertains to immovable rights or actions.

If the subject-matter of the compromise is of an indeterminate value or if its value exceeds five hundred Lebanese pounds, the compromise must be homologated by the court.

The bankrupt shall be summoned to attend the homologation proceedings, and he shall in all cases have the right to object thereto; his objection shall suffice to prevent the compromise if its subject-matter is immovable property.

Acts of waiver, discontinuance and acquiescence may only be performed by the trustees in the same manner.

From the issuance of the judgment declaring bankruptcy, the creditors may deliver to the bankruptcy trustees their instruments together with a schedule indicating the papers delivered and the amounts claimed.

The creditor or his proxy shall sign this schedule, and the proxy's authorisation shall be attached thereto.

The trustees shall give a receipt for the file of produced papers, and this file may be sent to them by registered letter with acknowledgment of receipt.

After the convening of the composition assembly, the trustees shall return the papers delivered to them and shall only be liable for the instruments for a period of one year from the date of the convening of that assembly.

Creditors whose names are entered in the balance sheet and who have not produced the instruments of their debts within the eight days following the judgment declaring bankruptcy shall be notified at the end of that time limit, by publication in the newspapers or by a letter from the trustees, that they must deliver their instruments together with the detailed schedule to the bankruptcy trustees within fifteen days from the date of publication.

This time limit shall be extended for creditors residing outside Lebanese territory in accordance with the rules prescribed in the chapter on service of process in the Code of Civil Procedure.

The verification of debts shall be conducted by the bankruptcy trustees with the assistance of the controllers, if any, subject to the approval of the delegated judge and in the presence of the bankrupt or after he has been duly summoned.

If the bankruptcy trustees contest the validity of the whole or part of the debt, they shall notify the creditor thereof by registered letter. The creditor shall be given ten days to submit his written or oral explanations.

Immediately upon completion of the verification of debts, and within three months at most from the date of the judgment declaring bankruptcy, the trustees shall deposit with the court registry a statement of the debts which they have verified, stating the decision taken by the delegated judge upon their proposal in respect of each of them.

The clerk shall without delay inform the creditors of the deposit of this statement by publication in the newspapers, and shall in addition send to them a letter indicating to each of them the amount entered for him in the statement.

In very exceptional circumstances, the time limit specified in the first paragraph may be exceeded pursuant to a decision of the delegated judge.

Every creditor whose debt has been proved or whose name has been entered in the balance sheet may, within eight days from the date of the publications referred to in the preceding Article, submit claims or objections to the court registry by an annotation on the statement placed by himself or through a proxy. The bankrupt is granted the same right.

After the expiry of this time limit, upon the proposals of the trustees and subject to the claims and objections submitted to the court, the delegated judge shall finally determine the statement of debts, and the trustees shall execute his decision by signing the following declaration on the schedule of proved debts:

"Upon the proof of Mr...........or the company................ he (or it) was admitted in the capacity of an (ordinary, preferred or secured) creditor in the bankruptcy for the sum of............".

Disputed debts shall be referred through the care of the clerk to the Commercial Court to be examined by it at a hearing held within thirty days from the date of the publication mentioned in Article 550, and it shall adjudicate thereon upon the report of the delegated judge; the date of the hearing shall be notified to the two parties by means of a registered letter sent by the clerk at least three days before the hearing.

The court has the right to decide provisionally that the creditor must be admitted to the deliberations for an amount fixed by the decision itself, and this decision shall not be subject to any avenue of recourse.
A creditor the dispute in respect of whom concerns only his right to priority or mortgage shall be admitted to the deliberations of the bankruptcy as an ordinary creditor.

Creditors who have failed to appear or to produce the instruments of their debts within the time limits fixed for them, whether they are known or unknown, shall not participate in the distribution that will take place, provided that the door of objection remains open to them until the completion of the distribution of the funds.

The costs of the objection shall remain borne by them.

Their objection shall not stay the execution of the distributions ordered by the delegated judge, but if new distributions are commenced before the adjudication of their objection, they shall be included therein for the amount that the court fixes provisionally, and this amount shall be reserved until after the adjudication of their objection. If they are subsequently recognised in the capacity of creditors, they shall have no right to claim anything from the distributions that had been ordered by the delegated judge, but they shall have the right to deduct from the unallocated assets the shares appertaining to their debts from the first distributions.
Bonds issued by a commercial company in a lawful manner shall not be subject to the procedure of verification of debts.

The delegated judge must, within the three days following the closure of the schedule of debts or within the three days following the decision of the court issued pursuant to the provisions of Article 553 if there is a dispute, invite through the clerk the creditors whose debts have been proved to negotiate the composition agreement.

The newspaper publications and the letters of invitation must specify the purpose for which the meeting is held. As for the creditors whose debts have been provisionally admitted, each one of them shall be invited by a registered letter within the three days following the decision of the court concerning them.

The assembly shall convene under the presidency of the delegated judge at the place, day, and hour designated by him. The creditors whose debts have been finally proved or provisionally admitted shall participate therein either in person or through representatives authorised by them.

The bankrupt shall be invited to this meeting and must attend in person, and he may not send someone to represent him except for valid reasons approved by the delegated judge.

The trustees in bankruptcy shall submit a report on its state and on the formalities and operations that have been carried out, and the statements of the bankrupt must be heard.

The report of the trustees in bankruptcy bearing their signatures shall be handed over to the delegated judge, and this judge shall draw up a record of what was said and decided at the assembly.

The deliberating creditors may not accept the composition agreement after bankruptcy unless the following conditions are met, failing which the agreement shall be null and void.

This agreement shall only be concluded by the vote of a number of creditors constituting the majority and holding two-thirds of the amount of the debts finally or provisionally admitted in accordance with the provisions of Part Three of Chapter Three.

However, the debts owed to those who did not participate in the voting shall be deducted when calculating the majority of votes and the majority of amounts.

The spouse of the bankrupt, his relatives by blood and his relatives by marriage up to the fourth degree, as well as the persons who are their assignees in accordance with the conditions set forth in the Title on Preventive Composition, shall not participate in the voting.

Creditors holding a real estate mortgage or a privilege of a movable pledge shall not have the right to vote unless they waive their securities in accordance with the conditions set forth in the Title on Preventive Composition.

The composition agreement must be signed at the same sitting, failing which it shall be void. Where the composition is approved only by a majority in number of the creditors or by a majority holding two-thirds of the debts among them, the deliberation shall be adjourned for eight days with no further extension.

In such case, the creditors who attended the first assembly or were lawfully represented therein and signed the minutes of its sitting shall not be required to attend the second assembly.

The resolutions which they adopted and the approvals which they supported shall remain valid and taken into account if they came and amended them at the final meeting. The signature of the creditors at the assemblies may be replaced by a signature from them on a voting ballot annexed to the minutes.

A composition may not be concluded for a bankrupt convicted of fraudulent bankruptcy, and where an investigation is underway regarding fraudulent bankruptcy, the creditors shall be convened to decide whether they intend to deliberate on the matter of the composition in the event of acquittal and accordingly adjourn the determination of this matter until after the conclusion of the proceedings.

However, such adjournment may only be decided if the majority in number and the majority in amount specified heretofore are met.

Where the circumstances require holding the deliberation on the matter of the composition after the expiry of the period of adjournment, the rules specified in the preceding Article shall apply to the new deliberation.

Where the bankrupt is convicted of simple bankruptcy, the conclusion of a composition shall be possible.

However, the creditors may, in the event of the commencement of proceedings, adjourn the deliberation until after the conclusion thereof in accordance with the provisions of the preceding Article.

Where the matter relates to a commercial company that has issued debentures, the composition may not be concluded unless the assembly of debenture holders approves it and expresses its opinion in the cases and under the conditions set out in the Title on Preventive Composition.

An objection to the composition may be lodged by all creditors who had the right to participate in the conclusion of the composition, by those whose rights have been subsequently acknowledged, and by the representatives of the body of debenture holders, if any. The objection must be reasoned and must be served on the bankruptcy trustee and on the bankrupt within the eight days following the conclusion of the composition or the holding of the assembly of debenture holders, failing which it shall be void.

It must include a summons for them to appear at the first sitting held by the court.

Where there is only one trustee for the bankruptcy and he opposes the conclusion of the composition, he must request the appointment of a new trustee, and he shall be bound with respect to this trustee to apply the formalities provided for in this Article.

The homologation of the composition shall be pursued before the court upon the petition of the most diligent party.

The court may not decide prior to the expiry of the eight-day period provided for in the preceding Article, and if objections are lodged during the said period, the court shall decide the matter of the objections and the matter of the homologation in a single judgment.

If the objection is admitted, the judgment annulling the composition shall apply to all interested parties.

In all cases, the supervisory judge shall, before judgment is given on the matter of homologation, draw up a report on the characteristics of the bankruptcy and on the admissibility of the composition.

If the rules provided for above have not been observed, or if it appears that grounds pertaining to the public interest or to the interest of the creditors preclude the composition, the court must then refuse homologation.

It may also refuse to homologate the composition agreement if it does not contain a provision authorising the president of the court to appoint one or more commissioners charged with supervising the execution and the release of the mortgage belonging to the body of creditors if they have authorised it, and with monitoring the conversion of the assets into cash.

The homologation of the composition agreement renders it binding upon all creditors, whether or not they are mentioned in the balance sheet, and whether their debts are verified or unverified. It is effective even against creditors residing outside Lebanese territory and against those who have been provisionally admitted to take part in the deliberations, whatever the sum that may subsequently be allocated to them pursuant to the final judgment.

However, the composition shall not be effective against privileged and secured creditors if they have not waived their privileges or securities, nor against ordinary creditors if their debt arose during the period of the bankruptcy.

As soon as the judgment of homologation has been rendered and has acquired the force of res judicata, the effects of the bankruptcy shall cease, subject to the forfeiture of the political rights provided for in Article 500.

The bankruptcy trustees, whose functions come to an end, shall render their final account to the bankrupt in the presence of the judge; it shall be discussed and approved. The trustees shall then hand over to the bankrupt the entirety of his property, books, papers, and effects, and he shall give them a receipt in return for their delivery.

The supervisory judge shall draw up a record of all the foregoing, and his functions shall come to an end.

Should a dispute arise, the decision thereon shall rest with the court.

The composition agreement shall include time limits for the payment of debts in instalments at successive maturities, as well as, generally, a remission to the debtor of a large or small portion of his debt. However, such remission shall leave a natural obligation binding upon him.

The composition may be concluded subject to the condition of payment should the debtor return to better fortune, in accordance with the conditions set forth in the title on preventive composition.
The real estate mortgage established in favour of the body of creditors shall remain as security for the payment of the amount of the debt provided for in the composition agreement.
Beyond that, the creditors shall be entitled to demand one or more sureties to guarantee the execution of the composition agreement.

So long as the amount provided for in the composition agreement has not been paid in full, the debtor may not carry out any extraordinary disposition not required by the course of the trade itself, unless there is an agreement to the contrary.

In this regard, the provisions set forth in the Title on Preventive Composition must be observed.

No action for the annulment of the composition after homologation shall be admitted unless it is grounded on fraud discovered after such homologation and resulting from the concealment of the bankrupt's property or the exaggeration of the debts owed by him.

Every creditor may bring this action. However, it must be brought within five years after the discovery of the fraud.

The composition agreement shall also be annulled if the bankrupt is convicted of committing fraudulent bankruptcy. The annulment of the composition agreement shall discharge the sureties who did not participate in the fraud.

If, after the homologation of the composition agreement, a bankrupt is prosecuted for fraudulent bankruptcy and a warrant of provisional or non-provisional arrest is issued against him, the court may order such conservatory measures as it is entitled to take.

These measures shall be cancelled ipso jure upon the issuance of a decision barring trial or a judgment of acquittal or of exemption.

If the bankrupt fails to perform the conditions of the composition agreement, an action may be brought against him before the court for the rescission of this agreement, in the presence of the sureties or after they have been duly summoned, if there are sureties.

When the court takes cognisance of the judgment convicting of fraudulent bankruptcy, it shall proceed to appoint a delegated judge and one or more trustees in bankruptcy. It shall also proceed to make this appointment in the decision whereby it rules for the annulment or the rescission of the composition agreement. These trustees may affix the seals. They must proceed without delay, with the assistance of the Magistrate and on the basis of the old inventory list, to review the financial instruments and papers, and carry out, where necessary, a supplementary inventory.

They must also draw up a supplementary balance sheet. They are likewise required without delay to post up and to insert in the designated newspapers, together with an extract of the judgment appointing them, a notice inviting the new creditors - if any exist - to produce the instruments of their debts within fifteen days for their verification. This verification shall take place in the manner set out in Section Three of Chapter Three.

The verification of the debt instruments produced in accordance with the provisions of the preceding Article shall be commenced without delay. There shall be no need to conduct a new verification in respect of the debts that have previously been verified and confirmed, without prejudice to the right of rejection or reduction of the debts if they have then been discharged in whole or in part.
After the completion of the aforementioned acts, the creditors shall be summoned to give their opinion on the retention or replacement of the trustees if a new composition is not concluded.

The acts carried out by the bankrupt after the homologation of the composition agreement and prior to its annulment or rescission shall only be annulled in the event of fraud having prejudiced the rights of the creditors.

Creditors prior to the composition agreement shall be restored to all their rights as against the bankrupt alone. As regards the body of creditors, they may only enter into it within the following limits:

If they have not received anything of the percentage dividend upon distribution, they shall enter into it for the entirety of their debt.

If, however, they have recovered a portion of that dividend, they shall enter for a portion of their original debts equivalent to the portion of the percentage dividend that they were promised and did not receive.

The provisions of this Article shall apply in the event of a second bankruptcy occurring that was not preceded by the annulment or rescission of the composition agreement.

If no composition is concluded, the creditors shall by operation of law be in a state of union. The delegated judge shall consult them without delay regarding the acts of administration and regarding the retention or replacement of the bankruptcy trustees.

Preferential creditors or holders of a mortgage on immovable property or a pledge on movable property shall be admitted thereto.

A record of the statements and observations of the creditors shall be drawn up. Upon taking cognisance thereof, the court shall appoint the trustees of the union, and the bankruptcy trustees who have left office must render an account to the new trustees in the presence of the delegated judge and after the bankrupt has been duly summoned.

The creditors shall be consulted as to whether an allowance may be granted to the bankrupt out of the assets of the bankruptcy.

If the majority of the creditors present consent, a sum may be granted to him by way of allowance out of the assets of the bankruptcy; the trustees shall propose a sum and the delegated judge shall fix it by an order against which none other than the trustees may file an objection before the court.

If a partnership of persons is declared bankrupt, the creditors may accept the composition agreement solely with one or several partners.

In this case, the totality of the partnership's assets shall remain subject to the regime of the union of creditors. The personal assets belonging to those with whom the composition was concluded shall be excluded. This special agreement with them may not contain an obligation requiring them to pay any dividend except out of assets extraneous to the partnership's assets.

The partner with whom a special composition has been concluded shall be discharged from all joint and several liability.

The bankruptcy trustees shall represent the body of creditors and carry out the liquidation operations. However, the creditors may mandate them to continue operating the existing assets. The resolution mandating them shall specify the duration and extent of this operation, as well as the sums that may be retained in their hands to enable them to meet the costs and expenses.

However, this resolution may only be passed in the presence of the supervising judge and by a majority representing three-quarters of the creditors in number and three-quarters of the debts owed to them.

An objection to this resolution shall be admissible from the bankrupt and from the dissenting creditors.

However, the objection shall not entail a stay of execution.

If the acts of the trustees result in obligations whose value exceeds the assets of the union, the creditors who authorised such acts shall alone be personally liable for whatever exceeds their share in the said assets, provided that their liability shall not exceed the limits of the mandate they gave, and they shall share therein in proportion to the debts owed to them.

The trustees shall proceed to recover the debts that have not been paid. They may accept a compromise under the same conditions as were previously followed, notwithstanding any objection raised by the bankrupt.

As for lump-sum agreements, the creditors must submit them for deliberation at a meeting convened by the supervising judge at the request of the trustees or of any of the creditors. The court must grant the trustees authorisation in this respect.

The trustees must proceed with the sale of the movable property of all kinds, including the business concern, under the supervision of the supervising judge and without the need to summon the bankrupt, in accordance with the formalities prescribed for the sale of movables during the preparatory period.

If no compulsory sale proceeding has been commenced prior to the union, the conduct of the sale shall be entrusted exclusively to the trustees, and they shall be bound to initiate it within eight days with the authorisation of the supervising judge and through the Execution Department located at the situs of the properties.

The trustees shall draw up the book of conditions in accordance with which the auction shall take place, and they shall insert therein what is required to be stated by Article 744 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

In addition to the foregoing, Articles 746, 747 (first paragraph), 753 to 761, 763 to 767, and 778 to 792 of the Code of Civil Procedure shall apply to the sale, save for the provisions that do not conflict with the nature of this proceeding.

The auction, by the mere fact of its taking place, shall purge the properties of the registrations of privileges and mortgages.

If, at any time prior to the homologation of the composition or the formation of the union of creditors, the course of the bankruptcy proceedings is halted due to the insufficiency of assets, the court may, upon the report of the delegated judge or of its own motion, order the closure of the bankruptcy. By virtue of this judgment, each creditor recovers the right to bring individual legal proceedings.

The bankrupt and any interested party may at any time request the court to revoke this judgment if they prove the existence of sufficient funds to meet the expenses of the bankruptcy or hand over to the trustees the sum sufficient therefor.

In all cases, the expenses of the proceedings brought pursuant to the provisions of the preceding Article must first be discharged.

A creditor who holds debt instruments signed, endorsed, or guaranteed jointly and severally by the bankrupt and by his co-obligors who are also bankrupt shall participate in the distribution in each mass of creditors, and his participation therein shall be for the nominal amount of his debt until it is fully satisfied.

No recourse whatsoever before the courts shall lie among the bankruptcies of persons bound by the same obligation in respect of dividends paid, unless the aggregate of such dividends paid by the said bankruptcies exceeds the total amount of the principal of the debt and its accessories. In such case, the surplus shall devolve upon those obligors who are guaranteed by their remaining co-obligors, following the order of their obligations.

If a creditor holds instruments drawn jointly and severally against the bankrupt and other persons and has received part of his debt prior to the occurrence of the bankruptcy, he shall only participate in the mass of creditors after deducting the part received, and shall retain, as regards the remainder of the debt due to him, his rights against the co-obligor or the guarantor.

As for the co-obligor or the guarantor who made the partial payment, he shall participate in the same mass of creditors in respect of all that he has paid on behalf of the bankrupt.

Notwithstanding the conclusion of a composition, creditors shall retain the right to bring an action against the co-obligors of the bankrupt to claim the entirety of their debt, and such co-obligors shall have the right to intervene in the proceedings for the homologation of the composition in order to submit their observations.

Persons who claim ownership of property in the possession of the bankrupt may apply for its recovery, and the bankruptcy trustees may admit claims for recovery after the approval of the delegated judge.

However, if there is a dispute, the court shall adjudicate thereon after hearing the statements of the delegated judge.

The delegated judge shall convene the united creditors to a meeting at least once in the first year. And likewise in the following years if the case so requires.

The trustees must submit at the meetings an account of their administration.

The property of the bankruptcy shall be distributed among all the creditors in proportion to the verified debt of each of them, after deducting the expenses of the administration of the bankruptcy, the notices granted to the bankrupt or to his family, and the sums paid to the preferred creditors.

To this end, the trustees shall submit a monthly statement to the delegated judge on the status of the bankruptcy and the sums deposited with the bank designated to accept State deposits; the delegated judge shall then order, where necessary, the distribution of the money among the creditors, fix the amount thereof, and see to the notification of the order to all the creditors.

The trustees may not make any payment except against the presentation of the instrument establishing the debt. They shall mention on the instrument the sum which they have paid or ordered to be paid. If the presentation of the instrument is not possible, the delegated judge may order payment after examining the minutes of verification of debts.

In all cases, the creditor shall acknowledge receipt in the margin of the schedule of distribution.

After the completion of the liquidation of the bankruptcy, the delegated judge shall convene the creditors to a meeting. At this final meeting, the trustees shall submit their account, the bankrupt being present or duly summoned.

The creditors shall then express their opinion on the question of the excusability of the bankrupt, and minutes shall be drawn up for this purpose in which each creditor shall enter his statements and observations. After the adjournment of this meeting, the union shall be dissolved ipso jure.

The delegated judge shall submit to the court the resolution of the creditors concerning the excusability of the bankrupt and a report on the characteristics and circumstances of the bankruptcy. The court shall then issue its decision declaring the bankrupt excusable or inexcusable.
Perpetrators of fraudulent bankruptcy and persons convicted of forgery, theft, fraud, breach of trust, or embezzlement of public funds may not be deemed excusable.

A composition may be concluded by the total or partial abandonment of the assets of the bankrupt.

The conditions of this composition shall be the same as the conditions prescribed for the conclusion of a simple composition. However, the divestiture of the bankrupt with respect to the abandoned property shall not terminate by the conclusion of this composition; rather, such property shall be sold through the care of trustees appointed in the manner of the trustees of the union. The sale and the distribution of the money shall be subject to the same rules observed in the state of union.

There shall then be handed over to the debtor, out of the proceeds of the sale of the abandoned property, whatever exceeds the debts claimed from him.

In particular, the recovery of commercial papers and other unpaid instruments found in specie in the possession of the bankrupt at the time of the opening of the bankruptcy may be claimed if their owner had delivered them to the bankrupt by way of mandate to collect their value and keep it with him at the disposal of the owner, or if their delivery to him was allocated to a specific payment.

The recovery of banknotes deposited with the bankrupt may also be claimed if the depositor is able to prove their identity.

Likewise, the recovery of all or part of the goods may be claimed so long as they exist in specie, if they were delivered to the bankrupt by way of deposit or in order to be sold for the account of their owner.

The recovery of the price of those goods or part of their price may also be claimed if it has not been paid or set off in a current account between the bankrupt and the buyer.

The seller may withhold delivery of the goods and other movables which he has sold if they have not been delivered to the bankrupt or have not been dispatched to him or to another person for his account.

The seller may recover goods dispatched to the bankrupt in order to be able to exercise his right of retention over them, so long as they have not been delivered into the warehouses of the bankrupt, or into a place in which he has the appearance of disposal, or into the warehouses of a broker whom the bankrupt commissioned to sell them for his account.

However, a claim for recovery shall not be admitted if the goods have been resold before their arrival without fraud to another buyer in good faith.
If the buyer has taken delivery of the goods before his bankruptcy, the seller may not invoke an action for rescission, an action for recovery, or any privilege whatsoever.

In cases where the seller may exercise his right to retain the goods, the trustees in bankruptcy may, after obtaining authorisation from the delegated judge, insist upon the delivery of the goods after paying the agreed price for the goods.

If the trustees do not take this decision, the seller may rescind the sale provided that he pays to the body of creditors the amount which he received on account. He may obtain compensation for the damage which he sustained as a result of the rescission of the sale and participate for this purpose with the body of ordinary creditors.
The rights of recovery pertaining to the non-bankrupt spouse shall be determined in accordance with the rules set forth hereinafter.

Creditors of the bankrupt who legally hold a pledge or a special privilege over movable property shall not have their names entered on the schedule of the body of creditors except by way of memorandum.
The trustees may at any time, after obtaining authorisation from the judge-commissary, redeem for the benefit of the bankruptcy the pledged items upon payment of the debt.

If the trustees do not redeem the pledged property and the creditor sells it for a price exceeding the debt, the trustees shall collect the surplus, and if the price is less than the debt, the pledgee creditor shall participate for the remainder of his debt with the body of creditors in the capacity of an ordinary creditor.

The trustees shall submit to the judge-commissary a statement of the names of the creditors who claim a privilege over movable property, and this judge shall authorise, where necessary, the payment of their debts out of the first cash sum collected.

If a dispute arises over the privilege, the court shall adjudicate thereon.

If the distribution of the price of the immovable properties takes place before the distribution of the price of the movable properties, or if both distributions take place simultaneously, the creditors holding a privilege or a mortgage who have not recovered the whole of their debt out of the price of the immovable properties shall participate, in proportion to the remainder due to them, with the ordinary creditors in the distribution of the funds belonging to the body of those creditors, provided that their debts are verified in accordance with the forms prescribed above.

If one or more distributions of the cash proceeds from the price of the movable properties are carried out before the distribution of the price of the immovable properties, the creditors holding a privilege or a mortgage whose debts have been verified shall participate in the distribution in proportion to the total of their debts, subject, where necessary, to what they are required to return as set forth hereinafter.

After the sale of the immovable properties and the carrying out of the final liquidation of the account of the creditors holding a privilege or a mortgage according to the order of their ranks, whoever among them is entitled according to his rank to recover the whole of his debt from the price of the mortgaged immovable properties may not collect his share from the distribution of their prices except after deduction of what he has recovered from the body of ordinary creditors.

The sums deducted in this manner shall not remain with the body of mortgage creditors, but shall revert to the body of ordinary creditors for whose benefit these sums are withheld.

As for the creditors holding a mortgage whose share in the distribution of the price of the immovable properties satisfies only a part of their debt, the following procedure shall be followed with respect to them: their rights in the funds allocated to the body of ordinary creditors shall be finally determined in the amount of the sums that remain due to them after deduction of their share in the distribution of the price of the immovable properties.

Whatever they have received in excess of this amount in the previous distribution shall be deducted from their share in the price of the immovable properties and shall revert to the body of ordinary debts.

The aforementioned procedure shall differ from the ordinary procedure in the following characteristics:

First - The time limits for producing debt instruments and for opposition or appeal and the other time limits provided for in Articles 497, 512, 548, 566 and 579 of this Law shall be reduced by half.

If the time limit is fifteen days, it shall be reduced to eight days.

However, the extension of the time limit provided for in Article 548 for the benefit of creditors residing outside Lebanese territory shall not be subject to reduction.

Second - Seals shall not be affixed.

Third - Supervisors shall not be appointed.

Fourth - The delegated judge shall adjudicate disputes raised concerning debts, subject to the reservation of the right of appeal, where applicable, before the Court of Appeal.

Fifth - The delegated judge shall be entitled to authorise all settlements.

Sixth - Only one distribution of funds shall be made.

Seventh - The delegated judge shall determine disputes relating to the account of the bankruptcy trustee and his emoluments.

The Criminal Courts of First Instance shall hear cases of negligent bankruptcy upon the request of the bankruptcy trustees or any of the creditors or the Public Prosecution. The perpetrator of such bankruptcy shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year, with due regard to mitigating circumstances of the offence.

Every merchant who finds himself in one of the following cases shall be deemed a negligent bankrupt:

First - If his personal expenses or the expenses of his household are deemed excessive.

Second - If he has spent large sums on operations of the nature of pure gambling or on speculative ventures on the stock exchange or in the purchase of goods.

Third - If, prior to his cessation of payment and with the intent of delaying his bankruptcy, he purchased a quantity of goods in order to sell them below the ordinary price, or engaged with the same intent in contracting loans and circulating commercial papers or other onerous means for the purpose of obtaining cash.

Fourth - If, after his cessation of payment, he made payment to one of the creditors to the prejudice of the body of creditors.

Creditors who have no share in the distribution of the price of the immovable properties shall be deemed ordinary creditors and shall be subject in this capacity to the effects of the composition and to all operations pertaining to the body of ordinary debts.
The property of the non-bankrupt spouse, both movable and immovable, shall remain outside the assets of the bankruptcy estate.

The property of the non-bankrupt spouse which is proven to have been purchased with the funds of the bankrupt during the five years preceding the date of the declaration of bankruptcy shall be deemed part of the assets of the bankruptcy estate.

The aforementioned fact may be proven by all means of evidence admissible in commercial matters. Merely establishing proof that the non-bankrupt spouse had no personal resources at the date of acquiring such property shall be deemed sufficient proof, unless the latter provides proof to the contrary.

If the non-bankrupt spouse pays debts on behalf of the bankrupt spouse, he shall be entitled to claim his rights like the rest of the creditors in the bankruptcy estate, unless proof is established that such debts were paid out of the property of the bankrupt spouse.

If the spouse was a merchant at the time of conclusion of the marriage contract, or had at that time no other definite profession and then became a merchant during the same year, only the immovable properties which he owned at the time of the marriage or which devolved upon him by inheritance, by gift inter vivos, or by will shall be subject to the compulsory mortgage provided for in paragraph 2 of Article /131/ of the Real Property Ownership Law promulgated by Decision No. 3339.

The non-bankrupt spouse whose bankrupt spouse was a merchant at the time of conclusion of the marriage contract, or had at that time no other definite profession and then became a merchant within the year following the conclusion of the marriage contract, shall not be entitled to bring any action against the bankruptcy estate on account of the benefits provided for in the marriage deed. In this case, the creditors shall not be entitled, on their part, to avail themselves of the benefits granted by the non-bankrupt spouse in the said deed.

Gifts granted by the bankrupt spouse to his non-bankrupt spouse during the five years preceding the date of the declaration of bankruptcy shall be null and void ipso jure.

If it results from the balance sheet submitted by the bankrupt or from subsequent information that the assets of the bankruptcy estate do not exceed two thousand five hundred Lebanese pounds, or if it appears that the rate to be distributed cannot exceed ten per cent, the court may, either of its own motion or upon the request of the creditors, order that the bankruptcy proceedings be conducted in accordance with the procedure known as "summary".

Every merchant who finds himself in one of the following cases may be declared a negligent bankrupt:

First - If he has undertaken for the account of third parties, without consideration, obligations considered overly exorbitant having regard to his position at the time he undertook them.

Second - If he is declared bankrupt anew without having fulfilled the obligations imposed upon him pursuant to a previous composition.

Third - If he has not complied with the obligations relating to the Commercial Register.

Fourth - If he has not submitted to the registry of the court within twenty days from the date of his cessation of payments the declaration required by this Law, or if the said declaration does not include the names of all the jointly and severally liable partners.

Fifth - If he has not kept books and has not made a true inventory, or if his books and inventory lists are incomplete or irregular or do not reflect his true state of assets and liabilities, unless there is fraud.

The costs of the action brought by the Public Prosecution for negligent bankruptcy may in no case be borne by the body of creditors.

In the event that a composition is concluded, the Public Treasury may not claim from the bankrupt the costs it has paid until after the expiry of the time limits granted pursuant to the said agreement.

The costs of actions brought in the name of the creditors by the trustees in bankruptcy shall be borne by the body of creditors if the bankrupt is acquitted, and shall be borne by the Public Treasury if he is convicted, without prejudice to its right of recourse against the bankrupt in accordance with the preceding Article.

The trustees may neither bring an action for negligent bankruptcy nor join as a civil party in the name of the body of creditors except after being authorised to do so by a resolution adopted by a majority in number of the creditors present.
The costs of the criminal action brought by one of the creditors shall be paid by the Public Treasury if the bankrupt is convicted, and shall be paid by the prosecuting creditor if he is acquitted.

Every bankrupt merchant who has concealed his books, or misappropriated or concealed a part of his assets, or who is shown to have fraudulently acknowledged himself to be indebted for sums he does not owe, whether in the entries of his books and in authentic instruments or in undertakings under private signature and in the balance sheet, shall be deemed a fraudulent bankrupt and shall be punished with the penalty prescribed for fraudulent bankruptcy.

In no case may the costs of an action for fraudulent bankruptcy be placed upon the body of creditors, and if one or more creditors join as a civil party, the costs, in the event of acquittal, shall remain borne by them.

Shall be punished with the penalty for fraudulent bankruptcy:

First - Persons who are proven to have misappropriated or concealed, for the benefit of the bankrupt, all or part of his movable or immovable property, all without prejudice to the cases of accessory complicity provided for in the Penal Code.

Second - Persons who are proven to have fraudulently presented fictitious debts in the bankruptcy with the intention of having them proved, whether in their own name or in the name of nominal persons.

Third - Persons who carried on trade under the name of others or under a false name and committed acts considered to be of the nature of fraudulent bankruptcy.

The spouse of the bankrupt, his ascendants, his descendants, and his relatives by marriage of the same degree, if they misappropriate, divert, or conceal effects belonging to the bankruptcy without acting in collusion with the bankrupt, shall be punished with the penalty for theft.

In the cases provided for the preceding articles, the Court of First Instance or the Court of Appeal shall adjudicate upon the following matters, even if there is an acquittal:

First - It must order of its own motion the restitution of all fraudulently misappropriated property, rights, and shares to the body of creditors.

Second - It shall award such damages as may be claimed and shall fix the amount thereof in the judgment it renders.
Any bankruptcy trustee who commits misappropriation in the administration of his functions shall be liable to the penalty provided for the misdemeanour of breach of trust.

Every creditor who agrees with the bankrupt or with any other person upon special advantages to be obtained in return for his vote in the meetings of the bankruptcy, or who concludes a special agreement resulting in a special benefit to be obtained from the assets of the bankrupt, shall be punished with imprisonment from one month to one year and with a fine not exceeding two hundred and fifty Lebanese pounds, without prejudice to mitigating circumstances. The term of imprisonment may be increased to two years if the creditor is a trustee of the bankruptcy.

Furthermore, the annulment of the said agreements shall be declared with respect to all persons, including the bankrupt.

The creditor must restore the monies and sums that he obtained pursuant to these agreements to whomsoever is legally entitled thereto.
All decisions and judgments rendered pursuant to the provisions of this Title shall be posted and published in the forms prescribed for the publication of the judgment declaring bankruptcy.
Prosecutions conducted for negligent or fraudulent bankruptcy shall not entail any- modification of the ordinary rules relating to the administration of the bankruptcy.

The clerk of the court shall send, by registered letter, notice of the application for rehabilitation to each of the creditors whose debts have been proved in the bankruptcy or recognised in a subsequent judicial decision and who have not obtained full payment of their debts.

Every creditor who has not received in full the dividend fixed for him in the composition agreement or who has not granted his debtor a full discharge shall be entitled, within one month from the date of such notice, to file an opposition to the rehabilitation by a simple petition submitted to the registry of the court together with the supporting documents. The opposing creditor may, by means of a petition submitted to the court and served upon the debtor, intervene in the proceedings held for rehabilitation.

After the expiry of the time-limit, the result of the inquiries prescribed above and the oppositions lodged by the creditors shall be referred to the Public Prosecutor to whom the application was submitted, and he shall refer them, together with his reasoned opinion, to the President of the court.

Where necessary, the court shall summon the applicant for rehabilitation and the opposing parties and hear their statements inter partes in the council chamber. The applicant may be assisted by an advocate.

In the case of payment of the debts in full, the court shall confine itself to verifying the authenticity of the documents produced, and if it finds them to be in conformity with the law, it shall order the rehabilitation.

If the rehabilitation is discretionary, the court shall assess the circumstances of the case, and the judgment shall then be delivered in open court.

An appeal may be lodged against it, whether by the applicant for rehabilitation, by the Public Prosecutor, or by the creditors, within one month running from the notice sent to them by registered letter.

The judgment shall also be served upon the opposing creditors. The latter may exercise their right of opposition before the Court of Appeal.

After examination, the Court of Appeal shall adjudicate the case in accordance with the forms prescribed above.

If the application is dismissed, it may not be renewed until after the lapse of one year.

If the application is granted, the judgment delivered by the Court of First Instance or of Appeal shall be entered in the register of the bankruptcy court or of the court within the jurisdiction of which the applicant resides.

This judgment shall also be sent to the Public Prosecutor who received the application for rehabilitation, and the latter shall send it to the Public Prosecutor at the place of birth of the applicant, who shall make a note thereof opposite the declaration of bankruptcy in the judicial record.

This judgment shall also be registered in the Commercial Register.

No application for commercial rehabilitation shall be admitted in respect of fraudulent bankrupts or persons convicted of theft, fraud, or breach of trust, unless they have obtained penal rehabilitation.
A bankrupt may be rehabilitated after his death.
Provided that the trustees shall be bound in this case to deliver to the Public Prosecution all documents, instruments, papers and information required of them.

The documents, instruments and papers delivered by the trustees during the investigation shall be placed open to inspection at the registry of the court, and inspection thereof shall take place upon the application of the trustees.

They may take private extracts therefrom or request official copies thereof, which the clerk shall send to them.

As for the documents, instruments and papers for which no order has been issued to deposit them with the judiciary, they shall be delivered after the judgment of first instance or on appeal to the trustees against a receipt.

After the lapse of ten years from the declaration of bankruptcy, the bankrupt shall automatically recover his rehabilitation without performing any formality if he was neither a negligent nor a fraudulent bankrupt.

Recovery of rehabilitation in this manner may affect neither the functions of the trustees if their mission has not ended, nor the rights of the creditors if their debtors have not been completely discharged.

Rehabilitation shall automatically revert to the bankrupt who has paid in full all sums due from him in principal and interest together with expenses. He may not be required to pay interest for a period exceeding five years.

In order for rehabilitation to revert automatically to a partner in a partnership of persons that has fallen into bankruptcy, he must prove that he has paid under the aforementioned conditions the share incumbent upon him of the company's debts, even if he has obtained a special composition.

If one or several of the creditors have disappeared, absented themselves or refused to accept payment, the sum due to them shall be deposited with the bank authorised to accept State deposits, and proof of such deposit shall be deemed equivalent to a receipt.

Rehabilitation may be granted to the bankrupt whose probity is recognised:

First - If he has paid in full all the instalments promised by him in the deed of composition which he obtained. The provision of this paragraph shall apply to a partner in a partnership of persons whose bankruptcy has been declared and who has himself obtained a special composition from the creditors.

Second - If the bankrupt proves that the creditors have granted him a complete discharge from his debts or have unanimously consented to his rehabilitation.

Every application for rehabilitation shall be submitted to the Public Prosecutor at the court that issued the judgment of bankruptcy. Receipts and supporting papers shall be annexed thereto.

This judge shall refer all the papers to the President of the court that declared the bankruptcy and to the Public Prosecutor in the district in which the applicant resides, and shall charge them both to take all the information that can be obtained regarding the veracity of the facts set forth.

The mere production of the receipts and other papers required for rehabilitation shall not render their registration compulsory.
Single Article: The Judicial Fees Law contained in Decree No. 1777 dated 5 May 1950 is hereby ratified as amended by the Administration and Justice Committee in its report dated 14 July 1950

The registry fees are:

1- The registration fee

2- The lawsuit fee

3- The service fee

4- The copy fee

Article 2: Registration fee

The registration fee is set as follows:

A- LBP 1,000 for lawsuits the value of which does not exceed LBP 200000.

B - LBP 2,500 for lawsuits not subject to valuation, including the lawsuits provided for in Article 13

and lawsuits the value of which exceeds LBP 200000 and does not exceed LBP 1000000.

C - LBP 5,000 for lawsuits the value of which exceeds one million LBP and does not exceed five million pounds.

D - LBP 7,500 for lawsuits the value of which exceeds five million pounds and does not exceed ten million Lebanese pounds.

E - LBP 10,000 for lawsuits the value of which exceeds ten million Lebanese pounds.

Article 3: Summons fee

The summons fee is set as follows:

A- LBP 1,000 for lawsuits the value of which does not exceed LBP 200000.

B - LBP 2,500 for lawsuits not subject to valuation, including the lawsuits provided for in Article 13 and lawsuits the value of which exceeds LBP 200000 and does not exceed one million Lebanese pounds.

C - LBP 5,000 for lawsuits the value of which exceeds one million pounds and does not exceed five million Lebanese pounds.

D - LBP 7,500 for lawsuits the value of which exceeds five million pounds and does not exceed ten million Lebanese pounds.

E- LBP 10,000 for lawsuits the value of which exceeds ten million Lebanese pounds.

Article 4: Service fee

The service fee is set as follows:

A- LBP 1,000 for lawsuits the value of which does not exceed LBP 200000.

B - LBP 2,500 for lawsuits not subject to valuation, including the lawsuits provided for in Article 13 and lawsuits the value of which exceeds two hundred thousand pounds and does not exceed one million pounds.

C- LBP 5,000 for lawsuits the value of which exceeds one million pounds and does not exceed five million pounds.

D- LBP 7,500 for lawsuits the value of which exceeds five million pounds and does not exceed ten million.

E- LBP 10,000 for lawsuits the value of which exceeds ten million pounds.
Save for the rules set forth in the preceding Titles, companies shall be subject to the following provisions.

All commercial companies, with the exception of joint ventures, may obtain a preventive composition and may also be declared bankrupt. A company, even if in liquidation, may be declared bankrupt.

The same shall also apply even if the company has been judicially annulled, provided that the company is continuing in fact.

The petition for preventive composition or the declaration seeking a judgment of bankruptcy must bear the signature of the partner or partners who hold the right to sign on behalf of the company if it is a general partnership or a limited partnership, and the signature of the manager or the member of the board of directors discharging his function pursuant to a resolution of the board of directors if it is a joint-stock company.

If the company has entered the stage of liquidation, the liquidator must submit this declaration. The petition or declaration shall be lodged with the registry of the court within the jurisdiction of which the head office of the company is situated.

All partners in general partnerships and all managing partners in limited partnerships must also, each in so far as concerns him, make the declaration required pursuant to this Law within twenty days from the date of the company's cessation of payments.

The court shall declare in the same judgment the bankruptcy of the company and the bankruptcy of the general partners, and shall in principle appoint one bankruptcy judge and one trustee in bankruptcy, even though the bankruptcies are distinct from one another and the bodies of creditors therein are differently constituted.

The trustee in bankruptcy in all companies shall have the right to compel the partners to complete the payment of their capital even before the maturity date fixed in the articles of association of the company.

If the company becomes bankrupt by way of fraudulent or negligent bankruptcy, an action for criminal liability may, where applicable, be brought against the partners in a general partnership, the managing partners in a limited partnership, and the managers of joint-stock companies or the members of their boards of directors who perform the functions of managers.

All prior legislative provisions relating to the matters provided for in this Law:

Shall lose their legal force from the time this Law becomes enforceable.

Nothing is amended in the laws relating to the constitution of the commercial courts and the procedure before them.

This Law shall be put into effect after the expiry of six months starting from the date of its publication in the Official Gazette.

The amount of the copy fee shall be 20,000 L.L.

This fee shall be levied:

1- On copies of judgments and decisions which one of the parties requests to be served.

2- On copies requested by one of the parties or by a third party to the action.

Neither party shall be given a certified copy of the judgment prior to the collection of all the fees due on such judgment as set out in the second paragraph of Article 92, and the copy given as enforceable shall not be subject to the copy fee.

If a copy of the judgment is given to a third party to the action, an endorsement must be made thereon that it is valid for use solely for his own benefit

Article 6:

A fee in the amount of 20,000 L.L. shall be levied on copies of documents, reports, and all other papers of the action requested by the interested parties
The fee on an action shall be of two kinds: proportional and fixed

In actions susceptible of valuation, a proportional fee of 2.5%, two and a half per cent, shall be imposed, and fractions of a pound shall be counted as a full pound in calculating the fee.

This fee shall be charged on the amount and value of the claims asserted, whether principal, additional, incidental, or by way of counterclaim.

If the subject-matter of the action comprises two parts, one of which is susceptible of valuation and the other is not susceptible of valuation, a proportional fee shall be charged on the first and on

the second a fixed fee.

An application to renew an action ordered to be struck out in accordance with the provisions of Article 471 of the Code of Civil Procedure shall be deemed to constitute a new action.

The fee shall be levied on the basis of the value of the claim; the plaintiff shall specify this value in the statement of claim.

If it appears to the court during the course of the action that the value of the claim exceeds the value specified by the plaintiff, it may determine the value that must be taken as the basis for levying the fee by the means available to it or through an expert

One quarter of the applicable proportional fee shall be levied upon the filing of the action and the remainder upon extracting the judgment; however, in respect of a counterclaim claiming damages arising from the bringing of the action, and an application for intervention, the fee thereon shall not be levied until after the issuance of the judgment

The calculation of the proportional fee in the lawsuits set forth hereinafter shall be carried out in the following manner:

1- In lawsuits in which a specified sum or a thing capable of valuation is claimed: on the basis of the amount of the sum or the value of the thing claimed.

2- In real property lawsuits: on the basis of the current market value of the real property claimed on the date of filing the lawsuit.

3- In lawsuits concerning usufruct and bare ownership: on the basis of half the value of the real property.

4- (Repealed by Law 710 dated 5/11/1998)

5- In lawsuits for the annulment of executed contracts: in proportion to the difference between the value of the real property or movable things claimed to be recovered, and the price for which the real property or things were sold.

6- In lawsuits for the rescission of instruments and contracts: these lawsuits shall be subject in principle to the fixed fee; however, if they include a request for judgment for another claim capable of valuation, the proportional fee on the amount or value of this request shall then be levied in addition to the fixed fee.

7- In lawsuits requesting the annulment or execution of a commercial contract: these lawsuits shall be subject in principle to the fixed fee; however, if they include a request for judgment for a specified sum, the proportional fee shall then be levied on the sum claimed in addition to the fixed fee.

8- In lawsuits for the constitution of a life annuity: on the principal declared in the clause, or on a sum equal to ten times the annual income requested or previously existing, or on a sum equal to the total duration of the annual maturities if the duration of the income is less than ten years.

9- In lawsuits concerning insurance contracts of all kinds: on a sum equal to the total amount of the premiums due and the remaining maturities, provided that the said sum does not exceed ten years.

10- In lawsuits for the annulment of a gift or the revocation thereof: on the value of the gifted property.

11- In lawsuits for the reduction of a gift: in proportion to the value requested to be reduced.

12- (Repealed by Law 710 dated 5/11/1998)

13- In lawsuits for rendering an accounting brought by one of the partners to claim his share after the appointment of an expert: the fixed fee shall be taken upon the filing thereof if the sum claimed is not specified, provided that the proportional fee is levied after the issuance of the judgment.

14- In lawsuits for the liquidation of a company: the fixed fee shall be taken upon the filing of the lawsuit, provided that the proportional fee is levied after the issuance of the judgment.

15- (Repealed by Law 710 dated 5/11/1998)

16- In the case of homologation of a settlement after the institution of the lawsuit: on the amount of the value of the thing settled upon.

17- In lawsuits requesting the recovery of pledged shares, financial securities, or corporeal things, with the exception of pledged debt instruments: on the difference between the value of the securities and the value of the pledge.

18- In lawsuits to prove ownership of a deposit or a lost instrument: on the value of the things claimed.

19- In lawsuits for the recovery of a trust: on the value of what is requested to be recovered.

20- In lawsuits for the recovery of goods in the possession of a third party: on the value of those goods.

21- (Repealed by Law 710 dated 5/11/1998)

22- In lawsuits requesting the recovery of unpaid commercial paper from a bankruptcy estate (Article 608 of the Code of Commerce): on the value of the paper and instruments requested to be recovered.

23- In lawsuits brought by the wife of the bankrupt requesting the recovery of real property or movables belonging to her (Article 625 of the Code of Commerce): on the value of what is requested to be recovered.

24- In lawsuits requesting the recovery of goods in kind from a bankruptcy estate: on the value of those goods.

25- In lawsuits to prove a privileged debt in a bankruptcy: on the value of the debt requested to be proved.

26- (Repealed by Law 710 dated 5/11/1998).

27- (Repealed by Law 710 dated 5/11/1998).

28- In lawsuits requesting an exchange rate difference (Difference de change): on the amount of the difference claimed.

29- In all other cases: on the amount of the principal sums claimed.

Article 12: Flat Fee

A flat fee in the amount of /250,000/ L.L. (two hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese pounds) shall be imposed in lawsuits that are not susceptible of valuation.

The following actions shall be deemed equivalent to actions not susceptible of valuation and subject to the fixed fee:

1- Possessory actions.

2- Boundary actions.

3- Actions for partition, including the partition and liquidation of a waqf.

4- Actions of pre-emption.

5- Paulian actions.

6- Actions concerning easements.

7- Actions concerning the right of way, water passage, and the right of drawing water.

8- Actions for the annulment of a usufruct.

9- Actions of opposition to customs decisions.

10- Actions concerning enforcement difficulties.

11- Applications for attachment and the lifting thereof.

12- Actions for confirmation of attachment, if not coupled with a claim for judgment on the debt causing the attachment, failing which they shall be subject to the proportional fee.

13- Actions applying for the appointment of a judicial receiver.

14- Actions before the Judge of Urgent Matters.

15- Actions brought applying for the homologation of a settlement.

16- Actions for retrial: provided that the provisions of the third paragraph of Article 23 of this Law are observed.

17- Actions of opposition to judgments in absentia: provided that the provisions of the second paragraph of Article 23 of this Law are observed.

18- Actions of third-party opposition: provided that the provisions of the first paragraph of Article 23 of this Law are observed.

19- Applications for the recusal of judges.

20- Applications for the rectification or interpretation of judgments, provided that the fee is ultimately calculated on the basis of the rectified judgment.

21- Actions to grant exequatur to foreign judgments and instruments.

22- Actions for the rescission of instruments and contracts that do not contain another claim susceptible of valuation.

23- Actions for the annulment of a settlement contract that do not contain another claim susceptible of valuation.

24- Actions for the annulment of a will.

25- Actions for the performance or rescission of a lease and the delivery and vacation of the leased premises.

26- Actions applying for the annulment of an arbitral award.

27- Actions for the annulment of an insurance contract in which a specific sum is not claimed.

28- Actions applying for the registration, modification, striking off, or rectification of real rights in the Land Register.

29- Actions in which copies of deeds and entries of the Land Register are requested to be taken.

30- Actions brought by a depositary applying for the restitution of the deposit.

31- Actions for the recovery of pledged debt instruments.

32- Actions applying for the delivery of an instrument, provided that the provisions of paragraph 17 of Article 11 of this Law are observed.

33- Actions for the sale of attached items.

34- Actions concerning disputes arising from the consolidation and redistribution of land parcels.

35- Actions applying for the extinguishment of a debt or a right by prescription or for another cause.

36- Actions applying for the payment of a debt by instalments or a grace period for its discharge.

37- Actions applying for the preference of a privileged debt over another privileged debt.

38- Actions applying for the annulment or performance of a contract that do not contain another claim susceptible of valuation.

39- Actions for the dissolution or annulment of a company or opposition to its renewal.

40- Actions for the rendering of accounts brought by one of the partners to claim his share, provided that the provisions of paragraph 13 of Article 11 of this Law are observed.

41- Actions challenging decisions of the ordinary or extraordinary general assembly or the board of directors in joint-stock companies.

42- Actions applying for the confirmation of a company.

43- Actions applying for the exclusion of a partner from the company.

44- Actions challenging the validity of a commercial pledge.

45- Actions concerning the simulation of the endorsement of an instrument (giro).

46- Actions applying for the rectification of an account or the interpretation of a contract or the dissolution of a commercial contract due to death or loss of capacity.

47- Actions applying for commercial rehabilitation.

48- Actions by a guarantor applying for the discharge of his liability.

49- Actions applying for the registration, striking off, or modification of a real right over a vessel.

50- Actions applying for the annulment of an insurance contract for a defect, a false declaration, or concealment of information.

51- Actions applying for the inspection of insured goods.
