52- Actions applying for the transfer of the registration of a vessel from the name of the seller to the buyer if the price is paid.

53- Actions for the adjustment of maritime averages (Articles 269 and 270 of the Code of Maritime Commerce).

54- Actions applying for authorisation to contract a loan for a vessel (Articles 120 and 284 of the Code of Maritime Commerce).

55- Actions applying for the admission of an expense or loss among general maritime averages (Article 261 of the Code of Maritime Commerce).

56- Actions for the declaration of bankruptcy, the fixing and modification of the date of cessation of payments, or opposition to decisions and judgments rendered therein, and all actions deriving from bankruptcy, with the exception of the actions set forth in paragraphs 22, 23, 24, and 25 of Article 11 of this Law.

In bankruptcy cases, the creditor petitioning for bankruptcy shall deposit, in addition to the fixed fee, against the costs of the action, /50000/ Lebanese Pounds (fifty thousand Lebanese Pounds).

57- Actions of opposition to judicial distribution carried out before the Execution Department.

58- Actions for the annulment of enforcement proceedings.

59- Referral decisions issued by the courts.

60- Cases relating to the occupation of public domain.

61- Direct tax cases.

62- All other cases not susceptible of valuation.

The following paragraphs were added pursuant to Law 710 dated 5/11/98

63- Actions applying for the exchange of a waqf

64- Actions for the recovery of a payment made after the cessation of payments (Article 508 of the Code of Commerce).

65- Actions for the homologation of a composition (concordat)

66- Proceedings for the distribution of the bankrupt's assets in a state of union.

67- Actions arising from expropriation.

68- Granting exequatur to arbitral awards.

The following actions decided by the courts without summoning the adverse party shall be subject to a fixed fee of /250,000/ L.L. (two hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese pounds).

- Civil status actions.

- Actions for proof of death and determination of heirs.

- Actions requesting the appointment of a guardian, executor, or curator and the granting of leave to them to perform a specific act.

As for actions challenging judgments and decisions rendered in this regard, they shall be subject to a fixed fee of thirty-five thousand Lebanese pounds".
A fixed fee of 50,000 L.L. shall be levied for each signature upon the registration of a will before the courts.

Commercial Registration and Endorsement Fee

The following fees shall be collected in the court registries in return for endorsing registers and registering companies:

1- For endorsing merchants' books, 200 L.L. for each page.

2- For registering each commercial establishment or commercial company in the Commercial Register, 20,000 L.L.

3- For registering each amendment, change, or addition of striking off relating to companies and their articles of association and commercial establishments previously registered in the Commercial Register, 10.000 L.L.

- For each copy of the entries registered in the Commercial Register, 20.000 L.L. shall be collected.

Fees for Preparatory Decisions and Final Judgments

A copy fee of 20.000 L.L. shall be levied in advance for each preparatory decision rendered by the courts upon its extraction by the concerned parties.

As for actions whose value does not exceed 200000 L.L., this fee shall be 5,000 L.L.

In an action subject to the proportional fee, the judgment fee shall be collected in proportion to the value awarded, and only the execution fee in the Execution Department shall be paid on interest if the judgment deals with two parts, one of which is assessable and the other is unassessable, in which case, in addition to the fixed fee paid in advance, the proportional fee shall be collected on the assessable matter, and if there are multiple judgment creditors in a single judgment and the award to each of them is independent, the fee due from the person requesting the extraction of the judgment shall be collected from him in proportion to the value awarded to him, provided that this is indicated at the foot of the copy delivered to him and it is noted that it is valid for execution in his favour only

If judgment is rendered in favour of the plaintiff on his original claims, in favour of the defendant on his counterclaim, and in favour of the third party intervener in the action, the judgment fee shall be levied from each of them in proportion to the value awarded to him

If judgment is rendered ordering set-off between two amounts, one of which is in favour of the plaintiff and the other in favour of the defendant, the fee shall be levied on the balance remaining after the set-off

Where the fixed fee has been collected in any case and the trial leads to a judgment for a thing susceptible of valuation, the proportional fee shall then be collected on the value of such thing after deducting the fee collected in advance

In the event of the joinder of two or more actions and the issuance of a single judgment therein, the value of the fees paid in advance shall be counted towards the principal of the fee due on the judgment

The proportional fee shall be collected on judgments issued in cases subject upon their filing to the fixed fee, in the following instances:

1- In actions of third-party opposition - where judgment is rendered in favour of the opponent for a specified sum or for a thing susceptible of valuation

2- In actions of opposition to default judgments - where judgment is rendered for a thing susceptible of valuation that was not adjudged in the opposed judgment, the fee shall be collected on the excess adjudged

3- In actions for retrial - where judgment is rendered as a result of the retrial for a sum or for a thing susceptible of valuation exceeding what was adjudged in the impugned judgment, the fee shall be collected on such excess, provided that in all the preceding instances the fixed fee collected in advance must be deducted from the principal of the proportional fee due

Where a proportional fee has been paid in any case and its amount exceeds the fixed fee, the fee paid in advance shall be refunded after deducting the fixed fee, in the following cases:

1- Where the court rules to dismiss the action in form

2- Where the action is dismissed in its present state

3- Where the court declines jurisdiction over it for lack of jurisdiction, lis pendens, or any other reason

4- Where the proceedings are annulled

5- Where the court rules to accept the discontinuance by the plaintiff of his action or the withdrawal by the appellant of his appeal prior to the issuance of the judgment

6- Where the Court of Cassation rules to accept the withdrawal by the petitioner in cassation of his petition in cassation prior to the issuance of the judgment

7- Where the appeal and the petition in cassation are dismissed in form

Nothing of the fee paid in advance shall be refunded where judgment is rendered on the merits or in the event of the abatement of the action and the amount collected exceeds the fixed fee. The fee paid in advance shall then suffice

In the event that judgment is rendered for part of the claim, the fee shall be levied in proportion to the sum adjudged, and where such fee is less than the fee paid in advance, nothing thereof shall be refunded
All provisions prescribed in the tariff of the courts of first instance shall apply before the courts of appeal, subject to the provisions of the following articles

Tariff of the Courts of Appeal

The amount of the fixed fee before the Court of Appeal shall be fixed at /350,000/ L.L. (three hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese pounds).

The proportional fee shall be levied, whether from the principal appellant or the appellant in an incidental appeal, in proportion to the amount or the assessable thing that is the subject of the appeal; however, if the principal or incidental appeal concerns an unassessable thing, the fixed fee shall be levied from him.

If the appeal is dismissed in form, the fixed fee shall be due. If the appealed decision is overturned and the case is remitted to the court of first instance, the fixed fee shall be due. If the appeal aims to increase what was adjudged in first instance and the Court of Appeal upholds the appealed judgment and does not award the increase, such upholding shall be deemed a dismissal of the action on the merits and the fixed fee shall be due; however, if an increase is adjudged, the fee shall be levied on the basis of such increase. If the appeal aims to discharge the judgment debtor from liability or to reduce what was adjudged, and the Court of Appeal upholds or amends the judgment, the fee shall be levied on what is adjudged on appeal out of that which was the subject of the appeal.
Appeals brought against disciplinary judgments and decisions issued by councils of syndicates shall be subject to the fixed fee and to all other judicial fees and deposits set forth in this Law.

All the provisions stipulated in the tariff of the courts of first instance, and in Articles 29, 30 and 31 of the tariff of fees of the appellate courts, shall apply before the Court of Cassation, subject to the provisions of the following Articles:

Tariff of the Court of Cassation

The amount of the fixed fee before the Court of Cassation shall be set at /500,000/ L.L. (five hundred thousand Lebanese pounds)"

The following cases shall be subject to the fixed fee:

1- Complaint against judges

2- Applications for transfer of the action submitted by one of the litigants

3- Applications for designation of the competent authority submitted by one of the litigants

4- Objection to the jurisdiction of a confessional or Sharia court to issue judgment and to its enforceability

5- Applications for annulment on the ground of excess of power of administrative decrees, decisions and orders issued by administrative authorities

6- Disputes relating to the legality of elections for administrative councils

7- Applications for annulment of decisions issued in disciplinary cases of administrative employees

The registry fees are:

1- The registration fee

2- The copy fee

The amount of the registration fee is 10,000 L.L. This fee shall be collected in all criminal courts and the judicial departments attached thereto for the registration of all papers of complaint, counter-complaint, petitions, special powers of attorney, the expert's report and the documents attached thereto submitted to him by the two parties, and for all other pleadings, memoranda and written papers, and for every opposition, appeal or petition for cassation.

If several documents are copied onto a single sheet of paper, the registration fee shall be collected on each of those documents.

If a document is produced in a lawsuit and a registration fee is collected thereon, and it is subsequently produced in another lawsuit, a new registration fee shall be collected thereon. No registration fee shall be collected on a translation if it is attached to the original on which the fee has been collected.

The amount of the copy fee is 10,000 L.L.

This fee shall be collected on copies of judgments and decisions requested by one of the two parties or by a third party to the lawsuit.

There shall be levied on copies of judgments and decisions awarding personal damages a proportional fee in the amount of 2,5% two and a half per cent, whatever the amount of the sum awarded.

Neither of the two parties shall be given a certified copy of judgments and decisions prior to the collection of the proportional fee due.

A convicted person in felony cases, when filing a petition for cassation against the judgment, shall be exempted from paying the proportional fees provided for in this Article.

As for misdemeanor matters, he shall be exempted from these fees if he submits a certificate of indigence from the mukhtar.

It must be stated at the foot of the copy of the judgment that it is valid for use only for the benefit of the convicted person in the petition for cassation before the Court of Cassation.
There shall be collected on certified copies of documents, reports and all other papers lawfully given to the interested parties a fee in the amount of 10.000 L.L.

Fees for Criminal Decisions and Judgments

The following fees shall be levied on criminal decisions and judgments:

1 - For final decisions of the investigating judge issued against a single defendant: 20,000 L.L.

If there are multiple defendants, 10,000 L.L. shall be collected in respect of each of them.

These fees shall be collected upon the conclusion of the action.

B - For judgments issued by courts of first instance against a single defendant: 20,000 L.L.

If there are multiple convicted persons, 10.000 L.L. shall be collected in respect of each of them.

However, judgments issued - without summoning the defendant - for contraventions of municipal, health and traffic regulations pursuant to the provisions of Article 183 of the Code of Criminal Procedure shall not be subject to the judgment fee.

C- For judgments issued by non-felony Courts of Appeal, against a single convicted person: 40.000 L.L,

If there are multiple convicted persons, 20.000 L.L. shall be collected in respect of each of them.

D- For judgments issued by courts hearing felony cases against a single convicted person: 100,000 L.L,

If there are multiple convicted persons, 60,000 L.L. shall be collected in respect of each of them.

However, judgments issued pursuant to an appeal by the Public Prosecution without the plaintiff and the convicted person shall not be subject to the judgment fee if the appealed judgment is upheld.

E - For judgments issued by the Court of Cassation in non-felony criminal cases:

1- In the event that the appeal in cassation is dismissed on procedural grounds: 100,000 L.L. for each application for enforcement.

2- In the event that the judgment is upheld or quashed and the action is adjudicated anew: 100,000 L.L for each convicted person.

F- For felony judgments:

In the event that the appeal in cassation is dismissed on procedural grounds or in the event that the judgment is upheld or quashed and the action is adjudicated anew: 100,000 L.L for each convicted person.
Applications for the determination of jurisdiction and for retrial in criminal cases shall not be subject to the decision and judgment fee

The provisions of the criminal tariff shall apply before the Military Court, the provisions of the tariff pertaining to the Felony Court shall apply before the Judicial Council, and the tariff pertaining to the courts of first instance shall apply before the Courts of Appeal and the Publications Court

Judicial expenses in criminal cases are divided into two parts:

First- Expenses advanced by the Treasury and subsequently recovered from the convicted person

Second- Expenses borne by the Treasury Expenses of the first part:

1- Expenses of travel allowances for trial and investigating judges, public prosecutors, judicial assistants, experts, interpreters, and members of the armed forces who assist and accompany them when they travel to carry out acts of investigation

2- Fees of travel and accommodation allowances for witnesses

3- Fees of experts

4- Expenses of medical care and treatment of persons injured in criminal incidents

5- Expenses of custody, safekeeping, and affixing of seals

6- All other expenses ordered by the judicial authority to carry out an inspection or to establish an offence

7- Costs of enforcement of the judgment

Expenses of the second part are:

1- Fees of telegrams and postal correspondence

2- Costs of transporting confiscated objects and materials

3- Costs of transporting detainees and the expenses necessary for their subsistence

4- Every expense of this kind required by the criminal action

The civil claimant shall, upon filing the action, advance by way of security against the expenses and costs of the investigation the amount assessed by the judge to whom the action is submitted, and if he refuses and the action is of the nature of a felony or a misdemeanour that disturbs public security, it shall proceed in the name of the public right, whereas if it relates to an ordinary offence the investigation of which entails expenses and disbursements, the judge may decide to shelve it until the required amount is advanced on the basis of the facts and circumstances of the action; whereas in a direct action, the civil claimant must advance the deposit assessed by the judge, failing which his action shall be shelved; the judge may, during the investigation or the trial, request the civil claimant to advance an additional amount if it appears to him that the advanced expenses are insufficient; the deposit shall be placed in trust in the Treasury fund in the name of its owner, and the costs shall be paid therefrom when needed; the deposit, or what remains thereof, shall be returned to the civil claimant if it appears in the outcome that he is justified in his action; whereas if he is ordered to pay a decree and expenses, the deposit or what remains thereof shall not be returned to him until after he has paid the fees and expenses or after they have been deducted from the principal of the deposit

The civil claimant shall be exempted from advancing the expenses in the following cases:

1- If his financial condition does not enable him to advance them and he proves his inability by a certificate issued by the mukhtar of his place of residence and one of the members of the council of elders where a council of elders exists therein

2- If the case is of the nature of a felony

Judicial expenses in criminal actions

If there is no civil claimant in the case or if payment of the advance is impossible for the reasons set forth in the preceding Articles, the necessary expenses

shall be advanced by the Treasury, subject to subsequent recovery from the convicted person.

If the expenses do not exceed 250,000 L.L., the judge seized of the action may order their disbursement from the Treasury fund,

and if they exceed this amount, the approval of the Ministry of Justice must be obtained therefor.

In urgent cases where the disappearance of the traces of the offence is feared, approval may be obtained by telegram or by telephone, with mention thereof being made

in the record of the action and the disbursement decision.

If the expenses exceeding the amount of 250,000 L.L. are fixed by a provision, there shall be no need for the approval of the Ministry of Justice for their disbursement.

The provisions of Part One of Book One of this Law relating to the tariff of fees of the courts of first instance shall apply before the Sharia courts of first instance, subject to the provisions of the following Articles

Upon the submission of an application for the renewal of a representative judgment pursuant to the provisions of Article 153 of Legislative Decree No. 241 dated 4 November 1942, only a summons fee in respect of the plaintiff or plaintiffs and the registration fee shall be levied
An application for the renewal of an action ordered to be struck out pursuant to the provisions of Article 130 of Legislative Decree No. 341 shall be deemed to constitute a new action

The proportional fee in the actions set forth below shall be calculated in the following manner:

1- Actions concerning betrothal for marriage and its gift - on the basis of the amount or the value of the thing claimed

2- Actions concerning the trousseau - in proportion to its value

3- Actions concerning the dower - on the value claimed

4- Actions for the accounting of a guardian, a mutawalli, or a curator - the fixed fee provided for in Article 12 of this Law shall be levied in advance upon the submission of the action, and if the action results in a judgment for a specified amount, the proportional fee shall be levied on the amount adjudged after deducting the fixed fee already levied

5- In actions applying for the exchange of a waqf - on the value of the property given in exchange

The following actions shall be deemed equivalent to actions not susceptible of valuation and subject to the fixed fee:

1- Actions to establish marriage, divorce and separation

2- Actions to establish inheritance, lineage, puberty or majority

3- Actions for custody

4- Actions to join boys and girls to their legal guardians

5- Actions to lift an attachment

6- Actions for the removal of a testamentary guardian, curator or endowment administrator (mutawalli)

7- Actions for rendering the accounts of a testamentary guardian, curator or endowment administrator (mutawalli). Provided that the provisions of the fourth paragraph of Article 50 of this Law are observed

8- Actions challenging instruments issued by the Sharia courts

9- Actions for entitlement in an endowment (waqf) and all other actions relating to an endowment (waqf)

10- Actions of third-party opposition and opposition to judgments in absentia, provided that the provisions of the first and second paragraphs of Article 23 of this Law are observed

11- Actions for retrial, provided that the provisions of paragraph 3 of Article 23 of this Law are observed

12- Actions of opposition to travel ban decisions

13- Actions concerning execution difficulties

14- Applications for the interpretation or rectification of judgments - provided that the fee is ultimately calculated on the basis of the rectified judgment.

15- Applications for precautionary attachment or the release thereof.

16- Actions to establish the right to an attachment. If not accompanied by a claim for judgment on the debt which is the cause of the attachment, failing which they shall be subject to the proportional fee only.

17- Actions for the annulment of a will
Following the inventory of the estate, a registration fee of six per thousand of the value of the estate shall be levied.
In respect of the inventory of the estate - following its liquidation and the payment of the debts, liabilities and expenses due thereon - a fee of five per cent of the net value shall be levied.
A fee of two per thousand shall be levied on the debtor in respect of sums borrowed from the Orphans' Fund.

In respect of rendering the accounts of a testamentary guardian, curator or endowment administrator (mutawalli), a fee of two and a half per cent shall be levied on the remaining value after deducting the sums expended

Fees for Sharia instruments and others:

1- Instrument establishing death and determination of heirs 2.500 L.L.

2- Instrument appointing a testamentary guardian and a legal guardian curator 2.500 L.L.

3- Instrument appointing an administrator (mutawalli) for an endowment (waqf) 10.000 L.L.

4- Instrument granting authorisation to a legal guardian and a testamentary guardian 2.500 L.L.

5- Instrument granting authorisation to an administrator (mutawalli) over endowments (waqfs) 10.000 L.L.

6- Instrument of interdiction 5.000 L.L.

7- Instrument of marriage deed 5.000 L.L.

8- Instrument of divorce in absentia 5.000 L.L.

9- Drawing up and registering a deed of will 50.000 L.L.

10- Granting authorisation to conclude a marriage contract 2.500 L.L.

11- Drawing up and registering an endowment deed (waqfiyya) in proportion to the amount or value of the endowed property 5% (five per cent)

12- Other instruments not mentioned above 5.000 L.L.
The fees for documents shall be borne by the applicant for registration and shall be paid in advance.
A fee in the amount of 2,500 L.L. shall be collected for drawing up special powers of attorney in lawsuits and matters falling within the jurisdiction of the Sharia Courts.

All provisions stipulated in the tariff of the Sharia Courts of First Instance, and in the tariff of the Civil Courts of Appeal, shall apply before the Sharia Court of Appeal, subject to the provisions of the following Articles.
Lawsuits sent automatically to the Court of Appeal pursuant to the provisions of Article 160 of Legislative Decree No. 241 dated 4 November 1942 shall not be subject to appellate fees.

The following lawsuits shall be deemed equivalent to lawsuits not susceptible of valuation and subject to the fixed fee:

1- A request for the recusal and disqualification of judges

2- A complaint against judges

3- A request for the transfer of the lawsuit

4- A request for the designation of the competent authority

The provisions of Chapter One of Book One of this Law relating to the registry decree shall apply before the Execution Departments. The conditions of sale shall be subject to the registration fee. The fee for summonses, service of process and copies in execution difficulties cases shall be collected in accordance with the provisions of Articles 3, 4 and 5 of this Law.
Execution fees are of two types: fixed and proportional.

Execution fees - The fixed fee

A fixed fee shall be collected in advance for the following requests:

1- Precautionary attachment and the lifting thereof 250000 L.L.

2- Garnishment in the hands of a third party, the limitation thereof and the lifting thereof 250000 L.L.

3- Attachment in revendication and the lifting thereof 250000 L.L.

4 - Compulsory mortgage and the lifting thereof 250000 L.L.
Upon the execution of a will, a fixed fee in the amount of /1,000,000/ L.L. (one million Lebanese pounds) shall be levied."

There shall be levied in advance upon the execution of judicial judgments and official deeds relating to things not susceptible of valuation a fixed fee equal to the fee paid before the court which issued the judgment on the merits or before the officer who certified or accepted the official deed
Upon the execution of a will, a fixed fee in the amount of twenty-five Lebanese pounds shall be levied

(As amended by Law No. 14/81 dated 15/7/81) and by Law No. 710 dated 5/11/98.

In respect of the execution of judicial judgments and official deeds, a proportional fee in the amount of (2,5%) (two and a half per cent) shall be levied on the amount sought to be collected, even if its amount does not exceed one hundred pounds, in addition to the accrued interest, damages, attorneys' fees, trial fees and the awarded expenses.

One quarter of this fee shall be paid in advance and the remainder upon collection.

And the fee shall be finally liquidated on the basis of the value collected.

And the same fee shall be levied on all judgments and official deeds relating to things susceptible of valuation.

Explanatory text: Interpretation of certain provisions of Article 67 of the Judicial Fees Law

The Proportional Fee

If the judgment creditor requests the lifting of an attachment adjudged to be confirmed from the property of his debtor without having requested the collection of the value awarded to him, the proportional fee shall not be levied on this value, but rather the fixed fee for lifting the attachment in the amount of / 250,000/ L.L. (two hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese pounds).

If the two parties reach a settlement during the execution proceedings for an amount less than the amount which the judgment creditor requested to be collected, or if he withdraws from the execution and requests the lifting of the attachment or the performance of any formality, the fee shall be taken on the basis of the amount specified in the application requesting execution

Upon the execution of mortgage and pledge contracts, a proportional fee in the amount of (2,5%) two and a half per cent shall be levied on the amount sought to be collected including the accrued interest.

Upon foreign deeds and judgments granted the executory formula in accordance with the rules, there shall be levied the same fee due to be levied had the deed been drawn up before a Lebanese official officer

Judgments, decisions and instruments presented for enforcement without the fees due thereon having been collected in whole or in part by the court that issued them or by the officer who certified them shall not be proceeded with for enforcement unless the fees due thereon and the enforcement fees are collected.

An auction fee of two and a half per cent of the sale price shall be collected on sales by public auction of various movable and immovable articles and properties, provided that the sale shall not take place except in the presence of the delegate of the municipality or after summoning him. This fee shall be borne by the purchaser and shall be levied for the benefit of the municipality within the jurisdiction of which the sold item is located; whereas in places where there is no municipality, the auction fee shall accrue to the Treasury fund. The enforcement officer is prohibited from retaining the auction fee accruing to the municipalities, and it must be paid to the entitled municipality or deposited in trust with the Treasury fund, and the municipality shall be notified thereof in order to collect it.
All fees and expenses of enforcement shall ultimately be borne by the party against whom enforcement is carried out and shall be recovered without a judgment.

In the event of the lapse of the enforcement proceeding in accordance with the provisions of Legislative Decree No. 82 dated 20 January 1941, the fees paid shall become the right of the Treasury and shall not be claimed from the party against whom enforcement is carried out, and upon the submission of an application to renew the enforcement, the fee shall be collected anew.

In cases of legal aid, the proceeding shall be conducted for the holder thereof without advance payment of expenses, in accordance with the conditions and procedures stipulated in Articles 436 et seq. of the Code of Civil Procedure. From the funds resulting from enforcement and accruing to the holder of legal aid, the fees and expenses due must first be deducted and paid to the Treasury fund.
If the auction is awarded to the holder of legal aid, he may not obtain a copy of the decision of award until after the payment of all fees and expenses of the proceeding.

Judicial Deposits

First- Before the Civil Courts

1 - In cases of retrial and third-party opposition, whether before the courts of first instance or the courts of appeal:

a- If the value of the lawsuit does not exceed five hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds 50,000 L.L.

b- If its value exceeds five hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds or if it is among the cases that are not subject to valuation:

Before the courts of first instance 100,000 L.L.

Before the courts of appeal 150,000 L.L.

2- In appealed administrative and civil cases:

a- If the value of the lawsuit does not exceed five hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds 50,000 L.L.

b - If its value exceeds five hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds or if it is among the cases that are not subject to valuation 100.000 L.L.

c- In disciplinary cases issued by the councils of syndicates 100,000 L.L.

Second- Before the Court of Cassation

1 - In civil cases appealed in cassation 50,000 L.L.

2 - In criminal cases appealed in cassation 200.000 L.L.

3 - In a complaint against judges 400,000 L.L.

Third- Before the Sharia Courts

1- In cases of retrial before the courts of first instance 20.000 L.L.

2- In appealed Sharia cases 20.000 L.L.

3- In cases of retrial before the court of appeal 40.000.L.

4- In a complaint against judges 100.000 L.L.

The deposit specified in the preceding Article shall be collected from the principal petitioner. If there are multiple principal petitioners in a single petition, a single deposit shall suffice. If there are multiple applications for cassation and the petitioners have a unified interest, a single deposit shall suffice.
Lawsuits whose value does not exceed twenty-five thousand Pounds and all cases of means of recourse submitted in respect thereof shall be exempted from judicial fees or from deposits.

The State shall be exempted, in all actions brought by or against it, from paying judicial fees, fiscal stamps, and the pleading duty, in respect of all documents produced by it and formalities requested by it in the name and for the benefit of the public departments included in its budget, and from paying judicial deposits and furnishing security in all cases in which the law imposes the same upon litigants."

"This exemption shall include the Customs Departments, the National Lottery, the National Reconstruction Authority - and the Bank of Lebanon, and all official public institutions, autonomous services, and municipalities.

This exemption shall include the Customs Departments, the National Lottery, the National Reconstruction Authority - and the Bank of Lebanon, and all official public institutions and autonomous services."

Cases relating to the operation of the Tobacco and Tombac Monopoly Administration shall be exempted

from all judicial fees and deposits and fiscal stamps.

If the State or one of the departments referred to above wins the action, all fees and expenses that it did not pay by reason of the exemption shall be collected upon enforcement from the party against whom judgment is rendered and paid into the Treasury fund.

Actions and all formalities conducted before the Real Estate Judge shall be exempted from all judicial fees and stamp duties, and the exemption shall not extend to such actions before the Courts of Appeal and Cassation.

Cases of alimony, custody allowance, and nursing allowance shall be exempted from judicial fees and deposits and fiscal stamps in all ordinary and Sharia courts and enforcement departments; however, cases of enforcement difficulties raised by the party against whom enforcement is sought regarding the enforcement of judgments rendered in such cases shall not be covered by this exemption in respect of the party against whom enforcement is sought.
Labour actions submitted to the Arbitration Councils shall be exempted from all judicial fees and deposits and from enforcement fees.
Cases relating to the salaries of State employees, their retirement pensions, and their end-of-service indemnities shall be exempted from all judicial fees and deposits.
In cases of legal aid, the formality for the applicant therefor shall be conducted in accordance with the provisions of Articles 436 et seq. of the Code of Civil Procedure.

The calculation of fees in civil and Sharia cases shall be carried out by the court registry, and the amount shall be paid directly by the concerned parties to the Treasury fund; as for courts at whose seats there are no finance cash offices, the instructions issued by the Ministry of Justice in this regard shall be followed.

The judgment creditor may proceed to collect the fees and expenses after the judgment has acquired final force, by obtaining from the registry of the court an enforceable copy containing a statement of the fees and expenses which he has incurred
The fees, expenses and fines due to the Treasury shall be collected from the judgment debtor by the methods provided for in the Code of Criminal Procedure and in the Penal Code

If the judgment debtor has sums deposited in the Treasury fund by way of security bail for his release, or other sums belonging to him, the fees, expenses and fines may be collected from the said sums while observing the order of priority provided for in Article 116 of the Code of Criminal Procedure

Criminal judgments awarding personal damages the extraction of which is not requested by those in whose favour judgment is rendered within two months of their becoming final shall have an abstract thereof drawn up individually against the judgment debtor with respect to the fiscal fees and stamps due on such damages, and these abstracts shall be sent for enforcement after serving him with ten days' notice, and on the basis of these abstracts the collection of the fees and stamps shall be pursued in the same manner as judicial expenses are collected in criminal actions

Judicial fees and expenses awarded in favour of the Treasury shall lapse by the prescription period fixed for state funds pursuant to the provisions of Article 443 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, and every claim relating to the payment of a fee shall also lapse within the same period as from the date on which the document in respect of which the fee became due was submitted, completed or received

Every claim relating to the recovery of fees alleged to have been unduly levied and which are refundable pursuant to the provisions of this Law shall lapse after the passage of two years from the date of issuance of the final judgment or the decision finally disposing of the action

In actions the value of which does not exceed two thousand pounds, the power of attorney therein before the Single Judge may be drawn up before the Mukhtar or by a written declaration on the record of the proceedings, provided that the stamp duties imposed in these two cases are levied

The provisions of this Law shall apply to all actions and transactions submitted to all courts and judicial departments on the date it is put into force, and shall also apply to cases of means of recourse submitted in respect of judgments issued prior to the said date
The registries of the courts and the enforcement departments must indicate the type and amount of the fees collected on the statement of claim or the application for enforcement

If an error occurs in the collection of the fee, the registry shall require the party concerned to complete it. If a dispute arises over the amount of the fee between the registry and the parties concerned, the matter of deciding thereon shall rest with the court by a final decision rendered in chambers in accordance with the provisions of Article 423 et seq. of the Code of Civil Procedure

The registry of the court shall indicate in detail on the record of the trial and on the enforceable copy of the judgment all the fees and expenses legally established, whether accruing to the judgment creditor or to the Treasury, and all the fees and expenses must also be indicated at the foot of the documents produced by the Government and the departments exempted pursuant to the provisions of Article 80 of this Law or requested by them in their capacity as one of the litigants

Whatever the degree and type of the courts, final decisions and judgments the extraction of which is not requested by their holders within two months from the date of their issuance shall have an extract thereof drawn up individually against the judgment debtor with respect to the judicial fees and expenses due to the Treasury and the share accruing to the Lawyers' Retirement Fund from the lawyers' fees awarded, and this extract shall be sent for enforcement after the lapse of ten days from giving him formal notice, and the said fees and expenses shall be recovered from the party ordered to pay them in the same manner as fees and expenses are recovered in criminal actions. The judicial fees and expenses that must be recovered are:

1- The completion of the judgment fees

2- The fee for copies where service is legally required

3- The stamp duty due on the judgment and the copies

4- The amounts advanced by the Treasury

5- The amounts due to the Treasury pursuant to the provisions of Article 82 of this Law and Article 439 of the Code of Civil Procedure

6- The share accruing to the Lawyers' Retirement Fund from the lawyers' fees awarded, which shall be paid to the Bar Association entitled thereto or deposited in trust for its account in the Treasury fund, and it shall be notified thereof so that it may collect the same
The fees and expenses of the trial in the case of legal aid shall be governed by the provisions of Article 436 et seq. of the Code of Civil Procedure

The registries of the criminal courts and the investigating departments must indicate in the margin of the judgments and decisions the judicial fees and expenses that must be recovered for the benefit of the Treasury or for the benefit of individuals

The Judicial Fees Law promulgated on 8 January 1938 and all texts supplementing or amending it are hereby repealed, and every legislative text contrary to the provisions of this Law or inconsistent therewith is also repealed.
This Law shall be published in the Official Gazette.

The first paragraph of Article 18 of Legislative Decree No. 146 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Transfer Duty) is repealed and replaced by the following text: The duty is incurred by the beneficiaries of the waqf, with the exception of the founder of the waqf himself, and is levied on the value of the entitlement assessed in accordance with the third paragraph of Article 36 of this Legislative Decree after deducting an amount of one million six hundred thousand pounds from the value of the share of each beneficiary.

Article 19 of Legislative Decree No. 146 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Transfer Duty) is repealed and replaced by the following text: The duty is incurred upon the termination of the waqf on two-thirds of the value of the property and is levied on the value of the share of each right holder after deducting an amount of one million six hundred thousand pounds.

The text of Article 21 of Legislative Decree No. 146 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Transfer Duty) is repealed and replaced by the following text: The heirs, donees, beneficiaries of a waqf, and executors of wills and waqfs, or those who legally represent them, must submit to the competent financial departments, within 90 (ninety) days from the occurrence of the death, donation, execution of the will or waqf, or judgment declaring the death of an absent person, a declaration containing the name of the decedent, donor, founder of the waqf, or testator, and the names of the heirs, donees, legatees, beneficiaries of the waqf, and executors of the will or waqf, along with the place of residence of each of them and the contents of the transferred property of various kinds, in addition to its location and its true sale value. The concerned parties shall attach to the declaration the supporting documents (the death certificate, family civil status extracts for the deceased and for the heirs, title deeds or real estate certificates, the instrument of the will or the contract of donation), and the aforementioned concerned parties must also submit the remaining documents and proofs relating to their declaration within a period of six months at most from the date of the occurrence of the event by reason of which the duty was incurred (death, will, donation, waqf, termination of the waqf). The supporting documents that must be submitted for each type of event as a result of which the duty was incurred shall be determined by decisions issued by the Minister of Finance. The competent department must complete the estate file and issue the collection order relating to it within a time limit not exceeding three months from the date of submission of the documents and proofs relating to the declaration. In the event of failure to submit the declaration and documents, the competent department shall resort to direct assessment as at the date of death, provided that it completes the estate file and issues the collection order for the tax and fines incurred within a time limit of six months from the date of expiry of the time limit for submitting the documents.

The text of the fourth and fifth paragraphs of the ninth Article of Legislative Decree No. 146 dated 12/6/1959 (Transfer Duty) and its amendments has been amended and replaced by the following text:

4- Collections of antique books, decorations, and other collections and furniture located in the residence of the decedent, within a maximum limit of forty million pounds; as for scientific and literary books, they shall be exempted in full from the duty.

The last paragraph added pursuant to Law No. 7/68 dated 8/1/1968 to Article 13 of Legislative Decree No. 146 dated 12 June 1959 (Transfer Duty) has been repealed

The text of Article 16 of Legislative Decree No. 146 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Transfer Duty) has been repealed and replaced by the following text: All assistance, subsidies, and grants paid from public funds shall be exempted from duties, and every gift whose value does not exceed one million and six hundred thousand pounds shall also be exempted, and if it exceeds that, the duty shall be levied on the excess, unless the donee is a charitable institution or a sports, cultural, artistic, charitable, or religious association, including religious endowments (waqfs), in which case the exemption shall cover an amount of one hundred million pounds.

The text of Article 22 of Legislative Decree No. 146 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Transfer Duty) is hereby repealed and replaced by the following text: The time limit for submitting the declaration or the time limit for submitting the remaining documents and proofs shall not run against the heirs, donees, legatees and waqf beneficiaries in respect of any estate, gift, bequest or waqf that is the subject of a judicial dispute except with effect from the date of issuance of the final judgment in the dispute.

The text of Article 26 of Legislative Decree No. 146 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Transfer Duty) is hereby repealed and replaced by the following text: If any of the persons mentioned in the preceding Article delivers anything in his possession in violation of the provisions of that Article, he shall be deemed liable towards the Treasury for the duty payable on what he relinquished, in addition to being assessed a fine equal to the value of the said duty, and if the estate is not subject to the transfer duty, a fine of three hundred thousand pounds shall be imposed on the offender.

The fine imposed in the third paragraph of Article 28 of Legislative Decree No. 146 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Transfer Duty) has been raised so as to become from fifty thousand pounds to five hundred thousand pounds, and the text of the final paragraph of the same Article, added pursuant to Law No. 7/68 dated 8/1/1968, is hereby repealed.

The text of Article 29 of Legislative Decree No. 146 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Transfer Duty) is hereby repealed and replaced by the following text: The creditor of the estate or whoever holds a registered or unregistered right against it shall submit to the competent financial authorities, within three months from the date of his knowledge of the death, a statement of the original and current amount of the debt, its nature, its origin and its terms, and of the documents, instruments and apparent or concealed mortgages in his possession, and if the creditor does not submit the said statement within the specified time limit, a fine equal to the value of the duty that may be payable by the heirs due to the non-deduction of this debt from the basis of the estate shall be imposed on him, and if the estate is not subject to the transfer duty, a fine of three hundred thousand pounds shall be imposed on the offending creditor.

The fine provided for in Article 30 of Legislative Decree No. 146 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Transfer Duty) has been amended so as to range between twenty thousand pounds and one hundred thousand pounds.

The text of Article 46 of Legislative Decree No. 146 dated 12 June 1959 and its amendments (the Transfer Duty Law) is repealed and replaced by the following text: The duty must be paid in a single lump sum in accordance with the provisions relating to the collection of direct taxes and duties similar thereto whenever the share of the person liable therefor includes cash and financial instruments that can be sold and whose value exceeds the value of the transfer duty due from him, and if the share of the person liable is devoid of cash or financial instruments that can be sold for such value, the collection and recovery departments may divide the imposed transfer duties into five equal annual instalments, the first of which falls due six months from the date of issuance of the collection order, and an annotation of payment by instalments shall be placed on the real estate register sheet. The instalments shall fall due in full upon failure to pay any of the instalments on its due date. In the event of disposal of any of the transferred property, the consideration shall be allocated to the settlement of the deferred duties unless the Treasury's funds are secured by the equivalent of at least twice their value. Upon payment by instalments, the provisions relating to prescription shall not apply. Interest at the rate of one percent per month (1%) shall be due on the amounts paid by instalments in accordance with the provisions set out above. This interest shall be collected with each instalment, provided that it falls due in full when the full instalments fall due. For the purpose of calculating the interest, a fraction of a month shall be deemed a full month.

The text of Article 33 of Legislative Decree No. 146 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Transfer Duty) is repealed and replaced by the following text: If the concerned parties neglect to submit the declarations and their attachments, or neglect to submit the remaining documents within the time limits specified in Article 21 of this Legislative Decree, or are late in submitting them, they shall be punished for each of these two infractions with a fine equivalent to ten percent for each month of delay or fraction of a month of the value of the duty incurred on the property, rights or values not declared within the time limit, provided that the fine for each of these two infractions does not exceed the value of the duty on the basis of which it is imposed, and that it is not less in all cases, even if no duty is incurred, than two hundred and fifty thousand pounds for each concerned party.

The first paragraph of Article /34/ is amended and replaced by the following text: Whoever intentionally conceals a part of the property covered by the duty or issues false declarations regarding the debts or rights relating to the estate, gift, bequest or endowment shall be punished with a fine from one million pounds to five million pounds.

The second paragraph of Article /43/ of Legislative Decree No. 146 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Transfer Duty) is amended and replaced by the following text: This lump-sum additional duty shall be due on the part of the gross total value of the transferred rights, property and values that exceeds forty million Lebanese pounds, and it shall be considered among the debts and obligations incurred on the total of the aforementioned elements.

All movable and immovable rights and property that devolved to third parties by way of inheritance, bequest, gift or waqf shall be subject to the provisions of this Law with respect to chargeable events occurring as of 14/10/1994 for which the transfer duty has not been paid or which remain the subject of an objection by taxpayers of whatever kind as at the date of entry into force of this Law, and the values of the transferred property and rights based on the prices prevailing at the date of the chargeable event shall be taken as the basis for assessment. As for chargeable events occurring prior to 14/10/1994 for which assessments have not been issued up to the date of entry into force of this Law, each of them shall be subject to the registration fee with the competent departments on the basis of the following rates, provided that the valuation of the property and rights is carried out in accordance with the prices prevailing on 13/10/1994:

- 1% on descendants, spouses, parents, brothers and sisters and - 2% with respect to the remaining beneficiaries, as regards chargeable events occurring prior to 1/1/1992

- 2% on descendants, spouses, parents, brothers and sisters and 4% with respect to the remaining beneficiaries, as regards chargeable events occurring from 1/1/1992 until 13/10/1994

The competent judicial authorities shall be permitted, with regard to chargeable events occurring prior to 14/10/1994, to grant the determination of heirs and the execution of wills to the concerned parties without their producing the required authorisation issued by the competent financial departments.

The schedule of transfer duty rates on taxable shares and brackets is hereby repealed and replaced by the schedule annexed to this Law, provided that no surcharge shall be added to the amount of the duty notwithstanding any contrary provision.

The Treasury Directorate at the Ministry of Finance shall annually deduct a rate of 10% (ten per cent) in favour of the municipalities from the total amounts finally collected on account of the transfer duty.
Where necessary, the details of application of this Law shall be determined by decrees upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

No penalty shall be imposed that was not prescribed by the law at the time the offence was committed. An offence shall be deemed committed as soon as the acts of its execution are completed, regardless of the time at which the result occurs.
Every new law, even if more severe, shall apply to continuing, continuous and successive offences or offences of habit the execution of which has been persisted in under its authority.
Every new law that abolishes a lighter penalty shall apply to offences committed before its entry into force, unless an irrevocable judgment has been issued in respect thereof.

Every new law that imposes more severe penalties shall not apply to offences committed before its entry into force; provided that if the new law amends the rules of concurrence of offences and recidivism, the offences committed and the penalties imposed before its entry into force shall be taken into consideration upon the repression of an act committed under its authority.

Every new law that amends the manner of execution of one of the penalties by changing its nature shall not apply to acts committed before its entry into force unless it is more favourable to the defendant or the convicted person.

The nature of a penalty is changed when the new law amends the legal rules assigned to the chapter on penalties of this law.
Every new law that amends the period of prescription for a penalty shall apply in accordance with the conditions specified in the fifth article.
No precautionary measure or reformative measure shall be imposed except under the conditions and in the circumstances prescribed by the law.

Every new law that establishes a precautionary measure or a reformative measure shall apply to offences that have not been adjudicated by the last judicial body having jurisdiction as to the facts. As for penalties imposed before the entry into force of the new law, they shall be counted upon the repression of an act committed under its authority in applying the provisions relating to habitual criminality.

Every precautionary measure and every reformatory measure that the law has abolished or replaced with another measure shall cease to have any effect, and if a final judgment has been rendered, the trial shall be reopened to apply the new precautionary or reformatory measure.

Lebanese law shall apply to all offences committed in Lebanese territory. An offence shall be deemed committed in Lebanese territory:

1- If one of the elements constituting the offence, or an act of an indivisible offence, or an act of principal or accessory participation is carried out in this territory.

2- If the result occurs in this territory or was expected to occur therein.
Lebanese territory shall include the layer of air covering it, namely the airspace.

The following shall be treated as Lebanese territory for the purpose of applying the criminal law:

1- The territorial sea to a distance of twenty kilometres from the shore, starting from the lowest level of the ebb tide,

2- The airspace covering the territorial sea,

3- Lebanese vessels and aircraft

4- Foreign territory occupied by a Lebanese army, if the offences committed prejudice the safety or interests of the army.

5- The contiguous zone, the exclusive economic zone, and the continental shelf appertaining to Lebanon, and the fixed platforms on this continental shelf, in application of the provisions of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea signed on 10/12/1982 in Montego Bay (Jamaica), to which the Government was authorised to accede pursuant to Law No. 29 dated 22/02/1994.

Lebanese law shall not apply:

1- In the Lebanese airspace, to offences committed on board a foreign aircraft, if the offence does not extend beyond the boundary of the aircraft.

However, offences that do not extend beyond the boundary of the aircraft shall be subject to Lebanese law if the perpetrator or the victim is Lebanese, or if the aircraft lands in Lebanon after the commission of the offence,

2- In the Lebanese territorial sea or in the airspace covering it, to offences committed on board a foreign vessel or aircraft if the offence does not extend beyond the boundary of the vessel or aircraft

3- Repealed by the Law dated 12/1/1946

- Offences of seizure of foreign vessels or of goods transported thereon shall be subject to Lebanese law, if such vessels enter the Lebanese territorial waters.

- Every offence committed in or on the vessel while it is in this state shall be subject to Lebanese law, subject to international conventions approved by the Lebanese authorities.

- Furthermore, the offence of seizure of goods from vessels, occurring outside the territorial waters, shall be subject to Lebanese law if such goods are introduced into the Lebanese territory for local consumption or by way of "transit

e.

Lebanese laws shall apply to every Lebanese, foreign or stateless person, whether as a perpetrator, accomplice, instigator or accessory, who proceeds outside the Lebanese territory or on board a foreign aircraft or vessel:

1- To commit offences prejudicial to the security of the State, or counterfeiting the seal of the State, or counterfeiting or falsifying Lebanese or foreign currency notes or banknotes circulating legally or customarily in Lebanon, or falsifying Lebanese passports, entry visas, identity cards and civil registry extracts. However, these provisions shall not apply to a foreigner whose act is not contrary to the rules of international law.

2- To commit one of the felonies against the safety of air or maritime navigation provided for in Articles 641, 642 and 643, as amended, of the Penal Code.

3- To commit one of the offences against the safety of fixed platforms located on the continental shelf belonging to one of the Contracting States to the Rome Protocol concluded on 10/03/1988

4- To commit offences for the purpose of compelling Lebanon to perform or abstain from performing any act whatsoever, if during the commission thereof a Lebanese national is threatened, detained, wounded or killed.

Lebanese law shall apply to every Lebanese national, whether a perpetrator, instigator, or accessory, who commits, outside Lebanese territory, a felony or misdemeanour punishable under Lebanese law. This shall remain the case even if the defendant loses or acquires Lebanese nationality after the commission of the felony or misdemeanour.

Lebanese law shall apply outside Lebanese territory:

1- To offences committed by Lebanese public officials during the performance of their duties or in connection with the performance thereof,

2- To offences committed by Lebanese diplomatic officials and consuls insofar as they enjoy the immunity conferred upon them by public international law.

Lebanese law shall not apply within Lebanese territory to offences committed by foreign diplomatic officials and consuls insofar as they enjoy the immunity conferred upon them by public international law.

Lebanese laws shall also apply to every foreigner or stateless person resident or present in Lebanon who has proceeded abroad, as a perpetrator, co-perpetrator, instigator, or accessory, to commit a felony or misdemeanour not provided for in Articles 19 (paragraph 1), 20, and 21, if his extradition has not been requested or accepted.

And likewise if the felony or misdemeanour was committed by any person against or on board a foreign aircraft leased without crew to a lessee who has his principal place of business or permanent residence in Lebanon, if the extradition of the perpetrator has not been requested or accepted.

Lebanese law shall not apply to the misdemeanours referred to in Article 20 that are punishable by a penalty of imprisonment not reaching three years, to any offence referred to in Article 23, if the law of the State in whose territory these offences were committed does not punish them.

If Lebanese law and the law of the place of the offence differ, the judge may, when applying Lebanese law pursuant to Articles 20 and 23, take this difference into account in favour of the defendant.

Measures of precaution or reform, loss of capacity, and forfeiture of rights provided for in Lebanese law shall apply regardless of the law of the place of the offence.

With respect to offences committed in Lebanon or abroad, the personal law of the defendant shall be observed for the purpose of his incrimination:

1- When one of the constituent elements of the offence is subject to a law specific to personal status or capacity

2- When one of the aggravating circumstances or statutory excuses, other than criminal minority, arises from a law specific to personal status or capacity.

Save for the felonies provided for in Article 19 and the offences committed in Lebanese territory, no prosecution shall be brought in Lebanon against a Lebanese or a foreigner in any of the following cases:

1 - If he has been prosecuted for an offence of fraudulent bankruptcy or negligent bankruptcy, or for an offence connected with both or either of these two offences by reason of the bankruptcy or cessation of payments of a company or commercial establishment, and the head office of this company or establishment is situated outside Lebanese territory, and the prosecution has taken place in the country in which this head office is located.

2 - In all other offences, if a final judgment has been rendered abroad and, in the event of his conviction, if the sentence has been enforced against him or has lapsed in respect of him by prescription, or by amnesty..

Judgments rendered abroad shall not preclude the prosecution in Lebanon of any offence provided for in Article 19 or committed in Lebanese territory, unless the judgment of the foreign judiciary was rendered following an official notification from the Lebanese authorities.

Provided that the penalty and pre-trial detention executed abroad shall be deducted, in the amount determined by the judge, from the principal penalty which he pronounces.

Penal judgments rendered by a foreign judiciary concerning acts which Lebanese law characterises as felonies or misdemeanours may be relied upon:

1- In order to enforce the precautionary measures, incapacity and deprivation of rights resulting therefrom, so long as they are consistent with Lebanese law, and to enforce restitutions, damages and other civil consequences,

2- In order to adjudge the precautionary measures, incapacity and deprivation of rights provided for by Lebanese law, or restitutions, damages and other civil consequences,

3- In order to apply the provisions of Lebanese law concerning recidivism, habitual criminality, concurrence of offences, suspension of execution, and rehabilitation. The Lebanese judge may verify that the foreign judgment is in conformity with the law as to form and substance, by referring to the documents of the case.
No one shall be extradited to a foreign State, save in the cases provided for by the provisions of this Law, unless it be in application of a treaty having the force of law.

Extradition shall be permitted for:

1- Offences committed in the territory of the State requesting extradition,

2- Offences which impair its security or its financial standing,

3- Offences committed by one of its nationals

Extradition shall not be permitted for offences falling within the scope of the territorial, material and personal jurisdiction of Lebanese law as defined by Articles 15 to 17, the end of the first paragraph of Article 18, and Articles 19 to 21

The two penalties for contraventions are:

1- custodial arrest

2- fine.

Accessory or additional penalties are:

1- civic degradation,

2- imprisonment concomitant with civic degradation imposed as a principal penalty

3- felony fine,

4- deprivation of civil rights,

5- publication of the judgment,

6- posting of the judgment,

7- confiscation in personam.

A death sentence shall not be executed except after consulting the opinion of the Pardon Committee and the approval of the Head of State. The person sentenced to death shall be hanged inside the prison building or in any other place designated by the decree ordering the execution of the penalty.

The execution of the death penalty is prohibited on Sundays, Fridays, and national or religious holidays.

The execution of the death penalty on a pregnant woman shall be postponed until she gives birth.

Where the law contains no special provision, the minimum sentence of temporary hard labour, temporary detention, banishment, compulsory residence, and civic degradation shall be three years and the maximum fifteen years.
Persons sentenced to hard labour shall be compelled to perform strenuous work commensurate with their sex and age, whether inside or outside the prison.

Persons sentenced to detention shall be employed in one of the works organised by the prison administration in accordance with what they chose at the commencement of their penalty, and they may not be employed outside the prison except with their consent, nor shall they be compelled to wear prisoner uniform.

Banishment is the expulsion of the convicted person from the country.

If the banished person does not leave the country within fifteen days or if he returns to it before the expiry of the term of his penalty, the penalty of banishment shall be replaced by the penalty of detention for a term not less than the remaining time of the penalty and not exceeding double thereof, provided that it does not exceed the maximum limit of the penalty of temporary detention.

If the banished person is unable to leave the country or is compelled to return to it due to the refusal of all States to allow him to reside in their territory, the penalty of banishment shall be replaced by the penalty of detention or compulsory residence for a term not exceeding the remaining time of the penalty.

Compulsory residence is the designation for the convicted person of a place of abode chosen by the judge from a list established by decree, and under no circumstances may the designated place of abode be in a place where the convicted person had a domicile or residence, or in the place where the offence was committed, or in the place of residence of the victim or his relatives by blood or marriage up to the fourth degree. If the convicted person leaves the place of abode designated for him for any time whatsoever, compulsory residence shall be replaced by the penalty of detention for a term not exceeding the remaining time of the penalty.

Civic degradation shall automatically entail:

1- Dismissal and exclusion from all public offices and services and deprivation of any pension paid by the State.

2- Dismissal and exclusion from all offices and services in the administration of the religious community or syndicate to which the convicted person belongs and deprivation of any pension or salary paid by such religious community or syndicate.

3- Deprivation of his right to hold a concession or public contract from the State.

4- Deprivation of his right to be a voter or an elected representative and of all other civil, political, confessional and syndical rights.

5- Disqualification from being an owner, publisher or editor of a newspaper or any other periodical publication,

6- Deprivation of the right to run a school and any function in public and private education.

7- Deprivation of the right to wear Lebanese and foreign decorations and honorary titles, and furthermore, simple imprisonment from three months to three years may be imposed alongside civic degradation, and if the convicted person is a foreigner, the sentence of imprisonment shall be mandatory.

Every person sentenced to hard labour or detention shall, during the execution of his sentence, be under legal interdiction, and the exercise of his rights over his property, except for rights strictly personal to him, shall be transferred to a guardian in accordance with the provisions of the Personal Status Law relating to the appointment of guardians for interdicted persons, and every act, administration or disposition carried out by the convicted person shall be considered null and void ab initio, without prejudice to the rights of third parties acting in good faith, and no sum from his income may be handed over to the convicted person except for the sums permitted by law or prison regulations.

His property shall be restored to the convicted person upon his release, and the guardian shall render to him an account of his administration.

The term of imprisonment shall range between ten days and three years unless the law contains a special provision.

A person sentenced to imprisonment with labour shall be subject to the regime prescribed by Article 46 regarding persons sentenced to detention.

Persons sentenced to simple imprisonment shall not be compelled to work, provided that they may, if they so request, be employed in one of the works organised in the prison according to their choice, and if they choose a work, they shall be bound by it until the expiry of the term of their sentence.

The term of compulsory residence in misdemeanours shall range between three months and three years, and it shall be executed under the same conditions in which compulsory residence in felonies is executed, and if the convicted person leaves for any period whatsoever the place assigned to him, simple imprisonment shall be substituted for compulsory residence for a period not exceeding the remaining time of the sentence.

Extradition shall be refused:

1- If Lebanese law does not punish the offence with a felony or misdemeanour penalty, and the contrary shall be the case if the circumstances of the act constituting the offence cannot be met in Lebanon by reason of its geographical situation,

2- If the penalty prescribed in the law of the State requesting extradition or the law of the State in whose territory the acts were committed does not reach one year of imprisonment for the totality of the offences covered by the request.

And in the case of a judgment, if the penalty imposed is less than two months of imprisonment.

3- If the offence has been adjudicated by a final judgment in Lebanon, or if the public action or the penalty has lapsed in accordance with Lebanese law or the law of the State requesting extradition or the law of the State in whose territory the offence was committed.

Extradition shall likewise be refused:

1- If the extradition request arises from an offence of a political character, or if it appears that it is for a political purpose,

2- If the defendant had been enslaved in the territory of the State requesting extradition,

3- If the penalty prescribed in the law of the State requesting extradition is contrary to the social order.

The extradition request shall be referred to the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation, who shall undertake the investigation into the fulfilment or non-fulfilment of the legal conditions and into the extent to which the charge is established, and he may issue a warrant of arrest against the person whose extradition is requested after interrogating him, and then refer the file to the Minister of Justice accompanied by his report.

- The extradition request shall be decided upon by a decree taken upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice.

A defendant who is extradited may not be prosecuted in person, nor may a penalty be enforced against him, nor may he be surrendered to a third State for any offence prior to the extradition other than the offence that was the ground for it, unless the Government of the State from which extradition was requested consents thereto within the conditions set forth in the preceding Article.

Consent in this case shall not be bound by the provisions of the second paragraph of Article 33

Ordinary felony penalties are:

1- Death,

2- Hard labour for life,

3- Detention for life.

4- Temporary hard labour,

5- Temporary detention,

Political felony penalties are:

1- Detention for life,

2- Temporary detention,

3- Banishment,

4- Compulsory residence,

5- Civic degradation,

Ordinary misdemeanour penalties are:

1- Imprisonment with labour,

2- Simple imprisonment,

3- Fine,

Political misdemeanour penalties are:

1- Simple imprisonment,

2- Compulsory residence,

3- Fine,

Every person sentenced to imprisonment or to compulsory residence in misdemeanour cases is deprived, throughout the execution of his penalty, of the exercise of his following civil rights:

1- The right to assume public offices and services,

2- The right to assume offices and services in the administration of the civil affairs of the sect or the administration of the syndicate to which he belongs,

3- The right to be an elector or elected in all councils of the State,

4- The right to be an elector or elected in all organisations of sects and syndicates,

5- The right to wear Lebanese or foreign decorations.

In the special cases designated by the law, the prohibition from exercising one or more of the rights mentioned in the preceding Article may be adjudged together with every misdemeanour penalty; this prohibition shall be pronounced for a period ranging between one year and ten years.

Every decision entailing a felony penalty shall be posted for a period of one month on the door of the courtroom of the Criminal Court, in the nearest locality to the place of the felony, and in the locality where the convicted person had a domicile or residence.

In the cases permitted by the law by a special provision, the judgment entailing a misdemeanour penalty may be posted for a period of fifteen days in the places designated by the judge. Judgments shall be posted in abstracts at the expense of the convicted person. The judge may designate the size of the notice and the printing typeface.

The Criminal Court may order the publication of any felony decision in one or two newspapers which it designates. Likewise, any judgment that pronounced a misdemeanour penalty may be published in one or two newspapers designated by the judge if the law explicitly provides therefor. If the felony or the misdemeanour was committed by means of a newspaper or any other periodical publication, an additional notice may be published therein.

If no provision requires the publication of the judgment in its entirety, an abstract thereof shall be published.

And the convicted person shall be bound to pay the expenses of all of that. The publishing director of the newspaper chosen for the publication of the notice shall be punished by a fine ranging between twenty thousand pounds and one hundred thousand pounds if he refuses or postpones its publication.

Without prejudice to the rights of a third party in good faith, there may be confiscated all things that resulted from an intentional felony or misdemeanour or that were used or were prepared for the commission thereof, and these things may be confiscated in an unintentional misdemeanour or in a contravention if the law contains an explicit provision.

If that which must be confiscated has not been seized, the convicted person shall be granted a time limit in order to deliver it under pain of paying its value as assessed by the judge.

The court may, where necessary, seek the assistance of an expert to assess the value that must be paid, and the assessed value shall be collected in the manner followed in the collection of a fine.

Every convicted person sentenced to a custodial penalty amounting to at least three months shall have his treatment in prison improved in proportion to his good conduct.

Such improvement shall include food, the nature and number of hours of work, the obligation of silence, recreation, visits and correspondence. All of this shall be in the manner to be determined by the Execution of Penalties Law.

If the convicted person escapes, every temporary penalty definitively imposed for a felony or a misdemeanour shall be increased by one third to one half, except in the cases specifically provided for by law.

The duration of petty imprisonment ranges between one day and ten days and shall be executed upon convicted persons in places different from the places designated for persons sentenced to felony or misdemeanour penalties.

Persons sentenced to detention shall not be compelled to work.
The petty fine ranges between six thousand pounds and fifty thousand pounds.

The fine shall be substituted by simple imprisonment if it is not paid within a period of thirty days from the date on which the judgment becomes final, without prior notice.

The duration of the substituted detention shall be determined in the judgment imposing the penalty, or otherwise by a special decision, on the basis that one day of this penalty is equivalent to a fine ranging between one thousand pounds and four thousand pounds.

The substituted penalty may not exceed ten days and, in any event, the maximum limit of detention prescribed as an original penalty for the offence.

Any partial payment made before or during detention shall be deducted from this penalty in the proportion determined by the judgment as set forth in the second paragraph of this Article.

A sentence to hard labour for life, or to detention for life, entails civil degradation for life.

A sentence to temporary hard labour, or to temporary detention, or to banishment, or to compulsory residence in felonies entails civil degradation from the day on which the judgment becomes final until the expiry of the tenth year following the execution of the original penalty.

Except in the case of a fugitive convicted person, where it entails civil degradation even if the judgment in absentia is not final, from the date of its issuance until the date of its annulment in accordance with the provisions of Article 346 of the Criminal Procedure.

The felony fine ranges between one hundred thousand pounds and six million pounds and is subject to the provisions of Articles 53 and 54 relating to the misdemeanour fine.

In the event of non-payment, the fine shall be substituted by either the penalty of hard labour or the penalty of detention, depending on whether the original penalty imposed on the convicted person is hard labour or any other felony penalty.

The fine in misdemeanours shall range between fifty thousand Lebanese pounds and two million Lebanese pounds unless the law provides otherwise.

The fine may be paid, pursuant to a special provision in the operative part of the judgment, in instalments at least equal to the minimum limit of the penalty, provided that the maturity date of the final instalment does not exceed one year commencing from the day on which the judgment becomes final.

If any of the instalments is not paid on time, the fine shall fall due in full.

The fine shall be substituted by simple imprisonment if it is not paid within a period of thirty days commencing from the date the judgment becomes final without prior notice in accordance with the established rules of procedure.
