He shall be punished with temporary hard labour for at least five years if he communicates the same for the benefit of a foreign State; if the offender holds the aforementioned information and objects in his capacity as an official, agent or employee of the State, his penalty shall be temporary detention in the case provided for in the first paragraph and hard labour for life in the case provided for in the second paragraph; if one of the aforementioned persons is only chargeable with an unintentional fault, the penalty shall be imprisonment from two months to two years.
If the offences provided for in this Subdivision are committed in the interest of an enemy State, the penalty shall be increased in accordance with the provisions of Article 257.

Every fraud committed in the same circumstances with respect to the contracts referred to in the preceding Article shall be punishable by temporary hard labour and by a fine ranging between double the unlawful profit gained by the offender and three times thereof, provided that it is not less than one million pounds.

An attack aimed at changing the Constitution of the State by unlawful means shall be punishable by temporary detention for five years at least, and the penalty shall be life detention if the perpetrator resorts to violence.

Whoever attempts to sever a part of the Lebanese territory from the sovereignty of the State shall be punished by temporary detention or by exile, and the penalty shall be life detention if the perpetrator resorts to violence.

Every act committed with the intent to provoke an armed insurrection against the authorities established under the Constitution shall be punishable by temporary detention, if the insurrection breaks out the instigator shall be punished by life detention and the rest of the insurgents by temporary detention for five years at least.
An attack intended to prevent the established authorities from exercising their functions derived from the Constitution shall be punishable by temporary detention or by exile.
A conspiracy aimed at committing one of the offences mentioned in this Subsection- shall be punishable by exile or by felony compulsory residence.

Shall be punished by temporary detention for seven years at least whoever usurps a political or civil power or a military command, whoever retains, contrary to the order of the Government, a civil power or a military command.

Every military commander who keeps his troops assembled after the order has been issued to demobilise or disperse them.

Shall be liable to temporary detention whoever proceeds, without the consent of the authority, to form armed virtues of troops, or to enrol or recruit soldiers, or to equip them or supply them with weapons and ammunition.

If the offence committed on Lebanese territory or by the act of a Lebanese national against the head of a foreign State, one of his ministers, or his diplomatic representative in Lebanon is not subject to a special penalty, the legal penalty shall be increased in the manner set forth in Article 257.
The provisions of Articles 289 to 293 shall not apply unless there are similar provisions in the laws of the State concerned or in the treaty concluded with it.

Whoever engages in Lebanon, in time of war or when the outbreak thereof is expected, in propaganda aimed at weakening national sentiment or arousing racial or sectarian strife shall be punished by temporary detention.

Whoever transmits in Lebanon, in the same circumstances, news which he knows to be false or exaggerated that would weaken the morale of the nation shall be liable to the same penalty; if the perpetrator believes such news to be true, his penalty shall be imprisonment for at least three months.

Every Lebanese national who broadcasts abroad, while aware of the matter, false or exaggerated news that would detract from the prestige of the State or its financial standing shall be punished by imprisonment for at least six months and by a fine ranging between one hundred thousand pounds and one million pounds, and the court may order the publication of the judgment.

Whoever proceeds in Lebanon, without the permission of the Government, to join a political or social association of an international character or an organisation of such kind shall be punished by imprisonment or compulsory residence from three months to three years and by a fine ranging between fifty thousand and five hundred thousand pounds.

The penalty for anyone who holds a practical function in the aforementioned association or organisation may not be less than one year of imprisonment or compulsory residence and two hundred thousand pounds as a fine.

Whoever fails to perform, in time of war or when the outbreak thereof is expected, all the obligations imposed upon him by a contract of undertaking, manufacture, or provision of services relating to national defence, the public interests of the State, or the provisioning of the population shall be punished by temporary detention and by a fine ranging between the value of the unperformed obligation and double thereof, provided that it is not less than one million pounds.

If the non-performance results from an unintentional fault, the perpetrator shall be punished by imprisonment in addition to the fine specified in the preceding paragraph.

Half of the penalties provided for in this Article shall be reduced if the performance was merely delayed.

These penalties, with their preceding distinctions, shall be imposed on any other person who caused the non-performance of the contract or the delay in its performance.

Every Lebanese national and every person residing in Lebanon who enters into, or attempts to enter into, directly or through a nominee, a commercial transaction or any transaction of purchase, sale or barter with a national of the enemy or with a person residing in enemy territory shall be punishable by imprisonment for not less than one year and by a fine of not less than two hundred thousand pounds.

"Every Lebanese national and every person in Lebanon who is a national of an Arab State who enters enemy territory, directly or indirectly and without the prior approval of the Lebanese Government, shall be punishable by the same penalty, even if the purpose of his entry was not one of the acts provided for in the preceding paragraph of this Article".

The persons mentioned in the preceding Article shall incur the penalty set forth therein if they contribute to a loan or subscription for the benefit of a hostile State or facilitate its financial operations by any means whatsoever.

Whoever conceals or embezzles the property of a hostile State or the property of one of its nationals entrusted to a custodian shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years and by a fine of at least two hundred thousand pounds.

Shall be punishable by temporary detention:

Whoever violates the measures taken by the State to preserve its neutrality in war.

Whoever commits acts, or produces writings or speeches not authorised by the Government, thereby exposing Lebanon to the risk of hostile acts, or reversing its relations with a foreign State, or exposing Lebanese nationals to acts of reprisal against their persons or their property.

Every attack committed on Lebanese territory or perpetrated by a Lebanese national with the intent to alter by violence the constitution or government of a foreign State or to sever part of its territory shall be punishable by temporary detention.

A conspiracy aimed at committing any of the aforementioned felonies shall entail imprisonment for not less than one year.
Whoever recruits soldiers on Lebanese territory without the approval of the Government to fight on behalf of a foreign State shall be punished by temporary detention or by expulsion.

Every incitement committed in Lebanon or carried out by a Lebanese national by one of the means mentioned in Article 288 to induce the land, sea or air forces of a foreign State to desertion or mutiny shall be punishable by imprisonment from six months to two years and by a fine not exceeding four hundred thousand pounds.

Shall be punishable by the same penalties, upon the complaint of the injured party, for the following offences:

- Publicly disparaging a foreign State, its army, its flag or its national emblem.

- Disparaging the Head of a foreign State, its ministers or its diplomatic representative in Lebanon.

- Slander or defamation committed publicly against the Head of a foreign State, its ministers or its diplomatic representative in Lebanon.

Proof of the act that was the subject of the defamation shall not be admissible.

Any attack aimed either at provoking civil war or sectarian fighting by arming Lebanese or by inducing them to arm themselves against one another, or at inciting slaughter and pillage in one or more localities, shall be punishable by hard labour for life, and the death penalty shall be imposed if the attack is consummated.

Whoever heads armed gangs or assumes therein a function or command of any kind whatsoever, either with intent to invade a city, a locality, certain property of the State, or the property of a group of inhabitants, or with intent to attack or resist the public force operating against the perpetrators of these felonies, shall be punishable by hard labour for life.

Participants in armed gangs formed with intent to commit any of the felonies provided for in Articles 308 and 309 shall be punishable by hard labour for life. However, any of them who did not assume a function or service in the gang, was not arrested at the places of sedition, and surrendered with his weapon without resistance and prior to the pronouncement of any judgment shall be exempted from the penalty.

The penalty for whoever commits any of the felonies provided for in Articles 309 and 310 shall be increased in accordance with Article 257: if he carries a visible or concealed weapon, if he wears a uniform or bears another emblem, whether civilian or military, if he commits acts of sabotage or defacement in buildings dedicated to a public service or in means of telecommunications, communications, or transport.

Whoever, with intent to commit or facilitate any of the felonies mentioned in this Subdivision or any other felony against the State, manufactures, acquires, or possesses explosive or inflammable materials, toxic or incendiary products, or parts used in their assembly or manufacture shall be punishable by temporary hard labour, in addition to the more severe penalties incurred by accomplices in those felonies if they are committed, attempted, or remain unconsummated.
Conspiracy with intent to commit any of the felonies mentioned in this Subdivision shall be punishable by temporary hard labour.

Terrorist acts mean all acts intended to create a state of terror and committed by means such as explosive devices, inflammable materials, toxic or incendiary products, and epidemic or microbial agents capable of causing a public danger.

Every person who belongs to an association established for the purpose referred to in the preceding Article shall be liable to the same penalties.

Imprisonment shall not be less than one year and the fine shall not be less than two hundred thousand pounds if the said person holds an operational function in the association, all of which shall be in addition to ordering the dissolution of the association and the confiscation of its property pursuant to Articles 109 and 69.

Whosoever disseminates, by any of the means mentioned in the second and third paragraphs of Article 209, fabricated facts or false allegations in order to cause a depreciation in the national banknotes or to undermine confidence in the soundness of the currency of the State, its bonds, and all instruments connected with public financial confidence, shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years and by a fine from five hundred thousand pounds to two million pounds.

In addition thereto, the publication of the judgment may be ordered.

Every person who resorts to the same means to incite the public shall be liable to the same penalties: either to withdraw funds deposited in banks and public funds.

Or to sell State bonds and other public bonds, or to refrain from purchasing them.

When passing judgment on any of the misdemeanours provided for in this Title, the court may order deprivation of civil rights, prohibition of residence, or expulsion from the country pursuant to Articles 65, 82 and 88.

Bands, gatherings, and assemblies shall be deemed armed within the meaning intended in this Law if one or more of the persons of whom they are composed are carrying visible, hidden, or concealed weapons, provided that if some of them are carrying non-visible weapons, this matter shall not be held against the remaining persons if they were unaware thereof.

Every cutting, piercing, or bruising tool or instrument and every tool dangerous to public safety shall be deemed a weapon for the purpose of applying the preceding Article, Ordinary pocket knives and light canes that are not carried to be used when needed shall not be covered by this definition unless they are used in the commission of a felony or a misdemeanour.

If the purpose of carrying or possessing weapons or ammunition is the commission of a felony, the penalty, save for cases with which the law imposes a severer penalty, shall be imprisonment with labour from one year to three years and a fine from one hundred thousand pounds to six hundred thousand pounds.

A conspiracy aimed at committing an act or acts of terrorism shall be punishable by temporary hard labour; every terrorist act shall entail hard labour for at least five years, and it shall entail hard labour for life if it results in sabotage, even partially, in a public building, an industrial establishment, a vessel or other installations, or disruption of means of telecommunications, communications and transport, and the death penalty shall be imposed if the act leads to the death of a human being or the demolition of a structure in part or in whole while a person or several persons are inside it.

Every association established for the purpose of altering the economic or social entity of the State or the fundamental conditions of society by one of the means mentioned in Article 314 shall be dissolved and its members shall be sentenced to temporary hard labour, and the penalty for the founders and directors shall not be less than seven years; the absolving or mitigating excuse granted to conspirators pursuant to Article 272 shall extend to the perpetrators of the felony specified above.

Anyone who intentionally, by any means, directly or indirectly, carries out, attempts to carry out, directs or participates in financing, wholly or partially, or contributing to the financing of terrorism or terrorist acts, or financing an individual terrorist or terrorist organisations, or acts related thereto, including offering, providing or collecting movable or immovable funds, from legitimate or illegitimate sources, in Lebanon or abroad, whether the funds were used or not used, and whether the terrorist act was committed or not committed in Lebanon or abroad.

The crime of financing terrorism shall include travel, attempted travel, recruitment, planning, preparation, organisation, facilitation, participation, providing or receiving training, and any other act related thereto with the intent to commit terrorist acts and without such acts being linked to a specific terrorist act.

The perpetrators of the acts specified above shall be punished by temporary hard labour for a term of not less than three years and not exceeding seven years and by a fine of not less than the amount paid and not exceeding three times that amount, without prejudice to the application of the penalties provided for in Articles 212 to 222 inclusive of the Penal Code".

Every act, every writing and every speech intended to or resulting in provoking sectarian or racial strife or inciting conflict between the sects and the various elements of the nation shall be punishable by imprisonment from one year to three years and by a fine from one hundred thousand to eight hundred thousand pounds, as well as by prohibition from exercising the rights mentioned in the second and fourth paragraphs of Article 65, and the court may order the publication of the judgment.

If two or more persons proceed to form an association or conclude a written or oral agreement with the intent of committing felonies against people or property, or undermining the authority or prestige of the State, or attacking its civil, military, financial or economic institutions, they shall be punished with temporary hard labour, and this penalty shall not be less than ten years if the offenders' aim is to assault the lives of others or the lives of public officials in public institutions and administrations.

However, whoever discloses the matter of the association or agreement and divulges the information in his possession concerning the other offenders shall be exempted from the penalty.

Every group of three or more persons who roam the public roads and the countryside as armed gangs with the intent of robbing passers-by and assaulting persons or property, or committing any other act of brigandage, shall be liable to life temporary hard labour for a term of at least seven years, and they shall be sentenced to hard labour for life if they commit one of the aforementioned acts, and whoever among them proceeds, in execution of the felony, to commit murder or attempts it, or inflicts torture and barbaric acts upon the victims, shall incur the death penalty.

Every association or group that in fact has the character of an association shall be deemed secret if its purpose is contrary to the law and it carries out its activities, or part thereof, secretly; likewise, the very associations and groups whose purpose is proven to be contrary to the law and which have not notified the authorities, after having been requested to do so, of their bylaws, the names of their members and their functions, the subject of their meetings, a statement of their property and the source of their resources, or which have given false or incomplete information regarding these matters, shall be deemed secret.

Every secret association shall be dissolved and its funds confiscated, and whoever held an administrative or executive function therein shall be punished with imprisonment from six months to two years and with a fine from one hundred thousand to one million pounds, and as for the remaining members, with half of both penalties.

If a member of a secret association commits an offence in execution of the purpose of this association, the member who attended the meeting where the offence was decided upon shall be deemed an instigator and shall be punished with what is prescribed by Article 218, and the member who was present at the scene of the offence at the time of its commission shall be treated as an accomplice and shall be punished with his penalty in accordance with what is stated in Article 220.

Public officials who are bound to the State by a public contract shall be liable to civic degradation if they proceed by agreement to suspend their work, or agree to suspend it, or to submit their resignation under circumstances where the operation of one of the public services is thereby impeded.

Every act designed to hinder a Lebanese citizen from exercising his civic rights or duties shall be punishable by imprisonment from one month to one year, if committed by threat and violence or by any other means of physical or moral coercion.

If the offence is committed by an armed group composed of three or more persons, the penalty shall be imprisonment from six months to three years, and if the offence occurs without weapons, the penalty shall be imprisonment from two months to two years.

If any of the acts specified in the preceding Article is committed pursuant to a concerted plan intended to be executed throughout the territory of the State or in one or more localities thereof, each of the offenders shall be punished by temporary detention or by banishment.

Whoever attempts to influence the vote of a Lebanese citizen with the intent to corrupt the result of a general election: either byPutting him in fear of harm befalling his person, his family, his position, or his property, or by offers, gifts, or promises, or by promising a legal person or a group of people administrative grants, shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year and by a fine from one hundred thousand pounds to one million pounds.

Whoever accepts or solicits such gifts or promises shall incur the same penalty.
Every public official, worker, or employee of the State who uses his authority to influence the vote of a Lebanese citizen shall be punished by civic degradation.

Every person who alters or attempts to alter by fraud the result of an election shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years.

If the offender is entrusted with collecting the votes or ballot papers, preserving them, counting them, or performing any other act relating to a general election, he shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years.
The annulment of an election shall have no bearing on the offences committed during or because of it.

If two or more persons proceed to form an association or conclude an agreement for the purpose of committing felonies against persons or property, they shall be punished by temporary hard labour, and this penalty shall not be less than seven years if the aim of the offenders is to make an attempt upon the lives of others.

However, whoever discloses the existence of the association or agreement and reveals the information in his possession concerning the other offenders shall be exempted from the penalty.

- Every worker in the private sector, whether an employee, an expert, or a consultant, and anyone bound to an employer by an employment contract in return for remuneration, who solicits or accepts for himself or for another, a gift, a promise, or any other benefit, to disclose secrets or information harmful to the work or to perform an act or abstain therefrom with the intent to cause material or moral damage to the employer or to the interest of the work, shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years and by a fine from one hundred thousand to two hundred thousand pounds.

- The same penalty shall be imposed on the briber.

Whoever offers a person among the persons mentioned in Article 351 a gift or any other benefit or promises it to him by way of undue remuneration in order to perform or not perform an act of his office or to delay its execution shall be punished, if the offer or promise does not meet with acceptance, by imprisonment for at least three months and by a fine of not less than double the value of the thing offered or promised.

Every person among the persons referred to in Article 351 who accepts undue remuneration for an act of his office or mission that has already been performed shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year and by a fine the minimum of which is double the value of what he accepted.

Whoever takes or solicits undue remuneration or accepts the promise thereof, whether for himself or for another, with the intent to procure for others or to seek to procure for them an office, work, contracts, projects, other profits, or grants from the State or one of the public administrations, or with the intent to influence the conduct of the authorities in any manner whatsoever, shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years and by a fine the minimum of which is double the value of what he took or accepted.

If the act is committed by an attorney on the pretext of obtaining the favour of a judge, arbitrator, trustee in bankruptcy, or expert in a case, he shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to three years and shall be barred from practising his profession for life.

Every public official who embezzles money or other things belonging to the State or to a person, the management, collection, or preservation of which has been entrusted to him by virtue of his office, shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to three years and by a fine the minimum of which is the value of the restitution.

If the embezzlement takes place by inserting false entries in invoices or ledgers, or by altering or destroying accounts, papers, or other instruments, and in general by any artifice aimed at preventing the discovery of the embezzlement, the penalty of temporary hard labour shall be imposed in addition to the fine prescribed by the preceding Article.

Every public official who coerces a person or induces him to pay or promise to pay what he knows is not due from him or exceeds what is due from him in taxes, fees, and other revenues shall be punished by imprisonment for at least one year and by a fine the minimum of which is double the value of the restitution.

If people gather in this manner, they shall be warned to disperse by a representative of the administrative authority or an officer of the judicial police, who shall announce his arrival, if circumstances so require, by beating a drum, blowing a bugle or a whistle, or by any other similar means; those who act before the warning of the authority or who immediately comply with its warning without using their weapons or committing any other misdemeanour shall be exempted from the penalty prescribed above.

If those gathered do not disperse otherwise than by force, the penalty shall be imprisonment from two months to two years, and whoever uses a weapon shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to three years, in addition to any more severe penalty that he may incur.

Deprivation of civil rights, prohibition of residence, and expulsion from the country may bepronounced in accordance with Articles 65, 82, and 88 in the misdemeanours provided for in Chapters 2 to 5 of this Title.

Shall be deemed a public official within the meaning intended in this Title every official in public administrations and institutions, municipalities, the army, and the judiciary, every worker or employee in the State, and every person appointed or elected to perform a public service with or without remuneration.

Every public official and every person assigned to a public service, whether by election or by appointment, and every person entrusted with an official mission such as an arbitrator, an expert, and a trustee in bankruptcy (syndic), who solicits or accepts for himself or for another a gift, a promise, or any other benefit in order to perform a lawful act of his office shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to three years and by a fine of at least twice the value of what he took or accepted.

Every person among the aforementioned persons who solicits or accepts for himself or for another a gift, a promise, or any other benefit in order to perform an act contrary to his office, or which he claims to fall within his office, or to neglect or delay what it was his duty to perform, shall be punished by temporary hard labour and by a fine of not less than three times the value of what he took or accepted; the same penalty shall be imposed on a lawyer if he commits these acts.

The penalties provided for in Articles 351 and 352 shall also be imposed on the briber.

"The briber or the accessory shall be exempted from these penalties if he discloses the matter to the competent authorities or confesses to it before the case is referred to the court".

If any of the employers, heads of enterprises, employees or workmen cease work, either for the purpose of exerting pressure on the public authorities or in protest against a decision or measure issued by them, each of the offenders shall be punished by imprisonment or by forced residence for a term of at least three months.

Punishment by imprisonment, and by a fine, shall be imposed for every concerted stoppage carried out by more than twenty persons and followed by an attempt or the commencement of execution for the purpose of suspending:

1- Means of transport between parts of Lebanon or between it and other countries,

2- Postal, telegraphic and telephonic communications,

3- One of the public services responsible for the distribution of water or electricity.

The concessionaire of one of the aforementioned services shall incur the same penalty if he suspends its operation without legitimate cause, and if the offence is committed by acts of violence against persons or property, or by threat or other means of intimidation, or by fraudulent devices or false allegations calculated to produce an impression on the mind, or by gathering on public thoroughfares and in public squares, or by occupying workplaces, the perpetrators of these acts shall be punished by imprisonment for at least six months.

Whoever resorts to one of the means mentioned in the last paragraph of the preceding Article and thereby induces or attempts to induce others to suspend their work by agreement among themselves, or causes them to persist or attempts to cause them to persist in suspending such work, shall be punished by imprisonment for at most one year and by a fine not exceeding one hundred thousand pounds.

Every employer or head of an enterprise and every employee or workman who refuses or delays the execution of an arbitral award or any other decision issued by one of the labour courts shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to one year.

Whoever, being in a meeting which does not have the character of a private meeting, whether by reason of its aim or object, the number of persons invited to it or of whom it is composed, or the place where it is held, or being in a public place or a place open to the public or exposed to its view, utters cries or chants of riot, or displays any emblem in circumstances whereby public security is disturbed, or engages in any other riotous demonstration, shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year and by a fine from twenty thousand to two hundred thousand pounds.

Every crowd or procession on the public roads or in a place open to the public shall be deemed a riotous assembly and shall be punishable by imprisonment from one month to one year:

If it is composed of three or more persons for the purpose of committing a felony or a misdemeanour and at least one of them is armed.

If it is composed of at least seven persons for the purpose of protesting against a decision or measure taken by the public authorities for the purpose of exerting pressure on them.

If the number of persons exceeds twenty and they appear in a manner calculated to disturb public tranquillity.
Every official who grants an exemption from taxes, duties, fines and other revenues without the law authorizing that shall be punished with the same penalty.

Shall be punished with imprisonment from three months to three years and with a fine from two hundred thousand to one million pounds:

1- Whoever is entrusted with the sale, purchase or administration of movable or immovable property for the account of the State or for the account of a public administration or institution, a municipality, a public body, or an institution of public utility or in which the State owns a part of its shares, and commits fraud in one of these acts or violates the provisions applicable thereto, either to draw a personal gain, or out of favouritism to one party to the detriment of the other party, or to the detriment of the public interest or public funds, or commits gross and grave fault.

2- Whoever is bound, in time of peace, by a contract for undertaking works, public works, transport, manufacturing on order, maintenance, repairs, or the provision of services, supplies or provisioning with one of the entities indicated in the preceding paragraph, whether the contract is the result of a tender on the basis of a book of conditions or to forms of intentional procrastination or artifice to forms of intentional procrastination or artifice to obstruct execution or prolong the duration with the intent of harming State projects or drawing a benefit or for another, or commits fraud in the kind of materials used or provided, or in their composition, manufacture or essential specifications.

3- Contractors who agree in collusion among themselves to corrupt the tendering operation or to restrict the award to one of them to the detriment of the contracting official entity.

4- The official entrusted with supervising the tender or the award by mutual agreement or by any other method, or monitoring the stages of execution, or receiving the works after their completion, if he performs acts calculated to favour one party over another in the tendering or awarding, or if he turns a blind eye to recording the violation, or neglects supervision, or fails to take against the violator the measures provided for by the relevant laws.

5- The contractor, intermediary or any other person who provides, as a result of a tender, an award by mutual agreement or by any other method, spoiled or unfit materials to public administrations and institutions and municipalities, and the official or employee who accepts or receives these materials shall be considered an accomplice in the offence.

This is in addition to the penalties decreed for bribery in the event of its occurrence.

Every official who obtains a personal benefit from one of the transactions of the administration to which he belongs, whether he does so directly or through a nominee or by resorting to ostensible instruments, shall be punished with imprisonment from three months to two years and with a fine of at least two hundred thousand pounds.

Every public official who incites contempt for the national institutions or for the laws of the State, or who praises acts contrary to these laws or institutions, shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year and by a fine from fifty thousand to two hundred thousand pounds. This provision shall also apply to clergymen or members of the public or private teaching body.

If a public official in public administrations, public institutions, or municipalities commits, without a legitimate cause, neglect in the performance of his duties or fails to execute lawful orders issued to him by his superior, he shall be punished by imprisonment of up to two years and by a fine from two hundred thousand to one million pounds, or by one of these two penalties.

If damage to the interests of the administrations, institutions, and municipalities concerned results from this act, the penalty shall be aggravated in accordance with the provisions of Article 257, and he may be sentenced to a fine equivalent to the value of the damage.

Likewise, every officer or member of the public force, and every commander of a post or platoon, who refuses to comply with a lawful requisition issued by the judicial or administrative authority shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year.

Every public official, other than those mentioned in Article 306, who has been dismissed or suspended, and every person delegated to a public service by election or by appointment whose term has expired, shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to three years if he continues to exercise his functions contrary to the law.

Every public official who, with the intent of procuring a benefit for himself or for another, or with the intent of causing harm to another, commits an act not specifically provided for by a provision in the law which is contrary to the duties of his profession, shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to three years and by a fine from twenty thousand to two hundred thousand pounds.

Except in the cases where the law imposes special penalties for offences committed by public officials, those among them who, in their aforesaid capacity or by abusing the authority or influence derived from their functions, proceed to commit any offence whatsoever, whether as instigators, co-principals, or accomplices, shall incur the aggravated penalties imposed by Article 257.
The judge may, when adjudicating one of the misdemeanours provided for in this Chapter, pronounce deprivation of civil rights.

The penalties of the preceding Article shall be imposed upon judges, revenue collectors, representatives of the administration, officers of the State or the police, and all other holders of public authority who receive a salary from the State if they engage, openly or by resorting to simulated instruments, directly or through a nominee, in trading within the area in which they exercise authority in grains, foodstuffs, and all other necessities of primary need other than those produced by their own properties.

Half of the penalties prescribed in Articles 359 to 362 shall be reduced if the damage caused and the benefit sought by the offender are slight, or if he makes full compensation for the damage before the case is referred to the court, and if restitution or compensation takes place during the trial and before any judgment on the merits, even if not final, one quarter of the penalty shall be reduced.
Every official who arrests or imprisons a person in cases other than those provided for by the law shall be punished by temporary hard labour.

Directors and guards of prisons, disciplinary institutions, or reformatories, and any official who assumes their powers, if they admit a person without a judicial warrant or judicial decision or retain him beyond the fixed term, shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to three years.

The aforementioned persons and, in general, all officers and members of the public force and all administrative officials who refuse or delay bringing an arrested person or a prisoner before the competent judge who requests them to do so shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year, and anyone who does not immediately comply with the judge's request to produce the prison register and all registers of the places of detention to which they are attached shall be punished by the same penalty.

Every official who, in his capacity as an official, enters the dwelling of any person or the appurtenances of the dwelling in cases other than those provided for by the law and without observing the procedures which it imposes shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to three years, and the penalty shall not be less than six months if the act is accompanied by a search of the premises or any other arbitrary act committed by the perpetrator.

Every official who uses his authority or influence, directly or indirectly, to obstruct or delay the enforcement of laws or regulations, the collection of fees or taxes, or the execution of a judicial decision, a judicial warrant, or any order issued by the competent authority shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to two years.

If the person who used his authority or influence is not a public official, the penalty shall not exceed one year.

Contempt by words and gestures or a threat directed at a public official during the performance of his duty or on the occasion of the performance thereof, or communicated to him by the will of the perpetrator, and contempt by writing, drawing, or telegraphic or telephonic communication directed at a public official during the performance of his duty or on the occasion of the performance thereof, shall be punishable by imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months.

If the public official subjected to contempt is among those who exercise public authority, the penalty shall be from two months to one year.

And if the contempt by words, gestures or threat is committed against a judge on the bench, the penalty shall be imprisonment from six months to two years.

"A public official means any person appointed or elected to perform a public office or service, with or without remuneration".

Whoever commits contempt against the Head of State shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to two years, and the same penalty shall be imposed on whoever publicly commits contempt against the national flag or emblem by one of the means mentioned in Article 196.

Defamation is the imputation of a matter to a person, even in the form of doubt or interrogation, that prejudices his honour or dignity. Every word of disdain or invective and every expression or drawing that reveals contempt shall be deemed slander if it does not involve the imputation of any matter, without prejudice to the provisions of Article 383 which sets forth the definition of contempt.

Defamation by one of the means specified in Article 209 shall be punishable:

By imprisonment from two months to two years if committed against the Head of State.

By imprisonment for one year at most if directed at the courts, constituted bodies, the army or public administrations, or if directed at a public official among those who exercise public authority by reason of his office or capacity.

By imprisonment for three months at most or by a fine from twenty thousand to two hundred thousand pounds if committed against any other public official because of his office or capacity.
With the exception of defamation committed against the Head of State, the defendant shall be acquitted if the subject of the defamation is an act related to the office and its truth is proven.

Slander by one of the means set forth in Article 209 shall be punishable:

- By imprisonment from one month to one year if committed against the Head of State,

- By imprisonment for up to one month at most if directed at the courts, constituted bodies, the army or public administrations, or if directed at a public official among those who exercise public authority by reason of his office or capacity.

- By a fine from twenty thousand to one hundred thousand pounds or by summary detention if committed against any other public official by reason of his office or capacity.

Contempt, revilement or defamation directed at a judge without his office having any connection thereto shall be punishable by imprisonment for six months at most. The courts may order the publication of every judgment in an offence of contempt, defamation or revilement set forth above in the First Subdivision of the Second Chapter.

Whoever tears an official notice, removes it or destroys it, even partially, shall be punished by a fine from twenty thousand pounds to one hundred thousand pounds, and if the act is committed out of disdain for the authority or in protest against one of its acts, his penalty shall be imprisonment for a term not exceeding three months.

Whoever openly and without right proceeds to wear an official uniform or bear a decoration or insignia from among the uniforms, decorations or insignia of the Lebanese State or a foreign state, or wears a garment reserved by Lebanese law to a category of persons, shall be punished by imprisonment for six months at most or by a fine not exceeding two hundred thousand pounds.

This text shall apply, upon the complaint of the competent confessional authorities, to every person who wears without right clothing special to one of the religious functions.

Whoever appears usurping a public military or civil office or exercises its powers shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years, if the perpetrator during the act is wearing a uniform or insignia special to public officials, the imprisonment shall not be less than four months, and if the act is accompanied by another offence, its penalty shall be increased in accordance with the provisions of Article 257.
Whoever practises without right a profession subject to a legal regime shall be punished by imprisonment for six months at most and by a fine from fifty thousand to four hundred thousand pounds.
The judgment may be published in the misdemeanours provided for in this Subdivision.

Whoever intentionally proceeds to break seals affixed by order of the public authority or at the request of the spiritual or consular authorities operating within the limits of their legal competence in Lebanon shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year, and if he resorts to acts of violence against persons, from one year to three years.

Whoever takes, removes or destroys, completely or partially, papers or documents deposited in archive repositories, court registries or public depositories, or delivered to a public depositary in this capacity, shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to three years, if the act is committed by means of breaking seals, breaking and entering, scaling, or by means of acts of violence against persons, the penalty shall be temporary hard labour.

Whoever attacks or resists with violence an official working on the enforcement of laws or regulations, the collection of fees and taxes, or the execution of a judicial decision, a judicial warrant, or any order issued by the competent authority shall be punished as follows:

1- If the act is committed by an armed group whose number of persons exceeds twenty, they shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to three years, and if they are unarmed, imprisonment shall be from two months to two years.

2- And if the act is committed by persons whose number is under twenty, the penalty shall be imprisonment from two months to two years and if they are armed. And imprisonment from ten days to three months "and a fine from twenty thousand to two hundred thousand pounds if they are unarmed.

Every resistance, whether active or passive, that halts a lawful act performed by one of the persons described in the preceding Article shall be punished by imprisonment for one month at most and by a fine of up to one hundred thousand pounds.

Whoever strikes an official or treats him with violence and severity during the exercise of his office, or in the course of his exercise thereof, or because of it, shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years.

And if the act is committed against a judge at any time whatsoever, the penalty shall be from one year to three years. The penalties imposed in the two preceding paragraphs shall be increased in the manner set forth in Article 257 if the acts of violence are committed premeditatedly, or if they are committed by a group of at least three persons, or if wounds or illness result therefrom.

And if the acts of violence are of such gravity as to warrant a penalty more severe than the penalties provided for in the Article, the penalty incurred by the perpetrator as a result thereof shall be raised in accordance with Article 257 of the Penal Code.

Whoever threatens, by any means whatsoever, a judge, or any person performing a judicial mission or fulfilling a legal duty before the judiciary, such as an arbitrator, a lawyer, an expert, a trustee in bankruptcy, or a witness, with the intent to influence his immunity, his opinion, or his judgment, or to prevent him from performing his duty or his mission, shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to three years and by a fine from two hundred thousand to two million pounds.

And if the threat involves a menace to use a weapon or to commit an assault against persons or property, or if it is accompanied by one of these acts, the perpetrator shall be punished by temporary hard labour.

Criminalisation of Torture

"A - In this law, torture means any act committed, instigated, or expressly or impliedly consented to by a public official or any person acting in an official capacity during inquiry, preliminary investigation, judicial investigation, trials, and the execution of penalties,

which results in severe pain or severe suffering, whether physical or mental, intentionally inflicted on a person, in particular:

- To obtain from him or a third person information or a confession.

- Punishing any person for an act he or a third person has committed or is suspected of having committed.

- To intimidate or coerce any person - him or any third person - to do or refrain from doing any act.

- To subject any person to such severe pain or severe suffering for any reason based on discrimination of any kind.

The above definition does not include severe pain or severe suffering arising from, inherent in, or incidental to lawful sanctions.

B - Anyone who commits torture shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to three years if the torture does not lead to death or to a permanent or temporary physical or mental disorder or disability.

- If the torture leads to a temporary physical or mental disorder, harm, or disability, it shall be punished by detention from three years to seven years.

- If the torture leads to a permanent physical or mental disorder or disability, it shall be punished by detention from five years to ten years.

- If the torture leads to death, it shall be punished by detention from ten years to twenty years.

C - The court may decide to rehabilitate the victims of crimes of torture in addition to personal compensation."

Whoever informs the judicial authority or an authority that is obliged to notify the judicial authority of a crime which he knows was not committed, and whoever causes the initiation of a preliminary or judicial investigation by fabricating material evidence of such a crime, shall be punished by imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months and by a fine not exceeding one hundred thousand pounds, or by either of the two penalties.

Whoever submits a complaint or an information to the judicial authority or to an authority that is obliged to notify the judicial authority and attributes to any person a misdemeanour or a contravention of which he knows him to be innocent, or fabricates against him material evidence of the occurrence of such an offence, shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to three years , if the attributed act constitutes a felony, the calumniator shall be punished by temporary hard labour for ten years at most, and if the calumny leads to a sentence of death or a life penalty, the penalty of hard labour shall not be less than ten years and may be increased up to fifteen years.
If the false accuser retracts his false accusation before any prosecution, the penalties provided for in this subsection shall be reduced in accordance with the provisions of Article 251.

Any person who, when asked his name by a judge or an officer or member of the judicial police, states a name or capacity that is not his own, or gives a false statement regarding his place of residence or dwelling, shall be punished by imprisonment for six months at most or by a fine not exceeding one hundred thousand pounds.
Any person who assumes the name of another in a judicial investigation or judicial trial shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to three years.
A witness who puts forward a false excuse shall be liable to imprisonment for three months at most, in addition to the fine imposed upon him by reason of his failure to appear.

Any person who testifies before a judicial authority or a military or administrative court and asserts a falsehood, denies the truth, or conceals some or all of what he knows of the facts of the case about which he is questioned, shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to three years.

If the false testimony is given during a criminal investigation or a criminal trial, hard labour for ten years at most shall be imposed.

If the false testimony results in a sentence of death or a life penalty, the hard labour shall not be less than ten years and may be increased to fifteen years.

If the offender was heard without taking the oath, half the penalty shall be reduced.

Shall be exempted from the penalty:

1- A witness who gave the testimony during a penal investigation if he retracts the false statement before the investigation is closed and an information is submitted against him.

2- A witness who testified in any trial if he retracts his statement before any judgment on the merits of the case, even if not final.

Shall likewise be exempted from the penalty:

1- A witness who, if he tells the truth, would inevitably expose himself to a grave danger affecting liberty or honour, or would expose thereto his spouse, even if divorced, or one of his ascendants, descendants, brothers, sisters, or affinities of the same degrees.

2- A person who stated before the judge his name, surname, and capacity, and who ought not to have been heard as a witness, or who ought to have been cautioned that he has the right to abstain from giving testimony if he so wishes.

However, if the false testimony exposes another person to legal prosecution or to a judgment, the penalty shall be reduced by one half to two thirds.

Half the penalty shall be reduced for the person at whose instigation the false testimony was given, if the witness, had he told the truth, would inevitably have exposed him or exposed one of his relatives to a grave danger such as that set forth in the first paragraph of the preceding Article.

Whoever burns or destroys, even partially, registers, drafts, or originals of instruments belonging to the public authority shall incur the penalties of the preceding Article with the distinctions contained therein.

Every Lebanese national who becomes aware of a felony against the security of the State and fails to notify the public authority thereof immediately shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to three years and by deprivation of civil rights.

Every public official charged with investigating or prosecuting offences who neglects or delays reporting an offence connected with his work shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to three years and by a fine from twenty thousand to two hundred thousand pounds.

Every public official who neglects or delays informing the competent authority of a felony or misdemeanour of which he became aware during the performance of his duties or on the occasion of performing them shall be punished by the fine specified above.

All the foregoing shall apply unless the prosecution of the offence that was not reported is contingent upon the complaint of an individual.

Whoever, while practising one of the health professions, renders assistance to a person upon whom a felony or a misdemeanour that may be prosecuted without a complaint appears to have been committed, and fails to notify the authority thereof, shall be punished by the fine provided for in the preceding Article.

Any person entrusted with guarding or escorting a prisoner who enables or facilitates his escape shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to three years in the first case mentioned in the preceding Article, by hard labour from three to seven years in the second case, and by hard labour from five years to fifteen years in the third case.

If the escape occurs due to the negligence of the guard or escort, his penalty shall be imprisonment from one month to one year in the first case mentioned above, imprisonment from six months to two years in the second case, and from one year to three years in the third case.

Those entrusted with guarding or escorting prisoners who supply them, in order to facilitate their escape, with weapons or other instruments suitable for committing it by means of breaking or violence shall be punished for this act alone by temporary hard labour for not less than five years.

Any other person who commits this act shall be punished by temporary hard labour.

Half the penalty shall be reduced if the offender secures the arrest of the fugitive or induces him to surrender himself within three months of his escape without his having committed another offence characterised as a felony or misdemeanour.

Any person who, in order to obtain his right by himself while able to refer immediately to the competent authority, dispossesses property in the possession of a third party or uses violence against things and damages them shall be punished by a fine not exceeding two hundred thousand pounds.

If the act mentioned in the preceding Article is committed by means of violence against persons or by resorting to moral coercion, the perpetrator shall be punished by imprisonment for six months at most, in addition to the fine specified above.

His penalty shall be imprisonment from three months to two years if the violence or coercion is used by an armed person or a group of three or more persons, even if unarmed.
Prosecution shall depend upon the complaint of the injured party if the aforementioned misdemeanour is not accompanied by another offence that may be prosecuted without a complaint.
The penalty for duelling shall be from one month to one year.
Every challenge to a duel, even if refused, shall be punishable by a fine from fifty thousand to four hundred thousand pounds.

An expert appointed by the judicial authority who affirms a matter contrary to the truth or interprets it incorrectly while knowing its truth shall be punished by imprisonment for at least three months and by a fine of not less than one hundred thousand pounds, and shall moreover be barred from serving as an expert.

Hard labour shall be imposed if the mission of the expert relates to a felony case.

A translator who intentionally provides an incorrect translation in a judicial case shall be subject to the penalties of the preceding Article with the distinctions contained therein, and shall moreover be sentenced to be permanently barred from practising translation.
The provisions of Article 409 shall apply to the expert and the interpreter.

Whoever swears a false oath in a civil case shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years and by a fine from one hundred thousand to two hundred thousand pounds, and shall be exempted from punishment if he retracts his oath before the action that was the subject of the oath is decided by a judgment, even if not final.

Whoever disposes of, conceals, destroys or alters a document or another item after having produced it before the judiciary shall be punished by a fine from fifty thousand to six hundred thousand pounds, and this provision shall apply if the produced document and item had been left on condition that it be presented upon every request.
No action for defamation or slander shall arise from speeches and writings uttered or produced before the courts in good faith and within the limits of the legitimate right of defence.

Whoever is present in a place where a judicial investigation is being conducted and violates an order of removal issued by the judge presiding over the hearing shall be arrested by the judge and sentenced to disciplinary detention for twenty-four hours.

Whoever solicits from a judge, an arbitrator, or a person performing a judicial mission or an arbitral mission, by any means, any request relating to an action or a judicial recourse, shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years and by a fine ranging between ten times the minimum wage and one hundred times thereof.

This penalty shall be increased in accordance with the provisions of Article 257 of the Penal Code if the principal, accomplice, accessory or instigator is a public official within the meaning intended in Article 350 of this Law.

Any person who publishes any of the following shall be punished by a fine of fifty thousand to two hundred thousand pounds:

1- A document of a felony or misdemeanour investigation before it is read out in a public hearing.

2- Deliberations of the courts.

3- Trials of closed hearings.

4- Trials in an action of parentage.

5- Trials in actions of divorce or judicial separation.

6- Any trial the publication of which the courts have prohibited.

The preceding provisions shall not apply to judgments published in good faith by means other than notices or placards.

Any persons who publicly open or announce subscriptions in order to indemnify fines, fees or damages awarded by a criminal court shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than six months and by a fine not exceeding one hundred thousand pounds, or by either of these two penalties.

A judicial custodian who intentionally causes damage to, or disposes of, all or part of the things entrusted to him shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years and by a fine of twenty thousand to two hundred thousand pounds.

He shall be sentenced to the fine alone if the thing is damaged through his negligence.

Any other person who, being the owner of things placed under the authority of the judiciary or claiming ownership thereof, intentionally takes them or causes damage to them, or conceals what has been taken thereof or disposes thereof while aware of the matter, shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year and by a fine of twenty thousand to one hundred thousand pounds.

The following shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year and by a fine of one hundred thousand to one million pounds:

1- Any person who remains in an immovable property in disregard of an eviction decision, or takes possession of an immovable property from which he was evicted.

2- Any person who violates the measures taken by the judge to preserve ownership or possession.

If the act is accompanied by violence, from six months to two years.

Any person who conceals or tears up, even partially, a notice posted in execution of a judgment of conviction shall be punished by a fine of fifty thousand to two hundred thousand pounds.

If the person sentenced to the penalty of posting the judgment commits the aforementioned offence himself, or is an instigator of or an accomplice to it, he shall incur, in addition to the fine, imprisonment for up to six months.

Any person who enables or facilitates the escape of a person detained or imprisoned in accordance with the law for a misdemeanour or a contravention shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than six months.

If the escapee was detained or imprisoned for a felony punishable by a temporary felony penalty, the offender shall be sentenced to imprisonment from one year to three years, and if the penalty for the felony is more severe, the offender shall be subject to hard labour from three to seven years.

Any person who publicly insults another or exposes him to public contempt because he did not challenge someone to a duel or did not accept the challenge of one who challenged him shall be punished by the same penalty.
If the duel leads to death or to permanent disability, the penalty in the first case shall be detention from three to seven years, and in the second case imprisonment from one year to three years.
The physician or surgeon who attended to the duellists shall be exempted from the penalty.

Any person who counterfeits the seal of the Lebanese State or the seal of a foreign state, or uses the counterfeited seal with knowledge of the matter, shall be punished by hard labour for at least seven years.

Any person who uses without right the seal of the Lebanese State, or counterfeits the impression of its seal or the impression of the seal of a foreign state, shall be punished by temporary hard labour.

In both cases, the offender shall incur a fine of not less than five hundred thousand pounds.

Any person who counterfeits a seal, brand, stamp or marking hammer belonging to a public administration, whether Lebanese or foreign, or counterfeits the impression of those instruments.

And any person who uses for an unlawful purpose any of the official marks mentioned in the preceding paragraph, whether genuine or forged, shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to three years and by a fine from one hundred thousand to six hundred thousand pounds.
Any person who commits the counterfeiting punishable under this subdivision shall be exempted from punishment if he destroys the criminal material before any use or prosecution.

Any person who counterfeits gold or silver currency legally or customarily in circulation in Lebanon or in another state for the purpose of uttering it, or participates with knowledge of the matter in issuing the counterfeited currency, in uttering it, or in introducing it into Lebanese territory or the territory of a foreign state, shall be punished by hard labour for a term of not less than five years and by a fine amounting to at least five hundred thousand pounds.

If one of the offences provided for in the preceding Article relates to metallic currency other than gold and silver, the penalty shall be temporary hard labour and a fine from two hundred thousand to two million pounds.

Whoever counterfeits or forges stamped papers, fiscal stamps, receipt stamps or postage stamps with the intent to use them unlawfully, or puts them into circulation with knowledge of the matter, shall be punished by temporary hard labour for up to five years and by a fine of not less than one hundred thousand pounds.

Whoever uses, with knowledge of the matter, one of the counterfeited or forged stamps or a stamp that has already been used shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to one year and by a fine from fifty thousand to two hundred thousand pounds.

Whoever participates in one of the felonies provided for in the second and third subsections of this chapter and informs the authority of this felony before its completion shall be exempted from the penalty; however, a defendant who enables the arrest, even after prosecutions have begun, of the other offenders or of those whose hiding place he knows shall only have his penalty reduced in accordance with the provisions of Article 251.
Forgery is a deliberate distortion of the truth, in the facts or statements established by an instrument or manuscript constituting a document, motivated by causing material, moral or social harm.
Whoever uses a forged item with knowledge of the matter shall be punished by the same penalty as the perpetrator of the forgery.
If the forgery is committed or the forged item is used with the intent to prove a true matter, the penalty shall be reduced in accordance with Article 251.

A public official who commits material forgery in the course of performing his duty shall be punished by temporary hard labour for at least five years:

Either by misusing a signature, seal or fingerprint and, in general, by signing a forged signature, or by fabricating an instrument or manuscript, or by committing a deletion, addition or alteration in the content of an instrument or manuscript. The penalty shall not be less than seven years if the forged document is one of the documents that remain valid until challenged for forgery. The provisions of this article shall apply in the event of the total or partial destruction of the document.

A public official who draws up a document within his competence and causes a distortion in its subject matter or circumstances shall be punished by the penalties provided for in the preceding article, subject to the distinction set forth therein:

Either by misusing a blank signature entrusted to him.

Or by recording agreements or statements other than those issued by the contracting parties or dictated by them.

Or by certifying false facts as true or unacknowledged facts as acknowledged, or by distorting any other fact by omitting a matter or stating it in an incorrect manner.

For the application of the preceding Articles, clergymen shall be treated as public officials in transactions which they perform by virtue of the law relating to personal status and religious endowments (waqfs), as well as anyone who is authorised by virtue of the laws and regulations to confer an official character upon an instrument, a signature, or a seal.

All other persons who commit forgery in official documents by one of the means mentioned in the preceding Articles shall be punished by temporary hard labour in cases where the law does not provide otherwise.

The following shall be deemed as official documents for the application of the preceding Articles:

1- Shares, bonds, certificates of deposit, and all other transferable securities instruments provided for in Articles 453 et seq. of the Code of Commerce, whether registered, to bearer, or to order, which the law authorises companies or institutions to issue in Lebanon or in another State.

2- The registers, entries, documents, and financial instruments of the Bank of Lebanon.

3- Lebanese or foreign academic certificates issued by official authorities, higher institutes, or universities, and required for the practice of a profession, trade, or public office, or for admission to another academic institution.

4- Lottery tickets issued by official administrations and bodies.

Whoever is legally obliged to keep registers subject to the supervision of the authority and records false matters therein or omits to record true matters therein shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year and by a fine of at least one hundred thousand pounds, if the act is capable of misleading the authority into error.

The same penalty shall be imposed on anyone who, knowing the matter, produces a counterfeited or altered document, or one drawn up in a manner contrary to the truth, which is intended to serve as a basis either for the calculation of taxes, fees, or other revenues due to the State or to a public administration, or for the legal supervision over the offender's acts relating to his profession.

Whoever proceeds, by any material or moral means among the means provided for in Articles 456 and 457 of the Penal Code, to forge an identity card, an individual civil status extract certificate, a passport, or an entry visa, shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years.

Whoever, with the intent to utter currency circulating legally or customarily in Lebanon or in a foreign State, proceeds to debase it either by diminishing its weight or by coating it with a plating whereby it is falsely supposed to be of greater value, or participates, while aware of the matter, in issuing currency debased in this manner, or in uttering it, or in introducing it into Lebanese territory or into the territory of a foreign State, shall be punished with the penalties prescribed in the preceding Article.

Whoever counterfeits banknotes or Lebanese or foreign bank notes issued by permission of the State with the intent to utter them, or participates in issuing them or in uttering them, shall be punished with the penalties prescribed in Article 440.

Whoever falsifies instruments such as those mentioned above, or participates, while aware of the matter, in issuing debased notes or in uttering them or in introducing them into Lebanese territory or into the territory of another State, shall be punished with the penalties prescribed in Article 441.

Whoever manufactures, offers, transports for the purpose of trade, or utters metallic pieces imitating therewith currency circulating legally or customarily in Lebanon or in another country, or printed papers that may cause confusion between them and paper money or Lebanese or foreign bank notes issued by permission of the State, shall be punished with imprisonment and a fine.

Whoever receives in good faith pieces of currency, banknotes, or Lebanese or foreign bank notes issued by permission of the State that are counterfeited, debased, or falsified, and utters them after having ascertained their defects, shall be punished with a fine not exceeding two hundred thousand pounds.

Whoever returns into circulation, while aware of the matter, currency, banknotes, or Lebanese or foreign bank notes issued by permission of the State, or instruments to order, which have ceased to be in circulation, shall incur the same penalty.

Whoever manufactures machines or instruments prepared for the counterfeiting, debasing, or falsifying of currency or Lebanese or foreign bank notes issued by permission of the State, or obtains them with the intent to use them in an unlawful manner, shall be punished with temporary hard labour and with a fine of at least two hundred thousand pounds. Whoever acquires such machines or instruments with knowledge of their nature shall be punished with imprisonment for at least one year.

Whoever is found in possession of machines or instruments prepared for the manufacture of currency, paper money, or bank notes and uses them in a lawful manner shall be punished with the felony penalties prescribed in the preceding Article.
Whoever publicly blasphemes the name of God shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year.

Whoever, by one of the means provided for in Article 209, demeans religious rites (1) practised publicly or incites contempt for one of those rites shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years.

Shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years:

1- Whoever causes a disturbance during the performance of one of the religious rituals, ceremonies or observances relating to those rituals, or obstructs them by acts of violence or threat.

2- Whoever demolishes, shatters, defaces, desecrates or defiles buildings dedicated to a clinic, or their emblems and other things venerated by the followers of a religion or a group of people.

If a member of the clergy violates the legal provisions relating to the change of religion or sect, or celebrates a religious marriage without verifying, where necessary, that the said provisions have been observed, he shall be punished by a fine from fifty thousand to five hundred thousand pounds.

The offender may be barred from the rights mentioned in the second and fourth paragraphs of Article 65 if he commits one of the offences set forth in Articles 474 to 476, if he commits one of the offences set forth in Articles 474 to 476.
Whoever causes a disturbance at funerals or ceremonies for the dead or obstructs them by acts of violence or threat shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to one year.

Whoever steals or destroys a corpse in whole or in part shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year, and if the theft occurs with the intent to conceal death or birth, from two months to two years.

Shall be punished by a fine from fifty thousand to five hundred thousand pounds and by imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months, or by either of the two penalties, whoever, for a scientific or educational purpose and without the consent of the person entitled thereto, takes a corpse, dissects it, or uses it in any other manner.

Shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years:

1- Anyone who violates or profanes the sanctity of graves or funerary monuments, or intentionally proceeds to demolish, shatter or deface them.

2- Anyone who profanes, demolishes, shatters or defaces any other object dedicated to funeral rites or to the maintenance or decoration of cemeteries.

Shall be punished by disciplinary detention and by a fine from twenty thousand to two hundred thousand pounds:

Those who proceed to bury or cremate a dead person without observing the legal procedures, or violate in any manner whatsoever the laws and regulations relating to burial or cremation.

If the act is committed with the intent of concealing a death or a birth, the penalty shall be from two months to two years.

If a clergyman solemnises the marriage of a minor who has not completed the eighteenth year of his age without recording in the contract the consent of the person who holds guardianship over the minor, or having it replaced by the permission of the judge, he shall be punished by a fine from fifty thousand to five hundred thousand pounds.

The same penalty shall be incurred by a clergyman who solemnises a marriage before the completion of the publications and all other formalities prescribed by the law or by personal status, or who officiates at the marriage of a woman before the expiry of her waiting period (iddah).

Anyone who marries in a legal manner while knowing of the nullity of his marriage by reason of a prior marriage shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year, and the clergyman who officiates at the conclusion of the said marriage while knowing of the prior marital bond shall be subject to the same penalty.

- Every Lebanese who marries a foreign woman for the purpose of granting her Lebanese nationality shall be punished by temporary hard labour, and the forfeiture of the nationality acquired by the wife by virtue of this marriage shall be adjudged, and the same penalty shall be inflicted upon her.
The representatives of the contracting parties and the witnesses who attended the marriage in this capacity shall be assimilated to clergymen for the application of the preceding provisions.

Article 487: Adultery committed by either spouse shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to two years. The same penalty shall be imposed upon the partner in adultery if he is married, and otherwise by imprisonment from one month to one year.

Save for judicial confession and flagrante delicto, no evidence of proof shall be admitted against the partner except that which arises from letters and written documents which he has written.

The penalty shall be doubled for the offending spouse if the offence of adultery takes place in the conjugal home.

.
Either spouse shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year if he openly keeps a paramour in any place whatsoever. The same penalty shall be inflicted upon the partner.

Any person who, by fabrication, alteration or modification, forges a pass, a hunting licence, a licence to carry a weapon, a driving licence, a voter card, a transport document or a copy of the judicial record shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years.

The same penalty shall be imposed upon:

1- Any person who obtains one of these documents by stating a false identity, by assuming a name other than his own, or by any other misleading means.

2- Any person who uses one of these documents issued in a name other than his own or with an identity other than his own.

3- A public official who delivers one of these documents while knowing of the assumption of the name or identity.

Any person who, while exercising a public function, a public service, or a medical or health profession, issues a false certificate intended to be submitted to the public authority or which is liable to procure an unlawful benefit for a third party or to cause harm to the interest of any person.

And any person who, by assuming the name of one of the persons mentioned in the preceding paragraph, fabricates, or forges by means of alteration, a certificate such as that alluded to in the said Article, shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years.

If the false certificate was prepared in order to be produced before the judiciary or to justify exemption from a public service, imprisonment shall not be less than six months.

Service of process documents drawn up by process servers and other workers of the State and public administrations, as well as records and reports drawn up by judicial police officers, shall have the same standing as the documents mentioned in Article 463, and shall be punished by the penalty mentioned in this Article.

Any person who draws up under an assumed name or forges a certificate of good conduct or a certificate of indigence shall be punished by imprisonment for up to six months, and the penalty shall be from one month to one year if the certificate is drawn up under the name of a public official or if the forgery concerns a certificate issued by a public official.
