Any person who presents himself to a public authority with a false identity with the intent of procuring a benefit for himself or for another, or with the intention of harming the rights of any person, shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years, in addition to the felony penalties to which he may be subject in the event of his collusion with a public official.
The same penalty shall be imposed upon every person who knowingly attests, in the circumstances mentioned above, to the false identity of any person before the public authorities.

Any person who commits forgery in private documents by one of the means specified in Articles 456 and 457 shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to three years and by a fine of at least one hundred thousand pounds.

If the offender confesses to the criminal act before use and prosecution, he shall be exempted from punishment; however, if the confession to the offence takes place after the use of the forged item and before complaint or prosecution, the penalty shall be reduced in accordance with what is set forth in Article 251.

- The act of adultery may not be prosecuted except upon the complaint of one of the spouses and the complainant assuming the capacity of a civil claimant.

- The partner or accomplice shall only be prosecuted together with the adulterer.

- A complaint shall not be accepted from a spouse with whose consent the adultery was committed.

- A complaint shall not be accepted after the expiry of three months from the day on which the offence came to the knowledge of the complainant.

- A waiver of right in respect of the husband or wife shall extinguish the public prosecution and the civil actions in respect of all the other offenders.

- If the claimant consents to the resumption of the common life, the complaint shall lapse.

7 - a -

Whoever, for the purpose of obtaining marital rights to sexual intercourse or by reason thereof, beats or harms their spouse shall be punished by one of the penalties provided for in Articles 554 to 559 of the Penal Code.

In the event of recurrence of the beating and harming, the penalty shall be increased in accordance with the provisions of Article 257 of the Penal Code.

The withdrawal of the complainant shall extinguish the public prosecution in actions to which Articles 554 and 555 of the Penal Code apply.

The provisions governing cases of recidivism and habitual criminality shall remain in force where their conditions are met.

7 - b -

Whoever, for the purpose of obtaining marital rights to sexual intercourse or by reason thereof, threatens their spouse shall be punished by one of the penalties provided for in Articles 573 to 578 of the Penal Code.

In the event of recurrence of the threat, the penalty shall be increased in accordance with the provisions of Article 257 of the Penal Code.

The withdrawal of the complainant shall extinguish the public prosecution in actions to which Articles 577 and 578 of the Penal Code apply.

The provisions governing cases of recidivism and habitual criminality shall remain in force where their conditions are met.

Incest between ascendants and descendants, whether legitimate or illegitimate, or between full brothers and sisters and brothers and sisters on the father's or mother's side, or those who stand in the position of all the aforementioned among relatives by marriage, shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years, and if one of the offenders has legal or de facto authority over the other, the penalty shall be from one year to three years, and the offender may be barred from the right of guardianship.

The incest described in the preceding Article shall be prosecuted upon the complaint of a relative by blood or by marriage of one of the offenders up to the fourth degree, and prosecution shall be initiated without a complaint if the matter resulted in scandal.

Whoever abducts or conceals a child under seven years of age, substitutes one child for another, or attributes to a woman a child to whom she did not give birth shall be punished by temporary hard labour, and the penalty shall not be reduced below five years if the purpose of the offence or its consequence was to destroy or falsify the evidence relating to the personal status of the child or to record a fictitious personal status from the official registers.

Whoever deposits a child in a foundling home and conceals his identity while he is registered in the civil status registers as a legitimate child or an acknowledged illegitimate child shall be punished by temporary hard labour.

Every act other than the acts mentioned in the preceding articles that aims to destroy or falsify the evidence relating to the personal status of any person shall be punished by temporary hard labour.

Whoever abducts or removes a minor under eighteen years of age, even with his consent, for the purpose of removing him from the authority of the person having guardianship or custody over him shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years and by a fine from fifty thousand to two hundred thousand pounds, and if the minor has not completed twelve years of age, or was abducted or removed by fraud or force, the penalty shall be temporary hard labour.

The father, the mother, and any other person who does not comply with the order of the judge and refuses or delays producing a minor who has not completed eighteen years of age shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to two years and by a fine from fifty thousand to two hundred thousand pounds.

The penalties prescribed in the preceding articles shall be reduced to the extent specified in Article 251 for the offender who returns or produces the minor before the issuance of any judgment; this provision shall not apply in the case of recidivism.

Whoever casts away or abandons a child under seven years of age or any other person who is able to protect himself due to a physical or mental condition shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to one year; if the child or the incapacitated person is cast away or abandoned in a desolate place, the punishment shall be from one year to three years.

If the offence causes the victim an illness or injury or leads to his death, the offender shall be held liable therefor in accordance with the provisions of Article 191 in the case of casting away and abandonment in a non-desolate place if he did not foresee that consequence or believed that he could avoid it, and he shall be held liable therefor in accordance with the provisions of Article 189 in the case of casting away or abandonment in a desolate place whenever he foresaw the consequence and accepted the risks.

If the offender is one of the ascendants of the child or of the incapacitated person, or one of the persons entrusted with his custody, supervision, treatment, or upbringing, the penalty shall be aggravated in the manner provided for by Article 257, This text shall not apply to the mother who has proceeded, as an instigator, principal, or accomplice, to cast away or abandon her newborn to preserve her honour.

Whoever abandons or attempts to abandon, for a temporary or permanent period, a minor under eighteen years of age, even if with the intent of giving him up for adoption in return for financial consideration or any other benefit, shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to three years and by a fine from five million to twenty million Lebanese pounds.

The same penalty shall be imposed on the co-offender and the accomplice.

Shall be punished by the same penalty:

1- Whoever induces or attempts to induce the parents of a minor, or either of them, or the father or the mother of an illegitimate child acknowledged by them or by either of them, or anyone who holds the authority of parental guardianship or tutorship, to abandon the minor in return for sums of money or any other benefit.

2- Whoever induces or attempts to induce, by any direct or indirect means, the parents of a child who has been born or may be born to undertake to abandon the child or to contract to abandon him, and whoever possesses this undertaking, uses it, or attempts to use it.

3- Whoever induces or attempts to induce any other person to procreate, legitimately or not, with the intent of selling the newborn.

4- Whoever offers or attempts to offer his mediation in return for financial consideration or any other benefit, for the purpose of obtaining or adopting a child.

The penalty shall apply to instigation in all the cases mentioned above, regardless of the result to which it leads.

The penalty shall be aggravated in accordance with Article 257 of the Penal Code in the event of recidivism.

The father and mother who leave in a state of need their legitimate or illegitimate child, or a child they have adopted, whether they have refused to execute the obligation of maintenance incumbent upon them or have neglected to obtain the means enabling them to fulfil it, shall be punished by imprisonment with labour for three months at most and by a fine not exceeding two hundred thousand pounds.

Whoever has been ordered by a judgment that has acquired the force of res judicata to pay to his spouse, his former spouse, his ascendants, his descendants, or to any person whom he is obliged to maintain or bring up, and remains for two months without paying the instalments fixed in the court, shall be punished by imprisonment with labour from one month to six months and by a fine equal to the amount he was obliged to pay.

A decision issued by a foreign court accompanied by an enforcement order in Lebanon shall have the same standing as a decision issued by a Lebanese judge for the application of the preceding paragraph.

The penalties for the felonies provided for in this Chapter shall be increased pursuant to the provisions of Article 257: if they are committed by two or more persons who participated in overcoming the resistance of the victim or successively performed the act of indecency upon him, if the victim contracted a venereal disease or any other disease or harm resulting in an incapacitation exceeding ten days in duration or if the female victim was a virgin and her virginity was removed, if one of the aforementioned felonies led to the death of the victim and the perpetrator did not intend this result, the penalty shall not be less than twelve years.

Every public official who solicits the spouse of a prisoner or detainee or of a person subject to his supervision or authority, or solicits one of the relatives of that person, shall be punished by imprisonment for at least one year.

The same penalty shall be imposed on a public official who solicits the spouse or one of the relatives of a person who has a case the adjudication of which is entrusted to him or to his superiors.

The penalty shall be doubled if the offender achieves his purpose with one of the persons mentioned above.

In the event that the act is committed against a minor who has not completed eighteen years of age and has completed fifteen years of age, the penalty shall not be less than five years of imprisonment.

However, if the act is committed against a minor under fifteen years of age, the penalty shall not be less than seven years of imprisonment.

Whoever abducts by deception or violence a girl or a woman with the intent of marriage shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to three years.

The penalty shall not be less than five years of imprisonment where the minor victim has completed fifteen years of age and has not completed eighteen years of age.

However, if the minor is under fifteen years of age, the penalty of hard labour shall not be less than seven years.

Whoever abducts by deception or violence any person, whether male or female, with the intent to commit debauchery upon them, shall be punished by temporary hard labour, and if the said act is committed, the penalty shall not be less than seven years.

The penalty shall not be less than five years of hard labour where the minor victim has completed fifteen years of age and has not completed eighteen years of age.

However, if the minor is under fifteen years of age, the penalty of hard labour shall not be less than seven years.

If the act of debauchery is committed, a penalty of not less than seven years shall be imposed where the minor has completed fifteen years of age and has not completed eighteen years of age, whereas if the minor is under fifteen years of age, the penalty shall not be less than ten years of hard labour.

An offender who of his own accord returns the abducted person within forty-eight hours to a safe place and restores their liberty without committing against them an act contrary to modesty or another offence, whether a misdemeanour or a felony, shall benefit from the mitigating excuses provided for in Article 251.

Whoever compels a person other than his spouse, by violence and threat, to have sexual intercourse shall be punished by hard labour for at least five years, and the penalty shall not be less than seven years if the victim has not completed fifteen years of age.

Added pursuant to Law 204 dated 30/12/2020

Article 305 bis 1:

Whoever practises violence within the family that causes moral or economic harm to a family member, or leads to depriving one of them of basic needs, shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to three years and by a fine ranging between the minimum wage and three times that amount, or by either of these two penalties.

Whoever has sexual intercourse with a person other than his spouse who is unable to resist due to a physical or psychological deficiency or due to the forms of deceit used towards him shall be punished by hard labour for a period of at least five years.

The penalty shall not be less than seven years if the victim has not completed fifteen years of age.

Whoever has sexual intercourse with a minor under fifteen years of age shall be punished by temporary hard labour for a period of not less than five years.

The penalty shall not be less than seven years if the minor has not completed twelve years of age.

Whoever has sexual intercourse with a minor who has completed fifteen years of age and has not completed eighteen years of age shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years, and in this case, if a valid marriage is contracted between them, the prosecution or trial shall be stayed, and if a judgment has been issued in the case, the execution of the sentence imposed shall be suspended, provided that the judge's decision to suspend shall only be issued on the basis of a report prepared by a social worker taking into account the social and psychological circumstances of the minor.

If the decision to stay the prosecution or trial or to suspend the penalty is issued by reason of the marriage, the judge must assign the social worker to submit a report to him on the psychological and social condition of the minor after the marriage every six months during a period of three years from the date of issuance of his decision.

The prosecution or trial, or the execution of the penalty, shall be resumed before the expiry of the three-year period if the marriage ends in divorce without a legitimate reason or because of the perpetrator of the offence, or if it appears that there is any other legitimate reason justifying the resumption of the prosecution, trial, or execution of the penalty in light of the periodic reports referred to in this Article.

Whoever seduces a girl with a promise of marriage and deflowers her shall be punished, if the act does not warrant a more severe penalty, by imprisonment for at least six months and a fine ranging between three million and five million pounds, or by either of the two penalties.

The penalty shall not be less than five years' imprisonment if the assaulted minor has completed fifteen years of age and has not completed eighteen years of age.

In both of these two cases, if a valid marriage is contracted between them, the prosecution or the trial shall be stayed, and if a judgment has been issued in the case, the execution of the penalty imposed shall be suspended; if the assaulted person is a minor, the judge's decision of suspension shall only be issued on the basis of a report prepared by a social worker that takes into consideration the social and psychological circumstances of the minor.

If the decision to stay the prosecution or the trial or to suspend the penalty by reason of marriage is issued, the judge shall, if the assaulted person is a minor, assign the social worker to submit a report to him on the psychological and social condition of the minor after marriage every six months during a period of three years from the date of issuance of his decision.

The prosecution shall be resumed or the execution of the penalty shall be resumed before the expiry of the three-year period if the marriage ends in divorce without a legitimate reason or due to the perpetrator of the offence, or if the existence of any other legitimate reason justifying the resumption of the prosecution, the trial, or the execution of the penalty becomes apparent in the light of the periodic reports referred to in this Article.

Where the minor is under fifteen years of age, the penalty of hard labour shall not be less than seven years.

Save for confession, no evidence of proof against the offender shall be admitted other than that arising from letters and other documents which he has written.

Whoever touches or fondles in a manner contrary to decency a minor, whether male or female, who has completed fifteen years of age and has not completed eighteen years of age, or without his consent, shall be punished by imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months.

Where the act is committed against a minor under fifteen years of age, the penalty shall not be less than one year's imprisonment.

Whoever offers to a minor under fifteen years of age an act contrary to decency or addresses to him language offensive to modesty shall be punished by disciplinary detention or by a fine not exceeding one million pounds, or by both penalties together.

Every man who disguises himself in a woman's attire and enters a place reserved for women or into which entry at the time of the act is prohibited to persons other than women shall be punished by imprisonment for six months at most or by a fine of up to one million Lebanese pounds.

Where any ascendant, whether legitimate or illegitimate, any ascendant by marriage, any person exercising legal or de facto authority over a minor between fifteen and eighteen years of age, or any servant of those persons, has sexual intercourse with such minor, he shall be punished by hard labour for a term of not less than five years.

The same penalty shall be imposed if the offender is a public official or a cleric, or the director or an employee of an employment office, and commits the act by abusing the authority or facilities derived from his office.

The penalty shall not be less than seven years' hard labour if the minor is under fifteen years of age.

If, however, the minor is under twelve years of age, the penalty shall not be less than nine years' hard labour.

Whoever compels another by violence and threat to suffer or perform an indecent act shall be punished by hard labour for a term of not less than four years.

If the victim is a minor who has completed fifteen years of age and has not completed eighteen years of age, the offender shall be punished by hard labour for a term of not less than five years, and the minimum penalty shall be six years' hard labour if the act is committed against a minor who has not completed fifteen years of age.

Whoever resorts to various forms of deceit or takes advantage of a person's physical or mental infirmity and commits an indecent act upon him shall be punished by imprisonment for a term of ten years at most.

If, however, the act is committed upon a minor under fifteen years of age, the offender shall be sentenced to temporary hard labour.

Whoever commits an indecent act upon a minor under fifteen years of age shall be punished by temporary hard labour. The penalty shall not be less than four years if the minor has not completed twelve years of age.

Every person among the persons described in Article 506 who commits an indecent act upon a minor between fifteen and eighteen years of age shall be punished by hard labour for a term not exceeding ten years.

The penalty shall not be less than five years if the minor victim has not completed fifteen years of age.
The penalties prescribed in Articles 503 to 505 and 507 to 509 shall be increased in the manner set forth in Article 257 if the offender is one of the persons referred to in Article 506.

Whosoever incites one or more persons, whether male or female, who have not attained twenty-one years of age, to debauchery, or facilitates it for such person or assists such person in committing it, shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to three years and by a fine ranging between twice the minimum wage and four times its amount.

Whosoever engages in prostitution or facilitates it shall be punished by the same penalty.

Subject to the provisions of Article 529 read in conjunction with Article 506, the penalty shall be increased in accordance with the provisions of Article 257 of this Law if the offence takes place within the family, without regard to the age of the person against whom the offence is committed.

Whosoever, in order to gratify the passions of others, seduces, entices or leads away a person, even with that person's consent, shall be punished by imprisonment for at least one year and by a fine of not less than half the value of the official minimum wage.

Whosoever detains a person against that person's will in a house of debauchery on account of a debt owed to the offender by that person shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years and by a fine from one tenth to the value of the official minimum wage.

Whosoever habitually facilitates, for the purpose of gain, the seduction of the public into committing debauchery with others, and whosoever uses one of the means referred to in paragraphs 2 and 3 of Article 209 to attract people to debauchery, shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year and by a fine from twenty thousand pounds to two hundred thousand pounds.

Every person who relies for earning his livelihood, in whole or in part, on the prostitution of others shall be punished by imprisonment from two years to three years and by a fine ranging between five times the minimum wage and ten times its amount.

Subject to the provisions of Article 529 read in conjunction with Article 506 of this Law, the penalty shall be increased in accordance with the provisions of Article 257 of the Penal Code if the offence takes place within the family, and the penalty shall be doubled if the offence is accompanied by any form of violence or threat.
An attempt to commit the misdemeanours provided for in Articles 523 to 525 shall be punishable.
The penalties provided for in the aforementioned Articles shall be increased pursuant to the provision of Article 257 if the offenders are among those described in Article 506.
Expulsion from the country and supervised liberty may be ordered upon conviction for one of the misdemeanours provided for in this subdivision, and the closure of the premises shall also be ordered.

Whoever causes the death of a human being without intention to kill, by beating, violence, severity, or by any other intentional act, shall be punished by hard labour for five years at least, and the penalty shall not be less than seven years if the act is accompanied by one of the cases provided for in the two preceding Articles.

A mother who proceeds, in order to avert shame, to kill her newborn child whom she conceived out of wedlock shall be punished by temporary detention, and the penalty shall not be less than five years if the act takes place with premeditation.
Whoever intentionally kills a human being out of compassion upon his insistent request shall be punished by detention for ten years at most.

Whoever induces a human being by any means whatsoever to commit suicide or assists him, in one of the ways mentioned in Article 213 - the first, second, and fourth paragraphs - in killing himself, shall be punished by detention for ten years at most if the suicide takes place, by imprisonment from three months to two years in the case of an attempted suicide that results in harm or permanent disability, and if the person induced or assisted to commit suicide is a juvenile under fifteen years of age or an imbecile, the penalties for incitement to murder or complicity therein shall apply.

"Whoever intentionally proceeds to beat, wound, or harm a person, and these acts do not result in an illness or the incapacitation of a person from work for a period exceeding ten days, shall be punished, upon the complaint of the injured party, by imprisonment for six months at most or by disciplinary detention and by a fine from ten thousand to fifty thousand pounds, or by one of these two penalties.

The penalty shall be doubled if the offence is committed against a physician or one of his assistants or any worker in the medical field, during the practice of their work or by reason thereof.

The waiver of the complainant shall extinguish the public right of action and shall have the same effect on the penalty as the pardon of the civil claimant».

"If the harm caused results in an illness or the incapacitation of a person from work for a period exceeding ten days, the offender shall be punished by imprisonment for a period not exceeding one year and by a fine of one hundred thousand pounds at most, or by one of these two penalties.

The penalty shall be doubled if the offence is committed against a physician or one of his assistants or any worker in the medical field, during the practice of their work or by reason thereof.

If the complainant waives his right, the penalty shall be reduced by half».

"If the illness or incapacitation from work exceeds twenty days, the penalty of imprisonment from three months to three years shall be imposed, in addition to the aforementioned fine.

The penalty shall be doubled if the offence is committed against a physician or one of his assistants or any worker in the medical field, during the practice of their work or by reason thereof».
Any offence against public decency by one of the means mentioned in the first paragraph of Article 209 shall be punishable by imprisonment from one month to one year.

Any offence against public morals by one of the means mentioned in the second and third paragraphs of Article 209 shall be punishable by imprisonment from one month to one year and by a fine from twenty thousand to two hundred thousand pounds.

Whosoever manufactures, exports, supplies, or possesses writings, drawings, manual or photographic pictures, films, signs, or other indecent objects with the intent to trade in or distribute them, or advertises or gives notice of the means of obtaining them, shall be punishable by the same penalties.
Any sexual intercourse contrary to nature shall be punishable by imprisonment for up to one year.

Any propaganda by one of the means provided for in paragraphs 2 and 3 of Article 209 intended to disseminate, promote, or facilitate the use of means of abortion shall be punishable by imprisonment from two months to two years and by a fine from one hundred thousand to five hundred thousand pounds.

Whosoever sells, offers for sale, or possesses with the intent to sell substances prepared to induce abortion, or facilitates the use thereof in any manner whatsoever, shall be punishable by the same penalty.
Every woman who procures her own miscarriage by means she has used, or which another person has used with her consent, shall be punishable by imprisonment from six months to three years.

Whosoever, by any means whatsoever, procures the miscarriage of a woman or attempts to procure her miscarriage with her consent shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to three years, and if the abortion or the means used to that end results in the death of the woman, the perpetrator shall be punished by hard labour from four to seven years, and the penalty shall be from five years to ten years if death was caused by means more dangerous than the means to which the woman consented.

Whoever intentionally causes the miscarriage of a woman without her consent shall be punished with hard labour for five years at least, and the penalty shall not be less than ten years if the abortion or the means used lead to the death of the woman.
Articles 542 and 543 shall apply even if the woman upon whom the means of miscarriage were performed was not pregnant.

A woman who causes her own miscarriage to preserve her honour shall benefit from a mitigating excuse, and likewise whoever commits one of the offences provided for in Articles 542 and 543 to preserve the honour of one of his descendants or his female relatives up to the second degree shall benefit from the same excuse.

If one of the misdemeanours provided for in this Chapter is committed by a physician, a surgeon, a midwife, a druggist, a pharmacist, or one of their employees, whether as principals, instigators, or accessories, the penalty shall be increased in accordance with Article 257, and the same shall apply if the offender has been accustomed to selling drugs and other substances prepared for miscarriage, and the offender shall furthermore be subject to prohibition from practising his profession or his work even if they are not contingent upon the authorisation of the authority or the obtaining of a certificate, and the closure of the premises may also be ordered.

Whoever intentionally kills a human being shall be punished with hard labour from fifteen years to twenty years.

The penalty shall be from twenty years to twenty-five years if the act of killing is committed by one of the spouses against the other.

Intentional homicide shall be punishable with hard labour for life if it is committed:

1- For a base motive.

2- To obtain the benefit resulting from a misdemeanour.

3 - By the offender proceeding to mutilate the corpse after the killing.

4- Against a minor under fifteen years of age.

5- Against two or more persons.

Intentional homicide shall be punishable with death if it is committed:

1- With premeditation.

2- In preparation for a felony or a misdemeanour, or to facilitate or execute it, or to facilitate the flight of the instigators of that felony or its principals or accessories, or to prevent their punishment.

3- Against one of the offender's ascendants or descendants.

4 - Where the offender commits acts of torture or savagery against persons.

5 - Against a public official during the exercise of his duties or in the course of his exercise thereof or because of them.

6- Against a human being because of his sectarian affiliation or in vengeance against him for a felony committed by another person of his sect or of his relatives or of his partisans.

7- By using explosive materials.

8- In order to evade a felony or a misdemeanour or to conceal its traces.

"If the act leads to the severing or excision of an organ or the amputation of a limb, or to the disabling of either of them, or the disabling of one of the senses from functioning, or causes grave disfigurement or any other permanent infirmity or one having the appearance of a permanent infirmity, the offender shall be punished with temporary hard labour for ten years at most.

The penalty shall be doubled if the offence is committed against a physician or one of his assistants or any of the workers in the medical field, during the practice of their work or by reason thereof."
Any person who, by one of the acts mentioned in Article 554, causes the miscarriage of a pregnant woman while having knowledge of her pregnancy shall be punished with the same penalty.

"The penalties mentioned in this Subsection shall be increased in accordance with the provisions of Article 257 if the act is committed in one of the cases set forth in the second paragraph of Article 547 and in Articles 548 and 549 of this Law.

If the offence provided for in any of Articles 554, 555, 556 and 557 is committed against a physician or one of his assistants or any of the workers in the medical field, during the practice of their work or by reason thereof, intentionally, or if it is committed by a group of at least three persons, the penalty shall be increased in the manner set forth in Article 257 of the Penal Code."

If the killing or harming of a person occurs during a brawl in which a group participated and it is not possible to ascertain the actual perpetrator, all those who attempted to harm the victim shall be punished with the penalty for the committed crime after reducing the penalty by up to half.

If the crime entails the death penalty, Hard Labour for Life, or detention for life, the punishment imposed shall be not less than seven years.
The aforementioned penalties shall be increased in accordance with the provisions of Article 257 for whoever directly caused the brawl.

The following acts shall be deemed to be in self-defence:

1 - The act of one who defends himself or his property, or the person of another or his property, against whoever proceeds by using violence to commit theft or pillage.

2- The act committed when repelling a person who entered or attempted to enter at night into an inhabited house or its adjoining appurtenances by scaling enclosures, walls or entrances, or piercing or breaking them, or by using counterfeit keys or special tools; and if the act occurs during the day, the perpetrator shall benefit only from the mitigating excuse pursuant to Article 251.

The offender shall not be considered to be in a state of legitimate defence if he did not hold the belief that the assault on persons or property was the direct purpose of the aggressor or the result of the resistance he might encounter in executing his aims.

.
Whoever causes the death of a person through negligence, lack of precaution, or non-observance of laws or regulations shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years.

Where the offender's fault results only in harm such as that provided for in Articles 556 to 558, the penalty shall be from two months to one year, and every other unintentional harm shall be punished by imprisonment for six months at most or by a fine not exceeding two hundred thousand pounds.

Prosecution shall be contingent upon the complaint of the victim where the harm does not result in illness or incapacity for work for a period exceeding ten days, and the complainant's waiver of his right shall have the same effects set forth in Articles 554 and 555.

Every driver of a vehicle who causes an accident, even if material, and does not stop immediately, or does not attend to the victim, or attempts to evade liability by fleeing, shall be punished by imprisonment for a period not exceeding one month and by a fine not exceeding five hundred pounds.

The penalties mentioned in Articles 564 and 565 shall be increased by half if the offender commits one of these acts.

"The new Article 567:

Whoever wilfully abstains from relieving, rescuing, or assisting any person found in a state of imminent and immediate danger, when it was within his power to render assistance without exposing himself or others to danger, or wilfully abstains from preventing the occurrence of bodily harm of any kind whatsoever to another person, when it was within his power to avert the harm without exposing himself or others to danger, shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year and by a fine from two hundred thousand to two million pounds, or by one of these two penalties.

No liability whatsoever shall attach to anyone who undertakes to provide relief or rescue, particularly to those who suffer cardiac arrest by means of resuscitation with electric shocks or the like, even if his intervention does not lead to a result.

The same penalty shall be imposed on anyone who knows of the existence of evidence proving the innocence of a person detained or on trial in a case of a felony or misdemeanour and does not come forward of his own accord to testify thereto before the judiciary or the security authorities.

In this case, the perpetrator shall be exempted from the penalty if he subsequently comes forward of his own accord at a later time.

The perpetrator of the offence that is the subject of the prosecution, his accomplices, his accessories, and their relatives up to the fourth degree shall also be exempted from the penalty."

Where death and harm committed intentionally or unintentionally are the result of several causes unknown to the perpetrator and independent of his act, the penalty may be reduced to the extent set forth in Article 200.

Whoever deprives another of his personal liberty by abduction or by any other means shall be punished with the following hard labour: and the perpetrator shall be punished with hard labour for life in each of the following cases:

1- If the duration of the deprivation of liberty exceeds one month.

2- If physical or moral torture is inflicted upon the person deprived of his liberty.

3- If the offence is committed against a public official during the performance of his duty or in the course of performing it, or by reason of his belonging to it.

4- If the motives of the crime are sectarian or partisan or in revenge against the victim for an act committed by another person from his sect, his party members, or his relatives.

5- If the perpetrator uses his victim as a hostage to intimidate individuals, institutions, or the State for the purpose of extorting money or compelling the execution of a wish or the performance of an act or the abstention therefrom.

6- If the offence occurs consequent to an attack on a private or public motorised means of transport, such as a car, train, ship, or aircraft.

7- If the offence occurs by the act of a group of two or more persons who were armed at the time of its commission.

The penalty shall be increased in accordance with Article 257 if the offence results in the death of a human being as a consequence of terror or any other cause related to the incident.

If the person deprived of his liberty is released spontaneously within a period not exceeding three days and without another crime, whether a felony or a misdemeanour, being committed against him, the perpetrator shall be punished with imprisonment from six months to three years.

This penalty shall be reduced by half for the benefit of the perpetrator if he releases the victim spontaneously within twenty-four hours at most and without committing any other crime, whether a felony or a misdemeanour, against him.

Whoever enters a house or dwelling of another, or the appurtenances of his dwelling or house, contrary to his will, as well as whoever remains in the aforementioned places contrary to the will of the person who has the right to exclude him, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months.

Imprisonment from three months to three years shall be imposed if the act occurs at night, or by means of breaking or violence against persons, or by the use of a weapon, or is committed by several persons gathered together.

Prosecution in the case provided for in the first paragraph shall only take place upon the complaint of the injured party.

Whoever infiltrates by means of breaking or violence against persons into places belonging to others that are not open to the public, or remains therein despite the will of the person who has the right to exclude him, shall be punished with disciplinary detention or a fine not exceeding one hundred thousand pounds.

The offender shall only be prosecuted upon the complaint of the injured party.

Whoever threatens another with a weapon shall be punished with imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months, and the penalty shall range between two months and one year if the weapon is a firearm and the perpetrator uses it.

Defamation of any person committed by any of the means mentioned in Article 209 shall be punishable by imprisonment for up to three months and by a fine of up to two hundred thousand pounds, or by either of these two penalties.

A fine alone shall be imposed if the defamation was not committed publicly.
The perpetrator of defamation shall not be permitted, in justification of himself, to prove the truth of the act that is the subject of the defamation or to prove its notoriety.

Slander against any person committed by any of the means mentioned in Article 209, as well as contempt committed by any of the means set forth in Article 383, shall be punishable by imprisonment from one week to three months or by a fine from fifty thousand to four hundred thousand pounds.

A fine alone shall be imposed if the slander was not committed publicly.
The judge may exempt both parties or either of them from the penalty if the aggrieved party provoked the slander by an wrongful act or if the slander was mutual.

The action shall depend on the aggrieved party assuming the capacity of a personal claimant.

If the defamation or slander is directed at a deceased person, his relatives up to the fourth degree, to the exclusion of others, may exercise the right of prosecution, without prejudice to the right of any relative or heir who has personally suffered damage from the offence.

Whoever threatens another with a felony punishable by death, hard labour for life or for more than fifteen years, or detention for life, whether by means of writing, even if anonymous, or through a third party, shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to three years if the threat includes an order to perform an act, even if lawful, or to refrain therefrom.

If the threat of one of the felonies mentioned above does not include an order, or includes an order but was made verbally without the intermediary of another person, a sentence of imprisonment from three months to two years shall be imposed.

Imprisonment from one month to one year shall be imposed for threatening a felony less severe than the felonies mentioned in Article 574 if committed by one of the means set forth in the same Article.
Threatening a misdemeanour that includes an order, if made in writing or through a third party, shall be punished by imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months.

Every other threat to inflict unjust harm, if made by speech or by one of the means mentioned in Article 209, and which is of a nature to severely affect the mind of the victim, shall be punished, upon complaint, by a fine not exceeding one hundred thousand pounds.

Whoever, by virtue of his status, office, profession or art, has knowledge of a secret and discloses it without legitimate cause, or uses it for his own benefit or for the benefit of another, shall be punished by imprisonment for at most one year and by a fine not exceeding four hundred thousand pounds if the act is of a nature to cause harm, even if moral.

Every person attached to the Post and Telegraph Service who abuses this capacity of his by acquainting himself with a sealed letter, or destroying or embezzling one of the letters, or disclosing its contents to someone other than the addressee, shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years.

The same penalty shall be imposed upon whoever is attached to the Telephone Service and discloses a telephone communication with which he became acquainted by virtue of his office or work.

Every other person who intentionally destroys or opens a letter or telegram not addressed to him, or by deceit acquaints himself with a telephone communication, shall be punished by a fine not exceeding one hundred thousand pounds.

The same penalty shall be imposed upon whoever becomes acquainted with a letter or with a telegraphic or telephone communication the divulgence of which entails causing harm to another, and informs thereof someone other than the person to whom it was sent.

Shall be punished by detention for a period of ten years, and by a fine of two hundred times to four hundred times the official minimum wage where the perpetrator of the offence provided for in Article 586 (1), or the co-principal or accomplice therein or the instigator thereof, is:

1 - A public official, or any person entrusted with a public service, or the director of an employment agency or an employee therein.

2 - One of the ascendants of the victim, whether legitimate or illegitimate, or one of the members of his family, or any person exercising over him a legal or de facto authority, whether direct or indirect.

Shall be punished by detention for a period of fifteen years, and by a fine of three hundred times to six hundred times the official minimum wage if the offence provided for in Article 586 (1) is committed:

1 - By the act of a group of two or more persons committing criminal acts, whether in Lebanon or in more than one State.

2 - If the offence involves more than one victim.

Where any of the following circumstances is present, the criminal acts set forth in Article 586 (1) shall be punished by imprisonment from ten years to twelve years and by a fine of two hundred times to four hundred times the official minimum wage:

a) When the offence involves serious harm to the victim or to another person, or the death of the victim or another person, including death resulting from suicide.

b) When the offence relates to a person in a state of particular vulnerability, including a pregnant woman.

c) When the offence exposes the victim to contracting a life-threatening disease, including infection with the human immunodeficiency virus / acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS).

d) When the victim is physically or mentally disabled.

e) When the victim is under eighteen years of age.

Shall be exempted from penalties whoever takes the initiative to notify the administrative or judicial authority of the offences provided for in this Chapter and provides it with information that enables either the discovery of the offence before its occurrence or the arrest of its perpetrators, co-principals, accomplices therein or instigators thereof, provided that the person making the notification is not liable as the perpetrator of the offence set forth in Article 586 (1).

Shall benefit from the mitigating excuse whoever provides the competent authorities, after the commission of the offences provided for in this Chapter, with information that enables the prevention of their continuation.

A victim for whom it is established that he was compelled to commit acts punishable by law or violated the conditions of residence or work shall be exempted from punishment.

The investigating judge or the judge examining the case file may, pursuant to a decision issued by him, authorise the victim to reside in Lebanon during the period required by the investigation procedures.

The Minister of Justice may conclude agreements with specialised institutions or associations to provide assistance and protection to victims of the offences provided for in this Chapter.

The conditions that must be met by these institutions and associations and the procedures for providing assistance and protection shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice.

The sums derived from the offences provided for in this Chapter shall be confiscated and deposited in a special account at the Ministry of Social Affairs to assist the victims of these offences.

The regulations pertaining to the account shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, upon the proposal of the Minister of Social Affairs.
The Lebanese courts shall have jurisdiction in the event that any of the acts constituting the offence is committed on Lebanese territory.

Whoever intentionally sets fire to buildings, factories, workshops, warehouses, or any inhabited or uninhabited structures located in a city or village, or sets fire to railway carriages or vehicles carrying one or more persons other than the offender or attached to a train in which there is one or more than one person, or sets fire to ships sailing or anchored in one of the ports, or to aircraft flying or stationed at an airport, whether they are his property or not, shall be punished by temporary hard labour for a period of not less than seven years.

Whoever intentionally sets fire to inhabited buildings or buildings prepared for habitation located outside populated places, or to woods, or to forests for logging, or to orchards, or to crops before their harvest, whether they are his property or not, shall be punished by the same penalty.

Whoever intentionally sets fire to buildings that are neither inhabited nor used for habitation located outside populated places, to crops, or to stacks of straw, or to a harvest left in its place, or to firewood stacked, arranged or left in its place, whether he does not own these things or owns them and the fire spread or could have spread therefrom to the property of others, shall be punished by temporary hard labour.

Every arson or attempted arson other than the aforementioned committed with the intent of causing material damage to others or drawing an unlawful gain for the perpetrator or for another shall be punished by imprisonment and a fine.

- "Trafficking in persons" is:

A - The recruitment, transportation, reception, detention, or harbouring of a person.

B - By means of the threat or use of force, or abduction or deception, or the abuse of power or of a position of vulnerability, or the giving or receiving of sums of money or benefits, or the use of these means against a person having authority over another person.

C - For the purpose of exploiting him or facilitating his exploitation by third parties.

The consent of the victim shall be irrelevant where any of the means set forth in this Article have been used.

"Victim of trafficking":

For the purposes of this Law, "victim of trafficking" means any natural person who has been the subject of trafficking in persons or whom the competent authorities reasonably consider to be a victim of trafficking in persons, regardless of whether the perpetrator of the offence has been identified, arrested, prosecuted, or convicted.

Compelling a person to participate in any of the following acts shall be considered exploitation pursuant to the provisions of this Article:

A) Acts punishable by law.

B) Prostitution, or the exploitation of the prostitution of others.

C) Sexual exploitation.

D) Begging.

E) Slavery, or practices similar to slavery.

F) Forced or compulsory labour.

G) Including the forced or compulsory recruitment of children for use in armed conflicts.

H) Forced involvement in terrorist acts.

I) The removal of organs or tissues from the body of the victim.

- The consent of the victim, or of one of his ascendants, his legal guardian, or any other person exercising lawful or de facto authority over him, to the intended exploitation set forth in this paragraph shall not be taken into account.

- The recruitment, transportation, reception, detention, or harbouring of a victim, for the purpose of exploitation in respect of persons under eighteen years of age, shall be considered trafficking in persons, even if this is not accompanied by the use of any of the means set forth in paragraph (1) (B) of this Article.

The offence provided for in Article 586 (1) shall be punishable as follows:

1 - By detention for a term of five years, and a fine of one hundred times to two hundred times the official minimum wage where such acts are committed in exchange for the granting of sums of money or any other benefits, or the promise of granting or receiving them.

2 - By detention for a term of seven years, and a fine of one hundred and fifty times to three hundred times the official minimum wage where such acts are committed through the use of deception, violence, acts of severity, threats, or the exercise of influence over the victim or a member of his family.

Whoever intentionally interrupts the operation of telegraphic or telephonic communications or radio broadcasts, whether by causing damage to the machines or wires or by any other manner, shall be punished by imprisonment for up to six months, and if the act results in danger to public safety, imprisonment from three months to two years shall be imposed.

The penalties mentioned in the preceding Articles shall be increased by half if any person suffers a permanent disability, and the death penalty shall be imposed if the matter leads to the death of any person.
Whoever causes by fault the sabotage, demolition and the rest of the acts mentioned in the preceding Articles shall be punished by imprisonment for a period not exceeding six months.

Every industrialist or workshop foreman who omits to place machines or signals to prevent work accidents or does not keep them always fit for use shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to two years and by a fine from one hundred thousand to one million pounds.

Whoever causes, through lack of precaution, negligence, or non-observance of laws or regulations, the disabling of the aforementioned machines and signals shall be punished by imprisonment for a period not exceeding six months.

Whoever intentionally removes one of these tools or renders it unfit for use shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years,

and temporary hard labour shall be imposed if the act results in a serious accident, andhard labour for life if it leads to the loss of a life.

"New Article 604:

Whoever violates the preventive decisions or instructions issued by the competent authorities and aimed at limiting the spread of epidemics shall be punished by a fine equivalent to half the official minimum wage, and the penalty shall be doubled in cases of recidivism.

Whoever causes, through lack of precaution, negligence, or non-observance of laws or regulations, the spread of an epidemic disease of human diseases shall be punished by imprisonment for up to six months. If the perpetrator commits his act knowing of the matter without intending the death of anyone, he shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to three years in addition to the fine."

Whoever causes, through negligence, lack of precaution, or non-observance of laws or regulations, the spread of an epizootic disease among domestic animals or a dangerous germ to crops or forests, shall be punished by a fine ranging between twenty thousand and two hundred thousand pounds.

If he intentionally commits his act, he shall be punished by imprisonment in addition to the fine.

Any person who intentionally kills a human being "in preparation" for committing the offences of arson provided for in the preceding Articles, or to facilitate or execute them, shall be punished by death.

If the person who sets the fire foresaw the death of a human being or his affliction with a permanent disability and accepted the risk, he shall be punished by hard labour for life.

The preceding provisions shall apply, under the same conditions, to any person who destroys or attempts to destroy, even partially, one of the things mentioned therein through the effect of an explosive substance.

Any person who, through his negligence, lack of caution, or failure to observe laws or regulations, causes the burning of a thing owned by a third party shall be punished by imprisonment for one year at most, and if the offence is trivial, the penalty shall not exceed three months.

Any person who removes an installed fire-extinguishing apparatus, changes its place, or renders it unfit for operation shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to two years.

Any person who is obliged by virtue of the law or regulations to possess a fire-extinguishing apparatus and neglects to install it in accordance with the rules, or fails to keep it fit for operation at all times, shall be punished by the same penalty in addition to a fine ranging between two hundred thousand and one million pounds.

Any person who intentionally causes sabotage to a public road or to one of the public installations, or intentionally inflicts damage thereon, shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to two years if his act gives rise to a danger to the safety of traffic or to public safety.

Any contractor, executor, agent, or supervisor of electricity, water, telephone, sewerage, or road restoration or repair works who leaves debris, materials, pits, gaps, or traces on the roads during the works or after their completion which would unjustifiably obstruct the freedom of traffic thereon or reduce their former width in a manner that makes traffic difficult and exposes public safety to danger shall be punished by imprisonment for up to one year at most.

The same punishment shall be imposed upon the public official or employee responsible for monitoring and supervising these works and their proper execution.

Furthermore, any person who carries out private or public works on public roads without holding a permit therefor from the competent authorities shall be punished by imprisonment for up to one year.

Any person who disables a railway line or movement or signalling apparatuses, or places an object that prevents traffic, or uses any means whatsoever to cause a collision between trains or their derailment from the line, shall be punished by temporary hard labour for a term of not less than five years.

Any person who smashes or disables signalling apparatuses, or uses false signals or any other special means with the intent of sinking a vessel or bringing down an aircraft, shall be punished by the same penalty, and if the act results in the sinking of a vessel or the fall of the aircraft, the penalty shall be ten years at least.

Any person who fails to observe the special regulations for combating epidemics, epizootics, plant diseases, locusts and other harmful animals shall be punished by imprisonment for up to six months and by a fine of up to two hundred thousand pounds.

The following shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to one year and by a fine from fifty thousand to six hundred thousand pounds, or by either of these two penalties:

1- Any person who adulterates substances intended for the food of human beings or animals, or drugs, beverages, or industrial, agricultural or natural products prepared for sale. 2 - Any person who displays any of the aforementioned products or substances, offers them for sale or sells them while knowing that they are adulterated or spoiled.

3- Any person who displays products capable of causing adulteration, offers them for sale or sells them while knowing the manner of their use.

4 - Any person who incites, by one of the means provided for in Article 209, paragraphs 2 and 3, the use of the products or substances mentioned in the third paragraph.

In the event of recidivism, the offender shall be prohibited from practising the occupation that served as the means for committing the offence.

If the adulterated or spoiled products or substances are harmful to the health of human beings or animals, imprisonment from three months to two years and a fine from one hundred thousand to one million pounds shall be imposed.

These penalties shall apply even if the seller or the buyer was aware of the harmful adulteration or spoilage.

Any persons who keep in their possession in any place whatsoever, without a legitimate cause, products or substances of the kind described in the preceding Article shall be punished by a fine ranging between twenty thousand and one hundred thousand pounds and by imprisonment for three months at most, or by either of these two penalties.

Imprisonment from three months to one year and a fine from fifty thousand to six hundred thousand pounds shall be imposed if one of the counterfeit or adulterated substances or products is harmful to the health of human beings or animals.

Any person who has resources, or is able to obtain resources through work, and solicits public charity for his own benefit in any place whatsoever, whether openly or under the guise of commercial activities, shall be punished by imprisonment with labour for a period of one month at least and six months at most, and may, in addition, be placed in a workhouse in accordance with Article 79, and this measure shall mandatorily be imposed in the event of recidivism.

Any person who, by reason of his idleness or his addiction to drunkenness or gambling, becomes compelled to solicit public assistance or charity from people shall be punished by imprisonment with labour from one month to six months, and the judge may, in addition, order that the convicted person be placed in a workhouse and be prohibited from frequenting taverns in which beverages are sold, as provided for in Articles 79 and 80.
Any foreigner convicted pursuant to the Articles contained in this Chapter may be ordered in the judgment to be expelled from the Lebanese territory.
Whoever is found in a state of manifest intoxication in a public place or a place open to the public shall be punished by a fine from six thousand pounds to twenty thousand pounds.

In the event of recidivism, the defendant shall be liable to summary detention and shall be prohibited from frequenting taverns on pain of the penalty prescribed in Article 80, and if he offends again a second time, he shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to six months and shall, in addition, be sentenced to deprivation of civil rights and forfeiture of paternal authority and guardianship.

If it is established that the defendant is a habitual drunkard, he shall be sentenced, even if a recidivist for the first time, to confinement in a special ward of the precautionary shelter in order to be treated therein. The period of confinement shall be six months at least, terminating by a decision of the judicial authority that ordered it establishing the recovery of the convicted person, and such period may not exceed two years, during which period of confinement the period of the penalty of deprivation of liberty shall run.
Whoever serves to a minor under eighteen years of age spirituous beverages until he intoxicates him shall be punished by a fine from six thousand to twenty thousand pounds.

The proprietor of a tavern or the proprietor of another establishment open to the public, and likewise his employees, shall be punished by summary detention and by a fine from ten thousand to twenty thousand pounds if they serve spirituous beverages to a person until they intoxicate him, or serve them to a person in a state of manifest intoxication or to a minor under eighteen years of age.
The proprietor of a tavern who employs in his tavern girls or women not of his family who are under twenty-one years of age shall be liable to the same penalties.
In the event of recidivism in respect of any of the misdemeanours provided for in Articles 626 and 627, the permanent closure of the establishment may be ordered.
Whosoever leaves a charitable institution that cares for him and practices begging shall be punished, even if he is incapacitated, with imprisonment for the duration mentioned above.

A beggar who solicits charity in one of the following circumstances:

1- By threat or acts of violence,

2- By carrying a false certificate of poverty,

3- By feigning wounds or infirmities,

4- By disguising himself in any form whatsoever,

5- By being accompanied by a child who is neither his child nor one of his descendants and who is under seven years of age,

6- By carrying weapons and instruments specific to committing felonies or misdemeanours,

7- In a state of assembly, unless it is a husband and his wife or an incapacitated person and his guide, shall be punished with imprisonment with labour from six months to two years in addition to his placement in a workhouse if he is not incapacitated, and with simple imprisonment for the same duration if he is incapacitated, and the measure of supervised liberty may also be imposed on him.

Every able-bodied person who has neither a dwelling nor a means of subsistence, who has not practiced work for at least one month and has not proven that he made sufficient effort to obtain employment, shall be deemed a vagrant and punished for that with imprisonment with labour from one month to six months, and vagrants may also be placed in a workhouse, and they shall mandatorily be placed therein in the event of recidivism.

The penalties and precautionary measures provided for in Article 613 shall be imposed on every vagrant who carries a weapon or instruments specific to committing felonies or misdemeanours, or who commit or threaten to commit any act of violence against persons, or who disguise themselves in any form whatsoever, or who engage in vagrancy in assembly, two persons or more.

The parents of a minor who has not completed fifteen years of age, or his relatives charged with supporting and raising him, shall be punished with imprisonment from one month to six months and with a fine from twenty thousand to one hundred thousand pounds if they fail to sustain him despite their ability to do so and leave him as a vagrant.

Whosoever drives a minor under eighteen years of age to begging shall be punished with imprisonment from six months to two years and with a fine ranging between the minimum wage and three times its amount.

Gypsies and Bedouins, whether Lebanese or foreigners, who roam in Lebanon without a fixed abode, even if they have resources and practice one of the crafts, shall be deemed nomads within the meaning intended in this subsection.

Every individual among the nomads who roams in Lebanese territory for at least one month and does not carry an identity card containing his bodily measurements or does not prove that he requested it from the authority shall be punished with imprisonment from three months to one year and with a fine from twenty thousand to two hundred thousand pounds, and he may also be placed under supervised liberty.

The penalties provided for in Articles 625 and 626 shall be doubled if the offender leaves the intoxicated person wandering in a state of intoxication or fails to secure his return to his home or his delivery to an officer of the public authority.

Games of chance are those in which luck prevails over skill or acumen; in particular, roulette, baccarat, faro, petits chevaux and open poker, as well as games branching therefrom or generally similar thereto, shall be deemed games of gambling.

Whoever takes charge of a gambling place or organises prohibited games of gambling, whether in a public place or a place open to the public or in a private house used for this purpose.

And the cashiers, their assistants, the managers, the workers and the employees.

Shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to two years and by a fine from two hundred thousand pounds to two million pounds.

The offenders shall be subject to prohibition of residence, and if they are aliens, they shall be subject to expulsion from Lebanese territory. In addition to the objects resulting from the offence or used or intended for its commission, the furniture and all other movable things with which the place is furnished and decorated shall be confiscated, and the closure of the premises may be ordered.
