Every person who participates in playing in the places mentioned above or is caught by surprise therein while playing shall be punished by a fine from fifty thousand to four hundred thousand pounds.

Theft is the taking of the movable property of another, clandestinely or by force, with the intent to appropriate it. Harnessed energies shall have the status of movable things in the application of criminal provisions.

Theft for which no special penalty is prescribed pursuant to one of the other provisions of this Law shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to three years and by a fine from one hundred thousand to four hundred thousand pounds.

This penalty shall be increased in accordance with Article 257 if the theft is committed in one of the following cases:

1- In places of worship and inhabited buildings.

2- By pickpocketing passers-by, whether on roads or in other public places, or on trains, ships, aircraft or other means of transport.

3- By the act of a public official entrusted with maintaining security or guarding, even if the theft is committed outside working hours.

4- By the act of a hired servant who steals the property of his master or steals the property of another from his master's house, or by the act of an employee or worker who steals from the premises or factory of his employer or in the warehouses or other places appurtenant to the work or factory.

5- By the act of two or more persons.

Whoever steals anything from the crops of the land or from the fruit of its trees, the value of which is less than one hundred pounds, shall be punished by a fine of up to one hundred thousand pounds. In this case, prosecution shall depend upon the complaint of the injured party.

Theft shall be punishable by hard labour from three years to ten years in any of the following cases:

1- If the theft is committed against the funds or assets of a government institution or any centre or office of an official administration or a public body.

2- If the theft is committed against the funds or assets of a bank or a jewellery or money-changing shop.

3- If the theft is committed against a collection agent or any public official or any employee of a private institution while carrying money belonging to the administration or institution in which he works, and the intent is to steal this money.

The same penalty shall be imposed on the collection agent, public official or employee if he colludes with the offenders.

4- If the theft is committed against a car or any motorized land vehicle.

5- By the act of a person who is masked or carrying an overt or concealed weapon.

6- If the theft is committed using violence against persons.

Whoever commits theft in any of the following cases shall be punished by hard labour from three years to seven years:

1 - By means of breaking and entering in closed places protected by walls, whether inhabited or uninhabited.

Or by scaling them inside or outside, or by using fabricated keys or any other tool, or after entering them by trickery, or by impersonating an official, or under the pretext of an official mission, or in any other unusual manner.

2 - During the occurrence of acts of riot, revolution, war, fire, security disturbance, shipwreck, or any other calamity.

3 - By threat with a weapon, whether to prepare for the offence, facilitate it, seize the stolen property, or secure escape.

If any of the acts mentioned in the preceding Article is accompanied by violence against persons, whether to prepare for the offence, facilitate it, seize the stolen property, or secure escape, or if any of the acts is committed at night, the penalty shall be increased to hard labour for life.

If the perpetrator kills a human being for a reason connected with the aforementioned theft, he shall be punished by death.

Shall be punished by temporary hard labour whosoever:

- Unlawfully and by any means whatsoever seizes a moored or sailing vessel or the goods it is carrying, or engages in any act of maritime fraud or piracy, or takes control of the vessel or directs its navigation, or compels its master or commander to alter its course by threat or violence.

- Unlawfully and by any means whatsoever seizes a fixed platform on the continental shelf or takes control thereof by threat or violence.

- Unlawfully and intentionally commits one of the following acts which is likely to endanger the safety of navigation of the vessel, the safety of maritime navigation, or the safety of the fixed platform on the continental shelf:

a- Destroying the vessel or causing severe damage to it or to its cargo.

b- Placing or causing another person to place a device or substance on a vessel or on a fixed platform by any means whatsoever where doing so is likely to expose the vessel or the fixed platform to destruction or to cause damage to the vessel, its cargo, or the fixed platform.

c- Causing severe damage to a port used for maritime navigation or to maritime navigation facilities, equipment, or services, or gravely obstructing the operation thereof.

d- Communicating information which he knows to be false.

The penalty shall be increased in accordance with Article 257 of the Penal Code in respect of the master of the vessel if he is the perpetrator of one of these offences or is a co-perpetrator, accomplice, or preparer thereof.

The master may also be sentenced to permanent prohibition from practising the profession, and such prohibition shall likewise be imposed upon all other perpetrators, co-perpetrators, accomplices, and instigators if their profession is connected with maritime navigation or maritime commerce.

Shall be punished byhard labour for life if any of the offences provided for in Article 641 as amended of the Penal Code is committed by the act of two or more armed persons who used a weapon or threatened to use it, or if the commission of the offence is accompanied by violence against any person.

And shall be punished by death if the commission of the offence leads to the sinking of the vessel and the death of one of its passengers, or leads to the destruction of the fixed platform and the death of one of those on board, and by temporary hard labour if the commission of the offence leads to the destruction of maritime navigation facilities, equipment, or services, or the death of any person as a result of terror or any other cause connected with the offence.

Any person shall be punished by temporary hard labour who:

-Unlawfully and by any means whatsoever seized an aircraft in flight or exercised control over it or controlled its piloting or compelled its commander to change its course by threat or by violence.

-Unlawfully and intentionally committed one of the following acts, if it is likely to endanger the safety of air navigation or the safety of the navigation of the aircraft:

A- Inflicting deliberate damage on an aircraft in service which renders it incapable of flight.

B- Inflicting severe deliberate damage on air navigation facilities, equipment or services, or inflicting severe deliberate damage on the facilities of an airport used for air navigation.

C- Communicating information which he knows to be false. He shall be punished by hard labour for life if any of the offences provided for in this Article is committed through the act of two or more armed persons who used a weapon or threatened to use it, or if the commission of the offence is accompanied by violence against one of the persons.

He shall be punished by death if the perpetrator, by any means whatsoever, carries out an act of sabotage in the aircraft which exposes it to the risk of crashing or destruction, or if the act results in the death of a human being as a result of terror or any other cause connected with the incident.

Shall be punished by imprisonment for at least one year and by a fine from one hundred thousand to six hundred thousand Lebanese pounds:

1- Any person who, by threat or by violence and with the intent of procuring an unlawful benefit for himself or for another, extorted a writing containing an undertaking or a discharge or extorted a signature thereon.

2- Any person who coerced a person into performing an act or refraining from performing it to the detriment of his wealth and the wealth of another.

3- The penalty of temporary hard labour shall be imposed in all the cases set out in the two preceding paragraphs if the perpetrator was carrying a weapon with which he threatened the victim.

Any person who threatened a person with exposing, disclosing or reporting a matter which is of a nature to impair the dignity or honour of that person or the dignity or honour of one of his relatives, in order to induce him to procure an unlawful benefit for himself or for another, shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years and by a fine of up to six hundred thousand pounds.

The penalty shall be increased in accordance with Article 257 of the Penal Code against the perpetrator if the matter which he threatens to expose came to his knowledge by virtue of his office, profession or art.

Any person who used without right a thing belonging to another in a manner that causes damage to him, without intending to misappropriate the thing, shall be punished by imprisonment of up to six months and by a fine from fifty thousand to two hundred thousand pounds, or by one of these two penalties.
Punishment shall extend to the attempt to commit the misdemeanours provided for in this Chapter.
Any person sentenced to a penalty of deprivation of liberty for theft or attempted theft may be placed under supervised liberty or barred from residence.

Any person who has committed the offence of concealing stolen goods or the offence of harbouring accomplices provided for in Articles 221 and 222 shall be exempted from penalty if he informs the authority of those accomplices before any prosecution, or enables the arrest, even after the commencement of prosecutions, of those whose hiding place he knows; the provisions of this Article shall not apply to recidivists.

Any person who induces another, by fraudulent manoeuvres, to hand over to him movable or immovable property, or instruments containing an undertaking, a discharge or a benefit, and takes possession thereof, shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years and by a fine from one hundred thousand to one million pounds.

The following shall be deemed fraudulent manoeuvres:

1- Acts calculated to deceive the victim into believing in the existence of a fictitious enterprise, or which create in his mind the hope of a profit or the fear of a harm.

2- Fabricating a falsehood which the victim believes as a result of the corroboration of a third party, even in good faith, or as a result of a circumstance prepared by the offender or a circumstance of which he took advantage.

3- Disposing of movable or immovable property by a person who has no right or capacity to dispose thereof, or by a person who has a right or capacity to dispose thereof and abuses his right as a means of extorting money.

4- Using a false name or a false capacity to deceive and influence. The same punishment shall apply to an attempt to commit this offence.

Article 656: The penalty shall be doubled if the offence is committed in any of the following cases:

1- On the pretext of securing an office or employment in a public administration,

2- By the act of a person soliciting money from the public for the issue of shares, bonds or other documents for a company or an enterprise.

3- By the act of any authorized signatory for a company, association, institution or any other legal person.

Any person who exploits the needs, inexperience or passions of a minor under eighteen years of age, or of an imbecile or a mentally defective person, and thereby induces him to perform a legal act prejudicial to his interests or the interests of others, shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years and by a fine equivalent to the value of the damage, not being less than fifty thousand pounds.

Any person who induces another to hand over to him goods with an option or on promise while intending not to pay their price, or knowing that he is unable to pay, shall be punished by imprisonment for up to six months and by a fine of up to two hundred thousand pounds if he does not return them or pay their price after being served with notice.

Any person who procures for himself lodging, food or drink in a public place intending not to pay or knowing that he is unable to pay, shall be punished by petty detention and by a fine from twenty thousand to one hundred thousand pounds.
The same penalty shall be imposed on any person who fraudulently takes a means of land, sea or air transport without paying the fare
Any financial contract, for a non-commercial purpose, that imposes on the borrower an overt or covert total interest, at a rate exceeding 12 per cent per annum constitutes a loan of usury.

Any person who practices usury upon a person to exploit his straitened circumstances shall be punished by a fine which may reach half of the lent capital and by imprisonment not exceeding one year or by either of these two penalties.

Any person who practices usury in less than three years twice or more upon a single debtor or different debtors, shall be punished for the offence of habitual usury by the penalties prescribed in the preceding Article.

- The instigator or accomplice in this offence shall be punished, upon repeating his act at least twice within three years whether in connection with a loan of usury concluded between the same usurer and victim or between other persons.
The offence of habitual usury shall be inferred from a single loan with usury if committed in less than five years after conviction of one of the misdemeanours provided for in the preceding Articles.

Shall be punished by imprisonment up to six months and by a fine which may reach one quarter of the lent capital:

1- Any person who opens an establishment for lending against a pledge without permission even if he concludes a single contract.

2- Any person who obtains permission for lending against a pledge and fails to keep a ledger containing the value of the lent sums, the name and capacity of the borrower, and the nature and true value of the pledged property.

The provisions of this Article shall not apply to loans against a pledge concluded for the benefit of merchants in order to facilitate commercial operations.

Whoever draws a cheque without prior and available provision for payment or with insufficient provision.

- Whoever withdraws all or part of the provision after drawing the cheque.

- Whoever issues a stop payment order to the drawee in cases other than those provided for in Article 428 of the Code of Commerce.

Shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to three years and by a fine from one million pounds to four million pounds, and shall be ordered to pay the value of the cheque in addition to damages, if need be.

In the event of recidivism, the provisions of Articles 66 and 68 shall also apply in addition to the penalties for recidivism.

The waiver of civil rights in the aforementioned offences shall result in the abatement of the public prosecution.

The characterisation of an infamous offence used in other laws in force shall not apply to these offences, and none of the consequences specified in those laws that attach to a person convicted of an infamous offence shall attach to a person convicted of any of them.

Whoever knowingly receives a cheque without provision shall be punished by the penalties for complicity in the offence specified above. These penalties shall be doubled if the holder of the cheque obtained it to cover a usurious loan, even if he was not an accomplice.

With the exception of the case of obtaining a cheque to cover a usurious loan, the waiver of civil rights shall result in the abatement of the public prosecution.

Whoever procures or secures a promise of any benefit for himself or for another by fabricating news or concocting lies to induce a person to travel or to direct a traveller to a country other than the country to which he intended to go shall be sentenced to the penalty provided for in Article 655.

The same punishment shall apply to an attempt to commit this offence.
The publication of the judgment may be ordered when convicting of one of the misdemeanours provided for in Articles 656 and 664 upon the recidivism of any of the offences specified in this Chapter.

Whoever intentionally conceals, embezzles, dissipates, destroys or tears up an instrument containing an undertaking or a discharge, or any other movable thing delivered to him by way of deposit, agency, lease, loan for use or pledge, or for the performance of work with or without remuneration, on condition that he return it, present it, or use it for a specified purpose, shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years and by a fine ranging between one quarter and one half of the value of the restitution and damages, provided that it is not less than fifty thousand pounds.

Whoever disposes of a sum of money or of other fungible things delivered to him for a specific work, while knowing or when he ought to have known that he cannot return the like thereof, and does not discharge his liability despite formal notice, shall be punished by imprisonment for up to one year and by a fine of up to one quarter of the value of the restitutions and damages, provided that the fine shall not be less than fifty thousand pounds.

The persons mentioned hereinafter shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to three years when they commit breach of trust with respect to property delivered to them or entrusted to their charge in accordance with the text of either of the two preceding Articles 670 and 671:

1- The administrator of an endowment (waqf).

2- The director of a charitable institution or association and every person responsible for its property.

3- The guardian of a minor or of an legally incapacitated person, or his representative.

4- The executor of a will or of a marriage contract.

5- Every lawyer, notary public, or authorised business agent.

6- Every salaried employee or servant and every person bound by a contract of employment for remuneration with any private institution.

7- Every person deputised by the authority to administer or guard property belonging to the State or to individuals.

And the offender may be barred from practising the work by reason of which the offence was committed.

Whoever appropriates, embezzles, refuses to return, or conceals found property or any movable thing that came into his possession by error, fortuitously, or by force majeure, shall be punished by imprisonment for up to one year and by a fine of up to one quarter of the value of the restitutions and damages, provided that the fine shall not be less than twenty thousand pounds.

The provisions of this Article shall apply to whoever finds a treasure with respect to the share belonging to another.

The perpetrators of the offences provided for in the preceding chapters shall be exempted from punishment if they commit them to the prejudice of ascendants, descendants, the adoptive father, mother, or son, or a spouse not legally separated from his spouse.

If the offender repeats his offence within five years, he shall be sentenced, upon the complaint of the injured party, to the penalty provided for in the law reduced by one third.

Shall not be prosecuted except upon the complaint of the injured party - unless he is unknown, or the complaint is withdrawn,

- the misdemeanours provided for in Articles 4/6, 650, 651, 658, 660, 671, and 673.

The breach of trust punishable under Articles 670 and 671 shall be prosecuted ex officio if it is accompanied by one of the aggravating circumstances provided for in Article 672.

The misdemeanour penalties prescribed in the articles comprising the First, Second and Third Chapters shall be reduced by half if the damage resulting therefrom or the benefit which the perpetrator intended to derive therefrom is trivial, or if the damage has been wholly removed prior to the referral of the action to the court; however, if restitution is made or the damage is removed during the action, but prior to any judgment on the merits, even if not final, the penalty shall be reduced by one quarter.

Whoever uses or possesses in his warehouse, shop, sales carts, or other places prepared for trade, legal measuring instruments that do not conform to the laws and regulations governing measurement, shall be punished by disciplinary detention and by a fine from twenty million to thirty million pounds, or by one of these two penalties.

Whoever sells or places on the markets legal measuring instruments contrary to any of the conditions and provisions of the supervision system provided for in the Law on the Measurement System in Lebanon shall be punished by the same penalties.

Whoever sells, places on the markets, or possesses in the places mentioned above, measuring instruments, weights, dry measures, or weighing or measuring apparatus that are falsified or inaccurate, shall be punished by imprisonment for three months at most and by a fine from thirty million to fifty million pounds.

Whoever sells, places on the markets, or, by knowingly using measuring instruments, weights, dry measures, or weighing or measuring apparatus that are falsified or inaccurate, deceives the contracting party as to the quantity of the thing delivered, shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to two years and by a fine from fifty million to seventy-five million pounds.

Any other deception, whether as to the quantity of the thing delivered or as to its identity, where such identity is the motivating cause for the transaction, shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to one year and by a fine from fifty million to seventy-five million pounds, or by one of these two penalties.

There shall be confiscated, in accordance with the provisions of Article 98, weights, dry measures, and weighing and measuring apparatus that are falsified or that differ from the weights and dry measures prescribed by law.

Whoever deceives the contracting party, whether as to the nature of the goods, their essential qualities, their composition, or the quantity of useful elements that they contain, or as to their kind or origin when the designation of the kind and origin is considered, under the agreement or customs, the principal cause for the sale,

shall be punished by imprisonment with labour from one month to one year and by a fine from forty thousand to five hundred thousand pounds, or by one of these two penalties.

The penalty of imprisonment shall be increased to two years if the offence is committed:

Either through artifices or means aimed at corrupting the operations of analysis, composition and measurement, or at altering with intent to defraud the composition, weight or volume of the goods even prior to carrying out such operations,

Or through falsified statements aimed at persuading of the existence of a valid prior operation.

Anyone who, during a public auction, obstructs the freedom of bidding or of tenders by threat, violence or lies, or excludes bidders and tenderers by gifts or promises, shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to six months and by a fine from one hundred thousand to one million pounds.

Shall be punished by imprisonment with labour from six months to two years and by a fine from one million to six million pounds anyone who, through fraud, succeeds in raising or lowering the prices of goods or public or private commercial shares traded on the stock exchange, in particular by announcing different facts or false allegations, or by submitting offers of sale or purchase with the intent to disturb prices.

Or by undertaking any act calculated to corrupt the rule of supply and demand in the market.

The penalty shall be doubled if the rise or fall of prices takes place,

1- In respect of grains, flour, sugar, oil, meat or carcasses or other foodstuffs,

2- Or in respect of materials falling outside the profession of the offender,

3- Or by a group composed of three or more persons,
Punishment shall extend to the attempt to commit the offences provided for in Articles 680 et seq.

Upon convicting a recidivist of one of the offences mentioned in this Chapter, the court shall order the posting or publication of the judgment, and recidivism shall furthermore entail deprivation from practising the profession or trade even if the practice thereof does not depend on obtaining a certificate or an authorisation from the authority, and posting and publication may be ordered even if the perpetrator is convicted for the first time where the gravity of the act so requires.

Shall be deemed a fraudulent bankrupt and punished by temporary hard labour up to seven years every bankrupt merchant who conceals his books, or embezzles or dissipates part of his property, or collusively acknowledges debts not due by him, whether in books, official or private instruments, or in his balance sheet.

Every trader who has ceased payments shall be deemed a negligent bankrupt and shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year.

1- If he has consumed excessive sums in fictitious operations on goods or on the stock exchange.

2- If, after the cessation of payments and in order to delay bankruptcy, he has purchased goods to sell them for less than their price or has contracted, for the same purpose, loans, or circulated negotiable instruments, or resorted to other ruinous means to obtain funds.

3- If, after the cessation of payments, he has paid a creditor to the detriment of the body of creditors.

4- If his personal expenses or the expenses of his household are found to be excessive.

Every bankrupt trader may be deemed a negligent bankrupt and punished by the imprisonment prescribed above,

1- If he has contracted, for the benefit of third parties and without consideration, commitments that are excessive in relation to his situation when he undertook them,

2- If he has not complied with the rules relating to the organisation of the Commercial Register,

3- If he has not submitted, within twenty days of his cessation of payments, the required declaration pursuant to the Code of Commerce to the registry of the court, or if this declaration does not contain the names of all the joint and several partners,

4- If he has not kept commercial books or has not drawn up the inventory accurately, or if his books or his inventory are incomplete or irregular or do not show the true state of his assets and liabilities, without there being fraud nevertheless,

5- If he has been declared bankrupt again and has not fulfilled the conditions of a previous composition agreement.

Upon the bankruptcy of a commercial company, there shall incur the penalty provided for in Article 689, besides the partners in general partnerships and the general partners in limited partnerships:

1- Silent partners who have habitually intervened in the business of the company.

2- Managers of partnerships limited by shares and of limited liability companies.

3- Managers, members of the board of directors, authorised agents, members of supervisory boards, auditors, and employees of the aforementioned companies and of joint-stock companies, if they have themselves committed an act of fraudulent bankruptcy or have intentionally facilitated or enabled the commission thereof, or if they have published untrue statements or balance sheets or distributed fictitious dividends.

If a commercial company becomes bankrupt, any of the persons mentioned above who, in the management of the company or in working for its benefit, has committed one of the offences provided for in Article 690, paragraphs one, two and three thereof, shall be punished by the penalty for negligent bankruptcy,

And such person may incur the same penalty if, in the management of the company or in working for its benefit, he has committed one of the offences mentioned in Article 691, paragraphs one to four thereof.

A commercial company shall be subject, in the cases specified in Articles 692 and 693, to the penalties and precautionary measures provided for by Articles 210 and 211, with the exception of the fine.

The penalty for fraudulent bankruptcy shall be incurred by,

1 Whoever commits, for the benefit of the bankrupt, the embezzlement, concealment or withholding of all or part of his immovable or movable property,

2- Whoever fraudulently comes forward in his own name or under a fictitious name to prove fictitious debts in the bankruptcy estate,

3- Whoever commits, while engaging in trade under a fictitious name, the crime of fraudulent bankruptcy,

This is regardless of the liability arising from acts of instigation or accessory intervention.

A creditor who stipulates for himself, whether with the bankrupt or with any other person, a special benefit by reason of his participation in the vote of the body of creditors, or who concludes a private agreement to draw a benefit in his own interest from the property of the bankrupt,

shall be punished by imprisonment with labour from one month to one year and by a fine not exceeding six hundred thousand pounds, and the penalty of imprisonment may be increased to two years if the creditor is the trustee of the bankruptcy estate.

The spouse of the bankrupt, his descendants, his ascendants, and his relatives by marriage of the same degrees who embezzle, steal or conceal instruments belonging to the bankruptcy estate without acting in concert with the bankrupt or intervening as accessories with him shall be punished by the penalty for theft provided for in Article 648.

The posting and publication of the decision may be ordered for one of the crimes provided for in this Chapter; whoever is sentenced for fraudulent bankruptcy and whoever is sentenced as a repeat offender for negligent bankruptcy shall be subject to temporary or permanent prohibition from engaging in trade or performing in a company one of the functions specified in the second and third paragraphs of Article 692.

A debtor who, with the intent of defeating the rights of creditors or preventing execution against his movable or immovable property, proceeds to diminish his property in any manner whatsoever, and in particular, by signing fictitious instruments or by falsely acknowledging the existence of an obligation or the fulfilment of all or part thereof, or by withholding or smuggling part of his property, or by selling, destroying or designating part of his property, shall be punished by imprisonment with labour from one month to six months and by a fine from fifty thousand to six hundred thousand pounds.

Article 700: in Articles 210 and 211, regardless of the penalties incurred, in accordance with the provisions of Article 692, by those mentioned therein among the persons who contribute to the act or facilitate or enable its commission intentionally on their part.

Names written in a form that distinguishes them from others, designations, emblems, seals, stamps, letters, marks, reliefs, vignettes, numerals, and in general any sign aimed, in the interest of the consumer and the factory owner or merchant, at showing the nature of any goods and their origin or the nature of an industrial, commercial or agricultural product, or the products of forests and mines, shall be deemed industrial or commercial trademarks within the meaning intended in this subsection, provided these marks are registered and published in accordance with the laws in force.

Whoever knowingly proceeds:

To counterfeit a trademark belonging to another, even if he adds thereto other words such as "imitation", "similar", "class", "kind" or "recipe". Or to affix a mark belonging to another or a counterfeited mark onto his products or commercial goods. Or to sell or offer for sale a product bearing an usurped or counterfeited mark.

If his act is of such a nature as to deceive the buyer, he shall be punished by a fine from one hundred thousand to one million pounds and by imprisonment with labour from three months to three years, or by one of these two penalties.

Whoever makes a mark resemble another with intent to defraud, without counterfeiting it, and whoever uses such a mark or sells or offers for sale a product onto which he has affixed it, if his act is of such a nature as to deceive the buyer, shall be punished by a fine from one hundred thousand to five hundred thousand pounds and by imprisonment with labour from two months to two years, or by one of these two penalties.

Persons who sell or offer for sale or who use a counterfeited mark, or one made to resemble another with intent to defraud, may alone plead ignorance of the registration of the mark if they did not commit the act in concert with the person who counterfeited it or made it resemble another.

The penalty provided for in Article 703 shall be imposed on whoever depicts on the mark national or foreign decorations or words, images, marks or emblems that are seditious or contrary to public order or morals.

The judge may order the confiscation of the mark pursuant to Article ninety-eight even if the prosecution does not result in a conviction.

The same penalty shall be imposed on whoever fails to affix to his products the trademark that must be affixed pursuant to the law and regulations, or whoever sells or offers for sale a product that does not bear the trademark that must be affixed thereto, and the court shall order the affixing of the said mark in implementation of the provisions of Article 130.

Whoever knowingly inflicts damage upon registered and duly published industrial drawings and models guaranteed by the laws in force shall be punished by a fine from fifty thousand to five hundred thousand pounds.

The fine provided for in the preceding Article shall be imposed upon anyone who uses an industrial or commercial award without specifying precisely the name of the exhibition or the authority that granted it and the full date on which it was given, and upon anyone who uses a commercial or industrial award that he obtained in his capacity as an assistant without specifying the name of the establishment that employed him.
The courts shall assess counterfeiting and imitation by viewing them from the standpoint of the consumer or purchaser, and by considering the overall similarity rather than partial differences.

Deprivation of the rights specified in the third and fourth paragraphs of Article 65, as well as the publication and posting of the judgment in accordance with the provisions of Articles 67 and 68, shall be imposed where a conviction is pronounced for one of the misdemeanours mentioned in this Chapter. In the event of recidivism, the offender may be barred from practising the trade or industry during the practice of which the offence was committed.

Anyone who intentionally demolishes or destroys buildings, monuments, statues or other structures intended for the benefit of the public or for public ornamentation shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years and by a fine from one hundred thousand to six hundred thousand pounds.

The same penalty shall be incurred by anyone who intentionally proceeds to demolish or destroy a monument or any movable or immovable thing of historical value, or a registered statue or natural site, whether owned by him or by another.

Anyone who intentionally proceeds to demolish any building in whole or in part, knowing that it belongs to another, shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to two years and by a fine from fifty thousand to four hundred thousand pounds, and if the demolition occurs, even partially, to huts, unplastered walls, or walls built of rubble stone without mortar, the penalty shall be imprisonment from one month to six months and a fine from twenty thousand to one hundred thousand pounds.

Anyone who intentionally demolishes or destroys a thing belonging to another which is not specified in this Title shall be punished by a fine not exceeding the value of the damage, provided that it is not less than twenty thousand pounds, and if the value of the destroyed thing or the resulting damage exceeds twenty thousand pounds, the perpetrator may, in addition to the fine, be imprisoned for a term not exceeding six months.
If one of the misdemeanours mentioned in this Subdivision leads to the killing or wounding of a person, the offender shall be punished for this act, subject to the provisions of Articles 189 and 191

If the offender is an assistant of, or has in the past assisted in any capacity whatsoever, the injured person, he shall be punished, in addition to the fine, by imprisonment with labour from two months to six months.
Any person who proves his ignorance of the registration shall be exempted from the penalty.

If the trademark, patent of invention, or industrial designs and models duly registered had not been published at the time of the commission of the act, the perpetrator shall incur the penalty if it is proved that he came to know or was aware of the registration.

Any person who, by fraudulent means, false claims, or insinuation in bad faith, diverts the clientele of another to himself shall be punished, upon the complaint of the injured party, by a fine from one hundred thousand to five hundred thousand pounds. The penalty shall extend to the attempt to commit this offence.

The following shall be designated as a trade name:

1- Every name of a merchant, manufacturer, farmer or operator, provided it has not become the necessary and sole designation of the product.

2- Every business style that does not have a patronymic character.

3- The pseudonym assumed by the merchant, manufacturer, farmer or operator.

4- The distinctive name adopted by a group of persons among those mentioned above, even if such group does not constitute a body with a legal entity.

Any person who usurps the trade name of another shall incur the penalty provided for in Article 702:

Either by affixing or displaying it in any form whatsoever on natural or manufactured products or their accessories, or on wrappers or labels.

Or by circulating circulars, advertisements, invoices, letters or the like. These provisions shall apply even if the usurped name is altered, even slightly, or coupled with a surname other than that of its owner, or with any other expression that retains the distinctive letters of the name and induces confusion.

The penalty shall extend to the attempt to commit this offence.
Bad faith in the usurpation of a trade name shall be presumed until the contrary is proved.

Shall be punished by a fine from twenty thousand to five hundred thousand pounds and by imprisonment from three months to two years, or by one of these two penalties, provided that the fine shall not be less than one hundred thousand pounds if a custodial penalty is not imposed:

Any person who fraudulently attributes to himself industrial or commercial awards, whether real or fictitious, and uses them publicly by affixing them on trade labels and on wrappers of goods or commercial papers, or by inscribing them on signboards.

And any person who attempts to make the public believe that he holds commercial or industrial awards.

Whoever intentionally, without necessity, kills a draught, pack or riding animal, or livestock of various kinds belonging to another, shall be punished: by summary detention if the offence takes place on land, or in stables, pens or buildings and their appurtenances owned, leased or possessed in any capacity whatsoever by the perpetrator; by imprisonment for up to six months if the offence takes place in a location owned, leased or possessed in any capacity whatsoever by the owner of the animal; and by imprisonment from fifteen days to two months if the offence is committed in any other place. If one of the animals mentioned above is killed by poisoning, the penalty shall in every case be imprisonment from three months to two years.

Whoever intentionally destroys, breaks or disables agricultural implements shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to six months and by a fine from twenty thousand to one hundred thousand pounds.

If an armed band of no fewer than five persons plunders any of the properties described above or destroys them by force and violence, each of the perpetrators shall be punished by temporary hard labour and by a fine from fifty thousand to four hundred thousand pounds.

Whoever proceeds, even partially, to fill in a ditch, or demolish a wall irrespective of the materials of which it is built, or cut down or uproot a hedge whether green or dry, and whoever demolishes, destroys or removes any mark indicating the boundaries between different properties, shall be punished by imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months; the same penalty shall be imposed on anyone who demolishes, destroys or removes cadastral boundary stones, reference marks, demarcation monuments or land levelling marks.

If the aforementioned offence is committed in order to facilitate the usurpation of land, or by means of threat or coercion exercised against persons, the perpetrator shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to one year, in addition to a fine from fifty thousand to four hundred thousand pounds.

Whoever does not hold an official title of ownership or of disposal and takes possession of an immovable property or part of an immovable property in the possession of another shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year and by a fine from two hundred thousand to one million pounds. The penalty shall be increased in accordance with Article 257 in each of the following two cases:

1- If the act is accompanied by threat or violence against persons or things.

2- If the usurpation occurs upon all or part of public roads, State property, or communal property.

Whoever takes possession, without lawful justification, of an immovable property or part of an immovable property, for the purpose of residence, occupation, exploitation, or use for any other other purpose, shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year and by a fine from two hundred thousand to one million pounds. The penalty shall be increased in accordance with Article 257 in each of the following cases:

1- If the act is accompanied by threat or violence against persons or things.

2- If the taking of possession occurs upon a building occupied by one of the State administrations, one of the administrative bodies, or one of the public institutions or institutions of public utility.

3- If the perpetrator fails to leave and vacate the immovable property within a period of one week from the date of being notified of a written warning, or if he continues to hold possession thereof for a period exceeding two months.

Whoever cuts down, snaps or destroys standing crops, or trees or shrubs grown by nature or planted by the hand of man, or other plantings, knowing that they belong to another, shall be punished by imprisonment for up to three months.

If the destruction occurs upon grafts, fruit-bearing trees or their offshoots, or upon any other tree that is valuable from an agricultural, commercial or industrial standpoint, the perpetrator shall be punished by a fine from forty thousand to six hundred thousand pounds and by imprisonment from ten days to one month for each graft, tree or offshoot, provided that the total penalty does not exceed three years.
If the offence is limited to pruning the grafts, trees or offshoots, the penalty prescribed in the preceding Article shall be reduced by half.

Any person shall be punished by imprisonment for up to six months and by a fine from one hundred thousand to one million pounds, or by either of these two penalties:

1- Who floods public roads or the property of others by raising his water outlet above the level fixed pursuant to the regulations or by committing any other fault,

2- Who obstructs the public road without necessity or permission from the authority by placing or leaving thereon anything that prevents or narrows the freedom and safety of passage,

3- Who neglects to give warning by day and lighting by night in front of excavations and other works which he is permitted to carry out, or in front of other materials and other things which he is permitted to place in squares and on public roads,

4- Who extinguishes, removes or damages lamps or lanterns used for lighting the public road,

5- Who throws or places filth, sweepings or any other thing on the public road,

6- Who inadvertently throws or drops filth or other harmful things onto any person,

7- Who places advertisements on historical monuments, public buildings, cemeteries and buildings intended for worship. The advertisements or materials obstructing the road shall be removed at the expense of the perpetrator or by him.

Any person shall incur the penalty mentioned in the preceding Article who, in inhabited places, proceeds:

1- To make draught, pack and riding animals and other livestock run, or to let them loose,

2- To fire fireworks in a manner likely to cause danger to persons or things. The seized weapons and fireworks shall be confiscated. In the case provided for in the second paragraph, the penalty of petty detention may be imposed.

Directors of theatres and cinemas and their employees who admit, at the showing of a play or film of a kind prohibited to children, a child or an adolescent, whether male or female, or a girl who has not attained eighteen years of age unaccompanied by her father, her mother, her guardian or one of her adult close relatives, shall be punished by imprisonment for up to three months at most and by a fine from forty thousand to four hundred thousand pounds, or by either of these two penalties.

In the event of recidivism, the closure of the delimited place may be ordered for a period ranging between three days and three months.

Any person who demolishes, overturns or destroys all or part of the structures erected for the use of public waters or for their preservation or for the purpose of protection against the flooding of such waters, and in particular bridges, dams, crossings, irrigation, drainage or discharge canals, and exposed or buried water pipes, whether a concession has been granted in respect of the waters or not, shall be punishable by imprisonment for up to two years and by a fine of up to five hundred thousand pounds.

- The same penalty shall be imposed on any person who proceeds to encroach in any manner whatsoever upon the water sources of irrigation projects established by the State or by public administrations or bodies with the aim of affecting the quantity and flow of public waters, and upon irrigation canals, the boundaries of their passages and their easement area, or upon all structures of the project erected for public utility, as well as on any person who plants or cultivates these places or carries out excavation therein or builds thereon, and a ruling shall be passed to restore the state of affairs to what it was at the benefit of the offender.

The same penalty shall be imposed on any person who:

1- Discharges into public waters, whether a concession has been granted in respect thereof or not, or pours or throws therein liquids or substances harmful to public health or comfort or preventing the proper use of such waters.

2- Throws animal manure or places filth in lands falling within the perimeter defined by the authority for the protection of a spring used by the public,

3- Performs any act liable to pollute a spring or waters from which others drink.

Any person who intentionally proceeds to pollute a spring or water from which others drink shall be punishable by imprisonment from one year to three years and by a fine from fifty thousand to six hundred thousand pounds.

Any person who proceeds to commit any of the following shall be punishable by imprisonment for up to six months and by a fine from one hundred thousand to one million pounds, or by either of these two penalties:

1- Destroying public squares and roads or designating them,

2- Removing plates and numbers placed at street corners or on buildings, kilometric signs and milestones, or destroying them or designating them.

Any person who, without permission, proceeds to do any of the following shall be punished by imprisonment for up to one year and by a fine of up to five hundred thousand pounds, or by either of these two penalties:

1- Carrying out works of prospecting for underground or artesian waters or impounding them, unless the purpose is to dig non-artesian wells on private properties whose depth does not exceed one hundred and fifty metres.

2- Carrying out excavations at a distance from the edge of the banks of watercourses, aqueducts, and irrigation, drying, and drainage canals that is less than the depth of such excavations, and in any case less than three metres.

3- Removing stones, earth, sand, trees, shrubs, or plants from those banks, or from the beds of temporary or permanent watercourses, or from lakes, marshes, ponds, and pools.

4 Planting, sowing, or placing anything whatsoever on the banks of lakes, marshes, ponds, and pools, or on the banks of temporary or permanent watercourses or in their beds, or between the boundaries of the rights of way of irrigation, drying, and drainage canals, or of water pipes and aqueducts declared to be established for the utility .

5- Encroaching in any manner whatsoever upon the banks of springs, temporary or permanent watercourses, marshes, lakes, ponds, and pools, or upon the boundaries of the rights of way of irrigation, drying, and drainage canals, or of aqueducts or water pipes declared to be established for the public utility.

6- Preventing the free flow of public waters and cutting off drinking water from the beneficiaries thereof ..

7- Carrying out any permanent or temporary work capable of affecting the quantity and flow of public waters.

"and by a fine of up to five hundred thousand pounds" instead of "and by a fine of up to two thousand five hundred pounds".
Any person who, without permission, proceeds to clean, deepen, straighten, or regulate temporary or permanent watercourses shall be punished by the fine provided for in the preceding Article.

Whoever practises, for the purpose of profit, spiritualism, hypnosis, astrology, palmistry, card reading and everything related to the occult shall be punished by petty detention and by a fine from ten thousand to twenty thousand pounds, and the attire and implements used shall be confiscated. A recidivist shall be punished by imprisonment for up to six months and by a fine of up to two hundred thousand pounds, and he may be deported if he is a foreigner.

The following shall be punished by a fine from ten thousand to twenty thousand pounds:

1- Whoever neglects or refuses to obey the orders of the administrative authority to repair or demolish dilapidated buildings,

2- Every person, whether a person of the art or not, who abstains or delays without excuse from rendering relief or performing any work or service requested of him by the agents of authority upon the occurrence of an accident, drowning, flood, fire or any other calamity, or in case of brigandage, pillage, a flagrant offence, a call for help, or during the execution of judicial judgments,

In the case provided for in the first paragraph, the penalty of petty detention may be imposed.

Whoever contravenes the administrative or municipal regulations issued in accordance with the law shall be punished by imprisonment for up to three months, by a fine from one hundred thousand to six hundred thousand pounds, or by either of these two penalties.

Date of publication and entry into force of this Law

This Law shall be published immediately in the Official Gazette and shall be put into force on the first of October of the year 1944.

- The Ottoman Penal Code is repealed

- As well as the Law issued on 23 January 1946

- As well as Article 173 of the Penal Code

- And all other legislative texts contrary to the provisions of this Law.

Whoever offers on a public highway, without a licence, a lottery or any other game of chance shall be punished by imprisonment for up to three months at most and by a fine from forty thousand to four hundred thousand pounds, or by either of these two penalties, and the objects used to commit the act or prepared for its commission shall be confiscated.
Any animal living in the custody of the person who acquired and raised it shall be deemed domestic within the meaning intended in this subsection.
Every person who without cause proceeds to ill-treat or overwork a domestic animal shall be punished by disciplinary detention and by a fine from ten thousand to twenty thousand pounds.
Whoever publicly and without cause ill-treats a non-domestic animal shall be punished by the fine provided for above.

Whoever extracts from State property, without permission, grass, earth, stones or other materials shall be punished by disciplinary detention and by a fine from six thousand to twenty thousand pounds.

The following shall be punished by a fine from two thousand to twenty thousand pounds:

1- Whoever proceeds to enter the enclosed or cultivated land of another, or land containing crops, without having a right of way.

2- Whoever grazes or turns loose livestock or other draught, pack or riding animals on what belongs to another

- of land that is enclosed, planted with fruit-bearing trees, cultivated, or containing crops,

- and, in general, anyone who brings onto land that does not belong to him, or over which he has no right of way or right of pasture, animals capable of causing damage thereto.

3- Whoever through his fault causes the death, wounding or injury of another's animals.

Whoever proceeds to sell goods or demand a fee in excess of the price fixed in the tariff published in accordance with the law shall be punished by disciplinary detention and by a fine from ten thousand to twenty thousand pounds, unless the law has prescribed a severer penalty against him.
Whoever refuses to accept national currency at the value fixed therefor shall be punished by a fine from one thousand pounds to ten thousand pounds.

Any owner of a hotel, inn, or furnished house intended for rent who neglects to duly keep a register in which he records sequentially and without blank spaces the name of every person who slept or spent the night in his lodging, together with his occupation, place and date of birth, and the date of his entry and departure, and any person who fails to produce this register upon every request from the competent authority, shall be punished by imprisonment for up to three months at most and by a fine from forty thousand to four hundred thousand pounds, or by one of these two penalties.

Imprisonment for up to three months at most and a fine from 200 to 2000 pounds, or one of these two penalties, shall be imposed upon persons having the capacity referred to in the preceding Article, and managers of theatres, cinemas, and other public premises who do not attend to the cleaning of their premises.

Any person who neglects to maintain hearths and chimneys of ovens, factories, and other premises in which fire is used, or neglects to clean and repair them, shall be punished by imprisonment for up to three months at most and by a fine from forty thousand to four hundred thousand pounds, or by one of these two penalties.

Any person who bathes in view of passers-by in a posture contrary to decency, and any person who appears in a public place or a place open to the public in such a posture, shall be punished by imprisonment for up to three months at most and by a fine from forty thousand to four hundred thousand pounds, or by one of these two penalties.

The following shall be punished by imprisonment for up to three months at most and by a fine from forty thousand to four hundred thousand pounds, or by one of these two penalties:

1- Any person who causes noise or clamour in a manner that deprives the inhabitants of their peace, as well as any person who incites or participates in this act,

2- Any person who intentionally throws stones or similar solid objects or filth at vehicles, buildings, the dwellings or walls of others, gardens, and enclosures.

3- Any person who lets loose a harmful animal or releases an insane person who were in his custody.

4- Any person who urges on his dog when it attacks or pursues passers-by, or who fails to restrain it therefrom, even if no harm or damage is caused.

Any person who prints, sells, or offers for sale engravings, pictures, or drawings that give an untrue impression of the Lebanese which is likely to detract from their dignity and esteem shall be punished by imprisonment for up to three months at most and by a fine from forty thousand to four hundred thousand pounds, or by one of these two penalties, and those engravings, pictures, and drawings shall be confiscated.

A municipality is an administration of a public character and a moral personality enjoying administrative and financial autonomy, and it may expropriate, purchase, accept donations, sell, enter into contracts, and litigate before the courts, in accordance with the provisions of this Law and within the scope of the laws in force.

The draft Municipalities Law as amended by the Administration and Justice Committee is hereby approved, while retaining the amendments introduced by the Chamber of Deputies to the articles it examined, with the deletion of every expression relating to appointment; whereas Articles 114 and 115 appearing in the amendment of the Administration and Justice Committee shall remain as they appeared in Articles 115 and 116 in the Government's draft, and this Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication.

Municipalities shall be established, and their territorial jurisdiction and the prescribed number of their members shall be determined in accordance with the provisions of this Law, by a decision of the Minister of the Interior upon the proposal of the Governor (Muhafiz), and they shall be annexed and detached by decree.

In every city and in every village mentioned in Table No. (1) annexed to Legislative Decree No. 11 dated 29/12/1954, a municipality may be established. If the fees collected during the financial year fall below one thousand Lebanese pounds, the municipality shall automatically be moved from the share accruing to it of the revenues of the fees collected by the State and distributed to the municipalities during the year following it.

The determination of the municipal territorial jurisdiction is an administrative measure unrelated to the entries of the Real Estate Register. The determination shall take place upon the proposal of the Governor (Muhafiz) and shall be exempted from topographical fees, and the determination transaction together with the maps pertaining to it shall be joined to the file of the establishment of the municipality, and then all of them shall be submitted to the Minister of the Interior, who shall issue a single decision establishing the municipality and determining its territorial jurisdiction. As for the currently existing municipalities, the determination of their territorial jurisdiction shall take place in accordance with the provisions of the first paragraph of this Article within a period of one year from the date of the issuance of this Law.
A single municipality may be formed of two or several contiguous villages, in each of which the condition provided for in paragraph 1 of Article 3 is met
Two or more municipalities may be annexed to one another so that all of them form a unified municipality.

If the absolute majority of the registered voters in one of the villages that form a unified municipality request the detachment of their village from the unified municipality in order to form an independent municipality, the Government shall have the right to decide that by decree.

In the event of annexation, or in the event of the detachment of a village from a unified municipality, or the annexation of a village to a unified or non-unified municipality, the municipalities to which it is annexed, from which it is detached, or which are annexed to one another shall be deemed dissolved by operation of law, and the status of each of them shall be settled in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

A village that is annexed to another municipality shall remain the owner of the properties that belonged to it prior to the annexation, and its inhabitants shall continue to enjoy the in-kind yield of those properties. Likewise, a municipal section that is annexed to another municipality shall remain the owner of the property that belonged to it prior to this annexation. However, buildings and other real properties allocated for public benefit, whether located in the lands of the municipality or in the lands of the section annexed to it, shall become the property of the municipality to which the said section was annexed. As for a municipality established in an area detached from another municipality, it shall remain the owner of the buildings and private properties located therein. With respect to real properties allocated for public benefit, such as common lands and others, the right to exploit, enjoy, and dispose of them shall remain for the general inhabitants as was the case prior to the detachment and the establishment of the new municipality. These matters and others resulting from the annexation of land to one of the municipalities or its detachment therefrom shall be determined by the decrees ordering the detachment or annexation. Every municipality and every municipal section annexed to another municipality and every section made into an independent municipality shall recover, upon separation, the properties that belonged to it prior to the annexation. As for the properties acquired after the annexation, they shall remain in the ownership of the municipality in which they are located. The bureau owed to and by the municipality shall be distributed between the two separated municipalities in the decree ordering their separation or in a subsequent decree.
The municipal body shall consist of a decision-making authority of a decision-making authority and an executive authority.

The municipal council shall consist of: 8- members for a municipality whose registered population does not exceed 2000 10- members for a municipality whose registered population ranges between 2001 and 4000 12- members for a municipality whose registered population ranges between 4001 and 25000 14- members for a municipality whose registered population ranges between 25001 and 60000 16- members for a municipality whose registered population exceeds 60000 18- members for the Municipality of Tripoli 24- members for the Municipality of Beirut .
The members of the municipal council shall be elected by direct universal suffrage in accordance with the procedures followed in parliamentary elections.

No person may be elected to membership of the municipal council unless he is an elector whose name is registered on the electoral roll pertaining to the municipality in whose council he wishes to be a member.

Membership of the municipal council may not be combined with: 1- the office of Mukhtar and membership of the Ikhtiyariyya councils 2- membership of the councils of the governorates 3- offices of the State, autonomous authorities and municipalities 4- membership and offices of bodies and committees entrusted with the management of projects of public utility within the jurisdiction of the municipalities in which these institutions exist. 5- ownership of an electricity or water concession within the jurisdiction of the municipal council for which the owner of the concession stands as a candidate. 6- offices in the said concession.

The following shall not be eligible for membership of the municipal councils: 1- Those who do not know how to read and write. 2- Those sentenced to deprivation of civil rights or civil degradation. 3- Those sentenced for felonies or disgraceful misdemeanours as specified in paragraph 3 of Article 10 of the Law on the Election of Members of the Chamber of Deputies or for the misdemeanours provided for in Articles 329 to 334 of the Penal Code. 4- Those sentenced for crimes of belonging to secret societies. 5- Those judicially interdicted on grounds of imbecility and insanity. 6- Persons who are declared bankrupt until their rehabilitation.

Whoever wishes to nominate himself for membership of a municipality must submit to the Qaimaqam, at least ten days prior to the date of the election, a declaration signed by him personally and authenticated before a notary public, containing his name and the name of the municipality in which he wishes to nominate himself, accompanied by a notice proving that he has deposited with the finance fund of the centre of the district or the governorate a deposit in the amount of fifty Lebanese pounds.

The deposit shall not be returned to the candidate unless he obtains in the election twenty-five per cent of the votes of the voters legally cast if he withdraws his candidacy at least three days prior to the date of the election pursuant to a written notice which he submits to the Qaimaqam.
The electoral list specific to the election of the Chamber of Deputies shall be adopted for the election of the municipal councils.

The candidate shall be given a receipt within three days at the most from the date of submission of his declaration. If the competent authority abstains from giving him the receipt, he may petition the State Council by a simple application exempt from fees, and the said Council must decide upon his objection finally in the deliberation chamber within three days.

The names of the candidates who have been given the receipt shall be published without delay in the municipal areas in which they are running for office and on the door of the polling station, and a copy thereof shall be delivered to the committee provided for in Article 14 of the Law on the Election of Members of the Chamber of Deputies. Only an elector whose name is registered on the electoral list or who has obtained a decision to register his name from the competent registration committee or from the court hearing administrative cases shall take part in the ballot.

The municipal electoral bodies shall be convoked by a decision of the Minister of the Interior upon the proposal of the Governor, in which the polling centres shall be determined. The time limit between the date of publication of this decision and the date of the election shall be at least thirty days. The convocation decision shall be published in the municipal area and on the door of the district Government House at least fifteen days prior to the date of the election. The electoral operations shall continue from eight o'clock until sixteen o'clock and may not last more than one day.

The Governor shall appoint the presiding officer and clerks of the polling bureau and shall publish his decision at least three days prior to the commencement of the election. The presiding officer of the bureau shall direct the electoral operations with the assistance of four electors, half of whom he shall choose and the other half shall be chosen by the electors present before the polling bureau, failing which the presiding officer of the bureau shall choose them from the category to which the first half does not belong.

The presiding officer shall be assisted, where necessary, by one or several clerks from among the civil servants, and the presiding officer and at least half the number of assistants must be present throughout the duration of the electoral operations.

The presiding officer of the bureau alone is entrusted with maintaining order in the polling hall, and he may, when necessary, secure such order through the armed forces, and no armed force may enter the polling hall except at the request of the presiding officer of the bureau. The presiding officer of the bureau shall not have the right to expel any of his four assistants.

The presiding officer of the polling bureau must, upon commencing the electoral operations, verify the hour of their opening. When the hour for closing the electoral operations arrives, the presiding officer, with the assistance of one of the clerks, shall confine the electors present in the courtyard located in front of the polling station, and shall allow those persons to vote to the exclusion of all others.

The polling bureau shall decide provisionally on problems relating to the electoral operations, and its decisions must be recorded in the minutes and the documents or papers relating thereto must be annexed to them after it signs them.
Decision-making authority shall be vested in the Municipal Council.
The Municipal Council shall exercise its powers by virtue of resolutions it issues in sessions it holds for this purpose.

The Municipal Council shall meet at least once a month, pursuant to a convocation from its President. The President shall specify in his convocation the subjects that necessitate the meeting, and the Council may not examine other subjects at the time of the session. It shall be incumbent upon the President to convoke the Municipal Council to a meeting if requested to do so by the Governor, the District Commissioner, or the majority of the members of whom the Municipal Council is composed on the date the convocation is addressed. The convocation to the meeting must be in writing and must be sent at least one day prior to the session to the place of residence designated by the members.

The Municipal Council shall, during the month of October of each year, commence examining the budget of the municipality prior to any other subject. If it does not approve it prior to 31 December, it shall be submitted as drawn up by the President to the Governor to examine the matter of its ratification.
The President of the municipality shall preside over the sessions of the Municipal Council, and in the event of his absence, the Vice-President, and otherwise the oldest of the members in age.

The president of the session shall undertake the maintenance of order therein, and if a felony or misdemeanour is committed therein, he shall draw up a record of the facts and send it without delay to the competent judiciary, and shall notify the District Commissioner of a copy of this record. The Vice-President shall preside over the sessions in which the accounts of the administration of the municipality entrusted to the President are discussed, and the oldest of the members in age shall preside over them if the Vice-President has had any involvement in the financial administration of the municipality. The President of the municipality may attend the discussion of its administrative accounts, provided that he withdraws from the session prior to the commencement of voting. The president of the session shall send the resolution to the Governor through official channels.

The sessions of the Municipal Council shall be confidential. The Governor or the District Commissioner may attend them if they so request, provided that they shall not have the right to vote. The Secretary of the municipality, if any, and otherwise one of its employees designated by the President, shall perform the function of rapporteur on the matters submitted for discussion by the Municipal Council. The President of the municipality may invite any employee or any other person to attend the sessions of the Municipal Council in order to be heard.

A voter may cast only one ballot paper. The ballot paper may include only the number of candidates required to be elected, and if it includes a greater number, the last excess names shall not be taken into account.

The President of the polling station shall declare the close of the electoral proceedings at the hour specified in Article 21, subject to the provisions of Article 25, and shall proceed to open the ballot box and examine the voters' ballot papers, verify their number, and record that in the minutes. Each ballot paper shall then be read aloud in the presence of the assistants, and the votes shall be recorded on the sheets prepared for that purpose; as for the sorting of the voters' ballot papers, it shall be carried out by the polling station staff.

Blank ballot papers, ballot papers that do not sufficiently indicate the name recorded thereon, those bearing an indication of the identity of their voters, as well as coloured ballot papers, those that are illegible, those upon which a distinguishing mark has been placed, and ballot papers containing expressions insulting to the candidates or to other persons, shall not be taken into account in the result of the poll, but shall be annexed to the minutes.

Immediately following the count, the President of the polling station shall announce the provisional result of the poll, draw up a schedule thereof, and affix this result on the door of the polling station.

When the provisional result of the poll is announced, minutes of the proceedings shall be drawn up in duplicate, sealed, and then signed together with the tally sheets by all members of the polling station. Each candidate shall be entitled to obtain from the President of the polling station a certified true copy of the minutes; as for the two copies of these minutes and the documents annexed thereto, including the ballot papers and the checklist, the President of the polling station shall forward them without delay to the committee provided for in Article 14 of the Law on the Election of Members of the Chamber of Deputies, and this committee shall audit the counting process and announce the final result by drawing up minutes, a copy of which shall be affixed on the door of the Government House, with mention thereof made in the minutes, and shall forward the minutes together with all its decisions and the documents relating to the election to the Ministry of the Interior, and deposit a copy of the minutes with the Qaimaqam of the district or the Governorate.

After the count, the votes obtained by each candidate shall be totalled. The candidates who obtain the highest number of votes shall win the poll. If two or more candidates obtain an equal number of votes, the oldest among them shall be deemed the winner. If they are of equal age, recourse shall be had to drawing lots, through the committee provided for in Article 14 of the Law on the Election of Members of the Chamber of Deputies.

If the number of candidates is limited to the number of members to be elected, those candidates shall win by acclamation. And if the number of candidates is less than the number of members required to be elected, those candidates shall win by acclamation. Victory by acclamation shall be declared by a decision of the committee provided for in Article 14 of the Law on the Election of Members of the Chamber of Deputies.
The validity of the election may be challenged before the State Council within a period of fifteen days following the declaration of the result.
The provisions of Articles 329 to 334 of the Penal Code shall apply to acts committed to corrupt the election.

Municipal councils shall be elected for a term of four years, and their election shall be set within sixty days prior to the end of their term of office, and the Minister of the Interior may appoint the date of the election on a single day for all municipalities or appoint a special date for each governorate if public security so requires.

If one of the persons mentioned in Article 14 of this Law is elected as a municipal member, he must choose within a period of two weeks between the membership and his office, failing which he shall be deemed dismissed ipso jure, and the dismissal shall be declared by a decision of the Governor, and if one of the members of the municipality is found to be in one of the cases provided for in the aforementioned Article 15, he shall be deemed to have resigned ipso jure from the membership of the municipality by a decision of the Governor.

A single person may not be a member of several municipal councils, and likewise, in a single municipality, a father and one of the children, a mother and one of the children, a husband and wife, a father-in-law and a daughter's husband or a son's wife, a mother-in-law and a son's wife or a daughter's husband, brothers and sisters, a paternal uncle and a brother's son, a maternal uncle and a sister's son, and a sister's husband and a brother's husband, of whatever distinction, may not be members of a single municipal council. And if two of the relatives and in-laws mentioned above are elected and neither of them resigns, the Qaemaqam must dismiss the younger of the two in age, and if they are of equal age, one of them shall be dismissed by lot at the first meeting held by the municipal council.

The municipal council shall elect from among its members, at the first session it holds at the date and place determined by the Governor or the Qaemaqam within a period of fifteen days from the date of the declaration of the election result, a president and a vice-president for a term of four years by secret ballot and by relative majority. The Qaemaqam shall issue the convocation, and the oldest of the members in age shall preside over the session. In the event of an equality of votes between two members, the older in age shall win, and if they are of the same age, recourse shall be had to drawing lots. No member who is an employee of the president may be elected as vice-president.

The deliberation of the Municipal Council shall not be valid unless the session is attended by more than half of the members of whom the Council is composed on the date of holding the session in which the deliberation takes place, and if the said proportion is not met, the meeting shall be adjourned and the members shall be summoned to a new meeting to be fixed by a summons after twenty-four hours at least, and the session shall not be legal unless attended by one-third of the members at least, provided that the second summons must include an explicit summary of the provisions of this article. The second summons shall be dispensed with and the session shall be legal if the non-attendance arises from the existence of a personal interest of the absent members or of a person whose affairs they manage.

The Mayor, of his own accord or at the request of the Qaimaqam or the Governor, may request the Municipal Council to deliberate exceptionally, before anything else, on a matter requiring urgent study. He may prohibit deliberation on a subject outside the agenda.

Voting shall take place by way of open ballot, and voting by proxy shall not be permissible. Recourse shall be had to the method of secret ballot if the President or the majority of the members present so request, or if the voting relates to any election.
The resolutions of the Council shall be adopted by a majority of the votes of the members present. In the event of an equality of votes, the President shall have a casting vote.

Minutes of every session of the sessions of the Municipal Council shall be drawn up in a special register the pages of which shall be numbered and signed by the Qaimaqam or whoever he delegates.
