The minutes or a summary thereof shall be read out and signed at the same session, provided that they are ratified at the following session: the text of the decisions issued by the Council, the names of the persons who participated in the deliberation and a summary of their remarks, and the names of those who voted in the open ballot and the designation of the direction of their vote must also be mentioned in the minutes.

Municipal decisions shall be sent to the Qaimaqam within one week at most from the date of their issuance, and copies thereof shall be posted on the door of the municipality immediately upon their issuance.

The municipal committee shall consist of the president, his deputy and two members elected by the council in the first session it holds. The municipal committee shall study all matters relating to the administration of the municipality that are submitted to it by the president of the municipality or that are submitted to it in accordance with the laws and regulations; save as aforesaid, the municipal committee shall decide upon the matters referred to it by the municipal council. The municipal committee shall conduct tenders in accordance with the rules followed in the departments of the State and shall contract out municipal fees in accordance with the provisions of the laws in force. The municipal committee shall meet upon the convocation of its president, and the session shall not be legal except in the presence of the majority of the members of the committee, and the provisions relating to the deliberations of the municipal council shall apply to its deliberations.
Every work of a public character or utility, within the municipal scope, falls within the competence of the municipal council.

The municipal council shall undertake, without this being by way of limitation, the handling of the following matters: 1- Town planning, and the establishment and maintenance of streets, squares and public parks. 2- Public health affairs and public hygiene, and the establishment and administration of sewers and waste disposal facilities. 3- Water and lighting projects. 4- The establishment of slaughterhouses and the organisation of their administration. 5- The establishment of public utilities. 6- The organisation of means of transport. 7- The organisation of means of advertising. 8- The organisation, sale and pricing of foodstuffs. 9- The organisation of first aid and rescue works, relief of the needy, firefighting and the establishment of public shelters 10- The monitoring and supervision of the administration of municipal funds. 11- The preparation of the budget of the new financial year. 12- The discussion and preparation of the schedule of the final account for the ended financial year. 13- Deciding upon the collection of dues, fees and taxes allocated to the revenues of the council.

The municipal council may, within its area, establish or administer by itself or through an intermediary, or contribute to or assist in the execution of the following works and projects: 1- Public schools, nurseries and vocational schools. 2- Popular housing and public baths and wash-houses. 3- Public hospitals, sanatoriums, dispensaries and other health facilities and institutions. 4- Museums, public libraries, theatres, cinemas, places of entertainment, clubs, playgrounds and other public and sports premises, and social, cultural and artistic institutions. 5- Local means of public transport. 6- Public markets, food markets, fish, grain threshing floors and cold stores for preserving fruit and vegetables.

The Municipal Council shall undertake, within the scope of its competence, the supervision of the implementation of the laws and regulations in force relating to public health, planning, building and land subdivision affairs, roads, commercial and industrial establishments, and other special laws concerning the public utilities of the town. Every governmental body concerned with the implementation of these laws and regulations may supervise their proper implementation through the Municipal Council.

The Municipal Council may express its remarks regarding the public needs of the locality it represents, and the President of the Council or whoever acts in his stead shall undertake to communicate these wishes to the competent authorities through the Qaemaqam.

The opinion of the Municipal Council must be sought on the following matters: 1- Changing the name of the locality 2- Changing the boundaries of the locality 3- Regulating traffic and public transport 4- Projects for the alignment and extension of major public roads in the municipal area. 5- Establishing, transferring or abolishing public schools and governmental hospitals and dispensaries.-

6- Measures relating to public relief 7- Establishing charitable offices and institutions. - All matters on which the laws and regulations require the opinion of the Municipal Council to be sought, and the matters on which the Muhافظ (Governor) or the Qaemaqam consults it. - If the Municipal Council does not express its opinion within the period specified for it by the Qaemaqam in the request, its opinion may be dispensed with.
The decisions of the Municipal Council shall not become effective except after being coupled with the approval of the supervisory authority.
The supervisory authority shall be exercised by: - The Qaemaqam - The Governor - The Minister of the Interior

The decisions of the municipal council shall be recorded under serial numbers according to their dates in a register whose pages shall be numbered and which shall be signed by the Qaemaqam or the person delegated by him. No blank space shall be left in the register, and no striking out or writing in the margin shall be permitted therein, and where necessary, two lines shall be drawn across the blank space and the president and the clerk shall sign the striking out or the writing in the margin, and every violation shall be recorded at the foot of the decision. The omission to record one of the decisions in the special register shall not lead to its annulment and to and the annulment of the acts executed pursuant thereto, provided that the supervisory authority shall notify the municipal council of this omission and take measures to prevent its recurrence and to record the omitted decision. The pages of the register of decisions shall comprise a margin and four columns: in the margin opposite the text of the decision shall be recorded all particulars relating, where applicable, to its approval or its annulment, and in the first column shall be recorded the serial number of the decision, and in the second column the date of its posting on the door of the municipal hall, and in the third column the date of its dispatch to the Qaemaqam, and in the fourth column the text of the decision itself.

Every interested party in the municipal district may request to be given, at his own expense, a copy of the decisions of the municipal council or its president, certified by the secretary of the municipality or the acting secretary thereof, and to inspect the annual final account.

The municipal council may elect, at the beginning of each year, committees from among its members to examine the matters submitted to it, and it may seek the assistance of committees that it appoints for this purpose.

If a municipal member fails to answer the convocation to a meeting three consecutive times without a reason deemed legitimate by the council, the president shall notify the Qaemaqam thereof, together with the reasons that led to the absence, and the Qaemaqam may assess these reasons and deem the member to have resigned where appropriate. The member deemed independent may challenge the decision of the Qaemaqam before the State Council within ten days from the date it is notified to him.

The resignation of the president, the vice-president, or the municipal member shall be submitted to the Muhafez through the Qaemaqam and shall be deemed final from the date of its acceptance by a decision of the Muhafez. If no decision is taken regarding acceptance, the resignation shall be deemed final after the lapse of one month from the date of submitting a second resignation after the lapse of one month from the date of submitting a second resignation sent by registered letter. The expiration of fifteen days from the acceptance of the resignation of the president or his vice-president, or the resignation being deemed final, is counted, the municipal council shall meet to elect the successor in accordance with the provisions of Article 39 of this Law.

Decisions subject to the approval of the Minister of the Interior: - Decisions that constitute permanent regulations, such as the staff regulations. - Loans and extraordinary expenditures included in the ordinary municipal budget. - Contracts for supplies and works when their value exceeds fifty thousand Lebanese pounds. - Sale of municipal properties whose value exceeds 25 thousand Lebanese pounds. - Works executed by direct administration when their costs exceed two thousand Lebanese pounds. - Creation, planning, abolition, classification, or amendment of the classification of public streets and squares, and the alignment, extension, widening, and naming of those streets and squares. Likewise, the creation or abolition of public gardens, public parks, squares where public markets are held, and racecourses, and the drawing up of plans for the alignment or demarcation of public municipal streets, or the introduction of an amendment to plans relating to the alignment of streets. - Creation of syndicates comprising several municipal councils to undertake joint works of public utility.
The approval of each of the Qaimaqam, the Governor, and the Minister of the Interior must be in writing.
Each of the Qaimaqam, the Governor, and the Minister of the Interior must return the decisions after the expiry of fifteen days at most from the date of their receipt by him.

After the lapse of fifteen days from the date of receipt of the decisions by the Qaimaqam, it shall be incumbent upon the Mayor to inquire by means of a letter submitted by him to the Qaimaqam. If ten days elapse from the date of receipt of the Mayor's letter by the Qaimaqam and the Mayor receives no reply, the municipal decision shall be deemed approved. The Mayor, in such a case, must notify the Qaimaqam that the decision has become approved. These time limits shall not apply to decisions relating to planning and the budget. As for decisions subject to the Court of Accounts, the period in respect thereof shall run from the date of notification of the Court's decision to the administrative authority. The Governor or the Minister of the Interior may, at any time he wishes and for reasons relating to security, postpone the execution of a municipal decision previously approved, and this must be done pursuant to a reasoned decision.

The decisions of the Qaimaqam, the Governor, and the Minister of the Interior approving, not approving, or postponing the execution of the decisions of the municipal council are subject to appeal before the State Council. However, an appeal against the approval of a municipal decision shall not stay its execution.
All municipal decisions, and all correspondence issued by the municipality or addressed to it, must be sent to the Qaimaqam or through him.

Decisions subject to the approval of the Qaimaqam: - The municipal budget - Municipal fees - The purchase of real property the value of which does not exceed twenty thousand Lebanese pounds. - Lease contracts the annual rent of which does not exceed two thousand Lebanese pounds. - Placing municipal buildings under the insurance of an insurance company. - Accepting or refusing donations and items bequeathed to the municipality from which no encumbrances arise or which are not the subject of objection by the holders of rights in the donated or bequeathed property. - Relieving the poor and the destitute and assisting social, cultural, artistic, and athletic clubs and associations and the like. - Setting tariffs for public carriages and vehicles of all kinds and animals intended for riding, pack transport, and draught. - Contracts for supplies and works when their value does not exceed ten thousand Lebanese pounds. - Works by direct execution when their costs do not exceed one thousand pounds, and subdivision shall not be permitted. - Collecting taxes and fees and levying attachment upon the property of taxpayers who refrain from paying such taxes and fees on their due dates. - Any matter not mentioned in the following two Articles.

Decisions subject to the approval of the Governor: - Contracts for supplies and works when their value exceeds ten thousand Lebanese pounds and is less than fifty thousand Lebanese pounds. - Works by direct execution when they exceed two thousand Lebanese pounds, and subdivision of the works shall not be permitted. - The purchase of real property the value of which exceeds twenty thousand Lebanese pounds and is less than fifty thousand Lebanese pounds. - The sale of municipal properties the value of which amounts to twenty-five thousand Lebanese pounds or less. - The settlement of disagreements and disputes after obtaining the opinion of the Department of Cases. - Accepting or refusing donations and items bequeathed to the municipality from which encumbrances arise, or which are the subject of objection by the holders of rights in the bequeathed property, or in which any condition is stipulated. - Where the donations or bequeathed items are susceptible to spoilage or loss, the President of the Municipality shall be entitled to receive and retain them until the Municipal Council takes a decision thereon and the Governor approves it. - Allocating a municipal property to a particular service after it had been allocated to a public interest. - Lease contracts the annual rent of which exceeds two thousand Lebanese pounds.

If the Municipal Council or its President refuses or neglects to perform one of the acts which the laws and regulations impose upon it or him, or which the Qaemaqam has requested it or him in writing to perform, or refuses to pay mandatory expenditures, the Qaemaqam may, either of his own motion or pursuant to a request submitted to him by a holder of a right or an interest, address to the Council or to the President a written order requiring execution within a time limit specified in the written order. If the time limit expires, the Qaemaqam is entitled, after obtaining the approval of the Governor, to perform the same himself pursuant to a decision that replaces the decision required to be issued. The decision taken by the Qaemaqam shall be recorded in the special register of decisions. This decision shall not be executed until it has received the endorsement of the competent tutelage authority.

Save for urgent matters and conservatory measures, the municipality may not institute an action except with an authorisation from the Qaemaqam, and its right to institute actions and the existence of an interest requiring the institution thereof must be established. As for the decision of the Qaemaqam in this regard, it must be reasoned and must be issued within one month commencing from the day of the aforementioned request for authorisation. If its issuance is delayed beyond the expiry of this time limit, the municipality is entitled to institute the action and to plead therein.

Save for possessory actions, no action may be instituted against the municipality before the courts until the plaintiff sends to the Governor the memorandum in which he sets out the subject matter of his action and the grounds thereof, and if the plaintiff fails to submit the aforementioned memorandum, his action shall be dismissed. The action may not be instituted until the expiry of one month from the date of submitting the memorandum or sending it by registered letter, and the submission by the plaintiff of the aforementioned memorandum suspends prescription or forfeiture of right, provided that the action is instituted within three months after the submission of the memorandum. The Governor shall send without delay the aforementioned memorandum to the President of the Municipality and shall request him to convene the Council to deliberate on the matter.
The rules of procedure followed in the execution of judgments rendered against the State shall apply with respect to municipalities.
The refusal or neglect of the Municipal Council to perform the acts referred to in Article 76 renders it liable within the scope of the provisions of this Law.

The Municipal Council is deemed dissolved by operation of law, and the dissolution shall be declared by a decision of the Governor: if it loses the majority of its members. In the event of the annulment of the election by a decision of the State Council. If the Central Inspection recommends its dissolution. If the proportion of collected revenues falls below half of the estimated revenues for the financial year.

The municipal council shall be dissolved by a decision of the Minister of the Interior upon the proposal of the Governor, if it neglects the performance of its duties or commits repeated significant violations that have caused harm to the interests of the municipality. The neglect and the violations must be established by reports issued by the District Commissioner or the Governor.

If the municipal council is dissolved, it shall be reconstituted, in accordance with the provisions of this Law, within a period of two months from the date of dissolution. Provided, however, that the reconstitution may not take place within the six months preceding the date of the general municipal elections; rather, the District Commissioner or the Governor shall be entrusted to perform or the Governor to perform the functions of the dissolved municipal council by a decision issued by the Minister of the Interior.
The President, his Vice-President, or the municipal member may not be criminally prosecuted for an offence relating to their duties except pursuant to the written approval of the Governor.

If a criminal prosecution or a disgraceful misdemeanour takes place against the President of the municipality, the Vice-President, or one of the members, he may be suspended from duty by a decision of the Governor until the conclusion of the prosecution. If one of these is indicted of a felony or accused of a disgraceful misdemeanour, he must be suspended from duty by a decision of the Governor - until the conclusion of the action. If a final judgment of a felony or of a disgraceful misdemeanour is issued against one of these, he shall be deemed dismissed ipso jure, and the dismissal shall be declared by a decision of the Governor. If an arrest warrant, whether in absentia or in person, for any offence whatsoever, is issued against one of these, he shall be deemed suspended from duty ipso jure as of the date of the warrant. If the arrest warrant is withdrawn or he is released, he shall return ipso jure to the exercise of his functions unless he had been arrested for a felony or for a disgraceful offence relating to the functions of the office.

The President of the municipality, his Vice-President, or the municipal member who assumes the functions of the executive authority shall be dismissed if he commits gross negligence or a grave error, by a decision of the Governor upon the recommendation of the Central Inspection or pursuant to a decision of the Disciplinary Council.

When the circumstances of the administrative investigation require that the President, his Vice-President, or one of the members not continue in office, the Governor shall have the right to suspend him from duty until the cessation of the circumstances the assessment of which is vested in the Governor, and this right shall be granted to the President of the Central Inspection or to the Inspector General during the inspection or as a result thereof.

The Special Disciplinary Council for the presidents, vice-presidents and members of municipal councils from among those who exercise the functions of the executive authority shall be composed by a decree issued upon the proposal of each of the Minister of Justice and the Minister of the Interior and after consulting the President of the Civil Service Board, of: - A judge of at least the tenth grade, as President - A civil servant from the Civil Service Board of at least Category 3, as two members - A civil servant from the Ministry of the Interior of at least Category 3 - And the function of Government Commissioner shall be performed by an inspector from the Central Inspection

The presidents, vice-presidents and members of municipal councils who exercise the functions of the executive authority shall be referred to the Disciplinary Council by a decision of the Governor upon the proposal of the Qaemaqam based on an investigation conducted by the latter, or by a decision of the President of the Central Inspection.

Disciplinary penalties: - The disciplinary penalties that may be imposed upon the president, vice-president or member of the municipal council are the following: - Warning - Reprimand - Suspension from work for a period not exceeding one year - Dismissal
The executive authority shall be exercised by the president of the municipality.
The president of the municipality shall be assisted, in the course of exercising the executive authority, by municipal departments and a municipal committee.

The President of the Municipal Council, in his capacity as head of the executive authority, shall have the following competence: - He executes the decision of the departments of the Municipal Council - He manages the municipal departments and supervises them - He manages the funds and real property of the municipality and consequently performs all acts necessary for the preservation of its rights. - He manages the revenues of the municipality and supervises its accounts - He orders the expenditure of the municipal budget. - He monitors the works executed on behalf of the municipality - He represents the municipality before the courts - He takes local measures in matters entrusted to his care and authority pursuant to laws and regulations, and in particular in the following affairs: - Combating drunkenness and epidemic or contagious diseases - Undertaking the affairs of preserving public comfort, safety and health, provided that he does not interfere with the powers granted by laws and regulations to the competent departments in the State. - Securing traffic and facilitating circulation in streets, squares and public roads, removing rubble, and demolishing or repairing dilapidated buildings. - Regulating the procession of funerals and preserving the sanctity of cemeteries. - Everything relating to public morals and decency. - Licensing the stay or the temporary placement of goods on public roads and places, and he authorises temporarily, if the case requires, that goods be displayed on sidewalks, roadsides and public squares and that vendors stay thereon temporarily, and he also permits owners of restaurants and cafés and beverage vendors to place tables, benches and chairs on the aforementioned sidewalks, roadsides and squares. - Licensing the digging of channels in public roads, to lay water, gas or electricity conduits. - Stopping construction against a guarantee provided by the applicant for the stoppage for a period of fifteen days during which the concerned party is able to petition the judiciary.

All municipalities are required to establish staff regulations and a cadre for their employees, pursuant to a municipal decision subject to the approval of the Minister of Interior. The post of municipal clerk and treasurer shall be included as of right in the permanent cadre - and the municipal regulations must include in particular all conditions relating to the procedures of appointment, promotion, discipline, dismissal and termination of service.

If two months lapse from the publication of this law, without the municipalities proceeding to establish staff regulations and a cadre for their employees, the Qaemaqam or the Mohafez shall have the right to act, within this scope, in the place of the Municipal Council and to establish, by a decision from him, staff regulations and a cadre for the municipalities that prove to be devoid thereof. The decision of the Qaemaqam shall be registered in the register of decisions of the concerned municipality and shall be put into execution after being coupled with the approval of the Minister of Interior.

Municipalities may comprise the administrative and technical departments that they require, and this shall be effected by a decision of the municipal council subject to the ratification of the Minister of Interior. The decision issued in this regard shall be deemed an integral part of the staff regulations and establishment of the employees of the municipality.

All employees of the municipality shall be appointed within the framework of its ratified regulations and establishments by a decision of the mayor subject to the ratification of the governor, unless a contrary provision appears in its special regulations. They shall be subject to training in the institutes special to State employees. - Employees of the municipality shall be dismissed or suspended from duty in the same manner.

If the public interest requires that two or more municipalities cooperate in carrying out a project of joint benefit, the matter shall be submitted through hierarchical channels to the Minister of Interior, who shall order the conduct of an investigation into the project and its conditions. - The Minister of Interior may, in light of the aforementioned investigation, issue a decision ordering the establishment of a syndicate comprising the municipalities concerned. - There shall be designated in the decision of establishment: - The project for which the syndicate was established. The municipality that shall be the seat of the syndicate. - The committee that manages it

The syndicate shall be deemed a public institution endowed with moral personality and shall have an independent budget, and the laws and regulations special to administrative tutelage over municipalities shall apply to it.

The syndicate shall be managed by a committee composed of: - The mayors of the municipalities of which it is formed. - The eldest member in each of these municipalities - And if the municipality is under the charge of the governor or the Qaimaqam, it shall be represented in the syndicate by members who fulfil the conditions to be municipal members.

If the post of one or more members in the syndicate becomes vacant due to death, resignation, dismissal, or any other reason, the Minister of Interior shall appoint as his successor the eldest member among the serving members in the municipality to which he belonged.

The rules of accounting in municipalities shall apply in the syndicate. If there is in the syndicate a municipality subject to the provisions of the Public Accounting Law, this latter law shall apply to the syndicate. If it is impossible to apply its provisions or some of them, the rules of accounting in municipalities shall apply.

If the syndicate comprises municipalities affiliated with more than one governor, the governor in whom the authority of administrative tutelage over it is vested shall be designated in the decision of establishment. This authority shall be vested in the governor with whom the municipality taken as the seat of the syndicate is affiliated.

The presidency of the syndicate shall be vested ex officio in the Qaemaqam to whom the municipality chosen as the seat of the syndicate is subordinate, and if the municipality chosen as the seat of the syndicate falls within the jurisdiction of the Caza directly presided over by the Governor in his capacity as its Qaemaqam, the presidency of the syndicate shall be vested in the president of the municipality concerned. Within the scope of the supervisory authority over the syndicate, the Governor shall exercise the powers vested in the Qaemaqam pursuant to the provisions of Article 67 of this Law.
The syndicate shall meet upon the convocation of its president whenever he deems it necessary, or at the request of two-thirds of its active members.
The president of the syndicate shall exercise, in respect thereof, the powers exercised by the president of the municipality in his capacity as head of the executive authority.

The duties of the secretariat of the syndicate, its accounting, and its treasury shall be vested in the secretary, accountant, and treasurer of the municipality chosen as its seat. If the said municipality is devoid of these employees or of any one of them, the president of the syndicate shall appoint from among its members employees to perform these duties or any one of them. - The treasurer shall in all cases be subject to the suretyship regime.

With regard to the resolutions of the syndicate, their registration and publication, and with regard to the holding of its sessions, the special rules applicable to municipalities provided for in this Law shall apply.
The syndicate shall elect, at the first session it holds, three members who shall constitute the syndicate committee, provided that no single municipality is represented by more than one member
The syndicate committee shall exercise the powers vested in the municipal committee pursuant to the provisions of this- Law.
Subject to the provisions of Article 248 of Legislative Decree No. 117 dated 12/6/59, the accounting rules in municipalities shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.

The procedures for applying the Public Accounting Law to the municipalities subject thereto pursuant to Article 247 of Legislative Decree No. 117 dated 12/6/1959 shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.

The Minister of Interior may delegate to the Director General of the Interior the right to exercise some or all of the powers vested in him pursuant to the provisions of this Law, with the exception of the constitutional powers, and the Minister may also delegate some or all of these powers to the Governors, just as he may delegate some of his powers to the Director General of the Interior and some of them to the Governors.
The Governor shall assume the acts of the executive authority in Beirut. And the Minister of Interior shall exercise the powers provided for in Article 67 of this Law.

If the Governor in Beirut does not commence the execution of the decisions of the municipal council within one month from the date of their notification to him as enforceable, the municipal council shall put him on notice of the obligation of execution. If he does not comply with this notice within a time limit of ten days, the council shall entrust the execution to its president.

Subject to the provisions of the preceding Article, the Minister of Interior shall exercise, with respect to the municipalities of the capitals of the governorates, the powers vested in the Governor pursuant to the provisions of this Law, with the exception of Articles 22, 37, 42, 48

The budget of the municipalities subject to the provisions of the Public Accounting Law shall be subject to the authority of a Controller General appointed upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers for a period of four years, and his salary and allowances shall be determined in the decree of his appointment, and it shall not be permissible for him during the performance of his office to receive other allowances of whatever kind and from whatever authority. The salary and allowances of the Controller General shall be disbursed from the budget of the municipality over which he is appointed as a controller.
The powers of the Controller General shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.

The following conditions must be fulfilled in the Controller General: 1- That he be a civil servant of at least the third category who has spent in the service a period of not less than ten years. 2- That he be a specialist in financial affairs.
The Controller General may not be assigned to perform any other work.

The term of office of municipal councils that shall be established after the issuance of this Law and in which elections are held shall expire on the date of expiry of the term of office of the municipal councils that were elected pursuant to the provisions of this Law. As for newly established municipalities whose members were elected prior to the publication of this Law, their term of office shall expire on the date of expiry of the term of office of the upcoming municipal councils.
All texts and provisions contrary to this Law or inconsistent with its provisions are repealed.

Article 1: Civil Servants, Contractors and Wage-Earners 1 - Civil servants are divided into permanent civil servants and temporary civil servants. a - A permanent civil servant is a person appointed to a permanent post provided for in one of the permanent establishments, whether he is subject to the pension regime or is not subject thereto. b - A temporary civil servant is a person appointed to a temporary post created for a specified period or for incidental work. 2 - A contractor is a person with whom a contract has been concluded for a fixed term in order to perform specific work requiring special knowledge or qualifications. 3 - A wage-earner is a person employed to work in the public administrations and who does not belong to one of the categories set forth in items (1) and (2) of this Article.

Legal status Civil servants shall be subject to the statutory and regulatory provisions relating to the civil service. All subsequent statutory and regulatory provisions shall apply to them, without their having any acquired right to benefit from prior provisions. ه - The age of a new civil servant shall be stated in the instrument providing for his appointment, on the basis of a certified true copy of his entry in the personal status registers. If the date of the day of birth is unknown, the civil servant shall be deemed to have been born on the first day of the month of July of the year of his birth. If, however, the month of birth is known without the day, the civil servant shall be deemed to have been born on the fifteenth day of the month of his birth. و - In determining the age of a civil servant, no account shall be taken of any rectification made thereto after the announcement of the competitive examination, or after the issuance of the instrument of appointment with respect to civil servants whom the law permits to be appointed without a competitive examination. Nor shall any account be taken of any rectification made to the age of civil servants after the first of March of the year 1943, whatever the nature or cause of the rectification, and whether issued through non-contentious jurisdiction or through contentious jurisdiction. The execution by the Administration of judgments issued after the said date shall be deemed null and of no effect. As for a civil servant who left the service and was subsequently reappointed or reinstated in the service, no account shall be taken save of his age as at the date of his first appointment. ' 3 - That he be free from diseases and infirmities that prevent him from performing the duties of the post for which he is a candidate. He must produce as proof thereof a certificate from the Official Medical Committee at the Ministry of Public Health. 4 - That he enjoy his civil rights and not have been convicted of a felony or an attempted felony of any kind whatsoever, or of an infamous misdemeanour, or of an attempted infamous misdemeanour. The following shall be deemed infamous misdemeanours: theft, fraud, breach of trust, drawing a cheque without funds, embezzlement, bribery, rape, blackmail, forgery, use of a forged document, false testimony, perjury, offences against public morals provided for in Title VII of the Penal Code, and offences relating to the cultivation of or trafficking in narcotic substances. These provisions shall apply to persons who have been rehabilitated or who have benefited from a general amnesty or a special pardon. 5 - That he not be debarred from entering the service pursuant to the provisions of the National Service Law in the event that he is subject to the obligations of the said Law. He must prove this by a certificate issued by the competent authorities. 6 - That he not have previously been removed or dismissed from a post or service in any public administration, public institution, autonomous agency, or municipality for a disciplinary reason, and that his service not have previously been terminated or ended on the basis of exceptional provisions. 7 - That he hold the required academic and practical certificates and qualifications. 8 - That he successfully pass the competitive examination or qualifying examination for appointment in all cases where passing the competitive examination or qualifying examination is required. Second: The special or additional conditions that must be met by applicants for its technical posts or certain of its administrative posts shall be determined in the regulations of each Ministry by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers after the approval of the Civil Service Board.

Procedure for Organising Competitive Examinations and Qualifying Examinations 1 - The Civil Service Board shall lay down the regulations for competitive examinations and qualifying examinations and their syllabuses after seeking the opinion of the competent ministries. These regulations may provide for the granting of bonus marks not exceeding ten per cent of the total marks obtained by candidates who hold qualifications higher than the minimum required, and civil servants who have ten years of service or more, provided that such marks are awarded, upon determining the order of merit, to the successful candidates, and the Civil Service shall also lay down the regulations for competitive entrance examinations to the National Institute of Administration and Development, and the regulations for competitive examinations and qualifying examinations for candidates for specialisation abroad. 2 - The Personnel Department at the Civil Service Board shall organise the competitive examinations and qualifying examinations, with the exception of the competitive entrance examinations to the National Institute of Administration and Development, and the selective competitive examinations and qualifying examinations aimed at dispatching civil servants who are in service and persons intended to be prepared for the public service abroad for specialisation, which fall within the competence of the Preparation and Training Department. Each of the two aforementioned departments, according to its competence, shall determine the dates and places of these competitive examinations and qualifying examinations and the period within which applications must be submitted, and shall also determine the final deadline for announcing the results, and shall announce the same on the Lebanese Radio and in at least three local daily newspapers. The period for submitting applications must not be less than fifteen days as of the date of the last announcement on the radio or in the daily newspapers. 3 - The Civil Service Board may decide to hold joint competitive examinations or qualifying examinations for similar posts within the same category across all administrations, or in some of them, and it may also decide to hold competitive examinations on the basis of credentials for technical posts in the Third Category. '' 4 - The Civil Service Board shall appoint the members of the examining committees, provided that they are civil servants, or non-civil servants who are specialists. 5 - The Civil Service Board shall draw up, upon the proposal of the Personnel Department or the Preparation and Training Department according to the competence of each, a list of the candidates who fulfil the conditions for participating in the competitive examination or qualifying examination. Its decision in this regard shall not be subject to any form of appeal, including an application for annulment for ultra vires. 6 - The competent administration shall seek the assistance, where necessary, in conducting the competitive examinations and qualifying examinations, of civil servants of public administrations and municipalities and employees of public institutions, and workers therein. 7 - The results of the competitive examination or qualifying examination shall be announced, immediately upon their completion and after their endorsement by the President of the Civil Service Board, on the door of the Board. The list of successful candidates shall remain valid for a period of one year only from the date of its announcement, and this list shall have priority over the one following it. The validity of the list of successful candidates shall lapse upon the expiry of the one-year period. 8 - The Civil Service Board may cancel the competitive examination or qualifying examination upon the proposal of the Personnel Department or the Preparation and Training Department according to competence. Provided that the cancellation decision must precede the announcement of the results, and shall be deemed null and void if taken thereafter.

Conditions for appointment in the Fifth, Fourth and Third Categories First: Conditions for appointment in the Fifth Category: The Civil Service Board shall determine appointment in the Fifth Category, provided that the provisions of Article Four of this Legislative Decree are observed therein with the exception of the certificate requirement, and that the appointment takes place pursuant to an examination organised by the Personnel Administration at the Civil Service Board. Second: Conditions for appointment in the Fourth Category: 1 - Every applicant for a post in the Fourth Category is required to pass the qualifying competitive examination therefor. 2 - A special competitive examination shall be held for each of the two ranks of the Fourth Category, and those wishing to participate in the qualifying competitive examination for the posts of the Second Rank must hold the Lebanese Baccalaureate Certificate, Part One, at least, or - its equivalent, or any other certificate decided by the Council of Ministers upon the recommendation of the President of the Civil Service Board and the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers, and stenographers, typists, telephone switchboard operators and applicants for other posts in which the scientific aspect prevails shall be exempted from the certificate, provided that these posts are determined by a decree upon the recommendation of the President of the Civil Service Board and the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers. 3 - Those wishing to participate in the qualifying competitive examination for the posts of the First Rank must hold the Lebanese Baccalaureate Certificate, Part Two - or its equivalent, or be among the employees of the Second Rank in the Fourth Category who have spent in this rank six years at least, whatever certificate they hold. '' Third: Conditions for appointment in the Third Category: 1 - A candidate for appointment to one of the posts of the Third Category for which the National Institute of Administration and Development prepares must be a graduate of the Superior Degree of the preparation branch at the Institute. These posts shall be determined by a decision of the Civil Service Board and shall be reserved for graduates of the National Institute of Administration and Development. 2 - A candidate for participation in the qualifying competitive examination for appointment to one of the posts of the Third Category for which the National Institute of Administration and Development does not prepare must hold a Licence in Lebanese Law or its equivalent. This certificate may be substituted, in respect of technical posts, with special or additional certificates and conditions determined in the regulations of each ministry by decrees taken in the Council of Ministers after the approval of the Civil Service Board. Fourth: Common provisions: 1 - An employee who has spent six years in a given rank is entitled to participate in the qualifying competitive examination for appointment to a post in the rank immediately above his rank in the same category, whatever certificates he holds. An employee who has spent ten years in a given category is also entitled to participate in the qualifying competitive examination for appointment to a post in the category immediately above his category, whatever certificates he holds. 2 - The provisions of Item (1) of this Article shall not apply to employees who are applicants for technical posts in which appointment requires holding a specific specialisation certificate.

Appointment in the Fifth, Fourth and Third Categories 1 - Civil servants of the Fifth, Fourth and Third Categories shall be appointed by decree following the approval of the Civil Service Board. 2 - The order of ranks of success in the competitive examination shall be observed in the appointment. 3 - Appointment shall be made to the last step of the rank or category in which the post falls. As for the civil servants referred to in Clause (1) of (Fourth) of Article (5) of this Legislative Decree, they shall be appointed to the last step of the rank to the category if its salary exceeds their salary, or to the step the salary of which equals their salary. They shall retain the right to seniority qualifying for advancement in step in the event of parity in salary.

Conditions for Appointment in the Second Category 1 - Vacant positions in the Second Category shall be filled by selection from among the civil servants of the first and second grades of the Third Category who have successfully completed a training course at the National Institute of Administration and Development and whose names have been entered on the promotion roster. They shall be classified in the last grade of the category. They shall retain their right to seniority qualifying for step advancement if they are classified at a salary equal to their original salary. Exemption from the requirement of the training course may be granted for exceptional reasons the assessment of which rests with the Board of the Civil Service Council, provided that the exemption is coupled with the approval of the Council of Ministers. 2 - Vacant technical positions in the Second Category may be filled by way of a competitive examination in which civil servants of the Third Category and candidates from outside the cadre are entitled to participate, provided that the regulations of the Ministry permit that or the Civil Service Council decides the matter. All candidates, whether they are civil servants or from outside the cadre, shall be required to be holders of university degrees the duration of study for which is not less than four years, and to be persons with experience in the type of work required in the competent administration. 3 - The Civil Service Council may decide to hold competitive examinations on the basis of credentials for technical posts in the Second Category. 4 - The provisions of Article (6) and item (2) of Article (7) of this Legislative Decree shall apply to the competitive examination referred to in the preceding paragraph of this Article.

Appointment in the Second Category 1 - Civil servants of the Second Category shall be appointed by decree after the approval of the Civil Service Council. They shall be deemed confirmed immediately upon their appointment. 2 - Appointment shall take place in the last grade of the category if the candidate is outside the cadre. If the candidate is a civil servant, he shall be appointed in the last grade if its salary exceeds his salary, or in the grade the salary of which equals his salary. The civil servant shall retain his right to seniority qualifying for step advancement in his previous post unless his appointment results in an increase in his salary of not less than one grade.

Conditions of probation in the Fifth, Fourth, and Third Categories 1 - Those appointed in each of the Fifth, Fourth, and Third Categories shall remain probationers for a period of one year in the grade to which they were appointed. 2 - Each Ministry shall undertake the training of the probationers subordinate to it in accordance with the general principles determined by the Preparation and Training Administration in the Civil Service Board. 3 - Probationers shall be confirmed in appointment by a decision of the Minister after the approval of the Civil Service Board. The effect of the confirmation shall be deemed valid starting from the date of expiry of the probation period referred to in Clause (1) of this Article. 4 - The authority vested with the right to appoint them shall dismiss the probationers, before the expiry of their probation period or at its end, after an investigation conducted by the Central Inspection and the approval of the Civil Service Board. In this case, no dismissal indemnity shall be due to the probationer for the period he spent in service. The effect of the dismissal shall be deemed valid starting from the date of his notification thereof, or from the date of actual cessation of work if that occurred before the notification. '' However, if the appointment of the probationer took place by way of transferring him from another position, the authority vested with the right of appointment may, after an investigation conducted by the Central Inspection and the approval of the Civil Service Board, return him, before the expiry of the probation period or at its end, to his previous position, and his status shall be reconstituted with respect to his salary as he remained in this position. 5 - If the competent authority does not decide, within one month from the expiry of the probation period, to confirm the probationer, or to dismiss him, or to return him to his previous position if he was from among the civil servants, the probationer must request his confirmation within a time limit of another month, and must send a copy of his request directly to the Civil Service Board. If the administration does not decide upon the request within a time limit of one month from the date of its submission, the Civil Service Board must decide that, and its decisions on this matter shall be deemed final. 6 - The probation period shall be included in the count of the years of actual service.

Conditions of Appointment to Category One 1 - Vacant positions in Category One shall be filled by selection from among the employees of the top three grades of Category Two whose names are listed on the promotion roster. 2 - Exceptionally, persons from outside the cadre may be appointed to Category One, provided that they meet the general conditions of employment and hold university degrees for which the duration of study is not less than four years. The number of appointees from outside the cadre may not, at any time whatsoever, exceed the ratio of one-third of the number of Category One positions in the public administrations, with the exception of Category One positions in the Foreign Service, appointment to which shall remain subject to the special provisions governing them. For the purpose of applying the provisions of item 2 of this Article, the calculation of the number of Category One employees appointed from outside the cadre shall commence as of the first of January 1983, and all Category One employees appointed prior to this date shall be deemed to be from within the cadre. 3 - All special and additional conditions imposed for appointment to Category One positions in the public administrations are hereby repealed wherever they appear, and appointment to these positions shall remain subject to the provisions of this Article of this Legislative Decree, and Category One positions in the public administrations, to whichever cadre or service they belong in whichever ministry or wherever they are found, shall constitute a single service, with the exception of positions in the Foreign Service.

Appointment to Category One 1 - Category One employees shall be appointed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers after consulting the opinion of the Civil Service Board. They shall be deemed confirmed immediately upon their appointment. 2 - The provisions of item (2) of Article (10) of this Legislative Decree shall apply to those appointed to Category One.

Effect and Consequences of Appointment 1 - No one shall be appointed save to a vacant post in the establishment for which a specific appropriation is allocated in the budget, and in accordance with the procedures prescribed by law. 2 - Appointment shall be made to the lowest step of the grade or category, save in the cases where the law provides otherwise. 3 - The appointment shall take effect from the date of assumption of duties. It may not have any retroactive effect. 4 - Instruments of appointment shall be notified to the Civil Service Board, the Court of Audit, the Ministry of Finance, and the competent ministry. 5 - If the appointment is made to a post that is not vacant in the establishment or to a post for which no specific appropriation has been allocated in the budget, both the liquidator and the authorising officer shall be prohibited from liquidating and authorising the payment of the expenditure arising therefrom, even if they receive a written order to that effect. The authorising officer shall notify the matter to the Minister of Finance, the Civil Service Board, and the Court of Audit in order to take steps to annul the instrument of appointment. 6 - If the appointment is contrary to the legal rules and procedures, it shall be deemed ineffective and the administration shall be entitled to revoke it at any time, and no vested right shall accrue to the person concerned as a result thereof.

Conditions of entitlement to salary 1 - A new employee shall be entitled to the salary with effect from the date on which he commences work. However, if the seat of the post is outside Lebanon, the employee shall be entitled to his salary from the date on which he leaves Lebanese territory for the seat of his post pursuant to the instructions given to him, unless he has been temporarily retained in the central departments by a decision of the Minister to perform a specific work during a period not exceeding two months, in which case he shall be entitled to the salary with effect from the date on which he commences such work. 2 - A promoted employee shall be entitled to the new salary with effect from the first day of the month following the month in which the promotion took place. 3 - An employee advanced from one rank to another or from one category to another shall be entitled to the new salary with effect from the date of issuance of the instrument providing for his advancement. 4 - An employee sentenced to reduction of category, rank, or grade shall be entitled to the new salary with effect from the date on which the judgment becomes final.

Cases in which half the salary is paid 1 - An employee suspended from work or referred to the Supreme Disciplinary Board, whether or not he has been temporarily relieved of his duties, shall receive half his salary with effect from the day following his notification of the decree or decision providing for his suspension from work or his referral to the Supreme Disciplinary Board, or with effect from the date of his actual cessation of work if he had ceased work prior to being notified of the decree or decision. The other half shall not be paid to him unless the Supreme Disciplinary Board acquits him, or imposes upon him a penalty of the first degree at most, or if the Administration reverses its decision to refer him to the Supreme Disciplinary Board after the lapse of fifteen days from the date of his suspension from work. The withholding of half the salary of an employee referred to the Supreme Disciplinary Board may not continue for a period exceeding four months. 2 - An employee held in judicial custody on remand shall receive half his salary. The other half shall not be paid to him unless prosecution against him is barred, or he is acquitted, or he is sentenced to a penalty other than imprisonment.

Article 14: General duties of the civil servant It is incumbent upon the civil servant in general: 1 - To be guided in his work by the public interest alone, and to apply the laws and regulations in force with complete impartiality, integrity and neutrality, without any transgression, violation or negligence. 2 - To personally bear the responsibility for executing the tasks entrusted to him. 3 - To personally bear the responsibility for the orders and instructions that he gives to his subordinates. 4 - To execute with precision the orders of his direct superior and his instructions relating to the office unless these orders and instructions are in breach of the law in an explicit and clear manner. In this case, the civil servant must draw the attention of his superior in writing to the occurring violation, and he shall not be bound to execute his these orders and instructions. The subordinate shall be deemed responsible in the event of executing them. If the superior insists on these orders and instructions, the subordinate must refer the dispute through the administrative hierarchy to the Minister for a final decision thereon. However, if the dispute is between the Minister and the Director General, the Minister shall submit the dispute to the Council of Ministers, after seeking the opinion of the Civil Service Board, for a final decision thereon. In any event, the superior and the subordinate must directly communicate a copy of the correspondence to the Service Board and the Central Inspection. 5 - To abide by the official working hours and respect the times of work and devote them to the performance of the duties of his office, and to complete the transactions of stakeholders with speed, precision and fidelity within the limits of his competence. 6 - To preserve the interests of the State and its properties, funds and documents, and not to relinquish any right of its rights. 7 - To preserve the dignity of the office and conduct himself in a manner befitting it during office and outside it.

8 - To engage in political matters while holding a leadership position in any of the federations, associations, clubs or councils whatever the nature of their activity may be, or to nominate himself for a position in the aforementioned bodies. 9 - To engage in political matters while combining his office with the presidency or membership of confessional, Sharia or sectarian councils or similar councils and bodies. Or to exercise any activities within these councils and bodies if these activities have a political character. 10 - To solicit or accept any recommendation, or to solicit or accept directly or through an intermediary, by reason of the office which he occupies, gifts, gratuities or grants of any kind whatsoever. 11 - To perform any remunerated work that demeans the dignity of the office or has a connection with it. 12 - To combine his office with any other unremunerated work, if that is likely to demean the dignity of the office. 13 - To deliver or publish without written permission from the competent Minister in writing or articles or statements or publications in all affairs. 14 - To divulge official information of which he became aware during the performance of his office, even after the end of his period of service, unless the competent Minister authorises him to do so.

Article 15: Prohibited acts It is prohibited for a civil servant to perform any act forbidden by the laws and regulations in force, and in particular: 1 - To engage in political affairs, join political parties, or wear the emblem of any party. 2 - To join professional organisations or syndicates. 3 - To go on strike from work or incite others to strike. 4 - To organise or incite the organisation of collective petitions relating to the office, or participate in organising them, whatever the reasons and motives may be. 5 - To practise any commercial or industrial profession or any other remunerated profession or trade, with the exception of teaching at an institute of higher education or a secondary education school under conditions determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the recommendation of the President of the Civil Service Council and the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers. Teaching may also be prohibited in the same manner. 6 - To be a member of the board of directors of a joint-stock company or a partnership limited by shares, or to have a direct material interest, or an interest through a third party, in an enterprise subject to his supervision or to the supervision of the administration to which he belongs. 7 - To combine his office with parliamentary, municipal, or mukhtar elective offices, as set forth in the special laws governing such offices.

Article 16: General provisions 1 - Each grade shall have a salary determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the recommendation of the President of the Civil Service Council and the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers. 2 - Salaries and their accessories shall be liquidated monthly when they fall due. All months, without exception, shall be calculated as thirty days starting from the first day thereof. 3 - No advance on salaries may be made before they fall due. 4 - No person may receive the salary of an office unless he is legally appointed thereto and is actually performing the duties thereof, subject to the special cases provided for by law. Immediate superiors shall be held personally liable out of their own funds for the payment of the salaries of civil servants who do not actually perform the duties of their offices. 5 - No person may combine two salaries, or a salary and any other allowance or remuneration, unless expressly permitted by law.

Cases in which salary is withheld 1 - Salary shall be withheld from a civil servant placed outside the cadre or on availability at his own request or at the request of the administration, and from a civil servant suspended from work by a decision of the Higher Disciplinary Board or dismissed from service, or placed on retirement, or future, or removed from office, effective from the day following the date on which he is notified of the decree or decision, or since the date of his actual cessation of work if this occurred before notification was effected. 2 - Salary shall be withheld from a diplomatic or consular civil servant serving abroad, in the cases referred to in the preceding paragraph, commencing from the date of his return to Lebanon, provided that he returns within a period of one month from the date of his notification of the decree or decision. This period may be extended for a second month by a decision of the Minister. 3 - Salary shall be withheld from a civil servant who is deemed to have resigned, commencing from the day on which he ought to have returned to his post. 4 - Salary shall be withheld from a civil servant who reaches the statutory age for termination of service effective from the day following his attainment of this age, even if no instrument has been issued providing for his removal from service. '' 5 - Salary shall be withheld from a civil servant who ceases his work before being notified of the instrument providing for his placement or the renewal of his placement outside the cadre or on secondment or on availability or for his assignment to an official mission outside Lebanese territory throughout the duration of such cessation. The duration of cessation shall not be counted as part of his actual service. 6 - The Government may, in exceptional circumstances and cases the assessment of which rests with it, take certain special measures relating to the withholding of the salaries of civil servants, the wages of wage-earners, and the allowances of contractors and all other persons working in public sector administrations, whether wholly or at varying rates. These measures shall be implemented by a decision taken in the Council of Ministers.

Compensation for Overtime Work 1 - Civil servants may be granted compensation for overtime working hours that exceed their official working hours in the following cases: a - If the regulations applied in their department require them to work continuously during official working hours and outside them. b - If they are assigned overtime work that does not fall within the duties entrusted to them by virtue of their post. c - If they are assigned overtime work that falls within the duties entrusted to them by virtue of their post, provided that the work is urgent and must be performed by the civil servants themselves. 2 - Subject to the provisions of Article 125 of this Legislative Decree, entitlement to compensation for overtime work in each of the cases set out in item (1) of this Article shall be conditional upon the assignment of the overtime work being made by a decision of the Minister, or of the Director General after the approval of the Civil Service Board, prior to the commencement of the work. The decision shall specify the name of the civil servant and his post, the nature of the work he is assigned to perform, the times of its performance and the duration of the assignment. 3 - In the case provided for in paragraph (a) of item (1) of this Article, each administration that applies overtime work shall lay down special regulations specifying the procedures and rules it adopts for carrying out the overtime work; the regulations shall be specified by a decision of the competent Minister after the approval of the Civil Service Board. '' 4 - The Central Inspection shall undertake the supervision of overtime work and verify its performance in accordance with the rules. 5 - The rate of compensation for each hour of overtime work shall be determined pursuant to a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the recommendation of the President of the Civil Service Board and the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers. 6 - Compensation for overtime work shall be disbursed pursuant to a decision issued by the authority that issued the assignment decision, within the appropriations allocated for this purpose in special items of the budget. 7 - Civil servants may be granted a lump-sum monthly compensation for overtime work assigned to them outside official working hours, provided that the execution of such work requires a period of not less than six months, that the compensation does not exceed half of the salary, and that it is decided by a decree after the approval of the Civil Service Board, within the limits of the appropriations allocated in special items of the budget.

Special Cases 1 - An employee transferred to a post located outside his place of residence shall be entitled to continue receiving his salaries without interruption, provided that he complies with the written instructions issued by his superiors regarding his travel. 2 - An employee shall not receive a salary for the period he spends in prison in execution of a judicial sentence, unless he is convicted of an unintentional misdemeanour. 3 - If an employee disappears, or news of him is cut off as a result of an act related to the post, his salaries shall be paid to the beneficiaries provided for in the Retirement Law for a period of one year at most, and his service shall be deemed terminated after the expiry of the year, and the rights of his family members shall be provisionally liquidated in accordance with the provisions of the law. 4 - If an employee whose service has terminated is required to carry out the handover and takeover procedure, he shall receive an allowance equivalent to his salary with his allowances for the period he spends in carrying out the handover and takeover operation, provided that the allowance shall not in any case exceed the salary of one month with its allowances. The value of this allowance shall be determined by a decision of the competent minister, and shall be disbursed from the salaries item.

The monthly family allowance shall be determined as follows

- For the spouse: 20% of the minimum wage applied in public administrations.

- For each dependent child: 11% of the minimum wage mentioned above, provided that the amount of the allowance for the children does not exceed 55% thereof.

Special Allowance 1 - The Government may, in circumstances and cases left to its discretion, grant a special allowance to permanent employees or abolish it. 2 - In the event of granting the special allowance referred to in item (1) of this Article, the categories of employees who benefit from this allowance, its value and the conditions for benefiting therefrom shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the recommendation of the President of the Civil Service Board and the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers.

Article Thirty: Advancement in Step 1 - Every civil servant who has spent twenty-four months in a single step or in a step equivalent thereto since the date of commencing work after his appointment or the date of obtaining an increase in his salary of not less than one step shall acquire, by operation of law, one step within the category or rank. 2 - The Minister may, upon the proposal of the Director General or the President of the Central Inspection, defer the due date of the civil servant's advancement in step for a period of six months at most if it is established that he has committed a grave breach of his duties. This measure may not be taken except after seeking the opinion of the Civil Service Board. 3 - a - When the civil servant exceeds the ceiling in his category, he shall benefit every twenty-four months, by operation of law and in accordance with the provisions governing advancement in step, from an increase in his salary equivalent to one step of the steps of the corps to which he belongs. b - After the civil servant has benefited from six steps above the ceiling of his category in accordance with the provisions of paragraph (1) of this item, he shall benefit every three years, by operation of law and in accordance with the provisions governing advancement in step, from an increase in his salary equivalent to one step of the steps of the corps to which he belongs. c - As for a civil servant belonging to one of the special or technical cadres in the various public administrations, who has reached the ceiling in the highest category in his cadre, the increase from which he benefits in accordance with the provisions of paragraphs (a) and (b) of this item shall be equivalent to the value of the step parallel to his salary in the general administrative cadre. d - This increase shall be counted as part of the base salary. 4 - A civil servant benefiting from the provisions of item (3) of this Article shall remain in his category or rank, and he may benefit from the provisions of Article 31 of this Legislative Decree. 5 - Only the period of actual service for which the civil servant received a full salary shall be included in the calculation of the period of advancement in step.

Subsistence Allowance and Transport Fares 1 - Subject to the provisions of Article 125 of this Legislative Decree, employees traveling outside their duty station by reason of their function shall receive a daily subsistence allowance whose value and conditions shall be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the recommendation of the President of the Civil Service Board and the proposal of the Prime Minister. 2 - The daily subsistence allowance may be replaced by a lump-sum monthly allowance whose amount shall be determined by a decree after the approval of the Civil Service Board and allocated to an employee who is compelled by virtue of his function to travel frequently, provided that its rate does not exceed the rate specified for the daily allowance. 3 - The State shall provide means of transport for employees who travel outside their duty station by reason of their function, or reimburse them for the transport fares they incurred on the occasion of a mission officially assigned to them, under conditions determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the recommendation of the President of the Civil Service Board and the proposal of the Prime Minister. The State is not obliged to compensate for damages caused to means of transport of whatever kind. 4 - The payment of daily transport fares may be replaced by a lump-sum monthly allowance whose amount shall be determined by a decree after the approval of the Civil Service Board. It shall be allocated to an employee who is compelled by virtue of his function to commute continuously outside his duty station within the Governorate. 5 - An employee may be granted an advance on the subsistence allowance and transport fares that may accrue to him.

1 - An employee may be granted a full-time responsibility allowance, or a lump-sum allowance, or a car allowance, or a representation allowance, or a night-hours allowance, or an expatriation allowance, or a housing allowance, or an allowance to cover expenses incurred by him on the occasion of a public mission assigned to him, or an allowance for the completion of a mission or work, or other allowances provided for by law. 2 - The categories of employees who benefit from the allowances mentioned in Item (1) of this Article, and the value and conditions of these allowances, shall be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the recommendation of the President of the Civil Service Board and the proposal of the Prime Minister. Unless a legal provision states otherwise.

Cash Rewards Subject to the provisions of Article 125 of this Legislative Decree, an employee who performs a specific work warranting appreciation may be granted a cash reward determined by a decision of the Minister after the approval of the Civil Service Board and within the appropriations allocated for this purpose in special items of the budget, provided that the decision states the works that warranted the reward.

Promotion 1 - Promotion is the transfer of the employee within a single cadre from rank to rank within the same category, or is the transfer of the employee from the Third Category to the Second or from the Second Category to the First. 2 - Subject to the provisions of Clause (3) of this Article, the employee shall not be promoted from rank to rank unless he is in the first step in his rank and his name is listed in the promotion roster. 3 - Engineers shall be promoted from rank to rank if they are in the upper three steps in their rank and their name is listed in the promotion roster. 4 - Each administration shall draw up a promotion roster and send it to the Civil Service Board before the first of October of each year and include in it the names of the employees whom it nominates for transfer from rank to rank in a single category, or from the Third Category to the Second and from the Second Category to the First, and attach the explanatory reasons to the roster. And the Civil Service Board, upon the proposal of the Personnel Administration, shall decide finally on this roster before the end of or January, and if it does not take its decision within the specified deadline, the roster shall be deemed effective as received from the competent administration.

Administrative Leaves 1 - The employee shall have the right to benefit from an annual administrative leave at full salary for a duration of twenty days of actual work. Exempted therefrom are the employees who benefit from judicial and school vacations. 2 - The employee shall not benefit from the administrative leave for the first year of his appointment. 3 - Each administrative one shall schedule the dates of leaves for the employees subordinate to it in a manner that guarantees the continuity of work therein. And there must be mentioned in the leave decision the name of the employee who replaces the employee on leave and exercises all his powers and responsibilities, provided that he is of the same category unless that is impracticable. 4 - The employee shall inevitably benefit each year from his administrative leave. However, leaves may exceptionally accumulate year by year, for a maximum duration of three years, by a reasoned decision of the authority to which the right to grant the leave belongs. The administrative leave for each year shall fall due at the beginning thereof and the leave of the first year shall lapse ipso jure upon entering the fourth year, and it shall not be permissible, for any consideration whatsoever, to pay compensation for the administrative leaves from which the employee benefits. 5 - Administrative leaves shall lapse ipso jure for the employee placed outside the cadre or on secondment or on availability or whose service is terminated for any reason whatsoever.

Maximum limit of allowances 1 - Subject to the provisions of items (2) and (3) of this Article, and notwithstanding any previous text, the total of allowances and wages of whatever kind, rewards, proceeds, endeavours and amounts received by a civil servant by virtue of the exercise of his office, whatever the cadre or corps to which he belongs, including judges, military personnel, university professors and members of the teaching staff, from the State budget or from the budgets of public and private institutions and autonomous agencies, municipalities, Lebanese mixed-economy companies, and recovered utilities and installations, during a single financial year, shall not exceed seventy-five per cent of the total of his monthly salaries in that same year. 2 - There shall not be included in the calculation of the maximum limit of allowances provided for in item (1) of this Article: travel allowances, transport fares, family allowances, representation allowance, car allowance and housing allowance. 3 - The provisions of item (1) of this Article shall not apply to diplomatic and consular civil servants or to military and technical attachés actually serving abroad. Nor shall they apply to all physicians of Cadre (B) in the Ministry of Public Health.

Material losses 1 - A civil servant may be granted compensation for a material loss incurred during the performance of an official mission, if it resulted from circumstances of force majeure to which he was exposed by reason of the office. 2 - Compensation shall not be granted if the loss occurred by reason of the civil servant's negligence or a fault committed by him. 3 - The injured civil servant must submit an application for compensation within fifteen days from the date of occurrence of the damage. If circumstances of force majeure prevent the submission of the application within this time limit, it must be submitted immediately upon the cessation of those circumstances. The civil servant's right to compensation shall lapse if he does not comply with these conditions. 4 - Compensation shall be granted by decree upon the opinion of a committee appointed by the competent Minister consisting of a representative of his ministry, a representative of the Ministry of Finance, and a representative of the Central Inspection. The committee shall conduct its investigations by all means it deems fit.

Assistance, grants and other benefits A civil servant shall benefit from sickness and family assistance, grants and other benefits prescribed in the Regulations on Benefits and Services in the Civil Servants' Cooperative, in accordance with the provisions of the said Regulations.
