Promotion 1 - Promotion shall advance the due date of step advancement by six months. 2 - Every administration shall send to the Civil Service Board before the end of the month of June of each year a list of the names of the employees whom it proposes to promote, provided that their number does not exceed ten per cent of the total employees of the administration whose step advancement falls due in the following financial year, and that this number is distributed, as far as possible, among the various categories and ranks according to percentage. 3 - The list shall be accompanied by a statement of the grades and the explanatory reasons for promotion in accordance with the forms established by the Personnel Administration at the Civil Service Board. 4 - The Personnel Administration shall take a decision before the end of the month of October of each year on the lists received by it. 5 - The Personnel Administration, after the endorsement of the President of the Board, may approve the lists or reject them in whole or in part. Whatever it approves shall be deemed effective, and whatever it rejects shall be returned to the competent administration with a statement of the explanatory reasons for the rejection. The competent administration may submit before the end of the month of November new proposals or statements supporting its previous proposals. The Civil Service Board shall take the final decision regarding these proposals and statements before the end of the month of December. If it does not take a decision by this deadline, the proposals and statements shall be deemed effective as received by it. 6 - The promotion shall take effect starting from the date specified therefor in the decision of the Personnel Administration after its endorsement or the decision of the Civil Service Board, or on the date specified therefor in the lists and statements received from the administrations if the Board does not take a decision by the specified deadline. 7 - If it is not possible to disburse the expenditure resulting from the promotions from the appropriations allocated therefor in the budget, it shall be disbursed from the savings realised in the salary appropriations.

Family Leave: An employee shall be entitled, in addition to his administrative leave, to be absent with permission and on full salary: - for a period of one week at most in the event of his marriage, or upon the death of his spouse or one of his parents or children. - for a period of three days at most in the event of the death of one of his grandparents, grandchildren, brothers or sisters.

Special Leave Without Pay: 1 - An employee may be granted, for private reasons and at his request, special leave without pay not exceeding three months, which may be extended for another three months, provided that the total special leaves do not exceed six months during five consecutive years and that the granting of the leave does not affect the continuity of work in the administration. 2 - An employee may not, during the period of special leave without pay, request to benefit from any other leave. 3 - An employee is prohibited, during the period of special leave without pay, from engaging in any work prohibited by special laws and regulations, in particular the acts prohibited pursuant to Article 15 of this Legislative Decree.

Maternity Leave: 1 - A pregnant female employee shall be granted maternity leave on full salary for a maximum period of seventy days. Maternity leave shall not be included in the calculation of administrative leaves nor in the calculation of sick leaves. 2 - Maternity leave shall be granted all at once without division when the applicant therefor is about to give birth, and the leave shall terminate ipso jure upon the expiry of forty days from the date of delivery. 3 - In order to be granted maternity leave, the female employee must submit an application containing: a - The approximate date of delivery according to the physician's report. b - The start date of the leave. 4 - If the absence of the female employee benefiting from maternity leave exceeds thirty days prior to the date of delivery, or forty days after the date of delivery, the excess period shall, in both cases, be deemed an absence for which the corresponding amount shall be deducted from her salaries and shall not be counted in her actual service. 5 - A female employee shall not be entitled, during the period of maternity leave, to request to benefit from sick leave, nor shall she be entitled to divide the maternity leave.

The Authority Vested with the Right to Grant Leave 1 - Administrative leave regardless of its duration, family leave, maternity leave, and sick leave not exceeding one month in duration shall be granted by a decision of the head of the administration directly subordinate to the Minister. Such leave shall be granted by a decision of the Minister with respect to the head of the said administration. 2 - Sick leave exceeding one month in duration, and leave without pay, shall be granted by a decision of the Minister, upon the proposal of the competent head of administration.

Transfer from One Corps to Another 1 - A civil servant may be transferred from one corps to another if he meets the conditions for appointment in the corps to which he is sought to be transferred, including the condition of a competitive examination or test. 2 - The transfer shall be effected by decree upon the proposal of the Minister to whose ministry the transfer takes place and after the approval of the Civil Service Board. 3 - It shall be a condition for the transfer that the post to which the civil servant is sought to be transferred be vacant in the establishment and have a special appropriation allocated to it in the budget. 4 - The transferred civil servant shall retain the seniority qualifying for step advancement acquired in his previous corps, unless his transfer results in an increase in his salary of not less than one step.

Transfer within the Same Corps from One Administration to Another 1 - A civil servant may be transferred from one post to another within the same corps, whether from one ministry to another or from one administration to another within the same ministry. 2 - The transfer shall be effected: a - By a decree taken in the Council of Ministers after consulting the opinion of the Civil Service Board, for civil servants of the First Category. b - By a decree upon the proposal of the Minister to whose ministry the transfer takes place, after the approval of the Civil Service Board for civil servants of the other categories. 3 - The conditions provided for in items (3) and (4) of Article (39) of this Legislative Decree shall apply to transfer within the same corps. 4 - The transfer must be based on considerations derived from the interest of the service

Sick Leaves 1 - A civil servant who is absent for health reasons shall be granted sick leave on full salary for a period not exceeding nine months within one year or eighteen months within five consecutive years. The period of one year, or the period of five years, shall be calculated from the date of the commencement of the absence for health reasons back to the corresponding date one year prior, or five years prior, as the case may be. 2 - A civil servant who is absent for health reasons must immediately notify his direct superior on the first day of his absence of his current address and of the reasons necessitating the absence, and must send to him, during the period of absence, a medical report stating the nature of the illness and specifying the approximate duration of the absence. 3 - If the duration of the absence exceeds ten days, the superior must request the Ministry of Public Health to assign a physician to examine the absent civil servant and draw up a report on him. In this case, sick leave shall only be granted on the basis of the opinion of the examining physician. 4 - If the absence exceeds one uninterrupted month, or one month over several intervals within three months, leave on full salary shall only be granted on the basis of the opinion of the Official Medical Committee and for a period not exceeding three renewable months, subject to the provisions of Clause (1) of this Article. The Medical Committee shall be composed of three physicians in each Governorate, appointed by a decision of the Minister of Public Health. A reserve panel of three other physicians shall be appointed in the same decision. The civil servant may, if he so wishes, be assisted when appearing before it by a physician of his choice. If he is unable to travel, the Committee shall travel to the place of his presence at the expense of the Administration. The Medical Committee shall set out its opinion in a written report stating the nature of the illness and specifying the approximate duration of the absence. '' 5 - If the absence exceeds a period of nine months within one year or eighteen months within five consecutive years, the Administration must refer the civil servant to the Medical Committee to consider the likelihood of his recovery within a period of two years. If the civil servant is curable within this period, he shall be granted sick leave on half salary for a period of one year at most starting from the date of expiry of the sick leaves on full salary, and shall then be placed on availability without salary for one further year. Thereafter, he shall only be reinstated to his work on the basis of the opinion of the Medical Committee. If the civil servant is not curable within a period of two years, or if the Medical Committee deems during or at the end of this period that he is unable to resume his work, his service shall be terminated in accordance with the laws and regulations in force. 6 - A civil servant residing outside Lebanon by virtue of his office, or legally absent therefrom, shall be entitled to obtain sick leave or request the extension of a previous sick leave, within the limits referred to in the preceding clauses of this Article, on the basis of medical reports certified by the head of the Lebanese diplomatic or consular mission or certified by the local health departments where there is no Lebanese mission. Before certifying such reports, the head of the mission may assign one or more physicians to examine the civil servant to verify his health condition and draw up a report on him. However, if the civil servant has exhausted the sick leaves on full salary, the medical report shall not be accepted unless it is issued by a medical committee of three physicians chosen by the head of the mission, or by a local medical committee also of three physicians where there is no Lebanese mission. 7 - For the purpose of applying the provisions of Clause (6) of this Article, the absence of a civil servant benefiting from special leave without salary, family leave, maternity leave, or sick leave shall not be considered a legal absence from Lebanon unless the sick leave was granted for treatment abroad in accordance with the rules. 8 - If the civil servant violates the provisions imposed upon him pursuant to this Article in order to obtain sick leave, his absence shall ipso facto be considered an unlawful absence and the legal provisions in force shall be applied to him; the amount corresponding to this absence shall also be deducted from his salary, and its duration shall not be counted as part of his actual service. This shall not preclude the disciplinary prosecution of the civil servant.

Transfer within the same corps and the same administration 1 - An employee may be transferred from one post to another within the same corps and the same administration. 2 - The transfer shall be effected: a - By a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, for employees of the First Category. b - By a decree upon the proposal of the competent Minister for employees of the Third Category. c - By a decision of the competent Minister for employees of the Third Category. d - By a decision of the competent head of administration directly linked to the Minister, for employees of the Fourth and Fifth Categories. 3 - The conditions provided for in items (3) and (4) of Article 39 of this Legislative Decree shall apply to transfer within the same corps and the same administration. 4 - The transfer must be based on considerations derived from the interest of the service. 5 - Transfer within the same corps and the same administration shall be subject to seeking the opinion of the Civil Service Board in respect of employees of all categories, including the appointment, transfer or assignment of school principals and their supervisors in all stages and types of education, with the exception of decisions transferring members of the teaching staff in all stages and types of education, which shall be notified to the Civil Service Board within fifteen days from the date of their issuance in order to exercise oversight thereon.
Definition of acting capacity Acting capacity is the temporary assignment of an employee to occupy a post other than his original post.

Conditions for appointing an acting official 1 - An acting official may only be appointed to a vacant post or to a post whose incumbent is absent. 2 - The acting official must be from the corps of the incumbent. If that is not possible, he may be appointed from another corps. 3 - The acting official must fulfil the conditions prescribed for appointment to the vacant post or the post whose incumbent is absent, with the exception of the conditions of age and competitive examination. 4 - An acting official may not be appointed for a period exceeding one year, which may be renewed in the same manner. 5 - The acting official shall be appointed by the authority that appoints the incumbent, following the approval of the Civil Service Board. It may temporarily exempt him from the duties of his original post or retain him therein.

Cases of exemption By a decree taken in the Council of Ministers, a civil servant of the First Category may be exempted from the duties of his post in order to perform one of the duties specified below, and his post in this case shall be deemed vacant: 1 - The presidency or membership of the board of directors of a major public institution. 2 - The post of director general or director of a public institution. 3 - Placement at the disposal of the Prime Minister or one of the Ministers for a period of a period of two years.

Rights of the exempted civil servant 1 - The exempted civil servant shall retain his grade and salary in his previous post, and shall continue to advance in step in accordance with the salary scale pertaining to that post and the provisions relating thereto, and shall also continue to benefit from all other benefits and services from which civil servants of the First Category benefit in general, with the exception of those specifically designated for his previous post, from the authority whose duties he is performing or at whose disposal he is placed. 2 - If the civil servant placed at disposal is not entrusted with one of the duties specified in items 1 and 2 of Article 48 of this Legislative Decree, or is not returned to a post of the First Category, within a period of two years, he shall be offered upon the expiry of the two-year period a post of the Second Category in the public administrations. If he accepts it, he shall retain his salary, and if he does not accept it, his service shall be terminated and his rights to a retirement pension or dismissal indemnity shall be liquidated in accordance with the legislation in force. 3 - If the authority at whose disposal the civil servant is placed does not proceed to take the measures provided for in item (2) of this Article within the two-year time limit, the service of the civil servant shall be deemed terminated ipso jure upon the expiry of the said time limit without the need to issue any instrument to that effect. The civil servant shall thereupon benefit from his full right to a retirement pension or dismissal indemnity in accordance with the legislation in force. 4 - The civil servant placed at disposal shall have the right, at any time, to request the termination of his service by a letter which he submits to the authority at whose disposal he is placed. If no decision is taken on this request within a time limit of one month from the date of its submission, it shall be deemed accepted ipso jure without the need to issue any instrument to that effect. The civil servant shall thereupon benefit from his full right to a retirement pension or dismissal indemnity in accordance with the legislation in force, and from an additional sum equivalent to his basic salary with the family allowance only for six months, to be disbursed from the salary appropriations.

Rights and Duties of the Acting Official 1 - The acting official shall exercise all the powers of the incumbent and shall be bound to perform all his responsibilities and duties. 2 - The acting official shall have no acquired right to appointment to the post that he occupies in an acting capacity. 3 - The acting official shall receive the permanent allowances allocated to the post that he occupies in an acting capacity. Where permanent allowances are allocated to him in his original post, he shall receive the higher allowance. 4 - The acting official shall receive an acting allowance equivalent to three steps of the salary scale of the post to which he is appointed in an acting capacity. The allowance shall fall due by operation of law, even if not expressly mentioned in the instrument of appointment. 5 - The acting allowance shall be disbursed from the appropriations allocated to salaries or from the appropriations allocated to miscellaneous allowances. 6 - A civil servant who is appointed as an acting official outside his place of residence shall receive the travel allowance provided for in Article (24) of this Legislative Decree. 7 - The allowances set forth in this Article shall not fall due unless the civil servant is appointed in an acting capacity in accordance with the legal procedures provided for in this Article.

Definition of Secondment Secondment is the temporary exemption of a civil servant from the duties of his original post and the assignment of another mission to him. Secondment may not lead to appointment to a post in the establishment of the administration to which the civil servant is seconded, unless the law provides otherwise.

Cases in Which Secondment is Permissible 1 - A civil servant may be seconded to specialise in one of the branches in which the administration requires new specialists. The conditions of secondment for specialisation shall be laid down by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the recommendation of the President of the Civil Service Board and the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers. 2 - A civil servant may be seconded from one administration to another within the same ministry, and from one ministry to another following the approval of the two competent ministries, for a period of one year renewable twice. 3 - Secondment shall be decided by the authority vested with the power of appointment following the approval of the Civil Service Board.

Status of the Seconded Civil Servant 1 - The seconded civil servant shall receive his salary and allowances from the administration to which he is seconded and shall retain his right to step advancement, promotion and grade advancement in his original administration. The period of secondment shall be included in the calculation of the retirement pension or severance indemnity. 2 - From a disciplinary standpoint, the seconded civil servant shall be subject to the administration to which he is seconded. 3 - The post of the seconded civil servant shall remain vacant in the establishment of his original administration, and he shall return to it immediately upon the expiry of the period of secondment.

Conditions of Placement on Non-Active Status An employee may be placed on non-active status ex officio, or upon his request, or upon the request of the Administration. First: Placing the employee on non-active status ex officio: 1 - An employee of the Second Category and below may, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, be placed on non-active status ex officio, upon the proposal of the competent Minister and after the approval of the Civil Service Board. His post shall, in this case, be considered vacant. 2 - The duration of placement on non-active status ex officio may not exceed one non-renewable year. 3 - An employee placed on non-active status ex officio shall retain his rank in his former post, and shall continue to advance in step in accordance with the salary scale pertaining to that post and the provisions relating thereto, and shall also continue to benefit from all other benefits and services from which employees of his category generally benefit, from the budget of the Administration to which he belonged. 4 - A decision shall be taken, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, regarding the status of the employee placed on non-active status at the end of the year or during it, either by reinstating him to the post or by terminating his service by referring him to retirement or dismissing him from service, whereupon his rights shall be liquidated in accordance with the legislation in force. Second: Placing the employee on non-active status upon his request or the request of the Administration: 1 - An employee shall be placed on non-active status upon his request in each of the following cases: a - For a female employee to care for her newborn child. b - Where the employee suffers a grave accident, or the illness of his spouse or one of his ascendants or descendants. c - For the purpose of undertaking studies from which the Administration seeks a public benefit. The duration of placing an employee on non-active status upon his request may not exceed one year, which may be renewed twice. '' 2 - An employee shall be placed on non-active status upon the request of the Administration in the case provided for in Article 37 of this Legislative Decree. 3 - The placement of an employee on non-active status, upon his request or upon the request of the Administration, shall be effected after the approval of the Civil Service Board: a - By a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, for employees of the First Category. b - By a decree upon the proposal of the competent Minister, for employees of the Second Category. c - By a decision of the competent Minister, for employees of all other categories. 4 - The duration of placing an employee on non-active status, upon his request or the request of the Administration, shall be determined in the instrument providing for his placement on non-active status or for the renewal of this status. This instrument may not be given retroactive effect, with the exception of the instrument providing for the placement of the employee on non-active status ex officio.

Conditions for Placement Outside the Cadre 1 - An employee may be placed temporarily outside the cadre for the purpose of attaching him to one of the public administrations, public institutions, municipalities, Lebanese mixed-economy companies, recovered utilities and installations, international institutions, or States. 2 - An employee shall be placed temporarily outside the cadre at his request and after the approval of the Civil Service Board: a - By a decree taken in the Council of Ministers, for employees of the First Category. b - By a decree upon the proposal of the competent Minister, for employees of the Second Category. c - By a decision of the competent Minister, for employees of the remaining categories. The instrument providing for placing the employee outside the cadre or for renewing such placement may not be given retroactive effect. 3 - The period of placement outside the cadre may not exceed six years throughout the service of the employee. 4 - The post of the employee placed outside the cadre shall be deemed vacant on the date of entry into force of the instrument providing for such placement.

Rights of the Employee Placed Outside the Cadre 1 - An employee placed outside the cadre shall cease to receive his salaries and allowances from his original administration. 2 - An employee placed outside the cadre shall retain his right to step advancement in his cadre, and the period of placement outside the cadre shall be included in the calculation of the retirement pension or dismissal indemnity in his original administration, and he shall continue to pay the retirement deductions on the basis of his original salary. Any period on which three months have elapsed without the retirement deductions having been paid therefor shall not be included in this calculation. An employee placed outside the cadre for the purpose of attaching him to a public administration, a public institution, a municipality, a Lebanese mixed-economy company, or a recovered utility installation shall not be entitled, upon the termination of his service therein, to receive any retirement pension or dismissal indemnity from its budget for his services therein.

End of Placement Outside the Cadre An employee placed outside the cadre must place himself at the disposal of his administration immediately upon the expiry of the period of his placement outside the cadre. The employee shall be reinstated to his original post, if it is still vacant, by a decree or by a decision of the authority vested with the right to place him outside the cadre, after the approval of the Civil Service Board. If this post is not vacant, a post equivalent to it in category or rank in his corps shall be assigned to him by the authority competent to appoint. In the event that no vacant post exists, a post of a lower category or rank in his corps shall be offered to him while retaining his original salary. If he refuses the post, his service shall be terminated.

Rights and duties of a civil servant placed on unpaid leave at his request or at the request of the Administration 1 - A civil servant placed on unpaid leave, at his request or at the request of the Administration, shall cease to receive his salaries and allowances and shall lose his right to step advancement. The period of placement on unpaid leave shall not be included in the calculation of the retirement pension or the dismissal indemnity. 2 - A civil servant placed on unpaid leave, at his request or at the request of the Administration, must abide by the purpose for which he was placed on unpaid leave. The competent Administration must verify that the civil servant concerned does not violate this purpose, and must terminate the placement on unpaid leave if his violation of the said purpose is established.

Termination of placement on unpaid leave at the request of the civil servant or the Administration The provisions of Article 52 of this Legislative Decree shall apply, at the end of the period, to a civil servant placed on unpaid leave, at his request or at the request of the Administration. If a civil servant is placed on unpaid leave in order to undertake studies from which the Administration seeks a public benefit, his original post shall remain vacant and he shall mandatorily be reinstated therein.

Prohibition of other statuses With the exception of the statuses of permanent appointment, acting capacity, secondment, relief from duty, placement outside the cadre, and unpaid leave, no other status for active civil servants shall be considered legal, such as placement at the disposal of an administration or attachment of civil servants to the Minister, save for the other cases provided for by law.

Disciplinary liability A civil servant shall be considered liable from the disciplinary standpoint and shall be subject to disciplinary penalties if he intentionally or negligently breaches the duties imposed upon him by the laws and regulations in force, in particular the duties provided for in Articles 14 and 15 of this Legislative Decree. Disciplinary prosecution shall not preclude the prosecution of the civil servant, where applicable, before the competent civil or criminal courts.

Disciplinary penalties Disciplinary penalties are of two degrees: First degree: 1 - Warning. 2 - Reprimand. 3 - Salary deduction for a period of fifteen days at most. 4 - Deferral of step advancement for a period of six months at most. Second degree: 1 - Deferral of step advancement for a period exceeding six months and not exceeding thirty-six months. 2 - Suspension from work without salary for a period not exceeding six months. 3 - Reduction by one step or more within the same rank. 4 - Reduction in rank. 5 - Reduction in category. 6 - Termination of service by referral to retirement or dismissal from service. 7 - Removal from office.

The authority vested with the right to impose disciplinary penalties 1 - Each of the head of department, the head of section, and the remaining units in the Third Category shall have the right to impose the penalty of warning, the penalty of reprimand, and the penalty of salary deduction for a period not exceeding three days, upon the proposal of the immediate superior of the civil servant, if any. 2 - Each of the director, the head of service, the Qaemقام (District Commissioner), and the remaining heads of units in the Second Category shall have the right to impose the penalty of warning, the penalty of reprimand, and the penalty of salary deduction for a period not exceeding six days, upon the proposal of the immediate superior of the civil servant, if any. 3 - Each of the Director General, the Muhafiz (Governor), and the remaining heads of units in the First Category shall have the right to impose the penalty of warning, the penalty of reprimand, and the penalty of salary deduction for a period not exceeding ten days, upon the proposal of the immediate superior of the civil servant, if any. 4 - The Minister shall have the right, upon the proposal of the head of the unit reporting to him or the proposal of the President of the Central Inspection, to impose on the civil servant any penalty of the First Degree, provided that the fourth penalty thereof shall only be imposed if the civil servant commits a grave breach of his duties, and the imposition of this penalty shall be subject to seeking the opinion of the Civil Service Board. '' 5 - The Central Inspection Board shall have the right to impose disciplinary penalties in accordance with the specific texts governing it. 6 - The Higher Disciplinary Board shall have the right to impose any penalty of the penalties of the First or Second Degrees. 7 - Each of the authorities mentioned in the first three items of this Article shall have the right, after having imposed the penalty falling within the scope of its competence, to propose to the authority immediately superior to it the imposition of a more severe penalty. 8 - When more than one disciplinary penalty is imposed on the same civil servant, in the same case, by different authorities, the most severe penalty shall apply in this case, notwithstanding any other text, unless a penalty has been issued by the Higher Disciplinary Board, in which case that penalty alone shall apply. 9 - Notwithstanding any other text and subject to the provisions relating to the Higher Disciplinary Board, the civil servant may challenge the disciplinary decisions issued against him before the State Council.

Referral to the Higher Disciplinary Board 1 - A civil servant shall be referred to the Higher Disciplinary Board by a decree from the authority vested with the power of appointment after consulting the opinion of the Civil Service Board. They may also be referred by a decision of the Civil Service Board or of the Central Inspection Board. 2 - The Minister shall be entitled, by a reasoned decision of their own, to refer to the Higher Disciplinary Board the Inspectors General, Inspectors, and Assistant Inspectors who conduct inspection in their ministry or administration, and this may also be effected by a decision of the Central Inspection Board upon the proposal of its President. 3 - The decree or decision ordering referral to the Higher Disciplinary Board may provide for the suspension of the civil servant from work. The civil servant shall remain suspended from work until the Board adjudicates their case or the authority that referred them to the Higher Disciplinary Board revokes the decision of referral. 4 - A decree or decision of referral to the Higher Disciplinary Board may not be revoked after the file has been referred to the President of the Board. 5 - The Minister shall be entitled to suspend from work civil servants of the Second Category and below prior to their referral to the Higher Disciplinary Board, for a period not exceeding fifteen days. If they are not referred to the Higher Disciplinary Board at the end of this period, their salaries shall be restored to them in full.

Rules of procedure before the Higher Disciplinary Board The rules of procedure before the Higher Disciplinary Board shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice and after consulting the opinion of the Civil Service Board.

Effect of decisions issued by the Higher Disciplinary Board 1 - Penalties imposed by the Higher Disciplinary Board shall be executed immediately without a decree or decision. 2 - Penalties imposed by the Higher Disciplinary Board may not be pardoned. 3 - The acceptance of a civil servant's resignation, or considering them as having resigned, or their dismissal, or their referral to retirement, or their discharge from service, or the termination of their service for any reason whatsoever, shall not preclude their disciplinary prosecution. 4 - A civil servant whose service has been terminated by a decision of the former Disciplinary Councils or of the Higher Disciplinary Board may not be reinstated to service, reappointed, or employed in any capacity whatsoever, even temporarily, in any department of the State, municipalities, public institutions, Lebanese mixed-economy companies, or recovered utilities and installations.

Resignation upon the Request of the Employee 1 - An employee may submit his resignation in writing to the administration to which he belongs. He shall continue to perform his duties until a decision is made on his request. 2 - The authority vested with the power of appointment shall decide on the resignation request after consulting the Civil Service Board. If no instrument accepting or rejecting the resignation is issued within two months from the date of its registration, it shall be deemed accepted by operation of law. 3 - The instrument accepting the resignation may not be revoked after its issuance. 4 - A resigning employee shall not benefit from his rights to a retirement pension or dismissal indemnity; rather, the retirement deductions withheld from his salaries shall be paid to him. 5 - A resigned employee may not be reinstated into service unless he satisfies all the conditions of appointment, with the exception of the age requirement, and the competitive examination or test requirement if his appointment had taken place as a result of a competitive examination or test. In this case, he shall be reinstated to his former rank and grade, provided that he refunds to the Treasury in a single lump sum the full amounts he received pursuant to paragraph (4) of this Article, within the time limit specified in the laws and regulations in force. In this case, the employee shall not retain the seniority qualifying for step advancement acquired prior to the acceptance of his resignation.

Criminal Liability 1 - An employee shall be referred to the judiciary where it appears that the acts attributed to him constitute an offence punishable under the Penal Code and other laws in force. 2 - If the offence arises out of the function, the employee may not be prosecuted except after the approval of the administration to which he belongs. 3 - A public right action shall not be initiated by way of a direct personal claim. The Public Prosecution shall obtain the approval of the administration before initiating prosecution if the offence arises out of the function. 4 - If a dispute arises between the Public Prosecution and the competent administration regarding the characterisation of the offence, as to whether it arises out of the function or does not arise therefrom, the matter shall be submitted to the Civil Service Board to decide thereon if the employee belongs to the departments subject to its authority. However, if the employee does not belong to the departments subject to its authority, the final decision shall rest with the competent administration. 5 - A public right action is independent of the disciplinary action. The institution of a public right action shall not preclude the institution of a disciplinary action, proceeding therewith, and rendering judgment therein.

Civil Liability If an employee commits an act harmful to a third party during the exercise of his function or by reason of his exercise thereof, the State shall be liable towards the third party for the act of the employee. Where the State is ordered to pay damages, the administration shall have recourse against the employee if it considers that he committed a gross fault that could easily have been avoided.

Cases in which Service Terminates The service of an employee shall terminate and he shall permanently leave the cadre in each of the following cases: 1 - Resignation. 2 - Placement on retirement or dismissal from service. 3 - Discharge. 4 - Removal.

Deeming the Civil Servant to Have Resigned 1 - A civil servant shall be deemed to have resigned: a - The appointed or transferred civil servant who does not assume his post without a legitimate excuse within fifteen days from the date he is notified of the instrument providing for his appointment or transfer. b - The civil servant who absents himself from his work without legal leave and does not resume his work within fifteen days from the date of his absence from work. c - The civil servant who does not resume his work after the expiry of fifteen days from the date of the end of his leave. d - The civil servant who goes on strike from work or who incites other civil servants to go on strike, and in this case a replacement for him may be appointed from among those who meet the conditions of appointment to the post which he occupied, with the exception of the condition of the competitive examination or the qualifying examination. 2 - The resignation in the aforementioned cases shall be confirmed by a decree issued by the authority vested with the power of appointment following the approval of the Civil Service Board. This decree may not be revoked or amended after its issuance in the case provided for in Paragraph (d) of Clause (1) of this Article. 3 - The provisions of Clause (4) of Article 66 of this Legislative Decree shall apply to the civil servant deemed to have resigned. 4 - The civil servant deemed to have resigned may not be reinstated into service unless he meets all the conditions of appointment, with the exception of the condition of age, provided that the difference in all cases between his age and the statutory age for termination of service prescribed for the post for which he is a candidate is not less than the minimum period required for entitlement to a retirement pension, and with the exception of the condition of the competitive examination or the qualifying examination if his appointment had taken place as a result of a competitive examination or a qualifying examination. In this case, he shall be reinstated to the last step of his previous grade. As for the civil servant deemed to have resigned pursuant to Paragraph (d) of Clause (1) of this Article, he may not be reinstated to the post.

Placement on Retirement and Dismissal from Service 1 - Placement on retirement is the termination of the service of the civil servant and his final removal from the cadre, provided that a retirement pension is allocated to him. This measure shall apply to civil servants who have spent in service the minimum period required for entitlement to a retirement pension. 2 - Dismissal from service is the termination of the service of the civil servant and his final removal from the cadre, provided that he is granted a dismissal indemnity. This measure shall apply to civil servants who do not receive a retirement pension, either because they are not subject to the retirement regime, or because, despite being subject to the retirement regime, they do not meet the conditions prescribed for obtaining a retirement pension, or because they have requested the substitution of the dismissal indemnity for the retirement pension.

Cases of referral to retirement or dismissal from service A civil servant shall be referred to retirement or dismissed from service in the cases provided for by law, or by a decision of the Higher Disciplinary Board, or in each of the following cases: 1 - Attainment of the legal age. 2 - Completion by the civil servant in service of the maximum period for the termination of service. 3 - Voluntary termination of service. 4 - Abolition of the post 5 - Professional incompetence. 6 - Reorganisation of the departments.

Attainment by the civil servant of the legal age or completion by him in service of the maximum period for the termination of service 1 - The service of the civil servant shall be terminated automatically, and he shall be referred to retirement or dismissed from service, when forty-four years have elapsed since the date of his entry into service if he was appointed after 13 January 1955, and forty-six years if he was appointed before the date or if he is among the teachers. 2 - As for the civil servant who performs work requiring extraordinary physical efforts, his service shall be terminated automatically and he shall be referred to retirement or dismissed from service upon his attainment of the age of sixty or upon the lapse of forty years from the date of his entry into service if he was appointed after 13 January 1955, or the lapse of forty-two years if he was appointed before this date. '' The posts requiring extraordinary physical efforts shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the recommendation of the President of the Civil Service Board and the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers. 3 - There shall be taken into consideration, for the purpose of terminating the service of the civil servant automatically by referring him to retirement or dismissing him from service by reason of his completion in service of the maximum period specified in items (1) and (2) of this Article, the date of the entry of the civil servant for the first time into the service of the public administrations, whether such service was by way of permanent or temporary appointment or by way of employment or contracting, even if such services are not counted for the calculation of the retirement pension or the dismissal indemnity. 4 - The civil servant shall cease work immediately upon his attainment of the legal age or his completion in service of the maximum period. If he continues in work, no wage, salary, indemnity, or fee shall accrue to him for the services he performs after his attainment of the age limit or the limit of the maximum period of service, and he shall be subject to criminal prosecution. 5 - The referral of the civil servant to retirement or his dismissal from service for his attainment of the legal age or his completion in service of the maximum period shall be confirmed by a decision of the Civil Service Board after consulting the opinion of the competent administration and the Ministry of Finance.

Voluntary Termination of Service 1 - A civil servant whose actual service in the permanent cadres has reached at least twenty years may request to be placed on retirement or discharged from service at any time. The competent Minister shall accept or reject this request. Where the request is accepted, the termination of service shall be formalised by decree after the approval of the Civil Service Board. 2 - A married female civil servant shall have the right to request the termination of her service at any time. The termination of service shall be formalised by decree after seeking the opinion of the Civil Service Board. 3 - The entitlements of the civil servant whose service has been terminated in the two cases mentioned in items (1) and (2) of this Article, in respect of discharge indemnity or retirement pension, shall be settled in accordance with the laws and regulations in force.

Abolition of Post Where a post in the cadre is abolished and the appropriations allocated to it in the budget are deleted, the civil servant who occupied it shall be transferred to another vacant post in his corps and rank, in the administration to which he belongs in another administration, provided that he fulfils the conditions for appointment with the exception of the two conditions of competitive examination or test and age, and in this case the civil servant shall retain his salary. Where there is no vacant post in his corps and rank, or where he does not fulfil the conditions for appointment thereto, a lower post in his corps shall be offered to him. If he accepts it, he shall retain his salary and the right of priority to be appointed as of right to a post of his rank when it falls vacant. If he does not accept it, or if there is no vacant post in his corps, he shall be placed on retirement or discharged from service by decree after the approval of the Civil Service Board.

Reorganisation of departments 1 - The Prime Minister shall appoint, upon the proposal of the President of the Civil Service Board or the President of the Central Inspection, a committee or committees to undertake studies within the administrative unit designated by the competent Ministry, the Civil Service Board, the Central Inspection, or the Council of Ministers, and this study shall cover the tasks entrusted to the administrative unit concerned on the one hand, and the number of employees necessary to perform these tasks and their academic and professional qualifications on the other hand, with a view to determining redundant posts. 2 - The committee must submit its report on the date specified by the Prime Minister. And the competent Ministry or Administration must draw up, jointly with the Civil Service Board and the Central Inspection within a time limit of one month from the date of its notification of the report of the committee, a schedule of the names of a number of the employees of the unit equal to the redundant number specified in the report of the committee. And if it fails to do so, the Civil Service Board and the Central Inspection must immediately form a committee of at least three employees to prepare the required schedule within a time limit of two months at most. And the competent Ministry or Administration has the right to object to the schedule within a time limit of two weeks, whereupon the matter shall be submitted to the Council of Ministers to take the final decision. 3 - If it appears that there is in the administrative unit a number of employees who do not possess the qualifications required to perform their functions, the provisions of Article (37) of this Legislative Decree shall apply to them. 4 - The employees whose names are listed in the schedule referred to in Clause (2) of this Article shall cease practising their duties. And they shall continue to receive their salaries in full for a period of six months. And if they are not attached within these six months to a vacant post for which they fulfil the conditions of appointment, with the exception of the two conditions of age and competitive examination or qualifying examination, their service shall be terminated ipso jure by placing them on retirement or dismissing them from the service at the end of the said period, by decree after the approval of the Civil Service Board. And their rights shall be liquidated in accordance with the laws and regulations in force.

Professional Incompetence 1 - The Civil Service Board shall verify the professional competence of civil servants by a decision thereof or at the request of the competent administrations or the Central Inspection, either by means of collective professional examinations organised by the Directorate of Personnel for civil servants of either the Fourth or Fifth Category occupying similar positions, or by means of a personal investigation conducted by a committee appointed by the Civil Service Board and composed of a representative thereof, a representative of the Central Inspection and a representative of the administration to which the civil servant belongs, with a civil servant or a group of civil servants of whatever category they may be, and the committee shall be chaired by the representative of the Civil Service Board. 2 - Every civil servant with respect to whom the examination or investigation establishes that he does not possess the basic knowledge indispensable to him for the proper performance of his function shall be placed on retirement or dismissed from service. 3 - Placement on retirement or dismissal from service shall be decided by the authority vested with the power of appointment, upon the recommendation of the President of the Civil Service Board. Where two months have elapsed from such recommendation and no decree has been issued for placement on retirement or for dismissal from service, the Civil Service Board shall have the right to decide the same in its board sitting. Its decisions in this matter shall be deemed final. The rights of civil servants who have been placed on retirement or dismissed from service for professional incompetence shall be settled in accordance with the laws and regulations in force.

Effects of Placement on Retirement and Dismissal from Service 1 - A civil servant who has been placed on retirement or dismissed from service pursuant to a decision of the former Disciplinary Councils or the Higher Disciplinary Board, or for having reached the statutory age, or for having completed the maximum period for termination of service, in accordance with this Legislative Decree, may not be reinstated to service, reappointed, or employed in any capacity whatsoever, even temporarily or by contract, in any department of the State, municipalities, public institutions, Lebanese mixed-economy companies, or recovered public utilities and installations. He may be reinstated to service in other cases, provided that he fulfils the conditions of appointment with the exception of the condition of age and the condition of the competitive examination or qualifying examination if his appointment in his last grade had taken place as a result of a competitive examination or qualifying examination. In such case, he shall be reinstated to his former grade and step. If he had received a dismissal indemnity, his previous services shall not be added to his new services unless he refunds the dismissal indemnity, in a single lump sum, to the Treasury within a time limit of three months from the date of his assumption of duties after his reinstatement to service. However, if he was receiving a retirement pension, the payment of this pension to him shall be suspended. '' 2 - If the retired civil servant is appointed in a department of the State, municipalities, public institutions, Lebanese mixed-economy companies, or recovered public utilities and installations, he may only receive the difference between the retirement pension and the salary of the position to which he was appointed. If the civil servant had benefited from the dismissal indemnity instead of the retirement pension, he may only receive the difference between the retirement pension calculated on the basis of the services for which he received the dismissal indemnity, and the salary of the position to which he is appointed. 3 - By way of exception to the provisions of Clause (1) of this Article, the Government may, by a decision taken in the Council of Ministers, approve the assignment of a civil servant whose service was terminated for having reached the statutory age or for having completed in service the maximum period for termination of service, to a special mission that does not have the nature of continuity.
Discharge Discharge is the termination of the service of the civil servant and his final removal from the cadre, without his having the right to a retirement pension or a dismissal indemnity.

Assessment of Needs 1 - Every administration wishing to employ temporary civil servants shall draw up a statement of the designations of the temporary positions it requires, their number, the explanatory reasons for their creation, and the draft regulations to which they must be subject, and shall refer them to the Civil Service Board. 2 - The Civil Service Board may request the Research and Guidance Administration to express its opinion on the request, which shall study it by conducting an investigation in the competent administration showing its real needs for new civil servants, and whether it is possible to meet these needs by transferring civil servants working in the same administration or in another, or by reorganising the departments concerned, or by other means. 3 - The Civil Service Board may take a decision on the request of the competent administration; if it approves it, the file shall be returned to this administration so that it may prepare the subsequent legal measures. If it rejects it wholly or partially, its decision must be acted upon.

Creation of Temporary Positions The following shall be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers after the approval of the Civil Service Board: - The designations of the temporary positions and their number. - The special regulations to which these positions are subject. - The duration of service in these positions, provided that it does not exceed six non-renewable years.

Request for Appropriations The appropriations necessary for the creation of temporary positions shall not be requested in the annual budget or pursuant to special laws except after completion of the procedures and conditions set forth in the preceding Article.

Conditions for the Appointment of Temporary Civil Servants 1 - The Civil Servants Administration at the Civil Service Board shall draw up, by way of competitive examination, examination, or other methods provided for in the regulations of temporary positions, a list of persons who fulfil the prescribed conditions for appointment. This list shall be acted upon after its endorsement by the President of the Civil Service Board. 2 - Candidates participating in the competitive examination or examination must fulfil: - The general conditions of employment, with the exception of the age requirement. - The special conditions of appointment determined in the special regulations governing these positions. 3 - Temporary civil servants shall be appointed by a decree upon the proposal of the competent Minister and after the approval of the Civil Service Board. The duration of the civil servant's appointment shall be specified in the decree, and the duration of the appointment may not exceed the term fixed for the position to which he is appointed. 4 - A temporary civil servant shall be transferred by a decision of the Minister, even if the transfer requires a change of duty station.

Conditions of Discharge and its Consequences 1 - The following shall be discharged by operation of law: a - Every civil servant who loses Lebanese nationality or is deprived thereof, with effect from the date of its loss or deprivation thereof. b - Every civil servant who is deprived of his exercise of his civil rights, or is convicted of a felony or an attempted felony or a disgraceful misdemeanour or an attempted disgraceful misdemeanour among the misdemeanours defined in Item (4) of (First) of Article (4) of this Legislative Decree, with effect from the date the judgment becomes final. 2 - The discharge shall be confirmed by a decree following the approval of the Civil Service Board. 3 - The discharged civil servant shall forfeit his right to severance indemnity and to a retirement pension. However, he shall be entitled to recover the pension deductions. 4 - Under no circumstances whatsoever may the discharged civil servant be reinstated into service or be reappointed or be employed in any capacity whatsoever, even on a temporary basis or by contract, in any department of the State, municipalities, public institutions, Lebanese mixed-economy companies, or recovered public utilities and installations.

Dismissal 1 - A civil servant shall be dismissed by a decision of the Higher Disciplinary Board if he commits a grave breach of one of his professional duties specified in the laws and regulations in force, and in particular in Articles (14) and (15) of this Legislative Decree. 2 - The dismissed civil servant shall forfeit his right to severance indemnity and to a retirement pension. He shall not forfeit his right to recover the pension deductions unless the Higher Disciplinary Board so decides in the dismissal decision. 3 - Under no circumstances whatsoever may the dismissed civil servant be reinstated into service or be reappointed or be employed in any capacity whatsoever, even on a temporary basis or by contract in any department of the State, municipalities, public institutions, Lebanese mixed-economy companies, or recovered public utilities and installations.
Temporary Posts Temporary posts are the posts that are created for a specified period or for incidental work.

Article 84: Cases in which the service of a temporary employee terminates The service of a temporary employee shall terminate in the cases provided for by the regulations to which he is subject and in each of the following cases: 1 - Resignation. 2 - Expiry of the term or completion of the work for which he was appointed or attainment of the legal age. 3 - Dismissal. 4 - Removal from office.
Article 85: Resignation The provisions applicable to a permanent employee shall apply to a temporary employee with respect to resignation or the cases in which he is deemed to have resigned.

Article 86: Expiry of the term, or completion of the work, or attainment of the legal age 1 - The service of a temporary employee shall terminate ipso jure on the day on which the term for which he was appointed expires or on the day on which the work for which he was appointed is completed, or on the day on which he attains the age of sixty-four, and his salaries and allowances shall cease as of that date, even if no instrument terminating his service has been issued. 2 - A temporary employee shall cease work immediately upon the expiry of the term for which he was appointed or the completion of the work for which he was appointed or his attainment of the legal age. If he continues to work, no wage, salary, allowance or fee shall accrue to him for the services he renders thereafter, and he shall be liable to criminal prosecution. 3 - The termination of the service of a temporary employee by reason of the expiry of the term for which he was appointed, or the completion of the work for which he was appointed, or his attainment of the legal age shall be confirmed by a decision of the Civil Service Board after consulting the competent administration and the Ministry of Finance.

Article 87: Dismissal 1 - A temporary employee may be dismissed at any time by decree after the approval of the Civil Service Board. He shall also be dismissed ipso jure if he loses or is deprived of Lebanese nationality, or is deprived of his civil rights, or is convicted of a felony or an attempted felony or a disgraceful misdemeanour or an attempted disgraceful misdemeanour. 2 - The provisions of items (1) and (2) ,(4) of Article (77) of this Legislative Decree shall apply to a temporary employee dismissed ipso jure.
Article 88: Removal from office The provisions of items (1) and (3) of Article 78 of this Legislative Decree shall apply to a temporary employee.

Indemnity
The following provisions shall apply to temporary employees who are not mandatorily or optionally affiliated with the end-of-service indemnity branch in the National Social Security Fund: 1 - A temporary employee who resigns, is deemed to have resigned, is discharged by operation of law, or is dismissed from office shall not be entitled to any severance indemnity. 2 - In other cases, a temporary employee shall be entitled to a severance indemnity equivalent to one month's salary for each year of actual service in the post, calculated on the basis of the last salary received by him. Allowances of whatever kind shall not be included in the calculation of the salary. 3 - It is a condition for granting the severance indemnity that the temporary employee shall have continued in service each time for a period exceeding one year. Any intermittent service prior to the terminated service shall not be taken into consideration. 4 - A month shall be calculated as one twelfth of a year, and a day as one thirtieth of a month. '' 5 - Any service performed by a temporary employee before reaching the age of twenty or after completing the statutory age shall not be included in the calculation of the indemnity. 6 - If a temporary employee dies before the expiration of the period of his service, the members of his family shall be granted the severance indemnity as follows: a - The full indemnity that would have accrued to him, to the spouse, the children, the father, and the mother, within the conditions specified in the Retirement and Severance from Service Regulations. b - If the employee dies unmarried and the conditions prescribed in the Retirement and Severance from Service Regulations are not met by his parents, they, or whichever of them is surviving, shall be granted half of the severance indemnity. In the absence of both parents, half of the indemnity shall be granted in equal shares to his brothers and sisters whom he was supporting prior to his death. 7 - The application for indemnity shall be submitted to the Ministry of Finance within two years from the date of termination of service. The right shall lapse upon the expiration of this time limit. 8 - The indemnity shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Finance. Receipt of the indemnity shall not preclude challenging the decision.

Rights of the temporary employee
The following provisions shall apply to the temporary employee: - Articles 16, 17 (items 1 and 4), 18, and 19 (items 3, 4, and 5) relating to salaries. - Articles 22, 23, 24, 26, 27, 28, and 29 relating to allowances and grants. - Article 30 - (items 1, 2, and 4) relating to step advancement. - Articles 33, 34, 36, and 37 relating to leave, provided that special leave without pay shall not exceed one month in a year and three months within five years, and provided that the temporary employee shall be discharged from service if the duration of his sick leave exceeds three months in a single year, and that the leave shall not exceed the term of appointment.

Duties of the temporary employee. The following provisions shall apply to the temporary employee: - Articles 14 and 15 relating to the duties of the employee. - Articles 57 to 62 inclusive relating to discipline. - Article 63 relating to criminal liability. - Article 64 relating to civil liability.

Assessment of needs and request for appropriations. In assessing the needs of public administrations for contracted personnel, and in requesting the appropriations necessary for them, the provisions of Articles 80 and 81 of this Legislative Decree shall apply.

Conditions of contracting. 1 - The Minister shall contract, after the approval of the Civil Service Board, with Lebanese nationals or foreigners for a specified period and to perform a specific work requiring special knowledge or qualifications, within the limits of the appropriations allocated for this purpose in the budget and within the scope of the number specified therein. 2 - It is not permissible to contract for positions provided for in the permanent or temporary cadres unless the law or the regulations provide otherwise, nor is it permissible to contract for the designations provided for in the Wage Earners Regulations. 3 - It is not permissible to contract with persons to perform tasks similar to the tasks performed by employees and wage earners. 4 - The contract shall not be renewed tacitly.

Rights and duties of the contracted person. 1 - Subject to the provisions of the following items of this Article, the contracted person shall benefit from the rights and be subject to the obligations provided for in the contract concluded with him. 2 - The following provisions shall apply to the contracted person: - Articles 14 and 15 relating to and the duties of the employee. - Article 57 relating to disciplinary liability. - Article 63 relating to criminal liability. - Article 64 relating to civil liability. - Article 70 (Item 4) relating to the employee reaching the legal age or spending in service the maximum period for end of service. 3 - The administration may terminate the contract at any time whatsoever. 4 - The contract shall be deemed terminated ipso jure if, instead of the tasks specified for him in the contract, other tasks different therefrom are assigned to the contracted person. And the head of the administration to which the contracted person belongs shall be personally liable in his private property for the amounts paid to the contracted person for the period during which he does not perform the tasks specified in his contract.

Severance indemnity. Contracted personnel who are not compulsorily or voluntarily affiliated with the end-of-service indemnity branch at the National Social Security Fund shall be granted a severance indemnity calculated in accordance with the bases specified in Article 89 of this Legislative Decree.
Employment of Wage-Earners: Wage-earners are employed in each public administration in accordance with the General Regulations for Wage-Earners and the Special Regulations for Wage-Earners therein.

General Regulations for Wage-Earners: 1 - General regulations for wage-earners in all public administrations shall be established by virtue of a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the recommendation of the President of the Civil Service Board and the proposal of the Prime Minister. 2 - The aforementioned regulations shall cover all matters common to wage-earners across all public administrations, and in particular: - Definition of wage-earners. - Types of wage-earners. - Procedures and conditions for the employment of wage-earners. - Determination of the titles of wage-earners. - Determination of the duration and schedule of work. - Determination of leaves of all kinds. - Determination of wages and allowances. - Determination of the provisions for transfer. - Determination of the provisions for discipline. - Determination of the provisions for the termination of service of a wage-earner. - And in general all other matters required by the general conditions of wage-earners.

Special Regulations for Wage-Earners: 1 - Each public administration shall establish special regulations for wage-earners addressing the conditions particular to it, in addition to the other matters assigned to it by the General Regulations for Wage-Earners. 2 - The special regulations shall be issued by a decree upon the proposal of the competent minister after the approval of the Civil Service Board. The regulations of each public administration shall include the determination of the number of wage-earners therein. 3 - It is prohibited to employ wage-earners in all public administrations, whatever the form of employment, except within the limits of the number determined for each administration by virtue of its special regulations for wage-earners, and within the limits of the appropriations allocated for this purpose in the budget. 4 - A wage-earner shall cease work immediately upon the expiry of the period for which he was employed or upon reaching the legal age. If he continues to work, no wage, allowance, or fee shall accrue to him for the services he performs thereafter, and he shall be subject to criminal prosecution.
The legal provisions relating to work emergencies shall apply to wage-earners.
Wage-earners shall be dismissed in accordance with the provisions of the regulations to which they are subject.

Rights and Duties of a Wage-Earner: A wage-earner shall benefit from the rights and be subject to the obligations provided for in the General Regulations for Wage-Earners and in the Special Regulations for Wage-Earners in the administration to which he belongs. The provisions of item 6 of Article 13 of this Legislative Decree shall also apply to him.

Severance Indemnity 1 - Lebanese wage earners working in public administrations shall be entitled to receive a severance indemnity, if the following conditions are met in respect of them: a- That they are assigned to the duties entrusted to them in accordance with the legal rules prescribed in the regulations specific to each category thereof. b - That the duration of their service is not less than five hundred days of actual work. c - That the average number of days of their actual work during the period of their service is not less than one hundred and eighty days per single year. d - That they have not ceased work of their own accord or failed or declined to comply with work orders addressed to them by the administration without a legitimate reason among the reasons provided for in the regulations of the category to which the wage earner belongs. e - That they have not been dismissed for one of the reasons set forth in the following clause (2). 2 - A wage earner shall not be entitled to a severance indemnity in any of the following cases: a - If he commits an intentional act or omission aimed at causing damage to the interests of the administration. b - If he commits serious violations of the instructions of the administration to which he belongs or of the regulations in force therein. c - If he commits an intentional felony or misdemeanour at the workplace or during the performance of work. d - If it is established that he accepted a bribe or embezzled State funds, deposits entrusted to him, or materials handed over to him. 3 - A wage earner shall be entitled to request his dismissal from service in any of the following cases: a - If the days of his actual work in a year fall below one hundred and eighty days for a reason attributable to the administration. b - If he reaches sixty years of age. c - If he is afflicted with an infirmity or illness that prevents him from performing service. '' 4 - The severance indemnity for wage earners shall be liquidated in accordance with the following bases: 1/30 or the wage of one day for every thirty days of actual work in respect of the first nine hundred days. 1/20 or the wage of one day for every twenty days of actual work in respect of the following nine hundred days. 1/10 or the wage of one day for every ten days of actual work in respect of what exceeds one thousand eight hundred days. 5 - Services rendered by the wage earner before the age of eighteen and after the age of sixty, as well as services rendered by him prior to the first of January 1953, shall not be included in the calculation of the indemnity. 6 - The days of actual service for the purpose of liquidating the severance indemnity shall be determined on the basis of the decision or memorandum of employment and the records and registers of the competent department. As regards services prior to the date of enforcement of Legislative Decree No. 113 dated 12/6/1959, the days of actual service may be determined on the basis of the records and registers of the competent department, provided that no certificate, whatever its source, shall be relied upon unless it is corroborated by the said records and registers. 7 - If the wage earner dies while in service, the Lebanese members of his family provided for in Article 89 of this Legislative Decree shall be granted the indemnity to which he would have been entitled had he been dismissed from service. 8 - The application for indemnity shall be submitted to the Ministry of Finance through the competent ministry within two years from the date of termination of service. The wage earner shall forfeit his right to the indemnity upon the expiry of the said time limit.

Official working hours and work schedules in public administrations and for state workers shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the recommendation of the President of the Civil Service Board and the proposal of the Prime Minister.
In the appointment of civil servants, the provisions of Article 95 of the Constitution shall be observed.

If a disagreement arises between the Civil Service Board and the competent ministry regarding the application of the provisions of this Legislative Decree, the matter shall be submitted to the Council of Ministers for adjudication. Its decision in this case shall be deemed final and must be acted upon.

Civil servants whose positions are specified below may not be appointed in the regions of which they are natives: - Governors and Secretaries-General in the Governorate. - District Commissioners in the District and the adjacent Districts within the Governorate. - All other positions determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.

1 - Civil servants whose positions are specified below shall reside in the region in which their place of work is located: - Governors. - Secretaries-General. - District Commissioners. 2 - Decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers shall determine the other positions whose incumbents must reside in the region in which their place of work is located.

It is prohibited to combine membership of the Chamber of Deputies with a public office, whatever the form of its assumption, whether by way of appointment, contracting, or employment, even on a temporary basis, in public administrations, public institutions, municipalities, Lebanese mixed-economy companies, and recovered utilities and installations.

1 - A civil servant is prohibited, during five years after leaving the service: a - From working in an enterprise that was subject to his supervision in the administration to which he belonged, or that customarily supplied materials to this administration or carried out works for its benefit during the civil servant's affiliation with it. b - From having an interest in this enterprise, or representing it, or undertaking its defence before the judiciary in disputes brought by it against public administrations, public institutions, and municipalities. 2 - A civil servant who violates these provisions shall be punished by forfeiture of the right to benefit from the retirement pension and by the recovery of the dismissal indemnity he received, or by a fine not exceeding twenty-five thousand pounds, which shall be doubled in the event of recurrence, if his service ended otherwise than by way of placement on retirement or dismissal from service.

By way of exception to the provisions of Article 75 of this Legislative Decree. 1 - A civil servant whose service has ended pursuant to items (1), (2), (3), (4) and (6) of Article 69 of this Legislative Decree may be appointed to the boards of directors of public institutions, Lebanese mixed-economy companies, and recovered utilities and installations, by a decree adopted in the Councils of Ministers. 2 - During a period ending on 31/12/1986, a contract may be concluded with a civil servant whose service has ended pursuant to items (1), (2), (3), (4) and (6) of Article 69 of this Legislative Decree in public administrations, public institutions, municipalities, mixed-economy companies, and recovered utilities and installations, following the approval of the Council of Ministers.

A special medal called the "Administrative Medal" shall be established and awarded to civil servants in public administrations on the basis of exemplary competence, model conduct, or distinguished activity. 2 - The ranks of this medal, the procedures for awarding it, the form of its patent, and all matters relating thereto shall be regulated by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the recommendation of the President of the Civil Service Board and the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers.

For the purpose of applying the provisions of this Legislative Decree, and with respect to administrative and financial powers only, the word "Minister" or the phrase "Competent Minister", wherever they appear, shall mean the Minister or the civil servant who exercises by operation of law the administrative and financial powers of the Minister.

The texts relating to the granting of indemnities of all kinds and allowances of whatever nature, wherever they appear, shall remain in force until the date on which the abolition or amendment of the said indemnities and allowances is determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the recommendation of the President of the Civil Service Board and the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers.

The provisions of Article 27 of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments, as well as the provisions of paragraph 3 of Article 22 of Law No. 14/81 dated 15/7/1981 (the General Budget Law for the year 1981), shall remain in force until the date on which the date of entry into force of the provisions of Article 27 of this Legislative Decree is determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the recommendation of the President of the Civil Service Board and the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers.

Contrary to the provisions of the first Article of Law No. 16/75 dated 11/4/1975 (amending the ninth Article of the Social Security Law), permanent State civil servants defined in paragraph (1) of item (1) of the first Article of this Legislative Decree shall not be subject to the Sickness and Maternity Insurance Branch at the National Social Security Fund, and they shall continue to benefit from the benefits of the State Civil Servants' Cooperative in the two cases of sickness and maternity.

1 - Until the forms and instructions relating to the promotion roster are laid down, the Civil Service Board may subject candidates for promotion from rank to rank within the same category to a qualifying examination conducted by the Personnel Department at the Civil Service Board in accordance with the provisions of items (2) and (7) of Article (6) of this Legislative Decree. 2 - The Civil Service Board shall lay down the regulations and subjects of the qualifying examinations. It may organise joint examinations for similar posts in all or some administrations, and it may also organise a special examination for each administration.

The creation of temporary posts created prior to the date of entry into force of this Legislative Decree may be extended for a period of six years at most with effect from the date of its entry into force.

Contracting may not be renewed or extended for a period exceeding the end of the year 1986 with any of the contracted persons in service on the date of entry into force of this Legislative Decree, unless such contracting is in compliance with the provisions of Article 92 of this Legislative Decree.

- Within a period of one year from the date of entry into force of this Legislative Decree, the unlawful situations of civil servants in service on the date of entry into force of this Legislative Decree may be regularised.
