The rules and conditions of such regularisation shall be determined by decisions issued by the Council of Ministers, and such decisions may be given retroactive effect.
The time limit specified in item 2 of Article 50 of this Legislative Decree shall run with effect from the date of its entry into force.

- 1 - By way of exception to the provisions of (Third) of the Fifth Article of this Legislative Decree and within a period of one year from the date of its entry into force, the Civil Service Board may - where necessary - decide to hold competitive examinations to fill posts in the Third Category from among those for which the National Institute of Administration and Development prepares. 2 - Notwithstanding any other text, in appointing the successful candidates in the competitive examinations held by the National Institute of Administration and Development to fill the posts of the Third Category for which it prepares, the order of merit of success in these competitive examinations shall be respected, without any priority.

Until the establishment of the Higher Disciplinary Authority, the expression (Higher Disciplinary Authority) wherever it occurs shall mean (the General Disciplinary Council) and this Council shall continue to exercise its powers and functions.

The Government shall establish, by decrees taken in the Council of Ministers within one year from the date of entry into force of this Legislative Decree, the cadres with the number of posts, ranks, categories and salary scale for all administrations of the State and the regulatory decrees relating to allowances.

Surplus Posts 1 - If the number of civil servants working in a given administration exceeds the posts specified for this administration in the numerical cadres, it must draw up within a period not exceeding three months starting from the date of the text determining the cadres a list of the names of civil servants whose number equals the number of surplus posts. And if it does not draw up this list within the appointed period, it shall be drawn up in accordance with the provisions of Article 74 of this Legislative Decree. 2 - In drawing up this list, consideration must be given to the civil servant's professional grades, and then to his family burdens, such that civil servants of low competence are dismissed first, and in the event of equality, whoever among them has fewer family burdens than others. 3 - The provisions of Article 74 of this Legislative Decree shall apply to the surplus civil servants whose names are included in the list.

The acts provided for in Articles 23, 24 and 26 of this Legislative Decree shall remain subject to the approval of the Civil Service Board, until the date on which the regulations relating to the said acts are determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers, upon the recommendation of the President of the Civil Service Board, and the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers.

The time limit specified in Article 49 of this Legislative Decree for terminating the service of current First Category civil servants placed at the disposal of the President of the Council of Ministers and the other Ministers and who have been at their disposal for more than two years shall be extended until 31/12/1984.

All provisions contrary to the provisions of this Legislative Decree or inconsistent with its content are hereby repealed, in particular: 1 - Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6/1959 (Civil Servants Regulations) 2 - The Law implemented by Decree No. 3169 dated 29/4/1972 (Determining certain special provisions relating to civil servants and amending certain provisions of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6/1959 - Civil Servants Regulations). 3 - Sections One and Three, with the exception of Article 25 of Section Three, of the Law implemented by Decree No. 58 dated 15/12/1982 (Amending certain provisions of Legislative Decrees No. 111 and 112 dated 12/6/1959 and authorising the filling of vacant posts in certain positions of the cadres of public administrations from among the permanent, temporary and contracted civil servants and wage-earners working therein). 4 - Decree No. 5580 dated 25/11/1960 (Determining the conditions for the admission of applicants for a position among the positions of the Fifth Category). 5 - Decree No. 70 dated 30/3/1977 (Determining the bases for acting appointment in the positions of the First Category). - Articles 120 and 121 of Law No. 3/79 dated 24/3/1979 (National Defence Law).
This Legislative Decree shall enter into force immediately upon its publication by posting on the entrance of the seat of the Presidency of the Government.

National defence aims to strengthen the capabilities of the State and develop its capacities to confront and resist any attack on the territory of the homeland, on the national airspace and on the sovereign rights in the national maritime zones, and any aggression directed against it, and to guarantee the sovereignty of the State and preserve the safety and security of the homeland, its national airspace, its sovereign rights in the maritime zones, and the safety of the citizens.

The armed forces mean: the Army, the Internal Security Forces, General Security and State Security, and in general all personnel working in public administrations, public institutions and municipalities who bear arms by virtue of their function."

1 - If the homeland or a part of its territories, or its airspace, or any part of its maritime zones or of its sovereign rights over these zones, or a sector of its public sectors, or the population as a whole is exposed to danger, the following may be declared:

A - A state of total or partial alert to limit the exposure of the population and vital installations to danger, and to secure mobilisation operations and the use of the armed forces.

B - A state of mobilisation or partial mobilisation to implement all or some of the established plans.

2 - The aforementioned measures shall be declared by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the recommendation of the Higher Defence Council.

3 - These decrees may include special provisions aimed at:

A - Imposing control over energy sources and regulating their distribution.

B - Imposing control over raw materials, industrial production and supply materials, and regulating their import, storage, export and distribution.

C - Regulating and monitoring transport, movement, communications and telecommunications.

D - Requisitioning persons and property and imposing services on legal and natural persons, in which case the constitutional and legal provisions relating to the declaration of a state of emergency shall be observed."

Related text: Tasking the military and security forces and the municipal police with imposing control over energy sources and regulating their distribution, and working to empty and close all containers designated for storing fuel that are in violation of the rules and regulations in force across all Lebanese territories

If the country is exposed to the dangers specified in Article 1 of Legislative Decree No. 52 dated 5/8/1967, a state of emergency or a military zone shall be declared, and the competent authorities shall exercise the powers provided for in the aforementioned Legislative Decree.

The Army shall be placed at the disposal of the President of the Republic, who exercises his powers in accordance with the provisions laid down in the Constitution and the laws in force, and in particular Articles 6 and 7 of this Legislative Decree.
The Council of Ministers shall determine the general defence and security policy, define its objectives, and supervise its implementation.

1 - The Higher Defence Council shall decide upon the procedures necessary for the implementation of the defence policy as determined by the Council of Ministers, and the resolutions of the Higher Defence Council shall remain secret, and the Council shall accord special importance to defensive mobilisation which addresses the following fundamental matters:

a - Military service and compulsory conscription.

b - Educational mobilisation.

c - Mobilisation of economic activity in its agricultural, industrial, financial and commercial branches.

d - Mobilisation of health and medical activity.

e - General mobilisation of the State and citizens, and in particular civil defence.

f - Mobilisation of guidance and awareness activities.

2 - The Higher Defence Council shall distribute the defence tasks among the ministers and the bodies concerned, and shall issue the necessary directives and instructions in respect thereof, and shall follow up on their implementation.

And it shall approve the personnel and equipment plan laid down for these tasks.

1 - The Higher Defence Council shall be convened to meet by its President.

2 - The President of the Council shall submit for deliberation and the taking of the appropriate decision the matters that necessitated the convening of the Council.

Or upon a request from at least one third of its members.

1 - The Vice-President of the Higher Defence Council shall oversee the implementation of the resolutions of the Council.

2 - There shall be attached and directly linked to the Vice-President of the Council, for the purpose of carrying out his duties, a General Secretariat of the Higher Defence Council which shall undertake:

a - Collecting information from the competent departments.

b - Preparing the files entrusted to it and the studies needed by the Higher Defence Council.

c - Notifying the resolutions of the Higher Defence Council to the administrations concerned.

d - Informing the Higher Defence Council of the progress of implementation of the resolutions taken.

3 - The establishment table of the General Secretariat of the Higher Defence Council, the conditions of appointment, the rules of procedure therein, and the powers and responsibilities of the employees shall be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers after consulting the opinion of the State Consultative Council.

4 - The General Secretariat of the Higher Defence Council shall be headed by a general officer holding a staff diploma from among the Army officers in active service who has not previously been placed in the reserve, appointed by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of each of the President of the Council of Ministers and the Minister of National Defence.

Every minister shall be considered responsible for the defence and security tasks pertaining to his ministry, and he must circulate the necessary measures in respect thereof and oversee their implementation.

The responsibility for maintaining internal security shall fall upon the Minister of the Interior, subject to the provisions stipulated by special laws. And the Ministry of National Defence may, by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers, be tasked with securing military equipment and training courses for the benefit of the Ministry of the Interior.

If the State is exposed in one region or several regions to acts harmful to its safety or its interests, the Army shall be tasked with maintaining security in this region or regions in accordance with the following provisions:

1 - The assignment shall be effected by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior and the Minister of National Defence, and shall be for a specified period to be extended where necessary in the same manner.

2 - Immediately upon the issuance of the decree referred to in Clause 1 above, the Army shall assume the authority to maintain security and protect the State against any act harmful to its safety or its interests.

And all armed forces that perform their duties in accordance with their own laws and regulations shall be placed under the command of the Commander of the Army, assisted by the Military Council and under the supervision of the Higher Defence Council.

Armed forces, for the application of the provisions of this Clause, shall mean:

The Army, the Internal Security Forces, General Security, State Security, and all other personnel in the public sector who bear arms by virtue of their office.

3 - The Commander of the Army may take all measures conducive to maintaining security, in particular:

- Searching buildings and all other places at any time whatsoever following the approval of the competent Public Prosecution.

- Monitoring ports, vessels, installations, and everything installed in the territorial waters, the contiguous zone to the territorial waters, the exclusive economic zone in the territorial waters, and the continental shelf zone.

- Monitoring the entry of foreigners into Lebanon and their exit therefrom.

- Monitoring and protecting the Lebanese airspace.

- Prohibiting unauthorized public gatherings or those of a military nature.

- Pursuing perpetrators of breaches of security and referring them to the judiciary within five days from the date of their arrest.

- Combating smuggling.

4 - The measures taken shall be communicated immediately to the Higher Defence Council, the Minister of Interior, and the Minister of National Defence.

5 - All acts breaching security, including the violation of the measures taken within the framework of Paragraph 3 above, shall be referred to the Military Courts.

6 - Any person who violates or prevents the execution of the measures taken pursuant to Clause 3 of this Article shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year and by a fine from two to five times the official minimum wage, or by either of these two penalties.

In cases where the law provides for punishing the offender with a more severe penalty, the provisions of ideal concurrence of offences shall apply by imposing the most severe penalty.

7 - Upon the expiration of the period of validity of the decree provided for in this Article, the Military Courts shall remain competent to continue hearing the cases referred to them.

A Higher Council of Defence shall be established and shall be composed of:

1 - The President of the Republic - President.

- The Prime Minister - Vice-President.

- The Minister of Defence - Member.

- The Minister of Finance - Member.

- The Minister of Interior - Member.

- The Minister of Economy - Member.

2 - The President of the Higher Council of Defence shall have the right to summon whomever he wishes among those whose attendance is required by the nature of the business of the Council.

3 - The Secretary-General of the Higher Council of Defence mentioned in Article Ten below shall perform the duties of the secretariat of this Council

4 - One or more ministers may be added to the Higher Council of Defence as active members by a decree issued in the Council of Ministers.

5 - A Directorate General called the "Directorate General of State Security" shall be established at the Higher Council of Defence, subject to the authority of the Council and subordinate to its President and Vice-President.

This Directorate General shall undertake the following tasks:

First - Collecting information relating to the internal security of the State, by means of its own special networks covering the Lebanese territory, and seeking external information from the existing agencies, and verifying, analysing, classifying, preserving or referring it to the competent authorities.

Second - Monitoring foreigners by investigating acts committed by them that prejudice the security of the State, and monitoring the relations of citizens with foreign parties in matters relating to the security of the State.

Third - Combating espionage and hostile activity in its various forms.

Fourth - Conducting preliminary investigations into acts that prejudice the internal and external security of the State through the Director General, the Deputy Director General, the regular officers of the Directorate General, the officers seconded to it, and the non-commissioned officers designated by the Vice-President of the Higher Council of Defence, whereby they perform their duties in the capacity of auxiliary judicial police officers to the Appellate Public Prosecutor and to the Government Commissioner at the Military Court in accordance with the laws in force.

Fifth - Coordinating with the other competent security authorities in the Directorate General of General Security, the Internal Security Forces, and the Directorate of Intelligence in the Army in matters of intelligence and exchange of information.

The details of implementation of this item shall be determined by a decree issued in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers.

Sixth - Preparing periodic reports to inform the Higher Council of Defence of the general security and political situation, preparing appropriate proposals to confront internal and external dangers, and permanently informing the President of the Higher Council of Defence and his Vice-President of the security and political situations.

In order to perform these tasks, one or more detachments from the Internal Security Forces or from the General Security or from both together shall be detached to this Directorate General, and their military command shall be vested in the Director General, and the Director General may, notwithstanding any other legal text, transfer officers, non-commissioned officers and personnel from the Ministry of Interior or request the secondment of employees from State administrations in accordance with the laws in force, provided that this takes place with the approval of the competent authorities in these bodies. Official bodies shall be obliged to provide the required information on everything that prejudices the internal and external security of the State to this Directorate General.

The establishment of the Directorate General, the ranks, salaries and conditions of appointment of the employees therein, their powers, rights and duties, the rules governing their discipline, promotion, transfer and dismissal from service, and all their personal affairs, as well as the procedures of work at the Directorate General and its organisation, shall be determined by a decree issued in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers and the recommendation of the Director General. The Director General of State Security shall be appointed by a decree issued in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Armed Forces from the rank of Colonel and above, or from among the employees of the top three grades of the First Category, or from among Lebanese nationals from outside the establishment who hold university degrees.

The Director General of State Security shall be assisted by a Deputy Director General appointed by a decree issued in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers, who shall replace the Director General in the event of his absence.

The Director General of State Security shall exercise the administrative and financial powers vested in Directors General in State administrations.

He shall undertake the commitment and liquidation of expenditures pertaining to the Directorate General within the limits of the appropriations, whatever their value may be.

In particular, the Director General of State Security shall undertake the following tasks:

- Managing the Directorate General of State Security to execute the tasks entrusted to it.

- Securing and qualifying human resources at various levels.

- Securing and maintaining the material means of work for the various agencies subordinate to him.

- Issuing instructions that determine the rules of work.

The boundaries of the governorates shall be deemed the boundaries of the military regions.

As for the military region within the meaning of Legislative Decree No. 52 dated 5 August 1967, it is the part of the territory declared and defined in accordance with the aforementioned Legislative Decree.
The defensive sectors shall be designated and their number and duties defined by special instructions issued by the Army Command in accordance with the defence plans.
The Ministry of National Defence, with all its institutions, shall be subject to the authority of the Minister of National Defence, and he shall be responsible for the execution of all its duties.

The Ministry of National Defence shall consist of the following principal institutions:

- The Army.

- The Directorate General of Administration.

- The Inspectorate General.

- The Military Council.

1 - A Military Bureau shall be established at the office of the Minister of National Defence, headed by an officer holding the rank of Colonel or above, and comprising:

- The Secretariat.

- The Department of Administrative Control, which shall undertake the following duties:

a - Monitoring the legality of administrative acts in the Ministry of National Defence

b - Exercising the power of ex-post control over the accounting of materiel and works

- The Department of Public Relations and Information.

- The Department of Lebanese Military Attachés Abroad.

- The Department of Legal Affairs and Military Judiciary.

- The Department of Veterans.

The Head of the Military Bureau shall be appointed by decree upon the proposal of the Minister of National Defence after consulting the opinion of the Commander of the Army.

The cadre of the Military Bureau, the conditions of appointment thereto, the rules of procedure therein, and the powers and responsibilities of its personnel shall be defined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of National Defence.

2 - The appointment of military judges shall take place by a decision of the Minister of National Defence upon the proposal of the Military Council.

- The Army shall include integrated land, air and naval forces under the command of the Commander of the Army.

The Army shall consist of:

- The Army Command.

- The Land Forces

- The Air Forces

- The Naval Forces

- The Military Institutes.

The Army Command:

The Army Command shall consist of:

- The Commander of the Army.

- The Staff.

The Staff shall be subject to the direct authority of the Commander of the Army and shall consist of:

- The Chief of Staff

- The Deputy Chiefs of Staff.

- Specialized directorates, branches, departments and organs.

Appointment of the Commander of the Army:

The Commander of the Army shall be appointed from among the general officers certified in staff studies who have not previously been placed in the reserve, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of National Defence.

The Commander of the Army shall hold the rank of General and shall be titled "General, Commander of the Army", and shall report directly to the Minister of National Defence.

Functions of the Army Commander:

The Army Commander shall undertake the preparation of the Army for the tasks entrusted to it, the raising of its combat level, and the command of military operations, which requires:

- Executing voluntary and compulsory recruitment.

- Organising the formations and units, defining their tasks, and administering them.

- Executing alert and mobilisation operations when declared.

- Preparing combat plans and orders and establishing logistical programmes therefor.

- Providing for the needs of the Army and maintaining the level of equipment and materiel after receiving them from the Directorate General of Administration.

- Commanding military operations.

- Commanding security operations when the Army is entrusted with tasks of maintaining security.

The Directorate of Intelligence shall report to the Army Commander, except in matters relating to military security, in which case it shall report to the Chief of Staff, and it shall provide the President of the Council of Ministers, Vice-President of the Higher Defence Council, with all information.

Appointment of the Chief of Staff and the Deputy Chiefs of Staff:

The Chief of Staff shall be appointed from among the general officers holding a staff diploma who have not previously been placed in the reserve, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of National Defence after consulting the opinion of the Army Commander.

The Chief of Staff shall deputise for the Army Commander in the event of his absence and shall exercise his functions and powers throughout the period of his absence.

The Deputy Chiefs of Staff shall be appointed from among the officers of the rank of Colonel and above who have not previously been placed in the reserve, by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of National Defence and the recommendation of the Army Commander after consulting the opinion of the Chief of Staff.

Functions of the Chief of Staff:

The Chief of Staff shall undertake to assist the Army Commander in bearing his responsibilities and executing his functions by regulating the work of the Staff, coordinating among them, and ascertaining the combat level of the Army, which requires:

- Expressing an opinion on transactions submitted to the Army Commander in order to take the appropriate decisions thereon.

- Ensuring the execution of the decisions taken.

- Supervising the readiness of the Army in materiel and personnel.

- Proposing ways and means that help develop the work of the Staff and improve the level of services for combat units.

- Supervising training and administering the affairs of the reserve forces. In operational cases determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, the Chief of Staff shall have the right to refer to the Higher Defence Council through the Minister of National Defence in the event of a difference in points of view between him and the Army Commander. The procedures and time limits for this referral shall be determined in the said decree.

The Directorate General of Administration:

1 - Appointment of the Director General of Administration:

The Director General of Administration shall be appointed from among the general officers certified in staff or administration (quartermaster) who have not previously been placed in the reserve, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of National Defence. The Director General shall report directly to the Minister of National Defence.

2 - Duties of the Director General General of Administration:

First - Subject to the provisions of the Public Accounting Law and the powers of each of the Minister of National Defence and the Military Council set forth in this Legislative Decree, and the Director General of Administration shall take the legal and regulatory measures and procedures:

a - To secure the various needs of the Army and the services necessary therefor.

b - To prepare the budget and supervise the execution thereof.

c - To supervise the use of the funds of the institutions affiliated with the Army Institution.

d - To administer the secondary institutions provided for in this Article.

Second - The working procedures between the Army Command and the Directorate General of Administration shall be determined pursuant to instructions issued by the Minister of National Defence upon the proposal of the Military Council.

3 - The Directorate General of Administration shall be composed of the following units:

- The Secretariat.

- The Materiel Service.

- The Quartermaster Service.

- The Engineering Service.

- The Geography Service.

- The Health Service.

- Finance.

- The following secondary institutions:

- The Commissary Institution.

- The Mutual Aid Institution for Officers.

- The Mutual Aid Institution for Non-Commissioned Officers and Enlisted Men.

- The Mutual Aid Institution for Civilian Employees.

1 - Appointment of the Inspector General:

The Inspector General shall be appointed from among the general officers certified in staff who have not previously been placed in the reserve, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of National Defence. The Inspector General shall report directly to the Minister of National Defence.

2 - Duties of the Inspector General:

a - The Inspector General shall undertake the task of inspecting all institutions and administrations of the Ministry of National Defence, and he shall:

- Verify the application of laws and regulations and the execution of orders and instructions.

- Submit the necessary proposals for the proper functioning of work in the various sectors of the Army and the Directorate General of Administration and the activities thereof.

b - The working procedures between each of the Army Command and the General Inspectorate shall be determined pursuant to instructions issued by the Minister of National Defence upon the proposal of the Military Council.

The Inspectorate General shall be composed of:

- The Secretariat.

- The Inspectorate of Education, Training, and Sports.

- The Inspectorate of Weapons of All Kinds.

- The Inspectorate of Health.

- The Inspectorate of Administration for Personnel, Materiel, and Finance.

1- The Military Council shall be composed of:

- The Commander of the Army - Chairman.

- The Chief of Staff - Vice-Chairman.

- The Director General of Administration - Member.

- The Inspector General - Member.

- The Secretary General of the Higher Council of Defence - Member.

- A general officer appointed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of National Defence after consulting the opinion of the Commander of the Army - Member.

2 - The Chairman of the Council may summon whomever he deems appropriate to attend the meetings of the Council.

3 - A secretariat called the "Secretariat of the Military Council" shall be established at the Military Council, and its establishment shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of National Defence.

Powers of the Military Council:

1 - The Military Council shall approve:

A - The organisation of all main institutions affiliated with the Ministry of National Defence contained in this Legislative Decree.

B - The postings of commanders of regions, divisions and brigades, the commanders of the Air and Naval Forces, the commanders of military institutes and equivalent positions in the remaining main institutions upon the proposal of the heads of these institutions, each regarding his own officers, and they shall be issued by decree.

C - The postings of directors, heads of branches and battalion commanders in the Army Institution upon the proposal of the Army Commander.

In the event that the Military Council approves the proposal of the Army Commander, the postings shall be issued by a decision from the Minister of National Defence, and in the event that the Military Council does not approve the proposal of the Army Commander, the matter shall be submitted to the Supreme Defence Council, which shall decide: either to approve the proposal of the Army Commander or to return it to the Army Commander to submit another proposal. The same procedures shall apply in the other main institutions upon the proposal of the heads of these institutions.

D - The detachment of officers of the rank of Major and above and for a period of more than one month.

E - The promotion of officers to the rank of Captain and above in the various main institutions upon the proposal of the heads of these institutions. These promotions shall be issued by decrees upon the proposal of the Minister of National Defence.

F - The granting of seniorities to officers by decrees upon the proposal of the heads of the main institutions.

G - Entitlement to medals.

2 - The Military Council shall undertake the approval of the following matters, and they shall be issued by a decision from the Minister of National Defence:

A - The conditions for the admission of civilians to military institutes and the conditions for appointment therein upon the proposal of the Army Commander.

B - The establishment and organisation of military institutes upon the proposal of the Army Commander.

C - The referral of officers to the Disciplinary Council upon the proposal of the heads of the main institutions.

D - The deputation of military personnel to attend study or training courses or special missions abroad upon the proposal of the heads of the main institutions.

E - The categories and specifications of military supplies, provisions, weapons, equipment, ammunition, materiel, installations and vehicles and their models upon the proposal of the Army Commander.

F - The list of candidates to participate in the entrance competitive examination to the Military Academy.

G - The list of successful candidates in the entrance competitive examination to the Military Academy and those among them accepted into this Academy.

H - The entry of officers on the promotion tables for the rank of Captain and above in the various main institutions upon the proposal of the heads of these main institutions.

I - The appointment of the presidents and members of the tendering and reception committees upon the proposal of the Director General of Administration.

J - The appointment of liquidators and officers commissioned to sign expenditure contracts upon the proposal of the Director General of Administration.

3 - The Military Council shall draw up, and they shall be issued by a decision from the Minister of National Defence:

A - The standing instructions provided for by this Legislative Decree and which the Military Council deems necessary for the proper functioning of work in the main institutions.

B - The tables of personnel strength and the tables of equipment for the institutions of the Ministry of National Defence, and the methods of completing the personnel strength and equipment.

4 - The Military Council shall audit procurement transactions in their various stages, and shall examine on the merits the special books of specifications, and it shall have the right to approve them as submitted, to amend them or to reject them, provided that the files of the procurement transactions, after their approval, are submitted to the Minister of National Defence to take the measures provided for by the Public Accounting Law.

5 - The Military Council shall submit to the Minister of National Defence its recommendations regarding:

A - The draft budget of the Ministry of National Defence.

B - Strengthening defence and amending the defence policy.

C - Naming military attachés.

Meetings of the Military Council.

The Military Council shall meet periodically in accordance with a schedule determined by the President of the Council by a decision issued by him at the beginning of each year. The Council may also meet exceptionally upon the request of the Minister of National Defence, or an invitation from the President of the Military Council, or a request from half of its members. A meeting of the Council shall not be legal except in the presence of five members.

The decisions of the Military Council shall be issued by a majority, and in the event of a tie of votes, the President shall have a casting vote. The Chief of Staff shall assume the presidency of the Military Council in the event of the absence of the President.

The deliberations and decisions of the Military Council shall be of a strictly confidential nature.

Military personnel are volunteers, conscripts during the period of their service, and reservists during the period of their call-up:

- Volunteers are officers, non-commissioned officers, and enlisted men in active service.

- Conscripts are those subject to the Flag Service Law.

- Reservists are those subject to the Reserve Law.

Volunteering and its conditions.

1 - The volunteering of non-commissioned officers and enlisted men shall be accepted by a decision of the Army Commander within the limits of the vacant positions and the appropriations allocated in the budget.

2 - A volunteer is required:

a - To have been Lebanese for at least ten years.

b - To be not less than 18 years of age and not more than 25 years of age upon his confirmation in service. In exceptional cases decided by the Minister of National Defence upon the proposal of the Army Commander, the age may be raised to 30 years.

c - To be sound of body and of strong build.

d - Not to have been convicted of a felony or an attempted felony of any kind whatsoever, or of an infamous misdemeanour or an attempted infamous misdemeanour, or of imprisonment for a period exceeding six months, and these provisions shall apply to persons who have been rehabilitated and have benefited from an amnesty (general amnesty or special pardon).

The following misdemeanours shall be considered infamous: theft, fraud, breach of trust, embezzlement, bribery, rape, intimidation, forgery, use of forged documents, offences against public morals provided for in Title VII of the General Penal Code, drawing a cheque without funds, false testimony, false oath, offences related to narcotics.

3 - The Minister of National Defence may, by a decision issued by him upon the proposal of the Army Commander, impose additional conditions on applicants for volunteering in certain branches, cadres, and institutes of the Army relating to academic qualifications.

Appointment of Officers

1- Officers shall be appointed by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of National Defence.

2- Second Lieutenants shall be appointed from among:

a- Cadets of the Military Academy who have obtained the university degree (Bachelor's) in military sciences.

b- Non-commissioned officers, of the rank of Warrant Officer and above, after their success in a qualifying competition for the rank of Second Lieutenant in their specialty.

Hierarchy of Enlisted Personnel and Non-Commissioned Officers:

1 - Enlisted personnel: Private - Private First Class - Corporal - Master Corporal.

2 - Non-commissioned officers: Sergeant - Staff Sergeant - Warrant Officer - First Warrant Officer - Chief Warrant Officer - First Chief Warrant Officer.

Right of Command for Non-Commissioned Officers and Enlisted Personnel:

1 - Each non-commissioned officer has the right of command over those of lower rank, and where the rank is equal, command shall belong to the senior therein, and where seniority in the rank is equal, command shall belong to the senior in the preceding rank, and in the event of equal seniority in promotion to the rank of Master Corporal, command shall belong to the senior in promotion to the rank of Corporal.

2 - A Corporal has the right of command over Privates First Class, Privates, and Corporals whom he preceded to this promotion, and in the case of equal seniority in promotion to Corporal, command shall belong to the senior in promotion to Private First Class, and otherwise to the senior in service.

3 - In the event of equal rank between reservists and volunteers, command shall belong to the one who has greater seniority in active service for his rank.

Hierarchy of Officers:

The hierarchy of ranks of officers shall be determined as follows:

1 - Junior Officers: Second Lieutenant - First Lieutenant - Captain.

2 - Senior Officers: Major - Lieutenant Colonel - Colonel.

3 - General Officers: Brigadier General, Major General, General.

The rank of General shall be reserved for the Commander of the Army only.

Right of Command for Officers:

1 - Every officer has the right of command over those of lower rank.

2 - In the event of equal rank, command shall belong to the senior in the rank, and if seniority in the rank is equal, the order of names on the promotion decree to this rank shall be adopted.

3 - In the event of equal rank and seniority between volunteer officers and reserve officers who are called up to resume service, command shall belong to the officer who has greater seniority in active service for his rank.
Promotion is the transition from one rank to a higher rank.

Enlistment contract:

1 - With the exception of special cases provided for in this Legislative Decree, the appointment of volunteers in the Army shall take place pursuant to an enlistment contract the duration of which ranges between three years and ten years.

2 - The enlistment contract shall be signed by the Army Commander and the applicant.

3 - Immediately upon signing his enlistment contract, the volunteer shall be considered a trainee soldier for a maximum period of one year, during which military laws and regulations shall apply to him, and he shall not have the right to terminate his enlistment contract except for reasons approved by the Army Command.

4 - If the trainee soldier is not confirmed by the Volunteers Confirmation Committee, he shall be discharged without any compensation. However, if the year elapses without the Committee having examined his case, he shall be considered confirmed ipso jure, and the period he spent as a trainee soldier shall be included in the calculation of his service subject to the pension system, provided that the pension deductions therefor are paid.

5 - If the trainee soldier is afflicted, prior to his confirmation, with an accident or illness not attributable to service, he shall be discharged after his treatment for a maximum period of three months. However, if the accident or illness arises from service, the provisions governing conditions of disability shall apply to him.

Enlistment and appointment of specialist, technical and technological volunteers:

The types and cadres of specialists, technicians and technologists for the various categories and ranks, the allowances, the conditions of promotion and end of service, and the rights due from pension or severance compensation shall be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of National Defence following the recommendation of the Army Commander and after consulting the opinion of the State Council.

1 - Notwithstanding any text, the enlistment contract of specialist officer cadets in the Air Force shall be for a period of fifteen years, including the period of study at the rank of officer.

2 - The Minister of National Defence shall have the right to cancel the enlistment contract of the cadets mentioned in the first paragraph of this Article whose unfitness for service in the Air Force is established, upon the proposal of the Army Commander.

3 - The cadets mentioned in the paragraph above shall be given the choice between being discharged from service in the Army or continuing service in other forces compatible with their qualifications, and in this case the first enlistment contract shall be terminated and a new enlistment contract shall be drawn up for them in accordance with the provisions of Article 31 of this Legislative Decree.

Admission to military institutes:

Notwithstanding any other text, the conditions for the admission and appointment of officer cadets shall be determined, and their admission and appointment shall take place, by decisions issued by the Minister of National Defence upon the proposal of the Army Commander.

Promotion of non-commissioned officers and enlisted personnel:

1 - A private may not be promoted to private first class before completing one year in service, and the proportion of privates first class may not exceed (25 %) of the basic strength of privates and privates first class.

2 - Promotion to the rank of corporal shall not be permitted except after completing two years in service.

3 - A corporal shall not be promoted to master corporal except after completing one year in service in the rank of corporal, and the proportion of master corporals may not exceed (25 %) of the basic strength of corporals and master corporals.

4 - Promotion to the rank of sergeant up to chief warrant officer shall not be permitted unless the candidate has spent two years in the preceding rank, provided that seniority in service for a corporal and a master corporal shall be calculated together for promotion to the rank of sergeant.

5 - Non-commissioned officers and enlisted personnel may not be promoted unless they have fulfilled the legal conditions specified in special regulations issued by a decision of the Military Council.

6 - Direct superiors shall draw up nomination rosters for the promotion of non-commissioned officers and enlisted personnel, which shall be submitted through the chain of command to the Army Commander for decision.

7 - Promotion of non-commissioned officers and enlisted personnel shall take place by selection and by a decision of the Army Commander.

8 - Officer cadets of the Military Academy and cadets of the Non-Commissioned Officers' School, who are subject with regard to promotion to the provisions of the special regulations of each of these two schools, shall be exempted from the provisions of this Article.

9 - Non-commissioned officers and enlisted personnel may not be promoted after reaching the statutory age limit specified for their rank.

- While retaining their qualifying seniority for promotion, non-commissioned officers and enlisted personnel shall be promoted exceptionally, notwithstanding the conditions of promotion and even during the period of extension of their service, if it is proven that they performed distinguished acts during war operations, security maintenance operations, or an armed clash in the interior, pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of National Defence upon the proposal of the Army Commander and after the approval of the Military Council.

- Notwithstanding any other text, a non-commissioned officer or enlisted person who falls as a martyr in any of the circumstances mentioned above, or in an ordered aviation or navigation accident, shall be promoted to a higher rank, and the volunteer shall be deemed to have fallen as a martyr in the rank to which he was promoted, pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of National Defence upon the proposal of the Army Commander and after the approval of the Military Council.

- If the martyred non-commissioned officer or enlisted person had been designated to attend a course of study for a higher rank prior to the date of his martyrdom, he shall be promoted to that rank by a decision of the Minister of National Defence upon the proposal of the Army Commander and after the approval of the Military Council prior to the application of the provisions of the paragraph above.

- Notwithstanding any other text, a non-commissioned officer or enlisted person who falls as a martyr in any of the circumstances mentioned above, or in an ordered aviation or navigation accident, or who is killed or dies in accordance with what is specified in Item 1 of Article 94, in the event that he did not benefit from a promotion for distinguished acts for the same circumstance, shall be promoted to a higher rank, and the volunteer shall be deemed to have fallen as a martyr in the rank to which he was promoted, pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of National Defence upon the proposal of the Army Commander and after the approval of the Military Council.

10 - A chief warrant officer shall be promoted exceptionally to the rank of lieutenant upon the fulfilment of any of the cases set out in Item 9 above, in accordance with the rules governing the promotion of officers.

11 - Non-commissioned officers and enlisted personnel may not be promoted after being placed on retirement for reaching the statutory age limit, except in the event that they are recalled to resume service and perform outstanding acts of bravery, and in such case they shall benefit from the statutory age limit specified for the new rank.

12 - A cadet non-commissioned officer (first year - second year - third year) who is killed or dies in one of the circumstances specified in Item 1 of Article 94 of the National Defence Law shall be promoted to the rank of "sergeant", pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of National Defence upon the proposal of the Army Commander and after the approval of the Military Council, and the effects of Item 1 of Article 94 of the National Defence Law shall apply to him.

Promotion of Officers:

1 - Officers shall be promoted within the limits of vacant positions and within the appropriations allocated in the budget, provided that the candidate's name has been entered on the promotion roster. As for the Military Academy and all other military schools in Lebanon or abroad, the promotion of cadet officers therein shall be subject to regulations determined by a decision of the Minister of National Defence upon the proposal of the Commander of the Army, provided that promotion in these schools does not exceed the rank of Chief Warrant Officer and provided that the cadet officer has successfully completed the third year of study if it exceeds three years, including those he has spent at the Military Academy.

2 - The period spent in the rank of First Sergeant in accordance with the conditions of item (1) of this Article shall be counted as seniority in the rank of Lieutenant for promotion and for receiving the salary difference. As for the period spent in repeating years of study after promotion to the rank of Chief Warrant Officer, it shall not be counted towards seniority in the rank of Lieutenant nor for receiving the salary difference.

3 - In selecting a candidate for promotion, consideration shall be given to seniority in rank and service, his qualifications, his general, professional and disciplinary competencies, and the evaluation of his superiors.

4 - The promotion of officers shall be issued by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of National Defence.

5 - The names of candidates shall be entered on the promotion roster in accordance with their seniority in rank, and promotion shall take place in accordance with the order of this roster. However, priority may be given when ordering the names on the promotion roster to those who have distinguished themselves by their services.

- A Lieutenant shall be promoted to the rank of First Lieutenant:

- By examination after three years in the rank.

- By seniority after four years in the rank.

1 - Promotion to the rank of Captain, Colonel, or Major General shall take place by selection after the candidate has spent at least four years in the rank immediately below it.

2 - Promotion to the rank of Major, Lieutenant Colonel, or Brigadier General shall take place by selection after the candidate has spent at least five years in the rank immediately below it.

The percentage of officers graduated from the ranks out of the total number of officers specified in the Army cadre provided for in Article (21) of this Legislative Decree shall be determined by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of National Defence and the recommendation of the Commander of the Army.

Granting of seniority for promotion:

1 - Officers may be granted seniority for promotion ranging between three months and two years in recognition of outstanding acts which he performed during war operations, security maintenance operations, or an armed clash in the interior.

2 - Seniority for promotion shall be granted by decree upon the proposal of the Minister of National Defence based on the recommendation of the Army Commander and the approval of the Military Council.

1 - The nomination of officers for promotion shall take place once a year during the month of November. The nomination list must include all officers who have fulfilled the conditions for nomination.

2 - Exempted from the provisions of Clause (1) of this Article are the cadets of the Military Academy and all other schools for specialists and technicians, Second Lieutenants nominated for promotion to the rank of First Lieutenant, and Brigadiers nominated for the rank of Major General, as the promotion of cadets to the rank of Second Lieutenant shall take place in accordance with the procedures specified in the regulations of their institutes, and to the rank of First Lieutenant in accordance with the provisions of Article 43 of this Legislative Decree.

3 - Prior to the first of December of each year, the Army Commander shall submit to the Minister of National Defence draft decisions entering officers up to the rank of Colonel on the promotion roster.

4 - The Minister of National Defence shall issue and circulate during the month of December of each year a decision entering officers up to the rank of Colonel on the promotion roster on the basis of the drafts that are the subject of Clause (3) of this Article.

5 - The Minister of National Defence shall issue and circulate during the month of December of each year a decision entering officers for the rank of Brigadier on the promotion roster on the basis of the draft decisions that are the subject of Paragraph - h - 2 - of Article 27 of this Legislative Decree.

6 - Decrees promoting officers to the rank of Captain up to the rank of Brigadier shall be issued on the first of January and the first of July of each year, and the names of the officers shall be arranged in this decree in accordance with military hierarchy, with due regard to the provisions of Paragraph (5) of Article (42) of this Legislative Decree.

7 - The promotion of officers after their referral to retirement for having reached the statutory age shall not be permissible except in the event that they are recalled to resume service and perform prominent acts of bravery, in which case they shall benefit from the statutory age specified for the new rank.

8 - Notwithstanding any other text, an officer who is martyred during internal security-keeping operations or an armed clash, or in an aviation or navigation accident ordered of him, or who is killed or dies in accordance with what is specified in Clause 1 of Article 94, shall be promoted to a higher rank and shall be deemed martyred at the rank to which he is promoted.

If he was entered on the promotion roster for a higher rank prior to the date of his martyrdom, he may be promoted to this rank after granting him the necessary seniority prior to applying the provisions of the first part of this Clause.

Where the martyred officer held the rank of General, his entitlements shall be settled on the basis of the salary allocated to the highest step in his rank.

9 - In the event of the death of an officer without having exercised the right granted to him in Clauses 6, 7, 8 and 9 of Article 51 of this Legislative Decree on the basis of the seniority and nominations referred to in those Clauses, he may be referred to retirement at the higher rank after being promoted thereto and at the step to which he is entitled in this rank, notwithstanding any other text and whatever the duration of actual service he has completed.

10 - In the event of the death of an officer entered on the promotion roster for a higher rank, his promotion to this rank and to the step to which he is entitled therein shall take place and his entitlements shall be settled in accordance with the laws in force.

11 - An officer cadet (first year - second year - third year) who is killed or dies in one of the circumstances specified in Clause 1 of Article 94 of the National Defence Law shall be promoted to the rank of Second Lieutenant, and the effects of Clause 1 of Article 94 of the National Defence Law shall apply to him.

The rank of an officer is his property; he shall neither lose it nor be deprived thereof except in the cases provided for by law.
The placement of an officer in one of these statuses shall be decided by a decree adopted upon the proposal of the Minister of National Defence.

An officer who is in one of the following statuses:

- Temporary infirmity, shall remain counted within his cadre.

The Minister of National Defence, upon the proposal of the Commander of the Army, may recall him if the interest of the service so requires or if improvement appears in his conduct or in his health.

True Age for Discharge and Liquidation of the Retirement Pension:

1 - The age recorded in the first enlistment contract, based on the identity papers presented to the Enlistment Committee which approved their validity, shall be deemed the true age for discharge and for the liquidation of the retirement pension.

2 - The true age of volunteers who were in service on 19/1/1955 shall be deemed the age recorded pursuant to the 1932 census and thereafter, including the amendments made thereto prior to 1/8/1945 in accordance with the provisions in force, provided that the Ministry of National Defence was notified of these amendments within a maximum period of one full year from the date of their issuance. No amendment or correction after this date shall be acted upon, whether issued through non-contentious jurisdiction or through contentious jurisdiction.

3 - Age shall be calculated starting from the date of the day of birth recorded on the civil identity card. However, if the date of birth is unknown, the military person shall be deemed born on the first of July of the year established for his birth.

4 - In the liquidation of the retirement pension and the dismissal indemnity, the services performed by volunteers while under the statutory age shall be calculated if these services were completed between 2/9/1939 and 21/7/1945.

Postponement of Discharge The discharge of a volunteer shall be postponed even if he reaches the statutory age in the following cases:

1 - If he is in a status of infirmity that has not been adjudicated upon, and in this case he shall remain in his previous capacity until the issuance of the decisions of the Medical Committee.

2 - Pursuant to a decision of the Minister of National Defence based on the proposal of the Commander of the Army in cases of war or declaration of a state of emergency or while the Army is assigned to maintain security.

Discharge of Officers:

Subject to the provisions of Article (55) of this Legislative Decree, an officer shall be discharged ipso jure when he reaches the age or service limit indicated below:
