An officer shall be in one of the following statuses:

1 - Active service: which is the status of an officer performing his duties, or sick at home or in hospital, or absent on leave, furlough, or a mission, or in captivity.

2 - Interruption of service: which is the status of an officer removed from his duties temporarily or permanently for a disciplinary reason.

3 - Infirmity: an officer is deemed to be in the status of infirmity when he is unable to perform his duties for health reasons pursuant to a decision of the Medical Inquiry Committee, and infirmity shall be temporary or permanent.

4 - Resignation: which is the interruption of the officer from service upon his written request and the acceptance of his resignation by decree.

5 - Retirement: an officer is deemed retired:

a - Upon his discharge from service at his request after completing at least twenty years in service, including the period spent in the status of temporary infirmity.

b - Upon his mandatory discharge for reaching the legal age, provided that his service is not less than twenty years.

c - This amendment to the duration of service shall be adopted wherever it appears in this Legislative Decree

6 - A Brigadier General, upon reaching four years of seniority in his rank, shall have the right to submit a written resignation request once only, during the month of January for those who reach the said seniority on 1/1 and during the month of July for those who reach this seniority on 1/7; he shall then be referred to retirement and his entitlements shall be settled on the basis of his salary at the rank of Brigadier General had he remained in service until the age of fifty-eight, plus two steps, provided that on the date of exercising this right he is under fifty-six years of age.

7 - In the event that a Colonel is not promoted to a higher rank after his nomination for the first, second, or third time, he shall have the right to submit a written resignation request during the month of January for nominees on 1/1 and during the month of July for nominees on 1/7; he shall then be referred to retirement at the higher rank after being promoted thereto and at the step to which he is entitled in this rank, notwithstanding any other text and whatever the duration of active service he has spent.

8 - In the event that a Lieutenant Colonel is not promoted to a higher rank pursuant to his nomination for the first, second, or third time, he shall have the right to submit a written resignation request during the month of January for nominees on 1/1 and during the month of July for nominees on 1/7; he shall then be referred to retirement at the higher rank after being promoted thereto and at the step to which he is entitled in this rank, notwithstanding any other text and whatever the duration of active service he has spent.

9 - In the event that a Captain is not promoted to a higher rank pursuant to his nomination for the third time, he shall have the right to submit a written resignation request during the month of January; he shall then be referred to retirement at the higher rank after being promoted thereto and at the step to which he is entitled in this rank, notwithstanding any other text and whatever the duration of active service he has spent. Excluded from the provisions of this item are officers who are appointed directly as specialist officers and have not completed fifteen years in active service.

10 - The calculation of the number of nominations for promotion to a higher rank for the officers who are the subject of items 7, 8, and 9 of this Article shall commence after the effective date of this Law.

11- In the event that a Colonel, Lieutenant Colonel, or Captain does not exercise the right provided for in items 7, 8, and 9 of this Article, he shall then continue in his rank until the end of his service and shall lose the right to nomination for promotion and even to promotion to a higher rank.

12 - Exceptionally, and within a period of one month from the date of publication of this Law, Brigadier Generals in active service not covered by Law No. 217 dated 29/5/2000, and Colonels and Lieutenant Colonels in active service, shall have the right to submit their resignation and be referred to retirement whatever the duration of their service, and their entitlements shall be settled as follows:

- Brigadier Generals: their entitlements shall be settled on the basis of the salary to which each of them would have been entitled had he remained in service until the age of fifty-eight, plus four steps, provided that it does not exceed the eleventh step in this rank.

- Colonels: their entitlements shall be settled on the basis of the higher rank after their promotion thereto and in accordance with the following:

- Those who have seniority in their rank of up to two years shall be taken at the step to which they are entitled upon promotion, plus one step.

- Those who have seniority in their rank of more than two years and up to four years shall be taken at the step to which they are entitled, plus two steps.

- Those who have seniority in their rank of more than four years shall be taken at the step to which they are entitled, plus three steps.

- Lieutenant Colonels: their entitlements shall be settled on the basis of the higher rank after their promotion thereto and in accordance with the following:

- Those who have seniority in their rank of up to two years shall be taken at the step to which they are entitled upon promotion, plus one step.

- Those who have seniority in their rank of more than two years and up to three years shall be taken at the step to which they are entitled, plus two steps.

- Those who have seniority in their rank of more than three years shall be taken at the step to which they are entitled, plus three steps.

- All officers whose names were placed on the promotion rosters during the year of issuance of this Law and for the same year shall benefit from the provisions of the above paragraphs of item 12 in accordance with the rank to which they are nominated.

Discharge of non-commissioned officers and enlisted personnel Subject to the provisions of Article 55 of this Legislative Decree, non-commissioned officers and enlisted personnel shall be discharged pursuant to a decision issued by the Army Commander, in the following cases:

1- By operation of law: upon their reaching the statutory age limit, which is the following:

a - For non-commissioned officers: 48 years

b - For enlisted personnel: 45 years

2 - Discretionarily:

Upon their completing the statutory period that entitles them to obtain a retirement pension, which is eighteen years. This period shall be reduced to fifteen years in respect of volunteers who are in service on the date of entry into force of this Legislative Decree in the event that they reach the statutory age limit prior to completing a service period of eighteen years.

3 - Upon their request: upon the expiry of their enlistment contract and their unwillingness to renew it.

4 - For health reasons: if their state of health does not permit them to continue in service, pursuant to a decision of the Medical Inquiry Committee.

5 - Upon the expiry of the enlistment contract if the Army Commander does not approve its renewal.

6 - By expulsion:

a - If a penal judgment providing for expulsion is issued against them.

b - For disciplinary reasons pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of National Defence on the basis of the opinion of the Inquiry Committee in accordance with the provisions of Article 65 of this Legislative Decree.

Prohibited Acts:

1 - Military personnel in active service are prohibited from joining professional syndicates without obtaining a prior authorisation from the Army Command.

2 - Military personnel who are members of syndicates are prohibited, on pain of the penalties provided for in the laws and regulations in force, from the following:

a - Undertaking any electoral activity, participating in elections, or being elected to the councils and bodies of the said syndicates (by nomination, voting, or election).

b - Undertaking any act incompatible with the military instructions, regulations, and laws in force.

3 - Military personnel in active service are prohibited, on pain of the penalties provided for in the laws and regulations in force, from:

a - Joining political parties and associations.

b - Attending political and partisan meetings.

c - Publishing articles, delivering lectures, or making statements to the media prior to obtaining a prior permission issued by the Minister of National Defence.

d - Practising any remunerated work outside the Ministry of National Defence.

e - Striking from work or inciting thereto.

f - Organising or signing collective petitions on any subject whatsoever.

g - Acts that offend public decency and morals.

The decree of the General Disciplinary Regulations for volunteers shall observe the following provisions:

1 - The penalties set out in paragraphs 11- 12- 15- 16- 17 - 18 of Article 62- above shall be imposed on non-commissioned officers and enlisted personnel pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of National Defence following the approval of the Military Council based on the report of the Investigation Committee.

2 - The penalties set out in paragraphs 13 to 18 of Article 62 above shall be executed upon officers by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of National Defence based on the decision of the Disciplinary Council.
The value of deductions from salary by reason of a penalty shall revert as revenue to the Treasury.

The Investigation Committee:

The Minister of National Defence shall appoint, upon the proposal of the Military Council and by a decision from him at the beginning of each year, a committee of three officers called the Investigation Committee.

1 - The Disciplinary Council shall be formed by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of National Defence of two members holding the rank of Colonel and above, and it shall be chaired by a General Officer, and the Government shall be represented before it by an officer called the Government Commissioner before the Disciplinary Council.

2 - The Disciplinary Council shall examine serious disciplinary infractions the penalties for which are set out in the second paragraph of Article 63 above.

3 - The Disciplinary Council shall issue decisions of a judicial nature subject to appeal before the Military Court of- Cassation within a time limit of fifteen days from the date of notification.

4 - The manner of referring the case before the Disciplinary Council and the rules of trial procedure before it shall be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers after consulting the opinion of the State Council.

1 - The nature and rules of training inside the country shall be determined by a decision of the Commander of the Army pursuant to standing instructions within the following framework:

A - Basic training for all military personnel upon their volunteering.

B - Supplementary training in each specialisation.

2 - The nature of study and training courses outside the country and the conditions of nomination and selection therefor shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of National Defence upon the proposal of the Commander of the Army in accordance with the needs of the Army.

1 - The following shall benefit from free medical care and treatment:

(a) Military personnel in active service and their families, including lawful wives who engage in paid work, provided that they do not receive medical care and treatment expenses from another authority. The manner of applying this provision shall be determined by special instructions issued by the Minister of National Defence.

(b) Military personnel whom it has been decided to place in permanent disability for health reasons attributable to service, and their families who remain dependent.

(c) Retired military personnel who are entitled to a retirement pension and the members of their families who remain dependent on them.

(d) Retired military personnel who are entitled to a retirement pension, yet have received severance compensation, and the members of their families who remain dependent on them.

(e) The families of volunteers who were martyred in service or who died during the performance of service or by reason thereof, whatever their service may be, who remain dependent.

(f) The members of the families of volunteers who remain dependent, in respect of volunteers who died following an illness or an accident not attributable to service, provided that they have spent at least five years in active service."

(g) The members of the families of deceased retired military personnel who remain dependent.

2 - Every member of the families referred to in sub-paragraphs: "b, c, d, e, f, g" of this Article must fulfil the conditions prescribed by law to benefit from the retirement pension, with the exception of lawful wives who engage in paid work, provided that they do not receive medical care and treatment expenses from another authority.

The manner of applying this provision shall be determined by special instructions issued by the Minister of National Defence.

3 - The Minister of Defence may, upon the proposal of the Commander of the Army, suspend the benefit of free medical care and treatment on each occasion for a maximum period of one year for anyone who abuses this right.

1 - The salaries of volunteers are determined in the laws in force. As for allowances of all kinds, they shall be determined pursuant to a decree taken in the Council of Ministers.

2 - The method of payment and settlement of salaries, allowances, and emoluments shall be determined by instructions issued by the Minister of National Defence upon the proposal of the Commander of the Army.

Active service:

The volunteer shall receive the full salary, allowances, and emoluments supplementary to the salary.

Convalescence:

The volunteer shall receive the active service salary for a maximum period of three months.

Rewards:

Rewards shall be determined as follows:

1 - Oral congratulation.

2 - Written congratulation.

3 - Reward leave.

4 - Financial awards (for non-commissioned officers and enlisted personnel).

5 - Commendation.

6 - Decorations.

7 - Granting seniority for promotion in accordance with Article (47) of this Legislative Decree.

8 - Exceptional promotion in accordance with Articles (41 and 48) of this Legislative Decree.

Leaves:

1 - Volunteers shall be granted leave of thirty days with active-duty pay for each year they have spent in service, and it may exceptionally be raised to 45 days with active-duty pay by a decision of the Army Commander as a reward for distinguished service.

2 - Volunteers shall be granted exceptional leave with active-duty pay of up to seven days on grounds of the death of one of his ascendants, descendants, brothers, or sisters, and of up to four days for other family reasons.

3 - Volunteers may, upon their request, be granted leave without pay for a period of three months renewable once, which shall be counted as an interruption of service.

4 - The duration of leave may be reduced or cancelled for anyone whose services are unsatisfactory.

Volunteers who violate military laws and regulations shall be subject, in addition to the penalties imposed upon them by the military courts, to disciplinary penalties.

A volunteer shall not be prosecuted if the offence arises out of the function except after the issuance of permission to prosecute him by the Minister of National Defence upon the proposal of the Army Commander.

Disciplinary penalties:

1 - Oral remark.

2 - Written remark.

3 - Reprimand.

4 - Confinement to quarters for a maximum period of fifteen days.

5 - Reduction or cancellation of leave.

6 - Arrest for a maximum period of sixty days.

7 - Arrest for a maximum period of sixty days with deduction of pay.

8 - Fortress arrest for a maximum period of sixty days.

9 - Disciplinary transfer.

10 - Assignment to disciplinary detachments.

11 - Delay of promotion.

12 - Striking off the promotion roster.

13 - Temporary interruption of service.

14 - Permanent interruption of service.

15 - Disciplinary placement on retirement.

16 - Reduction in rank.

17 - Loss of rank.

18 - Disciplinary discharge.

19 - Total or partial pecuniary fine due to the loss or destruction of equipment and supplies.

Elements of the retirement pension and the severance indemnity.

1 - The following elements shall enter into the calculation for the liquidation of the retirement pension or the severance indemnity: the number of years of active service, the supplements, and the additions.

2 - The supplements added to the years of active service are:

a - Twice the duration of active services completed in the zone of military operations in time of war or during security-keeping operations of the first degree in times of war and peace.

b - Once the duration of active services completed outside the zone of military operations in time of war and during security-keeping operations of the second degree in times of peace and war.

c - Half the duration of active services completed on the front lines during a truce or during security-keeping operations of the third degree in times of peace and war.

d - An addition equivalent to three days for every hour of military flight for airmen and student pilots, provided that the total of these additions does not exceed 18 months for each year of active service, and only half thereof shall be counted when receiving the severance indemnity.

The additions that are the subject of paragraph "d" shall be counted in full for the liquidation of the retirement pension within the maximum limit provided for in Article 82 of this Legislative Decree, and only half thereof shall be counted when receiving the severance indemnity.

e - An addition equivalent to three months for each year of active service in time of peace aboard a naval unit in Lebanon or abroad.

f - An addition for specialist officers equivalent to the number of years of university study which they pursued at their own expense.

g - An addition for specialist physicians equivalent to the number of years of university and specialist study which they pursued at their expense.

h - Disability additions, which are granted to volunteers who have acquired the right to a retirement pension if it is established upon their referral to retirement that they are afflicted with a disability resulting from wounds or illnesses attributable to service or aggravated by reason thereof, and these additions shall be calculated as follows:

- One year if the degree of disability is ten percent and below twenty.

- Two years if the degree of disability is 20 percent and below 40 percent.

- Three years if the degree of disability is 40 percent and below 60 percent.

- Four years if the degree of disability is 60 percent and below 70 percent.

- Five years if the degree of disability is 70 percent and below 80 percent.

- Six years if the degree of disability is 80 percent and below 90 percent.

- Seven years if the degree of disability is 90 percent and above.

3 - The supplements and additions provided for in Clause Two of this Article shall not confer upon the volunteer a right to a retirement pension if he has not completed in active service the minimum duration specified in this Legislative Decree, but they shall enter into the calculation of the severance indemnity.

With the exception of the additions that are the subject of paragraphs f - g - h, which shall only enter into the calculation of retirement.

4 - The supplements and additions shall be calculated in months, and fractions of a month shall be disregarded after summing the supplements and additions with the active services, and whatever exceeds 24 months of supplements and additions for each year of active service shall likewise be disregarded.

5 - The zones, circumstances, and cases that confer the right to war supplements shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of National Defence.

Allowances during a State of Emergency or War:

In the event that a state of emergency or war is declared, a volunteer shall be granted an allowance equivalent to one month's salary and all salary-supplementing allowances and emoluments:

1 - Each time a general state of emergency or a state of war is declared, and this paragraph shall apply to all volunteers in active service on Lebanese territory.

2 - Each time a partial state of emergency is declared in a given region, the allowance shall be granted to a volunteer present in this region.

3 - The same allowance shall be granted to reservists who resume service, upon the lapse of one month from their resumption of this service.

4 - The same allowance shall be granted to civilians and to volunteers attached to the Ministry of National Defence in the event that they are confined to their posts by virtue of the need for them.

Calculation of Retirement Pensions:

1 - The retirement pension shall be liquidated on the basis of one-fortieth of the last monthly salary, calculated in accordance with the provisions of the following Clause (2), multiplied by the number of years of service up to forty years only, and the volunteer or the family of a volunteer deceased in service shall be granted, in addition thereto, a severance indemnity equivalent to three months' salary for each year beyond forty.

2 - For the purpose of calculating the retirement pension and the severance indemnity, there shall be added to the last basic monthly salary that the volunteer was receiving on the date of termination of his service or on the date of his death, one twenty-fourth of the value of his last step in active service multiplied by the number of months that the volunteer has spent in service following his last step advancement.

- The product shall be multiplied by a rate of 85% (eighty-five percent).

For the purpose of calculating the retirement pension and the severance indemnity for military personnel whose service ended during the years 1996, 1997 and 1998, there shall apply to them the provisions of this Law that apply to their peers whose service ended after 1/1/1999, including the conversion of salaries and the new bases for calculating the retirement pension and the severance indemnity, and their entitlements shall be re-liquidated on this basis.

The retirement pension and the severance indemnity calculated in accordance with the preceding paragraphs of this Article may not be less than the retirement pension and the severance indemnity calculated in accordance with the provisions of the laws previously in force.

Infirmity:

1 - Temporary infirmity: for a period of one year renewable for another year.

a - Infirmity attributable to service: the volunteer shall receive the active service salary and all allowances and indemnities supplementary thereto.

b - Infirmity not attributable to service: the volunteer shall receive half the salary and all allowances and indemnities supplementary to the salary

c - This salary shall be subject to retirement deductions on the full salary and to income tax and stamp deductions on the salary which he receives.

2 - Permanent infirmity: the retirement rights or severance indemnity of the volunteer shall be settled in accordance with the provisions of this Legislative Decree.

Cessation of service (for officers only):

1 - Temporary cessation of service (for a maximum period of two years) the officer shall receive one-third of the salary and all allowances and indemnities supplementary to the salary, and this salary shall not be subject to retirement deductions, but shall be subject to income tax and stamp deductions.

2 - Permanent cessation of service: the retirement rights or severance indemnity of the officer shall be settled in accordance with the provisions of this Legislative Decree.

Absence:

1 - Lawful absence: is the absence resulting from force majeure for a maximum period of one year during which the right holder shall receive his salary, and thereafter the decision to determine his status shall rest with the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of National Defence.

2 - Unlawful absence: the salary of the volunteer shall be suspended as from the first of the month following the absence until the date of his rejoining if he does not rejoin.

Disappearance:

If the volunteer goes missing during service or by reason thereof and news of him ceases such that it is not known whether he is alive or dead, the right holder shall receive the full attendance salary for a period of two years.

This period may, by decree upon the proposal of the Minister of National Defence, be fixed at up to ten years as a maximum limit.

The period of years during which the missing volunteer receives the attendance salary pursuant to the provisions of the two preceding paragraphs shall be considered active service, after which the missing volunteer shall be automatically referred to retirement and his rights shall be settled in favour of his lawful heirs in accordance with the provisions in force.

All military personnel who have reached the maximum limit in the state of disappearance prior to the entry into force of this Law shall benefit from the provisions of the paragraph above.

Resignation:

The severance indemnity or retirement pension shall be paid to the volunteer, and if he is not entitled thereto, he shall recover the retirement deductions that were deducted from his salaries.

Retirement:

The volunteer shall receive his rights in accordance with the texts set forth in this Legislative Decree.

Adjustment of the retirement pension:

1 - The retirement pension may not be adjusted unless the pensioner performs new service for a period of at least one continuous or interrupted year, and periods of compulsory training which reservists are called upon to perform shall not be included in the calculation of this period unless the period exceeds thirty continuous days.

2 - The retirement pension shall not be added to the active service salary or its equivalent except for reservists in the event that they are called up, and within the limits of Articles 137 and 138 of this Legislative Decree.

3 - The pension of an enlisted volunteer retiring after 1/7/1974 may not be less than the pension of an enlisted volunteer who retired before this date and benefited from the provisions of Law No. 40/64 issued on 17/12/1964 if he has the same seniority in service and rank or exceeds it.

The right to choose between the retirement pension and severance pay.

1 - Every officer who is discharged after acquiring the right to claim a retirement pension, and who has at least twenty-five years in active service, shall have the right within one month from the date of his discharge to request the substitution of this pension with the severance pay provided for in Article 91 of this Legislative Decree.

2 - Every enlisted volunteer other than an officer who is discharged after acquiring the right to claim the retirement pension shall be allocated this pension and shall not have the right to request its substitution with severance pay unless he is placed on retirement for having reached the legal age.

3 - An enlisted volunteer who joins State institutions after his discharge shall not receive severance pay or a retirement pension; rather, the period he spent at the Ministry of National Defence shall be added to his subsequent service in the State.

Types of disability pension:

1 - The disability pension shall be allocated to enlisted volunteers who are permanently placed on retirement for health reasons resulting from illnesses or wounds attributable to service.

2 - The disability pension shall be:

A - Temporary when the infirmity is incurable and the degree of disablement is subject to increase or decrease.

B - Permanent when the infirmity is incurable and the degree of disablement has been permanently determined within four years from the date of discharge.

Aggregation of previous services:

1 - There shall be counted for retirement and in the salary grade and the services which he spent in one of the armies and military formations set forth below, for every Lebanese military person who was under arms on 2/10/1950; as for the military formations and armies concerned, they are the following:

a - The Gendarmerie and all other military formations that were affiliated with the State covered by the French Mandate.

b - The formations of the regular Allied armies during the 1939- 1945 war.

- These services shall not be counted unless the retirement deductions have been paid in respect thereof and the military person was under arms on 20/6/1963.

- These retirement deductions shall be calculated on the basis of the salaries of the Special Armies of the East, whereas the supplementary war allowances completed during this period shall enter into the calculation of the retirement pension and the severance indemnity.

2 - If the volunteer is returned to active service, he shall be entitled to request the inclusion of his previous services in the calculation of his retirement pension or in the severance indemnity, provided that he submits a request to that effect within a period of three months calculated as from the date of his return to service and that he refunds to the Treasury the amounts that he received pursuant to the provisions of this Legislative Decree in the following manner:

a - By deducting 15 percent from his salary subject to retirement deductions if he is called to resume service as a reservist.

b - In a single payment or in monthly instalments for the duration of his new enlistment contract if he resumes service at his own request.

3 - If he is discharged again, the following measures shall be taken:

a - If he is discharged for health reasons not attributable to service or at his own request before paying these instalments in full, he shall be granted the severance indemnity instead of retirement, and the balance of the debt due from him shall be deducted therefrom.

b - If he is discharged by expulsion before paying the instalments in full, half of the paid instalments shall be refunded to him and his rights shall be liquidated on the basis of his new service.

c - However, if he is discharged for health reasons attributable to service and receives a retirement pension, the deduction of the fifteen percent from his retirement pension shall be maintained until payment thereof, and if he receives the severance indemnity, the balance of the debt due from him shall be deducted therefrom.

4 - However, if he dies during service for any reason whatsoever, the provisions of paragraph (c) of item (3) of this Article shall apply to his heirs.

Invalidity pensions and severance pay for volunteers who are finally discharged for health reasons shall be liquidated according to the degree of disability as follows:

1 - If the volunteer is discharged, regardless of his seniority in service, for having sustained an infirmity, diseases or wounds in one of the following cases:

- During an armed clash with an enemy, gangs or groups disrupting security.

- Following an assault to which he was subjected during the performance of his duty.

- His performance of an act of bravery to save the life of others.

- During military manoeuvres, baptism of fire, or during other executed trainings.

He shall receive an invalidity pension equivalent to:

A - 60 % of the last month's salary subject to pension deductions if the degree of disability is 30 % and below 50 %

B - 85 % of the last month's salary subject to pension deductions if the degree of disability is 50 % and below 75 %

C - 75 % of the salary subject to pension deductions allocated to the highest step of the rank immediately above his rank, including the steps above the ceiling, if the degree of disability is 75 % and above, with the clarification that the pension allocated to a corporal and a cadet non-commissioned officer shall be calculated on the basis of the rank of sergeant, and the pension allocated to a chief warrant officer and a cadet officer shall be calculated on the basis of the rank of lieutenant, provided that the salary of the rank above his rank exceeds by at least one step the salary to which he is entitled for his rank.

D - 30 % of the last month's salary subject to pension deductions if the degree of disability is 20 % and below 30 %

E - However, if the degree of his disability is below 20 %, he shall receive the severance pay plus one hundred percent.

2 - If the volunteer is discharged, regardless of his seniority in service, for having sustained an infirmity or ailment resulting from diseases, wounds or accidents arising from the service in cases other than those set out in Clause 1 of this Article, he shall receive an invalidity pension equivalent to:

A - One third of the last month's salary subject to pension deductions if the degree of disability is 30 % and below 50 %

B - Half of the last month's salary subject to pension deductions if the degree of disability is 50 % and below 75 %

C - 75 % of the last month's salary subject to pension deductions if the degree of disability is above 75 %

D - One quarter of the last month's salary subject to pension deductions if the degree of disability is 20 % and below 30 %

E - However, if the degree of his disability is below 20 %, he shall receive the severance pay plus 75 %

3 - If the volunteer is discharged for having sustained an accident or disease not attributable to the service, yet aggravated by reason thereof, his rights shall be liquidated as follows:

A - If he has completed 15 years in service, he shall be granted a retirement pension on the basis of his services, including 50 % of the disability supplements provided for in Article 80 of this Legislative Decree.

B - If he has not completed fifteen years in service, he shall be granted the severance pay due to him plus an addition of 30 % of this pay.

4 - If the volunteer has completed fifteen years, he shall be placed on retirement and shall benefit from the supplements - provided for in Article 80 of this Legislative Decree and according to the degree of disability.

5 - If the rights of the volunteer after liquidation in accordance with Clauses 1, 2 and 3 of this Article differ from his rights in accordance with Clause 4 of this Article, he shall be granted the most favourable rights.

Determination of the temporary disability pension .

1 - The temporary disability pension for volunteers of various ranks shall be determined for a period of two years which may be renewed once after a medical examination, and the temporary disability pension shall be reviewed for increase or decrease at the end of each period if the disablement undergoes a modification of not less than 10 per cent. In all cases, the temporary disability pension may not be increased if the increase in the degree of disablement results wholly or partially from factors extraneous to the primary cause of the disability, such as old age, exhaustion, intemperance, misconduct, etc...

2 - The disability pension shall be cancelled when the degree of disablement ceases or its percentage becomes such as not to entitle the holder to claim this pension, and the following measures shall be taken:

a - The sums received by the volunteer while in temporary disability shall remain a vested right for him.

b - The competent authority may, if he fulfils the conditions of fitness for military service, reinstate him into active service either to complete the period of his previous volunteer contract which was suspended due to his disability or pursuant to a new contract.

c - The rights of the person concerned (retirement- severance indemnity ) shall be liquidated upon his final discharge in accordance with the laws in force on the basis of the total completed services.

d - The person concerned shall be entitled, in the event that he does not resume service, to claim the severance indemnity or the pension deductions in accordance with the laws in force starting from the date of cancellation of his temporary disability pension on the total of his services prior to the status of temporary disability, taking into account the remaining degree of disablement.

e - The time spent by the volunteer in retirement due to temporary disability shall not be counted as active service.

f - The authority that decided to grant the temporary disability pension is the one that decides to cancel it for the reasons set forth in the first paragraph of this Article.

Affliction with insanity, blindness or paralysis If a volunteer is afflicted with insanity after completing five years and above in service, he shall receive a disability pension equivalent to half the salary of the last month subject to pension deductions and the full family allowance.

He shall receive such a salary regardless of the duration of his service in the event that he is afflicted, in circumstances not attributable to service, with general paralysis, or total blindness, or weakness of sight to a degree threatening total blindness within four years from the occurrence of the affliction, or with similar infirmities that render the afflicted person incapable of attending to his personal affairs, provided that such infirmities are determined by the Health Investigation Committee.

Right to choose the larger pension If a volunteer is entitled to a temporary or permanent disability pension and his services confer upon him a right to a retirement pension, he shall benefit from the larger of the two pensions in amount.

Granting family allowances to retirees:

Retired military personnel shall receive the family allowances provided for in the laws in force.

The right to severance indemnity or to retirement deductions shall arise in the following manner:

1 - Every non-commissioned officer or enlisted man who is discharged from service in accordance with the provisions of paragraph (3) of Article 57 of this Legislative Decree before acquiring the right to claim a retirement pension shall be subject to the following provisions:

a - The retirement deductions withheld from his salaries shall be refunded to him if his actual service is less than ten years.

b - He shall be granted severance indemnity if his service is ten years and above.

2 - Every non-commissioned officer or enlisted man who is discharged from service in accordance with the provisions of items 4 and 5 of Article 57 of this Legislative Decree shall be granted severance indemnity regardless of his seniority in service.

However, if he is discharged pursuant to the provisions of item 6 of the aforementioned Article, he shall only be granted half of his rights.

3 - Every officer who is discharged before acquiring the right to claim a retirement pension shall be subject to the following provisions:

a - He shall receive severance indemnity:

- If he is permanently discharged from service in accordance with the provisions of Articles 51 and 53 of this Legislative Decree, with the exception of resignation, even if he has not completed ten years in service.

- If he is a pilot officer and is discharged from service at his request, provided that he has completed at least 12 years of actual service, including eight years as a licensed pilot officer in air operations.

- If he is a specialist officer and is discharged from service upon his written request in accordance with the provisions and regulations in force in the Army for a minimum period of five years.

b - He shall receive severance indemnity and an addition of five thousand Lebanese pounds:

- A pilot officer discharged with severance indemnity, provided that his actual service has not reached 15 years and that a period of eighteen months has elapsed since his return from a study course abroad.

c - He shall receive severance indemnity in the event of his resignation after completing ten years in service, and in the event of his resignation before completing ten years in service, he shall receive the retirement deductions.

Calculation of the severance indemnity:

1 - The severance indemnity provided for in Article 91 and specified in item (2) of Article 79 shall be calculated as follows:

a - One month's salary for each year of the first ten years in service.

b - Two months' salary for each year of the years following the tenth year and up to thirty years in service.

c - Three months' salary for each year exceeding thirty years in service.

2 - The additions and supplements provided for in Article 80 shall be included in the calculation of the severance indemnity when the actual services are ten years and above.

3 - An enlisted volunteer discharged from service for health reasons, if his actual services are less than ten years, shall be granted a severance indemnity equivalent to:

- One month's salary for each year of actual service.

- Two months' salary for each additional year.

Limits of the severance indemnity:

Severance indemnities from service shall be granted within the limits set forth in this Legislative Decree.

Assistance to the families of deceased volunteers:

In addition to the retirement pension, the families of the volunteers who are the subject of Article 94 above shall be granted the material assistance set forth below:

1 - A volunteer who is the subject of either Item 1 or 2 of Article 94:

a - Financial assistance equivalent to one year's salary, including the allowances supplementary to the salary of a volunteer who dies in active service.

b - His children shall be admitted to schools at the expense of the State within the limits of the appropriations allocated therefor in the budget.

2 - A volunteer who is the subject of Article 94 - 3: financial assistance equivalent to one year's salary, including the allowances supplementary to the salary of a volunteer who dies in active service.

3 - A volunteer who is the subject of either Item 4 or 5 of Article 94:

Financial assistance equivalent to six months' salary, including the allowances supplementary to the salary of a volunteer who dies in active service.

Notwithstanding any other provision, the spouse of a martyr of the field of honour shall benefit from his full share of the retirement pension or of the severance indemnity and in the Mutual Fund, regardless of his financial situation.

The share of the parents in the entitlements of a martyred or deceased volunteer .

1 - The father and mother of a martyred volunteer shall receive their share in the retirement pension or in the severance indemnity and in the Mutual Fund, regardless of their financial or family situation, if he was unmarried or married without children; and in the event of the martyrdom of an unmarried volunteer after the death of his parents, his minor or disabled brothers and his unmarried sisters shall receive the share of their parents in the retirement pension or in the severance indemnity and in the Mutual Fund. The provisions of the preceding paragraph shall apply as of the date of 16/9/1983.

2 - The father and mother of a volunteer who dies in service or in retirement shall receive their share in the retirement pension or in the severance indemnity and in the Mutual Fund, even if they have one or more other children besides the deceased, provided that the following conditions are met cumulatively:

a - If the deceased was unmarried or married without children.

b - If the father is unable to work.

c - If the father and mother are of poor means.

As for the widowed mother, she shall receive her share if she is of poor means, regardless of the family situation of her deceased child.

Financial grant to the father of the deceased volunteer:

1 - The father of the deceased single volunteer or volunteer married without children and his mother, if they do not fulfil the conditions specified in Article 96 for receiving a retirement pension or a dismissal indemnity, shall receive a financial grant to settle the funeral expenses of their son, and this grant shall be determined as follows:

a - One year's salary, including the allowances supplementary to the salary of the volunteer deceased in active service, if the death resulted from the circumstances specified in Article 94 (1) of this Legislative Decree.

b - Six months' salary, including the allowances supplementary to the salary of the volunteer deceased in active service, if the death resulted from the circumstances specified in Clauses 2 and 3 of Article 94 of this Legislative Decree.

c - Three months' salary, including the allowances supplementary to the salary of the volunteer deceased in active service, if the death resulted from the circumstances specified in either the fourth or fifth clause of Article 94 of this Legislative Decree.

2 - The grants specified in this Article shall be given to the person who advances the funeral expenses, whether the father or the mother; however, if it is not possible for the father or the mother to receive the grant, it shall be given to one of the relatives of the deceased serviceman who undertakes the funeral expenses.

The wife of the General, Commander of the Army, who dies in active service and by reason thereof, as long as she has not lost her right to the retirement pension or the indemnity for dismissal from service, shall continue to benefit from one military car driver or from an allowance equivalent to the salary of a first step, at her choice.

Committee for the Liquidation of Retirement Pensions and Dismissal Indemnity:

A Committee for the Liquidation of Retirement Pensions and Dismissal Indemnities shall be formed by decree. This Committee shall be composed of:

- A commanding officer or a general officer - as Chairman.

- Two officers - as two members.

- An employee from the Ministry of Finance with the rank of Head of Department and above - as a member.

- The Head of the Retirement Bureau in the Army - as a member and rapporteur.

The manner and procedures for completing the administrative and financial transactions pertaining to the Ministry of National Defence shall be determined by virtue of a decree taken in the Council of Ministers, in which the principles and procedures provided for in the laws and regulations in force in the State shall be observed.

The provisions relating to State employees shall apply to civilian employees in the permanent and temporary cadres, contracted personnel, and wage earners in the Ministry of National Defence in all matters regarding which no special provision for them is stipulated in the laws and regulations in force in the Ministry of National Defence.

Service to the Flag is an honour and a duty to which Lebanese males are subject pursuant to the provisions of this Legislative Decree and the regulations completing it.

Service to the Flag includes:

- Military service.

- Civil service.

- Developmental service.

Military service aims to prepare the citizen as a combatant and employ him so that he carries out, within the scope of national defence, the tasks of military defence in the Armed Forces.

Civil service aims to prepare the citizen and employ him to support the Armed Forces in all that relates to internal and external defence, and particularly in the field of civil defence and in supporting the public and private sectors that facilitate the tasks of the Armed Forces.

Developmental service aims to prepare the citizen and employ him within the scope of national defence to carry out his share of the social effort to develop the various public sectors and the private sectors of public utility inside and outside the country.

The Ministry of National Defence assumes the task of executing Service to the Flag in its various forms in coordination with the competent Ministries of the State.

Lebanese males shall be compulsorily subject to Service to the Flag after completing their eighteenth year of age, whereas Lebanese females shall be subject to this service when necessary by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers in which the conditions and fields of their employment are determined.

The duration of Service to the Flag is reduced to six months until the final abolition provided for in the first Article of this Law.

- Everyone who has actually performed military service, civil service, or developmental service shall be deemed to have fulfilled the duty of Service to the Flag and consequently acquires the status of reserve conscript.

- Conscripts are taken in the capacity of officers, non-commissioned officers, or enlisted men in accordance with the conditions determined by the Ministry of National Defence - Army Command.

In accordance with the need of the Army Command and the Armed Forces, the service of those conscripted non-commissioned officers and enlisted men who so wish may be extended after the end of their compulsory service for a period not exceeding five years at the rank in which they were, during which they shall receive a monthly allowance equivalent to the salary of the first step due for the rank of volunteer in which each of them is, and all legal provisions governing the status of conscripts shall apply to them throughout the duration of their service. The conscript who extended his service retains the right to terminate his service at the end of any year of the years of extension.

The Ministry of the Interior - Directorate General of Personal Status sends in the first month of each year - to the Ministry of National Defence - Army Command - lists containing the information determined by the Ministry of National Defence - Army Command.

Transfer of retirement pensions and dismissal indemnities to the families of volunteers:

Retirement pensions and dismissal indemnities shall be transferred to the families of volunteers in accordance with the general regime of retirement and dismissal from service.

1 - If the volunteer is killed by bullets or by any other weapon during an armed clash with the enemy in time of war, or during security maintenance operations inside the country in times of war and peace, or in an aviation or navigation accident ordered of him, or during military manoeuvres or baptism of fire or during other executed trainings, or if he dies during the period of his placement on infirmity leave and until his final discharge from the Army for health reasons and the injury he sustained in the aforementioned circumstances was a direct cause of his death, his family shall be granted a retirement pension equal to the basic salary subject to retirement deductions and allocated to the highest step of the rank immediately superior to his rank, including the steps above the ceiling, provided that the salary of the rank superior to his rank exceeds by at least one step the salary due to him for his rank.

2 - If the volunteer is killed by an assault to which he was subjected during the exercise of his function or on the occasion of his performing a selfless act to save the life of others, his family shall be granted a retirement pension equal to 75 % of the pension determined in accordance with the provisions of Clause 1 of this Article. However, if the application of the provisions of Paragraph (1) of Clause 4 below confers better rights upon it, it shall be granted those rights.

3 - If the volunteer dies following an accident or illness attributable to service that occurred in circumstances other than those specified in the preceding two Clauses, his family shall be granted a retirement pension equal to fifty per cent of the pension determined in Clause 1 of this Article. However, if the application of the provisions of Paragraph a of Clause 4 below confers better rights upon it, it shall be granted those rights.

4 - If the volunteer dies following an illness not attributable to service but aggravated by reason thereof:

a - If his service is eighteen years and above:

- His family shall be granted the retirement pension to which he would have been entitled on the day following the date of his death.

b - If his service is under eighteen years and not less than five years:

His family shall be granted a retirement pension equal to 75 % of the principal rights calculated on the basis of one forty-fifth of his salary for the last month prior to his death for each year of service, including war increments.

c - If his service is under five years: his family shall be granted the dismissal indemnity plus an indemnity equal to 100 % of the dismissal indemnity.

5 - If the volunteer dies following an accident or illness not attributable to service:

a - If his service is eighteen years and above: his family shall be granted the retirement pension to which he would have been entitled on the day following the date of his death.

b - If his service is less than eighteen years: his family shall be granted the dismissal indemnity plus an indemnity equal to 50 % of the dismissal indemnity.

6 - If the actual service of the non-commissioned officer or soldier reaches 18 years and above, his family shall be granted the retirement pension and shall not be entitled to commute it for the dismissal indemnity.

7 - The heirs of officers who die in service shall be entitled to request, within three months from the date of death, the substitution of the dismissal indemnity for the retirement pension.

8 - This Clause was repealed pursuant to Law 239 dated 22/11/2012, Official Gazette 45.

9 - In the event of the death of one of the family members receiving a retirement pension, or in the event that the pension is discontinued for one of them for any reason whatsoever, the remaining family members benefiting from the pension shall receive the entirety of this pension, and it shall be redistributed among them equally.

10 - The provisions of this Article shall apply as of the date of entry into force of this Legislative Decree to unmarried volunteers and to the families of volunteers martyred and deceased after 12/6/1959.

1 - The Ministry of National Defence - Army Command shall undertake calling up those subject to compulsory military service and notifying them of the conditions of this service through the various information media.

2 - Those of them who are outside Lebanese territory shall be notified through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants in accordance with lists drawn up by the Army Command.

3 - Every Lebanese residing on Lebanese territory who has completed eighteen years of age and has not been notified of the call-up for compulsory military service must apply within three months of reaching this age to the bodies competent in compulsory military service affairs in the Army in the region where he permanently resides, in order to be notified of the call-up for compulsory military service and to declare his place of residence, failing which he shall be deemed a defaulter.

4 - Every Lebanese who is subject to the obligations of compulsory military service and wishes to leave Lebanese territory to reside abroad for one year or more must file his address prior to his departure with the Ministry of National Defence, - Army Command and the Directorate General of General Security and, upon his arrival in the country of destination, with the consular department to which he reports.

Consular departments and embassies must file the addresses of the persons concerned with the Ministry of National Defence - Army Command -.

1 - The cases in which a Lebanese is deemed exempted ipso jure from compulsory military service, and the cases in which the deferment of his call-up to perform compulsory military service is permitted, shall be determined by a decree issued in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of National Defence.

2 - Every Lebanese who has submitted an application proving that he meets the conditions determined for that purpose in the decree referred to in the first paragraph of this Article shall be exempted permanently or for a term from compulsory military service by a decision of the Army Commander.

The call-up of a citizen for compulsory military service shall be deferred for up to one renewable year within the conditions referred to in paragraph /1/ of Article 108 above, provided that this period does not exceed the limit of his completion of thirty-three years of age, whereupon he shall be called up to perform his service.

He may be permanently exempted from compulsory military service pursuant to a decision of the Army Commander in the cases determined by the instructions for the application of this Legislative Decree.
Applications for exemption and deferment shall be submitted by the persons concerned to the Ministers of National Defence - Army Command.
Deferment or exemption shall be revoked by a decision of the Army Commander upon the request of the person concerned.

1 - The salary or wage of a civil servant or employee who is called up for compulsory military service shall cease immediately upon his discontinuance from his post or work.

2 - The civil servant or employee shall be reinstated by operation of law immediately upon his discharge to the post or work to which he was appointed prior to performing compulsory military service, provided that the period he spent in compulsory military service shall be counted for advancement in seniority and salary.

If the employer delays in reinstating him to his work or handing over his work to him, he shall be entitled to the salary or wage starting from the date of his discharge, provided that his status is finally decided in accordance with the provisions of Article 126 of this Legislative Decree.

3 - The conscript may, upon the completion of his compulsory military service and at his request, be transferred to active service as a volunteer at the same rank in accordance with conditions determined by the Army Command, and in this case the period of his compulsory military service shall be added to his account.

A conscript who does not wish to return to his previous post or work must notify his military superiors thereof at least forty-five days prior to the date of his discharge, in order to notify the employer of this matter within a time limit of not less than thirty days prior to the date of discharge.

A discharged conscript who does not report to his place of work within fifteen days from the date of his discharge shall be deemed to have resigned unless there are cases of force majeure, the assessment of which shall rest with:

- The Civil Service Board, if he is a civil servant, contracted employee, wage earner, or retiree in all administrations and institutions of the public sector.

- The Military Courts, if he is a worker in the private sector.

- The rights of a discharged person deemed to have resigned from his previous post or work shall be settled in accordance with the laws and regulations in force.

If a conscript suffers an injury or accident during his presence in service, the provisions applicable under this Legislative Decree to a volunteer of equal rank shall apply to him, and on the basis of the salary of the latter.

In the event that the employer refuses to reinstate the conscript to his previous work, the latter shall be entitled, in addition to his rights accruing to him under the laws in force with the exception of the compensation specified in Paragraph (a) of the amended Article 50 of the Labour Law, to a special compensation of not less than the salary or wage of a full year on the basis of the salary or wage he was receiving on the date of his call-up to compulsory military service, by way of damages, if he remains physically fit for his work.

If the conscript was working in the public sector prior to his call-up to service, he shall be reinstated by operation of law to his work after the end of his period of service in accordance with the provisions of Paragraph 2 of Article 117 of the Legislative Decree, and the period of his military service shall be counted as part of the actual service in the post he occupied upon his call-up.

To the text of Article 24 of the Code of Military Justice shall be added Paragraph 10, the text of which is as follows:

- Infractions of the provisions relating to compulsory military service.

To the text of Article 117 of the Code of Military Justice shall be added the paragraph the text of which is as follows:

And there shall be punished by the same penalty every person who defaults on reporting for compulsory military service or facilitates the same, and the ascendants of the defaulters, their descendants, their husbands, their wives, and their full brothers and full sisters shall be exempted from punishment.

To the text of Article 118 of the Code of Military Justice shall be added the paragraph the text of which is as follows:

There shall be punished by the same penalty every person who conceals a defaulter from reporting for compulsory military service or performs any act capable of facilitating the matter of his concealment, and ascendants, descendants, husbands, wives, and full brothers and full sisters shall be excepted therefrom.

To the end of Article 120 of the Code of Military Justice shall be added the following text:

And there shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years every person called up for compulsory military service who intentionally renders himself unfit for service temporarily or permanently, and accomplices other than ascendants, descendants, the husband, the wife, and full brothers and full sisters shall be punished by the very penalty of the perpetrator.

If the accomplices are physicians, pharmacists, or nurses, the penalty of imprisonment shall be doubled, and a fine from one thousand to two thousand pounds shall be adjudged, and the licence to practise his profession shall be withdrawn from the convicted person for a period ranging between six months and two years.

The military courts shall hear disputes arising from the application of the provisions of Articles 117 and 121 of this Legislative Decree and relating to conscripts who were working in the private sector.

The provisions of the Social Security Law shall continue to apply with respect to conscripts who were working in the private sector in all matters Regarding which no contrary text is set forth in this Legislative Decree.

The Ministry of National Defence - Army Command - shall determine annually and within the limits of the allocated appropriations the following:

1 - The number of conscripts required to be called up for military service in the light of the shortage occurring in the strength.

2 - The number of conscripts required to be called up annually for service in the light of the need of the designated ministries.

3 - The number of conscripts required to be called up for developmental service in the light of the plans of the ministries concerned and their needs.

The Ministry of National Defence - Army Command shall determine the implementing instructions for the provisions of Title Five of this Legislative Decree, particularly with respect to the administration, equipping, and training of conscripts.

1 - Every Lebanese who is subject to the obligations of the Service to the Flag and does not prove his performance of these obligations is prohibited from exercising the following rights:

a - Elections and standing as a candidate for the various bodies, councils, and others.

b - Employment in any post or any work in the public and private sectors, including contracting.

c - Practising any liberal profession.

d - Leaving the Lebanese territory.

e - Enrolling in schools and universities.

2 - Preference, the conditions of which shall be determined by decrees taken in the Council of Ministers, shall be given to conscripts who have fulfilled the obligations of the Service to the Flag in entering the various armed forces.

3 - In a legal manner - Every Lebanese subject to the obligations of the Service to the Flag who proves that he is exempted therefrom or deferred in intention or against whom a judicial judgment has been issued that necessitated his defaulting thereon shall be excluded from the provisions of the first paragraph of this Article.

(Prosecution against defaulters from the Service to the Flag shall cease and all proceedings and judgments against them in this respect shall lapse immediately upon the issuance of Law 665 dated 4/2/2005, and they shall be rehabilitated ipso jure - Article 3 of Law 665 dated 4/2/2005).
There shall apply to conscripts throughout the duration of their active service the laws, regulations, and instructions applicable to volunteers pursuant to this Legislative Decree.

The conscript shall receive during the duration of his service a symbolic monthly lump-sum allowance determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers. The conditions of nutrition, housing, and clothing shall be determined in the same manner, and the Army Commander may grant additional allowances as an incentive for work while conscripts are performing civil or developmental services within the limits of the available appropriations, provided that they do not exceed 50 % of the symbolic monthly lump-sum allowance mentioned above.
The conscript shall personally benefit during the duration of his service from all the rights and services from which volunteers benefit, with the exception of the salary.

The conscript shall have the right to sit during the duration of his service for the competitive examinations or examinations conducted by public administrations and institutions, autonomous services, municipalities, or private institutions.

Reservists are:

1 - Volunteers discharged from active service who remain within the reserve period set out in Article 131 of this Legislative Decree.

2 - Conscripts who have completed military service and were discharged at the end thereof and who remain within the reserve period set out in Article 131 of this Legislative Decree.

3 - Civilians who have successfully attended military training courses organised by the Army Command and were discharged at the end thereof.

The reserve period shall be determined in accordance with the following conditions:

1 - For volunteers

a - Officers:

For a period of fifteen years following their discharge from service, provided that they do not exceed the age set for their ranks plus five years.

b - Non-commissioned officers and enlisted personnel:

For a period of fifteen years following their discharge from service, provided that they do not exceed the age of fifty-five.

2 - For conscripts after completing their service and until they reach forty years of age.

3 - For civilians who are the subject of paragraph (3) of Article 130, until they reach forty years of age.

The procedures and conditions for calling up and exempting reservists, and the obligations imposed on them during the period of their presence in the reserve, shall be determined by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of National Defence based on the recommendation of the Army Commander.
The Army Command shall determine the manner of administering, training, calling up and discharging reservists.

Reservists shall be promoted under the same conditions applicable to volunteers and conscripts, provided that they:

1 - Complete, in active service and in the reserve, the seniority set for each rank.

2 - Have attended the training periods prescribed for them.

3 - Pass the training courses that qualify them for promotion.

Reservists shall not be promoted after reaching the statutory age set out in Articles 56 and 57 of this Legislative Decree.

However, exceptional promotion is permissible if the conditions set out therefor in Articles 41 and 48 of this Legislative Decree are met.
Reservists in civilian life shall not receive any salaries and allowances, with the exception of the entitlements prescribed for them by law.

Reservists called up for training periods and stages shall benefit from the same entitlements allocated to volunteers, with the exception of the salary and its supplementary allowances if the training period does not exceed one month.

However, if this period exceeds one month, they shall also benefit from a monthly allowance equivalent to the salary and its supplementary allowances pertaining to their ranks.

Reservists called up pursuant to this Legislative Decree shall, if the duration of the call-up exceeds two months, benefit from the difference between the salaries and supplementary allowances pertaining to their ranks and their retirement pension.

If, however, they have received severance pay instead of a retirement pension, they shall benefit from the difference between the salaries and supplementary allowances pertaining to their ranks and the retirement pension calculated on the basis of the services for which the severance pay was received.

Services performed by reservists called up pursuant to this Legislative Decree shall not be counted for the revision of the retirement pension and severance pay unless the duration of the recall exceeds one year, whether continuously or intermittently, in which case they shall benefit from the increments and additions for the duration of their service.

Reservists employed in public administrations, public institutions, autonomous services and municipalities, and called up pursuant to this Legislative Decree, shall retain the posts from which they were recalled and shall return to them or to other similar posts in the same competent administration.

If a reservist is called up for a period not exceeding one month and is employed by a natural or legal person, that person must pay him his wage and reinstate him in his former work.

If, however, the period exceeds one month, the natural or legal person must reinstate the reservist in his former work or in similar work, provided that the said period does not exceed one year, whereupon the reservist's rights shall be liquidated in accordance with the laws in force.
The State shall bear the transport allowances of called-up reservists if they are outside the country pursuant to a prior authorisation from the Army Command.

Reservists called up at least twice in a single year, for periods none of which exceeds one month, shall benefit from an allowance equivalent to the monthly salary pertaining to their ranks together with the allowances at the end of the year during which the call-ups took place, and this allowance may be cancelled or reduced by a decision of the Army Commander for disciplinary or conduct-related reasons or for incompetence in fulfilling the duties of the rank.
Called-up reservists shall, throughout the duration of their recall, be subject to all laws, regulations and instructions applicable to volunteers.
The military courts shall hear disputes arising from the application of Article 146 of this Legislative Decree.

A reservist who fails to comply with the call to report to the post designated for him for a period exceeding 48 hours shall be deemed a defaulter and shall be punished by the penalty provided for in Article 107 of the Military Justice Code.

Reservists called to service for a period exceeding one month shall benefit, throughout this period and together with their dependent family members, from the rights pertaining to volunteers and defined in Article 68 of this Legislative Decree.

Conscripted reservists shall be entitled, during their presence in the reserve, to apply to volunteer for active service at the rank they hold, provided that they undergo a qualifying examination the procedures and conditions of which shall be determined by a decision of the Commander of the Army.

Their enlistment as volunteers at this rank shall take place in accordance with the procedures defined for volunteers pursuant to this Legislative Decree. As for the reservists who are the subject of item 3 of Article 130 of this Legislative Decree and who are called to service for a period exceeding one year and are discharged thereafter, they shall be entitled to receive a severance indemnity equivalent to two months' salary for each year of service, calculated on the basis of the last basic salary they were receiving.
The Law of State Employees shall apply to military personnel in all matters not mentioned in this Legislative Decree.

The Minister of National Defence, upon the proposal of the Commander of the Army, may:

a - Grant military personnel or the families of the deceased among them, and civilian employees in the Army and their families, social, medical, and educational allowances, allowances in the event of death, and financial rewards.

b - Grant retired volunteers, their widows, and their relatives social allowances, the amount of which shall be determined in the light of the allocated appropriations and the condition of the applicant for the allowance.

c - Grant educational institutions and orphanages financial allowances in consideration for housing and educating the children of volunteers and of retired or deceased volunteers.

1 - Notwithstanding the laws in force, expenditures resulting from the following cases shall not be subject to the prior audit of the Court of Audit:

a - Admission of volunteers of the various categories.

b - Reinstatement of discharged volunteers into service.

c - Promotion of military personnel.

d - Granting of military decorations that confer the right to financial allowances.

2 - All of these cases shall be subject to the subsequent audit of the Court of Audit.

1 - Discharged volunteers shall be granted a preference of up to 25 % in filling positions in the cadres of the State, municipalities, public institutions, and institutions the majority of whose resources are secured by the State, in the following manner:

a - In the Ministry of Posts and Wired and Wireless Telecommunications: distributor, inspector of telephone and telegraph lines.

b - In the Ministry of Public Works and Transport: works inspector, foreman of labourers or of a workshop, firefighter.

c - In the Ministry of Public Health: health inspector.

d - In the Ministry of Finance: collector, customs guard.

e - In the Ministry of Justice: bailiff.

f - In all administrations, usher, attendant, guard.

g - In municipalities: municipal police officer, firefighter, foreman of labourers, works inspector.

h - In the positions determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers after consulting the Civil Service Board.

2 - It is required for a candidate from among the discharged volunteers applying for one of the positions mentioned above, or that there be fulfilled in him in addition to the conditions imposed on the job applicant, the following conditions:

a - That he has spent at least ten years in active service, and whoever was discharged following an accident or illness attributable to the service shall be exempted from this period.

b - That his age be at least five years less than the legal age prescribed for the termination of service in the requested position.

c - That he obtain the approval of the Army Command if five years have not elapsed since his discharge.

When discharged volunteers are appointed to the positions mentioned in Article 152 above, they may combine the salary of the position to which they are appointed and their retirement pension.

- If the discharged volunteer is appointed to a position subject to retirement, he may request the aggregation of his previous services in accordance with the conditions stipulated in the Civil Servants Law.

- If the civil retirement pension is lower than the former military retirement pension, the person concerned shall retain the latter pension, and the retirement deductions that have been collected from him in respect of his civil position shall be refunded to him.

- Laws No. 3/79 dated 24/3/1979 (National Defence Law) are hereby repealed.

- And No. 38/75 dated 6/12/1958 (Flag Service Law),

- And No. 3/81 dated 20/2/1981,

- And the supplemental implementing regulations and instructions thereof that contravene the provisions of this Legislative Decree or are inconsistent with its content.

- All other legislative and regulatory texts that contravene the provisions of this Legislative Decree or are inconsistent with its content are likewise hereby repealed.

This Legislative Decree shall enter into force as from the day following its publication in the Official Gazette, with the exception of Articles 79 to 99 inclusive, which shall enter into force as from 30/6/1983.

1 - The Civil Defence provided for in Legislative Decree No. 50 dated 5 August 1967 shall be attached to the Ministry of the Interior.

2 - The provisions of the aforementioned Legislative Decree, and the provisions of Law No. 57/71 dated 9 September 1971, shall be amended where the phrase "Ministry of National Defence" and the phrase "Ministry of National Defence - Army Command" are replaced by the phrase "Ministry of the Interior", and the phrase "Minister of National Defence" and the phrase "Higher Military Authority" are replaced by the phrase "Minister of the Interior" wherever they appear in the two aforementioned texts.

3 - The text of Article 16 of Legislative Decree No. 50 dated 5 August 1967 shall be repealed and replaced by the following text:

"All organs of the Civil Defence shall be subject to the authority of the Minister of the Interior"

4 - The phrase "upon the proposal of the Higher Military Authority" appearing in Article 19, paragraph (4), of Legislative Decree No. 50 dated 5 August 1967 shall be repealed, and the phrase "upon the recommendation of the Higher Army Command" appearing in the final paragraph of Article 27 of the aforementioned Legislative Decree shall also be repealed.

5 - The text of Article 31 of Legislative Decree No. 50 dated 5 August 1967 shall be repealed and replaced by the following text:

"Operations of revenues and expenditures shall be conducted in accordance with the procedures specified in the Public Accounting Law".

6 - The provisions of Decree No. 7563 dated 8 September 1961 shall be amended by subsequent decrees in accordance with what is provided for in the body of this Article.

1 - The land located within the perimeter established around military installations to preserve their safety shall be called a "prohibited zone".

2 - Without prejudice to the personal rights of individuals, the real servitudes pertaining to each type of military installation shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of National Defence based on the recommendation of the Army Commander.

The mutual benefit and commissary institutions in the Army shall be considered persons of private law and shall be linked to the Director General of Administration; their regulations shall be issued by decrees upon the proposal of the Minister of National Defence, and all their revenues, transactions and operations shall be exempted from taxes and fees of all kinds.
The authorities concerned shall issue the decrees, decisions and instructions implementing the provisions of this Legislative Decree within a time limit expiring on 31/12/1984.

- A - Name of the Ministry: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants B - The word "Ministry", wherever it appears in this Legislative Decree, means the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants. C - The word "Minister", wherever it appears in this Legislative Decree, means the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants. D - The expression "Secretary-General", wherever it appears in this Legislative Decree, means the Secretary-General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants.
