The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants shall be responsible for the affairs of Lebanon's foreign policy in terms of preparation, coordination and execution, and shall look after the affairs of the Lebanese abroad and their diaspora across the world.
The Minister shall exercise executive authority over the Ministry and shall be entrusted with the execution of its tasks and the enforcement of the laws and regulations pertaining thereto.

1 - The establishment of the Ministry shall consist of a Foreign Corps (diplomatic and consular) and an Administrative Corps in accordance with Tables No. (1) and No. (2) annexed to this Legislative Decree. 2 - The categories and the scale of ranks and salaries of the employees of the Foreign Corps shall be determined in accordance with Table No. (4) annexed to this Legislative Decree. 3 - The category, ranks and salaries of the employees of the Administrative Corps shall be the same as those determined in the Civil Service Regulations.

A - The Central Administration shall consist of the General Secretariat and the following units: 1 - The Directorate of Political Affairs. 2 - The Directorate of Emigrants and the Lebanese Diaspora. 3 - The Directorate of Protocol. 4 - The Directorate of Economic Affairs. 5 - The Directorate of International Organizations, Conferences and Cultural and Social Affairs. 6 - The Directorate of Administrative Affairs. 7 - The Directorate of Documentation and Legal Studies. 8 - The Directorate of Ciphers and Communications. 9 - The Directorate of Media Affairs. B - The Minister shall choose one of the ambassadors in the Central Administration of the first grade and above from the permanent establishment and shall assign him, by a decision issued by him, to the task of inspecting the missions when necessary. C - Attached to the Minister shall be an office consisting of his advisors, two diplomats and five administrative employees. D - Attached to the Secretary-General shall be an office consisting of two diplomats and three administrative employees. E - The administrative units shall be organized and the employees distributed among them in accordance with Table No. (3) annexed to this Legislative Decree.

The powers of the Director-General of the Ministry shall be exercised, and supervision over the Central Administration and the missions shall be carried out, by a Secretary-General who shall be appointed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers from among the employees of the First Category in the permanent establishment of the Foreign Corps.

1 - Vacant posts in the First and Second Categories of the Foreign Service shall be filled from among the employees of the same Service by selection from among the employees of the First and Second Grades in the Third Category for vacant posts in the Second Category, and from among the three highest grades in the Second Category for vacant posts in the First Category. 2 - In addition to the conditions for promotion provided for in the General Regulations, an employee may not be promoted from the Third Category to the Second Category unless he has completed at least eight years of actual service in the Foreign Service.
The provisions and conditions of the Civil Servants Regulations shall apply to the appointment and promotion of administrative, technical and contracted employees in the Ministry.

1 - An ambassador abroad shall be appointed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers. 2 - An ambassador accredited to a country may be appointed as a non-resident ambassador to one or several other States.

1 - Where necessary, one of the employees of the Foreign Service from the three highest grades of the Second Category may be appointed, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, as head of a diplomatic mission with the title of ambassador without modification in salary, provided that he retains this title only for the duration of his performance of the duties of the post to which he is appointed. 2 - Save in the cases provided for in the first paragraph of this Article, no employee may be given a title higher than or different from his actual rank in the Service.

1 - Ambassadors from outside the cadre may, exceptionally, be appointed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, provided that: a - Their total number does not exceed fifteen ambassadors. b - And that the age of each of them is not less than forty years. c - And that he holds a university degree. 2 - The salary of the ambassador from outside the cadre shall be determined as follows: a - The ambassador shall receive the salary of the lowest step of the First Category, and this salary shall be subject to increase through advancement in step. b - If the ambassador appointed from outside the cadre had previously held one of the following positions: the position of President of the Republic, or Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies, or Prime Minister, or Minister, he may be appointed at a salary higher than the lowest step, provided that it does not exceed the salary of the highest step in the First Category, and that in this case he shall not be subject to advancement in step. 3 - The services of the ambassador appointed from outside the cadre may be terminated at any time, and he shall thereupon lose his official title. 4 - Any post in the units of the central administration may at any time be assigned to the ambassador appointed pursuant to this Article, who works in principle abroad, on an equal footing with ambassadors included in the cadre. 5 - The ambassador from outside the cadre shall be deemed to have resigned ipso jure upon the end of the term of office of the Head of State who appointed him, and he shall thereafter continue to conduct the affairs of the mission for a period not exceeding two months, such that if this period expires and no decree reappointing him is issued, he shall be obliged to leave his duty station within a period of one month and then benefit from the administrative leaves due to him, and if he is reappointed, he must be transferred to the central administration after the expiry of the maximum period for serving abroad. 6 - The services of the ambassador appointed from outside the cadre shall terminate ipso jure upon his reaching the legal age prescribed in the Civil Servants Regulations.

An exceptional diplomatic mission may be entrusted, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, to a Lebanese figure from outside the cadre who is granted the title of ambassador until the end of the mission entrusted to him, provided that its maximum duration is three months, renewable once for the same mission.

1 - The establishment of honorary consulates may be accepted in each of Beirut and the capitals of the governorates for foreign States that do not have resident diplomatic or consular missions in the places referred to. 2 - In no case may the appointment of more than one honorary representative for each State in each of the aforementioned places be accepted.

The Directors and Ambassadors in the Central Administration, presided over by the Secretary-General, shall constitute an advisory council for planning attached to the Minister, whose functions shall be to monitor and analyse international and regional events, to oversee the preparation and coordination of Lebanon's foreign policy, and to submit options and recommendations relating thereto.

1 - An Administrative Committee shall be constituted in the Central Administration, presided over ex officio by the Secretary-General and with the membership of the Director of Political Affairs and the Director of Administrative Affairs. 2 - The powers of the Committee shall be to express opinions and submit proposals and recommendations regarding promotions, transfers, allowances, and the marriage of Foreign Service officers, to hear the taking of the oath, and all other administrative matters assigned to it by the Minister where necessary.

1 - Diplomatic or consular missions shall be established and abolished by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers. 2 - Upon the establishment of a new diplomatic or consular mission, two posts of the Third Category shall be added ex officio in the decree of establishment to the cadre of the Foreign Service.

Foreign Service officers shall be attached to missions in accordance with the following: 1 - From two to five officers at most, including the head of mission, in each of the diplomatic missions, in accordance with its importance and the volume of its work. 2 - Two officers, including the head of mission, in each of the consular missions.

1 - Vacant posts in the Third Category of the Foreign Service shall be filled in accordance with the following conditions: a - The candidate must satisfy the general conditions for public employment. b - The candidate must be among the graduates of the Higher Division of the Public Administration Department at the National Institute for Administration and Development. c - The candidate must hold at least a university degree. d - A female candidate must be unmarried. e - The candidate must pass a special competitive examination whose regulations shall be laid down by the Civil Service Board after consulting the Ministry. 2 - If the number of successful candidates in the competitive examination is insufficient to fill the vacant posts, the remaining posts shall then be filled in accordance with sub-paragraphs a, c, d, and e of paragraph (1) above.

1 - The successful candidate shall be appointed to the lowest grade of the Third Category in the Foreign Service with the rank and salary of Attaché or Vice-Consul. 2 - An officer in the Foreign Service shall remain an Attaché or Vice-Consul for a period of at least two years, and may thereafter be promoted by a decision of the Minister to the rank of Secretary or Consul. 3 - Such officer shall not be attached to a post abroad until he has completed, after his appointment, at least two years of training in the Central Administration.

1 - Lebanese honorary consulates shall be established and abolished by a decree enacted in the Council of Ministers. 2 - Honorary consuls shall be appointed by a decree based on a proposal from the head of the diplomatic mission accredited in the country in which the appointment takes place, in accordance with rules and conditions determined by a decision of the Minister. 3 - An honorary consul may be Lebanese or foreign. 4 - No honorary consuls shall be appointed in cities where Lebanese career diplomatic or consular missions exist. 5 - Not more than one honorary consul may be appointed for a single city and a single consulate. 6 - The maximum term of the mission of an honorary consul is five years, renewable in the same manner in which the appointment takes place. 7 - The mission of an honorary consul may be terminated at any time. 8 - An honorary consul shall not receive any salary, wage or allowance of any kind whatsoever for the expenses he incurs in his consulate, nor shall he be entitled to any compensation upon the termination of his services.
It shall not be permissible to create honorary diplomatic posts or posts for honorary technical attachés, nor to grant honorary diplomatic titles.

1 - It shall not be permissible to accept the appointment of non-Lebanese persons who are permanent residents in Lebanon or business owners to career diplomatic or consular posts in foreign missions in Lebanon. 2 - It shall not be permissible to accept the appointment of persons holding Lebanese nationality to career diplomatic or consular posts in foreign missions in Lebanon except in accordance with the provisions of Article 1 of the Lebanese Nationality Law issued on 31/1/1946, and provided that prior to his appointment he is not a permanent resident in Lebanon and is not a business owner therein.

1 - Military, cultural or media attachés, or specialists holding university degrees in the capacity of technical attachés, may be seconded from one of the cadres of the State to diplomatic missions. 2 - The territorial jurisdiction of the attaché may cover several missions. 3 - The secondment shall be made for a period of one year, renewable by a decree enacted upon the proposal of the Minister and the approval of the minister to whose ministry the employee belongs. 4 - The seconded employee shall remain in his original cadre and corps; however, he shall be subject to the authority of the Minister and shall receive his instructions from the Ministry through the head of the mission. 5 - The provisions of Articles 31, 32, 33, 39, 40, 44, 45 and 46 of this Legislative Decree shall apply to the seconded employee.

The head of the office of the National Council for External Economic Relations shall perform the duties of the Economic Attaché of the mission in the country to which he is appointed and shall receive his salaries and allowances from the said Council, provided that he is administratively subject to the head of the mission.

1 - Transfers for employees of the Foreign Service shall take place during the month of May of each year, provided that they are executed within a maximum period of the end of July of the same year. 2 - However, Ambassadors may be transferred on a date other than this for reasons the assessment of which rests with the Council of Ministers. 3 - a - The maximum period for remaining abroad is nine years for employees of the First Category and seven years for employees of the Second and Third Categories. Thereafter, the employee shall be transferred to the Central Administration for a period of at least two years, provided that an employee of the First Category may, exceptionally and when necessary, be kept abroad for an additional period not exceeding three years by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers. b - The maximum period shall be shortened or extended according to its proximity to the month of transfers. 4 - The period that an employee of the Foreign Service may spend in a single post is, in principle, half the maximum period for remaining abroad. However, adaptation may be made in this regard to the interest of the service to extend or shorten this period. 5 - If an employee of the Foreign Service is transferred to the Central Administration before the expiry of the maximum period of his presence abroad, the period that he must spend in the Central Administration may be shortened in a proportional manner. 6 - The period provided for in the preceding paragraphs of this Article shall be calculated with effect from the date on which the employee assumes his post.

1 - Employees of the Foreign Service of the First Category and of the Second Category holding the title of Ambassador shall be transferred from the Central Administration to posts abroad and vice versa, and from one post to another abroad, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, and the other employees shall be transferred by a decision of the Minister. 2 - Transfers within the Central Administration shall be effected by a decree for employees of the First Category and Directors, by a decision of the Minister for employees of the Second Category, and by a decision of the Secretary-General for employees of the other categories.

1 - The Minister may at any time decide to recall any employee of the Foreign Service from abroad to the Central Administration, either to retain him therein pending his transfer to another post or for consultation. 2 - In this case, paragraph (3) of Article 33 of this Legislative Decree shall apply to the employee recalled for consultation, and paragraph (4) of the said Article 33 shall apply to the employee recalled to be retained pending his transfer to another post.

If a Foreign Service officer present in the Central Administration is assigned to a mission at one of the diplomatic or consular missions for a period exceeding three months, he may not be transferred abroad until after the lapse of an equal additional period beyond the period of his service in the Central Administration.
Appointments, promotions and transfers in the cadres of the Ministry shall be carried out, and allowances shall be determined, after the approval of the Board of the Civil Service Council.

1 - Representation car allowances determined by decree shall be allocated to the Secretary-General, Category One employees working in the Central Administration, and Directors. 2 - Allowances determined by decree shall be allocated to certain employees of the Central Administration upon whom the nature of their work imposes a specific specialisation or the performance of continuous effort outside official working hours.

1 - A Foreign Service officer shall be granted, in addition to transport expenses, a special relocation allowance upon his appointment to the Service, upon his transfer from the Central Administration to a post abroad and vice versa, upon his transfer from one post to another post abroad, and upon the termination of his service for non-disciplinary reasons if he is abroad at that time. 2 - This allowance shall be determined by decree.

Foreign Service officers who are assigned to missions by written instructions from the Minister shall be granted a travel allowance, and this allowance shall be determined by decree, in addition to transport expenses.

1 - The expatriation allowance for a Foreign Service officer shall be determined by decree on the basis of the cost of living and currency exchange abroad, and this allowance shall be increased by twenty-five per cent- for officers working in the countries mentioned in paragraph (1) of Article 39 of this Legislative Decree. 2 - The officer shall receive the expatriation allowance effective from the date of travel, and it shall be discontinued for him upon his transfer to the Central Administration effective from the date of his arrival in Lebanon and after he has used his administrative leaves and after he has used the administrative leaves due to him for his service abroad. 3 - An officer recalled to the Central Administration for consultation may receive the full expatriation allowance for a period of one month effective from the date he leaves the post of his function, and in which case no travel allowance shall be due to him other than travel expenses. If the period exceeds one month, he may be granted the expatriation allowance by decree. 4 - The expatriation allowance shall be discontinued for an officer recalled to the Central Administration in preparation for his transfer to another post effective from the date of his arrival in Lebanon and after he has used the administrative leaves due to him for his service abroad.

1 - Housing for heads of diplomatic and consular missions shall be provided at the expense of the Treasury in the mission building, and the housing and the offices may be in one building or separate. 2 - Heads of diplomatic and consular missions shall bear an amount of the expenses of lighting, heating, cooling, water and telephone, which shall be determined by decree. 3 - Other foreign service employees working abroad shall be granted a housing allowance, the amount of which shall be determined by decree. In cases where housing is provided for them at the expense of the Treasury, the housing allowance shall be discontinued for them and they shall personally bear the full domestic expenses of lighting, heating, cooling, water and telephone. 4 - The housing allowance shall fall due starting from the date of arrival of the employee at his duty station. It shall be discontinued upon the date of his final departure from this station and after his enjoyment of the leaves due to him. 5 - Every head of a diplomatic mission shall have the right to employ a cook, a servant and a driver, whose wages shall be paid from the appropriation for local employees.

1 - The head of a diplomatic mission shall receive a lump-sum allowance for his car, the value of which shall be determined by decree, and this allowance shall fall due to him starting from the date of his arrival at his duty station. 2 - Upon the absence of the head of the mission for a period of one month or more for any reason whatsoever, the chargé d'affaires ad interim shall receive half the value of this allowance throughout the period of absence, provided that the other half remains due to the head of the mission on condition that he is not assigned any task for which a car allowance falls due to him, and in this case the other half shall revert to the Treasury.

Notwithstanding any other text, there shall be determined by a decision of the Minister and the Minister of Finance: a - The fees required to be assessed and collected in missions and in honorary consulates and the manner of transferring them to the Treasury fund. b - The rules of expenditure in the mission and the regulations for executing it. c - The rules of accounting in the mission in general.

a - The annual appropriations for the missions shall be determined by a decision of the Minister. b - The stamp duty on the salaries of local employees is abolished. c - Heads of missions shall be exempted from the financial guarantee in return for the stamp advances granted in their name.
The special regulations governing local employees attached to the missions shall be determined by a decision of the Minister.

1 - The duration of the annual administrative leave for an official of the Foreign Service working abroad shall be fixed at one month. As for an official in the Arabian Peninsula, Pakistan, India, Indonesia, and Africa, excluding Northern and Southern Africa, he shall benefit from a leave of two months annually. 2 - The duration of travel to Lebanon and return to the duty station by the direct route without stopover, whatever the means of travel, shall not be counted as part of the leave. 3 - If the official exceeds the duration of the leave due to him, his salary and allowances shall be withheld for the duration of the excess. 4 - Leaves may be accumulated over a period not exceeding three years, provided that their total does not exceed four months.

The travel expenses from his duty station to Lebanon, for the outward and return journeys, shall be provided at the expense of the Treasury to the official on leave and to the members of his family once every two years for one who is entitled to a leave of two months annually and once every three years for one who is entitled to a leave of one month annually, and the family shall include the spouse, sons who have not exceeded eighteen years of age or who are pursuing their studies in educational institutions up to twenty-five years of age, unmarried daughters who do not engage in paid work, and parents who have exceeded sixty-four years of age and who are proven to be dependent on the official.

1 - The Treasury shall bear the travel expenses of officials of the Foreign Service and the members of their families specified in Article 40, and an amount equivalent to the price of their travel tickets by the direct route by aeroplane in accordance with the international tariff shall be transferred to them. The official shall have the right to choose the means of transport. 2 - Travel shall be in first class for ambassadors and officials of the second category appointed as heads of diplomatic missions with the title of ambassador or who occupy the post of director, and their families, and travel shall be in tourist class for other officials and their families.

The ambassador assigned to inspection shall undertake the task of inspecting the missions in disciplinary matters; as for the financial field, inspection shall remain subject to the authority of the Central Inspection within the limits provided for in the laws and regulations in force.

1 - An official of the Foreign Service may not marry except with prior permission from the Minister, and anyone who does not comply with the provisions of this Article shall be deemed to have resigned. 2 - If a female official in the Foreign Service marries a foreigner, she shall be transferred to the Administrative Corps within a period not exceeding three months from the date of her marriage. And if she loses her Lebanese nationality, she shall be dismissed from service immediately.

An employee of the Foreign Service may not, for any reason whatsoever, leave the country to which he is appointed except with written permission from the Ministry; otherwise, his salaries and the allowances supplementary thereto shall be withheld from him for the period of his absence from his duty station, in addition to the disciplinary penalties provided for in the Civil Servants Regulations.

If an employee of the Foreign Service or one of the members of his family specified in Article 40 dies abroad, the Treasury shall bear the expenses of preparing and transporting the body to Lebanon. It shall also bear the round-trip travel expenses for the members of his family accompanying him.

1 - An employee of the Foreign Service appointed abroad may not practice another work, including teaching. Nor may his wife practice any work. 2 - A female employee in the Foreign Service whose husband practices a work not approved by the Minister shall be transferred to the Administration. 3 - Neither the wife nor the husband of the Head of Mission may practice any work abroad, including diplomatic or consular work in one of the Lebanese missions.

If an employee is transferred from the Foreign Service to any other cadre, he may not subsequently be reinstated to the permanent cadre in the Foreign Service, and he may only be appointed from outside the cadre in accordance with the provisions of Article 18 of this Legislative Decree.

All allowances that were granted pursuant to decrees issued on the basis of the provisions of Articles 9 and 23 of Decree No. 1306 dated 18/6/1971 and its amendments are hereby repealed, and the allowances provided for in Paragraph (2) of Article 30 of this Legislative Decree shall be determined by a subsequent decree. The payment of allowances to those currently receiving them shall continue until the issuance of the special decree concerning allowances provided for in Paragraph (2) of Article 30 of this Legislative Decree.

The administrative and technical posts that were provided for in the previous establishment table of the Ministry and which are not mentioned in the tables annexed to this Legislative Decree are hereby abolished and replaced by other posts in the new cadre of the same category, without this leading to any modification in the rank or salary of the employee.

Notwithstanding the provisions of Article 25, Paragraph (1), of this Legislative Decree, transfers of employees of the Foreign Service may be carried out at any time for a period ending on 31/12/1983.
The details of execution of this Legislative Decree shall be determined, where necessary, by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister.
All texts that conflict with the provisions of this Legislative Decree or are inconsistent with its content are hereby repealed.
This Legislative Decree shall enter into force as of the day following its publication in the Official Gazette.

Within the framework of environmental protection and the management of natural resources, every natural or legal person, whether public or private, shall abide by the following principles:

(a) The precautionary principle, which requires the adoption of effective and appropriate measures based on scientific information and the best available clean technologies aimed at preventing any threat of potential and irreversible damage to the environment.

(b) The principle of preventive action against all damage affecting the environment, through the use of the best available technologies.

(c) The "polluter-pays" principle, which requires that the polluter bear the costs of preventive measures and of combating and reducing pollution.

(d) The principle of conserving biological diversity, which requires that all activities avoid causing damage to the various components of biological diversity.

(e) The principle of avoiding the degradation of natural resources, which requires that all activities avoid causing any irreversible damage to natural resources such as water, air, soil, forests, the sea, rivers, and others.

(f) The principle of participation, which requires that:

1 - Every citizen shall have the right of access to information relating to the environment, in accordance with the laws and regulations in force.

2 - Every natural or legal person, whether public or private, shall watch over the safety of the environment, contribute to its protection, and report any danger that may threaten it.

(g) The principle of cooperation, which requires that public and local authorities and citizens cooperate in protecting the environment at all levels.

(h) The principle of the importance of the customary standard in the rural environment, which requires that such custom be taken into account in the absence of a statutory text.

(i) The principle of pollution monitoring, which aims at preventing and controlling pollution in all environmental media, including water, air, soil, flora, and waste, such that the treatment of pollution in one environmental medium does not lead to the transfer of pollution to, or impact on, another medium.

(j) The principle of relying on economic incentives as a monitoring and regulatory tool in order to eliminate and/or mitigate all sources of pollution and promote a policy of sustainable development.

(k) The principle of environmental impact assessment as a means of planning and management in order to combat, reduce, or minimise to the lowest level the sources of pollution and the degradation of natural resources.

- The draft Law set forth in Decree No. 8171 aiming at the protection of the environment, as amended by the Administration and Justice Committee, is hereby ratified.

- This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

This Law determines the general legal framework for implementing the national environmental protection policy with a view to preventing and curbing all forms of degradation, pollution and harm, promoting the sustainable use of natural resources, and securing a sound and environmentally stable living framework.

For the purposes of this Law, the following expressions shall mean:

a - Environment: The natural (i.e. physical, chemical and biological) and social surroundings in which all living organisms live, and the systems of interaction within the surroundings, within the organisms, and between the surroundings and the organisms.

b - Initial Environmental Examination: A preliminary study aiming at identifying the potential environmental impacts of a given project in order to determine the extent of the necessity of conducting an environmental impact assessment study for the project.

c - Environmental Impact Assessment: Identifying, estimating and assessing the impacts of a given project on the environment and determining the necessary measures to mitigate negative impacts and increase positive impacts on the environment and natural resources prior to issuing the decision to approve or reject the project.

d - Environmental Management Plan: The set of mitigation measures, monitoring and supervision means, and institutional procedures taken during the construction, operation or dismantling of the project, which would eliminate negative environmental impacts or reduce them to locally acceptable levels, if any, and otherwise in accordance with United Nations standards.

The "Environmental Management Plan" shall be deemed an integral part of the "Environmental Impact Assessment" report and the "Initial Environmental Examination" report.

e - Biological Diversity: The variability among living organic organisms derived from all sources including, inter alia, terrestrial, marine and aquatic ecosystems and the ecological complexes of which they are part; this includes biological diversity within species, between species and of ecosystems.

f- Natural Resources: The following elements of the environment: air, water, land and living organisms.

g- Ecosystems: (Ecosystemes) A dynamic complex of plant and animal living organism communities interacting with the non-living environment as representing an ecological unit.

Every human being has the right to a sound and stable environment, and it is the duty of every citizen to watch over the protection of the environment and secure the needs of present generations without prejudice to the rights of future generations.

1 - For the purposes of implementing this Law, the Minister of the Environment shall draw up a master plan for the protection of the environment upon the proposal of the National Council for the Environment, and the plan shall be approved by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of the Environment.

2 - The master plan for the protection of the environment shall be subject to a periodic review conducted by the Minister of the Environment every two years upon the proposal of the National Council for the Environment, and the amendments thereto shall be approved by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of the Environment.

3 - The review conducted every two years shall take into consideration, in particular, the activities carried out for the environment, as well as the damage affecting the environment and the risks identified, as well as the progress achieved in scientific and technological research.

A National Council for the Environment composed of fourteen members shall be established, and the composition of the National Council for the Environment and the manner of its operation shall be determined pursuant to a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of the Environment, provided that representation is shared equally between the ministries concerned with the environment and the stakeholders from the private sector (environmental associations, environmental experts, and members of the syndicates of liberal professions).

The National Council for the Environment shall undertake, in addition to the tasks entrusted to it pursuant to the Law Establishing the Ministry of the Environment, the following advisory tasks:

a - Recommending the determination of environmental objectives and priorities, and proposing amendments to environmental policies.

b - Assessing the environmental impacts of every activity related to natural resources and issuing the necessary recommendations.

c - Coordinating the orientations of the institutions, administrations, and ministries concerned with the protection of the environment.

d - Recommending the amendment of national laws, regulations, specifications, standards, and quality metrics relating to the protection of the environment and its constants.

A National Fund for the Environment shall be established enjoying legal personality and financial and administrative autonomy, and it shall be subject to the ex-post audit of the Court of Accounts and to the tutelage of the Minister of the Environment.

1 - In order to achieve integrated pollution control, national environmental quality standards, as well as the methods for granting the necessary permits, monitoring their enforcement and the procedures for assessing the state of the environment and protecting it, shall be determined by a decree enacted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Environment.

2 - The Ministry of Environment may, to this end, seek the assistance of any national or international expert in the process of determining these national standards, which shall be reviewed periodically.

This shall take into consideration the state of scientific knowledge, technological progress and internationally recognised standards.

Assessing the state of the environment and protecting it shall include the implementation of environmental management programmes carried out by classified establishments and other establishments engaged in polluting activities, and self-monitoring or environmental auditing programmes, with a view to an objective and periodic assessment of the effectiveness of the measures taken in the field of combating or reducing pollution and informing public opinion of the results of these measures.

1) A system for the management of information relating to the environment and the methods for its protection shall be established, which shall be implemented under the supervision of the Ministry of Environment, provided that the methods of organising the management of environmental information shall be determined by a decree enacted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Environment and after consultation with the National Council for the Environment.

2) For any natural or legal person concerned with environmental management and sustainable development, in accordance with the provisions of this Law and its implementing texts.

Every person shall have the right to obtain objective information relating to the state of the environment, with the exception of information relating to national security or professional secrecy.

This information must be provided within a period of one month, and every refusal to provide the requested information must be reasoned.

The Ministry of Environment shall oversee the implementation of the information, consultation and alert systems provided for in the international and regional treaties relating to the environment to which Lebanon has acceded or will accede.

1 - Every educational institution, whether primary, intermediate, secondary or university, and whether public or private, and every other academic institution, must incorporate into its curriculum educational programmes relating to the environment.

2 - The programmes mentioned in clause 1 of this Article shall be subject to the approval of the Ministry of Environment in accordance with conditions determined by a decree enacted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Environment and the competent Ministers.

Public and private institutions operating in the fields of teaching, training, education, research, media and culture must cooperate with the Ministry of Environment and the competent Ministries to develop information and awareness-raising campaigns on the protection of environmental media and natural resources and the application of prevention techniques.

The National Environment Fund shall be entrusted with the following functions and powers:

a - Contributing to the financing of monitoring and supervision measures for the implementation of this Law and its implementing texts.

b - Recommending the conditions for granting the loans referred to in this Article.

c - Recommending the granting of the incentive measures referred to in Article (20) of this Law.

d - Supporting the development of research and technological advancement in matters of environmental protection.

e - Supporting and encouraging sustainable development activities and projects aimed at protecting the environment, combating desertification, forest regression and soil erosion, and protecting biological diversity.

f - Supporting initiatives and activities undertaken by unofficial associations.

g - Contributing to preventive activities that have an impact on the environment in general.

h - Granting loans under conditions determined by a decree enacted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Environment and Finance, to anyone who undertakes an activity capable of improving the quality of the environment.

1) The revenues of the National Environment Fund shall consist of:

a - An annual financial contribution provided for in the General Budget laws and determined in accordance with its needs.

b - Special fees for environmental protection imposed pursuant to this Law or by special laws.

c - Subsidies, grants, donations and bequests presented to it, particularly from official and private national and foreign bodies, with the aim of protecting and developing the environment.

d - Fines and compensations adjudicated or agreed upon regarding damages affecting the environment in implementation of the provisions of this Law and the settlements concluded in respect thereof.

e - Returns, proceeds and interest on its funds.

2) The Fund shall have a special budget and its funds shall be considered public funds.

3) The resources of the Fund shall be allocated towards achieving its objectives.

4) The revenues and the proceeds and interest they generate shall be considered funds of the Fund and shall be deposited in a special account at the Bank of Lebanon in accordance with procedures determined in the bylaws of the Fund.

The manner of organising the National Environment Fund and the procedures for performing its functions shall be determined by a decree enacted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Environment and Finance, and the bylaws of the Fund and the procedures for performing its functions may be amended in the same manner.

Citizens' participation in the management and protection of the environment shall be ensured through:

1 - Free access to environmental information in accordance with the laws and regulations in force.

2 - Establishing consultative mechanisms at the national and local levels comprising citizens and associations concerned with environmental affairs.

3 - Developing environmental education in the national educational system.

4 - Awareness and information campaigns for citizens regarding environmental issues.

5 - Organising activities of public interest within the framework of environmental protection.

6 - Developing technologies specific to recycling and centres for the collection, sorting and disposal of waste, particularly at the local level.

7 - Preparing guidelines on the use of specific technologies, alternative energy and materials, and the conservation of natural resources, and establishing monitoring indicators that encourage the prevention, reduction and control of pollution.

8 - Every person shall have the duty to inform the Ministry of Environment of any damage that may affect the environment.

The procedures for implementing the citizens' participation system mentioned in Article eighteen of this Law shall be determined by decrees taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Environment, after consulting the competent ministries.

1) Whoever uses equipment and technologies that allow the avoidance, reduction or elimination of all forms of pollution as well as the treatment, recycling and reuse of waste shall benefit from reductions on the customs duties due on such equipment and technologies, at a maximum rate of 50% (fifty per cent) in accordance with the conditions and procedures determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Environment and Finance.

2) Every natural or legal person who carries out activities that conserve the environment shall benefit from reductions on the taxes covering such activities, at a maximum rate of 50% (fifty per cent) in accordance with the conditions and procedures determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Environment and Finance.

3) The Council of Ministers may, upon the proposal of the Ministers of Environment and Finance and the competent minister, adopt any other economic or financial incentive measure.

The concerned entities in the public and private sectors shall conduct initial environmental examination studies or environmental impact assessments for projects that may threaten the environment, due to their size, nature, impact or activities.

The Ministry of Environment shall review these studies and approve them after verifying their compliance with the conditions of environmental safety and the sustainability of natural resources.

1) The word "project" means:

أ - The execution of construction works or other installations.

ب - Any intervention in the natural surroundings including those comprising works of extraction or addition of natural resources.

ج - Any proposal for a programme, study, investment or regulation affecting an entire Lebanese region or an entire sector of activity.

د - Any modification, addition, expansion, rehabilitation or closure of the activities referred to in paragraphs (أ), (ب), and (ج) of this Clause.

2) The preparation of the initial examination study or the environmental impact assessment shall be carried out at the expense and for the account of the project owner.

As well as all monitoring expenses and costs.

The details of the application of this Title shall be determined, a list of projects subject to the initial environmental examination study and a list of projects subject to the environmental impact assessment study shall be established, and the fees and cost of the review referred to in Article Twenty-One shall be determined by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Environment and Finance.

1) Every natural or legal person, public or private, in the course of exercising his activity, shall undertake not to emit or leak air pollutants, including annoying or harmful odours, prohibited pursuant to this Law, its implementing texts and other laws in force, or in excess of the maximum permissible limits determined by the national environmental quality standards, taking into consideration the text of Paragraph "د" of Article Two of this Law.

2) It is prohibited to possess, use or operate machines, engines or vehicles resulting in the emission or leakage of air pollutants, including annoying or harmful odours prohibited pursuant to this Law, its implementing texts and other laws in force, or in excess of the maximum permissible limits determined by the national environmental quality standards, taking into consideration the text of Paragraph (د) of Article Two of this Law.

1) Upon the burning of any kind of fuel, hydrocarbons, or otherwise, whether for industrial purposes, power generation, or any other purpose, emissions of all kinds must remain within the maximum permissible limits.

2) The specifications of chimneys and other means of controlling emissions of all kinds leaking from the combustion process shall be determined in accordance with the national environmental quality standards, in addition to the maximum permissible limits.

Every natural or legal person, public or private, particularly when using machines, engines, equipment, or vehicles, or when using horns and loudspeakers, shall comply with not exceeding the maximum permissible limits for noise intensity determined by the national environmental quality standards, taking into consideration the text of Paragraph (d) of Article of this Law.

Every natural or legal person who violates the provisions of Articles 24 and 25 or 26 of this Law shall be served notice by the competent local authority, which shall undertake to notify the Ministry of Environment and the competent ministries or administrations with a copy of the notice.

If the violator does not comply with the contents of the notice within the time limit specified therein, as well as in emergency cases, the Minister of Environment may take all legal measures aimed at stopping the activity polluting the air environment after identifying it.
The decree provided for in Article Twelve of this Law shall determine the procedures for monitoring the implementation of the provisions of Articles 24, 25, 26, and 27 of this Law.

1) The protection of the marine environment from pollution aims to achieve the following purposes:

a - Protecting the shores of the Lebanese Republic, its natural resources, and its ports from the risks of pollution in all its forms and shapes.

b - Protecting the living and non-living natural Lebanese territorial waters from the risks of pollution in all its forms and shapes.

2) The Ministry of Environment, in coordination with the Ministry of Public Works and Transport and the competent administrations and authorities, each within its respective competence, shall undertake to achieve the purposes mentioned in Clause (1) of this Article, including coastal management and protection plans.

1- Subject to the provisions of international and regional treaties to which Lebanon has acceded, any discharge, immersion or incineration in the Lebanese territorial waters of any substance which may, directly or indirectly, is strictly prohibited:

a - Prejudice human health and marine natural resources.

b - Harm marine activities and organisms, including navigation, fishing, plants and algae.

c -Spoil the quality of marine waters.

d - Reduce the recreational value and the tourism potential of the Lebanese sea and beaches.

2) A list of the substances referred to in paragraph one of this Article shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Environment and Public Works and Transport.

1) The Minister of Public Works and Transport may, on the basis of the Initial Environmental Examination study or the Environmental Impact Assessment study carried out in accordance with the provisions of this Law and its implementing texts, license the discharge, immersion or incineration in the territorial waters and in the marine subsoil in the territorial waters, of substances that do not give rise to the hazards mentioned in Article thirty of this Law, and under conditions that prevent the licensed operations from causing damage to the marine environment.

2) The decree mentioned in paragraph "1" of Article thirty of this Law shall determine the conditions and procedures for granting the permits provided for in paragraph "1" of this Article and the monitoring procedures, as well as the conditions for applying these provisions to discharge, immersion, burial and incineration operations.

Subject to the provisions of the laws and regulations in force and the international and regional treaties to which Lebanon has acceded, the decree mentioned in paragraph "2" of Article thirty shall determine the measures necessary for the prevention of any marine pollution resulting from ships, marine tankers, vessels or installations in the Lebanese territorial waters.

Subject to the provisions in force relating to public domain works, works on the maritime or riverine public domain that obstruct free access to the coasts and sandy beaches or lead to the erosion or degradation of the site or cause a threat to the interests mentioned in paragraph "1" of Article twenty-nine shall be prohibited.

Wetlands and their ecosystems shall be subject to special protection the conditions of which shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Environment, taking into consideration the role and importance of these areas in preserving marine and/or riverine biological diversity and the overall coastal environmental balances.

There shall be determined by a decree enacted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Environment and the competent Minister, within time limits determined by the said decree:

a - The rules for drawing up a general inventory to measure the level of pollution of waters, springs, rivers, their courses and their banks, lakes, pools, lagoons, marshes, drinking water reservoirs and distribution networks, and irrigation canals, provided that this general inventory is reviewed whenever the need arises.

b - The national, chemical, biological and bacteriological standards that must be met in waters, springs, rivers, their courses and their banks, lakes, pools, lagoons, marshes, drinking water reservoirs and distribution networks, and irrigation canals.

c - The national quality standards that must be met in waters intended for human consumption and for all other uses.

d - The methods for analysing and monitoring the physical, chemical, biological, bacteriological and quality characteristics of water.

e - The procedures for the direct or indirect discharge, burial, dumping, disposal and deposit of substances capable of causing pollution of surface or underground waters, or of increasing the degradation of their quality by altering their physical, chemical, biological or bacteriological characteristics, and the procedures for monitoring these operations.

f - The special protection measures that the Ministry of Environment or the competent authorities may impose for the purpose of preventing or limiting any harm affecting the aquatic environment.

g - The rules for subjecting existing installations to the provisions of this Law and its implementing texts.

Subject to the laws and regulations in force, every installation that undertakes the treatment of water shall be subject to a prior licence to commence operations issued by the Minister of Environment.

The implementing decrees of this Law shall determine the rules and time limits for subjecting installations to the provisions of this Article.

1) Subject to the legal provisions in force relating to the conservation and use of public domain waters, these waters shall be subject to the protection measures provided for in this Law and its implementing texts, taking into account the national environmental standards, in order to:

a - Protect surface and ground waters from the risks of pollution in its various forms and restore the quality of these waters.

b - Protect environmental balances, wetlands and their ecosystems.

c - Develop, protect and evaluate natural resources as economic resources, and ensure their distribution across their various uses.

2) Every measure or policy aimed at developing an integrated management of natural resources relating to the environment shall be determined by a joint decision issued by the Ministers of Energy and Water and of the Environment.

3) The measures referred to in item /2/ of this Article shall apply to every discharge, dumping, throwing or depositing, direct or indirect, of substances likely to cause the pollution of surface or ground waters, or to increase the degradation of their quality by altering their physical, chemical, biological or bacteriological characteristics.

There shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Environment and the competent ministers:

A - The special protection conditions aimed at limiting soil degradation and erosion, combating desertification and the pollution of the land, the subsoil and their natural resources, and losses of arable land.

B - The measures aimed at encouraging the rational use of the land or the subsoil and their natural resources.

C - A list of the activities which, by reason of their nature, their importance or their results, have caused the pollution of the land, the subsoil and their natural resources.

D - The procedures for subjecting the aforementioned activities to prior licensing from the Ministry of Environment.

E - A list of the fertilisers and insecticides and disease pesticides permitted to be used for the purpose of protecting the environment and the subsoil from all harm that may befall them.

F - The procedures for supervision and the measures that may be imposed to ensure the protection of the terrestrial environment and the subsoil from all harm that may befall them.

There shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Environment and the competent ministers:

A - The conditions for determining the locations of and establishing treatment plants and waste dumps, of all kinds, the conditions for their operation, the technical standards that must be followed in these plants dumps, the determination of the fate of abandoned waste, and the procedures for monitoring these provisions.

B - The procedures for the supervision by the Ministry of Environment of the procedures for the complete treatment of waste pursuant to the provisions of this Law and Law No. 64/88 issued on 12/8/1988 (Preservation of the Environment against Pollution from Harmful Waste and Hazardous Substances) and the Law Establishing the Ministry of Environment and its amendments).

Subject to the provisions of Law No. 64/88 dated 12/8/1988, there shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Environment:

A - A list of hazardous or harmful wastes which contain substances hazardous to public health and safety and which are prohibited from being imported, introduced, disposed of, stored, used, traded in, or transported across or within Lebanese territory.

B - A list of wastes permitted to be imported, disposed of, stored, used, traded in, and transported across and within Lebanese territory.

C - The methods and conditions for importing waste-generating substances or products, and introducing, disposing of, possessing, using, trading in, and transporting them across and within Lebanese territory.

Where the operation of one of the classified establishments is a source of damage to one of the elements of the environment, the local authority shall notify the Ministry of Environment of the matter in order to conduct the required investigation, and the local authority shall serve notice upon the operator of the necessity of taking all necessary measures to prevent or eliminate this danger at his own expense.

In the event that the operator fails to comply with the content of the notice within the time limit specified therein, the measures and penalties provided for in the laws and regulations in force shall apply to him.

The Minister of Environment may initiate any investigation aimed at monitoring the impact of the activity of the establishment on the environment.

He may, after serving notice upon the operator and without notice in cases of emergency, take the necessary measures to protect the environment, at the expense of the operator.

The expenses of investigation, monitoring and the measures taken shall be assessed and collected in accordance with the Public Accounting Law and the Collection of Direct Taxes and Fees Law.

The persons responsible for monitoring classified establishments shall be subject to professional secrecy.

Subject to the provisions of Title Six of this Law, sites damaged as a result of works carried out without complying with the legal and regulatory provisions in force, and sites polluted due to wild dumps or unauthorised landfilling, shall be subject to measures aimed at eliminating pollution and rehabilitating the environment, at the expense of the person responsible for these sites with a view to restoring them as far as possible to their original state in accordance with what is determined by the Ministry of Environment.

The details of the application of this Article shall be determined by the decrees issued in the Council of Ministers in implementation of the provisions of this Law.

1 - Every facility must have available capabilities for environmental auditing and self-monitoring for the purpose of the systematic measurement of its polluting emissions and the effects of its activities on the environment.

2 - Every facility shall be subject to prior operating authorisation which specifies the particular limits for all types of polluting emissions, including those relating to waste treatment, and the other effects of the facility's activities on the environment, as well as the conditions for implementing the environmental auditing and self-monitoring referred to in item (1) of this Article.

3 - There shall be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Environment and the competent Ministers, the national standards specific to each category of facilities, the details of the application of this Article and the procedures for applying its provisions to facilities existing on the date of entry into force of this Law, and the conditions for the suspension, closure or striking off of each facility, when such facility constitutes a danger to the environment that the measures provided for in this Law cannot avert.

There shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Environment and the competent ministers:

1 - The conditions for regulating any emission of noise or sounds that may be harmful to human health or may cause excessive nuisance or prejudice the environment, particularly that resulting from installations, vehicles and others.

2 - The measures that may be imposed, particularly in emergency cases, to prevent acoustic harm and noise or to limit their negative effects.

The protection of nature, the prevention and combating of desertification, and the conservation of animal and plant species and their habitats, of biological balances and ecosystems, and of biological diversity, in the face of all causes of degradation, pollution and risks of extinction, shall be considered to be of public interest.

1 - The management of natural resources and the conservation of biological diversity in Lebanon shall be based on:

a - Establishing an inventory of existing animal and plant species, particularly those threatened with the risk of extinction.

b - Subjecting any activity capable of prejudicing the environment to prior notification to the Ministry of Environment.

c - Proposing plans for the protection of the habitat of animal and plant species and the conditions of their life and development.

d - Proposing the establishment of national parks, nature reserves and protected areas, and proposing the conditions for the protection of natural sites and landscapes.

e - Establishing a control system for access to biological and genetic resources and their uses in accordance with the international agreements and treaties which Lebanon has concluded or concludes, in agreement with the ministries concerned.

f - The participation of citizens and public and private institutions in the conservation of biological diversity and the sustainable use of natural resources.

2 - The details of the application of the provisions of this Article shall be determined by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Environment and the competent ministers.

The management of resources shared with other States shall be carried out in a sustainable manner and on the basis of cooperation, mutual notification and consultation, in accordance with the provisions of the international and regional treaties concluded between the States with which Lebanon shares the said resources.

A national plan for the management of disasters and natural risks shall be established for each region of Lebanon, and it shall include an environmental management plan prepared by the Ministry of Environment in cooperation with the competent ministries.

The preventive measures that must be taken to confront any serious environmental pollution resulting from natural disasters or due to wars or otherwise, and the powers of the competent administrations and authorities in implementing these measures, shall be determined by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Environment and the competent ministers.

1 - Subject to the provisions of the laws and regulations in force, in particular Law No. in particular dated 12 August 1988, the importation, production, extraction, transformation, marketing, transport, possession, use, or destruction of harmful and/or hazardous chemical substances which, by reason of their composition, nature, and effects, in particular toxic or radioactive, or their quantity, constitute or may constitute a danger to public health and safety and to the environment in general, shall be subject to a prior authorisation granted under conditions determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Environment and the competent ministers, and to the supervision of the Ministry of Environment.

2 - The provisions of this Law and its implementing texts shall apply to marketed preparations made from the substances mentioned in item "1" of this Article.

3 - This decree shall include:

a - A list of the substances whose importation, production, extraction, transformation, marketing, possession, use, destruction, or transport across Lebanese territory is prohibited or subject to prior authorisation.

b - The conditions, procedures, and time limits for granting the prior authorisation.

c - The conditions and procedures of disposal for each group of products.

d - The conditions of production, storage, packaging, classification, transport, marketing, and recycling specific to the substances that are the subject of this Chapter.

e - The supervision procedures and the measures that may be imposed to ensure the protection of the environment, in particular in emergency cases.

f - The rules for applying the provisions of this Chapter to harmful and/or hazardous chemical substances present on Lebanese territory on the date of entry into force of this Law.

4 - For the purpose of applying the decree mentioned in item "1" of this Article, the guidelines and technical standards harmonised at the international level by specialised institutions shall be taken into consideration.

1 - Subject to the provisions of the Penal Code, and the provisions of Law No. 64/88 dated 12 August 1988, upon violation of the provisions of this Chapter, the offending substances shall be seized, and the means of transport may be seized and the establishment temporarily closed.

2 - Contrary to the provisions of Title Six of this Law, when these substances constitute a real and imminent danger, the competent local authorities shall undertake the destruction thereof or the elimination of their effects at the expense of the owner of these substances, under the supervision of the Ministry of Environment.

The expenses shall be imposed and collected in accordance with the two laws on Public Accounting and the Collection of Direct Taxes and Fees.

Subject to the provisions of the Code of Obligations and Contracts and the Penal Code, the perpetrator of any violation of the environment that causes harm to persons or to the environment shall be liable for the compensation due.

The State, represented by the Ministry of Environment, may claim special compensation resulting from the damage caused to the environment.

1 - The persons responsible for any damage affecting the environment due to works carried out without a permit or in a manner contrary to the legal and regulatory provisions in force, particularly those relating to initial environmental examination studies or environmental impact assessment, shall be obliged to take all measures that lead to the removal of the damage, at their own expense.

2 - The expenses resulting from the measures taken by the competent authorities to prevent any damage affecting the environment shall be borne by the person responsible for such damage.

Every person who operates a classified establishment or uses harmful and/or hazardous chemical substances as defined by this Law and its implementing texts must sign an insurance contract against all risks that threaten the environment.

1 - Violations of the provisions of this Law and its implementing texts shall be recorded by virtue of seizure reports drawn up by members of the judicial police in accordance with the laws in force.

2 - In order to record violations and monitor compliance with this Law and its implementing texts, members of the judicial police and inspectors of the Ministry of Environment may, in accordance with the laws in force:

a - Enter the premises and buildings of the facilities and establishments covered by the provisions of this Law.

b - Inspect the premises, buildings, constructions, equipment and warehouses of the facilities and establishments mentioned above.

c - Examine all documents and records relating to the environmental working conditions and procedures of the facilities and establishments covered by the provisions of this Law, or to their activities.

d - Take samples and quantities to conduct the necessary analyses.

3 - The exercise by members of the judicial police of their function in other places where the practice of activities or the presence of substances capable of harming the environment is suspected shall be conditional upon obtaining prior written approval from the Public Prosecution and seeking the assistance of members of the Internal Security Forces.

The seizure reports, together with all documents, statements and information relating thereto, shall be referred to the Public Prosecution, and a copy thereof shall be notified to the Ministry of Environment.

Violations recorded in accordance with the provisions of this Law and its implementing texts shall be heard by the competent single judges in the Governorate in which the violation occurred; the summary trial procedures relating to flagrante delicto offences shall apply to these violations, and their judgments shall be subject to appeal only.

- The application of criminal penalties shall not preclude the power of the competent administrations and authorities, following a written notice served upon the offender through administrative channels, to take against him all or some of the following administrative measures:

a - Imposing special conditions to permit the continued carrying out of a specific activity, in addition to preventive measures, self-monitoring and an environmental audit, on a continuous basis, and suspending the licence pertaining to such activity until compliance with the said special conditions and measures.

b - Prohibiting a specific activity due to grave hazards it causes to the environment, revoking the licence pertaining thereto and closing the establishment.

c - Remediation works such as pollution removal, reforestation and maintenance of sites, at the expense of the offender.

d - Imposing obligations and fines.

e - Any other measure aimed at preventing or limiting any harm to the environment.

1 - Shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year and by a fine from fifteen million to two hundred million Lebanese pounds, or by either of these two penalties, any person who:

- Implements a project requiring an initial environmental examination study or an environmental impact assessment without conducting such study in advance or submitting it to the supervision of the Ministry of Environment and the competent ministries and administrations.

- Implements a project requiring an initial environmental examination study or an environmental impact assessment in violation of the content of the study submitted by him which has obtained the approval of the Ministry of Environment and the competent ministries and administrations.

- Implements a project not requiring an initial environmental examination study or an environmental impact assessment and not in conformity with national standards.

- Opposes or obstructs the procedures of monitoring, inspection and analysis provided for in this Law and/or its implementing texts.

2 - In the event of recurrence of the offence, the penalty shall be doubled.

Subject to the provisions of Law No. 64/88 dated 12/8/1988, shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year and by a fine from two million to ten million Lebanese pounds, or by either of these two penalties, any person who violates the provisions of this Law and its implementing texts relating to the protection of the air, marine, water or terrestrial environment and the subsoil.

In the event of recurrence, the penalty shall be doubled.

Shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year and by a fine from two million to ten million Lebanese pounds, or by either of these two penalties, any person who violates the provisions of this Law and its implementing texts relating to classified establishments.

In the event of recurrence, the penalty shall be doubled.

Subject to the provisions of Law No. 64/88 dated 12/8/1988 relating to the preservation of the environment against pollution from harmful waste and hazardous substances, the fines provided for in the aforementioned Law shall be raised: from ten million to one hundred million Lebanese pounds.

1 - Every person who violates the provisions of this Law and its implementing texts relating to waste other than that provided for in Article sixty-one of this Law shall be punished by a fine from one million to ten million Lebanese pounds.

2 - In the event of repetition of the violation, the penalty shall be doubled.

1 - Every other violation of the provisions of this Law and of its implementing texts shall be punished by a fine from five hundred thousand to five million Lebanese pounds.

2 - In the event of repetition of the violation, the penalty shall be doubled.

The penalties provided for in this Law shall not preclude the application of the penalties provided for in the Penal Code and other penal legislation, administrative measures and penalties, or the obligation of compensation by virtue of civil liability.

Notwithstanding the provisions of the Forests Law issued on 7 January 1949, in particular its Article 98, the total of the fines and compensations awarded pursuant to the provisions of this Law and its implementing texts shall revert to the National Environment Fund.

The Minister of Environment shall be entitled to effect a compounding on the fines and on the compensations awarded in respect of the damages that affect the environment, in application of the provisions of this Law and its implementing texts, provided that the settlement does not cover more than half the value of the fine or the compensation.
All provisions contrary to this Law or that conflict with its content are repealed.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Mandatory Nature of the Permit: The construction, conversion, restoration, and renovation of buildings of all kinds shall be subject to obtaining a prior permit granted in accordance with the provisions in force and based on the approval of the competent technical departments founded upon a technical inspection conducted by them for this purpose. The application for the prior permit and the building plans must be signed by an engineer and registered with one of the two Orders of Engineers in Beirut and Tripoli according to the geographical location of the building intended to be constructed. The prior permit is mandatory for all buildings, even those belonging to public administrations and public institutions, municipalities, and legal persons. The prior permit shall be granted by: - The head of the executive authority in the competent municipality for buildings intended to be constructed within the municipal boundaries. - The Governor or the District Commissioner (Qaimaqam) for buildings intended to be constructed outside the municipal boundaries.

Works Exempted from the Permit: The application for a prior permit shall be replaced by a written declaration in the following works: 1- Ordinary maintenance, beautification, and restoration works that do not relate to the main structure of the building. 2- Construction of enclosures, retaining walls, land reclamation works, and demolition works. The details of the works exempted from the permit shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport.

Conditions and Documents for the Permit Application: The conditions that must be met in the application for a prior permit or the written declaration, the documents that must be attached thereto, the conditions for keeping building permit registers, and the methods of notifying them to the concerned administrations and authorities shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Public Works and Transport upon the proposal of the Directorate General of Urban Planning.

Conditions for granting the permit and the period of its validity: In granting the prior permit, alignment plans and regulations in force must be complied with, in particular those thereof relating to urban planning, health and public safety. The permit shall not be granted except after the approval of the technical departments and the payment of the full fees due thereon. A copy of the granted prior permit shall be posted prominently at the site of the worksite immediately upon commencing the works, throughout the duration of the works and until obtaining the occupancy (habitation) permit. It shall not be permissible to commence building works, or demolition, excavation or earth-levelling works preparatory to building, except after obtaining the permit or after submitting and paying the fees due. The permit shall be valid for a period of four years, renewable once and for a period of four years exempted from fees, provided that the renewal application is submitted during the last three months prior to the expiry of the period of its validity and that there is no legal impediment preventing the renewal. In this case, the permit may be amended in the event that the possibility of amending it exists, with exemption from fees if no increase occurs in the area of the amended building. The declaration for works exempted from the permit shall be valid for a period of one year. If the works that are the subject of the permit or the declaration are not executed within the legal time limit, the permit or the declaration shall be deemed cancelled. ' If the full works that are the subject of the permit or the declaration are not executed within the legal time limits, the unexecuted works or parts thereof shall be deemed unlicensed, and the execution thereof shall be subject to obtaining a new permit or submitting a new declaration according to their nature and to paying the fees due thereon. The building shall be deemed completed upon the completion of its load-bearing parts (foundations, load-bearing walls, columns, beams, ceilings) and the completion of all the works of its facades; whereas the remaining internal works shall be deemed complementary works. When the works executed upon the expiry of the period of the permit do not allow the building to be deemed completed within the meaning of the preceding paragraph above, a fine equivalent to the basic permit fee for the uncompleted parts or storeys, in addition to a fee equivalent to the restoration fee for the internal complementary works, shall be imposed upon applying to obtain a new permit. However, if only the internal works are unexecuted or uncompleted upon the expiry of the time limit of the permit, a fee equivalent to the restoration fee shall be imposed upon applying for a permit therefor.
