The building permit must be granted, or refused, with a statement of all the reasoned grounds for refusal, within the time limits set out below, to be calculated as from the date of registration of the application in the competent technical departments: 1- Within a time limit of two months at most if the building real property that is the subject of the permit application stands on an executed road or the sides of an approved alignment plan. 2- Within a time limit of six months at most if the said real property is not located on an executed road or on the sides of an approved alignment plan, or if this real property is affected by or adjacent to a draft alignment plan or an amendment to an alignment plan or a draft general master plan referred for approval, or if the application requires consulting the opinion of the Higher Council for Urban Planning or the Directorate General of Antiquities or the Directorate General of Civil Aviation or other public administrations. '' If the administration does not take its decision, whether by approval or by refusal, and notify it within the aforementioned time limits, the applicant for the permit may deem himself licensed to commence the works, provided that they are executed in accordance with the approved alignment plans and the laws and regulations in force, and that the legal fees are paid within a time limit of one month at most from the expiry of the time limits specified above.

Remnants of Public Property: Where the alignment plan or the existing situation requires the annexation of a remnant of public or private property belonging to the State or to the municipalities to the property that is the subject of the prior permit application, and where the existing situation with respect to the execution of the alignment plan permits such annexation, the granting of the permit shall be conditional upon the payment of a deposit by the owner equivalent at least to the price of the remnant estimated on the basis of the valuation adopted for the property for the imposition of the building fee, provided that the formalities of declassification, demarcation, and annexation are subsequently carried out at the expense of the owner. In this case, the remnant shall be deemed guaranteed to the principal property. The price of the remnant shall be finally determined by the competent committees, and in the event of a dispute over the price, the competent expropriation committees shall adjudicate thereon. The operation of annexing the remnant to the property shall not be mandatory for the Administration if it declares the allocation thereof for public use.

Occupancy (Habitation) Permit: Upon completion of the licensed building, the owner shall submit to the competent technical departments an application to obtain the occupancy (habitation) permit accompanied by a certificate from the responsible engineer registered with the competent Order of Engineers, showing that the execution was carried out under his supervision in accordance with the licence. The conditions for submitting this application and keeping the registers pertaining thereto shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Public Works and Transport upon the proposal of the Directorate General of Urban Planning. Where there are modifications to the licence, plans showing the state of the building after execution signed by the responsible engineer must be submitted, and in the event of an increase in the licensed area, these modified plans shall be registered with one of the two Orders of Engineers in Beirut and Tripoli. If it is established that the building conforms to the designs on the basis of which the licence was granted, or differs therefrom yet remains in conformity with the texts in force at the time of its execution, the occupancy (habitation) permit shall be granted after the approval of the competent technical departments and after the fees and fines due as at the date of the occupancy permit for the areas in excess of the total licensed areas have, where applicable, been paid. '' In the event of non-conformity of the building or any part thereof with the texts in force, the owner shall, under the supervision of the responsible engineer who signed the permit application, carry out the necessary works for the building to become conformable, and he shall thereafter notify the Administration and submit, where applicable, new plans signed by the responsible engineer and registered with one of the two Orders of Engineers in Beirut or Tripoli. The occupancy (habitation) permit shall be granted by the authority that granted the prior building permit on the basis of the approval of the competent technical departments. The occupancy permit must be granted or refused within one month at the most from the date of submission of the application, and in the event of refusal, the reasons therefor must be stated and the nature and location of the violation specified. However, if the said period expires and no decision of approval or refusal has been taken on the application, the permit applicant may consider himself licensed ipso jure for occupancy on his own responsibility, provided that the constructions are in conformity with the planning line and the texts in force and that he pays the legal fees, in the event of increases over the areas stated in the original licence, within one month at the most from the date of expiry of the time-limit specified above.

Subdivision of the building and connecting it to water, electricity and telephone: Public administrations, autonomous authorities, all other public institutions and concessionary companies, each within its respective competence, are prohibited from subdividing the building into different rights and connecting the owner or occupant of the real property to the telephone, electricity or water unless the party concerned produces an occupancy (habitation) permit duly issued. The occupancy permit may be substituted by one of the following documents: 1- A certificate based on official records issued by the head of the executive authority in the competent municipality, or by the competent Governor (Muhafiz) or District Commissioner (Qaimaqam) if the building falls outside the municipal boundaries, proving that the building was licensed for construction before the date of 2/9/1961 and that its construction was completed within the validity period of the permit. 2- A certificate based on official records issued by the head of the executive authority in the municipality or by the competent financial departments outside the municipal boundaries proving that the building was completed before the date of 26/3/1964. 3- A certificate from the competent departments proving that the occupancy permit application was not decided upon by approval or rejection within the period stipulated in the Sixth Article above, accompanied by a certificate from the responsible engineer (the signatory of the permit application) proving the conformity of the building with the granted permit.

Contents of the Permit - Modifications - Violations: The permit shall, in principle, be limited to the matters set forth therein, and any modification sought to be introduced to the permitted building which would alter the external footprint of the building, its internal partitioning, or its height in a manner that affects the line of sight or the building envelopes, or increases the permitted areas, must be declared by submitting modified plans. In such case, the fee shall be levied on that which exceeds the basic permitted areas on the basis of the unit fee resulting from the assessment as at the date of submitting the application for modification, and a supplementary modification permit shall be granted whose effect expires upon the expiry of the basic permit. The permit shall be granted to the owner of the property or to whoever legally succeeds him, without prejudice to the rights of third parties, and the employer, his engineers, and his contractors shall be liable, each in respect of what concerns him, and they must take the necessary arrangements prior to commencing the work and during the course thereof to ensure the maintenance, safety, and stability of public and private structures, the safety of persons, and the non-obstruction of traffic. If violations occur in the building that necessitate demolition during the period falling between the date of obtaining the occupancy (habitation) permit, the responsible engineer shall withdraw his undertaking immediately upon the occurrence of the violation and notify the property owner and the Order of Engineers thereof, and the President of the Order of Engineers must notify the matter to the competent technical departments and the concerned municipalities by means of registered letters with acknowledgment of receipt. '' If the responsible engineer fails to withdraw his undertaking and notify the matter to the Order of Engineers, the following measures shall be taken against him: 1- A warning by the President of the Order of Engineers at the request of the Director General of Urban Planning, the Governor of the region, or the head of the executive authority in the concerned municipality, for the first violation, within a time limit of one month from the receipt of the request by the President of the Order of Engineers. 2- In the event of repetition after the warning, prohibition, by a decision of the President of the Order of Engineers at the request of the Director General of Urban Planning, the Governor of the region, or the president of the concerned municipality, from submitting plans annexed to applications for building and restoration permits, from submitting applications for new building permits, and from managing the works of new construction sites for a period ranging between six months and three years according to the gravity of the violation, within a time limit of one month from the receipt of the request by the President of the Order of Engineers. 3- In the event of repetition for the third time, the engineer shall be excluded, by a decision of the Minister of Public Works and Transport at the request of the Director General of Urban Planning, the Governor of the region, or the president of the concerned municipality, from all contracts concluded by public administrations, public institutions, and municipalities, in addition to the administrative measures that may be taken against him before the departments of the State and which may be included in this decision, within a time limit of one month from the receipt of the request by the Minister of Public Works and Transport. '' In this case, it shall rest with the Disciplinary Council at the concerned Order of Engineers to take harsher measures where necessary, within a maximum time limit of three months from the date of its notification of the violation by the Director General of Urban Planning or the Governor of the region. The execution contractor (builder) shall be subject to the confiscation of equipment and to the penalties to which the violating owner is subject, and shall also be temporarily or permanently excluded from all contracts concluded by public administrations, public institutions, and municipalities pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Public Works and Transport at the request of the Director General of Urban Planning, the Governor of the region, or the president of the concerned municipality. The investigation conducted into the permit application and the building designs, as well as the supervision carried out by the administration during the execution of the permit, shall not bind the latter in any way where liability exists.

Extent of the Line of Sight: The extent of the line of sight is the distance between the vertical line stipulated in contact with the facade at the axis of the opening that lights and ventilates the room and the vertical line stipulated on the boundaries of the real property or another vertical line. This distance shall be measured within the field of the line of sight and along the axis of the opening (a window, a glass door, or a glass facade) from the most prominent point of the structure of the building opposite the opening. The extent of the line of sight may extend across the boundaries of the real property to another real property if easements and rights to this effect exist and are registered in the folio of the two real properties concerned. Rooms intended for habitation or for occupancy by day or by night and day must have at least one extent of the line of sight onto open spaces or onto roads, the specifications and conditions of which shall be determined by a decree adopted upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport. The following shall not be considered rooms requiring an extent of the line of sight: 1- Stairwells - bathrooms - water closets - entrances passages - the hall - the pantry - ironing rooms - larder rooms - laundry rooms and kitchens, provided that the area of the kitchen or the laundry, ironing, or larder room does not exceed six square metres and that the rooms mentioned in this item are independent from one another. 2- Rooms of buildings or rooms of sections of buildings allocated to special activities according to the nature of their function, whether in industry, commerce, education, agriculture, or places of amusement and in other places not allocated to ordinary habitation, which shall be determined together with the manner of their ventilation by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport.

Setback of Buildings: Subject to the setback easements imposed and which may be imposed subsequently pursuant to special regulations, buildings must be erected: 1- Along the sides of international, main, secondary, and local roads: in accordance with the setback imposed pursuant to their special setback decree. 2- Along the sides of internal roads: behind a line situated at least three metres from the axis of these roads if the width of the road is less than six metres. 3- Along the sides of railways: behind a line situated at least two metres from the boundaries of the railway property in the absence of a regulation imposing more than that. 4- Along the sides of canals, watercourses, and other public property: behind a line situated at least two metres from the boundaries of the canals, watercourses, and other public property.

The Envelope: The building envelope is the volume within which the building must remain, and it consists of vertical and inclined planes and lines. This envelope and the methods of its application shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport.

Projections beyond the Envelope: 1- Projections beyond the envelope line erected on the road side: Projection beyond the envelope line erected on the road side shall be permitted only for free unenclosed balconies, canopies, sunshades Brise Soleil, cornices, means of decoration and beautification, advertisements, tiled roof structures, and parapets erected above the roof of the top floor to screen from view staircase and lift shafts, water tanks, and technical installations. 2- Projection beyond the envelope line erected on the side of open spaces: Projection beyond the envelope line erected on the side of open spaces shall be permitted only for cornices, means of decoration and beautification, tiled roof structures, and parapets erected above the roof of the top floor to screen from view staircase and lift shafts, water tanks, and technical installations. The conditions and specifications of the projections that are the subject of items (1) and (2) of this Article shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport. 3- Projection beyond the inclined envelope line: By virtue of a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport after consulting the opinion of the Higher Council of Urban Planning, projection beyond the envelope line may be permitted for certain parts of industrial buildings and places of worship if the nature of their composition and their designation so requires, provided that there are no reasons preventing the projection, such as the safety of air navigation.

Surface exploitation rate and general exploitation factor: First: The surface exploitation rate is the ratio between the area of the horizontal projection of the building and the area of the real property. As for the general exploitation factor, it is the ratio between the area of the building for all its floors and the area of the real property. The surface exploitation rate and the general exploitation factor shall be calculated on the basis of the area of the real property after the approved alignment plan, regardless of the existence of easements for the benefit of neighbouring real properties. In the event that the exploitation factors in a given real property are exhausted, it shall not be permissible to build on any parcel severed therefrom, whatever the reasons for such severance, even if it is in execution of an approved alignment plan. In the event of the existence of a built real property in which the exploitation factors have not yet been exhausted in their entirety, it shall only be permissible to build on the parcel severed therefrom within the limits of what remains of the exploitation of the original real property prior to the severance. Second: The following shall not be included in the calculation of the exploitation rate and factor and the number of floors: 1- The area of unenclosed balconies, verandas, and loggias, and unenclosed roofed spaces on each floor, to the extent that the total area thereof does not exceed 20% of the area of this floor, as well as the pillar floor (pilotis) erected within the horizontal projection of the largest floor in the building, and the pillar floor shall be considered part of the common areas when the building is subdivided into different rights. '' 2- The area of the basement floors the ceiling height of which does not exceed one metre above ground level on all sides, whatever their area may be, if they are designated for use as car garages, warehouses, or for machinery pertaining to the service of the building such as heating and cooling; as for the basement floors or parts of a basement floor designated for uses other than the three preceding uses, their total area must not exceed 50% of the general exploitation factor permitted in the zone, with the exception of hotels, hospitals, and tourist establishments which by their nature require a greater basement floor area than that. The details of the application of this paragraph shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport. 3- The area of stairwell shafts, elevators, and water tanks above the roof of the top floor. 4- Projections intended for decoration and crowning, sunshades, cornices, and eaves. 5- Mezzanines (lofts) if used as a technical floor (Etage Technique) and their height does not exceed 180 centimetres, or used in residential dwellings above laundry rooms, garbage rooms, bathrooms, lavatories, pantries (Office), and corridors. '' 6- Rooms designated for electrical power transformer stations, provided that they are not taken from the area intended for the garage and that they conform to the models established for this purpose by Electricité du Liban and approved by the Minister of Public Works and Transport after consulting the Higher Council of Urban Planning. 7- Parts of pitched tile roofs (gables) where the clear height of their sloping ceiling does not exceed 225 cm above the roof of the top floor, provided that these parts are part of the pitched roof the slope of which is not less than 25 degrees relative to the horizontal plane. As for the remaining parts of this pitched roof, they shall be included in the calculation of the general exploitation factor only. 8- The area of a single floor erected within the horizontal projection of the largest upper floor, the ceiling height of which does not exceed three and a half metres above the lowest point in contact with the facade and one metre above the level of the highest point of the ground of the real property adjacent to one of the facades, in zones where the number of floors or the maximum height is specified.

Article 13: Special easements relating to public safety, health and architectural vistas: 1- By decree adopted upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport, conditions and principles may be imposed for studying the structural soundness of buildings and for using various construction materials, and special conditions may be imposed to protect buildings from fire hazards or for the building to withstand the effects of natural factors, and the use of certain materials in construction may be prohibited or additional conditions may be imposed regarding the possibility of using them if they pose a danger to public safety and health. 2- Additional special conditions are imposed on certain buildings relating to public safety, health, and architectural vistas, and to Lebanese technical specifications, and to the provision of additional installations proportionate to the importance of the building. The buildings and special conditions mentioned above shall be determined by a decree adopted upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport. 3- A building permit may be granted subject to compliance with special provisions, and it may be refused if the buildings, in view of their locations, volumes, external appearances, and the structures intended to be erected or altered, are likely to harm public health and safety, natural vistas, the environment, or architectural vistas, or if such buildings require public authorities to carry out new installations. 4- The permit applicant may be required upon being granted the permit, pursuant to the special provisions mentioned in the preceding paragraphs, to carry out various works, in particular a road network, a water network and connecting it to the public network or constructing a tank to collect rainwater for domestic use, wastewater disposal (connecting the building to the public sewage network where it exists or constructing a septic tank of a design and size suitable for the needs of the building), lighting, arranging and equipping areas designated for playgrounds, parking, and open or wooded spaces or planting new trees, a contribution either in cash or by providing land free of charge to carry out public installations related to the needs of the buildings intended to be erected and which become necessary by the mere erection of these buildings. ' These special provisions shall be specified in the building permit and expressly mentioned in the decision granting it, and the occupancy (habitation) permit shall not be delivered until the permit holder has fulfilled the imposed obligations. Whenever the competent technical departments or the authority entrusted with granting the building permit consider that this permit must be subjected to special provisions not specified by the technical approval, or consider that the special provisions that were specified are unsuitable, the authority entrusted with granting the permit shall be bound by the decision taken by the Higher Council of Urban Planning in this regard. 5- A building permit may be refused or granted only under conditions specified in the technical approval for licensing if the properties that are the subject of the application are located in areas where the building and its occupants are exposed to danger, such as floods or land prone to landslides or collapses. These areas shall be determined by a decree adopted upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport after consulting the opinion of the Higher Council of Urban Planning, and no compensation of any kind shall be due to the permit applicant in the event of its refusal or as a result of imposing conditions that result in additional costs for the beneficiary. 6- When a permit is refused or when it is granted subject to compliance with special provisions pursuant to the five items mentioned above, the permit applicant may, if he considers that the special provisions are unlawful, excessive, or inappropriate, refer the matter to the Minister of Public Works and Transport within three months from the date of being notified of the decision. The Minister of Public Works and Transport shall decide on the matter after consulting the opinion of the Higher Council of Urban Planning, and this shall not preclude the judicial remedies to which the permit applicant and the authorities entrusted with granting the building permit are entitled to resort.

Constructions within the legally mandated setback: 1- Within the setback from the boundaries or alignment of roads and from public domain properties: it is prohibited to erect underground, ground-level, or overhead constructions of any materials whatsoever, whether roofed or unroofed or enclosed on some of their sides, and it is prohibited to install vehicles and trailers used for a purpose other than transport, with the exception of concierge rooms and the enclosure wall, the conditions of which shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport. 2- Within the setback from the boundaries of neighbouring properties: it is permitted to erect basement floors located below the level of one metre above ground level, and the projection of certain constructions pertaining to protection, ornamentation, and beautification is permitted, the conditions of which shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport.

Large Complexes: There shall be deemed large complexes, within the meaning of this Legislative Decree, building projects in which the following conditions are met: 1- That they be designed on a property having an area of not less than ten times the minimum subdivision area to which the zone is subject, with a minimum of /3000/ m2 in the administrative centres of the Governorates and /15000/ m2 outside them. 2- That a proportion of not less than 25% of the area of the property be allocated, equipped, and used as gardens or sports fields, and a proportion of 10% of the area of the property shall be deducted at the total exploitation factor when its area exceeds /10000/ m2. 3- That they be subject to a volumetric plan submitted for the approval of the Higher Council of Urban Planning, and to special conditions relating to setbacks, architectural perspectives, public health, public safety, and the provision of special facilities proportionate to the importance of the project, all of which shall be determined by a decree issued in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport. The construction of large complexes to which the conditions specified above apply may be exempted from the application of the envelope lines provided for in this Legislative Decree and from the surface exploitation, contiguity, number of floor, and height imposed in the regulations of the zone, if distinctive architectural specifications result therefrom for the project itself and for the zone in which the property is located.

Regulated Zones and Unregulated Zones: Regulated zones for which easements are defined for the surface exploitation ratio and total exploitation factor and for height or for the number of storeys shall be subject to their own regulations. As for unregulated zones, and pending their regulation, construction therein shall be permitted in accordance with the following: 1- In unregulated summer resort zones: within a surface exploitation ratio of 30% and a total exploitation factor of 0.90, with a minimum building setback of three metres from the boundaries of adjoining properties and from the boundaries of roads or the alignment or public domain, provided that the number of storeys of the building does not exceed three excluding the basement. 2- In all other unregulated zones: within a maximum surface exploitation ratio of 40% and a maximum total exploitation factor of 0.80, and provided that the number of storeys of the building does not exceed three excluding the basement, with a minimum building setback of three metres from the boundaries of adjoining properties and from the boundaries of roads or the alignment and public domain. The exploitation ratios with respect to industrial buildings permitted to be erected outside the populated area shall be raised to 60% for the surface exploitation ratio and to 0.90 for the total exploitation factor, following the approval of the Higher Council of Urban Planning.

The minimum and maximum clear height under the ceiling for the various types of rooms and buildings, according to their intended use, shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport.

The intended use of a garage may not be altered for any reason whatsoever. An owner who changes the intended use of a mandatory garage or grants the right to use it for other than its purpose shall have his act deemed null and void and shall be required to restore the garage to its former state, and shall also be punished by a fine equivalent to ten per cent of the construction value of the garage whose intended use was modified, to which shall be added a rate of five per cent of the value of the fine for each month of delay in removing the violation from the date of its recording up to six months, and this rate shall be doubled thereafter in the event that the violation continues, and by imprisonment from one month to six months, or by either of these two penalties. The owner's agent who commits the aforementioned violations and the tenant who proceeds to lease or exploit the area allocated for the garage shall be subject to the same penalties, and the contracts of sale, lease, and exploitation shall be deemed null and void together with all rights that may have resulted therefrom. The construction value of the garage whose intended use was modified shall be assessed, for the purpose of determining the fine, as of the date of recording the violation and in accordance with the method of assessing the fee provided for in Article 19 above. However, in the event that the intended use of the building is altered wholly or partially to another intended use permitted in the zone, and if the new intended use requires a garage larger than the area allocated as a garage for the original intended use, the owner shall be required either to provide the additional garage or to pay the fee in lieu for the unprovided portion of the garage in an amount equal to the actual costs of its construction, provided that they are calculated in accordance with Article 19 above, and the alteration of the intended use of the building and everything resulting therefrom shall be deemed null and void in the event of failure to provide the necessary additional garage or to pay the fee in lieu.

Garage: The construction of a garage for parking vehicles is required in buildings that shall be erected in all zones. Certain buildings may be exempted from this obligation where there is an impossibility or force majeure technical difficulties that prevent the construction of the garage, provided that in such cases a special fee is imposed to be collected by the municipality, the Governorate, or the Qaimaqamate outside the municipal boundaries. The fee shall be calculated on the basis of the area required for the garage. The value of the fee per single square metre of the required garage area shall be determined in an amount equivalent to the actual costs of constructing it as a roofed structure and on the basis of the area required therefor, which shall be determined by a decree issued pursuant to item 3 of this Article. The assessment of the actual costs of constructing the garage shall be carried out by the Higher Council for Urban Planning during the month of December of each year and shall remain in force throughout the following year and across all Lebanese territory. The collected fees shall be placed in a special account in the budget of the municipality or in a special fund in the Governorate or the Qaimaqamate outside the municipal boundaries, and they may only be used for the construction of collective garages. 2- The garage for each section of the building must appear on the licensing plans, and this garage shall be deemed an integral part of the section of the building to which it pertains (whether for a residential apartment, a shop, an office, or for the practice of a profession..) upon the leasing, subdivision, or sale of this section. Where the design of the building, the placement of columns, or the presence of walls in the areas to be allocated for the garage prevents the entry or accommodation of the number or part of the required vehicles, the technical body examining the licensing file shall have the right to request a revision of the building design or the placement of columns and walls in order to secure the necessary garage required for the full exploitation of the property, even if the subject of the licence covers only a part of such exploitation. '' Incentive elements may be granted to whoever constructs an additional garage in the building in excess of what is required. 3- The cases in which buildings may be exempted from the garage in the instances set forth in paragraph (1) of this Article shall be determined by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport; the area required for the garage, the conditions and specifications of the garage, the bases for the incentive elements for buildings or parts of buildings constructed and operated as collective garages or for the additional garage in the building in excess of what is legally required, and the penalties applicable upon failure to secure the garage shall likewise be determined in the same manner. 4- The head of the executive authority in the municipality, and the Governor or the Qaimaqam outside the municipal boundaries, may temporarily requisition private unbuilt properties to convert them into vehicle parking lots in return for an annual consideration determined by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport. The property shall be released ipso jure upon the request of the owner immediately upon his obtaining a building permit for the said property for the full general exploitation permitted in the easement zone in which the property is located. '' The municipality shall have the right to re-occupy the property if the owner does not commence execution of the building within a period of three months from the date the property is returned to him, and it shall also have the right to fine him an amount equivalent to the costs of reconverting the property into a garage; in this case, the owner of the property shall not have the right to recover it for construction save after the lapse of two years from its re-occupation as a garage and subject to the actual commencement of construction. 5- In existing buildings for which a vehicle garage is wholly or partially not secured in accordance with the required conditions, the municipality shall have the right to require the owner to secure the garage in the unbuilt area of the property if the condition of this area technically permits it; if the owner abstains from securing the garage, the competent municipality shall either undertake the execution of the necessary works at his expense and under his responsibility, or impose an annual fine equivalent to ten times all the fees imposed for building in respect of the area of the existing building for which a garage is required, until the garage is secured. 6- In the event of an application for a licence to add a building to an existing building, and where it is possible to secure a garage on the property, this garage shall be counted first for the existing building and then for the additional building, and the consideration in lieu shall be paid for the required garage that is wholly or partially not secured for the additional building.

Every excavation of foundations, construction, restoration, or conversion commenced without a permit or declaration, according as the work is subject to a permit or a declaration, or carried out in violation of the permit or the declaration receipt, shall mandatorily be halted, and a violation report shall be drawn up against the owner and the person responsible for execution, and against the holder of a permit or by declaration, as the case may be. If it appears that the constructions do not conflict with the planning layout or with the legal conditions, the permit or the declaration receipt shall be granted with the imposition of a fine equivalent to three times the value of all fees due for the portion that has been completed. Every building whose roof has been poured shall be deemed completed. The fine and the fees shall be deemed a privileged debt on the property, and a clearance certificate from the municipality shall not be granted until after their collection and the regularisation of the status of the violation. The owner of constructions that conflict with the planning layout or that violate the building laws and regulations in force must demolish them, and if he fails to do so, the Administration shall undertake the demolition at his expense and under his responsibility, and the costs shall be collected from him in the manner of collecting State and municipal fees. The building violation report must specify the location of the violation, its nature, the date of its occurrence in a precise manner, and the stage reached by the violator on the date the violation report is drawn up. The violation shall be registered, upon the request of the municipality or the competent technical departments, on the real folio of the property and shall not be struck off except after the regularisation of its status or its removal.

The responsible person who violates the provisions of this Legislative Decree and the texts adopted for its implementation shall be punished by a fine from /1000/ to /50000/ Lebanese Pounds and by imprisonment from one week to 15 days, or by either of these two penalties. A violator who continues the work after it has been halted shall be punished by a fine from / 2000/ to /- 100000/ Lebanese Pounds and by imprisonment from one week to 15 days, or by either of these two penalties, provided- that this shall not preclude the execution of demolition where applicable.

The owner is prohibited from selling or leasing any part of the building prior to obtaining the building permit, and occupying the building is likewise prohibited prior to obtaining the occupancy permit pertaining thereto. Whoever violates this shall be punished by a fine from /2000/ to /1000/ Lebanese Pounds, in addition to the lease contract being deemed null and void. The cases and conditions to be adopted in contracts of sale relating to buildings or parts thereof shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport and the Minister of Justice.

Subject to the provisions of Legislative Decree No. 148 dated 16/09/1983 with respect to the extent of the prospect, the provisions of the Building Law shall apply within the boundaries of each property individually or of a group of contiguous properties that cannot be legally amalgamated, provided that a notation has been recorded on the real property folio of each of the properties of which it is composed indicating that they constitute an indivisible real property unit. However, if the contiguous properties can be legally amalgamated, they must be amalgamated to become a single property. Applications for the settlement of building violations that had been submitted and registered at the Municipality of Beirut or the Municipality of Tripoli or at the branches and offices of Urban Planning in the regions prior to 25/02/1983 shall remain subject to the provisions of the draft law put into effect pursuant to Decree No. 2347 dated 08/10/1979 aimed at the settlement of building violations.

The implementing decrees of this Legislative Decree, including those providing for the tolerance of certain minor building violations in return for the payment of a fine, shall be adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport and after consulting the opinion of the Higher Council of Urban Planning, except in the cases for which Legislative Decree No. 148 dated 16/09/1983 has provided for the manner of issuance of the implementing texts thereof.

All implementing texts of this Legislative Decree shall be issued after consulting the opinion of the Higher Council of Urban Planning.

Legislative Decree No. 61/L issued on 30 August 1940, the Law issued on 20 January 1945, the Seventh, Eighth, Ninth, Tenth, Eleventh, Twelfth and Thirteenth Articles of the draft law put into effect pursuant to Decree No. 15838 dated 20 March 1964, Law No. 59/71 dated 13 September 1971, the draft law put into effect pursuant to Decree No. 10899 dated 27 February 1976, Law No. 42/71 dated 21 June 1971, and all texts contrary to the provisions of this Legislative Decree are hereby repealed. The implementing decrees and decisions annexed to Building Law No. 59/71 dated 13 September 1971 repealed pursuant to this Article shall remain in force until the issuance of the implementing decrees and decisions annexed to this Legislative Decree, in all that does not conflict with the content of this Legislative Decree.
This Legislative Decree shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The urgent draft law referred to the Chamber of Deputies pursuant to Decree No. 1882 dated 5/4/1979 concerning the adjudication of individual labour disputes and disputes arising from the application of the Social Security Law, the text of which follows, is hereby put into effect:
This Decree shall be published and notified where needed, and shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

There shall be subject to the provisions of this Law, as regards the rules of jurisdiction and avenues of recourse:

1- Individual labour disputes arising from employment relationships within the meaning of Article 624, first paragraph, of the Code of Obligations and Contracts.

2- Controversies and disputes provided for in Article 85 of the Social Security Law.

The text of Article 77 of the Labour Law is repealed and replaced with the following text: One or more Labour Arbitration Councils shall be established at the seat of each governorate to adjudicate the disputes referred to in the first Article of this Law, composed as follows:

- A judge of the eleventh grade and above - as President, appointed by decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice and the approval of the Supreme Judicial Council

- A representative of employers and a representative of employees

- as two members appointed by decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and Social Affairs.

- Two alternate members shall also be appointed, one for employers and another for employees, each to act in the place of the titular representative in the event of his absence or inability to attend, by decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and Social Affairs.

A Government Commissioner shall be appointed to the Council, chosen from among civil servants of the third category in public administrations, provided that he holds a licence degree in law.

The duties and powers of the Government Commissioner shall be determined by decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and Social Affairs. The appointment of the Government Commissioner shall take place in the same manner.
All actions brought before the Labour Arbitration Councils shall be exempt from judicial fees and from stamp duty, excluding expenses.
Actions may be filed and appearance made before the Labour Arbitration Councils without the assistance of a lawyer.

Judgments rendered by the Labour Arbitration Councils shall not be subject to any avenues of recourse other than opposition, third-party opposition, and cassation in accordance with the procedures provided for in the Code of Civil Procedure and in the Judicial Organisation Law, subject to the special provisions set forth in the following Articles:

1- Applications for cassation shall be exempt from judicial fees, with the exception of the deposit and expenses.

2- The time limit for appeal before the Court of Cassation is thirty days, and this time limit shall run, in respect of adversarial judgments, from the date of service of the final judgment, and in respect of judgments in default, from the date of expiry of the time limit for opposition thereto.

3- The Court of Cassation shall issue its decision within six months at most from the date of completion of services.

4- A petition for cassation shall not stay the judgment. The Court of Cassation may decide to stay execution within a time limit not exceeding five days from the date of submission of the application therefor, provided that the stay of execution shall not in any case exceed the period of six months specified in the preceding paragraph for issuing the cassation decision. Upon the expiry of the time limit of the decision staying execution, and notwithstanding the provisions of Article 75 of the Judicial Organisation Law promulgated by Decree No. 7855 dated 16/10/ 1961, the judgment creditor shall have the right to execute without security.

5- The Cases Authority at the Ministry of Justice may, of its own motion or at the request of the Minister of Labour and Social Affairs, lodge an appeal before the Court of Cassation in the interest of the law against any decision issued by the Labour Arbitration Council. The decision of the Court of Cassation shall neither benefit nor prejudice the litigants.

If the judgment debtor refuses or delays without legitimate cause the execution of the judgment issued against him and ten days elapse from the date of his being served with a formal notice to that effect by the Execution Department, a coercive fine of one per cent of the total amounts adjudged shall run against him by operation of law for each day of delay, in addition to the application of the provisions of Article 344 of the Penal Code against him, and the Execution Department before which execution is taking place shall liquidate the said fine.

The procedures and rules for conducting the investigation by the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs in actions referred to it where necessary by the Labour Arbitration Councils shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Justice and of Labour and Social Affairs. The Labour Councils may conduct the investigation or expand it outside official working hours through their President.

The courts and judicial bodies having jurisdiction under previous laws shall continue to hear actions pending before them on the date of entry into force of this Law in accordance with the procedures followed before them; however, final judgments issued after the said date shall be subject to cassation in accordance with what this Law provides for.
All legal or regulatory texts that conflict with the provisions of this Law or are inconsistent with its content are repealed.
This Law shall come into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The urgent draft law referred to the Chamber of Deputies pursuant to Decree No. 8085 dated 31/5/1974 relating to the Statute of the State Shura Council, the text of which follows, is hereby put into effect:
This Decree shall be published and notified where needed and shall enter into force as of the day following the date of its publication in the Official Gazette

- The administrative judiciary shall consist of the State Shura Council and of administrative courts; at the head of the administrative courts is a supreme court which is the State Shura Council, with its seat in Beirut.

- In addition to its duties, the State Shura Council shall undertake the review of regulatory texts in the manner set forth in this Law.
The administrative judiciary (the State Shura Council and the administrative courts) shall form part of the judicial organisations of the Ministry of Justice.
The President of the State Shura Council shall exercise the powers of the highest hierarchical superior from both the administrative and financial standpoints.

- The State Shura Council shall consist of a President, a Government Commissioner, Chamber Presidents, Councillors and Assistant Councillors.

- The administrative courts shall consist of Presidents and Councillors, and they are courts of first instance whose judgments are rendered by a President and two members for each court.

- Administrative judges (the State Shura Council and the administrative courts) are independent in the performance of their judicial functions and may not be transferred or dismissed, nor may any measure capable of affecting their professional status be taken, except within the limits of this Law.

- The number of administrative judges, their categories, their grades and their salaries shall be determined in Tables No. 1 and 2 annexed to this Law.

The President of the State Shura Council and the Government Commissioner shall be appointed by decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice from among the Chamber Presidents who are in one of the four highest grades and above or from among the Councillors who are in the first grade and above.

They may be appointed by decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice from among the judges who are in the twelfth grade and above.

- A Chamber President in the State Shura Council or a President of an administrative court shall be appointed by decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice after the approval of the Bureau of the State Shura Council from among the Councillors who are in the tenth grade and above.

- A Chamber President or a President of an administrative court may be appointed by decree upon the proposal of

the Minister of Justice after the approval of the Bureau of the State Shura Council from among the judicial judges who are in the tenth grade and above.

- A Councillor shall be appointed by decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice, following the approval of the Bureau of the State Council, from among Assistant Councillors or Councillors in the Administrative Courts who are of the seventh grade and above.

- A Councillor may be appointed by decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice, following the approval of the Bureau of the State Council, from among:

1 - Judicial judges who are of the seventh grade and above, and judges of the Court of Accounts at the grade equivalent to the seventh grade.

2 - First Category civil servants holding a Lebanese licence degree in law who have practised for at least five years in a position requiring the holding of a licence degree in law in the Civil Service Board, the Central Inspection, or the General Disciplinary Council.

3 - First Category civil servants in public administrations, public institutions, and the Chamber of Deputies holding a Lebanese licence degree in law and who have practised this position for at least five years. And Second Category civil servants holding a State Doctorate degree in Public Law in public administrations and public institutions.

4 - Holders of a State Doctorate degree in Law who have practised higher education as a tenured professor for at least ten full years in officially recognised faculties and institutes of law and business administration.

5 - Lawyers registered on the General Roll for at least fifteen years, provided that they have not exceeded forty-eight years of age.

- The number of Councillors appointed from outside the category of Assistant Councillors or Councillors in the Administrative Courts shall not exceed half of the total number of Councillors provided for in the establishment.

Notwithstanding any general or special text, a judge in the State Council or the Administrative Courts may, subject to his consent, be transferred to the establishment of any of the various ministries, public administrations, or public institutions by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice and the competent minister, and following the approval of the Bureau of the Council.

- The Civil Servants Regulations shall apply to the judges of the State Council and the Administrative Courts in all matters that do not conflict with the provisions of this Law.

- Trainee judges whose eligibility has been declared shall be appointed as tenured judges at the lowest grade in the Administrative Courts by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice.

- After the lapse of at least five years, a judge may be transferred from the Administrative Court to the State Council with the rank of Assistant Councillor, following the approval of the Bureau of the State Council, by a decision of the Minister of Justice.

- An Assistant Councillor or a Councillor in the Administrative Court may be appointed from among:

Judicial judges who are at the fourth grade and above, and lawyers registered on the General Roll for at least five years, provided that they have not exceeded forty years of age.

- A judge in the administrative judiciary shall be appointed by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice and following the approval of the Bureau of the State Council from among the successful candidates in the competitive examination.

- The appointment shall take place at the lowest grade of the rank. If his salary exceeds the salary of the lowest grade, he shall be appointed at the grade whose salary is equivalent to his salary while retaining the seniority qualifying for advancement, by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice following the approval of the Bureau of the State Council.

- The Minister of Justice, after consulting the Bureau of the State Council, shall determine the number of trainee judges intended to be appointed and shall request the Bureau of the Council to organise a competitive examination for this purpose.

- The Bureau of the State Council shall organise the entrance competitive examination to the Institute, determining the subjects of the competitive examination and the passing grade average, and shall appoint the examining committee at the beginning of each competitive examination from among the judges whom it selects for this purpose.

A candidate applying for the competitive examination must:

1 - Be a Lebanese national for at least ten years.

2 - Have completed twenty-one years of age and not have exceeded thirty-one years of age.

3 - Enjoy his civil rights and not have been convicted of a felony or an attempted felony of any kind whatsoever, or of a dishonourable misdemeanour as defined in the Civil Servants Regulations.

4 - Be free from diseases and infirmities that prevent the performance of the duties of the office, be of good conduct, and produce a certificate from the Official Medical Committee in proof thereof.

5 - Hold a licence in law, with Lebanese law being required for those who are subject to it.

6 - And he may be appointed without a competitive examination if he holds a State Doctorate in law, following the approval of the Bureau of the Council.

- The Bureau of the State Council shall examine the status of the administrative judge upon the expiry of two years from his appointment and may decide to remove him from the cadre if it appears that he does not possess the qualifications required by his duties.

- The Bureau of the Council must decide on removal from the cadre or confirmation therein within a time limit of six months at most from the date of expiry of the two years. If the time limit expires without any decision being taken by the Bureau, the judge shall be deemed confirmed ipso jure without the need for any other instrument.

- An administrative judge whom the Bureau of the Council decides to remove from the cadre shall be deemed placed on availability and shall remain in this status until he is attached to another cadre or dismissed from service in accordance with the special provisions governing availability laid down in the Civil Servants' Statute.

- A judge whose confirmation is decided in the absence of a vacant post, shall be attached by a decision of the President of the State Council to one of the administrative courts.

Upon his confirmation, the administrative judge, and upon their appointment to the cadre, the other judges of the State Council, shall take the following oath before the Bureau of the State Council:

"I swear by Almighty God to perform my duties with all faithfulness and honesty, to strictly preserve the secrecy of deliberations, and to conduct myself in all my actions as an honest and honourable judge".

Assistant Councillors and members of the administrative courts shall be attached by a decision of the President of the

State Council, after taking the opinion of the Bureau of the Council, to one of the judicial chambers or to the Government Commissariat or to one of the administrative courts, and they shall be attached to the Ministry of Justice by a decision of the Minister after the approval of the President of the State Council.

Precedence shall be given to the President of the Council, then to the Government Commissioner, then to the member of the highest category; if the category is equal, then to the member of the highest grade, and if the category, grade and seniority are equal, then to the member with the longest service in the Council, and in case of equal tenure in the Council, then to the oldest in age.

Members of the State Council may participate for a limited period in work consistent with their legal qualifications with ministries and administrations or public institutions or municipalities, or be assigned a mission abroad. The assignment shall be made by a decision of the President of the State Council.

- Counsellors and Assistant Counsellors may be seconded to various posts with ministries, administrations, public institutions, or municipalities.

- Notwithstanding any other text, as of the date of entry into force (of this Law 144/2019), the secondment or transfer of any judge from the cadre of the administrative judiciary to public administrations and public institutions is prohibited (this paragraph was annulled pursuant to Constitutional Council Decision 23/2019)

The preceding paragraph shall not apply to a judge seconded to one of the bodies of the Ministry of Justice.

In no case may the number of seconded judges from each category exceed one third of the number provided for in the cadre

A seconded judge shall retain his capacity and position in the administrative judiciary, no other person shall be appointed in his place, and he shall participate in the General Assembly and continue to receive his salaries due in respect of his category and grade from the budget of the State Council.

A seconded judge shall receive the allowances pertaining to the post to which he is seconded and all other allowances granted to him by reason of his secondment from the budget of the administration to which he is seconded.

The judicial recess regime shall not apply to a seconded judge, and he shall benefit from the administrative leaves provided for in the Civil Servants Statute.

Members of the State Council may not be transferred to the administration except after the lapse of at least one year from their appointment thereto and after the approval of the Bureau of the Council. The transfer shall take place upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice and the competent Minister.

1- The Bureau of the State Council shall be composed as follows:

- The President of the State Council (President).

- The Government Commissioner at the State Council (Vice-President).

- The President of the Judicial Inspection Board and the Presidents of the Chambers at the State Council (Members).

- And the three highest-grade Presidents of Administrative Courts (Members).

2 - The Bureau of the State Council shall watch over the proper functioning of the administrative judiciary, its prestige, its independence and the proper conduct of work, and shall take the necessary decisions in this regard.

3 - The decisions of the Bureau of the State Council shall be enforceable in themselves without the need to issue any other instrument. However, in cases where the law requires the approval of the Minister of Justice on the decisions of the Bureau, a joint session shall be held between them to examine the points of disagreement. If the disagreement persists, the matter shall be submitted to the Council of Ministers within a time limit of one month at most to decide thereon.

The Council of Ministers shall decide thereon after hearing the President of the State Council, who shall present the viewpoint of the Bureau.

4 - In all that does not conflict with this Law, the Bureau of the State Council shall exercise the same powers exercised by the Supreme Judicial Council towards judges pursuant to the Law on the Judicial Judiciary.

5 - The Bureau of the State Council shall meet upon a convocation by its President and, in his absence, upon a convocation by the Vice-President.

6 - The Minister of Justice shall have the right to convene the Bureau of the Council to discuss a specific matter; the convocation shall include the date of the meeting and the agenda.

7 - A meeting of the Bureau of the Council shall not be lawful save in the presence of the President or his Vice-President and half of the members of whom the Council is legally composed.

8 - The decisions of the Bureau shall be taken by a majority of the votes of those present, and in the event of a tie, the President of the session shall have a casting vote. Where a decision of the Bureau is issued by a majority of opinions, that shall be indicated therein, and the dissenting judge must record his dissent.

9 - The decisions of the Bureau of the State Council shall be submitted immediately upon being taken to the Minister of Justice. Serial minutes of the meetings and decisions of the Bureau shall be drawn up according to their dates and kept with the President of the State Council after being signed by the President and the members.

10- The President and members of the Bureau of the Council shall be bound to maintain secrecy, and disclosing the secrecy of deliberation at a Bureau shall be deemed a disclosure of the secrecy of deliberation at the courts.

11- The President and members of the Bureau of the State Council, wearing judicial robes, shall take the following oath before the President of the Republic and in the presence of the Minister of Justice: "I swear by Almighty God to perform my duties in the Bureau of the State Council with all honesty and devotion, to keep the secrecy of deliberation, and to seek in all my actions the proper functioning of the judiciary, its dignity and its independence".

An administrative judge who has reached the top of his category or rank shall continue to advance in step by benefiting from an increase in his salary equivalent to one step in accordance with the scale of steps of the judges of the State Council in the categories superior to his category or rank, provided that he does not benefit from more than six steps following the highest step in the cadre.

Appointment shall take place at the lowest step; however, the appointment of judicial judges, judges at the Court of Accounts, and other public servants subject to the pension system shall be deemed equivalent to a transfer from one cadre to another.
Every breach of the duties of office and every act detrimental to honour, dignity, or decency constitutes a disciplinary offence punishable before the Disciplinary Council provided for in Article 24.

The Minister of Justice may request the President of the Council to conduct an investigation into any matter that appears to him to warrant disciplinary prosecution.

The investigation shall be conducted upon assignment by the President of the Council through a member from among the members who are equal to or outrank the member complained against according to the rule of precedence. The result of this investigation shall be submitted to the Minister of Justice through the President of the State Council.

The Minister of Justice shall refer the member complained against to the Disciplinary Council if he finds in the investigation that which justifies such referral.

The Disciplinary Council shall be composed of five members:

- The President of the State Council (President).

- The Government Commissioner at the State Council (Vice-President).

- The two highest-step Presidents from among the Presidents of the Chambers (Members).

- The highest-step President of the Administrative Court (Member).

The President shall appoint a rapporteur from among the members of the Disciplinary Council.

The rapporteur shall conduct the necessary investigations, hear the concerned party and the complainant where necessary, receive the testimonies of witnesses under oath, and submit his report without delay to the Disciplinary Council.

The President shall immediately summon the concerned party to inspect the file and the report of the rapporteur and to appear before the Disciplinary Council at the hearing which he appoints for him.

The trial shall be held in camera. The report of the rapporteur shall be read out and the concerned party shall be asked to present his defence regarding the matters attributed to him.

The concerned party has the right to be assisted by a single lawyer or by one of his colleagues.

If he fails to appear, the Council shall examine the case in the light of the documents alone.

The Council shall issue its decision on the same day or adjourn it to the following day at the latest, and this decision shall be reasoned.

The decision of the Disciplinary Council shall not be subject to any avenue of recourse, including cassation, and shall be enforceable ipso jure immediately upon its notification to the concerned party through administrative channels.

*The text of this Article was repealed pursuant to Law 259 dated 6/10/93, then this Article was reinstated pursuant to Law 375 dated 4/11/94, Official Gazette Supplement 45 dated 10/11/94)

Members of the State Consultative Council who have exercised their office for a period of twenty years and have not incurred a disciplinary penalty may be admitted by decree to the honorary position at their rank upon leaving office. They shall thereupon enjoy the privileges set forth in this Law.

The services performed by the members of the Council in the judicial judiciary or in the Court of Accounts shall be added to their services in the State Consultative Council with respect to the application of this Article.

Save for the cases and procedures provided for in the preceding Articles, and notwithstanding any other text, no measure capable of prejudicing their status may be taken against the members of the State Consultative Council.

The disciplinary penalties that may be imposed are:

1 - Reprimand.

2 - Suspension from work without salary for a period not exceeding one year.

3 - Delay of advancement in step for a period not exceeding two years.

4 - Reduction in step.

5 - Reduction in category.

6 - Termination of service.

7 - Dismissal with deprivation of termination indemnity or retirement pension.

In the event of a reduction in step or category, the member shall retain his period of seniority for advancement in step, and in the event of dismissal with deprivation of termination indemnity or retirement pension, the retirement deductions shall be refunded to him.

The procedures followed in the prosecution of members of the Court of Cassation shall apply to the prosecution of members of the State Council for offences committed by them; however, if the member belongs to the category of assistant councillors of the first or second rank, the procedures followed in the prosecution of members of the Court of Appeal shall apply to him.

In all cases, the special provisions set forth in the following article shall be observed.

Members of the State Council shall not be prosecuted for felonies and misdemeanours arising out of their office except after consulting the Bureau of the Council and upon the request of the Minister of Justice, and if the public interest requires their immediate detention, the Minister of Justice may authorise the same after consulting the President of the State Council.

In the event that members of the State Council are prosecuted for felonies and misdemeanours not arising out of their office, they may not be detained except with the approval of the Minister of Justice after consulting the President of the State Council.

Every decision of conviction or acquittal rendered in a felony or misdemeanour against any member of the State Council shall be notified through the Minister of Justice to the Disciplinary Council to adjudicate upon the disciplinary consequences resulting from the acts that led to the criminal prosecution, unless removal from office has occurred by operation of law.

A member referred to trial for a felony or misdemeanour arising out of office shall be suspended from work by a decision of the Minister of Justice after consulting the President of the Council until the final decision is rendered in his regard.

The Minister of Justice may suspend from work:

1 - A member prosecuted for a felony or misdemeanour not arising out of office after consulting the President of the Council.

2 - A member referred to the Disciplinary Council.

The Council of Cases shall be composed of:

1 - The President of the State Consultative Council as President, and where it is impossible for him to attend, the Chamber President who has precedence in accordance with the rule provided for in Article 14 of the Statute of the State Consultative Council.

2 - The Chamber Presidents and three Counsellors chosen by the President of the State Consultative Council at the beginning of each judicial year, as members.

Decisions shall be issued by a bench composed of the President and at least four members, and in the event of a tie vote, the President shall have a casting vote.

The principles contained in its decisions shall serve as guidance for unifying the case law of the Chambers of the State Consultative Council.

The President of the State Consultative Council shall preside over the Administrative Chamber and may delegate one of the Chamber Presidents to act on his behalf. The President may assign one or more of the Counsellors or Assistant Counsellors to participate in the work of this Chamber in the capacity of a titular member.

Each Judicial Chamber shall be composed of a President and at least two Counsellors, and one or more Assistant Counsellors shall be attached to it to assist it in its work. The Chamber President may appoint a rapporteur and complete the bench where necessary. In addition to the Administrative Chamber over which he presides, the President of the Council may preside over any of the Judicial Chambers. In the event of the absence of the Chamber President, the Counsellor highest in grade shall perform his duties.

In the event that the post is vacant, or that the President is absent or unable to exercise his office, the Chamber President who has precedence in accordance with the rule provided for in Article Fourteen shall act in his stead, and the person acting in the stead of the titular President shall not benefit from the allowances of the office.

The Chambers shall be formed and the work distributed among them by a decision of the Minister of Justice upon the proposal of the Bureau of the State Consultative Council. A Counsellor may be a member of two Judicial Chambers at most. Where one of the Chambers is unable to perform its work due to the incompleteness of its quorum on account of vacancy, absence or any other reason, the Bureau of the State Consultative Council shall delegate Counsellors in the other Chambers to form or complete the incomplete Chambers.

A single Chamber may not include members related to one another by consanguinity or affinity up to the fourth degree.

None of them may participate in a case in which one of his relatives by blood or marriage is a party or an attorney, or in which one of his relatives by blood or marriage up to the same degree has adjudicated.

The provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure relating to the transfer of a case for legitimate suspicion and the recusal and withdrawal of judges shall apply before the State Consultative Council, provided that the application for transfer for legitimate suspicion must be submitted to the Council of Cases.

An action shall be referred to the Assembly of Litigation by a decision of the President of the State Consultative Council at any stage of the trial, and in such case the Chamber shall be divested of the action ipso jure upon the issuance of the decision. The Government Commissioner or the President of the Chamber may request the referral of an action to the Assembly of Litigation, and the Bureau of the State Consultative Council may take the decision to grant or to dismiss within three days from the date on which the request is lodged with it. The decision of the President of the Council to grant or to dismiss shall not be reasoned and this decision shall not be subject to any avenue of review. The actions of judges and the actions submitted are considered ipso jure. With the exception of the actions provided for in the preceding paragraph, the President of the State Consultative Council shall have the right to decide to consider any petition pending before the Assembly of Litigation on the date of entry into force of this Law to be within the jurisdiction of a judicial Chamber, provided that no report has been issued therein by the Rapporteur Counsellor.

The Government Commissioner shall assist the Chambers at the State Consultative Council and shall have four assistants at most appointed from among the Counsellors or Assistant Counsellors by a decree taken upon the recommendation of the Bureau of the Council and the proposal of the Minister of Justice.

The Government Commissioner or the Assistant Commissioner whom he delegates shall submit his reasoned submissions in all actions submitted to the State Consultative Council.

The Government Commissioner shall submit his submissions in person before the Assembly of Litigation, and where this is not possible his first assistant shall deputise for him.

The State Consultative Council shall meet in a General Assembly once every year in the month of October upon the convocation of the President.

The General Assembly shall be composed of all the members of the Council. It may not deliberate unless at least half of its members are present, and resolutions shall be taken by a majority of the votes of those present, and in the event of an equality of votes the President shall have a casting vote.

Meetings shall be secret, and the Chief Clerk shall draw up the minutes thereof, which may not be made public in any manner.

The President shall submit for discussion a report containing the work of the State Consultative Council during the preceding year and indicating the legislative, regulatory and administrative reforms which he deems to be in conformity with the public interest.

The President of the State Consultative Council shall notify the resolutions of the General Assembly to the Minister of Justice.

The President of the State Consultative Council shall undertake, in addition to the functions and duties assigned to him in this Law, the acts of administration, and shall carry out judicial and administrative inspection himself or through a member whom he delegates, and he may define the duties of the employees, distribute work among them, and delegate some of his administrative powers to the Assistant Counsellor supervising the administrative departments or to any other Assistant Counsellor.

The registry of the State Council and the registries of the administrative courts shall be composed of judicial assistants, ushers and process servers, and their number, categories, grades and salaries shall be determined in Schedules No. 3 and No. 4 annexed to this Law.

The judicial assistants are the heads of registries, chief clerks, process servers and stenographers in the registries of the State Council and the administrative courts, and their number and category shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice.

The judicial assistants shall undertake the clerical work provided for by law and all other work required for the conduct of business in the judicial departments.

The provisions set forth in the Law of the Judicial Judiciary shall apply to the judicial assistants attached to the administrative judiciary in all matters not inconsistent with the provisions of this Law.

The head of the registry shall be responsible for the proper conduct of business before the head of the judicial department, and shall have towards the employees of the registry the powers vested by the regulations of administrative employees in the head of a department.

The Disciplinary Council for judicial assistants at the administrative judiciary shall be composed of three administrative judges appointed by a decision of the Minister of Justice after taking the opinion of the Bureau of the Council for a term of three judicial years renewable once.

The function of Government Commissioner before the Disciplinary Council shall be performed by a judicial inspector delegated by the President of the Judicial Inspection Board.

The provisions of Articles 25, 26 and 27 of the Statute of the State Council shall apply before the Disciplinary Council.
The decisions of the Disciplinary Council for judicial assistants shall be taken by a majority and shall be subject to appeal before the State Council.

A judicial assistant shall be referred to the Disciplinary Council by a decision of the President of the State Council or by a decision of the President of the Judicial Inspection Board, and he may be suspended from work pursuant to the same decision.

The general Civil Service Statute shall apply to the judicial assistants in all matters not inconsistent with the provisions of this Law, and they shall be disciplinarily subject to the Judicial Inspection.

The judicial vacation in the State Council shall begin on 15 July and end on the first of October of each year, and work during it shall be organised by a decision of the Bureau of the Council.

Members of the State Council shall not be entitled to any allowance in addition to this vacation; however, it shall pertain to the Minister of Justice to grant them leave not exceeding fifteen days per year at full salary upon a written request submitted to him through hierarchical channels.

The State Consultative Council shall participate in the preparation of draft laws; it shall give its opinion on the drafts referred to it by the Ministers, propose the amendments that it deems necessary, and prepare and draft the texts that it is requested to draw up.
