To this end, it may carry out the necessary investigations and seek the assistance of persons of opinion and expertise.

The State Consultative Council must be consulted on draft legislative decrees, on draft regulatory texts, and on all matters in which laws and regulations provide for the obligation to consult it.

It may be consulted on draft international treaties, draft circulars, and on any important subject on which the Council of Ministers decides to consult it.

The competent Minister shall refer to the State Consultative Council the drafts and matters provided for in the two preceding Articles.

The panel shall deliberate on the basis of the report of one of its members.

The Minister of Justice may request the President of the State Consultative Council to appoint one of the members of the Council to assist the administrations in preparing one of the drafts provided for in the two preceding Articles 56 and 57.

The Administrative Courts are the ordinary courts for administrative cases.

The State Consultative Council is the appellate authority for all judgments issued by the Administrative Courts, the appellate or cassation authority in administrative cases for which the law has designated a special court, and the court of first and last instance for certain cases.

The Administrative Courts shall adjudicate in the first instance in particular:

1 - On claims for compensation for damages that occur by reason of public works or the execution of public services, or damages resulting from the operation of administrative work in the Chamber of Deputies.

2 - On administrative cases relating to administrative contracts, procurement deals, concessions, or franchises concluded by public administrations or administrative departments in the Chamber of Deputies to ensure the operation of public services.

3 - On employees' cases and individual disputes relating to the employees of the Chamber of Deputies.

4 - On cases relating to the occupation of public property.

5 - On cases in which the administrative authority has recourse against employees in the event that they commit a fault that was the cause of a judgment being rendered against it.

6 - On cases of direct and indirect taxes and fees, notwithstanding any other general or special text.

- Claims for compensation for damages resulting from vehicle accidents shall fall outside the jurisdiction of the administrative judiciary and shall be adjudicated by the judicial courts.

All committees for objections to direct and indirect taxes and to state and municipal fees established under the various laws on taxes and fees are hereby abolished.

All objections pending before these committees shall be referred through administrative channels to the Administrative Courts in accordance with their territorial jurisdiction within one month from the date of entry into force of this Law.

The interested party in the various cases of taxes and fees must file an objection thereto before the competent financial department prior to bringing an action before the Administrative Court, under penalty of dismissal of the objection. For this purpose, the provisions of Articles 2 to 9 and Article 17 of Decree No. 15947 dated 31 March 1964 concerning the determination of the procedures for objections to taxes and fees and the time limits for deciding thereon shall remain in force.

1 - The Administrative Courts shall hear applications for annulment on the ground of abuse of power of decisions of an administrative nature, whether they relate to individuals or to regulations, issued by a local public authority (Governor - Kaymakam - Municipal Council, etc...).

2 - Disputes relating to the legality of the elections of administrative councils such as municipal councils, elective bodies (mukhtars and councils of elders) and others.

3 - Disputes relating to the discipline of local employees.

Notwithstanding any other provision, the State Council shall hear disputes relating to the discipline of civil servants.

Disciplinary decisions issued by the Supreme Judicial Council shall not be subject to recourse, including recourse in cassation.

The preceding paragraph shall apply to recourses in which no final binding judgment has been rendered.

(The provisions of the first paragraph of Article 64 of Law No. 227 dated 31 May 2000 amending certain articles of the Statute of the State Council shall apply to all pending recourses that have not been accompanied by a final binding judgment, including judgments that are the subject of an application for retrial.(L428/2002)

(The second and third paragraphs of this Article, added pursuant to Law No. 227 d. 31/5/2000, were annulled for violating the Constitution and principles of constitutional value pursuant to the Decision of the Constitutional Council dated 2000/6/27).

The State Council shall adjudicate at first and last instance the following disputes:

1 - Applications for annulment on the ground of excess of power against implementing and individual decrees and regulatory acts issued by ministers.

2 - Cases concerning civil servants appointed by decree.

3 - Appeals concerning individual administrative decisions the scope of application of which exceeds the territorial jurisdiction of a single administrative court.

4 - Applications for the interpretation or assessment of the validity of administrative acts that fall within the jurisdiction of the State Council at first and last instance.

The judicial courts shall stay the determination of actions brought before them if the resolution of such actions requires the interpretation or assessment of the validity of an administrative act the examination of which falls outside their jurisdiction.

5 - The most diligent party shall refer the question to the State Council, and the Council shall deliver an opinion binding on the judicial courts in the case for which the opinion was given.

6 - Cases of connexity.

First: The President of the State Council, the President of the Administrative Court, or a judge delegated by either of them may, upon the request of the party concerned and within one week from the receipt of the request, appoint an expert tasked with inspecting the facts that are likely to give rise to an application before the Administrative Courts or the State Council.

The decision shall be notified to the person against whom a claim is likely to be brought, and such person shall be summoned to attend the inspection.

Every report prepared by an expert appointed in violation of the provisions of the first paragraph of this Article shall be deemed null and void, shall not be admitted before the administrative judiciary, and may not be relied upon.

The President of the State Council, the President of the Court, or the judge delegated by him shall determine the fees of the expert.

The parties and the expert shall have the right to file an opposition against the decision determining the fees before the chamber presided over by the judge who issued the decision, within a time limit of one week from the date of notification, under penalty of dismissal as to form. The decision issued shall be final and enforceable upon its original.

Second: Prior to the filing of any application, the President of the State Council, the President of the Administrative Court, or the judge delegated by either of them may, in cases of urgency and upon the request of the party concerned, take, within one week at most from the receipt of the request, all necessary and possible provisional and conservatory measures calculated to preserve rights and prevent damage, without prejudice to the merits of the right, and he may decide that a guarantee be furnished.

The judge of urgent matters shall not have the right to take measures or procedures calculated to stay the execution of an administrative act, in whole or in part, and he may impose a fine on the adversary who abstains from executing his decision referred to in the preceding paragraph.

Third: Without prejudice to the merits of the right, the President of the State Council, the President of the Administrative Court, or the judge delegated by either of them may, upon the request of the party concerned who has filed an action on the merits, order his adversary to pay him an advance on the amount claimed where his application is based on serious and important grounds, in return for furnishing a bank guarantee from a bank approved by the Central Bank guaranteeing the execution of a judgment against him to return the advance together with the compensation deemed appropriate by the Council as a result of his having received the advance beforehand.

- Adversaries shall be granted, from the date of notification of the request, a time limit ranging between twenty-four hours and one week to reply to the request of the party concerned referred to in Items Second and Third mentioned above.

Fourth: An opposition may be filed before the competent chamber or the Court against the decision on urgent matters taken in accordance with Items Second and Third within a time limit of eight days from the date of notification.

The opposition shall be adjudicated in the council chamber by a separate decision within one week without following any other procedure, and the rapporteur shall participate in the judgment.

Decisions on urgent matters taken in accordance with the second and third paragraphs of this Article shall not carry the force of res judicata and may be amended or revoked upon the request of one of the parties if new circumstances arise that justify the same.

Fifth: An application may be made to the President of the Administrative Court or the person delegated by him in the event of a breach of the obligations of publicity and ensuring competition to which public procurement contracts and agreements relating to the management of a public service are subject.

The persons having standing to bring the action are those who have an interest in concluding the contract and who may be harmed by such breach, as well as the representative of the State in the administration concerned where the contract is concluded or is to be concluded by a municipality or a public institution.

An application may be made to the President of the Administrative Court prior to the conclusion of the contract, and he may order the party in breach to comply with his obligations and may suspend the signing of the contract or the execution of every decision relating thereto, and he may also annul such decisions and strike out the clauses intended to be inserted in the contract which violate the aforementioned obligations.

The President of the Administrative Court or the person delegated by him shall adjudicate in accordance with the summary procedure.

Adversaries shall be granted, from the date of being notified of the request, a time limit ranging between twenty-four hours and one week to reply to the request of the party concerned. The decision of the President of the Administrative Court or the person delegated by him shall be subject to appeal before the State Council within a time limit of one week from the date of notification, and the State Council shall adjudicate the appeal in the same manner.

Article 18: Appearance and soundness of buildings: 1- The construction of buildings in the form of a bridge over roads is prohibited unless the approved zoning regulations of the area so provide, or in exceptional cases justified by aesthetic architectural considerations, provided that the exception is made by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport and after consulting the opinion of the Higher Council for Urban Planning, and the conditions for constructing such buildings shall be determined in this decree. 2- The shape and colouring of facades and boundary walls must be acceptable, and the Administration shall have the right to assess this. 3- Owners may be required to enclose their properties with boundary walls towards the road, and if they abstain, the Administration shall have the right, after serving notice upon them, to construct the said boundary wall at their expense. 4- Owners must maintain the cleanliness of the facades of their buildings and their other parts, and they are required, where necessary, to paint, plaster, whitewash or repair them, and if they abstain, the Administration shall have the right, after serving notice upon them, to carry out the said work at their expense. 5- The owner must always ensure the maintenance of his built properties and secure the necessary stability and soundness thereof in order to preserve the safety of the occupants and the neighbourhood. Whenever the need arises, or at the request of the Administration, he must commission one or more engineers to inspect the building, investigate by appropriate technical means, and submit a detailed report on the condition of the building. '' If it appears to the engineer that the building or parts thereof have shown signs of weakness, he must indicate in his report, as far as possible, the cause of this weakness and its probable consequences, and propose the works that must be carried out while indicating the degree of urgency thereof. If it is established as a result of the engineer's report that the stability or soundness of the building is impaired, the owner must carry out, under the supervision of the responsible engineer, the necessary temporary construction and shoring works, and inform the municipality, or the Qaemaqam outside the municipal area, of what he has done. Thereafter, he must take the necessary measures, after agreement with the occupants of the building or by applying to the court of urgent matters, if necessary, to carry out the final strengthening works after obtaining a permit from the municipality. Upon completion of the work, the engineer shall draw up a report on the works he has carried out, indicating therein the new condition of the building. 6- When a danger of collapse appears in the building, the owner is obliged to carry out the necessary shoring without delay at his own expense and responsibility, and to inform the municipality, or the Mukhtar where there is no municipality, thereof immediately. 7- When a building, walls, or otherwise threatens to collapse and its remaining constitutes a danger of any kind, and the owner does not proceed to fulfill his obligations, either because he is unable to carry out the necessary strengthening works or because he abstains from doing so, it must be demolished within a period of not less than fifteen days and not more than two months, and the municipality concerned may evacuate the building of its occupants. '' If it is impossible to notify the owner, or if he abstains from receiving the demolition warning, a record of the fact must be drawn up by the employees of the municipality, or the Mukhtar where there is no municipality. In this case, a copy of the demolition warning shall be affixed to the building required to be demolished and another copy to the door of the municipality headquarters, or to the door of the governorate or Qaemaqamiyya headquarters outside the municipal area. The demolition period shall commence as from the date of notification or affixing of the demolition warning. If the period expires and the owner has not executed the orders of the Administration, the municipality shall proceed to execute the demolition at his expense, and the municipality may sell the rubble resulting from the demolition in recovery of the expenses. In the event of an extreme necessity to demolish one of the buildings pursuant to a report of the technical departments, the warning period may be reduced to one day, in which case the provisions of this paragraph must be mentioned in the demolition warning. 8- By a decree adopted upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport and after consulting the opinion of the Higher Council for Urban Planning, special conditions may be imposed for the shape of the building, its external appearance, and the materials used in respect of building and restoration permits in certain areas. 9- The creation of covered passages and pavements within buildings for public use may be imposed, the conditions and specifications of which shall be determined by a decree adopted upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport.

The rules of procedure before the State Council shall apply before the administrative courts.

No individual may bring an action before the administrative judiciary except by way of an application for review against a decision issued by the administrative authority.

Where the authority has not issued a decision, the interested party shall obtain in advance a decision from the competent authority, and to that end shall submit a lawful request to the authority, which shall issue him, free of charge, a receipt stating the subject of the request and the date of its receipt. If the authority does not grant his request within a period of two months from the date of its receipt of the request submitted by him, its silence shall be deemed a decision of rejection, except in the following two cases:

1- If the administrative authority is a deliberative body that convenes only in specified sessions, the two-month time limit shall be extended, where necessary, until the conclusion of the first session held after the submission of the request.

2- If the determination of the subject of the request is subject to statutory time limits exceeding two months in total, the silence of the Administration shall not constitute an implicit decision of rejection until the expiry of those time limits.

The time limit for an application for review shall be two months commencing from the date of publication of the contested decision, unless it is an individual decision, in which case the time limit shall commence from the date of notification or execution. Where the administrative decision is an implicit decision of rejection resulting from the silence of the Administration, the two-month time limit provided for in the preceding paragraph shall commence upon the expiry of the period specified in Article 68. If an express decision is issued before the expiry of the said two-month time limit, the time limit for the application for review shall run anew from that decision, and if such decision is issued after the expiry of the two-month time limit, it shall not give rise to a new time limit. Where the time limit for a judicial application for review has expired and the interested party thereafter submits an administrative appeal to the same authority or to its superior authority, the Administration's proceeding to examine the matter anew shall not reopen the recourse to an application for review if the decision issued as a result of such examination confirms the initial decision. An action brought after the expiry of the time limit shall be inadmissible.

A full-jurisdiction application for review founded upon the illegality of an administrative decision against which the time limit for challenge has expired shall not be heard if the application is based on the same legal ground upon which an application for annulment against that decision could have been founded and if it has the same financial consequences as would have resulted from an application for annulment. The provisions of this Article shall not apply to applications for review submitted on a date prior to the entry into force of this Law, nor to those the right to submit which lapsed under the previous law.

The time limit for the recourse shall be interrupted:

1- If the interested party submits, within the time limit, an administrative recourse to the same authority or to its superior authority, in which case the time limit shall commence from the date of notification of the explicit decision or from the date of the implicit decision issued regarding this administrative recourse, and the time limit shall only be interrupted by reason of a single recourse.

2- If the interested party requests legal aid within the time limit for the recourse, in which case the time limit for the recourse shall commence anew as of the date of notifying the interested party of the decision issued regarding the legal aid.

3- If the interested party submits a recourse before an incompetent court, in which case the time limit shall commence anew from the date of notifying him of the judgment

Recourses of individuals shall be brought by a petition lodged with the registry of the Council, and this petition must include the following:

1- The first name, surname, profession, and place of residence of the petitioner, and, where applicable, the first name, surname, profession, and place of residence of the respondent.

2- The subject matter of the petition, a statement of the facts, and a mention of the points of law upon which the petition is based.

3- A mention of the documents attached to the petition.

4- The appointment of a lawyer, and the signature of the lawyer on the petition or the reply brief shall be deemed an election of domicile by his client at his office. The legal stamp shall be affixed to the petition.

The following documents must be attached to the petition:

1- Copies thereof certified by the petitioner as true copies of the original, the number of which shall be equal to the number of adversaries in the action.

2- A copy certified as a true copy of the original of the contested decision or of the receipt provided for in Article 68

3- A certificate from the judge or the president of the court hearing the principal action if the recourse is submitted regarding a request for the interpretation or assessment of the validity of an administrative act.

4- A copy, where applicable, of the decision granting the petitioner legal aid.

5- The receipt proving payment of the fine provided for in Article 131

6- The power of attorney granted by the plaintiff to his lawyer in the legal form.

Recourses of the administrative authority shall be brought before the State Consultative Council in accordance with the provisions of the two preceding Articles and shall be exempted from stamp duties, the fine, and the appointment of a lawyer.

Petitions by virtue of which an action is brought shall be registered upon receipt at the Registry of the Council in a register kept by the clerk, which shall be sequentially numbered and initialled in due form. Petitions shall be stamped with a seal indicating the date of their submission and a receipt shall be given therefor. The Assistant Councillor supervising the administrative departments shall notify the petitioner within one week of any deficiency existing in the petition. Such deficiency must be remedied within fifteen days from notification, and if this period expires without it being remedied, the Council may issue a decision declaring the nullity of the petition. Unless the action has become ready for judgment, the course of the trial shall be stayed for a period of one year if the Council becomes aware of the death of one of the litigants, or its dissolution if it is a legal person, or the resignation or death of the legal representative. If this period expires and the interested parties have not proceeded to regularise the litigation and pursue the action in due form, the bench seized thereof may decide, in the deliberation chamber, the nullity of the petition.

Once the subject-matter of the claim and the legal grounds justifying it have been specified in the petition, any additional claims and new legal grounds raised by the petitioner during the action shall be deemed null and void, unless the time limit for the recourse has not yet expired. However, the Council must rule on legal grounds that are of a public policy nature even if none of the parties has raised them.

A recourse shall not stay the execution of the impugned administrative act or judicial decision. The State Council may order a stay of execution on the basis of an express request by the petitioner if it appears from the case file that execution may cause severe damage to the petitioner and that the recourse rests on important new grounds. However, a stay of execution shall not be permissible if the recourse seeks the annulment of a regulatory decree or the annulment of a decision relating to the preservation of public order, security, public safety, or public health. The opposing party shall be granted a time limit of two weeks at most to reply to the request for a stay of execution, and the State Council must rule thereon within a time limit of two weeks at most from the date on which the reply of the opposing party is filed.

Within the three days following the conclusion of the exchange of pleadings, the President of the Chamber seized of the action shall appoint a rapporteur to whom he shall refer the file, and the President may perform the function of rapporteur.
The rapporteur shall conduct the investigation of the recourse and carry out such inquiries as he deems fit to elucidate the case.

Notifications shall be made in administrative form against a receipt, and the time limits shall be fixed as follows: four months to reply to the petition. Two months to reply to the briefs. The said time limits shall commence in principle from the date of notification, and with respect to the State or public institutions and municipalities on the eighth day following the date of delivery of the documents to the registry of the Cases Authority at the Ministry of Justice with respect to the State and the competent registry in public institutions and municipalities, and the employee receiving the documents must sign the notification instrument in acknowledgement of receipt. The time limits referred to shall commence with respect to the other parties from the date of notification. And the concerned person shall be notified at his actual or elected place of residence. Notification shall be effected through process servers attached to the administrative judiciary who are seconded for this purpose by a decision of the Minister of Justice.
The petitioner shall not have the right to submit more than one reply except by special authorisation from the rapporteur.

The parties and their lawyers shall have the right to inspect the case documents in the registry of the Council without removing them from their place and under the supervision of the supervising assistant councillor.

Every interested party may intervene in the action, and the Council or the rapporteur may also join him therein. The request for intervention shall be submitted by a separate petition and this request may only contain support for the standpoint of one of the parties.

The rapporteur shall determine the form in which the investigation proceedings shall be conducted, and in so doing he shall be guided by the principles set forth in the Code of Civil Procedure without being bound to adhere to them literally, and he shall ensure that all investigation proceedings are complete and impartial and that the right of defence is respected. Each party shall have the right to inspect the record drawn up at the end of every investigation.

The rapporteur may take, either of his own motion or at the request of the parties, the measures that he deems necessary for the investigation, such as appointing experts, hearing witnesses under oath, conducting an on-site inspection, examining entries and questioning individuals, and he may request public administrations to submit reports, opinions and registers and summon the competent employees to seek clarification from them on technical and material aspects.

The decisions taken by the rapporteur shall be notified to the parties, and they shall not be reasoned, and they may be appealed before the Chamber within a time limit of five days after depositing a security of fifty pounds. The opposing party shall be invited to submit his observations within forty-eight hours. The Chamber shall rule on the appeal without any formality within eight days, and the rapporteur shall participate in the judgment.

Where the State Council considers that an appeal filed by a party other than public administrations against a decision of the rapporteur is intended only to delay the determination of the action and is not based on any serious ground, it shall adjudge the forfeiture of the deposit against the appellant.

Upon the completion of the investigation procedure, the rapporteur shall draw up a report which he shall send with the file to the Government Commissioner. This report shall include a summary of the case, the facts and the points of law that must be resolved, as well as the opinion of the rapporteur.

The Government Commissioner shall examine all the documents sent to him and shall then refer it to the President of the Chamber accompanied by his written submissions.

The parties shall be summoned to examine the report and the submissions, and they may obtain a copy thereof upon their request. The summons shall be effected by means of a notice containing the names of the parties and the numbers of the actions, which shall be published in the Official Gazette, and a copy thereof shall be posted on the door of the Registry of the State Council in the first week of every month, and the Chief Clerk shall draw up a record thereof.

The parties and their lawyers acting as counsel may submit their written observations regarding the report and the submissions within a time limit of one month from the date of publication of the notice in the Official Gazette.

Save for the provisions relating to the composition of the Cases Assembly, each action shall be heard by a bench composed of a president and two members, one of whom shall be the rapporteur, and the bench shall deliberate in secret and shall take its decision unanimously or by a majority, and the decision shall be pronounced in a public hearing the date of which shall be notified to the parties, within a maximum time limit of three months from the date of expiry of the time limit granted to the parties to submit their observations regarding the report and the submissions.

The decision shall be issued in the name of the Lebanese People by a unanimity of opinions or by a majority thereof, and if it is issued by a majority of opinions, reference thereto shall be made therein, and the dissenting judge shall record his dissent.

The decision must include the following:

1 - The names of the judges who participated in issuing it.

2 - The names of the parties, their place of residence, and a statement of their claims.

3 - Reference to the principal documents in the file.

4 - Reference to the legislative, regulatory or contractual texts applied in the decision.

5 - The factual and legal grounds.

6 - The operative part.

7 - The date of pronouncement of the decision in the public hearing.

The decision shall be limited to declaring the legal situations that constitute solely the subject matter of the action which it determines. The State Council shall not be entitled to act in the place of the competent administrative authority to deduce from such situations the legal consequences resulting therefrom and to take the decisions required thereby.

The decision shall be signed by the President, the members who participated in issuing it, and the Clerk of the Council, and the decision shall be transcribed into a special register and notified ex officio to the Government Commissioner and the litigants.

The judgments of the State Council are binding upon the administration. The administrative authorities must abide by the legal situations as described by these judgments. A legal person of public law must execute within a reasonable time limit the final judgments issued by the State Council under pain of liability, and if it delays in the execution without cause, it may, upon the request of the aggrieved party, be ordered to pay a coercive fine assessed by the State Council which shall remain in effect until the execution of the judgment.

Every official who uses his authority or his influence directly or indirectly to obstruct or delay the execution of the judicial decision mentioned in the preceding paragraph shall be fined before the Court of Accounts in an amount not less than the salary of three months and not exceeding the salary of six months.

The judgments of the administrative courts shall not be subject to any means of recourse except third-party opposition and appeal.

In actions of full jurisdiction (with the exception of tax actions), an appeal shall only be admissible against judgments the value of which exceeds fifty million Lebanese pounds.

The decisions of the State Council shall not be subject to any means of recourse except opposition, third-party opposition, retrial, and a request for the correction of a material error.

Decisions issued in absentia are subject to opposition. Opposition does not stay execution unless the State Council decides so. Opposition shall be submitted within a time limit of two months starting from the date of notification of the decision in absentia, and every opposition submitted after the expiry of the time limit shall be dismissed in form.

If a decision is issued inter partes with respect to one party and in absentia with respect to another party, the latter shall not have the right to file an opposition against the decision if his interest does not differ from the interest of the other party.

If the decision causes damage to a person who was neither a party to the action nor represented therein, this person shall have the right to oppose the decision by way of third-party opposition. Applications for third-party opposition must be submitted. Applications for third-party opposition must be submitted under pain of dismissal within a time limit of two months from the date of knowledge of the issuance of the judgment, provided that the time limit does not exceed, in any event, five years from the date of its issuance.

An application for retrial shall not be admissible except in the following cases:

1 - If the decision was based on forged documents.

2 - If judgment was rendered against one of the adversaries for his failure to produce a decisive document held in the possession of his adversary.

3 - If the essential rules of procedure prescribed by the law were not observed in the investigation and judgment.

Applications for retrial must be submitted under pain of dismissal:

In the first case within two months from the date of issuance of a final judgment establishing the forgery and in the second and third cases within two months from the date of notification of the contested decision.

If a decision of the State Council is tainted by a material error that had an effect on the judgment, the concerned party may submit to the Council an application for rectification. This application must be submitted within a period of two months from the date of receipt of notification of the decision whose rectification is sought.

Decisions issued regarding applications for retrial and rectification of a material error shall not be subject to any avenue of recourse, and this Article shall apply to recourses submitted prior to the promulgation of this Law which are still pending.

Actions of opposition, third-party opposition, retrial, and rectification shall be subject to the same rules to which the actions in respect of which the contested decision was issued are subject, subject to observance of the special provisions mentioned above. The Chamber that issued the contested decision shall hear these cases.

Summary procedure shall apply:

1- In the recourses provided for in Articles 63 and 64 of this Law.

2- In recourses of full jurisdiction when the value of the action does not exceed two thousand pounds. The petitioner shall assess the value of the action.

When applying summary procedure, the ordinary rules of trial procedure shall apply with the exception of the following:

1 - Individuals may bring their action without a prior decision from the administrative authority, and their petition shall be exempted from the appointment of an advocate.

2 - The Rapporteur must investigate the action within the shortest possible time limit and his decisions shall not be subject to appeal, whereas the time limit fixed for the adversaries to submit their defence or their reply shall be eight days at least and fifteen days at most, and no rejoinder to the reply brief may be submitted nor may its submission be authorised except by a decision of the Bench.

3 - The Rapporteur shall draw up a summary report which he shall send with the file to the Government Commissioner, and the latter must return it with his submissions within eight days to the President, and the adversaries may submit their observations on the report of the Rapporteur and the submissions of the Government Commissioner within a time limit of five days from the date of notification, and judgment in the case must be rendered without delay.

The President of the Chamber may authorise by a special decision, and in full-jurisdiction recourses exclusively, upon a request submitted by one of the adversaries and after taking the opinion of the Government Commissioner, the application of summary procedure rules if he considers that this matter does not inflict any harm upon the litigants, provided that in this case the prior administrative decision remained mandatory.

An application for annulment on the ground of excess of power may not be submitted except against purely administrative decisions that have enforceable force and are capable of inflicting harm, and the recourse may not in any case be admitted with respect to acts having a legislative or judicial character.

An application for annulment on the ground of excess of power shall not be admitted except from a person who proves that he has a direct, personal, and legitimate interest in the annulment of the impugned decision.
An application for annulment on the ground of excess of power shall not be admitted from a person who is able to resort to another judicial recourse in order to obtain the same result.

The State Council must annul administrative acts tainted by one of the defects mentioned below:

1 - If they are issued by an incompetent authority.

2 - If they are taken contrary to the essential formalities provided for in the laws and regulations.

3 - If they are taken contrary to the law or the regulations or contrary to res judicata.

4 - If they are taken for a purpose other than the purpose for which the law vested the competent authority with the right to take them.

An objection to the validity of the elections of administrative councils, such as municipal councils and optional bodies, may be made by every voter in the relevant district, by every person who submitted his candidacy therein in a legal manner, and by the State upon the request of the Minister of Interior.

The objections of voters and candidates shall be submitted, under penalty of dismissal, within a time limit of fifteen days from the proclamation of the results of the elections, and a written petition without any other formality shall suffice, and the objection shall be notified to the State and to the persons whose election is impugned.
The objection of the State shall be submitted, under penalty of dismissal, within a time limit of one month from the proclamation of the results of the elections.
In disciplinary cases, the concerned employee shall submit the application for annulment or cassation within thirty days following the notification to him of the disciplinary decision.
The State Council shall not be entitled, in disciplinary cases, to examine the appropriateness of the prescribed penalty.

The appeal of judgments rendered in the first instance by administrative bodies of a judicial nature shall be subject to the rules provided for in the laws and regulations specific to the said bodies, and the time limit for appeal shall be two months from the date of notification in the absence of a contrary provision.

- An appeal transfers the action to the State Council, whereupon the Council shall re-examine it and adjudicate upon it anew.

- When the State Council examines an action as an appellate instance, it also becomes competent to examine an action brought in the first instance and containing claims connected to the appellate action, and the State Council also becomes competent in the first instance when the action brought before the Administrative Court contains claims interrelated with an action previously brought before it.

- The Administrative Court examining an action within the scope of its territorial jurisdiction becomes

competent as well to examine interrelated claims that fall within the jurisdiction of a second Administrative Court.

- If petitions are brought before two Administrative Courts and there exists an interrelation between them, the two actions shall be referred to the President of the State Council, who must take a decision without any modification designating the competent court. The decision of the President of the Council shall not be subject to any avenue of recourse.

- The court declared competent pursuant to the decision of the President of the State Council must comply with this decision, with the exception of declaring the lack of jurisdiction of the administrative judiciary to examine the present petition.

- All trial proceedings that have been completed shall remain in effect before the Administrative Court or the State Council.
An appeal lodged within the legal time limit shall not stay the execution of the appealed judgment, unless the State Council decides otherwise.
Judgments rendered in the last instance by administrative bodies of a judicial nature may be challenged by way of cassation even if the law does not provide therefor.
Cassation does not transfer the action to the State Council; rather, the right of the Council is confined to verifying that the trial judge drew from the facts their legal consequences.

The time limit for cassation is two months from the date of notification of the judgment, and it shall only be heard if it is submitted by one of the litigants and founded upon one of the grounds set forth in paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 of Article 108
Where the State Consultative Council quashes the contested judgment, the court that issued it shall be bound to comply with the decision of the Council.

Subject to the rules referred to in this Chapter, the State Consultative Council shall follow, in appeals and cassation proceedings, the procedures provided for in Chapter Two of Title Four of this Law.

The Cases Authority at the Ministry of Justice may submit, of its own motion or upon the request of the competent Minister, applications in the interest of the law against any administrative or judicial decision once such decision has become final. If the State Consultative Council rules for annulment, such decision may neither benefit nor prejudice the litigants.

The competent Enforcement Department shall ensure, in accordance with the rules provided for in the Code of Civil Procedure, the enforcement of decisions issued by the State Consultative Council and the administrative courts against individuals where the laws do not permit their enforcement by administrative means.
In the enforcement proceedings mentioned in the preceding Article, the procedures observed in the Code of Civil Procedure shall be followed.

The President of the Enforcement Department shall adjudicate on the merits of enforcement difficulties relating to procedures, and the administrative court that issued the decision being enforced shall adjudicate on the merits of all other difficulties. However, with respect to decisions issued by the State Consultative Council as an appellate authority, adjudicating on the difficulty shall fall within the jurisdiction of the State Consultative Council if it ruled to set aside the appealed decision, and within the jurisdiction of the administrative court that issued the decision at first instance if a judgment was rendered affirming the said decision.

Applications for the enforcement of decisions issued against the administrative authority shall be submitted to the President of the State Consultative Council, who shall refer them without delay, together with the copy valid for enforcement, to the competent authorities to take the necessary action.

Trial expenses shall include judicial fees, investigation expenses such as the expenses of expertise and witnesses, the expenses of procedures whose tariff is officially fixed, the fees of the Judges' Mutual Fund, and advocacy fees.

The Tribunal of Conflicts shall be composed of:

The President: the President of the State Consultative Council or the First President of the Court of Cassation.

The Members:

1 - The Vice-President of the State Consultative Council and a Councillor of the State Consultative Council appointed by the President of the Council at the beginning of each judicial year.

2 - A Chamber President and a Councillor of the Court of Cassation or a President of a Court of Appeal appointed by the President of the Supreme Judicial Council at the beginning of each judicial year.

The Government Commissioner: the Government Commissioner at the State Consultative Council or the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation.

Two Alternate Members: a Councillor of the State Consultative Council and a Councillor of the Court of Cassation appointed in the manner set out above to complete the bench where necessary.

The presidency of the Tribunal of Conflicts shall rotate between the President of the State Consultative Council and the First President of the Court of Cassation for the duration of one judicial year.

When the Tribunal is presided over by the President of the State Consultative Council, the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation shall perform the function of Government Commissioner, and when it is presided over by the First President of the Court of Cassation, the function of Government Commissioner shall be performed by the Government Commissioner at the State Consultative Council.

The Tribunal of Conflicts shall convene at the invitation of its President at his place of work and shall always be composed of a President and four members.

The administrative departments at the State Consultative Council shall provide the registry services of the Tribunal.
The Tribunal of Conflicts shall apply the rules of procedure of the State Consultative Council, and its decisions shall not be subject to any avenue of recourse.

The Tribunal of Conflicts shall hear negative conflicts of jurisdiction.

A negative conflict of jurisdiction is a conflict resulting from two decisions declining jurisdiction rendered in the same case, the first by an administrative court and the second by a judicial court.

These two decisions need not have been rendered at last instance.

The application shall be lodged by the interested party. The application shall not stay execution and may only be lodged within a time limit of two months from the notification to him of the last decision declining jurisdiction.

The Tribunal of Conflicts shall render its judgment annulling the erroneous decision declining jurisdiction and shall refer the parties back to the court that erroneously held itself to lack jurisdiction.

The court to which the action is referred must comply with the decision of the Tribunal of Conflicts.

The Tribunal of Conflicts shall also hear contradictions between two judgments resulting in a denial of justice.

The two judgments must have been rendered one by a judicial court and the second by an administrative court, and must have adjudicated upon the merits of a dispute having the same subject-matter, and it is not necessary that the litigants be the same or the grounds identical.

There shall apply before the State Council and the administrative courts all the provisions provided for in the tariff of the courts of first instance designated in Chapters One, Two, Four and Five of Title One of the Law on Judicial Fees issued on 10/10/1950 and its amendments and in Articles 80, 81, 82, 86, 87, 88, 89, 91, 92, 93, 99 and 100 of the aforementioned Law.

Half of the proportional fee shall be collected upon the submission of the petition, and the remainder upon the issuance of the decision. The amount of the fixed fee before the State Council is /50,000/ Lebanese pounds (fifty thousand pounds) and it shall be collected in full at the time of submitting the petition.
Requests for interpretation and for rendering an opinion on the validity of an administrative act shall be subject to the fixed fee.

In cases of appeal, cassation, third-party opposition, retrial and correction of a material error, the petitioner, with the exception of the State, must deposit with the Treasury fund upon submitting the petition the following securities, under penalty of dismissal of the petition in form:

1 - Ten thousand L.L. if the value of the petition does not exceed four hundred thousand Lebanese pounds.

2 - Twenty thousand L.L. if the value of the petition exceeds four hundred thousand Lebanese pounds.

3 - Twenty thousand L.L. if the petition is not susceptible of valuation.

4 - Twenty thousand L.L. in cases of correction of a material error.

5 - One hundred thousand L.L. in cases of retrial.

6 - Ten thousand L.L. upon appealing the decision of the rapporteur or the decision appointing the expert; a single security shall suffice if there are multiple original petitioners in a single application.

The security shall be forfeited as revenue to the Treasury if the petition is dismissed in form or on the merits.

The provisions of this Article shall not apply to actions that were submitted under the previous law.

Costs shall be liquidated in the final decision.
One of the judges of the corps appointed by the President shall adjudicate cases of legal aid, and his decision shall be subject to appeal before the Chamber within a period of fifteen days.

The State Council may award compensation for any damage arising from a claim, defence or plea made in bad faith.

It may, when it deems it inequitable to leave the expenses not included in the trial costs upon one of the litigants who incurred them, compel the other litigant to pay him the amount that it determines, including lawyer's fees.
This Law shall enter into force as from the day following the date of its publication in the Official Gazette.

The petition must be submitted within a time limit of two months starting from the day on which the latter judgment became final.

The Court of Conflicts shall rule on the merits with respect to all the litigants, and it may conduct investigations if it deems that appropriate, and it shall also award the costs of the action before both the administrative and judicial courts.

Lastly, the Court of Conflicts shall hear the contradiction resulting from a divergence of jurisprudence between the administrative courts and the judicial courts.

The Court shall decide these cases in the interest of the law, and the provisions of Article 122 of this Law shall then apply.
Petitions submitted to the Court of Conflicts shall not be subject to any fee whatsoever except the stamp duty.
The interest awarded by the courts against the State, public institutions, or municipalities may not exceed nine percent (9%).

Legislative Decree No. 3 dated 30/11/1954 is repealed. The State Council shall hear the actions pending before the Special Administrative Court, which shall be referred to it through administrative channels, unless a judgment has been rendered therein divesting the Special Administrative Court of jurisdiction as of the date this Law enters into force, and the judgments rendered by it shall remain subject to the avenues of recourse that were in force on the date they were rendered.

The employees of the administrative cadre at the Special Administrative Court who are in service on the date this Law enters into force shall be transferred by operation of law, and without the need to issue any instrument, to the administrative cadre at the State Council, and the appropriations allocated in the budget and earmarked for the Special Administrative Court shall be transferred by operation of law and without the need to issue any instrument and added to the appropriations earmarked for the State Council.

The date on which the courts of first instance shall commence work, their number, their seats, and the number of judges in each chamber shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Justice after the approval of the Bureau of the State Council.

First:- The jurisdiction of the Regional Administrative Court shall be determined in accordance with the following rules:

1 - The place of residence of the petitioner in disputes relating to individual acts pertaining to security.

2 - The location of built and unbuilt properties in disputes relating generally to acts pertaining to those properties.

3 - The place of performance of the contract, and in the event that performance extends beyond the scope of jurisdiction of the Regional Administrative Court, the place where the contract was signed.

4 - The place of residence of the petitioner if the damage results from an administrative act.

5 - The place of the event giving rise to the damage if the damage results from public works or from an administrative action.

6 - The place of appointment in civil servants' cases the hearing of which falls outside the jurisdiction of the State Council in the first instance.

7 - The location of the administrative councils in disputes relating to elections.

8 - The location of the administrative councils or public and private institutions in disputes relating to their organisation and the functioning of their work, in particular regarding supervision and tutelage decisions taken in their regard.

9 - Where it is not possible to apply the rules mentioned above, the location of the seat of the authority that took the impugned administrative act or the location of the seat of the authority to which such act was delegated, or the place where the contract was signed.

- The court having jurisdiction to hear the principal claim shall also have jurisdiction to hear every ancillary, incidental, counter or connected claim and every defence.

- The court having jurisdiction to hear requests for the interpretation and assessment of the validity of administrative acts shall be the court having jurisdiction to hear the impugned act.

Second:

1 - The Minister of Justice may authorise the chambers of the Administrative Courts to hold their sittings outside their seat in places determined by a decision taken by him after the approval of the Bureau of the State Council.

2 - The distribution of work among the chambers in a single seat shall be by a decision of the President of the State Council after taking the opinion of the Bureau of the Council.

3 - The President of the Court shall preside over the judicial circuit, and if the registry is shared among several chambers, the President of the chamber of the highest grade shall be deemed President of the judicial circuit; in the event of equality of grade, the longest-serving President in the judiciary; in the event of equality of seniority, the oldest in age; and in the event of equality of age, the President of the circuit shall be appointed by a decision of the President of the State Council.

4 - The President of the judicial circuit is responsible for the proper functioning of the work in his circuit, and he is the administrative superior of the registry staff working therein, and he has toward them (literally: his disregarding them) the powers conferred upon a director by the regulations governing administrative civil servants.

5 - The Administrative Courts shall be composed of judges graduated from the Institute of Judicial Studies - Public Law Section - and from among the judges appointed in accordance with the provisions of Article Eight of this Law, and judges of the State Council may be appointed to these courts by a decision of the President of the Council.

- If one of the judges attached to the Administrative Court is unable to perform his duties for any reason, the President of the judicial circuit may assign one of the judges attached to him to carry out the duties of the said judge. (The text of the last paragraph of Paragraph 5 was annulled pursuant to the Decision of the Constitutional Council dated 27/6/2000)

Third: The State Council is divided into seven units

1- The Cases Assembly.

2 - Six chambers: one of which is administrative and the remaining five judicial.

7 - The word Lebanon and the word indicating the intended use of the vehicle or cycle shall be written in the font Din Schrift }. n Schrift}.

Every owner of a private passenger car registration plate shall be entitled to retain the registration number assigned to his car prior to the date of issuance of this Decision, provided that he submits a letter to the Cars and Vehicles Registration Department accompanied by the supporting documents notifying it therein of his wish to retain this number.

The owner of the car shall be deemed to have waived his right to retain the registration number if he does not notify the Administration of this wish of his within a period of three months at most from the date this Decision enters into force.

The descriptions of the vehicle registration plates that are the subject of the second Article shall be as follows:

Paragraph (1):

1 - The plate shall be divided vertically into three sections such that the middle section equals the sum of the two side sections.

2 - The Lebanese flag shall be drawn in the central section.

3 - The right section of the plate shall contain the number of the car in Arabic and the left section in Latin, and the numbers in both languages shall be of the same size.

4 - The background of the plate is black and the writing is in white colour or Métal colour.

Paragraph (2):

1 - The plate shall be divided by a horizontal line such that the lower section is twice the upper section.

2 - The upper section shall be divided vertically into three equal sections, and in the middle section shall be written (Governmental), and in the right section (Lebanon) in Arabic, and in the left section in Latin.

3 - The lower section shall be divided vertically into two equal sections, and the number of the car shall be written in Arabic in the right section and in Latin in the left section and in the same size.

4 - The background of the plate shall be black and the writing in white colour or Métal colour

Paragraph (3):

The specifications of the vehicle registration plate that is the subject of Paragraph (3) shall remain in accordance with the model currently adopted. Coordination shall take place with the Presidency of the Chamber of Deputies regarding any measure relating to these plates.

With the exception of the special specifications and colours specified in the body of this Decision, the background colour of the plates of cars, machinery, vehicles, and equipment bearing a private plate shall be (black and the lettering shall be in white or Métal).

- Public cars and machinery: the colour of the registration plate they bear shall be red and the lettering in white.

- Private passenger cars prepared for rental to tourists or third parties: the background of the plate shall be orange and the lettering in black.

- Transcontinental registered buses: the background of the plate shall be green and the lettering in black.

- The background colour of the plate shall be pistachio green and the lettering in black in respect of external transport cars.

- The size of the two plates of motorcycles shall be half the size of the remaining plates, and it may be reduced in accordance with the placement of the plate on the motorcycle, while permitting the front plate to be curved for mounting it on the front fender of the motorcycle.

The background of the plate shall be of the white colour and the lettering in black.

Certain cars of the Army, the Internal Security Forces, General Security, and State Security may be registered in the category of private passenger cars specified in this Decision, and this shall be effected by a decision of the Minister of Interior.

The numbers and specifications of military motor vehicles of all kinds belonging to the Army, the Internal Security Forces, the General Inspectorate of the Internal Security Forces, General Security, State Security, the Parliament Police, Civil Defence, and the Airport Security Apparatus shall remain as they currently are, such that the plates borne by the vehicles belonging to these administrations shall bear the name of the administration on the plate, and shall be distinguished in their current state.

The plate must bear a lead seal duly stamped by the registration centre, and in the event that a special sticker is adopted to prove payment of the annual mechanical fee on the plate, this sticker must always be affixed to the plate in the place designated for it.

Every car circulating with a plate that contravenes the provisions of this Decision, or bearing writings, insignia, or distinctive marks of whatever kind, or placing various marks or insignia next to the plates in contravention of the provisions of Article 99 of the Traffic Law, shall be subject to the penalties provided for in the said Law.

All the conditions set forth in Article 107 of Law No. 76/67 dated 26/12/1967 (the Traffic Law) shall apply to those who practise the profession of manufacturing car registration plates, under penalty of legal measures being taken against them.

The replacement of the old plate with a new plate in accordance with the provisions of this Decision shall not entail any fee on the owner of each plate for motor cars and motor vehicles registered before the date of issuance of this Decision.

The new numbering and coding shall begin immediately upon the entry into force of this Decision, and the plates of motor cars and motor vehicles that are the subject of Articles Two, Three and Four and Item First of Article Five shall be gradually replaced starting from 01/05/1998 and until 31/12/1998 so that their numbering and specifications conform to this Decision.

As for the registration plates of private motor cars that are the subject of Item Second of Article Five, the date of their replacement shall be determined pursuant to subsequent decisions issued by the Minister of the Interior, in which the dates for commencing the application of the numbering and coding in the branches, and consequently the replacement of the plates, shall be determined in the light of the progress of computerisation works in the Motor Car and Vehicle Registration Department.
The measures relating to the manner of implementation of this Decision shall be determined, where necessary, by instructions from the Minister of the Interior.
All decisions and texts contrary to this Decision or inconsistent with its content are hereby repealed.
Decision No. 356 dated 20/8/1997 is hereby withdrawn and replaced by this Decision.
