The urgent draft law referred to the Chamber of Deputies pursuant to Decree No. 759 dated 11/3/1971 containing the Regulations of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants and Determining its Numerical Cadres, the text of which follows, is hereby put into effect:
This Decree shall be published and notified where needed, and shall take effect as from the date of its publication in the Official Gazette.
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants shall assume the affairs of Lebanon's foreign policy in terms of preparation, coordination and execution, and shall look after the affairs of emigrants.

The cadre of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants shall consist of a foreign service (diplomatic and consular) and an administrative service, in accordance with Tables No. (1) and No.

(2) attached to this Law.

The Central Administration shall consist of the following units:

1 - The Directorate of Political and Consular Affairs.

2 - The Directorate of Economic Affairs.

3 - The Directorate of Emigrants.

4 - The Directorate of Protocol.

5 - The Directorate of International Organizations, Conferences and Cultural Relations.

6 - The Directorate of Administrative and Financial Affairs.

7 - The Center for Legal Consultations, Research and Documentation.

8 - The Inspection.

9 - The Ciphers.

10- The Archives Secretariat.

11 - The Bureau.

12 - The Press Department.

These units shall be organized and employees shall be distributed among them in accordance with Table No. 3 attached to this Law.

The powers of the Director General of the Ministry shall be exercised, and the Central Administration and missions shall be supervised, by a Secretary General who shall be appointed from among the employees of the foreign service of the First Category or Ambassadors outside the cadre.

The Director of Political Affairs shall assume the duties of the Secretary General in the event of his absence in the capacity of Acting Secretary General.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants shall have a Legal Advisor who may be chosen from among the employees of either the First or Second Category of the foreign service, or contracted with if he is not an employee, and this Advisor shall be the Head of the Center for Consultations, Research and Documentation.

The person contracted with shall be required to hold a State Doctorate in Law, to have at least five years of experience in public law, and to devote himself full-time to his post.

The Secretary General, the employees of the First Category present in the Central Administration, the Directors, and the Legal Advisor shall be allocated allowances that shall be determined by decree upon the proposal of the Board of the Civil Service Council.

An Administrative Committee shall be formed in the Central Administration, chaired by the Secretary General and with the membership of each of the Director of Political and Consular Affairs and the Director of Administrative and Financial Affairs, and it shall exercise the powers provided for in this law and the powers that the Minister may entrust to it by a decision issued by him.

Permanent positions in the Fourth and Fifth Categories in the Administrative Corps shall be distributed, and this distribution shall be amended by a decision of the Minister. That is following an investigation conducted by the Central Inspection - Directorate of Research and Guidance and the approval of the Civil Service Board, or upon a proposal of the Central Inspection - Directorate of Research and Guidance - and the approval of the Civil Service.

There shall be established in the Central Administration and attached to the General Secretariat a Centre for Legal Consultations, Research and Documentation and an Archives Secretariat, and the regulations of each of them, its cadre, its powers, and the conditions for joining it and working therein shall be determined by a decree issued in the Council of Ministers within a period of one year from the date of entry into force of this Law, provided that the following provisions are observed therein:

1 - That the purpose of establishing the Centre is to provide the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants with the legal consultations, studies, documents and information it needs concerning the political, economic and cultural relations of Lebanon with foreign States and with international regional organisations.

2 - The library of the Ministry shall be attached to the Centre.

3 - The employees of each of the Centre and the Archives Secretariat shall be taken from among the employees within the cadre or the contracted personnel in accordance with the conditions determined by the organisational decree referred to at the beginning of this Article.

4 - It shall be required in selecting the researchers, documentalists and librarians that they be specialists and have practical experience in the tasks entrusted to them. Contracting shall be effected between them and the Minister of Foreign Affairs upon the recommendation of the Head of the Centre, the proposal of the Administrative Committee and the approval of the Civil Service Board.

5 - Contracting shall be effected between each of the Head of the Centre or the Keeper of the Archives and the other administrative employees within the appropriations allocated for that purpose, and the contracting shall become effective after the approval of the Secretary-General of the Ministry and the Civil Service Board.

6 - The Head of the Centre, if he is within the cadre, the employees of the Centre who are within the cadre, and the employees of the Archives Secretariat who are within the cadre shall receive a specialisation allowance to be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers after consulting the opinion of the Civil Service Board.

7 - Two lump-sum appropriations shall be provided for in the budget of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants to cover the salaries of the employees of each of the Centre and the Archives Secretariat, their allowances and all other administrative expenses, and each of the Head of the Centre and the Keeper of the Archives, in agreement with the Administrative Committee, shall draw up a draft detailing the execution of this appropriation, which shall become effective upon the ratification of each of the two drafts by the Minister of Foreign Affairs.

1 - Diplomatic and consular missions and honorary consulates shall be established by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers.

2 - Upon the establishment of a new diplomatic or consular mission, two new posts of the Third Category shall be added ipso jure in the decree of establishment to the cadre of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants in the diplomatic and consular corps.

Wired and wireless communications employees shall be appointed by an examination conducted by the Civil Service Board in participation with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants.

Candidates shall be required to be holders of the Complementary Certificate or its official equivalent.

A diplomatic or consular employee shall not be attached to a post abroad until after he has spent at least two years in the central administration after his appointment and has been trained in the work across its various departments.

1 - One of the counsellors from the three highest grades may be appointed, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, as head of a diplomatic mission with the title of Minister Plenipotentiary or Ambassador without modification in salary, provided that he retains this title only for the duration of his performance of the duties of the post to which he is appointed.

Likewise, in exceptional cases where the work of the mission requires that and the assessment of which rests with the Council of Ministers, the title of Minister Plenipotentiary may be granted to a counsellor from the three highest grades without modification in salary, provided that he retains this title only for the duration of his work in the mission.

2 - Save for the cases provided for in the first paragraph of this Article, no employee may be granted a title that is higher than or differs from his actual rank in the corps.

Foreign Service officers shall be attached to missions abroad according to the following ratios:

1 - From two officers to five officers at most, including the Head of Mission, in each of the diplomatic missions, according to its importance and the volume of its work, including the permanent missions to the United Nations in New York and Geneva and to UNESCO in Paris.

2 - Of two officers at most, including the Head of Mission, in each of the consular missions.

Category Three officers in the Diplomatic and Consular Corps shall be appointed in accordance with the following conditions:

1 - (This paragraph was repealed pursuant to the Law promulgated by Decree No. 2220 dated 18/8/1979 and replaced by the following text):

These officers shall be drawn from among the graduates of the Public Administration Department of the Higher Division at the National Institute for Administration and Development who hold at least a degree in law or an equivalent university degree. It is required that the age of the candidate among them does not exceed thirty-five years of age and that he successfully passes a special examination organised by the Civil Service Board in conjunction with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants, the conditions of which require, at a minimum, knowledge of public international law and at least one foreign language, in which the personal conduct of the candidate shall be taken into consideration.

2 - If the number of successful candidates in the examination referred to in the preceding paragraph is not sufficient to fill the vacant positions in the establishment of the Ministry, a special competitive examination shall be organised to fill these positions in accordance with regulations laid down by the Civil Service Board in conjunction with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants.

3 - An officer in the Foreign Service shall remain an attaché or vice-consul for a period of at least two years. He may thereafter be appointed as a secretary or consul upon the proposal of the Administrative Committee and the approval of the Civil Service Board.

(Paragraph added pursuant to the Law promulgated by Decree No. 2220 dated 18/8/1979):

Provided that the age of the applicant for the competitive examination does not exceed thirty-five years, whether he is an civil servant or a non-civil servant, and that he holds at least a degree in law or a university degree equivalent thereto.

4 - A female candidate is required to be unmarried.

Positions of Categories One and Two in the Foreign Service shall be filled by way of promotion within the same service.

As for appointment to positions of Category Two of the Administrative Corps, it shall be subject to the conditions provided for in the first paragraph of Article 11 of Legislative Decree No. 112 issued on 12/6/1959.

1 - The Government may exceptionally appoint, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, ambassadors from outside the cadre within the appropriations entered for this purpose in the budget, provided that their total number does not exceed fifteen ambassadors and that the age of any one of them is not less than forty years, provided that he holds a bachelor's degree in law or an officially recognised university degree.

2 - The ambassador appointed from outside the cadre shall receive a salary determined in the decree of his appointment, which shall be subject to increase by way of advancement in grade in accordance with the salary scale applicable to ambassadors within the cadre and the provisions governing their advancement in grade.

3 - The salary scale of the first category in the general administrative cadre, together with his right to advancement in grade, shall apply to an ambassador appointed from outside the cadre who originally belongs to the permanent cadres in public administrations. If, however, he belongs to the corps of Directors-General in public institutions, he shall be classified in the step closest to his salary in the public institution to which he belongs, provided that the due date for advancement in grade is postponed or brought forward in proportion to the increase or decrease affecting the salary.

4 - The Government may at any time assign to ambassadors appointed pursuant to this Article, who in principle serve abroad, any post in the Central Administration on an equal footing with diplomatic civil servants within the cadre.

5 - Ambassadors from outside the cadre shall be deemed to have resigned by operation of law upon the expiry of the term of office of the Head of State who appointed them. They must make the necessary arrangements to leave their post after the lapse of a period of two months from the commencement of the term of office of the new President. If they are reappointed, they must be transferred to the Central Administration after spending ten years abroad.

6 - The services of ambassadors appointed from outside the cadre shall terminate by operation of law upon their completion of the statutory age prescribed in the Civil Servants Law.

Lebanese and non-Lebanese honorary consuls may be appointed by decree in certain foreign countries, provided that the following rules are observed in such appointment:

1 - That the appointment be based on a reasoned proposal issued by the head of the Lebanese mission officially accredited in the country in which the appointment takes place.

2 - In cities not inhabited by large Lebanese communities, priority in appointment shall be given to a candidate who is a native of the country.

3 - The mission of an honorary consul may be terminated at any time without any condition and without his being entitled to any compensation.

4 - Honorary consuls shall not be appointed in cities where career diplomatic or consular missions are established.

1 - It shall not be permissible to create honorary diplomatic posts or posts for honorary technical attachés, nor to grant honorary diplomatic titles.

2 - However, the Government may, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, entrust an exceptional diplomatic mission to a Lebanese personality from outside the cadre, who shall temporarily be granted the title of Ambassador or Minister Plenipotentiary until the termination of the mission entrusted to him, provided that its duration shall be three months at most, renewable once for the same mission.

(Paragraphs 3 and 4 added to this Article pursuant to Law No. 13/80 dated 17/5/1980 - Official Gazette No. 22):

3 - a- It shall not be permissible to accept the establishment of honorary consulates in Beirut or in other Lebanese cities for foreign States that have resident diplomatic or consular missions in Lebanon.

Nor shall it be permissible to approve the appointment of more than one honorary consul for each State in each of the Lebanese cities.

4 - It shall not be permissible to accept the appointment of Lebanese citizens to career diplomatic or consular posts in foreign missions accredited in Lebanon.

1 - Military, economic, or cultural attachés, or specialised employees holding university degrees from one of the cadres of the State, may be seconded in the capacity of technical attachés to diplomatic missions.

2 - The territorial competence of the attaché may cover several missions.

3 - Secondment shall take place for a period of one year, renewable by a decree adopted upon the proposal of the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants and the approval of the Minister to whose Ministry the employee belongs.

4 - The seconded employee shall be subject to the authority of the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants in all cases and shall receive his instructions from him through the Head of the Mission. However, he shall remain in his original cadre and corps and shall receive his salaries and allowances from the administration to which he belongs.

5 - The provisions of Articles 23-24-25-26-35-42-43 shall apply to the seconded employee.

6 - The military attaché may correspond directly with the Army Command, provided that he submits a copy of such correspondence to the Head of the Mission.

Economic or cultural attachés may be contracted from outside the cadre following the approval of the Civil Service Board, under conditions laid down by a decree issued by the Council of Ministers after consulting the opinion of the Civil Service Board.

1 - A diplomatic or consular official may at any time be transferred to the Central Administration or to another post abroad. Provided that the maximum legal period for staying abroad is ten years for officials of the First Category and seven years for officials of the Second and Third Categories. Provided that the Government may keep officials of the First Category abroad for an additional period not exceeding five years, by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers.

2 - A diplomatic or consular official must spend a period of at least two years in the Central Administration, and if the interest calls for shortening this period, he may be appointed abroad before its expiry, upon a reasoned proposal submitted by the Administrative Committee and approved by the Civil Service Board.

3 - If a diplomatic or consular official is transferred to the Central Administration before the expiry of the maximum period for his presence abroad, the period which he must spend in the Central Administration may be shortened in a proportional manner, upon a reasoned proposal submitted by the Administrative Committee and approved by the Civil Service Board.

4 - The period stipulated in the preceding paragraphs shall be calculated from the date the official assumes his post.

5 - Officials of the First Category shall be transferred from one post to another post within the Central Administration by decree, officials of the Second Category by a decision of the Minister, and officials of the Third Category by a decision of the Secretary General, after the approval of the Civil Service Board.

A diplomatic or consular official shall be granted an ordinary transfer allowance upon his appointment to the Service, upon his transfer from the Central Administration to abroad and vice versa, upon his transfer from one post to another post abroad, and upon the termination of his services for non-disciplinary reasons if he is abroad at that time.
The ordinary transfer allowance shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Board of the Civil Service Board.

Officials of the Foreign Service who are assigned to emergency missions by written instructions from the Minister shall be granted an incidental transfer allowance determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Board of the Civil Service Board.

a - The expatriation allowance for officials of the Foreign Service is determined adopted in the Council of Ministers after consulting the opinion of the Administrative Committee and upon the proposal of the Board of the Civil Service Council, on the basis of the cost of living and social obligations. This allowance shall be increased by twenty-five per cent for officials working in the countries mentioned in paragraph (1) of Article 34 of this Law.

b - The official's entitlement to the country of expatriation commences as of the date of travel, and is discontinued upon his transfer to the Central Administration as of the date of his arrival in Lebanon.

c - The expatriation allowance shall be reduced by one quarter during sick leave after the lapse of three months.

d - An official recalled to the Central Administration on an official mission may receive the expatriation allowance in full for a period of one month, as of the date of his departure from his duty station, and in this case no transfer indemnity shall be due to him other than travel expenses. If the period exceeds one month, he may be granted this indemnity by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.

e - The expatriation allowance shall be discontinued for an official recalled to the Central Administration in preparation for his transfer to another post as of the date of his arrival in Lebanon.
The amount of representation expenses for each diplomatic and consular mission shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Foreign Affairs.

1 - The Government shall provide housing for the heads of diplomatic and consular missions in the mission residence, and the housing and the offices may be in one building or separate.

2 - The heads of diplomatic and consular missions shall bear a portion of the expenses of lighting, heating, cooling, water, and telephone, to be determined by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants and after the approval of the Civil Service Council.

3 - Other officials of the Foreign Service working abroad shall be granted a housing indemnity, the amount of which shall be determined by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants and the approval of the Civil Service Council. In cases where the Government provides housing for these officials, they shall bear out of their own pocket all domestic expenses of lighting, heating, cooling, and telephone.

4 - The housing indemnity shall fall due starting from the date of the official's arrival at his duty station. It shall be discontinued on the date of his final departure from this station.

5 - Each head of a diplomatic mission shall be entitled to employ a cook and an orderly, whose wages shall be paid from the appropriation for local employees.

A - The duration of the annual administration leave shall be fixed at two months for employees of missions in the Arabian Peninsula, Pakistan, India, Indonesia, and Africa excluding the northern and southern parts thereof, and at one month for employees of all other missions.

B - The duration of travel to Lebanon and return to the duty station by the direct route without stopover, whatever the means of travel may be, shall not be counted as part of the leave.

C - Leaves may be accumulated over a period not exceeding three years, provided that their total does not exceed four months.

D - If an employee exceeds the duration of the leave to which he is entitled, his salary and allowances shall be withheld for the duration of the excess.

The Government shall cover the round-trip travel expenses to Lebanon for employees on leave and for the members of their families.

A - Once every two years for those entitled to two months of leave annually

B - Once every three years for those entitled to one month of leave annually, and the family shall include the wife and those supported at the employee's expense among sons who have not exceeded eighteen years of age or who are pursuing their studies in educational institutes up to twenty-five years of age, and among daughters, ascendants, and unmarried minors who are unable to support themselves.

One of the ambassadors serving in the central administration shall undertake the periodic inspection of missions by assignment from the Minister in accordance with a programme drawn up by the Administrative Committee in agreement with the assigned ambassador and approved by the Minister.

The inspection of missions abroad shall remain subject to the authority of the Central Inspection in the financial field within the limits prescribed in the laws and regulations in force, and the Central Financial Inspection shall have the right, in the course of carrying out the inspection of Lebanese missions abroad, to investigate concomitant administrative matters or those liable to lead to financial repercussions of any kind whatsoever, whether in relation to public funds or other matters related to the employees of the mission or third parties.
The special regulations governing local employees attached to Lebanese missions abroad shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants.
Ambassadors and ministers plenipotentiary shall place their posts at the disposal of the new Head of State upon his assumption of the duties of the Presidency.

1 - No employee of the Foreign Service may marry without prior permission from the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants, granted after consulting the opinion of the Administrative Committee. Anyone who fails to comply with the provisions of this Article shall be deemed to have resigned.

Heads of diplomatic or consular missions and their employees shall not leave the country to which they are appointed, whether to spend a leave, for an official mission, or for a private need, except with written permission from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants; otherwise, their salaries and the allowances supplementary thereto shall be withheld from them as of the date of departure until the date of return, in addition to the disciplinary penalties provided for in the general law.

1 - The Treasury shall bear the travel expenses of Foreign Service employees and the members of their families referred to in Article 34.

The Ministry shall transfer to them an amount equivalent to the price of their travel tickets by direct route by aeroplane in accordance with the international tariff. The employee may choose the means of transport he wishes.

2 - Employees of the First and Second Categories shall travel in first class by aeroplane, and other employees in second class.
If one of the Foreign Service employees or one of the members of his family referred to in Article 34 dies abroad, the Government shall bear the expenses of repatriating the body to Lebanon.
Heads of missions shall be exempted from the financial guarantee in return for the stamp advances granted in their name.

An employee of the diplomatic and consular corps abroad shall not practise another work, including teaching. His wife shall not work in any institution except with prior authorisation from the Minister of Foreign Affairs upon the proposal of the Administrative Committee.

If an employee is transferred from the Foreign Service to any other corps, he may not be returned thereafter to the permanent cadre in the Foreign Service, and he can only be appointed from outside the cadre in accordance with the provisions of Article 17 of this Law.
The scale of categories, ranks and salaries for Foreign Service employees shall be determined in accordance with Schedule No. (4) annexed to this Law.
The details of the application of this Law shall be determined by subsequent decrees taken in the Council of Ministers after consulting the opinion of the Civil Service Board.

The Head of the Diplomatic Mission shall receive a lump-sum car allowance, the value of which shall be determined by a decree issued after consulting the Administrative Committee, and this allowance shall fall due starting from the date of arrival of the Head of Mission at his duty station.

When the substantive Head of Mission is absent for a period exceeding one month for any reason whatsoever, the Chargé d'Affaires ad interim shall receive half the value of this allowance throughout the period of absence, provided that the other half remains due to the Head of Mission on condition that no mission is assigned to him for which a car allowance falls due to him, in which case the other half shall revert to the Treasury.

The Honorary Consul shall receive, in return for the expenses he incurs to ensure the conduct of consular business, including representation expenses, an allowance determined as follows:

A - The entirety of the collected revenues if they do not exceed two thousand Lebanese pounds per year.

B - Ten percent of whatever exceeds the two thousand pounds, provided that the total allowance stipulated in this paragraph and the preceding paragraph does not exceed five thousand Lebanese pounds per year. The Honorary Consul shall not be entitled to receive any other amount in return for the expenses he incurs for the sake of the Consulate.

The Honorary Consul shall render a monthly account of the revenues of the Consulate and shall deposit in the name of the Consulate with one of the approved banks the amounts that remain after deducting the allowance referred to in this article. He shall transfer them on 31 December of every year in the name of the Treasurer of the Treasury through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants shall determine the rules for rendering accounts of the expenses and revenues of the missions by financial instructions countersigned by the Minister of Finance and the President of the Court of Audit.

The Financial Affairs Department shall cease sending any amount to every Head of Mission who delays for three months in submitting the accounts of revenues or the monthly accounts of expenses, and shall likewise cease disbursing his salaries and allowances. No amount shall be transferred to him except by order of the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants and the Minister of Finance.

Special allowances shall be determined by decree upon the proposal of the Board of the Civil Service Council for certain employees of the Central Administration upon whom and the nature of their work impose the performance of continuous effort outside official working hours, such as cipher and archives employees.

This Law shall enter into force as from the date of its publication in the Official Gazette.

All provisions contrary to its provisions or inconsistent therewith shall be repealed as from that date.

The Equipment and Supply Section shall undertake:

- Controlling the inward and outward movement of supplies, clothing, equipment, furniture, medicines, movable or immovable materials, and consumable and transformable materials in the warehouses, in use, and in all units of the Ministry of Public Health.

- Receiving draft annual budgets from all public health units.

- Studying and coordinating these budgets and determining their quantities in cooperation with the central directorates and departments to which these units report, on the basis of the quantities consumed in the past, and submitting them to the Accounting Section within the time limits legally prescribed therefor.

- Ensuring the preparation and delivery of the quantities of materials, supplies, equipment, furniture, medicines, etc... required by the units of the Ministry of Public Health, after auditing them and verifying the conformity of the quantities provided for these units in their annual budget.

- Studying the books of specifications for tenders drawn up by the central directorates and departments to secure the needs of the units reporting to them in the central and regional sections provided for in the budget, then coordinating and unifying them in cooperation with these departments, and putting them into final form within the dates legally prescribed therefor.

- Collecting the quantities of stationery, printed matter, and clothing necessary for all units of the Ministry on the basis of the requests received from these units, and submitting them to the Civil Service Board to secure them.

- Drawing up purchase authorisations for materials, medicines, supplies, etc... that are necessary and unavailable in the warehouse.

- Attending to the buildings belonging to the Ministry of Public Health, securing their needs, and maintaining them, and in general everything relating to materials accounting in accordance with the provisions of the laws and regulations in force.

There shall be attached to the Equipment and Supply Section:

- The Supplies and Equipment Warehouse.

- The Medicines Warehouse.

The Supplies and Equipment Warehouse shall undertake:

- Receiving all materials, equipment, apparatus, kitchen utensils, supplies, furniture, stationery, printed matter, clothing, and everything needed by the institutions of the Ministry, purchased whether by way of tenders or by purchase authorisations, or delivered by the Civil Service or any other institution.

- Keeping and maintaining the materials and keeping the accounts thereof.

- Delivering to the units of the Ministry and the quantities pertaining to them these materials, and delivering everything requested in accordance with the rules in force for the delivery of materials.
Regulatory Decree 2879 dated 16/12/1959 relating to the organisation of the Ministry of Public Health is amended to read as follows:

The Ministry of Public Health shall be concerned with preserving public health and raising its standard by ensuring the prevention of diseases and the treatment of needy patients, and supervising private health institutions in accordance with the provisions of the laws specific to them. It shall also undertake the preparation of proposals for legislation and amendment to the laws and regulations relating to all rights of public health.....

The Ministry of Public Health shall consist of:

- The Central Departments.

- The Regional Departments.

- The Department of Projects and Programmes.

The Central Departments shall consist of:

- The Bureau (Diwan).

- The Directorate of Health Prevention.

- The Directorate of Medical Care.

- The Directorate of the Central Public Health Laboratory.
The Bureau (Diwan) of the Directorate General of the Ministry of Public Health shall exercise the powers vested in the Bureau by the laws and regulations.

There shall be attached to the Bureau (Diwan):

- The Accounting Department.

- The Equipment and Supply Department.

- The Secretariat Section.

- The Personnel Section.

- The Section of Studies, Legal Affairs, and Health and International Relations.

The Accounting Department shall undertake:

- The preparation of the draft budget in its final form on the basis of the proposals of the competent units after their coordination by the Equipment and Supply Department.

- The drawing up of draft expenditure commitments on the basis of the requests of the heads of the competent units.

- The drawing up of the schedules of salaries, wages, allowances, bonuses and grants, and ensuring the payment of what falls due thereof on time.

- The carrying out of liquidation transactions.

- The keeping of the budget accounts.

And, in general, all transactions relating to the preparation of the budget, its execution and the keeping of its accounts, including the accounts of the Equipment and Supply Department, and all tasks provided for in the laws and regulations in force.

The Medicines Warehouse shall undertake:

- Receiving all medicines purchased by the Ministry of Public Health by tenders and receiving medicines purchased under purchase authorisations on behalf of the central departments in Beirut.

- Keeping and monitoring the expiry of the validity of medical preparations and keeping their accounts.

- Preparing and delivering what is requested of these medicines to the institutions of the Ministry of Public Health in accordance with the rules in force for the delivery of materials.

The Secretariat Section shall undertake:

- Ensuring the examination of incoming and outgoing general mail and submitting it to the Director General and the Head of the Diwan, each in so far as concerns him.

- Registering incoming and outgoing mail and distributing it.

- Ensuring the works of administrative drafting and translation, typing on typewriters, reproduction and archives.

- Receiving the representations of interested parties and their complaints and notifying the parties concerned of the results coupled with their representations, and in general all duties relating to the Secretariat and provided for in the laws and regulations in force.

The Personnel Section shall undertake:

- Preparing the transactions specific to everything relating to the personal affairs of employees.

- Organising the personal files of employees.

- Preparing advancement schedules on the basis of the proposals of the competent departments, and in general all transactions provided for in the laws and regulations in force regarding the affairs of employees.

The Division of Studies, Legal Affairs and International Relations shall be responsible for:

- Attending to lawsuits and giving opinions on settlement contracts.

- Drafting the texts of agreements in their legal form.

- Providing legal advice.

- Participating with the competent departments in the Ministry in drafting legislative proposals in their final form.

- Participating with the central departments in the Ministry in issuing the Health Directory every three years and preparing the supplements completed during this period.

- Studying the lists of duties and the stages of the duties of each employee drawn up by the central directorates with respect to their conformity with the legal texts, and putting them in their final form in agreement with these directorates before referring them to the Central Inspection Administration.

- Ensuring liaison between international and foreign health organisations and the competent departments in the Ministry.

- Preparing the means of participation in international, regional and social conferences and lectures held in Lebanon, and cooperating with the competent departments in the Ministry of Public Health as well as with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants.

- Managing the library, meeting the requests of the units of the Ministry for publications and scientific books, and carrying out technical translation work.

- Supplying the competent administrations with publicity materials received from international health organisations.

- Ensuring the preparation of draft reports, statements, announcements and communiqués.

And, in general, all duties relating to legal affairs and studies and to international health affairs provided for in the laws and regulations.

The Directorate of Preventive Health shall be in charge of:

- Preparing draft amendments to the laws and regulations relating to preventive health affairs imposed by social and scientific developments, and preparing the draft laws and regulations relating thereto.

- Preparing the draft decrees provided for by the preventive laws.

- Preparing the control programmes established by the central departments subordinate to it in their final form.

- Extracting the tasks from the texts and establishing their stages and the procedures to be followed therein jointly with the central units subordinate to it in cooperation with the various central services in the Ministry, particularly the Section of Studies and Legal Affairs.

- Distributing these tasks among the employees to whom they pertain in accordance with the provisions of item 2 of Article 4 of Legislative Decree No. 111 dated 12/6/1959.

- Coordinating, supervising, and inspecting the work of the central units subordinate to it, and supervising and inspecting the executive work in the regional units.

- Receiving the budgets of the units subordinate to it, unifying them with its own budget, coordinating them, and submitting them to the Accounting Department through the Equipment and Supply Department within the time limit specified therefor.

- Receiving statistical reports on the extent of activity of the units subordinate to it and drawing up an annual statistical report on the activity of all these units.

- Undertaking the preparation, training, and raising of the level of preventive knowledge of physicians, engineers, instructors, inspectors, health officers, and all workers in the field of preventive health, by organizing periodic brief theoretical and practical seminars in the field of preventive services.

The Directorate of Preventive Health shall be composed of:

- The Preventive Medicine Service.

- The Social Health Service.

- The Occupational Diseases and Labour Medicine Service.

- The Sanitary Engineering Service.

- The Department of Vital and Health Statistics.

The Preventive Medicine Service shall be in charge of:

- Establishing programmes for the control of communicable diseases in cooperation with the competent departments.

- Conducting studies relating to the course and evolution of communicable diseases.

- Supervising the progress of work relating to the control and prevention of these diseases and to the investigation of cases, sources of infection, and preventive inquiries.

- Supervising and inspecting all units subordinate to it.

- Preparing draft agreements with private sanatoriums and supervising the treatment of patients treated at the expense of the Government in these sanatoriums jointly with the head office of the Tuberculosis Control Centre in Beirut.

The Presidency of the Tuberculosis Control Centre in Beirut shall undertake:

- Carrying out studies relating to the course and development of tuberculosis and proposing programmes aimed at the prevention thereof in participation with the Head of the Preventive Medicine Department.

- Undertaking the preparation, training and raising the level of knowledge of the staff of the tuberculosis centres in Beirut and the regions and the district physicians, etc., by organising periodic and brief theoretical seminars in the field of tuberculosis control.

- Technical supervision and control over the control programmes carried out by the regional centres.

- Studying the monthly reports drawn up by the regional control centres, collecting the statistics and information contained therein, laying down directives regarding them, and preparing proposals in the light thereof.

The Tuberculosis Control Centre in Beirut shall carry out the necessary investigations to detect persons infected with tuberculosis in the Governorates of Beirut and Mount, and perform diagnostic, preventive and curative services for them and for their contacts.

The Rabies Control Dispensary shall undertake:

Examining bitten persons and vaccinating them against rabies where necessary.

- Direct liaison with the competent administrations to apply the provisions of the laws and regulations relating to rabies control and the destruction of stray dogs and rabid animals.

- Proposing programmes aimed at controlling and eradicating rabies.

The Communicable Diseases Hospital shall undertake:

- Examining and treating persons infected with infectious diseases, with the exception of tuberculosis and leprosy.

The Venereal Diseases Branch for prostitutes and women of easy virtue shall undertake.

- Conducting the raids provided for by the laws in brothels.

- Treating women infected with venereal diseases.

The Leprosy Control Centre shall undertake:

- Providing services for the diagnosis of leprosy, treating lepers, and proposing programmes aimed at investigating lepers and preventing and controlling leprosy.

The Malaria Control Centre shall undertake:

- Ensuring all curative, medical preventive, and technical preventive works to ensure the continued consolidation of the eradication of the disease from the country in participation with the Directorate of Sanitary Engineering.

The following shall be attached to the Preventive Medicine Service:

- The Communicable Diseases Control Department.

- The Quarantine Department.

- The Tuberculosis Control Centre in Beirut, and this centre includes a mobile unit.

- The Rabies Control Dispensary.

- The Contagious Diseases Hospital.

- The Venereal Diseases Branch for Prostitutes and Women of Loose Morals.

- The Leprosy Control Centre.

- The Malaria Control Centre.

The Communicable Diseases Control Department shall undertake:

- Carrying out studies relating to the course of communicable diseases and their development.

- Supervising the progress of work relating to the control and prevention of these diseases, and carrying out epidemiological investigations locally when necessary to assist the District Physicians.

The Quarantine Department shall undertake:

- Protecting the country from the infiltration of epidemic diseases, preventing their transmission abroad, and taking measures for this purpose at the land, sea, and air borders in accordance with the International Health Regulations.

- Ensuring the vaccination of travellers at the international vaccination centres in the Ports of Beirut and Tripoli - and Beirut International Airport.

The Quarantine Department shall be composed of:

1 - At the central level:

The Quarantine Department.

2 - In all Lebanese regions:

a - Airports:

- The Quarantine Centre at Rafic Hariri International Airport - Beirut

- The Quarantine Centre at Rene Mouawad Airport (Qlaiaat) - Akkar.

b - Ports:

- The Quarantine Centre at Chekka Port - Batroun

- The Quarantine Centre at Selaata Port - Batroun

- The Quarantine Centre at Tripoli Port

- The Quarantine Centre at Beirut Port

- The Quarantine Centre at Jounieh Port - Keserwan

- The Quarantine Centre at Jiyeh Port - Chouf

- The Quarantine Centre at Saida Port - South

- The Quarantine Centre at Tyre Port - South

- The Quarantine Centre at Zahrani Port - South

- The Quarantine Centre at Naqoura Port - South.

c - Land crossings:

- The Quarantine Centre at Arida Crossing - Akkar

- The Quarantine Centre at Abboudieh Crossing - Akkar

- The Quarantine Centre at Buqayaa Crossing - Jisr Deir Amar - Akkar

- The Quarantine Centre at Qaa Crossing - Baalbek

- The Quarantine Centre at Masnaa Crossing - Zahle.

The quarantine centres shall undertake the collection of the quarantine fees due and their monthly payment to the Quarantine Treasurer, in addition to their technical and administrative powers.

The Social Health Directorate shall assume:

- Undertaking the study of public health problems related to issues of maternity, childhood, health guidance, and school health.

- Monitoring the work of the departments subordinate to it and laying down programmes aimed at raising the health level in the country.

- Technical supervision of the work tending towards the implementation of the aforementioned programmes, and cooperating with governmental and private institutions to achieve the objectives at which these programmes aim.

- Studying the reports received from the departments subordinate to it, collecting the statistics and information recorded therein, laying down directives regarding them, and preparing proposals in light thereof.

- Participating with the Directorate of Hospitals, Dispensaries, and Medical Professions in supervising maternity homes and children's hospitals in accordance with the provisions of the laws in force.

The Social Health Directorate shall be composed of:

- The Department of Maternal, Child, and School Health.

- The Department of Health Guidance.

The Department of Maternal, Child, and School Health shall assume:

- Studying health problems related to issues of maternity and childhood.

- Laying down programmes to raise the level of care for the mother in her home and in maternity homes, for the newborn and in his first year of age, for the premature infant, for children of pre-school age, and for disabled and deformed children.

- Cooperating with governmental and private institutions to achieve the objectives of care.

- Preparing draft agreements with private maternity homes and children's hospitals, and monitoring the treatment of mothers and children treated at the expense of the Government therein.

- Undertaking studies related to the health condition in public and private schools, and proposing programmes consistent with the legal texts to secure the raising of the health level therein.

- Undertaking the training and raising the level of knowledge of public health midwives, assistant social midwives, and midwives in the Ministry of Health and municipalities, by organising brief periodic theoretical and practical study seminars in the field of maternal and child health.

- There shall be attached to the Department of Maternal, Child, and School Health. The Maternal and Child Health Care Centre and the Milk Station in Beirut

The Maternal and Child Health Care Centre and the Milk Station in Beirut shall assume:

- All diagnostic, preventive, and therapeutic work related to maternal and child health, including:

- Distributing milk and food, and training mothers on how to prepare nursing meals in terms of sterilisation and preparation.

- Visiting nursing and pregnant women in their homes, and guiding mothers regarding the care of their children.

The Sanitary Engineering Service shall undertake:

- Conducting studies and proposing programmes consistent with the legal texts in force and aimed at ensuring the safety of the environment from factors that constitute a hazard to public health.

- Conducting studies and proposing programmes consistent with the legal texts and aimed at the extermination of harmful insects and disease-vector insects, in particular malaria-vector mosquitoes.

- Conducting studies and proposing programmes consistent with the legal texts to ensure wholesome foodstuffs in cooperation with the competent bodies in the Ministries of Agriculture and National Economy.

- Drafting decisions on the sanitary and preventive conditions that must be met in every type of classified establishment to ensure the prevention of the hazards provided for by law.

- Proposing the specifications and technical conditions that must be met in the construction of public and private sewers, projects for the construction of drinking water networks, and projects for the collection and disposal of waste.

- Drafting the classification of industrial establishments not listed in the classification schedule or the reclassification of establishments whose reclassification is required by necessity.

- Approving projects for the construction of slaughterhouses and the laying of sewer networks in the City of Beirut.

- Participating in the execution of the sanitary engineering works carried out by the Malaria Control Centre.

The Sanitary Engineering Service shall consist of:

- The Studies and Preparation Department.

- The Insect and Rodent Control Department.

There shall be attached to the Insect and Rodent Control Department:

- A statistician expert in insects, Head of Section.

The Department of Vital and Health Statistics shall undertake:

- Collecting information on vital events, including births, deaths and the causes thereof, and diseases, particularly communicable ones.

- Obtaining from the Directorate General of Statistics and Personal Status the documents relating to births and deaths.

- Collecting other health information relating to the operations of the Ministry of Public Health, its institutions and the municipalities, and to the operations of hospitals and private health institutions.

- Carrying out statistical studies and analyses and sample surveys to determine the extent of the gravity of health problems.

- Publishing vital and health statistics, research and statistical studies, and communicating them to the competent authorities, particularly the General Statistics Service in the Ministry of Planning.

- Coordinating, supervising and inspecting the operations of the central units attached to it, and supervising and inspecting the executive operations in the regional units.

- Receiving statistics from the various units attached to it and preparing an annual statistical report on the activity of all such units.

- Receiving the budgets of the units attached to it, consolidating them with its own budget, coordinating them, and submitting them to the Department of Accounting through the Department of Equipment and Supply designated for that purpose.

The Department of Health Guidance shall be in charge of:

- Proposing curricula for disseminating health guidance to the inhabitants in accordance with their ages and according to their environments.

- Supervising the implementation of these curricula and directing the employees entrusted with disseminating health guidance.

- Participating with the competent Service in the Ministry of National Education in general health education in the academic subjects and establishing the curricula therefor.

- The Health Guidance Detachment in the Governorate of Beirut shall be attached to the Department of Health Guidance and shall carry out the implementation and application of the curricula for disseminating health guidance to the inhabitants established by the Department in accordance with a monthly programme.

The Service of Occupational Diseases and Occupational Medicine shall be in charge of:

- Conducting studies relating to the course of occupational diseases, their developments, and the extent of their spread.

- Establishing curricula for the early detection of pathological conditions resulting from work.

- Proposing the health and preventive specifications and conditions that must be available in factories, occupancies, workshops, and all other classified establishments to limit the spread of occupational diseases.

- Proposing the health and preventive conditions that must be provided to workers to ensure their safety and their non-exposure to occupational diseases resulting from the nature of each industry.

- Preparing, training, and raising occupational physicians and the employees subordinate to them in Beirut and the regions.

- Studying the monthly reports prepared by occupational physicians, collecting the statistics and information contained therein, establishing directives in respect thereof, and preparing proposals in the light thereof.

The Directorate of Medical Care shall undertake:

- All affairs aimed at treating needy patients and at supervising therapeutic and pharmaceutical institutions, working to strengthen them, ensuring contact with institutes teaching the medical professions in order to raise their standard, ensuring contact with the syndicates of the medical professions, and participating with the Ministry of National Education in the verification of the certificates of candidates of the medical professions for the Colloquium examination.

- Preparing draft amendments to the laws and regulations relating to the affairs of the medical professions and care, and preparing draft laws relating thereto.

- Preparing the draft decrees provided for by the laws.

- Drawing up draft internal regulations for hospitals and institutions affiliated with the Care.

- Reviewing the distribution of beds in each hospital among the various branches in the light of the proposals of the Chief Physicians of the hospitals.

- Extracting tasks from the texts and laying down their stages and the procedures to be followed therein, in participation with the central units affiliated with it and in cooperation with the various central services affiliated with it and in cooperation with the various central services in the Ministry, particularly the Section of Studies and Contentious Affairs.

- Distributing these tasks among the employees to whom they pertain, in accordance with the provisions of Item 2 of Article 4 of Legislative Decree 111 dated 12/6/1959.

- Carrying out the preparation, training, and raising of the standard of registered female nurses, assistant female nurses, and female employees in therapeutic hospitals and dispensaries, by organizing brief periodic theoretical and practical study seminars in the field of nursing services, in cooperation with the physicians of the hospitals and dispensaries - and the matrons in the hospitals.

The Directorate of Medical Care shall consist of:

- The Service of Hospitals, Dispensaries, and Medical Professions.

- The Service of Pharmacy.

The Service of Dispensaries, Dispensaries, and Medical Professions shall undertake:

- Carrying out studies and investigations relating to private therapeutic facilities in the country.

- Studying and preparing licensing transactions for the practice of the professions of medicine, dentistry, midwifery, nursing, massage, and all other professions of a medical nature, with the exception of pharmacy, and registering specialists in the various types of medical branches.

- Studying and preparing licensing transactions for opening hospitals, dispensaries, and laboratories - medical, and all other private institutions of a medical nature, with the exception of pharmacies and drug depots.

The Service of Hospitals, Dispensaries, and Medical Professions shall consist of:

- The Department of Hospitals, Dispensaries, and Contracted Institutions.

- The Administrative Section for Hospitals, Dispensaries, and Contracted Institutions.

There shall be attached to the branches of Beirut Hospital:

- The Contagious Diseases Branch, 30 beds.

- The Venereal Diseases Branch for prostitutes and women of ill repute, 20 beds.

And of radiology, a pharmacy, a laboratory, and an administrative section.
The Radiology Branch at Beirut Hospital shall perform the radiographic imaging referred to it by the Central Dispensary.

The Pharmacy Service shall undertake:

- Technical supervision over the progress of work in the pharmacies of the Ministry.

- Studying and preparing licensing transactions for practising the profession of pharmacy and opening pharmacies and drug depots.

- Conducting the necessary studies to determine the selling prices of drugs and proposing these prices.

- Studying applications for licences to manufacture proprietary preparations and to open drug production factories, and preparing the transactions necessary for licensing.

- Studying applications for licences to import narcotics.

- Participating with the Ministry of National Education in verifying the diplomas of candidates for the profession of pharmacy for the colloquium examination.

- Monitoring and inspecting the employees of the departments subordinate to it.

The Pharmacy Service shall consist of:

- The Narcotics Department.

- The Drug Import and Export Department.

- The Inspection Department.

The Narcotics Department shall undertake:

- Monitoring the importation of narcotics and their distribution to licensed importers.

- Monitoring the production and preparation of narcotics.

- Distributing narcotics to licensed producing establishments and to pharmacies.

- Compiling statistics relating to narcotics.

- Ensuring international transactions relating to narcotics at the appointed times.

- Participating in the medical committee for granting sickness assistance to employees.

The Drug Import and Export Department shall undertake:

- Participating with the competent committee provided for in the Pharmacy Law to approve the introduction of medical preparations not previously used in the country.

- Approving transactions relating to the importation of drugs, milk, cosmetics, etc. provided for in the laws in force.

The Pharmaceutical Inspection Department shall undertake:

- Inspecting pharmacies, drug depots, drug production factories, pharmacies of private hospitals, etc... in the Governorate of Beirut with respect to the operation of these establishments, monitoring drug prices, monitoring the use of narcotics, and monitoring drugs in terms of their efficacy and safety, in accordance with the provisions of the laws in force.

- Combating the unlawful practice of the profession of pharmacy and preventing the trading in and sale of drugs by unlicensed persons.

The Department of Hospitals, Dispensaries, and Contracted Institutions shall undertake:

- Supervising the hospitals and dispensaries of the Ministry and the institutions contracted therewith, and monitoring the progress of work therein.

- Monitoring and inspecting clinics, sanatoriums, maternity homes, hospitals, dispensaries, medical laboratories, dental clinics, nurses, and midwives in the Governorate of Beirut, as well as all other private institutions of a medical nature, with the exception of pharmacy, in cooperation with the Municipal Health Service.

The Administrative Section for Hospitals and Dispensaries shall undertake:

- Supervising the movement of patients in the hospitals and dispensaries of the Ministry and the institutions contracted therewith, and collecting the statistics relating thereto.

- Receiving, coordinating, and unifying the annual budgets received from the hospitals and dispensaries of the Ministry.

- Monitoring the treatment by the institutions contracted with the Ministry of patients who are at the expense of the Government, and monitoring the implementation of the terms of contracting.

- Auditing the invoices received from the contracted institutions and matching them against the lists of patients sent by these institutions.

- Conducting administrative inspection in government hospitals, applying administrative regulations, training administrative employees, and establishing and unifying the administrative principles and regulations followed.

There shall be attached to the Service of Hospitals, Dispensaries, and Medical Professions:

- The Central Dispensary in Beirut.

- The Department of Employees' Medical Care.

- Beirut Hospital.

The Central Dispensary in Beirut shall consist of the following clinics:

- General surgery and urological surgery.

- Internal diseases.

- Diseases of the head, ear, nose, and throat.

- Eye diseases.

- Dermatological and venereal diseases.

- Pediatric diseases.

- Gynecology and obstetrics.

- Mental diseases.

- Dentistry branch.

- And of a pharmacy and a laboratory.

The Department of Employees' Medical Care shall undertake:

- Examining sick employees and granting them the necessary reports.

- Participating in the Medical Committee charged with examining sick employees residing in Beirut.

- Beirut Hospital shall consist of the following branches:

- Urological, orthopedic, and general surgeries 50 beds.

- Eye, nose, ear, and throat disease surgery 20 beds.

- Internal, dermatological, and heart diseases 90 beds.

- Obstetrics and gynecology 20 beds.

- Pediatrics 20 beds.

The Directorate of the Central Public Health Laboratory shall be responsible for:

- Preparing draft amendments to the laws and regulations relating to medical laboratory affairs, preparing draft laws and regulations relating thereto.

- Preparing the draft decrees provided for by the laws.

- Extracting tasks from the texts and establishing their stages and the procedures to be followed therein jointly with the central units attached to it and in cooperation with the Section of Studies and Cases.

- Distributing these tasks among the employees to whom they pertain in accordance with the provisions of Clause 2 of Article 4 of Legislative Decree No. 111 dated 12/6/1959.

- Undertaking the preparation, training, and raising of the level of laboratory preparators and employees of the central and branch laboratories attached to the Ministry of Public Health in cooperation with the heads of the branches of the Central Laboratory, by organising periodic brief theoretical and practical study seminars in the field of laboratory tests.

- Coordinating, supervising, and inspecting the work of the central units attached to it and supervising the inspection of laboratory work in the laboratory branches attached to the Ministry of Public Health.

- Receiving the budgets of the units attached to it, consolidating them with its budget, coordinating them, and submitting them to the Accounting Department through the Equipment and Supply Department within the time limit specified therefor.

The Directorate of Public Health Laboratories shall consist of:

- A central unit in Beirut called (the Central Public Health Laboratory).

- Six branches in the governorates called (the Regional Public Health Laboratories).

Their locations shall be determined and the appropriations for the costs of their establishment, amounting to /4500000,00/ L.L. (four million five hundred thousand pounds), shall be distributed over three years as shown in the schedule attached to this Decree, which shall be deemed an integral part thereof.

The Administrative Section shall be responsible for:

- Drafting, registration, and keeping of administrative papers.

- Accounting work of the Central Public Health Laboratory and the practice of technical materials in the laboratories and dispensaries attached to hospitals.

- Supervising the transport and receipt of samples and the sending of results.

- Ensuring discipline, general cleanliness, and guard and service work.

- Supervising the movement of the laboratory's vehicles.

- Supervising the laboratory's library and the workshop.

- The work pertaining to ensuring necessary utilities such as water, lighting, heating, and telephone, and ensuring their maintenance.

The Head of the Administrative Section shall be deemed a custodian of all materials and assets in the Central Public Health Laboratory and of the technical materials with which the Central Laboratory supplies the laboratories attached to hospitals and dispensaries.

The Bacteriology Branch shall be in charge of:

- The bacteriological, parasitological, mycological, and serological examinations required for diagnosing communicable diseases, monitoring their course, and preventing them, and it shall also be in charge of examinations of water and foodstuffs.

- This branch shall provide for the breeding of animals required for scientific tests.

- Determining the maximum limit of bacteria that drinking water and foodstuffs may contain while still being considered fit for drinking and consumption.

The Virology (Virus) Branch shall carry out:

- Examinations aimed at diagnosing diseases caused by viruses, monitoring their course, and assessing the degree of immunity against them.

The Chemistry Branch shall be in charge of:

- Biochemical analyses and chemical analyses of water, including drinking water and saline water, analyses of foodstuffs, alcoholic beverages, and all substances used in their preparation, colouring, and preservation, and it shall also carry out the chemical analyses required for the prevention of occupational diseases.

- Proposing the conditions to which foodstuffs must be subject along with quality standards, determining the substances that may be introduced into them, including colourings, preservatives, sweeteners, and others, along with determining their quantities, and participating with the competent authorities to put them into final form and prepare them in the form of draft laws or enforceable regulations.

- And this branch shall provide for the analyses and tests relating to the composition and safety of medicines and medical preparations.

There shall be established in the Ministry of Public Health a permanent advisory council called the Supreme Health Council.

- The Director General of Social Affairs as a member.

- The Dean of the French Faculty of Medicine as a member.

- A physician representing the Lebanese Red Cross as a member.

- Two representatives of the non-governmental sector operating in the health sector as a member.
The members of the Supreme Health Council shall be appointed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers for a renewable term of three years upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Health.

A member who absents himself from the meetings of the Health Council without a legitimate excuse three consecutive times shall be relieved by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, and the succeeding member shall complete the remaining period of the term of office of his predecessor.
