Customs is a public administration that undertakes:

1- The collection of customs duties and all other duties and taxes the collection of which is entrusted to it on goods imported into Lebanon, within the provisions set out by this Law or any other law or the agreements to which Lebanon is a party, and the same shall apply with respect to export duties that may be imposed on certain exports.

2- Preventing the entry of goods into Lebanon, or their exportation therefrom, in violation of the law.

1- Customs shall exercise its functions, in accordance with the provisions of this Law, over the customs territory, which comprises the Lebanese lands, airspace, territorial waters and the contiguous zone thereof.

2- Free zones and duty-free markets may be established within the customs territory, which shall be isolated from the customs regime and subject to their special provisions set forth in this Law.

3- Customs shall take special measures to supervise the transport and possession of certain types of goods in a zone adjacent to the land and sea borders constituting what is known as the customs zone.

The delimitation of this zone, the types of goods subject to supervision therein and the procedures of such supervision are specified in Title Seven of this Law.

1- All goods entering or leaving the customs territory shall be subject to the provisions of this Law.

2- The same customs provisions shall apply throughout the customs territory, unless otherwise provided.

3- Customs laws and regulations shall apply regardless of the capacity of persons, subject to the exceptions provided for by law.

1 - The principles of simplification, publicity, transparency, and mutual interest between Customs and the concerned parties shall be observed in all customs procedures.

2 - In application of the provisions of the first paragraph above, the Customs Administration shall undertake to adopt modern methods and advanced and developed systems with regard to the conduct of customs transactions, particularly in respect of:

a - Accepting cargo manifests, declarations of goods, and all other documents and information relating thereto, electronically.

b - Receiving and reviewing in advance the documents and information relating to the goods before the arrival of the imported goods or before the receipt of the exported goods.

c Adopting internationally applicable goods clearance procedures in accordance with the provisions of the Kyoto Convention.

d - Authorising the direct delivery of incoming goods or permitting the shipment of outgoing goods, prior to the payment of duties thereon or prior to the completion of their customs procedures, within certain conditions determined by the Customs Administration.

e - Inspecting goods rapidly, simply, and selectively, whenever Customs sees a result or benefit from resorting to inspection.

f- Adopting a post-release audit system for goods and their documents.

g- Generalising the use of electronic data interchange and developing customs operations and procedures in a paperless electronic environment.

h - Simplifying customs declaration forms and following the Single Administrative Document system whenever possible.

i - Accepting the drawing up of a single declaration for goods imported or exported, in instalments, within a specified period.

j - Permitting declaration in a single declaration upon importation and exportation, for goods pertaining to more than one manifest or to more than one entry in the customs warehouses records.

k - Adopting internationally applicable facilities in the application of customs regimes relating to duty suspension arrangements, exportation, re-exportation, and drawback.

l - Encouraging the establishment of free zones and customs warehouses in all their forms in order to stimulate commercial and industrial activity and facilitate re-exportation operations.

m - Simplifying and facilitating methods of payment of customs duties by means of credit accounts, bank guarantees, and other means of payment conducive to facilitating and stimulating commercial activity.

3 - In the application of the customs procedures provided for in this Chapter, the principle of the necessity of facilitating trade without prejudice to effective customs control shall be observed, and guidance shall be sought, to that end, from modern methods of risk assessment and management.

Customs shall observe publicity in the publication of customs laws, regulations and decisions, including decisions relating to tariff amendments and other customs measures and procedures, by publishing them in the Official Gazette, and where necessary in other national media, including electronic means, provided that such texts shall, in principle, take effect thirty days after the date of their publication, with the exception of those relating to tariff amendments, the provisions of which shall be applied within the time limits, effects and publication rules provided for in Article 16 of this Law.

1- Every interested party shall have the right to submit to Customs a written request inquiring about a customs procedure relating to the classification of particular goods or the rate of duties payable thereon, or the extent of their exemption from duties, or requesting information on the rules of valuation of goods or the rules of their origin or on other customs measures, procedures and regulations in force.

2 - The competent authorities at Customs shall undertake to reply to the subjects and information requested in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph, within a period not exceeding, in principle, 15 days from the date of registration of the request with those authorities, and to the extent that it does not entail the disclosure of information of a confidential nature or relating to a third party.

1 - Customs duties on goods imported into Lebanon, and where necessary on goods exported therefrom, shall be established and amended by decisions of the Higher Council of Customs pursuant to a delegation from the competent authority in accordance with the rules.

2 - Anti-dumping duties and countervailing duties on certain types of goods imported into Lebanon from particular countries shall be established and amended by decisions of the Higher Council of Customs, in implementation of the texts issued by the competent authorities pursuant to the legislation in force. Within the same rules, any necessary measures may be applied, including the imposition of quantitative restrictions in order to counter measures taken by certain countries that result in causing loss to national production.

3 - The types of goods, their tariff codes, the rates of duties to which they are subject, and the general rules governing their classification or tariff heading assignment shall be determined within a schedule entitled "Customs Tariff Schedule According to the Harmonized System".

1- The customs tariff on importation shall consist of: the ordinary tariff and the preferential tariff.

2- The ordinary tariff shall apply to goods that do not benefit from the preferential tariff.

3- The preferential tariff shall apply to all or part of the goods originating in one of the States, or a group of States, that are bound with Lebanon by special customs agreements pursuant to which they benefit from preferential status, within the limits of those agreements.

Tariff duties shall be either ad valorem (a percentage of the value of the goods) or specific (a lump-sum duty on each unit of the goods), and tariff duties may be both ad valorem and specific together for a single kind of goods.

1- Goods subject to prohibitive duties, wherever mentioned in this Law, shall be deemed to be any goods designated by the Higher Council of Customs, after consulting the opinion of the Director General of Customs, from among the goods subject upon importation, or upon exportation where applicable, to customs duties and other duties and taxes the total rates of which are not less than 35%, regardless of whether they are combined with specific duties.

2- Goods subject to revenue duties, wherever mentioned in this Law, shall be deemed to be any goods yielding revenue for the Treasury even if the total rates of their customs duties and other duties and taxes are less than 35% and even if combined with specific duties, as well as any goods subject to specific duties only, provided that all categories of these goods are determined by decisions issued by the Higher Council of Customs, after consulting the opinion of the Director General of Customs.

1- The customs duties specified in the customs tariff shall apply to all goods entering Lebanon, and where applicable, to all goods exiting it, regardless of the capacity of the persons to whom they are consigned, with the exception of the exemptions provided for in this Law or in any other law or in any agreement to which Lebanon is a party.

2- Goods imported or exported by the State or for its account shall be subject to customs duties in accordance with the procedures provided for in Article 172 of this Law, unless they are the subject of exemptions in accordance with the provisions of paragraph (1) of this Article.

1 - Subject to the exceptions set forth in Article 11, customs officers are prohibited, under penalty of being charged with bribery and prosecuted criminally before the courts, from:

a - Granting exemptions or reductions in customs duties other than those provided for in the laws and regulations, and every person who benefits from such granting shall be prosecuted as an accomplice.

b - Levying customs duties other than those specified in the tariffs, or duties exceeding them.

2- The provisions of this Article shall apply to the duties and taxes the collection of which is legally entrusted to the Customs Administration.

1- The customs duties in force shall apply to goods subject to ad valorem duties according to the value of these goods in the condition in which they are presented to the Customs for the payment of duties thereon.

2- The specific duties set forth in the customs tariff shall apply in their entirety, in principle, to the quantities presented to the Customs, regardless of the nature of the goods subject to these duties, their relative value, and their condition.

3- For the purpose of applying the provisions of this Article, the Customs may allow, for a single consignment, the separation of the part of the goods that has suffered any defect or damage due to factors that occurred prior to the registration of the detailed declaration.

Goods that have suffered any defect or damage shall be subject to customs duties according to the condition in which they are presented, or shall be re-exported, or shall be destroyed at the expense of their owner in accordance with the established procedures.
Duties levied upon entry may be refunded within the procedures and conditions set forth in Chapter Seven of Title Three of this Law.

1- When an amendment to the tariff occurs, the rate of duties due for collection shall be determined on the basis of the date of registration of the declarations of entry for consumption at the customs office, except for the exceptions provided for in this Law or in the text of the amendment itself.

2 - For the purpose of applying the provisions of this Article, the declarations of entry for consumption must have been registered during official working hours in the register of the customs office, and the goods must be present in the customs precinct so that they may be presented for inspection where necessary.

1- Decisions providing for the amendment of the tariff shall, in principle, apply after the expiry of three clear days from the date of their publication in accordance with the provisions of paragraph (2) below, unless otherwise provided for in the amendment decision.

If one or more days of the said period coincide with an official holiday, a number of days equal to the number of days of the official holiday shall be added to this period.

2 - The aforementioned tariff amendment decisions shall be published by affixing them in the place designated for official announcements at the headquarters of each of the Council of Ministers, the Higher Council of Customs and the Directorate General of Customs.

3- Contrary to the provisions of paragraph (1) above, goods of the kinds on which customs duties have been increased may benefit from the previous duties, if it is proven to the Customs that they were shipped directly to Lebanon before the date of publication of the decision providing for the increase of duties and provided that these duties are paid, secured or guaranteed within a period not exceeding three clear days from the date of their entry into the customs warehouses.

This period shall be determined in accordance with the conditions set forth in the second subparagraph of paragraph (1) above.

The Higher Council of Customs shall determine, after consulting the Director General of Customs, the rules for the application of this paragraph.

Goods that are present in the customs warehouses on the date of publication of the decision providing for the increase of the tariff may benefit from the previous duties that are more favourable to them, in the event that their duties are paid, secured or guaranteed, within the period provided for in Article 16 or in the increase decision.

Goods the duties of which are suspended under guaranteed undertaking declarations and which are presented to the Customs and declared for local consumption, shall be subject to the duties in force on the date of registration of the declarations relating to placing them into consumption.

The following operations, which are considered secondary, shall not be taken into account when determining origin, even if accompanied by a change in the customs tariff heading:

4 - He must produce a tax clearance certificate from the State financial departments.

B - If the packages entering the stores or warehouses are in an apparently unsound condition, the body operating such stores or warehouses must, jointly with the Customs and the carrier company, establish this condition in the receipt report and verify their weight, contents, and number, and the operating body must take the necessary measures for their safe preservation; and liability in this case shall fall upon the carrier unless there is a reservation on the manifest endorsed by the customs of the country of origin or unless the carrier produces documents proving that it received the packages and their contents in the condition in which they were observed upon their entry into the stores or warehouses, in which case prosecution shall be dispensed with.

1- Following the registration of the declarations, the Customs may, if it deems it useful, inspect the declared goods.

3 - The Service's right of inspection covers all the packages mentioned in a single declaration; however, such examination may be partial or total at the discretion of the Service or in accordance with the instructions laid down by the Administration, and the declarant shall have the right to reject the results of the partial inspection and request a full inspection.

4 - In laying down the instructions mentioned in the preceding paragraph, due regard shall be given to the necessity of facilitating trade without prejudice to effective control, guided therein by modern methods of risk assessment and management in order to determine the declarations that must be audited, the goods that must be inspected, and the necessary extent of auditing and inspection.

1 - The inspection shall be conducted at the customs offices and during the official working hours of such offices.

However, the Customs may authorise, at the request and expense of the declarant, that it be conducted outside such places and hours, within the available capabilities and in a manner that ensures the integrity of the customs procedures.

2 - The transport of the goods to the places of examination, their opening, their repacking, and all operations required for the inspection shall be borne by the declarant and under his responsibility.

3 - Goods that have been transported to the places of inspection may not be removed from such places without an authorisation from the Customs.

1 - The inspection may only be conducted in the presence of the person submitting the declaration or his legally authorised representative, and they alone shall be responsible for any shortage occurring during the inspection.

If the Customs are unable to verify, with certainty, the accuracy of the particulars of the declaration through the inspection of the goods or the examination of the submitted documents, the temporary suspension of the inspection may be decided and recorded on the submitted transaction until the Customs have gathered the elements necessary to carry out such verification, provided that all useful measures are taken to shorten the duration of the suspension in order to prevent harm to the interests of the concerned parties.

1 - If a discrepancy becomes apparent between the kind, quantity, origin or value of the declared goods and their kind, quantity, origin or value determined on the basis of the inspection, the duties shall be collected on the basis of the results of the inspection.

3 - The duties payable are those in force on the date of registration of the detailed declarations; however, in the event of a reduction in the rate of customs duties, the declarant may request the application of the new tariff that is more favourable than that in force on the date of registration of the declaration if the goods remain within the customs precinct and their duties have not been paid.

Once the duties have been collected as revenue, petitions relating to the elements of the declaration, to the inspection of the goods or to the assessment of duties thereon shall not be admitted unless the goods are still under the supervision of the Administration and are susceptible to examination or counter-examination.

In other cases, such applications must be rejected unless the declarants have special justifying grounds, which must then be submitted to the Higher Council of Customs to decide on the matter.

1 - Customs shall have the right to analyse samples of goods in order to verify their kind, specifications, or conformity with the laws and regulations in force.

Transit is a duty-suspensive customs regime whereby goods of foreign origin are permitted to be transported under customs supervision from a customs office, a customs warehouse, or a free zone to a customs office, a customs warehouse, or a free zone within Lebanon, or abroad through a customs office in Lebanon.

Goods passing in transit shall not, in principle, be subject to the prohibition restrictions applicable to the importation or exportation of goods; however, the following shall be ipso jure excluded from the transit regime:

a - Goods excluded from this regime pursuant to applicable laws and regulations or pursuant to decisions issued by the competent Lebanese authorities.

b - Goods the transit of which is prohibited in implementation of international agreements to which Lebanon is a party or has acceded.

Included within this latter category are:

- Goods bearing false indications of foreign provenance or origin, or unlawfully bearing a factory mark, trademark, or trade name that benefits from legal protection in Lebanon, in application of the provisions of Article 63 of this Law.

- Goods bearing, on themselves or on their wrappings, false marks or indications of a nature to create the impression that they were manufactured in Lebanon or that their origin is Lebanon, in application of the provisions of Article 62 of this Law.

1 - The customs warehousing regime is a duty-suspensive regime permitting the temporary entry of goods exempt from duties either for their storage or for their processing.

2 - The installations in which storage and processing take place shall be either within the customs compound or outside it, and in both cases shall remain subject to the supervision of the Customs Administration and be managed by public or private entities, with the approval of the Customs.

3 - Storage warehouses are:

a - Public warehouses, which are those in which goods are stored for the account of third parties.

b - Private warehouses, which are those in which the owner of the warehouse stores his goods which he is licensed to store.

Branching out from them are private warehouses dedicated to petroleum products, and others prepared for the storage of specific goods determined by the Supreme Council of Customs pursuant to decisions issued by it, and called specialised warehouses.

4 - Processing warehouses are industrial warehouses.

Unless there are special provisions to the contrary, the deposit of goods in customs warehouses suspends the application of duties, the provisions on prohibitions, and the other measures to which the goods are subject.

Prohibitions or restrictions on entry into storage or processing warehouses may be established where justified on grounds relating to public morality, public security, public policy, public health and the environment, and for the protection of national treasures of artistic, historic or archaeological value, or for the protection of intellectual property, as well as on grounds relating to the characteristics of the storage installations or to the nature and condition of the goods.

Goods placed in a public warehouse, a private warehouse or a specialised warehouse shall be deemed as though they were located outside the territory of Lebanon in respect of the collection of duties and taxes. Upon the exit of the goods from these warehouses, they may be declared for all the regimes that apply to directly imported goods.

In the event that the goods are released for consumption, the duties and taxes thereon shall be collected on the basis of the customs value determined in Article 35 et seq. of this Law, and in accordance with the rates in force on the date of registration of the declaration of release for consumption.

All openings of a public warehouse or a private warehouse shall be locked with locks that are not operable, except for the entry and exit doors, which shall be locked with two different keys, one of which shall remain in the possession of the Customs.

1- A public warehouse is open to every natural or legal person for depositing goods of all kinds subject to customs duties or other fees and taxes, including clearances of the temporary admission procedure and the industrial warehouse procedure, with the exception of the goods provided for in the following Article, as well as those which can only be stored in a private warehouse in view of their nature, their condition, and the characteristics of the facilities required therefor.

2- Goods exempt from customs duties and other fees and taxes shall not, in principle, be admitted into a public warehouse.

The Higher Council of Customs shall determine, after consulting the Director General of Customs, the cases in which the application of the provisions of this paragraph may be waived.

There shall not be admitted under the public warehouse procedure products bearing false marks or suspicious marks, gunpowder of all kinds, explosives and similar substances, inflammable substances, goods showing signs of spoilage or damage, goods whose presence in the warehouse exposes it to hazards or which may harm the quality of other products, goods whose preservation requires special installations not available in the public warehouse, and goods in bulk.

Goods located in a public warehouse may be assigned in favour of a third party, whereby the assignment shall be recorded in the transfers column under the names of the new owners and discharged from the names of the assigning depositors in the registers kept by the Customs and provided for in clause (3) of Article 200 above, and the new owners shall become liable towards the Customs.

Upon the expiry of the period prescribed for the public warehouse, these goods shall be re-exported or subjected to duties; in cases other than these two, the duties shall be assessed ipso jure on the basis of the tariff in force upon the expiry of the legal deposit time limit, and the depositor shall be given formal notice to pay them within one month; if he fails to do so, the goods shall be sold by public auction and their duties shall be assessed in accordance with the tariff on the date of sale and on the basis of the sale price, and the proceeds of the sale, after deducting the amount of the customs duties, storage expenses and others, shall be deposited in trust with the Customs treasury, to be delivered to the owner thereof if he claims them within the year commencing from the date of the day of the sale, and if he does not claim them within this period, the proceeds of the sale shall accrue, definitively, to the Public Treasury.

Goods the importation of which is restricted may not be sold for local consumption except in the event that the restriction thereon is lifted, failing which they shall be re-exported.

Violations of the industrial warehouse regime shall be repressed in accordance with the provisions set forth in Article 421 or in Article 425, as the case may be.

It shall also be permissible, after obtaining the approval of the operating body, to allocate areas of the free zone and subject them to continuous customs supervision pursuant to an executive mechanism prepared in coordination with the said body, in order for the foreign goods deposited in those areas to benefit, as the case may be, from the provisions of trade agreements to which Lebanon is a party or has acceded.

2 - The refund of duties on these goods shall be subject to the fulfilment of the following conditions:

a - That they remain in their original packagings, unless they are of the kinds that are imported without packagings, in which case it is required that they remain in their original condition upon importation.

b - That they are re-exported by their original importer himself.

c - That not more than three years have elapsed since the date of their importation.

3 - The value declared upon the re-exportation of these goods shall be subject to the valuation rules provided for in Chapter Five of Title One of this Law, provided that it does not exceed, as a maximum, the value accepted by Customs when declared in the import declaration.

4 - Duties on these goods shall be refunded on the basis of the tariff that was in force on the date of their importation, unless these goods have been subjected to a lower tariff on the date of re-exportation, in which case the duties shall then be refunded on the basis of this latter reduced tariff.

5 - Goods that were subjected to duties upon their importation and have become exempt therefrom on the date of re-exportation shall not benefit from the refund of duties.

1 - Goods in respect of which the drawback of duties is requested upon their re-exportation shall be subject to the submission of a re-exportation declaration on a special form determined by the Supreme Council of Customs, upon a proposal from the Director General of Customs, and shall be subject to the formalities of the detailed declaration and the rules of inspection provided for in this Law. Reference must be made in this declaration to the number and date of the customs declaration under which the goods were imported, and the receipt under which the duties were paid upon their importation must be produced.

2 - The drawback of duties shall not include the fiscal stamp duty.

3 - The Supreme Council of Customs shall determine, by decisions issued by it after seeking the opinion of the Director General of Customs, the customs offices at which re-exportation declarations for the refund of duties are submitted, and shall also determine all the conditions and guarantees relating to the application of this Chapter.

The duties shall be refunded within a period not exceeding thirty days from the date of claiming them.

Duties levied at importation may be refunded, subject to the conditions determined by the Supreme Council of Customs after seeking the opinion of the Director General of Customs, in respect of equipment, machinery and supplies purchased by the United Nations Organization and its affiliated bodies from the Lebanese local market, which are proven to have been regularly imported and to have had the customs duties paid thereon.
False declarations aimed at obtaining an undue drawback of duties shall be penalized in accordance with the provisions of Article 424 of this Law.

3 - The formalities and inspection of re-exported goods shall be, in principle, the same formalities provided for in Article 95 or the articles following it, and Article 138 and the articles following it.

4 - In the event of re-exportation in the same port in which the goods were unloaded and by maritime agencies, re-exportation applications shall suffice, notwithstanding the provisions of the preceding paragraph

(3), and the goods shall be exempted, in principle, from inspection procedures and from proof of arrival.

1- All articles imported in the name of representatives of foreign States, who are non-Lebanese and non-honorary, mentioned hereinafter and intended solely for their personal use or for the use of the members of their families, shall be exempted from customs duties and from the procedures of opening and inspection, within the conditions and rules provided for in Article 307 of this Law:

a - The Head of the diplomatic mission, counsellors, secretaries and attachés who belong to the diplomatic corps.

b - Technical attachés and assistant military attachés of the various branches of the armed forces, provided that they are nominated by the Head of the mission and accepted by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants in Lebanon.

c - Consuls-General, consuls and vice-consuls, provided that the number of those among them who benefit from the exemption does not exceed two in the capital and one in the other cities.

3 - The requirements imported and admitted under the exemption, in accordance with the provisions of the first paragraph of this Article, must be commensurate with the actual personal needs of the representatives of the foreign States concerned, and the Higher Council of Customs may, where necessary, fix the maximum limit for certain types of imports upon the proposal of a committee composed of representatives of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Customs Administration.

Personal effects, furniture and new household appliances arriving for diplomatic and consular officials who do not enjoy customs exemption shall be exempted from customs duties, in accordance with the following conditions:

1- That the importation takes place within three months as from the arrival of the applicant for the exemption in Lebanon, and this period may be extended in certain special circumstances the assessment of which is left to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, provided that the additional period does not exceed six months.

Third: Cultural, scientific or social cinematographic films, provided that they are not screened in public or private halls for commercial exploitation.

2 - For the purpose of applying the provisions of the first paragraph of this Article, the beneficiary shall undertake to keep the motor vehicle for which he requests exemption from duties in his use for a period of at least three years, and to notify the Customs in the event of the transfer of its ownership after this period, for any reason whatsoever, in order to collect the duties thereon on the basis of its value and the rates of duties applicable on the date of the transfer of ownership.

2 - That the person who benefits from the exemption and customs facilities is devoted exclusively to his function and does not engage in any other work and does not practice trade directly or indirectly.

1- Subject to the exception set forth in paragraph (2) below, assigned vehicles admitted under exemption in accordance with the provisions of Articles 296, 297 and 300 shall be subject to customs duties on the basis of the duty rates in force and in accordance with the value of the vehicles, upon their assignment.

a - Termination of the mission of the diplomatic or consular member benefiting from the exemption in the country.

The privileges and exemptions provided for in this Chapter shall only be granted if the legislation of the State to which the diplomatic or consular mission or its members belong grants the same or better privileges and exemptions to the Lebanese mission and its members; otherwise, the privileges and exemptions shall be granted within the limits of what is applied thereof in the State concerned.

The tariff of the storage fee shall be determined, in application of the provisions of paragraphs (1) and (2) of Article 321, as follows, in Lebanese pounds and starting from the sixth day:

First:

a - In the warehouses of Beirut International Airport: /10,000/ ten thousand pounds per one hundred kilograms for each week.

b - In the warehouses of all other customs offices: /2,000/ two thousand Lebanese pounds per one hundred kilograms for each week.

Second: The following rules shall be observed in determining and collecting the aforementioned fee:

1 - Every fraction of 100 kilograms shall pay the fee imposed on one hundred kilograms.

2 - Every week begun shall incur the full fee.

Third: If the duration of storage exceeds 30 days, and whatever the place of storage, there shall be collected in addition to the fees stated above per one hundred kilograms and for each day:

a - In the warehouses of Beirut International Airport:

1- From the sixty-first day up to the sixtieth day: /2,000/ two thousand Lebanese pounds.

2 - From the sixty-first day and above: /4,000/ four thousand Lebanese pounds.

b - In the warehouses of all other customs offices:

1 - From the thirty-first day up to the sixtieth day: 8 eight Lebanese pounds.

2 - From the sixty-first day up to the ninetieth day: 16 sixteen Lebanese pounds.

3 - From the ninety-first day to the one hundred and twentieth day: 24 twenty-four Lebanese pounds.

4 - From the one hundred and twenty-first day and above: 32 thirty-two Lebanese pounds As for the goods remaining in the warehouses and repositories directly managed by the Customs Administration following a judicial receivership or an attachment decided at the request of any person or administration other than the Customs, the amount of the storage fee in respect thereof shall be determined by the authority that decided the judicial receivership or the attachment, taking into consideration the tariff mentioned above.

3 - Packages unloaded in a state of apparent damage, verified in accordance with the rules, within five days starting from the date of their unloading.

5- Goods that were not withdrawn due to force majeure, the assessment of which remains the sole right of the Customs.

In this case, it shall be incumbent upon the owner of the packages to request the Customs officers to verify, on the very day on which the withdrawal request was submitted, that the packages were indeed of unknown location.

If only a part of these packages is missing, their owner must withdraw the existing packages after paying the imposed duties.

The time limit of five full days, provided for in Article 321, shall be raised to 30 full days with respect to goods in transit and to 15 full days with respect to goods intended for exportation.

3 - When they cannot, without the use of weapons, stop vehicles, vessels and other means of transport whose drivers do not comply with the warnings provided for in paragraph (4) of this Article and with the signals that must accompany them. 4 - When they warn persons attempting to flee or escape from them to stop, or repeat within their hearing the warning in a loud voice more than once "Customs, stop", and those persons refuse to comply with the warning, and it is then not possible to compel them to stop except by the use of weapons.

In this case, the decision (or flight) must have been preceded or accompanied by general or specific evidence establishing or rendering probable the near-certain participation of those persons in an offence or in an attempt by them to carry out a smuggling operation.

Every customs officer who leaves the service for any reason whatsoever (dismissal or placement on non-active status or resignation or retirement... etc.) must immediately return to his direct superior his service commission, registers, seals, weapons and the items with which he was equipped to perform his function.

If he fails to do so, the Head of the Region to which this officer reported shall have the right to issue a writ of constraint against him in accordance with the conditions provided for in paragraphs (3), (5) and (6) of Article 171, provided that this is done by means of a copy of the administrative order striking the officer off the establishment of the administration, and, in order to enable its service and execution, it must be endorsed by the Single Judge in the district to which the officer belonged when he was struck off the establishment.
Customs officers shall have the right, for the purpose of applying the provisions of this Law and verifying smuggling, to inspect goods, means of transport and persons.

1 - Drivers of means of transport must comply with the orders of customs officers.

2 - Those officers shall have the right to use all appropriate means to stop means of transport when their drivers do not comply with their orders, including the use of weapons, where necessary, provided that this is done within the conditions provided for in paragraph (3) of Article 351 above.

Where the necessities of control so require, an open account may be kept in the customs offices located within the customs zone, in which every producer or merchant shall compulsorily register the quantities of goods subject to the customs zone regulations as well as the live animals in his possession, whether resulting from production or breeding, or resulting from imports from abroad or arrivals from within the Lebanese territory, provided that the right of verification is reserved for the Customs Department.

The Customs Department may conduct sudden inventories on the premises of the persons mentioned in the preceding paragraph. The rules for the practical implementation of the open account regime shall be determined by the Director General of Customs.

Any irregular circulation or possession within the customs zone of goods subject to the customs zone regulations, any circulation that fails to comply with the provisions of the transport document, and any unjustified surplus or deficit in the open account, shall be deemed to constitute importation or exportation by way of smuggling and shall entail the application of the penalties provided for in Article 421 of this Law.

The application of the customs zone regime and the customs zone regulations shall not introduce any modification to the status of goods in transit, and in particular to the special provisions provided for in the agreements concluded with neighbouring countries concerning transit trade with these countries.

1 - Customs officers are under the protection of the law, and it is prohibited for any person whomsoever to insult, threaten, mistreat or oppose them during the performance of their duties, under penalty of exposing the perpetrators of such acts and their accomplices to the penalties provided for in Article 426 of this Law.

2 - The civil and military authorities shall extend assistance to customs officers upon their first request for the purpose of exercising their duties, and the Customs Administration shall likewise provide its assistance to public administrations and departments within the conditions set forth in the laws and regulations in force.
Customs officers of all ranks shall, upon entering into service, take the legal oath before the Single Judge in the district to which they have been appointed.

Customs officers shall receive, upon entering into service, a service commission issued by the Director General of Customs in accordance with a model determined by him.

They must carry this commission at all times during the performance of their duties and present it upon first request.

Directors and inspectors of Customs and officers of the Anti-Smuggling Department attached to the Customs Administration, as well as officers, sergeants and guards who are members of the public forces, are authorised to carry service weapons for the performance of the duties of their office.
Customs officers are entitled to inspect vessels under the conditions set forth in Articles 69 to 74 of this Law.

1 - The offences provided for in this Law and in the texts relating to Customs may be established and may lead to seizure:

a - Whatever the category of the goods, whether prohibited, monopolised, subject to customs duties or exempt:

- in Customs offices, posts and precincts, and in all places subject to customs control or in which Customs may conduct investigations and audits, such as customs warehouses of all kinds and premises in which goods are manufactured under the temporary admission regime.

- in the land and maritime customs zone.

- throughout Lebanese territory and outside the coastal waters, in the case of hot pursuit in sight.

b - With respect to goods prohibited from transit or internal movement or prohibited from being held or sold, or monopolised goods moving or held irregularly, or goods designated specifically by decisions of the Higher Council of Customs published in the Official Gazette:

 - throughout Lebanese territory.

1 - Every person apprehended in a flagrant offence of smuggling shall be brought without delay before the local Head of the Customs Service, who shall decide whether or not to retain him in custody under investigation.

2 - The Head of the Service, if he decides to retain the offender in custody, shall immediately notify the Appellate Public Prosecution, which shall have the authority to retain him in custody for a period not exceeding three days, provided that he is referred within such period to the competent court.

3 - The Appellate Public Prosecutor may, during the period of detention, proceed to the place of detention to examine the conditions thereof and the documents relating thereto, or he may appoint a physician, where necessary, to examine the detainee.

4 - The conditions for continuing the state of detention before the court are specified in Article 395 of this Law.

The following shall be deemed a flagrant offence of smuggling for the purpose of applying the provisions laid down in the preceding Article 358:

1 - The importation or attempted importation, without a written or oral declaration, of monopolised goods or prohibited goods.

2 - The exportation or attempted exportation, under the same conditions, of goods the taking out of which is prohibited.

3 - The transport of monopolised goods or goods the bringing in or taking out of which is prohibited, whether mentioned in the manifest or not mentioned therein, on board vessels, whatever their flag, having a tonnage of less than 150 maritime tons, at anchor or cruising within the limits of twelve miles from the coasts, save in the case resulting from proven force majeure.

4 - The stopping or cruising of vessels having a tonnage of less than 150 maritime tons, and carrying goods subject to high duties or to fiscal duties specified pursuant to decisions of the Higher Council of Customs published in the Official Gazette, within the maritime zone, save in the case resulting from proven force majeure, or the re-exportation of goods of the same kind on board vessels of the same tonnage.

Detention shall also be permissible in accordance with the procedures provided for in Article 358:

a- For every person who commits acts of resistance that obstruct the investigation into smuggling contraventions.

b - For every person who is feared to flee or abscond in order to evade the penalties, fines, and compensations to which he may be sentenced.

First: Customs officers of the second category, or of the rank of lieutenant and above, or those holding the position of head of office, by special authorisation from the Director General of Customs or from the head of the region to which they belong, and the head of the Audit and Anti-Smuggling Service and the head and officers of the Anti-Smuggling Department, as well as the head and officers of the Control Service at the Higher Council of Customs in cases required by the investigations they have initiated with officers, shall have the right to compel the production for their inspection of registers, papers, and documents of whatever kind relating to operations of interest to the Service, and to investigate them:

a - In railway offices and stations and at air, land, and maritime transport companies or their agencies, (invoices, loading documents, transport manifests, bills of lading, shipping notices, delivery orders, dispatch notes and schedules, delivery notes and schedules, warehouse registers, delivery registers, parcel registration books, delivery books, waybills, shipping papers, etc...)

b - At agencies concerned with receiving, collecting, or dispatching all types of parcels by all means of transport (detailed schedules of the total consignment, receipts, delivery books, etc...)

c - At brokers and agents (papers and registers kept in accordance with the provisions of Article 127 of this Law).

d - At operators of warehouses, docks, and general stores (registers and deposit files, and books of entry and exit of goods, etc...)

e - At merchants and establishments to whom goods declared at Customs are consigned or at their true senders.

f - At institutions connected with commercial consignments.

g- And in general, at all natural and legal persons who have a direct or indirect connection with regular or irregular operations falling within the scope of competence of the Customs Administration.

Second: All natural or legal persons mentioned in paragraphs (a, b, c, d, e, f, g) of item "First" above must retain all documents, instruments, and registers that they handle in connection with operations with which Customs is concerned, for a period of three years starting from the date of dispatch of the parcels with respect to senders and brokers and starting from the date of receipt with respect to consignees or brokers.

Third: The customs officers referred to in paragraph "First" above shall have the right to seize, during the inspection or investigation they conduct at the aforementioned companies and persons, all documents, instruments, and registers of whatever kind (accounting books, invoices, correspondence and copies thereof, cheque books, bills of exchange, bank accounts, etc...) that would facilitate the performance of their mission, against a receipt for the seized items, provided that they are returned to their owners immediately upon the conclusion of the investigation.

Fourth: Failure to retain the documents, instruments, and registers referred to in this Article and in Article 127, or refusal to hand them over, as well as failure to keep the registers provided for in the latter Article in accordance with the rules and conditions set forth therein, as well as lending a name or signature referred to in the aforementioned Article 129, shall constitute customs offences punishable by a flat fine ranging between two million and ten million Lebanese pounds, imposed on each operation, transaction, trip, or lending of a signature, and in addition thereto, where applicable, the penalty provided for in Article 131 above shall apply, and any unjustified delay shall be deemed equivalent to refusal.

Fifth: The Customs Administration may, subject to reciprocity, hand over to the competent authorities in foreign countries all information, certificates, reports, and other documents capable of proving the violation of the laws and regulations applicable in the territories of those countries upon entry or exit.

Sixth: Any address disposed of in a customs transaction that subsequently proves to be contrary to the truth and reality shall constitute a customs offence governed by the same rule as the offence of failing to retain the documents, instruments, and registers referred to in this Article and in Article 127 or refusing to hand them over.

1- Domiciliary investigations and searches to look for smuggling in Lebanese territory may be carried out:

First: Throughout the land customs zone, with respect to all categories of goods.

Second: Throughout Lebanese territory:

a - With respect to all categories of smuggled goods pursued in plain sight by customs officers, either after they saw them entering this territory or after they saw them being extracted from the customs zone, provided that they arrive at the time when these goods are being brought into the residences.

b - With respect to goods prohibited from transit or internal circulation, or banned, or whose possession or sale is prohibited, or monopolised goods circulating or possessed irregularly, or goods specifically designated by decisions of the Higher Council of Customs published in the Official Gazette.

2 - A domiciliary investigation and search shall be based on a warrant from the Public Prosecution.

The warrant must include the address of the premises authorised to be entered and searched, together with a statement of the factual and legal grounds justifying this measure.

3 - A domiciliary investigation and search shall be exempted from the condition mentioned in paragraph 2 of this Article when the matter relates to an offence in flagrante delicto, or pursuits in plain sight, or when the person concerned consents to the search.

Provided that the competent Public Prosecution is immediately notified, which shall take the decision it deems appropriate.

4 - A domiciliary investigation and search may only be conducted between sunrise and sunset, even in the case of pursuit in plain sight.

However, an investigation and search commenced during the day and not concluded by sunset may be continued at night until their completion.

5 - A residence may be opened by force in the presence of the mukhtar if the conditions mentioned above are observed and the householder refuses to allow the officers to enter.

6 - Public premises may be entered at night so long as they are open, provided that the investigation and search therein are confined to the sections to which the public is permitted access.

7 - If domiciliary investigations and searches lead to the discovery of records and documents relating to smuggling operations, customs officers shall have the right to seize such records and documents.

a- Customs officers shall have the right to patrol, in the performance of their ordered service:

1- In public or national properties and village commons adjoining the maritime borders.

2- On railway lines located at a distance from the maritime and land borders not exceeding 1000 metres.

3- On private properties not enclosed by a wall, adjoining the land borders or located on the shore bank or the high rocks alongside the sea or the banks of rivers up to 500 metres from their mouth.

Owners adjacent to rivers and borders may not erect any barrier preventing freedom of passage for customs officers along the land borders and on the seashore or the high rocks on the sides of the sea and on the banks of rivers up to 500 metres from their mouth.

b - Any hindrance or opposition to the freedom of movement of customs officers and any infringement of the prohibitions and obligations resulting from this Article shall be deemed an opposition during the performance of duty and shall be prosecuted in accordance with Article 426 .

1 - Customs officers shall have the right to enter post offices, including sorting halls having direct connection with abroad, to search, in the presence of postal officers, for closed or open consignments, of internal or external origin, with the exception of transit consignments, which contain or appear to contain articles of the kind mentioned in this Article.

2 - The Postal Administration is authorised to subject to customs control, within the conditions provided for in the conventions and regulations of the Universal Postal Union, consignments prohibited from importation, or those subject to duties collected by the Customs Administration, or to special restrictions and procedures upon entry.

3 - The Postal Administration is also authorised to subject to customs control consignments prohibited from exportation or subject to duties collected by the Customs Administration, or to special restrictions and procedures upon exit.

4 - The principle of the secrecy of correspondence may under no circumstances be infringed.

1 - Every natural or legal person who, on the occasion of carrying out organised and continuous commercial operations, sends from abroad to persons in the customs territory, including free zones, postal parcels or consignments by post, must authorise a representative residing in Lebanon to carry out before the Customs Administration the clearance operations for these imports.

2- The conditions for the application of this Article shall be determined by decisions issued by the Director General of Customs.

Customs officers may verify the identity of persons entering or leaving the customs territory or moving within the customs zone.

1- For the purpose of establishing customs offences in cases of importation, exportation and possession of narcotic drugs, and with the aim of uncovering the identity of their perpetrators and beneficiaries and working to confiscate them, customs officers are authorised, under conditions determined by the Director General of Customs in cooperation with the Central Directorate for Combating Narcotic Drugs and after notifying the Cassation Public Prosecution, to conduct surveillance and track the movement of such substances in accordance with the provisions of Article 220 of Law No. 673, dated 16/3/98, relating to Narcotic Drugs, Psychotropic Substances and Precursors.

2- No criminal liability shall attach to the officers when the Cassation Public Prosecution authorises them, under its supervision, to undertake the possession and transport of the aforementioned substances and their delivery to suspects with the aim of uncovering the identity of the offenders.

Likewise, no liability shall attach as a result of the officers' use of means of transport for these substances, or the depositing of these substances, or communicating in relation thereto, or using funds for the aforementioned purpose.

3 - The provisions of the first and second paragraphs of this Article shall also apply to equipment for the illicit manufacture of narcotic substances specified in the laws in force.

1- The establishment of customs offences must be carried out by at least two persons, both of whom are customs officers or State employees, regardless of their civilian or military capacity.

This establishment may also be carried out by a customs officer and another State employee, or by a customs officer and a private individual provided that he is of legal age.

2 - The establishment of offences shall be effected by means of a seizure report.

3 - Officers of the Tobacco and Tombac Monopoly Administration shall exercise the same powers granted to customs officers with regard to establishing customs offences relating to tobacco, tombac and cigarette papers.

1 - Persons effecting seizures shall conduct the smuggled goods, the goods used to conceal the smuggling, and the means of transport to a customs office or post which is, insofar as circumstances permit, the nearest to the place where the precautionary seizure was carried out. If this proves impossible for serious reasons, they must deny these reasons in the seizure report.

2 - Where the circumstances of the seizure so require, the seized goods, the goods used to conceal the smuggling, and the means of transport may be placed in the custody of a third party, at the place where they were seized or at another place.

3 - The retention of persons under investigation shall take place in accordance with the cases enumerated in Articles 358, 359 and 360 and within the conditions set forth in Article 395 of this Law.

Those ordering the retention of persons under investigation must specify in the seizure report the duration required by the investigation, the date of opening the report and the date of closing it, and this information shall be recorded in a special register at the post, prepared for this purpose.

4 - The seizure report shall be drawn up at the place of seizure of the goods or at the place of discovery of the offence, immediately upon verification of the offence and at the latest after the transfer of the seized goods, the goods used to conceal the smuggling, and the means of transport to the customs office or post, unless there is an impeding cause mentioned in the report.

The seizure report shall state:

1- The place, date and hour of drawing up the report, in words and in figures.

2 - The date of the seizure and the hour of its occurrence, in words and in figures.

3 - The place of the seizure and its circumstances.

4 - The names of the seizing officers, their signatures, their ranks, their capacity and the office or post to which they belong.

5- The names of the offenders, their capacities, their profession, their detailed addresses and their elected domicile, whenever possible.

6 - The kind of seized goods, their descriptions, their quantities, their weights, their value and the duties and taxes at risk of being lost, whenever possible.

7- The goods that escaped seizure, to the extent that could be known or inferred.

8 - Detailed facts, sensory observations, and the statements of the offenders and witnesses, if any.

9 - The legal provisions applicable to the offence, whenever possible.

10 - The presence of the offenders when describing the seized goods or the notice addressed to them to attend this description.

11 - If the accused is present, it shall be stated in the seizure report that it was read out to him, that he was invited to sign it and that he will be summoned to appear before the court hearing customs cases, and if the accused is absent or refuses to sign, this shall be stated in the report and a copy thereof shall be posted on the door of the customs office within a period of 24 hours from the closing of the report, and this shall also be stated in the report.

12- The place, date and hour of closing the report, in words and in figures.

1- An offer may be made to deliver the seized goods, the objects used to conceal the fraud and the seized means of transport to the offender, if they are not prohibited, against the provision of a bail, a guarantee or a deposit of an amount at least equivalent to their value. This delivery may also be made to a third party against the same

guarantees. This offer and its outcome shall be stated in the seizure report.

2- The Director or the Head of the Region may release the public means of transport in favour of its owner or operator without bail or without depositing its value if he engages in transport operations and it is established that the offender concluded with him the contract of carriage or the contract of hire of the means of transport in accordance with legal rules and professional customs, and that the driver of the means of transport fulfilled the obligation of supervision sufficiently, provided that the means of transport is not equipped to facilitate smuggling. However, the release shall not exempt from paying the value of the expenses incurred by the Customs Administration for guarding and maintaining the means of transport.

Where the seizure report concerns forged documents or documents containing an alteration, the seizure report must state the nature of the forgery and the alterations or additions, after the seizing officer has initialled them with the phrase so that they are not "altered" and after requesting the user thereof to sign them as well and recording his reply in the report.

1- Upon the seizure of smuggled goods in shops, warehouses, and commercial premises, as well as in residences following domestic investigations and searches conducted in accordance with the provisions of Article 357 of this Law, non-prohibited goods shall be exempted from seizure if the person against whom the seizure is made provides a guarantee for their value; and if he fails to do so, or if the goods are prohibited, restricted, or monopolised, the seizing officers shall convey them to the nearest customs post or deliver them to a third party to guard them at the place of seizure or at any other place.

2 - The drawing up of the seizure report must take place in the presence of a member of the Judicial Police, and in the event of his refusal, it shall suffice to mention the matter in the report.

Where the seizure concerns goods on board anchored vessels and their immediate unloading proves impossible, the seizing officers shall affix seals to the hatches, cabins, compartments, lockers, cases, bales, barrels, and other packages or receptacles.

Where the seizure report coincides with the unloading, the report must include the number, numbers, and marks of the cases, bundles, and barrels. As for the details, they shall be recorded at the office in the presence of the offender or after serving him with formal notice to attend, and a copy of each detailed unloading shall then be delivered to him.

Where the seizure concerns smuggled goods in the case of pursuit in sight or in the case of an offence in flagrante delicto, or in the case of the goods being prohibited, restricted, or monopolised, or where it is explicitly inferred from the statements of the holders thereof or from the documents in their possession that they are smuggled, the circumstance that has been verified must be mentioned in the report. In the event that the goods are seized as a result of pursuit in sight, the report must also mention:

A - With respect to goods subject to a movement permit which were not in a regular state of movement, that the pursuit commenced from the date the goods crossed the internal boundary of the customs zone until the time of their seizure.

B - With respect to all other goods, that the pursuit was uninterrupted from the time they crossed the external borders of the country until the time of their seizure.

1 - An offender who wishes to enter a civil plea of forgery of the seizure report shall submit a written declaration to that effect either in person or through an authorised lawyer holding a special power of attorney executed before a notary public, at the commencement of the action, at the first hearing held by the court hearing customs cases, and he shall, within the following three days, file with the registry of the said court the evidence of forgery and the names and capacities of the witnesses whose testimony he wishes to have heard. All of the foregoing shall be on pain of forfeiture of the forgery claim.

2 - If the declarant does not know how to write and sign, he shall deliver his declaration directly to the President of the said court, who shall refer it to the court after recording thereon that the declarant does not know how to write and sign.

3 - A declaration entering a plea of forgery by one of the offenders shall not prevent the continuation of the examination of the action with respect to the others.

4 - If the seizure report is declared forged in whole or in part, the court shall order either its rectification or its annulment.

5 - If the claimant in forgery loses his action or withdraws from it without the consent of his opponent, he shall be sentenced to a pecuniary penalty, in favour of the Customs, ranging between four hundred thousand pounds and four million Lebanese pounds, in addition to the penalties prescribed in respect of the offence itself.

1 - Offences provided for in the customs laws and regulations may be prosecuted and proved by all legal means of proof, even if such offences were not seized within the customs zone or outside it or were not discovered upon the declaration of the goods under customs declarations. For this purpose, information received from foreign authorities and seizure reports and documents issued by them may be considered as evidence of the commission of the offence.

2 - The Public Prosecutions before the criminal courts shall conduct the public prosecution aimed at applying criminal penalties for ordinary offences concomitant with or connected to customs offences.

The Customs Administration shall conduct the action aimed at applying duties and fines.

The judicial authority shall provide the Customs Administration with any information that comes to its knowledge in the course of a civil, commercial or criminal dispute, even if accompanied by a ruling of non-suit, which is capable of constituting a presumption that an offence against the Customs Law and its regulations has been committed.

If the offender dies before the issuance of the final decision convicting him or before the completion of the settlement, the Customs Administration shall be entitled to bring an action before the competent court for the seizure of the smuggled goods in his estate which could not be attached, or failing that, for judgment to be awarded to it against the estate for an amount equivalent to the value of such goods as at the date on which the offence occurred.

1- Except for the cases in which the method of constraint is used in accordance with Articles 171 and 352, the Director or the Regional Head of Customs may issue a writ of constraint against the principal obligor or against his guarantors whenever the Customs Administration has a debt of duties, whether they are evaded or unpaid duties or duties guaranteed by bonded instruments, various undertakings, judicial undertakings, or settlements, which the obligors refuse to pay or delay in doing so.

2- These writs of constraint shall be issued within the conditions provided for in Article 171.

3- An objection to the writs of constraint shall not stay execution unless the obligor deposits the duties for which he is being prosecuted by way of security.

1 - The Customs Administration may conclude settlements with offenders before judicial prosecution, during it, and after the issuance of the decision of the court hearing customs cases provided for in Article 391 of this Law, by replacing the statutory penalties (fixed or variable pecuniary penalties and the confiscation of goods, means of transport, and objects used to conceal the fraud) with a pecuniary penalty that varies according to the circumstances of the seizure and is paid, where applicable, in addition to the amount of duties due on the goods imported or exported by way of fraud, and the Customs Administration is also authorised, if the circumstances of the establishment of the offences justify it, to overlook the offences detected by its officers.

2- Nothing of the duties due to the State Treasury may be waived pursuant to the settlement.

3- The Administration is prohibited from concluding a settlement after the judicial decision becomes final.

A settlement concluded between the Customs Administration, on the one hand, and the perpetrators of the offences and their accomplices, on the other hand, shall have the effect of extinguishing both the civil action and the public prosecution if the subject matter of this latter action is fiscal customs offences not subject to corporal penalties. However, the settlement concluded with the perpetrators of the offences shall not preclude the prosecution of the accomplices and accessories in the offence, unless otherwise provided for in the text of the settlement, nor shall it preclude the action exercised by the Public Prosecution or any other administration for the suppression of ordinary misdemeanours or others committed at the same time in which the customs offences were committed.

If several seizures occur against unknown fugitive persons and the Department does not see a need to draw up seizure reports thereon, given the minor importance of the smuggled goods, and in any case if there are no precedents and the value of the goods for each seizure does not exceed 400.000 pounds, the court provided for in Article 391 may decide the seizure of those goods by a single decision.

The impoundment and confiscation of the seized goods within the conditions provided for in the preceding Article 375 shall be decided by the court hearing customs cases and executed by the Customs Administration after the expiry of eight days from the posting of the decision issued in this regard in the registry of the said court.

1- The contraventions provided for in the decisions and texts relating to customs may be ascertained and proved by means of verification reports drawn up by customs officers with the results of their investigations, inquiries and the interrogations which they have conducted, even if no seizures have taken place inside or outside the customs zone.

2 - The verification report must contain the names of those who drew it up and their capacity, the date (hour, day, year), the place of the inspection and investigation conducted, the material facts witnessed in person by those who drew up the report and the information available in respect thereof, and a mention of the impoundment of the documents relating thereto where applicable. It shall also be mentioned in the report that the persons with whom the investigations were conducted were informed of the time of drawing up the report (hour, day, year) and its place and that they were invited to attend its writing, and in the case of their attendance its content shall be read out to them and they shall be asked to sign it, and that shall be mentioned in the report.

Customs contraventions provided for in the laws and regulations relating to customs may be ascertained and proved by all other legal ways and means and from all official authorities by means of reports, even if no confiscation has taken place inside or outside the customs zone.

1 - Seizure reports and verification reports drawn up in the form set out in Articles 367 to 377 shall be deemed authentic and probative of the material facts witnessed in person by those who drew up the report until their forgery is alleged criminally or civilly.

As for the remaining entries, they shall be established until the contrary is proved.

2 - The courts may not accept grounds for invalidating these reports except such as results from the omission of the formalities imposed pursuant to the aforementioned Articles. A mere formal deficiency therein shall not be deemed a ground for their nullity, as they may be returned to those who drew them up in order to complete this deficiency. These reports may not be returned for their completion if the deficiency relates to the material facts.

1- The right of compounding in cases relating to the infringement of customs laws and regulations belongs, as the case may be, either to the Higher Council of Customs, or to the Director General of Customs, or to the Regional Heads:

First: The Regional Heads shall exercise the right of compounding in the following manner:

1- The Regional Heads shall decide finally upon infringements falling under the provisions of Article 425.

2- The Regional Heads shall decide, subject to the approval of the Director General, in the following cases:

a - In infringements falling under the provisions of Articles 426 to 432.

b - In all other infringements when the value of the goods does not exceed twenty-five million Lebanese pounds, and in cases in which there are evaded duties or duties exposed to loss even if the value of the goods exceeds twenty-five million Lebanese pounds, if the amount of these duties does not exceed six million.

Second: The Director General of Customs shall decide upon the following infringements:

a- Infringements provided for in Paragraph Fourth of Article 361.

b- Infringements provided for in the last paragraph of Article 423 (goods of unknown kind and value).

c- Other infringements if the value of the goods therein exceeds twenty-five million Lebanese pounds and does not exceed one hundred million pounds, and in cases in which there are evaded duties or duties exposed to loss even if the value of the goods exceeds one hundred million Lebanese pounds, if the amount of these duties does not exceed twenty-five million Lebanese pounds.

Third: The Higher Council of Customs shall decide in the other cases not provided for above upon the proposal of the Director General of Customs. 2- Customs duties and all other duties and taxes the collection of which is entrusted to the Customs Administration shall enter into the calculation of the evaded duties or duties exposed to loss

1- The limitation period for customs actions and for penalties shall be:

10 years for the collection of duties which the taxpayer evaded paying by means of fraudulent manoeuvres or false or incomplete declarations. This period shall commence from the date of discovery of the fraud.

10 years for the enforcement of any judgment or decision of concern to the Administration, including the collection of duties the payment of which is pursued by writs of constraint issued pursuant to Article 171.

5 years for the collection of duties not paid due to an error by the Administration, as well as for the collection of pecuniary penalties and confiscations.

2 - Apart from the causes by which the limitation period is interrupted in high rights, the limitation period in customs cases shall be interrupted either by a claim by registered letter or by the opening of an investigation in respect thereof before the court hearing customs cases, notified to the person concerned.

No person shall be entitled to claim from the Customs Administration the refund of duties after three years have elapsed from the date of their payment. Securities, of all kinds, shall be definitively converted into duties and proceeds within the time limits and conditions determined by the Customs Administration, if the persons concerned do not submit, within the specified time limits, the proofs enabling the settlement of such securities.

In all cases, the portion in excess of the duties actually due (the remainder) may not be claimed after three years have elapsed from the date of payment of the security, unless the delay in settlement is caused by the Administration. As for securities resulting from the amendment of customs duties, the three-year limitation period in respect thereof shall commence from the date of approval of the amendment decisions relating thereto by the competent authority.

The Customs Administration shall be released towards taxpayers, after five years have elapsed from each completed year, from the obligation to keep receipt registers and other registers and papers pertaining to the said year, and it may not be compelled to produce such registers and papers if there are cases still pending examination, even if the said registers and papers are necessary for the investigation and for the rendering of judgments therein.

1 - Subject to the jurisdiction of the competent criminal courts in accordance with the provisions of the laws in force, the seizure report drawn up in accordance with the provisions of the preceding articles shall, if the dispute is not settled by way of compromise, be referred to one of the chambers of the Court of First Instance in Beirut.

2 - By a decision of the Minister of Justice, after consulting the Supreme Judicial Council, and upon the proposal of the First President of the Court of Appeal of Beirut, one of the chambers of the Court of First Instance in Beirut shall be designated to hear all customs cases investigated throughout the Lebanese territory.

3 - The Minister of Justice may, by a decision taken by him after consulting the Supreme Judicial Council, authorise the chamber of the Court of First Instance competent to hear customs cases in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraphs to hold its hearings outside its seat in premises allocated to it at the Customs Administration.

4 - The provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure shall be followed before the court hearing customs cases, subject to the special provisions stipulated in this Decree.

5 - The first trial hearing in customs actions shall be scheduled without being bound by the time limits for the exchange of pleadings.

The Court of First Instance shall hear the following cases:

1 - Infringements provided for in the Customs Law and other texts relating to customs.

2 - Every dispute or every litigation or action of whatever kind, where the Customs is plaintiff or defendant with respect to customs duties and other duties and taxes the collection of which is entrusted to the Customs Administration, and the enforcement of undertakings concluded or connected in this regard.

3 - Objections to writs of constraint.

4 - Actions for the annulment of arbitral decisions provided for in Article 161 of this Law.

5 - Continuation of detention provided for in Articles 358, 359 and 360 of this Law.

All cases pending before the Customs Commission on the date this Law enters into force shall be referred administratively.
The Customs Administration shall sue and be sued before all courts and enforcement departments in the person of the Director General or his representative.
The court may issue a rogatory commission to any investigating body or adjudicating body and any public administration.

1 - Every person detained under the cases set out in Articles 358, 359 and 360 of this Law shall be referred within a maximum period of three days to the competent court, which shall rule on the matter of continuing the state of detention.

2 - The court may decide to detain the person referred to it, to leave him free, or to release him against a bond of residence or against a security not exceeding what may be adjudged.

3 - The period of detention may not exceed fifteen days.

Customs officers may serve writs of summons, citations, notifications, and all documents relating to legal procedure required for collecting the customs tax, levying pecuniary penalties, and effecting confiscations, in accordance with the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure.

1 - Service of the judgment of the court shall be effected upon the person concerned in person, or at his last known place of residence, or at his elected domicile, or at his place of business.

If the person concerned is absent, service may be effected upon any adult person residing with him. Service may be made upon a servant or a commercial employee. In the event of refusal to sign, this shall be recorded and the service shall remain valid.

2 - If the person concerned changes his declared place of residence or his place of business after the date of the seizure report drawn up against him without notifying the Customs thereof in writing, or if he gives a false address, the formality of service shall be effected by affixing on the door of his last, known, or declared place of residence and on the outer door of the Customs.

3 - Writs of summons shall be served according to the same procedures mentioned above relating to the service of the judgment of the court.
