4 - If the offence is committed by an unknown person and the total value of the seized articles does not exceed one million Lebanese pounds, service of the summons of the offender or the judgment of the court shall be effected by affixing on the door of the court registry.

And if the total value of the seized articles exceeds one million pounds, service shall be effected by affixing on the door of the court registry and by publication in two local newspapers.

5 - If the offence is committed by a person residing abroad, the summons documents of the offender and the judgment of the court shall be sent to the Appellate Public Prosecution, which shall ensure their service in the manner it deems appropriate.

The Customs Administration may request the Public Prosecution to prevent offenders and those responsible for smuggling from leaving Lebanese territory in the event that the seized articles are insufficient to cover the duties, taxes, and fines. The request or the prohibition order shall be revoked:

1 - If the offender or the person responsible for smuggling provides a guarantee accepted by the Customs Administration equivalent to the amounts that may be claimed from him.

2 - If it subsequently appears that the detained funds are sufficient to cover the amounts.

Decisions issued by the court shall be final and not subject to appeal when the total of the penalties imposed (the pecuniary penalty and the confiscation of the goods, means of transport, and articles used to conceal the fraud) does not exceed the amount of five million pounds.

The court hearing customs cases may order the provisional execution of its judgments, whether against the debtor's property or against his person, notwithstanding any remedy to which he may resort.

It may also dispense with the time limit for the notice addressed to the debtor so that it may detain the convicted person immediately; however, the debtor may apply to the Court of Appeal, which may stay the execution of imprisonment on condition that the convicted person provide a financial guarantee covering the duties and fines that may be adjudged. The application provided for in the preceding paragraph shall be conducted in accordance with the rules of procedure followed in summary matters.

1- For the purpose of executing judgments rendered in favour of the Customs, the Administration may, while reserving its right to imprison the debtor, attach and put up for sale by public auction simultaneously all of his movable and immovable property.

2- If no one comes forward to purchase the immovable property or if bids below the reserve price are submitted in respect thereof for the second time, such property shall be adjudicated by operation of law in the name of the Customs Administration at the reserve price.

3- By a decision of the Director General of Customs, a committee shall be appointed to fix the reserve price for the sale and to conduct the auction.

The rules followed in the Law on the Collection of Assessed Taxes shall apply.

In all cases in which it is impossible to collect in full the customs duties and the other duties and taxes collected by the Customs, as well as the pecuniary penalties imposed and the costs, the penalty of imprisonment shall be executed at the rate of one day for every 25000 pounds uncollected, provided that the term of imprisonment shall not in any event exceed one year.
The term of imprisonment shall be calculated separately for each judgment.

Imprisonment in customs actions shall be executed without any need to prove the debtor's ability to pay, unless he is in a state of bankruptcy, and such bankruptcy is not due to a criminal fault on his part, and with respect to the age of the person sought to be imprisoned, the general provisions set forth in Article 146 of the Penal Code read in conjunction with Article 1003 of the Code of Civil Procedure" shall apply, and this text shall apply to pending cases.

By way of exception to the legal provisions in force, if the Customs requests the imprisonment of the same debtor once again, after having accepted or requested his release, its request must be granted.
Warrants to bring before the court and imprisonment orders may be executed at the hands of customs officers. All attachments and notifications may be effected through the same officers.
The pecuniary penalties and confiscations provided for in the customs laws and regulations shall be deemed civil compensation to the Customs Administration.

Judgments rendered by the court as a result of an objection to a seizure report, a verification report, or an administrative decision shall be deemed rendered in the presence of the parties even if the objector fails to appear.

Judgments rendered by the court may not be appealed by the party ordered to pay duties and fines unless such party deposits with the Treasury a cash security guaranteeing the entirety of the duties ordered to be collected, plus, in the event that penalties are applied, an amount equivalent to 25% of the value of the penalties imposed in the appealed decision, provided that the total security for the penalties does not exceed ten million Lebanese pounds.

1 - Judgments of the court hearing customs cases shall be appealed before the competent Court of Appeal in Beirut, within the thirty days following service of the judgment in accordance with the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, and the first hearing shall be scheduled without being bound by the time limits for the exchange of pleadings.

2 - One of the chambers of the Court of Appeal in Beirut shall be designated, by decision of the Minister of Justice, after consulting the Supreme Judicial Council upon the proposal of the First President of the Court of Appeal in Beirut, to hear challenges against judgments rendered by the Court of First Instance hearing customs cases.

3 - The chamber of the Court of Appeal in Beirut hearing appeals against judgments rendered in customs cases may be authorised to hold its hearings in premises allocated to it at the Customs Administration, by a decree adopted after consulting the Supreme Judicial Council and upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice.
The appellate decision shall be subject to cassation in accordance with the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure.

The court shall issue its judgments as expeditiously as possible, and the Chief Clerk of the court shall serve the judgments of first instance upon the litigants within fifteen days at most from the date of their issuance.

1- The Customs Administration is exempted from affixing stamps to all documents which it may be required to submit to the court or the production of which it may request, and from paying all judicial expenses incurred in actions which it may institute or which may be instituted against it, and it is also exempted from all enforcement expenses.

2- If the Customs Administration loses the action, it shall bear the expenses and costs awarded against it in favour of the other party.

3- The Customs Administration is also exempted from providing a guarantee, security, or advance to cover expenses in all cases in which the law imposes such obligation upon litigants.
No plea for the striking out of the action or prosecution may be raised against the Customs.
Pecuniary penalties and confiscations may be combined where the material offences concur.

Civil liability in the course of the application of this Law shall arise upon the fulfilment of the material elements of the offence, and good faith may not be pleaded as a defence.

However, a person shall be exempted from liability where he proves that he was the victim of force majeure or a sudden accident, as well as where he proves that he did not commit any of the acts that constituted the offence, caused its occurrence, or led to its commission.

The sums adjudged (duties, fines, and confiscations) shall be imposed on and recovered jointly and severally from the principal perpetrators of the offences, the guarantors, the accomplices, the intermediaries, the seamen, the masters of the means of transport, and all carriers, and from the owners of the offending goods, the consignees thereof, the owners of the means of transport, the owners of the goods used to conceal the fraud, and the owners of the premises in which the smuggled goods were deposited. The owner or operator of a public means of transport shall be discharged from liability if he proves that the customs offence occurred independently of his will, that it was impossible for him to discover it despite his performance of the duties imposed upon him by the rules of his profession, and that he concluded the contract of carriage in accordance with the rules and conditions referred to in paragraph (2) of Article 370 of this Law.
Heirs shall be liable for the payment of the sums due from the deceased convicted person within the limits of their hereditary shares.

The Customs Administration shall enjoy, for the recovery of all duties, penalties, confiscations, and restitutions, a general lien over the movable property of taxpayers. This lien shall operate in all circumstances, even in the event of bankruptcy, and in priority over all debts, except those relating to the preservation of things, judicial costs advanced by a third party, and debts having a general lien over movables. The said lien shall include motor vehicles and motorcycles, in respect of which the Customs Administration shall have priority over the seller's right provided for in the third Article of the Law of 20 May 1935, and the lien of the Customs Administration shall be of the first rank over the sums deposited as security by taxpayers prior to judicial recourse.

A guarantor who pays to the Customs Administration the guaranteed value shall be subrogated to the Administration in its rights, privileges, and mortgages. Furthermore, the Customs Administration may, without the consent of the debtor or notifying him, assign and transfer to any third party, even to joint and several debtors, and even if its right is the subject of a dispute or a lawsuit, every debt due to it in whatever capacity, and subrogate this third party to itself in all its rights, privileges, and mortgages against the debtor and his guarantor.

The subrogation approved by the Administration shall always take place for the benefit of the subrogee under the same conditions that applied to the Administration. In all cases, the rights, privileges, and mortgages of the Administration shall pass to the subrogee after he has paid to the Customs treasury the value of the debt.

The instrument of subrogation shall be constituted, without the need for any other formality, by the receipt given by the Customs in which the conditions and limits of the subrogation are specified.

In all cases in which the courts decide to confiscate the smuggled goods, they must, subject to the provisions of the second paragraph of Article 417, decide at the same time, in addition to the pecuniary penalty provided for in Article 423, to confiscate the means of transport, goods, and objects of whatever kind that were used to conceal the fraud (even if a valid declaration was submitted therefor), and their value shall be added to the amount of the pecuniary penalty.

The amount of the pecuniary penalty provided for in Article 421, regardless of the regulatory confiscations, shall be determined as follows:

1 - In the event of the seizure of the goods, means of transport, and objects that were used to conceal the fraud:

a - If the goods and objects are neither prohibited, nor restricted, nor monopolised: at an amount equivalent to twice the duties up to three times the amount thereof.

b - If such goods are subject to high duties or revenue duties, designated pursuant to decisions issued by the Supreme Council of Customs, or subject to the control of the customs zone within the conditions provided for in Article 340 of this Law: at an amount equivalent to three times the duties up to four times the amount thereof.

c - If such goods are prohibited or monopolised: at an amount equivalent to twice the value up to three times the amount thereof, including the customs duties.

d - If such goods are restricted: at an amount equivalent to the value up to twice the amount thereof, including the customs duties.

2 - If the goods, means of transport, and objects that were used to conceal the fraud have escaped seizure:

The court shall rule, in addition to the pecuniary penalty mentioned above, in compensation for the confiscation, for the payment of an amount equivalent to the value of such goods, means of transport, and objects that were used to conceal the fraud (including the customs duties), according to the price on the domestic market and on the date of commission of the fraud in cases where it is not possible to ascertain sufficient elements to determine the value of the goods and objects that escaped seizure, even approximately, a fine ranging between one million and ten million Lebanese pounds shall be imposed.

The following offences shall be liable to the imposition of a pecuniary penalty equivalent to from double to triple the duties sought:

No. 1 - A false declaration aimed at obtaining, without right, by any means whatsoever, an illegal or irregular refund of the customs duties in whole or in part, even if such duties were deposited as security.

No. 2 - A false declaration as to nature, kind, quality, number, quantity, measurement, volume, weight or origin, which is aimed at obtaining a recovery of a duty exceeding the duty which may rightfully be refunded.

No. 3 - A false declaration as to value, aimed at obtaining a refund of a duty exceeding the duty which may rightfully be refunded, if the declared value exceeds by a proportion of 1/20 or more the value determined by the Customs.

The following shall be liable to the imposition of a pecuniary penalty in the amount of one hundred thousand Lebanese pounds:

No. 1 - Importing or attempting to import goods exempt from duties by way of smuggling or without a manifest or without a customs declaration.

No. 2 - Exporting or attempting to export goods exempt from duties, without a declaration or by way of smuggling.

No. 3 - A false declaration as to nature, kind, quality, origin, quantity or value of goods exempt from duties, or which does not expose any duty to loss.

No. 4 - The offences set forth in Nos. 10, 11 and 12 of Article 421 whenever the goods dispatched in transit or re-exported are exempt from customs duties.

No. 5 - Presenting the goods to the office of exit or to the office of destination, after the expiry of the time limits fixed in the guaranteed undertaking declaration, and returning a certificate of discharge of a guaranteed undertaking declaration after the lapse of one month from the expiry of the time limit granted pursuant to this declaration, except in the case of force majeure legally established.

No. 6 - Breaking the lead seals or seals of goods dispatched in transit, without justification and without a shortage or substitution being ascertained.

No. 7 - The absence of a manifest upon exit or failure to submit the exit manifest to the Customs, and the excess or shortage in the packages mentioned in the exit manifest and ascertained after loading.

No. 8 - Any omission, error or failure to mention the indications or information which must be contained in the manifests or the documents standing in their stead, when that does not affect the application of the duties due or the restrictions loaned and the master proves it through the documents that are in his possession.

1 - When customs officers conduct an inspection on board vessels, within the conditions provided for in Articles 69, 70, 72, and 79, and one or more of the following contraventions are established:

1 - If the single general manifest is not produced.

2 - If several manifests are found.

3 - If goods not mentioned in the manifest are found.

4 - If discrepancies between the goods and the manifest are found.

5 - If some of the goods mentioned in the manifest are not presented for inspection.

The master of the vessel shall be sentenced to a pecuniary penalty of four hundred thousand pounds for each contravention.

2 - The master of the vessel shall also be sentenced to pay an amount equivalent to the value of the goods that are the subject of the contraventions mentioned under numbers (3), (4), and

(5) above,

3 - The vessel shall be seized in all the aforementioned cases and shall remain as security for the payment of the pecuniary penalties specified above, and in addition thereto, the prohibited or monopolised goods and articles that are in excess of the manifest shall be confiscated.

When customs officers search steamships within the conditions provided for in Article 69, if the cargo of these steamships includes prohibited goods or specified goods and materials that are monopolised or subject to high duties or to fiscal duties, whether mentioned in the manifest or not mentioned, these steamships shall be confiscated together with their cargo and their masters shall be fined a pecuniary penalty of 100000 Lebanese pounds.

Vessels shall be exempted from confiscation if the master proves that force majeure circumstances (maritime emergencies or breakdown) forced him to change the course of the vessel or cast anchor within the twelve-mile limit from the coast or take refuge in one of the Lebanese ports, provided that these circumstances have been recorded in the logbook of the vessel prior to its inspection by the customs personnel.

The resistance of the master to the investigations of customs officers, during the search of steamships provided for in Articles 429 and 430 of this Law, before or after the intervention of the public officer in accordance with the provisions of Article 73 thereof, shall subject this master to a fine of a pecuniary penalty of one hundred thousand pounds, and the steamship and its cargo shall be seized and remain as security for the execution of this penalty.

The failure to enter what must be entered of the goods in the schedules provided for in Article 71, and any shortage in these schedules established upon the departure of the steamship, shall be recorded against the master undertaking the transport or against his duly authorised representative and shall lead to the application of the penalties provided for in Article 430, subject, where applicable, to the application of the penalties provided for in Article 431.

The following shall be liable to the imposition of a pecuniary penalty of one hundred thousand Lebanese pounds:

No. 1 - Any deficiency in the packages mentioned in the manifest or the other documents acting as a substitute therefor, ascertained after the unloading of the means of transport, whatever they may be.

The pecuniary penalty amounting to 100 thousand Lebanese pounds shall be payable for each missing package. This offence shall be recorded against the person in charge of operating the carriers, or the carrier, or the duly authorised representative of either of them, and in general against all the persons mentioned in Article 417. Proof that the deficiency compared to what is listed in the manifest, occurring prior to the delivery of the goods to the Customs, took place outside the land borders shall be deemed a justification therefor.

No. 2 - Delay in submitting the inward or outward manifest or whatever acts as a substitute therefor.

No. 3- The transport of passengers or goods within Lebanese territory by the foreign motor vehicles referred to in Article 284.

This offence shall result in the payment of customs duties on such motor vehicles in addition to the pecuniary penalty.

No. 4 - Insults, affronts, threats and ill-treatment directed at customs officers, as well as the opposition and disturbance to which they are subjected during the exercise of their functions. This pecuniary penalty shall be adjudged personally against the perpetrators of these acts and their accomplices. This is in addition to the penalties

prescribed in the Penal Code.

The following shall be liable to the imposition of a pecuniary penalty of 400000 Lebanese pounds:

No. 1 - Failure to have the original manifest endorsed by the customs authorities at the port of loading.

No. 2 - The presence of several manifests or other documents acting as a substitute therefor in the possession of the persons in charge of operating the carriers.

These offences shall be recorded against the persons in charge of operating the carriers and the carrier or the duly authorised representative of either of them, and in general against all the persons mentioned in Article 417.

No. 3 - Failure to produce the bills of lading and the other documents specified by the Customs Administration.

The following shall be liable to the imposition of a pecuniary penalty of one million Lebanese pounds:

Failure to submit the original invoice specified in Article 28 or failure to submit a certified true copy thereof authenticated by the entity that issued it, subject, where applicable, to the application of the penalties imposed in the event of submitting false declarations or false documents.

1 - The Customs Administration may not, in principle, sell the goods seized in its possession on account of their contravention of the Customs Law or customs regulations, unless they become its property either pursuant to a final judgment ordering confiscation or pursuant to the abandonment contained in the settlement concluded with the offenders and after the approval of the competent authority specified in Article 387 of the Law.

2 - However, the Customs Administration is permitted, notwithstanding the provisions of the first paragraph above, and where it is impossible to notify the party concerned, to proceed, prior to the judgment of the court, with the sale of perishable goods or means of transport, or goods subject to leakage, or animals, which are kept with the Customs following a dispute, if it is compelled to do so or if that is in the interest of the rightful owners.

3 - The sale shall take place by public auction after establishing the circumstances justifying it in a seizure report drawn up by the customs officers.

4 - If the court rules, after the sale, to return the sold goods, means of transport, or animals to the rightful owner, the proceeds of the sale shall be paid to him in cash after deducting the expenses.

5 - Sales carried out under the conditions provided for in this Article may not lead to the bringing of any action for damages against the Customs Administration except in the case where the Administration has committed a gross fault.

The sale of goods carried out by the Customs Administration covers the following categories:

1 - Confiscated goods and articles that have become the final property of the Customs.

2 - Perishable goods referred to in the preceding Article 434.

3 - Goods that have become the property of the Customs after their owners abandoned them in writing.

4 - Goods left with the Customs referred to in Article 435.

5 - Goods that have not been withdrawn from public warehouses, private warehouses, and specialised warehouses within the regulatory time limits and which are sold under the conditions provided for in Articles 207, 221 and 231.

1 - In application of paragraph (4) of Article 434, goods that have not been withdrawn from customs stores and premises, other than public warehouses and private and specialised warehouses, after the expiry of a time limit of six months and one day from their deposit therein, shall be considered goods abandoned in customs.

This time limit shall be reduced to three months and one day for goods deposited in the stores of Beirut International Airport and in the various passenger halls, and shall also be reduced to ten full days from the date of inspection for goods that have not been withdrawn from the inspection rooms in the various customs offices and posts.

2 - The goods mentioned in the first paragraph above may be sold before the expiry of the specified time limits if they are perishable or in a poor state of preservation or if signs of spoilage appear thereon, provided that the provisions of paragraphs (2), (3), (4) and (5) of Article 433 are applied thereto.

1 - Goods abandoned in customs shall remain at the responsibility of their owners, and any damage, spoilage or loss incurred thereby during the period of their abandonment shall not entitle them to claim damages for any reason whatsoever.

2 - The owners of the goods shall bear the expenses, of whatever kind, resulting from the abandonment of the goods in customs stores.

1 - The sale of goods carried out by the Customs Administration shall take place by public auction, with the exception of monopolised goods or absolutely prohibited goods such as arms, war ammunition, explosives, narcotics and similar banned substances other than those intended for pharmaceutical uses the sale of which is approved by the Ministry of Health.

2 - The goods shall be sold free of all duties and expenses owed thereon.

3 - The price of the goods shall be paid in cash, and the purchaser to whom the auction was awarded may dispose of the goods as if they were imported from abroad, and he shall have the right to assign to them all regimes permitted by the laws and regulations in force, subject to the lifting of restrictions thereon if any exist.

4 - Minor quantities of perishable foodstuffs where the proceeds of sale do not cover their expenses shall be exempted from the sale procedures and shall be delivered to hospitals or charitable institutions free of charge or shall be destroyed in a regular manner.

The Director General of Customs shall determine the conditions of application of this paragraph.

Related text: Exemption from sale procedures for minor quantities of perishable foodstuffs

The Director General of Customs shall, in principle, grant the authorisation for sale by public auction, and he may delegate this authorisation, by a decision issued by him, to the heads of regions, departments and brigades.

By way of derogation from the rules governing sale by public auction, tobacco products abandoned in Customs, or not withdrawn from warehouses, or which have become the property of the Administration by way of abandonment, as well as those seized thereof, shall be sold to the Régie Libanaise des Tabacs et Tombacs for re-exportation at prices determined by a decision of the Minister of Finance. However, if the tobacco products satisfy the regulatory conditions prescribed for importation, and the Régie wishes to place them into local consumption, there shall be added to the sale price the customs duties and the other duties and taxes the collection of which is entrusted to the Customs Administration.

1 - By way of derogation from the legal provisions in force, customs sales shall be announced to the public, at the option of the Customs Administration, by a notice published in one or several newspapers or posted on the doors of the Customs premises. The publication or posting of the notice must precede the sale by at least ten clear days. This time limit may be reduced, and this matter shall be left to the discretion of the Customs Administration in the event of the sale of perishable goods. It shall also be permissible to suffice with announcing the sale on the door of the customs office if the goods to be sold are of negligible value. The sale shall take place at the premises and under the conditions specified in the published or posted notice.

2 - The Service shall, prior to initiating the procedures for the sale of abandoned goods or goods not withdrawn from customs warehouses within the regulatory time limit, send a notification thereof to their owners in order to enable them to withdraw their goods should they so wish.

Where it is not possible to notify the owners of the abandoned goods individually, for justified reasons, the notification shall be sent to the shipping agencies if they have not issued delivery orders for those goods.

Where it appears that those agencies have given delivery orders for the goods and that the addresses of their owners are unknown, the notification shall be made collectively by publication in one or several newspapers or by posting on the doors of the Customs premises.

1 - The determination of the reserve price of the goods shall be left to the discretion of the Customs Administration and, in principle, this price may not be lower than the amount of the duty if the goods are subject to a specific duty. The Customs Administration shall have the right, when circumstances so require, to authorise the sale of the goods even if the price offered does not equal the amount of the duties payable; in this case, the entire proceeds of the sale, after deduction of the privileged expenses, shall be allocated to the recovery of the duties. If no buyers come forward for these goods after two consecutive offerings for sale under the conditions provided for in the two preceding paragraphs, the Customs Administration shall have the right to offer these goods for sale to a public administration, a public institution, or a municipality at the highest price offered in either of the two auctions, or at the minimum price fixed by the Customs Administration in the second offering in the event that no one came forward to bid, by way of publication in the Official Gazette and in two local newspapers at least one month before the date of the sale. If no public administration, public institution, or municipality comes forward to purchase these goods, the Customs Administration may place them into its own use. If the goods are of a perishable nature and it proves impossible to sell them in accordance with what is set out above, the Director General of Customs shall have the right to authorise their destruction, in which case an official report of such destruction shall be drawn up. However, if the goods consist of foodstuffs fit for human consumption or of other categories whose condition permits their use or consumption in hospitals and charitable institutions, destruction may be replaced by delivering them to one of these entities free of charge, by a decision of the Director General of Customs, after obtaining the necessary visas. An official report of the delivery and receipt operation shall be drawn up and signed by the Service and the receiving entity.

2 - If the goods are of a kind prohibited from being placed into consumption, and the Administration has been unable to sell them for re-exportation, they may be placed into use for the benefit of the Customs Brigade, the Army, the Internal Security Forces, General Security, or State Security, following the approval of the Minister of Finance. An official report of delivery and receipt shall be drawn up and signed by the Service and the using entity.

In principle, the legal provisions in force relating to the adjournment of sales and to reckless bidding (folle enchère) shall apply to customs sales, and the Customs Administration itself shall undertake the modification or adjournment of the sales in place of the Execution Offices.

The proceeds of the sales shall be allocated as follows:

- If the goods sold are abandoned, the balance of the sale price, after deducting the privileged debts, shall be deposited in the Sundry Deposits Account to be delivered to its owner if he claims it within the year commencing from the date of the day of the sale, and if it is not claimed within this period, the proceeds of the sale shall finally revert to the Treasury.

- If the goods sold are relinquished to the Customs Administration, the proceeds of the sale shall be credited to the account of the Treasury.

- If the goods sold are confiscated for the account of the Customs, the proceeds of the sale shall be credited to the account of the case.

The Customs Law promulgated by Decision No. 422, dated 30/06/1954 and its amendments, is hereby repealed, as are repealed all provisions, regulations, decisions and administrative instructions contrary to this Law or inconsistent with the provisions thereof.

The proceeds of the sale shall be distributed in accordance with the following order:

1 - Expenses of whatever kind incurred by the Administration.

2 - Customs duties, and these duties shall be calculated under the conditions mentioned in Article 445.

3 - Other duties and taxes according to their priority in the date of promulgation of the legislation specific thereto.

4 - Storage and porterage fees.

5 - Freight charges and specified expenses that accompany the goods and are recorded on the documents pertaining thereto.

By way of derogation from the aforementioned order:

a - The costs of transporting the goods prepared for sale and the costs of porterage in the sales room at the Port of Beirut shall be privileged and their rank shall come before the customs duties.

b - The customs duties upon the sale of goods to which have not been withdrawn from private warehouses in shall be deducted from the proceeds of the sale before expenses of all kinds.

By way of exception to the provisions of the preceding Article, if the Customs Administration is unable, following a seizure carried out outside the customs offices, to reward the informants or the seizing officers, in a satisfactory manner, from the proceeds of the pecuniary penalty, it may, in order to achieve this purpose, conduct the sale with exemption from duties after its confiscation of the goods, the means of transport, and the objects used to conceal the fraud.

The proceeds of this sale shall be distributed pursuant to a special measure by the competent authority in accordance with the provisions of Article 387.

Specific customs duties shall be levied in accordance with the rules of Article 13 to the extent permitted by the proceeds of the sale. However, if the sold goods are subject to an ad valorem duty, this duty shall be levied on the basis of the sale price.

Goods sold in customs shall be subject to the duties in force on the day of the sale unless these goods are the subject of an unpaid declaration of entry into consumption, in which case the duties in force on the date of registration of this declaration shall be levied and on the basis of the value declared therein.

Sales shall take place under the supervision of a committee composed of customs officers that also includes a delegate from the local Chamber of Commerce, or, in the absence thereof, a delegate from the local authority (the municipality or the mukhtar). If this delegate is absent, it shall be mentioned in the minutes of the sale report that he was duly summoned, and he shall be dispensed with. In Beirut, the committee shall be assisted by an employee from the Gestión et Exploitation du Port de Beyrouth (Administration and Exploitation of the Port of Beirut) assigned to deliver the goods. If the sales take place in post offices, the committee shall be assisted by an employee from the Ministry of Telecommunications. The members of the committee may not enter the bidding themselves or through others or through figureheads or in their capacity as proxies, under penalty of nullity of the sale, irrespective of the penalties provided for in the legal provisions in force.

On Limited Liability Companies

A limited liability company is a commercial company formed by one partner or several partners who bear losses only to the extent of their contributions.

In the case of a company incorporated by a single person, such person shall be called the "Single Partner". The Single Partner shall exercise the powers vested in the assembly of partners.
A Title Seven under the heading "Limited Liability Companies" shall be added to Book Two of the Code of Commerce, comprising the following provisions:

A limited liability company shall be subject to the commercial laws and customs and to the provisions set forth in this Legislative Decree.

Such company shall be evidenced by an authentic instrument or an instrument under private signature and shall be registered in the Commercial Register.
This Legislative Decree shall be published and notified where needed and shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Such company is prohibited from evidencing the shares of partners by negotiable instruments, whether registered, to order, or to bearer, and is likewise prohibited from issuing for its own account by way of public subscription any transferable securities, shares, debentures, founders' shares, or the like.

The object of such company may not be the carrying out of insurance, capitalisation, savings, regular air transport projects, banking operations, or the investment of capital for the account of third parties.

Such company shall be formed by one person, designated as the Single Partner, or more, provided that the number of partners does not exceed twenty except in the case of transmission of shares by inheritance.

However, if the number of partners exceeds thirty, the company must, within a period of two years, be converted into a joint-stock company, failing which it must be dissolved.

The right to request the dissolution of the company for the reason set out in the preceding paragraph shall lapse if the cause thereof ceases to exist within the prescribed period.

In the event that all the shares are held by one of the partners in a limited liability company, this shall not result in the dissolution or termination of the company.

A limited liability company formed by a single partner may not be the single partner in another limited liability company.

In the event of a breach of the provisions of paragraph five above by reason of all the shares being held by a single partner in a multi-partner company, the single partner must regularise the offending situation within a period of one year, and any interested party may request dissolution after the lapse of one year from the holding of all the shares together.

In all cases, the court may grant a period of 6 months in order to regularise the situation, and the right to request the dissolution of the company shall lapse if the cause ceases to exist within the prescribed period.

The company shall be named according to the object of its enterprise or by adopting a common business name including the name of one or more of the partners. The following phrase must be clearly mentioned beside the name of the company in all papers, advertisements, publications and all other documents issued by the company: "Limited Liability Company" or "L.L.C.", with an indication of the amount of its capital and the registration number in the Commercial Register.

Violation of the preceding provisions shall be punished by a fine ranging between the equivalent of the official minimum wage and double thereof.

If this violation results in deceiving third parties as to the type of the company, the provisions relating to general partnerships may be applied to determine the obligations of the partners.

The capital of the limited liability company may not be less than five million Lebanese pounds, and the capital, whatever its amount, shall be divided into equal shares.

If the capital decreases for any reason whatsoever below five million Lebanese pounds, it must, within a period of one year, be completed or the company converted into another type with the exception of the joint-stock company. If the company fails to fulfil one of these two obligations, any interested party may request its judicial dissolution after serving a formal notice upon its manager in order to regularise its status.

The company shall not be deemed definitively constituted except after the distribution of the shares among the partners and the determination of the number of shares of each of them, or the restriction thereof to the sole partner, the payment of their value in full, and the deposit of the paid amounts in a bank.

The founders must expressly declare in the articles of association of the company that all these conditions have been fulfilled.

The manager of the company may not withdraw the deposited amounts prior to the registration of the company in the Commercial Register.

If this registration is not completed within a period of six months from the date of the first deposit, each of the partners may apply to the Judge of Urgent Matters requesting authorisation to recover what he has paid.

The contributions of the partners may be in cash or in kind, and the inclusion of the hire of service or industry among the contributions is prohibited.

Where there are contributions in kind, the value of these contributions must be determined in the articles of association of the company, and recourse must be had to the opinion of one or several experts appointed by the President of the Court of First Instance in the district of the head office of the company in order to verify the accuracy of the determination of such value.

Where there is a plurality of partners, the report of the experts shall be placed at the disposal of the prospective partners, and the latter shall be entitled to withdraw from their undertaking to enter into partnership if the valuation of the contributions by the partner exceeds the value estimated by the expert or experts by more than twenty per cent.

The makers of contributions in kind, the first managers and the experts shall be jointly and severally liable towards third parties, for a period of five years from the date of incorporation, for the inaccuracy of the valuation of the value of the said contributions at the time of incorporation of the company.

Every new partner who approves a balance sheet or an annual inventory that fixes the value of the contributions or of other new contributions at more than they are in reality shall be subject to the same liability, for a period of five years from the date of the balance sheet or inventory.
Save for the obligation to register limited liability companies in the competent register, a limited liability company shall not be subject upon incorporation to any other rules of publication.

Every limited liability company incorporated contrary to the conditions set forth in the preceding Articles shall be deemed null and void and of no effect as between the partners; however, neither the sole partner nor the partners may invoke its nullity against third parties.

When the nullity of the company is declared pursuant to the provisions of the preceding Article, the sole partner and the partners who caused the nullity, the first managers and the founders shall be jointly and severally liable towards third parties and towards the other partners for the damage resulting from the nullity.

An action for nullity shall not be heard if the cause thereof has ceased to exist prior to the institution of the action. It shall remain possible to remove such cause during the trial and prior to the issuance of the judgment.

In the event of a plurality of partners, and if the removal of the nullity requires convening the assembly of partners, the proceedings in the action for nullity shall be stayed as from the date on which that assembly is duly convened until its resolution is issued.

Actions for nullity and for liability shall be subject to limitation under the conditions prescribed for the nullity of a joint-stock company.

The shares of the sole partner or of the partners shall pass by inheritance to their heirs. However, in the event of a plurality of partners, it may be stipulated, by an express clause in the instrument of incorporation, that the company is given the option not to admit the heirs or some of them as partners and to pay out to those heirs their rights, which shall be determined amicably or through the courts. Provided that the period for exercising the option may not exceed two months from the date of death.

The company shall not be dissolved by the bankruptcy or interdiction of the sole partner or of one of the partners, and in each of these two cases his legal representative shall take his place.

The assignment of shares in the company shall be evidenced by an authentic or private deed notified to the manager of the company and to each of the partners.

The company shall have a right of pre-emption to purchase all the shares intended to be assigned to a person from outside the partners, provided that it expresses its desire to purchase within a period of fifteen days from its notification, through any of its managers, of the draft assignment, which shall mandatorily include the name of the prospective purchaser, the conditions of sale, and the price, and provided that it exercises its right to purchase within fifteen days from the date of expressing its desire.

In the event that the company does not exercise this right within the period mentioned above, any of the partners may purchase all the shares within a period of thirty days from the date of his notification of the company's refusal to exercise the right, provided that the manager of the company supplies all the partners with a copy of the draft assignment. In the event that more than one partner exercises this right, the shares shall be distributed among them, each in proportion to his participation in the capital of the company.

In any event, shares in the company may not be assigned to a third party thereto except with the approval of partners representing at least three quarters of the capital.

The provisions of this Article shall not apply in the case where there is a sole partner.

The management of the company shall be entrusted to the sole partner or to one or several managers from among the partners or others, appointed by the articles of association of the company or by a subsequent instrument for a limited or unlimited period, provided that they are natural persons.

The manager or managers shall be vested with all the powers necessary to conduct the business of the company in a regular manner, unless otherwise provided in the articles of association.

Notwithstanding any clause to the contrary, the managers or some of them may be dismissed by a decision of the sole partner or of the assembly of partners, or by a judicial decision where there is a legitimate reason justifying such dismissal.

If the sole partner decides or if the assembly of partners decides to dismiss a manager without a legitimate reason, the latter shall be entitled to claim damages.
The managers shall deduct every year ten per cent of the net profits to form a reserve fund equivalent to fifty per cent of the capital.

The manager, and the managers where there are several of them, and the sole partner or the partners, shall be prohibited, under penalty of nullity, from obtaining from the company loans, guarantees, or endorsements for themselves or for their spouses, ascendants, or descendants, even if obtained under assumed names.

Managers shall be liable individually or jointly and severally, as the case may be, towards the company and third parties for their contravention of the provisions of this Legislative Decree and the provisions of the company's articles of association, and for their faults in management.

If several managers participate in the same acts that expose them to liability, the court shall determine the proportion of compensation for the damage to be borne by each of them.

The sole partner or any of the partners shall have the right to bring the liability action against the managers in the interest of the company in order to claim full compensation for the damage caused to it.

Any clause in the memorandum of association that would make the right to bring this action conditional upon a prior opinion or authorisation from the meeting of partners, or constitute an advance waiver of the exercise of this right, shall be deemed unwritten.

No effect shall be given to any resolution issued by the meeting of partners to extinguish a liability action brought against the managers on account of their faults relating to management.

The right to bring the liability actions provided for in Article 19 shall lapse after the expiry of five years from the date of the harmful acts upon which they are based if they were apparent, or from the date of their discovery if they were concealed. However, if one of these acts constitutes a felony, the right to bring an action shall not lapse until after the expiry of ten years from its occurrence.

At the end of each year, the manager or managers shall draw up a report on the operations of the company in that year and the financial statements, notify them to the partners, and convene them within six months from the closing of the accounts of the year to a general meeting during which the acts of the managers shall be approved.

At least twenty days before the time appointed for the holding of the meeting of partners, the original of all the documents specified in the preceding paragraph shall be deposited at the head office of the company, together with the report of the auditor, where one exists, and each partner shall have the right to inspect them and to address written questions to the manager to be answered by him at the session of the meeting.

Each partner may, moreover, request whenever he wishes to inspect the entries and documents relating to the operations of the three preceding years.

Any clause contrary to this Article shall be deemed unwritten.

Resolutions shall be taken at the sessions held by the partners. However, pursuant to a clause in the articles of association, it may be agreed to permit the issuance of resolutions, with the exception of those relating to the application of the provisions of Article 21, by way of written consultations.

Where there is a plurality of them, the partners shall be convened to the general meetings by a notice published in two local daily newspapers, or by registered letters, or by any other means specified in the articles of association of the company.

The notice of convocation shall be addressed to the partners at least fifteen days prior to the time fixed for the meeting, unless the articles of association of the company provide otherwise.

The notice of convocation shall be addressed by the manager or by any of the managers where there is a plurality of them, failing which, by the supervisory commissioner, where one exists; upon the default of all of the foregoing, any one or more partners representing at least one quarter of the capital shall have the right to apply to the courts to appoint a person to convene the general meeting and draw up its agenda.

Every clause contrary to these provisions shall be deemed unwritten.

Every partner may participate in the general meetings with a number of votes equal to the number of shares which he owns or represents, and in the absence of a clause to the contrary in the constitutive articles, a partner may not appoint a person other than one of the partners as proxy to represent him.

A partner may not appoint another person as proxy to represent him in respect of part of his shares while personally representing the remaining shares. Every clause contrary to the provisions of this article shall be deemed unwritten.

In the general meetings or in written consultations, resolutions shall be adopted by partners representing at least half of the capital. If this majority is not attained, and unless there is a provision to the contrary in the articles of association of the company, the partners shall be convened or consulted a second time, and resolutions shall be passed by a majority of the votes cast, regardless of the proportion of the capital which they represent.

Where the company comprises only a "sole partner", he shall sign the resolutions alone.

Resolutions relating to the financial statements shall be recorded in minutes registered in the Commercial Register.

The nationality of the company may not be changed, nor may a partner be compelled to increase his contributions or his obligations, except by the unanimous consent of the partners.

Nor may any amendment be introduced to the articles of association of the company unless a majority of the partners representing at least three quarters of the capital is secured.

In the event of an increase of the capital by way of subscription by the partners for cash shares, the subscription amounts must be deposited in a bank, and the manager of the company may not withdraw them until the shares have been paid up in full and the capital increase has been registered in the Commercial Register.

If such registration is not effected within a period of six months from the date of deposit of the first amount, the provisions of the last paragraph of the eighth article of this Legislative Decree shall apply.

If the increase of the capital is effected, wholly or in part, by way of contributions in kind, the provisions of the ninth and tenth articles of this Legislative Decree shall apply, and such increase shall be registered in the Commercial Register.

The assembly of partners, by its majority specified for amending the articles of association, may resolve to reduce the capital without any prejudice to the equality of the partners.

Where there is an auditor, the latter must be notified of the draft reduction of the capital so as to give his opinion on the reasons for this measure and its conditions when the assembly is held.

If the assembly resolves to approve the reduction of the capital for a reason other than losses, its resolution shall be registered in the Commercial Register and published in two local newspapers, and every creditor shall have the right to object thereto within two months from the date of the last publication formality before the court of the company's head office, which shall decide, according to the circumstances, either to dismiss the objection, or to compel the company to provide guarantees for the rights of the objectors which it determines in its decision. The formalities of reducing the capital may not be commenced before the expiry of the time-limit for objection.

The company is prohibited from purchasing its own shares. However, the assembly which resolved to reduce the capital for a reason other than losses may authorise its manager to purchase a specific number of the partners' shares for the purpose of cancelling them.

The provisions of Articles 21, 23, 26 and 29 shall not apply if the company is composed of a sole partner. In this case, the manager shall draw up a report on the business of the company and its annual financial statements. And the sole partner shall approve the accounts of the company, after taking cognizance of the report of the auditor, where one exists, within a time-limit of six months from the end of the financial year.

The sole partner may not delegate his powers as a partner to third parties.

Limited Liability Companies

The partners may appoint one or more auditors by a resolution adopted by the majority specified in Article 25 of this Legislative Decree.

Such appointment shall be mandatory:

a- If the number of partners exceeds twenty.

b- If the capital of the company reaches thirty million Lebanese Pounds.

c- If the appointment of the auditor is requested by one or more partners representing at least one-fifth of the capital.

When the company is composed of a sole partner, the appointment of the auditor shall be mandatory if the capital of the company reaches thirty million Pounds.

Shall be punished by the penalties for fraud:

- The founders who included in the company's articles of association a false declaration regarding the distribution of shares among the partners and the paying up of these shares.

- The initial partners and the managers who opened, directly or through third parties, a public subscription for any transferable security, shares or debentures.

- Any person who gives to contributions in kind, by means of fraudulent manoeuvres, a valuation exceeding their real value by twenty per cent.

- Any manager who distributes fictitious dividends to the partners in the absence of a balance sheet and a profit and loss account, or by means of a balance sheet and a profit and loss account that are inconsistent with reality.

- The managers and partners who create or attempt to create an artificial majority in a meeting of partners.

- The manager who withdraws the contributions deposited in a bank before the completion of the incorporation.

The provisions of this Article shall not preclude the application of the provisions on ideal concurrence of offences to give the acts provided for therein a more severe qualification, particularly in the event of bankruptcy.

Limited Liability Companies

The auditor shall be chosen from among the persons registered on the roll of experts.

The following shall not be appointed as auditors:

1- The partners, the sole partner, the managers, and their spouses, ascendants, and descendants.

2- Persons who receive periodic remuneration from the company or from its manager, and their spouses, ascendants, and descendants. Within five years from the termination of the functions of the auditors, such auditors may not be appointed as managers of the company whose operations they audited. Nor may they, within the same period, be appointed as managers, members of the board of directors, or auditors of companies holding ten per cent of the capital of the company in which they were auditors, or in whose capital the latter holds ten per cent. The provisions applicable to joint-stock companies shall apply to the auditors to the extent that they are compatible with the specific provisions set forth in this Legislative Decree.

Dividends distributed to the partners may be recovered when they are not based on real profits actually realised.

The action for recovery shall be subject to a five-year limitation period from the date of the day fixed for the distribution of the dividends.

In the event of the loss of three-quarters of the capital, the partners must decide, within a period of four months following the approval of the accounts that revealed such loss, whether the company should be dissolved. If they do not decide to dissolve it by the majority prescribed for amending the articles of association, they shall immediately be required to reduce the capital by the amount of the loss, unless such majority decides to reconstitute the capital as it was.

The decision adopting any of the aforementioned solutions shall be published in two local newspapers and registered in the Commercial Register.

If the partners do not issue their decision within the period prescribed in the first paragraph, every interested party shall have the right to apply for the judicial dissolution of the company.

The transformation of a limited liability company into a general partnership, a simple limited partnership, or a partnership limited by shares requires the unanimity of the partners.

Its transformation into a joint-stock company, however, may be decided by the majority prescribed for amending the articles of association, provided that the partners have approved the accounts of the two preceding years.

If it appears from the accounts of the company, after their approval, that the value of its net assets exceeds fifty million pounds, the majority representing half of the capital may decide to transform the company into a joint-stock company, after reviewing the report of the auditor certifying the accuracy of the accounts.

A change in the type of the company effected in violation of the provisions of this Article shall be null and void.
The urgent bill referred to the Chamber of Deputies pursuant to Decree No. 12825 dated 21 May 1963 is hereby put into effect, the text of which reads as follows:
This Decree shall be published in the Official Gazette.
The monetary unit of the Lebanese Republic is the Lebanese Pound and its official abbreviation is L.L.
The law shall determine the value of the Lebanese Pound in fine gold.

The Pound shall be divided into one hundred equal parts called piastres. The official abbreviation of the Lebanese piastre is P.-L.

The piastre shall be divided into one hundred equal parts called centimes.

Currency tokens shall be divided into:

a - Banknotes the value of which is equal to or exceeds the monetary unit

b - Metallic coins the value of which is equal to one Pound - one hundred Pounds - two hundred and fifty Pounds - five hundred Pounds. Gold coins may also be issued when the law authorises the redemption of the value of banknotes in gold. The characteristics of the gold coins and the conditions of their issue shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.

Banknotes may be issued in denominations of one Pound, five Pounds, fifty Pounds, one hundred Pounds, two hundred and fifty Pounds, five hundred Pounds, one thousand Pounds, five thousand Pounds, ten thousand Pounds, fifty thousand Pounds, and one hundred thousand Pounds.

Fractional notes and coins may be in denominations of:

one piastre - two and a half piastres - five piastres - ten piastres - twenty-five piastres - fifty piastres - one Pound - five Pounds - ten Pounds - twenty-five Pounds - fifty Pounds - one hundred Pounds - two hundred and fifty Pounds - five hundred Pounds.
Banknotes whose value equals five hundred pounds and above shall have unlimited legal tender power in the territories of the Lebanese Republic.

The legal tender power of small money is the following:

a - Two pounds for coins whose nominal value equals 10 piastres or less than 10 piastres.

b - Ten pounds for notes or coins of 25 piastres.

c - Twenty pounds for notes or coins of 50 piastres.

d - One thousand pounds for notes and for coins whose value equals one pound - five pounds - ten pounds - twenty-five pounds - and fifty pounds.

e - Five thousand pounds for notes and for coins whose value equals two hundred and fifty pounds.
The currency issuing institution and the public treasuries shall accept small banknotes and small metal coins without any limitation as to their amount.
The issue of currency is an exclusive privilege of the State. The State may grant this privilege to a central bank that it establishes.

It is prohibited to issue or put into circulation or accept:

- All tokens denominated in Lebanese currency for their use as means of payment instead of the monetary tokens authorised by law.

- All bearer debt instruments not bearing interest, even if they are denominated in a currency other than the Lebanese currency.
A central bank is established under the name of "Bank of Lebanon" and is referred to hereinafter as "the Bank" or "the Central Bank".

"The Bank" is a legal person of public law and enjoys financial autonomy.

It is considered a merchant in its relations with third parties. It conducts its operations and organises its accounts in accordance with commercial and banking rules and with commercial and banking custom.

It is not subject to the rules of administration and management of business and to the controls to which public sector institutions are subject, and in particular to the provisions of Legislative Decrees No. 114, 115, 117 and 118 dated 12 June 1959. The provisions of the Code of Commerce relating to registration in the Trade Register shall not apply to it.

The courts of Beirut alone shall have jurisdiction to hear all disputes between the Bank and third parties.

The head office of the Bank is Beirut.

"The Bank" shall establish branches for itself in Tripoli, Sidon and Zahle.

It may establish branches in other places in Lebanon and close such of these branches as it deems to have become useless, and it may also appoint for itself representatives and agents in Lebanon and abroad.

The capital of "the Bank" shall consist of an amount allocated to it by the State in the value of (15000000) fifteen million Lebanese Pounds.

The capital may be increased either by a new amount allocated by the State pursuant to a law, or by the incorporation of reserve funds authorised by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the request of "the Bank" or the proposal of the Minister of Finance.
"The Bank" shall not be dissolved except pursuant to a law determining, where necessary, the methods of its liquidation.

The management of "the Bank" shall be ensured by a Governor assisted by a First Vice-Governor and a Second Vice-Governor.

And a Third Vice-Governor and a Fourth Vice-Governor and by a Central Council hereinafter referred to as "the Council".

The Governor shall be appointed for six years by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

The Vice-Governors shall be appointed for five years by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers adopted upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance and the consultation of the Governor, and they shall exercise the functions assigned to them by the Governor.

The Governor and his Vice-Governors must possess the university degrees, experience, and moral qualities required for the exercise of their functions.

The term of office of the Governor and the Vice-Governors may be renewed once or several times.

The Governor and the Vice-Governors shall take an oath, before the President of the Republic, to perform their functions with loyalty and precision, respecting the law and honour.

Save in the case of voluntary resignation, the Governor may not be dismissed from his office except for medically proven incapacity established in accordance with the rules, or for breach of the duties of his office within the meaning of Chapter One of Title Three of the Penal Code, or for violation of the provisions of Article 20, or for gross fault in the conduct of business.

The Vice-Governors may not be dismissed from their office except for the same reasons enumerated in the preceding paragraph, upon the proposal of the Governor or after seeking his opinion.

The Governor and the Vice-Governors must devote themselves entirely to the Bank. They may not combine their functions with any parliamentary membership, or public office, or any activity in any enterprise of whatever nature, or any professional work, whether such activity or work is remunerated or unremunerated.

It shall be prohibited for them during their term of office to retain, take, or receive any interest in a private enterprise.

Every participation or association in any form or by any means whatsoever, even by way of a simple loan, shall be considered an interest within the meaning of the preceding paragraph. The holding of a portfolio of securities issued by joint-stock companies shall not be considered an "interest".

No commitment bearing the signature of the Governor or the Vice-Governors may be accepted in the portfolio of "the Bank".

The Governor, and the Vice-Governors subject to his approval, shall be entitled, notwithstanding the first paragraph of the preceding Article,

- to be appointed to committees formed by the Government.

- to be appointed as governors or members of the board of directors of the International Monetary Fund, of the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development, or of any other international institution of which Lebanon is a member.

- to represent Lebanon at international conferences.
The emoluments of the Governor and of the Vice-Governors shall be determined in the special rules provided for in Article 33.

The Governor and the Vice-Governors may not, for a period of two years from the date of termination of their functions at the Central Bank, enter the board of directors of any bank or any financial institution subject to this Law, or of any institution controlled by the said bank or financial institution, nor hold any office therein or participate therein in any manner whatsoever.

In the event of termination of the services of the Governor or of the Vice-Governors due to duly established physical incapacity, or to a resignation accepted by the Government, or to the non-renewal of the term of office, or in the event of death, an indemnity equal to two years of their salaries shall be paid to them or to their heirs.
In the event of vacancy in the post of Governor, the First Vice-Governor shall assume the functions of the Governor pending the appointment of a new Governor.

The Governor shall enjoy the broadest powers for the general management of the Bank and the conduct of its affairs. He is charged with the implementation of this Law and the resolutions of the Council.

He is the legal representative of the Bank; he signs on behalf of the Bank all instruments, contracts and agreements, authorises the institution of all legal proceedings and takes all enforcement or conservatory measures as he deems fit, including real estate securities.

He organises the departments of the Bank and defines their tasks, appoints and dismisses the employees of the Bank of all ranks, and may contract with technicians either in the capacity of advisers, or for study assignments, or to complete the vocational training of the employees of the Bank.

None of the foregoing is exhaustive in character.

In the event of the absence or impediment of the Governor, he shall be replaced by the First Vice-Governor and, in the event of the impediment of the First, by the Second Vice-Governor, in accordance with the conditions determined by the Governor.

The Governor may delegate the entirety of his powers to the person replacing him.

The Council shall consist of:

- the Governor, as Chairman.

- the Vice-Governors,

- the Director-General of the Ministry of Finance.

- the Director-General of the Ministry of National Economy, and these last two members may not act within the Council as delegates of the Government.

They shall exercise at the Bank only the functions inherent in their capacity as members of the Central Council.

They shall take before the President of the Republic the same oath as that taken by the Governor and the Vice-Governors.
The Council shall meet whenever convened by the Governor, and at least once every month. The Minister of Finance may also request the Governor to convene the Council to a meeting.
The Central Council may meet neither in the absence of the Governor or his deputy nor in the absence of the Director General of Finance or the Director General of National Economy.

The presence of at least four members is necessary for the validity of deliberations. Decisions shall be taken by a majority of the votes of the members present. In the event of an equality of votes, the Governor shall have a casting vote.

The Council may, at the request of one of its members, if it considers such request to be sufficiently reasoned, suspend the execution of a decision for three days at most. A new deliberation on the suspended matter shall take place within the specified time limit. The decision taken at the new meeting may be put into execution.

(As amended by Law No. 8/75 dated 5/3/1975, Official Gazette No. 21):

The Council, within the scope of the powers granted to the Bank pursuant to this Law, shall enjoy in particular the following powers, without this enumeration having an exhaustive character:

1 - It determines the monetary and credit policy of the Bank.

2 - It establishes the regulations for the implementation of this Law.

3 - It determines, in the light of economic conditions, the discount rate and the interest rate on the Bank's advances and deliberates on all measures relating to banks.

4 - And it deliberates on the establishment and organisation of clearing houses.

5 - And it deliberates on matters relating to currency issue.

6 - And it deliberates on loan applications submitted in the public sector.

7 - It establishes all other regulations relating to the operations of the Bank.

8 - It deliberates on matters relating to the immovable properties of the Bank, or its real rights, and it also deliberates on the lifting of real estate attachments, objections or real estate mortgages, and on the waiver of privileges or rights, and on draft arbitrations and settlements relating to the interests of the Bank.

9 - It establishes the special regulations relating to the Governor and the Deputy Governors provided for in Article 22 and the general regulations for the employees of the Bank. These two sets of regulations must be accompanied by the approval of the Minister of Finance.

The employees of the Bank shall be appointed in accordance with the rules of private law; however, they are prohibited from joining political parties and from combining work at the Bank with parliamentary, municipal and mukhtar elective offices, and they are also prohibited from holding positions as members of boards of directors in companies.

The payment of any remuneration or any allowances in any form of commission or proportional allowances on the basis of the Bank's revenues or profits is prohibited.

10 - The Council approves the expenditure budget of the Bank and introduces thereto, during the year, the necessary amendments.

11 - It also closes the accounts of the financial year.

12 - It approves the draft annual report which the Governor must address to the Minister of Finance in accordance with the provisions of Article 117.

The mission allowance of the Director General of Finance and the Director General of National Economy shall be determined by decree and paid by the Bank.

This allowance shall not be subject to the provisions of Article 27 of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12 June 1959.

An Advisory Committee shall be established at the Central Bank, composed of six members:

1 - Four chosen in view of their experience in the banking, commercial, industrial, and agricultural fields.

To this end, a list of five to ten qualified persons shall be submitted to the Minister of Finance by the bodies representing each of the banking, commercial, industrial, and agricultural sectors, and from each of the four lists one person shall be chosen to be appointed as a member of the Advisory Committee.

These members shall not be considered, and may not act within the Committee, as representatives or delegates of the interests of the sectors from which they were chosen.

2 - One chosen from the Planning Board.

3 - The sixth member shall be chosen from among university professors of economics of Lebanese nationality.

The members of the Committee shall be appointed by decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance after consulting the Council of the Central Bank. Their term of office shall be for two years.

It may be determined repeatedly, and the allowances for their mission shall be determined in agreement with the Minister of Finance and borne by the Bank.

The Committee shall itself establish its internal regulations.

The members shall take an oath before the President of the Republic to perform their duties faithfully and accurately, respecting the law and honour, and shall be bound by the obligation to preserve the banking secrecy imposed by Article 151 in conjunction with the Law issued on 3 September 1956 relating to Banking Secrecy (Paragraph added by the Law put into effect by Decree No. 6102 dated 5/10/1973 - Official Gazette No. 81 Supplement).
The Bank shall provide the Committee with its premises and the secretariat required for it.

The Governor may consult the Committee on matters of a general nature and on matters relating to monetary and credit policy, and he may also seek its enlightenment regarding the measures which he intends to take and on which he deems it appropriate to know the Committee's point of view.

The Committee may:

a - Submit to the Governor studies on the economic situation in general, or on the economic situation in a specific region or in a specific sector, and submit proposals to him in this regard.

b - Submit proposals aimed at developing deposits, reducing the hoarding of banknotes, expanding the use of deposits, and mobilising the ready funds of individuals for the public interest.

c - Propose all necessary measures to ensure the guarantee of bank deposits and the safety of invested funds.
Persons who hold parliamentary membership, civil servants, or the persons referred to in Article 127 may not be members of the Committee.

A "Government Commissariat to the Central Bank" shall be established in the Ministry of Finance. This service shall be directed by an official holding the rank of Director General who shall bear the title of Government Commissioner to the Central Bank.

The Commissioner shall be charged with:

a - Overseeing the application of this Law.

b - Supervising the accounting of the Bank, and he shall be assisted in this part of his mission by an official from his service belonging at least to the third category of the cadre of the Ministry of Finance.

The Government Commissariat to the Central Bank shall include, on the other hand, a research department for affairs relating to money and credit.

Decisions of the Council shall be notified immediately to the Commissioner, and he may, within the two days following notification, request the Governor to suspend any decision which he deems contrary to the law and the regulations and refer to the Minister of Finance in this regard; and if the matter is not decided upon within five days from the date of the suspension, the decision may be put into execution.

The Commissioner and his assistant, referred to in paragraph (b) of Article 42, shall have the right to inspect all registers of the Central Bank and its accounting documents, with the exception of the accounts and files of third parties protected by the banking secrecy established by the Law of 3 September 1956. They shall verify the cash offices of the Central Bank and its holdings, and they may not interfere, in any manner whatsoever, in the conduct of the operations of the Central Bank.

The Commissioner shall periodically inform the Minister of Finance and the Council of the supervisory operations he has carried out, and he shall also inform the Minister of Finance, after the closing of each financial year, of the mission he has performed during the elapsed year, by virtue of a report a copy of which he shall send to the Governor.

The organisation of the Government Commissariat to the Bank, the conduct of its operations, and its cadres shall be determined by decree; the special allowance which shall be granted to the Government Commissioner shall alone be borne by the Bank, and this allowance shall not be subject to Article 27 of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12 June 1959
The Bank of Lebanon, to the exclusion of all others, shall be granted the privilege of issuing currency provided for in the Tenth Article.

(As amended by Legislative Decree No. 31 dated 2/5/1977 - Official Gazette No. 12).

Banknotes the value of which is equal to or exceeds one pound shall bear the facsimile of the two signatures of the Governor of the Bank and the First Deputy Governor.

In the event that the First Governor assumes the functions of the Governor in accordance with the provisions of Article 25 of this Law, the banknotes referred to in the preceding paragraph shall bear the facsimile of his signature and the facsimile of the signature of the Second Deputy Governor.
The Bank shall determine the size of the banknotes intended to be issued, their designs, their texts, and all their other characteristics.
The Bank shall inform the public of the types and characteristics of the notes that it intends to put into circulation.
The Bank may decide to withdraw one or several types of its banknotes from circulation in order to replace them with new types.

The notice informing the public of this decision must specify the period during which the notes decided to be replaced may be presented to one of the teller offices of the Bank.
