After the expiry of this period, the Bank shall only exchange the notes decided to be replaced at its central teller office in Beirut.

Three years after the expiry of the period provided for in the first paragraph of the preceding Article, the Bank shall credit the value of the notes decided to be withdrawn and which have not been presented for replacement to a reserve account, from which the value of the notes that will be replaced thereafter shall be drawn.
Notes whose value has been credited to the reserve account provided for in the preceding Article shall be deducted from the value of the notes issued.

Seven years after the expiry of the period specified in Article 53, the right of replacement shall lapse and the balance of the reserve account shall be transferred to the special account provided for in Article 115.
The Bank shall not be obliged to pay the value of destroyed or lost notes, nor to accept counterfeit notes or reimburse their value.

The Bank shall pay the value of mutilated notes provided that the surface area of the fragment presented is greater than half of the note and that it contains all the markings necessary for its identification.
No opposition may be notified to the Bank on the occasion of the loss or theft of banknotes.
The Bank may issue small banknotes or fractional coins of silver or of any other metal.
Small banknotes shall bear the facsimile signature of the Chief Cashier of the Bank.

The Bank shall determine the dimensions, designs and texts of the small banknotes, the dimensions, weight, fineness and tolerance in weight and fineness of the fractional coins, and all other characteristics of such notes and coins.
The Bank shall inform the public of the descriptions of the small notes and coins which it intends to put into circulation.

In the event of the withdrawal of one or several denominations of small notes or coins, their holders shall be granted a time limit of two years in order to exchange them at the counters of the Bank. Upon the expiry of this time limit, the right of exchange shall lapse and the notes or coins decided to be withdrawn shall cease to have any discharging power.
The value of unexchanged small notes and coins shall be transferred to the special account provided for in Article 115.
The provisions of Articles 56 and 57 shall apply to small-denomination banknotes.
Small-denomination coins which have become impossible to identify, or which have suffered loss of weight or defacement, shall neither be accepted nor reimbursed.
The provisions of Article 58 shall apply to small-denomination currency.

The Bank shall show in its balance sheets and in its statements of position, under two separate headings, the value of the banknotes it issues and the value of the small-denomination currency it issues.

(As amended by the Law put into effect by Decree No. 6102 dated 5/10/1973 - Official Gazette No. 81, Supplement):

- The Bank shall maintain in its assets funds in gold and foreign currencies ensuring the soundness of the coverage of the Lebanese currency equivalent to at least (30 per cent) thirty per cent of the value of the currency it has issued and the value of its demand deposits, provided that the ratio of the said gold and currencies shall not be less than (50 per cent) fifty per cent of the value of the currency issued.

The Bank's holdings of Lebanese currency shall not be taken into consideration for the calculation of the two ratios specified in the preceding paragraph.

(As amended by the Law put into effect by Decree No. 6102 dated 5/10/1973 - Official Gazette No. 81, Supplement):

- The general mission of the Bank is to safeguard the currency in order to secure the basis for sustained economic and social growth, and the mission of the Bank includes in particular the following:

- Safeguarding the soundness of the Lebanese currency.

- Safeguarding economic stability.

- Safeguarding the soundness of the conditions of the banking system.

- Developing the monetary and financial market.

- For this purpose, the Bank shall exercise the powers vested in it under this Law.

The Central Bank shall cooperate with the Government and shall tender to it all advice relating to financial and economic policy with a view to securing the greatest harmony between its mission and the objectives of the Government.

The Bank may propose to the Government such measures as it deems likely to have a beneficial effect on the balance of payments, price movements, public finance, and economic growth in general. The Bank shall apprise the Government of matters which it considers detrimental to the economy and the currency. And it shall ensure the Government's relations with international financial institutions.

The Government shall consult the Bank on matters relating to currency and shall invite the Governor of the Bank to participate in its deliberations on such matters.
Government departments, public sector institutions and mixed economy institutions shall provide to the Central Bank the statistics and information that it may need in its economic studies.

The Government shall ensure the safety and protection of the Bank's buildings and shall reinforce these buildings free of charge with sufficient guarding, and shall also provide the necessary guard for the safety of the transport of funds or valuables.

Amended by the Law promulgated by Decree No. 6102 dated 5/10/1973 - Official Gazette No. 81 Supplement):

- The Bank shall use the means that it deems capable of ensuring the stability of the exchange, and for that purpose it may in particular operate in the market, in agreement with the Minister of Finance, as a buyer or seller of gold or foreign currencies, subject to the provisions of Article 69.

The Bank's operations in foreign currencies shall be recorded in a special account called the "Exchange Stabilisation Fund".

(Amended by the Law enforced by Decree No. 6102 dated 5/10/1973 - Official Gazette No. 81, Supplement):

- In order to maintain harmony between banking liquidity and the volume of credit and its general mission provided for

in Article 70, the Central Bank is empowered to take all measures it deems appropriate, and in particular the following measures, which it may take individually, collectively, or

together with the measures provided for in Title Three of this Law:

a - Determining and modifying discount rates and their ceilings, as well as the rates of other credits it is authorised to grant to banks and financial institutions and their ceilings.

b - Resorting to the operations referred to in Article 75.

c - Purchasing and selling securities on the open market in accordance with Articles 106, 107 and 108.

The words "in Lebanese currency" were repealed from this paragraph by Law No. 28 dated 09/05/1967.

d - Obliging banks to deposit funds with it (a minimum reserve) up to a certain percentage of their liabilities arising from deposits and borrowed funds defined by "the Bank", with the exception of their liabilities of the same kind towards other banks that are also obliged to deposit these reserve funds.

The Central Bank may, if it deems fit, consider the banks' investments in government securities or securities issued with a government guarantee as part of the reserve up to a certain percentage, the determination of which is left to it.

The Central Bank may not set the minimum reserve ratio at more than 25 percent of demand liabilities and more than 15 percent of fixed-term liabilities.

The Central Bank may impose different percentages on different categories of banks' liabilities within the limits mentioned in the preceding paragraph.

It may also, in exceptional cases, impose special marginal ratios, without being bound by the aforementioned limits, on the amount by which these liabilities

or any categories thereof exceed a certain limit, or on the increase realised in these liabilities or in any categories thereof after a certain date.

e - Obliging banks to deposit funds with it (a special minimum reserve) up to a certain percentage of the assets defined by the Bank.

f - Accepting, in the light of the general monetary situation, deposits in return for interest determined by the Bank.

The monthly assets of a bank with the Central Bank (the actual reserve) must reach at least the percentages

that shall have been determined, of the monthly average of the liabilities subject to the obligation of establishing reserve funds (the compulsory reserve).

The Central Bank is entitled to levy, on the amount by which the actual reserve falls below the compulsory reserve, a penalty interest that may reach a rate exceeding by three points the rate applied at the time to its advances against financial securities. This shall not preclude the application of the administrative penalties provided for in Section Three of Title Four of this Law.

The Central Bank may refrain from applying this penalty if it appears to it that the shortfall was an inevitable consequence of unforeseen circumstances or if the bank in which the shortfall appeared is in a state of liquidation.
Banks shall be granted a time limit of at least 30 days to apply the instructions requiring the establishment of compulsory reserve funds or the modification of their rate.

(As amended by the Law put into effect by Decree No. 6102 dated 5/10/1973 - Official Gazette No. 81 Supplement):

- The Central Bank may also act to influence general credit conditions by limiting the volume of credit of certain types or granted for certain purposes or to certain sectors, and by regulating the conditions of such credit.
The Bank shall establish and organise clearing houses in cities wherever it deems this necessary.

(As amended by the Law promulgated by Decree No. 6102 dated 5/10/1973 - Official Gazette Issue 81 Supplement):

- The Bank is authorised:

1 - To buy, sell, import and export gold and other precious metals, and to carry out all other operations on these materials.

2 - To accept on deposit with it gold coins or gold bullion and to issue in favour of such depositors as request them gold deposit certificates in the form of bearer or order instruments.

3 - To discount, rediscount, buy and sell commercial bills, means of payment and call funds denominated in foreign currencies.

The maturity period of the bills must not exceed six months.

4 - To buy and sell debt securities issued or guaranteed by foreign governments or international institutions, which are denominated in foreign currencies and which are readily marketable.

5 - To maintain accounts with central banks or with correspondents abroad.

6 - To open accounts for central banks, foreign banks and international institutions and to act as correspondent for these banks and institutions.

7 - To lend to and borrow from central banks, foreign banks and financial institutions, and international financial institutions, provided that these operations are short-term and fall within the scope of its functions as a central bank.

The Bank may carry out the operations authorised by the preceding Article only with or for the account of the following entities:

A - The public sector.

B - Banks and financial institutions resident in Lebanon.

C - Central banks, banks and financial institutions abroad.

D - International financial institutions.

Notwithstanding the provisions of the preceding Article, the Bank may:

A - Issue the gold deposit certificates referred to in the second paragraph of Article 81 in favour of all persons, and buy or sell gold without the intermediation of banks.

B - Directly buy foreign currencies from and sell them to the public, in exceptional cases and in agreement with the Minister of Finance.
The public sector, within the meaning of this Law, includes the State, municipalities and legal persons of public law provided for in Article 2 of Legislative Decree No. 117 dated 12 June 1959.

The Central Bank is the banker of the public sector, and in this capacity:

a - The funds of the public sector shall be deposited with it exclusively.

b - It shall pay the sums that the public sector orders to be disbursed, up to the value of the latter's assets held with it.

c - It shall effect the transfer of funds requested of it by the public sector, up to the value of the latter's assets held with it.

d - It shall provide for the safekeeping of securities delivered to it by the public sector where necessary, and for their management, and in general it shall render all banking services to this sector.

e - It may, finally, and in the cases provided for in Articles 88, 91 and 92, grant loans to the public sector.

Deposits of the public sector with the Central Bank shall not bear interest; provided, however, that this Bank may, by agreement with the Minister of Finance, pay interest on deposits of the public sector other than deposits of the State.
The Bank shall provide free of charge the services provided for in paragraphs (b), (c) and (d) of Article 85.

The Bank is authorised to grant the Treasury, at the request of the Minister of Finance, cash facilities the value of which may not exceed ten per cent of the average ordinary revenues of the State budget in the last three years for which the accounts have been closed, and the duration of these facilities may not exceed four months.

The Government is granted a permanent authorisation empowering it to resort to the borrowing provided for in the preceding Article whenever it appears to the Ministry of Finance and to the Central Bank that the ready assets of the Treasury with this Bank are insufficient to meet the immediate obligations of the State. However, this authorisation may not be used more than once during twelve months.
With the exception of the cash facilities provided for in Articles 88 and 89, the principle is that the Central Bank shall not grant loans to the public sector.

However, in circumstances of exceptional gravity or in cases of extreme necessity, if the Government contemplates borrowing from the Central Bank, it shall inform the Governor of the Bank thereof.

The Bank shall examine with the Government the possibility of replacing its assistance by other means, such as issuing an internal loan, contracting an external loan, effecting savings in certain other items of expenditure, or finding new tax resources, etc...

And only in the case where it is established that there is no other solution, and if the Government nevertheless insists on its request, the Central Bank may grant the requested loan.

Thereupon the Bank shall propose to the Government, if necessary, the measures capable of limiting the adverse economic consequences that its loan might have, and in particular limiting its effect, in the situation in which it was granted, on the internal and external purchasing power of the currency.

Public sector entities other than the State may not apply for loans from the Central Bank except in the circumstances or cases provided for in the first paragraph of Article 91.

Applications issued by these entities shall be addressed directly to the Bank.

The Bank shall examine these applications from the perspectives provided for in paragraphs 1 and 2 of Article 91, and it shall also scrutinise, on the other hand, the position of the project for the financing of which the loan is requested and the capacities of the applicant to repay the loan. Lastly, it shall take into consideration the position of the Treasury and its commitments

in view of the possibility of its being guaranteed by the State.

The Bank may not contemplate granting the requested loan unless its study establishes that there is neither any circumstance nor any objection preventing the carrying out of the transaction.

In this case, the Bank shall submit to the Minister of Finance a detailed report on the matter, and if the Government approves the project and declares its readiness to give the guarantee of the State for the transaction, the Bank may grant the requested loan, and the Bank must likewise inform the Minister of Finance of the reasons that may have led it not to accede to a loan application submitted by an entity belonging to the public sector other than the State...

Loans granted pursuant to Articles 88, 91 and 92 shall bear interest in favour of the Bank. The interest rate shall be determined in relation to market conditions.

The interest rate on the cash facilities referred to in Article 88 may not be less than the discount rate applied at the Bank reduced by one.

As for the interest rate on the loans referred to in Articles 91 and 92, it may not be less than the discount rate applied at the Bank increased by one.
The loans referred to in Articles 91 and 92 may not be granted for a term longer than ten years.

The determination of the interest rate, the term of the loan and its other conditions shall be made in a contract signed between the Bank and the borrower.

The contract shall be referred to the Chamber of Deputies together with the complete file of the studies and reports of the Administration and the Bank.

In effecting the loans referred to in Articles 88, 91 and 92, the Central Bank may require the borrower to issue and deliver to the Bank negotiable financial bonds capable of being sold to the public.

The Bank is also the financial agent of the public sector, and in this capacity:

a - It assists free of charge in promoting the domestic and foreign loans of the public sector.

b - It effects, without expense or commission, the payment of interest on the said loans and the settlement of their matured instalments out of the provisions that have been deposited with it at least ten days before maturity.

c - It participates in negotiations aimed at concluding payment or clearing agreements.

d - It is exclusively entrusted with keeping the accounts relating to these agreements and may contract for the arrangements necessary for this purpose.

The action of the Central Bank in the agreements mentioned above is carried out for the account of the State, which benefits from all profits and bears all risks, expenses, commissions, interest and charges whatsoever.

The Bank opens cash deposit accounts for banks and financial institutions.

These accounts do not bear interest.
The Bank is not bound by a mandatory principle to grant loans to banks, rather it does so to the extent that it deems its assistance serves the public interest.

(As amended by the Law of 9/5/1967):

The Bank may discount commercial bills resulting from genuine debts based on commercial, industrial or agricultural operations. These bills must have fixed maturity dates, their term must not exceed 180 days, and they must bear three signatures known for their solvency.

The Bank may accept the replacement of the third signature:

- By a warehouse receipt (warrant) representing goods accepted by it.

- Or by a pledge of the type of securities against which it is permitted to grant advances pursuant to Article 102, and in this case the Bank may pursue the two signatories without enforcing the pledge prior to such pursuit.

The Central Bank may purchase under a repurchase agreement system (Pension) commercial bills fulfilling the conditions set out in the preceding Article, for a maximum period of thirty days renewable once. If the selling bank does not terminate the operation at the end of the contract, the Central Bank shall convert the repurchase agreement into a discount.

(As amended by the Law enforced by Decree No. 6102 dated 5/10/1973 - Official Gazette No. 81, Supplement):

The Bank may grant loans by current account in the form of the opening of credits for a period of twelve months, renewable once in cases of necessity, provided that they are guaranteed by commercial bills whose maturity does not exceed one year, or by gold, foreign currencies, or securities.

The Bank may accept as collateral for the loans provided for in the preceding paragraph bills whose maturity does not exceed three years if they relate to agricultural or industrial financing operations, public works contracts, or the export of Lebanese products abroad, in accordance with special conditions that it may lay down for this purpose.

The Board of the Bank may, in circumstances of exceptional gravity, or in cases of extreme necessity that may compel it to meet the urgent needs of the economy in order to preserve the stability of credit, decide to grant exceptional advances, secured to the extent necessary by real collateral other than the collateral referred to in the two preceding paragraphs, and furnished either by the borrowing bank itself, or by the members of its board of directors, or by its customers, and the Board of the Bank shall determine the type of necessary collateral and the conditions for granting exceptional advances and their maturities.

The Bank shall determine, in the regulations governing its operations, the interest rates and the minimum exchange commissions, charges, and commissions applicable to discounting, repurchase agreements (pensions), and loans. It shall also fix the haircuts on pledges and the rules governing them and all other conditions relating to discounting, repurchase agreements (pensions), and loans.
The Central Bank may also fix the maximum limit of its assistance to each bank, whatever its form, particularly in proportion to the importance of that bank and the sound management of its business.

(As amended by the Law enforced by Decree No. 6102 dated 5/10/1973 - Official Gazette No. 81, Supplement):

- In the event that public bonds issued by the State

or with its guarantee are held by the public, the Bank may discount or purchase such bonds under a repurchase agreement (pension), provided that their maturity does not exceed 180 days.

The Bank may also discount or accept in pledge for its loans government bonds or bonds issued with the guarantee of the Government whose maturity does not exceed five years if such bonds relate to the execution of development projects, provided that the interest rate is not less than the interest originally paid on such bonds plus at least two points.

(As amended by Legislative Decree No. 41 dated 5/8/1967):

The Central Bank is prohibited from:

a - Carrying out commercial operations falling outside the scope of its functions as defined by this Law.

b - Participating, in any form whatsoever, in any enterprise whatsoever, with the exception of the companies provided for in paragraph (f) of Article 110.

c - Purchasing or retaining immovable property other than that provided for in the preceding Article.

d - Carrying out authorised operations under conditions, or with guarantees, or with persons other than the conditions, guarantees, or persons specified in this Law.

The financial year of the Bank shall correspond to the calendar year. The first financial year shall include, by way of exception, the period ranging between the day on which the Central Bank commenced its operations and 31 December 1964.

The net profit shall consist of the surplus of revenues over general expenses, charges, amortisations, and all other provisions.

50% of this net profit shall be credited to an account of the Central Bank called the "General Reserve" and 50% shall be paid to the Treasury.

When the General Reserve reaches half of the capital of the Bank, the net profit shall be distributed at the rate of 20 per cent to the General Reserve and 80 per cent to the Treasury.

If the result of any year is a deficit, the loss shall be covered from the General Reserve, and in the absence or insufficiency of this reserve, the loss shall be covered by an equivalent payment from the Treasury.

If the balance of the "General Reserve" account becomes, as a result of a deduction of an amount pursuant to the preceding paragraph, less than half of the capital, the distribution of the net profit shall again be effected at the rate of 50% to this account and 50% to the Treasury until the account again reaches half of the capital.
The assets of the Bank in gold and foreign currencies shall be recorded in its accounts at the equivalent of their value at the legal rate of the Lebanese pound.

A special account shall be opened in the name of the Treasury, to which shall be credited or debited:

a - The differences between the equivalent of the assets of the Bank in gold and foreign currencies at the legal rate and the actual purchase or sale price of these assets.

b - The profits or losses resulting, in the assets of the Bank in gold and foreign currencies, from the modification of the legal rate of the Lebanese pound or the rate of one of the foreign currencies.

c - The amounts provided for in Articles 55 and 64.

(As amended by the Law promulgated by Decree No. 6210 dated 5/10/1973 - Official Gazette No. 81 Supplement):

- The Bank may, pursuant to Paragraph "c" of Article 76, purchase and sell without endorsement private bills whose maturity does not exceed 180 days, Treasury bills, and bills issued with the guarantee of the Government, whose maturity does not exceed one year from the date of their purchase.
In no case whatsoever may the operations on public bills provided for in Articles 105 and 106 be carried out in favour of the Treasury or in favour of other issuing bodies of the public sector.

(As amended by the Law promulgated by Decree No. 6102 dated 5/10/1973 - Official Gazette No. 81 Supplement):

- The Central Bank may discount Treasury bills and bills issued with the guarantee of the Government, or hold them under the regime of a contract of trust, or

purchase them in accordance with the conditions set forth in Articles 105 and 106, within the limits permitted by the requirements of monetary stability.

(As amended by the Law promulgated by Decree No. 6102 dated 5/10/1973 - Official Gazette Supplement 81):

- The Central Bank shall not carry out the operations authorised by Articles 98 to 108 inclusive except with banks and financial institutions.

The Bank may carry out operations of purchase or sale of Treasury bills or bills issued with the guarantee of the Government through the Beirut Stock Exchange where necessary if it deems this appropriate.

(As amended by Legislative Decree No. 41 dated 5/8/1967):

The Bank may also:

a - Purchase, construct and equip, out of its own funds, the real property necessary for the conduct of its business, and sell or exchange such real property.

b - Purchase by mutual agreement or by way of forced sale movable property in satisfaction of any of its debts, provided that it sells such property within

the shortest possible time unless it uses it for the conduct of its business.

c - Manage the funds constituted in favour of its employees, such as provisions set aside for end-of-service indemnities, reserve funds, and others.

d - Open deposit accounts for its employees and grant him loans out of its own funds.

e - And in general, carry out all operations that may arise secondarily from the execution or liquidation of the operations authorised by this Law.

f - Participate in Lebanese companies of public utility or national mixed companies, within the limits of its own funds.

The debit balance of the special account referred to in the preceding Article shall not fall due and shall not bear interest so long as its value does not exceed 25 % of the equivalent of the Bank's holdings of gold and foreign currencies at the legal rate.

The State shall cover the amounts exceeding this 25 % limit, either in cash or, under conditions to be determined by agreement with the Bank, by interest-bearing Treasury bonds.

If the special account becomes in credit, it shall be used for the advance redemption of the Treasury bonds issued pursuant to Decree No. 581 dated 8 December 1949, as amended by Decree No. 3453 dated 21 November 1950, and for the redemption of the Treasury bonds that may have been issued pursuant to the preceding paragraph of this Article.

In the event that the balance of this special account becomes in credit after the redemptions referred to in the preceding paragraph, the equivalent of 20% twenty per cent thereof must mandatorily be kept with the Bank as a Treasury deposit and the remaining eighty per cent shall be transferred to the Treasury account.

The Governor of the Bank shall submit to the Minister of Finance before 30 June of each year the balance sheet and the profit and loss account for the ended year and a report on the operations of the Bank during the same.

The balance sheet and the report shall be published in the Official Gazette during the month following their submission to the Minister of Finance. A summary statement of position shall be published every 15 days.
The Bank shall be exempted from all taxes, duties and excises, whatsoever established or to be established for the benefit of the State, the municipalities or any other body.

The Bank shall be exempted, in judicial proceedings, from furnishing security or an advance in all cases in which the law imposes this obligation upon the parties. The Bank shall have a general right of pledge over the funds and other valuables that are in its possession, for whatsoever reason, in the name of its debtors or for their account.

(As amended by the Law promulgated by Decree No. 6102 dated 5/10/1973 - Official Gazette No. 81 Supplement):

No person may establish, manage, or be employed by a bank.

1 - If he has been convicted less than ten years ago:

a - For committing any ordinary crime, or theft, or breach of trust, or fraud, or a misdemeanour to which the penalties for fraud apply, or embezzlement of funds or securities, or issuing cheques without provision in bad faith, or undermining the financial standing of the State within the meaning of Articles 219 and 320 of the Penal Code, or concealing objects obtained from the Penal Code, or concealing objects obtained by means of these offences.

b - For committing any offence punishable under any of Articles 689 700 of the Penal Code.

c - For attempting to commit the offences provided for in paragraphs (a) and (b) above, or being an accomplice therein.

The prohibition provided for in the first paragraph of this Article shall apply to persons convicted abroad for committing offences which constitute, under Lebanese law, one of the crimes or misdemeanours set out in paragraphs (a), (b) and (c) above, after verification of the validity of the foreign judgment in accordance with the last paragraph of Article 29 of the Penal Code.

2 - If he has been declared bankrupt and has not been rehabilitated for at least ten years; and if the bankruptcy was declared abroad, it shall be enforceable in Lebanon after verification of the validity of the foreign judgment in accordance with the last paragraph of Article 29 of the Penal Code.

3 - If he has been convicted of violating the provisions of the Law of 3 September 1956 relating to banking secrecy.

The provisions of this Article shall also apply to the Central Bank.

- Nor shall they be entitled to be members of the boards of directors of companies.

- Nor shall any person holding the position of Chairman of the Board of Directors, General Manager, Assistant General Manager, Manager, or Assistant Manager be entitled to engage in private commercial business or to be a member of partnerships in respect of which he incurs unlimited liability.

(Paragraph added by the Law promulgated by Decree No. 6102 dated 5/10/1973 - Official Gazette No. 81 Supplement).

Repealed by Legislative Decree No. 77 dated 27/6/1977 Official Gazette Issue 19 Supplement and replaced by the following text: (1)

a - The establishment of every Lebanese bank and the opening of every branch of a foreign bank in Lebanon shall be subject to a licence from the Council of the Central Bank.

b - Every amendment to the articles of association of Lebanese banks shall be subject to the approval of the Bank of Lebanon.

While reserving the right to benefit from all present or future provisions that are more favourable to pledgee creditors, the Bank is authorised to enforce the pledge granted to it as security for its debt, in accordance with the following procedures:

1 - If a debt due for payment is not settled, the Bank may, notwithstanding any objection and after the lapse of fifteen days from a notice registered with the Notary Public and served upon the debtor, proceed with the sale of the pledge in order to recover the amounts owed to it in principal, interest, commissions and expenses, and this shall not preclude other proceedings that may be brought against the debtor, his guarantors, or those jointly liable with him.

2 - The sale shall be ordered by the President of the Court of First Instance upon a mere request from the Bank without there being any need to summon the debtor.

3 - The Bank shall recover its debt directly from the proceeds of the sale and without carrying out any other formality.

In order to benefit from the authorised procedures set out in this Article, the Bank must have obtained the borrower's written consent to all the provisions of this Article prior to or upon the conclusion of the loan contract.
An institution whose primary object is to use for its own account in credit operations the funds which it receives from the public is called a bank.
Deposits and the proceeds of loans are considered funds received from the public by a bank..
Deposits shall be subject to the provisions of Article 307 of the Code of Commerce.

The following shall not be considered funds received from the public by a bank established constituting a joint-stock company:

a - Capital subscribed by the shareholders, reserve funds, share issue premiums and retained earnings.

b - Funds obtained by the bank, by way of loans of whatever form, from other banks or financial institutions.
Every natural or legal person who does not practise the banking profession is prohibited from receiving deposits within the meaning of Article 122.

(As amended by the Law promulgated by Decree No. 6102 dated 5/10/1973 - Official Gazette No. 81 Supplement):

- Only institutions established in the form of joint-stock or shareholding companies may practise the banking profession in Lebanon.

Establishments of foreign banks operating in Lebanon at the date of promulgation of this Law shall not be subject to the provisions of the preceding paragraph, provided that such foreign banks are considered as banks under the law to which they are subject.

(Repealed by Decree No. 41 issued on 5/8/1967 and replaced by the following text):

Upon the establishment of a bank or a subsequent increase in its capital, such capital must be paid up in cash at the Banque du Liban, with the exception of contributions in kind authorised in accordance with the provisions of Article 132.

The Bank shall carry out the intermediation provided for in the preceding paragraph without charging any "expense" or "commission."

Repealed by Legislative Decree No. 77 dated 27/6/1977 - Official Gazette, Supplement to Issue No. 19) and replaced by the following text:

Every foreign bank intending to establish a branch for itself in Lebanon must obtain the licence provided for in Article 128 before carrying out the formalities of declaration and publication provided for in Decision No. 96 dated 30 January 1926 and in Article 29 of the Code of Commerce.

(Repealed by Legislative Decree No. 77 dated 27/6/1877 - Official Gazette, Supplement to Issue No. 19) and replaced by the following text:

The Council of the Central Bank shall grant the licence referred to in Article 128 to the extent that it deems that it serves the public interest. The Council shall enjoy discretionary power in granting or refusing the licence.

(Repealed by Legislative Decree No. 77 dated 27/6/1977 - Official Gazette, Supplement to Issue 19, and replaced by the following text):

a - Every Lebanese bank existing before 9 May 1977 must have a minimum paid-up capital of three million Lebanese pounds allocated to its operations in Lebanon.

The Banque du Liban may decide to increase the minimum capital up to five million Lebanese pounds and fix the time limits for paying up this increase.

b - Every Lebanese bank licensed to be established after 9 May 1977 must have a minimum paid-up capital of fifteen million Lebanese pounds, out of the principal of which seven million and five hundred thousand L.L. shall be paid before commencing its operations as a blocked deposit for its account with the Lebanese Treasury and shall be returned to it without interest upon the liquidation of its operations.

This deposit shall be considered one of the elements of the fixed assets defined in Article 153.

All its shares must be registered shares, and at least 50 % of these shares must be owned by Lebanese natural persons or by companies or institutions all the members of which are Lebanese natural persons, and they may only be assigned to Lebanese persons.

A bank formed by the merger or absorption of existing banks shall not be considered a new bank, provided that prior approval is obtained for this purpose from the Banque du Liban.

c - Every Lebanese bank must constitute a reserve fund by deducting 10 % of its net annual profits.

d - Except in cases of absorption, merger, or conversion of a branch of a foreign bank into a Lebanese joint-stock company, the capital of the Lebanese bank must be paid up in cash with the Banque du Liban. However, following the approval of the Banque du Liban, half of the capital may be paid up in kind in real properties necessary for the bank's operations.

e - No Lebanese bank may reduce its declared capital or recover any part thereof.

(As amended by Legislative Decree No. 41 dated 5/8/1967 and by the Law promulgated by Decree No. 6102 dated 5/10/1973 - Official Gazette No. 81, Supplement):

- The Central Bank shall determine the principles for valuing the asset elements that constitute the counterpart of the capital of a bank.

It shall require every bank to prove that its assets actually exceed the liabilities owed by it to third parties, by an amount at least equal to the value of its capital.

A bank that has incurred losses must reconstitute its capital within a period of one year at most.

However, additional periods not exceeding one year in total may be granted by the Central Bank if the concerned bank provides sufficient guarantees regarding its ability to reconstitute its capital within the specified period.

The matter of determining losses shall be subject to the assessment of the Banking Control Commission.

In the event of an objection by the concerned bank or any interested third party to the assessment of the Control Commission, the matter shall be referred to the Central Council.

The decision of the Central Council in this regard shall be final and not subject to any administrative or judicial recourse.

Banks must submit an application for their registration with the Central Bank.

The application shall be accepted if its applicants meet the provisions of this Law and the provisions of the Code of Commerce apply to them.

The Central Bank shall draw up the list of banks whose registration it has accepted, hereinafter referred to as "the List".

The Central Bank shall publish the List in the Official Gazette during the month of January of each year, and shall likewise publish in the Gazette every amendment made to this List.

Any person may inspect this List free of charge at the head office of the Central Bank or at its branches.

No institution that is not registered on the List of Banks may practise the banking profession, nor include the terms "bank", "banker", "banking", or any other similar term in any language whatsoever, whether in its trade name, in its object, or in its advertisements, nor may it use these terms in any manner that may mislead the public as to its capacity.

Banks registered on the List provided for in Article 136 must mention the registration number assigned to them on this List, under the same conditions, on the same documents, and under pain of the same penalties relating to registration in the Commercial Register.

The registration of banks on the List provided for in Article 136 shall replace the authorisation of the Ministry of Finance required pursuant to the First Article of the Law of 3 September of the year 1956 relating to Banking Secrecy.

(Repealed by Legislative Decree No. 77 dated 27/6/1977, Official Gazette Supplement to Issue No. 19, and replaced by the following text):

A - Every foreign bank licensed to establish a branch in Lebanon prior to 9 May 1977 shall prove that it has allocated to this branch a capital of at least three million Lebanese pounds.

The Bank of Lebanon may decide to increase the minimum capital up to five million Lebanese pounds and fix the time limits for paying up this increase.

B - Every foreign bank licensed to engage in banking operations by establishing a branch in Lebanon after 9 May 1977 shall allocate to this branch a minimum capital of fifteen million Lebanese pounds, out of the principal of which, and prior to commencing its operations, an amount of seven million five hundred thousand Lebanese pounds shall be paid as a blocked deposit for its account with the Lebanese Treasury, to be returned to it without interest upon the liquidation of its operations.

A bank formed from the merger or absorption of existing banks, or from the transformation of an existing Lebanese bank in the form of a joint-stock company into a branch of a foreign bank, shall not be deemed a new bank; however, it shall be required for this purpose to obtain prior approval from the Bank of Lebanon.

C - Every foreign bank shall constitute a reserve fund by deducting 10 % of the net profits of its branch in Lebanon.

D - With the exception of cases of absorption, merger, or transformation of a bank established in the form of a Lebanese joint-stock company into a branch of a foreign bank, the capital must be paid up in cash with the Bank of Lebanon.

E - No foreign bank may reduce its declared capital allocated to its branch in Lebanon for any reason whatsoever.

Supervision of banks shall be entrusted to a department at the Central Bank that is completely separate and independent from its remaining departments and linked directly to the Governor.

All employees of this department shall take an oath and shall be bound, in the interest of the banks and their clients, to maintain the secrecy imposed by Article 2 of the Law of 3 September 1956, even towards persons belonging to the other departments of the Bank, with the exception of the Governor, provided that this shall not prevent the application of

Article 151.

The Central Bank shall exercise its supervision in the following manner:

1 - By auditing the statements, documents, information, clarifications and proofs that the banks must submit or that the Central Bank is entitled to request from them pursuant to the provisions of this Law.

2 - By requesting, whenever it sees a need therefor, from the responsible managers of the banks, any additional information, clarifications or proofs, and by requesting them to confirm the same in writing and under their personal liability.

3 - By the Governor of the Central Bank being entitled to decide to conduct a more thorough audit through his examiners, if he deems it necessary, in order to verify all or some of what is mentioned in the two preceding paragraphs.

In the event that the Governor takes such a decision, the responsible managers at the concerned bank or banks must place at the disposal of the examiners whom the Governor has selected from among the examiners affiliated with the department provided for in Article 148, the documents that enable them to accomplish their mission and submit a reasoned report.

The examiners of the Central Bank shall not be entitled, in any case, to compel the managers of banks to disclose the names of their clients, with the exception of the holders of debit accounts, nor shall they be entitled to contact any person other than the responsible manager of the bank.

Banks may organise their accounts in a manner in which the names of clients do not appear, with the exception of the holders of debit accounts.

It is strictly prohibited for the examiners of the Central Bank, on the occasion of exercising their supervision, to inquire into any matter of a tax nature or to intervene therein or to inform any person whomsoever thereof.

The provisions of the Banking Secrecy Law issued on 3/9/1956 shall not prevent any administration or any employee of the employees of the Central Bank and the Banking Control Commission from performing their duties.

The details of the application of this Article shall be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance and after consulting the opinion of the Central Council of the Bank of Lebanon and the Banking Control Commission.

Every person who belongs or belonged to the Central Bank, in any capacity whatsoever, must keep the secrecy established by the Law of 3 September 1956.

This obligation covers all information and all facts relating not only to the clients of the Central Bank, banks and financial institutions, but also to all the aforementioned institutions themselves, of which he became aware through his belonging to the Central Bank.

(Repealed by Legislative Decree No. 41 dated 5/8/1967 and replaced by the following text):

A bank shall be struck off the list of banks:

a - If it is placed under liquidation.

b - If it declares itself that it is in a state of cessation of payment.

c - If it appears to the Higher Banking Authority that it is no longer in a position enabling it to continue its business.

d - If it does not exercise its activity within a year from its registration on the list.

e - If it ceases to exercise its activity for more than a year.

f- If it does not reconstitute its capital within the time limits specified pursuant to Article 134.

g- In the cases provided for in Article 208.

The Governor shall decide the striking off in the two cases (a) and (b) and the Higher Banking Authority shall decide it in the other cases.

Striking off shall automatically entail the prohibition provided for in Article 125 and the liquidation of the bank struck off in accordance with the laws in force.

A bank which is in a state of liquidation may continue to use its designation "as a bank" provided that it clearly states after its name that it is under liquidation.

The Public Prosecution shall request the court, upon the request of the Central Bank, to order all other measures capable of protecting the interests of the depositors of the bank struck off, and in particular sealing with red wax, taking an inventory, appointing a custodian, etc...
Banks must keep separate accounting for the totality of their operations carried out in Lebanon.
The branches or agencies in Lebanon of a single bank, whether Lebanese or foreign, shall constitute a single group in the application of the provisions of this Law.
The financial year of banks must correspond to the calendar year.

Banks must draw up annual accounts closed on 31 December comprising a balance sheet and profit and loss accounts. As well as all other periodic accounting or statistical statements that the Central Bank may require of them within the conditions, forms and time limits specified by this Bank.

They must also submit to the Bank, with regard to the documents referred to in the preceding paragraph, all the information, clarifications and proofs that this Bank may require of them.

Banks must, on the other hand, submit to the Central Bank, for the operation of its Central Office of Banking Risks, periodic statements on the credits granted by them, in accordance with forms established by the Central Bank and within the time limits specified by it.

The expenses of this Office shall be covered by the banks under the conditions and rules that the Central Bank shall specify.

(Amended by the Law enforced by Decree No. 6102 dated 5/10/1973- Official Gazette No. 81 Supplement):

- The total of the elements of a bank's assets representing its initial establishment expenses, its equipment, its furniture, its real estate investments, and the partnership shares or equity participations of whatever form belonging to it in any enterprise whatever its object may be, added to the total of the credits granted pursuant to the preceding Article, may not exceed the total of its own funds at any time whatsoever.

The fixed properties in the total of these asset elements may only be represented by properties accepted by the Bank of Lebanon in accordance with a special regulation laid down by the Central Council of the Bank.

(Amended by the Law enforced by Decree No. 6102 dated 5/10/1973- Official Gazette No. 81 Supplement):

- Notwithstanding the second paragraph of Article 152 and Article 153, a bank may purchase partnership shares, equity participations, or real estate the value of which exceeds the permitted limit, provided that the purchase took place for the recovery of suspended debts or debts of doubtful collection. However, this bank must liquidate these assets within a period not exceeding two years, and if it is unable to comply with this time limit due to circumstances beyond its control, it shall refer the matter to the Central Bank.

The temporary acquisition of real estate in accordance with the preceding paragraph is exempted from the licence provided for in the Law on the Acquisition of Real Estate by Foreigners, but is subject to a licence granted by the Banking Control Commission after verifying that the purchase is actually taking place in recovery of a suspended debt or a debt of doubtful collection.

The Central Bank has the authority to assess, in the light of the definitions set out in Article 177, and whether certain elements composing the assets of a bank constitute participations, equity holdings, or fixed assets, contrary to the provisions of Articles 152 and 153. If the bank concerned objects to the viewpoint of the Central Bank, the matter shall be decided by way of ordinary arbitration, in accordance with the Code of Civil Procedure.

The arbitration agreement must take place within the month following the date of the objection.

The arbitral award shall not be subject to appeal.

The arbitrators and the umpire are bound by the secrecy obligation imposed pursuant to the Law of 3 September 1956.

Banks must observe, in the use of the funds they receive from the public, the rules that ensure the safeguarding of its rights.

In particular, they must match the term of their placements with the nature of their resources.
Placements of banks are classified into short-term operations and medium- or long-term operations.

(Amended by Legislative Decree No. 41 dated 5/8/67 and by the Law promulgated by Decree No. 6102 dated 5/8/1973 - Official Gazette No. 81 Supplement):

- Banks are prohibited from:

1 - Practising any commerce, industry or activity foreign to the banking profession.

2 - Participating, in any form whatsoever, in industrial, commercial, agricultural or other enterprises, subject to the provisions of Article 153.

3 - Granting, in any form whatsoever, credits to their auditors, to the Central Council, to the staff of the Central Bank, of all ranks, and to the family members of each of those persons.

4 - Granting, directly or indirectly, credits to the members of their boards of directors or the persons in charge of their management and their major shareholders and to the family members of those persons without complying with the conditions set forth below:

a - The credits must be the subject of a prior authorisation in principle from the general assembly of shareholders, in which at least the maximum limit of the credits that may be granted to each person is specified, and the board of directors and the auditors must inform the annual ordinary general assembly of shareholders of the conditions for granting these credits, and of the execution of these conditions, and the authorisation of this assembly must be renewed, where necessary, every year.

b - Each credit shall be granted pursuant to an express authorisation from the board of directors specifying the amount of the credit and its conditions.

c - The credits must be covered by real securities, or by a bank guarantee or by a guarantee from a financial institution registered in Lebanon that is acceptable to the Control Commission.

d - The total of these credits must not exceed 25 per cent of the bank's own funds.

e - Any bank may grant credits to the members of its board of directors, to the persons in charge of its management and to its major shareholders without complying with the conditions contained in this Article within the limit of 6 per cent of its own funds and within the maximum limit provided for in paragraph (d) above.

f- It rests with the Banking Control Commission to assess the extent of the impression of the provisions of this Article on certain accounts or risks, particularly as regards the extent of the existence of an indirect interest, for each case individually. In the event of a divergence of views between the Banking Control Commission and the management of the bank concerned, the matter shall be referred to the Central Council for decision, and the decision of the Central Council in this respect shall be deemed final and shall not be subject to any form of administrative or judicial recourse.

Loans granted by a bank to a credit institution that it owns in fact shall not be subject to the provisions of this Article, even if the persons in charge of the management of this institution are at the same time members of its board of directors or employees thereof, provided that this institution has been registered with the Bank of Lebanon.

In the application of paragraphs 3 and 4 of this Article, the family shall consist of the spouse, ascendants, descendants, brothers and sisters if they are dependants of the borrower.

Short-term loans are essentially the temporary assistance that banks extend to the treasury of their clients or the credits the repayment of which is naturally ensured by the completion of the operations for which they were granted within a period not exceeding one year.

Medium-term or long-term loans are those that commit the banker, in his capacity as lender, to financing operations or projects which, by their nature, do not allow the borrower to repay, within the period of one year, the amounts he has borrowed to carry out such operations and projects.
Banks must require every applicant for credit to submit a statement of condition or a balance sheet.
Banks must monitor the use of the credits they grant in order to ascertain, as far as possible, that the funds they have advanced have not been diverted from the declared purpose.

Where a commercial contract between a bank and its client requires the latter to create, in representation of the advance on account granted to him, bills for a fixed term, such bills shall, notwithstanding the provisions of the ninth Article of Legislative Decree No. 130/L dated 20 December 1933, be subject only to a flat stamp duty of one Lebanese pound for bills the value of which does not exceed 5000 Lebanese pounds, two Lebanese pounds for bills the value of which ranges between 5001 and 10000 Lebanese pounds, and 5 Lebanese pounds for bills the value of which exceeds 10000 Lebanese pounds.
(Repealed by the Law promulgated by Decree No. 6102 dated 5/10/1973 - Official Gazette No. 81, Supplement):

A bank is prohibited from encumbering the securities pledged with it with any obligation or borrowing funds thereon without obtaining in advance, by virtue of a special instrument, the consent of the pledging debtor. In no event may the bank encumber the securities pledged with it with any obligation, nor borrow funds thereon, for an amount exceeding the value of the debt owed to it by the pledging debtor.
A bank may neither purchase its own shares nor accept them as a pledge for loans it grants.
Banks may receive savings deposits from natural persons or from non-profit associations.
Funds deposited by way of forming a capital shall be deemed savings deposits.

Opening a savings account shall result in the bank delivering a personal passbook to the account holder; the passbook shall serve as a debt instrument for the depositor and shall not be transferable either by assignment or by endorsement.

Amounts may only be paid in and withdrawn upon presentation of the passbook to the department that issued this document, in which the said transactions must be recorded. The withdrawal of amounts by means of cheques or transfers shall not be permitted.
Banks may determine the other conditions under which savings accounts are opened.
Savings accounts shall be exempted from the income tax established pursuant to Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12 June 1959.
Registration on the "List" shall exempt banks from the formality referred to in Article 186 of Legislative Decree No. 126 dated 12 June 1959.

The issuance of "travellers' cheques" shall be subject to prior authorisation from the Central Bank, which shall lay down the conditions that must be fulfilled by the bank in order to obtain this authorisation.

(As amended by the Law promulgated by Decree No. 6102 dated 5/10/1973 - Official Gazette No. 81 Supplement):

- The Central Bank shall have the authority to issue recommendations and use means likely to ensure the conduct of sound banking operations.

Such recommendations and means may be general or individual.

In particular, the Central Bank may, after consulting the Association of Banks in Lebanon, establish the general regulations necessary to ensure good relations between banks and their depositors and clients.

It may also determine and amend, whenever it deems it necessary, the business conduct rules with which banks must comply in order to preserve their liquidity and solvency status.

(As amended by the Law promulgated by Decree No. 6102 dated 5/10/1973 - Official Gazette No. 81 Supplement):

- In order to ensure the soundness of banking operations, the Central Bank may determine from time to time, either generally or for each bank individually, the ratios that must be maintained between assets and liabilities or specify certain elements of these assets and liabilities among themselves.

Own funds shall be considered as liabilities within the meaning of this Article.

The provisions that may be issued pursuant to the preceding Article cannot be of immediate application or have retroactive effect. Rather, the Central Bank shall specify, in the instructions it addresses to banks on this occasion, the time limit at the end of which the application of the prescribed ratios shall commence, and shall also specify the rules in accordance with which these ratios are calculated.

The Central Bank shall define, in the regulations and instructions it establishes in implementation of this Law, the meaning of the terms: "liquid funds", "liquidity status", "mobilisable assets", "short-term commitments", "own funds or capital", "immobilised funds", etc....

(As amended by the Law promulgated by Decree No. 6102 dated 5/10/1973 - Official Gazette No. 81 Supplement):

- Within the framework of the special provisions stipulated by this Law, institutions whose principal object is to carry out credit operations of whatever kind and which fulfil the conditions stipulated in Articles 179, 180, 181, and 182 of this Law shall be considered financial institutions.

(As amended by the Law promulgated by Decree No. 6102 dated 5/10/1973 - Official Gazette No. 81 Supplement):

- Lebanese financial institutions shall be established in the form of joint-stock companies.

Foreign financial institutions shall not be authorised to establish themselves in Lebanon except for foreign companies or branches of foreign companies established in their country of origin in the form of joint-stock companies.

The provisions laid down in Articles 125 and 127, as well as the provisions of Articles 128, 130, 131, 143, 144, 145, 146, 147 of this Law, shall apply to financial institutions.

The following elements shall not be deemed deposits in the application of the provisions of Article 125 to financial institutions.

a - Capital, reserve funds, retained earnings, share issue premiums.

b - Funds obtained by financial institutions through their operations with banks and other financial institutions or through the issuance of debt securities.

(As amended by the Law promulgated by Decree No. 6102 dated 5/10/ 1973 - Official Gazette No. 81 Supplement):

- Every Lebanese financial institution must have a minimum paid-up capital of two million Lebanese pounds.

Every foreign financial institution must prove that it has allocated to its investments in Lebanon a capital of at least two million Lebanese pounds.

(As amended by the Law promulgated by Decree No. 6102 dated 5/10/1973 - Official Gazette No. 81 Supplement):

- The prohibition provided for in Article 125 shall apply to these institutions. Financial institutions must apply for their registration with the Bank of Lebanon.

Applications fulfilling the legal conditions shall be accepted.

The Bank of Lebanon shall publish the list of registered financial institutions in accordance with the provisions laid down in respect of banks in Article 136 of the Code of Money and Credit.

No institution shall be entitled to assume the capacity of a financial institution unless it is registered and entered on the list of financial institutions.

Natural and legal persons previously registered as financial institutions pursuant to the provisions of the Code of Money and Credit shall be granted a period of one year from the date of issuance of this Law to comply with the provisions of Articles 178 to 181 of this Law, and if they do not close down by the end of this period, they shall become ipso jure subject to the provisions of Articles 183, 184 and 222 of this Law.

(As amended by the Law promulgated by Decree No. 6102 dated 5/10/1973 - Official Gazette No. 81 Supplement):

- Financial institutions shall implement all the measures taken by the Bank of Lebanon concerning credit, and particularly those relating to the operations referred to in Article 79 of this Law, and they shall comply with the directives with which the Central Bank may provide them regarding their management.

The supervision of financial institutions shall be entrusted to the Banking Control Commission, and the Commission shall be vested, towards these institutions, with the same powers as it exercises towards banks.

The provisions relating to the auditing commissioners at banks shall apply to financial institutions and to their auditing commissioners.

The administrative penalties that apply to banks pursuant to Article 208 shall apply to financial institutions, and in the event that their registration is struck off, they may either continue their business within the framework of Article 183 below, or be liquidated.

(As amended by the Law promulgated by Decree No. 6102 dated 5/10/1973 - Official Gazette No. 81 Supplement):

- The regime governing financial institutions shall not apply to natural or legal persons who carry out one or some of the operations provided for in Article 178 and who do not fulfill the conditions for registration as financial institutions.

The provisions set forth in Articles 125 and 127 shall apply to such persons.

There shall not be considered as deposits received by the institutions concerned in this Article the elements specified in Article 124 and the funds placed at the disposal of the institution by the jointly liable partners if the institution is established in the form of a general partnership, and by the general partners and the limited partners if the company is established in the form of a simple limited partnership, by the general partners, if the institution is established in the form of a partnership limited by shares, as well as the funds obtained by joint-stock companies through the issuance of debt securities in accordance with Article 22 et seq. of the Code of Commerce.

- The institutions concerned by the preceding article must submit to the Bank of Lebanon, within the six months following the date of entry into force of this Law if they were established after it, a declaration comprising their trade name or denomination, their postal address, the value of their capital and the nature of the operations in which they engage.

They must also submit a copy of their registration file in the Commercial Register, as well as a copy of their registration file with the Ministry of National Economy if they are a branch of a foreign institution, and they must send to the Central Bank, on the conditions, in accordance with the forms and within the time limits set by it, all the accounting or statistical statements that it requests from them.

They must comply with the measures that the Bank of Lebanon may take with regard to credit, especially those relating to the operations concerned by Article 79, and the directives with which it may provide them regarding their management.
No person may be appointed as an auditor at a bank if he is in one of the situations provided for in Article 127.

(As amended by Legislative Decree No. 41 dated 5/8/1967):

During the year, the commissioners must immediately inform the responsible authorities in the bank which they are entrusted with supervising of the discrepancies and violations they may have observed, requesting these authorities to regularise the situation as soon as possible.

Furthermore, they must draw up a detailed annual report on the supervisory operations they have carried out and their results, and this report shall be submitted to the responsible authorities in the bank concerned, at the latest by the end of the month of March following the year during which the supervision took place.

In addition to the reports which they draw up pursuant to the provisions of the Code of Commerce, the supervisory commissioners must submit to the General Assembly of the bank to which they have been appointed a detailed special report on the credits granted by this bank, directly or indirectly, to the members of its Board of Directors and to those in charge of its management.

(Repealed by Legislative Decree No. 41 dated 5/8/1967 and replaced by the following text):

The supervisory commissioners must send, directly and simultaneously, to the Governor of the Central Bank and the Chairman of the Banking Control Commission copies of their reports mentioned in the preceding Article. Furthermore, they must comply within the shortest possible time limit with any request for information or clarifications addressed to them by these two authorities.

If this report contains the names of clients, these names must be replaced by numbers on the copy sent to the Governor.

(As amended by the Law put into force by Decree No. 6102 dated 5/10/1973 - Official Gazette No. 81 Supplement):

- Every foreign bank must appoint to it a supervisory commissioner in accordance with the procedures provided for in Article 186. These commissioners shall ensure the supervision of the operations of foreign banks in Lebanon within the conditions specified in this Law.
Supervisory commissioners shall be bound by banking secrecy in the same manner as the persons referred to in the second Article of the Law of 3 September 1956.

The Government is authorised to regulate the profession of supervisory commissioners at banks by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Central Bank and after the approval of the Minister of Finance.
Whoever refrains from accepting Lebanese currency under the conditions specified in Articles 7 and 8 shall be subject to the penalties provided for in Article 319 of the Penal Code.
Violation of the provisions of Article 11 of this Law shall be subject to the penalties provided for in Article 44 of the Penal Code.

(As amended by the Law promulgated by Decree No. 6102 dated 5/10/1973 - Official Gazette No. 81 Supplement):

- Notwithstanding the provisions of Articles 172 and 173 of the Code of Commerce, the following procedures shall be adopted in the appointment of auditors at registered banks and financial institutions:

Auditors shall be appointed by the General Assembly of Shareholders for a term of three years ending at the convening of the General Assembly that examines the accounts of the third year.

As for the auditor who is appointed in the place of another before the expiry of the term of three years, this to determine the duration of his term of office, by the remaining duration of the term of office of his predecessor.

If the General Assembly fails to appoint the auditor, every shareholder shall have the right to request the competent court to appoint a temporary auditor whose term of office shall end upon the appointment of a principal auditor by the General Assembly.

Auditors must fulfil the conditions and possess the qualifications that qualify them to be accepted as experts before the courts and they must be sworn.

A single shareholder or a group of shareholders representing at least ten percent of the capital of the bank or financial institution shall have the right to object to the appointment of one or more of the auditors appointed by the General Assembly and to request the competent court to appoint others, and if the court grants the request of these shareholders, the auditors appointed in this manner may not be dismissed before the expiry of their term of office except by a decision of the competent court.

Banks and financial institutions shall be exempted from the necessity of the appointment of an additional auditor by the court, subject to the provisions of the Banking Secrecy Law, a single shareholder or a group of shareholders representing at least ten percent of the capital of the bank or financial institution shall have the right to request the competent court to appoint an expert to investigate specific matters and the court must, if it finds this request and responds to it, determine the mission of the expert, his powers and his fees. The expert shall submit his report to the petitioning shareholder or shareholders and to the Board of Directors and this report must be presented to the first General Assembly held by the shareholders.

The penalties provided for in Article 356 of the Penal Code shall apply to any violation of the provisions of Article 23.

The banks, financial institutions, and institutions referred to in Article 23 shall be deemed accomplices to the persons who have accepted from them a mandate, an office, or a participation in violation of the provisions of the aforementioned Article 23.
The penalties provided for in Article 655 of the Penal Code shall apply to any violation of the provisions of Articles 125, 137, and 141, first paragraph.

Any person who violates the prohibitions enumerated in Article 127 shall be punished by imprisonment for a term of at least one month and at most three months and by a fine of at least 300 Lebanese pounds and at most 1000 Lebanese pounds, or by either of these two penalties alone.

Any person who violates the provisions of Articles 152 and 153 shall be punished by imprisonment for a term of at least one month and at most three months, and by a fine of at least 100 Lebanese pounds and at most 5000 Lebanese pounds, or by either of these two penalties alone.

The penalties provided for in Article 655 of the Penal Code shall apply to any person who has obtained credit from a bank by giving it incorrect or incomplete information in reply to the request addressed to him by that bank pursuant to the provisions of Article 160. A bank that has not requested the statement of position or the balance sheet provided for in Article 160 shall be punished by a fine ranging between 1000 and 5000 Lebanese pounds.

Any person who violates the provisions of Articles 164 and 165 shall be punished by imprisonment for a term of at least one month and at most three months and by a fine of at least 1000 Lebanese pounds and at most 5000 Lebanese pounds, or by either of these two penalties alone.

(As amended by Legislative Decree No. 41 dated 5/8/1967)

and by the Law put into force by Decree No. 6102 dated 5/10/1973 - Official Gazette No. 81, Supplement):

- Any person who issues travellers' cheques without the authorisation of the Central Bank or in violation of the conditions imposed by it pursuant to Article 173 shall be punished by the penalties provided for in Article 655 of the Penal Code.

Any person who habitually engages in credit operations, of whatever kind, without being registered with the Banque du Liban in accordance with the provisions of Article 181 or without having made the declaration required under Article 184 of this Law shall be punished by the same penalty.

Every person accredited to sign on behalf of a bank or a financial institution, or who is a member of the board of directors, a manager, or an employee at a bank or a financial institution, who has intentionally submitted to the Central Bank incomplete or untrue accounting statements, statistics, information, or explanations, shall be punished by imprisonment from 8 days to 30 days and by a fine from 100 to 1000 Lebanese pounds, or by either of these two penalties only.

Furthermore, a bank that has not declared to the Central Risk Office a client or some of the risks of a client may be sentenced to damages towards the other creditor banks of this client in the event of his cessation of payments.

Auditors who have, intentionally or by negligence, breached their duties defined in this Law shall be deemed accomplices and the same penalties that apply to the principal offenders shall apply to them. The penalties provided for in Article 256 of the Penal Code shall apply to the violation of the provisions of the last paragraph of Article 186. The court may also prohibit the auditors convicted pursuant to the two preceding paragraphs from practising the profession temporarily or permanently.

Whoever among the persons referred to in Articles 148, 151, 155, and 190 discloses banking secrecy shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to two years, without prejudice to the application of Articles 127 and 185.

If a violation is established against a legal person, the personal penalties that the violation may entail shall be imposed on the manager, managers, or employees of this legal person who are responsible for the violation. The responsible person or persons referred to shall be jointly and severally liable with the legal person for the payment of all fines, damages, and expenses.

Neither a bank nor a financial institution may invoke the supervision exercised by the Central Bank to evade the civil or criminal liabilities they may have incurred. Nor may they use this supervision as an element of publicity.

Violations of this Law shall be prosecuted before the criminal courts in accordance with summary procedure, and the action shall be brought by the Public Prosecution upon the request of the Central Bank.

The court shall order the publication of the judgment or its posting, or both measures, in part or in full, at the expense of the convicted person.

A fine, which may reach one hundred Lebanese pounds per day, shall be imposed on every bank that does not comply within the time limits with the obligations provided for in Articles 146, 147, 175 and 176 or obstructs the supervision operations entrusted to the Central Bank and referred to in Article 149. This shall not preclude the application of the penal or administrative sanctions to which it is subject.

The same sanctions shall be imposed on financial institutions that do not comply with the obligations provided for in Article 182.

The fine shall be determined by the Central Bank and shall become payable starting from the day following the date of the notice which it shall have sent by registered letter to the bank or financial institution concerned.

a - Warning.

b - Reduction or suspension of credit facilities granted to it.

c - Prohibition from carrying out certain operations or imposition of any other limitations in its practice of the profession.

d - Appointment of a controller or a provisional manager.

e - Striking it off the list of banks.

This shall not preclude the application of the fines and penal sanctions to which the violating bank is subject.

Pending the fixing in gold of a new rate for the Lebanese pound in agreement with the International Monetary Fund and pending the confirmation of this rate by a law in accordance with the second article, the Minister of Finance shall take the following transitional measures, which shall enter into force on the dates that he shall determine.

1 - He shall adopt for the Lebanese pound, in relation to the American dollar fixed at 0,888681 grams of fine gold, a real exchange rate as close as possible to the free market rate, which shall be the "legal transitional rate" of the Lebanese pound.

2 - The gold element in the cover of the banknotes issued by the current Institution of Issue shall be entered on the basis of the "legal transitional rate".

3 - The differences between, on the one hand, the equivalent, at the transitional rate, of the gold included in the cover and the foreign currencies that may be included therein, and on the other hand, the effective price of this gold and these currencies, shall remain subject to the provisions of Decree No. K/15105 dated 27

May 1949 until these elements are transferred to the Central Bank. As from the date of this transfer, the aforementioned elements, together with the other gold and foreign currency assets of the Central Bank, shall be subject to the provisions of Article 115

4 - Taxes and duties collected on amounts denominated in foreign currencies, which are currently calculated on the basis of the rate fixed in the first article of the Law of 24 May 1949, shall be calculated on the basis of the "legal transitional rate".

The application of the new conversion rate must not lead to any increase in the taxes and duties collected on amounts denominated in foreign currencies, the Minister of Finance shall determine, by decisions, the methods capable of ensuring this principle.

5 - Foreign currencies collected by the State shall be entered into the accounts at the legal transitional rate.

6 - The external expenditures of the State fixed in Lebanese pounds shall be adjusted in relation to the legal transitional rate and shall henceforth be converted at the free market rate.

- Notwithstanding the provisions of Article Twenty-Eight of Law No. 4 dated 20/08/1990 relating to the ratification of the General Budget and Annexed Budgets for the year 1990, the two types of lottery, Lotto and Instant, established pursuant to the provisions of Article Forty-Eight of Law No. 7/85 dated 10/08/1985 (1985 Budget), are reinstated and their regulations shall be amended in accordance with the procedures for their approval, and the Ministry of Finance is authorised to award them by tender in whole or in part to third parties, and their reinstatement shall take effect as from 04/03/1993 in respect of the award of the first type (Lotto) and as from 08/08/1993 in respect of the award of the second type (Instant) and until the date of commencement of execution of the new award for each of them.
