The Ministry of National Education and Fine Arts shall undertake the stimulation of cultural activity, the organisation of education affairs, its generalisation and the raising of its standard, the promotion of the sporting and scouting spirit, the protection of antiquities, and the encouragement of the arts.

The Ministry of National Education and Fine Arts shall consist of the following administrations and bodies: First: The Central Administration Second: The Lebanese University Third: Secondary Education Fourth: Primary and Complementary Education Fifth: Pedagogical and Vocational Education Sixth: The Conservatory of Music Seventh: The Directorate of Antiquities Eighth: The National Library
The cadres of the Ministry of National Education shall be determined in the eleven schedules annexed to this Legislative Decree.

The Central Administration shall consist of: - The Directorate General - The Bureau - The Department of Cultural Affairs - The Department of Inspection - The Department of Administrative and Financial Affairs - The Sub-Divisions in the Governorates

The Minister shall be assisted by a Director General who shall be considered the direct head of the administrations attached to the Ministry and the highest superior of its employees. He shall exercise, in addition to the powers provided for in the second Article of the Legislative Decree issued on 7 January 1953 under number 13, the following duties and powers: 1- Signing transactions that do not involve a general principle. 2- Approving expenditure transactions the value of which does not exceed one thousand Lebanese pounds 3- Approving lease contracts and expenditure contracts relating to salaries, wages and purchases, whatever their value may be. 4- Signing correspondence with the administrations attached to the Ministry and travel orders for the employees attached to it within the Lebanese territories.

The Bureau shall undertake the following duties: - Registering incoming and outgoing correspondence and communicating it to the competent authority. - Keeping and organising the papers, registers and documents of the Ministry. - Organising official examinations and supervising their proper conduct in cooperation with the Department of Cultural Affairs in accordance with the instructions issued by the Minister in a special decision. - Organising educational statistics in accordance with the instructions issued by the Minister in a special decision. - Attending to scholarship affairs and ensuring the application of the special regulations relating thereto. - Keeping official certificates and delivering them to those entitled to them.

The Cultural Affairs Department shall undertake the following tasks: - Studying the cultural movement in the country in general, and the state of education in particular, and proposing the means capable of revitalising and directing it. - Studying the needs of the country in terms of education and proposing the means capable of securing them. - Studying the curricula followed in the various educational institutions, whether governmental or private, and proposing the suitable means for applying or amending them. - Studying school books and supplies in general with a view to improving them and making them accessible to all. - Sponsoring the artistic movement in the country and proposing the means capable of encouraging and disseminating the fine arts. - Watching over the proper conduct of cultural relations between Lebanon, on the one hand, and foreign countries and international institutions, on the other hand, and over organising and strengthening them.

The Inspection Department shall undertake the following tasks: - Watching over the application of education regulations and compliance therewith. - Inspecting all official schools to verify the proper conduct of work therein from both the administrative and technical aspects. - Inspecting private educational institutions, whether national or foreign, within the scope of the rights officially recognised for these institutions. - Inspecting vocational education in the various regions. - Supervising the sports and scouting movement in the country, particularly in official schools.

The Administrative and Financial Affairs Department shall undertake the following tasks: - Securing accounting work. - Keeping employee registers, organising their personal files, and carrying out all administrative transactions relating to their personal and career status. - Caring for school buildings: by constructing, purchasing, expanding, and repairing them. - Securing supplies, furniture, and all other movable acquisitions.

Sub-departments of the Ministry of National Education and Fine Arts shall be established in the governorates, which shall represent the Ministry, be considered the direct authority for all educational institutions in the governorates, whether national or foreign, study the needs of cities and villages in terms of education, collect information relating to all institutes and supply the Ministry therewith, receive instructions from the central administration, and communicate them to their relevant authorities.
An institution for higher education shall be established under the name of the "Lebanese University", comprising faculties and institutes, each of which shall be established and organised by a law.

The Lebanese University shall have the right to accept donations from Lebanese nationals by a decision of its Council and the approval of the Minister of National Education, and it shall have the right to accept donations from foreigners by a decision of its Council and the approval of the Council of Ministers.
The Lebanese University shall carry out the functions of public higher education in its various branches and degrees and shall organise its examinations.

The President of the Lebanese University shall be appointed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, or the Ministry shall conclude an agreement with him which is ratified by the Council of Ministers.

The President of the Lebanese University shall assume the management of its academic, financial, and administrative affairs. He shall represent the University in the rights it holds and the obligations incumbent upon it. He shall have a permanent delegation from the Minister of National Education to exercise the financial powers enjoyed by the Minister, with respect to the financial affairs of the University.
At the end of each academic year, the President of the University shall submit a report to the Minister on the financial, administrative, and academic affairs of the University.

The Secretary-General of the University, the deans of the faculties, and the directors of the institutes shall be appointed by decree, upon the recommendation of the President of the Lebanese University. The professors and assistant professors shall be appointed upon his recommendation and the approval of the University Council.

The University Council shall be composed of: the President of the University as Chairman, the deans of the faculties, the directors of the institutes, and one professor from each faculty and institute elected by his colleagues as members, and the Secretary of the University as Secretary. The competence of the Council shall include examining the affairs of the University in general, proposing the establishment of such faculties and institutes as it may need, considering the nominations of professors, assistant professors, contracted lecturers, and lecturers, and establishing and amending the curricula.

The University Council shall meet upon the convocation of the President of the University at least four times a year. This shall be in October, January, April, and June, on the date fixed by the President of the University. The President may convene the Council to meet whenever he deems it necessary, and whenever half of the members submit to him a reasoned written request.

Each faculty or institute shall have a board of administration composed of the dean of the faculty or the director of the institute as Chairman, and four professors elected by the professors of the faculty or institute as members. Its function shall be to examine the particular affairs of the faculty or institute.

The sessions of the University Council and the councils of the faculties and institutes shall not be legal unless attended by more than half of the members. Decisions shall be taken by a majority of votes; in the event of a tie, the side which includes the President shall prevail.

The professors of each faculty or institute, the assistant professors, and the contracted professors therein shall nominate one of themselves as dean or director. The result shall be submitted to the University Council. If it approves it, the President of the University shall propose to the Minister of National Education the appointment of the elected person as dean or director for a period of three years. The dean or director shall receive a monthly allowance equivalent to one third of his salary.
The deans of the faculties and the directors of the institutes shall submit, at the end of each term of the academic year, a detailed report to the President of the University.

The teaching body at the University shall consist of: - Professors and assistant professors, who are permanent cadre employees. - Contracted professors, who are those with whom the University contracts to give hours in the various teaching subjects. - Lecturers, who are those whom the University assigns to deliver lectures on special topics.

For the appointment of an assistant professor, it is required: that he hold a teaching licence degree or its equivalent and have practised teaching in higher or secondary institutes for a period of eight years at least. Or that he hold a certificate of competency from the Higher Teachers Institute and have practised teaching in higher or secondary institutes for a period of five years at least. Or that he hold a "State Doctorate" degree or its equivalent, and have practised teaching in higher or secondary institutes for a period of three years at least.
The assistant professor shall be confirmed in his post after the expiry of one year from his appointment, or dismissed from service for professional incompetence.

For the appointment of a professor, it is required: - That he hold a "State Doctorate" degree or its equivalent. - That he have practised higher education for a period of ten years at least. - That the University Council nominate him for direct appointment to this rank.
The professor shall be deemed confirmed in his post immediately upon his appointment.
An assistant professor of the first grade shall be promoted to the rank of professor if the University Council nominates him for a vacant post.

For the appointment of contracted professors and lecturers, it shall be required that they hold at least a teaching licence degree or its equivalent, or be among those who have a literary, scientific, or artistic work of recognised value, the assessment of which shall revert to the University Council, and that they have practised higher education for a period of at least five years or secondary or vocational educational teaching for a period of at least ten years.

Contracted professors and lecturers may be civil servants or others, Lebanese or foreigners. No distinction shall be made between them in salary, allowance, and remuneration except with respect to the academic degree in accordance with the rates proposed by the University Council.

For the appointment of the Higher Education Inspector, it shall be required: - That he hold a "State Doctorate" certificate or its equivalent. - That he have practised higher education for a period of at least ten years.
There shall be established in the Lebanese University the "Higher Teachers Institute" to prepare teachers for secondary schools.

The duration of study at the Higher Teachers Institute shall be three years, at the end of which a teaching licence (Licence) shall be awarded in each of the branches of specialisation set forth in Articles Thirty-Eight and Thirty-Nine. This study shall be completed by a fourth year dedicated to educational studies and applications, at the end of which the Certificate of Competency for Secondary Teaching shall be awarded.

The Higher Teachers Institute shall comprise two branches: literary and scientific. The professors of each branch shall nominate a professor from among themselves to head it, and shall submit the nomination to the University Council for approval. a- The literary branch shall comprise five sections: 1- Arabic Language and its Literature. 2- French Language and its Literature. 3- English Language and its Literature. 4- History and Geography. 5- Philosophy and Social Sciences. b - The scientific branch shall comprise four sections: 1- Mathematics. 2- Physical Sciences. 3- Chemical Sciences. 4- Natural Sciences.
Arabic shall be the language of instruction at the Higher Teachers Institute except in cases where that is impracticable.

(a)- At most thirty students, from among those who pass the entrance competitive examination referred to in Articles 44-48, shall be granted a scholarship for eight months. (b)- The value of this scholarship shall be determined by a decision taken by the President of the University prior to 15 August of each year, within the appropriations allocated for this purpose in the budget of the Institute. (c)- The students to whom the scholarships are allocated shall be selected from among the successful candidates according to the order of their passing ranks. Exempted therefrom shall be those who do not need financial assistance, and the non-official students referred to in Article 50. (d)- Students who win the first thirty places in the final examinations of each year shall be granted a scholarship for the year that follows it. (e)- If the number of eligible students is less than thirty, they shall suffice.

The Literary Branch shall prepare for the following teaching licences: a- Licence in Arabic Language and its Literature b- Licence in French Language and its Literature c- Licence in English Language and its Literature d- Licence in History and Geography e- Licence in Philosophy and Social Sciences
The Scientific Branch shall prepare for the following teaching licences: a- Licence in Mathematics and Physics b- Licence in Physics and Chemistry c- Licence in Natural Sciences

Each licence in the Literary Branch shall consist of a certificate in general culture whose curriculum is laid down by the University Council and which is granted to those who pass the examinations of the first academic year, and of four other certificates as set forth in the forty-first Article. And each licence in the Scientific Branch shall consist of four certificates as set forth in the forty-second Article, provided that the University Council lays down a special curriculum for the first academic year which is added to the curriculum of the certificate prepared in this year, for the purpose of completing the general culture of the students.

Degrees (Licences) in the Literary Branch shall consist, in addition to the Certificate of General Culture provided for in the preceding Article, of the following certificates: A- The Degree in Arabic Language and Literature: 1- A certificate in the History of Arabic Literature 2- A certificate in Arabic Philology and Semitic Languages 3- A certificate in the Civilisation of the Arab Countries 4- A certificate in the History of French Literature or in the History of English Literature B - The Degree in French Language and Literature: 1- A certificate in the History of French Literature 2- A certificate in French Philology 3- A certificate in French Civilisation 4- A certificate in the History of Arabic Literature C- The Degree in English Language and Literature: 1- A certificate in the History of English Literature 2- A certificate in English Philology 3- A certificate in Anglo-Saxon Civilisation 4- A certificate in the History of Arabic Literature D- The Degree in History and Geography of four certificates chosen from among the following certificates: 1- A certificate in Ancient History 2- A certificate in the History of the Middle Ages 3- A certificate in Modern and Contemporary History 4- A certificate in General Geography 5- A certificate in Physical Geography 6- A certificate in Human Geography 7- A certificate in Economic Geography Provided that a student who specialises in History must choose certificates (1), (2), (3) and (4), and a student who specialises in Geography must choose certificate (4), two certificates from among certificates (5), (6) and (7), and one certificate from among certificates (1), (2) and (3). E- The Degree in Philosophy and Social Sciences: 1- A certificate in the History of Philosophy 2- A certificate in Ethics and Sociology, or a certificate in Applied Sociology 3- A certificate in General Psychology 4- A certificate in General Philosophy and Logic

Degrees (Licences) in the Scientific Branch shall consist of the following certificates: A- The Degree in Mathematics and Physics: 1- A certificate in Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry 2- A certificate in Integral and Differential Calculus 3- A certificate in Rational Mechanics 4- A certificate in General Physics B - The Degree in Physics and Chemistry 1- A certificate in Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry 2- A certificate in General Chemistry 3- A certificate in Applied Chemistry 4- A certificate in Integral and Differential Calculus or a certificate in Rational Mechanics C- The Degree in Natural Sciences: 1- A certificate in Physics, Chemistry and Geology 2- A certificate in Botany 3- A certificate in Zoology 4- A certificate in Physiology and Human Anatomy

Courses in the fourth year shall be organised and their curriculum determined, and the curricula of courses in each of the certificates set forth in the forty-first and forty-second Articles shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of National Education and Fine Arts upon the proposal of the President of the University based on the approval of the University Council.
Only students who succeed in the competitive examination organised for this purpose at the beginning of each academic year shall be admitted to the Higher Teachers Training Institute.

The maximum number of students who may be admitted to the Higher Teachers Training Institute shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of National Education upon the proposal of the President of the University at least one month prior to the date of the competitive examination. This number shall be taken from the successful candidates in the competitive examination according to the order of their grades in passing. However, if the number of successful candidates is less than the determined number, the successful candidates shall suffice.

Every person wishing to participate in the competitive examination must be Lebanese, have completed eighteen years of age and not exceeded twenty-five at the end of the year in which the competitive examination is organised, and must hold the Literary Second Part of the Secondary Certificate or its equivalent if he wishes to enrol in the Literary Branch or the Natural Sciences Section in the Scientific Branch, and the Scientific Second Part or its equivalent if he wishes to enrol in the Scientific Branch.
The competitive examination shall be organised and the examining committee appointed by a decision issued by the President of the University upon the proposal of its Council.

The President of the University shall announce the results of the competitive examination based on the report of the examining committee, and the Minister of National Education shall issue a decision admitting the successful candidates as students in the Higher Teachers Training Institute. Whoever among them is an employee shall have his salaries discontinued throughout the years of study, and the period which he spends at the Institute shall not be included in the calculation of his pension.

Every student at the Higher Teachers Training Institute shall submit, immediately upon the issuance of the decision admitting him, an undertaking certified before the Notary Public, to serve for a period of ten years in the position entrusted to him by the Ministry of National Education starting from the date of his leaving the Institute, or to pay five hundred Lebanese pounds for each year he spent therein, and to return the value of the scholarships which he may have received. The Minister of National Education may, if he so wishes, require a reliable guarantee securing this undertaking. If the student is not appointed three months after his graduation to a vacant position, at the rank to which he is legally entitled, he shall be exempted from executing this undertaking.

The Higher Teachers' Institute shall admit unofficial students presented by the bodies supervising private education from among those whom they nominate to practise secondary education in their schools. It shall be a condition for them that they fulfil the conditions imposed on official students. They shall follow the courses and sit for examinations and to obtain diplomas like official students. Unofficial students shall not receive a scholarship and the Ministry shall not undertake to employ them, nor shall they undertake to work in official schools.

After the end of the first year of study at the Higher Teachers' Institute and the announcement of the results of the examinations, the President of the University shall take, upon the proposal of the Director of the Institute, and after consulting the University Council, a decision distributing the successful candidates among the various sections. In this distribution, consideration shall be given to the needs of secondary education and the wishes of the students themselves, and particularly those of them who excel.

The Director of the Higher Teachers' Institute shall draw up, jointly with the Board of Administration, the draft internal regulations of the Institute, and shall submit it to the President of the University for approval and publication.
Official secondary schools shall be established by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers.
The system of education in official secondary schools shall be non-boarding and free of charge.
The number of members of the teaching staff and the number of administrative employees in official secondary schools shall be determined each year in the Budget Law.

The principals of official secondary schools shall be appointed from among the members of their teaching staffs by a decision of the Minister of National Education, provided that they have practised secondary education for a period of at least five years. The principal shall receive an allowance amounting to one quarter of his salary.
The general internal regulations of official secondary schools shall be laid down by a decision issued by the Minister of National Education.

Teaching in public secondary schools shall be undertaken by teachers, secondary education professors, and assistant professors of higher education. Teachers shall teach only in classes corresponding to complementary education classes. Secondary education professors and assistant professors of higher education may teach in all secondary education classes according to their specialisation.

The conditions mentioned in Articles 78 and 79 shall apply to the appointment and confirmation of teachers, and it shall be required for the appointment of secondary education professors that they hold at least a teaching licence, and preference in appointment shall be given to holders of the certificate of competency from the Higher Teachers Institute and then to holders of a teaching licence from the same institute. They shall be appointed as probationers for a period of one year at the end of which they shall be confirmed or dismissed from service for professional incompetence. The conditions mentioned in Article 25 shall apply to the appointment of assistant professors of higher education. A secondary education professor of the first grade may transfer to the rank of assistant professor if a post falls vacant and the candidate fulfils the conditions provided for in Article 25.

It shall be required for the appointment of physical education teachers in secondary schools that they hold a final official diploma from a higher institute of physical education, and that they pass a competitive examination organised by the Ministry of National Education.

It shall be required for the appointment of secondary education inspectors: First: That they hold one of the diplomas mentioned in Article 25 Second: That they have practised teaching for a period of at least ten years in secondary schools or have managed a secondary school for a period of at least five years.

It shall be required for the appointment of physical education inspectors in secondary education that they pass a competitive examination organised by the Ministry, in which the right to participate shall belong: First: To those who hold a diploma from a recognised higher institute of physical education, provided that they have spent a period of at least five years teaching physical education. Second: To physical education inspectors in primary schools if they have spent at least three years in active service.

The Minister of Education shall determine by a decision issued before the first of September each year the maximum number of pupils who may be admitted to each of the secondary schools. These pupils shall be selected from among the successful candidates in a competitive examination organised for this purpose in the first week of October. If a number smaller than the determined number passes the competitive examination, the successful candidates shall suffice.
An annual plan for the construction and equipping of schools shall be drawn up and entered in the budget of the Ministry of National Education.
The school year shall begin on the Monday following the fifth of October and end at the end of June.
General internal regulations for primary and complementary schools shall be established by a decision of the Minister of National Education.
The number of instructors and teachers shall be determined every year in the Budget Law.
Instructors shall work in primary classes alone, and teachers in primary and complementary classes alike.

For the appointment of instructors, it is required that they hold the Primary Teaching Certificate or that they succeed in a competitive examination organised by the Ministry among holders of the Secondary Certificate or its equivalent. Preference in appointment shall be given to holders of the Primary Teaching Certificate. For the appointment of physical education instructors, it is required that they hold the Certificate of the School of Physical Education, and for music and drawing teachers, that they succeed in a competitive examination organised by the Ministry. Physical education, music and drawing instructors shall be entitled to practise teaching in their branch of specialisation in primary and complementary classes alike.

For the appointment of teachers, it is required that they hold the Complementary Teaching Certificate or its equivalent, or that they succeed in a competitive examination organised by the Ministry, in which any person who holds at least the Secondary Certificate or its equivalent and has spent at least five years in teaching shall be entitled to participate. Preference in appointment shall be given to holders of the Complementary Teaching Certificate.
Instructors and teachers shall be appointed as probationers for a period of one year, and shall be confirmed at the end thereof or dismissed from service for professional incompetence.
Every pupil whose average marks in the Elementary Certificate examinations reached at least 13 out of 20 shall be entitled to enroll in secondary schools without a competitive examination.

The conditions applicable to members of the teaching staff in elementary schools, referred to in Articles 81 and 83 of this Legislative Decree, shall apply to the appointment of members of the teaching staff in secondary schools and to their transfer from one post to another.

In addition to the members of the teaching staff included in the cadre, the Ministry of Education may contract with teachers or procure the issuance of a decree appointing teachers to give lessons by the hour.

An elementary school shall be established in every quarter or village if the number of children who are of elementary school age exceeds thirty. Complementary classes shall be added thereto if the number of graduates from the elementary school exceeds twenty pupils. Priority in the establishment of schools shall be given to quarters or villages that are deprived of private schools.

If the number of females who are of elementary school age reaches fifty, a separate school shall be established for them. Otherwise, they shall be admitted with the males, provided that their ages do not exceed twelve.
Elementary and complementary schools shall be free of charge.
Elementary and complementary schools shall be established by decree.

The Government and the local authorities or the inhabitants shall cooperate in bearing the expenses of the schools; the Government shall provide the members of the teaching and administrative staff and pay their salaries, and the local authority or the inhabitants shall provide the school building and its furniture in accordance with the engineering and health conditions determined by the Ministry. As for the rents and equipment expenses that were borne by the State prior to the entry into force of this Legislative Decree, they shall remain at its expense until the end of 1953.
Where there is a vacant post, an instructor of the First Step shall be transferred to the rank of teacher by virtue of career promotion.

The Ministry shall designate, before 15 September of each year, the posts of instructors and teachers. If they fail to join their posts within fifteen days from the date of the opening of the academic year, they shall be deemed to have resigned from service.
New instructors and teachers shall be appointed outside the cities for a period of at least three years.

Instructors and teachers shall not be transferred from their posts to new posts before the expiry of a period of at least three years, except for health or disciplinary reasons or exceptional circumstances, upon a reasoned proposal submitted by the Head of the Inspection Department and referred by the Director to the Minister after approving it. Transfer requests shall only be considered if received from the instructors or teachers concerned, or from school principals, or from the inspector, or from the local administrative authority.

Every school shall have a principal or a head teacher responsible for the proper conduct of work therein from both the administrative and technical standpoints and for the preservation of its building and contents. The principal shall be appointed by the Ministry from among the teachers or instructors where their number in the school exceeds four. Where that number is less than four, it shall appoint a head teacher. As for schools in which there is only one teacher, that teacher shall be responsible for their administration.
The principal or the teacher in charge must contribute to teaching by giving weekly hours determined by the Ministry in proportion to the number of pupils and classes.
The conditions for determining the number of teachers, instructors, and attendants in proportion to the number of pupils and classes in each school shall be laid down by decree.

For the appointment of primary and complementary education inspectors, it shall be required that: First: They have practised primary or complementary teaching for a period of at least ten years. Second: They hold at least the Complementary Teaching Certificate, or its equivalent. Third: They succeed in a competitive examination organised for this purpose.

It is required for the appointment of physical education inspectors in elementary and complementary schools that they succeed in a competitive examination organised by the Ministry of National Education, in which the following shall be entitled to participate: First: Those who hold a certificate from a recognised elementary institute of physical education, provided that they have spent a period of at least five years in teaching. Second: Those who hold a certificate from a recognised higher institute of physical education, provided that they have spent a period of at least three years in teaching.

Pedagogical education comprises the following institutions: First: The Male and Female Teachers' Training College in Beirut. Second: The Rural Teachers' Training Colleges. Third: The School of Physical Education.
The mission of the Male and Female Teachers' Training College is to prepare instructors and teachers for elementary and complementary schools.

The Male and Female Teachers' Training College consists of two branches: an elementary branch, and a complementary branch. The duration of study in each branch is two years, at the end of which are awarded, in the elementary branch, the Elementary Teaching Certificate, and in the complementary branch, the Complementary Teaching Certificate.
Arabic is the language of instruction in the Male and Female Teachers' Training College, except in subjects where this is not feasible.

The Male and Female Teachers' Training College is directly linked to the Central Administration in the Ministry of National Education, provided that it maintains a technical connection with the Higher Teachers' Institute in order to achieve harmony in teaching methods and curricula. Therefore, the Director of the Male and Female Teachers' Training College must continually keep the Director of the Higher Teachers' Institute informed, through the President of the University, of the conditions and affairs of the College, and must take into consideration the technical observations which both of them express in this regard.

The teaching body in the Male and Female Teachers' Training College consists of assistant professors and secondary education professors who are part of the permanent establishment, and of contracted professors who teach by the hour. If the contracted professors do not possess the certificates required under Article Thirty, it is required of them at least that they have practised secondary or pedagogical vocational education for a period of ten years.
Contracted professors may be from among civil servants or others, whether Lebanese or foreign, and the rules that must be adopted to determine their salaries shall be laid down by decree.

As amended by Decree 9322 dated 5/4/1962 (1)

Pupils shall be admitted to each of the two branches of the Male and Female Teachers' Training College following a competitive examination, the date of which shall be set in the second half of September and which shall be organised by a decision issued by the Minister of National Education.

The Minister shall determine, by a decision issued before the first of September, the maximum number of pupils who may be admitted to each of the two branches of the Male and Female Teachers' Training College. The pupils shall be selected from among the successful candidates in the competitive examination according to their order of merit. However, if the number of successful candidates is less than the specified number, only the successful candidates shall be admitted.

(a)- At most seventy pupils from among those who pass the entrance competitive examination for the primary branch shall be granted a scholarship for eight months. (b)- The value of this scholarship shall be determined by a decision taken by the Minister of National Education before 15 August of each year, within the appropriations allocated for this purpose in the Ministry's budget. (c)- The pupils to whom the scholarships are allocated shall be selected from among the successful candidates in the competitive examination according to the order of their grades of success, with the exception of those who do not need financial assistance. (d)- Students who win the first seventy places in the final examinations in the first year shall be granted a scholarship for the second year. (e)- If the number of eligible candidates is less than seventy, only those eligible shall be granted scholarships. (f)- The conditions set forth in the preceding paragraphs shall apply to the successful candidates in the entrance competitive examination for the complementary branch, provided that the number of scholarships allocated to the pupils of each year does not exceed thirty.
The primary branch in the Male and Female Teachers' Training College shall be divided into two sections: a section for male teachers and a section for female teachers.

Instruction in each section shall comprise: 1- General education, particularly in the first year. 2- Technical vocational education, from both the theoretical and scientific aspects, particularly in the second year.

General education shall cover: 1- The Arabic language and its literature. 2- The French language and its literature or the English language and its literature. 3- History and geography, mathematics, sciences, psychology applied to education, sociology and ethics, civic instruction, agriculture, drawing, music, and physical education.

The candidate who wishes to take part in this competitive examination shall submit an application to the Men's and Women's Teacher Training College declaring his wish therein, and shall attach to it the following documents: 1- A certified copy of the identity card. 2- The certificate that entitles him to take part in the competitive examination or an officially certified copy thereof. 3- A health certificate issued by the official medical committee proving that the candidate is free from every illness or infirmity. 4- A certificate of good conduct from the principal of the school in which he was studying or from the local authorities 5- A certified official undertaking to teach in Lebanese public schools for a period of five years, signed by the candidate, in which he and his father or guardian undertake, jointly and severally, to pay one hundred Lebanese pounds for each academic year and to refund the value of the scholarships that may have been paid to him, if he leaves the school or refuses to undertake teaching at the post designated for him by the Ministry, or is expelled from the school or from the post before the expiry of the period of the undertaking. A graduate who is not appointed within three months from the date of his graduation shall be exempted from executing the undertaking.
The entrance competitive examination shall comprise written examinations the subjects of which are taken from the curriculum of the higher primary education stage.

Upon the conclusion of the examinations, the examining committee shall draw up a list of the names of the successful candidates in order of merit, and the Minister shall issue a decision admitting the pupils to the Men's and Women's Teacher Training College in accordance with the provisions of Article ninety-seven.

a- A pupil shall not be promoted from the first year to the second year except after passing the examinations of the first year. b - It shall not be permissible to grant exceptional permission to certain pupils who fail, for compelling reasons, in the examinations of the first year or the second year to return to continue their studies upon the proposal of the Director of the Men's and Women's Teacher Training College based on the marks obtained by the student during the course of the year. However, the student shall not be entitled to spend more than two years in the same class, and in any case, he shall no longer be entitled to receive the scholarship if he had previously received it.

Teachers who are not pupils of the primary section and who are actually practising their functions shall be entitled to sit for the examinations of the first year. Their admission shall be subject to the following conditions: 1- That they hold at least the complementary certificate or its equivalent. 2- That they have taught for at least two years in public schools. Those among them who pass shall be entitled to sit for the examinations of the second year thereafter.
The purpose of the complementary section is to graduate teachers for the complementary classes.

Vocational technical education shall cover. 1- Lessons in ethics relating to the teaching profession, and lessons in school administration. 2- The explanation and interpretation of the curriculum of primary schools and the study and critique of teaching methods and educational means. 3- Lessons in a primary school prepared and delivered by the pupils of the two sections before their peers and under the direction of their teachers. 4- Training for a period of one month out of the last three months of the school year in a primary school with the assistance of the regular teacher of the class, and such training must be organised in a manner that enables the pupil to deliver lessons in each class of the school successively. 5- Preparation for teaching manual work, agricultural exercises, experiments in chemistry and physics, and home economics.
The curricula of these lessons, their subjects, and their weekly hours shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of National Education and Fine Arts.
The Minister shall have the right to divide each class into two or more groups in the two sections of the primary branch.

As amended by Decree No. 70 dated 21/11/1970 and Decree

3801/72)

Every person wishing to participate in the entrance competitive examination for the primary

branch must.

1- Be Lebanese.

2- Every person wishing to participate in the entrance competitive examination to the primary

branch of the male and female teacher training colleges must have completed

nineteen years of age at most during the year in which

the competitive examination is held.

3- Hold at least the Lebanese Intermediate Certificate

or its equivalent.

4- Be free from any illness or infirmity.

5- Undertake to teach in Lebanese public schools for a period of

five years .

6- Undertake to accept the post assigned to him by the Ministry.

Admission to the Complementary Branch shall be open: First: without a competitive examination, to those who excel in the final examinations of the Elementary Branch, provided that their average grade in the subject in which they wish to specialise is at least 12/20, and that they submit a written application, prior to 15 August, expressing their desire to be admitted to the Complementary Branch and specifying the subject in which they wish to specialise. Second: following a competitive examination, to Lebanese nationals holding at least the Lebanese Secondary Certificate or its equivalent, provided that they are between eighteen and twenty-four years of age, are free from any infirmity or disability, and undertake to teach in public schools for a period of five years at the post to which the Ministry appoints them. They must submit an application accompanied by the documents referred to in Article One Hundred and Six.

The subjects of study in the Complementary Branch shall include: First: general lessons delivered to all pupils Second: special lessons delivered to pupils according to the branch of specialisation Third: tests, practical work or lessons under the supervision of the professor Fourth: teaching the subject chosen by the pupil in one of the classes

The Complementary Branch shall be divided into five sections: First: the section of Arabic Language and Literature Second: the section of Foreign Language and Literature Third: the section of History and Geography Fourth: the section of Mathematical, Physical, Chemical, and Natural Sciences Fifth: the section of Home Economics
The subjects of the lessons, their curriculum and their weekly hours shall be determined by a decision of the Minister.
The conditions applicable to the pupils of the Elementary Branch pursuant to Article One Hundred and Nine shall apply to the pupils of the Complementary Branch.
The examinations for the two Teaching Certificates shall have two sessions: the first session in June and the second in October on a date appointed by the Minister.
The Minister of Education shall appoint the examining committees and organise the examinations, and the Director General or the person delegated by him shall preside over them.

The Chairman of the Committee shall announce the names of the successful candidates together with a statement of the following ratings: - Fair: for one whose average grade is 12/20 - Good: for one whose average grade is 14/20 - Very Good: for one whose average grade is 16/20
The Minister shall award the two teaching diplomas.

The current specialisation year at the Male and Female Teachers' Training College shall be deemed equivalent to the first year of the complementary section. Its students shall be entitled to pursue their studies in the second year of this section if they pass the final examination. Article One Hundred and Two

Those who previously graduated from the specialisation year shall be entitled to pursue the studies of the second year of the complementary section in October 1953, provided that they submit an application before the end of July 1953 and attach to it a professional certificate from their direct superior. Article One Hundred and Two

Rural colleges may be established by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers to graduate male and female teachers for primary schools in villages, subject to the following conditions: 1- Students shall be admitted following a competitive examination organised by the Ministry of National Education, in which holders of at least the Primary Certificate shall be entitled to participate. 2- The Minister shall determine, annually, the number of students who may be admitted. 3- The duration of study shall be five years. 4- Graduates of the rural teachers' training colleges shall only be appointed in villages whose population is less than one thousand inhabitants, and they may not subsequently be transferred to others. 5- The Male and Female Teachers' Training College shall supervise the organisation of the rural teachers' training colleges. 6- The cadre of graduates from the rural teachers' training colleges shall be equivalent to the cadre of instructors in primary schools in rank and grades. Article One Hundred and Two
The purpose of the School of Physical Education is to prepare physical education instructors in primary and complementary schools. Article One Hundred and Two

The duration of study at the School of Physical Education shall be two years, at the end of which the Diploma of the School of Physical Education shall be granted to the successful candidates. Article One Hundred and Two
The curricula of theoretical and professional instruction at the School of Physical Education shall be laid down by decree. Article One Hundred and Two
The regime for students at the School of Physical Education shall be non-boarding and free of charge. Article One Hundred and Two

The Minister of National Education shall determine, by a decision issued before the first of September of every year, the number of students who may be admitted to the School of Physical Education, and ten scholarships at most shall be distributed among those who succeed in the competitive examination provided for in the following Article, under conditions similar to the conditions mentioned in Article 98.

There shall be admitted to the first year of the School of Physical Education candidates who hold at least the complementary certificate and succeed in a competitive examination organised by the Ministry of National Education. The students shall be taken from among those who succeed in the competitive examination according to the order of their passing grades. If a number less than the number that may be admitted succeeds, those who succeeded shall suffice.

There shall apply to the organisation of the competitive examination and to the promotion of students from class to class the conditions applicable in the Male and Female Teachers' Training College mentioned in Articles 105 to 109.

Theoretical instruction in the School of Physical Education shall be undertaken by professors to whom apply the conditions applicable to the professors of the Male and Female Teachers' Training College, mentioned in Articles 94 and 95. Vocational instruction shall be undertaken by professors to whom apply the conditions required of physical education inspectors in elementary complementary schools or in secondary schools, referred to in Articles 62 and 88. The cadre of these latter shall be equivalent to the cadre of physical education inspectors.

There shall apply to the graduates of the School of Physical Education the conditions applicable to the graduates of the elementary branch of the Male and Female Teachers' Training College in respect of appointment and confirmation of tenure.
Vocational education shall comprise the following institutions: 1- The School of Arts and Crafts. 2- The vocational schools. 3- The School of Hotelier Education.

Vocational education shall be supervised by a steering council composed in the following manner: The Director General of the Ministry of National Education and Fine Arts, President; The Director of Vocational Education } A delegate from the Ministry of Public Works } A delegate from the Ministry of National Economy } A delegate from the Ministry of Finance } Members; A delegate from the Order of Engineers } A delegate from the Association of Industrialists } The Head of the Cultural Affairs Service at the Ministry of National Education or whomever he delegates, Rapporteur.
Only day pupils shall be admitted to the School of Arts and Crafts. Article One Hundred and Two
Vocational schools shall be established by a decree issued in the Council of Ministers. Article One Hundred and Two

The purpose of vocational schools is to prepare skilled craftsmen and workers in the following trades: carpentry, blacksmithing, electricity, automobile repair, fitting, turning, oxy-acetylene welding, casting, ceramics, weaving, modern plumbing, pipefitting and sanitary installations. Article One Hundred and Two
Some of these trades may be abolished from the curricula of the vocational schools, or new trades may be added by decree. Article One Hundred and Two
The duration of study in the vocational schools shall be three years, at the end of which the "Certificate of Vocational Proficiency" shall be awarded. Article One Hundred and Two

The maximum number of pupils who may be admitted to each of the vocational schools shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of National Education and Fine Arts issued before the first of September of each year. The value of the scholarships referred to in Article 151 shall be determined in the same decision.

An annual competitive examination shall be organised in the first week of October for admission to the vocational schools, and pupils shall be selected from among the successful candidates according to their order of merit. If the number of successful candidates is less than the specified number, only the successful candidates shall be admitted.
Only Lebanese nationals holding at least the Primary Certificate shall be entitled to take part in the competitive examination.

The regulations of the Steering Council shall be laid down and its powers determined by decree, provided that they include studying vocational education programmes and methods with a view to improving and amending them when necessary, assisting the Director of Vocational Education in preparing the budget, determining the quantities and types of materials, supplies, machinery and tools needed by each institution, and laying down regulations for the disposal of factory products. The One Hundred and Second Article
Study curricula shall be laid down by decree upon the proposal of the Minister of National Education and Fine Arts, after consulting the Steering Council. The One Hundred and Second Article

The purpose of the School of Arts and Crafts is to graduate foremen and instructors in the following branches: 1- The Building Branch. 2- The Civil Engineering Branch. 3- The Mechanics Branch. 4- The Industrial Chemistry Branch. The One Hundred and Second Article

The duration of study at the School of Arts and Crafts shall be three years, at the end of which a "Deputy Engineer" certificate in the branch in which he specialises shall be awarded to anyone who obtains an average of 20/13 and above, and a "Completion of Studies" certificate shall be awarded to anyone who obtains an average between 20/10 and 20/13. The One Hundred and Second Article

The maximum number of pupils who may be admitted to the first year of the School of Arts and Crafts shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of National Education and Fine Arts issued before the first of September of each year. The value of the scholarships referred to in Article 142 shall be determined in the same decision. The One Hundred and Second Article

An annual competitive examination shall be organised in the first week of October for admission to the School of Arts and Crafts. Pupils shall be taken from among the successful candidates therein according to the sequence of their passing grades. However, if the number of successful candidates is less than the specified number, the successful candidates shall suffice. The One Hundred and Second Article
Only Lebanese holding at least the Complementary Certificate or its equivalent shall be entitled to participate in the competitive examination. The One Hundred and Second Article

The first ten successful candidates in the competitive examination shall be granted a monthly scholarship for nine months, whereas the other pupils shall not receive any scholarship. The same number of scholarships shall be given to the first ten successful candidates in the final annual examinations. If the number of successful candidates is less than ten, the successful candidates shall suffice. The One Hundred and Second Article

In every vocational school, the first ten successful candidates in the competitive examination shall be granted a monthly stipend for nine months. The other pupils shall not receive any stipend. The same number of stipends shall be given to the first ten successful candidates in the final annual examinations. If the number of successful candidates is less than ten, the stipends shall be limited to those successful candidates.
Only day students shall be admitted to vocational schools.
The purpose of the School of Hotel Instruction is to prepare ordinary employees and specialist employees for hotels, restaurants, and cafes.

The School of Hotel Instruction shall have two branches: an elementary branch for graduating ordinary employees, the duration of study in which shall be two years, and a higher branch for graduating specialist employees in management, cooking, and service, the duration of study in which shall be three years.

The maximum number of pupils who may be admitted annually to each of the two branches shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of National Education and Fine Arts prior to the first of September after consulting the Ministry of National Economy (Tourism and Summer Resorting).

An annual competitive examination shall be organised in the first week of October for admission to the two branches of the School of Hotel Instruction, and pupils shall be selected from among the successful candidates according to their order of merit in passing. If the number of successful candidates is less than the specified number, admission shall be limited to those successful candidates.

Only Lebanese nationals holding at least the Elementary Certificate shall be entitled to participate in the competitive examination of the elementary branch, and only Lebanese nationals holding at least the Complementary Certificate shall be entitled to participate in the competitive examination of the higher branch, provided that graduates of the elementary branch shall be entitled to enrol in the higher branch without a competitive examination, if they submit an application therefor prior to 15 August.
Only boarding pupils shall be admitted to the School of Hotel Instruction, and they shall not be given any stipend.

For the appointment of a vocational instructor, it is required that he hold the old certificate of the School of Arts and Crafts or the Certificate of Vocational Competency, or that he be a specialist, and that he succeed in a competitive examination organised for this purpose. Holders of the Certificate of Completion of Studies from the School of Arts and Crafts shall be exempted from the competitive examination.

For the appointment of a vocational workshop foreman, it is required that he be one of the employees mentioned in the preceding Article who have spent at least ten years in service, or that he hold the "Assistant Engineer" certificate from the School of Arts and Crafts, and that he pass a competitive examination organised for this purpose. Holders of the Certificate in Engineering from a recognised institute shall be exempted from the competitive examination.

For the appointment of a technical professor and chief of workshops, it is required that he hold a higher degree in engineering or in sciences from a recognised institute, or that he pass a competitive examination organised for this purpose, in which the employees mentioned in the preceding Article are entitled to participate if they have spent at least ten years in service.
Hourly teachers may be appointed by decree, in addition to the members of the teaching staff included in the cadre, within the limits of the appropriations allocated in the budget.

The Minister of National Education shall grant the two certificates of the School of Arts and Crafts and of Higher Hotel Education, and the Director General shall grant the two certificates of Vocational Competency and of Primary Hotel Education.

The School of Arts and Crafts and the vocational schools may sell their manufactured products under conditions proposed by the Steering Council and approved by decree, provided that the price of the materials used in these manufactured products reverts to the Public Treasury, and that the net profits are distributed among the pupils at the rate of twenty percent for outstanding pupils, and eighty percent as a trust for graduates to assist them in establishing a business for themselves after leaving the school.
The purpose of the Conservatory of Music is to disseminate the musical art and to graduate musicians and music teachers.
The curricula of studies at the Conservatory of Music shall be established, and its branches and the years of study therein shall be determined, by decree.
The Directorate of Antiquities shall consist of departments and sections whose powers shall be determined by decree.

The technical cadre in the Directorate of Antiquities shall consist of employees subject to pension deductions and employees not subject thereto. As for the employees subject to pension deductions, they are: the Conservator-General of Antiquities, archaeologists and engineers - and heads of laboratories - trainee archaeologists. As for the employees not subject thereto, they are: foremen of works - workshop heads and specialist technicians - specialist workers and supervisors.

The following rules shall apply to the appointment of employees not subject to pension deductions: (a) Specialist workers are required to pass a competitive examination open to holders of the Vocational Proficiency Certificate or to specialists, and supervisors are required to be from among the antiquities guards who have completed at least five years in service. (b) Workshop heads and specialist technicians are required to pass a competitive examination open to holders of a "Certificate in Engineering" from a recognised institute or an "Assistant Engineer" certificate from the School of Arts and Crafts or its equivalent, or to specialist workers who have spent at least ten years in service, if they are required to carry out drafting or surveying works. They are required to possess sufficient experience if they are required to work as instructors or photographers. (c) Foremen of works are required to be from among the workshop heads or specialist technicians who have spent at least four years in the first grade.

The following rules shall apply to the appointment of employees subject to pension deductions: (a) Trainee archaeologists are required to hold at least the certificate of the Institute of Oriental Letters in Beirut (Diploma) or a Bachelor of Science degree from the American University in the Department of History. (b) Archaeologists are required to hold the certificate of the Higher Schools of Antiquities. Engineers are required to hold a certificate from a recognised school of engineering. Heads of laboratories are required to hold a teaching licence (Licence d'enseignement) in chemistry or in physics-chemistry or to be graduates of higher institutes specialised in chemistry. If the engineer is an architect and a graduate of a higher institute specialised in the restoration of antiquities, he shall be classified upon his appointment in the sixth grade. (c) The Conservator-General of Antiquities is required to be from among the archaeologists or architects who have spent at least fifteen years in office.
All technical and administrative employees shall be appointed upon the recommendation of the Conservator-General. Priority in the appointment of guards shall be given to retired members of the Army.
The duties and posts of administrative employees shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of National Education upon the recommendation of the Conservator-General.
The Ministry of Education may contract with specialists to carry out technical excavation, restoration and classification works upon the recommendation of the Conservator-General.

For the appointment of the Curator of the National Library, it is required that he be a graduate of an institute specialising in the art of library organisation, hold its final certificate and possess attested experience.

For the appointment of the Assistant Curators at the National Library, it is required that they be graduates of institutes specialising in the art of library organisation and hold the final certificate in those institutes. They shall be appointed after obtaining the opinion of the Curator of the National Library.
Trainee Curators shall be appointed from among graduates of institutes of Oriental letters, Orientalism or archives.

A committee shall be formed composed of: The Director-General of the Ministry of National Education and Fine Arts or whomever he delegates. Chairman The President of the Lebanese University } The Conservator-General of Antiquities } Members The Curator of the National Library } Its mission shall be to examine the affairs of the National Library in general, prepare its budget, draw up a programme for the purchase of the books, periodicals and other publications and archives it requires and establish regulations enabling the National Library to fulfil its mission in the fullest manner.

University students and pupils who currently benefit from a maintenance grant at one of the institutes affiliated with the Ministry, shall retain their grant until the end of their studies, and if one of them fails the examinations the grant shall be discontinued for him.
The system of education at the Conservatory of Music shall be non-residential and free of charge.
The Minister of National Education shall determine, prior to the first of September of each year, the number of students who may be admitted to the first year of the Conservatory of Music.

A competitive examination for admission to the Conservatory shall be organized during the first week of October, the conditions of which shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of National Education.

The examinations of the Conservatory of Music shall have a single session, the date of which shall be determined at the end of the school year, and the conditions of which shall be laid down by the Minister of National Education.

The Minister of National Education shall grant those who pass the final examinations the "Diploma of the Conservatory of Music", and the diploma shall state the name of the branch in which the student specialized and the grade of his success.
The Director of the Conservatory of Music and its professors shall be engaged by way of contract for the academic year or for a number of weekly hours.

The Directorate of Antiquities shall undertake all administrative and technical works relating to antiquities. (a)- Its administrative competence shall include, in particular, preparing draft laws and regulations relating to antiquities and excavation works, supervising their implementation and completing the administrative transactions required therefor, supervising the trade in and exportation of antiquities, and pursuing contraventions and offences provided for in the laws and regulations relating to antiquities. (b)- And its technical competence shall include, in particular, establishing and managing museums and striving to expand them and develop their archaeological wealth, organizing temporary exhibitions and archaeological zones and carrying out archaeological excavations, supervising the activity of scientific excavation missions, exploring historical sites and collecting information relating thereto, maintaining archaeological buildings, issuing temporary or permanent publications on antiquities, museums and historical sites, and photographing antiquities and publishing the photographs.

A Conservator-General of Antiquities, Museums and Archaeological Buildings, appointed by decree in accordance with the provisions set forth in Article one hundred and seventy-eight, shall head the Directorate of Antiquities and its employees and supervise its works.

The following principles shall be adopted in the special regulations governing domestic scholarships, referred to in the Sixth Article of this Legislative Decree, commencing from the financial year 1954: a- The children of martyrs in respect of whom a decree requiring their assistance has been issued shall be granted scholarships for primary, secondary and higher education if they are still pursuing their studies and succeeding therein. b - The Minister of National Education shall determine, by a decision issued prior to the first of May of each year, within the appropriations allocated in the budget, the number and amount of scholarships that may be allocated to students and pupils of higher and secondary education in private institutes other than the children of martyrs. c- Every applicant for a scholarship must be Lebanese, his guardians must be unable to cover the expenses of his studies, and he must be of attested competence. d- Schools shall attest to the competence of the students and pupils belonging to them and to their financial need. They shall nominate, under conditions determined by decree, a number of their students or pupils to benefit from the scholarships. e- The Ministry of National Education shall have the right, in order to verify competences, to conduct such investigations as it deems fit prior to taking a final decision regarding the scholarships, or to hold competitive examinations among the candidates.

Equivalences of certificates shall be adjudicated by a committee composed of: The Director General of the Ministry of National Education, Chairman; The President of the Lebanese University or a delegate thereof } The President of Saint Joseph University or a delegate thereof } The President of the American University or a delegate thereof } Members; The President of the Lebanese Academy or a delegate thereof } The Head of the Cultural Affairs Service at the Ministry of National Education, Rapporteur. The regulations of this Committee shall be laid down by decree, provided that allowance is made therein for each Ministry to delegate a representative thereof, upon the invitation of the Committee, whenever the deliberations concern a certificate pertaining to that Ministry. The representative of the Ministry shall be deemed a member of the Committee participating in deliberations and voting.
All provisions contrary to this Legislative Decree or inconsistent with its content are hereby repealed.
This Legislative Decree shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The School of Home Economics, the Institute of Statistics attached to the Lebanese University, and the Technical Branch in the Higher Teachers' Training College are hereby abolished, provided that the students and pupils currently enrolled in these institutions shall continue their studies until the completion thereof, unless they fail the examinations.

Substitute teachers shall be confirmed in the rank of instructor of the tenth grade or dismissed from service. The Ministry of National Education shall entrust to special committees the matter of verifying their competence.

Administrative and technical employees in the various departments and institutions attached to the Ministry of National Education shall be appointed without being bound by the provisions of appointment, promotion, transfer, and classification stipulated in this Legislative Decree, during a period ending on 15 April 1953.

The following principles shall be adopted in the special regulations governing scholarships for specialization abroad, referred to in the sixth Article of this Legislative Decree: a- The Minister of National Education shall determine, by a decision issued before 15 August of each year, within the appropriations allocated in the budget, and after consulting the institutions of higher education and the Ministries of the State, the number and amount of scholarships that may be granted for specialization abroad, the branches of specialization, and the duration of study for each scholarship, and he may designate the institute or institutes in which courses must be pursued. b - A competitive examination shall be organized before the first of October of each year to select the candidates, and these candidates shall be required to be Lebanese, not of wealthy means, and to fulfil the academic conditions determined in the regulations. c- The Ministry of National Education shall follow up the activity of the students to verify the good progress of their studies and their compliance with the conditions under which they were granted the scholarship. d- The scholarship shall be cancelled if the student fails in his studies, or changes the branch of specialization for which he was dispatched. e- The Minister of National Education may make the granting of certain scholarships conditional upon the submission of an undertaking by the students to work in Government departments for a period of five years at least after completing their studies. f- Employees shall be entitled to obtain a scholarship within the conditions specified in the preceding paragraphs, provided that their salaries shall be suspended throughout the duration of their absence, and the period they spend abroad shall not be included in their pension calculation.
The urgent draft law referred to the Chamber of Deputies pursuant to Decree No. 12539 dated 16 April 1963 is hereby put into effect, and its text is as follows:
This Decree shall be published in the Official Gazette.

1 - A National Social Security Fund is hereby established, referred to in the course of this Law as "the Fund", which shall undertake the administration of the social security system and its various branches.

2 - The Fund is an independent institution of a social nature subject to the provisions of this Law and enjoying legal personality and financial and administrative autonomy. Its head office shall be in Beirut and it shall have the right to establish regional and local offices.

3 - Within the limits set forth in Article 3 of this Law, the Fund shall be subject to:

A - The tutelage of the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs through a Government Commissioner whose powers shall be determined by an implementing decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.

B - The prior tutelage of the Council of Ministers.

C - The subsequent audit of the Court of Accounts without any prior audit.

4 - A  The organs of the Fund shall consist of:

- A Board of Directors,

- A Technical Committee,

- An Investment Committee,

- The Director General of the Fund, to whom the Secretariat shall be subordinate.

5 - The Fund shall not be subject to the supervision of the Civil Service nor to the supervision of the Central Inspection, and the provisions of Legislative Decree No. 150 issued on 12 June 1959 shall not apply to it.

The powers of the Board of Directors of the Fund shall cover in particular the following matters:

1- Acts requiring a decree taken in the Council of Ministers:

b - Authorising the Director General to acquire or sell immovable property the value of which exceeds the amount specified in the internal regulations, where such property is allocated to the internal operation of the Fund or to the social services under its direct authority.

2 - Acts requiring the approval of the supervisory authority:

(As amended by Law No. 12/78 dated 24/4/78 - Official Gazette No. 18):

a - Approving all the internal regulations of the Fund, the staff regulations, and the scale of ranks and salaries for the various bodies of the Fund.

b - Approving the administrative budget of the Fund and the annexed budgets.

c - Deciding on the closing of the accounts of the administrative budget, the annexed budgets, and all other accounts of the Fund, and approving the balance sheet and the reports and explanatory statements specified in the regulations of the Fund.

d - Determining priorities in social investments.

e - Determining the bases for establishing local and regional offices.

3 - Acts decided upon by the Bureau:

(As amended by Law No. 12/78 dated 24/4/78 - Official Gazette No. 18):

a - Decisions which the law does not require to be submitted to the Council of Ministers and those which do not require the approval of the supervisory authority.

b - Decisions that must be taken as a result of the reports of the Technical Committee or the observations of the supervisory authority which are of an administrative or technical nature and do not require re-submission to the Council of Ministers or to the supervisory authority.

c - Appointing employees of the third and second categories as a result of a competitive examination in accordance with the provisions of Article Six of this Law.

4 - The Board of Directors shall submit within a period of eight days to the supervisory authority, through the Government Commissioner and accompanied by his opinion, the decisions provided for in the first and second paragraphs of this Article, and shall attach thereto the minutes of the meeting relating to them.

5 - If the supervisory authority does not notify the Board of Directors of its reasoned refusal,

within a period of one month from the date of its receipt of the decisions submitted to it, such decisions shall be deemed approved by operation of law upon the expiry of the said period.

The same shall also apply with respect to the decisions submitted to the Council of Ministers pursuant to the first paragraph, item, b, of this Article.

6 - The Board of Directors may request the Council of Ministers to settle any dispute that may arise between it and the supervisory authority

1 - Composition of the Board of Directors of the Fund

The Board of Directors shall be composed of delegates, among whom are specialised experts, representing the State, employers and workers, in accordance with the following:

(a) - The Expert Delegates:

- Two (2) experts with an alternate expert, representing the State, who shall be selected from the schedule mentioned in clause (e) below.

- Four (4) experts with an alternate expert representing the "most representative professional bodies" of employers,

- Four (4) experts with an alternate expert representing the "most representative professional bodies" of wage-earners.

(b) - Within three months from the date of publication of this Law, and upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour, there shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers the "most representative bodies" referred to in clause (a) above, and the conditions and manner of electing the delegates representing these bodies, both ordinary and expert, provided that the widest possible representation of existing sectors is observed therein.

(c) - Within three months from the date of publication of this Law, and at the request of the Minister of Labour, the Civil Service Board shall prepare:

- A special list for the category of experts representing the State,

- A special list for the experts representing each of the employers and the wage-earners,

each of which shall include the university degrees, specialisations, the "matrix" of required skills and competencies, experiences and years of experience in subjects related to social insurance, provided that the two principal expert delegates and the alternate representing the workers shall have experience of not less than seven (7) years.

(d) - The two lists mentioned in clause (c) above shall be issued by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour.

(e) - The Civil Service Board shall draw up a schedule for the category of experts representing the State containing the names of the experts who fulfil the conditions and specifications in accordance with the special list pertaining to them above, so that the State may select from among them its representatives referred to in clause (a) above, and shall notify it to the Minister of Labour.

(f) - The Civil Service Board shall, at the request of the Minister of Labour, undertake the review of these lists, the two lists mentioned in clause (c) and the schedule mentioned in clause (e) above, three months prior to the expiry of the term of office of each Board of Directors of the Fund.

2 - Mechanism for Appointing Delegates

(a) - The representatives of the State shall be appointed pursuant to a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour.

(b) - The election of the experts and delegates representing the employers and wage-earners, who are elected in accordance with clause (1 b) of this Article, shall be ratified pursuant to a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour.

3 - Term of Office and Allowances

(a) - A delegate shall be appointed for a term of five years, renewable once.

(b) - New delegates shall be appointed, or their election ratified, at least two months prior to the expiry of the current term of office.

(c) - The Board of Directors shall, after the expiry of its term of office, continue to perform its duties until a new Board of Directors is appointed.

(d) - The Board of Directors shall elect, at its first meeting, a Chairman, a Vice-Chairman and a Secretary, and in the event of an equality of votes for each of them, the oldest shall be appointed.

(e) - All the delegates, the Chairman, the Vice-Chairman and the Secretary shall receive a lump-sum allowance for actual attendance at each meeting of the Board,
