- The amount of this allowance and the maximum limit of the sums that may be received per month shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour,

- The Chairman of the Board, the Vice-Chairman, the Secretary and the other delegates may not receive any other wage or allowance in consideration of any work performed for the benefit of the Fund.

4 - Decision-Making and Voting:

Decisions in the Board shall be taken by an absolute majority, and each delegate shall have one vote; in the event of an equality of votes, the Chairman shall have a casting vote. Provided that the majority that voted in the Board of Directors for the decision taken shall include the absolute majority of each of the representatives of the State, the employers and the wage-earners; and if that is not achieved in a first sitting, the Board shall be convened to a second sitting to vote on the same decision by the absolute majority of the members of the Board without distinction, provided that the interval between the date of the first sitting and the convening of the second sitting shall not be less than a period of two weeks.

5 - Internal Regulations:

The Board shall lay down its internal regulations and determine the dates of its meetings, and it shall meet at the convocation of its Chairman once a month, and it may hold extraordinary meetings if so requested of it in writing by at least five delegates or at the request of the Minister of Labour, the Chairman of the Technical Committee, the Chairman of the Investment Committee or the Director General.

6 - Engagement of Experts:

The Board of Directors may engage specialised and qualified external experts and seek their opinion and expertise, in accordance with their specialisations, on the various subjects submitted to it for study and/or for taking decisions thereon.

1 - The Technical Committee is a permanent body among the bodies of the Fund that exercises the functions specified for it in this Law and in the regulations of the Fund.

a - With respect to the Chairman of the Committee: that he be from among the First Category employees in the general administrative cadre of the State or from among those entitled to be promoted to this Category. Or that he hold a university degree (licence) obtained after having obtained the Baccalaureate, Part Two, or its equivalent in the fields of law or financial, economic or commercial sciences, with practical experience in his field of specialisation of not less than ten years after obtaining the degree.

b - With respect to the two members: that he be from among the Second Category employees in the general administrative cadre of the State or from among those entitled to be promoted to this Category, or that he hold a university degree for which the duration of study is not less than three years after having obtained the Baccalaureate, Part Two, or its equivalent in the same fields required for appointment to the post of Chairman of the Technical Committee, with experience in the member's field of specialisation for a period of not less than five years after obtaining the university degrees.

5 - The service of the Chairman of the Committee or of either of its two members may be terminated by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, for any of the reasons provided for in paragraph a of the Fifth Article of this Law and after conducting an investigation whose rules and manner of conduct shall be determined in special regulations approved by the Board of Directors and subject to ratification by the Supervisory Authority.

12 -

a - The appropriations pertaining to the Technical Committee shall be provided for in the administrative budget of the Fund.

13 - The Technical Committee shall undertake:

Social Security shall comprise the following branches:

a - Sickness and maternity insurance.

b - Work accidents and occupational diseases insurance.

c - The system of family and educational allowances.

d - The end-of-service indemnity system.

And it shall be implemented in three stages.

The first stage shall commence at most eighteen months from the date of publication of this Law in the Official Gazette, and a decree taken in the Council of Ministers, upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and Social Affairs and the recommendation of the Board of Directors, shall determine the date on which the implementation of each of the branches set out in the preceding Article shall commence.

The second stage shall commence at most two years from the date of putting the last branch of the first stage into effect.

The third stage shall commence at least two years from the date of putting the second stage into effect.

In the second stage, all Lebanese wage-earners, whether workers or employees, trainees or apprentices, working on Lebanese territory in an agricultural enterprise for the account of one or more employers, whether Lebanese or foreign, shall be subject to the provisions of this Law.

If such wage-earners are foreigners, they shall not be subject to the provisions of this Law except under the conditions set forth in paragraph 4 of the preceding Article.

In each of the first three branches mentioned in Article 7 above, a special section shall be established for voluntarily insured persons.

It shall be an independent accounting section in which financial balance must be achieved.

The persons mentioned below may affiliate with each section from the first stage:

a - Persons who perform work or render services for the account of their spouses or their direct ascendants or descendants, at the request of their employer.

b - Persons who were affiliated with the branches of sickness and maternity, work accidents, and end-of-service, and who no longer fulfil the affiliation therewith. Provided that they are residing on Lebanese territory and that they submit their application within the three months following the date on which their compulsory affiliation ended.

The persons referred to below may affiliate with each section from the second stage:

a - Employers and agricultural workers belonging to each of the categories mentioned in paragraphs a and b of this Article.

b - Non-agricultural employers and self-employed workers, unless the Council of Ministers accepts, upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and Social Affairs and the recommendation of the Board of Directors, their affiliation with the Fund from the first stage.

1 - Insurance shall cover insured persons and the members of their families.

b - The partner (the husband and the wife) who does not engage in remunerated employment or is not a worker or a producer in any capacity and does not receive a retirement pension. Lawful wives.

c - The legitimate and adopted children of the insured person and the children under his guardianship or compulsory tutorship, until they attain the age of eighteen completed years, and if the children are unable to earn their living by reason of devoting their full time to their studies, they shall benefit from the insurance until the age of twenty-five completed years.

1 - Sickness and maternity benefits shall not be due unless the insured person has been a contributor to social security throughout at least three months during the six months preceding the date of medical verification or the date of death.

1 - An insured person who suffers, as a result of a work accident or an occupational disease, a temporary incapacity for work verified by a physician approved by the Fund, shall be entitled to receive a temporary incapacity indemnity for the cessation of his wage for each day of interruption from work, without distinction between the working days of the establishment and its non-working days, starting from the eleventh day of the date of cessation of work. The employer shall be obliged to pay the full wages of the first ten days of the incapacity, and he shall also bear, in the cases determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and Social Affairs and the recommendation of the Board of Directors of the Fund in accordance with the types of occupational activities of the establishments, the whole or part of the difference between the incapacity indemnity as determined in paragraph 2 of this Article and the average daily earnings determined in paragraph 3 thereof, and for the periods determined by the same decree.

2 - The amount of the indemnity for temporary incapacity shall be equal to three quarters of the average daily earnings, and half of such earnings in the event that the insured person is in hospital.

3 - The average daily earnings adopted for calculating the temporary incapacity indemnity is that resulting from the total earnings defined in Articles 68 and following of this Law which the person concerned received during the twelve months preceding the date of cessation of work divided by 360. However, if the insured person did not work during the period of the twelve months, or if the commencement of his work goes back to less than the period of twelve months, the wages adopted for calculating the average daily earnings shall be those which the insured person would have actually received had he worked under the same conditions during the said period.

In the event that the annual earnings taken as a basis for calculating the indemnity exceed twice the annual maximum limit fixed in Article 68 of the Social Security Law, it shall be reduced to that amount. The Council of Ministers may fix a minimum limit for the daily indemnity for temporary incapacity by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and Social Affairs and the recommendation of the Board of Directors after taking into consideration the legislation relating to the minimum wage and cost-of-living increases.

4 - Temporary incapacity indemnities shall be paid either until the recovery of the insured person or until the date of commencement of the permanent incapacity pension as determined in paragraph 6 of Article 35 below.

5 - The provisions of paragraph 3 of Article 24 and Article 25 of this Law shall apply to work accident indemnities.

6 - The internal regulations of the Fund shall determine the manner of application of the provisions of the paragraphs set out above.

The survivors' pension shall fall due:

A - In the event of the death of an insured person who was receiving a disability pension, as from the first day of the month following the month during which the death of the insured person occurred.

B - In the event of the death of an insured person who had not yet received a disability pension, as from the date of death.

C - The pension shall be payable as from the two dates set out above if the application for the pension is submitted within the six months following the date of death. In other cases, the pension shall fall due as from the first day of the month following the month during which the application was submitted.
The survivors' pension shall be paid in advance, and the methods of its payment shall be determined in the Internal Regulations.

The right to the pension shall lapse upon the death of the beneficiary thereof or on the date of the marriage of the widow or widower. In this latter case, the widower or widow shall be entitled to a sum of money equal to the total of his or her pensions for three years.

The right of the remaining beneficiaries to the survivors' pension shall lapse if the conditions required for obtaining it are no longer met by them, as from the end of the month during which the said conditions ceased to be met. In the event that the right of one of the beneficiaries lapses for the reasons set out above, his share shall be distributed among the remaining beneficiaries, subject to the application of the provisions of paragraph 2 of Article 40.

In the event of the death of the insured person as a result of a work accident or an occupational disease, a lump-sum compensation shall be paid to the survivors specified in Article 39 of this Law, the amount of which shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and Social Affairs and the recommendation of the Board of Directors of the Fund.

A Family and Educational Allowances Fund shall be established; its organisation is determined in this Title and its resources in Chapter Three, Title One, Book Three, of this Law.

1 - Family and educational allowances shall be granted to the wage-earners mentioned in paragraph /1/ of Article 9 and in Article 10 of this Law, to persons entitled to sickness and maternity insurance or work accident insurance, as well as to persons incapacitated for work in accordance with Article 35 if the degree of disability exceeds /50/ percent.

2 - Family and educational benefits shall fall due:

A - For each dependent child, as defined in item (C), paragraph /2/ of Article 14.

B - For each dependent child with an infirmity without age limit, as well as for each unmarried and non-working female child up to the completion of her twenty-fifth year of age.

C - For the partner (husband and wife) who does not engage in any remunerated or productive work in any capacity and does not receive a retirement pension. Legitimate wives.

1 - The Fund must review the amount of the pension, either of its own motion or upon the request of the person concerned, if it is established by the medical control in the Fund that a significant aggravation or improvement has occurred after the liquidation of the disability pension. A review shall also take place in the event of the beneficiary's return to work.

2 - However, the pension may not be reviewed when two years have elapsed since its liquidation, except from year to year at least, and this rule shall not apply if a new curative treatment has been used during that time, or if the temporary aggravation of the consequences of the work accident or occupational disease has ceased, or in the event of the beneficiary's return to work.

If the beneficiary of the disability pension is afflicted once again by a work accident or an occupational disease, so that the amount of the pension shall be determined after taking into consideration the total injuries sustained.

And if the annual earnings of the beneficiary upon the occurrence of the last accident or disease exceed the annual earnings that were adopted for calculating the first pension, the new pension shall be calculated on the basis of the higher earnings.

1 - The work accident or occupational disease pension shall be cancelled and the compensations paid without right shall be recovered, where applicable, in the following cases:

a - When the person concerned has obtained or attempted to obtain by way of fraud benefits to which he has no right.

b - When the disease or accident results from a felony or misdemeanour committed by the person concerned or from an intentional fault on his part.

2 - The Fund may suspend the payment of compensations or reduce their value:

a - When the person concerned refuses to submit to the medical and administrative control and examinations provided for in the internal regulations of the Fund, or if he does not comply with the requisition instructions in the event that he has obtained permission to stop work.

b - Throughout the presence of the person concerned outside the country, unless the internal regulations contain contrary provisions.

c - Throughout the period during which the person concerned is serving a custodial penalty.

In the event of the death of the insured person as a result of a work accident or an occupational disease, the persons exclusively specified in the Law put into force pursuant to Decree No. 8496 dated 2/8/1974, and in accordance with the order of priority and the percentages stated therein, shall be entitled to benefit from the survivors' pension specified in Article 40 below.

1 - This pension shall amount to two thirds of the annual earnings as defined in paragraph 5 of Article 35 above.

2 - In the event of the existence of one, single, rightful claimant, this pension shall be reduced to 50 percent of the said earnings.
If the insured person leaves several lawful widows, they shall share equally the compensation provided for the widow.

49-2: Persons compulsorily subject:

1 - The categories concerned:

Every person belonging to the categories set out below, whose age is not less than the minimum working age specified in the laws and regulations in force, irrespective of the duration or form of the employment contract, and whatever the nature of the wage, shall be compulsorily subject to the provisions of this scheme, provided that the work is performed within Lebanese territory:

a - Employees working under an employment contract, for the account of one or more employers, whether Lebanese or foreign.

b - Permanent employees working in an agricultural enterprise provided for in Law No. 8/74 dated 25/3/1974, and in Decree No. 7757 dated 7/5/1974.

c - Lebanese nationals working for the account of the State, municipalities, or any administration, public institution, or autonomous service. Every sector governed by special legal provisions on retirement that differ from those provided for by the Social Security Law shall be exempted from the provisions of this item.

d - Members of the teaching staff in higher education institutions provided for in the Law Regulating Private Higher Education, issued on 26/12/1961, and in the technical institutes provided for in Article 12 of Regulatory Decree No. 7880 dated 25/7/1967, unless they have a compulsory special retirement scheme.

e - Employees contracted in Lebanon with an enterprise having a head office or branch therein, who have commenced their work in Lebanon and have been transferred to work abroad. In this case, the earnings or basic wage shall be taken as the basis for calculating contributions, excluding the allowances paid to them during, or on the occasion of, working abroad.

f - Employers, self-employed persons, and non-permanent employees in agriculture, pursuant to a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the recommendation of the Board of Directors of the Fund and the proposal of the Minister of Labour.

2 - All other categories of persons not mentioned in this Article, for whom the necessity of subjecting them compulsorily to this scheme becomes apparent, shall be determined by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers, upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour after the recommendation of the Board of Directors, and under the conditions specified therein.

3 - Foreign employees

a - Foreign employees working on Lebanese territory, bound to one or more specific employers, and the employers who employ them, shall be subject to all the obligations provided for in the retirement scheme.

b - The foreign employees mentioned in accordance with Paragraph "a" above shall not benefit from the benefits provided for in this scheme unless they hold a work permit in accordance with the laws and regulations in force, provided that the State to which they belong grants reciprocity to Lebanese nationals with respect to the retirement scheme.

c - The States that grant reciprocity to Lebanon shall be determined pursuant to decisions issued by the Board of Directors of the Fund, after consulting the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants.

d If a foreign national entitled to a retirement or disability pension leaves Lebanese territory permanently, his pension shall be converted into a lump sum, unless a law provides otherwise through international agreements between Lebanon and other countries, and the Fund shall have the right to impose a deduction thereon, in accordance with rules determined in its regulations, particularly where the foreign insured person benefits from the minimum guarantees subsidy.

e - In the event that a foreign national who is not eligible to obtain the benefits of this scheme in accordance with items b and c of this Article suffers a disability, dies, or leaves Lebanese territory indefinitely, the notional account of the insured person shall be liquidated and converted into a lump sum, in accordance with the regulations determined by the Board of Directors of the Fund, without applying the minimum guarantees.

f - Foreign employees working in Lebanon under contracts concluded abroad with foreign enterprises shall not be subject to the provisions of this scheme if the employer proves that they benefit, in the country where the contract was concluded or the country to which they belong, from benefits similar to the benefits prescribed in this scheme.

1 - A child shall not confer entitlement to more than one family allowance pursuant to the preceding Article. If several persons meet the required conditions with respect to a single child pursuant to the provisions of the preceding Article, the family allowances shall be paid:

a - To the father if both the father and the mother meet the aforementioned conditions, unless the custody of the children is entrusted to the mother alone.

b - To the adoptive parents or to the guardians when they, like the father and the mother, fulfil the aforementioned conditions.

2 - Family and educational benefits shall be granted for up to five children only for each head of household.

The monthly value of the family benefits provided for in Articles 46 to 48 of the Social Security Law shall be fixed at a maximum amount of /2.250.000/ Lebanese Pounds (only two million two hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese Pounds and no more), distributed as follows:

/600.000/ Lebanese Pounds (six hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds) for the partner (the husband or the wife)

/330.000/ Lebanese Pounds (three hundred and thirty thousand Lebanese Pounds) for each child (for up to five children only).

- Family and educational benefits shall be paid monthly to the wage-earners entitled to the allowance by the employer for the account of the Fund. The debt of family and educational benefits shall be considered a privileged debt and shall rank after the debt of the Treasury, judicial fees and compulsory insurances, even in the event of bankruptcy.

3 - Family and educational benefits paid directly by the employer to his wage-earners in accordance with the procedures specified in the internal regulations of the Fund shall lapse by prescription, if the employer does not settle the account thereof with the Fund within one year from the date of expiry of the time-limit for the maturity of contributions for the same period for which the aforementioned allowances are due.

4 - The period of prescription for family and educational benefits due to insured persons shall be two years starting from the date of their maturity as determined by the internal regulations of the Fund.

5 - The period of prescription for benefits unduly received is two years starting from the date on which the Fund becomes aware that they were not due.

49-1: Establishment of a Retirement Scheme:

A retirement scheme is hereby established, to replace the end-of-service indemnity scheme in all its rights and obligations. Its organisation is defined in this Title and its resources in Chapter Six thereof.

This new scheme shall apply to the persons specified in Articles (49-2) and (49-3) set forth below.

The provisions of the end-of-service indemnity scheme shall remain applicable, on a transitional basis, to the persons referred to in Paragraph (2) of Article (49-4).

49-3: Voluntarily participating persons:

1 - In addition to the insured persons in accordance with Article 49-2, the following may participate in the retirement scheme on a voluntary basis:

a - Lebanese residents in Lebanon who are self-employed, family assistants, employers and non-permanent wage-earners in agriculture, pending the issuance of the decision mentioned in Article (49-2), Paragraph (1), Item (f).

b - Lebanese working abroad, whether wage-earners or non-wage-earners, who are not compulsorily subject to this scheme.

c - Insured persons affiliated with the retirement scheme who, for any reason whatsoever, no longer fulfil the conditions of compulsory subjection.

2 - With respect to voluntary participants, the following provisions shall be observed:

a - The person concerned shall submit an application for affiliation to the Fund, accompanied by the documents specified by the regulations of the Fund.

b - The Fund must decide on the application and notify the person concerned of its decision within a period of two months from the date of registration of the application. Failure to reply within this period shall be deemed an approval of the application.

c - The effect of affiliation, whether the approval is express or tacit, shall commence on the first day of the quarter following the quarter in which the application was registered.

d - Contributions shall be paid monthly or quarterly, and shall be assessed on the basis of a flat-rate income consisting of four brackets or more, from which the insured person chooses the bracket on the basis of which he wishes to contribute.

e - This income, as well as the brackets where necessary, shall be determined and amended by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and the recommendation of the Board of Directors of the National Social Security Fund. The highest bracket must not exceed four times the average wage, subject to any adjustment of the ceiling in accordance with Article (54-1), Paragraph (3), Item (a).

f - Voluntarily insured persons shall benefit from the benefits of this scheme under the conditions specified for compulsorily insured persons.

g - Where necessary, the details of application of this Article, particularly with regard to the effects of early withdrawal from the scheme, shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour after the recommendation of the Board of Directors of the Fund.

49-4: Compulsory subjection and the option of choice:

1 - The following shall be compulsorily subject to the provisions of the retirement system:

a - Persons who enter employment for the first time after the date the system is put into execution.

b - All other previously insured persons who have not reached the age of forty-nine on the date the system is put into execution.

And all other previously insured persons who have reached the age of forty-nine and have not reached the age of fifty-eight shall be optionally subject, provided that the period of their affiliation to the end-of-service system in addition to the period remaining to reach the retirement age is 15 years at least, which entitles them to obtain the retirement pension in accordance with Article (50-2) paragraph (1).

2 - The other insured persons shall have the choice between one of the two cases:

a - To remain subject to the end-of-service indemnity system.

b - To choose affiliation to the retirement system prescribed in this Title, which is irrevocable, within a time limit of one year starting from the date it is put into execution.

3 - Upon the acceptance of the subject and affiliated insured persons mentioned in paragraphs (1) and (2 b) of this Article, the previous years of employment that the insured person spent under the end-of-service indemnity system shall be added to his subsequent period of employment under the retirement system, and all his financial rights accrued to him under the previous system up to the date of his affiliation shall be transferred to his notional individual account, and the previous periods of employment and their rights shall be calculated in accordance with the transitional provisions that shall be provided for by the decree referred to in Article (54-6) below.

4 - Without prejudice to the provisions of paragraph (2) item (b) above, the door of optional affiliation to this system may be reopened pursuant to a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and the recommendation of the Board of Directors of the Fund.

49-5: Benefits of the system:

The system shall provide one of the following benefits:

1 - Retirement pension

2 - Disability pension

3- Survivors' pension of the insured person

Article 50-1: Components of the Retirement Pension:

The System shall provide the insured person with a retirement pension depending on the following components combined:

1 - The accumulated notional individual account (notional) of the insured person, closed on the day preceding the date of accrual of the right, as set forth in Article (50-6) of this Law.

2 - The age attained by the insured person.

3 - The number of years of contribution.

4 - The conversion factor (conversion factor) of the accumulated notional individual account into an annual retirement pension.

The conversion factor shall be based on the components that are likely to affect the formation of the retirement pension, such as age at the date of retirement, disability, or death, the future indexation (Indexation) of the retirement pension based on the expected evolution of the consumer price index, life expectancy, and the existence of successors to the insured person upon retirement, based on a methodology included in the Fund's financing policy mentioned in Article (54-4).

The conversion factor shall be determined, and amended, on the basis of the statistical and actuarial data prepared within the framework of the financial and actuarial valuation in accordance with the provisions of Article (54-4).

50-2: Entitlement to the Retirement Pension:

1 - The insured person shall be entitled to the retirement pension when the following two conditions are met combined:

a - The insured person attaining the legal retirement age fixed at 64 completed years.

b - The duration of contribution of the insured person reaching at least fifteen years.

2 - The insured person shall have the right to continue working after attaining the legal retirement age and shall remain subject, together with the employer, to all the provisions of the Social Security Law.

3 - No amendment, or correction, to the date of birth of the insured person occurring after the date of his first affiliation with the National Social Security Fund shall be taken into consideration.

4 - If the pensioner returns to work that subjects him to the provisions of this Law, the new period of work shall be considered an independent period, for which his rights shall be settled in accordance with its provisions, provided that he shall not benefit from the value of the subsidy for the minimum guarantees throughout his new period of work.

50-3: Early retirement:

1 - Within six (6) years prior to reaching the statutory retirement age, an insured person who is in a physical, mental or psychological condition that does not enable him to exercise his work without causing serious harm to his health, and whose incapacity for work has been medically established, in accordance with the proper procedures, may request the liquidation of his retirement pension in accordance with the provisions in force.

The rate of incapacity shall be set at fifty percent (50%) of his general capacity.

The internal regulations of the Fund shall determine the procedures for submitting the application, the documents that must be attached thereto and the competent authority to decide thereon.

The liquidation set out above shall preclude the accrual of new retirement rights if the person concerned engages in a professional activity after the date of closing the account.

2 - The insured person shall have the right, within four (4) years prior to reaching the statutory retirement age, to request the liquidation of his retirement rights, provided that his contribution period is not less than twenty (20) years, and that his notional individual account secures a retirement pension equal to or exceeding the maximum of the two guarantees calculated in paragraph (3) of Article (50-7).

50-4: Categories of employees with special status:

The contribution rates, age and special conditions for benefiting from the salary for certain categories of employees who perform arduous work or whose nature of work does not allow them long service shall be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour following the recommendation of the Board of Directors of the Fund, and based on actuarial studies conducted for this purpose by a qualified actuary in accordance with Article (54-2).

50-7: The Two Minimum Guarantees:

1 - Upon the fulfilment of the conditions of retirement, the accumulated notional individual account shall be adopted and converted into a retirement pension for the subscriber or for the successors, in accordance with the bases and rules specified therefor, pursuant to Article (50-1) (Conversion Factor).

2 - The Fund may pay to the insured person who has no successors, upon his retirement, at his request, a lump sum from his notional individual account, provided that the total remaining capital in this account is sufficient to obtain a pension equivalent, at least, to the maximum of both guarantees provided for in Paragraph 3 of this Article.

3 - This scheme guarantees that the retirement pension shall not be less than the better of either of the two guarantees:

a - For the insured person who has subscribed for a period of fifteen (15) full years, a rate of fifty-five percent (55%) of the official minimum wage adopted on the date of retirement, and this rate shall be increased by one point seventy-five percent (1.75%) for each additional year of subscription, to reach at its maximum eighty percent (80%) of the official minimum wage adopted on the date of retirement, of that minimum.

b - A rate of one point thirty-three percent (1.33%) of the average wages of the subscriber declared throughout the period of his subscription to this scheme, and revalued up to the date of retirement, for each year of subscription of the insured person.

The revaluation and indexation (Indexation) of the subscriber's wages shall be carried out in accordance with the increase in the index of the average wages of subscribers pursuant to the mechanism provided for in Paragraph (3) of Article (54-4) of this scheme.

4 - The rates mentioned in Paragraphs (3-a) and (-3b) of this Article may be reviewed by virtue of a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Labour and Finance and the recommendation of the Board of Directors of the Fund, and in light of the recommendation of the qualified actuary referred to in Article (54-4).

5 - In the event of early retirement, in accordance with Paragraph (2) of Article (50-3), the following two calculations shall be carried out:

a - The insured person's notional individual account shall be converted into a retirement pension on the basis of the conversion factor pertaining to his age on the date of his early retirement.

b - The extent of the insured person's benefit from either of the two minimum pension guarantees provided for in Paragraph (3) of Article (50-7) above shall be calculated, and after reducing them by a rate of half a percent (5,0%) for each month preceding the legal retirement age mentioned in Paragraph (a-1) of Article (50-2).

50-5: Contribution periods:

Years of contribution mean the periods in respect of which retirement contributions have been paid or have fallen due to be paid.

For this purpose, an insurance month shall be deemed to be the month during which the insured person became uninterruptedly subject to insurance, and in respect of which contributions have been paid or have fallen due to be paid.

If the insured person was not uninterruptedly subject to insurance, the total of the periods equivalent to twenty-five (25) days, or to four (4) weeks, or to two hundred (200) working hours in respect of which contributions have been paid or have fallen due to be paid shall be deemed to constitute an insurance month.

For this purpose, a month shall be deemed to be one twelfth (1/12) of a year, and a fraction of elapsed months shall be deemed a full month.

The Board of Directors of the Fund shall determine, in its internal bylaws, the rules for calculating the contribution periods of part-time and/or seasonal or intermittent workers, and the rules for calculating the contributions due from them and from their employers, and shall also determine the rules for calculating the benefits provided by this scheme to them and to their successors.

50-6: The Accumulated Notional Individual Account:

1 - The accumulated notional individual account of the insured person shall consist of:

A - The balance of the end-of-service indemnity transferred to this retirement scheme and liquidated pursuant to the provisions set forth in Articles 51, 52, 53 and 54 of the Social Security Law and governed by the transitional provisions provided for in the implementing decree referred to in Article (54-6) below.

B  The contributions paid or fallen due to be paid, and credited to the notional individual account, according to the rate determined in accordance with the provisions of Article (54-1), Paragraph (3).

C - An annual increase in line with the increase in the average income of contributors.

The Fund shall, on a specific and identical date of each year, announce the percentage increase in the index of the average income of contributors in the elapsed year. On the same date, this percentage increase shall be applied to index the notional account of each insured person, and this mechanism shall be adopted until the year preceding retirement.

The annual increase on the notional individual accounts may be adjusted upwards if the actuarial valuation of the scheme shows an exceptional surplus in the reserve determined in the funding policy approved by the Board of Directors, as detailed in Article (54-4).

2 - For the purpose of calculating retirement pensions, all amounts pertaining to the accumulated notional individual account of the insured person up to the date of entitlement to the pension shall be taken into account.

50-8: Liquidation of the accumulated notional individual account for a person who has not fulfilled the condition of years of contribution:

If the affiliate reaches the statutory retirement age, without the condition of years of contribution being met, his accumulated notional individual account shall be liquidated, and the funds due to him shall be paid as a single lump sum. At the request of the insured person, the said amounts may be paid in instalments, or converted into a retirement pension, without the right to benefit from the two minimum pension guarantees provided for in paragraph (3) of the preceding Article (50-7)

50-9: Date of entitlement to the pension:

The retirement pension shall fall due starting from the beginning of the month following the date on which the conditions of entitlement are met.

Article 51-1: The disabled person:

Any person afflicted with a permanent and total disability, whether physical, mental or psychological, which reduces his capacity to work by two-thirds, shall be considered disabled within the meaning of this scheme. No account shall be taken of the said disability if the insured person was afflicted with it prior to becoming subject to the scheme.

51-2: Determination of the state of disability:

The state of disability shall be assessed by the Medical Committee provided for in Article (6) paragraph (5) of the Social Security Law, in accordance with the remaining capacity for work of the insured person, his general state of health, his age, and his physical, mental, and psychological faculties.

51-3: Conditions of entitlement:

1- The retirement scheme shall provide the insured person afflicted with a disability with a retirement pension in accordance with the following conditions conjointly:

a - That he has been a contributor to the scheme for a period of at least three years prior to the date on which the state of disability is established.

b  That the disability did not occur prior to the entry of the insured person into the scheme, taking into consideration the Law relating to the Rights of Disabled Persons No. 220 dated 29/5/2000 (persons with additional needs).

2 - If the disability results from a non-occupational accident or a sudden illness, the period of contribution to the scheme shall be reduced to twelve months.

51-4: Method of calculating the pension:

1 - Upon fulfilment of the conditions of disability, the accumulated notional account, closed on the date of completion of disability after its revaluation, shall be adopted, and this account shall be converted into a disability pension, in accordance with the mechanism specified in Article (50-1)

2 - This scheme guarantees to the disabled person, who has fulfilled the conditions of disability, a disability pension not less than the better of the following two guarantees:

a - For the insured person who has contributed for a period of fifteen full years, a rate of fifty-five per cent (55%) of the official minimum wage adopted on the date of retirement, and this rate shall be increased by one point seventy-five per cent (1.75%) for each additional year of contribution, to reach at its maximum eighty per cent (80%) of the official minimum wage adopted on the date of disability. The guarantee shall be calculated according to the years of contribution after adding a notional period extending from the day following the date of completion of disability until the disabled insured person reaches the legal retirement age.

b - A rate of one point thirty-three per cent (1.33%) of the average wages of the disabled person, revalued up to the date of completion of disability, for each year of his actual period of service, extending from the date the insured person commenced work until the date of completion of disability. The guarantee shall be calculated according to the years of contribution after adding a notional period extending from the day following the date of completion of disability until the disabled insured person reaches the legal retirement age, provided that the total of the two periods does not exceed thirty (30) years as a maximum.

3 - The revaluation and indexation (Indexation) of the wages calculated for the disabled insured person shall be carried out in accordance with the increase in the index of average wages of contributors according to the mechanism provided for in paragraph (3) of Article (54-4) of this scheme.

4- Upon non-fulfilment of the condition of years of contribution provided for in paragraph (1) of Article (51-3) of this scheme, the accumulated amounts of the disabled insured person recorded in his individual notional account shall be liquidated and paid to him as a single lump sum.

Article 52-1: Successors of the insured:

1 - The successors of the insured are:

a - The surviving spouse, provided that the marriage has been in existence for at least two years, and the condition of duration shall be waived in the event that there are children from this marriage.

b - Legitimate children, or those expected to be born within a period of nine (9) months, or those adopted at least two (2) years prior, who are dependent on the insured at the time of his death.

Children shall benefit from their capacity as successors until they reach the completed age of eighteen (18), or until the completed age of twenty-five (25) for children devoted full-time to study, and without age limit for unmarried children with additional invasions whose condition renders them unable to earn their livelihood.

51-5: Mechanism for Applying for a Disability Pension:

The insured person or his official representative shall submit the application for a disability pension to the Fund within a period of twelve (12) months following, as the case may be, either the date of completion of the state of disability, or the date of medical verification of the disability if such disability results from premature bodily wear, in accordance with the medical and objective criteria established in the Medical Committee, or the date of stabilisation of the insured person's condition, or the date of expiry of the legal period of entitlement to medical care benefits.

If the pension application is rejected, or if a previously awarded pension is cancelled, the insured person may submit a new application within a period of twelve (12) months. In the event that the disability rate does not reach two-thirds (2/3) except during the last twelve (12) months, the state of disability shall then be assessed as at the date of aggravation of the disability.

51-6: Deciding on the Disability Pension Application:

The Fund shall decide on the disability pension application within a period of three (3) months from the date of its submission, on the basis of the opinion of the Medical Committee provided for in paragraph (5) of Article (6) of the Social Security Law. The rules for submitting and deciding on the application shall be determined in the Internal Regulations of the Fund.

Failure to decide within this period shall be deemed an approval of the application. The Fund shall notify its decision on the matter to the person concerned by means of an acknowledgment of receipt within the three-month period mentioned above.

Failure to notify, within the period specified above, shall entitle the insured person to seek recourse.

51-7: Date of Entitlement to the Disability Pension:

The pension shall fall due as from the first of the month following the date on which the state of disability is established.

51-8: Provisional Determination of the Disability Pension:

The disability pension shall be granted provisionally, and may be reviewed according to the development of the insured person's condition.

The Fund may request the Medical Committee to assess the remaining earning capacity of the person concerned. It may cancel, suspend or modify the disability pension when the beneficiary's capacity exceeds 50% (fifty percent), and the Fund shall determine the mechanism for modifying the pension in the Internal Regulations.

51-9: Method of Calculating the Retirement Pension if the Insured Person Returns to Work:

If the insured person returns to work covered by the provisions of this scheme, after the cancellation of the disability pension, the period during which he received the pension shall be deemed a period of actual work taken into account for the application of the provisions of Article (16) of the Social Security Law and for entitlement to the retirement pension in accordance with the provisions of this scheme.

52-2: Rights of the Insured's Survivors/ Survivors' Pension:

1 - In the event of the death of the insured prior to retirement:

(a) - The benefits obtained by the survivors shall be determined on the basis of the accumulated notional individual account of the deceased insured, which shall be converted, after its revaluation, into a survivors' pension calculated in accordance with the same mechanisms provided for in Article (50-1).

(b) - This scheme guarantees a survivors' pension that is not less than the better of the following two guarantees:

1 - For an insured who has contributed for a full period of fifteen years, a rate of fifty-five percent (55%) of the official minimum wage adopted on the date of death, and this rate shall be increased by one point seventy-five percent (1.75%) for each additional year of contribution, up to a maximum of eighty percent (80%) of the official minimum wage adopted on the date of death. To calculate the guarantee, the period of actual service shall be added to the period extending from the day following the date of death until the date of retirement age.

2 - A rate of one point thirty-three percent (1.33%) of the deceased's average wages revalued up to the date of death, for each year of his period of actual service extending from the date the insured commenced work until the date of death, added to the period extending from the day following the date of his death until the date of the legal retirement age, provided that the total of the two periods does not exceed a maximum of thirty years.

The revaluation and indexation (Indexation) of the wages calculated for the deceased insured shall be carried out in accordance with the increase in the index of average wages of subscribers according to the mechanism provided for in paragraph 3 of Article (54-4) of this scheme.

2 - In the case of a deceased who was receiving a retirement pension or an invalidity pension at the time of his death:

The survivors' benefits shall be distributed on the basis of eighty percent (80%) of the insured's retirement benefits due upon retirement as follows:

- 40% (forty percent) to the surviving spouse.

- 40% (forty percent) to the children, distributed equally among them if there are more than one. Upon the lapse of the conditions of entitlement of the children or in the absence of such children, their share shall devolve to the spouse, and vice versa.

3 - Where the deceased insured had liquidated his entitlements pursuant to Article (50-8), the survivors shall not be entitled to obtain a retirement pension, but shall be entitled to receive the value of the remaining instalments according to their due dates.

4 - The survivors' pension shall take effect:

(a) - On the first day of the month following the month in which the death occurred, if the application is submitted within a period of two (2) years from the date of death.

(b) - On the first day of the month following the date of submission of the application, if this application is submitted after the expiry of a period of two (2) years from the date of death, provided that the time limit remains open with respect to minor children.

52-3: Cases of cessation of the pension for the husband/wife:

The pension shall cease for the beneficiary husband or the beneficiary wife if he or she marries or dies, and his or her share shall be transferred to the beneficiary children.

52-4: In the absence of successors:

In the absence of any of the successors mentioned in Article (52-1) at the time of the death of the insured person, his notional individual account shall be liquidated and paid as a single lump sum to the right holders (the mother or the father) specified in the draft law put into force by virtue of Decree No. 8496 dated 2/8/1974.

52-5: Upon loss of the right to the disability pension:

1 - If the insured person holding a retirement pension or a disability pension, or a person who fulfils the conditions of entitlement to such pension, goes missing, his traces disappear, news of him ceases, and a judicial decision is issued declaring his disappearance, one of his successors set forth in Article (52-1) may obtain, pursuant to a judicial authorisation, a provisional liquidation of the rights he would have obtained from the pension in the event of the death of the insured person.

2 - The provisional liquidation shall be reviewed upon the return of the missing person, or the provisional liquidation of the rights shall become final upon the official declaration of death.

3 - Pensions shall be disbursed to the successors of the insured person starting from the first day of the month following the month in which the judicial decision regarding the disappearance of the insured person was declared.

52-6: Rights of the surviving husband or wife:

Notwithstanding any other text, the surviving husband or wife shall have the right to combine the pension of the successors of the insured person and the retirement pension or disability pension due to him or her personally, and the children shall also have the right to combine the pension received from both parents, provided that no benefit is drawn from the minimum pension subsidy, if any.

1 - Upon the voluntary affiliation of his employees to the end-of-service indemnity scheme, the employer shall draw up the account of the indemnity for the period of continuous service spent by the employee from his employment until the date of his application to affiliate to the said scheme. The calculation of the indemnity shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of the Labour Law relating to dismissal indemnity.

The employer shall notify the employees in writing of the account mentioned in the preceding paragraph, stating the duration of services and the rate of wage.

In the event a dispute arises over this account, the employee shall be given a time limit of six months starting from the day he is notified of the said account to object to it before the Labour Court.

The regulations of the Fund shall specify the papers and documents that employers must submit to the Fund when their employees voluntarily affiliate to the end-of-service indemnity scheme.

2 - Where the employee has worked for several employers during the period of service conferring entitlement to the indemnity, the account of his indemnities shall consist of the total of his accounts frozen upon each change of employment, plus the indemnity payable by the last employer. This account shall be frozen in the Fund and interest shall accrue thereon at the rate fixed in the internal regulations of the Fund.

3 - The indemnity pertaining to the voluntarily insured person shall remain in the hands of his employer until it falls due for payment pursuant to the provisions of paragraphs 1 and 2 of Article 50 and in the cases set out in the following paragraph:

4 - If the voluntarily insured employee leaves his employment before serving at least twenty years, the employer shall, whatever the reason for leaving the service, pay to the Fund the indemnity provided for in Article 51 or 52 above for the period of continuous service from the commencement of the employee's employment until the date of his application for affiliation to the scheme. This indemnity, plus interest at the rate fixed in the regulations, shall be frozen until the occurrence of one of the contingencies referred to in Article 50 above. The same shall apply if the compulsorily insured person leaves employment of his own accord before completing twenty years of service.

5 - The regulations of the Fund shall provide for the time limits that may be granted to employers for settling the indemnities remaining with them and due for payment, with or without the addition of interest thereto, and may also provide for the settlement of indemnities not yet due in annual instalments in return for a discount thereon, where applicable.

The same regulations shall determine the time limits and methods for submitting declarations by the employer and the employee in the event of termination of service, and the conditions for reconciling this Law with the consensual schemes applicable on the date of publication of this Law in the Official Gazette when they are more beneficial to the employees with respect to the end-of-service indemnity, and the regulations shall likewise determine the liquidation of debts that may be owed to the employer by his employees.

6 - The Fund shall have the right of direct action to recover the indemnities referred to in the preceding paragraph, and the said debt shall be considered a privileged debt and shall rank immediately after the debt of the Treasury.

54-2: Penalty for the Employer's Default in Paying Contributions:

In addition to the provisions of Articles (79) and (80) of this Law, and as of the due date specified in the regulations of the Fund, an employer who defaults in paying the contributions within the regularly specified time limits shall be subject to an additional penalty at the rate of three percent (3%) per month of the total contributions due, provided that this rate shall not exceed fifteen percent (15%) of this total.54-2: Penalty for the Employer's Default in Paying Contributions:In addition to the provisions of Articles (79) and (80) of this Law, and as of the due date specified in the regulations of the Fund, an employer who defaults in paying the contributions within the regularly specified time limits shall be subject to an additional penalty at the rate of three percent (3%) per month of the total contributions due, provided that this rate shall not exceed fifteen percent (15%) of this total.

54-3: Indexation (Indexation) and Payment of Retirement Pensions:

1 - Every year, and on a specified date, the Fund shall carry out a revaluation of all pensions due and currently being paid in accordance with the provisions of this retirement system.

The revaluation shall be based on the increase in the index of the average income of subscribers issued by the National Social Security Fund in accordance with Paragraph (1-b) of Article (50-6) and pertaining to the year preceding the year of revaluation. The mechanism for the revaluation of pensions and the annual maximum limit for the rate of increase thereon shall take place in accordance with the financing policy adopted by the Board of Directors, and the revaluation process shall be subject to the mechanism mentioned in Paragraph (3) of Article (54-4) below.

When appropriate economic conditions are available, the consumer price index issued by the Central Administration of Statistics may be adopted in the revaluation process instead of the wage increase index, pursuant to a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and following the recommendation of the Board of Directors of the Fund based on the recommendation of the qualified actuary.

2 - Pensions shall be paid on their due dates, in accordance with the procedures and dates determined by the internal regulations of the Fund.

Article 54-1: Sources of financing:

1 - The sources of financing of the "Retirement Scheme" shall consist of:

a - Contributions.

b - Returns on the investment and placement of funds derived from these sources.

c - Amounts credited to the notional account of the insured person, which shall be liquidated in accordance with the transitional provisions provided for in the implementing decree referred to in Article (54-6) below.

d - Late payment surcharges, interest, and additional fines incurred for non-compliance with the provisions of this Law.

e - The annual contribution of the State, which shall be determined as a percentage of the total earnings of the persons subject to this scheme, allocated, inter alia, to support the categories that do not have sufficient capacity to contribute to the scheme; these categories and the contribution percentage shall be determined by the implementing decree mentioned in Article (54-6), and may be amended, where necessary, by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Labour and Finance and following the submission of the Board of Directors of the Fund, based on the recommendation of the qualified actuary and on the financing policy referred to in Article (54-4).

This contribution shall be provided for annually in the General Budget Law.

f - Fees allocated to support the General Account, which are imposed by decrees adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Labour and Finance and following the submission of the Board of Directors of the National Social Security Fund.

2 -

a - The State is the ultimate guarantor of the financial sustainability of the scheme, and this shall be clearly reflected in its General Budget when needed.

b - Contributions shall be borne by employers and insured persons.

c - The employer shall pay the contributions due from him and from the insured persons employed by him in full to the Retirement Scheme, and shall notify them annually of the balance of their contribution accounts.

3 -

a - Contributions shall be determined as a percentage of the total earnings of the employee provided for in paragraph (1) of Article (68) of the Social Security Law, within a ceiling limited to four (4) times the average declared wages.

b - The Fund shall announce, on a similar specific date of each year, the amount/level of the ceiling/limit after adjusting it based on the change in the average declared wages for the preceding year.

c - This ceiling shall be amended by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Finance and Labour, following the submission of the Board of Directors of the Fund, and based on the actuarial financial examination of the Retirement Scheme.

d - The percentage of contributions due from each of the employer and the employee shall be determined and distributed by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and the submission of the Board of Directors of the Fund,

In the body of this decree, the percentages of the above contributions shall be determined and distributed in percentages to each of: the notional individual account, the account for supporting the minimum guarantees for retirement, disability, and death pensions, and administrative expenses, based on the recommendation of the qualified actuary and on the financing policy referred to in Article (54-4).

The Council of Ministers shall adopt the aforementioned decree in accordance with the provisions of Article (54-6) below on the basis of the schedule of contributions set forth in Annex No. 3.

4 - The contribution percentages, the method of their distribution, and the earnings subject to contributions may be reviewed by decrees adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Finance and Labour and the submission of the Board of Directors of the Fund, based on the recommendation of the qualified actuary and on the financing policy referred to in Article (54-4).

5 - The General Account of the Retirement Scheme:

a - The General Account of the Fund means the account allocated to provide retirement, disability, and death pensions and to support and supplement these pensions.

b - The General Account of the Fund shall include:

- Balances of the End-of-Service Scheme transferred to this Retirement Scheme pursuant to the transitional provisions to be provided for in the decree referred to in Article (54-6) below.

- Contributions provided for in items (a) and (b) of paragraph (3) of this Article,

- Investment returns of the Fund,

- The annual contribution of the State determined in item (e) of paragraph (1) of this Article

- Allocated fees provided for in item (f) of paragraph (1) of this Article,

- The balance of late payment surcharges and fines incurred upon non-compliance with the provisions of this scheme.

54-4: Examination and evaluation of the financial position once every three years:

1 - The Board of Directors of the Fund must issue a funding policy defining the standards and bases to ensure the long-term financial sustainability of the scheme within one year from the entry into force of this scheme.

The financial policy shall be approved by the Board of Directors of the Fund, upon the recommendation of the qualified actuary.

2 - The financial position of this scheme must be examined actuarially at most once every three years, in accordance with the standards and bases provided for in the adopted funding policy.

The actuarial examination and evaluation shall be carried out by an accredited actuarial company or institution of recognised professional credibility in accordance with international standards, and it may assign, under its responsibility and supervision, one of its actuaries.

The actuarial company or institution shall be appointed and its tasks and duration shall be determined by a decision issued by the Board of Directors of the Fund and subject to the approval of the Minister of Labour.

3 - Upon each actuarial examination and evaluation, the actuary who carried them out must note in his report submitted to the Board of Directors of the Fund, on the basis of the long-term funding policy duly adopted by the Board of Directors of the Fund, whether the position of the Fund permits the indexation (Indexation) of wages and pensions provided for in:

- Item (b) of paragraph (3) of Article (50-7) and,

- Paragraph (3) of Article (51-4) and,

- Item (b-2) of paragraph (1) of Article (52-2) and,

- Paragraph (1) of Article (54-3),

for the period covered by the examination and evaluation.

The indexation (Indexation) of wages and pensions shall be suspended if the results of the evaluation are negative until the date of the subsequent examination and evaluation, and the Board of Directors shall take the necessary measures for correction and rectification in accordance with the funding policy.

If it appears that the result of the subsequent examination and evaluation is positive, the indexation (Indexation) may be carried out on the wages and/or pensions mentioned above, even with retroactive effect, for the previous years during which the indexation (Indexation) of those wages and/or pensions was not permitted, and this shall be done in accordance with the rules defined for the funding policy approved by the Board of Directors.

4 - The evaluation of the actuarial financial position shall be reviewed every three (3) years, and a recommendation shall be made by the actuarial company or institution to take the necessary measures and, where necessary, to amend the conversion factor on the basis of the methodology for calculating conversion factors provided for in the funding policy.

5 - Any amendments to the funding policy and its elements shall be reviewed where necessary, in accordance with rules determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and the submission of the Board of Directors of the Fund.

6 - In the event that the expert issues a qualified opinion or discovers some negligence, the administration shall take the necessary measures to rectify the negligence immediately.

54-5: Method of notifying insured persons of the statements of their accounts:

The internal regulations of the Fund shall determine the method of notifying insured persons of the statements of their notional individual accounts and the benefits, and the times of such notification.

For the purpose of acquiring the right to sickness and maternity insurance benefits, the entire period of employment and training prior to the date of the employee's compulsory affiliation with this insurance shall be deemed included within the insurance period.

The limitation period for sickness and maternity insurance benefits and work accidents and occupational diseases insurance benefits shall be six months as from the date on which they fall due.

The limitation period for permanent disability or death benefits shall be two years as from the date on which they fall due.

Arrears of a disability pension shall not be paid for a period exceeding six months.

Subject to the provisions of Article (81) and notwithstanding the provisions of paragraph (5) of Article (48) of this Law, the limitation period for uncollected retirement, disability, and death pensions shall be five (5) years, as from the date on which they fall due.

The limitation period for retirement, disability, and death pensions, and for sickness and maternity insurance benefits and family and educational benefits, collected unduly, shall be five years running from the date of their payment.

Cash benefits may not be the subject of assignment, set-off, or an undertaking of any kind whatsoever, and they shall not be subject to attachment except in execution of lawful maintenance obligations. In this case, they may be attached up to half of their value.

1 - In the event of the occurrence of a work accident or an occupational disease, the employer shall notify the Fund within forty-eight hours at most from the date of occurrence of the accident. Upon the occurrence of the accident or occupational disease, the employer shall take all measures capable of preventing the aggravation of the injured person's condition.

2 - The employer shall transfer the employee to work more suitable to his health condition when it becomes apparent to the medical control at the Fund that the insured person has been afflicted with an occupational disease or a work accident that threatens to increase and worsen if he continues in his previous work. This measure shall be taken, where necessary, in cooperation with the enterprise.

54-6: Implementing and transitional provisions:

1 - The decrees appointing the Board of Directors of the "National Social Security Fund" shall be issued in accordance with the contents of the ninth Article of this Law within six months (6) from the date of publication of this Law.

2 - The Council of Ministers shall adopt the decree appointing the "Investment Committee", in accordance with the contents of Article (64-4) of this Law, within one year from the date of publication of this Law.

3 - The Council of Ministers shall adopt an implementing decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and the recommendation of the Board of Directors of the Fund, in which it determines the rates of contributions and their distribution in accordance with the provisions of Article (54-1) on the basis of the results of an updated actuarial valuation carried out by a qualified actuary commissioned by the Board of Directors of the Fund, provided that it takes into consideration the economic conditions and circumstances prevailing in the short and medium terms while taking into consideration the inflation rates, within one year from the date of publication of this Law.

The implementing decree must include all transitional provisions relating to the processing and liquidation of the acquired rights of employees under the end-of-service indemnity scheme, including the mechanisms for dealing with objections raised after the application of these transitional provisions.

The decree must observe the following principles:

a - All provisions of the new scheme shall apply to persons who transfer to this scheme, and the period of contribution to the Fund shall be calculated from the day following the date on which their end-of-service indemnity fell due if they have already received it, and otherwise from the date of commencement of their subjection and contribution to social security.

b - For those who transfer to the new scheme, the minimum guarantees shall be applied in proportion to the years of contribution, even for those who do not fulfil 15 years of contribution.

c - The value of the entitlements accumulated within the end-of-service indemnity scheme shall be credited to the notional individual account of each insured person affiliated with the new scheme.

d - If a surplus results in the assets of the end-of-service indemnity scheme at the end of the transitional period, this surplus shall be used to constitute a reserve fund in favour of the new scheme; during the transitional period, the first guarantee, referred to in Article (50-7), may be linked to the average incomes of the contributors instead of being linked to the minimum wage and in a manner that preserves the same value of the guarantee.

4 - After the lapse of one year from the date of issuance of the implementing decree mentioned in paragraph (3) above, the provisions of the third Article thereof shall be put into effect, subject to the time limits and provisions contained in Article (54-6).

1 - As and to the extent that the social security scheme is applied, wholly or partially, to the beneficiaries thereof, all provisions of the laws relating to family allowances and to benefits granted in cases of sickness, maternity, work accidents and occupational diseases, as well as the provisions relating to dismissal indemnity, in respect of compulsory and voluntary insured persons in the end-of-service indemnity scheme, are repealed.

2 - The details of application of the preceding paragraph shall be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers, upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and Social Affairs and following the submission of the Board of Directors.

Article 64-1: Financial autonomy:

Each branch of the branches of social security provided for in Article 7 of this Law shall enjoy financial autonomy, and shall dispose of its own resources to cover its benefits. The revenues and properties of the Fund may only be used for the purposes specified in this Law.

In all cases, it is prohibited to use any resources from any branch for the account of another branch under any pretext and for any reason whatsoever. Each branch shall have a specific and separate account.

1 - The Fund shall contribute to the measures taken for the prevention of illnesses and contingencies in cooperation with the Minister of Labour and Social Affairs and the Minister of Public Health and with the occupational bodies of employers and employees and individual establishments. A Higher Committee for Prevention and Health shall be formed for this purpose, the manner of formation and powers of which shall be specified in the Internal Regulations.

2 - It shall be incumbent upon the employer to take all measures ensuring the conditions of safety and health in workplaces. The Fund may specify in its Internal Regulations certain mandatory measures to monitor the health condition of employees and to carry out means relating to prevention in workplaces.

3 - The Fund shall cooperate with the physicians of establishments to prepare measures for the prevention of illnesses and work contingencies, and likewise, where necessary, to prepare and implement the measures imposed pursuant to Paragraph 2 above, and likewise to guide and direct the insured persons from the health standpoint.

The Fund may enable persons injured by a work contingency or an occupational disease to benefit from the means of vocational training to rehabilitate them for another suitable work, and employers must cooperate in this field with the Fund in accordance with the conditions specified in the Internal Regulations of the Fund.

Agreements and internal regulations which grant benefits more substantial than those provided for by the Labour Law and which are practically in force in a given establishment up to the date of implementation of each branch of social security shall remain applicable and on a mandatory basis in all that exceeds the benefits provided for in this Law, with respect to each branch of security, and shall constitute an acquired right for the employees of the establishment.

In this case, the benefits provided for in this Law shall be deducted from the agreed benefits, and the excess shall be determined pursuant to an agreement between the management and the employees.

A copy of this agreement shall be delivered to the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs, and upon the occurrence of a dispute and Social Affairs, and upon the occurrence of a dispute in this regard, the Minister of Justice and Social Affairs shall adjudicate thereon.

1 - The application of this Law shall not preclude the right of the insured persons, or their successors in title after them, to claim from the persons who caused the accident compensation for the damage incurred. The total of the amounts paid by the Fund shall be deducted from the principal of this compensation.

2 - The Fund shall have the right, in all circumstances, to have recourse by way of a direct action against the persons who caused the accident for the amounts which it has paid as a result thereof.

Article 64-2: Investment Definitions:

The following definitions shall be adopted for investment terms:

They are the principles and orientations that determine the long-term investment objectives and the development of the various investment policies and strategies, and which establish the basis for decisions relating to the funds of the Fund.

They are represented in the long-term allocation of the funds of the Fund across the various asset classes,

in addition to numerous other matters relating to the investment of funds, in particular the classes of investments and loans, return objectives, risk management and diversification, delegations of authority entrusted to asset managers, liquidity of investments, valuation of investments, as well as performance measurement tools.

3 - Long-term Strategic Investment Plan - Long-term Strategic Investment Plan .

Means the long-term action plan (of five years or more) which determines the strategies, policies, and operational programmes that must be selected in a manner that increases the possibility of achieving the specified objectives, in accordance with the "Investment Pillars" and "Investment Policies and Procedures".

4 - Yearly Investment Plan Yearly Investment Plan.

Describes the policies and operational programmes that will be implemented during the following year in a manner consistent with the Long-term Strategic Investment Plan, in accordance with the "Investment Pillars" and "Investment Policies and Procedures".

5 - Statement of Approval of Investment Transactions: Schedule and Powers

(Matrix of Authority for Approval of Investment Transactions) The statement of schedule and powers is that which describes, for each class of asset classes, the level and value of individual investment transactions that may be approved by any of the following bodies:

the Board of Directors, the Investment Committee, the Executive Investment Management, the Chief Investment Officer and the heads of the various operational investment units, and the external managers of assets.

Is the annual report on investment operations, which is prepared by the Investment Committee at the end of each financial year and submitted by it to the Board of Directors. The report shall include, at least, a description of the investment strategies adopted for the past financial year, in addition to those planned for the subsequent year, with a statement of the performance results and returns thereof for all asset classes and for the Fund as a whole, and shall also include the audited financial statements for the past financial year.

Is a company, institution, or financial centre for investment management accredited by the Investment Committee and delegated by it with the external investment management of the assets of the Fund, in accordance with the provisions of Article (64-14).

8 - Custodian of Financial Instruments Custodian

Is the institution or financial centre with which the assets, instruments, papers, and financial securities belonging to the Fund and allocated for investment are deposited for safekeeping, and in accordance with the provisions of Paragraph (64-15) of this Law, and which is licensed in accordance with the laws in force.

The concept of conflict of interest includes any position or act in which the Chairman or one of the members of the Investment Committee, or the Chief Investment Officer, or one of the heads of the executive units and the personnel working therein, or others who influence the business, contracts, calls for tenders, and awards of contracts relating to investment, has a private interest, whether financial, economic, or moral, direct or indirect, that threatens the impartiality and independence of investment procedures, and which is detailed in Paragraph (64-7-III-5-a).

10 - Executive Investment Structure

Is the organizational and executive structure for investment within which the authority of powers, responsibilities, and mechanisms for all investment operations are distributed, under the supervision of the Investment Committee

Structure of the Investment Committee:
