1 - The investment of the Fund's funds shall be undertaken by a body headed by the "Investment Committee", which shall report to the Board of Directors of the Fund and enjoy administrative and financial autonomy.

2 - The Investment Committee shall bear the responsibility of setting the policies for investing all the funds of the Fund.

3 - Subordinate to this body shall be an "Executive Investment Structure", which shall be under the authority of the "Investment Committee", and shall undertake, through the "Executive Investment Management", the execution of the investments of the funds of the National Social Security Fund.

4 - The "Executive Investment Management" shall be composed of the "Executive Investment Director", the "Heads of the Executive Units", and executive employees, workers, and contractors, and shall be headed by the "Executive Investment Director".

Article 64-4: Composition of the Investment Committee:

1 - The Investment Committee shall be composed of six (6) qualified independent experts, in addition to the Director General of the Fund and the Chief Investment Officer ex officio, without either of them having the right to stand for the presidency of the Committee, or to elect and vote.

2 - The experts must satisfy the mandatory conditions imposed below:

a - Holding a university postgraduate degree in financial or economic sciences or in related fields, or a Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) certificate, with experience in the fields of investment of not less than twelve (12) years within investment institutions or funds of a recognised standing.

b - Or holding a university degree and having experience and being seasoned in the fields of investment and for a period of not less than fifteen (15) years within investment institutions or funds with an acknowledged standing.

c - The availability of at least one of the competencies and experiences specified and recorded in the table set forth in Annex No. (1) to this Law.

These conditions, competencies and experiences may be amended when necessary by virtue of a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and the Minister of Finance.

3 - Inviting experts to stand as candidates

3-1 Invitation to stand as candidates and list of accepted candidates

a - Within six (6) months from the date of publication of this Law, the Civil Service Board shall undertake the announcement of an invitation to experts who satisfy the conditions mentioned in paragraph (2) above, including in the announcement the conditions imposed for appointment, and a time limit for accepting candidacies shall be fixed.

b - Upon the expiry of the time limit for accepting candidacies, the Civil Service Board shall examine the candidacies and prepare a list of the accepted candidates who satisfy the mandatory conditions, indicating the competencies and experiences they possess on the basis of Annex No. (1) to this Law.

c - The Civil Service Board shall invite the accepted candidates to personal interviews which it shall conduct for each of them, and it may seek the assistance of external experts who possess extensive experiences in the fields of investment to involve them in these interviews.

d - Upon the completion of this process, the President of the Civil Service Board shall send the list of accepted candidates, accompanied by the table of competencies and experiences contained in Annex No. (1) that are satisfied by each of them, to the Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Fund.

e - The Civil Service Board shall be given a time limit of three (3) months to complete the mission above.

f - The Civil Service Board shall update this list every five (5) years at least, or whenever necessary, and in accordance with the mechanism mentioned above, and communicate it to the Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Fund immediately upon its completion.

3-2 Mechanism for selecting experts

a - At the request of the Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Fund, each of the representatives of the State, the employers and the workers on the Board shall submit to him, within a time limit of one month, a list each containing four (4) names selected from the list received from the Civil Service Board.

b - The Chairman of the Board shall submit the lists prepared above, in addition to the list received from the Civil Service Board and its attachments, immediately upon receiving them, to the Minister of Labour.

c - The Minister of Labour shall submit the lists to the Council of Ministers, recommending three (3) names from each list, two to be appointed as full members, and one name to be appointed as an alternate member.

d - The six experts, members of the Investment Committee, as well as the alternate experts, shall be appointed from among the names appearing on the lists submitted to it, and in accordance with the tripartite distribution of the Board of Directors of the Fund, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.

e - At all stages of appointment, adherence is required to the diversity of the required competencies and experiences and their distribution in accordance with the table set forth in the aforementioned Annex No. (1) among the names proposed for appointment as full members, as well as among the names of the alternate experts.

4 - Impediments to appointment

No person may be appointed to the Investment Committee, nor may he complete his term of office on the Committee, who:

a - Has had a judgment rendered against him barring him from holding public office.

b - Has been declared in cessation of payments or has been judicially declared bankrupt.

c - Has been afflicted with a physical or mental infirmity and has become incapable of performing his duties for a period exceeding six months, and the incapacity shall be verified by the Medical Committee provided for in paragraph (5) of Article (6) of the Social Security Law.

d - Has failed to attend three consecutive ordinary meetings without a legitimate excuse.

e - Has intentionally or as a result of negligence committed, or allowed another person to commit, a violation of the provisions of the Social Security Law.

In the event that it is not permissible to complete the term of office, for any of the cases above, the Chairman of the Committee shall refer the matter to the Minister of Labour to present it to the Council of Ministers to decide thereon or for dismissal or removal from office.

5 - Election of the Chairman of the Committee

Within a time limit of one month from the issuance of the decree forming the Investment Committee, the Minister of Labour shall invite the members of the Committee to a meeting to be held at the headquarters of the Fund to elect a Chairman of the Committee, and if the votes are tied between the candidates, the oldest among them shall be the Chairman, and the Chief Investment Officer shall assume the duties of the secretariat of the Committee.

Article 64-5: Term of Office of the Committee, Liability for Performance, and Allowances:

1 - The term of office of the Chairman and members of the Investment Committee shall be fixed at five years, renewable once.

2 - The Chairman of the Investment Committee and its members shall be liable in respect of their private property and criminally for acts of breach of trust and fraud committed by them in the exercise of their duties.

3 - Decisions taken by the Investment Committee that are subject to accountability shall be the responsibility of those who approved them, with the exception of anyone who dissented from the decision and recorded his dissent in the minutes of the meeting.

4 - Each of the Chairman and members of the Investment Committee shall receive a lump-sum allowance for actual attendance at each meeting in consideration of their performance of the duties and responsibilities entrusted to them pursuant to this Article.

The amount of these allowances, and the maximum limit of the sums that each of them may receive in a single month, shall be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of each of the Minister of Labour and the Minister of Finance.

5 - The Chairman and members of the Investment Committee shall be bound, throughout their term of office and even after its expiry, by professional secrecy with respect to all information of which they have become aware on the occasion of or by reason of the performance of their duties, and they shall be prohibited from disclosing it except before supervisory and judicial bodies.

This obligation shall include information classified by the Investment Committee as confidential in accordance with its regulations and decisions.

6 - Each of the Chairman and members of the Committee must recuse himself and abstain from participating in the discussions and deliberations of the Committee on matters and draft investment contracts if any of them has a personal interest therein, whether direct or indirect, and this shall be recorded in the minutes of the meeting.

The member having an interest may not participate in voting on the relevant draft decisions.

7 - In all cases, the "Code of Conduct" mentioned in Item (III-A-5) of Article (64-7) below shall remain the reference for defining and detailing cases of "conflict of interest" that impede or affect the performance of the Chairman and members of the Committee, the Executive Management for Investment, or other personnel working in the executive structure for investment on the occasion of the performance of their duties.

8 - Each of the Chairman and members of the Investment Committee shall be required to disclose in writing any new developments liable to affect his membership in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

Article 64-6: Internal Regulations of the Investment Committee:

1 - The Investment Committee shall meet at the invitation of its Chairman at least once a month, and it may hold extraordinary meetings upon a written request signed by at least four members, or upon the request of the Minister of Labour or the Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Fund.

2 - Decisions in the Committee shall be taken by an absolute majority, and in the event of a tie, the Chairman shall have a casting vote.

3 - The Chairman of the Investment Committee shall notify the Board of Directors of the Fund with a copy of the minutes of the meetings of the Committee.

4 - Upon an invitation from the Chairman of the Board of Directors, both the Chairman of the Investment Committee and the Executive Director of Investment shall attend and participate in the sessions of the Board of Directors and the Bureau dedicated to matters of the placement and investment of the funds of the Fund without having the right to vote.

5 - Upon the resignation, dismissal, or death of one of the six members, and within a period exceeding six months from the date of expiry of the term of office of the Investment Committee, the Minister of Labour shall invite the alternate member corresponding to him in terms of representation, previously appointed by the Council of Ministers, to join the Committee until the expiry of its term of office.

In the absence of the alternate member, or upon his refusal or excuse, the Council of Ministers shall appoint a replacement member to complete the term of office of the Investment Committee from the entity that was represented by the resigned, dismissed, or deceased member.

In the event that the vacancy affects the position of Chairman of the Committee, the Minister of Labour shall invite the Committee, within a period of one month from the appointment of the alternate member, to elect the Chairman, and the election shall take place in accordance with the mechanism mentioned in Article (64-4) above.

Article 64-7: Duties and responsibilities of the Investment Committee:

The Investment Committee shall undertake the following duties and responsibilities:

I. Organisational and administrative duties and the operational budget:

The duties and responsibilities that must be submitted to the Board of Directors for examination and approval in accordance with the rules or for its information:

1 - The first Investment Committee shall draw up the draft internal regulations of the Executive Investment Structure, within a period of three months from the date of the election of the Chairman, and shall include therein the operational establishment, its grades, the methods of appointing its members and their salary scale, which shall be approved by the Board of Directors in accordance with the rules.

2 - Proposing names for the position of Chief Investment Officer in accordance with the provisions of Article (64-9) below.

3 - Preparing its draft annual budget, including the appropriations for allowances, equipment and the operational cost for the requirements and occupied posts of the establishment of the Executive Investment Structure.

The Chairman of the Committee shall refer the draft budget to the Directorate General of the Fund, which shall automatically include these appropriations within the administrative budget of the Fund, which is approved by the Board of Directors in accordance with the adopted rules.

II. Investment principles and foundations: principles, procedures, policies and guidelines of the duties and responsibilities that must be submitted to the Board of Directors for examination and approval in accordance with the rules or for its information:

1 - Preparing the "Investment Pillars" and submitting them to the Board of Directors for approval.

The Chairman of the Board of Directors shall submit this document to the Minister of Labour for endorsement after seeking the opinion of the Minister of Finance.

2 - Preparing the "Investment Policies and Procedures" for each branch of the Fund and submitting them to the Board of Directors for review and endorsement.

3 - Preparing other relevant policies, such as the risk policy, the conflict of interest policy, and the foreign investment policy, provided for in the "Investment Policies and Procedures".

4 - Reviewing the "Investment Policies and Procedures" annually, and whenever necessary, and submitting recommendations to the Board of Directors regarding changes occurring to these documents.

III. Duties related to the conduct of the business of the Executive Investment Structure and to conduct

A. Duties of the Committee that must be approved by the Board of Directors

1 - Preparing the "Long-Term Strategic Investment Plan".

2 - Adopting the "Statement of Approval of Investment Operations: Schedule and Powers", according to asset class and amounts, which are entrusted either to the Board of Directors, the Investment Committee, the Executive Management, the Investment Director, the heads of executive units, or external asset managers.

3 - Selecting the custodian of financial instruments who shall be accredited as an entity for keeping all securities held by asset managers and accounting for them, and preparing the contracts with it and its remuneration.

4 - Adopting the annual report and the audited financial statements of the funds.

5 - Establishing a "Code of Conduct" to deal with actual and potential cases of conflict of interest, which may affect the performance of the Chairman and members of the Committee, the Executive Investment Management, or other staff working in the Committee on the occasion of performing their duties.

The "Code of Conduct" must include, in addition to the foregoing, the basic requirements and ethics that ensure integrity, transparency and impartiality, provided that it is in line with the codes of conduct adopted by highly rated international investment institutions.

B. Duties prepared, endorsed and adopted by the Committee:

1 - Adopting the "Annual Investment Plan" in accordance with the "Investment Policies and Procedures", and in accordance with the "Long-Term Strategic Investment Plan" adopted by the Board, and establishing the necessary procedures for its implementation.

2 - Preparing the internal regulations necessary for the work of the investment units and for the management of investments in the Executive Investment Structure in a manner that ensures the achievement of the investment objectives and priorities provided for in the "Long-Term Strategic Investment Plan" and the "Investment Policies and Procedures".

3 - Approving the investment mandates to be given to internal investment units or to external asset managers.

4 - Approving the selection of external asset managers who will be accredited for specific investment tasks and approving the contracts and fees of external service providers.

5 - Supervising all activities of the Executive Investment Management.

IV. Reports and performance:

The Investment Committee must:

1 - Prepare the "Annual Investment Report", and submit it to the Board of Directors for approval.

After its approval, the Chairman of the Board of Directors shall submit this report to the Minister of Labour.

The Minister of Labour shall communicate a copy of the report to the Minister of Finance to seek an opinion thereon.

Both the Minister of Labour and the Minister of Finance may express comments and request clarifications on the report, which shall be communicated to the Chairman of the Board of Directors within a period of one month.

After the expiry of the one-month period from the date the Ministry of Labour is notified of a copy of the report and/or after the date of expiry of a one-month period from the date of requesting clarifications, this report shall be published on the electronic platform of the Fund.

With regard to obtaining additional information thereon, the provisions of Law No. 28 dated 10/2/2017 and its amendments (the Right of Access to Information Law) shall apply.

2 - Prepare quarterly reports covering the progress of investment operations and the extent of their compliance with investment policies, standards and procedures, which the Chairman of the Committee shall submit to the Board of Directors.

3 - Upon the invitation of the Chairman of the Board of Directors, the Chairman of the Investment Committee, accompanied by the Chief Investment Officer, shall attend a meeting of the Board of Directors held every three months dedicated to discussing the quarterly reports and evaluating investment performance.

Article 64-8: The Chief Investment Officer:

1 - The Chief Investment Officer shall be appointed pursuant to a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, and the term of his mandate shall be fixed at five years, renewable once.

2 - The Chief Investment Officer must satisfy the mandatory requirements prescribed below:

(a) Hold a postgraduate university degree in financial or economic sciences or in related fields, or a Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) certificate, with experience in the fields of investment of not less than fifteen years within investment institutions or funds of recognized standing.

(b) Possess in-depth expertise in investment management across various asset classes, including equity investments, fixed-income investments, and real assets such as real estate and infrastructure.

(c) Be conversant with the related subjects detailed in the schedule set out in Annex No. (2) to this Law.

3 - Mechanism for appointing the Chief Investment Officer

(a) Immediately upon the formation of the Investment Committee and the election of a Chairman thereof, the Chairman of the Committee shall issue an announcement inviting persons who satisfy the mandatory requirements and some of the additional competencies and experience mentioned in (b) above, for appointment to the post of Chief Investment Officer, and a time limit of one month for accepting applications shall be fixed in the announcement, running from the date of publication of the announcement.

(b) The Investment Committee shall meet within a period of two weeks from the date of expiry of the time limit for accepting applications in a session dedicated to examining the applications and preparing a list of accepted candidates, and shall invite them to personal interviews conducted by it for each of them, in order to assess the extent to which the mandatory and additional requirements for appointment to this post, detailed for each of them, are satisfied.

(c) Each group of experts, the representatives of the Government, employers, and workers in the Investment Committee, shall, within a week from the date of preparing the list of accepted candidates, submit to the Chairman of the Committee a list containing two names for the position of Chief Investment Officer, from among the names set out in the prepared list.

(d) The Chairman of the Investment Committee shall submit the three lists within a week from receiving them, accompanied by a complete list of the accepted candidates, pre-selected, to the Chairman of the Board of Directors for perusal and taking note, and he in turn shall submit these lists, within a time limit of one week from receiving them, to the Minister of Labour.

(e) The Minister of Labour shall present the three lists to the Council of Ministers, recommending two names therefrom, and shall propose to the Council of Ministers the appointment of the Chief Investment Officer from among them.

4 - Impediments to appointment

There shall be prohibited from being appointed thereto:

- Any person who is a member of the Board of Directors or of the Technical Committee.

- Any person whose cessation of payments has been declared or who has been judicially declared bankrupt.

5 - Dismissal of the Chief Investment Officer

(a) The Chief Investment Officer may be dismissed for one of the following reasons:

- His commission of a felony or a dishonourable misdemeanour,

- His commission of a gross fault in the exercise of his responsibilities and duties,

- His incompetence or gross negligence in the exercise of his post.

(b) The dismissal of the Chief Investment Officer shall take place pursuant to a reasoned recommendation approved by the Investment Committee.

(c) The Chairman of the Committee shall refer the recommendation for dismissal together with its supporting documents to the Chairman of the Board of Directors for perusal thereof and submission to the Tutelage Minister.

(d) The Tutelage Minister shall submit the recommendation for dismissal, including his proposal, to the Council of Ministers to decide thereon.

6 - In the event of the resignation of the Chief Investment Officer, he shall submit his request to the Chairman of the Investment Committee, who shall refer the request, accompanied by the opinion of the Committee, to the Chairman of the Board of Directors for perusal and submission to the Tutelage Minister, who in turn shall refer it to the Council of Ministers to decide on the resignation.

Article 64-9: Duties of the Executive Director of Investment:

I. Administrative Duties:

1 - Preparing the organisational structure of the Executive Investment Structure, defining the functional duties, and submitting them to the Investment Committee for adoption.

2 - Managing and supervising the Executive Investment Structure and all its operational units.

3 - Preparing the draft annual budget pertaining to the Investment Body, including the appropriations for allowances, equipment, and the operational cost of the occupied posts of its cadre and its requirements.

4 - Committing the expenditures of the Investment Body, which shall be disbursed and paid in accordance with the procedures established in the Financial Regulations of the Fund.

5 - Preparing for and attending the meetings of the Investment Committee and participating in its deliberations; he shall be entrusted with the secretariat of the Committee in recording and keeping its minutes, and he may reinforce it with human resources and provide it with the equipment necessary for its work.

6 - Preparing quarterly and annual reports and submitting them to the Investment Committee on the activity of the Executive Investment Structure, its financial statements relating to investment activities, and the final accounts for the end of the financial year.

Provided that such reports include the financial statements showing a detailed comparison of the funds during the reporting period, the closing balance, and the composition of the portfolios at the end of the period.

7 - Coordinating with any person delegated with duties relating to the Executive Investment Structure and its responsibilities in the other directorates of the Fund or with external parties.

8 - Coordinating with the Director General of the Fund to implement the orientations approved by the Board of Directors in transferring the assets allocated for investment in accordance with Article (64-16) below.

II. Investment-Related Duties:

The Executive Director shall assume, in cooperation and coordination with the heads of the investment units, the following duties:

1 - Implementing the policies relating to investments approved by the Board of Directors and/or the Investment Committee.

2 - Implementing the decisions of the Investment Committee.

3 - Approving the investment transactions that fall within the scope of its competence, in accordance with the "Statement of Approval of Investment Operations: Schedule and Powers" adopted by the Board.

4 - Ensuring that the Investment Directorate adheres to the application of high standards of performance.

Article 64-10: Executive Management of Investment:

The Executive Management of Investment shall consist of the Executive Director of Investment and the heads of the investment units, concerned with execution and operations management, control management, accounting, and risk management.

Article 64-11: Functions of the Executive Management of Investment:

The Executive Management of Investment shall undertake the following functions:

1 - Approving investment transactions falling within the scope of its competence, according to the "Statement of Approval of Investment Operations: Schedule and Powers" adopted by the Board.

2 - Coordinating all the activities of the executive structure of investment.

3 - Developing various policies, procedures, rules and guidelines for submission to the Investment Committee.

4 - Drawing up the "Annual Investment Plan" in accordance with the "Investment Policies and Procedures" adopted by the Board and submitting it to the Investment Committee for adoption.

5 - Establishing the necessary procedures for implementing the Annual Investment Plan adopted by the Investment Committee.

6 - Providing all necessary assistance to the Executive Director of Investments in any of the tasks and responsibilities falling under his responsibility in accordance with Article (649).

7 - Submitting a recommendation to the Investment Committee for the selection of the securities custodian, external investment managers and any relevant external supplier, for their adoption, and preparing the relevant mandates and contracts.

8 - Submitting a monthly report to the Investment Committee on the investment activities and strategies and the performance of the various investment portfolios.

Article 64-12: Heads of the Investment Units in the Executive Management of Investment:

The internal regulations of the Investment Committee shall determine the qualifications of each head of unit, his skills, his experience, the methods of their appointment, their responsibilities, and their duties within their units.

Article 64-13: Investment Mandates:

1 - The Investment Committee shall determine the investment structure for the various branches of the Fund in accordance with the provisions of the statement of “Investment Policies and Procedures” and the “Strategic Investment Plan”, and the investment mandate shall be determined for each asset class.

2 - Investment mandates may be managed internally by the investment units under the supervision of the Executive Director or may be delegated to external investment managers.

3 - Each delegation of an investment mandate shall be approved by the Investment Committee, and the mandate shall include a general description thereof, a list of eligible investments, the expected return targets measured against market indices and for similar investments, the appropriate diversification metric for the investments, the restrictions necessary for risk control and the relevant conditions.

4 - Each investment transaction shall be approved in accordance with the “Statement of Approval of Investment Transactions: Schedule and Powers”.

Custodian of Financial Instruments:

1- The Fund shall contract with a specialized financial institution or centre to act as "Custodian of Financial Instruments".

2 - The "Custodian of Financial Instruments" must be authorized and licensed in accordance with the provisions of the laws in force, in particular the provisions of Law No. 161 dated 17/8/2011 (Capital Markets). The "Custodian of Financial Instruments" shall be responsible for the safe custody of all assets, instruments, values, and financial securities under its management.

3 - For this purpose, the "Custodian of Financial Instruments" must maintain a separate fund for each of the branch funds managed by the National Social Security Fund.

4 - The "Custodian of Financial Instruments" shall undertake the execution of all transactions requested by the Executive Investment Management in relation to investment operations managed internally, whether by the executive investment units or by the external investment managers.

5 - The "Custodian of Financial Instruments" shall undertake to provide the Investment Committee with quarterly reports on the portfolio of assets, values, and securities, and monthly reports on the transactions carried out during the period.

6 - As part of developing its proposal, the "Executive Investment Directorate" must obtain from the Capital Markets Authority established by Law No. 161 dated 17/8/2011 a list of licensed and qualified financial centres and institutions to perform the duties of "Custodian of Financial Instruments".

For this purpose, the "Investment Committee" must give its prior approval to the list of financial centres and institutions that will be invited to submit tenders for potential applicants for this mission, and approve the content and details of the announcement of this invitation.

The announcement of the invitation must include a detailed description of all the services and works that the "Custodian of Financial Instruments" must provide, as well as the criteria that will be used in the selection process and a comprehensive questionnaire to obtain all information deemed necessary in the selection process to ensure an accurate evaluation.

The "Executive Investment Directorate" must prepare and propose a draft agreement between the "Custodian of Financial Instruments" and the Fund, which must be adopted and approved by the Investment Committee before awarding the contract.

Article 64-14: External Asset Managers:

I - On the Selection of the External Asset Manager

1 - The Investment Committee shall select an external investment manager for any investment mandate upon the recommendation of the Executive Investment Management.

2 - In drawing up its recommendation, the Executive Investment Management shall obtain proposals relating to investments from institutions and companies qualified and licensed to provide the required investment management services, and shall analyse them thoroughly.

3 - To achieve this purpose, the Investment Committee shall approve in advance a list of external investment managers who will be invited to submit their proposals in the fields of investment of the Fund's monies, and this shall take place prior to issuing the request for proposals to potential bidders.

4 - The request for proposals shall include a detailed description of the investment mandate, the qualitative and quantitative criteria to be used in the selection process, and a complete questionnaire to obtain all information deemed necessary in the selection process to ensure an accurate evaluation of the proposals.

5 - The Executive Investment Management shall include in its recommendation a draft investment mandate contract between the external investment manager and the Fund, following the approval of the Investment Committee of the said recommendation.

II - On the Responsibilities of the External Asset Manager:

1 - The external asset manager, as well as the employees subordinate to such manager, delegated by the Fund, shall be deemed a fiduciary under this Law.

2 - Every external asset manager delegated with managing the investment shall bear legal liability for damages that may result from failure to perform the responsibility thereof specified in this Law or in its regulations, or in any contract signed thereby with the Fund. Such liability may not be excluded or limited by contract or agreement.

3 - The external asset manager may delegate the responsibilities or duties thereof towards the Fund or the Fund's assets to any third party following the written approval of the Investment Committee, provided that such delegation shall not limit the legal liability of the external asset manager.

4 - The external asset manager and every person working for or with such manager who manages the investment shall provide appropriate insurance contracts for the purpose of protecting the Fund from losses resulting from any forgery or any unlawful act committed by them directly or through a third party.

5 - The adoption of the type of insurance, the volume of coverage, and the insurance company granting such coverage shall be subject to the approval of the Investment Committee, which shall lay down the appropriate regulations therefor, including what they contain as to the nature of the amounts and the nature of the coverage.

6 - The Fund's assets shall not be deemed the property of the external asset manager. They shall not enter into the execution of any judgment against such manager, nor shall they be counted among the assets thereof if declared bankrupt.

7 - The external asset manager shall keep complete and accurate documents and records covering the investment operations for which such manager is responsible and the cost incurred thereby, and shall submit them when necessary to the Investment Committee for supervision and auditing.

8 - The Investment Committee reserves the right to rescind and terminate the delegation with the external investment manager in the following cases:

a - If the external investment manager ceases to be qualified and licensed to act in the management of investments in accordance with the laws and regulations in force.

b - If it is established by the Investment Committee that the manager's performance has failed to achieve the objectives and the expected return specified in the investment delegation contract thereof.

c - In the event of the bankruptcy thereof or the liquidation of the assets thereof.

9 - In the event of termination of the delegation contract, or the non-renewal thereof, the external asset manager shall return all documents, records, and accounts to the Executive Investment Structure or to any new external asset manager appointed by the Investment Committee, and at its request within the period agreed upon between the parties without delay and in a manner that ensures the continuous performance of the Fund's management activities.

In the event that a number of documents, records, and accounts remain in the possession of the asset manager, for one reason or another, after the termination of the contract with the knowledge and approval of the Fund, such manager shall retain them for a period of ten years from the date of expiry of the contract between the manager and the Fund. The external asset manager shall not destroy or dispose of the records and accounts before granting the Fund an opportunity to place them in its custody.

Article 64-16: Mechanisms for transferring assets allocated for investment:

1 - Within three (3) months from the appointment of the Executive Director of Investment, the latter, together with the Director General of the Fund, shall prepare a draft regulation to determine the following necessary criteria, mechanisms and delegations:

a - Payment of benefits, indemnities and pensions that are due and that will fall due, and for each of the operating branches, in addition to the amounts necessary to execute the administrative budget and to conduct the operations and requirements of the Fund, with due regard to the provisions of Article (66) of the Social Security Law relating to the constitution of a reserve fund for each branch.

b - Transfer of all financial balances in excess of the estimates mentioned above, from each of the operating branches, to the asset funds held for each of these branches with the "Custodian of Financial Instruments".

c - Transfer of amounts, where necessary, from the balances of investment assets and returns for each branch held with the "Custodian of Financial Instruments", to the Financial Directorate at the Fund to replenish the requirements of the branch.

d - The draft regulation must include the requirement to obtain the documented opinion, when preparing the periodic valuation, of both the Financial Directorate and the qualified actuary accredited by the Fund in order to determine the estimates detailed above.

2 - The Executive Director shall submit the draft regulation to the Investment Committee to examine and adopt it, and the Chairman of the Committee shall refer it to the Board of Directors for approval.

3 - Fund transfer operations shall take place every three months (3) at most, and at a shorter interval if possible, provided that the regulation mentioned above includes the mechanisms for coordination between the Executive Directorate of Investment and the Financial Directorate, and the determination of the necessary documents, to regulate the transfer of funds allocated for investment to the "Custodian of Financial Instruments".

Article 64-17: Enjoyment by the Fund of a preferential right:

The Fund shall enjoy a preferential right in acquiring the shares of public companies privatised by the State or the instruments resulting from the securitisation of the revenues and profits of public institutions. This preferential right shall amount to a maximum proportion of fifteen percent (15%) of the issued or offered shares or instruments, provided that the Fund acquires them at the lowest price determined or resulting from a call for tenders, and the Investment Committee shall undertake the completion of the acquisition mechanism.

Case of a Dispute with the Board of Directors of the Fund:

Any dispute arising between the Board of Directors of the Fund and the Investment Committee shall be submitted to the Minister of Labour, and in the event of failure to reach a settlement of the dispute, the Minister shall refer it to the Council of Ministers to adjudicate thereon.

External Audit:

The Board of Directors of the Fund must contract with an auditing firm of attested competence that fulfils the international professional requirements, which shall undertake the auditing of its accounts and its risks, whether in respect of liabilities or assets, provided that the detailed annual financial audit reports shall be published during the first half of the following year, and the management of the Fund shall periodically and regularly publish quarterly reports, which shall be made available to the public.

1 - A permanent reserve fund shall be established for each of the social security branches provided for in items a - b - c of Article 7 of this Law, the minimum threshold of which at the end of the financial year shall reach:

a - One-sixth with respect to sickness and maternity insurance and the family and educational allowances scheme.

b - One-third of the expenditures incurred during the three years preceding the financial year in question with respect to work accidents and occupational diseases insurance. The said minimum threshold must be secured for each of the aforementioned branches at the latest at the end of the fourth financial year following the entry into effect of the branch.

2 - If the expenses of one of the branches provided for in the preceding paragraph, with the exception of the sickness and maternity insurance branch, exceed its revenues during a single financial year, the difference shall automatically be drawn from the reserve fund pertaining to it.

If it appears at the end of the same financial year that the reserve fund has not reached the minimum threshold, the Council of Ministers, upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and Social Affairs and the recommendation of the Board of Directors, shall decide to raise the rate of contributions starting from the first of July of the year following the financial year suffering from the deficit, such that the contributions become sufficient to restore financial balance and for the reserve fund to reach the required minimum threshold, within a period of three years at most.

However, if the expenses of the sickness and maternity insurance branch increase, it shall be decided to raise the rate of contributions within the limits of the same procedures in accordance with the following percentages:

- 40 % State.

- 40 % Employers.

- 20 % Employees.

3 - The State may, during the financial year, grant advances to the Fund to achieve balance in its budget; a decree taken in the Council of Ministers shall determine the conditions of these advances and the manner of their repayment.

4 - If a national disaster occurs leading to a severe deficit in the Fund, the State may grant the Fund an exceptional assistance determined on the basis of restoring financial balance without increasing contributions.

Second:

1 - Every natural or legal employer governed by private law shall obtain, from the Fund, a clearance certificate proving the payment of contributions and all other financial obligations relating to the implementation of this Law, in the cases specified in this Article and the following Articles contained in this Law.

The receipt issued by the Fund shall be deemed equivalent to the required clearance certificate and shall be valid for a period of twelve months. Where necessary, the validity of the clearance certificate may be extended by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and Social Affairs.

2 - The clearance certificate provided for in item 1 of this paragraph shall be submitted where the transaction is in the interest of the establishment and not in the interest of persons in their individual capacity, in the following cases:

- Registration transactions in the Chambers of Commerce and Industry provided for in Legislative Decree No. 36 dated 5/8/1968 and its amendments, as well as in the cases provided for in paragraphs 3, 8 and 9 of Article Eight of the said Legislative Decree.

- Real estate transactions relating to the dissolution and liquidation of commercial establishments and commercial companies owned by employers, before the Real Estate Register or any other official authority.

- Transactions for import, export and re-export licences and customs transactions of all kinds relating to commercial establishments and commercial companies.

- Transactions for participation in public and restricted tenders, calls for tenders and mutual agreements before all State administrations, autonomous agencies, municipalities and all other public institutions.

- Transactions for bank credits and commercial, industrial, agricultural and tourism loans conducted by public sector institutions.

- Transactions for grants given or awarded by public administrations and all other public sector institutions to associations, syndicates, federations and all other professional bodies.

- Transactions for the registration of private educational institutions of all kinds or the making of amendments thereto before the Ministry of National Education and Fine Arts, as well as when conducting transactions for the payment of grants to free private schools.

1 - The Fund shall be exempted from the payment of all taxes and fees, including stamp duty, judicial and real estate fees, and taxes due on real properties that the Fund may acquire. Correspondence addressed to the Fund and issued by it shall benefit from postal exemption.

2 - Pharmaceutical preparations, prosthetic appliances, spectacles, and other medical or surgical instruments imported on behalf of the Fund may be exempted from customs duties. The modalities of this exemption shall be determined by the Higher Council of Customs and the Minister of Finance.

3 - Insured persons who benefit from social security benefits shall be exempted from all taxes and fees on moneys received and on all transactions and disputes arising from the application of this Law, and in particular applications for benefits issued by insured persons.

- The earnings taken as a basis for the calculation of contributions shall include the total income paid to the worker in consideration of work or on the occasion of work, including all elements and accessories, in particular wages, gains, paid leave allowances, amounts deducted from the wage for workers' contributions, allowances, grants, bonuses, and all other cash or in-kind benefits, as well as amounts paid directly or by third parties in the form of gratuities.

2 - There shall be taken into consideration as a maximum limit for the income subject to deductions the income the value of which amounts to twice the official minimum of salaries and wages. This maximum limit may be amended by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and Social Affairs and following the submission of the Board of Directors.

3 - The provisions of paragraph 2 above shall not apply to the calculation of end-of-service indemnity.

The wage adopted for the purpose of the said calculation is that set forth in Article 51 of this Law.

4 - Contributions in respect of Lebanese persons working for the account of municipalities shall be calculated on the basis of the earnings provided for in the preceding paragraphs, provided that such earnings shall not be computationally, and in any event, less than the minimum wage applied in public administrations. If the municipalities fail to pay the contributions due by them, the value thereof shall be deducted ipso jure and annually from the revenues allocated to the municipalities concerned from the funds of the Independent Municipal Fund in the same decree that distributes such revenues, and the Ministry of the Interior shall pay the same directly to the National Social Security Fund.

5 - The maximum limit of earnings subject to deductions with respect to the Family and Educational Benefits Scheme branch provided for in Decree No. 3561 dated 21/10/1980 shall be amended so as to become 1500000 L.L. one million five hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds per month.

The maximum limit of earnings subject to deductions for the Sickness and Maternity Insurance branch provided for in Article 68 (paragraph 2) of the Social Security Law shall be amended to become /216.000.000/ L.L. per year (two hundred and sixteen million Lebanese Pounds) (pursuant to Decree 11928 dated 18/8/2023)

The maximum limit of earnings subject to deductions for the Sickness and Maternity Insurance branch provided for in Article 68 (paragraph 2) of the Social Security Law shall be amended to become five times the official minimum monthly wage.

Travel and tourism agencies subject to the provisions of this Decree shall mean individual or corporate establishments whose owners practise, in the capacity of a representative or agent, directly or indirectly, commercial activities for the purpose of profit by selling travel tickets or issuing travel and tourism vouchers to individuals or the public on all transport companies operating in the country and abroad, and in general all operations and services relating to travel, transport and accommodation activities and other complementary activities.

The activities and operations of the agencies shall be defined as follows:

1 - Selling and procuring travel tickets or issuing vouchers in lieu thereof, as well as organising individual or group tourist trips from Lebanon to abroad and vice versa in accordance with specific programmes setting out all the services and activities relating to accommodation, visits, transfers and other required services.

2 - Issuing vouchers or selling travel tickets for the organisation of domestic or international tourist trips by land by means of transport owned by the agency or through land transport companies operating regularly in the country, for specific tourist programmes.

3 - Renting out tourist cars to foreign tourists, summer visitors or Lebanese expatriates without a driver in order to visit tourist and archaeological sites in Lebanon or in neighbouring Arab countries or other countries.

4 - Providing event services through the rental of cars with a driver for each car, provided that the rental period is on an hourly basis and does not exceed twenty-four hours.

5 - Renting out four-wheel drive motorcycles ATV and utility task vehicles UTV without a driver in order to visit natural, tourist and archaeological sites in Lebanon within the routes permitted for this type of vehicle.

The supplementary activities permitted to be carried on by travel and tourism agencies, as necessary, at the request of the tourist or traveller and in accordance with his wishes, shall be determined as follows:

1 - Completing formalities relating to passports and obtaining the necessary visas thereon from the competent official administrations and embassies.

2 - Facilitating and securing currency exchange operations.

3 - Effecting insurance transactions for the benefit of the traveller and his baggage with recognised insurance companies.

4 - Reserving rooms in hotels or residences to secure accommodation for the traveller or tourist.

5 - Selling tickets for public places of entertainment as well as private events and reserving the necessary seats therefor.

6 - Buying and selling collections of commemorative stamps or tourist publications issued by official administrations or other private bodies. These activities shall be determined pursuant to written agreements between the owner of the agency and the person concerned, and nothing existing orally shall be taken into consideration.

Other activities that may be carried on by travel and tourism agencies shall be determined, when needed, by a subsequent decision of the Minister of Tourism.

Classification of travel and tourism agencies:

Travel and tourism agencies shall be classified in the following manner:

1 - First Category (Travel and Tourism Agencies). These are the agencies licensed to carry on all the activities mentioned in the first paragraph of Article Two.

2 - Second Category (Tourist Transport Agencies) These are the agencies licensed to carry on all the activities mentioned in the second paragraph of Article Two.

3 - Third Category (Tourist Car Rental Agencies), these are the agencies licensed to carry on all the activities mentioned in the third paragraph of Article Two.

4 - Fourth Category (Event Car Rental Agencies), these are the agencies licensed to carry on all the activities mentioned in the fourth paragraph of Article Two.

5 - Fifth Category (Agencies for the Rental of Four-Wheel Drive Motorcycles ATV and Utility Vehicles UTV). These are the agencies licensed to carry on all the activities mentioned in the fifth paragraph of Article Two.

The documents required to obtain a licence for the various agencies, which must be submitted at least two months

prior to commencing work, shall be determined as follows:

1 - An application to the Ministry of Tourism signed by the person concerned.

2 - An extract of civil registry proving that the applicant is Lebanese and has completed twenty-one years of age.

3 - A judicial record for the owner of the agency, its directors and all responsible persons therein, provided that the person concerned has not been convicted of a felony or a dishonourable misdemeanour and is of good conduct.

4 - A document proving that the owner of the establishment or the person entrusted with its management possesses the necessary technical and professional qualifications.

5 - A document proving the registration of the establishment at the Commercial Court and clearly showing its type and capital.

6 - A document showing the name of the establishment, subject to the approval thereof by the Ministry of Tourism.

7 - A document proving that the companies concerned have a legal entity in Lebanon, in which case the laws in force shall apply to them.

8 - An occupancy permit or its equivalent from the competent administrations.

9 - A lease agreement if the operator is a tenant, or a title deed if the operator is on his own property; as for the required plans, they shall be determined by the Ministry of

Tourism by a subsequent decision.

10- A work permit for every foreigner who practises work in the agency, whether as a partner, an employee or an owner of the establishment.

11- A certificate from the competent authorities proving reciprocity on the part of the country to which the foreign licence holder belongs.

The practice of the business activities mentioned in the first article shall be subject to a prior licence granted in accordance with the following two stages:

First- The applicant for the licence must submit an application to the Ministry of Tourism setting out the concept of the project, accompanied by economic and financial studies. The Ministry of Tourism may provide advice to the concerned party regarding the location and direction of the investment of his project. If the Ministry accepts the concept of the project, its owner shall be granted an approval called "First Stage Approval".

Second - After obtaining the First Stage Approval, the concerned party shall submit an application accompanied by the legal documents.

A decision on the application and the documents shall be made within a period not exceeding two months from the date of their submission.

If the legal documents are available and the necessary inspections are completed and their result is positive with respect to the conditions imposed in the regulations in force, the licence shall be granted by a decision of the Minister of Tourism upon the proposal of the Director General and after taking the opinion of the Advisory Tourism Committee. The licence may be granted to nationals of foreign states or foreign companies by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Tourism if the legal conditions are met by the applicants for the licence, provided that the countries to which they belong grant Lebanese nationals or Lebanese companies reciprocity, and provided that the foreign companies fulfil the legal conditions imposed in the laws and regulations in force.

The licence shall specify the name of the office, the name of its owner, its category, and all the necessary restrictions, and a temporary licence may be granted for a period of two months, renewable once and for the same period according to the requirements of the interest, provided that the basic conditions are met. In all cases, if two months elapse from the submission of the licence application and if the Ministry of Tourism has not replied to it, the application shall be deemed rejected.

Amendments pertaining to the ownership of agencies :

The licence shall be granted in the name of the natural or legal person who practises the profession of travel and tourism or tourist transport, and it shall not be permissible to assign it wholly or partially or sell it to third parties except after carrying out the legal formalities therefor at the Ministry of Tourism.

The assignment of agencies whose owners have committed bankruptcy or fraud shall not be accepted in the event of the existence of attachment notices or lawsuits concerning them, and the adjudication thereof shall rest with the competent courts.

The owner of the establishment may transfer his establishment to another place or admit a partner or a responsible manager, provided that he applies the laws in force and obtains the approval of the Ministry of Tourism.

The heirs shall have the right to continue the business in the establishment, provided that the conditions previously existing continue to be met and that a manager is appointed for the agency who possesses the experience in accordance with what is provided for each agency in the seventh article, and in addition thereto, all the conditions set forth in the Lebanese laws in force shall apply with respect to the heirs.

2 - A layout plan of the workplace showing the arrangements taken therein, provided that its area is at least 35 square metres and is on the ground floors, in addition to a spacious place for housing cars not more than 70 metres away from it.

3 - An undertaking from the owner of the agency to employ at least three employees, provided that this is pursuant to a statement issued by him containing the names and the tasks assigned to them together with a criminal record certificate for each of them .

4 - A certificate of ownership of at least five cars equipped for occasions that are not attached, provided that these cars have special registration plates of their own, and the agencies must also insure their aforementioned vehicles on a permanent basis with comprehensive insurance against all risks as follows:

- In the event of the death of the driver or passengers.

- In the event of medical treatment and hospitalisation resulting from any accident.

- Against third parties.

- Theft.

- Fire.

5 - The value of the financial or bank guarantees and the insurance shall be reviewed, when necessary, by a decision of the Minister of Tourism in accordance with the fluctuations in the value of the Lebanese currency .

6 - A certificate proving competence or experience in travel and tourism business for the owner of the office or the responsible manager, provided that it is not less than 5 years of service in a principal position in one of the transport companies or tourism offices of the first category, or a professional certificate in the fields of tourism from a recognised institute with experience of at least two years after obtaining the certificate, and these conditions are required to be met in the agency on a permanent basis.

* Paragraph E: The documents required to be submitted to agencies of the fifth category:

In addition to the conditions set forth in the Traffic Law and all regulations relating thereto, the application of the following is required :

1 - A cash or bank guarantee in the amount of ten million Lebanese pounds in favour of the agency of the fourth category issued by a recognised bank.

2 - A layout plan of the workplace showing the arrangements taken therein, provided that its area is at least 35 square metres and is on the ground floors, in addition to a spacious place for housing four-wheel drive motorcycles ATV and utility vehicles UTV not more than 70 metres away from it.

3 - An undertaking from the owner of the agency to employ at least three employees, provided that this is pursuant to a statement issued by him containing the names and the tasks assigned to them together with a criminal record certificate for each of them .

4 - A certificate of ownership of at least ten four-wheel drive motorcycles , and utility vehicles that are not attached , provided that these motorcycles and vehicles have special registration plates of their own, and the agencies must also insure their aforementioned vehicles on a permanent basis with comprehensive insurance against all risks as follows:- In the event of the death of the driver or passengers.

- In the event of medical treatment and hospitalisation resulting from any accident.

- Against third parties.

- Theft.

- Fire.

5 - The value of the financial or bank guarantees and the insurance shall be reviewed, when necessary, by a decision of the Minister of Tourism in accordance with the fluctuations in the value of the Lebanese currency .

6 - A certificate proving competence or experience in travel and tourism business for the owner of the office or the responsible manager, provided that it is not less than 5 years of service in a principal position in one of the transport companies or tourism offices of the first category, or a professional certificate in the fields of tourism from a recognised institute with experience of at least two years after obtaining the certificate, and these conditions are required to be met in the agency on a permanent basis.

* Paragraph F : If the minimum number of cars or motorcycles or vehicles required to be available at any agency decreases and is not completed within one month and for any reason whatsoever, the agency shall be deemed in breach of the conditions of licensing or establishment .

* Paragraph G :

Applicants for a licence for agencies of the third, fourth and fifth categories (rental of tourist cars - rental of occasion cars - rental of four-wheel drive motorcycles ATV mentioned in Paragraphs 3, 4 and 5 of Article Four , must submit all the documents and studies required by the Ministry of Tourism in Articles Five, Six and Seven (Paragraphs "C", "D" and "E" ) all at once, and the licensing of these agencies shall not be subject to the rules of temporary licensing or licensing in stages; rather, the licence shall be granted by a decision of the Minister of Tourism upon the proposal of the Director General and after taking the opinion of the Advisory Tourism Committee, within a period not exceeding two months from the date of submitting the application.

Establishment of branches:

Travel and tourism agencies shall be entitled to establish branches within Lebanese territory of the same category for which they are licensed, provided that they obtain prior approval from the Ministry of Tourism, and provided that the premises of the branch are suitable and equipped with the necessary equipment and that their area is not less than 60 per cent of what is originally required.

The manager of the branch must also possess the competence provided for in the original requirements.

The owner of the agency must also notify the Ministry of Tourism of the agents and canvassers who work for its account and shall bear responsibility for their acts.

The owner of a travel and tourism agency shall be bound to duly carry out brokerage operations and secure travel tickets for the concerned parties as requested of him inside the country and abroad.

He shall also be bound to carry out the execution of tourist trips in accordance with the programmes issued by him, and in general to execute all services requested of him in accordance with established practices and in accordance with the regulations in force with the official administrations and with international institutions.

a - The owner of the agency must renew the bank guarantee mentioned in Article Seven 15 days prior to the date of expiry of its term, and in the event that the bank ceases operations or its name is struck off at the Ministry of Finance, he must submit a new guarantee from another bank within a period of one month from

the date of the striking off or cessation.

b - The financial guarantee shall not be returned to its owners until after the lapse of six months from the date of closure of the agency and its final cessation of work, and the competent departments at the Ministry of Tourism may verify this by the means they deem appropriate for this purpose.

c - This guarantee shall be allocated by way of priority to secure the obligations specified in this Decree and its attachment by third parties shall not be accepted.

d - The owner of the agency must replenish its original value within two weeks from the date he is notified of the deduction of any amount therefrom.

The owner of a travel and tourism agency, of whatever category, must notify the Ministry of Tourism of the tourist programmes and publications that he issues in order to obtain its approval thereof.

If the Ministry does not reject the application or does not request the making of any amendment or change to the programmes and publications within five days from the date of registration of the application with it, it shall be deemed to have approved by operation of law and the owner of the agency shall be entitled to commence his operations.

In all cases, the advertisement must be of matters that are true, customarily acceptable and capable of being carried out without impediment. The programme may be printed in foreign languages if prepared for abroad, whereas those used and published in Lebanon must be drafted in the Arabic language with their translation into foreign languages where necessary in accordance with the wish of the agency.

The Garage:

First: General Provisions

The construction of a garage for parking motor vehicles shall be required in buildings to be erected in all zones.

The garage for each section of the building must appear on the permit plans, and this garage shall be considered an integral part of the section of the building to which it pertains (for a residential apartment, a shop, an office, or a professional practice..) upon the leasing, subdivision, or sale of this section. Where the design of the building, the placement of columns, or the presence of walls in the areas to be allocated for the garage prevents the entry or accommodation of the number or part of the required motor vehicles, the competent technical administration shall be entitled to request a reconsideration of the design of the building or the placement of columns and walls in order to secure the necessary garage required for the total exploitation of the real property, even if the subject of the permit covers only a part of this exploitation.

An application for a permit to construct a building or a group of buildings requiring more than fifty motor vehicles, as well as buildings for public use, must include a study of the impact of the building on traffic movement (Traffic Impact Study) and the manner of addressing these variables.

Second: Substitution for the Garage:

1 - Certain buildings may be exempted from the requirement of securing a garage where there is a compelling technical impossibility preventing the construction of the garage, provided that in such cases a special fee is imposed, to be collected by the municipality, or by the Governorate or the Qaemقامية (District Administration) outside the municipal area.

The cases permitting the exemption of certain buildings from the garage and the substitution therefor by paying the due fees shall be determined by a decree adopted upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport after consulting the opinion of the Higher Council for Urban Planning; the number of required parking spaces according to the intended use of the building, the conditions and specifications of the garage, the details of the incentive elements for buildings or parts of buildings constructed and exploited as collective garages in the building in excess of what is legally required, and the penalties applicable upon failure to secure the garage shall also be determined in the same manner. The due garage fee in lieu shall be determined by a decision issued by the Higher Council for Urban Planning based on the cost of its roofed construction equivalent to 25 m2 for each motor vehicle, taking into account the price per square metre of the land of the real property and the general exploitation factor in the zone, and it shall remain in force throughout the following years and across all Lebanese territory unless another valuation is issued.

2 - Upon the granting of a prior permit, and in the event of a technical impossibility preventing the construction of the garage and requiring its replacement by a special fee, the authority that granted the permit shall request the competent Land Registry Registrar to enter a restriction on the real folio of the real property stating that the current owner is owed by it a number of motor vehicles for which the fee in lieu has been paid. This entry shall remain in effect until the settlement of the status of the garage between the permit-granting authority and the owner. A special account for the garage shall be established in the Public Treasury in favour of each municipality, provided that the revenues of this garage are allocated exclusively for establishing collective garages or for settling the status of those for whom garages have not been secured.

The revenues of the garage and the grants pertaining thereto shall be deposited into this account, provided that the procedures for operating the garage account and the manner in which each municipality finances its garage shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Finance and of Interior and Municipalities, provided that the expenditures of each municipality do not exceed its revenues from the garage fee or the collective garages.

The owner of the real property who has paid the garage substitution fees shall be entitled, if the competent authorities do not proceed within a maximum period of eight years from the date of collection of the fees to secure a garage, to recover the amounts paid and to cancel the annotation of the motor vehicle fee in lieu recorded on the real folio of the real property, provided that they secure the required parking spaces in accordance with the provisions of this Article. Payment of the aforementioned fee in lieu may be substituted by purchasing motor vehicle parking spaces in other real properties or buildings containing additional parking spaces or a collective garage for the public and within a radius of 500 m, in accordance with conditions to be determined by a decree adopted upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport after consulting the opinion of the Higher Council for Urban Planning.

3 - No building complex comprising more than one building on the real property may be exempted from the requirement of securing a motor vehicle garage, and consequently, in this case, securing the garage may not be substituted by paying the fee.

Third: In Legally Existing Buildings (Licensed or in Which Building Violations Have Been Settled):

1 - Upon applying to change the intended use of legally existing buildings, in whole or in part, as permitted by the zoning regulations, or upon modifying the number of units of which they are composed, the number of additional motor vehicle parking spaces required to be secured for the modified parts shall be determined in accordance with conditions

to be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport after consulting the opinion of the Higher Council for Urban Planning.

2 - No parking space is required to be secured in legally existing buildings (licensed or settled) upon applying for a modification therein without an increase in the number of units and without a change in the intended use.

3 - Upon granting a permit for the addition of a building on a built real property, whether such addition is above the existing building or on an unbuilt area of the land of the real property, the required motor vehicle parking spaces shall be secured for the added building only, in accordance with the building regulations or the laws in force at the time of granting the permit for the addition of the building.

Fourth: The Additional and Collective Garage (for the Public):

1 - The Additional Garage:

- In the event of securing an additional garage in excess of the legally required garage, the area of the additional garage equivalent to an area of twenty-five square metres /25 m2/ for each additional motor vehicle whose parking is secured therein, up to a maximum equal to the area of the legally required garage, as well as an area equal thereto from the legally required garage, shall be exempted from the building permit fee, and it shall be required to register on the real property folio that the intended use of this section of the building is as an additional garage for motor vehicles.

- It is permitted to secure the additional garage in the basement floors and within the free spaces of the land of the real property. The owner may, if they so wish, secure the additional garage on the piloti floor (column floor) as well as on the upper floors of the building and not count this additional garage in the general exploitation factor and the number of floors, provided that they comply with the building envelope line and the height required in the zoning regulations.

2 - The Collective Garage for the Public:

- A permit may be granted for the construction of a building allocated as a collective garage for the public on real properties whose area is not less than one thousand square metres, and a section of the building may be allocated for commercial use provided that the number of motor vehicle parking spaces allocated for the public is not less than one hundred motor vehicles.

- The area of the building or the section of the building allocated as a collective garage for the public shall not be counted within the general exploitation factor and the surface exploitation ratio, provided that it complies with the legally required setbacks and the building envelope line, and the exemptions set forth in Item Fourth - Paragraph /1/ above of this Article (The Additional Garage) shall apply to the collective garage.

The owner of the real property built as a collective garage for the public is permitted to transfer three-quarters of the balance of the general exploitation factor (not used for a commercial building) to another real property or properties within the same cadastral area and the same easement zone, provided that the remaining conditions

for the building permit are complied with in the real property or properties to which the balance of the general exploitation factor has been transferred, including the building envelope line.

It shall not be permissible to transfer to any real property in the same cadastral area and the same easement zone more than twenty percent (20

%) of the exploitation factor of this real property, and subject to the approval of the Higher Council for Urban Planning of the proposed location for the increase.

Notwithstanding any other text, a permit may be granted to occupy properties belonging to each of the State and the municipalities for the purpose of building garages for the public and exploiting them for a specified term, pursuant to contracts concluded by the competent Minister as a result of a public auction in which the duration of the occupancy, the fees due therefor, and the rights of the occupant in the event of cancellation of the occupancy licence are determined, provided that these contracts are ratified by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the competent Minister.

Subject to the general provisions set forth in Articles Fourteen and Nineteen of this Law regarding the garage and basement floors, buildings whose height exceeds fifty metres / 50 m/ and large complexes shall benefit from an increase in the general exploitation factor in the event that the owner of the building or complex secures an independent additional garage having its own entrance and exit connected directly to the public road, accommodating at least fifty motor vehicles in independent parking spaces, provided that the ownership of this garage is registered in the name of the competent municipality.

The rate of increase in the general exploitation factor shall be determined at twelve square metres /12 m2/ for each motor vehicle parking space, provided that this increase does not exceed one thousand five hundred square metres /1500 m2/ regardless of the number of parking spaces in the additional garage, and a rate of ten percent /10%/ of the general exploitation factor, provided that it does not exceed two floors at most and after the approval of the Higher Council for Urban Planning.

The details of the management of garages shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.

In the event that it is impossible for a tourist establishment to secure a legally required garage in buildings existing on the date of entry into force of this Law, the tourist establishment occupying the existing building or any section thereof may pay an annual garage fee in favour of the municipality amounting to a rate of five percent /5%/ of the value of the garage fee determined according to the assessments adopted in accordance with the regulations in force.

The provisions of the first paragraph shall apply to tourist establishments that will occupy buildings or sections of buildings existing on the date of entry into force of this Law

provided that these buildings are legally licensed and not in violation of the building laws in force.

3 - General Conditions:

- The clear height must not exceed two metres and fifty centimetres (2.50 m) under the ceiling and two metres and twenty centimetres (2.20 m) under drop beams.

- An application for a permit to construct a collective garage for the public must include a study of the impact of its building on traffic movement (Traffic Impact

Study) and the manner of addressing these variables, and in the case of a collective garage, a detailed study of the facades of the building must be submitted.

In the event of a change in the intended use of the additional garage or the collective garage for the public, the constructions licensed for this purpose shall be considered

illegal and the State or the municipalities may demolish or confiscate them.

Areas allocated as additional parking spaces or collective garages for the public may be sold or leased without the possibility of changing their intended use, and in the event of a change in the intended use of the garage (additional or collective for the public), the constructions licensed for this purpose shall be considered illegal

and the State or the municipalities may demolish or confiscate them.

First - Subject to the condition of practising work within the Lebanese territories, the following shall be subject to the provisions of this Law as of the first phase:

1 - With regard to all the branches mentioned in Article 7:

a - Lebanese employees (workers and salaried employees), whether permanent, temporary, trainees, seasonal, or apprentices, who work for the account of one or more Lebanese or foreign employers, whatever the duration, type, nature, form, or validity of the contracts binding them to their employer, and whatever the form or nature of their earnings or wages, even if such earnings or wages are paid wholly or partially in the form of a commission, a share of profits, or based on production, and whether paid by the employer or by third parties.

b - Lebanese employees not bound to a specific employer who work in the maritime, ports, contracting, construction, loading, and unloading sectors, as well as Lebanese employees not bound to a specific employer, whatever the form, nature, or method of their earnings or wages.

c - Members of the teaching staff in higher education institutions provided for in the Higher Education Organisation Law issued on 26/12/1961 and the technical institutes provided for in Article 12 of Regulatory Decree No. 7880 dated 25/7/1967.
