Decrees passed in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and Social Affairs and the recommendation of the Board of Directors of the Fund, and under the conditions specified therein, shall determine the dates on which the implementation of each branch of social security shall commence for each of the sectors and categories mentioned in Sub-clauses (b - c) above of this Clause (1), and the conditions for the subjection of the two categories of temporary and seasonal employees mentioned in Sub-clause (a) of this Clause shall be determined in the same manner.

d - Lebanese persons who work for the account of the State, municipalities, or any public administration or public institution or autonomous service, whatever the duration, type, nature, form, or validity of their appointment or contracting with them, including collaborators with the Ministry of Information.

The persons mentioned above shall be subject to the End-of-Service Indemnity branch, and contributions shall be paid on their behalf as of the date of their entry into service if they are compulsory. Persons who entered into service before 1/5/1965 and continued therein may elect to join the End-of-Service Indemnity Fund within six months from the date of publication of this Law in the Official Gazette, in accordance with the procedures and under the conditions specified in Law No. 27/74 dated 25/9/1974. With regard to the branches of Family and Educational Allowances and Sickness and Maternity, no benefits actually paid to the aforementioned persons or any contributions actually paid on their behalf for the account of these two branches shall be recovered, and save for that, no retroactive effect shall be recognised.

Permanent State civil servants defined in Paragraph 2 of the First Article of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6/1959 shall be exempted from the provisions of this Sub-clause (d).

- Lebanese persons working for the account of municipalities shall be exempted from the effective date of subjection provided for in this Sub-clause above, and shall be subject to the branches of Sickness and Maternity, Family and Educational Allowances, and End-of-Service in accordance with the following provisions:

1 - To the two branches of Sickness and Maternity and Family and Educational Allowances, and contributions shall fall due on their behalf as of 1/4/1982 without any retroactive effect.

2 - To the End-of-Service branch, and contributions shall fall due on their behalf, whatever the date of their entry into service, as of the aforementioned date (1/4/1982), provided that they have continued in service until this date.

The municipalities shall liquidate their indemnities prior thereto in accordance with the provisions of Article 53 and submit the statement of the liquidation account to the Fund within a time limit of four months from the effective date of this Law, and these accounts shall remain frozen with the municipalities until the request for liquidation of the indemnity upon the fulfilment of one of the cases provided for by law. Upon the maturity of the indemnity, the account of the previous period shall be paid together with the settlement amount resulting from a liquidation in accordance with the legal provisions within a time limit of one month from the date of the demand for payment addressed by the Fund. No contributions paid to the Fund pursuant to the provisions of Law No. 16/75 shall be refunded to the municipalities, and no benefits actually paid by it in execution of the aforementioned Law shall be recovered.

- Lebanese persons working for the account of the National Council for Scientific Research shall be exempted from the effective date of subjection provided for in this Sub-clause above, and shall be subject to the branches of Sickness and Maternity, Family and Educational Allowances, and End-of-Service in accordance with the following provisions:

1 - To the two branches of Sickness and Maternity and Family and Educational Allowances, and contributions shall fall due on their behalf as of 1/1/86 without any retroactive effect.

2 - To the End-of-Service branch. Contributions shall fall due on their behalf, whatever the date of their entry into service, as of the date mentioned above (1/1/1986), provided that they have continued in service until this date. The National Council for Scientific Research shall liquidate their indemnities prior thereto in accordance with the provisions of Article 53 and submit the statement of the liquidation accounts to the Fund within a time limit of four months from the effective date of this Law, and these accounts shall remain frozen with the National Council for Scientific Research until the request for liquidation of the indemnities upon the fulfilment of one of the cases provided for by law, and upon the maturity of the indemnity, the account of the previous period shall be paid together with the settlement amount resulting from a liquidation in accordance with the legal provisions within one month from the date of the demand for payment addressed by the Fund. No contributions paid to the Fund pursuant to the provisions of Law No. 16/75 shall be refunded to the aforementioned Council, and no benefits actually paid by it in execution of the aforementioned Law shall be recovered.

e - Decrees passed in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and Social Affairs and the recommendation of the Board of Directors of the Fund, and under the conditions specified therein, shall determine the categories of public motor vehicle drivers, artisans, and all other categories of Lebanese persons not mentioned in this Article whom it proves necessary to subject, as of the first phase, to some or all of the branches of social security.

2 - With regard to the provision of medical care in cases of sickness, maternity, work accidents, and occupational diseases:

a - Permanent State civil servants defined in Sub-clause (d) of Clause (1) above of this Paragraph (First), with the exception of military personnel and members of the Internal Security Forces and General Security. The State Employees' Cooperative shall continue to grant the benefits or differences in benefits that the Social Security Fund does not provide to those affiliated with it, provided that the percentage of the financial contribution paid by the State to the Cooperative is determined by a decree passed in the Council of Ministers.

b - Members of the teaching staff in all private schools, whether tenured or non-tenured.

3 - With regard to medical care in cases of sickness and maternity only:

a - Lebanese students and students who do not hold a specific nationality or hold nationalities under study, in higher education institutions and technical institutes.

b - Foreign students residing in Lebanon, in accordance with bilateral agreements concluded between Lebanon and the States to which they belong. The conditions for the subjection and benefit of the categories mentioned in this Clause (3) shall be determined by decrees passed in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and Social Affairs and the recommendation of the Board of Directors of the Fund.

**- "Lebanese journalists and photographers who are not subject to the provisions of the Social Security Law and do not benefit from the benefits of any other public insurance scheme administered by any public entity, in any other capacity, subject to the condition of practising the work personally and actually on the Lebanese territories, provided that the journalists and photographers concerned by this Law shall be understood to mean Lebanese persons registered on the roll of their Syndicate for a period of not less than two years and who do not practise any other work as a principal occupation".

4 - With regard to some or all of the medical care benefits, in cases of sickness and maternity:

First:- Physicians accredited by the Fund in accordance with the provisions of the Social Security Law and the Internal Regulations, pursuant to a decree passed in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and Social Affairs and the recommendation of the Board of Directors of the Fund.

Second: Lebanese employees who have contracted in Lebanon with an establishment having a head office or a branch therein and who work abroad shall neither be subject to nor benefit from all or some of the branches, if in the country in which they work they are subject to and benefit from benefits at least equivalent to the benefits provided for in the Social Security Law, and the burden of proof shall lie with the employer. In all cases, the aforementioned employees who commenced their work in Lebanon and were transferred to work abroad, or who contracted to work abroad and were returned to work in Lebanon, shall be subject to the provisions of the End-of-Service Indemnity branch. In this case, the basic earnings or basic wage, excluding the allowances paid to them during or on the occasion of working abroad, shall be taken as a basis for calculating the contributions.

Third:

1 - Foreign employees working on the Lebanese territories who are bound to one or more employers, and the employers who employ them, shall be subject to all the obligations provided for in the Social Security Law under the conditions specified therein, with respect to the Sickness and Maternity insurance branch, the Family and Educational Allowances scheme, and the Work Accidents and Occupational Diseases insurance. Employers shall not be subject to the obligations relating to the End-of-Service branch unless the employees are entitled to benefit from benefits of this kind.

2 - The aforementioned foreign employees shall benefit from the benefits provided for in the Social Security Law, provided that they hold a work permit in accordance with the laws and regulations in force and that the State to which they belong recognises for Lebanese nationals the principle of equality of treatment with its own nationals with regard to social security.

3 - The States that grant Lebanon reciprocity with regard to social security and some or all of its branches, and the conditions for the benefit of their nationals, shall be determined pursuant to decisions issued by the Board of Directors of the Fund after consulting the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants.

4 - Family members of a foreign insured person who do not reside permanently on the territories of the Lebanese Republic shall not benefit from the social security scheme, with the exception of the end-of-service indemnity.

5 - The provisions of this Paragraph (Third) shall not apply to the employees set forth in Sub-clause (b) of Clause (1) of Paragraph (First) of this Article, such that only Lebanese employees shall be subject to and benefit from the provisions of the aforementioned Sub-clause.

- A working Palestinian refugee residing in Lebanon and registered with the Directorate of Political Affairs and Refugees - Ministry of Interior and Municipalities shall be subject exclusively to the provisions of the Labour Law with respect to end-of-service indemnity and work accidents.

A beneficiary among Palestinian refugee workers shall be exempted from the conditions of reciprocity provided for in the Labour Law and the Social Security Law, and shall benefit from the benefits of the end-of-service indemnity under the conditions under which a Lebanese worker benefits.

The administration of the National Social Security Fund must allocate a separate, independent account with it for the contributions pertaining to Palestinian refugee workers, provided that neither the Treasury nor the National Social Security Fund shall bear any financial commitment or obligation towards it.

Persons covered by the provisions of this Law shall not benefit from the benefits of the Sickness and Maternity Insurance and Family and Educational Benefits funds.

Fourth:

Foreign employees working in Lebanon pursuant to contracts concluded abroad with foreign establishments shall not be subject to the provisions of the Social Security Law if the employer proves that they benefit in the country where the contract was drawn up or the country to which they belong from social benefits that are in their totality at least equivalent to the benefits prescribed in the Lebanese Social Security Law.

Fifth:

1 - Journalists defined in Articles 10 and 11 of the Press Law issued on 14 September 1962 shall be subject to all branches of social security, and all texts of Law 56/65 relating to them shall be repealed.

2 - With respect to the End-of-Service branch, the following provisions shall be observed in respect of these journalists: The employer must draw up for the journalists working for him the account of the indemnity pertaining to each of them for the period of continuous work spent by them since their employment until the effective date of this Law.

3 - The calculation of this indemnity shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of the Labour Law, and the employer must deposit the indemnity account with the Fund within a time limit of one month from the effective date of this Law, and he must also notify a copy thereof to the journalist. Should he abstain from drawing up this account within the one-month time limit, the National Social Security Fund shall be entitled to draw it up automatically on the basis of the information available to it and the declaration of the journalist, and the account drawn up by the Fund shall be notified to the employer by one of the legal methods and shall become final after the expiry of a time limit of one month from the date of its notification if the objection provided for in Article 53 of the Social Security Law is not raised in respect thereof.

4 - The end-of-service indemnity recorded in the statement of account referred to in the preceding Clause shall be deemed due and payable immediately upon the entry into force of this Law, and the time limits and methods for settling the amounts owed by the employer shall be determined in accordance with the provisions of the Internal Regulations of the Fund.

Sixth:

1 - For the application of the provisions of this Paragraph, the word "retiree" shall mean the insured person whose service has ended due to reaching the legal age and the insured person whose service has ended due to disability.

Insured persons whose compulsory affiliation has ended due to retirement shall be subject to the Sickness and Maternity insurance branch in the National Social Security Fund, and shall benefit from the benefits of this branch (medical care in cases of sickness and maternity) in accordance with the conditions and obligations applicable to active insured persons.

2- The provisions of Clause (1) above shall cover insured persons who belong to one of the following categories:

a - The category of employees in the private sector provided for in Sub-clause (a) of Clause (1) of Paragraph (First) and Paragraph (Third) of the Ninth Article of the Social Security Law.

b - The category of Lebanese persons who work for the account of the State or any public administration or public institution or autonomous service, provided for in Sub-clause (d) of Clause (1) of Paragraph (First) of the aforementioned Ninth Article.

c - Permanent employees working in an agricultural enterprise who are subject pursuant to the provisions of Law No. 8/74 and the decrees completing it.

d - Physicians accredited by the Fund provided for in Clause (4) of Paragraph (First) of the Ninth Article of the Social Security Law.

e- This scheme may cover any other category determined by a decree passed in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and the recommendation of the Board of Directors of the National Social Security Fund.

3- In order for these persons to benefit, the following is required:

a - That the insured person has reached the legal retirement age (60 - 64 completed years) and has given up remunerated work or ceased his affiliation with the Order of Physicians, or that he has suffered a total and permanent disability reducing his earning capacity by at least 50%".

b - That he is not affiliated with another public health coverage scheme.

c - That he has a period of actual contribution to the Sickness and Maternity insurance branch of not less than twenty years.

d- That the beneficiary is residing on the Lebanese territories.

4 - a - Together with the retiree, his family members within the meaning of Article 14 of the Social Security Law who are dependent on him on the date of retirement or disability shall benefit.

b - In the event of the death of the retiree, or the death of the insured person prior to his retirement after completing a period of actual contribution of not less than twenty years, the right to benefit shall pass exclusively to:

- The partner, provided:

* That he or she has not remarried.

* And that he or she is not personally benefiting from another public health coverage scheme.

* And that he or she is not practising a liberal profession.

* And that he or she is not registered in the Commercial Register.

- The children until they reach the age of eighteen completed years, and if the children are unable to support themselves due to devoting their full time to their studies, they shall benefit from the insurance until the age of twenty-five completed years.

If the disabled children holding the personal disability card are unable to support themselves due to a disability preventing them from working, they shall benefit from the insurance benefits without an age limit.

5- The contributions necessary to cover the benefits shall be borne by each of:

a - Employees and working persons subject to this scheme who do not have an employer; the contribution rate referred to above shall be distributed as follows:

2% borne by the insured person and 1% borne by the State.

b - Retirees, and their contribution rate shall be fixed at the applicable official ordinary rate of a lump-sum income equal to the official minimum wage.

c - The State's contribution provided for in Article 73 of the Social Security Law shall apply to the benefits of retirees.

d - In the case provided for in Sub-clause (b) of Clause (4), the contributions shall fall due on the beneficiary partner, or on the adult child, or on the natural or legal guardians of minors, according to the status of the beneficiary individuals.

6 - The contribution rates and the income subject to contributions shall be amended, where necessary, by decrees passed in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and the recommendation of the Board of Directors of the Fund.

7 - This scheme shall have independent accounting within the scope of the Sickness and Maternity Insurance Fund, and the Fund shall conduct an actuarial study every three years to maintain the financial equilibrium of this scheme.

8 - The details of the application of this Law shall be determined, where necessary, pursuant to decisions issued by the Board of Directors and approved by the tutelage authority.

The travel agent shall keep the statutory registers, and in particular an inspection register in which shall be entered the names of the passengers and tourists who travelled through the agency, so that it may be inspected when necessary.

A - Proprietors of travel and tourism agencies shall charge the commissions determined by the official authorities on the basis of the rules and regulations

applied by the international organisations recognised by the Lebanese Government and which are consistent with the factual situation.

- The provisions of Articles 685 and 714 of the Penal Code shall apply to persons who contravene the contents of this Article.

B - A travel agency shall be entitled to retain at most 10 per cent of the value of the travel ticket the price of which has been paid to the carrier company where

the passenger cancels the trip due to force majeure or due to special circumstances that prevented him from travelling.

It shall likewise be entitled to retain at most 20 per cent of the original value of the travel ticket where the matter relates to a tourist trip abroad.

In exceptional cases, the travel agent shall submit the matter to the Ministry of Tourism to decide what is appropriate on the basis of the regulations issued by the international organisations which do not constitute an infringement of rights and which are consistent with the factual situation of the case in question, and in all events the passenger shall pay at least all the expenses caused by the rescission of the contract, save in the event of his death.

A travel and tourism agency shall be liable for the genuineness and suitability of the purchases made by a tourist from the shops to which it guides him, and it shall assist him in purchasing them at their true prices without any surcharge; the agency shall bear no liability where the tourist or the tourist groups are not accompanied by one of its representatives entrusted with this task.

A tourism agency may, when necessary, submit the matters and information available to it in this regard to the Ministry of Tourism for the appropriate measures to be taken in respect thereof.

Persons or tourist establishments sustaining damage as a result of a breach by a travel and tourism agency of the provisions of this Decree or of the specific acts relating to travel and tourism affairs may submit their complaints to the Ministry of Tourism directly or through the Lebanese missions if they are outside the country.

- The Ministry of Tourism shall be entitled, after taking the opinion of the Consultative Tourism Committee and by a decision of the Minister, to deduct the sums that may have accrued against it as a result of its breach of its obligations towards the passenger, the tourist or any other party from the principal of the bank guarantee furnished by the agency.
The Minister of Tourism may issue the necessary regulatory decisions that ensure the proper implementation of the provisions of this Decree.

The licence granted to the agency shall be displayed prominently in the place of work and at the head office. A copy of this licence shall also be placed at the premises of the branches belonging to the agency after its certification by the Ministry of Tourism.

Every travel and tourism agency shall submit to the Ministry of Tourism at the beginning of every year a statement of the names of the responsible persons authorised to sign travel tickets or instruments issued by it, as well as a statement of the names of the remaining employees who work at the agency, indicating their nationalities and the duties entrusted to them.

Religious, cultural and sports bodies may be granted temporary licences to undertake group trips, provided that the trip is for those affiliated with them and does not bear any profit-making character, and that the distribution of programmes is restricted within the offices of the body and to the members affiliated with it.

This must be carried out through one of the duly licensed travel and tourism agencies.

1 - Travel and tourism offices of all categories are prohibited from engaging in unfair competition relating to travel and transportation fares as well as established or approved tariffs and commissions.

2 - Every person is prohibited from dealing with travel and tourism agencies that are not officially licensed, or working to assist them and facilitate their operations directly or indirectly, especially itinerant individuals and brokers.

3 - Owners of hotels and nightclubs and other individuals, establishments, and companies are prohibited from carrying out operations similar to the operations of officially licensed travel and tourism agencies.

4 - It is prohibited to modify tourist programmes during the trip or less than seven days prior to the date of its commencement, and the aggrieved traveller or tourist shall have the right to claim damages resulting therefrom through the competent courts.

5 - Travel and tourism offices of all categories are prohibited from employing persons who have previously committed repeated violations or irregular conduct that harmed the reputation and dignity of the profession or the reputation of the country and tourism abroad.

6 - A travel and tourism agency of all categories is prohibited from issuing to a traveller or tourist a travel ticket, travel vouchers, or any other document before verifying the validity of the passport he holds, particularly when travel requires a special visa to enter the country to which he intends to go. Where the traveller or tourist requests it on his own responsibility, an undertaking to this effect shall be obtained from him and kept with the agency until requested.

7 - Representatives of foreign travel and tourism agencies are prohibited from carrying out tourist operations within Lebanese territory without accrediting a Lebanese agent duly licensed to engage in travel and tourism operations, and anyone other than licensed agencies who deals with such representatives shall bear the

liability for violating the provisions of this Decree, and legal measures shall be taken against him if the violation is proven.

8 - Every person is prohibited from publishing or distributing a brochure relating to travels or tourist trips, or advertising in any form that he engages in travel and tourism operations, except after obtaining an official licence from the Ministry of Tourism in due form and a special approval to this effect.

9 - Travel and tourism agencies are prohibited from publishing advertisements or distributing programmes for tourist trips that include unusual things and incorrect information that cause disruption in travel and transport operations, particularly with regard to the pilgrimage season or other religious, cultural, or sporting occasions.

10- Owners of travel and tourism agencies and the persons in charge therein are prohibited from utilising the services of guides who do not hold an official licence from the Ministry of Tourism.

The competent departments of the Ministry of Tourism shall have the right to propose the withdrawal of the licence granted to the agency if the following matters occur:

1 - If the company ceases operations and requests the cancellation of the licence.

2 - If the agency effectively ceases operations for a period exceeding one year.

3 - If the agency violates the conditions of establishment or any one of them.

4 - If the agency fails to renew the financial guarantee fifteen days prior to the date of expiry of its validity.

5 - If the agency commits an act that causes grave harm to the tourist reputation of Lebanon.

- The Ministry of Tourism shall have the right to assess exceptional cases and force majeure relating to these cases.

The Minister of Tourism may, upon the proposal of the competent departments of the Ministry, issue a decision closing a travel and tourism agency of any category if it engages in business without a licence, and confiscating the publications, printed matter, advertisements, and all elements belonging to the agency. The offender shall be referred to the competent court and shall not be granted a licence until after the execution of the judgment rendered against him in this regard.

Penalties:

Every violation of the provisions of this Decree shall be subject to the fine provided for in Article Ten of the Law promulgated on 2 June 1949 concerning companies and individuals engaging in passenger transport (imprisonment from one month to one year and a fine from 200 to 3000 Lebanese pounds), and apart from that, the laws in force shall apply to offenders.

- The trial shall be conducted in accordance with the summary procedures provided for in Articles 182 to 191 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

All agencies previously licensed prior to the promulgation of this Decree shall remain in their current status and shall be classified in the category suited to the nature of the business carried out therein, and the material circumstances preventing the fulfilment of the conditions imposed herein shall be taken into consideration in applying this Decree.

The provisions of this Decree shall apply at any subsequent time to previously licensed agencies in the event of a request to carry out the following amendments jointly:

1- A complete change of ownership.

2 - A change of trade name.

3 - A change of place of business.

The provisions of Annex No. 3 of Decree No. 15598 dated 21 September 1970 concerning the regulations on the supervision of tourist establishments and professions shall be observed in the supervision of travel and tourism agencies of all categories, and the Ministry of Tourism (Directorate of Tourist Equipment) is charged with the application thereof.

The Ministry of Tourism shall classify, pursuant to a decision by its Minister within a period of two years from the date of issuance of this Decree, the agencies licensed prior to the issuance of this Decree, No. 9429 dated 7/2/1968, in accordance with the division provided for in this Decree.

The classified agencies must submit, within a period of six months after being notified of their classification, the cash guarantee provided for in Article Seven thereof, under penalty of being deemed to be operating without a licence.

The provisions of Decree No. 9429 dated 7/2/1968 are hereby repealed.

As well as all decrees and regulations contrary to the provisions of this Decree or inconsistent with its content.
This Decree shall be published and notified where needed and shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Sole Article: The draft law relating to medical ethics, as amended by the Parliamentary Committees of Administration and Justice and of Public Health and by the Chamber of Deputies, is hereby ratified. This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.
All physicians registered with the two Orders of Physicians shall be subject to the provisions of this Law.

The mission of the physician consists in preserving the physical and mental health of the human being, both preventively and curatively, alleviating his suffering, and raising the general standard of health.

1- A physician, guided by his professional conscience, shall treat any patient, whether in time of war or peace, regardless of the financial or social status of such patient, and without regard to his race, nationality, creed, political opinions, feelings, or reputation.

2- The will of the patient shall be respected as far as possible, and where the patient is unable to express his opinion, the physician shall inform his relatives of the condition of their patient, except in cases of emergency or impossibility.

3- A physician shall refuse, whether in time of peace or war, and even under threat, to allow his professional qualifications to be exploited to assist in, participate in, or accept any inhuman treatment; and if he is requested to treat or examine an legally incapacitated person, and it becomes apparent to him that such person has been subjected to torture, he shall notify the judicial authorities.

A physician shall equip his clinic with appropriate equipment and sufficient technical means, and shall ensure that he does not practise his profession under circumstances and conditions that may prejudice his dignity or the quality of the treatment he prescribes.

1- Every physician, whatever his occupation and speciality, who is present with a sick or wounded person in danger, or is informed of the presence of a sick or wounded person in danger, shall assist such sick or wounded person or ensure that he receives the necessary first aid, except in cases of force majeure.

2- A physician may not refrain from answering a call for an emergency case unless he has ascertained the absence of any imminent danger to the patient or if he is detained for an urgent reason of equal importance to the condition of such patient, and in both cases he shall reply without delay stating his inability to attend and the reason therefor.

In the event of the outbreak of epidemics or the occurrence of disasters, the physician shall:

a- Not abandon the patients whom he is treating until he has ensured the continuation of such treatment by the best possible means.

b- Respond to the request of health officials to participate voluntarily in public vaccination campaigns and in the relief of disaster victims.

c- Comply with the laws and regulations relating to communicable diseases, notify the competent authorities thereof, and take the necessary preventive measures.

Professional secrecy imposed on a physician is a matter of public policy, and he must abide by it in all circumstances in which he is called upon to treat a patient or for consultation, subject to the exceptions imposed by public safety, laws, regulations, and contracts. This secrecy encompasses the information confided to him by the patient, and everything that he may have seen, learned, discovered, or deduced in the course of practising his profession or as a result of the examinations he has conducted, and accordingly:

1- The patient's release of his physician from professional secrecy shall not suffice to extinguish this obligation, as the physician remains bound to observe the interest of the patient and the requirements of public policy.

2- The physician must deliver to the patient in person, if the latter so requests of him, a certificate of his state of health, and he may omit from this certificate information which he deems to be in the patient's interest to withhold from him.

3- If the patient requests a certificate in order to benefit from social benefits, the physician may forward this certificate directly to the physician of the institution granting such benefits, provided that this is accompanied by the written consent of the patient or of one of his relatives where necessary, subject to the provisions of item 2 above.

4- When summoned by the judicial police to give his testimony regarding facts covered by professional secrecy, the physician may withhold some of his information, and he must disclose all of his information before the criminal courts when required to disclose it after being sworn in.

5- The physician is prohibited from reporting a patient who has confessed to him the commission of an offence. Where the physician discovers the commission of an offence during his examination of a patient, he must notify the Public Prosecution, and likewise if he is convinced that reporting will prevent the person concerned from committing other offences.

6- The physician must give his testimony before the courts when his giving thereof would prevent the conviction of an innocent person.

7- The physician shall be exempted from the duty of professional secrecy when called upon by the court in the capacity of an expert to examine a patient or to study his file, within the limits of the mission entrusted to him.

8- The physician must notify the health authorities of any contagious patient if this disease, as diagnosed by him, is included in the list of diseases legally required to be reported.

9- The physician must notify the competent authorities within three days of every delivery he has performed, and he may, where necessary, refrain from disclosing the name of the newborn's mother and the place of birth.

10- The physician must notify the health authorities of venereal diseases that are required to be reported by an official measure, and the notification shall include the name of the patient suffering from a venereal disease who refuses treatment, thereby exposing society to the spread of the disease.

11- If his patient dies of a disease that is required to be reported by an official measure, the physician must submit to the competent authorities a death certificate containing the patient's name, age, and date of death.

12- If the family of a person suffering from a serious mental or neurological illness requests the competent authorities to detain him on a precautionary basis, the physician examining him must draw up a report specifying the characteristics of the illness, accompanied by an explanation indicating that the patient poses a danger to himself or to others.

13- Physicians, and particularly those practising in dispensaries, hospitals, and mental institutions, may notify the health authorities of any alcohol or drug addict who refuses treatment or poses a danger to others.

14- If the physician discovers in the course of practice cases of rape and indecent assault, he must notify the Public Prosecutor, subject to the written consent of the victim.

15- If the physician discovers in the course of practice a case of arbitrary detention of a minor, or ill-treatment or deprivation, he must notify the competent authorities.

16- If the physician is prosecuted in a liability action by a patient or his family, he shall be entitled to disclose the facts necessary to establish the truth in self-defence.

17- A physician accused before the Disciplinary Council of the Order shall not be entitled to invoke professional secrecy.

18- The physician must ensure that his assistants abide by the obligation to preserve professional secrecy.

1- The freedom of the patient to choose his physician shall be respected, and the physician, if consulted by a patient, shall not impede his exercise of this right, nor his freedom to consult another physician.

2- The freedom of the physician to give the necessary instructions to his patient may not be restricted, and he shall have complete freedom to choose the most suitable treatment for him according to the best medical regulations in force.

3- The fees of the physician shall be determined by direct agreement with the patient unless there are unified tariffs determined by the Ministry of Public Health in respect of patients of official guaranteeing institutions in agreement with the Order of Physicians. The physician shall provide the patient with the necessary clarifications regarding the invoice for his fees, and he is not entitled to impose the method of payment, or to impose an additional lump-sum fee in return for an assurance of recovery.

4- The patient, his proxy, or his representative by contract with the physician, shall pay the fees due to the physician directly.

5- Hospital institutions shall pay the physician his full fees to which he is entitled.

1- When determining the fees of the physician, consideration shall be given to his professional standing, the financial condition of the patient, and the special circumstances of each case, with emphasis on the fact that the mission of the physician requires him to deal humanely with the indigent patient.

2- If several physicians cooperate in the diagnosis or treatment, and their cooperation is justified from the scientific standpoint. And they agree on collective fees. The fees of each of them shall be stated separately.

3- The physician shall abide by the tariff applied by the institution pursuant to hospitalisation contracts with private guaranteeing entities after agreement with the medical committee.

A physician may not reduce his fee for the purpose of competition below the minimum tariff by the Order of Physicians in agreement with the Ministry of Public Health. A physician may provide his assistance free of charge if he deems it appropriate It is prohibited to pay fees in advance as well as to agree on a lump-sum fee with a guarantee of recovery. In all cases, the provisions of general law and humanitarian principles shall be observed.

- It is strictly prohibited to split the fee between the attending physician and the consulting physician, or the surgeon or the specialist during the consultation or the surgical operation.

- When submitting a comprehensive statement of fees to the patient from the surgeon, the specialist, or the physician, the fee of the attending physician shall be stated therein.
With regard to surgical acts in which more than one physician participates, including the anaesthesiologist, the share of each of them shall be specified in the statement of fees.
If the physician attends a surgical operation at the request of the patient or those responsible for him, he shall be entitled to claim a special fee.

A physician shall not waive his professional independence, which is a right of the patient to obtain the care necessary for his cure and the relief of his pain, and the physician shall refuse, during practice, to submit to any pressure liable to influence his decisions.
A physician is prohibited from engaging in any other occupation alongside his profession that is incompatible with the dignity of this profession, or that is liable to demean its standing.

- The medical profession shall not be exploited for a commercial purpose.

- A physician is prohibited from resorting to direct and indirect methods of advertising. Except for advertising for a period of one month only the commencement of his practice or the relocation of his clinic, or the date of his departure and the date of his return.

- And he shall refuse the publication of articles in publications directed to the public that refer to his work, and that include his name and his address. He is entitled to participate, after notifying the Council of the Order of Physicians, in public discussions, and the Council may draw his attention to the fact that he is liable to prosecution if his participation therein results in a breach of medical ethics.

A physician shall not mention on his stationery, and on the sign of his clinic, anything other than:

1- Information that facilitates patients contacting him.

2- The specialty recognised for him by the Ministry of Public Health.

3- The titles granted to him by the State or the missions entrusted to him by it, provided that such information is stated in a form devoid of publicity.
Every physician is responsible for his professional acts.

Subject to the regulations of the institution contracted with and the provisions of the contract:

- A physician is not entitled to appoint as a substitute to carry out his professional activities and for a limited term anyone other than a colleague of his registered with the Order of Physicians.

- The substitute physician acts in the name of the principal physician and under his responsibility, and the substitute physician is bound to issue treatment prescriptions in his own name and under his own signature.

- A qualified specialist physician is not entitled to appoint a colleague of his as a substitute unless he is of the same specialty.

A physician is prohibited from:

1- Any act liable to procure for his patient an illicit, or unjustified, material benefit.

2- Paying commissions to anyone whomsoever, and in any form, with a view to attracting clientele or keeping them under treatment in the hospital or obtaining any private benefit.

3- Accepting commissions in return for laboratory tests and radiographic images or in return for prescribing certain medicines or using certain medical devices.

4- Accepting commissions from hospitals or health institutions in return for admitting a patient thereto.
A physician is prohibited from facilitating the work of anyone who practises medicine unlawfully.

Any financial sharing between physicians, pharmacists, physician assistants, or any other person is strictly prohibited. A physician is prohibited from conducting examinations in commercial premises and their annexes where medicines and medical instruments are displayed, as well as in pharmacies and laboratories, except in emergency cases that require hastening to treat an injured or sick person.

A physician is prohibited from practising any other profession or trade that would increase his profit by means of his medical prescriptions or his professional opinions, and if he holds a public office or is elected to an actual administrative function, he is prohibited from exploiting it in his profession and for the purpose of attracting clientele.

Advertising by any media means any method that is new of its kind for diagnosis or for treatment with the intent of inducing patients or colleagues to use it constitutes a fault for which the physician shall be held liable, particularly when the advertisement lacks a warning to patients or colleagues regarding the risks that may occur when using the advertised method.
Every report, certificate, or document issued by the physician must bear his signature, in accordance with the specimen registered at the Ministry of Public Health.
A physician is prohibited from issuing false reports or certificates of accommodation.

1- While treating the patient, the physician shall treat him with humanity, gentleness, and uprightness, and shall surround him with care and attention.

2- If the physician accepts to treat a patient, he shall be bound to ensure the continuity of his treatment, whether by himself or in cooperation with a qualified person, with full precision and a conscientious spirit and in accordance with the latest scientific data whose development he must follow.

3- The physician is prohibited from pursuing during his practice any interest other than the interest of the patient, or from exploiting in any manner his information to achieve private purposes.

4- The physician shall always respect the will of the patient, and if the condition of this patient does not allow him to express his will, inform his family, except in emergency cases or in the case of impossibility.

5- When the patient loses his liberty, this must not negatively affect the relations between him and the physician. The prisoner has the right to accept or refuse treatment, if that does not expose him to danger according to the report of the physician.

6- In the event of the patient going on a hunger strike, the physician shall intervene to persuade him to end his strike, and it shall be his duty to prescribe treatment in the hospital when the life of the patient becomes exposed to imminent danger.

7- If those whose beliefs prohibit them from undergoing vaccinations imposed by the competent health authorities refuse, the physician must confront them with their responsibilities and notify those authorities thereof.

8- If those whose beliefs prohibit them from blood transfusion refuse, the physician must respect their wish, except in the case of imminent danger, where he must, after obtaining the permission of the competent judicial authorities, act in accordance with what his professional conscience dictates, bearing his full responsibility.

9- If the afflicted or mentally retarded person refuses to take the proposed treatments, his relatives and the physician are permitted to dispense with his prior consent. If the patient is afflicted with dementia or insanity or constitutes a danger to others, the physician must ensure care for him in a hospital, and subject him when necessary to administrative detention therein, subject to the approval of a medical committee of at least three specialists.

10- If the patient is afflicted with an incurable disease, the mission of the physician shall be limited to alleviating his physical and psychological pains, and giving him the appropriate treatments to preserve his life as much as possible. - The physician does not have the right to intentionally cause the death of the patient; rather, it is preferable not to resort to technical means and exaggeration in treatment to prolong the duration of dying, and it remains necessary to assist the dying person until the end in a manner that preserves his dignity.

11- In the case of a collective work stoppage, the physician shall remain responsible for his duties towards his patients and for ensuring the continuity of treatment for them, and for any other emergency patient.

12- The physician shall leave to the patient in private classes the freedom to choose the surgeon, and the latter has the right to refuse any decision to perform an operation if it is not sufficiently reasoned, or for any other legitimate reason.

13- The surgeon shall, when the need arises, seek the assistance of assistant surgeons from within the hospital institution, if any, with the aim of ensuring the best care for his patient.

14- The anesthesiologist shall obtain from the surgeon before anesthesia or before preparing the patient for the operation all useful information, and he shall bear his responsibilities in monitoring the patient from the moment of anesthesia until full recovery, and he has the right to choose on his own responsibility the necessary available equipment and to choose his assistants from among the physicians and paramedics in the hospital institution in accordance with the regulations of the hospital in which he works, if any.

No surgical operation of any kind whatsoever that requires general anesthesia may be performed except under the supervision and in the presence of the anesthesiologist throughout all stages of the operation in its entirety.

A physician shall not be bound by an obligation of result in treating the patient, but rather by an obligation to ensure the best appropriate treatment for him. In light of this, the physician shall be subject to the following duties:

1- The physician shall always establish the diagnosis and the treatment in cooperation, if necessary, with qualified assistants, in accordance with the current state of medicine and without arbitrary practice.

2- After prescribing and determining the treatment to be followed, the physician shall oversee the follow-up of its execution.

3- In the event that the patient refuses the treatment, the physician shall have the right to cease following up with him, and if it appears to him that the patient is in danger, he shall exert his effort to convince him of the treatment, and where necessary, he shall consult one or more other physicians for this purpose.

1- Every physician shall keep a medical file for each of his patients in his clinic, for the preservation of which he shall be responsible, and the physician shall deliver a copy of the file to the patient when requested to do so, provided that the file includes all the information necessary to complete the diagnosis or to follow up on the treatment.

2- In the event of the physician's death or cessation of work, his replacement or the person to whom the clinic legally devolves shall, upon the request of the patients, transfer their files to the physicians who assume their treatment, and if no replacement physician or heirs are available, the Council of the Order shall have the right to take delivery of the files and preserve them.

3- If the files are the result of the work of several physicians and are imaged in a single institution, only the treating physicians and researchers shall have the right to inspect them. Such files or a copy thereof may be delivered to a third party bound by professional secrecy.

4- Medical files in hospital departments shall remain under the responsibility of the head of the department, who shall oversee their preservation and safety.

5- A visiting physician shall not have the right to inspect the medical file without the approval of the responsible physician.

6- A treating physician or researcher shall have the right to make use of the medical files under his responsibility to serve scientific development, provided that the names of his patients are not disclosed and provided that professional secrecy is maintained.

7- The investigating judge or the judicial police shall have the right to conduct a search of a physician's clinic or a medical department and to seize medical documents in his presence and in the presence of a member of the Council of the Order. In such case, the physician shall not have the right to oppose the search measures.

1- A physician shall be prohibited from performing or pursuing treatments that do not fall within his speciality, except in exceptional cases.

2- A physician shall be prohibited from prescribing, for the purpose of experimentation, treatments that are likely to harm the patient or expose him to danger.

3- New treatments may only be used after obtaining the consent of the patient, and provided that the treatment affords him a direct benefit, and after protective and appropriate scientific studies have been conducted for each case, and the consent of the parents or the legal representative shall be necessary when the matter concerns minor children or legally incapacitated persons. In the event that the treatment takes place in a hospital institution, the approval of the competent authority in this institution shall also be required, and after the approval of the Scientific Committee of the Order of Physicians when it is used outside the hospital.

4- No medical act that is likely to lead to the mutilation of the patient may be performed except in cases of emergency and extreme necessity, and except by a decision of at least two specialist physicians, and with the consent of the patient, or of his relatives if he is unable to decide, and the surgeon alone may decide, during emergency treatment, to perform an operation leading to mutilation, subject to the consent of the patient if he is conscious and aware or the consent of his relatives if they are present.

5- Every medical or surgical treatment that leads to a change of sex, and affects the future of the patient, shall be considered a mutilation.

6- The removal of an organ may be performed on a living adult human being enjoying his full mental faculties, for the purpose of performing a transplant operation having a therapeutic aim, after the free and explicit written consent of the donor and in the presence of a witness, and after the consequences of this removal have been explained to him.

- A donor may not be induced to donate an organ that affects his life.

- The removal of organs from the bodies of deceased persons may be performed, provided that they have bequeathed the same or after the consent of their families and for therapeutic or scientific aims.

7- Trafficking in human organs is strictly prohibited.

8- Artificial insemination or pregnancy by means of assisted fertility techniques may only be performed between spouses and with their written consent.

A physician who is called upon to treat a minor or a legally incapacitated person must ascertain the consent of his relatives, and in emergency cases he must carry out the necessary treatment if it is impossible to obtain the consent of his legal representative.

Performing an abortion is prohibited by law. As for therapeutic abortion, subject to doctrinal reservations, it may not be performed except under the following conditions and reservations:

1- That this abortion be the sole means of saving the life of the mother who is exposed to grave danger.

2- That the attending physician or surgeon mandatorily consult two physicians who agree with him by signing in writing on four copies, following medical examination and deliberation, that the life of the mother cannot be saved except by means of abortion, and one copy shall be delivered to the attending physician and one copy shall be kept with each of the two consulting physicians, and a registered record of the facts not bearing the name of the female patient shall be sent to the President of the Council of the Order of Physicians. Furthermore, an abortion may not be performed except upon the consent of the pregnant woman after informing her of the situation she is in; however, if she is in a state of grave danger and unconscious, and the therapeutic abortion is necessary for the safety of her life, the physician shall perform it even if her husband or her relatives object, and if the doctrine of the physician does not permit him to advise an abortion or to perform it, he may withdraw, leaving the continuation of care for the pregnant woman to another colleague who is a specialist.

In the event of obstructed or abnormal labour, the physician shall act in accordance with what medical art dictates in the interest of the mother and the child, without being influenced by family considerations.
The physician shall cooperate with the competent authorities for the purpose of preserving public health, taking into consideration his age, his specialty and his state of health.
The physician shall abide by the provisions of Article 28 of this Law, whatever the party that assigned him to perform the medical examination.

1- The engagement of a physician for medical work with any hospital institution must be documented by a written contract, provided that its provisions do not conflict with the provisions of this Law and the general laws and regulations.

2- Contracts binding physicians with public administrations and institutions shall be subject to the provisions of this Law, and to the general laws and regulations.

3- Each hospital institution shall have internal bylaws in a manner that does not conflict with the provisions of this Law.

4- Physicians contracted with a hospital institution must elect from among themselves a medical committee concerned with professional matters. The election of the members of the committee shall take place in accordance with rules and provisions that observe the internal bylaws of the hospital institution and do not conflict with the provisions of this Law.

The committee shall undertake the following tasks:

- Watching over the ethics and dignity of the medical profession.

- Striving to raise the professional standard by organising general meetings for the physicians in the hospital to discuss professional matters with regard to developing and improving professional work.

- Uniting the voice of physicians and preserving their rights and interests.

- Striving to resolve disputes that may arise between physicians or between them and their patients in cooperation with the hospital administration.

- Stimulating medical research and scientific exploration in cooperation with the Scientific Committee of the Order of Physicians.

- Expressing an opinion in an advisory capacity on matters pertaining to the hospital at the request of the administration.

- Expressing an opinion in an advisory capacity on the medical file of a physician with whom the hospital administration wishes to contract.

- Cooperating with the hospital administration in all common matters that concern the medical body and relate to hospital work.

- Within the framework of professional work, the committee shall be subject to the supervision of the Order of Physicians in accordance with the laws and regulations in force.

It is preferable that the work of a physician entrusted with preventive medicine in a given institution be limited to this mission, and that he not practise curative medicine at the same time except in emergency cases required by the exigencies of the public interest.
It is preferable that a supervising physician in a given institution not be a treating physician therein.

- A physician entrusted with medical supervision in a given administration must maintain professional secrecy and limit himself to giving information that is relevant or useful from the administrative standpoint without stating the medical reasons therefor.

- He is prohibited from giving the medical information recorded in the medical files to third parties or to any administration unless the general laws so provide or the patient concerned personally consents thereto.

A physician appointed as a sworn expert may not be the treating physician of the same patient concerning whose condition he is requested to draw up a report, and he may not accept to perform his mission as an expert if the matter relates to one of his clients or relatives, or if he has a personal interest in the case that is the subject of the assignment, unless the parties agree thereto.
A physician assigned a mission as an expert shall declare his capacity and his mission to the person whom he is assigned to examine before commencing the examination.

- A physician assigned the mission of an expert shall withdraw from the mission immediately if he observes that the questions put to him fall outside the scope of his medical profession.

- And he shall confine himself in his report to answering the questions put, and shall not address matters that may become apparent to him on the occasion of performing his mission, if they fall outside the scope of this mission, unless he assesses that remaining silent thereon would be detrimental to the course of justice.

A physician assigned to medical work in an institution shall, upon the occurrence of a serious pathological condition, and except for the cases mentioned in Article 31, inform the patient's family, and accept the calling in of any other physician if that is beneficial to the patient.

A physician shall communicate the result of the diagnosis to the patient, and he may conceal from him the result of a serious diagnosis, and shall not disclose the diagnosis of fatal cases except on an exceptional basis, and in a tactful manner, and he may communicate it to the family or the patient's relatives, unless the patient has previously requested not to reveal the truth of his illness to his family and designated to him the persons whom he may apprise thereof, in which case the physician shall be required to apprise those persons thereof.
A physician may refuse to care for a patient for professional or personal reasons, except in a case of necessity and in a case where he would be considered in breach of his humanitarian duties.

A physician may not interfere in the private affairs of his patient's family unless he is requested to do so. Nor may he act as an partisan of a family or of any person with the intent to influence the patient, unless that is in the medical interest of the patient.

A physician shall advise the betrothed couple to undergo the medical examinations required by the competent authorities prior to their marriage, and if they do so, he shall give each of them a certificate containing the result of these examinations.

1- Physicians must ensure the establishment of the best relations of collegiality and mutual assistance among themselves, while having regard for the interest of the patient.

2- A physician is prohibited from disparaging a colleague of his, gossiping about him, or spreading defamatory rumours about him that are liable to harm his professional practice.

3- The medical corps is a united whole, to ensure the honour and dignity of each member thereof.

4- Every physician must defend his colleague if he is subjected to false accusations.

5- In the event that disputes arise between physicians, they must be resolved amicably, and among themselves, and if that is not possible, then through the medical committee or the management of the institution, and otherwise through the Council of the Order in its capacity as the final authority to examine professional disputes.

6- A professional disagreement may not lead to a public controversy, and in the event of recourse to the judiciary, the competent President of the Order of Physicians must be notified prior thereto.

7- In the event of the termination of a physician's contract with a hospital institution or the suspension of his professional activity, it is advisable for the physician who wishes to fill the vacant position to contact his colleague whose contract was terminated or whose activity was suspended, and he must inform the Council of the Order in preservation of the ethics and laws of the profession and the rights of the physician and the patient.
- A physician must not charge fees to his colleagues and the members of their families who are their dependants, unless they are paid by a third party.

- The practice of the profession of medicine must take place within the scope of fair competition among colleagues, and any solicitation, diversion, or attempt at diversion of patients, and any unfair competition, fee-splitting, or monopoly shall be deemed a grave fault.

- Agreement among physicians must not turn into collusion at the expense of the patient. - The common fund within each hospital institution must exclusively include the fees of colleagues in the same specialty.

If a physician is called to treat a patient who is being treated by another colleague, he shall abide by the following rules:

1- If the patient intends to dispense with his first physician, the new physician shall ask the patient or the persons responsible for him to inform the first physician thereof.

2- If the patient desires only to consult the new physician while retaining the first physician, the new physician shall, after ensuring urgent treatment, propose an examination jointly with his colleague.

- Where a joint examination is impracticable, impossible, or inappropriate, the new physician may examine the patient and leave to his colleague the result of his diagnosis and the treatment he proposes.

3- If the treating physician is absent and the patient calls in a colleague of his, the latter shall ensure the treatment and withdraw upon the return of the first physician, after informing him of his findings.

4- A physician shall not have the right to treat the patients of a hospital institution attached to a principal physician in charge of treatment, except after obtaining the permission of the latter or in the cases permitted by the contract in force with the principal physician or the bylaws of the institution concerned. - In the event that a dispute arises between the two physicians, it shall be submitted to the Council of the Order.

A physician may receive in his clinic patients who have their own treating physician, provided that he informs the latter and consults with him after obtaining the patient's consent, and if that is in his interest.

The treating physician shall, when necessary, propose a medical consultation or accept it if requested by the patient or the persons responsible for him, and in both cases he shall submit the name of the physician whom he proposes, taking into consideration the wish of the patient, or accept to meet with any proposed physician registered on the roll of the Order and arrange for the meeting unless prevented by force majeure, and he may withdraw without justification if he considers that his position does not permit him to do so.

At the end of the consultation session, regardless of the number of physicians participating therein, a written report shall be drawn up, signed by all of them and containing the various opinions, and if this report is not drawn up, that shall be deemed proof that the opinion of the participating physician or physicians is in agreement with the opinion of the treating physician. In the event of a divergence of opinions, the treating physician shall have the right to withdraw if the opinion of the other physicians prevails.

The consulting physician shall not have the right to return a second time to visit the same patient in the absence of the treating physician or without his consent, during the period of the illness for which the consultation took place.

- Subject to the provisions of Article 19 of this Law, a physician is prohibited from substituting a colleague of his to treat his patients, except on a temporary basis and with their consent, and in such case the fees shall belong by right to the substitute physician alone. - A physician who is barred by a judicial or disciplinary decision from practising the profession may not have a colleague of his substitute for him throughout the period of the penalty, and this shall not exempt him from taking the necessary measures to ensure the continuity of care for his patients undergoing treatment when the penalty is imposed. - The Council of the Order must be notified of every decision barring practice, in order to take the necessary measures. - The substitute physician must relinquish his temporary mission once the continuity of care is ensured.

1- Physicians of a single speciality may form a civil professional partnership with or without legal personality, provided that every partnership contract is submitted for the approval of the Council of the Order.

2- The partnership shall pool the medical activities of the members and pool the fees in a single statement, and practice shall be restricted to the partner physicians.

3- If a group of physicians agrees to organise a statement of fees, this group must only include active physicians who participate in the care and practise the same speciality.

4- Physicians of different specialities may enter into a partnership by pooling the necessary means with a view to facilitating practice for each of them, and cooperation among them must be documented by a written contract or by a civil partnership enjoying moral personality, provided that the medical fees remain entirely independent of the partnership and are not in a single statement.

- No such partnership may be established in a hospital institution.

5- Every contract, whatever its nature, must comply with the professional rules, and a copy thereof must be communicated to the Order to verify its conformity with the model contract established by it.

6- No physician or medical student may work as an employee of another physician.

7- Whatever the nature of the partnership, the practice of the profession shall remain personal and each partner physician therein shall remain liable solely for his own work.

A physician must avoid, as far as possible, offending anyone connected with the medical field, and in particular pharmacists, dentists, midwives, nurses and assistants, when dealing with them in medical matters.

Upon his registration with the Order, a physician must declare that he has taken cognisance of this Law and must take the oath to abide by its provisions. The President of the Council of the Order shall draw up a record thereof, which he shall sign with the physician, and which shall be kept in the file of the latter.
Every physician who ceases to practise the profession in Lebanon must notify the Order thereof.
Every violation of the provisions of this Law shall expose its perpetrator to referral to the Disciplinary Council.
Decree No. 13187 dated 10/10/1969 and all provisions of decrees and decisions contrary to the provisions of this Law are repealed.
The details of application of the provisions of this Law shall be determined, where necessary, by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Health.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.
The urgent draft law referred to the Chamber of Deputies pursuant to Decree No. 11825 dated 19 January of the year 1963 is hereby put into effect, the text of which is as follows:
This Decree shall be published in the Official Gazette.

A Cooperative of State Employees shall be established, the competence of which shall cover all public administrations, personnel on the cadre of the Lebanese University other than members of the teaching staff, and civilian employees in the Customs, with the exception of the Judiciary, the Army, the Internal Security Forces, General Security, State Security, civilian personnel attached thereto, and the Customs Brigade.

It may cover employees of public institutions, autonomous agencies, and municipalities subject to the supervision of the Civil Service Board in accordance with the provisions of Article Three of this Law.

It may also cover permanent employees and guards of the Chamber of Deputies by a decision issued by the Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies.

The Cooperative shall be considered a public institution and shall enjoy legal personality and financial and administrative autonomy, and shall be subject to the tutelage of the Civil Service Board and to the ex post audit of the Court of Accounts.

It shall not be subject to the provisions of the Public Accounting Laws and the regulations of State employees except within the conditions set forth in this Law and subsequent regulations.

It shall have the right to litigate, to acquire movable and immovable property and to dispose thereof, and to accept donations and gifts.

Affiliation to the Cooperative, with all its benefits and obligations, is compulsory for permanent employees, whether or not they are subject to the retirement regime.

The regulations of the Cooperative shall, subsequently, determine the conditions for the admission of non-permanent employees and the extent to which they benefit from its services.

As for the employees of public institutions, autonomous agencies, and municipalities, the tutelage authority may decide, upon their request and upon the proposal of the Board of Directors of the Cooperative, to admit them therein after agreement with each institution concerned on the conditions of admission and the amount of the contribution that may be incurred by each of them.

The Cooperative shall provide to the permanent employees affiliated thereto:

First: All the benefits provided for in Article 29 of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12 June 1959 and in Articles 42 to 51 of Decree No. 3950 dated 27 April 1960, pending such time as the Social Security is able to provide these benefits.

Second: The benefits provided for in Articles 30 and 31 of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12 June 1959 (family benefit in the event of the death of the employee - employee benefit in the event of the death of one of the members of his family).

In addition to the allowances provided for in the preceding Article Four, the Cooperative shall provide to the affiliated members the following:

1- A lump-sum grant, the amount of which shall be determined in the regulations of the Cooperative, and which shall be paid to the contributors in the Cooperative Savings Fund provided for in Article 13 of this Law upon their leaving the service at any time whatsoever and for whatever reason, in addition to the amounts due to the employees in accordance with the laws in force.

2- A lump-sum grant on the occasion of marriage and birth.

3- Other allowances and grants that may be provided for in the regulations of the Cooperative.

4- Discounts in tariffs and prices through agreements concluded by the Cooperative with commercial and non-commercial private establishments.

The tutelage authority shall, by a decision issued by it and within the limits of the powers and jurisdictions of the Cooperative, undertake the formation of the committees arising from the application of the provisions of Articles 29, 30 and 31 of the Personnel Regulations and of Legislative Decree No. 113, particularly Article 23 thereof, both issued on 12 June 1959, and shall determine the manner of operation of these committees.

1- A mandatory monthly contribution deducted from the salary of every member affiliated with it in the amount of (3%) three percent of the gross basic salary.

2- An annual lump-sum subsidy provided by the State to the Cooperative, the effect of which shall be that the State is released thereby from its obligations towards the employees affiliated with the Cooperative as defined in Articles 29, 30 and 31 of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12 June 1959 and in Articles 42 to 51 of Decree No. 3950 dated 27 April of the year 1960.

This subsidy shall be determined every year in the budget, provided that it is not less than six percent of the total gross basic annual salaries of the employees affiliated with the Cooperative.

The rate of this subsidy may be amended, after the establishment of Social Security, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the recommendation of the tutelage authority.

3- Revenues from the investment of the funds of the Cooperative.

4- Gifts and donations the acceptance of which is approved by the Cooperative after the approval of the tutelage authority.

The subsidy of the State to the Cooperative shall be appropriated in the budget of the Presidency of the Council of Ministers (Civil Service Board) in the name of the "State Employees' Cooperative" and shall be paid to the Cooperative in two instalments: the first on the first of February and the second on the first of July, and the subsidies of the State to the Cooperative may be paid in the form of a budget advance if the ratification of the budget is delayed, provided that it is settled from the budget item mentioned above.

If the Cooperative falls into a financial deficit, and the reserve is insufficient to cover it, or if the supervisory authority objects to the use of this reserve, the State and the members affiliated with the Cooperative shall bear this deficit in a proportion equal to the proportion of the contribution specified for each of them in the seventh article of this Law.
The administrative expenses of the Cooperative shall be met from its revenues, and a special annual budget shall be drawn up for it, subject to the approval of the supervisory authority.

Following the publication of this Law, the Government is authorised to open in the budget of the year in which it is published supplementary appropriations not exceeding a total of /250000/ L.L. to be taken from the reserve fund by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers to cover the various expenses required by the establishment of the Cooperative.

The appropriation provided for in the preceding article shall be used in accordance with the following exceptional procedures:

1- The President of the Civil Service Board, or whomever he delegates for this purpose, shall undertake the commitment and liquidation of the expenditure.

2- From this appropriation shall be disbursed the salaries, wages, and various allowances due to employees, experts, and others, and the price of machinery and technical equipment and their maintenance, as well as all other supplies, communications, and other general expenses required by the establishment of the Cooperative and the provision of its equipment.

3- The purchase of whatever the Cooperative needs from this appropriation is authorised by mutual agreement, regardless of the value.
A cooperative savings fund shall be established within the Cooperative, in which deposits shall be accepted on an optional basis in return for interest.

The supervisory authority shall lay down the special regulations for this fund and the manner of managing its operations.

It shall enter into force after its approval by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.
The State guarantees all amounts deposited in the cooperative savings fund and their return to their owners together with the accrued interest.

The supervisory authority has the right, two years after the entry into force of this Law, to decide, where necessary, and after obtaining the approval of the Council of Ministers, to make the contribution of the affiliated members to the cooperative savings fund compulsory.

The supervisory authority shall lay down, within six months starting from the date of issuance of this Law, all the regulations required by the operations of the Cooperative. These regulations shall become effective after being approved by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.

There shall be determined in these regulations in particular:

1- The manner of appointing the Board of Directors of the Cooperative and defining its powers.

2- The administrative and technical bodies of the Cooperative.

3- The internal administrative and financial organisation.

4- The manner of applying the supervision of the Civil Service Board.

5- The rules of audit by the Court of Audit provided for in the second Article of this Law.

6- The benefits that members may obtain and the conditions imposed therefor.
