Secretariat of the Board Session: 23/2003 Item: 9 Decision No. 292/2003 The Central Inspection Board, Having perused the file of the case registered under No. 5/3/98 and 65/7/99 with all its contents

1775/99 Having perused the report of the Administrative Inspector Miss Muntaha Aoun dated 1/6/98, resulting from the investigation into the continuation in service of employees, wage earners and contractors at the Ministry of Information despite having reached the legal age. Having perused the two reports of the Financial Inspectors Mr. Mohammad Halawi and Mr. Michel Dib dated 27/4/2002 and 2/7/2002, resulting from the investigation into the violations attributed to certain workers at the Ministry of Information regarding the disbursement of allowances and fees and the payment thereof contrary to the laws and regulations in force. Having perused the two reports of the Financial Inspector Mr. Mohammad Halawi dated 19/10/2002 and 22/1/2003 Having perused the opinion of the Administrative Inspector General dated 4/6/ 98 Having perused the two opinions of the Financial Inspector General dated 25/7 /2002 and 26/10/2002 Having perused the opinion of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Audit No. 74/467 dated 24/2/2003 Having perused the opinion of the President of the Central Inspection dated 8/ 3/2003 And whereas it has been established from the documents of the file that an investigation was conducted into the conditions of the Ministry of Information, pursuant to the two assignments No. 5/3/98 and No. 65/7/99, based on: - Letter ......... to the Ministry No. 82 dated 3/2/98, relating to the continuation in service of employees, wage earners and contractors at the Ministry despite having reached the legal age. - Letter of the Civil Service Board No. 1414 dated 30/3/99, relating to certain full-time wage earners, contractors and producers at the Ministry of Information also working in public and private institutions. - Letter of the Secretary General of the Council of Ministers No. 781/3 S dated 11/5/99, containing a request to conduct an investigation into the conditions of the Ministry of Information, based on the opinion issued by the Council of Ministers in its session held on 28/4/99, in accordance with the contents of the report of the Accounting Office. And whereas it has been established from the investigation that collaboration with the Ministry of Information, which was regulated pursuant to Decision of the Minister of Information No. 103/ 72, and which aims to produce media programmes in the broadcasting, news and publicity fields and in all other activities of the units of the Ministry, has departed from the purpose for which it was established and turned into a labour market, in accordance with the contents of the two letters of the Civil Service Board No. 3918/95 and No. 420 dated 20/3/98, and the investigations conducted by both the Comprehensive Survey Committee and the company specialised in accounting and auditing works, and that there are administrative and financial irregularities that appeared as a result of auditing the documents relating to collaborators at the Ministry of Information, particularly in the financial schedules and the annexes thereto.

And whereas it has been established that the schedules of allowances for collaborators in the Ministry of Information, pertaining to the period prior to the year 1999, were being prepared at the Administrative Secretariat attached to the National News Agency pursuant to the instructions of the Director of the Agency, prior to their bearing the signature of......., the Minister of Information, in violation of the provisions of Article 13 of Decree No. 8588/ 62, which does not vest the Administrative Secretariat with any accounting task, and of the provisions of Article 3 of the same Decree, which entrusted the central accounting of the Ministry and all of its units to the Accounting Department attached to the Diwan Service in the Ministry, such that the role of........ was restricted solely to liquidation operations and the reservation of appropriations, to the exclusion of all else. And whereas it has been established that more than one-third of the number of collaborators in the Ministry of Information do not hold academic degrees or qualifications and do not possess media competence and experience and have not provided, as a result thereof, any media, guidance, or technical services or consultations, in fulfilment of the provisions of Articles 7 and 8 of Decree No. 7276/61, and the provisions of Article 7 of Legislative Decree No. 25/83, and Articles: 3, 5, 6, 7 of the Decision allocated to those who possess the required qualifications, and that is in violation of the provisions of Article Five of Decision No. 103/72, which stipulated that collaboration shall be strictly within the limits of the production provided by the collaborator without any mention of other additions, and of the provisions of Article Six of the same Decision, which explicitly stipulates that collaboration does not confer upon its holder any of the rights of public office, employment, or contracting, in particular allowances, regardless of the duration of the collaboration. And whereas it has been established that the names of civil servants, wage earners, and contracted personnel were included in the schedules of allowances specific to the National News Agency and Studies, in violation of the provisions of Article 16 of the Civil Servants Regulations, and of the provisions of Articles 17 and 19 of the General Regulations for Wage Earners, and furthermore that 68 civil servants, wage earners, contracted personnel, and collaborators had reached the statutory age and continued to work in the capacity of collaborators in the Ministry and received fixed monthly allowances in violation of the provisions of Article 68 of the Civil Servants Regulations and Article 33 of the General Regulations for Wage Earners, and of the opinion of the Civil Service Board, which authorised, pursuant to its letter No. 420 dated 20/3/98, the engagement of the services of persons who have reached sixty-four years of age to provide intellectual activity and production and to receive fees therefor commensurate with the volume of deliverables, rather than receiving fixed monthly allocations tantamount to salaries in accordance with what was taking place with the collaborators referred to above. And whereas it has been established that the cheques drawn for the value of the allowances and pertaining to dozens of collaborators were delivered to persons other than their rightful holders without the existence of legal powers of attorney or official authorisation held by the collaborators and civil servants who received the aforementioned cheques, and that........, Mr........, justified the delivery of the cheques to persons other than their rightful holders as being the execution of verbal instructions that he used to receive from higher authorities in the Ministry, a matter which violates the provisions of Article 186 of the Public Accounting Law, which required...... to verify, on his own responsibility, the identity of the rightful payee and the authenticity of his signature. And whereas it has been established that there is manipulation in the inclusion of the names of collaborators in the Ministry of Information with respect to the failure to adopt alphabetical order, and with respect to the inclusion of the name of the same collaborator in different forms in order to conceal the true amount received by each collaborator, which consequently necessitates recommending the adoption of alphabetical order and the tripartite name in writing the names on the payment schedules, and placing the date alongside the name and signature of the person who receives the cheque from the disbursement officer.

Whereas it was established that the allowances included in the liquidation of the end-of-service indemnity were restricted, according to the statement of...... to the basic allowance without any other allowance, pursuant to an agreement with the National Social Security Fund, which contravenes the provisions of Article 68 of the Social Security Law, which stipulated that the earnings taken as a basis for calculating contributions must include the total income resulting from work, including all elements and accessories, in particular the overtime hours allowance paid on a customary basis and the amounts customarily paid by third parties (gratuities), as well as the benefits provided in kind to the worker, which requires recommending taking action to liquidate the end-of-service indemnities for those affiliated with the National Social Security Fund in accordance with the provisions of the aforementioned Article. Whereas it was established that a number exceeding seventy contractors submitted statements including their performance of work in other official and non-official administrations and institutions during working hours that conflict with their working hours at the Ministry of Information, contrary to the law and in particular to the provisions of Article 16 of the Civil Servants Regulations, which requires recommending not contracting with any person working full-time in other administrations or institutions, and in general not contracting with any person whose work at the Ministry conflicts with any other work. Whereas it was established that travel missions abroad were carried out in the Ministry of Information pursuant to an assignment by the Minister of Information based on a memorandum issued by him in this regard bearing the number 16/79, contrary to the texts in force, in particular Decree No. 3950/60 and Council of Ministers Decision No. 43 dated 24/4 /74, which requires recommending the reconsideration of the aforementioned memorandum with regard to complying with the aforementioned Decision of the Council of Ministers, which requires obtaining its prior approval for travelling abroad. Whereas the issue of contractors at the Ministry of Information in its entirety was and still is accompanied by known circumstances (political and social), as the employment of all or most of the contractors did not originally arise from a genuine need of the Ministry, and the employment in itself was often not carried out in accordance with legal procedures and rules, with the administrative and financial defect it entails at the same time, making it impossible for the successive Directors General at the Ministry to address this issue with appropriate solutions unless political cover and support were available to them, which was not taking place at the time, as evidenced by the Council of Ministers recently resolving the matter through its Decision No. /71/ taken in its session held on 22/2/2001, resulting in the issuance of Decree No. 5240 dated 5/4/2001, which considered all contractors at the Ministry of Information to be surplus, and entrusted the Civil Service Board with finding appropriate solutions for them by distributing them to public administrations, public institutions and municipalities according to their needs, while continuing to pay their wages until their status is settled. Whereas, in view of the foregoing, it is possible to take into consideration the totality of the social and political circumstances referred to above and not hold the competent civil servants at the Ministry of Information, namely Messrs:.......,.......,......., disciplinarily liable in this regard; however, the financial liability of these civil servants remains standing as a result of disbursing allowances to the contractors in a manner that caused damage and loss to public funds, which requires referring the file to the Court of Audit in accordance with the submission of the Public Prosecution.

(e) - Not to contract with any person working full-time in other administrations or institutions, whether official or unofficial, and in general not to contract with any person whose work at the Ministry conflicts with any other work. (f) - To abide by the provisions of Decree No. 3950/60 by Decision of the Council of Ministers No. 43 dated 24/4/74 relating to travel abroad on official missions with respect to obtaining the prior approval of the Council of Ministers in this field. 3 - To dispense with the disciplinary responsibilities of the employees working at the Ministry of Information. A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the eighteenth day of the month of June of the year two thousand and three.

Whereas it has been established that the Ministry of Information proceeded, with effect from late 1999, to organise and keep a personal file for each freelancer containing the documents relating to his employment status and to adopt his tripartite name on the schedules of allowances and remunerations, and to have the heads of the competent units in the Ministry sign these schedules on their own responsibility in confirmation that those freelancers have performed actual service, and that the Ministry expressed its wish to fill certain vacant and newly created positions from among the surplus of freelancers determined pursuant to Decree No. 5240/2001, referred to above, whereby Decision No. 125/2002 of the Civil Service Board was issued, pursuant to which approximately /650/ freelancers were attached in the capacity of contractors at the Ministry, which requires recommending the continuation of addressing the deficiencies that impede the workflow in the Ministry of Information and proceeding with the regularisation of the situation in its various aspects. Following deliberation, and in the light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided: 1 - To refer the investigation file to the Court of Audit. 2 - To recommend to the Ministry of Information the following: a - To keep and preserve the personal files of all workers in the Ministry of Information with the Registry Department and to deposit copies thereof with the units concerned, where necessary. b - To adopt alphabetical order and the tripartite name in writing the names on the payment schedules and to place the date next to the name and signature of the person who receives the cheque from the paymaster. c - To follow up the measures which the Ministry of Information proceeded to implement since late 99, in particular with respect to: - Including in the personal file of each of its workers all the documents relating to his employment status and adopting his tripartite name in every document relating to him. - Restricting the matter of engaging persons as freelancers in the future within the limits of Decision No. 103/72, particularly with respect to the conditions adopted for the payment of remunerations. - Disbursing entitlements to their holders by means of cheques payable to the first beneficiary, provided that the cheques shall be delivered only to the person concerned in person or to another person pursuant to a legal power of attorney, and retaining the cheque stubs for reference thereto where necessary until salaries and their accessories are domiciled in the same manner as in other public administrations. - Carrying out monthly reconciliation operations for the banks account. d - Liquidating the end-of-service indemnities of persons affiliated with the National Social Security Fund in accordance with the provisions of Article 68 of the Social Security Law.

Secretariat of the Board Session: 1/2003 Item: 2 Decision No. 2/2003 The Central Inspection Board, Having perused the file of the case registered under No. 44/3B/ 2002 with all its contents. Having perused the report of the Administrative Inspectors Mr. Rabih Al-Timani and Miss Rania Al-Jamal dated 17/10/2002, resulting from the investigation into the violations attributed to the head and physicians of........ Governmental Hospital. Having perused the opinion of the Administrative Inspector General dated 26/ 11/2002 Having perused the opinion of the President of the Central Inspection dated 10 /12/2002 Whereas it appeared that a complaint was received by the Central Inspection against the head of...... Governmental Hospital and the physicians working therein, regarding their non-compliance with the provisions of the laws and regulations in force, particularly the provisions on working hours, and their sharing of the medicines sent by the Ministry of Public Health and selling them contrary to the rules, and other points set forth in the aforementioned complaint, and that the competent inspectors undertook the investigation of the matter within the scope of the annual inspection programme for the year 2002 And whereas it appeared from the investigation that the physician........ contracted with the Ministry of Public Health, to work at...... Governmental Hospital, has not fulfilled since the beginning of the year 2002 the working hours specified pursuant to the contract signed between her and the aforementioned Ministry, as she was attending nine hours instead of eighteen hours per week, and she also left the Lebanese territory on 29/6/2000 for a period of two months without any decision permitting her to do so, and again left the Lebanese territory on 12/7/2001 prior to the entry into effect of her administrative leave, then absented herself from her duty station on 3/7/2002 and left abroad without legal justification, thereby violating the provisions of Articles One and Four of the contract signed between her and the Ministry of Public Health, which entails disciplinary liability on her part. And whereas it appeared that Dr......... in addition to her grave violations of the provisions of the contract signed between her and the Ministry of Public Health, was, up to the date of preparation of the inspection report, still outside the Lebanese territory, and that she has come, according to the statement of the head of....... Governmental Hospital, to reside abroad permanently, and that the latter has referred the matter to the concerned authorities in the aforementioned Ministry to take the necessary action, which requires recommending to the Ministry of Public Health to work on terminating the contract signed between it and Dr......... pursuant to the provisions of Article Nine thereof. And whereas it appeared that the contractor with the Ministry of Public Health Dr........, head of........ Governmental Hospital, was covering up the unlawful absence of Dr........ from her duty station, and was allowing her husband Dr......... to examine patients during his wife's presence abroad, and to sign on her behalf in the physicians' attendance register, and he was also allowing the collection of an amount of five thousand L.L. from patients who undergo medical examination and from those for whom hospitalisation cards are drawn up for the benefit of the support committee of the aforementioned hospital, without basing this conduct of his on a legal or regulatory text authorising him to do so, thereby violating the provisions of Article Four of the agreement signed between him and the Ministry of Public Health, which entails disciplinary liability on his part. And whereas nothing appeared from the interrogation record of....... and from his written defence that would exempt him from liability, which requires taking the appropriate disciplinary measures against him pursuant to the provisions of Article Eight of the agreement signed between him and the Ministry of Public Health.

Whereas it has been established that the Central Inspection Board had previously made recommendations to the Ministry of Public Health regarding the committees for the support of public hospitals, and that it proceeded to take the appropriate measures in respect thereof successively, and whereas that which was stated in the complaint referred to above, regarding the doctors at ........ Public Hospital dividing medicines among themselves, and regarding their failure to comply with the provisions of working hours and other violations, has not been proven to be true, which requires closing the case in this respect. Following deliberation, and in the circumstances of the case. It is decided 1 - To deduct the contractual allowance of the contractor with the Ministry of Public Health, the Head of ....... Public Hospital, Doctor ......... for six days as a disciplinary measure. 2 - To recommend to the Ministry of Public Health, to work on rescinding the contract signed between it and Doctor ........ for the reasons referred to in the body of this decision. 3 - To close the case in respect of all other points. A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the eighth of the month of January of the year two thousand and three.

Secretariat of the Board Session: 2/2003 Item: 2 Decision No. 17/2003 The Central Inspection Board, Having perused the file of the case registered under No. 42/3/2002 with all its contents. Having perused the report of the Administrative Inspector Mr. Naji Mustafa dated 13/11/2002, resulting from the investigation into the violations attributed to an employee of the Ministry of Finance. Having perused the opinion of the Administrative Inspector General dated 12/ 12/2002 Having perused the opinion of the President of the Central Inspection dated 26 /12/2002 Whereas it was established that the Minister of Finance, pursuant to his letter No. 2123/S 1 dated 16/10/2002, deposited with the Central Inspection a copy of the record of the preliminary investigation conducted by the Nabatieh Judicial Detachment with the employee at the Ministry of Finance Mr........, regarding the complaint filed against him for the offence of fraud, requesting an investigation into the information contained in the said record given that this employee has a prior record, and Assignment No. 42/3/2002 was issued to investigate the matter. Whereas it was established that the employee at the Ministry of Finance,........ at the Finance Department of Nabatieh, Mr........, confessed in the investigation conducted with him by the Nabatieh Judicial Detachment, that he agreed with one of the concerned parties, Mr.......... to release one of his real properties from the estate of the heirs of........, in return for an amount of four thousand US dollars and two million and eighty-five thousand L.L. Whereas it was established that the claim of Mr........ during his interrogation by the competent inspector, that he received from Mr......... the amount referred to above, to pay it as a fee due at the Directorate of Revenues in return for completing his transaction, and not as a commission, contradicts the truth and reality, since the fee due for releasing one of the two real properties owned by the concerned party from the estate exceeds ninety million L.L. Whereas it was established that Mr......... and in addition to the foregoing, gave during his interrogation different and contradictory information from that which he had previously confessed during the investigation conducted with him by the Judicial Detachment in Nabatieh, and contrary to what was stated by the concerned parties directly or through their legal representatives, thereby attempting to mislead the investigation. Whereas it was established that Mr......... follows up on the transactions of the concerned parties in the various administrative units, in return for receiving sums of money other than the fees due for completing them, a matter which falls outside the scope of his powers and constitutes a grave breach of his functional duties provided for in Articles 14 and 15 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 and its amendments (Personnel Statute), which entails disciplinary liability upon him.

Whereas it did not appear from the record of interrogation of Mr........ and from his written defence anything that would exempt him from liability, which necessitates taking the appropriate disciplinary measures against him pursuant to the provisions of Articles 54 and 55 of Legislative Decree No. 112 /59 and its amendments (Civil Servants Regulations), and referring him before the Higher Disciplinary Board. Whereas it appeared that some concerned parties have brought a claim against Mr....... before the competent judiciary, for the offence of fraud and abuse of his official position, and he was also judicially detained twice during the years 2001 and 2002, which necessitates lodging with the Cassation Public Prosecution a copy of the investigation file in connection with the ongoing investigations before the competent judiciary in this matter. Whereas the public prosecution action, pursuant to the provisions of the fifth paragraph of Article 61 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 and its amendments (Civil Servants Regulations), is independent of the disciplinary action, and the institution of the public prosecution action does not preclude the institution of the disciplinary action, proceeding therewith, and ruling thereon. And after deliberation, and in light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided: 1 - To delay the advancement in step of the civil servant in the Ministry of Finance, Nabatieh Finance Department, Mr....... (his financial number.......) for a period of twelve months by way of discipline, and to refer him before the Higher Disciplinary Board. 2 - To lodge with the Cassation Public Prosecution a copy of the investigation file, in connection with the ongoing investigations before the competent judiciary in this matter. A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the fifteenth of the month of January in the year two thousand and three.

Secretariat of the Board Session: 7/2003 Item: 11 Decision No. 104/2003 The Central Inspection Board, having perused the file of the case registered under No. 23/5/2001 and 27/7/2001 with all its contents.

1464/M 2001 Having perused the report of the two Educational Inspectors, Mr. Fawzi Ishac and Mr. Faraj Farah, and the Financial Inspector, Mr. Antoine Nohra, dated 2/10/2002, concerning the investigation into the violations attributed to....... Halba, Akkar. Halba, Akkar, Mr........., and Assignment Orders No. 23/5/2001 (educational) and 27/7/2001 (financial) dated 6/6/2001 were issued to investigate the matter. Whereas it appeared that........ Halba, Mr. ......., Mr. ......., entail disciplinary liability on their part pursuant to the provisions of Article 14 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 and its amendments (Civil Servants Regulations). Whereas what was stated in the two interrogation records of Mr. ......., and in their two written defences, is not such as to exempt them from liability, which requires taking the appropriate disciplinary measures against them pursuant to the provisions of Articles 54 and 55 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 and its amendments (Civil Servants Regulations), and referring Mr. ...... before the Court of Accounts pursuant to the provisions of Article 60 of Legislative Decree No. 82/83 (Organisation of the Court of Accounts). Secretariat of the Board Session: 35/2003 Item: 4 Decision No. 405/2003 The Central Inspection Board, Having perused the file of the case registered under No. 86/3B/ 2003 with all its contents. Whereas it appeared that the employee at the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities, Directorate General of Personal Status, Nabatieh Civil Status Registry, Mrs. ......, exchanged inside the said Registry with her colleague Mr. ....... foul speech, during the verbal altercation that took place between them on 20/6/2003, thereby violating the provisions of Article 14 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 and its amendments (Personnel Regulations), which entails disciplinary liability on her part. (born in ......1), (financial number .......) for one day as a disciplinary measure. 3 - To recommend to the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities, Directorate General of Personal Status, to work towards transferring the clerk on its establishment, Mr. ......., to another duty station where the reputation of the public service will be safeguarded from exposure. Secretariat of the Board Session: 2/2003 Item: 6 Decision No. 21/2003 The Central Inspection Board, having perused the file of the case registered under No. 25/7/2001 in all its contents. Having perused the report of the Financial Inspector, Mr. Khaled Al-Fawwaz, dated 5/10/2002, resulting from the investigation into the violations committed in the execution of the works contract for the Abdeh -aan- Berkayel -aan- Fnaydek -aan- Qammouaa road. Having perused the opinion of the Financial Inspector General dated 4/11/ 2002 Having perused the opinion of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Accounts No. 466/3884 dated 17/12/2002 Having perused the opinion of the President of the Central Inspection dated 31 /12/2002 And whereas it appeared from the documents of the file that there is a financial violation in the Ministry of Public Works and Transport, relating to the execution of a public works contract, and that the Minister of Finance requested, pursuant to his two letters No. 748 /S 1 dated 21/5/2001, and No. 948/S 1 dated 20/ 5/2002, an investigation into the execution of the aforementioned contract pertaining to the Abdeh - Berkayel - Fnaydek - Qammouaa road with respect to ascertaining the rightful claimants to the amounts due for the execution of these works, and the President of the Central Inspection issued the assignment No. 25/7/2001 dated 24/5/2001 to investigate the matter. And whereas it appeared as a result of the investigation that the Ministry of Public Works and Transport concluded, through the Maintenance Department affiliated to it, a contract for the execution of the works of the road mentioned above, by mutual agreement with ....... Trading Establishment, for a total value amounting to /836000000 /L.L. (eight hundred and thirty-six million Lebanese Pounds) and a supervision contract also by mutual agreement with the office of Engineer......, in return for 3% of the value of the executed works, and that these works were divided into nine interconnected sections. And whereas it appeared that the Maintenance Department stated that the execution of the aforementioned works was carried out by way of direct administration (amana) and invoice based on instructions issued by the Minister of Public Works and Transport - at the time - however, the actual manner in which the work was carried out violates the concept of works by direct administration, which means the Administration itself undertaking the execution of the works, supervising their execution, and purchasing their materials in accordance with the ordinary rules, which renders the use by the Ministry of Public Works of the term works by direct administration legally misplaced and in violation of the provisions of the Public Accounting Law. And whereas it appeared that the Maintenance Department in the Ministry of Public Works and Transport, and other administrative units, exercised their duties in the procedures of this contract under the organizational Decree No. 11609 dated 7/11/62, and that those duties must be amended pursuant to Decree No. 13379 dated 5/11/98, which requires recommending to the Ministry of Public Works and Transport to work on applying the provisions of Decree No. 13379/98 referred to above. And whereas it appeared that the Maintenance Department, after contracting with the contractor who executed the road works, resorted to presenting his dues divided into invoices, from which it is understood that the expenditure was executed by way of invoice, and that the value of each single invoice thereof was below three million Lebanese Pounds, such that these invoices amounted to 68 invoices, however, this matter changes nothing of the reality because the contract was concluded by way of mutual agreement, and that the Directorate of Roads justified the division by the decision of the Minister of Public Works and Transport No. 312/99, which permitted the division of amounts pertaining to several budget lines, including the appropriation of main roads to carry out urgent maintenance works on the public road network.

Whereas it has been established that the road subject to the investigation is not a main road and that the works carried out thereon relate to its rehabilitation, and not to its urgent maintenance, which renders the justifications of the said Administration in splitting this transaction misplaced, thereby requiring that a request be made to the Ministry of Public Works and Transport to observe the provisions of Article 123 of the Public Accounting Law when splitting expenditures. Whereas it has been established that the Head of....... in the Ministry of Public Works and Transport, Mr......, concluded the transaction relating to the Abdeh - Berkayel - Fnaidek - Qammoua road by mutual agreement, distributed the entitlements of the contractor within invoices, and referred them to the Accounting Service to be liquidated on the basis that the contracting was carried out by way of invoice, and also issued nine letters without number or date containing orders to commence work without registering these letters in the registers of the Service, in addition to his issuing sixty-eight letters without number and without date relating to the execution of works and the purchase of materials pertaining to the five sections of which delivery was taken. Whereas it has been established that....... Mr...... - at the time - in the Ministry of Public Works and Transport, split the project of the single road into nine sections and drew up an estimated statement for each section containing the specification of the nature of the required works, their quantities and their cost, and considered that the works were executed under direct administration and by invoice whereas they were carried out by mutual agreement, knowing that it ought to have been concluded by way of public tender. Whereas that which Mr...... - in the Ministry of Public Works and Transport committed constitutes a breach of his official duties pursuant to the provisions of Article 14 of the provisions of the Civil Servants Regulations, which entails disciplinary liability on his part in this regard, and also constitutes a financial infringement and requires his referral before the Court of Audit pursuant to the provisions of the law organising it issued by Legislative Decree No. 82/83 And whereas that which Mr....... - committed constitutes a disciplinary and financial infringement, thereby requiring his referral before the Court of Audit pursuant to the provisions of the law organising it, and the closing of his disciplinary liability due to the termination of his services upon his reaching the legal age. Whereas nothing has been established from the record of interrogation of Mr....... and from his written defence that would exempt him from disciplinary liability, thereby requiring that the appropriate disciplinary measures be taken against him pursuant to the provisions of Articles 54 and 55 of the provisions of Legislative Decree No. 112 dated 12/6/59 and its amendments. Whereas it has been established as a result of the investigation that the contractor for the execution of the works of the Abdeh - Berkayel - Fnaidek - Qammoua - road is the...... Establishment for Trade and Contracting, and that he is the same contractor who carried out the execution of the works, and that the directorates of Public Works and Transport had not previously known or dealt with the persons in whose names the invoices of the works were issued, thereby requiring that the....... Establishment for Trade and Contracting be considered the rightful claimant by law in respect of the consideration for the execution of the said works, and consequently notifying the Ministry of Finance thereof to take the necessary legal measures in this regard.

After deliberation, and in light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided 1 - To deduct the salary of the Engineer - Head of....... - at the Ministry of Public Works and Transport - Mr....... (his financial number......) for fifteen days as a disciplinary measure. 2 - To refer Messrs....... before the Court of Accounts. 3 - To recommend to the Ministry of Public Works and Transport - the Directorate General of Roads and Buildings: - To apply the provisions of the Public Accounting Law promulgated by Decree No. 14969/63 and its amendments when carrying out the execution of public works contracts, and not to apply the decisions issued by it relating to the purchase of supplies and services by way of invoice for their violation of the provisions of the Public Accounting Law. - To apply the provisions of Regulatory Decree No. 13379 dated 5/ 11/98 relating to the determination of the tasks of the administrative units in the Directorate General of Roads and Buildings and the Regional Directorates. A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the fifteenth of the month of January in the year two thousand and three.

Secretariat of the Board Session: 4/2003 Item: 8 Decision No. 55/2003 The Central Inspection Board, Having perused the file of the case registered under No. 55/7B/ 2002 in all its contents. Having perused the report of the Financial Inspector, Mr. Jamil Doueik, dated 30/11/2002, resulting from the inspection of the Ministry of Public Works and Transport - Directorate General of Roads and Buildings. Having perused the two opinions of the Financial Inspector General dated 10/ 12/2002 and 16/12/2002 Having perused the opinion of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Accounts No. 472/4043 dated 24/12/2002 Having perused the opinion of the President of the Central Inspection dated 7/ 1/2003 Whereas it appeared from the documents of the file that an inspection was conducted of the Directorate General of Roads and Buildings at the Ministry of Public Works and Transport by the Financial Inspectorate General, and that the mission covered reviewing the existing relationship between the administrative units in the Accounting Department, and the methods adopted by the Ministry to execute paving and asphalting works, and industrial works in all Lebanese regions, on the basis of the annual Central Inspection programme for the year 2002 Whereas it appeared that the Head of...... at the Ministry of Public Works and Transport entrusted the task of delivering payment orders to Mr....... in the aforementioned Department, pursuant to the two memoranda issued by...... under No. 4/23 dated 16/4/1999, and No. 1 dated 6/3/ 2002, and that it appeared to the investigation that....... delivers some of those payment orders directly to the concerned parties contrary to the content of the two memoranda issued by him in this regard. Whereas it appeared that the texts pertaining to the Ministry of Public Works and Transport did not exclusively define the powers of the Presidency of the Accounting Department affiliated with the Ministry, nor did they define the powers of the Head of the Bureau and the Heads of the two Sections affiliated with it, which led to a conflict in the tasks undertaken to be completed by the aforementioned units, which requires recommending working towards issuing the decisions whereby the tasks that must be performed by each employee of the Accounting Department, including......, are defined, after seeking the opinion of the Central Inspection Administration, and communicating these decisions to the Civil Service Board, in accordance with the provisions of the second paragraph of Article Four of Legislative Decree No. 111/59 dated 12/6/1959 Whereas it appeared that there were issued by the Council of Ministers Decisions No. 30 dated 26/4/2000 and No. 27 dated 25/10/2001, whereby the Ministry of Public Works and Transport was authorised to award works on an on-call basis, after the aforementioned Ministry requested, pursuant to its two letters No. 65/S dated 20/3/2000 and No. 87 /S dated 7/4/2000, approval to award works on an on-call basis by way of mutual agreement after conducting a price inquiry and outside the general programme of tenders, justifying this by the exceptional circumstances under which it sometimes operates, and to confront urgent emergency cases that are impossible to deal with by ordinary methods, and therefore require taking exceptional measures to confront them. Whereas it appeared that the Ministry of Public Works and Transport went too far in adopting "on-call" awards until such awards became the principle and public tendering the exception, with the violation of the provisions of the laws and regulations in force that this entails, with respect to the lack of the element of full competition in the contracts concluded by way of "on-call" such that those contracts have become, and for several years, restricted to /58/ contractors, given that the conditions imposed in their special book of conditions stipulate specifications restricted to the contractors who undertake them, in addition to the lack of accuracy that accompanies the awarding process and resulting from the lack of prior determination of the works and services intended to be executed.

Whereas it was established that the Ministry of Public Works and Transport adopts the method of "direct execution and invoice" in a single contract awards process despite the independence of the nature, concept, and conditions of each of these two methods as well as the specific legal cases relating thereto in accordance with the provisions of the Public Accounting Law, and that the adoption of the said method, although it leads to expediting the completion of transactions and the execution of works due to the abridgement of public tender procedures, deprives the administration of the percentage discount based on the estimated statement, deprives the Treasury of the fiscal stamp duty payable on contracts in general, and leads to the fragmentation of expenditure and the overwhelming of the administration with numerous documents and transactions that are difficult to study, audit, and complete on time, in addition to the fact that it excludes the element of competition among contractors who could submit prices lower than the prices specified in the tariffs issued by the administration or any recognized international body, and places the contracting process outside the scope of oversight, which prevents the control of matters and the preservation and protection of public funds. Whereas it was established that the Financial Inspector General presented the observations of the Central Inspection at the meeting convened by the Minister of Finance on 3/12/2002 regarding the expenditures of works executed in the Ministry of Public Works and Transport, and the accompanying shortcoming in establishing prior plans and programmes for anticipated works, the absence of appropriation allocations in the budget, the inclusion of works of a structural nature within an on-demand contract, the adoption of the "direct execution and invoice" method contrary to the law, the fragmentation of expenditure and the resulting decline in the technical standard of the works, the deficiency in the contracting files, the absence of oversight, the burdening of the administration with thousands of transactions, and the provision of conditions conducive to causing damage to public funds, and that the Minister of Public Works and Transport, who attended the said meeting, expressed his understanding of the aforementioned observations as well as his readiness to proceed with possible measures to make the work of the Ministry more consistent with the laws, and also affirmed his endeavour, in another meeting held on 9/12/2002, to take into account the observations of the Inspection when preparing for the works of the coming year, and to abide by the rules stipulated in the Public Accounting Law. Whereas it was established that the Central Inspection Board had previously taken Decision No. 480/2002 dated 16/11/2002, regarding the ongoing on-demand contracts in the Ministry of Public Works and Transport, whereby it communicated to the said Ministry a copy of the Inspection report and recommended that it act upon the recommendations contained therein to address the loopholes resulting from the execution of on-demand works, and direct execution and invoice, which are contracted in the Ministry of Public Works and Transport without determining priority in execution, without relying on engineering data, and in accordance with studies characterized by after accuracy, and which are supervised by resorting to private offices despite the presence of employees possessing the competence to perform this work, which requires confirming this decision. Whereas it was established that there is a delay in issuing decisions to carry over appropriations for committed expenditures or those that the administration was unable to commit against the budget of the current fiscal year, which leads to a delay in completing liquidation transactions and their accumulation as well as a delay in executing the works relating thereto until the last months of the year, which requires recommending working on increasing the number of employees in charge of preparing and completing decisions to carry over committed or uncommitted appropriations at the Ministry of Finance, particularly in the Directorates of Budget and Expenditure Commitment Control, the Directorate of Disbursements, and the accountants of the competent administration, in order to be able to expedite the completion of liquidation transactions.

Whereas it has appeared that the number of committees for the acceptance of road and building contracts at the Ministry of Public Works and Transport, formed pursuant to Decision No. 233/A.T.M dated 26/9/2000, as amended by Decision No. 248 /A.T.M dated 5/9/2001, has reached twenty-seven committees, and that there is a necessity to work towards increasing the number of the said committees so that each one of them is entrusted with the acceptance of the works of a single Caza and not the works of four Cazas as is the case at the present time, which requires recommending the increase of the number of the aforementioned committees within the available human capabilities, and examining, annually, the possibility of renewing their members. And after deliberation, and in the light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided 1 - To confirm its Decision No. 480/2002 dated 16/11/2002 2 - To recommend to the Ministry of Public Works and Transport - the Directorate General of Roads and Buildings - the following: a - Restricting recourse to "on demand" contract awards to emergency cases whose condition requires hastening their execution due to their connection with public safety. b - Examining the establishment of a prior programme for the necessary works on roads and highways, provided that it is placed under contract award through the Administration of Tenders or the competent administration in accordance with the Public Accounting Law, and provided that priority is given to contract awarding by means of public tenders. c - Adopting either the invoice method in accordance with the provisions of Article 151 of the Public Accounting Law, or the method of works by direct execution (amana) in accordance with the provisions of Article 152 of the aforementioned Law, and not both methods together in a single contract award. d - Increasing the number of acceptance committees within the available human capabilities, and examining the possibility of renewing the members of the said committees every year. e - Procuring the issuance of decisions whereby the duties that must be performed by each employee of the Service of........ including...... are determined, after seeking the opinion of the Central Inspection Administration, provided that these decisions are notified to the Civil Service Board in accordance with the provisions of the fourth Article of Legislative Decree No. 111/59 and its amendments. 3 - To recommend to the Ministry of Finance - the Directorate of Public Finance - the following: a - Delivering payment orders through the delegate of the concerned ministry and not directly to the concerned parties. b - Not delaying the issuance of decisions for carrying over appropriations. A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the twenty-ninth of the month of January of the year two thousand and three.

Secretariat of the Board Session: 42/2003 Item: 3 Decision No. 472/2003 The Central Inspection Board, having reviewed the file of the case registered under No.

55/3B/2002 in all its contents.

2115/2003 Having reviewed the report of the Administrative Inspector Mr. Mahmoud Kahil dated 13/10/2003, following the investigation into certain administrations and public institutions carrying out excavation works on public roads contrary to the laws and regulations in force. Having reviewed the report of the Engineering Inspectors Mr. Jalal Suleiman and Ms. Maha Al-Daqqaq dated 31/10/2003 Having reviewed the report of the Engineering Inspectors Messrs.: Youssef Ibrahim, Ahmad Al-Hajjar, Issam Shabani, Dr. Anis Qattan, and Dr. Bashir Fawwaz. Dated 10/11/2003 Having reviewed the opinion of the Administrative Inspector General dated 28/ 10/2003 Having reviewed the opinion of the Engineering Inspector General dated 17/ 11/2003 Having reviewed the two opinions of the President of the Central Inspection dated 5 /11/2003 and dated 18/11/2003 And whereas it appeared from the documents of the file that...... lodged with the Central Inspection, pursuant to its letter No. 268/S.T.M dated 22/7/ 2003, a detailed report containing the places and roads on which works were executed in the South region without coordination with the competent authorities, contrary to the law, pointing to similar cases recurring across all Lebanese regions, which inflicts waste on public funds and constitutes a danger to public safety, and that both the Engineering General Inspectorate and the Administrative General Inspectorate prepared a report on the subject based on Referral No. 2115/2003 issued by the Presidency of the Central Inspection on 31/7/2003 And whereas it appeared from reviewing certain files of works contracting in the Regional Directorate General of Public Works in the South, that a number of contracting companies obtained the necessary licences to carry out excavation works on public roads from the competent authorities, whereas there are other companies executing such works without observing the procedures required to be followed in this regard. And whereas it appeared that the private contracting companies that executed excavations on public roads in the district of Marjayoun subsequently removed the damage from those roads, where the excavations were paved and the state of the roads was restored to what it was previously. And whereas excavation works for laying public utility lines in roads and their clearances were regulated pursuant to Legislative Decree No. 68 dated 9/9/1983, the provisions of which prohibited carrying out excavation works within the expropriation limits of roads for laying public utility lines of various kinds, or reinforcing or maintaining them, unless the licence to excavate is issued by...... with respect to classified roads whose affairs are overseen by the Ministry of Public Works and Transport, and by the competent....... with respect to internal roads located within its scope, under conditions enumerated in the course of the text of the fifth Article of the aforementioned Legislative Decree.

Whereas it has appeared that His Excellency the President of the Council of Ministers had previously issued circulars to all public administrations, public institutions, and municipalities, bearing the following numbers and dates: 6/95 dated 12/3/1995, 16/98 dated 8/8/1998, 48/99 dated 15/10/1999, relating to the granting of permits or the carrying out of excavations on public roads, and affirming the procedures that must be followed when executing excavation projects on public and internal roads, after it appeared that some of those administrations still resort to excavating public roads to lay water pipes, sanitary sewers, or electrical or telephone cables and others without a prior permit from the authorities specified in the legislative decree set forth above and without complying with the provisions thereof, which consequently requires recommending that the administrations concerned abide by the provisions of the aforementioned circulars when executing excavation projects on public roads, in such a manner as to lead to coordination among these administrations and to avoid duplication in execution and waste of public funds. Whereas it has appeared that the specifications relating to excavation, backfilling, paving, and asphalting works contained in the permits issued by the Ministry of Public Works and Transport and contained in the Implementing Decree No. 13495/98 differ from the specifications contained in the contracting agreements in the other administrations, which consequently requires requesting the Office of the Presidency of the Council of Ministers to ask the Lebanese Standards Institution (........ to work on unifying the technical specifications for the special books of conditions and contracts relating to the construction and maintenance of roads in all State administrations. Whereas it has appeared that the permits for excavating public roads issued by....... in the Ministry of Public Works and Transport, are circulated to the maintenance departments affiliated with the Regional Directorates of Public Works in the governorates without the knowledge of the execution departments therein, which leads to the occurrence of a conflict between the works of these departments and the works of the other administrations, and calls for recommending that action be taken to notify a copy of the permits issued by the Ministry of Public Works and Transport to the execution departments in the Regional Directorates of Public Works in addition to the maintenance departments therein, as well as to the Central Inspection Administration - the General Engineering Inspectorate - for the purpose of follow-up.

Following deliberation, and in the light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided 1 - To request the Office of the Presidency of the Council of Ministers to call upon the Lebanese Standards Institution....... to work on standardising the technical specifications of the special books of conditions and contracts relating to the construction and maintenance of roads across all administrations of the State. 2 - To recommend to the following Ministries: the Interior and Municipalities, Telecommunications, Energy and Water, Public Works and Transport, each within its respective competence, to call upon the administrations subordinate to them and those subject to their tutelage, the municipalities, and the unions of municipalities to comply with the provisions of Circulars Nos.: 6/95, 16/98, and 48/99, issued by the Presidency of the Council of Ministers, relating to the granting of licences or the carrying out of excavations on public roads, and confirming the procedures that must be followed when executing excavation projects on public and internal roads. 3 - To recommend to the Ministry of Public Works and Transport, to work on notifying a copy of the licences issued by it to each of the execution departments and maintenance departments in the Regional Directorates of Public Works in the governorates, in addition to the Central Inspection Administration - the General Engineering Inspectorate. 4 - To close the case with respect to the other points. A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the nineteenth of the month of November of the year two thousand and three.

Secretariat of the Board Session: 1/2003 Item: 1 Decision No. 1/2003 The Central Inspection Board, Having examined the file of the case registered under No. 23/3/2002 in all its contents. Having examined the report of the Administrative Inspector Mr. Mahmoud Abboud dated 15/10/2002, regarding the act of a female teacher in falsifying the date of birth of her daughter in order to benefit from the education grant payable in respect of her, contrary to the rules. Having examined the opinion of the Administrative Inspector General dated 29/ 11/2002 Having examined the opinion of the President of the Central Inspection dated 10 /12/2002 Whereas it has been established that the Director General of the Civil Servants Cooperative, pursuant to his letter No. 991/S 1 dated 10/5/2002, referred to the Central Inspection the file pertaining to the female teacher on the establishment of the Ministry of Education and Higher Education, Mrs. ......., relating to the application for her to benefit from an education grant for the 2000 - 2001 academic year in respect of her daughter, and Assignment No. 23/3/2002 was issued to investigate the matter. Whereas it has been established from the investigation that the female teacher on the establishment of the Ministry of Education and Higher Education, Directorate General of Education, ...... Public School, Mrs. ......, falsified the date of birth of her daughter called "......." by making it 18/6/76 instead of 18/6/75, in the contents of the application which she submitted with its attachments to the Civil Servants Cooperative to obtain an education grant in respect of her daughter for the 2000 - 2001 academic year, with the aim of benefiting from an education grant in respect of her said daughter for the last time, as she had reached the age of twenty-five, the maximum limit permitted for a civil servant to benefit from an education grant in respect of his children pursuant to the provisions of Article Three of the Education Grants Regulations adopted by the Civil Servants Cooperative, thereby violating the provisions of the said Regulations and the provisions of Article 14 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 and its amendments (Civil Servants Regulations), which entails disciplinary liability on her part. Whereas it has been established that Mrs. ........ submitted to the Civil Servants Cooperative an application for an education grant in respect of her youngest daughter called "......" pertaining to the 99 - 2000 academic year, despite the fact that her daughter was married during the said year, and consequently an application for an education grant cannot be submitted in respect of her on the basis of the Education Grants Regulations adopted by the Cooperative, thereby violating the provisions of the said Regulations and the provisions of Article 14 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 and its amendments (Civil Servants Regulations), which entails disciplinary liability on her part. Whereas the application for the education grant referred to above resulted in the disbursement of an amount of 750000 L.L. in favour of Mrs. ......., which requires recommending to the Civil Servants Cooperative to work on recovering the value of the said grant as it was paid without right.

Whereas nothing was revealed in the record of the interrogation of Mrs. ......., or in her written defence, that would exempt her from liability, which consequently requires taking the appropriate disciplinary measures against her pursuant to the provisions of Articles 54 and 55 of Legislative Decree No. 112 /59 and its amendments (Civil Servants Regulations). And after deliberation, and in the light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided: 1 - To delay the advancement in step of the teacher in the cadre of the Ministry of Education and Higher Education, Directorate General of Education, Mrs. ......... (her financial number .........) for a period of twelve months as a disciplinary measure. 2 - To recommend to the Directorate General of the Civil Servants Cooperative to act to recover the value of the education grant given to Mrs. ........ in respect of her married daughter in accordance with what has been set out in the body of this decision. A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the eighth of the month of January of the year two thousand and three.

Whereas it has been established that the salary of the employee......... was frozen on 21/11/2001, and that he was suspended from work and referred to the Disciplinary Board at the Ogero Authority, and that the Board of Directors of the said Authority decided on 13/12/2001 to defer the acceptance of the resignation of the said employee after the latter had submitted it on 24/11/2001, which requires recommending taking action to revoke Decision No. 877/97 dated 19/12/1997 with respect to the employment of Mr......... in the establishment of the Ogero Authority, to cease the liquidation and disbursement of any salary or compensation to him, and to draw the financial consequences resulting from the revocation of the decision appointing him. Whereas the Board of Directors of the Ogero Authority, composed at the time of Engineer......... and of each of Messrs.:........, proceeded to appoint Mr.......... on the basis of a certificate issued by a foreign institute the invalidity of which was established on a date subsequent to the date of appointment without the competent committee having had the opportunity to rule on its equivalence, which enabled Mr.......... to receive salaries and compensations on the basis of an appointment contrary to the law, a matter which entails for the gentlemen mentioned above disciplinary and financial liability for their violation of the duties of office and their causing damage to public funds. Whereas the......... of the Ogero Authority referred to above had their services terminated on 28/12/99 and consequently fell outside the scope of disciplinary accountability, yet their financial liability remains standing pursuant to the provisions of Article 65 of Legislative Decree No. 82/83, which requires referring them before the Court of Accounts pursuant to the provisions of Articles 60 and 61 of the Law organising it. Whereas the receipt by Mr.......... of salaries and compensations from the Ogero Authority in the manner described above constitutes a violation of the texts relating to the use of public funds, which is the violation provided for in Article 60 of the Law organising the Court of Accounts, and whereas Article 59 of Legislative Decree No. 82/ 83 vested in the Court of Accounts the oversight over the acts of anyone who manages or uses public funds, which requires referring Mr.......... before the Court of Accounts pursuant to the provisions of Articles 59, 60 and 61 of the Law organising it. Whereas it has been established that the doctorate certificate which Mr.......... claimed to have obtained from the IFAD Institute in France was considered by the Equivalence Committee at the Ministry of Education and Higher Education as a doctorate in itself after the said Committee had been misled by the documents submitted by Mr.......... bearing stamps other than the stamps with which the certificates are required to be affixed, and that the Equivalence Committee annulled its decision granting the equivalence after having ascertained the invalidity of the documents, which requires recommending the use of more accurate means by the Committee referred to in its correspondence with foreign universities and the verification of certificates and documents prior to its granting the equivalences requested of it. Whereas it has been established that the Ministry of Education and Higher Education has recently proceeded to draw up a special guide to the universities operating in Lebanon, both public and private, and to the certificates awarded by each of these universities, and that circulating the said guide on the Internet and requesting friendly States to place a similar guide within the framework of cultural exchange on the same network would preclude any similar attempt at fraud in the future. Whereas it has been established that the Minister of Education and Higher Education deposited with the Cassation Public Prosecution, pursuant to his Letter No. 729/2001 dated 4/12/2001, the entire file relating to the forgery of the doctorate certificate which Mr.......... claimed to have obtained, in order to take the appropriate decision in respect thereof, which requires depositing a copy of the investigation file with the Cassation Public Prosecution with reference to the investigations ongoing before it on the subject.

Secretariat of the Board Session: 6/2003 Item: 8 Decision No. 89/2003 The Central Inspection Board, after reviewing the file of the case registered under No. 1/7/2002 with all its contents.

120/M 2002 After reviewing the report of the Financial Inspector Mrs. Sanaa Younes dated 11/1/2003, concerning the employment status of Mr. ......... at the Ogero Authority. After reviewing the opinion of the Financial Inspector General dated 13/1/ 2003 After reviewing the opinion of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Accounts No. 28/275 dated 22/1/2003 After reviewing the opinion of the President of the Central Inspection dated 30 /1/2003 Whereas it appeared from the documents of the file that the Minister of Telecommunications referred to the Central Inspection, pursuant to his letter No. 3637/1/M dated 10/1/2002, the file of ........ at the Ogero Authority, Mr. ........ known as ........ regarding his act of forging the Doctorate degree in Commercial Sciences/ Telecommunications, requesting that the necessary measures be taken, and Assignment No. 1/7/ 2002 was issued to investigate the matter. Whereas it appeared from the investigation that Mr. ....... was appointed at the Ogero Authority in the eighth grade of the second category on 3/11/97 as a sales representative for insurance and shipping companies, pursuant to a decision issued by the Board of Directors of the aforementioned Authority based on a Master's degree in Management and International Trade submitted by the concerned party as being issued by IFAD University in France, without the issuance of any decision by the Equivalence Committee at the Ministry of Education and Higher Education deciding on the equivalence of the Master's degree referred to above to any Lebanese government degree, in fulfillment of the text of the first Article of Decree No. 9355 dated 28/4/62 (Regulations of the Equivalence Committee and the general rules to be observed for granting equivalences). Whereas it appeared that Mr. ........ requested, on 26/5/99, the competent authorities at the Ministry of Telecommunications to correct his category, considering that the Master's degree he held entitled him to move to a category higher than the category in which he was appointed, and he also requested on 20/10/2001, that action be taken to correct his employment status with respect to promoting him to the tenth category after obtaining a Doctorate in Commercial Sciences/ Telecommunications, which he obtained from the IFAD Institute in France. Whereas it appeared from the correspondence conducted with the IFAD Institute through the Lebanese Embassy in Paris that both the Master's degree on the basis of which Mr. ........ was employed, and the Doctorate degree in Commercial Sciences on the basis of which he requested his promotion, are forged degrees and were not issued by the aforementioned Institute. Whereas the employment of Mr. ........., based on a forged degree, lacks a legal basis, and is considered non-existent and cannot establish a right for the concerned party due to the inadmissibility of anyone benefiting from a fraud he committed, and that it is for the Administration to withdraw the appointment of Mr. ......... in every goodness and the latter cannot invoke acquired rights or the statute of limitations, as there is no room to apply the jurisprudence relating to the withdrawal of unlawful administrative decisions that confer rights and which can only be revoked within the time limit for appeal.

Following deliberation, and in the light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided: 1 - To lodge a copy of the investigation file with the Public Prosecution Office at the Court of Cassation further to the investigations under way before it regarding the matter. 2 - To recommend to the Ogero Authority that it act to revoke the decision appointing the employee on the establishment of the said Authority, Mr. ........., and to draw the financial consequences resulting from the revocation of the decision of his appointment. 3 - To refer each of the former ......... of the Ogero Authority, the engineer, and Messrs.: ........., and the employee at the said Authority, Mr. ........., before the Court of Audit. 4 - To recommend to the Ministry of Education and Higher Education the following: a - To circulate the directory of public and private universities in Lebanon on the Internet, and to request friendly States to place similar directories on the same network, or to supply the Directorate General of Higher Education with similar university directories. b - To request the Equivalence Committee to use more accurate means in its correspondence with foreign universities and in verifying the certificates and documents attached to applications for the granting of equivalences, and not to accept certified true copies of certificates except where the original certificate authenticated directly by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the country that granted it is present, without relying on any other local authentication. A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the nineteenth of the month of February in the year two thousand and three.

Secretariat of the Board Session: 11/2003 Item: 7 Decision No. 139/2003 The Central Inspection Board, Having perused the file of the case registered under No. 13/4/2002 with all its contents.

2331/W 2002 Having perused the report of the Engineering Inspectors Mrs. Hoda Salloum and Mr. Hussein Yahya dated 30/12/2002, as a result of the investigation conducted into the alteration of the technical inspection report pertaining to the building on Property No. 200/ Bkennaya. Secretariat of the Board Session: 41/2003 Item: 5 Decision No. 467/2003 The Central Inspection Board, having reviewed the file of the case registered under No. 2/5 B 2/2003 in its entirety.

3066/W 2003 Having reviewed the report of the educational inspectors Ms. Rita Semaan and Mr. Samir Murad dated 5/7/2003, concerning the violations attributed to.......... of.......... Public School, Ms........... Having reviewed the opinion of the Educational Inspector General dated 29/7 /2003 Having reviewed the opinion of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Audit No. 489/2823 dated 20/10/2003 Having reviewed the opinion of the President of the Central Inspection dated 4/ 11/2003 Whereas it appears from the documents of the file that a complaint was received by the Central Inspection indicating violations attributed to..........,.........., which was investigated within the framework of the annual inspection programme for the year 2003 of the Educational General Inspectorate. Whereas it appears that.......... Public,.........., neglected to organise and supervise the daily attendance register of the school's employees, and to abide by the obligations of official working hours with respect to failing to sign at the time of arrival and departure and with respect to leaving blank fields in the body of the register, and did not organise the weekly work distribution schedules for the supervisors and substitute teachers, in addition to contracting with teachers before completing the teaching quotas of permanent staff teachers, and assigning degree holders who underwent training courses to perform administrative work, and also omitted to obtain the signatures of the members of the teaching staff on the register of the minutes of the teachers' council, and proceeded on various occasions to direct foul words and expressions rejected by upbringing and morals at some members of the teaching staff and pupils, thereby violating the provisions of Articles 17, 18, 23, 34 and 64 of Decision No. 1130/M/2001 (Internal Regulations of Public Kindergartens and Basic Education Schools). Secretariat of the Board Session: 14/2003 Item: 14 Decision No. 184/2003 The Central Inspection Board, Having perused the file of the case registered under No. 2192/W 2002 with all its contents.

336/S 4/2002 Having perused the report of the two Engineering Inspectors, Ms. Hoda Salloum and Mr. Hussein Yahya, dated 30/12/2002 and 20/3/2003, resulting from the investigation into the alteration of the technical inspection report and the occupancy permit pertaining to Property No. 943/ Jal El Dib real estate area. Secretariat of the Board Session: 6/2003 Item: 11 Decision No. 92/2003 The Central Inspection Board, Having examined the file of the case registered under No. 13/4/2001 with all its contents.

2461/W2001 Having examined the report of the Engineering Inspector, Mr. Oussama Al-Chidiac, dated 31/10/2002, resulting from the investigation into the subdivision of Property No. 579/ Assoun in a manner contrary to reality. Whereas it appeared that Parcel No. 1185, resulting from the subdivision project referred to above, and which separates Parcel No. 579 from the rest of the sections resulting from the subdivision, was allocated as a road for the project, and was also annexed to the public domain as it is affected by the alignment approved by Decree No. 4135/66 dated 25/3/1966 Whereas it appeared that the owner of Parcel No. 579 erected three buildings on the said parcel, and carried out a settlement for them in the year 1981, and that the civil engineer.......... is the one who completed the settlement file based on the measurements, dimensions, and areas that he took upon his own responsibility without attaching any map of the constructions existing on the property at the time, and the owner also, in the year 1985, subdivided Parcel No. 579, where the construction and subdivision works were executed pursuant to Assignment No. 655/85 by the surveyor in the Survey Department in Tripoli, Mr........... Whereas it appeared that the General Engineering Inspectorate conducted a physical inspection of the site of the property in the presence of one of the surveyors working in the Survey Department in the North, as a result of which it drew up a map of the reality of the constructions existing thereon, through which it appeared that there are large discrepancies in the status of the constructions between the map referred to on the one hand, and each of the map drawn up by Mr........... and the file of the settlement that took place in the year 1981 on the other hand, as the map drawn up by the General Engineering Inspectorate and the Survey Department in the North showed that parts of the buildings existing on the property under No. 579/ Assoun fall within Road No. 1185, which was annexed to the public domain, and within Property No. 1187 subdivided from the original Property No. 579

And whereas the surveyor at the Cadastral Department in Tripoli, Mr. .........., by drawing up a plan of the constructions standing on Property No. 579/Assoun contrary to reality, has violated the construction laws and regulations and the duties of office provided for in Article 14 of the Civil Servants Regulations, which entails disciplinary liability on his part in this regard, and whereas what he invoked in the minutes of his interrogation regarding his being prevented from continuing his work by unknown persons and his drawing up, as a result thereof, a plan of the constructions in his office without submitting it to his immediate superior or informing him of what happened, cannot be taken into consideration to justify the violation committed by him and consequently exempt him from liability, which requires taking the appropriate disciplinary measures against him pursuant to the provisions of Articles 54 and 55 of Legislative Decree No. 112 /59 and its amendments, (the Civil Servants Regulations). And whereas it is required to recommend to the Ministry of Public Works and Transport to request the Order of Engineers in the North to investigate the civil engineer Mr. .......... (his registration number in the Order ..........), for his issuing a certificate contrary to reality which led to the occurrence of an illegal subdivision and an encroachment upon the public road, as well as to recommend to the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities to request the Municipality of Assoun to work on determining the extent of the encroachment upon the public road and taking the legal measures conducive to removing it, and placing an annotation of an offending building on the real property folio pertaining to Property No. 579/Assoun until the removal of the violation. And after deliberation, and in the light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided: 1 - To delay the advancement in grade of the surveyor at the Cadastral Department in Tripoli, Mr. .......... (his financial number ..........) for a period of twelve months by way of discipline. 2 - To recommend to the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities to request from the Municipality of Assoun: a - To work on determining the extent of the encroachment occurring upon Public Road No. 1185/Assoun and taking the legal measures conducive to removing it. b - To work on placing an annotation of an offending building on the real property folio pertaining to Property No. 579/Assoun. 3 - To recommend to the Ministry of Public Works and Transport to request from the Order of Engineers in the North to investigate the engineer (his registration number in the Order ..........), for the reasons set forth in the body of this decision. A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the nineteenth of the month of February in the year two thousand and three.

Whereas it was established, on the other hand, that the owner of property No. 1986/ Qab Elias proceeded to construct a second floor above the building standing on his property without obtaining a permit therefor from the competent authorities, and that an annotation of an offending building was placed on the real property folio pertaining to the aforementioned property. Mr. .........., for the reasons set forth in the body of this decision. 2 - Pursuing the suspension of construction works on the properties bearing Nos. 1985 - 1986 - 1987/ .......... real estate area, and maintaining the annotation of an offending building, which was placed on the real property folios pertaining to those properties, until their owners regularise their status in accordance with the rules. 476/S 4/2002 Having reviewed the report of the Engineering Inspector, Mr. Bassam Al-Jadoua, dated 21/1/2003, following the investigation into the encroachment occurring on Property No. 1986/ Qab Elias Cadastral Area.
