Secretariat of the Board Session: 17/2003 Item: 6 Decision No. 216/2003 The Central Inspection Board, having reviewed the file of the case registered under No. 10/4/2002 with all its contents.

358/S 4/2002

2419/W 2002 Having reviewed the report of the Engineering Inspectors, Messrs. Hussein Yehia, Jalal Suleiman, and Amal Shamseddine, dated 2/1/2003, resulting from the investigation into technical violations occurring in the permits granted for construction on real properties in the Hadath area. Having reviewed the opinion of the Engineering Inspector General dated 25/3 /2003 Having reviewed the opinion of the President of the Central Inspection dated 14 /4/2003 Whereas it appeared from the documents of the file that there are numerous technical errors in the permits granted for construction on the real properties bearing the numbers: 233, 4338, 4339, 4340, 4341/ Hadath cadastral area, and Assignment No. 10/4/2002 was issued to investigate the matter. Whereas it appeared from the investigation that the real properties referred to above, belonging to a single owner, were classified within the zoning area 1, 1B, in which the surface exploitation ratio is 30% and the general exploitation ratio is 65,1 and that the owner obtained permits for construction thereon on 8/9/2000 and 9/9/2000 based on technical inspection reports issued by the Urban Planning Department in Mount Lebanon. Whereas it appeared that the technical approval relating to the permit for construction on the real properties referred to above was granted despite the existence of vast discrepancies in the surface areas between what is stated in the surface area verification schedule and what is stated on the covers of the permits, and the non-conformity of the surface area stated in each of the schedules and the covers with the surface area noted in the permit plans, in addition to the manipulation contained in those plans in the measurements of the buildings with respect to reducing them in a manner consistent with the setbacks and exploitation ratios, and enlarging the shapes of the real properties to reach the same end. Whereas it appeared that.......... in the Urban Planning Department in Mount Lebanon, Mr........... drew up the verification schedules of the surface areas intended to be built on the real properties that are the subject of this case, despite their contradiction with the permit plans attached thereto, without requesting their correction or amendment, or informing his immediate superior of this matter, and he also recorded the surface exploitation factor on those schedules as being 50%, instead of 30%, which is the applicable ratio in accordance with the zoning area within the scope of which the permitted real properties are located, in addition to his endorsement of all the violating permit plans, and the failure to indicate the contradiction occurring between the construction permits and the buildings executed on the ground, and what that entailed by way of omission to mention the true executed surface areas, thereby violating the provisions of Article Two of Decree No. 9365 dated 25/10/74, which obliges.......... to draw up technical inspection reports on the violations committed in buildings and to determine the extent of their violation of the laws in force and to refer them to the competent authorities to take the appropriate action in their regard, and the provisions of Article 14 of the Civil Servants Regulations, which require the civil servant in general to be guided by the public interest alone in his work, and to ensure the application of the laws and regulations in force without any transgression, violation or negligence, a matter which entails disciplinary liability on his part for which he must be prosecuted, and that what was stated in the minutes of his interrogation and in his written defence is not such as to exempt him from liability, which requires taking the appropriate disciplinary measures against him pursuant to the provisions of Articles 54 and 55 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 and its amendments (Civil Servants Regulations).

Whereas it was established that.......... at the Department of Urban Planning in Mount Lebanon, Mr..........., who was entrusted with auditing the transactions relating to technical inspections, signed the area schedules and all the licensed plans without paying attention to the manipulation occurring in the plans or noticing the error occurring in the surface exploitation factor entered on the area audit schedules, in addition to his approval of the conformity of the buildings under construction without conducting an inspection of the site of the properties, and that the aforementioned engineer has died, which requires disregarding his disciplinary liability for this reason. And whereas it was established that the engineer at the Directorate General of Urban Planning, Mr........... signed, while performing the duties of.......... at the Hazmieh branch between the date of 6/9/2000 and 9/9/2000, the permits granted for building on the properties that are the subject of this case, based on the signature of each of.......... and the engineer.........., without auditing the documents and plans pertaining to the properties referred to, or noticing the vast discrepancies between the areas being audited in the Department and those entered on the covers of the permits, and consequently verifying the conformity of the aforementioned permits with the law, particularly with regard to the exploitation factors adopted in the easement zone within the scope of which the properties fall, a matter which entails disciplinary liability on his part for violating the provisions of Article Eight of Legislative Decree No. 111/59, which requires.........., to ensure the proper performance by the employees subordinate to him of the duties entrusted to them, read in conjunction with Article 14 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 and its amendments with regard to breach of the duties of office. And whereas what was stated by Mr........... in the record of his interrogation, that no one drew his attention to the violations occurring in the documents, cannot be relied upon, especially since he is the employee who is presumed to know the elements of exploitation in the zone (ZONE) and the surface and total exploitation area permitted to be built on the properties, and although he was temporarily assigned to replace.......... in running the business of the technical office within the scope of which the transactions that are the subject of the case fall during the period of his administrative leave, he holds in an original capacity another.......... that performs the same duties entrusted to the technical office in which he was temporarily assigned to complete the transactions, and he undertakes the supervision of similar transactions on a daily basis, which requires taking the appropriate disciplinary measures against him pursuant to the provisions of Articles 54 and 55 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 and its amendments (the Civil Service Regulations). And whereas it was established that the properties that are the subject of this case were amalgamated with one another so that they came to constitute a single property bearing the number 233/ Al-Hadath, and the permits granted for building thereon included an increase in the surface and total exploitation factors the rate of which amounted to the following: - The approximate increase in surface exploitation before amalgamation: 800 square metres. - The approximate increase in total exploitation before amalgamation: 7298 square metres. - The approximate increase in surface exploitation after amalgamation: 730 square metres. - The approximate increase in total exploitation after amalgamation: 5689 square metres. And that the construction works were executed in accordance with the violating and certified plans, and the buildings were subdivided into different sections based on the provisions of Article Twenty-Six of Law No. 539/96 (establishing the Public Corporation for Housing), which permits the subdivision of a building before obtaining the occupancy permit.

C - Circulating to all departments and sections of the Directorate General of Urban Planning, the obligation to request a plan of a building under construction prior to approving the conformity of buildings to the subdivision carried out pursuant to Law No. 539/96 (Establishing the Public Corporation for Housing). D - Requesting the Order of Engineers in Beirut to conduct the necessary investigations with each of the two civil engineers: Mrs. .......... (her number in the Order /........../) and Mr. .......... (his number in the Order /........../) for the reasons set forth in the body of this decision, a decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the seventh of the month of May in the year two thousand and three.

Whereas it has been established that the Director General of Urban Planning requested the Central Inspection, pursuant to his referral No. 112/S dated 5/3/2003, to inquire about the possibility of granting the application of the concerned party aimed at issuing a habitation permit on Property No. 233/ Al-Hadath (after amalgamation), whereas deciding upon this matter rests with the Directorate General of Urban Planning itself, in light of the provisions of the laws and regulations in force, and in particular the provisions of the sixth Article of Legislative Decree No. 148/83 (Building Law). And whereas it has been established that the civil engineer, Mrs. .........., is the one who undertook on her responsibility the management of the work and the execution of the plans pertaining to the building on the properties that are the subject of this case, and is consequently deemed responsible for the manipulation that occurred in the contents of the plans and for the violations committed in the execution, and is also deemed responsible for failing to inform the competent authorities of the violations that occurred, upon withdrawing her undertaking and the replacement of her by the civil engineer Mr. .........., to follow up the execution works. And whereas it has been established that the civil engineer Mr. .........., failed in his turn to make the necessary modifications to the building works, which requires requesting the Order of Engineers in Beirut to conduct the necessary investigations with the two engineers, Mr. and Mrs. .......... for their violation of the rules relating to the practice of the engineering profession. And whereas it is required to recommend to the Directorate General of Urban Planning to assign the task of heading the Urban Planning Section during the absence of the titular head in one of the sections, to one of the engineers working in the said section, and to circulate to all departments and sections of the Directorate General the necessity of requesting a plan of a building under construction prior to approving the conformity of the buildings to the subdivision carried out pursuant to Law No. 539/ 96 (Establishment of the Public Corporation for Housing). And after deliberation, and in light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided 1 - To delay the advancement in step of .......... in the Urban Planning Section in Mount Lebanon, Mr. .......... (his financial number..........), for a period of twenty-four months as a disciplinary measure. 2 - To delay the advancement in step of the engineer in the Directorate General of Urban Planning, Mr. .......... (his financial number..........), for a period of four months as a disciplinary measure. 3 - To disregard the responsibility of the engineer.......... due to death. 4 - To recommend to the Ministry of Public Works and Transport - Directorate General of Urban Planning - the following: a - Taking the necessary legal measures regarding the issuance of the habitation permit on Property No. 233/ Al-Hadath in light of the provisions of the laws and regulations in force. b - Assigning the task of heading the Urban Planning Section, during the absence of the titular head in one of the sections, to one of the engineers working in the said section.

Whereas the responsibility for these violations falls upon .......... for his approval of plans not conforming to reality and for preparing and signing Technical Inspection Report No. 674/Construction contrary to the provisions of Legislative Decree No. 148/83 (the Construction Law), to the provisions of Implementing Decree No. 2791/92, to Decision of the Minister of Public Works and Transport No. 216/1 dated 24/7/1996, and to the provisions of Article 14 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 (the Civil Servants Regulations) for his failure to be guided by the public interest in his work and for his failure to apply the laws and regulations in force, in addition to each of the engineers .......... Urban Planning in Mount Lebanon at the time, Messrs. .........., and the services of each of Messrs. .......... were terminated outside the framework of disciplinary accountability, which requires filing the case with respect to them. Secretariat of the Board Session: 35/2003 Item: 10 Decision No. 411/2003 The Central Inspection Board, having reviewed the file of the case registered under No. 12/4/2002 with all its contents.

2250/M2002 Having reviewed the report of the two engineering inspectors, Mr. Hussein Yahya and Ms. Hoda Salloum, dated 4/11/2002 and 18/8/ 2003, as a result of the investigation into the violations committed in the permit granted for construction on plot No. 1830/ Deir El Zahrani. Inspectorate conducted an investigation into the matter pursuant to Special Assignment No. 12/ 4/2002 issued by the Presidency of the Central Inspection on 5/9/ 2002 Whereas it appeared from the basement floor holding an occupancy (habitation) permit despite the absence of such a permit in the registers and archives of the Technical Office in Nabatieh, and that Engineer.......... is the one Civil referred the file relating to the forgery committed in the construction permit on Property No. 1830/ Deir Al-Zahrani to the Governor of Nabatieh on 18/7/ 2002 to take the necessary legal action, and that the said file was lodged with the Appellate Public Prosecution in Nabatieh on 10/10/2002, in accordance with the referral of the Governor of Nabatieh in this regard. Secretariat of the Board Session: 41/2003 Item: 3 Decision No. 465/2003 The Central Inspection Board, having reviewed the file of the case registered under No. 1868 and 2107/2002 in all its contents.

Secretariat of the Board Session: 12/2003 Item: 14 Decision No. 155/2003 The Central Inspection Board, having perused the file of the case registered under No. 55/S 4/ 2003 with all its contents.

109/7/2003

292/2002 Having perused the report of the two Administrative Inspectors, Messrs. Rabih Al-Timani and Jeries Atmeh, the Engineering Inspector, Mr. Ahmad Al-Hajjar, and the Financial Inspector, Mr. Naji Shaaban, dated 3/2/ 2003, resulting from the application of the general inspection indicators and the standards of quality control and institutional performance in the Ministry of Public Works and Transport, Directorate General of Roads and Buildings. Having perused the opinion of the Financial Inspector General dated 10/2/ 2003 Having perused the opinion of the Administrative Inspector General dated 24/2 /2003 Having perused the opinion of the Engineering Inspector General dated 1/3/ 2003 Having perused the opinion of the President of the Central Inspection dated 6/ 3/2003 Whereas it has been established from the documents of the file that two working teams were formed from a number of inspectors working in the Central Inspection Administration, pursuant to Decision No. 151/M/2002, to which the mission of applying the general inspection indicators and the standards of quality control and performance was assigned on the basis of the letter of the Minister of State for Administrative Development Affairs No. 910/S/2002 dated 12/11/2002, and in accordance with the form attached thereto. Whereas it has been established that the mission assigned to the two aforementioned inspection teams is the first in the programme for the application of institutional performance evaluation for the sake thereof, and it placed the performance of the administration and those working therein under the microscope of oversight aimed at guidance and development, and generated a sense in the employee, regardless of his rank and position, that he has a role in the administrative process. Whereas it has been established that the mission of applying the general inspection indicators and the standards of quality control and institutional performance in the Directorate General of Roads and Buildings contributed to highlighting the points of weakness and the points of strength in the said administration, a matter which enables those in charge of this administration, in the future, to support the points of strength and work on reinforcing and increasing them, and to attend, as well, to addressing the points of weakness as a prelude to limiting them and thereafter removing them, so as to achieve a transparent and effective administration. Whereas it has been established that the inspection report drawn up as a result of executing the mission of institutional performance evaluation in the Directorate General of Roads and Buildings indicated the existence of points of strength that can be summarised by the availability of competent human elements, the existence of regional directorates capable of meeting the needs of citizens in the regions, as well as the existence of a comprehensive administrative organisation that provides for the tasks of all units in a semi-detailed manner; however, the usurpation of the powers of the regional directorates in favour of the central administration, and the lack of respect for the comprehensive administrative organisation calls for not including these two points among the points of strength so long as the administration does not benefit from their positive repercussions on the workflow therein, which necessitates including them within the points of weakness from which the said Directorate General suffers.

Whereas it has been established that the Directorate General of Roads and Buildings suffers, in addition to the two points of weakness referred to above, from numerous other points of weakness which may be summarised as follows: - The failure of the Nine-Year Plan prepared by the World Bank to receive official approval. - A severance in the relationship between the administration and the citizen. - The absence of job descriptions for leadership positions. - The contracting out of the tasks of studies and supervision, which are at the core of the tasks of the Directorate of Roads, to private offices. - The absence of documents specifying the time limits and documents required for the completion of transactions. - The determination of appropriations in an arbitrary manner in the absence of any plan studied with precision and seriousness.

- Failure to comply with the applicable legal rules and procedures when awarding contracts, and the adoption of the "on-demand" method. - The lack of effective internal control and the reliance on the individual work of the units instead of the cooperation presumed to exist among them and the exchange of views. Whereas it is necessary to recommend to the Ministry of Public Works and Transport, the Directorate General of Roads and Buildings, to expedite the adoption of the Nine-Year Plan aimed at developing and rehabilitating the road network in Lebanon, and to secure the necessary appropriations therefor, and to fill vacancies and secure equipment, in addition to preparing task cards for employees, and adopting minutes of sessions for the meetings held with the heads of departments and having the latter prepare accurate and comprehensive annual reports, while establishing a plan to qualify employees in accordance with the requirements of the work of each of them, in cooperation with both the Civil Service Board and the Office of the Minister of State for Administrative Reform OMSAR.

Following deliberation, and in the light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided - to recommend that the Ministry of Public Works and Transport, Directorate General of Roads and Buildings, work towards the following: 1 - Expediting the adoption of the nine-year plan drawn up by the PIU for the development and rehabilitation of the road network in Lebanon. 2 - Securing the necessary appropriations for the plan whilst adopting the contracting methods provided for in the Public Accounting Law and refraining from expanding the adoption of the "on-demand" method. 3 - Filling the vacant positions after taking into account the number of wage-earners and contractors. 4 - Seeking to secure the necessary equipment and fittings for the employees to enable them to perform their duties in preparing technical studies and supervising implementation, in order to prevent the expenditure of vast sums on private offices and consultants. 5 - Organising job description cards for leading employees as a first stage, whilst establishing a comprehensive manual of transactions and procedures and the manner of their completion. 6 - Adopting minutes of sittings for the meetings held with the heads of services and urging them to prepare comprehensive and accurate annual reports. 7 - Establishing a plan to qualify employees in accordance with the requirements of the work of each of them, in cooperation with both the Civil Service Board and the Office of the Minister of State for Administrative Reform OMSAR. A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the twenty-sixth day of the month of March in the year two thousand and three.

Secretariat of the Board Session: 33/2003 Item: 10 Decision No. 391/2003 The Central Inspection Board, Having perused the file of the case registered under Nos. 2009 and 115/2003 with all its contents. Having perused the report of the Administrative Inspectors Messrs. Rabih Al-Timani, Ali Al-Hajj Diab and Jeries Atmeh, the Financial Inspector Mr. Naji Shaaban, and the Engineering Inspector Mr. Ahmad Al-Hajjar, dated 10/7/2003, following the application of the general inspection indicators and the standards of quality control and institutional performance in each of the Directorate of Buildings and the Joint Administrative Directorate in the Ministry of Public Works and Transport. Having perused the opinion of the Administrative Inspector General dated 30/7/2003 Having perused the opinion of the Engineering Inspector General dated 12/8/2003 Having perused the opinion of the Financial Inspector General dated 19/8/2003 Having perused the opinion of the President of the Central Inspection dated 21/8/2003 Whereas it appears from the documents of the file that two working teams of inspectors working in the Central Inspection Administration were formed, pursuant to the decision issued by the Presidency of the Central Inspection under No. 52/M/2003 dated 16/4/2003, and were entrusted with the task of applying the general inspection indicators and the standards of quality control and institutional performance, the first in the Directorate General of Urban Planning and the second in the Directorate of Buildings and the Joint Administrative Directorate in the Ministry of Public Works and Transport, (in completion of a previous evaluation covering...., the subject of Central Inspection Board Decision No. 155/2003), on the basis of the letter of the Minister of State for Administrative Development Affairs No. 910/S/2002 dated 12/11/2002, and in accordance with the form attached thereto. Whereas it appears that the task of applying the general inspection indicators and the standards of quality control and institutional performance in each of the Directorate of Buildings and the Joint Administrative Directorate in the Ministry of Public Works and Transport contributed to highlighting the points of weakness and the points of strength in each of the two aforementioned administrative units, which enables those in charge of them in the future to support the points of strength and work to enhance and increase them, and to devote themselves, likewise, to addressing the points of weakness in preparation for limiting them and subsequently eliminating them, so as to reach a transparent and effective administration. And whereas it appears that there exist points of strength.......... which are summed up in the performance by the aforementioned Directorate of the tasks entrusted to it despite the acute vacancy in its cadre and the lack of availability of the technical equipment required for the work of the engineers therein, and the existence of points of weakness that may be summarised as follows, along with the recommendation to work on eliminating them: - The absence of a detailed and time-distributed long-term strategic plan. - The existence of other official authorities that undertake the execution of maintenance works for government buildings, which leads to duplication of work and overlapping of powers. - The failure of heads of units to abide by drawing up annual reports. - The failure to prepare prior written agendas for meetings, and the failure to draw up written minutes as a result of those meetings. - The high rate of vacancy in the cadre (69%). - The absence of job descriptions, particularly at the level of engineers.

- The absence of a statement on the progress of transactions and the determination of the time limits necessary to complete each type thereof. - The non-application of the performance evaluation system during the year 2002 - The failure to provide for dedicated appropriations.......... due to their merger within the appropriations of the Directorate General of Roads and Buildings. - The absence of an accountant in charge of keeping accounting records and monitoring the movement of appropriations at the Directorate of Buildings. And whereas it was found that there are strengths in the Joint Administrative Directorate summarised in the conformity of the adopted structure with the objectives and tasks entrusted to the said Directorate, and the availability of a database (personal files) for all employees and the application of the performance evaluation system to them, and the existence of weaknesses that may be summarised as follows, with the recommendation to work on removing them: - The absence of a long-term strategic plan or an annual or quarterly plan. - The failure to hold periodic meetings between the director and his subordinates. - The existence of a defect in the work of the Personnel Department as a unit for personnel management due to its lack of competent elements, and the absence of a plan for human resources development. - The absence of a register of complaints kept in accordance with the rules. - The absence of task cards for employees and the Directorate's lack of job descriptions. - The absence of a comprehensive guide for transactions showing the time limits necessary to complete each type thereof. - Weak communication between the director and his subordinates. - The failure to base the budget on clear plans and programmes. - The failure to take carried-over appropriations into consideration when preparing the budget. - The existence of a defect in the computerisation programme leading to the occurrence of errors in the carried-over appropriations. - The existence of a fragmentation of expenditures that is not legally justified. - The failure to keep a special register for transactions returned by.........., and consequently, stating their value and the reason for their return. - The failure of.......... to conduct inspection tours of the units affiliated to him. And whereas it is required to transmit to the Ministry of Public Works and Transport, the Directorate General of Roads and Buildings, and the Joint Administrative Directorate, a copy of the form that was prepared on the two said units within the framework of the operation of inspecting and measuring institutional performance in each of them, to examine its content. And after deliberation, and in light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided to transmit to the Ministry of Public Works and Transport a copy of the two forms that were prepared on each of the Directorate of Buildings, and the Joint Administrative Directorate, and to recommend to it the following: First: With regard to the Directorate of Buildings: 1 - Adopting a long-term strategic plan based on practical studies and distributing it over time stages. 2 - Examining the possibility of restricting maintenance, construction and furniture works in public administrations and unifying them under a single authority. 3 - Organising task cards for all employees in the Directorate of Buildings. 4 - Organising job description cards. 5 - Adopting written procedures for the progress of each transaction and circulating them to the employees of the Directorate.

6 - Enhancing the use of computers. 7 - Drawing up agendas for working sessions and preparing official minutes of the outcome thereof. 8 - Issuing a circular to the heads of units in the Directorate of Buildings to abide by preparing the required annual reports in accordance with Legislative Decree No. 111/59. 9 - Abiding by the application of the performance evaluation system in accordance with the rules. 10 - Considering the possibility of separating the appropriations allocated to the Directorate of Buildings from the appropriations allocated to the Directorate of Roads when preparing the budget in order to implement the required plan. 11 - Considering the possibility of providing for the post of accountant in the establishment of the Directorate of Buildings. 12 - Securing the necessary technical equipment for the Directorate of Buildings to enable the engineers working therein to perform the tasks required of them, and dispensing with the works of the private sector in order to rationalise expenditure. Second: With regard to the Joint Administrative Directorate: 1 - Adopting a long-term strategic plan for its works and programmes distributed annually. 2 - Abiding by holding periodic working meetings and preparing written minutes of the outcome thereof, securing continuous communication with subordinates, and activating hierarchical oversight over their works. 3 - Reinforcing the Personnel Department as a personnel management unit with competent staff to enable it to draw up a plan for human resources development in cooperation with the competent authorities. 4 - Keeping a special register for complaints in due form. 5 - Preparing task cards for employees in accordance with the adopted rules and working on job descriptions. 6 - Drawing up a comprehensive citizen's guide to transactions and the procedures relating to their completion. 7 - Taking into consideration carried-over appropriations when preparing the budget in order to rationalise expenditure. 8 - Removing the defect occurring in the computerisation programme in order to be able to control the appropriations carried over from all previous years. 9 - Adopting legal procedures in executing contracts and not resorting to fragmentation except in legally justified cases. 10 - Keeping a special register for transactions returned by .......... and the Directorate of Expenditures to show their value and the reasons for their return. A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the third of the month of September in the year two thousand and three.

Secretariat of the Board Session: 33/2003 Item: 11 Decision No. 392/2003 The Central Inspection Board, Having perused the file of the case registered under No. 2010 and 115/ 2003 in all its contents. Having perused the report of the Administrative Inspectors: Mr. Afif Rizk and Mr. Nawal Nasser, the Engineering Inspectors: Mr. Bachir Fawaz and Mrs. Hoda Salloum, and the Financial Inspector Mr. Antoine Nohra dated 30/6/2003, resulting from the application of the general inspection indicators and the standards of quality control and institutional performance in the Directorate General of Urban Planning. Having perused the opinion of the Administrative Inspector General dated 30/7 /2003 Having perused the opinion of the Engineering Inspector General dated 12/8 /2003 Having perused the opinion of the Financial Inspector General dated 19/8/ 2003 Having perused the opinion of the President of the Central Inspection dated 21 /8/2003 Whereas it appears from the documents of the file that two working teams of inspectors working in the Central Inspection Administration were formed pursuant to the Decision issued by the Presidency of the Central Inspection under No. 52/M/ 2003 dated 16/4/2003, to which was assigned the mission of applying the general inspection indicators and the standards of quality control and institutional performance, the first in the Directorate General of Urban Planning, and the second in the Directorate General of Roads and Buildings and the Joint Administrative Directorate in the Ministry of Public Works and Transport, on the basis of the letter of the Minister of State for Administrative Development Affairs No. 910 /S/2002 dated 12/11/2002, and in accordance with the form attached thereto. Whereas it appears that the mission of applying the general inspection indicators and the standards of quality control and institutional performance in the Directorate General of Urban Planning contributed to highlighting the points of weakness and the points of strength in the said Administration, which enables those in charge thereof in the future to support the points of strength and work to strengthen and increase them, and to apply themselves, likewise, to addressing the points of weakness in preparation for limiting them and subsequently removing them, so as to reach a transparent and effective administration. Whereas it appears that the inspection report drawn up as a result of executing the mission of evaluating the institutional performance in the Directorate General of Urban Planning identified the points of strength as the existence of a good and effective administrative deconcentration in all the districts, the issuance of explanatory memoranda and circulars whether with respect to guiding the citizens concerned or with respect to facilitating the work of the employees, and the adoption of a computerisation system in the central administration which is being developed to cover the regional offices, in addition to the availability of readiness on the part of .......... to address complaints and to activate the work, as well as on the part of the human staff in the central administration to complete the studies which are entrusted, at the present time, to private offices.

Whereas it has transpired that the Directorate General of Urban Planning suffers from numerous points of weakness which may be summarised as follows: - The absence of strategic planning at the central level. - The existence of vacant positions in the establishment of the Directorate General, especially in the technical leadership Second and Third Categories, which are currently filled in an acting capacity. - The absence of a one-stop shop system for services. - The non-application of the employee performance appraisal system due to the vacancy of leadership positions. - The scarcity of periodic meetings (horizontally and vertically). - The existence of uncommitted appropriations in Part Two "B" that are carried over annually without being committed. - The lack of a clear and defined classification for private study offices that undertake the preparation of technical studies. - The non-participation of the Directorate General in financial affairs, particularly with regard to the preparation of the budget and the execution of expenditures. - The non-preparation of the semi-annual report on the conditions of the Directorate General which is supposed to be prepared by.......... Whereas it has transpired that there is no specific system for monitoring the quality of services provided in the Directorate General of Urban Planning, and that.......... undertakes personal initiatives to monitor quality by inquiring about the fate of certain transactions and the difficulties obstructing their completion, and that there are no survey operations to determine the extent of the citizen's satisfaction with the services provided to him, and that the absence of such criteria referred to renders some of the items contained in the form adopted for measuring institutional performance in public administrations (..........) of no value. Whereas it is required to furnish the Ministry of Public Works and Transport, the Directorate General of Urban Planning, with a copy of the form that was prepared regarding the said Directorate General, within the framework of the operation of inspecting and measuring institutional performance therein, and the main conclusions attached thereto and the recommendations pertaining to it, in order to examine its contents, particularly as regards establishing an annual plan with defined objectives and expected stages of implementation, allowing for the conduct of an effective and constructive operation of inspection and institutional performance measurement in the light of the results achieved at the end of the prescribed period. And after deliberation, and in the light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided - To furnish the Ministry of Public Works and Transport - the Directorate General of Urban Planning - with a copy of the form that was prepared regarding the said Directorate General, within the framework of the operation of monitoring and measuring institutional performance therein, and the main conclusions attached thereto, and the recommendations pertaining to it, in order to examine its contents, particularly as regards establishing an annual plan with defined objectives and expected stages of implementation allowing for the conduct of an effective and constructive operation of inspection and institutional performance measurement in the light of the results and achievements realised. A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the third of the month of September of the year two thousand and three.

Secretariat of the Board Session: 1/2003 Item: 6 Decision No. 6/2003 The Central Inspection Board, Having perused the file of the case registered under No. 48/7 B/ 2001 with all its contents. Having perused the report of the two Financial Inspectors, Messrs. Mohammad Hallawi and Michel Dib, dated 18/5/2002 and 15/6/2002, resulting from the investigation into the opening of two accounts in a private commercial bank in the name of the Directorate General of the Ministry of Information contrary to the rules. Having perused the minutes of the interrogation of.......... of Information.......... on 8/6/2002, and his written defence regarding the charges attributed to him. Having perused the two opinions of the Financial Inspector General dated 20/5 /2002 and 17/6/2002 Having perused the opinion of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Accounts No. 436/1986 dated 26/11/2002 Having perused the opinion of the President of the Central Inspection dated 12 /12/2002 Whereas it appears from the documents of the file that the Minister of Information deposited with the Central Inspection a copy of his letter No. 1688 dated 6/10/ 2001, addressed to the management of Bank.........., and relating to the closing of two accounts at the said bank, belonging to the Directorate General of the Ministry of Information, which had been opened contrary to the Public Accounting Law, and that the General Financial Inspectorate conducted an investigation into the matter within the framework of the annual inspection programme for the year 2001 Whereas it appears from the investigation that the.......... of the Ministry of Information, Mr........... requested on 24/5/84, from the management of Bank.......... to open a "current account" in US Dollars in the name of the Directorate General of the Ministry of Information at the said bank, and that the operation of the aforementioned account became, as of 13/12/84, vested in the Minister and the Director General, after having been restricted to the latter alone on the date of opening the account, and another account in Lebanese Pounds was also opened, in the name of the same entity, at the bank referred to above pursuant to the letter of the Minister of Information No. 1740 dated 17/10/85, provided that this account be operated by the joint signature of both the Minister and the Director General, and that the opening of the two said accounts was contrary to the provisions of Article 243 of the Public Accounting Law, which prohibits public administrations, municipalities and public institutions from opening accounts in private banks. Whereas it appears that the Council of Ministers accepted on 26/12/84 a financial grant in the amount of /159840/ one hundred and fifty-nine thousand eight hundred and forty US Dollars offered by the League of Arab States, allocated to organizing a media campaign in support of the South, West Bekaa and Rashaya, and that the Directorate General of the Ministry of Information proceeded to transfer the amount of the said grant to the account opened at Bank.......... approximately seven months prior to the approval thereof by the Council of Ministers, and without making any entry of the aforementioned grant in the revenues section of the budget, or opening appropriations for its amount in the expenditures section in application of the provisions of Article 52 of the Public Accounting Law. Whereas it appears that the Minister of Information restricted on 15/6/93 the authority to operate the account deposited in Bank.......... to the Minister alone, and that an amount of /12724864/ USD was withdrawn from the bank after this date, whereas the value of the amounts withdrawn during the preceding period, during which the authority to withdraw was vested in the Minister and the Director General, amounted to /16001005/ USD, noting that an amount of /100000/ USD was added to the balance deposited at the bank on 16 and 17/2/95 without the records of the Ministry of Information indicating the source of this amount or the destination of expenditure of most of the withdrawn amounts or the rules adopted in disbursing them.

Whereas it appeared that the .......... of the Ministry of Information, Mr. .........., placed at the disposal of the President of the Council of Ministers pursuant to Decree No. 119 dated 25/1/99, had knowledge of the two accounts opened at a commercial bank, and that he did not take the initiative to prepare a report on this matter or refer it to the competent authorities, and during his tenure of duties at the Ministry he drew up an agreement for the production of a documentary motion picture on South Lebanon with the director Mr. .........., and the expenditures of this work amounting to / 23000/ USD were disbursed from the balance of the account opened at .......... Bank, despite the irregularities that accompanied the operation of opening this account and depositing the amounts therein, a matter which entails disciplinary and financial liability on his part in this regard; however, the positive results achieved by the aforementioned work in the media field in terms of showing the suffering of Southern citizens would mitigate this liability without removing it, which requires taking the appropriate disciplinary measures against him pursuant to the provisions of Articles 54 and 55 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59, and referring him before the Court of Accounts pursuant to the provisions of Article 60 of the Law of its Organisation. Whereas it did not appear that any withdrawal operation in dollars took place since the opening of the first account on 24/5/84 and until 31/10/85, that is during the period in which Mr. .......... assumed his duties at the Ministry as its Director General, yet the act of the latter in opening two bank accounts at a private bank in the name of the Directorate General of the Ministry of Information in violation of the provisions of Article 243 of the Public Accounting Law entails financial and disciplinary liability on his part for which he must be held accountable. Whereas Mr. .......... has left the public service and there is no longer any room to prosecute him disciplinarily, yet his financial liability remains standing, which requires referring him before the Court of Accounts pursuant to the provisions of the Law of its Organisation promulgated by Legislative Decree No. 82/ 83. Whereas it appeared that the account opened at .......... Bank in Lebanese currency was funded by means of transfers taken from the account opened in American currency at the aforementioned bank, and that the two accounts opened at this bank were finally closed on 24/1/2002 and that the balance amounting to /120014 / USD on the date of closure was transferred to the Lebanese Treasury after deducting the bank commission and the fee for the account statement expenses. And after deliberation, and in light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided: 1 - To reprimand the .......... of the Ministry of Information, Mr. .......... 2 - To refer Messrs. .......... before the Court of Accounts. A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the eighth of the month of January of the year two thousand and three.

Secretariat of the Board Session: 1/2003 Item: 14 Decision No. 14/2003 The Central Inspection Board, Having perused the file of the case registered under No. 63/7/2000 in all its contents. Having perused the two reports of the Financial Inspectors Messrs.: Mohammad Hallawi, Michel Dib, and Nemer Zein dated 29/5/2001 and 5/9 /2002 as a result of the investigation into violations attributed to certain employees of the Electricité du Liban Corporation relating to the receipt of cheques without mentioning the date of issue and without the availability of provision. Having perused the two opinions of the Financial Inspector General dated 26/7 /2001 and 5/11/2002 Having perused the two opinions of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Accounts No. 356/2296 dated 16/9/2001 and No. 437/ 3549 dated 26/11/2002 Having perused the decision of the Central Inspection Board No. 579/ 2001 dated 28/11/2001 Having perused the two opinions of the Central Inspection dated 4/10/ 2001 and 12/12/2002 And whereas it appeared from the documents of the file that the Central Inspection Board took Decision No. 579/2001 dated 28/11/2001, as a result of the investigation into the violations attributed to certain employees of the Electricité du Liban Corporation, the subject of the referral of the Minister of Energy and Water No. 3290/W dated 23/5/2000, and relating to the receipt of cheques without mentioning the date of issue, and without the availability of provision, pursuant to which it returned the file to the General Financial Inspectorate to expand the investigation into the overlooking by each of the Distribution Directorate in Beirut and Mount Lebanon, and the Directorate of Financial Affairs, of the application of the provisions of the two books of specifications against the contractor of collection works in the two departments of.........., Mr..........., which led to his receiving commissions at their maximum limit without right, and inflicting upon the Corporation a financial loss starting from the year 1996 and up to date, and that the Central Inspection Board examined the case anew in light of the report drawn up by the General Financial Inspectorate on 5/9 /2002 for this purpose. And whereas it appeared from the investigation that the Electricité du Liban Corporation approved since the year 1996 to contract with Mr........... for a period of two years to carry out the works of leasing the reading of subscribers' meters in the two departments of.........., and collecting the value of consumption invoices in accordance with what is specified in the two books of specifications and the two contracts attached thereto, signed by Mr........... And whereas it appeared that the Third, Fifth, and Eighth Articles of the book of specifications specified the work regime of collection and the rate of commission due to the contractor in accordance with the following: - Starting from the second day of the date of his receipt of the collection receipts from the department, the contractor must immediately commence collecting the values of these receipts within a time limit of 24 days and until the date specified for him in accordance with the book of specifications to return these receipts, and must deposit the collected cash values day by day in the fund of the department or the bank specified for him by the Corporation, to the exclusion of any other, and as for the cheques issued by the subscribers, he deposits them in the fund of the department directly, and upon the expiry of the period of /24/ days, the contractor immediately returns the uncollected communications to the department so that the operation of calculating the rate of commission due to him is carried out in accordance with the provisions of the Eighth Article of the book of specifications. - The calculation of the rate of commission for the contractor is carried out on the basis of the number of receipts collected within the specified period of 24 days out of the total number of receipts delivered to him, whereby the prescribed commission is calculated from the value of the collected receipts.

- The rate of the delay penalty shall be deducted from the commission due to the contractor out of the values of the receipts collected within a time limit of 24 days. - Uncollected receipts which the contractor had returned to the department upon the expiry of the specified period of /24/ days shall be returned again to the contractor in order for him to collect them anew, provided that he obtains a commission at a rate of 4% of the value of what he collects of these receipts in accordance with the provisions of the Fifth Article. Whereas it was established that Mr. .......... did not abide by the clauses of the contract concluded with him with respect to: - His failure to abide by the time limit of /24/ days specified for settling the receipts. - His continuous delay in closing the issuances delivered to him. - His continuous delay in settling the cash amounts collected from the issuances delivered to him. - His failure to return the uncollected receipts after the expiry of the period of /24/ days specified for each issuance. - His failure to deposit the collected cash amounts with the treasury of the department or with the Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce - .......... Branch - in accordance with the book of conditions, and his depositing them into his personal account for the purpose of benefiting from the bank commission for his personal interest, and his giving in exchange therefor cheques either without provision, or without a date, or not issued by him personally but by another drawer, and that these cheques are not certified, and that the financial amounts collected by Mr. .......... which he retained in his possession and did not proceed to settle with the treasuries of the service in accordance with the rules, amounted to /684596985 / L.L., six hundred and eighty-four million five hundred and ninety-six thousand nine hundred and eighty-five Lebanese Pounds, including the delay penalty amounting to /19374000/ L.L., nineteen million three hundred and seventy-four thousand Lebanese Pounds. Whereas it was established that Electricité du Liban proceeded in early 2000 to rescind the contract with Mr. .......... under his liability, pursuant to the provisions of the first paragraph of the Twelfth Article of the book of conditions, and also confiscated on 26/4/2000 the two bank guarantees submitted by him amounting in value to eighty-three million Lebanese Pounds, and lodged two criminal complaints before the competent judiciary in Mount Lebanon, as a result of the investigation into which two arrest warrants in absentia were issued against Mr. .........., for the offence of embezzlement of public funds and issuance of cheques without provision, which requires recommending working on following up the prosecution against Mr. .......... in light of the provisions of the texts in force. Whereas it was established that the employee in the capacity of collector of Category 5/1 at Electricité du Liban, Mr. .........., assigned to the duties of the treasury of the Department of Jbeil, accepted cheques issued by someone other than the party concerned and bearing no date, contrary to the content of Regulatory Memorandum No. 711/98, and to the content of Memorandum No. 262/94, which provides for not accepting cheques without a date, and that what Mr. .......... pleaded with respect to his lack of knowledge of the texts governing his work as a treasurer cannot be accepted, due to the inadmissibility of pleading ignorance of the law, and because the latter memorandum referred to above is addressed in principle to the collectors working at the Establishment, including him, and also that the Head of the Department of .......... Mr. .......... participated with Mr. .........., in endorsing the undated cheques delivered to the treasury of the department which he heads, a matter which entails upon Messrs. .......... disciplinary and financial liability for which they must be held accountable. Whereas it was established that the employee at the Special Substations Unit, Mrs. .........., delivered to Mr. .........., brother of the contractor Mr. .........., the issuance of the month of 3/2000 pertaining to the two Departments of .......... from the head office of the Establishment in Beirut instead of his receiving them at the office of the two aforementioned departments, despite the fact that the instructions given to her by the Head of the Special Substations Unit require delivering the medium-voltage issuance to the Distribution Service in Mount Lebanon and not directly to the contractor, which entails upon her disciplinary and financial liability as a result of this violation.

Whereas it is necessary to recommend that the Electricité du Liban Corporation work on amending Administrative Order No. 37 dated 22/4/2000 relating to informing the Directorate General of a Corporation of violations occurring in the Corporation, such that this amendment provides for the necessity for the employee in the Corporation to give notice of the violations that he encounters directly and immediately to both his hierarchical superiors and the Financial Controller simultaneously, in application of the principle of administrative hierarchy on the one hand, and to facilitate financial auditing operations on the other hand. And after deliberation, and in light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided: 1 - To deduct the wage of each of the Treasurer of the Jbeil Department affiliated with the Electricité du Liban Corporation, Mr. .........., the current Head of the Two Departments of .........., Mr. .......... and the female employee in the Private Substations Apparatus, Mrs. .......... for one day as a disciplinary measure. 2 - To address a written remark to each of .......... of the Two Departments of .......... Engineer .........., Department of .......... Mr. .........., and the technical employee in the aforementioned Department Mr. .......... 3 - To refer each of Messrs. .........., before the Court of Audit. 4 - To defer deciding upon the responsibilities of .......... Financial and the Distribution Director of .......... and anyone shown by the investigations to be involved in the case that is the subject of this decision until the issuance of the final decision by the judiciary so that the necessary action may be taken accordingly. 5 - To recommend to the Electricité du Liban Corporation the following: a - To pursue the prosecution against the contractor Mr. .......... for the offence of issuing cheques without provision and embezzlement of public funds in light of the provisions of the laws and regulations in force. b - To emphasize to the concerned employees the necessity of adhering to the content of Memoranda No. 262/94 and 2/91, particularly the collectors and treasurers, regarding how to verify cheques and the cases of their non-acceptance. c - To confirm the recommendation of the Central Inspection Board in its Decision No. 523 /2001 regarding employing a sufficient number of collectors in preparation for dispensing with fee-based collectors and collection contractors, increasing the value of the guarantees of fee-based collection contractors pending the dispensing with their services, and tightening hierarchical field supervision over collection operations. d - To amend the Administrative Order issued by the Director General of the Electricité du Liban Corporation under No. 37 dated 22/4/2000 regarding including therein a request to employees who encounter financial violations to inform the Financial Controller thereof immediately and directly as well as informing their hierarchical superiors thereof in accordance with the rules. A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the eighth of the month of January in the year two thousand and three.

Whereas it was established that each of.......... of the two Departments of.......... Engineer.........., the technical employee in the Department of Kartaba, Mr.........., and the current treasurer of the Department of Kartaba, Mr.........., endorsed the cheques issued by persons other than the collection contractor, in addition to Mr.......... accepting the said cheques, thereby violating the content of Regulatory Memorandum No. 711/98, and the duties imposed by the laws and regulations in force, which entails disciplinary liability upon them in this regard. Secretariat of the Board Session: 13/2003 Item: 8 Decision No. 163/2003 The Central Inspection Board, Having examined the file of the case registered under No. 40/7/2002 in all its contents

2549/W 2002 Having examined the report of the financial inspectors Ms Najwa Sakr and Mr Mikhael Fayyad dated 26/2/2003, following the investigation into the irregularities occurring in the Ministry of Agriculture. Having examined the opinion of the Financial Inspector General dated 27/2/ 2003 Having examined the opinion of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Audit No. 101/806 dated 12/3/2003 Having examined the opinion of the President of the Central Inspection dated 21 /3/2003 Whereas it appeared from the documents of the file that the Secretary-General of the Council of Ministers deposited with the Central Inspection, pursuant to his letter No. 2152/M.S dated 29/8/2002, a copy of the question submitted by.......... concerning the irregularities occurring in the Ministry of Agriculture, for perusal and for providing the Council of Ministers with the appropriate answer regarding the administrative and financial aspects, and Assignment No. 40/7/2002 dated 31/8/2002 was issued to investigate the matter. Whereas it appeared from the investigation that the Lebanese Government was authorised, pursuant to Law No. 645 dated 2/6/97 and Law No. 236 dated 7/8/ 2000, to conclude the two loan agreements signed between the Government of the Lebanese Republic and the Government of the United States of America, the first in the amount of /6000000/ U.S.D. six million United States dollars, and the second in the amount of /15000000/ U.S.D. fifteen million United States dollars in order to contribute to financing the Lebanese-American Agricultural Cooperation Project, the objectives of which were defined as rehabilitating productivity among small farmers and livestock breeders through a comprehensive development programme comprising the importation of a total of /8000/ purebred dairy heifers (Holstein), (3000 heifers in the first agreement, 5000 heifers in the second agreement) from the United States of America, and their distribution to small farmers in the various Lebanese regions, and that the management unit entrusted with executing the project operates under the direct supervision of the Board of Directors chaired by the Minister of Agriculture, pursuant to the two loan agreements referred to above. Whereas it appeared that the management of the Lebanese-American Agricultural Cooperation Project commissioned an independent office to audit the accounts of the project, the subject of the agreement the conclusion of which was authorised by Law No. 645/97, and that the report drawn up following the audit indicated discrepancies in the account resulting from the failure to enter into the accounts of the project a large portion of the dead cows, the owners of which recovered the first instalment of their price, and the said report also indicated the existence of /294/ cows of undetermined fate, of which the inspection team was able to determine the fate of / 132/ cows. Whereas it appeared that the farmers benefiting from the three shipments of cows imported within the framework of the second loan agreement (Law No. 236/2000), and who entered into contracts with the project under which the price of the cows distributed to them was payable by instalments, did not fulfil their obligations, with respect to failing to pay the value of the promissory notes that they signed, upon their maturity, and that /53/ cows from the first shipment were delivered to beneficiaries without the existence of documents justifying the delivery of this number of cows to them, in addition to the existence of three cows of undetermined fate, and that there is manipulation occurring in the delivery orders of this batch which led to a number of beneficiaries failing to perform the obligations required of them towards the management of the project, in addition to the existence of a contradiction between the information issued by the American University, and that issued by the management of the project concerning the delivery of the original orders pertaining to the first shipment of cows.

Whereas it has appeared from the audit of the documents of the second shipment of cows, carried out within the framework of the implementation of Law No. 236/2000, that there are /51/ cows, the majority of which were distributed free of charge, pursuant to the order or with the knowledge of the Minister of Agriculture without specifying the legal basis for such free distribution. And that there is clear tampering in delivery orders pertaining to /21/ beneficiaries who received cows from the aforementioned shipment, and that the investigations conducted by the project management did not reach a determination of the causes of this tampering, nor did the management proceed to rectify the situation with respect to removing the effects resulting therefrom, represented by achieving material gains at the expense of public funds, which calls for prosecuting the perpetrators thereof before the competent judicial authorities. And whereas it has appeared, within the framework of the distribution of the third shipment of cows, that twenty pedigree cows were delivered to Mr. .......... the Agricultural Cooperative in Sarein, for subsequent distribution to certain farmers, and that this measure was not coupled with the approval of the Minister of Agriculture, which prompted the project management to regularise the status of the cows by concluding an agreement with Mr. .......... whereby the Cooperative pays a down payment of the price of the cows, provided that the remainder is paid in semi-annual instalments, in addition to other obligations set forth in the text of the said contract, including the submission by the Cooperative of quarterly reports on the conditions of the cows, and that the Cooperative has not, to date, paid the instalment due from it to the project management nor has it submitted the required quarterly reports, which constitutes a breach of the obligations of the contract necessitating the application of the provisions contained therein with respect to recovering all the cows and counting the down payment as a financial penalty resulting from the non-performance thereof. And whereas it has appeared that the management of the Lebanese-American Agricultural Cooperation Project proceeded, within the framework of seeking to increase the potato productivity of the Lebanese farmer, to introduce new varieties of industrial potatoes into the Lebanese market, which were sold to farmers after they paid 20% of the price thereof and signed promissory notes for the remaining value of the price, and that there is a clear discrepancy between the documents pertaining to delivery and those delivered to the inspection team by the project management with respect to the quantity of seed potatoes delivered and the quantity of damaged seed potatoes, and it also appeared to the inspection that there is a quantity of agricultural pesticides which are supposed to have been received with the potatoes, regarding which no information was available as to the manner of their use and their fate. And whereas it has appeared that an agreement was concluded between the management of the Lebanese-American Agricultural Cooperation Project and Mr. .......... to carry out a pilot project for the cultivation of industrial potatoes, and that a contradiction occurred in the reports relating to the area of cultivated land, the quantity of seed potatoes delivered, and the productivity of the pilot project, and that the management of the Agricultural Cooperation Project accepted, under the guise of the loss suffered by Mr. .......... to receive the price of the potatoes from the project's share by way of a deferred payment promissory note until the end of the year 2002, the value of which has not been paid until this date. And whereas it has appeared, with regard to the information referred to by His Excellency the Deputy Mr. .......... concerning the alteration that occurred in the report of the committee formed to study the problems of potato cultivation and propose appropriate solutions therefor, that one of the members of the committee, Dr. .........., confirmed the occurrence of an amendment to the report through its correction after its printing at the American University, and that Dr. .........., one of the other members of the committee, neither denied nor confirmed the fact of the alteration, whereas .........., .........., considered that all the members of the committee signed the report without any reservation, and that it was not conclusively proven to the investigation that there was tampering in the said report, which requires closing the case in this respect.

Whereas it appeared from the totality of the facts of the investigation that the works of the Lebanese-American Agricultural Cooperation Project have ended, and that there are physical assets, physical bonds and financial bonds other than the bonds signed by the farmers benefiting from the cows, which remained without collection or settlement, and which may be stated as follows: - The compensation due from the American supplier for the death of /27/ cows before the end of the quarantine period, estimated at /64800/ USD, sixty-four thousand eight hundred United States dollars. - The bond signed by Mr. .......... as the price of the Ministry's share in the pilot project for potato cultivation, valued at /25500/ USD, twenty-five thousand five hundred United States dollars. - The training cows located at the American University, numbering /32/ cows, and what resulted therefrom during the previous years. - The agricultural vehicle shipped by the supplier of industrial potatoes, which the director of the Cooperation Project stated is located at the American University, which requires recommending to the Directorate General of Agriculture, to which the assets of the project were handed over, to look into the possibility of claiming from the American supplier the value of the compensation due from it in favour of the project, working to collect the bond signed by Mr. .........., and receiving the cows and the vehicle located at the American University, in accordance with what was indicated above. And whereas it appeared that the workers in the Lebanese-American Agricultural Cooperation Project were dismissed as a result of the cessation of the project's works, which places them outside the scope of disciplinary prosecution, yet this matter does not preclude prosecuting them before the Court of Accounts pursuant to the provisions of Article 65 of Legislative Decree No. 82/83, as the financial violations they committed fall under the provisions of Article 60 of the Law on the Organisation of the Court of Accounts, and referring the file to the Cassation Public Prosecution to look into the facts contained therein which may constitute criminal offences punishable by law.

Secretariat of the Board Session: 15/2003 Item: 11 Decision No. 194/2003 The Central Inspection Board, having perused the case file under No. 32/7/2002 with all its contents.

1952/W 2002 Having perused the report of the Financial Inspector, Mr. Duraid Al-Jammal, dated 10/2/2002, resulting from the investigation into the act of.......... at the Lebanese University, Mr..........., of issuing a cheque without cover, and retaining public funds in his liability unpaid to those entitled thereto. Having perused the opinion of the Financial Inspector General dated 18/3/ 2003 Having perused the opinion of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Audit No. 121/1985 dated 25/3/2003 Having perused the opinion of the President of the Central Inspection dated 31 /3/2003 Whereas it appeared from the documents of the file that the President of the Lebanese University requested the Central Inspection, pursuant to his letter No. 492/R, dated 26/6/2002, to conduct the necessary investigations with one of.......... at the Lebanese University for proceeding to issue a cheque without provision, and for the existence of funds in his liability that were not paid to their owners, and Assignment No. 32/7/2002 was issued to investigate the matter. Whereas it appeared from the investigation that.......... at the Lebanese University, Mr..........., assigned to the duties of a receipt officer to collect registration fees, library subscription fees, competitive examination fees, health insurance fees, and other fees pertaining to the Faculty of Letters and Human Sciences - First Branch - issued on 15/5/ 2002 a cheque in the value of /11130000/ L.L. eleven million one hundred and thirty thousand Lebanese Pounds, representing a portion of the proceeds of registration fees, drawn on.......... Bank, Al-Mazraa Branch, which subsequently appeared to be without provision, and that the value of this cheque was secured through assistance received by Mr........... from a number of professors working in the Faculty by waiving their entitlements in his favour, out of a humanitarian motive. Whereas it appeared that there was a financial deficit during the academic year 98 - 99 in the cashbox of.......... Mr..........., and that the latter proceeded to cover the said deficit by resorting to borrowing from a number of banks, and that the total value of the borrowed amounts approached the value of the amounts due to the professors working in the Faculty of Letters - First Branch - without informing the Central Accountant of the Lebanese University or.......... of the Faculty of the matter, and that Mr........... attributed this to his fear of being subjected to judicial prosecution, and the negative repercussions on his functional status that might result therefrom. Whereas it appeared that Mr........... retained in his cashbox cash funds approaching sixty million Lebanese Pounds during a period ranging between one week and twenty days, without paying them in accordance with the established rules in this regard, in addition to the existence of errors in the entries and accounts that led to the accumulation of financial amounts in his liability, the value of which the inspection report determined at /17544255/ L.L. seventeen million five hundred and forty-four thousand two hundred and fifty-five Lebanese Pounds, which necessitates recommending the issuance of a collection order therefor in favour of the Lebanese University.

And after deliberation, and in the light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided 1 - To deposit this decision with the General Secretariat of the Council of Ministers. 2 - To deposit the file with the Cassation Public Prosecution to examine the facts contained therein and take the appropriate measures regarding them. 3 - To refer the file to the Court of Audit pursuant to the provisions of Article 60 of the Law of its Organisation. 4 - To recommend to the Ministry of Agriculture, the Directorate General of Agriculture, the following: a - Examining the possibility of claiming from the American supplier the amount of / 64800/ USD as compensation for the dead cows in the third shipment carried out pursuant to Law No. 236/2000 b - Collecting the value of the promissory note signed by Mr. .......... amounting in value to /25500/ USD twenty-five thousand and five hundred US dollars. c - Recovering and receiving the cows present at the American University, pertaining to the necessities of training, together with the cows born during the period of raising these cows. d - Recovering and receiving the agricultural machinery that was shipped with the industrial potatoes and currently present at the American University. e - Applying the conditions of the contract signed with the Agricultural Cooperative of Sarein, which require recovering the cows sold thereto due to its failure to execute the clauses of the contract. A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the second of the month of April of the year two thousand and three.

Whereas it has become evident that there are errors in the transcription of the names of the students registered in the Faculty of Letters and Human Sciences - First Branch - in the academic year 99 - 2000, and in the determination of the departments to which the said students belong, in addition to the inclusion of the names of twenty-eight students in the registers pertaining to the said Faculty without those names appearing in the central statistics lists of the Lebanese University, which requires, alongside the recommendation, working to form a committee entrusted with correcting the entries relating to the names of the students and their specialisations, whose names appear on the financial receipts for the academic year 99 - 2000, and comparing them with the names included in the registers and the nominal computer lists, and ascertaining the fate of the entries of /28/ students whose names appeared in the approved registers at the Faculty in excess of the total names appearing on the nominal computer lists. Whereas Mr. .........., by issuing a cheque without provision, and retaining cash funds in his safe without paying them in accordance with the rules, and causing the safe to fall into a financial deficit, and accumulating financial amounts owed by him, has violated the duties imposed by the laws and regulations in force, and in particular the financial regulations in effect at the Lebanese University, and the Circular of the Presidency of the University No. 14 dated 24/10/91, and Circular No. 1 dated 23/1/2002 issued by the Central Accountant of the University, and Circular No. 732 dated 12/2/2002, and the provisions of Article 18 of Decision No. 706 /M.J/1999 (Special Regulations for Hired Workers of the Lebanese University), a matter which entails disciplinary and financial liability on his part, and whereas what he stated in the minutes of his interrogation and in his written defence is not such as to exempt him from this liability, which requires holding him accountable therefor. Whereas it has become evident that .......... at the Lebanese University .........., Mr. .......... neglected to perform the duty of supervision over .........., Mr. .........., a matter which enabled the latter to persist in committing violations, and in particular retaining funds pertaining to a number of professors working in the Faculty of Letters and Human Sciences - First Branch - starting from the year 1996 and until his suspension from work on 22/5/2002, and whereas what Mr. .......... stated in the course of justifying this violation does not exempt him from bearing the liability resulting therefrom, for his violation of the provisions of Article 143 of Decree No. 14246/70 (Financial Regulations of the Lebanese University) which impose on .......... the supervision of the work of the employees and treasurers subordinate to him and holding them to account for every violation or delay in their work. Whereas the seventeenth Article of Law No. 75/67 (Reorganisation of the Lebanese University), vested the tasks performed by the Central Inspection Board, in so far as concerns the technical and administrative employees of the University, in the University Council, which requires recommending that the said Council take the required legal measures against Messrs. .......... in the light of the provisions of Articles 54 and 55 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 and its amendments (Personnel Regulations) and the provisions of Article 18 of Decision No. 706/M.J/99 (Special Regulations for Hired Workers of the Lebanese University).

After deliberation, and in the light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided 1 - To recommend to the Council of the Lebanese University the following: a - Taking the required legal measures against each of Messrs.:.......... at the Lebanese University,.......... at the Lebanese University for the reasons set forth in the body of this decision. b - Issuing a collection order in the name of Mr........... in the amount of / 17544255/ Lebanese Pounds, in favour of the Lebanese University. c - Forming a committee entrusted with the matter of correcting the entries relating to the names of the students registered in the Faculty of Letters and Human Sciences - First Branch - and their specialisations, stated in the financial receipts in the academic year 99 - 2000 and comparing them with the names listed in the registers and the nominal computer lists, and ascertaining the fate of the entries of /28/ students, whose names were stated in the registers adopted by the Faculty in excess of the total names stated in the nominal computer lists. 2 - To refer Mr........... before the Court of Accounts. A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the sixteenth of the month of April of the year two thousand and three.

Secretariat of the Board Session: 17/2003 Item: 2 Decision No. 213/2003 The Central Inspection Board, Having perused the file of the case registered under No. 51/3B/2002 3665/W2001 in all its contents. _____________ ________________ 71/7B/2003 698/W2003 Having perused the reports of the Inspectors: the Administrative Inspector, Mr. Afif Rizk, dated 17/9/2002 and 12/10/2002, the Health Inspector, Dr. Riad Shaaban, dated 5/3/2003, and the Financial Inspector, Dr. Wafic Rihan, dated 27/3/2003 and 3/4/2003, as a result of the investigation into the violations committed at the Marjayoun Governmental Hospital.
