Having perused the two opinions of the Administrative Inspector General dated 18/9/2002 and 26/10/2002 Having perused the opinion of the Health, Social and Agricultural Inspector General dated 8/3/2003 Having perused the two opinions of the Financial Inspector General dated 28/3/2003 and 4/4/2003 Having perused the opinion of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Audit No. 142/1146 dated 8/4/2003 Having perused the opinion of the President of the Central Inspection dated 23/4/2003 Whereas it has been established that the Administrative Inspectorate General, the Health, Social and Agricultural Inspectorate General, and the Financial Inspectorate General, each within its respective competence, conducted an investigation into the violations committed at the Marjayoun Governmental Hospital, and that the Central Inspection Board examined all the reports drawn up by the aforementioned Inspectorates General, due to the unity of the subject matter. Whereas it has been established from the investigation that on 8 and 9/5/2001, and pursuant to the decision of the Board of Directors of the Marjayoun Governmental Hospital, a competitive examination was held to appoint employees at the aforementioned hospital, and based on the results yielded by this competitive examination, Decision No. 2/2001 dated 17/5/2001 was issued by the Chairman of the Board of Directors, pursuant to which (151) employees were appointed to medical, technical, administrative and financial positions; however, this decision was not based on the proposal of the Director of the hospital as stated in its recitals, since the executory formula of the agreement concluded between the Lebanese State, represented in the person of the Minister of Public Health, and Dr. .......... to perform the function of Director of the hospital, was granted on a date subsequent to the issuance of the aforementioned decision, which violates the provisions of Article Ten of Decree No. 12255 dated 21/5/98 (Regulations of Employees and Contractors in Public Institutions that Manage Public Hospitals), which stipulated that "the Board of Directors shall determine the conditions and regulations of competitive examinations upon the proposal of the Director or the Director General.....". Whereas it has been established that the appointments made pursuant to Decision No. 2/2001 issued by the Chairman of the Board of Directors, which came based on the results of the competitive examination held on 8 and 9/5/2001 (nursing positions), included the appointment of employees in technical, administrative and financial positions, which places those appointments outside the purpose for which the aforementioned competitive examination was held. Whereas it has been established that other appointments were made after the date on which the competitive examination referred to above was held, and that those appointments were not based on the provisions of Decree No. 12255 dated 21/5/98 (Regulations of Employees and Contractors in Public Institutions that Manage Public Hospitals), in addition to the fact that they entailed new financial burdens on the budget of the hospital.

And whereas it has been established that .......... of the hospital, and in his capacity as directly responsible for .........., entrusted the duties of this department to Dr. .........., pursuant to his Decision No. 37/2001 dated 24/8/2001, and fixed his monthly salary at one million six hundred thousand L.L., and also accredited in the same decision, in addition to Dr. .........., Dr. .........., and Dr. .........., as dentists at the hospital, without holding any competitive examinations and without the approval of the supervisory ministry pursuant to the provisions of the ninth article of Decree No. 12255/98, which provided that "no person may be employed except pursuant to a competitive examination, unless the Board of Directors decides, exceptionally and after stating reasons, otherwise with respect to physicians, in which case the appointment shall be made after the approval of the supervisory minister, and no person may be appointed except to a vacant position, which requires reconsidering the content of this decision in the light of the provisions of the aforementioned article. And whereas it has been established that the President of .......... permitted Dr. .......... to withdraw an amount of six million L.L. from the hospital cash custody in violation of the administrative and financial rules defined by Decree No. 12399 dated 23/6/98 (the Financial Regulations of the Hospital), and that the aforementioned amount was returned following the objection of the Director of the Hospital - at the time - to the matter. And whereas it has been established that a number of employees of the Ministry of Public Health work at the Marjeyoun Governmental Hospital, even though their attachment to the aforementioned hospital does not conform to the administrative and legal rules in force, and that those employees, in addition to their salaries which they receive from the budget of their ministry, were receiving, with the approval of .........., fee allowances from the budget of the hospital even though they do not perform any additional work outside their duties, which requires recommending action to regularise the employment status of those employees, in accordance with the rules. And whereas it has been established that .......... formed, unilaterally, a procurement committee and appointed a chairman for it and intervened in its work, however this committee ceased work at the end of the month of July of the year 2002, which requires recommending the formation of a new committee for procurement in accordance with the rules. And whereas it has been established .........., approved certain purchases pertaining to the operating room, at prices higher than the prevailing prices and in violation of the adopted rules, and approved their receipt despite the objection of each of .......... the Administration .......... to that. However, the intervention of .......... and his contact with the bidding companies led to a noticeable reduction in the prices. And whereas it has been established that there exist invoices in the name of the Marjeyoun Governmental Hospital paid to a private establishment, which relate to the purchase of cellular devices and their accessories for each of .......... and the aforementioned Dr. .........., above, in addition to an invoice for telephone calls paid from the hospital fund for the account of Dr. .......... himself, bearing his personal telephone number, which indicates the use of public funds to achieve personal benefits, which requires recommending the recovery of the value of those invoices that were paid without right. And whereas it has been established that .......... has been abstaining from attending the sessions of the Board since the month of December of the year 2002, despite the repeated invitations to him by .......... the Board of Directors .........., which reflects negatively on the proper performance of this vital public facility, and threatens the regularity of work therein, particularly in light of the mutual accusations among its various parties, which requires recommending the continued holding of the meetings of the Board of Directors until the matter is decided upon by the concerned authorities.

Whereas it was established that the number of personnel working at the Marjayoun Governmental Hospital has reached one hundred and fifty-four employees, in addition to fifteen civil servants from the Ministry of Public Health who were attached to the Hospital irregularly as indicated above, and that thirty-five civil servants working in the nursing, radiology and laboratory staff do not possess the practical qualifications and the requirements for practising the profession legally, in addition to the presence of twenty civil servants whose ages exceed forty-four years who were appointed without the approval of the Board of Directors and the competent authorities, contrary to the provisions of Decree No. 12255/98 (Regulations for Employees and Contractors in Public Institutions that Manage Public Hospitals); moreover, despite the large number of personnel, which exceeds the actual need of the Hospital, certain positions, particularly in the nursing department, the medical staff, the maternity department and the radiology department, are still in need of a number of employees. Whereas it was established that the monthly expenditures of the Marjayoun Governmental Hospital exceed one hundred and fifty million L.L., including salaries, wages and allowances which amount to one hundred million L.L. monthly, whereas its monthly revenues do not exceed thirty-five million L.L., a matter which calls for reconsidering the recruitment policy and the work mechanism followed and rationalising expenditure in accordance with the provisions of the fifth Article of Decree No. 11214 dated 29/10/97 (determining the conditions for appointing a Board of Directors and a Government Commissioner for each governmental hospital and determining the duties and powers of each of them), which provided that "if the expenditures of the Institution exceed its revenues, the Board of Directors shall be responsible for controlling expenditure, by reconsidering the recruitment policy and the work mechanism...". Whereas, in view of the foregoing, it is necessary to recommend the formation of a special investigation committee to follow up on the conditions of the Marjayoun Governmental Hospital, determine responsibilities, regularise the status of the personnel working therein and improve financial and administrative work procedures. Whereas the actions committed by.......... of the Marjayoun Governmental Hospital.........., namely issuing appointment decisions contrary to due process, taking a decision to appoint.......... and interfering in the work of this committee, and approving the purchase of medical equipment and supplies at prices exceeding prevailing prices, in addition to purchasing cellular telephone devices and their accessories and paying bills from the Hospital's fund, have caused damage to public funds, which necessitates referring him before the Court of Accounts pursuant to the provisions of Articles 60 and 61 of its Law of Organisation. Whereas the presence of.......... at the Marjayoun Governmental Hospital was not established, despite the fact that the Financial Regulations for Public Institutions that Manage Public Hospitals, issued pursuant to Decree No. 12399 dated 23/6/98, required submitting decisions to open additional appropriations for the approval of the Ministry of Finance through.......... and also indicated the necessity of the approval of.......... for transferring appropriations from one paragraph to another.........., and whereas Law No. 544 dated 24/7/96 and its amendments (establishing public institutions to manage the hospitals of the Ministry of Public Health) provided in its first Article that those public institutions shall be subject to the provisions of Decree No. 4517/72 relating to the General Regulations for Public Institutions, which provided for the secondment of.......... by the Minister of Finance to each public institution, which necessitates recommending that both the Ministries of Public Health and Finance endeavour to second.......... to the Marjayoun Governmental Hospital and all other public institutions that manage governmental hospitals, in order to control the financial conditions therein and consequently improve the level of administrative performance.

Whereas it appeared, with regard to the complaint submitted by Ms. .......... at Marjayoun Governmental Hospital concerning the failure to calculate her end-of-service indemnity and transportation allowances upon the settlement of her entitlements at the said hospital, that the Financial Affairs Department at the hospital, following the acceptance of her resignation, settled and paid all her entitlements (lump-sum fee allowances including transportation allowances), and that the said lady received the amounts due to her with the exception of the end-of-service indemnity. Whereas the Lebanese Labour Law defined the end-of-service indemnity as "the indemnity due to the employee on the occasion of leaving work, whatever the reason calling therefor..." and the employee receives this indemnity from the National Social Security Fund; however, in the event that he is not affiliated with the said Fund for any reason whatsoever, the employee takes his indemnity directly from the employer, at the rate of one month for each year of service, and at the rate of half a month for a fraction of a year, on the basis of the last basic wage paid prior to leaving work, including fixed allowances which are legally considered an integral part of the wage. Whereas it is required, given that Ms. .......... was not affiliated with the National Social Security Fund, to recommend to the Board of Directors of Marjayoun Governmental Hospital to work on recalculating her end-of-service indemnity in accordance with the provisions of the Lebanese Labour Law, and to notify the concerned party of the possibility of submitting an objection before the Arbitral Labour Councils in the event of disagreement with the hospital administration over this calculation process. Following deliberation, and in light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided: 1 - To refer .......... of Marjayoun Governmental Hospital, .........., before the Court of Audit.

2 - Recommending to the Board of Directors of Marjeyoun Governmental Hospital to work on the following: a - Holding periodic meetings of the Board of Directors, pending a decision on the matter of reconstituting it through legal and administrative means, in order to preserve the continuity of the work of this vital institution. b - Reconsidering the recruitment policy and the followed work mechanism, and rationalising expenditure in accordance with the provisions of the laws and regulations in force. c - Forming a new procurement committee in accordance with the rules. d - Reconsidering the content of Decision No. 37/2001 dated 24 /8/2001 issued by the Chairman of the Board of Directors contrary to the rules. e - Recovering the amounts unduly paid on behalf of.........., from the fund of the hospital, in return for the purchase and service charges of his private cellular telephone in accordance with what is set forth in the body of this decision. f - Recovering the amounts paid from the fund of the hospital in return for the purchase of cellular telephone devices and accessories for the use of.......... g - Recalculating the end-of-service indemnity due to the assistant nurse Mrs........... in accordance with the provisions of the Lebanese Labour Law. 3 - Recommending to the Ministry of Public Health - Directorate General of Health - to work on the following: a - Forming a special investigation committee to follow up on the conditions of Marjeyoun Governmental Hospital, determine responsibilities, rectify the status of the workers therein, and improve administrative and financial work procedures. b - Considering the possibility of appointing.......... Marjeyoun Governmental Hospital in order to ensure the regularity of work in the aforementioned facility. c - Regularising the status of the employees attached to Marjeyoun Governmental Hospital contrary to the rules. d - Seeking with the Ministry of Finance to second.......... to Marjeyoun Governmental Hospital and to all other similar public institutions. 4 - Closing the case with respect to all other points. A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the seventh of the month of May of the year two thousand and three.

Secretariat of the Board Session: 18/2003 Item: 3 Decision No. 225/2003 The Central Inspection Board, having perused the file of the case registered under No. 51/7/2002 with all its contents.

72/3B/2002 Having perused the report of the Administrative Inspector Mr. Naji Mustafa dated 28/9/2002, concerning the result of the inspection of the Tyre Telephone Operation Section. Having perused the opinion of the Administrative Inspector General dated 7/11 /2002 Having perused the report of the Financial Inspectors Mr. Mohammad Salim Tabbara and Miss Badia Al-Khoury dated 10/1/2003, concerning the violation attributed to Mr........... of Tyre Telephone, with respect to encumbering his liability with amounts he did not pay to the Central Bank. Having perused the opinion of the Financial Inspector General dated 12/3/ 2003 Having perused the two opinions of the Public Prosecution of the Court of Accounts No. 460/3885 dated 17/12/2002, and No. 148/1161 dated 14/4/2003 Having perused the two opinions of the President of the Central Inspection dated 31/12/2002 and 29/4/2003 And whereas it has been established that the Director General of Operation and Maintenance of Wired and Wireless Telecommunications at the Ministry of Telecommunications deposited with the Central Inspection, pursuant to his letter No. 6878/1 S dated 5/10/ 2002, the preliminary investigations conducted by the competent administration regarding the embezzlement of public funds by.......... of Tyre Telephone, requesting completion and the taking of the appropriate measures. Whereupon the President of the Central Inspection issued an assignment under No. 51/7/2002 to investigate the matter. And whereas it has been established as a result of the investigation that.......... of Tyre Telephone, Mr..........., carried out, starting from the end of the year 2001, reversal operations on subscribers' invoices, which he would subsequently settle by carrying out new reversals on other invoices. And these reversals accumulated with him, such that he was compelled to retain for himself the receipts of the two days of 6 and 9 September 2002, amounting in value to /147385200/ L.L., one hundred and forty-seven million, three hundred and eighty-five thousand, and two hundred Lebanese Pounds, which he did not deliver at the time to the branch of the Central Bank in Tyre, with the aim of settling the values of the aforementioned reversals and covering up his act. Furthermore, he did not inform his superiors or his assistants of the reversal operations that had taken place, a matter which violates the provisions of the circulars and texts issued by the Ministry of Telecommunications in this regard, most notably Circular No. 78/Sh.M dated 25/2/94, and the two Memoranda No. 987/Sh.M dated 16/11/99 and No. 1555/Sh.M dated 30/8/2001, which require not allowing cashiers to carry out reversal operations for any reason whatsoever or prior to referring back to the administration, and also violates the provisions of Article 14 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 and its amendments (Personnel Regulations), which obligate the employee to be guided by the public interest in his work, and to ensure the application of the laws and regulations without any transgression, violation or negligence, and conflicts with the provisions of Articles 182 et seq. of the Public Accounting Law, and consequently constitutes a financial violation falling under the penalty of Articles 60 and 61 of the Law on the Organization of the Court of Accounts, which entails disciplinary and financial liability on his part in this regard. And whereas what was stated in the record of his interrogation and in his written defence is not such as to exempt him from liability, a matter which requires taking the appropriate disciplinary measures against him pursuant to the provisions of Articles 54 and 55 of the Personnel Regulations, read in conjunction with the provisions of the articles of Law No. 82/ 83 concerning the organization of the Court of Accounts.

And whereas it has been established that the Department of Financial Affairs reported, by its letter No. 1901/Sh.M. dated 26/2/2003, that Mr.......... had paid the full amounts due from him, such that he was deemed discharged of liability, and furthermore that the Criminal Court of Tyre has taken cognizance of the case that is the subject of this decision, which requires communicating to the Public Prosecution at the Court of Cassation a copy of all the documents of the file in connection with the criminal investigations being conducted by the competent judiciary. And after deliberation, and in the light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided 1 - To delay the step advancement of.......... of Tyre Telephone, Mr.......... (his financial number..........) for a period of twenty-four months as a disciplinary measure, and to refer him before both the Higher Disciplinary Board and the Court of Audit. 2 - To deduct the salary of.......... of Tyre, Mr.......... (his financial number..........) for seven days as a disciplinary measure. 3 - To deduct the salary of.......... of Exploitation, Mr.......... (his financial number..........) for two days as a disciplinary measure. 4 - To dispense with the liability of.......... of South Lebanon, Mr.......... 5 - To lodge a copy of the entire investigation file with the Public Prosecution at the Court of Cassation in connection with the investigations underway in this regard before the Criminal Court of Tyre in the public action brought against Mr.......... A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the fourteenth of the month of May in the year two thousand and three.

Whereas it has been established that .......... of Tyre Telephone, Mr. .........., neglected his official duties by failing to exercise his hierarchical supervision over .......... Mr. .........., particularly with regard to failing to audit the daily statements of receipts sent to him at the end of every working day, which allowed Mr. .......... to persist in the violation, and he has thereby violated the provisions of the tenth paragraph of the second Article of Decision No. 335/1 issued by the Minister of Telecommunications on 31/12/80, which requires the operating offices to audit and organise the accounting and statistical statements of telephone calls... and of the bills collected by them, and also violated the provisions of the eighth Article of Legislative Decree No. 111/59, which requires the head of the administrative unit to ensure the proper performance by the employees subordinate to him of the tasks entrusted to them and to be responsible for the works of the units subordinate to him, read in conjunction with the provisions of Article 14 of the Staff Regulations, and that what was stated in his written defence to the effect that he did not notice the apparent reversal in the daily statements of receipts due to the accumulation of work is not such as to exempt him from liability, especially since the statement of receipts consists of a single page and sometimes a few pages, which requires taking the appropriate disciplinary measures against him, pursuant to the provisions of Articles 54 and 55 of the Staff Regulations. And whereas it has been established that .......... Mr. .........., neglected, in turn, his supervisory official duties, except that what was stated in the record of his interrogation and in his written defence, with regard to the absence of accounting employees in his department, and the limitation of his task to conducting the reconciliation operation between receipts and payments and verifying the soundness thereof, which is carried out by a single employee under him and under his supervision, is such as to mitigate his liability rather than eliminate it, a matter which necessitates taking disciplinary measures against him, pursuant to the provisions of Articles 54 and 55 of the Staff Regulations. And whereas it has been established that the provisions of Regulatory Decree No. 3585/80, as well as Decisions No. 332 and No. 335/80, defined the mechanism for completing, auditing and supervising financial statements at the Financial Affairs Service, through the Cash Offices Supervision Department therein in coordination with the Revenue Departments and the Operating Offices Departments, except that it cannot ascertain the existence of reversal operations in the bills except by conducting a field audit in the various cash offices spread across the regions and numbering 120 cash offices, a matter which is practically impossible, which allows for not establishing disciplinary liability against .......... Mrs. .......... and against .......... of South Lebanon, Mr. .......... especially since the competent administration, after exercising its powers, has taken certain disciplinary measures against the assistant treasurers, which are considered sufficient in themselves.

Secretariat of the Board Session: 21/2003 Item: 5 Decision No. 259/2003 The Central Inspection Board, having perused the file of the case registered under No. 38/7/99 with all its contents.

83/99 Having perused the report of the Financial Inspector Mr. Abdel Sattar Al-Ayoubi dated 26/12/2002, resulting from the investigation into violations relating to invoices and prices by certain employees of the Mutual Fund for Members of the Teaching Staff at the Lebanese University. Having perused the opinion of the Financial Inspector General dated 20/2/ 2003 Having perused the opinion of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Accounts No. 147/1145 dated 14/4/2003 Having perused the opinion of the President of the Central Inspection dated 29 /4/2003 Whereas it appeared from the documents of the file that a complaint was received by the Central Inspection, indicating the existence of violations in the Mutual Fund for Members of the Teaching Staff at the Lebanese University, relating to the payment of sums of money to fictitious names, and the inappropriateness of the purchase prices of certain materials, and the President of the Central Inspection issued Assignment No. 38/ 7/99 to investigate the matter. Whereas it appeared as a result of the investigation that.......... Dr........... used to sign certain purchase authorisation transactions and insist on their disbursement contrary to the provisions of the Financial Regulations of the Fund which provide for the necessity of submitting them to the Board of Directors when the endorsement thereof is refused by.........., and he also signed payment orders No. 1113 and 1369 in the name of the two ladies.........., considering them as seconded from the Civil Servants Cooperative, whereas they have no relation to the Cooperative, and he also used to assign workers to enter and code information based on the proposal of.........., contrary to what he stated in his interrogation that the workers in the computer department perform their work under the supervision of.........., and he did not act to notify the competent judicial authorities of the acts committed by.......... Mr........... of destroying documents and computer disks belonging to the Fund and he did not act to submit these violations occurring in the Fund to the Board of Directors to take the necessary legal measures in respect thereof. Whereas what Dr........... committed constitutes a violation of the provisions of Article 14 of the Personnel Regulations, and what was stated in the minutes of his interrogation and in his written defence is not such as to exempt him from liability, which requires taking the appropriate disciplinary measures against him pursuant to the provisions of Articles 54 and 55 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 dated 12/6/59 and its amendments. Whereas it appeared that.........., in the Mutual Fund for Members of the Teaching Staff at the Lebanese University,.......... used to endorse certain transactions contrary to the provisions of Article 33 of the Financial Regulations of the Fund, and transactions considered as splitting of expenditure without drawing the attention of the Director and the concerned authorities, notably the Court of Accounts, to the occurring violation, in addition to his writing the phrase "provided that it is disbursed for one last time", and this matter was repeated several times, in order to cover illegal employment cases, which constitutes a disciplinary violation for his breach of his functional duties, and what he stated in his written defence and the minutes of his interrogation is not such as to exempt him from liability, which requires taking the appropriate disciplinary measures against him pursuant to the provisions of Article 25 of Decree No. 5883 dated 3/11/94 and its amendments (General Regulations for Hired Workers).

Following deliberation, and in the light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided: 1 - To delay the advancement in grade of .......... members of the teaching staff at the Lebanese University (his financial number ..........) for a period of four months as a disciplinary measure. 2 - To delay the periodic increment of .......... the Mutual Fund, Mr. .......... for a period of two months as a disciplinary measure. 3 - To deduct the salary of Mr. ........... seconded to the Mutual Fund for three days as a disciplinary measure. 4 - To deduct the salary of Miss .......... (her financial number ..........) for one day as a disciplinary measure. 5 - To deduct the salary of Mrs. .......... for one day as a disciplinary measure. 6 - To refer a copy of the entire file to the Cassation Public Prosecution. 7 - To refer a copy of the entire file to the Court of Accounts pursuant to the submission of the Public Prosecution attached thereto. A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the fourth of June of the year two thousand and three.

Whereas it has been established that .......... - at the time - Mr. .......... Al-Qarout signed a purchase authorisation pertaining to Mr. .......... and the liquidation invoice pertaining thereto despite its not being signed by the person concerned, and also signed a payment order which .......... refused to endorse, which violates the provisions of Article 33 of the Financial Regulations applicable at the Fund, and violates the provisions of Article 14 of the Personnel Regulations, and that what he stated in the minutes of his interrogation and in his written defence is not such as to exempt him from liability, which requires taking disciplinary measures against him pursuant to the provisions of Articles 54 and 55 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 dated 12/6/59, as amended. Whereas it has been established that Mrs. .......... at the Lebanese University, seconded to the Mutual Fund, and Miss .......... at the Fund, were appointed to the Price Estimation Committee, and were signing purchase authorisation transactions as a mere formality and did not endeavour to ascertain the reality of what the Purchasing Committee was doing with regard to the appropriateness of prices, and did not notify .......... of the Fund and the Board of Directors of this fact, which constitutes a violation of their functional duties pursuant to the provisions of Article 14 of the Personnel Regulations with respect to Mrs. .........., and to the provisions of the General Regulations .......... with respect to Miss .........., and that what was stated in the minutes of their interrogation and in their written defences is such as to mitigate their liability and not to exempt them therefrom, which requires taking the appropriate disciplinary measures against them pursuant to the provisions of Articles 54 and 55 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59, as amended, with respect to Mrs. .........., and pursuant to the provisions of the General Regulations .......... with respect to Miss .......... Whereas it has been established as a result of the investigation that the workers at the Fund did not recognise some of the persons who worked as data entry clerks, namely Messrs.: .........., and amounts of three million pounds were disbursed to each one of them, without any actual presence of theirs at the Fund, and furthermore Mrs. .........., who worked for one month at the Fund, namely the month of August of the year 1999, did not sign any invoice, and that the signature pertaining to liquidation transaction No. 73/76 is not her signature according to what she stated, and Miss .......... considered that she knew nothing about the money order issued in her name on 14/12/98 under No. 1369 and that she was forced to sign it and did not receive any amount therefrom, in addition to the fact that .......... Mr. .......... proceeded to destroy some documents and computer disks at the Fund prior to submitting his resignation, and the management of the Fund did not take any measure against him, and that these acts referred to above may constitute criminal offences, which requires depositing a copy of the entire file with the Public Prosecution at the Court of Cassation. Whereas it has been established that the Public Prosecution at the Court of Accounts opined in its submission No. 147/1145 to prosecute each of .......... of the Mutual Fund for Members of the Teaching Staff at the Lebanese University, .......... Dr. .......... and Messrs.: .........., pursuant to the provisions of Article 60 of the Law organising it, which requires depositing a copy of the entire file with the Court of Accounts to take whatever action it deems appropriate in this regard.

Secretariat of the Board Session: 30/2003 Item: 5 Decision No. 363/2003 The Central Inspection Board, having perused the file of the case registered under No. 35/7/2001 in all its contents.

And 1925/ 2001 Having perused the two reports of the Financial Inspectors, Ms. Badiaa El-Khoury and Mr. Naji Shaaban, dated 16/5/2003 and 23/6/ 2003, resulting from the investigation into the violations attributed to .......... Assistant Controller Mr. .......... with regard to his embezzlement of public funds from the cash office of the accounting unit of the aforementioned office. Having perused the opinion of the Financial Inspector General dated 26/6/ 2003 Having perused the opinion of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Accounts No. 423/2043 dated 15/7/2003 Having perused the opinion of the President of the Central Inspection dated 21 /7/2003 And whereas it appeared from the documents of the file that .......... deposited with the Central Inspection, pursuant to his letter No. 27/Confidential/2001 dated 19/6 /2001, a copy of the minutes of verification of the assets of the cash office custody of the Customs Office of .........., following which it appeared that the aforementioned .........., Assistant Controller .........., embezzled an amount of /138897000/ L.L. and departed the Lebanese territories heading to Cyprus, requesting that the necessary investigation be conducted so that appropriate action be taken accordingly, indicating in his letter set out above that he notified the Public Prosecution of the matter for the necessary judicial prosecution, and that he assigned the Control Service to carry out the required administrative investigations, and Assignment No. 35/7/2001 was issued to investigate the matter. And whereas it appeared from the investigation that the Assistant Controller in the Customs Administration, Mr. .........., was transferred from the Accounting Department at the Port to the Customs Office of .......... pursuant to Decision No. 19/ 99 for disciplinary reasons, where his handling of public funds capabilities continued without taking into consideration his official misconduct, and without his having submitted any legal bond or taken the legal oath before the Court of Accounts in implementation of the provisions of Article 169 of the Public Accounting Law, and that the aforementioned Controller embezzled approximately /170/ million Lebanese pounds of public funds in the Customs Office of .........., then disappeared from sight on the night of 14 June of the year 2001 And whereas it appeared that .......... of the Customs Office of .........., Mr. .........., assumed by himself alone both operations of registering the declarations in their special register and detaching the receipts for the duties pertaining thereto simultaneously, which enabled him to carry out the embezzlement operation, in addition to his taking possession of the receipts delivered to the office, used and unused, and his sole receipt of the keys to the safe, and his enjoyment of the freedom to dispose of the public funds collected from the duties, and his refusal to accept those duties except in cash and his failure to transfer them to the Bank of Lebanon in accordance with the rules and his retention thereof in large amounts and for a long period, contrary to the provisions of Article 192 of the Public Accounting Law, in the absence of any effective supervision by his hierarchical superiors over the manner in which he performed the duties of his office.

Whereas it appeared that .......... of .......... Customs, the Controller Mr. .........., refused to accept customs duties by way of a cheque presented to him by a customs clearing agent, requesting that payment be made in cash on the pretext that his signature was unknown to the Banque du Liban, without requesting that the cheque be drawn in the name of the Central Customs Accountant in accordance with the rules, and he also failed to comply with the provisions of Decision No. 551/S 16/ 97, which provides that cash assets shall not exceed five million Lebanese pounds, and which was duly notified to the office over which he presides, and that what was stated by Mr. Oweida, regarding his not having been officially notified of Decision No. 551/S 16/97, does not correspond to reality, as the aforementioned Decision was registered in the incoming register adopted at the office under No. 600 dated 5/6/ 1997 And whereas it appeared that Mr. .......... placed all the receipts pertaining to the collection of duties at the disposal of .......... without taking into consideration the principle of separation between administrative operations and accounting operations, which enabled .......... to detach two receipts from outside the regular sequence, and to mislead the process of exercising accounting control over the operations of the latter, and that what was stated by Mr. .......... that his assignment of most administrative and accounting duties to .......... was due to the absence of another employee at the Jounieh office, cannot be relied upon in light of his having been personally assigned as a local .......... for the aforementioned office by the Customs Administration. And whereas it appeared that Mr. .......... failed to comply with the provisions of Articles: 159 - 160 - 163 - 164 - 166 of the Public Accounting Law, which require the .......... to secure collection operations for the account of the Treasury, and consider him responsible for budget revenues, keeping the accounts of public funds, recording the operations pertaining thereto, securing receipts of whatever kind, and preserving the supporting documents pertaining to those operations, considering himself a de facto .......... and not a titular .........., which cannot be accepted due to the inadmissibility of his refraining from performing his duties as a de facto .......... to whom applies that which applies to the titular .........., pursuant to the provisions of Article 181 of the Public Accounting Law. And whereas it appeared that Mr. .........., assigned by the Customs Administration as a local .......... for the Jounieh Customs Office, did not submit the statutory bond, nor did he take the statutory oath before the Court of Accounts, thereby violating the provisions of Article 169 of the Public Accounting Law, and Article 11 of Decision No. 430/1 issued by the Minister of Finance on 6/6/74, which requires the submission of a bond by every employee assigned to perform the duties of the post of .......... even if such assignment is made on a temporary basis, and that what was stated by Mr. .......... regarding his lack of knowledge that he occupied the post of local .......... cannot be invoked by him, particularly since he used to draw up the annual closing minutes of his accounts and the weekly accounting reports which were drawn up by him personally or in his presence. And whereas it appeared that the texts in force in the Customs Administration oblige every customs .......... to prepare quarterly administrative and accounting reports to be submitted to the Directorate General through the Regional Director, as well as to prepare weekly accounting reports to be submitted directly to .......... the Principal Receivership in accordance with the provisions of Memorandum No. 2671/1 R B/96 dated 31/12/96, which indicates that all .......... the Central, were aware, on a periodic basis, of the cash assets in the offices and centres, including the cash box of the Jounieh office, which gives rise to their responsibility for failing to hold accountable both the aforementioned .......... and .......... for the excesses occurring therein, and raises the question as to the reason why the assets of this office in public funds reached the limit of /140/ million Lebanese pounds without being transferred to the Banque du Liban or to the Treasury coffers.

Whereas it has been established that.......... Mr........... did not draw attention to the infringement occurring in the Jounieh Customs Office, regarding the amounts retained exceeding the limits set pursuant to the law, during his undertaking of an inspection tour at the said office and his initialling of its accounting registers, despite the fact that the quarterly reports which he prepared were reaching, on time, their hierarchical authorities, including the two quarterly reports, the last quarter of the year 2000, and the first quarter of the year 2001, which both clearly indicated a notable exceeding of the limits permitted to be retained in the cashbox of the Jounieh office, thereby violating the provisions of Article Eight of Legislative Decree No. 111/59, and the content of Memorandum No. 9031/96, issued by the Director General of Customs on 26/1/96, which imposes upon.......... the undertaking of auditing.........., and the operations of the customs offices, even on a documentary basis, through the quarterly reports that reach him regularly, as well as the provisions of Decision No. 551/S 16/97 which Mr........... personally undertook to notify to the customs offices where he occupied at the time, the position of central.......... of the Customs Administration. And whereas it has been established that.......... Mr........... audited and initialled the two quarterly reports pertaining to the Jounieh Customs Office for the last quarter of the year 2000 and the first quarter of the year 2001 in acknowledgment by him of their validity, despite the clear exceeding that marred them in the assets of the cashbox which reached the limits of /140/ million Lebanese pounds in cash, thereby violating the provisions of the Public Accounting Decision No. 551/S 16/97, and the content of Memorandum No. 55/64 which stipulated that the works of.......... in the customs offices shall cover the auditing of all transactions including the cashbox and accounting operations for the purpose of verifying their conformity with the laws and regulations in force, noting that the quarterly reports, all of them, were presented continuously and periodically to Mr..........., since the attachment of.......... Mr........... to the office on 10/11/99, with the exceeding in the assets of the cashbox that marred them, without Mr........... taking the initiative to draw the attention of.......... to this exceeding, or to any legal measure against them both pursuant to the provisions of the laws and regulations in force. And whereas it has been established that Mr........... had his services terminated effective from the date of 1/7/2003 pursuant to the Decision of the Board of the Civil Service Council No. 1225 dated 28/12/2002, and there is no longer any room to prosecute him disciplinarily for the violations committed by him. And whereas it has been established that the Central.......... in the Customs Administration, Mr........... was receiving the reports relating to the accounting statements in the journals of financial resources, submitted to him on Monday of every week by.......... Jounieh, in implementation of the content of Memorandum No. 2671/1 R B/96, issued by the Central.......... on 31/12/96, and without drawing attention to the exceedings occurring successively in the assets of the cashbox, and in particular the exceeding occurring in the report referred to him during the last week preceding the embezzlement operation where the value of the assets of the cashbox reached /140/ million Lebanese pounds, and furthermore Mr........... did not take any measure against each of.......... Jounieh Customs.......... therein, following his assignment of two controllers to examine the accounting of this office and the appearance of an increase in its assets that reached /12/ million Lebanese pounds in the year 99, and /107/ million Lebanese pounds in the year 2000, despite his being notified of the two reports drawn up by them both in accordance with the rules, in addition to the non-conduct of any inspection tour on his part of the works of the Main Treasury Department and the works of the local accountants subordinate to him, in implementation of the content of Memorandum No. 9031/96 which entrusted him with undertaking the aforementioned mission.

Whereas it has been established that Mr. .......... had his services terminated upon reaching the statutory age pursuant to Decision No. 275 issued by the Board of the Civil Service Council on 26/6/2002, and there is no longer any ground to prosecute him disciplinarily for the violations referred to above. Whereas it has been established that the two Assistant Controllers at the Principal Secretariat Department in the Customs Administration, Messrs. .........., were assigned to audit the revenues in the local accounting offices in the Customs Administration, provided that they submit periodic reports on the results of their work to the Head of the Department, pursuant to Memorandum No. 1402 issued by the Head of the Principal Secretariat Department on 8/5/ 2000, and that the two aforementioned Controllers did not audit the Jounieh accounting office in execution of the contents of the aforementioned memorandum, which necessitated holding them disciplinarily accountable by the Customs Administration by deducting the salary of each of them for five days as a disciplinary measure, which requires sufficing with this penalty taken against them, and referring them before the Court of Accounts pursuant to the provisions of Article 60 of the Law of its Organisation. Whereas it has been established that .......... indicated in his Letter No. 27/Confidential/ 2001 dated 19/6/2001, that he had notified the Financial Public Prosecution of the matter of the embezzlement that took place at the Jounieh Customs Office for the necessary judicial prosecution, and that the Indictment Chamber in Mount Lebanon decided to indict the Assistant Controller in the Customs Administration, Mr. .........., of the felony provided for in Articles 359 and 360 of the Penal Code, and to issue an arrest warrant against him for embezzling the customs duties the collection of which was entrusted to him, and for resorting to using receipts contrary to the numerical sequence required to be adopted, and for giving one of the customs declarations a fictitious number in order to conceal the operation of embezzlement, pursuant to its Decision No. 287/2002 dated 3/4/2002, and that the final judicial decision in the aforementioned embezzlement case has not been issued up to this date. Whereas the fifth paragraph of Article 61 of the Civil Servants Regulations provides that the public prosecution action is independent of the disciplinary action and the institution of the public prosecution action does not preclude the institution of the disciplinary action, proceeding therewith, and ruling thereon; however, the criminal judgment, even though it does not bind the disciplinary judgment with respect to the liabilities that may result therefrom, remains binding on the Administration not only with respect to the facts established thereby, but also with respect to the characterisation reached by the judge for these facts. Whereas the transgressions committed by the employees working at the Jounieh Customs Office and their hierarchical superiors, some of which are considered sufficiently established and in a manner that does not restrict the authority of the Administration, require taking the necessary disciplinary measures in respect thereof, pursuant to the provisions of Articles 54 and 55 of Legislative Decree No. 112 /59 and its amendments (Civil Servants Regulations), and transmitting the file to the competent judiciary, further to the investigations underway before it regarding the matter. Whereas the duties entrusted to the employees working at the Jounieh Customs Office and to their hierarchical superiors fall under the concept of the management of public funds, and the breach in managing those funds in a manner that caused damage and loss thereto falls under the provisions of the Law of Organisation of the Court of Accounts, which requires referring each of Messrs.: .........., before the Court of Accounts pursuant to the provisions of Articles 60 and 61 of the Law of its Organisation. Whereas the Controller in the Customs Administration, .......... Jounieh Customs, Mr. .........., by committing the violations referred to in the body of this Decision, has breached the duties of the public office, and Article Nineteen of Legislative Decree No. 115/59 (Establishment of the Central Inspection) vests the Central Inspection Board, after imposing the penalty, with referring the offending employee to the Higher Disciplinary Board. Whereas the Board deems, in light of the above, and after imposing the penalty against Mr. .........., to refer the latter before the Higher Disciplinary Board, pursuant to the provisions of Articles 14, 54, and 55 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 and its amendments (Civil Servants Regulations).

Whereas it appeared from the content of the decision of the esteemed Indictment Chamber in Mount Lebanon that the counsel of the Assistant Controller, Mr..........., filed a lawsuit before the Cassation Public Prosecution against Mr. Bassam Daoud (the partner of Mr........... in the (.......... nightclub) regarding disputed amounts, which necessitates recommending to the Customs Administration to task its counsel with working to join the said Administration in this lawsuit in order to preserve the rights of the Treasury in this context. And whereas it is required to recommend to the Customs Administration to take the necessary disciplinary measures against the Assistant Controller Mr..........., who has ceased practising his work in the said Administration with effect from 14 June of the year 2001, in light of the provisions of the Civil Servants Regulations and in particular the provisions of Article 65 thereof, which govern such a case. And after deliberation, and in light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided 1 - To delay the advancement in step of the Controller in the Customs Administration, Mr..........., born in 1949 (his financial number..........) for a period of eighteen months as a disciplinary measure and to refer him before the Higher Disciplinary Board. 2 - To deduct the salary of the First Controller in the Customs Administration,.......... Mr........... born in 1941 (his financial number..........) for ten days as a disciplinary measure. 3 - To transmit the file to the esteemed Cassation Public Prosecution further to the ongoing investigations regarding the matter. 4 - To refer each of Messrs.:.......... before the Court of Accounts. 5 - To reserve disciplinary liability against the two Messrs........... due to the termination of their services, in accordance with what was indicated in the body of this decision. 6 - To recommend to the esteemed Customs Administration the following: a - To examine the possibility of joining the Administration in the lawsuit brought by the counsel of Mr........... against Mr........... (the partner of Mr........... in the (.......... nightclub) regarding the disputed amounts, in order to preserve public funds. b - To take the necessary disciplinary measures against the Assistant Controller, Mr..........., who has ceased practising his work with effect from the date of 14 June 2001, in light of the provisions of Article 65 of the Civil Servants Regulations. A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the sixth of the month of August in the year two thousand and three.

Whereas it was established that .......... approved the provision by Dr. .......... of medical and surgical consultations to the Medical Committee at the Fund upon the request of the latter, pursuant to his letter No. 1006/S dated 29/6/99, and that Dr. .......... violated the capacity under which he was permitted to work, as he examined hospitalisation and medical treatment transactions, and visited patients in hospitals since he commenced work at the Fund in the month of October of the year 97, submitting invoices that included his examination of /100/ medical treatment transactions per month, and he also violated the Second Article of Law No. 6/70 dated 23/2/70, which authorised members of the teaching staff at the Lebanese University to carry out, in addition to their primary duties at the University, scientific, legal, literary, technical or other consultations, after notifying the administration of the faculty or institute, provided that they do not have a continuous character; thus, by this work of his, and pursuant to the provisions of Article 7 of Law No. 75/67 dated 26/12/67 and its amendments, relating to the reorganisation of the Lebanese University, Dr. .......... has violated his official duties defined in Article 14 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 and its amendments (Personnel Statute), which requires taking the appropriate disciplinary measures against him pursuant to the provisions of Article 4 of Decree No. 9333 dated 11/10/96, relating to the rules of trial of members of the teaching staff and members of the technical cadre before the Disciplinary Council at the Lebanese University, read in conjunction with the provisions of the final paragraph of Article 17 of Law No. 65/67 mentioned above. Whereas it was established that the working hours of the physicians working in the Medical Committee at the Mutual Fund for Members of the Teaching Staff at the Lebanese University were limited and not characterised by continuity and discipline, and that this situation was taking place with the knowledge of .......... which did not keep attendance registers, replacing that with special sheets effective from the date of 14/5/2001, despite attention having been drawn by the Inspection on 3/4/2001 to the necessity for physicians contracted with the Fund to adhere to working hours, and the necessity for them to sign the register upon their arrival and departure. And that the working hours of the physicians, according to the sheets referred to above, do not correspond with the content of the statement given by the Director of the Fund, with regard to the arrival of the physicians, their departure, and the days of their attendance, and in particular the working hours of the two physicians .......... at the Fund. Whereas it was established that there is duplication in the work relating to data entry into the computer of the Board of Directors of the Fund, such that numerous persons were employed in the year 98 to carry out this task, despite the fact that the two ladies .........., employed against an invoice, were performing this work, and a number of cleaning workers were employed at the Fund contrary to the rules, such that the value of the funds paid to these workers in the years: 97, 98, 99, 2000, and 2001 amounted to the equivalent of /113869800/ L.L., one hundred and thirteen million, eight hundred and sixty-nine thousand, and eight hundred Lebanese Pounds, and that the cost of the two floors occupied by the Fund escalated from one million Pounds per month, in the initial stage of its establishment, until it reached three million Pounds in a single month. Whereas it was established from the examination of the liquidation transactions taking place at the Mutual Fund for Members of the Teaching Staff at the Lebanese University, that there are numerous invoices submitted by some of those contracted with it, to provide studies and works for the benefit of the Fund, and that many of them were completed by Mr. .......... during the year 1997, and prior to the Fund contracting with the subsequent contractors, a matter which raises questions as to the reason for which the administration of the Fund commissioned different persons to carry out a study pertaining to a single subject, and the submission by these persons of invoices of different values in consideration of their carrying out the studies referred to, noting that the contracting that took place with one of them was effected contrary to the rules.

Secretariat of the Board Session: 36/2003 Item: 8 Decision No. 421/2003 The Central Inspection Board, having perused the file of the case registered under No. 69/7/2001 and 34/7/2002 in all its contents.

3693/W 2001 and 2155/W 2002 Having perused the report of the financial inspectors Ms. Batoul Choucair and Mr. Rabih Charafeddine dated 21/3/2003, as a result of the investigation into the conclusion of agreements by mutual consent and the commitment and disbursement of expenditures without the availability of the necessary appropriations therefor in the Sidon Port Exploitation Authority, contrary to the rules. Having perused the opinion of the Financial Inspector General dated 6/6/ 2003 Having perused the opinion of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Audit No. 414/1903 dated 27/6/2003 Having perused the opinion of the President of the Central Inspection dated 5/ 7/2003 And whereas it appeared from the documents of the file that the Minister of Finance notified the Central Inspection, pursuant to his letter No. 1791/S dated 30/ 10/2001, of a copy of his letter addressed to the Court of Audit relating to reporting a financial violation in the Sidon Port Exploitation Authority resulting from the conclusion of an agreement by mutual consent contrary to the provisions of Decree No. 6994 dated 11/7/1995, and also notified the Central Inspection, pursuant to his letter No. 955/S 16 dated 20/7/ 2002, of a copy of his letter addressed to the Court of Audit, relating to reporting a financial violation in the aforementioned Authority resulting from the commitment and disbursement of expenditures without the availability of the necessary appropriations therefor, and the two assignments No. 69/7/2001 and No. 34 /7/2002 were issued to investigate the matter. And whereas it appeared from the investigation that the Sidon Port Exploitation Authority was granted a treasury advance pursuant to Decree No. 6994 dated 11/7/1995 on account of its revenues from port fees, provided that the duration of the advance be one year from the date of its payment, and that it be repaid in cash, principal and interest, with the impermissibility of using it for other than the purpose for which it was granted, defined as covering the fees of Dar Al-Handasah and various administrative expenditures. And whereas it appeared that the Sidon Port Exploitation Authority did not repay the value of the advance granted to it pursuant to Decree No. 6994/95, however it was allocating and carrying over the necessary appropriations to repay its value without the availability of the necessary liquidity for that due to the scarcity of port revenues, especially since the collection of port fees began on 8/1 /96 according to what was shown by the audit of the schedules of the final accounts of the Authority pertaining to the years between 1996 and 2001, and that what was stated by each of.......... to justify the non-repayment of the advance on time may be taken into consideration and the case closed regarding their liability in this respect. And whereas it appeared that the Board of Directors of the Sidon Port Exploitation Authority approved, pursuant to its Decision No. 25 dated 31/1/97, coupled with the approval of the tutelage authority, the awarding to.......... Company of the contract for conducting geological drilling studies, in accordance with a special book of conditions drawn up by the consultant Dar Al-Handasah, however it contracted on 20/2/97, pursuant to a consensual agreement, with.........., to execute the aforementioned studies on the basis that this company is represented by.......... Company based on a letter issued by the latter, and without the existence of a legal document proving the validity of this representation, in fulfilment of the provisions of Article 29 of the Code of Commerce, which violates the provisions of Article 108 of the Financial Regulations of the Authority, which stipulate that the contract shall be provisionally awarded to the one who submitted the lowest prices or to the one who submitted the best offers, and also violates the provisions of the special book of conditions for the geological drilling works which do not permit subcontracting.

Whereas the financial irregularities consisting in the violation of the provisions relating to the management or use of public funds, which have been referred to in the body of this decision, are the responsibility of each of.......... the Board of Directors of the Sidon Port Exploitation Authority, namely Messrs.:.........., in addition to each of the two Messrs..........., which requires referring them before the Court of Accounts pursuant to the provisions of Article 60 of the Law organising it. Whereas it has been established that the studies carried out by each of the two companies.........., were all received through.......... Mr........... at the Sidon Port Exploitation Authority, due to the absence of a cadre belonging to the said Authority during the period between the commencement of the studies and their completion, which violates the provisions of Article 121 of the Financial Regulations in force at the Authority, which stipulate that supplies, works and services shall be received by a committee appointed by a decision of.......... and which may include among its members persons who are not employees at the Authority who possess experience and specialisation after the approval of the Board, which requires recommending working on forming the reception committee at the Authority in accordance with what is specified in its own Financial Regulations. Whereas it has been established that the state of unpaid Treasury advances is worsening due to the inability of public administrations and public institutions, including the Sidon Port Exploitation Authority, to repay, as the value of unpaid advances between the years 1991 and 2001 reached a total of /1725445721709/ L.L. (one thousand seven hundred and twenty-five billion, four hundred and forty-five million, seven hundred and twenty-one thousand, seven hundred and nine Lebanese pounds) out of the value of paid advances amounting to / 1776663282886/ L.L. (one thousand seven hundred and seventy-six billion, six hundred and sixty-three million, two hundred and eighty-two thousand, eight hundred and eighty-six Lebanese pounds). Whereas it has been established that Article Eighteen of the Budget Law for the year 2001 authorised the Government to postpone the collection of unpaid Treasury advances provided that the mechanism is determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance, however the said decree has not been issued up to this date, which requires recommending to the Ministry of Finance, Directorate General of Finance, to work on issuing the decree that determines the mechanism for postponing unpaid Treasury advances pursuant to the provisions of the Article referred to above. Whereas it is required to recommend to the Sidon Port Exploitation Authority to work on amending the Financial Regulations adopted by it with respect to subjecting mutual agreements to the provisions applicable to public tenders, especially the guarantee necessary to ensure the proper execution of works, and translating into Arabic the books of specifications and correspondence adopted at the Authority in order to facilitate oversight by the competent employees.

Whereas it was established that.......... at the Ministry of Social Affairs.......... at the Saida Port Exploitation Authority, endorsed the expenditure commitment requests by aggregating the appropriations in a lump sum as a precaution and from Whereas it was established that.......... at the Ministry of Social Affairs, Mr. .........., at the Saida Port Exploitation Authority, endorsed the expenditure commitment requests by aggregating the appropriations in a lump sum as a precaution and through a single commitment contrary to the provisions of Article 57 of the Financial Regulations specific to the Authority, which require the preparation of a separate appropriation commitment request whenever necessary, and he also endorsed the appropriation commitment request relating to the mutual agreement concluded with the company.........., contrary to the provisions of Article 59 of the aforementioned Financial Regulations, which stipulate that the purpose of the audit of.......... is to verify the conformity of the transaction with the laws and regulations, a matter which entails disciplinary liability on his part pursuant to the provisions of Article 14 of the Civil Servants Regulations issued by Legislative Decree No. 112/59 and its amendments, and whereas what was stated in the record of his interrogation and in his written defence does not absolve him of this liability, which requires taking the appropriate disciplinary measures against him pursuant to the provisions of Articles 54 and 55 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 and its amendments (Civil Servants Regulations). Whereas it was established that.......... at the Saida Port Exploitation Authority Mr. .........., was verbally assigned by.......... to carry out the duties of the liquidator at the said Authority in light of the impermissibility of combining the duties of.........., and that Mr. liquidated the expenditure relating to the mutual agreement with the two companies.......... without the availability of the required documents contrary to the provisions of Paragraph "c" of Article 67 of the Financial Regulations of the Authority, which stipulate that liquidation, with regard to supplies and works, shall be based on the documents capable of proving the debt, and he also approved the adoption of the cheque submitted by the company.......... as a guarantee for the geological drilling works, in breach of the Special Book of Conditions which specified the model of the bank guarantee to be adopted in this regard, a matter which entails disciplinary liability on his part pursuant to the provisions of Article Six of the Employees Regulations of the Authority, which required the employee, in general, to ensure the application of the laws and regulations without any transgression, violation or negligence, and whereas what was stated in the record of his interrogation and in his written defence does not absolve him of the liability resulting from the aforementioned violations, which requires taking the appropriate disciplinary measures against him pursuant to the provisions of Articles 41 and 42 of the Employees Regulations in force at the said Authority. Whereas it was established that.......... Saida Port Exploitation Mr. .........., approved contracting with the company.......... in a manner contrary to the rules, and the preparation of the contract relating to the first part of the consultancy studies with the company.......... prior to obtaining the approval of the tutelage minister, and submitted the appropriation commitment request to.......... in a lump sum and as a precaution, which prevented showing the existing and allocated amounts in the budget of the Authority in a clear manner, contrary to the provisions of Article 7 of the Financial Regulations of the Authority, and he also prepared and issued the payment orders relating to the mutual agreement concluded with the two companies.......... without complying with the provisions of Article 71 of the Financial Regulations of the Authority, which stipulate the impermissibility of issuing disbursement orders except after verifying the conformity of the liquidation transaction with the financial laws and regulations, or complying with the provisions of Article 73 of the same Regulations, which stipulate that the order shall be drawn up in the name of the creditor even if he appoints an agent or representative on his behalf to collect, in addition to his approval of the adoption of the cheque submitted by the company.......... as a guarantee for the geological drilling works despite this matter being contrary to the Special Book of Conditions which specified the model of the bank guarantee Employees in force at the Authority, and whereas what was stated by Mr. .......... in the record of his interrogation and in his written defence does not absolve him of liability. Which requires taking the appropriate disciplinary measures against him pursuant to the provisions of Articles 41 and 42 of the Employees Regulations referred to above.

Following deliberation, and in light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided: 1 - To deduct the salary of each of.......... Exploitation of the Port of Sidon, Mr..........., and Mr........... Nabaa Al-Tassa and its dependencies, the aforementioned Service, for five days as a disciplinary measure. 2 - To deduct the salary of Mr........... Service of Exploitation of the Port of Sidon (his financial number..........), for two days as a disciplinary measure. 3 - To refer each of Messrs........... Service of Exploitation of the Port of Sidon: and Messrs.:.........., before the Court of Audit. 4 - To recommend to the Service of Exploitation of the Port of Sidon the following: a - To work in accordance with due process to amend the financial regulations in force in the Service with regard to subjecting mutual agreement contracts to the provisions applicable to public tenders, particularly with regard to the guarantee required to ensure the proper execution of works. b - To translate into Arabic the books of specifications and correspondence adopted in the Service in order to facilitate the conduct of oversight by the competent employees. c - To abide by the principle of separation between administrative functions and accounting functions with regard to not combining the function of accountant with any function related to the commitment, liquidation, or disbursement of expenditures. d - To form the reception committee in the Service pursuant to the provisions stipulated in the financial regulations adopted therein. e - To reserve appropriations by the expenditure commitment controller in accordance with the provisions stipulated in the financial regulations adopted therein. 5 - To recommend to the Ministry of Finance - Directorate General of Finance - to work on issuing the decree aimed at determining the mechanism for postponing the collection of unpaid treasury advances pursuant to the provisions of Article Eighteen of the 2001 Budget Law, by a decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the twenty-fourth of the month of September in the year two thousand and three.

Secretariat of the Board Session: 39/2003 Item: 10 Decision No. 448/2003 The Central Inspection Board, Having perused the file of the case registered under Nos. 17/7/2002, 1/6/2002, 22/3/2002, and 28/3/2002, with all its contents. Having perused the two reports of the Administrative Inspectors, Messrs. Ali Al-Hajj Diab and Claude Al-Kassouf, and the Financial Inspector, Ms. Samia Daher, dated 31/12/2002, and 31/3/2003, on the result of the investigation into violations attributed to a number of employees working at the Ministry of Public Health. Having perused the report of the Engineering Inspectors, Mr. Younes Al-Rabih and Ms. Roula Abou Daher, dated 11/6/2003 Having perused the two reports of the Administrative Inspectors, Messrs. Ali Al-Hajj Diab and Claude Al-Kassouf, dated 16/6/2003 and 22/9/2003 Having perused the two opinions of the Financial Inspector General dated 7/5/2003 and 30/7/2003 Having perused the opinion of the Engineering Inspector General dated 13/6/2003 Having perused the opinions of the Administrative Inspector General dated 9/4/2003, 28/8/2003, and 29/9/2003 Having perused the opinion of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Audit No. 454/2563 dated 15/9/2003 Having perused the two opinions of the President of the Central Inspection dated 30/9/2003 and 8/10/2003 Whereas it appeared from the documents of the file that the Director General of the Presidency of the Council of Ministers deposited with the Central Inspection, pursuant to his letters Nos. 547/S dated 17/4/2002, 884/S dated 24/6/2002, and 1298/S dated 12/9/2002, three complaints relating to financial and administrative violations committed by certain employees working at the Ministry of Public Health, requesting that the necessary investigations be conducted in respect thereof, and the assignments bearing Nos. 17/7/2002, 1/6/2002, 22/3/2002, and 28/3/2002 were issued to investigate the matter. Whereas it appeared from the investigation that on 6/2/97 a purchase authorisation was drawn up for the supply and installation of a telephone switchboard at the Directorate of Medical Care affiliated with the Ministry of Public Health, and that on 31/3/98 another purchase authorisation was drawn up for the supply and installation of an electronic telephone switchboard at the same Directorate, and that.......... of Medical Care justified this matter on the ground that the telephone switchboard installed in the year 1997 would not have met the required need due to its inability to secure internal telephone communications with all the employees working at the Directorate of Medical Care, in addition to the breakdown of the said switchboard and the impossibility of repairing it at an acceptable cost, in accordance with what was stated in the letter of.......... of the Ministry No. 6092/2003 dated 23/7/2003, in the course of seeking clarification from him by the Presidency of the Central Inspection regarding this matter. And whereas it appeared that the Ministry of Public Health installed telephone switchboards in the year 1998 in certain of its units, pursuant to five purchase authorisations separated by closely spaced intervals, three of which were committed under the same budget line, which indicates that a splitting of expenditure took place, and that.......... of the Ministry justified the drawing up of the two authorisations made on 18/3/98 and 10/9/98 pertaining to the purchase of a telephone switchboard for the Department of Hospitals, Dispensaries and Medical Professions and another for his office, as being in fulfilment of a need that was not foreseen in advance, and that the other purchase authorisations were all accompanied by the signature of the Minister of Public Health, either in his capacity as the authority committing the expenditure or with respect to approving them in terms of need, and that the non-receipt of requests from the competent units at the beginning of the years 1997 and 1998 regarding the telephone switchboards prevented the purchase of all of them through a single regular transaction.

Whereas, notwithstanding that which was stated by .......... of the Ministry of Public Health and which may be taken into consideration, the splitting of expenditure in the manner described above occurred in violation of the provisions of Article 123 of the Public Accounting Law due to its not being based on a decision authorising it issued by the Minister of Public Health, which requires recommending that the Ministry of Public Health abide by the provisions of Article 123 of the Public Accounting Law and refrain from resorting to the splitting of expenditures save in the cases permitted by the legal and regulatory texts in force. Whereas each of .........., did not draw attention in writing to the occurrence of a splitting of expenditure regarding the subject of purchasing telephone exchanges and did not request the conducting of a regular transaction for the aforementioned exchanges, which requires recommending that the aforementioned employees be cautioned as to the necessity of abiding by the provisions of the laws and regulations in force when performing the duties of their positions. Whereas it appeared that the transactions concluded in the Ministry of Public Health during the years 1999 - 2000 - 2001 and 2002, were conducted in accordance with the procedures specified pursuant to the law and there is nothing that calls for observation in respect thereof. Whereas it appeared that the General Engineering Inspectorate conducted an investigation into the subject of wiretapping the telephones of the Head of the Department of Hospitals and Dispensaries and the Card Issuance Centre in the Ministry of Public Health, pursuant to which it appeared to it that the subject of wiretapping was untrue and that there is no other technical subject requiring investigation on its part in the Ministry. Whereas it appeared that certain departments, divisions and directorates affiliated with the Ministry of Public Health prepare purchase authorisations and refer them directly to the Diwan Department without passing through the Equipment and Supply Division in the Ministry, in violation of the provisions of the Eighth Article of the Law Organizing the Ministry of Public Health, which specified the concerns of the Equipment and Supply Division, including controlling the incoming and outgoing movement of supplies, clothing, equipment and furniture, and drawing up purchase authorisations for necessary materials, medicines and supplies not available in the warehouse, which requires recommending that the Ministry of Public Health circulate to all administrative units affiliated with it the necessity of abiding by the provisions of the Eighth Article referred to above. Whereas it appeared that the subject of the workers to the Artificial Kidney Centre, Aisha Bakkar, is handled by the Civil Service Board through a request to provide it with the names of all workers in the public administrations in order to determine the surplus of employees and distribute it among the public administrations according to need, and that the two contracted physicians in the aforementioned centre, Doctor .......... and Doctor .........., abide by the working hours in the centre, and that what was done by Doctor .......... with respect to advancing the time of attendance of patients at their request, does not affect the productivity of the work of the centre, and satisfies a humanitarian need that enables these patients to pursue their work as usual, which requires filing the case in this respect.
