Whereas it appeared that Doctor .......... settled the value of the emergency advances paid to him in the years 2000 and 2001 pursuant to invoices that were duly approved, and that the technical bids and samples submitted by the bidders within the framework of the public tender taking place at the Tenders Administration in the Central Inspection, which were studied by a number of experts in the light of the special book of conditions drawn up therefor and observe the recognised technical specifications, which indicates the untruthfulness of the allegation relating to the imposition of filters for kidney dialysis machines contrary to international specifications, and consequently calls for filing the case in this respect. Whereas it appeared that a public tender took place in the year 2000 for the purchase of the fluid used in the artificial kidney dialysis operation, which was awarded to the company .......... acceptable, in comparison with the prices specified in the previous purchase authorisations, which renders the allegation relating to the purchase of this fluid by mutual agreement from the aforementioned company and at multiples of its real price, unfounded.

And whereas it has been established that Mr. .......... received Complaint No. 398 registered in the Registry of the Bureau of the Ministry of Public Health without discharging it in the incoming and outgoing register, on the pretext of having sent it to the office of the Minister to be delivered to one of the interested parties in the same manner as other transactions that were delivered by him to the interested parties without obtaining their signatures thereon, which entails disciplinary liability on his part for which he must be prosecuted. And whereas nothing has been established from the record of interrogation of Mr. .......... or from his written defence that would exempt him from liability, which requires taking the appropriate disciplinary measures against him pursuant to the provisions of the laws and regulations in force. And whereas it is necessary to recommend to the Ministry of Public Health to take the necessary measures against .......... Mr. .......... for his unjustified absence from his duty station on 4/5/2001 And whereas it has been established that Mr. .......... undertakes clerical work in the Bureau of the Ministry of Public Health pursuant to a verbal assignment from .........., contrary to the provisions of the agreement signed between him and the Ministry of Public Health, which does not entrust him with performing such a task, which requires recommending that he be suspended from working in the capacity of .......... and requesting him to abide by the provisions of the agreement signed between him and the Ministry, in the capacity of .......... And whereas it has been established that the transaction of .......... in the Department of the Bureau of the Ministry of Public Health, Mr. .........., relating to his transfer to the Karantina Hospital was closed due to the establishment of a public institution to manage this hospital, and that the complaint submitted by .......... was closed due to the latter having submitted a request to withdraw it. And whereas it has been established that Dr. .........., the physician .......... with the Ministry of Public Health maintains working hours in accordance with the provisions of the contract signed with him, and that .......... in the Ministry of Public Health, the Dibbiyeh Governmental Dispensary, Mr. .........., abides by the official working hours and performs his duties in accordance with the rules. And whereas it has been established that Dr. .......... had previously been appointed .......... for the Reproductive Health Project carried out in cooperation between the Ministry of Public Health and the United Nations Population Fund between the years 1995 and 1999, and that during this period he was working .......... with the Ministry and ceased receiving any allowance from the Fund starting from the year 1999, the date of his appointment to the cadre of the Ministry of Public Health, and that the representative of the United Nations Population Fund confirmed the validity of that information by his letter dated 18/4/2003 And whereas it has been established that the allowances of .......... formed to address the year 2000 problem were paid pursuant to the letter of the President of the Council of Ministers No. 559/S dated 14/3/2000, and that the two advances that were granted to secure the needs of the Ministry of Public Health for stationery were settled pursuant to duly drawn up invoices, and also that the health record booklets required for the Directorate of Preventive Health were secured during the year 2000 by way of a regular contract for which a special book of conditions was drawn up, as well as the securing of the printed materials specific to the Ministry during the year 2001 pursuant to two regular contracts in accordance with the rules, and that the restoration of the Ministry's building carried out in the year 1992 did not include the external facades of the building contrary to what was stated in the complaint, and that it was established to the Inspection, through telephone calls made during the conduct of the investigation with a number of patients whose names appeared in certain authorisations for the purchase of medical prostheses (Prothese), that all of them had received those prostheses.

Whereas it has been established that the Ministry of Public Health proceeded to purchase the fluid used in artificial kidney dialysis pursuant to eight purchase authorisations during the years 98 - 99 - and 2002, and pursuant to two public tenders in the years 99 and 2002, and that the price of the aforementioned fluid was lower in the two public tenders than it was in the purchase authorisations, which requires recommending that the Ministry of Public Health work on determining the quantity it needs of this fluid and securing it pursuant to a regular contract that allows it to obtain the required specifications and at the best prices. And whereas it has been established that the equipment and fittings present in the Artificial Kidney Centre, Aisha Bakkar, are very old, and that some kidney dialysis machines are out of order and in need of maintenance, and furthermore the Centre is in need of a new water purification machine, noting that the contract signed between the Ministry of Public Health and .......... Company in its capacity as the exclusive agent of .......... Company for the maintenance of kidney dialysis machines in all government centres expired on 12/6/2002 without the Ministry being able to conclude another maintenance contract with the aforementioned company due to the latter's failure to submit new prices despite the numerous contacts conducted with it in this regard, which requires recommending working on supplying the Government Artificial Kidney Centre, Aisha Bakkar, with the necessary fittings, and securing permanent maintenance for the kidney dialysis machines present in the aforementioned centre. And whereas it has been established that the final determination of the authenticity of the visa affixed to the body of Memorandum No. 14 dated 17/6/2000, issued by .......... Dr. .........., relating to assigning Dr. .......... to medical supervision over certain private hospitals contracted with the Ministry of Public Health, as regards knowing whether that visa belongs to .......... Dr. .......... or to someone else, requires technical expertise, and that there is no utility in knowing this matter, given that the aforementioned memorandum did not entail any financial consequences, and did not cause any harm to the rights of third parties, and furthermore the delay in executing Decree No. 7763/2002 relating to the rules of contracting and the distribution of beds among contracted institutions allocated for treatment at the expense of the Ministry of Public Health is attributable to the failure to include in the aforementioned decree the number of beds intended to be contracted for with each hospital, which does not entail any liability on the part of .......... Dr. .........., in addition to the fact that the latter supervises the working hours of the workers in the card issuance centre such that no case of unjustified absence was recorded in the aforementioned centre, which requires filing the case away as regards the points set out above. And whereas it has been established that the contractor with the Ministry of Public Health, Mr. .........., absented himself from his duty station on 4/5/2001 without a legitimate excuse, and that the letter registered in the registry of the Hospitals and Dispensaries Department under No. 317/M.M., which establishes the state of absence, was referred to the Bureau Department on 5/5/2001 with a proposal to deduct the contractual compensation of Mr. .......... for three days, and it has been established to the Inspection that the aforementioned letter does not exist in the archives of the Ministry such that the proposed penalty was not approved, and was not, consequently, put into execution. And whereas it has been established from reviewing the entries of the outgoing and incoming register adopted in the registry of the Bureau Department that Referral No. 317/M.M. was received on 7/5/2001 and registered under No. 3779 and its receipt was signed for by Mr. .........., the contractor with the Ministry of Public Health in the capacity of .......... and that the latter recorded in the register of the Bureau registry that the referral was returned to the Hospitals and Dispensaries Department on 15/5/2001 without there being any registration thereof in the internal delivery ledger adopted in the Bureau establishing that the Hospitals and Dispensaries Department received it, and furthermore Mr. .......... recorded that the referral was returned to the Hospitals and Dispensaries Department establishing that the Bureau Department received it, which gives rise to the liability of Mr. .........., whether as regards the loss of the transaction or as regards recording information in official registers, that does not conform to reality.

Whereas it has been established that a number of motor vehicles were placed at the disposal of the heads of the central units at the Ministry of Public Health, and that these motor vehicles remain at the disposal of the employees even after the end of official working hours, due to the absence of a dedicated garage belonging to the Ministry to house and preserve the motor vehicles, and that most of the employees who use the Ministry's motor vehicles do not keep a special logbook for each motor vehicle with the exception of each of.........., which requires recommending compliance with the provisions of the Circular issued by the Office of the Prime Minister under No. 26 dated 26/7/74, pertaining to the instructions and forms relating to the motor vehicles and machinery of public administrations, public institutions, and municipalities, and the use thereof. And following deliberation, and in light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided: 1 - To deduct the contractual allowance.......... with the Ministry of Public Health, Mr..........., for three days as a disciplinary measure. 2 - To recommend to the Ministry of Public Health, Directorate General of Health, the following: a - To comply with the provisions of Article 123 of the Public Accounting Law and not to resort to splitting expenditures except in the cases permitted by the legal and regulatory texts in force. b - To caution the concerned employees mentioned in the body of this decision as to the necessity of full compliance with the provisions of the laws and regulations in force when performing the duties of their positions and exercising their powers. c - To take the necessary measures against.......... with the Ministry, Mr..........., for the unjustified purpose from his place of work on 4/ 5/2001 d - To suspend Mr........... from working in the capacity of.......... at the Bureau Department in the Ministry and to request him to abide by the provisions of the agreement signed with him to work in the capacity of.......... e - To comply with the provisions of Circular No. 26 issued by the Presidency of the Council of Ministers on 26/7/74 (Instructions and forms relating to the motor vehicles and machinery of public administrations, public institutions, and municipalities, and the use thereof). f - To circulate to all administrative units affiliated with the Ministry the necessity of complying with the provisions of Article Eight of the Law Organizing the Ministry of Public Health, referred to in the body of this decision. g - To supply the governmental artificial kidney center, Aisha Bakkar, with the necessary equipment and to secure permanent maintenance for the dialysis machines present in the center, along with securing the fluid used in dialysis pursuant to a regular contract. h - To close the case with respect to the other points. A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the fifteenth of the month of October in the year two thousand and three.

Whereas it has been established that the Governor of North Lebanon held in his referral No. 158 /B/2002, that any disbursement or expenditure in accordance with Decision No. 81/ 2001 prior to its ratification remains under the personal responsibility of.........., and that the latter, notwithstanding that, requested.......... to disburse sums of money pursuant to Decision No. 81/2001, and that an amount of /54000000/ L.L. was actually disbursed in the name of.......... and under his personal responsibility in order to pay them to those entitled thereto, prior to the said Decision being joined with the ratification of the supervisory authority in accordance with the rules, and issued a decision referring.......... Mr.........., to the Higher Disciplinary Board due to the latter drawing the attention of.......... to the legal violations which he commits. Whereas it has been established that.......... of Sir Mr.......... received funds from the collectors and disbursed them in violation of the legal rules governing that, and in particular Articles 91 and 92 of the Municipalities Law and without any presidential or council decisions being issued in respect thereof, and that the statements and invoices submitted by Mr.......... as supporting documents to prove the operation of disbursing the collected funds, consist of ordinary papers in which.......... requests the payment of sums of money to specified persons under various designations such as a fee allowance or expenses to ministries, without any proof of the missions and without the existence of any official assignment for the persons concerned. Whereas it has been established from the two statements of both.......... Mr..........,.......... in Sir Mr.........., that the role of the two said committees is purely nominal, and that.......... is the one who undertakes the operations of purchase and receipt without any intervention on the part of these two committees, and also that there are decisions issued by the Municipal Council that are registered in the register of decisions pertaining thereto without the knowledge of the members of the Municipal Council thereof, and that.......... proceeds to regularise the status of those decisions in subsequent sessions in violation of the rules, in addition to the fact that the decisions relating to the appointment of a substitute treasurer, and the determination of the compensation of each of.........., and the approval of the budget of the year 2003, which were approved by some members of the Municipal Council (Messrs..........) on 23/3/2003, were discussed and ratified in sessions in which a quorum was not secured. Whereas it has been established that the said.......... of Sir paid sums of money in consideration of conducting studies pertaining to the restoration of the municipality building standing on plot No. 1125/ Sir, despite the fact that the Municipal Council approved the submission of the aforementioned studies free of charge to the municipality, and that Mr.......... one of the members of the Municipal Council in Sir, stated upon being questioned about the matter that.......... said that he would pay this amount by way of a bribe to one of the employees to facilitate obtaining the electricity dues pertaining to the municipality, a matter which falls, if proven true, under penalty of the provisions of Article 355 et seq. of the Lebanese Penal Code, which requires recommending the referral of the investigation file to the Cassation Public Prosecutor's Office to take whatever it deems appropriate in respect thereof. Whereas it has been established that the tenders file pertaining to the project of.......... is not present in the building of the Municipality of Sir, and that all the documents pertaining to the two public tenders that took place regarding the matter are in the possession of.......... Mr.........., and that the latter agreed to provide the Inspection with the necessary clarifications regarding the said file and regarding the points raised in the course of this Decision, however he did not attend at the appointment which he personally fixed nor did he justify his non-attendance, which requires recommending to the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities to investigate with.......... of Sir regarding the awarding of a project and the other violations to which reference has been made in the body of this Decision due to the acts of the deliberative and executive authorities in the municipalities not being subject to the oversight of the Central Inspection, pursuant to the text of Article 137 of Legislative Decree No. 118/77 and its amendments. (The Municipalities Law).

Whereas it has transpired from reviewing the register of vehicles belonging to the Municipality of Sir that the vehicle bearing the number 171987/M Lebanon, which is of the type Toyota Dyna, still remains to date registered in the name of.......... Mr.,.........., pursuant to a special power of attorney for the sale of a vehicle, as.......... did not proceed to transfer its ownership to the Municipality in accordance with the due procedures, and whereas the Municipality of Sir lacks a vehicle logbook, which requires recommending the issuance of a circular to all municipalities on the necessity of registering the machinery and vehicles belonging to the municipality in the name of the municipality, and adopting a logbook for vehicles in accordance with Circular No. 26 dated 26/7/74, issued by the Presidency of the Council of Ministers in this regard. And after deliberation, and in light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided to recommend to the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities - the Directorate General of Local Administrations and Councils - the following: 1 - To investigate.......... of Sir, Mr..........., in the case relating to the awarding of the project of.........., and in all other points referred to in the body of this decision. 2 - To investigate.......... in Sir, Messrs.:.........., who approved the adoption of the budget for the year 2003 and the granting of allowances.........., in violation of the law. 3 - To request the Municipality of Sir to work on transferring the ownership of the vehicle of the make Toyota Dyna, licence plate number 171987/M Lebanon, to the name of the Municipality in accordance with the due procedures, and to work on recovering the funds received by each of.......... of Sir, Mr..........., Mr..........., as allowances, on the basis of the Municipal Council decision taken in the session held on 23/9/2002, due to the lack of legal standing of this decision. 4 - To issue a circular to all municipalities on the obligation to register vehicles in the name of the municipality, and to adopt a logbook for vehicles in accordance with Circular No. 26 dated 26/7/74, issued by the Presidency of the Council of Ministers in this regard. 5 - To refer the file to the Public Prosecutor's Office at the Court of Cassation. A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the third of the month of December of the year two thousand and three.

After deliberation, and in the light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided 1 - To refer the investigation file to the Financial Public Prosecution, and to defer the determination of disciplinary liabilities until the issuance of the judicial judgment. 2 - To notify the Decision to the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities, the Directorate General of Local Administrations and Councils, for information and to take the necessary measures. A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the seventeenth day of the month of December of the year two thousand and three.

Secretariat of the Board Session: 45/2003 Item: 5 Decision No. 515/2003 The Central Inspection Board, Having perused the file of the case registered under No. 38/07/2003 with all its contents.

2865/W 2003 Having perused the report of the Inspector Mr. Mahmoud Al-Moussawi dated 1/12/2003, following the investigation into the financial violations occurring in the Municipality of.......... Having perused the opinion of the Financial Inspector General dated 2/12/ 2003 Having perused the opinion of the President of the Central Inspection dated 4/ 12/2003 Whereas it appeared from the documents of the file that a complaint was received by the Central Inspection submitted by the Municipal Council of..........,.........., indicating the existence of financial violations and transgressions on the part of.........., relating to collection and expenditure operations, and an investigation was conducted into the matter pursuant to Assignment No. 38/7/2003 And whereas it appeared as a result of the investigation that.......... the Municipality of.........., issued a decision.......... under No. 195 dated 5/10/2002 whereby he assigned the citizen.......... to carry out collection operations, by virtue of receipt books delivered to him by.........., and that.......... himself carried out collection operations, according to the statement of.......... And whereas it appeared that the fees collected by.......... and by.......... are paid into the fund of the Municipality, in addition to the impossibility of inspecting the assets of the fund, its registers, and the receipt books, due to the refusal of.........., the Municipality of.......... to the Investigating Inspector the entries and registers, in implementation of the instructions issued to him by.........., which rendered it impossible to complete the investigation into these violations due to the unavailability of the necessary documents for the reasons set forth above. And whereas the acts of the deliberative and executive authorities in the Municipality are not subject to the supervision of the Central Inspection, in accordance with the provisions of Article 137 of Legislative Decree No. 118 dated 30/6 /1977, which requires referring the investigation file to the Financial Public Prosecution andstaying the determination of disciplinary responsibilities until the issuance of the judicial judgment in this regard, and notifying the Decision to the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities, the Directorate General of Local Administration and Councils, for information and to take the required measures.

Secretariat of the Board Session: 43/2003 Item: 11 Decision No. 493/2003 The Central Inspection Board, Having reviewed the file of the case registered under No. 88/7 B/ 2002 in all its contents. Having reviewed the report of the Financial Inspector, Mr. Abdel Sattar Al-Ayoubi, dated 27/10/2003, regarding the execution of the instructions of.......... of Sir in violation of the law by.........., and the receipt of collected funds by.......... Having reviewed the opinion of the Financial Inspector General dated 11/11 /2003 Having reviewed the opinion of the President of the Central Inspection dated 13 /11/2003 Whereas it appears from the documents of the file that the Governor of North Lebanon requested the Central Inspection, pursuant to his letter No. 5512/B/ 2001 dated 12/2/2002, to conduct the necessary investigations in the Municipality of Sir, District of Miniyeh - Danniyeh, regarding the act of.......... in executing the instructions of.........., which included giving him an order to withdraw and pay financial sums out of an unratified municipal decision, and the act of.......... in receiving collected funds and failing to hand them over to.......... in violation of the law, and that the Financial Inspectorate General conducted an investigation into the matter pursuant to the annual inspection programme pertaining to the year 2002 Whereas it appears from the investigation that the Minister of Interior and Municipalities formed, pursuant to his referral No. 8628/D dated 3/1/2001, a committee chaired by the Governor of North Lebanon, to which he entrusted the task of conducting an investigation into the transactions and decisions taken in the Municipality of Sir, and that the said committee indicated, as a result of the investigation conducted by it, the existence of fragmentation in expenditure under decisions in principle, and the creation of financial liabilities in the amount of /255140223/L.L. resulting from the execution of works without decisions having been issued by the Municipal Council in respect thereof, in violation of the provisions of the Municipalities Act and the provisions of Decree No. 5595 dated 22/9/82, (Accounting Rules in Municipalities and Unions of Municipalities Not Subject to the Public Accounting Act) where they were executed under the responsibility of.......... without following the legal rules for committing, liquidating and disbursing the expenditure, and without following the technical rules for those works regarding obtaining the approval of the competent authorities in the Directorate General of Urban Planning. Whereas it appears that the Minister of Interior and Municipalities approved the proposals set forth in the report of the investigation committee formed by him, including concluding settlement contracts with the entitled parties, and also instructed the Governor of North Lebanon to summon.......... to his office and notify him of the imposition of the penalty of reprimand against him pursuant to the provisions of Article 104 of the Municipalities Act, promulgated by Legislative Decree No. 118 dated 20/6/1977 and its amendments. Whereas it appears that the Municipal Council of Sir took Decision No. 81 dated 26/10/2001, relating to the disbursement of an amount of /147466000 /L.L. representing the value of workers' wages and the value of invoices pertaining to the year 2000, which were not paid on time, and that.......... by his letter No. 16 addressed to the Governor of North Lebanon on 10/1/2002, deemed the decision ratified pursuant to the provisions of Article 63 of the Municipalities Act, despite the fact that the aforementioned Article does not apply to the course of the municipal decision set forth above, due to the fundamental defects marring it, and because it was referred to the Minister to express an opinion on the manner and entitlement of paying financial sums as expenditures for works that were executed without appropriations existing therefor at the time.

Whereas it appeared that.......... in the Directorate General of Education, Mrs........... issued on 3/5/99 a certificate pursuant to which she confirmed the work of Mrs........... in the department headed by her during the period falling between 17/7/96 and until 1/12/96, contrary to the facts, and that Mrs........... stated in the minutes of her interrogation that the issuance of this certificate came pursuant to an oral request addressed to her by.......... of the Joint Administrative Directorate in the Ministry without presenting the evidence demonstrating the validity of her claim, which entails disciplinary liability on her part in this regard, thereby requiring that the appropriate disciplinary measures be taken against her pursuant to the provisions of Articles 54 and 55 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 and its amendments. And whereas it appeared that.......... of the Tariq El Jdideh Public Intermediate School for Girls did not pay to Mrs........... her salary for the month of February 1991 due to her interruption of the practice of her work in the aforementioned school, and that the principal returned the cheque belonging to Mrs........... along with the payroll relating to the same month, to the paymaster, Mrs..........., and that it appeared to the Inspection that the salary of Mrs........... was disbursed for the month of February 1991 in the name of Mrs........... whose interrogation was not possible due to the termination of her services, thereby requiring the referral of both Mrs........... before the Court of Audit pursuant to the provisions of Articles 60 and 61 of the Law organising it. And after deliberation, and in the light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided: 1 - To delay the advancement in step of the teacher in the Ministry of Education and Higher Education, Mrs..........., (her financial number..........) for a period of twelve months by way of disciplinary action. 2 - To deduct the salary of.......... in the Ministry of Education and Higher Education, Miss.......... (her financial number..........) for one day by way of disciplinary action 3 - To refer each of Messrs.:........, before the Court of Audit. 4 - To notify the Civil Service Board of the non-establishment of the fact of the attendance of Mrs......., during the period specified from the date of 1/1/93 and until the date of 20/8/1997 and consequently the non-entitlement to her salaries for this period. 5 - To file the case with respect to the other points. A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the twenty-sixth of the month of February of the year two thousand and three.

Secretariat of the Board Session: 7/2003 Item: 10 Decision No. 103/2003 The Central Inspection Board, Having perused the file of the case registered under No. 12/7/2000 with all its contents.

14/5/2000

58/3/98 Having perused the report of the financial inspectors Messrs: Michel Dib, Antoine Nohra, Naji Shaaban, and the educational inspectors the two Messrs: Ahmad Al-Samad, Talal Youssef dated 11/4/2002, as a result of the verification into the employment status of the teacher Mrs. .......... Having perused the report of the financial inspectors the two Messrs Michel Dib and Antoine Nohra dated 8/8/2002 Having perused the Educational Inspector General dated 23/8/2002 Having perused the two opinions of the Financial Inspector General dated 3/9/ 2002 and 17/12/2002 Having perused the opinion of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Audit No. 441/3548 dated 26/11/2002 Having perused the opinion of the President of the Central Inspection dated 6/ 2/2003 And whereas it appeared from the documents of the file that the Civil Service Board deposited with the Central Inspection a copy of its letter No. 4168 dated 30/10/1998, addressed to the Ministry of Finance, and relating to the employment status of the teacher at the Ministry of Education and Higher Education, Mrs. .........., in reply to the letter of the Minister of Finance No. 835/S 1 dated 12/9/1998, in which he requested the statement of the opinion of the Civil Service Board on the employment status of Mrs. .......... on the basis of Article 65 of the Personnel Regulations, and that is after it appeared that the disbursement of the salaries of Mrs. .......... stopped since the date of 1/1/ 93 due to her failure to resume her work since the expiry of the period of the maternity leave and the sick leave on 22/12/90 and until now, and that the Financial Inspectorate General conducted the necessary investigations on the subject. And whereas it appeared from the investigation that the teacher at the Tariq Al-Jadida Intermediate School for Girls Mrs. .......... ceased attending her workplace at the aforementioned school definitively with effect from the date of 22/12/1990, as she joined the General Secretariat of the Chamber of Deputies without notifying her administration of any document in this regard, and that the Administrative Memorandum No. 152/91 which authorised her attachment to the General Secretariat of the Chamber of Deputies was issued by the Minister of Education and Higher Education on 15/10/91, that is after the lapse of approximately one year from her commencement of her work at the General Secretariat of the Chamber of Deputies. And whereas it appeared that Mrs. .......... obtained, during her attachment to her workplace at the Tariq Al-Jadida Intermediate School for Girls, a maternity leave for a period of forty days ending on 6/12/ 1990, and that Mrs. .......... did not resume her work after the expiry of the maternity leave, and submitted on 17/12/1990 a sick leave regarding which the necessary decision was issued in accordance with the rules, such that the period of absence extending from the end of the maternity leave to the beginning of the aforementioned sick leave, amounting to ten days, remained without legal justification, a matter which entails upon Mrs. .........., disciplinary liability as a result of this violation.

And whereas Ms. .........., by ceasing to report to her place of work and joining another administration without notifying her original administration of the matter and before the issuance of any instrument in this regard, and by her absence during her assignment to the Tariq El Jdideh School from her place of work without legal justification, has violated the provisions of the Civil Servants Regulations, in particular the duties of office provided for in Article 14 of the said Regulations, which entails disciplinary liability on her part, and whereas what was stated in the record of her interrogation and in her written defence is not such as to exempt her from this liability, which requires taking the appropriate disciplinary measures in her regard pursuant to the provisions of Articles 54 and 55 of Legislative Decree No. 59112 and its amendments (Civil Servants Regulations). And whereas it has been established that Ms. .......... was returned to the Ministry of Education and Higher Education where she was assigned to the Secretariat of the Minister, and thereafter to the Joint Administrative Service attached to the Ministry, pursuant to Memoranda No. 207/M/92 dated 20/12/92 and No. 79/1/97 dated 20/1/97 issued, respectively, by the Minister of Education and Higher Education in this regard. And whereas it has been established from the letter of the Civil Service Board No. 4168 dated 30/10/98, that none of the heads of units who certified that Ms. .......... worked in their units during the period extending from 22/12/90 until the date of her assignment to the Joint Administrative Service on 20/8/97, signed the payroll schedules of Ms. .......... and her allowances, whereas the latter was supposed to receive her salaries and allowances under the responsibility of her immediate superiors if she had actually been performing her duties according to their attached statements, and whereas the Civil Service Board pointed out in its aforementioned letter to another aspect of the employment status of Ms. .......... based on the fact that the latter did not report to any of the places of work specified in the attached statements, and for this reason her immediate superiors did not assume the responsibility of signing the schedules of her salaries and allowances. And whereas it has been established that the Minister of Education and Higher Education requested, pursuant to his letter No. 2970/11 dated 28/4/98, action to disburse the salaries of Ms. .......... suspended since 31/12/ 92 and up to date, on the basis of the memoranda of her assignment referred to above, and whereas the Civil Service Board requested the Ministry of Finance not to pay any salary to Ms. .......... for the period of her absence preceding the date of 20/8/1997, pending the results of the investigation of the Central Inspection in this regard. And whereas it has been established, in addition to the failure of the immediate superiors to sign the payroll schedules of the lady, that the latter did not, during her presence in the various administrative units, assuming the validity thereof, sign the attendance registers or use the time clocks as proof of her presence in the units referred to, which indicates that her actual performance of the duties of her office has not been proven, a matter upon which is founded her lack of entitlement to any salary for the period preceding her actual assignment to the Joint Administrative Service at the Ministry of Education and Higher Education. And whereas it has been established that each of .......... in an acting capacity at the time, Mr. .........., at the time, Mr. .........., gave a statement that facilitated action to disburse undue salaries to Ms. .......... which violates the duties of office provided for in Article 14 of the Civil Servants Regulations, and constitutes a fault liable to cause damage to public funds, and whereas Messrs. .........., were placed on retirement for having reached the legal age, and there is no longer any scope to prosecute them disciplinarily, yet their financial liability remains standing, which requires referring them on account thereof before the Court of Audit pursuant to the provisions of Articles 60 and 61 of the Law organising it.

Whereas the acts committed by each of: Mrs.........., and Mr.......... entail disciplinary liability on their part pursuant to the provisions of Article 14 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 and its amendments (Civil Servants Regulations), and whereas what was stated in the minutes of their interrogation and in their written defences does not absolve them of liability, which requires taking the appropriate disciplinary measures against them pursuant to the provisions of Articles 54 and 55 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 and its amendments (Civil Servants Regulations). Whereas Paragraph B of Article 65 of the Civil Servants Regulations deems a civil servant who absents himself from his work without legal leave and does not resume his work within fifteen days from the date of his absence from work to have resigned, which requires recommending that the Ministry of Education and Higher Education take the necessary legal measures against each of Mr.........., and Mrs.........., for their continuous absence from their place of work without legal justification, pursuant to the provisions of the Civil Servants Regulations (Legislative Decree No. 112/59 and its amendments). Following deliberation, and in light of the circumstances of the case. It is decided 1 - To delay the advancement in step of the female teacher at Ammar Al-Bikat Official School - Akkar.........., (her financial number..........) for a period of six months as a disciplinary measure. 2 - To delay the advancement in step of the male teacher at Ammar Al-Bikat Official School - Akkar Mr.......... (his financial number..........) for a period of six months as a disciplinary measure. 3 - To recommend that the Ministry of Education and Higher Education, the Directorate General of Education, take the necessary legal measures against each of Mrs.........., and Mr.......... for their continuous absence from their place of work without legal justification, pursuant to the provisions of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 (Civil Servants Regulations) and its amendments. A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the fourth of the month of June of the year two thousand and three.

Secretariat of the Board Session: 21/2003 Item: 14 Decision No. 268/2003 The Central Inspection Board, having perused the file of the case registered under No. 3/5/2000 with all its contents.

5611/W 99 Having perused the report of the educational inspectors Messrs.: Talal Youssef, Mohammad Halwani and Hisham Qaziha dated 19/9/2002, concerning the violations attributed to the teacher at the Ammar Al-Bikat Public School, District of Akkar, Mr. .........., and the female teacher in the same school, Mrs. .........., regarding their non-compliance with the obligations of official working hours. Secretariat of the Board Session: 34/2003 Item: 2 Decision No. 394/2003 The Central Inspection Board, Having perused the file of the case registered under No. 40/3/2002 in all its contents.

2824/W 2002 Having perused the report of the Administrative Inspector Mr. Ihsan Al-Hassan dated 15/7/2003 resulting from the investigation into the violations attributed to an employee at the Ministry of Agriculture. Secretariat of the Board Session: 2/2003 Item: 1 Decision No. 16/2003 The Central Inspection Board, having reviewed the file of the case registered under No. 21/3/2002 in all its contents.

2/6/2002 Having reviewed the report of the Administrative Inspector Mr. Mahmoud Kahil, the Agricultural Inspector Mr. Osama Mortada and the Veterinary Inspector Mr. Joseph Kahouch dated 25/6/2002 and 2/10/2002, following the investigation into the violations committed at the centre of.......... in the port of.......... Having reviewed the opinion of the Health, Social and Agricultural Inspector General dated 15/10/2002 Having reviewed the opinion of the Administrative Inspector General dated 11/ 11/2002 Having reviewed the opinion of the President of the Central Inspection dated 18 /12/2002 And whereas it appears that an investigation was conducted into the violations and transgressions committed at the centre of.........., particularly with regard to the failure to follow legal procedures and apply technical conditions in monitoring the importation of animal production and its derivatives, pursuant to Assignment No. 21/3 /2002

2/6/2002 And whereas it appears from the investigation that there are numerous violations and transgressions at the Veterinary Quarantine Centre in the port of.......... with regard to: - The existence of certain veterinary health certificates not stamped with the official seal and not signed by the person in charge of the centre, the veterinarian Dr........... - The issuance of health certificates to the concerned parties, based on laboratory analysis results and referrals that have no entries in the registers of the.......... laboratory accredited by the Ministry of Agriculture. The issuance of veterinary certificates for chilled or frozen meat and fish on the same day on which the referral sending the sample to the laboratory for examination was drawn up, knowing that the examination of chilled meat samples requires 24 hours, and the examination of frozen meat samples requires 48 hours, which means that such meat was never examined at all. - The existence of laboratory analysis results copied from one another with a change made to the referral number and its date, with the intent of misusing the signature and seal of a head of laboratory. - Allowing the concerned parties to take the samples to the laboratory themselves, contrary to administrative procedures which require sending such samples with a technical employee attached to the said centre. And whereas it appears from the contents of the file that the case is pending in its penal aspect before the competent judiciary, which requires depositing a copy of all the documents of the investigation file with the Cassation Public Prosecution to decide what is appropriate regarding the matters stated therein with respect to the validity of the health certificates and the laboratory analysis certificates, and the possibility of the participation of other persons in the matter and the liability entailed for them.

Whereas it was established that the contraventions occurring at the Veterinary Quarantine Centre at the Port of Beirut and referred to above, fall upon each of the Head of the said Centre, the physician contracted with the Ministry of Agriculture, Dr.........., and the two veterinary technical assistants, Messrs.........., each insofar as he is concerned, which constitutes a breach of their functional duties stipulated in Article 14 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 and its amendments (Civil Servants Regulations), and entails disciplinary liability on their part. And whereas it was established that the civil servant at the Ministry of Agriculture,.........., Dr.........., neglected to perform his functional duties as regards exercising supervision over his subordinates working at the Port Centre, and as regards his absence from the said Centre to supervise the proper functioning of the work, and to monitor the application of the regulations in force and the health and technical conditions to the importation of meat, animal products and their derivatives, thereby contravening the provisions of Article 8 of Legislative Decree No. 111/59 (Organisation of Public Administrations), the provisions of Article 14 of Legislative Decree No. 115/59 and its amendments (Civil Servants Regulations), and the provisions of Article 89 of Decree No. 5246/94 (Organisation of the Ministry of Agriculture), which entails disciplinary liability on his part. And whereas nothing was established from the record of interrogation of Messrs:.........., or from the written defence of each of them, that would exempt them from liability, which requires taking the appropriate disciplinary measures against them pursuant to the provisions of Articles 54 and 55 of Legislative Decree No. 112 /59 and its amendments (Civil Servants Regulations). And whereas it was established that the veterinarian, Dr.........., has been contracted with the Ministry of Agriculture since the year 1966 and has been working at the Veterinary Quarantine Centre at the Port of.......... since the date of his contracting, which contravenes the provisions of the Seventh Article of Legislative Decree No. 130 dated 12/6/59 (Special Provisions Relating to the Ministry of Agriculture and Special Conditions of Appointment Therein), which stipulated that it is not permissible for civil servants of border centres, including the airport and the port, to remain in their posts for more than three years, which requires recommending that the said Ministry work to apply the provisions of the Seventh Article referred to above. And whereas it was established that the Veterinary Quarantine Centre at the Port of.......... occupies an iron container that does not possess the administrative specifications necessary to accommodate those working therein, which requires recommending to the Ministry of Agriculture to work on securing a suitable place for the said Centre in which the conditions necessary for the proper functioning of the work are met.

Following deliberation, and in the light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided: 1 - To deduct the salary of the employee at the Ministry of Agriculture..........,..........,.......... (his financial number for five days by way of discipline. 2 - To deduct the contractual remuneration of the physician contracted with the Ministry of Agriculture, Dr........... for ten days by way of discipline. 3 - To deduct the salary of the employee at the Ministry of Agriculture,.........., Mr. (his financial number) for three days by way of discipline. 4 - To dispense with the liability of.........., Mr..........., due to the termination of his services. 5 - To refer the file to the Cassation Public Prosecution. 6 - To recommend to the Ministry of Agriculture to act on the following: a - Securing a suitable premises endowed with the necessary specifications to accommodate the workers at the Veterinary Quarantine Centre in the Port of.........., and ensuring the proper functioning of the work therein. b - Applying the provisions of the Seventh Article of Legislative Decree No. 130/59 as regards employees of posts located at the borders, including the Airport and the Port, not remaining in their posts for a period exceeding three years. A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the fifteenth day of the month of January in the year two thousand and three.

Secretariat of the Board Session: 4/2003 Item: 11 Decision No. 58/2003 The Central Inspection Board, Having perused the file of the case registered under No. 7/6B/2001 with all its contents. Having perused the report of the Social Inspector Miss Marie Dib dated 7/11/2002, resulting from the inspection of day nurseries belonging to civil associations and bodies in the Caza of Sidon, contracted with the Ministry of Social Affairs. Having perused the opinion of the Health, Social and Agricultural Inspector General dated 26/11/2002 Having perused the opinion of the President of the Central Inspection dated 14 /12/2002 Whereas it appeared from the documents of the file that an inspection was conducted of the day nurseries belonging to civil associations and bodies in the Caza of Sidon, contracted with the Ministry of Social Affairs, and that the mission covered examining the extent of compliance with the proper execution of the contracts, auditing the documents sent by those nurseries to the Ministry, and verifying their conformity with reality, pursuant to the annual inspection programme of the Health, Social and Agricultural General Inspectorate for the year 2001 And whereas it appeared from the inspection of the Cultural and Social Development Association located in the town of Ghazieh - Caza of Sidon, that the said Association complied with the execution of the clauses of the contract concluded therewith, and that there is nothing warranting remark regarding it. And whereas it appeared from the statement of.......... Association.........., that the said Association did not receive any contribution from the Ministry since the date of concluding the first contract with it in the year 1998 and until the month of January of the year 2002, although the Association fulfilled the obligations incumbent upon it pursuant to the contract concluded with it in this regard. And whereas it appeared that there are three payment statements in favour of the.......... Social Association in the Joint Projects Accounting Department, and that the aforementioned statements, pertaining to invoices issued in the years 1999 and 2000, were not accompanied by the signature of.......... in accordance with the rules, which gives rise to the liability of Mr..........., the employee responsible for delaying the submission of those statements to the Head of the Service. And whereas the services of Mr........... have been terminated upon his reaching the legal age and there is no longer any ground to pursue him disciplinarily, which requires dispensing with holding him accountable and filing the case in this respect.

Whereas it appeared upon auditing the registers specific to the joint committees in the Joint Projects Accounting Department at the Ministry of Social Affairs that the payment statements bearing the numbers: 2306/2001, 2790/2000, 91/2000 were registered without mentioning the date of their issuance, which calls for recommending the adoption of the applicable administrative rules regarding mentioning the day, month, and year when registering statements and payment orders in their respective registers; and whereas it appeared that it is possible.......... for the civil associations to undertake the collection of their dues and deliver them to the concerned parties, in the absence of employees at the joint project, in accordance with what.......... Social clarified in this regard, which requires recommending working on naming a civil servant to whom the matter of collecting the dues of the aforementioned associations is assigned pursuant to a specific text, in order to prevent obstructing the work of the associations and paralysing their activities, and to enable the administration to exercise its oversight when necessary. Whereas it appeared that hygiene conditions are not secured in the nursery of the.......... Social Association - which reflects negatively on the health of the children whose care the said nursery undertakes, which requires recommending working on drawing the attention of those in charge of the aforementioned association to the necessity of abiding by the social conditions, particularly regarding hygiene and tidiness. Whereas it is required to close the case regarding the remaining points. After deliberation, and in light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided: 1 - To recommend to the Ministry of Social Affairs - Directorate General of Social Affairs - the following: a - To hold off on concluding joint contracts when the appropriations required for their execution are not available. b - To assign the task of collecting the dues of civil associations to a civil servant who shall undertake this task pursuant to a text drawn up for this purpose, in order to prevent delay in paying the dues to their rightful claimants, and to determine responsibilities when necessary. c - To request the Accounting Service at the Ministry to work on registering the statements and payment orders in their respective registers while mentioning the date (day, month, and year) in accordance with the followed administrative rules. d - To draw the attention of those in charge of the.......... Association, to the necessity of abiding by the social conditions stipulated in the contract concluded with it, particularly regarding hygiene and tidiness........... 2 - To dispense with holding Mr........... accountable due to the termination of his services. 3 - To close the case regarding the remaining points. A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the twenty-ninth of the month of January in the year two thousand and three.

Secretariat of the Board Session: 5/2003 Item: 3 Decision No. 67/2003 The Central Inspection Board, Having perused the file of the case registered under No. 33/7/2001 with all its contents.

251/W2001 Having perused the report of the Financial Inspectors, Messrs.: Duraid Al-Jammal, Samia Daher and Badia Al-Khoury, dated 14/5/2002, resulting from the investigation into the violations attributed to certain employees of the Ministry of Public Health. Having perused the report of the Financial Inspectors, Mesdames Samia Daher and Badia Al-Khoury, dated 19/6/2002, relating to the same subject. Having perused the two opinions of the Financial Inspector General dated 23/7 /2002 and 26/7/2002 Having perused the opinion of the President of the Central Inspection dated 31 /10/2002 And whereas it appeared from the documents of the file that numerous complaints were received by the Central Inspection relating to the reporting that certain employees of the Ministry of.......... Public committed numerous excesses and violations, particularly with respect to their processing of hospitalisation cards pertaining to certain open-heart patients in an irregular manner, and other points set forth in those complaints, and that the competent inspectors undertook the investigation into the matter. And whereas it appeared from the investigation that.......... with the Ministry of Public Health, Doctor.........., omitted to affix certain required stamps and signatures on the coverage cards, and that he also approved certain hospitalisation cards pertaining to open-heart patients, issued after the lapse of more than 48 hours from the admission of the patients to the hospital, thereby violating the provisions of Memoranda No. 39 issued by the Director General of Health on 16/6/94, and No. 1 issued by the Director of Medical Care on 1/1/95 (relating to the regulation of granting hospitalisation cards of the first, second and third categories and medical and administrative control), and the provisions of Article 14 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 and its amendments (Staff Regulations), which entails disciplinary liability on his part. And whereas it appeared that.......... with the Ministry of Public Health, Doctor..........at the American University of Beirut Hospital, despite his signature on the hospitalisation application and on the overall schedule of open-heart patients, omitted to sign the coverage cards relating to these patients, and pertaining to the month of May of the year 2002, thereby violating the provisions of Memorandum No. 5 issued by the Director of Medical Care on 2/4/97 (relating to the signing of transactions), and the provisions of Article 14 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 and its amendments (Staff Regulations), which entails disciplinary liability on his part. And whereas it appeared that.......... on the establishment of the Ministry of Public Health, Doctor.........., was performing, during official working hours, private surgical operations, thereby violating the provisions of Article 14 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 and its amendments (Staff Regulations), which entails disciplinary liability on his part, and requires recommending to the said Ministry to work on taking the necessary measures against doctors who practise medical work during official working hours. And whereas nothing appeared from the minutes of interrogation of each of Messrs.:.........., and from the written defence of each of them, that would exempt them from liability, which requires taking the appropriate disciplinary measures against them pursuant to the provisions of Articles 54 and 55 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 and its amendments (Staff Regulations).

And whereas it has been established that numerous hospitalisation applications, particularly those relating to open-heart patients, are completed without the presence of the parties concerned or one of the members of their families, contrary to the provisions of Memoranda No. 39 issued by the Director General of Health on 16/6/94, and No. 1 issued by the Director of Medical Care on 1/1/95 (relating to the regulation of the issuance of hospitalisation cards of the first, second, and third categories and medical and administrative supervision), and that most of the supervising physicians, according to what has been demonstrated above, do not comply with the provisions of these two Memoranda, which requires recommending that the Ministry of Public Health strictly enforce the provisions of the two Memoranda referred to above, and not proceed with transactions that do not fulfil the required legal and regulatory conditions. And whereas it has been established, in addition to the foregoing, that some of the supervising physicians or those assigned to medical supervision, and some of the physicians assigned to issue coverage cards and the employees who assist in this task, do not place the date next to their signatures on those transactions, contrary to the content of Memorandum No. 5 issued by the Director of Medical Care on 2/4/97 (relating to the signing of transactions), which requires recommending that the Ministry of Public Health strictly enforce the content of the aforementioned Memorandum. And whereas it has been established from the contents of the file that the failure to define the duties and responsibilities of the physicians and employees working at the hospitalisation card issuance centre at the Ministry of Public Health allows each of them the possibility of signing those cards in his capacity as the authority responsible for issuing them, which requires recommending that the Ministry of Public Health work on defining the duties and powers of those working for it, particularly at the said centre, in accordance with the provisions of the laws and regulations in force. And after deliberation, and in light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided: 1 - To reprimand each of the employees and contractors with the Ministry of Public Health, the physicians Messrs.: .......... 2 - To recommend that the Ministry of Public Health, Directorate General of Health, work on the following: a - Taking the necessary measures against the physicians who practise medical work during official working hours. b - Strictly enforcing the provisions of Memoranda No. 39 issued by the Director General of Health on 16/6/94, and No. 1 issued by the Director of Medical Care on 1/1/95, referred to above in the body of this Decision, and not proceeding with transactions that do not fulfil the required legal and regulatory conditions. c - Emphasising to all supervising physicians or those assigned to medical supervision, and the physicians assigned to issue coverage cards and the employees who assist them, the necessity of complying with the provisions of Memorandum No. 5 issued by the Director of Medical Care on 2/4/97 d - Defining the duties and powers of those working for it, particularly at the hospitalisation card issuance centre, in accordance with the provisions of the laws and regulations in force. A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the fifth of the month of February of the year two thousand and three.

Board Secretariat Session: 18/2003 Item: 1 Decision No. 223/2003 The Central Inspection Board, Having perused the file of the case registered under No. 30/3/2002 in all its contents.

2069/W 2002 Having perused the report of the Administrative Inspector Miss Fatima Awada dated 27/1/2003, as a result of the investigation into the violations committed at the Sidon Civil Status Registry Office.
