Whereas it has been established from the investigation that at the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities, Directorate General of Personal Status, South Lebanon Civil Status Department, Mr. .........., who was responsible for keeping the special register of legal and administrative texts established at the Sidon Civil Status Registry Office in application of Circular No. 15/S issued by the Director General of Personal Status on 7/8/99, neglected to preserve the said register and failed to inspect it upon resuming his duties following the expiration of the effects of the administrative leave granted to him on 8/10/2001, and did not become aware of its disappearance until 13/6/2002, the date on which the register was requested by .........., which led to the inability to determine the date of its loss, thereby violating the applicable administrative rules and the provisions of Article 14 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 and its amendments (Civil Servants Regulations), which entails his disciplinary liability. Whereas it has been established that .......... at the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities, Directorate General of Personal Status, Sidon Civil Status Registry Office, .........., who was responsible for the incoming and outgoing mail register at the said Registry Office, neglected to keep this register by leaving some registration fields blank, and also failed to comply with the deadlines set for completing the transactions assigned to him, thereby violating the administrative rules that must be observed and the provisions of Article 14 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 and its amendments (Civil Servants Regulations), which entails his disciplinary liability. Whereas it has been established that .......... the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities, Directorate General of Personal Status, assigned to the duties of .........., Mr. .........., delayed the execution of a set of decisions and transactions relating to naturalisation that had been referred to him during the years 99 - 2000 - 2001, and did not execute them until after follow-up with him by .......... South Lebanon Civil Status, and that he also neglected the supervision of the work of his subordinates and failed to inspect the special register of legal and administrative texts referred to above for a period of approximately nine months, which indicates his lack of proficiency in the tasks and duties of his position and his failure to be guided by the public interest in his work, thereby abusing the exercise of his administrative powers and violating the provisions of Article 14 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 and its amendments (Civil Servants Regulations), which entails his disciplinary liability. Whereas nothing has been established from the minutes of the interrogation of Messrs.: .........., nor from the written defence of each of them, that would exempt them from liability, which requires taking the appropriate disciplinary measures against them, pursuant to the provisions of Articles 54 and 55 of Legislative Decree No. 112 /59 and its amendments (Civil Servants Regulations).

Secretariat of the Board Session: 19/2003 Item: 11 Decision No. 240/2003 The Central Inspection Board, Having perused the file of the case registered under No. 43/7B/2002 with all its contents. Having perused the reports of the Financial Inspector Mr. Edouard Eid dated 3/1/2003, 26/2/2003 and 2/4/2003, resulting from the inspection of the Traffic, Trucks and Vehicles Management Authority. Having perused the opinions of the Financial Inspector General dated 8/1/2003, 27/2/2003 and 2/4/2003 Having perused the two opinions of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Accounts No. 50/268 dated 4/2/2003 and No. 154/1218 dated 23/4/2003 Having perused the opinion of the President of the Central Inspection dated 8/5/2003 Whereas it transpired from the documents of the file that an inspection of the Traffic, Trucks and Vehicles Management Authority was conducted, and that the mission covered examining the administrative conditions of the Authority, the manner of granting local and international driving licences, the payment by instalments of then public licence plates, and the payment of traffic fees in banks as well as the cash counts of the treasuries affiliated to the Ministry of Finance, pursuant to the annual inspection programme pertaining to the General Financial Inspectorate for the year 2002 Whereas it transpired that the Traffic, Trucks and Vehicles Management Authority was established pursuant to Decree No. 4082 dated 14/10/2000 (Organisation of the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities) as a public institution enjoying moral personality and financial and administrative autonomy, linked to the Minister of Interior and Municipalities who exercises administrative tutelage over it, and that the texts governing the workflow in the said public institution have not been laid down to date, which led to the occurrence of an overlap in powers between.......... on the one hand and.......... in the Ministry of Interior on the other hand, notably with respect to the retention by the latter of employee files and other files pertaining to the Authority including the file of public licence plates, which necessitates recommending working to expedite the laying down of the regulatory texts necessary for the Authority and handing over to it all the files pertaining to it. Whereas it transpired that the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities has been accustomed to appointing chairmen and members of driving committees without them fulfilling the conditions stipulated in Article 55 of the Traffic Law with respect to the chairman of the committee being of the Third Category at least, and its members of the First Rank in the Fourth Category at least, and all of them being permanent employees on the cadre of the said Ministry, and that the allowances received by the chairmen and members of the driving committees, set pursuant to Decree No. 13304 dated 8/7/63 at /22/ L.L. for the chairman and /16/ L.L. for the member, for each session, are no longer commensurate with the current living conditions, which requires recommending working to observe the conditions set in Article 55 of the Traffic Law, and increasing the allowances of the chairmen and members of the driving committees in a manner commensurate with the current situation of the exchange rate of the Lebanese Pound. Whereas it transpired that the places designated for conducting driving examinations do not enjoy the technical specifications, and that the certificates issued by the majority of Mukhtars do not have the due fiscal stamps affixed to them, and also that the renewal of driving licences is calculated from the date of submitting the renewal application and not from the date of expiry of the validity of the old licence, which requires recommending to the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities to work on establishing places for conducting driving examinations that fulfil the required technical conditions, and circulating to the Mukhtars the necessity of abiding by the contents of the Schedule annexed to the Fiscal Stamp Fee Law with respect to affixing stamps on the certificates and attestations issued by them, and coordinating with the Ministry of Finance to work on issuing the necessary text in order to impose a delay fine on those who default on renewing driving licences on their due dates, and the necessity of calculating the renewal of the licence with effect from the date of expiry of the validity of the old licence.

Whereas it has been established that .......... Mr. .........., has exercised his powers in accordance with his specified duties, and has supervised and inspected the Civil Status Registry of Sidon, and has checked its conditions and the progress of work therein in accordance with the rules, and has also initiated the taking of the necessary measures upon his discovery of the violations occurring in the aforementioned registry, a matter which requires disregarding his liability and closing the case in this respect. Whereas it has been established that the custody ledger pertaining to the transactions referred from the Civil Status Registry of Sidon to the Civil Status Registry of South Lebanon, was lost from the aforementioned knowledge, and that the employee responsible for keeping this register reported its disappearance on 2/7/2002, after it had been in his possession until the end of the official working hours of the previous day, noting that the loss of the aforementioned ledger did not affect the progress and completion of the transactions of the concerned parties, as they are also recorded in the outgoing and incoming register in accordance with the rules. Whereas it is required, and given that the investigation did not arrive at discovering and determining the person responsible for the loss of the register of legal and administrative texts and the custody ledger, to recommend to the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities to take the appropriate measures regarding the loss of the two aforementioned registers. After deliberation, and in light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided: 1 - To deduct the salary of .......... at the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities, Directorate General of Personal Status, assigned .......... Sidon, Mr. .......... (his financial number ..........) for seven days by way of discipline. 2 - To deduct the salary of .......... at the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities, Directorate General of Personal Status, Civil Status Registry of Sidon, Mr. .......... (his financial number ..........), for one day by way of discipline. 3 - To reprimand .......... at the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities, Directorate General of Personal Status, Civil Status Registry of South Lebanon, Mr. .......... 4 - To disregard the liability of .......... South Lebanon, Mr. .......... 5 - To recommend to the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities, Directorate General of Personal Status, to take the appropriate measures and procedures regarding the loss of the two registers of the custody ledger and the legal and administrative texts from the Civil Status Registry of Sidon. A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the fourteenth of the month of May of the year two thousand and three.

And whereas it has been established that the operation of issuing international driving licences is entrusted to the offices of the administration and to the Automobile and Touring Club of Lebanon, which is internationally licensed to issue such licences, yet there are other clubs that proceed with issuing international driving licences without having obtained a legal licence to do so, some of which proceed with remitting the fees collected by them to the Treasury cash office (..........), and some of which retain those fees for their own benefit without remitting them to the Treasury (..........), and that the competent administrative authorities do not exercise any operation of supervision or control over the printing of the forms of international driving licences issued by the offices of.......... in order to verify the number of licences granted and the total of their actual revenues, which consequently requires recommending that the requisite legal measures be taken against the clubs referred to above, and that the printing of the forms of international driving licences issued by the entities licensed to grant them be supervised. And whereas it has been established that many of those who acquired ownership of public licence plates pursuant to Law No. 384 dated 4/11/1994 have ceased to pay the due instalments after having settled the value of the first payment thereof, and that Article Seven of Decision No. 263/A.D., issued by the Minister of the Interior on 31/10/95, relating to the administrative and legal procedures for executing the payment by instalments of the price of public licence plates, provided that if the purchaser defaults on the payment of any of the due instalments, a formal notice to pay shall be served upon him in accordance with the rules of procedure, and if the default on payment continues after the maturity of the following instalment, all remaining instalments shall fall due in a single lump sum within a period of one month from the date of service of the second formal notice under penalty of forfeiture of his right to the plate allocated to him, and the amount that he may have paid shall be refunded to him after deducting a rate of 5% therefrom, which consequently requires recommending that the appropriate legal measures be taken against those in default of settling the due instalments of the price of public licence plates in order to safeguard the funds of the Treasury. And whereas the cash count of the cash offices at the Traffic, Trucks and Vehicles Management Authority did not reveal the existence of significant discrepancies between the holdings of those cash offices and the balances extracted from the records, a matter which necessitates disregarding the liability of the employees in this respect.

And after deliberation, and in light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided - to recommend to the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities, and the Traffic, Trucks and Vehicles Management Authority, each within its own jurisdiction, the following: 1 - To expedite the issuance of the regulatory texts for the Traffic, Trucks and Vehicles Management Authority, and to hand over to the aforementioned Authority all files pertaining to it. 2 - To appoint the driving committees in accordance with the conditions specified in the Traffic Law, and to increase the allowances of each of their chairmen and members in proportion to the current situation of the exchange rate of the Lebanese pound. 3 - To establish venues for conducting driving examinations that fulfil all required technical conditions. 4 - To circulate to the mukhtars the necessity of abiding by the content of the schedule annexed to the Fiscal Stamp Duty Law, with respect to affixing a stamp of the /1000/ L.L. denomination on every statement or certificate issued by any of them. 5 - To issue the necessary text in coordination with the Ministry of Finance, in order to impose a late fine on those who default on renewing driving licences on their due dates, and the necessity of calculating the renewal of the licence with effect from the date of expiry of the validity of the old licence. 6 - To supervise the printing of driving licence forms the issuance of which is entrusted to the offices of.......... to the exclusion of others, and to take the appropriate legal measures against each of.......... and Tourism, for their having proceeded to issue international driving licences without a legal licence. 7 - To prosecute the.......... Club before the competent judiciary, and to compel it to pay the fees and fines due from it in favour of the Treasury, and to prohibit it from issuing international driving licences permanently. 8 - To take the appropriate measures against those who default on paying the due instalments of the price of public number plates, in accordance with what is provided for in the preceding Article of Decision No. 263/A.D. dated 31/10/ 1995 9 - To close the case with respect to liability. A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the twentieth of the month of May in the year two thousand and three.

And whereas Mrs..........., in the foregoing circumstances, has violated the duties of office stipulated in Article 14 of the Civil Servants Regulations, which entails disciplinary liability on her part in this regard pursuant to the provisions of the aforementioned Article, and whereas that which was stated in the record of her interrogation and in her written defence does not absolve her of this liability, which requires taking the appropriate disciplinary measures against her pursuant to the provisions of Articles 54 and 55 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 and its amendments. And whereas it was established that.......... Mr..........., approved the disbursement of the expenditure relating to the maintenance of the elevator in the Directorate General of Cooperatives despite the works having been received only by.......... on the committee, and without auditing the transaction to ascertain the extent of its conformity with the laws and regulations in force, and also neglected the supervision over the acts of.......... in the Directorate General Mrs........... who signed an administrative leave decision for one of the employees working in the Directorate General of Cooperatives after the expiry of the period of delegation granted to her in this respect, in addition to his acceptance of the daily attendance of a former contractor with the Directorate General after the expiry of the term of the contract, and his proceeding with the processing of a mutual agreement contract to complete a study with a former contractor with the Ministry where a period of five years had not elapsed since his leaving the Directorate General. And whereas Mr..........., in the foregoing circumstances, has violated the provisions of the seventh paragraph of Item Second of the seventh Article of Legislative Decree No. 111/59 (supervising the workflow in the administration) and the fifth paragraph of the eighth Article of the same Legislative Decree (responsibility for the acts of the administration), and Article 68 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59, which does not permit contracting with a civil servant placed on retirement or dismissed from service for having reached the legal age, which entails disciplinary liability on his part in this regard, and whereas that which was stated in the record of his interrogation and in his written defence does not absolve him of this liability, which requires taking the appropriate measures against him pursuant to the provisions of Articles 54 and 55 of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 and its amendments. And whereas the violation committed by.......... in the Directorate General of Cooperatives Mrs.........., consisting in her referral of one of the transactions to the Accounting Department to complete the legal procedures without giving it a registration number or a correct date, did not cause a waste of public funds and was committed in good faith, whereby her liability may be disregarded.

And whereas it has been established that the approval of the establishment of cooperative associations is carried out in an arbitrary manner and without the fulfilment of the required conditions, and that financial assistance is granted to those associations without verifying that its disbursement is carried out in accordance with the prescribed objectives, which requires recommending the necessity of strictness in applying the laws and regulations in force governing the establishment of cooperative associations, monitoring the purpose of the agreement of the financial assistance granted to the associations, auditing the records of the latter and verifying the feasibility of their activities. And after deliberation, and in light of the circumstances of the case. It was decided 1 - To deduct the salary of.......... Mr.........., for three days by way of reprimand. 2 - To deduct the salary of.........., Mrs.........., (her financial number..........) for two days by way of discipline. 3 - To disregard the liability of.......... in the Directorate General of Cooperatives, Mrs.........., for the reasons set forth in the body of this decision. 4 - To recommend to the Ministry of Agriculture - Directorate General of Cooperatives - the necessity of strictness in applying the provisions of the laws and regulations in force with respect to: a - Forming cooperative training committees. b - The fulfilment of the required conditions for establishing cooperative associations. c - Monitoring the purpose of expenditure of the financial assistance granted to cooperative associations, auditing the records of the latter and investigating the utility of their activity. A decision issued unanimously in Beirut on the twenty-fifth of the month of June in the year two thousand and three.

Secretariat of the Board Session: 26/2003 Item: 5 Decision No. 322/2003 The Central Inspection Board, having reviewed the file of the case registered under No. 58 W2/7B/2003 in all its contents.

1598/W2003 Having reviewed the two reports of the Financial Inspector Mr. Ahmad Al-Husari dated 24/3/2003 and 15/5/2003, relating to the comprehensive inspection of both the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Energy and Water. Having reviewed the opinion of the Financial Inspector General dated 6/6/ 2003 Having reviewed the opinion of the President of the Central Inspection dated 27 /6/2003 Whereas it appeared from the documents of the file that an audit by sampling was conducted on the transactions received by the Directorate of Expenditures, Audit and Disbursement Department, in the Ministry of Finance, particularly those received from the Ministry of Energy and Water, pursuant to the annual inspection programme pertaining to the General Financial Inspectorate for the year 2002 Whereas it appeared that the Directorate of Expenditures in the Ministry of Finance issued on 17/9/2002 a payment order in the amount of twenty-three million and ninety-nine thousand Lebanese pounds, bearing the number 150414 in favour of.........., and that the said payment order was free of any notation of attachment or assignment, and was delivered on 30/9/ 2002 to the employee Mr........... Ministry of Energy and Water, who in turn delivered it to.......... in the Ministry. Whereas it appeared that.......... in the Ministry of Energy and Water had previously received a notice of service of a precautionary attachment issued by the Execution Department in Baakline upon the entitlements belonging to the company.......... in order to secure the debt of the attaching party Mr........... Alameh, which was registered in the said Ministry under No. 587/31 dated 5/9 /2002, contrary to the provisions of the eighty-sixth article of the Public Accounting Law, which provides that attachment decisions and deeds of assignment relating to debts owed by the State shall be served upon the competent authority for issuing payment orders, and no service addressed to anyone else shall be recognised, and the said authority must record the attachment or assignment on the payment order before issuing it. Whereas the seventy-ninth article of the Public Accounting Law provided that the issuance of payment orders shall be undertaken, in the name of the Minister of Finance, by.......... which indicates that the act of the Ministry of Justice in depositing the notice referred to above with the Ministry of Energy and Water was done by mistake, noting that the investigation into this matter falls outside the jurisdiction of the Central Inspection. Whereas it appeared that.......... in the Ministry of Energy and Water, and Mr..........., retained the original attachment addressed to him by mistake in the Ministry of Justice, without returning it to the said Ministry for it to be deposited with the competent authority, or submitting the matter to his superiors, or informing the Directorate of Expenditures, the sole entity authorised to receive and execute attachments, so as to proceed with describing the issuance of the payment order by it, pending its official notification of the attachment decision by the Ministry of Justice, especially since the time period separating the receipt of the notice by him and the issuance of the payment order by the Ministry of Finance approached twelve days, a matter which entails disciplinary liability on his part for which he must be prosecuted.

Whereas it has been established, on the other hand, that .......... at the Ministry of Energy and Water requested from the Directorate of Expenditures at the Ministry of Finance, pursuant to his referral No. 587/31 dated 1/10/2002, the retrieval of the payment order due to his inability to deliver it to its beneficiary, yet he retained the aforementioned referral until 2/1/2003, when it was sent to the Ministry of Finance and registered at the Directorate of Expenditures on the said date, and that .......... of the said Directorate denied any knowledge of the matter until that date, that is, after the lapse of more than three months from the receipt of the payment order by .......... of the Ministry of Energy and Water. Whereas it has been established that .......... at the Ministry of Energy and Water misbehaved during his interrogation by the Inspection, uttering profane words and thereby exceeding the bounds of disciplinary propriety, and that his personal file contains several decisions pursuant to which he was penalised by his superiors, which indicates his persistence in violating the duties imposed by the laws and regulations in force. Whereas it has been established that .......... at the Ministry of Energy and Water, Mr .........., declared before the Inspection that he was verbally instructed on 1/10/2002 to seek clarification from the Ministry of Finance regarding the manner of delivering the payment order pertaining to the company .......... after the Ministry had received the attachment decision from the Ministry of Justice on 5/9/2002, whereas Mr .......... stated before .......... at the Ministry of Energy and Water that he went to the registry of the Directorate of Expenditures to deliver the aforementioned transaction, thereby giving two contradictory statements, which entails disciplinary liability on his part in this regard, and that what he submitted in his written defence, namely that the reason for the contradiction was due to his failure to remember the transaction under investigation, cannot be relied upon to justify this matter.

Secretariat of the Board Session: 30/2003 Item: 6 Decision No. 364/2003 The Central Inspection Board, having perused the file of the case registered under No. 37/7/2002 in all its contents.

2363/2002 Having perused the report of the Financial Inspector Mr. Jean Haddad dated 29/5/2003, following the investigation into the violations attributed to certain employees working at the Chtaura Telephone Centre. And whereas it appeared from the statement of.......... of Chtaura Telephone, Mr..........., that.......... Mr...........,.........., used to assist him in the event of severe work pressure, and used the stamp present on his desk to stamp the receipts for the settlement of telephone fees, while Mr........... undertook, solely, the registration of the receipts in the detailed statement book of collections, and Mr........... also stated that there existed a number of receipts in the possession of certain subscribers which were stamped and unsigned, and pertaining to the period between the months of April and May of the year 2002, and that these receipts were not settled into the cash office and not registered on the detailed statement of collections, which indicates that Mr........... relinquished his responsibilities. Whereas it has been established that .......... of Chtaura Telephone, Mr. .........., proceeded to assign .......... at the center, Mr. .......... to assist .......... verbally, contrary to the law, and he also proceeded, with Mr. .......... through assisting him, in the event of his presence, to stamp, withdraw and settle the invoices and use the stamps, or during his absence where Mr. .......... used to perform the duties of .......... with the knowledge and approval of ........... Secretariat of the Board Session: 20/2003 Item: 5 Decision No. 247/2003 The Central Inspection Board, Having examined the file of the case registered under No. 56/7/2002 with all its contents.

3444/W2002 Having examined the reports of the Financial Inspectors Messrs.: Mahmoud Al-Moussawi, Wafic Rihan, Mohammad Mashmoushi, Mohammad Salim Tabbara, and Emilie Asbar dated 23/12/2002, 21/1/2003, 3/2/ 2003, 20/2/2003 and 8/4/2003 respectively, as a result of the investigation into the delivery to certain governmental hospitals, dispensaries, and health centres of medicines nearing their expiry date from the warehouses of the Ministry of Public Health. Having examined the opinion of the Financial Inspector General dated 14/4/ 2003 Having examined the opinion of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Audit No. 161/1327 dated 5/5/2003 Having examined the opinion of the President of the Central Inspection dated 15 /5/2003 Whereas it appears from the documents of the file that, within the framework of the Financial Inspection conducting an investigation into the subject of foodstuff purchases at the Tyre Governmental Hospital, the aforementioned .......... raised the issue of his receipt of medicines nearing their expiry date from the warehouses of the Ministry of Public Health, and the President of the Central Inspection issued Assignment No. 56/7/2002 to investigate the matter. Whereas it appears as a result of the investigation that the Ministry of Public Health purchases medicines from agents and warehouses pursuant to consensual contracts, and that these contracts include clauses capable of preserving the rights of the Administration, particularly with respect to the validity period of the purchased medicines, which must not be less than eighteen months, and other clauses relating to the right of the Administration to replace medicines whose validity period has expired with similar items or items of the same kind, whereas it appears on the other hand that the contracts signed with the United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) do not include such clauses, which leads to a waste of public funds in the event that they are not consumed within the validity period, which consequently requires recommending that the Ministry of Public Health work to include in the contracts signed with the United Nations Organization (UNICEF) clauses permitting the replacement of items whose validity period has expired. Whereas it appears, secondly, that the Ministry of Public Health delivers medicines to the governmental hospitals, dispensaries, and health centres affiliated with it in all Lebanese regions, pursuant to delivery documents based on requests drawn up by these centres, and that these documents clearly indicate the expiry date of the validity of these medicines, and it issues the necessary instructions to the hospitals and health centres with regard to the medicines delivered to them which are nearing their expiry date. Whereas it appears as a result of the audit and by way of sampling certain documents issued by the Central Warehouse at the Ministry of Public Health that all the lists bear the validity expiry dates, and that they range between one week or two months, four years, and sometimes nine years, and that despite the existence of short validity periods for certain medicines, no use was made of them, as these centres are aware of the matter and proceed to return them to the Ministry of Public Health to be replaced by it, in accordance with the contracts signed with the agents, which consequently requires recommending that the Ministry of Public Health - Directorate General of Health - refrain from delivering medicines nearing their expiry date, work to replace the items whose period has expired, and work to replace the medicine propofol supplied by the agent, .......... Company, whose validity period expired on 1/7/2001, which was delivered to the Tripoli Governmental Hospital on 26/ 6/2001

- The draft Law promulgated by Decree No. 13068 dated 5 August 2004 concerning Consumer Protection, as amended by the Joint Parliamentary Committees and the Chamber of Deputies, is hereby ratified.

- This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

This Law aims to:

Establish the general rules governing consumer protection and the health, safety and quality of goods and services.

Safeguard the rights of the consumer and ensure the transparency of economic transactions to which the consumer is a party.

Protect the consumer against fraud and misleading advertising and prevent the exploitation thereof.

The provisions of this Law shall not govern the relations binding professionals among themselves.

The consumer enjoys the following rights, which he exercises in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

The right to the preservation of his health and safety when using, in an appropriate manner, the good or service with respect to quality and kind.

The right to benefit from fair treatment and without discrimination on the part of the professional, for the product prepared for local use or for export.

The right to obtain accurate, clear and comprehensive information relating to the good or service, its price, its characteristics, the methods of its use, and the hazards that may result from such use.

The right to have the good replaced or repaired or to recover its price, as well as to be refunded the amounts he may have paid in consideration of a service, in the event of its non-conformity, when properly used, whether with the agreed-upon or applicable specifications, or with the purpose for which it was obtained.

The right to full and appropriate compensation for damages resulting from the consumption of a good or the enjoyment of a service when properly used.

The right to establish consumer protection associations and to join them. The right to litigate directly or collectively through consumer associations, to safeguard his rights or to compensate him for the damages that may have been sustained by him.

The professional must provide the consumer with accurate, comprehensive, and clear information covering:

The essential data of the good or service and the methods of using it.

The price and the terms and procedures of contracting, the risks that may result from use

The professional must:

Display the price in Lebanese Pounds in a visible manner by affixing it either on the good or on the shelf on which it is displayed.

Comply with the official system of measurement relating to weights and volumes.
Prices must be displayed, in a prominent place, in establishments that provide services, in particular hotels, furnished apartments, restaurants, cafes, and entertainment venues.

There must be included on the labels of the good or packaging the information specified by the competent Administration, according to the nature of each good, its characteristics, and in accordance with the applicable specifications. The aforementioned information includes, by way of example and not limitation:

The nature of the good and its type, its elements and/or its composition or its ingredients. The net weight of the good or its volume or its number.

The validity period of the good.

The country of origin, or the entity of origin with respect to recognised unions of States.

The name of the manufacturer or professional and his address.

The risks and precautions arising from the use of the good.
Unpackaged foodstuffs sold in the grocery trade (mal al-qabban) shall be subject to the supervision of the Consumer Protection Directorate.

The Arabic language shall be adopted in principle for drafting the information required to be included whether on the label of the commodity or on the packaging, and in general in every act aimed at displaying the commodity or the service.

The cases in which either the English or French language may be adopted as an alternative to the Arabic language shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Economy and Trade.

A professional who displays commodities that are used or refurbished or that contain a defect that does not result in any harm to the health and safety of the consumer shall declare the condition of the said commodity visibly and clearly on the commodity as well as in the place where he carries out his activity, and he shall indicate the same whether in the contract that he may draw up or on the invoice that he issues.

Deceptive advertising is advertising, conducted by any means whatsoever, that deals with a commodity or a service, and includes a false presentation, statement or claim or is drafted in terms liable to lead, directly or indirectly, to deceiving or misleading the consumer.

The presentation, statement or claim referred to above which deals with one of the following matters, by way of example and not limitation, shall be considered deceptive:

- The nature of the commodity, its composition, its essential qualities, or the elements of which it consists and the quantity of these elements.

- The origin of the commodity, its weight, its volume, its method of manufacture, its expiry date, the conditions of its use, or the precautions of such use.

- The type of service, the place agreed upon for providing it, the precautions of its use, and its essential qualities whether in terms of quality or in terms of the intended benefits.

- The conditions of contracting, the amount of the total price, and the manner of its payment.

- The obligations undertaken by the advertiser.

- The identity, qualifications, and qualities of the manufacturer or the professional.

The following shall also be considered deceptive advertising:

Advertising in which the advertiser falsely attributes to himself that he holds official or private awards, certificates, attestations, or medals, as well as the claim of the existence of scientific grounds whereas in reality they are unavailable or unserious.

Advertising that includes the use of an emblem or a trademark without right, or the use of a counterfeit or imitated mark.

The advertiser shall prove the accuracy of the information contained in his advertisement and provide each of the Consumer Protection Directorate or the competent court hearing the case with the documents that it may request.

For the purpose of applying the provisions of this Law, the following definitions shall be adopted:

- "Consumer" is the natural or legal person who purchases, leases, uses or benefits from a service or a good, for purposes not directly related to his professional activity.

- "Professional" is the natural or legal person, from the private or public sector, who exercises, in his own name or on behalf of third parties, an activity consisting of distributing, selling or leasing goods or providing services.

Shall also be deemed a professional, for the purpose of applying the provisions of this Law, any person who imports the good with the aim of selling, leasing or distributing it within the framework of exercising his professional activity.

- "Manufacturer" is the person who transforms or assembles raw or intermediate materials.

- "Good" is any immovable property, as well as movable property whether foodstuff or transformed or manufactured natural property.

- "Service" is any work consisting of a technical, craft or intellectual activity, whatever the description given to it by the professional and the consumer.

"Price" and it includes the sale price or the consideration for lease or use.

- "Specifications" are the mandatory specifications and technical rules that determine the characteristics of the service or the product or the methods of production and management systems, and may also include the terminology, symbols, data, packaging, marking and labelling requirements that apply to the product or its methods of production or are confined to any of them, and compliance with which is mandatory.

- "Consumer Associations" is every association established for non-political, non-commercial or non-economic purposes, and aiming to raise the awareness of consumers, educate them, guide them, protect their interests and rights, and represent them before all authorities, official and private.

- "Advertiser" is every person who requests the broadcasting or publication of the advertisement by any means whatsoever.

- "Emergency Cases" are the cases that cannot bear passing through normal procedures and have a major impact on national security and the health and safety of humans, animals and plants and call for taking immediate measures to address them.

The Ministry of Economy and Trade shall request the advertiser to correct or amend his advertisement and to republish or broadcast the correction or amendment through the means that were used to broadcast or publish the deceptive advertisement. The court before which the case is pending may decide, of its own motion, to suspend the broadcasting of the deceptive advertisement. The decision taken in this regard shall be enforceable on the original.

The judicial authority that took the decision may revoke it.

A decree taken in the Council of Ministers, upon the proposal of the Minister of Economy and Trade, shall determine the general principles governing advertisements dealing with goods and services and the basic conditions that must be met in these advertisements.

A professional who resorts to advertising a special offer, for the purpose of promoting a good or a service, shall specify either the period during which this good or service will be available or the available quantity, and he shall also announce, where applicable, the conditions of contracting.

In the event that the period or the quantity is not specified, the offer shall be deemed valid for a period of one month starting from the date of the first advertisement, unless the professional announces in the same manner and through the same advertising medium the date of the end of his offer.

If the professional is unable to provide the promoted good or service in accordance with the announced conditions, the consumer shall be entitled to one of the following two rights:

Accepting a good or service equivalent to the announced good or service if the professional offers that, or cancelling the contract and recovering any amount that the consumer may have paid in addition to claiming compensation for the damage sustained by him, provided that its amount is not less than the difference between the price of the good or service during the offer and its price thereafter.

The provisions of this Law relating to contracts binding the professional to the consumer shall apply in all that does not conflict with the legal texts governing the work of liberal professions, banks, and insurance companies.

Contracts shall be interpreted in the interest of the consumer; into consideration shall be taken, to determine the extent of the availability of the consumer's consent, the circumstances of contracting, the benefits that the contract grants him, and the balance between the rights and obligations of the two parties.

The professional and the service provider shall deliver to the consumer an invoice setting out the following particulars:

The name of the establishment, its registration number in the Commercial Register and its address, the identification of the good or service, the unit of sale or lease and its price, the agreed quantity, the amount of taxes and fees levied, the total value of the invoice in Lebanese currency and the date of its issuance.

In the event that the good or service is not delivered immediately, the invoice shall include mention of the place, date and conditions of delivery.

Clauses aimed at or capable of causing an imbalance between the rights and obligations of the professional and the consumer to the detriment of the latter shall be deemed abusive clauses.

The abusive nature of a clause shall be assessed as at the date of contracting and by reference to the provisions of the contract and its annexes, with the exception of those relating to the price.

Any of the following clauses, by way of example and not limitation, shall be deemed abusive clauses:

- Clauses excluding the liability of the professional.

- Waiver by the consumer of any of his rights provided for in the laws and regulations.

- Placing the burden of proof on the consumer in cases other than those provided for by law.

- Granting the professional, unilaterally, the authority to amend all or some of the provisions of the contract, particularly those relating to the price or the date or place of delivery.

- Granting the professional the right to terminate a contract of indefinite duration without notifying the consumer of his wish to do so within a reasonable period.

- Obliging the consumer, in the event of his failure to perform any of his contractual obligations, to pay the professional compensation disproportionate to the damages resulting therefrom.

- Granting the professional the right to interpret the provisions of the contract.

- Obliging the consumer to perform his obligations in the event that the professional abstains from performing what he undertook to do.

- Prohibiting recourse to mediation or arbitration for the settlement of disputes in accordance with the provisions of this Law, or charging the consumer with the expenses that may be incurred by following the said procedures.

Abusive clauses shall be deemed null and void with absolute nullity, provided that the other provisions of the contract produce all their effects.

The contract prepared by the professional, or the adoption of which is approved by the official administrations, or the provisions of which the consumer is not permitted to amend, must fulfill the following conditions:

That it be drafted in the Arabic language and in clear and comprehensible terms.

Provided that a contract may be concluded by adopting a foreign language in the event of agreement of the contracting parties thereon.

That it neither refer to nor incorporate texts or documents that were not placed at the disposal of the consumer prior to signature.

That it specify explicitly and clearly the price and the date and manner of its payment as well as the date and place of delivery.
The professional shall deliver to the consumer a copy of the contract which he adopts in order to examine its content prior to signing it.

The professional who offers that the price of the good or service be paid in instalments must or provide the consumer with the following information:

The price in the event of payment in cash and without instalments. The adopted annual interest, and whether the interest is simple or compound, and the manner of calculating it the total amount which represents the sum of the interest due and the expenses of whatever kind.

The number of instalments and the value and maturity date of each of them.

The total value after division into instalments such as to include the value of the good or service in the event that its price was paid in cash with the interest and expenses added thereto.

The rights and obligations of each of the professional and the consumer in the event of breach by either of them of the conditions of the agreement.

The professional must also include in the contract which he concludes all the information mentioned above.
The professional shall deliver to the consumer a copy of the contract signed by him, and this copy shall be exempt from all fees, in particular the fiscal stamp duty.

The consumer may, at any time, pay the value of all the instalments prior to their maturity provided that the amount of the interest that was due shall be deducted from this value.

The procedures for the application of the preceding paragraph and, where applicable, the resulting penalties shall be specified in the contract which financial or banking institutions conclude with the consumer.

Paid amounts shall not be considered earnest money unless the consumer has been informed in advance and in writing that his withdrawal from contracting entails the inadmissibility of recovering these amounts.

The professional or manufacturer must:

- Provide the parts or components necessary for the use of a specific good or service.

- Provide maintenance and after-sales service.

The professional or manufacturer shall be deemed bound by these obligations during a reasonable period commensurate with the expected duration of use of the good or service, unless he informs the consumer, expressly and in writing, of a different period.

The professional or manufacturer shall be exempted from the obligations mentioned above, in the event that he informed the consumer, expressly and in writing, and in a prominent and unambiguous manner, of his non-commitment to any of them.

The professional warrants the quality of the good or service and the availability of the specifications that he determined or those whose existence the consumer stipulated in writing.

He also warrants the consumer's possession of the good or service without opposition issuing from any third party whatsoever.

The professional may not include in the contracts that he concludes any clause exempting him from the obligations mentioned above.

The professional warrants against latent defects that appreciably diminish the value of the good or service or render it unfit for use for that for which it was intended in accordance with its nature or the provisions of the contract.

As for defects that only slightly diminish the value of the good or service or the enjoyment thereof, as well as defects customarily tolerated, they do not entail warranty.

The professional must include the text of the preceding paragraph in all documents that he delivers to the consumer.

The professional may undertake additional warranties. In this case, these warranties shall be added to those provided for in this Law.

The consumer or his allies must prove, by all means, the existence of the latent defect at the date of delivery and that there resulted from this defect either an appreciable diminution of the value of the good or service or the rendering of it unfit for use for that for which it was intended.

The warranty action must be brought or the mediation or dispute resolution procedures provided for in this Law must be initiated within a time limit of one month following the date of discovery of the defect, unless his non-compliance with this time limit is due to the professional's resort to dilatory means.

The consumer may request the cancellation of the contract and the recovery of the price paid by him in the event of failure to replace the good or service that contains any of the defects provided for in Articles 28 and 29 of this Law, or in the event of failure to repair it within a reasonable time limit commensurate with the nature of the good or service.

The consumer may also, in addition to the foregoing, claim compensation for the damages that may have been sustained by him.

Prior to carrying out any repairs to a good, the professional shall inform the consumer in writing and free of charge of his estimate of the cost of repair and the validity period of his offer. The professional shall also, after carrying out the repair operation, specify in the invoice he issues the parts that have been replaced and their price, and specify whether these parts are new, used, or refurbished.

The professional shall warrant the replaced parts and bear the cost of labour for a period of three months running from the date of delivery of the good after its repair.

This warranty shall not cover the case where the good, which has been repaired, is used in an inappropriate manner.
The provisions of this Chapter shall be deemed of public policy.

The provisions of this Law relating to the safety and health of the consumer shall apply in addition to the provisions contained in the laws and regulations in force that set out special specifications for a specific good or service and the conditions for placing it on the market.

The professional shall provide the consumer with the essential information concerning the assessment of the risks associated with the use of the good or service during the foreseeable period of its use.

Every manufacturer or professional shall indicate to the consumer, in writing and clearly, the optimal method for using the good or service, and shall warn of the risks that may befall the consumer if it is used in a contrary manner.

The information mentioned above must be included in the Arabic language.

The professional who offers, for the first time, a good or service for circulation in the markets shall verify its conformity with the specifications provided for in the laws and regulations in force.

He shall also prove that the safety standards are met in the said good or service when used in an appropriate and normal manner.

The Lebanese Accreditation Council, established pursuant to Law No. 572 dated 11/2/2004, shall designate the local and international laboratories, accreditation agencies, and pre-inspection and control offices whose certificates relating to the safety of goods, particularly food products, are recognised in Lebanon.

The Lebanese Accreditation Council, established pursuant to Law No. 572 dated 11/2/2004, shall determine the conditions for granting scientific institutions the authority to issue certificates relating to the conformity of goods and services with approved specifications.

The Consumer Protection Directorate at the Ministry of Economy and Trade may request that a specific commodity be subjected to testing in accredited laboratories at the expense of the professional or manufacturer, particularly when it is offered on the markets for the first time or where it is suspected that it may pose a danger to the health and safety of the consumer.

The Director General of Economy and Trade may, where necessary, authorise the re-testing of the said commodity, provided that the professional shall bear the expenses of the re-testing if it is decided upon at his request.

The Minister of Economy and Trade may also, upon the proposal of the Director General of Economy and Trade, suspend trading in these commodities until the test results are received.
The professional shall refrain from trading in a commodity or service that does not conform to the approved specifications relating to public safety.

The injured party or his successors shall prove the lack of the approved specifications relating to safety that may legitimately be expected when the commodity or service is used in an appropriate and proper manner.

He shall also prove that damages resulted from the foregoing and the amount of such damages.

If it becomes apparent to the manufacturer or the professional, on the basis of his expertise or the information available to him, that the commodity or service that he placed into circulation contains one or more defects capable of harming the safety or health of the consumer or that it may pose a danger to him, the manufacturer or the professional shall take all necessary measures to inform the public, through the media, of these defects and warn it of the risks that may result therefrom. In this case, the manufacturer and the professional shall, in addition to the foregoing, take the following measures:

- Cease trading in the commodity or service.

- Withdraw the commodity from the markets.

- Recover the commodities that have been sold or leased and refund the price paid.

- Replace the commodities at his own expense or refund the price paid if it is impossible to repair them.

The professional or the manufacturer shall also, in the cases referred to above, notify the Consumer Protection Directorate at the Ministry of Economy of the said risks and shall specify the measures that he has taken.

Following the measures mentioned above shall not preclude obligating the professional or the manufacturer to compensate the consumer for the damages that may have been sustained by him.

The professional or manufacturer must refrain from performing any of the following acts:

Manufacturing, preparing, possessing, transporting, displaying or distributing any commodity or service, of whatever type, in a manner that conceals its true nature, its essential qualities or the proportion of the basic elements constituting it.

Counterfeiting or attempting to counterfeit a specific commodity. Manufacturing a commodity or providing a service that does not conform to the adopted mandatory specifications and constitutes a hazard to the health or safety of the consumer, or displaying or distributing this commodity or service or promoting, by all means, its use or purchase.

Delivering a commodity or service that does not conform to the adopted or agreed specifications, particularly with respect to its quantity, type, characteristics or origin.

Deceiving the consumer, whatever the means adopted therefor, such as omitting or concealing information or providing him with false information concerning the nature, type or source of the commodity or service, the essential qualities of each of them, its composition and components, or the manner of its use and its expiry period.

Any person is prohibited from performing any of the following acts:

Using uncalibrated scales or measures or other inaccurate machines intended for weighing, measuring by volume or measuring the commodity.

Using instruments or machines for the purpose of fraud.

Subject to the provisions of Article 11 of this Law, the professional is prohibited from:

Refraining from contracting or restricting the contracting to a number of commodities or services or to a specific quantity of each of them while his shops or warehouses are open for the sale of other commodities, unless these commodities or services are subject to a special official regime.

Making the sale of a commodity or the provision of a service conditional upon the purchase of a specific quantity or of another commodity or service, provided that there shall be exempted therefrom the case in which the consumer is able to purchase separately each commodity or service included in a combined offer or when these commodities and services constitute an indivisible unit.

Selling or leasing any commodity at a price exceeding the declared price.

Delivering a commodity or service to the consumer without the latter having expressed his desire to purchase or lease it.

Providing the consumer with false information concerning any of the following matters:

The date of delivery of the commodity or service.

The terms of contracting and the manner of determining and paying the price.

The Ministry of Economy and Trade shall, in the event that scientific information is established before it from an international or local body whose authority is officially recognised, regarding a risk to public health or safety that may result from the use or consumption of a specific good or service, whether such risk is occurring or anticipated, inform the public of the risks and the preventive measures to be followed, and in this case the Minister of Economy and Trade shall determine, by virtue of decisions issued by him, the measures conducive to preserving public health and safety, including:

- Prohibiting the import or export of the good in emergency cases.

- Determining special conditions for the import or export of the good.

- Prohibiting trading in the good or service.

- Withdrawing the good from circulation, provided that this is done at the expense of the professional or the manufacturer.

- Destroying the good at the expense of the professional and the manufacturer, jointly and severally between them, if this measure constitutes the sole

means of preserving public health and safety.

These decisions shall be announced through the media and notified to the Council of Ministers for approval thereof.

In normal circumstances, however, the approval of the Council of Ministers must be obtained prior to taking a decision prohibiting the import or export of the good.

The professional and the manufacturer shall remain liable for damage caused to public health and safety and resulting from a good or service in respect of which the competent administration had granted licences of whatever kind.

In this case, and unless the existence of a fault upon the granting of the licence is proven, the State or public institutions shall not be held liable for such damage.

There shall be determined, where necessary, by decrees issued upon the proposal of both the Minister of Economy and Trade and the competent Minister, and after consulting the "National Council for Consumer Protection" provided for in Article 60 of this Law, the special conditions relating to the import or export of a specific good.

Notwithstanding any other text, a consumer who enters into a contract in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter may withdraw from his decision to purchase or lease a commodity or to benefit from the service within a period of ten days running either from the date of contracting, in respect of services, or from the date of delivery, in respect of the commodity.

However, the consumer may not exercise the right provided for in the preceding paragraph in the following cases:

- If he has benefited from the service or used the commodity before the expiry of the ten-day period.

- If the agreement relates to commodities manufactured at his request or in accordance with specifications determined by him.

- If the agreement relates to video tapes, records, compact discs or computer software, in the event that their wrapping has been removed.

- If the purchase relates to newspapers, magazines and publications, in particular books.

- If the commodity has become defective as a result of improper possession thereof by the consumer.

The professional shall, in the event that the consumer exercises his right provided for in Article 55, refund the amounts that he has received, provided that the consumer bears, in the event that he withdraws from his decision to contract after delivery has taken place, the delivery expenses.
The method adopted for payment shall be secure and easy to use, and the consumer shall be provided with the conditions applicable to the method of payment.

The professional with whom the contract is concluded shall preserve the information that he obtains and shall not dispose thereof, unless the consumer expressly agrees thereto.

He shall also take all measures to preserve the confidentiality of such information.
A professional who uses indirect means for sale or leasing shall comply with the provisions of this Law, in particular those relating to deceptive advertising, promotion and public safety.

The provisions of this Chapter shall govern transactions conducted by a professional at a distance or at the consumer's place of residence, in particular those concluded at the consumer's place of residence or by telephone or the internet, or by any other means adopted for that purpose.

The provisions of this Chapter shall not govern financial and banking transactions, sales by public auction, and transactions involving immovable property.

The consumer must, in the cases provided for in Article 51, be provided with clear and explicit information covering the subjects that enable him to take his decision to enter into a contract, in particular:

- The identification of the professional, his name, address, registration number and place of registration, and his electronic mail address, in addition to any information allowing the identification of the professional.

- The good and service offered, the manner of its use, and the risks that may result from such use.

- The duration of the offer.

- The price of the good or service, the adopted currency, all amounts that may be added to the price, in particular fees, taxes and expenses of whatever kind, and the manner of payment of these amounts.

- The guarantees offered by the professional, and where applicable, the services provided by him after contracting.

- The duration of a contract involving goods or services supplied periodically.

- The date and place of delivery and the expenses payable in this respect.

- The procedures to be followed to terminate a contract that is automatically renewed upon the expiry of its term.

- The specification of the period during which the consumer may withdraw from his decision to purchase.

- The law governing the transaction and the bodies, courts or authorities competent to adjudicate any dispute that may arise from the contracting.

- The cost of communication.
The professional shall be required to deliver to the consumer a written document containing all the information provided for in Article 52

The information provided by the professional must enable the consumer to determine accurately and clearly the good or service offered, and to inspect a specimen of the adopted agreement.

The consumer must also be granted the right to correct or amend his order, in which case both parties shall retain a record of the entire transaction conducted by them.

There shall be established at the Ministry of Economy and Trade a body known as the "National Council for Consumer Protection", having an advisory capacity, chaired by the Minister of Economy and Trade, and composed of each of:

- The Director General of Economy and Trade

- The Director General of Agriculture

- The Director General of Public Health

- The Director General of Environment

- The Director General of Tourism

- The Director General of Telecommunications

- The Director General of Information

- The Director General of Education

- The Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Lebanese Standards Institution.

- Two representatives of the Federation of Chambers of Commerce, Industry and Agriculture in Lebanon, one of whom representing agriculturalists and the second merchants, appointed by the Minister of Economy and Trade upon the proposal of the Federation of Chambers of Commerce, Industry and Agriculture in Lebanon.

- A representative of industrialists appointed by the Minister of Economy and Trade upon the proposal of the Association of Lebanese Industrialists.

- A representative of the Syndicate of Advertising Agencies and Companies in Lebanon appointed by the Minister of Economy and Trade, upon the proposal of the Syndicate of Advertising Agencies and Companies in Lebanon.

- Two representatives of consumer associations appointed by the Minister of Economy and Trade upon the proposal of duly registered consumer associations.

The Chairman of the Council may invite any administration or institution concerned with any of the subjects placed on the agenda to attend working sessions, and may also seek the assistance of experts.

The "National Council for Consumer Protection" shall undertake to submit proposals conducive to achieving the following objectives:

- Supporting the role of the consumer in the national economy.

- Preserving the health, safety and rights of the consumer.

- Ensuring the safety of goods and services and improving their quality.

- Raising the awareness of the consumer, informing and guiding him, and urging him to use sustainable consumption patterns and to adopt goods and services that preserve the environment.

- Proposing the determination of the procedures for applying the provisions of this Law.
The work of the "National Council for Consumer Protection" shall be regulated by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Economy and Trade.

The Consumer Protection Department provided for in Article / 4/ of the Law put into force by Decree No. 6821 dated 28/12/ 1973 (determining the missions and cadres of the Ministry of Economy and Trade) is repealed, and there shall be established at the Directorate General of Economy and Trade the "Directorate of Consumer Protection".

1) The text of Article 8 of the Law implemented by Decree No. 6821 dated 28/12/1973 (defining the functions and cadres of the Ministry of Economy and Trade) is repealed and replaced by the following text:

-Article 8 (New):

First: The Consumer Protection Directorate shall undertake, in coordination with official and private bodies, the application of laws and regulations relating to consumer protection, in particular:

- Verifying the quality and safety of services and goods, especially food items among them, and carrying out the necessary examinations in respect thereof.

- Monitoring prices and their movement.

- Preparing documents and publications specific to raising the awareness of the consumer and guiding him.

- Carrying out research relating to the subjects mentioned above.

Second: The Consumer Protection Directorate shall be composed of:

1- The Department of Studies and Awareness, which shall undertake giving information relating to the laws and regulations governing consumer protection, preparing studies, submitting proposals and carrying out awareness campaigns, in coordination with official and private bodies.

2 - The Department of Control, which shall undertake receiving complaints, investigating them and applying the laws and regulations relating to consumer protection.

2) - Schedule No. (1) annexed to the Law implemented by Decree No. 6821 dated 28/12/1973 (defining the functions and cadres of the Ministry of Economy and Trade) is amended and replaced by Schedule No. (1) annexed to this Law.

3) The special conditions for appointment in the cadre of the Consumer Protection Directorate are defined in Schedule No. (2) annexed to this Law.

The Regional Departments in the governorates, each within its scope, shall represent the central administration.

They shall undertake in particular the application of the laws and regulations relating to consumer protection.

These Departments shall also undertake investigating complaints, combating fraud, monitoring prices, verifying the quality and safety of goods and services, and implementing the food safety policy.

The Regional Departments shall be functionally linked to the concerned unit in the central administration, with due regard to the provisions of Legislative Decree No. 116 dated 12/6/1959 (Administrative Organisation).
The expression "Consumer Protection Department" wherever it appears in legislative and regulatory texts is replaced by the expression "Consumer Protection Directorate".

First: The officials referred to in Article 71 may request the concerned parties to submit all documents, instruments and registers that prove the accuracy of the information they provide, and they may obtain copies of the aforementioned instruments and verify their accuracy by all legal means.

Second: The concerned party shall have the right, after being informed of the content of the provisions of Article 107 of this Law, to specify the nature of the documents and information that he wishes to keep confidential.

The officials mentioned in Article 71 of this Law, when performing their duties, shall take any of the following measures:

- Seize the papers provided for in Article 73 that prove the occurrence of the violation or that enable the identification of all persons who

participated in committing it, and they shall, in this case, hand over a receipt thereof to the concerned party.

- Seize the goods that turn out to be counterfeit, toxic, unfit for consumption or non-compliant with the approved standards or that

expose the health and safety of the consumer to a risk.

In this case, the commodity shall remain under the custody of the persons who hold it until the issuance of the results of the analyses or inspection,

provided that the seizure period does not exceed 45 days.

The officials mentioned in Article 71 of this Law shall, pursuant to a written authorisation from the competent Public Prosecution:

1 - Seize the materials, machinery and equipment that were used to manufacture, assemble and package adulterated goods or goods non-compliant with the approved standards or that expose the health and safety of the consumer to risk.

2 - Seal the premises with red wax and refer the file to the judiciary after conducting the necessary investigations .

The materials, machinery and equipment referred to above shall remain deposited with the person in whose possession they were found and under his custody unless they are transferred

to a place specified by the officials who drew up the report.

A commodity proven to be toxic or unfit for consumption must be destroyed, and a commodity proven to be counterfeit may also be destroyed, and in both cases the destruction process shall be carried out at the expense of the concerned party, after obtaining a written authorisation from the competent Public Prosecution.

Where necessary, the conditions and procedures of destruction shall be determined by decisions issued by the Minister of Economy and Trade.

Consumer associations aim at:

Defending the interests and rights of the consumer. Representing consumers collectively and free of charge before official bodies and administrations and professionals, and litigating for the purpose of preserving their rights.

Collecting and publishing information, analyses, tests and comparisons relating to goods and services and the manner of using them.

Carrying out campaigns to raise awareness among and guide consumers, issuing magazines, bulletins and publications, and preparing advertising and broadcast programmes intended for broadcasting or publication through the media, all in accordance with the laws in force.

Providing consultations.
The legal texts governing associations shall apply to consumer associations, in addition to the provisions laid down in this Law.

A special register for consumer associations shall be established at the Ministry of Economy and Trade, the manner of keeping which and the determination of the effects of its entries shall be regulated by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Economy and Trade.

Every consumer association must notify the Ministry of Economy and Trade of the completion of the procedures of its incorporation prior to commencing its activity.

The said association must also: Notify the Ministry of Economy and Trade of any amendment affecting either its bylaws or the bodies managing it.

Deposit with the Ministry of Economy and Trade, annually, a copy of its balance sheet and a report covering its means of financing.

Employees of the Consumer Protection Directorate and the regional departments, commissioned in writing in accordance with the due rules, shall undertake the supervision of the application of the provisions of this Law.

The application of the provisions of this Law shall also be supervised, each within the limits of their competence, by: Officially commissioned members of the Judicial Police, and, pursuant to written commissions, the competent employees in each of the Ministries of Agriculture, Public Health, Tourism, and Interior and Municipalities, and the Customs Administration.

The employees mentioned in Article 71 shall exercise, pursuant to written commissions, the powers vested in each of them, in accordance with the laws and regulations governing their work, in all places designated for the exercise by the professional or the manufacturer of his activity therein, and they may also carry out their duties during the transport of goods.

However, the said employees may not enter other places unless the professional explicitly agrees thereto, or after obtaining prior written permission from the competent Public Prosecution.

In all cases, the said employees shall have the right, where necessary, to request the assistance of the Internal Security Forces to carry out their duties after the approval of the competent Public Prosecution.

The employees mentioned in Article 71 may take samples, provided that the applicable international standards and specifications are observed in accordance with the provisions of Article 79 of this Law.

The samples taken shall be subject to analysis in any of the laboratories designated by the National Council for Accreditation. Laboratory analyses may be dispensed with where fraud or counterfeiting is evident, as well as where the unfitness of the commodity for consumption or its non-conformity with the approved specifications is evident.

The person from whose establishment the sample was taken shall be given a receipt stating the type of the commodity from which a sample was taken, its quantity, and its selling price, and the receipt number shall be recorded in the report.

The concerned party may object in writing before the Director of Consumer Protection at the Ministry of Economy and Trade to this measure or to the size, number, or quantity of the sample, and may also serve a copy of his objection upon the Central Inspection.

By a decision issued by the Minister of Economy and Trade and the competent Minister, in coordination with the accredited laboratories and in accordance with the applicable specifications, there shall be determined the quantity that must be taken of each commodity, the methods that must be followed to obtain homogeneous samples, and the precautionary measures necessary for transporting and preserving these samples, and the types of commodities from which there is no need to take samples shall also be determined.

If it appears from the results of the analyses that there is no fraud or counterfeiting, or that the commodity is fit for consumption and conforms to the approved standards and specifications, the competent administration must notify the concerned party thereof in writing within a period of three days following its receipt of the laboratory report.

The professional may, in this case, dispose of the commodities. However, if the aforementioned analyses show the existence of fraud or counterfeiting, or that the commodity is unfit for consumption or does not conform to the approved specifications, the administration shall annex the laboratory report to the seizure report and the documents attached thereto and refer them to the "Consumer Protection Directorate" within a period of seven days following the arrival of the laboratory report.

All the employees mentioned in Article 71 of this Law shall refer all the reports and their documents and supporting records to the Consumer Protection Directorate, which shall in turn undertake to refer them to the Public Prosecution or to conduct an additional investigation or analysis at the request of the Minister of Economy and Trade or at the request of the concerned party within a period of thirty days after the approval of the Minister of Economy and Trade.

Disputes arising between a consumer, a professional or a manufacturer and resulting from the application or interpretation of the provisions of this Law, the value of which does not exceed three million Lebanese pounds, shall be subject to mediation with a view to attempting conciliation between the parties to the dispute.

The dispute shall be submitted to the Dispute Resolution Committee provided for in Article 97 of this Law if the value of the dispute exceeds three million Lebanese pounds, or in the event that mediation fails to find a full or partial solution if the value of the dispute is less than the aforementioned amount.

The role of mediator shall be performed by one or more employees at the Ministry of Economy and Trade, of the third category and above, appointed by a decision issued by the Minister of Economy and Trade upon the proposal of the Director General, provided that they are not concerned with the dispute that is the subject of the mediation.
The mediator shall hold his sessions at the places designated by the Director General of Economy and Trade.

The dispute shall be submitted to the mediator by virtue of a written petition from the consumer, the professional or the manufacturer, submitted against a receipt, containing a presentation of the dispute.

A fiscal stamp duty in the amount of ten thousand Lebanese pounds must be levied on the petition.

The mediator shall summon the disputants to a session within a time limit of three days following the date of submission of the petition.

The date and place of the meeting and the subject of the dispute shall be specified in the summons.
