Both parties to the dispute shall have the right to examine all papers, documents and summonses before the mediator.

If either party to the dispute fails to attend the session of the date of which he was duly notified, the mediator shall set a date for a second session.

In the event that the same party fails to attend the second session of the date of which he was duly notified, the mediation stage shall be concluded and the mediator shall refer the file to the Dispute Resolution Committee provided for in Article 97 of this Law.
Each party to the dispute must be present or represented at all stages of the mediation.
Each party to the dispute may submit memoranda and documents to the mediator, who must notify copies thereof to the other party within three days from the date of receipt thereof.

The mediator may seek the assistance of any experts of his choice to help him in performing his mission, and each party to the dispute must submit to both the expert and the mediator all the documents and information that may be requested.

The mediation stage must be concluded within a period of fifteen days running from the date on which the first session is held.

This period may be extended for a similar duration by agreement of both parties or upon the request of the mediator.

The mediator shall present the solutions he proposes, in light of the statements of the parties to the dispute and the documents and memoranda that may have been submitted to him. The mediator shall grant the parties to the dispute a period of forty-eight hours to take a position on the proposed solutions.

If the parties to the dispute agree on a comprehensive or partial solution, the agreement shall be recorded in the minutes and signed by the mediator and the parties to the dispute, and it shall constitute a binding agreement.

Where no partial agreement is reached, the disagreements that remained in dispute shall be referred to the Dispute Resolution Committee provided for in Article 97 of this Law.

Each of the parties to the dispute shall have the right to obtain a certified true copy of the minutes of mediation in return for a flat fee of ten thousand Lebanese pounds collected against a receipt.

If it appears to the mediator that the acts of one of the parties to the dispute are punishable by law, he must refer a copy of the entire file to the Director General of Economy and Trade, who shall in turn refer it, where necessary, to the competent Public Prosecution in accordance with the provisions of Article 81 of this Law.

The mediator must prepare a quarterly report, in accordance with a model determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Economy and Trade, which he shall submit to the Director General of Economy and Trade and notify a copy thereof to the Consumer Protection Directorate.

The said report must include a list of the cases brought before the mediator, the outcome reached, the obstacles facing him during the execution of his duties, and the solutions he proposes.

One or more Dispute Resolution Committees shall be established to examine the disputes provided for in Article 98 of this Law.

These Committees shall be composed of an honorary judge or a judge of the sixth grade or above, as Chairman, and the membership of a representative of the Chambers of Commerce, Industry and Agriculture and a representative of consumer protection associations.

During a transitional period not exceeding six months, and pending the formation of the aforementioned Committees, these disputes shall be examined by an honorary judge or a judge of the sixth grade or above appointed by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice, after the approval of the Supreme Judicial Council.

The judges who are Chairmen of the Committees shall be appointed by decrees issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice, after the approval of the Supreme Judicial Council, and the members of the Committees shall be appointed by decrees issued by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Economy and Trade.

The remuneration of each of the Chairman and the two members of the Dispute Resolution Committee provided for has been determined as follows:

- The Chairman: ninety-six thousand Lebanese Pounds for each public session, provided that the amount of the monthly allowance does not exceed six hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds regardless of the number of sessions.

- The Member: sixty-two thousand Lebanese Pounds for each public session, provided that the amount of the monthly allowance does not exceed four hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds regardless of the number of sessions.

The Dispute Resolution Committee shall have exclusive jurisdiction to examine disputes arising between a professional and a consumer or a manufacturer and resulting from the application or interpretation of the provisions of this Law regardless of the value of the dispute, with the exception of criminal prosecutions, which shall remain within the jurisdiction of the competent criminal courts. If it appears to the Dispute Resolution Committee that the acts of one of the parties to the dispute are punishable under the law, it must refer a copy of the entire file to the Director General of Economy and Trade, for him to refer it in turn, where applicable, after the approval of the Minister of Economy and Trade, to the competent Public Prosecution in accordance with the provisions of Article 81 of this Law.

However, actions involving a dispute the value of which is less than three million Lebanese Pounds may not be brought directly before the Dispute Resolution Committee before exhausting the mediation stage provided for in Articles 83 et seq. of this Law.
On disputes brought before the Dispute Resolution Committee, half of the fixed fee levied on judicial actions shall be levied.
Appearance before the Dispute Resolution Committee shall be permissible without the assistance of a lawyer.

The rules and procedures stipulated in the Code of Civil Procedure shall be followed before the Dispute Resolution Committee.

Provided that the Committee shall issue its decision within a time limit not exceeding six months from the date of filing the lawsuit.

The decision issued by the Dispute Resolution Committee must be reasoned and shall not be subject to any avenue of review except opposition, third-party opposition, correction of a material error, and appeal before the Civil Court of Appeal.

The decision of the Committee shall be executed through the competent Execution Department.

If the judgment debtor refuses to execute the final decision issued against him, after the expiry of a time limit of ten days from his notification of a warning to that effect by the Execution Department, a coercive fine of three percent of the total amounts awarded shall apply against him ipso jure for each month or part thereof.

The provisions of this Chapter may be applied, as of the date of formation of the Committee or the Dispute Resolution Committees stipulated in Article 97, to disputes arising prior to the aforementioned date in the event that the parties to the dispute agree thereon, unless they are pending before the courts.

Shall be punished by imprisonment from one month up to three months and by a fine from ten million to fifty million Lebanese Pounds, or by one of these two penalties, whoever commits any of the acts stipulated in Article 11 of this Law.

Whoever broadcasts or publishes the deceptive advertisement shall be deemed a perpetrator.

Subject to the provisions of Articles 564 and 565 of the Penal Code, the manufacturer, the professional, and the provider of the need shall be deemed liable for the damages resulting from the proper use of the good or service that he provides.

The persons mentioned in Article 71 of this Law shall abide, during the performance of their duties, by complete secrecy.

The results of the examinations and analyses conducted on the samples shall not be considered secret.

Shall be punished by imprisonment from ten days to six months and by a fine from four million to fifteen million Lebanese Pounds whoever discloses the content of the documents or information that he became acquainted with despite the concern of the person concerned to keep them confidential.

Shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to two years and by a fine from fifty million to one hundred and fifty million pounds whoever:

1- Dealt in goods or services or placed thereon the conformity mark knowing that they do not conform with the decrees that confer the character of legal obligation upon national standards or with the essential conditions provided for in a technical regulation without subjecting them to conformity procedures, or displayed these goods or services or distributed them or promoted their use, by any means.

2- Manufactured a commodity displayed in local markets that does not conform with the decrees that confer the character of legal obligation upon national standards or with the essential conditions provided for in a technical regulation.

3- Refused to implement the provisions of Article 44 of this Law."

Shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to three years and by a fine from one hundred million to three hundred million pounds whoever proceeded, while knowing of the matter, to:

- Commit fraud in substances pertaining to human or animal food or in drugs or beverages or industrial, agricultural or natural products.

- Trade in spoiled or contaminated foodstuffs or foodstuffs the period of use of which has expired, or deal therein.

- Possess products or substances of those described in the two preceding paragraphs.

- Incite, by one of the means provided for in paragraphs 2 and 3 of Article 209 of the Penal Code, the use of one of

the substances mentioned in this Article.

He shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to four years and by a fine from one hundred and fifty million to four hundred million Lebanese pounds if one of the acts mentioned in the preceding Article results in the affliction of one of the consumers with poisoning or with an illness that led to his incapacitation from work for a period of ten days at least.

He shall be punished by temporary hard labour from five years to fifteen years and by a fine from five hundred million to one billion Lebanese pounds if the act leads to the spread of an epidemic disease or to causing the death of a human being.

These penalties shall apply even if the buyer had knowledge of the fraud or spoilage.

Shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to two years and by a fine from fifty million to one hundred and fifty million Lebanese pounds every professional, manufacturer or service provider who defrauded the contracting party whether in the nature of the merchandise or service, or its essential qualities, or its composition, or the quantity of useful elements that it contains, or in its kind and origin, when the kind or origin is considered pursuant to agreement and customs the principal cause of the sale, or in its fitness for the use for which it was prepared.

The maximum limit of the penalty of imprisonment provided for in the preceding Article shall be raised to three years and the fine shall be doubled if the offence is committed:

- By resorting to manoeuvres and artifices aimed at corrupting the conformity procedures or the analysis of the goods by effecting a change in their composition, measure, weight or volume.

- By making use of falsified data aimed at convincing the contracting party that the goods are identical to goods previously subjected to conformity procedures or to operations of analysis and verification of their safety.

Any person who, with knowledge of the matter, uses falsified or inaccurate weighing or measuring instruments with the intent to defraud the contracting party as to the quantity of the thing delivered shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to two years and by a fine from thirty million to fifty million pounds. Every fraud, by whatever means, as to the quantity of the thing delivered or its nature, if such nature is the motivating cause for the transaction, shall be punished by the same penalty.

Any person who, with knowledge of the matter, proceeds to defraud the buyer:

1- By placing a counterfeit trademark belonging to a third party on his products or commercial goods.

2- By selling or offering a product bearing a usurped or counterfeit mark;

shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to three years and by a fine from forty million to seventy-five million pounds.

Any person who possesses or uses, in his warehouse, shop, sales carts or other places designated for trade, weights or measures or other weighing or measuring apparatuses that differ from the weights and measures specified in the law or that are unstamped shall be punished by imprisonment from ten days to one month and by a fine from four million to ten million pounds.

Any person who possesses, in the places mentioned in the preceding Article, falsified or inaccurate weights, measures, or weighing or measuring apparatuses shall be punished by imprisonment from ten days to one month and by a fine from four million to ten million pounds.

The perpetrator shall be punished by one of the two penalties provided for in each of the preceding Articles if the damage resulting from the offence is wholly removed before the referral of the action to the court. Where the damage is removed before the issuance of the judgment on the merits, each penalty shall be reduced by one quarter thereof.

The provisions of this Article shall not apply in the case of recidivism.

The provisions of this Article shall not apply in the case of committing the offences relating to food goods provided for and punished under this Law.

Shall be punished by a fine of forty million to seventy-five million Lebanese pounds:

- Whoever refrains from including the information determined by the competent administrations, in accordance with the provisions of Article 7 of this Law, on the labels of the commodity or the packaging.

- Whoever refrains from providing the consumer with the essential information that enables him to assess the risks associated with the use of a commodity or service during the expected period of its use.

- Whoever refrains from specifying in writing the optimal method for using a commodity or service and the risks that may result from using it in a contrary manner.

- Whoever violates the provisions of either of Articles 50 and 58 of this Law.
Whoever violates the provisions of any of Articles 10, 25, 52, 53 and 54 of this Law shall be punished by a fine of fifteen million to thirty million Lebanese pounds.
Whoever violates the provisions of Articles 4, 5, 6, and 19, 20 and of this Law shall be punished by a fine of five million to twenty million Lebanese pounds.

In the event of admitting mitigating circumstances, and by a reasoned decision, the penalty imposed may not be less than half the minimum penalty prescribed in this Law.

- A stay of execution of the penalty may not be ordered.

- In the event of recidivism, the penalties provided for in this Law shall be doubled."

The competent Court of Appeal shall hear the offences recorded in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

The competent court shall publish the judgment in full or a summary thereof in the newspapers it designates at the expense of the convicted person.

It may order that a summary of the judgment be affixed to the doors of the premises in which the professional, manufacturer or service provider carries on his activity.

The court may order that the offender be barred from carrying on his activity permanently or for a period of at least five years, even if the practice is not contingent upon obtaining a certificate or authorisation from the authority. It may order, in this case, the temporary or permanent closure of the premises in which the convicted person carries on his activity.

The court shall order the precautionary measures provided for in the first paragraph of this Article, in the event of recidivism in any of the offences provided for in this Law.

The court may decide, temporarily and until the issuance of the final judgment, to suspend dealing in the commodity or service that is the subject of the violation.

Its decision shall be enforceable forthwith.

The court may order, in addition to the penalties provided for in this Law, the confiscation of the adulterated commodities and the counterfeit and uncalibrated instruments of weight, capacity or measure, and the destruction thereof at the expense of the convicted person.
Where the confiscation of goods seized administratively is ordered, and they are fit for use, the competent administration may distribute them to associations of public utility.

Where the confiscation of goods seized administratively is not ordered, and their owner does not request their recovery within six months following the date of issuance of the final judgment, they shall revert to the benefit of the Treasury.

Notwithstanding any other text, the fines and the price of the goods ordered shall be distributed in accordance with the following:

أ - 60% to the Treasury.

ب - 20% to the Judges' Mutual Fund and the Judicial Assistants' Mutual Fund in equal shares.

ج - 20% to a joint fund established at the Consumer Protection Directorate, the proceeds of which shall be distributed in accordance with the following:

- 45% in individual shares to the competent inspectors who are neither assigned nor seconded to perform other tasks or functions independently of their function, and these shares shall be distributed as follows:

- Three shares to the inspector who drew up the record, and his right shall lapse after three years from the date of the end of his service.

- Two shares to the competent inspector, and his right shall lapse after three years from the date of the end of his service.

- One share to the registry employees, and their right shall lapse after three years from the date of the end of his service.

- 45% distributed to the heads and employees of the Consumer Protection Directorate pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Economy and Trade upon the proposal of the Director General of Economy and Trade. This right shall lapse after six months from the date of the end of the employee's service.

- 10% to consumer associations operating in Lebanon.

- Legislative Decree No. 54 dated 29/7/1983 (Combating Fraud) is repealed,

- And the articles contrary to the provisions of this Law in Legislative Decree No. 71 dated 9/9/1983 (Safety of Foodstuffs of All Kinds) are repealed,

- And the articles contrary to the provisions of this Law in Legislative Decree No. 73 dated 9 /9/1983 (Possession of and Trading in Goods, Materials and Produce),

- And the legal provisions, decrees and decisions that conflict with the provisions of this Law or are inconsistent with its content are also repealed.

The Minister of Economy and Trade shall exercise the powers provided for in Articles 39 and 40 of this Law until the Lebanese Accreditation Council established pursuant to Law No. 572 dated 11/2/2004 commences the exercise of its activity.
The details of implementation of the provisions of this Law shall be determined, where necessary, by decrees taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Economy and Trade.
This Law shall be published and shall enter into force upon the expiry of a period of three months following the date of its publication in the Official Gazette.

Leisure Hill S.A.L. is licensed to occupy sections of the public domain in accordance with the following: Contrary to the provisions of Decree No. 4810 dated 24/6/1966, Leisure Hill S.A.L. is temporarily and exceptionally licensed to occupy, exploit, and backfill an area of the maritime public domain in the Dbayeh cadastral zone measuring 58825 m2 delineated by the letters (A - B - C - D - E - F - A) as shown on the attached plan. Leisure Hill S.A.L. is also licensed to occupy a section of the terrestrial public domain in the Dbayeh cadastral zone shown on the attached plan and delineated by the letters (G - H - I - J - K - L - G) measuring 700 m2. This is for the purpose of establishing tourist equipment and water basins, in addition to constructing a cable car linking the tourist installations standing on its property No. 78 Zouk El Kharab to the sea passing over the public domain and the two properties No. 61 and 1050 Zouk El Kharab.
The licensee, Leisure Hill S.A.L., must obtain the licence in accordance with the laws in force to pass over the two private properties No. 61 and 1050 Zouk El Kharab.

This licence has been granted for a period of one year, tacitly renewable, and the Administration may revoke it pursuant to a decree at any time whatsoever, if the public interest requires such a measure, without the licensee having the right to object or claim any compensation, damages, or loss in respect of the installations and equipment established within the project, and these installations and equipment shall remain the property of the State upon the expiry of the term of the licence or its revocation.

The licensee shall pay to the fund of the Beirut Port Authority, in consideration of this occupancy, an annual fee amounting to /141181000/ L.L. (one hundred and forty-one million, one hundred and eighty-one thousand Lebanese Pounds), in advance and during the first month of the year. As for the first year, this fee shall be paid proportionally for the period extending from the date of issuance of this Decree until the end of the year, within one month from the date of notification of this Decree to the party concerned, provided that a fraction of a month shall be deemed a full month, and this annual fee shall be considered subject to modification by virtue of a decree, in accordance with the bases adopted in the event of approval of a new tariff for private properties adjacent to the maritime public domain.

The licensee shall pay into the State Treasury at the Ministry of Finance, in consideration of the occupancy of the terrestre public domain, an annual fee amounting to /47250000/ L.L. (forty-seven million, two hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese Pounds), based on the method followed at the Directorate General of Roads and Buildings with respect to the public domain in its custody.

In the event of licensing the erection of constructions on the areas of the maritime domain licensed to it in this Decree by virtue of a licence issued by the competent authorities in accordance with the rules, the occupancy fees pertaining to these constructions shall be determined by virtue of a decision issued by the Minister of Public Works and Transport in accordance with the provisions of Decree No. 2522 dated 15/7/1992 or any amendment that may be made thereto.
This licence may not be assigned to third parties except after prior approval from the authority by which it was issued.

The licensee shall preserve the rights of third parties and shall not exceed the occupancy of the licensed areas; the rights of third parties are reserved ipso jure and may be established, where necessary, before the competent judicial authorities.

This Decree shall not be deemed effective unless the licensee hereunder obtains from the competent authorities a licence to establish a cable car (téléphérique) authorising it to cross private real properties and the terrestrial public domain in order to reach the facing maritime public domain, under penalty of considering this licence to occupy the maritime and terrestrial public domain null and void.

The Ministry of Public Works and Transport shall have the right to revoke this licence by decree at any time and to confiscate the security deposit for the benefit of the Treasury without any compensation or damages to the licence holder, during the execution of the project, in the following cases, except for faults of the said Ministry and force majeure: - If the licensee assigns the licence to a third party without the prior approval of the Ministry of Public Works and Transport. - If the area licensed for occupation is used for a purpose other than that specified in the first Article of this Decree. - If the licensee fails to commence the backfilling works within the period of eight months specified in the fifth Article of this Decree. - If the licensee fails to pay the annual fee within the time limit specified in the eighth Article of this Decree. - If the licensed company fails to preserve the rights of third parties in respect of private real properties Nos. 61 and 1050/Zouk El-Kharab over which the cable car will pass. - If the licensee breaches any of the conditions mentioned in this Decree.

The competent employees of the Ministry of Public Works and Transport who are officially assigned shall have the right to inspect the constructions and all the licensed sections and to conduct technical and legal inspections in accordance with the tasks entrusted to them at any time and under any circumstances whatsoever.
This Decree shall be published and notified where needed.

1 - The licensed company must submit an environmental impact assessment study for the occupation of the maritime and terrestrial public domain referred to in the first Article of this Decree, in accordance with guidelines determined by a decision of the Minister of Environment, and subject this study to the approval of the Ministry of Environment, prior to commencing the execution of the works referred to in the first Article of this Decree, and the environmental impact assessment study shall include the identification, estimation and assessment of the environmental impacts of the works of the maritime public domain both referred to in the first Article of this Decree and the preparation of the environmental management plan to mitigate the negative impacts and increase the positive impacts on the environment and natural resources. 2 - The licensed company must comply with the content of the study approved by the Ministry of Environment and referred to in the first paragraph of this Article, particularly with regard to the management and environmental plan, during the stages of execution and works. 3 - In the event of a violation of either of paragraphs (1) or (2) of this Article, the licence under this Decree shall be deemed null and void as if it had never been.

The licence holder must commence the erection and completion of all the backfills allocated for the breakwater in the maritime public domain within a period of eight months from the date of issuance of this Decree.
The licensee may not make any addition or modification to the constructions licensed to it pursuant to the design submitted by it before obtaining the approval of the competent Minister.

The bank guarantee that the licensee is required to deposit with the Ministry of Public Works and Transport before commencing work is set at the value of /300000000/ L.L. (three hundred million Lebanese pounds), and this guarantee shall remain at the disposal of the Ministry of Public Works and Transport to ensure the licensee's compliance with all the imposed conditions, provided that it is returned to it after the completion of the project established in the maritime and terrestrial public domain and the verification of its conformity with these conditions.

Decree No. 6341 dated 24/10/1951, relating to the regulation of health protection and prevention in all establishments subject to the Labour Law, is hereby repealed and replaced by the following provisions:
The provisions of this Decree shall apply to all employers and to all establishments provided for in Article Eight of the Labour Law, as well as to craft and family establishments.

The employer shall install a secure fence in the following places:

1 - Around every flywheel connected directly to the prime mover and around every moving part of the engine, whether the flywheel or the prime mover is installed in the engine house or not.

2 - Around the head and tail of every water wheel and every rotary water machine.

3 - Around all electric generators, rotary motors, and flywheels related thereto, unless they are in such a position or of such construction as not to constitute a danger just as if they were surrounded by a secure fence.

4 - Around every part of the transmission machinery that may constitute a danger.

5 - Around every dangerous part of any machinery whatsoever other than prime movers and transmission machinery, unless that part is in such a position or of such construction as not to constitute a danger. The protective guards referred to above must satisfy the following:

- That they operate to achieve complete protection from the danger they were installed to avoid.

- That they prevent employees from coming into contact with the danger zone throughout the operating period.

- That they do not hinder employees in performing their work or disrupt production.

It is prohibited to remove safety devices or protective guards from machines or to damage them. However, if they are removed from their place for the purpose of carrying out maintenance work, the electric current must be disconnected from them before carrying out such work and before restarting them again.

All mobile mechanical work equipment used on public roads must be equipped with strong brakes and clutches, in addition to means for securing them firmly during work on the roads, and they must also be equipped with front and rear audible or visual warning signals.

Every crane driver shall be medically fit and hold a valid licence to drive the crane, and he must follow the rules of safety in driving and must also disconnect the battery cables therefrom upon finishing work.

Instructional signs must be posted next to the machines in the workplace to guide employees on the correct methods of work and the preventive precautions they must follow.

Employers shall take the following measures:

1 - Verify periodically, by themselves or through specialists, that the machines, equipment, or substances used by employees do not entail any risks to the health and safety of those who use them properly. Provide sufficient and necessary information regarding the correct method of installing and using the machines and equipment and the proper use of substances. And provide information on the hazards of the machines and equipment and on the dangerous properties of chemical substances and physical and biological agents or products, as well as instructions on how to avoid the hazards.

2 - Conduct scientific and technical studies and research to meet the prevention and safety obligations mentioned in this Decree.
The use of new machinery by means of mechanical power shall be subject to prior authorisation at the Ministry of Labour based on a report submitted by the engineer labour inspector.
Whosoever uses a new machine by means of mechanical power without prior authorisation shall be punished in accordance with Articles /107/ and /108/ of the Labour Code.

Every establishment that has been subjected to an accident or fire must notify the Ministry of Labour in writing of the matter within a maximum period of 24 hours, and it must send a register of work accidents to the Ministry once every six months. The engineer labour inspector shall carry out an inspection of the machinery that was subjected to the accident or to the fire and the Director General of the Ministry of Labour shall take, as a result of the investigation, the appropriate decision regarding the licence to use the engines. The employer must provide the necessary means to prevent fire and must secure appropriate extinguishing devices for the materials present in the establishment and the materials used in the industries, and he must comply in particular with the following:

1 - Providing entrances, exits and stairs at workplaces in such a way as to facilitate for employees the speed of exit upon crowding upon the outbreak of a fire and placing appropriate signs and notices for emergency exits.

2 - Securing fire-fighting means and devices so that they are always fit to serve their purpose and free from every obstacle, and in places that are easy to reach with the placement of notices indicating their location.

3 - Securing a means of alarm in the event of the outbreak of a fire.

4 - Posting instructive notices to avoid fire or its causes in flammable places at worksites.

5 - Preparing an emergency and rescue plan, appointing a person responsible for it, and training a special team from among the establishment's employees to implement the procedures of this plan.

Subject to the legal provisions in force relating to the regulatory conditions specific to public safety and fire prevention in buildings, the Ministry of Labour shall determine the measures to be taken in establishments subject to the provisions of the Labour Code in order to secure escape following a fire and the measures to be taken to avoid its occurrence.

The employer must post in a conspicuous place in the workplaces detailed instructions regarding the means of preventing fire and protecting employees from the hazards to which they may be exposed during the performance of their work, in the Arabic language and in another language understood by the employees.

Every fixed vessel or pit rising more than one metre above the adjacent ground or adjacent platform must be covered with a secure fence whose height is not less than 90 centimetres, and if that is impossible in view of the nature of the work, protective measures must be taken to ward off the hazard with the knowledge and approval of the competent labour inspector.

Subject to the legal provisions in force relating to the determination of the technical and preventive conditions specific to the public safety requirements in lift equipment, every hoist or lift shall be of sound mechanical construction, and its doors and the locks connected thereto shall be maintained such that they do not open except when the cabin stops at the door openings, and the lift shall not move except after the door is locked.

A notice of its load capacity shall be placed on every lift, and it is prohibited to load it in excess of what is prescribed therefor. Flammable materials shall not enter into its manufacture, and it shall be equipped with a means of sufficient ventilation and lighting and a means for calling for help in the event the lift stops. There shall be periodic maintenance of the lift by a company specialised in lifts.

A handrail of sound construction shall be placed on every ladder or staircase. All staircases, passageways, and gangways shall be safeguarded with sturdy barriers. Every opening present in the floor of the establishment shall also be safeguarded.

Every structure intended to be erected whose height exceeds three metres shall be safeguarded and a barrier shall be placed around it, and it shall be equipped with the tools that enable the persons present therein to secure their feet and their hands when necessary.

If work is carried out inside a chamber, a tank basin, a pit, a chimney pipe, or any other place from which dangerous vapours rise to an extent that exposes the employees to danger, the necessary measures determined by a decision of the Minister of Labour shall be taken.

The employer shall provide suitable personal protective equipment and shall work on maintaining it, and the employee shall be obliged to use the personal protective equipment placed at his disposal and to preserve it.

A special device (exhaust fan) shall be placed around the machines used for grinding or sifting materials that emit flammable or explosive dust, and a device shall also be placed to prevent the dust from leaking into the interior of the establishment or to prevent its accumulation therein.

Subject to the laws and regulations in force, the following conditions shall apply to every steam boiler, whether it is single or one of several stages in a single class:

1 - A suitable stop valve preventing the boiler from being operated at a pressure exceeding the limit rated for it.

2 - A suitable stop valve connecting the boiler to the steam pipe.

3 - An accurate gauge for regulating the steam connected to the space designated for steam, which the employee can easily view.

4 - At least one water gauge made of a transparent material to indicate the level of water present in the boiler.

5 - A device for measuring the extent of the pressure present in it.

6 - Every part of the parts of the steam boiler must be of sound construction.

7 - All fittings and accessories of the boiler shall be maintained by adequate means.

8 - Every steam boiler shall be inspected at least once a year, and its owner shall be given a certificate of the result of the inspection, which must be produced to the competent labour inspector upon request.

9 - A used steam boiler may not be used in a new place except after it has been inspected and approved by the competent authorities.

Every steam receiver that is not constructed and maintained in such a manner as to withstand the maximum pressure permitted for operating the boilers, or the maximum pressure that may exist in the pipe connecting the receiver and any other source of steam, must be equipped with the following:

1 - A reducing valve or a suitable automatic device preventing the exceeding of the maximum pressure at which the boiler is permitted to be operated.

2 - A suitable valve enabling the steam to escape, or a suitable device that cuts off the steam automatically.

3 - An accurate gauge for regulating the steam pressure.

4 - A suitable stop valve.

5 - A plate bearing the distinguishing number, fitted to the steam receiver so that it can be easily seen.

The receiver must be inspected at least once every two years, and the inspection certificate shall be kept for the labour inspector to examine when necessary.

Every air receiver must meet the following conditions:

1 - An indication of the maximum pressure permitted to be operated in it, in a manner that can be seen.

2 - If the air receiver is connected to an air compressing mechanism, it must be constructed so as to be able to withstand the maximum pressure that can be generated in the air compressing machine, or be fitted with a device preventing the exceeding of this maximum limit, and be equipped with a suitable safety valve allowing the air to escape immediately upon exceeding the maximum limit, and it must also be equipped with an accurate pressure gauge to indicate the extent of the pressure present in the receiver and with a suitable device for draining the receiver, and an opening must be provided in it for cleaning it from the inside, and it must be inspected at least once every two years.
The employer shall keep a register in which the result of these examinations is recorded, and shall produce it to the competent bodies when necessary.

Without prejudice to the legal provisions in force relating to the special specifications and ratios for limiting the pollution of air, water, and soil, every establishment or every factory from which dust, smoke, noise, or any other harmful or polluting substance causing harm to employees emanates shall install one or more special devices on the source of the harm, preventing their leakage into the workplaces and into the surrounding environment.

No stationary combustion machine may be used unless a device has been prepared to draw the gases exiting the engine into the open air after treatment, and unless the machine is isolated from the workrooms.

The exposure of employees to noise, din and vibrations must be limited such that the duration of exposure does not exceed the amount specified in Table No. (1) annexed to this Decree, and a medical examination of hearing must be conducted before appointment, as well as periodic examinations for employees in the din zone and compared with the initial examination, and the owner of the establishment must place signs at the entrance of the establishment and throughout all the workplaces most exposed to din alerting employees to the mandatory use of personal protective devices against din. When it is discovered that the continuous work of the employee involves exposure to air pollution and noise or vibrations that is medically inadvisable, every effort shall be made, within the laws and regulations in force, to transfer the employee to suitable alternative work while preserving his salary, rank and professional level.... The employer must also use the possible scientific methods to prevent or reduce din in the following order of priority:

A - Preventing din at its source, either by removing this source, oiling it, greasing it, or insulating it with known and appropriate suitable insulators.

B - Keeping the source away from the employees.

C - Using sound-insulating or sound-absorbing barriers.

D - Periodic examination of the health conditions of employees exposed or likely to be exposed to occupational hazards resulting from air pollution, noise and vibrations in the working environment.

The concerned employee shall not bear any cost as a result thereof, and he must comply with the safety procedures relating to prevention of occupational hazards resulting from air pollution, noise and vibrations in the working environment. These prevention and protection measures may not lead to effects that prejudice the legal rights of employees. Protection must also be guaranteed to an employee who withdraws from a workplace which he believes for a reasonable cause poses an imminent and serious threat to his life or health, from the consequences that his withdrawal may entail, in accordance with the provisions and regulations in force.

Every establishment that has any source of ionising radiation, or handles it or uses it, shall obtain a licence therefor from the Ministry of Labour, and it shall take all necessary precautions to ensure effective protection for workers with regard to their health and safety from ionising radiation to the lowest level practically possible in accordance with Schedule No. (2) attached to this Decree.

The Minister of Labour shall determine by decision the measures to be taken:

- To reduce the degree of exposure of employees to radiation and limit it.

- To determine the maximum permissible limit of doses and quantities of ionising radiation and review them regularly.

- To determine appropriate levels of radiation exposure for workers who work directly in radiation work and who are aged 18 years or over.

- To determine appropriate levels of radiation exposure for workers who are likely to be exposed to it temporarily.

- To give warning of works that may involve radiation.

- To train and inform employees exposed to radiation.

- To carry out appropriate measurements to verify observance of radiation exposure levels.

- To determine the cases in respect of which immediate necessary measures must be taken as a result of radiation exposure and its degree.

The establishment shall notify the Ministry of Labour and the competent bodies, by any means and within the shortest possible period of time, upon the occurrence of any accident that has led to pollution of the environment or exposure of any person to a radiation dose exceeding the maximum dose, or upon the loss of any source of radiation or the occurrence of damage thereto or loss of control over it, while clarifying the details and stating the causes.

The establishment is required to establish special registers for radiation sources and for the occupational medical examination of workers in the field of radiation, for accidents that occur to persons or to devices and equipment.... These registers shall be of a confidential nature and shall be placed at the disposal of the competent technical labour inspection body.

Refraining from eating food or drinking in places not designated for that purpose shall be mandatory. The necessary precautions shall be provided to protect employees from the hazards of exposure to used chemical substances that leak into the work atmosphere, such that it does not exceed the internationally adopted limits.

Full compliance with the general preventive precautions for storing hazardous substances shall be mandatory, such as separating the warehouse from the production hall and other facilities, and that it be built in accordance with fire-fighting and thermal insulation specifications, and that appropriate ventilation for the substances stored therein and sufficient passages facilitating access to all its sections be available inside it, and that it be equipped with the necessary and appropriate fire-extinguishing equipment.

The establishment shall be required to place warning signs in Arabic and in a language understood by the employees in the workplaces for all workers who are exposed to the hazard of hazardous or carcinogenic chemical substances, and to prepare educational and guidance programmes on occupational cancer and take the necessary steps, and with all available information regarding the hazards that such exposure may entail and the measures that must be taken.

It is prohibited for any employee to be assigned or permitted to manually transport any load which, by reason of its weight, may endanger his health or safety, having regard to all the conditions under which the work is to be performed in accordance with Table No. (3).

The establishment must use, as far as practicable, suitable technical devices in order to limit or facilitate the manual transport of loads. It must also take appropriate steps to ensure that every employee assigned to the manual transport of loads other than light loads is qualified to do so and has received, prior to the assignment, adequate training or instruction in technical working methods with the aim of protecting health and preventing accidents. It is prohibited to assign women and juveniles to the manual transport of loads other than light loads, whereas the maximum weights of loads which they are permitted to carry, push or pull are specified in the scheduling No. (3) annexed to this Decree.

The Ministry of Labour shall specify the measures necessary for the protection of employees' eyes from particles or splinters flying during the performance of work, the special measures for the protection of hands and hearing when using machines that emit disturbing noises, and the measures necessary for the protection of employees from dampness in workplaces located underground, and the following measures for regulating prevention and safety at work shall also be specified by decisions of the Minister of Labour:

1 - Working methods, substances and exposure agents which must be prohibited, restricted, or made subject to an authorisation from the Ministry or to its supervision, taking into account the health hazards resulting from simultaneous exposure to several substances or to several agents.

2 - Establishing and applying procedures regarding the notification by employers of occupational accidents and diseases, and preparing the statistics relating thereto.

3 - Conducting investigations where it appears that cases of occupational accidents, occupational diseases or other injuries to health occurring in the course of work or in connection therewith reflect the existence of hazardous conditions.

4 - Introducing or extending a system for examining chemical, physical, mechanical and biological agents in respect of their hazard to the health of employees.

The employer must provide personal prevention and protection equipment and clothing for the employees, and maintain and keep them in a condition fit for inquiry without charging the employees any cost, provided that the use of the clothing outside the workplaces shall be prohibited.

Potable water shall be provided through sources placed in suitable locations in a manner that makes it easy for all employees to access it, and such water shall be from a public source or any other source approved by the District Physician or the physician of the establishment.

As for the water consumed by employees from containers, it must be renewed at least once daily, and such containers shall be clearly marked with the phrase (Drinking Water).

Sufficient and suitable places equipped with adequate means of ventilation and lighting and lockers for placing or changing employees' clothes during working hours must be established, and the clothes must be in good and clean condition. Women's rooms shall be separated from men's rooms.

The Director General of the Ministry of Labour may decide on alternatives to the measures mentioned in the preceding Article, or to some of them, either due to lack of space or due to the existence of special circumstances to be stated in his decision.

The necessary and sufficient means must be provided for the seating of male and female employees who perform their work while standing, as well as during the breaks afforded to them for rest during working hours.

A box or cabinet containing the materials necessary for first aid must be placed. If the number of employees exceeds fifty persons, additional boxes must be placed at a rate of at least one box for every fifty persons. The contents of the box or cabinet are defined as:

1 - An antiseptic or sterilising medication whose validity period has not expired.

2 - Sterile gauze of various sizes whose validity period has not expired.

3 - A medication for burns whose validity period has not expired.

4 - Medical bandages of various sizes, including a rubber pressure bandage (tourniquet) to stop bleeding.

5 - Various splints (metal or wooden strips) to immobilise fractures and sprains.

The box or cabinet may not contain instruments other than first aid supply instruments. The box or cabinet shall be placed in a conspicuous location, and its use shall be entrusted to a person responsible for providing medical first aid.

All establishments subject to the Labour Law in which the number of employees exceeds fifteen employees must have a physician acting in the capacity of an "Occupational Physician" in the event of the latter's absence, in order to monitor the health condition of the employees, implement preventive and health measures in the workplaces, and reduce the risk of exposure to ordinary and occupational diseases and work accidents.

Such establishments must notify the Ministry of Labour of the name of the physician or occupational physicians therein. The medical examination of employees prior to their employment is mandatory regardless of the number of employees in the establishment.
The working hours of the physician shall be determined in proportion to the number of employees, at a rate of at least one hour per month for every fifteen employees.

Every establishment shall maintain the cleanliness of workplaces, keeping them free from odours harmful to health emitted from any drain or sanitary facility, and shall prevent putrescible materials from remaining inside the workplaces by disposing of them gradually or placing them in tightly sealed metal containers that are emptied and cleaned daily.

Non-harmful solid waste shall, in the workplace, be separated from solid waste containing harmful substances.

Non-harmful solid waste shall be disposed of by means of bags and containers dedicated thereto, where it is eliminated daily. As for solid waste containing harmful substances, it shall be separated and placed in special containers to be transported subsequently to special places designated by the competent authorities.

No work may be carried out in wells, gas conduits, cesspools, or in any place containing harmful gases except after treating the working environment and taking the necessary precautions to protect the employees from damages resulting from any gas, smoke, or waste that may be generated during work.

Where the nature of the work leads to wetting the floor to an extent where water accumulates thereon, the floor shall be equipped with sufficient means for draining water and such means shall remain in good condition. Furthermore, the floor shall be solid, level, and free from pits, holes, and other obstacles that may cause tripping, falling, or collision. Floor openings necessary for the performance of the work shall be covered with sturdy covers or surrounded by a fence to prevent employees and objects from falling into these openings.

Sufficient and suitable sanitary facilities shall be established for the employees working in the establishment, and their cleanliness and lighting shall be maintained, their floors shall be made of a solid material, and full doors that lock from the inside shall be fitted thereto. A lavatory consisting of a toilet and a washbasin with a tap shall be allocated at the rate of one lavatory for every 15 employees, and the lavatory shall be nearby and in places that can be reached quickly, and shall not open directly onto the workplaces; rather, entry thereto shall be through a well-ventilated main corridor. Separate sanitary facilities shall be allocated for females.

Showers (douches) shall be mandatory at the rate of one for every 15 employees or fewer in industries resulting in the contamination of the employees' bodies with substances that are harmful to health, toxic, or affect their cleanliness. Sanitary facilities and showers shall be supplied with soap and a personal towel for each employee kept in a clean condition, or with appropriate drying means.

Several establishments may agree among themselves to establish a single medical dispensary, and such establishments shall notify the Ministry of Labour of the existence of this dispensary and its rules of operation.
Employers shall pay the fees of their physicians, and no costs shall be incurred by the employee on account of clinical examinations and laboratory and radiological tests.

All workers in the establishment shall be subjected to the following medical examinations:

أ - The medical examination prior to commencing work.

ب - The periodic medical examination during the period of work in accordance with what the laws and lighting in force determine, and in particular for pregnant women and mothers of children under the second year of age.

ج - Laboratory tests to monitor the development of the health condition of the employee. These medical and laboratory tests and examinations shall take place during working hours.

د - The physician in the establishment shall provide the necessary primary medical care prior to referring the employee to a specialist physician, and shall contribute to improving working conditions in a manner commensurate with human physiological capacity.

ه - The physician in the establishment shall decide, on the basis of the medical, laboratory and radiological tests, either to return those employees who have suffered work accidents or an occupational disease to their work after recovery or to change their work where necessary.

و - The employer must notify the Ministry of Labour of work accidents within 24 hours of their occurrence, and he must also give notice of occupational diseases as quickly as possible.

Until the Branch of Work Emergencies and Occupational Diseases Insurance in the National Social Security Fund is put into implementation, the Director General of the Ministry of Labour shall determine a list of occupational diseases and all cases that must be reported.

This list shall be completed or amended as circumstances require.

The physician in the establishment shall determine the number, manner and timing of these examinations, and a file shall be organised for each employee showing the result of the medical check-ups, cases of illness and their types, stages and treatment, and the duration of interruption from work due to illness.

This file shall be placed at the disposal of the Physician Labour Inspector upon request.

The employer shall take general measures of health prevention in workplaces, particularly with respect to safety measures, lighting, ventilation, air renewal, potable water, washbasins, and dust extraction to protect employees, and hygiene measures to protect employees from contamination by living disease-causing agents, and shall also take the necessary preventive precautions to store hazardous materials in special warehouses completely separate from other materials.

Related text: Determination of Occupational Diseases

Employers shall:

a - Adopt occupational prevention, safety and health measures and means, and use engineering control means to protect employees from the hazards of exposure to chemical substances.

b - Provide personal prevention and protective equipment and clothing to employees, and maintain and keep them in a condition fit for use without charging employees any additional cost. It is prohibited to wear such clothing outside the workplace, and the employer shall be responsible for washing, cleaning or sterilising it when necessary.

c - Provide sufficient water for employees to wash or shower after finishing their work and before leaving the establishment, and provide hygiene supplies such as: soap, towels...

d - Secure sufficient quantities of fresh milk for employees to drink.

e - Train employees, on a continuous basis, in the procedures and methods for using chemical substances in a sound and safe manner.

f - Place warning signs to indicate the locations where hazardous or carcinogenic chemical substances are present.
Hazardous chemical substances shall be replaced with non-hazardous substances or with less hazardous substances.

Hazardous chemical substances and their empty containers and receptacles shall be disposed of in a manner that is not harmful to the environment, the safety of the population and their health, in accordance with the laws in force.

All workers handling chemical substances shall be subject, in addition to what is stated in Article 38 of this Decree regarding medical and laboratory examinations for employees, to periodic laboratory examinations to assess the degree of exposure to these substances and to monitor the development of the employees' health condition.

Employees shall comply with the following:

a - Cooperating with their employers in complying with prevention and safety procedures in the use of chemical substances at work.

b - Refraining from taking work clothing outside the workplaces and to their places of residence.

c - Refraining from eating and smoking in the workplaces.

d - Washing in showers before leaving their work.

1 - The employer shall provide all preventive means and sufficient fire-fighting equipment, including alarm devices, and shall inspect them periodically so that they remain fit for use.

2 - Chemical substances shall be stored in buildings and rooms isolated by walls possessing fire-resistance and thermal insulation properties.

3 - A low temperature must be maintained in chemical substance warehouses, in accordance with the nature of these substances, through an effective cooling system.

4 - The width of aisles in chemical substance storage warehouses ought to be at least 60 cm.

5 - Standby exits for escape and survival in the event of a fire must be available in workplaces.

6 - Electrical cables, wires and connections shall be protected by insulating materials and within a safe system, and shall be maintained periodically by a competent person.

7 - An emergency and rescue plan must be available with a team specially trained for that purpose.

The Labour, Prevention and Safety Inspection Service at the Ministry of Labour shall be entitled to inspect the trade and scientific names of the chemical substances used in all establishments subject to the Labour Law, in order to determine the safety levels for hazardous chemical substances that are harmful to health.
Where the use of hazardous substances, technologies or processes is prohibited in a country exporting such substances, the employer must obtain all information relating to their hazard and their use.

The employer shall be entitled to entrust the physician at the establishment with verifying the validity of the sick leave reports submitted by the employee in accordance with the provisions of the Labour Law.

The Minister of Labour may, upon the proposal of the Director General, and after consultation with the employer and the employees at the establishment, issue a decision determining the measures necessary for the welfare of the employees (dining areas - rest room - library, etc...)

Identification labels shall be affixed to all receptacles containing hazardous chemical substances, and such labels shall be written in a language easily understood by the employees, and such labels shall indicate the hazards of using these substances and the safety precautions.

Employers shall comply with the following:

a - Ensuring that identification labels or markings are affixed to all containers and receptacles of chemical substances used at work, located in warehouses, or used for commercial purposes.

b - Providing chemical safety data sheets and enabling the employees (or their representatives) to inspect such data.

c - Refraining from using chemical substances except after obtaining sufficient information regarding the identity of the substances, their properties, and the hazards of using them.

d - Maintaining a register of hazardous chemical substances used in the workplace and facilitating access to such register by the employees (or their representatives) concerned with the use, transport, or production of these substances.

Employers shall, during their transfer of chemical substances in containers or any other equipment, comply with the following:

a - Ensuring that the identity of the containers is indicated in a manner that makes it easy for the employees to know the identity of the substances and their hazards.

b - Ensuring that the safety precautions required to be followed and observed are indicated.

Employers in the working environment shall:

a - Ensure that employees are not exposed to chemical substances in excess of the permissible exposure limits in the working environment determined by the competent authorities, or recognized by the competent authority in accordance with national or international standards.

b - Ensure the maintenance of records monitoring the working environment and the exposure of employees who use hazardous chemical substances.

c - Ensure that access to these records is facilitated for the employees and their representatives.

d - Comply with providing these records to the Labour Inspection, Prevention and Safety Service at the Ministry of Labour.

1 - Measures capable of preventing the leakage of aromatic benzene (C6H6) vapours must be taken at work sites, in its warehouses, and from containers and receptacles of aromatic benzene (C6H6) and all its derivatives.

2 - Operations involving the use of aromatic benzene and its derivatives must be carried out in enclosed apparatus isolated from the working environment.

3 - Harmless or less harmful substitute products shall be used to replace benzene or products containing benzene.

4 - The employer shall ensure that the concentration of benzene in the atmosphere of workplaces in which employees are exposed to benzene or to products containing benzene does not exceed an upper limit whose maximum value does not exceed (80 mg/m3).

5 - Employees who may come into contact with benzene or products containing benzene shall be provided with adequate means of personal protection against the hazards of absorbing benzene through the skin.

6 - Employees who may, for special reasons, be exposed to degrees of concentration of benzene in the atmosphere of workplaces exceeding the maximum limits referred to above shall be provided with means of personal protection against the hazards of inhaling benzene vapour, and the duration of exposure shall be limited as far as possible.

Employees who are to be employed in work operations involving exposure to benzene or to products containing benzene shall be subject to a comprehensive medical examination prior to appointment to prove their fitness for such work, including a blood test, and to periodic medical examinations, every six months, during work, including biological tests comprising a blood test.

These medical examinations shall be conducted under the responsibility of a qualified physician, whose name shall be notified to the Ministry of Labour. The examinations shall be officially certified in accordance with the rules. No expenses shall be incurred by the employees as a result thereof.
Women who are medically proven to be pregnant, nursing mothers, and juveniles shall not be employed in work involving exposure to benzene or to products containing benzene.
The word "Benzene" and the necessary "danger" symbols shall be placed so as to be clearly legible on any container containing benzene or products containing benzene.

Two lists, one for hazardous chemical substances and another for carcinogenic chemical substances, shall be issued by the Ministry of Labour in coordination with the other concerned ministries.

Each list shall specify the substances the use of which is absolutely prohibited and the substances the use of which is permitted after obtaining prior approval from the Ministry of Labour.
This Decree shall be published and notified where needed.

Employees shall be sufficiently and appropriately informed of the hazards that may be associated with their work, and they may remove themselves from any workplace if circumstances arise that appear to constitute a reasonable justification for believing that there is a severe hazard to their safety or their health, and they must notify the supervisor of their work thereof, and employees shall also be notified of any legal texts or guidelines relating to the rules of occupational safety and health.
Employees must strictly comply with all instructions relating to the rules of safety at work.
No licence for the establishment of any industrial enterprise may be granted after the issuance of this Decree except after the approval of the Ministry of Labour and the other competent ministries.

The courts hearing cases arising from the violation of the provisions of this Decree shall be granted the right to suspend the use of machinery, to suspend the work resulting in damage, and to specify the measures that must be taken to avert the hazard, in addition to the penalty provided for in the laws in force...

Confidential information sent to the competent authority, the disclosure of which could harm the employer's undertaking, shall be protected, in such a manner that this confidentiality does not lead to major hazards to the employees, the public, or the environment.
The provisions of this Decree shall apply upon the expiry of three months from its publication in the Official Gazette.

The Minister of Labour shall have the right to grant an additional period not exceeding three months for the application of the provisions of this Decree if special difficulties exist in carrying out the required modifications.
All previous texts that violate the provisions of this Decree or conflict with its provisions are hereby repealed.

The following shall be added to Title Two of Law No. 58 dated 29/5/1991:

"5 - Urgent Expropriation Article Fifty-Eight bis:

Where a declaration is made by a decree issued in the Council of Ministers conferring an urgent character upon the expropriation, the expropriation shall be subject to the following rules and procedures:

1- The detailed map and the schedule from Article Four of the Expropriation Law shall be attached to the decree declaring public utility.

2- The decree declaring public utility or the decree approving the alignment plan shall be notified by way of publication in the Official Gazette and in two local newspapers, and copies thereof shall be posted in the public square of the town and at the entrance of the main municipal headquarters, or at the office of the Mukhtar in villages that have no municipality.

3- Additional expropriation committees, of first instance and of appeal, may be appointed in accordance with the rules and conditions specified in the Expropriation Law to examine urgent expropriations.

4- The expropriation committees of first instance examining urgent expropriations shall follow the following rules:

a- Immediately upon taking cognisance of the expropriation file, the committee shall conduct an inspection of the real properties decided to be expropriated.

The committee shall describe each real property accurately and comprehensively, including all of its contents, take photographs thereof where necessary, then appraise its value and the value of every right potentially existing in favour of a person other than its owner, and draw up a record of all of the foregoing.

b- If the expropriated real property is land devoid of structures, plantings and crops, the president of the committee shall submit the record to the Administration requesting the expropriation and to the Minister of Public Works and Transport, who shall take a decision to take possession of the real property immediately after the deposit of the determined compensation.

c- However, if the real property contains structures, plantings or crops, and its owners and other right holders were not present when the inspection was conducted, the president of the committee shall summon the known owners and right holders through administrative channels to examine the aforementioned record.

The summons instrument must include, in prominent letters, a notice to the owners of the obligation to inform the committee of the right holders, such as occupants, tenants and operators, the date of commencement of occupancy, and the consideration they pay.

d- The Administration, the owners and the right holders shall have the right to submit their observations on the record within a time limit of one week from being notified of the summons.

e- After the submission of these observations, the committee may conduct a new inspection where necessary, and shall then rule on these observations and issue its decision, and it shall have the right to amend the value of the compensation by way of increase or reduction on the basis of the elements of assessment that it deduces from the inspection record and elsewhere.

f- Decisions of the committee of first instance shall be notified in accordance with the rules specified in Item (2) above, with the exception of publication in the Official Gazette.

g- The Administration shall have the right to deposit the compensation and to obtain a decision to take possession of the real property on the basis of the decision of the committee.

h- Beyond the foregoing, the proceedings shall be pursued in accordance with the rules of ordinary expropriation."

Subject-matter and scope of application of the Tax Procedures Law:

This Law determines the common rules and procedures for the various types of taxes in the following matters:

1 - The rules and procedures relating to the bases for the assessment and collection of taxes.

2 - The rights and duties of the tax administration and taxpayers.

3 - The fines due by taxpayers in the event of non-compliance with the required obligations.

4 - The remedies against decisions issued by the tax administration and the procedures for objecting thereto.

The Tax Procedures Law and other laws:

1 - Tax matters shall be subject to the provisions of this Law and to the provisions of other legislation and international treaties.

2 - In the event of conflict between the provisions of this Law, as well as the provisions of the tax laws in force in Lebanon, and the provisions of international treaties, the provisions of the latter shall apply.

3 - Tax matters shall be subject to the provisions of this Law in the event of conflict between them and the provisions of other legislation, whether of a general or special nature.

Principle of legality of the text:

Taxes and the fines relating thereto shall be established, amended and repealed, and exemptions therefrom shall be authorised, pursuant to a statutory text.

Publication of implementing and regulatory texts:

Decisions and texts issued by the Minister of Finance and the tax administration and relating to tax matters of a general nature shall be published in the Official Gazette and on the website of the Ministry of Finance, and in cases of urgency, the Minister may decide to publish by posting on the door of the administration concerned, provided that publication is subsequently repeated in the Official Gazette.

The tax administration may publish these texts in other media.

The following expressions, wherever they appear in this Law, shall have the meanings indicated opposite each of them:

1 - Tax: Any tax or duty, with the exception of customs and real estate duties,

the assessment and collection of which are undertaken by the Ministry of Finance, including:

a - Income tax

b - Built property tax

c - Transfer duty

d - Betterment tax

e - Value added tax

f - Indirect taxes and similar duties

g - Taxes and duties that may be introduced

Unless this Law provides otherwise, the word "tax", wherever it appears in this Law, includes the principal of the tax and its accessories, namely fines, interest, and compulsory collection expenses related to the tax.

2 - Taxpayer: Every person bound by virtue of the tax laws by tax obligations, and the provisions of this Law applicable to the taxpayer shall apply to the tax withholder except in cases where the Law provides otherwise.

3 - Tax period: The period of time that comprises the chargeable event or events giving rise to the tax, upon the expiry of which the tax must be declared or paid within a specified time limit in accordance with the legal provisions for each tax.

4 - Tax Administration: The competent unit in the Ministry of Finance - Directorate General of Finance - entrusted with the tasks of administering, assessing, auditing, and collecting the tax, in accordance with the powers specified by law.

5 - Person: A natural and legal person, according to the context of the text.

6 - Tax withholder: The person who is legally required to withhold the tax at source from the amounts due to another person (the primary taxpayer) and pay it to the Treasury.

7 - Additional tax: The tax resulting from the rectification of any concealment or shortfall in the tax due, whether the rectification is carried out by the taxpayer or by the Tax Administration.

8 - Return: The annual and periodic tax return, any other return, the periodic statement, the attached statements, and applications for the refund of value added tax.

9 - Joint-stock companies: Corporations (sociétés anonymes) and partnerships limited by shares (sociétés en commandite par actions).

10 - Exempted institutions: Institutions exempted from income tax on profits.

11 - Resident:

Shall be deemed a resident in Lebanon:

1 - Every legal person established or registered in accordance with Lebanese laws or having a place of business in Lebanon.

2 - Every natural person who meets one of the following conditions:

a - He has a place in Lebanon for practising the profession.

b - He has at his disposal a permanent home in Lebanon that constitutes his habitual place of residence or the habitual place of residence of his family.

A person's family shall be understood to mean the spouse and dependent children.

c - His presence in Lebanon has exceeded 183 days, consecutively or intermittently, during a continuous twelve-month period.

Shall not be counted within the 183-day period the period spent by a natural person in Lebanon if he is present therein:

Exclusively for the purpose of transiting from one State to another.

Exclusively for undergoing medical treatment.

12- Beneficial Owner: Shall be deemed a beneficial owner (Beneficial Owner) every natural person, whatever his residence, who actually owns or controls, in the final outcome (Ultimately), directly or indirectly, an activity carried out by any other natural or legal person on Lebanese territory.

Shall be deemed cases of indirect ownership and/or control, the cases in which the ownership and/or control is through chains of ownership or through other serial means of indirect control.

Related text: Determining the tax treatment of transactions transferring the beneficial interest from its owner as defined in Item 12 of Article One of Law No. 44 dated 11/11/2008 and its amendments (Tax Procedures Law) to third parties by way of assignment or by way of inheritance

13- Tax Evasion

Tax evasion is the act of a person bound by tax obligations, intentionally, failing to declare taxes and duties due to the State and levied on his income or wealth, and failing to pay the taxes and duties that he is required to withhold or collect, or reducing those taxes and duties, or cancelling them, or deducting them, or refunding them without right, through the use of unlawful methods and practices, the most important of which are:

- Concealing taxable revenues.

- Carrying out taxable or dutiable acts or transactions without complying with the obligation to submit a notice of commencement of business and consequently the obligation to declare those acts and transactions.

- Creating accounts outside the accounting records.

- Carrying out operations without recording them in the records or without showing them adequately.

- Recording fictitious expenses.

- Recording fictitious financial liabilities or liabilities for other than their actual purpose.

- Using falsified documents.

- Intentionally destroying accounting documents before the date prescribed by law.

- Failing to submit returns and statements related to business results or to the tax base.

- Exercising a tax deduction or refund without right.

- Carrying out transactions and procedures designed to incur fictitious obligations and burdens towards third parties, even if they take a legal form.

- Failing to declare import and export operations at their true value.

- Failing to declare all employees.

- Failing to issue invoices or similar documents in due form.

- Concealing the beneficial owner, in accordance with the definition specified for him by law, from any source of funds and in any manner whatsoever.

Entry into force of tax laws:

1 - Unless the text provides otherwise, the effects of this Law shall apply in accordance with the following principles:

a - This Law shall apply to tax procedures starting from the stages that such procedures have reached under the previous texts.

b - The period prior to the date of issuance of this Law shall be taken into account in calculating limitation periods.

2 - The provisions of tax laws that impose new fines and/or interest or increase the amount of fines and/or interest shall apply to violations committed after the date of entry into force of such laws. The provisions of tax laws that reduce or exempt from the amount of fines and/or interest shall apply to all violations for which the fines due thereon have not been paid on the date of entry into force of those laws.

Amounts paid in instalments in accordance with the provisions of Article 61 of this Law and unpaid shall benefit from the reduction of or exemption from fines and/or interest in accordance with what is set forth above.

Implementing decree for this Article

Tax on unlawful revenues and transactions:

The unlawfulness of taxable revenues or transactions shall not be taken into consideration in the imposition of taxes, unless such revenues or the tax-generating funds are confiscated in favour of the Treasury.

Interpretation of tax legal texts:
