Where there is a text that may be interpreted in more than one meaning, the meaning that renders the text consistent with its purpose and ensures harmony between it and other texts must be adopted. In this case, the Ministry of Finance shall proceed to issue decisions, circulars and instructions to interpret such texts and the methods of their application, provided that they are published in the Official Gazette.

Legality of the Exercise of a Right:

1 - For the purposes of determining the tax due on a given transaction, the Tax Administration shall be entitled to recharacterise that transaction in accordance with its true nature in the following cases:

a) Where the taxpayer has carried out a fictitious transaction in order to evade tax.

b) Where the taxpayer has carried out a transaction that is legal in form, but whose principal purpose is to evade tax.

Implementing Decree for this Item

2 - The Tax Administration shall be entitled to adjust the value and terms of transactions concluded between related persons on the basis of the value and terms obtained in comparable transactions between two independent persons under conditions of full competition.

Persons shall be deemed to be related where one of them has the authority of direction and supervision over the other, that is, where such person enjoys administrative authority over the other capable of determining the course of its business in financial, economic and organisational respects. The detailed rules for the application of this paragraph shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

Implementing Decision for this Item

3 - The Tax Administration shall apply the laws without abuse, arbitrariness or excess, and without relinquishing the rights of the Treasury.

The Tax Obligation:

1 - The tax obligation is the liability to pay the tax due, which falls upon the taxpayer, the withholding agent, or a third party who is jointly and severally liable or who is a debtor of the taxpayer or of the withholding agent in accordance with the provisions of the law.

2 - With the exception of cases of joint and several liability provided for by law, the liability of a third party who is legally required to pay the taxes due from the taxpayer out of the latter's own funds shall be a secondary liability limited to the amounts that such third party is required to pay.

3 - In addition to the liability of the taxpayer or the withholding agent, the third party shall be jointly and severally liable with the taxpayer or the withholding agent for the tax resulting from the third party's intentional failure to perform the tax obligations incumbent upon them, or the intentional performance thereof in a manner contrary to the provisions of the law which led to tax evasion.

4 - In the absence of a special provision, and in cases where the conditions for the liability of a third party are met by more than one person, such persons shall be jointly and severally liable among themselves for the payment of the tax due.

5 - The third party liable for the payment of the tax on behalf of the taxpayer or the withholding agent shall enjoy all the rights relating to that tax that belong to the taxpayer or the withholding agent in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

Time limits:

1 - Where the law does not specify a special time limit for a given procedure or for the performance of a specific obligation, the Tax Administration shall grant the taxpayer a time limit for this purpose, the duration of which shall be proportionate to the nature of the procedure or the performance of the obligation, provided that such time limit is not less than three working days.

2 - In calculating time limits, the day of notification or the day of the occurrence of the event that gave rise to the time limit shall not be included within the time limit.

3 - Time limits fixed in months or in years shall expire on the corresponding day of the last month of the time limit, and where there is no corresponding day, the time limit shall end on the last day of that month.

4 - Time limits shall be calculated from midnight of the date on which the time limit commences until midnight of the day appointed for its expiry, or upon the expiry of the last hour of official working hours where the Tax Administration has official working hours for the taxpayer to attend before it.

5 - If the last day of the time limit falls on an official holiday, including Sunday, the time limit shall be extended to the first working day following it.

6 - Unless the law provides otherwise, the time limits appointed in this Law for the exercise of a right by the taxpayer shall be forfeiture time limits, the exceeding of which leads to the forfeiture of that right.

7 - Subject to the provisions of Article 39 and Article 61 of this Law, the Minister of Finance may, in cases of necessity, extend the statutory time limits provided for in this Law and the tax laws, in a general and comprehensive manner for all taxpayers.

8 - The submission of required documents shall be deemed to have taken place within the statutory time limit if those documents are sent by ordinary or registered mail or by electronic mail in accordance with a mechanism established for this purpose by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance, or if they are submitted directly to the Tax Administration before the expiry of that time limit.

For this purpose, the date of posting by mail or the date of the electronic message conforming to the content of the electronic document in accordance with due process shall be relied upon.

Implementing decree for this Article

Creation and extinction of the tax obligation:

1 - The tax obligation arises starting from the date of occurrence of the event that generates the revenues legally subject to tax.

2 - The tax obligation is extinguished in the following cases:

a - Collection of the tax (payment, set-off...) in accordance with the provisions of this Law

b - Prescription of the assessment or collection of the tax.

c - Cancellation of the tax pursuant to the law.

d - Other cases provided for by law.

On legal capacity and representation:

1 - A person enjoying legal capacity shall carry out all procedures specified in this Law and in the tax laws, in person or through an appointed representative.

2 - A taxpayer not enjoying legal capacity shall be represented before the tax administration by his legal guardians or curators.

3 - Legal persons shall be represented before the tax administration by their legal representatives.

4 - The presence of a representative of the taxpayer before the tax administration shall not prevent the taxpayer from the right of personal participation in his relationship with this administration.

5 - The rules and scope of representation shall be determined in accordance with the provisions of this Law and other laws in force.

6 - Employees of the tax administration or any other person legally prohibited from representing taxpayers shall not have the right to be appointed as a representative of such taxpayers.

Payment of the tax due by the tax withholding agent:

1 - The withholding agent is responsible for paying the tax due by the primary taxpayer.

2 - The tax withheld and paid by the withholding agent shall be deemed as if paid by the person from whose dues and for whose account it was withheld, and the primary taxpayer shall have the right to inspect at the tax administration the value of the tax withheld and paid to the Treasury.

3 - A withholding agent who refrains from withholding the tax when doing so is mandatory shall be personally, jointly and severally liable with the primary taxpayer for the amounts not withheld, even in cases where the refraining from withholding is the result of incorrect information given by the original taxpayer to the withholding agent.

4 - In cases where the withheld tax is not paid to the Treasury, the tax withholding agent shall be personally liable for the unpaid amounts, and the primary taxpayer shall be exempted from the liability to pay them except in the case of collusion between the two parties.

Payment of the tax due in the event of liquidation or bankruptcy:

1 - The liquidator or the bankruptcy trustee shall pay the tax that is due from the taxpayer, out of the revenues of the establishment or from the sale of its fixed assets.

2 - Where the liquidation is carried out voluntarily by the owners of the establishment, they shall continue to submit the necessary declarations to the competent financial unit and pay the taxes and fees due from them to the Treasury within the legal time limits throughout the period of voluntary liquidation.

3 - Where a natural person who is the owner of an establishment, or the jointly liable partners in partnerships under liquidation, do not have sufficient tangible and intangible property belonging to the establishment or the company in order to pay the tax, they shall pay the tax out of their personal property.

4 - Where a legal person under liquidation does not have sufficient tangible and intangible property in order to pay the full tax due, the unpaid tax due shall be paid by other persons where they are jointly and severally liable for paying the debts of the legal person, in accordance with the provisions of the law, the articles of association, or the partnership agreement.

5 - In the event of declaration of the bankruptcy of the taxpayer, the court hearing the bankruptcy shall provide the Ministry of Finance with all documents and information available to it, and the competent tax administration shall examine his operations and notify the result to the court and to the concerned authorities.

An implementing decree for this item

Payment of the tax due in the event of a change in the legal form of the legal person:

1 - The tax due by the legal person whose legal form has changed shall be paid by the legal person that replaced it.

2 - The new legal person shall be deemed liable for all amounts resulting from the non-payment of the tax previously due.

3 - The time limits for the payment of the tax that was originally due by the former legal person and that was transferred to the liability of the new legal person as a result of the change in the legal form shall remain unchanged.

4 - The new legal person shall replace the former legal person in all its rights and obligations towards the Tax Administration, including paid taxes the refund of which is permitted by law.

5 - In the event of a plurality of new legal persons, they shall be jointly and severally liable for the performance of the tax that was due by the former legal person.

6 - A change introduced into the organisation of the management of the legal person or into its ownership shall not affect the obligation to pay the tax due.

7 - In the event of conversion from a partnership of persons into a capital company, the general partners shall remain liable for the payment of the tax due by them and by the company out of their own assets.

Implementing Decree for this item 7

Payment of the tax due in the event of the assignment of the establishment:

In the event that the taxpayer assigns his establishment or the essential elements thereof to a third party, the seller and the buyer shall be deemed jointly liable for the performance of the taxes owed by the establishment in respect of the operations of the year during which the assignment took place and the operations of the preceding years that have not lapsed by prescription. Joint liability shall not include the assessments imposed on the establishment after the expiry of one year from the date on which the Administration is notified of the sale transaction.

Payment of the tax due in the event of death, absence and lack of legal capacity:

1 - The tax due by a natural person for the tax period occurring prior to the date of death shall be paid out of the value of the elements of the estate or out of the income arising therefrom prior to its distribution to the heirs or legatees.

2 - Unless the law provides otherwise, each heir shall pay the tax due by the deceased taxpayer, within the limits of his share of the value of the estate.

3 - The tax due by an incapacitated person, or by an absent or missing person, or a person of unknown place of residence, shall be paid by his legal representative out of the funds and property of the person whom he represents.

4 - If the incapacitated or missing persons mentioned in item (3) of this Article do not have sufficient movable or immovable property to pay the tax due by them, the tax shall be written off in respect of the unpaid part of the debt in accordance with procedures to be determined by a decision of the Minister of Finance.

Implementing decision for this item

5 - The decision to write off the tax may be revoked in the event that the person provided for in item (3) of this Article regains his legal capacity or is found, without interest and penalty running on the unpaid balance for the period during which the person lacked legal capacity or was missing.

Interest and penalty shall resume running from the date of regaining legal capacity or the return of the missing person.

Liability of partners in partnerships of persons:

Partners in partnerships of persons who are legally jointly and severally liable for the debts of the partnership shall be personally liable for the taxes due by them, jointly and severally among themselves and with the partnership.

Liability in joint situations not enjoying legal personality:

1 - In the event that several persons share in the ownership of real property or where there is any partnership in activities not enjoying legal personality, each person shall be liable for his share. In the event that such joint ownership assumes the character of an independent entity from a tax perspective (joint venture, de facto partnership...), those persons shall be jointly and severally liable among themselves for the tax obligations arising from the joint ownership.

2 - The partnership shares referred to in the first paragraph of this Article shall be deemed equal where it is not possible to prove the value of each of them.

Cooperation between the Various Public and Private Administrations and the Concerned Parties

1- Every person, including governmental administrations, legal persons of a public character, public institutions, municipalities, and unions of municipalities, in addition to the various private sector bodies and syndicates, shall provide the Tax Administration with any information it requests, including information protected by banking secrecy, in order to carry out its duties, including tax audit operations or measures aimed at enhancing tax compliance and detecting tax evasion.

2- The mechanism for requesting information from banks and the scope thereof shall be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

3- No one may invoke professional secrecy to prevent the employees of the Tax Administration from reviewing the accounting records and documents that allow the verification of the extent of taxpayers' compliance with their tax obligations, or that enable them to respond to requests for information received by the Tax Administration pursuant to double taxation avoidance agreements.

4- The employees of the Tax Administration shall be bound by professional secrecy with respect to the information they obtain in their aforementioned capacity. Such information may only be used for the purposes for which it was obtained, under penalty of administrative, civil, and criminal prosecution in accordance with the laws in force.

5 - The Public Prosecutions shall refer to the Tax Administration, through the Ministry of Justice, any information arising in lawsuits brought before the courts that involves suspicions that one of the taxpayers has defrauded or attempted to defraud the financial departments in relation to all taxes and fees, whether the lawsuit is civil, commercial, or criminal, with the exception of lawsuits or indictments that ended in a dismissal of proceedings.

Liability of Legal Persons in Addition to the Primary Liability of Legal Persons:

The General Manager in limited liability companies, and the Chairman of the Board of Directors and/or the General Manager in joint-stock companies, shall be jointly and severally liable with the legal person and among themselves, for the tax resulting from deliberate non-compliance with tax obligations, including their performance of, or approval of the performance of, acts that led to tax evasion, if proven pursuant to a judicial judgment.

An implementation decree for this Article

Conflict of Interest:

1 - An employee of the Tax Administration is prohibited from undertaking or participating in any tax procedures that affect the tax base and concern a specific taxpayer, in the following cases:

A - In the event of the existence of a kinship relationship up to the fifth degree between the taxpayer and the employee.

B - In the event of the existence of a material interest between the employee and the taxpayer or between one of their relatives up to the third degree.

C - In the event of the existence of an existing dispute or an official complaint between the employee and the taxpayer.

2 - In the event of a conflict of interest between the employee of the Tax Administration and the taxpayer in accordance with the cases referred to in the first Clause of this Article, the employee and the Tax Administration are prohibited from continuing the tax procedure by this employee, and another employee shall be assigned to this task.

Professional Secrecy:

1 - Current or former workers at the Tax Administration shall be bound by professional secrecy with respect to the information that they have obtained in their capacity as employees, and such information may only be disclosed to the following parties:

a - To the employees of the Tax Administration, the Director General of Finance, and the Minister of Finance in the course of performing their official duties.

b - To the Public Prosecution, the Court of Audit, or the courts in the event of prosecuting a person who committed financial infractions pursuant to decisions issued thereby.

c - To the tax administrations belonging to foreign states in execution of international treaties.

d - To the assessment or collection audit departments at the Ministry of Finance or the Financial Inspection in the course of these departments performing their official duties.

e - To the taxpayers, at their request, with respect to their files and the taxes and fees due from them.

f - To any party, subject to the existence of prior written consent from the taxpayer.

2 - The employees subordinate to the persons mentioned in the paragraphs set forth in Clause 1 of this Article shall be bound not to divulge or use the information except for the purpose for which they obtained it.

3 - Any violation of the professional secrecy provided for in this Article shall entail administrative, civil, and criminal liability in accordance with the laws in force.

An implementation decree for this Article

Notifying the Tax Administration of the Establishment of Enterprises and their Amendments, and of Affiliation with Syndicates:

1 - The Chief Clerks of the competent Commercial Courts shall notify the Tax Administration of the registrations made in the Commercial Register and, in particular, of information regarding the establishment, name, legal form, place and nature of business, capital, distribution of shares and stocks and their transfer by inheritance or assignment, merger, reorganization, liquidation, bankruptcy, striking off, as well as any other information of benefit to the Tax Administration, each month by a deadline not exceeding the tenth day of the following month.

2 - The Chief Clerks of the Civil Courts responsible for registering civil companies, as well as the syndicates and private bodies responsible for registering persons practicing non-commercial professions, shall inform the Tax Administration of every registration, cancellation of registration or transfer of registration, each month by a deadline not exceeding the tenth day of the following month.

3 - The Personal Status Departments shall notify the Tax Administration of the deaths that have occurred and of every case of declaration of death of a person who was deemed missing, every three months by a deadline not exceeding the fifteenth day of the month following the three-month period concerned.

4 - The procedures for notifying the information referred to in the items of this Article shall be determined by decisions issued by the Minister of Finance.

Implementing decision for this Article

Tax inquiries:

1 - Any person who wishes to embark upon an activity or transaction shall be entitled to inquire with the competent tax administration as to how the tax law applies to the activity that he intends to undertake, provided that it has not been completed as of the date of submitting the request for clarification.

2 - The request for inquiry shall be based on an actual and not a hypothetical transaction and shall state all details of the subject matter and the transaction inquired about and the points regarding which the taxpayer requests clarifications, in particular the facts, evidence, documents and all information pertaining to this activity, and the tax administration may request any additional information it deems appropriate.

The tax administration shall reply in writing to the taxpayer regarding his request within a time limit that it determines, provided that it does not exceed two months from the date of completion of the information.

3 - Where the taxpayer executes the activity in accordance with the bases set out in the reply of the tax administration to the request, such execution shall become binding on both the tax administration and the taxpayer exclusively within the scope of the executed activity, without preventing the taxpayer from the right to contest the tax assessments resulting from this activity in accordance with the provisions of Chapter 12 of this Law.

4 - A fee shall be imposed on every request for inquiry provided for in this Article, the conditions and amount of which shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

Implementing decree for this item

5 - The procedures for the application of this Article shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

Implementing decision for this Article

Notification:

1- A natural or legal person shall be notified at the elected domicile declared thereby to the tax administration.

If the taxpayer changes the elected domicile, the notification papers shall be sent to the new address thereof provided that the tax administration has been informed of such address in accordance with the provisions of Clause (2) of Article 32 of this Law; otherwise, the notification shall be legally valid when sent to the last declared address.

2 - In cases where the person has not informed the tax administration of the elected domicile, such person shall be notified in accordance with the following:

a - With respect to a natural person: at their principal place of business, and in the absence of a place of business, they shall be notified at their principal residence.

b - With respect to a legal person: at its head office, and if the taxpayer is a branch of a foreign company, it shall be notified at the main branch located in Lebanese territory.

c - With respect to an undisclosed person: publication shall be made in two local newspapers and on the website of the Ministry of Finance.

3 - In cases where the tax administration is obliged to notify the taxpayer, notification shall be effected either by delivering the notification papers in person to the taxpayer or to their legal representative, or by registered mail with acknowledgment of receipt in due form, for which purpose the date of receipt shall be relied upon, or by electronic mail with respect to taxpayers who adopt electronic filing, or by any other legal means.

4 - A joint venture shall be notified through the partner entrusted by the company to perform the tax obligations on its behalf, in accordance with the rules provided for in this Chapter.

5 - With respect to persons who jointly own real property or where there is any partnership in activities that do not enjoy legal personality, each person in the partnership shall be notified in accordance with the rules provided for in this Chapter.

6 - Taxpayers subject to income tax on the basis of estimated profit and taxpayers subject to built property tax who are not legally obliged to self-assess shall be notified of tax assessments by publishing a notice in the Official Gazette, in two local newspapers, and on the website of the Ministry of Finance, and such taxpayers shall be deemed notified as of the day following the date of publication in the Official Gazette. These procedures shall be adopted to notify defaulting taxpayers among those provided for in this paragraph of the personal notice to pay provided for in Article 63 of this Law.

The method of notification referred to above shall also be adopted for all tax assessments that exclusively include the minimum assessment fines.

7- Taxpayers who adopt electronic filing shall be notified via electronic mail in accordance with procedures to be determined by a decree passed in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance, including the mechanism for proving the taxpayer's receipt of the electronic notification document.

Implementing Decree for this Article

Notification Procedures:

1 - Where a natural person is notified at the elected domicile, at his place of business, or at his residence, the concerned party must be notified in person after verifying his identity. The taxpayer shall not be notified outside his place of business or his residence or at the elected domicile which he has elected except after inspecting an official document proving his identity.

2 - If the person required to be notified is not present at his place of business, at his residence, or at the domicile which he has elected, notification may be made to any person who declares that he is residing with him from among spouses and relatives, or from among those working with him or in his service.

3 - Notification on behalf of legal persons of all kinds shall be received by the person designated by them to receive mail notifications.

4 - In the absence of any of the persons who may be notified and where it is impossible to notify them on two consecutive occasions, the official assigned to effect notification or the postal employee shall, after the approval of the Tax Administration, affix a notice on the door of the place of notification of the concerned taxpayer, and this notice shall be published in two local newspapers and on the website of the Ministry of Finance.

The notice must include the date of affixation and a request for the concerned taxpayer to report to the Tax Administration within a period of thirty days from the date of publication.

Where the place of business or domicile of the person intended to be notified is unknown, publication in two local newspapers and on the website of the Ministry of Finance shall suffice.

Notification shall be deemed to have been validly effected upon the expiry of the period for reporting referred to above.

5 - In the event of refusal to accept notification, the official entrusted with notification or the mail carrier must record the fact of refusal and its date on the envelope along with his signature, return the document required to be notified to its source, and inform the taxpayer of the address of this source, whereupon notification shall be deemed to have been validly effected as of the date of refusal.

6 - Subject to the provisions of special laws, notification in certain cases shall be effected as follows:

a - With respect to members of the Army and the Security Forces, through the unit command.

b - With respect to prisoners, through the prison director.

Implementing Decision for this Article

1- Persons liable to income tax on the basis of actual profit must keep the journal, inventory book, general ledger, and payroll register.

Joint-stock companies must also keep the register of registered shares, and a special register in which the names of shareholders present at general meetings are recorded regardless of the class and number of their shares.

2- With respect to persons liable to income tax on a basis other than actual profit, they must keep the journal, fixed assets register, and payroll register,

3- Companies exempted from income tax on profits must keep the registers required to be kept by taxpayers on the basis of actual profit. As for establishments exempted from income tax on profits other than companies, they may keep the registers required to be kept by taxpayers on the basis of actual profit, or content themselves with keeping cash-basis accounting consisting mandatorily of the two registers required to be kept by taxpayers on the basis of lump-sum profit in addition to the payroll register.

4- Public establishments, municipalities, and unions of municipalities must keep the payroll register.

5- With respect to value added tax.

Persons subject to value added tax as well as beneficiaries of the provisions of Article 59 of Law No. 379/2001 (Value Added Tax) and its amendments are required to keep the registers of taxpayers liable to income tax on the basis of actual profit, subject to the following:

a - Public administrations and establishments, municipalities, and unions of municipalities shall keep their registers and documents in accordance with the legal rules governing their operations, provided that they retain the registers and documents necessary to verify the accuracy of the calculation, declaration, and payment of the tax.

b - Non-profit establishments benefiting solely from the right of refund provided for in Article 59 of Law No. 379/2001 (Value Added Tax) and its amendments must retain the registers and documents necessary to prove the validity of the refund applications and their operations,

6- The registers provided for in the items above of this Article shall be kept in accordance with the laws in force, manually or by computer.

7- The contents and manner of keeping these registers and organizing accounting documents shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

8- For the purposes of levying taxes and fees, these registers may be kept without being stamped or initialed.

9- With the exception of income tax taxpayers on the basis of estimated profit who are not subject to value added tax, every taxpayer must issue an invoice or any other document serving in its stead to prove the validity of the revenue of every transaction they carry out.

The details of application of this item, including the contents of the invoice, shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

10- All taxpayers mentioned in items 123 of this Article must keep and update a special register of beneficial owners containing: the full three-part name, nationality, date of birth, residential address and correspondence address, identity card or passport number for Lebanese nationals, passport number for foreigners, place of tax residence, tax identification number, and percentage of distribution of the right.

These taxpayers must also retain the documents showing how the ownership of the legal person is structured and/or how it is controlled and all information and documents relating to the beneficial owners for a period of ten years, even after the capacity of beneficial owner ceases to apply to the person concerned, or even after they cease operations.

The details of application of this item shall be determined pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

Preservation of Accounting Records and Documents:

Accounting records and documents shall be preserved for a period of ten years from the end of the year to which these records and documents relate, at the place of business or at the place of residence of the taxpayer, provided that their preservation is done in a sound manner that prevents their damage, and that they remain throughout this period legible and verifiable.

Such records and documents may also be preserved by means of a computer or any other modern technology in accordance with a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

All taxpayers obliged to issue invoices or documents similar to invoices shall quarterly provide the Directorate of Revenues at the Ministry of Finance electronically within 15 days from the end of the quarter with the following:

- A statement containing the numbers of the invoices and documents similar to invoices, their dates of issuance, their values, and the value of the tax stated therein where applicable. In addition to the name of the customer and their tax number, with the exception of the final consumer among natural persons with respect to the name and the tax number.

- A statement of the invoices and documents similar to invoices that they obtained from the suppliers with whom they deal, containing their date of issuance, their value, and the value of the tax stated therein where applicable, in addition to the name of the supplier and their tax number.

The Minister of Finance may also oblige categories of taxpayers to issue invoices or documents similar to invoices electronically, the details of which appear upon their issuance on the electronic system adopted at the Ministry of Finance.

Accounting Records and Documents Drawn Up in a Foreign Language:

The accounting records and documents provided for by law shall be kept in the Arabic language, and they may also be kept in the French or English language.

The tax administration shall have the right to request from the taxpayer an official translation into the Arabic language of whatever contracts and correspondence it needs, at the taxpayer's expense and responsibility.

1- Subject to the provisions of special laws, every person who commences a taxable activity shall notify the Tax Administration thereof pursuant to a registration application submitted to it within two months from the date of commencing the activity, and shall also specify the beneficial owner of his activity.

Every person who meets the conditions for mandatory subjection to the Value Added Tax shall submit an application for registration in the Value Added Tax within two months from the end of the quarter in which the conditions for subjection to that tax were met.

Every employer shall submit a registration application for the worker employed by him, within a period of three months from the date the employee/wage earner commences work.

The registration criteria and procedures shall be determined pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

2 -

a - Every resident legal person registered with the Tax Administration shall notify this Administration annually, within the annual declaration period, of every change affecting:

1 - Its name, address, place of business, trade name (goodwill) or the nature of its main activity.

2 - The legal form through which it carries out the activity.

3 - Any modification occurring to the capital in terms of its reduction or increase.

4 - Any change occurring to the names of the shareholders, partners or beneficial owners, or any modification occurring to the percentage of their shareholding or participation.

Every foreign company operating in Lebanon shall notify the Tax Administration annually, within the annual declaration period, of every change affecting the information referred to in 1 and 2 of Paragraph a of this Item.

b - Every natural person residing in Lebanon registered with the Tax Administration shall notify this Administration within a period of two months of every change affecting his trade name or goodwill, his address, his place of business, the nature of his main activity, or the beneficial owner of his activity.

Cessation of activity:

1 - A taxpayer who permanently ceases activity shall notify the competent tax administration thereof within a period of two months from the date of such cessation, provided that the rules, procedures and time limits for issuing assessments are determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

The principles for auditing the files of taxpayers who have ceased activity shall be determined in accordance with selection criteria established for this purpose by the said administration.

Implementing decision for this item

2 - Subject to the legal provisions providing for joint and several liability, the declaration of permanent cessation of activity shall not extinguish the liability of the taxpayer to pay the taxes due by him for the period of his activity even if such taxes are assessed or become due for collection after such cessation.

3 - The tax administration shall complete the audit of the file of a taxpayer who has permanently ceased activity within a period of four months from the date of notification.

The tax identification number:

1 - The tax administration shall grant the taxpayer upon his registration a single tax identification number for all types of taxes including customs and real estate duties, in accordance with procedures determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

2 - All public and private establishments, municipalities, unions of municipalities, bodies, associations and all other legal and natural persons shall adopt their registration number with the Ministry of Finance on all documents issued by them and shall be bound to use the registration numbers granted by the Ministry of Finance to their employees and persons dealing with them in all their documents.

Implementing decision for this Article

The taxpayer's account:

1 - A single tax account classified according to each type of tax shall be allocated to each taxpayer registered with the tax administration.

2 - The taxpayer's account must show the movement of transactions relating to the various types of taxes.

3 - Subject to every special provision, documents relating to the accounts of taxpayers shall be kept with the tax administration for a period of ten years.

4 - The taxpayer or his representative or proxy shall have the right to request in writing from the tax administration to be provided with the information relating to his account, and the tax administration shall give him a certificate of such information within a period not exceeding three days from the date of submission of the request.

Rights of the taxpayer:

Subject to the provisions of the tax laws, the taxpayer shall have the right to:

A - Benefit from the tax deductions prescribed by law, from the right to deduct tax, and from the reduction of fines when the legal conditions are met.

B - Attend field audit operations and be notified of the audit results with a statement of the reasons and the legal articles requiring the imposition of additional taxes.

C - Request from the tax administration that it acquaint him with the content of the information and documents on the basis of which the administration founded the tax assessment.

D - Provide clarification to the tax administration regarding the calculation and payment of the tax.

E - Challenge the decisions of the tax administration in accordance with the law.

F- Obtain declarations forms and tax publications free of charge.

G- Amend the declarations he has submitted within the legal conditions that permit such amendment.

H - Be treated by the tax administration with respect and objectivity.

I - Have the tax administration maintain the confidentiality of the information he provides.

J - Request the competent employees to present their identification cards and the mission order before commencing any inspection or audit.

K - Review the audit results and request certificates or extracts relating solely to the declarations and documents previously submitted by the taxpayer.

Obligations of the taxpayer:

Subject to the provisions of the tax laws, the taxpayer shall be obliged in particular to:

A - Keep accounting records and documents.

B - Pay taxes and fees and submit declarations within the time limits specified therefor.

C - Comply with the requests of the tax administration within the framework of performing its duties, in particular by lodging with it information regarding his activity or regarding the persons with whom he deals and regarding the beneficial owners in his activity, subject to the provisions of the Law on Banking Secrecy and professional secrecy.

D - Facilitate the mission of the employees of the tax administration entrusted with auditing.

F- Notify the tax administration, by virtue of a written letter, when a partner or shareholder refrains from giving him information regarding the beneficial owners in his activity, within the time limit for the annual declaration, with an explanation of all the measures taken by the taxpayer to obtain this information.

Obligation to Submit the Tax Return :

1 - Taxpayers who are obliged pursuant to the special tax laws to submit returns and statements that indicate the tax base must submit such returns and statements to the Tax Administration within the legal time limits and in accordance with the procedures prescribed therefor.

2 - Those taxpayers may send the tax returns and statements to the Tax Administration by electronic mail, in accordance with the rules and procedures determined by the Minister of Finance by a decision issued by him.

3 - The return must be signed by the taxpayer or by his legal representatives.

4 - In respect of tax self-assessment, the taxpayer must record the name of any person who contributed to preparing the return submitted by him and must enter the tax identification number of that person and his address.

The taxpayer, the accounting expert and every person who contributed to preparing the return shall remain subject to the provisions of Legislative Decree No. 156 dated 16/9/1983 as amended by Law No. 276 dated 4/11/1993.

5 - Subject to the rules prescribed for filing a return by electronic mail, the Tax Administration may not refuse to receive any return unless it is not duly accompanied by the signatures of the persons mentioned in this Article. Failure to pay the amount of tax due shall not affect the obligation of the Tax Administration to receive the return; however, the submission of a return outside the legal time limit must be accompanied by the taxpayer's payment of the assessment penalty due for that delay and the collection penalty on that penalty.

6 - The Minister of Finance may oblige certain categories of taxpayers subject to self-assessment to submit their tax returns and statements by electronic mail or by any other advanced means. In this case, the use of the secret access number given to the taxpayer shall be deemed equivalent to signing the return.

The details of implementation of this item shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

Implementing decision for this Article

Extension of the time limits for filing returns:

1 - Subject to the provisions of the tax laws, the tax administration may extend the time limits for filing returns by a maximum of one month upon a written request submitted by the taxpayer if there are substantial reasons necessitating the extension.

2 - The request to extend the return shall be submitted at most ten days prior to the expiry of the original time limit for filing returns, and the tax administration shall decide upon the request at most five days prior to the expiry of the original time limit for filing returns.

The concerned party must apply to the tax administration to ascertain its decision regarding his request commencing from the day following the date of expiry of the time limit allotted for examining the request. Failure by the tax administration to decide upon the request shall be deemed an implicit rejection, and in all cases the decision of the tax administration to this effect shall not be subject to any appeal.

3 - In the event of delay in filing returns after the expiry of the statutory time limit for filing them or the time limit of the granted extension thereof, the late penalty in respect of such returns shall apply with effect from the date of expiry of these time limits.

4 - Except for the cases provided for by law, the extension of the time limits for the return shall not cancel the time limits for payment, nor shall this extension suspend the running of the penalty due on unpaid amounts.

Implementing decree for this article

Amendment of returns by the taxpayer:

1 - If the taxpayer discovers that the return he submitted to the Tax Administration contains an error or omission resulting in an additional tax, he shall be entitled to submit an amended return showing the error or omission that occurred, and to pay the deficient tax and its accessories where due, provided that the amendment is made on a date prior to the date of issuance of the audit mission order for the tax period that is the subject of the return.

2 - If the taxpayer submits the amendment to the return within the time limit for the original return, the amended return shall be deemed an annex to the original return, and no assessment fine shall be due on the additional tax, where due.

3 - If the taxpayer submits the amendment to the return within a time limit of three months from the date of expiry of the time limit for the annual return and 30 days from the date of expiry of the time limit for the original return with respect to the remaining returns, no assessment fine shall be due, provided that this amendment does not result in an additional tax exceeding a rate of ten per cent (10%) of the value of the tax due, in which case the fine provided for in Article 110 of this Law shall be imposed.

4 - In the event of an error in the return that led to an excess in the tax paid over the tax due after the amendment, the taxpayer shall be entitled to submit an amendment to his return within the limitation period and to request the refund of this excess, if he has previously paid it, in accordance with the provisions of Article 54 of this Law.

An Implementing Decree for this Article

Information statements:

The Tax Administration may request any person who obtains goods or services from the taxpayer, or provides goods or services to the taxpayer, to provide information on the amounts he paid to this taxpayer or obtained in consideration of those goods and services.

Limitation Period for the Recovery of Treasury Rights:

1 - Without prejudice to the provisions of Legislative Decree No. 146 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments relating to transfer duty, the Tax Administration shall be entitled to recover the rights of the Treasury in respect of the tax within a time limit of four years following the end of the year succeeding the year of operations, and six years in respect of undisclosed taxpayers, namely those not registered with the Tax Administration where such registration is mandatory, provided that the assessment is issued and deposited by registered mail for notification to the taxpayer by no later than 31/12/ of the year of assessment.

2 - The taxpayer shall be entitled to claim a refund of tax permitted by law within a time limit of four years following the end of the year during which the right to a refund arises.

3- Following the expiry of the time limit provided for in Clause 1 of this Article, assessments may be recovered and rectified and tax may be imposed on any profit or revenue established pursuant to a judicial judgment, an arbitral award, or the liquidation of an estate, up to the end of the calendar year following the year during which the Tax Administration was notified of the judgment, award, or liquidation.

Related texts: Implementing Decree for this Article

Determination of the year of operations on the basis of which the limitation period on the right of the Tax Administration to recover Treasury rights begins to run

Desk and Field Audit:

1 - For the purpose of verifying the validity of the assessment and collection of the tax, the Tax Administration shall be entitled to review and audit the taxpayer's returns and operations on the basis of samples of files selected in accordance with selection criteria established for this purpose by the said Administration as a result of a risk analysis process.

2 - Officials of the competent Tax Administration shall be entitled, within the framework of the audit process, to inspect all elements of the tax base and the identity of the beneficial owners benefiting from those elements, and to examine the accounting registers and documents pertaining to the taxpayer or to any other person related to him, and they shall, where information is available indicating the existence of beneficial owners, take the necessary measures for assessment.

Officials of the competent Tax Administration shall also be entitled to enter the taxpayer's place of business or the place where the accounting registers and documents are kept, provided that this is done in coordination with the taxpayer.

If the taxpayer refuses the above requests of the Tax Administration, the provisions of Paragraph (6) of Article 42 shall apply to him.

Related text: Determination of the detailed rules for the application of the provisions of Law No. 44 dated 11/11/2008 (Tax Procedures Law)

Tax audit mission order:

The competent officer shall carry out the tax audit at the taxpayer's premises pursuant to a mission order issued by the head of the competent tax unit.

The mission order must include the following information:

A - The number of the mission order and the date of its registration.

B - The name of the inspector entrusted with the audit.

C - The name of the taxpayer, his address and his tax identification number.

D - The tax periods and types of taxes subject to the audit.

E - The name of the head of the unit and his signature.

Notifying the taxpayer of the tax audit mission order:

1 - The Tax Administration shall notify the taxpayer of the mission order, in accordance with the provisions of Article 27 of this Law, and of the date of commencement of the audit process within a period of no less than fifteen days from the date of notification, and the notification shall include specifying the accounting records and documents pertaining to the tax period subject to the audit which the taxpayer is required to produce.

2 - The head of the competent Tax Administration shall be entitled to assign the officer to inspect and verify the accounting records and documents and other material elements related to the exercise of the activity in execution of a special written mission order that is not notified in advance to the taxpayer, in the event that it has serious doubts that notifying him may expose the audit process to failure, provided that such doubts are based on reliable information received by the Tax Administration, or on the taxpayer's precedents with this Administration.

Concept of Tax Assessment:

1 - Tax assessment, pursuant to the provisions of this Law, means determining and recording the amount of the tax due in the taxpayer's account with the Tax Administration for a specific tax period and for a specific tax or type of tax.

2 - Self-assessment of tax means the calculation by the taxpayer or the person responsible for withholding the tax at source of the tax due pursuant to the legal rules, declaring it, and paying it to the Treasury within the legal time limits.

3 - In cases where the tax laws mandate self-assessment of tax, as with income tax and value-added tax, the taxpayer or the tax withholder shall be responsible for declaring the tax due and paying it without the need for the issuance of a tax notice or an assessment roll by the Tax Administration.

However, in cases where the tax laws do not mandate self-assessment of tax, the Tax Administration shall impose the tax due pursuant to a mechanism determined by virtue of a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

4 - The Tax Administration shall have the right to review and audit the declarations of taxpayers pursuant to the procedures specified in this Law, and in the event that it finds grounds requiring the amendment of the declaration or the imposition of an additional tax, it shall issue the necessary assessments and notify the taxpayer thereof by virtue of individual tax notices. If it appears to the Tax Administration that there are no grounds for amendment, it shall notify the taxpayer of this matter.

5 - Tax assessment by the Tax Administration shall be carried out on the basis of the following sources of information:

a - Information extracted from the declarations and records of the taxpayer.

b - Information available pursuant to the provisions of Article 41 of this Law.

c - Information resulting from auditing and field inspection.

d - Any information obtained by the Tax Administration.

6 - If the taxpayer fails to submit the declarations, fails to keep the legal accounting records and documents, or fails to give the Tax Administration the information useful for calculating the tax base, the Tax Administration shall notify him that it will proceed, within one month from the date of his notification of the notice, to determine the tax base pursuant to the provisions of Item (5) of this Article and such declarations as the taxpayer may have submitted and documents as he may have produced during the month.

This one-month time limit shall not be included in the calculation of the prescription period.

Implementing Decision for this Article

Limits of the audit operation:

1 - The official entrusted with the audit shall present to the taxpayer, upon commencing his mission, his service identity card and the mission order.

2 - The audit operation shall be conducted in the field during official working hours, and exceptionally during the working hours of the taxpayer.

The field audit operation at the taxpayer's premises may not exceed a period of three months from the date of commencing the audit mission.

The Head of the Tax Administration may extend this period for a maximum duration of three additional months based on a reasoned request from the official entrusted with the audit mission, in accordance with administrative procedures.

3 - The audit operation shall be restricted to the tax periods specified in the mission order; however, it may also cover other tax periods with the approval of the head of the competent unit.

4 - The audit operation shall cover only the tax periods that have not yet lapsed by prescription and shall include the deficit of previous tax periods covered by prescription that has been carried forward to the tax period subject to the mission order.

In this case, the audit shall be restricted to matters relating to the acceptance of this deficit, the modification of its amount by increase or decrease, or its cancellation.

5 - The taxpayer shall cooperate with the official entrusted with the audit and facilitate his mission, and the said official shall not have the right to remove the registers and documents placed at his disposal from their place, but must review them in that place.

6 - A previously audited tax period may not be re-audited except where new information arises that affects the calculation of the value of the tax due, and solely within the scope of such information.

Related text: Determining the details of the application of Clause 6 of Article 47 of Law No. 44 dated 11/11/2008 and its amendments (Tax Procedures Law)

General Provisions:

1 - Collection duties shall be undertaken by the Revenue Directorate and the regional finance offices in respect of the taxes and fees which they undertake to assess, and by the Value Added Tax Directorate in respect of this tax.

2 - The collection of the tax shall be carried out voluntarily or compulsorily.

3 - Voluntary collection means the payment of the tax directly by the taxpayer.

As for compulsory collection, it is the collection of unpaid taxes by the tax administration in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

Time Limits for Payment of the Tax:

1 - The special law for each tax shall determine the time limit for its payment.

2 - With the exception of the cases provided for by the laws in force, assessments that impose an additional tax must be paid within a time limit of two months from the date of personal notification of the assessment.

Audit results:

1 - Subject to the provisions of Article 43 of this Law, the Tax Administration must notify the taxpayer of the preliminary results of the audit and grant him a time limit of thirty days to submit his remarks thereon, prior to officially issuing the tax assessment, and granting the said time limit shall not lead to the forfeiture of the taxes that are the subject of these assessments by limitation.

2 - Where the taxpayer produces new data or supporting documents, the Tax Administration may, on the basis of such data and documents after examining them, amend the preliminary results of the audit that it had reached.

3 - The Tax Administration shall proceed to issue the final assessment within a maximum time limit of one month commencing from the date it receives the taxpayer's remarks, or from the date the taxpayer states that he has no remarks, or upon the expiry of the time limit provided for in item 1 of this Article, and this additional time limit shall not lead to the forfeiture of the taxes that are the subject of these assessments by limitation.

The taxpayer shall be notified of the final result of the audit by means of a tax notice, and where this audit results in tax adjustments, the Tax Administration shall state in this notice the amount of these adjustments and the reasons therefor.

4 - The details for implementing this Article shall be determined pursuant to decisions issued by the Minister of Finance.

Implementing decision for this Article

Content of the tax notice:

The tax notice shall contain the following:

1 - The number and date of the notice.

2 - The name and address of the taxpayer.

3 - His tax identification number.

4 - The taxable amounts, specifying the tax periods to which they pertain.

5 - The reasons for the assessment.

6 - The value of the tax, interest and fines due.

7 - A request to pay the amounts due within the legal time limit.

8 - A statement of the permissible methods of payment that may be adopted.

9 - The time limits for objection.

10- The signature of the Head of the Tax Administration or of the person delegated by him for this purpose.

Burden of proof:

The burden of proving the accuracy of the tax return shall fall upon the taxpayer, and this burden shall fall upon the Tax Administration to prove the accuracy of the additional assessments where it has made adjustments to the return.

Right to Obtain Information:

1 - For the purpose of carrying out the audit process, the tax administration has the right to request in writing, within the framework of the laws and regulations in force, from any person who possesses information useful for verifying the accuracy of the tax due from any taxpayer, and for identifying the beneficial owner, to provide it with the information it specifies within a time limit determined by the administration.

2 - The employee in charge of the audit process may obtain copies of the registers and documents, which shall have the same probative force as their original copies, provided that such copies bear the signature of the employee and the taxpayer certifying that they are true copies of the original. He also has the right to request the concerned party or his representative to attend at the audit premises, answer the questions put to him for the proper execution of the mission, and do all that is required by cooperation with the tax administration.

3 - Where the registers and documents are kept or preserved electronically, the employees of the competent tax administration have the right to request access to the computerised accounting software and the information recorded therein, and to obtain such information in the form of readable digital or paper documents.

4 - Where the taxpayer or any other person refuses to comply with what is specified in the items above of this Article, the provisions of Paragraph (6) of Article 42 and the fines provided for in this Law shall apply.

Tax Refund

1 - If the value of the tax paid exceeds the value of the tax due, and unless this Law or other laws provide otherwise, the tax administration shall be entitled to use the resulting excess in order to collect the amounts due from the taxpayer in respect of other taxes, provided that it notifies him thereof and provided that the order specified in Clause (2) of this Article and the provisions of Paragraph (2) of Article 59 of this Law relating to the allocation of paid amounts are observed.

2 - The remaining balance of the excess shall be refunded to the taxpayer within a time limit of forty-five days from the date of submitting the refund request, provided that the time limit shall be extended for a period of three months, once only, if the tax administration finds it necessary to place the taxpayer on the tax audit programme for periods prior to the refund request.

In the event that the excess results from the discovery of an error by the tax administration, the said administration must return the excess automatically and without a request within a time limit of thirty days from the date of discovering the error. The time limit shall be extended for a period of three months, once only, if the tax administration finds it necessary to place the taxpayer on the tax audit programme for periods prior to the refund request.

3 - Interest shall be calculated on the paid amounts whose value exceeds the value of the tax due at a rate equal to the average interest on one-year Treasury bills on the amount of those sums, provided that such rate does not exceed 9% per annum, starting from the date of expiry of the time limit provided for in the first Clause of this Article.

However, if the refunded tax results from an invalid decision annulled or amended by the tax administration or pursuant to a judicial decision, or in the event of a material error committed by the tax administration that led to the payment of a tax whose value exceeds what is legally due, interest shall then be calculated from the day on which the taxpayer paid this tax.

An implementation decree for this Article.

Date of payment:

1 - The tax shall be deemed paid on the day on which its value is settled by the taxpayer or the withholding agent, whether to the Treasury or to the authority that handles collecting it for the account of the Treasury.

2 - Taxes and fees subject to the advance payment system, the annual and periodic ones only, shall be paid at any of the private banks or their branches operating in Lebanon or at any of the offices affiliated with LibanPost or any other company with which the Ministry of Finance contracts for this purpose, whereas additional and supplementary assessments shall be settled at the competent Treasury cash offices and may also be paid at banks or their branches or at any of the offices of LibanPost or any other company with which the Ministry of Finance contracts for this purpose.

The tax may also be paid electronically in accordance with a mechanism determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

Related text: Determining the rules for collecting taxes and fees administered by the Directorate of Public Finance from taxpayers outside the scope of the cash offices of the Ministry of Finance

3 - Payment shall be deemed to have taken place:

- On the date of cash payment.

- On the date of submitting the means of payment to the cash office designated for such payment.

- On the date of sending the amounts due to this cash office with a valid date.

Allocation of amounts paid:

1 - The taxpayer is permitted to pay amounts on account of the taxes due from him, and in this case the taxpayer must specify the type of tax due and the tax period to which it pertains. The details of the application of this paragraph shall be determined pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

2 - In the event that the amount paid is insufficient to settle the full value of the tax due, this amount shall be allocated according to the following sequence:

A - Interest.

B - The penalty for delay in payment of the tax, if any.

C - The tax assessment penalties, if any.

D - The tax.

Implementing decision for this Article

Penalty for late payment of tax (collection penalty)

- In the event of failure to pay the tax due for a given tax period within the statutory time limits or where there is a shortfall in the tax paid, a penalty for late payment (collection penalty) shall be added to the unpaid or underpaid tax as follows:

- With respect to the tax issued by the Tax Administration pursuant to primary assessment rolls:

· At a rate of 1% per month of the amount of the unpaid tax, a fraction of a month being deemed a full month.

· With respect to the tax resulting from self-assessment and the remaining assessments issued by the Tax Administration: at a rate of 2% per month of the amount of the unpaid tax and 3% per month in respect of taxes withheld at source and in respect of Value Added Tax, a fraction of a month being deemed a full month.

2- The penalty for late payment shall apply:

- In cases of tax self-assessment and in cases where the Tax Administration assesses an additional tax: with effect from the date of expiry of the primary payment time limit.

- In cases where the tax laws do not require tax self-assessment: with effect from the date of expiry of the time limit set for payment.

Limitation period for tax collection:

Subject to the provisions of paragraph (4) of Article 64 of this Law relating to the commencement of compulsory collection proceedings.

- Unpaid taxes issued pursuant to assessment rolls or collection orders, or declared in accordance with the self-assessment system, shall lapse by limitation upon the expiry of five years following the year in which the tax was issued.

- This provision shall not apply to assessments issued prior to the entry into force of this Law, to which the provisions in force on the date of issuance of such assessments shall apply.

Methods of tax payment:

Unless this Law provides otherwise, the tax must be paid by settling the amount due by various means, in accordance with rules and procedures to be determined by decisions issued by the Minister of Finance.

Implementing decision for this Article

The general privilege of the Treasury:

1 - For the purpose of collecting the taxes due from the taxpayer pursuant to the tax laws, the Treasury shall enjoy a first-rank general privilege over all of his movable and immovable property.

2 - The general privilege shall also extend to the property of the persons who are deemed liable in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

3 - The general privilege of the Treasury shall have priority over other special and general privileges. Secured and mortgaged immovable property and pledged movable property shall enjoy priority over the privilege of the Treasury where their registration or deposit is established by a valid date prior to the date of registration of the privilege of the Treasury.

4 - The Tax Administration may register the general privilege of the Treasury on the real property folio of the taxpayer's real properties and in the competent official registers that stand in its stead upon addressing the payment notice to the taxpayer provided for in Article 63 of this Law, and the effect of this privilege shall be enforceable against third parties as from the date of registration of the said annotation.

5 - The privilege of the Treasury shall also apply in the event of preventive composition or bankruptcy.

Payment of Tax by Instalments:

1 - Subject to the provisions relating to the payment of inheritance and transfer duty by instalments contained in Legislative Decree No. 146 dated 12/6/1959 and the amendments thereof, the tax administration shall be entitled to permit payment by instalments of the whole or part of the additional tax due, pursuant to a justified written petition for relief from the taxpayer setting forth the reasons preventing him from paying the tax due, where the payment thereof within the time prescribed therefor:

a - Constitutes a heavy burden upon the taxpayer.

b - Or leads to causing severe material damage to him.

2 - The authority to accept or reject an application for the payment of tax by instalments shall vest in the Director General of Finance or any person delegated by him: the tax administration shall, within a time-limit of ten days, accept or reject the application, stating the reasons for the acceptance or rejection.

The decision of the tax administration shall not be subject to any avenue of review, including applications for annulment for excess of power.

3 - Payment of the tax by instalments shall be executed pursuant to an instalment schedule drawn up by the tax administration and signed by the taxpayer in approval thereof.

4 - The tax may not be paid by instalments over a period exceeding three years and the instalment schedule may not be rescheduled.

5 - Should the taxpayer fail to implement any clause of the instalment schedule or in the event of the declaration of his bankruptcy or the liquidation of his business, the instalment measures and the time-limits thereof shall lapse ipso jure and the tax administration shall initiate the measures for the collection of the tax due in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

6 - The prescription time-limits shall run in respect of each instalment amount as from the due date for the payment thereof.

7 - The interest due on the amounts paid by instalments shall be calculated at the interest rate fixed on Treasury bills for the time-limits of the instalments.

8 - All taxes subject to the system of withholding at source as well as the Value Added Tax shall be excluded from the provisions on the payment of tax by instalments provided for in this Article.

9 - In the event of the rejection of an application for payment by instalments, the taxpayer shall not be entitled to submit a new application for the payment of the tax by instalments at once unless the new application includes an explanation of new reasons and circumstances justifying the reconsideration thereof.

10- The details for the application of this Article shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

Implementing Decision for this Article

Guarantees in the Event of Payment of Tax by Instalments:

In accordance with the provisions of Article 61 of this Law, a notation of payment by instalments shall be entered against the movable and immovable property of the taxpayer in an amount equivalent to at least twice the value of the tax paid by instalments.

Formal Notice to Pay:

1 - Where the taxpayer fails to pay the tax due from him within the statutory time limits, the tax administration shall address to him a personal formal notice with acknowledgement of receipt calling upon him to pay the tax within a time limit of one month from the date of his notification of the notice, provided that the provisions of Articles 27 and 28 of this Law are observed in the service of process.

2 - The formal notice must include the type of tax due, the fines, the accrued interest, the tax periods to which they relate, the time limits for payment, as well as the collection measures that may be resorted to in the event of non-payment.

Commencement of Compulsory Collection Procedures:

1 - In the event that the taxpayer fails to pay within the time limit specified in the formal notice to pay, the tax administration shall, with the approval of the Director General of Finance or whomever he delegates, proceed to issue a written decision for the compulsory collection of taxes, which shall be notified to the taxpayer.

2 - The decision referred to in Item 1 of this Article shall specify the amounts due that remain unpaid.

3 - The compulsory collection decision shall become enforceable on the day following the date of its notification to the taxpayer.

4 - The decision ordering the compulsory collection of taxes shall suspend the running of the statute of limitations for the collection of the amounts covered thereby, without suspending the running of fines and interest against the taxpayer.

5 - The taxpayer shall have the right to object to the compulsory collection decision in accordance with the provisions of Chapter Twelve of this Law.

6 - The tax administration may request the concerned authorities to deduct the taxes owed by the taxpayer from the principal of the debts due to him from the Treasury.

7 - The Ministry of Finance may request the competent enforcement departments at the Ministry of Justice to collect the taxes owed to it by taxpayers.

The procedures provided for in this Law shall apply before the competent enforcement departments that undertake the execution of collection requests received from the Ministry of Finance.

Compulsory Collection Procedures:

Compulsory collection shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of this Law through the performance by the tax administration of the following sequential procedures:

A - Attachment of the taxpayer's movable and immovable property, with the exception of that which is not permitted to be attached under the laws and regulations in force.

B - Sale of such property at public auction.

Termination of compulsory collection procedures:

1 - Compulsory collection procedures shall terminate in the following cases:

a - If the taxpayer settles what is due from him

b - Upon the discovery of a material error the correction of which would cancel the entire tax.

2 - Where the conditions provided for in Item One of this Article are met, the Tax Administration shall, with the approval of the Director General of Finance, issue a decision terminating the compulsory collection procedures and notify the taxpayer thereof.

3 - The termination of compulsory collection procedures shall neither affect attachments placed in favour of other administrations, nor the liability of the taxpayer to bear the costs of collection, unless the error set forth in Paragraph (b) of Item One of this Article was caused by the act of the Tax Administration.

Continuation of compulsory collection procedures in the event of a dispute over the capacity of the heirs or right holders or the impossibility of identifying them:

1 - In the event of the death of the taxpayer, his heirs shall be pursued for the taxes that were due from him within the limits permitted by the law.

2 - In the event of a dispute over the capacity of the heirs or right holders, or in the event that it is impossible to identify them, the competent Tax Administration may request the appointment of a representative of the heirs and continue the compulsory collection procedures after the appointment of such representative or after the lapse of three months from the date of submission of the said request.

The right of the Tax Administration and of the heirs shall remain reserved in respect of the differences that may arise upon the settlement of the dispute over the capacity of the heirs or right holders.

Attachment of the taxpayer's property:

In the event that the taxpayer does not pay the tax after the expiry of the time-limit of the personal notice to pay and the issuance by the Tax Administration of a decision to commence compulsory collection procedures in accordance with the provisions of Article 64 of this Law, the Tax Administration shall proceed to obtain a decision from the Director General of Finance to attach the property of the taxpayer in his possession or in the possession of a third party and to sell it.

Competence to execute the attachment:

The Tax Administration shall, with the approval of the Director General of Finance, assume the competence to execute the attachment directly, and it may seek the assistance of the security forces where necessary.

Suspension of compulsory collection procedures:

1 - The execution of procedures relating to a compulsory collection decision shall be temporarily suspended in the following cases:

a - If the taxpayer submits a request to pay the tax by instalments as provided for in Article 61 of this Law, until a decision is made on the said request.

This suspension shall continue in respect of the amounts approved to be paid by instalments for as long as the taxpayer complies with the payment of the instalments on their due dates in accordance with the instalment conditions.

b - Within a period of three months from the occurrence of the following cases:

- Death of the taxpayer

- Loss of his legal capacity

- Cessation of the legal capacity of the person who was representing the taxpayer.

c - In the event that the taxpayer objects to the assessment decision upon which the compulsory collection is based in accordance with the provisions of Article 97 et seq. of this Law, until the taxpayer is notified of the final and irrevocable decision issued in respect of this objection.

This sub-paragraph shall apply only to the collection of the contested tax.

2 - The suspension of procedures shall commence on the date of approval by the Tax Administration of the grounds for suspension, and this suspension shall result in the interruption of all time limits relating to these procedures. Once the grounds for suspension cease to exist, the Tax Administration shall resume carrying out the collection procedures.

3 - Subject to the provisions of paragraph (1) of Article 102 of this Law, the late payment penalty provided for in Article 55 of this Law shall continue to run throughout the period of suspension of compulsory collection procedures, provided that such period does not exceed twenty months, failing which the said penalty shall cease to run from the date of expiry of this period.

4 - The taxpayer's objection to the compulsory collection decision shall not suspend the procedures for its execution unless a decision staying execution is issued by the State Council.

Exemption from compulsory collection procedures:

Exemption from compulsory collection procedures may only be granted pursuant to a law providing either for the cancellation of the tax or for exemption from its payment, or pursuant to a final decision issued by the competent authorities as a result of an objection providing for the cancellation of the assessment.

Attachment in the hands of a third party and collection of the sums due:

1 - Attachment in the hands of a third party is the attachment of funds belonging to the attached taxpayer and held in the hands of a third party (the garnishee) and the collection of the sums due from this third-party garnishee in favour of the taxpayer.

2 - The attachment decision and its supporting documents shall be notified to the garnishee and the attached party.

3 - In the event of attachment in the hands of a third party, payments which this person claims to have settled prior to the dates appointed therefor shall not be taken into consideration unless the payment is established by an authenticated instrument or supported by a certain date.
