4 - The garnishee must declare to the Tax Administration within five days from the date on which he is notified of the attachment decision whatever funds or debt he owes to the attached party, the amount or balance of the debt, its cause and its conditions, the attachments placed thereon, as well as fungible things and movable tangible property. He must also subsequently declare every attachment or assignment affecting the funds or the debt and every loss affecting the funds, within five days from the date of the occurrence of the event.

5 - If the garnishee does not send the primary declaration to the Tax Administration within the appointed time limit, he shall become liable towards the Treasury for the sum due from him to the taxpayer, unless he puts forward an excuse worthy of acceptance as assessed by the Tax Administration.

6 - If it appears that the declaration mentioned in Clause 4 of this Article and submitted by the garnishee is incorrect, the latter shall become liable for the difference between the declared sums and the sums due from him to the taxpayer, while preserving the right of the Treasury to compensation for the damage it has suffered on account of what this delay caused or the expenses incurred.

7 - Where the garnishee conceals in bad faith the funds subject to the attachment, he shall become liable for the sums due from him to the taxpayer in addition to the penalties provided for in the laws in force.

Effects of the attachment:

1 - The attachment entails freezing the attached property in its entirety in the hands of the taxpayer against whom the attachment is levied and the third party garnishee, from the date of notification of the attachment, and in this case the taxpayer or the garnishee shall be deemed a custodian of the attached property.

2 - The third party garnishee is prohibited from delivering the attached property or paying it to his creditor or effecting a set-off with him against the debt. Likewise, the party against whom the attachment is levied is prohibited from taking delivery of the attached property or collecting the debt or waiving it or reducing its value or granting a time limit to his debtor and from disposing of the attached property.

The taxpayer against whom the attachment is levied or the third party garnishee must manage the attached property as a person mindful of the interests of the Treasury and the other debtors.

The attachment does not stop the running of interest against the garnishee so long as the property is attached in his possession.

3 - If the attachment is levied on registered bonds and shares and on other registered transferable securities, the taxpayer or the garnishee is prohibited from disposing of them or of their interest or their proceeds.

4 - In the event of disposal of the attached property contrary to the provisions of this Article, the provisions of the Penal Code shall apply to the offenders.

5 - The tax administration may, upon a request from the taxpayer, restrict the attachment to a portion of the property that is sufficient to settle the debt.

The privilege of the Treasury shall apply to the portion to which the attachment has been restricted.

Entry into premises to execute the attachment:

The employee charged with levying an attachment on the property of the taxpayer or executing the attachment in the hands of a third party must proceed to the places where the items and property are located in order to levy the attachment thereon, and he must not enter the home of the taxpayer or the garnishee except after declaring his official capacity in the presence of the mukhtar of the locality.

Assistance may be sought, where necessary, from the public authority forces.

Competence of the Sale Committee:

1 - The Sale Committee provided for in Article 77 of this Law shall undertake the valuation and sale of the attached assets by public auction.

2 - The Sale Committee shall commence its duties immediately upon the referral to it by the Director General of Finance of the file of the imposition of attachments on the assets of the defaulting taxpayer.

3 - The Committee shall meet at the invitation of its Chairman within fifteen days from the date of the referral of the file to it at the latest, and the session shall not be considered valid unless attended by the Chairman and all the members.

In the event that the Committee does not meet within fifteen days without a legitimate excuse, its meeting shall be valid at the invitation of the Chairman and in his presence and with whichever members attend, and the absentee shall be subject to disciplinary prosecution by the authority he represents.

4 - The Sale Committee may, where necessary, invite the taxpayer subject to attachment to attend its sessions.

Attachment of Real Property:

1 - Attachment of real property shall be effected in accordance with the following procedures:

a - The tax administration shall notify the competent Real Estate Registrar of the attachment decision so that he may record it in the real folio of the real property.

b - In the event that the real property is not subject to the Real Estate Register system, the tax administration shall notify the attachment decision to the Mukhtar of the locality, who shall immediately record the attachment in the register held by him or in a register that he establishes for this purpose, and another copy to the competent Real Estate Registrar, who must immediately record the attachment in a special register that he keeps for each village, town, or cadastral area.

c - If the real property is under demarcation and census, a copy of the attachment decision shall be notified to the Real Estate Judge to record the attachment on the demarcation and census record.

d - The authority that undertook the recording of the attachment in its registers pursuant to this Article shall return the notification document to the tax administration signed by it beside its official seal and stating the date of notification.

2 - The competent tax administration may authorise, upon the request of the concerned parties, the harvesting of the crops and their sale in the appropriate manner and the deposit of the price in the Treasury fund.

Sale of Attached Property:

Attached property shall be sold by public auction in accordance with the procedures provided for in this Law, with the exception of securities traded on local and international financial markets, which shall be sold directly on those markets.

The Sale Committee:

The sale by public auction in each governorate shall be undertaken by a committee formed by decree, composed of:

- A judge appointed upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice (Chairman)

- The Real Estate Registrar in the centre of the governorate in the case of the sale of attached real property (Member)

- A representative of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry in the governorate (Member)

- An employee belonging to the administrative unit competent for forced collection duties from the third category (Member and Rapporteur).

The committee shall take its decisions by majority vote, and in the event of a tie, the Chairman shall have a casting vote.

List of Conditions of Sale:

1 - The Sale Committee shall draw up a list of the conditions of sale within a time limit of ten days from the date of drawing up the list of enumeration and classification of the property subject to attachment provided for in Item (1) of Article 79 of this Law.

2 - The list of conditions shall set out the following information:

a - The types of property put up for auction, their specifications, and the place where they are located.

b - The appraised value of the said property, and the reserve price that must be taken as a basis for the auction, provided that it is equivalent to two-thirds of the appraised value.

c - The amount of the security that enables participation in the auction and its conditions.

d - The conditions of payment

e - Such other information and conditions as the auction may require.

3 - The Sale Committee shall send, within three days from the date of drawing up the list of conditions, a letter to the defaulting taxpayer to inspect this list and to state his observations thereon and submit them to the Sale Committee within a time limit of five days from the date of service.

4 - After the expiry of the five-day time limit provided for in the third Item of this Article, the Sale Committee shall examine the observations submitted by the taxpayer, and the list of conditions shall be amended on the basis thereof where necessary, and its decision regarding the ratification of the list of conditions shall be final without the need for the approval of any other authority or for any service.

Notice of the auction:

1 - The Sales Committee shall give notice of the auction in the Official Gazette, in two daily newspapers, and on the electronic website of the Ministry of Finance, provided that the period of the notice shall not be less than fifteen days prior to the date fixed for the auction, and a copy of the notice shall be posted on the noticeboard of the Tax Administration and in the governorates pursuant to a record certifying the date of posting.

2 - The notice shall state:

a - The identity of the executing party and of the taxpayer executed against, and the domicile of each of them.

b - The subject-matter of the auction and the amount of the sums required to be paid.

c - The valuation amount, the upset price, and the expenses required to be paid in addition to the price as estimated by the Sales Committee.

d - A description of the attached real property or properties, if any, the upset price fixed for each of them, and the date of registration of the attachment in the Land Register, or the special register relating to real properties not subject to the Land Register system, or the Mukhtar's register, or the demarcation and census register before the Real Estate Judge. The Land Register, or the Mukhtar's register, or the demarcation and census register before the Real Estate Judge.

e - The place where the auction is to be held and the time thereof by month, day, and hour.

f - The place where the schedule of conditions may be inspected.

g - Such other information as the auction may require.

Cancellation of the auction The person subject to attachment whose property has been put up for sale shall have the right to request the cancellation of the auction, provided that he pays in full the sums due from him prior to the time of the opening of the auction session.

Participation in the auction:

1 - The auction shall be conducted publicly at the place and time fixed therefor.

2 - Every person wishing to participate in the auction shall deposit, in the name of the Head of the Tax Administration, prior to the commencement of the auction, with the Treasury cash office or one of the banks, a sum equivalent to the upset price pertaining to the property put up for sale as fixed in the schedule of conditions provided for in Article 81 of this Law, or submit a bank guarantee securing such sum.

3 - Any person who participated in the auction, having made the deposit or provided the guarantee, and who was not the highest bidder, may withdraw the deposited money or the guarantee on the day following the date of the conclusion of the auction session.

Order of Sale of Attached Property:

1 - The Sale Committee shall determine the order of sale of the attached property pursuant to a formal record and in accordance with a list prepared thereby, such that the property the deprivation of which causes the least detriment to the taxpayer shall be sold in priority.

2 - If the attached property is perishable, the Chairman of the Sale Committee must decide, at the request of the concerned parties or the judicial custodian if any, to sell it without necessarily complying with the procedures stipulated in the law, in the manner that suits the interest of the Treasury.

3 - The right to harvest agricultural crops shall be sold by auction; however, the Chairman of the Sale Committee may delegate the matter of harvesting them to the custodian, or the Committee may undertake this matter in the appropriate manner if ripeness has reached a degree where it is feared that the planted crops or fruits may suffer damage, in which case the harvested fruits or planted crops shall be sold in accordance with what the Sale Committee decides, and the custodian or the Treasury shall recover what may have been incurred of the expenses of harvesting the agricultural crops, what may have been expended on such harvesting.

4 - If the attachment covers wrought articles or ingots of gold or silver or of a precious metal, or jewellery or precious stones, they must be weighed, their descriptions accurately specified, and appraised by an expert, and transferred in a sealed package to a place determined by the Committee and sealed by it with red wax.

5 - If the attachment falls upon property kept in a safe which the taxpayer had leased from a bank or upon property displayed in a public exhibition, the officer in charge of execution shall immediately appoint the manager of the bank or the manager of the exhibition as custodian thereof, and the safe shall be sealed with red wax until he is able to open it and inventory its contents in the presence of the party subject to attachment and in the presence of the Mukhtar of the locality.

The custodianship shall terminate upon the Tax Administration receiving the attached property.

Determination of the Appraised Value of Property The appraised value of movable and immovable property put up for auction shall be determined by the Sale Committee stipulated in Article 77 of this Law, which may seek the assistance of sworn experts for this purpose.

The value of property traded in local and international financial markets shall be determined at the value at which it is traded in those markets.

Prohibitions:

Participation in the auction, whether directly or through an intermediary, shall be prohibited for:

(a) - The Chairman and members of the Sales Committee.

(b) - The employees of the Ministry of Finance.

(c) - One of the relatives of the persons mentioned in sub-clauses (a) and (b) of this Article who is related to the participant in the auction up to the fourth degree.

The sale shall be deemed null and void in the above cases, and the offending employee shall be referred to the Disciplinary Board.

Procedures of the auction session:

1 - The Sales Committee shall hold the auction session in public and shall commence by calling out the sale and the amount of the opening price.

2 - Every higher bid shall extinguish the higher bid that preceded it.

Postponement of the sale:

The sale shall be postponed in the cases in which compulsory collection is stayed pursuant to the provisions of Article 65 of this Law.

Stay of the sale The sale shall be stayed for one of the following reasons:

(a) - The issuance of a decision by a competent judicial authority ordering a stay of execution.

(b) - Where execution is based on an instrument alleged to be forged.

(c) - The death of the distrainee taxpayer prior to the auction session if such death is notified to the Tax Administration, and the stay of the sale shall continue for a period of three months from the date of death. The resumption of execution procedures shall be announced within a time limit of fifteen days from the date of expiry of the three-month period by means of the Official Gazette and two local newspapers and on the website of the Ministry of Finance, and the heirs shall also be notified of the new date for the auction.

Continuation of sale procedures:

The Sales Committee shall continue its work in selling the property of the distrainee pursuant to the order of sale of property established by it pursuant to Article 79 of this Law until the proceeds of the sale become sufficient to settle the amounts due from the taxpayer.

Sale of property:

The auction, with respect to movable and immovable property, shall be awarded to the person offering the best prices and shall become final after the approval thereof by the Sales Committee.

Failure of bidders to come forward at the appraised price for property offered for sale:

1 - If the attached property is offered for sale and no bidders come forward for it at the appraised price, it shall be offered a second time within a period of thirty days after reducing the appraised price by ten percent (10%).

2 - And if the second auction yields no result, it shall be offered a third time under the same conditions and after reducing the appraised price by an additional ten percent (10%) of the reduced price.

3 - And if the final auction yields no result:

a - Ownership of the real properties shall be transferred to the name of the State at the price of the final offering, and shall be registered with the Land Registry Offices within a period of ten days commencing after the expiry of the period provided for in Item (2) of Article 91 of this Law.

b - Ownership of the movable property shall be transferred to the State at the price of the final offering, and it shall dispose thereof in accordance with the laws in force.

Transfer of ownership of the real property to the name of the State:

1 - In the event that ownership of the real property is transferred to the name of the State, in accordance with Item (3) of Article 92 of this Law, an appropriation shall be opened in the budget in the amount of its price, by a decision of the Minister of Finance, to settle the amounts due to the Treasury, and any excess over these amounts shall, where applicable, be paid to the owner of the real property.

2 - In the event that ownership of a real property or real properties is transferred to the name of the State in the manner mentioned in the first item of this Article, they may not be sold before the lapse of one year from their registration in the Land Register.

3 - The owner of the real property registered in the name of the State shall have the right to redeem it within one year from the date of its registration, provided that:

a - He settles all the taxes due from him together with interest calculated at the rate of (0.75%) per month of the total of these amounts, a fraction of a month being considered a full month.

b - He settles the tax accrued on the real property for the period during which it was registered in the name of the State.

c - He pays to the Treasury the amounts that it may have expended on the real property during the said period for its maintenance and improvement, together with interest calculated at the rate of (0.75%) per month of the total of these amounts, a fraction of a month being considered a full month.

And the Treasury shall return to the owner of the real property the yield from which it may have benefited during the period in which it was registered in its name.

Refusal of the last bidder to fulfill his undertaking:

1 - If the last bidder refuses to fulfill his undertaking, the guarantee submitted by him or the deposited amount shall be confiscated, and a second auction shall be conducted; if the best price submitted in the second auction equals or exceeds the price at which the first auction was awarded, the confiscated guarantee or the deposited amount shall be returned to its owner after deducting therefrom the expenses of the second auction.

2 - And if the best of the prices submitted in the second auction is less than the price at which the first auction was awarded, the guarantee or the deposited amount shall be used respectively to cover the expenses of the second auction and the difference between the two prices, and if the value of the guarantee or the deposited amount exceeds the expenses and the difference, the difference shall be returned to the bidder who owns the confiscated guarantee or deposited amount.

Expenses:

The taxpayer shall bear all the expenses of attachment, publication, expertise and auction, and these expenses shall be deducted from the proceeds of the sale before settling the amounts due to the Treasury.

Distribution of the price:

1 - If the price collected from the sale of the attached property is sufficient to settle the taxes due and the expenses relating to compulsory collection, the tax administration must settle its debts within a period not exceeding ten days from the date of payment of the price and deliver what remains thereof to the debtor taxpayer.

2 - If the price is not sufficient to satisfy the rights of the Treasury in full, the debtor taxpayer shall be pursued for the difference.

3 - The tax administration must, within ten days from the date of its receipt of the price, draw up a distribution scheme adopting the order of priority as follows:

A - Execution expenses.

B - Rights of the Treasury coupled with a right of priority, taking into account the ranks of the various debts.

C - The remaining amount for the taxpayer, if any.

Execution of the final auction decision:

1 - The issuance of the final auction decision shall entail:

a - Performance by the purchaser of the obligations incumbent upon him, and in particular payment of the price, fees and expenses without the need for notice or demand, within a period of twenty days commencing after the expiry of the time limit provided for in Item (2) of this Article.

These amounts shall be deposited in the Treasury fund in trust in favour of the Sales Committee.

b - Deeming the purchaser to be the owner of the movable and immovable property immediately upon the expiry of the time limit provided for in Item (2) of this Article, and granting the taxpayer a time limit of one month from the date of expiry of the said time limit to vacate the real property where the taxpayer occupies it, and to take delivery of his assets.

2 - The taxpayer subject to enforcement shall have the right, within ten days from the issuance of the final auction decision, to deposit in the Treasury fund an amount sufficient to settle all taxes and costs, and such deposit shall entail the lapse of the final auction decision and the lifting of the attachment.

3 - The Tax Administration shall, after the lapse of the time limit specified in the preceding paragraph and payment by the purchaser of the price and fees, and pursuant to the report of the Sales Committee and its confirmation of the deposit of the price, request the registration of the final auction decision in the name of the purchaser or in the name of any person he chooses in the Land Register, or in the mukhtar's register, or in the special register relating to real property not subject to the Land Register system, or in the demarcation and census record kept with the Real Estate Judge.

4 - The registration provided for in the preceding paragraph shall entail the transfer of ownership with respect to third parties and the striking off of the entries of pledge, mortgage and privilege recorded on the real property in favour of the Treasury.

5 - No objection against the final auction decision shall be admissible; however, an appeal before the State Council shall be admissible within five days from the date of its issuance on the following grounds:

a - The existence of a substantial defect in the auction procedures or in the wording of the decision.

b - The issuance of the decision notwithstanding the obligation to stay its execution.

c - Violation of the law in an incidental dispute addressed by the adjudication decision, if it is such as to affect the validity of the procedures.

Right of appeal against the decisions of the Tax Administration:

1 - An appeal may be lodged against the decisions of the Tax Administration issued in accordance with the provisions of Articles 97 and 98 of this Law and dismissing the objection wholly or in part before the Administrative Court within a time limit of two months from the date of notification of the decision of the Tax Administration resulting from the examination of the objection, failing which the application for appeal shall be dismissed as to form.

2 - Until the establishment and constitution of the Administrative Courts, an appeal may be lodged against the decisions of the Tax Administration before the Objection Committees which shall be established and constituted in each Governorate pursuant to a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance and the Minister of Justice, in accordance with the procedures provided for in Article 100 et seq. of this Law.

Implementing decree for this Chapter

Objection Committees:

1 - Each of the Objection Committees provided for in Article 99 of this Law shall be composed of:

1 - A serving judge or an honorary judicial, administrative or financial judge of the fourth grade at least (Chairman).

2 - A principal tax controller from outside the unit competent for the assessment (Member).

3 - A representative of the competent Chamber of Commerce and Industry chosen by the President of the said Chamber (Member).

4 - An employee from the Tax Administration that examined the objection or carried out the assessment belonging to the third category at least as a rapporteur who is not entitled to vote, and the Committee may seek the assistance of experts of competence.

These Committees shall adopt the procedures followed before the summary judiciary and shall take their decisions by a majority.

2 - A tax controller from the competent department shall be placed at the disposal of each Committee in the capacity of secretary.

3 - The rapporteur must notify the decision of the Committee to the Tax Administration and to the taxpayer within thirty days from the date of its issuance.

Implementing decree for this Chapter

Filing an Objection before the Tax Administration:

1 - Every interested party shall be entitled to object to tax assessments and special tax decisions concerning him if he finds therein an error, an excess, an unfairness against his rights, or a violation of the law, within a period of two months from the date of his notification of the assessment or decision, or from the date of payment where the competent Tax Administration has not issued a payment decision or where the taxpayer has paid the tax or penalties prior to being notified of such decision, under penalty of dismissal of the objection as to form.

2 - The objection shall be filed before the Tax Administration by means of a written petition signed by the interested party or his legal representative, and it must include the grounds for the objection and the claims of the objector, accompanied by copies of the documents justifying this objection; otherwise, the objection shall be dismissed as to form.

Implementing decree for this Chapter

Adjudication of the Objection by the Tax Administration:

1 - The Tax Administration shall examine all points set forth in the objection and adjudicate thereon within a period of six months from the date of its receipt of the objection. The unit competent to examine the objection shall be entitled to submit to the Head of the Tax Administration a reasoned request to extend the period mentioned in this item for three additional months, once only.

2 - The decision of the competent Tax Administration may be contrary to, or partially or wholly upholding of, the decision objected to. In the course of examining the objection, the Tax Administration may reconsider the assessment in the event of the discovery of new or concealed facts or elements related to the subject matter of the objection.

3 - In the event of the expiry of the original and additional period for adjudicating the objection provided for in item (1) of this Article without the Tax Administration issuing any decision in respect thereof, its silence shall then be deemed an implicit decision accepting the objection.

Copies of implicit decisions of acceptance shall be notified to the Director General of Finance to take the necessary measures against negligent employees of his administration where applicable...

4 - The adjudication resulting from the examination of the objection must be in writing and reasoned.

Implementing decree for this Chapter

Appeal before the State Council:

1 - Both the taxpayer and the Tax Administration shall be entitled to appeal the decision of the Administrative Court or the Objections Committee before the State Council in accordance with its rules of procedure, within a time limit of one month from the date of notification of the decision.

This time limit shall be deemed a forfeiture period for both the Tax Administration and the taxpayer alike.

2 - The admissibility of the appeal lodged by the taxpayer shall be conditional upon the deposit of a security deposit equal to five per cent (5%) of the amount of the contested sums in tax and fines, with the exception of the late payment fine.

Any petition for challenge not accompanied by a receipt proving payment of the security deposit shall be dismissed as to form.

Upon the issuance of the final decision, in the event the petition is accepted, this security deposit shall be used to settle the tax due, and the balance, if any, shall be refunded to the taxpayer.

In the event of rejection, the security deposit paid in accordance with the provisions of this Article shall be forfeited.

An implementation decree for this Chapter

Common provisions:

1 - The late payment fine for settling the tax provided for in Article 55 of this Law shall continue to run throughout the duration of the objection, provided that such duration does not exceed twelve months from the date of submitting the objection before the Tax Administration within the time limit provided for in Article 97; otherwise, the running of the said fine shall cease as of the date of expiry of this duration.

2 - In the event of the partial or total acceptance of the objection by the Tax Administration, the Administrative Courts, the Objections Committees, or the State Council, the taxpayer who has previously paid the amounts imposed upon him shall be entitled to obtain:

a - The balance overpaid by him.

b - The statutory interest due on this balance.

An implementation decree for this Chapter

Cessation of the Taxpayer's Liability:

1 - The liability of the taxpayer for tax violations occurring due to force majeure or exceptional circumstances shall cease for the tax period during which the cause of the force majeure occurred, with respect to the fines relating to the following violations:

a - Delay in submitting declarations of commencement of work and applications for registration to the tax administration.

b - Failure to produce statutory registers and supporting documents.

c - Failure to pay taxes and failure to submit periodic statements and annual declarations within the statutory time limits.

2 - In order to benefit from the provisions of paragraph 1 of this Article, the taxpayer must notify the tax administration of the state of force majeure or exceptional circumstances within a period of one month from the date of its occurrence, provided that it is proven by documents issued by official authorities, and he must also proceed to regularise his tax status by reconstituting his registers, submitting the statutory declarations, and paying the taxes and duties due from him within a period of two months from the date of cessation of the force majeure or exceptional circumstances.

Implementing Decree for this Article

Fines of Tax Laws:

The fines provided for in the tax laws are hereby repealed and the fines provided for in this Law are substituted.

Fine on the Tax Difference :

Upon the occurrence of a violation involving one or several documents common to several taxes, the highest fine on the tax difference shall be enforced.

The details of the application of this Article shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

Penal Financial Violations:

Penal financial violations shall be prosecuted in accordance with the provisions of Legislative Decree No. 156 dated 16/9/1983 and its amendments, and the penalties prescribed therefor shall be imposed by the courts upon the request of the Ministry of Finance without the need for prior formal notice to the taxpayer to correct his declaration.

Delay in or failure to submit a registration application:

1 - A fine shall be imposed on every person who fails to submit his application for registration with the Tax Administration within the statutory time limits, and fails to identify the beneficial owner of his activity, as provided for in paragraph one of Article 32 of this Law, or in the tax laws, in the amount of:

- 2.000.000 L.L. (two million Lebanese pounds) for joint-stock companies,

- 1.000.000 L.L. (one million Lebanese pounds) for partnerships, limited liability companies and tax-exempt institutions,

- 300.000 L.L. (three hundred thousand Lebanese pounds) for individuals and other taxpayers.

2 - A fine shall be imposed on every person who fails to notify the Tax Administration of any amendment to the information provided for in item two of Article 32 of this Law, in the amount of: 200.000 L.L. (two hundred thousand Lebanese pounds) for joint-stock companies 100.000 L.L. (one hundred thousand Lebanese pounds) for partnerships, limited liability companies and tax-exempt institutions, 50.000 L.L. (fifty thousand Lebanese pounds) for individuals and other taxpayers. If the amendments set out in item 2 of Article 32 of this Law relate to several taxes, the fine shall apply once.

Delay in or failure to declare definitive cessation of business:

A fine shall be imposed on every person who fails to notify the Tax Administration of his definitive cessation of business within the statutory time limits as provided for in Article 33 of this Law, and in the tax laws, in the amount of:

- 2.000.000 L.L. (two million Lebanese pounds) for joint-stock companies,

- 1.000.000 L.L. (one million Lebanese pounds) for partnerships, limited liability companies and tax-exempt institutions,

- 300.000 L.L. (three hundred thousand Lebanese pounds) for individuals and other taxpayers.

- Delay in or failure to submit the tax declaration

There shall be imposed on every taxpayer who has failed to submit the declaration provided for in Item One of Article 38 of this Law, a fine of ten percent (10%) of the value of the tax due in accordance with the declaration or the profit determined by the Tax Administration for each month of delay (or fraction of a month), provided that the fine shall not exceed one hundred percent (100%) of the value of the tax due for each declaration, and shall not be less than:

- 6.750.000 L.L. (six million seven hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese Pounds) for joint-stock companies,

- 4.500.000 L.L. (four million five hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds) for partnerships, limited liability companies and institutions exempted from tax,

- 750.000 L.L. (seven hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese Pounds) for individuals and other taxpayers.

Article 110- Incorrect tax declarations

There shall be imposed on every person who declares less than the tax required to be declared, a fine of twenty percent (20%) of the value of the difference between the net tax due and the net tax declared, provided that the fine shall not be less than:

- 6.750.000 L.L. (six million seven hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese Pounds) for joint-stock companies,

- 4.500.000 L.L. (four million five hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds) for partnerships, limited liability companies and institutions exempted from tax,

- 750.000 L.L. (seven hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese Pounds) for individuals and other taxpayers.

Omission to declare information:

There shall be imposed, on every person who has omitted to declare information when filling out the declarations and statements required to be submitted in accordance with the provisions of this Law and the special tax laws, where such omission did not result in an additional tax, a fine for each declaration of:

- 200.000 (two hundred thousand Pounds of Lebanon) for joint-stock companies.

- 100.000 (one hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds) for partnerships, limited liability companies and institutions exempted from tax,

- 50.000 (fifty thousand Lebanese Pounds) for individuals and other taxpayers.

Implementing decree for this Article

Omission to submit the auditor's report:

There shall be imposed on a person who has failed to submit the auditor's report in accordance with the provisions of the tax laws the fine relating to failure to submit or delay in submitting the declaration provided for in Article 109 of this Law.

Violations relating to invoices:

1 - A fine of two percent (2%) of the value of the transaction that is the subject of the invoice shall be imposed on every taxpayer who fails to issue an invoice when doing so is mandatory in accordance with the law.

2 - A fine of 0.5% of the value of the transaction that is the subject of the invoice shall be imposed on every taxpayer who fails to show, on the invoices or similar documents that he is legally obliged to issue, his tax identification number or other formal information that does not affect the verification of the validity of the tax due.

Failure to keep accounting records and documents:

A fine of fifty percent (50%) of the undeclared net tax shall be imposed on anyone who fails to keep the accounting records and documents provided for in Article 29 of this Law or in the tax laws, provided that it is not less than:

- 750.000 L.L. (seven hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese Pounds) for joint-stock companies,

- 500.000 (five hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds) for partnerships and limited liability companies and for establishments exempted from tax,

- 100.000 L.L. (one hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds) for individuals and for other taxpayers.

Obstruction of tax audit procedures:

A fine of fifty percent (50%) of the value of the unpaid tax due shall be imposed on anyone who refrains from producing the records or documents proving the validity of the declaration, or refrains from recording certain transactions therein in accordance with due form, provided that it is not less than:

- 750.000 L.L. (seven hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese Pounds) for joint-stock companies,

- 500.000 L.L. (five hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds) for partnerships and limited liability companies and for establishments exempted from tax,

- 100.000 (one hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds) for individuals and for other taxpayers.

Liability of persons entrusted with the task of withholding and declaring the tax due:

A fine of five percent (5%) of the value of the tax due for each month of delay shall be imposed on anyone who omits to withhold and declare the tax, or who violates the provisions of Clause (4) of Article 14 of this Law, provided that it does not exceed the amount of the tax and is not less than:

- 750.000 L.L. (seven hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese Pounds) for joint-stock companies,

- 500.000 L.L. (five hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds) for partnerships and limited liability companies and for establishments exempted from tax,

- 100.000 L.L. (one hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds) for individuals and the other taxpayers.

Obstructing the execution of compulsory collection procedures:

A fine of five per cent (5%) per month of the value of the tax required to be collected compulsorily shall be imposed on the taxpayer or any other person who prevents the Tax Administration from being able to carry out the execution of the compulsory collection procedures provided for in Chapter Eleven of Title Three of this Law, provided that it does not exceed the amount of the tax required to be collected and is not less than:

- 750.000 L.L. (seven hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese pounds) for joint-stock companies,

- 500.000 L.L. (five hundred thousand Lebanese pounds) for partnerships, limited liability companies and tax-exempt institutions,

- 100.000 L.L. (one hundred thousand Lebanese pounds) for individuals and the remaining taxpayers.

Fines specific to the beneficial owner:

1 - Every shareholder or quota-holder in a capital company who refrains from giving the correct information regarding the beneficial owner of his shareholding or quota in the company shall be subject to a fine equivalent to 100% of his share of the tax that falls upon him, calculated on the basis of the sum of the value of the commercial profits tax payable by the company and the tax on distributions, in the year in which the violation was committed, provided that it is not less than the minimum threshold specified in this Law according to his legal form.

2 - A partner in a partnership or the owner of a sole proprietorship or a profession, in the event that he refrains from giving the company information regarding the beneficial owner of his partnership, shall be subject to a fine equivalent to 100% of the value of the tax payable on his share, provided that it is not less than the minimum threshold specified in this Law according to his legal form.

3 - Every person who omits to declare information relating to the beneficial owner when filling out the declarations and statements required to be submitted in accordance with the provisions of this Law and the special tax laws, or refrains from notifying the Tax Administration of the refusal of the partner or shareholder to give him information regarding the beneficial owners in his activity referred to in Item «f» of Article 37 of this Law, shall be subject to a flat fine as follows:

- 2.000.000 L.L. (two million Lebanese pounds) for joint-stock companies,

- 1.000.000 L.L. (one million Lebanese pounds) for partnerships, limited liability companies and tax-exempt institutions,

- 500.000 L.L. (five hundred thousand Lebanese pounds) for individuals and the remaining taxpayers.

Delay in submitting or failure to submit the declaration on the leasing of residential premises located in summer resort areas:

A fine of five per cent (5%) of the value of the tax due on the revenues generated during the said leasing period shall be imposed on anyone who violates the provisions of Article 19 of the Built Property Tax Law relating to the declaration on the leasing of residential premises located in summer resort areas during the summer season, provided that the fine shall not be less than 200.000 L.L. (two hundred thousand Lebanese pounds).

Delay in submitting or failure to submit the declaration on changes occurring to a building:

A fine of five per cent (5%) of the value of the annual tax due for each year, with fractions of a year considered a full year, shall be imposed on anyone who violates the provisions of Article 23 of the Built Property Tax Law relating to notifying the competent tax administration of anything that occurs to buildings (change in their intended use, their occupancy or leasing, etc.).

Failure to register contracts or registration of a simulated contract:

Anyone who violates the provisions of the Built Property Tax Law relating to the registration of contracts shall be punished by a fine equivalent to five per cent (5%) of the amount of the annual tax due for each year in which the violation continues, with fractions of a year considered a full year. Anyone who violates the provisions of the Built Property Tax Law relating to the registration of simulated contracts shall be punished by a fine equivalent to ten per cent (10%) of the amount of the annual tax due for each year in which the violation continues, with fractions of a year considered a full year.

Delay in declaring or failure to declare the accrual of the right to tax:

A fine of ten per cent (10%) of the value of the annual tax due for each year in which the violation continues, with fractions of a year considered a full year, shall be imposed on anyone who violates the provisions of Article 50 of the Built Property Tax Law relating to the declaration on the accrual of the right to tax (completion of buildings or parts thereof, re-leasing, alteration and restoration, cessation of the grounds for exemption).

Failure by the enterprise to complete the investment operation for which a portion of the profits was allocated:

In the event of a violation of the provisions of paragraph (5) of Item "First" of Article 5 bis of the Income Tax Law relating to the failure to invest the amounts deducted from profits or the breach of any of the conditions specified to benefit from the exemption, a fine of one per cent (1%) of the value of the uninvested deducted amounts shall be imposed for each month, provided that a fraction of a month shall be considered a full month, starting from the year following the financial year from the profits of which those amounts were deducted.

Failure to keep a register of employees or refusal to enable the Tax Administration to inspect it:

A fine of 25.000 L.L. (twenty-five thousand Lebanese pounds) for each name omitted from being recorded in this register shall be imposed on anyone who does not keep a register of employees in accordance with the provisions of Article 51 of the Income Tax Law, or refuses to enable the Tax Administration to inspect it.

Failure to register employees with the Tax Administration within the statutory time limits:

For every violation of the provisions relating to the obligation to register employees with the Tax Administration, a flat fine of fifty thousand Lebanese pounds shall be imposed for each salaried person or employee who is not registered within the specified time limits, or concerning whom false information is provided.

Failure to draw up the periodic statement of salaries and wages and failure to submit it to the Tax Administration:

A fine of five per cent (5%) of the amount of tax due, provided that this fine does not exceed 1.000.000 L.L. (one million Lebanese pounds) and is not less than 100.000 (one hundred thousand Lebanese pounds) for each period for which the corresponding periodic statement was not submitted, shall be imposed on anyone who violates the provisions of paragraph (5) of Article 63 of the Income Tax Law relating to drawing up the periodic statement of salaries and wages and submitting it to the competent Tax Administration within the statutory time limit specified for each of the periodic payments.

The Tax Administration shall send a copy of the tax declaration submitted by the employer relating exclusively to the salaries, wages and allowances of salaried persons to the National Social Security Fund, to compare it with the declarations submitted to this Fund by the employer, and to notify the Tax Administration immediately of the non-conforming declarations.

In the event of a violation of the provisions of Article 52 of the Income Tax Law as regards the non-conformity of the declaration submitted by the employer to the Tax Administration with the declaration submitted by him to the National Social Security Fund with respect to the names of the salaried persons and the total salaries, wages and allowances paid to them, a fine equal to ten times the difference between each of the two declarations shall be imposed.

Failure to draw up schedules of coupons and securities:

A fine of 300.000 L.L. (three hundred thousand Lebanese pounds) shall be imposed on a person who did not draw up the schedules of coupons or securities in accordance with the provisions of Article 79 of the Income Tax Law.

Drawing up inventories of estates without the attendance of a representative of the competent financial departments:

Where inventories of estates have been drawn up without the attendance of a representative of the competent financial departments contrary to the provisions of Article 30 of the Inheritance Duty Law, the competent financial departments shall have the right to proceed to draw up a new inventory of any estate or to impose upon the offending drafter a fine equal to the value of the duty that may be payable on the difference between the two inventories.

If the estate is not subject to inheritance duty, a fine in the amount of 200.000 L.L. (two hundred thousand Lebanese pounds) shall be imposed upon the offending drafter.

Delay in submitting or failure to submit declarations and their attachments or to submit the remaining documents:

Where the concerned parties fail to submit the declaration and its attachments or the declaration of the remaining documents within the time limits specified in Article 21 of the Inheritance Duty Law, they shall be punished by a fine equal to three percent (3%) for the infringement of failure to declare or delay in submitting the declaration and two percent

(2%) for the infringement of failure to submit the documents or delay in submitting them for each month of delay or fraction of a month, of the value of the duty that is payable on the property, rights or values not declared within the specified time limits, provided that the fine for each of these two infringements shall not exceed the value of fifty percent (50%) of the duty on the basis of which it is imposed and shall not be less, even if no duty is payable, than one hundred thousand pounds, for each of these two infringements for each chargeable event, including the chargeable events occurring prior to the issuance of this Law for which the duty due thereon has not been liquidated.

A fine equal to five times the duty or part of the duty that the Treasury was exposed to losing as a result of the infringement shall be imposed on anyone who commits any of the following infringements:

1 - Failure to affix stamps of the value of the duty due or affixing stamps whose value is less than the value of the duty due.

2 - Failure to place a franking impression of the value of the duty due or placing a franking impression whose value is less than the value of the duty due.

3 - Failure to collect and concealment of part of the duty that establishments subject to the periodic payment method are required to collect from the concerned parties, or concealment of what was actually collected thereof, wholly or partially, and failure to declare it to the competent financial department upon paying the proceeds of the said duty to the Treasury fund.

Failure to cancel stamps affixed to instruments and writings:

A fine of fifty per cent (50%) of the value of the stamps that are uncancelled or unlawfully cancelled shall be imposed on anyone who fails to cancel stamps affixed to instruments and writings or cancels them in violation of the provisions of Article 25 of the Fiscal Stamp Duty Law.

Delay in paying the duty in cash to the Treasury fund:

A fine equivalent to five times the said duty shall be imposed on anyone who delays in paying the duty in cash to the Treasury fund beyond the specified time limit, whenever payment thereof in this manner is required pursuant to the Fiscal Stamp Duty Law.

Delay in or failure to keep statutory registers:

1 - In the event of delay in or failure to keep the register provided for in Article 32 of the Fiscal Stamp Duty Law as well as the register provided for in Article 52 of the Fiscal Stamp Duty Law, a fine of fifty per cent (50%) of the value of the duty due as a result of such violation shall be imposed.

2 - In the event of failure to record the information required by law to be recorded in the registers mentioned in item 1 of this Article, a lump-sum fine of 250.000 L.L. (two hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese Pounds) shall be imposed.

Sale of fiscal stamps without a licence:

A fine of 250.000 (two hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese Pounds) shall be imposed on anyone who sells fiscal stamps without a licence, and the stamps offered for sale shall be confiscated and shall become an acquired right of the Treasury without the person concerned having any right to consideration or compensation. The Minister of Finance may decide to close the premises, when the violation occurs in unlicensed premises, for a period ranging between three days and one month if the violation is repeated within three years.

Defacing a stamp impression to the extent of rendering its value unknown:

A lump-sum fine of 250.000 L.L. (two hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese Pounds) shall be imposed on anyone who writes on the stamp impression or places thereon any print, writing, drawing or mark of any kind whatsoever resulting in its value not being known.

Violation of the provisions relating to licensing the manufacture, import and sale of stamping machines:

A fine of 250.0000 L.L. (two hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese Pounds) shall be imposed on anyone who violates the provisions of Article 38 of the Fiscal Stamp Duty Law relating to licensing the manufacture, import, sale and trading of stamping machines, and the offending stamping machines shall be confiscated and shall become an acquired right of the Treasury without the person concerned having any right to consideration or compensation.

Failure to keep the two registers relating to the payment, sale or purchase of coupons or other financial securities:

In the event of failure to keep the two registers provided for in Article 80 of the Income Tax Law and relating to the recording of transactions of payment, sale or purchase of coupons or other financial securities from which tax must be withheld, a fine equal to 300.000 L.L. (three hundred thousand Lebanese pounds) shall be imposed.

Failure to draw up an abstract of Register No. 1 and failure to pay the withheld tax:

A fine of 300.000 L.L. (three hundred thousand Lebanese pounds) shall be imposed on the tax withholder who violates the provisions of Article 81 of the Income Tax Law relating to drawing up an abstract of Register No. 1.

In the event of delay in paying the withheld tax within the legal time limits, the late payment fine provided for in Article 55 of this Law shall be imposed on the unpaid amounts.

Delivery by a debtor to an estate of what is in his possession contrary to the provisions of the law:

If one of the debtors to an estate delivers anything in his possession contrary to the provisions of Article 25 of the Inheritance Duty Law, he shall be deemed liable towards the Treasury for the duty due on what he relinquished.

If the company is not subject to the inheritance duty, a fine of 150.000 L.L. (one hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese pounds) shall be imposed on the offender.

Violation of the rules for opening safes or boxes:

Any person who violates the provisions of Article 28 of the Inheritance Duty Law relating to the rules for opening leased safes or boxes after the death of the lessee shall be deemed liable towards the Treasury for the duty due on the funds deposited in those safes or boxes.

Delay or failure by a creditor of the estate to submit a statement of the amount of the debt:

If a creditor of the estate fails to submit a statement of the amount of the debt provided for in Article 29 of the Inheritance Duty Law within the specified time limit, a fine equal to the value of the duty that may become due from the heirs by reason of the non-deduction of this debt from the basis of the estate shall be imposed on him.

If the estate is not subject to the inheritance duty, a fine of 200.000 L.L. (two hundred thousand Lebanese pounds) shall be imposed on the offending creditor.

Forcibly preventing or attempting to prevent employees charged with recording violations from performing their duties, or treating them with violence or severity, or subjecting them to contempt, slander, and defamation:

Whoever forcibly prevents or attempts to prevent the employees charged with recording violations of the Fiscal Stamp Duty Law from performing the duties of their office, or treats them with violence or severity, or subjects them to contempt, slander, or defamation in any form whatsoever, shall be prosecuted in accordance with the provisions of Articles 381 et seq. of the Penal Code.

Issuing an invoice without right:

Every person not registered for Value Added Tax who issues an invoice without right shall be punished by a fine equivalent to three times the tax recorded on that invoice.

Issuing an invoice in violation of the law:

A fine of twenty-five (25%) of the tax due on the transaction that is the subject of the invoice shall be imposed on every person subject to Value Added Tax who issues an invoice or similar document in violation of the provisions of Article 38 of the Value Added Tax Law with respect to stating the tax due or describing the transaction.

Violations related to import and export:

In operations of importing and exporting goods, the verification, recording, collection, and settlement of violations of the provisions of the Value Added Tax Law shall take place in accordance with the provisions stipulated in the customs legislation.

Exemption from fiscal stamp duties:

Declarations, objections, statements, and other papers and documents stipulated in this Law or in the tax laws, which are submitted to the various public administrations, shall be exempted from treasury stamp duties.

Reduction of fines:

Notwithstanding any other text, all fines due on taxes and duties assessed and collected by the Directorate General of Finance, which have been issued or will be issued, or which are declared and the tax due thereon is paid in accordance with the advance payment system, resulting from violations occurring during the period extending up to the date of publication of this Law, shall be reduced by ninety percent (90%), provided that the taxes, duties, and reduced fines are paid within a time limit not exceeding 30/4/2009, and provided that a monthly interest at the rate of 1.5% shall apply starting from 1/2/2009 and up to the date of payment, with a fraction of a month being considered a full month.

Fines paid prior to the entry into force of this Law shall be considered a vested right of the Treasury and may not be refunded unless they were the result of a material error in the assessment.

Misuse of stamping machines and commission of violations:

The licence to use a stamping machine shall be revoked, without the concerned party having any right to compensation, if the licensee misuses the said machine, commits one of the violations or abuses provided for in Article 31, or neglects to comply with the provisions of Articles 32, 34 and 35 of the Fiscal Stamp Duty Law.

Failure to retain instruments and writings subject to the duty throughout the legal period:

A fixed fine of 500.000 L.L. (five hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds) shall be imposed on anyone who fails to retain the instruments and writings subject to the duty throughout the retention period provided for in Article 99 of the Fiscal Stamp Duty Law.

Using, selling or attempting to sell, with prior knowledge, previously used fiscal stamps:

Anyone who, with prior knowledge, uses, sells or attempts to sell previously used fiscal stamps shall be punished by imprisonment from fifteen days to two months and by a fine of 250.000 L.L. (two hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese Pounds), or by either of these two penalties.

Counterfeiting the special die placed in stamping machines:

Anyone who counterfeits or attempts to counterfeit the special die placed in the stamping machines provided for in Article 40 of the Fiscal Stamp Duty Law, as well as anyone who counterfeits or attempts to counterfeit the impression of that die, shall be prosecuted in accordance with the provisions of Articles 450 and 451 of the Penal Code.

Counterfeiting or forging fiscal stamps or using forged or counterfeit fiscal stamps with prior knowledge:

Anyone who counterfeits, forges or attempts to counterfeit or forge fiscal stamps, or uses counterfeit or forged stamps with prior knowledge, shall be prosecuted in accordance with the provisions of Articles 450 and 451 of the Penal Code.

Entering false or erroneous information or omitting to enter correct information in the registers:

Anyone who enters false or erroneous information in the register provided for in Article 32 or in Article 52 of the Fiscal Stamp Duty Law, or omits to enter correct information that ought to have been entered, shall be prosecuted in accordance with the provisions of Articles 461 and 462 of the Penal Code.

Article 153 bis was added pursuant to Budget Law 324 /2024

Article 153- bis

All fines due under this Law shall be imposed on taxpayers who are obliged to declare and pay the tax in a currency other than the Lebanese currency, in the currency of the tax due in accordance with each type of violation, provided that the fine shall not exceed the amount of the tax and shall not be less than:

- 250 USD (two hundred and fifty United States dollars) for joint-stock companies,

- 150 USD (one hundred and fifty United States dollars) for partnerships and limited liability companies and for establishments exempted from tax,

- 50 USD (fifty United States dollars) for individuals and the remaining taxpayers.

Article 154- Lapsed amounts and rounding of fractions

* Lapsed amounts: With the exception of taxes resulting from returns submitted by the taxpayer on the basis of self-assessment, or pursuant to applications for the collection of taxes submitted by taxpayers from the competent financial offices, amounts due from taxpayers, including the assessment fines attached thereto prior to the reduction in force pursuant to Law No. 662/2005, the value of which does not exceed 500.000 L.L. (five hundred thousand Lebanese pounds), for all tax periods, shall be deemed lapsed, and the competent financial units shall be exempted from issuing assessment rolls or collection orders for those amounts and from collecting them.

* Rounding of a fraction of tax: A fraction of ten thousand Lebanese pounds (10.000 L.L.) shall be rounded up in favour of the Treasury to ten thousand Lebanese pounds (10.000 L.L.) in assessment and collection transactions and all various types of duties and expenditure, including allocations, salaries, wages, and their ancillaries.

Duties collected in favour of the Treasury, and which are paid into its funds, must include in every transaction in which a rounding of a fraction of ten thousand Lebanese pounds ( 10.000 L.L.) occurs, a rounding up to ten thousand Lebanese pounds (10.000 L.L.).

The detailed rules for the application of this Article shall be determined, where necessary, by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

Repealed provisions of other laws:

As from the date of entry into force of this Law, all legal texts contrary to it or inconsistent with its content, whether general or special, shall be repealed.

Detailed rules for the application of the Law:

The detailed rules for the application of this Law, with respect to the Articles that do not specify the competent authority to determine the detailed rules for their application, shall be determined by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

-The draft Law set forth in Decree No. 11752 dated 15 January 2004 concerning the organisation of the academic councils at the Lebanese University, as amended by the Administration and Justice Committee, is hereby approved.

-This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The following Article (1) bis is hereby added to Law No. 75 dated 26/12/1967 and its amendments:

Article 1 bis:

Wherever they appear in this Law, the following words and expressions shall have the following meanings:

"The University": The Lebanese University

"The Council": The Council of the Lebanese University

"The Minister": The Supervising Minister

"The Unit": A faculty or an institute

The text of Article 10 of Law No. 75 dated 26/12/1967 and its amendments is hereby repealed and replaced in the following text:

New Article 10:

1- The President of the University shall be appointed from among five candidates holding the rank of professor or having fulfilled the conditions for the rank, nominated by the University Council. The appointment shall be made by a decree pursuant to a decision taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister, at least two months prior to the expiry of the term of office of the President of the University.

2- The nomination mechanism shall be determined by a decision taken in the University Council.

3- The term of office of the President shall be fixed at five years, non-renewable except after the lapse of a full term of office.

4- The President shall be exempted from his teaching load.

5- In the event of the absence of the President, the eldest of the deans shall deputise for him.

6- In the event of a vacancy in the post of the President, a new President shall be appointed by the same mechanism provided for in this Article.

The text of Article 24 of Law No. 75 dated 26/12/1967 and its amendments is hereby repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 24: A university unit shall be administered by a dean and a council.

The text of Article 26 of Law No. 75 dated 26/12/1967 and its amendments is hereby repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 26: The dean of the unit shall be exempted from at most half of his teaching load.

Effective Date of the Law

This Law shall be published in the Official Gazette and shall apply with effect from 1/1/2009.

Paragraph added by Law 231 dated 22/10/2012 O.G. 45

- The application of penalties arising from the following violations shall be suspended up to the operations of the year 2012:

- The obligation to keep accounting records for taxpayers assessed on the basis of estimated profit who are not subject to Value Added Tax, provided for in Item (2) of Article (29) of this Law.

- The obligation of employers to register their employees with the Tax Administration, provided for in Article (32) of this Law.

- The obligation of employers to declare employees who have left their employment, provided for in Item (1) of Article (33) of this Law.

- The obligation of taxpayers not subject to Value Added Tax to adopt their registration number on documents issued by them, the obligation of all taxpayers to comply with the use of the registration numbers of their employees and persons dealing with them, and the obligation of the taxpayer to display the formal information on invoices or similar documents, provided for in Item (2) of Article (34) and Item (2) of Article (113) of this Law.

- The obligation not to omit declaring information that does not result in additional tax when filling out tax returns and statements, the penalty prescribed for which is provided for in Article 111 of this Law.

The details of application of this Article shall be determined by decisions issued by the Minister of Finance.

The text of Article 25 of Law No. 75 dated 26/12/1967 and its amendments is repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 25: On the appointment of the Dean of the Unit:

1- The Dean shall be appointed for a term of four years, non-renewable except after the expiry of a full term, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Tutelage.

2- The proposal of the Minister shall be based on a list of nominations bearing three names submitted by the University Council from among five names proposed by the Council of the Unit concerned.

3- The selection of the candidates referred to in item 2 shall be made from among the professors of the Unit who are part of the permanent staff of the faculty holding the rank of professor or those who have fulfilled the conditions of the rank, and failing that, the candidates may be selected from among the full-time contracted faculty who hold the rank of professor or who have fulfilled the conditions of the rank, provided that the appointed Dean is admitted by the same decree into the permanent staff of the University if he meets the conditions for admission into the permanent staff. In the event of the unavailability of those holding the rank of professor or those who have fulfilled the conditions of the rank, they may be selected from among the professors of another unit, subject to homogeneity in specialisation.

4- In the event of the absence of the Dean of the Unit for more than fifteen days, the highest-ranking or highest-grade director shall deputise for him. In the event of a vacancy, a new Dean shall be appointed to complete the term in accordance with the mechanism provided for in this Article.

The text of Article 31 of Law No. 75 26/12/1967 and its amendments is repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 31: The provisions applicable to the meetings of the University Council shall apply to the meetings of the Unit Council.

The text of Article 29 of Law No. 75 dated 26/12/1967 and its amendments is hereby repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 29:

A- The Unit Council shall be composed of:

1- The Dean of the Unit, as President.

2- The Directors of the branches of the Unit.

3- The representatives of the teaching staff on the Branch Councils.

4- The Head of the Research Centre, if any.

5- Two student representatives in the Unit, in accordance with a mechanism established by the University Council.

6- The representative of the professors of the Unit on the University Council, without having the right to vote.

B- In the absence of branches, the Unit Council shall be composed of:

1- The Dean of the Unit, as President.

2- The Heads of the Academic Departments, and in the absence of departments, four members elected by the members of the teaching staff from among themselves.

3- An elected representative of the teaching staff.

4- The Head of the Research Centre, if any.

5- Two student representatives.

6- The representative of the professors of the Unit on the University Council shall attend the meetings of the Unit Council without having the right to vote.

The text of Article 30 of Law No. 75 dated 26/12/1967 and its amendments is hereby repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 30:

- The Unit Council shall meet at least once every two weeks upon convocation by its President, or pursuant to a reasoned written request by one-third of the members, or pursuant to a request by the University Council or its President.

- The sittings of the Council shall be valid if attended by at least two-thirds of the members upon the first convocation, failing which, by an absolute majority upon the second convocation.

- Decisions shall be taken by an absolute majority, and in the event of a tie, the President shall have a casting vote.

- The Secretary of the University Unit shall perform the duties of Secretary of this Council, and shall draw up the minutes of the sittings and keep them in due form, after they are signed by the President and the members, and in the event of his absence, the Dean of the Unit shall designate a person to perform the duties of Secretary of the Council.

The text of Article 32 of Law No. 75 dated 26/12/1967 and its amendments is hereby repealed and replaced with the following text:

New Article 32: Duties of the Unit Council:

The duties of the Unit Council shall cover the following:

1- Establishing the internal bylaws of the unit, provided that they are coupled with the approval of the University Council.

2- Submitting proposals in the various affairs of the unit, particularly in relation to curricula, research, research contracts, examination regulations and the entrance competitive examination.

3- Proposing full-time contracts and nominations for appointment based on the recommendations of the branch councils or the departments in faculties that have no branches, in accordance with the mechanism provided for in Decree No. 9084 dated 13/11/2002. And proposing hourly teaching and training contracts pertaining to the unit.

4- Nominating members of the technical and administrative staff for appointment, contracting and promotion based on the recommendations of the branch councils.

6- Proposing the draft budget of the unit based on the proposals of the branch councils.

7- Discussing and approving the annual report prepared by the Dean on the administrative, financial and academic affairs of the unit, in preparation for submitting it to the University Council before the end of the month of March.

8- Proposing the names of outstanding students nominated to benefit from specialisation scholarships based on the recommendations of the branches or the departments in faculties that have no branches. This shall be in accordance with the regulations in force and the designation of missions.

9- Proposing candidates from among the members of the teaching staff to benefit from scholarships and to pursue further education, based on the recommendations of the branch councils.

10- Deciding on applications by members of the teaching staff to benefit from the sabbatical year (seventh year).

11- Proposing cooperation and exchange projects with public and private institutions at home and abroad, and participation in scientific seminars and specialised conferences.

12- Proposing registration fees and fees for the use of the unit's facilities.

13- Proposing the approval of grants, donations, contributions and gifts offered to the unit or to any of its components.

14- Discussing the semi-annual reports and recommendations of the branch directors submitted to the Unit Council.

15- Submitting nominations for the position of Dean of the unit and Director of the Research Centre.

16- Reviewing the results of examinations and the results of the entrance competitive examination to the unit.

17- Proposing to the University Council, by absolute majority, the annulment of decisions taken by the Dean of the unit which contravene the adopted regulations and laws.

18- Proposing to the University Council, by absolute majority, the annulment of decisions taken by any of the directors of branches and centres and heads of departments which contravene the adopted regulations and laws. With reservation of the right of the maker of the contested decision to petition the University Council.

19- All other duties provided for by the laws and regulations in force.
Articles 75 and 76 of Law No. 75 dated 26/12/1967 and its amendments are hereby repealed.

A new chapter shall be added to Law No. 75 dated 26/12/1967, which is Chapter Ten: The Branch Council, in the following form:

Chapter Ten - The Branch Council

New Article Seventy-Five: The branch shall be managed by a Director and a Council. New Article Seventy-Six:

The Branch Council shall be composed of at least five members:

1- The Director as President

2- A representative of the members of the teaching body in the branch.

3- The Heads of the academic departments in the branch. In the absence of departments, the Branch Council shall be completed by electing at most five members by the members of the teaching body.

4- A representative of the students.

5- The Secretary of the branch shall perform the function of Secretary of this Council, and shall draw up the minutes of the sessions and keep them in due form after their signature by the President and the members.

Article Seventy-Seven: - The Council shall meet upon convocation by its President once every two weeks, and it may also meet upon convocation by the Dean or whenever one-third of the members submit a reasoned written request.

- If the Dean attends, he shall preside over the session.

- The sessions of the Council shall not be legal unless attended by two-thirds of the members upon the first convocation or by an absolute majority upon the second convocation.

Decisions shall be taken by an absolute majority. In the event of an equality of votes, the side of the President shall prevail.

- The provisions governing the meetings of the Unit Council shall apply to the meetings of the Branch Council.

Article Seventy-Eight:

- On the appointment of the Branch Director:

1- The Branch Council concerned shall submit, to the Unit Council, a nomination list of five names of professors holding the rank of Professor or Assistant Professor, or who have fulfilled the conditions for promotion to this rank, or an Instructor with at least ten years of experience on the permanent staff of the University or on a full-time basis.

2- The Unit Council shall select, from among the five names submitted to it by the Branch Council, three names which it shall in turn submit to the President of the University.

3- The President of the University shall appoint, by a decision issued by him, one of the three names submitted to him to be the Director of the branch concerned.

4- The term of office of the Director shall be three years, non-renewable except after the expiry of a full term.

5- The Director shall be exempted from at most one-third of his teaching load at his request and by a decision of the University Council based on the recommendation of the Unit Council.

6- The Director shall assume the management of business in the branch from the administrative and financial aspects in accordance with the law and regulations of the University.

7- In the event of vacancy of the post of Director, the appointment shall take place in accordance with the same mechanism.

In the event of absence, the oldest member of the Branch Council shall replace him.

Article Seventy-Nine: Tasks of the Branch Council:

The Branch Council shall assume the supervision of the academic, administrative and financial affairs of the branch, and the coordination between its various departments and the follow-up of the educational performance and academic activities therein.

Within this framework, the Branch Council shall perform the following tasks:

1- Following up the implementation of the decisions of the Unit Council relating to the branch.

2- Recommending the establishment or amendment of teaching curricula and examination and evaluation regulations in the faculty or institute.

3- Proposing the internal regulations of the branch.

4- Proposing the budget of the branch.

5- Proposing the examining committees and examination committees.

6- Proposing the distribution of subjects and courses among the members of the teaching body in the branch.

7- Submitting the requests of the members of the teaching body to benefit from the sabbatical year.

8- Nominating students to benefit from scholarships in accordance with the ranking submitted by the departments concerned, and in accordance with the scholarship regulations in force.

9- Determining the needs of the branch for members of the teaching body for entry into the permanent staff, or full-time contracting, or hourly contracting.

10- Proposing the needs of the branch and submitting them to the Unit Council.

11- Discussing and approving the semi-annual report prepared by the Director on the academic, administrative and financial affairs in the branch and submitting it to the Unit Council.

12- Studying the proposals of the departments and their projects, following up the educational work in the departments and taking recommendations regarding them. Reviewing and approving the examination results of the branch before submitting them to the Unit Council.

A new chapter shall be added to Law No. 75 dated 26/12/1967, which is Chapter Eleven: Academic Departments, as follows:

Chapter Eleven: Academic Departments

Article Eighty: Organisation and Administration of the Department:

A- The branches of university units shall be composed of academic departments.

B- The department shall be administered by a head and a department council composed of six members elected from all the academic ranks present in the department. Where the number of members of the teaching staff in the department is ten or fewer, the department council shall be composed of a head and three members elected from all the academic ranks available in the department.
