C- Departments shall be established by a decision of the University Council, upon the proposal of the unit council based on the proposal of the branch councils in the unit, where both exist.

D- The department shall include the members of the teaching staff who teach its subjects.

A group of subjects that constitute a single specialisation, or closely related specialisations, shall be deemed a department.

Article Eighty-One: The head and the council of the department shall take charge of the academic and educational affairs of the department.

A- The head shall take charge of:

1- Representing the department on the council of the branch, or of the faculty if it has no branches.

2- Preparing the agenda of the department council, chairing its meetings and following up on its recommendations.

3- Submitting a termly report to the branch council, after discussing it in the department council, on the conditions of the department.

4- Submitting an annual report, after discussing it in the department, on the needs of the teaching staff, the technical, administrative and academic works, and all other material requirements for improving academic performance.

5- Convening the regular and extraordinary meetings of the department and of the department council.

B- The dean or the director may convene the department to meet whenever the need arises to deliberate on the academic affairs of the department.

C- The term of office of the head of the department and of the department council shall be two years, renewable once.

In the event of the absence of the head of the department, the highest-ranking member of the department council shall deputise for him, and in the event of equality of rank, the highest in grade.

If the post of head of the department becomes vacant for any reason whatsoever more than three months prior to the expiry of his term, the highest-ranking member of the department council, and in the event of equality of ranks, the highest in grade, shall deputise for him until new elections are held.

Article Eighty-Two: On the Functions of the Department Council:

1- Proposing the distribution of subjects and courses among the members of the teaching staff according to specialisation and teaching experience.

2- Proposing the programmes of annual activities.

3- Determining the educational affairs in the department.

4- Determining the needs of the department for members of the teaching staff.

5- Recommending the formation of examination committees.

6- Participating in the amendment of curricula and programmes relating to the department.

7- Nominating those who have fulfilled the conditions for supervising postgraduate studies in the department.

8- Proposing the scientific content of the teaching subjects in the department, the coordination among them, the means of developing them, and the systems of study and examinations therein.

9- Determining the needs of the department and submitting them to the branch council.

Upon the expiry of the term of office of any of the members of the academic councils provided for in this Law, they shall continue to exercise their functions until their replacements are appointed or elected.

Article nine of Legislative Decree No. 122 dated 30/6/1977 concerning the amendment of certain provisions of the Law of the Lebanese University is hereby repealed, and all general and special texts in Law No. 75 dated 26/12/1967 and its amendments that are contrary to this Law or inconsistent with its content are also hereby repealed.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

A new chapter shall be added to Law No. 75 dated 26/12/1967, which is Chapter Twelve: Rules of Candidacy and Elections, in the following form:

Chapter Twelve: Rules of Candidacy and Elections

Article Eighty-Three: On Candidacy:

1- For the representatives of the members of the teaching staff in a single branch: The candidate must be:

a- On the permanent cadre of the Lebanese University or a full-time faculty member in one of its faculties and institutes; in the absence of permanent cadre or full-time faculty members, one of the hourly contracted instructors may be elected provided that his teaching load is not less than 200 hours and at least five years have elapsed since he has been teaching.

b- In possession of the general specialisation of the branch or unit for which he is running as a candidate.

c- And in the event that he teaches in more than one branch or unit, he must have the highest teaching load, and in the event that the teaching load is equal, he shall run as a candidate for the unit or branch closest to his specialisation in accordance with his degree.

2- For the heads of the academic departments: The candidate for the headship of the department must be:

a- On the permanent cadre of the Lebanese University or a full-time faculty member in one of its faculties from the two highest ranks in the department who has spent at least ten years in university teaching; in the absence of full-time faculty members in the specialisation, one of the hourly contracted instructors from the parallel categories, namely the first or second category, may be elected, with a teaching load of not less than 200 hours and where at least ten years have elapsed since he has been teaching.

b- In possession of one of the main specialisations of the department. c- And in the event that he teaches in more than one branch or unit, his candidacy must be where he has the highest teaching load, and in the event that his teaching load is equal with another department, he shall run as a candidate in the unit or branch closest to his specialisation in accordance with his degree.

3- For the members of the councils of the academic departments: The candidate for membership of the council of the academic department must:

Be:

a- On the permanent cadre of the Lebanese University or a full-time faculty member in one of its faculties, who has spent at least five years in university teaching; in the absence of full-time faculty members in the specialisation, one of the hourly contracted instructors from the parallel categories, namely the first or second category, may be elected, with a teaching load of not less than 200 hours and where at least five years have elapsed since he has been teaching.

b- In possession of one of the main specialisations in the department. c- And in the event that he teaches in more than one branch or unit, his candidacy must be where he has the highest teaching load, and in the event that his teaching load is equal with another department, in the unit or branch closest to his specialisation in accordance with his degree.

4- In the event that there are special cases in certain faculties, these cases shall be referred to the University Council to decide thereon, upon the recommendation of the Unit Council.

Article Eighty-Four: On Election

a- Professors on the permanent cadre and in full-time service shall have the right to vote; as for hourly contracted instructors, the teaching load must not be less than 200 hours.

b- The contracted full-time faculty member or the member on the permanent cadre must have the general specialisation and the highest teaching load in the unit, branch, or department, and in the event that the teaching load is equal, he shall vote in the unit, branch, or department closest to his specialisation in accordance with his degree, and in the event that he teaches in more than one branch or unit, he must have the highest teaching load.

- The candidate who has obtained the greatest number of votes shall be deemed the winner, and in the event of a tie, the highest in rank, then the highest in grade, then the oldest in age.

- The results of the elections may be challenged before the University Council within three days from the date of their announcement, and the objection shall be decided within a period of ten days from the date of its submission.

The decision of the University Council may be challenged in accordance with the provisions of Article 63 of the Statute of the State Council.

- The elections of the Unit Council and the councils of the branches shall be held upon a call by the Dean and under his supervision.

- A copy of the results shall be notified to the Presidency of the University. Article Eighty-Five: On the Rules of Student Representation Students shall be delegated to the University Council, to the Unit Council, or to the Branch Council by their union in accordance with its own bylaws, provided that they are students of the second year or its equivalent and above.

Article Eighty-Six: The rights and duties of students in the councils of the unit and the branch, in terms of attendance, voting, and otherwise, shall be subject to the provisions set forth in Legislative Decree No. /115/ dated 30 June 1977, which determined the rules of student participation in the administration of the Lebanese University.

- The proposed New Traffic Law, as amended by the Joint Parliamentary Committees and the Chamber of Deputies, is hereby ratified.

- This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The regulation of traffic, the use of public roads, driver training, driving examinations, roadworthiness requirements for vehicles, and public safety shall be subject to the provisions of this Law, the schedules and annexes attached hereto, and the Lebanese Charter of Pedestrians' Rights.

1- Pedestrians are prohibited from walking or stopping on bridges and in tunnels except in the event of an emergency incident.

2- Pedestrians are prohibited from using pavements or the carriageway for the purpose of boarding motor vehicles within a distance of twenty-five metres from roundabouts, intersections, bends, crests of hills and traffic lights.

Pedestrians walking in organised groups shall use at night a white or yellow light in front and a red light from behind which can be clearly seen at a distance of one hundred and fifty metres during clear visibility.

The provisions of this Chapter shall not apply to formations of the armed forces, to pedestrian processions marching in an organised manner or funeral processions, and to members of the public force while performing their duties.

However, these formations and processions must keep to the side of the carriageway so as to leave the other side thereof as free as possible for the passage of at least one vehicle.

And if they are composed of several detachments, they shall leave between one detachment and another a space sufficient for vehicles to pass each other.
Persons who work at night on roads shall wear light-reflective vests to avoid being exposed to collision accidents.
Every vehicle must have a driver holding a valid driving licence.

The driver of a vehicle, in the case of normal traffic, shall keep to the right lane of the carriageway and he shall keep to the extreme edge thereof in the following cases:

1- When another road user approaches him from the opposite direction.

2- When another road user wishes to overtake him.

3- When visibility of the road ahead is insufficient.

4- When he is compelled to drive his vehicle for a temporary period below the speed applicable on the road, and in this case he shall use warning lights so that other road users are not surprised by him.

And in all cases, drivers of public transport vehicles, trucks whose gross weight is 7,5 tonnes and above, and vehicles transporting hazardous materials shall keep to the right lane of the carriageway.

1- The following shall be deemed equivalent to pedestrians:

a- Persons who push or pull a baby carriage, an invalid's or disabled person's chair, or any other small carriage without a motor.

b- Persons who wheel a bicycle or a motorised cycle by hand.

2- It is prohibited to use pavements in a manner that obstructs the movement of pedestrians. Persons with special needs who move about in a special carriage travelling at walking pace may use the pavements or the sides of the road, and in such case they shall be deemed pedestrians.

3- Where a section of the road is designated for a specific category of road users, that category shall be bound to keep to it and the remaining categories shall avoid it.

Pedestrians shall use the pavements, crossings, bridges or tunnels designated for them, and in the absence thereof, they shall not cross or step onto the carriageway except after ascertaining that they are able to do so without any danger, and where such exist, they shall have priority of passage in the absence of a traffic light or a security officer directing traffic.

1- Pedestrians are permitted to move about on other parts of the road, provided that they take measures of caution and prudence, when it is impossible for them to use the places designated for them or in the absence thereof.

2- Pedestrians crossing the carriageway shall use the crossings designated for them where such exist within a distance of one hundred and fifty metres, and they shall take into account visibility, the distance separating them from the vehicle and the extent of its speed.

3- Where traffic lights exist, pedestrians shall cross the carriageway on the pedestrian crossing when the signal designated for them is illuminated.

4- Where a member of the Internal Security Forces or the Municipal Police is regulating the crossing of the carriageway, pedestrians shall comply with his signal.

5- Pedestrians shall cross the carriageway at a right angle.

6- Pedestrians shall cross the carriageway of an intersection, roundabout or square on the crossing designated for that purpose, and in the absence of a crossing, they shall go around the intersection, roundabout or square and cross the roads surrounding it by crossing the necessary number of roads.

Pedestrians walking on the carriageway shall keep to the left edge of the road, in the direction of their movement, and they shall move to the furthest edge nearest to them upon hearing the warning of any vehicle or animals approaching them, as well as on bends, road junctions and the crests of gradients and when approaching such locations, and in general in every place where visibility is insufficient.

The following terms, wherever they appear in this Law, shall have the meanings set forth below:

1- Road: Any way open to the movement of pedestrians, animals, and various types of vehicles.

2- Highway (Autostrade): Any road and its appurtenances and all subsidiary constructions and installations attached thereto, such as entrances, exits, monitoring and maintenance centres, etc., entry into and exit from which is prohibited except through the entrances and exits designated for this purpose, and which is designated by a decree declaring public utility or by a decree approving alignment plans.

3- Carriageway: The part of the road prepared for the movement of vehicles.

4- Directional roadway: A side of the carriageway prepared for the movement of vehicles in one direction.

5- Lane: A division of the directional roadway whose width allows vehicles to pass in succession and whose sides are clearly delineated. A lane may be designated for the movement of bicycles and may be raised above the road or clearly separated therefrom. It may also be characterised by additional specifications where designated for specific traffic.

6- Sidewalk: A part of the road designated for the movement of pedestrians.

7- Road user or "Beneficiary": Any user of the road, such as pedestrians, drivers of various types of vehicles, and animal drovers.

8- Built-up area: Any group of contiguous or closely spaced buildings standing on one or both sides of the road.

9 - Intersection: Any area where two or more roads meet, or where a road meets a railway section.

10- Roundabout: Any intersection in the centre of which is a circular area around which traffic moves counter-clockwise.

11- Vehicle: Any wheeled means of transport propelled by mechanical or physical power.

12- Motor vehicle: Any vehicle propelled by an engine and prepared for transport or for towing trailers or semi-trailers.

13- Motor car: Any motor vehicle having three or more wheels designed to run on public roads whose unladen weight exceeds /400 kg prepared for the transport of persons or goods, any vehicle prepared for the transport of persons if connected to an electric current and not confined to a rail track, and any motor vehicle not prepared for the transport of persons or goods but equipped with mechanical machinery for special use, with the exception of agricultural and public works vehicles.

14- Agricultural vehicle "Agricultural tractor": A motor vehicle manufactured specifically for towing or operating equipment designated for agricultural exploitation.

15- Self-propelled agricultural machine: A machine capable of moving by its own means, designated for agricultural exploitation.

16- Public works vehicle: A motor vehicle manufactured specifically for a public works project or for towing or operating equipment designated for public works, which is not used for transporting materials and goods on roads, and which may be registered in favour of the public or private sector.

17- Public works equipment: Equipment manufactured specifically for a public works project, which is not used for transporting goods, materials, and persons on roads, and ownership of which may belong to the public or private sector.

18- "Tractor, trailer, and semi-trailer":

a- Trailer: Any trailer for the transport of goods or persons designed and manufactured to be towed by another vehicle operating for the same purpose without any part thereof resting upon the towing vehicle.

b- Semi-trailers: Any means for the transport of goods or persons equipped with one or more rear axles and without a front axle, designed and manufactured to be towed by another vehicle in such a manner that part of its weight rests upon the towing vehicle.

c- Agricultural trailers and semi-trailers: Vehicles hitched to an agricultural tractor used for transporting crops, materials, and equipment necessary for agriculture to or from an agricultural project, and used where necessary for transporting the workers of such project.

d- Public works trailer: Any trailer not prepared for the transport of goods or persons, equipped with one or more axles and towed by a public works vehicle.

e- "Towing vehicle": A motor vehicle designed and equipped to tow a trailer behind it.

f- Tractor unit: A motor vehicle designed and equipped to tow a semi-trailer behind it.

19- Motorcycle: Any motor vehicle having two or three wheels whose unladen weight does not exceed four hundred kilograms.

20- Bicycle: Any vehicle having two, three, or four wheels and not equipped with an engine, which is propelled by the power of its rider.

21- Stopping: Halting for a limited period of time necessitated by traffic requirements, or for setting down or picking up passengers, or for unloading or loading goods.

22- Parking: Remaining stationary in a place for a duration exceeding the period of stopping, or leaving the vehicle without its driver.

23- Paid parking: Remaining stationary in a specified place for a specified time in return for a set fee.

24- Competent Authority: The Traffic, Trucks, and Vehicles Management Authority.

25- Competent Department: The Motor Vehicles and Trucks Registration Department.

26- The Council: The National Road Safety Council.

27- The Committee: The National Road Safety Committee

28- Concessions: Concessions relating to the public interest.

29- Engine power: A traffic rating of a motor vehicle on the basis of which annual road circulation fees are calculated and which is directly linked to the specifications of the engine, and is not the actual power of the engine.

30- Unladen weight: The weight of the motor vehicle when empty, together with the toolkit, spare tyre, and fire extinguisher, with its tanks filled with fuel and fluids, ready for use and operation.

31- Technical gross weight: The maximum weight of the motor vehicle specified by the manufacturing company.

32- Gross weight: The weight of the vehicle or combination of vehicles when empty, plus the weight of the load authorised to be carried therein and recorded on the vehicle circulation permit.

33- Maximum axle weight: Represents the maximum weight limit imposed to ensure the safety of traffic and roads.

34- Payload: The weight of what is carried by the motor vehicle, which is the result of subtracting the unladen weight plus /75 kg/ seventy-five kilograms (the weight of the driver) from the gross weight.

35- Axle: The part of the vehicle that carries on both of its ends the tyres specific to its movement.

36- Technical axle weight: The maximum weight specified by the manufacturer for each axle of the motor vehicle.

37- Axle weight: The maximum weight legally permitted for each axle of the vehicle, which does not exceed the technical axle weight.

38- Axle spacing: The distance existing between two adjacent axles.

39- Tandem axle: An axle composed of two axles closely linked mechanically so as to render them non-independent and thus constituting a single axle.

40- Tridem axle: An axle composed of three adjacent axles closely linked mechanically so as to render them non-independent and thus constituting a single axle.

41- Overall height: The vertical height of the highest point on the vehicle from the surface of the road.

42- Overall width: The actual horizontal transverse distance between the two furthest points on either side of the motor vehicle, excluding mirrors and antennas.

43- Overall length: The length of the vehicle or combination of vehicles between the foremost point at its front and that at its rear.

44- Warning beacon: A device that illuminates with intermittent lights placed on the roof of certain vehicles granted priority in accordance with their special missions.

45- Mobile signal: A signal illuminated with an intermittent light mounted on a metal stand that can be placed on the road, used for warning or for diverting traffic direction to avoid accidents.

46- Speedometer: A device present in a motor vehicle that indicates its speed.

47- Fire extinguisher: An extinguishing cylinder for putting out fires in a motor vehicle.

48- Brake inspection device: A device used to determine the serviceability of the brakes.

49- Load measuring device: A device used to indicate the weight of the load or a device for measuring its volume.

50- Light monitoring device: A device used to determine the intensity of the lights and their suitability for road visibility.

51- Alcohol testing device: A device used to determine the blood alcohol concentration.

52- Pollution testing device: A device used to measure the proportion of substances emitted from the exhaust.

53- Tyre inspection device: A device used to inspect the thickness of the rubber "tread" on tyres.

54- Lamps: That which emits light or illumination.

55- Speed reducers: Structures installed on the carriageway to reduce or limit speed.

56- Reflectors: Plates that reflect lights directed at them, thereby alerting a driver to the presence of a car ahead at night, in the form of triangles and other shapes, affixed to the car at the front, rear, and both sides.

57- "A.T.V. - A T V" vehicle: Any motor vehicle having four wheels which, if its unladen weight exceeds four hundred kilograms, is deemed to be a motor car, or if its unladen weight is less than four hundred kilograms, is deemed to be a motorcycle.

58- Line: A marking of paint or any other material having a specific meaning on the road according to its shape, position, or colour.

59- Barrier: Anything constructed on the carriageway of stone, cement, metal, or any other material that rises above the carriageway to separate traffic directions.

60- Road shoulder: A side passage adjacent to the carriageway used for emergency stopping and for ambulances.

61- Island: Anything constructed on the road that may rise above the level of the carriageway and separates the two directional roadways of the road or the lanes, such as: a central island, etc.

62- Public transport vehicle: Any private or public motor vehicle prepared for the transport of passengers for hire or in return for a fare.

63- Special mechanical inspection: An inspection to verify the conformity of motor cars with the manufacturer's specifications.

It is prohibited for anyone:

1- To cut through the ranks of the armed forces and convoys of all kinds while they are in motion.

2- To cling to the external parts of a vehicle and to board or alight from a vehicle while it is in motion.

3- To use wheeled sports skates on the public road.

4- To stick the head or any body part out of the motor vehicle, with the exception of what is provided for in the second paragraph of Article 67 of this Law, or to sit on its windows while in motion.

5- To wash vehicles or perform any act leading to the leakage of any liquid onto the public road.

6- To repair vehicles on the public road except in cases of extreme necessity after keeping to the far right, using hazard warning lights, and placing a warning triangle in accordance with Article 58 of this Law.

Drivers of vehicles are prohibited from:

1- Driving a vehicle under the influence of alcohol at a concentration exceeding half a gram per litre of blood (0.5 g/l) or 0.25 mg/litre in exhaled breath, provided that this concentration is reduced to zero grams per litre of blood or its equivalent in exhaled breath for drivers who have held their driving licence for less than three years and for drivers of buses, public transport vehicles, trucks weighing more than 7.5 tonnes, and vehicles transporting hazardous materials; or driving under the influence of narcotics; or refusing to submit to a test for the concentration of alcohol or narcotics; or transporting bottles or containers of alcohol not sealed by their manufacturer inside the vehicle.

2- Stopping the engines of their vehicles from running for the purpose of coasting down slopes by the force of their momentum.

3- Driving abreast on a single-lane road except when overtaking.

4- Performing a U-turn manoeuvre in the middle of the public road within built-up areas.

5- Driving in a direction other than the designated direction of traffic.

6- Using any communication devices while driving.

Riders of motorcycles and bicycles and their passengers are prohibited from:

1- Using other vehicles for the purpose of towing or pushing their motorcycles or bicycles.

2- Riding motorcycles, A T V (A. T. V.), or bicycles without wearing a securely fastened protective helmet that protects them from impacts while riding, the specifications of which shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities.

1- If the carriageway is divided into two tracks delimited by continuous lines or dividers, a driver proceeding on either track is prohibited from crossing these lines or dividers or driving upon them.

2- If the carriageway is divided into two tracks delimited by broken yellow lines, the driver must, in the case of normal traffic, use the right-hand track, and must not cross these lines except for the purpose of overtaking in accordance with the provisions of Chapter Three of this Title.

3- If the track is delimited by a broken yellow line adjacent to a continuous yellow line, the two lines may be crossed from the side of the broken line and crossing is prohibited from the side of the continuous line.

4- The driver of a vehicle shall keep to the middle of the lane delimited by continuous or broken longitudinal lines, and is prohibited from driving over or upon these lines.

A driver who prepares to make a significant change in the speed or direction of his vehicle or animals shall ensure beforehand that this can be done without danger and shall warn other road users thereof.

1- Prior to commencing a manoeuvre, or exiting from a building, a property, or a line of parked vehicles, or reversing, or making a lateral movement, the driver shall warn all other road users of the operation he intends to perform, and shall not proceed to execute it until after ensuring that it can be performed without danger threatening the safety of other road users.

2- The driver shall reduce his speed or stop to allow the passage of pedestrians and disabled persons.

3- Upon encountering any hazard to public safety while driving on the road, the driver shall use the hazard warning lights to alert other road users.

4- The driver shall give priority to the passage of school pupils when they are entering or exiting their schools or when school buses are stopped.

Drivers of hire transport vehicles are prohibited from:

1- Slowing down in their travel or stopping suddenly or in other than the side adjacent to the pavement in order to pick up passengers or set them down, except in places where stopping is permitted without causing an obstruction to traffic movement.

2- Demanding fares exceeding the imposed tariff.

3- Eating or smoking whilst transporting passengers.
Bus drivers are prohibited from distracting themselves by talking with anyone, or eating or smoking whilst transporting passengers.

If there stands on a carriageway, a square or a road intersection any building, monument, memorial, traffic island or roundabout that prevents the vehicle from continuing in a straight line, the driver shall go around with his vehicle on the right-hand side, unless there are instructions to the contrary.

1- A driver shall remain, in all cases, alert and in control of his vehicle in a manner enabling him to perform all required operations and manoeuvres. When determining the speed of his vehicle, he shall take into consideration the layout of the roads and their condition, the load of his vehicle, the weather conditions and the density of traffic.

This is so that he is able to stop his vehicle within the range of visibility available to him ahead or before any obstacle that he is likely to encounter. He shall reduce the speed of his vehicle or stop it whenever circumstances so require, and in particular when visibility is poor.

2- A driver is prohibited from causing hindrance to the movement of other vehicles by persisting in driving his vehicle slowly without reason, or by delaying in moving off upon receiving the regulatory signal.

3- The driver of a vehicle travelling behind another vehicle shall leave between his vehicle and the vehicle preceding him a sufficient safety distance to avoid a collision in the event that the driver of the latter proceeds to reduce its speed or stop it suddenly. The safety distance increases in proportion to the increase in the speed of the vehicle and in a manner equivalent to the distance covered by the vehicle during a period of at least two seconds.

4 - Outside cities, the safety distance referred to in the third paragraph for vehicles or a combination of vehicles whose total weight exceeds 7,5 tonnes or whose length exceeds 7 metres, and which are travelling at the same speed, shall be at least 50 metres.

The provisions of this paragraph do not apply to vehicles of the Armed Forces.

5 - The authority having competence over road structures may specify longer safety distances between vehicles in order to reduce the risks to such structures so as to ensure their safety.

1- In the absence of signs specifying the maximum permitted speed on local, main, and secondary roads, all drivers must not exceed the maximum speed as follows:

a- 100 km / h on motorways.

b- 70 km / h outside populated areas.

c- 50 km / h inside populated areas.

2- With regard to unclassified internal roads, the competent local authority may, by a reasoned decision issued by it, reduce the maximum speed limit in populated areas as required by public safety.

3- By a reasoned decision of the Minister of Public Works and Transport, the maximum speed limit may be reduced on certain roads in populated areas or on parts thereof as required by public safety.

4- The maximum speed for trucks, public transport vehicles, vehicles transporting hazardous materials, new drivers for whom three years have not elapsed since receiving their driving licence, and during rainfall or when the road is not dry, shall be determined by a decision issued by the Ministers of Public Works and Transport and of the Interior and Municipalities upon the proposal of the Committee.

5- When visibility is below fifty metres, the maximum speed must be reduced to 50 km per hour on all roads.

Passing between two cars travelling in opposite directions shall take place on the right of the road for each of them, and overtaking shall take place on the left:

1- In the event of passing oncoming traffic, the driver must keep to the right side of the road to the extent permitted by the presence of other road users thereon.

2- Before commencing an overtaking manoeuvre, the driver must ensure that he can return to the lane in which he is travelling, that he can carry out the overtaking without danger, that he has sufficient distance and time for that, and that no driver following him has yet commenced a similar overtaking operation, and he must alert the road user whom he wishes to overtake.

3- During overtaking, the driver must veer sufficiently to the left to avoid disturbing the drivers of the vehicles being overtaken.

In all cases, the lateral distance must not be less than:

a- 75 centimetres from pedestrians, a motorcycle, a bicycle, or animals.

b- 50 centimetres when overtaking other vehicles.

4- In the event of overtaking, a driver may not use the left half of the carriageway unless doing so does not impede those travelling in the opposite direction.

The driver shall reduce the speed of his vehicle whenever circumstances so require, in particular in the following cases:

1- When passing through inhabited areas.

2- Outside inhabited areas:

- At bends, slopes, narrow sections of the road, and road intersections.

- When approaching the crest of an elevation.

- When meeting or overtaking a civilian or military group of pedestrians.

- When meeting or overtaking draught, pack, or riding animals, or livestock.

- When approaching public transport vehicles while persons are boarding or alighting from these vehicles.

- When approaching areas of public works sites on the roads.

- When approaching pedestrian crossings.

- When visibility is unclear due to rain, fog, or other natural factors.

- Near schools and educational institutions.

1- The driver shall not exceed the maximum speed or drive below the minimum speed specified in the regulations in force; exempted from this are drivers of vehicles of the armed forces, fire brigade, and ambulance when performing a mission requiring rapid intervention, as well as any driver of a motor vehicle transporting an injured person in a state of danger.

2- Drivers of vehicles whose maximum speed is below the speed posted on the roads are prohibited from entering these roads or driving on them.

3- The maximum speed for agricultural vehicles and equipment and public works equipment on public roads is set at thirty kilometres per hour.

All drivers are prohibited from obstructing the traffic of other vehicles or causing anything that threatens public safety, in particular:

1- Stopping suddenly without a legitimate reason on the carriageway.

2- Performing dangerous operations, movements, and manoeuvres while driving or causing sounds resulting from the friction of tyres against the road surface.

In the event that the driver causes an obstruction to traffic beyond his control, he shall alert and warn other road users of it in accordance with Article 58 of this Law, and take the necessary measures to remove the causes obstructing traffic movement as quickly as possible.

1- Contrary to the rule set forth in Article 27 of this Law, overtaking on the right of a vehicle is permitted if its driver signals that he intends to turn to the left under the conditions provided for in this Law.

2- Overtaking vehicles running on railway tracks extending on the carriageway shall take place from the right side if the space between these vehicles and the edge of the carriageway is sufficient.

The aforementioned vehicles may be overtaken from the left side:

a- On roads where traffic is one-way.

b- On other roads if the overtaking allows meeting another vehicle in the free part of the carriageway.

1- Overtaking vehicles is prohibited:

a- At unguarded railway crossings.

b- At bends and intersections, unless the driver is travelling on a section of the road on which he has the right of priority.

c- If the vehicle intended to be overtaken is in turn overtaking another vehicle.

d- In the event that a line of motor vehicles has stopped due to traffic obstruction or due to the presence of a signal for it to stop.

e- When approaching pedestrian crossings and speed bumps.

f- In all cases where visibility is insufficient, particularly during rainfall or the presence of fog.

g- When passing through narrow tunnels and on narrow bridges with a single lane for each direction.

h- In all cases where overtaking is prohibited by road signs or markings.

2- If the carriageway is not divided into lanes demarcated by lines, overtaking is prohibited at bends, at the crests of hills, and in general if visibility ahead is insufficient, except on condition that the left half of the carriageway remains free.

3- If the traffic direction is two-way on a carriageway containing two lanes in opposite directions with a shared middle lane, all demarcated by broken lines, the overtaking driver is prohibited from using the lane located to his far left and is permitted to use the middle lane during the overtaking manoeuvre only.

4- The overtaking driver shall immediately return to keeping to his right after ensuring that he can do so without any hazard.

1- Drivers who are about to be overtaken shall immediately keep to the far right of the road without increasing the speed of their vehicles.

2- In cases where the configuration of the carriageway, its condition, or the clear space of its width does not allow passing oncoming traffic or overtaking easily and in complete safety, the drivers of vehicles whose width or the width of whose load exceeds two metres or whose length exceeds seven metres shall, if necessary, stop or pull aside in order to facilitate the passage of smaller vehicles.

3- In the same cases, if a vehicle belonging to the Armed Forces, the Fire Brigade, the Civil Defence, or an ambulance gives warning of its approach, other road users shall pull aside and reduce their speed, and if necessary stop, in order to facilitate the passage of such vehicles.

4- On mountain roads or roads with a steep gradient, where passing oncoming traffic is difficult or impossible, the driver of the descending vehicle shall stop first and pull their vehicle aside to make way for the passage of the ascending vehicle.

5- Where passing oncoming traffic requires reversing, backing up shall be incumbent upon the drivers of:

a- A single vehicle as against a combination of vehicles.

b- A light vehicle as against a heavy vehicle.

c- A truck as against a bus.

d- The descending vehicle if the ascending vehicle is of the same category.

A driver of a vehicle or of animals shall ascertain, when approaching a road intersection, that the carriageway which they intend to cross is clear, and shall proceed at a speed reduced in proportion to the worsening of visibility, and shall give warning, where necessary, of their approach.

1- Rights of way at road intersections vary according to the type of intersection and the signals, signs and markings used in the intersection area:

a- An intersection controlled by traffic lights.

b- An intersection controlled by signs and markings that determine the right of way.

c- An intersection devoid of signals, markings and signs that determine the right of way, where the volume and movement of traffic are usually light.

2- In the event that two drivers coming from two different roads approach a road intersection without signals determining the right of way, the driver must give way to the driver coming from his right.

However, if the intersection consists of three branches, two of which form a straight road, the right of way shall be for traffic on the straight and continuous road, and the driver coming from or entering the branch must give way.

3- A driver coming from a road with ordinary traffic to a road with major traffic must give way to vehicles travelling on the second road.

Roads with major traffic shall be determined:

a- On internal roads: by a decision of the competent municipality.

b- On classified roads: by a decision of the Minister of Public Works and Transport.

When roads are not classified by a decision of the competent authority, they shall all be considered of the same degree of importance, in which case the provisions of paragraph /2/ of this Article shall apply.

In the case of roundabouts:

1- A driver entering the roundabout must give way to vehicles present inside the roundabout.

2- Overtaking vehicles travelling within the roundabout is prohibited.

3- Priority shall be given to the vehicle that begins to leave the roundabout over other vehicles, and the driver must activate the indicator light before leaving the roundabout alongside the road preceding the exit.

4- A driver preparing to enter a roundabout and exit from it at a distance of less than half of it or onto the carriageway opposite him must keep to his right and continue towards the right side of the roundabout.

5- A driver preparing to enter a roundabout and exit from it at a distance exceeding half of it must keep to his left and continue towards the left side of the roundabout.

1- A road user shall, in all cases, comply with the instructions specified by traffic lights and signs placed on the sides of roads and their intersections, or road surface markings.

2- The three colours shall be adopted in the traffic light: red, yellow and green. A driver shall comply with the instructions of the traffic light in accordance with Articles 68 to 71 of this Law.

3- A road user shall not enter a road intersection, even if the traffic light permits him to do so, if the traffic condition will compel him to stop in the middle of the intersection and disturb or obstruct traffic from the other directions.

4- A road user shall be prohibited from stopping in the intersection area, and he shall continue proceeding by taking any of the available and permitted directions in order not to obstruct the movement of traffic in the intersection.

5- A road user shall comply, in all circumstances, with the orders of the security officer assigned to direct traffic in exceptional cases, even if such orders differ from the instructions given by traffic lights and signs, or from the general traffic rules.

1- A driver shall give the right of way to vehicles of the armed forces, fire brigade, civil defence and ambulance that warn of their approach by using the special devices therefor.

2- A driver shall give way to public transport vehicles to enable them to carry out the necessary manoeuvres to pull in towards their designated stops or set off therefrom.

1- Where there is a "Stop" sign at a road intersection, a driver shall come to a complete stop at the boundary of the road on which he is travelling.

He shall also give way to vehicles travelling on another road or other roads, and shall not resume his course except after making sure that this can be done without danger.

2- Where there is a "Slow Down" or "Give Way" sign at a road intersection, a driver shall slow down to give way to vehicles travelling on another road or other roads, and shall not resume his course except after making sure that this can be done without danger.

1- The use of audible warning devices is prohibited except in the following cases:

a- Giving other road users the necessary warnings to avoid the occurrence of accidents.

b- When there is a need to warn other road users of an overtaking manoeuvre outside built-up areas.

2- With the exception of vehicles of the Armed Forces, Civil Defence, Fire Brigade, Red Cross and ambulance institutions, while carrying out missions requiring their rapid intervention and when there are obstacles in front of them, the use of multi-tone horns, sirens and whistles is prohibited.

3- The devices provided for in Paragraph 2 above shall be seized if used, and shall be destroyed three months after the date of drawing up the record under the supervision of the direct authority of those who drew up the record, unless a judicial decision has been issued within the said period returning the confiscated items to their owner.

4- It is required that the warning signal be intermittent, short and of great moderation.

At night, warnings shall be given by means of light signals and audible warning devices shall not be used except in case of extreme necessity.

5- The competent local authorities may restrict the use of audible warning devices within built-up areas, or prohibit them except in cases of imminent danger.

It is prohibited:

1– To stop or leave a vehicle or an animal on the road if doing so constitutes an obstruction or misuse of the road.

2– For a driver to move away from the place where his vehicle is parked without taking the necessary precautions to forestall any accident that may result from his absence.

3– For a passenger of a vehicle to alight from it, board it, or open one of its exits in places where there are signs or road surface markings prohibiting the same. In the absence of such signs or markings, he must alight or board from the right-hand side of his direction of travel.

In the absence of such signs or markings, he may alight or board from the right-hand side of his direction of travel on two-way streets, and from the right-hand or left-hand side on one-way streets. In all cases, the passenger must ascertain beforehand that it is possible to do so without any hazards.

1- A driver who wishes to exit from a place not open to public traffic, or from an unpaved plot of land, or from a roadside parking space, onto a public road, shall yield the right of way to other vehicles, after ascertaining that it is possible to do so without danger and at a very low speed.

2- A driver who prepares to leave the road in order to take another road located to his right, shall keep to the right-hand edge of the carriageway. In all cases, he shall make way and yield the right of way to motor vehicles proceeding on this road, and shall make the necessary turn at a moderate speed, and after ascertaining that it is possible to do so without any danger or inconvenience to others.

3- A driver who prepares to leave the road in order to take another road located to his left, shall move towards the left without crossing the dividing line of the lane in which he is travelling where the carriageway is two-way.

In all cases, he shall make way and yield the right of way to motor vehicles proceeding on this road and shall make the necessary turn at a moderate speed, and after ascertaining that it is possible to do so without any danger or inconvenience to others.

1- Where there is a railway track on the road, whether across or along it, the right of way shall belong to the equipment that normally runs on the track. Every road user shall clear the railway track immediately upon the approach of the said equipment, making way for it to pass.

2- If the railway crossing on the road is not equipped with a barrier or is not subject to guarding, a person using the road shall, upon seeing or hearing the regulatory signal indicating the presence of the crossing, not cross it except after ascertaining the possibility of passing safely and that there is nothing indicating the approach of a train towards it.

3- If the crossing is equipped with barriers, the road user shall not cross the intersection of the road with the railway tracks when its barriers or half-barriers are extended across the width of the road or are in motion.

4- If the crossing is subject to guarding, the road user shall comply with the instructions of the crossing guard, and in all cases, he shall not cross the intersection of the road with the railway tracks except after ascertaining that he can do so without danger.

5- It is prohibited to stop on sections of the road occupied or crossed by railway tracks, and it is also prohibited to leave vehicles or animals standing thereon, or to use the railway tracks to run vehicles foreign to them.

6- Upon approaching the intersection of the road with the railway tracks, the driver shall:

- Reduce his speed.

- Comply with stop signals and signs.

1- A vehicle, or an animal, must be stopped on the road in a manner that does not result in any hindrance to traffic movement, or obstruction of entry into adjacent properties. Such stopping shall take place in the direction of traffic and parallel to the road, save in the presence of markings to the contrary.

2- A vehicle or an animal must in all cases be stopped at the far right edge of the road, so as to leave clear the largest possible portion of the carriageway, unless that side is designated for special traffic or the condition of the right edge of the road does not permit this.

Stopping is prohibited:

1- In places indicated by a no-stopping sign.

2- In places located less than ten metres from stops for vehicles intended for public transport.

3- In places where stopping obstructs the departure of another stopped vehicle.

4- On pedestrian crossings, and at entrances and exits, in particular garages, public parks, places of worship, schools and hospital emergency departments.

5- In front of the entrances of roads leading to official public or private buildings.

6- On pavements intended for pedestrian traffic, on railway tracks and on lanes intended for fast traffic.

7- For any vehicle in a stopping place designated for a category of vehicles other than the category to which it belongs.

8- For vehicles intended for sale or displayed for the purpose of trade, whether new or used, on public roads even in places where stopping is permitted.

9- In places located near fire hydrants and at a distance of less than five metres on each side thereof.

10- In places designated for the stopping of vehicles of disabled persons and the passages reserved for them. In places where stopping obstructs the visibility of road signs and electric signals.

Parking and stopping shall be prohibited:

1- In places indicated by a no parking and stopping sign.

2- In dangerous places that threaten public safety.

3- In places where visibility is insufficient.

4- On the crests of hills and on bends, intersections, roundabouts, and traffic lights up to a distance of 25 metres.

5- On and under bridges, inside tunnels, and at the entrances and exits thereof up to a distance of 25 metres, and in places not prepared for that purpose.

6- For buses, in places other than those designated for them to pick up passengers.

7- On stop lines before traffic lights.

8- On broken lines designated for pedestrian crossings at traffic lights.

9- On both sides of the carriageway demarcated by continuous white longitudinal lines.

11- In places where public works are taking place.

- The owners of offending vehicles whose towing requires the use of cranes belonging to the Security Forces, or whomever they commission, shall be subject to a fine double the fines imposed by the law as a fee for the use of the crane, provided that the value of the doubling is allocated to the Reserve Fund of the Internal Security Forces.

Prolonged parking

1- - Prolonged parking, which is the continuous parking of motor vehicles on public roads in one place for a period exceeding fifteen days, shall be prohibited, even if parking in that place is legally permitted.

2- Anyone who violates the provisions of Paragraph One above shall be punished by the penalty for Category Two offences set forth in this Law.

3- If the owner of the motor vehicle is absent or refrains from removing it from the place, the vehicle shall be impounded for a period of two weeks.

4- The details of the implementation of this Article shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities.

The provisions relating to abandoned vehicles and their wreckage are stipulated in Article One of the Public Hygiene Law promulgated by Decree No. 8735 dated 23/8/1974, which reads as follows:

"It is prohibited on public streets and squares, their appurtenances, sides, and channels up to the limits of the legal setback, in watercourses and on their banks, on maritime public domain and the communal lands of villages, and on the private property of the State and the municipality, to dump building rubble, excavation soil, stones, and the like, waste, agricultural and industrial refuse, and to dump abandoned vehicles and cars struck off by the Car Registration Department, as well as their wreckage, chassis, and parts."
Anyone who violates the provisions of this Article set forth above shall be punished by the penalties stipulated in the Public Hygiene Law promulgated by Decree No. 8735 dated 23/8/1974.
All drivers shall use direction indicator lights a sufficient distance before every swerving or turning manoeuvre of the vehicle.
Drivers of agricultural vehicles, public works vehicles, and towing vehicles shall use dipped-beam headlights permanently.

Any person is prohibited from:

1- Throwing or leaving on the public road anything that may obstruct traffic movement or cause hazards threatening public safety, such as waste, soil, stones, building materials, and other items.

Should a person be compelled to do so, he must remove them immediately, and if that is not possible, he shall place signs indicating the hazard resulting therefrom until their removal as soon as possible.

2- Placing on the public road or hanging above it papers or objects by way of publicity and publication.

3- Throwing waste, food remnants, and the like from vehicles onto public roads and their sides.

Any person is prohibited from causing damage to the public road by any means whatsoever or excavating a road for any reason without prior authorisation from the competent authority.

In applying this Article, due regard shall be given to the provisions relating to works on public roads stipulated in Articles 595, 599 and 600 of the Penal Code.

Those carrying out work sites on public roads shall take the necessary safety measures to warn and protect road users.

The details of application of this Article shall be determined by a decision issued by the Ministers of Interior and Municipalities and of Public Works and Transport upon the proposal of the Committee.
Road users, except in cases of force majeure, shall restrict their movement to the passages, lanes, and pavements designated for the movement of the category to which they belong.

With the exception of vehicles and machinery belonging to the Armed Forces, the use of motorways is prohibited for the following categories:

1- Pedestrians and persons with special needs.

2- Animals.

3- Vehicles not mechanically drawn.

4- Vehicles whose speed does not exceed 60 km/h.

5- Tractors, agricultural vehicles, public works vehicles, and industrial vehicles.

1- A driver must, at night, and by day where necessary, particularly in time of fog or heavy rainfall or snow or when passing through a tunnel:

a- Switch on the main-beam headlights or the dipped-beam headlights.

b- Switch on the side marker lights if the vehicle is equipped therewith in accordance with the provisions of Article 109 of this Law.

2- A driver shall use the dipped-beam headlights in all circumstances that require doing so in order to avoid dazzling the eyes of other drivers, and particularly:

a- When meeting oncoming traffic.

b- When driving behind another vehicle at a short distance.

3- The use of main-beam headlights is prohibited:

a- When meeting oncoming traffic.

b- In built-up areas when public lighting is sufficient.

c- Outside built-up areas when public lighting is continuous in a manner that allows the driver to see to a sufficient distance.

d- When the vehicle is stationary.

1- At night, and by day where necessary, particularly in time of fog, every vehicle standing on a road not equipped with public lighting or equipped with insufficient public lighting must be indicated, subject to the application of the special provisions referred to in Titles Five, Six, Seven and Eight of this Law, either by the front and rear position lights or by the parking lights.

2- If the length of the vehicle or a combination of vehicles exceeds six metres, or if its width exceeds two metres, it must be indicated, while standing, by the front, rear and side position lights.

3- If, as a result of force majeure, it is impossible to stop the vehicle within the conditions set out in Articles 41 to 43, or in the event that the load of the vehicle or part thereof falls onto the road, the driver must, particularly at night, take all necessary measures to indicate the existing obstacles, including activating the hazard warning lights and placing the warning triangle in accordance with Article 58 of this Law.

1- It is prohibited to equip vehicles, with the exception of vehicles that may be used for special transport and for which special regulations are established, with lighting or signalling devices other than those set out in this Law.

2- These provisions do not cover interior lighting devices in the vehicle, provided that such devices do not inconvenience other drivers.

3- Drivers of vehicles are prohibited from using any illuminated or light-reflecting sign intended for advertising without obtaining a special permit to that effect from the competent authority, provided that the use thereof does not cause annoyance to road users.
A driver must permanently ensure the soundness of the brake lights and the reversing lights.

In the event that a vehicle stops for an emergency reason beyond the driver's control, he must do everything within his power to remove the vehicle from the carriageway onto the road shoulder designated for emergency parking where one exists, and if he is unable to do so, he must use the hazard warning lights and place the warning triangle in front of or behind the vehicle, depending on the direction of traffic, at a distance of thirty metres on ordinary roads and fifty metres on motorways so that the triangle can be clearly seen by day and by night.

The hazard warning lights may be turned off after placing the warning triangle if visibility is sufficient. Where it is not possible to observe the distance of thirty metres within built-up areas, the triangle may be placed at a lesser distance, provided that it exceeds ten metres.

The driver may, in addition thereto, use other warning means, such as placing a yellow hand lamp.

All drivers are prohibited from performing the following operations on roads, particularly motorways:

1- Using the central reservation between the two carriageways, particularly for stopping, parking or making a U-turn.

2- Reversing.

3- Driving on the road shoulder.

Parking or stopping on the carriageway and particularly on the road shoulder, except in cases of extreme necessity.

Where there is a sign on a motorway indicating a diversion or a direction towards another road, all drivers who wish to exit must, immediately upon seeing this sign, gradually move over towards:

1- The right or the left direction according to the direction of the diversion they wish to take.

2- A lane or one of the traffic lanes leading to the other road they wish to take at the junction, and the manoeuvre must be completed before passing the signs placed at the beginning of the slip road or the junction.

1- It is prohibited to transport children who have not reached the age of ten years in the front seats of vehicles.

2- It is prohibited to transport children under the age of five years without placing them properly in the safety seat designated for them in the rear seat and fastening them with the belt fitted inside this seat.

The details of the application of this paragraph shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities upon a proposal by the Committee.

3- The use of the seat belt is mandatory for all occupants of the front and rear seats in all types of vehicles equipped with such belts by the manufacturer, with the exception of members of the armed forces when carrying out security missions.

1- Manual signals of police officers

a- Road users shall comply immediately with the signals of police officers assigned to regulate traffic.

b- The signals of police officers assigned to regulate traffic relating to stopping at intersections are as follows:

- A hand raised vertically: this signal means "Caution - Stop" for all road users, except vehicles unable to stop in a safe manner and road users located within the intersection area.

- A hand or both hands extended horizontally: this signal means "Stop" for all road users coming from directions that intersect with the directions of the extended hand or hands, whether located opposite the police officer or behind him.

After making this signal, the police officer assigned to regulate traffic may lower the hand or hands, while the stopping status continues.

- A red light used to signal, which means stop for all road users coming towards the red light.

c- The signals of police officers assigned to regulate traffic prevail in exceptional cases over all other rules of light signals, signs, road markings or others.

2- Manual signals of the driver In addition to the direction-change signal, and in emergency cases for the purpose of alerting road users, the driver may inform them of the action he will take by using his left arm through the left window of the vehicle and perform the necessary signals as follows:

a- Lowering and raising the arm alongside the vehicle means reducing speed and stopping

b- Extending the arm straight horizontally means turning to the left

c- Raising the arm vertically means turning to the right.
Light signals are divided into signals dedicated to vehicles and signals dedicated to pedestrians.

It shall be prohibited for motor vehicles to circulate without doors or without a bonnet for the engine compartment, or with the doors or bonnet open, or without mudguards (fenders) for the wheels, and it shall also be prohibited for freight motor vehicles to leave the rear door of their body hanging down.

It shall be permitted to transport the suitcases and luggage of passengers on a rack fixed to the roof of buses and passenger motor vehicles provided that their height does not exceed one metre and that it does not extend beyond, in any case whatsoever, the outer surface of the motor vehicle, in addition to the necessity of tying this load securely and properly so as to ensure the requirements of public safety.

The form of the signals, signs and markings that must be used to inform the public of traffic measures and set forth in an annex to this Law, are those adopted in the International Convention concluded in Vienna in the year 1968 or any other international convention ratified or to be ratified by Lebanon.

The forms of the additional and local signals, signs and markings set forth in the aforementioned Convention shall be determined by a decision of the Ministers of Interior and Municipalities and of Public Works and Transport.

1- At the entrances and exits of bridges and tunnels, special signs and signals shall be placed announcing the instructions that must be followed to preserve them or to ensure the safety of traffic.

2- Road users must comply with the special signals and instructions placed at the entrances and exits of bridges and tunnels to preserve them or to ensure the safety of traffic.
It shall be prohibited for anyone whomsoever to inflict any damage upon traffic signs and signals or to affix advertisements or notices thereon or to alter their features, positions or directions.

Signals, signs and road surface markings shall consist of four types:

1- Manual traffic signals.

2- Light signals.

3- Signs.

4- Road surface markings.

1- Traffic light signals relating to vehicles shall consist of a system of three circular colours in the following order:

a- The red light: means that vehicles are prohibited from crossing the stop line. In the absence of a stop line, the red light means refraining from passing the traffic light signal itself or refraining from entering the intersection.

b- The steady yellow light: is used when the signal changes from the green light to the red light to warn drivers of the necessity of slowing down in preparation for stopping when the red colour is illuminated, and moving vehicles are permitted to continue proceeding if they have entered the stop line at the intersection or have advanced into the intersection in the absence of a stop line.

c- The green light: means permission to pass while exercising caution.

2- The red light, the steady yellow light and the green light may be equipped with one or more arrows of a red, yellow or green colour. These arrows shall have the same meaning as the ordinary traffic light signals, except that the prohibition or permission shall be restricted to the traffic directions indicated by the arrows.

3- Crossing the red signal is permitted for vehicles heading right, provided that they stop at the signal and then ensure crossing without exposing pedestrians and other traffic movements to any danger or inconvenience, and provided that there is no sign prohibiting the same.

Warning Signs:

They are signs for warning of hazards on the road that impose upon road users special attention and a reduction of speed in a manner commensurate with the type of hazard indicated within the sign (such as dangerous curves, steep gradients, the risk of skidding, and rockfalls,.. etc.).

These signs shall be in the shape of an equilateral triangle with a horizontal base and its apex pointing upwards.

The background shall be of a reflective white colour, the outer border in reflective red colour, and the drawings, figures and symbols in black colour.

(From Sign 1 to Sign 26 of the Traffic Signs Annex)

1- Traffic lights specific to pedestrian traffic shall be of two colours, red and green, and shall mean the following:

a- The red light means that pedestrians are prohibited from crossing the carriageway.

b- The green light means that crossing the carriageway in the crossing designated for pedestrians is permitted with caution.

Provided that these lights are accompanied by symbols indicating stopping or walking for pedestrians.

2- Traffic lights consisting of a two-colour system may be used in certain crossing cases as follows:

a- The red light in the shape of an X mark (×): a prohibited direction on the carriageway or lane with respect to the driver towards whom the light is directed.

b- The green light in the shape of an arrow pointing downwards: and it means a permitted direction on the carriageway and lane with respect to the driver towards whom the light is directed.

3- The flashing yellow light shall be used to permit passing the signal after slowing down and redoubling attention without changing the rules of priority. The use of the flashing yellow light may relate to the following:

a- A light placed singly or two lights operating alternately.

b- A light belonging to a three-colour traffic light system if the system is not working.

4- The flashing red light belonging to a three-colour traffic light system means that entering the intersection is prohibited except after stopping and redoubling attention before proceeding, without changing the rules of priority.

5- In the event of the presence of a traffic light at an intersection operating intermittently between the red light and the yellow light, the driver towards whom the flashing red light is directed shall come to a complete stop and ascertain the possibility of his entering the intersection safely before proceeding on his way, and the driver towards whom the flashing yellow light is directed shall slow down to ascertain that the intersection is clear of vehicles before proceeding on his way.

6- A system consisting of two flashing red lights operating alternately and placed at intersections of roads with railways shall be used, and it means a prohibition on passing the stop line, or in the event of the absence of this line, that entering the intersection is prohibited with respect to all road users.
In the event of the presence of an unlit traffic light, and the absence of signs and markings, right of way shall be determined in accordance with Article 32 of this Law.

Traffic signs placed alongside roads are divided into three types:

1- Warning signs.

2- Regulatory signs.

3- Informative signs.

Regulatory signs:

They aim to provide road users with certain rules specific to regulating traffic movement, and they are divided into five categories:

1- Intersection and priority signs (from sign 27 to sign 33 of the Traffic Signs Annex)

a- The stop sign, which is in the shape of a regular hexagon with a red background and a white border, and on which the words "قف" and " STOP" are written.

b- The slow down (give way) sign, which is in the shape of an equilateral triangle with its horizontal base at the top and its apex at the bottom, with a white background and a red outer border.

c- The roundabout sign and intersection signs, which are in the shape of an equilateral triangle with a horizontal base and its apex at the top, with a reflective white background and a reflective red outer border, and bearing symbols and terms in black.

d- Priority signs are in the shape of a square of sides of a reflective white colour containing inside it another square of a reflective yellow colour and bearing symbols and terms in black.

2- Prohibition signs:

a- Prohibition signs, which aim to alert drivers to manoeuvres that are prohibited to be performed (such as no entry, no overtaking, no U-turn, and others). They are circular in shape with a white background and a red outer border, and bearing symbols and terms in black and red. (From sign 34 to sign 60 of the Traffic Signs Annex).

b- No parking and no stopping signs:

No parking and no stopping signs are circular in shape with a blue background and a red outer border, and bearing symbols and terms in red. (From sign 61 to sign 63 of the Traffic Signs Annex).

3- Mandatory (compulsory) signs:

Mandatory signs aim to direct drivers to perform mandatory manoeuvres or to comply with specific rules. They are circular in shape with a blue background, and bearing white symbols and arrows. (From sign 64 to sign 79 of the Traffic Signs Annex)

4- End of prohibition signs:

"End of prohibition" signs, which are circular with a white background, without an outer border, and bearing black or dark grey parallel lines running diagonally from right to left. (From sign 80 to sign 84 of the Traffic Signs Annex)

5- End of mandatory signs:

End of mandatory signs are circular with a blue background and an outer border, and bearing a set of symbols and terms in white and parallel red lines running diagonally from right to left. (From sign 85 to sign 90 of the Traffic Signs Annex).

Informative signs and alert markers:

1- Informative signs, which are divided into:

a- Information and service signs, which aim to give road users certain instructions and directions, and signs indicating facilities and services (such as car parks, hospitals and otherwise), and they shall be in the following form:

- Information signs, which are square or rectangular with a blue background with symbols and inscriptions in white or red colour.

(From sign 91 to sign 110 of the Traffic Signs Annex).

- Service signs, which are square or rectangular with a white background with a blue border and symbols and inscriptions in black or white colour.

(From sign 111 to sign 125 of the Traffic Signs Annex).

b- Signs indicating destination (direction), which are rectangular, square or in the form of arrows with a green-coloured background to indicate motorways, or blue to indicate roads, or white for guidance inside cities, or brown for tourist or cultural places, or yellow for roadworks, with inscriptions and symbols in white colour, with the exception of white and yellow signs, on which the inscription shall be in black colour, and which help road users reach their destination.

(From sign 126 to sign 135 of the Traffic Signs Annex).

2 - Alert markers:

These markers are used to alert road users at certain locations such as sharp or dangerous bends (curves), intersections or central islands. (From sign 136 to sign 141 of the Traffic Signs Annex).

These markers consist of:

a- Markers in the form of white-coloured cylindrical posts fixed at the outer edge of the road on dangerous bends with a reflective red "band" or "collar" and also fixed at intersections, and which have a reflective red cap higher than the snow level on roads located in areas where snow accumulates.

b- Markers in the form of white-coloured cylindrical posts with a reflective black rectangle, fixed on both sides of the road to delineate its outer boundaries.

c- Rectangular signs with a blue background bearing reflective white arrows, to alert of dangerous bends, fixed at the outer edge of the road facing the driver.

d- Markers in the form of semi-cylindrical posts of reflective yellow colour, to delineate the heads of central islands.

1- It shall not be permissible to hold any race of whatever kind, on public roads, except after obtaining a special licence from the Minister of Interior and Municipalities specifying the conditions that must be complied with.

2- It shall be required, in all cases, in automobile and motorcycle races, to produce an insurance contract against damages that may be caused to third parties and to their property.

3- The organisers of speed races shall be required to secure sufficient protection for the public attending to watch them, in accordance with standards determined by the Council.

The vehicle must be designed and manufactured in accordance with the requirements of the standards of the art and industry, and all of its parts must be sturdy, sound and completely fastened, and the vehicle must always be in a condition fit for use and circulation and fulfil the conditions of safety and durability prescribed in this Law so as not to expose to danger its driver, its passenger or road users or cause damage to roads or to public or private property.

The body or structure of the vehicle must be in good condition and firmly fastened to the chassis, and the vehicle must be manufactured in a manner that secures for its driver a sufficient field of vision in all directions so that he is able to drive in complete security and safety, and the doors and windows must be sound, easy to use and tight when closed, and the seats must be sound and comfortable and their dimensions must conform to the customary standard.

Furthermore, the glass of the vehicle must be of the safety type that does not cause wounds if shattered, and must be of a transparent material that does not obstruct vision from the inside and the outside.

The body of the vehicle must be painted with paint in accordance with the manufacturer's specifications.

The vehicle must be equipped with:

1- A rear-view mirror, by means of which the driver is able to see vehicles and objects approaching from behind, and two side rear-view mirrors located on the outside of the vehicle to the right and left of the driver.

2- An automatic windscreen wiper on the front glass that is in a sound condition.

3- Seat belts in the front and rear seats.

4- A first-aid kit for passenger transport cars for hire.

Its specifications shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities.

5- A fire extinguisher for extinguishing fires when necessary, which shall always be fit for use.

Its specifications shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities.

Road surface markings are divided into continuous or broken longitudinal lines and transverse lines:

1- Yellow longitudinal lines: They separate the two tracks of the carriageway, and are located on the left of the driver to indicate the presence of traffic on his left in the opposite direction.

2- White longitudinal lines: They separate traffic lanes of the same direction.

3- Continuous longitudinal lines: It is prohibited to cross them into the adjacent track or lane.

4- Broken longitudinal lines: It is permitted to cross them when overtaking or for the purpose of moving into the adjacent lane or track.

5- Transverse lines: They indicate the place where the driver must stop in compliance with traffic lights and signs in order to give way to pedestrians and vehicles that have priority of passage.

Road surface markings include a set of supplementary drawings, the most important of which are:

- Deflection (merging) arrows.

- Direction arrows.

- Pedestrian crossing markings.

1- Deflection arrows are used between broken longitudinal lines, to indicate that these broken lines will become continuous.

Deflection arrows are also used inside a lane to indicate the end of the lane and its merging into the adjacent lane.

Deflection arrows are slightly inclined according to the intended direction.

2- Direction arrows are used in the middle of lanes near road junctions and intersections to indicate to road users the lane that must be adhered to towards the intended direction.

3- Pedestrian crossings are demarcated by white-coloured lines parallel to the axis of the carriageway.

They indicate to road users that they must give way to crossing pedestrians or those who have priority of passage.

Stopping or parking of vehicles on them is prohibited.

1- A specific lane may be designated for the traffic of public transport buses (coaches), in which case they are demarcated by continuous longitudinal lines with special drawings within this lane, and it is not permitted to stop within this lane except at the stations designated for stopping.

2- Other vehicles, with the exception of vehicles of the Armed Forces, Civil Defence and ambulances in emergency cases, may not cross this lane, except at the level of road junctions and intersections or when leaving or entering an adjacent property.

1- It is possible at times to indicate the information contained in road signs by means of road markings through writing in white colour on the surface of the carriageway.

2- Road reflectors, which are metallic or non-metallic plates of different sizes that reflect light, may be used to demarcate the edges of the carriageway or the lane at night.

No additions may be placed on the vehicle, such as reflective tinted glass, reflectors or additional lamps.

Nor may antennas for wireless devices unauthorised by the competent authorities be installed, or any writings or stickers be placed on the body of the vehicle that conflict with the laws, regulations and decisions in force.

1- The vehicle must be equipped with a front bumper and a rear bumper firmly fixed to the chassis in a manner that fulfils their purpose.

A single front crash barrier shall suffice for certain vehicles in accordance with the manufacturer's specifications.

It is prohibited to place any bumper that violates the manufacturer's specifications.
