2- Trucks must comply with the bumper specifications in a manner that limits the potential damage to other vehicles in the event of skidding and collision, conforming to the manufacturer's specifications and having obtained the approval of the competent department.

1- The vehicle base (chassis) must be of such durability and strength as to withstand the pressure exerted upon it by the loads it is designed to bear.

2- No joints or welds may be made in the parts of the vehicle base (chassis), unless this is done with the knowledge, testing and approval of the producing factory, such that these modifications do not affect its balance and durability, in addition to the condition of the approval of the competent department therefor.

1- The design of the engine must be of such strength and durability as is consistent with the design of the vehicle and the purpose of its use when at its maximum weight.

2- The engine must be firmly mounted on its designated mounts, and its hood must be sound and tightly closed.

1- The engine must be in good condition and not emit smoke that pollutes the environment or is harmful to public health or traffic safety, and must not emit emissions exceeding the legally specified specifications as measured by a pollution testing device.

2- The vehicle or its devices may not produce noise that causes disturbance to road users or persons adjacent thereto.

3- It is prohibited to use fuel in the engine other than those legally specified, and it is also prohibited to use types of fuel other than those conforming to the specifications of the vehicle's manufacturer.

1- Engines must be fitted with a permanently serviceable exhaust (silencer), and it is required that this device be constructed in a manner that does not allow the driver, while the engine is running, to interrupt or reduce its effectiveness, and the free discharge of gases is prohibited.

2- The engine exhaust in cars, vehicles and motorcycles must be equipped with baffles that limit the noise of the engine's operation, and in the event that any modification, replacement or repair is carried out on this exhaust, its sound or noise must not exceed the limit produced by it upon its arrival from its original factory.

3- It is prohibited to register cars not equipped with a catalytic converter device (pot catalytique) that are put into circulation for the first time from the date of entry into force of this Law, and this converter must also be inspected at every inspection to verify its effectiveness.

4- The Minister of Interior and Municipalities may specify by a decision issued by him, with regard to electrical equipment, the fitting of an anti-interference device meeting certain technical conditions, and a special device in motorcycles that limits their noise.

Fuel tanks and the pipes connected between the various devices of the circuit must be sound and not allow the slightest leakage of fuel, and the fuel tank opening must be far from the exhaust pipe and covered with a tight cap. It is prohibited for a motor vehicle to break down on the public road due to the depletion of fuel from the tank.

The remaining devices of the vehicle, including without limitation the cooling system, the transmission devices and the electrical network, must all be sound, in good condition, fit to perform their function and capable of withstanding the maximum capacity for which they are designed.

1- The steering device (steering wheel) must be fixed to the left of the motor vehicle, and all its linkages must be sound and in good condition so as to enable the driver to change the direction of the vehicle easily, accurately and without delay.

2- No modification may be made to the specifications of the steering device.

3- The position of the steering wheel may be modified from the right to the left after the prior approval of the competent service and the subjection of the vehicle to mechanical inspection.

4- The importation of vehicles that do not conform to the provisions of this Article is prohibited from the date of entry into force of this Law.
The vehicle must be fitted with a warning device with a clear sound, and it may not be multi-toned.

1- Every motor car, motor vehicle or combination of vehicles must be equipped with at least two brakes, each independent of the other, one of which ensures control in reducing the speed of movement of the vehicle and stopping it completely and rapidly, and the second of which ensures keeping it stationary in a parking position, and which do not affect, when used, the direction of the vehicle or motor car while it is moving in a straight line.

2- The brakes shall be required to have rapid effectiveness and sufficient power to stop, immobilise and hold the vehicle or combination of vehicles in place even on the steepest gradients.

Brakes are of two types:

1- Service brakes (main brake)

a- Their operation shall be either mechanical, by compressed air, by fluid pressure, or by any other means characterised by safety specifications, and their effect must be balanced on all wheels.

If the operation of the brakes is by air pressure or by fluid pressure, all of their devices, including pipes, hoses or the air tank, must be technically sound.

b- The main brake shall be required to have its effectiveness on the wheels, to hold at least two-thirds of the weight of the motor car or motor vehicle when laden, and for its effectiveness on dry or flat ground to reach at least fifty percent on each of the wheels.

2- Parking brakes (reserve brake) Their operation shall be by hand or by foot, they shall be completely independent in their operation, their effect shall be on the wheels or on the drive shaft (transmission), and it must remain mechanically applied during the absence of the driver.
Single trailers shall be exempted from brakes, provided that their authorised gross weight does not exceed 750 kilograms and does not exceed half the weight of the towing vehicle when unladen.

1- The axles must be balanced, properly fitted and fixed in place according to the design of the vehicle manufacturer, and must bear the load placed upon them, and there may not be any welding inside the axles whatsoever.

2- The wheel rim must be made of metal, and its dimensions and load-bearing capacity must conform to the design of the vehicle and its axles without any welding being present in it.

3- The tyres must be made of pneumatic rubber and be in a condition that does not allow the skidding of the vehicle, and their dimensions must conform to the design of the vehicle, its axles and its wheel rims according to the manufacturer's specifications, taking into account the symbols engraved on the sidewall of the tyre which indicate the date of manufacture, speed symbol, load index, rim diameter, tyre structure, aspect ratio of height to width, section width and other dimensions, and they must be tightly secured, and they must also bear the maximum weight of the vehicle.

Taxis, that is, cars for hire that operate on demand, must be equipped with a meter (taximeter) that records the transport fare that the passenger must pay.

A decision issued by the Ministers of Interior and Municipalities and of Public Works and Transport shall determine the specifications of this meter, the conditions for its installation and inspection, and the time limits that must be given to the owners of public passenger cars to equip their cars with the said meter.
All lights with which the vehicle is equipped from the factory must be intact and fit for use.

Driving lights or high beam:

All vehicles must be equipped at the front with two driving lights that project forward a white or yellow light that illuminates the road at night in clear weather over a distance of one hundred metres at least.

Passing lights:

1- All vehicles must be equipped at the front with two passing lights that project forward a white or yellow light that illuminates the road at night in clear weather over a distance of thirty metres at least without dazzling the sight of other drivers.

2- If any point of the projector of the passing light is more than forty centimetres away from the edge of the width of the vehicle, the front position lights must be lit.

Front position lights:

All vehicles must be equipped on both sides of the front with two small lights that project forward a white or yellow light, and these lights must indicate the front width of the vehicle, and be visible from a distance of 150 metres in clear weather at night and without dazzling the sight of other drivers.

Rear position lights:

1- All types of vehicles or trailers attached to them must be equipped at the rear with two lights at least that emit backward a red light, and these lights must indicate the width of the rear of the vehicle, non-dazzling to the sight, visible at night, in clear weather over a distance of one hundred and fifty metres.

2- The lighting of the front position lights, the driving lights, or the passing lights must result in the lighting of the rear position lights.

Side marker lights:

Every motor vehicle or every combination of vehicles whose length exceeds six metres, or whose width, including the load, exceeds two metres, must have both its sides equipped with lights in order to define the projections of the vehicle and its dimensions in length, width and height in accordance with internationally adopted standards, in a manner that allows road users to see it at night and clearly distinguish its size and dimensions, provided that these lights are non-dazzling to the sight.

Rear registration plate illumination device:

1- All vehicles and their attached trailers shall be equipped with a device that illuminates at night, in clear weather, and at a distance of at least twenty metres, the number inscribed on the registration plate placed at the rear.

2- Turning on the front position lamps, the driving beam headlamps, or the passing beam headlamps shall cause the illumination of the device mentioned above.

Stop lamps:

1- All vehicles and their attached trailers shall be equipped with two or three deceleration lamps emitting to the rear a non-dazzling red light that illuminates as soon as the driver begins to apply the service brake.

2- This light shall be stronger than the light emitted by the rear position lamp, when the stop lamps are grouped with the rear position lamps or combined with them, provided that this light remains in all cases non-dazzling.

3- The installation of these lamps on trailers or semi-trailers shall be mandatory even if their dimensions do not conceal from a driver approaching from the rear the stop lamps installed on the towing vehicle.

Direction-indicator signals or indicator lamp:

Every vehicle shall be provided with indicator lamps at the front and rear corners, provided that the flashing indicator light is visible when changing direction to the right and to the left.

Hazard warning lamps:

The vehicle shall be equipped with hazard warning lamps emitting flashing lights produced by all four indicator lamps simultaneously and warning of the occurrence of an emergency.

Parking lamps:

A vehicle may be equipped on both of its sides either with parking lamps emitting orange lights to the front and to the rear, or emitting to the front and to the rear the same lights emitted by the front and rear position lamps.

Reversing lamps:

The vehicle shall be provided with white lamps placed at the rear in accordance with the manufacturer's specifications, to facilitate visibility to the rear, which illuminate as soon as the reversing gear is engaged, provided that their light does not extend beyond ten metres, and that they do not dazzle.

Fog lamps:

Vehicles may be equipped at the front with two fog lamps emitting a yellow or white light and at the rear with one or two fog lamps emitting a red light to the rear.

Steerable lamps:

The use of a searchlight (projector) for the purpose of illuminating the road shall be strictly prohibited, with the exception of vehicles of the Armed Forces, the Fire Brigade, ambulances, and the Civil Defence.

A vehicle must be equipped with at least one spare tyre in a condition ready for use, in addition to a vehicle lifting jack and the equipment required for changing tyres.

Vehicles issued from their factory not equipped with a spare tyre shall be exempted from the provisions of this Article.

1- The tyres of vehicles and of their trailers must be of sufficient elasticity.

2- The outer tyres must be in good condition, and the thickness of the rubber (tread) above the grooves engraved therein must not be less than 1.6 millimetres, in accordance with the specifications of the European Union.

The thickness of the rubber shall be measured by means of a tyre inspection device.

3- The age of the tyres must not exceed six years from the date of their manufacture.

4- It shall not be permissible to use tyres treated by regrooving or otherwise.

It is prohibited to fit metallic parts forming a protrusion on the surface of the tyres that touches the ground, with the exception of metallic chains specially prepared for driving on roads covered with snow.

1- A vehicle must be manufactured in a manner that secures for its driver a sufficient field of vision in all directions, such that he is able to drive it in complete safety.

2- The windscreen must not distort the shape of objects, and in the event of breakage, must not prevent continuing to see the road clearly.

3- The windscreen must be equipped with a mechanical windscreen wiper whose field of operation allows the driver to see the road clearly from his seat.

4- Every motor vehicle whose weight exceeds four hundred kilograms / 400 kg/ must have a reversing mechanism.

5- A motor car must be equipped with a central mirror inside it and at least one rear-view mirror for each side, placed in a manner that allows the driver to see the road at the rear of the vehicle and on both its sides, such that the field of vision does not form a blind spot leading to the concealment of a vehicle preparing to overtake.

1- A vehicle must be equipped with a device indicating speed, which shall always be in working order.

2- Vehicles designated by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities must be equipped with a device for monitoring and recording speed and other traffic safety metrics and standards, which shall always be in working order.

The information shall be retained in the memory of the device for a period of at least one year and shall be placed at the disposal of the competent officers when necessary.

The Minister of Interior and Municipalities shall determine, by a decision issued by him, the specifications of the device and the conditions for its installation and monitoring.

Warning triangle:

Every motor vehicle, with the exception of cycles, shall be equipped with a warning triangle to be used in cases of emergency stopping in accordance with Article 58 of this Law.

Its specifications shall conform to the specifications set out in the International Convention concluded in Vienna in 1968, or any other international convention ratified by Lebanon.

Reflectors:

1- Motor cars and trailers shall be equipped at the rear with two reflectors reflecting a red light to the rear, which shall be triangular in shape for trailers and non-triangular for motor cars.

2- Every motor car and trailer exceeding six metres in length, or motorcycle or bicycle, shall be fitted on both sides with one or two reflectors that are orange in colour and non-triangular in shape.

3- Every motor car shall be fitted at the front with two non-triangular reflectors reflecting a white light to the front.

Transport of trees and pieces of extended length Pursuant to the provisions of Article 139 of this Law, vehicles transporting trees or pieces of extended length that project beyond the rear of the vehicle by more than one metre and do not exceed two metres shall be subject to the following conditions:

1- By day, a bright red flag measuring not less than 40 (multiplied by) 25 centimetres shall be placed at the rear of the load.

2- By night, a lamp emitting a clear, non-dazzling red light shall be placed at the rear of the load.

1- Where there is symmetry or two devices signifying the same thing and capable of being used at the same time, they shall be mounted at the extremities of the vehicle symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, and shall emit or reflect luminous rays of the same colour and the same intensity.

2- The intensity of lights and signals shall not be variable, with the exception of direction-indicator lights.

3- It is prohibited to fit any type of vehicle at the front with lights of any colour other than white or yellow.

1- Owners and drivers of public vehicles and public passenger transport establishments and companies who engage in or wish to engage in public passenger transport on Lebanese territory or between Lebanon and abroad shall obtain a prior licence from the Ministry of Public Works and Transport - Directorate General of Land and Maritime Transport authorising them to carry out such work, pursuant to a decision issued by the Ministers of Public Works and Transport and of the Interior and Municipalities concerning the regulation of the profession of public passenger transport, whereby the conditions required for obtaining such licences are determined in addition to determining the regulatory frameworks governing the process of issuing, renewing and revoking such licences and their practical application.

2- No owner of a public transport vehicle, whether an individual, establishment or company, and no public passenger transport driver may practise public passenger transport without a prior licence from the Ministry of Public Works and Transport - Directorate General of Land and Maritime Transport, in accordance with the mechanism determined in the decision mentioned above.

The Mechanics Department in the competent service shall have the right, where the inaccuracy of the information and documents submitted to it is established, to amend the gross weight, engine power, number of seats or unladen weight, without the party concerned having the right to claim compensation for damages.

1- Vehicles designated for freight shall be authorised to carry two persons beside the driver, provided that such vehicles are designed therefor by the manufacturer of such vehicles.

2- Freight motor vehicles shall be authorised to carry at most three workers in their body, with or without a load, provided that they are equipped with the necessary seats and that the insurance policy covers the workers.

Every motor vehicle, trailer or semi-trailer intended to be put into circulation must be manufactured and equipped in a manner that limits, in the event of a collision, the risks of bodily accidents both to its users and to other road users.

The Ministers of the Interior and Municipalities and of Public Works and Transport shall determine, by a decision issued by them, the conditions that must be met in all types of motor vehicles, vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers, whether with respect to the manufacture of bodies or internal and external dimensions, or for the purpose of ensuring the safety and comfort of passengers and securing the transported load.

1- Taxis In addition to the general conditions referred to above in Chapter One of Part Two, the following conditions must be met in taxis of all kinds:

a- That they have at least four doors, two on each side.

b- That the seats be comfortable and clean. c- That the vehicle be equipped on the inside with electric lighting.

d- That the registration plate numbers and the name and address of the owner of the vehicle be written in the Arabic and French languages on two small plates, one of which is placed clearly on the back of the front seat and the second in front of the passenger in the front seat next to the driver.

e- That the identification sticker be affixed on both of its sides on the outside in accordance with the decision issued by the Ministers of Public Works and Transport and of Interior and Municipalities in this regard.

f- That a sign be placed on the roof of the vehicle bearing the word (Taxi) which is illuminated when it is empty of passengers, and taxis operating on demand shall be exempted from placing this sign.

g- That each taxi be provided with a fire extinguisher that is always fit for use and within the reach of the driver.

No change or modification may be made to the body of the vehicle, the steering apparatus or the seats in a manner contrary to the specifications of the manufacturing company.

2- Buses In addition to the general conditions, the following conditions must be met in buses:

a - That each bus have at least two doors on the right side, provided that buses currently registered contrary to this text shall remain in circulation as long as they are fit for that and in the name of their owner, in accordance with the laws in force.

b- That each bus have a sufficient number of windows and steps that are easy to use and do not protrude from the structure of the bus, and the windows may be provided with curtains.

c- That the seats be fixed to the floor of the bus with legs and in a secure manner.

d- No change or modification may be made to the body of the vehicle, the steering apparatus or the seats in a manner contrary to the specifications of the manufacturing company.

e- That clear signs and instructions be placed inside the buses requesting all passengers not to speak with the driver while he is driving the vehicle in order to ensure the driver's concentration on the task of driving.

f- That these buses be provided with sufficient lighting on the inside.

g- That each bus be provided with sufficient fire extinguishers, not less than two extinguishers, which are always fit for use, provided that one of them is within the reach of the driver.

h- That each bus have a first-aid box containing the necessary materials for first aid.

i- That the identification sticker be affixed on the vehicle in accordance with a decision issued by the Ministers of Public Works and Transport and of Interior and Municipalities in this regard.

3- Any additional conditions relating to safety, security and the general condition in terms of the internal and external appearance may be determined pursuant to a decision issued by the Ministers of Interior and Municipalities and of Public Works and Transport.

Engine power:

1- Subject to the provisions of this Law, the Head of the Mechanics Department at the competent service shall determine the authorised gross weight for every motor vehicle designed for the transport of loads or for the transport of more than eight persons or for towing a trailer or semi-trailer, in relation to the strength of the chassis of the vehicle, its tyres, the power of its engine and its mechanical devices.

He shall also determine the power of the engines of motor vehicles as follows:

- Four-stroke petrol engines. D2 (multiplied by) N (multiplied by) 0.062

- Two-stroke petrol engines D2 (multiplied by) N (multiplied by) 0.062 (multiplied by) 1.06

- Four-stroke gasoil (diesel) engines D2 (multiplied by) N (multiplied by) S (multiplied by) 0.005

- Two-stroke diesel engines D2 (multiplied by) N (multiplied by) S (multiplied by) 0.005 (multiplied by) 1.06

The letters set out in the rules above shall mean the following: D = the diameter of a single cylinder in centimetres N = the number of engine cylinders S = the piston stroke.

2- The power of the engines of motor vehicles not indicated above shall be determined on the basis of the technical specifications determined by the producing manufacturer by adopting the same power as petrol engines of equivalent actual power.

3- A fraction resulting from the multiplication operation in determining engine power shall be considered a whole unit if it exceeds one half.

4- Engine power shall be determined on the basis of the specifications issued by the producing manufacturer or its agent in Lebanon, provided that the accuracy of the submitted information remains their responsibility and they consequently bear all that results from the inaccuracy of this information towards the competent service.

5- In the event that the necessary documents are not available, physical inspection and comparison with other vehicles of similar specifications may be resorted to.

6- If the producing manufacturer of the vehicle is in Lebanon, the manufacturer or its agent present in Lebanon must subject the vehicle to ordinary and special mechanical inspection before putting it into circulation in Lebanon in order to prove its roadworthiness and the validity of its conformity with internationally adopted specifications and standards.

The details of the application of this paragraph shall be determined by a decision issued by the Ministers of Interior and Municipalities and of Industry.

The gross weight shall comprise the unladen weight of the vehicle or combination of vehicles and the weight of the load authorised to be transported therein, and shall be the lesser of the technical gross weight and the maximum gross weight determined in Article 134 of this Law.

1- Subject to the provisions of Article 140 of this Law (exceptional transport), the maximum gross weights of vehicles shall be determined in accordance with Table of Weights No. 1 annexed to this Law.

2 -

a: The permissible weights for trucks of the lowboy/dual-wheeled category for indivisible loads shall be determined in accordance with Table of Weights No. 2-(a) annexed to this Law.

b: The permissible weights for trucks of the lowboy/multi-wheeled category shall be determined in accordance with Table of Weights No. 2-(b) annexed to this Law.

c: If the gross weight of the truck exceeds the five tonnes set out in Table No. 2 annexed to this Law, it shall be required, in order to operate in Lebanon, to obtain a prior permit from the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities.

- The permissible gross weight in Table No. 2 shall be adopted for loads that cannot be divided; otherwise, it may be held accountable according to the permissible weights pursuant to Table No. 1.

3- The maximum gross weight shall be determined on the basis of the specifications provided by the manufacturing factory of the vehicles, provided that the maximum gross weight of any vehicle may not exceed the gross weight prescribed for it in this Law, even if so stated in the manufacturer's statement.

4- The axle and gross weights, dimensions and measurements of vehicles prescribed in this Chapter may be amended in accordance with what is agreed upon under memoranda of understanding or regional or international agreements, by virtue of a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Public Works and Transport and of Interior and Municipalities.

5- The axle and gross weights of vehicles may also be amended, or exceptions thereto may be established, for a specified period required by the public interest, by virtue of a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Public Works and Transport and of Interior and Municipalities.

1- The effective engine power must not be less than (5,5) five and a half horsepower for each tonne of the gross weight of the vehicle.

2- A vehicle towing more than one trailer shall not be permitted to operate.
The weight on the driving axle or driving axles may not be less than 25 % of the weight of the motor vehicle or combination of vehicles when laden.

The unladen weight of a vehicle, or of a combination of vehicles, shall comprise all its constituent elements and equipment as issued by the manufacturing company, and which enable it to operate normally, in addition to the following:

- Coolant fluid.

- Oils.

- Windscreen washer fluid.

- A fuel tank filled to at least 90%.

- One spare wheel.

- A fire extinguisher.

- The lifting jack and the necessary toolkit ordinarily delivered with the car placed in a normal moderate box.

- An ordinary cover if the vehicle is open-topped.

The operations of weighing vehicles when unladen shall be carried out by the centres legally accredited to conduct the periodic mechanical inspection, and the weights issued by them shall be adopted, provided that these weights remain subject to modification or correction if any doubt as to their accuracy becomes apparent to the Mechanics Department.

Motor vehicles arriving from their factories fully equipped, and upon which no modification has been made locally, shall be exempted from weighing operations.

This weight shall be determined by the Head of the Mechanics Department based on the specifications issued by the producing factory.

Subject to the provisions of Articles 134, 137 and 140 of this Law, it shall not be permissible to put into circulation a vehicle whose weight exceeds by twenty percent (20%) the gross weight determined for it and recorded in the circulation permit granted to it.

1- The maximum axle loads on each axle of the vehicle’s axles shall be determined as follows:

A- Steerable axles:

1- Single axle: 7 tonnes.

2- Tandem axles: 6 tonnes for each axle.

B- Non-steerable axles

1- Single axle: 13 tonnes.

2- Dual axle as follows:

- If the distance between axles is less than two metres: 10 tonnes for each axle

- If the distance between axles is not less than two metres

it shall be treated as a single axle: 13 tonnes for each axle.

3- Triple axle: 8 tonnes for each axle.

4- Quadruple axle: 7 tonnes for each axle.

C- Notwithstanding the provisions of item (B) of this Article, the axle loads for a trailer shall be as follows:

1- Single axle: 9 tonnes for each axle.

2- Dual axle: 7.5 tonnes for each axle.

2- Two-axle motor lorries, the maximum gross weight of which is determined at 21 tonnes, shall be exempted from the first paragraph.

1- Subject to the provisions of Article 140 of this Law, the dimensions of a vehicle or combination of vehicles may not exceed the following limits:

- Overall height or elevation above the road surface-- 2,4 m.

With the exception of lorries loaded with containers, which are permitted a maximum height of 4,5 m., provided that this does not conflict with the permitted height specified on the signs at bridge and tunnel sites.

- Length of a single one-axle trailer with towing equipment-- 7.5 m.

- Length of a single two-axle trailer with towing equipment-- 12 m.

- Length of a motor vehicle-- 12 m.

- Length of a tractor and semi-trailer --17.5 m.

- Length of a tractor and trailer-- 18.35 m.

- Horizontal distance between the vertical axis of the semi-trailer and its rear-- 12 m.

- Horizontal distance between the exterior back of the driver's cabin and the rear of the trailer-- 16 m.

- Horizontal distance between the vertical axis of the semi-trailer and any point of its front-- 2.04 m.

2- The distance between the rear axle of the tractor and the front axle of the trailer may not be less than three metres.

3- The dimensions of the vehicles specified in this Article may be amended by a decision issued by the Ministers of Interior and Municipalities, and Public Works and Transport.

1- All necessary precautions shall be taken when loading vehicles, avoiding:

- The falling and scattering of the load

- Restricting the driver's field of vision and freedom of movement while driving

- Disrupting the balance of the vehicle

- Loading in a manner that conceals the vehicle's lighting devices and its registration plates

- Causing noise and din while driving

2- An indivisible load may extend in length beyond the rear of the car and not its front, provided that it does not exceed three-tenths of the length of the vehicle without exceeding the total length prescribed pursuant to this Law, and in all cases two metres.

3- If need or necessity requires that the load extend in width beyond the outer frame, this shall not exceed thirty centimetres on each side and without exceeding the specified total width of 265 cm including all projections of the vehicle, and provided that the load consists of objects that are easy to notice and pay attention to, as it is prohibited in such a case to transport poles and similar objects projecting in width in a manner that makes them difficult to notice.

4- Loads that extend beyond the limits of the car may not exceed by their swaying the maximum limits prescribed pursuant to this Law and shall be securely tied together.

5- It is prohibited to transport loads that may touch the public road even if they are carried on wheels.

6- The height of the vehicle's body or its load from the roadway surface may not exceed six-tenths of the length of its frame (chassis), and in all cases this shall not exceed 4,2 m.

7- The dimensions of the load specified in this Article may be amended by a decision issued by the Ministers of Interior and Municipalities and of Public Works and Transport.

1- Where the need arises to transport or operate indivisible parts, agricultural or public works equipment, or motor vehicles or trailers designed to transport indivisible parts, the dimensions or weights of which exceed the regulatory limits, the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities - Traffic, Trucks and Vehicles Management Authority may, after consulting the Minister of Public Works and Transport, license and supervise the movement thereof for a single journey or for several journeys in accordance with the requirements.

The licence shall specify the roads, weights and times to be adopted, and the measures to be taken to ensure traffic safety and to avoid causing damage to roads, structures and appurtenances of the public domain.

Loads shall be deemed indivisible where dividing them would result in damage to and impairment of the parts or objects transported, or where doing so would compromise the safety of transport.

2- Vehicles and equipment that do not conform to the provisions of Article 138 of this Law shall be permitted to cross public roads, with the exception of motorways, transversely from one side to the other within their areas of operation, after verifying that they do not obstruct traffic or pose a hazard to the roads or to the users thereof.

3- Public works vehicles and their equipment, and agricultural tractors equipped with a trailer, shall be prohibited from travelling on international and main roads and motorways while laden.

However, they shall be permitted to cross such roads transversely from one side to the other after verifying that they do not obstruct traffic or pose a hazard to the roads or to the users thereof.

4- The competent administration may grant the owners of agricultural vehicles with a trailer only an exceptional licence permitting them to travel on a section of main roads while laden with agricultural crops and materials and equipment necessary for agriculture for a distance not exceeding fifteen kilometres, provided that the licence specifies the materials licensed to be transported, the route plan, the times, the points of departure and arrival, and the validity period of the licence, and provided that such transport takes place in all cases within agricultural areas and does not result in any obstruction of traffic or hazard to public safety.

Such a licence may be granted for the transport of a specified number of agricultural workers, provided that the transport does not take place on international roads and inside cities.

The aforementioned agricultural areas shall be defined by a decree adopted upon the proposal of the Ministers of Interior and Municipalities and of Agriculture.

1- A vehicle is permitted to tow a single trailer or semi-trailer, provided that the trailer is of the very same category as the towing vehicle.

2- Passenger cars are prohibited from towing trailers for commercial, industrial or agricultural purposes, with the exception of trailers prepared for excursions, tourism, hunting and the like for personal use.

3- Goods vehicles specially designed to tow trailers are permitted to tow a single trailer designated for transporting loads. Other goods vehicles are also permitted, when necessary, to tow agricultural or public works equipment.

4- Transport buses are prohibited from towing any trailer, whatever the reasons.

5- - Motor vehicles are prohibited from towing behind them another broken-down vehicle by means of towing. With the exception of trucks whose gross weight reaches 7.5 tonnes and above, provided that the weight of the towing truck is not less than that which is being towed.

6- The maximum permissible weight of the trailer is determined by the fraction resulting between the gross weight of the trailer with its full load and the weight of the towing vehicle with its full load which form the combination consisting of a tractor and a trailer. The ratio of this fraction, after rounding it, must not exceed:

a- 1.45 if the combination is equipped with continuous and direct automatic brakes.

b- 0.8 if the combination is not equipped with continuous and direct automatic brakes. As for dual-weight cars (for passenger and transport) or caravan cars, the weight of the trailer must not, in all cases, exceed the unladen weight of the towing car.

c- 0.5 if the trailer is not equipped with brakes.

7- No combination consisting of a towing vehicle or a trailer or a semi-trailer may be put into circulation before completing all legal formalities for it and stamping the chassis number of the tractor on the trailer or semi-trailer.

8- The use of the tractor is permitted to tow any trailer or semi-trailer bearing the chassis number belonging to the tractor which has been stamped by the competent department at the competent service, and independent circulation permits in which the specifications specified in Article 170 of this Law are recorded shall be delivered to the owner of the tractor and the trailer or semi-trailer.

9- Towing equipment must be issued by specialised companies that can be held responsible for its manufacture in terms of bearing the weights and pressures placed upon it without any danger.

10- The lighting and braking devices between the tractor and the trailer must be coordinated and direct with one another.

1- Every motor vehicle must bear a plate known as the /manufacturer's plate/ on which are clearly stated the make of the motor vehicle, its model and the serial number of the model therein, and the manufacturer shall affix this plate to the motor vehicle.

2- In addition to this plate, the serial number of the model must be stamped by the manufacturer on the chassis or body of the motor vehicle.

3- The engine of the motor vehicle must bear a serial number engraved thereon, failing which it shall be stamped by the competent Service.

4- Where the serial number of the model is originally absent (not stamped by the manufacturer on the chassis or body of the motor vehicle) or has been subjected to rust or wear and tear and has become indistinct and difficult to read, the six digits or characters thereof located on the right-hand side and two additional digits indicating the year in which the stamping operation takes place shall be stamped, in addition to the mark of the competent Department in the competent Service on both ends of the number that has been stamped.

5- The importation of motor vehicles shall be subject to the conditions imposed pursuant to this Article, provided that the original classification of the motor vehicle as received from its manufacturer and as imposed pursuant to Article 175 of this Law is complied with.

Any importation contrary thereto shall remain at the responsibility of the owner of the motor vehicle, and he may not claim any compensation for damages.

6- The manufacturer of the motor vehicle, his agent in Lebanon and the owner of each vehicle shall be jointly and severally liable for the accuracy of the particulars mentioned in this Article.

7- Whoever alters, removes, replaces or obliterates the engine number or the serial number of the model shall be punished by imprisonment for a term of three years, a fine of twenty million Lebanese pounds and the impoundment of the vehicle.

Every motor vehicle intended for the carriage of goods must bear on its right side a visible plate clearly stating the unladen weight of the motor vehicle and its authorised gross weight, and these weights may also be clearly written on its body.

1- Every vehicle must be equipped with two plates known as registration plates bearing the vehicle registration number, one of which shall be affixed to the front and the second to the rear in a manner that renders them always visible and legible to the eye, and it shall not be permitted to remove them or for the vehicle to circulate without them.

The two registration plates may not be transferred to another vehicle even after they have been temporarily or permanently withdrawn from circulation, except in order to place them on another car owned by the owner of the vehicle or one of his ascendants or descendants, with the exception of the two plates of public cars, and it shall be prohibited to use registration plates other than those licensed in accordance with legal procedures.

2- Every trailer or semi-trailer must bear a single registration plate affixed to its rear in a visible and legible manner and it shall not be permitted to circulate without it, provided that the trailer or semi-trailer bears the same plate number as the tractor.

3- Public trucks and trucks designated for external transport shall be permitted to use their registration plate on more than one trailer or semi-trailer having specifications different from the tractor head, provided that the very same chassis number is stamped on these trailers or semi-trailers by the competent department, thereby allowing the use of any of them on the tractor head according to work requirements and market needs.

1- Registration plates must be made of high-quality materials and formed of reflective materials and thermal stamping, and must be visible and legible in broad daylight, and illuminated and legible at night, and stamped with the stamp of the competent department.

2- The plates must be securely affixed in the place prepared for that purpose in accordance with the manufacturer's recommendations and in accordance with the manner approved by the competent administration.

3- The owner of the vehicle and its driver must maintain these plates and inspect them continuously so that they remain clean, intact, and of clear features.

4- It shall be prohibited to place any writings, insignia, marks, letters, numbers, or any additions either on the plates or next to them.

Every violator of this paragraph shall be punished by imprisonment for three months and a fine of two million Lebanese pounds, in addition to the deduction of six points and the impoundment of the vehicle.

5- Registration plates shall be equipped with modern technologies for reading plates and identifying vehicle registration details automatically.

The details of these technologies shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities.

Diplomatic and Consular Plates:

Diplomatic and consular plates shall be allocated to diplomatic and consular missions and regional and international bodies pursuant to a written approval from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants, provided that the vehicle is owned by those missions or by one of their employees who hold diplomatic status.

Temporary Registration and Circulation Plates:

Temporary registration and circulation plates shall be allocated to agents of motor vehicles, with the exception of new motorcycles and "ATV" vehicles put into circulation for the first time.

Temporary Importation Plates:

Temporary importation plates shall be allocated to vehicles that are imported into Lebanon on a temporary basis.

Trial Plates:

1- Every motor car or combination of vehicles that has not yet been registered and is intended to be driven on the roads for the purpose of trial must be equipped with two trial plates, the first placed at the front and the second at the rear.

2- The circulation of vehicles equipped with two trial plates shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities.

3- The driver must carry, while the vehicle is circulating, the circulation permit relating to its plates and an authorisation from the customs authorities to remove the motor car from its customs warehouse in order to try it, or a declaration from the said authorities of the payment of the customs duties due thereon, or a declaration from approved motor car agents proving under their responsibility that the customs receipt (with an indication of its number and date) pertaining to it is in their possession.

Transit Plate:

1- Every motor car or combination of vehicles that has not yet been registered and is prepared for exportation abroad, must be equipped with two transit plates, the first placed at its front and the second at its rear.

2- The driver must carry, while the vehicle is circulating on the roads, the legal customs declarations relating to it, and a transit permit drawn up by the competent department in which are mentioned the name of the agent of the motor car company or the holder of the transit plate, his place of residence, the make and model of the vehicle, the serial chassis number, the engine number, the place of destination, the route of roads that must be followed, and the period of validity of the permit.

1- Accredited agents of motor vehicle companies in Lebanon, motor vehicle dealers, concessionaire companies, and United Nations organisations shall be granted a number of trial and transit plates for their use when needed.

2- These plates shall be granted for a renewable period of one year, provided that their number is determined by the competent service in respect of each natural or legal person from among the categories of persons mentioned above.

3- Natural persons engaged in transport brokerage activities shall be granted transit plates for a renewable period of one year.

The competent administration may permit, where necessary and on an exceptional basis, the delivery of trial and transit plates to individuals, provided that they are used only once and for a period not exceeding three days.

If the vehicle intended to be tested or exported is accompanied by a trailer or semi-trailer, two trial or transit plates must be placed, one at the front of the vehicle and the second at the rear of the trailer or semi-trailer.

1- In the event of the loss of one or both of the two registration plates, the owner of the vehicle must prove this by virtue of a report before the Internal Security Forces and then complete the procedures for obtaining replacement plates for those lost.

2- In the event of the damage of one or both of the two registration plates, the owner of the vehicle must inform the competent service.

3- Vehicles shall not be permitted to circulate before completing the procedures for obtaining replacement plates for those lost or damaged and obtaining the replacement plates.

4- In the event of the loss of one or both of the two plates outside the Lebanese territory, the owner of the vehicle must notify the Internal Security Forces and bring proof thereof from the competent authorities in the State in which they were lost.

And the security authorities must correspond with the local and international security authorities regarding the lost plates to ensure that they are not used unlawfully.

5- In the event of the loss of diplomatic or consular plates, the Internal Security Forces and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants must be notified, and then the procedures for obtaining replacement plates must be completed.

1- Every motor vehicle, every trailer, and every semi-trailer submitted for registration for the first time, or for which re-registration is requested after its withdrawal from circulation, must be inspected by the competent service in order to verify that all the conditions imposed thereon in this Law are met therein.

2- Private passenger cars, new motorcycles, and unused A.T.V. (ATV) vehicles that are registered for the first time shall be exempted from the inspection provided for in the first paragraph of this Article.

If it appears to the competent department that the motor vehicle, trailer, or semi-trailer which it has inspected meets all the imposed conditions, an inspection report shall be drawn up in respect thereof, upon which reliance shall be placed for registration and for granting the circulation permit.

Motor cars and trailers whose weight or dimensions exceed the regulatory limits, and the circulation of which is governed by Article 140 of this Law, shall be subject to a mechanical inspection and an inspection report shall be drawn up in respect thereof, upon which reliance shall be placed to grant a temporary circulation permit for a maximum of five days, renewable once.

The details of the registration plates mentioned in Chapter One of Part Three, and their dimensions, shapes, specifications, and colours according to the intended use of the motor vehicles, their categories, and their types, shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities in accordance with the following principles:

- 1 Registration plates shall be equipped with modern technologies to store data relating to the plate, the vehicle, and the owner, provided that these technologies allow the data to be read electronically

remotely. The details of these technologies shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities.

The plate, with its details, shall remain on the car and its ownership shall be transferred to third parties along with the car.

The owner of the plate may transfer its number to any new car he acquires. It may also be transferred to the owner's heirs.

2 - The plate number shall consist of one Latin letter on the left side and three Arabic numerals on the right side (1, 2, 3...).

3 - The Latin letter (A) shall be used for all uncoded plate numbers currently in use, including the plates of cars allocated to the Presidency of the Republic, the Speaker of Parliament, the Prime Minister, and the Members of Parliament, provided that the shape of the plate pertaining to private passenger cars is adopted.

The white colour shall be adopted for all plates except for the red colour for public cars, and the colours of the plates pertaining exclusively to the following categories shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Interior and Municipalities:

- Cars of diplomatic and consular missions.

- Military cars.

- Cars of rental companies.

- Trial plates.

- Temporary admission plates.

- Temporary registration and circulation plates.

- Transit plates.

- Plates of buses registered for intercontinental travel and external transport trucks.

4 - The Latin letters B -- G -- J -- M -- N -- O -- R -- S -- T -- Z shall be used for private car plates pertaining to all citizens. The letter P shall also be used for public cars, the letter D for the diplomatic corps, and the letter C for the consular corps.

5 - Plate numbers adopted prior to the issuance of this Law shall remain as they are, including those consisting of seven digits, and in accordance with what is provided for in paragraphs 2 and 3 above, without allocating codes according to regions, and without distinction for any official, judicial, religious, or other body.

6 - All adopted plates, whether coded or uncoded, shall be replaced, provided that this is done in accordance with the fees legally prescribed and within a period of one year from the date of issuance of this Law.

The Minister of Interior and Municipalities may, where necessary, extend the period for a duration not exceeding six months.

7 - Military numbers shall be affixed to vehicles and used exclusively in the performance of actual military and security service.

8 - New plate numbers shall be issued by an advanced computer programme that generates the plate number randomly once for each vehicle registration transaction, provided that the programme maintains a detailed database of its users, and that it issues the plate number after entering the necessary information about the vehicle and its owner.

9 - Registration plates shall be manufactured by the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities.

The implementing details of this paragraph shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities.

10 - Any violation of the shapes, numbers, or details of the plates shall subject its perpetrators to the following penalties:

a - Imprisonment from one month to three months and a fine from two million to three million Lebanese pounds for anyone who violates the adopted models, shapes, and colours, and six points shall be deducted from him and the vehicle shall be impounded.

b - Imprisonment from six months to one year and a fine from five to ten million Lebanese pounds for anyone who uses plates other than the plates allocated to the vehicle, and six points shall be deducted from him and the vehicle shall be impounded.

c - Imprisonment from six months to one year and a fine from five to ten million Lebanese pounds for anyone who drives a motor vehicle without plates, and six points shall be deducted from him and the vehicle shall be impounded.

d - Imprisonment from one year to two years and a fine from ten million to twenty million Lebanese pounds for anyone who tampers with or alters the numbers, and six points shall be deducted from him and the vehicle shall be impounded.

e - Imprisonment from one year to two years and a fine from ten million to twenty million Lebanese pounds for anyone who manufactures illegal plates.

11 - Anyone who tampers with the computer programme or who provides a plate number to a citizen in a manner contrary to the method of issuing these numbers in accordance with paragraph 8 above shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to two years and a fine from ten million to twenty million Lebanese pounds.

If the owner of a motor vehicle fails to pay the annual traffic fees that are determined in accordance with the deadlines issued by the competent administration, a late penalty of ten percent (10%) of the value of the annual fee shall be collected from him for each month of delay, provided that the value of the imposed penalty does not exceed double the value of the annual fee, in addition to the other penalties provided for in this Law, unless it is proven that the vehicle was impounded, detained, located outside the country, or stolen.

No vehicle may be driven unless it is registered and licensed in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

Automobiles, motorcycles, agricultural tractors, public works equipment, and generally motor vehicles shall be registered in special registers or cards with the Head of the competent department; whereas animal-drawn carts and hand-drawn vehicles and equipment shall be registered at municipal centres.

The following shall be subject to periodic mechanical inspection:

1- Private passenger motor cars, motorcycles, and "A T V" vehicles once every year after the lapse of three years from the date of their being put into circulation for the first time in Lebanon or abroad.

2- All other vehicles once in every year in accordance with special schedules to that effect issued by the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities.

3- Motor vehicles equipped with an engine powered by diesel (fuel oil), once a year for vehicles whose age does not exceed seven years from the date of their being put into circulation for the first time in Lebanon or abroad, and once every six months thereafter, to verify the fulfilment of all requirements imposed thereon, including the conformity of their emissions with acceptable specifications.

4- All types of motor cars, vehicles, and trailers shall, while moving on the roads, be subject to a mechanical inspection conducted at any time whatsoever by the employees of the competent administration assisted by members of the Internal Security Forces, in order to verify the fulfilment of all requirements imposed thereon.

5- No vehicle may be used on the road unless it is in good technical condition, and to this end, vehicles of all categories shall be subject to mechanical inspection to ensure that the technical and legal specifications and requirements are met therein.

6- The conditions of the technical (mechanical) inspection, the manner of conducting it, the places where the inspection is carried out, as well as the means that must be available in vehicles to ensure the comfort of their passengers, public safety, and environmental protection, shall be determined pursuant to a decision issued by the Council.

A permanent committee shall be formed, composed of the Head of the competent Service as Chairman, and the membership of each of the Head of the Mechanical Department, the Head of the Registration Department, and the Head of the Section concerned with the application, whose task shall be to decide upon applications relating to the refusal by one of the sections in the said Service to draw up an inspection report.

It is prohibited to lease out or rent tyres or any spare parts for any motor vehicle, or to replace them temporarily, with the aim of cheating in the compulsory mechanical inspection.

The details of implementation of this Article shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities.

1- The registers mentioned in the preceding Article shall be numbered and stamped by the head of the competent service, and their contents shall be relied upon unless their forgery is proven.

2- Except in the cases provided for in the Law dated 20 May 1935, relating to the sale of motorcars by instalments, it shall not be permissible to sell or mortgage motorcars, motorcycles, agricultural tractors and all motor vehicles subject to registration pursuant to Article 163 above, except before the competent service and through the assigned officer, and any sale or mortgage that takes place outside this administration shall have no effect towards a third party or before the State.

Anyone who contributes to the violation of the provisions of this Article shall be deemed a partner in liability.

3- Only the first power of attorney for the registration of vehicles shall be recognised, the validity of which shall run for a period of two months from the date of its execution.

The notary public must notify the competent service of his execution of a power of attorney for its sale within a time limit of two working days from the date of executing the power of attorney, indicating the full identity of the attorney-in-fact and the detailed address pursuant to items "b" and "h" of the first paragraph and items "a" and "b" of the second paragraph of Article 210 of this Law, after payment of all traffic fees and fines due thereon.

4- Anyone who delays registration shall be liable to a fine in the amount of one hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds /100,000/ L.L. for each week of delay, and a fraction of a week shall be deemed a full week, after the expiry of a period of two months from its execution, and in this case the aforementioned service must notify the Internal Security Forces for the purpose of impounding the motorcar until its registration.

5- Powers of attorney executed in favour of companies and establishments for the sale of motorcars and motor vehicles, duly registered in the Commercial Register, shall be exempted from the provisions of the time limit specified in paragraph "3" of this Article, provided that the motorcar is temporarily withdrawn from circulation and a salvage certificate is issued for it prior to the execution of the aforementioned power of attorney. Dealers of new motorcars shall have the right to execute a second power of attorney for sale on an exceptional basis in favour of companies and establishments trading in used motorcars, registered in accordance with the laws and regulations.

6- The details of application of the provisions of this Article shall be determined by a decision issued by the Ministers of Justice and of the Interior and Municipalities.

Employees entrusted with keeping the registers or entrusted with hearing all types of contracts relating to vehicles shall take the following oath before the Single Criminal Judge where their workplace is located and prior to commencing such work:

(I swear to perform my duty with honesty and fidelity)

These employees may hear contracts in private sessions pursuant to a petition submitted by one of the contracting parties to the head of the competent unit, in return for a travel allowance determined by a decision of the Minister of Interior and Municipalities, to be provided by the concerned party along with the means of transport.

1- Vehicles shall be registered at the competent department in the names of their owners after the registration applicant submits the required documents and instruments in addition to his first name, surname, and residential address in accordance with items "b" and "h" of the first paragraph and items "a" and "b" of the second paragraph of Article 210 of this Law.

2- In the event of the mortgage of any motor vehicle subject to registration in accordance with Article 163 of this Law, it may remain in the possession of the debtor, provided that the mortgage contract expressly stipulates the same.

1- No vehicle may be registered, put back into circulation, or have its annual circulation fee paid, except after submitting an insurance contract with an insurance company licensed to operate in the Lebanese Republic and authorised to practice vehicle insurance business, provided that such contract covers civil liability for bodily and material damage caused to third parties and resulting from the use of that vehicle.

2- No non-Lebanese vehicle may be permitted to enter the territory of the Lebanese Republic except after submitting an insurance contract covering civil liability for bodily and material damage caused to third parties and resulting from the use of the vehicle in the Lebanese Republic in accordance with the laws in force.

1- Transactions for the transfer of ownership of vehicles, their mortgage, and all other legal dispositions relating thereto, of whatever kind, shall be deemed null and void unless they are registered and authenticated at the competent service.

2- Employees working at the competent service shall be vested with the authority to draw up and authenticate contracts specific to vehicles, including contracts for the transfer of their ownership, their mortgage, and all other legal dispositions relating thereto, and to hear and record the acknowledgements and statements of the parties thereto or to authenticate their signatures, in accordance with the rules and procedures applied by the Notary Public in drawing up and authenticating contracts.

3- If it becomes apparent to the competent administration that there is an encumbrance preventing the transfer of ownership of the vehicle or that the vehicle is mortgaged, its ownership may not be transferred except after the removal of the encumbrance or the consent of the mortgagee creditor.

1- Officially accredited agents in Lebanon of factories of motor vehicles, including new ATV vehicles and motorcycles, shall carry out the registration formalities for these vehicles put into circulation for the first time, in accordance with the conditions determined by a decision issued by the Ministers of Interior and Municipalities and of Finance. Provided that they stamp the chassis numbers of the motor vehicles, with the exception of cycles and ATV vehicles, that do not bear engraved numbers, in accordance with the method and number models adopted by the competent Service.

2- Importers of used motor vehicles, including ATV vehicles and motorcycles, shall carry out the registration formalities for these vehicles put into circulation for the first time, in accordance with the conditions determined by a decision issued by the Ministers of Interior and Municipalities and of Finance.

3- Whoever violates the two paragraphs above shall be punished by a fine of ten million Lebanese pounds, and a warning shall be addressed to the offender. In the event of repetition of the violation, the fine shall be doubled.

1- The competent Service shall deliver to the owner of the vehicle a circulation permit which it draws up on the basis of the content of its documents and an inspection report, in which the following specifications are recorded:

- The first name and surname of its owner and his detailed place of residence.

- The type of vehicle, and its intended use.

- Its make and model.

- The chassis and engine number.

- The number of cylinders and engine power.

- Its shape, colour and the specifications of its body.

- Its unladen weight and its net and gross payload if the motor car is designed for the transport of loads.

- The registration number licensed for it. -The date on which it was put into circulation for the first time.

- Special endorsements and remarks.

- The number of passengers licensed to be transported and the manner of their distribution.

2- The owner of the vehicle or his legal representative shall immediately notify the competent Service in the event of loss or damage of the vehicle circulation permit, by proving the same pursuant to a report before the Internal Security Forces, and submit an application to obtain a replacement for a lost item or a replacement for a damaged item and pay the prescribed fees.

3- The circulation permit shall feature several security points determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities.

The owner of every private vehicle registered in Lebanon who permanently transfers his place of residence abroad shall submit to the competent service a written declaration to that effect, to which he shall attach the circulation licence and the registration plates pertaining to the vehicle.

Motor vehicles registered under the temporary admission regime shall be exempted from handing over the plates and the circulation licence, provided that their registration entries are struck off upon their exit from Lebanese territory, and their circulation thereafter shall be subject to the regime of the International Convention concluded in Geneva on 19 September 1949, or any other international convention ratified by Lebanon.

It is prohibited to carry out any substantial modification to a motor vehicle before obtaining prior approval from the Mechanics Department of the competent Service.

Substantial modifications shall mean the following:

- Modification in the number of axles and the distance between them, and reinforcement of the chassis. Should the need arise to carry out one of the modifications specified above, the concerned party must submit an application to the Mechanics Department of the competent Service and present the motor vehicle together with its circulation permit and the following documents:

1- Upon replacing the engine, producing an official document proving the legality of the engine (a customs schedule containing the engine number or a customs certificate - the circulation permit or the wreckage certificate of the motor vehicle from which it was removed).

It is stipulated for this modification that the power of the new engine shall not be less than the power of the old engine.

2- Upon replacing the cabin, a customs document for the cabin must be produced containing the chassis number located on the manufacturer's plate or engraved thereon, or a customs stamping number proving its legality, or a wreckage certificate of the vehicle to which the cabin belonged, provided that the replaced cabin is of the same make.

3- Upon replacing and manufacturing motor vehicle bodies, it must be consistent with the purpose for which they are intended: it is not permissible to overburden motor vehicles with huge, ill-considered bodies and to use heavy materials that increase their tare weight and limit their payload in a manner that conflicts with the purpose for which they are intended.

It is not permissible to add elements to the chassis that increase its strength and constitute an additional burden that increases the tare weight at the expense of the payload (reinforcement of the chassis).

The tare weight of a motor vehicle may not exceed 55% of its gross weight specified for it pursuant to the laws in force, with the exception of motor vehicles whose gross weight does not exceed ten tonnes. For tanker motor vehicles, the net volume of the tank may not exceed by 10% the volume of the payload licensed to be transported.

Payload = Gross weight - Tare weight

Volume of payload = Payload % Specific gravity of the liquid

Net volume of the tank = Volume of the internal void intended for transport

4- Upon modifying the number of axles and the distance between them, this matter is linked to what is issued by the manufacturing company, whereby the concerned party is required to produce the manufacturer's catalogue or the official documents showing the technical specifications pertaining to the vehicle as well as all the manufacturer's measurements for the model intended to be modified.

In the event that the submitted catalogue does not provide for the possibility of carrying out this requested modification, the Mechanics Department must request the concerned party to obtain a certificate from the manufacturer of the vehicle in the country of origin, duly authenticated by the competent authorities, stating that the requested modification is technically acceptable.

After examining the applications submitted to it regarding the substantial modifications specified above, the Mechanics Department may set forth all the technical conditions available for this modification in the event that it is technically approved, and state the reasons for refusal in the event of non-approval.

A declaration alone shall suffice for a change of colour, and the owner of the vehicle must present to the Mechanics Department the vehicle together with its circulation permit in order to make the necessary corrections thereto.

1- It shall be incumbent upon the owner of the vehicle, if it is dismantled or destroyed or if he ceases to use it due to its unfitness, to notify the competent department thereof in writing, for the purpose of permanently withdrawing it from circulation, within a period not exceeding 7 days from the date of the occurrence of any of those cases, and to surrender to the competent department during this period the vehicle circulation licence and its two number plates in the event that the car is registered as private; and the written declaration shall suffice in the event of the loss of the licence and the two number plates as a result of force majeure, after verifying that pursuant to a report drawn up before the Internal Security Forces.

2- In the event of the temporary withdrawal of a vehicle registered as private from circulation after its two number plates and its circulation licence have been surrendered and all fees imposed thereon have been paid, no fee shall be payable thereon upon returning it to circulation, except for the year in which it was returned to circulation.

3- The cars of members of the diplomatic and consular corps shall be exempted when replacing diplomatic number plates with ordinary number plates or other diplomatic number plates and vice versa, and cars registered under the temporary admission regime shall also be exempted from the fee for replacing number plates.

4- Whoever drives a motor vehicle that has been permanently or temporarily withdrawn from circulation (salvage) shall be punished by imprisonment for three months and by a pecuniary fine in the amount of one million Lebanese pounds, and six points shall be deducted from him in addition to the impoundment of the vehicle.

The competent administration may strike off the registration of the vehicle if it is established to it that it is no longer fit for use, provided that the bases and conditions of the striking off are determined pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities.

Motor vehicles shall be divided into five categories:

1- Passenger cars: This category includes every motor vehicle designed for the transport of persons and having eight seats or fewer, excluding the driver.

2- Buses: This category includes every motor vehicle designed for the transport of persons and having more than eight seats, excluding the driver's seat, as well as every motor vehicle of this type designed for the transport of passengers and goods together.

3- Goods vehicles: This category includes every motor vehicle designed for the transport of loads, goods or animals, as well as the towing vehicle, the trailer, the tractor unit and the semi-trailer.

4- Passenger and transport cars: This category includes every passenger car designed at times for the transport of persons and at other times for the transport of loads, as well as every passenger car designed for the transport of persons and loads simultaneously, provided that its gross weight does not exceed 3500 kg, or 4500 kg if it runs on electric power.

5- Special-use motor vehicles: This category includes every motor vehicle which originally belongs to any of the four categories defined above, but is permanently equipped with mechanical machinery for a special use and is not used for the transport of loads or persons other than the persons necessary to carry out the works for which it was designed, including motor vehicles equipped with heavy-lifting machinery, with machinery for prospecting for water, minerals and liquid combustible materials, with machinery and lamps or ladders for repairing lamps and lighting lines, with concrete machinery and pumps, with mobile repair workshops, with health, agricultural or veterinary laboratories, for advertising, publishing and publicity provided that it is not used for any other purpose and is manufactured in a manner that does not allow objects inside its body to fly out and endanger public safety, with mobile restaurants ... and similar motor vehicles.

6- Specific-transport motor vehicle: This category includes every motor vehicle which originally belongs to any of the four categories of this Article, permanently designated and equipped for the transport of objects or persons in specific positions and under specific conditions, including motor vehicles equipped with closed, thermally insulated bodies and refrigeration devices for transporting objects under a temperature-control system, with bodies for loading, compacting and unloading waste, with special tankers or containers for transporting liquid or powdered materials, with flatbeds equipped with fastening means for transporting containers or swap bodies of standardised dimensions, with concrete mixers, with flatbeds, rails and special devices for transporting motor vehicles, for ambulance service, for hearses, for transporting prisoners, for transporting funds, with tankers for transporting cesspool sludge, with tankers for irrigating or spraying crops or for disinfecting places from insects, and those equipped with household furniture and beds accommodating the transport and sleeping of not more than seven persons including the driver (caravan motor vehicles), and similar motor vehicles.
Motor vehicles shall be registered as private or public.

1- A passenger car shall be registered as private in the name of its owner (whether a natural or legal person) when carriage therein is effected without consideration of whatever kind.

2- Permission is granted for the registration as private of passenger cars whose number of seats, excluding the driver, is for eight persons and fewer:

a- In the name of legally registered Lebanese establishments dedicated to renting private motor vehicles to tourists, provided that such tourists drive the motor vehicles themselves and that such motor vehicles have special plates of their own distinguishing them from others.

In all cases, insurance of these motor vehicles against all risks must be effected, and the additional fees in the schedule annexed to this Law must be paid.

b - In the name of driving schools licensed therefor in order to transport their students to the places of instruction and examination and to train them thereon.

The competent service shall determine the itinerary for these motor vehicles, which must be distinguished by visible writing on both sides thereof showing the purpose of their use, and insurance for the motor vehicles and their passengers must be effected.

1- In order to meet their needs, private buses shall be registered in the name of the following departments and entities:

a- Departments of the State, municipalities, unions of municipalities, and public institutions affiliated with the State, municipalities, or unions of municipalities.

b- International organisations and political, diplomatic, and consular missions operating in Lebanon.

c- Hospitals and scientific, educational, charitable, and sports institutions, provided that each institution restricts the use of the vehicle to transporting patients, employees, workers, pupils, teachers, or athletes who are in its care.

d- Airlines and travel and tourism agencies for the purpose of transporting their passengers, their luggage, their workers, and their employees from their premises to the airport or the port. Provided that such transport takes place without consideration. The competent department shall determine the route of these vehicles.

e- Hotels of the third class and above for the benefit of their guests, workers, and employees within the areas determined by the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities.

f- Factories and establishments whose employees and workers exceed ten in number, provided that their use is restricted to transporting them only, and without consideration.

g- Officially licensed travel and tourism agencies that provide tourist services for the purpose of transporting tourists from Beirut or land and air ports to archaeological and tourist sites in Lebanon and vice versa, under conditions determined by a decree passed in the Council of Ministers, provided that the buses are equipped with air-conditioning units and "Pullman" seats.

The specifications and equipment of the vehicles mentioned in this Article and others shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Interior and Municipalities, and the tariffs to be applied by a decision of the Minister of Public Works and Transport.

h- Licensed driving schools for teaching applicants for driving licences how to drive buses, subject to compliance with the conditions imposed thereon pursuant to this Law. It is prohibited to use these vehicles for any purpose other than the licensed purpose.

2- Private buses shall be registered in the name of the Lebanese State Railways and Public Transport Authority to provide public transport for consideration.

This registration shall not entitle owners of public vehicles of any category whatsoever to claim any compensation.

It shall be permitted to register private buses in the name of enterprises that engage in international transport under the following conditions:

1- That the operation of these vehicles be restricted to the transport of passengers across continents or across the desert.
