2- That the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities determine the technical specifications and mechanical equipment required to be available in the vehicle to ensure the safety and comfort of travelers.

3- That the circulation permit specify the routes which the vehicle must follow and the places where it may stop.

4- That the name of the enterprise concerned be inscribed on the vehicle in large, visible and clear letters in the Arabic language and in a foreign language (French or English) after the phrase: "Equipped for transcontinental and trans-desert transport".

5- That no traveler be transported except after verifying that he holds a regular entry visa permitting disembarkation in the country of destination, or in the place through which the means of transport passes, where applicable.

6- It shall be prohibited to use these vehicles for any purpose other than that for which they are licensed.

Goods vehicles shall be registered as private if transport therein is carried out without consideration, and if they are dedicated exclusively to the service of their owner (a natural or legal person), provided that they are registered in his name. Provided that their gross weight does not exceed 21 tonnes.

The following shall benefit from the registration:

1- State departments, unions of municipalities, municipalities and public institutions affiliated therewith.

2- International organisations and political, diplomatic and consular missions in Lebanon.

3- Owners of industries and manual workshops; the numbers of trucks, their gross weights, the materials permitted to be transported and their distribution zones shall be determined by a decision of the Ministers of Interior and Municipalities and of Industry, taking into account their financial capacity.

4- Concessionaires, whether companies or individuals.

5- Owners of agricultural tractors and self-propelled agricultural mechanical machinery, including those equipped with a crane by their manufacturer, and self-propelled and non-self-propelled drilling machinery, in order to transport the equipment or fuels necessary for their operation.

6- Farm owners, farmers, and owners of nurseries, ornamental plants and flowers, within the conditions set forth in Article 182 of this Law.

7- Owners of apiaries, provided that the number of their beehives is not less than 25 numbered and coded beehives and provided that the gross weight of the vehicle does not exceed eight and a half tonnes, and owners of animal pens and farms and agricultural cooperatives. The numbers of trucks and their gross weights for owners of animal farms and pens and agricultural cooperatives shall be determined by a decision of the Ministers of Interior and Municipalities and of Agriculture.

8- Contractors for the State, municipalities or public institutions affiliated with the State or municipalities, in their works relating to their contract, provided that they are registered with the Chambers of Commerce, Industry and Agriculture, and that their financial solvency is not less than one hundred million Lebanese Pounds.

9- Hospitals, scientific, charitable and religious institutions, schools, and airlines, provided that the gross weight of the vehicle dedicated to each branch does not exceed four and a half tonnes.

10- Owners of goods vehicles dedicated to external transport.

11- Owners of shops, establishments and commercial companies that distribute their goods to homes, other shops, restaurants, hotels and cafés, provided that their gross weight does not exceed eight and a half tonnes; the numbers of trucks, their gross weights, the materials permitted to be transported and their distribution zones for each establishment in accordance with its classification in the Chamber of Commerce, Industry and Agriculture shall be determined by a decision of the Ministers of Interior and Municipalities and of Economy and Trade.

12- Licensed driving schools for teaching driving licence applicants how to drive goods vehicles, subject to compliance with the conditions imposed thereon pursuant to this Law.

It is prohibited to use these vehicles for any purpose other than that for which they are licensed.

With the exception of private goods vehicles registered in accordance with the provisions of Paragraphs 1, 2, 10 and 12 of Article 180 of this Law, the registration of private goods vehicles shall be subject to an additional annual fee specified in the Schedule annexed to this Law.

1- The gross weight of the vehicle or vehicles that may be registered in the name of farm owners, farmers, and owners of nurseries, ornamental plants and flowers shall be determined as follows:

A- Up to seven and a half tonnes:

- If the land is planted with vegetables as protected cultivation (under greenhouses) or with ornamental plants and flowers, or is a nursery, and its area ranges between two thousand metres and ten thousand square metres.

- If the land is planted with field vegetables (unprotected) or planted with fruit trees and its area ranges between three thousand and twenty thousand square metres.

B- From seven and a half tonnes to fourteen tonnes:

- If the land is planted with vegetables as protected cultivation (under greenhouses) or with ornamental plants and flowers, or is a nursery, and its area ranges between ten thousand and thirty thousand square metres.

- If the land is planted with field vegetables (unprotected) or planted with fruit trees and its area ranges between twenty thousand and fifty thousand square metres.

C- From fourteen tonnes to nineteen tonnes:

- If the land is planted with vegetables as protected cultivation (under greenhouses) and its area exceeds thirty thousand square metres.

- If the land is planted with field vegetables (unprotected) or planted with fruit trees and its area is over fifty thousand square metres.

D- Up to nineteen tonnes, if the land is not planted with trees or not planted with vegetables, but is planted with grains, and its area exceeds five hundred thousand square metres. The application shall be submitted to the competent service, provided that the required documents and supporting records are specified pursuant to a decision issued by the Ministers of Interior and Municipalities and of Agriculture.

2- It shall not be permissible to register a vehicle or vehicles whose gross weight exceeds the licensed weight.

Public administrations and institutions, municipalities, unions of municipalities, concession holders whether companies or individuals, and owners of farms and agricultural cooperatives shall be licensed to transport workers in goods vehicles registered as private in their name, provided that they are equipped with the necessary seats in accordance with the conditions determined by the competent departments for the purpose of preserving the safety of workers inside these vehicles.

Concession holders whether companies or individuals, and owners of farms and agricultural cooperatives, shall insure the workers required to be transported.

A passenger vehicle whose capacity does not exceed five passengers shall be registered as a public vehicle if the registration applicant submits the licence plates of a passenger vehicle registered as a public vehicle that is intended to be withdrawn from public circulation.

An additional fee of seven hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese pounds shall be due for each additional passenger.

A public licence plate may not be transferred from one name to another unless the beneficiary of the transfer presents a vehicle to which the transferred licence plate is to be allocated.

1- A bus vehicle shall be registered as a public vehicle if the registration applicant submits the licence plates of a bus vehicle registered as a public vehicle that is intended to be withdrawn from public circulation.

2- If the number of seats of the bus vehicle requested to be registered exceeds the number of seats in the vehicle to which the submitted registration licence plates belong, the registration applicant shall be required to pay an amount of four hundred thousand Lebanese pounds for each missing seat.

3- If the holder of the registration submits the licence plates of a bus vehicle whose number of seats exceeds the seats of the vehicle intended to be registered, the excess submitted seats shall be considered cancelled ipso jure.

4- Under no circumstances may plates be divided or merged, nor may a public licence plate be transferred from one name to another unless the beneficiary of the transfer presents a vehicle to which the transferred licence plate is to be allocated.

A vehicle shall always be considered a bus vehicle if it is originally of this category and is prepared at the same time for the transport of persons and goods, and the conditions imposed in the preceding Article shall apply to its registration as a public vehicle, provided that at least half of it remains allocated to the transport of passengers, and that the net payload of the goods that it may transport is determined on the basis of seventy kilograms /70 kg/ for each seat it lacks, provided that the gross weight does not exceed the technically authorised weight.

With the exception of private passenger cars provided for in the first paragraph of Article 177, the competent department shall grant prior approval for registration, on the basis of proof of the capacity of the parties mentioned in Articles 177 to 178 of this Law.

The beneficiary parties shall submit the necessary official documents issued by the competent department, with the exception of owners of goods vehicles with bodies fitted out as refrigerators and for external transport.

And the owners of shops, establishments and companies mentioned in paragraph /11/ of Article 180 of this Law shall submit the document of their registration in the Commercial Register before the competent courts.

The persons and entities, mentioned in paragraphs 3, 6, 7, 9 and 11 of Article 180 of this Law, shall be authorised to use the private passenger cars registered in their name to transport their goods in the trunks of the cars within a limit of /80/ kilograms in the trunk of a single car, or at the load capacity specified for the car by its manufacturer if it is of the type known as "station" designated for transporting passengers and goods, provided that its net payload does not exceed 750 kilograms.

And this shall be subject to the authorisation referred to in Articles 184 and 187 of this Law. Owners of private passenger cars shall be permitted to transport therein luggage or items belonging to them, provided that such transport does not have the purpose of selling them on public roads and that rear visibility remains completely clear.
The itinerary that private buses must follow shall be specified in a permit annexed to the circulation permit.

The itinerary that private goods vehicles and private passenger cars set out in paragraphs 2 and 4 of Article 177 and in Article 185 of this Law, as well as special-use cars provided for in paragraph 5 of Article 175 of this Law, must follow shall be specified in a permit annexed to the circulation permit.

Ambulances belonging to hospitals, official and health institutions, charitable associations and private establishments whose number of workers exceeds twenty-five workers, as well as cars fitted out for transporting the dead, shall be registered in the category of specific transport cars.

The use of these vehicles for any purpose other than that for which they are fitted out shall be prohibited.

1- Goods vehicles shall be registered if the registration applicant submits the number plates of a goods vehicle registered as a public vehicle which is intended to be withdrawn from public circulation.

2- If the goods vehicle requested to be registered as a public vehicle has a net payload exceeding the net payload of the vehicle intended to be withdrawn from circulation, the registration applicant must pay in consideration of the difference in payload:

- Six hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds /600,000 L.L./ up to the first two tons /2 tons/.

- Three hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds /300,000 L.L./ for each additional ton.

A fraction of a ton shall be deemed a full ton.

3- If the registration holder submits the number plates of a goods vehicle whose net payload exceeds the payload of the vehicle intended to be registered, the excess payload shall be deemed cancelled ipso jure.

4- Under no circumstances may number plates be split or merged, nor may a public number plate be transferred from one name to another unless the beneficiary of the transfer presents a vehicle to which the transferred number plate is to be allocated.

5- Goods vehicles, consisting of a tractor and trailer, may not be registered as public vehicles except where they are designated to operate in the transport of goods outside Lebanese territory.

Number plates of public vehicles shall not be surrendered on a temporary basis except for the purpose of withdrawing them from circulation in order to register another public vehicle in their stead, provided that the period of their surrender shall under no circumstances exceed one month for passenger cars, two months for buses, and three months for trucks, and provided that no more than two public number plates are withdrawn from circulation for a single owner and his ascendants and descendants.

The vehicle or combination of vehicles mentioned in the fifth paragraph of Article 175 of this Law may be registered as a private vehicle in the name of its owner and shall be subject to the fees specified in the schedule of fees annexed to this Law.

The provisions of Chapter Three concerning registration shall not apply to:

1- Vehicles subject to the regime of the International Convention on International Transport concluded in Geneva on 19 September 1949, or registered in neighbouring countries with which a special agreement has been concluded, provided that their circulation permits are in due form.

2- To vehicles of foreign tourists and summer visitors, who shall be granted temporary admission permits by Customs, provided that the vehicle's circulation permit is valid in its country of registration and that the duration of the permit does not exceed the period of validity of the circulation permit, and provided that it does not exceed six months renewable once, and that the vehicle is insured against third-party liability.

3- Vehicles bearing trial or transit number plates provided for in Articles 149 and 150 of this Law.

4- To vehicles of the Army and the Security Forces registered in special categories.

International Traffic:

1- A vehicle shall be deemed to be in a state of "International Traffic" on Lebanese territory when the following conditions are met therein:

a- Its owner is a natural or legal person who has a permanent place of residence abroad.

b- It is not registered in Lebanon.

c- It is present in Lebanon temporarily.

d- Its holder carries an insurance contract valid in Lebanon covering bodily and material damages caused by the vehicle to third parties.

2- The vehicle shall be admitted in the state mentioned in the first paragraph above for a period of six months.

This period may be renewed once only after the approval of the Customs Administration.

1- No person may drive any motor vehicle on the road unless he holds a driving licence authorising him to drive such a vehicle, and the driver shall carry this licence while driving the vehicle.

The holder of a driving licence for a certain category of vehicles may not use it to drive a vehicle of another category unless it is below the category or subcategory he is licensed to drive, provided that this principle shall apply to motorcycles and "A T V" vehicles separately.

2- The competent department shall issue the driving licence based on the result of the driver's examination and the verification that he possesses the necessary qualifications to drive the category of vehicle he is licensed to drive within a specified validity period, subject to compliance with the laws and regulations in force and the observance of public safety.

1- Driving licences shall be divided into the following categories:

Category One: Motorcycle driving licence.

Category Two: Driving licence for passenger cars or transport cars whose gross weight does not exceed 3500 kilograms.

Category Three: Driving licence for trucks and the cars provided for in Paragraph 5 of Article 175.

Category Four: Bus driving licence.

Category Five: Driving licence for agricultural vehicles, public works vehicles, and their equipment.

Category Six: Driving licence for persons with special needs (disabled persons).

2- The purpose of use of driving licences shall be divided into two types, private and public.

3- The driving licence shall feature several security features to be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities.

Each of the categories of driving licences mentioned above shall be divided into sub-categories, and the minimum age of the driving licence applicant shall be determined as follows:

Motorcycle Category - "1"

A two-wheeled motorised cycle whose engine capacity does not exceed 125 cc and whose power does not exceed 11 kilowatts, or a three-wheeled cycle whose power does not exceed 15 kilowatts. Minimum age 18 years - private.

Motorcycle Category

- A two-wheeled motorised cycle whose engine capacity exceeds 125 cc or a three-wheeled cycle whose power exceeds 15 kilowatts. Minimum age 21 years - private.

Car Category - "1"

An "A T V" vehicle. Minimum age 18 years - private.

Car Category

- Passenger cars or transport cars whose total weight does not exceed 3500 kilograms and whose number of seats, excluding the driver, is eight or fewer, and a trailer not exceeding 750 kg, provided that the total weight of the vehicle and the trailer together does not exceed 4250 kg. Minimum age 18 years - private / Minimum age 21 years - public.

Truck Category - "1"

A truck whose total weight exceeds 3500 kg and up to 7500 kg. Minimum age 21 years - public.

Truck Category

- A truck whose total weight exceeds 7500 kg and the cars provided for in Paragraph 5 of Article 175 of this Law. Minimum age 21 years - public.

Truck + Trailer (T) Category

A truck having the specifications of the "Truck" category plus a trailer or semi-trailer whose combined total weight exceeds 12 tonnes. Six months after obtaining the Truck category - public.

Bus Category - "1"

A passenger bus whose number of seats does not exceed 16 passengers excluding the driver, and of a length not exceeding 8 metres. Minimum age 21 years - public.

"Bus" Category

A passenger bus whose number of seats exceeds 16 passengers. Six months after obtaining the licence of the "Bus - 1" category - public.

Works Equipment and Agricultural Vehicles Category

An agricultural vehicle. Minimum age 18 years - public.

A public works vehicle. Minimum age 21 years - public.
Children who are under the age of eight years and who ride in vehicles of the "Car" category mentioned above shall be considered as half a passenger, provided that their number does not exceed six.

A special field shall be designated in the body of the driving licence for driving vehicles with an automatic transmission (boite de vitesse automatique), provided that the driving examination is conducted on this type of vehicle and that the driver does not drive any other.

Drivers of vehicles with electric motors shall be exempted from the driving licence if the power of their motor does not exceed one kilowatt, and the competent department shall verify, where necessary, the power of these motors.

Provided that these vehicles are not used on public roads.

1- A private car category driving licence shall entitle its holder to drive a private passenger car, provided that he is not hired by a third party for a driving task or work, and a public car category driving licence shall entitle its holder to drive a private or public passenger car for remuneration.

2- A public car category driving licence shall only be granted to a person who holds a private car category driving licence.

3- A Truck -1 category and Bus -1 category driving licence shall only be granted to a person who holds a public car category driving licence.

4- A Truck category driving licence shall only be granted after six months from holding a Truck - 1 category driving licence.

For the granting of each category of the driving licence categories mentioned in Article 199 of this Law, the licence applicant shall be required to meet the following:

1- The minimum age provided for above.

2- Actual residence in Lebanon.

3- A medical certificate specific to driving.

4- His judicial record being free from the disqualifying entries determined by this Law.

5- The necessary training specific to each category, proven by a certificate from the driving school at which he studied.

6- Passing the driving examination in accordance with the rules and procedures set out in the driving examination conditions.

7- Payment of the prescribed fee for the examination and the licence.

1- The validity of private driving licences shall run for a period of ten years, renewable without being subject to an examination every ten years until the age of 50, five years until the age of 65 and every three years after the age of 65.

2- The validities of public driving licences shall run for a period of five years, renewable without being subject to an examination every five years until the age of 50, three years until the age of 65 and every two years after the age of 65.

3- In all cases, the renewal period granted must not be less than the subsequent renewal period mentioned in the two clauses above.

Every owner of a private car who employs one or more hired drivers shall be required to ensure that the driver is Lebanese, and to register with the competent department, or to send through the postal operator, the first name of this driver, his surname, his place of residence, the type and number of the car or cars he drives, and other information requested by the department.

The details of the application of the provisions of this Article shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities.

Driving licences granted prior to the application of this Law shall be equated with their equivalents among the new driving licences pursuant to an equivalence table issued by a decision of the Minister of Interior and Municipalities.

A driving licence of all categories, whatever its type, shall not be granted:

1- Except after the lapse of six months from the date of completion of the execution of a sentence for manifest drunkenness where the convicted person does not hold a driving licence.

2- Except after the lapse of one year from the date of completion of the execution of the sentence for any person who uses narcotics without holding a driving licence.

3- Except after the lapse of five years from the date of completion of the execution of the sentence for any person who manufactures, prepares, uses, possesses, transports, trades in, imports, exports, or acts as a broker in narcotics, or commits any act contrary to the law relating thereto.

Every driver who is convicted of one of these offences shall be punished, in addition to the penalties provided for in the Narcotics Law, by the cancellation of the driving licence and by prohibiting him from applying to obtain a new licence for a period of five years from the date of completion of the execution of the sentence.

Public driving licences shall be granted to Lebanese nationals.

And after the rehabilitation of any person who was convicted of a felony or of one of the following offences: embezzlement - use of a forged document - offences against public morals provided for in Title VII of the Penal Code - offences relating to trading with the enemy or transporting passengers or goods to and from its territories - offences relating to terrorism and offences that entail the deprivation of their perpetrators of civil rights.

A judgment may be rendered cancelling every public driving licence against the holder of which a final judgment is issued for committing one of the offences set forth above.

It shall be a condition for the grant of a driving licence that the applicant be conversant with reading at least and pass a theoretical and practical examination in accordance with the conditions, rules and procedures issued by the Council upon the proposal of the Committee.

1- Every person who wishes to obtain a driving licence shall submit an application therefor in person or through one of his ascendants or descendants or through the postal operator, and driving schools may likewise submit the application to the competent department, stating therein:

أ- His given name, surname and the names of his parents.

ب- The address of his actual place of residence in which he resides for more than 165 days in the year, which shall include the building number, floor, street, quarter, area, and the landline and mobile telephone numbers, where they exist, in addition to his electronic mail, and the registered address shall be deemed to be the legal postal address of the licence applicant.

ج- His place and date of birth.

د- The category or categories of the licence which he wishes to obtain.

ه- The type of licence: private or public.

و- Specification of whether the driving licence is specific to a vehicle with an automatic transmission (Boite de Vitesse Automatique).

ز- A request to fix an urgent examination appointment, at the wish of the licence applicant.

ح- The name and address of two relatives and their landline and mobile telephone numbers to contact them in the event of the occurrence of an accident.

ط- The address for delivery of the licence, if it differs from the address of residence.

2- He shall also attach to the application the following documents:

أ- His identity card, or his passport, or a civil status extract certified by the Civil Status Department whose date of issue does not exceed three months, or any other official document.

ب- A certificate of residence from the Mukhtar of the locality in which he resides, accompanied by an official document proving the place of residence such as a title deed, a lease contract, or a telephone, electricity or water bill.

ج- His judicial record dating back to less than three months.

د- Colour photographs, 2 in number, measuring 4 (by) 4 centimetres, showing the full face, certified by the Mukhtar of the locality in which he resides, and not dating back to more than three months, or an instant photograph taken by the competent department of the licence applicant.

ه- A medical certificate specific to driving.

ز- A blood group certificate.

ح- A certificate from the driving school stating the number of hours which the applicant spent learning and training on the road.

ط- A copy of the current driving licence, where it exists.

ي- A receipt proving that he has paid the examination and licence fee.

ك- A receipt proving that he has paid the expedited examination fee, which takes place within three working days, in the amount of fifty per cent of the examination and licence fee, in the event that the applicant chooses that.

The Speaker and members of the Chamber of Deputies, the President and members of the Council of Ministers, judges, civil and military State employees, and members of the diplomatic and consular corps shall be exempted from submitting a copy of the judicial record.

A medical certificate specific to driving dating back to less than three months shall establish that its holder enjoys the physical and mental qualities, in particular the senses of hearing and sight required for driving vehicles, and that he is in a state of health permitting him to drive the category or categories of vehicles for which he is applying for a driving licence. The conditions for granting this certificate shall be determined by a decision of the Council upon the proposal of the Committee, provided that the decision includes the health conditions and physical disabilities that are incompatible with the conditions for obtaining a driving licence and those whose holders may be granted a driving licence under certain conditions.

On the basis of the application and the attached documents, the competent department shall open a special file for the applicant, and shall notify him of the date and place of the theoretical examination pursuant to the examination document in which it sets out the conditions of the theoretical and practical examinations.

1- The candidate must sit for the theoretical test on the date specified on the examination document, and he must receive the slip of the result of the theoretical examination upon leaving the examination centre, pursuant to which he shall either sit for a new theoretical examination in the event of failure after paying the re-examination fee, or proceed to the stage of the practical examination within a period of one week at most in the event of passing.

2- The practical driving examination shall be conducted in accordance with conditions determined by a decision of the Council upon the proposal of the Committee.

The examination may be conducted on vehicles owned by the licence applicant or one of his ascendants or descendants.

Every candidate who fails to sit for the theoretical or practical examination at the place and date specified for him for any reason whatsoever shall forfeit the amount of the fee fixed for the examination.

1- The Committee shall prepare at the beginning of every year new theoretical driving examinations for each category.

2- The Committee shall submit to the Council an annual report during the month of December of every year on the outcome of the conduct of the theoretical examinations.

1- The Minister of Interior and Municipalities shall appoint, whenever the need arises, the presidents and members of the practical driving examination committees from among:

- Employees of the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities holding a university degree.

- Personnel of the Internal Security Forces holding a university degree.

- Personnel of the Internal Security Forces who have served in traffic detachments for a period of at least five years.

- Retired personnel of the Security Forces holding a university degree.

It shall be required that these persons be of attested competence and discipline, have at least ten years of actual service, and hold a driving licence for no less than five years, after having undergone a competency competition in accordance with a training curriculum and examination specifications determined by the Council and conducted by the Institute mentioned in the following Article.

2- The presidents and members of the practical driving examination committees shall receive, when conducting examinations, allowances the value of which shall be determined by a decision of the Council upon a proposal by the Committee.

The employees assigned to conduct the theoretical examination shall also receive appropriate allowances in accordance with the provisions governing allowances for overtime work.

3- The detailed rules for the application of this Article shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities.

There shall be established within the Internal Security Forces an institute specialised in preparation and training in traffic policing, accidentology, traffic safety and culture, and driving, the missions and powers of which shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon a proposal by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities after consulting the Command Council of the Internal Security Forces.

If the licence applicant fails the theoretical driving examination, he may pay the re-examination fee and sit for a new theoretical examination after at least two weeks.

However, if the licence applicant fails the practical driving examination, he shall be prohibited from sitting for a new practical examination before the expiry of a period of one month from the date of the first examination and one month from the date of the examinations following it, within a period of six months from the date of submitting the application for the first examination, after paying the re-examination fee for each retake, under pain of forfeiture of his right to retake the examination after the expiry of the six-month period.

No fee shall be refunded, even in part, to a licence applicant who fails the examination.

1- The examination shall be deemed null and void ipso jure if the applicant for the licence sits for it:

a- During one of the periods mentioned in Article 219 above, and he shall be fined double the value of the examination and licence fee.

b- During the period in which the driver is not entitled to drive a vehicle following the issuance of an administrative decision or a judicial judgment withdrawing his previous licence, and he shall be fined three times the value of the examination and licence fee.

c- If the applicant submits false statements relating to his identity, or if he substitutes another person in his place for the examination or attempts to substitute him, and he shall be fined ten times the value of the examination and licence fee.

2- Every driving licence obtained by the applicant in any of the cases mentioned above shall be immediately withdrawn administratively, without prejudice to the necessary criminal prosecutions against him.

1- If the result of the applicant for the licence in the practical examination is positive, the Committee shall draw up a record thereof within two days and refer it to the competent service, and the successful candidate shall be entitled to obtain a driving licence of the category or categories mentioned in his application within a period of one week at most.

2- The requested licence shall be issued on the form specified in the Licence Format Annex attached to this Law after verifying the absence of any legal impediment.

1- The validity period of a driving licence may be shortened pursuant to a report by the Medical Committee if it appears that the applicant therefor suffers from a health impediment that does not currently prevent him from driving but may worsen thereafter.

2- If it appears after the delivery of the licence that its holder suffers from a temporary or permanent health impediment that is incompatible with the medical conditions for obtaining the licence, the competent service shall temporarily withdraw the licence and refer its holder to the Medical Committee, which shall submit a report to cancel it permanently or to determine its validity period for a specified period.

3- The Medical Committee shall be appointed by a decision of the Minister of Interior and Municipalities upon the proposal of the Committee.

A driving licence shall be dated and numbered in accordance with the order of its issuance and its registration in the Register of Issued Driving Licences, and the following shall be recorded in this Register and on the licence:

1- A coloured photograph of the driver.

2- The driver's first name and surname in the Arabic and Latin scripts

3- His place and date of birth in the Arabic and Latin scripts.

4- The names of his parents.

5- The place of his civil registration of residence and the register number according to the identity card.

6- Blood type.

7- The date of licensing of the licensed driving category or categories.

8- Special restrictions on the licence: in accordance with the provisions of Articles 201, 212 and 222 of this Law.

9- The expiry date.

10- A coded field containing the remaining information set out in the driver's register.

The holder of a driving licence shall notify the competent service, either in person or through the postal operator, of any change in his residential address within one month at most, in accordance with items "b" of the first and second paragraphs of Article 210 of this Law.

An application for the renewal of a driving licence shall be submitted within fifteen days prior to the date of expiry of its validity, and the old licence shall be accompanied by a coloured photograph dating back no more than three months or an instant photograph taken by the competent service, a medical certificate specific to driving, and a judicial record extract dating back less than three months.

The licence shall be issued after verifying the settlement of the fines adjudicated for violating the provisions of the Traffic Law, and the payment of the fees prescribed therefor.

If a driving licence is lost, its holder may obtain a copy thereof after submitting a certified true copy of an investigation report drawn up before the Internal Security Forces or before the Lebanese consulate in the country in which it was lost, provided that the lost licence is surrendered to the competent service in the event that it is found.

On the basis of military driving licences granted by the competent authorities in the armed forces of all ranks, such persons may be granted private or public driving licences for the category of vehicles indicated in their permits without subjecting them to the prescribed examination, after collecting the licence fee provided for in the schedule of fees annexed to this Law.

The holder of a foreign driving licence issued by the States party to the Geneva Convention of 1949 and the Vienna Convention of 1968 may obtain a Lebanese driving licence, provided that he fulfils the conditions specified in Article 223 of this Law, and the replacement shall be within the period of validity of the licence only and subject to reciprocity.

The provisions of this Chapter shall not apply to:

1- Drivers holding an international driving licence for the category of motor vehicles specified in their licences.

2- Drivers holding driving licences of the model specified in Annex 9 to the International Convention on Road Traffic concluded at Geneva on 19 September 1949, and within the period of validity of the licence.

3- Drivers of armed forces vehicles, who must carry driving permits issued to them by their administrations, provided that such permits shall only be valid for driving armed forces vehicles.

4- Drivers who enter Lebanon and carry foreign driving licences other than those specified in the preceding first and second paragraphs, provided that they obtain, within one week of their entry into Lebanon, from the competent department, an endorsement on their licences authorising them to use them within Lebanese territory for a period of six months, renewable once for a further period of six months, if the validity of the licence so permits.

The endorsement may be obtained through the postal operator.

5- Drivers who carry driving licences issued to them by countries with which a special agreement is concluded.

International driving and circulation licences:

The competent department and the legally licensed Lebanese automobile and touring clubs shall undertake the issuance of international driving licences in accordance with the approved models under the following conditions:

1- That the applicant for the licence holds a driving licence in accordance with the provisions of the Traffic Law, and that the licence is valid.

2- That the international driving licence is issued according to the categories held by the applicant for the licence in his Lebanese licence.

3- That the duration of the international licence is one year, and an international licence issued in Lebanon shall not authorise its holder to drive vehicles within Lebanese territory.

The Lebanese automobile and touring clubs authorised to issue international driving licences and international circulation licences must register the licences they issue in a special register in which shall be recorded the serial number of the issued licence and the date of its issuance, and the number and date of issuance of the original licence issued by the competent authorities, and the licensing authority shall be notified of these schedules within a period not exceeding three months from the date of issuance, and the licensing authority may verify the validity of the procedures followed.

The international circulation permit shall be issued by the competent service and the legally licensed Lebanese automobile and touring clubs on the approved forms under the following conditions:

1- That the vehicle for which the international circulation permit is requested is registered in Lebanon bearing a registration certificate.

2- That the driver of the vehicle holds an international driving licence valid for driving this vehicle.

3- That the duration of the permit is one year. The permit may be renewed for a similar duration under the same conditions.

The entity that issued the carnet shall notify the licensing authority with which the vehicle is registered of the carnets it issues and of the data relating to the vehicle, and such data shall be noted in the records of the vehicle. The licensing authority shall have the right to verify the validity of these carnets and their data.

Legally licensed automobile clubs shall pay the fees due by them for the benefit of the Treasury quarterly and within the fifteen days following each quarter of the year, pursuant to collection orders issued by the Indirect Taxes Department at the Ministry of Finance.

Every violation in the payment of the collected fees shall subject the violating club to a fine of ten percent of the value of the fees due for each month of delay, a fraction of a month being considered a full month, provided that the value of the imposed fine does not exceed the full amount of the fees due, and the authorisation may be revoked in the event of repetition of the violation.

Driving Instructor:

1- No person may teach or train another person to drive a motor vehicle, in closed grounds designated for instruction or on parts of public roads designated for instruction or on public roads, unless he is licensed to teach the driving of that category and is carrying the instruction licence while performing his work.

2- A driving instructor may not allow the trainee to drive a motor vehicle on public roads outside the basic training areas unless he has successfully passed the basic theoretical and practical training at the driving school, in accordance with the specifications, curricula and conditions determined by the Council.

3- The instructor is prohibited from accompanying any person other than the trainee in the vehicle designated for instruction during training.

The Trainee:

1- No trainee may learn to drive motor vehicles in training grounds designated for instruction, or on parts of roads designated for instruction, or on public roads, except in the company of a driving instructor.

2- The trainee shall carry with him during the stages of training a training permit from the driving school.

3- The trainee on public roads shall carry with him a certificate from the driving school stating that he has successfully completed the basic theoretical and practical instruction.

The Training Ground:

1- Closed grounds shall be considered as places for basic practical driving training, and in the absence thereof, parts of public roads shall be designated for this purpose by a decision of the competent Governor, and they shall be selected and changed according to the development of the volume and density of traffic thereon, provided that standard traffic safety conditions are met therein with respect to road markings and signs, traffic signals, safety barriers on both sides of the road, and others.

2- The specifications of closed training grounds or parts of public roads, for individual and multi-vehicle training, as well as the maximum number of training vehicles according to their areas, shall be determined.

3- The details of the implementation of this Article shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Interior and Municipalities upon the proposal of the Committee.

The Instructor's Licence:

In order to obtain an instructor's licence for teaching the driving of vehicles, it is required to submit an application to the competent Department accompanied by the following:

1- An individual civil status extract proving that he has been Lebanese for more than ten years.

2- Three coloured passport photographs dating back less than three months.

3- A copy of a valid public driving licence covering the category of vehicles on which he undertakes instruction.

4- A Technical Superior Certificate (TS) or its equivalent in a traffic specialisation issued by the Directorate General of Vocational and Technical Education.

The curriculum of this specialisation shall be determined by a decision of the Director General of Vocational and Technical Education pursuant to the minutes of the technical committee that he forms for this purpose after the approval of the National Traffic Safety Committee.

5- A certificate of passing a course for the category of vehicle which he is authorised to train on, the curriculum and method of obtaining of which shall be determined by a decision of the Council.

6- A medical certificate specific to driving.

7- A judicial record dating back not more than three months showing that he has not been convicted of any felony or disgraceful misdemeanour.

8- A traffic record free of violations of the fifth, fourth and third categories during two years from the date of submitting the application.

9- A certificate of tax registration.

Instruction Register:

1- The school shall keep an instruction register stamped by the competent department, in which shall be recorded, under serial numbers, the name of the student, his address, the date of his registration therewith, the number of hours of basic theoretical and practical instruction, the number of hours of practical training on public roads, and the number and date of issuance of the instruction certificate. The school shall produce this register upon every request from the competent department.

2- The school shall provide its trainee with a training certificate signed by the director of the school and stamped with the seal of the school, to be attached to the examination application.

1- A register for the supervision of driving schools shall be allocated in the competent department, in which shall be recorded the names of the persons licensed to open a driving school, the numbers of their licences, and the violations committed by them, and in which shall also be recorded the names of the licensed driving instructors and the violations committed by them.

2- This register shall be presented to the head of the competent department whenever the need arises.

3- In the event that the school violates the driving instruction curriculum issued by a decision of the Council, the competent department shall warn the violating school in writing to rectify its situation within a period not exceeding one month; in the event of repetition or continuation of the violation, the head of the competent department may suspend the effect of the school's licence for a maximum period of one month; and in the event of repetition of the violation, the licence shall be permanently revoked and the violating school shall be fined an amount of 15 million Lebanese pounds.

In the event that it is proven that the school has issued an incorrect instruction certificate as regards failing to train the student, manipulating the number of training hours, or failing to train him in the full curriculum, the violating school shall be fined an amount of 20 million Lebanese pounds for each certificate, and in the event of repetition, the fine shall be doubled and the school's licence shall be permanently revoked.

1- Driving instruction offices licensed prior to the issuance of this Law shall fulfil all the licensing conditions for driving schools and instructors provided for in this Chapter within a maximum period of one year from the date of issuance of the implementing decisions relating thereto, with the exception of paragraphs 4 and 5 of Article 237 of this Law.

2- Driving instructors licensed prior to the issuance of this Law shall be qualified through courses determined by the Committee.

The instructor shall renew his licence annually at the competent department in person or through the postal operator, provided that he attaches to the renewal application the expired licence, a medical certificate, and a copy of the judicial record extract and the traffic record.

For opening a motor vehicle driving school, it shall be required that the location of the school be at a distance of no less than one hundred metres (100 m) from another driving school within administrative Beirut and 250 metres (250 m) in the remaining places, and that no profession other than driving instruction be practised in the rooms of the school. The school must contain at least two halls, one designated for teaching, the specifications of which shall be determined by a decision issued by the Council.

The school shall also be entitled to open other branches, provided that each branch fulfils the conditions imposed on the school itself.

Vehicles designated for driving instruction shall be equipped in accordance with unified standards and criteria issued by a decision of the Council, and the equipment must not be less than:

1- Additional brakes in front of the instructor's seat and an additional rear-view mirror for the instructor.

2- A sign indicating that it is designated for training.

3- Two warning signs placed on the front and rear windscreens, to alert road users that a trainee is driving the vehicle.

Motor vehicle driving school licence:

The licensing application for a vehicle driving school shall be submitted by the person concerned in person to the competent department, accompanied by the following:

1- A certified true copy of the identity card or an individual civil status extract dating back to three months at most.

2- A certificate from the competent department proving his practice of the profession of driving instructor for three consecutive years.

3- A title deed or a lease contract in addition to a real estate certificate and a survey map determining the location of the school, with a building map showing the teaching halls and the place of the equipment.

4- A list of the number of vehicles designated and equipped for driving instruction, in accordance with the provisions of the preceding Article of this Law, provided that their number is not less than two vehicles.

A copy of the road tax receipt and the material and bodily insurance receipt for each vehicle shall be attached to this list.

The school licence shall be granted within a period of one month at most after the inspection conducted by the competent department.

The licence shall be renewed annually by the person concerned in person or through the postal operator at the competent department, and the renewal application shall be accompanied by the two schedules of the vehicles used for instruction and the instructors employed at the school, in addition to a copy of the road tax receipt and the material and bodily insurance receipt for each vehicle.

1- The provisions of this Part shall apply to the vehicles defined in paragraphs 14 to 17 and items "c" and "d" of paragraph 18 of Article Two of this Law.

2- Public works vehicles, in terms of manufacturing, differ in their frame (chassis) from the frames of conventional motor vehicles specified in Article 175 of this Law.

They are vehicles that are self-propelled, towed, or trailed, and are equipped with tyres or metal tracks and with special equipment designated for work on public roads and in workshops and projects, and they are not used for transporting materials, goods, and persons on roads.

3- Public works vehicles may be equipped with a number of seats not exceeding three, including the driver, to carry out the works for which they are designed.

4- The technical specifications of public works vehicles do not allow their speed on a flat road to exceed 40 km/h if they are equipped with pneumatic tyres and 15 km/h if they are equipped with other tyres or metal tracks.

5- The following shall be considered public works vehicles and equipment, by way of example and without limitation: vehicles used for demolishing, constructing, maintaining, and equipping public facilities, infrastructure, and the like, and among these vehicles are: vehicles for snow ploughing, earth trenching, spreading gravel and asphalt, compacting (rolling) and sweeping roads, and the like of these vehicles, and vehicles for lifting and moving objects on public roads and the like.

6- The Minister of Interior and Municipalities may subject to some of the provisions of this Part certain special vehicles whose speed by manufacture does not exceed twenty-five kilometres per hour, and may specify other vehicles if he deems it necessary on the grounds that they are not covered by paragraph 5 of this Article.
The provisions of Article 81 of this Law shall apply to agricultural and public works vehicles and equipment.
The provisions of Article 86 of this Law shall apply to agricultural and public works vehicles.
The provisions of Articles 87, 88, 90, and 91 of this Law shall apply to agricultural tractors, mobile machinery, and public works equipment.

Agricultural vehicles and equipment and mobile public works equipment must be fitted with a warning device whose intensity shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Interior and Municipalities.
The provisions of Articles 94 and 95 of this Law shall apply to agricultural vehicles and equipment and public works vehicles and their equipment.

If agricultural vehicles and equipment are not equipped with pneumatic tyres, their pressure on the ground shall not exceed at any time one hundred and fifty kilograms per square centimetre of the width of the tyre.

The Minister of Interior and Municipalities shall determine the characteristics and specifications that must be met in the metallic tyres with which agricultural vehicles and equipment and public works vehicles and their equipment are equipped, the traction chains that are used when necessary, and the height of their pneumatic tyres.
Equipment and tractors equipped with tracks may not be driven on public roads.

If the driver's range of vision in every direction is insufficient to enable him to drive in complete safety, another person must guide him to proceed in safety.

The provisions of paragraphs 3, 4 and 5 of Article 101 of this Law shall apply to mobile agricultural tractors and public works equipment.

However, the rear-view mirror mentioned in paragraph 5 of Article 101 is not necessary on vehicles and equipment not equipped with an enclosed driver's cabin.

Agricultural tractors shall be subject to the provisions of paragraph 4 of Article 101, and if one of these vehicles is equipped with a windscreen, it must be fitted with a windscreen wiper.

1- The provisions of Articles 104 to 115 of this Law shall apply to agricultural vehicles and equipment and public works vehicles and their equipment when moving or standing on roads at night and during fog.

2- The provisions of Article 108 of this Law shall apply to towed agricultural vehicles and equipment and public works vehicles when moving or standing on roads at night and during fog.

If the conditions stipulated in Article 108 are not met in these vehicles and equipment, they may be illuminated by means of a lamp with a red light placed on their left side.

If the width of mobile agricultural machinery or towed agricultural machinery or equipment or the width of mobile and towed public works equipment exceeds two metres and sixty-five centimetres, the towing vehicle must bear at the top of its front a square panel illuminated at night and visible from the front and from the rear of the vehicle up to a distance of one hundred and fifty metres, without being dazzling to the sight, and it must display in white on a black background the word "Danger" with a height of at least thirty centimetres.

If the panel is not visible from the rear of the vehicle or the combination, the last towed vehicle must bear at its rear a light-reflecting device displaying, in white on a black background, the word "Danger" with the same dimensions mentioned above.

Agricultural vehicles or equipment or public works equipment may, in order to facilitate their work at night, be fitted with lighting devices other than the devices mentioned in this Chapter, and these devices may not be used on the roads.

The Ministers of Interior and Municipalities and of Public Works and Transport shall determine by a decision issued by them the characteristics that must be met in the lighting and signalling devices placed on agricultural vehicles and equipment, and public works equipment, and where necessary their location, and the conditions for their installation in order to become compliant with the provisions of this Chapter, and they may prohibit the use of devices that do not conform to the prescribed devices.

The provisions of Articles 133 to 137 of this Law shall apply to agricultural vehicles and equipment and to their trailers and semi-trailers.

The provisions of Articles 128 to 131 of this Law shall also apply to trailers and semi-trailers.
The provisions of Article 138 (dimensions of vehicles) of this Law shall apply to agricultural vehicles and equipment and public works equipment only when they are travelling on public roads.
The movable or easily detachable parts of the vehicles or equipment mentioned in this Part shall be folded inwards while travelling on the public road.

The provisions of Article 139 of this Law shall apply to agricultural vehicles and equipment and public works equipment, and public works equipment shall be exempted from the provisions of paragraphs 3 and 6 of Article 139 of this Law if the width of their load does not in any case exceed the width of the towing vehicle.
The provisions of Article 141 of this Law shall apply to agricultural trailers, towed agricultural machinery and equipment, and towed public works equipment.
The provisions of Article 142 of this Law shall apply to motor vehicles designated for agriculture and public works.

The provisions of Article 144, 145, 154 and 155 of this Law shall apply to agricultural vehicles and equipment and public works vehicles and their equipment, provided that only one registration plate is affixed to the rear.

Agricultural vehicles and equipment and public works equipment shall be fitted with an identification plate called an "exploitation plate" indicating the type of work it performs, and it shall be affixed to the rear end of the vehicle in a visible and non-removable manner.
The provisions of Articles 149 to 153 of this Law shall apply to agricultural vehicles and equipment intended for testing or export abroad.

The models of this plate and the manner of its installation shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Interior and Municipalities, on the basis that it is readable by speed monitoring radars and by the naked eye.
The Minister of Interior and Municipalities shall determine the conditions for applying this Section to public works equipment if the need arises.
The provisions of Articles 156, 157, 158, 160 and 172 of this Law shall apply to agricultural and public works vehicles and equipment.

Agricultural vehicles and equipment and public works vehicles, their equipment and their trailers shall be subject, while travelling on the roads, to an emergency mechanical inspection conducted by the competent administration.

Agricultural vehicles and equipment and public works vehicles and their equipment shall be subject to the provisions of Articles 163 to 173 of this Law and shall be registered as private, provided that the provisions of Articles 184 and 186 of this Law shall apply thereto when towing the trailer.

The Minister of Interior and Municipalities may exempt from Article 273 of this Law certain agricultural vehicles and equipment and public works vehicles and their equipment owned by the State, municipalities, and public institutions.

Every motor vehicle with two or three wheels whose unladen weight does not exceed four hundred kilograms, as well as every vehicle of this type with four wheels specially manufactured to be driven by persons with special needs, shall be considered a motorcycle.

Every motor vehicle with four wheels whose unladen weight exceeds four hundred kilograms, and which is deemed equivalent to a car, or whose unladen weight is less than four hundred kilograms, and which is deemed equivalent to a motorcycle, shall be considered an ATV vehicle.

Its operation on or off the public road shall be determined according to the manufacturer's specifications, provided that this is stated on the vehicle circulation permit.

1 -

The importation of used motorcycles with an engine capacity below 125 cc is prohibited.

2- The importation of used motorcycles with an engine capacity exceeding 125 cc and used ATV vehicles over three years from the date of their manufacture is prohibited.

3- Excluded from the provisions of this Article are motorcycles of an antique nature over thirty years from their manufacture.

4- The importation of new and used motorcycles and ATV vehicles shall be carried out exclusively by:

a- Company agents.

b- Merchants registered in the Commercial Register to engage in the trade of cars, motorcycles, and "ATV" vehicles.

c- A Lebanese or foreign national who owns a motorcycle or an "ATV" vehicle registered in his name in the country in which he resides may bring in the motorcycle or the ATV in compliance with the legal rules for importation.
It is prohibited to drive motorcycles without obtaining a driving licence specific thereto, and without the driver and the pillion passenger properly and securely wearing protective helmets.
It is prohibited to perform acrobatic manoeuvres while driving motorcycles on public roads, such as riding on one wheel, standing on the seat while in motion, or weaving between vehicles.
It is prohibited to use and park motorcycles on sidewalks or lanes designated for pedestrians and for other categories of road users.

1- A two-wheeled motorcycle must be fitted with a stand to maintain its balance while stationary.

2- Another person shall not be permitted to ride behind the rider of the motorcycle unless it is fitted, according to its original design, with a dedicated securely fastened seat and a footrest on each side designated to support the passenger's leg, provided that the age of the other passenger is not less than ten years.

3- It is prohibited to equip motorcycles with a box for carrying goods unless the manufacturer has authorised this, and provided that it conforms to the measurements and dimensions specified by the manufacturer, is securely fastened and fitted with suitable and sufficient vibration dampers, and that this is recorded on the circulation permit.
Engine system The provisions of Articles 88 and 89 of this Law shall apply to the vehicles mentioned in this Part.
Fuel tank The provisions of Article 90 of this Law shall apply to the vehicles mentioned in this Part.

A bicycle shall be deemed to be any vehicle with two, three or four wheels not equipped with an engine, and either propelled by the power of its rider.
Riders of bicycles are prohibited from riding abreast except when overtaking, and they must permanently keep to the far right of the carriageway and in a straight course.
Where a section of the road is designated for the traffic of bicycles, riders of such bicycles must keep to that section.

Bicycles may ride on places designated for pedestrians subject to the approval of the competent authorities pursuant to a decision issued in this regard, and the rider of the bicycle must ride at walking pace and not cause inconvenience to pedestrians.

Two-wheeled bicycles may travel on pavements and pathways designated for pedestrians on paved roads outside populated areas that are under maintenance. In such case, riders shall travel at a moderate pace near houses and at walking pace when encountering pedestrians.

Riders of two-wheeled bicycles shall be prohibited from carrying a second person with them unless the bicycle is designed by its manufacturer to carry more than one person; however, it shall be permitted to be fitted with a basket intended for carrying certain items whose weight does not exceed twenty-five kilograms.

If the other passenger is under the age of five years, the bicycle shall be fitted with a special child seat securely attached to the bicycle, and the rider shall ensure that the feet of the other passenger do not become caught between the fixed and moving parts of the bicycle.
A bicycle shall be fitted with two effective brakes.

By night, and by day where circumstances so require, a bicycle shall be fitted at the front with a single front position lamp emitting a non-dazzling light forward, and at the rear with a rear position lamp visible from behind.

Bicycles may be moved on public roads without a light if they are pushed by hand, in which case the rider shall comply with the regulations imposed on pedestrians.

1- A bicycle shall be fitted, by night and by day, at the rear with one or more reflectors emitting a non-dazzling red light to the rear.

2- A bicycle shall be fitted with a white reflector at the front.
Where a bicycle has three wheels and includes a side basket designated for carrying certain items, the outermost edge of the basket shall be fitted with a non-dazzling red position light.
A bicycle shall be fitted with a warning device (a bell) or a "trilling bell" audible at a distance of at least 25 metres, and the use of any other warning device shall be prohibited.

Draught, pack or riding animals, for individual livestock or herds, must have a number of drovers in accordance with the following rate:

1- Ten heads of sheep and goats or fewer, or three heads of cattle and others or fewer: at least one drover.

2- From eleven to twenty heads of sheep, or from four to ten heads of cattle and others: at least two drovers.

3- For every fifty heads of sheep and goats or for every twenty heads of cattle and others in excess of the preceding rates: one additional drover.

The driving of herds and individual or grouped animals walking on the road must be ensured in a manner that does not result in any obstruction to public traffic. In all cases, drovers of animals must keep to the right side of the carriageway.

Drovers of herds and individual or grouped animals must indicate them, especially at the rear thereof, with a hand-held light that is clearly visible at night, outside inhabited areas whose roads are lit, and these provisions shall not apply to horsemen or to handlers of animals walking on roads not used by motor vehicles.

It is prohibited to leave animals straying on the public road, and it is prohibited for herds of livestock to stand on the public road, and their driving must be organised in a manner that makes crossing, meeting or overtaking them possible without obstructing traffic.

Except for the cases set out in Articles 140 and 321 of this Law, there may not be hitched:

1- To vehicles used for the transport of goods: more than five horses or draught animals if the vehicle has two wheels, and more than eight horses or other draught animals if the vehicle has four wheels, provided that in the latter case there are no more than five animals in tandem.

2- To vehicles used for the transport of persons: more than three horses if the vehicle has two wheels and more than six if the vehicle has four wheels.
If the number of draught animals exceeds six or is more than five animals in tandem, an assistant must be added to the driver.
The provisions of the first paragraph of Article 318 of this Law relating to limiting the number of animals shall not apply to sections of roads whose gradient is exceptional.
A single driver may drive a convoy of animal-drawn vehicles, provided that the number of such vehicles does not exceed three.
If the driver is not walking on foot, he must be on the first vehicle.
If the convoy consists of two vehicles only, the number of draught animals may not exceed four for the first vehicle and two for the second vehicle.
If the convoy consists of three vehicles, the first vehicle only may be drawn by two animals, and each of the second and third vehicles must be drawn by a single animal.

The animals drawing the second vehicle and the third vehicle must be tethered to the rear of the preceding vehicle in a manner that keeps the cart drawn by them from deviating appreciably from the line in which the preceding cart is travelling.
A vehicle drawn by animals must be equipped with a special device for reducing speed and for stopping.

If the wheels of an animal-drawn vehicle are not equipped with rubber tyres, their pressure on the ground must not exceed, at any time, one hundred and fifty kilograms per single square centimetre of the width of the tyre.
There must be no protrusion on the face of metal tyres in contact with the ground, and it is prohibited for metal parts forming a protrusion to be introduced onto the flat surface of the tyres.

1- Vehicles drawn by animals must be equipped during the night and during the day, when circumstances so require and especially in time of fog, with the following devices:

a- At the front, one or two lights emitting a white or yellow light to the front.

b- At the rear, one or two lights emitting a red light to the rear.

2- These lights must be visible at night and in clear weather, at a distance of one hundred and fifty metres, without dazzling the sight of other drivers.

Where there are two lights with white light or two lights with red light, they must be placed symmetrically in relation to the vehicle, and where there is only one white light, or one red light, it must be placed on the left of the vehicle when it is in motion, and on the side opposite to the pavement or to the side of the road when it is stationary.

Signalling may be effected by a single light placed on the side opposite to the pavement or to the side of the road, emitting a white light to the front and a red light to the rear, in the following vehicles:

(a) Carts drawn by hand.

(b) All animal-drawn vehicles having a single axle.

(c) Animal-drawn vehicles assigned for an agricultural purpose.

It must be mounted on the vehicle or carried by hand by an escort positioned immediately to the left of the vehicle.

(d) All other animal-drawn vehicles when stationary, provided that their length does not exceed six metres.

When several animal-drawn vehicles are travelling in a convoy under the conditions specified in Articles 321 to 325 of this Law, the first vehicle of each group composed of two or three consecutive vehicles without separation must be equipped with one or two lights (white or yellow) and the last vehicle with one red light or two lights referred to in Articles 329 and 330 of this Law.

As for the vehicle located in the middle, it shall be exempted from all lighting.
Animal-drawn vehicles must carry at their rear, under the conditions set forth in the first paragraph of Article 329 of this Law, two reflectors reflecting a red light.

If the length of the vehicle, including the load, exceeds six metres or if its width exceeds two metres, these reflectors must be placed at the outer limits of the vehicle and it must be equipped at its front with two reflectors placed at its outer limits and reflecting a white light to the front.
Handcarts must carry at their rear a reflector reflecting a red light placed on their left at a distance not exceeding forty centimetres from the outer limit of the cart including its load.

The lights and reflectors mentioned in Articles 329 to 335 of this Law must be mounted in such a manner that no part of the vehicle or of its load can lead to obscuring them wholly or partially, and consequently to limiting their effect.

Every vehicle driver who causes an accident, even if material, and does not stop immediately or does not attend to the victim or attempts to evade liability by fleeing, shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year and by a fine from one million to three million pounds, and six points shall be deducted from him.

1- Every driver who, while driving a vehicle, causes the death of a human being through negligence, lack of precaution, or non-observance of laws or regulations, shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years and by a fine from one million to three million Lebanese pounds.

2- The penalty shall be increased to imprisonment for four years and a fine of up to six million Lebanese pounds if:

a) The driver was in a state of manifest drunkenness or under the influence of alcohol at a rate exceeding 0,8 g/l in the blood, after undergoing the test, or if the alcohol level in the exhaled air is equivalent to the rate mentioned above, or if the driver refused to undergo the required tests intended to determine whether the driver is under the influence of alcohol.

b) It is shown in blood analyses that the driver has consumed any type of narcotic substances, or if he refused to undergo the required tests intended to determine whether he had consumed narcotics.

c) The driver did not hold a driving licence, or if the driving licence was revoked, withdrawn, or invalid.

d) The driver had exceeded the maximum permitted speed by more than 50 km/h.

e) The driver did not stop despite being aware that he caused an accident and attempted to evade the criminal or civil liability incumbent upon him.

f) The driver committed any deliberate violation of one of the duties of caution and safety provided for in this Law and in the laws in force.

3- The penalty of imprisonment shall be increased to up to five years and the fine to up to twelve million Lebanese pounds when the driver of the vehicle has committed three or more of the six cases mentioned in the second paragraph of this Article.

4- In the two cases provided for in items (2) and (3) of this Article, the following measures shall be taken:

- The driving licence shall be revoked with a prohibition from obtaining a new licence from two to four years from the date the judgment becomes final.

- The convicted person shall undergo a special course on traffic safety awareness at his own expense.

The vehicle used by the convicted person shall be impounded for a maximum period of one year, in the event that it is owned by him.

Animal-drawn vehicles carrying trees or pieces extending beyond the rear of the vehicle must bear by day, at the rear of the load, a crimson red flag measuring not less than 30 (by) 20 centimetres, and by night, a lamp emitting a non-dazzling red light.

The provisions of Article 138 of this Law shall apply to animal-drawn vehicles.

Every other animal-drawn vehicle whose body or mudguard does not protrude beyond the wheel must not have the most protruding part of its axle end, wheel hub, braking mechanisms, and all its accessory parts protruding more than twenty centimetres beyond the plane passing through the outer rim of its tyre.
The provisions of Article 139 of this Law shall apply to animal-drawn vehicles.
