1- If an accident occurs, the driver must stop his vehicle immediately; if the damage is purely material, he must stop and not resume driving until after he has disclosed to the aggrieved party his vehicle number, his name, and his address, together with the name and address of the vehicle owner, and he must request a sworn expert where necessary. In all cases, the colliding parties must immediately draw marks around the tyres to determine their position and then place the colliding vehicles off the carriageway, if the condition of the vehicle so permits, in order to clear the way for the passage of other road users.

2- If any person sustains bodily injury, the driver of the vehicle must immediately contact the emergency services to transport him to the nearest medical centre in order to provide him with the necessary first aid. The driver may not leave the scene of the accident permanently before the arrival of the emergency services or before the initiation of legal proceedings.

3- If the driver is exposed to any danger to his person or his vehicle as a result of remaining at the scene of the accident, he may leave the scene heading to the nearest Security Forces station, notify it of the matter, and return accompanied by it to the scene of the accident.

In this case, he shall not be punished for leaving the scene.

1- Any driver who, while driving a vehicle, causes harm to a person through negligence, lack of precaution, or non-observance of laws or regulations, resulting in incapacity for work for a period exceeding three months, shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to one year and by a fine from five hundred thousand to two million Lebanese pounds.

2- The penalty of imprisonment shall be increased up to one year and a half and the fine up to four million Lebanese pounds if one of the six cases provided for in paragraph (2) of Article 345 is fulfilled.

3- The penalty of imprisonment shall be increased up to two years and the fine up to six million Lebanese pounds when the driver of the vehicle has committed three or more of the six cases mentioned in paragraph (2) of Article 345.

4- In the two cases provided for in paragraphs (2) and (3) of this Article, the following measures shall be taken:

- The driving licence shall be cancelled, with a ban on obtaining a new licence for a period ranging between one year to two years from the date the judgment becomes final.

- The convicted person shall undergo a special course on traffic safety awareness at his own expense.

The vehicle used by the convicted person shall be impounded for a maximum period of one year, if it is his property.

1- Any driver who, while driving a vehicle, causes harm through negligence, lack of precaution, or non-observance of laws or regulations, resulting in incapacity for work for a period not exceeding three months, shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to six months and by a fine from two hundred thousand to one million Lebanese pounds.

2- The penalty of imprisonment shall be increased up to nine months and the fine up to two million Lebanese pounds in the event that one of the six cases mentioned in

paragraph (2) of Article 345 is fulfilled.

3- The penalty of imprisonment shall be increased up to one year and the fine up to three million Lebanese pounds when the driver of the vehicle has committed three or more of the six cases mentioned in paragraph (2) of Article 345.

4- In the two cases provided for in paragraphs (2) and (3) of this Article, the following measures shall be taken:

- The driving licence shall be cancelled, with a ban on obtaining a new licence for a period ranging from six months to one year from the date the judgment becomes final.

- The convicted person shall undergo a special course on traffic safety awareness at his own expense.

The vehicle used by the convicted person shall be impounded for a maximum period of three months, if it is his property.

1- It is prohibited to import motor vehicles that are unroadworthy and pose a danger to public safety, such as vehicles that have suffered collision damage to their main chassis or those that have been subjected to welding, splicing, fire, flooding or corrosion in a manner that affects their structural integrity or their alignment, as well as the importation of half-vehicles, whether their front halves or rear halves, in order to prevent their reassembly by welding or splicing upon entering Lebanese territory.

2- At the maritime and land ports of entry that receive used vehicles imported from abroad, special mechanical inspection centres shall be established to verify the conformity of these vehicles with the manufacturer's specifications, and the details for the implementation of this paragraph shall be determined by a decision issued by the Ministers of Finance, Interior and Municipalities, and Public Works and Transport.

3- Pending the establishment of these centres, the importer, when importing used vehicles, shall present to the Customs Administration the vehicle circulation permit and a certificate from a mechanical inspection centre from the country of export dated no more than two months prior to the date of actual shipment confirming its roadworthiness.

As for vehicles arriving from the United States of America, the importer shall present the vehicle circulation permit which determines its roadworthiness with respect to public safety or lack thereof (when the word "Salvage" or Reconstructed" is written thereon). As regards the importation of used vehicles from outside the countries mentioned above, either of the two models may be adopted depending on what is adopted in the exporting country.

4- If it is proven as a result of the technical inspection that the vehicle does not conform to the manufacturer's specifications, or if it becomes apparent to the Customs Administration that the data required in the third paragraph are incorrect, the importer shall be required to re-export the vehicle immediately at his own expense.

Motor cars under temporary admission shall, upon being registered for the first time, be subject to an ordinary and special mechanical inspection dating back to one month at most from the date of applying for registration.

Whoever violates the provisions of this Article shall be punished by a fine of three million to ten million Lebanese pounds, and the vehicle that is the subject of the violation shall be impounded.

1- For every motor vehicle that has been involved in a traffic accident and purchased by an insurance company after paying its value to its owner in accordance with the terms of the insurance contract, or any motor vehicle for which the traffic expert's report indicates that the traffic accident has affected it and that it has come to constitute a danger to public safety pursuant to the first paragraph of Article 348 of this Law, insurance companies and traffic experts shall notify the competent service in order to prohibit it from operating on the road until the presentation of both the regular and special mechanical inspection certificates for the purpose of verifying its roadworthiness prior to permitting it to operate on the road.

2- Any motor vehicle repair garage shall not repair any car that has been involved in an accident or collision except after notifying the traffic detachment within whose territorial jurisdiction the accident occurred.

3- Garages or owners of car scrapyards are prohibited from receiving any motor vehicle for the purpose of scrapping it except after the presentation of a salvage certificate signed by the competent service.

Whoever violates this Article shall be punished by imprisonment for up to three months and by a fine from three to ten million Lebanese pounds, and the vehicle shall be impounded.

In the event that public property is damaged as a result of a traffic accident, the Ministry of Public Works and Transport or the municipalities, depending on the location where the accident occurred, shall immediately proceed to repair the damage in order to preserve public safety.

The Ministry of Finance shall allocate the financial compensation collected in favour of the entity that carried out the repair of the damage.

The details of the implementation of this paragraph shall be determined by a decision issued by the Ministers of Interior and Municipalities, Finance, and Public Works and Transport.

1- Upon arriving at the scene of the accident, the expert shall abide by the requirements of public safety imposed by the laws and regulations, and shall draw up the technical report in accordance with criteria and a special form determined by a decision issued by the Ministers of Interior and Municipalities, Justice, and Economy and Trade, upon the proposal of the Committee.

2- A traffic accident expert shall hold a Technicien Supérieur diploma (TS) or its equivalent in a traffic specialization issued by the Directorate General of Vocational and Technical Education, provided that the curriculum of this specialization is determined by a decision of the Director General of Vocational and Technical Education on the basis of the minutes of the technical committee that he forms for this purpose after the approval of the National Road Safety Committee.

3- Candidates for traffic accident expertise shall pass a competency competition determined and supervised by the Ministry of Economy and Trade - Insurance Control Commission, after the approval of the Committee.

4- Traffic experts licensed prior to the issuance of this Law shall be qualified through courses determined and supervised by the Ministry of Economy and Trade - Insurance Control Commission in coordination with the two Ministries of Justice and after the approval of the Committee.

5- For the practice of the profession of expert, the provisions of Articles 41 and 42 of the Law Regulating Insurance Companies promulgated by Decree No. 9812 dated 4 May 1968 and its amendments shall be observed.

Insurance against bodily and material damages is compulsory for all cars and motor vehicles.

It is required that the insurance contract be issued by one of the insurance companies duly registered in Lebanon to practice motor vehicle insurance operations in accordance with the provisions of the law:

1- The expression bodily damages means: death and every bodily injury resulting from accidents, fires, or explosions caused by the vehicle, its parts, its pieces, or the tools or materials used in operating or moving it, or the objects or materials transported therein.

2- The expression material damages means: damages affecting the private and public property and assets of third parties, whatever their kind, resulting from accidents, fires, or explosions caused by the vehicle, its parts, its pieces, or the tools or materials used in operating or moving it, or the objects or materials transported therein.

3- Whoever fails to apply the provisions of this Article shall be punished by a fine of one million Lebanese pounds, the motor vehicle shall be impounded until the violation is removed, and three points shall be deducted from the violator.

The procedures and conditions to be followed in compulsory insurance on motor cars and motor vehicles, between individuals and companies, shall be determined pursuant to the provisions of Article 44 of the Law on the Regulation of Insurance Bodies promulgated by Decree No. 9812 dated 4 May 1968 and its amendments.

Work on applying the compulsory material damage insurance provided for in this Law shall commence after the issuance of the implementing decrees by the Council of Ministers.

A National Council for Traffic Safety shall be formed under the presidency of the President of the Council of Ministers, and in the event of his absence the Vice-President of the Council of Ministers shall preside over the Council, and with the membership of each of:

1- The Minister of Interior and Municipalities.

2- The Minister of Public Works and Transport.

3- The Minister of Justice.

4- The Minister of Education and Higher Education.

The President of the Council of Ministers may invite whomever he deems necessary when needed.

The Council shall lay down its internal regulations, which shall be approved by an absolute majority.

Its powers

The National Council for Traffic Safety shall exercise the following powers:

1- Formulating the general policy for traffic safety and overseeing its implementation.

2- Working on developing the Traffic Law.

3- Setting the frameworks and curricula for practical driving examinations.

4- Determining the qualifications of driving examiners and their qualification examinations.

5- Setting the examination for driving instructors.

6- Setting the curricula for instruction and training in driving schools.

7- Approving the curricula for competency competitions for candidates for traffic accident expertise.

8- Monitoring and supervising public and private institutions and administrations concerned with traffic affairs.

9- Organising and sponsoring media campaigns and activities relating to traffic safety, vehicle driving safety, and transport safety.

10- Issuing an annual report on its achievements and what has been accomplished in terms of traffic safety, and publishing it in the media.

1- The Council shall meet periodically once every three months, and whenever the need arises, at the invitation of its President.

2- Invitations shall be addressed and the agenda distributed by the Secretariat, three days prior to the date of the meeting.

1- The Council may seek the assistance of experts and entities whose participation therein it deems beneficial to its work and to the achievement of its objectives.

2- The Council may form, upon the proposal of the National Road Safety Committee, joint executive committees composed of public administrations and civil society associations in the governorates, in order to follow up on the implementation of its decisions at the level of the governorates and to submit recommendations to the Council through the Secretariat.

3- The Council may form, upon the proposal of the National Road Safety Committee, sub-committees to follow up on its work and the decisions it takes, and to study projects and proposals submitted to the Council.

A committee named the National Road Safety Committee shall be established, which shall report to the Council and be chaired by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities; it shall meet at least once a month at the call of its chairperson and whenever the need arises, and shall be composed of:

- The Director General of the Traffic, Trucks and Vehicles Management Authority.

- The Director General of Land and Maritime Transport.

- The Director General of Roads and Buildings.

- The Director General of Vocational and Technical Education.

- The Director General of the Ministry of Tourism.

- A judge specialised in traffic affairs representing the Ministry of Justice.

- An officer specialised in traffic affairs representing the Directorate General of the Internal Security Forces.

- A representative of the Council for Development and Reconstruction specialised in traffic engineering.

- A representative of the two Orders of Engineers specialised in traffic engineering.

- The President of the Land Transport Union.

- The President of the Syndicate of Driving Schools.

- The President of the Syndicate of Traffic Experts.

- The President of the Insurance Control Commission.

- The President of the Association of Insurance Companies.

- The President of the Automobile Importers' Association in Lebanon.

- Two representatives of non-governmental associations concerned with road safety, selected by the Chairperson of the Committee.

Any member of the Committee may delegate a person to represent them to attend any of the meetings, subject to the prior approval of the Minister of Interior and Municipalities.

Furthermore, the Minister of Interior and Municipalities may invite whomever he deems necessary to the meetings of the Committee.

Functions of the Committee The Committee shall assume the following functions:

1- Conducting studies and research to develop road safety and submitting them to the Council to take a decision thereon.

2- Submitting the necessary proposals to develop the Traffic Law and expressing an opinion on draft laws and regulatory decrees relating to road safety and amendments to the Traffic Law.

3- Proposing the curricula for practical driving examinations.

4- Establishing the theoretical driving examination.

5- Proposing the standards and qualifications of driving examiners and their qualification examinations.

6- Proposing the examinations of driving instructors.

7- Proposing the education and training curricula in driving schools.

8- Approving the curricula of the qualification courses for traffic experts licensed prior to the issuance of the Law.

9- Proposing curricula for road safety awareness in basic, intermediate and secondary education.

10- Proposing awareness campaigns and activities specific to road safety, safe driving and transport safety.

11- Following up and pursuing the repair of damages caused to public property on the roads resulting from traffic accidents or otherwise, in order to preserve public safety.

12- Submitting reports to the Council regarding traffic safety affairs.

13- Preparing the annual report on the achievements of the Council and what has been accomplished at the level of road safety.

The secretariat of the Council shall be assumed by a full-time secretary who has extensive experience in traffic affairs or holds a degree in traffic engineering, assisted by an administrative and technical body specialised in road safety, who are appointed by the President of the Council and report directly to the presidency of the Council.

The secretary shall participate in all the meetings held by the Council and the Committee.

Functions of the Secretariat The Secretariat shall exercise the following functions:

1- Issuing invitations to the meetings of the Council and preparing the agenda at the request of the President of the Council.

2- Issuing invitations to the meetings of the Committee and preparing the agenda.

3- Following up on the implementation of the decisions of the Council, and submitting reports thereon.

4- Drawing up minutes of the meetings of the Council and the Committee.

5- Coordinating and cooperating with public and private administrations and institutions, municipalities, and all other parties concerned with traffic affairs and road safety in order to apply the policies of the Council and achieve its objectives.

6- Executing the tasks assigned to it by the Council or the Committee.

7- Managing the affairs of the workers and employees in the Council and ensuring the proper functioning of the work.

8- Studying and utilising statistics on traffic accidents and black spots on public roads.

9- Determining the damage caused to public property on roads resulting from traffic accidents or otherwise, in preservation of public safety.

10- Receiving complaints and proposals submitted to the Council.
The details of the application of the provisions of this Part shall be determined by decisions issued by the Council by an absolute majority.

The points system shall apply to the violations set forth in this Law and the schedules of violations annexed hereto.

A computerised traffic record shall be established with the Internal Security Forces for each driver for the purpose of applying this system, and the acts relating to this system shall be of an administrative nature.

Every driver holding a valid driving licence shall be granted twelve points (12 points) as a balance in the traffic record.

These points shall be deducted in proportion to the violations committed as set forth in this Law and the schedules of violations annexed to this Law.

When the driver loses the total of his points, the driving licence shall lose its validity and shall be withdrawn from him for a period of six months during which the driver shall undergo a specialised course at one of the driving schools.

Upon the repetition of the loss of the total points within three years, the licence shall be withdrawn for a period of one year, provided that the offender undergoes the aforementioned course, in addition to retaking the driving examination.

This rule shall apply whenever the entirety of the points is withdrawn.

A driver who has lost the total points of his licence shall surrender it to the Internal Security Forces within a period not exceeding five days from the date he is notified of the loss of the total points.

After the lapse of two years from the date of payment of the fine or from the date of issuance of the final judgment without the driver committing any new violation on the basis of which points must be deducted, all deducted points shall be restored to him by operation of law.

Three points shall also be restored if one year passes without committing any violation on the basis of which points must be deducted.

With the exception of cases in which all points are withdrawn, when a driver commits several violations at the same time, the points shall be aggregated, provided that the number of points withdrawn does not exceed eight.

The details for the application of the points system shall be determined by a decision issued by the Council upon the proposal of the National Road Safety Committee.

In addition to their duties, the Traffic Judgments Enforcement Offices shall undertake the work of the traffic record for traffic violations, and these offices shall be linked directly, electronically and live (online), to the database and files at the competent administration.

The competent courts shall send to the Traffic Judgments Enforcement Offices the final and conclusive judgments issued in respect of these violations, as well as the ordinary and stamped reports that have been paid, after the expiry of the legal review periods, the competent courts shall send to the Traffic Judgments Enforcement Offices the final and conclusive judgments issued in respect of these violations, as well as the ordinary and stamped reports that have been paid, after the expiry of the legal review periods.

The Traffic Judgments Enforcement Office shall place an annotation on the file of the offending vehicle in the database of the competent administration, whereby the completion of transactions relating to the Traffic, Trucks and Vehicles Management Authority and its branches, and transactions relating to the payment of annual traffic fees conducted outside the centres of the competent administration and its branches in the governorates, shall be conditional upon proof that the file relating to the vehicle is free from any judgments in violation of the Traffic Law issued against it, and upon payment of what is due by it to remove the annotation.

The traffic record, documents, files and programmes through which information may be obtained regarding vehicle owners, drivers and offenders shall be deemed to be of a confidential nature.

Whoever proceeds to disclose the information shall be punished by imprisonment for six months and by a financial fine in the amount of one million Lebanese pounds.

There shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Justice and of Interior and Municipalities, and after consulting the opinion of the Committee, the public administrations, bodies and persons authorised to access these documents, files, programmes and records by reason of the nature of their function.
The penalties set forth in this Law, in addition to the penalties provided for in the Penal Code, shall apply to traffic violations.

Violations for which a record is drawn up shall be classified into the following categories:

- Category of pedestrian violations: The violations set forth in the Schedule of Pedestrian Violations annexed to this Law, which entail a pecuniary fine ranging between fifty thousand and one hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds.

- First category: The violations set forth in Schedule No. (1) annexed to this Law, which entail a financial fine ranging between one hundred thousand and one hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese Pounds.

- Second category: The violations set forth in Schedule No. (2) annexed to this Law, which entail a financial fine ranging between two hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds and three hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds.

- Third category: The violations set forth in Schedule No. (3) annexed to this Law, which entail a financial fine ranging between three hundred and fifty thousand and four hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese Pounds.

- Fourth category: The violations set forth in Schedule No. (4) annexed to this Law, which entail a financial fine ranging between five hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds and seven hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds.

- Fifth category: The violations set forth in Schedule No. (5) annexed to this Law, which entail imprisonment from one month to two years and a financial fine ranging between one million and three million Lebanese Pounds.

Points shall be deducted from offenders according to each violation as stated in the Schedules annexed to this Law.

1- Penalties, fines, and violations are set forth in this Law and in the Schedules of Violations annexed hereto.

2- Violations not provided for in the Schedules of Violations shall be deemed first category violations, with the exception of pedestrian violations, which are subject to the Schedule of Pedestrian Violations.

3- Violations of the provisions of decisions issued by administrative and municipal authorities in execution of the provisions of this Law shall likewise be deemed first category violations if they are not punishable under another text.

All traffic violations shall be drawn up in a stamped record, or by means of automated marking, with the exception of fifth category violations, violations that carry a penalty of imprisonment, and those that require the impoundment of the vehicle.

The value of stamped tickets or fines paid within thirty days from the date the ticket is drawn up or from the date the offender is notified where the ticket is drawn up in his absence shall be determined as follows:

- Pedestrian offence: twenty thousand pounds in the first 15 days. In the event of non-payment within this period, the value of the fine shall rise to thirty thousand pounds during the following 15-day period.

- First Category offence: fifty thousand pounds in the first 15 days. In the event of non-payment within this period, the value of the fine shall rise to seventy thousand pounds during the following 15-day period.

- Second Category offence: one hundred thousand pounds in the first 15 days. In the event of non-payment within this period, the value of the fine shall rise to one hundred and fifty thousand pounds during the following 15-day period.

- Third Category offence: two hundred thousand pounds in the first 15 days. In the event of non-payment within this period, the value of the fine shall rise to three hundred and fifty thousand pounds during the following 15-day period.

- Fourth Category offence: three hundred and fifty thousand pounds in the first 15 days. In the event of non-payment within this period, the value of the fine shall rise to four hundred and fifty thousand pounds during the following 15-day period.
Where another law punishes any of the acts punishable under this Law, the more severe penalty shall be applied.
An offence shall be deemed a single offence between the point of departure of the vehicle and the point towards which it is heading, unless it was possible to avoid the same offence while driving.

Every offence provided for in this Law or in Article 770 of the Penal Code shall render its perpetrator liable to double the penalty prescribed therefor if a final judgment has been issued against him within a period of one year at most for the very same offence, and upon every repetition within the said period this rule shall be applied, provided that the driving licence is withdrawn for a period of one month at least, without the doubling extending to the deduction of points.
The provisions of Article 254 of the Penal Code relating to mitigating causes shall not apply to the monetary penalties provided for in this Law.
The value of the fine due for any established offence may not, in the event of an objection, be reduced below the minimum limit prescribed in the categories of offences.

1- If the taximeter does not conform to the specified standards or is out of order, each of the owner of the car, its driver, and anyone whose complicity is proven shall be punished by a fine ranging between two hundred and fifty thousand and seven hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese pounds and by imprisonment from one month to three months, or by either of these two penalties, and the car shall be impounded until the violation is remedied, three points shall be deducted, and the penalty shall be doubled in the event of repetition.

2- The custodian of the vehicle and anyone whose complicity in the act of fraud is proven through introducing modifications to the taximeter so that it records prices exceeding the specified tariff shall be punished by a fine ranging between two million pounds and three million Lebanese pounds, and by imprisonment from three months to six months, or by either of these two penalties, and the car shall be impounded, six points shall be deducted, and the penalty shall be doubled in the event of repetition.

Anyone who undertakes an act with the aim of obstructing the operation of devices, equipment, or systems used to detect violations of traffic laws shall be punished by imprisonment for a period of two years and by a fine in the amount of ten million Lebanese pounds, in addition to compensation for the damages and harm caused to the devices and equipment.

Anyone who uses, while driving a motor vehicle, devices capable of detecting speed radars shall be punished by the deduction of six points, and by a fine in the amount of three million Lebanese pounds.

The annual fees imposed on vehicles shall be collected pursuant to payment orders issued by the competent administration, and the deadlines for paying these fees shall be determined by decisions issued by the Ministers of Interior and Municipalities and of Finance. As for vehicles whose owners fail to pay the fees due from them within the specified time limits, nominal schedules shall be drawn up for them, in which the address of the taxpayer, the number of the car, and the amount due shall be stated, according to each district (qada), in three copies:

- The original copy shall be deposited with the Ministry of Finance - Treasury Department - for the purpose of collecting the fees and fines incurred in accordance with the procedures for collecting direct taxes.

- The second copy shall be deposited with the Internal Security Forces to impound the vehicle.

- The third copy shall be retained by the competent administration.

1- It is prohibited for anyone other than the concerned parties, their ascendants, their descendants, or those legally authorised by them, to enter the competent Administration and its branches for the purpose of carrying out any transaction.

2- The concerned parties shall send their transactions to the competent Administration through the postal operator if the type of transaction being carried out does not require their attendance or the inspection of the vehicle. Road Inspection The driver of a motor vehicle or a combination of vehicles shall present, upon every request addressed to him by an officer of the competent authorities:

1- The driving licence.

2- The circulation permit of the car or the combination which he is driving.

3- The insurance contract specific to the car.

4- The receipt for the annual fee paid in respect of the car.

5- All other documents required by this Law or any subsequent traffic regulations.

Violations of the provisions of this Law shall be established by offence reports drawn up by:

- Members of the Internal Security Forces.

- Members of the Municipal Police entrusted with traffic policing.

- Sworn employees of the competent Administration assigned by a decision of the Minister of Interior and Municipalities, in respect of violations of a mechanical nature, excess load violations, and parking violations within the scope of streets subject to paid parking, provided that the details of enforcement of this latter type of violations shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities.

Reports shall be drawn up in a number of copies equal to the number of competent administrative bodies and judicial authorities to which they will be sent, in addition to one copy which shall be delivered to the perpetrator of the violation.

When drawing up a report, the descriptions of this vehicle must be recorded in the report: (registration number, colour, type, and make of the vehicle, and chassis number or engine number... etc.).

Where it is impossible to ascertain one of these descriptions, the reason therefor shall be stated in the body of the report.

Members of the Internal Security Forces and the Municipal Police may draw up violation reports on the basis of a photographic or moving image, captured by machines operating automatically or manually, in which appear the position of the vehicle during the violation, one of the two registration plates, and the time at which the image was captured (the year, month, day, hour, and minute).

These reports shall be deemed valid until the contrary is proven.

The details of application of this Article shall be determined by a decision issued by the Ministers of Interior and Municipalities and of Justice the details of application of this Article.

The offender shall be granted a period of thirty days to pay the reduced fine from the date of drawing up the stamped report or the mechanically marked report, or from the date of notification when drawn up in the absence of the offender; otherwise, a copy thereof shall be referred to the court, where a penal decision shall be issued against him to be executed in accordance with judicial procedures, and the offender shall have the right to object thereto within the time limits specified in the Code of Criminal Procedure.

Parking and stopping violations provided for in Articles 40 to 44 shall be exempted from the provisions of this Article, as they shall be referred to the Traffic Judgments Execution and Traffic Record Office for the purpose of placing an annotation on the file of the offending vehicle.

The minimum fines provided for in Article 374 according to their categories shall apply to these violations, while reserving the offender's right to object.
The payment of the fines of stamped reports within a period of thirty days from the date of notification of the report shall result in the abatement of the public prosecution.

In cases where drawing up the report constitutes an obstacle to traffic movement, security forces personnel may administratively withdraw the driving licence for a period not exceeding twenty-four hours in addition to the penalties provided for in this Law.

Twenty percent of the proceeds of the total collected traffic fines shall be allocated in favour of the Reserve Fund of the Internal Security Forces.

Sixteen percent of the proceeds of the total collected traffic fines shall be allocated in favour of the municipalities, and these allocations shall be distributed among the municipalities in accordance with the bases adopted in the distribution of municipal allocations from joint fees.

A rate of thirty percent of the fines collected from judicial judgments issued in accordance with the provisions of this Law shall be deducted in favour of the Judges' Mutual Fund. Where a traffic offence report is drawn up in the absence of the owner of the vehicle, he shall have the right to submit the necessary evidence to the competent judiciary regarding who was driving the vehicle when the report was drawn up.

The validity of a report drawn up before the Internal Security Forces upon the loss of a driving licence or a vehicle registration licence shall not exceed two months from the date of issuance of the report.

Custodians of impounded vehicles shall be deemed judicial custodians with all the legal consequences arising therefrom, and they shall receive in return a daily allowance charged to the owner of the vehicle, the value of which shall be determined by the decree referred to in Article 396 of this Law, as well as the conditions required to be met by the judicial custodian.

The conditions for enforcing the impoundment of motor vehicles and vehicles of all kinds, or their retention, deposit and custody, shall be determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Ministers of Justice and of Interior and Municipalities.

This decree shall also include the conditions for selling impounded motor vehicles and vehicles of all kinds in the event that their owner fails to claim them within a specified period and does not pay the fees and expenses incurred thereon.

1-In the event that a vehicle is retained administratively, the vehicle shall remain retained under the authority of the direct superior of the officers who drew up the offence report, and the said authority may return the vehicle to circulation after the cessation of the causes that led to the retention. If the offender does not proceed to remove the causes that led to the retention within thirty days from the date of drawing up the report, the retention shall become an impoundment and the procedures followed in impoundment cases shall then apply.

2-In the event that the condition of the vehicle upon retention requires carrying out repairs outside the place of retention or undergoing a mechanical inspection or an examination at the competent department, the vehicle registration licence may be retained for a maximum period of two weeks against a temporary notice authorising its owner to drive it for the purpose of removing the causes of the offence. In the event that the offence is not removed within this period, the retention of the vehicle registration licence shall be converted into an impoundment of the vehicle and the procedures followed in impoundment cases shall then apply.

Traffic personnel in the Internal Security Forces working on the roads shall be granted a rate of thirty percent of the basic salary monthly and an additional rate of ten percent for traffic personnel who ride motorcycles, provided that these rates may be increased by a decision of the National Road Safety Council upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior and Municipalities.

1- Every person against whom a report is drawn up for one of the infractions set forth in this Law and who wishes to object shall declare such in the report drawn up against him in his presence, or notify the competent court within thirty days of his wish to object if the report was drawn up in his absence; and in all cases, he shall not be entitled to exercise this right except after paying the amount of the fine imposed.

2- The person who has declared his wish to object in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph shall submit, under pain of forfeiture of his right to object, a petition clarifying the grounds for his objection to the competent court within thirty days from the date of his notification if the report was drawn up in his absence, or from the date of the occurrence of the infraction if the report was drawn up in his presence, or in the case of parking and stopping infractions when the report is drawn up by affixation to the vehicle. This objection shall be exempted from the fiscal stamp duty, and it may be sent to the competent court by registered mail.

3- The petition submitted in accordance with what is set forth in the preceding paragraph shall be deemed an objection to a judgment rendered according to summary proceedings, and the objection shall be heard in a public hearing in accordance with ordinary trial procedure.

1- Judges hearing traffic cases shall adjudicate any infraction of the provisions of this Law.

2- In application of the provisions of Article Three of the Judicial Organisation Law, the trial in absentia may be conducted outside the seat of the court.
Judges shall, prior to adjudicating the infraction report, examine the traffic record of each driver and base the judgment upon the traffic antecedents of the offender.

The court shall adjudge, in favour of the objector whose innocence is proven, the recovery of the value of the fine, and it may request the judicial prosecution of the drawers of the report in the event that it is convinced of their abuse of the authority granted to them or their violation of the law, and this judgment shall not preclude the taking of disciplinary measures against them.

All infractions of the provisions of this Law shall be subject to the procedures provided for in Articles 203 to 207 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

Provided that, notwithstanding the provisions of Article 205 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, in the event that the objection is dismissed, the penalty adjudged may not be increased, by a reasoned decision.

Notwithstanding the rules of service provided for in the Code of Criminal Procedure, judgments issued in respect of traffic violations and entailing a pecuniary penalty only shall be served by registered letter with acknowledgment of receipt at the address declared by the perpetrator of the violation on the record of infraction or recorded with the Traffic, Trucks and Vehicles Management Authority.

As for judgments that include a decision of imprisonment, they shall be referred and executed in accordance with judicial procedures like other decisions of imprisonment.

The provisions of this Law shall not limit the authority vested in the Ministers of Public Works and Transport and of the Interior and Municipalities, pursuant to the laws and regulations in force, to impose, within their respective powers and whenever public safety and order so require, measures other than the measures provided for in this Law. It shall rest with the Minister of Public Works and Transport to take all necessary measures to regulate the operation of the sectors of public passenger transport and goods transport, to determine the working methods of workers in these two sectors, and to issue the necessary regulations and decisions in this regard.

The Government shall have the right, upon the proposal of the Ministers of the Interior and Municipalities and of Public Works and Transport, to regulate, by decrees taken in the Council of Ministers, the use of public roads inside and outside inhabited areas according to traffic developments.

The Ministry of Public Works and Transport and of the Interior and Municipalities shall each have the right, within the powers granted to them, to carry out on international, public, main and internal roads and on their branches, all works necessary for the installation of traffic signs and signals and publicity and advertising boards. The Council for Development and Reconstruction shall also have the right to carry out all works necessary for the installation of traffic signs and signals on the roads the execution and rehabilitation of which it undertakes, with due regard for the provisions of the laws and regulations in force.
