- The draft law aiming to amend certain provisions of Law No. 288 dated 22/2/1994 (Medical Ethics), as amended by the Committees on Administration and Justice, and on Public Health, Labour and Social Affairs, and by the Chamber of Deputies, is hereby ratified.

- This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.
All physicians registered with the two Orders of Physicians in Lebanon shall be subject to the provisions of this Law.

The mission of the physician consists in preserving the physical and mental health of the human being, both preventively and curatively, rehabilitating him, alleviating his pain, and raising the general level of health.

1- The physician shall, guided by his professional conscience, treat any patient, whether in time of war or peace, whatever the financial or social condition of such patient, and regardless of his race, nationality, creed, political opinions, feelings, or reputation.

2- The will of the patient must be respected in every medical act, and if the patient is unable to give his consent, the physician must obtain the consent of his family starting from the first degree, or of the person of trust designated in writing by him, or of the legal representative in the event that he is a minor or lacking his mental faculties, except in case of emergency or impossibility.

3- The physician shall refuse, whether in time of peace or war, and even under threat, the exploitation of his professional qualifications to assist in, participate in, or accept any inhuman treatment, and if he is requested to treat or examine an incapacitated person, and it becomes apparent to him that this person has been subjected to torture, he must notify the judicial authorities and the Order of Physicians immediately.

1- The physician is required to pursue continuing medical education in order to develop his medical knowledge and technical capabilities to keep pace with modern scientific findings, in accordance with the continuing medical education programme adopted by the Order of Physicians.

If the physician violates this obligation, the Order of Physicians shall take disciplinary measures against him and notify the official guaranteeing bodies thereof.

2- The physician is required to equip his clinic with appropriate equipment and with technical means sufficient for his medical practice.

The health and technical conditions for equipping medical clinics shall be determined by the Ministry of Public Health after taking the opinion of the two Orders of Physicians in Lebanon.

3- The physician shall ensure that he does not practise his profession under circumstances and conditions that may harm his dignity or the quality of the treatment he prescribes.

1- Every physician, whatever his occupation and speciality, if he is present with a sick or injured person in a state of danger, or is notified of the presence of a sick or injured person in a state of danger, shall assist such sick or injured person or ensure that he receives the necessary first aid, except in the case of force majeure.

2- A physician may not refrain from answering a call for an emergency case unless he is certain of the absence of any imminent danger to the patient or if he is engaged for an urgent reason equal in importance to the condition of such patient, and in both cases he shall reply without delay stating the inability to attend and the reason.

In the event of the outbreak of epidemics or in the event of the occurrence of disasters, and with the exception of the case of force majeure, the physician shall:

a- Not abandon the patients whom he is treating except after securing the continuation of such treatment by the best possible means.

b- Comply with the request of the Order of Physicians and health officials for voluntary participation in public vaccination campaigns and in providing first aid to those injured in disasters.

c- Abide by the laws and regulations relating to communicable diseases and environmental hazards and by notifying the Ministry of Public Health thereof, and taking the necessary preventive measures in implementation of the instructions of the Ministry of Public Health.

1- The freedom of the patient to choose his physician, and to request the consultation of other physicians, must be respected.

2- The freedom of the physician to give the necessary instructions to his patient may not be restricted and he shall have complete freedom to choose the appropriate treatment according to the best medical regimens in force.

3- The fees of the physician shall be determined by direct agreement with the patient unless there are unified tariffs determined by the Ministry of Public Health with respect to the patients of official guarantor bodies by agreement with the latter and with the two Orders of Physicians, and the physician must provide the patient with the necessary clarifications regarding the invoice for his fees and he shall not be entitled to impose the method of payment or to impose an additional lump-sum consideration in return for confirming recovery.

4- The patient, his proxy, or the person representing him by contract with the physician, must pay the fees due to the physician directly.

5- Hospital institutions must issue the invoice for the physician's fees separately from the hospitalisation invoice and pay the physician his full fees to which he is entitled and which they have collected through their cashier's office.

6- The patient, his proxy, or the person representing him by contract with the physician must pay the fees due to the physician directly.

7- Official and private guarantor institutions must pay the fees of physicians to them directly.

1- When determining the fees of the physician, the financial condition of the patient and the special circumstances of each case shall be taken into consideration, while emphasising that the mission of the physician requires him to deal humanely with the patient.

2- If several physicians cooperate in the diagnosis or treatment, and their cooperation is justified from the scientific standpoint, and they agree upon collective fees, the fees of each of them must be stated separately.

3- The physician must abide by the tariff applied by the institution pursuant to contracts with private guarantor entities after the written approval of the medical committee, which must observe the directives of the two Orders of Physicians in this regard.

A physician may not reduce the consideration for his fees for the purpose of competition below the minimum tariff determined by the Order of Physicians by agreement with the Ministry of Public Health.

A physician may provide his assistance free of charge if he deems it appropriate.

The payment of fees in advance is prohibited, as is agreeing upon a lump-sum fee consideration with a guarantee of recovery. In all cases, the provisions of the general law and humanitarian principles shall be observed.

Professional secrecy imposed on a physician is a matter of public policy, and he must abide by it in all circumstances in which he is called upon to treat a patient or for consultation, subject to the exceptions imposed by public safety, laws, regulations, and contracts.

This secrecy covers the information confided to him by the patient, and everything that he may have seen, learned, discovered, or deduced in the course of practising his profession or as a result of the examinations he has conducted, and accordingly:

1- A patient's release of his physician from professional secrecy is not sufficient to discharge this obligation, as the physician remains bound to observe the interest of the patient and the requirements of public policy.

2- The physician must deliver to the patient in person, or to whomever he delegates in writing upon request, a certificate of his health condition, and he may omit from this certificate information that he deems to be in the patient's interest to conceal from him.

3- If the patient requests a certificate in order to benefit from social benefits, the physician may refer this certificate directly to the physician of the institution that grants these benefits, provided that this is accompanied by the written consent of the patient or of one of his relatives where necessary, subject to the provisions of item 2 above.

4- When summoned by the judicial police to give his testimony regarding facts covered by professional secrecy, a physician may withhold some of his information, and he must disclose all of his information before the criminal judiciary when requested to disclose it after being sworn in.

5- A physician is prohibited from reporting a patient who has confessed to him to having committed an offence. In the event that the physician discovers the commission of an offence during his examination of a patient, he must notify the Public Prosecution, as well as if he is convinced that reporting will prevent the person concerned from committing other offences.

6- The physician must give his testimony before the courts when giving it would prevent the conviction of an innocent person.

7- A physician is exempted from the duty of professional secrecy when summoned by the court as an expert to examine a patient or to study his file, within the limits of the mission assigned to him.

8- The physician must draw up and sign a birth certificate within three working days for every delivery procedure he has performed.

9- The physician must notify the Ministry of Public Health of venereal diseases that are required to be reported by an official measure, in order to prevent the spread of the disease in society, and he must also indicate in the notification the acceptance or refusal by the patient to receive the necessary treatment.

10- If his patient dies, the physician must draw up a death certificate containing the patient's name, age, and the date and cause of death. If the death occurred outside the hospital, the physician must inform the competent authorities thereof.

If the physician is unable to determine the cause of death, he must request the family to have an autopsy performed and must record this in the death certificate.

11- If his patient dies due to a disease that is required to be reported by an official measure, the physician must submit to the competent authorities a death certificate containing the patient's name, age, and the date of his death.

12- If the family of a person suffering from a serious mental or neurological illness requests the competent authorities to detain him on a precautionary basis, the physician who examines him must draw up a report specifying the characteristics of the illness, accompanied by an explanation indicating that the patient poses a danger to himself or to others.

13- If the physician discovers in the course of practice cases of rape and indecent assault, he must notify the Public Prosecutor, subject to the written consent of the victim.

14- If the physician discovers in the course of practice a case of arbitrary detention of an incapacitated person or a minor, or ill-treatment or deprivation, or rape or sexual assault, he must notify the competent authorities.

15- If the physician discovers in the course of practice a case of arbitrary detention of a minor, or ill-treatment or deprivation, he must notify the competent authorities.

16- If a physician is prosecuted in a liability action by a patient or his family, he is entitled to disclose the facts necessary to reveal the truth in self-defence.

17- A physician accused before the Disciplinary Council of the Order is not entitled to invoke professional secrecy.

18- The physician must ensure that his assistants abide by the obligation to maintain professional secrecy.

- Subject to the system of cooperation among physicians of the same specialty, the splitting of fees between the attending physician and the consulted physician, or the surgeon or the specialist during consultation or a surgical operation, is strictly prohibited.

- When submitting a comprehensive statement of fees to the patient, the fee of each physician who participated in the treatment must be mentioned therein.
With respect to surgical acts in which more than one physician participates, including the anaesthetist, the share of each of them shall be specified in the statement of fees.
If a physician attends a surgical operation at the request of the patient or the persons responsible for him, he shall be entitled to claim a special fee.

A physician may not waive his professional freedom while treating the patient and while providing the necessary care for his recovery and the relief of his pain.

A physician must refuse, during practice, any pressure capable of influencing his decisions.

A physician is prohibited from engaging in any other work alongside his profession that is incompatible with the dignity and ethics of this profession, or that demeans its standing or conflicts with the professional independence of the physician.

The profession of medicine may not be exploited for a commercial purpose.

1- With the exception of medical conferences supervised by the Scientific Committee of the Order, a physician is prohibited from participating in any educational professional work in any visual, audio or written media outlet without a notice registered at least three days in advance with the registry of the Order of Physicians.

In this case, he must abide by scientifically documented medical data, and he must exercise caution and attention to the effect of his statements on public opinion.

2- A physician is entitled to participate in public scientific discussions after notifying the Council of the Order in advance.

3- A physician is prohibited from resorting to direct and indirect methods of advertising.

4- A physician may exclusively advertise for a period of one week at most the commencement of his practice, the relocation of his clinic, or the date of his travel, and the date of his return.

5- A physician is prohibited from resorting to any promotional conduct, directly or indirectly, for his personal interest or for the institution to which he belongs, in which he works, or in the ownership of which he holds a share.

A physician may not mention on his private stationery, and on the sign of his clinic, anything other than:

1- Information that facilitates patients' contact with him.

2- The specialty recognised by the Ministry of Public Health and the Order of Physicians.

3- Titles conferred upon him by the State and academic institutions, specifying their source and the functions entrusted to him.

This information shall be stated in a form devoid of publicity.
Every physician is responsible for his professional acts.

Subject to the regulations of the contracted institution and the provisions of the contract:

- A physician shall not be entitled to delegate the performance of his professional activities, for a limited period, to anyone other than a colleague registered with the Order of Physicians.

- The substitute physician shall practice under his own responsibility and in the name of the principal physician, and the substitute physician shall be bound to issue treatment prescriptions in his own name and under his own signature.

- A qualified specialist physician shall not be entitled to appoint a colleague as his substitute unless he is of the same specialty.

A physician is prohibited from:

1- Any act likely to procure for his patient an unlawful or unjustified material benefit.

2- Paying commissions to anyone whomsoever, in any manner, for the purpose of attracting clientele, keeping them under treatment in the hospital, or obtaining any private benefit.

3- Accepting commissions in consideration of laboratory tests and radiographic imaging, or in consideration of prescribing specific medications or using specific medical devices.

4- Accepting commissions from hospitals or sanatoriums in consideration of admitting a patient thereto.
A physician is prohibited from facilitating the work of anyone who practices medicine unlawfully, and every physician who becomes aware of such practice must notify the Order of Physicians thereof.

1- Any fee-splitting among physicians, or between them and any other person, is strictly prohibited.

2- A physician is prohibited from conducting examinations in commercial premises and their annexes where medications and medical instruments are displayed, as well as in pharmacies and laboratories, except in emergency cases requiring urgent intervention to treat an injured or sick person.

If a physician holds a public office or is elected to an actual administrative function, he is prohibited from exploiting it in his profession for private benefit and for the purpose of attracting clientele.

Advertising by any media means any novel method of diagnosis or treatment for the purpose of inducing patients or colleagues to use it shall constitute a fault for which the physician shall be held liable, particularly where the advertisement lacks a warning to patients or colleagues regarding the risks that may arise from using the advertised method.

Every report, certificate or document issued by a physician must bear his signature and his registration number with the Order, in accordance with the form approved and distributed exclusively by the Order of Physicians, which collects the Order's stamp fees thereon.
A physician is prohibited from issuing false reports or certificates of accommodation.

A physician is not bound by an obligation of result in treating the patient, but by an obligation to secure the best appropriate treatment for him. In light of that, the following duties shall be incumbent upon the physician:

1- The physician must carry out the necessary diagnosis and treatment, if necessary in cooperation with qualified assisting persons, and in accordance with modern scientific data.

2- After prescribing and determining the treatment to be followed, the physician shall oversee the follow-up of its execution.

3- In the event that the patient refuses the treatment, the physician shall have the right to cease following up on him, and if it becomes apparent to him that the patient is in danger, he must exert his effort to persuade him to accept the treatment, and where necessary, he shall consult one or more other physicians for this purpose.

1- During the treatment of a patient, a physician shall treat him with humanity, compassion and integrity, and shall surround him with care and attention.

2- If a physician accepts to treat a patient, he shall be bound to ensure the continuity of his treatment, whether by himself or in cooperation with a qualified person, with all precision and conscientiousness and in accordance with the latest scientific data whose development he ought to have followed.

3- A physician is prohibited from pursuing, during his practice, any interest other than the interest of the patient, or from exploiting his information under any circumstances to achieve personal purposes.

4- A physician shall always respect the will of the patient, and if the condition of such patient does not allow him to express his will, his relatives must be informed, except in emergency cases or in the case of impossibility.

5- Where a patient loses his liberty, this ought not negatively affect the relations between him and the physician.

6- A prisoner shall have the right to accept or refuse treatment, unless he exposes his safety or the safety of others to danger according to the physician's report, and the competent Public Prosecution may take the appropriate measures in this regard.

7- In the event that a patient goes on a hunger strike, the physician shall intervene to convince him to end his strike. In case of impossibility and in the event that the patient's condition becomes exposed to an imminent danger, the physician must request the transfer of the patient to the hospital.

8- If those whose beliefs prohibit them from undergoing vaccinations imposed by the competent health authorities refuse the same, the physician must place them before their responsibilities and notify the said authorities thereof.

9- If those whose beliefs prohibit them from blood transfusion refuse the same, the physician must respect their wish, except in the case of permanent danger, where he must, after obtaining the permission of the competent judicial authorities, act as dictated by his professional conscience while bearing his full responsibilities.

10- If a mentally retarded person refuses to take the proposed treatments, his relatives or his legal representative, as well as the physician, shall be permitted to dispense with his prior consent. If the patient is afflicted with dementia or insanity or constitutes a danger to others, the physician must ensure the possible medical care for him in a hospital, and the hospital administration shall notify the competent health or judicial authorities thereof.

11- A physician shall not have the right to end the life of a patient out of compassion even if the patient requests so, namely euthanasia.

If the patient is afflicted with an incurable disease from which there is no hope of recovery, the mission of the physician shall be limited to alleviating his physical and psychological pains and giving him the appropriate treatments to preserve his life as much as possible.

It is preferable not to resort to technical means and therapeutic obstinacy with the consent of the family based on a joint report from the attending physician and the head of the concerned department. It remains necessary to assist the patient until the end in a manner that preserves his dignity.

12- In the case of a collective cessation of work by physicians, the physician shall remain responsible for his duties towards his patients and for ensuring the continuity of treatment for them, and for any other emergency patient.

13- A physician shall leave to the patient the freedom to choose the consulting physician, the anaesthetist and the surgeon, and the latter may refuse any decision to perform an operation if it is not sufficiently reasoned, or for any other legitimate reason.

14- A surgeon shall, when the need arises, seek the assistance of assistant surgeons from within the hospital institution, if any, with a view to ensuring the best care for his patient.

15- Prior to any surgical procedure, a specialist physician in anaesthesia and intensive care shall examine the patient, review his medical file, obtain from the surgeon all useful information, and record all his information in the medical file; he shall also, after performing the surgical procedure, record in the medical file any additional information relating to the acts of anaesthesia and resuscitation during the operation and thereafter until the patient leaves the operating room.

He shall bear his responsibilities in monitoring the patient from the moment of anaesthesia until full recovery, and he shall have the right to choose, on his own responsibility, the necessary equipment available in the hospital and to choose his assistants from among the paramedical physicians in the hospital institution in accordance with the regulations of the hospital in which he works, if any.

No surgical operation of any kind whatsoever requiring anaesthesia may be performed except under the supervision and in the presence of the anaesthetist throughout all stages of the operation in their entirety, with the exception of minor surgical procedures carried out in emergency rooms.

1- Every physician shall keep a medical file for each of his patients in his clinic and shall be responsible for its preservation, and the physician shall deliver a copy of the file to the patient when the latter requests him to do so, provided that it includes a report comprising all the information necessary to complete the diagnosis or to follow up on the treatment.

2- In the event of the physician's death or cessation of practice, his replacement or the person to whom the clinic legally devolves shall, upon the request of the patients, transfer their files to the physicians who undertake their treatment, and if no replacement physician or heirs are available, the files must be delivered to the Council of the Order for their preservation.

3- If the files are the result of the work of several physicians and are confined to a single institution, exclusively the treating physicians, researchers, and medical controllers in insurance institutions shall have the right to inspect them.

4- Medical files in hospital departments shall remain under the responsibility of the administration entrusted with their preservation and safety. The patient or his legal representative, by virtue of a power of attorney explicitly authorising him to do so, shall have the right to obtain from the hospital a copy of his medical file.

5- No physician shall have the right to inspect the medical file of the patient except upon the request of the latter or his legal representative and after informing the treating physician, except in emergency cases.

6- The treating physician, the researcher, or the health authorities shall have the right to make use of medical files to serve scientific advancement, provided that the names of his patients are not disclosed and provided that professional secrecy is maintained.

7- The investigating judge or the judicial police shall have the right to conduct a search of a physician's clinic or a medical department and seize medical documents in his presence and in the presence of a member of the Council of the Order.

The physician shall not then have the right to oppose the search procedures.

8- The judicial and health authorities and the Order of Physicians shall have the right to obtain a copy of any medical file that is the subject of a complaint and investigation.

9- Physicians and health institutions shall preserve medical files for a period of at least ten years unless the interest of the patient requires the extension of this time limit.

Human Experimentation and Clinical Research:

1- A physician is prohibited from prescribing any medication or using any experimental treatment except under the following conditions:

- That adequate, safe, and appropriate scientific studies and research have been conducted for each case, in a specialized university medical centre under the supervision of the Faculty of Medicine at the centre concerned.

- That the Ethics Committee at the university medical centre expresses its approval of prescribing the medication or using the treatment, and informs the Order of Physicians thereof in advance.

- That the treatment has been duly registered in a special register for experimental treatments at the Ministry of Public Health.

- That the patient gives his prior written consent.

- That the consent of the parents or legal representative is mandatory in writing when the matter concerns minor children or legally incapacitated persons.

- That the treatment is free of charge.

2- The establishment of ethics committees to follow up on medical research and clinical trials in hospitals, their missions, objectives, the principles governing them, the methods of their appointment, and the means of supervising them shall be determined by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Health. Donation and Transplantation of Organs:

3- Trafficking in human organs is strictly prohibited.

4- The removal of organs from the bodies of deceased persons may be performed, provided that they have bequeathed the same or following written consent from their family of the first degree, and for therapeutic or scientific purposes in accordance with the applicable legal rules.

5- The transplantation and donation of organs from living and deceased donors must be consistent with scientific progress, the requirements of modern medicine, scientific resolutions regulating the donation and transplantation of organs, and principles of medical ethics.

It is not permitted to take human tissues and organs from the body of a living person or from deceased persons to treat the disease or injuries of another person except after the approval of the National Committee for Organ and Tissue Donation and Transplantation in Lebanon, in accordance with conditions and principles determined by decrees issued by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Health after consulting the two Orders of Physicians, and comprising:

* The general conditions and principles for the donation and transplantation of organs.

* The role of the specialist physician and the assisting medical team.

* The mechanisms and procedures for consents.

* The role of the competent authorities in supervising the mechanism of organ donation.

* The procedures in the event of violation of the conditions and mechanisms for the donation and transplantation of organs.

The implementing mechanisms and the composition of the responsible bodies, including the National Committee for Organ and Tissue Donation and Transplantation in Lebanon and its missions, the licensing conditions for organ donation and transplantation centres, the responsible medical team, a judge seconded from the Ministry of Justice, the working mechanisms, the reporting of deaths, the national registers, and other matters related to the donation and transplantation of organs shall be determined by decrees issued by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Health after consulting the two Orders of Physicians.

* Assisted Reproductive Technologies:

6- Artificial insemination or pregnancy by means of assisted fertility technologies may be performed for spouses with their written consent, with due regard to the laws in force before the civil, Sharia, sectarian, spiritual, and civil courts.

7- Assisted reproductive technologies, the possibility of resorting to them, medical ethics when using these technologies, the special conditions for licensing assisted reproduction centres and the conditions of their operation, and other procedural provisions governing these technologies, as well as the conditions of the embryo preservation unit and the possibility of their destruction, and the procedures in the event of a violation, shall be determined by a decree issued by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Health after consulting the National Consultative Committee on Ethics for Health and Life Sciences.

8- The objectives, conditions, and procedures for research on the embryo, the ethics of research, the permission to use embryonic cells, and the use of cryopreserved embryos for research or their destruction shall be determined by a decree issued by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Health after consulting the National Consultative Committee on Ethics for Health and Life Sciences.

In Emergency Cases of Mutilation

9- No medical act likely to lead to the mutilation of the patient may be performed except in cases of emergency and extreme necessity, and only by a decision of at least two specialist physicians with the consent of the patient or the consent of his family of the first degree or his legal representative if he is unable to decide.

10- In emergency treatment, the surgeon alone may decide to perform an operation leading to mutilation, subject to the consent of the patient if he is conscious and aware, or the written consent of his family of the first degree, if any, or his legal representative.

11- Any medical or surgical treatment that leads to a change of sex and affects the future of the patient shall be considered mutilation.

* Stem Cells:

Stem cell transplantation technologies may be used for therapeutic purposes in accordance with the following conditions:

12- That the necessary scientific research has been conducted in accordance with the requirements of modern medicine, scientific progress, and the principles of medical ethics.

13- That these technologies are carried out in a university medical centre licensed by the Ministry of Public Health.

14- That the Medical Ethics Committee at the university medical centre expresses its approval for each case.

15- That the patient or his legal representative gives his written consent to the use of this technology.

16- The technologies for using stem cells, the possibility of resorting to them, the health and technical conditions for their preservation, the possibility of their destruction, the means of supervising them, and other procedural matters shall be determined by decrees adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Health.

A physician called upon to treat a minor or an incapacitated person must ensure the consent of his relatives, and in emergency cases, he must perform the necessary treatment if it is impossible to obtain the consent of his legal representative.

Performing an abortion is prohibited by law.

However, with regard to therapeutic abortion, subject to doctrinal reservations, it may only be performed under the following conditions and reservations:

1- That this abortion is the sole means of saving the life of the mother who is exposed to grave danger.

2- That the attending physician or surgeon must inevitably consult two physicians who concur with him by signing in writing on four copies, after medical examination and deliberation, that the mother's life can only be saved by means of abortion; one copy shall be delivered to the attending physician and one copy shall be kept with each of the two consulting physicians, and a registered report of the facts not bearing the name of the patient must be sent to the President of the Council of the Order of Physicians. Furthermore, the abortion may only be performed upon the consent of the pregnant woman after informing her of the situation she is in.

However, if she is in a state of grave danger and unconscious, and the therapeutic abortion is necessary for the safety of her life, the physician must perform it even if her husband or her relatives object; and if the physician's doctrine does not permit him to advise or perform an abortion, he may withdraw, leaving the continuation of the care of the pregnant woman to another colleague of competence.

In the event of a difficult or abnormal delivery, the physician must act in accordance with what medical art dictates in the interest of the mother and the child, without being influenced by family considerations.

The physician must cooperate with the competent authorities in order to preserve public health.

Taking into consideration his health condition and force majeure.
The physician must comply with the provisions of Article 28 of this Law, regardless of the party that commissioned him to conduct the medical examination.

1- The engagement of a physician for medical work with any hospital institution must be documented by a written contract, provided that its provisions do not conflict with the provisions of this Law and the public laws and regulations in force.

- A physician who practises his work in the hospital prior to the publication of this Law shall be deemed to be under contract, particularly as the bond existing between him and the hospital is governed by a contractual relationship.

2- Contracts binding physicians with public administrations and public institutions shall be subject to the provisions of this Law, and to the public laws and regulations.

3- Every hospital institution shall have internal regulations in a manner that does not conflict with the provisions of this Law.

4- Physicians contracted with a hospital institution shall elect from among themselves a medical committee concerned with professional, scientific, and moral matters and with the rights of physicians relating to their fees. The election of the president and members of the medical committee shall take place under the supervision of the Order of Physicians in accordance with rules and provisions that observe the internal regulations of the hospital institution and do not conflict with the provisions of this Law. In electing the medical committee, representation of the various categories of physicians contracted with the institution shall be observed.

5- The committee shall undertake the following tasks:

a- Watching over the ethics and dignity of the medical profession.

b- Striving to raise the professional standard through organising general meetings of the physicians in the hospital to discuss professional matters with regard to developing and improving professional work.

c- Uniting the voice of the physicians and safeguarding their rights and interests.

d- Assisting physicians in collecting their fees in coordination with the hospital administration.

e- Striving to resolve disputes that may arise between physicians in cooperation with the hospital administration.

f- Promoting medical research and scientific investigation in cooperation with the scientific committee of the Order of Physicians.

g- Expressing an opinion in an advisory capacity on matters concerning the hospital at the request of the administration.

h- Expressing an opinion in an advisory capacity on the medical file of a physician with whom the hospital administration wishes to contract.

i- Cooperating with the hospital administration in all common matters of interest to the medical body and relating to hospital work, and consequently striving to amicably resolve disputes that may arise between a physician and the hospital administration.

In professional matters, the committee shall be subject to the supervision of the Order of Physicians in accordance with the laws and regulations in force.

It is preferable that the work of a physician entrusted with preventive medicine in an institution be limited to this task and that he not practise curative medicine at the same time, except in emergency cases required by the exigencies of the public interest.
A medical inspector of a guaranteeing institution must not be an attending physician for the patients of such institution in any hospital.

- A physician entrusted with medical inspection in any administration shall maintain professional secrecy when inspecting the medical file, whether in the presence of the attending physician or with his prior consent, and shall limit himself to providing information that has a connection or utility from the administrative standpoint without stating the medical reasons therefor.

- Subject to the provisions of Article Seven of this Law, a medical inspector is prohibited from giving medical information recorded in medical files to third parties or to any administration unless general laws so provide or the concerned patient personally consents thereto.

- A physician appointed as a sworn expert may not be the attending physician of the same patient concerning whose condition he is requested to draw up a report.

- Likewise, he may not accept to perform his mission as an expert if the matter relates to one of his patients or relatives, or if he has a personal interest in the case that is the subject of the assignment.
A physician assigned an expert mission shall declare his capacity and his mission to the person whom he is assigned to examine prior to commencing the examination.

A physician assigned an expert mission shall recuse himself from the mission immediately if he observes that the questions put to him fall outside the scope of his medical profession. He shall limit himself in his report to answering the questions put to him, and shall not address matters that may become apparent to him on the occasion of performing his mission, if they fall outside the scope of this mission, unless he estimates that remaining silent thereon would be prejudicial to the course of justice.

A physician assigned to medical work in any institution, upon the occurrence of a serious pathological condition.

And save for the cases mentioned in Article 31, shall inform the patient's next of kin, and shall accept the summoning of any other physician, if that is beneficial to the patient.

A physician shall communicate the result of the diagnosis to the patient, and he may conceal from him the result of a grave diagnosis and not disclose the diagnosis of fatal cases except on an exceptional basis, and in a tactful manner, and he may communicate it to the family or the patient's next of kin, unless the patient has previously requested not to divulge the truth of his illness to his family and has specified to him the persons whom he may inform thereof, in which case the physician shall inform those persons thereof.
A physician may refuse to care for a patient for professional or personal reasons except in a case of necessity and in a case where he would be considered in breach of his humanitarian duties.

- The practice of the medical profession must take place within the scope of fair competition among colleagues, and any solicitation, diversion, or attempt to divert patients for the purpose of unlawful benefit, and any unfair competition, fee-splitting, or monopoly shall subject the perpetrator thereof to professional accountability before the Disciplinary Council.

- Agreement among physicians must not turn into collusion at the expense of the patient.

- The common fund managed by the medical committee must exclusively include the fees of colleagues in the same specialty in technical cooperation with the hospital administration.

Where a physician is called upon to treat a patient who is being treated by another colleague in a hospital institution, he must abide by the following rules:

1- Where the patient intends to dispense with his first physician, the new physician must ask the patient or those responsible for him to notify the first physician thereof and to record in writing their choice of the new physician, and in such case the first physician must provide the new physician with full information relating to the patient.

2- Where the patient wishes to consult any physician other than the attending physician, the latter must comply with his request, and in such case the consulting physician must leave to his colleague the result of his diagnosis and the treatment he proposes.

- In the event that a joint examination is impracticable, impossible, or inappropriate, the new physician may examine the patient and leave to his colleague the result of his diagnosis and the treatment he proposes in writing.

3- Where the attending physician is absent and the patient summons a colleague of his, the latter must ensure the treatment, and withdraw upon the return of the first physician, after informing him of his findings.

4- A physician shall not have the right to treat the patients of a hospital institution bound to an original attending physician except after obtaining the permission of the latter or in the cases permitted by the ongoing contract with the original physician or the regulations of the institution concerned.

- In the event that a dispute arises between the two physicians, it must be referred to the Council of the Order.

A physician may receive in his clinic patients who have their own attending physician, and he may notify the latter and consult with him after the consent of the patient, where that is in his interest.

The attending physician must, when required, propose a medical consultation or accept it if requested by the patient or by his legal representative on his behalf in the event that the patient lacks legal capacity, and he must in both cases present the name of the physician whom he proposes, taking into consideration the wish of the patient, or accept to meet with any proposed physician registered on the roll of the Order.

A physician may not interfere in the private affairs of his patient's family unless he is requested to do so.

Nor may he act as a partisan of a family or of any person with the intent of influencing the patient, unless that is in the medical interest of the patient.

A- The physician shall request the performance of the medical examinations imposed by the competent authorities on prospective spouses prior to their marriage, inform each of them of the results of these examinations, and advise them on the necessary preventive measures and health guidance; the information shall remain confidential and shall be kept in a file with the physician.

The physician shall notify the marriage officiant that he has performed what is required of him by means of a written certificate in accordance with the form issued by the Order of Physicians.

B- After verifying the health fitness of an applicant for a driving licence, the physician shall fill out a medical certificate for obtaining a motor vehicle driving licence in accordance with the printed form bearing a serial number issued by the Order of Physicians.

1- Physicians must endeavour to establish the best relations of fellowship and mutual assistance among themselves, with due regard to the interest of the patient.

2- A physician is prohibited from defaming a colleague of his, gossiping about him, or spreading defamatory rumours about him that would harm his professional practice.

3- The medical body is a united whole under the banner of the Order of Physicians, to guarantee the honour and dignity of every member thereof.

4- Every physician shall defend his colleague if he is subjected to false accusations.

5- In the event that professional disputes arise between physicians, they must be resolved amicably, and among themselves, and if that is not possible, then through the Medical Committee, and otherwise through the Council of the Order competent to examine professional disputes.

6- A professional dispute between physicians may not lead to a public controversy. In the event of recourse to the judiciary, the decision granting or refusing permission must be issued by the Council of the Order within one month from the date of registering the written request for permission with the registry of the Order of Physicians; if that time limit expires and the decision has not been issued, the permission shall be deemed to have been implicitly granted.

7- In the event of the termination of a physician's contract with a hospital institution or the suspension of his professional activity, it is advisable for the physician who wishes to fill the vacant position to contact his colleague whose contract was terminated or whose activity was suspended, and he shall inform the Council of the Order in order to preserve the ethics and laws of the profession and the rights of the physician and the patient.

A physician must not charge fees from his colleague and the members of his family who are dependent upon him, namely the husband or wife, ascendants, and descendants, unless they are paid by a third party.

1- Physicians of the same specialty may form a civil professional partnership with or without legal personality, provided that every partnership contract and its amendments are submitted to the prior approval of the Council of the Order.

2- The partnership shall pool the medical activities of the members and pool the fees in a single statement, and practice shall be restricted to the partner physicians.

3- If a group of physicians agrees to draw up a statement of fees, this group shall only include active physicians who participate in the care and practice the same specialty.

4- Physicians of different specialties may partner by pooling the necessary means in order to facilitate the practice of each of them, and the cooperation between them shall be documented by a cooperation contract or a civil partnership enjoying moral personality, provided that the medical fees remain completely independent of the partnership and are not in a single statement, and provided that this contract is submitted to the prior approval of the Council of the Order.

- No such partnership may be established in a hospital institution.

5- Every contract, whatever its nature, shall comply with the professional rules, and a copy thereof shall be communicated to the Order to verify its conformity with the model contract drawn up by it.

6- No physician or medical student may work as an employee of another physician.

7- Whatever the nature of the partnership, the practice of the profession shall remain personal and each partner physician therein shall remain liable solely for his own acts.

A physician shall avoid, as far as possible, harming anything related to the medical field, and in particular pharmacists, dentists, midwives, nurses and assistants, when dealing with them in medical matters.

Upon registering with the Order, a physician shall declare that he has taken cognisance of this Law and shall take the oath to abide by its provisions.

The President of the Order of Physicians shall draw up a record thereof, which he shall sign with the physician, and which shall be kept in the latter's file.
Every physician who ceases to practice the profession in Lebanon shall notify the Order thereof.
Every violation of the provisions of this Law shall render its perpetrator liable to referral to the Disciplinary Council.
All legislative texts and all other texts of decrees and decisions contrary to the provisions of this Law or inconsistent with its content are hereby repealed.
The details of enforcement of the provisions of this Law shall be determined, where necessary, by decrees taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Health.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

At the end of the consultation session, and regardless of the number of participating physicians, all physicians, individually or jointly, must draw up a written report, signed by them and containing the various opinions. In the event of a difference of opinions, the attending physician must inform the patient of all opinions, and the latter, or his representative if he lacks legal capacity, must decide in writing under his own responsibility who will continue his treatment.

The patient himself shall be entitled to request again the opinion of the consulting physician with the consent of the attending physician, during the period of the illness for which the consultation took place, and in the event that the attending physician does not consent, it shall be up to the patient to decide what he deems appropriate.

Subject to the provisions of Article 19 of this Law, a physician is prohibited from substituting a colleague to treat his patients, except on a temporary basis and with their consent, and in this case the fees shall be the right of the substitute physician alone.

- A physician prohibited by a judicial or disciplinary decision from practising the profession may not have a colleague substitute for him throughout the period of the penalty, and this shall not exempt him from taking the necessary measures to ensure the continuity of care for his patients undergoing treatment when the penalty is imposed.

- The Council of the Order must be notified of every decision of prohibition in order to take the necessary measures.

- The substitute physician must relinquish his temporary mission when the continuity of care is ensured.

There shall be added to the Code of Criminal Procedure, after Article 11, an Article 11 bis as follows:

"Article 11 bis:

a- Among the Advocates General provided for in the third paragraph of Article 11, there shall be one or more full-time Environmental Advocates General assigned by the Appellate Public Prosecutor to prosecute environmental offences in accordance with the procedures set forth in the laws in force.

b- The Environmental Advocate General shall bring charges for the environmental offence and specify the names of the defendants. He may bring charges against a person unknown before the Investigating Judge, thereby initiating the public prosecution by his charge, or bring charges directly before the competent courts.

c- Environmental offences shall be deemed to be offences resulting from:

1- Violation of the laws and regulations relating to the protection of woodland wealth, forests, nature reserves and biological diversity, the protection of air, water and soil from pollution, and those relating to combating damage resulting from sound and noise.

2- Violation of the laws and regulations relating to quarries, sandpits and crushers.

3- Violation of the environmental laws and regulations specific to determining the environmental conditions for classified establishments of all kinds.

4- Violation of the environmental laws and environmental regulations that protect the public and private property of the State and municipalities and territorial waters, and environmental encroachments on maritime and riverine property and groundwater.

5- Violation of the laws relating to the disposal of waste of all kinds, particularly medical waste and waste resulting from hospitals, and chemical and nuclear waste.

6- Violation of the provisions set forth in Law No. 444 dated 29/7/2002 and all other legal provisions relating to the protection of the environment wherever they are found.

7- Violation of the laws and regulations that protect antiquities and the cultural and natural heritage.

d- The Environmental Advocate General may seek the assistance of specialists in environmental affairs and in the affairs of antiquities and cultural heritage to carry out the technical and artistic tasks that he assigns to them, after administering the legal oath to them if they are not sworn experts.

e- The chief clerks in the competent courts shall notify the Ministry of Environment of every final environmental criminal judgment issued against a natural or legal person in order to record it in the special register referred to in item (b) of Article (5) of this Law, within three months from the date on which it becomes final.

f- Judgments and decisions issued in environmental cases shall be published in two local newspapers, including the decision to shelve the action."

"The First Investigating Judge shall assign one or more investigating judges to cases of environmental offences, in addition to the duties entrusted to him"

The following text shall be added to Item 3 of Article (54) of Legislative Decree No. 150 of 16/9/1983 (Judicial Judiciary Law):

b- A special register shall be kept at the Ministry of Environment in which criminal prosecutions and judgments issued against natural and legal persons in environmental offences shall be recorded".
