Higher education institutions:

Higher education institutions shall be concerned with teaching, scientific research, and community service in the fields of higher education and shall be of three types:

The university, the university college, the higher technical institute.

First - The University, which is every higher education institution in which the following conditions are met:

1. It comprises at least three faculties, each of which specialises in one of the major fields of study adopted by international organisations, particularly UNESCO.

These fields shall be determined by a decision of the Minister upon the recommendation of the Council based on the proposal of the Technical Academic Committee;

2. It provides programmes in at least nine specialisations leading to degrees of the first level provided for in this Law;

3. It allocates a percentage equivalent to at least five per cent of its annual operating budget to scientific research and its requirements;

4. Teaching and research therein are carried out by members of a teaching staff holding a recognised doctorate degree or the highest degree awarded in the specialisation, who undertake the teaching of not less than 50% of the total credits in the first level, 70% in the second level, and 100% in the third level determined in this Law.

The conditions for instructors who do not hold a doctorate shall be laid down by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister based on the recommendation of the Council for Higher Education; and the Council for Higher Education may determine other percentages according to the nature of certain specialisations upon the proposal of the Technical Academic Committee.

5. It secures full-time teaching staff members for at least 50% of the total educational courses.

6. The number of members of its teaching staff shall be proportionate to the total number of its students, provided that the ratio does not exceed thirty students for each member of the staff.

7. The percentage of Lebanese professors holding a doctorate shall not fall below 60% of the number of full-time professors therein.

Second - The University College, which is every independent higher education institution that specialises in one or two of the fields of study referred to above, and to which conditions (4), (5), and (6) of Item First of this Article apply.

1. The university college may provide education of an academic or technological nature;

2. For providing technological education, it is required that the programmes offered by the college specialise in the applications of basic, engineering, medical, or nutritional sciences, or any of the information technologies, and in this case the percentage referred to in paragraph 5 of Item First of this Article shall be reduced to 40% of the total courses, unless it provides education leading to degrees in the second level, in which case conditions (4), (5), and (6) of Item First of this Article shall apply.

Colleges that exclusively provide education of a technological nature shall grant only degrees of the first and second levels in the specialisations legally licensed for them.

University institutes may be established within universities or university colleges, which are units that assume the responsibility of education in a specific field of knowledge, and enjoy autonomy within the scope of the university or college to which they belong.

Third - The Higher Technical Institute,

Which is every higher education institution that specialises in preparing intermediate technical cadres and the programmes offered by which specialise in one of the fields of technical applications, particularly industry, agriculture, water, and administrative and human services.

This institute shall be subject to the supervision of the Ministry of Education and Higher Education and to the regulations prescribed specifically for it.

- The draft law transmitted by Decree No. 5520 dated 14 December 2010 relating to Higher Education, as amended by the Joint Parliamentary Committees and the Chamber of Deputies, is hereby ratified.

- This law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Title of the Law and its Scope of Application:

This law shall be entitled the "Higher Education Law" and all public and private higher education institutions lawfully licensed on the date of its promulgation or licensed pursuant to its provisions shall be subject to its general provisions, insofar as it does not conflict with the laws and regulations governing the Lebanese University.

Objectives of Higher Education:

Within the framework of higher education as a public service higher education is a public service provided by higher education institutions, and it meets the need of society in building its capacities and developing its capabilities and in scientific research, while respecting the fundamental freedoms of individuals and groups and the supreme values stipulated in international charters, particularly with regard to academic freedoms.

Specialised Training Programmes:

The higher education institutions referred to in items First and Second of Article Five may establish specialised training programmes in areas of a theoretical, applied or technical nature, within the fields for which they are licensed, and these programmes shall lead to the award of special certificates.

Description of Curricula and Programmes:

In application of the provisions of this Law and the decrees and regulations issued pursuant thereto, each institution shall adopt a unified template for the description of the programmes and courses that it offers, and shall adopt a teaching system based on courses and credits.

The general frameworks for organising and describing curricula and programmes in private higher education institutions shall be determined by a decision of the Minister upon the recommendation of the Higher Education Council based on the opinion of the Academic Technical Committee provided for in this Law.

General Regime for the Master's and Doctorate Degrees:

The general regime for the Master's and Doctorate degrees of their various types shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister based on a recommendation from the Higher Education Council supported by the opinion of the Academic Technical Committee.

Obligation to Deposit Documents:

Private higher education institutions shall deposit with the Directorate General of Higher Education the documents provided for in this Law and in the decrees issued in application thereof, which are requested by the Ministry of Education and Higher Education in accordance with a mechanism determined by a decision of the Minister upon the proposal of the Higher Education Council.

Rules of Procedure of the Council for Higher Education:

First - Meetings of the Council:

1. The Council for Higher Education shall compulsorily meet at least once a month upon a convocation by its President, and it shall also meet extraordinarily upon a convocation by its President or upon a written request from at least one-third of its members, and its meetings shall be valid in the presence of the absolute majority of those of whom it is legally composed, and decisions and recommendations shall be taken by the absolute majority of the members of the Council, and in the event of a tie vote, the Minister shall have the casting vote;

2. In the event of his absence, the Minister shall delegate one of the members of the Council to preside over the sessions.

Second - Committees:

The Council The Council may form, from among its members or from among specialists who are not its members, permanent or temporary sub-committees to which it entrusts the matter of studying certain affairs submitted to it, other than the tasks vested in the Academic Technical Committee and the specialised committees in accordance with what is provided for in this Law.

Secretariat of the Council for Higher Education:

The work of the Secretariat of the Council shall be carried out by a Secretary who shall be from among the employees of at least the third category on the establishment of the Ministry of Education and Higher Education - Directorate General of Higher Education, appointed by the Minister, and assisted as needed by employees assigned by the Director General of Higher Education.

The Academic Technical Committee and the Committees Specialised in Programmes:

An Academic Technical Committee linked in its work to the Council for Higher Education shall be established, assisted by committees specialised in the various university programmes.

This Committee shall undertake the tasks vested in it provided for in this Law and in the decrees issued in implementation thereof, and it shall also undertake the performance of whatever the Council for Higher Education assigns to it.

Functions of the Technical Academic Committee:

First- Functions of the Technical Academic Committee with respect to the licensing of the establishment of a higher education institution:

1. Preparing a reference guide for the examination of the documents required from the legal person applying for the licence relating to its legal entity and to the bylaws of the institution,

2. Examining the bylaws of the institution applying for the licence, in the light of the reports of the committees specialised in programmes, and preparing a report containing its proposals regarding such bylaws, which it shall submit to the Council for Higher Education if it is positive.

If, however, the Committee finds that the file does not satisfy the conditions for approval, it shall return it to the concerned party accompanied by the reasons for the return in order for such party to remedy them within a period of two months at most.

Upon the expiry of the period, the Committee shall prepare a report which it shall submit to the Council for Higher Education containing its opinion on the file and its recommendations.

Second - Functions of the Technical Academic Committee with respect to the commencement of instruction in an institution:

1. Preparing a reference guide for the conditions of the commencement of instruction,

2. Carrying out verification including a field inspection of the actual state of the institution and examining the reports of the committees specialised in programmes and in field visits prior to recommending the grant to it of permission to commence instruction;

3. Preparing a report which it shall submit to the Council if it is positive.

If it is negative, the Director General of Higher Education shall send it to the institution requesting that the deficiencies specified therein be remedied within a period not exceeding two months, and upon the expiry of the period, the Committee shall prepare a final report which it shall submit to the Council for Higher Education containing its opinion on the file and its recommendations.

Third- Functions of the Technical Academic Committee with respect to the commencement of instruction in a faculty or programme:

1. Examining the reports of the committees specialised in programmes and in field visits prior to recommending the grant to the institution of permission to commence instruction in a faculty or programme;

2. Preparing a report which it shall submit to the Council if it is positive.

If it is negative, the Director General of Higher Education shall send it to the institution requesting that the deficiencies specified therein be remedied within a period not exceeding two months, and upon the expiry of the period, the Committee shall prepare a final report which it shall submit to the Council for Higher Education containing its opinion on the file and its recommendations.

Fourth- Functions of the Technical Academic Committee with respect to the periodic verification of the actual state of the institution:

1. Preparing a reference guide for the periodic verification of the actual state of the institution,

2. Undertaking the periodic verification of the actual state of the institution after it has commenced instruction, pursuant to a timetable which it shall set for that purpose;

3. Preparing a report which it shall submit to the Council if it is positive.

If it is negative, the Director General of Higher Education shall send it to the institution requesting that the deficiencies specified therein be remedied within a period not exceeding two months, and upon the expiry of the period, the Committee shall prepare a final report which it shall submit to the Council for Higher Education containing its opinion and its recommendations.

Fifth: Functions of the Technical Academic Committee with respect to the periodic evaluation of programmes

1. Reviewing the periodic reports prepared by the committees specialised in programmes.

2. Adopting recommendations to deem the programmes recognised for a specified period of time;

The Minister shall approve the guides provided for in this Article upon the recommendation of the Council for Higher Education based on the opinion of the Technical Academic Committee, and they shall be published in the Official Gazette.

Functions of the Committees Specialised in Programmes:

The committees specialised in programmes shall examine the files relating to the fields and academic programmes, examine the fulfilment by the programmes of the academic requirements, carry out the necessary field visits to verify the course of the academic work after the commencement of instruction and until the graduation of the first cohort of students in the specialisations concerned, draw up detailed reports thereon showing the extent to which the file conforms to the adopted reference conditions, and submit the same to the Academic Technical Committee.

First - Functions of the committees specialised in programmes with respect to licensing:

1. Proposing a reference guide relating to the documents required for licensing faculties and their programmes at the various levels.

2. Examining the files of the faculties, their regulations and their programmes; drawing up a report containing proposals thereon and submitting it to the Academic Technical Committee.

Second - Functions of the committees specialised in programmes with respect to the commencement of instruction:

1. Proposing a reference guide for the conditions of commencing instruction in a faculty or programme.

2. Carrying out a verification including a field inspection of the actual state of the faculty prior to recommending that it be granted permission to commence instruction in each of the specialisations it is licensed to establish;

3. Drawing up a report on the results of such verification, which it shall submit to the Academic Technical Committee if it is positive.

Where it is negative, the Director General of Higher Education shall send it to the institution requesting that the deficiencies specified therein be remedied within a time limit not exceeding two months, and upon the expiry of the time limit the committee shall draw up a final report which it shall submit to the Academic Technical Committee containing its opinion on the file and its recommendations.

Third - Functions of the committees specialised in programmes with respect to the periodic evaluation of programmes.

1. Proposing a reference guide for the periodic evaluation of programmes at the various levels,

2. Conducting the periodic evaluation of provisionally recognised programmes that are not subject to accreditation.

Formation of the Committees Specialised in Programmes:

1. The Committee Specialised in Programmes shall be formed by a decision of the Minister upon the proposal of the Academic Technical Committee of:

Three experts within the required specialisation, from the list provided for in Article 26 of this Law, one of whom shall be a coordinator, provided that academic experience is taken into consideration in their selection, a representative of the syndicate of the liberal profession concerned when the specialisation leads to obtaining a degree that permits the practice of a profession regulated by law;

2. A member of the Committee Specialised in Programmes shall be required to be a holder of a doctorate or the highest degree in the specialisation with at least five years of experience in higher education within the required field.

Examination of a Specialisation Not Available in Lebanon:

If an application for a licence to teach a specialisation that did not previously prevail in the field of higher education in Lebanon is submitted to the Council for Higher Education, and it becomes apparent to it that it is impossible for the file to be examined by the specialists whose names are listed on the roster approved by it and that it is also impossible to call upon local experts to examine this file, the determination of the application shall be conditional upon the party that submitted it producing an academic cooperation agreement with a higher education institution abroad accredited by an internationally recognised accreditation body, provided that the agreement includes in particular the provision of the requirements for teaching this specialisation in terms of teaching staff members and the supervision thereof until the graduation of at least one cohort.

Establishment of the Committee:

There shall be established in the Ministry of Education and Higher Education a committee concerned with the recognition of studies and the equivalence of higher education qualifications pursued or obtained by their holders from outside Lebanon with their equivalents in Lebanese studies and qualifications provided for in this Law, which shall be called the "Equivalence Committee in Higher Education".

Plurality of membership:

Experts representing private higher education institutions and the Lebanese University may not hold membership in more than one permanent body mentioned in this Title.

Remuneration of the Committees:

The remuneration of the members of the Council and of the Committees established in this Title, and the remuneration of their secretariats, shall be determined by a decree passed in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister.

Vacancy of positions in the permanent councils and committees:

In the event of a vacancy in any position in the Council or in any of the permanent committees provided for in this Law, for whatever reason, at least six months prior to the expiry of the term of office of the person concerned, in particular by reason of death, incapacity, loss of the qualifying capacity to occupy such position, resignation, or dismissal for one of the reasons provided for in the laws and regulations in force, a replacement shall be selected on the basis of the principles specified in this Law and in the decrees and regulations adopted in implementation thereof, and the replacement shall occupy the vacant position until the expiry of the term of office of the original member.

Evaluation and Accreditation Bodies and Institutions:

A National Commission for Quality Assurance shall be established pursuant to a special law enacted for this purpose, and this Commission shall determine the national standards that must be met to ensure quality in higher education. Private institutions accredited from outside Lebanon must undergo accreditation in accordance with mechanisms determined by a decree in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister, based on the opinion of the National Commission for Quality Assurance.

General Eligibility to Submit a Licensing Application:

Persons of private law possessing legally recognised moral personality, whether Lebanese or foreign nationals belonging to a State recognised by the Lebanese State, may submit an application for a licence to establish a private higher education institution.

Elements of the licence:

The licence consists of:

1. An establishment licence granted by a decree issued in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister based on the recommendation of the Council supported by the report of the Academic Technical Committee; this licence shall specify the basic particulars relating to it, and the period within which, or upon the expiry of which at the latest, the institution must commence its operations, on pain of lapse of this licence ipso jure, and this period may not exceed five years.

2. A permit to commence instruction granted by a decision of the Minister upon the recommendation of the Council supported by the report of the Academic Technical Committee.

Documents relating to the legal person:

The documents relating to the legal person applying for a licence shall be determined as follows:

1. If it is Lebanese: an official certificate proving its legal entity, in accordance with the provisions of this Law;

2- If it is non-Lebanese: the following documents certified by the Lebanese Embassy in the country to which it belongs:

a. A certificate issued by the competent authority in the country to which it belongs, proving that it is a higher education institution operating therein.

b. A certificate issued by the competent authority in the country concerned proving recognition of the degrees and diplomas it awards.

c. The bylaws clarifying the mechanism of supervision by the parent institution over the branch requested to be established.

d. A certificate proving the qualifications held by the Lebanese representative of the institution applying for the licence.

e. The documents proving that the Lebanese party with which it wishes to cooperate fulfils the conditions provided for in this Law.

Amendment of programmes in licensed institutions:

Licensed private higher education institutions must submit the amendments relating to the academic organisation of the programmes to the Directorate General of Higher Education. If it appears to the Director General of Higher Education that the proposed amendment is considered fundamental, he shall refer the matter to the Specialized Technical Committee for Programmes to prepare a report, upon which the Council for Higher Education shall rely to issue its decision approving or rejecting the amendment.

Conditions for establishing a Master's programme:

Upon submitting an application for a licence to establish a programme at the Master's level, the following conditions must be fulfilled in the institution:

1. That the required conditions for offering programmes leading to this degree be satisfied in accordance with the standards and procedures referred to in this Law; and in the regulations issued in implementation thereof.

2. That it have a plan for the development of scientific research that provides for the human and material capacities to put it into effect;

3. That it provide for a special regulation on the conditions of admission and graduation for this stage;

4. That the institution have the administrative, technical and human capacities capable of providing the requirements of the programme.

5. The special conditions for teaching Master's programmes shall be laid down by a decree in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister based on the recommendation of the Council for Higher Education.

Mechanisms:

The general mechanisms relating to licensing, the granting of permission to commence teaching, and the renewal of the recognition of degrees shall be issued by a decree in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister based on the recommendation of the Council for Higher Education.

Special conditions:

The special conditions relating to licensing, the granting of permission to commence teaching, and the renewal of the recognition of degrees shall be issued by a decision of the Minister upon the recommendation of the Council for Higher Education based on the proposal of the Technical Academic Committee.

Periodic Audit of Institutions:

The Academic Technical Committee shall periodically every six years, and when necessary, audit the status of private higher education institutions pursuant to an assignment from the Council for Higher Education, and the audit shall cover the extent to which the status of the institution conforms to the provisions of the legislative and regulatory texts governing private higher education institutions.

The periodic audit of institutions that have not obtained institutional accreditation shall be conducted at least every six years to ascertain their reality and take the appropriate measures in accordance with what is provided for in Title Seven of this Law, pursuant to an annual programme specifying the institutions covered thereby, and this programme shall be approved by a decision of the Minister upon the proposal of the Council.

This Committee shall draw up reports on each of the tasks assigned to it and submit them to the Council through the Director General of Higher Education, and shall include in its reports proposals based on the results of the audit.

Examination of Periodic Audit Reports:

The Council for Higher Education shall examine the report submitted to it, and if it appears to it that a legally operating private higher education institution has come to be in a position violating the provisions of this Law or the provisions of the decrees and decisions issued pursuant thereto, it shall address a warning to it to remove the violation within a time limit that it specifies for it, provided that it is not less than six months; if it fails to take the initiative to comply with the requirements thereof, it shall recommend the imposition of the appropriate penalties in accordance with the provisions set forth in this Law.

The Supreme Body of the Institution:

1. Every private higher education institution shall establish a supreme body representing the legal person holding the license, which shall be responsible for adopting the plans and measures aimed at securing all the requirements for the institution's fulfillment of the obligations legally incumbent upon it:

2. The powers of the license holder in the institution shall be determined by what is provided for in the regulations pertaining to it.

The terms of reference for the formation of the supreme body shall be issued by a decision of the Minister based on the recommendation of the Council for Higher Education supported by the proposal of the Specialized Academic Committee, provided that the diversity of the management systems in force at higher education institutions in Lebanon shall automatically be taken into account.

Budget of the Institution:

1. The private institution of higher education must draw up an annual budget of its own that is independent of the licence holder;

2. The revenues of the institution shall consist of the following:

A. Tuition fees collected by the institution from the students enrolled therein,

B. Returns on its movable and immovable property,

C. Fees for consultancy activities and proceeds arising from its productive projects and from the operation of its facilities,

D. Contributions, gifts, donations, and aid.

3. The private institution of higher education shall open a bank account of its own that is independent of the account of the licence holder, in which the funds of the institution shall be deposited and from which expenditure shall be made in accordance with its own financial regulations;

4. The final financial reports of the institution shall be subject annually to a statutory audit by a recognised firm for auditing company accounts.

These reports shall be subject to ratification by the supreme body that supervises the institution;

5. The institution shall submit to the Council of Higher Education a summary of the above audit prepared by the auditing firm showing the compliance of the institution with the articles provided for in this law relating to the budget of the university.

Rights of Students:

1. Students enrolled in private institutions of higher education shall have the following rights:

A. To obtain academic preparation in accordance with internationally recognised and nationally approved standards.

B. A guarantee that the institution will continue to offer the programme in which they are enrolled until their graduation therefrom.

C. Freedom of expression within the framework of public order, and the establishment of representative bodies and cultural, social, sports, environmental, and similar clubs

D. To obtain social, cultural, sports, and health services.

E. To obtain an annual guide to the institution of higher education in which they are enrolled, containing its programmes and its administrative, academic, and financial regulations that relate to student affairs, copies of which it shall deposit with the Council of Higher Education.

2. Every private institution of higher education must establish its own policy and programmes, published and deposited with the Council of Higher Education, pursuant to which it provides financial aid and scholarships to needy and outstanding students; the private institution of higher education must adopt a special system to facilitate the enrolment of qualified persons with disabilities to study in its programmes and to facilitate their pursuit of such study until graduation.

Provision of education prior to the licensing of the establishment of the institution:

1. If it becomes apparent to the Council for Higher Education that any person of private law is providing formal higher education leading to one of the degrees provided for in this Law, prior to obtaining a licence for the establishment of an institution for this purpose, the Minister shall issue a decision to close it immediately and shall request the Public Prosecution of Cassation, through the Minister of Justice, to initiate a public action against the person responsible for violating the laws regulating higher education, and the commission of this violation shall be punishable by imprisonment from three months to one year and by a pecuniary fine ranging between five hundred and one thousand times the monthly minimum wage.

A person harmed by this violation may assume the capacity of a civil party in a separate action, or join the public action.

2. If the offender is licensed to open an institution for non-university education, in addition to the penalties set out in the first paragraph of this Article, the Minister shall address a formal notice to him to comply immediately with what the licensing decree authorised him to do, and if he does not comply pursuant to the formal notice, the Minister shall issue a decision to close the institution and shall propose the issuance of a decree withdrawing the licence.

Categories of Violations and Penalties Therefor:

Violations are divided into four categories:

First Category:

This includes:

Teaching prior to obtaining the authorisation to commence operations for the institution, leasing out the licence, using a name for the institution that does not conform to the designation in the licensing decree; in such case, the following penalties shall apply:

1. Immediate closure by decision of the Minister upon the recommendation of the Council, and the decision shall remain in force until the removal of the violation.

2. A financial fine in the amount of three hundred times the monthly minimum wage for each violation.

3. In the event of failure to remove the violation, the licence for establishment shall be revoked by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister based on the recommendation of the Council of Higher Education;

Second Category:

This includes:

- Teaching on a new unlicensed campus,

- Teaching in unlicensed faculties,

- Teaching at unlicensed degree levels,

- Teaching in unlicensed specialisations,

In such case, the following penalties shall apply:

1. Immediate cessation of operations on the campus or in the faculty, specialisation, or level, by decision of the Minister upon the recommendation of the Council.

2. A financial fine in the amount of three hundred times the monthly minimum wage for each violation.

3. In the event of repetition of the violation, the fine shall be doubled.

4. In the event of failure to remove the violation, the institution shall be prohibited, by a decision taken by the Minister upon the recommendation of the Council, from admitting new students for a full academic year.

If it fails to rectify its violation upon the expiry of the term of this penalty, it shall be placed under the guardianship of the Council of Higher Education until the graduation of the students enrolled therein, and it shall be prohibited throughout the period of its placement under guardianship from admitting new students;

Third Category: This includes:

- Transferring the campus and teaching therein prior to obtaining the necessary approval from the Council,

- Violating the senior management regulations of the institution with respect to the appointment of the president, deans, and senior staff,

- Admitting students in contravention of the conditions prescribed by law,

- Enabling non-Lebanese higher education institutions to award degrees in Lebanon without a licence to do so,

- Introducing substantive changes to the programmes and implementing them in the institution prior to obtaining the approval of the Council,

- Violating the application of the percentages for the teaching staff and surface areas,

- Lack of independence of the buildings for the purposes of the institution,

- Failure to cooperate with the committees assigned by the Ministry for the matters set forth in this Law,

In such case, the following penalties shall apply:

1. A formal warning to remove the violation with a financial fine in the amount of one hundred times the monthly minimum wage for each violation.

2. In the event of repetition of the violation, the fine shall be doubled.

3. In the event of failure to remove the violation, the institution shall be prohibited from admitting new students for a full academic year, and the prohibition from admitting new students shall be renewed in the event of continuation of the violation.

Fourth Category:

This includes:

All other violations of the provisions of this Law other than those set forth in the three categories above.

In such case, the institution shall be given a formal warning of the obligation to remove the violation with a financial fine in the amount of fifty times the monthly minimum wage for each violation, and the fine shall be doubled in the event of repetition of the violation.

The imposition of penalties shall not preclude judicial prosecution by the Administration or the injured party.

Placing the institution under guardianship:

If circumstances arise in the institution leading to the demise of the legal entity holding the licence, or the legal loss by this entity of the constituent elements of its establishment, or its failure to undertake the legal procedures to form the supreme body of the institution, or the impossibility of forming it, or the impossibility of its performing its duties or exercising its powers in accordance with the provisions of the regulations of the institution, the Minister may take the decision, upon the recommendation of the Council, after verifying the occurrence of the aforementioned circumstances, to place it under the guardianship of the Council, which shall appoint a committee to manage it temporarily until the end of the academic year, and the work of the committee may be extended until the end of the following academic year by a reasoned decision of the Minister upon the recommendation of the Council.

This committee shall enjoy all the academic, administrative and financial powers enjoyed by the supreme body of the institution provided for in this Law, and it shall propose appropriate solutions that guarantee the rights of the students of the institution and the rights of those working therein, and the various cases that lead to the cessation of the course of work therein completely, or in a disturbed manner negatively affecting the academic educational process therein, shall be considered circumstances leading to the impossibility of the institution continuing to perform its duties, whether the origin of these cases is an emergency force majeure circumstance with whose occurrence the institution has nothing to do, or the result of internal conditions specific to this institution.

The membership of any institution placed under the guardianship provided for in this Article in any of the permanent councils, bodies and committees shall be frozen until the rehabilitation of the institution or the final revocation of this membership.

Total lapse of the licence for establishment

1. The licence to establish a private institution of higher education or one of its components shall lapse ipso jure if the licensee does not obtain the authorisation to commence teaching within the time limit specified in the decree licensing the establishment;

2. The Minister shall declare the revocation of the licence upon the recommendation of the Council of Higher Education, and it shall be published in the Official Gazette.

3. The institution may submit an application to extend the validity of the decree licensing the establishment prior to the expiry of the period and once only.

General conditions for university buildings:

The general conditions for university buildings and the specifications, criteria and standards that must be met therein shall be determined by virtue of a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Education and Higher Education and of Public Works after seeking the opinion of the Higher Council of Urban Planning.

Procedures for Preparing the Technical Inspection for Granting Building Permits for University Buildings:

The concerned official departments competent to prepare technical inspection reports for granting building permits, whether for construction, addition, modification, or restoration, on the basis of the application files received by them to obtain technical approval for the requested permit, are prohibited from conducting the inspection if it becomes apparent to them that the maps and designs contained in the file submitted for their approval pertain to university buildings, and that the file is devoid of a certified true copy of the decree containing the licence to open the private higher education institution concerned with the building works that are the subject of the application.

And the technical inspection must specify, where it is permissible to prepare a report thereon, the intended use of the structures as being for the purposes of higher education.

Necessity of Specifying the Intended Use of University Buildings in the Technical Inspection:

Heads of municipalities are prohibited from granting a permit for building, or addition, or modification, or restoration, for structures belonging to a higher education institution unless the prior technical inspection report duly prepared has specified the intended use of these structures for the purposes of higher education, and this prohibition shall also apply to District Commissioners (Qa'immaqams) whenever they are the competent authority to grant such permit.

Necessity of the Availability of the Occupancy Permit for the University Building in order to Connect it to Public Services:

The administrations concerned with public services, including telephone, water, electricity, and others, are prohibited from connecting any building of a private higher education institution to the public network providing the service unless the subscription application includes a certified true copy of the "Occupancy Permit".

Penalties in the Event of Violating the Preceding Three Articles:

Whoever is responsible for violating the provisions of any of the articles numbered 68, 69 and 70 shall be punished by imprisonment from three months up to one year and by a fine of between fifty and one hundred times the official minimum wage, or by either of these two penalties.

Conditions and Procedures for a Private Higher Education Institution Advertising its Activity:

The conditions and procedures for a private higher education institution advertising its educational and academic activity shall be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister based on the recommendation of the Council after seeking the opinion of the Academic Technical Committee.

Naming of Institutions All private higher education institutions shall be known by their name in the Arabic language, and the adoption of any other additional name in a foreign language shall be subject to the approval of the Council for Higher Education.

Repeal of Contrary Provisions The provisions of the Private Higher Education Law promulgated on 26 December 1961 and all provisions contrary to the provisions of this Law or inconsistent with the content thereof are hereby repealed, with the exception of the laws on public higher education and on public and private higher vocational and technical education, and the provisions of Law No. 83/67 promulgated on 28 December 1967 relating to the establishment of a Supreme Advisory Council for Universities in Lebanon are likewise repealed.

Determination of the Details of Implementation of the Law The details of implementation of the provisions of this Law shall be determined by decrees taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister based on the recommendation of the Council for Higher Education, and the regulatory provisions in force shall remain applicable until the issuance and implementation of the new regulatory texts.
Publication of the Law This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The fees shall be deposited in a special account at the Central Bank in the name of the Ministry of Education and Higher Education - Fees on Private Higher Education Institutions, and from it shall be disbursed, in accordance with the procedures adopted pursuant to decisions taken by the Minister, the remuneration fees of the Technical Committee and the committees specialised in programmes, and the surplus in this account, once realised, may be used for the benefit of studies and the development of programmes which it is duly decided to conduct in the Ministry of Education and Higher Education - Directorate General of Higher Education.

This account shall be subject to the ex post audit of the Court of Accounts.

Statutory Time Limit for Bringing the Status of Existing Institutions into Compliance with This Law Legally licensed private higher education institutions shall be granted a time limit of three years as from the first academic year following the date of issuance of this Law to ensure the compliance of their status with the conditions and specifications set forth in this Law.

With respect to constructions, the time limit may be extended for a maximum period of three further years by a decision of the Minister upon the recommendation of the Council for Higher Education. The procedures and measures provided for in this Law shall be taken against any institution that violates the provisions of this Article.

Article /19/ of Law No. 337/1994 (Statute of Notaries Public), as amended by Law No. 224 dated 29/5/2000, is hereby amended to read as follows:

"The Mutual Aid and Retirement Fund shall be managed by a committee composed of six members, four of whom are incumbent notaries public, and two of whom are retired notaries public, selected by the Minister of Justice, who shall designate a chairperson from among them, provided that he is one of the incumbent notaries public.

The Minister of Justice shall reconstitute the Management Committee of the Mutual Aid and Retirement Fund referred to above within a period of six months from the date of entry into force of the present Law.

The term of office of the existing committee shall then be deemed terminated automatically upon the constitution of the new committee by the Minister of Justice.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

A new Title shall be added after Article (44) of Law No. 337/1994 dated 8/6/1994 (Statute of Notaries Public) as follows:

Title Seven - The Council of Notaries Public

Chapter One - Establishment and Functions of the Council

Article 45: Establishment of the Council

1- A Council of Notaries Public in Lebanon (hereinafter referred to as "the Council") shall be established; it shall be of a professional nature and shall enjoy legal personality.

2- The Council shall consist of two bodies: the General Assembly and the Bureau of the Council (hereinafter referred to as "the Bureau").

3- All tenured Notaries Public in the Lebanese Republic shall be deemed affiliated ipso jure with "the Council".

4- Any retired Notary Public who so wishes may also affiliate with the Council.

The application for affiliation of retired Notaries Public shall be submitted to the Bureau.

Article 46: Functions of the Council

The functions of "the Council" shall be defined as follows:

1- Working to attend to the affairs of Notaries Public, develop the profession, and elevate its standing.

2- Cooperating with international organisations that have a similar activity.

Chapter Two - Organisation and Management of the Council

First: The General Assembly

Article 47: Its Powers and Functions

a- The General Assembly shall consist of all tenured Notaries Public and the affiliated retired Notaries Public.

b- Subject to what is stated below regarding the first meeting held by the General Assembly after the enactment of the present Law, the General Assembly shall hold its ordinary meeting on the first Sunday of the month of November of each year. In the event that a quorum is not reached, it shall be adjourned ipso jure to the third Sunday of the same month.

c- The General Assembly shall also hold an extraordinary meeting whenever "the Bureau" deems it necessary or in the event that a request therefor is submitted to it by one-fourth of the number of tenured Notaries Public who are entitled to participate in such meeting.

d- The meeting of the General Assembly, at the first session, shall be deemed lawful if attended by more than half the number of Notaries Public who are entitled to participate in the General Assembly. If such quorum is not met, a second session shall be held two weeks later and shall be deemed lawful with whoever attends.

e- The General Assembly shall be chaired by the President of "the Bureau" and, in the event of his absence, by the Vice-President, and then by the eldest of the members of "the Bureau" present.

f- Decisions shall be taken by a relative majority.

g- The business of the annual ordinary General Assembly shall cover:

1- Electing the members of "the Bureau".

2- Determining the annual subscription fee payable by tenured Notaries Public in favour of "the Council", provided that the subscription fee payable by affiliated retired Notaries Public is equal thereto.

3- Approving the accounts of the preceding financial year and adopting the budget of the following financial year.

The financial year shall begin on the first of January and end on the thirty-first of December.

As for the first financial year, it shall begin on the date of the election of the first "Bureau" and end on the following thirty-first of December.

4- Matters that the Bureau decides to submit to the General Assembly.

Decisions relating to the preceding items 1, 2, and 3 shall be taken by an absolute majority of the number of Notaries Public participating in the General Assembly.

h- Adopting the internal regulations of "the Council" prepared by the Bureau, provided that these regulations shall not enter into force until approved by the Minister of Justice.

i- The internal regulations shall determine the manner of operation of "the Council" and "the Bureau", including the powers of each of the President, the Vice-President, the Secretary, and the Treasurer, the rules for holding elections, as well as the procedural rules. They shall designate the location of the permanent seat of the Council.

j- The legal quorum required for convening the General Assembly relating to the adoption or amendment of the internal regulations shall be at least two-thirds of the number of Notaries Public who are entitled to participate in this General Assembly at the first session.

In the event that a quorum is not reached, the legal quorum for convening the second session shall be the absolute majority of the number of Notaries Public who are entitled to participate in this session.

Decisions regarding the adoption and amendment of the internal regulations shall be taken by a two-thirds majority of the Notaries Public present.

The General Assembly must convene to adopt the internal regulations within a period of six months from the date of the election of the first "Bureau".

k- After the annual subscription fee is determined, a Notary Public shall not be entitled to participate in the General Assembly unless he has paid his subscription fee prior to the sixteenth of the month of October of each year.

Second: The Bureau of the Council

Article 48: Elections of the Bureau

1- "The Council" shall be managed by a bureau composed of eight members elected by the General Assembly from among the tenured Notaries Public (referred to in this Law as "the Bureau").

2- The General Assembly shall also elect two persons, from among the retired Notaries Public affiliated with the Council, who shall join "the Bureau".

They shall have the right to deliberate without the right to vote, and shall not be counted in the quorum of "the Bureau".

For the purposes of the first electoral process referred to hereinafter, the tenured Notaries Public shall be deemed affiliated with the Council, and retired Notaries Public who have submitted an application for affiliation to the Ministry of Justice at least one week prior to the date fixed for convening the first meeting of the General Assembly that will be called to elect the first bureau shall also be deemed affiliated therewith.

3- The term of office of the members of "the Bureau" shall be three years, renewable once. They may not run for election again until after a full term has elapsed.

4- The process of electing the members of the first "Bureau" shall take place on a Sunday within a period of six months from the date of publication of this Law in the Official Gazette, by means of a call addressed by the Minister of Justice and published in two local newspapers and in the Official Gazette, specifying the date of the first and second sessions for the election as stated below.

5- The first electoral process shall take place in the courtyard of the Palace of Justice in Beirut.

6- The quorum required at the first session for the election shall be the absolute majority of the tenured Notaries Public in Lebanon. If a quorum is not reached, a second session for the election shall be held two weeks from the date of the first session, and the quorum shall be lawful with whoever attends.

7- The first electoral session shall be held under the chairmanship of the eldest of those present, and two of the youngest Notaries Public from among those present shall perform the functions of Secretary and teller, and all of them shall certify the minutes of the election session.

8- In the event that the first electoral session is not convened within the six-month period mentioned above for any reason whatsoever, the session shall be deemed convened ipso jure in the courtyard of the Palace of Justice in Beirut on the first Sunday following the expiry of this period, and shall remain in session until the members of the first "Bureau" of "the Council" are elected.

9- The election of the members of "the Bureau" by the General Assembly shall take place by secret ballot, and the candidate who obtains the highest number of votes shall win; in the event of a tie vote, the candidate with greater seniority in the profession shall win membership of "the Bureau", and in the event of equality, the eldest.

10- It is always required that a member of "the Bureau", on the date of his election, has been a Notary Public for at least seven years, including the traineeship period. 11- The eldest member of "the Bureau" shall call the remaining members to a session to be held within a period of three days from the date of their election, in order to elect each of the President, the Vice-President, the Secretary, and the Treasurer by secret ballot and in succession.

The tenured Notary Public who obtains the highest number of votes shall win the post; in the event of a tie vote, the candidate with greater seniority in the profession shall win the post, and in the event of equality, the eldest.

12- In the event that the session is not convened within the three-day period mentioned above for any reason whatsoever, "the Bureau" shall be deemed to be in session ipso jure as of the fourth day until the elections referred to above are held.

13- A year shall be defined as the period extending between the date fixed for convening the General Assembly in a given year and the date fixed for convening it in the following year.

As for the first year, it shall extend from the date of convening the first General Assembly until the date fixed for convening the General Assembly in the following year.

14- The members of "the Bureau" shall not receive any fees or allowances in return for their membership and their performance of the functions entrusted to them.

Article 49: Meetings of "the Bureau"

1- "The Bureau" shall hold periodic meetings and whenever the need arises, at the headquarters of "the Council", upon a call from its President or from three of its members in the event that the President fails to address the call.

2- The President shall chair the sessions, or his Vice-President in the event of his absence, or the eldest of the members in the event of the absence of the President and the Vice-President.

3- The sessions of "the Bureau" shall only be lawful with the attendance of the absolute majority of its members who are tenured Notaries Public.

4- Decisions of the Bureau shall be issued by a majority, and in the event of a tie vote, the President shall have a casting vote.

5- If one or more seats of the members of the Bureau fall vacant, the Bureau shall continue its business composed of the remaining members until the convening of the first General Assembly, during which those who will fill the vacant seat or seats shall be elected. The successor shall replace his predecessor for the remainder of the term of his membership.

6- However, in the event that "the Bureau" loses half or more of its members who are tenured Notaries Public for any reason whatsoever, the Bureau with all its members shall be deemed resigned and its term of office expired.

In this case, and notwithstanding the expiry of its term of office, "the Bureau" must, within a period of two weeks, call the General Assembly to convene within a period of at most two months from the date of the call in order to elect a new bureau.

If "the Bureau" abstains from addressing the call, the Minister of Justice shall address the call within a period of ten days following the expiry of the two-week period referred to above.

7- "The Bureau" shall continue to conduct current business until a new "Bureau" is elected.

8- In the event of the temporary absence of the President of "the Bureau", the Vice-President shall replace him during the period of his absence.

In the event that the seat of the President of "the Bureau" falls permanently vacant, the Vice-President shall replace him for the remainder of his term of office.

9- In the event that the Vice-President permanently assumes the post of President, "the Bureau" shall elect a Vice-President within a period of fifteen days from the assumption by the Vice-President of the presidency of the Council.

10- Any member of "the Bureau" who absents himself from its meetings three consecutive times without an acceptable excuse shall be deemed resigned ipso jure.

Article 50: Powers and Functions of "the Bureau"

The Bureau shall work to attend to the affairs of Notaries Public, oversee the proper performance of their functions, and undertake whatever enhances the role of their profession, in particular:

- Expressing an opinion on all draft laws, proposed laws, and decrees relating to the affairs of the profession.

- Establishing a code of ethics for the notarial profession and conduct of Notaries Public, to be approved by the Minister of Justice.

- Seeking to resolve professional disputes and conflicts among Notaries Public amicably.

- Representing "the Council" vis-a-vis public authorities and third parties and before the courts.

- Accepting gifts, bequests, and grants after the approval thereof by the Minister of Justice.

- Expressing an opinion, within a period not exceeding ten days, on complaints and judicial prosecutions against Notaries Public arising from the exercise of their functions which the Minister of Justice may refer to it.

- Submitting proposals on all matters relating to the affairs of the profession and the proper performance of Notaries Public.

- Expressing an opinion on establishing new notarial offices or abolishing or transferring existing offices.

- Organising training courses for tenured and trainee Notaries Public and drawing upon, for this purpose, retired Notaries Public when needed.

- Holding seminars and conferences with the aim of enhancing the profession and improving the performance of Notaries Public.

- Coordinating permanently with the various state bodies in all matters related to the affairs of the profession, and providing advice when requested.

- Coordinating with unions of Notaries Public in various countries of the world, exchanging expertise, participating in national and international conferences and meetings, and strengthening Lebanon's international relations in this field.

- Preparing and executing the annual budget.

- Calling General Assemblies and executing their resolutions.

- The possibility of contracting with an insurance company to establish a collective insurance policy covering the professional civil liability of Notaries Public.

Article 51: Revenues of the Council

The revenues of the Council of Notaries Public shall consist of:

1- Subscription fees of Notaries Public.

2- Gifts, bequests, and grants that "the Council" decides to accept in accordance with what is set forth above."
All lease contracts of built real properties concluded prior to 23/7/1992 shall be subject to the provisions of this Law.

Single Article: - The draft law set forth in Decree No. 7104 dated 3 January 2002, aiming to enact the Rent Law, as amended by the Administration and Justice Committee, has been ratified. This Law shall be published in the Official Gazette and shall enter into force six months after the date of its publication.

The following shall be exempted from the provisions of this Law:

a) Lease contracts of agricultural lands and the buildings appurtenant thereto.

b) Seasonal lease contracts relating to summer and winter resorts.

c) Contracts pursuant to which employers provide premises for the housing of their employees free of charge or for consideration.

d) Occupation of the public domain of the State and municipalities.

e) Lease contracts of villas that meet the following specifications: that they consist of one or more storeys, are leased for the residence of a single tenant, and have a garden, a garage, a heating system, and a special system providing hot water, even if the tenant bears the expenses of providing the same, provided that these specifications were met on the date of commencement of the original lease.

A special fund for residential leases covered by the provisions of this Law (referred to in this Law as the Fund) shall be established, which shall be affiliated with the Ministry of Finance and its accounts shall be kept at the Treasury Directorate in this Ministry. This Fund aims to assist all tenants concerned by this Law whose average monthly income does not exceed three (3) times the minimum wage, by contributing to the payment of the increases, wholly or partially as the case may be, that occur to their rents in implementation of the provisions of this Law. Wherever mentioned in this Law, the tenant shall mean the tenant or whoever legally succeeded him. Upon requesting to benefit from the contribution of the Fund, and for the purpose of determining the average monthly family income, the beneficiary or the benefiting party, wherever mentioned in this Law, shall mean the tenant and the legal occupants of the leased premises with him.

A tenant who leased pursuant to the provisions of either of the two Laws 29/67 and 10/74 in buildings that were considered luxurious, and a non-Lebanese tenant, shall not benefit from the allowances of this Fund.

A tenant wishing to obtain a contribution from the Fund shall submit an application to the Committee under whose jurisdiction the leased premises fall, exempt from all fees, and the submission of this application shall result in suspending the time limit for payment of the increases in the rent resulting from the implementation of this Law until the entry into force of the decision of the Committee approving or refusing the contribution. The application must fulfil the following conditions:

1 - That it be submitted within a time limit of two months from the date of determining the fair market rent by mutual consent or judicially in respect of the first extended year, and within the same time limit at the beginning of each of the other extended years, on pain of forfeiture of his right to benefit from the contribution.

2 - That the following documents be attached to the application:

(a) - A schedule of the names of the members of the beneficiary group.

(b) - An employment certificate for each of the members of the beneficiary group issued by the competent authority showing the amount of the wage or salary according to the status of each of them as an employee, worker or public servant.

(c) - A personal declaration of income for each of the members of the beneficiary group if he is self-employed.

The Committee shall examine the applications for a contribution with respect to the average monthly family income of the beneficiary and shall decide thereon in accordance with the following:

(a) - If the members of the beneficiary group are employees, workers or public servants, the average monthly family income of the beneficiary shall be the sum of the monthly incomes pertaining to each of them.

(b) - If any of the members of the beneficiary group is self-employed, it shall rest with the Committee to verify, by such means as it deems appropriate, his average monthly income, and consequently the average monthly family income of the beneficiary shall be equal to the sum of the average monthly incomes pertaining to each of the members of the beneficiary group. It shall rest with the Committee, in all cases, to verify by such means as it deems appropriate the number and names of the members of the beneficiary group and the average monthly income of the tenant and of each of those members, and the average monthly family income of the beneficiary shall then be calculated in accordance with what is set forth in this Article. Either of the two parties concerned may submit evidence and documents that assist in proving his claims. The Committee may summon both the lessor and the tenant to hear them, pursuant to a notice served upon them in accordance with the Code of Civil Procedure, and it must issue its decision within a time limit not exceeding two months from the date of submission of the application.

The revenues of the Fund shall consist of:

- Annual contributions from the State allocated in the budget of the Ministry of Finance to cover the obligations of the Fund.

- Grants, donations and bequests following the approval thereof by the Council of Ministers, and the value of such grants and bequests shall be deducted from the amounts taken as a basis for determining the income tax due, and shall also be deducted from the amounts taken as a basis for determining inheritance duties, and shall be exempted from the duties imposed on grants.

The management of the funds of this Fund, including the rules of expenditure and collection, shall be subject to financial regulations approved by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

A committee composed of a sitting or retired judge as chairman and four members, the first representing the landlords, the second representing the tenants, the third delegated by the Ministry of Finance, and the fourth delegated by the Ministry of Social Affairs, shall examine the application of the provisions relating to the payment of increases on rent. The committee shall be appointed within a period of two months from the date of entry into force of this Law pursuant to a decree upon the proposal of each of the Ministers of Justice, Finance, and Social Affairs, and an alternate judge and four alternate members representing the same entities provided for above shall be appointed in the same decree. More than one similar committee may be appointed in each governorate where necessary. A clerk and a bailiff shall be attached to each committee by a decision of the Minister of Justice. The remunerations of each of the chairman, the members, the clerk, and the bailiff shall be determined by decisions of the Ministers concerned. The committee shall hold its meetings during or outside official working hours at the places determined by the Minister of Justice. This committee shall have a judicial character.

Subject to the provisions of each of Articles 8 and 11 of this Law, the Committee shall decide, in the light of the outcomes of its procedures with respect to determining the average monthly family income of the beneficiary, on the entitlement of the application for contribution from the Fund or the lack thereof, as well as on the value of the contribution, in accordance with the following:

1- If the Committee decides that the average monthly family income of the beneficiary exceeds three times the minimum wage, it shall refuse the contribution for lack of entitlement thereto, and the tenant shall be required to pay the new rent resulting from the application of the increases provided for in this Law, under pain of being deemed in default, whereupon the provisions of this Law shall apply to him.

2- If the Committee decides that the average monthly family income of the beneficiary does not exceed three times the minimum wage, the Chairman of the Committee shall notify the decision to the financial department in the region to which the leased premises belong, and the latter shall pay to the lessor the contribution due in monthly instalments for the extended year in respect of which the tenant submitted the application for contribution, as shown below:

a- The case of the average monthly family income of the beneficiary that does not exceed twice the minimum wage. The Committee shall determine by its decision the value of the monthly instalment such that it is equal monthly to the difference between the value of the rent and the value of the new rent. The Committee shall notify its decision to the competent financial department to take the necessary action in accordance with what is shown in this item.

b- The case of the average monthly family income of the beneficiary that exceeds twice the minimum wage and does not exceed three times this minimum. The Committee shall determine by its decision the value of the monthly instalment such that it is equal monthly to the difference, if any, between 30% of the average monthly family income of the beneficiary and the value of the new rent. The Committee shall notify its decision to the competent financial department to take the necessary action in accordance with what is shown in this item.

The contributions that the Fund is required to pay to the lessor shall remain incumbent upon this Fund, and the lessor may not invoke them for any reason and before any authority against the tenant as being a part of the rent unpaid by the latter.

In the event that the tenant wishes to continue to benefit from the contribution of the Fund for the subsequent extended years, he must follow the working mechanism referred to above with the Committee at the beginning of each extended year up to the ninth year inclusive. The application for contribution, as provided for in Article 8, shall lead to the suspension of the time limit for paying the increases resulting from the provisions of this Law, until the decision of the Committee approving or disapproving takes effect.

Whoever gives the Committee a false certificate or declaration, or uses or benefits from either of them, shall be prosecuted for the offence of forgery and the use of a forged document. Upon discovering any false declaration or certificate and its use and benefit therefrom, the Committee shall, as the case may be, notify the Public Prosecution of the matter, and the tenant's right to obtain the contribution from the Fund shall be forfeited.
In all cases, the decision issued by the Committee shall be deemed final and enforceable upon its original and shall not be subject to any avenue of review.

Lease contracts of residential built properties concluded before 23/7/1992 shall be subject to the provisions of this Part. A residential lease contract shall be deemed to be a contract relating to premises designated for residence; whereas premises leased under a single contract for residence and for purposes other than residence shall be deemed residential premises by the mere fact of their being used for residence.

Lease contracts of residential premises shall be extended for up to nine years from the date of entry into force of this Law, provided that the tenant pays the value of the fair rent gradually in accordance with the following:

A- Subject to the provisions of Article (20) of this Law, the value of the fair rent shall be determined by mutual agreement or judicially in accordance with what is provided for in Article (18).

B- The rent due on the date of entry into force of this Law shall be increased annually and consecutively in accordance with the following:

15% fifteen percent of the value of the difference of the increase between the rent in force before the entry into force of this Law and the fair rent referred to above, for each year of the first four extended years following the date of entry into force of this Law.

20% twenty percent of the value of the difference of the increase mentioned above, for each of the fifth and sixth years of the extension period, until the rent in the sixth extended year reaches the value of the fair rent referred to in item (A) above.

C- The rent in the seventh, eighth, and ninth extended years shall be equal to the value of the fair rent referred to in item (A) above.

D- At the end of the ninth extended year, the lease shall become free.

1- A tenant who continues to satisfy the conditions for benefitting from the benefits of the Fund shall have the right to request from the owner in writing, and three months prior to the expiry of the term of the contract in the ninth extended year under penalty of forfeiture of the right, the drawing up of a new lease contract for a maximum term of three years for a rent equal to the fair market rent referred to in Paragraph (a) of Article 15 above, provided that he proves within the same time limit that he has obtained a decision from the Committee that he satisfies the conditions for benefitting from the benefits of the Fund, in accordance with the mechanism provided for in this Law.

2- This tenant shall have the right to waive his right to request the drawing up of a new lease contract and to notify the owner in writing, within the same time limit mentioned above, of his wish to vacate the leased premises in return for obtaining a financial contribution paid to him by the Fund, in monthly instalments as provided for below. The owner shall not have the right to invoke the tenant's written wish to vacate the leased premises unless this tenant has obtained the contribution of the Fund.

3- To obtain the contribution, the tenant must observe the following:

a- The tenant shall submit to the Committee, within the time limit mentioned above, an application to obtain the contribution. The submission of this application shall not result in suspending the time limit for payment of the increases in the rent resulting from the implementation of this Law.

b- He shall attach to the application the following documents:

- A copy of the letter notifying the owner of his wish to waive the tenancy and vacate the leased premises.

- An undertaking to vacate the leased premises and deliver them vacant to the owner within a time limit of three months from the date on which he is notified of the Committee's approval to pay the contribution, and during this time limit he shall continue to pay the amount of rent due from him.

4- The Committee shall rule, in light of the attached documents, on the amount of the monthly instalments and their due dates, starting from the first of the month following the actual vacation of the leased premises and delivery of the keys, evidenced by a written acknowledgment signed by the owner and the tenant, or by the tenant alone, before the Notary Public, and until the expiry of the term of the new lease contract.

5- The Committee shall notify its decision to the Finance Department in the district to which the leased premises belong, whereupon the contribution shall be paid in monthly instalments on their due dates.

6- The tenant shall have the right to assign these instalments to a financing source of his choice, which lends him in return the value of the contribution as a single lump sum, and the loan granted to him shall be deemed to constitute a housing loan, whereupon the tenant shall benefit from the exemptions provided for in Law No. 543 dated 24/7/1996.

7- If the Committee decides that the tenant does not fulfil the conditions for benefitting from the benefits of the Fund, his lease shall become free from the date of the Committee's decision.

In the event that the tenant vacates the leased premises at his own wish in return for a financial contribution that he obtains from the Fund, if he fulfils the conditions for benefitting from this Fund, the provisions of Article 27 of this Law shall apply.

The fair rent shall be determined:

A- Amicably by agreement between the lessor and the tenant, provided that this rent shall be subject to the decision of the Committee in the event that the tenant requests from it to obtain a financial contribution from the Fund.

B- If the determination of the fair rent is not reached amicably by agreement between the lessor and the tenant within the first three months following the effective date of this Law, the lessor may follow the following procedures:

1- The lessor shall engage the assistance of two experts from the list of sworn experts in the governorate registered with the courts, one of whom shall be a civil engineer or an architect and the second from among those working in real estate valuation registered on the roll of experts. The two experts shall undertake to draw up a valuation of the fair rent for the leased premises in accordance with the procedures provided for in Article (19) of this Law.

2- The lessor shall, through the notary public, serve the fair valuation report upon the tenant, who must, within two months of being served with the report, either approve it and adopt it in determining the fair rent or submit a counter valuation report by engaging the assistance of two experts from the list of sworn experts in the governorate registered with the courts, one of whom shall be a civil engineer or an architect and the second from among those working in real estate valuation and registered on the roll of experts. The two experts appointed by the tenant shall undertake to draw up a valuation of the fair rent for the leased premises in accordance with the procedures provided for in Article 19 of this Law.

3- The tenant must serve the valuation report drawn up by the two experts appointed by him to be served upon the owner through the notary public within the aforementioned two-month period, under penalty of forfeiture of his right to object to the valuation sent by the owner or even to invoke the content of a counter report.

4- If the two reports differ, each of the lessor and the tenant may resort to the Committee in the governorate to which the leased premises belong in order to adjudicate the dispute arising from the difference, attaching to his application a copy of the two reports and their enclosures, including copies of the service documents. The Committee shall issue a reasoned decision, and its decision shall be final and not subject to any form of recourse.

The report must include, under penalty of nullity, the names of the authors of the report and their reference in the roster of experts, a statement of the party who commissioned them to draw up the report and a statement of the date on which the valuation was conducted, the means adopted in conducting the valuation, from the area of the apartment to the type of building and the estimation of the average building costs (popular, medium to popular, medium to luxury, luxury), and the share of the area of the real property pertaining to the apartment, taking into consideration the status of the ground floor if the floor is prepared for commerce, together with a valuation of the sale price per square metre in a vacant building and a leased building, and a statement of what reduces the value of the average cost per square metre of the building due to age or misuse, or what increases the value of the building other than the improvements introduced by the lessee and which may result from the location, the view, or otherwise, and the sales or estimations by official administrations to which the experts have had recourse in estimating the sale price per square metre. The report and its annexes must bear the signature of the two experts on every page thereof and the date on which the report was drawn up.
The fair rent shall be determined on the basis of a rate of (5%) five per cent of the sale value of the leased premises in their existing condition as if they were vacant.

The experts shall be liable for the content of the report they have drawn up, for the authenticity of the documents annexed thereto, and for the result of the valuation. For the purpose of applying this Law, the two experts appointed by each of the owner or the lessee shall be deemed as though they were appointed by the judiciary.

The owner of the leased premises that were leased during the period of validity of either of the two Laws 29/67 and 10/74 in the buildings that were considered luxury may recover the leased premises in cases other than the two cases of family necessity and demolition, in return for paying the tenant a compensation equal to half of the compensation due in the case of demolition and provided for in Clause 2 of Article 22 above, and in this case, the provisions of the said Article regarding the proportional decrease of the compensation with the remaining period of the extension period shall not apply.
