Subject to the provisions of Articles 22, 23 and 24 of this Law, the owner shall, in all cases of recovery provided for in this Law, tender and deposit with the Notary Public in the area in which the leased premises are located the compensation determined under this Law or agreed upon amicably with the tenant, while clearly indicating its proportional decrease with the remaining extension period. The applicant for recovery shall attach to the tender and deposit proof of the determination of the fair rent amicably or judicially. In the event of the tenant's approval of the tender and deposit, he shall follow the procedures provided for in Clause 4 of Article 23, and thereupon the Notary Public shall deliver to the tenant a rate of 90% of the value of the tender and deposit in accordance with the rules, provided that the remaining value is paid upon completion of the actual vacation proven by a written acknowledgment by the owner and the tenant, or by the tenant alone, signed before the Notary Public.

The tenant who has received the amount of 90% of the value of the tender and deposit referred to in Article 25 above shall have a period of six months from the date of his receipt of the said amount to vacate the leased premises, during which he shall continue to pay the rent due, and after which he shall become an occupant of the leased premises without lawful justification, and shall be subject, for each day of delay, to a non-reducible coercive fine payable to the lessor, equal to the rent of (5) five days calculated on the basis of the fair rent.

Subject to the provisions of Article 32 of this Law, if the owner wishes to recover the leased premises for family necessity during the first year of the extension period (the nine years), he shall pay to the tenant compensation equal to four years' rent calculated on the basis of the fair market rent that has been determined. However, if the owner wishes to recover the leased premises during the first year of the extension period (the nine years) in order to demolish the building in which the leased premises are located and erect a new building in its place, he shall pay to the tenant compensation equal to six years' rent calculated on the basis of the fair market rent that has been determined. In the two aforementioned cases, the tenant who meets the conditions for obtaining a financial contribution from the Fund shall be entitled to submit to the Committee an application to obtain the financial contribution as set out below:

1- The application shall be submitted accompanied by the following documents:

a- A copy of the determination of the fair market rent determined by mutual consent or judicially.

b- A copy of the actual tender and deposit with the Notary Public. In the light of the documents, the Committee shall decide on the value of the contribution that the Fund would have paid to the lessor on behalf of the tenant from the date the contribution fell due until the end of the extended period, and shall deduct therefrom what the Fund has previously paid to the lessor in respect of increases occurring on the rent pursuant to this Law, in addition to the value of the compensation that the tenant received from the owner in return for the recovery of the leased premises in either of the two cases provided for in this Article, and the Committee shall notify the balance to the competent financial department to pay it to the tenant in equal monthly instalments starting from the first of the month following the date of actual vacation of the leased premises and until the end of the extended period.

2- However, if the leased premises sought to be recovered for family necessity or for demolition were leased while one of Law 29/67 and 10/74 was in force in buildings that were considered luxury, the compensation due to the tenant shall be reduced by half.

3- The owner shall pay the compensation to the tenant either directly by himself or by borrowing from any source he chooses, and the loan granted to the owner shall be deemed equivalent to a housing loan, whereupon the owner shall benefit from the exemptions provided for in Law No. 543 dated 24/7/1996.

4- Non-Lebanese tenants shall be excluded from the compensation if they own another residence in Lebanon.

5- In all the cases mentioned above and in the event of a request for recovery of the leased premises during the other extended years, the compensation that falls due to the tenant shall decrease proportionally with the remaining duration of the extension time-limit, that is at the rate of one ninth (1/9) for each year that has elapsed of the extension period.

If the owner wishes to recover the leased premises for cases other than the two cases of family necessity and demolition, he shall comply with the following:

1- Notify the tenant in writing of his initial wish to recover the leased premises within a time limit not exceeding two months from the date of determining the fair market rent by mutual consent or judicially with respect to the first extended year, and within the same time limit at the beginning of each year of the remaining extended years.

2- Obtain the initial approval of the tenant in writing to vacate the leased premises in exchange for compensation the value of which shall be agreed upon by the two parties. In all cases, neither the owner nor the tenant may invoke the initial approval issued by either of them for any reason whatsoever and before any authority.

3- The owner shall pay the compensation to the tenant directly from himself or by borrowing from any source he chooses, and the loan granted to the owner shall be deemed equivalent to a housing loan, and the owner shall then benefit from the exemptions provided for in Law No. 543 dated 24/7/1996.

4- The owner shall make a tender and deposit with the Notary Public in the district in which the leased premises are located the value of the compensation agreed upon with the tenant. In the event of the tenant's approval of the tender and deposit, he shall execute a declaration of approval and an undertaking to vacate the leased premises and deliver them vacant with the keys to the owner within the time limit agreed upon with the latter, during which the tenant shall continue to pay the rent due; the Notary Public shall then deliver to the tenant a rate of 90% of the value of the tender and deposit in accordance with the rules, provided that the remaining value is paid upon completion of the actual vacation of the leased premises and delivery of the keys by a written acknowledgment by the two parties or by the tenant alone signed before the Notary Public. If the tenant fails to vacate within the aforementioned time limit for vacating the leased premises and delivering them vacant to the owner, the tenant shall thereafter become an occupant of the leased premises without lawful justification and shall be subject, for each day of delay, to a non-reducible coercive fine paid to the lessor, equivalent to the rent of five days calculated on the basis of the fair market rent, and the lessor shall then be entitled to request directly from the President of the Execution Department to which the leased premises are subject to order the eviction by virtue of a petition to which is attached: a copy of each of the agreement executed between him and the tenant on the eviction, the actual tender and deposit with the Notary Public referred to above, and the receipt for collecting 90% of the value of the compensation, and this request shall be subject to the fixed fee. The decisions of the President of the Execution Department taken within the framework of the provisions of this paragraph shall not be subject to any avenue of appeal except opposition.

1- During the extended period that is the subject of Clause 1 of Article 15 of this Law, if the tenant who meets the conditions for obtaining a financial contribution from the Fund wishes to waive his tenancy, vacate the leased premises and hand them over vacant to the owner in return for obtaining a financial contribution paid to him by the Fund in monthly instalments as provided for in this Law, he must notify the owner in writing of this wish of his within a time limit not exceeding two months from the date of determination of the fair rent by mutual agreement or by judicial decision in respect of the first extended year and within the same time limit at the beginning of each year of the other extended years. The owner shall not be entitled to invoke the tenant's written wish to vacate the leased premises unless this tenant has obtained the contribution of the Fund.

2- For the purpose of calculating the value of the contribution, the calculation of the average monthly family income of the beneficiary shall be limited to the sum of the two average monthly incomes of the husband and wife only, to the exclusion of the remaining members of the beneficiary party.

3- The value of the contribution paid in monthly instalments as referred to in this Law shall be equal to the balance of the total monthly contributions that the Fund would have paid to the lessor on behalf of the tenant as provided for in Article 10 et seq. of this Law had the latter continued to occupy the leased premises, from the date on which the contribution falls due until the end of the extended period that is the subject of Clause 1 of Article 15 of this Law.

4- Subject to the provisions of Article 10 of this Law, the value of the monthly instalment in each year of the extended years shall be equal to the monthly contribution that the Fund would have paid to the owner on behalf of the tenant in settlement of the annual increase accruing on the rent pursuant to this Law.

5- In order to obtain the contribution, the tenant must follow the following:

(a)- The tenant shall submit to the Committee an application to obtain the contribution exempt from all fees, and the submission of this application shall not result in suspending the time limit for paying the increases on the rent resulting from the implementation of this Law.

(b)- The application must satisfy the following conditions:

- A copy of the lease contract or any document proving the tenancy.

(b)- 1- That it be submitted within a time limit not exceeding two months from the date of notifying the owner of his wish to waive the tenancy and vacate the leased premises.

(b)- 2- That the following documents be attached to the application:

- A copy of the determination of the fair rent by mutual agreement or by judicial decision.

- A copy of the letter notifying the owner of his wish to waive the tenancy and to vacate the leased premises.

- An undertaking to vacate the leased premises and hand them over vacant to the owner within a time limit of three months from the date on which he is notified of the Committee's approval of the payment of the contribution, during which time limit he shall continue to pay the rent value due from him.

6- In the light of the attached documents, the Committee shall decide on the value of the monthly instalments and their due dates, starting from the first of the month following the actual vacation of the leased premises and the handing over of the keys, proven "by a written acknowledgment signed by the owner and the tenant or by the tenant alone before the Notary Public, and until the end of the extended period provided for in Clause (a) of Article 15 of this Law.

7- The Committee shall notify its decision to the Finance Department in the region to which the leased premises belong, whereupon the contribution shall be paid in monthly instalments on their due dates.

8- The tenant shall be entitled to assign these instalments to a financing source of his choice which in return lends him the value of the contribution as a single lump sum, and the loan granted to him shall be deemed to be in the nature of a housing loan, in which case the tenant shall benefit from the exemptions provided for in Law No. 543/96 dated 24/7/1996.

Subject to the legal provisions relating to financial affairs which require the presentation of a fiscal or municipal clearance certificate, the payment of the contribution to the landlord or to the tenant may not in any case whatsoever be made conditional upon the necessity of presenting a fiscal or municipal clearance certificate.

In the event of the death of the tenant or his abandonment of the leased premises, the following shall ipso jure replace him in benefiting from the original lease contract, or the extended lease contract where applicable, with all its latest terms or those amended by operation of law:

1 - The spouse of the tenant or of the person who legally replaced him prior to 23/7/1992 .

2 - His relatives who entered the leased premises with him at the commencement of the execution of the lease and have continued to occupy it without interruption.

The judicial petition for the enforcement of eviction and all matters branching therefrom shall be subject to a fixed fee. Transactions shall be exempted from any proportional fee and from stamp duty on all court registry procedures relating to appraisals and their notification, or formal notices, or tender and deposit.

The tenant may not assign the leased premises or sublet it in whole or in part except with the written consent of the landlord and under the conditions agreed upon. If the original tenant assigns the leased premises and was expressly authorised to do so in the original lease contract or the contract extended by operation of law, the assignees shall benefit from the statutory extension and shall replace the original tenant, and their relationship with the landlord shall become direct. In the event of total or partial subletting with the express permission of the landlord in the original or extended contract, the lease relationship shall remain confined between the landlord and the original tenant, and the term of the sublease shall expire upon the expiry of the term of the original lease. A sublease concluded as from 23/7/1992 shall be subject to freedom of contract in accordance with the provisions of Law No. 159/92 . The landlord and the original tenant must request the joinder of the subtenant in every lawsuit brought against the original tenant, so that the judgment rendered against the original tenant shall have the force of res judicata against the subtenant, provided that the subtenant shall be entitled to claim compensation from the original tenant in the event that bad faith, fault, or negligence on the part of the latter is proven.

a) Subject to the provisions of Article 22 of this Law, the owner may request, for the purpose of his residence or the residence of one of his children, the recovery of the residential leased premises, provided that he proves a family necessity compelling him to recover it, and that neither he nor the person for whose benefit recovery is requested owns another dwelling that is suitable and fit for habitation, unoccupied, and equivalent in its standard to the leased premises sought to be recovered within the same municipal territory or a neighbouring municipal territory. The owner may also request the recovery of leased premises contiguous to the dwelling in which he resides, whether such contiguity is horizontal or vertical, if the purpose of the recovery is to annex the recovered leased premises to his residence and render it a dwelling securing the needs of the family. These provisions shall benefit whoever owns at least three-quarters of the shares of the leased real property, as well as the owner who obtains the written consent of his co-owners in common to secure this majority.

b) The owner of a hospital, an educational, instructional, or charitable institution, or an orphanage, a portion of whose real property or contiguous real properties is leased for residence, may recover such portion, provided that it is added to the principal premises and used for the purposes of the institution.

c) The owner may request the recovery of the leased premises for the purpose of demolishing the building in which the leased premises are located and erecting a new building in its place. For the purpose of erecting one or more storeys, he may request the recovery of the structure standing on the roof if such structure occupies less than half of the area permitted by the Building Law. In such a case, the owner shall bring a single action for recovery against all the tenants and shall prove that the real property on which a new building is intended to be constructed is buildable in accordance with the Building Law and urban planning requirements.

d) The provisions of this Law shall apply to pending actions for recovery in which no final and binding decision has been rendered prior to the date of entry into force of this Law.

An owner who has recovered his leased premises pursuant to the provisions of Article 22 of this Law shall be required to pay to the tenant an additional compensation equivalent to half the value of the compensation that he paid to the tenant, without the tenant being obliged to prove the damage that he suffered, in the two cases set forth below:

1- If the leased premises were recovered in accordance with either of the two purposes provided for in paragraphs (a) and (b) of Article (32) of this Law and the owner did not, without a legitimate justification, use them in accordance with the required purpose within a period of one year from the date of vacation, or did not continue, without a legitimate justification, to use them in that manner for at least three years.

2- If the leased premises were recovered for the purpose of demolition and reconstruction in accordance with the purpose provided for in paragraph (c) of Article (32) of this Law and the owner did not commence construction, without a legitimate justification, within a period of eighteen months from the date of vacation by the last tenant and did not complete it within a period not exceeding five years from the date of commencement of the work without a legitimate justification, or if he used the recovered leased premises for his residence or for his personal benefit or leased them to a third party during the one-year period set forth above.

The right to extension shall be forfeited and the tenant shall be ordered to vacate in the following cases:

a- If he fails to pay the rent due from him within two months after being notified in person or through an adult member of his family residing with him, of a formal notice addressed to him by means of an unsealed registered postcard with acknowledgment of receipt, or by means of a letter through a notary public, or by means of a formal notice issued by the Execution Department in accordance with the provisions of Article (51) of this Law. As for a legal person, it must, within a period of two months from the date of entry into force of this Law, elect a domicile, failing which the service procedures provided for in the Code of Civil Procedure shall apply to it. In the event that it is impossible to effect the notifications referred to in the preceding paragraph, service shall be effected by publication in two local daily newspapers designated by the judge of urgent matters after verifying the impossibility of service, upon the request of the lessor by a petition not subject to any fee or stamp of any kind whatsoever, and a copy of the formal notice shall be affixed to the door of the leased premises by a process server, and the two-month period shall run from the date of the last publication or affixation formality. In the event that it is impossible to effect service of the formal notice issued by the Execution Department, service shall be effected by publication and affixation in accordance with the same procedures pursuant to a decision issued by the Head of the Execution Department. The tenant shall bear the expenses of these formalities.

b- If the tenant misuses the leased premises by causing damage thereto not resulting from normal use, or uses it or allows it to be used in a manner inconsistent with the terms of the contract without the written approval of the lessor. It shall not be considered a misuse of the leased premises for a tenant who practices a liberal profession to practice his profession in a part of the leased premises designated for his residence for security reasons that forced him to leave the premises where he practiced his profession; in this case, the owner shall not be entitled to claim any compensation from the tenant, nor may the tenant claim any additional compensation therefor from the owner in cases of recovery. Installations set up by the tenant at his own expense shall not be considered a misuse of the leased premises, provided that they do not harm the structural soundness of the building; considered as such are works of installing an elevator and a water tank or providing heating, cooling, or hot water. Furthermore, works relating to the rehabilitation of the leased premises or the entrances of the building that are necessary for the needs of a disabled person residing therein, in accordance with the minimum standards for buildings and facilities pursuant to the Law relating to the Rights of Disabled Persons, shall not be considered a misuse of the leased premises, provided that such works are technically feasible and do not harm the structural soundness of the building. With the exception of simple superficial decoration and ornamental works and the installation of individual cooling and heating units, a tenant who wishes to benefit from the provisions of this Article must summon the lessor before the judge of urgent matters to seek permission to carry out the works he wishes to perform, which he must specify in order to enable the court to assess their legality and appropriateness. The tenant must take out insurance, bearing its costs alone, against all risks that may result from the works he carries out, as well as the expenses of the aforementioned works and the expenses of restoring the parts of the building that may have been damaged because of the works to their former state, without having the right of recourse against the owner to claim them or a part thereof, whether during his occupancy of the leased premises or on the date of termination of such occupancy. The value of the improvements resulting from the works mentioned in this paragraph shall not be included in the calculation of the recovery compensation.

c- If he assigns the leased premises or sublets it wholly or partially without the written approval of the lessor; in this case, the subtenant or the assignee must be joined as a party to the proceedings.

d- If the tenant constructs a building for residence, or if one becomes vacant for him, or if he acquires a vacant building of which he owns at least three-quarters and which is fit and suitable for his residence and equivalent to the standard of the leased premises he occupies in the same city or village, or in a place not more than ten kilometers away in a radial line from the leased premises. In these cases, the husband, the wife, the minor children residing with the tenant, as well as the adult children of the tenant who are his dependents, shall be deemed as one person for the application of the provisions of this paragraph, unless the condition of family necessity provided for in paragraph (a) of Article 32 of this Law is met in the situation of the children, subject to actual residence within a period not exceeding one year from the date of completion of the building, acquisition, or vacancy, and continuation of residence for a period of at least three years. Excluded from the provisions of this paragraph is the case where the tenant, or whoever is deemed with him as one person, acquires an apartment to use it as a commercial or tourist office or to practice a profession, and actually uses it for this purpose within six months from the date of acquisition and continues in the same use for a period of at least three years.

e- If he abandons the leased premises for a period of one year without interruption, despite his continuing to pay the rent. Lebanese officials and employees in official Lebanese missions abroad shall be excluded from the provisions of this item.

f- If he abandons the leased premises for a period of six months without interruption while owing any part of the rent, and has no domicile known to the owner at which to be served with the formal notice to pay, or has not elected a domicile in Lebanon at which to be served with this formal notice designated by him to the lessor by means of a letter or an unsealed registered postcard with acknowledgment of receipt in accordance with the service procedures provided for in paragraph (a) of this Article.

g- If the non-Lebanese tenant does not actually occupy the leased premises for a period of six months without interruption despite his payment of the rent.

The following shall benefit from the extension in the event of the lessee's death or abandonment of the leased premises:

First: With respect to premises leased for commercial or industrial purposes:

1- The lessee's heirs up to the third degree, or some of them according to the agreement among them.

2- The lessee's partners whose partnership is established on the date of the lease contract or on a prior date.

3- The beneficiaries of the provisions of Article 5 et seq. of Legislative Decree No. 11/1967 (relating to the commercial establishment). In this case, the lease of the premises allocated for operating the commercial establishment shall be extended and shall be transferred to the person to whom the said establishment is transferred. Premises leased for the purposes enumerated in Articles 6, 7 and 8 of the Code of Land Commerce shall be deemed commercial or industrial.

Second: With respect to premises leased for practising a liberal profession regulated by law:

1- The lessee's heirs, or some of them according to the agreement among them, provided that the heir practises any liberal profession regulated by law.

2- Any person to whom the leased premises have devolved by way of assignment from the lessee or from his heirs, provided that the assignee practises any liberal profession regulated by law, and provided that the assignment takes place, in the event of the lessee's death, within a period not exceeding two years from the date of death. If the leased premises are occupied by more than one person practising a liberal profession and one of them dies and none of his heirs practises the very same profession, his partners shall replace him in the lease under the same conditions of the contract, in return for compensation to the heirs equivalent to ten times the deceased's share in the annual rent in force on the date of death. In the event that the partner-lessee abandons the leased premises for any reason whatsoever, his partners shall replace him under the very same conditions of the contract.

Third: With respect to other premises:

1- The spouse, ascendants and descendants of the lessee, or some of them according to the agreement among them, provided that they practise the very same profession.

2- The lessee's partners whose partnership is established on the date of the lease contract or on a prior date.

3- Any person to whom the leased premises have devolved by way of assignment from the lessee or from the heirs mentioned in paragraph (1) above, provided that the assignee practises the very same profession, and provided that the assignment takes place officially before the notary public, in the event of the lessee's death, within a period not exceeding one year from the date of death. The owner shall have the right to double the rent in accordance with the provisions of Article (42) of this Law.

All persons benefiting from the extension pursuant to the provisions of this Article shall be deemed jointly and severally liable towards the lessor in the performance of their obligations.

A tenant subject to the provisions of this Law who acquires ownership of the dwelling that he occupies shall be exempted:

1- From the conveyance, mortgage and mortgage discharge fees relating to the dwelling that he occupies.

2- From the stamp duty payable on the contracts, documents and transactions drawn up on the occasion of the purchase of the said dwelling.

3- From the built property tax payable on the said dwelling for a period of ten years following the date of purchase. In such case, the owner shall also recover all legal fees payable on the building subdivision transaction and the stamp duty on all transactions and contracts that he executes for this purpose, provided that he submits to the Ministry of Finance, within a period of three months from the date of completion of this transaction, the documents proving the sale of the dwelling to its occupant, and provided that the proportion of the refund is equivalent to the proportion of the residential units that have been subdivided which he sells.

A tenant who vacates the leased premises during the extended period in accordance with the provisions of this Law shall benefit from the exemptions provided for in the preceding Article with respect to the dwelling of which he acquires ownership.

Subject to the dates set for the liberalisation of lease contracts provided for in Article (15) of this Law, priority in the granting of housing loans by both the Housing Bank and the Public Corporation for Housing shall be given to tenants subject to its provisions.

Until the entry into force of a special law regulating the relationship between the owner and the tenant in these contracts, lease contracts of non-residential premises concluded prior to 23/7/1992 shall be extended until 31/12/2018. During this period, the rents shall be indexed as of the date of entry into force of this Law and shall be increased annually at a rate equivalent to the annual inflation rate according to the official index issued by the Central Administration of Statistics in the preceding year, provided that the increase does not exceed five per cent (5%).

The tenant's right to extension shall be forfeited, in non-residential premises, in accordance with the provisions of paragraphs (a), (b), (c), (e), (f) and (g) of Article (34) of this Law, or if he effects a change in the intended use of the leased premises as specified in the lease contract.

The owner of real property leased for non-residential purposes has the right to recover the leased premises in accordance with the provisions of paragraphs (b) and (c) of Article (32) of this Law, and the owner shall be liable, in addition to the compensation specified in this Article, for another compensation for the loss to which the tenant is exposed as a result of the eviction (such as key money, loss of location and clientele, cessation of business and other matters). The provisions of Article 33 of this Law relating to additional compensation shall apply to the owner who has recovered his leased premises if its conditions are met.

Rentals shall be doubled once in the following cases:

a- For premises leased to a natural or legal person who is or becomes the owner of buildings or undivided shares in premises where his share of the total of their actual rentals exceeds ten times the rental of the leased premises which he occupies. For the purpose of calculating these rentals, the husband, wife and children residing with the tenant shall be deemed to be a single person, and the owner does not have the right to request this doubling from a single tenant or whoever replaces him by operation of this Law except once. An owner who previously claimed the fair rental under Law No. 160/1992, and benefited from this doubling, shall not benefit from the provisions of this paragraph.

b- For leases considered to be an element of a commercial establishment and which are the subject of an assignment contract or a free management contract in accordance with the provisions of Legislative Decree No. 11/1967, throughout the period of the free management.

c- For premises leased for the practice of a liberal profession regulated by law in the event of assignment thereof in accordance with the provisions of paragraph 2 of Item Second of Article (39) of this Law.

Unless there is an agreement placing the burden of all common expenses on the tenant, the owner shall bear 20% (twenty per cent) of the expenses of common services and maintenance, provided that his contribution does not exceed 5% (five per cent) of the total rents of the premises that benefit from these services, and the remainder shall be distributed among the units of which the building is composed, whether vacant or occupied by the owner or others. The expenses of renovating the external appearance of the building and the common parts or whatever is treated as such shall be incurred if the competent administration imposes the execution thereof. The area of each leased premises shall be taken into consideration when distributing the contribution shares among the occupants. Every dispute arising between the parties regarding the utility of the works, their value, or the distribution of the contribution shares shall be adjudicated by the Summary Affairs Judge in accordance with the rules of procedure followed before him pursuant to a decision enforceable expeditiously upon its original copy.

The lessor shall not be entitled to refrain from providing the common services that he has been accustomed to providing and that were originally agreed upon in the lease contract. Where such services include heating, cooling, or hot water, the lessor must provide adequate heating regularly from 15 November until 31 March of the following year, and cooling from the first of June until 15 October of the same year. As for hot water, he must provide it throughout the days of the year, all of the foregoing unless there is a contrary agreement in the contract. If the owner fails to perform, without legitimate justification, all or some of the services agreed upon or legally due, the tenant shall be entitled, after verification thereof through an expert appointed by the Summary Affairs Judge without the collection of any fee, to compensation equal to two months' rent, provided that the total compensation awarded, in a single lease year, does not exceed four months' rent.

1- Following the expiry of the term of the original contract, the lessee may, notwithstanding any agreement to the contrary, pay the rent on a monthly basis and in advance if the monthly rent exceeds the minimum wage on the due date of such rent.

2- The lessee shall not be adjudged to have forfeited the right of extension:

a) If he sends the rents to the lessor by means of a postal money order in a registered letter with acknowledgment of receipt within the statutory time limit to the place of residence of the lessor.

b) If he deposits the rents within the statutory time limit with the notary public practising in the district or city within the jurisdiction of either of which the leased premises are located. The notary public shall notify the lessor at his last address of the content of the deposit and invite him to collect the value thereof.

Both the owner and the lessee may enforce the judgment ordering recovery of possession, and if the owner fails to pay the amount of compensation due from him at the Execution Department, after being given formal notice by it, he shall be liable to an additional compensation of two percent per month of the value of the compensation, not subject to modification, which shall be calculated, enforced and collected directly through the Execution Department.

Common expenses referred to in this Law shall mean:

1- Common service expenses, which are:

a- Expenses for the consumption or generation of electrical current pertaining to the concierge's quarters, the lift, and all other common parts in a subdivided building and whatever is deemed as such in an unsubdivided building.

b- Expenses for the supply of cold water, including that extracted from artesian wells, hot water, heating and cooling.

c- The wage of the concierge equivalent to the minimum wage, in addition to increases including step increments, allowances, statutory compensations, contributions due to the National Social Security Fund and end-of-service indemnity; the housing allowance shall not be included in the calculation of the wage.

2- Maintenance expenses, which are: expenses for the maintenance of the building, whitewashing, painting, and repairs relating to water supply, cooling and heating equipment and their common installations, and to the lift and its insurance with an insurance company.

3- Refitting expenses, which are: expenses for refitting the building with machinery and equipment that provide common services; expenses for renovating the exterior appearance of the building and the common parts, or whatever is deemed as such, shall be deemed as refitting expenses.

The provisions of Article 847 and the articles following it of the Code of Civil Procedure relating to the enforcement of deeds and written undertakings shall apply to the collection of the rent fixed in lease contracts.

The original lease contract may be relied upon accompanied by a certificate issued by the municipality or the competent administration proving the renewal of the registration of the contract. Notwithstanding the provisions of Article 852 of the Code of Civil Procedure, an objection shall not stay enforcement unless the competent court decides otherwise, with or without security.

In all cases of repossession and forfeiture of extension, the court shall take into consideration the necessary expenses that the lessee has personally borne to carry out restoration works in the repossessed leased premises, as well as the period that has elapsed since the restoration works.

1- A sinking-rent contract means a contract whereby the owner of a real property permits another person to erect constructions or buildings on the said real property at his own expense in return for operating them for a period of time in return for rent specified in the contract.

2- Sinking-rent lease contracts concluded on or after 23/7/1992 shall be subject to the provisions contained therein. The same shall apply to lease contracts concluded by the operator over the constructions or buildings with third parties, provided that their term does not exceed the term of the original contract.

3- Sinking-rent lease contracts concluded before 23/7/1992 shall be extended for a period of three years starting from the date of entry into force of this Law if the original term ended before its entry into force. If their original term has not yet ended, they shall remain in force until the expiry of that term.

4- Lease contracts concluded between the operator and third parties before 22/7/1992 shall be subject to the provisions of this Law.

5- If the operator occupies the building or any part thereof and the occupancy dates back to before 23/7/1992, the operator shall be deemed a lessee and the provisions of this Law shall apply to him.

Notwithstanding any other provision, lease contracts relating to premises containing violations of the building or urban planning laws shall not be deemed void unless such violations are not capable of settlement under the laws in force. However, in the latter case, the judgment evicting the lessee shall not be enforced except concurrently with the removal of the violation by the lessor and in return for compensation paid to the lessee in accordance with the provisions on repossession for demolition provided for in this Law.
Subject to Article 22 of this Law, lawsuits instituted before the date of its entry into force shall remain subject to the provisions of the laws under which they were instituted.

1 - The lessor may request from the lessee, once a year, an advance on account to secure the common expenses equivalent to a rate of 75% of what he paid for the previous year, and in this case the lessees shall be entitled to appoint one of themselves to supervise the process of expending this advance.

2 - The lessor must draw up annually a detailed account of the expenses and a distribution thereof between himself and the lessees, showing the share of contribution of each of them, and serve it upon them, and each of them shall be entitled to inspect the invoices evidencing these expenses and to request a copy thereof at his own expense when necessary in order to object to their validity if he so wishes.

3 - The delay of the lessee in paying the advance or in paying his due share of the annual contribution after the final accounting shall be deemed tantamount to a delay in paying the rent and shall produce the effects provided for in paragraph (a) of Article (34) of this Law, provided that the formal notice is accompanied by a copy of all the documents evidencing the expenses.

1 - Notwithstanding any previous text or agreement, the lessee shall bear the full expenses of the non-common repairs specific to the leased premises.

2 - Any written agreement concluded between the occupants of three quarters of the units intended for lease or for occupation by the owner concerning the exemption of the owner from performing all or some of the common services shall be binding upon the owner and upon all the lessees.

The Single Civil Judge shall be vested with jurisdiction to hear and adjudicate all lease actions and all claims and defences ancillary thereto, whatever the amount of the annual rent may be. The first trial hearing in lease actions shall be scheduled without being bound by the time limits for the exchange of pleadings, and the judgment of first instance rendered in actions concerning the lease of built real property subject to this Law shall not be open to any of the ordinary or extraordinary means of recourse except opposition within the limits of Article 468 of the Code of Civil Procedure and appeal within a time limit of fifteen days from the date of service thereof, and the appellate judgment shall not be open to any of the ordinary or extraordinary means of recourse except opposition within the limits of Article 657 of the Code of Civil Procedure. However, the appellate judgment shall be open to cassation if there is a contradiction between it and the judgment of first instance with respect to forfeiture of the right to extension only. This shall apply to appellate judgments rendered as from 1/1/1987, whatever the law relied upon in those judgments may be. The summary jurisdiction within the scope of the provisions of the general law shall remain competent to hear emergent and urgent matters the adjudication of which does not touch upon the merits of the dispute.

A tenant covered by the provisions of paragraph (d) of the seventh Article of Law No. 539 dated 24/7/1996 and its amendments (Establishment of the Public Corporation for Housing) shall be granted absolute priority in subscribing to the special system of rent-to-own.
The details of application of the provisions of this Law shall be determined, where necessary, by decrees taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Justice and Finance.
This Law shall be published in the Official Gazette and shall enter into force six months after the date of its publication.

- The bill set forth in Decree No. 4116 dated 28 May 2010 aiming to protect women from domestic violence, as amended by the Joint Parliamentary Committees, has been ratified.

- This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.
The provisions of this Law shall apply to cases of domestic violence in accordance with the rules set forth in the subsequent articles.

The following terms, wherever they appear in the Law, shall mean the following:

Family: Includes either of the spouses, the father and mother of either of them, brothers and sisters, ascendants and descendants whether legitimate or illegitimate, and those bound by a tie of adoption, affinity up to the second degree, guardianship, tutorship, sponsorship of an orphan, or stepfathers or stepmothers.

Domestic Violence: Any act, omission, or threat thereof committed by one of its members against one or more family members, according to the concept set forth in the definition of the family, occurring during marital life or because of it, and resulting in killing or physical, psychological, sexual, or economic harm.

Upon receiving complaints and reports, and after consulting the Advocate General assigned to look into domestic violence cases and under his supervision, the Judicial Police shall:

- Hear the victim and the suspects, in the presence of the social worker mentioned in Article 5 of this Law at the victim's wish, after informing them of the rights provided for in Article 47 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

- Hear witnesses to domestic violence, including minor children, in the presence of the social delegate provided for in Article 34 of Law 422 dated 6/6/2002.

Members of the Judicial Police shall inform the victim of her right to obtain a protection order in accordance with the provisions of Article 12 et seq. of this Law, and to seek the assistance of a lawyer if she so wishes, in addition to informing her of all other rights provided for in Article 47 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

Offences of domestic violence shall be punished as follows:

1- Article 618 of the Penal Code is amended to read as follows:

Article 618: Whosoever drives a minor under eighteen years of age into begging shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to two years and by a fine ranging between the minimum wage and three times the amount thereof.

2- Article 523 of the Penal Code is amended to read as follows:

Article 523: Whosoever incites one or more persons, whether male or female, who have not attained twenty-one years of age, to debauchery, or facilitates it for them or assists them in committing it, shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to three years and by a fine ranging between twice the minimum wage and four times the amount thereof.

Whosoever engages in prostitution or facilitates it shall be punished by the same penalty.

Without prejudice to the provisions of Article 529 read in conjunction with Article 506, the penalty shall be increased in accordance with the provisions of Article 257 of this Law if the offence takes place within the family, regardless of the age of the person against whom the offence is committed.

3- Article 527 of the Penal Code is amended and a new paragraph is added thereto to read as follows:

Every person who relies, for earning his livelihood or part thereof, on the prostitution of others shall be punished by imprisonment from two years to three years and by a fine ranging between five times the minimum wage and ten times the amount thereof.

Without prejudice to the provisions of Article 529 read in conjunction with Article 506 of this Law, the penalty shall be increased in accordance with the provisions of Article 257 of the Penal Code if the offence takes place within the family, and the penalty shall be doubled if the offence is accompanied by any form of violence or threat.

4- A new paragraph is added to Article 547 of the Penal Code to read as follows:

Article 547: Whosoever intentionally kills a human being shall be punished by hard labour from fifteen years to twenty years.

The penalty shall be from twenty years to twenty-five years if the act of homicide is committed by one of the spouses against the other.

5- Article 559 of the Penal Code is amended to read as follows:

The penalties mentioned in this Sub-section shall be increased in accordance with the provisions of Article 257 if the act is committed in one of the circumstances set out in the second paragraph of Article 547 and in Articles 548 and 549 of this Law, insofar as applicable to the offence of causing bodily harm.

6- Articles 487, 488 and 489 of the Penal Code are amended to read as follows:

Article 487: Adultery committed by either of the spouses shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to two years. The same penalty shall be imposed on the partner in adultery if married; otherwise, by imprisonment from one month to one year.

Save for judicial confession and flagrante delicto, no evidence of proof shall be admitted against the partner other than such as arises from letters and written documents written by him.

The penalty shall be doubled for the offending spouse if the offence of adultery takes place in the matrimonial home.

Article 488: Either of the spouses shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year if he or she openly keeps a paramour in any place whatsoever. The same penalty shall be imposed on the partner.

Article 489:

- The act of adultery may not be prosecuted except upon the complaint of one of the spouses and the complainant taking the capacity of a civil party.

- The partner or accessory shall only be prosecuted together with the adulterer.

- A complaint shall not be admitted from the spouse with whose consent the adultery was committed.

- A complaint shall not be admitted upon the lapse of three months from the day on which the offence came to the knowledge of the complainant.

- Waiver of right in respect of the husband or wife shall extinguish the public prosecution and the civil actions in respect of all the offenders.

- If the plaintiff consents to resume life in common, the complaint shall lapse.

7 - a -

Whosoever, with the intent of exacting his marital rights to sexual intercourse or by reason thereof, batters his spouse or inflicts bodily harm upon him or her, shall be punished by one of the penalties provided for in Articles 554 to 559 of the Penal Code.

In the event of recurrence of the battery and infliction of bodily harm, the penalty shall be increased in accordance with the provisions of Article 257 of the Penal Code.

The withdrawal of the complainant shall extinguish the public prosecution in actions to which Articles 554 and 555 of the Penal Code apply.

The provisions governing recidivism and habitual criminality shall remain in force where the conditions thereof are met.

7 - b -

Whosoever, with the intent of exacting his marital rights to sexual intercourse or by reason thereof, threatens his spouse, shall be punished by one of the penalties provided for in Articles 573 to 578 of the Penal Code.

In the event of recurrence of the threat, the penalty shall be increased in accordance with the provisions of Article 257 of the Penal Code.

The withdrawal of the complainant shall extinguish the public prosecution in actions to which Articles 577 and 578 of the Penal Code apply.

The provisions governing recidivism and habitual criminality shall remain in force where the conditions thereof are met.

8 -- There is added to Sub-section 6 of Chapter Two of Title Six of Book Two of the Penal Code Article 503 bis 1, the text of which is as follows:

Whosoever exercises violence within the family that causes moral or economic harm to a family member, or leads to depriving any of them of basic needs, shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to three years and by a fine ranging between the minimum wage and three times the amount thereof, or by one of these two penalties.

The Appellate Public Prosecutor shall assign one or more Advocates General in the Governorate to receive and follow up on complaints relating to offences of domestic violence.

The First Investigating Judge shall also assign one or more Investigating Judges in the Governorate to investigate complaints relating to offences of domestic violence.

The First President of the Courts of Appeal shall assign one or more Criminal Single Judges, a Court of Appeal and a Criminal Court to hear actions relating to domestic violence, where there are multiple divisions or chambers, pursuant to a distribution of business decision.

There shall be established within the Directorate General of the Internal Security Forces a specialised unit for offences of domestic violence, which shall assume the duties of the Judicial Police in complaints submitted and referred to it in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

The unit shall be organised in accordance with the laws and regulations governing the Internal Security Forces so as to cover all Lebanese territory.

In forming the unit, consideration shall be given to including female personnel and ensuring that its personnel are sufficiently trained in conflict resolution and social guidance.

The members of the unit shall conduct their investigations in the presence of social workers specialised in family affairs and conflict resolution, chosen from a list drawn up by the Ministry of Social Affairs at the request of the victim after being informed by the investigating non-commissioned officer of her right to seek the assistance of a social worker. The jurisdiction of the unit shall remain in effect in the event of criminal complicity. The personnel of the unit may proceed to the scene of the crime whenever necessary and within the limits of the laws in force.
In addition to territorial jurisdiction in accordance with the general rules, the victim shall have the right to institute the action at her place of temporary or permanent residence.

Subject to the provisions of Article /41/ of the Code of Criminal Procedure, Judicial Police personnel shall proceed to the scene of the domestic violence without delay, after informing the Advocate General assigned to look into domestic violence cases, as follows:

. Where an offence of domestic violence in flagrante delicto is established.

. Where they are informed that a protection order concerning domestic violence is being breached.

Any Judicial Police officer who attempts to coerce the abused person or exert pressure on him with the aim of causing the latter to withdraw his complaint shall be punished by the penalty prescribed in Article 376 of the Penal Code.

Neglect by a Judicial Police officer of complaints and notifications in offences of domestic violence shall be deemed a serious disciplinary offence in accordance with the provisions of Article 130, paragraph 2, of Law No. 17 dated 6/9/1990 (Organisation of the Internal Security Forces), and the perpetrator thereof shall be referred to the Disciplinary Board.

The Advocate General assigned to receive complaints relating to domestic violence may, prior to the issuance of a protection order by the competent authority, instruct the Judicial Police, under his supervision, to take one or more of the following measures:

A- Obtaining an undertaking from the respondent to refrain from harassing the victim and the other persons enumerated in Article 12 of this Law, or from inciting harassment against them, on pain of the application of Sub-paragraph (1) or (2) of Paragraph (B) of this Article.

B - In the event of danger to the persons themselves:

1- Prohibiting the respondent from entering the family home for a period of 48 hours, renewable once, if there is no other means to secure protection for the victim, her children, and the other persons enumerated in Article 12 of this Law.

2- Detaining the respondent in accordance with Article 47 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

3- Transferring the victim and the other persons enumerated in Article 12, if they so wish, to a safe place at the expense of the respondent according to his financial capacity.

C - If the violence results in anything requiring medical or hospital treatment, the victims of the violence shall be transferred to the hospital, provided that the respondent advances the expenses of the treatment.

If the respondent abstains from advancing the expenses set forth in Sub-paragraph "3" of Paragraph "B" and in Paragraph "C" of this Article and the advances decided in the body of the protection decision, the procedures followed for the execution of alimony judgments in the Code of Civil Procedure shall apply against him.

Contrary to Article 999 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the decision to imprison the respondent who abstains from advancing the aforementioned expenses shall be issued by the Public Prosecution.

A protection order is a temporary measure issued by the competent judicial authority in accordance with the provisions of this Law on the occasion of examining cases of domestic violence.

The protection order aims to protect the victim and her children. As for the remaining descendants and the other persons residing with her, they shall benefit from the protection order if they are exposed to danger, as well as social workers, witnesses, and any other person providing assistance to the victim, in order to prevent the continuation of the violence or the threat of its repetition.

The children automatically covered by the protection order mean those who are at the age of thirteen and under.

A protection order shall comprise compelling the respondent to abide by one or more of the following measures:

1- Prohibiting interference with the victim and the other persons enumerated in Article 12 of this Law, or incitement to interfere with them.

2- Not interfering with the continued occupation of the family home by the victim and the persons residing with her who are covered by protection.

3- Removing the perpetrator of the violence from the home, temporarily and for a period determined by the competent authority, upon sensing any danger to the victim.

4- Removing the victim and those residing with her who are covered by protection, upon sensing any actual danger to them that may result from their continued occupation of the family home, to safe and suitable temporary accommodation.

In the event that the victim is removed from the home, her children who are aged thirteen and under shall be removed with her by operation of law, and the other children and residents shall also be removed with her if they are exposed to danger.

The respondent shall, according to his capacity, advance the accommodation expenses.

5- Advancing a sum, according to the capacity of the respondent, for food, clothing, and education, for those towards whom he is under an obligation.

6- Advancing a sum, according to the capacity of the respondent, on account of the expenses necessary for the medical or hospital treatment of the victim and the other persons enumerated in Article 12 of this Law if the violence committed resulted in that which necessitates such treatment.

7- Refraining from causing damage to any of the private property of the victim and of the persons covered by the protection order.

8- Refraining from causing damage to household furniture and common movable property and prohibiting the disposal thereof.

9- Enabling the victim, or whomever she authorises in the event of leaving the home, to enter it to take her personal property pursuant to a receipt record.

In every temporary advance, the victim or the respondent shall retain the right to apply to the competent courts to obtain the appropriate judgment in accordance with the rules in force before them.

The enforcement of a maintenance judgment issued by the competent courts shall stay the advance decided in the protection order.
The submission of an application for protection shall not preclude the right of the victim or the respondent to institute or pursue an action before the courts of all kinds and jurisdictions.
An application for protection shall be submitted without the need for the assistance of a lawyer and shall be exempted from judicial fees and expenses.

The application for protection shall be submitted before the Investigating Judge seized of the case or the Criminal Court examining it, and it shall be examined in chambers.

In all cases, the application may validly be submitted before the Judge of Urgent Matters by way of an ex parte petition.

Any minor may also apply for a protection order without his legal guardian.

The decision rendered by the Investigating Judge or the Single Criminal Judge shall be subject to appeal in accordance with the procedures established in the Code of Criminal Procedure.

The decision rendered by the Judge of Urgent Matters shall be subject to challenge in accordance with the procedures established for ex parte decisions in the Code of Civil Procedure.

Appealing or challenging the decision containing the protection order shall not stay execution unless the competent court decides otherwise.

The decision rendered by any of the judicial authorities mentioned in this article shall not be subject to cassation.

The protection decision shall be issued in all cases within a time limit not exceeding forty-eight hours.

A protection order issued by the competent judiciary shall be enforceable forthwith upon the original.

The judge of urgent matters may seek the assistance of the public force to enforce the protection order.

The protection order shall be enforced through the Family Public Prosecution in accordance with Article 11 of this Law.

Each of the victim, the other beneficiaries of the protection order, and the respondent or the defendant may request the judicial authority that issued the order to revoke or amend it upon the emergence of new circumstances.

The appeal mechanism provided for in Article 13 of this Law shall apply to the decision ordering the revocation or amendment.

Whoever violates a protection order shall be punished by imprisonment for up to one year and by a fine not exceeding twice the minimum wage, or by either of these two penalties.

If the violation is accompanied by the use of violence, the offender shall be punished by imprisonment for up to one year and by a fine not exceeding four times the minimum wage.

The penalty shall be doubled in the event of recidivism.
Trials before the authorities hearing offences of domestic violence shall be conducted in camera.

In addition to the penalties prescribed in accordance with the provisions of this Law, the court may oblige the perpetrator of a domestic violence offence to undergo anti-violence rehabilitation courses at specialised centres.

A special account shall be established in the Ministry of Social Affairs to undertake the assistance of victims of domestic violence and secure care for them, and to provide the means conducive to reducing and preventing offences of domestic violence and rehabilitating the perpetrators thereof.

This account shall be funded by:

- State contributions, for which purpose a nominal appropriation shall be allocated in the annual budget of the Ministry of Social Affairs.

- Donations.

- Funds resulting from fines imposed pursuant to this Law.

The regulations pertaining to the account shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Social Affairs.

With the exception of the rules of jurisdiction of the personal status courts and the provisions of personal status, which shall remain exclusively applicable within the scope of their jurisdiction, and the provisions of Law No. 422 dated 6/6/2002 (Protection of Juveniles in Conflict with the Law or at Risk), all texts contrary to this Law or inconsistent with the content thereof are hereby repealed.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The management of the funds of this Fund, including the rules of expenditure and collection, shall be subject to financial regulations ratified by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

The application of the provisions relating to the payment of increases on the rents shall be examined by a committee composed of an active or retired judge as chairman and of four members, one of whom represents the owners, the second the tenants, the third delegated by the Ministry of Finance, and the fourth delegated by the Ministry of Social Affairs.

The committee shall be appointed within a period of two months from the date of entry into force of this Law pursuant to a decree upon the proposal of each of the Ministers of Justice, Finance, and Social Affairs, and in the very same decree an alternate judge and four alternate members representing the very same entities provided for above shall be appointed.

More than one similar committee may be appointed in each governorate when necessary.

A clerk and a bailiff shall be attached to each committee, by a decision of the Minister of Justice.

The allowances of each of the chairman, the members, the clerk, and the bailiff shall be determined by decisions of the Ministers concerned.

The committee shall hold its meetings during or outside official working hours in the places determined by the Minister of Justice.

This committee shall have judicial capacity.

The tenant wishing to obtain a contribution from the Fund shall submit an application to the committee under whose jurisdiction the leased premises fall, exempted from all fees, and the submission of this application shall lead to the suspension of the period for payment of the increases on the rent resulting from the implementation of this Law until the entry into force of the committee's decision approving or disapproving the contribution.

The application must meet the following conditions:

1- That it be submitted within a period of two months from the date of determining the fair rent amicably or judicially with respect to the first extended year, and within the same period at the beginning of each year of the other extended years, under penalty of forfeiture of his right to benefit from the contribution.

2 - That the following documents be attached to the application:

A - A schedule of the names of the members of the benefiting group.

B - An employment certificate for each of the members of the benefiting group issued by the competent authority showing the value of the wage or salary according to the status of each of them as an employee, worker, or civil servant.

C - A personal income declaration for each of the members of the benefiting group in the event that he is self-employed.

The Committee shall examine applications for contribution in respect of the average monthly family income of the beneficiary and shall decide thereon in accordance with the following:

A- If the members of the benefiting party are wage earners, workers or employees, the average monthly family income of the beneficiary shall be the sum of the monthly incomes pertaining to each of them.

B- If any of the members of the benefiting party is self-employed, it shall lie with the Committee to verify, by the means it deems appropriate, his average monthly income, and consequently the average monthly family income of the beneficiary shall be equal to the sum of the average monthly incomes pertaining to each of the members of the benefiting party.

It shall lie with the Committee, in all cases, to verify by the means it deems appropriate the number and names of the members of the benefiting party and the average monthly income of the tenant and of each of those members, whereupon the average monthly family income of the beneficiary shall be calculated in accordance with what is set forth in this Article. Either of the two concerned parties may submit evidence and documents that assist in proving his claims.

The Committee may summon both the lessor and the tenant in order to hear them pursuant to a notice served upon them in accordance with the Code of Civil Procedure, and it must issue its decision within a time limit not exceeding two months from the date of submission of the application.

Sole Article: The draft law set forth in Decree No. 7104 dated 3 January 2002 aiming at enacting the Rent Law, as amended by the Administration and Justice Committee, has been ratified.

- This Law shall be published in the Official Gazette and shall enter into force six months after the date of its publication.
All lease contracts of built real properties concluded before 23/7/1992 shall be subject to the provisions of this Law.

The following shall be exempted from the provisions of this Law:

a) Lease contracts of agricultural lands and the buildings annexed thereto.

b) Seasonal lease contracts relating to summer and winter resort premises.

c) Contracts pursuant to which employers provide premises for the housing of their employees free of charge or for consideration.

d) Occupation of public property of the State and municipalities.

e) Lease contracts of villas that meet the following specifications:

That they consist of one or more storeys and are leased for the dwelling of a single tenant, and have a garden, a garage, a heating system, and a private system providing hot water even if the tenant bears the expenses of providing the same, provided that these specifications were met on the date of commencement of the original lease.

A special fund for residential leases covered by the provisions of this Law (referred to in this Law as the Fund) shall be established, which shall be attached to the Ministry of Finance and whose accounts shall be kept at the Treasury Directorate in the said Ministry.

This Fund aims to assist all tenants concerned by this Law whose average monthly income does not exceed three times (3) the minimum wage, by contributing to the payment of the increases, in whole or in part as the case may be, that occur to their rents in implementation of the provisions of this Law. Wherever mentioned in this Law, the tenant shall mean the tenant or whoever has legally succeeded him.

Upon requesting to benefit from the contribution of the Fund, and for the purpose of determining the average monthly family income, the beneficiary or the beneficiary party, wherever mentioned in this Law, shall mean the tenant and the legal occupants of the leased premises with him.

A tenant who leased in accordance with the provisions of either of the two Laws 29/67 and 10/74 in buildings that were considered luxury buildings, and a non-Lebanese tenant, shall not benefit from the benefits of this Fund.

The revenues of the Fund shall consist of:

- Annual contributions from the State allocated in the budget of the Ministry of Finance to cover the obligations of the Fund.

- Grants, donations, and bequests after the approval thereof by the Council of Ministers; the value of these grants and bequests shall be deducted from the amounts taken as a basis for determining the income tax due, as well as deducted from the amounts taken as a basis for determining transfer duties, and shall be exempted from the duties imposed on grants.

Subject to the provisions of each of Articles 8 and 11 of this Law, the Committee shall rule, in the light of the outcomes of its procedures regarding the determination of the average monthly family income of the beneficiary, on the eligibility for the application for contribution from the Fund or the lack thereof, as well as on the value of the contribution, in accordance with the following:

1- If the Committee decides that the average monthly family income of the beneficiary exceeds three times the minimum wage, it shall reject the contribution for lack of eligibility therefor, and the lessee shall be required to pay the new rent resulting from the application of the increases provided for in this Law under pain of being deemed in default, whereupon the provisions of this Law shall apply to him.

2 - If the Committee decides that the average monthly family income of the beneficiary does not exceed three times the minimum wage, the President of the Committee shall notify the decision to the Financial Department in the district to which the leased premises belong, and the latter shall pay to the lessor the contribution due in monthly instalments for the extended year for which the lessee submitted the application for contribution, as set out below:

A - The case of an average monthly family income of the beneficiary that does not exceed twice the minimum wage. The Committee shall determine by its decision the value of the monthly instalment such that it is equal monthly to the difference between the value of the rent and the value of the new rent. The Committee shall notify its decision to the competent Financial Department to take the necessary action in accordance with what is set out in this item.

B - The case of an average monthly family income of the beneficiary that exceeds twice the minimum wage and does not exceed three times this wage.

The Committee shall determine by its decision the value of the monthly instalment such that it is equal monthly to the difference, if any, between 30% of the average monthly family income of the beneficiary and the value of the new rent. The Committee shall notify its decision to the competent Financial Department to take the necessary action in accordance with what is set out in this item.

The contributions that the Fund is required to pay to the lessor shall remain incumbent upon this Fund, and the lessor may not invoke them for any reason and before any authority against the lessee as being a part of the rent not paid by the latter.

In the event that the lessee wishes to continue to benefit from the contribution of the Fund for the subsequent extended years, he must follow the working mechanism referred to above with the Committee, at the beginning of each extended year up to the ninth year inclusive.

The application for contribution as provided for in Article 8 shall result in suspending the time limit for the payment of the increases resulting from the provisions of this Law, until the entry into force of the decision of the Committee approving or disapproving the same.

Any person who gives the Committee a false certificate or declaration, or uses or benefits from either of them, shall be prosecuted for the offence of forgery and the use of forged documents, and upon the discovery of any false declaration or certificate and its use and benefit therefrom, the Committee shall, as the case may be, notify the Public Prosecution of the matter, and the tenant's right to obtain the contribution from the Fund shall lapse.
In all cases, the decision issued by the Committee shall be deemed final and enforceable upon its original and shall not be subject to any form of appeal.

Lease contracts for residential built real properties concluded before 23/7/1992 shall be subject to the provisions of this Title.

A residential lease contract shall be deemed to be a contract pertaining to premises designated for residence; as for premises leased under a single contract for residence and for non-residence, they shall be deemed residential premises merely by virtue of their use for residence.

Lease contracts for residential premises shall be extended for up to nine years from the date of entry into force of this Law, provided that the tenant pays the value of the fair rent gradually in accordance with the following:

A - Subject to the provisions of Article (20) of this Law, the value of the fair rent shall be determined by mutual agreement or judicially in accordance with what is provided for in Article (18).

B - The rent due on the date of entry into force of this Law shall be increased annually and successively in accordance with the following:

15% fifteen per cent of the value of the increase difference between the rent in force prior to the entry into force of this Law and the fair rent referred to above, for each year of the first four extended years following the date of entry into force of this Law.

20% twenty per cent of the value of the increase difference noted above, for each of the fifth and sixth years of the extended period until the rent in the sixth extended year reaches the value of the fair rent referred to in Item (A) above.

C - The rent in the seventh, eighth, and ninth extended years shall be equal to the value of the fair rent referred to in Item (A) above.

D - At the end of the ninth extended year, the lease shall become free.

1- A tenant who continues to satisfy the conditions for benefiting from the contributions of the Fund may request from the landlord in writing, three months before the expiry of the term of the lease in the ninth extended year on pain of forfeiture of the right, the drawing up of a new lease agreement for a maximum term of three years at a rent equal to the fair market rent referred to in paragraph (a) of Article 15 above, provided that he proves within the same time limit that he has obtained a decision from the Committee that he satisfies the conditions for benefiting from the contributions of the Fund, in accordance with the mechanism provided for in this Law.

2- Such tenant may waive his right to request the drawing up of a new lease agreement and notify the landlord in writing within the same time limit mentioned above of his wish to vacate the leased premises in return for obtaining a financial contribution paid to him by the Fund in monthly instalments as provided for below. The landlord may not invoke the tenant's written wish to vacate the leased premises unless the said tenant has obtained the contribution of the Fund.

3- To obtain the contribution, the tenant shall observe the following:

a- The tenant shall submit to the Committee within the time limit mentioned above an application to obtain the contribution. The submission of this application shall not result in suspending the time limit for payment of the increases on the rent resulting from the implementation of this Law.

b- He shall attach to the application the following documents:

- A copy of the letter notifying the landlord of his wish to waive the tenancy and vacate the leased premises.

- An undertaking to vacate the leased premises and deliver them vacant to the landlord within a period of three months from the date on which he is notified of the Committee's approval of the payment of the contribution, and during this period he shall continue to pay what is due from him of the amount of the rent.

4- The Committee shall rule, in the light of the attached documents, on the amount of the monthly instalments and their due dates, starting from the first of the month following the actual vacating of the leased premises and the delivery of the keys, evidenced by a written acknowledgment signed by the landlord and the tenant, or by the tenant alone, before a notary public, and until the expiry of the term of the new lease agreement.

5- The Committee shall notify its decision to the Finance Department in the district to which the leased premises belong, whereupon the contribution shall be paid in monthly instalments on their due dates.

6- The tenant may assign these instalments to a financing source of his choice, which in return lends him the amount of the contribution as a single lump sum; the loan granted to him shall be deemed to be a housing loan, and the tenant shall then benefit from the exemptions provided for in Law No. 543 dated 24/7/1996.

7- If the Committee decides that the tenant does not fulfil the conditions for benefiting from the contributions of the Fund, his tenancy shall become free as from the date of the Committee's decision.

In the case where the tenant vacates the leased premises of his own accord in return for a financial contribution obtained by him from the Fund, if he meets the conditions for benefiting from this Fund, the provisions of Article 27 of this Law shall apply.

The fair rent shall be determined:

a - Amicably by agreement between the lessor and the tenant, provided that this rent shall be subject to the decision of the Committee in the event that the tenant requests from it to obtain a financial contribution from the Fund.
