b - If the determination of the fair rent is not reached amicably by agreement between the lessor and the tenant within the first three months following the date of entry into force of this Law, the lessor may follow the following procedures:

1- The lessor shall seek the assistance of two experts from the list of sworn experts in the governorate registered with the courts, one of whom shall be a civil engineer or an architect and the second from among those working in real estate valuation registered on the roll of experts. The two experts shall undertake to draw up a valuation of the fair rent of the leased premises in accordance with the rules provided for in Article (19) of this Law.

2 - The lessor shall, through the notary public, serve the report of the fair valuation upon the tenant, who must, within two months from being served with the report, either approve it and adopt it in determining the fair rental value or submit a counter-valuation report by seeking the assistance of two experts from the list of sworn experts in the governorate registered with the courts, one of whom shall be a civil engineer or an architect and the second from among those working in real estate valuation and registered on the roll of experts. The two experts appointed by the tenant shall undertake to draw up a valuation of the fair rent of the leased premises in accordance with the rules provided for in Article 19 of this Law.

3 - The tenant must serve the valuation report drawn up by the two experts appointed by him in order to serve it upon the owner through the notary public within the aforementioned two-month period, under penalty of forfeiture of his right to object to the valuation sent by the owner or even to invoke the content of a counter-report.

4 - If the two reports differ, each of the lessor and the tenant may resort to the Committee in the governorate to which the leased premises belong in order to adjudicate the dispute arising from the discrepancy, attaching to his application a copy of the two reports and their annexes, including copies of the service documents.

The Committee shall issue a reasoned decision, and its decision shall be final and not subject to any form of appeal.

The report must include, under penalty of nullity, the names of the drafters, the drafters of the report, and their reference on the roster of experts, a statement of the person who commissioned them to draw up the report, a statement of the date on which the valuation was carried out, and the means relied upon in carrying out the valuation, from the area of the apartment to the type of building and the estimation of the average building costs (popular, medium to popular, medium to luxury, luxury), and the share of the area of the real property appertaining to the apartment, taking into account the status of the ground floor if the floor is intended for commerce, with the valuation of the sale price per square metre in an unencumbered building and in a leased building, and a statement of that which diminishes the value of the average cost per square metre of the building due to age or misuse, or that which increases the value of the building apart from the improvements introduced by the tenant and which may result from the location, the view, or otherwise, and that upon which the experts have relied in estimating the sale price per square metre by way of sales or valuations by official administrations.

The report and its annexes must bear the signature of the two experts on every page thereof and the date on which the report was drawn up.
The fair rent shall be determined on the basis of a rate of (5%) five per cent of the sale value of the leased premises in their existing condition as if they were vacant.

The experts shall be liable for the content of the report which they have drawn up, for the authenticity of the documents annexed thereto, and for the outcome of the valuation.

For the purposes of this Law, the two experts appointed by either the owner or the tenant shall be deemed as if they were appointed by the judiciary.

Subject to the provisions of Article 32 of this Law, if the owner wishes to recover the leased premises for family necessity during the first year of the extension period (the nine years), he must pay the tenant compensation equal to four years' rent calculated on the basis of the fair market rent that has been determined.

However, if the owner wishes to recover the leased premises during the first year of the extension period (the nine years) in order to demolish the building in which the leased premises are located and erect a new building in its place, he must pay the tenant compensation equal to six years' rent calculated on the basis of the fair market rent that has been determined. In the two aforementioned cases, the tenant who meets the conditions for obtaining a financial contribution from the Fund is entitled to submit an application to the Committee to obtain the financial contribution as set out below:

1- The application shall be submitted accompanied by the following documents:

أ - A copy of the determination of the fair market rent determined by mutual consent or judicially.

ب - A copy of the formal tender and deposit with the Notary Public. In light of the documents, the Committee shall decide on the amount of the contribution that the Fund would have paid to the lessor on behalf of the tenant from the due date of the contribution until the end of the extended period, and shall deduct therefrom what the Fund has previously paid to the lessor of increases accruing to the rent pursuant to this Law, in addition to the amount of the compensation that the tenant received from the owner in return for the recovery of the leased premises in either of the two cases provided for in this Article, and the Committee shall notify the balance to the competent financial department to pay it to the tenant in equal monthly instalments starting from the first of the month following the date of the actual vacation of the leased premises and until the end of the extended period.

2 - However, if the leased premises sought to be recovered for family necessity or for demolition were leased while one of the Law 29/67 and 10/74 was in force in buildings that were considered luxury, the compensation payable to the tenant shall be reduced by half.

3 - The owner shall pay the compensation to the tenant either directly from himself or by borrowing from any source he chooses, and the loan granted to the owner shall be deemed equivalent to a housing loan, and the owner shall then benefit from the exemptions provided for in Law No. 543 dated 24/7/1996.

4 - Non-Lebanese tenants are exempted from the compensation if they own another residence in Lebanon.

5 - In all the cases mentioned above and in the event of an application to recover the leased premises during the other extended years, the compensation to which the tenant is entitled decreases proportionally with the remaining duration of the extension period, i.e. at the rate of one-ninth (1/9) for each year that has elapsed of the extension period.

The owner of leased premises leased during the validity of either of the two Laws 29/67 and 10/74 in buildings that were considered luxury may recover the leased premises in cases other than the two cases of family necessity and demolition in return for his paying to the tenant a compensation equal to half of the compensation due in the case of demolition and provided for in Clause 2 of Article 22 above, and in this case the provisions of the aforementioned Article shall not apply in respect of the contradiction of the compensation proportionally with the remaining period of the extension time limit.

Subject to the provisions of Articles 22, 23 and 24 of this Law, the owner shall, in all cases of recovery provided for in this Law, tender and deposit with the Notary Public in the area in which the leased premises are located the compensation determined under this Law or agreed upon amicably with the tenant, with a clear reference to its proportional decrease with the remaining extension period.

The applicant for recovery shall attach to the tender and deposit proof of the determination of the fair rent amicably or judicially.

In the event that the tenant agrees to the tender and deposit, he shall follow the procedures provided for in Clause 4 of Article 23, and thereupon the Notary Public shall deliver to the tenant a rate of 90% of the value of the tender and deposit in due form, provided that he pays the remaining value upon completion of the actual vacation proven by a written acknowledgment by the owner and the tenant or by the tenant alone signed before the Notary Public.

The tenant who received the 90% of the value of the tender and deposit referred to in Article 26 above shall have a time limit of six months from the date of his receipt of the aforementioned amount to vacate the leased premises, during which he shall continue to pay the rent due, and after which he shall become an occupant of the leased premises without lawful justification, and shall be subject, for each day of delay, to an non-reducible coercive fine paid to the lessor, equivalent to the rent of (5) five days calculated on the basis of the fair rent.

If the owner wishes to recover the leased premises for other than the two cases of family necessity and demolition, he must follow the following:

1- Notify the tenant in writing of his preliminary desire to recover the leased premises within a period not exceeding two months from the date of determining the fair rent amicably or judicially with respect to the first extended year and within the same period at the beginning of each year of the remaining extended years.

2 - Obtain the preliminary consent of the tenant in writing to vacate the leased premises in return for compensation the value of which is agreed upon by the two parties. In all cases, neither the owner nor the tenant may invoke the preliminary consent issued by either of them for any reason whatsoever and before any authority.

3 - The owner shall pay the compensation to the tenant directly from himself or by borrowing from any source he chooses, and the loan granted to the owner shall be deemed equivalent to a housing loan, and the owner shall then benefit from the exemptions provided for in Law No. 543 dated 24/7/1996.

4 - The owner must tender and deposit with the Notary Public in the area in which the leased premises are located the value of the compensation agreed upon with the tenant.

In the event that the tenant agrees to the tender and deposit, he must draw up a declaration of consent and an undertaking to vacate the leased premises and hand them over vacant with the keys to the owner within the period agreed upon with the latter, during which the tenant shall continue to pay the rent due, whereupon the Notary Public shall deliver to the tenant 90% of the value of the tender and deposit in accordance with due process, provided that the remaining value is paid upon completion of the actual vacation of the leased premises and the handing over of the keys by a written acknowledgment by the two parties or by the tenant alone signed before the Notary Public.

If the tenant fails to vacate within the aforementioned period for vacating the leased premises and handing them over vacant to the owner, the tenant shall thereafter become an occupant of the leased premises without lawful justification and shall be subject, for each day of delay, to a non-reducible coercive fine paid to the lessor, equivalent to the rent of five days calculated on the basis of "the fair rent", and the lessor shall then have the right to request directly from the Head of the Execution Department to which the leased premises belong to order the vacation by virtue of a petition to which is attached:

A copy of each of the agreement drawn up between him and the tenant on the vacation, the actual tender and deposit with the Notary Public referred to above, and the receipt for receiving 90% of the value of the compensation, and this request shall be subject to the fixed fee.

The decisions of the Head of the Execution Department taken within the framework of the provisions of this paragraph shall not be subject to any means of recourse except opposition.

1- During the extended period that is the subject of Item 1 of Article 15 of this Law, if a tenant who meets the conditions for obtaining a financial contribution from the Fund wishes to waive his lease, vacate the leased premises, and deliver them vacant to the owner in return for obtaining a financial contribution paid to him by the Fund in monthly instalments as provided for in this Law, he must notify the owner in writing of this wish of his within a time limit not exceeding two months from the date on which the fair rent is determined amicably or judicially in respect of the first extended year, and within the same time limit at the beginning of each of the other extended years.

The owner shall not be entitled to invoke the tenant's written wish to vacate the leased premises unless the said tenant has obtained the contribution of the Fund.

2 - For the purpose of calculating the value of the contribution, the calculation of the average monthly family income of the beneficiary shall be limited to the sum of the two average monthly incomes of the husband and the wife only, to the exclusion of the remaining members of the beneficiary group.

3 - The value of the contribution paid in monthly instalments as mentioned in this Law shall be equal to the balance of the total monthly contributions that the Fund would have paid to the lessor on behalf of the tenant, as provided for in Article 10 and the following articles of this Law, had the latter continued to occupy the leased premises, from the date the contribution falls due until the end of the extended period that is the subject of Item 1 of Article 15 of this Law.

4 - Subject to the provisions of Article 10 of this Law, the value of the monthly instalment in each of the extended years shall be equal to the monthly contribution that the Fund would have paid to the owner on behalf of the tenant in settlement of the annual increase occurring to the rent pursuant to this Law.

5 - In order to obtain the contribution, the tenant must follow the following:

a- The tenant submits to the Committee an application to obtain the contribution, exempted from all fees, and the submission of this application shall not result in suspending the time limit for paying the increases to the rent resulting from the implementation of this Law.

b- The application must meet the following conditions:

- A copy of the lease contract or any document proving the lease.

b- 1- That it be submitted within a time limit not exceeding two months from the date of notifying the owner of his wish to waive the lease and vacate the leased premises.

b- 2- That the following documents be attached to the application:

- A copy of the amicable or judicial determination of the fair rent.

- A copy of the letter notifying the owner of his wish to waive the lease and vacate the leased premises.

- An undertaking to vacate the leased premises and deliver them vacant to the owner within a time limit of three months from the date on which he is notified of the Committee's approval to pay the contribution, while continuing during this time limit to pay the amount of rent due from him.

6 - In light of the attached documents, the Committee shall rule on the value of the monthly instalments and their due dates, starting from the first of the month following the actual vacation of the leased premises and the delivery of the keys, evidenced " "by a written acknowledgement signed by the owner and the tenant, or by the tenant alone before the notary public, and until the end of the extension period provided for in Item (a) of Article 15 of this Law.

7 - The Committee shall notify its decision to the Finance Department in the district to which the leased premises belong, whereupon the contribution shall be paid in monthly instalments on their due dates.

8 - The tenant shall be entitled to assign these instalments to a financing source of his choice which lends him in return the value of the contribution in a single lump sum, and the loan granted to him shall be deemed equivalent to a housing loan, whereupon the tenant shall benefit from the exemptions provided for in Law No. 543/96 dated 24/7/1996.

a) Subject to the provisions of Article 22 of this Law, the owner may request, for the purpose of his own residence or the residence of one of his children, the recovery of the residential leased premises, provided that he proves a family necessity compelling him to recover them, and that neither he nor the person in whose interest recovery is requested owns another dwelling that is suitable and fit for habitation, unoccupied, and equivalent in standard to the leased premises sought to be recovered within the same municipal area or an adjacent municipal area. The owner may also request the recovery of leased premises contiguous to the dwelling in which he resides, whether such contiguity is horizontal or vertical, if the purpose of the recovery is to annex the recovered leased premises to his residence and make it a dwelling meeting the needs of the family.

Whoever owns at least three-quarters of the shares in the leased property, and the owner who obtains the written consent of his co-owners in common to secure this majority, shall benefit from these provisions.

b) The owner who is the proprietor of a hospital, or an educational, instructional, or charitable institution, or an orphanage, a part of whose property or contiguous properties is leased for habitation, may recover such part, provided that it is added to the principal property and used for the purposes of the institution.

c) The owner may request the recovery of the leased premises for the purpose of demolishing the building in which the leased premises are located and erecting a new building in its place.

He may also, in order to erect one or more storeys, request the recovery of the structure standing on the roof if such structure occupies less than half of the area permitted by the Building Law.

In such a case, the owner must bring a single recovery action against all the tenants, and he must prove that the property on which a new building is intended to be constructed is buildable in accordance with the Building Law and the requirements of urban planning.

d) The provisions of this Law shall apply to pending recovery actions in which no final and binding decision has been issued prior to the date of entry into force of this Law.

The owner who has recovered his leased premises pursuant to the provisions of Article 22 of this Law shall be obliged to pay to the tenant an additional compensation equivalent to half the value of the compensation that he paid to the tenant without the tenant being obliged to prove the damage that befell him, in the two cases set forth below:

1- If the leased premises were recovered in accordance with one of the two purposes provided for in paragraphs (a) and (b) of Article (32) of this Law and the owner did not use them without a legitimate justification in accordance with the required purpose within a period of one year from the date of eviction, or did not continue without a legitimate justification to use them in that manner for at least three years.

2 - If the leased premises were recovered for the purpose of demolition and reconstruction in accordance with the purpose provided for in paragraph (c) of Article (32) of this Law and the owner did not commence construction without a legitimate justification within a period of eighteen months from the date of eviction of the last tenant and did not complete it within a period not exceeding five years from the date of commencement of the work without a legitimate justification, or if he used the recovered leased premises for his residence or for his personal benefit or leased them to a third party during the period of one year set forth above.

Subject to the legal provisions relating to financial affairs which require the presentation of a financial or municipal clearance certificate,

The payment of the contribution to the owner or to the tenant may not in any case whatsoever be conditional upon the necessity of presenting a financial or municipal clearance certificate.

In the event of the death of the tenant or his vacating the leased premises, he shall be replaced ipso jure in benefitting from the original lease contract, or the extended lease contract as the case may be, with all its latest terms or those amended by operation of law, by:

1- The spouse of the tenant or of the person who legally replaced him prior to the date of 23/7/1992.

2- His relatives who entered the leased premises with him at the commencement of the execution of the lease and who have continued to occupy them without interruption.

Judicial proceedings for the enforcement of eviction and all matters branching therefrom shall be subject to the fixed fee. Transactions shall be exempted from any proportional fee and from stamp duty on all notary public procedures relating to assessments and their notification, or formal notices, or tender and deposit.

The tenant may not assign the leased premises or sublease them wholly or partially except with the written consent of the owner and under the conditions agreed upon. If the original tenant assigns the leased premises and was expressly authorised to do so in the original lease contract or the lease contract extended by operation of law, the assignees shall benefit from the statutory extension, shall replace the original tenant, and their relationship with the owner shall become direct.

In the event of a total or partial sublease with the express permission of the owner in the original or extended contract, the lease relationship shall remain confined between the owner and the original tenant, and the term of the sublease shall expire upon the expiry of the term of the original lease.

A sublease concluded as from 23/7/1992 shall be subject to freedom of contract in accordance with the provisions of Law No. 159/92.

The owner and the original tenant must request the joinder of the subtenant in every action brought against the original tenant, in order for the judgment rendered against the original tenant to have the force of res judicata against the subtenant, provided that the subtenant shall be entitled to claim compensation from the original tenant in the event that bad faith, fault, or negligence on the part of the latter is established.

A tenant subject to the provisions of this Law who acquires ownership of the dwelling that he occupies shall be exempted:

1- From the transfer, mortgage registration and mortgage release fees relating to the dwelling that he occupies.

2 - From the stamp duty payable on the contracts, documents and transactions executed on the occasion of the purchase of the said dwelling.

3 - From the built property tax payable on the said dwelling for a period of ten years following the date of purchase. In this case, the owner shall also recover all the legal fees payable on the building subdivision transaction and the stamp duty on all transactions and contracts that he carries out for this purpose, provided that he submits to the Ministry of Finance, within a period of three months from the date of completion of this transaction, the documents proving the sale of the dwelling to its occupant, and provided that the proportion of the refund is equivalent to the proportion of the residential units that have been subdivided which he sells.

A tenant who vacates the leased premises during the extended period in accordance with the provisions of this Law shall benefit from the exemptions provided for in the preceding Article with respect to the dwelling of which he acquires ownership.

Subject to the dates set for the liberalisation of lease contracts provided for in Article (15) of this Law, priority in granting housing loans by both the Housing Bank and the Public Corporation for Housing shall be given to tenants subject to its provisions.

"Until the entry into force of a special law regulating the relationship between the owner and the tenant in these contracts, lease contracts for non-residential premises concluded prior to 23/7/1992 shall be extended until 30/6/2022 inclusive".

During this period, rents shall be indexed as of the date of entry into force of this Law and shall be increased annually at a rate equivalent to the annual inflation rate according to the official index issued by the Central Administration of Statistics in the preceding year, provided that the increase does not exceed five percent (5%).

The right to extension shall lapse and the tenant shall be ordered to vacate in the following cases:

A- If he fails to pay the rent that has fallen due from him within two months after being served, in person or through one of the adult members of his family residing with him, with a formal notice addressed to him by means of an open registered card with acknowledgment of receipt, or by means of a letter through the Notary Public, or by means of a formal notice issued by the Execution Department in accordance with the provisions of Article (51) of this Law.

As for a legal person, it must, within a period of two months from the date of entry into force of this Law, elect a domicile, failing which the rules of service provided for in the Code of Civil Procedure shall apply to it. Where it is impossible to effect the notifications referred to in the preceding paragraph, service shall be effected by publication in two local daily newspapers designated by the Judge of Urgent Matters after verifying the impossibility of service, upon the request of the lessor by a petition not subject to any fee or stamp of any kind whatsoever, and a copy of the formal notice shall be affixed to the door of the leased premises through a bailiff, and the two-month period shall run from the date on which the last formality of publication or affixing took place.

Where it is impossible to effect service of the formal notice issued by the Execution Department, service shall be effected by publication and affixing in accordance with the same rules pursuant to a decision taken by the Head of the Execution Department. The tenant shall bear the expenses of these formalities.

B - If the tenant misuses the leased premises by causing damage therein not arising from normal use, or uses them or allows them to be used in a manner inconsistent with the terms of the contract without the written consent of the lessor.

The practice by a tenant who is a liberal professional of his profession in a part of the leased premises designated for his residence, for security reasons that forced him to leave the seat where he practiced his profession, shall not be deemed a misuse of the leased premises; in this case, the owner shall not be entitled to claim any compensation from the tenant, nor may the tenant claim any additional compensation therefor from the owner in cases of recovery.

Installations erected by the tenant at his own expense shall not be deemed a misuse of the leased premises, provided that they do not impair the structural soundness of the building; works for the installation of an elevator and a water tank or the provision of heating, cooling, or hot water shall be deemed as such. Likewise, works relating to the rehabilitation of the leased premises or the entrances of the building that are necessary for the needs of a disabled person residing therein, in accordance with the minimum standards for buildings and facilities pursuant to the Law relating to the Rights of Disabled Persons, shall not be deemed a misuse of the leased premises, provided that such works are technically feasible and do not impair the structural soundness of the building.

With the exception of simple superficial ornamentation and decoration works and the installation of individual cooling and heating units, a tenant who wishes to avail himself of the provisions of this Article must summon the lessor before the Judge of Urgent Matters to seek permission to carry out the works that he wishes to perform, which he must specify in order to enable the court to assess their legality and appropriateness.

The tenant must take out insurance, the expenses of which he alone shall bear, against all risks that may result from the works he performs, as well as the expenses of the aforementioned works and the expenses of restoring the parts of the building that may have been damaged because of the works to their former condition, without having the right of recourse against the owner to claim the same or any part thereof, whether during his occupancy of the leased premises or on the date of termination of such occupancy.

The value of the improvements resulting from the works mentioned in this paragraph shall not be included in the calculation of the recovery compensation.

C - If he assigns the leased premises or sublets them in whole or in part without the written consent of the lessor, in which case the subtenant or assignee must be joined in the proceedings.

D - If the tenant constructs a building for residence, or if one becomes vacant for him, or if he acquires a vacant building of which he owns at least three-quarters and which is fit and suitable for his residence and equivalent to the standard of the leased premises that he occupies in the same city or village, or in a place not more than ten kilometers distant from the leased premises in a radial line.

In these cases, the husband, the wife, the minor children residing with the tenant, as well as the adult children of the tenant who are his dependents, shall be deemed as a single person for the application of the provisions of this paragraph, unless the condition of family necessity provided for in paragraph (A) of Article 32 of this Law is met in the situation of the children, subject to actual residence within a period not exceeding one year from the date of completion of construction, acquisition, or vacancy, and continuation of residence for a period of at least three years.

There shall be excluded from the provisions of this paragraph the case in which the tenant, or whoever is deemed with him as a single person, acquires an apartment to use it as a commercial or tourist office or to practice one of the professions, and actually uses it for this purpose within six months from the date of acquisition and continues in the same use for a period of at least three years.

E - If he abandons the leased premises for a period of one year without interruption, notwithstanding his continuation in paying the rent. Lebanese officials and employees in official Lebanese missions abroad shall be excluded from the provisions of this item.

F - If he abandons the leased premises for a period of six months without interruption while owing any part of the rent, and has no domicile known to the owner at which to be served with the formal notice to pay, or has not elected a domicile in Lebanon at which to be served with this formal notice designated by him to the lessor by means of a letter or an open registered postal card with acknowledgment of receipt in accordance with the rules of service provided for in paragraph (A) of this Article.

G- If a non-Lebanese tenant does not actually occupy the leased premises for a period of six months without interruption, notwithstanding his payment of the rent.

The following shall benefit from the extension in the event of the tenant's death or abandonment of the leased premises:

First: With respect to premises leased for commercial or industrial purposes:

1 - The tenant's heirs up to the third degree, or some of them in accordance with the agreement among them.

2 - The tenant's partners whose partnership is established as of the date of the lease contract or as of a prior date.

3 - The beneficiaries of the provisions of Article 5 et seq. of Legislative Decree No. 11/1967 (relating to the commercial establishment). In this case, the lease of the premises allocated for operating the commercial establishment shall be extended and transferred to the person to whom the said establishment is transferred. Premises leased for the purposes set out in Articles 6, 7 and 8 of the Code of Land Commerce shall be deemed commercial or industrial.

Second: With respect to premises leased for the practice of a liberal profession regulated by law:

1 - The tenant's heirs, or some of them in accordance with the agreement among them, provided that the heir practices any liberal profession regulated by law.

2 - Any person to whom the leased premises have devolved by way of assignment from the tenant or from his heirs, provided that the assignee practices any liberal profession regulated by law and provided that the assignment, in the event of the tenant's death, takes place within a period not exceeding two years from the date of death.

If the leased premises are occupied by more than one person practicing a liberal profession and one of them dies without having among his heirs anyone who practices his same profession, his partners shall replace him in the lease under the same conditions of the contract, in return for compensation to the heirs equivalent to ten times the deceased's share in the annual rent in force on the date of death. However, in the event that the partner tenant abandons the leased premises for any reason whatsoever, his partners shall replace him under the same conditions of the contract.

Third: With respect to other premises:

1- The spouse, ascendants and descendants of the tenant, or some of them in accordance with the agreement among them, provided that they practice the same profession.

2 - The tenant's partners whose partnership is established as of the date of the lease contract or as of a prior date.

3 - Any person to whom the leased premises have devolved by way of assignment from the tenant or from the heirs mentioned in paragraph (1) above, provided that the assignee practices the same profession, and provided that the assignment takes place officially before a notary public, in the event of the tenant's death, within a period not exceeding one year from the date of death. The owner shall have the right to double the rent in accordance with the provisions of Article (42) of this Law.

All persons benefiting from the extension pursuant to the provisions of this Article shall be deemed jointly and severally liable towards the lessor for the performance of their obligations.

1 - Following the expiry of the term of the original contract, the lessee may, notwithstanding any agreement to the contrary, pay the rent monthly and in advance if the monthly rent exceeds the minimum wage on the date this rent falls due.

2 - The lessee shall not be adjudged to have forfeited the right of extension:

A) If he sends the rents to the lessor by means of a postal money order in a registered letter with acknowledgment of receipt within the legal time limit to the lessor's place of residence.

B) If he deposits the rents within the legal time limit with the notary public operating in the district or city within the jurisdiction of either of which the leased premises are located.

And the notary public must notify the lessor at his last address of the content of the deposit and invite him to collect its value.

Both the owner and the lessee may execute the judgment ordering repossession, and if the owner fails to pay the amount of compensation due from him at the Execution Department, after being served notice by it, he shall be liable for an additional compensation of two percent per month of the value of the compensation, not subject to modification, which shall be calculated, executed and collected directly through the Execution Department.

Common expenses referred to in this Law shall mean:

1- Common services expenses, which are:

A - Expenses for the consumption or generation of electric current, pertaining to the concierge's quarters, the lift, and all other common parts in a subdivided building and what is deemed as such in an unsubdivided building.

B - Expenses for the supply of cold water, including that extracted from artesian wells, hot water, heating and cooling.

C - The wage of the concierge equivalent to the minimum wage, in addition to increases including step increments, allowances, statutory indemnities, contributions due to the National Social Security Fund and end-of-service indemnity; the housing allowance shall not be included in the calculation of the wage.

2 - Maintenance expenses, which are: expenses for the maintenance of the building, whitewashing, painting, and repairs relating to the equipment for the supply of water, cooling and heating and their common installations, and to the lift and its insurance with an insurance company.

3 - Re-equipping expenses, which are: expenses for re-equipping the building with machinery and equipment that provide common services, and expenses for renewing the external appearance of the building and the common parts or what is deemed as such shall be considered as re-equipping expenses.

The tenant's right to extension shall lapse, in non-residential premises, in accordance with the provisions of paragraphs (a), (b), (c), (e), (f) and (g) of Article (34) of this Law, or if he effects a change in the intended use of the leased premises as specified in the lease contract.

The owner of real property leased for non-residential purposes shall have the right to recover the leased premises in accordance with the provisions of paragraphs (b) and (c) of Article (32) of this Law, and the owner shall be liable, in addition to the compensation specified in this Article, for further compensation for the loss incurred by the tenant as a result of eviction (such as key money, loss of location and clientele, interruption of business and others). The provisions of Article 33 of this Law relating to additional compensation shall apply to the owner who has recovered his leased premises where the conditions thereof are met.

Rents shall be doubled once in the following cases:

a - For premises leased to a natural or legal person who is or becomes the owner of buildings or undivided shares in premises where his share of the total actual rents thereof exceeds ten times the rent of the leased premises which he occupies.

For the purpose of calculating these rents, the husband, wife and children residing with the tenant shall be deemed as one person, and the owner shall not have the right to request this doubling from a single tenant or whoever replaces him by operation of this Law more than once.

An owner who has previously claimed the fair rent under Law No. 160/1992 and benefited from this doubling shall not benefit from the provisions of this paragraph.

b - For leases deemed an element of a commercial establishment and which are the subject of an assignment contract or a free management contract in accordance with the provisions of Legislative Decree No. 11/1967, throughout the period of free management.

c - For premises leased for the practice of a liberal profession regulated by law in the event of assignment thereof in accordance with the provisions of paragraph 2 of item Second of Article (39) of this Law.

Unless there is an agreement charging the tenant with all common expenses, the owner shall bear a rate of 20% (twenty per cent) of the expenses of common services and maintenance, provided that his contribution does not exceed 5% (five per cent) of the total rents of the premises that benefit from these services, and the remainder shall be distributed among the units of which the building is composed, whether they are vacant or occupied by the owner or alike.

The expenses of renovating the exterior appearance of the building and the common parts, or that which governs them, shall be incurred if the competent administration imposes carrying them out.

The area of each leased premises shall be taken into consideration when distributing the contribution shares among the occupants.

Every dispute that arises between the parties regarding the utility of the works, their value, or the distribution of the contribution shares shall be adjudicated by the judge of urgent matters in accordance with the procedure followed before him, pursuant to a decision enforceable immediately upon the original.

The lessor shall not have the right to refrain from providing the common services that he has been accustomed to providing and that were originally agreed upon in the lease contract.

If these services include heating, cooling, or hot water, the lessor must provide sufficient heating on a regular basis from 15 November until 31 March of the second year, and cooling from the first of June until 15 October of the same year.

As for hot water, he must provide it throughout the days of the year, all of this unless there is a contrary agreement in the contract.

If the owner fails to perform, without a legitimate justification, all or some of the services agreed upon or legally due, the tenant shall be entitled, after verification thereof through an expert appointed by the judge of urgent matters without levying any fee, to compensation equal to the rent of two months, provided that the total compensation awarded, in a single rental year, does not exceed the rent of four months.

The provisions of Article 847 et seq. of the Code of Civil Procedure relating to the execution of instruments and written undertakings shall apply for the collection of the rents specified in lease contracts. The original lease contract may be relied upon accompanied by a certificate issued by the municipality or the competent administration proving the renewal of the registration of the contract.

Notwithstanding the provisions of Article 852 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the opposition shall not stay execution unless the competent court decides otherwise, against a guarantee or without it.

In all cases of repossession and forfeiture of extension, the court shall take into consideration the necessary expenses that the lessee has personally borne to carry out restoration works in the repossessed leased premises as well as the period that has elapsed since the restoration works.

1 - A contract with sunken consideration means the contract whereby the owner of the real property authorises another person to erect constructions or buildings on the said real property at his own expense in return for operating them for a period of time against considerations specified in the contract.

2 - Lease contracts with sunken consideration concluded as of 23/7/1992 and thereafter shall be subject to the provisions contained therein. Likewise the lease contracts that the operator concluded on the constructions or buildings with third parties, provided that their term does not exceed the term of the original contract.

3 - Lease contracts with sunken consideration concluded before 23/7/1992 shall be extended for a period of three years starting from the date of entry into force of this Law if the original term had expired before its entry into force. And if their original term has not yet expired, they shall remain in force until the expiry of this term.

4 - Lease contracts concluded between the operator and third parties before 22/7/1992 shall be subject to the provisions of this Law.

5 - If the operator occupies the building or any part thereof and the occupancy dates back to before 23/7/1992, the operator shall be deemed a lessee and the provisions of this Law shall apply to him.

Notwithstanding any other text, lease contracts relating to premises containing violations of the building or urban planning laws shall not be deemed null and void unless these violations are not amenable to settlement under the laws in force.

However, in the case, the judgment evicting the lessee shall not be executed except concurrently with the removal of the violation by the lessor and against compensation paid to the lessee in accordance with the provisions on repossession for demolition provided for in this Law.
Subject to Article 22 of this Law, lawsuits instituted before the date of its entry into force shall remain subject to the provisions of the laws under which they were instituted.

1 - The lessor may request from the lessee, once a year, an advance on account to secure the common expenses equivalent to a rate of 75% of what he paid for the previous year, and in this case the lessees shall have the right to appoint one of themselves to supervise the process of the agreement of this advance.

2 - The lessor shall prepare annually a detailed account of the expenses and a distribution thereof between himself and the lessees, showing the share of contribution of each of them, and shall notify them thereof, and each of them shall have the right to inspect the invoices proving these expenses and to request a copy thereof at his own expense, where necessary, in order to object to their validity if he so wishes.

3 - Delay by the lessee in paying the advance or in paying his due share of the annual contribution after the final accounting shall be deemed equivalent to delay in paying the rentals and shall produce the effects provided for in Paragraph (a) of Article (34) of this Law, provided that the formal notice is accompanied by a copy of all the documents proving the expenses.

1 - Notwithstanding any previous text or agreement, the lessee shall bear the full expenses of the non-common repairs specific to the leased premises.

2 - Every written agreement concluded between the occupants of three-quarters of the units intended for lease or for occupancy by the owner concerning the exemption of the owner from performing all or some of the common services shall be binding upon the owner and upon all the lessees.

The Single Civil Judge shall be vested with jurisdiction to hear and adjudicate all lease actions and all claims and defences connected therewith, whatever the amount of the annual rent may be. The first trial hearing in lease actions shall be scheduled without being bound by the time limits for the exchange of pleadings, and the preliminary judgment rendered in actions concerning the lease of built real properties subject to this Law shall not be open to any of the ordinary or extraordinary means of recourse except opposition within the limits of Article 468 of the Code of Civil Procedure and appeal within a time limit of fifteen days from the date of notification thereof, and the appellate judgment shall not be open to any of the ordinary or extraordinary means of recourse except opposition within the limits of Article 657 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

However, the appellate judgment shall be open to cassation if there is a contradiction between it and the preliminary judgment with respect to forfeiture of the right to extension only, and this shall apply to appellate judgments rendered with effect from 1/1/1987, whatever the law applied in those judgments may be.

The court of urgent matters shall remain competent, within the scope of the provisions of the general law, to hear emergent and urgent matters the adjudication of which does not address the merits of the dispute.

A tenant covered by the provisions of paragraph (d) of the seventh Article of Law No. 539 dated 24/7/1996 and its amendments (Establishment of the Public Corporation for Housing) shall be granted absolute priority to participate in the special system of rent-to-own.
Where necessary, the details of application of the provisions of this Law shall be determined by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Justice and Finance.
This Law shall be published in the Official Gazette and shall enter into force six months after the date of its publication.

- The draft law contained in Decree No. 8759 dated 25/9/2002 relating to patients' rights and informed consent, as amended by the Administration and Justice Committee, is hereby ratified.

- This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The patient has the right, within the framework of a health system and social protection, to receive rational medical care appropriate to his condition, and in keeping with current scientific data.

This protection takes the form of prevention, or treatment, or palliative care, or rehabilitation, or education.

Every patient whose care is undertaken by a physician or a health institution is entitled to obtain complete information regarding his health condition. This information includes:

The proposed examinations, treatments, and medical procedures, and also includes their benefits and negative complications, the customary or major risks they entail, and other possible alternatives, in addition to the expected consequences in the event they are not performed.

In the event that new data subsequently arise requiring new decisions to be taken, the patient must also be informed thereof, where possible.

Except in cases of emergency and impossibility, this information shall be given at the appropriate time, during a conversation conducted with the patient in private.

This information must be characterised by truthfulness and clarity, be comprehensible to the patient, and be adapted to his personality, needs, and requests.

The patient must also be handed a written file containing this information, particularly in the event a surgical operation entailing risks is proposed. Except in cases of emergency, the patient is granted the right to take sufficient time for reflection in order to give his consent, and the physician shall verify that he has understood it well.

Reference to this conversation with the patient shall be made in his medical file, and it shall be signed by the patient in person, where necessary, in the event that the nature of the medical intervention or the relationship between the patient and his physician makes this signature necessary.

The signature of the patient on a pre-prepared consent form does not justify dispensing with the conversation with him.

Any sick person may refuse a specific medical act or treatment, and may also discontinue such treatment at his own responsibility.

The physician is bound to respect such refusal, after having informed the patient of its consequences, and he may therefore himself propose to the patient to consult another physician.

However, in the event that he considers that he cannot provide the necessary medical care in accordance with the conditions set by the patient, he may request the latter to relieve him of his responsibilities.

During treatment, it shall be proposed to the patient to designate in writing a person of trust to be consulted in the event that the patient himself becomes in a condition that does not allow him to express his will and to receive the information necessary for making a decision.

Likewise, this person designated in writing enjoys the right to remain informed of the patient's state of health, particularly if the latter is admitted to intensive care.

This measure shall not apply to minors or to adults under guardianship.

Where the patient is in a condition that does not allow him to express his will, he may not be subjected to any medical act or any treatment without consulting the person of trust mentioned in the preceding Article or the family, except in cases of emergency or impossibility.

Likewise, the consent of minors or adults under guardianship shall be sought in the event that it appears that the degree of maturity of the former or the mental faculties enjoyed by the latter qualify them to express their will to participate in making the decision.

However, this does not negate the necessity for the holders of parental authority or the guardians to express such consent or to confirm it legally.

Nevertheless, in the event that the health of the minor or of the adult under guardianship, or their physical integrity, would be endangered due to the refusal of their legal representative, the physician in charge shall refer the matter to the Public Prosecution to secure the necessary care for this patient.

Examining a patient within the framework of clinical teaching requires the prior consent of this patient; however, the patient's consent to be examined by an intern or a resident physician shall be presumed in principle merely by his admission to a university hospital, unless the patient declares his non-consent to this procedure upon his admission to the hospital.

The patient's consent to receive care shall not signify his consent to participate in clinical research; the participation of a person undergoing treatment in clinical research of scientific benefit, or in the testing of medicines, requires that he consent thereto in writing, provided that such participation shall not bear any compulsory character in respect of the patient, and that his refusal thereof shall not lead to any discriminatory measure against him.

It likewise presupposes that it not entail any foreseeable actual risk to his health, but rather that it be of therapeutic benefit to this patient specifically or to persons of his age suffering from his same illness. Finally, it requires that the Ethics Committee at the Order of Physicians or at the healthcare institution, if it is a university institution, or the National Consultative Committee for Health and Life Sciences Ethics, grant explicit approval of the research protocol, after having verified the scientific rigour of this project, its conformity with ethical laws and its benefit, and that the supervisor thereof and those carrying it out possess the required qualifications, in addition to the existence of insurance guaranteeing their civil liability, and after it ratifies the information file given to the person whose consent is sought, and the form submitted to him for his signature.

As with consent to medical care, so too with participation in clinical research: where the patient is in a condition that does not allow him to express his will, such participation requires the consent of a person of trust appointed by the patient personally or with the consent of his family.

As for the participation of a minor or an adult under guardianship in clinical research, it requires the consent of the holder of parental authority or the guardian.

Likewise, the consent of the person concerned himself must be sought if he is capable of expressing his will, and his refusal or withdrawal of consent may not be disregarded.

Every patient cared for by a physician or a healthcare institution shall have the right to respect for his private life and the confidentiality of the information relating thereto.

Where the patient is under the care of a medical care team in a healthcare institution, this team shall be deemed entrusted with the information relating to him, and shall be bound by professional secrecy, as is the case for the attending physician in accordance with the provisions of the Penal Code and the Code of Medical Ethics.

The information given to guaranteeing institutions, in the public and private sectors, in order to settle medical costs, shall be limited to the necessary information that they require to audit such costs, in accordance with the provisions of the Code of Medical Ethics.

In the event that the patient wishes that a serious diagnosis or medical prognosis be withheld from him, his wish must be respected and this must be noted in his file, except when third parties are exposed to the risk of contracting the infection of the disease.

And the patient may appoint a representative to receive information on his behalf and continue to be informed of the stages of treatment. If it appears that a piece of information bears a nature that may negatively affect the progression of the disease or the success of the treatment, the physician may exceptionally be compelled to restrict the information that he gives, in the therapeutic interest of the patient.

Where there exist specific reasons calling for not informing the ill person of a medical prognosis regarding the possibility of his death, his closest family members must be informed of this prognosis, subject to the provisions of Article Seven of the Code of Medical Ethics.

Minors shall be provided with information regarding the examinations and medical acts necessary for their health condition, in accordance with their age and their capacity to understand, regardless of the information with which it is always necessary that their legal representatives be provided.

Likewise, guardians of adults have the right to obtain the appropriate information.

Every patient has the right, upon his request, to obtain the information given by the concerned health institution and the attending physicians regarding the expected approximate costs that he may be obliged to pay in return for treatment, and medical and hospitalisation acts, as well as regarding the conditions under which the guaranteeing institutions bear these costs.

No medical act may be performed, nor any treatment applied, without the prior consent of the person concerned, except in the two cases of emergency and impossibility.

And this consent must be given clearly, that is, it must be preceded by all the necessary information provided for in Article Two of this Law, and it must be decided by the patient freely and he must be able to withdraw it whenever he wishes.

Likewise, this consent must be renewed for any new medical act that was not previously foreseen, except in the two cases of emergency and impossibility.

The expression of this consent shall be in writing for major surgical operations; likewise, it may be subjected to additional conditions in specific cases, such as the medical termination of pregnancy, the removal and transplantation of organs, medically assisted reproduction, and participation in clinical research...
In the event that a diagnosis or medical prognosis of the patient's death is reached, professional secrecy shall not conflict with the patient's family obtaining the necessary information.

Every patient, or his legal representative if he is a minor or under guardianship, has the right to inspect the objective information relating to his health held by healthcare professionals or institutions, as recorded in his medical file.

Pursuant to his request addressed to the director of the medical institution concerned or the physician concerned, he may obtain this information in person or through a physician or a third party bound by secrecy.

Any of the aforementioned may inspect the file in situ or request a copy of the documents at the patient's expense.

The medical file that is mandatorily opened for every patient undergoing hospitalisation in a health institution shall contain the documents drawn up upon his admission to the hospital and during his stay therein.

These documents are specifically: the patient's identification card and the original document stating the reason for his admission to the hospital, the results of clinical examinations and check-ups, the anaesthesia chart, surgical operation or delivery reports, therapeutic prescriptions, a report on the patient's medical history (Antecedent) and daily follow-up reports (Evolution).

The medical file shall also include the documents drawn up at the end of each stay in the hospital, which are the following: the hospitalisation report with the diagnosis upon the patient's discharge from the hospital, and the prescriptions given to him upon his discharge.

In the event of the patient's death, his successors in title may inspect the information contained in his medical file insofar as it is necessary to enable them to know the causes of his death, to defend his memory or to establish their rights, unless the patient expressed his refusal thereof prior to his death.
In the event of a violation of any of the articles of this Law, the provisions of the laws in force shall apply, in particular Article 61 of the Code of Medical Ethics.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

It is prohibited:

1 - To ruin, demolish, or disable in any manner whatsoever all or part of the installations constructed for the use or preservation of the waters of the public domain, whether granted by concession or without a concession, such as bridges, dams, aqueducts, navigation, irrigation, drying and drainage canals, pipes laid on the surface of the ground or buried therein, distribution devices, etc. This prohibition also covers the appurtenances of the said installations and the structures constructed for protection from the waters of the public domain.

2 - To discharge into the waters of the public domain, whether granted by concession or without a concession, or to spill or throw therein water or substances harmful to health conditions, public comfort, or the proper use of these waters

3 - To throw animal manure onto lands falling within the protection zone of a water spring used for public needs, to establish repositories for filth, and in general to carry out any act whatsoever liable to pollute that spring.

The boundaries of the protection zone shall be determined in each case by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister for this purpose.

The following matters shall be subject to the regime relating to temporary occupation permits within the conditions specified in Article 17 of Decision No. 144, which are granted by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister, and these matters are:

1 - The construction of structures not having a permanent character, the purpose of which is the use of the waters of the public domain.

2 - The extraction of materials of any kind whatsoever from the bed of temporary or permanent watercourses and from lakes, ponds, and swamps.

3 - The establishment of repositories, the planting of trees, and the cultivation of land on the banks of waters, in the bed of watercourses, and in lakes, swamps, ponds, and basins

4 - Works relating to prospecting for underground or gushing waters or to the harnessing of waters, with the exception of their use.

5 - Structures intended for harnessing and using the waters of natural springs the volume of which is insufficient to justify their use for public utility.

6 - The cleaning, deepening, straightening, and regulation of temporary or permanent watercourses.

It is prohibited, without a licence granted by the Administration under the conditions specified in Decision (144/S 1) and in this Decision:

1 - To prevent the waters of the public domain from flowing freely.

2 - To encroach in any manner whatsoever upon the boundaries of the lands belonging to the banks of temporary or permanent watercourses, marshes, lakes, pools, ponds and springs, as well as upon the boundaries of the passages of aqueducts and water pipes, and navigation, irrigation, drying and drainage canals declared to have been established for the public utility; however, buildings previously erected may be restored and repaired subject to the following two conditions, namely that nothing be added to their external dimensions and that the materials used for the repair be of the same materials as those previously used.

3 - To make any deposit whatsoever, or to plant or sow upon the land belonging to the banks of temporary or permanent watercourses and in their beds, and in lakes, marshes, pools and ponds, and between the boundaries of the passages of water pipes and aqueducts, and navigation, irrigation, drying and drainage canals declared to have been established for the public utility.

4 - To remove grass, trees, shrubs, earth or stones from the lands belonging to the banks of temporary or permanent waters, lakes, marshes, pools and ponds.

5 - To clean, deepen, straighten or regulate temporary or permanent watercourses.

6 - To carry out excavations of any kind whatsoever at a distance from the boundary of the banks of watercourses, aqueducts, and navigation, irrigation, drying and drainage canals, after its measurement is less than or the measurement of the depth of such excavations, provided that this distance may not be less than three metres

8 - It is generally prohibited to carry out any work whatsoever, whether permanent or temporary, that may have an effect on the quantity of the waters of the public domain or on their flow.

The Head of State shall have the right to compel, by virtue of a notice, the owners of installations for which a licence must be obtained in accordance with this Decision and which exist on the day of its publication, to apply for such licence.

If the Administration refuses the licence henceforth required in whole or in part, and if the owners are compelled by reason thereof to demolish all or part of these installations and buildings, including those permitted, they shall receive in advance fair compensation therefor, and if a dispute arises and no amicable agreement is reached on this matter, it shall be adjudicated by the competent Administrative Courts.

If public utility requires the removal or alteration of installations lawfully erected pursuant to a licence or a concession, the holder of the licence or the holder of the concession shall have the right to receive compensation equivalent to the value of the damage only, unless there are provisions to the contrary in the concession instrument.

The holder of the licence or the concession shall have the right, in respect of the execution of the works mentioned in the licence or in the concession, to benefit, within the conditions set forth in the following Articles, from the easements (Servitudes) mentioned below:

1 - The right to occupy private properties necessary for the construction of installations relating to the impoundment and intake of water and the construction of canals necessary for conveying, draining or discharging water.

2 - The right to abut dams constructed in watercourses.

3 - The right to submerge banks by raising the water level and the right to submerge lands if water reservoirs are constructed.

Buildings, courtyards and orchards adjoining dwellings shall be exempted from these rights.

The licence shall specify the particular conditions under which this licence has been granted. There shall be stated in this licence, in particular, the following matters:

1 - If it relates to prospecting for water, there shall be specified therein the area in which the works shall take place, the methods to be used for prospecting for water and for discharging it, the information or samples that the holder of the licence must submit to the Administration, and the conditions under which supervision of the works shall be carried out.

2 - And if it relates to the construction of a structure on watercourses, or a structure to connect them, or any project whatsoever relating to the regime of water flow, there shall be stated the location of the licensed works, their nature, their arrangement, their principal dimensions, and the conditions of supervision over the construction, maintenance, and exploitation of the structure.

If a concession is granted, a book of specifications must be annexed to the instrument of concession, specifying in particular:

1 - The general arrangements relating to the water intake, the installations, the quantity of water drawn, and, where applicable, the times of use of the water and the conditions imposed for discharging the water, supervising the works, and exploiting the water.

2 - The measures to be taken for protection against the overflowing of water or for the preservation of public health and the satisfaction of the domestic needs of the neighbouring inhabitants for drinking and otherwise.

3 - The determination of the maximum power of the waterfall that is the subject of the concession and the estimation of its normal power.

4 - The period required for the completion of the works and the conditions for the forfeiture of the concession.

5 - The duration of the concession starting from the approval thereof by the High Commissioner.

6 - The reserve water and reserve power that must be preserved, where applicable, for the public administrations.

7 - The financial conditions of the concession.

8 - The fate of the installations upon the expiry of the duration of the concession.

9 - The conditions and clauses that must be complied with if the concession is sold.

The granting of licences and concessions shall entail the payment of a fee to the State, which may be revised under the conditions specified in the text of the licence or concession.

No total or partial assignment whatsoever of the concession, and no change or substitution of its holder, may be effected except after the approval of the Head of State ratified by the High Commissioner.

The concession shall vest in its holder, with respect to the execution of the public installations mentioned in the book of specifications, in addition to the rights provided for in Articles 18, 19, and 20 of this Decision, all the rights granted by the laws and regulations to the Administration concerning expropriation for public utility, and the holder of the concession shall remain subject at the same time to all the obligations arising for the Administration from those laws and regulations.

In the absence of an amicable agreement with the owners of the land, the Head of State may, after hearing them, issue an order authorising the holder of the licence or concession to enjoy the rights mentioned in the preceding Article, subject to the prior deposit of a security fixed by the Head of State. The authorisation order shall be notified to the owners of the properties through administrative channels at the diligence of the holder of the licence or the holder of the concession, and in all cases the owner of the land shall be entitled to receive compensation fixed as follows:

Where the works undertaken are only temporary works, the compensation shall be fixed at an indivisible annual sum, provided that it does not exceed twice the rental value of the occupied lands at the time their occupation takes place.

Where the occupation of the land deprives its owner of the enjoyment thereof for a period exceeding five years, or where, after the completion of such works, the land becomes unfit for agriculture, its owner shall be entitled to require the holder of the licence or the holder of the concession to purchase the land.

Plots of land which suffer heavy damage or diminish greatly in value must be purchased in their entirety if their owner so requests.

The compensation or the purchase price of the lands shall be fixed by an agreement concluded between the two parties, and in the absence of an amicable agreement, the same shall be fixed by an arbitral commission composed of two members, one of whom shall be appointed by the Head of State and the second by the owner of the property; in the event of disagreement between these two members, the matter shall be decided by an umpire appointed by the first two by mutual agreement.

Where the owner of the land fails to appoint his arbitrator within a period of one month after the notice sent to him in this regard, and where no agreement is reached on the selection of the umpire, such appointments shall be made by the President of the highest judicial authority in the State.

The concessionaire shall have the right to buy out private rights relating to the use of water existing at the time the concession is granted, and to purchase legally established water intakes in return for compensation in kind or monetary compensation.

If these rights are being exercised on the said date, the concessionaire must restore in kind the water or the power used and bear, where necessary, all the expenses of replacement carried out in the necessary installations and proved to be necessary by reason of the changes introduced in the conditions of use, unless a contrary order is issued by the arbitrator examining the matter as mentioned in the penultimate paragraph of this Article. With regard to the restoration of water necessary for irrigation, the concessionaire shall have the right to dispose of the rights resulting from the application of Articles 15, 18, 19 and 62 of this Decision.

With regard to the restoration of power in electrical form, the concessionaire shall have the right to benefit from the rights of support, wayleave and lopping of branches provided for in Decision No. 145 issued on 11 June 1925. If a dispute arises as to the nature or value of the compensation claimed, the dispute shall be brought before the Administrative Authority. In rendering his judgment, the judge must reconcile the rights existing prior to the undertaking with the interest of the undertaking for which the concession is granted.

The compensation claimed for rights not being exercised on the date the concession is granted shall be fixed in accordance with the conditions previously provided for, failing an amicable agreement between the two parties. If the concession relates to hydraulic power, the total value of the compensation payable to the interested parties may not exceed the sum of 200 piastres for each kilowatt of normal gross power of the waterfall for which the concession is granted.

This value shall be apportioned among the interested parties at the expense of the concessionaire in accordance with the report of experts appointed by the Administrative Court.

The administrative recognition of the rights of individuals with regard to rights of ownership, usufruct or use legally acquired over springs, watercourses, lakes, ponds and marshes and, in general, over the waters of the public domain shall be subject to the provisions mentioned in the following Articles: such recognition shall take place at the diligence of the owner who wishes to have the right at his disposal recognised and preserved, or at the diligence of the Head of State if the matter relates to a general study for the development of a water basin or for the drawing up of an inventory of the hydraulic resources existing in a region.
