The preparation register shall contain the name of the instructor, the distribution of his weekly work and the annual distribution of his subjects, and shall include a daily and dated preparation covering every lesson, assignment, review, examination, correction or any other school work, clarifying the elements of the subject and the stages and means of the work. He shall record, in a special register, the marks of lessons, assignments and examinations, and monthly remarks on the development of the conduct and diligence of each pupil. Teachers of experimental science subjects shall prepare their experiments and tests in the school laboratory, prior to the official time for giving the lesson.

The class teacher, or the teachers who participate in teaching a single class, shall take the utmost care of the rotating notebooks, number their pages, and hand them over, every day, to a pupil to write therein the exercises given in class and the daily written assignments for each subject, provided that two notebooks are allocated to each primary class: one for subjects written in Arabic and one for subjects written in the foreign language. In intermediate classes, however, one notebook shall be allocated to each single subject, or to what is deemed equivalent to a single subject. The rotating notebooks shall be kept with the archives of the school.

Attendance control: The person in charge of the school and all its employees shall record their names in the attendance register, and sign therein immediately and in the order of their arrival at the school, and state accurately the time of arrival in the morning and in the afternoon and the reasons for their tardiness and its duration whenever they are late. The person in charge of the school shall record his remarks, where necessary, with full clarity, in the morning and in the afternoon, regarding the attendance of the school employees, and shall note, before noon and in the afternoon, that he has monitored the attendance, and then sign again in confirmation of the monitoring, and every remark recorded in the attendance register must be signed by its writer regardless of its content.

- Coverage: Teaching during the absence of one of the teachers shall be covered by the supplementary teacher, where present, then by the other teachers in rotation, during their free hours, and, where necessary, by the supervisors and the person in charge of the school. The person in charge of the school shall draw up a schedule showing the distribution of the hours of the absent teacher, notify those assigned to work in his class thereof, and post a copy thereof in a prominent place.

- The supplementary teacher: A supplementary teacher may be attached to each school at the rate of one teacher for every fifteen teachers. The supplementary teacher shall cover the work entrusted to him by the person in charge of the school, in particular teaching in the event of the absence of some teachers, and organising the library and reading.

- One or more supplementary female teachers may be attached to schools in which female teachers work who may obtain maternity leave during the school year, in order to cover teaching during their absence.
- General duties: The person in charge of the school and all its employees shall maintain order, and shall place the public interest above their personal interests.

- Teachers shall cooperate with the school administration in school work, observe their working hours accurately, refer to the person in charge of the school in all matters relating to their school work, and heed his remarks and respect his will for the proper conduct of school work. If one of the school employees objects to the instructions of the person in charge and the person in charge then confirms his instructions, he shall be bound to execute them. This employee may refer the matter to the competent Head of the Department of Education through the chain of command.

Each member of the teaching staff shall:

1- Be a role model for the pupils in discipline and respect for laws and regulations.

2- Ensure the performance of such of the following duties as he is assigned to carry out: - Accompanying the pupils upon entering the classrooms, and supervising their exit therefrom until the last pupil. - Contributing, according to his inclination and competence, to school activity work, such as art, literature, social affairs, and sports... - Attending meetings of the General Teachers' Council, subject committees, and school examination committees, and such other meetings as the organisation of school work and the ensuring of its execution may require. - Organising registers, cards, and files. - Attending to the pupils' notebooks and correcting them accurately.

Each member of the teaching staff is prohibited from:

1- Engaging in any ideological, political, or partisan activity, of whatever kind, inside or outside the school.

2- Any activity or work that harms their educational mission, or participating in anything that is inconsistent with the principles of the teaching mission. 3- Divulging official information that comes to his knowledge by virtue of his office, particularly discussions taking place in the Teachers' Council, the Disciplinary Council, or other activity committees in the school.

4- Any act that detracts from the dignity of the office.

5- Leaving the classroom or turning away from teaching for any other work.

6- Smoking in classrooms.

7- Admitting a pupil who is late or returning after an absence save by permission of the person in charge of the school or the proctor.

8- Accepting gifts from pupils or their guardians.

9- Going on strike from work or inciting thereto, and signing collective petitions relating to the office.

Members of the teaching staff are prohibited from inflicting any corporal punishment upon a pupil, and they are likewise prohibited from reprimanding with humiliating words repugnant to upbringing and personal dignity.

The subjects of instruction, in each curricular year, are the subjects designated in the prescribed official curricula of education. They must be adopted, without any other reference, when organising the annual schedule for the distribution of subjects.

The person in charge of the school shall organise, prior to the beginning of the academic year, the weekly schedule for the distribution of lessons and assignments for all curricular years, and it may not be amended save for an acceptable justification (such as the occurrence of staff transfers or maternity leave). In the primary stage, teachers must be distributed on the basis of classes rather than on the basis of subjects, insofar as possible, and a single subject must not be divided among several instructors in a single class.

The teachers of a single subject shall form a committee that meets under the supervision of the person in charge of the school outside of working hours at the beginning of every academic term, and whenever the need arises, to discuss the difficulties that prevent the pupils from comprehending the subject, and to organise a coordinated work plan among the teachers of the subject to raise the level of the pupils. The person in charge must prepare in advance the agendas of these committees, and he may seek the assistance of the teachers of the subject to prepare the said agenda. The minutes of this committee shall be recorded and signed by all its members in the register of minutes of the Teachers' Council.

The teachers of subjects that require practical illustration may, together with their pupils, practically undertake visits to technical institutions, productive factories, or archaeological and geographical sites, outside of school working hours, and after the written approval of the pupils' guardians to bear all responsibility resulting from these trips.

1- Teaching staff must rely on the books and sources available in the school library or elsewhere and urge their pupils to read.

2- Teachers of languages, literature, and social and applied sciences shall request of their pupils, at least once every two months, to submit summaries of what they have read in reading books, which shall be discussed in class, and the teacher shall express his remarks on each of them and return it to its owner.

It is prohibited, under penalty of disciplinary liability, to change the prescribed books in public schools, or to add any new book or publication, except for fundamental educational reasons the main features of which shall be defined by explanatory memoranda issued by the Directorate of Primary Education.

The textbooks prescribed to be taught in public schools shall be determined by a decision issued by the Director of Primary Education, in accordance with the following procedures:

a- Pursuant to studies conducted by the Directorate of Primary Education:

b- Or by following the following steps:

1- The teacher of the subject or the committee of teachers of the subject of the textbook proposed to be changed shall study it and the new textbook proposed as a substitute therefor, or the new work proposed to be added, and shall draw up a report on the result of the study setting out the essential educational reasons calling for the change.

2- The said report shall be submitted to the council of teachers in the school to be discussed and for a recommendation to be adopted in respect thereof before the fifteenth of the month of March of each year, and the discussions and the recommendation shall be recorded in the register of minutes of the council of teachers, and the report referred to shall be kept in the archives of the school.

3- The person in charge of the school shall immediately submit the recommendation of the council of teachers to the Directorate of Primary Education for approval, and if the month of May expires without a decision having been issued by the Director of Primary Education in respect of the recommendation, it shall be deemed ineffective, and the list of prescribed textbooks shall be announced ten days before the end of the school year, in accordance with the conditions provided for in paragraph c of Article 47.

The person in charge of the school shall lodge directly with the competent Department of Education and the Educational Inspectorate, during the first week from the start of the school year, a copy of each of:

1- The general schedule of the distribution of weekly lessons and assignments among the classes.

2- The general schedule of the distribution of weekly working hours and free hours among the teaching staff.

3- The comparative list of the names of the school textbooks.

Article 58: - The guiding principle of the Guidance and Disciplinary Council is reform, prevention, awakening of conscience, and the sense of responsibility. First- Its composition: This Council is composed of five members, who are:

- The person in charge of the school, as President

- The homeroom educator of the class to which the pupil who is the subject of investigation or complaint belongs - The most senior supervisor in rank at the school

- The most senior educator in rank at the school

- The most senior teacher in rank at the school, as members. And if the homeroom educator of the class is the most senior educator or the most senior teacher or both together, he shall be joined in the Council by the one who directly follows him in rank and seniority.

And if the Council is convened in the absence of the most senior supervisor in rank, he shall be deputised for by the supervisor who follows him in rank, and the same applies with respect to the most senior educator and the most senior teacher. And if the number of teaching staff at the school does not exceed five, this Council shall be formed of all of them.

Second- Its powers: The Guidance and Disciplinary Council has two powers:

1- Addressing special behavioural and educational cases that appear incidentally among pupils and which the homeroom educator of the class is unable to address by himself, and which one of the educators refers to the Council.

2- Taking disciplinary decisions within the limits of the penalties prescribed in Article 70 of these Regulations. Third- Its rules of procedure: a- The Guidance and Disciplinary Council meets upon a request from: - Its President. - Or two of its members. - Or a complaint from one of the teachers or supervisors.

b- The sessions of this Council shall not be lawful unless attended by the President and at least three members.

c- Decisions are taken by majority and announced immediately by the person in charge, and in the event of a tie vote, the President shall have the casting vote.

d- Deliberations shall remain confidential and shall be recorded in the special register for the minutes of the Guidance and Disciplinary Council, and decisions shall be signed by the President and all members present.

e- In the work of the Council, recourse shall be had to the observations recorded in the pupil's personal card, written statements, and interviews between the persons concerned.

f- The pupil must be questioned separately from the complainant, and the complaining teacher may not attend the meeting of the Council when considering the subject of his complaint. And if the complaining teacher is a member of the Disciplinary Council, he shall be replaced by the most senior teacher in rank after him from among those who are not members of this Council.

g- The rule of gradation in imposing penalties must be adopted as far as possible. h- A complete copy of the case file, together with copies of all supporting documents, shall be submitted to the competent Head of Department.
Article 59: - Schools shall be closed on Friday and Sunday of each week; as for other holidays, they shall be designated by the Ministry of National Education.

A teachers' council shall be formed in the school, composed of the person in charge as chairman, and of the rest of the teaching staff therein as members, and one of them, after being assigned by the person in charge, shall undertake to record the discussions and draw up the minutes, which shall be signed by the chairman and the members present, and shall be notified to those among them who were absent upon their return to work, to be signed and acted upon. The teachers' council shall examine educational affairs, and it shall not be permissible for it to examine non-school subjects or for anyone from outside the school to attend its sittings. Decisions shall be taken by majority, and the chairman shall have a casting vote in the event of an equality of votes. Administrative affairs, however, shall fall within the competence of the person in charge of the school alone. The teachers' council shall meet outside working hours in ordinary sessions, once every two months at least, upon convocation by its chairman, and in extraordinary sessions pursuant to a written request by at least one-third of the members, or upon convocation by the person in charge of the school, wherein the date and time of such meeting and the agenda shall be stated, and the convocation or the aforementioned request shall be kept in the archives of the school, provided that the convocation is notified at least two days prior to the appointed time.

School activity committees shall be composed of teachers and pupils, and those possessing talents, competence and experience shall participate therein, guiding the pupils to appreciate literary, artistic, athletic, social and other works, which helps the pupil to complete his attainment and education and the formation of his personality. These committees shall meet periodically or when the need arises, under the chairmanship of the person in charge of the school or under the chairmanship of whomever he delegates in writing. The minutes of the sittings of these committees shall be recorded in a special register.

- A pupil who has been admitted to the school shall: - Comply with the school laws and regulations, the decisions and instructions of the administration, and all the duties required of him. - Maintain complete order and observe the general rules of conduct, morals, and hygiene, inside and outside the school. - Obey the orders of the person in charge, the supervisors, and the teachers. - Take complete and comprehensive care of cleanliness, and preserve the school building, its furniture, and its contents.

- Pupils are prohibited from the following matters: - Smoking, joining partisan bodies or promoting their principles among the pupils, religious disputation, carrying weapons, participating in demonstrations, and striking from school work or inciting thereto. - Leaving the school during school hours, except at the request of their guardians and with the approval of the person in charge of the school. - Quarrelling, shouting, improper behaviour, and entering the classrooms during recesses, except with special permission from the person in charge of the school or the supervisor. - Performing any act liable to disrupt the general order of the school.
- All harmful and dangerous publications and possessions whatsoever shall be confiscated from the pupils, and shall be delivered immediately to the person in charge of the school.

- A pupil who takes his lunch at the school shall not be permitted to leave it before or after taking the meal, except upon a written request from his guardian, and he shall be deemed to be in the custody of his guardian for the duration of his absence from the school.

- An absent pupil shall not be admitted until he proves the legitimacy of his absence in the presence of his guardian or whoever represents him. However, if his absence was without a legitimate excuse, one of the penalties provided for in these regulations shall be imposed upon him.

- If the absence is partial for certain teaching hours, every five hours of absence shall be calculated as equivalent to one day of absence. If the pupil is late by a few minutes for an illegitimate excuse, he shall be permitted to enter the class, provided that the appropriate penalty is imposed upon him.

- In the event that a pupil violates the laws and regulations of the school and public morals, one of the following penalties shall be imposed upon him:

1- Written caution, which consists of a deterrent warning.

2- Written reprimand, which consists of a stricter deterrence of the pupil, for his persistence in the path of error.

3- Registered warning by a letter to the pupil's guardian, signed by the person in charge of the school, which consists of placing the pupil under strict observation.

4- Temporary suspension from the school, which is a threat of final expulsion, and the total temporary suspension may not exceed fifteen days in the year.

5- Final expulsion from the school.

- The person in charge shall impose: the first three penalties and execute them, and the teaching staff shall also impose and execute them, after the prior approval of the person in charge. The person in charge shall undertake to notify the pupil's guardian of the penalty imposed and the reasons therefor. - The Guidance and Discipline Council at the school shall impose any of the penalties set forth in the preceding Article, and the penalty of temporary suspension for a period not exceeding one week shall be executed as of right; whereas in all other cases of temporary and permanent expulsion, the penalty shall not become enforceable until after the approval of the Director of Primary Education, who has the right to amend it. The pupil must be given, during his execution of one of the penalties of temporary suspension, useful schoolwork that can be completed during the period of the penalty.

- The person in charge shall organise the examinations and written tests, and shall agree with the teachers on the questions that must be given from the official curriculum, and the final results shall be decided under his supervision and with the approval of the teachers concerned.

- School written tests and assessments shall be conducted in accordance with the following arrangement:

1- Written tests for written subjects, conducted by the teacher of the subject, at least once a month, within an overall schedule of written tests approved by the person in charge of the school, before the beginning of each school term. The average of the marks of these written tests shall be added to the average of the marks of lessons and homework, and the mean of both shall be considered the monthly mark.

2- The mid-academic-year examination, the date of which is in the first week of the month of February, and which shall not exceed five working days. 3- The end-of-academic-year examination, which begins on 15 June. In exceptional cases, this date may be amended after the approval of the Director of Primary Education.

4- The written tests set forth in the first paragraph of this Article shall be marked by the teacher of the subject, whereas the mid-year and end-of-year examinations shall be marked by the subject committees if possible, each committee according to its specialisation.

5- Marks shall be assessed from zero to twenty.

6- The summary of marks for each pupil for the academic year shall be taken as follows:

a- The average of the monthly marks for the first half of the year shall be added to the marks of the mid-year examination, and their mean shall be considered the mid-year summary of marks, and shall constitute the first third of the general summary.

b- The average of the monthly marks for the second half of the year, which shall constitute the second third of the general summary.

c- To the sum of the two preceding thirds shall be added the marks of the end-of-year examination, and the total shall then be divided by three, which shall be the final average or the general summary.

If one of the employees of the school is absent for health or other reasons, he must: 1- Immediately notify the person in charge of the school of: - His condition that necessitated his absence, and the expected duration of the absence. - His address during the period of illness. 2- Send to the person in charge of his duty station a medical report within 24 hours from the commencement of the absence, stating the nature of the illness, the duration of the absence, and that the physician verified his identity. 3- Comply with the instructions issued by the Ministry of National Education and Fine Arts in this regard.

If the employee requests leave without pay, for personal reasons, he must comply with the following:

- Submit a written application, through the administrative hierarchy, stating therein the duration of the leave and the reasons calling for it and enclosing therewith the necessary documents and supporting papers, and a copy of this application together with the supporting papers shall be kept in the file of the employee.

2- The employee requesting the leave may not leave his duty station prior to the issuance of the leave decision, except in proven cases of necessity in which the duration of the absence does not exceed three days at most, provided that it is accompanied by the written approval of the immediate superior, under penalty of severe disciplinary sanctions. The immediate superior shall refer the application immediately to the competent authority after expressing his opinion thereon in writing and with full accuracy.

1- Working days may not be fractionalised. Every partial absence from the day shall be deemed an absence of a full day.

2- Holidays shall be included within the duration of the leave, if official holidays fall within the leave.

3- An employee who is absent from his duty station without lawful leave shall forfeit his right to salary for the duration of his absence, in addition to the disciplinary sanctions that may be imposed upon him, in accordance with the laws and regulations in force.

If the employee does not resume his work at the end of the leave -whatever its nature may be- the person in charge of the school must immediately inform the competent Education Department thereof. He must, upon the return of the absent employee, inform the Education Department anew, stating the duration of his additional absence and the reasons therefor. However, if the absence without lawful leave exceeds fifteen days, the person in charge of the school shall not be entitled to allow the teacher to resume his work unless he receives a written order to that effect from the Director of Primary Education.

Every pupil who has cheated or attempted to cheat shall have a report drawn up against him to be kept at the school, shall be given a zero in the subject that was the object of the cheating, and his guardian shall be informed of the fact. If the cheating is repeated, the pupil shall be deemed to have failed.

The person in charge of the school may not nominate for the examination of either of the Elementary and Higher Elementary Certificates pupils a statement of whose names he had not submitted, through hierarchical channels, to the competent department, prior to the date fixed for this purpose, in accordance with the regulations in force.

The person in charge of the school shall nominate for the official examinations, for each of the Elementary and Higher Elementary Certificates, all pupils who are pursuing their studies in the two classes of these two certificates, provided that he may refrain from nominating for these examinations a pupil who is absent from attendance at a rate exceeding 20% of the total annual school days.

The ushers, servants, and hired workers of the school shall obey the orders of the person in charge thereof or whoever deputises for him, in relation to the school, and in particular ensuring its cleanliness, preserving its furniture, and guarding its entrances, especially during daily recess periods, safeguarding the pupils' food placed in their custody, and their books and supplies deposited with them, as well as transporting official mail.
A pupil who is a candidate for the end-of-year examination is required to have a rate of absence from attendance not exceeding 20% of the total annual school days.
The pupil's report card shall be sent to his guardians to be signed and returned, once at the end of every month.

-A- A pupil shall be deemed successful in the primary stage, and shall be promoted to a higher class if he obtains at least 10/20 in the final average of the total marks and does not receive below 5/20 in more than two basic subjects.

B- A pupil shall be deemed successful in the complementary stage, and shall be promoted to a higher class if he obtains at least 10/20 in the final average of the total marks and does not receive below 5/20 in any basic subject.

C- A pupil shall be deemed subject to a make-up examination in the complementary stage if he obtains at least 10/20 in the final average of the total marks and his mark does not fall below 5/20 in more than two basic subjects.

A pupil subject to a make-up examination shall not be deemed successful unless he receives at least 5/20 in each of the make-up subjects.

D- A pupil shall be deemed to have failed:

1- If he does not obtain the promotion average.

2- If he receives a mark below 5 out of 20 in more than two basic subjects.

3- If he does not receive a mark of at least 5 out of 20 in each of the subjects of the make-up examination.

4- If he is barred from sitting the examination pursuant to Article 74 of these Regulations.
Every pupil who fails two consecutive school years in a single curricular year, other than for a legitimate reason approved by the Teachers' Council, shall be dismissed from the school.

The basic subjects in the complementary stage are: - Composition, in each of the Arabic and foreign languages. - The average of history and geography. - The average of ethics and civic and national affairs. As for the basic subjects in the primary stage, they are: - The average of conversation and composition. - The average of grammar and dictation. - Arithmetic. - Object lessons. - The average of history and geography. - The average of arts (drawing, music, singing, handicrafts, calligraphy) and physical education.

Every pupil who is absent from the mid-year examination or the end-of-year examination for illegitimate reasons shall be given a zero in the subject from which he was absent. However, if the absence is for legitimate reasons approved by the Teachers' Council, he shall sit an examination upon his return to the school, or at the beginning of the following school year, and at the date fixed for the entrance examinations, in the event of his absence from the end-of-year examination. The marks of both examinations shall be included in the final average, or the general summary, in accordance with the provisions of Article 73 of these Regulations.

-1- The maximum working hours for permanent or daily attendants is 48 hours per week, distributed over a year of working days in the week.

2- The person in charge of the school shall organise the working hours of the attendants and wage-earners assigned to carry out the cleaning of the school, before, during and after official hours, according to a schedule which he shall post in the administration room and notify to the persons concerned.

3- The attendant shall refer to the person in charge of the school in all matters relating to the pupils.

4- The person assigned to clean the school buildings must perform the following:

A- Sweeping all rooms, halls, stairs and corridors daily, after the end of official hours.

B- Cleaning the rooms, halls, stairs and corridors with water and soap, at least once a week, and whenever the need arises.

C- Cleaning the drinking fountains and the various washrooms daily.

D- Cleaning the lavatories and sanitary fixtures daily, while applying special disinfectants to prevent odours and germs.

E- Daily cleaning and wiping of tables, cupboards, seats, curtains and other furniture.

F- Washing the glass facades once every two weeks.

G- Weekly cleaning of doors, windows and banisters.

H- Cleaning the carpets daily.

I- Cleaning the lighting fixtures once a month.

J- Washing and cleaning the laboratory instruments and apparatus, under the supervision of the science teachers and the persons in charge of the scientific laboratories. K- Cleaning the playgrounds and roofs and tending to the gardens and saplings, and everything relating to the school.

L- Locking the doors and windows, after finishing the cleaning.

5- The permanent attendant, in addition to the duties mentioned above, must inspect the school once a day during short holidays, and once a week during the summer holiday, and must inform the person in charge of the school of any emergencies that arise in the school.

6- School doorkeepers and attendants working therein are prohibited from taking up residence in the school building or engaging in commercial transactions of buying and selling, or commissioning anyone to act on their behalf therein.

- The person in charge of the school is prohibited from holding public ceremonies to which parents are invited, except with prior permission from the competent Department of Education, with the exception of Teacher's Day, Arbor Day, sports events, and exhibitions of drawing and handicrafts belonging to the pupils.
- School employees are strictly prohibited from conducting lotteries and selling books and school supplies of various kinds.

Teaching staff must care for the health of the pupils, supervise their seating and their general conduct, and remain alert to medical conditions that may spread among them, in order to take the necessary preventive and therapeutic measures.

The person in charge of the school shall supervise the execution of maintenance, sanitation, restoration, and various repair works scheduled for the school building, and shall ensure their execution during weekly days off and school holidays. School buildings may not be evacuated and closed on working days except with prior permission from the competent Department of Education.

At the end of each academic year, the person in charge of the school shall prepare a report on the progress of work in his school, submit it to his superiors, and send a copy thereof to the Educational Inspectorate.

Paymasters in public schools may be absent from their workplace for one day per month, after obtaining permission from the person in charge for one day per month, after obtaining permission from the person in charge of the school. This absence shall be recorded in the attendance register.
The provisions of this Decision shall apply to teachers contracted to teach in remote villages, in all matters that do not conflict with the provisions of the special texts relating to them.

If the guardian is unable to submit the pupil's identity card or a copy of his civil registry extract, any other supporting document, such as a mukhtar's certificate or a baptismal certificate, may be accepted, for a period not exceeding one academic year, with the approval of the competent Department of Education.

Former pupils who wish to re-register themselves in the same school shall be exempted from submitting the school certificate, the report card, or the identity card or a certified copy thereof, as provided for in Article 3 of these Regulations.
In exceptional cases where vacant places remain in the school, non-Lebanese pupils may be admitted.

The Director of Primary Education may reconsider the status of the officials currently assuming the school administrations, in the light of the conditions set forth in these Regulations, and propose to the competent authority the relief and assignment of the officials in charge of the administration of these schools.

Decisions No. 3389 dated 14/09/1953, No. 3543 dated 11/03/1954, No. 196 dated 22/04/1961 and No. 321 dated 16/04/1962, and all texts contrary to the provisions of this Decision or inconsistent with its content, are hereby repealed.
This Decision shall be published and notified where needed. Signature Beirut on 5 September 1968 Minister of National Education and Fine Arts

Teaching staff are prohibited from going on outings or trips with pupils on holidays without the written consent of their parents to bear all liability resulting therefrom, and subject to the written consent of the person in charge thereto. They are also prohibited, under penalty of liability, from assigning any pupils of their school to perform work unrelated to education, or to render any private services inside or outside the school.
Teaching staff may not under any circumstances bring into the school any book, bulletin, magazine or publication that is not closely related to the nature of their school work.

Public school staff must abide by the following in all their correspondence:

1- Following the rule of administrative hierarchy.

2- Stating the subject at the top of the letter.

3- Stating the place of work: the school, the district and the locality:

4- Stating the financial number.

5- Writing the name clearly beneath the signature, as it appears in the decree of appointment.

6- Stating the date.

A transferred employee shall file with the competent Department of Education a notice of assumption of duties, in which he states the number and date of the decision and to which he attaches a certificate from the person in charge of his former school, or the mukhtar of the village if he is a sole teacher, showing the date of his leaving work. In the event of his transfer to a school in which there is one or more other teachers, the person in charge thereof shall submit this notice of assumption of duties. As for a new sole teacher, he shall submit the notice of assumption of duties after it is certified by the mukhtar, stating therein the number of the decree relating to the appointment and the decision of assignment and their dates. In the event of his assignment to a school in which there is more than one teacher, the person in charge thereof shall submit this notice of assumption of duties.
The buildings of public schools and their contents may not be used for purposes other than official school business, except in the special cases provided for in the laws and regulations in force.

The persons in charge of public schools in which there is an official telephone apparatus shall: 1- Refrain from using the apparatus for purposes other than the interest of the service. 2- Record the calls that they make outside the town in a special register, clearly showing the date on which they were made and the reason therefor.

No staff member of primary and complementary public schools may leave Lebanese territory during school vacations before obtaining written permission from the Director of Primary Education, and he shall in this case submit an application in accordance with the rules prior to the date of travel thereto, and the reasons calling therefor.
Physical education teachers shall be subject to this Decision in all that does not conflict with the laws and regulations governing their affairs.

Subject and Terminology: 1- This Decision determines the internal regulations of public secondary schools 2- The following words and expressions used in this Decision shall have the meanings assigned to them: Teacher: anyone entrusted with teaching in one of the curricular years Principal: anyone assigned to manage the affairs of the secondary school Teaching Staff: the principal of the secondary school, its supervisors, and its teachers Secondary School Staff: all personnel working therein Guardian of the Student: his father, his mother, or one of the adult persons pursuant to an authorization accepted by the principal of the secondary school

Priority in enrolment shall be given: 1- to Lebanese nationals before others 2- to the children of employees working in secondary education and their siblings, and for this purpose they shall be exempted from the principle of adherence to the order of total marks - except among themselves after passing the examinations provided for in these Regulations

Admission of Pupils:

First - The new candidate pupil must submit the following documents:

1- A written application from his guardian indicating therein the guardian's identity, his profession, his degree of kinship to the pupil, and the required curricular year

2- His identity card or a photocopy thereof, or an extract of civil status registration, or whatever officially substitutes therefor, proving that the candidate pupil has not exceeded:

In the secondary schools of Beirut and the Governorate centres:

- The thirteenth year of his age for enrolment in the first intermediate year

- The fourteenth year of his age for enrolment in the second intermediate year

- The fifteenth year of his age for enrolment in the third intermediate year

- The sixteenth year of his age for enrolment in the fourth intermediate year

- The nineteenth year of his age - for enrolment in the first secondary year

- The twentieth year of his age for enrolment in the second secondary year

- The twenty-first year of his age for enrolment in the third secondary year

In all other secondary schools:

- The fourteenth year of his age, for enrolment in the first intermediate year

- The fifteenth year of his age for enrolment in the second intermediate year

- The sixteenth year of his age for enrolment in the third intermediate year

- The seventeenth year of his age for enrolment in the fourth intermediate year

- The twentieth year of his age for enrolment in the first secondary year

- The twenty-first year of his age for enrolment in the second secondary year

- The twenty-second year of his age for enrolment in the third secondary year

For determining age, the year in which registration takes place shall be adopted

As for candidates whose age exceeds the age mentioned above, the principal of the concerned secondary school shall submit their names to the Director of Secondary Education, who shall decide on their status in the light of his personal conviction and in the event that vacant places exist

3-a- The report card of grades for the previous year or a written certificate clearly showing the pupil's conduct and the final result with which his school year concluded, specified as promotion or failure, for candidates for entry into the various curricular years except the first and third secondary years

b- The Lebanese Higher Primary Studies Certificate or its equivalent containing the total official grades for candidates for entry into the first secondary year, or a written certificate from the principal of the previous school proving that the candidate passed in the final school results and that the school does not present its pupils for the official examinations (pursuant to a certificate issued by the Examinations Department determining the schools that do not nominate their pupils to obtain that certificate)

c- The Lebanese Baccalaureate Certificate Part One containing the total official grades in detail for candidates for entry into the third secondary year

4- If the report card of grades does not contain a sufficient clarification of conduct, a separate certificate of the pupil's conduct in the previous school shall be required

5- A certificate of successful completion of studies for the candidate for the fourth intermediate year or the second secondary year containing the list number of the previous school and the pupil's number therein, certified by the competent authority in the Ministry of National Education and Fine Arts

Second - The pupil must pass the entrance examinations organised for this purpose and in the cases required by these Internal Regulations

Third - All school fees shall be collected from the admitted pupil in accordance with the provisions of the laws and regulations in force, and he shall be accompanied by his guardian upon final registration

Fourth - For a returning pupil admitted for the new school year, it shall suffice that he pay the statutory fees

Fifth - All registered pupils shall be informed that they lose their places if they fail to join the secondary school three days after the commencement of classes without a legitimate reason of which the administration is notified and which it accepts
Special repeating classes: 1- Repeating classes may be established in public secondary schools, or in some of them. 2- The operation of these classes shall be regulated in a special decision.

The conditions of admission to the experimental technical sections established in some public secondary schools shall be determined by a special regulation issued by the Center for Educational Research and Development.

Those failing the entrance examinations: Candidates failing the entrance examinations to the second, third and fourth intermediate years and to the first and second secondary years shall be admitted to the lower curricular year in the event of available vacancies, provided that the total of their grades is not less than 60% of the passing average required in the entrance examinations.

Entrance examinations: In all entrance examinations provided for in these regulations, papers with a concealed name shall be used in the tests and shall be kept at the secondary school after the issuance of the results for a period of one school year, and the grades of the examination and the results pertaining thereto shall be recorded in the register of acceptance of applications for admission.

Transfer of pupils: 1- Pupils of public secondary schools who are compelled to transfer from one secondary school to another due to the transfer of the work of their guardians or due to the relocation of their residences shall be admitted during the academic year into the curricular year in which they were enrolled if there are vacancies, provided that the pupil submits a certificate proving the justification for this transfer, and outside of these stipulated cases, the approval of the Director of Secondary Education shall be obtained for the transfer. 2- If the interest of the secondary school or the educational interest of the pupil requires his transfer to a new secondary school, that shall be permissible, provided that the transfer takes place at the appropriate time after the approval of the Director of Secondary Education.
Commencement and end of the school year: The school year shall commence on the first working day following 20 September and shall end between 6 or 10 July.

Preparatory Work:

1- The preparatory work for the academic year shall be conducted over two periods:

The First Period: Starts immediately upon the announcement of the school results and ends within a period ranging between 6 and 10 July according to need, and includes the following work:

a- Registration of returning pupils

b- Acceptance of applications for admission to the years of the intermediate cycle and the first year of the secondary cycle, conducting entrance examinations for candidates, and registering the successful ones accepted from among them

- The Director of Secondary Education may extend this registration period by three working days at most if the public interest so requires and pursuant to a written request submitted by the principal of the secondary school concerned

The Second Period: Starts on the first working day following the twentieth of September and ends on the last working day preceding the beginning of the academic year, and includes the following work:

a- Conducting make-up examinations for returning pupils and registering the successful ones from among them

b- Acceptance of applications for admission to the remaining curricular years according to the vacant places therein, conducting entrance examinations for candidates, and registering the accepted ones from among them

c- Registration of returning pupils who failed to register during the first period if vacant places remain

d- All other preparatory work required for the proper functioning of work in the secondary school

2- All staff members of the secondary school belonging to the permanent cadre shall participate in the preparatory work in accordance with a schedule drawn up by the principal of the secondary school, and they must attend daily from eight o'clock until thirteen thirty

The principal of the secondary school may organize a shift schedule ensuring the presence of the necessary and appropriate number of staff members to secure the progress of the required work

Accommodating Applications for Admission:

1- In the event that applications for the second cycle fulfilling the conditions remain, the Director of Secondary Education shall seek to secure places for their applicants either by creating new sections or by referring these applications to nearby schools in which places are available

2- In the event that vacant places remain in the classes of the secondary cycle, and in addition to what is stated in Article Four (4:e) (5 - First: 2, Second: 2, Third: 2), the principal of the secondary school shall set a single new date for accepting new pupils, no later than 20 October, provided that the necessary examinations are conducted for them and the accepted ones are registered within a time limit and exceeding the end of the said month

The following registers, files and cards shall be kept in the secondary school:

1- Register of applications for admission

2- Annual enrolment register of pupils

3- Daily attendance register of pupils

4- Register of marks

5- Daily attendance register of contracted teachers

6- Daily attendance register of secondary school employees on the permanent staff

7- Register of incoming and outgoing transactions

8- Register of school furniture and illustrative aids

9- Register of laboratory equipment

10- Library register

11- Register of minutes of teachers' meetings

12- Register of minutes of meetings of the Council of Discipline and Guidance

13- Health register in which the physician's observations are recorded when necessary

14- Parents' Council register

15- Inspection register, in which summaries of the work of educational inspectors and administrative investigators are recorded

16- Files of school employees, in which the following documents are kept:

a- The employee's card

b- All documents, records and correspondence relating to the employee concerned from his entry into the secondary school until the date of his transfer, his placement outside the permanent staff, or his referral to retirement

These documents shall be sent to the entity to which he is transferred

17- Personal files of pupils, in which the following documents are kept:

a- Documents relating to their admission to the secondary school and all papers specific to them

Which shall be destroyed one year after the pupil leaves the secondary school

b- The personal card that accompanies the pupil throughout the duration of his study

Provided that it is kept in alphabetical order after he leaves the secondary school

18- A general register of all persons working in the secondary school, indicating their functions, their certificates, and the cycle and subject taught by each of them

Designation of the Principal and Conditions of His Assignment:

1- Administration is the designation of one of the teaching staff members to manage the affairs of a specific secondary school

2- The secondary school principal shall be assigned by a decision issued by the Minister of National Education and Fine Arts upon the proposal of the Director of Secondary Education and the approval of the Director General of National Education, in accordance with the following conditions:

a- That he be one of the public secondary education teachers, and that at least five years have elapsed since his entry into the cadre of public secondary education

b- That he have demonstrated during his work competence and capability qualifying him to manage the secondary school

c- That he have not been sentenced (during the last five years) to a penalty of the second degree provided for in the Civil Servants Regulations, or to the last two penalties together of the penalties of the first degree at their maximum limit, or twice to either of them at its maximum limit, and the prohibition from the right of appointment shall lapse after the passage of five years from the last penalty pursuant to an application submitted by the person concerned in which his direct superior expresses his opinion and on which the competent administration decides

d- That he be among those who are proficient in the foreign language adopted by the secondary school

e- That he undergo a personal aptitude test by a committee formed under the chairmanship of the Director General of National Education or whoever he delegates, and the membership of the Director of Secondary Education and one of the secondary education inspectors or one of the members of the teaching body in the cadre of the Lebanese University (1)

3- Principals who were assigned in accordance with the rules prior to the entry into force of this decision shall be exempted from the provisions of paragraphs a, b, d,

4- The following Item 4 was added pursuant to Decision No. 534 dated 22/10/1977:

The successful candidate shall be appointed principal of a secondary school for a single probationary year, at the end of which he shall be confirmed or returned to teaching

5- The following Item 5 was added pursuant to Decision No. 534 dated 22/10/1977:

The term of office of the principal shall in all cases be three years, renewable upon the recommendation of the committee referred to in paragraph "e" of Item 2 of this Article (2) (1)

Article 3 of Decision 534 dated 22/10/77: The General Supervisor and the Supervisor may be required to teach 5 regular hours weekly out of the weekly working hours legally prescribed for him within the school to which he is attached - Article 4 of Decision 534/1977: An hour of actual teaching shall be considered equivalent to an hour and a half of administrative working hours

Article 15: Ensuring Administrative Duties in an Acting Capacity: 1- In the cases in which the position of the Administration becomes vacant (such as death, leave, suspension from work, judicial detention, or relief from the Administration, etc...), the General Supervisor shall ensure the duties of the Administration until the incumbent Principal returns or someone is assigned to replace him. 2- In the event of the absence of the General Supervisor or the vacancy of his position, the administrative duties shall be ensured by the Supervisor whom the Principal assigns in writing to do so.

Article 16: Relief of the Principal: The Principal shall be relieved of his administrative duties in the following cases:

1- If the school which he manages is permanently closed

2- If a penalty among the penalties mentioned in paragraph C of Article 14 of these Regulations is imposed

3- If it is proven that he has failed in his mission

4- If he is transferred to another secondary school at his request

The General Supervisor and the Supervisors:

1- A General Supervisor selected from among the tenured teachers upon the proposal of the Principal of the Secondary School and the approval of the Director of Secondary Education shall assist the Principal of the Secondary School in his duties, and shall carry out the duties assigned to him in accordance with the directives of the Principal

2- The Supervisors shall be selected from among the tenured secondary education teachers upon the proposal of the Principal of the Secondary School and the approval of the Director of Secondary Education

3- The number of Supervisors shall be determined at the rate of one Supervisor for every one hundred and fifty pupils, and the Director of Secondary Education may amend this ratio upon the proposal of the Principal of the Secondary School and on the basis of the number of floors and the number of classes on each of them

4- The Supervisors shall carry out all the duties assigned to them by the Administration in a manner within their competence, including guidance, sponsoring activities, attending to the affairs of the pupils, and everything relating to their discipline, supervising them in the playground, monitoring their attendance, and organising their grade cards and their personal files

5- The distribution of the working hours of the General Supervisor and the Supervisors shall cover supervision and monitoring in the Secondary School on a continuous basis during school hours, the noon break, and half an hour before the start of lessons in the morning

6- The Director of Secondary Education shall have the right to return the General Supervisor or the Supervisor to teaching at the request of the person concerned or upon the proposal of the Principal of the Secondary School on grounds of public interest

1- - There shall be attached to every secondary school:

a- One laboratory preparer if the number of sections therein does not exceed 15 sections

b- Two preparers if the number of sections therein does not exceed 25 sections

c- Three preparers if the number of sections therein exceeds 25 sections

2- The laboratory preparer must attend to the affairs of the laboratories of the Secondary School, and consequently

a- Prepare the visual aids and experiments requested of him by the teachers of scientific subjects

b- Organise registers of the instruments and equipment of the laboratories

c- Maintain the apparatus and equipment and preserve them from damage

d- Carry out all the duties required for the proper functioning of work in the laboratories within a programme drawn up by the persons in charge of those laboratories and approved by the Principal of the Secondary School

Coordinators:

1- The principal of the secondary school shall assign, after the approval of the Director of Secondary Education, one of the teachers in respect of each subject the task of coordinating work among his colleagues, provided that he is among those who teach at the secondary stage if he undertakes coordination in both the intermediate and secondary stages together or in the secondary stage alone.

2- The weekly teaching load of the coordinator shall be reduced at the rate of one teaching hour for every 15 hours of the total hours of each subject and every fraction exceeding one third, provided that the number of coordination hours for each subject does not exceed ten hours weekly.

3- The coordinator shall undertake the following matters:

a- Distributing the prescribed curriculum for the subject in each class over the months of the year at the end of the academic year in preparation for the following year, in cooperation with the teachers of the subject.

b- Agreeing on the general steps for teaching methods and correcting school homework.

c- Attending lessons and recording educational observations to discuss them with the teachers after the dismissal of the pupils or in a special meeting, and the coordinator shall receive his colleagues to attend lessons with him in his class when necessary.

d- Supervising assignments, quizzes, and examinations.

e- Holding monthly meetings for all teachers of the subject and recording the summary of these meetings in a special register to be submitted to the principal of the secondary school at the end of each term.

f- Informing the teachers of the subject of what has been introduced in the field of education within the specified specialisation and assisting them in applying it inside and outside the classes.

g- Ensuring the application of the provisions of the internal regulations of public secondary schools regarding assignments, tests, the preparation notebook, and the grades notebook.

h- Setting examination and test questions and the grading scale after consulting the opinion of the teachers concerned, and submitting them to the principal of the secondary school to select what is suitable therefrom.

i- All other works required by the general educational interest.

4- The coordinators of the subjects of natural sciences and chemistry shall undertake, in addition to the tasks mentioned above, responsibility for the laboratory, provided that the teaching hours for each of them are not less than nine hours weekly.

Determining the number of sections annually: The Director of Secondary Education shall determine, annually, the number of sections in each secondary school after consulting the opinion of its principal.

New classes: New classes shall be established if a number of pupils amounting to at least twenty pupils in the years of the intermediate stage and at least fifteen pupils in the years of the secondary stage is secured for each of them.

Article 23: Number of pupils in each class: The maximum number of pupils in each class shall be set at forty pupils, except for the classes in which the foreign language is given by the audio-visual method, in which the number in each of them shall be set at twenty-six pupils, and the Director of Secondary Education shall have the right to increase the number within the limits of six pupils if the conditions of registration require this measure and if the capacity in the classrooms permits it

Article 24: The academic year and holidays:

1- Lessons in public secondary schools shall commence on the first working day following the fifth of the month of October

2- The weekly holiday in public secondary schools shall be determined by a special decision issued by the Minister of National Education and Fine Arts

Article 25: Working hours:

1- The daily school working hours are:

a- Four teaching periods before noon interspersed with a break period of not less than thirty minutes

b- Two periods or three periods in the afternoon c- A single teaching period shall be set at fifty-five minutes

2- The principal of the secondary school may propose an amendment to this schedule if the interest of the secondary school so requires, and this amendment shall not take effect until after the approval of both the Director General of National Education and the Director of Secondary Education

3- The working hours for all employees of the secondary school included in the cadre shall be distributed over five days a week, and the Director of Secondary Education shall have the right to exempt some employees from this measure if he is convinced of the justifying reasons submitted to him in writing and through the hierarchical channel by the persons concerned

4-a- During the month of June, a single-session schedule shall be applied, provided that the pupils are given all the periods prescribed in the weekly lesson timetable, and the period shall then be fifty minutes

b- The working hours of the supervisors shall be adjusted to conform with this schedule, provided that the total of their working hours does not fall below 27 hours per week

Article 26: The weekly quota:

1- The weekly quota for the employees of the secondary school shall be set as follows:

a- Thirty hours for the principal

b- Twenty-seven hours for the general supervisor, the supervisors, and the laboratory preparers

c- Twenty teaching hours for the teacher

2- If the teacher's schedule is distributed between teaching and administrative work, each hour and a half of the administrative schedule shall be counted as equivalent to one teaching hour

2- The schedule of servants, guards, ushers, and all other wage-earners and the conditions of their work shall be determined by a special decision

Control of Attendance:

1- All employees of the secondary school (with the exception of contractual teachers, servants, ushers and guards) shall sign the attendance register immediately upon their arrival and in accordance with the sequence of their attendance at the secondary school, and the principal or whomever he delegates from among the supervisors shall record his observations where necessary

2- Contractual teachers shall sign a special register

Duties of Teachers:

The duties of teachers are determined as follows:

1- Cooperating with the administration in school work, abiding

by the Employees' Regulations and all other regulations governing their affairs, and performing

their duties in a manner consistent with the educational mission

2- Organising a detailed schedule comprising the distribution of the curriculum of the subjects prescribed

for the class over the months of the year, in cooperation with the subject coordinator,

if any

3- Organising a notebook (or cards) for lesson preparation and for marks

and presenting it to the principal of the secondary school, the educational inspector or the subject coordinator

where necessary

4- Joining the class when the bell rings and before the pupils enter it

5- Attending the meetings called by the administration, which must

usually be held outside teaching hours, and every absence from

the meetings without a legitimate excuse approved by the principal of the secondary school shall be considered a breach

of the teacher's professional duties

6- Giving the pupils:

a- Preparations and exercises in the subjects of mathematics and sciences following

the lessons given, provided that the work is corrected in class

b- An assignment in each of the subjects of mathematics and sciences once every two weeks,

provided that it is corrected and evaluated by the teacher, for all curricular

years

c- Geographical exercises according to the need agreed upon with the subject

coordinator or the administration, for all curricular years

d-1- Exercises in grammar following the lessons given, corrected in class

2- Applied dictation once a week, corrected and evaluated in class

3- Fifteen composition assignments at least per year, corrected and evaluated

by the teacher, in each of the Arabic and foreign languages

and in the classes of the intermediate cycle

e- Seven assignments at least per year in each of the subjects of language

and its literature and philosophy, in the classes of the secondary cycle; these assignments shall be accompanied by

preparations in class

7- Teachers of the subjects of experimental sciences shall notify the laboratory preparer

in advance of what they need for their experiments, and teachers of other

subjects shall prepare the necessary illustrative aids before the time of the lesson

8- Teachers of subjects that require practical illustration shall accompany

their pupils to the places they wish to visit, and after obtaining

written approval from the guardians of the pupils

Attendance during the end-of-year examinations period: All teachers shall abide by the attendance schedule established by the director of the secondary school for the end-of-year examinations period, and teachers who are examiners in the official examinations shall not be entitled to participate in the grading process except after securing their primary work at the secondary school

The Teachers' Council: 1- The Teachers' Council shall be composed of the director of the secondary school as chairman and the remaining teaching staff as members, and its mission shall be to examine educational and cultural affairs relating to the secondary school 2- The Council shall meet once at the beginning of the year and whenever convened in writing by the director of the secondary school or pursuant to a written request submitted by one third of the members of the teaching staff at the secondary school stating the subject of the meeting therein, and the director of the secondary school shall set the agenda of the session and notify each of the teachers thereof at least twenty-four hours prior to the time of the meeting, and no person from outside the secondary school may attend these sessions 3- The general supervisor or one of the supervisors shall undertake the recording of the minutes of the sessions

The Coordinators' Council: The Coordinators' Council shall meet at the invitation of the director of the secondary school or pursuant to a written request submitted by two of them, stating therein the subject of the meeting and its agenda

The Discipline and Guidance Council:

1- The guiding principle of the Discipline and Guidance Council is reform, prevention, and the awakening of conscience and the sense of responsibility; it shall study general behavioural and educational cases, and shall take disciplinary measures within the limits of the penalties prescribed in Article 39 of these Regulations

2- The Discipline and Guidance Council shall consist of the director of the secondary school as chairman, the general supervisor as rapporteur, the supervisor responsible at the time the infraction occurred, and five members elected by the Teachers' Council at the beginning of the school year from among the tenured teachers excluding the supervisors, and if the required number of tenured teachers is unavailable, the remaining members may be elected from among the contracted teachers

Rules for the Convening of the Discipline and Guidance Council:

1-a- The Discipline and Guidance Council shall meet upon a convocation by its Chairman or upon a reasoned request from one of the members of the teaching staff or the supervisors approved by the Principal of the secondary school.

b- The meetings of the Council shall not be valid unless an absolute majority of the members is present. c- None of the members of the Council shall participate in its meetings if he himself is the complainant; the Principal shall be exempted from this prohibition. d- Decisions shall be taken by a majority, and in the event of a tie, the Chairman shall have a casting vote.

2-a- In the event that the Council convenes as a disciplinary board, the Chairman of the Council shall verify, prior to commencing the proceedings, that the offender who is the subject of the complaint has been notified of the date of the session and the subject of the charge brought against him, and that he has been given the opportunity to defend himself. b- The General Supervisor shall undertake the direct investigation and submit a written report to the Council prior to the commencement of its meeting.

c- Deliberations shall remain confidential, and only the facts and the decisions taken, signed by the Principal of the secondary school and all members present, shall be recorded in the register of the Discipline and Guidance Council.

d- The General Supervisor shall notify the concerned parties of the decisions taken against them.
The Parents' Council: This Council, in the event of its establishment, shall be composed of the guardians of the pupils of the secondary school in accordance with special regulations.

Types thereof:

1- Sick leave, substantiated by a medical certificate from the competent authority.

2- Marriage leave.

3- Leave due to the death of one of the ascendants, descendants, brothers, sisters, husband, or wife.

4- Maternity leave.

5- Leave for private affairs.

Obtaining it:

1- If one of the employees of the secondary school is absent for any reason whatsoever, he must immediately notify the principal of the secondary school of the condition that necessitated his absence, the expected duration of the absence, and his address during the period of absence

2- In the event of a health impediment, the employee shall send to the principal of the secondary school a medical report within 24 hours from the commencement of the absence indicating the nature of the impediment, the expected duration of the absence, and that the physician has verified his identity, and he shall abide by the instructions issued in this regard 3- If the employee requests leave without pay for personal reasons, he must abide by the following:

A- He shall submit a written application through the administrative hierarchy indicating therein the duration of the leave and the reasons calling for it, and attach to it the necessary documents and supporting papers, and a copy of this application together with the supporting papers shall be kept in the file of the employee

B- The employee applying for leave may not leave his place of work prior to the issuance of the leave decision except in proven cases of necessity in which the duration of absence does not exceed three days at most, provided that it is accompanied by the written approval of the principal of the secondary school The immediate superior shall immediately refer the application to the competent authority and enclose the supporting papers therewith after expressing his opinion thereon in writing

C- Working days may not be divided, and every partial absence from the day shall be considered an absence of a full day

4- Holidays shall be included within the duration of the leave if school holidays intervene during the leave

5- The principal of the secondary school shall have the right to authorize the employees of the secondary school, in cases of urgent necessity, without a medical report, and on his own responsibility, to be absent from their work with full pay for part of a day or for a full day for health or social reasons, provided that this does not exceed two days in a single school year This absence and its reason shall be recorded in the card of the person concerned

6- An employee who is absent from his place of work without lawful leave shall forfeit his right to salary for the duration of his absence, in addition to the disciplinary penalties that may be imposed upon him in accordance with the laws and regulations in force, with the possibility of considering him as having resigned if the unlawful absence exceeds a period of 15 days

7- If the employee does not resume his work at the end of the leave, whatever its nature may be, the principal of the secondary school must inform his superior thereof immediately, and upon the return of the absent employee, in this case only, he must inform his superior again, indicating the duration of the additional absence and its reasons However, if the absence without lawful leave exceeds fifteen days, the principal of the secondary school shall not have the right to allow the employee to resume his work unless he receives a written order to that effect from the Director of Secondary Education

Duties of the pupil: A pupil who has been admitted to the secondary school shall:

First- 1- Abide by the school regulations and laws and the decisions of the administration

2- Maintain order and the general rules of conduct

3- Take care of cleanliness and preserve the furniture, building and contents of the secondary school

4- Act in accordance with the instructions of the administration regarding attire and outward appearance

5- Participate effectively in one of the extracurricular activities Second- The following matters are prohibited to pupils:

1- Propagating the principles of partisan and political bodies among the pupils or displaying partisan insignia inside the secondary school

2- Participating in demonstrations and strikes and inciting thereto

3- Smoking inside the secondary school

4- Leaving the secondary school during official hours except on account of illness, or upon a request from his guardian in person, by telephone or in writing in the cases determined by the principal of the secondary school, or by special permission from the principal or the general supervisor

5- Selling tickets for parties and lotteries or carrying and distributing leaflets, newspapers and magazines - Harmful and dangerous printed matter and possessions shall be confiscated from the pupils and handed over immediately to the principal of the secondary school or the general supervisor

Status of the absent pupil:

1- An absent pupil shall not be admitted except in the presence of his guardian in person, and where the attendance of the guardian is not possible, the absent pupil shall be admitted in the cases assessed by the principal of the secondary school, and the absence shall be deemed legitimate if the pupil submits an excuse acceptable to the administration or a medical report

2- If the absence is partial from certain teaching hours, every four hours shall be counted as one day of absence, whereas if the pupil is late by a few minutes without a legitimate excuse for one of the lesson hours, he shall be barred from entering the classroom during that hour and one hour of absence shall be counted against him, and certain other additional penalties may also be imposed upon him

Penalties:

1- In the event that the pupil violates the laws of the secondary school or its regulations and public morals, one of the following penalties shall be imposed upon him without adhering to their gradation:

a- Written caution

b- Reprimand

c- Deduction of conduct marks

d- Warning by a letter to the pupil's guardian signed by the principal of the secondary school

e- Suspension from the secondary school for a period not exceeding one week

f- Suspension from the secondary school for a period exceeding one week and not exceeding four weeks

g- Expulsion All penalties shall be recorded in the pupil's personal card, and penalties d, d, and f shall be accompanied by the dropping of more than the conduct marks

2- The teacher and the supervisors shall impose the first penalty, the principal shall impose the first five penalties, and the Discipline and Guidance Council shall take one of the last two penalties The penalty of the last degree shall not become final until after the approval of the Director of Secondary Education, and the pupil shall remain suspended from the secondary school until the approval is received

Dismissal from the secondary school:

1- A pupil shall be dismissed automatically from the secondary school and shall not be readmitted thereto:

a- If he fails in his class and obtains less than 60% of the required passing average, and that is for pupils of the intermediate stage and the first secondary year

b- If he fails for two consecutive years in one curricular year or fails in more than two curricular years of either of the intermediate and secondary stages

c- If a decision of final dismissal is issued against him by the Discipline and Guidance Council

d- If the administrative body recommends by a two-thirds majority not to admit him due to his participation in demonstrations or strikes and incitement thereto

e- If the teachers of his class and the responsible supervisor recommend by a two-thirds majority not to admit him due to his misconduct or his negligence in school duties or his discontinuance of attendance at the secondary school before the specified date

f- If he does not attend two-thirds of the days of the annual school work, except in exceptional circumstances assessed by the Director of Secondary Education based on the opinion of the principal of the secondary school

g- If he does not persevere in attending the secondary school until the last working day preceding the end-of-year examinations without an acceptable excuse h- If he fails to attend the secondary school for more than ten days of the annual school work attendance without an acceptable excuse

i- If his conduct average falls below 10/20 2- A dismissed pupil may submit an application for enrolment in another secondary school if the conditions of enrolment are met in him, with the exception of a pupil who was dismissed pursuant to paragraphs a-d- of this Article

Tests and the End-of-Year Examination:

1- Four tests shall be organised during the school year and one examination at the end thereof called the end-of-year examination

2- The dates of the four tests shall be determined by the Administration during the second half of November, January and March and the first half of May

3- The classes of the second and third secondary years shall be exempted from the May test

4- The end-of-year examination shall be held: a- in respect of the classes of the second and third secondary years, during the month of May b- in respect of the fourth intermediate year, during the first week of the month of June

c- in respect of the remaining curricular years:

1- Seven working days prior to the date fixed for the commencement of the official examinations for the Lebanese Baccalaureate certificate in the secondary schools that are taken as centres for the official examinations, and if the date of the examination for the Intermediate Certificate is fixed during the period of the seven working days mentioned above, the principal of the secondary school may bring forward the date of the end-of-year examination by two days at most

2- Starting from the eighteenth of the month of June in secondary schools where the number of pupils exceeds 300 pupils

3- Starting from the twenty-second of the month of June in secondary schools where the number of pupils does not exceed 300 pupils

5- The end-of-year examination shall cover:

a- In respect of the pupils of the secondary stage: the subjects of the prescribed official curriculum in its entirety

b- In respect of the pupils of the intermediate stage: topics or parts of the curriculum selected by the coordinator in consultation with the teachers of the subject, provided that they are not less than half of the curriculum prescribed for each subject in the given curricular year, and they shall be announced to the pupils at least two weeks prior to the date of commencement of the examination papers

6- The principal of the secondary school shall grant the pupils only a leave of one working day, if need be, preceding the end-of-year examination, during which they shall cease attending the secondary school

7- The marks of each subject and their averages shall be organised in accordance with Article 43 of these Regulations

Determination of the Final Result:

First- 1- The average of the grades of the written and oral recitations and the assignments shall be deemed one-third of the annual grade and shall be called the daily effort grade

2- The average of the tests shall be deemed the second third of the annual grade
