Every inhabited place the number of whose resident inhabitants exceeds fifty souls shall be administered by one mukhtar assisted by an ikhtiyariyya council, whereas a village whose inhabitants reach such number shall be administered by the mukhtar and council of the village nearest to it.

Places the number of whose resident inhabitants exceeds 3000 souls shall have the status of a town and shall be divided into quarters, and the quarter shall be considered as a village and the provisions of the two preceding Articles shall apply with respect to it. Quarters shall be considered as they are registered in the census, and no new quarter may be established or a quarter merged with another except by a decision of the Minister of the Interior.

The provisions relating to the election of municipal councils shall apply to the electoral lists for mukhtars and members of ikhtiyariyya councils, their preparation, publication, and objection thereto, ensuring the conduct of the election, the appointment of polling committees, the regulations, and the proclamation and notification of the electoral results.
There shall be imposed upon the ikhtiyariyya elector and elected person the conditions required of the municipal elector and elected person, save for the special cases provided for in this Law.

A single person may not be a mukhtar or an ikhtiyariyya member for more than one locality, and likewise a father and son, father-in-law and son-in-law, brothers, and relatives by marriage of whatever kind may not be mukhtars or members of an ikhtiyariyya council in a single locality; if two of the relatives and affinities aforementioned are elected and neither of them resigns, the Governor or the Qaimaqam must dismiss the younger of the two in age, and if they are equal in age one of them shall be dismissed by lot.

The office of mukhtar may not be combined with the office of municipal council member, administrative council member, or any public office; if it happens that the two offices are combined in one person, the elected person shall be granted a time limit of seven days to choose one of them, and if this time limit expires and he has not done so, he shall be deemed by operation of law to have relinquished the office that is earlier in date.

Before exercising his office, the mukhtar must swear before the Justice of the Peace of the district the following oath:

- I swear by Almighty God that I shall carry out the mission entrusted to me with all impartiality, honesty, and fidelity.

The term of office of mukhtars and members of the ikhtiyariyah councils shall be six years commencing from the date of the election. If the post of mukhtar becomes vacant or he is suspended from duty at any time whatsoever, the Minister of the Interior shall appoint the eldest member of the ikhtiyariyah council as an alternate mukhtar in his place to complete the term of office.

In mukhtariyahs in which there are no ikhtiyariyah members, the Minister of the Interior may appoint as mukhtar the person who received in the last ikhtiyariyah election the largest number of votes in the quarter in which the post of mukhtar became vacant.

If the post of an ikhtiyariyah member becomes vacant at any time whatsoever, the Minister of the Interior shall appoint to his vacant post the person who received in the last ikhtiyariyah election the largest number of votes after the elected ikhtiyariyah members. This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The mukhtar must register the transactions received by him and issued by him in a register whose pages are stamped and signed by the Muhafiz or the Qaimaqam, and he must register at the centre of the Qada his signature and the special seal which is made in accordance with a uniform model established by the Ministry of the Interior; and if this seal is lost, he must obtain another from the Ministry of the Interior.

The functions of mukhtars are gratuitous; however, they may levy fees, the amount of which shall be determined by decree, for the original certificates which they issue:

1 - For a travel transaction.

2 - For succession determination transactions.

3 - For executing a contract of mortgage or a contract of sale.

4 - For the legal authentication of a signature.

5 - For issuing a certificate pertaining to proof of attachment of property.

6 - For registering an estate inventory list.

7 - For confirming the limitation of property.

8 - For civil status events.

9 - For individuals within the regulations in force.

Every mukhtar whose term of office expires and who continues to exercise it or abstains from handing over the documents pertaining to his function to the administrative authority shall be punished pursuant to Article 375 of the Penal Code.

The mukhtar may resign at any time, and his letter of resignation shall be submitted to the Muhafiz, who shall decide upon its acceptance within one month from the date of its receipt; and if he does not decide upon the request within this period, the resignation shall be deemed final after the lapse of one month from the date of its submission once again by registered letter.

The mukhtar may not absent himself from his village or his quarter for a period exceeding ten days without leave from the Muhafiz or the Qaimaqam, and one of the members of the ikhtiyariyah who is delegated in his place in the leave decision shall deputise for him during the period of his absence.

If the Mukhtar or a member of the Ikhtiyariyya Council commits an offence relating to the office, the Qa'immaqam or the Muhafiz may order the conduct of an investigation against him, to be referred to the Minister of the Interior, who shall authorise the conduct of a judicial investigation or suspend from office the judiciary decides on the matter, and he shall not return to office unless a judgment of his acquittal or of his non-liability is rendered.
The Mukhtar and the members of the Ikhtiyariyya Council shall work for the good of the village and the facilitation of the affairs of its inhabitants.

The following documents signed by the Mukhtar must also be accompanied by the signature of one of the members of the Ikhtiyariyya Council:

1 - Clarifications relating to the disposal and transfer of properties, their survey, and the designation of the owner concerned and his co-owners in the property.

2 - Certificates given as to the identity of the transferor and the transferee, or either of them, and that they are still alive, that they are in the legally recognized capacity, and that the transfer did not issue from duress.

3 - Statements relating to possessors of lands whose owners do not hold registered deeds.

The Mukhtar shall preside over the Ikhtiyariyya Council and represent the village or the quarter in petitioning the authorities regarding that which brings benefit to the inhabitants, and he shall represent the Administration in the affairs set forth below:

General administration and public security.

The Mukhtar must:

1 - Promulgate laws, regulations and instructions in accordance with the orders of the authority.

2 - Perform the duties imposed upon him by the laws and decisions that are put into execution.

3 - Issue certificates of good conduct to those worthy thereof and the certificates required in transactions for the restoration of forfeited rights.

4 - Issue the certificates required by the Passports Department.

5 - Inform the administrative authority of acts which may to the disturbance of public security.

6 - Issue an official notice registered in the outgoing register of every misdemeanour and felony occurring within his village or quarter which is among the offences prosecuted through public action upon mere notice thereof, and issue notice of every secret or public meeting that is unauthorized.

7 - Facilitate the mission of officials of the Administration when performing their duty within the scope of his village or quarter personal status.

The Mukhtar must, in accordance with the laws and regulations in force, perform the following duties:

1 - Maintaining the civil status register of the village or neighbourhood and recording all new events communicated to him by the Civil Status Department.

2 - Certifying census events when a census takes place and distributing identity cards.

3 - Issuing certificates that serve as a basis for correcting age or name, renewing identity registration, and obtaining a replacement for a lost document.

4 - Certifying the birth certificate after verifying the declarations of the parents through the statement of a physician or a midwife or through his personal knowledge.

5 - Certifying the certificate of marriage, divorce, or annulment of marriage.

6 - Drawing up the death certificate, stating the cause and date of death.

7 - Refraining from certifying the authenticity of a signature or fingerprint except after verifying the identity of the person and stating the number of his identity card in the certification clause.

8 - Executing the laws, decisions, and instructions that provide for measures requiring the Mukhtar to perform them and that relate to personal status Financial affairs.

The Mukhtar must:

1 - Assist and aid tax collectors in collecting taxes and carrying out attachment proceedings against the property of taxpayers, and assist finance officers and the Tobacco and Alcohol Monopoly Administration in performing their functions in the area.

2 - Aid tax committees operating within his area.

3 - Issue the written certificates requested of him concerning the financial solvency of guarantors or concerning guarantees.

4 - Notify the competent department of every plot of land that becomes the property of the State following the death of its owner without an heir.

5 - Broadcast the notices and instructions issued by the Ministry of Finance concerning taxes and judicial fees.

The Mukhtar must:

1 - Assist the bailiffs of the regular courts and the Sharia courts in effecting all judicial notifications and providing an endorsement regarding them.

2 - Accompany security officers when entering premises required to be searched.

3 - Perform what is imposed upon him by his office in his capacity as an officer of the judicial police.

In Real Estate Affairs:

(Amended by the Law of 21 June 1950) The Mukhtar must:

1 - Preserve the old cadastral register and the register known as the Jarida in the regions where the modern cadastral survey has not yet been completed.

2 - Refrain from recording alterations or new occurrences in this register except on the basis of registered deeds.

3 - Keep in a special file the registered copy of every certificate of notice and knowledge that he issues, and give these statements serial numbers.

4 - State the origin of possession and the manner of its acquisition in the statements that he issues.

5 - Preserve the ledger of the apportionment of irrigation rights from public springs in the regions where such apportionment has been conducted, and refrain from recording new occurrences in this register except on the basis of established deeds.

6 - Represent the village that has no municipality or communal land committee in actions in rem arising in respect of communal lands Agricultural Affairs.

The Mukhtar must:

1 - Execute all instructions that he receives through the administrative authority from the agents of the Departments of Agriculture and Forests.

2 - Notify the agriculture officers through the administration upon ascertaining the occurrence of the felling of forest trees without a licence, or upon ascertaining the felling of quantities exceeding the quantity licensed to be felled.

3 - Promptly notify the authority of the presence of epidemic diseases in plants, such as the vine for example, or upon the appearance of insects that threaten crops in general.

4 - Undertake the collection of the remunerations of public rural watchmen from property owners in accordance with the procedures followed for the collection of state revenues.

5 - Register the reports submitted to him by the public rural watchman in a special register and submit them to the Qaemقام with his own annotation regarding what has come to his knowledge as to the veracity of the report Health Affairs.

The Mukhtar must:

1 - Notify the administrative authority of infectious and epidemic diseases that afflict persons and animals.

2 - Induce the inhabitants to be vaccinated upon the occurrence of an epidemic, and endeavour by all means to prevent contact until the Government takes the final health measures.

3 - Notify the authority of incidents that occur by reason of eating poisoned meat or cheese or similar incidents Education and Fine Arts.

The Mukhtar must:

1 - Urge the inhabitants to send their children to schools.

2 - Undertake the protection of archaeological buildings and notify the administrative authority of any damage that occurs therein.

3 - Endeavour to apply the law on the protection of juveniles and the non-employment thereof.

(Corrected by the Law of 17 February 1948:)

The electoral bodies shall be convened within six months following the entry into force of this Law to elect the mukhtars and the members of the mukhtar councils.
On the date of the announcement of the electoral results, every former mukhtar and mukhtar council member who on that date is still exercising this function of his shall be deemed to have resigned.

All laws and regulations contrary to this Law and inconsistent with its provisions are hereby repealed, in particular:

- The Law promulgated on 13 January 1928 and its addendum promulgated on 20 February 1928.

- And Legislative Decree No. 2 promulgated on 18 October 1939.
This Law shall be published in the Official Gazette.

Article One: The text of Article 543 of the Code of Obligations and Contracts is repealed in respect of lease contracts concluded after the date of entry into force of this Law and is replaced by the following text: Lease contracts of built real properties prepared for residential and non-residential use shall be subject to the freedom of the contracting party and the will of the contracting parties in all that does not conflict with the following mandatory provisions: First: Term: If the term specified in the contract is less than three years, the lease shall be deemed concluded for a period of time of three years. However, if the lessee benefiting from the extension wishes to vacate the leased premises, he must notify the lessor two months before the end of the extended year by an open registered card with acknowledgment of receipt or by virtue of a letter addressed through the Notary Public. Second: The following are exempted from the preceding provisions: a- Seasonal lease contracts relating to summer and winter resorts. b- Lease contracts of premises provided by employers to their employees free of charge or for consideration. Third: If a lease contract of real property, whether built or unbuilt, exceeds a term of three years, it shall not be valid with respect to a third party unless the contract is registered in the Real Property Register, and the registration of the tacit renewal of the lease contract shall be subject to the same rule.

Article Two: This Law shall enter into force upon its publication in the Official Gazette. The working mechanism set forth in the articles of this Decree shall be adopted in preventive and rescue archaeological excavations and other field interventions executed by the Directorate General of Antiquities directly through its own archaeologists and/or by engaging archaeologists and specialists who do not work for it and/or from local and foreign scientific bodies, notably the Lebanese University within the framework of the Memorandum of Understanding signed by it with the Ministry of Culture, and other universities having expertise similar to that accumulated by the said university, with which agreements may be concluded for this purpose.

The following designations shall be adopted for the application of the provisions of this Decree:

1 - The Scientific Director: The person scientifically and practically responsible for an archaeological excavation and for all scientific archaeological studies relating thereto. Where he is from outside the cadre of the Directorate, he must hold a doctorate degree in archaeology and even have 3 years' experience in archaeological excavations with scientific publications; it shall be incumbent upon the Scientific Director to select the archaeologists and experts with whom he wishes to work, and he shall bear the responsibility of conducting all necessary studies for the excavations that he directs, as well as publishing them by known and recognised scientific methods.

2 - The Responsible Archaeologist: The archaeologist employed by or contracted with the Directorate General of Antiquities who is assigned by the Director General of Antiquities to the tasks of supervising a specific archaeological excavation or archaeological excavations in general or the sections in the regions, holding a master's degree in archaeology or having a seniority exceeding five years within the Directorate General of Antiquities.

3 - The Archaeologist: Every person from outside the Directorate General of Antiquities holding a university degree in archaeology issued by a recognised university or technical institute whose assistance is enlisted by the said Directorate or the scientific body in order to carry out specific archaeological works.

4 - The Site Coordinator: The archaeologist whose assistance is enlisted from outside the administration and who is assigned by the Director General of Antiquities to the matter of practical coordination on the site in accordance with the list of qualifications and rates (Grading) established by the Directorate General of Antiquities, or any archaeologist from within the Directorate General of Antiquities who is designated by the Director General of Antiquities.

5 - The Real Property: The real property situated in a specific cadastral zone and which contains the discovered antiquities.

6 - The Owner: The owning entity of the real property and/or all owners of subdivided floors, whether residential apartments or commercial or industrial offices and otherwise... or their legal representative.

7 - The Entity Responsible for the Real Property: The owner or the official or local administrative entity in respect of national and municipal public domain.

8 - Field Interventions: Every archaeological work in a given real property or a given site which includes, by way of example and not limitation, evaluative works and archaeological excavations.

9 - Urban Contexts: Known as Urban Contexts, being the areas that have taken on an urban character such that they have become part of major cities and towns.

10 - Archaeological Supervision Methodology: Known as Archaeological watching Brief, being a working methodology followed when supervising mechanical digging works in real properties or sites in which infrastructure works or construction works are taking place and during which rapid and brief field interventions are carried out in order to ascertain the existence of an archaeological deposit, its nature, and its extents.

11 - Archaeological Finds: Include all antiquities discovered in a given site, whether movable or immovable (finds), within the meaning set forth in Decision 166 L.R. /1933.

12 - The Competent Administrative Authority: The official or local administrative authority concerned with the area in which the field interventions take place (the Governor, the Qaemaqam, the President of the Municipality or the Mukhtar of the locality or others where necessary).

13 - Temporary Archaeological Repositories: Being the repositories located in the regions, the management of which pertains to the heads of sections in the Excavations Unit.

The process of field interventions shall take place in two stages:

First:

1 - Evaluative archaeological works are in principle the first stage of targeted field interventions which evaluate the archaeological reserve in a given site. They consist of the necessary works that lead to determining the nature of the archaeological reserve in the site and include, by way of example and without limitation: desk-based research, monitoring mechanical excavation works with the possibility of rapid intervention to document the archaeological layers, removing modern layers to reach the highest archaeological layers, documenting sections, and carrying out soundings and surveys.

2 - Field archaeological excavations are the second stage of the process of field interventions in urban environments and they include archaeological excavation and documentation in areas with a threatened archaeological reserve, uncovered during construction works or any development works of a real property or of a given site.

Second:

During field excavations, the necessary measures must be taken to salvage the archaeological reserve with the necessary speed and on flexible bases within scientific and methodological frameworks in view of the emergency and urgent nature of the works.

Third:

1 - All excavation works and field interventions in real properties belonging to the category of private property owned by persons of private law shall be funded by the Directorate General of Antiquities.

2 - The owner of the real property concerned with the works mentioned in the sub-paragraph above may offer to the Directorate General of Antiquities to fund them in whole or in part.

3 - Works that take place in national or municipal public property or in the private property of the State or of the municipalities shall be funded by any official entity.

Fourth:

A special computerised system (Data Management System -- DMS) shall be established in which all documents, reports, photographs, maps, drawings, and all types of databases and information relating to all the stages of the archaeological excavations mentioned above (evaluative archaeological works or field archaeological excavations) shall be preserved.

Where it is necessary to restore or conserve any of the archaeological finds, whether movable or immovable, restoration specialists proposed by the archaeologist in charge shall be engaged following the approval of the Director General of Antiquities, provided that detailed reports on such works are submitted and attached to the monthly report mentioned in Article sixteen of this Decree.

Such reports shall include a detailed description of the restoration and/or conservation works carried out and the materials used in these restoration works, accompanied, where necessary, by photographs or drawings showing the condition of the restored antiquities before, during, and after the carrying out of the restoration and/or conservation works thereon.

Restoration works shall be deemed an integral part of the archaeological excavation works, and expenditure thereon shall be covered within the budget of the archaeological works, whether evaluative, preventive or salvage.

All documents, reports, photographs, maps, drawings, and all types of databases and information relating to the restorations and the materials used during them shall be preserved in the special computerised system mentioned in Article three of this Decree.

A blank copy of the databases and the method for encoding the documents shall be given to the scientific director or the archaeologist in charge of any archaeological site to enable him to enter the information resulting from the archaeological excavations.

Recourse shall be had to evaluative archaeological works in any of the following cases:

1 - Upon the Directorate General of Antiquities being notified of the discovery of antiquities in caves or grottoes, or of the discovery thereof during excavation works, whether carried out for agricultural, industrial, constructional, urban development or other purposes, by the excavation contractor, the owner of the real property, or any public or private third party.

2 - Upon one of the public administrations concerned with public constructions and infrastructure submitting its plans to the Directorate General of Antiquities for an opinion thereon during the planning stage.

3 - Upon a legal person governed by public law or private law submitting an application for a permit for urban development constructions in areas of known archaeological potential designated or having been designated by the Directorate General of Antiquities and notified by it to the concerned administrative and local authorities in accordance with the rules.

4 - Upon the Directorate General of Antiquities becoming aware of the presence of antiquities during constructional or urban development works or any other excavation works.

Upon the occurrence of any of the cases provided for in Article Five, the following steps shall be followed in stages or concurrently among such stages:

1 - The Director General of Antiquities shall address a written letter to the owner or the party responsible for the site, by a letter notifying him therein of the obligation to immediately cease conducting any works at the site and the obligation not to make any alteration to its features before the works of assessing the archaeological potential begin under the direct supervision of the Directorate General of Antiquities.

2 - The preliminary inspection and the assessment of the archaeological potential shall be conducted with the necessary speed by the responsible archaeologist in person, who shall submit to the Director General of Antiquities a brief study of the site or the area concerned showing the previous and current archaeological discoveries, their type and the historical periods they cover, in order to determine the method of intervention intended to be implemented by the Directorate General of Antiquities.

3 - The archaeologist referred to in item 2 above shall propose either conducting assessment works or a preventive or rescue archaeological excavation directly.

1 - In the event of a proposal to conduct a preventive or rescue archaeological excavation directly, and after setting forth the justifying reasons therefor (proximity of the site to a previously conducted excavation or its location in an area with a known archaeological reserve...), the working mechanism specific to preventive or rescue archaeological excavations provided for in Chapter Three of this Decree shall be followed.

2 - In the event that it is required to conduct evaluative archaeological works, such works shall be determined (number of test trenches according to the area intended to be exploited and the depth intended to be excavated during construction works...) in order to show the extent and nature of the archaeological reserve in the property, and the following practical steps shall then be followed:

1 - The owner of the property or the entity responsible for the site, the competent Governor, the concerned municipality, and the competent security authorities when necessary shall be notified of the necessity of conducting evaluative archaeological works, and the Director General of Antiquities shall form the team necessary to conduct these works.

b - Whosoever may be the financier of the evaluative archaeological works, and wheresoever they may be conducted, the owner of the property or the entity responsible for the site shall sign the working mechanism set out in Form No. 1 attached to this Decree, which is filled out by the archaeologist in charge, stating therein the number of archaeologists and specialists intended to be engaged, in addition to a preliminary estimate of the costs based on the list of qualifications and rates (Grading) established by the Directorate General of Antiquities and attached to this Decree (Annex No. 2), in addition to the costs of the labour force intended to be engaged and the equipment required to accomplish the mission, which shall be determined at the time (in accordance with the prevailing prices at that time).

c - The owner or the entity responsible for the site shall be granted a period of 15 days from the date of being notified of the working mechanism to submit his comments thereon, and in the event that no comments are received during that period, this shall be deemed as tacit approval.

d - The Directorate General of Antiquities shall examine the comments of the owner, if any, and notify him of its final decision thereon.

e - In the event that the owner rejects the decision of the Directorate General of Antiquities, he shall be prohibited from completing the excavation works in the aforementioned property until the necessary consensual solution is reached.

f - Following the final approval of the owner or the entity responsible for the property to finance the evaluative archaeological works in accordance with the methodology proposed in Paragraph - b - of this Article, he shall sign the form adopted for this approval (Form \No. 3 attached hereto), which includes his explicit approval to finance the evaluative archaeological works. The Director General of Antiquities shall appoint a team working under the supervision of the archaeologist in charge, after examining the curriculum vitae of each of the members of this team.

g - The owner of the property or the entity responsible for the site and the competent administrative authority shall be notified of the commencement of the evaluative archaeological works through the applicable administrative channels.

The site coordinator, in coordination with the archaeologist in charge or the scientific director, shall draw up every fifteen days a schedule signed by the owner's representative, the archaeologist in charge, and the site coordinator or the scientific director, showing the names of the members of the archaeological team whose services were engaged from outside the Directorate General of Antiquities, their job description, the period of their work, and the wages due. These records shall be submitted to the owner or the entity responsible for the site and shall be paid within a maximum period of two weeks from the date of notification thereof. Where this time limit expires without payment having been made, the Director General of Antiquities may suspend all works within the property.

As for works carried out in coordination between the Directorate General of Antiquities and the Council for Development and Reconstruction, financial matters shall be agreed upon by the appropriate means between the two parties.

The site coordinator and the designated team shall carry out the evaluative archaeological works according to the prepared plan, and he shall submit his report to the archaeologist in charge periodically (monthly), including photographs and sections relating to the excavation in addition to a general evaluation explaining the progress of the work and the most prominent finds, and attaching thereto the attendance schedule of the archaeologists and antiquarians. This report shall be submitted to the Director General of Antiquities by the archaeologist in charge for the necessary action to be taken.

The archaeologist in charge shall submit a final report upon the completion of the evaluative works including drawings, sections, and photographs in addition to the reports of the specialists concerned with the finds, if any, within a maximum period of one month from the completion of the works, taking into consideration the volume of the works (number of soundings, areas covered by the works, ...) that have been executed. The report shall conclude with clear findings determining the manner and nature of the intervention, or the absence thereof, in the subsequent stage, through:

1 - Allowing the owner of the property to commence excavation and construction works, or to complete them, without any scientific supervision or field intervention where there are no archaeological features in the property.

2 - Allowing the owner of the property to commence excavation and construction works, or to complete them, under archaeological supervision, whereby the methodology of archaeological supervision (Watching Brief) shall be followed, where there is a possibility of the presence of scattered archaeological remains in the specified property or site.

3 - Requesting that full archaeological excavations be conducted where there is an archaeological reserve of importance, which necessitates following the methodology of preventive or rescue archaeological excavations provided for in Chapter Three of this Decree.

The owner of the property or the entity responsible for the site and the competent administrative authority shall be notified of the decision taken in accordance with the provisions of Article Ten, in its three paragraphs, through the applicable administrative channels.

In the event of adopting the second solution mentioned in Article Nine, namely permitting the commencement or completion of excavation works by following the archaeological supervision methodology, the following steps shall be followed:

1 - The Director General of Antiquities shall appoint one of the archaeologists of the Administration or one of the archaeologists from outside the Administration along with an assisting team for him, after reviewing his curriculum vitae and that of each of the members of the team working with him where necessary, to undertake the monitoring of the excavation works (by means of workers and/or machinery) and carry out the necessary documentation or even halt these works in order to conduct rapid archaeological excavations if the matter so requires.

2 - The appointed archaeologist shall carry out the supervision works and submit the necessary periodic reports containing photographs and drawings - in the event of the presence or absence of archaeological deposits - and shall submit therewith the attendance sheet to the archaeologist in charge at the Directorate General of Antiquities, provided that the latter shall decide, according to the findings, whether the ongoing works do not require the execution of a preventive or salvage archaeological excavation or whether the discovered deposits necessitate converting the property or the site or a part of either of them into a preventive or salvage archaeological excavation in order to conduct the necessary archaeological excavations therein.

3 - Upon the completion of the archaeological supervision works, the owner or the entity responsible for the site and the competent administrative authority shall be notified of the summary of the archaeological works on the site through the applicable administrative channels, as follows:

a - In the event that the archaeological supervision works show the absence of archaeological deposits or the presence of limited archaeological deposits that were dealt with in accordance with scientific standards during the supervision works, the owner of the property or the entity responsible for the site shall be permitted to complete the excavation, shoring and construction works on the property or the site.

b - In the event that it is necessary to convert the property or the site or a part thereof into a preventive or salvage archaeological excavation in order to conduct the necessary archaeological excavations therein, the owner of the property or the entity responsible for the site and the competent administrative authority shall be notified thereof, and the articles of Chapter Three of this Decree shall then be applied.

Upon ascertaining the presence of an archaeological stock in a specific site and after conducting the preliminary inspection or the evaluative archaeological works, the archaeologist in charge shall submit the mechanism of archaeological work to the Director General of Antiquities for approval, and it shall thereafter be sent to the owner of the real property or the entity responsible for the site to notify of the current situation and the necessity of conducting preventive or salvage archaeological excavations at the site.

The following practical steps shall then be followed:

1 - The owner of the real property or the entity responsible for the site, the competent Governor, and the concerned municipality shall be notified of the necessity of conducting urban archaeological excavations, and the Director General of Antiquities shall form the team necessary to conduct these works.

2 - Whoever the financier of the preventive and salvage archaeological excavation works may be, and wherever the place of their execution may be, the owner of the real property or the entity responsible for the site shall sign the mechanism of work set out in Form No. 4 attached to this Decree, which shall be filled out by the archaeologist in charge, stating therein the number of archaeologists and specialists intended to be engaged, in addition to a preliminary estimate of the costs based on the schedule of qualifications and rates (Grading) established by the Directorate General of Antiquities, as well as the workforce intended to be engaged and the equipment required to accomplish the mission.

3 - The owner shall be granted a time limit of 15 days from the date of being notified of the mechanism of work to submit his observations thereon, and in the event that he does not submit any observations during that paragraph, this shall be deemed as tacit approval.

4 - The Directorate General of Antiquities shall examine the observations of the owner, where they exist, and shall notify him of its final decision regarding them.

5 - In the event that the owner rejects the decision of the Directorate General of Antiquities, he shall be prohibited from completing the excavation works in the aforementioned real property until the necessary consensual solution is reached.

6 - Following the final approval of the owner or the entity responsible for the real property to finance the works in accordance with the methodology proposed in the second paragraph of this Article, he shall sign the approval form (Form No. 5 attached hereto) which includes his explicit approval to finance the preventive or salvage archaeological excavations. The Director General of Antiquities shall appoint a team working under the supervision of the archaeologist in charge after examining the curriculum vitae pertaining to each of the members of this team, and shall also proceed to appoint a site coordinator or a scientific entity to work under the supervision of this archaeologist in charge.

7 - The site coordinator or the scientific director, together with his work team, under the supervision of the archaeologist in charge, shall prepare for the phase of archaeological excavations, which includes securing all the logistical requirements necessary for the proper conduct of the works and preparing the site for the archaeological excavations, in addition to completing the securing of human resources of specialized archaeologists, surveyors, and workers...

8 - Upon the readiness of the site for archaeological excavation, the archaeologist in charge shall notify the Director General of Antiquities in writing of the commencement of the preventive or salvage archaeological excavations, provided that the excavation works are executed within the time limit specified in the current mechanism of work. This archaeologist shall be the scientific director of the archaeological excavation in the event that he holds a doctorate degree in archaeology, and in the event that he does not hold the aforementioned degree, the Director General of Antiquities shall then appoint a scientific director according to the requirements and the scientific nature of the site.

9 - The owner of the real property or the entity responsible for the site and the competent administrative authority shall be notified of the commencement of the archaeological excavation works through the applicable administrative channels.

1 . None of the immovable archaeological discoveries at the site may be dismantled, during the conduct of the archaeological works or after their completion, except by a prior decision of the Director General of Antiquities based on a reasoned and documented report by the Archaeologist in Charge or the Scientific Director showing the nature of the discoveries, their importance, and the historical period to which they date back, in addition to the intervention methodology and the entity proposed to carry out the works.

2 . It shall be for the Director General of Antiquities to decide the fate of these discoveries requested to be dismantled in accordance with the provisions of Article Eighteen of this Decree, after reviewing the findings of the report mentioned in Paragraph 1 of this Article and in the light of the resolutions and recommendations of UNESCO relating to this matter. The Director General may also seek the guidance of a specialised scientific opinion if necessary.

3 . Where the immovable archaeological discoveries are of great importance, the decision as to their fate shall rest with the Minister of Culture upon the proposal of the Director General of Antiquities.

Movable archaeological discoveries and dismantled immovable archaeological discoveries shall be placed in the storehouses of the excavations site where their treatment, study and documentation shall begin, and their management and control shall rest with the Scientific Director or the Site Coordinator in coordination with the Archaeologist in Charge and the Head of the Excavations Unit; and the Movable Archaeological Property Unit shall be notified in accordance with the administrative hierarchy in force.

The archaeological discoveries shall be transferred from the excavations site to the temporary storehouses in the area in which the excavations took place according to the programme of the Scientific Director or the Site Coordinator and in coordination with the Archaeologist in Charge, where their treatment, study and documentation shall be completed, accompanied by a transfer permit signed by the Director General of Antiquities showing the name of the Archaeologist in Charge, the origin of the finds, and the entity to which they are sent, in addition to the means of transport. (A copy of the registration papers of the motor vehicle and the driver's driving licence shall be attached).

The archaeological discoveries shall be accompanied by the Archaeologist in Charge or the Scientific Director, and shall be delivered to the Archaeologist in Charge and the archaeologist assigned to manage the temporary storehouses of the Directorate General of Antiquities in the area in which the excavations are taking place, both of whom shall sign a receipt record in accordance with the attached list.

No archaeologist (in the event that he holds a doctorate degree in archaeology) shall have the right to be a scientific director for more than two archaeological excavations at the same time, unless the Director General of Antiquities deems otherwise in accordance with the requirements of the work and the public interest.

The site coordinator shall draw up, in coordination with the archaeologist in charge or the scientific director every fifteen days, a schedule signed by the representative of the owner, the archaeologist in charge, and the site coordinator or the scientific director, indicating therein the names of the members of the archaeological team whose services were enlisted from outside the Directorate General of Antiquities, their job description, their period of work, and the wages incurred. These records shall be submitted to the owner or the entity responsible for the site and shall be paid within a maximum period of two weeks from the date of notification thereof. In the event of the expiry of this time limit without payment being made, the Director General of Antiquities may suspend all works within the property.

As for the works carried out in coordination between the Directorate General of Antiquities and the Council for Development and Reconstruction, agreement regarding financial matters shall be reached by appropriate means between the two parties.

The archaeologist in charge shall submit a periodic (monthly) report to the Director General of Antiquities on the progress of the works, accompanied by photographs showing the most prominent movable and immovable discoveries with a clear explanation of the nature of these discoveries, and shall attach thereto the daily attendance schedules of the work team during the past month.

In the event that the archaeological excavations are carried out in stages, the archaeologist in charge or the scientific director shall submit a detailed and documented report upon the completion of each stage, and shall also notify the administration in writing of the commencement of the works in the subsequent stage.

Upon the completion of the archaeological excavations, the responsible archaeologist or the scientific director shall submit a report to the Director General of Antiquities notifying him of the completion of the archaeological field works, and shall prepare a list indicating the nature and quantity of the remaining basic works to be carried out, whether at the level of documentation and the archaeological report or at the level of packing and treating samples and finds:

1 - In the event that no archaeological stock remains at the site, the Director General of Antiquities shall send a letter to the owner notifying him of the completion of the archaeological works and the possibility of resuming the excavation, shoring and construction works at the site.

2 - In the event of the presence of immovable archaeological discoveries remaining in situ, a preliminary report must be submitted by the responsible archaeologist or the scientific director evaluating these discoveries together with a proposal for their fate, indicating their importance and justifying his proposal, as a preliminary step to enable the Director General of Antiquities to take the appropriate decision regarding them, and attaching thereto all the necessary documents (sections, descriptions, photographs and specialised reports).

3 - In principle, the Administration shall not disclose these documents to anyone except in cases of necessity, in which case it shall notify the holder of the scientific rights, whether the latter is the responsible archaeologist or the scientific director, and the rights of the latter shall be reserved throughout the period during which he has the right to study and publish, as specified in Article 21 of Chapter Four of this Decree.

1 - The Director General of Antiquities, in coordination with the Scientific Director and/or the Responsible Archaeologist, shall specify a time limit of one year or two years to complete the works necessary to finish the study of the archaeological discoveries from a given site and issue their preliminary scientific reports thereon.

2 - The Scientific Director and/or the Responsible Archaeologist and the working team assisting him at the site shall have their full scientific rights to study and publish the results of their archaeological discoveries definitively within a period ranging between two years and six years, subject to the approval of the Director General of Antiquities based on the size of the site and the quantity of documents and finds resulting from the archaeological works, in addition to the extent of availability of sufficient human resources to study the finds and the necessary funding to complete the studies.

3 - These time limits may be extended once for a reasonable period not exceeding half of the original time limit upon a reasoned written request from the Responsible Archaeologist and/or the Scientific Director, and the Director General of Antiquities shall decide on this matter. Upon the expiry of the two time limits specified above without a positive result, the Director General of Antiquities shall have the right to intervene to decide the fate of the Second Party's publication rights.

4 - In this respect, the cooperation frameworks provided for in the Memorandum of Understanding signed between the Ministry of Culture and the Lebanese University may be applied.

5 - Publication shall take place in a specialised scientific journal issued by the Ministry of Culture, currently bearing the name "BAAL", whether in the regular annual issues or in special issues compiling the results of preventive or rescue excavations. Publication may also take place in any other scientific journal recognised in the Lebanese State after the lapse of two years from the deposit of the reports ready for publication with the journal issued by the Ministry of Culture.

This Decree shall apply immediately upon its entry into force to all ongoing and completed field interventions that have not yet been studied and published. The Responsible Archaeologist shall be granted a period not exceeding two months for each site in which excavations have been completed in order to assess the current condition of the finds and documents pertaining to each site. In this case, the provisions of Article /21/ of this Decree shall apply.
This Decree shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

On the basis of the data submitted by the archaeologist in charge or the scientific director, the Director General of Antiquities shall propose the appropriate solution regarding the archaeological discoveries to the Minister of Culture based on the resolutions and recommendations of UNESCO and in accordance with the following:

1 - Dismantling the archaeological discoveries completely after completing their excavation by the appropriate scientific methods and documenting them in full (Preservation by records).

2 - And reintegrating the archaeological discoveries wholly or partially into the new building (Reintegration).

3 - Keeping the archaeological discoveries in place and integrating them into the new building (In situ integration) without exposing them to any destructive factors and without moving them, tampering with them, or placing them in a condition that affects their preservation and their protection during the execution of the construction works on the property or thereafter, upon the completion of the construction works and the occupancy of the project/building according to the intended purpose thereof.

4 - Preserving the entirety of the archaeological discoveries in place inasmuch as the site is of major importance, with the necessity of proposing expropriation in accordance with the laws in force (Expropriation).

One or more of the aforementioned solutions shall be adopted by a decision issued by the Minister of Culture upon a proposal by the Director General of Antiquities, and this decision shall be notified to the owner of the property or the entity responsible for the site and the competent administrative authorities.

The working mechanism set forth in the articles of this Decree shall be adopted with respect to immovable antiquities discovered in urban perimeters which are decided to be integrated or reintegrated into private and public civil buildings and installations. These discoveries constitute, in principle, an importance at the historical, heritage and archaeological levels, and their integration or reintegration into the place of their discovery provides a public interest, particularly in terms of preserving the "memory of the place" on the one hand, and on the other hand consolidating the links between the inhabitants and the material culture related to their history, antiquities and heritage, given the benefit thereof at the level of strengthening the cultural identity of society as a whole and by allowing them to increase the sites of these antiquities and view them in accordance with what is specified in the body of this Decree.

Upon agreement on all details relating to the manner and method of constructing the building as well as the method of integrating or re-integrating the antiquities discovered therein, the owner must sign before the Notary Public the undertaking provided for in Article Nine of this Decree; however, in the event that the owner refuses to sign this undertaking, he shall be prohibited from building due to the impossibility for him at that time to obtain the approval of the Directorate General of Antiquities for the building, and the provisions of Articles /1/ to /7/ and Article /18/ of Decision 166/L.R. shall then apply.

A plaque shall be placed at the entrance of the building in a visible place containing scientific information about the discovered antiquities and indicating the integration or re-integration project being executed.

1 - The works of construction and integration or re-integration (after dismantling) on the site of the property shall be commenced after completing all the procedures provided for above in the preceding articles as well as the articles provided for in Chapters Two and Three of this Decree allocated to each of those works.

2 - The aforementioned works shall be carried out under the direct supervision of the Directorate General of Antiquities to verify the proper conduct of these works from their beginning until their completion in all matters relating to the antiquities.

3 - The works shall be stopped immediately by a decision of the Minister of Culture upon the proposal of the Director General of Antiquities in the event that the Directorate General of Antiquities observes any violation in the execution of the building permit or any damage to the discovered antiquities, after sending a formal notice to the owner and his abstention from executing its content.

The owner shall sign an undertaking (Form No. 1 attached hereto) before the Notary Public containing the following:

1 - His explicit and unambiguous approval of the operation of integrating the antiquities discovered on his property or dismantling them for their re-integration therein in accordance with the plans and documents of the file kept at the Directorate General of Antiquities under a specified number and date.

2 - His explicit and final waiver of claiming any financial compensation in return for the limitation by the integration or re-integration operation of his right to exercise his full ownership over his property.

3 - His approval that all expenses of financing the integration or re-integration operation shall be borne by him alone, with his explicit waiver of his right to claim from the Ministry of Culture any compensation for this operation.

4 - His approval of the conditions of management of the part of the building constructed on his property as provided for in Article Ten of this Decree.

5 - His approval of registering an annotation of this undertaking on the Real Property Folio of the property as well as the undertaking to insert the provisions of Article Ten of this Decree into the co-ownership regulations of the property.

Pursuant to Article /19/ of Decree No. 3057 dated 12/3/2016 (regulating the mechanism of archaeological field interventions carried out by the Directorate General of Antiquities in the field of preventive and rescue excavations), the archaeologist in charge or the scientific director shall prepare a detailed report on the antiquities discovered in a given property or site and submit it to the Director General of Antiquities, explaining therein the importance of the discoveries and the reasons necessitating their retention in situ, together with a proposal for integration or reintegration. The said scientific report shall be submitted within a period not exceeding one month after the completion of the archaeological excavation works.

The Minister of Culture shall decide, in accordance with the proposal of the Director General of Antiquities and on the basis of the said report, to retain all of the discovered immovable antiquities in situ, or to integrate them or reintegrate them into the building intended to be constructed on the property or site, on the basis of the resolutions and recommendations of UNESCO in this regard.

The owner of the property shall be notified in accordance with the legal procedures of the decision of the Minister of Culture to integrate the discovered antiquities or to dismantle them for their reintegration. The owner of the property shall also be required to amend the executive and architectural plans of the building intended to be constructed which provides for the integration or reintegration of the antiquities therein in the manner proposed by the Ministry of Culture - Directorate General of Antiquities, while preserving as much as possible the general orientation of the urban layout of the discoveries.

The Minister of Culture shall request, on the proposal of the Director General of Antiquities, the issuance of a registration decree for the discoveries intended to be integrated pursuant to the provisions of Article /26/ et seq. of Decision No. 166/L.R. dated 7/11/1933 and its amendments (Regulations on Ancient Antiquities), or the issuance of a decree of permanent loan for the antiquities intended to be dismantled and reintegrated pursuant to the aforementioned Decision 166/L.R.

A detailed file shall be prepared, drawn up by specialists in integration or reintegration works (archaeologists, restoration engineers and restorers specialised in archaeological finds) numbering between three and seven specialists, who shall be designated by mutual agreement between the Directorate General of Antiquities and the owner or by way of a call for tenders, containing the manner of carrying out the works of restoration, conservation and integration or dismantling and reintegration of the archaeological discoveries in the building intended to be constructed, for the purpose of examining it and obtaining prior technical approval thereof from the Directorate General of Antiquities.

The following terms shall be adopted for the application of the provisions of this Decree:

1 - Scientific Director: The person scientifically and practically responsible for an archaeological excavation and for all scientific archaeological studies relating thereto. If he is from outside the Directorate, he must hold a doctorate degree in archaeology and have 3 years of experience in archaeological excavations with scientific publications; the Scientific Director shall be required to select the archaeologists and experts with whom he wishes to work, and he shall bear the responsibility for conducting all necessary studies for the excavations that he directs, in addition to publishing them by known and recognised scientific methods.

2 - Responsible Archaeologist: The archaeologist who is an employee of or contracted with the Directorate General of Antiquities and who is assigned by the Director General of Antiquities to the tasks of supervising a specific archaeological excavation or archaeological excavations in general or the departments in the regions, holding a master's degree in archaeology or having a seniority exceeding five years within the Directorate General of Antiquities.

3 - Archaeologist: Any person from outside the cadre of the Directorate General of Antiquities holding a university degree in archaeology issued by a recognised university or technical institute, whose assistance is enlisted by the said Directorate or the competent scientific body in order to carry out specific archaeological works.

4 - Restorer Engineer: An architectural or structural engineer specialised in the restoration and conservation of monuments and historical sites, having not less than three years of experience during which he has carried out assignments, including two archaeological excavations similar in nature to the excavation in which he has been selected to work, as well as shoring, restoration, and dismantling works.

5 - Real Property: The real property located in a specific cadastral area and which contains the discovered antiquities.

6 - Building: The building constructed or intended to be constructed on the real property and in which the discovered antiquities are integrated or reintegrated.

7 - Owner: The entity owning the real property and/or the association of owners of common parts and/or all owners of subdivided stories, whether residential apartments or commercial or industrial offices and others... or whoever legally represents them.

8 - Entity Responsible for the Real Property: The Owner or the official or local administrative entity with respect to national and municipal public domain properties.

9 - Urban Environs: Known as Urban Contexts, being the areas that have acquired an urban character such that they have become part of major cities and towns.

10 - Archaeological Discoveries: Include all antiquities discovered at a given site, whether movable or immovable (finds), within the meaning set forth in Decision 166 L.R./ 1933.

11 - Competent Administrative Authority: The official or local administrative authority concerned with the area in which the field interventions take place (the Governor, the District Commissioner (Qaemaqam), the President of the Municipality, the Mukhtar of the locality, or others where necessary).

The following matters shall be the sole responsibility of the owner:

1 - Bearing the damages that may result from the theft, loss, destruction, breakage or disfigurement of any of the discovered or existing antiquities.

2 - Executing the following works and bearing the costs thereof:

a - Maintaining and restoring all integrated or re-integrated antiquities through specialists in restoration and antiquities chosen in agreement with the Directorate General of Antiquities or by way of a call for tenders on a periodic basis (annually) in accordance with a book of specifications drawn up by the specialised scientific body approved by the Directorate General of Antiquities.

b - Insuring and reinsuring all integrated or re-integrated antiquities in accordance with the internationally adopted standards in this field (Form No. 2 attached hereto).

c - Providing security protection for the building and for the antiquities integrated or re-integrated therein by the owner or by a private company concerned with such matters, through the presence of one or more security personnel 24/24 hours.

d - Providing a special entrance for the integrated or re-integrated antiquities separate from the entrance of the building to allow visitors to view the existing antiquities, and opening this part on a periodic basis with the specification of the days and hours.

e - Providing the required infrastructure (water, electricity, etc...) for the integrated antiquities.

f - Placing a sign or plaque in a visible place at the entrance of the constructed building in accordance with a model established by the Directorate General of Antiquities, clearly containing brief historical and scientific information on the antiquities present at the site and specifying the visiting hours for the public, which shall be free of charge.

Integration means the process of keeping immovable antiquities in the place of their discovery within a property or site during archaeological excavation works pursuant to Article /19/ of Decree No. ... dated .... (Regulating the Mechanism of Archaeological Field Interventions Carried Out by the Directorate General of Antiquities in the Field of Preventive and Rescue Excavations), with the express and written consent of the owner thereof.

The provisions of this Chapter shall apply in particular to integration operations in addition to the general provisions provided for in Chapter One of this Decree.

The owner of the property or the entity responsible for the site shall, prior to commencing the construction and integration works, and after obtaining the written approval of the Directorate General of Antiquities, allocate an area within the discoveries intended to be integrated into the site or near the area allocated for the integrated antiquities to serve as a permanent exhibition in which panels or any explanatory audiovisual materials concerning the discoveries and their geographical and historical surroundings shall be placed, in addition to a model or a three-dimensional diagram of the site, if made available by the archaeologist in charge or the scientific director, showing the relationship of the site to its urban, historical and archaeological surroundings.

The construction and integration works at the site shall not be commenced except after the issuance of the building permit by the competent authorities concerned, including the required amendments approved by the Ministry of Culture - Directorate General of Antiquities, and after verifying that the discoveries will be in public places of the property which the general public may enter and frequent.

The Directorate General of Antiquities shall directly supervise the proper progress of the works from their commencement until their completion in all matters relating to the antiquities.

Such antiquities shall not be moved, tampered with or placed in a condition that affects their preservation and protection during the execution of the construction works on the property or thereafter, upon the completion of the construction works and the occupancy of the project/building in accordance with its intended purpose.

Re-integration means the process of dismantling and reassembling immovable antiquities discovered on a given property or site during archaeological excavation works pursuant to Article /19/ of Decree No. ... dated .... (Regulating the Mechanism of Archaeological Field Interventions Undertaken by the Directorate General of Antiquities in the Field of Preventive and Salvage Excavations).

The provisions of this Chapter shall apply specifically to re-integration operations, in addition to the general provisions stipulated in Chapter One of this Decree.

The owner of the property or the entity responsible for the site shall, prior to commencing the dismantling process, and after obtaining the written approval of the Directorate General of Antiquities, allocate an area within or near the area allocated for the elements integrated in accordance with their original plan, while preserving as far as possible the orientation of the surfaces, to serve as a permanent exhibition in which panels or any explanatory audiovisual means concerning the discoveries and their geographical and historical surroundings shall be placed, in addition to a model or a three-dimensional diagram of the site, if made available by the archaeologist in charge or the scientific director, showing the relationship of the site to its urban, historical and archaeological surroundings.

The dismantling operation shall not commence except after the availability of the following elements:

1 . The written approval of the Director General of Antiquities of the dismantling programme proposed by the restoration architect in accordance with the directives of the archaeologist in charge or the scientific director, provided that this programme includes, in particular, the following: the timetable, the dismantling technique and the loading and transport of the parts, the type of labels adopted, the method of storage, the protection factors,...

2 . The issuance of the building permit by the competent authorities containing the required amendments approved by the Directorate General of Antiquities. This shall be after the Directorate General of Antiquities notifies the competent authorities in writing of its decision approving the dismantling and reintegration.

The scientific director or the archaeologist in charge of the archaeological mission that carried out the archaeological excavations and discoveries in the real property or the site in which the antiquities are to be dismantled and reintegrated shall draw up a detailed report on the outcome of the dismantling of the archaeological finds concerned, the methodology followed in dismantling them, the place of their deposit, and all explanatory information relating thereto, such as the site, the guards, and the duration of the availability of this site for this purpose, within a period not exceeding one month from the date of completion of the dismantling operation, provided that it is submitted to the Director General of Antiquities.

The owner of the real property or the entity responsible for the site - in the event that the Directorate General of Antiquities is unable to do so - shall secure a temporary and safe site at his own expense for the transfer of the archaeological finds that will be dismantled in preparation for their reassembly in the project after the completion of the construction works.

Upon the completion of all the dismantling works and the archaeological works in the real property, the owner of the real property or the entity responsible for the site shall have the right to complete the excavation, shoring and construction works therein after the written approval of the Director General of Antiquities.

The reintegration works shall be commenced in accordance with a timetable determined by agreement between the owner and the Directorate General of Antiquities through a detailed programme containing the conditions for the execution of the works with which the restoration architect must comply under the supervision of the archaeologist in charge or the scientific director. In the event of the necessity of making any amendments to the executive drawings concerned with the reintegration, these amendments shall be submitted to the Director General of Antiquities in order to obtain his written approval thereof.

1 . Immediately upon the completion of the reintegration operation, a permanent loan decree shall be issued for the antiquities intended to be reintegrated into the building and shall be notified to the owner of the real property or the entity responsible for the site in accordance with the rules.

2 . The permanent loan decree shall determine the responsibilities and conditions that the owner must bear with regard to the antiquities reintegrated into his real property, in addition to his bearing responsibility for the theft, loss, smashing, or breaking of any of the existing pieces, as provided for in the tenth article above of this Decree.

3 . The discoveries that are the subject of this integration shall be entered into a special list with the Archaeological and Heritage Installations Unit, whereby this unit shall carry out periodic inspections of the site (at least once a year).

The scientific director or the archaeologist in charge of the aforementioned archaeological mission shall draw up a detailed report on the outcome of the operation of reintegrating the archaeological discoveries concerned within the urban development project in the real property and all explanatory information related thereto, within a time limit not exceeding one month from the date of completion of the integration operation, which shall be submitted to the Director General of Antiquities.

This Decree shall apply immediately upon its entry into force to all completed integration and reintegration projects, those in which the works have not been completed, and also future ones. The archaeologist in charge or the scientific director shall be granted a period not exceeding two months for each site in which the integration or reintegration works have been completed in order to prepare the necessary documents and records provided for in the body of this Decree, and a time limit of one year to submit an article or a final report on the restoration and integration or reintegration works after their completion.

Publication shall take place in a specialised scientific journal issued by the Ministry of Culture, currently bearing the name "BAAL", whether in the regular annual issues or in special issues compiling the results of preventive or rescue excavations. Publication may also take place in any other scientific journal recognised in the Lebanese State after the lapse of two years from the deposit of the reports ready for publication with the journal issued by the Ministry of Culture.
This Decree shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

For the purposes of this Decree, the expressions listed below shall have the following meanings:

- The Ministry: The Ministry of Youth and Sports.

- The Minister: The Minister of Youth and Sports.

- The Directorate General: The Directorate General of Youth and Sports.

- The Director General: The Director General of Youth and Sports.

- The Olympic Committee: The Lebanese Olympic Committee.

- Bodies: The associations and federations operating in the fields of sports, youth and scouting, licensed by the Ministry of Youth and Sports, and specified in Article Three of this Decree.

- The Association: It is the sports, youth or scouting "Club" /or/ "Association", defined as a group of individuals bound together by national, educational, cultural, social, developmental, intellectual, recreational, health and/or sports objectives for able-bodied persons and persons with special needs without discrimination on the basis of origin, colour, creed or sex, and which exercises its activities in accordance with its general bylaws, the laws and regulations in force, and the bylaws of its national federation, in a manner that does not conflict with international regulations.

- Institutions: Public and private institutions and commercial companies.

- Educational Institution: Schools and universities.

- General Bylaws: The bylaws adopted for each body.

The Ministry shall be concerned with the affairs of sports, scouting and youth, their bodies and all activities related thereto in the developmental, cultural, moral, civic, social and recreational fields, the preparatory stages for building up the youth in terms of sports and physical fitness, licensing the establishment thereof and verifying that they fulfil the conditions in accordance with the laws and decrees in force.

Sports, scout, and youth bodies shall be divided into:

First: Sports bodies.

1 . Sports associations.

2 . Sports federations.

3 . Sports associations for persons with special needs.

4 . The Lebanese Paralympic Committee.

5 . Popular clubs.

6 . The Lebanese Federation for Sport for All.

7 . Traditional and heritage sports associations and their federation.

Second: Scout bodies:

8 . Scout associations (males and females).

9 . The Lebanese Scout Federation.

10 . Girl Guides and Girl Scouts associations (females).

11 . The Lebanese Federation of Girl Guides and Girl Scouts.

Third: Youth bodies:

12 . Children and youth summer camp associations and their federation.

13 . Voluntary work associations and their federation.

14 . Scientific activities associations and their federation.

15 . Youth hostels associations and their federation.

16 . Folkloric activities associations and their federation.

- Employees (permanent - contracted - wage earners) in the Ministry of Youth and Sports may not be founding members or members of the administrative boards of the bodies specified in Article Three of this Decree.

1 . Each body shall have its own designation, and names, badges, and activities that are inconsistent with public order or that are liable to stir up sensitivities shall be prohibited.

2 . The right to use the following shall be restricted to the Lebanese Olympic Committee, the administrations affiliated with it, and the members and employees authorised to do so:

- The international Olympic emblem, torch, and badge composed of the five rings and their words regardless of their order.

- The Lebanese Olympic emblem, torch, and badge composed of the Lebanese flag and the five interlaced rings.

- The words: Olympic (masculine) - Olympic (feminine) - Olympiad and their derivatives in any language whatsoever.

- Natural and legal persons within Lebanese territory shall be prohibited from using the foregoing for commercial, artistic, or sports purposes, or for any other purpose, except with the approval of the Lebanese Olympic Committee.

3 . The right to use the following shall be restricted to the Lebanese Scout Federation and the scout associations affiliated with it and belonging to it:

- The emblem of the Lebanese Scout Federation.

- The emblem of the World Scout Movement.

4 . The right to use the emblem and badge established by the Lebanese Youth Hostels Federation hostelling international, and the words "بيوت الشباب" (Youth Hostels) and "الاتحاد اللبناني لبيوت الشباب" (Lebanese Youth Hostels Federation) and {Auberge de Jeunesse} and {Youth Hostels}, shall be restricted to the Lebanese Youth Hostels Federation, the associations joined to it, and the authorised members and employees.

Sports, scout and youth bodies shall keep the following registers:

- The register of minutes of the General Assembly sessions.

- The register of members of the General Assembly.

- The register of minutes of the Administrative Board.

- The register of the Treasury.

- The register of activities, the schedule and results of official competitions, and the annual calendar.

- The register of outgoing and incoming correspondence, circulars and decisions.

These registers may be organised through administrative information technology means (on the computer), provided that the Secretariat holds a paper copy thereof, signed and certified in due form.

Sessions of the General Assembly in bodies shall be divided into two types, which are:

A. An ordinary session, which is the annual session dedicated to approving the administrative and financial reports for the past year, the budget for the coming year, and any other matters.

B. An extraordinary session held on an urgent basis when necessary.

- Unless this conflicts with the regulations of international federations, the quorum for sessions of the General Assembly of members fulfilling the legal requirements shall be as follows:

A. In the annual ordinary sessions of the General Assembly, the quorum for the first session shall be more than half, and the quorum for the second session shall be constituted by those in attendance.

B. In the sessions of the General Assembly dedicated to amending the bylaws, the quorum for the first session shall be two-thirds, the quorum for the second session shall be more than half, and the quorum for the third session shall be one-third; and if the quorum cannot be reached, the amendments shall lapse.

C. In the remaining sessions of the General Assembly, including election sessions, the quorum for the first session shall be two-thirds, the quorum for the second session shall be more than half, and the quorum for the third session shall be constituted by those in attendance.

- If the number of candidates exceeds half the total number of the Administrative Board, the elections shall be held on time with their candidates, and the elected Administrative Board shall then determine in its first session a date to hold by-elections, taking into account new legal time limits for candidacy and election.

- If the number of candidates is complete upon the closing of candidacy, and some of them subsequently withdraw before the date of the election session such that the number of remaining candidates is more than half the number of seats, the electoral process shall be completed, provided that by-elections are held subsequently to fill the vacant positions, taking into account new legal time limits for candidacy and election.

- If the number of candidates is equal to the number of members of the Administrative Board, the General Assembly shall convene in a single session provided that the legal quorum is met, and it shall be deemed elected by acclamation.
