- Members of the General Assembly of any body shall be obliged to remain from the beginning of the session until its end, and the quorum shall be deemed non-existent if it is lost during the session.

- Two-thirds of the General Assembly shall have the right to propose a vote of confidence in the Administrative Board of the body, and to call for an extraordinary session to be held for this purpose if the Administrative Board fails to fulfil its duty to issue the call in due form within a period of one month from the lodging of the proposal with it.

- The Administrative Board shall fall if an absolute majority (half plus one) of the number of members of the General Assembly present and fulfilling the legal requirements votes in favour thereof.
Upon the dissolution of the bodies covered by this Decree, their movable and immovable assets shall be distributed in accordance with the provisions of their general by-laws.

Official certificates relating to the bodies covered by this Decree shall be issued upon their request by the Ministry - the Directorate General, which shall base the issuance of such certificates on the minutes of the General Assembly meeting and the minutes of the Administrative Committee meeting held for the distribution of offices.

A - The establishment of associations shall be subject to the following conditions:

- The number of founding members shall not be less than seven in respect of sports and youth associations, and seven in respect of scout associations.

- The term of office of the founding committee shall not exceed two years from the date of issuance of the licensing decision.

- The association shall have general by-laws and their provisions shall be consistent with this Decree, the regulations in force, and public policy.

B - The general by-laws of the association shall include provisions relating to the following matters:

- The name, purpose, and headquarters of the association.

- The conditions for the admission, resignation, and expulsion of members.

- The powers of the General Assembly and the rules governing its meetings.

- The number of members of the Administrative Committee, its powers, its term of office, and the duties of its members.

- The manner and conditions for electing the members of the Administrative Committee, distributing offices among them, and forfeiting their membership.

- The assets of the association, the manner of their investment and disposal, and their devolution in the event of the dissolution of the association.

- The conditions for amending the general by-laws of the association and for its dissolution.

The Ministry shall receive licence applications, and shall, within a period of one month at most, verify that they fulfil the administrative and technical conditions, and then refer them to the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities, which shall express an opinion thereon while stating the reasons in the event of non-approval, within a period of two months at most. The Ministry must issue the licensing decision immediately upon the expiry of this period, failing which its silence shall be deemed a tacit decision of approval.

- The licensing decision shall be published in the Official Gazette at the expense of the founders within a maximum period of three months from the date of obtaining the licence, failing which the licence shall be deemed null and void.

Associations must fulfil the technical conditions - each according to its licence - which are issued by regulatory decisions of the Minister upon the proposal of the Director General in accordance with the technical conditions adopted by international federations, namely:

- The technical and special conditions relating to centres, courts, fields,

swimming pools, technical equipment and other technologies pertaining to sports associations, in accordance with the adopted regulations.

- The technical and special conditions, installations and technologies pertaining to sports associations for persons with special needs.

- The technical and special conditions for centres, technical equipment and other technologies pertaining to scout associations, in accordance with the adopted regulations.

- The technical and special conditions for activities, centres, the places designated for holding them and the means adopted therein with respect to youth associations, in accordance with the adopted regulations.

- The technical and special conditions for activities, centres, the places designated for holding them and the means adopted therein with respect to sports clubs in educational institutions and sports associations in institutions.

- The Ministry shall establish a model for the general bylaws of associations, which shall observe this model when establishing their "General Bylaws".

The application for licensing the association shall be submitted to the Ministry accompanied by the following documents:

- Three copies of the general bylaws signed by all members of the founding committee on all of their pages.

- Three copies signed by all members of the founding committee of schedules of the names of the founding members, including the tripartite name of each member, his date of birth, his profession, and his address including telephone, fax, postal address, and electronic mail.

- An individual civil status extract or a copy of the identity card and a judicial record for each of the members of the founding committee.

- Minutes of the meeting of the founding committee signed by all members, provided that one of them is authorised to sign the contracts and correspondence necessary in preparation for founding the association.

- Two legal occupancy documents for both the headquarters of the association and the approved facility or facilities

(for practising sports games such as the stadium, the hall, the field, the swimming pool, or a youth hostel for youth hostel associations, or a place for practising scouting activities), provided that they are based on one of the following options:

a - A lease contract registered with the municipality in the name of the founding committee of the association for a term of not less than three years.

b - An agreement contract of "acknowledgement of tolerance" between the owner and the founding committee of the association certified before a notary public for a term of not less than three years.

c - A headquarters placed by the public administration, the public institution, or the municipality at the disposal of the associations pursuant to an official letter issued in accordance with the rules.

- A map of the headquarters signed and stamped by an architect or civil engineer affiliated with one of the two Orders of Engineers.

- A real estate certificate for the headquarters, or a certificate of notice and knowledge for non-surveyed areas.

- A map of the stadium, the hall, the field, the swimming pool, or the facilities designated for practising the games or activities, signed and stamped by an architect or civil engineer affiliated with one of the two Orders of Engineers.

- A real estate certificate for the stadium, the hall, the field, the swimming pool, or the facilities, or a certificate of notice and knowledge for non-surveyed areas.

- An undertaking to provide the Ministry with a specimen of the official seal of the association after the issuance of the licensing decision within a period of one month at most, stamped on a specimen of the official letterhead approved by the association and signed by all members of the founding committee.

Associations shall deposit with the Ministry, within a period not exceeding the end of the month of March of each year, the documents listed below after their approval by the General Assembly:

- An administrative statement containing a report on the works and activities completed during the ended year and the programme of works and activities intended to be completed during the new year.

- A list of the members of the General Assembly signed by the President and the Secretary containing the joined and active members, by which is meant all affiliated members whose affiliation has lasted a full year.

- An annual insurance policy with respect to scouting associations.

- The Administrative Board of associations must address the invitation to the sessions of the General Assembly of all kinds in writing within a period of not less than fifteen days and not more than thirty from their date.

- Likewise, in the case of sessions of the General Assembly designated for elections or the loss of legitimacy by the Administrative Board for any reason whatsoever, the invitation thereto shall be addressed before the expiry of the term of office of the Administrative Board within a period of not less than fifteen days from their date and not more than thirty from the date of expiry of the term of office. That shall be by virtue of a letter signed by the President and the Secretary containing the fixing of the date of the election session and accompanied by a list of the members of the General Assembly whose affiliation has lasted a year and who have the right to vote, provided that those who have not paid their subscriptions undertake to pay before the start of the session, failing which they shall not have the right to participate therein.

- If the time limit expires without the invitation to the elections being addressed, one quarter of the members of the General Assembly shall have the right to request the Ministry to address the invitation, provided that it includes naming a committee from the members of the General Assembly and charging it with conducting the elections.

- In the case of the resignation of the Administrative Board of the association or the legal loss of its legitimacy for any reason whatsoever during its term of office, a new Administrative Board shall be elected in accordance with the rules.

- Associations shall notify the Ministry of:

- A copy of the letter of invitation to the elections addressed to the General Assembly, referred to in Article seventeen of this Decree, within a period of no less than fifteen days preceding the date of holding the elections.

- Any amendment occurring to the distribution of positions in the Administrative Board.

- A list of the new members of the General Assembly successively, signed by the President and the Secretary, containing the tripartite name, and the letter shall be accompanied by the minutes of the meeting of the Administrative Board.

- A list of the members of the General Assembly whose membership has lapsed successively, signed by the President and the Secretary, containing the reasons for the lapse of membership, and the letter shall be accompanied by a copy of the minutes of the meeting of the Administrative Board.

Membership in the General Assembly shall lapse by death, resignation, dismissal for violating the General Bylaws, or due to failure to pay the annual subscription for two consecutive years, provided that the violating member has been warned in writing and officially notified thereof.

With regard to youth and scout associations:

- The licence of associations shall be revoked by a decision of the Minister upon the proposal of the Director General if:

A. They do not practise their activities throughout two consecutive years.

B. If it is proven that they have violated the provisions of their General Bylaws or the provisions of the laws and regulations in force, and they have been warned in writing by the Ministry to rectify their situation and comply with the aforementioned laws and regulations, without responding to the written warning within a time limit not exceeding three months from the date of their notification.

C. If they do not join the competent Federation, where it exists, within a time limit of two years for reasons relating to them and not to the Federation.

With regard to sports associations:

- If the association does not practise its activities throughout two consecutive sports seasons, the sport subject of the licence shall be revoked by a decision of the Minister upon the proposal of the Director General after the issuance of a decision by the competent Federation revoking the affiliation thereto. In this case, the concerned Federation shall address a letter to the Ministry containing notification of the association's non-practice of the activity for which it is licensed and a copy of the federal circulars or the minutes of the meetings of the Federation that note this matter.

- The sport subject of the licence shall be revoked from the association by a decision of the Minister upon the proposal of the Director General if it does not join the Federation competent for the sport for which it is licensed within a time limit of one year or if it loses the conditions under which it was licensed.

- If the licence of the sport is revoked from the association and its activity is restricted to this sport only, its licence shall be converted to the category of popular clubs.

The associations governed by this Decree shall:

- Confine their activities to that for which they are licensed.

- Exercise their activities in accordance with the laws and regulations in force and in accordance with their general bylaws and the regulations of their national federation.

- Submit an application for affiliation to the federations of the games and activities for which they are licensed within a time limit not exceeding one year from the date of issuance of the licensing decision in respect of sports and youth associations and two years in respect of scout associations.

- The federation that receives an application within this time limit shall provide the applicant association with a receipt proving the date of submission of the application thereto and its registration number therewith.

- In the event that the federation does not approve the affiliation of the association thereto, it must notify the Ministry and the applicant association within a maximum time limit of one year from the date of submission of the application thereto, while indicating the reasons warranting the non-approval.

The General Assembly of the association shall be composed of all members affiliated thereto in accordance with its general bylaws.

- In order to exercise his right to vote or to stand as a candidate for membership of the Administrative Committee of the association, a member of the General Assembly shall be required:

A - To be Lebanese and to have completed eighteen years of age (a copy of the identity card - an individual civil status extract - etc...).

B - To prove his enjoyment of his civil rights and not to have been convicted of a felony or an infamous misdemeanour (a judicial record dating back not more than three months).

C - To have his name listed on the General Assembly list notified to the Ministry, provided that he became affiliated at least one year prior to the date fixed for the election session, and that he has settled his due financial obligations.

The affairs of the association shall be managed by a body called the Administrative Committee, the term of office of which shall be fixed at between two and four years.

- The affairs of the scout association shall be managed by a body called the Administrative Committee or the General Command, the term of office of which shall be fixed at between two and four years.

- The General Assembly shall elect the members of the Administrative Committee.

- Every administrative correspondence issued by the associations must be stamped with the official seal and signed by the President and the Secretary.

- Every financial correspondence and transaction issued by the associations must be stamped with the official seal and signed by the President and the Treasurer.

Where the Administrative Board of a federation commits an administrative violation of the provisions of its General Bylaws or the provisions of the laws and regulations in force:

- The Ministry shall coordinate with the Lebanese Olympic Committee in this regard.

- The Ministry shall simultaneously address a written notice to the Lebanese Olympic Committee and to the offending Board, specifying therein the type and nature of the violation and requesting the rectification of the irregularity within a time limit proportionate to the nature of the violation.

- If the offending Administrative Board fails to rectify the irregularity, the Ministry shall take an administrative measure suspending administrative dealings with it, and the Lebanese Olympic Committee shall notify the competent International Federation.

- If the federation is not an Olympic federation or recognized as an Olympic federation, the Ministry shall take the necessary measures.

The members of the Administrative Board of any federation shall be elected by the General Assembly and shall thereafter distribute the offices among themselves, and such members may be elected directly to their offices by the General Assembly, in accordance with the General Bylaws of the federation, which must necessarily specify the number of members of the Administrative Board.

- The number of members of the Administrative Board of team sports federations shall be fifteen members at most.

- The number of members of the Administrative Board of the various individual sports federations shall be eleven members at most.

- An association shall not be entitled to participate in voting in the election of the Administrative Board of the federation until after the lapse of one year from its affiliation with the federation. And (with respect to a sports association) it must have participated in the mandatory annual competitions that the federation is required to specify expressly in its General Bylaws and technical regulations, during the sports season preceding the voting or election, in accordance with the bylaws of the federation.

- An association shall be represented in the General Assembly of the federation to which it is affiliated by whomever its Administrative Board delegates from among its members pursuant to a resolution adopted by it in a lawful meeting, and by virtue of an official authorization from it, provided that the authorization is stamped with the seal of the association, signed by its president and its secretary, and accompanied by a statement clearly specifying the number and date of the minutes of the meeting in which the Administrative Board of the association adopted the authorization resolution.

- The term of office of the Administrative Board of youth and scout federations shall be fixed at between two and four years.

- The term of office of the Administrative Board of sports federations shall be fixed at four years, provided that elections are held after the conclusion of the Summer Olympic Games, whether they are held or not.

- Every administrative correspondence issued by the federations shall be stamped with the official seal and signed by the President and the Secretary.

- Every financial correspondence and transaction issued by the federations shall be stamped with the official seal and signed by the President and the Treasurer.

- If the general bylaws of the federation have abolished the position of Secretary from among the elected members in accordance with the regulations of its international federation, then every administrative correspondence issued by the concerned federation shall be stamped with the official seal and signed by the employee assigned to this task, and with the signature of the President.

Elections for the administrative bodies of the federations must be held before the end of their term of office, provided that the time limits specified in their general bylaws are adopted.

- In the event that the term of office of the administrative body of the federation expires without issuing the call for elections in accordance with the rules and time limits, the General Assembly shall convene at the call of one-third of its members and shall assign a provisional tripartite committee whose mission shall be limited to conducting the elections in accordance with the general bylaws of the federation.

- In the event of the resignation of the administrative body of the federation or the loss of its legal legitimacy for any reason whatsoever during its term of office, a new administrative body shall be elected to complete the term if it exceeds six months, unless the federation's bylaws stipulate otherwise based on the requirements of its international federation.

- However, if the remaining term is less than six months, then the elections shall be held on the basis of a full term in accordance with the federation's bylaws.

The bodies must notify the Ministry of:

A. A copy of the letter calling for the elections addressed to the General Assembly, within a period of no less than fifteen days prior to the date of holding the elections.

B. A list signed by the President and the Secretary of the members of the General Assembly who have been affiliated for one year and are entitled to vote.

A candidate for membership of the administrative body of the federation is required:

- To be Lebanese and to have completed eighteen years of age (copy of identity card - individual civil status extract ...).

- To prove enjoyment of civil rights and not to be convicted of a felony or an infamous misdemeanour (a judicial record dating back no more than three months).

- Not to be a member of any administrative body of another federation in the same field of sports, youth, or scouting.

- To be, with regard to scout associations and girl guides and girl scouts associations, a member of the administrative body of his or her association affiliated with the federation.

- To abide by any additional conditions contained in the general bylaws of the federation.

Every sport shall have one local federation only, composed of associations licensed to practise this sport whose number shall not be less than four, and the mission of the federation shall be:

- Organising the affairs of the sport and its spread across all Lebanese territories.

- Holding the championships and sports activities specific to the sport annually on the basis of the classification and divisions adopted by it.

- Preparing the national teams and securing representation and participation at the Arab, regional, continental and international levels.

- Advancing the sport to the highest levels at the Arab, regional, continental and international levels.

- Federations of team sports may hold a special championship in accordance with special technical regulations approved in the General Assembly, provided that it does not affect, in form or in substance, the fate of the annual calendar of the federation.
Olympic and Olympically recognised sports federations must join the international federation of the sport and the Lebanese Olympic Committee.

There shall be formed, by a decision of the Minister upon the proposal of the Director General, a committee to manage every sport for which no licensed federation exists due to the unavailability of the required number of associations \

in accordance with Article Twenty, provided that it undertakes all the tasks and activities entrusted to a licensed federation except for the rights of candidacy and voting in the meetings of the General Assembly of the Lebanese Olympic Committee, and that:

1 . The number of its members does not exceed seven and is not less than five, among whom there shall be ex officio a representative of each licensed association.

2 . The Lebanese Olympic Committee names a member to this committee if the sport is Olympic or Olympically recognised.

3 . The term of office of the committee expires ex officio upon the conclusion of the Summer Olympic Games, and its term of office also expires ex officio upon the completion of the conditions for electing a federation for the sport in accordance with the regulations in force.

4 . The committee may adopt the designation "Federation" in its external correspondence

- The School Sports Federation shall examine the licensing file of the school sports club and then refer the proposal for licensing to the Ministry of Youth and Sports within a period of one month at most from the date of registration of the application with it. In the event of refusal and non-referral, the reasons must be stated.

- The licensing decision shall be issued by the Minister of Youth and Sports upon the proposal of the Director General within a period not exceeding one month from the date of registration of the licensing application with it. In the event that the Ministry refuses the licence, it shall be required to state the reasons.

- The administrative certificate shall be granted by the Ministry - the Directorate General.

- Participation in school championships shall not be permissible without obtaining the official licence.

The school sports club must, during the months of September and October of every year, provide the General School Sports Federation with a list of the names of the members of the administrative body and specify the president among them, and it must also provide this Federation with any amendment that may occur to this list or the distribution of duties therein, and the sports club shall also provide the General School Sports Federation with a list of the facilities, including courts, halls or a swimming pool, indicating therein the fulfilment of the technical conditions in accordance with the established rules, for the purpose of using them in official championships.

The school sports club shall be obliged to participate in the official championships of the games included in its licensing decision.

- In the event that the school sports club fails to comply with participating in the official championships of the games for which it is licensed for two consecutive academic years, its right to practise the game shall lapse and it shall be revoked from its licence if it is licensed in more than one game.

- In the event that the school sports club is licensed to practise a single sports game, its licence shall be revoked by a decision of the Minister upon the proposal of the Director General and the report received from the General School Sports Federation.

- The school sports club shall be obliged to join the General School Sports Federation within a period not exceeding one month from the issuance of the licensing decision.

- The school sports club shall be obliged to submit the technical lists of the players accredited by it to the General School Sports Federation within a period ending at the latest in the middle of the month of December of every year, in accordance with forms provided to it by the Federation, provided that they are signed by the president of the club.

There shall be formed in Lebanon a single federation for school sport called: "The General School Sports Federation".

- The General School Sports Federation shall have sole responsibility for competitive school sport in Lebanon, and for developing school sport, coordinating with the competent national federations, building and preparing school teams, representing Lebanon abroad, and joining counterpart Arab, regional, continental and international federations.

- The General Assembly of the General School Sports Federation shall consist of the school clubs affiliated to it.

- The term of office of the General School Sports Federation shall be four years.

The General School Sports Federation shall be composed of:

1 . The General Assembly.

2 . The Supreme Committee.

3 . The Executive Committee.

4 . The technical and sub-committees.

The Supreme Committee shall be composed of 17 members in accordance with the following mechanism:

- Seven members from among the employees of the administrative and teaching corps in the cadre of the Ministry of Education and Higher Education - the Directorate General of Education or the Joint Administrative Directorate upon the proposal of the Director General of Education, and two members from among the employees of the administrative and teaching corps in the Directorate General of Vocational and Technical Education upon the proposal of the Director General of Vocational and Technical Education; the nine members shall be appointed by a decision of the Minister of Education and Higher Education, provided that among them are the President of the Supreme Committee of the General School Sports Federation, the Financial Officer of the Federation, and the Executive Director of the Federation, who shall be ex officio from among the physical education teachers and instructors in the cadre of the Ministry of Education and Higher Education.

- Six members elected by secret ballot by the school sports clubs in private schools and institutes.

- Two members of experience and specialisation, appointed by a decision of the Minister of Education and Higher Education upon the proposals of the Director General of Education and the Director General of the Ministry of Youth and Sports.

The financial resources of the General School Sports Federation shall consist of:

- The annual subscriptions of the school sports clubs.

- The school sports card issued by the Federation.

- The revenue resulting from any advertising rights and television broadcasting rights.

- The financial contributions of the Ministries of Education and Higher Education, and of Youth and Sports.

- Gifts and donations, which must be coupled with the approval of the Supreme Committee.

The numbers of associations in team sports federations shall be determined as follows:

- First Division: not exceeding 12 associations.

- Second Division: not exceeding 16 associations.

- Third Division: not exceeding 24 associations.

- Fourth Division: not exceeding 48 associations, provided that the voting power of this division is equal to its counterpart in any of the higher divisions. In the event that the number exceeds 48 associations, the voting power of this division must remain approximately equal to each of one of the higher divisions.

- Fifth Division: open in number, and the associations of this division shall not have the right to vote in the general assemblies.

1 . Every duly licensed school, whether private or public, shall have the right to establish a school sports club.

2 . In establishing the school sports club, the school shall undertake that:

- The club is named after the school.

- The administrative board of the school club is composed of the director of sports or a person of equivalent status as president, the physical education teachers and coaches ex officio, and teachers from the teaching or administrative staff selected by the school principal, provided that the total number does not exceed five members.

The application for licensing the school sports club is submitted to the "General School Sports Federation" at its headquarters located in one of the facilities of the Ministry of Education and Higher Education, or at one of its branches, signed by the school principal, stamped with its seal, and accompanied by the following documents:

- The written approval of the Directorate General of Education or the Directorate General of Vocational and Technical Education, each according to its competence, on the application submitted to establish the club with respect to public schools and public schools, secondary schools, and technical institutes.

A copy of the licensing decree of the private school certified by the Directorate General of Education - Private Education Department or the Directorate General of Vocational and Technical Education, each according to its competence.

- A schedule of the names of the administrative board signed by the school principal, specifying the name of the president authorised to liaise with official authorities.

- A schedule of the sports that the school wishes to license in order to participate in their championships.

- A map of the facilities designated for practising the approved sports, with a certificate signed by the school principal certifying that these facilities belong to the school, or a certificate of permission from the municipality for the school to use municipal facilities.

- The seal of the school sports club, which shall be the same seal as that of the school with the addition of "Sports Club" to it.

The application for a licence to practise federal university sports activities shall be submitted to the Ministry signed by the president of the university, or whoever has the same status, or whoever deputises for him administratively, or by the competent authority therein, accompanied by the following documents:

- A copy of the licensing decree of the private university certified by the Ministry of Education and Higher Education.

- A list of the names of the supervising body.

- A schedule of the sports games which the university has decided to practise and participate in the official championships thereof.

- A document of legal occupancy of the facilities approved for practising the sports games.

- A plan of the facilities approved for practising the sports games signed and stamped by the university administration.

- A specimen of the approved seal.

- The Ministry shall receive the licence application and shall, within a time limit of one month at most, verify that it satisfies the required conditions, and the Ministry must issue the licensing decision immediately after the expiry of this time limit; otherwise, its silence shall be deemed a tacit decision of approval.

- The licensing decision shall be issued by the Minister upon the proposal of the Director General.

- Administrative certificates shall be given to university clubs by the Ministry - the Directorate General.

- Participation in university championships organised by the Lebanese University Sports Federation shall not be permitted without obtaining the official licence; however, universities shall have the right to hold internal and external friendly sports activities in accordance with their annual programme, provided that it does not conflict with the calendar of the Federation agreed upon at the beginning of the academic year.

- The university shall undertake to participate in the official championships of the sports games included in its licensing decision.

- In the event that the university fails to abide by participation in the official championships of the games for which it is licensed for two academic years, its right to practise the game shall lapse and it shall be cancelled from its licence if it is licensed for more than one game.

- In the event that the university is licensed to practise a single sports game, its licence shall be cancelled as a whole by a decision of the Minister upon the proposal of the Director General and the report received from the General Sports Federation for Universities.

- Universities shall undertake to join the Lebanese University Sports Federation within a time limit not exceeding one month from the issuance of the licensing decision.

- A technical committee shall be formed for each accredited sport such that it includes specialists therein and is linked to the Executive Committee, and a delegate of the national federation for the sport is represented therein, provided that the number of its members does not exceed seven.

- The General Scholastic Sports Federation shall establish the annual programme for all competitions and activities while committing to non-conflict between this programme and the calendar of the national federations, and in the event that any conflict occurs, absolute priority shall be given to the presence of athletes in the competitions of the national federations to the exclusion of others.

The Executive Committee shall be formed by a decision of the Higher Committee of the General Scholastic Sports Federation and shall be composed of:

- The Executive Director as Chairman.

- The Secretary.

- The Chairmen of the Central Committees (the Public Relations Committee - the Finance Committee - the Publications Committee - the Informatics Committee - the Media Committee - the Marketing and Advertising Committee - the Oversight Committee and other committees according to the necessity and need deemed fit by the Federation).

- The Chairmen of the technical and branch committees.

The Higher Committee of the General Scholastic Sports Federation shall appoint the Chairmen of the Central Committees from among persons of competence and experience.

As for the members of these committees, they shall be appointed by a decision of the Chairman of the Higher Committee upon the proposal of the Chairman of the Executive Committee, provided that the number of members of the committee is not less than three and does not exceed five, and branch committees may be formed in the governorates linked to the Central Committees.
The national federations shall work to secure logistical matters to ensure the success of the competitions and activities organised by the General Scholastic Sports Federation.

Every duly licensed university shall have the right to submit an application for a licence to practise federally accredited university sports activities in the name of "the University", through a supervisory body managed by the sports administration at the university.

The supervisory body shall consist of the Director of Sports at the university, the Head of the Sports Activity Department, or the Sports Official therein as Chairman, and the membership of whomever is chosen by the sports administration or the competent authority at the university.

- Universities shall submit the technical lists of players accredited by them from among the students enrolled in the university only to the Lebanese University Sports Federation during the months of October and November of each year in accordance with forms provided to them by the Federation, provided that they are signed by the President of the Supervisory Body.

- Universities may submit an application to amend the lists during the month of February in order to allow new students enrolled in the second semester to participate in federal university sports activities.

The supervisory bodies in universities may establish branches for themselves in the governorates to practice the sports activities for which they are licensed, provided that the central supervisory body in the parent university is represented in the General Assembly of the Lebanese University Sports Federation.

- A single federation for university sports shall be formed in Lebanon called: "The Lebanese University Sports Federation".

- The Lebanese University Sports Federation shall be solely responsible for competitive university sports in Lebanon, for developing university sports, coordinating with the competent national federations, building university national teams, representing Lebanon abroad, and its joining similar Arab, regional, continental, and international federations.

- The term of office of the Administrative Body of the Lebanese University Sports Federation shall be four years.

The Lebanese University Sports Federation shall consist of:

- The Administrative Body.

- The General Assembly.

- The Federation may form sub-committees and technical committees.

- The General Assembly of the Lebanese University Sports Federation shall be composed of the licensed universities that have joined it.

- Each university or higher education institute licensed to practice sports activities shall be represented in the General Assembly of the Federation by whomever it delegates pursuant to an official authorisation signed by the competent authority in the university.

- A university shall not have the right to participate in voting in the elections of the Administrative Body of the Federation until after the lapse of one year from its affiliation with the Federation, and provided that it has participated in the mandatory annual competitions during the academic year preceding the voting or election.

- The Administrative Body of the Lebanese University Sports Federation shall consist of 13 members.

- The General Assembly shall elect the members of the Administrative Body and the elected members shall distribute the positions among themselves; the General Assembly may also elect the members of the Administrative Body each in his position in accordance with the bylaws of the Federation.

- The Lebanese University Sports Federation must form a committee to manage each of the approved sports in coordination with the competent national federation for the sport.

- The Lebanese University Sports Federation shall draw up the annual programme for all competitions and activities while committing not to conflict with the calendar of the national federations,

and in the event of any conflict occurring, absolute priority shall be given to the presence of athletes in the competitions of the national federations to the exclusion of others.

- The national federations shall work to secure logistical matters to ensure the success of the competitions and activities organised by the Lebanese University Sports Federation.

- If the administrative body of the federation violates the provisions of its general bylaws or the provisions of the laws and regulations in force, the Ministry shall address a written warning to it specifying therein the types and nature of the violation and requesting it to rectify the defect and retract the violations within a period of one week. If the violating administrative body does not comply with the warning at the end of the given period or refuses to receive it, it shall be dissolved by a decision of the Minister upon the proposal of the Director General.

- The federation must notify the Ministry of:

أ. Every amendment that occurs to the distribution of positions in the administrative body.

ب. A list of the new members of the general assembly successively, signed by the president and the secretary, and the letter shall be accompanied by the minutes of the meeting of the administrative body.

ت. A list of the members of the general assembly whose membership has lapsed successively, signed by the president and the secretary, including the reasons for the lapse of membership, and the letter shall be accompanied by the minutes of the meeting of the administrative body.

- Institutions have the right to establish sports associations that adhere to the following conditions:

- That the number of members of the administrative or founding body is not less than five, among whom are a president, a secretary, and a treasurer.

- That it has bylaws comprising provisions relating to the following matters:

1 . The name of the association, its purpose, and its headquarters.

2 . The number of members of the administrative body, its powers, and the duties of its members.

3 . The conditions for forming the administrative body, distributing positions among its members, and the forfeiture of their membership.

4 . The funds of the association and the manner of investing and disposing of them.

5 . The conditions for amending the general bylaws of the association and dissolving it.

The application for licensing the association shall be submitted to the Ministry, signed by the Chairman of the Board of Directors of the institution to which the association under establishment is affiliated, or by the Director General for institutions that do not have boards of directors, accompanied by the following documents:

1 . A copy of the association's bylaws signed on all its pages by the same person specified above.

2 . A schedule of the names of the members selected to form the founding administrative committee, including the full three-part name of each member, his date of birth, his profession, and his address including telephone, fax, postal address, and electronic mail.

- A legal occupancy document for the facilities approved for the practice of sports games.

- A plan of the facilities approved for the practice of sports games, signed and stamped by an architect or civil engineer registered with one of the two Orders of Engineers.

3 . A specimen of the approved seal.

- The Ministry shall receive the licensing application and shall verify, within a period of one month at most, that it fulfils the required conditions, and the Ministry shall issue the licensing decision immediately after the expiry of this period, failing which its silence shall be deemed an implicit decision of approval, provided that this is done without referring to the opinion of the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities since this institution is originally licensed, and provided that the licensing decision is published in the Official Gazette at the expense of the founders.

- The licensing decision shall be issued by the Minister upon the proposal of the Director General.

- Administrative certificates for sports associations in institutions shall be issued by the Ministry - the Directorate General.

- Such institutions may not be of an educational nature.

- Such associations may only be established by a licence from the Ministry and for non-commercial purposes.

An institutional sports association shall be required to participate in the annual competitions determined and conducted by the Lebanese Federation of Institutions, and its licence shall be revoked by a decision of the Minister upon the proposal of the Director General if:

- It abstains from participating in the annual competitions of the sports for which it is licensed for two consecutive sports seasons. In such case, the Lebanese Federation of Institutions shall address a letter to the Ministry containing notification of the association's non-practice of the activities for which it is licensed and copies of the federal circulars or minutes of the meetings of the Federation that note this matter.

- It is proven that it has violated the provisions of its bylaws or the provisions of the laws and regulations in force, and it has been warned in writing by the Ministry to rectify its status and comply with the said laws and regulations, without responding to the written warning within a period not exceeding three months from the date of its notification thereof.

- It fails to join the Lebanese Federation of Institutions within the period of one year, for reasons attributable to it and not to the Federation.

- However, if the association is licensed to practise more than one sport and abstains from participating in the annual competitions for some of these sports, its licence for these sports exclusively shall be revoked by a decision of the Minister upon the proposal of the Director General.

The founding and administrative bodies of these associations shall be formed by the boards of directors of the institutions from which they emanate, or by the directors general of the institutions that do not have boards of directors, and they shall undertake the management of the association.

Like sports associations, institutional sports associations shall be required to keep the registers specified in the fifth Article of this Decree, and to provide the Ministry at the end of the month of March of each year with the documents specified in the sixteenth Article of this Decree (without their approval by the general assembly with respect to institutional sports associations due to the absence thereof), and shall also be required to:

1 . Confine their activities to the acts specified in their general bylaws and for which they are licensed.

2 . Practise their activities in accordance with the laws and regulations in force and in accordance with their bylaws and the regulations of their federation.

3 . Join the competent federation within a period not exceeding one year from the date of issuance of the licensing decision. The federation that receives the application within this period shall provide the applicant association with a receipt proving the date of submission of the application to it and the registration number with it. In the event that it does not approve the association's joining it, it must justify this to the Ministry and the association within a maximum period of one month from the date of registration of the application with it.

- Sports associations in institutions shall have one federation, which is the Lebanese Federation for Institutions, composed of the associations affiliated with it, the number of which shall not be less than eight, provided that sub-committees emanate from the administrative board of this federation to manage each sport.

- The Lebanese Federation for Institutions shall establish an annual programme for its activities and competitions, in which it shall strictly commit to avoiding any conflict with the calendars of the sports federations.

- In the event of any kind of conflict, absolute priority shall be given to athletes affiliated with sports associations.

- The Lebanese Federation for Institutions shall commit to full coordination with the sports federations with regard to its calendar and its use of stadiums, referees, various technical bodies, and other points of intersection.

1 . The general assembly of the Lebanese Federation for Institutions shall adopt the same conditions adopted in the sports federations with regard to its meetings and the conditions of candidates, candidacy, and election to the membership of its administrative boards, particularly Articles Six, Twenty-Four, Twenty-Six, and Twenty-Eight of this Decree.

2 . The number of members of the administrative board of the Lebanese Federation for Institutions must not exceed fifteen members.

3 . If the administrative board of the federation violates the provisions of its general bylaws or the provisions of the laws and regulations in force, the Ministry shall address a written warning to it specifying the types and nature of the violation and requesting it to rectify the defect and retract the violations within a period of one week. If the violating administrative board does not comply with the warning by the end of the given period or refuses to receive it, it shall be dissolved by a decision of the Minister upon the proposal of the Director General.

4 . The federation must notify the Ministry of:

a. Every amendment that occurs to the distribution of positions in the administrative board.

b. A list of the new members of the general assembly successively, signed by the president and the secretary, and the letter shall be accompanied by the minutes of the meeting of the administrative board.

c. A list of the members of the general assembly whose membership has lapsed successively, signed by the president and the secretary, including the reasons for the lapse of membership, and the letter shall be accompanied by the minutes of the meeting of the administrative board.

5 . Each association shall have one vote in the general assembly of the Lebanese Federation for Institutions.

Sports associations for persons with special needs shall have a federation, which is the "Lebanese Paralympic Committee", to which all the preceding provisions relating to sports federations shall apply.
A sports association for persons with special needs shall conduct an annual medical fitness examination with a specialist physician for the players participating in matches.

Popular clubs mean clubs which undertake, within their local scope, and in accordance with the laws and regulations in force and their general bylaws, the following:

- Practising one or more sports games solely by way of recreation, education and bringing youth together; provided that a popular club may not be licensed to practise weightlifting, powerlifting and physical culture games.

- Practising youth activities of all kinds solely by way of recreation and education.

- Scout activities shall not fall within the powers of these clubs under any circumstances.

- These clubs may not, under any circumstances, under penalty of revocation of their licence, exploit sports activities for profit-seeking purposes.

A popular club shall be subject, as to the conditions for its establishment and licensing, to the following:

- As to establishment: the same administrative conditions specific to the establishment of associations, as specified in Article Nine of this Decree.

- Licensing procedure: a popular club shall rely, in submitting a licence application, on the same procedure and manner specific to the licensing of associations, as specified in Articles Ten and Eleven of this Decree, with the exception of the technical conditions.

- Technical sports conditions: unlike sports associations, a popular club shall not be required, upon applying for a licence, to provide courts/playing fields and the facilities attached thereto in any form whatsoever, and its fulfilment of the administrative conditions shall suffice.

- Technical youth conditions: a popular club shall be bound, in the same manner as youth associations, and after obtaining its licence, to provide the technical conditions for any of the youth activities that it wishes to hold.

A popular club shall be bound in all its activities to observe the conditions of public safety and public order, and it shall have the right, within its local scope, to:

- Practise sports activities.

- Hold sports tournaments.

- Hold youth activities.

- Hold activities of a social nature.

Like associations, popular clubs shall be bound to keep the registers specified in the Fifth Article of this Decree, and to provide the Ministry at the end of the month of March of each year with the documents specified in the Sixteenth Article of this Decree, and they shall be required, in accordance with the text of the Eighteenth Article of this Decree, to notify the Ministry of any amendments to the distribution of positions in their administrative boards and to their general assemblies and to comply with the time limits specific to elections, and they shall also be bound to:

1 . Confine their activities to that for which they are licensed.

2 . Exercise their activities in accordance with the laws and regulations in force and in accordance with their general bylaws.

1 . A popular club shall not be entitled to affiliate with any federation other than the Lebanese Federation for Sport for All and shall consequently not be bound to participate in any official activities, nor shall it be permissible under any circumstances and for any reason whatsoever to combine its licence with the licence of a sports or youth association.

2 . In the event that the club decides to join a federation of one of the sports games, or one of the youth federations, pursuant to a proposal by the administrative board, ratified by the general assembly, it shall be required to:

A. Submit an application to the Ministry to amend its licence from a popular club to a sports association or a youth association, accompanied by the minutes of the meeting of the administrative board designated for this purpose and the minutes of the meeting of the general assembly designated to ratify the proposal of the administrative board.

B. Submit the necessary documents and plans relating to the playing fields and facilities so that they conform from the technical standpoint with the licence application to practise one or more sports games or youth activities.

3 . A popular club shall be revoked by a decision of the Minister upon the proposal of the Director General if its violation of the provisions of its general bylaws or the provisions of the laws and regulations in force is established, and it has been served with a written warning by the Ministry to regularise its status and comply with the aforementioned laws and regulations, without having complied with the written warning within a time limit not exceeding three months from the date of its notification thereof.

- A popular club shall have general bylaws like associations, provided that it observes the model prepared by the Ministry for this purpose, and it shall have a general assembly and an administrative board.

- The general assembly and the administrative board shall be composed in accordance with the same general conditions that govern the work of associations.

- Popular clubs shall join - if they so wish - the Lebanese Federation of Sport for All, whose mission shall be to supervise their activities and manage collective programmes of a national character.

- Where a popular club wishes to bring in any foreign club to play a friendly match or organise a tournament in a given sport, or to carry out a youth activity in which specialised foreign entities participate, it must first obtain the approval of the Ministry and then abide by the technical supervision of the competent federation.

- Traditional and heritage sports mean games such as wood sawing, crowbar lifting, mortar lifting, walnut cracking, tug of war, bell lifting, roller lifting, stick fighting, ramming, backgammon, card games, spinning top, marbles, water drinking, slingshot and jar carrying, by way of example and not limitation.

- In addition to the items specified in Articles Nine and Ten of this Decree, the association must have, at its headquarters or outside it, a hall with an area of not less than forty square metres allocated for training in the various activities and containing a space allocated for storage.

- Traditional and heritage sports associations may hold any of the activities specified in this Article, provided that they abide by the following:

1 . The conditions specified in the regulatory decisions issued by the Ministry in respect of each activity.

2 . Communicating the calendar of activities to the Ministry at the beginning of each year and a report thereon after its conclusion.

3 . Notifying the Lebanese Federation of Heritage Activities and the Ministry in writing of the activity and its programme, and obtaining the written approval of the Ministry if such activity is wholly or partially funded by it, provided that a report thereon is submitted after its conclusion.

- Traditional and heritage sports associations shall constitute the General Assembly of the Lebanese Federation of Traditional and Heritage Sports and shall elect its Administrative Board, and each of them shall have one vote in this General Assembly.

The Lebanese Olympic Committee is an independent civil body supported by the State that derives its laws and regulations from the International Olympic Charter and the regulations in force in Lebanon, in a manner that does not conflict with the International Olympic Charter.

- The General Assembly of the Lebanese Olympic Committee shall be composed, in accordance with its general bylaws and in a manner that does not conflict with the International Olympic Charter, of the members affiliated therewith and the member of the International Olympic Committee, if any.

- The member of the International Olympic Committee (if any) shall be an ex officio member of the Executive Committee and shall have the right to vote and to stand as a candidate for any position therein.

- A federation shall be represented at the meetings of the General Assembly of the Lebanese Olympic Committee by its president without any authorisation; in the event of the president's absence, the delegate of the federation must be a member of the administrative board and provided with an official authorisation therefrom pursuant to a decision taken in a lawful session.

- The right to vote in the General Assembly of the Lebanese Olympic Committee shall be vested in the federations listed on the programme of the Summer and Winter Olympic Games, the Paralympic Committee, the Olympians Association, and the member of the International Olympic Committee, if any.

- Only sports federations listed on the programme of the Olympic Games and olympically recognised federations shall have the right to stand as candidates for the Executive Committee of the Lebanese Olympic Committee.

- The number of winners, with respect to olympically recognised federations, must not exceed one-third of the members of the Executive Committee, in accordance with the mechanism provided for in the bylaws of the Lebanese Olympic Committee.

- The election of the Executive Committee of the Lebanese Olympic Committee shall take place after the conclusion of the events of the Summer Olympic Games, whether held or not held, and in accordance with the general bylaws of the Committee.

- It shall fall within the duties and role of the Executive Committee the Lebanese Olympic Committee to organise and participate in Olympic, continental, and regional sports activity and to disseminate Olympic principles and methods in accordance with what is determined by the Olympic Charter.

1 . Scout associations and Girl Guide and Guide associations shall derive their bylaws and teachings from the world Scout principles, the resolutions and recommendations issued by international and Arab Scout bodies, and the laws and regulations in force in Lebanon, provided that they do not conflict with the Lebanese laws in force.

2 . Scout associations shall carry out their activities in the following circles:

- Male circles.

- Joint male and female circles.

3 . Guide and Girl Guide associations shall be concerned with spreading the Scout and Guiding movement and carrying out their activities in female circles.

4 . Only male and female members affiliated with officially recognised Scout and Girl Guide associations shall be recognised in Lebanon in the capacity of Scouts and Girl Guides, be called a Male Beaver, Female Beaver, Cub, Brownie, Male Junior Scout, Female Junior Scout, Male Scout, Female Scout, Girl Guide, Guide, Venture Scout, Senior Guide, Male Rover, Female Rover, Ranger, or Young Wayfarers, wear the Scout uniform, and use the Scout badges and insignia.

A Scout association shall be managed, in accordance with its general bylaws, in the following manner:

1 . Where the presidential system is adopted for the association: the association shall be managed by a Chief Commissioner elected by the General Assembly, who shall appoint the remaining members of the bureau in accordance with the general bylaws of the association.

2 . Where the administrative committee system is adopted: a body called the Administrative Committee whose mission shall be to manage, organise, and direct the affairs of the association, the members of which shall be elected in accordance with the general bylaws of the association.

3 . In addition to the conditions set forth in Article fourteen of this Decree, a member of the General Assembly must be an invested leader.

- One Scout Federation for males or for males and females together shall be recognised in Lebanon, named the "Lebanese Scout Federation", whereby its General Assembly shall be composed of the Scout associations and the National Education Scouts, and each of them shall have one vote in the General Assembly of the Federation.

- One Scout Federation for females shall be recognised in Lebanon, named the "Lebanese Federation of Girl Guides and Girl Scouts", whereby its General Assembly shall be composed of all the Girl Guides and Girl Scouts associations and the National Education Girl Guides and Girl Scouts association, and each of them shall have one vote in the General Assembly of the Federation.

- The number of members of the Administrative Board of each of these two Federations shall not be less than nine members and shall not exceed fourteen members.

- The Lebanese Scout Federation, the Lebanese Federation of Girl Guides and Girl Scouts, and the Scout associations shall be required to do the following:

1 . Hold and organise annual general activities.

2 . Hold training courses and studies for leaders and scouts at various levels and specialisations.

3 . Adopt a special register for the results of the training courses and studies for leaders and youth at their various levels.

4 . Notify the Ministry at the beginning of each year of the calendar and of the results of the training courses and studies at the end thereof.

Youth associations shall work to achieve the following principles:

1 . Empowering youth so that they play a positive role in their own interest and the interest of their society.

2 . Addressing the aspirations, concerns, and issues of interest to youth, and the political, intellectual, social, economic, and humanitarian challenges that they face.

3 . Strengthening identity, adherence to heritage, concepts of citizenship and belonging, the system of national and social values and ideals, and the participation of youth to play an effective, leading, and positive role.

4 . Consolidating the values of democracy and the role of youth in formulating national decisions, and strengthening their belief in human rights, the individual rights of the citizen, freedom of expression, and accepting and engaging in dialogue with the other.

5 . Strengthening the role of youth in development.

6 . Combating doping and addiction of all kinds.

7 . Strengthening the will for innovation and creativity and the relationship of youth with technology and the means of knowledge.

8 . Spreading the culture of voluntary work.

Youth associations are of six types, which are:

1 . Children and youth summer camp associations.

2 . Voluntary work associations.

3 . Scientific activities associations.

4 . Youth hostels associations.

5 . Folkloric activities associations.

6 . Various youth activities associations.

Subject to the provisions of the ninth and tenth Articles of this Decree, the licensing application for a Scout association must include the following:

1 . That it observes, in drafting its general bylaws, the provisions of the international bylaws for Scout, Girl Guide, and Ranger associations, unless they conflict with the Lebanese laws in force.

2 . That it has at least a second headquarters in another Governorate other than the Governorate in which its main headquarters is located, and that the licensing application is accompanied by the occupancy document as specified in the tenth Article of this Decree, a plan for this headquarters signed and stamped by an architect or civil engineer affiliated with one of the two Orders of Engineers, and a real estate certificate for it or a notice and acknowledgement certificate for unsurveyed areas.

3 . That its founding body undertakes, pursuant to a written letter signed by all of its members, to have within a maximum period of two years from the date of issuance of the licence:

أ. A number of affiliates amounting to /1000/ one thousand members with respect to Scout associations and /500/ five hundred members with respect to Girl Guide or Ranger associations.

ب. A number of units not less than thirty Scout units with respect to Scout associations and not less than twenty units with respect to Girl Guide and Ranger associations.

ت. Twenty leaders holding a leader certificate (Wood Badge) or a similar internationally recognized certificate among the Girl Guides, in addition to five Scout trainers holding a Scout trainer or Assistant Leader Trainer certificate, and one leader holding a Leader Trainer certificate.

In the event that the association does not comply with what is stated in its licensing application with regard to the content of the third item of the eightieth Article, the provisions of the nineteenth Article of this Decree shall apply to it.

Youth associations that obtained the Acknowledgement of Receipt and Notice from the Ministry of Interior prior to the date of issuance of this Decree shall have the right to be accredited at the Ministry of Youth and Sports, provided that they submit an application in accordance with the form prepared for this purpose, accompanied by:

- A certified true copy of the Acknowledgement of Receipt and Notice issued by the Ministry of Interior.

- A copy of the General Bylaws of the association stamped by the Ministry of Interior and signed by all members of the Administrative Board on all its pages, provided that these General Bylaws include the items specified in the ninth Article of this Decree.

- A copy signed by all members of the Administrative Board on all its pages of schedules containing the names of the members of the Administrative Board, including the full three-part name of each member, his date of birth, his profession, and his address including the telephone, fax, postal address, and electronic mail.

- An individual civil status extract or a copy of the identity card, and a judicial record for each of the members of the Administrative Board.

- A legal occupancy document for the headquarters of the association in accordance with one of the following options:

a. A lease contract registered at the municipality in the name of the Administrative Board of the association for a term of not less than three years.

b. A "declaration of tolerance" agreement between the owner and the Administrative Board of the association certified before a notary public for a term of not less than three years.

c. A headquarters placed by a public administration, a public institution, or a municipality at the disposal of the association pursuant to an official letter duly issued.

- A map of the headquarters signed and stamped by an architect or civil engineer affiliated with one of the two Orders of Engineers.

- A real estate certificate for the headquarters or a certificate of notice and knowledge for uncadastred areas.

- A specimen of the official seal stamped on a specimen of the official letterhead adopted by the association, signed by all members of the Administrative Board.

These associations shall be accredited pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister upon the proposal of the Director General, provided that the decision is published in the Official Gazette at the expense of the association.

Youth associations, in holding activities or programmes, shall be required to:

1 . Comply with the conditions specified in the regulatory decisions issued by the Ministry with respect to each activity.

2 . Notify the Ministry and the competent federation in writing of the activity and its programme.

3 . Obtain the prior written approval of the Ministry if such activity is wholly or partially funded by it, provided that a report thereon is submitted after its completion.

- The Ministry shall lay down specific conditions for each programme or activity, and shall issue them periodically by regulatory decisions of the Minister.

- The Ministry shall have the right to supervise activities and cancel them if it is established that they violate the regulatory decisions issued by the Ministry.

- Youth associations wishing to organise training activities under which certificates are granted shall be required to obtain:

1 . The written approval of the competent federation, where one exists.

2 . The written approval of the Ministry on the application, which shall include a copy of the federation's approval and the programme and curriculum of the activity, at least one month prior to the date on which it is to be held.

3 . The authentication of the competent federation and the Ministry on the certificates granted.

- In addition to the technical conditions specified in Article Twelve of this Decree, youth associations shall comply, each within the scope of its competence, with the regulatory decisions issued by the Ministry.

- Youth associations shall have the right to request the addition of a licence for any of the youth activities mentioned in Article Eighty-Four above, provided that they comply with the conditions specified in the laws, decrees and regulatory decisions issued by the Ministry.

With the exception of youth hostel activities, any youth association may organise a specialised activity, even if it is not included within its licence, or if it is not a member of the competent federation, provided that it complies with:

- The conditions specified in the regulatory decisions issued by the Ministry.

- Obtaining the written approval of the competent federation and the Ministry for the activity and its programme, provided that the Ministry, in coordination with the competent federation, shall have the right to supervise the activity and cancel it if it is established that it violates the provisions of the laws and regulations in force.

With the exception of "Various Youth Activities Associations", each type of the youth associations specified in Article Eighty-Four shall have only one local federation, composed of at least five associations licensed to practise this type of activity, and the member associations in the General Assembly shall elect the Administrative Board of the Federation such that each of them has one vote in this Assembly.

The mission of the Federation shall be:

- Organising the affairs of youth activity and working to spread it across all Lebanese territories.

- Establishing the necessary plans and studies to achieve the principles specified in Article Eighty-Three of this Decree.

- Forming committees of specialists whose mission is to provide the Administrative Board of the Federation with the means of developing curricula and plans in a manner consistent with modern scientific educational concepts and the needs of youth.

- Working to coordinate among the associations affiliated with it and developing networks of direct and indirect communication among them.

- Supervising the training activities organised by the associations affiliated with it on the basis of the curricula approved by the Ministry and certifying the certificates resulting therefrom.

- Representing Lebanon in international, continental, regional and Arab missions and activities.

Children and Youth Summer Camp Associations are associations concerned with establishing the recreational, educational and sports programmes and plans necessary to bring together children or youth within the context of extracurricular summer activities, laying down the foundations for supervising these activities, and preparing the cadres necessary for implementation.

In addition to the items specified in Articles Nine and Ten of this Decree, the licensing application for a Children and Youth Summer Camp Association must include the drafting of its general bylaws in a manner consistent with the provisions of the international and national bylaws of Children and Youth Summer Camp Associations.

Voluntary Work Associations are associations concerned with every specialised unpaid work in the service of humanity and society, by providing qualitative and organised services to the members of society, and working towards the balance and continuity of social interaction among the various segments of society.

In addition to the items specified in Articles Nine and Ten of this Decree, the licensing application for a Voluntary Work Association must include the drafting of its general bylaws in a manner consistent with the provisions of the international and national bylaws of Voluntary Work Associations.

Scientific activity associations are associations concerned with all fields relating to informatics, accompanying software, and the internet, and that work to educate and train youth, develop their scientific capacities and their artistic and technical skills, and encourage them to innovate and create.

In addition to the items specified in Articles Nine and Ten of this Decree, a scientific activity association must have, within its premises or outside thereof, a hall with an area of not less than forty square metres allocated for training in various activities.

Youth hostels are houses for reception and accommodation, and they shall be either permanent, opening throughout the days of the year, or seasonal, opening during specific periods, and the guest therein must abide by the local and international regulations in force.

- Subject to the provisions of Articles Nine and Ten of this Decree, the licensing application for a youth hostel association must include the drafting of its general bylaws in a manner consistent with the provisions of the international and national bylaws of youth hostel associations.

- Pursuant to Article Twelve, youth hostel associations shall abide by the technical conditions issued by regulatory decisions of the Minister upon the proposal of the Director General.

Youth hostel associations must keep the following registers:

1 . A statistics register comprising the guest's three-part name and nationality, the number, date, and expiry date of his passport, the name of the authority that issued it, the name of his country of residence and his address, the date of arrival, the duration of stay, the date of departure, and any other information where necessary.

2 . Daily and monthly statements of guests.

3 . Notice boards containing the bylaws of the hostel in three languages, one of which is the Arabic language, the floor plan of the hostel and its divisions, and a map showing the location of the hostel in relation to the most important places in the city such as post offices, banks, universities, public libraries, hospitals, important stores, and restaurants, in addition to the name of the supervisor and his working hours.

Youth hostel associations shall abide by the following:

1 . Determining the times for opening and closing the doors of the youth hostel.

2 . Securing a sound, healthy climate and environment, and ensuring easy access to the hostel away from any danger.

3 . Permanently maintaining cleanliness, security, and safety for the guests.

Youth hostel associations shall constitute the general assembly of the Lebanese Federation of Youth Hostels and shall elect its administrative board, and each of them shall have one vote in this general assembly.

1 . If the delegations require financing from the Ministry, applications for bringing in and dispatching delegations shall be submitted thereto at least two months prior to the scheduled date, accompanied by the following documents:

a. With regard to sports federations, the Olympic Committee and the Lebanese Paralympic Committee, the application shall include:

- A presentation of the nature of the activity, its importance, the participating entities, and the desired technical and administrative outcomes based on facts and projections, including the estimated number of participants in the delegation.

- An estimated statement of expenditures and revenues.

- A copy of the invitation.

- The approval of the Lebanese Olympic Committee with regard to sports federations.

b. With regard to scout or youth federations, the application shall include:

- A presentation of the nature of the activity, its importance, the participating entities, the nature of the meetings, the expected topics and dialogues, and the desired technical and administrative outcomes based on facts and projections, including the estimated number of participants in the delegation.

- An estimated statement of expenditures and revenues.

- A copy of the invitation.

2 . The Ministry shall decide on the need to submit the application received by it from one of the bodies, the Federation of Establishments, the General School Sports Federation, or the Lebanese Federation of University Sports to the Council of Ministers.

3 . Approval for participation in the conference or championship shall be granted once, such that participation in the same conference or championship does not require a second approval, and notifying the Ministry thereof shall suffice.

1. The Minister shall decide, upon the proposal of the Director General, the amount of the Ministry's contribution to the expenditures of bringing in and dispatching delegations.

2 . The financial contribution shall be granted for the following matters:

a. Preparation.

b. Travel and accommodation expenditures.

c. Technical and in-kind equipment.

d. Insurance.

e. Anti-doping laboratory tests.

f. Miscellaneous expenses.
