Those responsible for delegations inside the country or abroad shall notify the Ministry or the Lebanese embassies or consulates of any accident or emergency to which the delegation or its members are exposed immediately upon its occurrence.

«Major events» shall mean Arab, regional, Mediterranean, continental, Olympic and international multi-sport games or championships, or Arab, regional, Mediterranean, continental and international scout or youth activities hosted by Lebanon.

Any of the bodies must obtain the written approval of the Ministry before commencing the submission of an application to host major multi-game events, whether the hosting requires funding from the Ministry or does not require it, provided that the application includes:

1 . A study explaining the importance of the event from the sports or youth, economic, touristic and political aspects, and including the determination of the tasks and roles required for the success of the hosting from each of the Lebanese State, the Lebanese Olympic Committee, the Lebanese Paralympic Committee, the competent federation and civil society.

2 . The nature and size of the expected participation, including a list of the countries expected to participate.

3 . The desired technical and administrative results from the Lebanese delegation based on facts and expectations.

4 . An estimated statement of expenditures and revenues (if the hosting requires funding from the Ministry).

5 . A copy of the hosting conditions.

6 . The opinion of the Lebanese Olympic Committee with regard to sports federations.

With regard to hosting major events that require the approval of the Council of Ministers, it shall be for the Council to form, after approving the hosting in accordance with international regulations and upon the proposal of the Minister, a supreme committee whose mission is to organise the event and to grant it the widest powers, provided that the competent official authorities shall facilitate its work.

The Ministry may also propose to the Council of Ministers the formation of a similar committee to organise a given event even if the decision to approve its hosting is restricted to the Ministry and does not require the approval of the Council.

The objectives of the "National Committee for Sports, Scouting and Youth" shall be defined as preparing strategies to study the establishment of sports, youth and scouting complexes in all Lebanese regions, and studying the means and laying down the plans and executive mechanisms to generalise sports culture, the youth movement and youth activities across the territory of the nation, whereby these strategies, plans and executive mechanisms shall be submitted to the Ministry, which adopts them and works on implementing them directly or in coordination with associations, federations, municipalities, a grouping of municipalities, a federation of municipalities, or civil society bodies.

Associations of Folkloric Recreational Activities are associations concerned with performance activities linked to national heritage, such as Dabke and folklore of all kinds, and that work to introduce youth to all fields related thereto and to work on training them and developing their artistic and technical skills.

In addition to the items specified in Articles Nine and Ten of this Decree, an association of recreational and folkloric activities must have, at its headquarters or outside it, a hall with an area of not less than forty square metres allocated for training in various activities and containing an area allocated for storage.

- "Various Youth Activities" means activities concerned with implementing diverse youth programmes, whether recreational, intellectual, educational, social, developmental or environmental... by way of example and not limitation.

- And "Associations of Various Youth Activities" means associations that work in the service of youth in the various fields that concern them through diverse executive programmes and activities in fulfilment of the objectives specified in Article Eighty-Three of this Decree.

"Missions" means delegations representing Lebanon in official multi-sport athletic, scouting and youth activities organised domestically or participated in abroad by athletic, scouting and youth federations, the Lebanese Olympic Committee, the Lebanese Paralympic Committee, the General School Sports Federation, the General University Sports Federation, the Lebanese Federation of Institutions and the Lebanese Federation of Popular Clubs, in the following fields:

- Tournaments and championships: International - Olympic - Continental - Mediterranean - Regional - Arab.

- Youth or scouting festivals, camps or gatherings.

- Official athletic, scouting and youth conferences abroad or domestically.

Financial contributions shall be granted pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister upon the proposal of the Director General, in accordance with the following:

First, with regard to the Lebanese Olympic Committee:

- To pay its Arab, regional, continental, Olympic, and international annual subscriptions and fees.

- To cover a portion of its annual budget for administrative expenses with regard to the rentals of headquarters and their equipment, office, administrative, and information technology supplies, and fees and allowances for employees and wage earners.

- To cover a portion of its technical expenses related to external participations.

- To implement activities or programmes in cooperation with the Ministry.

Second, with regard to the Lebanese Paralympic Committee:

- To pay its Arab, regional, continental, Olympic, and international annual subscriptions and fees.

- To cover a portion of its annual budget for administrative expenses with regard to the rentals of headquarters and their equipment, office, administrative, and information technology supplies, and fees and allowances for employees and wage earners.

- To cover a portion of its technical expenses related to external participations.

- To implement activities or programmes in cooperation with the Ministry.

- For the maintenance of facilities dedicated to persons with special needs.

Third, with regard to sports federations:

- To pay their annual subscriptions and fees in counterpart Arab, regional, continental, Olympic, and international federations.

- To cover a portion of their annual budget for administrative expenses with regard to the rentals of headquarters and their equipment, office, administrative, and information technology supplies, and fees and allowances for employees and wage earners.

- To cover a portion of the expenses of organising local official championships and competitions, including stadium rentals, referees, observers, and the like.

- To prepare, train, ready, and equip national teams to participate in Arab, regional, continental, Olympic, and international official competitions and activities, and to cover all or part of the potential expenses of travel, accommodation, transportation, incidental expenses, and the like.

- To host official external competitions and championships in Lebanon.

- To implement activities or programmes in cooperation with the Ministry.

Fourth, with regard to youth and scout federations:

- To pay their annual subscriptions and fees in counterpart Arab, regional, continental, Olympic, and international federations.

- To cover a portion of their annual budget for administrative expenses with regard to the rentals of headquarters and their equipment, office, administrative, and information technology supplies, and fees and allowances for employees and wage earners.

- To host official youth and scout activities in Lebanon.

- To implement activities or programmes in cooperation with the Ministry or to participate in external programmes with its approval, provided that this includes all or part of the potential expenses of travel, accommodation, transportation, incidental expenses, and the like.

Fifth, with regard to the Lebanese Federation for Sport for All, the Lebanese Federation for Traditional and Heritage Sports, the Public School Sports Federation, the Lebanese University Sports Federation, the Lebanese Federation for Corporations, and the Lebanese Sports Media Federation:

- To pay the Arab, regional, continental, Olympic, and international annual subscriptions and fees.

- To cover a portion of the annual budget for administrative expenses with regard to the rentals of headquarters and their equipment, office, administrative, and information technology supplies, and fees and allowances for employees and wage earners.

- To cover a portion of the expenses related to external participations.

- To implement independent activities or programmes or in cooperation with the Ministry.

The financial contribution to the specified bodies or federations above may be in-kind contributions (administrative or technical equipment), provided that they are among the supplies required for developing administrative and technical work and performance.

The Ministry may also provide in-kind contributions to school sports clubs or to the bodies supervising the administration of sports in universities.

The «National Committee for Sports, Scouting and Youth» shall be formed by a decision of the Minister upon the proposal of the Director General once every four years following the conclusion of the activities of the Summer Olympic Games, as follows:

- The Director General of the Ministry, as Chairman.

- The President of the Lebanese Olympic Committee, as Vice-Chairman.

- The member of the International Olympic Committee, if any, as a member.

- The Secretary General of the Lebanese Olympic Committee, as a member.

- The Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Public Institution for Sports, Youth and Scouting Facilities, as a member.

- The Head of the Sports Department at the Ministry, as a member.

- The Head of the Youth Department at the Ministry, as a member.

- The Mayor of the Municipality of Beirut and the Presidents of the Unions of Municipalities in Lebanon, as members.

- The President of the Lebanese Federation of Sport for All, as a member.

- The Secretary General of the Lebanese Paralympic Committee, as a member.

- The President of the Lebanese Federation of Institutions, as a member.

- The President of the Lebanese University Sports Federation, as a member.

- The President of the General School Sports Federation, as a member.

- The President of the Lebanese Scout Federation, as a member.

- The President of the Lebanese Federation of Girl Guides and Girl Scouts, as a member.

- The President of the Lebanese Federation of Summer Camps for Children and Youth, as a member.

- The President of the Lebanese Federation for Voluntary Work, as a member.

- The President of the Lebanese Federation for Scientific Activities, as a member.

- The President of the Lebanese Federation of Youth Hostels, as a member.

- The President of the Lebanese Federation for Folkloric Activities, as a member.

- Three experts in the field of sports, as members.

- Three experts in the field of scouting, as members.

- Three experts in the field of youth, as members.

Provided that the membership of these members shall be voluntary, and provided that the Committee shall appoint employees in the capacity of an Executive Director, a Financial Director and a Secretariat, and provided that the Ministry shall allocate premises for it and a budget for its expenses.

A. The bodies and federations specified in Article one hundred and thirteen shall submit the application for the annual financial contribution to the Ministry accompanied by:

1 . A copy of the minutes of the meeting of the annual ordinary General Assembly that was dedicated to approving the closing of accounts of the ended year and the budget of the current year, the annual report of the activities of the previous year, and the annual programme of the activities of the current year, accompanied by a list of the present and non-present members of the General Assembly.

2 . The comprehensive estimated budget for the current year, including the following:

- A schedule of the annual subscriptions and fees in the Arab, regional, continental, Olympic, and international counterpart entities.

- A schedule of the annual administrative expenditures with respect to the rents of headquarters and their equipment, their office, administrative, and information technology supplies, and the fees and allowances for employees and wage earners.

- A schedule of the expenditures resulting from the organisation of youth and scouting activities and local official championships and competitions.

- A schedule of potential external participations and programmes for preparing national teams and their estimated costs.

3 . A schedule of the activities or programmes proposed to be implemented in cooperation with the Ministry and their costs.

4 . A detailed financial statement duly signed, or a copy of the statement of the mission account for the funds granted by the State with respect to the sports federations, the Olympic Committee, the Lebanese Paralympic Committee, the Lebanese Federation of Sport for All, the Lebanese Federation for Traditional and Heritage Sports, the General School Sports Federation, the Lebanese University Sports Federation, the Lebanese Federation for Corporations, and the Lebanese Sports Media Federation, and a detailed copy of the closing of accounts of the ended year duly signed with respect to the scouting or youth federations.

5 . A clearance certificate from the National Social Security Fund.

6 . A certificate of registration with the Ministry of Finance.

7 . The complete financial and engineering study for the maintenance of the facilities dedicated to persons with special needs with respect to the Lebanese Paralympic Committee.

B. If the bodies and federations specified in Article one hundred and thirteen wish to obtain a financial contribution to implement activities or programmes in cooperation with the Ministry of which no mention was made in the submitted budget, and they have completed providing the Ministry with the documents referred to above, they shall submit an application at least two months prior to the date of the said activity or programme.

C. If the bodies and federations specified in Article one hundred and thirteen wish to obtain in-kind benefits, they shall submit a written application containing a detailed statement of the requested items and a justification of the need for them.

D. In determining the value of the contribution for the bodies, consideration shall be given to the extent of the legality and regularity of their annual documents required to be submitted to the Ministry, the quality and volume of the activities or programmes intended to be held, their geographical or social reach, and the extent of their contribution to the implementation of its plans and programmes.

- "Individuals" means: athletes, coaches, administrators, referees, media professionals, physicians, physiotherapists, escorts of delegations, and distinguished cadres in the fields of youth, scouting, and sports.

- Financial contributions or rewards shall be granted to these individuals by a decision of the Minister upon the proposal of the Director General in the following cases:

1 . To cover advance expenses for preparation, training, readiness, equipping, and participation in official Arab, regional, continental, Olympic, and international competitions and activities.

2 . As a reward in return for their achieving advanced accomplishments or a distinguished presence.

- The financial contribution shall be granted in these two cases:

1 . By a decision of the Ministry and on its initiative, provided that it includes the grounds for which the contribution or reward was granted.

2 . Based on a written letter from the federation to which the individual belongs, containing an explanation of the accomplishment and its grounds, and administrative or media documents proving its achievement.

- The value of the financial contributions or rewards in this case shall be determined pursuant to decisions issued by the Minister upon the proposal of the Director General.

- Municipalities or unions of municipalities may be granted a financial contribution for the construction, completion of construction, rehabilitation, or maintenance of sports, scout, or youth facilities, provided that they submit an application to the Ministry accompanied by:

1 . A certificate proving the ownership by the municipality or the unions of municipalities of the real property designated for the construction, completion of construction, or rehabilitation of sports, scout, or youth facilities, or an allocation contract by the State, or a lease contract registered with the municipality for a term of not less than fifteen years, or a tolerance agreement contract authenticated before a notary public for a term of not less than fifteen years, provided that the area of the real property ranges between two thousand and four thousand square metres with respect to municipalities, and provided that the area of the real property ranges between six thousand and ten thousand square metres with respect to the union of municipalities.

2 . A comprehensive executive engineering study of the project containing all information relating thereto, including the estimated budget signed by a civil Engineer or architect affiliated with one of the two Orders of Engineers, and a copy of the building permit and the plans, or an approval from the municipality or from the unions of municipalities for the establishment of the facilities.

3 . A written undertaking to commit to the periodic maintenance and development of the building or facility, and not to make any change to its intended use during a period of twenty years from its establishment.

- The facility shall mandatorily include:

1 . With respect to the real property whose area ranges between six thousand and ten thousand square metres, one court that may be used for practising the games of basketball, volleyball, and tennis, and one field for practising mini-football surrounded by a four-lane running track, and an administrative building with an area of not less than two hundred metres, a children's garden, a car park, and amenities.

2 . With respect to the real property whose area amounts to four thousand metres, one court that may be used for practising the games of basketball, volleyball, and tennis, and one field for practising mini-football, and an administrative building with an area of not less than one hundred square metres, a children's garden, a car park, and amenities.

3 . With respect to the real property whose area amounts to at least two thousand metres, one court that may be used either for practising the games of basketball, volleyball, and tennis or for practising mini-football, and an administrative building with an area of not less than one hundred square metres, and amenities.

4 . With respect to scout or youth camping centres: a real property with an area of not less than ten thousand metres, containing various amenities including an administrative building with an area of not less than two hundred square metres, a garden, a car park, bathrooms, and showers.

Financial contributions shall be granted to associations licensed by the Ministry and continuing their participation in annual competitions and mandatory activities in each of the following cases:

* Preparation and readying to represent Lebanon abroad, where the avenues of expenditure of the financial contribution in this case shall be determined to cover all or part of the expenses of preparation, training, readying, equipping, travel, accommodation and sundry expenses for participating in official Arab, regional, continental or international competitions and activities in which the sports association is assigned by the competent federation to represent Lebanon based on its advanced local results, or similar youth or scout activities in which Lebanon is present through specialized associations and with the approval of their federation, if any, or with the approval of the Ministry.

The association must submit a file to the Ministry at least two months prior to the date of the competition or activity, including the following:

1 - An application to obtain a financial contribution to cover specified expenses relating to preparation, training, readying, equipping, travel, accommodation or sundry expenses to represent Lebanon in:

- An official sports activity or competition specified by name, place and time, including a comprehensive and detailed study and technical expectations.

- A youth or scout activity specified by name, place and time, including a comprehensive and detailed study including the objectives sought from the participation.

2 - If the participation in this activity or competition is of a recurring nature requiring preparation, training, readying, equipping, travel, accommodation and sundry expenses several times, the probabilities and the expenses relating to each probability shall be itemized.

3 - A copy of the letter of the competent federation (if any) assigning the association to represent Lebanon in this competition.

4 - A detailed financial statement duly signed, or a copy of the mission account statement for the avenues of expenditure of the last financial contribution given by the Ministry in previous years, if any.

5 - A clearance certificate from the National Social Security Fund.

6 . A certificate of registration with the Ministry of Finance.

The association undertakes, within fifteen days from the end of the activity or competition, to submit a report to the Ministry and the competent federation (if any) containing the full details of the participation in terms of results and behaviors inside and outside the field, and copies of press articles relating to the results, if any.

* Achieving an advanced accomplishment in external representation

1 - If the association achieves, in its Arab, regional, continental or international participations, a prominent presence with respect to youth or scout participations, or advanced results in official sports competitions and activities in which it is assigned by the competent federation to represent Lebanon, and the Ministry receives the mandatory report in this regard and a letter from the competent federation confirming the validity of the information contained in the report, the Minister may issue a decision based on the proposal of the Director General granting the association a financial reward pursuant thereto.

2 - The value of the financial rewards in this case shall be determined through the evaluation of the prominent presence or through the ranks achieved by the associations, pursuant to decisions issued by the Minister based on the proposal of the Director General.

* To construct, complete the construction of, or rehabilitate facilities:

Associations may be granted a financial contribution to construct, complete the construction of, or rehabilitate sports, youth or scout facilities, provided that they submit an application to the Ministry accompanied by:

1 - A certificate proving ownership of the real property, or a lease contract registered with the municipality whose term is not less than fifteen years, or a tolerance agreement authenticated before a notary public whose term is not less than fifteen years.

2 - A comprehensive executive engineering study for the project containing all information relating thereto, including the estimated budget signed by a civil Engineer or architect affiliated with one of the two Orders of Engineers, and a copy of the building permit and maps or an approval from the municipality for the establishment of the facilities.

3 - A written undertaking to commit to maintaining and developing the building or facility periodically, and not to make any change to its intended use during a period of fifteen years from its establishment, completion or rehabilitation.

4 - A copy of the contracting agreements after the commencement of the execution of the project.

5 - A clearance certificate from the National Social Security Fund.

6 - A certificate of registration with the Ministry of Finance.

The aforementioned contribution shall be granted pursuant to an agreement contract signed between the Ministry and the association accompanied by a book of specifications for the execution of the project, and the Ministry shall supervise the proper execution.

* To carry out special activities or programs:

Associations may be granted a financial contribution to carry out special activities or programs outside the scope of official activities or competitions, pursuant to a decision by the Minister based on the proposal of the Director General, and the association must submit a file to the Ministry at least two months prior to the date of the activity or program, including the following:

1 - An application to obtain a financial contribution including a comprehensive and detailed study.

2 - A detailed financial statement of the avenues of expenditure of the last financial contribution given by the Ministry in previous years, if any.

3 - A clearance certificate from the National Social Security Fund.

4 - A certificate of registration with the Ministry of Finance.

5 - A copy of the subscription receipt in the competent federation for the previous year.

The Minister may also, based on the proposal of the Director General, grant associations a financial contribution in order to secure their continuity in performing their developmental role in the fields of sports, youth or scouting in accordance with the requirements of the public interest.

The application for a contribution shall be submitted to the Registry of the Ministry, which shall examine it as to form and refer it to the competent administrative unit, which shall prepare a report on its content and return it within fifteen days at most together with its proposal.

- If the application requires investigations, the competent administrative unit shall have the right to seek clarification from the concerned parties and carry out the necessary investigations to verify the information and data, provided that it completes the same within a time limit not exceeding one month.

- The Registry shall refer the application to the Director General, who shall examine it and refer it, including his proposal, to the Minister.

- The contribution shall be granted by a decision of the Minister upon the proposal of the Director General.

There shall be established in Lebanon the "Lebanese Sports Media Federation", which is an independent private body supported by the State and which derives its laws and bylaws from the laws of the International Sports Press Association and the laws and regulations in force in Lebanon.

Media professionals working in the sports media sector shall form a Founding Board whose mission is to draw up the General Bylaws and submit the licensing application to the Ministry, provided that no media institution is represented by more than one delegate on the Founding Board, and that the licensing application includes:

1 . Three copies of the General Bylaws bearing the signatures of all members of the Founding Board on all pages thereof.

2 . Three copies signed by all members of the Founding Board of lists of the names of the founding members, including the three-part name of each member, his date of birth, his profession, his address including telephone, fax, postal address and electronic mail, and the signature of each of the members.

3 . An individual civil status extract or a copy of the identity card and a judicial record for each member of the Founding Board, which acts in the place of the Administrative Board.

4 . A copy of the minutes of the meeting of the Founding Board signed by all members, including the name of the member of the Founding Board who represents the association vis-à-vis the Government.

5 . A legal occupancy document for the headquarters of the Federation, which shall be either a title deed, a lease contract registered with the municipality, an agreement contract of "acknowledgement of tolerance" notarised before a notary public for a duration of not less than three years, or premises placed by the public administration at the disposal of the Federation establishing its headquarters.

6 . A compact disc containing all the documents mentioned above.

The Ministry shall receive the licensing application and shall verify, within a period of one month at most, that it meets the administrative and technical conditions, and shall then refer it to the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities, which shall express its opinion thereon, stating the reasons in case of non-approval, within a period of two months at most; the Ministry shall issue the licensing decision immediately upon the expiry of this period, failing which its silence shall be deemed a tacit decision of approval.

1 . The Lebanese Sports Media Federation shall be licensed by a decision of the Minister based upon the proposal of the Director General after the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities has expressed its opinion.

2 . The licensing decision shall be published in the Official Gazette at the expense of the founders.

Visual, audio, written and electronic media institutions shall join the Lebanese Sports Media Federation, provided that each institution attaches to the application for joining a list of the media professionals working for it.

The general bylaws of the Federation must include a distribution of the representatives of these institutions in its administrative committee, such that each of the visual, audio, written and electronic media institutions obtains a specified "quota" for each of them.
The bodies concerned with this Decree shall be granted a period of one year from the date of its publication to regularise their status in accordance with its provisions.
The provisions of Decree No. 8990 dated 29/9/2012 are hereby repealed, as are all provisions contrary to the provisions of this Decree or inconsistent with its content.
This Decree shall be published and notified wherever needed.

- The draft law concerning the regulation of licences for medical aesthetic centres, as amended by the Administration and Justice Committee, has been ratified.

- This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

A - Medical aesthetics is a set of medical acts aimed at improving the external appearance of a person, including reducing and delaying the effects of ageing, and for the purposes of this Law it means exclusively:

1 - Hair removal and skin treatments and problems thereof, by various types of rays, in particular by means of LASER and IPL machines.

2 - Hair transplantation in its various techniques.

3 - Therapeutic skin peeling at its medium and deep levels (peeling 2-3

4 - Slimming by means of machines aimed at breaking down fat cells in the body (lipolysis).

5 - Injection of the skin, body and face, in particular for the purpose of removing wrinkles or increasing or reducing volume by means of needles with scientifically permitted substances licensed by the Ministry of Public Health.

6 - Any other medical aesthetic therapeutic acts or methods that may emerge in the future and the performance of which requires specialised medical and scientific skill, provided that such methods shall be determined by virtue of a decision issued by the Minister of Public Health upon the proposal of the Director General of the Ministry after consulting the opinion of the two Orders of Physicians in Lebanon.

B - In the application of the provisions of this Article, the special laws governing the syndicates of health professions shall be observed, in particular Law No. 8/78 dated 20 February 1978 (Regulation of the Profession of Physical Therapy).

A - Medical aesthetic centres are institutions licensed and operating in accordance with the provisions of this Law so as to be permitted to perform any of the medical aesthetic acts specified in Article 1.

B - The use of general or spinal anaesthesia in any of the medical aesthetic centres is prohibited.

A - Private medical aesthetic centres shall be established and managed under a licence issued by the Minister of Public Health upon the proposal of the Director General of the Ministry.

B - The licence shall be issued in the name of the applicant party and shall be recorded in a special public register of medical aesthetic centres in accordance with conditions determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Public Health upon the proposal of the Director General of the Ministry.

C - No other branch of a medical aesthetic centre may be opened under the same licence.

The categories set forth below shall be entitled to submit an application for a licence for a medical aesthetic centre:

A - Physicians licensed to manage a medical aesthetic centre who hold the title of specialist in:

1 - Dermatology.

2 - Plastic surgery.

3 - Otorhinolaryngology surgery.

4 - Maxillofacial reconstructive surgery.

5 - Any specialist subsequently added to the schedule of medical specialties having its relation specified in Article One, by a decision issued by the Minister of Public Health after consulting the two Orders of Physicians in Lebanon.

These physicians shall work full-time in the medical aesthetic centre and may not manage more than one medical aesthetic centre.

6 - Hospitals, provided that they are contracted with a physician licensed in accordance with paragraph (A) above, and the hospital must notify the Ministry immediately in the event of a change of the director.

A - The area of the medical aesthetic centre must not be less than one hundred and fifty square metres, within which the spaces necessary to perform the following tasks are available: receiving patients, conducting examinations and licensed medical aesthetic procedures provided that they are conducted in accordance with scientific standards and separately, sterilisation, and preparation of the materials used, and the necessary sanitary facilities for patients and for the workers in the centre.

B - The technical and health conditions shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Public Health upon the proposal of the Director General of the Ministry.

C - The aesthetic centre must, within the conditions of the licence, conclude a compulsory insurance contract to cover medical risks (Malpractice) resulting from treatments and damages resulting from medical equipment and installations and their use, provided that the value of the coverage is not less than 20 times the annual minimum wage in force at any given time.
The licence holder must notify the Ministry of the date of commencement of work in the private medical aesthetic centre within one month from the date of beginning its work.
The details of application of this Law shall be determined, where necessary, by decrees issued by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Health.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

A - Physicians, persons in charge, and all other staff in private medical cosmetic centres, including technicians and medical assistants, under the supervision and responsibility of the physician holding the licence, shall:

1 - Open a numbered register, or the equivalent thereof in electronic means, in which they shall record all cosmetic procedures they perform, stating the name of the patient, the name of the physician performing the procedure, and its outcome; this register shall be kept at the centre and the legal provisions relating to medical confidentiality shall apply thereto.

2 - Take all necessary measures to protect the persons working in such centres and the patients from any potential harm arising from the types of treatment and from the use of machines, and ensure the proper application of therapeutic protocols and established scientific medical rules.

3 - Comply with the provisions of the Law on Patients' Rights and Informed Consent and the Code of Medical Ethics.

4 - Have physicians attend continuing medical education programmes organised by the two Orders of Physicians, and have the staff of the centre attend appropriate continuing technical studies and training.

B - The Minister of Public Health may urgently close, by a decision issued by him, any centre that poses any danger to public health, and the resumption of work in such centres shall not be authorised until after it has been ascertained that the danger has ceased.

C - The Minister of Public Health shall decide to close any unlicensed cosmetic centre.

D - The Minister of Public Health shall decide to close any cosmetic centre that ceases to fulfil one of the licensing conditions after it has been served notice to regularise its status within a period not exceeding three months.

It shall be prohibited for a medical cosmetic centre and for the physician licensed to manage it to carry out any advertising for the purpose of promotion, publicity, or unfair competition; the centre shall only be permitted to provide information regarding its address, the specialisation of the physician licensed to manage it, and the techniques it uses.

Any person who opens or manages a cosmetic centre without a licence shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to three years and by a fine from ten million to fifty million pounds, or by either of these two penalties.

Existing medical cosmetic centres shall be granted a period of six months to regularise their legal status from the date of publication of this Law, under penalty of compulsory closure by a decision of the Minister of Public Health.

The licence shall be subject to a fiscal stamp duty, the value of which shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Finance and Public Health.
All texts contrary to the provisions of this Law or inconsistent with its content are hereby repealed.
