All lease contracts of built real property concluded prior to 23/7/1992 shall be subject to the provisions of this Law.

The following shall be exempted from the provisions of this Law:

a) Lease contracts of agricultural lands and the buildings appurtenant thereto.

b) Seasonal lease contracts relating to summer and winter resorts.

c) Contracts pursuant to which employers provide premises for the housing of their employees free of charge or for consideration.

d) Occupation of the public domain of the State and municipalities.

e) Lease contracts of villas that meet the following specifications:

That they consist of one or more storeys and are leased for the dwelling of a single tenant and have a garden, a garage, a heating system, and a special system providing hot water even if the tenant bears the expenses of providing the same, provided that these specifications were met on the date of commencement of the original lease.

A debit account for residential leases covered by the provisions of this Law (hereinafter referred to in this Law as the Fund) shall be established within four months from the date of publication of this Law, which shall be attached to the Ministry of Finance and its accounts shall be kept at the Treasury Directorate in the said Ministry.

This Fund aims to assist all tenants concerned by this Law whose average monthly income does not exceed five times the official minimum wage, by contributing to the payment of the increases, wholly or partially as the case may be, that occur to their rents in implementation of the provisions of this Law.

Wherever mentioned in this Law, the tenant shall mean the tenant or whoever has legally succeeded him.

When applying to benefit from the contribution of the Fund, and for the purpose of determining the average monthly family income, the beneficiary or the benefiting party, wherever mentioned in this Law, shall mean the tenant and the legal occupants of the leased premises with him.
A non-Lebanese tenant shall not benefit from the benefits of this Fund.

The revenues of the Fund shall consist of:

- Annual contributions from the State provided for in the budget of the Ministry of Finance to cover the obligations of the Fund.

- Gifts, donations, and bequests after the approval thereof by the Council of Ministers, and the value of such gifts and bequests shall be deducted from the amounts taken as a basis for determining the income tax due, and shall also be deducted from the amounts taken as a basis for determining transfer duties, and shall be exempted from the duties imposed on gifts.

The management of the funds of this Fund, including the rules of expenditure and collection, shall be subject to financial regulations approved by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

A committee of a judicial nature composed in the following manner shall look into the application of the provisions relating to the application of increases to rents:

a - An active judge of at least the third grade or an honorary judge as President, designated by the Minister of Justice.

b - A member designated by the Minister of Finance from among the employees of the Directorate of Revenues at the Ministry of Finance of at least the third category.

c - A member designated by the Minister of Social Affairs from among the employees of the Ministry of at least the third category.

The members of the Committee shall exercise their functions with impartiality and independence from the authority that proposed or designated them.

The employee members of the Committee may not be replaced or dismissed for reasons relating to their work therein even if they are promoted or transferred from their positions that were the reason for their selection.

The dispute shall be submitted to the Committee by both parties pursuant to a joint petition or by the more diligent among them.

The Committee shall have the right to seek the assistance of whomever it wishes and by any means it deems necessary to verify the right of the tenant to request to benefit from the Fund or the accuracy of the assessment of the fair rent.

The decision of the Committee shall be issued by a majority.

Every interested party may take the initiative to request the service of notice of the decision issued by the Committee.

The Committee shall be appointed within a period of two months from the date of entry into force of this Law pursuant to a decree based on the proposal of each of the Ministers of Justice, Finance, and Social Affairs.

At least one committee shall be appointed in each governorate.

A clerk and a bailiff shall be attached to each committee by a decision of the Minister of Justice.

The allowances of each of the President, the members, the clerk, and the bailiff shall be determined by a decree.

The Committee shall hold its meetings during or outside official working hours in the places determined by the Minister of Justice.

A tenant wishing to obtain a contribution from the Fund shall submit an application to the Committee under whose jurisdiction the leased premises fall, exempt from all fees, and the submission of this application shall suspend the time limit for paying the increases to the rent resulting from the implementation of this Law until the decision of the Committee approving or refusing the contribution enters into force.

The application must satisfy the following conditions:

1 - It shall be submitted within a time limit of two months from the date of determination of the fair market rent by mutual consent or by judicial decision in respect of the first extended year, and within the same time limit at the beginning of each of the other extended years, under pain of forfeiture of his right to benefit from the contribution.

However, and subject to the provisions of Article 11 of this Law, the tenant shall be entitled, at any time a modification occurs to his average monthly family income, to submit a new application to the aforementioned Committee for consideration and to take the appropriate decision in light of the modifications that occurred to such income as to maintaining or modifying its previous decision. In the event of modification, the decision of the Committee shall take effect as of the month following the decision.

2 - The following documents shall be attached to the application:

a - A schedule of the names of the members of the beneficiary group.

b - An employment certificate for each of the members of the beneficiary group issued by the competent authority showing the amount of the wage or salary according to the status of each of them as a wage earner, worker, or employee.

c - A personal declaration of income for each of the members of the beneficiary group if he is self-employed.

The Committee shall examine the applications for contribution with respect to the beneficiary's average monthly family income and decide thereon in accordance with the following:

(a) - If the members of the benefiting party are wage earners, workers, or employees, the beneficiary's average monthly family income shall be the sum of the monthly incomes pertaining to each of them.

(b) - If any of the members of the benefiting party is self-employed, it shall be for the Committee to verify, by the means it deems appropriate, his average monthly income, and consequently the beneficiary's average monthly family income shall be equal to the sum of the average monthly incomes pertaining to each of the members of the benefiting party.

It shall be for the Committee, in all cases, to verify by the means it deems appropriate the number and names of the members of the benefiting party and the average monthly income of the lessee and of each of them, whereupon the beneficiary's average monthly family income shall be calculated in accordance with what is set forth in this Article. Either of the two concerned parties may submit evidence and documents that assist in proving his claims.

The Committee may summon both the lessor and the lessee to hear them pursuant to a notice served upon them in accordance with the Code of Civil Procedure, and it must issue its decision within a period not exceeding two months from the date of submission of the application.

Without prejudice to the provisions of both Articles 8 and 11 of this Law, the Committee shall decide, in light of the results of its proceedings regarding the determination of the beneficiary's average monthly family income, on the entitlement or non-entitlement to the application for a contribution from the Fund, as well as on the value of the contribution, in accordance with the following:

1 - If the Committee decides that the beneficiary's average monthly family income exceeds five times the official minimum wage, it shall reject the contribution as not being due, and the tenant shall be required to pay the new rent resulting from the application of the increases provided

for in this Law, under penalty of being deemed in default, whereupon the provisions of this Law shall apply to him.

2 - If the Committee decides that the beneficiary's average monthly family income does not exceed five times the official minimum wage, the President of the Committee shall notify the decision to the Financial Department in the district to which the leased premises belong, and the latter shall pay to the lessor the contribution due in monthly instalments for the extended year, or the remainder thereof as the case may be, for which the tenant submitted the application for a contribution, as set out below:

A - The case where the beneficiary's average monthly family income does not exceed three times the official minimum wage

The Committee shall determine in its decision the value of the monthly instalment such that it is equal monthly to the difference between the value of the rent and the value of the new rent.

The Committee shall notify its decision to the competent Financial Department to take the necessary action in accordance with what is set out in this item.

B - The case where the beneficiary's average monthly family income exceeds three times the official minimum wage and does not exceed five times this minimum.

The Committee shall determine in its decision the value of the monthly instalment such that it is equal monthly to the difference, if any, between 20% of the beneficiary's average monthly family income and the value of the new rent.

The Committee shall notify its decision to the competent Financial Department to take the necessary action in accordance with what is set out in this item.

The contributions that the Fund is required to pay to the lessor shall remain borne by this Fund, and the lessor may not invoke them for any reason and before any authority against the tenant as being a part of the rent not paid by the latter.

In the event that the tenant wishes to continue to benefit from the contribution of the Fund for the subsequent extended years, he must follow the working mechanism referred to in Article 8 above with the Committee, at the beginning of each extended year up to the ninth year inclusively.

The application for contribution as provided for in Article 8 shall lead to the suspension of the time limit for the payment of the increases resulting from the provisions of this Law, until the decision of the Committee approving or disapproving takes effect.

Whoever gives the Committee a false certificate or declaration, or uses or benefits from either of them, shall be prosecuted for the offence of forgery and use of forged documents. Upon the discovery of any false declaration or certificate and its use and benefitting therefrom, the Committee must, as the case may be, notify the Public Prosecution of the matter, and the tenant's right to obtain the contribution from the Fund shall be forfeited.

All disputes examined by the Committee provided for in Article 7 of this Law shall be subject to the summary procedure provided for in Law No. 154 issued on 17/8/2011, regardless of the value of the matter in dispute.

The decisions of the Committee may be appealed before the Court of Appeal within the jurisdiction of which the leased premises are located.

The decisions of the Committee shall be subject to the provisions on expedited enforcement, the time limit for appeal, and stay of execution provided for in Law 154 issued on 17/8/2011.

The decision issued by the Court of Appeal shall not be subject to any form of challenge.

Lease contracts of residential built real properties concluded before 23/7/1992 shall be subject to the provisions of this Title.

A contract entered into in respect of premises intended for residence shall be deemed a residential lease contract, whereas premises leased under a single contract for residence and for non-residence shall be deemed residential premises by the mere fact of their being used for residence.

Lease contracts of residential premises shall be extended for up to nine years, and for beneficiaries of the allowances of the Fund for up to 12 years, from the date of entry into force of this Law, provided that the tenant pays the value of the fair rent gradually in accordance with the following:

a - Subject to the provisions of Article (20) of this Law, the value of the fair rent shall be determined amicably or judicially in accordance with what is provided for in Article (18).

b - The rent due on the date of entry into force of this Law shall be increased annually and successively in accordance with the following:

15% fifteen percent of the value of the increase difference between the rent in force prior to the entry into force of this Law and the fair rent referred to above, for each year of the first four extended years following the date of entry into force of this Law.

20% twenty percent of the value of the increase difference noted above, for each of the fifth and sixth years of the extended period until the rent reaches, in the sixth extended year, the value of the fair rent referred to in Clause (a) above.

c - The rent in the seventh, eighth, and ninth extended years shall be equal to the value of the fair rent referred to in Clause (a) above.

d - By the end of the ninth extended year, the lease shall become free.

1 - A tenant who still meets the conditions for benefiting from the contributions of the Fund shall have the right to request from the landlord in writing, three months prior to the expiry of the term of the contract in the ninth extended year, under penalty of forfeiture of the right, the execution of a new lease contract for a maximum period of three years at a rent equal to the fair market rent referred to in Paragraph (a) of Article 15 above, provided that he proves within the same time limit that he has obtained a decision from the Committee stating that he meets the conditions for benefiting from the contributions of the Fund, in accordance with the mechanism provided for in this Law.

2 - This tenant shall have the right to waive his right to request the execution of a new lease contract and to notify the landlord in writing, within the same time limit mentioned above, of his desire to vacate the leased premises in return for obtaining a financial contribution paid to him by the Fund in monthly instalments, as provided for below.

The landlord shall not have the right to invoke the tenant's written desire to vacate the leased premises unless this tenant has obtained the contribution of the Fund.

3 - In order to obtain the contribution, the tenant must observe the following:

a - The tenant shall submit to the Committee, within the time limit mentioned above, an application to obtain the contribution.

The submission of this application shall not result in the suspension of the time limit for paying the increases to the rent resulting from the implementation of this Law.

b - He shall attach to the application the following documents:

- A copy of the letter notifying the landlord of his desire to waive the lease and vacate the leased premises.

- An undertaking to vacate the leased premises and hand them over vacant to the landlord within a period of three months from the date on which he is notified of the Committee's approval to pay the contribution, during which period he shall continue to pay the rent due from him.

4 - In light of the attached documents, the Committee shall decide on the value of the monthly instalments and their due dates, starting from the first of the month following the actual vacation of the leased premises and the handing over of the keys, evidenced by a written acknowledgment signed by the landlord and the tenant, or by the tenant alone, before a notary public, and until the expiry of the term of the new lease contract.

5 - The Committee shall notify its decision to the Finance Department in the area to which the leased premises belong, whereupon the contribution shall be paid in monthly instalments on their due dates.

6 - The tenant shall have the right to assign these instalments to a financing source of his choice, which in return lends him the value of the contribution as a single lump sum; the loan granted to him shall be deemed a housing loan, and the tenant shall then benefit from the exemptions provided for in Law No. 543 dated 24/7/1996.

7 - If the Committee decides that the tenant does not fulfil the conditions for benefiting from the contributions of the Fund, his lease shall become free from the date of the Committee's decision.

1 - In the event that the tenant vacates the leased premises at his own wish in return for a financial contribution that he obtains from the Fund, if he fulfils the conditions for benefiting from this Fund, the provisions of Article 27 of this Law shall apply.

2 - The tenant may, during the extension period, offer to the owner to purchase the leased premises. The offer shall be submitted before the Notary Public in the district in which the leased premises are located, stating therein the purchase value. If the owner refuses the tenant's offer and then proceeds to agree with a third party on the sale of the leased premises, within a period of one year from the date of the said offer, for a value not exceeding the value offered by the tenant, he shall notify the latter in due form.

3 - Furthermore, the tenant shall have a right of preference to purchase the leased premises at the same price offered to the owner by a third party, and in this respect he shall deposit the price with the Notary Public in due form and notify the owner with a copy of this deposit within a time limit of one month from the date of being notified of the owner's letter, under penalty of forfeiture of his right of preference.

The fair market rent shall be determined:

A - Amicably by agreement between the lessor and the lessee, provided that such rent shall be subject to the decision of the Committee in the event that the lessee applies thereto to obtain a financial contribution from the Fund.

B - If the fair market rent is not determined amicably by agreement between the lessor and the lessee within the first three months following the date of entry into force of this Law, the lessor may follow the following procedures:

1 - The lessor shall engage the assistance of two experts from the list of local experts in the governorate registered with the courts, one of whom shall be a civil engineer or an architect and the second from among those working in real estate appraisal who are registered on the roll of experts.

The two experts shall undertake the drawing up of an appraisal of the fair market rent of the leased premises in accordance with the procedures stipulated in Article (19) of this Law.

2 - The lessor shall, through the notary public, serve the appraisal report of the fair market rent upon the lessee, who must, within two months from being served with the report, either approve it and adopt it in determining the fair market rental value or submit a counter-appraisal report by engaging the assistance of two experts from the list of local experts in the governorate registered with the courts, one of whom shall be a civil engineer or an architect and the second from among those working in real estate appraisal and registered on the roll of experts.

The two experts appointed by the lessee shall undertake the drawing up of an appraisal of the fair market rent of the leased premises in accordance with the procedures stipulated in Article 19 of this Law.

3 - The lessee must serve the appraisal report drawn up by the two experts appointed by him in order to have it served upon the owner through the notary public within the aforementioned two-month time limit, under penalty of forfeiture of his right to object to the appraisal sent by the owner or even to invoke the content of a counter-report.

4 - If the two reports differ, each of the lessor and the lessee may resort to the Committee stipulated in Article 7 of this Law within whose jurisdiction the leased premises are located, in order to adjudicate the dispute arising from the discrepancy, provided that he attaches to his application a copy of the two reports and their enclosures, including copies of the service documents.

The summary procedures referred to in Article 13 of this Law shall apply to this dispute.

The decision issued by the Committee in this regard shall be subject to challenge by way of appeal.

The decision issued by the Court of Appeal shall not be subject to any avenue of challenge.

Under pain of nullity, the report must contain the names of the authors of the report and their reference in the roster of experts, a statement of the party who commissioned them to draw up the report and a statement of the date on which the appraisal was carried out, the means adopted in carrying out the appraisal, from the area of the apartment to the type of building and the estimation of the average building costs (popular, medium to popular, medium to luxury, luxury), and the apartment's share of the area of the property with due regard to the state of the ground floor if the floor is designated for commerce, together with the appraisal of the sale price per square metre in the unencumbered building and the leased building, and a statement of what reduces the value of the average building cost per square metre due to age or misuse, or what increases the value of the building apart from improvements introduced by the tenant and which may result from the location, the view, or otherwise, and the sales or assessments by official administrations upon which the experts relied in estimating the sale price per square metre.

The report and its annexes must bear the signature of the two experts on every page thereof and the date on which the report was drawn up.
The fair rent shall be determined on the basis of a rate of (4%) four per cent of the sale value of the leased premises in their existing condition as if they were vacant.

The experts shall be liable for the content of the report they have drawn up, for the authenticity of the documents annexed thereto, and for the outcome of the appraisal.

For the purposes of applying this Law, the two experts appointed by either the owner or the tenant shall be deemed as if they were appointed by the judiciary.

Subject to the provisions of Article 32 of this Law, if the owner wishes to recover the leased premises for family necessity during the first year of the extension period (the nine years), he shall pay to the tenant compensation equal to five years' rent calculated on the basis of the fair market rent that has been determined.

If, however, the owner wishes to recover the leased premises during the first year of the extension period (the nine years) in order to demolish the building in which the leased premises are located and erect a new building in its place, he shall pay to the tenant compensation equal to six years' rent calculated on the basis of the fair market rent that has been determined, provided that such compensation shall be equal to seven years' rent, calculated on the basis of the fair market rent that has been determined, for a tenant who meets the conditions for benefiting from the contributions of the Fund.

In both aforementioned cases, a tenant who meets the conditions for obtaining a financial contribution from the Fund shall be entitled to submit an application to the Committee to obtain the financial contribution as set out below:

1 - The application shall be submitted accompanied by the following documents:

(a) - A copy of the determination of the fair market rent determined by mutual agreement or judicially.

(b) - A copy of the formal tender and deposit with the Notary Public.

The Committee shall decide, in light of the documents, the amount of the contribution that the Fund would have paid to the lessor on behalf of the tenant from the date the contribution fell due until the end of the extended period, and shall deduct therefrom what the Fund had previously paid to the lessor by way of increases incurred on the rent pursuant to this Law, in addition to the amount of the compensation received by the tenant from the owner in return for the recovery of the leased premises in either of the two cases provided for in this Article, and the Committee shall notify the balance to the competent financial department to be paid to the tenant in equal monthly instalments starting from the first of the month following the date of the actual vacation of the leased premises and until the end of the extended period.

2 - If, however, the leased premises sought to be recovered for family necessity or for demolition were leased under the validity of either of the two Laws 29/67 and 10/74 in buildings that were considered luxury buildings, the compensation due to the tenant shall be reduced by half.

3 - The owner shall pay the compensation to the tenant either directly from himself or by borrowing from any source he chooses, and the loan granted to the owner shall be deemed a housing loan, in which case the owner shall benefit from the exemptions provided for in Law No. 543 dated 24/7/1996.

4 - Non-Lebanese tenants shall be excluded from the compensation.

5 - In the event of an application for the recovery of the leased premises for family necessity during the other extended years, the compensation to which the tenant is entitled shall decrease proportionally with the remaining duration of the extension time limit, that is at the rate of one-ninth (1/9) for each year that has elapsed of the extension period.

If the owner wishes to recover the leased premises in cases other than those of family necessity and demolition, he must observe the following:

1 - Notify the tenant in writing of his preliminary wish to recover the leased premises within a period not exceeding two months from the date on which the fair market rent is determined by mutual consent or judicially in respect of the first extended year, and within the same period at the beginning of each of the remaining extended years.

2 - Obtain the preliminary approval of the tenant in writing to vacate the leased premises in return for compensation the amount of which is agreed upon by the two parties.

In all events, neither the owner nor the tenant may invoke the preliminary approval issued by either of them for any reason whatsoever and before any authority.

3 - The owner shall pay the compensation to the tenant directly from himself or by borrowing from any source he chooses, and the loan granted to the owner shall be deemed a housing loan, in which case the owner shall benefit from the exemptions provided for in Law No. 543 dated 24/7/1996.

4 - The owner must tender and deposit with the Notary Public in the district in which the leased premises are located the amount of compensation agreed upon with the tenant.

In the event that the tenant agrees to the tender and deposit, he must draw up a declaration of approval and an undertaking to vacate the leased premises and deliver them vacant with the keys to the owner within the period agreed upon with the latter, during which the tenant shall continue to pay the rent due, whereupon the Notary Public shall deliver to the tenant 90% of the amount of the tender and deposit in due form, provided that the remaining amount is paid upon completion of the actual vacation of the leased premises and delivery of the keys by a written acknowledgment from both parties or from the tenant alone signed before the Notary Public.

If the tenant fails to vacate within the period referred to above for vacating the leased premises and delivering them vacant to the owner, the tenant shall thereafter become an occupant of the leased premises without lawful justification and shall be subject, for each day of delay, to a non-reducible coercive fine payable to the lessor, equivalent to the rent of five days calculated on the basis of the fair market rent, in which case the lessor shall have the right to request directly from the Head of the Execution Department having jurisdiction over the leased premises to order the vacation pursuant to a petition accompanied by: a copy of each of the agreement drawn up between him and the tenant on vacation, the formal tender and deposit with the Notary Public referred to above, and the receipt for the collection of 90% of the amount of the compensation, and this request shall be subject to the fixed fee.

The decisions of the Head of the Execution Department taken within the framework of the provisions of this paragraph shall not be subject to any avenue of recourse except opposition.

The owner of leased premises leased while either Law 29/67 or 10/74 was in force in buildings that were considered luxury buildings may recover the leased premises in cases other than those of family necessity and demolition in return for paying to the tenant compensation equal to half the compensation due in the case of demolition and provided for in item 2 of Article 22 above, and in such case the provisions of the said Article with respect to the proportional decrease of the compensation in accordance with the remaining duration of the extension period shall not apply.

Subject to the provisions of Articles 22, 23 and 24 of this Law, the owner shall, in all cases of recovery provided for in this Law, tender and deposit with the notary public in the district in which the leased premises are located the compensation determined under this Law or agreed upon amicably with the tenant, with a clear indication of its proportional decrease in accordance with the remaining extension period pursuant to the provisions of paragraph 5 of Article 22 above.

The applicant for recovery shall attach to the tender and deposit proof of the determination of the fair rent amicably or judicially.

In the event that the tenant agrees to the tender and deposit, he shall follow the procedures provided for in item 4 of Article 23, whereupon the notary public shall deliver to the tenant 90% of the value of the tender and deposit in accordance with the rules, provided that the remaining value is paid upon completion of the actual vacation proven by a written acknowledgment by the owner and the tenant or by the tenant alone signed before the notary public.

A tenant who has received the amount of 90% of the value of the tender and deposit referred to in Article 25 above shall have a period of six months from the date of his receipt of the said amount to vacate the leased premises, during which he shall continue to pay the rent due and after which he shall become an occupant of the leased premises without lawful justification, and shall be subject, for each day of delay, to a non-reducible coercive fine payable to the lessor, equivalent to the rent of (5) five days calculated on the basis of the fair rent.

1- During the extended period that is the subject of Clause 1 of Article 15 of this Law, if the tenant who fulfils the conditions for obtaining a financial contribution from the Fund wishes to waive his tenancy, vacate the leased premises, and deliver them vacant to the owner in return for obtaining a financial contribution paid to him by the Fund in monthly instalments as provided for in this Law, he must notify the owner in writing of this wish within a period not exceeding two months from the date of determining the fair market rent by mutual consent or judicially with respect to the first extended year, and within the same period at the beginning of each of the other extended years.

The owner may not invoke the tenant's written wish to vacate the leased premises unless this tenant has obtained the contribution of the Fund.

2 - For the purpose of calculating the value of the contribution, the calculation of the average monthly family income of the beneficiary shall be limited to the sum of the two average monthly incomes of the husband and wife only, to the exclusion of the remaining members of the beneficiary group. However, in the event of the death of the tenant and his spouse, the calculation of the average monthly family income of the beneficiary group shall be limited to the lawful occupants of the leased premises determined in accordance with the provisions of Article 29 of this Law.

3 - The value of the contribution paid in monthly instalments as mentioned in this Law shall be equal to the balance of the total monthly contributions that the Fund would have paid to the lessor on behalf of the tenant as provided for in Article 10 et seq. of this Law had the latter continued to occupy the leased premises, from the due date of the contribution until the end of the extended period that is the subject of Clause 1 of Article 15 of this Law, and the three new years that are the subject of Paragraph 1 of Article 16 of this Law.

4 - Subject to the provisions of Article 10 of this Law, the value of the monthly instalment in each year of the extended years and the three new years shall be equal to the monthly contribution that the Fund would have paid to the owner on behalf of the tenant in settlement of the annual increase accruing to the rent pursuant to this Law.

5 - To obtain the contribution, the tenant must follow the following:

a - The tenant shall submit to the Committee an application to obtain the contribution, exempt from all fees, and the submission of this application shall not result in suspending the time limit for paying the increases on the rent resulting from the implementation of this Law.

b - The application must fulfil the following conditions:

b - 1 - It shall be submitted within a period not exceeding two months from the date of notifying the owner of his wish to waive the tenancy and vacate the leased premises.

b - 2 - The following documents shall be attached to the application:

- A copy of the lease contract or any document proving the tenancy.

- A copy of the determination of the fair market rent by mutual consent or judicially.

- A copy of the letter notifying the owner of his wish to waive the tenancy and vacate the leased premises.

- An undertaking to vacate the leased premises and deliver them vacant to the owner within a period of three months from the date of being notified of the Committee's approval to pay the contribution, during which period he shall continue to pay the amount of rent due from him.

6 - In light of the attached documents, the Committee shall decide on the value of the monthly instalments and their due dates starting from the first of the month following the actual vacation of the leased premises and the delivery of the keys, evidenced by a written acknowledgment signed by the owner and the tenant or by the tenant alone before the Notary Public, and until the end of the extension period provided for in Clause (a) of Article 15 of this Law.

7 - The Committee shall notify its decision to the Finance Department in the district to which the leased premises belong, whereupon the contribution shall be paid in monthly instalments on their due dates.

8 - The tenant shall have the right to assign these instalments to a financing source of his choice that lends him in return the value of the contribution in a single lump sum, and the loan granted to him shall be deemed a housing loan, whereupon the tenant shall benefit from the exemptions provided for in Law No. 543/96 dated 24/07/1996.

Without prejudice to the legal provisions relating to financial matters that require the presentation of a fiscal or municipal clearance certificate, the payment of the contribution to the owner or to the tenant may not in any case be made conditional upon the requirement to present a fiscal or municipal clearance certificate.

In the event of the death of the tenant or his vacating the leased premises, the following shall replace him ipso jure in benefiting from the original lease contract, or the extended lease contract where applicable, with all its latest terms or those amended by operation of law:

1 - The spouse of the tenant

2 - The children of the original tenant who entered the leased premises with him at the commencement of the execution of the lease and his children who were born after the commencement of the execution of the lease and who have continued to occupy the leased premises without interruption.

3 - The relatives of the original tenant who entered the leased premises with him at the commencement of the execution of the lease and who have continued to occupy it without interruption.

Judicial proceedings for the enforcement of eviction and all matters branching therefrom shall be subject to the fixed fee.

Transactions shall be exempted from any proportional fee and from the stamp duty on all notary public procedures relating to valuations and their notification, formal notices, or tender and deposit.

The tenant may not assign the leased premises or sublet them in whole or in part except with the written consent of the owner and under the conditions agreed upon.

If the original tenant assigns the leased premises and was expressly authorised to do so in the original lease contract or the lease contract extended by operation of law, the assignees shall benefit from the statutory extension and shall replace the original tenant, and their relationship shall become direct with the owner.

In the event of total or partial subletting with the express permission of the owner in the original or extended contract, the tenancy relationship shall remain confined between the owner and the original tenant, and the term of the sublease shall expire upon the expiry of the term of the original lease.

Subleases concluded as of 23/7/1992 shall be subject to freedom of contract in accordance with the provisions of Law No. 159/92.

The owner and the original tenant must request the joinder of the subtenant in every action brought against the original tenant, so that the judgment rendered against the original tenant may have the force of res judicata against the subtenant, provided that the subtenant shall have the right to claim compensation from the original tenant in the event that bad faith, fault, or negligence on the part of the latter is established.

a) Subject to the provisions of Article 22 of this Law, the owner may request, for the purpose of his residence or the residence of one of his children, the recovery of the residential leased premises, provided that he proves a family necessity compelling him to recover it, and that neither he nor the person for whose benefit the recovery is requested owns another dwelling that is suitable and fit for habitation, unoccupied, and equivalent in its standard to the leased premises sought to be recovered within the same municipal area or an adjacent municipal area.

And the owner may request the recovery of leased premises contiguous to the dwelling in which he resides, whether such contiguity is horizontal or vertical, if the purpose of the recovery is to annex the recovered leased premises to his residence and make it a dwelling meeting the needs of the family.

Any person who owns at least three-quarters of the shares of the leased real property, and the owner who obtains the written consent of his co-owners in common to secure this majority, shall benefit from these provisions.

b) The owner who is the proprietor of a hospital, an educational, instructional or charitable institution, or an orphanage, a part of whose real property or contiguous real properties is leased for residence, may recover this part, provided that he adds it to the principal property and uses it for the purposes of the institution.

c) The owner may request the recovery of the leased premises for the purpose of demolishing the building in which the leased premises are located and erecting a new building in its place. And he may, for the purpose of erecting one or more floors, request the recovery of the structure standing on the roof if this structure occupies less than half of the area permitted by the Building Law.

The owner must, in such a case, institute a single recovery action against all the tenants, and he must prove that the real property on which a new building is intended to be constructed is buildable according to the Building Law and the requirements of urban planning.

d) The provisions of this Law shall apply to pending recovery actions in which no final and binding decision has been issued prior to the date of entry into force of this Law.

An owner who has recovered his leased premises pursuant to the provisions of Article 22 of this Law shall be obliged to pay to the tenant additional compensation equal to half the value of the compensation that he paid to the tenant, without the tenant being obliged to prove the damage that he suffered, in the two cases set forth below:

1 - If the leased premises were recovered in accordance with either of the two purposes provided for in paragraphs (a) and (b) of Article (32) of this Law and the owner did not use them, without lawful justification, in accordance with the required purpose within a period of one year from the date of eviction, or did not continue, without lawful justification, to use them in that manner for at least three years.

2 - If the leased premises were recovered for demolition and reconstruction in accordance with the purpose provided for in paragraph (c) of Article (32) of this Law and the owner did not commence construction, without lawful justification, within a period of eighteen months from the date of eviction of the last tenant and did not complete it within a period not exceeding five years from the date of commencement of work without lawful justification, or if he used the recovered leased premises for his residence or for his personal benefit or leased them to a third party during the period of one year set forth above.

A tenant subject to the provisions of this Law who acquires ownership of the dwelling he occupies shall be exempted:

1 - From conveyance, mortgage, and mortgage discharge fees relating to the dwelling he occupies.

2 - From the stamp duty due on contracts, documents, and transactions drawn up on the occasion of the purchase of the said dwelling.

3 - From the built property tax due on the said dwelling for a period of ten years following the date of purchase.

In such case, the owner shall also recover all statutory fees due on the building subdivision transaction, and the stamp duty on all transactions and contracts he executes for this purpose, provided that he submits to the Ministry of Finance, within a period of three months from the date of completion of this transaction, the documents proving the sale of the dwelling to its occupant. Provided that the recovery ratio shall be equivalent to the ratio of the residential units he sells out of those that have been subdivided.

A tenant who vacates the leased premises during the extended period in accordance with the provisions of this Law shall benefit from the exemptions provided for in the preceding Article, with respect to the dwelling of which he acquires ownership.

Subject to the dates set for the liberalisation of lease contracts provided for in Article (15) of this Law, priority in the granting of housing loans by both the Housing Bank and the Public Corporation for Housing shall be given to tenants subject to its provisions.

During this period, rents shall be indexed as of the date of entry into force of this Law and shall be increased annually at a rate equivalent to the annual inflation rate according to the official index issued by the Central Administration of Statistics in the preceding year, provided that the increase shall not exceed five percent (5%)

In the event of the death of the lessee or his vacating the leased premises, the following shall benefit from the extension:

1 - The heirs of the lessee up to the third degree, or some of them as agreed among themselves.

2 - The partners of the lessee whose partnership is established as of the date of the lease contract or a prior date.3  The beneficiaries of the provisions of Article 5 et seq. of Legislative Decree No. 11/1967 (relating to the business concern).

In this case, the lease of the premises designated for operating the business concern shall be extended and shall be transferred to the person to whom the said business concern is transferred.

Premises leased for the purposes enumerated in Articles 6, 7 and 8 of the Code of Land Commerce shall be deemed commercial or industrial.

Second: With respect to premises leased for the practice of a liberal profession regulated by law:

1 - The heirs of the lessee, or some of them as agreed among themselves, provided that the heir practices any liberal profession regulated by law.

2 - Anyone to whom the leased premises have devolved by way of assignment from the lessee or from his heirs, provided that the assignee practices any liberal profession regulated by law, and provided that, in the event of the death of the lessee, the assignment takes place within a period not exceeding two years from the date of death.

If the leased premises are occupied by more than one person practicing a liberal profession and one of them dies and none of his heirs practices the very same profession, his partners shall replace him in the lease under the same conditions of the contract, in return for compensation to the heirs equivalent to ten times the deceased's share in the annual rent in force on the date of death.

Whereas, in the event that the partner-lessee vacates the leased premises for any reason whatsoever, his partners shall replace him under the very same conditions of the contract.

Third: With respect to other premises:

1 - The spouse, ascendants and descendants of the lessee, or some of them as agreed among themselves, provided that they practice the very same profession.

2 - The partners of the lessee whose partnership is established as of the date of the lease contract or a prior date.

3 - Anyone to whom the leased premises have devolved by way of assignment from the lessee or from the heirs mentioned in paragraph (1) above, provided that the assignee practices the very same profession, and provided that, in the event of the death of the lessee, the assignment takes place officially before a notary public within a period not exceeding one year from the date of death.

All persons benefiting from the extension pursuant to the provisions of this Article shall be deemed jointly and severally liable towards the lessor in performing their obligations.

The right to extension shall be forfeited and the tenant shall be ordered to vacate in the following cases:

A - If he does not pay the rent that has fallen due on him within two months after being served in person, or through an adult member of his family residing with him, with a formal notice addressed to him by means of a registered open postcard with acknowledgment of receipt, or by means of a letter through a Notary Public, or by means of a formal notice issued by the Execution Department in accordance with the provisions of Article (51) of this Law.

As for a legal person, it must, within a period of two months from the date of entry into force of this Law, elect a domicile; otherwise, the rules of service provided for in the Code of Civil Procedure shall apply to it.

Where it proves impossible to effect the services referred to in the preceding paragraph, service shall be effected by publication in two local daily newspapers designated by the Judge of Urgent Matters after verifying the impossibility of service, upon the request of the lessor by way of a petition that shall not be subject to any fee or stamp of any kind whatsoever, and a copy of the formal notice shall be affixed to the door of the leased premises by a process server, and the two-month period shall run from the date of completion of the last formality of publication or affixation.

Where it proves impossible to effect service of the formal notice issued by the Execution Department, service shall be effected by publication and affixation in accordance with the same rules pursuant to a decision taken by the Head of the Execution Department.

The tenant shall bear the expenses of these formalities.

B - If the tenant misuses the leased premises by causing damage therein not arising from normal use, or uses them or permits them to be used in a manner inconsistent with the terms of the contract without the written consent of the lessor.

The practice by a tenant who is a liberal professional of his profession in a part of the leased premises designated for his residence, for security reasons that compelled him to leave the premises where he practices his profession, shall not be deemed a misuse of the leased premises; in this case, the owner shall not be entitled to claim any compensation from the tenant, nor may the tenant claim any additional compensation therefor from the owner in cases of recovery.

Installations erected by the tenant at his own expense shall not be deemed a misuse of the leased premises, provided that they do not impair the structural soundness of the building. Works for installing an elevator and a water tank, or providing heating, cooling, or hot water, shall be deemed of this nature. Likewise, works relating to the rehabilitation of the leased premises or the entrances of the building that are necessary for the needs of a disabled person residing therein, in accordance with the minimum standards for buildings and facilities pursuant to the Law relating to the Rights of Disabled Persons, shall not be deemed a misuse of the leased premises, provided that such works are technically feasible and do not impair the structural soundness of the building.

With the exception of simple superficial decoration and interior design works and the installation of individual cooling and heating units, a tenant who wishes to benefit from the provisions of this Article must summon the lessor before the Judge of Urgent Matters to seek permission to carry out the works he wishes to perform, which he must specify in order to enable the court to assess their legality and appropriateness.

The tenant must take out insurance, the costs of which he alone shall bear, against all risks that may result from the works he undertakes, as well as the expenses of the aforementioned works and the expenses of restoring the parts of the building that may have been damaged as a result of the works to their former condition, without having any right of recourse against the owner to claim the same or any part thereof, whether during his occupancy of the leased premises or on the date of termination of such occupancy.

The value of improvements resulting from the works mentioned in this paragraph shall not be included in the calculation of the recovery compensation.

C - If he assigns the leased premises or sublets them in whole or in part without the written consent of the lessor, in which case the subtenant or assignee must be joined in the proceedings.

D - If the tenant constructs a building for residence, or one becomes vacant for him, or he acquires a vacant building of which he owns at least three-quarters and which is fit and suitable for his residence and equivalent to the standard of the leased premises he occupies in the same city or village, or in a location not more than ten kilometers away from the leased premises in a radial line.

In these cases, the husband, the wife, the minor children residing with the tenant, as well as the adult children of the tenant who are dependent on him, shall be deemed as a single person for the application of the provisions of this paragraph, unless the condition of family necessity provided for in Paragraph (A) of Article 32 of this Law is met with respect to the situation of the children, subject to actual residence within a period not exceeding one year from the date of completion of the construction, acquisition, or vacancy, and continued residence for a period of at least three years.

Excluded from the provisions of this paragraph is the case where the tenant, or whoever is deemed with him as a single person, acquires an apartment to use it as a commercial or tourist office or to practice a profession, and actually uses it for this purpose within six months from the date of acquisition and continues in the same use for a period of at least three years.

E - If he abandons the leased premises for an uninterrupted period of one year, notwithstanding his continued payment of the rent.

Lebanese officials and employees serving in official Lebanese missions abroad shall be excluded from the provisions of this item.

F - If he abandons the leased premises for an uninterrupted period of six months while owing any part of the rent and having no domicile known to the owner at which he may be served with the formal notice to pay, or having failed to elect a domicile in Lebanon at which he may be served with such formal notice, designated by him to the lessor by means of a letter or a registered open postcard with acknowledgment of receipt in accordance with the rules of service provided for in Paragraph (A) of this Article.

G - If a non-Lebanese tenant does not actually occupy the leased premises for an uninterrupted period of six months, notwithstanding his payment of the rent.

Common expenses referred to in this Law shall mean:

1 - Expenses of common services, which are:

a - Expenses for the consumption or generation of electric current pertaining to the concierge's quarters, the lift and all other common parts in a subdivided building and what is deemed as such in an unsubdivided building.

b - Expenses for the supply of cold water, including that extracted from artesian wells, hot water, heating and cooling.

c - The wage of the concierge equivalent to the minimum wage, in addition to increases including step increments, allowances, legal indemnities, contributions owed to the National Social Security Fund and end-of-service indemnity. Housing allowance shall not be included in the calculation of the wage.

2 - Maintenance expenses, which are:

Expenses for the maintenance of the building, whitewashing, painting and repairs relating to water supply, cooling and heating installations and their common extensions, and to the lift and its insurance with an insurance company.

3 - Re-equipping expenses, which are:

Expenses for re-equipping the building with machinery and equipment that provide the common services; expenses for renovating the exterior appearance of the building and the common parts or what is deemed as such shall be deemed re-equipping expenses.

Unless there is an agreement requiring the tenant to bear all common expenses, the owner shall bear a rate of 20% (twenty per cent) of the expenses of common services and maintenance, provided that his contribution does not exceed 5% (five per cent) of the total rent of the premises that benefit from these services, and the remainder shall be apportioned among the units of which the building is composed, whether vacant or occupied by the owner or by any other person.

The expenses of renovating the exterior appearance of the building and the common parts, or whatever is treated as such, shall be incurred if the competent authority imposes the carrying out thereof.

The lessor shall not be entitled to refrain from providing the common services which he has been accustomed to providing and which were originally agreed upon in the lease contract.

If these services include heating, cooling, or hot water, the lessor must provide sufficient heating on a regular basis from 15 November until 31 March of the following year, and cooling from the first of June until 15 October of the same year.

As for hot water, he must provide it throughout all the days of the year, all of the foregoing unless there is a contrary agreement in the contract.

If the owner fails to perform, without a legitimate justification, all or some of the services agreed upon or legally due, the tenant shall be entitled, after verification thereof through an expert appointed by the judge of urgent matters without levying any fee, to compensation equal to two months' rent, provided that the total compensation awarded, in a single rental year, does not exceed four months' rent.

Sole Article:

- The urgent draft law transmitted by Decree 883 dated 14/6/2017 relating to the Law on the Election of Members of the Chamber of Deputies, as amended by the General Assembly of the Chamber of Deputies, is hereby ratified.

- This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette, with its promulgation expedited in accordance with the first paragraph of Article /56/ of the Constitution.

On the Voting System and the Number of Deputies:

The Chamber of Deputies shall be composed of one hundred and twenty-eight members whose term of office shall be four years, elected on the basis of the proportional system, and voting shall be universal, secret, and in a single round.

On Parliamentary Seats and Electoral Constituencies:

A - The number of parliamentary seats and their distribution among the sects according to the electoral constituencies shall be determined in accordance with the table attached to this Law (Annex No. 1), and candidacy for these seats shall be conducted on the basis thereof, and the table shall be deemed an integral part of this Law.

B - All voters in the electoral constituency, regardless of their different sects, shall vote for the candidates for that constituency.

On the Right to Vote:

Every Lebanese man or woman who has completed the age specified in the Constitution, whether resident or non-resident on Lebanese territory, enjoying his or her civil and political rights and not subject to any of the cases of disqualification provided for in this Law, shall be entitled to exercise his or her right to vote.

On Deprivation of the Right to Vote:

The following shall be deprived of exercising the right to vote:

1 - Persons sentenced to deprivation of civil rights.

2 - Persons sentenced to perpetual deprivation of public ranks and offices.

3 - Persons deprived of their ranks and offices for a fixed term, until the expiration thereof.

4 - Persons convicted of a felony.

5 - Persons convicted of one of the following infamous misdemeanours: theft, fraud, breach of trust, embezzlement, bribery, perjury, rape, intimidation, forgery, use of forged documents, false testimony, offences against public morals provided for in Title VII of the Penal Code, and offences relating to the cultivation, manufacture, and trafficking of narcotic substances.

6 - Persons placed under judicial interdiction throughout the duration of such interdiction.

7 - Persons declared fraudulently bankrupt, or those sentenced to the penalties provided for in Articles 689 to 698 of the Penal Code.

8 - Persons sentenced to the penalties provided for in Articles 329 to 334 of the Penal Code.

The persons set forth above shall not recover the right to vote until after their rehabilitation.

On the voting and candidacy of a naturalised person:

A person naturalised as Lebanese may not vote or stand as a candidate in the elections except after the lapse of ten years from the execution of his naturalisation decree, and this Article shall not apply to a foreign woman who becomes Lebanese by her marriage to a Lebanese man.

On the voting of military personnel:

Non-retired military personnel of various ranks shall not take part in voting, whether they are from the Army or from the Internal Security Forces, General Security, State Security, the Chamber of Deputies Police, the Customs Police, and those having the same status.

On the right of candidacy for membership of the Chamber of Deputies:

No person may stand as a candidate for membership of the Chamber of Deputies unless he is Lebanese, has completed twenty-five years of age, is registered on the list of voters, and enjoys his civil and political rights.

On the Electoral Supervisory Commission:

A permanent commission shall be established under the name of the "Electoral Supervisory Commission", hereinafter referred to as "the Commission".

The Commission shall exercise supervision over the elections in accordance with the functions assigned to it in this Law independently and in coordination with the Minister of Interior and Municipalities, hereinafter referred to as "the Minister".

The Minister shall follow up on the work of the Commission, designate its seat, provide it with a separate and independent seat, and attend its meetings when necessary, without participating in voting.

On the composition of the Commission:

1- The Commission shall be composed of eleven members as follows:

a- A retired judicial judge holding the honorary rank of the judiciary who has exercised judicial functions for a period of at least 20 years, chosen from among three names nominated by the Supreme Judicial Council.

b- A retired administrative judge holding the honorary rank of the judiciary who has exercised judicial functions for a period of at least 20 years, chosen from among three names nominated by the Bureau of the State Council.

c- A retired financial judge holding the honorary rank of the judiciary who has exercised judicial functions for a period of at least 20 years, chosen from among three names nominated by the Council of the Court of Accounts.

d- A former President of the Bar Association chosen from among three former Presidents nominated by the Council of the Beirut Bar Association (as a member).

e- A former President of the Bar Association chosen from among three former Presidents nominated by the Council of the Tripoli Bar Association (as a member).

f- A representative of the Press Syndicate chosen from among three nominated by the Council of the Syndicate (as a member).

g- An expert in media and advertising affairs chosen from among three nominated by the National Council for Audio-Visual Media (as a member).

h - A former President of the Syndicate of Certified Public Accountants chosen from among three nominated by the Syndicate (as a member).

i - Two members of extensive experience in disciplines related to elections (including the administration, financing, or advertising related thereto) from among 6 names nominated by the Minister.

j - A representative of civil society organisations that meet the conditions set forth in Article 20 of this Law, chosen from among three persons of experience in elections nominated by these organisations in accordance with a mechanism established by the Minister.

2- Representation of both sexes shall be taken into account in choosing the candidates for membership of the Commission.

3- The Commission shall be chaired by the judge of the highest grade between the judicial and administrative judges, and in the event of equality in grade, by the eldest, and the elder of the two former Presidents of the Bar Association shall be ex officio Vice-President.

The bodies referred to in this Article shall designate the candidates on their part within a time limit of one month from the date of being notified of the request to submit the names.

If the designation of a candidate from a specific category is impossible or delayed, the Council of Ministers shall, upon the proposal of the Minister, appoint a substitute therefor from the said category.

On ineligibility for candidacy:

1- The persons mentioned below may not run for candidacy during the term of performance of their duties or offices, and during the periods following the date of termination of their services or the date of acceptance of their resignations, in accordance with the following:

a- Members of the Constitutional Council and judges of all categories and grades, whether in the judicial, administrative, financial, Sharia, sectarian, or spiritual judiciary, unless they submit their resignations and effectively cease their office at least two years prior to the date of expiry of the term of the Chamber.

b- Civil servants of the First and Second Categories, unless they submit their resignations and effectively cease their office at least six months prior to the date of expiry of the term of the Chamber of Deputies.

c- Military personnel of all ranks, whether from the Army, the Internal Security Forces, General Security, State Security, Customs Police, the Chamber of Deputies Police, and those of equivalent status, may not run for membership of the Chamber of Deputies except after being referred to retirement or submitting their resignation and having it accepted at least six months prior to the date of expiry of the term of the Chamber of Deputies.

d- Full-time chairpersons and members of boards of directors in public institutions, public bodies, mixed-economy companies, companies with public capital, and institutions of public law, and their directors general, unless they submit their resignations and effectively cease their duties at least six months prior to the date of expiry of the term of the Chamber of Deputies.

e- Presidents and vice-presidents of municipal councils and presidents of federations of municipalities, unless they submit their resignations in accordance with the provisions of the Municipalities Law and effectively cease their duties at least two years prior to the date of expiry of the term of the Chamber of Deputies.

Exceptionally and for one time only, presidents of municipal councils and presidents of federations of municipalities wishing to run for the parliamentary elections must submit their resignation from the presidency and membership within thirty days from the date of publication of the Law in the Official Gazette.

f- The President, Vice-President, and members of the Supervisory Commission for Elections.

2- Notwithstanding any other text, the resignation for the reasons mentioned above shall be deemed accepted by operation of law from the date of its submission to the competent authority and the effective cessation of work by the persons concerned.

3- Members of the teaching staff on the permanent establishment of the Lebanese University, or working full-time thereat, or contracted therewith, shall be exempted from the provisions of this Article.

On Incompatibility:

A- It shall not be permissible to combine membership, presidency, or vice-presidency of the Commission with the presidency or membership of the Council of Ministers or the Chamber of Deputies, the presidency or membership of the board of directors of a public institution, the presidency or membership of a municipal council, or any office of a public nature, with the exception of members of the teaching staff in the cadre of the Lebanese University or those employed full-time thereby or contracted therewith, in addition to the cases of incompatibility set forth in Paragraphs D and E of Article 8 of this Law and in the second paragraph of Article 109 of this Law.

B - The President of the Commission, his Vice-President, and the members of the Commission are prohibited from running as candidates in municipal or mukhtar elections during their term of office and the year following the expiration of the term.

C - If any of the persons mentioned in Paragraph (A) above is appointed as a member of the Commission, he must choose within a period of two weeks between the membership and his office, failing which he shall be deemed to have resigned ipso jure from the membership of the Commission.

On Prohibited Acts:

The President and members of the Commission shall not, during their term of office, undertake any work or activity that conflicts with the functions and neutrality of the Commission.

The President and members shall be bound, throughout the period of the Commission's work, by the obligation to refrain from delivering any lecture, participating in any seminar, or making any statement in a personal capacity the subject of which relates to the elections, except by authorization from the Commission.

The Commission shall decide to revoke the membership of a member in the event that he violates the obligations provided for in this Law, by a two-thirds majority of the members of the Commission, with due observance of the adversarial principle and the right of defense in accordance with the provisions of its rules of procedure, provided that the decision of the Commission is coupled with the approval of the Council of Ministers.

Exceptionally and for one time only, for the purpose of holding the parliamentary elections after the promulgation of this Law exclusively, namely Law Enacted by Operation of Law No. 8 dated 3/11/2021

On the Appointment of the Commission and its Term of Office

The members shall be appointed by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister, and the term of office of the Commission shall be one year from the date of appointment.

The Council of Ministers shall appoint the members of the Commission six months prior to the expiry of the term of the Chamber.

The incumbent Commission shall continue to carry out its duties until a new Commission is appointed.

On Vacancy:

In the event that the seat of any member becomes vacant for any reason, the Commission shall declare the vacancy and the President of the Commission shall notify the "Minister" of the matter within one week to take note and to take the necessary measures to appoint the replacement.

The replacement member shall be appointed within a maximum period of fifteen days from the date of taking note, in the same manner in which the original member was appointed and for the remainder of his term of office.

On the Oath:

Before assuming their duties, the members of the Commission shall take, before the President of the Republic, within a maximum period of fifteen days from the date of their appointment, the following oath:

"I swear by Almighty God to perform my work in the Supervisory Commission for Elections with all honesty, impartiality, devotion and independence, and to ensure absolute compliance with the laws and regulations, particularly those governing the elections, so as to guarantee their freedom, integrity and transparency."

On the Rules of Procedure:

The Commission shall prepare and amend its rules of procedure, which shall include the rules and procedures governing the conduct of its work in implementation of the provisions of this Law. Such rules of procedure and any amendment thereto shall be approved by a decision adopted by the Council of Ministers within a period of fifteen days from the date of their filing with the General Secretariat of the Council of Ministers.

On Criminal Prosecution:

No criminal action may be instituted against one of the members, nor may any criminal measure be taken against him, nor may he be arrested throughout the duration of his term of office for acts relating to his work on the Commission, without authorization from the Commission. Likewise, no decision for pre-trial detention may be taken against members of the Commission for acts not relating to their work on the Commission, except in cases of flagrante delicto.

The Minister of Justice shall submit the request for authorization to prosecute or to take the appropriate legal measure on the basis of a memorandum from the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation comprising the nature of the act, the time and place of its commission, and a summary of the evidence that justifies prosecution and the taking of the necessary criminal measures.

The request for authorization to prosecute shall be submitted to the Minister, and the Commission shall be convened within a period of one week to examine and decide upon the request after hearing the member concerned, without his participating in the vote, and the Commission shall issue its decision regarding prosecution by an absolute majority within a similar period and refer it to the Minister.

On the Compensation of the Commission:

The President of the Commission shall receive a monthly compensation, throughout the duration of his term of office, to be determined in the decree establishing the Commission, provided that he abstains from any other work. As for all the other members of the Commission, they shall abstain from any other work during the electoral process and shall receive a lump-sum allowance during this period to be determined in the decree establishing the Commission.

On the Functions of the Commission:

The Commission shall assume the following functions and powers:

1 - Issuing the decisions and circulars that fall within its functions and submitting the proposals it deems appropriate to the Minister.

2 - Receiving the applications of the audiovisual, print and electronic media outlets wishing to participate in covering the polling and counting process, delivering to them the permits necessary therefor, and laying down a code of conduct for media coverage.

3 - Receiving the applications of the private print, visual and audio media outlets wishing to participate in paid electoral advertising in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

4 - Monitoring the compliance of lists, candidates and the various media outlets with the laws and regulations governing electoral competition in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

5 - Determining the conditions and rules for conducting opinion polls as well as publishing, broadcasting or distributing the results during the electoral campaign, and monitoring compliance with the electoral silence period.

6 - Receiving the financial statements relating to the electoral campaigns and auditing them within a time limit of one month from the date of holding the elections.

7 - Receiving the applications for registering the financial delegates for the electoral campaign of each candidate and delivering to him a receipt therefor.

8 - Exercising oversight over electoral expenditure in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

9 - Accepting and examining the applications of local and international election observers, granting them permits and laying down a code of conduct for them.

10- Spreading electoral culture, guiding voters and strengthening democratic practice by all available means.

11- Receiving complaints in matters relating to its functions and adjudicating thereon, and it may act of its own motion upon ascertaining any violation and take the necessary action in respect thereof.

12- The Commission may, where necessary, seek the assistance of persons of recognised expertise in the disciplines connected with elections and their affairs.

The Commission shall submit a report on its work upon the expiry of its term of office and shall refer it to each of the Presidency of the Republic, the Presidency of the Chamber of Deputies, the Presidency of the Council of Ministers, the Minister of Interior and Municipalities and the Presidency of the Constitutional Council.

This report shall be published in the Official Gazette.

On monitoring the elections:

A- Relevant civil society bodies shall have the right, under the supervision of the Commission, to accompany the elections and monitor their course, provided that they cumulatively satisfy the following conditions:

- That the association be a non-political Lebanese association holding a receipt of notification and acknowledgment for at least two years prior to the date of submitting the application to the Commission.

- That it not be linked to any political side or party, and that neither its general assembly nor its administrative board include any candidate for the elections.

- That its articles of association provide, for at least two years, for objectives linked to democracy, human rights, elections, transparency, or training on such subjects.

- That it disclose its sources of funding to the Commission.

- That it deposit with the Commission its final statement of accounts specific to its election monitoring activity within a time limit of one month at most after the end of the electoral process.

- That the number of members affiliated with the association, in accordance with the lists duly deposited with the competent official authorities, amount to at least one hundred members on the date of submitting the application.

- That its administrative board commit to a code of honour established by the Commission.

The Commission shall examine the accreditation applications received by it and verify the fulfilment of the above conditions, and it rests with it to accept or reject the application.

The Commission shall determine the procedures and mechanisms for accompanying the elections and monitoring their course by decisions issued by it at least one month prior to the date of the elections.

B- The Commission shall examine the applications of foreign bodies concerned with elections seeking to participate in accompanying the electoral process in accordance with conditions and procedures established by it at least one month prior to the date of the elections.

C- The Commission shall have the right to revoke the accreditation of any entity or any of the members affiliated with such entity authorised to accompany the electoral process in the event of a breach of the conditions specified in the laws and regulations.

On the decisions of the Commission:

Meetings of the Commission shall not be legal unless attended by at least seven members, and the decisions of the Commission shall be taken by an absolute majority of the members who legally compose it, and its decisions shall be subject to appeal before the State Council within a time limit of three days from the date of their notification or publication, provided that the State Council rules thereon within a time limit of three days from the date of filing the petition.

On the delegation of powers:

The Commission may, by a decision thereof, delegate one or some of its members to carry out a specific task within its powers, and it may also form committees to carry out such specific tasks.

The President of the Commission shall have the right to delegate some of his powers to his Vice-President or to one of its members.

On the administrative staff and budget of the Commission:

A- The financial and administrative regulations of the Commission shall be determined by decrees adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister based on the proposal of the Commission.

B- An administrative staff shall be attached to the Commission, and it may contract with specialists as it deems appropriate to assist it in performing its functions. The Commission may also request the temporary secondment to it of a number of employees working in public administrations and institutions of the fourth category or its equivalent, in return for allowances determined by the Minister.
