Such secondment shall be effected by a decision of the competent Minister upon the request of the Minister based on the proposal of the Commission, and the duration of the secondment shall be specified in this decision.

C- The Commission shall prepare its draft budget, and upon the proposal of the Minister, special appropriations shall be allocated for the budget of the Commission within the budget of the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities.

On registration on the electoral rolls:

Registration on the electoral rolls shall be mandatory for voters, and no person may be registered on more than one roll, under penalty of the application of the provisions of Article 461 of the Penal Code.

On the permanence and amendment of the electoral rolls:

The electoral rolls shall be considered permanent; however, they shall be periodically revised in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

On the voters on the electoral rolls:

The Directorate General of Personal Status shall draw up for each electoral constituency automated electoral rolls containing the names of voters in accordance with the personal status registers, and these rolls shall include the names of all voters whose period of registration in the electoral constituency has reached at least one year on the date of commencement of the re-verification of the electoral rolls, namely the twentieth of November of each year.

On the entries of the rolls:

The electoral rolls shall mandatorily include:

The three-part name of each voter and the name of his mother, his register number as recorded in the personal status registers, his sex, his date of birth and his confession. A special column shall be designated in each roll in which shall be recorded, where applicable, the amendments occurring to the registration entries by way of correction or alteration, together with a mention of their legal basis.

The names of persons since whose date of birth one hundred years or more have elapsed shall be struck off the voters' rolls automatically.

Such striking off shall not preclude their re-registration upon an application submitted by the person concerned to the Ministry within a time limit of one month from the date of publication of the electoral rolls.

On an exceptional basis and for one time for the purpose of holding the parliamentary elections after the issuance of this Law exclusively, namely Law Effective Ipso Jure No. 8 dated 3/11/2021

On the Obligations of the Civil Status Departments

The heads of the civil status departments and offices in the regions shall send annually to the Directorate General of Personal Status, between the twentieth of November and the fifth of December, preliminary lists containing the names of registered persons who meet the legal conditions for registration on the electoral rolls, and the names of persons who will meet these conditions on the date of freezing the electoral rolls, as well as the names of those whose registration was omitted, or who died, or whose names were struck off the personal status registers for any reason whatsoever.

On an exceptional basis and for one time for the purpose of holding the parliamentary elections after the issuance of this Law exclusively, namely Law Effective Ipso Jure No. 8 dated 3/11/2021

On the Obligations of the Judicial Record Department

The Judicial Record Department in each governorate shall send to the Directorate General of Personal Status, annually between the twentieth of November and the fifth of December, a list of the names of persons convicted of offences that prevent them from exercising the right to vote in accordance with the provisions of Article 4 of this Law.

On an exceptional basis and for one time for the purpose of holding the parliamentary elections after the issuance of this Law exclusively, namely Law Effective Ipso Jure No. 8 dated 3/11/2021

On the Obligations of the Judicial Courts

The judicial courts shall send to the Directorate General of Personal Status, annually, between the twentieth of November to the fifth of December, a list of the final judgments issued by them in the offences provided for in Article 4 of this Law, as well as irrevocable judgments of interdiction.

On the Revision of the Electoral Rolls:

The Directorate General of Personal Status shall revise the electoral rolls according to what it receives from the authorities mentioned in the preceding articles, after verifying them.

Each roll shall include a special column in which the reasons for the revision and the operations of transferring the civil status registration from one roll to another are recorded. In the case of transfer, the name of the locality in the registration, the register number, and the date of transfer shall mandatorily be mentioned.

No voluntary transfer of a civil status registration shall be taken into account for the purpose of applying this Law if it occurred during the year preceding the start date of the re-verification of the electoral rolls. A transfer of registration due to marriage shall not be considered voluntary. The wife shall have the right to vote if the transfer of her civil status registration took place during the year mentioned above.

By way of exception and for one time only for the sole purpose of holding the parliamentary elections after the promulgation of this Law, namely Law enforceable ipso jure No. 8 dated 3/11/2021

On the Correction of the Lists

1 - Every interested party shall be entitled to submit, from the fifteenth of December 2021 until the first of January 2022, to the competent Registration Committee provided for in this Law, an application seeking to correct any defect concerning him in the electoral lists, such as if his registration was omitted or an error occurred in his name due to negligence, material error, or any other reason.

The petition for correction shall be submitted to the Registration Committee within a time limit ending on the first of January of the year 2022, provided that it is accompanied by the documents and evidence supporting the validity of his application, and the application shall be exempt from any fee.

Applications for correction relating to the addition of names whose registration was omitted shall be accompanied by a judicial record bearing a date not exceeding one month.

2 - Every voter registered on one of the electoral lists that have been frozen and that pertain to the electoral period (311/3/2021 to 30/3/022) shall also be entitled to request the competent Registration Committee to strike off or add the name of any person whose registration was effected or whose registration was omitted on the same list contrary to the law.

Each of the Governor, the Kaymakam, and the competent Mukhtar may exercise this right, within the one-month period ending on the first of January of the year 2022.

3 - Voters not resident on Lebanese territory shall be entitled to submit the same applications provided for in items 1 and 2 of this Article before the Lebanese embassies and consulates abroad, which shall refer them immediately to the Directorate General of Personal Status through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants before the first of January of the year 2022.

The Directorate General of Personal Status shall, in turn, refer these applications to the competent Registration Committees to take the necessary action.

4 - With respect to Lebanese resident outside Lebanese territory, the Directorate General of Personal Status shall send, through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants, on the fifteenth of December 2021, the preliminary lists of voters containing the number of voters entitled to exercise the right to vote in each embassy or consulate, such that each of them must designate one polling station or more than one polling station in the event that the number of persons registered at the centre exceeds four hundred voters.

The diplomatic missions and embassies shall deposit with the Directorate General of Personal Status, through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants, schedules of the polling stations proposed by them within a time limit not exceeding the fifteenth of January 2022.

Exceptionally and for one time, for the purpose of holding the parliamentary elections following the promulgation of this Law exclusively, namely Law Enacted by Operation of Law No. 8 dated 3/11/2021

On the Publication and Circulation of the Lists

Prior to the fifteenth of December 2021, the Directorate General of Personal Status shall send copies of the preliminary electoral lists that were previously frozen on 30/3/2021, in addition to the names of the voters who have reached twenty-one years of age on the date of the upcoming election day, to the municipalities, the mukhtars, and the centres of the governorates and districts, for the purpose of publishing and circulating them to facilitate the final revision, provided that the recipients receive these lists prior to the fifteenth of December 2021 at the latest, so that they may invite the voters to inspect them, and so that they may revise them in accordance with the documented information available to them.

Exceptionally and for one time, for the purpose of holding the parliamentary elections following the promulgation of this Law exclusively, namely Law Enacted by Operation of Law No. 8 dated 3/11/2021

On the Announcement of the Lists in the Media

The Ministry of Interior and Municipalities shall announce, through visual, audio, and print media, between the fifteenth of December 2021 and the first of January 2022, the readiness of the electoral lists frozen in accordance with the preceding Article, and shall invite the voters to inspect them. For this purpose as well, the Ministry must publish the preliminary electoral lists within the same time limit on its page on the electronic network (Website) and issue compact discs containing them. Any person shall be entitled to obtain copies thereof for a price determined by the Ministry.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants shall publish the preliminary electoral lists, within the same time limit, on its page on the electronic network (Website) and issue compact discs containing them.

No reliance shall be placed on the compact discs issued by the Directorate General of Personal Status after the date of 30/3/2021 and until 1/2/2022.

By way of exception and for one time for the purpose of holding the parliamentary elections after the promulgation of this Law exclusively, namely Law ipso facto in force No. 8 dated 3/11/2021

On the freezing of the electoral lists

The Directorate General of Personal Status shall take into account, when preparing the final electoral lists, the revision and registration transfer operations provided for in this Law.

The electoral list shall be frozen on the first of February and shall remain in force until the thirtieth of March 2023.

On the first of the month of February of the year 2022, the Directorate General of Personal Status shall send a copy of the final lists to the Directorate General of Political Affairs and Refugees to be adopted in the upcoming elections.

The electoral lists frozen on the first of February 2022 shall be adopted in any elections held during the period starting on 1 February 2022 and until 1 February 2023.

On the Primary Registration Committees:

One or more Primary Registration Committees shall be established in each electoral constituency.

Each Registration Committee shall be composed of a serving judicial or administrative judge as President, and of one of the presidents or members of the municipal councils in the electoral constituency and an employee of the Personal Status as two members.

One or more Personal Status employees shall be attached to each Registration Committee by decision of the Minister.

On the duties of the Primary Registration Committees:

The Primary Registration Committee shall undertake the following duties:

1 - Examining applications for correction to the electoral lists in accordance with the provisions of this Law, issuing decisions thereon within three working days from the date of submitting the application for correction, and notifying them to the concerned parties and to the Directorate General of Personal Status.

These decisions shall be subject to appeal before the competent Higher Registration Committee referred to hereinafter in this Law, within a period of three days from their notification.

The application for correction and the appeal shall be exempted from any fee, and the applicant for correction and the appellant shall be exempted from appointing a lawyer.

2 - Receiving the ballot boxes immediately upon the closing of the polling stations, auditing the minutes and documents, and taking the appropriate decisions thereon.

3 - Counting and tallying the votes, drawing up the general schedule of the result obtained by each list and each candidate, and submitting it to the competent Higher Registration Committees.

On the Convocation of the Electoral Bodies:

The electoral bodies shall be convoked by a decree published in the Official Gazette, and the time limit between the date of publication of this decree and the meeting of the electoral bodies shall be ninety days at least.

On By-Elections:

1- If any seat of the seats of the Chamber of Deputies becomes vacant due to death, resignation, annulment of the parliamentary mandate, or for any other reason, elections shall be held to fill the vacant seat within two months from the date of the vacancy, or from the date of publication in the Official Gazette of the decision of the Constitutional Council annulling the parliamentary mandate.

No successor shall be elected if the vacancy occurs in the last six months prior to the expiration of the term of office of the Chamber.

2 - The electoral bodies shall be convoked by a decree published in the Official Gazette. The time limit between the date of publication of this decree and the meeting of the electoral bodies shall be thirty days at least.

3 - The period for candidacy for parliamentary by-elections shall close at least 15 days prior to the date set for the election, and the period for withdrawal of candidacy shall close at least 10 days prior to the date of the election.

4 - By-elections to fill the vacant seat shall be held at the level of the minor constituency to which this seat belongs, in accordance with the single-round majoritarian voting system, and the polling centres within this constituency shall be determined by a decision of the Minister; however, if the vacancy exceeds two seats in the major electoral constituency, the proportional voting system shall be adopted in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

5 - Resident and non-resident voters shall participate in the voting process, provided that they exercise their right to vote on Lebanese territory.

6 - The parliamentary mandate of a deputy who wins in a by-election may not exceed the term of the parliamentary mandate of the person whom he replaced.

7 - Notwithstanding the provisions of paragraph (c) of the provisions of Article 8 of this Law, the persons mentioned therein may stand as candidates if they resign and effectively cease their functions within fifteen days commencing from the date of issuance of the decree convoking the electoral bodies.

8 - The provisions of Law No. 25 dated 8-10-2008 relating to parliamentary elections shall exceptionally apply with respect to majoritarian voting to the provisions of this Article insofar as they do not conflict with the provisions of this Law.

On Candidacy for the Electoral Constituency:

Whoever fulfils the conditions to be a member of the Chamber of Deputies may nominate himself as a candidate for any electoral constituency; however, no one may nominate himself as a candidate in more than one electoral constituency at the same time.

On the Higher Registration Committees:

A Higher Registration Committee shall be established in each electoral constituency for the duration of a single electoral cycle.

Each Higher Registration Committee shall be composed of a Chamber President or a Counsellor at the Court of Cassation, or a President of a Chamber of Appeal, or a Chamber President or a Counsellor at the State Council, as Chairman, of a sitting judicial or administrative judge and an inspector from the Central Inspection as two members, and of a Head of a Civil Status Department or a Head of Section or an employee in the Directorate General of Personal Status as Rapporteur.

On the functions of the Higher Registration Committees:

The Higher Registration Committee shall assume the following functions:

1 - Examining applications for appeal against the decisions of the Registration Committees and adjudicating them within three working days from the date of their receipt by it.

2 - Receiving the minutes of the results issued by all the Primary Registration Committees operating within the jurisdiction of the Committee and the schedules annexed to these minutes, auditing them, conducting the operations of tallying the votes, organising general schedules of the results obtained by each list and by each candidate within the latter, and submitting them immediately to the Minister through the Governor or whomever he delegates.

3 - The Committee shall notify the results of its work mentioned in items 1 and 2 above to the Supervisory Commission for Elections.

Exceptionally and for a single time for the purpose of holding the parliamentary elections after the promulgation of this Law exclusively, namely Law Enforceable ipso jure No. 8 dated 3/11/2021

On the term of the Registration Committees

The Supreme Judicial Council and the Bureau of the State Council shall submit a nominal list of judges for their appointment as Chairmen of the Higher and Primary Registration Committees.

The Central Inspection Board shall submit a nominal list of inspectors for their appointment.

The Chairmen, members and rapporteurs of the Higher and Primary Registration Committees shall be appointed for this electoral cycle before the first of December of the year 2021, by a decision issued by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities.

On the date of the elections:

The parliamentary elections shall take place on a single day for all electoral constituencies within the sixty days preceding the expiry of the term of the Chamber of Deputies, with the exception of the case where the said Chamber is dissolved, in which case the elections shall take place within the three months following the publication of the decree of dissolution.

The term of the current Chamber of Deputies shall exceptionally expire on 21 May 2018, in order to enable the Government to take the necessary measures to apply the new provisions and procedures for the parliamentary elections provided for in this Law.

By way of exception and for one time only in order to conduct the parliamentary elections after the issuance of this Law exclusively, namely Law in Force by Operation of Law No. 8 dated 3/11/2021

Concerning Candidacy Applications:

Every person who nominates himself for the parliamentary elections must submit:

1. A declaration to the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities - Directorate General of Political Affairs and Refugees, signed by him in person and with his signature notarised before a Notary Public in accordance with a standard form prepared by the latter, containing:

- The full three-part name of the candidate

- The designation of the seat, either in the minor constituency or in the constituency not composed of minor constituencies, for which he wishes to nominate himself.

2 . The following documents shall be attached to the declaration:

- An individual civil status extract dated no more than one month earlier.

- A judicial record extract dated no more than one month earlier.

- Two passport-style photographs certified by the Mukhtar.

- A financial receipt from the Treasury Fund proving that he has deposited the candidacy fee for the parliamentary elections set at 200.000.000 L.L.

- A bank certificate proving the opening of the electoral campaign account provided for in this Law, containing the name of the person authorised to operate the account approved by the candidate.

- A copy of the final electoral rolls authenticated by the Director General of Personal Status proving the registration of the candidate on the electoral rolls adopted in the parliamentary elections for the year 2022

- A declaration from the candidate executed before a Notary Public containing the name of the auditor, provided that a certified copy thereof is deposited with the Supervisory Commission for Parliamentary Elections.

- A letter executed before a Notary Public granting the Commission permission to inspect and examine the bank account relating to the electoral campaign of the candidate.

On the closing of candidacy nominations and deciding upon applications:

1 - The candidacy nomination period shall close sixty days prior to the date set for the elections.

2 - A candidate shall file with the Ministry his declaration of candidacy accompanied by all required documents by a date no later than the closing day of the candidacy nomination period.

3 - The Ministry shall give the candidate a provisional receipt acknowledging receipt of the declaration and its documents.

4 - The Ministry shall decide upon the declarations of candidacy within a period of five days from the date of their receipt, and it shall be required, in the event of acceptance of the candidacy, to deliver to the candidate a final receipt registering his declaration of candidacy, and it shall also be required, in the event of rejection of the declaration of candidacy, to inform the candidate of the reasons for this rejection.

5 - The non-issuance of a decision by the Ministry after the lapse of five days from the registration of the declaration of candidacy with it shall be deemed an acceptance thereof. The Ministry shall be required to deliver to the candidate the final receipt registering his candidacy.

6 - If the Ministry refuses to accept the declaration of candidacy, the candidate shall have the right, within a period of three days from the date of being notified of the explicit rejection decision, to apply to the State Council by way of a petition exempt from fees. The said Council shall adjudicate his objection in the deliberation chamber within three days from its receipt. Its decision in this case shall be final and not subject to any ordinary or extraordinary means of recourse.

On the extension of the candidacy nomination period:

1 - If the candidacy nomination period expires and no candidate has come forward for a particular seat, the candidacy nomination period shall be extended ipso jure by seven days; the Ministry shall decide upon the declarations of candidacy within a period of 24 hours from the date of their receipt, and it shall be required, in the event of acceptance of the candidacy, to deliver to the candidate a final receipt registering his declaration of candidacy, and it shall also be required, in the event of rejection of the declaration of candidacy, to inform the candidate of the reasons for this rejection.

2 - The non-issuance of a decision by the Ministry after the lapse of the period mentioned above, following the registration of the declaration of candidacy with it, shall be deemed an acceptance thereof. The Ministry shall be required to deliver to the candidate the final receipt registering his candidacy.

3 - If the Ministry refuses to accept the declaration of candidacy, the candidate shall have the right, within a period of 48 hours from the date of being notified of the explicit rejection decision, to apply to the State Council by way of a petition exempt from fees. The said Council shall adjudicate his objection in the deliberation chamber within 48 hours from its receipt, and its decision in this case shall be final and not subject to any ordinary or extraordinary means of recourse.

On Winning by Acclamation:

A - If the candidacy period expires and only one candidate has come forward for a specific seat in a minor electoral constituency, this candidate shall be deemed elected by acclamation, and the lists in this case shall be composed of the remaining seats in the electoral constituency.

B - Lists shall be registered at least forty days prior to the date of the elections; if the period for registering lists expires and only one complete list has come forward for the seats of a specific constituency, this list shall be deemed elected by acclamation.

In both cases, the Ministry shall immediately address a letter to that effect to the Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies and the President of the Constitutional Council.

On the Invalidity of Candidacy Declarations:

Candidacy declarations that violate the provisions of the preceding Articles shall be deemed null and void, as well as declarations submitted, on the same date, by a single candidate in more than one constituency. However, if such declarations are submitted on different dates, only the last of them shall be taken into consideration, and the previous declarations shall be deemed null and void.

On Withdrawal of Candidacy:

A candidate may not withdraw his candidacy except by virtue of a legal declaration notarized by a notary public and deposited with the Ministry at least forty-five days prior to the date of the elections. In the event that a candidate announces his withdrawal after the aforementioned period, the withdrawal shall not be taken into consideration with respect to the electoral process.

If such withdrawal renders it impossible to elect the required number in the constituency, new candidacies for that constituency may be accepted if submitted within a period of seven days from the date of that withdrawal. The time limits stipulated in Article 47 of this Law shall apply to candidacy applications and to their administrative and judicial adjudication.

On the Announcement of Accepted Candidates:

Following the closing of candidacy registration, the Ministry shall announce the names of the accepted candidates, immediately notify the Governors (Muhafizs), the District Commissioners (Qaimaqams) and the Supervisory Commission for Elections thereof, and publish them wherever required.

On candidate lists:

Candidates shall form into lists no later than forty days before the date of the elections, provided that each list includes a minimum of 40% (forty percent) of the number of seats in the electoral constituency, being no fewer than 3 seats, and provided that it includes at least one seat from each minor constituency in constituencies composed of more than one minor constituency. The largest fraction shall be adopted in calculating the minimum limit in constituencies with an odd number of seats.

A list shall bear the responsibility of failing to fill a seat allocated to it for which it nominated no one, and the seat shall be transferred to the holder of the highest preferential votes on the other lists in the minor constituency and from the sect in which the number was short.

The Ministry shall respect the serial order of the names set out in the lists under which the candidates formed in the minor constituencies, and the withdrawal of any candidate from the list after its registration shall not be recognised, and it shall also abide by the order of the lists on the ballot paper in accordance with the date of their registration.

The applications of candidates who did not form into lists in accordance with the text of this Article shall be cancelled.

In the event of the death of one of the candidates after the registration of the lists, the list shall have the right to nominate in place of the deceased up to ten days before the date of the elections, and the nomination time limits shall lapse exclusively in this case.

On the Registration of Lists:

Candidates must join into lists and authorise one of them by virtue of a power of attorney signed by all of them before a notary public to register this list with the Ministry within a time limit not exceeding forty days before the date fixed for the elections, and after this date neither the registration of lists nor the amendment of their composition shall be accepted. Upon registering it, the commissioner of the list must submit:

* The triple name of all its members

* The receipts of acceptance of the candidacy of the members

* Their sequential order according to the minor constituency of the list

* The designation of the constituency in which the list is standing for election

* The name and colour of the list

* A coloured passport photograph of each candidate

* A declaration appointing the auditor in accordance with the provisions of this Law and his approval of this appointment

* A bank certificate proving the opening of an account for the list in the name of the commissioner of the list

The Ministry shall issue a receipt of acceptance of the registration of the list (within 24 hours) if the application satisfies all legal conditions; however, if this application does not satisfy all or some of these conditions, the Ministry shall grant the members of the list requested to be registered a time limit of 24 hours in order to rectify the registration application, on pain of its rejection.

This time limit shall run from the date of notification of the commissioner of the list referred to in the item above.

The decision issued by the Ministry rejecting the registration shall be subject to challenge before the State Consultative Council within a time limit of 24 hours from the date of notification of the commissioner of the list referred to above, provided that the State Consultative Council rules on the challenge within a similar time limit, and its decision in this case shall be final and not subject to any ordinary or extraordinary means of recourse.

On the Announcement of Accepted Lists:

Immediately upon the expiry of the time limit for the registration of lists referred to in Article 52 of this Law, the Ministry shall announce the names of the lists whose registration has been accepted and the names of their members, notify them to the Governors, the District Commissioners and the Supervisory Commission for Parliamentary Elections, and publish them where necessary.

On Electoral Campaign Financing:

The financing of electoral campaigns and the expenditure of candidates and lists during the electoral campaign period, which begins on the date of the opening of candidacy and ends upon the closing of the ballot boxes, shall be subject to the provisions of this Law.

On Electoral Contributions:

Any grant, donation, cash or in-kind gift, loan, advance, financial payment or anything of material value provided to the list or to the candidate shall be considered a contribution within the meaning of this Law.

On Electoral Expenditure:

Electoral expenditure within the meaning of this Law shall be deemed to be the total expenditure paid by the list or the candidate, as well as the expenditure paid for the account or benefit of either of them with their express or implied consent by natural or legal persons, parties, associations or any other party, provided that they relate directly to the electoral campaign, the polling process, and the achievement of lawful communication between the list or the candidate and the voter, including, by way of illustration and not limitation:

Securing electoral offices and all other expenses of such offices, holding gatherings, rallies, public meetings and banquets for an electoral purpose, expenses relating to the equipment used during the campaign, preparing, publishing and distributing media and promotional materials consisting of books, booklets, bulletins, leaflets and letters in the form of printed matter or via regular or digital mail, preparing, distributing and hanging photographs, posters, banners and billboards, compensation and allowances paid in cash or in kind to persons working in the electoral campaign and to delegates, transport and travel expenses of electoral campaign personnel and voters, travel expenses of voters from abroad, electoral advertising expenses, opinion poll expenses, and any expenses paid for the electoral campaign to any radio or television broadcasting station or any newspaper, magazine or other publication medium, including electronic ones.

On expenditure and funding:

1 - A candidate may expend amounts from his own funds for the purpose of his electoral campaign. The funds of a spouse or of any ascendants or descendants shall be deemed to constitute the own funds of the candidate.

All expenditures incurred or paid by a candidate from his own funds for the purpose of his electoral campaign shall be subject to the expenditure ceiling.

2 - No contribution to the electoral campaign of a candidate or a list may be made except by Lebanese natural or legal persons.

3 - It is strictly prohibited for a candidate or a list to accept or receive contributions or assistance originating from a foreign State or from a non-Lebanese person, whether natural or legal, directly or indirectly.

4 - The services of individuals who volunteer without remuneration shall not be deemed a contribution within the meaning of this Law.

5 - A contribution made by a single Lebanese natural or legal person for the purpose of funding the electoral campaign of a candidate or a list may not exceed an amount of 50% of the electoral expenditure ceiling set in Article 61 of this Law and must always be made by way of a banking transaction (transfer, cheque, credit card...) subject to the fourth paragraph of Article 59 of this Law.

6 - The total contributions received by any candidate may not exceed the electoral expenditure ceiling as set in Article 61 of this Law, nor may contributions be accepted through an intermediary.

Exceptionally and for one time only for the purpose of holding the parliamentary elections after the promulgation of this Law exclusively, namely Law Effective Ipso Jure No. 8 dated 3/11/2021

On the expenditure ceiling

The ceiling of the maximum amount that each candidate may expend during the electoral campaign period shall be set as follows:

A fixed lump-sum portion amounting to seven hundred and fifty million Lebanese pounds, to which shall be added a variable portion linked to the number of voters in the major electoral constituency in which he is elected and amounting to and fifty thousand Lebanese pounds for each voter registered on the voter rolls in the major electoral constituency.

As for the electoral expenditure ceiling for a list, it shall be a fixed lump-sum amount of seven hundred and fifty million Lebanese pounds for each candidate therein.

This ceiling may be reconsidered upon the opening of the electoral campaign period in light of economic conditions, pursuant to a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior and Municipalities and after consulting the opinion of the Commission.

On prohibited acts:

1 - Commitments and expenditures that involve providing services or paying sums to voters shall be considered prohibited during the election campaign period, including, by way of example and not limitation:

In-kind and cash contributions and assistance to individuals, charitable, social, cultural, family, religious or other associations, sports clubs, and all public institutions.

2 - The contributions and assistance mentioned above shall not be considered prohibited if they are provided by candidates, or institutions owned or managed by candidates, or parties that have customarily and regularly provided them in the same volume and quantity for not less than three years prior to the start of the election campaign period, and in this case, the payments and assistance provided during the election campaign shall not be considered subject to the electoral ceiling provided for in Article 61 above.

On the obligations of the accredited auditor:

The accredited auditor for each of the candidates and lists shall periodically submit to the Commission, within a period of one week from the expiry of each month of the months of the election campaign period, a monthly accounting statement showing the receipts, payments and financial commitments for the past month, accompanied by a statement of the bank account pertaining to the election campaign issued by the accredited bank, and shall also submit upon the completion of his mission a statement of account and a report on the acts of his administration to the candidate.

On the electoral campaign account and the appointment of an auditor:

1 - Every candidate and list must open an account with a bank operating in Lebanon called the "Electoral Campaign Account", and attach to the declaration of candidacy a certificate from the bank proving the opening of the said account with it and showing the account number and the name of its holder.

2 - The electoral campaign account shall not be subject to banking secrecy, and the candidate and the list shall be deemed to have waived banking secrecy ipso jure for this account merely by opening it.

3 - The receipt of all contributions and the payment of all electoral expenditures must take place exclusively through this account throughout the entire electoral campaign period.

4 - It shall be for every candidate and list to regulate the procedures adopted thereby for receiving the funds and contributions allocated to financing the electoral campaign and the authority to pay electoral expenditures, subject to the provisions of this Law.

No amount exceeding one million pounds may be received or paid except by cheque.

5 - Every candidate and list must, upon submitting the declarations of candidacy, declare the name of the auditor by virtue of a written instrument registered with the notary public and submit it to the Commission.

6 - Where it is impossible to open and operate a bank account for any candidate or list for reasons beyond the control of either of them, the funds allocated to the electoral campaign of the candidate or the list shall be deposited in a public fund established with the Ministry of Finance, which shall replace the bank account in all its particulars.

On the comprehensive statement of account:

1 - Every candidate and list must, after the conclusion of the elections, prepare a comprehensive statement of account certified by the accredited auditor and including in detail the total revenues received and contributions in kind, according to their sources and dates, and the total expenditures, paid or incurred according to their nature and dates, since the start of the electoral campaign.

2 - This statement must be submitted to the Commission within a period of thirty days from the date of the announcement of the official results of the elections, accompanied by the supporting documents relating to all items of the account, such as receipts, payment vouchers and others, and by a comprehensive bank statement for the account relating to the campaign showing all operations that took place on this account from the date of its opening until the date of submission of this statement.

3 - Attached to the statement of account shall be a declaration signed by the candidate and certified before a notary public. Pursuant to this declaration and on his own responsibility, the candidate acknowledges that the attached account is accurate and comprehensive and includes the entirety of the revenues collected and expenditures paid or incurred for the electoral campaign, and also expressly acknowledges that there are no other cash or in-kind expenditures or funds paid in cash or from other bank accounts or through third parties.

4 - The accredited auditor must, if the statement of account does not include any electoral revenues or expenditures, draw up a certificate to that effect.

5 - The Commission shall examine and audit the statement of account of each candidate and conduct investigations relating to its accuracy or the accuracy of some of its elements, and for this purpose it may seek the assistance of whomever it deems appropriate from among experts and others, including members of the judicial police, after the approval of the competent Public Prosecution.

6 - The Commission shall rule on the accuracy of the above statement of account within a period of thirty days from the date of its submission, and decide either to approve it or, after observing the adversarial principle and the right of defence, not to approve it, or request its amendment or correction in whole or in part. The Commission shall file its reasoned decision, accompanied by the statement of account, with the Constitutional Council.

If a period of one month elapses from the submission of the statement of account without a decision being issued by the Commission regarding it, this statement shall be deemed approved by operation of law.

7 - The Commission shall reject the statement of account if it becomes apparent to it that it is inaccurate or that it includes, after its correction or amendment, an exceeding of the spending ceiling, provided that in these cases the Commission shall inform both the Presidency of the Chamber of Deputies and the Presidency of the Constitutional Council of this matter.

8 - If it becomes apparent to the Commission that the value of one of the electoral expenditures declared in the statement of account and its attachments is lower than the prevailing value customarily adopted for such expenditure, the Commission shall, after observing the adversarial principle and the right of defence, assess the difference by comparison with several sources, and enter it by operation of law among the expenditures. This difference shall be deemed subject to the spending ceiling provided for in this law.

9 - The provisions of paragraph 8 above shall apply to direct or indirect benefits and all in-kind contributions and services from which the candidate benefited.

On Terminology:

The terms set out below, when used for the application of this Law whether in the singular or plural form, shall have the following meanings:

Electoral Media:

Any media material, such as news, analyses, statements, interviews, debates, dialogues, investigations, press conferences, and meetings, that relates directly or indirectly to the elections and is broadcast free of charge within the regular or exceptional programmes of a media institution.

Electoral Campaigning:

Any material that relates to the programmes of nominating entities, their electoral campaigns, and their electoral and political positions, which is recorded inside or outside the studios of a media institution, and which the nominating entity wishes to address to voters by broadcasting it for its own account within the programmes of media institutions designated for that purpose and in return for financial consideration.

Electoral Advertising:

Any promotional material or publication for a nominating entity that is broadcast or published in return for financial consideration within the breaks and spaces designated for commercial advertisements at media and advertising institutions.

Electoral Materials:

Electoral media, electoral campaigning, and electoral advertising.

Media Outlets:

Any public or private audiovisual, print, read, or electronic media outlet, whatever its technology.

On Explaining the Electoral Programme:

Every list or candidate may organise various lawful activities in order to explain the electoral programme in the appropriate style and manner, in a way that does not conflict with laws and regulations.

On the Electoral Campaigning Period:

Electoral materials broadcast across the various media and advertising outlets during the electoral campaign period specified in this Law, which begins on the date of submission of candidacy and ends upon the closing of the ballot boxes, shall be subject to the provisions set out in this Chapter.

On Complaints and Criminal Prosecution :

1 - The Commission shall refer a breach of the provisions of this Chapter to the competent Public Prosecution if it appears to it that such breach meets the description of a criminal offence.

2 - Whoever intentionally commits a breach in accordance with the provisions of the first paragraph shall be punished by imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months and by a fine ranging between fifty million Lebanese pounds and one hundred million Lebanese pounds, or by either of these two penalties, without prejudice to the penalties covering criminal offences provided for in the Penal Code and in special criminal laws.

3 - The disbursement of prohibited electoral expenditures referred to in Article 62 of this Law shall be deemed tantamount to the offence of bribery provided for in the Penal Code.

4 - The penalties provided for in the second paragraph above shall apply to a legal person in accordance with Article 210 of the Penal Code.

5 - The public action and the civil action relating to the offences provided for in the second paragraph above shall lapse by prescription after a period of six months from the date of the announcement of the election results.

6 - The decisions of the Constitutional Council issued on electoral challenges enjoy the force of res judicata binding upon all judicial and administrative courts and upon all administrations of the State, such that the outcome of the complaint and the criminal prosecution shall be determined on the basis of the said decision.

On Special Penalties Relating to the Statement of Account:

1 - A candidate who has not submitted the comprehensive statement of account provided for in Article 64 of this Law shall be punished by a financial fine of one million Lebanese pounds for each day of delay. This fine shall be imposed by the Ministry at the request of the Commission.

2 - A candidate who has exceeded the electoral spending ceiling shall be punished by a fine equal to three times the value of the excess in favour of the Treasury, and the file shall be referred by the Commission to the Constitutional Council.

On the Fine :

A candidate who has not won in the elections and who has not submitted the statement of account shall be punished by a financial fine of one million Lebanese pounds for each day of delay, imposed by the Ministry on the basis of a report issued by the Commission.

A candidate who has not won in the elections and who has exceeded the electoral spending ceiling shall also be punished by a fine equal to three times the value of the excess.

On paid electoral advertising:

A - Paid electoral publicity and advertising in the media and advertising outlets shall be permitted in accordance with the following provisions:

1 - Media and advertising outlets wishing to participate in electoral publicity and advertising must submit to the Commission, at least ten days prior to the beginning of the electoral campaign period, a declaration announcing their wish to participate, accompanied by their price list and the spaces or airtime they wish to allocate to electoral publicity or advertising.

2 - Media and advertising outlets shall abide by the price list and the spaces or airtime they have submitted, and shall not have the right to refuse any electoral advertisement requested by a list or candidate that abides by them.

3 - Media and advertising outlets that fail to submit their declaration within the specified time limit shall be prohibited from carrying out any advertising or publicity activity related to the elections throughout the entire electoral campaign period.

4 - Media and advertising outlets must explicitly make clear, when broadcasting or publishing electoral advertisements, that such advertisements are paid for, and must specify the party that requested their broadcast or publication.

5 - Media and advertising outlets shall be prohibited from accepting free advertisements or advertisements in return for a consideration that differs from that stated in the price list submitted by them.

6 - The nominating party or its legal representative shall undertake to deliver a copy of the electoral publicity and advertising tapes, accompanied by a written booking request, to both the Commission and the media and advertising establishments for the purpose of broadcasting or publishing them, at least three days prior to the date scheduled for their first broadcast or publication.

7- Every media or advertising establishment shall submit a subsequent weekly report to the Commission containing a statement of the electoral publicity and advertisements broadcast or published during the past week, together with the times of broadcast or publication of each of them and the consideration collected therefor.

8 - No nominating party may allocate to a single media or advertising establishment more than 50% of its total publicity or advertising expenditure with respect to each category of media or advertising establishments.

B - The Commission shall determine the maximum space or airtime specified for each media or advertising outlet for the purpose of broadcasting or publishing media or advertising programmes related to lists or candidates, and shall also determine the times of broadcast or publication of such spaces or airtime.

C - In determining and distributing the maximum media spaces or airtime, the Commission shall observe the requirements of fairness and the right of candidates to equal media appearance within the limits of the law and legitimate electoral competition in accordance with the criteria stipulated above.

On the Commission's oversight over the media:

1 - The Commission shall verify the compliance of the media in Lebanon with the provisions relating to electoral publicity stipulated in this Law and the decisions taken in implementation of these provisions.

2 - The Commission shall ensure respect for the freedom of expression of various opinions and intellectual currents in media programmes during the electoral campaign period, by issuing binding recommendations to such media, so as to guarantee the provision of fairness, balance and neutrality in treatment between candidates and between lists.

3 - The first paragraph above shall apply to all political and general news programmes, including news bulletins, political debate programmes, interviews, meetings, dialogues, roundtables and the live broadcast of electoral rallies, which shall remain free of charge.

4 - The Commission must ensure balance in media appearances among competitors from among lists and candidates, such that it obliges a media outlet, upon hosting a representative of a list or a candidate, to ensure in return the hosting of his competitors under similar conditions in terms of timing, duration and type of programme.

5 - The Commission shall have the authority to assess whether the appearance of candidates on satellite media ought to be counted within the advertising or media spaces allocated by the Commission to each list or candidate, and it shall also have the authority to determine the extent of such counting.

6 - The Commission shall undertake an immediate investigation into any complaint submitted by an aggrieved list or an aggrieved candidate and shall take its decision regarding referral to the competent Court of Publications within 24 hours from the date of its submission.

The media are required to maintain a recorded archive of all programmes broadcast during the electoral campaign for a period of six months from the date of the end of the elections.

7- The Commission shall determine, prior to the commencement of the electoral process, the criteria that allow for distinguishing between electoral media coverage and electoral advertising, and it shall have the right at all times to verify whether any programme conceals, under the guise of media coverage, illicit disguised electoral advertising, and to take all legal measures to put an end to this matter.

On the obligations of the official media:

1 - A list or a candidate shall have the right to use the official media free of charge in order to present the electoral programmes in accordance with the provisions of this Law and the rules laid down by the Commission.

2 - Each list or candidate wishing to exercise this right shall submit a written application in this regard to the Commission. The Commission shall draw up a list of the names of the candidates and lists authorised to use the official media.

3 - The Commission shall establish a special schedule in which it determines the times and conditions for the distribution of broadcasting times among the various lists and candidates, whilst adhering to the necessity of providing balanced broadcasting times so as to ensure the achievement of equality and equal opportunities among the various candidates and among the various lists.

4 - The official media shall adhere to a position of neutrality at all stages of the electoral process, and neither it nor any of its bodies or employees may carry out any activity that may be interpreted as supporting a candidate or a list at the expense of another candidate or another list.

On the obligations of the private media:

1 - No private media outlet may declare its support for any candidate or electoral list. With due regard for the principle of independence, the aforementioned media outlets shall, during the electoral campaign period, clearly distinguish between facts and truths on the one hand and opinions and commentary on the other hand, in their various news bulletins or political programmes.

2 - During the electoral campaign period, the private media outlets, lists and candidates shall adhere to the following obligations:

- Refraining from defamation, slander or libel, and from disparaging any of the lists or candidates.

- Refraining from broadcasting anything that includes incitement of sectarian, confessional or ethnic strife, or instigation to commit acts of violence or rioting, or support for terrorism, crime or acts of sabotage.

- Refraining from broadcasting anything that would constitute a means of pressure, intimidation, accusation of treason, accusation of apostasy, holding out enticements, or promising material or moral gains.

- Refraining from distorting, withholding, falsifying, omitting or misrepresenting information.

- Refraining from transmitting or rebroadcasting any material showing the violations mentioned above, on pain of holding the institution liable for violating this Law.

On Electoral Educational Programmes:

Audio-visual media outlets must allocate during the electoral campaign period at least three hours weekly in order to broadcast electoral educational programmes produced by the Ministries of Information and of Interior and Municipalities in coordination with the concerned media outlets.

On Places Designated for Electoral Advertisements:

1 - The competent local authority, under the supervision of the administrative authority, shall designate in every city or town the places designated for hanging and posting electoral advertisements and pictures throughout the electoral campaign period.

2 - It is prohibited to hang or post any advertisement or pictures of candidates or lists outside the places designated for advertisements, and it is also prohibited for any candidate or list to hang or post an advertisement or pictures on the places designated for another. The responsibility for removing the above violations shall fall upon the list or the candidate.

3 - The competent local authority shall undertake the distribution of the places specified in accordance with the first paragraph of this Article between the lists and the candidates according to the order of lodging the nomination applications.

Local authorities and companies operating the places designated for advertisements shall cooperate with the Commission for the proper implementation of the provisions of this Article.

4 - No candidate or list may waive the places designated for his or its electoral advertisement in favour of another candidate or another list.

On Prohibitions:

1 - Public facilities, government departments, public institutions, universities, faculties, institutes, public and private schools, and places of worship may not be used in order to hold electoral rallies and hold electoral meetings and gatherings or to conduct electoral publicity.

2 - Employees of the State, public institutions, municipalities, unions of municipalities, and those of similar status may not engage in electoral promotion in favour of a candidate or a list, nor may they distribute leaflets in favour of or against any candidate or list.

3 - It is prohibited to distribute leaflets or any other documents in favour of or against a candidate or a list throughout polling day at the doors of the polling centre or any other place located within the polling centre, under penalty of confiscation without prejudice to the other penalties provided for in this Law.

On Penalties and Fines:

1 - Without prejudice to the provisions of the Penal Code, the Publications Law and the Audio-Visual Media Law, the Commission may take whichever of the following two measures it deems appropriate against any media or advertising outlet that violates the provisions of this Chapter relating to electoral media and advertising:

a - Issuing a warning to the offending media outlet, or obliging it to broadcast an apology, or obliging it to enable the aggrieved candidate to exercise the right of reply.

b - Referring the offending media outlet to the competent Court of Publications, which shall take whichever of the following measures it deems appropriate:

• Imposing a financial fine on the offending media outlet ranging in value between fifty and one hundred million Lebanese pounds.

• Partially suspending the offending media outlet from operating for a period not exceeding three days, such that this suspension encompasses all political and news programmes, bulletins, interviews and seminars.

• In the event of recurrence of the violation, totally suspending the offending media outlet from operating and completely shutting down all of its programmes for a maximum period of three days.

The Public Prosecution shall prosecute the offending outlet before the Court of Publications ex officio or at the request of the aggrieved party, and the media outlet complained against may submit a memorandum to the Court within a time limit of 24 hours from the time it is notified.

The Court of Publications shall issue its decision within a time limit of 24 hours at most, and both the Public Prosecution and the convicted party may appeal the decision before the Court of Cassation within a time limit of 24 hours starting, in respect of the Public Prosecution, from the time of its issuance and, in respect of the convicted party, from the time of its notification.

The appeal shall not stay the execution of the decision unless the Court of Cassation takes a decision to stay its execution within a time limit of 24 hours from the time the appeal is lodged before it.

2 - Without prejudice to the provisions of the Penal Code, the Commission may take whichever of the following measures it deems appropriate against any opinion polling institution or any other person that violates Article 79 of this Law:

a - Issuing a warning.

b - An obligation to broadcast an apology or a correction through the media outlets.

c - A financial fine ranging between ten million and twenty-five million, imposed pursuant to a collection order issued by the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities at the request of the Commission.

This fine shall be doubled in the event that the violation occurs during the electoral silence period.

On Damages:

A party aggrieved by one of the above violations shall have the right to claim compensation for the damage sustained thereby.

On Correction and the Right of Reply:

Media outlets shall broadcast and publish corrections and replies received from lists and candidates within a time limit of 24 hours from the broadcast of the news item complained of. Media outlets shall have the right to refuse to broadcast the reply if it is contrary to the laws.

On the Magnetic Electronic Card:

The Government shall, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers by a two-thirds majority upon the proposal of the Minister, take the measures conducive to adopting the magnetic electronic card in the upcoming electoral process, and shall propose to the Chamber of Deputies the necessary amendments to this Law required by the adoption of the magnetic electronic card.

The application of Article 84 of the Law on the Election of Members of the Chamber of Deputies No. 44 dated 17/6/2017 shall be suspended, exceptionally and for one time only, exclusively for the parliamentary election cycle scheduled to be held in the spring of the year 2022, provided that the aforementioned Article shall return into force in the subsequent cycles. (Pursuant to Law Enforceable Ipso Jure No. 8 dated 3/11/2021)

Polling Centres and Stations:

The electoral constituency shall be divided, by a decision of the Minister, into a number of polling centres comprising a number of polling stations. Every village in which the number of voters is at least one hundred and at most four hundred shall have one polling station.

This number may be increased to more than four hundred voters in a single polling station if the soundness of the electoral process so requires, provided that the number does not exceed six hundred voters, and the number of polling stations in each centre may not exceed twenty polling stations.

The decision of the Minister on the distribution of polling stations shall be published in the Official Gazette and on the website of the Ministry at least twenty days prior to the date scheduled for holding the elections, and this distribution may not be amended during the week preceding the date of holding the elections except for serious reasons and by a reasoned decision.

On the electoral silence period:

Starting from zero hour of the day preceding Election Day and until the closing of the ballot boxes, all media outlets shall be prohibited from broadcasting any advertisement, campaign material or direct electoral appeal, with the exception of sound and/or image that is difficult to avoid during the live coverage of the course of electoral operations.

On polling day, media coverage shall be limited to reporting the facts of the electoral process.

On opinion polls:

1 - The Commission shall determine the conditions for conducting opinion polling operations during the electoral campaign, and it shall also determine the procedures to be followed to ensure the credibility, integrity and neutral character of the polling process.

2 - The Commission shall determine the conditions and procedures to which the publication, broadcasting or distribution of the results of an opinion poll during the electoral campaign is subject. It shall have full powers in order to verify the conformity of the opinion poll with the laws, regulations and the decision of the Commission, and it shall also be entitled to take all necessary measures in order to stop violations or rectify them as against media outlets, opinion polling institutions or any other person.

3 - The announcement, publication, broadcasting or distribution of the result of an opinion poll must be accompanied by a clarification of the following matters, at least, on the responsibility of the institution that conducted the poll:

- The name of the entity that conducted the poll.

- The name of the entity that commissioned the poll and paid its cost.

- The dates on which the poll was conducted in the field.

- The size of the polled sample and the method of its selection and distribution.

- The technique used in the poll.

- The verbatim text of the questions asked.

- The limits of interpretation of the results and the percentage of the margin of error therein, where applicable.

4 - During the ten days preceding Election Day and until the closing of all ballot boxes, the publication, broadcasting or distribution of all opinion polls and commentary thereon, in any form whatsoever, shall be prohibited.

On media coverage of polling and counting operations:

Media outlets wishing to participate in the coverage of polling and counting operations must obtain written permits from the Commission for this purpose in accordance with the provisions of the second paragraph of Article 19 of this Law. They shall abide by the code of conduct established by the Commission.

On the Polling Station Board and its Work:

1 - The Governor or the District Commissioner, each within his jurisdiction, shall appoint for each polling station a presiding officer and one or more clerks, assigned from among State employees on the basis of nominal lists sent by the Ministry - Directorate General of Political Affairs and Refugees, at most one week before the date of the election, provided that they shall not be notified of the place of their assignment in the centre of the Governorate or District until five days before the said date.

2 - The presiding officer of the polling station shall be assisted by two assistants, one of whom he shall choose from among the voters present at the opening of the polling station, and the other voters shall choose the second assistant from among themselves, provided that the two assistants know how to read and write; the presiding officer of the polling station shall record the names of the two assistants in the minutes of the polling station provided for in this Law along with taking their signatures, and the Governor or the District Commissioner may appoint reserve employees when necessary.

3 - The presiding officer of the polling station and the clerk must be present throughout the duration of the electoral process.

4 - The presiding officer of the polling station alone shall enjoy the authority to maintain order inside the polling station, and no member of the security forces may be present inside the polling station except at his request, temporarily and exclusively for the purpose of ensuring the safety of the electoral process.

5 - The presiding officer of the polling station shall not be entitled under any circumstances to prevent candidates or their delegates and accredited observers from exercising the right to monitor the electoral operations, nor to expel any delegate of a candidate or of a list unless he commits a breach of order despite having been warned and such warning having been recorded in the minutes.

6 - If the presiding officer of the polling station takes such a measure, he shall be required to draw up minutes thereof in which he mentions the facts and reasons that necessitated taking such measure and the time of its occurrence, and all other delegates present shall sign it with him, and it shall be submitted immediately to the competent Registration Committee.

7 - Any employee who fails, without a legitimate excuse, to report to the polling station centre in which he was appointed as presiding officer or clerk shall be punished by imprisonment for a period of one month or by a fine of one million Lebanese pounds. In this case, only medical reports submitted by the official medical committee shall be accepted.

8 - Either the presiding officer of the polling station or its clerk, if he breaches the obligations imposed upon him and fails to follow the procedures prescribed for him in this Law, shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to three years or by a fine from one million to three million Lebanese pounds. In this case, and notwithstanding the provisions of Article 61 of the Civil Servants Law issued by Legislative Decree No. 112 /59 dated 12/6/1959, the public prosecution shall be initiated by a personal claim filed by the candidate, or upon the prosecution of the Public Prosecutor's Office, or upon a request from the head of the competent Registration Committee, and the prosecution shall not require the approval of the administration to which this employee belongs.

On Polling Hours:

Polling operations across all of Lebanon shall commence at seven o'clock in the morning and shall conclude at nineteen hundred hours, and shall last for one day, which shall always be a Sunday.

On the Voting of Polling Station Staff:

The Ministry shall organise, in each electoral constituency, a polling operation dedicated to the staff seconded to manage the polling stations, on the Thursday preceding election day.

The ballot boxes pertaining to the staff polling stations shall be closed after counting the number of papers contained in each ballot box, and shall be sent immediately, closed, under the escort of the security forces to the Bank of Lebanon or one of its branches. At the end of the polling operation on Sunday, these ballot boxes shall be sent to the competent Registration Committee to be counted by it and to have their results added to the results of the remaining ballot boxes, and the rules provided for in Chapter Eleven of this Law shall be observed in this operation.

On the Checklists:

1 - The Ministry - the Directorate General of Political Affairs and Refugees - shall issue, on the basis of the electoral lists, checklists, which shall be adopted in all polling stations on Lebanese territory and abroad. Each checklist shall include, in addition to the information contained in the electoral list, the identity card number, and the passport number if available on the date of drawing up these lists, as well as three columns, the first dedicated to the signature of the voter, the second to the signature of the polling station member assigned to verify the voting and the third to observations that may accompany the polling operation.

2 - All pages of the checklist pertaining to each polling station shall be bound together, numbered and initialled with the seal of the Ministry.

3 - No person may vote unless his name is registered on the checklist pertaining to the polling station or if he has obtained from the competent Registration Committee a decision to register his name before the twenty-fifth of the month of March after consulting the Ministry.

On Agents:

1 - Every candidate within a list shall have the right to delegate voters from the electoral constituency to enter the polling station at a rate of at most one fixed agent for each polling station. It shall also have the right to choose roving agents to enter all polling stations in the constituency from among the voters in the latter at a rate of one agent for every two polling stations in villages and one agent for every three polling stations in cities.

2 - The Governor or the District Commissioner shall issue special permits to the agents in accordance with procedures determined by the Ministry.

On Maintaining Security:

The forces tasked with security shall ensure the maintenance of order at the entrances of the polling centers and in their vicinity, and any electoral or promotional activity, particularly loudspeakers, loud music, party flags, and motorcades, shall be prohibited within the vicinity of the polling center.

On Polling Station Supplies:

1 - The Ministry shall supply the polling stations with the supplies, stationery, and printed materials required by the electoral process, and it shall also supply each polling station with a ballot box made of a solid, transparent material with a single slot.

2 - The Ministry shall supply the heads of polling stations with a number of official ballot papers pre-printed by it and their stamped envelopes exactly equal to the number of registered voters, and it shall also deliver to them an additional number of official ballot papers and unstamped envelopes at a rate of 20% of the number of registered voters.

3 - A polling station shall have one or more voting booths.

4 - It shall be prohibited to conduct any electoral process without the presence of the voting booth, under penalty of nullity of the process in the polling station concerned.

On Ballot Papers:

1 - Voting shall take place by means of the official ballot papers provided for in the provisions of this Law, which the Ministry prepares in advance for each minor constituency and distributes with the electoral materials to the polling station officials.

2 - The official ballot papers shall include the names of all lists and their members, and they shall also include the specifications determined in the model prepared by the Ministry, particularly: the color of the list, its name, and a blank square designated for each one of them, the full three-part name of each candidate, his confessional denomination, and the minor constituency or the constituency not composed of minor constituencies for which he is running. Next to the name of each candidate shall be placed a photograph of him, and next to it a blank square designated for the voter to exercise his right to cast, from within the list, his preferential vote in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

3 - The voter shall vote exclusively with these papers to the exclusion of all others, and he may not use any other papers in order to exercise the right to vote.

On Preparatory Procedures:

1- Prior to commencing the voting process, the presiding officer of the polling station shall open the ballot box and verify, together with the polling station committee and the delegates, that it is empty, and shall then lock it securely in accordance with the instructions of the Ministry.

2 - Throughout the electoral process, an official copy of the electoral roll pertaining to each polling station and a copy of the decision of the Minister establishing and designating the polling station shall be posted at its entrance. A copy of the Electoral Law and a list of the names of the candidates' delegates shall be placed on a table in the polling station room, in addition to posters and explanatory materials concerning the course of the electoral process, such that voters, candidates, and their delegates may inspect them.

3 - Prior to the start of the electoral process and until its conclusion, every picture, symbol, writing, or slogan of any kind whatsoever, save for the explanatory materials provided by the Ministry, shall be removed from inside every polling station, under the responsibility of the presiding officer of the polling station.

4 - Prior to commencing the voting process, the presiding officer of the polling station shall verify that the number of ballot papers is exactly equal to the number of registered voters.

If a shortage occurs in the number of ballot papers due to force majeure aimed at impugning the validity of the vote or for any other reason, the presiding officer of the polling station shall replace those papers with the supplementary papers which he received and which he must stamp with the seal of the polling station together with the date, and the reason for such replacement shall be indicated in the minutes. Unused supplementary ballot papers shall be annexed to the minutes.

5 - Permanent and roving delegates shall be permitted to use computers, electronic tablets, and mobile telephones inside the polling stations.

On the voting procedure:

1 - Upon the voter's entry into the polling station, the Presiding Officer of the polling station shall verify his identity on the basis of his identity card or his valid ordinary Lebanese passport. Where there is a material discrepancy in the civil status particulars between the identity card or the passport, on the one hand, and the checklists, on the other hand, the number of the identity card or the number of the passport shall prevail.

2 - After the polling station officers verify that the voter's name is entered on the checklists pertaining to the polling station, the Presiding Officer of the polling station shall provide the voter with the ballot paper, after he and the clerk have signed the back of the paper, and with an envelope stamped with the official seal after he has signed it, and shall instruct him to proceed mandatorily behind the voting booth to exercise his electoral right freely, under penalty of being barred from voting.

3 - The voter shall choose the list or the name of the candidate in accordance with Article 98 of this Law.

The voter shall approach the polling station officers and show the Presiding Officer thereof that he is carrying only one stamped, folded ballot paper; the Presiding Officer of the polling station shall verify this without touching the paper and shall authorise him to place it with his own hand into the ballot box.

4 - The Presiding Officer of the polling station must ensure that the voter has gone into the voting booth alone, under penalty of being barred from voting. The voter is prohibited from displaying the ballot paper upon exiting the voting booth.

5 - The casting of the voter's vote shall be attested by his signature on the checklists and by the placement of a special mark on his finger, the materials for which shall be provided by the Ministry to all polling stations, provided that such mark is of a kind that does not wear off for at least 24 hours; any voter bearing this mark on his finger shall be barred from voting again.

6 - The Presiding Officer of the polling station must, under penalty of liability, bar any voter from casting his vote if he fails to observe the provisions of paragraph 4 of this Article.

7 - No voter shall be entitled to appoint any other person as proxy to exercise the right to vote.

On Voting by Persons with Special Needs:

1- A voter with special needs, in accordance with the provisions of the Law on the Rights of Disabled Persons, who suffers from an impairment that renders him unable to record his choice, place the ballot paper in the envelope and insert it into the ballot box, shall be entitled to seek the assistance of another voter of his own choosing to help him do so under the supervision of the polling station committee. Reference to this fact shall be made in the column designated for remarks on the checklists.

2 - The Ministry shall take into consideration the needs of disabled persons when organising the electoral operations and shall facilitate for them the procedures that allow them to exercise their right to vote without obstacles.

The Ministry shall lay down the detailed rules for the implementation of this Article after consulting the associations of disabled persons.

On the Closing of the Voting Process:

The president of the polling station shall declare the close of the voting process by seven o'clock in the evening, unless there are voters present in the courtyard of the polling centre who have not yet cast their votes, in which case the period shall be extended until they are enabled to vote and reference to this fact shall be made in the minutes.

On Voting for the List and the Preferential Vote:

1 - Every voter may vote for one list from among the competing lists, and he shall be entitled to cast one preferential vote for a candidate from the minor electoral constituency within the list that he has chosen.

2 - Where the voter does not cast a preferential vote, his vote shall remain valid, and only the list shall be counted. However, if he casts more than one preferential vote within the list, no preferential vote shall be counted and the list alone shall be counted.

3 - Where the voter votes for a list and casts a preferential vote within another list or within a list for a minor constituency other than that to which he belongs, no preferential vote shall be counted and the list alone shall be counted.

4 - Where the voter does not vote for any list and casts a preferential vote within a single list, the list and the preferential vote shall be counted.

In the proportional system:
