1 - The number of seats allocated to each list shall be determined on the basis of the electoral quotient.

2 - In order to determine the electoral quotient, the number of voters in each major electoral constituency shall be divided by the number of seats therein.

3 - The lists that did not obtain the electoral quotient shall be excluded from the calculation of seats, and the electoral quotient shall be determined anew after deducting the votes obtained by these lists.

4 - The remaining seats shall be awarded to the qualifying lists that obtained the largest remainder of the votes remaining from the first division in order of rank, provided that this operation is repeated in the same manner until all remaining seats are distributed.

In the event that one seat remains and the largest remainder is tied between two qualifying lists, the seat shall be awarded to the list that had obtained the greater number of seats. In the event that both lists hold the same seats, the seat shall then be awarded to the list whose candidate, who ranked first, obtained the highest percentage of preferential votes. In the event of a tie in the percentage of preferential votes for the first-ranked candidates on both lists, the seat shall be awarded to the list whose candidate, who ranked second, obtained the highest percentage of preferential votes. And so forth.

5 - After determining the number of seats obtained by each qualifying list, the names of the candidates shall be arranged on a single roster from highest to lowest in accordance with the percentage of preferential votes obtained by each candidate in his minor constituency or in his constituency that is not composed of minor constituencies.

The percentage of preferential votes for each candidate shall be calculated on the basis of dividing his preferential votes by the total preferential votes obtained by the qualifying lists in the minor constituency or in the constituency that is not composed of minor constituencies.

In the event of a tie in the percentage of preferential votes between two candidates, the older candidate shall take precedence in the ranking, and if they are of equal age, recourse shall be had to drawing lots by the Higher Registration Committee.

6 - The operation of distributing the seats to the winning candidates shall take place starting from the top of the single roster that includes all the candidates on the lists; thus, the first seat shall be given to the candidate who obtained the highest percentage of preferential votes, and the second seat shall be awarded to the candidate holding the second rank on the roster regardless of the list to which he belongs, and so on with respect to the third seat until all the seats of the constituency are distributed to the candidates belonging to the remaining qualifying lists.

7 - In distributing the seats to the lists, the following two conditions shall be observed:

- That the seat is vacant in accordance with the confessional distribution of seats and/or in the minor constituency, as once the quota of a denomination and/or the minor constituency within the electoral constituency is filled, the remaining candidates of this denomination and/or minor constituency shall be automatically eliminated from the competition after it has fulfilled its quota of seats.

- That the list has not fulfilled its specified share of seats; thus, if the distribution operation reaches a candidate belonging to a list that has fulfilled its quota of seats, this candidate shall be bypassed in favour of the candidate who follows him.

On the Vote Counting Operations Inside the Polling Stations:

Following the close of the polling process, the polling door shall be locked and no one shall be permitted to remain inside the station except the polling station officers, the fixed and/or roving delegates of the lists, the accredited observers, and the representatives of the media holding a permit from the Commission for coverage and filming inside the polling stations.

The president of the station shall open the ballot box and the papers contained therein shall be counted; if their number exceeds or falls short of the number of names that voted on the checklists, this shall be indicated in the minutes.

The president shall open each paper separately, and shall read aloud the name of each list voted for by the voters and then the name of the candidate who obtained the preferential votes on each list, under the effective supervision of the candidates or their delegates, and the accredited observers if present.

On Equipping the Polling Stations:

The Ministry must equip the polling stations with special cameras and television sets such that the camera device is directed at the ballot paper in a manner that allows its contents to appear on the television screen, thereby enabling the members of the polling station committee, the candidates' delegates, and the accredited observers to easily view the lists and the names contained therein during the vote counting process.

On Invalid Papers:

Every paper that includes any additional mark other than those set forth in the provisions of this Law shall be deemed invalid, and every unofficial ballot paper shall also be deemed invalid.

The president of the station must attach the invalid papers to the minutes after they are signed by the polling station officers, and the reasons requiring the attachment shall be mentioned therein, provided that their number is deducted from the total number of voters.

On Blank Papers:

Papers that do not include any vote for a list and for preferential votes shall be considered blank papers and shall be counted among the number of counted voters' votes.

On the Announcement of the Result of the Station:

1 - Following the counting of the official ballot papers, the president shall announce the provisional result and sign it, and shall immediately affix the announcement containing this result to the door of the polling station, and shall give each of the candidates or their delegates a certified true copy of this announcement upon their request.

2 - The announcement shall include the number of votes obtained by each list and the number of preferential votes obtained by each candidate.

On the minutes of the polling station:

Upon the announcement of the provisional result of the voting in the polling station, the president of the polling station shall draw up minutes of the proceedings in two copies, all pages of which shall be signed by the members of the polling station board.

The president of the polling station shall place in a special file the voter checklists signed by the voters, all ballot papers, the aforementioned minutes of the proceedings, and the tally sheet of the votes for the lists and candidates.

This envelope shall be sealed with red wax and transported by the president of the polling station and his assistant to the centre of the Registration Committee under security escort, where it shall be delivered together with the documents contained therein to the President of the Registration Committee or his delegate, who shall subsequently open it in the presence of the candidates' representatives.

The president of the polling station and the clerk shall be held liable if the envelope arrives open or not in conformity with the announcement.

On the vote counting operations before the Registration Committees:

1 - The competent Registration Committee shall receive all the minutes of the polling stations falling within its jurisdiction. Delivery shall take place through the president of the polling station pursuant to minutes drawn up for this purpose. The Ministry shall provide the supplies necessary for the work of the Registration Committee, in particular a large transparent container to hold the ballot papers, a programmed computer and a large screen to display the results, in addition to any other equipment that ensures the proper computerisation of the electoral process.

2 - The Registration Committees shall examine the minutes and documents and take the necessary decisions thereon.

The process of counting the votes for each polling station shall begin through the programmed computer, which shall carry out the counting process automatically.

The count shall be repeated manually if there is a discrepancy in the number of votes between the results of the polling station minutes and the results of the programmed computer.

After verifying the number of votes obtained by each list and each candidate and totalling them, the result of the totalling of the votes shall be submitted in accordance with tables and minutes drawn up by the Registration Committee in two copies, after being signed by all its members, to the Higher Registration Committee in the major electoral constituency.

The Directorate General of Political Affairs and Refugees at the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities shall appoint an employee to receive the envelopes of the polling stations, the ballot papers and the documents attached thereto successively, after the Registration Committee has completed its work on each envelope, and the said employee shall sign a receipt statement for each envelope and its documents.

On the announcement of the final results:

The Higher Registration Committee in the electoral constituency shall receive the figures submitted to it by the Registration Committees in the electoral constituency concerned.

The Higher Registration Committee shall audit the schedules and minutes, and it shall be entitled to rectify clerical and arithmetical errors only, if any, and shall rectify the result in the light thereof.

It shall then undertake the aggregation of the votes received from the Primary Registration Committees by means of an automated computer programmed for this purpose, and shall record the final result in the electoral constituency on the final schedule in figures and words written out in full, and all its members shall sign the minutes and the final general schedule.

It shall thereupon announce, before the candidates or their delegates, the final results with the number of seats won by each list and the names of the winning candidates.

The Higher Registration Committee shall deliver to the Governor or the Qaimaqam, each within his respective jurisdiction, the final minutes and the general schedule of results, and shall draw up minutes of delivery and receipt signed by the Governor or the Qaimaqam and one of the members of the Higher Registration Committee designated by the President of the Committee.

The results, together with the final minutes and the general schedule appended thereto, shall be sent forthwith to the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities, which shall undertake the announcement of the official final results and the names of the winning candidates, and the Minister shall notify this result forthwith to the Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies and to the President of the Constitutional Council.

On the preservation of ballot papers:

The ballot papers shall be preserved on a confidential basis at the Bank of Lebanon in bundles indicating the polling stations from which they originated, for a period of three months from the date of the announcement of the results, whereafter they shall be destroyed by the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities pursuant to minutes drawn up in accordance with due form, unless they are the subject of an application for review or challenge before the Constitutional Council.

On Specific Cases of Incompatibility:

1 - Membership of the Chamber of Deputies may not be combined with the presidency or membership of the board of directors of any public institution or any institution of public law, or a post in a public administration, a public institution, a municipality, a union of municipalities, a concessionary company, a mixed-economy company, or a company with public capital.

Membership of the Chamber of Deputies may also not be combined with any religious office the holder of which receives any salary or allowance from the State Treasury.

Anyone among these who is elected as a Deputy shall be deemed dismissed ipso jure from his office if he does not notify his refusal of membership of the Chamber of Deputies within a month following the announcement of the result of his election.

2 - Membership of the Chamber of Deputies may not be combined with legal representation for the State or one of its services or public institutions, or for municipalities or unions of municipalities, or for any of the institutions or companies mentioned in the first paragraph of this Article.

Anyone among these legal representatives who is elected as a Deputy shall have his mandate deemed lapsed ipso jure.

On Prohibited Professional Activities:

A Deputy shall not be granted any monopoly, concession, or public contract from the State, public institutions, or municipalities, and his spouse and his children shall be deemed as a single person.

On the Right of the Non-Resident to Vote:

Every Lebanese non-resident on Lebanese territory has the right to exercise the right to vote in polling centres at embassies or consulates or in other places determined by the Ministry in accordance with the provisions of this Law and in coordination with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants, provided that his name is entered in the personal status registers and that there is no legal impediment preventing his right to vote pursuant to the provisions of the fourth Article of this Law.

On Candidates for Non-Residents:

The seats allocated in the Chamber of Deputies for non-residents are six, determined equally between Christians and Muslims, distributed as follows: Maronite - Orthodox - Catholic - Sunni - Shia - Druze, and equally among the six continents.

The enforcement of Article 112 of the Law on the Election of Members of the Chamber of Deputies No. 44 dated 17/6/2017 shall be suspended, exceptionally and for one time, exclusively for the parliamentary electoral cycle scheduled to be held in the spring of the year 2022. Provided that the aforementioned Article shall return into force in the cycles that follow. (Pursuant to Law Enforceable Ipso Jure No. 8 dated 3/11/2021)

By way of exception and for one time for the purpose of conducting the parliamentary elections after the issuance of this Law exclusively, namely Law in force ipso jure No. 8 dated 3/11/2021

On the registration of voters:

The Ministry, in coordination with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants through the Lebanese embassies and consulates abroad, shall invite Lebanese who fulfil the conditions mentioned above to declare their wish to vote abroad, by registering their names through their personal attendance or pursuant to a signed and duly authenticated letter or pursuant to electronic registration in the event of its adoption.

The Ministry, in cooperation with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants, shall lay down the rules for the registration of non-resident electors in the embassies or consulates that they choose, together with all required information relating to their identity, their register number, their confession and the number of their ordinary Lebanese passport where available.

The time limit granted for the registration of Lebanese electors not residing on Lebanese territory must not exceed the twentieth of the month of November of the year 2021. Thereafter, the right to vote abroad shall lapse, and the embassies must send these lists successively to the Directorate General of Personal Status through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants before the first of December 2021.

On the separate electoral lists:

The competent departments at the Directorate General of Personal Status shall verify the entry of the name in the register and shall draw up, after the expiry of the time limit granted for registration, separate electoral lists for each embassy or consulate containing the names of those who will fulfil the legal conditions, provided that the number of registered persons in a single polling centre shall not be less than 200 electors, and shall place a notation preventing the possibility of their voting in their original place of residence in addition to mentioning the place of registration abroad.

On the polling process:

Polling abroad shall take place on the basis of the proportional system and a single electoral constituency at most 15 days before the date appointed for the elections in Lebanon, by means of pre-printed ballot papers adopted by the Ministry and stamped with its seal.

Ballot boxes shall be opened from seven o'clock in the morning until ten o'clock at night.

Upon the entry of the voter into the polling station, the president of the polling station shall verify his identity, on the basis of his identity card or his valid ordinary Lebanese passport and the inclusion of his name on the independent electoral list referred to in the Article and referred to in this Law.

Where there is a material discrepancy in the particulars between the identity card or passport on the one hand and the independent electoral lists on the other hand, the identity card number or passport number shall prevail.

After the polling station committee verifies that the name of the voter is included in the independent electoral list pertaining to the polling station, the president of the polling station shall provide the voter with the ballot paper and with an envelope stamped with the official seal after signing it.

The general provisions governing the polling of Lebanese resident in Lebanon which do not conflict with the provisions of this Law shall apply to the polling process of Lebanese non-resident on Lebanese territory.

The application of the first paragraph of Article 118 of the Law on the Election of Members of the Chamber of Deputies No. 44 dated 17/6/2017 shall be suspended, exceptionally and for one time, exclusively for the parliamentary election cycle scheduled to be held in the spring of the year 2022. Provided that the above-mentioned first paragraph of Article 118 shall return to force in the cycles that follow. (Pursuant to Law Enforceable ipso jure No. 8 dated 3/11/2021)

On counting and distributing the papers:

After the conclusion of the polling process, the polling station committee shall open the ballot box or boxes in the presence of the ambassador or the consul in person or whoever they delegate in the event that their attendance is not possible.

The polling station committee shall count the papers in the presence of the accredited delegates, observers and media outlets if present, and shall place the papers pertaining to the constituency in a special large envelope on which the name of the polling station is recorded and which is sealed with red wax.

Exceptionally and for one time only for the purpose of holding the parliamentary elections exclusively after the issuance of this Law, namely Law Enacted by Operation of Law No. 8 dated 3/11/2021

On the announcement and revision of the separate electoral rolls:

1- The Ministry shall, before the fifteenth of December 2021, send, through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants, to the embassies and consulates of Lebanon abroad, the preliminary electoral rolls containing the names of the persons who have expressed their wish to vote abroad in accordance with the provisions of this Law, in the form of compact discs (CD).

2 - The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants shall publish and circulate the above rolls by all possible means and invite the voters to inspect them and revise them where necessary. Each embassy and consulate shall provide copies of these rolls at its premises and publish them on its website, if available.

3 - Every interested party shall have the right to submit an objection to the electoral rolls before the embassy or consulate, accompanied by the required documents and supporting instruments. The embassy or consulate shall verify them and send them to the Ministry through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants before the twentieth of February of each year. The operations of revising the rolls and correcting and striking off registrations shall be subject to the rules and procedures provided for in Chapter Four of this Law.

Exceptionally and for one time only for the purpose of holding the parliamentary elections exclusively after the issuance of this Law, namely Law Enacted by Operation of Law No. 8 dated 3/11/2021

On the designation of polling stations

Polling stations shall be designated by a decision issued by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities after coordination with the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants, at least twenty days before the date set for holding the elections.

On the polling station officers:

The Ambassador or Consul shall, in coordination with the Ministry, through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants, appoint the officers of each polling station, provided that they are not fewer than a president and a clerk from among the employees working at the embassy or consulate, or from among contractors where necessary, provided that they are Lebanese and that all relevant Lebanese laws apply to them, and provided that the powers of each of them are defined.

Agents of candidates may be present during the voting procedures after obtaining permits issued by the embassy or consulate.

On the Deposit of Envelopes and the Remaining Electoral Documents:

Each polling station shall draw up a record of the electoral operation in two copies, stating the number of voters, those who cast votes, and the number of ballot papers. This record shall be signed by the polling station board and by the accredited agents present, if any. One copy thereof shall remain in the embassy or consulate in the custody of the ambassador or consul, and the second copy shall be sent immediately, together with the large special envelopes pertaining to the ballot papers and the remaining electoral documents, to the Bank of Lebanon through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants.

At the end of the voting operation on the Sunday scheduled for holding the parliamentary elections in Lebanon, the said envelopes shall be sent, together with the remaining electoral documents, to the Higher Registration Committee in Beirut to be sorted by it and to have their results documented, and the rules stipulated in this Law regarding the safety of transport and the monitoring of sorting shall be observed in this operation.

On Vacancy in the Constituency of Lebanese Residing Abroad:

If any seat of the Chamber of Deputies in the constituency of Lebanese residing abroad becomes vacant due to death, resignation, invalidation of the mandate, or for any other reason, by-elections shall be held to fill the vacant seat on the same bases adopted for the election of residents.

No successor shall be elected if the vacancy occurs in the last six months prior to the expiration of the mandate of the Chamber.

The enforcement of the first paragraph of Article 121 of Law No. 44 dated 17/6/2017 on the Election of Members of the Chamber of Deputies shall be suspended, exceptionally and for one time, exclusively for the parliamentary election cycle scheduled to be held in the spring of the year 2022. Provided that the first paragraph of the aforementioned Article 121 shall return into force in the subsequent cycles. (Pursuant to Law in Force ipso jure No. 8 d. 3/11/2021)

The minimum for salaries and wages in public administrations, municipalities, federations of municipalities, the Lebanese University, and public institutions not subject to the Labour Law is raised to /675.000/ L.L. (six hundred and seventy-five thousand Lebanese pounds).

On the six seats allocated to non-residents:

Six seats for non-residents shall be added to the number of members of the Chamber of Deputies so that it becomes 134 members in the electoral cycle that will follow the first electoral cycle to be held in accordance with this Law.

In the subsequent cycle, six seats shall be reduced from the 128 members of the Chamber of Deputies from the same confessions allocated to non-residents in Article 112 of this Law, by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister.

On the application of the provisions of this Chapter:

A joint committee from the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants shall be established pursuant to a decision issued by the two Ministers, the task of which shall be to apply the details of the provisions of this Chapter.

On the details of the application of the Law:

The details of the application of this Law shall be determined by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers by a two-thirds majority upon the proposal of the Minister of Interior and Municipalities.

On the repeal of contrary provisions:

All provisions contrary to the provisions of this Law are hereby repealed, in particular Law No. 25 dated 8-10-2008, with the exception of the provisions of the articles relating to parliamentary by-elections with respect to cases in which the majoritarian electoral system applies, and municipal and mukhtar elections.

On the entry into force of the Law:

This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette, with its promulgation expedited in accordance with the first paragraph of Article /56/ of the Constitution.

There shall be added to the monthly allowance received by contracted personnel in the public administrations, administrative contracted personnel in the Lebanese University, and contracted personnel in the temporary cadre of the Green Plan and in the Council of the South, a cost-of-living increase calculated in accordance with the following mechanism:

1 - The value of the increase added pursuant to Law No. 63 dated 31/12/2008 shall be deducted from the monthly allowance.

2 - A cost-of-living increase shall be added to the balance at the rate of:

- 100 % on the first bracket thereof up to 400 thousand Lebanese Pounds, provided that the increase shall not be less than 375 thousand Lebanese Pounds.

- 9 % on the second bracket thereof that exceeds 400 thousand Lebanese Pounds and does not exceed one million five hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds.

- Nothing on the bracket that exceeds one million five hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds.

3 - The difference between the total amount resulting from the preceding paragraph and the monthly allowance that the contracted person was receiving on 31/1/2012 shall be calculated, and this difference shall be the increase that is added to the monthly allowance that the contracted person was receiving on 31/1/2012.

4 - The monthly allowances of contracted personnel may not, as a result of their increase in the manner set forth above, fall below the salary of the corresponding or closest step in the salary scale of the post identical or similar to their duties after its conversion in accordance with the tables annexed to this Law with effect from the date of its entry into force.

A cost-of-living increase shall be added to the wage received by permanent and temporary wage earners and invoice-based wage earners (who receive monthly allowances deemed equivalent to a salary or wage) in public administrations, in the Lebanese University, in the Executive Office of the Green Plan, and in the Council of the South, calculated in accordance with the following mechanism:

1 - The value of the increase that was added pursuant to Law No. 63 dated 31/12/2008 shall be deducted from the monthly wage.

2 - A cost-of-living increase shall be added to the balance at the rate of:

- 100 % on the first bracket thereof up to 400 thousand Lebanese pounds, provided that the increase shall not be less than 375 thousand Lebanese pounds.

- 9 % on the second bracket thereof that exceeds 400 thousand Lebanese pounds and does not exceed one million five hundred thousand Lebanese pounds.

- Nothing on the bracket that exceeds one million five hundred thousand Lebanese pounds.

3 - The difference between the total amount resulting from the preceding paragraph and the monthly wage that the wage earner was receiving on 31/1/2012 shall be calculated, and this difference shall be the increase added to the monthly wage that the wage earner was receiving on 31/1/2012.

4 - For the purpose of calculating the value of the daily wage, the new monthly wage shall be divided by thirty and any fraction of one thousand pounds shall be rounded up to one thousand pounds in favour of the beneficiary.

- Contractual personnel teaching by the hour in the field of public pre-university education, vocational and technical education, and higher education shall be granted a cost-of-living increase, provided that the new hourly rate is determined by a joint decision issued by the Minister of Finance and the competent Minister, after consulting the Civil Service Board, taking into consideration the increases granted previously.

- The monthly allowances of contractual personnel duly contracted under annual contracts with the Department of Agricultural Education and Extension to teach in public agricultural schools may not be less than the salary of the corresponding or closest step in the salary scale of the post similar or comparable to their duties in the cadre of public agricultural education after its conversion in accordance with the tables annexed to this Law.

The provisions of this Law shall apply to members of the teaching staff in private schools who are tenured in the cadre.

A contractual teacher in private schools shall benefit, at a percentage calculated on the basis of the number of his weekly teaching hours, from the increase accrued to those tenured in the cadre in the said schools as a result of the converted scale of ranks and salaries.

The Judicial Recess

The duration of the annual judicial recess for each judge shall be one month and a half, and it shall be for the Supreme Judicial Council, the Bureau of the State Council, and the Council of the Court of Accounts to determine its timing for each section, chamber, or judicial department within the period falling between 15 July and 30 September of each year.

- Mondays, Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays: from eight o'clock in the morning until fifteen thirty hours.

- And on Friday from eight o'clock in the morning until fifteen hundred hours, provided that two hours are granted for prayer.
