Half-time working hours for the married female employee

- A married female employee may benefit from half-time working hours for personal reasons for a maximum period of three years during her period of service, and half-time working hours means that the beneficiary of such working hours works half the number of hours legally prescribed, provided that the rounding of the hour shall be in favour of the administration.

- Half-time working hours shall be granted by decision of the Minister after the approval of the Civil Service Board, pursuant to a reasoned request from the person concerned.

- The period of half-time working hours shall be set at twelve consecutive months which may be renewed for the same period, and the female employee may not be assigned overtime work throughout the period of her benefiting from half-time working hours.

- The request to benefit from half-time working hours shall be submitted in writing one month prior to the date on which the benefit commences, and the request for its renewal shall be submitted in writing, where applicable, one month prior to the date of its expiry. As for a married female member of the teaching staff who wishes to benefit from half-time working hours, she must submit the request to benefit in writing between the first of June and the fifth of July of the academic year during which it is intended to benefit from half-time working hours.

- A beneficiary of half-time working hours shall be entitled to half of the salary; as for family allowances, the benefits of the State Employees' Cooperative and other allowances or benefits, she shall continue to benefit from them in full, provided that the full mandatory monthly contribution legally due in favour of the Cooperative is deducted from the half-salaries disbursed to her.

- A beneficiary of these working hours shall be prohibited from engaging in any paid work or any profession of whatever kind in accordance with what is required by the fourth paragraph of Article fifteen of the Staff Regulations, under penalty of revocation of this measure at any time her violation of this prohibition is established, in addition to the incurring of disciplinary liability in accordance with the regulations in force.

- Notwithstanding any other provision, one year of half-time working hours shall be counted as half a year of actual service in respect of step advancement and end-of-service indemnity, retirement pension, or pension deductions.

Overtime work

- The maximum number of hours of assignment to overtime work shall be fixed at thirty-five hours per month as a maximum.

- Direct and hierarchical superiors and the Central Inspection shall bear the responsibility of supervising overtime work and verifying its performance in accordance with the rules, and all concerned administrations and those working therein must facilitate the work of the inspectors and enable them to carry out their duties.

The text of Article 25 of Legislative Decree No. 47 dated 29/6/1983 (Retirement and Dismissal from Service System) is repealed and replaced by the following text:

- If a civil servant dies, and his period of service is less than ten years, the Lebanese beneficiaries among the members of his family shall be granted the full dismissal indemnity to which he was entitled on the date of death.

If his services have exceeded ten years, the members of his family referred to above shall have the right to benefit from the retirement pension if they opt for this pension. Under no circumstances may the retirement pension be lower than the official minimum wage in force at any time.

Addition of a paragraph to the text of Article 26 of Legislative Decree No. 47 dated 29/6/1983 and its amendments (Retirement and Dismissal from Service System)

There shall be added to the text of Article 26 of Legislative Decree No. 47 dated 29/6/1983 and its amendments (Retirement and Dismissal from Service System) the new paragraph reading as follows:

"The pension shall be discontinued for married infirm male children if their male sons have completed the eighteenth year of their age, or the twenty-fifth year in the event that they are pursuing their studies, unless, in both cases, the latter are infirm and incapable of earning a living and their infirmity is established by a report from the Permanent Medical Committee provided for in Article 22 of this Legislative Decree.
The salary of a civil servant shall not resume running after its suspension for any reason whatsoever except upon the resumption by this civil servant of his duties in accordance with the due rules.

Preservation of the right to seniority

- A civil servant who is promoted from the Second Category to the First Category shall retain half the number of steps that he held in his previous category.

- For the purpose of determining the new basic salary of the civil servant concerned, the steps which he has retained and which are referred to above shall be added to the step of his appointment in the salary scale pertaining to his new post, and a half-step, where it exists, shall be considered one year of seniority.

- These provisions shall apply to civil servants who have been or are promoted to the First Category after 1/1/1999, and their basic salary shall be reconstituted in accordance with the provisions set out above without this entailing any sums or financial rights for the period prior to the date of entry into force of this Law.

Provisions Relating to the Appointment of Teachers in Public Basic Education

With effect from the date of publication of this Law in the Official Gazette, Article Six of Law No. 223 dated 2/4/2012 is hereby repealed, and the following provisions shall be adopted for the appointment of teachers in public basic education:

- Teachers in public basic education who hold a university degree and a teaching degree shall be appointed at the ninth step of the unified scale for members of the teaching staff.

- Persons concerned under the provisions of this Article shall not benefit from the exceptional steps provided for in Law No. 344 dated 6/8/2001. As for holders of a university degree who may obtain a teaching degree after their appointment, they shall benefit from two exceptional steps only in accordance with the rules provided for in the aforementioned Law.

- Under no circumstances may the salaries of the persons concerned by the provisions of this Article, as a result of the reconstitution of their financial status, fall below the salaries they were receiving prior to the promulgation of this Law.

Establishment of a Unified System of Social Benefits (Marriage Grant, Birth Grant, Education Grant, Death Assistance) Covering All Workers in the Public Sector

Within a period of one year from the date of entry into force of this Law, the Government shall establish a unified system of social benefits (marriage grant, birth grant, education grant, death assistance) covering all workers in the public sector, to be applied in the Civil Servants' Cooperative, the mutual funds of judicial and Sharia judges and professors of the Lebanese University, all military corps, public institutions, councils, bodies, municipalities and federations thereof, by virtue of a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers.

There is hereby added to the text of Paragraph (h) of Article 152 of Law No. 102 dated 16/9/1983, the National Defence Law, the following:

Notwithstanding any other text, positions of the first and second categories may not be reserved for military veterans, as appointment to these two positions shall remain subject to the provisions of the Civil Servants' Regulations.

Employees who were appointed prior to the effective date of this Law shall continue to occupy the position to which they were appointed until the end of their service.

Review of the Subsidy Policy and State Contributions to the Funds

The Government shall, within a period of six months from the date of publication of this Law, review the subsidy policy across the various sectors by conducting a comparative study between the amounts paid and the economic and/or social feasibility resulting from such subsidy, with a view to taking the appropriate decision in the light of the findings of that study, and shall inform the Chamber of Deputies of the outcome of the study.

Limitation of Expenditure on Fuels in Public Administrations

1 - Notwithstanding any other text, it shall be prohibited to expend the fuel appropriations provided for in the budgets of the various public administrations, save for military and civilian vehicles assigned to missions by the competent authority and in the interest of the public service only.

2 - All exemptions from duties, surcharges and royalties are hereby repealed, and the fuels consumed by all military and security agencies and civilian public administrations shall be purchased at the market price.

Evaluation of the Performance of Civil Servants

The Government shall, within six months from the date of entry into force of this Law, establish, by virtue of a draft law, a modern system for job performance evaluation, in the light of the job description across the various administrative cadres, taking into account the criteria of productivity and competence.

Performance evaluation shall be relied upon for holding civil servants accountable in accordance with the texts in force and newly enacted texts, while preserving the jurisdiction of the oversight and disciplinary bodies and the administrative judiciary to hear grievances against any measure affecting civil servants in this context.
This Law, in all its articles, shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Conditions that must be met in the facilities subject to this Law:

Facilities subject to the provisions of this Law must comply at all times with the following conditions:

1.3 Providing enclosed spaces proportionate to the number of animals in terms of area, building materials, designs and maintenance in accordance with the conditions set forth in this Law and any other legislative texts.

2.3 Enabling animals to express their natural behaviour as much as possible, and to interact with animals with which they are compatible of the same species or other species, taking into account the requirements of public safety and comfort.

3.3 Providing suitable equipment for heating, lighting, ventilation and humidity.

4.3 Taking the necessary measures to maintain public hygiene and environmental conditions.

5.3 Providing the necessary equipment to supply the animals with food and water and storing sufficient quantities thereof.

6.3 Surrounding the facility, where necessary, with fences and/or barriers to ensure public safety, the safety of the animals and their non-escape.

7.3 Equipping a place for the quarantine of sick and injured animals to ensure their comfort and the non-transmission of disease until their recovery.

8.3 Physical and visual separation between animals that are not compatible with them.

9.3 Establishing an emergency plan by the owner of the facility to protect the animals during disasters.

10.3 Anything decided by the competent authorities in accordance with the objectives of this Law, after consulting the Ministry of Agriculture.

Definition of terms:

The following terms, wherever they appear in this Law, shall have the meanings set out opposite each of them:

1.1 CITES Convention: the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora.

2.1 IATA Live Animals Regulations: the international standards adopted by the "International Air Transport Association", for the transport of live animals by air.

3.1 Zoo: a facility primarily prepared to shelter wild animals for the purpose of protecting them and educating about them.

4.1 Animals: multicellular organisms in the animal kingdom, including all mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians and fish.

5.1 Wild animal: an undomesticated animal.

6.1 Farm animal: a domesticated animal raised on farms for human consumption or for use in agricultural work.

7.1 Stray animal: a domesticated animal that has no person supervising it or an animal that roams freely.

8.1 Domesticated animal: an animal of a species or breed that has been able over several generations to adapt to the human environment.

9.1 Circus: a facility dedicated to entertaining the public that usually includes acrobatic shows, clowns and animal shows.

10.1 Veterinarian: a holder of a degree in veterinary medicine from a recognised university who fulfils the conditions provided for in the Law on the Practice of Veterinary Medicine in Lebanon.

11.1 Rescue centre: a non-profit facility prepared to shelter domesticated and/or wild animals in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

12.1 Facility: every temporary or permanent establishment or installation regulated in the body of this Law that is owned or managed by a person governed by public or private law in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

13.1 World Organisation for Animal Health (OIE): an intergovernmental organisation concerned with improving animal health.

Objectives of this Law:

This Law aims to protect live animals and ensure their welfare and to regulate the facilities that deal with or use such animals, taking into account the relevant international conventions and recommendations, in particular the CITES Convention and the recommendations of the World Organisation for Animal Health (OIE).

Conditions for the transport of animals:

Subject to the provisions of Articles 3 and 4 of this Law, the transport of animals by land, sea or air shall be subject to the following conditions:

5.1 Compliance with the IATA Live Animals Regulations during operations for transporting animals by air, and with the recommendations of the World Organisation for Animal Health (OIE) during operations for transporting animals by land or by sea, or with the provisions of the CITES Convention regarding the transport of animals listed in its appendices, and with the additional conditions adopted in the exporting and importing country.

5.2 Use of the means of transport, loading and unloading most suitable for animal welfare and for ensuring their safety. The details of the application of this paragraph shall be determined by a decision issued by the Ministry of Agriculture.

5.3 Application of veterinary health measures in accordance with the recommendations of the World Organisation for Animal Health (OIE) during import, export and transit.

5.4 Transport of animals fulfilling the conditions for export or import without delay from or to the facilities and means equipped to house or transport them.

In the event that the conditions for export or import are not fulfilled, the legal rules in force shall apply in a manner that does not conflict with the provisions of this Law and animal welfare.

5.5 Everything decided by the competent authorities in accordance with the objectives of this Law after consulting the opinion of the Ministry of Agriculture.

Killing of animals for prevention against the spread of diseases:

In the event of risks of the spread of a disease transmissible from an animal to any other living organism, a decision may be taken, by a joint decision of the Ministers of Public Health and Agriculture, to euthanise specific animals after verifying that this measure is proportionate to the damage incurred and the necessity of preventing the spread of any contagious or dangerous disease or epidemic, and taking into account the recommendations of the World Organisation for Animal Health (OIE).

The owner shall be obliged to declare the animals present therein and to assist in implementing the measures mentioned above.

Ownership and custody of wild animals:

It shall be prohibited to own or have custody of the animals whose names are listed in Appendix 1 of CITES, whether captured in the wild or born in captivity, as well as endangered or dangerous animals specified by a decision of the Minister of Agriculture, except inside zoos or rescue centres licensed in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

General obligations for dealing with animals:

Every natural or legal person shall observe the following obligations in dealing with animals:

1.4 With the exception of the cases permitted by law, refraining from performing any act capable of causing animals any distress, pain or suffering, or exposing them to danger or torture.

2.4 The obligation to secure the basic needs and vaccines for animals in accordance with their species and age.

3.4 Not organising any fighting between animals or between them and human beings.

4.4 Not using animals in entertainment, exhibitions, advertising campaigns, artistic works and the circus if their use causes pain, harm or suffering to the animals.

5.4 Not offering animals as prizes.

6.4 Adopting one of the cases and means of euthanasia specified by a decision of the Minister of Agriculture, and solely under the supervision of a veterinarian and in accordance with the recommendations of the World Organisation for Animal Health (OIE).

7.4 Immediately notifying the Ministry of Agriculture of any emergency incident relating to the death of three or more animals, or of the appearance of the clinical symptoms of one of the diseases subject to mandatory notification or any epidemic outbreak specified by a decision of the Ministry of Agriculture.

8.4 Notifying the Ministry of Agriculture and the competent security agencies of the escape of any of the animals used in Chapter Five and Article 7 within 6 hours of its occurrence.

9.4 All that the competent authorities decide in accordance with the objectives of this Law, after seeking the opinion of the Ministry of Agriculture.

Obligation to obtain a licence or submit a declaration:

Every establishment for the sale or breeding of animals shall be subject to the obligation to obtain a prior licence or to submit a declaration to the competent authorities in accordance with the laws in force, after consulting the Ministry of Agriculture, and after verifying the fulfilment of the conditions set forth in this Law.

Subject to the provisions of this Law, the Minister of Agriculture shall issue a decision determining the list of animals that are permitted to be sold or bred in these establishments.

In the event of failure by the holder of the licence at any time to comply with the obligations set forth in this Law, the competent authority shall have the right to issue a decision suspending the execution of work under the licence or revoking it and referring it to the competent judiciary.

In the event of failure by the holder of the declaration at any time to comply with the obligations of this Law, the competent authority shall have the right to issue a decision prohibiting the holder of the declaration from carrying out the activities that are the subject of the declaration for a period of one year at most and referring it to the competent judiciary.

Special obligations for establishments for the sale of animals:

In addition to the obligations provided for in Chapter One of this Law, the owner of the establishment shall be bound to fulfil the following obligations:

1.9 Ensuring periodic health supervision over the animals by a veterinarian.

2.9 Keeping records of the sources of the animals displayed in the establishment and the transfer of their custody.

3.9 Subject to Article 7 of this Law, if the animals displayed for sale are imported from abroad and listed in any of the appendices to the CITES Convention, the establishment must retain the documents relating to import and export in accordance with the laws in force. Copies thereof must be delivered to the new custodian.

4.9 Training the workers in the establishment in the care and welfare of animals.

5.9 Keeping a general medical record for the animals present in a single establishment and delivering a health certificate issued by a veterinarian to the new custodian.

6.9 Not exceeding the number of animals permitted in accordance with the specifications and area of the establishment.

7.9 Ensuring the implantation of electronic identification chips by a veterinarian in dogs and animals intended for sale in the establishment. These animals and the types of chips shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Agriculture.

8.9 Refraining from selling any animal to a person under 16 years of age without the express consent of his guardian.

9.9 Refraining from selling stray animals.

Slaughtering of animals:

Slaughtering shall not be permitted except in licensed slaughterhouses and establishments designed for the slaughtering of agricultural animals.

Subject to the provisions of this Law and the recommendations of the World Organisation for Animal Health (OIE), the technical and health conditions to which slaughterhouses and establishments designed for the slaughtering of agricultural animals are subject shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, upon the proposal of the Minister of Agriculture.

Use of animals in work:

It shall be prohibited to employ animals whose health or age does not permit them to work, or where the working conditions or the equipment used therein threaten their safety or growth, exceed their natural capacities, or expose them to any distress, pain, or suffering. The types of animals that may be used in work shall be determined pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Agriculture.

Requirement of prior declaration:

Every scientific experiment in which animals are used shall be subject to the requirement of prior declaration to the Ministry of Agriculture.

The use of animals in scientific experiments shall be restricted to licensed medical institutions, research centres, and universities, and any other entity authorised to use animals in scientific experiments pursuant to a decision issued by the Council of Ministers. The types and number of animals used, as well as the procedures and conditions for the declaration, shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Agriculture.

In the event that the establishment fails at any time to comply with the obligations of this Law, the Minister of Agriculture shall have the right to issue a decision prohibiting the establishment from using animals in scientific experiments for a period of two months and referring it to the competent judiciary.

Specifications of the experimentation centre:

The specifications of experimentation centres shall be determined by a joint decision of the Ministries of Agriculture, Public Health, and Education and Higher Education, provided that they are permanently equipped with the medical supplies necessary for treatment, pain relief, and euthanasia, and in accordance with the recommendations of the World Organisation for Animal Health (OIE).

Special Obligations for Breeding Centres:

In addition to the general conditions, breeding centres shall be subject to special conditions to be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Agriculture, provided that the species, age, safety and health of the animal are taken into consideration therein.

Obligations of the Custodian:

A person wishing to take custody of an animal must comply with the conditions specified in this Law.

A person wishing to take custody of a dog or any other animal specified in the decision of the Minister of Agriculture referred to in item 7.9 of Article 9 above must register the transfer of custody to him with the Ministry of Agriculture, and this may be done through the establishment that carried out the transfer of custody operation or by registered mail.

The custodian shall pay a fee in the amount of fifty thousand Lebanese pounds. Any subsequent assignment of custody shall be registered in accordance with the same procedures and in return for a similar fee.

Persons with disabilities and rescue centres established in accordance with the provisions of Article 23 of this Law shall be exempted from the registration fee.

The custodian must ensure that an electronic microchip is implanted in the body of the animal and that it is not left to stray.

Stray Animals

Without prejudice to the provisions of this Law, and in particular Article 4 thereof, the Ministry of Agriculture shall lay down the general guidelines for dealing with stray animals, including the acceptable means for controlling reproduction and for capturing them, monitoring rabies, the obligation to grant their owners a reasonable period of time to reclaim them, shelter standards and disease control measures.

Municipalities shall lay down a plan for dealing with stray animals based on the guidelines of the Ministry of Agriculture and shall work to implement it either directly or by contracting with one of the entities provided for in Article 23 below.

Obligation to Obtain a Licence:

Without prejudice to the provisions applicable to the granting of licences for the establishment and operation of agricultural animal breeding establishments and slaughterhouses, these establishments shall be subject to the provisions of this Law to the extent compatible with their nature.

A joint decision by the Ministers of Agriculture and of the Interior and Municipalities shall determine the establishments whose nature is compatible with the provisions of this Law.

Filing of Periodic Medical Reports:

Every owner of an agricultural animal breeding establishment shall file with the Ministry of Agriculture, during the first month of every year, a report drawn up by his accredited veterinarian regarding the health status of the animals and the status of the farm in general.

Obligation to obtain prior approval:

The use of animals in the field of entertainment (circuses, animal riding, pulling carts, involving animals in competitions, etc...) shall be subject to the obligation of obtaining prior approval from the Ministry of Agriculture after verifying the fulfilment of the conditions set forth in this Law. The details of implementation of this Article shall be determined pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Agriculture after consulting the opinion of the competent administrations.

The person concerned shall be bound to comply with the conditions set out in this Law under penalty of withdrawal of the approval.

Subject to the provisions of Article 7 of this Law, the Minister of Agriculture may prohibit the use of certain species of animals in certain types of entertainment or competitions for reasons relating to animal welfare.

Operation of a zoological garden:

The operation of a zoological garden shall be subject to the obligation of obtaining the approval of the Ministry of Agriculture after verifying the fulfilment of the conditions set forth in this Law.

In addition to the general conditions set forth in this Law, the granting of prior approval shall require the fulfilment of the following conditions:

1 . That one of the objectives of the project be the conservation of species and animal wealth with regard to biodiversity, the provision of a suitable environment for the animals present in zoological gardens, and the provision of information on the exhibited species.

2 . That the maximum limit of animals that may be placed in the garden be determined according to their species.

That the number of animals present and their species be determined.

3 . That a detailed study be submitted explaining how to raise and meet the needs of each species of animals, in addition to the specifications of the enclosures and the surrounding environment in a manner that allows the animals to behave as much as possible in accordance with their natural behaviour.

4 . That the necessary human resources be secured to respond to the needs of the animals, and that the owner of the facility or at least one of the persons working therein hold a university degree in animal sciences or possess experience of no less than three years in a facility concerned with animal welfare.

Animals present in gardens:

The Ministry of Agriculture shall establish a list of the animals that are prohibited from being exhibited in zoological gardens.

It shall be prohibited to introduce any new species of animals into the zoological garden except after obtaining the prior approval of the Ministry of Agriculture. It shall also be prohibited for the owners of gardens to sell the animals, offer them as a gift, lend them, or deposit them with third parties without obtaining prior approval from the Ministry of Agriculture.

Obligations of the owner of the zoo:

The owner of the zoo shall be deemed a custodian of the animals, subject to compliance with the following obligations:

1 . To comply with the conditions set forth in this Law, under penalty of withdrawal or suspension of the prior approval in accordance with due process.

2 . To notify the Ministry of Agriculture of every new animal introduced into the zoo from among the species previously approved, indicating its source within a period of one month from its arrival, while retaining the legal certificates for such sources. The Ministry of Agriculture must also be notified of every case of birth or death, indicating the causes thereof, within the period specified above.

3 . To take the necessary measures in order to prevent visitors from harming the animals.

4 . To ensure the permanent safety of the animals of the zoo.

The right to establish animal rescue centres:

Public law persons, non-governmental organisations, and legal persons

of private law that do not seek profit and that work in the field of animal protection and welfare shall have the right to obtain a prior licence from the Ministry of Agriculture to establish rescue centres after fulfilling the conditions provided for in Article 3 of this Law. The licence shall specify the species of animals that may be placed in the centre.

In the event of the introduction of a species of animals not provided for in the licence, the Ministry of Agriculture must be notified within 24 hours.

Rescue centres shall be prohibited from selling animals.

Rescue centres must inform the Ministry of Agriculture of the occurrence of any transfer of custody within one month of its occurrence. In such case, the custodian shall be bound to comply with the obligations provided for in this Law, in particular Article 11 thereof.

Recording of Violations and Seizure of Animals:

In the event of a violation of any of the provisions of this Law, in particular Articles 4, 5, 6, 7 and 11, the Minister of Agriculture may issue a decision to seize the animals and place them, at their owner's expense, in the custody of one of the entities provided for in Article 23 above, and refer their owner to the competent judiciary, in accordance with the procedures provided for in the Veterinary Quarantine Law.

The competent court may lift the seizure temporarily until the issuance of a final judgment, with or without bail, upon the request of the owner of the animals after seeking the opinion of the Ministry of Agriculture (Directorate of Animal Resources).

If five days elapse from the date of the seizure after notifying the concerned party and no one claims the seized animals, the competent court shall be entitled to return them to their original habitat or hand them over to a rescue centre. If that is not possible, the court shall be entitled to order that they be killed by one of the means of euthanasia. In addition to the options mentioned above, the court shall be entitled to order the sale of the seized animals at public auction if they are not listed in any of the CITES appendices. From the sale price there shall be collected the cost of custody, then the cost of sale, then the value of the fine and compensation determined by the judge on the basis of a provisional assessment by the official of the Animal Resources Department, and the remainder of the sale value is not deposited in the Treasury fund as security for the rights of the concerned parties.

Closure of the facility:

In the event of the partial or total closure of the facility or the revocation of the licence or prior approval in the cases specified in this Law, the owner of the facility shall, at his own expense, and following the approval of the Ministry of Agriculture, return the animals to their original habitat or deliver them to a rescue centre or a similar facility. Where the owner fails to execute the provisions stipulated above within one week from the occurrence of the closure or the revocation of the licence or prior approval, the Ministry may take his place in this regard, provided that he shall be obliged to pay the expenses incurred by it.

Where that proves impossible, the court may order that they be killed by one of the means of euthanasia or, where they are not listed in any of the CITES appendices, sold at public auction in accordance with the procedures specified in Article 24 above.

In the event of the suspension of the licence or prior approval or the temporary prohibition of the facility from carrying out its activities that are the subject of the declaration, visitors shall be prohibited from entering the facility and a Ministry shall appoint a veterinarian and one of the bodies stipulated in Article 23 above to take the place of the owner of the facility and at his expense throughout the duration of the suspension of the licence or prior approval or the prohibition from carrying out its activities.

Sole Article:

The proposed Law aiming at regulating Public-Private Partnership, as amended by the Administration and Justice Committee and the Chamber of Deputies, is hereby ratified.

This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

For the purpose of applying the provisions of this Law, the following terms shall have the meanings corresponding to each of them:

Public Entity:

The State, public institutions including regulatory authorities, municipalities, unions of municipalities, and all other legal persons under public law.

Private Partner:

A local and/or foreign company or consortium of companies from the private sector that has been awarded the Partnership Contract.

Joint Project:

Any project of public utility to which the private sector contributes through financing, management, and at least one of the following operations: design, establishment, construction, development, restoration, equipping, maintenance, rehabilitation, and operation.

Partnership Contract:

The set of contracts, annexes, undertakings, and guarantees governing the contractual relationship between the Public Entity, the Project Company, and the other concerned parties.

Council:

The Higher Council for Privatisation and Partnership.

Project Company:

The Lebanese joint-stock company established by the Private Partner for the purpose of implementing the Joint Project.

Competent Minister

The Minister within the scope of whose subordinate administrations' powers, or the public institutions including regulatory authorities, municipalities, or unions of municipalities subject to his tutelage or administrative supervision, the Joint Project falls.

Foundational Phase:

The phase commencing on the date of signature of the Partnership Contract by its parties and lasting until the completion of design and establishment, and/or construction, and/or development, and/or restoration, and/or equipping, and/or rehabilitation, as specified in the Partnership Contract.

Operational Phase:

The phase commencing on the date of the start of provision of the project services and the operation and maintenance activities and lasting until their completion as specified in the Partnership Contract.

Penalties:

Whoever violates the provisions of any of the articles of this Law shall be punished by a fine of three to ten times the official minimum wage.

Whoever establishes any of the facilities mentioned contrary to the procedures provided for in this Law, or violates the provisions governing the withdrawal of a licence or prior approval, the suspension thereof, or the prohibition from practising the activities subject to declaration, or where the offence is committed against an animal listed in any appendix to the CITES Convention, shall be punished by imprisonment from three months up to two years and by a fine of twenty to fifty million Lebanese pounds.

The court may order that the convicted person be prohibited from carrying out any of the activities provided for in this Law for a period of at least one year. The court may order the temporary or permanent closure of any facility owned by the convicted person.

The court may order, in addition to the penalties provided for in this Law, the confiscation of the animals and their placement in a rescue centre or, where necessary, their killing by one of the means of euthanasia, at the expense of the convicted person. The court shall have the right to order the sale of the animals at public auction if they are not listed in any of the CITES appendices. In such case, the procedures set forth in Article 24 above shall apply.

The penalties provided for in this Law shall be doubled in the event of recidivism.

Participation of the Private Sector:

The Ministry may establish joint projects with legal persons governed by private law in order to implement the provisions of this Law. The detailed rules for the application of this Article shall be determined by joint decisions issued by the Ministers of Agriculture and Finance.

Transitional Provisions:

The implementing decrees and decisions for this Law shall be issued within a maximum period of three years from the date of publication of the Law in the Official Gazette.

Facilities subject to this Law that were established prior to its issuance shall take the necessary measures to obtain the licences or approvals or submit the declarations

provided for in Articles 7, 9, 13, 17, 19 and 20 within a period of eighteen months from its entry into force, under pain of administrative, criminal and civil prosecution.

Other Legal Texts:

All texts that conflict with the provisions of this Law are hereby repealed.

Publication of the Law and Entry into Force:

This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

1 - Joint projects undertaken by the State, public institutions and other legal persons governed by public law shall be subject to the provisions of this Law, with the exception of municipalities or federations of municipalities, which may subject the joint projects pertaining to them to the provisions of this Law.

2 - Notwithstanding any other text, joint projects provided for in the laws regulating the telecommunications, electricity and civil aviation sectors shall be subject to the provisions of this Law.

3 - Upon the Council expressing its approval to proceed with the joint project, the regulatory authority of the sector shall exercise its functions with respect to the issuance of the licence through participation in the project committee. In the event of the vacancy of the seat of the president and members of the regulatory authority of the sector, the approval of the Council of Ministers on the book of specifications shall be deemed to constitute the licence.

4 - The regulatory authority shall exercise its work in accordance with the law of its establishment and in a manner that does not contravene the provisions of this Law and the provisions of the conditions of the partnership contract, particularly those relating to the modification of the prices of services in the contract and the imposition of fines and the suspension, modification, renewal, cancellation and withdrawal of licences.

1 - The designation of the Higher Council for Privatisation established pursuant to Law No. 228 dated 31 May 2000 shall be replaced wherever it appears by the designation of the Higher Council for Privatisation and Partnership.

The Council shall assume, in addition to its functions provided for in the aforementioned Law, the functions envisaged in this Law.

2 - The competent Minister shall join the members of the Council ex officio.

3 - The post of General Recording Secretary of the Higher Council for Privatisation appearing in Decree No. 5540 dated 23 May 2001 shall be replaced by the post of Secretary-General of the Higher Council for Privatisation and Partnership. The latter shall head the General Secretariat of the Council and shall conduct and execute the ordinary business of the Council.

1 - Partnership projects shall be proposed by the President of the Council or the competent Minister. Partnership projects of a municipal character shall be proposed by the President of the Municipal Council or the President of the Council of the Federation. The proposal shall be made by submitting a file to the Council containing a preliminary study of the project.

2 - The General Secretariat of the Council shall prepare a thorough study of the proposed partnership project and shall submit to the Council a report containing its recommendation as to the feasibility of executing the proposed project by way of a partnership contract, and the extent of the private sector's interest in financing and investing in it, as a preliminary step to the Council taking its decision to accept or reject the proposal.

3 - Upon the approval of the Council to accept the proposal and consequently to proceed with the project, the Council shall form a project committee chaired by the Secretary-General of the Council and comprising a representative of the competent Minister, a representative of the Ministry of Finance designated by the Minister of Finance, the President of the Regulatory Authority for the sector where one exists, and the President of the Municipal Council or the President of the Council of the Federation when examining projects of a municipal character which have been subjected to the provisions of this Law. The project committee shall select financial, legal and technical consultancy firms to assist it in its work, provided that the Council contracts with them.

4 - The project committee shall be assisted in its work by a working group whose activities shall be coordinated by a delegate from the General Secretariat of the Council designated by the Secretary-General of the Council, provided that this group comprises a representative of the public legal person benefiting from the partnership project, representatives of the financial, legal and technical consultancy firms with which contracts have been concluded, persons of specific expertise, as needed, from the ministries and the concerned and existing regulatory authorities, and any person governed by public law where the project committee considers that certain aspects of the partnership project fall within the scope of its powers.

Any additional remuneration that may be due to a member of the project committee or the working group who is subject to the provisions of public law shall be borne by the public legal person to which such member belongs and shall be paid in accordance with its regulations.

The project committee, assisted by the working group, shall undertake the preparation of a comprehensive study on the partnership project covering the technical, economic, legal and financial aspects, including the qualification criteria, the extent of investors' interest and the feasibility of attracting the necessary financing, and shall submit a report containing its recommendation thereon to the Council.

Following the Council's approval to proceed with the joint project in projects undertaken by the State, public institutions, or any legal person governed by public law, with the exception of municipalities or federations of municipalities, the project file shall be referred to the Council of Ministers through its President. Following the Council of Ministers' approval to proceed with the joint project, the Project Committee shall launch the procedures for selecting the private partner, which must be conducted in accordance with the principles set forth in this Law.

And following the Council's approval to proceed with a joint project of a municipal nature subjected to the provisions of this Law, the project file shall be referred through the President of the Council to the President of the Municipal Council or the President of the Council of the Federation concerned in order to obtain the necessary ratifications thereon in accordance with the provisions of Legislative Decree No. 118 dated 30 June 1977, and thereafter the Project Committee shall launch the procedures for selecting the private partner, which must be conducted in accordance with the principles set forth in this Law.

The contract shall be awarded to the candidate who submitted the best offer according to the evaluation of the Project Committee based on the evaluation criteria stipulated in the tender document, and with the approval of the Council. The Project Committee shall announce the result reached by the selection process and shall notify the remaining bidders of the reasons for the failure of their offers.

1 - The private partner must establish a Lebanese joint-stock company for the project (the Project Company), all the shares of which shall be registered shares subject to the provisions of the Code of Commerce promulgated by Legislative Decree No. 304 dated 24/12/1942, and it shall be exempted from the nationality condition stipulated in Articles 78 and 144 thereof and from the obligation to appoint an additional auditor, and the non-Lebanese Chairman of the Board of Directors and/or General Manager shall be exempted from the obligation to obtain a work permit.

2 - In projects undertaken by the State, public institutions and other legal persons of public law with the exception of municipalities or federations of municipalities, the private partner may not assign its shares in the Project Company to third parties before the project reaches the operational phase as defined in the partnership contract without the approval of the Council of Ministers; whereas in projects of a municipal nature, it is required to obtain the approval of the municipal council or the council of the federation.

3 - The public legal person is permitted to participate in the establishment of the Project Company and contribute to its capital, and its contributions in kind shall be exempted from the verification procedure stipulated in Article 86 of the Code of Commerce, provided that the valuation is carried out by an independent entity with international expertise. The members of the Board of Directors shall be selected by the General Assembly, provided that the public legal person is represented throughout the duration of its shareholding in the company by at least one member appointed by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the competent Minister.

4 - The Project Company shall not be subject to the audit of the Court of Accounts.

1 - The procedures for selecting the Private Partner shall be subject to the principles of transparency, freedom of participation for competing candidates, and equality in their treatment, and must be preceded by sufficient publicity to ensure a multiplicity of competing bids to win the contract.

2 - The procedures for selecting the Private Partner shall begin with the announcement of a public invitation for those wishing to apply to win the Joint Project, including the qualification criteria that are commensurate with the size and nature of the Joint Project. This invitation shall be published at least one month prior to the final deadline for submitting expressions of interest in local and international newspapers, specialised magazines, and on the Council's website.

3 - The Project Committee shall provide those wishing to qualify with the necessary information and instructions on the basis of which to submit their applications. It is prohibited to qualify or select a Private Partner that has been declared bankrupt, is in a state of liquidation, or against which Lebanese or foreign judicial judgments have been rendered convicting it of committing acts of collusion or corrupt practices. Where the Private Partner is a consortium of companies, each company of this consortium must fulfil these conditions. It is prohibited to contract with a Project Company against the chairman or a member of the board of directors of which a final judgment has been rendered convicting him of committing a felony or a disgraceful misdemeanour.

4 - The Project Committee, assisted by the working team, shall study the submitted qualification applications and audit their documents. The Project Committee shall evaluate the qualification applications in accordance with the announced qualification criteria and submit a reasoned report to the Council including a proposal with the names of the qualified candidates and the non-qualified candidates in order to take the appropriate decision. After the Council decides on the report, the qualification results shall be announced, provided that the number of qualified candidates is not less than three.

5 - In the event that at least three candidates do not qualify, the public invitation for those wishing to qualify shall be re-announced anew.

6 - The Project Committee shall notify the non-qualified candidates of the reasons for their non-qualification.

7 - The Project Committee, assisted by the working team, shall undertake the preparation of a draft tender document. The draft must include, by way of enumeration and not limitation:

a - The evaluation criteria specific to the Joint Project, which must be objective, commensurate with the size and nature of the project, directly connected to it, and verifiable and demonstrable.

b - The project data, which include the procedures for submitting bids, the financial, technical, and administrative elements of the project, and the mechanisms for inquiry and for submitting and deciding on objections.

c - The draft Partnership Contract and its annexes.

8 - The Project Committee shall notify the draft tender document to the qualified candidates.

9 - The Project Committee, assisted by the working team, shall hold consultations (Consultations) with all qualified candidates and financing entities in a neutral and transparent manner with a view to reaching a comprehensive and final conception to determine the technical requirements, practical means, and best financial structure to achieve the Joint Project, and the draft tender document shall be amended where necessary by the Project Committee in light of the results of those consultations.

10 - The Project Committee shall submit the tender document in its final form to the Council,

and after its approval, the tender document shall be submitted through its President to the Council of Ministers to obtain final approval thereof. As for Joint Projects of a municipal nature that have been subjected to the provisions of this Law, and after the Council's approval of the tender document in its final form, it shall be referred through the President of the Council to the President of the Municipal Council or the President of the Council of the Union concerned to obtain the necessary ratifications in accordance with the provisions of Legislative Decree No. 118 dated 30 June 1977.

11 - The tender document shall be notified to the qualified candidates by the Project Committee.

12 - The qualified candidates shall prepare their technical and financial bids and submit them to the Project Committee in accordance with the procedures specified in the tender document.

13 - In the event that at least three bids are not submitted, the Joint Project shall be re-tendered anew, and in the event that this does not result in three bids, two bids may then suffice after the approval of the Council.

14 - The Project Committee shall open the submitted technical bids in the presence of the bidders to verify that they fulfil the submission conditions stipulated in the tender document. The Project Committee may request the bidders to submit the necessary clarifications, complete deficiencies, and confirm the commitments that the bid may contain within a period it specifies.

15 - Technical bids that do not conform to the requirements of the tender document shall be rejected, and the financial bids pertaining to them shall be returned to their owners without being disclosed. The owners of the rejected bids shall be notified of the reasons for rejection.

16 - The Project Committee, assisted by the working team, shall evaluate the remaining technical bids in accordance with the criteria specified by the tender document, and the Project Committee shall determine the accepted technical bids in light of this evaluation. In the event that at least two technical bids are not accepted, the Joint Project shall be re-tendered anew, in order to ensure competition.

17 - The Project Committee shall open the financial bids pertaining to the accepted technical bids in the presence of their bidders and thereafter submit a report to the Council in which it ranks the bidders in light of the technical and financial evaluations. The Project Committee shall attach to this report its recommendation regarding the best bid based on the evaluation criteria stipulated in the tender document.

The Project Committee, by delegation from the Council, may conduct negotiations with the bidder of the best bid with a view to improving the bid from the technical aspect.

The Partnership Agreement shall be signed by the authority empowered to sign in the name of the Public Person and by the representative of the Project Company. It shall also be signed, where required, by the Private Partner and any other concerned party.

The Partnership Agreement must contain the following matters:

1 - The obligations of the parties of all kinds and their rights.

2 - The bases of financing the Joint Project.

3 - The term of the Partnership Agreement, provided that such term does not exceed thirty-five years from the date of signing the Partnership Agreement.

4 - The revenues that the Project Company shall receive from the Public Person, or that the Public Person shall receive from the Project Company according to the nature of the Joint Project, in consideration of the Project Company performing the works entrusted to it pursuant to the Partnership Agreement, and the manner of receiving such revenues.

5 - The fees, charges and royalties pertaining to the Joint Project which the Government, the Municipal Council or the Council of the Union authorises the Project Company to collect in the name of the concerned Public Person and for its account.

6 - The performance evaluation indicators of the Project Company (Key Performance Indicators).

7 - The reports that the Project Company must prepare on the implementation of the Joint Project and which it must mandatorily refer to the Public Person and the Council.

8 - The allocation of risks between the Public Person and the Project Company in addition to the measures and procedures that must be followed to limit the impact of those risks.

9 - The controls governing the amendment of the essential conditions of the Agreement.

10 - The guarantees, undertakings and commitments that may be given for the implementation of the Joint Project by the Project Company and/or the Private Partner and/or the Public Person.

11 - The funds and properties belonging to the Public Person that are placed throughout the term of the Partnership Agreement at the disposal of the Project Company for the fulfilment of its obligations, in addition to the rights and obligations of the Project Company in respect of these properties and funds.

12 - The manner of transferring the Joint Project upon the expiry of its term to the Public Person when the nature of the Project so requires.

13 - The procedures for securing the continuity of the Project and the works that are the subject of the Partnership Agreement upon its termination by the expiry of its term or by its rescission, or in the event of breach by the Project Company in performing its contractual obligations.

14 - The procedures and penalties that attach to the parties to the Agreement in the event of their breach of any of their contractual obligations and the detailed mechanisms for applying those penalties.

15 - The procedures followed for dispute resolution, including mediation and domestic and international arbitration.

The Public Legal Person shall undertake the monitoring of the execution of the Joint Project in all its aspects in accordance with the provisions stipulated in the Partnership Agreement. The monitoring thereof shall be carried out in two phases, the establishment phase and the operational phase.

1 - The Establishment Phase

a - Immediately upon the signing of the Partnership Agreement by its parties, the Public Legal Person must appoint:

. A Steering Committee chaired by a representative of the Public Legal Person and also comprising representatives of the Competent Minister in the event that the Public Legal Person is other than the State, of the General Secretariat of the Council, of the Ministry of Finance and of the Regulatory Authority of the sector, where it exists.

. A Foundation Phase Management Office comprising, in addition to its appointed members, such local and/or international specialised experts and consultants as may be necessary according to the nature of the Joint Project, and the Project Management Office shall serve as the liaison between the Steering Committee and the Project Company.

b - The Project Management Office shall receive and evaluate the reports relating to the execution and the progress of works prepared by the Project Company, and shall draw up quarterly monitoring reports and submit them to the Steering Committee. The monitoring reports must show the extent of the Project Company's compliance with the timetable for the execution of the works specified in the contract and must include proposals with respect to emergency matters that require resolution.

c - The Steering Committee shall meet quarterly and upon the occurrence of any emergency for the purpose of reviewing the monitoring reports submitted by the Project Management Office, giving the necessary directives and submitting reports to the Public Legal Person, the Competent Minister in the event that the Public Legal Person is other than the State, and the General Secretariat of the Council.

d - A Public Legal Person other than the State may, subject to the approval of the Competent Minister, take the necessary measures and decisions on the basis of the reports of the Steering Committee and the Project Management Office.

2 - The Operational Phase

a - Prior to the commencement of this phase, the Public Legal Person must appoint an Operational Phase Management Office comprising, in addition to its appointed members, a representative of the Regulatory Authority of the sector, where it exists, and such local or international specialised experts and consultants as may be necessary.

b - The Operational Phase Management Office shall undertake, by way of enumeration and not limitation, the following tasks:

. Monitoring the operations carried out by the Project Company in terms of outputs and the required levels and quality of services with respect to the established standards and the allocation of risks.

. Submitting proposals relating to the plan for addressing the breach by the Project Company of its obligations and imposing the penalties stipulated in the Partnership Agreement.

. Contributing to the management of the settlement of existing disputes.

. Ensuring in general the conformity of the operations of the Project Company with the conditions stipulated in the Partnership Agreement.

c - The Operational Phase Management Office shall draw up semi-annual reports on the monitoring results, and whenever the need arises. A copy of these reports shall be notified to the Public Legal Person to take the appropriate decisions in respect thereof, to the Competent Minister in the event that the Public Legal Person is other than the State, and to the General Secretariat of the Council for review, expression of opinion and referral to the Council whenever the need arises.

The General Secretariat of the Council shall undertake:

a - Preparing annual reports on the programme of joint projects, submitting proposals aimed at developing and stimulating partnership between the public and private sectors in general, and referring them to the Council in order to forward them to the Council of Ministers.

b - Training personnel working in the public sector to develop their capacities and to enable them to study and accompany partnership projects effectively.

1 - Notwithstanding any other text, the public entity may place at the disposal of the project company the real properties belonging to it and necessary for the implementation of the joint project, throughout the term of the partnership contract.

2 - If the implementation of the joint project requires the expropriation of private real properties, the Council or the project company may request the public entity to expropriate those real properties. In this case, the rules of expropriation shall apply, and the decisions of taking possession and transfer of ownership must be issued within a maximum period of six months from the date of issuance of the decree declaring public utility. The expropriated real properties shall be registered in the Land Registry in the name of the public entity, and the project company shall be granted the right to occupy them throughout the term of the partnership contract.

3 - The project company or the private partner shall be permitted to contribute wholly or partially with the public entity in financing the cost of expropriation compensation for the real properties required to be expropriated, provided that such contribution shall be deemed an integral element of the elements of financing the joint project.
The expenditures of the joint project that are borne by the State shall be provided for in the general budget of the State.

Each of the Council and the public entity shall contract with the experts and consulting firms provided for in this Law on the basis of their own regulations where they exist, and otherwise on the basis of the provisions of the Public Accounting Law.

The provisions of this Law shall not prevent the private partner and the project company from benefiting from the provisions of Law No. 360 issued on 16 August 2001 relating to the encouragement of investments in Lebanon and the provisions of Law No. 705 dated 9/12/2005 relating to asset securitisation, in a manner that does not cause prejudice to the interest of the public entity.
The details of implementation of this Law shall be determined, as required, by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers, upon the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Amendment of Article 45 of Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (the Income Tax Law)

Article 45 of Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (the Income Tax Law) is amended to read as follows:

First: Establishments subject to the real profit assessment method may revalue their fixed asset items every five years in accordance with the procedures set forth in the Code of Commerce for the valuation of contributions in kind in capital companies.

The valuation record shall be notified to the competent tax office, which may object to it before the Income Tax Objections Committee within three months from the date of notification, and the said Committee shall issue its decision regarding the objection and determine the final valuation within a maximum period of six months from the date the establishment submits its comments on the rapporteur's report, failing which the valuation record shall be deemed effective,

Second: Where fixed asset items are valued higher than their original cost price or its remaining balance after depreciation, the increase shall be deemed a capital gain.

This gain shall not be subject to income tax in either of the following two cases:

1 - If it remains separate in a special account on both the assets and liabilities sides of the balance sheet.

2 - If it is used to cover losses that are still shown and specified in the balance sheet, within the limits of the amount thereof used to cover such losses.

This gain shall be subject to income tax at the rate of 10% in other cases. Depreciation may then be calculated on the new value shown as a result of the revaluation.

Third: The capital gain resulting from a total or partial disposal shall be subject to income tax at the rate of 15%; however, a taxpayer who reinvests all or part of this gain before the expiry of two years following the year in which it was realised shall be entitled to request a deduction of the tax imposed in proportion to the amount thereof reinvested in building permanent housing to accommodate employees and wage-earners working in the establishment. In this case, the provisions and conditions of Article 5 bis of the Income Tax Law shall apply.

The capital gain resulting from disposal shall also be exempt to the extent that it is used to write off losses incurred by the establishment.

Capital companies assessed on the basis of lump-sum profit may revalue their fixed asset items every five years in accordance with the procedures set forth for taxpayers assessed under the real profit method.

B - Gains on the disposal of fixed assets, including real properties, belonging to natural and legal persons subject to income tax on the basis of lump-sum or estimated profit shall be subject to tax at the rate of fifteen percent (15%).

C - Gains on the disposal of real properties belonging to natural and legal persons not subject to income tax, or who enjoyed permanent, special or exceptional exemptions from that tax, or belonging to natural persons subject to income tax where such real properties do not constitute an asset used in the practice of the profession, shall be subject to tax at the rate of fifteen percent (15%), in accordance with the following:

Gains on the disposal of the primary residences of a natural person shall be excluded from the tax mentioned above, provided that they do not exceed two residences.

For the purpose of calculating the taxable disposal gain, a rate of 8% of the value of the disposal gain shall be deducted for each full year separating the date of acquisition of the real property and the date of disposal thereof. The gain on the disposal of the real property shall be exempt from tax if the transferor has continued to hold it for a period of 12 full years and above, provided that the difference is paid in the year during which the disposal takes place.

When carrying out a taxable disposal transaction, the persons referred to above must declare the disposal transaction and pay the tax due thereon within a period of two months from the date of disposal.

In the event of a violation of the provisions of this Article, the fines provided for in Law No. 44 dated 11/11/2008 (the Tax Procedures Law) shall be imposed.

The detailed rules for the application of this Article shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

Terms and Definitions

The following words and expressions, wherever they appear in this Decree, shall have the following meanings:

a - The Minister: The Minister of Education and Higher Education,

b - The Law: Law No. 285 dated 30/4/2014 (General Provisions of Higher Education and the Organisation of Private Higher Education),

c - The Council: The Council of Higher Education referred to in Article 13 of the Law,

d - The Committee: The Academic Technical Committee.

e - The Specialised Committees: The committees specialised in examining programmes.

f - The University Unit: The faculty, institute, or department within the university.

On the mechanisms for granting permission to commence teaching

A higher education institution shall not have the right to commence teaching in any specialisation before obtaining permission to do so issued by a decision of the Minister upon the recommendation of the Council based on the reports of the Committee and the specialised committees.

First: Submitting the application to commence teaching

The mechanisms provided for in Item First of Article One of this Decree shall be adopted.

Second: Examining the application to commence teaching

The mechanisms provided for in Item Second of Article One of this Decree shall be adopted, in addition to verifying the availability of the teaching requirements in the institution in accordance with forms prepared for this purpose by the Committee and the specialised committees pursuant to the licensing file. The verification shall necessarily include field visits and documented meetings with the officials in the institution. As a result of the audit, the visits and the reports received by it from the competent committees, the Committee shall draw up a detailed report.

Second: The decision to commence

Upon the issuance of a recommendation to license the granting of permission to commence teaching, the Directorate General of Higher Education shall request the institution to provide a letter of guarantee or a financial security in accordance with what is provided for by the law within a period of one month at most.

The Minister shall issue, within one month at most from the date of providing the letter of guarantee or the security, the decision of permission to commence and shall notify it to the institution concerned therewith, and this decision shall be published in the Official Gazette, and the decision shall include:

1. The name of the licensed university institution.

2. The university campus in which the requested establishment will take place.

3. The faculty and/or the specialisations and/or the educational level.

On the mechanisms of recognition or renewal of recognition of degrees

First: Submission of the application for recognition or renewal of recognition

The institution shall submit to the Directorate General of Higher Education an application for the recognition of the degree one year prior to the graduation of the first cohort, and shall also submit an application for the renewal of the recognition of the degree one year prior to the expiration of the recognition period, and the review of the application shall be subject to a financial fee in accordance with what is specified in the Law.

The application shall be submitted according to a specific form at the Directorate General of Higher Education including an information form and additional documents, among which:

1. A list comprising the head of the university unit to which the specialisation belongs and the names of the members of the unit council in accordance with terms of reference established by the Committee for that purpose.

2. A list of the names of the academic officials in charge of the specialisation indicating their university qualifications and their academic experience.

3. A list of the names of the teaching staff for the specialisation for which the institution wishes to obtain recognition or renewal of recognition, indicating their academic and research qualifications and a list of their publications for the last five years in accordance with the internationally adopted standards for citing research and publications.

4. A list of the technicians and administrators.

5. A list of the facilities, laboratories and equipment related to the specialisation.

6. The library resources available for the specialisation (books, references, journals, electronic library).

7. A document proving the deposit of the financial fee.

Second: Review of the application for recognition or renewal of recognition

The Director General of Higher Education shall present the file to the Committee at its first meeting following the submission of the application. The Committee, and whichever specialised committees it assigns, shall verify the availability of the teaching requirements in the specialisation within a maximum period of two months from its receipt of the application, in accordance with forms prepared by the Committee for this purpose on the basis of the file previously deposited by the institution upon the commencement of teaching or the previous renewal of recognition. The verification shall include field visits and documented meetings with the officials in the institution. The Committee may adopt self-evaluation and external evaluation mechanisms for the programmes in accordance with criteria and indicators established for that purpose.

Third: The recognition decision

If it appears to the Committee, as a result of the audit, visits and reports received by it from the specialised committees, or the programme meets the technical, academic and legal conditions, it shall issue a recommendation upon which the decision of the Minister is based to recognise or renew the recognition of the specialisation and the level of study concerned therewith and the validity period of this recognition, provided that it is not less than three years and does not exceed six years, and this decision shall be published in the Official Gazette

Fourth: Violations and penalties

If it appears to the Technical Committee that the programme does not meet the legal conditions, and that there is one of the violations set forth in Clause Third of Article 63 of the Law, it shall draw up a detailed report in which it includes the types of violations and shall submit it to the Minister to apply the necessary penalties in accordance with the following:

. The Minister shall put the institution on notice to remove the violations within one year from the date of issuance of the report, and it shall not be permitted during this period to admit new students in this specialisation, in addition to a financial fine of one hundred times the monthly minimum wage for each violation.

. In the event that the violation is not removed by the end of the specified period, the institution shall be prohibited from receiving new students in the specialisation for another academic year, after which a decision shall be issued by the Minister prohibiting the admission of student registration in the specialisation, and the institution shall be required to submit a new application for commencement after the lapse of at least one year from the decision of the Minister.

. If it appears to the Technical Committee that the institution has removed the violations, it shall issue a recommendation upon which the decision of the Minister is based to recognise or renew the recognition of the specialisation and the level of study concerned therewith and the validity period of this recognition, and this decision shall be published in the Official Gazette.

There shall be established within the Directorate General of Higher Education a Secretariat of the Academic Technical Committee, among the duties of which shall be:

. To keep the applications submitted by higher education institutions for licensing, or for obtaining permission to commence instruction, or for recognition, or for renewal of recognition of degrees, within a computerised information system put in place for that purpose.

. To keep a register of matters relating to licensing applications.

. To keep a register of matters relating to applications for permission to commence.

. To keep a register of matters relating to applications for recognition and renewal of recognition.

. To organise the schedules of meetings of the Technical Committee and of the specialised programme committees and to keep their reports.
