Authorisation of Collection

The collection of the various taxes, fees, proceeds and revenues set out in Tables No. (5, 6, 7 and 8) annexed to this Law is authorised in accordance with the provisions of this Law and the provisions of the laws in force.

Authorisation to Borrow

1 - The Government is authorised, within the framework of financing the maturities of debt principal, and within the limits of the estimated deficit in the execution of the Budget and in the expenditure of appropriations carried forward to the year 2018 and additional appropriations, to issue Treasury bonds in Lebanese currency for short, medium, and long terms to cover this deficit, pursuant to decisions issued by the Minister of Finance.

2 - The Government is authorised to issue Treasury bonds in foreign currencies up to an amount not exceeding six billion United States dollars, provided that the funds borrowed pursuant to this authorisation are used within the framework of restructuring the public debt, in order to finance external debt maturities and/or to convert the equivalent of their value of the public debt in Lebanese pounds into foreign currencies and/or for the purpose of financing the needs of the Treasury in foreign currencies on better terms.

3 - All bonds issued under Item Two of this Article must be repaid within a period not exceeding thirty years from the date of commencement of the operations authorised pursuant to Item Two above.

4 - When the Government issues Treasury bonds in foreign currency for periods shorter than the maximum period specified in Item Three of this Article, the Government shall have the right, as from the maturity date of any of the bonds, to carry out a new operation or operations in foreign currency for an additional period or periods, provided that the total value of these operations does not at any time exceed the volume of the amount the Government is authorised to borrow in accordance with Item Two above, and that the total period of all these operations does not exceed the maximum period specified in Item Three, namely thirty years as from the date of commencement of the first issue of those bonds or the first borrowing operation.

5 - The Ministry of Finance shall inform the Chamber of Deputies quarterly of:

- The actual deficit in the execution of the Budget and the Treasury,

- The expenditure of carried-forward and additional appropriations,

- The instalments of internal and external debts that have been repaid,

- The outcome of the issuance of Treasury bonds in Lebanese currency authorised to be issued pursuant to Item One of this Article,

- Treasury advances.

Loan Accounts

Special Treasury accounts shall be opened for the loans, to which shall be credited the value received from the principal of these loans, and to which shall be debited the values paid in repayment of due instalments and bonds.

Application of the provisions of foreign grant and loan agreements to the entirety of the agreement relating to externally funded projects

1- Expenditure from cash grant and foreign loan agreements concluded with the various public administrations, public institutions and municipalities after their approval by decrees issued by the Council of Ministers or laws issued by the Chamber of Deputies, whether such expenditure is from the local portion or from the foreign portion, shall be subject to the audit of the Court of Audit in accordance with the rules, and the application of the provisions stipulated in the agreements and decrees relating to cash grants must not under any circumstances conflict with the recording of cash grants in accordance with the rules in the budget.

2 - The transfer of funds incoming from donor entities to public administrations shall take place through the Ministry of Finance. Throughout the duration of the implementation of the project, and after the issuance of the decree accepting the grant, the Ministry of Finance shall open the appropriations necessary therefor and included therein, all at once or successively, in the budget of the current fiscal year and in the budgets of subsequent fiscal years, according to the cash value transferred in each fiscal year by the donor entities to the donations and grants account pertaining to the Lebanese Treasury.

3 - The provisions of the second paragraph of Article 27 of the draft law put into effect by Decree No. 14969 issued on 30/12/1963 shall not apply to additional appropriations relating to cash grants, whereby such appropriations may be transferred from one item to another by a decision of the competent minister and the Minister of Finance after the endorsement of the Central Controller of Expenditure Commitment, and after the concerned administration proves the desire of the donor entity to carry out such transfer.

4 - The provisions of Article 104 of the draft law put into effect by Decree No. 14969 dated 30/12/1963 and its amendments (the Public Accounting Law) shall apply to emergency financial advances granted for the payment of expenditures funded by cash grants, and the appropriations reserved for emergency financial advances relating to grants given during a specific fiscal year to perform obligations the execution of which exceeds the year for the payment of expenditures funded by cash grants may be carried over, until the completion of the execution of the works relating to the grant, to the budgets of subsequent fiscal years.

5 - All balances of uncommitted appropriations funded by cash grants shall be carried over to the budgets of subsequent years.

Opening of Extraordinary Appropriations

In implementation of the provisions of Article 85 of the Constitution, the President of the Republic may, if emergency circumstances call for urgent expenditures, issue a decree based on a decision issued by the Council of Ministers, to open extraordinary or supplementary appropriations or to transfer appropriations in the 2018 budget, provided that these appropriations do not exceed one hundred billion Lebanese pounds, and these measures must be submitted for the approval of the Chamber of Deputies at the first session in which it convenes thereafter.

Authorisation to Transfer Appropriations

1- Transfer within the reserve of the general budget from one chapter to another and from one item to another within this reserve is authorised by a decision of the Council of Ministers based on the proposal of the Minister of Finance, and this measure shall apply to the reserve of each annexed budget.

Allocation of Appropriations to Subsidise Interest on Investment Loans

There shall be allocated in the general budget (Ministry of Finance - Directorate of Public Finance) the appropriations required to subsidise interest on investment loans (agricultural, industrial, tourist, and technology and informatics) and profit margins on these loans with respect to Islamic banks.

The procedures and conditions for benefiting from the subsidised interest, and the profit margins on these loans with respect to Islamic banks, shall be determined pursuant to regulations issued by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers based on the proposal of the Minister of Finance and after seeking the opinion of the Governor of the Banque du Liban, and the expenditure shall be subject to the procedures provided for in the Public Accounting Law.

Healthcare Appropriations

There shall be distributed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, based on the joint proposal of the competent minister and the Minister of Finance, the appropriations allocated as a lump sum in the various parts of the general budget designated for treatment in private and public institutions and hospitals and contracts with physicians in the private sector.

Deduction of a Share from the Revenues Collected in Favour of Municipalities for Villages that Do Not Have Municipalities

The Ministry of Finance shall deduct from the revenues collected in favour of municipalities, prior to their distribution, an amount of six billion pounds, which shall be allocated for lighting, works, and cleaning in villages that do not have municipalities (energy, maintenance, equipment, and cleaning allowances) through the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities; the revenues shall be distributed by a decree based on the proposal of the Ministers of Finance and of Interior and Municipalities, provided that the decree includes all villages that do not have municipalities.

The phrase "municipal fee on fuels" shall be replaced by the phrase "revenues collected in favour of municipalities" wherever it appears in the budgets of previous years.

Granting Électricité du Liban a Treasury Advance and Addressing the Issue of Accumulated Debts

"Électricité du Liban shall be granted a long-term Treasury advance in the amount of 2742 billion LBP (two thousand seven hundred and forty-two billion Lebanese pounds) to settle the fuel purchase deficit (2728 billion LBP) and to settle the interest and instalments of loans in favour of Électricité du Liban (14 billion LBP), provided that the advance is paid by order of the Central Finance Accountant following the approval of the Minister of Finance, and is settled in cash, and provided that the mere use of this advance by the borrowing entity is deemed an acknowledgment on its part of the ability to repay in accordance with the bases stipulated in this Article".

Électricité du Liban may not, on its own responsibility, use the advance or any part thereof for a purpose other than that for which it was granted.

The manner of repayment of this advance, in addition to the scheduling of the debts accumulated on Électricité du Liban, shall be determined pursuant to a mechanism established by a joint decision between the Ministry of Finance and Électricité du Liban represented by the Ministry of Energy and Water, provided that the mechanism is issued within a time limit of at most six months from the date of issuance of this Law.

Appointment of Regulatory Authorities and Boards of Directors

The Council of Ministers must appoint the regulatory authorities and the boards of directors of public institutions within a period of six months from the date of publication of this Law.

Reduction of assessment and collection fines imposed and levied by the Directorate of Public Finance at the Ministry of Finance

Assessment and collection fines due as at the date of publication of this Law relating to taxes and fees imposed and levied by the Directorate of Public Finance pursuant to the laws on direct and indirect taxes and fees shall be exceptionally reduced in accordance with the following:

A- By 100% for the following violations:

- Failure to keep accounting records by taxpayers subject to estimated profit.

- Issuing invoices or documents therefor that do not contain the information required to be included in the invoice or the document similar thereto with respect to stating the rate of the Value Added Tax, or the address of the issuer of the invoice, or the address or the tax number of the person in whose favour the invoice was issued.

B- By 90% on all other violations.

To benefit from the reduction referred to in items (A and B), taxpayers shall pay the taxes and fees incurred by them in full within a period of six months from the date of publication of this Law, and the balance of the fines incurred by them in accordance with item (B) within a period of six months from the date of publication of this Law.

Reduction of fines due on arrears of collection orders received from public administrations and institutions, municipalities, unions of municipalities, and all other persons under public law

Fines due on arrears of collection orders received from public administrations, public institutions, municipalities, unions of municipalities, and all other persons under public law shall be reduced by 90% (ninety percent), provided that these arrears are paid together with the reduced fines within a period of six months from the date of publication of this Law.

Reduction of fines due on arrears of mechanical fees

Fines due on arrears of mechanical fees shall be reduced by 90% (ninety percent), provided that these arrears are paid together with the reduced fines within a period of six months from the date of publication of this Law.

Reduction of fines due on arrears of municipal fees

Fines due on arrears of municipal fees shall be reduced by 90% (ninety percent), provided that these arrears are paid together with the reduced fines within a period of six months from the date of publication of this Law.

Reduction of Fines Due on Arrears of Municipal Fees on Tourist Establishments

1- Fines due on arrears of municipal fees on tourist establishments shall be reduced by 90% (ninety percent), provided that these arrears together with the reduced fines are paid within a period of six months from the date of publication of this Law.

2 - Liable tourist establishments that have previously paid in instalments by operation of law, or upon their request, the municipal fees, surcharges, or fines accrued thereon shall benefit from the reduction, in the event that they are paid in full or their balances are paid within the same period specified above.

3 - All late payment fines paid in accordance with the laws in force and prior to the entry into force of this Law shall be deemed a right of the municipality and cannot be refunded.

4 - These establishments may pay the amounts due from them in instalments over a maximum period of five years at an interest rate of 5% per annum, provided that 20% of the value of the arrears together with the reduced fines are paid within a period of six months from the date of publication of this Law, and in the event of default in paying any of the instalments on the specified due date, an interest rate of 12% shall be imposed on the amounts paid in instalments.

Reduction of Fines and Late Payment Surcharges Accrued on Arrears of the National Social Security Fund

Fines and late payment surcharges due on arrears of the National Social Security Fund across all its branches shall be reduced by a rate of 90% (ninety percent), provided that the establishments pay these arrears together with the fines within a maximum period of six months from the date of publication of this Law.

Those establishments may pay the amounts due from them in instalments over a maximum period of five years at an interest rate of 5% per annum, provided that 20% of the value of the arrears together with the reduced fines are paid within a period of six months from the date of publication of this Law, and in the event of default in paying any of the instalments on the specified due date, an interest rate of 12% shall be imposed on the amounts paid in instalments.

Granting an additional time limit to object to taxes and fees assessed by the Directorate of Public Finance

Taxpayers liable for taxes and fees assessed by the Directorate of Public Finance who were notified of such taxes and fees starting from 1/1/2009 and have not paid them in full up to the date of issuance of this Law and did not object to them in Articles 97 and 99 of Law No. 44 dated 11/11/2008 and its amendments (Tax Procedures Law), or objected to them and they were rejected as to form at the stage of objection before the tax administration or before the objection committees, shall be granted an additional time limit to submit their objections thereto before the said administration or before the said committees for a period of six months from the date of issuance of this Law, provided that they pay 10% of the taxes, fees and fines due, prior to submitting such objections.

The tax administration shall examine the objections submitted to it in accordance with this Law and shall decide upon them before the end of the year following the year of publication of this Law.

Exemption of taxpayers concerned by the provisions of Article 53 of the Income Tax Law from assessment and collection fines

Employees, workers and wage-earners provided for in Article 53 of Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Income Tax Law), who simultaneously hold a post or work in several establishments or premises, or simultaneously practice a profession subject to the tax of Title One of the same Legislative Decree, shall be exempted from fines for late submission of declarations and from fines for late payment of tax, for the years 2016 and prior, provided that they declare and pay the taxes due from them or pay those assessed upon them, within a time limit of six months from the date of publication of this Law, and they may also pay these taxes in instalments without interest over three years, provided that an advance payment at a rate of twenty-five (25%) of the value of the taxes is paid within a time limit of six months from the date of publication of this Law, and fines paid prior to the publication of this Law shall be deemed a right of the Treasury that cannot be refunded.

Payment by instalments of taxes withheld at source and value added tax

Notwithstanding any other text, by way of exception and for one time only, taxes withheld at source and value added tax due by taxpayers for the tax periods up to 31/12/2016 may be paid by instalments in accordance with the provisions of Article 61 of Law No. 44 dated 11/11/2008 (the Tax Procedures Law), pursuant to a written petition for grace submitted by the taxpayer within a period of six months from the date of publication of this Law, provided that the first payment amounting to 15% of the value of the taxes paid by instalments is settled within the same period.

In the event of default in settling the instalments on their due dates, all the instalments shall fall due and interest at the rate of 12% shall be payable thereon.

Where necessary, the details of application of this Article shall be determined pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

On the mechanisms of licensing for the establishment of a private institution of higher education, or for the creation of a faculty, a geographical branch, an educational level, or a specialisation in a licensed faculty within an existing institution or in one of its geographical branches.

First: Submission of the Licence Application

An application for a licence to establish a new institution, or to create a faculty within an existing institution, or a geographical branch, a specialisation, or an educational level in a licensed faculty within an existing institution or in one of its geographical branches shall be submitted in accordance with a standard form specified at the Directorate General of Higher Education, and shall be duly registered with all its annexes required pursuant to the laws and regulations in force, as follows:

1. The party concerned shall submit two original copies of the application file to the Secretariat of the Council of Higher Education, together with two compact discs containing all the required documents.

2. The Secretariat of the Council shall place the application file on its agenda.

3. The Council shall examine the submitted application at the session following the submission of the application in accordance with its agenda, and shall recommend either its study by the Committee or the rejection of the application.

4. The file which the Council recommends for study shall be referred to the Secretariat of the Committee, which shall place it on its agenda in the order of submission of the applications.

5. The Committee shall verify as to form that the file which is the subject of the application contains all the documents required to be submitted according to the laws and regulations in force, within fifteen days from the date of its receipt of the transaction; should it appear that the file is incomplete as to form due to the existence of deficiencies, the file shall be returned to the party concerned for completion in accordance with its request within a time limit specified by it not exceeding three months.

6. If it appears to the Committee that the file contains all the documents required as to form, it shall draw up a report in which it shall include:

A - The fees for the study of the file in accordance with the provisions of the law and the content of the application.

B - A proposal of a list of the specialised committees to study the file and the names of their members.

C - The determination of the number of copies of the file in a manner consistent with the needs of its study in the Committee and the specialised committees.

7. The Directorate General of Higher Education shall notify the party concerned of the requests of the Committee regarding the value of the file study allowances required to be deposited and the required number of copies of the file.

8. Upon the provision of the copies of the file and the presentation of the certificate of deposit of the allowances and financial solvency by the licence applicant, the Director General of Higher Education shall issue the requisite assignments and refer the files to the Committee and the specialised committees.

Second: Study of the Licence Application

The Committee and the specialised committees shall study the documents of the files referred to them in accordance with the requirements of the law in order to verify that the conditions required for licensing are met, in accordance with the following mechanism:

1. The Committee shall study the file of the regulations, the feasibility study, the buildings, and the financing, and the specialised committees shall study the programmes within two months from their receipt of the application file in the same period.

2. The Committee shall review the reports of the specialised committees and shall draw up a report on the entire file within a period not exceeding one month.

. If the report contains negative observations, the Director General of Higher Education shall notify them to the licence applicant in order to respond thereto within a maximum time limit of two months from the date of his notification thereof, and his reply shall be referred to the Committee so that it may draw up its final report containing its observations on the contents of the file and its opinion regarding the requested licence, and submit it to the Council within a time limit of one month from the date of its notification of the reply.

. In the event that the report does not contain negative observations requiring a response from the licence applicant, the report shall be submitted directly to the Council, and the report shall include, alongside the description of the contents of the file, a clear and reasoned recommendation by the Committee.

3. The Council shall study the report of the Committee submitted to it within a maximum time limit of one month, and shall adopt a reasoned recommendation approving or rejecting the application. In the event that the Council of Higher Education recommends licensing contrary to the opinion of the Committee, it must state the reasons for the recommendation on the basis of the provisions of the law.

4. Upon the recommendation to grant a licence, the Minister shall refer the draft licensing decree to the Council of Ministers accompanied by the recommendation of the Council and the report of the Committee, and the draft decree shall include the following information in accordance with the licence application:

1 - Application for the establishment of an institution of higher education (a university or a university college):

. The name of the licensed legal person and its legal capacity.

. The name of the licensed institution.

. The location of the institution (the cadastral area).

. The type of the institution (university - faculty).

. The faculties and specialisations approved for licensing.

. The system of education and the languages adopted in teaching.

. The degrees authorised to be awarded.

. The time limit within which it must commence instruction, provided that it does not exceed five years from the date of issuance of the decree.

2 - Application for the establishment of a geographical branch of a legally existing institution or the creation of a university campus:

. The name of the licensed university institution.

. The location of the geographical branch (the cadastral area).

. The licensed specialisations approved for licensing in the branch and the degrees authorised to be awarded.

. The time limit within which it must commence instruction, provided that it does not exceed four years from the date of issuance of the decree.

3 - Application for the creation of a faculty in an existing university:

. The name of the licensed university institution.

. The university campus in which the requested creation will take place.

. The faculty, specialisations, and educational levels approved for licensing.

. The time limit within which it must commence instruction, provided that it does not exceed three years from the date of issuance of the decree.

4 - Application for the creation of a specialisation or an educational level in an existing university:

. The name of the licensed university institution.

. The university campus in which the creation of the specialisation will take place.

. The specialisation or specialisations and the educational levels approved for licensing.

. The time limit within which it must commence instruction, provided that it does not exceed two years from the date of issuance of the decree.

Third: Licensing in the Council of Ministers

The Council of Ministers shall decide upon the application which is the subject of the recommendation; if it decides to accept it, it shall issue a decree to that effect.

Granting incentives to enterprises to employ new Lebanese employees

The Lebanese State shall bear the payment of the contributions due to the National Social Security Fund, across all its branches, for a period of two years, in respect of Lebanese employees who are employed during the period extending from the date of publication of this Law until 31/12/2019, for the first time or who were unemployed or had left employment at least six months prior to the publication of this Law, provided that the value of the wage of a single employee does not exceed eighteen million Lebanese pounds per year.

The details of the application of this Article shall be determined, where necessary, pursuant to a decision issued by the Ministers of Finance and Labour.

Raising the deduction specific to certain residential dwellings

The text of Article 52 of the Built Property Tax Law dated 17/9/1962 and its amendments is hereby repealed and replaced with the following text:

Starting from the revenues of the year 2018, an amount of twenty million pounds shall be deducted from the net taxable revenues for each residential unit occupied by a natural person in the capacity of owner or one of the co-owners or a person deemed to be an owner.

The persons referred to in the first paragraph shall benefit, each in proportion to his share in the ownership, in respect of two residential units only, regardless of the number of residential dwellings they have occupied or occupy, namely in respect of the two units having the highest rental values.

The right of the owner to benefit from the deduction for his residence for the years preceding and subsequent to the date of this amendment is preserved starting from the date of his occupancy without applying the provisions of prescription, provided that the taxes paid shall be deemed a right of the Treasury and cannot be refunded.

The details of the application of this Article shall be determined, where necessary, by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

Effecting a settlement on assessments relating to Income Tax and Value Added Tax submitted before the Objections Committees

Notwithstanding any other text, exceptionally, and for one time only, assessments relating to Income Tax and Value Added Tax objected to before the Objections Committees, and which have not been decided upon up to the date of publication of this Law, shall be settled in accordance with the following:

- With respect to assessments relating to Income Tax: for the years 2012 and prior.

- With respect to assessments relating to Value Added Tax: for all years up to 2016 inclusive.

The value of the settlement shall be fixed at fifty percent (50%) of the value of the objected taxes only, excluding the assessment and collection fines that were due.

To benefit from this settlement, the taxpayer is required to submit a written application to the competent tax administration and to pay the amount due from him as a result of the settlement within a period of four months from the effective date of this Law, and the taxpayer may also pay 25% of the value of the settlement within the period of four months specified above, and pay the remaining amounts in three annual instalments, the first of which shall fall due after the lapse of one year from the payment of the first instalment of the value of the settlement at the interest rate provided for in the Tax Procedures Law, and in the event of default in paying any of the instalments, an interest at the rate of 12% per annum on the unpaid amounts shall be due from the taxpayer.

The taxpayer may not choose to benefit from the settlement for part of a single assessment issued by the tax administration, such that the settlement shall cover all objected points within the single assessment.

The Objections Committees notified by the tax administration of the taxpayer's application to effect the settlement shall cease deciding upon the objection.

Sole Article:

- The draft law set forth in Decree No. 1808 dated 3 November 2017 relating to the Water Law is hereby ratified.

- This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Objectives of the Water Law

This Law aims to regulate, develop, rationalise and exploit water resources, to protect them from depletion and pollution, and to raise the efficiency of transmission and distribution systems and the proper maintenance and operation of water installations, with the objective of securing sustainable management of the natural water resources of the Lebanese State.

Rights of Water Beneficiaries

Every beneficiary of any water resource enjoys the right to benefit therefrom in a manner that does not harm such resources or the interests of others, and bears the same obligations imposed with regard to preserving these resources and protecting them from depletion and pollution, and the exploitation of groundwater resources without a prior licence is prohibited, and the State intervenes to regulate the rights and obligations of benefiting from water in accordance with the provisions of this Law and the implementing decrees that will be issued in enforcement of its provisions.

The terms wherever they occur in this Law shall have the following meanings:

1. "Groundwater Aquifer" (Aquifère): A layer or several rocky or geological layers the porous and permeable nature of which allows the flow of groundwater or the accumulation of large quantities of groundwater.

2. "Hydrographic Basin" (Bassin Hydrographique): Any area into which all waters draining through a network of streams and rivers and sometimes lakes flow towards the sea where they empty through a single mouth or opening onto a gulf or delta;

3. "Sub-Basin" (Sous -- Bassin): Any area into which all waters draining through a network of streams and rivers and sometimes lakes flow at a given point of a watercourse.

4. "Water Deficit" (Déficit Hydrique): The noticeable decrease in the quantities of fresh water available in the entire country or in a region or an aquatic ecosystem which is unable to secure its own ecological balance or to respond to the water needs that it usually met.

5. "Surface Waters" (Eaux de Surface): Inland waters, with the exception of groundwater, and coastal waters save in respect of their chemical status, which also include territorial waters;

6. "Groundwater" (Eaux Souterraines): All waters located beneath the surface of the ground in the saturation zone in direct contact with the surface of the ground or the subsoil;

7. "Lake" (Lac): A body of inland water with a still surface whatever the source of its supply;

8. "Body of Groundwater" (Masse d'Eau Souterraine): A distinct (distinct) volume of groundwater within a groundwater aquifer.

9. "Body of Surface Water" (Masse d'Eau Superficielle): A significant element of surface waters such as a lake, a reservoir, a stream, a river, a canal, part of a stream, river or canal, or a stretch of coastal waters.

10. "Water Pollution" (Pollution de l'Eau): The direct or indirect introduction, as a result of human activity, of substances or heat into the air, water or land which may be harmful to human health or to the quality of aquatic ecosystems or terrestrial ecosystems directly dependent on aquatic ecosystems, and which is also liable to result in damage to material property or impairment of or interference with the enjoyment of a sound and stable environment and other legitimate uses thereof;

11. "Stream" (River (Rivière)): A body of inland water flowing for the most part on the surface of the ground and which may flow underground for part of its course;

12. Eau non conventionelle: Non-conventional water resources, which include the treatment and reuse of treated water, the exploitation of marine water springs, the desalination of seawater, and greywater.

13. Nouvelle masse d'eau: Meaning the quantity of conventional and non-conventional water that enters into the water balance of the Lebanese State.

14. Hydrodiplomacie: Namely water diplomacy applied to international basins pursuant to international agreements and United Nations conventions.

Sustainable Water Management: (G.I.R.E) Which is a process that promotes the coordinated development and management of water, land and related resources, in order to maximise the economic and social welfare in an equitable manner without compromising the sustainability of vital ecosystems.

15. Association, meaning an association of irrigation water users, whether of surface water or groundwater, established pursuant to this Law.

16. Irrigation water, which is the water allocated, from the available water resources, for the irrigation of agricultural lands, and which is subject to the provisions of this Law.

17. Irrigation water project, meaning any of the projects established, or under construction as of the date hereof, or to be established in the future, for the purpose of securing the distribution of available water from a specific source to those who meet the conditions for benefiting therefrom.

18. Irrigation water user, who is one of the owners of the lands located within the service area of the Association, or his legal representative, and any person having the right to benefit from the use of the water of irrigation projects, and anyone subsequently authorised to do so.

19. Service area of the Association, meaning the defined geographical area of land that may benefit from a given irrigation project.

20. Irrigated lands, which include lands suitable for irrigation located within the geographical perimeter of any project that is established, under execution, or to be established in the future.

21. Agricultural lands, which are any land that benefits from an established irrigation project, or is granted the right to benefit from one of the projects. It shall be subject to the provisions of this classification even if it was not previously classified on this basis.

22. Transmission network, meaning the set of water infrastructures, previously established or subsequently established, to be used in order to convey water from its source to one or more distribution networks. It consists of the primary network, which is composed of a main network to secure irrigation water, the ownership and management of which remain public, as well as the secondary network which branches off from the main network to be distributed to the regions, where the ownership and management thereof remain public, while the Administration concerned may assign all or part of the management powers in respect of supervision, control and maintenance in favour of an association or union of associations of irrigation water users.

23. Distribution network: Meaning the set of water structures fed from a single specific supply point, which may be used to distribute water to fields for irrigation at the level of agricultural holdings, and which is also defined as the tertiary network. The management, maintenance and operation of this network shall vest in the associations of irrigation water users where they exist.

24. Water supply point, which is the intake or point that constitutes the source from which the service area of the Association is supplied with irrigation water, and which may comprise a structure or an outlet from the transmission network, a water spring, a dam, a river, a well, or any other source of water.

25. Union, meaning a union of a number of associations of irrigation water users established pursuant to this Law.

The Right to Water

This Law recognises the fundamental right of every human being to obtain the water necessary for his needs, and which secures the basic requirements for a dignified life, which justifies obligating beneficiaries to pay subscription fees for their use of water,

Sanitation, that is, the discharge and treatment of wastewater, shall be considered one of the elements of the right to water.

Water as a National Wealth

Water in all its forms is a national wealth the quality of which must be preserved, as well as the rights of the Lebanese State in international watercourses. It includes surface water and groundwater, including fluctuating plumes of fresh water off the coasts and water as an element of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems.

Management of the Public Water Domain

The Ministry of Energy and Water has competence to manage the public water domain.

Elements of the Public Ownership of Water

Water is public property and is not subject to acquisition, ownership, or disposal in any form whatsoever. Subject to the provisions of the two Decisions No. 144 S dated 10 June 1925 and Decision No. 320 dated 26 May 1926, the public ownership of water includes the following cases: water in all its natural states, its geomorphological sites, its appurtenances, and the public installations allocated or necessary for its management, and comprises on this basis:

A - Watercourses, including their beds, and the banks up to the highest limit reached by the water before its overflow, and up to the lands appurtenant to the banks of watercourses; the banks of watercourses, their easements, and their setbacks shall be determined by decrees.

B - Natural or artificial lakes, coastal lagoons, marshes, and, in general, water bodies.

C - Groundwater, including submarine freshwater springs gushing at sea off the Lebanese coasts.

D - Springs, wells, drillings, irrigation channels, water sources, and other water resources allocated to the public, as well as their potential protection zones for the areas surrounding them and designated for their direct protection.

E - Marine or riverine dams, water dams, passages, and the installations appurtenant thereto.

F - Irrigation, sanitation, and drainage canals, water conveyance canals and their branches, pipes, water treatment installations, pumping stations, reservoirs, and wastewater purification plants when such installations are allocated for public use, as well as the equipment and lands appertaining thereto.

G - Waterfalls suitable for generating electrical energy.

Non-Public Waters

Whoever collects rainwater and stores it in a private installation and in swimming pools, pools designated for recreation, marshes, ponds and reservoirs has the full right to use it, and it does not form part of the public domain of the Lebanese State.

Groundwater

Groundwater, whatever its degree of depth may reach, is subject to a special regime with respect to protection and monitoring, such that no person may extract groundwater by drilling artesian wells or by any other means without obtaining a prior permit or licence from the Ministry of Energy and Water, within the conditions set forth pursuant to the provisions of this Law.

Boundaries of the Public Water Domain

The boundaries of the public water domain of the Lebanese State and its appurtenances are those designated pursuant to the provisions of Title II of Decision No. 144/S dated 10 June 1925 relating to the definition, delimitation and temporary occupation of the public domain.

Acquired Rights over Water

Acquired rights over water prior to the issuance of Decision 144/S dated 10/6/1925 shall be exercised in accordance with the customs and usages that justified their recognition, so long as they do not conflict with the requirements of sustainable water management, subject to the following provisions:

The invocation of acquired rights shall cease when such rights become of no avail and the reasons for which they were recognised cease to exist, such that the exercise of these rights becomes impossible for material reasons, including, for example, the selection of the purpose prepared for them in the real properties.

Acquired rights over water may not be assigned separately from the real property upon which these rights are exercised.

The rules governing the exercise of the lapse of acquired rights, as well as the potential conditions for suspending them in order to confront any water deficit, shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Energy and Water.

The Water Register

A Water Register shall be established in the Ministry of Energy and Water. The Water Register shall consist of the register of acquired rights referred to in the preceding article above of this Law and of the general inventory of waters that constitute the aquatic ecosystem of the Lebanese State, and it is a non-probative administrative document prepared and periodically updated by the Ministry of Energy and Water.

The Land Registry Secretariat, the Directorate General of Urban Planning, the municipalities and, in general, all public administrations affiliated with the Lebanese State that possess records and data relating to water must provide the Water Register with such data and information.

The National Water Authority

A national authority called the "National Water Authority" shall be established at the Presidency of the Council of Ministers, chaired by the President of the Council of Ministers and with the Minister of Energy and Water as Vice-President, and composed of the Ministers of Environment, Industry, Agriculture, Public Health and Tourism, in addition to the Director General of Hydraulic and Electric Resources, the Director General of Exploitation, the Chairmen of the Boards of Directors of the Public Water Establishments and their Directors General, persons specialised in this field, and representatives of municipalities and of non-governmental associations active in the field of preserving aquatic environmental activities,

General Provisions

Sustainable water management shall be achieved through a General Master Plan for Water applicable to the entire Lebanese territory and including coastal waters (les eaux Cotieres) and basin networks Schemas de (bassin) within the scope of the hydrographic basin (Bassin Hydrographique), and, where necessary, through long-term agreements ensuring sustainable water management.

The General Master Plan for Water

The Lebanese Republic shall be divided into water or administrative basins and regions, and the water resources of each of them shall be assessed and their development and use shall be planned as existing and indivisible units, and they shall be regulated on the basis of the principle of integrated water resources management in accordance with the orientations of social and economic development and the preservation of the environment. The Ministry of Energy and Water shall prepare the General Master Plan, and it shall be approved by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.

Preparation of the General Master Plan for Water

The Ministry of Energy and Water, in cooperation with the Public Water Exploitation Establishments, shall draw up the General Master Plan for Water, and it shall be approved pursuant to a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Energy and Water.

Scope of Application of the General Master Plan for Water and Its Legal Effects

When applying the General Master Plan for Water, the Administration concerned shall take into consideration all plans, programmes, basin plans, and granted licences and permits, as well as urban planning, population ratios in the regions, and the status of classified establishments, and in general take into consideration all prior administrative decisions relating to water.

Evaluation of the General Master Plan for Water

The General Master Plan for Water shall be subject to evaluation and reconsideration once every five years and whenever the need therefor arises.

The Ministry of Energy and Water shall be responsible for establishing the principles of general water planning for the Lebanese Republic in light of the results of the assessment of basins or water service areas, such that it includes the general indicators of the status of water basins in the various Lebanese regions and the trends in water demand for all water uses in the short, medium and long term, in accordance with the following:

The Ministry of Energy and Water shall be required to prepare plans for the main and secondary water basins in areas suffering from a decline in their water resources or from pollution in the aquatic ecosystems therein.

The scope of the basin plans shall be determined in coordination with the public water exploitation establishment or establishments.

The Minister of Energy and Water shall prepare and put into effect the basin plan that is prepared.

The details of implementation of this Article shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, upon the proposal of the Minister of Energy and Water.

Second - Content of the Basin Plans

The basin plans shall include the following:

1- A detailed report presenting the characteristics of the basin that justify preparing the plan for it, based on a comprehensive assessment of the status of water and ecosystems therein.

2- An administrative document determining:

a - The qualitative and quantitative objectives and the presumed time limits for achieving them,

b - An assessment of the water resources in the water basin in terms of quantity and quality;

c - Measures for monitoring the discharge of waste and the necessity of preserving water, aquatic ecosystems, and animal, fish and plant wealth.

d - Priority of allocation for the equitable distribution of water, the treatment and reuse of water, and control and monitoring measures that ensure the equitable and equal use of water;

e - The manner of distributing water among the various categories of beneficiaries.

f - Identification of non-conventional water sources (Non -- Conventionnelles).

g - Conditions for managing the resource during crises, such as pollution, water scarcity, floods and fires.

h - Identification of the means to be used to reach the defined objectives,

i - Identification of the indicators that allow following up on completed works and evaluating the measures, programmes and commitments undertaken in relation to the objectives.

3- Maps that allow identifying the locations targeted in the plan.

Decisions relating to basin plans must be consistent with the provisions of the General Water Master Plan.

Basin Classification System

The Ministry of Energy and Water shall establish a system for the classification of basins and water areas in the light of their water conditions, the purpose of which shall be to place those that are similar under a single pattern of measures.

Basin Plans

Each basin or area shall have a water plan consistent with the water policy and with the principle of general water planning of the Lebanese Republic, and these established plans, once approved, shall be deemed an integral part of the General Master Plan.

Agreements for the Sustainable Management of Water:

In order to ensure the sustainable management of a surface or underground body of water, the Ministry of Energy and Water shall undertake the conclusion of agreements with the public and private sectors, with the necessity of complying with the provisions of the Public Accounting Law and ensuring the principles of competition and transparency; these agreements shall address the implementation of investment projects for the waters of lakes, rivers, groundwater reservoirs, and all other water sources.

The aforementioned agreements shall determine the programme of works and operations to be completed to achieve these objectives, the period required for implementation, and the contributions of the partners in financing these projects, and shall, in their implementation, observe the provisions of the General Master Plan for Water and the basin plans.

General Provisions

Subject to the provisions of Articles (1) and (2) of Decision No. 320 dated 26 May 1926 and pursuant to Law No. 221 dated 29 May 2000 and its amendments, and with the aim of achieving the sustainable management of water and aquatic ecosystems, the Ministry of Energy and Water shall contribute, with the Lebanese Standards Institution and the Ministry of Environment, quality standards and the provisions necessary for the preservation of water and the ecosystems necessary therefor, and in particular shall determine the various types of water consumption and their cumulative impacts on the aquatic environment.

Competence for the Protection of Water Resources

The Ministry of Energy and Water shall assume competence for the protection of water resources from pollution, emission standards, pollution sources, the conditions for achieving monitoring of the equipment belonging to these facilities, the prevention of activities that may lead to the pollution or degradation of water quality, and the combating of cases of emergency pollution in accordance with what is stated in the preceding Article above;

Technical Inspection and Water Quality

The Ministry of Energy and Water, in cooperation with the concerned public water investment establishments, shall undertake the technical inspection of equipment, installations, and works in order to verify the quality of the extracted water and to monitor and protect water systems from pollution. It shall also ensure the monitoring of the quality of surface, ground, coastal, and gushing waters, including springs, wells, and exploited or abandoned borings;

Compliance with the Provisions of the Environment Law

Every owner of an industrial installation must comply with the provisions of the Law on the Protection of the Environment in Lebanon, in particular Articles 24 to 48 of Law No. 444/2002,

Time Limit for Regularising the Status of Existing Installations

Owners of industrial installations existing prior to the issuance of this Law and all other persons practising any of the activities provided for in the preceding Article must apply to the competent authorities within six months from the date of entry into force of this Law to regularise the status of their installations in accordance with the provisions of this Law, under penalty of withdrawal of the licences previously granted to them.

Preservation of the Grade and Quality of Water

The public water establishments shall determine the rules for the equitable distribution of water among the various categories of beneficiaries, while preserving the grade and quality of water; whereby they must prohibit any form of discharge and deposition (jet et rejet) or storage (dépot), whether direct or indirect, of wastewater or polluted water, prohibit the performance of any act of any kind whatsoever that leads to altering the quality of water or aquatic ecosystems, and impose the necessary measures to preserve the quality of water;

Monitoring Water Quality

The Ministry of Energy and Water and the public water establishments, each within its respective competence, shall undertake the monitoring of water quality at the level of resources so as to guarantee its suitability for use, and the public water establishments shall undertake monitoring during transport, distribution, and use.

Conditions for Transporting Water by Tankers and Barrels

It is prohibited to sell or distribute water for drinking purposes by means of barrels, mobile tankers, distribution networks, or by any means whatsoever, unless such means conform to the imposed standards and the applicable controls for transporting water designated for such purposes, subject to the provisions of Law No. 210 dated 30/3/2012.

The Water Code

The installations, facilities, works and activities mentioned in the preceding Article above must be set out in a code regulated by virtue of a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Energy and Water. This code shall clarify the nature of the controls to which these activities are subject, taking into consideration the effects that may result therefrom on the quality or level of waters and on aquatic ecosystems.

The specific levels that apply to the water scarcity areas defined in the General Master Plan shall be precisely determined in the code.

Traditional Usufruct Rights

Traditional rights in the use of rainwater harvesting waters and naturally flowing torrent waters shall be observed with respect to their use for irrigation and their connection to the agricultural land benefiting therefrom.

Public Interest and the Right of Usufruct

The Ministry of Energy and Water shall determine the cases in which the Lebanese State may take possession of the rights of usufruct over waters if the public interest or the necessity of rationalising water uses so requires, with fair compensation to the beneficiaries in accordance with the laws in force.

Regularisation of the Status of Drilled Wells

Holders of rights of usufruct over the waters of groundwater wells drilled by virtue of a notice and acknowledgement or by virtue of subsequent licences, and prior to the issuance of this Law, shall be required to apply to the competent authority at the Ministry of Energy and Water to regularise their status within a period not exceeding one year from the date of entry into force of this Law, under penalty of forfeiture of the right of usufruct over these waters.

System of Declarations

Installations, facilities, works and activities that do not have the magnitude of risks provided for in the preceding Article, but that may affect water and aquatic ecosystems, shall be subject to declaration.

The Ministry of Energy and Water shall deliver to the applicant a declaration receipt specifying the instructions with which he is required to comply.

Procedures of Application

The procedures for applying the provisions set forth in this Chapter shall be determined pursuant to a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Energy and Water, and this decree must include: the applicable procedures, environmental impact analysis, in particular the procedures relating to the amendment of licences and declarations for extractions, and specifically the cases in which a minimum water level may be imposed, and the measures imposed for monitoring compliance with the provisions of this Chapter.

Administrative Penalties

Whoever commits a violation of the provisions of the system of licences and declarations provided for under the provisions of the thirty-ninth, fortieth and forty-first Articles of this Law and Articles 745 to 749 of the Penal Code, shall be subject, in addition to criminal prosecution specified in the body of Title Eight of this Law, to administrative penalties determined as follows:

1- Warning the offender, operator or owner to comply, within a period determined by the Ministry of Energy and Water, with the provisions and instructions relating to the subject matter of the violation.

2- Determining the measures that the offender is required to undertake in order to put an end to the damage he has caused;

3- In the event of the existence of a risk of pollution or of deterioration of the conditions of the aquatic ecosystem, or damage to public health, or a threat affecting the supply of potable water, taking immediate measures at the expense and responsibility of the persons referred to above to limit and prevent the occurring pollution.

4- Suspending or withdrawing the licence.

5- Drawing up an infringement report against the offender and referring it by the Minister of Energy and Water to the competent Public Prosecution.

The Ministry of Energy and Water and the Public Water Establishments, upon becoming aware of the occurrence of any damage to aquatic ecosystems, are required to immediately take the initiative to remedy the causes of the occurring damage, and shall be entitled to recover the expenses they have incurred from the person or persons who bear the responsibility for causing the damage, before the competent judicial authorities.

Incidents

Every person who has knowledge of an incident that poses a danger to public safety and to the quality, distribution and preservation of water, as well as to aquatic flora and fish resources, shall promptly notify the competent authorities.

Every person who has caused any act that constitutes damage to water quality must, immediately upon learning of the matter, proceed to take all appropriate measures to put an end to the danger or to the damage caused to the aquatic environment and proceed to remedy the same.

The competent administration that has intervened to take the measures aimed at putting an end to the damage caused to aquatic ecosystems shall have the right to recover the costs it has incurred from the person who caused the damage.

The Industrial and Commercial Character of the Public Water Utility

The public water utility comprises the public investment establishments for potable water, irrigation and wastewater. It shall be managed essentially as any public utility of an industrial and commercial character, subject to observance of the principle of continuity of the public utility. It shall be financed primarily from the fees paid by the beneficiaries of this sector.

Fees

The fees or tariffs pertaining to public water services are determined through the application of the general legal principles in this regard, which require the consumer to pay the fees for his water consumption, and the polluter to pay the fees for repairing the damage he has caused.

These fees shall be determined after taking into consideration the necessary financial equilibrium for each service and the social and economic conditions of the beneficiaries, and these fees shall take a progressive course based on the quantity of consumption.

The Principle of Financial Equilibrium

The principles of financial equilibrium and the financing of public water utilities must be achieved from the revenues of the subscriptions paid by the users or beneficiaries, and these principles must be realised progressively.

Public Aid

The Lebanese State may, whenever the need arises, provide aid to the public water utility, either by securing the necessary financing through raising the value of the subscription fees for the services provided thereby or for the purpose of ensuring the protection of the water resource, or finally, on a temporary basis and by way of exception to the principle set forth in the above Article, in which latter case the State may contribute to financing the expenses of renewing, modernising and expanding the project works of the public water investment establishments, as well as securing the operating expenses of such projects.

The State may also secure financial grants for the public water investment establishments in light of the objectives and the quantity and quality of the production results achieved for each public establishment.

Financial Provisions

1- The budget and accounts of each of the public water exploitation establishments shall show in detail the manner of distributing the operations of operation, exploitation, and maintenance with respect to each of drinking water, wastewater, and agricultural irrigation, provided that the charges pertaining to each of these uses are used to finance the burdens thereof.

The funds and fees collected from the above operations of operation may not be used to finance the exploitation and maintenance of precipitation collection water stations.

2- The operating charges of each service shall be financed exclusively from the revenues thereof, and such revenues may not be transferred to another service. They shall include the operating expenditures, including the remuneration of the manager in the event of delegation of management, the burdens of renewing and expanding the installations, the provision for bad debts, and all provisions necessary to maintain the requirements of the public utility.

A special accounting plan must be prepared for each service within the public water exploitation establishments.

Approval of Charges

The public water establishments shall propose the tariffs of charges for public water services, including the charges for connection to the public networks within the scope of the perimeter of the exploitation area of the establishment, provided that they are coupled with the approval of the tutelage authority.

Charges (Tariffs)

The charges established pursuant to this Law shall include:

Charges for the conservation of the water resource and the protection of aquatic systems from pollution,

Charges resulting from pollution and charges for potable water services, wastewater treatment, and irrigation.

Charges Relating to the Conservation of Water Resources and the Protection of Aquatic Systems

Natural and legal persons who use water shall be subject to a charge based on the number of cubic metres withdrawn, consumed, or allocated for supply, provided that this charge is used to finance the works of conserving the water resource and protecting aquatic ecosystems. The application of the flat-rate tariff shall also continue temporarily in certain areas not qualified for the volumetric tariff, until the completion of the procedures leading to the application thereof, provided that they are determined by a decree.

When determining the persons liable, the activities concerned, and the value of the charges, consideration shall be given to the economic, social, cultural, and environmental importance of such activities, and the revenues and profits of whatever kind.

The revenues of the charges enumerated above shall be paid into a special account opened at the Bank of Lebanon.

The public establishments shall collect the charges for the conservation of the resource and the protection of aquatic systems, whoever the beneficiary may be.

Pollution Compensation Charges

Natural and legal persons the nature of whose activities leads to the pollution or an increase in the rate of pollution of water or to the deterioration of the aquatic environment shall be subject to a compensation charge to be determined by decree and allocated to finance the measures that the Administration must take and to ensure the preservation of the aquatic environment.

The compensation charge referred to above must be proportionate to the gravity of the pollution and the volume of damage caused to the aquatic environment, and this charge may be reduced in light of the measures taken by the person causing the damage to remediate it, and this charge must also include the funding disbursed from the Public Treasury for this purpose.

This compensation charge shall be paid into a special account opened at the Bank of Lebanon.

The payment of pollution compensation charges shall not constitute an impediment to the arising of criminal liability upon the person liable in the case where his acts are a source of damage or constitute a criminal offence.

Potable Water Charges

The annual subscription charge for potable water shall be determined by decree based on what is determined by the Public Water Exploitation Establishments for the region to which the subscriber belongs,

and these charges and subscriptions shall fall due from every person occupying an independent dwelling or a section in a building connected to the public water network.

Where a building is equipped with a water meter, the determination of the subscription charge for the public potable water network shall be determined on the basis of the quantity of water consumed by the subscriber, without any additional fee being due on this charge.

Sanitation Charges

The sanitation charges determined pursuant to the provisions of this Law shall include collective sanitation charges and non-collective sanitation charges.

1. Collective sanitation charges shall be payable by every person who occupies or owns a dwelling in an independent real property or a unit in a building connected to the public sanitation network, and this charge shall be determined by decree on the basis of the volume of water discharged by the beneficiaries of the service, whether its source is the public potable water network or any other source.

The charge for the non-domestic use of the public sanitation network shall be determined by decree on the basis of the volume of water discharged and the pollution load of the emissions resulting therefrom.

Natural or legal persons bound by the obligation to connect to the collective sanitation network pursuant to the provisions of this Law and who do not comply with this obligation shall be subject automatically to a fine equal to the value of the charge determined for connection to the collective sanitation network.

2. As for non-collective sanitation charges, they shall also be payable by every person who occupies an independent house or a unit of a building not connected to the sanitation network as defined in Paragraph «1» above, on the basis of the quantity of water discharged.

Irrigation Charge

The irrigation charge shall be due from every beneficiary or owner of a real property connected to the public irrigation network.

The value of the charges payable in respect of the irrigated area, the quantities of water consumed, and the nature of the irrigated crops shall be determined by decree.

The irrigation charge aims to finance the depreciation, expenses, maintenance, and modernisation of agricultural irrigation installations.

Issuance of Subscription Invoices

Whatever the method adopted for the management of the public utility, the amounts payable by the beneficiaries of this utility shall be determined by invoices issued in accordance with the principles of the Public Accounting Law; the invoice shall clearly indicate the charges pertaining to each utility.

Procedures for Issuing and Settling Invoices

Public Water Exploitation Establishments may issue several invoices per year, for each beneficiary of the water of this utility who has the option to settle the value of the subscriptions due per year in several instalments.

Notification Relating to Tariffs

Water beneficiaries shall be notified of the new tariffs, the justifications for their amendment, and the date of their entry into force by an official notice circulated to the media. The invoice issued after the amendment of the tariff must specify the old and new tariffs.

Polling the opinion of beneficiaries

The Public Water Investment Establishments shall conduct, every three years, an opinion poll of the beneficiaries; the results of this study shall be sent to the Minister of Energy and Water and the Minister of Finance, and its result shall be published through the media.

Public water utilities

1- The public drinking water utility includes the service of collecting, producing, treating, transporting, storing and distributing water. Distribution to subscribers shall take place primarily by means of branch connections from the network. Water may not be provided otherwise than as mentioned except in exceptional and temporary cases.

2- The collective public wastewater utility includes collecting, transporting and treating wastewater. The objective of purifying wastewater is the elimination of pollutants so that it is compatible with the receiving environments. Purification operations include treating and cleaning all pollutants and wastes in the network and purification plants up to the outfalls.

3- Wastewater is primarily of domestic origin, and by virtue of ordinary or special agreements in this regard, wastewater resulting from commercial or industrial activities may be connected to the public wastewater network provided that such water is compatible with the technical standards of the networks and purification plants.

4- The Public Water Investment Establishments and the National Authority for the Litani River may supply water for agricultural purposes by means of the irrigation network or by means of a set of hydraulic works {Ouvrages hydrauliques}.

The Public Water Investment Establishments

The Public Water Investment Establishments shall manage the public water utility in accordance with the provisions of Law No. 221 dated 29/5/2000 and its amendments and the regulations issued in implementation thereof.

Rules for private sector participation

First: Management of the public utility by delegation

The public utility for drinking water, wastewater and irrigation may be managed by way of management by delegation, and management by delegation is a contract whereby a legal person of public law entrusts the management of a public utility to a public or private operator, whose remuneration is mostly linked to the results of operating the utility. The delegatee may also be entrusted with constructing installations and acquiring the properties necessary for the utility.

Second: Forms of private sector participation

Private sector participation takes forms including a concession for a public benefit, or a lease contract (affermage), or a management contract, or being the subject of a contract (design, build, operate and transfer), etc. (BOT) and (DBOT).

The legal regime governing the procedures of delegation in the public water utility

First: Duration of delegation

The duration of the contracts for the management of the public utility by delegation, their effective date and their expiry date shall be clearly specified in such contracts, provided that it shall in no case exceed thirty years from the date of signing the contract.

Second: Delegated management contracts

Delegated management contracts may not include anything contrary to the object of operating the public water utility.

The scope of the delegated management of the public utility, its conditions and the tariffs imposed on ratepayers, which may be reviewed so as to secure the public interest and the interests of ratepayers whenever the need arises, shall be specified in the contract and the book of specifications.

Third: Delegation procedures

Subject to the legal provisions applicable to public utility concessions, the delegation relating to the public utility shall take place in accordance with procedures specified in a decree that allows for fair competition among tenderers.

Water quality

Distributed water must be potable. This applies regardless of the form of management of the utility, and the competent administrations shall ensure, under the supervision of the Ministers of Energy and Water and of Public Health, the application of the standards and specifications in force.

Principle of exclusivity of the utility

Within the scope of operation, the public potable water utility shall enjoy exclusivity of distribution and shall also enjoy within this scope the exclusive right to maintain all installations and water conduits necessary for the utility.

Obligation of connection

Every building owner is obliged to connect his building and all sections therein to the public network for the distribution of potable water prior to their occupancy, and the connection shall be carried out in accordance with the regulations established by the Public Water Exploitation Establishment.

Special subscription contracts

The public potable water utility may distribute water to beneficiaries for non-domestic purposes, and special subscriptions shall be determined in this case.

Performance of the utility

Pursuant to the regulations or to the provisions of a performance contract concluded with the Administration, the public potable water utility is obliged to meet the requirements relating to the continuity and quality of the supplied water, as well as to observe the time limits relating to applications for subscriptions or the termination thereof.

Measurement of potable water consumption

Connection to the network shall be carried out in accordance with the contract subscribed to by the subscriber, and this shall include a suitable meter to measure his consumption. As for connections not equipped with meters, they must meet this condition within a time limit specified by the Public Water Exploitation Establishment.

General provisions

Subject to the legal provisions in force, the public investment establishments and the National Authority for the Litani River shall undertake the management of irrigation water, including the maintenance of water conveyance systems, and its storage, transport, distribution and the preservation of its quality.

Applications for a licence to withdraw water or the declarations provided for in Articles thirty-nine and forty of this Law shall include a document specifying the supply perimeter, the nature of the irrigated crops and the seasonal quantities withdrawn.

Every amendment to the irrigation perimeter or increase in the seasonal quantities shall require a new declaration or an amendment to the granted licence.

The establishments entrusted with irrigation shall establish a register showing the names of the beneficiaries, the irrigated areas, the adopted crops and the quantities withdrawn, which shall be continuously updated.

The Association

The Association shall be established in accordance with the provisions of this Law. It shall have an independent legal personality not seeking profit, and it is of public utility, not subject to any kind of taxes and fees,

without the need for the issuance of any other text consecrating this exemption.

Each association shall operate, exclusively, within its perimeter. The perimeter of an association may not overlap with the perimeter of another association.

Each association shall have its own unique designation, which may bear the name of its place of operation, or other distinctive names, which must begin with the following phrase: "Irrigation Water Users Association".

Regulations of the Public Potable Water Utility

The regulations of the public potable water utility shall define the relations with the beneficiaries of water, and in particular the rules governing private connections and subscriptions, the performance of the utility, and the places designated for the installation of meters and gauges.

Principle of Exclusivity of the Utility

Within the scope of exploitation defined in the General Master Plan for Water provided for in Article Fourteen of this Law, the public collective sanitation utility shall enjoy, exclusively, the right to collect wastewater, and shall also enjoy within this scope the exclusive right to maintain all installations and conduits necessary for this utility.

Obligation to Connect to the Public Sanitation Network

Within the scope of collective sanitation, every owner of a building must connect the building to the network within a period not exceeding two years from the date of execution of this network.

As for buildings or sections not designated for habitation, they must be connected to the sanitation network within the aforementioned period, with respect to waste of a domestic nature.

Every person is obliged to connect to the sanitation network. However, if he benefits wholly or partially from a private water source, he must declare this to the establishment that manages the public utility. The consumption carried out through this source shall be measured in the same manner in which consumptions on the public potable water network are measured.

Special Subscription Contracts

The public sanitation utility shall have the right to approve the connection of non-domestic wastewater pursuant to a special connection agreement, and it may also refuse the same if the nature or volume of such waste leads to a disruption in the operation of the sanitation and wastewater treatment installations. The rules for assessing pollution and discharged volumes shall be defined in the aforementioned agreement.

Exceptionally, temporary agreements for a specified period may be approved in the event that no damage results therefrom to the conveyance or wastewater treatment installations or to the receiving medium into which they discharge.

Performance of the Utility

The public collective sanitation utility shall undertake to guarantee the continuity and quality of the collection, treatment and purification of wastewater.

Regulations of the Public Collective Sanitation Utility

Relations with the beneficiaries of the collective sanitation network shall be governed by the service rules established by the public water exploitation establishments for the management of this utility, and approved by the tutelage authority.

Supervision of Non-Collective Sanitation Installations

The rules adopted by the administration for the supervision and management of non-collective sanitation installations shall be defined by decree.

Activities of the Association

The activities of the Water Association shall consist of the following:

- Operating, maintaining and preserving the distribution network within its scope.

- Taking measures to combat soil erosion and salinity, and promoting the protection of the environment.

- Regulating the process of benefiting from and using irrigation water and collecting the fees due and payable from the members, in return for the services provided to them.

- Providing irrigation equipment, machinery, tools and installations necessary for operating and preserving the relevant water distribution network, as well as ensuring their replacement, operation and maintenance.

- Training its members in the use of modern irrigation techniques, aspects of irrigated agriculture, and methods of saving in water consumption.

- Contributing to and assisting in the establishment, improvement, rehabilitation, operation and maintenance of the infrastructure complementary to irrigation projects, and in particular the main and secondary drainage canals within the scope of the Association.

- Endeavouring to resolve disputes arising between members of the Association or with third parties.

- Working to observe, respect and guarantee the interests of the members of the Association.

- Complying, in accordance with the public groundwater management plan, with the permitted annual usage limits for the wells located within the scope of the Association, and enforcing compliance with those limits.

Fundamental Principles

Every association shall adhere to and respect in its work the following principles:
