- Justice and equity, meaning that it shall seek to respect the rights of its members on an equal footing, and that the association shall operate in a fair and just manner with regard to making decisions and distributing irrigation water to the beneficiaries, and in a manner that observes proportionality and reconciliation between needs and available capabilities.

- Rationalisation of the use of resources, meaning that the association shall manage the distribution network within its scope in a rational manner that prevents the excessive use of water, soil erosion, salinity and pollution, in addition to promoting environmental protection.

- Non-discrimination, meaning equality in dealing with the members of the association, which means not causing any suffering from discrimination, in any case, and on any basis whatsoever.

- Transparency and participation, meaning that the association shall operate in a public, clear, and transparent manner, and encourage members to participate effectively in its administrative bodies.

- Cost recovery and providing the possibility of financial sustainability and continuity, which requires that fees be determined so as to provide the appropriate and necessary financial resources to enable it to fulfil all its obligations and responsibilities, provided that all reasonable efforts are made to ensure the collection of these fees. The association shall work to determine its fees in the light of the obligations, burdens and expenses resulting from its activity, and in particular the fees due to the relevant Service or Public Establishment.

Main objectives for establishing irrigation associations

The objectives set forth below are mentioned by way of example and not limitation:

- Providing the possibility of using the water of the irrigation project and benefiting from it for all its members.

- Contributing to the implementation and management of irrigation projects and working towards their sustainability.

- Reducing State expropriations and encouraging the right of way easement between irrigated properties.

- Participating in drawing up plans for intakes and manholes of the tertiary network water.

- Assisting in land reclamation.

- Contributing and expressing an opinion regarding real estate regulation, and expressing an opinion on land consolidation and subdivision operations and other real estate affairs within the scope of the association.

- Improving and developing irrigation techniques.

- Managing distribution networks (the tertiary network), and maintaining, operating and exploiting them.

- Protecting the irrigation water network and all equipment and structures appertaining thereto.

- Seeking to resolve disputes that arise between members of the association or with third parties.

- Representing the association and following up on the affairs of its members before the competent official authorities.

- Acquiring real estate, machinery and equipment necessary for developing the work.

- Monitoring the quality of the irrigation water used and providing the necessary quality and standard.

- Granting aid and compensation and accepting gifts, contributions and donations.

- Ensuring that water is used for irrigation works and imposing fines and penalties on violators in accordance with the provisions of this Law and the laws in force.

- Urging members to resort to the association in the event of any dispute between them so as to prevent the act of taking the law into one's own hands.

Union of Irrigation Water Users Associations

A union of irrigation water users associations may be established, for the purpose of managing the transmission/conveyance network, or a part thereof, in order to coordinate the supply of irrigation water to two or more water associations.

A union shall be established ipso jure pursuant to a decision by the Ministry of Energy and Water, or on a voluntary basis and pursuant to a decision by the majority of the water associations supplied with irrigation water from a transmission network that is expected to be managed by the union.

Two or more established associations may found a union of associations, in accordance with the same conditions stipulated for the establishment of an irrigation water users association.

Every association that benefits from the water of the transmission/conveyance network managed by the union shall be considered a member of that union.

The union is prohibited from supplying irrigation water to entities other than the water associations that are considered members thereof. It must not undertake any activities within an area that is subject to the responsibility of any of its member associations, except upon the request of that member.

General Obligations of the State

The State shall undertake the maintenance of the public water utility, and the works and operations relating thereto may be ensured pursuant to agreements or contracts. The State, its contractors and the beneficiaries of rights over the public water utility must ensure the maintenance of aquatic environments and the protection of the national fish wealth. They must also ensure the free flow of water and the maintenance of the installations connected therewith.

Obligations of Owners of Riverbanks

The owner of the real property adjacent to the bank must ensure proper care of the banks and the preservation of plant and animal life while respecting the balance of aquatic ecosystems.

Establishments, Cooperatives, and Associations Prior to the Provisions of This Law

Any existing legal establishment or cooperative established to collectively operate and maintain a distribution network, including any association established in accordance with the Law on Associations of 1909, must be re-registered in accordance with the provisions of this Law, within two years from the entry into force of this Law.

Annual Report of the Public Water Establishments

The Public Water Establishments shall each prepare, within its geographical scope, an annual report on the water utilities subject to its geographical scope, in accordance with what is provided for under the provisions of Article /6/ of Law No. 221/2000 and its amendments.

The report shall set out the administrative, technical, and financial characteristics and conditions, operating procedures, and utility performance, the changes occurring in the quality of distributed water, the exploitation rate, the fees, the status of bill collection, the current and future water needs, as well as the completed extension and network renewal works and the programmes established therefor.

This report shall be submitted to the Minister of Energy and Water following its approval by the boards of directors of each of the Public Water Exploitation Establishments.

Principles

Every individual must contribute effectively to the preservation and to aquatic ecosystems and water and their protection across all Lebanese territory, and inform the competent Administration of any defect or damage to which they may be exposed.

The public authorities, and in particular the Public Water Establishments, the Governors,

and the Ministry of Environment, shall each within the scope of its competence oversee the protection of water and aquatic ecosystems in accordance with the legal provisions in force.

Preservation of Aquatic Environments

The preservation of aquatic environments shall be considered an element of the management of the public water utility.

Protection of Water Collection Sites

First - Scope of Protection:

With a view to ensuring the protection of water quality, it shall be required, prior to or upon licensing works and installations erected for the diversion of surface water and the extraction of groundwater intended for human consumption, to designate the pivot point of the extractions and the perimeter of each of the immediate protection, the adjacent protection, and, if necessary, the remote protection.

This perimeter shall also be determined in cases of diversion and extractions subject to declarations, so long as the water is allocated partially or wholly for human consumption.

Second - Regime of Protection Zones

The State shall expropriate in full, in favour of the Public Water Exploitation Establishments, the lands located within the immediate protection perimeter, and these Establishments shall undertake to fence them and to ensure that they are allocated exclusively for water diversion and maintained regularly for this purpose.

There shall be prohibited within the adjacent protection perimeter all constructions and activities that are liable to harm, directly or indirectly, the quality of the water or the aquifer, or that may render such water unfit for human consumption.

This prohibition shall apply in particular to waste and refuse dumps, the spreading of fertilisers, depots of hydrocarbons and any substances involving toxic hazards, in particular chemical substances, pesticides and fertilisers, the drilling of wells, and the extraction of mineral substances.

In complement to the immediate perimeter and the adjacent perimeter, the competent authority may determine a remote protection perimeter within which the depots, installations and activities mentioned in the preceding paragraph are regulated in order to avoid the pollution risks that they may pose to the extracted water.

Third - Protection of the Natural and Cultural Water Heritage

In public parks (parcs nationaux) and natural reserves, as well as in wetlands of international importance included on the list provided for by the Ramsar Convention (Ramsar) dated 2 February 1971, acts that are liable to compromise the balance of these ecosystems or that may affect their biological diversity (diversite biologique) shall be subject to regulation and, if necessary, prohibited therein, by which is meant in particular: uses of water that lead to modifying its level, the spreading of chemical substances for any purpose whatsoever and especially agricultural pesticides, or the discharge of liquid waste (rejets d'effluents) or toxic substances, or the drainage of wastewater, and the accumulation of filth or household or industrial waste.

If need be, the regulation or prohibition may extend to acts carried out or anticipated outside the perimeter of the protected area or the wetland.

A plan prepared for this purpose must regulate the wetlands of international importance included on the list provided for by the Ramsar Convention.

Fourth - Cultural Water Heritage

Natural environmental sites and landscapes represent, from the aesthetic and cultural standpoint, a special interest linked to the presence of water, and they may be the object of special protection based in particular on the regulation of activities and installations that may cause damage to them, or the prohibition thereof if necessary.

The protection measures referred to above shall result from decisions taken jointly by the Ministers of Energy and Water, Environment, and Culture. They shall also apply to water areas and underwater areas that are of archaeological interest.

Fifth - Protection of Coastal Submarine Springs:

Freshwater submarine spring sources along the Lebanese coast shall be identified pursuant to a decision taken by the Minister of Energy and Water, and these springs shall be subject to a special protection perimeter for which immediate protection zones shall be determined, within which the carrying out of certain activities, in particular fishing, navigation, and any underwater activities or work, shall be prohibited.

The conditions for the implementation of this Article, as well as the detailed rules for allocating the submarine spring water to supply the population or for other uses, shall be determined pursuant to a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Energy and Water and the Minister of Environment.

General Provisions

In the zones susceptible to the risks of floods and torrents specified in the General Master Plan for Water, the Minister of Energy and Water shall take the appropriate precautionary measures to limit the damage that may result therefrom, subject to the conditions and provisions of sustainable water management.

Agreements of Public Utility

In the zones where flood risks prevail as specified in the General Master Plan for Water, there shall be specified by a decree taken upon the proposal of the Minister of Energy and Water, the Minister of Public Works and Transport - Directorate General of Urban Planning, and the Ministers of Environment and Agriculture:

1- The sectors in which all constructions, works, arrangements or acts may be prohibited and, if necessary, the acts that may be permitted to be carried out without exposing the population to danger may be subjected to specific rules.

2- The sectors in which constructions, works, installations or activities that may increase the risks of floods or their harmful repercussions may be regulated and, if necessary, prohibited.

The works required by these provisions or rules shall be borne by the owners, operators or beneficiaries.

The restrictions relating to land use and resulting from the provisions of this Article shall constitute easements of public utility.

Principles

In the water-deficit zones specified in the General Master Plan for Water, the Ministry of Energy and Water must put into implementation the administrative procedures in this regard that ensure the regulation and rationalisation of water use, while maintaining a sufficient flow rate in the watercourses to ensure the balance of the ecosystem.

Meeting the domestic water needs and irrigation needs of the population shall be considered a priority in the water-deficit zones specified in the General Master Plan for Water. The Ministry of Energy and Water must put into implementation the decisions relating to usage controls that ensure the regulation and rationalisation of water use while preserving a sufficient water level to ensure the balance of the ecosystem, and non-conventional water may be used to bridge the deficit, provided that it complies with health standards.

Infractions at Sea

The penalties provided for in the preceding Article above of this Law shall apply to anyone who proceeds to throw and discharge or abandon waste, whatever its nature may be, into surface or underground waters or into sea waters within the limits of the territorial waters of the Lebanese State, or on the banks of rivers or on the seashore.

The provisions of this Article shall not apply to authorised substances that ships discharge into sea waters.

Aggravation of Penalties for Infractions

- Shall be punished by imprisonment from one day to ten days and by a fine from one million to fifteen million Lebanese pounds, or by either of these two penalties, anyone who abstracts water in breach by such act of the obligation to obtain the licence provided for pursuant to the provisions of Article 40 of this Law.

The same penalties shall apply to anyone who establishes, modifies, or operates an installation or carries out works or activities therein without obtaining a licence for the works.

- Shall be punished by a fine from one million to ten million Lebanese pounds anyone who abstracts water without complying with the provisions of Article forty of this Law.

- Shall be punished by a fine from one million to ten million Lebanese pounds anyone who erects an installation or equipment, carries out works, or exercises an activity without complying with the conditions specified in the licence document.

Misdemeanour Offences

Shall be punished by imprisonment from fifteen days to one month and by a fine from one million to twenty-five million Lebanese pounds, or by either of these two penalties, anyone who operates an installation or equipment, carries out works, or exercises an activity in violation of a measure involving a prohibition, suspension, or destruction ordered by the court in application of Article one hundred and three of this Law.

Fines

Shall be punished by a fine from five hundred thousand to two million Lebanese pounds anyone who violates the provisions contained in this Law other than those provided for in Articles ninety-six to the ninety-ninth.

Doubling of Fines

In the event of recidivism, the penalties relating to the offences provided for in Articles ninety-six to the hundredth of this Law shall be doubled.

Criminal Prosecution Shall Not Stay Administrative Prosecution

The application of criminal provisions shall not preclude the competent administrative authorities from exercising the power to take decisions or execute the measures provided for in Article Thirty-Seven of this Law.

Settlement on Fines

The Minister of Energy and Water, upon the proposal of the Chairmen of the Boards of Directors - Directors General of the Public Water Exploitation Establishments, may conclude settlements covering fines and compensations awarded pursuant to the provisions of Chapter Two of this Title, while preserving the rights of third parties.

However, the reduction may not exceed half of the fine or compensation awarded.

Follow-up of the Water Policy

The Ministry of Energy and Water and the National Water Authority shall undertake the follow-up of the water policy.

On Preventive Measures

The measures necessary to ensure sustainable water management shall be taken in consultation with the public authorities, the public water investment establishments, the syndical associations of owners, the social and economic stakeholders, and the environmental and consumer protection associations.

When the existence of a water deficit is verified, certain categories of water uses may be subjected to specific measures which may include the temporary suspension of acquired rights over water or the reduction of the corresponding water quantities.

The measures taken shall be proportionate to the crisis situation and shall determine:

1 - The conditions for meeting priority services.

2 - The uses subject to prohibition and those subject to rules, as well as the time limits and details for the application of such prohibition and such rules.

3 - The rules for distributing water to and among beneficiaries.

4 - And, if necessary, the conditions for transferring water between basins.

In exceptional cases, special measures may be imposed by decree.

Related Laws

There shall remain in force the provisions of Decision No. 320 dated 26 May 1926 and Decision No. 144 dated 10 June 1925, Articles 745 to 749 of the Penal Code relating to offences concerning the water regime, the Law promulgated by Decree No. 8735 dated 23 August 1974 relating to public hygiene, Law No. 64 dated 12 August 1988 relating to toxic, harmful and hazardous waste, Law No. 623 dated 23 April 1997 relating to increasing penalties for infringements on electrical, telephone and water networks, and Title Six of Law No. 444 dated 29 July 2002 relating to environmental protection.

Violations

Whoever intentionally or unintentionally dumps, discharges, throws or pours a substance or substances harmful to surface or underground water or to seawater within the territorial waters of the Lebanese State, directly or indirectly, the action or reaction of which leads, even temporarily, to:

1- A harmful effect on public health,

2- Serious alterations to the normal water supply regime,

3- Damage to flora and fauna,

4- The death of fish or damage to the conditions of their feeding, reproduction or nutritional value,

5- Restriction of the use of swimming areas.

Shall be punished by imprisonment from one day to ten days and by a fine from one million to fifteen million Lebanese pounds, or by one of these two penalties only:

Subject to the provisions of Article 99 of the Tax Procedures Law, the competent revenue unit shall, in the event that it objects to the valuation report before the Objections Committee, notify the enterprise or company of a copy of its objection, and the enterprise or company may submit its observations before the Objections Committee within a period not exceeding two months from the date of notification of the copy of the objection.

The six-month period granted to the Committee to decide on the objection shall commence from the date of its receipt of the observations of the enterprise or company on the objection of the revenue unit, or from the date of expiry of the two-month period provided for above.

If the Objections Committee reduces the valuation amount and the enterprise or company has paid the tax in accordance with the declared value, the enterprise or company may submit an application to refund the tax difference in accordance with the procedures relating to refund applications.

The losses that the enterprise or company may write off from the revaluation surplus resulting from the revaluation are the revenue losses shown and specified in the balance sheet and pertaining to taxpayers assessed on the basis of actual profit, within the limits of what may be carried forward in accordance with the provisions of Article 16 of the Income Tax Law.

If the revaluation surplus is greater than the written-off losses permitted to be carried forward, the balance shall be subject to tax at a rate of 10%, and revaluation surpluses resulting from the revaluation may not be used to write off losses of subsequent years.

No tax recognition shall be given to accounting losses that may appear at companies and enterprises compulsorily subject to assessment on the basis of lump-sum profit pursuant to the provisions of Article 44 of the Income Tax Law, and consequently the writing off of their accounting losses from the revaluation surplus resulting from the revaluation shall not be accepted, and if such companies and enterprises show the revaluation surplus in the value of the asset, the surplus shall then be subject to the tax of Article 45 of the Law. However, if this surplus remains separate in a special account on both the assets and liabilities sides of the balance sheet, it shall not be subject to that tax.

The revaluation surplus realised by capital companies as a result of the revaluation of their fixed assets shall be exempted from the tax on distributions when they use it to increase their capital, if they have previously paid the tax of Article 45 thereon, or if they are exempted from the tax of Title I pursuant to Articles 5 and 5 bis of the Income Tax Law.

Enterprises subject to the method of assessment on real profit, whether they are individual enterprises, partnerships or capital companies, shall benefit from the provisions of Item First of Article 45 of Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (the Income Tax Law), and capital companies assessed on the basis of lump-sum profit pursuant to the provisions of Article 44 of the same Legislative Decree shall also benefit from the provisions of this Item.

The phrase "what it holds" appearing in Item First of Article 45 referred to in Article One of this Decision means all tangible and intangible fixed assets and financial assets held by the enterprise as at the date of the valuation report, and the report must include the valuation of all elements of fixed assets whose value has depreciated or on which an appreciation has or has not occurred.

In the event that the elements of fixed assets are valued higher than their net book value after depreciation, if the assets are depreciable, and higher than their book value, if the assets are non-depreciable, the increase shall be considered a capital gain.

In the event that some of those elements are valued lower than their book value, this depreciation shall not be used to reduce the capital gains resulting from the valuation of other asset elements, nor may it be shown in the book value of the asset itself, and the enterprise or company may set aside a provision for it that is not tax-deductible pursuant to the provisions of Article 7 of the Income Tax Law.

An enterprise or company that has carried out a revaluation operation, in accordance with the procedures specified in the Code of Commerce for the valuation of contributions in kind in capital companies, must notify the valuation report to the competent financial department by virtue of a letter accompanied by the receipt of payment of the tax if due, prior to the expiry of the time limit for declaring the results of its operations for the year during which the valuation report was prepared.

The enterprises and companies referred to in Article One of this Decision may not revalue the elements of their fixed assets prior to the expiry of five full years from the commencement of their operations, or five full years from the date of a previous valuation report of which the tax administration was duly notified.

Collection of Information

The Ministry of Energy and Water shall undertake the collection and documentation of all information and data available with the public sector and private organisations operating in the field of water protection and relating to aquatic ecosystems and the management of public utilities entrusted with the management of drinking water services and supplies, the wastewater network and irrigation.

The Ministry of Energy and Water shall draw up an annual report on the status and sustainable management of water mentioned in Article eighty-five of this Law.

Informing Citizens

Information and education enable citizens and the concerned workers to exercise their rights and fulfil their duties to ensure the sustainable management of resources and aquatic ecosystems.

The competent authorities shall regularly publish information relating to the quality of drinking water provided to consumers, in the areas exposed to the risks mentioned in Title Seven of this Law, the competent authorities shall place at the disposal of citizens information relating to the prevention and management of these risks.

Training on the Law and the Sustainable Management of Water

The Ministry of Energy and Water shall undertake the task of informing and training public employees as well as the judicial authorities regarding the application of this Law and the sustainable management of water.

The water management authorities must ensure the publication of relevant information.

And training programmes for the sustainable management of water shall include levels proportionate to the levels of education in its various stages.

The Ministry of Environment, environmental protection associations and the private sector shall participate in educating citizens regarding the concept of the right to water and water culture.

Implementing Decrees

The Ministry of Energy and Water is responsible for the application of this Law, and for proposing the implementing decrees necessary therefor.

Repealed Texts

Article 5 of Decree No. 4537 dated 15 December 1972 and all previous provisions contrary thereto upon its entry into force are repealed (to be completed as an annex).

Publication

This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Concessionary companies, whatever their legal form, may conduct a revaluation of the fixed assets they hold in the manner set forth in this Decision, and a concessionary company whose book of specifications stipulates the handing over of the concession installations and equipment in good condition to the State without consideration upon the expiry of the term of the concession must show the share of the State in the positive revaluation differences in a special account outside equity.

The capital gain from disposal is determined by the difference between the disposal value of the asset, whether the disposal is voluntary or compulsory, and its net book value after depreciation, if the asset is depreciable, and its book value, if the asset is not depreciable, provided that all costs incurred by the taxpayer in maintaining and improving this asset are added to the book value in both cases, unless such expenses are general expenses.

All taxpayers (whether subject to assessment on the basis of actual profit, lump-sum profit or estimated profit) may use the capital profit or the revenue profit to write off capital losses, provided that the capital losses pertain to the same year during which that profit was realised.

Taxpayers assessed on the basis of actual profit may also use the capital gain resulting from disposal in order to write off the revenue losses that the law permits to be carried forward in accordance with the provisions of Article 16 of the Income Tax Law.

The capital gain realised by the taxpayer, whether subject to assessment on the basis of actual, lump-sum or estimated profit, as a result of a total or partial, voluntary or compulsory disposal of a fixed asset, shall be subject to income tax at the rate of 10% in respect of profits resulting from disposal transactions occurring prior to 27/10/2017 and at the rate of 15% in respect of profits resulting from disposal transactions occurring as from 27/10/2017.

Revenue profit and revenue loss mean the profit resulting or the loss resulting from the exercise of a commercial, industrial or professional activity, capital profit means the profit resulting from the disposal of a fixed asset or from its revaluation, capital loss means the loss resulting from the disposal of a fixed asset or from its revaluation, and capital loss means the loss resulting from the disposal of a fixed asset.

The phrase «still appearing and specified in the balance sheet appearing in Item Secondly in Article 45 of the Income Tax Law means the losses eligible to be carried forward in accordance with the provisions of Article 16 of the same Law.

"The categories of persons subject to the tax provided for in Item "c" of Article 13 of Law No. 64 dated 20/10/2017 shall be determined as follows:

- Natural and legal persons who do not carry on a work subject to income tax on profits, regardless of the place of residence or nationality of the transferor, unless the transfer transaction is in the form of a partition among heirs with respect to natural persons.

- Natural persons who are subject to income tax on profits and the transferred real property does not constitute an asset of the assets of practising the profession, unless the transfer transaction is in the form of a partition among heirs.

- Natural and legal persons who enjoy permanent, special or exceptional exemptions from income tax on profits, whatever their legal form may be, unless the transfer transaction is in the form of a partition among heirs with respect to natural persons.

- Public institutions, municipalities, unions of municipalities and all other persons of public law.

1 - Profits from the disposal of real properties, sections of real properties, or shares in real properties situated in Lebanon and belonging to the persons referred to in Article 18 of this Decision shall be subject to tax at a rate of 15%, resulting from disposal transactions occurring with effect from 27/10/2017.

2 - The profit from the disposal of the real property, a section of the real property, or shares in the real property shall be determined by the difference between the acquisition value and the disposal value; thereafter, for the purpose of determining the taxable base, a rate of 8% of the value of the disposal profit shall be deducted for each full year separating the date of acquisition of the real property and the date of disposal thereof, and no other amount may be deducted.

Accordingly, the disposal profit shall be exempted from the tax if the transferor has continued to hold title thereto for a period exceeding 12 full years, even if the disposal took place at the beginning of the thirteenth year.

3 - In order to calculate the disposal profit referred to in Clause 2, and consequently the taxable base, the following shall be adopted:

a - The acquisition date shall be determined as follows:

. With respect to real properties, sections of real properties, or shares in real properties devolved by inheritance: the date of death of the decedent shall be deemed to be the date of acquisition by the heir unless there is a judicial dispute regarding the determination of the heirs, in which case the date of issuance of the judgment determining the heirs shall be deemed to be the acquisition date.

. With respect to real properties, sections of real properties, or shares in real properties devolved by will: the date of issuance of the judgment proving the death and the execution of the will shall be deemed to be the date of acquisition by the legatee.

. With respect to real properties, sections of real properties, or shares in real properties devolved by way of donation: the date of signature of the donation contract between the donor and the donee drawn up before the notary public shall be deemed to be the date of acquisition by the donee if the contract is not registered in the Real Property Folio, and the date of registration in the Real Property Folio if the contract is registered therein.

. With respect to real properties, sections of real properties, or shares in real properties devolved by way of surveyed sale contracts: the date of registration thereof in the Real Property Folio if registered, and otherwise the date of the surveyed sale contract if not registered in the Real Property Folio, shall be deemed to be an acquisition date.

. In the event of a judicial dispute over ownership: the date of issuance of the judicial judgment establishing ownership shall be relied upon.

b - The acquisition value shall be determined as follows:

If the acquisition results from devolution (inheritance, will, donation...), the value appraised for the purposes of completing the estate file before the competent transfer duty unit shall be adopted as the acquisition value.

If the acquisition is by purchase, the acquisition value shall be determined in accordance with what is registered in the Real Property Folio or in accordance with the value stated for the purchase contract if the contract is not registered in the Real Property Folio.

If the building was completed by its owner on a date subsequent to his acquisition thereof, a distinction shall be made in this respect between the case where the owner does not hold supporting documents for the cost of constructions, whereby the taxable disposal profit is determined at a rate of 15% of the disposal value, and the case where the owner retains the supporting documents, in which case the cost of constructions is added to the cost of the real property in order to determine the acquisition value, and the taxable base is determined after deducting from the disposal profit (represented by the difference between the sale value and the acquisition value) a rate of 8% of its value for each full year separating the date of the last supporting document relating to the cost of constructions and the date of the disposal contract.

A natural person shall be exempted from the tax on gains from the disposal of two residences only throughout his lifetime, provided that the two residences are occupied by him with the approval of the competent financial units; however, the declaration regarding the disposal transaction must be submitted.

All natural and legal persons concerned with this tax, in accordance with what is stated in the eighteenth Article of this Decision, must adopt the special forms established by the Ministry of Finance for this tax, whether for declaring or for paying the tax, regardless of the forms adopted by the taxpayers among them pursuant to the submission of the annual declaration. They must also declare and pay the tax due within a period of two months from the date of disposal. For the purpose of declaring and paying the tax, the procedures provided for in Law No. 44 dated 11/11/2008 (Tax Procedures Law) shall be adopted.

In the event of delay in submitting the declaration, or in the event of submitting an incorrect declaration, or in the event of delay in paying the tax due, the fines provided for in the Tax Procedures Law shall be imposed.
Public administrations shall be exempted from this tax.

The tax administration may recharacterise the valuation operations and the disposal transactions referred to in this Decision, in accordance with the provisions of Article 1 of the Tax Procedures Law; however, in the case of sale by public auction, the value determined as a result of the auction shall be accepted as a final value for the disposal.
This Decision shall be published in the Official Gazette and on the website of the Ministry of Finance.

Insurance contracts for medical and hospitalisation operations must include a clause guaranteeing the renewal of the contract in accordance with its basic conditions, known as the Guaranteed Renewability Option or any other designation bearing the same meaning.

The guaranteed contract renewal coverage in accordance with its basic conditions provided for in Article One above shall apply within a period not exceeding one month from the effective date of this Decision, in respect of every renewal of a medical and hospitalisation insurance contract and every new contract issued after the aforementioned date.

Insurance companies may include an observation period for new contracts prior to confirming the basic conditions of the contract, provided that such period does not exceed one hundred and eighty (180) days following the effective date of the insurance.

1- Insurance companies may not exclude the insured patient from the scope of insurance by reason of his illness, or exercise discretion in suspending the effect of all or part of the benefits pertaining to medical and hospitalisation insurance contracts or limiting them for individuals belonging to the same class of insurance coverage.

2- Insurance companies may not impose variable premium pricing based on the health status of each person within the same class of insurance policyholders except upon the first issuance of the contract.

3- Upon the aggravation of his illness or his contracting an illness, no increase in the insurance premiums that he previously paid shall be imposed on the patient.

4- Insurance companies must classify the classes in accordance with considerations chosen from among the factors of age and/or gender and/or class of hospitalisation. The inclusion of additional factors shall be subject to the condition of obtaining the prior approval of the Insurance Control Commission.

Insurance companies must fully comply with the content of the directives issued by the Insurance Control Commission pursuant to Circular No. 2288/I.C.C. 2015 dated 16/09/2015, which require setting pricing policies or any amendments thereto in accordance with studied technical bases and submitting them to the Insurance Control Commission.

Insurance companies must comply with the following conditions when drawing up insurance contracts for medical and hospitalisation operations:

1- The ceiling of insurance for hospitalisation benefits shall be set at no less than seven hundred and twenty days.

2- The network of medical service providers must include, at a minimum, one of the following five centres:

- The American University of Beirut Medical Center.

- The Medical Center of the Saint Joseph University in Beirut - Hôtel-Dieu Hospital Saint George Hospital

- Clemenceau Medical Center

- The Lebanese American University Medical Center - Rizk Hospital.

An insured member under a group insurance contract shall be entitled to secure the renewal of his contract on an individual basis with the same institution in the event of his exit from the group insurance contract due to resignation from work, retirement, or other reasons, provided that he has completed a full year within the group insurance contract, and provided that the renewal takes place in accordance with the insurance contract adopted by the company for individuals.

In this case, the insurance institution must submit an offer to sign an individual insurance contract with the member within a period of one month from the date of his exit from the group insurance contract, provided that the member submits an application to benefit from this offer within a period of one month from the date of submission of the said offer.

The abovementioned institution shall, in this case, draw up an individual insurance contract for the member, and the insurance premium shall be calculated in accordance with the policy adopted by it, subject to the provisions of Article Three of this Decision.

All insurance institutions shall deposit the texts of the general conditions of the insurance contracts amended pursuant to this Decision with the Insurance Control Commission within a period not exceeding fifteen working days following the date of entry into force of this Decision.
This Decision shall be published in the Official Gazette and notified where needed.

Every natural person, whatever his place of residence may be, who actually owns or controls, in the final analysis (Ultimately), directly or indirectly, his activity practised by any other natural or legal person on Lebanese territory, shall be deemed a "Beneficial Owner" Beneficial Owner.

Cases in which ownership and/or control is held through a chain of ownership or through a chain of other means of indirect control shall be deemed cases of indirect ownership and/or control.

Every legal person, whatever its legal form may be, shall take the necessary measures to identify the "Beneficial Owner" in the activity that it practises. The identity of the beneficial owner shall be determined as follows:

1 - Every natural person who owns, directly or indirectly, the equivalent of or more than at least 20% of the capital of the legal person, or every actual beneficiary behind such person,

2- Where there is doubt as to whether the natural person or natural persons identified in accordance with item 1 are the beneficial owners, or in the absence of any natural person who owns, directly or indirectly, the equivalent of or more than at least 20% of the capital of the legal person, the identity of the natural persons who exercise control over the legal person through other means (such as owning the majority of voting rights or the rights to take fundamental decisions therein, including the appointment and dismissal of the members of the administrative body or the supervisory body) shall then be determined.

3 - Where no natural person is identified as specified in items 1 and 2 of this Article, the necessary measures shall then be taken to determine and disclose the identity of the persons who hold positions in senior management.

Taxpayers of the category of legal structures (legal, legal arrangements entity) shall take the necessary measures to ascertain the identity of the beneficial owner, in accordance with the following:

1- With respect to the activity of the (trustee) in accordance with Law No. 74/2016, it is required to identify each of:

- The protector (Protector)

- The beneficiary (Beneficiary), and where his identity is not determined or disclosed, the classes of persons in whose interest the legal structure (legal arrangement) was established.

- Every other natural person who exercises the right of effective control over the (trust)

through direct or indirect ownership or through other means.

2- With respect to other types of legal structures (legal arranggement), including structures similar to a (trust), it is required to identify the persons who hold positions similar to those specified in item (1) of this Article.

3 - With respect to a (legal entity), the necessary measures shall be taken to identify the persons who obtain debt instruments or shares, in accordance with what is stated above.

All taxpayers shall keep and update a special register of beneficial owners containing: the three-part name, nationality, date of birth, residential address and mailing address, identity card or passport number for Lebanese nationals, passport number for foreign nationals, place of tax residence, tax identification number, and percentage of distribution of the right.

They shall declare the information relating to "beneficial owners" within the declaration of commencement of business and the annual declarations in accordance with Article 38 of the Tax Procedures Law.

All taxpayers shall also retain the documents showing how the ownership of the legal person is structured and/or how it is controlled, and all information and documents relating to beneficial owners, for a period of ten years even after the person concerned ceases to have the capacity of beneficial owner, or even after they cease business.

The Lebanese Association of Certified Public Accountants, the Bar Associations of Beirut and Tripoli, and notaries public shall immediately provide the Ministry of Finance with any documents drawn up before them or of which they have knowledge by virtue of their profession that relate directly or indirectly to transactions or operations involving information relating to a beneficial owner, when requested to do so by the Tax Administration at the Ministry of Finance.
The Ministry of Finance shall establish the necessary forms to ensure that the Tax Administration obtains the information relating to beneficial owners.

The competent audit units in the Tax Administration shall verify, upon every desk or field audit operation, the compliance of taxpayers with the obligations incumbent upon them relating to beneficial owners, and shall impose on the violators among them the fines provided for in the Tax Procedures Law; they shall also take the necessary measures to assess the beneficial owners for the taxes due from them along with the legal fines provided for in the same Law, as well as to apply the provisions of Article 106 of the Tax Procedures Law.

The Tax Administration may coordinate with the Special Investigation Commission provided for in Law No. 44 dated 24/11/2015 relating to Fighting Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, to obtain from it information on beneficial owners upon the receipt of a request for non-banking information, and in this case, the information relating to the beneficial owner shall be requested from it in accordance with the provisions of Law 55/2016 and the same notification procedures shall be followed. It may also obtain information on the beneficial owner from the taxpayer pursuant to a targeted or comprehensive audit operation.

However, in the event that the request for information is urgent, or if notifying the taxpayer would affect the results of the investigation carried out by the foreign State within the meaning set out in Article 7 of Decree No. 1550/2017, then the taxpayer shall not be notified of the fact that information has been requested about them from the Special Investigation Commission, and the Tax Administration shall carry out a comprehensive audit operation of their tax file.
This Decision shall be published in the Official Gazette and on the website of the Ministry of Finance.

The principle of integrated management of solid household waste:

The principle of integrated management of solid household waste must be applied, which is based on the following stages: reduction of waste production, reuse, sorting at source and sorting in plants and recycling, composting and energy recovery, and final disposal of rejects.

Principles of reduction, reuse, and recycling:

(1) The principles of reduction of solid waste production, reuse, and recycling must be given primary priority over the other stages of integrated solid waste management in Lebanon, with the aim of reducing their negative impacts on the environment.

(2) Following the application of the principles referred to in Paragraph (1) of this Article, and following composting, the energy resources present in solid waste must be recovered insofar as this operation is feasible and economically acceptable and does not cause any negative impact on the environment. As for solid waste that cannot be reused, recovered, or recycled, it must be disposed of in an environmentally sound manner and in accordance with the provisions of this Law, the applicable national environmental standards, particularly those relating to air emissions or those relating to the surrounding environment, and the conditions of public health and safety.

The principle of sustainability:

1) Solid waste must be managed from the source of its production to the sites of its final disposal in an environmentally appropriate manner that does not lead to an increase in social and economic burdens and prevents:

a) Pollution of surface and groundwater, air, soil, flora, and fauna.

b) Harm to public health.

c) Causing nuisance due to the spread of odours and noise.

d) Negatively affecting nature reserves and natural sites.

e) Threatening nature and biodiversity.

2) Local administrations and/or the central authority may entrust the management of any stage of the integrated management of waste, in whole or in part, to the private sector, provided that the provisions of this Law are complied with.

The principle of proximity:

Solid waste must be sorted, treated, and then disposed of in licensed centres as close as possible to the source of its production and far from residential areas, with the aim of shortening the transport distance, the emission of pollutants, and the consumption of petroleum derivatives in transport, provided that such centres are technically licensed and economically viable.
