The Precautionary Principle:

Appropriate measures must be taken to avoid any negative impact the possibility of whose occurrence is shown by the latest technical and scientific information due to certain stages of solid waste management, prior to obtaining conclusive scientific proof of the risks that may occur.

The Principle of Prohibition of Indiscriminate Dumping, Burying, and Burning of Solid Waste:

It is prohibited to dump, discharge, bury, burn, or dispose of solid waste in the soil, hollow pits (cavities) and rock caves, surface watercourses, groundwater, the air, sewage networks, and other infrastructure or sites not licensed for this purpose.

The Polluter Pays Principle:

The polluter shall bear the costs of managing its solid waste, in addition to the cost of the measures that must be taken to address the problems resulting from the waste or that may result therefrom, provided that these costs are proportionate to the quantity and quality of the waste.

Decentralisation and the Principle of Substitution:

(1) Administrative decentralisation must be adopted in the implementation of integrated solid waste management through local administrations undertaking the stages of integrated solid waste management, in whole or in part, in accordance with environmental and economic feasibility, provided that this does not exempt the central authority from assuming its responsibilities when the local authorities are unable to do so.

(2) The central authority must ensure the efficiency of resource distribution through the implementation of central projects where the need arises.

The National Strategy for Integrated Solid Waste Management:

(1) The Ministry of Environment shall prepare a draft National Strategy for Integrated Solid Waste Management, through a participatory methodology covering the public and private sectors, including civil society; the Ministry shall submit this draft to the Council of Ministers for approval in due form.

(2) The Strategy referred to in Paragraph (1) of this Article must be approved within a period not exceeding six months from the date of issuance of this Law, provided that it is amended whenever necessary or after the lapse of ten years at the maximum.

(3) The draft Strategy referred to in Paragraph (1) of this Article must include the following items:

a) Mission, vision and values.

b) Assessment of the current situation to identify strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and challenges, as well as to identify the concerned parties.

c) Assessment of the general situation of solid waste management, including random dumps and centres established for the treatment of solid waste. Both operational and non-operational ones.

d) Assessment of future needs (services, infrastructure, ...) regarding solid waste management.

e) Short-term and long-term objectives and priorities for integrated solid waste management, including but not limited to the types of solid waste to be treated, the random dumps to be closed and rehabilitated, etc.

f) Means of managing the various types of solid waste, the best techniques to be adopted, and encouraging the principles of reduction, reuse and recycling therein, and recovering the largest possible proportion of waste towards a circular economy.

g) Sites for sorting, treating, preparing and finally disposing of solid waste.

h) Means of rehabilitating and closing random dumps.

i) The estimated timetable for implementation.

j) The estimated cost of construction and operation.

k) Sources of funding and manner of cost recovery.

l) A list of possible or necessary material or non-material incentives.

m) The activities to be carried out by Local Administrations (environmental guidance; collection and transport; treatment and final disposal; etc.), which they set within local programmes in accordance with what is specified in Article 11 of this Law.

n) Special requirements for producers, users, transporters and importers of materials that generate non-household waste: periodic declaration of the type and quantities of waste; reduction of solid waste generation at each of the stages of manufacturing, design, use and final disposal; treatment; protection of the environment from the potential negative impacts of such waste.

o) How to facilitate the participation of the private sector in all stages of integrated solid waste management.

p) How to encourage local initiatives and civil society participation aimed at reducing the quantity of solid waste, reusing it and sorting it at source.

q) Marketing materials recovered from waste through treatment (reuse, recycling, composting, biodegradation and production of energy resources, ...) with the aim of reducing the quantity of raw materials consumed.

r) Means of strengthening capacities related to integrated solid waste management (training courses and others).

s) Supervision, monitoring and evaluation.

(4) The draft Strategy referred to in Paragraph (1) of this Article shall be accompanied by a Strategic Environmental Assessment study in due form.

Local Solid Waste Management Programmes:

(1) Every local administration shall prepare a draft local solid waste management programme in accordance with what is specified in Paragraph (3) of this Article and in accordance with the content of the Strategy approved by the Council of Ministers, and submit it to the Ministry of Environment, with a copy to the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities, for approval in due form, within a maximum time limit of three months from the date of approval of the Strategy.

(2) The Ministry of Environment must approve the programmes referred to in Paragraph (1) of this Article within a period not exceeding three months from the date of issuance of this Law, provided that they are amended whenever necessary or after the lapse of ten years at the most.

(3) The items that must be included in the programmes referred to in Paragraph (1) of this Article shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Environment, by way of example and not limitation:

(a) Information on the local administration and the characteristics of its solid waste.

(b) Means of collection and transport - including draft books of specifications.

(c) Projects for sorting, treatment and final disposal by environmentally and economically feasible methods.

(d) Supervision, monitoring and evaluation of the operations of collection, transport and marketing of sorted and treated materials and others.

(e) Available human, technical and financial resources; and the need for technical or financial assistance.

(f) Cooperation with civil society to provide guidance on reducing the generation of solid waste, and on sorting, treating and finally disposing of it.

(g) Cooperation with the private sector to implement the local programme.

(4) Local administrations facing similar problems in solid waste management may join their efforts for the purpose of drawing up the draft programmes referred to in Paragraph (1) of this Article, and ensuring their proper implementation.

Coordination Committee:

(1) A committee shall be formed under the chairmanship of the Minister of Environment and with the membership of the concerned public administrations, economic and academic bodies, and associations concerned with environmental affairs, the purpose of which is to coordinate the affairs of the solid waste sector.

(2) The composition of this committee and the manner of its operation shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Environment.

Establishment of the National Solid Waste Management Authority:

(1) There shall be established pursuant to this Law an authority named the "National Solid Waste Management Authority", which shall enjoy financial and administrative autonomy and be linked to the Minister of Environment; it shall also be subject to its internal regulations and the provisions of this Law, and it shall not be subject to the provisions of the General Regulations for Public Institutions ratified by Decree 4517/1972

(2) The Board of Directors of the Authority shall be appointed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Environment.

(3) The bylaws of the Authority, its operating procedures, its recruitment procedures, and the scale of ranks and salaries shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Environment, and it shall be vested with the following powers:

- Preparing the technical and administrative specifications for central projects relating to the implementation of the National Strategy for Integrated Solid Waste Management, and environmental impact assessment studies.

- Supervising the implementation of central projects.

- Providing advice to the Minister of Environment regarding joint projects and those proposed by local administrations for solid waste management in terms of their environmental and economic feasibility, and regarding waste treatment technologies in general.

(4) Tenders for central projects relating to the implementation of the National Strategy shall be conducted through the Tenders Administration in accordance with legal procedures.

Implementation of Joint and Decentralised Projects:

(1) The implementation of joint projects shall be carried out in accordance with the principles provided for in Law No. 48 dated 7/9/2017 (Regulating Public-Private Partnership), provided that they are subject to environmental impact assessment studies in due form.

(2) With regard to projects implemented by local administrations, their implementation shall be carried out in accordance with the laws of these administrations.

Self-Monitoring:

(1) Producers, users, transporters, and importers of materials that generate non-household solid waste, service providers, and operators shall be obliged to carry out daily self-monitoring, keep records, and submit monthly and annual reports to the Ministry of Environment directly or through the contracted official administration, where applicable.

(2) The items of the self-monitoring reports shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Environment.

Supervision:

(1) The National Solid Waste Management Authority shall supervise the central projects.

(2) With regard to joint projects that are awarded in accordance with the provisions of Law No. 48 dated 7/9/2017, the supervision and monitoring procedures provided for in the aforementioned Law shall apply.

(3) Local administrations shall supervise the service providers and operators with whom they have contracted.

Compliance monitoring:

(1) The Ministry of Environment shall periodically monitor the producers, users, transporters and importers of materials that generate non-household solid waste, as well as service providers and operators, by auditing self-monitoring reports and conducting field inspections at least every 3 months.

(2) The mechanism for field inspections and their respective reports shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Environment.

Preparation of an information system and a database:

(1) The Ministry of Environment shall, within a period of 3 months from the date of issuance of this Law, establish a national information system and database for managing information related to solid waste and the methods of its management in cooperation with the local administrations.

(2) The provisions of this system shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Environment.

Management of the information system and the database:

(1) The Ministry of Environment shall undertake the management of the information system database by publishing, analysing and updating information in an accurate and transparent manner.

(2) Obtaining the information provided by the information system and the database shall be free of charge and available; and it must be accessed rapidly.

Collection and transport:

Service providers (a municipality, a union of municipalities, decentralised organisations, or a contracted private sector ... etc.) must bear the responsibility of collecting solid waste and transporting it from collection points to the designated centres in a manner that does not cause harm to the environment, in accordance with the standards and conditions determined by the Ministry of Environment pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Environment.

Sorting:

Non-hazardous solid waste must be sorted at the source and at sorting centres for the purpose of separating biodegradable solid waste and the remaining recyclable and reusable materials, provided that technologies are available that make this possible without causing pollution to the environment, in conformity with the National Strategy for Integrated Solid Waste Management and the approved local programme, and with the environmental standards and conditions determined by the Ministry of Environment pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Environment.

Preparation:

Prior to the final disposal of solid waste, it shall be prepared with the aim of mitigating its negative impacts on the environment in a manner compatible with the environmental standards and conditions for the preparation of solid waste determined by the Ministry of Environment pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Environment.

Final Disposal:

(1) Solid waste that cannot be treated shall be disposed of through special operations compatible with the National Strategy for Integrated Waste Management, and with the environmental standards and conditions determined by the Ministry of Environment pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Environment.

(2) Sanitary Landfilling: According to the type of waste to be disposed of, sanitary landfills are classified as follows:

* Sanitary landfills specific to hazardous solid waste.

* Sanitary landfills for inert waste.

* Sanitary landfills for non-hazardous solid waste.

a) The technical specifications for each type of the landfills mentioned above shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Environment.

b) It is prohibited to dispose of waste in landfills that are not compatible with its type and that has not been subjected to treatment and preparation. Waste shall be landfilled in a manner compatible with the environmental standards and conditions determined by the Ministry of Environment, including the conditions for liner layers, pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Environment.

c) Sanitary landfills for inert waste shall be used to landfill this type of solid waste only. However, and notwithstanding paragraph (b) of this Article, in the event that sanitary landfills for inert waste are not available, inert waste may be disposed of in sanitary landfills designated for non-hazardous solid waste.

d) Sanitary landfills designated for non-hazardous solid waste may be used to landfill the following solid waste:

* Non-hazardous solid waste from whatever source that is compatible with the type of solid waste permitted to be landfilled in non-hazardous solid waste landfills.

* Inert waste.

Updating the National List of Hazardous Solid Waste:

The National List relating to hazardous and industrial solid waste, determined pursuant to Article Two of Law No. 88/64, shall be updated by virtue of a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Environment, every three years at most or whenever the need arises, with the aim of ensuring sustainability and effectiveness and keeping pace with scientific development in the field of hazardous solid waste management.

Treatment:

The recoverable portion of solid waste, consisting of organic waste, waste amenable to reuse or recycling, must be treated with the aim of reuse, recycling, composting, or recovery of energy resources, prior to its disposal, except where such treatment causes greater pollution to the environment. The treatment of solid waste must take into account, by way of example and not limitation, the following points:

- Pollutants resulting from materials that negatively affect air, water, and soil.

- The use of natural resources.

- Energy that can be reused or renewed.

- The content of hazardous substances in solid waste after its treatment.

a) Reuse and recycling:

Materials amenable to this type of operations must be reused or recycled with the aim of reducing the quantity of solid waste that reaches the treatment stage, without causing environmental damage and without using technologies and operations that may pose a hazard to the environment. This must be carried out in accordance with the standards and conditions determined by the Ministry of Environment pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Environment.

b) Composting, biological decomposition, and fuel production:

The biodegradable organic portion of solid waste must be composted or converted as set out below:

- Proper sorting of biodegradable solid waste from other solid waste prior to its treatment.

- The use of a suitable technology for composting and biological decomposition approved by the Ministry of Environment.

- Proper use of composted or biologically converted materials in accordance with their type.

Provided that the detailed conditions shall be determined pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Environment.

c) Conversion of waste to energy through thermal decomposition:

Solid waste may be used as a source for energy production, provided that this operation and the by-products resulting therefrom do not affect the safety of the environment, and that they comply with the standards and conditions determined pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Environment.

d) Possibility of using other modern technologies for solid waste management:

In view of the development of sciences and technologies and based on research and studies, modern technologies other than those referred to in this Law may be used (for example, incineration of solid waste in high-thermal-capacity furnaces...) provided that they do not cause damage to the environment and a hazard thereto, following the approval of the Ministry of Environment.

Import, export and transport of hazardous waste:

No import or export of hazardous solid waste may take place except after the approval of the Ministry of Environment and in accordance with the provisions of Law No. 387 issued on 4 December 1994, which authorised the Government to accede to the Basel Convention on the Control of Transboundary Movements of Hazardous Solid Wastes and Their Disposal.

General rules in the management of hazardous solid waste:

(1) Mixing different categories of hazardous solid waste with other categories of hazardous solid waste as well as with other categories of non-hazardous solid waste is prohibited. However, during the treatment or disposal of solid waste in a licensed manner, the Ministry of Environment may exceptionally allow, upon the request of the entity or person licensed to manage hazardous solid waste, the mixing of a certain percentage of some hazardous solid waste with other non-hazardous solid waste, provided that such mixing does not cause any hazard to the environment and improves the safety of treatment and preparation operations.

(2) The rules for managing hazardous waste shall be determined by a decree or decrees enacted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Environment.

(3) Service providers, operators, and producers, users, importers and transporters of hazardous solid waste must manage such waste in a manner that does not cause any harm to the environment and complies with the environmental standards and conditions specified pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Environment.

Sources of financing for integrated solid waste management:

The implementation of the National Strategy for Integrated Solid Waste Management, and the local programmes, may be financed from the following sources:

1 - The general budget, through appropriations allocated to the National Solid Waste Management Authority.

2 - The budgets of local administrations,

3 - Loans and grants,

4 - The National Environment Fund (upon commencement of its operation).

5 - Private sector investments in the solid waste management process, whereby, notwithstanding any other text, legal or natural persons from the private sector and municipalities and unions of municipalities, who are owners of licensed plants for the treatment of solid waste and/or final disposal facilities therefor, are permitted to connect the electrical energy produced from their plants to the grid at their own expense, provided that they obtain the necessary licence in the Ministry of Energy and Water, and provided that Electricité du Liban undertakes to purchase the quantities of energy produced at a price fifteen per cent lower than the average electricity sale tariff adopted by it, the licence granted by the Ministry of Energy and Water shall be cancelled, withdrawn or suspended in the event that the licensee violates the conditions on the basis of which the licence was granted, and without any compensation accruing to the violator. The aforementioned price may be amended pursuant to a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Energy and Water and of Environment.

Non-material incentives:

(1) The ministries and administrations concerned with solid waste management shall encourage projects related to integrated solid waste management, in particular the process of recycling, reuse and recovery of energy resources in a sound and effective manner, by providing non-material incentives such as simplifying licensing procedures for service providers and operators, and exporting materials resulting from the treatment of solid waste, etc.

(2) The methods of encouraging solid waste management shall be determined pursuant to a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Environment.

General responsibilities:

(1) The responsibility for collecting and transporting household waste shall lie with the local administration, which may engage the private sector under its supervision, in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

(2) The responsibility for treating, preparing and finally disposing of waste shall lie with the local administrations and the National Solid Waste Management Authority, which shall engage the private sector under their supervision, in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

(3) The responsibility for managing non-household waste shall lie with its producers, users, importers and distributors under the supervision and guidance of the Ministry of Environment in accordance with what is specified in the National Strategy for Integrated Solid Waste Management, and they must bear the cost of managing the solid waste resulting from their operations and activities in addition to the costs resulting from managing the solid waste resulting from their products. They must also provide preventive actions and reduce the production of solid waste during the processes of designing, producing, consuming and disposing of these products.

(4) The Ministry of Environment, in coordination with the local administrations, shall have the competence to take all necessary measures and steps to remove the hazards affecting the safety of the environment and resulting from solid waste or the process of managing it.

Removal of solid waste unlawfully present on private and public property:

(1) Where such waste is dumped after the date of issuance of this Law:

(a) The responsibility for removing solid waste present on private property and which may cause harm to the environment shall lie with the owner or operator of such property. Should he refrain from doing so, the local administration shall be obliged to transport it at the expense of the owner or operator.

(b) Where solid waste is dumped on private property without the knowledge or permission of the owner or operator, he shall be obliged to notify the local administration, which must take the appropriate measures and charge the expense of such measures to the person who caused them.

(c) The responsibility for removing solid waste present on public property shall lie with the local administration, which must take the appropriate measures and charge the expense of such measures to the person who caused them.

(2) Where such waste was present prior to the date of issuance of this Law:

The responsibility for removing solid waste present on private or public property shall lie with the Ministry of Environment in cooperation with the local administration.

Obligation to Declare a Real Estate Encumbrance for Environmental Requirements:

Owners of properties that have been used as facilities for sorting, treating, preparing, or finally disposing of waste must take the following measures:

- Notifying the Land Registry Secretariat to record this in the field designated for the description of the property in the real estate folio.

- In the event of the sale of the property, declaring the previous use of the property, under penalty of annulment of the contract.

- In the event of the sale of the property and the obligation to carry out works related to the post-closure of the waste management facility, the buyer must be informed and must sign an agreement whereby he assumes full liability for executing the required works.

Rules and Provisions of Civil Liability:

(1) Service providers, operators, and producers, users, importers, and distributors of waste shall bear civil liability for any damage or risk to the environment or to others resulting from the solid waste under their custody, from the activities they carry out, and from the by-products generated therefrom.

(2) The natural or legal persons mentioned in Paragraph (1) above of this Article must bear the responsibility of remediating and removing the various damages and risks to the environment or to third parties resulting from their waste, from their management of solid waste, and from the by-products generated therefrom by taking the necessary and appropriate measures.

Recording of Misdemeanours:

(1) Violations of the provisions of this Law shall be recorded by means of infringement reports drawn up by members of the Judicial Police and the Environmental Police, which shall be referred to the competent courts, with copies thereof sent to the Ministry of Environment.

(2) The provisions of the Fifty-Fourth Article (54) of Chapter Two of Title Six of Environmental Protection Law No. 444/2002 shall also apply.

Deterrent administrative penalties:

In accordance with Article 57 of the Environmental Protection Law (444/2002), and upon the proposal of the Ministry of Environment or other concerned administrations, after serving a written warning upon the offender, and his failure to remove the violation, administrative penalties may be imposed for concerned administrations, after serving a written warning upon the offender, and his failure to remove the violation, deterrent administrative penalties may be imposed upon him, which are:

- Imposing conditions aimed at preserving rights and conserving the environment.

- Monitoring all environmental management means and centres at any time whatsoever to verify the extent of compliance of solid waste management operations with the provisions of this Law, the regulations in force, and the conditions of the licence.

- Imposing remediation measures such as afforestation and rehabilitation at the expense of the polluter.

- Setting conditions before permitting the continuation of certain activities, in addition to continuous preventive measures, self-monitoring and environmental auditing, and suspending the licence of certain activities until the implementation of the required conditions.

- Prohibiting certain activities that cause severe environmental damage, revoking the licence, and closing the establishment.

- Closing the establishment in the event of non-observance of the provisions of this Law and the impossibility of applying the conditions that would achieve compliance with this Law.

- Imposing astreintes and fines.

Other provisions relating to penalties:

The penalties set forth in this Law shall not replace those set forth in other laws, including Law No. 444/2002 (Articles 58 to 63), Law No. 64/88 (Articles 9 to 13) or the Penal Code.
All legal texts that conflict with this Law or are inconsistent with its provisions are hereby repealed.
This Law shall be published and shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Penal Sanctions:

1- Waste producers and users, importers and distributors of materials that generate waste, service providers, and operators shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year and/or by payment of a fine ranging between 14 and 70 times the minimum wage in the event of:

a. Dumping non-hazardous solid waste of less than 500 kg in water, soil, sewage networks, or other infrastructure and sensitive natural sites.

b. When non-hazardous solid waste is not collected, transported, or sorted in accordance with the provisions of this Law, and with the conditions and standards specified by the Ministry of Environment.

c. When they collect, transport, or sort non-hazardous solid waste without the due approval of the Ministry of Environment.

d. When they do not notify the Ministry of Environment of the negative impacts resulting from the operations of producing, collecting, transporting, or sorting non-hazardous solid waste.

2- Waste producers, users, importers, and distributors, service providers, and operators shall be punished by imprisonment from 6 months to 3 years and/or by payment of a fine ranging between 70 and 700 times the minimum wage in the event of:

a. Dumping the equivalent of or more than 500 kg of non-hazardous solid waste in water, soil, sewage networks, or other infrastructure and natural sites.

b. Dumping solid waste of less than 10 kg in water, soil, sewage networks, or other infrastructure and natural sites.

c. When non-hazardous solid waste is not treated, prepared, or disposed of in accordance with the provisions of this Law, and with the conditions and standards specified by the Ministry of Environment, including burning, dumping, and indiscriminate.

d. When the periodic reports relating to non-hazardous solid waste are not submitted to the Ministry of Environment as specified in this Law.

e . When self-monitoring works and the keeping of daily records on non-hazardous solid waste are not carried out.

f. When they treat, prepare, or dispose of non-hazardous solid waste without the due approval of the Ministry of Environment.

g. When they do not notify the Ministry of Environment of the negative environmental impacts resulting from the operation of treating, preparing, or disposing of non-hazardous solid waste.

3- Waste producers, users, importers, and distributors, service providers, and operators shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to 10 years and/or by payment of a fine ranging between 700 and 7000 times the minimum wage in the event of:

a. Dumping the equivalent of or more than 10 kg of hazardous solid waste in water, soil, sewage networks, or other infrastructure and natural sites.

b. When hazardous solid waste is not collected, transported, sorted, treated, prepared, or disposed of in accordance with the provisions of this Law, and with the conditions and standards specified by the Ministry of Environment.

c. When they collect, transport, sort, treat, prepare, or dispose of hazardous solid waste without the due approval of the Ministry of Environment, including burning and indiscriminate dumping.

d. When the periodic reports relating to hazardous solid waste are not submitted to the Ministry of Environment as specified in this Law.

e. When self-monitoring works and the keeping of daily records pertaining to hazardous solid waste are not carried out.

f. When hazardous solid waste is mixed with other hazardous and/or non-hazardous waste for the purpose of diluting its hazardous properties without the approval of the Ministry of Environment.

g. When they do not notify the Ministry of Environment of the negative impacts resulting from the operation of producing, collecting, transporting, sorting, treating, preparing, or disposing of hazardous solid waste.

In all that is provided for above, the penalty of imprisonment and a doubled fine shall be imposed in the event of repetition of the offence.

4 . In the event that the offence set out in paragraphs (1), (2), (3) above of this Article is committed by the local administration or any public administration, the penalty provided for in paragraphs (1), (2), (3) above of this Article shall apply to the natural person responsible for this offence, and to the mayor, his deputy, and the members of the municipal council, notwithstanding any other text.

Information technology is at the service of every person, provided that it does not infringe upon their individual identity, their rights, their private life, or individual or public freedoms.
The provisions stipulated in the laws in force shall apply to everything not mentioned and not provided for in this Law, and to everything that does not conflict with its provisions.

Electronic writing and signature produce the same legal effects as those enjoyed by writing and signature on a paper medium or any other type of medium, provided that it is possible to identify the person from whom they emanate, and that they are drawn up and preserved in a manner that guarantees their integrity.

Every electronic writing in which the conditions mentioned above are not met may be considered prima facie written evidence.

The preservation of electronic data, stipulated in the first paragraph of Article 4 above, means recording them in full on a storage medium on a condition that guarantees its integrity and ensures permanent access to their content and the extraction of copies thereof.

The Code of Civil Procedure and other laws in force shall apply to electronic instruments in a manner consistent with their electronic nature and with the special provisions contained in this Law.

Commercial books shall be subject to the special provisions governing them in the Code of Land Commerce.

An electronic instrument is admissible as evidence and shall have the same rank and probative force as that enjoyed by a written instrument recorded on paper, provided that it is possible to identify the person from whom it emanates and that it is drawn up and preserved in a manner that guarantees its integrity.

Electronic authentic instruments shall not produce any legal effects except after their approval and regulation by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice.

This decree shall regulate the special procedures and guarantees relating to these instruments and their scope.

Related text: Application of the provisions of Article 8 (Electronic Authentic Instruments) of Law No. 81 dated 10/10/2018 "Electronic Transactions and Personal Data Law"

An electronic signature is issued through the use of a secure device that identifies the signatory and constitutes a guarantee of the link between the signature and the legal act to which it is attached.

If the electronic signature is coupled with protection procedures certified by an accredited certification service provider in accordance with the provisions of Chapter Four, it shall be deemed to be issued in accordance with the conditions of the first paragraph of this Article until proven otherwise.

For the purpose of applying the provisions of this Law, each of the terms mentioned below shall have the meaning indicated next to each of them:

- Writing ((L'ecrit /Writing): is the recording or registration of letters, numbers, figures, symbols or data, provided that they are legible and have an intelligible meaning, whatever the medium used (paper or electronic) and the methods of transmitting the information.

- Electronic Instrument: is the private or authentic instrument, as defined by the Code of Civil Procedure, which is issued in electronic form, subject to the provisions of Article 8 of this Law.

- Signature: the signature necessary for the completion of a legal act that identifies its holder and proves his consent to the legal act bearing the signature.

- Certification Service Provider (Prestataire de service de certification/Certification Service provider): is a public or private law person who issues certification certificates after putting into application the protection measures that secure the functions specified in Article 15 of this Law or one of them.

- Electronic Commerce: (Le Commerce Electronique/Electronic Commerce): is the activity whereby a person performs or offers remotely by electronic means the supply of goods or the provision of services to third parties.

- Bank Card: (Carte Bancaire/Bank Card) is an instrument issued by a bank or by an institution licensed to issue it by the Bank of Lebanon, which allows its holder to withdraw cash funds or perform an electronic payment transaction of cash funds or any other banking or financial services.

- Electronic and Digital Money: (Monnaie Electronique et nume(rique/Digital or Electronic Money) are units called electronic money units that can be stored on an electronic medium.

- Network Service Provider (Fournisseur d'acce s/Network Service provider): is anyone who enables the user to access an electronic communications network and provides it directly with information transmission services. The provision of these services may include transient and temporary storage of the transmitted information, provided that it does not lead to any modification in the stored data, and provided that this storage is used for the proper execution of the service and does not exceed the time necessary to complete it.

- Data Host: (Hebergeur de donnees/Data host) is anyone who stores information of whatever nature, on behalf of third parties, for consideration or without consideration, and places it at the disposal of the public through direct communication services.

- Traffic Data (Donnees de trafic/ Traffic data): is any information relating to a communication operation by means of a computer system. - connected to an information network: this information is issued by a computer system connected to the network, and indicates the source of the communication, its recipient, the route of the information, the time, the date, the volume, the duration, or similar information.

- Domain Name (Nom de domaine/Domain Name): is the equivalent in alphabetical or numerical symbols or otherwise of the digital address assigned to a website on the Internet.

- Personal Data (Donnees a caractere personnel/Personal Data): is all types of information relating to a natural person that enables his identification, directly or indirectly, including by comparing information from multiple sources or cross-referencing between them.

- Processing of Personal Data (Traitement des Donnees a caractere personnel/ Processing of Personal Data): is any operation or set of operations performed on such data whatever the means used, in particular operations of collection, recording, organisation, storage, adaptation, modification, extraction, reading, use, transmission, copying, publication, erasure, destruction, and every other form of placing the information at disposal.

- Data Subject: (also known as the person concerned by the personal data) is the natural person to whom such data relates.

- Personal Data Controller: is the natural or legal person who determines the purposes and methods of the processing.

- Personal Data Recipient: is the person authorised to receive the personal data, other than the person concerned by the processing, the controller, or the person who carries it out. Public authorities legally authorised within their duties to request personal data shall not be deemed recipients.

The rule of multiplicity of originals provided for in Article 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure shall be deemed satisfied where the private instrument is drawn up in accordance with the conditions of reliability provided for in this Law, and where the mechanism used enables each party to obtain a copy of the instrument or to have access thereto.

Where the law does not lay down other rules and in the absence of an agreement concluded by the parties in this regard, the judge shall adjudicate disputes relating to written proof in the event of a plurality of instruments, and shall determine by all means the most credible instrument regardless of its medium, with due regard to the probative force pertaining to an authentic instrument.

Where the denial, refusal of acknowledgment, or plea of forgery does not relate to an electronic instrument or an electronic signature, the judge shall, when conducting the verification provided for in the Code of Civil Procedure, ascertain the fulfilment of the conditions of reliability necessary for the validity of the electronic instrument or signature, namely by ascertaining that the instrument was drawn up and preserved under conditions that guarantee its integrity and that the person from whom the instrument emanates can be identified by means of a reliable mechanism for signatures in accordance with the provisions of Articles 7 and 9 of this Law.

The judge may require the parties to produce all the electronic traces in their possession or commission an expert to search for them, and may also seek the assistance of technical expertise.

In all cases, the general rules relating to the denial of signatures and the plea of forgery shall apply to electronic instruments and electronic signatures, in a manner consistent with the nature of such instruments and signatures.
An electronic instrument that does not fulfil all the conditions specified in Articles 7, 9 and 10 of this Law may be deemed to constitute a commencement of proof in writing.
Electronic writing is free, and no one shall be compelled to resort to means of protection unless the law provides otherwise.

The means of protection applied to electronic writings and signatures aim to enhance their reliability.

The function of the means of protection shall be to verify the identity of the author of the instrument and/or to confer auethentic date thereon and/or to guarantee the integrity of its terms and ensure its preservation.

These functions, or each of them, shall be provided by one or more certification service providers, who shall, upon completion thereof, deliver a certificate of authentication to the holder of capacity.

These functions, or each of them, may be provided by means of other technologies.

Subject to the provisions of Article 133 of this Law, the provision of authentication services shall not be subject to prior authorisation.

However, upon an application by an authentication service provider meeting the conditions, an accreditation certificate may be obtained, issued by the Lebanese Council for Accreditation (COLIBAC) established pursuant to Law No. 572/2004 (hereinafter referred to in this Law as the Council) in accordance with the provisions of Chapter Four of this Title, by way of exception to the provisions set out in Articles 4 and 11 of Law No. 572/2004.

When an electronic signature is created and authenticated in accordance with procedures provided by an accredited authentication service provider, it shall be deemed to fulfil the conditions stipulated in Article 9 of this Law, and shall enjoy a presumption of reliability until the contrary is proven.

Where an electronic signature is created or an electronic writing is drawn up, dated and preserved in accordance with authentication procedures provided by an unaccredited authentication service provider, it shall lie with the judge to assess its probative force, unless the parties agree otherwise.

An authentication service provider, whether accredited or unaccredited, shall be subject to the obligation of professional secrecy in respect of data subject to authentication, with the exception of those contained in the certificate which it issues.

This professional secrecy shall be lifted, where necessary, by a decision issued by the competent judicial authority in the course of disputes or prosecutions pending before it.

The Council shall have competence to accredit authentication service providers who issue certificates granting electronic writings and signatures the presumption of fulfilment of the conditions stipulated in Articles 7 and 9 of this Law.

The decisions of the Council relating to the application of this Law shall be subject to appeal before the State Council.

The Council shall draw up a book of specifications defining the conditions and obligations imposed in the protection procedures offered by the authentication service provider applying for accreditation, and defining the elements necessary to properly complete the evaluation process, in particular the elements of an administrative, technical and financial nature that must be attached to the application for accreditation.

For the purpose of defining the specifications of the technical book of specifications, the Council shall take into consideration international standards and norms in the field of electronic signatures and other products, services or programmes (software) related to electronic signatures and writings.

The Council shall review the book of specifications at least annually and whenever the need arises, in the light of technical development.

For the purpose of issuing or renewing an accreditation certificate, the Council shall take into consideration the following criteria:

1 - The infrastructure and technical measures for the protection of electronic writing, as well as the organisational procedures and human resources put into application by the authentication service provider, which must conform to international standards.

2 - The regularity and scope of audit operations to verify the conformity of the authentication service provider's services with the declarations and policies issued thereby.

3 - The availability of financial guarantees for the exercise of the service provider's activity.

4 - The existence of an insurance contract covering the financial consequences of its civil liability.

5 - The guarantees of neutrality, independence, and integrity of the authentication service provider.

6 - The accreditation or evaluation previously conducted of the quality of the protection means, which must observe international standards, by a competent authority if the authentication service provider is resident abroad.

The criteria set out above shall be taken into consideration to assess the reliability of the protection means provided by an unaccredited authentication service provider.

The Council shall audit the accreditation application at the expense of the authentication service provider applying for accreditation. To that end, it may request additional information from the service provider, including requesting the conduct of an investigation at its offices and with its employees.

The audit shall aim to verify that the conditions of accreditation, in particular the protection means for which the service provider requests accreditation, conform to the specifications of the book of specifications.

Upon conclusion of the audit procedure, the Council shall draw up a report, which shall be notified to the authentication service provider in order to enable it to submit its observations.

In light of the evaluation report and the observations of the authentication service provider, if any, the Council shall issue, within a period of two months, a reasoned decision as to whether or not the required conditions are met by the authentication service provider.

If the period specified in the first paragraph expires without the Council taking any decision, the expiry of the period shall be deemed an implicit decision of refusal.

If the Council decides that the authentication service provider satisfies the conditions, it shall issue an accreditation certificate indicating the protection means covered by the accreditation, and shall determine the period of its validity, provided that it does not exceed three years.

The authentication service provider shall be subject, throughout the period of accreditation, to audit by the Council, which may, as a result thereof, suspend the accreditation certificate or withdraw it immediately upon breach of the conditions for issuing the accreditation certificate, the book of specifications, or the elements of a technical, administrative and financial nature prescribed by law.

A decision to suspend the operation of the accreditation certificate or to withdraw it may only be taken after enabling the representative of the authentication service provider to submit his observations within a time limit determined by a decision issued by the Council.

The accredited authentication service provider must notify the Council in writing, by means of a letter registered therewith, of every change affecting the elements submitted in the accreditation application file, under penalty of applying the provisions of Article 25 of this Law.

The accredited authentication service provider must deliver a copy of the certificate issued by the Council to anyone who requests it.

The Council shall place at the disposal of the public a list of accredited authentication service providers, which shall be continuously updated, in particular on the Council's website.
An authentication service provider residing outside Lebanese territory may request the Council to grant him an accreditation certificate if he meets the required conditions.

The accredited authentication service provider shall be deemed liable for the reliability of the means of protection covered by the accreditation certificate, notwithstanding any agreement to the contrary, and shall be bound to compensate for the damages that may befall his clients as a result of the poor performance of his contractual obligations.

The practice of electronic commerce shall be free within the limits of the prohibitions and restrictions provided for by law.

Electronic commerce contracts shall be subject, in all matters not provided for in this Law, to the laws in force, in particular the Code of Commerce, the Code of Obligations and Contracts, the Code of Civil Procedure and the Consumer Protection Law.

The offeror shall notify the other party of the receipt of the acceptance within a reasonable time limit or within the time limit specified in the offer.

The offeror shall be liable to compensate for any breach of this obligation resulting in damage.

The provisions of Articles 33 and 35 of this Law shall not apply to contracts concluded exclusively by way of the exchange of messages via electronic mail or through independent personal communications.

In contracts concluded between merchants or in contracts concluded between professionals in the field of electronic commerce or between merchants and such professionals, the parties may derogate from the rules provided for in Articles 33 and 35 of this Law.

Where acceptance is issued by electronic means in civil and commercial contracts, such acceptance shall not be deemed to form the contract unless it is confirmed a second time by the offeree after having verified the content of the obligations of both parties.

Where negotiations in civil and commercial contracts have taken place by electronic means, the contract shall not be deemed formed except at the time when the acceptance reaches the offeror.

An electronic message shall be deemed to have been sent when it enters the first information system outside the control of the sender.

An electronic message shall be deemed to have been received by the addressee in the following two cases:

1 - When it enters the system designated for receipt by him.

2 - When he retrieves it at an electronic address of his own, if no specific information system has been designated for receiving electronic messages.

Unless the contrary is proven, an electronic message shall be deemed to have been sent from the place of business of the sender and received at the place of business of the addressee. If the sender or the addressee has more than one place of business, the place of business which has the closest relationship to the transaction concerned shall be relied upon, and in the absence of such a transaction, the principal place of business shall be adopted. If the sender or the addressee does not have a place of business, his legal or actual place of residence shall be adopted.

The sender and the addressee may agree on special rules governing the sending and receipt of messages.

Where, in civil and commercial contracts, the drawing up of a written instrument is required for the validity of the legal act, such instrument may be drawn up and preserved in electronic form if the instrument and the signature satisfy the requirements for proof, as defined in Articles 7 and 9 of this Law.

Where a statement must be written in the handwriting of the obligor, he may make such entry in electronic form if it ensures that it could only have been issued by the obligor.

Every person who engages in electronic commerce shall provide the persons with whom he deals with easy, direct, and permanent access to the following information:

1 - His first name, surname, and place of residence, if such person is a natural person.

2 - Its name, the name of its legal representative, its head office, and its business address, if it is a legal person.

3 - The detailed address of the person's place of residence, his electronic mail address, the address of the website used, and telephone numbers or any other means of communication.

4 - The number and place of his registration in the Commercial Register and with the competent tax department.

5 - His professional capacity and a reference to the professional rules applicable to him, if he is a member of a regulated profession or a syndicate.

6 - A detailed statement of the price or consideration showing all taxes, fees, and additional expenses due.

Every promotional advertisement accessible online by any means of electronic communication must include an indication that it is a promotional advertisement, and must also include an identification of the person on whose behalf the advertisement is made.

Unsolicited promotion and marketing (SPAM) that use the name and address of a real person are prohibited, unless such person has given prior consent to this type of advertisement.

Excepted from this principle is the case where the sender of the unsolicited advertisement addressed to a customer has previously obtained his address by lawful means during a prior transaction conducted with him.

Every promotional message or marketing message must include a specification of the address to which the recipient may send a request aimed at permanently stopping this type of message without incurring any expenses.

Every person who, by virtue of his profession, offers goods or services by electronic means shall include in the offer the following:

1 - The stages to be followed to conclude the contract by electronic means.

2 - The terms of the contract in a manner that allows for their preservation and reproduction.

3 - The technical means that allow the recipient of the offer to verify errors committed when using electronic means and to correct them prior to the final acceptance leading to the conclusion of the contract.

4 - The extent of the offeror's obligation to preserve the electronic traces of the negotiation and of the concluded contract, and where such an obligation exists, the specification of the duration of this obligation, the manner of preserving the electronic traces, and the conditions of access to the preserved documents.

5 - The adopted language of the contract.
An offer shall remain binding on the offeror for so long as it remains possible to access such offer by electronic means.

The institutions referred to in Article 41 of this Law shall notify the customer in writing, at least 30 days in advance, of their wish to make any amendment to the terms of contracting.

It shall be for the customer either to approve these amendments or to rescind the contract with the institution concerned.

However, in justified exceptional cases, such as the case of the necessity of meeting protection and security standards and preserving the safety of the customer's account or the safety of the electronic payment or electronic transfer system, the institutions referred to in Article 41 of this Law may place restrictions on the electronic payment and electronic transfer operations carried out by the customer, provided that he is immediately notified of the restrictions without bearing any financial burdens as a result thereof.

The electronic means used shall be capable of transmitting the order to carry out the electronic payment operation or the electronic transfer of monetary funds and of storing it, and shall allow reference thereto by the customer or the institution where necessary.

The institutions referred to in Article 41 of this Law shall adopt a technical system enabling them to identify the party issuing the electronic payment or transfer order and to prove that the customer sent this order to the institution concerned.

The institutions referred to in Article 41 of this Law shall adopt an information system that immediately enables the party ordering the electronic payment or transfer operation to know the result of this order in writing in terms of acceptance or rejection and specifying the reasons for this rejection.

In the event of a material error that led to this rejection, the possibility and method of correcting it must be specified. It shall be for the Banque du Liban to determine the basic standards for the said system.

Except in cases of gross fault, grave negligence or bad faith, the customer shall not be held liable for any debit to his account made as a result of an electronic payment or transfer operation if he notifies without delay the institutions referred to in Article 41 of this Law, in writing, within a period of 90 days from the date of debiting the operation resulting from one of the following cases:

- The possibility of a third party accessing his account without right.

- The likelihood of a third party knowing the identification code specific to his account.

- His knowledge of the execution of any operation on his account without his prior consent or knowledge, or in an erroneous or unlawful manner.

The customer shall be deemed to have notified the institution concerned in accordance with the preceding paragraph if he follows the rules and procedures determined by the Banque du Liban.

It falls within the jurisdiction of the competent summary affairs judge to enforce compliance with the obligations provided for in Articles 31 and 32 of this Law under pain of a coercive fine.

The jurisdiction of the summary affairs judge shall not preclude bringing an action for damages before the civil courts and filing a claim before the competent criminal judiciary.
The provisions of the Consumer Protection Law shall apply to all matters relating to electronic commerce in all that does not conflict with the provisions of this Law.

An order to execute an electronic payment transaction or an electronic transfer of monetary funds is any order that is created, wholly or partially, by an electronic means and pursuant to which the client authorises the bank, financial institution or any other institution licensed by the Banque du Liban or legally authorised to do so, to execute an electronic payment transaction or an electronic transfer of monetary funds or to effect a credit or debit entry to his account or to another account.

The electronic means mentioned in the first paragraph shall mean any electronic means or set of electronic means, including digital means, provided by one of the institutions mentioned above or any of its subsidiary companies and used by the client to execute or give the order to execute one or more electronic payment transactions or electronic transfers of monetary funds.

The institutions referred to in Article 41 of this Law must, when carrying out electronic payment transactions or electronic transfers of monetary funds, ensure that such transactions comply with the laws in force and the regulations issued by the Banque du Liban.

The client must consent in writing and in advance to the conditions relating to electronic payment or transfer transactions or their cancellation, provided that such conditions are clear, explicit and compliant with the regulations issued by the Banque du Liban and include the rights and obligations relating to electronic banking services and specify the fees, expenses, commissions and taxes, if any.

Definitions:

For the purposes of this Law, the following terms shall have the meanings assigned to each of them:

1- Waste: Substances or objects which are disposed of, or are intended to be disposed of, or are required to be disposed of.

2- Solid waste: Waste containing solid, liquid or gaseous components, resulting from any source whatsoever (household or non-household), and which may have hazardous or non-hazardous characteristics. Excluded from solid waste are radioactive waste, gaseous emissions into the atmosphere, and wastewater.

3- Household waste: Solid waste resulting from households; as well as any other type of waste similar to household waste resulting from commercial, industrial and administrative establishments, and also includes waste resulting from municipal sweeping and maintenance operations; and such that it may have hazardous or non-hazardous characteristics.

4- Non-household waste: Solid waste resulting from commercial, industrial, or administrative establishments or others, with the exception of household waste as defined above.

It includes, by way of example and without limitation, industrial waste, agricultural waste, waste from healthcare establishments, slaughterhouse waste, and construction and demolition waste, sludge resulting from the treatment of wastewater, and leachate resulting from solid waste management, etc...

5- Hazardous waste: Waste belonging to any category set out in Annex I of Law No. 387 issued on 4 December 1994 which authorised the Government to accede to the Basel Convention regulating the transboundary movement of hazardous wastes and their disposal, unless it does not possess any of the characteristics set out in Annex III to Law 387/1994, as well as waste which is defined or considered, under domestic legislation for methods of export, import or transit, to be hazardous waste.

6- Non-hazardous waste: Waste with non-hazardous characteristics which is not included in the list of hazardous waste prepared on the basis of the definition of hazardous waste.

7- Biodegradable waste: Waste capable of aerobic or anaerobic microbial biological degradation.

8- Inert waste or residues (Inert materials): Solid waste that resists physical, chemical and biological changes, and is consequently insoluble, non-combustible, non-physically and chemically reactive, and non-biodegradable, and does not affect, like the leachate resulting therefrom, any other materials and does not pose a hazard to the environment; likewise considered as inert waste are fine particles of ash not classified as fly ash, of street sweeping, of broken glass, of cement, of brick (brick), of tiles and ceramics, of soil and rocks, of fibreglass, of metals that can pass through a small-sized sieve (strainer).

9- Fly ash (Fly ash): Materials resulting from the cleaning of the filtration system inside incinerators and which contain a certain proportion of heavy metals and toxic substances.

10- Slag (Slag): Materials resulting from the process of converting waste after burning it by means of thermal decomposition technology, which are harmless materials having numerous uses, particularly in road construction.

11- Solid waste management: Operations of prevention, reduction of production, sorting at source, collection, transport, sorting, treatment, preparation and disposal of solid waste, in addition to monitoring all of these works, and determining the measures to be taken during their performance and during the monitoring period following them, with the aim of protecting the environment.

12- Waste collection: A set of organised activities aimed at removing waste from its source or from containers designated for its accumulation or from its accumulation centres, and includes carrying out the necessary preparations for transporting the waste.

13- Waste sorting: Manual or mechanical operations aimed at sorting the recoverable fraction of waste.

14- Waste treatment: Operations designated for converting waste through any of the following means: recycling, composting, biological decomposition, and thermal decomposition.

15- Recycling (Recycling): The process of obtaining materials contained in solid waste that can be reused as substitute materials for raw materials used in the manufacturing process, or using the properties of those materials to remanufacture those materials or manufacture other materials. Excluded from this is the direct use of the energy resources contained in this waste.

16- Composting (Composting): The controlled microbial biological degradation of organic solid waste by microorganisms and its conversion into a product that can be used as a soil improver provided that the necessary conditions are met therein in accordance with the provisions of this Law (compost)

17- Biological decomposition: The various technologies that rely on microbial biological degradation (other than composting), with or without aeration, and aimed at reproducing materials similar to composted materials and producing energy resources.

18- Thermal decomposition: The process of utilising the calorific value of a waste component with the aim of reducing its volume and producing energy.

19- Refuse-derived fuel (RDF): An alternative fuel extracted from a waste component with a high calorific value, which can be used from generating energy and as an alternative fuel in the cement industry and other industries.

20- Waste preparation: Physical, chemical, or biological operations that result in changing the characteristics of the waste, with a focus on reducing its volume or its hazardous nature, and facilitating its handling or its better treatment.

21- Disposal of solid waste residues: The integrated process that follows the stages of treatment and preparation and that secures the final discharge of solid waste residues that cannot be subjected to any additional treatment operations, provided that the final discharge complies with environmental and public health regulations and standards.

22- Sanitary landfilling: The process of disposing of solid waste residues at a site selected and equipped in accordance with specific engineering and environmental standards.

23- Waste - primary product: Fresh or old waste that is unmodified in its nature and composition and resulting, by way of example and without limitation, from households, importers, manufacturers, and distributors, and others...

24- Waste - secondary product: Waste that is modified in its nature and composition and resulting, by way of example and without limitation, from composting, biological conversion, and thermal decomposition centres, and others...

25- Waste producer: A natural or legal person from the public or private sector who produces household or non-household waste (primary producer), and/or a natural or legal person from whom waste results as a consequence of operations of treatment, preparation or mixing of waste (secondary producer).

26- Service provider: A natural or legal person authorised by this Law to carry out the collection and transport of waste, or recyclable materials.

27- Operator (Contractor): A natural or legal person authorised by this Law to carry out the works of sorting, treatment, preparation and disposal of solid waste.

28- Local administrations: Municipalities, unions of municipalities, groupings of municipalities, administrative decentralisation bodies and entities entrusted with performing the tasks of a municipality in the cases specified in the Law.

29- Joint project: Any project of public utility to which the private sector contributes through financing and management and at least one of the following operations: design, construction, building, development, restoration, equipping, maintenance, rehabilitation and operation (as defined in Law No. 48 dated 7/9/2017 aimed at regulating Public-Private Partnership).

In the event that any of the institutions referred to in Article 41 of this Law is notified of an unexecuted electronic payment or transfer transaction or of any of the cases mentioned in the preceding Article, such institution shall investigate the matter and notify the client in writing of the result of such investigation. In all cases, the burden of proving the contrary of what the client has notified it of shall rest upon the concerned institution.

In the event that the result of the investigation reveals the existence of an unexecuted transaction or the occurrence of one of the cases that require notification pursuant to Article 46, the duly notified institution shall, without charging the client any fees or expenses:

1 - Execute the unexecuted transaction in due form, under its full responsibility and as soon as possible.

2 - Take the appropriate measures to protect the client's account.

3 - Rectify any error or unlawful entry.

4 - Compensate for any losses incurred by the client's account.

Orders to carry out electronic payment and transfer transactions of monetary funds shall be given in writing, signed manually or electronically, under penalty of nullity.

If such orders are given and signed electronically, such signature must be certified in accordance with the rules issued by the Banque du Liban.

An electronic payment or transfer order of monetary funds issued by the payer or transferor may not be revoked after the amount has been debited from his account, except with the consent of the beneficiary and the concerned institution referred to in Article 41 of this Law.

Electronic payment or transfer orders of a periodic nature may be revoked, provided that the institutions referred to in Article 41 of this Law receive the revocation order at least two full working days prior to the date of the next nearest subsequent transfer transaction.

The institutions referred to in Article 41 of this Law shall bear liability for the total or partial non-execution of electronic payment or transfer orders, unless they prove the existence of one of the following cases:

1 - That the non-execution resulted from an error, negligence, or deficiency in the instructions issued by the client, or from his bad faith.

2 - The insufficiency of the funds available in the client's account to execute this transaction, unless otherwise agreed with the client.

3 - The occurrence of a case of force majeure or a case beyond its control, where the institution concerned had exerted all efforts to avoid such a case.

4 - In the other cases determined by the Bank of Lebanon.

In the event that liability is incurred by the aforementioned institutions, they must return the disputed amounts to the client and compensate, where applicable, for the damage sustained by him.

The institutions referred to in Article 41 of this Law may not levy any of the fees, or expenses, or and commissions, or taxes from the value of the amount requested to be paid or transferred electronically except after expressly informing the client thereof and obtaining his approval in writing.

The institutions referred to in Article 41 of this Law shall be obliged to provide the client in writing with periodic statements of the entries made to his account, provided that they include information regarding the executed electronic payment or transfer transactions, in particular specifying the outgoing and incoming transactions, the dates on which they were made, and their values.

The application or the contract concluded to obtain the bank card must be in writing, and the entity issuing the bank card must comply with the regulations determined by the Bank of Lebanon.

None of the banks or institutions licensed to issue bank cards by the Bank of Lebanon may issue to deliver a bank card that has been activated in favour of any person if he had not requested it or contracted for it, except in the case of renewal or replacement of a card previously agreed upon.

The entity issuing the bank card shall:

1 - Deliver to the holder of the bank card the identification information that authorises him to use it.

2 - Guarantee the confidentiality of the identification information mentioned in the preceding paragraph by adopting a modern technical system that secures the confidentiality of such information.

3 - Retain complete statements of the operations executed by means of the card for a period determined by the Banque du Liban.

4 - Secure for the holder of the bank card the appropriate means that enable him to report its loss or theft.

5 - Prevent any use of the bank card immediately upon reporting its loss or theft.

The entity issuing bank cards shall deliver or send immediate notifications of every operation carried out by way of the bank card, provided that such notifications include the basic information relating to the payment or transfer operation, including the date of the order and the identity of the client.

The holder of the bank card shall use his card in accordance with the agreed conditions, and shall take all necessary precautions to protect the card and the identification information that authorises its use.

The holder of the bank card may not revoke the electronic payment order or the electronic undertaking to pay issued by means of this card except after the approval of the beneficiary and the institution issuing the card.

In addition to the cases of reporting and their consequences set forth in Articles 46 and 47 of this Law, the holder of the bank card shall, immediately upon his knowledge of the loss or theft of the bank card or of the information that allows its unlawful or fraudulent use by a third party, or of either of the two cases mentioned in Article 58 below, report orally, in writing, or electronically to the entity issuing the card, which shall suspend it and prevent its use immediately.

The holder of the bank card shall not bear the consequences resulting from the loss or theft of the card or its unlawful or fraudulent use by a third party, in the event that he notifies the institutions referred to in Article 41 of this Law, in writing or electronically, within a period determined by the Banque du Liban. The issuing entity shall recredit the disputed amounts to the account of the cardholder without imposing additional financial burdens on him, within a period not exceeding one month from the date of such reporting.

The holder of the bank card shall bear full liability if the concerned institution proves that he committed a gross fault or major negligence beyond the ordinary, or acted in bad faith, or if he failed to fulfil the obligation of reporting in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph.

No liability shall be incurred by the holder of the bank card in the event that he notifies, in writing or electronically, the institution issuing the card and within the time limit specified by the Bank of Lebanon, of:

1 - Payment transactions executed remotely in an unlawful or fraudulent manner, without the physical presentation of the bank card or the identification of the payment orderer.

2 - Payment transactions executed by means of a counterfeit bank card despite the possession of the original card by its holder stopping the execution of the disputed transaction.

In both of these cases, the issuing entity shall re-credit the disputed amounts to his account without imposing financial charges upon him, within a maximum time limit of one month from the date of such notification.

The entity issuing the bank card shall be liable for the non-execution of the orders issued by the cardholder and/or for the defective execution thereof and/or for the transactions executed without his consent and/or for the errors occurring in the management of his account.

The provisions set forth in the First Section of this Chapter relating to electronic payment transactions and the electronic transfer of cash funds shall apply to bank cards insofar as they do not conflict with the provisions of this Section.
The regulations issued by the Bank of Lebanon shall determine the nature of electronic and digital money, the manner of its issuance and use, and the technologies and regulations governing it.

An electronic cheque is a cheque that is created, signed and circulated electronically.

The digital image of the cheque is the image resulting from the optical scanning of the paper cheque and coupled with full technical guarantees in accordance with the regulations laid down by the Bank of Lebanon.

The digital representation of the cheque is the process of extracting data from the paper cheque, in whole or in part, in accordance with the regulations issued by the Bank of Lebanon.

The Bank of Lebanon shall define the concept of the digital cheque, the manner of its issuance and use, and the technologies and regulations governing it.

The electronic cheque and the paper cheque, prior to the conversion of the latter into a digital image, must contain all the information referred to in Article 409 of the Code of Land Commerce.

No right granted to any person pursuant to the provisions set forth in this Chapter may be waived, and every clause or agreement whereby any party waives any of these rights shall be deemed null and void.

The general provisions relating to the retention of banking records shall apply to electronic records and signatures pertaining to banking transactions.

Banque du Liban shall have the right to issue the necessary regulations relating to the rules provided for in this Chapter, in particular with respect to regulating payment orders, electronic and digital money, transfers, electronic cheques, the digital image of the cheque, the digital representation of the cheque and the digital cheque, the manner of issuing and using them, the rules for retaining banking records and the duration of their retention, in addition to the necessary protection and security means.

Communication to the public by digital means shall mean anything placed at the disposal of the public or categories of the public by a digital means, consisting of signs, writings, images, sounds and messages of whatever nature which do not have the character of private correspondence.
Communication to the public by a digital means is free within the limits of the requirements of respect for the Constitution, the laws and public policy.

If the contract concerned by this Part is subject to a foreign law, the acts which it regulates shall remain mandatorily subject to the provisions of Lebanese law if they relate to the following:

1 - Practices harmful to competition.

2 - Rights protected by intellectual property laws.

3 - Unfair terms affecting consumer protection.

4 - Public policy rules governing the conduct of commercial activities.
Both the communication service provider and the data host shall be deemed a technical service provider.
