A communication service provider shall not be obliged to monitor the information which it transmits or which it stores temporarily. However, it shall be required immediately, on pain of liability, to withdraw the temporarily stored information or to render access thereto impossible upon the request of the sender of the information or pursuant to a decision by the judicial authority.

A data host shall not be obliged to monitor the information which it stores for the purpose of placing it at the disposal of the public, provided that liability shall attach to it if it does not withdraw such information or if it does not render access thereto impossible immediately upon its actual knowledge of its manifestly unlawful character.

The same person may simultaneously carry on the activity of a communication service provider and a data host.

Such activities shall fall within the framework of electronic commerce, and shall be subject to the provisions of Articles 30, 31 and 32 of this Law.

Technical service providers shall retain the information relating to data traffic for all persons who use their services, which enables the identification of such persons, as well as the other technical data of communications, for a period of three years running from the date of performance of the service.

The judicial police may, within the framework of investigation proceedings in a criminal action, and after informing the competent judicial authority, request technical service providers to retain technical data additional to that provided for in the first paragraph of this Article for a maximum period of thirty days and concerning a specific fact and specific persons, having regard to the urgent nature and the possibility of such data being exposed to loss or modification. Such data shall only be handed over to the judicial police pursuant to a decision by the competent judicial authority.

A technical service provider may not invoke any technical defect that leads to the non-retention of the technical data, and shall be bound to take the appropriate technical measures determined by a decision of the Minister of Telecommunications.

Technical data shall be subject to the professional secrecy by which the technical service provider is bound. However, he may not invoke such secrecy against the competent judiciary, within the limits of the requirements of investigations and trials.

The retention obligation provided for in the first paragraph shall not include the stored or transmitted content or substance expressing the thoughts of the person who authored it, such as exchanged correspondence or the content of stored or transmitted information or websites.

The mechanism for retaining the information relating to data traffic and the nature of such information or the erasure thereof shall be determined pursuant to a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice.

A technical service provider shall be liable towards his clients for the proper performance of his contractual obligations.

Contracts signed with clients and the annexes thereto must include a specification of the level of the service, the type thereof, and the extent of the continuity thereof.

A technical service provider shall be wholly or partially exempted from liability if he proves that the non-performance or improper performance of the contract resulted from a fault committed by the client, or resulted from force majeure or from the act of a third party.

Any person who places information at the disposal of the public by means of an online communication service (online), in a professional capacity, shall also place, by means thereof, the personal identification elements provided for in Article 31 of this Law.

A person who places, in a non-professional capacity, information for the public by means of an online communication service (online) may preserve the confidentiality of his identity and place within the reach of the public only identification elements pertaining to the data host, and he shall supply the data host with his personal identification data specified in Article 31 of this Law. The data host shall retain them for a period of ten years.

A technical service provider shall be deemed to have taken up legal domicile in Lebanon when he is permanently established therein to exercise his activity, whatever his nationality and whatever its head office in the event that it is a legal person.

Technical service providers shall cooperate with the competent judiciary and the authorities provided for in Law No. 140/99 and within limits to reveal the truth in every investigation it conducts or in every action pending before it.

The competent judiciary and the authorities provided for in Law No. 99/140 and within the limits thereof may, within the framework of an investigation or an action, compel the technical service provider to hand over to them the data in his possession or placed under his control, in performance of the two line obligations provided for in Articles 72 and 74 of this Law, within the limits of the requirements of investigations and trials.

The technical service provider shall, pursuant to a decision of the competent judicial authority or the authorities provided for in Law No. 99/140 and within the limits thereof, immediately supply it with the information relating to data traffic and with the other technical data provided for in Articles 72 and 74 of this Law, and empower them to access the aforementioned information in real time (real time) for any communication operation transiting through his network.

A breach by a technical service provider of any of the obligations provided for Articles 72, 74 and 76 of this Law shall be deemed a misdemeanour punishable by imprisonment from three to six months and by a fine from ten to fifty million Lebanese pounds, or by either of these two penalties.
Each of the domain lb and the domain .لبنان, within the top level of the addressing system of websites on the Internet, defines the names pertaining to the country code of Lebanon.

The courts shall have jurisdiction to adjudicate disputes relating to domain names.

The Authority shall not be deemed a party to the dispute, but shall enforce the judgments rendered in the disputes by the Lebanese courts.

Disputes capable of settlement relating to domain names may be settled by non-judicial means, and the entity authorised to grant and manage domain names shall select one or more centres to settle disputes relating to domain names by non-judicial means.

Awards rendered by arbitration centres shall be vested with the executory formula by operation of law and shall be valid for direct enforcement through the competent enforcement departments.

The charter for naming domain names on the Internet network must include a list of the names of the centres and the rules they adopt for resolving disputes.

The exercise by the entity authorised to grant and manage domain names of its tasks shall not vest it with any rights over the domain names that it grants or manages.

The entity authorised to grant and manage domain names shall not be deemed liable for the expressions chosen by registration applicants for domain names, provided that it shall be required to verify that they respect the charter for naming domain names on the Internet network.

The entity authorised to grant and manage domain names may of its own motion cancel or refuse a domain name if its holder fails to pay the fees due from him, or if it appears that the registration applicant does not meet the conditions qualifying him to benefit from this name, or if the information submitted is incomplete, incorrect or not updated, or if the expression chosen as a domain name is contrary to public order or public morals.

The charter for naming domain names shall determine the rules followed for the automatic cancellation or refusal of a domain name and the period granted to the violator to submit his observations therein.

The fees shall be determined pursuant to a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

The provisions set forth in this Part shall apply to all automated and non-automated processing of personal data. However, they shall not apply to processing relating to personal activities carried out by a person exclusively for his own needs.

No agreement may be made in derogation of the provisions set forth in this Part which regulate the rights of data subjects and the obligations of the controllers of such processing. Furthermore, no contrary agreement or clause, nor any unilateral undertaking, may be invoked..

There shall be established pursuant to this Law an authority named the "National Authority for the Management of Domains Specific to Lebanon" (Registry)

The Authority shall assume the tasks of managing and registering domain names within the domains specific to Lebanon (.Lb and .لبنان and other domain names) after conducting the necessary investigations in accordance with a tariff compatible with the development of the registration operations market.

The Authority shall be composed of representatives from each of the Ministry of Telecommunications, the Ministry of Economy and Trade and the Ministry of Finance, the Ministry of Justice, the Minister of State for Administrative Reform, the Telecommunications Regulatory Authority, the Federation of Chambers of Commerce, Industry and Agriculture, the Bar Association, and representatives from a number of active associations concerned with this sector ranging in number between three or five, provided that they are named by the aforementioned Authority, and any association that becomes inactive shall be replaced by this Authority.

The Authority shall determine the administrative and technical conditions for granting and managing the names belonging to Lebanese domains, and for accrediting registrars (registrars), taking into consideration the rules established by the international authorities concerned with the registration of internet sites.

The Authority shall incorporate these conditions in the form of a charter on the naming of domain names on the internet, place it at the disposal of the public and publish it on its website on the internet.

The naming charter shall include objective conditions for obtaining domain names and without discrimination, subject to the observance of public order, the laws in force and the rules established by the international authorities concerned with the registration of internet sites.

The Minister of State for Administrative Reform shall assume the tasks of managing and registering government domain names in coordination with the competent ministries and administrations.

A domain name may be registered and managed remotely via electronic means.

A domain name shall be registered subject to the preservation of the rights of third parties.

In the event of a violation of these provisions, legal liabilities shall be incurred, where applicable, by the applicant for the domain name, which may lead to the cancellation or transfer of ownership of the granted domain name.

Every person shall have the right to inspect and object, before the controller of the processing of personal data, to the information and analyses used in the automated processing operations relating to him and invoked against him.

No judicial or administrative decision requiring an assessment of human conduct may be based solely on an automated processing of data intended to determine a person's characteristics or to evaluate certain aspects of his personality.

Personal data shall be collected fairly and for legitimate, specified and explicit purposes.

The data must be adequate and not excessive in relation to the declared purposes, and must be accurate and complete and kept up to date to the extent necessary.

Such data may not at a subsequent stage be processed for purposes incompatible with the declared ends, unless the matter relates to the processing of data for statistical, historical or scientific research purposes.

The controller of the processing of personal data or his representative shall inform the persons from whom the personal data are collected of the following:

1 - The identity of the controller of the processing or the identity of his representative.

2 - The purposes of the processing.

3 - The mandatory or optional nature of replying to the questions asked.

4 - The consequences that may result from failing to reply.

5 - The persons to whom the data will be sent.

6 - The right of access to and rectification of the information and the means provided therefor.

The forms used for collecting the data must contain an explicit and clear statement of the information specified in the first paragraph of this Article.

Where the personal data have not been collected from the data subject, the controller of the processing shall inform the latter personally and explicitly of the content of such data, of the purposes of the processing, and of his right to object to the carrying out of the processing.

This obligation shall lapse where the data subject is aware of the matter or where informing him proves impossible or involves an effort disproportionate to the benefit of the measure.
The retention of personal data shall only be lawful during the period indicated in the declaration of processing or in the decision authorising it.

It is prohibited to collect or process personal data if it reveals, directly or indirectly, the health status, genetic identity, or sexual life of the data subject.

This prohibition shall not apply in the following cases:

1 - Where the data subject has made such data available to the public or has explicitly consented to the processing thereof, unless there is a legal impediment.

2 - Where the collection or processing of the data is necessary for establishing a medical diagnosis or providing medical treatment by a member of a health profession.

3 - Upon establishing or defending a right before the judiciary.

4 - In the event of obtaining a permit in accordance with the provisions of Article 97 of this Law.

Every natural person shall have the right to object, on legitimate grounds, before the data controller to the collection and processing of personal data relating to him, including collection and processing for the purpose of commercial promotion.

However, a person shall not be entitled to exercise the right to object in the following two cases:

1 - If the data controller is obliged to collect the data pursuant to the law.

2 - If he has consented to the processing of the personal data relating to him.

The controller of personal data shall take all measures, in light of the nature of the data and the risks resulting from the processing, to ensure the integrity and security of the data and to prevent it from being distorted, damaged, or accessed by persons not authorised to view it.

No declaration shall be required to be submitted nor any permit requested for the processing of personal data in the following cases:

1 - In processing operations carried out by persons of public law, each within the scope of its powers.

2 - Where non-profit associations keep the registers relating to their members and persons dealing with them within the scope of the normal and lawful exercise of their tasks.

3 - In processing operations the object of which is the keeping of registers intended, pursuant to statutory or regulatory provisions, to inform the public and which may be inspected by any person or persons having a legitimate interest.

4 - In processing operations the object of which is pupils and students by educational institutions for educational or administrative purposes specific to the institution.

5 - In processing operations the object of which is employees or members in commercial establishments and companies, syndicates, associations and practitioners of the liberal professions, within the limits and for the needs of the lawful exercise of their activities.

6 - In processing operations the object of which is clients and persons dealing with commercial establishments and companies, syndicates, associations and practitioners of the liberal professions, within the limits and for the needs of the lawful exercise of their activities.

7 - Where the data subject has consented in advance to the processing of his personal data unless there is a legal impediment.

Certain processing operations or certain categories thereof may also be exempted from the declaration or permit procedures if it appears that putting them into effect does not entail any risk threatening private life or personal liberties, pursuant to a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Justice and of Economy and Trade.

8 - In the processing operations provided for in Law No. 140/99 and within its limits.

With the exception of the exemptions provided for in the preceding Article, any person who wishes to collect and process personal data must notify the Ministry of Economy and Trade by means of a declaration made in due form against a receipt.

The declaration submitted to the Ministry of Economy and Trade pursuant to the preceding Article must include the following information:

1 - The purposes of the processing.

2 - The personal data that are the subject of the processing and their source.

3 - The categories of data subjects.

4 - The third parties or categories of third parties to whom the data may be disclosed.

5 - The period of retention of the data.

6 - The identity and address of the data controller.

7 - The identity and address of the data controller if that controller is resident outside Lebanese territory.

8 - The department or departments entrusted with carrying out the processing.

9 - The person or department before whom the right of access is exercised and the manner of exercising it.

10 - The sub-concessionaire or subcontractor, if any.

11 - Where applicable, the methods of interconnection or any other form of linking between the data and other processing operations, in addition to possible assignments of the data to third parties.

12 - Where applicable, the transfer of personal data to another State in any form whatsoever.

13 - The measures taken to ensure the security of personal data and to ensure the preservation of secrets protected by law, the obligation of the proper implementation of which rests upon the data controller.

14 - Confirmation that the processing shall be carried out in accordance with the law.

Processing operations of personal data relating to the following shall be subject to licensing:

1 - The external and internal security of the State, pursuant to a joint decision issued by the Ministers of National Defence and of the Interior and Municipalities.

2 - Criminal offences and judicial proceedings of all kinds, pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Justice.

3 - Health conditions, genetic identity, or the sex life of individuals, pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Public Health.

The licensing decision shall be issued within a time limit of two months from the date of submission of the application, failing which it shall be deemed implicitly rejected upon the expiry of the time limit.

The decision granting or refusing the licence shall be notified in writing to the Ministry of Economy and Trade and to the applicant.

The Ministry of Economy and Trade shall make available to the public, particularly on its website on the internet, a list of the automated processings that have fulfilled the licensing or declaration procedures provided for in this Chapter.

This list shall specify for each licensed or declared processing:

1 - The declaration submitted or the licence granted therefor, their dates, and the date of commencement of the processing.

2 - The designation of the processing and the purpose thereof.

3 - The identity and address of the controller of the processing.

4 - The identity and address of the representative of the controller of the processing if this controller is resident outside Lebanon.

5 - The categories of personal data that are the subject of the processing.

6 - The person or administration before whom the right of access to the data is exercised.

7 - The third parties or categories thereof authorised to have access to the data.

8 - And, where applicable, the personal data intended to be transferred to a foreign State.

Every data subject of personal data or any of his heirs shall have the right to inquire of the controller of the processing of personal data in order to know whether or not such data pertaining to him are the subject of processing.

The controller of the processing of personal data must deliver to the data subject of personal data or to any of his heirs a copy of the data pertaining to him upon his request. If such data are coded, compressed or encrypted, the data subject of personal data or any of his heirs must be given an intelligible copy.

The data subject of personal data or any of his heirs may also request from the controller of the processing of personal data, in accordance with the conditions specified in the second paragraph above, to be delivered the following additional information:

The purposes of the processing, the categories thereof, the source thereof, the subject and nature of the processing, the identification of the persons and the categories thereof to whom the personal data are sent or who may have access thereto, the timings thereof, and the purposes of such access.

The personal data processing controller may charge a fee in return for providing a copy of the personal data belonging to the personal data subject or to any of his heirs as stipulated in the preceding Article, provided that the fee does not exceed the cost of copying.

The personal data processing controller may object to requests of an abusive nature, particularly with regard to their number or their repetitive or systematic nature.

In the event of a dispute, the burden of proving the abusive nature of the requests mentioned above shall fall upon the personal data processing controller who receives them.

The personal data subject or any of his heirs shall have the right to request from the controller of the processing of such data the rectification, completion, updating and erasure thereof, where they are inaccurate, incomplete, ambiguous, expired, or incompatible with the purposes of the processing, or where the processing, collection, use, retention or transfer thereof is prohibited.

If the personal data that are the subject of the rectification request have been sent to a third party, the controller of their processing must notify the latter of the amendments made thereto pursuant to the request of the subject thereof or any of his heirs.

The personal data processing controller shall, upon the request of the subject thereof or any of his heirs, carry out the requested operations free of charge within a period of ten days at most starting from the date of submission of the rectification request, and prove that he has done so.

The personal data processing controller shall rectify them automatically when he becomes aware of one of the reasons that oblige him to amend or cancel them.

The personal data subject or any of his heirs may have recourse to the competent courts, in particular the judge of urgent matters in accordance with adversarial procedures, to ensure the exercise of the right of access and rectification and to order compliance with the provisions of this Title with regard to the personal data relating to him.

Where the processing operations relate to the internal or external security of the State, the personal data subject may not be given access to his data that are the subject of the processing if doing so would jeopardise the purposes thereof or the internal or external security of the State.

The right of individuals to access public records and files and medical files that contain personal data shall be subject to the legal and regulatory provisions that govern them.

The processing of personal data and the right to access and rectify it in ministries, public administrations, and public institutions outside the frameworks of their specific legal and regulatory texts shall be subject to the provisions of this Law and to a prior permit issued by the Council of Ministers upon a proposal by the competent minister.

The provisions of Articles 99, 100, and 101 of this Law shall not apply to the processing of personal data carried out solely for the purposes of literary and artistic expression or for the purposes of the professional exercise of a journalistic activity within the limits of compliance with the laws in force.

The preceding paragraph shall not preclude the application of laws that provide for the conditions of exercising the right of reply and that regulate infringement upon private life and the reputation of persons.

Any person who commits any of the following acts shall be punished by a fine from one million Lebanese pounds to thirty million Lebanese pounds and by imprisonment from three months up to three years, or by either of these two penalties:

Whoever proceeds to process personal data without submitting a declaration, or without obtaining a prior permit before commencing his work in accordance with the provisions of Chapter Three of this Title.

Whoever proceeds to collect or process personal data without complying with the rules established in accordance with the provisions of Chapter Two of this Title.

Whoever proceeds, even by negligence, to disclose information of a personal nature that is the subject of processing to persons not authorised to view it.

Every personal data processing controller who refuses to reply within a time limit of ten working days, or replies incorrectly or incompletely to the request of the data subject or his proxy regarding the right of access or rectification referred to in Chapter Four of this Title, shall be punished by a fine from one million Lebanese pounds to fifteen million Lebanese pounds.
In the event of repetition of any of the acts provided for in this Chapter, the penalties and fines mentioned in the Articles above shall be increased by one third to one half.

Criminal prosecution in respect of the criminal acts provided for in Paragraph 3 of Article 106 and in Article 107 shall only be instituted upon a complaint by the injured party.

The public right of action shall lapse consequential to the waiver of the private right of action in respect of these criminal acts if such waiver occurs before the judgment in the action becomes final and irrevocable.

Unlawful access to an information system:

Any person who, with fraudulent intent, accesses or enters the whole or part of an information system or remains therein shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to two years and by a fine from one million to twenty million Lebanese Pounds, or by either of these two penalties.

The penalty shall be increased to imprisonment from six months to three years and a fine from two million to forty million Pounds if the act results in the deletion, copying or modification of digital data or computer programs, or in the impairment of the operation of the information system.

Infringement of the integrity of the system:

Any person who, with fraudulent intent and by any means, hinders the operation of an information system or corrupts it shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years and by a fine from three million to two hundred million Lebanese Pounds, or by either of these two penalties.

Infringement of the integrity of digital data:

Any person who enters digital data, with fraudulent intent, into an information system and any person who deletes or modifies, with fraudulent intent, the digital data contained in an information system shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years and by a fine from three million to two hundred million Lebanese Pounds, or by either of these two penalties.

Hindering, disrupting or disabling:

Any person who intentionally and by any means, through the information network or a computer device or the like, hinders, disrupts or disables access to a service or entry into devices, programs, or sources of data or information shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to two years and by a fine from two million to thirty million Lebanese Pounds, or by either of these two penalties.

Misuse of computer devices and programs:

Any person who imports, produces, possesses, provides, makes available or disseminates, without a legitimate reason, a computer device or program or any data designed or adapted for the purpose of committing any of the offences provided for in the preceding articles of this Chapter shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years and by a fine from three million to two hundred million Lebanese Pounds, or by either of these two penalties.
An attempt to commit the offences provided for in this Chapter shall be punished by the same penalty.

Subsection Three of Chapter Two of Title Seven entitled ":On Offences Contrary to Public Morals and Decency" of Legislative Decree No. 340 dated 1/3/1943 (the Penal Code) shall be repealed and replaced by the following provisions:

"Subsection 3 - On Offences of Exploiting Minors in Pornographic Materials

Article 535 - The exploitation of minors in pornographic materials means the depiction, display or material representation of any minor, by any means whatsoever, such as drawings, pictures, writings, films or signs, engaging in real or simulated explicit sexual activities, or any depiction of the sexual organs of a minor.

The provisions of the Penal Code shall apply, where the conditions thereof are met, to criminal acts relating to the exploitation of minors in pornographic materials, subject to the provisions of the following Article.

Article 536 - The preparation or production of pornographic materials in which minors actually participate, and which relate to the exploitation of minors in pornographic materials, shall be deemed to constitute the offence of trafficking in persons, and the perpetrator thereof shall be punished in accordance with the text of Article 586 (1) et seq. of the Penal Code relating to trafficking in persons.

However, if minors do not actually participate in the pornographic materials relating to the exploitation of minors, the perpetrator shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to three years and by a fine from five hundred thousand to two million Lebanese pounds.

Any person who provides, transmits, copies, displays, makes available, distributes, exports, imports, publishes, broadcasts or promotes, by any means whatsoever, pornographic materials relating to the exploitation of minors shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to three years and by a fine from five hundred thousand to two million Lebanese pounds.

The penalties provided for in this Article shall be increased in accordance with Article 257 of the Penal Code if an electronic communications network, such as the Internet, or radio broadcasting or television broadcasting is used in order to publish or distribute pornographic materials relating to the exploitation of minors to an unspecified public.

The same penalties shall apply to an attempt to commit the offences mentioned in the preceding paragraphs.

Notwithstanding any other text, any person who habitually captures or views, by means of radio or television broadcasting, or by using a communication service directed to the public, or by any means, pornographic materials relating to the exploitation of minors, or intentionally retains them by any means whatsoever, shall be punished by imprisonment for up to one year at most and by a fine not exceeding two million Lebanese pounds, or by either of these two penalties.

The provisions of this Article shall apply to pornographic images of a person whose appearance seems to be that of a minor.

Where the criminal act provided for in this Article is committed by a legal person, it may also be sentenced to suspension from work for a period ranging between one month at least and two years at most".

Shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to three years and by a fine from ten million to two hundred million Lebanese Pounds, or by either of these two penalties, whoever:

1 - Counterfeits or falsifies a bank card.

2 - Uses or circulates, with his knowledge of the matter, a falsified or counterfeited bank card.

3 - Accepts to receive sums of money with his knowledge that the payment was made by means of a falsified or counterfeited bank card.

4 - Counterfeits electronic or digital money.

5 - Uses, with his knowledge of the matter, counterfeited electronic or digital money.

6 - Counterfeits an electronic or digital cheque.

7 - Uses, with his knowledge of the matter, a counterfeited electronic or digital cheque.

The provisions of Articles 114 and 115 shall apply to the criminal acts mentioned in this Article.

Shall be punished by a fine from two million Lebanese Pounds to twenty million Lebanese Pounds whoever violates the obligations imposed on the sender of an unsolicited promotional or marketing message (SPAM), as provided for in Article 32 of this Law.

The text of Item 3 of Article (209) of the Penal Code shall be amended as follows:

«Writing, drawings, paintings, photographs, films, badges, and depictions of all kinds if displayed in a public place or a place open to the public or exposed to view, or if sold, offered for sale, or distributed to one or more persons, whatever the means adopted therefor, including electronic means».

The text of Article (453) of the Penal Code shall be amended as follows:

«Forgery is an intentional distortion of the truth, in the facts or data established by a deed, manuscript, paper or electronic medium, or any other medium of expression constituting a document, with the motive of causing material, moral, or social harm».

Information technology traces, which are in the nature of digital or information technology evidence, are the data committed by persons voluntarily or involuntarily on systems, databases, information technology services and information technology networks.

Information technology evidence includes: information technology equipment, programs, data, applications, information technology traces and the like.

The rules set forth in this Chapter shall be followed when seizing information technology evidence pursuant to a decision of the Public Prosecution or the competent judicial authority.

Privacy shall be respected with regard to information technology traces, in particular data and images unrelated to the criminal action.

The judicial police shall carry out the procedures for seizing and preserving information technology evidence provided for in this Chapter, pursuant to a decision of the competent judicial authority.

A specialised office shall assist the judicial police in seizing and preserving information technology evidence.

It shall be for the court to assess the digital or information technology evidence and its probative value in proof, provided that it has not been subjected to any alteration during the process of its seizure, preservation or analysis.

A record shall be drawn up of every operation of seizure, preservation, analysis, examination, transfer or other operation from one authority to another of any information technology or digital evidence, provided that it includes a detailed presentation of all the procedures and acts carried out, all the authorities that held the evidence in their possession and the manner of its transfer, in particular those ensuring the integrity of the evidence and that no modification has been made thereto since the moment of its seizure.

In all cases, a true copy of the original (of the data and programs) as seized from the digital evidence shall be retained, seals shall be affixed to the electronic medium on which it is preserved, and it shall be deposited with the judicial authority that ordered the measure together with the records drawn up.

Subject to the provisions set forth in this Chapter, the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure relating to search and the seizure of evidence in flagrante delicto and non-flagrante delicto offences, in particular Articles 33 and 41 thereof, shall apply to the seizure of information technology evidence or data on a portable electronic medium, such as compact discs or a computer device.

Upon the seizure of computer data and programs, the rights of persons acting in good faith and the rights of the person concerned must be observed by copying the seized data and programs and refraining from seizing the computer equipment on which they are located, in particular if such equipment is used for other legitimate purposes.

Upon seizure, in the event that the data or computer evidence is downloaded or transferred from a website or from any computer, its source must be stated.

Any data or digital evidence stored in an information system located in Lebanese territory may be seized if it is accessible from the information system ordered to be searched.

Any data stored in an information system may be accessed and seized, regardless of its location inside or outside Lebanon, if it is made available to the public or in the event of the consent of the person legally authorised to disclose such data through an information system located in Lebanese territory.

Upon the seizure of computer evidence, the Public Prosecution or the judicial authority hearing the case may decide that the process of downloading, transferring or copying the data or programs shall take place in the presence of the person concerned or in the presence of a technical specialist in information technology appointed by that person pursuant to a written authorisation. Where necessary, the premises where the operation takes place, or the electronic medium where the data and programs are located, shall be sealed with red wax until the attendance of that technical specialist within the specified time limit; otherwise, the operation shall take place in the presence of two relatives of the person concerned, his representative, or two witnesses, or their presence shall be dispensed with as decided by the competent judicial authority.

By decision of the judicial authority that ordered the measure, a copy of the seized computer data and programs may be given to the person concerned at the time of their seizure.

The judicial authority may request any person having knowledge of the methods of operation of an information system or the protection measures applied to it to provide the authority entrusted with the investigation with the information required in order to access the required data and programs.

It may also request any person in possession of data or programs that may be the subject of computer evidence to make a copy thereof and preserve it in his possession until it is seized from him.

The court hearing the case may, pursuant to its final judgment, suspend electronic services, block websites, or cancel accounts thereon if they relate to offences relating to terrorism, child pornography, prohibited gambling games, organised electronic fraud operations, money laundering, offences against internal and external security, or offences relating to infringing the integrity of information systems such as spreading viruses.

The Public Prosecution may decide to suspend electronic services, block websites, or freeze accounts thereon temporarily for a maximum period of thirty days, renewable once by a reasoned decision, provided that the effect of this measure shall lapse automatically upon the expiry of the specified time limit.

The Investigating Judge or the competent court hearing the case may decide the same temporarily pending the issuance of the final judgment in the case. The judicial authority may also revoke its decision where new circumstances arise justifying the same. The decision of the Investigating Judge and of the court to suspend electronic services, block websites, or freeze accounts thereon shall be subject to appeal in accordance with the procedures and time limits applicable to a decision of release.

Evidence seized or preserved contrary to the procedures specified in this Chapter shall be null and void. Investigation measures based thereon shall consequentially be null and void.

Nullity shall not preclude taking into account available information that benefits the investigation, resulting from the seizure or processing, where corroborated by supporting evidence.

The following paragraph is added to Article (51) of Consumer Protection Law No. 659 dated 4/2/2005:

In contracts concluded electronically, the provisions of Articles 33, 34, 35, and 38 of the Electronic Transactions and Personal Data Law must be observed.

The text of Article (55) of the Consumer Protection Law No. 659 dated 2005/2/4 shall be repealed and replaced with the following text:

Notwithstanding any other provision, the consumer who contracts in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter may withdraw from his decision to purchase or lease a good or benefit from the service within a period of ten days running either from the date of contracting with respect to services, or from the date of delivery with respect to goods. However, in the event that a longer period is agreed upon in the contract, the period mentioned in the contract shall then be adopted.

However, the consumer may not exercise the right provided for in the preceding paragraph in the following cases:

1 - If he benefited from the service or used the good before the expiry of the ten-day period.

2 - If the contract concerns goods manufactured upon his request or in accordance with specifications determined by him.

3 - If the contract concerns video tapes, records or compact discs, in the event that their wrapping has been removed.

4 - If the contract concerns the purchase of newspapers, magazines and publications.

5 - If a defect appeared in the good as a result of improper possession thereof by the consumer.

6 - If the contract includes accommodation, transport, catering or entertainment services provided on a specific date or on a specified periodic basis.

7 - If the contract concerns the purchase of a software service over the internet, except in the event that downloading or operation has not occurred.

The text of Article (59) of the Consumer Protection Law No. 659 dated 2005/2/4 shall be repealed and replaced with the following text:

The professional who uses indirect means or electronic means for sale or lease must comply with the provisions of this Law, in particular those relating to deceptive advertising, promotion and public safety.

There shall be added to the members of the Board of Directors of the Lebanese Accreditation Council a member representing the Ministry of Telecommunications, appointed in accordance with the provisions of Article Five of Law No. 572/2004.

The provisions of the Banking Secrecy Law issued on 3/9/1956, the provisions of Article 151 of the Code of Money and Credit, the provisions of Law No. 133 dated 26/10/1999 relating to the missions of the Banque du Liban, the provisions of Law No. 140 dated 27/10/1999 relating to safeguarding the right to secrecy of communications (conducted through any means of communication), and the rules of professional ethics regulated by laws shall be observed when applying the provisions of this Law.

By way of exception to the provisions of Article 20 and the subsequent articles set out in Chapter Four of this Law, the Banque du Liban shall have the authority, with respect to financial and banking operations, to issue:

1 - Authentication certificates relating to electronic signatures for banks and institutions subject to its supervision and to the supervision of the Capital Markets Authority, as well as for institutions, administrations, and bodies with which it deals in accordance with the laws governing its operations.

2 - Accreditation certificates for banks and institutions subject to its supervision and to the supervision of the Capital Markets Authority, in their capacity as authentication service providers for the electronic signatures of their clients.

The Banque du Liban shall establish the technical standards and rules for the procedures provided for in this Article.

Subject to the provisions of Article 64, the details of application of the provisions of this Law shall be determined, where necessary, by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Justice, Economy and Trade, Finance, Industry, and Telecommunications, each within the scope of their respective competence.

Electronic commerce transactions shall be subject to the taxes and duties imposed on non-electronic transactions in accordance with the laws in force. The provisions of Law No. 44 dated 11/11/2008 and its amendments (the Tax Procedures Law) and its amendments shall be observed, particularly with respect to the right of the tax administration to obtain information.
This Law shall enter into force upon the expiry of three months from its publication in the Official Gazette.

For the purposes of applying the provisions of this Law, the following definitions are adopted:

a) Mediation: is an alternative means of dispute resolution in which the parties rely on a neutral third party (the mediator) whose role consists in assisting and encouraging them to communicate and negotiate in order to resolve the dispute that has arisen between them.

b) Judicial mediation: is the mediation resorted to in order to resolve a dispute after it has been referred to the court and at any stage of the proceedings.

c) The mediator: is every natural person to whom the mission of mediation is entrusted, and whose name is entered on the list of mediators in accordance with the criteria provided for in this Law and pursuant to its implementing decrees.

d) The parties: are anyone who has accepted to be a party to the mediation, whether a natural or legal person.

e) Mediation agreement: is every agreement concluded by contract whereby the parties aim to resort to mediation in order to settle an existing dispute or a dispute that may arise subsequently between them.

f) The competent court: is the court seised of the dispute and which refers it to mediation.

g) The referral decision: is a decision issued by the competent court referring the parties to the dispute to mediation to attempt to reach a settlement between them.

h) The mediation centre: is every legal person, institution or body operating on Lebanese territory, accredited by the Ministry of Justice and having among its core duties the administration of the judicial mediation process and the appointment of mediators.

i) The list of mediators: is a list drawn up by the mediation centre, in which the names of the mediators are entered according to the criteria for entry and striking off provided for in this Law and pursuant to its implementing decrees. This list must be adopted when selecting a mediator within the framework of judicial mediation.

j) The settlement agreement: is the agreement reached as a result of mediation as a partial or total resolution of the existing dispute and signed by the parties.

k) Mediation expenses: are the administrative fees due to the centre, and the fees due to the mediator for the judicial mediation process.

Mediation may be conducted in all types of disputes that are capable of conciliation, in a manner that does not conflict with public policy and the mandatory laws in force.

All judicial mediation operations shall be subject to the provisions of this Law.

The competent court may issue a decision referring the dispute to mediation at any stage of the action, whether upon its own proposal coupled with the consent of the parties, upon their request, or in enforcement of a mediation agreement.

The competent court must state in the decision of judicial referral to mediation the following information:

A. The consent of the parties to resort to judicial mediation.

B. The name of the appointed mediation centre.

C. The subject matter of the mediation.

The parties undertake to provide the appointed mediation centre with their brief observations on the dispute referred to mediation, within three working days from the date of the referral decision.
Referral decisions issued by the competent court shall not be subject to any ordinary or extraordinary means of recourse.

Upon the issuance of the referral decision, all statutory and judicial time limits shall be suspended, and shall not resume running until the termination of the mediation, provided that the competent court retains the power to take the necessary measures to protect the rights of the parties.

The mediation centre shall be appointed by agreement between the parties from the list established by the Ministry of Justice. Where the parties fail to agree on the appointment of the centre during the trial hearing in which consent to the referral was given, the competent court shall appoint the mediation centre during the same hearing and the court registry shall notify the referral decision to the parties and the mediation centre.

The appointed mediation centre shall notify the competent court in writing of its acceptance or refusal to organise the mediation, within four (4) working days from the date it is notified of the referral decision.

Where the parties fail to agree on the appointment of a mediator within three (3) working days starting from the date of the mediation centre's acceptance, the latter shall appoint one or more mediators from among the names listed on its roster of mediators, within a time limit of ten (10) working days from the date they are notified of the referral decision.

The mediator shall sign a statement confirming his impartiality and independence towards the parties and the subject matter of the dispute within three (3) working days starting from the date of his appointment. He shall also, during the course of the mediation process, inform the centre by means of a written declaration of any facts or circumstances, which have arisen or may arise, that may lead one of the parties to question his impartiality or independence. In both cases, the mediation centre shall notify this declaration to the parties in due form, and invite them to submit their observations within three (3) working days from the date of notification.

In the event that any of the parties objects to the mediator and requests his recusal, or in the event that the mediator is unable to continue his mission for any reason whatsoever during any stage of the mediation process, the centre shall appoint another mediator within a period of three (3) working days from the date of the objection to the mediator or of the notification of his inability to continue his mission. The same provisions of Articles 120 and 121 of the Code of Civil Procedure relating to the grounds for requesting the recusal of a judge or his withdrawal shall apply to the mediator.

The centres to be accredited by the Ministry of Justice shall be required to fulfil the following requirements:

A - That every mediator accredited and registered with them on the list of mediators:

- Has not been convicted of a felony or a dishonourable misdemeanour, and that no disciplinary decision has been issued against him by a professional syndicate,

- Holds a university degree in any field whatsoever,

- Has completed a training course on mediation at an institute or centre accredited by the Ministry of Justice of no less than forty-five (45) hours of in-person lessons of role-playing followed by an assessment,

- Has practised the role of mediator in at least two civil, commercial or social mediation cases during the twelve (12) months preceding the possibility of appointment as a principal mediator. One of these mediation processes may have been conducted as a role-playing exercise,

- Is subject to continuous professional development specific to mediation through courses and lectures of no less than six (6) hours per year;

B- That they adopt the rules of professional conduct for the mediator attached to this Law (Annex No. 1)

C- That they have an integrated system for assessment and dealing with complaints;

D- That they have a system for reviewing the list of mediators and the requirements for continuous professional development;

E- That they are equipped with all the administrative and logistical facilities required to carry out the mediation process effectively.

Every mediator who does not meet the criteria mentioned in this Law shall be struck off the list of mediators.

The mediator shall determine, in consultation with the parties, the date and time of the sessions, provided that the duration of the mediation does not exceed thirty (30) working days starting from the date of the referral decision. The mediation centre may extend the duration of the mediation by thirty (30) additional working days by a decision thereof based on a written request signed by all the parties and the mediator, provided that the centre notifies the court of the extension decision within three (3) working days from the date of this decision.

Judicial mediation shall terminate in any of the following cases:

A. The signing of a settlement agreement by the parties.

B. The agreement of the parties and the mediator to terminate the judicial mediation.

C. The declaration by any of the parties, by virtue of a written notice notified to the mediator or the Centre, of his unwillingness to pursue the judicial mediation.

D. The declaration by the mediator, by virtue of a written notice notified to the Centre, of the futility of the judicial mediation and the absence of any possibility of reaching a solution.

E. The absence of any of the parties from two consecutive judicial mediation sessions without a legitimate excuse. In this case, the mediator shall notify the Centre by virtue of a written notice of the termination of the judicial mediation for this reason.

F. The expiry of the time limit for judicial mediation and its non-extension in due form.

The mediator shall provide the mediation centre with a written report on the outcome of the judicial mediation within three (3) working days starting from the date of termination of the judicial mediation for any reason whatsoever. Thereupon, the Centre shall notify the parties and the court of the outcome of the judicial mediation within a maximum time limit of five (5) working days from the date of its receipt of the mediator's report. In the event that the dispute remains standing, the competent court shall restore the lawsuit to the pleading schedule.

Upon the termination of the mediation and the reaching by the parties of a settlement agreement, the competent court shall homologate this agreement and grant it the executory formula upon the request of all the parties or one of them in the light of the clauses of the settlement agreement submitted to it. The request for homologation shall be decided through non-contentious proceedings, and the rules relating to the expedited enforcement of judgments shall apply to the decision taken in respect thereof.

The decision homologating the settlement agreement shall not be subject to any of the ordinary or extraordinary means of recourse.

Third-party opposition may be lodged against the decision granting the executory formula before the competent court in accordance with the provisions of Article 681, paragraph 1, of the Code of Civil Procedure.
The parties shall pay the expenses of the mediation in full and directly to the mediation centre to which the dispute is referred, prior to commencing the mediation process.

All laws, decrees and decisions that conflict with the provisions of this Law or are inconsistent with its content are repealed, with the exception of the provisions of the Lebanese Labour Law promulgated on 23 September 1946 and all its amendments.

The details of implementation of the provisions of this Law shall be determined, where necessary, by implementing decrees taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice, provided that they are issued within a time limit of six (6) months from the date of publication of this Law.
This Law shall be published in the Official Gazette and shall enter into force upon the expiry of a period of six (6) months following the date of its publication.
An Embassy of the Lebanese Republic shall be established in the Kingdom of Denmark in Copenhagen.

Two Grade Three posts in the Foreign Service shall be added to the establishment of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants specified pursuant to Table No. 1 annexed to the draft law brought into force pursuant to Decree No. 1306 dated 18/6/1971 and its amendments (Regulations of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants).
This Decree shall be published and notified where needed.

The parties shall attend the mediation sessions in person or through a legal representative vested with the authority to waive and settle if they are legal persons.

The parties shall be entitled to the assistance of advisers to attend the mediation and support them during the course thereof. The mediator may limit the number of advisers attending the mediation with a given party.

Mediation sessions shall be deemed confidential, and persons who are not concerned with the dispute and who do not represent them, in accordance with what is set forth above, shall not be entitled to attend them.

The mediator shall carry out his mission with independence, neutrality and impartiality, and shall work through mutual dialogue to assist the parties in identifying their contentious issues, their interests and their needs, within a framework of respect and equality among them, so that they may reach a solution established of their own free will. The mediator shall not provide a solution to the dispute, nor is he vested with the power of investigation; however, for the necessities of the mediation mission, and with the approval of all the parties, he may hear third parties with their consent.

The mediator shall be entitled to hold private sessions with each party to the mediation. He shall not be entitled to disclose to the other party any information exchanged in the private session except after obtaining the approval of the party who disclosed it.

In multi-party disputes, and with the approval of the competent court, the parties may agree to continue the mediation proceedings when one of them refrains from participating therein, provided that such refraining does not affect the course thereof and the resolution of the dispute among them.

The parties, the mediator, every participant in the mediation, and the mediation centre are prohibited from disclosing any information raised during the mediation proceedings except with the approval of all the parties.
The parties shall participate in the mediation process in good faith and with transparency, and shall cooperate effectively.

In the event that the mediator breaches the conditions of confidentiality, independence, neutrality and impartiality provided for in this Law, the aggrieved party shall have recourse to the mediation centre to take the necessary disciplinary measures against the mediator.

He may also petition the competent court to claim compensation for the damages sustained by him. The court shall apply the rules of procedure followed before the judge of urgent matters when examining this petition, and its decision shall be subject to appeal in accordance with the rules of procedure followed in appealing judgments rendered by the urgent matters judiciary.

The text of Article 26 of the Code of Commerce is repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 26:

Companies having a principal office in Lebanon must be registered in the Commercial Register having jurisdiction over the district of their office, and the legal representative of the company must apply for registration within the month following its formation:

The applicant for registration shall submit to the registry of the court a copy of the instrument of formation and an abstract thereof written in duplicate, bearing the stamps and his signature, and containing in particular the following particulars:

1- The first name and surname of each of the partners and shareholders, the nationality of each of them, and the date and place of his birth.

2- The commercial name or style of the company.

3- The object of the company.

4- The places where the company has branches or agencies, whether in Lebanon or abroad

5- The names and the partners or other persons authorised to manage the company or to sign on its behalf.

6- The capital of the company and the sums or securities required to be contributed by the shareholders or limited partners, as well as the value of what is contributed to the company, whether in cash or in other property.

7- The date of commencement of the company and the date of its termination.

8- The type of the company.

9- The minimum capital of the company if it is of variable capital.

10- The lease contract of the premises in which the company will carry on its business, or a document evidencing its ownership thereof, or a document evidencing its election of domicile with its legal representative, or any legal instrument permitted by the laws in force justifying the occupation of the company's office.

11- The identity of the beneficial owner or owners.

The text of Article 27 of the Code of Commerce is repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 27:

There must also be mentioned in the Commercial Register:

1- Every amendment or change to the matters required to be registered pursuant to the preceding Article.

2- The first name, surname, date and place of birth, and nationality of each of the managers of the company's business, the members of its board of directors, and its directors appointed for the duration of its existence.

As for the application for registration, it shall be submitted by the legal representative of the company at the time when registration is required.

3- The exploited patents of invention and the factory marks (Marque de fabrique) and trade marks used by the company.

4- Judgments or decisions ordering the dissolution of the company or its annulment.

5- Judgments or decisions declaring the bankruptcy of the company or homologating the preventive composition and the resolutions relating thereto.

The proposed law amending the Code of Land Commerce promulgated by Legislative Decree No. 304 dated 24/12/1942 and its amendments, adding new provisions thereto, and amending Article 844 of the Code of Obligations and Contracts, as amended by the Joint Parliamentary Committees, has been ratified,
This Law shall be published in the Official Gazette and shall enter into force three months after the date of its publication.

The text of Article 16 of the Code of Commerce is hereby repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 16:

Every natural or legal person having the status of a merchant must keep, manually or by means of a secured digital application whose specifications conform to the standards determined by a decree issued upon the proposal of the Ministers of Justice and Finance, the following documents:

- The journal, in which financial transactions are recorded day by day at a minimum, or in which the results of such transactions are recorded monthly if the nature of the business prevents this, provided that in this case all documents enabling a day-by-day audit thereof are retained.

- The general ledger, for opening and monitoring accounts.

He must also conduct an annual inventory of all the elements of his enterprise and close all accounts in order to draw up the balance sheet and the "income statement", and the documents relating thereto must be drawn up and preserved throughout the period provided for in Article 19 of the Code of Commerce.

- The keeping of commercial books by means of the digital application prescribed in this Article shall become mandatory two years after the date of promulgation of this Law.

The text of Article 18 of the Code of Commerce is hereby repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 18:

Manually kept books must be numbered, initialled and signed by the President of the Court of First Instance in the towns where this Court sits.

The text of Article 42 of the Code of Commerce is repealed and replaced with the following text:

New Article 42:

The rules provided for by the Code of Obligations and Contracts with respect to the company contract shall apply to commercial companies provided that such rules are not explicitly or implicitly contrary to the rules of this Code.

Without prejudice to the rights of third parties acting in good faith, if the number of partners or shareholders in commercial companies of various types falls below the number required by law for each of them, the dissolution of the company must be declared by a resolution of the remaining partners within a period of three months from the occurrence of the aforementioned ground unless rectification takes place.

The court shall, upon the request of any interested party, declare the dissolution of the company after the expiry of the three months granted for rectification.

The text of Article 43 of the Code of Commerce is repealed and replaced with the following text:

New Article 43:

All commercial companies, except joint ventures, must be evidenced by a written contract; however, third parties may, where necessary, prove by all means the existence of the company or the existence of any provision relating thereto.

All companies incorporated in Lebanon must have a head office therein, and they shall be deemed of Lebanese nationality notwithstanding any provision to the contrary.

The text of Article 45 of the Code of Commerce is repealed and replaced with the following text:

New Article 45:

All commercial companies - except joint ventures - shall enjoy legal personality.

The modification of the form of the company shall not lead to the creation of a new legal personality therefor; rather, the legal personality shall remain in existence and the new company shall continue with the same legal personality that existed prior to the conversion. This modification shall not be effective vis-à-vis third parties except as of the registration in the Commercial Register and the expiry of a period of one month from the publication of this modification in the Official Gazette and in a local daily newspaper designated by the judge supervising the Commercial Register.

Persons who have acted in the name of a company under incorporation prior to its acquisition of legal personality shall be deemed personally and jointly and severally liable among themselves for the acts performed unless the company assumes such acts after its incorporation, in which case those acts shall be deemed ratified by the company since their occurrence.

The text of Article 77 of the Code of Commerce is repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 77:

A joint-stock company is a company whose capital is divided into shares, that is, negotiable securities, which operates under a trade name and is formed among a number of persons not less than three who subscribe for shares, and who are liable for the debts of the company only to the extent of their contributions.

The text of Article 78 of the Code of Commerce is repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 78:

Every joint-stock company, whatever its object may be, shall be subject to the Code of Commerce and its usages.

One third of the capital of joint-stock companies whose object is the operation of a public utility or a public service must consist of registered shares held by Lebanese natural person shareholders or by companies whose capital consists of parts or registered shares wholly owned by Lebanese persons and whose articles of association prohibit the assignment of the parts or shares therein except to Lebanese persons.

Any assignment of these shares in breach of the provisions of the preceding paragraph shall be null and void ab initio.

The text of Article 80 of the Code of Commerce is repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 80:

Without prejudice to the provisions of the laws and regulations that subject the exercise of certain activities to prior authorisation, the incorporation of joint-stock companies shall not require authorisation.

The articles of association of a joint-stock company and every subsequent amendment thereto must be deposited and registered with any notary public on Lebanese territory.

The text of Article 81 of the Code of Commerce is repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 81:

If the invitation is addressed to the public to subscribe to the capital of the company, the founders must publish in the Official Gazette and in two newspapers, one of which is a local daily and the second an economic newspaper, a prospectus containing the name, signature and address of each of them and including, in particular, the denomination of the company, its head office and the offices of its branches, its object, its duration, the amount of its capital, the price of the shares and the amount thereof payable immediately, the value of the contributions in kind, the fixed interest clause, the conditions for the distribution of profits, if any, and the number of members of the board of directors, their remuneration stipulated in the company's articles of association, and their powers.

The particulars contained in the prospectus must also be inserted in the personal subscription document, the share certificate, the posted notices, the broadcasts and the circulars, with reference to the issues of the newspapers in which the prospectus was published.

The text of Article 82 of the Code of Commerce is repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 82:

Every violation of the provisions of the preceding Article shall entail the payment of a fine from two million to ten million Lebanese Pounds, and the court shall have the right, where necessary, to annul the subscriptions concluded.

The text of Article 84 of the Code of Commerce is repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 84:

The minimum price per single share is one thousand Lebanese Pounds, and every subscriber shall pay in advance at least one-quarter of the nominal value of each share subscribed for by him.

The text of Article 85 of the Code of Commerce is repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 85:

The founders shall deposit the sums paid by the subscribers prior to the definitive incorporation of the company in one of the banks operating in Lebanon in the form of an account opened in the name of the company under incorporation, together with the list of subscribers and the sum paid by each of them.

These sums shall be withdrawn after the incorporation after the incorporation of the company under the signature of the person or persons appointed pursuant to the company's articles of association, following the production of a certified copy of the articles of association and of the minutes of the constituent assembly.

In the event of failure to deposit, or the withdrawal of all or part of the deposited sums, or the disposal thereof prior to the completion of the incorporation of the company, the offenders shall be punished by a fine equivalent to ten percent of the value of the sums not deposited, withdrawn or disposed of, and they shall be liable, where applicable, to the penalties for breach of trust or other offences to which their act applies, in addition to the civil liability incurred by them.

If the company is not incorporated within a period of six months from the date of signing the articles of association before the Notary Public, every subscriber shall have the right to apply to the Judge of Urgent Matters for the appointment of a provisional administrator entrusted with withdrawing the sums and returning them to the subscribers after deducting the distribution expenses, where applicable.

In the event that the founders agree, even prior to the expiry of the six-month period mentioned in the preceding paragraph, not to proceed with the process of incorporating the company and prior to any subscription by shareholders, they may unanimously take the decision to withdraw the sums deposited with the bank, provided that they produce a letter duly certified before the Notary Public with whom the articles of association were deposited, cancelling the company's articles of association deposited with the Notary Public, in addition to producing proof of payment of the fees and taxes due on the company's articles of association, where applicable.

Article 86 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 86:

The validity of the valuation of contributions in kind shall be subject to the assessment of one or more experts appointed by the president of the court of the district in which the head office of the company is located, pursuant to a decision issued by him at the request of the founders.

It is prohibited to grant special advantages to any person in the articles of association of the company.

Article 91 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 91:

The completion of the aforementioned formalities shall not preclude a subsequent action for liability, which may be brought jointly and severally within five years from the date of incorporation of the company against the founders, the contributors in kind, the first members of the board of directors, and the experts, when a gross overvaluation of the contributions in kind becomes evident.

Article 94 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 94:

If a joint-stock company is unlawfully incorporated, any person having standing and interest may, within a period of five years running from the date on which the defect occurred, serve formal notice upon it to complete the omitted formality.

If the company does not proceed within one month to carry out the rectification formality, any person having standing and interest may apply for a judgment declaring the nullity of the company.

The shareholders may not invoke the nullity of the company against third parties.

The annulled company shall be liquidated as a de facto company.

Article 95 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 95:

If the incorporation of the company is unlawful, the shareholders and third parties shall have the right to bring, in addition to the action for nullity, an action for joint and several liability against the founders, the first members of the board of directors, and the first supervisory commissioners, as well as against the contributors in kind and the experts if the verification formalities were not carried out truthfully and faithfully.

The establishment of liability requires proof of the existence of the causal link between the defect in incorporation and the damage suffered by the plaintiff. The action for liability shall be brought within the same period prescribed for the action for nullity.

Article 96 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 96:

Persons who have delivered, even in good faith, to subscribers definitive share certificates of an unlawfully incorporated joint-stock company, as well as persons who have sold or participated in the sale of these shares or officially published their price, shall be punished by a fine of two million to twenty million Lebanese pounds. It is required for the declaration of liability that at least the defect in incorporation be apparent.

The text of Article 98 of the Code of Commerce is repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 98:

The members of the board of directors must, after the incorporation of the company, carry out the initial formalities relating to publication by way of filing and registration with the competent Trade Registry Secretariat, during the month following the incorporation, on pain of a fine determined by the judge supervising the Trade Registry, imposed on the company and ranging between five hundred thousand and one million Lebanese pounds.

The formalities mentioned in the preceding paragraph may be completed through the electronic means specified by the Minister of Justice, provided that they are carried out exclusively by electronic means two years after the entry into force of this Law. Electronic publication on the website of the Trade Registry shall be available for inspection by the public.

The text of Article 100 of the Code of Commerce is repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 100:

The company is, moreover, subject to a form of continuous publication:

The articles of association of the company must be posted in its offices.

Every person shall have the right to request a certified true copy thereof in return for a moderate fee.

The name of the company must be stated on all its printed, handwritten and electronic papers, with the indication that it is a joint-stock company and with the specification of the amount of its capital and the portion thereof that has been paid up.

The text of Article 101 of the Code of Commerce is repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 101:

The members of the board of directors must deposit with the competent Secretariat of the Commercial Register each year, within two months from the date of the general assembly's approval of the financial statements, and without this deposit exceeding the thirty-first of December of the current year, the following documents:

1- The report of the auditors to which are attached the individual financial statements for the elapsed year prepared in accordance with the accounting standards in force, in particular the balance sheet, the income statement, the statement of changes in shareholders' equity and the notes to the financial statements.

2- The report of the auditors to which are attached the consolidated financial statements for the elapsed year prepared for the accounting standards in force.

3- The special report of the auditors in accordance with the provisions of Article 158 of this Law.

4- The report of the board of directors on the business of the company for the elapsed year.

5- The report of the board of directors in accordance with the provisions of Article 158 of this Law.

6- The attendance sheet and the minutes of the meeting of the general assembly approving the financial statements for the elapsed year and the report of the board of directors for the elapsed year and the special reports relating to the transactions subject to the provisions of Article 158 of this Law where applicable, provided that the said report includes the following information:

- The result of the elapsed year.

- The accumulated results, in particular those requiring that any measure be taken pursuant to Article 216 of this Law.

- The names of the members of the elected board of directors whenever its election falls due and any modification occurring thereto.

- The appointment of the auditors whenever the appointment falls due.

A copy of the documents mentioned in this Article may be obtained from the Commercial Register at the applicant's expense.

The formalities mentioned in this Article may be completed through the electronic means determined by the Minister of Justice, provided that publication on the website of the Commercial Register after two years from the entry into force of this Law shall be mandatory and available to the public.
