The text of Article 102 of the Code of Commerce is repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 102:

The judge supervising the Commercial Register shall fine the company an amount of one hundred thousand Lebanese pounds annually for each document that is not duly deposited.

In order to deposit and register the documents provided for in Article 101 within the time limits provided for in the Article, the company shall be exempted from a clearance certificate issued by the National Social Security Fund.

The text of Article 110 of the Code of Commerce is repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 110:

In principle, all shareholders in the same company must have the same rights and participate in the same benefits.

However, in all cases where the articles of association of the company do not provide for an express prohibition, preference shares may be created pursuant to a resolution of an extraordinary assembly deliberating thereon in the manner set forth below.

These shares grant their holders a right of priority either in receiving certain shares of the profits, or in the recovery of capital, or in both of these advantages together, or any other pecuniary benefit.

Article 115 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 115:

The company may redeem its capital by allocating an amount of its profits to a special reserve or to amortisation, both prepared for this purpose.

Redemption shall take place in accordance with the methods provided for in the articles of association of the company or the methods approved by the general assembly.

When redemption takes place, the redeemed shares shall be replaced by shares called enjoyment shares (jouissance), and these shares grant their holders the privileges of circulating shares except for the interest specified in the articles of association of the company and the nominal amount of the shares upon the dissolution of the company.

The text of Article 104 of the Code of Commerce is repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 104:

Shares are equal, indivisible fractions of the capital of the company represented by negotiable instruments which shall be registered.

The text of Article 107 of the Code of Commerce is repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 107:

Every distribution of fictitious dividends shall render the members of the board of directors civilly liable towards any person who suffers harm therefrom, and shall also render the supervisory commissioners liable in the same manner with the members of the board of directors, unless the supervisory commissioners prove that they committed no fault in supervision.

The members of the board of directors and the supervisory commissioners shall be criminally liable if the dividends are distributed without a balance sheet or pursuant to a fraudulent inventory, balance sheet or financial statements, and they shall be punished with the penalty for fraud or with any other penalty provided for by law.

The text of Article 108 of the Code of Commerce is repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 108:

Shareholders who received those dividends of profit shall not be bound to return them unless their bad faith or their commission of a gross fault equivalent to deceit is proven.

As for the action for recovery which the company, its creditors or any of the shareholders are entitled to bring against them, it shall bind them to return the amount which they received without right, together with interest thereon from the day of payment.

This action shall lapse by prescription upon the expiry of five years from the date of distribution.

The text of Article 109 of the Code of Commerce is repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 109:

Amounts distributed pursuant to the provision relating to fixed interest (Interets fixes) paid to shareholders under any circumstance whatsoever and included among the charges of the company shall not be deemed fictitious profits.

However, this provision shall not be lawful unless the following two conditions are met: namely, that the rate of interest does not exceed four per cent and that the period of application of the provision is five years at most.

This provision must be published by depositing it in the company's file at the Commercial Register Secretariat, on pain of nullity.

Article 116 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 116:

Every shareholder shall be entitled to attend the various meetings convened to incorporate the company and to conduct its business, and shall, in principle, have upon voting a number of votes equal to the number of his shares.

If the company is notified of the existence of a right of usufruct over specified shares, it shall be obliged to notify the holder of the right of usufruct of all notices of meetings and matters without exception, including resolutions to distribute any economic benefits.

The holder of the right of usufruct of the share alone shall have the right to attend ordinary general meetings and to vote therein, and the bare owner shall be the person authorised to be notified of all notices of meetings, documents and all matters without exception, including being notified of resolutions to distribute any economic benefits.

The holder of the right of usufruct and the bare owner may agree to derogate from the provisions of the preceding paragraph in accordance with the manner they deem fit, provided that a contract is signed between them and subject to notifying the company thereof and publishing it and in the Commercial Register.

In the event of co-ownership of shares, all co-owners must choose one person from among themselves or a third party to attend ordinary and extraordinary general meetings and to vote therein. If they fail to agree on the appointment of one person, the President of the competent Court of First Instance within the jurisdiction of which the company's head office is located shall appoint a representative of the co-owners, upon the request of any of the owners, pursuant to a decision enforceable on an expedited basis, issued in accordance with summary procedure and after hearing the remaining owners. The appointed representative shall continue to perform his duties until the convening of the annual general meeting to approve the accounts for the President of the Court to renew the appointment in accordance with the same procedures.

Amendment of Article 117 to read as follows:

New Article 117:

Provided that fully paid-up shares which have remained with a single owner for at least two years prior to the notice convening each meeting shall each carry two votes.

With regard to the aforementioned period, the shares shall be deemed to have belonged to the same owner when they have been acquired by way of inheritance, gift or bequest.

Extraordinary meetings may, by unanimous vote of the shareholders, resolve to abolish the double vote provided for above.

The text of the first and second paragraphs of this Article shall not apply to companies incorporated after the promulgation of this Law.

Article 121 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 121:

If the called-up value of the price of the share is not paid, the company shall have the right, after serving notice upon the defaulting shareholder, to sell the share and charge to his account the expenses and losses resulting from the sale, and if the price at which the share is sold is less than the amount called up, the shareholder shall remain bound to pay the difference, jointly and severally with the shareholders who acquired the share before him.

All those who acquired the share before him shall remain jointly and severally liable for the unpaid amount for a period of two years only from the date of transfer.

In the event that there is a usufructuary and a bare owner for a single share, the bare owner shall be bound to make payment in accordance with Articles 119, 120 and 121 of this Law, except where there is an agreement to the contrary between them duly notified to the board of directors of the company, in accordance with the provisions of Article 116 of this Law.

Article 118 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 118:

Subject to the restrictions relating to shares in kind, every shareholder may freely assign his shares to another person, and such person shall succeed him in his rights and obligations in the capacity of a shareholder.

However, a provision may be inserted in the company's articles of association stipulating that pre-emption in purchase shall belong to the shareholders, or to a group of them, or to the company itself, provided that this right is exercised in accordance with the time limit and the price-fixing mechanism provided for in the company's articles of association. However, the exercise of this right may not be abused by rendering the share practically non-negotiable or by inflicting gross prejudice upon the shareholder.

Where there is a usufructuary and a bare owner of the same share, the bare owner alone shall be entitled to exercise the right of pre-emption where applicable.

The company may not exercise the right of pre-emption stipulated in its favour except out of its free reserve funds.

A company whose shares are listed on the financial markets may also purchase, out of the free reserve funds available to it, shares issued by it, provided that their value does not exceed a percentage of the total of its shares to be determined in accordance with the regulations governing the Capital Markets Law.

Article 119 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 119:

The holder of a share the price of which has not been paid in full shall be bound to comply with the request of the board of directors to pay the balance of the price or a part thereof, in accordance with the mechanism and conditions provided for in the resolution containing the call for payment.

All those who acquired the share before him shall remain, for a period of two years only from the date of the assignment, jointly and severally liable for the unpaid amount.

Every provision in the company's articles of association or every resolution contrary to the provisions of this Article shall be deemed absolutely null and void.

Article 120 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 120:

A former shareholder who has been compelled to pay the balance or a part of the price of the share which he assigned shall be subrogated to the rights of the company and to its right of action against all those who acquired the share after him.

In all cases, the former shareholder shall have a right of recourse against the shareholder who acquired the share after him.

Article 124 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 124:

Subject to the rules applicable to real estate credit companies, debentures may not be issued for an amount exceeding twice the existing capital of the company according to the financial statement audited by the auditors and approved by the general meeting, provided that its date does not go back more than six months from the date of issue of the debentures.

Article 144 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 144:

A joint-stock company shall be managed by a board of directors composed of at least three members and at most twelve members; subject to what may be provided for by special laws governing certain joint-stock companies, the number of Lebanese nationals on the board of directors must not be less than one-third.

The board of directors must appoint one of its members to the chairmanship.

The chairman of the board of directors shall not require a work permit if he is a non-Lebanese national who is not resident in Lebanon.

Article 145 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 145:

The members of the board of directors shall receive their remuneration either by the fixing of an annual sum for them, or by the fixing of a lump sum for each meeting they attend, or by the allocation of a proportional rate of the net profits, or by a method combining these various benefits.

As for the profits from which the proportional rate allocated to the members of the board of directors is taken, they must in principle include only the net proceeds of the operation that constitutes the object of the company.

Accordingly, the income of the securities portfolio may not be merged therein except by way of exception and pursuant to a special resolution passed by the general meeting and renewed every year.

Article 146 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 146:

The ordinary general assembly shall elect the members of the board of directors, provided that the first members may be appointed in the articles of association of the company.

In the event that there is a holder of a right of usufruct and a holder of bare ownership for a single share, the holder of the bare ownership alone shall be entitled to be a member of the board of directors, except in the event of the existence of a contrary servitude between the holder of the bare ownership and the holder of the right of usufruct, in accordance with what is provided for in Article 116 of this Law.

In the event that there are co-owners in common of a single share, the provisions of Article 116 of this Law shall also apply, and consequently only one person representing the co-owners in common shall be eligible for membership of the board of directors.

In the period falling between two annual assemblies, if the number of acting members falls, by reason of death and resignation or other reasons, below half of the minimum number fixed in the articles of association or below three, the remaining members must convene the general assembly within two months at most to fill the vacant positions.

Article 147 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 147:

The ordinary general assembly shall elect the members of the board of directors from among the shareholders or from among non-shareholders.

Article 148 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 148:

No person may be chosen as a member of the board of directors if he has been declared bankrupt and has not been rehabilitated for at least ten years, or if he has been convicted in Lebanon or abroad less than ten years ago for committing or attempting to commit a felony or a misdemeanour, and the same conditions shall apply to the representatives of legal persons on the board of directors.

Article 149 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 149:

The members of the board of directors appointed pursuant to the articles of association of the company shall have a term of office of five years at most, whereas those who are appointed by a resolution of the assembly of shareholders shall have a term of office of three years at most, and they may be re-elected, and the articles of association of the company may include special provisions for the partial renewal of the body of the board of directors.

Article 152 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 152:

Every change in the composition of the board of directors must be published through depositing the minutes with the competent commercial register by the care of the members of the board of directors.

The notice of service whereby the company takes a year of the resignation of one of the members of the board of directors shall also be registered in the same commercial register.

In both cases, the publication or registration shall take place without the need to produce any other document of any kind whatsoever, whether official or unofficial.

Article 153 shall be amended to take the following form:

New Article 153:

The management of the company shall be vested in the Chairman of the Board of Directors - General Manager, elected by the board of directors from among the natural persons of whom the board is composed.

The articles of association of the company may include the possibility of separating the chairmanship of the board of directors on the one hand and the management of the company on the other hand.

The board of directors shall appoint, from among natural persons, a General Manager from among the shareholders or from among non-shareholders.

It shall be for the Chairman of the Board of Directors - General Manager, or for the General Manager exclusively in the event of separation between the two positions, to propose to the board the appointment of one or more Assistant General Managers; the board of directors shall appoint the Assistant General Manager or Assistant General Managers from outside the board of directors and from among the shareholders or non-shareholders, provided that they are natural persons.

The Assistant General Manager shall perform his duties under the personal liability of the authority that proposed his appointment.

Where the Chairman is in a state that temporarily prevents him from performing his duties, he may delegate all or part of them to one of the members of the board of directors, provided that such delegation must always be for a fixed period.

However, if the Chairman is in a state in which he cannot permanently perform his duties, the board of directors may consider him to have resigned and elect another in his stead.

Members of the board of directors may occupy managerial positions in the company in consideration of a remuneration determined by the board of directors; however, they shall not benefit from the provisions of the Labour Law unless they have been employees of the company for at least two years upon assuming office.

Article 154 shall be amended and shall read as follows:

New Article 154:

No person may hold the chairmanship of a board of directors in more than six companies in Lebanon, nor may any person be a general manager or an assistant general manager in more than three companies whose head office is in Lebanon.

A natural person may not be a member of more than eight boards of directors of companies whose head office is in Lebanon.

Holding the chairmanship and membership on boards of directors belonging to different insurance companies having one trade name is considered as one chairmanship or membership.

In the event of a violation of the provisions of this Article, every interested party may serve notice upon the violator and the company to comply therewith. If the violator does not regularise his status within a period of two months after being notified of the formal notice, he shall be deemed to have resigned ipso jure upon the expiry of this period, and every interested party may, in the event that the violation continues, request a judgment annulling the resolutions adopted by the board of directors in the presence of the violator.

Neither the violator nor the company may invoke the nullity of these resolutions against third parties.

In all cases, the violator must refund to the company the remuneration and rewards he received since the occurrence of the violation.

Article 155 shall be amended to read in the following form:

New Article 155:

The chairman of the board of directors and the general manager shall not be deemed merchants except in respect of the following matters:

The competent court may rule against them, or against either of them, the forfeiture of the rights which the law has attached to bankruptcy if the company goes bankrupt and its bankruptcy results from fraud or grave faults in the management of the affairs of the company.

If the functions of the chairman have been delegated in whole or in part to one of the persons specified in Article 153, the person to whom the functions of the chairman have been delegated shall bear, in proportion to what has been delegated to him of those functions, the liabilities specified in this Article in place of the chairman of the board of directors.

Article 156 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 156:

For the resolutions of the Board to be lawful, at least half of the members must attend the meeting or be represented therein, and a member may represent only one member.

The company's articles of association may, within the framework of calculating the majority and the quorum at meetings of the Board, provide for the possibility of considering members who participate in meetings of the Board of Directors through remote audiovisual communication technology or other technical means, the conditions of which shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Justice, as present at the meeting, provided that verification of the identity of the connected member is ensured and the security, continuity and reliability of the connection and the effective participation of the connected member in the discussions are ensured, provided that the company's articles of association set out the mechanism to be adopted in this framework, and the articles of association may also provide for prohibiting the issuance and certain resolutions by a Board of Directors in which members participate remotely through the aforementioned communication technology.

Recourse to the use of any of these technologies is prohibited in the case of preparing and approving the annual accounts, the annual financial statements and the reports on the past year mentioned in Article 101.

The content of the remote communication in all meetings of the Board of Directors must be recorded, such that the recordings shall be considered an integral part of the minutes of the meeting and shall be kept therewith.

Article 157 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 157:

The Board of Directors shall have broad powers to execute the resolutions of the General Assembly and to carry out all acts required by the operation of the enterprise in the ordinary course which are not considered part of day-to-day business. These powers shall have no limit or reservations other than what is provided for in the law or in the company's articles of association.

The Board of Directors may delegate some of its powers to the Chairman of the Board of Directors-General Manager in the event that no General Manager is appointed, or to the General Manager, for a short and specified period, provided that such delegation is subject to publication in the Commercial Register.

The Chairman of the Board of Directors-General Manager shall have all powers to represent the company before third parties, execute the resolutions of the Board of Directors, and conduct the day-to-day business of the company as set forth in the articles of association or custom, under the supervision and control of the Board of Directors.

In the event that a General Manager is appointed in accordance with the provisions of Article 153 of this Law, the Chairman of the Board of Directors shall have the authority of general supervision over the course of business in the company, without interfering in day-to-day business, and he shall chair the Board of Directors and issue general directives to the General Manager, without these being binding on the latter. In this case, the General Manager shall have all powers to represent the company before third parties, execute the resolutions of the Board of Directors, and conduct the day-to-day business of the company as set forth in the articles of association or custom, under the supervision and control of the Board of Directors.

Article 158 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 158:

1- The members and the Chairman of the Board of Directors, the Assistant General Manager, and every shareholder holding directly or indirectly voting rights of five percent (5%) in the company's capital, shall be subject to the prior authorisation of the Board of Directors regarding every contract, agreement or commitment intended to be concluded with the company, whether the said contract, agreement or commitment is conducted directly or indirectly or under the guise of a third party.

None of those mentioned above shall be entitled to participate in the vote on the resolution granting or refusing the authorisation relating to him, and the votes of those mentioned above shall not be counted within the quorum for attendance or voting when discussing the said authorisation.

Contracts, agreements and commitments whose subject matter consists of ordinary operations between the company and its customers shall be exempted from this obligation and from the provisions of authorisation.

2- Every agreement between the company and another company shall be subject to the prior authorisation of the Board of Directors if any of the persons mentioned in the first paragraph of this Article is:

a- A partner holding directly or indirectly voting rights exceeding five percent (5%) in the capital of that company.

b- Or a general partner or an authorised partner in that company regardless of the percentage of his shares in its capital in the event that it is a general partnership or a limited partnership.

c- Or a manager of that company or a member of its board of directors.

Such person shall not be entitled to participate in the vote on the resolution granting or refusing the authorisation relating to that company, and his vote shall not be counted within the quorum for attendance or voting when discussing the authorisation.

3- A person to whom one of the cases mentioned in the two paragraphs above applies must inform the Board of Directors thereof immediately, in writing and in detail.

4- The Board of Directors must.

a- Examine the authorisations of the contracts, agreements and commitments mentioned in the first and second paragraphs of this Article, within a reasonable period and prior to the convening of the General Assembly, and in the event of approval of the authorisations, submit a special report thereon to the first General Assembly, whether ordinary or extraordinary, for ratification thereof.

The persons mentioned in the first paragraph of this Article shall not be entitled to participate in the vote on the ratification resolution, and their shares shall not be counted within the quorum.

b- Notify the auditors of the contracts, agreements and commitments that have been authorised, within a period of fifteen days from the authorisation resolution.

The auditors shall submit to the General Assembly their special report relating to the contracts, agreements and commitments mentioned in the first and second paragraphs of this Article while expressing their opinion regarding the impact of those contracts and agreements on the financial statements the explanatory notes thereto, to be voted upon in accordance with the rules.

5- Subject to the provisions of the laws and regulations specific to banks and financial markets, each of the members and the Chairman of the Board of Directors, the General Manager, the Assistant General Manager, its auditors, and any shareholder holding directly or indirectly voting rights exceeding five percent (5%) in its capital shall be prohibited from obtaining from the company, in any manner whatsoever, a loan, facilities, a suretyship, or any guarantee towards third parties.

In all cases, the authorisation shall not be deemed effective until after its ratification by the General Assembly.

Article 159 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 159:

The Chairman and members of the Board of Directors and the Assistant General Manager may not participate in the management of a company similar in its object or in its activity to their company unless they obtain prior authorisation from the Ordinary General Assembly, and such authorisation shall be renewed every year.

Article 160 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 160:

The Chairman and members of the Board of Directors and the Assistant General Manager and the Assistant General Manager may not have any interest whatsoever in any company, association, syndicate or other group that carries out operations intended to bring about an effect on the stock exchange prices relating to the securities issued by the company, whatever their nature.

Article 161 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 161:

The members of the Board of Directors must, at the end of the first six months of the financial year, draw up the interim financial statements for that period. They must also prepare, at the end of the year, the financial statements referred to in Article 101 of this Law.

Article 162 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 162:

The financial statements must be clear. Any change that occurs from one year to another in the method of their preparation or presentation must be disclosed in the complementary notes to the audited financial statements.

Article 163 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 163:

In addition to the financial statements referred to in Article 101 of this Law, the Board of Directors must prepare a report on the position of the company and its activity during the ended year for submission to the shareholders fifteen days prior to the date of the meeting of the General Assembly.

The report of the Board of Directors must clearly and accurately include the following subjects:

- The position of the company and its activity during the ended year.

- The results of this activity.

- The progress achieved and the problems encountered.

- The expected development of the position of the company.

- A statement of the expected risks.

- The important operations that occurred between the date of the end of the year and the date of the meeting of the General Assembly.

Article 164 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 164:

The Board of Directors shall convene the shareholders to hold General Assemblies.

Article 165 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 165:

The Board of Directors must constitute a reserve fund by deducting ten percent of the net profits after deduction of prior losses until the reserve fund becomes equivalent to one-third of the capital of the company.

Article 166 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 166:

The members of the board of directors and the general manager shall be liable, even towards third parties, for all acts of fraud and for every violation of the law and of the company's articles of association. However, the action which the injured party is entitled to bring is an individual action, and it may not, even with regard to the shareholders, be stayed by a vote of the general assembly discharging the members of the board of directors and the general manager.

Article 167 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 167:

The persons referred to in Article 166 shall also be liable towards the shareholders for their fault in management.

In general, the members of the board of directors and the general manager shall not be liable towards third parties for their fault in management. However, in the event of the bankruptcy of the company and the appearance of a deficit in the assets, the court is entitled, upon the request of the bankruptcy trustee or the Public Prosecution, or of its own motion, to decide that the debts of the company shall be borne by the members of the board of directors and/or the general manager or any other person entrusted with the management or supervision of the company's affairs, including the auditors, and the court shall determine the amounts for which they shall be liable and whether or not they are jointly and severally liable; in order to be absolved from this liability, they must furnish proof that they attended to the management and supervision of the company's affairs with the care of a diligent and active professional.

In the event of separation between the office of chairman of the board of directors and that of general manager by the board of directors, the chairman of the board of directors shall be liable only in the event of a violation of the law or of the company's articles of association.

Article 168 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 168:

The right to bring an action against the chairman and members of the board of directors and the general manager pursuant to the first paragraph of the preceding Article belongs to the company, and if it fails to do so, every shareholder is entitled to bring an action on its behalf to the extent of the interest he has in the company.

Article 170 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 170:

Liability shall be either individual, pertaining to one member of the board of directors or the general manager, or common among them all. In the latter case, they shall all be jointly and severally bound to pay compensation, unless a group of them objected to the resolution adopted despite them and their objection was recorded in the minutes.

The final apportionment of liability among those liable shall be in accordance with each one's share in the fault committed.

Article 171 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 171:

An action for liability, whether brought by a shareholder or by a third party, shall be time-barred upon the lapse of five years from the date of the holding of the general meeting at which the members rendered an account of their management.

Article 172 is amended and reads as follows:

New Article 172:

The constituent general meeting and thereafter the subsequent ordinary general meetings shall appoint one or more supervisory commissioners, and they may not remain in their office for more than one year; however, their appointment may be renewed for a period of five consecutive years at most.

Article 173 is amended and reads as follows:

New Article 173:

A shareholder or a group of shareholders, either of whom represents at least ten per cent (10%) of the capital of the company, may apply to the President of the Chamber of First Instance within the jurisdiction of which the registered office of the company is located in order to appoint an additional supervisory commissioner chosen from among the accounting experts before the court, who shall have the same authority and a fee not exceeding the fee fixed for the supervisory commissioner appointed pursuant to Article 172.

Article 174 is amended and reads as follows:

New Article 174:

The supervisory commissioners shall audit the financial statements provided for in Article 101 of this Law prepared by the board of directors in order to express their opinion on the accuracy thereof, provided that their report includes an indication of the cases of non-compliance by the company with its articles of association and the laws and regulations in force.

The board of directors the general manager shall provide the supervisory commissioners with all the information, documents, papers, instruments, and accounting registers necessary for them to complete the audit procedures and works, at any time of the year.

The board of directors shall provide the supervisory commissioners with the financial statements provided for in Article 101 of this Law at least sixty days before the convening of the general meeting.

Article 175 is amended and reads as follows:

New Article 175:

The supervisory commissioners shall submit to the general meeting their report on the financial statements for the approval thereof. If they do not submit this report, the resolution of the general meeting relating to the approval of the statements shall be null and void.

Article 176 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 176:

The auditors must convene the general assembly whenever the members of the board of directors fail to convene it in the cases prescribed by law or by the company's articles of association.

They shall also be entitled to convene it whenever they deem its convening useful.

Indeed, they must convene the general assembly if requested to do so by a group of shareholders representing one-fifth of the company's capital.

Article 177 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 177:

The supervisory auditors shall not have any direct or indirect interest in a group whose purpose is to influence the prices of any class of the company's securities.

Nor shall the supervisory auditors have any interest falling outside the scope of their mandate, particularly through consultancy contracts of whatever kind, (with the company or with a corporate shareholder or a shareholder or group of shareholders owning ten per cent or more of the company's capital).

Article 178 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 178:

The supervisory auditors shall be liable either individually or jointly and severally, even towards third parties, whenever they commit a fault in supervision, subject to the rule of prescription after five years.

Article 181 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 181:

Shareholders who are unable to attend the assembly may appoint proxies to represent them, provided that such representatives are themselves shareholders, unless the articles of association provide that such representatives may be non-shareholders, with the exception of the legal representatives of incapacitated persons.

The company's articles of association may, within the framework of calculating the majority and quorum at meetings of the general assembly of shareholders, provide for the possibility of considering shareholders who participate in assembly meetings via remote audio-visual communication technology or other technical means, the conditions of which shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Justice, to be present at the meeting, provided that verification of the identity of the connecting member is ensured and the integrity, continuity and reliability of the connection and the effective participation of the connecting member in the discussions are guaranteed, and provided that the company's articles of association set out the mechanism to be adopted in this framework.

The content of the remote communication in all sessions of the general assembly must be recorded, such that the recordings shall be deemed an integral part of the minutes of the assembly and shall be preserved therewith.

Article 182 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 182:

An attendance sheet shall be drawn up in which shall be stated the names of the shareholders who are present, represented, or participating through means of remote communication, where applicable, the number of shares owned by each of them, and the number of votes attached to those shares.

This sheet shall be deposited at the registered office of the company and may be inspected by any applicant who proves that he is a shareholder.

Article 183 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 183:

A bureau composed at least of a chairman and a secretary shall be established.

The members of the bureau must be present in person.

Article 186 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 186:

Subject to the special provisions relating to registered shares provided for in Article 117, every shareholder shall have a number of votes equal to the number of shares that he owns or represents, without limitation, unless the company's articles of association expressly provide for a limitation, provided in such case that the limitation is uniform for all shares whatever their class.

Article 190 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 190:

If the shareholders present find that their information on the matters submitted to them for discussion is insufficient, the meeting shall be adjourned for eight days at least and fifteen days at most, provided that one quarter of the members of the assembly request such adjournment.

Article 192 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 192:

Resolutions passed in accordance with due process and observing the requirements of legal quorum and the majority applicable to each general assembly, and which are free from fraud or abuse of power, shall bind all shareholders, including those who are absent and those who dissent.

Article 195 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 195:

In the assemblies provided for in Articles 193 and 194, resolutions shall be passed by a majority of two thirds of the votes of the shareholders present or represented. Holders of contributions in kind shall not participate in passing resolutions relating to the verification of such contributions.

Article 197 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 197:

All shareholders and bondholders shall have the right to inspect, at the registered office of the company or through a dedicated electronic means approved by the company:

- The documents provided for in items 1 to 5 of Article 101 of this Law.

- The list of shareholders

Interested parties may take or request, at their own expense, copies of all the aforementioned documents.

The company shall not be entitled to charge for delivering such copies anything other than the fees fixed by a tariff determined by the Minister of National Economy.

Article 198 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 198:

The ordinary general meeting must be composed of shareholders representing at least one-third of the company's capital.

And if this quorum is not reached, a second meeting shall be held and its deliberations shall be lawful regardless of the portion of the company's capital that it represents.

Article 199 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 199:

In all cases regarding which no contrary provision exists, resolutions at ordinary general meetings shall be adopted by the absolute majority of the number of votes of the shares of the shareholders present or represented or participating remotely and of whom the meeting is duly composed.

Article 204 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 204:

Resolutions at extraordinary general meetings shall be adopted by a majority of two-thirds of the votes of the shares of the shareholders present and represented and participating remotely.

Article 205 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 205:

The company's capital may not be increased except after payment of the full value of the previous capital in accordance with Article 119 of this Law, under pain of nullity of the capital increase.

In the event that there is a holder of the right of usufruct and a holder of the right of bare ownership over a single share, the holder of the right of bare ownership shall have the right to subscribe to the increase of the company's capital, unless the holder of the right of usufruct and the holder of the right of bare ownership have agreed prior to the resolution to increase the company's capital otherwise and have notified their agreement to the company in accordance with the provisions of Article 116 of this Law.

Article 206 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 206:

The legal rules relating to the incorporation of joint-stock companies must be observed in respect of the newly issued shares. The same penalties relating to the annulment of the capital increase and to the fines and to the liability of the chairman and members of the board of directors and the general manager or general managers then in office and the shareholders whose contributions were not duly approved and the auditors and the experts shall apply.

Article 214 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 214:

Pursuant to the legal rules relating to the formal conditions that must be observed in the deliberations of general assemblies, any resolution contrary to these conditions shall be null and void whenever it is proven that such violation actually vitiated the resulting outcome.

Every person having standing and interest shall have the right to invoke such annulment before the competent authority.

The effect of nullity shall lapse by the rectification of the deliberations or by the expiry of one year starting from the day on which the assembly was held with respect to the shareholders and from the publication of the resolution in the Commercial Register with respect to non-shareholders.

Article 216 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 216:

Joint-stock companies shall be dissolved upon the expiry of the term fixed for them, or upon the completion of the undertaking for which they were formed, or upon the impossibility of completing it.

They shall also be dissolved by the will of the partners expressed in a general meeting under the conditions set forth in Articles 202 and 204, just as they shall be dissolved in all specific cases provided for in the articles of association.

If the company loses three-quarters of the capital, the members of the board of directors must convene an extraordinary general assembly to decide whether the situation requires the dissolution of the company before the term, or the reduction of the capital, or the taking of other appropriate measures.

Article 217 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 217:

In any event, if the members of the board of directors neglect to convene the assembly, or if it cannot be constituted due to the lack of the legal quorum, or if the assembly refuses to dissolve the company, every shareholder shall retain the right to have recourse to the competent court to take the appropriate measure or dissolve the company.

Article 220 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 220:

If the liquidators are not appointed in the company's articles of association, they shall be appointed by a vote of the ordinary general assembly, unless the intention is to dissolve the company before the expiry of its term, in which case the extraordinary general assembly shall appoint them at the same time.

If the general assembly does not appoint the liquidators, the matter of their appointment shall then revert to the competent court upon the request of any interested party.

Article 222 shall be amended to read as follows:

New Article 222:

The liquidators shall receive the accounts of the acts of management performed by the members of the board of directors and the general manager since the approval by the general assembly of the last balance sheet until the opening of the liquidation, and they shall either approve them or submit to the competent court the difficulties that appear to them.

Article 223 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 223:

If the duration of the liquidation exceeds one year, the liquidators must draw up the annual balance sheet and publish it.

Article 224 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 224:

After the completion of the liquidation operations, the liquidators shall draw up the final balance sheet in which they determine the share of each shareholder in the distribution of the company's assets.

Article 225 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 225:

The supervisory commissioners shall draw up a report on the accounts submitted by the liquidators; thereafter, the Ordinary General Assembly shall approve them and decide to grant discharge to the liquidators, or object to the accounts, in which case the dispute shall be referred to the competent court.

Article 236 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 236:

(Legislative Decree No. 304 issued on 24 December 1942 and its amendments)

The number of supervisory commissioners must be at least three, including the accounting expert appointed by the President of the Court pursuant to a decision. They may not be chosen from among the managing partners.

They shall meet as a board whenever the supervision and investigations that they must carry out require their meeting.

As for the term of office of the Supervisory Board, it shall be determined in the company's articles of association, provided that the first Board shall only be appointed for a period of one year.

Article 844 of the Code of Obligations and Contracts is amended to read as follows:

New Article 844 of the Code of Obligations and Contracts:

"A company is a reciprocal contract pursuant to which two or several persons pool something with the intention of sharing the profit resulting therefrom.

It may, in the cases provided for by law, be established by an act proceeding from the will of a single person."

On Limited Liability Companies

Article 1 of Legislative Decree 35 dated 5/8/1967 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 1 of Legislative Decree 35 dated 5/8/1967:

A limited liability company is a commercial company formed by one partner or several partners who do not bear losses except to the extent of their contributions.

In the case of a company established by a single person, such person is called the "Sole Partner". The Sole Partner shall exercise the powers vested in the Assembly of Partners.

Article 5 of Legislative Decree 35 dated 5/8/1967 is amended and shall read as follows:

New Article 5 of Legislative Decree No. 35 issued on 5/8/1967:

This company is formed by one person, designated as the sole partner, or more, provided that the number of partners does not exceed twenty except in the case of devolution of shares by inheritance.

However, if the number of partners exceeds thirty, the company must, within a period of two years, be transformed into a joint-stock company; if it is not transformed, it must be dissolved.

The right to request the dissolution of the company for the reason set forth in the preceding paragraph shall lapse if the cause thereof ceases to exist within the specified period.

In the event that the shares are consolidated in the hands of one of the partners in a limited liability company, this shall not lead to the dissolution or termination of the company.

A limited liability company formed of a sole partner may not be the sole partner in another limited liability company.

In the event of a violation of the provisions of the fifth paragraph above due to the consolidation of shares in the hands of one partner in a multi-partner company, the sole partner must rectify the irregular situation within a period of one year, any interested party may request the dissolution after the lapse of one year from the consolidation of the shares.

In all cases, the court is entitled to grant a period of 6 months in order to rectify the situation, and the right to request the dissolution of the company shall lapse if the cause ceases to exist within the specified period.

Article 6 of Legislative Decree 35 dated 5/8/1967 is amended and shall read as follows:

New Article 6 of Legislative Decree No. 35 issued on 5/8/1967:

The company shall be named according to the object of its enterprise or by adopting a common business name that includes the name of one or more of the partners. There must be clearly stated next to the name of the company on all papers, advertisements, publications and all other documents issued by the company the following phrase: "Limited Liability Company" or "L.L.C.", along with an indication of the amount of its capital and the registration number in the Commercial Register.

Any violation of the preceding provisions shall be punishable by a fine ranging between the equivalent of the official minimum wage and double the amount thereof.

If this violation results in deceiving third parties as to the nature of the company, the provisions relating to general partnerships may be applied to determine the obligations of the partners.

Article 7 of Legislative Decree 35 dated 5/8/1967 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 7 of Legislative Decree No. 35 issued on 5/8/1967:

The capital of a limited liability company may not be less than five million Lebanese Pounds and the capital, whatever its amount, shall be divided into equal shares.

If the capital decreases for any reason whatsoever below five million Lebanese Pounds, it must within a time limit of one year be completed or the company be converted into another form with the exception of the joint-stock company. If the company fails to fulfil either of these two obligations, any interested party may apply for its judicial dissolution following a formal notice addressed by him to its manager in order to rectify its situation.

Article 8 of Legislative Decree 35 dated 5/8/1967 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 8 of Legislative Decree No. 35 issued on 5/8/1967:

The company shall not be considered definitively constituted until after the allocation of shares among the partners has been effected and the number of shares of each of them has been determined or restricted to the sole partner, their value has been paid up in full and the amounts paid have been deposited with a bank.

The founders must expressly declare in the articles of association of the company that all these conditions have been fulfilled.

The manager of the company may not withdraw the deposited amounts prior to the registration of the company in the Commercial Register.

If this registration is not effected within a time limit of six months from the date of the first deposit, each of the partners may apply to the summary judge requesting authorisation to recover what he has paid.

Article 9 of Legislative Decree 35 dated 5/8/1967 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 9 of Legislative Decree No. 35 issued on 5/8/1967:

The contributions of the partners may be in cash or in kind, and it is prohibited to include the hire of services or industry among the contributions.

Where there are contributions in kind, the value of these contributions must be determined in the articles of association of the company and recourse must be had to the opinion of one or several experts appointed by the President of the Court of First Instance in the district of the company's registered office in order to verify the accuracy of the determination of such value.

Where there is a plurality of partners, the report of the experts shall be placed at the disposal of the prospective partners and they shall have the right to withdraw from their undertaking to enter into partnership if the appraisal of the contributions by the partner exceeds the value estimated by the expert or experts by more than twenty per cent.

Article 11 of Legislative Decree 35 dated 5/8/1967 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 11 of Legislative Decree No. 35 issued on 5/8/1967:

Save for the obligation of registering limited liability companies in the competent register, the limited liability company shall not be subject upon incorporation to any other rules of publication.

Article 12 of Legislative Decree 35 dated 5/8/1967 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 12 of Legislative Decree No. 35 issued on 5/8/1967:

Every limited liability company incorporated in violation of the conditions set forth in the preceding Articles shall be deemed null and void and of no effect among the partners; however, the sole partner or the partners may not invoke its nullity against third parties.

Article 13 of Legislative Decree 35 dated 5/8/1967 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 13 of Legislative Decree No. 35 issued on 5/8/1967:

When the nullity of the company is declared pursuant to the provisions of the preceding Article, the sole partner, the partners who caused the nullity, the first managers and the founders shall be jointly and severally liable towards third parties and towards the other partners for the damage resulting from the nullity.

The action for nullity shall not be heard if its cause has ceased to exist prior to the filing of the action. It remains possible to remove that cause during the trial and prior to the rendering of the judgment.

In the event of multiple partners, and if the removal of the nullity requires convening the assembly of partners, the course of the action for nullity shall be stayed starting from the date of duly convening that assembly until the issuance of its resolution.

Actions for nullity and liability shall be subject to prescription under the conditions specified for the nullity of the joint-stock company.

Article 14 of Legislative Decree 35 dated 5/8/1967 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 14 of Legislative Decree No. 35 issued on 5/8/1967:

The shares of the sole partner or the partners shall pass by inheritance to their heirs. However, in the event of multiple partners, it may be stipulated, pursuant to an express clause in the articles of association, to grant the option to the company not to accept the heirs or some of them as partners and to pay those heirs their rights, which shall be determined amicably or through the judiciary. Provided that the period for exercising the option may not exceed two months from the date of death.

The company shall not be dissolved by the bankruptcy or interdiction of the sole partner or one of the partners, and in each of these two cases, his legal representative shall replace him.

Article 15 of Legislative Decree 35 dated 5/8/1967 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 15 of Legislative Decree No. 35 issued on 5/8/1967:

The assignment of shares in the company shall be established by an official or private instrument notified to the manager of the company and to each of the partners.

The company shall have a right of preference to purchase all the shares intended to be assigned to a person outside the partners, provided that it expresses its desire to purchase within a period of fifteen days from its notification, through any of its managers, of the draft assignment, which must obligatorily include the name of the prospective buyer, the conditions of the sale and the price, and provided that it exercises its right to purchase within fifteen days from the date of expressing its desire.

In the event that the company does not exercise this right within the period mentioned above, any of the partners may purchase all the shares within a period of thirty days from the date of his notification of the company's refusal to exercise the right, provided that the manager of the company supplies all the partners with a copy of the draft assignment. In the event that more than one partner exercises this right, the shares shall be distributed among them, each in proportion to his participation in the capital of the company.

In any case, shares in the company may not be assigned to a third party extraneous to it except with the approval of partners representing at least three-quarters of the capital.

The provisions of this Article shall not apply in the case of the existence of a sole partner.

Article 16 of Legislative Decree 35 dated 5/8/1967 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 16 of Legislative Decree No. 35 issued on 5/8/1967:

The management of the company shall be entrusted to the sole partner or to one or several managers from among the partners or others, appointed by the articles of association of the company or by a subsequent instrument for a limited or unlimited period, provided that they are natural persons.

The manager or managers shall be vested with all the powers necessary for the regular conduct of the business of the company unless a contrary provision is stated in the constitutive articles of association.

Notwithstanding any contrary clause, the managers or some of them may be dismissed by a decision of the sole partner or of the assembly of partners or by a judicial decision where there is a legitimate reason justifying this dismissal.

If the sole partner decides or if the assembly of partners decides to dismiss a manager without a legitimate reason, the latter shall have the right to claim damages.

Article 18 of Legislative Decree 35 dated 5/8/1967 is amended and shall read as follows:

New Article 18 of Legislative Decree No. 35 issued on 5/8/1967:

The manager, and the managers where there are several of them, and the sole partner or the partners are prohibited, under pain of nullity, from obtaining from the company loans, guarantees or aval endorsements for themselves or for their spouses, ascendants or descendants, even if obtained under assumed names.

Article 19 of Legislative Decree 35 dated 5/8/1967 is amended and shall read as follows:

New Article 19 of Legislative Decree No. 35 issued on 5/8/1967:

The managers are liable individually or jointly and severally, depending on the circumstances, towards the company and third parties for their infringement of the provisions of this Legislative Decree and the provisions of the company's articles of association and for their faults in management.

If several managers participate in the same acts that expose them to liability, the court shall determine the proportion of the compensation for damage to be borne by each of them.

The sole partner or any of the partners shall have the right to bring the liability action against the managers for the benefit of the company in order to claim full compensation for the damage caused to it.

Any clause in the memorandum of association that would make the right to bring this action subject to the prior opinion or authorisation of the assembly of partners, or would waive in advance the exercise of this right, shall be deemed unwritten.

No resolution issued by the assembly of partners to extinguish a liability action brought against the managers on account of their faults relating to management shall have any effect.

Article 20 of Legislative Decree 35 dated 5/8/1967 is amended and shall read as follows:

New Article 20 of Legislative Decree No. 35 issued on 5/8/1967:

The right to bring the liability actions provided for in Article 19 shall lapse after the expiry of five years from the date of the harmful acts on which they are based if they were apparent, or from the date of their discovery if they were apparent, or from the date of their discovery if they were concealed. However, if one of these acts constitutes a felony, the right of action shall not lapse until after the expiry of ten years from its occurrence.

Article 21 of Legislative Decree 25 dated 5/8/1967 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 21 of Legislative Decree No. 35 issued on 5/8/1967:

At the end of each year, the manager or managers shall draw up a report on the business of the company during that year and the financial statements, notify them to the partners, and convene them within six months from the closing of the accounts of the year to a general assembly during which the acts of the managers shall be ratified.

At least twenty days before the time fixed for the holding of the assembly of partners, the original of all the documents specified in the preceding paragraph shall be deposited at the head office of the company, together with the report of the auditor, where there is one, and every partner shall have the right to inspect them and to address written questions to the manager to be answered at the meeting of the assembly.

Every partner may, furthermore, request whenever he wishes to inspect the entries and documents relating to the business of the three preceding years.

Any clause contrary to this Article shall be deemed unwritten.

Article 23 of Legislative Decree 35 dated 5/8/1967 is amended to read as follows:

Article 23: New of Legislative Decree No. 35 issued on 5/8/1967:

Where there are several of them, the partners shall be convened to the assemblies by a notice published in two local daily newspapers or by registered letters or by any other means specified in the articles of association of the company.

The notice of convocation shall be addressed to the partners at least fifteen days before the time fixed for the meeting unless the articles of association of the company provide otherwise.

The notice of convocation shall be addressed by the manager or any of the managers where there are several of them, and failing that, by the auditor where there is one; should all of these fail to act, any one or more partners representing at least one quarter of the capital shall have the right to petition the court to appoint a person to undertake the convocation of the assembly and the drawing up of its agenda.

Any clause contrary to these provisions shall be deemed unwritten.

Article 25 of Legislative Decree 35 dated 5/8/1967 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 25 of Legislative Decree No. 35 issued on 5/8/1967:

In assemblies or in written consultations, resolutions shall be passed by partners representing at least half of the capital. If this majority is not attained, and unless there is a provision to the contrary in the articles of association of the company, the partners shall be convened or consulted a second time and resolutions shall be passed by a majority of votes regardless of the amount of capital they represent.

Where there is only the "sole partner" in the company, he shall sign the resolutions alone.

Resolutions relating to the financial statements shall be recorded in minutes registered in the Commercial Register.

Article 29 of Legislative Decree 35 dated 5/8/1967 is amended and shall read as follows:

New Article 29 of Legislative Decree No. 35 issued on 5/8/1967:

The Assembly of Partners may, by the majority prescribed for amending the Articles of Association, resolve to reduce the capital without any prejudice to the equality of the partners.

Where there is an auditor, the latter must be notified of the proposed capital reduction so that he may give his opinion on the reasons for this measure and its conditions when the Assembly is convened.

If the Assembly resolves to approve the reduction of capital for a reason other than losses, its resolution shall be registered in the Commercial Register and published in two local newspapers, and every creditor shall be entitled to object thereto within two months from the date of the last publication formality before the court of the company's registered office, which shall decide, according to the circumstances, either to dismiss the objection or to compel the company to furnish guarantees for the rights of the objectors as it shall determine by its decision. The formalities for the reduction of capital may not be commenced prior to the expiry of the time limit for objection.

The company is prohibited from purchasing its own shares. However, the Assembly that has resolved to reduce the capital for a reason other than losses may authorise its manager to purchase a specified number of the partners' shares for the purpose of cancelling them

The text of Articles 21, 23, 26 and 29 shall not apply if the company is composed of a sole partner. In this case, the manager shall draw up a report on the company's operations and its annual financial statements. The sole partner shall approve the accounts of the company after examining the report of the auditor, where one exists, within a time limit of six months from the end of the financial year.

The sole partner may not delegate his powers as a partner to third parties.

Article 30 of Legislative Decree 35 dated 5/8/1967 is amended and shall read as follows:

New Article 30 of Legislative Decree No. 35 dated 5/8/1967: Limited Liability Companies

The partners may appoint one or more auditors by a resolution adopted by the majority prescribed in Article 25 of this Legislative Decree.

Such appointment shall be mandatory:

a- If the number of partners exceeds twenty.

b- If the capital of the company reaches thirty million Lebanese Pounds.

c- If the appointment of the auditor is requested by one or more partners representing at least one-fifth of the capital.

When the company is composed of a sole partner, the appointment of the auditor shall be mandatory if the capital of the company reaches thirty million Pounds.

Article 31 of Legislative Decree 35 dated 5/8/1967 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 31 of Legislative Decree No. 35 dated 5/8/1967: Limited Liability Companies

The supervisory commissioner shall be chosen from among the persons enrolled on the roll of experts.

The following shall not be appointed as supervisory commissioners:

1- The partners, the sole partner, the managers, and their spouses, ascendants, and descendants.

2- Persons who receive periodic salaries from the company or from its manager, and their spouses, ascendants, and descendants. Within five years from the termination of the functions of the supervisory commissioners, those commissioners may not be appointed as managers of the company whose operations they supervised. Nor may they, within the same period, be appointed as managers, members of the board of directors, or supervisors of companies that own ten percent of the capital of the company in which they were supervisory commissioners, or in which the latter owns ten percent of their capital. The provisions applicable to joint-stock companies shall apply to the supervisory commissioners to the extent that they are compatible with the special provisions stipulated in this Legislative Decree.

Article 32 of Legislative Decree 35 dated 5/8/1967 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 32 of Legislative Decree No. 35 issued on 5/8/1967:

Dividends distributed to the partners may be recovered when they are not based on real profits realized.

The action for recovery shall be subject to the five-year limitation period from the date of the day fixed for the distribution of the dividends.

Article 33 of Legislative Decree 35 dated 5/8/1967 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 33 of Legislative Decree No. 35 issued on 5/8/1967:

In the event of the loss of three profits of the capital, the partners must decide within a period of four months following the approval of the accounts that showed that loss, whether the company must be dissolved. If they do not decide to dissolve it by the majority prescribed for amending the articles of association, they shall immediately be required to reduce the capital by the amount of the loss, unless this majority decides to reconstitute the capital as it was.

The decision adopting any of the solutions mentioned above shall be published in two local newspapers and registered in the Commercial Register.

If the partners do not issue their decision within the period prescribed in the first paragraph, every interested party shall have the right to request the judicial dissolution of the company.

Article 34 of Legislative Decree 35 dated 5/8/1967 is amended to read as follows:

New Article 34 of Legislative Decree No. 35 issued on 5/8/1967:

The transformation of a limited liability company into a general partnership, a simple limited partnership or a partnership limited by shares requires the unanimity of the partners.

As for its transformation into a joint-stock company, it may be decided by the majority prescribed for amending the articles of association, provided that the partners have approved the accounts of the two preceding years.

If it appears from the accounts of the company, after their approval, that the value of its net assets exceeds fifty million pounds, the majority representing half of the capital may decide to transform the company into a joint-stock company, after reviewing the report of the auditing commissioner confirming the accuracy of the accounts.

Any change of the type of the company that takes place contrary to the provisions of this Article shall be null and void.

An Eighth Title is added to the Second Book of the Code of Commerce in the following form:

On Certain Financial Offences

Article 253 bis 1:

Shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to three years and by a fine ranging from twenty-five to one hundred times the official minimum wage, or by one of these two penalties, the chairman and members of the board of directors, the managers and the authorised signatories who, in bad faith, proceed to harm the company:

a- By using the company's funds or its credit capacities in a manner harmful to its interests, for personal purposes.

b- Through acting for the benefit of another company, an enterprise or an individual in which any of them has a direct or indirect interest with any of those.

Article 253 bis 2:

Shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to three years and by a fine ranging from twenty-five to fifty times the official minimum wage or by one of these two penalties, the chairman and members of the board of directors, the managers and the authorised signatories who intentionally, with the aim of concealing the true situation of the company, proceed to draw up and publish untruthful financial statements.

The auditing commissioners who intentionally proceed to conceal these violations in their reports shall be punished by the same penalty.

Article 253 bis 3:

The three-year limitation period for prosecution of the offences provided for in the two preceding Articles shall run from the date of their occurrence if they were apparent and from the date of their discovery if they were concealed.

A new Title, which is Title Six under the heading of Depositary Receipts, shall be added to Book Four of the Code of Land Commerce.

Title Six

Global Depositary Receipts

Article 458 bis 1:

Global depositary receipts are negotiable registered instruments linked to registered shares (the underlying shares) of a Lebanese joint-stock company, issued abroad by an issuer licensed in the country of issuance and listed on regulated financial markets.

Article 458 bis 2:

Fully subject to the regulatory provisions relating to global depositary receipts linked to shares of banks, the company must verify on its own responsibility, when issuing global depositary receipts linked to its shares, that the following conditions are met:

1- The issuance by a bank or financial institution abroad of the global depositary receipts after receiving evidence that the underlying shares have been deposited for safekeeping with the Central Depository and Clearing House of Financial Instruments for Lebanon and the Middle East (Midclear) established pursuant to Law No. 139 dated 26/11/1999.

2- The approval of the board of directors of the company issuing the underlying shares of the information contained in the prospectus that may be prepared for this issuance.

3- The issuance of global depositary receipts either:

a- Pursuant to the provisions of a contract signed between the bank or financial institution, either of which intends to issue global depositary receipts, and the company issuing the underlying shares, against shares owned by it out of their shares or against shares owned by certain shareholders of the company in the issuing company Sponsored DRS

b- Against a letter of no objection from the company issuing the underlying shares in the absence of a contract as referred to in paragraph (a) of this item (3) (Unsponsored DRs). In this case, and on the basis of the information that may be available to it, Midclear shall also verify that the conditions of this Article are fulfilled upon the issuance of global depositary receipts.

4- The permissibility of granting the holders of global depositary receipts the right to exchange them for a number of underlying shares, provided that this does not conflict with legal or regulatory provisions, particularly those that restrict the ownership of the underlying shares to Lebanese persons.

5- The retention of the underlying shares in the possession of the Central Depository and Clearing House of Financial Instruments for Lebanon and the Middle East (Midclear) until the value of the global depositary receipts is settled in whole or in part, or until they are exchanged for the corresponding underlying shares in whole or in part, or until the dissolution and liquidation of the company issuing the underlying shares.

6- The possibility of granting the issuer of the global depositary receipts the right to attend the general assemblies of the company issuing the underlying shares and the right to participate in voting, provided that:

a- This right does not conflict with legal or regulatory provisions, particularly those that restrict the ownership of the underlying shares to Lebanese persons.

b- The issuer of the global depositary receipts votes at the meetings of the general assemblies in accordance with the instructions of the holders of these receipts, if the contract or the rules of issuance of these receipts permit this and determine the conditions and manner of exercising voting rights, failing which the issuer of the global depositary receipts must vote in accordance with what the interest of the company issuing the underlying shares requires.

7- The number of shares represented by global depositary receipts does not exceed 30% of the number of fully paid-up shares constituting the capital of the company issuing the underlying shares.

Article 458 bis 3: Upon the dissolution and liquidation of the company issuing the underlying shares, the holders of the global depositary receipts shall be entitled to all the rights pertaining to the underlying shares, subject to the provisions of the Law promulgated by Decree No. 10845 dated 10/9/1968 relating to the acquisition by non-Lebanese of real property rights in Lebanon.

A Ninth Title shall be added to the Second Book of the Code of Commerce as follows:

Articles 210 to 213 of the Code of Commerce are repealed and replaced by the following Ninth Title:

Title Nine: On the Merger and Demerger of Companies

Chapter One: General Provisions

Article 210:

The merger of companies is effected by the transfer of the patrimony of one or more companies to an existing company or to a new company created for this purpose.

The demerger of companies is effected by the transfer by a company of its patrimony to several existing or newly created companies.

Companies under liquidation may participate in merger and demerger operations provided that the implementation of the stage of partitioning the assets among the partners has not yet commenced.

By disappearing company is meant the company that loses its existence as a result of the merger or demerger.

By beneficiary company is meant the company to which all, some, or the net assets are transferred as a result of the merger or demerger.

The board of directors may be expanded to include a maximum of twenty members in the event of a merger operation.

Article 211:

These operations shall take place between various types of companies and within the conditions prescribed for amending the articles of association in each of them.

If this requires the establishment of a new company or companies, their establishment shall be subject to the rules of incorporation of each of them as defined in the law.

Article 212:

The merger or demerger leads to the dissolution of the disappearing companies without their liquidation and to the transfer of their patrimony to the beneficiary companies in the state in which it is upon the final completion of the operation, including the leasehold right.

The partners in the disappearing companies acquire the capacity of partners in the beneficiary companies within the conditions defined in the merger or demerger contract, and the old shares and parts are replaced by shares or parts in the beneficiary companies. These partners may receive a cash premium provided that its percentage does not exceed 10% of the nominal value of the parts or shares given to them.

This replacement shall not take place if the parts or shares are owned by the beneficiary company or the disappearing company, provided that their value is calculated when determining the value of the shares or parts in the concerned companies.

Article 213:

The effect of the merger or demerger shall commence:

1- From the date of registration of the new company in the Commercial Register, and if there are multiple companies, from the date of the last registration.

2- In other cases, from the date of registration of the minutes of the last general assembly that approved the operation, unless the agreement stipulates another date.

If another date is agreed upon, it must not be subsequent to the closing date of the accounts of the current financial year of the beneficiary company or companies, or prior to the closing date of the last accounts of the financial year of the disappearing company or companies.

Article 213 bis 2:
