The companies participating in any of the operations provided for in the first Article of the draft merger or demerger shall draw up and deposit it with the secretariat of the Commercial Register at their head office, and it shall be registered in their register, and an abstract thereof shall be published at their expense in the Official Gazette and in a local newspaper and/or by the electronic means referred to in Article 101 of this Law within one month from the date of approval of the extraordinary general assembly.

The draft merger or demerger shall include mention of the following:

1- The name, form, and head office of the contracting company or companies.

2- The purpose and conditions of the merger or demerger.

3- The determination of the value of the assets and liabilities.

4- The closing date of the accounts of the concerned companies.

5- The amount of the exchange ratio and the cash premium, if any.

6- The amount of the merger or demerger premium.

Chapter Two

Additional Provisions Specific to Joint-Stock Companies

Article 213 bis 3:

The auditors in the concerned companies must draw up a unified report on the merger operation, the valuation of the shares, and the exchange ratio.

The report must also show that the value of the net assets belonging to the disappearing company is not less than the value of the increase occurring in the capital of the beneficiary company.

Article 213 bis 4:

The auditors in the concerned companies must draw up a unified report on the merger operation, the valuation of the shares, and the exchange ratio.

The report must also show that the value of the net assets belonging to the disappearing company is not less than the value of the increase occurring in the capital of the beneficiary company.

The judge supervising the Commercial Register shall appoint one or more special auditors to examine the report mentioned in the preceding paragraph and express his observations within a period not exceeding three months from the date of being notified of the mission, provided that the report of the auditor appointed by the judge is reasoned.

Both the unified and the special reports shall be placed at the disposal of the shareholders at the head office of each concerned company at least one month prior to the date of the meeting of the general assembly to which the decision to merge is submitted.

The competent general assemblies in the concerned companies hold the final decision in the merger operation.

Each of the unified report and the special report shall be deposited with the secretariat of the Commercial Register.

Article 213 bis 5:

Every merger operation taking place between two companies shall be exempted from the unified and special reports if one of them acquires all the shares of the other between the date of depositing the draft merger with the secretariat of the Commercial Register and the date of the meeting of the extraordinary general assembly of the absorbing company.

Article 213 bis 6:

If the merger operation is completed by way of establishing a new company, this company may be incorporated by the contributions of the merged companies to the exclusion of any other contributions.

In all cases, the draft articles of association of the new company shall be approved by the extraordinary general assembly in each of the merged companies, and it shall not be required to obtain the approval of the general assembly of the new company.

Article 213 bis 7:

- The draft merger shall be submitted to the general assembly of debenture holders in the disappearing companies, which may approve it, whereby these debentures shall vest as liabilities of the absorbing company. Its rejection thereof shall not prevent the continuation of the merger operation, which shall not then be enforceable against those creditors, who shall recover their claims from the assets of the disappearing company without the participation of the creditors of the beneficiary company. This assembly shall also be entitled to authorise its representative or representatives to file an opposition in accordance with the provisions of Article 213 bis 9 of this Law.

- The submission of the merger set out in the preceding paragraph shall not be mandatory if the payment of the debt is offered to the debenture holders upon their request. In this case, the absorbing company becomes the debtor of what is owed to them by the disappearing company.

- The offer to pay the debt shall be made by announcing it in the Official Gazette and in a local newspaper and/or by the electronic means referred to in the new Article 101 of this Law, and if the debenture holder does not request the payment of his debt within a period of one month from the date of the last publication operation, he shall remain enjoying this capacity in the absorbing company within the conditions defined in the merger contract.

Article 213 bis 8:

The absorbing company shall remain the debtor of the creditors of the merged company other than the debenture holders and shall be subrogated to it in these debts without novation of the obligation.

Article 213 bis 9:

The creditors of the companies participating in the merger operation, other than the debenture holders, shall be entitled to file an opposition before the competent Court of First Instance against this draft within one month from the date of the last publication operation carried out in accordance with the provisions of Article 213 bis 7 above.

It shall be for this court to dismiss their opposition, or order the payment of their debts, or approve the guarantees offered by the absorbing company if it finds them sufficient, or impose additional guarantees.

In all cases, the opposition shall not prevent the continuation of the merger operation; however, if the debts are not paid or the prescribed guarantees are not provided, the merger shall not be enforceable against the opposing creditor.

Article 213 bis 10:

The draft merger shall not be submitted to the assembly of debenture holders in the absorbing company. However, this assembly may authorise its representative or representatives to file an opposition against the merger in accordance with the forms and conditions defined in the preceding Article 213 bis 9.

Article 213 bis 11:

The provisions of Articles 213 bis 7 and 213 bis 8 above shall apply upon demerger.

Article 213 bis 12:

When the realisation of the demerger is based on contributions to newly created joint-stock companies, each of these newly created companies may be incorporated by the contributions belonging to the demerged company to the exclusion of any others.

In such a case, and if the shares in the newly created companies are given to the shareholders of the demerged company in the same proportion as their rights in the capital of the latter, the two reports mentioned in Article 213 bis 4 above shall not be drawn up.

In all cases, the draft articles of association of the new companies shall be ratified by the extraordinary general assembly of the demerged company without the need to obtain the approval of the general assemblies of any of the new companies.

Article 213 bis 13:

The provisions of Article 213 bis 11 shall apply to the debenture holders in the demerged companies, and these shall have the same rights as those belonging to the debenture holders in the disappearing companies, subject to the text of Article 213 bis 19.

Article 213 bis 14:

The draft demerger shall not be submitted to the assembly of debenture holders in the beneficiary companies; however, this assembly shall be entitled to authorise representatives on its behalf to file an opposition against the demerger operation in accordance with the provisions and conditions of Article 213 bis 13 above.

Article 213 bis 15:

The companies benefiting from the contributions resulting from the demerger shall be considered jointly and severally liable towards the debenture holders and all other creditors of the demerged company.

The beneficiary companies shall be subrogated to the demerged companies in those debts without this subrogation resulting in a novation of the obligation with respect to the debenture holders or the creditors.

Article 213 bis 16:

A company that contributes a part of its assets to another company may agree with the beneficiary company to subject this operation to the provisions provided for in Articles 213 bis 15 to 213 bis 19.

Chapter Three

Provisions Specific to Limited Liability Companies

Article 213 bis 17:

The provisions of Articles 213 bis 8, 9, 12, 13, and 19 shall apply to the merger or demerger of limited liability companies in favour of companies of the same type.

If the operation is carried out by way of contributions in kind to existing limited liability companies, the general provisions relating to contributions in kind in limited liability companies shall also apply.

When the merger operation is carried out by means of contributions to a new limited liability company, the latter may be incorporated solely by the contributions of the merged company or companies.

When the demerger operation is carried out by means of contributions to new limited liability companies, the latter may be incorporated solely by the contributions of the demerged company. In this case, and if the parts in each of the new companies are given to the partners in the demerged company in the same proportion as their rights in the capital of this latter company, the two reports provided for in Article 213 bis 4 above shall not then be drawn up.

The partners in the disappearing companies in the two cases mentioned in the two items above may act ipso jure as founders of the new companies in accordance with the provisions in force in limited liability companies.

Article 213 bis 18:

A company that contributes to another company a part of its assets may, by agreement with it, subject that operation to the provisions governing demerger by contributions to existing limited liability companies.

Chapter Four

Miscellaneous Provisions

Article 213 bis 19:

When the operations mentioned in the first Article take place with the participation of joint-stock companies and limited liability companies, the provisions of Articles 213 bis 8, 9, 12, 13, 19, and 21 shall apply in particular.

Article 213 bis 20:

All procedures and formalities required by the merger and demerger operations mentioned in this Law shall be exempted from the fiscal stamp duty.

Article 213 bis 21:

All procedures and formalities required by the merger operation taking place between companies shall be exempted from all stamp, conveyance, transfer, notary public, and registration duties before the various official authorities.

Article 213 bis 22:

The merged companies must pay the taxes issued prior to the date of the merger, and all the provisions contained in the Tax Procedures Law shall be observed with respect to liability in paying the taxes issued subsequently. However, these companies shall be exempted from the obligation to submit a clearance certificate from the National Social Security Fund.

Article 213 bis 23:

The merged companies and the absorbing companies shall be subject to the tax provided for in Article 45 of the Income Tax Law at a reduced rate of 5% on the revaluation variances of the fixed assets of any of them.

The profits from the assignment of any of the fixed assets that were previously valued to complete the merger operation shall be subject to the tax provided for in Article 45 of the Income Tax Law without reduction, in the event that the assignment takes place within two years from the date of completion of the merger operation.

Article 213 bis 24:

All procedures and formalities required by the operation of demerging a company into two or more newly created companies shall be exempted from all stamp, conveyance, transfer, notary public, and registration duties before the various official authorities, and these duties shall remain due if the demerger takes place in favour of an existing company or companies.

Article 213 bis 25:

The demerged company must pay the taxes issued prior to the date of the demerger, and all the provisions contained in the Tax Procedures Law shall be observed with respect to liability in paying the taxes issued subsequently. However, these companies shall be exempted from the obligation to submit a clearance certificate from the National Social Security Fund.

Article 213 bis 26:

The demerged companies shall be subject to the tax provided for in Article 45 of the Income Tax Law at a reduced rate of 5% on the revaluation variances of their fixed assets in the event that the demerger takes place into two or more newly created companies.

However, if the demerger takes place into two or more existing companies, the revaluation variances shall be subject to the ordinary tax.

However, if the demerger takes place into existing and newly created companies, the demerger into the existing company shall be subject to the tax rate provided for in in Article 45 of the Income Tax Law.
The title of Part Five of the Code of Land Commerce is repealed and replaced by the following phrase: "On the Rights of the Spouse of the Bankrupt."

The text of Article 615 of the Code of Commerce is repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 615:

The recovery rights pertaining to the non-bankrupt spouse shall be determined in accordance with the rules set forth below.

The text of Article 625 of the Code of Commerce is repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 625:

The property of the non-bankrupt spouse, both movable and immovable, shall remain outside the assets of the bankruptcy estate.

The text of Article 626 of the Code of Commerce is repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 626:

The property of the non-bankrupt spouse which is proven to have been purchased with the funds of the bankrupt during the five years preceding the date of the declaration of bankruptcy shall be deemed part of the assets of the bankruptcy estate.

The aforementioned fact may be proven by all means of evidence admissible in commercial matters. Merely establishing proof that the non-bankrupt spouse had no personal resources on the date of acquiring such property shall constitute sufficient proof, unless the latter provides proof to the contrary.

The text of Article 627 of the Code of Commerce is repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 627:

If the non-bankrupt spouse pays debts on behalf of the bankrupt spouse, he shall be entitled to claim his rights like the other creditors in the bankruptcy, unless proof is established that such debts were paid out of the property of the bankrupt spouse.

The text of Article 628 of the Code of Commerce is repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 628:

If the spouse was a merchant at the time of the conclusion of the marriage or had no other specified profession at that time and then became a merchant during the same year, only the real property which he owned at the time of the marriage or which devolved upon him by inheritance, by gift inter vivos, or by will shall be subject to the compulsory mortgage provided for in Paragraph 2 of Article /131/ of the Real Property Ownership Law promulgated by Decision No. 3339.

The text of Article 629 of the Code of Commerce is repealed and replaced by the following text:

New Article 629:

The non-bankrupt spouse whose bankrupt spouse was a merchant at the time of celebration of the marriage, or then had no other determinate profession and became a merchant within the year following the celebration of the marriage, shall not be entitled to bring any action against the bankruptcy estate on account of the benefits stipulated in the marriage instrument. In such case, the creditors shall not be entitled, on their part, to avail themselves of the benefits granted by the non-bankrupt spouse in the said instrument.

Donations granted by the bankrupt spouse to his non-bankrupt spouse during the five years preceding the date of the declaration of bankruptcy shall be void by operation of law.
This Law shall be published in the Official Gazette and shall enter into force three months after the date of its publication.

Single Article:

- The draft law contained in Decree No. 2590 dated 23 March 2018 aiming at settling building violations incurred during the period from 13/9/1971 until 31/12/2018 inclusive, as amended by the Joint Parliamentary Committees and the Chamber of Deputies, is hereby ratified.

- This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The provisions of this Law shall apply to all buildings and parts of buildings constructed on the private property of their owners in violation of building laws and regulations between 13/9/1971 and 31/12/2018 inclusive.

Buildings and parts of buildings constructed within the setbacks pertaining to roads of any category whatsoever, as well as the setbacks from approved and unexecuted alignments, and within the setback from public property, shall be subject to the following:

1 - With the Administration reserving the right of demolition, the violator shall pay a fine equal to four times the total fees paid upon the legal licensing of the building, in addition to (1.5) one and a half times the notional land value.

2 - In the event that the Administration decides to expropriate to widen the road or to execute any alignment, the Administration shall pay the price of the expropriated land without the price of the building. The competent administration shall register the condition on the Real Property Folio of the plot upon carrying out the settlement.

3 - In the event that the violating section of the building collapses for any reason whatsoever, the settlement shall not confer any right to commit the violation anew.

The owners of buildings and parts of buildings erected on their private property in violation of the building laws and regulations shall choose, within a period of two years from the issuance of this Law, either to remove the violation at their own expense and responsibility or to regularise the violation in return for paying the following fees and fines:

1 - In the event of a violation of the exploitation ratios:

The fees and fines due for each violation shall be determined on the basis of brackets of the assessed value per square metre in accordance with the following:

a - For each land price per metre valued at one million Lebanese Pounds and below one million, the violator shall pay a fine amounting to twice the value of all the fees payable upon the legal licensing for building, in addition to the equivalent of one quarter of the price of the notional land for the violating areas.

b - If the land price per metre exceeds one million Lebanese Pounds and does not exceed three million, the violator shall pay the fees and the fine according to Paragraph (a) set out above for the first million, and shall pay a fine amounting to four times the fees and half the price of the notional land for that which exceeds one million Lebanese Pounds.

c - If the land price per metre exceeds three million Lebanese Pounds, the violator shall pay the fees and the fine according to Paragraph (a) set out above for the first million, and according to Paragraph (b) set out above for the other two million, and a fine amounting to four times the fees and once the price of the additional notional land for that which exceeds the same.

This fine shall be paid for the entire violating area until both the surface exploitation rate and the general exploitation ratio actually adopted in the violating building become in conformity with the surface exploitation rate and the general exploitation ratio permitted in the zone.

- If the violation of the exploitation ratios exceeds what is permitted in accordance with the regulations of the zone, the fine set out above shall be paid in accordance with the following:

. Once the value of this fine for the portion of the violating area equivalent to the legally permitted area.

. Twice the value of this fine for the portion of the violating area that exceeds the same.

And the following shall be considered a violation of the exploitation ratios:

The increase in the surface exploitation rate or in the general exploitation ratio.

- The increase in the number of storeys beyond what is permitted in the regulations of the zone.

- The increase in the number of storeys backfilled around in a manner violating the land reclamation regulations.

- Any building area located outside the building envelope (gabarit).

Every increase in the number of storeys or the area located outside the building envelope shall be considered a violation of the general exploitation ratio, even if its area does not exceed the general exploitation ratio permitted in the regulations of the zone.

d - In the event of erecting the building on a plot unsuitable for building, in accordance with the laws and regulations in force, the amount of the fine incurred for the notional land area shall be doubled.

e - In the event of violating the permitted height in the height of retaining walls, a fine equal to twice the value of the fees due on the building permit shall be imposed for each square metre of the area of the walls that exceeds the legally permitted height.

f - In the event of violating the permitted height in the height of boundary walls, a fine equal to the value of the fees due on the building permit shall be imposed for each square metre of the area of the boundary walls that exceeds the legally permitted height.

2 - In the event of other violations of the Building Law:

The violator shall pay a fine amounting to ten times the value of all the fees payable upon the legal licensing for building in addition to these fees, and that for the entire violating area for the various types of violations not set out in Clause «1» of this Article.

3 - The building permit fee shall be added to the aforementioned fines, and a special fee shall also be added for failing to provide the garage required for the violating building area for each car, the value of which is fifteen percent (15%) of the price of the land necessary to provide a garage with an area of twenty-five square metres (25 m2), with a minimum price of one million Lebanese Pounds (1.000.000 LBP) and a maximum price of twenty-five million Lebanese Pounds (25.000.000 LBP).

1 - The multiplicity of violations ipso jure results in the multiplicity of fees and fines and their aggregation to determine the final fee and fine if the settlement of one of them does not cover the

other violation, whereas if the settlement of one of the violations ipso jure results in the settlement of another violation, the maximum fine between the two violations shall be imposed.

2 - Every alteration in the designated use of the garage or the shelter, or the abolition of either of them in all buildings, shall be deemed a violation not subject to settlement.

3 - In buildings constructed without a legal permit, the provision of a garage on the ground floor shall be imposed ipso jure, either on the unbuilt land or on the basement floors where they exist (if possible), and any excess shall be subject to the special fee for failure to provide a garage in accordance with the provisions of paragraph "3" of Article Three of this Law.

1 - Buildings constructed in accordance with the building laws and regulations, without having obtained upon their construction the required legal permit, may have their status settled against payment of twice the value of all the fees due upon a legal building permit, if the concerned party submits the required file within a period of two years from the date of entry into force of this Law.

2 - These fees shall be multiplied to four times if the concerned parties submit the file after the expiry of the period of one year from the date of entry into force of this Law.

Permits and settlements granted contrary to the laws and regulations:

1 - Construction permits:

a - The holder of a construction permit, authorisation, or construction declaration granted contrary to the provisions of the Construction Law, the execution of which has not been commenced up to the date of 1/1/2019, is required to rectify his permit such that any violations of the Construction Law contained therein are cancelled, and his permit shall become valid after rectification; commencement of execution after 1/1/2019 shall not be taken into consideration, and the rectification of the permit shall remain required. This shall not preclude the prosecution of any person who granted, participated in, or intervened in granting the permit, authorisation, or construction declaration contrary to the provisions of the Construction Law, pursuant to the legal provisions in force.

b - Buildings executed wholly or partially, which were erected pursuant to permits, authorisations, or approvals granted contrary to the laws and regulations since 24/3/1994 (the date of issuance of Law No. 324/94 relating to the settlement of construction violations), regardless of the authority that granted the approval, shall be deemed offending buildings, and the offenders shall settle their violations in accordance with the provisions of this Law. The amounts previously paid by them shall be deemed part of the value of the fees and fines due for the settlement.

2 - Settlements contrary to the law and regulations:

All settlements of construction violations carried out contrary to the law and regulations, and all settlement transactions that have not yet been completed, shall be deemed cancelled and null and void, regardless of the authority that granted the approval to conduct the settlement. These violations shall be subject to the provisions of this Law, and the amounts legally paid by the owner shall be deemed part of the value of the fees and fines due for the settlement after their determination in accordance with the provisions of this Law, and these amounts shall be confiscated in favour of the municipality concerned if the violation is not eligible for settlement pursuant to the provisions of this Law.

3 - Habitation permits granted contrary to the law and regulations

All habitation (occupancy) permits granted contrary to the law and regulations shall be deemed cancelled and null and void, regardless of the authority that granted the approval for these permits.

4 - Municipalities within the municipal boundaries, and Governors and District Commissioners (Qaemaqams) outside the municipal boundaries, shall review the construction permits, settlements, and habitation permits granted contrary to the law and regulations in accordance with what is stated in paragraphs (1), (2), and (3) of this Article, and determine the value of the fees and fines due from the offending original owners on the basis of technical inspection reports drawn up at the Directorate General of Urban Planning departments, and notify them so that the remaining amounts due from them are paid immediately upon the entry into force of this Law.

5 - No fine shall apply where the owner had previously obtained a habitation permit and clean title deeds, or where the real estate register folio was free of any annotation of a construction violation on the date of issuance of the title deed.

Annotations placed before the date of 1/1/2019 indicating the existence of a construction violation after obtaining a title deed in application of the provisions of this Article shall be struck off pursuant to this Law.

The original perpetrator of the violation and every accomplice thereto shall be prosecuted for the fines that would have been due on the violation.

Declaration of infringements:

1 - With respect to all types of infringements, whatever their type and whatever the text applicable thereto, the offender shall submit to the Urban Planning Departments or to the Municipalities of Beirut and Tripoli, within a period of two years from the date on which this Law enters into force, a declaration of the infringement in which he announces his desire to remove the infringement or to pay the fees and fines due for the settlement.

2 - If the one-year time-limit expires and the offender has not submitted the required declaration, or if he has not completed the file of the application to carry out the settlement within the time-limit specified for him in accordance with the rules, or if he has chosen demolition without executing it, he shall become obliged to pay the fees and fines due.

3 - Where the offender chooses to pay the fees and fines and carry out the settlement, he shall attach to the declaration the following documents:

a - A statement describing the infringement and its location in detail (the adopted areas and the number of floors), signed by an engineer registered with one of the two Orders of Engineers in Beirut or Tripoli and certified by the Order concerned in accordance with a special form established by the Directorate General of Urban Planning.

b - An undertaking from the engineer that this infringement, if settled, will not constitute a danger to the safety of the building and to public safety, and that the (original) building and its foundations can bear it.

c - A certificate from the president of the municipality, or the Qa'immaqam or the Governor in areas where there are no municipalities, specifying the date of completion of the infringing construction.

d - Four photographs of the four facades of the building bearing a date within the body of the photograph, showing the infringement therein and signed by the engineer mentioned in paragraph (a) of this Article.

e - A copy of the infringement report from the Internal Security Forces bodies or the municipal police (if any).

f - A card (form) with the explicit name of the offender or his legal representative and his full address.

g - A financial receipt in an amount equal to 250.000 Lebanese Pounds (two hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese Pounds) for each wholly or partially infringing floor, provided that this amount shall not be calculated as part of the fees and fines due.

4 - The documents required to complete the file and carry out the settlement must be valid and in force on the date of submission of the file.

5 - The Urban Planning Departments shall decide on the validity of the signed documents after verification (in the governorates and districts), whereas the Municipalities of Beirut and Tripoli or the union of municipalities, where it has an engineering department, shall decide thereon within a period of one month from their submission. These documents shall be returned to the person who submitted them if they do not conform to reality, in order to complete the deficiencies within 15 days, and if the person concerned does not submit the documents complete and corrected within this period, the declaration shall be deemed rejected.

Calculation of Fees and Fines:

The value of the fees and fines due for the violation shall be calculated by the competent technical departments pursuant to a technical inspection report drawn up on the basis of the decision of the Valuation Committee provided for in Article Thirteen of this Law.

The publication of the assessment by affixing it to the door of the property and to the door of the competent administration (the municipality), and in the absence thereof to the door of the Qaimaqamiya or the Governorate for a period of at least one month, shall be deemed as personal notification to the person liable for the fees and fines, and an official record thereof shall be drawn up specifying the date of publication, and a notice thereof shall be sent to the person liable.

1 - A violator who submits the required declaration and file in due form within the two-year period specified in this Law shall be exempted from 40% (forty percent) of the value of the fines on the violation, provided that the amounts due from him are paid within a maximum period of three months from the date he is deemed notified pursuant to the law.

The file shall be deemed complete and its owner shall benefit from the exemption immediately upon obtaining an official receipt proving the filing of his file and the financial receipt with the administration, and it shall be stated on the receipt that the violator benefits from this exemption.

2 - If the violator does not pay the fees and fines due from him within a period of six months from the date of publication of the assessment, he shall be required to pay an additional fine of one percent (1%) of the total fees and fines due for each month of delay, and a fraction of a month shall be deemed a full month.

3 - If the violator fails to pay the amounts due from him pursuant to this Law (after the issuance of the technical inspection report by the competent authorities and the determination of the amounts due from him), they shall be registered as a privileged debt on the real estate folios pertaining to the property, bearing legal interest at the rate of twelve percent per annum, as from the date of expiry of the period specified in Paragraph (1) of Article Seven of this Law.

Levying and Collection of Fees and Fines:

1 - The fees and fines provided for in this Law shall be levied on offending buildings or parts of buildings, including types of offending buildings originally exempted from building permit fees, and shall be collected in accordance with the rules for the collection of municipal fees.

2 - An offender who has not benefited from the provisions of Paragraphs (1) and (2) of the ninth Article above may request to pay the fees and fines by instalments in three payments in accordance with the following provisions:

- That he submit the application within a time limit not exceeding six months from the date of his being notified thereof or his being deemed notified, and that he pay a first payment equal to 40% (forty per cent) of the value of the amounts due from him within the same time limit.

- The second payment, the value of which is 30% (thirty per cent) of the value of the amounts due from him, shall fall due after the lapse of one year from the date of payment of the first payment.

- The third payment, the value of which is 30% (thirty per cent) of the value of the amounts due, shall fall due at the end of the second year from the date of payment of the first payment.

- In the event of default in paying one of the instalments on its due date, all remaining instalments shall fall due in a single payment, and interest at the rate of 12% (twelve per cent) shall be added thereto until payment.

- The value of the total remaining instalments, including interest, shall be registered as a privileged debt on the real property folio of the property, provided that such registration shall authorise the recording of the constructions with the competent Land Registry Secretariat, and provided that they are paid in full prior to the subdivision of the property.

Deficiency in Occupancy:

1 - The violation shall be deemed settled on the date on which the offender pays the amount payable or pays the first instalment and arranges to pay the remainder by instalments in accordance with Paragraph 2 of the tenth Article of this Law. In such case, the Administration must grant the owner the habitation (occupancy) permit provided for in the Building Law if the building is completed within the meaning of the said Law; otherwise, the granting of this permit shall be suspended until the completion of the building and the execution of the works required by the laws and regulations in this regard.

2 - Any deficiency occurring in the works required pursuant to the laws and regulations, such as the use of specific materials such as stone and roof tiles, shall not be deemed a violation within the meaning of this Law and may not be settled pursuant to its provisions; rather, such deficiency must be completed on pain of not granting the occupancy permit.

Special provisions relating to individual and common parts:

Where a building is subdivided into individual parts (apartments, storeys), the regularisation of the violations occurring therein, which this Law permits to be regularised, shall take place in accordance with the following conditions:

1 - If the violations exist in the common parts of a building, the regularisation shall be effected on the basis of a decision of approval issued by the owners' association by a majority representing 75% (seventy-five per cent) of the owners of shares in the ownership of the common parts in accordance with the Law regulating common ownership in subdivided properties. In the absence of an owners' association, the regularisation shall be effected following the approval of the majority of owners representing 75% (seventy-five per cent) of the owners of shares in the ownership of the common parts, provided that such approval is registered with a notary public.

Exempted from this approval are buildings that have previously obtained a similar regularisation in one of their individual parts and buildings in which such violations constitute a proportion of 50% (fifty per cent) and above on the front facades and have not yet been regularised, whereas balconies pertaining to the remaining facades shall not be subject in their regularisation to any approval.

2 - If the violations exist in the individual parts (a subdivided apartment within the building), which are considered for the purposes of this Law as an independent property, the regularisation shall be effected upon the request of the concerned party without the need for the approval of the owners' association or of 75% (seventy-five per cent) of the owners of shares in the absence of an association, unless the violation does not cause a change to the external facades of the building.

3 - Where violations exist in the individual parts and in the common parts as well, the regularisation of the violations in the individual parts shall be conditional upon the fulfilment of the following two conditions:

a - That the owner of the individual part brings a lawsuit before the judiciary for the removal of the violation in the common parts, with a declaration that the violation occurred contrary to his will, and that this lawsuit is registered on the real property folio.

b - That the owner of the individual part submits an undertaking registered with a notary public whereby he authorises the municipality or the public authority to assume the responsibility of carrying out the demolition.

It shall suffice that the lawsuit and the authorisation be submitted by one owner only among the owners of the private parts in the property, without the need for them to be submitted by the remaining owners each time a real estate transaction requiring the same takes place.

4 - Where there is more than one offending building on a single property owned by more than one person, and where there is a multi-storey building on a single property owned by more than one person, the regularisation of the violations in each of these buildings may be carried out separately, subject to the approval of 51% (fifty-one per cent) of the owners of the land of the property, and the land area pertaining to such building for the purposes of the regularisation shall be calculated as equivalent to the shares owned by the applicant for regularisation in the ownership of the property.

A building in which the violations have been regularised in this manner shall be considered as a building in its own right and shall be registered as a separate individual part in the Land Register.

Where, however, there is more than one offending building on a single property owned by a single person, the regularisation must be carried out for all the offending buildings on the property at once.

5 - Regularisation, of whatever kind, shall not introduce any modification to the ownership rights in the common parts and in the individual parts of the building.

Valuation Procedures and Rules:

1 - The valuation of the price of the land on which the violation is located on private property shall be carried out by the committees that issue the valuation of the sale price per square metre for building permits.

2 - The valuation shall be carried out at the prices prevailing on the date of entry into force of this Law.

3 - No retroactive discount shall apply to violations committed between 1/1/2012 and 31/12/2018.

4 - A retroactive discount shall apply to violations committed prior to 1/1/2012, as follows:

- Violations committed from 13/9/1971 until 31/12/2002: a discount of 50% (fifty percent).

- Violations committed from 1/1/2003 until 31/12/2006: a discount of 40% (forty percent).

- Violations committed from 1/1/2007 until 31/12/2011: a discount of 30% (thirty percent).

Miscellaneous provisions:

1 - In all settlements effected pursuant to the application of the provisions of this Law, the liability of the violator towards third parties shall remain standing, and the rights of the latter in respect of the damage sustained by them by reason thereof shall be preserved pursuant to the laws in force.

2 - An application for the substitution of demolition by the payment of a fine shall not preclude the application of the laws and regulations relating to the exploitation of buildings, in particular those relating to classified establishments and the permitted locations of their presence, and establishments and businesses that cause nuisance to habitation, generate noise, or are detrimental to public health and safety.

3 - Violations shall be registered, until their final settlement or removal, on the real folio of the property. The value of the fees and fines shall also be registered as a privileged debt on the property, and the annotation shall not be lifted save on the basis of a written communication issued by the administration that requested its placement.

4 - Where the property is occupied by third parties or where a building exists on the property, whether subdivided or unsubdivided, and the violation was committed by the occupants or holders of the property against the will of the owner or one of the owners, transactions may be conducted on the property if the owner submits an irrevocable undertaking executed before a notary public and registers it on the real folio of the property, stating that the violation is subject to demolition and that he authorises the municipality or the public authority to carry out the demolition under his responsibility and at his expense; the owner may also settle the violation at his expense and under his responsibility.

5 - Violations occurring after the date of 1/1/2019 shall be demolished ipso jure.

6 - Fines incurred for delay in the total or partial payment of fees and fines on violations in respect of which assessments were issued on the basis of Law No. 324/94 shall be reduced, for one last time, by eighty per cent, provided that the amounts due are paid within a period of three months from the date of application of this Law.

In the absence of a sewage network, or in the event of non-connection thereto for any reason whatsoever, no building violation shall be settled until the building has been equipped with a sewage treatment plant in accordance with the required technical specifications and the lost-bottom wells for the discharge of wastewater have been sealed in accordance with technical standards and pursuant to the Law promulgated by Decree No. 8735 dated 23/5/1974 (Preservation of Public Hygiene), and after the submission of a plan and an engineer's certificate attesting thereto under his criminal liability and after an inspection by the competent authorities to verify the same.

Article One of the draft law put into effect by Decree No. 14273 dated 29/10/1963 and its amendments (Establishment of the State Employees' Cooperative) shall be amended as follows:

"A cooperative for state employees shall be established, the powers of which shall cover all public administrations, personnel on the cadre of the Lebanese University other than members of the teaching body, and civilian employees in the Customs, with the exception of the judiciary, the Army, the Internal Security Forces, the General Security, State Security, the civilian personnel attached thereto, and the Customs Brigade.

It may cover employees of public institutions, autonomous agencies, and municipalities subject to the oversight of the Civil Service Board in accordance with the provisions of Article Three of this Law."

The remainder shall remain without amendment.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Prescription:

The limitation period set forth in the laws in force, and in particular in the Public Accounting Law and the Law Determining the Rules of Accounting in Municipalities for rectifying concealment and deficiency in assessments or collection, shall not apply to the fees and fines provided for in the tenth Article of this Law.

Contrary Provisions:

All provisions contrary to this Law or inconsistent with its content are hereby repealed, and all provisions permitting the settlement of building conditions are also repealed, with the exception of Decree No. 11265 dated 11/11/1997 relating to the settlement of minor violations. The settlement of the building violations that are the subject of this Law shall be granted without prejudice to the rights of third parties.

The proceeds of the fees and fines resulting from the application of this Law shall be distributed as follows:

1 - The fees and fines arising from garage violations shall go in their entirety in favour of the municipality concerned, subject to the obligation to construct public garages.

2 - The proceeds of the remaining fees and fines arising from the application of this Law shall be distributed in the following manner:

- 30% in favour of the Public Corporation for Housing.

- 30% in favour of the municipalities concerned.

- 40% in favour of the Public Treasury.

Violations in respect of which lawsuits were instituted prior to the date of its entry into force, or those pursuant to which final judicial judgments were rendered prior to the date of entry into force of this Law, shall not be subject to the provisions of this Law.

Civil aviation easements and private real properties adjacent to the maritime domain The provisions of this Law shall not apply to violations committed:

1 - Within civil aviation easements.

2 - In private real properties located within nature reserves.

3 - In private real properties located within protection zones designated for antiquities.

4 - In private real properties adjacent to the maritime or riverine public domain, unless the owner of the real property produces a certificate from the competent authorities certifying the absence of any encroachment upon such domain or upon the legal setbacks from such domain, or any other reason preventing the carrying out of the settlement.

Details of Application of the Law:

Where necessary, the details of application of this Law shall be determined by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport after consulting the opinion of the Higher Council for Urban Planning.

Entry into Force:

This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

2- Commitment and payment appropriations shall be opened in the General Budget for loans contracted by the State, or contracted for its account.

Opening of Extraordinary Appropriations

In implementation of the provisions of Article 85 of the Constitution, the President of the Republic may, if emergency circumstances call for urgent expenditures, issue a decree based on a decision issued by the Council of Ministers, opening extraordinary or additional appropriations or transferring appropriations in the 2019 budget, provided that these appropriations do not exceed one hundred billion Lebanese pounds, and these measures must be submitted for the approval of the Chamber of Deputies at the first session in which it convenes thereafter.

Authorisation to Transfer Appropriations

1- Transfer within the reserve of the general budget from one item to another within this reserve is authorised by a decision of the Council of Ministers based on the proposal of the Minister of Finance. This measure shall apply to the reserve of each annexed budget.

2- Transfer of appropriations allocated to the salaries of the surplus of employees, contractors, wage earners and collaborators in public administrations, coupled with the approval of the Civil Service Board, from the administration from which they are transferred to the administration to which they are transferred, is authorised.

The transfer shall be effected by a decision of the Minister of Finance after the endorsement of the Central Controller of Expenditure Commitment.

3- Transfer of appropriations provided for in the budget of the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities - Administrative Departments - allocated to the Traffic, Trucks and Vehicles Management Authority to the budget of the said Authority after the issuance of its own regulations, is authorised by a decision of the Minister of Finance, after the endorsement of the Central Controller of Expenditure Commitment.

4- Transfer of appropriations provided for in the budget line "liquid fuels" for the benefit of the military bodies in the budget of the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities to the similar budget line in the other chapters is authorised by a decision of the Minister of Interior and Municipalities after the endorsement of the Central Controller of Expenditure Commitment.

Application of the provisions of foreign grant and loan agreements to the entirety of expenditure pertaining to externally financed projects

1- Expenditure under cash grant and foreign loan agreements concluded with the various public administrations, public institutions, and municipalities, following their approval pursuant to decrees issued by the Council of Ministers or laws enacted by the Parliament, whether such expenditure is from the local portion or the foreign portion, shall be subject to the oversight of the Court of Accounts in accordance with the rules, and the application of the provisions stipulated in the agreements and decrees relating to cash grants must in no case conflict with the recording of cash grants in the budget in accordance with the rules.

2- Funds received from donor entities shall be transferred to public administrations through the Ministry of Finance. Throughout the duration of the implementation of the project, and following the issuance of the decree accepting the grant, the Ministry of Finance shall open the appropriations necessary therefor and included therein, either all at once or successively, in the budget of the current fiscal year and in the budgets of subsequent fiscal years, according to the cash value transferred in each fiscal year by the donor entities to the donations and grants account pertaining to the Lebanese Treasury.

3- The provisions of the second paragraph of Article 27 of the draft law put into effect pursuant to Decree No. 14969 issued on 30/12/1963 shall not apply to supplementary appropriations relating to cash grants, whereby such appropriations may be transferred from one item to another by a decision of the competent minister and the Minister of Finance following the endorsement of the Central Controller of Expenditure Commitment, and after the concerned administration establishes the desire of the donor entity to effect such transfer.

4- The provisions of Article 104 of the draft law put into effect pursuant to Decree No. 14969 dated 30/12/1963 and its amendments (the Public Accounting Law) shall apply to emergency financial advances granted for the payment of expenditures financed by cash grants, and the appropriations reserved for emergency financial advances relating to grants given during a specific fiscal year to discharge obligations the execution of which extends beyond the year for the payment of expenditures financed by cash grants may be carried over to the budgets of subsequent fiscal years until the completion of the execution of the works relating to the grant.

5- All uncommitted balances of appropriations financed by cash grants shall be carried over to the budgets of subsequent years.

Granting Electricité du Liban a Treasury Advance and Addressing the Issue of Accumulated Debts

Electricité du Liban shall be granted a long-term Treasury advance in the amount of 1306 billion L.L. (one thousand three hundred and six billion Lebanese Pounds) to be added to the advance granted pursuant to Law No. 114 dated 22/3/2019 in the amount of 794 billion L.L. and to the advance granted pursuant to Decree No. 4341 dated 12/2/2019 in the amount of 400 billion L.L., that is a total of 2.500 billion Pounds (two thousand five hundred billion Lebanese Pounds), to settle the fuel purchase deficit and to settle the interest and instalments of loans in favour of Electricité du Liban, provided that the advance is paid by order of the Central Finance Accountant following the approval of the Minister of Finance and is settled in cash, and provided that the mere use of this advance by the borrowing entity is deemed an acknowledgment by it of the ability to repay in accordance with the bases stipulated in this Article.

Electricité du Liban may not, on its own responsibility, use the advance or any part thereof for other than the purpose for which it was granted.

The manner of repayment of this advance shall be determined in accordance with the provisions set forth in Article 13 of Law No. 79 dated 18/4/2018 (the Public Budget and Annexed Budgets Law for the Year 2018).

Provision of appropriations to subsidise the interest on investment loans

There shall be provided in the General Budget (Ministry of Finance – Directorate of Public Finance) the appropriations required to subsidise the interest on investment loans (agricultural, industrial, touristic, and technological, informational and environmental) and the profit margins on these loans with respect to Islamic banks.

The procedures and conditions for benefiting from the subsidised interest, and the profit margins on these loans with respect to Islamic banks, shall be determined pursuant to a special regulation issued by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance and after consulting the opinion of the Governor of the Bank of Lebanon, and the expenditure shall be subject to the procedures provided for in the Public Accounting Law.

As for the loans subsidised from the own funds of the Bank of Lebanon or the reserve funds held by it, it shall pertain to the Council of Ministers to issue a decision on the sectoral priorities for benefiting from the subsidy and its conditions, upon the proposal of the Ministers of Finance and of Economy and Trade after consulting the opinion of the Governor of the Bank of Lebanon.

Healthcare treatment appropriations

There shall be distributed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, upon the joint proposal of the competent Minister and the Minister of Finance, the appropriations allocated as a lump sum in the various titles of the General Budget designated for treatment in private and public institutions and hospitals and contracts with physicians in the private sector.

Deduction of a share of the revenues collected in favour of municipalities for villages that have no municipalities

The Ministry of Finance shall deduct from the revenues collected in favour of municipalities, prior to their distribution, an amount of six billion Lebanese Pounds, to be designated for lighting, works and cleaning in the villages that have no municipalities (charges for energy, maintenance, equipment and cleaning) through the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities. The revenues shall be distributed by a decree upon the proposal of the Ministers of Finance and of Interior and Municipalities, provided that the decree encompasses all the villages that have no municipalities.

Exemption of Public Institutions, Municipalities, Unions of Municipalities, and Other Persons of Public Law from the Fines Due from Them

Notwithstanding any other provision, municipalities, unions of municipalities, public institutions, and other persons of public law shall be exempted from all fines due from them resulting from violations relating to the tax on salaries and wages of their employees, in particular the delay in declaring that tax, or in paying it to the Treasury within the legal time limits, and from violations relating to the tax of Articles 41, 42 and 43 of the Income Tax Law (the tax on non-residents), and from violations relating to the fiscal stamp duty, including the failure to pay the fiscal stamp duty due on amounts paid by them to third parties, and the fines resulting from their occupation of public State property, provided that they carry out, within a time limit not exceeding 31/12/2019, the following:

- Paying all the taxes and fees due from them, including those pertaining to years barred by prescription, with respect to the taxes and fees that they withheld or collected and did not pay.

- Paying all the taxes and fees due from them pertaining to years not barred by prescription, with respect to the taxes and fees that they did not withhold or collect.

The time limit provided for in this Article shall be extended for up to six months from the date of 5/3/2020 (pursuant to Law Enacted by Operation of Law No. 6 dated 5/3/2020).

Reduction of Certain Fines Incurred in Favour of the State, Municipalities, Unions of Municipalities, Public Institutions, or Other Persons of Public Law

With the exception of fines resulting from violations for the settlement of which their special laws have laid down specific provisions, and fines resulting from the regularisation of violations on maritime public property, those resulting from building violations, and those incurred in favour of the National Social Security Fund, fines due to the State, municipalities, unions of municipalities, public institutions, or other persons of public law, whatever the method of their collection (receipt order, collection order...), shall exceptionally be reduced by 85%, provided that these arrears are paid together with the reduced fines within a time limit not exceeding 31/12/2019.

The time limit provided for in this Article shall be extended for up to six months from the date of 5/3/2020 (pursuant to Law Enacted by Operation of Law No. 6 dated 5/3/2020).

Amendment of Article 58 of the Income Tax Law

A- The tax rate for salaries, wages, and retirement pensions is set as follows:

- 2% (two percent) on the portion of net taxable income not exceeding /6.000.000/ L.L. six million Lebanese pounds. This rate shall be reduced by half on the basis of retirement pensions and the like.

- 7% (seven percent) on the portion of net taxable income exceeding /15.000.000/ L.L. fifteen million Lebanese pounds and not exceeding /30.000.000/ L.L. thirty million Lebanese pounds. This rate shall be reduced by half on the basis of retirement pensions and the like.

- 11% (eleven percent) on the portion of net taxable income exceeding /30.000.000/ L.L. thirty million Lebanese pounds and not exceeding /60.000.000/ L.L. sixty million Lebanese pounds. This rate shall be reduced by half on the basis of retirement pensions and the like.

- 15% (fifteen percent) on the portion of net taxable income exceeding /60.000.000/ L.L. sixty million pounds and not exceeding /120.000.000/ L.L. one hundred and twenty million Lebanese pounds. This rate shall be reduced by half on the basis of retirement pensions and the like.

- 20% (twenty percent) on the portion of net taxable income exceeding /120.000.000/ L.L. one hundred and twenty million Lebanese pounds and not exceeding /225.000.000/ L.L. two hundred and twenty-five million Lebanese pounds. - 25% (twenty-five percent) on the portion of net taxable income exceeding /225.000.000/ L.L. two hundred and twenty-five million pounds. This rate shall be reduced by half on the basis of retirement pensions and the like.

Amendment of Article 32 of Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (the Income Tax Law)

Article 32 of Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (the Income Tax Law) is amended to read as follows:

The rate of tax on the profits of commercial, industrial and non-commercial professions is set as follows:

- 4% (four per cent) on the taxable portion that does not exceed /9.000.000/ L.L. nine million pounds.

- 7% (seven per cent) on the taxable portion that exceeds /9.000.000/ L.L. nine million pounds and does not exceed /24.000.000/ L.L. twenty-four million pounds.

- 12% (twelve per cent) on the taxable portion that exceeds /24.000.000/ L.L. twenty-four million pounds and does not exceed /54.000.000/ L.L. fifty-four million pounds.

- 16% (sixteen per cent) on the taxable portion that exceeds /54.000.000/ L.L. fifty-four million pounds and does not exceed /104.000.000/ L.L. one hundred and four million pounds.

- 21% (twenty-one per cent) on the taxable portion that exceeds /104.000.000/ L.L. one hundred and four million pounds and does not exceed /225.000.000/ L.L. two hundred and twenty-five million pounds.

- 25% (twenty-five per cent) on the taxable portion that exceeds /225.000.000/ L.L. two hundred and twenty-five million pounds.

Repeal of exemptions from customs duties

Exemptions from customs duties granted prior to the issuance of this Law are repealed, and the repeal shall include exemptions from the minimum duty and from the domestic consumption duty, whether stipulated in the Customs Law or in other laws and regulations.

The following are excluded from the repeal:

a. Goods which agreements and treaties concluded between Lebanon and other parties stipulate shall benefit from full or partial exemption.

b. Machinery and raw materials used in agriculture and industry, and vehicles and equipment used by persons with special needs, within the rules stipulated in the laws governing these exemptions.

c. New environmentally non-polluting cars, whether operating on electricity (EV) or hybrid cars (Hybride)), in accordance with the provisions of Article 55 of Law No. 79 dated 18/4/2018.

d. Exemptions from customs duties stipulated in Law 57/2017 (Tax provisions related to petroleum activities in accordance with Law 132 dated 24/8/2010.

e. Goods proven to Customs to have been shipped directly to Lebanon prior to the publication of this Law, provided that the Higher Council of Customs, after consulting the opinion of the Director General of Customs, determines the mechanisms for applying this paragraph.

Repeal of certain exemptions on circulation and registration fees

Contrary to any other text, exemptions granted to certain persons and entities on the registration and circulation fees of all vehicles and machinery are repealed, with the exception of the exemptions granted to the following entities:

- Persons with special needs in accordance with their special law.

- The State and public institutions exclusively, and municipalities and unions of municipalities.

- Diplomatic and consular corps.

- The United Nations Organization and the agencies emanating therefrom.

- Ambulances and fire engines offered as donations to associations, municipalities, and unions of municipalities.

And that is within the rules stipulated in the laws governing these exemptions.

Construction Fees

Holders of rights in rem registered in the Real Estate Register who did not notify the Head of the Auxiliary Real Estate Office of the changes that occurred to the substance and contents of their real property within the period specified in the aforementioned Article shall be exempted from the double fee provided for in Article 60 of Decision No. 189 dated 15/3/1926 (Details relating to the implementation of Decision No. 188 dated 15/3/1926 concerning the Real Estate Register), if notification of these changes is made and the fee is paid within a time limit not exceeding 31/12/2019.

The time limit provided for in this Article shall be extended for up to six months from the date of 5/3/2020 (pursuant to Law Enforced by Operation of Law No. 6 dated 5/3/2020)

Addition of Article 154 - 1 to Law No. 243 issued on 22/10/2012 (the New Traffic Law), and amendment of the fourth paragraph of Article 154 thereof

There shall be added to Law No. 243 issued on 22/10/2012 (the New Traffic Law) Article 154-1, the text of which reads as follows:

"Article 154-1:

Notwithstanding paragraph 8 of Article 154 of this Law, distinctive passenger vehicle registration plate numbers shall be classified pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities, and all numbers falling outside this classification shall be deemed non-distinctive numbers".

Fees shall be imposed on owners of vehicle registration plates bearing distinctive numbers across all symbols except the symbols AP,AG,R,J,D,C, in accordance with the following:

First: Regarding the annual fee consideration on distinctive passenger registration plate numbers placed in circulation:

Flat-rate annual fees shall be imposed on distinctive registration plate numbers pertaining to vehicles in accordance with the classification set out in the annexed table.

These fees shall be paid annually together with the traffic fees, in accordance with the laws and decisions in force and the mechanisms prescribed therefor.

Default by the owner of the registration plate in paying this fee shall result in its accumulation to the following year, together with the accrual of fines calculated by the same mechanism applicable to annual traffic fees.

On a one-time basis, these fees shall be paid directly for the year 2019 independently of the traffic fees.

Second: Regarding the allocation consideration for a distinctive registration plate number:

1- A one-time allocation consideration shall be paid by a person wishing to acquire ownership of a registration plate bearing a distinctive number, after the date of entry into force of this Law, in accordance with the following:

1.1 Categories: (3.1,4.1,5.1,6.1,7.1) set out in the annexed table:

Distinctive numbers within these categories shall be offered to the public at a public auction, provided that each is put up at the opening bid price specified in the same table for each category.

A special committee shall undertake the organisation of this auction; the members of this committee shall be appointed and its operating mechanism shall be determined pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities.

1.2 The remaining categories:

The allocation consideration shall be paid in accordance with the amount specified in the annexed table opposite each category.

Upon payment of this consideration, the registration plate number shall become his property, and he shall be granted a deed of allocation from the Traffic, Trucks and Vehicles Management Authority in return therefor.

Third: Regarding the sale of a registration plate bearing a distinctive number to a third party:

It was made possible for owners of registration plates bearing distinctive numbers prior to the date of entry into force of this Law to obtain from the Traffic, Trucks and Vehicles Management Authority a deed of allocation for the number of each of them, in return for a fee equivalent to 5% of the allocation consideration pertaining to the category of the number in accordance with the annexed table, after paying the annual fees due from them.

Holders of deeds for distinctive numbers may sell their registration plates to third parties pursuant to a contract executed before a Notary Public; a transfer fee equivalent to 5% of the allocation consideration pertaining to the number shall be imposed on this sale, and as a result thereof the Authority shall issue a new deed in the name of the new owner.

A vehicle registered with a registration plate bearing a distinctive number may not be sold to third parties except after paying the allocation fee and obtaining the deed of allocation. Cases of transfer of ownership between ascendants and descendants shall be exempted therefrom, and this fee shall not fall due upon the execution of a determination of heirship.

Fourth: Regarding the waiver of a registration plate bearing a distinctive number in favour of the Administration:

The owner of a registration plate bearing distinctive numbers, including a registration plate placed in salvage, may waive their registration plates in favour of the Traffic, Trucks and Vehicles Management Authority, provided that his registration plate is replaced with a registration plate bearing a non-distinctive number without paying any fees, on a one-time basis only; this exemption shall cover more than one registration plate bearing a distinctive number owned by the same person.

The application for waiver shall be submitted to the Traffic, Vehicles and Trucks Management Authority, and this number shall be entered into the database of available distinctive numbers.

Fifth: Regarding the allocation consideration for a special non-distinctive number:

Any person wishing to register an available special non-distinctive number may register this number provided that he pays in return therefor, on a one-time basis, an allocation consideration equivalent to 400.000 Lebanese Pounds.

Sixth: Exemption from the payment of the traffic fee, of whatever kind, shall not cover exemption from the payment of the annual fee for a distinctive number, or the allocation consideration for a distinctive number, or the allocation consideration for a special non-distinctive number, provided for in this Article.

Seventh: The allocation considerations set out in the annexed table shall be exceptionally reduced by 20% for purchase transactions of registration plates bearing distinctive numbers during the year 2019.

The fee for the deed of allocation shall be exceptionally reduced to 3% of the allocation consideration as set out in the annexed table, if the fee is paid during the year 2019.

Eighth: Paragraph 4 of Article 154 of the New Traffic Law shall be amended so as to read as follows:

"4- The Latin letters Y-H-K-B-G-J-M-N-O-R-S-T-Z shall be used for private car registration plates belonging to all citizens. The letter P shall also be used for public cars, the letter D for the diplomatic corps, and the letter C for the consular corps".

Ninth: The detailed rules for the implementation of this Article shall be determined pursuant to a joint decision issued by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities and the Minister of Finance.

Execution of Sales in the Real Estate Register
