Extension of the time limits of the licences provided for in Article 11 of Decree No. 11614 dated 4/1/1969

1- The time limits of the licences provided for in Article 11 of Decree No. 11614 issued on 4/1/1969 and its amendments relating to the acquisition by non-Lebanese of real property rights in rem in Lebanon, whether expired or unexpired, may be extended for three years with effect from the date of entry into force of this text pursuant to a decree taken in the Council of Ministers.

2- In the event of the expiry of the extended time limit without commencing the construction of the building, a cumulative annual fine at the rate of 2% of the value of the real property shall be imposed on the owner of the real property, to be registered on the real property folio as a privileged debt in favour of the Treasury. When the value of the fine reaches 10% of the actual value of the real property, the real property shall be sold by public auction by the Ministry of Finance in accordance with the procedures set forth in the aforementioned Article 11. The fines accruing to the Treasury shall be collected.)

Reduction of Assessment and Collection Fines Imposed and Levied by the Directorate of Public Finance at the Ministry of Finance

With the exception of fines that require the approval of the Council of Ministers, assessment and collection fines due as of the date of publication of this Law relating to taxes and fees imposed and levied by the Directorate of Public Finance pursuant to the laws on direct and indirect taxes and fees shall be exceptionally reduced by 85%.

In order to benefit from the reduction referred to above, taxpayers shall pay the accrued taxes and fees in addition to the balance of the fines accrued thereon in full, within a maximum period ending on 31/12/2019.

The period provided for in this Article is extended for up to six months from the date of 5/3/2020 (by virtue of Law Effectively Enacted No. 6 dated 5/3/2020)

Reduction of Fines Due on Unpaid Collection Orders Issued by Public Administrations, Public Institutions, Municipalities, Unions of Municipalities and All Other Persons of Public Law

Fines due on unpaid collection orders issued by public administrations, public institutions, municipalities, unions of municipalities and all other persons of public law shall be reduced by 85%, provided that the collection orders together with the reduced fines are paid within a maximum period ending on 31/12/2019.

The period provided for in this Article is extended for up to six months from the date of 5/3/2020 (by virtue of Law Effectively Enacted No. 6 dated 5/3/2020)

Reduction of Fines Due on Motor Vehicle Inspection Fees (Mechanic Fees)

Fines due on motor vehicle inspection fees (mechanic fees) not paid within the legal deadlines shall be reduced by 85%, provided that these fees together with the reduced fines are paid within a maximum period ending on 31/12/2019.

The period provided for in this Article is extended for up to six months from the date of 5/3/2020 (by virtue of Law Effectively Enacted No. 6 dated 5/3/2020)

Amendment of Paragraph First of Article 51 of Law No. 497/2003, amended pursuant to Article Seventeen of Law No. 64/2017 and pursuant to Article Thirty-Six of Law No. 79/2018

Paragraph First of Article 51 of Law No. 497/2003, amended pursuant to Article Seventeen of Law No. 64/2017 and pursuant to Article Thirty-Six of Law No. 79/2018, is amended to read as follows:

First: Notwithstanding any other text, the following shall be subject to the provisions of the Income Tax Law (Legislative Decree No. 144/59 and its amendments) and to the tax of Title III thereof at the rate of ten percent (10%):

1. Interest, yields, and revenues of all credit accounts opened with banks, including savings (deposit) accounts, with the exception of accounts opened in the name of the Government, municipalities, unions of municipalities, and public institutions with the Bank of Lebanon, and the accounts of foreign diplomatic and consular missions in Lebanon.

2. Interest and yields of deposits and all other banking commitments in any currency whatsoever, including those pertaining to non-residents, with the exception of deposits between private banks (Interbank deposits.

3. Interest, revenues, and yields of fiduciary and fund management accounts.

4. Yields and interest of certificates of deposit issued by all banks and debentures issued by joint-stock companies.

5. Interest and revenues of Treasury bonds in Lebanese currency.

6. The rate of 10% shall apply as of the day following the date of publication of this Law, and shall remain in force for a period of three years, and the application of the rate of 7% shall be reinstated as of the day following the expiry of the third year.

The detailed rules for the application of this Article shall be determined, where necessary, by a decision of the Minister of Finance.

Reduction of Fines Due on Municipal Fees and Assessment Fines

1- Fines due on municipal fees and assessment fines not paid within the legal time limits shall be reduced by 85%, provided that such fees together with the reduced fines are paid within a time limit not exceeding 31/12/2019.

2- All late payment fines paid in accordance with the laws in force prior to the entry into force of this Law shall be deemed a right of the municipality and may not be refunded.

3- Such taxpayers may pay the amounts due from them in instalments over a maximum period of 5 years at an annual interest rate of 5%, provided that 20% of the value of the arrears together with the reduced fines is paid within a time limit not exceeding 31/12/2019. In the event of default in the payment of any instalment on the specified due date, an additional interest at a rate of 12% shall be imposed on the amounts paid in instalments.

The details of the application of this Article shall be determined, where necessary, pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities.

The time limit provided for in this Article shall be extended for up to six months from the date of 5/3/2020 ( pursuant to Law enforced ipso jure No. 6 dated 5/3/2020 )

Reduction of Fines Due on Municipal Fees Due from Tourist Establishments

A-

1. Fines due on municipal fees due from tourist establishments shall be reduced by 85%, provided that such arrears together with the reduced fines are paid within a time limit not exceeding 31/12/2019.

2. All late payment fines paid in accordance with the laws in force prior to the entry into force of this Law shall be deemed a right of the municipality and may not be refunded.

3- Such establishments may pay the amounts due from them in instalments over a maximum period of 5 years at an annual interest rate of 5%, provided that 20% of the value of the arrears together with the reduced fines is paid within a time limit not exceeding 31/12/2019. In the event of default in the payment of any instalment on the specified due date, an additional interest at a rate of 12% shall be imposed on the amounts paid in instalments.

B- Liable tourist establishments that have previously arranged to pay in instalments, by operation of law or at their request, the municipal fees, surcharges or fines incumbent upon them shall benefit from the reduction, in the event that they pay them in full or pay their balances within the same time limit specified above.

The time limit provided for in this Article shall be extended for up to six months from the date of 5/3/2020 ( pursuant to Law enforced ipso jure No. 6 dated 5/3/2020 )

Reduction of Fines and Late Surcharges Due on Contributions to the National Social Security Fund

Unpaid fines and late surcharges due on contributions to the National Social Security Fund in all its branches within their statutory time limits shall be reduced by 100% in respect of the years 2000 and earlier and by 85% in respect of the remaining years, provided that the establishments pay those contributions together with the reduced fines, if any, within a time limit not exceeding 31/12/2019, and it shall not be permissible to benefit from the reduction in respect of some periods to the exclusion of other periods.

Such establishments may pay the amounts due from them in instalments over a maximum period of five years at an annual interest rate of 5%, provided that 20% of the value of the contributions together with the reduced fines and surcharges is paid within a time limit not exceeding 31/12/2019, and in the event of default in the payment of one of the instalments on the fixed due date, an additional interest rate of 12% shall be imposed on the amounts paid in instalments.

The time limit provided for in this Article is extended for up to six months from the date of 5/3/2020 (pursuant to Law Enacted by Operation of Law No. 6 dated 5/3/2020)

Granting an Additional Time Limit to Object to Taxes and Duties Assessed by the Directorate of Public Finance

Taxpayers subject to taxes and duties assessed by the Directorate of Public Finance who have been notified of such taxes and duties and have not paid them in full up to the date of issuance of this Law and have not objected to them within the statutory time limit provided for in Articles 97 and 99 of Law No. 44 dated 11/11/2008 and its amendments (Tax Procedures Law), or who have objected to them and whose objections were rejected as to form at the stage of objection before the Tax Administration or before the Objection Committees, shall be granted an additional time limit to submit their objections thereto before that Administration or before those Committees for a period of six months from the date of issuance of this Law, provided that they pay 10% of the taxes, duties and fines due prior to submitting those objections, and where the amount required to be paid in accordance with the rate referred to above is less than the value of the fines due, the full value of the fines must be paid.

The Tax Administration shall examine the objections submitted to it in accordance with this Law and shall decide thereon before the end of the year following the year of publication of this Law.

The time limit provided for in this Article is extended for up to six months from the date of 5/3/2020 (pursuant to Law Enacted by Operation of Law No. 6 dated 5/3/2020)

Exemption of taxpayers subject to the provisions of Article 53 of the Income Tax Law from assessment and collection fines

Employees, workers, and wage earners provided for in Article 53 of Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (the Income Tax Law), who simultaneously hold a post or work in several establishments or premises, or who simultaneously practice a profession subject to the tax of Title I of the same Legislative Decree, shall be exempted from the fines for late filing of the declaration and from the fines for late payment of the tax, for the years 2018 and prior, provided that they declare and pay the taxes due from them or pay those assessed on them, within a time limit not exceeding 31/12/2019. They may also pay these taxes in instalments without interest over three years, provided that a down payment of twenty-five percent (25%) of the value of these taxes is paid within a time limit not exceeding 31/12/2019, and fines paid prior to the publication of this Law shall be deemed a right of the Treasury that cannot be refunded.

The time limit provided for in this Article shall be extended for up to six months from the date of 5/3/2020 (pursuant to Law Enacted Improved Ipso Jure No. 6 dated 5/3/2020)

Payment in instalments of taxes withheld at source and value added tax

Notwithstanding any other text, and exceptionally and for one time only, taxes withheld at source and value added tax due from taxpayers for the tax periods up to 31/12/2018 may be paid in instalments in accordance with the provisions governing payment in instalments in Law No. 44 dated 11/11/2008 (the Tax Procedures Law), pursuant to a written application submitted by the taxpayer within a time limit not exceeding 31/12/2019, provided that the first payment amounting to 15% of the value of the taxes paid in instalments is paid within the same time limit.

In the event of default in paying the remaining instalments on their due dates, all instalments shall fall due and an additional interest at a rate of 12% shall be payable thereon.

The details for the implementation of this Article shall, where necessary, be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

The time limit provided for in this Article shall be extended for up to six months from the date of 5/3/2020 (pursuant to Law Enacted Ipso Jure No. 6 dated 5/3/2020)

Conducting a settlement on assessments relating to taxes assessed and collected by the Directorate of Public Finance submitted before the Objections Committees

Notwithstanding any other text, and on an exceptional basis, assessments relating to taxes assessed by the Directorate of Public Finance, objected to before the Objections Committees and which have not been adjudicated up to 31/3/ 2019, shall be settled.

The value of the settlement shall be determined at fifty per cent (50 %) of the value of the objected-to taxes only, without the assessment and collection fines that were due.

In order to benefit from this settlement, the taxpayer must submit a written application to the competent tax administration and pay the amount that falls due on him as a result of the settlement within a time limit not exceeding 31/12/2019. The taxpayer may also pay 25% of the value of the settlement, within the same time limit, and pay the remaining amounts in three annual instalments, the first of which falls due upon the lapse of one year from the payment of the first instalment of the value of the settlement at the interest rate provided for in the Tax Procedures Law, and in the event of default in paying one of the instalments, all the instalments shall fall due and the taxpayer shall be liable for an interest rate of 12% per annum on the unpaid amounts.

The taxpayer may not choose to benefit from the settlement in respect of a part of a single assessment issued by the tax administration, such that the settlement covers all the objected-to points and periods within the single assessment.

The Objections Committees notified by the tax administration of the taxpayer's application to conduct the settlement shall cease adjudicating the objection.

Taxpayers who have paid in instalments the tax due from them prior to the entry into force of this Law and where all the instalments have not been paid, and taxpayers who have benefited from the provisions of Article 40 of Law No. 66 dated 3/11/2017 (the General Budget and Annexed Budgets Law for the year 2017) or the provisions of Article 23 of Law No. 79 dated 18/4/2018 (the General Budget and Annexed Budgets Law for the year 2018) prior to the entry into force of this Law, may benefit from the provisions of this Article in accordance with the following:

The value of the settlement shall be determined at:

Fifty per cent (50% of the value of the objected-to taxes) after deducting the paid portion of the tax only.

Related text: Determining the details of application of the provisions of Article 41 of Law No. 144 dated 1/7/2019 (the General Budget and Annexed Budgets Law for the year 2019) in respect of conducting a settlement on assessments relating to taxes assessed and collected by the Directorate of Public Finance submitted before the Objections Committees

The time limit provided for in this Article shall be extended up to six months from the date of 5/3/2020( pursuant to Law Enforceable by Operation of Law No. 6 dated 5/3/2020 )

Striking off Companies and Commercial Establishments from the Commercial Register and Civil Companies from the Special Register of Civil Companies

1. Companies and commercial establishments that have not actually practiced business or have ceased practicing their business and had no assets, or have liquidated their assets during the year preceding the year that lapses by prescription, and have no employees, shall be struck off ipso jure from the Commercial Register and from the Special Register of Civil Companies.

2. For the striking off of these companies and establishments, it is required that no debts to third parties be owed by them and that they have paid all taxes and fines due from them and the fees and fines pertaining to the National Social Security Fund, and to all other public administrations and public institutions for the periods during which they had practiced business prior to the year referred to in Paragraph 1 of this Article, and all fines and the fiscal stamp duty due for the renewal of their term, if any, shall be remitted for the periods subsequent to this date.

3. The Ministry of Finance shall prepare, within three months from the publication of this Law, a list of the establishments and companies that meet the conditions set forth in Paragraph 1 above, and notify it to the National Social Security Fund and to the Chief Clerks of the Commercial Register, and these bodies shall lodge with the Ministry of Finance, within a period of two months from the date of being notified of the list, their observations regarding it as to whether or not fees or fines are due from those establishments and companies in their favour.

The Ministry of Finance shall publish on its website, in the Official Gazette, and in two local newspapers on two dates separated by fifteen days, a detailed statement of the companies and establishments that will be struck off, within a maximum period of one month from the date of being notified of the reply of the National Social Security Fund and the replies of the Chief Clerks of the Commercial Register, and it must also notify those companies and establishments of its decision relating to striking them off from the Commercial Register or the Civil Register at the last correspondence address registered with it.

4. The Ministry of Finance shall comply with the provisions of Paragraph 3 of this Article within three months from the beginning of each year subsequent to the year in which this Law is published.

5. These companies, the owners of establishments, all other public administrations and public institutions, and creditors may object before the Ministry of Finance to the striking-off decision within a period of three months from the date of the last announcement in the Official Gazette, on the website of the Ministry of Finance, or in the two local newspapers, and the procedures for completing the striking-off operations for these companies and establishments shall be suspended until the objection is decided upon, and the interested parties may request the annulment of the administration's decision rejecting the objection before the State Council, which must decide upon it finally within a period of three months from the date of registration of the petition for review.

Summary procedures shall apply before the State Council in accordance with its regulations.

6. Companies and establishments whose striking-off decision has not been objected to within the period referred to in Paragraph 5 above shall be struck off from the assessment rolls in the Ministry of Finance and from the registers of the Commercial Register offices, the civil registers, and the registers of the National Social Security Fund, and the Ministry of Finance shall publish in the Official Gazette and on its website a list of the names of the companies and establishments that have been struck off.

7. The details of implementation of this Article shall be determined, where necessary, pursuant to a decision issued by the Ministers of Finance and Justice.

Repealing the text of Article 44 of Law No. 144 dated 31/7/2019 (General Budget and Annexed Budgets for the year 2019),

The text of Article 44 of Law No. 144 dated 31/7/2019 (General Budget and Annexed Budgets for the year 2019) shall be repealed and replaced with the following text:

Amending Article 46 of Law No. 173 dated 14/2/2000

Article 46 of Law No. 173 dated 14/2/2000 shall be amended to read as follows:

1- The value of the fines imposed on foreigners who violate the provisions of Articles 32, 33, 36 and 37 of the Law Regulating Entry into, Residence in, and Exit from Lebanon issued on 10/7/1962 and amended by Law 173/2000 shall be doubled.

2- An additional annual fee equal to half of the work permit fee, collected upon obtaining the permit for the first time and upon its renewal every year, shall be imposed on the foreign worker who brings his spouse or wife or one of his sons or one of his daughters to Lebanon, and this measure shall apply to the categories in accordance with the law and the regulations in force.

3- The second article of the Law issued on 17/9/1962 replacing Articles 107 and 108 as amended pursuant to Article 46 of Law 173 dated 14/2/2000 shall be amended as follows:

Every violation of the provisions of the Labour Law or the decrees and decisions adopted for its application and execution shall subject its perpetrators, both the employer, whether Lebanese or foreign, and the foreign worker, to the drawing up of a citation report with a value ranging between two million Lebanese pounds and five million Lebanese pounds.

In the event of settlement within fifteen days from the date of drawing up the citation report, it shall be replaced by an amount equivalent to twenty percent of the value of the citation report.

In the event that the settlement is not made within the period referred to above, the violation report shall be referred to the competent courts to impose the penalty of doubling the fine or imprisonment from one month to three months.

In the event of recidivism within a single year, the value of the citation report as well as the penalty of imprisonment shall be doubled.

Conducting an exceptional revaluation of the fixed assets of income tax taxpayers and of the real properties covered by the provisions of Item (c) of Third of Article 45 of the Income Tax Law amended pursuant to Article 13 of Law No. 64 dated 20/10/2017

1- An exceptional revaluation may be conducted of the fixed assets of income tax taxpayers and of the real properties covered by the provisions of Item (c) of Third of Article 45 of the Income Tax Law amended pursuant to Article 13 of Law No. 64 dated 20/10/2017, in accordance with the following:

a- Conducting an exceptional revaluation of the fixed assets of income tax taxpayers:

Natural and legal persons who are required to keep regular accounts pursuant to legal or regulatory provisions, with the exception of real estate companies, may, for one time only and within a time limit expiring on 31/3/2020, conduct an exceptional revaluation of the elements of fixed assets (including shares, debt securities, participation bonds and shares, real properties and other fixed assets) in order to correct the effects of monetary inflation resulting from the change in the values of those assets.

The revaluation operation shall cover all the assets referred to in the preceding paragraph that are recorded in the enterprise's books at a date prior to the first of January 2019, provided that the value of the revalued assets does not exceed the market price as at 31/3/2020.

The revaluation operation shall be carried out by an accounting firm or one or more court-accredited experts chosen by the party concerned.

The positive variances resulting from the revaluation operation shall be subject to a new proportional tax at a rate of 3% (three percent) of the value of these variances.

Taxpayers assessed on a lump-sum or estimated profit basis shall benefit from the revaluation set out in this Article, if the existence of documents permitting the revaluation of the elements of fixed assets is established.

In all events, these provisions may not, in respect of banks, conflict with the Code of Money and Credit and all other regulatory and implementing texts issued by the Banque du Liban.

Taxpayers who enjoy exemptions or exceptions from income tax on profits, or who previously enjoyed such exemptions or exceptions even if their term expired before the issuance of this Law, shall not benefit from the provisions of this paragraph.

In the event that any of the assets revalued in accordance with the provisions of this paragraph is disposed of before the lapse of three years from the date of the revaluation, the capital gain shall be calculated as the difference between the disposal value of the asset and its value prior to its revaluation.

b- Conducting an exceptional revaluation of the real properties covered by the provisions of Item (c) of Third of Article 45 of the Income Tax Law amended pursuant to Article 13 of Law No. 64 dated 20/10/2017:

Natural and legal persons referred to in Item "c" of Article Thirteen of Law No. 64 dated 20/10/2017 may, for one time only and within a time limit expiring on 31/12/2019, conduct an exceptional revaluation of the real properties that they own.

The revaluation operation shall be carried out by an accounting firm or a court-accredited expert chosen by the party concerned.

The positive variances resulting from the revaluation operation shall be subject to a new proportional tax at a rate of 2% (two percent) of the value of those variances.

2- The parties concerned referred to in paragraphs "a" and "b" above shall pay the tax difference resulting from the introduction of an increase to the revaluation result within a time limit of two months from being notified of the Administration's decision, under penalty of the accrual of interest at a rate equal to the interest rate on five-year Treasury bonds until payment, and they may recover the tax difference due to them in the event of a reduction of the valuation, pursuant to a written request submitted by them to the competent financial unit.

The tax on the positive variances resulting from the revaluation operation shall be paid in cash concurrently with the submission of the application for approval of the revaluation to the Tax Administration.

The competent financial unit shall decide on the revaluation operation, and if it refuses to approve its result or amends this result, it must notify the parties concerned of its decision of refusal or amendment, and the latter shall have the right to object before the Objections Committee competent for income tax in accordance with the rules provided for in the Tax Procedures Law.

3- The time limit granted for conducting the revaluation operation may be extended twice only, each time for a period of six months, pursuant to a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

4- The rules for implementing this Article shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

The time limit provided for in this Article is extended for up to six months from the date of 5/3/2020 (pursuant to Law Enacted Ipao Jure No. 6 dated 5/3/2020)

Obliging municipalities, when licensing the occupancy of real properties by commercial, industrial or professional companies and establishments within the jurisdiction of each of them, to notify the Ministry of Finance of the establishments and professions that do not have a tax number

Municipalities shall be obliged, upon an application for a licence, to grant a temporary licence for the occupancy of real properties by commercial, industrial or professional companies or establishments within the jurisdiction of each of them, provided that they grant a final licence after verifying, within a time limit of two months from their granting of the temporary licence, that the company, establishment or profession is registered with the Ministry of Finance, and they must notify the Ministry of Finance within fifteen days from the end of each quarter with a list showing the professions, establishments and companies that have obtained a licence from them and have not registered with the Ministry of Finance.

Registration of contracts for the assignment of rights in rem in the Real Estate Register within a specified time limit from the date of their execution

First: Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary, the concerned parties who execute before the Notary Public, or before Lebanese diplomatic missions, a contract of sale and irrevocable powers of attorney the subject of which is the assignment of rights in rem shall proceed to implement such contracts and powers of attorney at the Real Estate Registry offices and pay the due fees within a time limit of three years from the date of their execution.

Second: In the event of non-compliance with the time limit specified in Clause First, double the fee shall be imposed on the concerned party upon the implementation of the contracts of sale and powers of attorney that are the subject of the assignment, and each of the Notary Public and the Lebanese diplomatic missions shall inform the contracting party of the content of this Article and indicate the same in the text of the instrument.

Double the fee shall also be collected in the event of cancellation of the contract of sale or the irrevocable power of attorney and the execution of a new instrument in favour of the same purchaser or any of his relatives up to the fourth degree.

Third: Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary, the concerned parties who executed before the Notary Public, or before Lebanese diplomatic missions, a contract of sale and irrevocable powers of attorney the subject of which is the assignment of rights in rem prior to the effective date of this Law, shall proceed to implement such contracts and powers of attorney before the Real Estate Registry offices and pay the due fees within a time limit of four years from the effective date of this Law, and in the event of non-compliance with this time limit, the provisions of Clause Second regarding the doubling of the due fee shall apply to them.

Addition of Item 13 to Article 1 of Law No. 44 dated 11/11/2008 and its amendments (Tax Procedures Law)

There shall be added to the First Article of Law No. 44 dated 11/11/2008 and its amendments (Tax Procedures Law) Item 13 reading as follows:

13- Tax Evasion

Tax evasion is the deliberate act by a person bound by tax obligations of failing to declare taxes and duties due to the State and accruing on his income or wealth, and failing to pay the taxes and duties that he is obliged to withhold or collect, or reducing such taxes and duties, or cancelling them, or deducting them, or refunding them without legal right, through the use of unlawful means and methods, the most important of which are:

- Concealing taxable revenues.

- Undertaking taxable or dutiable business or transactions without complying with the obligation to submit a notice of commencement of business and consequently with the obligation to declare such business and transactions.

- Establishing accounts outside the accounting records.

- Conducting operations without recording them in the records or without disclosing them adequately.

- Recording fictitious expenses.

- Recording fictitious financial liabilities or liabilities for other than their actual purpose.

- Using falsified documents.

- Deliberate destruction of accounting documents before the date prescribed by law.

- Failing to submit returns and statements relating to business results or the tax base.

- Exercising a tax deduction or refund without legal right.

- Undertaking transactions and procedures designed to incur fictitious obligations and burdens towards third parties, even if they take a legal form.

- Failing to declare import and export operations at their true value.

- Failing to declare all employees.

- Failing to issue invoices or similar documents in due form.

- Concealing the beneficial owner, in accordance with the definition prescribed therefor by law, from any source of funds and in any manner whatsoever.

Treatment of Illegal Occupation of the Maritime Public Domain:

First:

The treatment of illegal occupation of the maritime public domain shall not confer upon the violator any vested rights against the State, which shall have the right at any time to revoke such occupation and recover its maritime public domain without any financial compensation of any kind whatsoever accruing to the violator as a result thereof.

The payment of the fine prescribed for previous periods, and the fines due for each year licensed pursuant to this Article, shall not be deemed a settlement of the violation or of the encroachment committed upon the maritime public domain, and consequently shall not create for the illegal occupant any right of any kind whatsoever, and the occupant of any area of the maritime public domain or of the bed, subsoil, or surface of the territorial waters who has not treated his illegal occupation of the maritime public domain shall be required to vacate such area, and the Ministry of Public Works and Transport - Directorate General of Land and Maritime Transport, referred to in the subsequent paragraphs as the Administration, shall take possession of such area.

Second:

By way of exception, pursuant to a decree issued upon the proposal of the Ministers of Public Works and Transport and of Finance, provided that the rights of third parties are not prejudiced, existing encroachments upon the maritime public domain shall be treated and temporary occupation of such domain shall be permitted, effective from the date of publication of this Law, subject to the fulfilment of the following conditions:

1 - That the illegal occupation takes place within the cases and conditions specified in Paragraph Third of this Article and is subject to the fines provided for in Paragraph Eighth of this Article.

2 - That the actual illegal occupation took place prior to 1/1/1994, and does not conflict with the designated use assigned to it in the zone in which the maritime public domain subject to the occupation is located, in accordance with the regulations in force.

3 - That the illegal occupation has not:

- Resulted in damage to archaeological or historical sites, or in posing a hazard to public safety and health, or to the safety of civil aviation, or in violating easements legally imposed for air navigation or broadcasting, or in violating any other conditions legally imposed.

- Resulted in the disfigurement of the coast or in damage to the environment.

- Occurred on public facilities or the exploitation of public ports, or services of public utility, or related to projects that can only be licensed pursuant to a law.

- Occurred on a public road leading to the seashore and/or the sea.

4 - Ensuring the continuity of the coast for the general public, while the Ministry of Public Works and Transport reserves the right to establish or maintain:

- Open parts of the maritime public domain occupied under a licence or requested to be permitted for occupation in accordance with the provisions of this Article, as passages for access to the seashore and/or to the sea in order to preserve the unity of the continuity of the coast.

- Main and secondary roads leading to the seashore and/or the sea.

- Encroachments occurring prior to the date of 1/1/1994:

Third:

Encroachments occurring on the maritime public domain occupied prior to 1/1/1994 in violation of the law shall be treated, and the amount of the annual fines to be paid shall be determined, effective from 1/1/1994 and in accordance with the nature of the violation and according to the status of each of them:

1 - If the real property contiguous to the maritime public domain occupied in violation of the law is public property of the State:

The Administration shall take possession of the occupied maritime public domain, and it shall be vacated in accordance with the provisions of Paragraph Seventh of this Article. In this case, an annual fine equal to twice (x 2) the annual fees in accordance with Decree 2522 dated 15/7/1992 shall be imposed for the period extending from 1/1/1994 until the date of vacation of the maritime public domain.

2 - If the real property contiguous to the public domain occupied in violation of the law is private property of the State or of public institutions or of municipalities, the Administration shall take possession of the illegally occupied maritime public domain and it shall be vacated unless the illegal occupant proves, within a period of nine months effective from the date of entry into force of this Law, that he has obtained a lease contract thereon for a term of not less than three years, provided that the total leased area amounts to half the area of the occupied maritime public domain and its frontage is not less than the frontage of the said domain, and in this case the annual fines provided for in the following table shall be imposed:

7 - If the violation occurs on private property contiguous to the maritime public domain, the provisions of the Building Violations Settlement Law No. 324/94 dated 24/3/1994 shall apply to the constructions and buildings erected in violation of the law on the private property contiguous to the maritime public domain and linked to the exploitation of the maritime public domain, for the violations whose status is treated in accordance with the provisions of this Article.

In all cases and situations resulting from the application of this Article, the liability of the violator shall remain standing towards third parties, and the rights of such parties to compensation for the damage sustained by them by reason thereof shall be preserved.

Fourth:

Permanent constructions on the maritime public domain that are not considered complementary annexes to the constructions erected on the private real property, such as sports, organizational, and recreational facilities, cabins, and restaurants that must be located close to the coast, shall be demolished at the expense and responsibility of the violator.

Permanent constructions on the maritime public domain that are considered complementary annexes to the constructions erected on the private real property, such as sports, organizational, and recreational facilities that must be located close to the coast, shall be maintained, provided that they are in conformity with the provisions of the Urban Planning Law and the implementing provisions relating to the maritime public domain.

Permanent constructions on the maritime public domain that exceed the standards specified above shall be demolished at the expense and responsibility of the violator.

Fifth:

1 - The violator must submit to the Administration, within a period of six months from the date of publication of Law 132 dated 30/4/2019, an application for the treatment of his status and for permission for temporary occupation.

Notwithstanding any other text, a violator who has not applied for the treatment of his status within the extended period shall be liable to a fine amounting to three times the fine calculated had he submitted an application for treatment, and the measures of vacation and taking of possession provided for in Paragraph Seventh of Article 11 of Law No. 64 dated 20/10/2017 shall be applied against him.

2 - The applications submitted shall be examined by the Administration, which shall prepare a report on the existing occupation and the extent of conformity of the violation with the terms of its treatment in accordance with the provisions of this Article.

The Administration must decide upon the application within a period of six months from the date of its submission.

The Minister of Public Works and Transport may, by a reasoned decision upon the request of the Administration, grant an additional period not exceeding six months to decide upon the application.

3 - In the event that the occupation or a part thereof is deemed to fall within the violations mentioned in Item 3 of Paragraph Second, the Administration shall require the occupant to remove all violations, disfigurements, or damages within a period of six months from the date of notification, under penalty of not granting him a licence and of the removal of the violations, disfigurements, or damages by the Administration at the responsibility and expense of the violator.

Upon verification of the removal of the violations set out above within the period of six months from the date of notification of removal, the Administration shall resume the examination of the application, and the six-month period shall run from the date of removal of the violation.

4 - Where the violation is deemed to fall within the violations whose status may be settled in accordance with the provisions of this Article, the Administration shall require the violator to prepare an environmental impact assessment study for the existing project in accordance with the provisions of Law No. 444 dated 29/7/2002 (Environment Protection Law) and its implementing decrees and decisions, in particular the Environmental Impact Assessment Procedures Decree No. 8633 dated 7/8/2012 and its amendments, and to prepare an environmental management plan which must provide for the following:

a - Compliance with the specifications and standards relating to air pollutants and liquid waste generated by classified establishments and water treatment plants as determined by the Ministry of Environment.

b - Compliance with sound management of solid waste, including the sorting operations of all recyclable materials (glass, plastic, paper, cardboard...) and transporting them to specialized institutions for recycling at the expense of the concerned party.

c - Preparation of a periodic report every six months on how the environmental standards specified in this Item are being observed.

The violator must prepare the environmental impact assessment study for the project within a period of three months from the date of the Administration's request.

5 - The Ministry of Environment must decide upon the environmental impact assessment study and the environmental management plan within a period of two months from the date of its submission.

6 - Upon the violator's completion of all the requirements set forth in the items of this Article, the Administration shall prepare a draft decree upon the proposal of the Ministers of Public Works and Transport and of Finance treating the encroachments and permitting temporary occupation within a period of one month from the date of the violator's completion of all the requirements set forth in the items of this Paragraph and payment of the amounts due in accordance with the provisions of Paragraph Eighth of this Article.

Sixth:

In all cases where temporary occupation is permitted on the basis of a lease or exploitation contract for the private real property contiguous to the maritime public domain, the contract shall be registered with the Notary Public and the concerned municipality and on the real propertyfolio of the property, and the permission for occupation shall be deemed terminated upon the expiration of the term of the said contract.

Seventh:

In all cases where the Administration takes possession of the occupied areas of the maritime public domain in accordance with the provisions of this Article.

1 - Such areas shall be vacated by their occupants without any right or compensation of any kind whatsoever accruing to them or to those deriving their rights from them against the Administration.

2 - An occupant who does not vacate the occupied areas shall be deemed an encroacher and the penal laws governing such situations shall apply to him.

3 - The annual fines shall remain due from the occupant for the period of occupation prior to the execution of the vacation, and he must pay them in accordance with the provisions of this Article.

4 - The Administration reserves its right to maintain the constructions and backfills existing on such areas or to require their demolition and removal by itself or by the violators, and in both cases at the expense and responsibility of the violators, and in this case the costs of such work shall be collected pursuant to collection orders issued by the Administration.

Eighth:

For the purpose of calculating the fines for the period prior to the date of occupation, the rates and values of the annual fees specified by Decree No. 12841 dated 25/4/1963 as amended by Decree No. 2522 dated 15/7/1992 shall be adopted for the period from 1/1/1994 until 31/12/2015, and Decree No. 2522 dated 15/7/1992 and its amendments shall apply in respect of the period subsequent to the date of 31/12/2015, in accordance with the following treatment: Fine due = (Annual fee for the occupied area (multiplied by) multiplier rates (multiplied by) number of years).

The occupant must pay the amount of the fees and fines as follows:

1 - For the period prior to the date of treatment:

- The violating occupant must pay the amounts due from him within a period of three months from the date of his notification of the collection order issued by the Administration, and in the event of payment of such amounts in a single lump sum, he shall be exempted from 20% of the fines due from him.

- The violating occupant may request, within a period of one month from the date of his notification of the collection orders, the payment by instalments of the amounts due over a period of five years in five or ten equal instalments, the first instalment of which shall fall due within the first month from the date of approval of the payment by instalments. In this case, an annual interest at a rate equal to the interest rate on five-year Treasury bonds on the date of approval of the payment by instalments shall apply to him, and the total value of the instalments with their interest shall be registered as a privileged debt on the real property folio of the contiguous real property owned by the occupant; otherwise, the violating occupant must submit a bank guarantee equivalent to the total value of the instalments with their interest.

In the event of delay in paying any instalment, all remaining instalments shall fall due in a single lump sum.

2 - For the period subsequent to the date of treatment:

In the cases that are treated in accordance with the provisions of this Article and for which occupation decrees are consequently issued, the fees for each year shall be paid within the first month of the year in accordance with the fees in force pursuant to this Article, for the entirety of the occupied areas according to the multiplier rates on the brackets as per the following table:

Ninth:

The permission for temporary occupation shall be deemed revoked ipso jure in the event of default in paying the due instalments on the dates specified pursuant to the approval granted for payment by instalments, and the occupation decree shall be revoked ipso jure. In this case, the Administration shall take possession of the occupied maritime public domain and it shall be vacated, and the amounts and instalments shall remain due in all events.

The payment of the fine in this context shall not be deemed a settlement of the violations or of the encroachment and shall not create for the violator any right of any kind whatsoever.

Tenth:

Penal prosecutions initiated prior to the entry into force of this Article against occupants of the maritime public domain prior to 1/1/1994 without a legal licence shall be stayed, and the annotation on the contiguous private real property subject to the treatment shall be struck off and the penal prosecutions shall lapse, in the event that the occupants obtain a decree permitting them occupation in accordance with the provisions of this Article. In the event that they do not obtain the said decree, the penal prosecutions shall be pursued and the Administration shall take possession of the occupied maritime public domain and it shall be vacated in accordance with Paragraph Seventh of this Article.

Encroachments occurring after the date of 1/1/1994

Eleventh:

In respect of encroachments occurring after the date of 1/1/1994, violators shall be required, on a one-time basis, to pay the following fines:

Fine = Area occupied by encroachment (multiplied by) 5 (multiplied by) the appraised price per square metre on the date of entry into force of this Law for the contiguous private real property according to the cadastral zone in which the violation is located as specified in Decree No. 2522 dated 15/7/1992 and its amendments.

The violating occupant must remove the violations and pay the amounts due from him within a period of three months from the date of publication of this Law, and he shall benefit from the reductions and the provisions on payment by instalments referred to above.

General and Transitional Provisions

Twelfth:

The prescription periods specified in the laws in force, and in particular in the Public Accounting Law, shall not apply to the fees and fines mentioned in this Article.

The fines and fees set forth in this Article shall be collected in accordance with the provisions of Law No. 147 dated 12/6/1959.

Thirteenth:

If the occupation involves more than one violation, the provisions provided for and set forth above shall apply to each violation separately.

Fourteenth:

In the cases set out above. And for the purpose of treating the violations occurring prior to the date of 1/1/1994, the provisions of Decree No. 4810 dated 24/6/1966 and its amendments that conflict with the bases adopted for treatment in this Article shall not apply.

Fifteenth:

Every occupant licensed to exploit the maritime public domain who violates the principle of access to the beaches via the main and secondary roads leading to the seashore and/or the sea, by imposing a direct or indirect measure or by placing or establishing any physical barrier, shall be punished by a fine of fifteen million to fifty million Lebanese pounds, and he must remove the violation immediately.

In the event of repetition of the violation, the maximum fine referred to above shall be imposed on the violator with the requirement to remove the violation; however, in the event of repetition twice, the maximum fine specified above shall be doubled and the operation of the licence shall be suspended until the removal of the violation, without the violator being entitled to any compensation or damages of any kind whatsoever.

Sixteenth:

The detailed rules for ensuring the continuity of the coast within the maritime public domain, and for determining all the conditions that secure this right on the one hand and protect private ownership on the other hand, as well as determining any measures that secure the right of citizens to access the coast, shall be determined by decrees taken in the Council of Ministers, within three months from the date of publication of this Article, upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport.

Every occupant licensed to exploit the maritime public domain who violates the provisions of the decrees shall be punished by a fine of fifteen million to fifty million Lebanese pounds, and he must remove the violation immediately,

In the event of repetition of the violation, the maximum fine referred to above shall be imposed on the violator with the requirement to remove the violation; however, in the event of repetition twice, the maximum fine specified above shall be doubled, and the operation of the licence shall be suspended until the removal of the violation, without the violator being entitled to any compensation or damages of any kind whatsoever.

Seventeenth:

A rate of 1% (one per cent) per annum shall be deducted from the revenues of the annual fines imposed on the occupation of the maritime public domain in accordance with the rules, to be allocated in the budget of the Directorate General of Land and Maritime Transport for the establishment, equipping, maintenance, and operation of free public swimming pools in implementation of the National Programme for Free Public Swimming Pools along the Lebanese coast.

"New Article 66:

First: In zones where the number of storeys and height are specified

A - In unbuilt real properties, it shall be permitted to license an additional storey with a pitched roof not included in the total exploitation ratio and the number of storeys and heights permitted in the zone, in accordance with the following conditions:

1- That the clear height of the pitched-roof storey shall not exceed one metre and eighty centimetres (1.80 m) at the edge of the storey and four metres and a half (4.5 m) as the maximum clear height, provided that the slope of the roof is not less than twenty-five degrees (25 degrees).

2- That the roof of the pitched storey be completely covered with tiles or with other materials to be determined by the Higher Council for Urban Planning, and that it include no less than fifteen percent (15%) of the area of the pitched storey in solar panels for power generation fully integrated with the cladding materials. The external building structure erected pursuant to this amendment shall be deemed an integrated unit with respect to the cladding and facing materials used on the exterior, both in the vertical sections, if any, and the pitched sections.

3- That the area allocated for common services shall not be less than fifteen percent (15%) of the roof area and with a minimum of thirty-five square metres (35 m2), and that it be completely covered with the same cladding materials and/or solar panels, and that independent access thereto be secured.

B - In built real properties subdivided into various rights, the following documents must be attached to the licensing file:

1- The approval of all owners of rights to the added building and the area allocated for common services, executed before a notary public.

2- A duly issued certificate attesting to the capacity of the existing building to bear the requested additions, in accordance with the conditions of the Public Safety Decree from the structural standpoint.

3- That the clear height of the pitched-roof storey shall not exceed one metre and eighty centimetres (1.80 m) at the edge of the storey, four metres and a half (4.5 m) as the maximum clear height, provided that the slope of the roof is not less than twenty-five degrees (25 degrees).

4- That the roof of the pitched storey be completely covered with tiles or with other materials to be determined by the Higher Council for Urban Planning, and that it include no less than fifteen percent (15%) of the area of the pitched storey in solar panels for power generation fully integrated with the cladding materials. The external building structure erected pursuant to this amendment shall be deemed an integrated unit with respect to the cladding and facing materials used on the exterior, both in the vertical sections, if any, and the pitched sections.

5- That the area allocated for common services shall not be less than fifteen percent (15%) of the roof area and with a minimum of thirty-five square metres (35 m2) and that it be completely covered with the same cladding materials and/or solar panels, and that independent access thereto be secured.

Second: In zones where the number of storeys and height are not specified

A- An increase of (0.25)% to the total exploitation ratio exclusively may be made.

B- In built real properties subdivided into various rights, only one storey may be added, provided that the increase to the total exploitation ratio does not exceed (0.25)%, and the following documents must be attached to the licensing file:

1- The approval of all owners of rights to the added building and the area allocated for common services, executed before a notary public.

2- A duly issued certificate, attesting to the capacity of the existing building to bear the requested additions, in accordance with the conditions of the Public Safety Decree from the structural standpoint.

C- The area allocated for common services must not be less than fifteen percent (15%) of the roof area and with a minimum of thirty-five square metres (35 m2), and it must be completely covered with the same cladding materials and/or solar panels, and independent access thereto must be secured.

D- That the roof of the top storey be completely covered with materials to be determined by the Higher Council for Urban Planning, and that the roof of the storey include no less than fifteen percent (15%) of the area of the storey in solar panels for power generation fully integrated with the cladding materials, and providing for a garden at a rate of no less than forty percent (40%) of the area of the top roof. The external building structure erected pursuant to this amendment shall be deemed an integrated unit with respect to the cladding and facing materials used on the exterior, both in the vertical sections, if any, and the pitched sections.

Third: In unbuilt real properties, licensing applicants wishing to benefit from the provisions of this Law must, in addition to what is set forth in paragraphs (First) and (Second), fulfil the following conditions:

A- Installing a wastewater treatment plant.

B- Securing tanks for water collection and treatment at a minimum rate of five cubic metres (5 m3) for each residential apartment.

Fourth: The following zones shall be exempted from the provisions of this Article:

A- Zones in which the building conditions impose special requirements for the shape of the tiled roof structure.

B- Zones allocated for villas and private residences.

C- Buildings that have been subject to laws on the settlement of building violations.

D- All buildings that have benefited from exceptional laws regarding heights or number of storeys.

E- Servitude zones whose regulations include special detailed maps in which the building regulations are specified.

Fifth: Property owners who wish to benefit from the provisions of this Article must pay a fee equivalent to:

- Thirty percent (30%) of the value of the notional land required to secure the area of the storey mentioned above when the total exploitation ratio does not exceed one (1) after the increase.

- Forty percent (40%) when the total exploitation ratio after the increase is higher than one (1) and does not exceed two (2).

- Fifty percent (50%) when the total exploitation ratio after the increase is higher than two (2).

The committees accredited to appraise the selling price per square metre for granting building permits shall appraise the price per square metre to determine the fees due.

Sixth: The revenues collected pursuant to this Article shall be distributed as follows:

- Thirty-five percent (35 %) of the fees to the account of the Central Treasury Fund.

- Thirty percent (30 %) of the fees to the account of the Public Corporation for Housing.

- Thirty-five percent (35 %) of the fees to the account of the municipality concerned.

Seventh: Where necessary, the implementing decrees of this Law shall be issued upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport.

Exemption of convicts from paying financial fines

By way of exception, and for one time only, all convicts who have served the term of their sentence and remain imprisoned for failure to pay the financial fines to which they were sentenced are exempted from all fines of any kind whatsoever so that they may be released from prison, and non-Lebanese prisoners handed over to the Lebanese General Security to be deported in accordance with the rules.

Convicts of the offence of facilitating drugs are excluded from this measure.

Rescheduling of instalment programmes for the various taxes and duties assessed and collected by the Directorate of Public Finance

Notwithstanding the provisions of Article 61 of the Tax Procedures Law, and for one time and by way of exception, the collection offices in the Directorate of Public Finance may reschedule the instalment programmes for the various taxes and duties assessed and collected by the Directorate of Public Finance, the instalments of which taxpayers failed to pay on their due dates prior to the effective date of this Law, provided that the rescheduling application is submitted and the first payment is paid within a time limit not exceeding three months from the effective date of this Law, that the instalment period does not exceed three years from the date of payment of the first payment, and that interest at the rate of 12% applies to the rescheduled amounts.

In the event that the taxpayer fails to pay any of the instalments on time, the remaining instalments shall fall due, and interest at the rate of 15% shall be imposed thereon.

The details of the application of this Article shall be determined, where necessary, by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

The time limit provided for in this Article is extended up to six months from the date of 5/3/2020 (pursuant to Law Enacted by Operation of Law No. 6 dated 5/3/2020)

Extension of the time limits of building permits

Notwithstanding any other text and by way of exception, all building permits whose original and additional time limits have expired are extended for two additional years, and building permits whose additional time limits expire within a period of one year from the date of publication of this Law are extended for one year.

A lump-sum fee shall be imposed on the owner of an electric generator who sells power to the public, in the amount of 100,000 L.L. (one hundred thousand Lebanese pounds) annually per KVA of the capacity of this generator, and the payment of this fee shall not be deemed a licence or a settlement of any violation. (Applicable from the date of) 1/1/2024

This fee confers any rights upon the owner of the generator, and he shall be prohibited from adding its value onto the persons who draw power from him, and he shall be required to abide by the tariff set by the Ministry of Energy and Water, and this fee shall be deemed one of the deductible charges from the revenues subject to tax of a taxpayer subject to income tax on the basis of actual profit.

This fee shall be declared and paid annually in advance in accordance with a form drawn up by the Ministry of Finance during the month of January of each year, and during the month following the month in which the generator is put into use when using the generator, and late declaration and payment shall be subject to the penalties provided for in the Tax Procedures Law with respect to the tax on profits.

Notwithstanding the provisions of the paragraph above, the declaration and payment of the fee for the year 2019 shall take place within a time limit not exceeding 31/03/2020.

All municipalities shall be obliged to conduct a comprehensive survey to enumerate all generators used in the field of selling power within their municipal jurisdiction, and to communicate the results of this enumeration to the Ministry of Finance within a time limit not exceeding 31/03/2020, and they shall also be obliged to notify the Ministry of Finance of every electric generator used in the future periodically during the month following the end of each quarter, on the basis of a detailed statement determined by the Ministry of Finance.

Municipalities that own electric generators and sell power to the public shall not be subject to this fee.

The details of application of this Article shall be determined, where necessary, pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

Freezing Referral to Retirement for a Period of Three Years

Notwithstanding any special or general provision, applications for referral to retirement shall be frozen - with the exception of the case of reaching the legal age, the cases governed by the provisions of Article 39 of the Civil Servants' Regulations, and the cases governed by the National Defence Law, Article 51 clauses 2 and 3 in respect of officers and Article 57 clauses 4 and 6 in respect of non-commissioned officers and enlisted personnel, for a period of three years from the date of entry into force of this Law.

The judicial corps, and officers of the rank of colonel and above, shall be exempted from these provisions.

Regulating Recruitment in the Military and Security Corps and Privileges

The Government shall be required, within a period of six months from the date of entry into force of this Law, to issue the necessary decrees and decisions to review:

- The adoption of new bases for recruitment in accordance with civilian and military duties within each military or security institution.

- The allocation of vehicles, mobile and landline telephone numbers, and fuel quantities, for non-military use.

Maximum reduction of expenditure shall be observed in the review.

Suspension of employment and contracting in public administrations and institutions

The Government undertakes to conduct a comprehensive functional survey across all State administrations, its public institutions, its autonomous services and funds, boards of directors, councils, and all institutions and designations funded partially or wholly by the State, and a survey of occupied and vacant cadres, and to establish a modern integrated vision in cooperation with specialised consulting firms and the State public institutions concerned with personnel affairs (the Civil Service Board, and the Central Inspection) provided that a copy thereof is notified to the Chamber of Deputies.

Notwithstanding any other text, and until the completion of the survey operation mentioned above, all cases of new employment and contracting shall be suspended in public administrations and institutions including the educational, military and security sectors in their various designations and specialisations under all designations: contracting, daily worker, purchase of services, (with the exception of expenditure within the limits of the appropriations allocated to each administration and contracts that are renewed annually) or the like in the public sector including the enlistment operation in replacement of those referred to retirement.

Judges, professors of the Lebanese University, First Category employees, chairmen and members of the boards of directors of public bodies and institutions, and the confirmation into the permanent cadre of Civil Defence volunteers shall be exempted from the provisions of the second paragraph.

The right of successful candidates in the competitive examinations and examinations conducted by the Civil Service Board pursuant to a decision of the Council of Ministers and the results of which were duly announced, to be appointed in the concerned administrations, shall be preserved.

The following articles shall be added to Part One of Chapter Two of Title Three of Book Two of the Code of Commerce:

Article 121 bis 1:

Subject to the provisions of Law No. 308 dated 3/4/2001 relating to the issue and trading of bank shares, any joint-stock company may create registered preferred shares enjoying certain privileges, rights, pecuniary benefits or priorities, and benefiting from all the rights provided for in Article 105 of this Code, with the exception of the right to participate in discussions and vote in general meetings, the right to hold office as a member of the board of directors, and the right to share in the assets of the company.

3- Notwithstanding the provisions of item (2) of this Article, the company may grant its shareholders a pre-emptive right to subscribe for the issued preferred shares, provided that the conditions for exercising this right are determined in the articles of association of the company or by virtue of a resolution of the extraordinary general meeting of shareholders that creates the preferred shares.

Article 121 bis 3:

Preferred shares are prohibited from representing a proportion exceeding thirty percent (30%) of the registered shares representing the capital of the company as at the date of issue of these shares.

Article 121 bis 4:

The articles of association of the company or the resolution of the extraordinary general meeting that decides to issue the preferred shares shall determine the privileges, priorities, rights or other pecuniary benefits enjoyed by these shares, in particular the priority dividend allocated to them and whether this dividend is cumulative or non-cumulative (cumulatif ou non cumulatif).

Where the company has profits for a given financial year, it must distribute the priority dividend allocated to the preferred shares, and if it appears to the company that it has no profits or that its profits are insufficient to pay the whole or part of the priority dividend allocated to the preferred shares, the available profits shall be distributed to the holders of the preferred shares in proportion to the shares they hold, and the recovery of the balance of the priority dividend due, where it is cumulative, shall be carried forward to the following financial year and, where necessary, to subsequent financial years.

The priority dividend shall not be distributed until after deduction of the amounts distributed pursuant to the provision relating to fixed interest provided for in Article 109 of this Code; as for the remaining balance, the decision on how to distribute it shall rest with the ordinary general meeting, provided that such distribution does not conflict with the articles of association of the company and with the resolution of the extraordinary general meeting that created the preferred shares.

The issue of new preferred shares may not prejudice any of the rights attached to the preferred shares, or to the priority shares provided for in Article 110 of this Code, or to the bonds convertible into shares, any of which were issued on a date prior to the issue of the new preferred shares, except after obtaining the approval of the special meeting composed of each class of holders of such shares or bonds.

Article 121 bis 5:

Notwithstanding the provisions of Article 121 bis, the holders of preferred shares shall acquire a voting right equal to the right of the other shareholders in proportion to what the shares they hold represent in the capital of the company in the following cases:

1- Where a cumulative or non-cumulative priority dividend has been determined for the preferred shares and has not been paid in full or in part, as the case may be, for a single financial year despite the availability of profits in the company for that year.

This right shall remain in effect until the expiry of the financial year in which the full priority dividend due is paid.

2- Where the company fails to secure for the preferred shares the benefit of the other privileges, priorities or rights established for them.

This right shall remain in effect for as long as the established privileges, priorities or rights have not been secured for the beneficiaries.

3- In general meetings relating to changing the object or form of the company, or paying up an increase of its capital in kind, or dissolving it before its term, or to absorption, merger or demerger operations to which it is a party.

Article 121 bis 6:

Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary, the holders of preferred shares shall, upon each issue, form a special meeting that shall be convened, held, and adopt its resolutions in the manner of the meeting of debenture holders in accordance with Articles 137, 138 and 139 of this Code.

The special meeting of holders of preferred shares may issue one or more advisory opinions on matters submitted to the general meetings of the company's shareholders or on any matter on which the holders of preferred shares consider it in their interest to express an opinion.

The special meeting of holders of preferred shares shall communicate this opinion to the company so that the general meeting may be informed thereof and so that it may be recorded in the minutes of the latter.

This special meeting may also appoint a representative of the holders of preferred shares to attend the general meetings of shareholders, and this representative shall, where applicable, have the right to express the opinion of the meeting he represents before the vote is taken, in which he is not entitled to participate. This opinion shall be recorded in the minutes of the general meeting of the company.

Article 121 bis 7:

The chairman and members of the board of directors, the general managers and assistant general managers appointed in accordance with the provisions of Article 153 of this Code, and their spouses and minor children are prohibited from owning preferred shares or acquiring any kind of rights over these shares, directly or indirectly, or under the guise of a natural or legal person, or in any manner whatsoever.

Article 121 bis 8:

In the event of an increase of the company's capital by the creation of new shares subscribed for in cash, the holders of preferred shares shall not have a pre-emptive right to subscribe for the new shares in accordance with the provisions of Article 112 of this Code; however, the company may grant the holders of preferred shares a pre-emptive right to subscribe for the new shares issued and determine the conditions for exercising this right in the articles of association or by virtue of a resolution of the extraordinary general meeting of shareholders, in which case the provisions of the second paragraph of Article 113 of this Code shall not apply.

If the company carries out an increase by incorporating reserve funds of whatever kind or retained earnings, or by distributing new bonus ordinary shares, or by increasing the nominal value of the share, the holders of preferred shares shall not benefit from this distribution or from this increase unless otherwise provided either in the articles of association of the company or in the resolutions issued by the extraordinary general meeting that created the preferred shares.

Article 121 bis 9:

The company is prohibited, from the date of issue of the preferred shares and throughout the period during which such shares exist, from carrying out any redemption of its capital in accordance with Article 115 of this Code.

In the event of a reduction of capital for reasons not resulting from losses, the company must purchase and cancel the preferred shares before any purchase of ordinary shares or reduction of their nominal value, without prejudice to the application of the provisions of Articles 208 and 209 of this Code, and provided that all priority dividends due and that will fall due up to the date of payment are paid in full. In this case, the value of the preferred shares shall be determined on a date prior to or simultaneous with the purchase by agreement between the company and the special meeting of holders of preferred shares, and in the event of disagreement, the actual value of the share as at the date of the resolution to reduce the capital shall be determined by one or more certified accounting experts appointed by the two parties by agreement; if such agreement cannot be reached, the expert or experts shall be appointed by the President of the Commercial Court within whose jurisdiction the head office of the company is located.

Article 121 bis 10:

The company shall be entitled to purchase the preferred shares provided that:

1- This right and the bases and conditions for its exercise, in particular the timing and price of the purchase, are provided for by an express clause in the articles of association of the company or in the resolution of the extraordinary general meeting that previously decided to issue the shares sought to be purchased.

2- This purchase takes place after all due and unpaid priority dividends attached to any issue of preferred shares made by the company have been paid in full, unless the resolution issuing the preferred shares provides otherwise.

Article 121 bis 11:

Upon the dissolution and liquidation of the company, the nominal value of the preferred shares and the unpaid priority dividend in full attached to those shares shall be paid before any payment of the value of the ordinary shares. Furthermore, and notwithstanding the provisions of Article 121 bis 1, the share of the liquidation proceeds attributable to the preferred shares may be paid where the articles of association of the company provide for, or the extraordinary general meeting that created the preferred shares resolved to grant, their right to benefit from the said proceeds. In the absence of benefiting from the liquidation proceeds, and notwithstanding any other provision, the holders of these shares shall be entitled by operation of law to the value of the issue premium paid by them upon subscribing for the said shares.

Article 121 bis 12:

Preferred shares may be converted into ordinary shares by virtue of a resolution of the extraordinary general meeting issued on the basis of a special report of the auditors, in accordance with the conditions, bases and time limits provided for in the articles of association of the company or determined by the extraordinary general meeting that created the preferred shares.
