For the purposes of applying this Decree and in addition to the definitions contained in Article 1 of Law No. 80/2018, the terms listed below shall have the meaning indicated next to each of them:

1 - The Convention:

The Basel Convention on the Control of Transboundary Movements of Hazardous Wastes and their Disposal, the conclusion of which was authorised by Law No. 387/1994.

- 2 Wastes:

Substances or objects which are disposed of, or are intended to be disposed of, or are required to be disposed of.

3 - Hazardous Wastes:

Solid, semi-solid, or liquid wastes resulting from any activity which contain residues or compounds of residues that lead to an actual hazard or a potential hazard to the environment by reason of their quantity, concentration, mixture, or physical, chemical, or biological characteristics, and these wastes include the following:

1 - Wastes that belong to any category contained in Annex I to the Convention and defined in this Decree as Appendix I (A);

2 - Wastes that belong to any category contained in Annex II to the Convention and defined in this Decree as Appendix II, and that possess any of the characteristics contained in Annex III to the Convention;

3 - Wastes listed in Annex VIII (List A) to the Convention and defined in this Decree as Appendix I (B);

4 - Wastes that possess any of the characteristics contained in Annex III to the Convention and defined in this Decree as Appendix III;

5 - A mixture of hazardous wastes belonging to any of the categories listed above with other substances or wastes, even if non-hazardous

4 - Non-Hazardous Wastes:

Wastes with non-hazardous characteristics which are not included in the list of hazardous wastes prepared on the basis of the definition of hazardous wastes.

5 - Radioactive Wastes:

Wastes that emit ionising radiation, whatever their nature.

6 - Hazardous and Infectious Wastes Resulting from Healthcare Establishments:

Those defined in Decree No. 13389/2004.

7 - Environmentally Sound Management of Hazardous Wastes:

The operations of prevention, reduction of production, sorting at source, collection, transport, storage, recovery, treatment, and final disposal of hazardous wastes by taking all steps to ensure that hazardous wastes are managed in a manner which will protect the environment and public health against the adverse effects which may result from the mismanagement of such wastes.

8 - Sorting of Hazardous Wastes:

Manual or automated operations aimed at separating types and classes of wastes from one another at the source of their production and according to their characteristics, for the purpose of managing them in an environmentally sound manner.

9 - Collection of Hazardous Wastes:

Organised activities aimed at removing wastes from the source of their production and transporting them to designated collection centres for the purpose of managing them in a manner suited to the type, class, and characteristics of the waste.

10 - Generator of Hazardous Wastes:

Any natural or legal person, public or private, whose activity leads to the generation of hazardous wastes, and if that person is unknown, the person who is in possession or control of those wastes.

11 - Carrier of Hazardous Wastes:

Any natural or legal person, public or private, who carries out the transport of hazardous wastes within the borders and who is licensed to transport hazardous wastes.

12 - Hazardous Waste Storage Facility:

A facility designated, designed, and licensed for storing hazardous wastes.

13 - Final Disposal of Hazardous Wastes:

Any operation specified in Section (A) of Annex IV to the Convention and defined in this Decree as Appendix IV (A) which does not lead to the possibility of resource recovery, recycling, reclamation, direct re-use, or alternative uses.

14 - Treatment of Hazardous Wastes:

Biological and/or physical and/or chemical treatment operations of hazardous wastes referred to by codes D2, D8, and D9 in Section (A) of Annex IV to the Convention and defined in this Decree as Appendix IV (A), which result in compounds or mixtures which are disposed of by means of any of the operations for the final disposal of hazardous wastes.

15 - Transboundary Movement:

Any movement of hazardous wastes or other wastes from an area under the national jurisdiction of a State to / or through an area under the national jurisdiction of another State, or to / or through an area not under the national jurisdiction of any State, provided at least two States are involved in the movement.

16 - Initial Environmental Examination:

A preliminary study aimed at identifying the potential environmental impacts of a given project in order to determine the extent of the necessity of conducting an environmental impact assessment study for the project.

17 - Environmental Impact Assessment:

Identifying, estimating, and assessing the impacts of a given project on the environment and determining the necessary measures to mitigate negative impacts and increase positive impacts on the environment and natural resources prior to issuing the decision to approve or reject the project.

18 - Environmental Management Plan:

The set of mitigation measures, monitoring and control means, and institutional procedures taken during the construction, operation, or decommissioning of a project which would eliminate negative impacts or reduce them to locally acceptable levels, if any, and otherwise in accordance with United Nations standards. The "Environmental Management Plan" shall be deemed an integral part of the "Environmental Impact Assessment" report.

19 - Environmental Licence:

The licence issued by the Ministry of Environment in accordance with the provisions of this Decree which authorises the carrier of hazardous wastes and/or the storage facility and/or the recovery facility and/or the treatment facility and/or the facility for the final disposal of hazardous wastes to carry out one or more of the aforementioned acts.

20 - Best Available Techniques:

Means the most effective and advanced stage in the development of activities and their methods of management which indicates the practical suitability of particular techniques for providing in principle the basis for imposing restrictions designed to prevent the generation of hazardous wastes and their impact on the environment and public health, and, where that is not practicable, generally to reduce the generation of hazardous wastes and their impact on the environment and public health.

21 - Off-site:

Means any site outside the boundaries of the property or properties in which the operations of generation and/or collection and/or storage and/or treatment and/or disposal take place.

This Decree aims to define the rules of hazardous waste management in application of Law No. 80 dated 10/10/2018 (Integrated Solid Waste Management), in particular Article 27 (Clause 2) thereof.

The rules of hazardous waste management include a characterization and classification of such waste, as well as the establishment of an appropriate monitoring and control system to regulate the operations of generation, sorting, collection, transport, storage, recovery, treatment and final disposal of hazardous waste, with the aim of limiting the negative impacts of such waste on the environment.
This Decree shall apply to every generator and/or transporter and/or storage facility and/or recovery facility and/or facility for the treatment and/or final disposal of hazardous waste.

There shall be excluded from the provisions of this Decree the types and categories of non-hazardous waste resulting either from industrial establishments, or from dangerous, unhealthy and noxious establishments, or from commercial activities, or from agricultural activities, or from household activities. There shall also be excluded from the provisions of this Decree radioactive waste and hazardous and infectious waste resulting from healthcare establishments, to which their own specific provisions shall apply.

The Minister of Environment shall define the environmental foundations for establishing and operating collection centres for hazardous waste resulting from industrial, commercial, agricultural and household activities, and shall issue specific instructions and guidelines relating to the manner of handling such waste by its generators, collectors, transporters, storers, processors and disposers.

In application of Law No. 80 dated 10/10/2018 (Integrated Solid Waste Management), in particular Article 25 thereof, the National List annexed to Law No. 64 issued on 12/8/1988 shall be amended with respect to hazardous and industrial solid waste and shall be replaced by the table annexed to this Decree; Annex Five, which is based on the international characterization set forth in the Convention.

The Minister of Environment shall issue a decision determining the principles for implementing a national inventory of hazardous waste from all sources of its generation. These principles shall be amended whenever the need arises.

The Ministry of Environment shall prepare a national inventory of hazardous waste from all sources of its generation in cooperation with the relevant national entities when needed.

The Ministry of Environment shall update the national inventory of hazardous waste every five years at most.

The Ministry of Environment shall establish, within a period of six months from the issuance of this decree, an information system and an electronic database for managing information related to hazardous waste, provided that the provisions of this system are determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Environment.

Every natural or legal person, public or private, shall work to reduce the rates of generation of hazardous waste resulting from its activity by adopting integrated environmental management, using less harmful raw materials such as environmentally friendly alternatives, and using the best available techniques.

Every generator of hazardous waste shall declare the same by filling out the waste data form and classifying and characterizing the hazardous waste among it at the site of its generation in accordance with the model approved by the Ministry of Environment.

The procedures, rules, models and particulars for submitting declarations, filling out forms and keeping records relating thereto, and the time limits for completing administrative transactions, shall be determined by decisions and circulars issued by the Minister of Environment.

The Ministry of Environment shall have the right to request the generator of hazardous waste to analyze the waste resulting from its activity in a laboratory if the need arises, provided that the sampling and analysis operations are carried out by an accredited laboratory and that the cost of sampling and analysis is borne by the waste generator. The tests and indicators required to be examined and the methods to be adopted in measurement shall be specified in the request.

1 - Every generator of hazardous waste shall sort it within the property or properties in which it is licensed to carry out a specific activity, and then pack the hazardous waste in dedicated and suitable containers conforming to the internationally recognized conditions for that purpose.

2 - The generator shall affix an adhesive identification label on the containers dedicated to packaging hazardous waste in accordance with the model approved by the Ministry of Environment.

3 - Every generator of hazardous waste shall store the hazardous waste packaged according to Item (1) above within the property or properties in which it is licensed to carry out the activity, for the purpose of transporting it to a licensed storage facility.

A hazardous waste generator shall not receive hazardous waste generated from other activities or facilities and store it within its facility unless the generator holds an environmental licence for a storage facility.

1) A hazardous waste generator may transport hazardous waste, provided that the provisions stipulated in this Decree in respect of a transporter of hazardous waste and other relevant texts in force are observed.

2) A hazardous waste generator may establish and operate a specialised facility or facilities for the storage and/or recovery and/or treatment and/or final disposal of hazardous waste within the property or properties in which it is licensed to carry out a specific activity where the hazardous waste is generated, provided that the provisions stipulated in this Decree in respect of facilities for the storage, recovery, treatment and final disposal of hazardous waste and other relevant texts in force are observed.

Every generator of hazardous waste shall comply with the following rules and procedures prior to commencing the operation of transporting it outside the property or properties of its generation:

1 - Ensuring that the hazardous waste is packaged in containers designated and suitable for packaging it and conforming to the internationally recognised conditions for that purpose.

2 - Ensuring the integrity of the containers designated for packaging the hazardous waste and the presence of an adhesive identification label thereon.

3 - Not permitting the transport of any shipment of hazardous waste outside the property or properties without using the hazardous waste movement form in accordance with the model adopted at the Ministry of Environment, provided that this form accompanies the shipment at all stages of its transit.

4 - Not handing over any shipment of hazardous waste to a transporter or a storage, recovery, treatment or final disposal facility not licensed by the Ministry of Environment.

5 - Not permitting the transport of any shipment of hazardous waste outside the property or properties without obtaining the preliminary written approval from the storage, recovery, treatment or final disposal facility, provided that the relevant approval is attached to the hazardous waste movement form at all stages of its transit.

The generator shall take back the hazardous waste generated by its activity in the event that it is not accepted upon delivery at the storage, recovery, treatment or final disposal facility for reasons relating to its failure to meet the technical conditions required to be satisfied according to the preliminary written approval, provided that the refusal by the facility is reasoned in writing.

The generator shall store the hazardous waste that has been taken back within the licensed real property or properties for a specified period of time not exceeding 30 days from the date it was taken back, provided that it takes the appropriate technical measures to manage it in an environmentally sound manner in accordance with the laws and regulations in force, with a view to resending it to the storage, recovery, treatment or final disposal facility.

The generator shall officially notify the Ministry of Environment of the aforementioned take-back operation within a time limit of three days from the date of its occurrence.

The generator of hazardous waste shall, with regard to keeping documents, records and reports, do the following:

1 - Keep a copy of all hazardous waste movement forms carried out by the generator for a period of five years.

2 - Keep a copy of all results of tests or analyses of hazardous waste and all reports, correspondence and documents relating thereto, for a period of five years.

3 - Submit a periodic report, in accordance with the form adopted at the Ministry of Environment, every three months to the Ministry of Environment showing therein the types and quantities of hazardous waste that have been transported outside the real property or properties where it was generated, the date of transport, the name of the transporter, and the facility for the storage and/or recovery and/or treatment and/or final disposal thereof, provided that the reports include all completed hazardous waste movement forms, and keep copies of these reports for a period of five years from the date of their submission.

The procedures, rules and content of the periodic reports required to be submitted by the generator of hazardous waste, as well as the time limits for reviewing the reports by the Ministry of Environment and expressing an opinion thereon, shall be determined by decisions and circulars issued by the Minister of Environment.
No natural or legal person, public or private, may transport hazardous waste without obtaining the environmental licence in accordance with the form set out in Annex VI of this Decree.

The environmental licence shall be granted to the transporter of hazardous waste for a renewable period of two years pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Environment.

In the event that any modification occurs to the transport operations such that the conditions on the basis of which the licence was granted have changed, the holder of the environmental licence must notify the Ministry of Environment of the modifications within a time limit of one month from their occurrence, on the basis of which an inspection shall be conducted by the Ministry, which is required to notify the transporter in writing within a time limit of one month of the results of this inspection and of the effect of these modifications on the validity of the environmental licence.

The holder of the environmental licence or his legal representative shall submit to the Ministry of Environment an application for the renewal of the licence three months prior to the date of expiry of its validity.

A technical report showing the following shall be attached to the renewal application:

A copy of the environmental licence that is the subject of the renewal

All the points set out in Article (19) of this Decree

The modifications that have occurred/or will occur to the transport activity

A summary of all periodic reports on the various transport works carried out by him during the period of the environmental licence that is the subject of the renewal

Copies of the completed forms relating to the movement of hazardous waste that took place during the period of the environmental licence that is the subject of the renewal

A copy of the insurance policy valid throughout the entire period of the environmental licence

The requested licence shall not be renewed unless the transporter is in compliance with the provisions of Article (22) below of this Decree.

The holder of the environmental permit or his legal representative shall submit to the Ministry of Environment an application for the renewal of the permit three months prior to the date of its expiry.

The following shall be attached to the renewal application:

- The written approval of the Ministry of Environment of an "environmental audit" report (in accordance with the provisions of Decree No. 8471 dated 4/7/2012)

- A copy of the environmental permit subject to renewal

- Information and documents showing any modifications that have occurred or will occur in the operation of the facility

A copy of an insurance policy valid throughout the entire period of the environmental permit

The requested permit shall not be renewed unless the storage facility is in compliance with the provisions of Article (29) of this Decree.

The procedures, rules, forms and particulars for submitting applications to obtain an environmental licence for a hazardous waste transporter, as well as renewal applications, instructions for filling them out, keeping registers specific to the applications, and the time limits for completing the administrative transactions shall be determined by decisions and circulars issued by the Minister of Environment.

The Ministry of Environment reserves the right to audit the proper compliance of the hazardous waste transporter with the conditions of the environmental permit granted thereto. Where it is established that the hazardous waste transporter has violated the conditions of the environmental permit and the conditions mentioned in Article (22) of this Decree, the measures mentioned in Part Six of Law No. 444/2002 shall be taken against him.
No natural or legal person, whether public or private, may store hazardous waste without obtaining the environmental permit in accordance with the form set out in Annex VII of this Decree.

Hazardous waste storage facilities must submit an application to obtain an environmental permit for a hazardous waste storage facility in accordance with the form approved at the Ministry of Environment.

The following shall be attached to the application:

*The written approval of the Ministry of Environment of the "Environmental Impact Assessment", "Initial Environmental Examination" or "Environmental Audit" report (pursuant to the provisions of Decree No. 8633 dated 7/8/2012 and Decree No. 8471 dated 4/7/2012).

*A copy of an insurance policy valid throughout the entire period of the environmental permit

The Ministry of Environment shall inspect the storage facility to verify that the site is suitable and that the technical conditions are suitable for this operation in accordance with the content of the approved "Environmental Impact Assessment", "Initial Environmental Examination" or "Environmental Audit" report.

Subject to the legal and regulatory provisions relating to industrial establishments and dangerous, unhealthy and inconvenient establishments (classified establishments), the environmental permit for a hazardous waste storage facility shall be granted for a period of five years, renewable by a decision of the Minister of Environment.

Where the facility wishes to modify the design of the storage facility such that the operating conditions of the facility, on the basis of which the environmental permit was granted, are altered, the holder of this permit shall notify the Ministry of Environment of the modifications prior to carrying them out, so that in light thereof an inspection may be conducted by the Ministry, which must notify the owner of the facility in writing either of approval, or of the requirement to modify the permit, or of its revocation.

The Ministry of Environment reserves the right to audit the proper compliance of the hazardous waste storage facility with the conditions of the environmental licence granted thereto. Should it become apparent that the facility has violated the conditions of the environmental licence and the conditions mentioned in Article (29) of this Decree, the measures mentioned in Part Six of Law No. 444/2002 shall be taken against it.

No natural or legal person, whether public or private, may establish and operate a facility for the recovery and/or treatment and/or final disposal of hazardous waste without obtaining the environmental licence in accordance with the form set out in Annex Seven of this Decree.

Facilities for the recovery and/or treatment and/or final disposal of hazardous waste must submit an application to obtain an environmental licence for a facility for the recovery and/or treatment and/or final disposal of hazardous waste according to the form approved by the Ministry of Environment.

The following shall be attached to the application:

The written approval of the Ministry of Environment on the "Environmental Impact Assessment" report (pursuant to the provisions of Decree No. 8633 dated 7/8/2012).

A copy of an insurance policy valid throughout the entire period of the environmental licence

The Ministry of Environment shall inspect the recovery and/or treatment and/or final disposal facilities to verify that the site is suitable and that the technical conditions are suitable for this operation in accordance with the content of the approved Environmental Impact Assessment report.

Subject to the legal and regulatory provisions relating to industrial establishments and classified establishments, the environmental licence shall be granted to the facility for a period of five years renewable by a decision issued by the Minister of Environment.

Should the facility wish to make any modification to the design of the facility for the recovery and/or treatment and/or final disposal of hazardous waste such that the operating conditions of the facility on the basis of which the licence was granted are altered, the holder of the environmental licence must inform the Ministry of Environment of the modifications prior to their occurrence, on the basis of which an inspection shall be conducted by the Ministry, which shall notify the owner of the facility in writing either of its approval, or of the obligation to amend the licence, or of its revocation.

The procedures, rules, forms, and particulars for submitting applications to obtain an environmental permit, as well as renewal applications, instructions for completing them, the keeping of registers relating to applications, and the time limits for completing administrative transactions shall be determined by decisions and circulars issued by the Minister of Environment.

The holder of the environmental licence or his legal representative shall submit to the Ministry of Environment an application for the renewal of the licence three months prior to the date of its expiry.

The following shall be attached to the renewal application:

- The written approval of the Ministry of Environment on an "environmental audit" report (pursuant to the provisions of Decree No. 8471 dated 4/7/2012)

- A copy of the environmental licence subject to renewal

- Information and documents showing any modifications that have occurred or will occur in the operation of the facility

A copy of an insurance policy valid throughout the entire period of the environmental licence

The requested licence shall not be renewed unless the hazardous waste recovery and/or treatment and/or final disposal facility is in compliance with the provisions of Article (36) below of this Decree.

The procedures, rules, forms and particulars for submitting applications for obtaining an environmental licence, as well as renewal applications, instructions for filling them out, keeping registers specific to the applications, and the time limits for completing administrative transactions shall be determined by decisions and circulars issued by the Minister of Environment.

The Ministry of Environment reserves the right to audit the proper compliance of a hazardous waste recovery and/or treatment and/or final disposal facility with the conditions of the environmental licence granted to it. Where it is established that the facility has violated the conditions of the environmental licence and the conditions mentioned in Article (36) of this Decree, the measures mentioned in Title Six of Law No. 444/2002 shall be taken against it.

None of the following environmental licences may be assigned to third parties:

An environmental licence as a hazardous waste carrier.

An environmental licence for a hazardous waste storage facility.

An environmental licence for a hazardous waste recovery and/or treatment and/or final disposal facility.

Holders of the environmental licences referred to in Article (39) above must:

Submit a financial guarantee in favour of the Ministry of Environment, to be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Environment according to its type, form and value.

If the holder of the environmental licence does not carry out the obligations, conditions and works incumbent upon him during or upon the expiry of his environmental licence, the Ministry of Environment shall carry them out at his expense, out of the principal of the value of the guarantee that is the subject of this Article.

The provisions of Law No. 64 dated 12/8/1988 (Preservation of the Environment against Pollution from Harmful Waste and Hazardous Materials), Law No. 444 dated 29/7/2002 (Environmental Protection Law), Law No. 80 dated 10/10/2018 (Integrated Solid Waste Management) and the Penal Code shall apply to anyone who violates this Decree.
All texts contrary to the provisions of this Decree or inconsistent with its content are repealed.
This Decree shall be published in the Official Gazette and shall enter into force from the date of its publication.

The text of Article (61) of Legislative Decree No. 112/1959 (Civil Servants Regulations) shall be repealed and replaced with the following text:

1 - A civil servant whose attributed acts are found to constitute an offence punishable under the Criminal Code and other laws in force shall be referred before the criminal judiciary.

2 - If the offence arises out of the function, the civil servant may not be prosecuted criminally except upon the approval of the administration to which he belongs.

A public action shall not be initiated by way of a personal complaint.

3 - The Public Prosecution shall submit to the competent authority defined by law a request seeking its approval to prosecute the civil servant, accompanied by the file. The competent authority defined by law shall decide on the request, by a reasoned decision, within a period of fifteen working days following the receipt of the request by the administration, and the expiry of this period without a decision thereon shall be deemed an implicit approval thereof.

The decision of the competent authority granting permission to prosecute shall not be subject to any avenue of appeal.

4 - If the competent authority defined by law refuses the request of the Public Prosecution to grant permission to prosecute, the Public Prosecution may, within a period of fifteen days from being notified of the refusal decision, refer the matter to the Public Prosecutor before the Court of Cassation, who shall decide thereon, by a reasoned decision notified to the concerned parties, within a similar period, and the expiry of this period without deciding on the approval shall be deemed an implicit approval of the prosecution.

5 - The President and the two members of each of the Board of the Civil Service Council, the Central Inspection, and the Higher Disciplinary Board shall remain subject to the special legal provisions applicable to them.

6 - The public action is independent of the disciplinary action, and the institution of a public action shall not preclude the institution of a disciplinary action, proceeding therewith, and ruling thereon.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

- The Law returned to the Chamber of Deputies pursuant to Decree No. 5272 dated 25 July 2019 relating to Combating Corruption in the Public Sector and Establishing the National Anti-Corruption Commission, as amended by the Joint Parliamentary Committees and the Chamber of Deputies, has been promulgated.

- This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Definitions:

For the application of the provisions of this Law, the following definitions and terms shall be adopted:

A - Corruption: The abuse of authority, office or work connected with public funds for the purpose of achieving illicit gains or benefits for oneself or for others, whether directly or indirectly.

Offences against the public administration provided for in Chapter One of Title Three of Book Two of the Penal Code, with the exception of Subdivision Four thereof, illicit enrichment, and acts of corruption set forth in international conventions and treaties to which Lebanon has acceded and will accede and which are concerned with combating corruption, shall be considered acts of corruption.

B - Disclosure: Any letter or document, regardless of its description or title recorded in its body by the whistleblower, such as a disclosure, report, complaint or letter, any of which contains information relating to corruption.

C - The Commission: The National Anti-Corruption Commission.
Every offence provided for in Lebanese laws that relates to an act of corruption according to the definition of Article One of this Law shall be considered an offence of corruption.

A - The following acts shall also be considered corruption offences:

1- Obtaining concessions, poorly executing them, or procuring licences from a public law entity for the purpose of bringing private benefit, if any of these occurs in violation of the law.

2- Using public funds, and the means of the State and other public law entities, in violation of the law for the purpose of bringing a private benefit.

3- The purchase or sale by any person of movable or immovable property if it occurs on the basis of information not available to the public and prior to the purchase or sale that its value will rise or fall due to laws or regulations under issuance or projects planned to be undertaken, which this person obtained by virtue of his office, authority, kinship, partnership, work, or service, and which led to a realised gain.

B - It shall not be required that the private benefit resulting from the corruption offences specified in paragraphs: 1, 2, and 3 of Clause (A) of this Article occur directly or immediately; rather, it may arise from benefiting from projects intended to be executed even if they are not executed.

C - Anyone who commits any of the acts provided for in this Article shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to three years and by a fine ranging between twice and three times the value of the expected or realised material benefit.

Offences of corruption shall be subject to the following special procedures:

a - Notwithstanding any other legal provision, inquiries, investigations and criminal prosecutions in offences of corruption may be conducted without the need to obtain any of the prior authorisations or permissions provided for by law whenever such prosecution takes place at the request of the National Anti-Corruption Commission.

b - Criminal prosecution shall not preclude disciplinary prosecution.

c - Criminal prosecution in offences of corruption shall not lapse in the event of resignation, dismissal from service, referral to retirement, termination of service, placement at disposal or similar functional statuses, or the expiry of the term of holding public service.

d - Obligations of a financial nature may be adjudged against anyone to whom funds have devolved by inheritance, bequest or gift, within the limits of such funds.

e - Obligations of a financial nature may be adjudged against particular successors other than those enumerated in Paragraph (d) of this Article, if it is established that they knew or ought to have known that the funds that devolved to them were derived from acts of corruption.

f - Obligations of a financial nature may be adjudged against directors, chairpersons and members of the board of directors, partners and members of a legal person, to whom funds derived from corruption have devolved, directly or indirectly, after the dissolution of the legal person, if it is established that they had knowledge or ought to have known that the funds that devolved to them were derived from acts of corruption.

Establishment of the Commission:

a - An independent administrative commission called the "National Anti-Corruption Commission" shall be established; it shall enjoy legal personality and financial and administrative independence, and shall be referred to in this Law as the "Commission".

b - The members of the Commission, its employees and all other persons working for it shall perform their duties in complete independence from any other authority within the framework of the provisions of this Law.

Composition of the Commission:

a - The Commission shall be composed of six members, including the President and the Vice-President, who shall be appointed by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers for a non-renewable term of six years.

b - The members shall be selected from among persons of high moral character known for their integrity, and possessing academic competence and experience, on the basis of a documented curriculum vitae, provided that the candidate meets the conditions required for the appointment of First Category civil servants and meets the following additional conditions:

1 - The candidate's age at the time of appointment shall not be less than forty years and shall not exceed seventy-four years.

2 - He shall not, at the time of appointment and during the preceding five years, hold or have held any political or partisan office, and shall not currently or during the said period be a member of any association that engages in political activity or a member of a political party.

3 - He shall not be in any of the cases of incompatibility provided for in Article 7 below or be a candidate therefor.

c - The Commission shall be composed as follows:

1- Two retired judges holding honorary status, elected in accordance with the rules governing the election of members of the Supreme Judicial Council, provided that the electoral college shall consist of all tenured judges of the judicial, administrative, and financial courts, and provided that the convocation and supervision of the elections shall be carried out by the judge highest in grade among the President of the Supreme Judicial Council, the President of the State Council, and the President of the Court of Accounts.

The Minister of Justice shall submit the names of the two elected judges to the Council of Ministers.

2- A lawyer or jurist from among four names, two of whom shall be nominated by the Council of the Beirut Bar Association and two by the Council of the Tripoli Bar Association.

3- An accounting expert, from among three names nominated by the Council of the Lebanese Association of Certified Public Accountants.

4- An expert in banking or economic matters, from among three names nominated by the Banking Control Commission.

5- An expert in public administration, public finance, or anti-corruption matters, from among three names nominated by the Minister of State for Administrative Reform.

d - The expert members provided for above shall be required to hold postgraduate degrees (Master's degree and above) in their field of specialisation in addition to experience of not less than ten years.

e - The bodies mentioned above shall make the nomination or hold the election for the first time within a period of three months from the date of publication of this Law in the Official Gazette.

This process must also take place on subsequent occasions at least two months prior to the expiry of the term of office of the members of the Commission.

f - The appointment process must be completed, for the first time, within a maximum period of one month following the three-month period provided for in this Article. This process must also take place on subsequent occasions at least one month prior to the expiry of the term of office of the members of the Commission.

g - The judge highest in grade at the time of retirement shall be the President of the Commission ex officio, and if the grades of the two elected judges are equal, the older judge shall be the President.

h - The members of the Commission shall execute the declarations provided for in the Illicit Enrichment Law within a period of two weeks from the date of taking the oath, and shall lift banking secrecy from their accounts and the accounts of their spouses and minor children, and the Commission shall publish these declarations immediately on the website of the Commission.

i - The members shall exercise their functions in their personal capacity and with complete independence and shall not be bound by instructions from any authority, including the body that nominated or elected them.

Vacancy:

A - The members of the Commission shall continue to exercise their functions despite the expiry of the term of office for any reason whatsoever until their replacements are appointed and take the legal oath.

B - If a position on the Commission becomes vacant by death, resignation, incapacity, or for any other reason at least six months prior to the expiry of its term of office, the Commission shall verify the occurrence of the vacancy and notify the Council of Ministers of the matter within one week to take note and take the necessary measures to select the replacement for the remaining period of the vacant term of office, provided that the selection takes place within 15 days from the date of taking note in accordance with the procedures provided for in Article 6 of this Law.

Immunity of the Members:

A - Except in the case of flagrant offences, no member of the Commission may be prosecuted by way of a criminal action, nor may any criminal measure be taken against them, nor may they be arrested or detained throughout the term of their mandate, except after obtaining permission from the Commission by a majority of at least two-thirds of the members entitled to vote, excluding the member concerned, who shall be heard and shall not participate in the voting session.

B - Except in the case of flagrant offences, none of the employees of the Commission or persons seconded by it may be prosecuted by way of a criminal action, nor may any criminal measure be taken or an arrest be made against them throughout the duration of their work at the Commission, for acts relating to such work, except after obtaining permission from the Commission by a majority of at least two-thirds of the members entitled to vote. The competence of the Commission in this case shall be limited to determining whether the act in respect of which prosecution is sought relates to work at the Commission, and it may not refuse to grant permission except where it finds that the act is connected to work at the Commission and that the prosecution in respect thereof is malicious and not founded on any serious ground.

C - The offices of the Commission may not be searched, nor may any judicial or administrative measure be taken in respect thereof, except after the approval of its President. For this purpose, the judicial authority concerned shall address a confidential letter to the President of the Commission for the purpose of granting permission. The President shall decide on the request within five days from the date of its receipt. In the event that the time limit expires without an express decision on the request, he shall be deemed to have granted permission.

In the case of flagrant offences, the offices of the Commission shall be searched by order of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation or by decision of the First Investigating Judge, provided that this takes place in the presence of the President of the Commission or whomever he delegates for this purpose.

D - The decisions of the President of the Commission regarding the search of the offices or any other judicial measure shall be subject to appeal before the Plenary Assembly of the Court of Cassation within a time limit of 15 days from the date of their notification to the authority that requested the prosecution.

Cases of Incompatibility and Full-Time Dedication:

A - Members of the Commission shall be prohibited from practising any other public or private work, whether remunerated or unremunerated, during the performance of their duties, including, by way of example, the presidency or membership of the Council of Ministers or the Chamber of Deputies, the chairmanship or membership of the board of directors of a public institution, a private company or a bank, the presidency or membership of a public body, the presidency or membership of a municipal council or a private company managing a public utility, and the presidency or membership of the councils of syndicates or the bodies nominating the members.

B - No member of the Commission may have any direct or indirect interest in any institution subject to the oversight of the Commission.

C - No member of the Commission may, prior to the lapse of six full years from the end of his membership, run for parliamentary, municipal or mukhtar elections, or assume any political, administrative, security or syndicate public office.

D - Tenured higher education professors and public servants shall be deemed to have resigned by operation of law upon their acceptance of appointment to the Commission.

Taking the Oath:

The members of the Commission shall take the following oath before the President of the Republic:

"I swear by Almighty God to perform my duties in the National Anti-Corruption Commission with honesty, loyalty and independence, and to act in all that I do with integrity in a manner that enhances confidence in the Commission and consolidates the rule of law."

Internal Regulations:

A - The Commission shall establish internal regulations comprising the detailed rules and procedures governing its organisation, the conduct of its work and its financial management, including the powers of each of the President, the Vice-President and other positions, within a period of three months from the date of issuance of the decree appointing the members of the Commission, pursuant to a regulatory decision issued by the Commission by a majority of two-thirds of the members entitled to vote and after the approval of the State Council.

B - The Commission may amend the internal regulations in accordance with the same procedures.

C - The Commission shall establish, in accordance with the procedures specified above, a mandatory code of conduct applicable to its work.

D - The Commission may establish committees to perform permanent or temporary tasks in accordance with what is specified by the internal regulations.

Financing:

A - The Commission shall have a special annual budget entered under a special title within the general budget, which shall be sufficient to cover the expenses and activities of the Commission. The Commission shall prepare the draft budget and its President shall submit it to the Minister of Finance, who shall incorporate it into the draft general budget submitted to the Council of Ministers, which shall undertake to refer it to the competent authorities in accordance with the rules.

B - A special account shall be opened for the Commission at the Bank of Lebanon, and the President of the Commission shall undertake the commitment of its expenditures and the oversight of their commitment in accordance with the rules stipulated in the Public Accounting Law. At the end of the financial year, the President of the Commission shall send schedules of the expended appropriations to the Ministry of Finance certified by him, and the provisions of the special financial regulations of the Commission shall apply in respect of these schedules.

C - The accounts of the Commission shall be subject to the internal audit system and to independent auditing by auditing and accounting firms in accordance with the provisions of Article 73 of Law No. 326 dated 28/6/2001 (the 2001 Budget Law), and the accounts and the audit reports pertaining thereto shall be published in the Official Gazette and on the official electronic website of the Commission.

D - An additional appropriation shall be opened in the general budget for the Commission for the first operational year following the entry into force of this Law, in the amount of ten billion Lebanese pounds.

Allowances of the Members:

The President and members of the Commission shall receive a lump-sum monthly allowance equivalent to the salary of the President and members of the Constitutional Council.

Right to Receive Documents and Information:

The Commission may request from any Lebanese or foreign entity to provide it with the documents or information that it deems useful for the proper exercise of its functions. The concerned Lebanese entities shall respond to the request without delay within the legal rules.

The request may be addressed directly to the competent employee provided that his superiors are informed thereof.

In the event of non-response by the concerned administration, the Commission may have recourse to the competent judiciary in this regard.

Inadmissibility of Dismissal of Members:

A - One or more members of the Commission may not be dismissed except by a decision of the Council of Ministers following the approval of two-thirds of the members of the Commission who are entitled to vote, excluding the person concerned, either at the request of the Council of Ministers or at the request of half of the members of the Commission and after the Commission has heard the member complained against, and solely in the following cases:

1- If he loses legal capacity, or any of the conditions of appointment, incompatibility, or full-time dedication.

2- If his health or mental condition prevents him from performing his duties.

3- If he commits a grave fault in the performance of his duties.

B - Dismissal shall take place ipso jure upon the issuance of a final judgment against the member for a felony or an infamous misdemeanour. It also pertains to the Commission to decide, by a majority of two-thirds of its members who are entitled to vote, excluding the person concerned, to suspend his membership immediately upon the issuance of an indictment decision or any judgment against him for the aforementioned offences.

C - The Council of Ministers shall be notified of the decision in order to appoint a replacement member for the dismissed or resigning member in accordance with the established procedures and within the time limits specified in this Law.

D - The Council of Ministers may not take a decision to suspend the work of the Commission, to halt it, or to dissolve it under any circumstances whatsoever, including states of emergency and wars.

Meetings of the Commission:

A - The Commission shall meet at least once every week and whenever the need arises upon a convocation by its President or one-third of its members.

B - A meeting shall be legally valid in the presence of the absolute majority of the members who are entitled to vote.

C - Decisions of the Commission shall be taken by the absolute majority of the members who are entitled to vote.

D - No member is entitled to be absent from any of the meetings of the Commission except with a legitimate excuse and for compelling reasons, and a member who is absent from three unjustified meetings within three months shall be deemed to have resigned ipso jure, and a replacement for him shall be appointed in accordance with the established procedures.

E - The Commission shall be deemed to have resigned ipso jure when it refrains from holding its weekly meetings three consecutive times, except for compelling reasons.

The Administrative Body:

A - The Commission shall be assisted by a full-time administrative body headed by a Secretary-General, who shall be appointed by the Commission following a competitive examination conducted by the Civil Service Board.

B - The procedures for appointing the Secretary-General and his duties, and the procedures for organising and appointing the administrative body and its duties, shall be determined in the internal regulations.

C - The Commission may seek the assistance of whomever it wishes among experts from outside the Commission and its employees.

D - The Secretary-General and the members of the administrative body shall be subject to the Personnel Regulations.

Investigative powers of the Commission:

a - The Commission shall enjoy the following powers:

Investigating crimes of corruption, ex officio or on the basis of disclosures it receives, and it may, notwithstanding any other text, request the assistance of the judicial police and its auxiliaries with respect to obtaining the information available to them while maintaining its confidentiality.

If the Commission deems during the investigations it conducts that it is necessary to investigate specific bank accounts, it may address a reasoned request to the "Special Investigation Commission" provided for in Urgent Law No. 44/2015 relating to Fighting Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing so that the latter exercises its powers provided for in the aforementioned Law. In the event that the Special Investigation Commission decides to lift banking secrecy from the accounts concerned, this shall also take place in favour of the Commission. The "Special Investigation Commission" shall notify the National Anti-Corruption Commission as soon as possible.

b - The Commission may delegate some of its powers in each case separately, to one of its members or one of its competent staff members.

c - Subject to the provisions of the Banking Secrecy Law and notwithstanding the provisions of Article 25 of the Tax Procedures Law, obtaining information or documents requested by the Commission in the course of its investigative work or addressed by it to non-judicial bodies shall be enforceable, under penalty of a fine ranging between ten times and twenty times the official minimum wage imposed on the concerned person who abstains from executing the decision or on whoever obstructs such execution, after serving him with a written warning by the Commission of the necessity to execute within a period of five days.

d - Fining the concerned person shall not preclude prosecuting him criminally or disciplinarily in the event that the conditions for such prosecution are met, particularly in accordance with the provisions of Article 371 of the Penal Code.

Definition of the Functions of the Commission:

A - The Commission shall work to combat, prevent and uncover corruption, to apply the relevant international conventions and treaties to which Lebanon is a party, and to perform the special functions entrusted to it as defined in this Law and other laws.

B - In particular, the Commission shall be entrusted with the following functions in accordance with the provisions of this Law:

1- Receiving the disclosures submitted to it relating to corruption, investigating offences of corruption, examining them and referring them, where necessary, to the other competent supervisory, disciplinary and judicial bodies.

2- Monitoring the state of corruption, its cost, its causes and the efforts to combat and prevent it in the light of the laws in force, the adopted policies and the binding bilateral and multilateral agreements, and preparing special or periodic reports on these matters and publishing them in the Official Gazette and on its website.

3- Expressing an opinion, of its own motion or at the request of the competent authorities, on legislation, decrees, decisions and drafts thereof, and on policies and strategies relating to combating and preventing corruption.

4- Contributing to disseminating a culture of integrity in public administrations and institutions and in society, as well as the knowledge necessary to combat and prevent corruption.

C - The Commission shall also undertake the functions entrusted to it by all laws, in addition to the following functions:

1- Receiving declarations of financial assets and liabilities, keeping, managing and auditing them in accordance with the provisions of the Illicit Enrichment Law.

2- Protecting and incentivising corruption whistleblowers in accordance with the provisions of the Law on the Protection of Corruption Whistleblowers.

3- Receiving complaints relating to the non-application of the Right of Access to Information Law, investigating them and issuing decisions thereon, providing advice to the competent authorities on the implementation of the Law, preparing and publishing an annual report thereon, and participating in educating society to consolidate this right.

D - The Commission shall exercise its functions within the framework of the principles of good governance and shall cooperate with public administrations and institutions, civil society organisations, the private sector and the media, as well as with regional and international organisations and its counterparts in other States.

Precautionary Measures:

The Commission shall have the standing and authority to request the competent authorities to take all available precautionary measures, including:

1- Requesting the Judge of Urgent Matters to issue a reasoned ex parte decision prohibiting the respondent from travel for a period not exceeding three months, which may be renewed upon the request of the Commission once where serious grounds justifying the same exist. The Commission shall be notified of the decisions issued in this regard.

2- Requesting the Judge of Urgent Matters to seize the assets of the suspected persons, prohibit the disposal thereof, and place a restraint against disposal on immovable or movable assets subject to registration by a reasoned decision and for a period of three months, which may be renewed upon the request of the Commission once where serious grounds justifying the same exist. The Commission shall be notified of the decisions issued in this regard.

3- Requesting the "Special Investigation Commission" provided for in Law No. 44/2015 dated 24/11/2015 (Fighting Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing) to take the available precautionary measures, including freezing the bank account or accounts belonging to the respondent and to all other suspected persons in accordance with the legal procedures in force in this respect.

Powers of referral:

A - As a result of the inquiry proceedings, the Commission shall take any of the following decisions:

1- To close the file if it appears that it does not warrant judicial or disciplinary prosecution or any other measure.

2- To refer the matter to the competent Public Prosecution, which must inform the Commission of the progress and outcome of the inquiry and investigation it conducts, and if the Public Prosecution decides to close the file, the Commission may request it to expand the investigation.

3- To bring an action directly before the competent judiciary to demand the punishment of the perpetrators and the award of civil obligations in favour of the State. The Commission may duly appeal the decisions issued in this regard within the time limits prescribed by law.

4- To file the necessary lawsuits and appeals before the competent judicial or administrative authorities, to demand the restoration of the status quo ante and the recovery of funds and compensation, as a result of acts of corruption proven by a final administrative or judicial decision.

B - In cases related to corruption, the Commission shall enjoy all the rights and powers granted to the State and to the civil party in the laws of civil, criminal and disciplinary procedure at all stages of the investigation and trial.

C - The Commission shall be exempted from all judicial and disciplinary fees, advances and guarantees.

Duty of confidentiality:

A - The inquiries conducted by the Commission, the information available to it regarding them, and the deliberations related thereto shall be deemed confidential, and any person who discloses any of them shall be punished by imprisonment for up to two years and by a fine ranging between twenty-five times the official minimum wage and seventy-five times thereof, or by either of these two penalties.

B - Any person who leaks information of which they became aware during their work at the Commission shall be punished by imprisonment for up to three years and by a fine ranging between forty times the official minimum wage and one hundred and ten times thereof, or by either of these two penalties.

C - These prosecutions shall not preclude the Commission from taking any disciplinary measures provided for in its internal regulations.

a - Expressing an opinion, proprio motu or upon request, on all legislation, decrees, decisions, and drafts thereof, and the policies followed regarding combating and preventing corruption.

b - Proposing the texts of codes of ethics and rules of conduct and probity required to be possessed by public servants, and following up on their adoption, proper implementation, and promotion.

c - The Commission shall mandatorily be consulted in setting the National Strategy for Combating and Preventing Corruption.

a - Preparing studies and research, issuing specialized reports, bulletins, and publications in the field of promoting integrity and combating and preventing corruption, and establishing a database.

b - Raising public awareness of the causes and consequences of corruption and the means of combating and preventing it by all available means, and establishing programmes for educating and promoting integrity, particularly through educational, university, and media institutions and civil and community society bodies.

c - Urging the Ministry of Education and Higher Education and all other official public and private educational bodies, and cooperating with them, to include in their educational programmes theoretical and practical subjects in the field of integrity and combating and preventing corruption, and to develop these subjects and the educational means related thereto.

d - Organizing conferences, seminars, and training courses for various official and private bodies on all subjects falling within its competence.

Details of application:

The details of application of this Law shall be determined, where necessary, by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice, proprio motu or at the request of the Commission.

Final provisions:

This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Monitoring and Evaluation:

a - Monitoring cases of corruption, documenting them, and following them up by all available means in order to put an end to impunity.

b - Evaluating all laws, decrees, administrative decisions, memoranda, and circulars in light of the standards of combating and preventing corruption.

c - Monitoring the progress achieved in the implementation of legislation, decrees, policies, and strategies related to combating and preventing corruption.

d - Evaluating the risks of corruption in the public sector in accordance with scientific methodologies and providing the necessary proposals and recommendations to combat and prevent corruption.

Reports:

a. The Commission shall issue annual reports relating to its activity that include at least information on the mechanism of its work, including the costs, objectives, rules, achievements, the difficulties that impeded the workflow of its work, and its audited accounts, as well as the adopted public policies, its projects that were executed and those that were not executed and the reasons therefor, and any proposals that contribute to developing its work. The Commission shall submit this report to the office of each of the Presidency of the Republic, the Presidency of the Chamber of Deputies, the Presidency of the Council of Ministers, the Deputies, and the Ministers, and shall publish a copy thereof in the Official Gazette and on its website.

b - The Commission shall issue special reports on the status of corruption in Lebanon, its cost, its causes, the progress achieved in combating and preventing it, and the recommendations capable of strengthening these efforts, provided that it issues the first comprehensive report in this regard at the end of the first year of its term of office, followed by periodic reports every six months. The Commission shall submit these reports to the office of each of the Presidency of the Republic, the Presidency of the Chamber of Deputies, the Presidency of the Council of Ministers, the Deputies, and the Ministers, and shall send a copy thereof to the President of the Supreme Judicial Council, the President of the State Council, and the President of the Court of Accounts. And it shall publish a copy thereof in the Official Gazette and on its website.

c - Providing advice in the course of preparing the reports incumbent upon the Lebanese State pursuant to international or regional conventions, proposing independent recommendations regarding them.

d - The Commission may urge the concerned administrations to submit the required reports within the times specified therefor and in accordance with the legal procedures.
