Notwithstanding any general or special text, this Law determines a permanent mechanism for appointment to positions that are vacant or that shall become vacant in the First Category in public administrations, until the issuance of new regulations for employees in the public sector, and to senior positions in public institutions, namely Chairmen of Boards of Directors, Directors-General, and Directors who undertake the management of the public institution.

Notwithstanding any other text, vacant positions in Grade One of the general administrative cadre shall be filled in accordance with the following mechanism:

A - At least two months before any Grade One post in the general administrative cadre becomes vacant, or when it becomes vacant for any unforeseen reason, the competent Minister shall immediately send a letter to that effect to the Civil Service Board and the Office of the Minister of State for Administrative Development Affairs.

B - The specifications and conditions of appointment for vacant posts in Grade One shall be determined by the Civil Service Board in coordination with the competent Minister and the Office of the Minister of State for Administrative Development Affairs.

C - The Civil Service Board shall draw up lists of Grade Two employees who are legally qualified for appointment to Grade One in accordance with its regulations, provided that the specifications and conditions of appointment referred to in the preceding paragraph are observed with respect to them. These lists shall be notified to the competent Minister within a period of two weeks from the date of receipt of the letter of vacancy in order to fix a date for conducting the oral interviews, provided that it rests with the Civil Service Board to notify the qualified employees of the date thereof.

D - The oral interviews shall be conducted at the fixed date at the Civil Service Board by the President of the Civil Service Board, the competent Minister, and the Minister of State for Administrative Development Affairs, or a representative of both of them from within the administration. Within a period of one week from the date of completion of the oral interviews conducted, the committee shall submit to the competent Minister a list of the names of the three candidates in accordance with the order of the marks they obtained. The Minister, in turn, shall submit this list to the Council of Ministers, which shall review it and select one name therefrom for appointment to the vacant post.

E - Priority in filling these posts shall be given from among Grade Two employees from within the general administrative cadre. However, in the event that none of the three qualified candidates from within the cadre is named in accordance with the mechanism set forth in Article One of this Law, the mechanism set forth below, which is in force with respect to appointment to senior positions in public institutions, shall be applied to the appointment to this post, within the limit of the one-third proportion provided for in paragraph 2 of Article 12 of the Personnel Regulations.

Notwithstanding any other text, senior positions in public institutions, including Chairmen of Boards of Directors, Directors General, and Directors who manage the public institution, shall be filled in accordance with the following mechanism:

A - In determining the appointment specifications specific to the vacant position:

- At least two months prior to the vacancy of any position in public institutions, or upon its vacancy for any emergent reason, the competent Minister (the Minister of Tutelage) shall immediately send a letter to that effect to the Civil Service Board and the Office of the Minister of State for Administrative Reform.

- The appointment specifications and conditions for vacant positions in public institutions shall be determined by both the Civil Service Board and the Office of the Minister of State for Administrative Reform in coordination with the competent Minister, provided that the general employment conditions and the special conditions stipulated in the regulations of the concerned public institution are observed, and they shall be communicated to the competent Minister for approval.

- The appointment specifications and conditions shall be published by the competent Minister in three local newspapers and on the website of the Office of the Minister of State for Administrative Reform and that of the concerned Ministry, and they shall also be announced by posting on the door of the competent Ministry, the Civil Service Board, and the Office of the Minister of State for Administrative Reform, in two consecutive stages, provided that the publication includes the time limit for submitting nomination applications.

B - In nomination applications and their screening:

- Nomination applications shall be submitted by those who meet the appointment specifications and conditions, whether from within the general administrative cadre or outside it, within the specified time limit, through a unified electronic form available on the website of the Office of the Minister of State for Administrative Reform, provided that nomination applications submitted by hand or otherwise, or to any other official body, shall not be accepted. A candidate is entitled to submit his nomination through the electronic form for more than one vacant position in public institutions.

- A preliminary screening process of the nomination applications shall be carried out automatically by the electronic program in order to identify the accepted applications in accordance with the specified appointment specifications and conditions. As a result thereof, illustrative tables of the accepted candidates' applications shall be issued without including the names of the accepted candidates and personal information. Provided that the Office of the Minister of State for Administrative Reform shall undertake to audit them manually.

- The Office of the Minister of State for Administrative Reform shall prepare a report on the preliminary screening process, including the numerical lists of accepted nomination applications, and nominal lists of unaccepted nomination applications with an indication of the reasons for their non-acceptance, and it shall be deposited with the Civil Service Board and the competent Minister or the Minister of Tutelage, as the case may be.

- A committee composed of a representative of the competent Minister, a representative of the President of the Civil Service Board, and a representative of the Minister of State for Administrative Reform shall carry out a second screening process of the accepted applications in accordance with the criteria of specialization, competence, qualifications, degrees, years and diversity of experience, foreign languages, and others... As a result thereof, it shall assign marks according to a general average agreed upon, on the basis of which a list of the names of candidates whose nomination applications are accepted shall be drawn up, with an indication of the reasons for the non-acceptance of the other applications, provided that the committee prepares a report on the results of its work, which it deposits with the competent Minister, the President of the Civil Service Board, and the Office of the Minister of State for Administrative Reform.

- The names of the accepted candidates shall remain unannounced until the oral interviews are conducted, provided that the names are only supplied to the Civil Service Board when setting the date of these interviews, which shall undertake to notify the accepted candidates of the date of the oral interviews.

C - In oral interviews:

- Oral interviews with candidates whose applications are accepted shall be conducted by the President of the Civil Service Board, the competent Minister, and the Minister of State for Administrative Reform, or a representative of each of the latter two from within the administration, in a meeting scheduled for this purpose, provided that the interviews take place at the Civil Service Board.

- The committee shall select three names of the accepted candidates, to be submitted according to the order of marks to the competent Minister (the Minister of Tutelage) within a time limit of one week from the date of completion of the conducted oral interviews, who in turn submits them with his proposal to the President of the Council of Ministers to be presented to the Council of Ministers, which must appoint one of them to the vacant position.

The Civil Service Board and the Office of the Minister of State for Administrative Reform shall determine the specifications for appointment to the vacant position and the conditions thereof, and publish them within a time limit of one month from the date of notification of the letter of the competent minister regarding the vacancy. Candidacy applications shall be submitted in due form within a time limit of two weeks from the date of publication of the first announcement in the local newspapers, provided that a list of the names of the candidates whose candidacy applications are accepted is drawn up, the screening processes and oral interviews are conducted, and the names of the three qualified candidates are submitted to the Council of Ministers within a maximum time limit of one month from the closing of candidacy.

Filling vacant Grade One posts in the Directorate General of the Presidency of the Council of Ministers and the heads of the oversight bodies shall be exempted from the application of the mechanism mentioned in this Law.

The Council of Ministers shall apply the mechanism provided for in Article Three of this Law to the appointment of Chairmen of Boards of Directors, Directors General, Directors, and those in leadership positions regardless of their designation, who assume the management of institutions that manage a public utility among persons of public law, and it may apply the same mechanism to the appointment of the same officials who manage a utility among persons of private law.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Determination of the budget figures:

The figures of the general budget and the annexed budgets for the financial year commencing on the first of January 2020 and ending on 31 December 2020 shall be determined in accordance with the provisions of the second and third articles of this Law.

Appropriations:

There shall be opened in the general budget and the annexed budgets the appropriations set forth as follows:

Revenues:

The revenues of the general budget and the annexed budgets shall be estimated as follows:

Authorisation of collection:

The collection of the various taxes, fees, proceeds and revenues set forth in Tables No. (5, 6, 7 and 8) annexed to this Law is authorised in accordance with the provisions of this Law and the provisions of the laws in force.

Authorisation to borrow:

1 - Within the framework of financing the maturities of the principal of debts, and within the limits of the estimated deficit in the execution of the budget and in the expenditure of appropriations carried forward to the year 2020 and supplementary appropriations, and in order to cover the Treasury advances granted to Electricité du Liban in accordance with what is stated in Article 13 of this Law, the Government is authorised to issue Treasury bonds in Lebanese currency for short, medium and long terms, by decisions issued by the Minister of Finance.

2 - The Government shall quarterly inform the Chamber of Deputies of:

- The deficit realised in the execution of the budget and the Treasury.

- The expenditure of carried-forward and supplementary appropriations.

- The instalments of internal and external debts that have been settled,

- The result of the issuance of Treasury bonds in Lebanese currency authorised to be issued pursuant to the first clause of this Article, as well as in foreign currencies authorised by special laws.

- Treasury advances.

Loan accounts:

1 - Special Treasury accounts shall be opened for loans pursuant to decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance and the competent Minister, to which the amounts received on account of these loans shall be credited and to which the amounts paid in settlement of due instalments and bonds shall be debited.

2 - Commitment and payment appropriations shall be opened in the general budget for loans contracted by the State, or contracted for its account.

Authorisation to transfer appropriations:

1 - Transfers within the reserve of the General Budget from one item to another within this reserve are authorised by a decision of the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance. This measure shall apply to the reserve of each annexed budget.

2 - The transfer of appropriations allocated for the salaries of surplus employees, contractors, wage-earners and collaborators in public administrations and public institutions, accompanied by the approval of the Civil Service Board, from the administration from which they are transferred to the administration to which they are transferred, is authorised.

The transfer shall take place by a decision of the Minister of Finance after the endorsement of the Central Controller of Expenditure Commitment.

3 - The transfer of appropriations provided for in the budget of the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities - Administrative Departments - allocated to the Traffic, Trucks and Vehicles Management Authority to the budget of the said Authority after the issuance of its own regulations, is authorised by a decision of the Minister of Finance, after the endorsement of the Central Controller of Expenditure Commitment.

4 - The transfer of appropriations provided for under the budget line "Liquid Fuels" in favour of the military bodies in the budget of the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities to the similar budget line in the other chapters is authorised by a decision of the Minister of Interior and Municipalities after the endorsement of the Central Controller of Expenditure Commitment.

Provision of appropriations to subsidise the interest on investment loans:

There shall be provided for in the General Budget (Ministry of Finance - Directorate General of Finance) the appropriations required to call (subsidise) the interest on investment loans (agricultural, industrial, tourist, and technological, informational and environmental) and the profit margins on these loans with respect to Islamic banks.

The procedures and conditions for benefiting from the subsidised interest, and the profit margins on these loans with respect to Islamic banks, shall be determined pursuant to special regulations issued by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance and after consulting the opinion of the Governor of the Bank of Lebanon, and expenditure shall be subject to the procedures provided for in the Public Accounting Law.

As for loans subsidised from the Bank of Lebanon's own funds or the reserve funds held by it, it shall pertain to the Council of Ministers to issue a decision on the sectoral priorities for benefiting from the subsidy and its conditions, upon the proposal of the Ministers of Finance and of Economy and Trade after consulting the opinion of the Governor of the Bank of Lebanon.

Determining the rules for the expenditure of grants and external loans:

1 - Grants and external loans provided to each of the public administrations, public institutions, and autonomous services of all kinds, and to councils, bodies, and funds regardless of their designations, and to municipalities, federations of municipalities, and all other institutions and bodies that manage public utilities, shall be accepted in accordance with the provisions of Article 52 of the Public Accounting Law and its amendments, or Article 52 of the Constitution, and expenditure from cash grants and from loans, whether from the local component or from the foreign component, shall be subject to the audit of the Court of Accounts in accordance with the applicable rules.

2 - The provisions of the second paragraph of Article 27 of the draft law put into effect pursuant to Decree No. 14969 issued on 30/12/1963 shall not apply to supplementary appropriations relating to cash grants, whereby such appropriations may be transferred from one item to another by a decision of the competent minister and the Minister of Finance after the endorsement of the Central Controller of the Commitment of Expenditures, and after the concerned administration establishes the desire of the donor party to effect such transfer.

3 - The provisions of Article 104 of the draft law put into effect pursuant to Decree No. 14969 dated 30/12/1963 and its amendments (the Public Accounting Law) shall apply to emergency financial advances granted for the payment of expenditures financed by cash grants, and appropriations reserved for emergency financial advances relating to grants provided during a given fiscal year to discharge obligations the execution of which extends beyond the year for the payment of expenditures financed by these grants may be carried over to the budgets of subsequent fiscal years until the completion of the execution of the works relating to the grant.

4 - All balances of uncommitted appropriations financed by cash grants and loans shall be carried over to the budgets of subsequent years.

Opening exceptional appropriations:

In implementation of the provisions of Article 85 of the Constitution, the President of the Republic may, if emergency circumstances call for urgent expenditures. issue a decree based on a decision issued by the Council of Ministers, opening exceptional or supplementary appropriations or transferring appropriations in the 2020 budget, provided that these appropriations do not exceed one hundred billion Lebanese pounds, and these measures must be submitted for the approval of the Chamber of Deputies at the first session in which it convenes thereafter.

Healthcare Treatment Appropriations:

The appropriations allocated as a lump sum across the various titles of the General Budget designated for treatment in private and public institutions and hospitals, and for contracts with physicians in the private sector, shall be distributed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the joint proposal of the competent Minister and the Minister of Finance.

Deduction of a Share of Revenues Collected for the Benefit of Municipalities for Villages Without Municipalities:

Prior to their distribution, the Ministry of Finance shall deduct from the revenues collected for the benefit of municipalities an amount of six billion pounds, which shall be allocated for lighting, public works, and sanitation in villages without municipalities (fees for energy, maintenance, equipment, and sanitation) through the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities. The revenues shall be distributed by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance and the Minister of Interior and Municipalities, provided that the decree covers all villages without municipalities.

Granting Electricité du Liban a Treasury Advance and Addressing the Issue of Accumulated Debts:

Electricité du Liban shall be granted a long-term treasury advance up to a maximum limit of 1500 billion pounds (one thousand five hundred billion Lebanese pounds), to settle the fuel purchase deficit and to pay the interest and instalments of loans for the benefit of Electricité du Liban, provided that the advance is disbursed by order of the Central Treasury Accountant following the approval of the Minister of Finance and is repaid in cash, and provided that the mere use of this advance by the borrowing entity shall be deemed an acknowledgment on its part of its ability to repay in accordance with the bases stipulated in this Article.

Electricité du Liban may not, under its own liability, use the advance or any part thereof for any purpose other than that for which it was granted.

The manner of repayment of this advance shall be determined in accordance with the provisions set forth in Article 13 of Law No. 79 dated 18/4/2018 (the General Budget and Annexed Budgets Law for the Year 2018).

Amendment of Article 59 of Law No. 379 dated 14/12/2001 (Value Added Tax and its amendments).

The text of Article 59 of Law No. 379 dated 14/12/2001 (Value Added Tax and its amendments) is amended to read as follows:

A refund may be claimed for the entirety of the tax incurred on fixed assets used to carry out the following operations exempt from tax in accordance with the provisions of Articles 16 and 17 of this Law:

- The manufacture of medicines.

- The manufacture of foodstuffs exempt from tax pursuant to the provisions of Paragraph (b) of Article 17 of this Law.

- Hospitalisation and medical laboratories.

- Education.

- The activities of bodies and associations enjoying public benefit status and those concerned with the care of persons with special needs, the elderly, orphans, children, and persons suffering from mental illnesses, cancer, and all other illnesses determined by a decision of the Council of Ministers.

- Collective passenger transport.

- The manufacture of books, newspapers, and magazines.

- The manufacture of pharmaceutical products, including items for hygienic and pharmaceutical use (such as contraceptives, male condoms, sanitary pads and protectors, baby diapers, and similar hygienic items).

- The manufacture of paper and cardboard of the types used for writing or printing, newsprint in rolls or sheets, and ink prepared for printing.

For the purposes of this Article, fixed assets mean machinery and equipment intended for permanent use in the enterprise.

A refund may also be claimed for 100% of the tax incurred on current expenses related to the operations referred to above.

The taxpayer may submit, at the end of any calendar year and within a period of 20 days, a refund application in respect of the operations exempt in accordance with the provisions of this Article, provided that the amount claimed for refund is not less than five million Lebanese pounds, and any amount less than five million pounds shall be carried forward to the following year; however, where the taxpayer is no longer classified in accordance with the provisions of this Article, he may submit the said refund application regardless of the value of the application.

The details of application of this Article shall be determined, where necessary, by a decree adopted upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

Imposition of a tax on banks, financial institutions, and financial brokerage institutions:

In addition to the tax on profits in accordance with the statutory rate, a lump-sum tax of 2% of the turnover of each of them during the year 2019 shall be imposed on banks, financial institutions, and financial brokerage institutions for the operations of the year 2020, to be paid in three equal instalments within the following time limits:

- Before 1/6/2020 with respect to the first instalment.

- Before 1/9/2020 with respect to the second instalment.

- Before 1/12/2020 with respect to the third instalment.

Anyone who delays in paying the tax within the time limits referred to above shall be liable to a fine of 2% for each month of delay, with a fraction of a month being considered a full month.

The elements that constitute the turnover and the form designated for payment shall be determined pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

Repeal of the text of Article Fifty-Six of Law 144 dated 31/7/2019 (The General Budget and Annexed Budgets for the Year 2019) and its replacement with another text:

The following Clause 12 is hereby added to the text of Article 16 of Law 379 dated 14/12/2001 and its amendments (Value Added Tax):

12- Activities carried out by nurseries licensed to operate in the field of child daycare on Lebanese territory.

Regularisation of the status of foreign workers in breach of the conditions of work and residency in Lebanon:

First: The status of foreign workers of various categories working on Lebanese territory pursuant to a work permit and a work residency permit, brought in to work by sponsors who are individuals, establishments, companies or others, and whose documents have expired and who have not renewed them prior to the date of entry into force of this Law, shall be regularised as follows:

- The sponsors of these workers shall be exempted from late fines of all kinds, deportation orders issued against some of them shall be cancelled, and they shall be liable for fees and taxes for the years of delay only, provided that applications for the regularisation of status are submitted to the Ministry of Labour and to the General Directorate of General Security to obtain the renewal of the permit and residency within a period of three months from the date of publication of this Law.

Second: With respect to foreign workers brought in by employment offices on the basis of fictitious sponsors, who obtained on that basis a lawful work permit and work residency permit, and whose documents have expired and who have not renewed them prior to the date of entry into force of this Law, their status shall be regularised in the following manner:

- All fees and fines incurred for the years of delay shall be collected from the employment offices that fraudulently brought them in, and those offices shall be struck off the list of those permitted to bring in foreign workers at the Ministry of Labour and the General Directorate of General Security.

The status of this category of workers shall be regularised by the submission of regularisation applications by a new sponsor to obtain the renewal of the permit and residency or to obtain a new permit and residency from the Ministry of Labour and the General Directorate of General Security, within a period of three months from the date of publication of this Law.

- In the event that they do not submit regularisation applications within that period, the appropriate deportation measures shall be taken against them.

- In the event that they fail to regularise their status and it is proven that they continue to work for a new employer, whether a person or a company, without legal papers, the employer shall be fined in accordance with the rules, including payment of the fees for the years of unlawful employment, and the worker shall be deported at the expense of the employer in accordance with the procedures of General Security.

Third: With respect to foreign workers who entered Lebanon unlawfully and who work without a work permit and work residency permit for a Lebanese employer, whether an individual, a company or an establishment, applications for the regularisation of their status shall be submitted by their employer in the manner and within the period specified above, and the fees for the years of employing the worker with him shall be collected from the employer while exempting him from all kinds of fines.

In the event that the employer refrains from regularising the status of his workers, he shall be liable for the full fees and late fines for the years of employing the offending worker with him, and measures to deport the worker shall be taken in accordance with the rules by the General Directorate of General Security and at the expense of the employer.

Fourth: With respect to foreign workers who entered Lebanon unlawfully and who work therein without a specific employer, they shall be given a period of three months to find a sponsor to regularise their status and employ them in accordance with the applicable rules.

In the event that the period expires without the submission of a regularisation application by a sponsor, the offending worker shall be deported in accordance with the rules adopted at the General Directorate of General Security, which shall collect the deportation fees and fines from the total of the employers for whom he worked during the years of the breach.

Fifth: The provisions of this Article shall not apply to workers whose status is governed by special legal texts or bilateral agreements, such that those texts and agreements shall be complied with in respect of them.

Sixth: The details of the implementation of this Article shall be determined, where necessary, by a joint decision of the Ministers of Labour and of the Interior and Municipalities.

Exceptional provisions relating to income tax on salaries and wages:

Notwithstanding any other, indemnities granted to employees and workers as compensation for their dismissal from service during the period extending from 1/7/2019 until the date of publication of this Law shall be exempted from the tax on salaries and wages, and shall also be considered as deductible charges from the revenues of employers assessed on the basis of actual profit, even if they exceed the limits stipulated in the laws in force in Lebanon, and the taxes paid on such indemnities shall be considered a right of the Treasury and may not be refunded.

Conducting a settlement on assessments relating to income tax and value added tax submitted before the Objections Committees as of 1/4/2019:

Notwithstanding any other provision, and exceptionally, assessments relating to income tax and value added tax objected to before the Objections Committees as of 1/4/2019 and which have not been adjudicated up to the date of publication of the Public Budget for the year 2020 shall be settled.

The value of the settlement shall be set at fifty percent (50%) of the value of the objected taxes only, excluding the assessment and collection fines that were due.

To benefit from this settlement, the taxpayer must submit a written request to the competent tax administration and pay the amount due from him as a result of the settlement in full within a maximum period ending on 31/3/2020.

The taxpayer may not choose to benefit from the settlement for a part of a single assessment issued by the tax administration, such that the settlement covers all objected points and periods within the single assessment.

The Objections Committees notified by the tax administration of the taxpayer's request to conduct the settlement shall cease adjudicating the objection.

Taxpayers who have paid the tax due from them in instalments prior to the entry into force of this Law and where not all instalments have been paid, and taxpayers who benefited from the provisions of Article 40 of Law No. 66 dated 3/11/2017 (the Public Budget and Annexed Budgets Law for the year 2017), or the provisions of Article 23 of Law No. 79 dated 18/4/2018 (the Public Budget and Annexed Budgets Law for the year 2018), or the provisions of Article 41 of Law No. 144 dated 31/7/2019 (the Public Budget and Annexed Budgets Law for the year 2019), may benefit from the provisions of this Article in accordance with the following:

"The value of the settlement shall be set at fifty percent of the value of the objected taxes after deducting the paid portion of the tax only".

Amendment of Article Twenty-Seven of Law No. 144 dated 31/07/2019 (General Budget and Annexed Budgets Law for the Year 2019):

Article Twenty-Seven of Law No. 144 dated 31/07/2019 (General Budget and Annexed Budgets Law for the Year 2019) shall be amended so as to read as follows:

There shall be added to Law No. 243 issued on 22/10/2012 (the New Traffic Law) Article 154-1, the text of which is as follows:

"Article 154-1:

Notwithstanding Paragraph 8 of Article 154 of this Law, distinctive passenger vehicle licence plate numbers shall be classified pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities, and all numbers falling outside this classification shall be deemed non-distinctive numbers, and the code MP shall be used instead of AP for Members of Parliament".

Fees shall be imposed on owners of vehicle licence plates bearing distinctive numbers of all codes except the codes AP,AG,R,J,D,C, in accordance with the following:

First: On the annual fee consideration for distinctive passenger licence plate numbers placed in circulation:

Lump-sum annual fees shall be imposed on distinctive licence plate numbers pertaining to vehicles in accordance with the classification set forth in the attached table.

These fees shall be paid annually as part of the traffic fees, in accordance with the laws and decisions in force and the mechanisms appertaining thereto.

Failure by the owner of the licence plate to pay this fee shall result in its accumulation to the following year, together with the accrual of fines calculated by the same mechanism applicable to annual traffic fees.

On a one-time basis, these fees shall be paid directly for the year 2019 independently of the traffic fees within a time limit not exceeding 30/06/2020.

Second: On the consideration for allocation of a distinctive licence plate number:

1- A one-time allocation consideration shall be paid by any person wishing to acquire ownership of a licence plate bearing a distinctive number, after the date of entry into force of this Law, in accordance with the following:

1.1 Categories: (5.1,6.1,7.1, 4.1, 3.1) set forth in the attached table:

The distinctive numbers within these categories shall be offered to the public at public auction, provided that they are put up at the reserve price specified in the same table for each category.

A special committee shall undertake the organisation of this auction; the members of this committee shall be appointed and the mechanism of its work shall be determined pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities.

1.2 Remaining categories:

The allocation consideration shall be paid in accordance with the amount specified in the attached table corresponding to each category.

Upon payment of this consideration, the licence plate number shall become his property, and he shall be given a deed of allocation by the Traffic, Trucks and Vehicles Management Authority in return therefor.

Third: On the sale of a licence plate bearing a distinctive number to a third party:

Owners of licence plates bearing distinctive numbers prior to the date of entry into force of this Law may obtain from the Traffic, Trucks and Vehicles Management Authority a deed of allocation for the number of each of them, in return for a fee equivalent to 5% of the allocation consideration pertaining to the category of the number in accordance with the attached table, after payment of the annual fees due from them.

Holders of deeds for distinctive numbers may sell their licence plates to third parties pursuant to a contract drawn up before a Notary Public; a transfer fee equivalent to 5% of the allocation consideration pertaining to the number shall be imposed on such sale, and the Authority shall as a result thereof issue a new deed in the name of the new owner.

A vehicle registered with a licence plate bearing a distinctive number may not be sold to a third party except after payment of the allocation fee and obtaining the deed of allocation. Cases of transfer of ownership between ascendants and descendants shall be exempted therefrom, and this fee shall not fall due upon the execution of a declaration of heirship.

Fourth: On the relinquishment of a licence plate bearing a distinctive number to the Administration:

The owner of a licence plate bearing distinctive numbers, including a licence plate placed in salvage, may relinquish their licence plates in favour of the Traffic, Trucks and Vehicles Management Authority, provided that his licence plate is replaced with a licence plate bearing a non-distinctive number without paying any fees, on a one-time basis only; this exemption shall cover more than one licence plate bearing a distinctive number owned by the same person.

The application for relinquishment shall be submitted to the Traffic, Vehicles and Trucks Management Authority, and this number shall be entered into the database of available distinctive numbers.

Fifth: On the consideration for allocation of a non-distinctive special number:

Any person wishing to register an available non-distinctive special number may register such number provided that he pays in return therefor, on a one-time basis, an allocation consideration equivalent to 400.000 Lebanese Pounds.

Sixth: Exemption from payment of the traffic fee, whatever the type of exemption, shall not cover payment of the annual fee for a distinctive number or the consideration for allocation of a distinctive number or the consideration for allocation of a non-distinctive special number, as provided for in this Article.

Seventh: By way of exception, the allocation considerations set forth in the attached table shall be reduced by 20% for transactions for the purchase of licence plates bearing distinctive numbers until 30/06/2020.

By way of exception, the deed of allocation fee shall be reduced to 3% of the allocation consideration as set forth in the attached table if the fee is paid within a time limit not exceeding 30/06/2020.

Eighth: Paragraph 4 of Article 154 of the New Traffic Law shall be amended so as to read as follows:

"4- The Latin letters Y-H-K-B-G-M-N-O-R-S-T-Z shall be used for private car licence plates pertaining to all citizens. The letter P shall also be used for public cars, the letter D for the diplomatic corps, and the letter C for the consular corps".

Ninth: The detailed rules for the implementation of this Article shall be determined pursuant to a joint decision issued by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities and the Minister of Finance.

Imposition of a flat fee on the sale of energy by owners of electric generators:

A flat fee shall be imposed on the owner of an electric generator who sells to the public, in the amount of 15,000 L.L. (fifteen thousand Lebanese pounds) annually on the capacity of this generator calculated on the basis of the KVA.

This fee shall not confer any rights upon the owner of the generator, and he shall be prohibited from adding its value to the persons who draw energy from him, and he shall be required to abide by the tariff set by the Ministry of Energy and Water, and this fee shall be considered among the charges deductible from the taxable revenues of a taxpayer subject to income tax on the basis of real profit.

This fee shall be declared and paid annually in advance in accordance with a form established by the Ministry of Finance during the month of January of each year. And during the month following the month in which the generator is put into use when the generator is used, and delay in declaration and payment shall be subject to the fines stipulated by the Tax Procedures Law in respect of the tax on profits.

Contrary to what is stated in the paragraph above, the declaration and payment of the fee for the year 2019 shall take place within a time limit not exceeding 31/03/2020.

All municipalities shall be required to conduct a comprehensive survey to enumerate all generators used in the field of selling energy within their municipal scope, and to communicate the results of this enumeration to the Ministry of Finance within a time limit not exceeding 31/03/2020, and they shall also be required to notify the Ministry of Finance of every electric generator that is used in the future on a periodic basis during the month following the end of each quarter, on the basis of a detailed statement determined by the Ministry of Finance.

Municipalities that own electric generators and sell energy to the public shall not be subject to this fee.

The details of application of this Article shall be determined, where necessary, pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

3- All the sectors referred to above are obliged to submit a copy of their annual budget to the Council of Ministers and the Ministry of Finance through the tutelage authority or Minister, or else through the Minister of Finance in the absence of a tutelage authority or Minister. It is for the Council of Ministers to designate the competent authority to audit those budgets, whether at the Ministry of Finance and the Court of Accounts or other financial auditing institutions possessing competence and standing.

Export support:

Duly licensed factories and industrial establishments shall be granted an amount of 5% (five per cent) of the value of their annual exports manufactured in Lebanon and holding a duly issued certificate of origin in Lebanon and which benefit from the provisions of this Law, namely:

3 - For their additional annual exports that exceed the value of manufactured goods exported in the previous year.

4 - For the value of manufactured goods that they export for the first time.

Suspension of legal proceedings relating to time limits arising from default in repaying called loans:

Obligating the companies operating the cellular sector to transfer revenues to the Treasury periodically:

Notwithstanding any other legal or contractual provision, and with the exception of salaries, the Administration of the Port of Beirut shall be obligated to transfer the collected revenues resulting from port services to the Treasury account at the Bank of Lebanon on Monday and Thursday of every week, provided that the mechanism for paying the amounts owed by the Treasury in favour of the Port Administration in respect of management fees, expenditures, charges, purchases, and otherwise, borne by this Administration in the course of its operations, shall be determined pursuant to a decision issued by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Finance and Public Works and Transport.

A - The following shall be collected in Lebanese pounds:

Amendment of the value of the guarantee of bank deposits covered by the guarantee of the National Institute for the Guarantee of Deposits and provided for in Article 14 of Law No. 28/67 dated 9/5/1967 and in Article 14 of Law No. 110 dated 7/11/1991:

First: Article 14 of Law No. 28/67 dated 9/5/1967 is amended to read as follows:

The purpose of the Institute is to guarantee, at banks operating in Lebanon, deposits in Lebanese currency and in foreign currencies, whatever the type or term of such deposits.

The guarantee covers, up to an amount of seventy-five million Lebanese pounds or its equivalent in foreign currencies, in principal and interest, the total deposit accounts belonging to a single depositor at any bank, and the head office of the bank and its branches shall be deemed a single institution.

These accounts shall not bear interest starting from the date the bank ceases payment.

Where one of the depositors at a bank that has ceased payment has debit accounts or other obligations towards the said bank, whether in Lebanese currency or in foreign currencies, a set-off shall be effected between the total of his credit accounts and the total of his debit accounts and his other obligations, and the guarantee shall cover only his credit balance at the bank up to an amount of seventy-five million Lebanese pounds.

Every joint account, regardless of the number of its holders, shall be deemed a single account.

Every estate account shall also be deemed a single account.

Accounts belonging to chairmen and members of the boards of directors of banks, managers, auditors, and the spouses, ascendants and descendants of the aforementioned persons at the bank to which they belong are excluded from the guarantee.

Second: The text of Article 1 of Law No. 110 dated 7/11/1991 relating to the reform of the banking situation is repealed.

Third: The text of Clauses (1), (2) and (3) of Article 14 of Law No. 110 dated 7/11/1991 is amended to read as follows:

1 - Deposits in Lebanese currency up to an amount of seventy-five million Lebanese pounds, as well as deposits in foreign currencies up to the equivalent of an amount of seventy-five million Lebanese pounds according to the exchange rate of the foreign currency on the date of the declaration of the bank's cessation of payment or the takeover decision, and whatever the total value of all deposits at the single bank may be.

The guarantee does not cover deposits in the bank's branches abroad, and the head office of the bank and all its branches in Lebanon shall be deemed a single institution with regard to the application of the provisions of this Article.

2 - Up to a rate of 30% of the principal of the guarantee mentioned in the preceding paragraph shall be paid immediately upon the issuance of the decision declaring the cessation of payment or the takeover decision, and the remaining balance shall be paid either in instalments or by way of treasury bonds within a period of one year in accordance with what the Central Council of the Bank of Lebanon decides.

3 - With regard to the guarantee only, and where one of the depositors at a bank that has ceased payment or has been subjected to takeover has debit accounts or other obligations towards the said bank, whether in Lebanese currency or in foreign currencies, a set-off shall be effected on the date of the declaration of the bank's cessation of payment or the decision of takeover thereof, between the total of his credit accounts and the total of his debit accounts and his other obligations, and the guarantee shall cover only his credit balance at the bank up to an amount of seventy-five million Lebanese pounds.

Amendment of Article 90 of the 2019 Budget Law:

A - A final paragraph is added to the text of the clause contained in Article "Ninety" of Law No. 144 dated 31/7/2019 (the General Budget and Annexed Budgets Law for the year 2019) under the heading "With respect to the Administrative Corps", providing as follows:

By way of exception, a civil servant whose actual service on the date of his mandatory referral to retirement has not reached the prescribed minimum for entitlement to a retirement pension shall be granted the right to choose between receiving a dismissal indemnity for his rendered service or requesting the substitution of the indemnity with a retirement pension within a period of one month from the date of termination of service, provided that his actual service on the date of entry into force of this Law would have entitled him to receive such pension had his service been terminated before 31/7/2019.

B - This text shall apply with effect from 31/7/2019.

Publication of the Law:

This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

- Definition of Terms:

For the application of the provisions of this Law, the following terms shall mean the following:

1 - Public Official: Any person who performs a public function or a public service, whether appointed or elected, permanent or temporary, paid or unpaid, in any public law or private law entity, at the central and decentralised levels, and in general any person who performs work in the interest of public property, a public facility, a public utility, a public institution, a public service, or public funds, whether owned, wholly or partially, by a public law entity, and whether assumed de jure or de facto, including any position of the constitutional authorities or any legislative, judicial, executive, administrative, military, financial, security, or advisory position.

2 - Public Official Subject to Declaration: Every public official, with the exception of the fourth category and below or its equivalent who are not assigned the duties of a higher category, and members of the teaching staff at the Lebanese University and public schools and institutes. Employees at the Ministry of Finance, employees of the Customs and the Real Estate Registries, and the president, members, employees, and staff of administrative committees and independent and regulatory authorities established by laws, of all ranks and categories, shall also be subject to the declaration of financial disclosure if their work entails financial consequences.

3 - The Commission: The National Anti-Corruption Commission that was established in its own special law.

Obligation to Submit the Declaration:

a - Every public official subject to declaration shall submit declarations signed by him, in which he sets out all the elements of financial disclosure and interests belonging to him, his spouse, and his minor children, whether male or female, in Lebanon and abroad, in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

b - Where both spouses are subject to the obligation of declaration, each of them must submit a separate declaration and indicate that in the declaration, provided that the guardian among them submits the declaration pertaining to his minor children.

Periodicity of declarations:

A - Declarations shall be submitted at the following times:

1. A first declaration within two months from the date of assuming the public office, and as one of the conditions for assuming such office. Any renewal or extension thereof for consecutive terms by election, delegation, or by any other manner provided for by law shall be considered an assumption of a public office.

2. An additional declaration every three years, from the date of submitting the previous declaration.

3. A final declaration within a period of two months from the date of the termination of his services for any reason whatsoever.

B - A public official subject to declaration shall submit a new first declaration of financial assets and liabilities pursuant to the provisions of this Law within a period of three months from the date of its entry into force, even if he had previously submitted the declaration provided for in Law No. 154/1999.

C - Where multiple offices covered by this Law are held by a single public official, one declaration shall suffice.

Lodging of declarations:

(a) The declarations provided for in this Law shall be lodged with the Commission against receipts, and shall be kept in physical and electronic registers.

As for the President and members of the Commission, they shall submit their declarations to the Presidency of the Council of Ministers, and they shall be published on the website of the Commission.

(b) Until the Commission is formed, declarations shall be lodged with the following authorities against receipts:

1 - The Presidency of the Constitutional Council: the President of the Republic, the Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies, the President of the Council of Ministers, the Deputy Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies, the Deputy President of the Council of Ministers, Ministers and Deputies, the President of the Economic and Social Council and its members.

2 - The Presidency of the Republic: employees of the Presidency of the Republic, the President of the Constitutional Council and its members.

3 - The Presidency of the Chamber of Deputies: employees of the Chamber of Deputies.

4 - The Presidency of the Council of Ministers: the Governor of the Bank of Lebanon, the President of the Court of Accounts, the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Accounts, judges of the Sharia and Confessional Courts, persons performing a public service and employees of public administrations and institutions, councils, bodies and funds attached to the Presidency of the Council of Ministers, and all presidents of independent bodies established by law, their members and their employees, and the Mediator of the Republic.

5 - The Ministry of Justice: the First President of the Court of Cassation, the President of the State Council, the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation, the Government Commissioner at the State Council, the President of the Judicial Inspection Board, the presidents of the Sharia and Confessional Courts, notaries public, the presidents of administrative bodies of a judicial character, their members and their employees, and court employees.

6 - The First President of the Court of Cassation: judicial judges.

7 - The President of the State Council: administrative judges.

8 - The President of the Court of Accounts: financial judges and employees of the Court.

9 - The President of the Sharia and Confessional Courts: judges and employees in these courts.

10- The Civil Service Board: public employees in the ministries and public administrations subject to the oversight of this Board.

11- The Registry of the Ministry to which they belong: all other civilian and military public employees in each ministry whose administrations are not subject to the oversight of the Civil Service Board.

12- The Registry of the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities: presidents of municipal councils and their members, federations of municipalities and their employees, mukhtars and members of ikhtiyariyah councils.

13 - The Registry of the Tutelage Ministry: presidents of the boards of directors of public institutions and autonomous agencies, their members and their employees, and the administrative committees attached to them.

14 - The Registry of the Competent Ministry: presidents of administrative bodies entrusted with managing public utilities other than public institutions and autonomous agencies, their members and their employees.

15 - The Governorship of the Bank of Lebanon: the Vice-Governors, the Chairman of the Banking Control Commission, its members and its employees, the Secretary-General of the Special Investigation Commission, its general members and its employees, and the employees of the Bank of Lebanon.

(c) The Commission or the competent authorities mentioned above shall keep the declarations with the Bank of Lebanon, and they shall be transferred to the Commission when the necessary means become available to it to keep them in a regular and secure manner.

Mechanism for submitting the declaration and its content:

A - The declaration shall be submitted in paper form inside a sealed and signed envelope or by any legally acceptable electronic means in a manner that preserves confidentiality, in accordance with the form attached to this Law. The Commission may, where necessary, amend the attached form, including the values requiring declaration.

B - The declaration must include an inventory of the entire financial estate and interests in Lebanon and abroad, and shall cover:

1. Any income from the sources provided by the public office.

2. Movable and immovable property in Lebanon and abroad, the manner of its acquisition (for example: purchase, inheritance, bequest, gift), and the revenues resulting therefrom; including immovable property devolved through irrevocable powers of attorney, fiduciary contracts or other similar legal mechanisms, as well as jewellery, precious stones and metals, and cash funds deposited in banks and/or financial institutions.

3. Liabilities and debts, specifying their value and terms (that is, the maturities and interest accruing thereon).

4. All interests resulting in any financial income from any source other than public office and movable and immovable property, and the value of such revenues, meaning by way of example and without limitation:

a - All activities and investments in any economic projects (for example: partnership, shares, stocks, bonds, and investment portfolios of all kinds, any certificates, instruments or bonds whose returns are linked to cash flows resulting from commercial papers, securities, stock dividends or bond interest); as well as all fiduciary interests.

b - Positions, roles, functions and memberships, whether by appointment or by election, in any person among:

* Persons of public law (for example: membership in boards of directors of public institutions, supervisory bodies, committees, and advisory functions in public administrations, including bodies regulated by laws, or municipalities or their federations, the office of mukhtar and mukhtar councils).

* And persons of private law (for example: membership in boards of directors, companies, associations, parties, clubs and professional syndicates, and any consortium of local and/or foreign companies that has won a concession or public-private partnership contract).

d - Any other interests that may fall within the scope of the declaration considering the declarant and those declared for as the holders of the direct right or the beneficial right.

e - All interests, as defined in paragraph three above, that do not result in any financial income;

C - In addition to the foregoing, the declarant must indicate in the additional and final declarations the differences and their causes between one declaration and another.

Administrative Circular on the Declaration:

The Commission and every entity temporarily concerned with receiving declarations shall issue a circular through the administration to which the public officials subject to declaration belong within a period of one month from the date of publication of this Law. It shall also issue, during the first month of each year, a circular for compliance with the content of the provisions of this Law, indicating therein the time limits to be complied with for submitting the various declarations and the legal consequences resulting from their violation.

Penalty for failure to submit the declaration:

A - The submission of the declarations provided for in this Law shall be deemed a condition for assuming public office, continuing therein, and becoming entitled to and receiving salaries, allowances and all other financial entitlements for all categories enumerated in the definition of the public official subject to declaration.

B - Anyone who fails to submit the first declaration on time and the subsequent required declarations on time without a legitimate excuse and continues in his failure for a period of three months, either from the date of being notified in person through administrative channels of a written notice requiring the submission of the declaration specified in paragraph (C) below, or from the date of suspension of the payment of his financial entitlements in accordance with paragraph (C) below, shall be deemed resigned by operation of law, and such suspension of payment shall be deemed a notification to the concerned public official.

C - The Commission or the concerned authorities temporarily entrusted with receiving the declarations must notify all public officials subject to declaration of the obligation to submit the declarations provided for in this Law if the legal time limits specified therefor have expired and such declarations have not been submitted. It must also simultaneously and immediately notify each of the administrations to which these public officials who failed to submit the declaration belong, and the Central Financial Accountant or whomever is delegated the tasks of disbursing the aforementioned expenditures, of the payment of their financial entitlements of all kinds, such as salaries, allowances, dismissal indemnity, end-of-service indemnity and all other allowances. Upon the occurrence of this notification, the payment of salaries and other financial dues shall be suspended immediately and shall remain so until the aforementioned concerned bodies are notified anew by the Commission or the concerned authorities of an authorization to resume payment after verifying the submission of the required declaration in accordance with the specified rules and conditions.

D - In all cases, financial entitlements of all kinds, such as salaries, allowances, dismissal indemnity and end-of-service indemnity, shall not be paid unless the persons required to declare submit, to the competent authority, the receipt proving that they have submitted the required declarations in accordance with the specified rules and conditions. However, in the event that any amount or allowance is received contrary to the mechanism specified under paragraph (C) above of this Article, such payments shall be deemed a debt owed by the beneficiary in favor of the Treasury, due for payment and bearing legal interest from the date of their receipt.

E - All acts resulting from the exercise of public office shall remain valid and standing notwithstanding any measure or penalty incurred by the public official as a result of his failure to submit the declaration.

F - In order to facilitate communication and carry out the notifications provided for in this Article and within the framework of the rules of digital government, the computers of the various concerned administrations shall be interconnected with an accompanying statistical database, and electronic interfaces allowing notification, suspension of payment and detection of gaps shall be created. Until that time, the Central Accountant, or whomever is delegated the tasks of disbursing the aforementioned expenditures, shall be deemed liable for any payment contrary to the mechanism specified under this Article, pursuant to the provisions of Articles 93 and 173 of the Public Accounting Law promulgated by Decree No. /14969/ dated 30/12/1963.

Confidentiality of Declarations:

Declarations are of a strictly confidential nature, and anyone who discloses their confidentiality shall be punished by imprisonment for up to one year and by a fine ranging between five and ten times the official minimum wage, or by either of these two penalties, in addition to the possibility of being prosecuted disciplinarily.

Such confidentiality may not be invoked against the Commission and the competent judiciary within the framework of a prosecution, investigation or trial.

False Declaration:

Anyone who submits a false declaration shall be punished by imprisonment from six months to one year and by a fine ranging between 10 and 20 times the official minimum wage.

Elements of the Offence of Illicit Enrichment:

a - Any significant increase occurring in Lebanon and abroad after assuming public office in the financial estate of any public official, whether subject to declaration or not subject thereto, shall be considered illicit enrichment whenever such increase cannot be reasonably justified in relation to his legitimate resources. The said lack of justification shall be considered an element of the offence.

b - For the application of the provisions of this Article, the spouse and minor children, as well as nominees and/or fiduciaries and/or trustees - through sequential ownerships or other sequential indirect means of control or outside thereof - in accordance with the laws in force, shall be considered as one and the same person.

Applicable Law:

a - The offence of illicit enrichment shall be deemed outside the concept of breach of duties and subject to the jurisdiction of the ordinary judiciary.

b - The provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure shall apply to illicit enrichment actions; and in all matters not inconsistent with the provisions of this Law, the procedures of inquiry, investigation and trials set forth in the Law on Combating Corruption in the Public Sector and Establishing the National Anti-Corruption Commission shall apply.

c - Notwithstanding any other text, prior authorisations or permissions provided for in the laws shall not preclude criminal prosecution.

Reports, Complaints, and Direct Actions:

A - Reports and complaints submitted to the Commission, as well as complaints and direct claims submitted by the Commission, shall be free of charge and not conditional upon the payment of any guarantee.

B - Direct claims submitted by the injured party to the competent judiciary shall be subject to a bank guarantee in the value of three million Lebanese Pounds, which shall be confiscated for the benefit of the Treasury and deposited in a special fund at the Ministry of Justice in the event that the action is dismissed by a final decision and the claimant is deemed to have abused the exercise of a right, otherwise it shall be returned to the claimant.

C - Notwithstanding any contrary text, and in the event of suspicion that the funds relate to illicit enrichment, both the Investigating Judge and the competent court may order ex officio:

1 - The freezing of the accounts of the concerned public official for a period of six months, renewable for a similar period.

2 - The placement of an annotation on the records and registers relating to movable or immovable property, indicating that such property is the subject of an investigation by either of them. This annotation shall remain in place until a final judgment is issued by the competent court barring prosecution or declaring an acquittal.

3 - The taking of precautionary measures with respect to movable and immovable property regarding which there are no records or registers, with the aim of restricting the disposal thereof.

4 - These decisions shall be subject to the appeal procedures provided for in the Code of Criminal Procedure.

Statute of Limitations:

The offence of illicit enrichment shall not be subject to the statute of limitations on the public action and on the civil action for the confiscation and recovery of public funds.

Penalty:

A - Whoever commits the offence of illicit enrichment shall be punished by detention from three to seven years and by a fine ranging from thirty times to two hundred times the official minimum wage.

B - The judgment shall order its publication in two local newspapers, and shall also order the restitution of the funds acquired by way of illicit enrichment to the concerned and injured parties, if any, otherwise their confiscation for the benefit of the Treasury.

C - Where necessary, a judgment shall be rendered confiscating funds owned by a third party in any form whatsoever, while preserving the rights of bona fide third parties.

Aggravation of the Penalty:

The penalty shall be increased by one-third to one-half for every public official who used violence, coercion, threat, inducement, trading in influence, or abuse of authority to influence proceedings relating to his prosecution or trial.

Repeal of Contrary Provisions:

Law No. 154 dated 27/12/1999 (Illicit Enrichment Law) and its amendments are hereby repealed, and Legislative Decree No. 38 dated 18/2/1953 (Illicit Enrichment Law), the Law promulgated on 14/4/1954 (Declarations Required to be Submitted by Public Officials and Persons Performing a Public Service Regarding Their Wealth), and any other text that contradicts or is inconsistent with the provisions of this Law shall remain repealed.

Entry into Force of the Law:

This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

- The proposed law aimed at amending Law No. 77 dated 13/4/2018 "Water Law", as amended by the Joint Parliamentary Committees and the Chamber of Deputies, is hereby ratified.

- This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Water is a national wealth:

Water, in all its forms, is a national wealth whose quality and the rights of the Lebanese State in internal, regional, and international watercourses must be preserved. It includes surface water, groundwater, and the fluctuating waves of freshwater off the coasts, and in general water as an element of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems.

The right to water:

Every human being has the fundamental right to obtain the water necessary for his needs, which secures the basic requirements for a dignified life, including sanitation. This shall be in return for paying subscription fees for his use of water.

Objectives of the Water Law:

This Law aims to regulate, develop, rationalise, and exploit water resources, protect them from depletion and pollution, and raise the efficiency of transmission and distribution systems and the proper maintenance and operation of water installations, with the aim of securing sustainable management of the natural water resources of the Lebanese State.

Rights of Beneficiaries of Water:

1 - Every person lawfully benefiting from any water resource shall enjoy the right of usufruct thereof, in a manner that does not harm such resources or the interests of others, and shall bear the same obligations imposed with respect to conserving such resources and protecting them from depletion and pollution.

2 - The exploitation of groundwater resources without a prior licence from the competent authority is prohibited.

3 - The Ministry and the Public Water Exploitation Establishments shall intervene to regulate the rights and obligations of usufruct of water in accordance with the provisions of this Law and the implementing decrees that shall be issued in enforcement of its provisions.

General Objectives through Sustainable Water Management:

1 - The Ministry shall undertake to establish a sustainable water policy for the purpose of conserving the water wealth of the Lebanese State. The Ministry and the Public Water Exploitation Establishments, each within the scope of its competences defined pursuant to Law No. 221/2000, shall also undertake to provide water services to users in all aspects of their uses. To achieve this purpose, it is incumbent upon them to do the following:

A - Priority of supplying citizens with potable water.

B - Achieving sanitation for wastewater.

C - Meeting the needs for water necessary for agriculture, livestock breeding, hunting, fishing and pisciculture in inland waters, mineral water extraction, and for the needs of industry, power generation, transport, tourism, the protection of aquatic, natural and terrestrial sites and landscapes, and all human activities lawfully practised.

D - Utilizing, wherever possible, non-conventional water sources: water desalination, treated water resulting from wastewater treatment plants, and others.

E - Combating floods, drought, and accidental or chronic pollution, in cooperation with the concerned ministries and administrations, and generally anticipating damages that may affect public health and safety and the methods of preventing them.

2 - It is incumbent upon the Ministry of Energy and Water, in cooperation with the Ministry of Environment, to do the following:

A - Combating chronic pollution.

B - Forestalling any further deterioration and conserving and restoring the aquatic environment, as well as the terrestrial ecosystems and wetlands linked thereto, with respect to their water needs.

C - Forestalling pollution and working to reduce it gradually.

Management of the Public Water Domain:

The Ministry of Energy and Water has the competence to manage the public water domain.

Elements of Public Ownership of Water:

1 - Water is public property and is not subject to acquisition, ownership, or disposal in any form whatsoever, subject to the provisions of Decision No. 144/S dated 10 June 1925 and Decision No. 320 dated 23 May 1926.

2 - Public ownership of water includes water in all its natural states, its geological locations, its appurtenances, and the public installations designated or necessary for its management, and comprises:

a - Watercourses of any kind within their boundaries defined by the level line of their running waters at full capacity prior to overflowing.

The banks of watercourses, their easements, and their setbacks shall be determined by decrees.

b - Natural or artificial lakes, coastal lagoons, marshes, and generally bodies of water.

c - Groundwater, including submarine freshwater springs gushing at sea off the Lebanese coasts.

d - Springs, wells, borings, watering places, fountains, and other water sources designated for the public, as well as the potential protection zone of the surrounding areas prepared for their direct protection.

e - Marine or riverine dams, water dams, passages, and the installations annexed thereto.

f - Irrigation, sewage, and drainage canals, water conveyance canals and their branches, pipes, water treatment installations, pumping stations, reservoirs, and wastewater treatment plants when such installations are designated for public use, as well as the equipment and lands pertaining thereto.

g - Waterfalls suitable for generating electrical energy.

Non-Public Water:

Whoever collects rainwater and stores it in a private installation and in swimming pools, pools designated for recreation, marshes, ponds, and reservoirs shall have the full right to use it without the right to sell it to third parties.

Such water shall not form part of the public property of the Lebanese State.

Groundwater:

1 - Groundwater, regardless of its depth, shall be subject to a special regime with respect to protection and monitoring.

2 - No person may extract groundwater by drilling artesian wells or by any other means without obtaining a prior permit or licence from the Ministry of Energy and Water, within the conditions specified under the provisions of this Law.

Boundaries of the Water Public Domain:

The boundaries of the water public domain of the Lebanese State and its appurtenances are those designated pursuant to the provisions of Title Two of Decision No. 144/S dated 10 June 1925 relating to the definition, delimitation and temporary occupation of the public domain.

Acquired Rights on Water:

1 - Acquired rights on water established prior to the issuance of Decision 144/S dated 10/6/1925 shall be exercised in accordance with the customs and usages that justified their acknowledgement, so long as they do not conflict with the requirements of sustainable water management, subject to the following provisions:

a - The invocation of acquired rights shall cease when such rights become useless and the causes for which they were acknowledged cease to exist, or when the exercise of such rights becomes impossible for material reasons.

b - Acquired rights on water may not be assigned separately from the real property upon which such rights are exercised.

2 - The rules governing the exercise, extinction and/or suspension of acquired rights to address any water deficit shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister.

The Water Register:

1 - A Water Register shall be established at the Ministry of Energy and Water, consisting of the register of acquired rights referred to in the preceding Article above, and of the general inventory of waters constituting the aquatic ecosystem of the Lebanese State.

2 - The regulations of the Water Register shall be issued, and its operation and manner of administration shall be organised, by decree.

3 - The Land Registry, the Directorate General of Urban Planning, municipalities, and all public administrations and public and private institutions holding records and data relating to water shall provide the Water Register with such data and information.

The National Water Authority:

1 - A national authority called "The National Water Authority" shall be established at the Presidency of the Council of Ministers, chaired by the President of the Council of Ministers,

and shall be composed of:

- The Minister of Energy and Water - Vice-President.

- The Ministers of (Environment, Industry, Agriculture, Public Works and Transport, Health, Finance, Interior and Municipalities, and Tourism) - Members.

- The Directors-General of the Public Water Investment Establishments - Members.

2 - The Authority may invite whomever it wishes from the public and private sectors and from civil associations to attend its meetings.

3 - The Authority shall lay down its working mechanism by a decision issued by the President of the Council of Ministers.

4 - The Authority may form a temporary technical committee chaired by the Minister of Energy and Water composed of the concerned Directors-General, joined where necessary by specialists and/or civil associations, to study a specific subject.

5 - The Authority shall prepare reports dealing with its work to be submitted to the Council of Ministers for its information.

Role of the National Water Authority:

The National Water Authority shall undertake:

1 - Contributing to the determination of the general objectives and guiding principles for a general and sustainable national policy for the water sector.

2 - Studying the General Master Plan for Water, which shall become effective by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers.

3 - Studying the capacity of the State to finance plans and projects, laying down financing programmes, and determining the sources thereof.

4 - Studying plans and programmes aimed at regulating the uses of water, preventing the waste thereof, and rationalising the consumption thereof.

5 - Approving projects and regulating the distribution of water of national and regional importance, in addition to determining the priorities of projects and the distribution thereof across regions.

6 - Studying the orientations and measures envisaged by the competent ministries for the application of integrated water management, particularly in the field of protecting aquatic ecosystems, including tourism, industry, energy, forest management, agricultural activities, livestock breeding, fishing, and urban planning.

7 - Formulating recommendations dealing with research, education, training, and information in the field of water, with a view to improving the management of this resource.

8 - Reviewing international treaties relating to the sharing of water in transboundary rivers or having an impact on national water security, and expressing an opinion thereon.

The General Master Plan for Water:

1 - The Lebanese Republic shall be divided into water or administrative basins and regions, and the water resources of each of them shall be assessed and their development and use shall be planned as existing units and shall be organised on the basis of the principle of integrated water resources management in accordance with the orientations of social and economic development and the preservation of the environment.

2 - Sustainable water management shall be achieved through a General Master Plan for Water applicable to the entire Lebanese territory and including coastal waters and basin networks within the scope of the hydrographic basin.

3 - Ministries, public administrations, administrative and investment public institutions, and municipalities shall abide by the General Master Plan for Water, after its issuance by the Council of Ministers.

Preparation of the General Master Plan for Water:

The Ministry, in cooperation with the public water investment institutions, shall draw up the General Master Plan for Water, in coordination with the Ministries of (Environment - Agriculture - Public Works and Transport and Industry). It shall be approved pursuant to a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister.

Contents of the Water Master Plan:

The General Water Master Plan shall include the following:

1 - An analysis of the characteristics of water and aquatic ecosystems, which primarily determines the following:

a - The quantities of water consumed and currently available and expected to become available, in the light of which the current and future needs for water may be determined.

b - The current needs for water in the main sectors: human consumption, agriculture, livestock breeding, industries and similar activities, hydroelectric power production, tourism and recreational activities (recreation)...

c - The development of expected needs, in the medium term and the long term, for water in the various sectors of the State.

d - The status of water installations, sanitation systems and non-conventional water source systems.

2 - Data and tables including:

a - The quantities of conventional and non-conventional, surface, ground and gushing (springs) water.

b - The conditions of surface and ground water.

c - The areas subject to special provisions.

d - The water conveyance areas designated for human supply.

3 - The objectives of sustainable water management, in particular:
