a - The quantitative objectives that must be achieved within a specific time period in the Master Plan, to meet the needs the basic needs for water and the necessity of reconciling them with the surrounding environment and with the basic needs of the population.

b - The qualitative objectives that allow reaching, within a time period determined by the Master Plan, an acceptable environmental status for surface, ground and coastal water.

c - Securing the necessary facilities and installations to avoid deterioration in water quality, provide protection therefor, and improve the status of water and aquatic ecosystems, and estimating their costs with a view to securing them.

d - Determining the rules and manner of informing citizens of the objectives and measures intended to be taken to maintain sustainable water management.

e - Determining the means for the optimal use of water in order to achieve the maximum benefit for all current and future needs in the main water sectors.

f - Establishing a plan for the prevention and treatment of water pollution.

4 - The maps that allow the accurate designation of the elements mentioned in the Master Plan, in particular:

a - Protected areas.

b - Polluted areas and areas exposed to pollution risks.

c - Water conveyance areas designated for human consumption.

d - Irrigation areas.

e - Areas exposed to a water deficit.

f - Areas in which connection to the collective sanitation network is mandatory.

g - Areas to which the Public Water Exploitation Establishments effectively provide potable water and collective sanitation.

h - The main facilities intended to be established to meet the urgent need for water and the objectives of sustainable water management specified in the Master Plan, in particular facilities for water extraction, potable water treatment, wastewater refining, discharge of treated or stored water, rainwater drainage, water desalination or electric power production.

The General Master Plan shall designate the areas subject thereto in accordance with what has been set out above.

Scope of Application of the General Master Plan for Water:

When applying the General Master Plan for Water, the Administration concerned shall take into account all plans, programmes, basin plans, granted licences and permits, urban planning, population ratios in the regions, the status of classified establishments, and, in general, shall take into account all previous administrative decisions relating to water.

Evaluation of the General Master Plan for Water:

The General Master Plan for Water shall be subject to evaluation and review once every five years, and whenever the need arises therefor.

Basin plans:

The Ministry shall undertake the establishment of the principles of general water planning in the light of the results of the assessment of the basins or water service areas, so that it includes the general indicators of the status of the water basins in the various Lebanese regions and the trends of water demand for all water uses in the short, medium and long term, in accordance with the following:

First - Preparation of basin plans:

The Ministry must prepare plans for the main and secondary water basins, particularly in areas suffering from a decline in their water resources or from pollution in the aquatic ecosystems therein.

The scope of the basin plans and coordination with the Public Water Investment Establishments shall be determined.

The details of the application of this Article shall be determined pursuant to a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister.

Second: Content of basin plans

Basin plans shall include the following:

1 - A detailed report setting out the characteristics of the basin that justify the preparation of its own plan, proceeding from a comprehensive assessment of the status of water and ecosystems therein.

2 - An administrative document determining:

a - The objectives, quality, quantity and the presumed time-limits for achieving them.

b - Assessment of the water resources in the water basin in terms of quantity and quality.

c - Environmental impact assessment.

d - Waste discharge monitoring measures.

e - Priority of allocating the equitable distribution of water, the treatment and reuse of water, and the control and monitoring measures that ensure the equitable and equal use of water.

f - The manner of distributing water among the various categories of beneficiaries.

g - Non-conventional water sources.

h - Conditions of management of the resource during crises, such as pollution, water shortage, floods and fires.

i - The means that must be used to reach the specified objectives.

j - The indicators that allow the follow-up of the completed works and the evaluation of the completed measures, programmes and commitments and the evaluation of the measures, programmes and commitments adopted with respect to the objectives.

3 - The maps that allow the identification of the sites targeted in the plan.

Decisions relating to basin plans must be consistent with the provisions of the General Master Plan for Water.

Basin classification system:

The Ministry shall establish a system for classifying basins and water areas in the light of their water conditions, the purpose of which shall be to place similar ones under a single pattern of measures.

Basin Plans:

Each basin or area shall have a water plan drawn up by the concerned Public Water Exploitation Establishment, consistent with the water policy and with the General Master Plan. Following their approval by the Ministry, these plans shall be deemed an integral part of the General Master Plan.

General Provisions:

Subject to the provisions of Law No. 221 dated 29 May 2000 and its amendments and the provisions of Articles (1) and (2) of Decision No. 320 dated 26 May 1926, and with the aim of achieving sustainable management of water and of aquatic ecosystems, the Ministry and the Ministry of Environment shall contribute with the Lebanese Standards Institution (LIBNOR) to setting the quality standards and necessary provisions for the preservation of water and the ecosystems required therefor, and in particular shall determine the various types of water consumption and their cumulative impacts on the aquatic environment.

Protection of Water Resources:

The Ministry and the Public Water Exploitation Establishments, each within its scope and competence, shall undertake the protection of water resources from pollution, the monitoring of emission standards and sources of pollution, the setting of rules and procedures for carrying out control over equipment belonging to water installations, the prevention of activities that may lead to the pollution or degradation of water quality, and the combating of cases of emergency pollution.

Each of the Ministry and the competent Public Water Exploitation Establishments may also take against the person causing the damage all or some of the following administrative measures:

a - Prohibiting a specific activity that causes grave risks to aquatic ecosystems or prohibiting the continuation of the execution of such activity.

b - Executing remediation works such as removing pollution and maintaining the sites at the expense of the person causing the damage.

c - Imposing administrative and technical obligations and fines.

d - Every measure aimed at preventing or limiting any damage affecting aquatic ecosystems.

Technical Control and Water Quality:

1 - The Ministry shall undertake to ensure the monitoring of the quality of surface, ground, coastal and gushing waters, including springs, wells and exploited or neglected techniques. The Public Water Exploitation Establishments shall abide by the monitoring obligations mentioned in this paragraph, when the water sources exploited by them are affected.

2 - The Ministry, in cooperation with the concerned Public Water Exploitation Establishments, shall undertake to carry out technical control over equipment, installations and works to verify the quality of extracted water and to monitor aquatic systems and protect them from pollution.

Supervision of Works and Operations:

Equipment, installations, works, and operations carried out by any natural or legal person belonging to either the public or private sector, and which lead to the following, shall be subject to the supervision regime:

1 - The extraction of surface, underground, artesian, or coastal waters and their return or non-return to their source.

2 - A modification in the level or mode of flow of water.

3 - A direct or indirect, chronic or occasional discharge, flow, disposal, or sedimentation leading to an impact on water or on aquatic ecosystems, even if it does not cause pollution in the aquatic ecosystem.

4 - The extraction of groundwater.

5 - The cleaning, deepening, straightening, or regulation of temporary or permanent watercourses.

The Water Code:

1 - A code shall be kept at the Ministry, which shall be regulated pursuant to a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister.

2 - The equipment, installations, works, and operations mentioned in the preceding Article above must be listed in the code.

3 - The code shall clarify the nature of the controls to which these operations are subject, taking into consideration the impacts that may result therefrom on the quality or level of water and aquatic ecosystems.

4 - The specific levels applicable to water scarcity areas defined in the General Master Plan shall be precisely determined in the code.

Compliance with the Provisions of the Environment Law:

Every owner of an installation must comply with the provisions of the Environmental Protection Law in Lebanon, in particular Articles 21 to 48 of Law No. 444/2002.

Preservation of Water Quality and Grade:

The Public Water Exploitation Establishments shall determine the rules for the equitable distribution of water among the various categories of beneficiaries, while preserving the quality and grade of the water. Accordingly, they must prevent any form of direct or indirect discharge and leakage of stagnant or polluted water, prevent the performance of any act of any kind whatsoever that leads to modifying the quality of water or aquatic ecosystems, and impose the necessary measures to preserve water quality.

Monitoring of Water Quality:

The Ministry and the Public Water Exploitation Establishments shall, each within its competence, undertake the monitoring of water quality at the level of the resources so as to ensure its suitability for use, and shall also undertake the monitoring of quality during transport, distribution, and use.

Obligations of the owners of installations:

The owners of industrial and classified establishments, the owners of industrial, commercial, agricultural and health installations, and all those who engage in any of the activities that generate waste shall abide by the provisions of this Law with respect to refraining from discharging, dumping, diverting or leaking waste of all kinds resulting from their activities into river courses and surface and underground aquatic environments, except after treating it in accordance with the rules provided for in the laws in force, under penalty of withdrawal of the licences granted to them.

The owners of industrial and classified establishments, and the owners of industrial, commercial, agricultural and health installations existing prior to the issuance of this Law shall submit to the competent authorities, within six months from the date of its entry into force, applications for the regularisation of the status of their installations in accordance with its provisions, under penalty of withdrawal of the licences granted to them.

Traditional rights of usufruct:

Traditional rights in the use of rainwater harvesting water and naturally flowing torrent water shall be observed, with respect to their use for irrigation and their connection to the agricultural land benefiting therefrom.

Traditional rights to irrigation from other water sources shall only be established outside the operational scope of irrigation projects belonging to the public water investment establishments.

The details of the application of this Article shall be determined by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister.

Public interest and the right of usufruct:

Subject to the provisions of Article 12 of this Law, the cases in which the Lebanese State may take possession of the rights of usufruct of water if the public interest so requires or due to the necessity of rationalising water uses, with fair compensation to the beneficiaries in accordance with the laws in force, shall be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister.

Rules of application:

1 - The conditions set forth in Decision No. 320 dated 26 May 1926 shall be observed in the licences, with the exception of what has been repealed or amended pursuant to this Law.

2 - The regulations and provisions for the application of the licensing system shall be laid down by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister, provided that it includes the following:

a - The applicable procedures.

b - The environmental impact assessment.

c - The rules relating to abstractions, and in particular the cases in which a minimum water level may be imposed.

d - The measures imposed to monitor compliance with the provisions of this Chapter.

Licensing System:

Licences shall be issued by the Minister in accordance with the following rules:

1- No natural or legal person may, after the issuance of this Law, construct any financial installation to impound or obstruct runoff water and flowing water in watercourses and valleys or divert them from their courses except after obtaining a prior licence. Provided that the Ministry carries out a comprehensive national survey of all installations built without a licence prior to the issuance of this Law, and studies them case by case and proposes technical modifications thereto and the required administrative measures where necessary.

2 - No water well may be deepened or cleaned out without obtaining a licence, under penalty of withdrawal of the previously granted licence and backfilling of the well at the expense of its owner.

3 - No new well or replacement well may be drilled, nor may any water installation be constructed, unless the beneficiary obtains a valid licence for this purpose.

4 - The beneficiary must comply with the conditions specified in the licence, which specifies the conditions necessary for implementation.

5 - All works that may cause hazards relating to public health and safety, or obstruct the flow of water, or reduce water resources, or significantly increase flood risks, or cause damage to the quality of the aquatic environment or to biodiversity in the aquatic medium, shall be subject to prior licensing.

6 - All works involving water intended for non-domestic purposes shall be subject to prior licensing, and the same shall apply to irrigation installations, hydroelectric installations, pisciculture, hydroponic equipment, and water prospecting.

7 - Subject to the application of the provisions of Decision No. 320 dated 26 May 1926, licences may be withdrawn or amended pursuant to a reasoned decision issued by the Minister, in the following cases:

a - If the decision is taken in the interest of the public good.

b - To avert dangerous situations such as water scarcity or floods.

c - In the event of the emergence of a grave danger to the natural components of water and aquatic ecosystems.

Licences may also be withdrawn pursuant to a reasoned decision issued by the Minister, and without compensation, in the following cases:

a - When water installations are abandoned and their operators no longer have need of them.

b - If the licensee does not commence drilling works within the time limits specified in the licensing system.

c - If he uses this licence for a purpose other than that for which it was granted.

d - If he violates the conditions set forth in the licence.

e - If he assigns this licence to a third party without the assignment including the property concerned, whether for consideration or without consideration, and without the approval of the licensing authority.

The liability of the granting authority shall remain in effect in accordance with the general principles governing abuse of authority, particularly in the event that the decision to withdraw the licence results in damages to the beneficiary of the licence without fault on his part.

Regularisation of the status of drilled wells:

- Beneficiaries of the waters of underground wells, drilled without a licence from the Ministry or drilled legally without their owners having obtained an exploitation licence therefor, shall be entitled to obtain an exploitation licence therefor after submitting applications to regularise their status within a maximum period of two years from the date of entry into force of this Law, under pain of closure of the well,

- The licence shall be refused in the following cases:

- If the well is drilled in the property of third parties, public property, or communal lands.

- If the well affects water sources and flowing springs or springs feeding lakes or rivers.

- Temporary licences shall be granted to those from whom licences are withheld for the above reasons pending the provision of alternatives by the competent water authorities, unless the well is drilled in private and public property.

Administrative measures:

Whoever contravenes the provisions of the licensing regime provided for pursuant to the provisions of Article 36 of this Law and Articles 745 to 749 of the Penal Code, shall be subject to the criminal prosecution specified in the body of Title Eight of this Law, and the Ministry shall also be entitled, in addition to criminal prosecution, to take specific administrative measures against the offender as follows:

1 - Warning the offender, the operator, or the owner to comply, within a period determined by the Ministry, with the provisions and instructions relating to the subject of the contravention.

2 - Determining the measures that the offender must undertake to remove the damage they have caused.

3 - In the event of the presence of a risk of pollution or of deterioration of the conditions of the aquatic ecosystem, or damage to public health, or a threat affecting the drinking water supply, taking immediate measures at the expense and responsibility of the persons referred to above to prevent and limit the occurring pollution.

4 - Suspending or withdrawing the licence.

5 - Drawing up an offence report against the offender and referring it to the Environmental Public Prosecution or to the competent Single Criminal Judge.

The Ministry and the Public Water Exploitation Establishments must, each within its powers, upon becoming aware of the occurrence of any damage to aquatic ecosystems, immediately take the initiative to address the causes of the damage that has occurred. They shall be entitled to recover the expenses they have incurred from the person or persons who bear responsibility for causing the damage before the competent judicial authorities.

Incidents:

1 - Every person who has knowledge of a fact constituting a threat to public safety and to the quality, distribution, and conservation of water, or to Lebanese water and fishery resources, must immediately notify the competent authorities.

2 - Every person who has caused any act constituting damage to water quality is required, immediately upon becoming aware of the matter, to take all appropriate measures to bring an end to the danger or the damage caused to the aquatic environment and to proceed to remediate it.

3 - The competent administration, which intervened to take measures aimed at bringing an end to the damage caused to aquatic ecosystems, is entitled to recover the costs it incurred from the party that caused the damage before the competent judicial authorities.

The Industrial and Commercial Nature of the Public Water Utility:

1 - The public water utility comprises the public operational establishments for potable water, irrigation, and wastewater.

2 - The public water utility shall be managed like any public utility of an industrial and commercial nature, subject to the principle of the continuity and development of the public utility.

The Principle of Financial Equilibrium:

1 - The public operational water establishments must achieve financial equilibrium for the water utility.

2 - In order to observe the principle of financial equilibrium of the utility, the public water utilities shall be financed from the fees and subscription revenues paid by the beneficiaries.

Financial Equilibrium of Services:

1 - The fees or tariffs pertaining to public water services shall be determined by applying the principle of financial equilibrium of services, which requires the beneficiary to pay the fees for their water consumption, and the polluter to pay the fees for treating and repairing the damage they have caused.

2 - The fees or tariffs shall be determined after taking into account the financial equilibrium of the establishment and the social and economic conditions of the beneficiaries, and these fees shall follow a progressive scale based on the quantity of consumption.

3 - Pending the completion of the measures aimed at applying the volumetric tariff, the flat-rate tariff shall be applied in non-rehabilitated areas.

State Contribution:

Notwithstanding the principles set forth in the articles above, the Lebanese State may provide contributions to the public water utility by contributing to the financing of the expenditure for renewing, modernising, and expanding the works of the projects of the public operational water establishments and securing the operating expenditure of these projects.

Financial provisions:

1 - The budget and accounts of each of the public water exploitation establishments shall show in detail the manner in which the operation, exploitation and maintenance operations are distributed in respect of each of drinking water, wastewater and agricultural irrigation.

The funds and fees collected from the operation operations above may not be used to finance the exploitation and maintenance of precipitation water collection installations that are not subject to the competence of the establishment.

2 - A special accounting plan must be prepared for each service within the public water exploitation establishments.

Approval of fees:

The public water exploitation establishments shall approve the fees for public water services, including the fees for connection to the public networks within the scope of the exploitation area of the establishment, provided that they are coupled with the ratification of the tutelage authority.

Fees:

The fees established pursuant to this Law may include:

- Drinking water service fees.

- Wastewater service fees.

- Irrigation service fees.

- Fees for the conservation of the water resource and the protection of aquatic ecosystems.

- Fees resulting from pollution.

- Fees for tourist and industrial exploitation, fishing, fish farming and power generation.

Drinking water fees:

1 - Drinking water fees and subscriptions shall fall due on every person who benefits from the public water network.

2 - The fee for subscription to the public drinking water network may be determined on the basis of the quantity of water consumed by the subscriber by means of a water meter.

Sanitation Charges:

The sanitation charges determined pursuant to the provisions of this Law shall include collective sanitation charges and non-collective sanitation charges.

1 - The payment of collective sanitation charges shall be due from every person connected to the public sanitation network, and this charge shall be determined on the basis of the volume of water withdrawn by the beneficiaries of the service, whether its source is the public potable water network or any other source.

The charges for non-domestic use of the public sanitation network shall be determined on the basis of:

a - The volume and quality of the discharged water, provided that it conforms to environmental standards and specifications, and where it does not conform to these standards and specifications, the provisions of Article 51 (Pollution Compensation Charge) shall apply thereto.

b - The quantity of pollution of the emissions resulting from such water.

Natural or legal persons who have not complied with the obligation to connect to the collective sanitation network shall be subject to a fine equal to the value of the charge determined for connecting to the collective sanitation network.

2 - Non-collective sanitation charges shall be due from every person who is not connected to the sanitation network in accordance with what is determined in paragraph "1" above, on the basis of the quantity and quality of the water withdrawn.

Irrigation Charge:

1 - The irrigation charge shall be payable by every beneficiary or owner of real property connected to the public irrigation network.

2 - The value of the charges due shall be determined in relation to the irrigated area or the quantities of water consumed, provided that the nature of the irrigated crops is taken into consideration.

Charges Relating to the Conservation of Water Resources and the Protection of Aquatic Systems:

1 - Where necessary, and for the purpose of conserving the water resource and protecting aquatic systems, Public Water Exploitation Establishments may impose on natural or legal persons benefiting from the water a charge based on the irrigated area or the number of cubic metres withdrawn, consumed or allocated for supply, provided that this charge is used to finance works for the conservation of the water resource and the protection of the relevant aquatic ecosystems.

2 - In determining the persons liable, the activities concerned and the value of the charges, account shall be taken of the economic, social, cultural and environmental importance of these activities and of revenues and profits of whatever kind.

Public Water Exploitation Establishments shall collect the charges for the conservation of the resource and the protection of aquatic systems regardless of who the beneficiary is.

Pollution compensation fee:

1 - Natural and legal persons the nature of whose activities leads to the pollution of ecological and water systems in a manner not amenable to mitigation and prior treatment, and the pollution rate of which does not exceed nationally and internationally acceptable standards, shall be subject to a compensation fee to be determined by decree upon the proposal of the Minister.

2 - The compensation fee referred to above shall be proportionate to the severity of the pollution and the extent of the damage caused to the water environment.

3 - The compensation fee may be reduced in light of the measures taken by the person causing the damage to remedy it.

4 - The payment of pollution compensation fees shall not constitute an impediment to the arising of criminal and civil liability upon the polluter in the event that his acts are a source of damage or constitute a criminal offence.

The concerned administrations must take the measures that lead to ensuring the preservation of the water environment.

Issuance of receipts:

Receipts issued by the Public Water Investment Establishments must clearly state the fees pertaining to each utility.

Procedures for the issuance and payment of receipts:

The Public Water Investment Establishments may issue several receipts per year, and every beneficiary of the water of this utility shall have the option to pay the value of the subscriptions due per year in several instalments.

Notification regarding fees:

Beneficiaries of water shall be notified of the new fees, the justifications for their amendment, and the date of their entry into force pursuant to an official notice circulated to the media and the concerned municipalities. Receipts issued after the amendment of the fees must specify the old and new fees.

Surveying the opinion of beneficiaries:

With the aim of improving the service and sustainable development, the Public Water Investment Establishments shall conduct, every three years, an opinion survey of the beneficiaries, the results of which shall be sent to the Minister and published through the media.

Public Water Investment Establishments:

The Public Water Investment Establishments shall manage the public water utility in accordance with the provisions of Law No. 221 dated 29/5/2000 and its amendments and the regulations issued in implementation thereof, and the provisions of this Law.

Public Water Utilities:

1 - The public drinking water utility comprises the service of collecting, producing, treating, conveying, storing and distributing water. Distribution to beneficiaries shall take place principally by means of connections from the network. Water may not be provided otherwise than as stated above except in exceptional and temporary cases.

2 - The collective public sanitation utility comprises the collection, conveyance and treatment of wastewater, and the objective of refining wastewater is to eliminate pollutants so that it is compatible with the receiving environments, and refining operations include treating and cleaning all pollutants and sludge in the network and refining stations up to the outfalls.

3 - Wastewater is primarily of domestic origin, and wastewater resulting from commercial or industrial activities may, pursuant to ordinary or special agreements concluded by the Public Water Exploitation Establishments in this regard, be connected to the public sanitation network, provided that such water complies with the technical standards for networks and refining stations.

4 - The Public Water Exploitation Establishments may supply water for agricultural purposes by means of the irrigation network or by means of a set of hydraulic installations.

Agreements with the Public Sector:

The Ministry and the Public Water Exploitation Establishments may, with due regard to the competence of each of them in accordance with the laws and regulations in force, conclude agreements with public law persons in order to ensure the sustainable management and development of the public water utility. Such agreements may be concluded with municipalities to regulate the application of the provisions of Article Eight of the Water Sector Organisation Law No. 221 issued on 29 May 2000 and in respect of the committees currently managing and exploiting drinking and irrigation water.

These agreements shall, in their implementation, observe the provisions of the General Master Plan for Water and the basin plans, and may not deal with anything contrary to the object of exploiting the public water utility.

Private Sector Participation through Joint Projects:

The provisions of Law No. 48 dated 7/9/2017, "Law Regulating Public-Private Partnership", shall apply upon the awarding of a contract relating to a "joint project".

These contracts shall observe the provisions of the General Master Plan for Water and the basin plans, and may not deal with anything contrary to the object of exploiting the public water utility.

Participation of the Private Sector through Other Forms:

The provisions of the regulations in force at the Public Water Investment Establishments shall remain in effect when awarding contracts pertaining to projects in which the participation of the private sector differs from the form provided for in the definition of the "Joint Venture". These contracts shall observe the provisions of the General Master Plan for Water and the basin plans and may not deal with anything that violates the subject of the exploitation of the public water utility.

Water Quality:

The distributed water must be potable regardless of the form of management of the utility, and the competent administrations, particularly the Ministry and the Ministry of Public Health, must oversee the application of the applicable standards and specifications.

Principle of Exclusivity of the Utility:

Within the scope of exploitation, the public potable water utility shall enjoy exclusivity of distribution and the exclusive right to maintain all installations and water channels necessary for the utility.

Each Public Water Investment Establishment shall take over all potable water committees and projects prior to Law No. 221/2000, which have not yet been taken over, within a period of one year from the date of issuance of this Law and in accordance with the procedures in force.

Duty to Connect:

Every building owner shall be obliged to connect his building and all sections therein to the public network for the distribution of potable water prior to occupying them, and the connection shall take place in accordance with the regulations established by the concerned Public Water Investment Establishment and in accordance with the contract signed between it and the beneficiary.

No transaction relating to a real right on a property subscribed to potable water shall be registered in the Real Estate Register, except after the property owner presents a clearance certificate issued by the Establishment certifying that the subscriber has paid all fees, charges, and fines due from him.

Special Subscription Contracts:

The public potable water utility may distribute water to beneficiaries for non-domestic purposes, and special subscriptions shall be determined in this case.

Performance of the Utility:

In application of the legal regime governing the rules of delegation in the public water utility or of what is provided for in the management contract concluded with the competent administration, the public potable water utility shall be obliged to meet the requirements relating to the continuity and quality of the supplied water as well as to observe the time limits relating to applications for subscriptions or their termination.

Measurement of Potable Water Consumption:

The consumption of the subscriber shall be measured by means of suitable meters in accordance with the contract signed by the beneficiary. As for connections not equipped with meters, they must meet this condition within a period determined by the Public Water Investment Establishment.

General provisions:

1 - Subject to the legal provisions in force, the public water exploitation establishments shall assume, each within its scope of exploitation, the management and exploitation of irrigation water, including the maintenance of water conveyance systems, and the storage, transport, distribution and preservation of the quality thereof.

2 - Applications for subscription to irrigation water shall include clauses specifying the supply area, the irrigated area, the types of crops, the irrigation schedule, the required quantities and the method of irrigation.

3 - Any amendment to the contents of the clause above requires an application for amendment of the subscription, provided that this application is submitted within the period specified in the exploitation regulations pertaining to each public water exploitation establishment.

4 - The establishments entrusted with irrigation shall keep a register showing the names of the beneficiaries, the irrigated areas, the adopted crops and the quantities withdrawn, which shall be updated on a continuous basis.

5 - No transaction relating to a real right over a property subscribed to irrigation water shall be registered in the Real Estate Register until the owner of the property produces a clearance certificate issued by the establishment attesting that the subscriber has paid all fees, charges and fines due from him.

6 - The regulations for the management and exploitation of irrigation projects and the amendments thereto shall have a binding nature in regulating the relationship between the beneficiaries and the public water exploitation establishment.

7 - Each public water exploitation establishment shall take over all irrigation water committees and projects prior to Law No. 221/2000, which have not yet been taken over, within a period of one year from the date of issuance of this Law and in accordance with the applicable procedures.

Regulations of the Public Drinking Water Utility:

The regulations of the Public Drinking Water Utility shall define the relations with the beneficiaries of the water, and in particular the rules governing connections, private subscriptions, and the places designated for installing consumption measuring devices, in addition to the performance of the utility.

Principle of Exclusivity of the Utility:

Within the scope of operation defined in the General Master Plan for Water provided for in Article 16 of this Law, the Public Collective Sanitation Utility shall exclusively enjoy the right to manage this sector and the exclusive right to maintain all installations and conduits necessary for this utility.

Duty to Connect to the Public Sanitation Network:

Within the scope of collective sanitation, every owner of a building shall be required to connect the building to the network within a period not exceeding one year from the date of full implementation of the sanitation system.

As for buildings or sections not designated for habitation, they must be connected to the sanitation network within the aforementioned period, with respect to waste of a domestic nature.

Every person is bound to connect to the sanitation network, and sanitation charges shall be determined on the basis of the subscriber's consumption on the public drinking water network. However, if he benefits wholly or partially from a private water source, he must declare this to the Establishment managing the public utility, and the sanitation charges due from him shall be determined by measuring the consumption drawn from the private source.

Special Subscription Contracts:

The Public Sanitation Utility may approve the connection of non-domestic wastewater pursuant to a special connection agreement, provided that the nature or volume of such waste does not lead to a disruption in the operation of the sanitation installations, and that the rules for assessing pollution and discharged volumes are defined in the aforementioned agreement.

With regard to seasonal activities, temporary agreements for the discharge of waste may be approved exceptionally and for a specified period, provided that they do not cause any damage to the conveyance or wastewater treatment installations or to the medium into which they discharge.

Performance of the Utilities:

The Public Collective Sanitation Utility shall be bound to ensure the continuity and quality of the collection and treatment of wastewater.

Regulations of the Public Collective Sanitation Utility:

Relations with the beneficiaries of the collective sanitation network shall be subject to the regulations established by the Public Water Operating Establishments for the management of this utility, and approved by the supervisory authority.

Supervision of Non-Collective Sanitation Installations:

The rules adopted by the Administration to supervise and manage non-collective sanitation installations shall be determined by decree.

Irrigation Water Users' Associations:

1 - Where necessary, in accordance with the provisions of this Law, irrigation water users' associations shall be established by a decree passed in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister based on the request of the concerned Public Water Exploitation Establishment, provided that their administrative board includes a representative of the concerned Public Water Exploitation Establishment.

2 - It is required that irrigation water users' associations be non-profit, and that at least 65% of the beneficiaries of a specified water source be affiliated therewith, representing at least 51% of the area of the benefiting geographical zone.

3 - The geographical zone within which the irrigation water users' associations operate and the water source mentioned in the preceding paragraph shall be determined in the decree establishing the association.

4 - Each of the irrigation water users' associations shall have its own unique name, which may be the name of its place of operation or another distinctive name, and which must begin with the following phrase: "Irrigation Water Users' Association", provided that its operation is confined within the geographical scope or water source specified for it, without the scope of any one of these associations overlapping with the scope of another association.

5 - The details of implementation of this Article, the administrative and financial regulations to which irrigation water users' associations are subject, and the mechanism for transforming existing committees into irrigation water users' associations shall be determined by a decree passed in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister.

Activities of Irrigation Water Users' Associations:

Irrigation water users' associations shall carry out the following activities:

1 - Operating and maintaining the secondary distribution network, in agreement with the Establishment, and preserving it within its area of jurisdiction.

2 - Organising the process of benefiting from and using irrigation water and collecting membership subscriptions to the association from the members, in return for the services provided to them.

3 - Taking appropriate measures to combat the affecting of soil and to combat salinity and pollution, and promoting the protection of the environment.

4 - Providing irrigation equipment, machinery, tools and installations necessary for operating the relevant water distribution network within its area of jurisdiction and preserving it, as well as ensuring their replacement, operation and maintenance.

5 - Training its members in the use of modern irrigation techniques, aspects of irrigated agriculture, methods of saving in water consumption, and rationalising the use of agricultural fertilisers and pesticides.

6 - Contributing and assisting, after the approval of the concerned Public Exploitation Establishment, in constructing, improving, rehabilitating, operating and maintaining infrastructure complementary to irrigation projects, in particular main and secondary drainage canals within the association's area of jurisdiction.

7 - Seeking to settle disputes arising between the members of the association or with third parties.

8 - Working to observe, respect and guarantee the interests of the members of the association.

Fundamental Principles:

Every irrigation water users' association shall abide by and respect in its work the following principles:

1 - Justice and fairness, so as to ensure respect for the rights of its members, particularly in decisions relating to the distribution of irrigation water to the beneficiaries in a manner that observes proportionality and reconciliation between the needs and the available capacities.

2 - Rationalising the use of resources, through the association managing the secondary distribution network, within its area of jurisdiction, in a rational manner that prevents excessive use of water, soil erosion, salinity and pollution, in addition to promoting the protection of the environment.

3 - Transparency and participation, through working in a public, clear and transparent manner, and encouraging the members to participate effectively in its administrative bodies.

General obligations of the State:

1 - The relevant public administrations shall undertake the protection of the public water utility, and the works and operations related thereto may be provided under agreements or contracts.

2 - The relevant public administrations, those contracting with them, and the beneficiaries of rights over the public water utility must ensure the maintenance of the aquatic environment and the protection of the national plant, animal, and fish wealth. In a manner that guarantees ensuring the free flow of water, limiting its pollution, and protecting the installations associated therewith.

Obligations of owners of real properties adjacent to riverbanks:

The owner of a real property adjacent to a riverbank shall be obliged to ensure proper care of the banks and the preservation of plant and animal life within the respect and balance of aquatic ecosystems.

Annual Report of the Public Water Exploitation Establishments:

The Public Water Exploitation Establishments, each within its geographic scope, shall prepare an annual report on the water utilities that fall within its geographic scope, in accordance with what is provided for pursuant to the provisions of Article (6) of Law No. 221/2000 and its amendments.

The report shall present the administrative, technical and financial characteristics and conditions, the operating procedures and performance of the utility, the variables occurring in the quality of the distributed water, the rate of exploitation, the fees, the status of bill collection, the current and future water needs, as well as the accomplished extension works and renewal of water installations and the programmes established therefor.

The annual report shall be submitted to the Minister following its approval by the Board of Directors of the Public Water Exploitation Establishment, and the Minister shall refer a copy of the annual report to the Chamber of Deputies in accordance with the established procedures, and the report shall be published on the official website of the Ministry of Energy and Water.

General Report on the Conditions and Sustainable Management of Water:

The Minister shall draw up each year a general report addressing the conditions of the sustainable management of water.

The report shall include in particular:

1 - The measures of application of this Law, whether in respect of decrees, decisions, circulars, plans and programmes, or ordinary measures.

2 - The development of the available quantitative and qualitative data.

3 - The outcome of the programme for the management and economic use of water.

4 - The measures taken by the Administration.

The annual report on the general situation and sustainable management of water shall be published in the Official Gazette, and a copy thereof shall be notified to the Chamber of Deputies and to the National Water Authority.

Principles:

1 - Every individual shall be required to contribute effectively to the conservation and protection of water across all Lebanese territory, and of aquatic ecosystems and water, and to inform the competent Administration of any defect or damage to which they may be subjected.

2 - The public administrations, and in particular the Ministry, the Ministry of Environment, the Public Water Exploitation Establishments and the Governors, each within the scope of its powers, shall undertake to ensure the protection of water and aquatic ecosystems in accordance with the legal provisions in force.

Conservation of the Aquatic Environment:

The conservation of the aquatic environment shall be deemed an element of the management of the public water utility.

Protection of water sites:

First: Scope of protection:

1 - With a view to securing the protection of water quality, prior to licensing the works and installations erected for drawing surface water and/or extracting groundwater intended for human consumption or upon licensing the same, the pivot point of the extractions and the scope of each of the immediate protection and the adjacent protection, and, where required, the scope of the further protection, shall be designated.

2 - This scope shall also be determined in cases of drawing and extractions subject to licences, for so long as the water is allocated in part or in whole for human consumption.

3 - The determination of the scope of protection shall take place by a decision issued by the Minister and/or the competent ministers, each within the scope of his competence.

Second: Regime of protection zones:

1 - The State shall expropriate, in favour of the Ministry or the public water exploitation establishments, the lands located within the scope of immediate protection by way of full expropriation, and these establishments shall undertake to fence them and see to their exclusive allocation for drawing and exploiting water and regularly maintaining them for this purpose.

2 - Within the scope of adjacent protection, all constructions and activities that would directly or indirectly harm the water quality or the subterranean stratum, or might lead to rendering this water unfit for human consumption, shall be prohibited.

3 - This prohibition shall extend in particular to waste and refuse dumps and the spreading of fertilisers, petroleum installations and installations and warehouses of chemical and organic intendeds and quarries, and any substances involving hazards of pollution or toxins, in particular chemical substances, pesticides, fertilisers and the drilling of water wells.

4 - In supplement to the immediate scope and the adjacent scope, the Ministry and/or the public water exploitation establishments may determine a distant protection scope in which lands are expropriated if necessary, and the warehouses, equipment and activities mentioned in the preceding paragraph are regulated in order to avoid the pollution risks that they may represent in respect of the extracted water.

Third: Protection of natural and cultural aquatic heritage:

1 - Public parks and nature reserves as well as wetlands of international importance included on the list provided for by the Ramsar Convention of 2 February 1971 shall be subject to regulation, and, where required, acts therein that would affect the balance of these ecosystems or that might affect their biodiversity shall be prohibited. By this is meant in particular water uses that lead to modifying its level and the spreading of chemical substances for any purpose whatsoever, in particular agricultural pesticides, or the discharge of liquid refuse or toxic substances, or the drainage of wastewater, and the accumulation of filth or domestic or industrial waste.

2 - Where need requires, the regulation or prohibition may extend to acts realised or anticipated outside the scope of the protected area or the wetland.

3 - The Ministry of Environment shall draw up a plan for the wetlands of international importance included on the list provided for by the Ramsar Convention.

Fourth: Financial cultural heritage:

1 - Natural environmental sites and landscapes that represent, from the aesthetic and cultural standpoint, a special interest may be the object of special protection, including the regulation of activities and equipment that may cause damage to them or the prohibition thereof where the matter so requires.

2 - The protection measures referred to above shall be taken by joint decisions issued by the Minister and the Ministers of Environment and Culture.

3 - The protection measures referred to shall apply to aquatic areas and areas located underwater which are of archaeological interest.

Fifth: Protection of coastal gushing waters:

1 - The sources of fresh gushing spring water along the Lebanese coast shall be determined pursuant to a decree upon the proposal of the Minister.

2 - These springs shall be subject to the scope of protection set out in the preceding paragraphs, and to special protection for which immediate protection zones are determined within which the carrying out of certain activities, in particular fishing, navigation and any underwater activities or works, is prohibited.

3 - The conditions of application of this Article as well as the particulars of allocating the gushing water to supply the population or for other uses shall be determined pursuant to a decree upon the proposal of the Minister and the Minister of Environment.

General provisions:

Subject to the conditions and provisions of sustainable water management, the Minister shall take the appropriate precautionary measures to limit floods and the damage resulting therefrom, in the areas exposed to the risks of floods and torrents and specified in the General Water Master Plan.

Easements of public utility:

1 - In the areas where flood risks prevail, and specified in the General Water Master Plan, the following shall be determined by a decree adopted upon the proposal of the Minister and the Ministers of (Public Works and Transport, Environment and Agriculture):

a - The geographical areas in which all constructions, works, arrangements or actions may be prohibited. And, where necessary, subjecting the actions that may be practised without exposing the population to danger, to specific rules.

b - The geographical areas in which constructions, works, arrangements or activities that may increase flood risks or their harmful repercussions may be regulated, and where necessary prohibited.

2 - The works required by these provisions or rules shall be borne by the owners, operators or beneficiaries.

3 - The restrictions relating to land use and resulting from the provisions of this Article shall constitute easements of public utility.

Principles:

1 - In the water-deficit areas specified in the General Water Master Plan, the Ministry must put into effect the required administrative measures, which ensure the regulation and rationalisation of water use, while maintaining, if possible, a sufficient rate in watercourses to ensure the balance of the ecosystem.

2 - Meeting domestic water needs shall be considered a priority for the population and then irrigation needs, in the water-deficit areas specified in the General Water Master Plan.

3 - Non-conventional water may be used to cover the deficit provided that it conforms to health standards.

On Preventive Measures:

1 - The Minister shall take, by decision, based on the General Master Plan for Water or upon the proposal of the Public Water Investment Establishments, the necessary measures to ensure sustainable water management.

2 - Upon verification of the existence of a water deficit, the Minister may, by decision, subject certain categories of water uses to specific measures which may include the temporary suspension of acquired rights to water or the reduction of the quantities of water that are the subject of such rights.

3 - The measures taken shall be proportionate to the crisis situation and shall determine:

a - The conditions for meeting priority services.

b - The uses subject to prohibition and those subject to rules, as well as the time limits and details for applying such prohibition and such rules.

c - The procedures for distributing water to and among beneficiaries.

d - Where necessary, the conditions for transferring water between basins.

4 - In exceptional cases, special measures may be imposed by decree upon the proposal of the Minister.

Relevant Laws:

Acts and offences arising from the violation of the provisions of this Law shall be subject to the following legal provisions:

- The penalties set forth in the text of this Law, in particular Articles 90 to 97 thereof.

- Articles 58 to 60 of Decision No. 320 dated 26 May 1926.

- Article 23 of Decision No. 144 dated 10 June 1925.

- Articles 74 to 749 of the Penal Code relating to offences concerning the water regime.

- The Law promulgated by Decree No. 8735 dated 23 August 1974 relating to public hygiene.

- Law No. 64 promulgated on 12 August 1988 relating to the preservation of the environment against pollution from toxic, harmful and hazardous waste.

- Law No. 623 promulgated on 23 April 1997 relating to increasing penalties for infringements upon electrical, telephone and water networks.

- Law No. 444 dated 29 July 2002 relating to the protection of the environment, in particular Title Six thereof.

- Law No. 80 promulgated on 18/10/2018 "Integrated Solid Waste Management Law".

Contraventions:

1 - Any person who withdraws water in violation of the obligation to obtain the licence provided for under the provisions of Article 36 of this Law shall be punished by imprisonment from one day to 10 days, and by a fine ranging between one and a half times the minimum wage and 22 times the minimum wage, or by either of these two penalties.

The same penalties shall apply to any person who constructs, modifies or operates a facility or carries out works or activities therein without obtaining a permit for the works.

2 - Any person who erects a facility or installations, carries out works or practises an activity without complying with the conditions specified in the licence document shall be punished by a fine ranging between one and a half times the minimum wage and 15 times the minimum wage.

Misdemeanours:

1 - Any person who intentionally or unintentionally dumps, discharges, throws or pours a substance or substances that harm surface or underground waters or seawater, or throws and unloads or leaves waste of whatever nature in surface or underground waters or in seawater within the limits of the territorial waters of the Lebanese State, shall be punished by imprisonment from ten days to three years, and by a fine ranging between 4 times the minimum wage and 220 times the minimum wage, or by either of these two penalties.

2 - These penalties shall apply in the event that these acts are committed on river banks or on the seashore.

3 - The penalties provided for above shall be aggravated in the event that these acts cause harm to public health or to flora, fishery and fauna resources, or lead to serious modifications in the normal water recharge regime, or to a restriction on the use of swimming areas.

Aggravated Misdemeanours:

Any person who operates a facility or installations, carries out works or practises an activity in violation of a measure involving a prohibition, suspension or destruction ordered by the court pursuant to Article 96 of this Law shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to three years and by a fine ranging between 7 times the minimum wage and 300 times the minimum wage, or by either of these two penalties.

Recidivism:

In the event of recidivism, the penalties relating to the offences provided for in Articles 90, 91 and 92 of this Law shall be doubled.

On the Ascertainment of Offences and Procedures for Prosecution:

1 - The employees of the Ministry and the Public Water Exploitation Establishments, each within its scope, shall be granted the powers of the Judicial Police with respect to recording the offences arising from the application of this Law and its implementing decrees.

For this purpose, they may perform the following:

- Enter the perimeter and buildings of the suspected installations, facilities, exploitations, and establishments.

- Inspect all installations or facilities, machinery, and warehouses.

- Obtain all documents and information relating to the relevant installations and activities.

- Take samples and take the necessary protective measures.

Furthermore, when needed and in order to perform their duties. They shall have the right to seek the assistance, within access, of the security forces, under the supervision of the competent Public Prosecution.

2 - Without prejudice to the provisions of Article 11 bis of the Code of Criminal Procedure relating to the Environmental Public Prosecution, the reports of offences drawn up by the employees of the Ministry and the Public Water Exploitation Establishments may be referred immediately to the competent Criminal Single Judge, who shall be seized of the public action pursuant thereto to rule in accordance with the ordinary procedures, and the judge may, upon referral, take one or some of the measures provided for in Article 95 of this Law.

3 - Where necessary, the procedures for the application of this Article shall be determined by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister and the Minister of Justice.

Penal Measures:

In addition to the penal sanctions and fines adjudicated, the court shall, where it appears that the damage resulting from the acts and offences committed leads to harming human health or aquatic ecosystems or harming water in quantity or quality, rule to:

1 - Suspend operations, activities, or works.

2 - Halt operations or prohibit the use of installations or facilities.

3 - Remove the installations or facilities and/or confiscate them.

4 - Impose the rehabilitation of the aquatic environment and/or the ecosystem.

5 - Take all measures aimed at removing the damage and preventing its aggravation.

On Expedited Execution:

An appeal shall not stay the execution of the appealed judgment.

The judgment of first instance may be executed prior to the expiry of the time limit for appeal and prior to its adjudication when appealed, unless the court decides otherwise within a time limit of ten days from the date of the appeal, pursuant to a thoroughly reasoned decision in which it sets out the factual and legal grounds upon which it relied to issue its decision.

Non-conflict between criminal prosecution and administrative prosecution:

The application of penal provisions shall not preclude the competent administrative authorities from exercising the power to take decisions or implement the measures provided for in Article 38 of this Law.

Follow-up of the water policy:

The Ministry, in coordination with the National Water Authority, shall undertake the follow-up of the water policy.

Collection of information:

The Ministry shall undertake the collection and documentation of all information and data available with the public and private sectors, international organisations, associations and non-governmental organisations operating in the field of water protection, relating to aquatic ecosystems and the management of public utilities entrusted with the management of drinking water services and supplies, the wastewater network, the rainwater network and irrigation.

Informing citizens:

1 - In order to enable citizens to exercise their rights and fulfil their obligations and to ensure the sustainable management of resources and aquatic ecosystems, the Ministry and the public water investment establishments shall regularly publish all information relating to the quality of drinking and irrigation water supplied to consumers.

2 - Publication shall take place via the website of the Ministry and of the concerned water establishments and by any other means.

3 - In areas exposed to the risks mentioned in Title Seven of this Law, the competent authorities shall place at the disposal of citizens the information relating to the prevention and management of such risks.

Training on the Law and the sustainable management of water:

1 - The Ministry shall undertake the task of informing and training working civil servants and employees on the application of this Law and the sustainable management of water. The training programmes for the sustainable management of water shall include levels proportionate to the levels of education in its various stages.

2 - The Ministries of (Environment, Education and Information), the public water investment establishments, environmental protection associations and the private sector shall participate in educating citizens on the concept of the right to water and water culture.

Implementing decrees:

The implementing decrees mentioned in this Law shall be issued upon the proposal of the Minister.

The penalties mentioned in this Sub-section shall be increased in accordance with the provisions of Article 257 if the act is committed in one of the cases set forth in the second paragraph of Article 547 and in Articles 548 and 549 of this Law, insofar as applicable to the offence of causing bodily harm.

6- Articles 487, 488 and 489 of the Criminal Code shall be amended to read as follows:

Article 487: Adultery committed by either spouse shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to two years. The partner in adultery shall be sentenced to the same penalty if married, and otherwise to imprisonment from one month to one year.

Save for judicial confession and flagrante delicto misdemeanour, no evidence of proof shall be admitted against the partner other than that which arises from letters and written documents written by him.

The penalty shall be doubled for the offending spouse if the offence of adultery takes place in the matrimonial home.

Article 488: Either spouse shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year if he openly takes a paramour in any place whatsoever. The same penalty shall be imposed on the partner.

Article 489:

- The act of adultery may only be prosecuted upon the complaint of one of the spouses and the complainant taking the capacity of a civil party.

- A partner or an accomplice shall only be prosecuted together with the adulterer.

- A complaint shall not be accepted from a spouse with whose consent the adultery was committed.

- A complaint shall not be accepted after the lapse of three months from the day on which the offence came to the knowledge of the complainant.

7 - a -

Article 4

Article 5 of Law No. 293/2014 (Protection of Women and Other Family Members from Domestic Violence) is amended to read as follows:

Article 5

Article 9 of Law No. 293/2014 (Protection of Women and All Other Family Members from Domestic Violence) shall be amended to read as follows:

Article 9

Upon receiving complaints and reports, and after consulting the Advocate General assigned to look into domestic violence cases and under his supervision, the Judicial Police shall:

- Hear the witnesses to domestic violence, including minor children, in the presence of the social delegate provided for in Article 34 of Law 422 dated 6/6/2002.

Article 11 of Law No. 293/2014 (Protection of Women and Other Family Members from Domestic Violence) is amended to read as follows:

Article 11

The Advocate General assigned to receive complaints relating to domestic violence may, prior to the issuance of a protection order by the competent authority, instruct the Judicial Police, under his supervision, to take one or more of the following measures:

a- Obtain an undertaking from the respondent to refrain from harassing the victim and the other persons enumerated in Article 12 of this Law or inciting the harassment thereof, under penalty of applying item (1) or (2) of paragraph (b) of this Article.

b - In the event of danger to the said persons:

3- Transfer the victim and the other persons enumerated in Article 12, if they so wish, to a safe place at the expense of the respondent according to his means.

c - If the violence results in conditions requiring medical or hospital treatment, the victims of violence shall be transferred to the hospital provided that the respondent advances the expenses of treatment.

Notwithstanding Article 999 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the decision to imprison the respondent who refrains from advancing the aforementioned expenses shall be issued by the Public Prosecution.

Article 12 of Law No. 293/2014 (Protection of Women and Other Family Members from Domestic Violence) is amended to read as follows:

Article 12

A protection order is a temporary measure issued by the competent judicial authority in accordance with the provisions of this Law on the occasion of examining cases of domestic violence.

Article 13 of Law No. 293/2014 (Protection of Women and Other Family Members from Domestic Violence) shall be amended to read as follows:

Article 13

The decision issued by the judge of urgent matters shall be subject to challenge in accordance with the procedures prescribed for ex parte decisions in the Code of Civil Procedure.

Article 14 of Law No. 293/2014 (Protection of Women and Other Family Members from Domestic Violence) shall be amended to read as follows:

Article 14

A protection order shall include obliging the respondent to abide by one or more of the following measures:

1- Prohibiting interference with the victim and the other persons enumerated in Article 12 of this Law, or incitement to interfere with them.

2- Non-interference with the continued occupancy of the family home by the victim and the persons residing with her who are covered by the protection.

3- Removing the perpetrator of the violence from the home, temporarily and for a period determined by the competent authority, upon sensing any danger to the victim.

4- Moving the victim and those residing with her who are covered by the protection, upon sensing any actual danger to them that may result from their continued occupancy of the family home, to safe and suitable temporary accommodation.

In the event that the victim is moved from the home, her children who are aged thirteen years and under shall automatically be moved with her, as well as the other children and residents if they are exposed to danger.

The respondent shall, according to his capacity, advance the accommodation expenses.

5- Advancing a sum, according to the capacity of the respondent, for food, clothing and education, for those towards whom he is under an obligation.

6- Advancing a sum, according to the capacity of the respondent, on account of the expenses necessary for the medical or hospital treatment of the victim and the other persons enumerated in Article 12 of this Law, if the violence committed results in that which necessitates such treatment.

7- Refraining from causing damage to any of the private property of the victim and of the persons covered by the protection order.

8- Refraining from causing damage to the household furniture and joint movable property, and prohibiting the disposal thereof.

9- Enabling the victim, or whomever she authorises in the event of leaving the home, to enter it to take her personal property pursuant to a receipt record.

In every temporary advance, the victim or the respondent shall retain the right to apply to the competent courts to obtain the appropriate judgment in accordance with the rules in force before them.

The enforcement of the maintenance judgment issued by the competent courts shall suspend the advance decided in the protection order.

Sexual harassment is any repeated improper conduct that is out of the ordinary, unwelcome by the victim, and of a sexual connotation, which constitutes a violation of the body, privacy, or feelings, perpetrated against the victim wherever she or he may be present, through sexual or pornographic words, acts, gestures, insinuations, or hints, and by whatever means the harassment is carried out, including electronic means.

Every act or endeavour, even if not repeated, that uses any kind of psychological, moral, material, or racial pressure actually aimed at obtaining a benefit of a sexual nature from which the perpetrator or a third party benefits shall also be deemed sexual harassment.

A - Whoever commits the offence of sexual harassment shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to one year and by a fine ranging between three times and ten times the official minimum wage, or by either of these two penalties.

B - Punishment shall be imprisonment from six months to two years and a fine from ten times to twenty times the official minimum wage, or either of these two penalties:

1- If the offence of harassment occurs within the framework of a relationship of subordination or an employment relationship.

2- If the harassment takes place in one of the public or military administrations, public institutions, municipalities, universities, schools, nurseries, institutes, clubs, or means of transport.

3- If the harasser is a public official in accordance with the definition provided for in Article 350 of the Criminal Code, and abuses the authority he enjoys by virtue of the duties entrusted to him, or in the course of performing the function or by reason thereof.

C - Punishment shall be imprisonment from two years to four years and a fine ranging from thirty to fifty times the official minimum wage in the following cases:

1- If the offence is committed against a juvenile, a person with additional needs, or a person who is unable to defend himself due to his physical or psychological health condition.

2- If the offender is a person who holds material, moral, functional, or educational authority over the victim.

3- If the act of harassment is committed by two or more persons.

4- If the offender uses severe psychological, moral, or material pressure in committing the offence to obtain a benefit of a sexual nature.

In the event of recidivism or repetition, the penalties of imprisonment and fine shall be doubled in both their minimum and maximum limits in all the cases mentioned above, and both penalties of imprisonment and fine shall be imposed together in the cases provided for in paragraphs (B) and (C) of this Article.

Article 17 of Law No. 293/2014 (Protection of Women and Other Family Members from Domestic Violence) shall be amended to read as follows:

Article 17

A protection order issued by the competent judiciary shall be enforceable forthwith upon its original.

The judge of urgent matters may seek the assistance of the public force to enforce the protection order.

The protection order shall be enforced through the Family Public Prosecution in accordance with Article 11 of this Law.

Each of the victim, the other beneficiaries of the protection order, and the respondent or defendant may request the judicial authority that issued the order to revoke or amend it upon the emergence of new circumstances.

The review mechanism provided for in Article 13 of this Law shall apply to the decision revoking or amending the order.

Article 18 of Law No. 293/2014 (Protection of Women and Other Family Members from Domestic Violence) shall be amended to read as follows:

Article 18

Whoever violates a protection order shall be punished by imprisonment for up to one year and by a fine not exceeding twice the minimum wage, or by either of these two penalties.

If the violation is accompanied by the use of violence, the offender shall be punished by imprisonment for up to one year and by a fine not exceeding four times the minimum wage.

The penalty shall be doubled in the event of recidivism.

Article 21 of Law No. 293/2014 (Protection of Women and Other Family Members from Domestic Violence) shall be amended to read as follows:

Article 21

A special account shall be established at the Ministry of Social Affairs to assist victims of domestic violence, provide them with care, and provide means conducive to reducing and preventing crimes of domestic violence and rehabilitating their perpetrators.

This account shall be funded by:

- Donations.

- Funds resulting from fines imposed pursuant to this Law.

The regulations governing the account shall be determined by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Social Affairs.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

A special fund shall be established within the Ministry of Social Affairs, tasked with assisting victims of sexual harassment and ensuring care for them so as to guarantee their rehabilitation and reintegration into society, and providing the means conducive to curbing and preventing these offences and rehabilitating their perpetrators.

The fund shall be financed by:

1 - Contributions of the State, and an appropriation shall be allocated for this purpose in the annual general budget of the Ministry of Social Affairs.

2 - Donations.

3 - Ten per cent (10 %) of the value of the fines provided for in Article Two of this Law, which shall be added by operation of law to the fine imposed by judgment and paid by the convicted person for the benefit of the fund, provided that the time limit for its payment is determined by the judge hearing the case, and it shall be collected in accordance with Article 63 et seq. of Law 44/2008, provided that the administration of the fund replaces the tax administration with regard to pursuing its collection.

The bylaws of the fund shall be determined by a regulatory decision issued by the Minister of Social Affairs.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Prosecution shall depend on a complaint by the aggrieved party, with the exception of the following cases:

1 - Where the victim is a person with additional needs or is unable to defend himself due to his physical or psychological health condition.

2 - Where the offence is committed against a juvenile.

3 - Where the offence is committed by two or more persons.

4 - Where the harasser uses severe material, psychological, moral or racial pressure on the victim in order to obtain a benefit of a sexual nature.

5 - Where the offence is committed by a person who holds material, moral or functional authority.

In the event of recidivism, sexual harassment shall be considered an infamous offence.

In all cases, prosecution for the crime of sexual harassment shall not require obtaining any prior authorisation.

When hearing the victim, her psychological state must be taken into consideration and all necessary measures must be taken to ensure her protection and the protection of witnesses, at all stages of the preliminary investigation, the initial investigation and the trial.

Any discrimination or prejudice to rights enshrined by law to which a victim who has refused to submit to acts of harassment is subjected, whether directly or indirectly, in particular with regard to wages, promotion, transfer, the renewal of her employment contract or the imposition of disciplinary sanctions against her, shall be prohibited.

Any discrimination or prejudice to rights enshrined by law to which a person who has reported harassment in cases where the public action is initiated without a complaint by the aggrieved party, or who has given testimony in any case, is subjected, or the imposition of disciplinary sanctions against her, shall likewise be prohibited.

Any person who violates the provisions of this Article shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to six months and by a fine ranging between five times and twenty times the official minimum wage, or by either of these two penalties.

Criminal prosecutions shall not preclude the imposition of disciplinary sanctions, including dismissal from service.

The initiation of disciplinary prosecution shall not be suspended pending criminal prosecution, and the victim shall always retain the right to compensation for the psychological, moral or material pain suffered by him.

Sole Article:

- The proposed law aimed at the recovery of funds derived from corruption offences, as amended by the Joint Parliamentary Committees and the Chamber of Deputies, has been approved.

- This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

This Law governs all operations for the recovery of funds of whatever nature derived from corruption offences, whether found within Lebanese territory or abroad, and whether they have remained in the ownership or possession of the perpetrator of the offence or have been transferred to the ownership or possession of a third party.

The provisions of this Law shall apply on the basis of the United Nations Convention against Corruption adopted by Resolution No. 58/4 issued by the General Assembly of the United Nations, to which Lebanon acceded pursuant to Law No. 33/2008, in particular Article 51 of the said Convention, and in harmony with the Law on Fighting Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing No. 44/2015, the Law on Combating Corruption in the Public Sector and Creating the National Anti-Corruption Commission No. 175/2020, and Law No. 189/2020 which amended the Illicit Enrichment Law No. 154/1999.

For the purposes of this Law, the following words and expressions shall have the meanings assigned to them below:
