1- Offences: the offences of corruption provided for in the Law on Combating Corruption in the Public Sector and Establishing the National Anti-Corruption Commission No. 175/2020, and the offences of money laundering, including those resulting from offences of corruption, and the offences provided for in the Law on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing No. 318/2001 and its amendments, in particular Law No. 44/2015; the offence of money laundering includes the acquisition, possession or use of funds, knowing at the time of their receipt that they are criminal proceeds.

2- Funds: all kinds of financial or non-material, tangible or intangible, movable or immovable assets, however acquired, and legal documents or instruments in any form, including electronic or digital, evidencing title to, or an interest in, such assets. This includes, by way of example and without limitation, economic resources, financial assets and all kinds of property.

3- Recovery: the entirety of the acts of tracing of funds, freezing, attachment, confiscation, repatriation and their equivalents, which enable the State to identify and reclaim funds, whether located in Lebanon or abroad, derived directly or indirectly from the offences, in addition to the rights attached to such funds and the income and profits resulting therefrom or on the occasion thereof, as the case may be.

4- Tracing of funds: the examination of information and documents, and the extraction, organisation and analysis of data indicating the movement of funds derived from the offences, including recourse to international cooperation where necessary, with a view to determining the nature and type of these funds, estimating their value, and the path and manner of transfer of their ownership among the legal and/or natural persons concerned, as the case may be, whether in Lebanon and/or abroad, starting from the moment the funds were derived by reason of those offences and ending at their final place of location.

5 - Repatriation: the final act in the series of acts of recovery of funds derived from the offences and located outside the jurisdiction of the Lebanese State, meaning the return to Lebanon of such funds by a foreign State to which the funds were smuggled, whether by means of a judicial judgment, a bilateral or multilateral agreement, or any other legally available means.

There shall be established within the National Anti-Corruption Commission provided for in Law No. 175/2020 the "Department for the Recovery of Funds Derived from Corruption Offences", hereinafter referred to as the "Department", which shall undertake the following duties:

1 - Coordinating with all judicial, oversight, and security agencies, as well as with the Investigation Commission provided for in Law No. 44/2015, regarding prosecutions, reports, and claims relating to corruption offences in the part thereof relating to the recovery of funds derived from corruption offences, in all that does not conflict with the jurisdictions reserved to the aforementioned agencies pursuant to the laws in force.

2 - Preparing strategies and plans concerning fund recovery operations in general across all their administrative and judicial stages, and any other related matter referred to it in particular.

3 - Following up on fund recovery operations with the relevant administrative and judicial authorities within the limits permitted by the laws and regulations of those authorities, with the right of the Department to obtain information connected to the files of the recovery of funds derived from corruption, and to provide the required information, and it shall do so until the Fund established pursuant to this Law assumes the management of those funds.

4 - Proposing negotiation strategies and mechanisms, in particular to the Cases Authority at the Ministry of Justice and the National Anti-Corruption Commission, concerning settlements, conciliations, and agreements that would expedite and render effective the efforts to recover funds without necessarily resorting to litigation, and proposing the procedures conducive thereto.

5 - Identifying the obstacles facing the recovery of funds, and recommending to the concerned authorities the necessary legislative and regulatory texts and legal and administrative measures to address them.

6 - Seeking the assistance, where necessary, of natural or legal persons, Lebanese or foreign, whom it deems appropriate from among persons of competence and expertise, on the basis of a documented curriculum vitae.

The "Fund Recovery Department" shall be composed of:

* The President of the National Anti-Corruption Commission (as President) and two members of the Commission selected pursuant to the rules of procedure referred to in Law No. 175/2020.

The "Fund Recovery Department" may invite to its meetings representatives of the Court of Accounts, the Central Inspection, and the security agencies, as well as any representative of other concerned authorities whose attendance it deems beneficial.

The deliberations of the "Asset Recovery Department" shall be confidential, and each of its members and the members of its secretariat, as well as anyone whose assistance is sought and/or who is invited to attend the meetings, shall maintain professional secrecy in respect of all information and documents that come to their knowledge in the course of performing their duties pursuant to this Law.

Anyone who violates the provisions of this Article shall be punished by imprisonment from two months to two years and by a fine of 10 to 20 times the minimum wage, without prejudice to the application of disciplinary penalties and disciplinary measures provided for in the laws in force.

The "Asset Recovery Department" may request from the Administration, in accordance with the definition provided for in the Right of Access to Information Law No. 28/2017, such information and documents in its possession as it requires, and the Administration shall supply it therewith within a period of fifteen days from the date of submission of the request, with the possibility of extending this period once only, and for a duration not exceeding fifteen days, if necessary, without being entitled to invoke professional secrecy against the Committee and without compliance with the Committee's requests entailing any liability for those entrusted with such secrecy.

The "Asset Recovery Department" shall hold a public session, every three months at most, with plaintiffs and whistleblowers in corruption offences and representatives of associations concerned with combating offences in order to inform them of the maximum possible amount of information regarding the files on which it is working concerning the work of the Committee, and to consult with them on ways to enhance cooperation regarding the application of this Law, with the exception of those whistleblowers who do not wish to do so.

The "Asset Recovery Department" shall prepare, during the month of January of each year, a detailed annual report on its activities in accordance with the provisions of the Right of Access to Information Law No. 28/2017, and the report shall be published on the website of the National Anti-Corruption Commission.

There shall be established pursuant to this Law the "National Fund for the Management and Investment of Assets Pending Recovery or Recovered", which shall enjoy legal personality and financial and administrative autonomy, and shall be linked to the National Anti-Corruption Commission in respect of the special budget of the Fund for the management of funds derived from offences, and shall hereinafter be referred to as the "National Fund".

The National Fund shall enjoy all powers to conclude contracts and take the necessary measures of all kinds with any party whatsoever, whether in the public or private sector, in Lebanon or abroad, with a view to effectively performing the mission entrusted to it under this Law. It may receive grants or assistance from domestic or foreign parties, subject to the publication and disclosure of the identity of the donors, and while avoiding any conflict of interest or impact on the course of its work.

The National Fund shall exercise, in respect of shares and participations in companies that are under recovery or have been recovered, the powers of holding companies in accordance with the provisions of Legislative Decree No. 45/1983 and its amendments.

All operations of management, investment and transfer of ownership of funds under recovery and recovered funds carried out by the National Fund, in addition to the rights attached to such funds and the revenues and profits resulting therefrom or on the occasion thereof, as the case may be, shall be exempted from all due fees and taxes.

The National Fund shall submit its annual report to the Chamber of Deputies, and its operations shall be subject to the ex-post audit of the Court of Accounts. The Minister of Finance shall also appoint, upon the recommendation of the National Anti-Corruption Commission, and pursuant to the provisions of Article 73 of Law No. 326/2001, an internationally recognised independent external auditor to audit the accounts of the National Fund.

The National Fund and its governance system, including the conditions for membership of the Board of Directors, the manner of nominating and appointing its members, their allocations, its management, the financial rules, the scope of investments, prohibitions, accountability, and transparency, shall be regulated in consistency with the “Santiago Principles” concerning sovereign wealth funds, pursuant to a decree based on a decision taken in the Council of Ministers, upon the proposal of the Ministers of Finance and Justice, and following the submission of the National Anti-Corruption Commission upon its establishment, within a period not exceeding six months from the date of publication of this Law.

The Ministry of Justice shall establish detailed regulations and procedures allowing the sending, receipt, and execution of requests for mutual international judicial assistance as expeditiously as possible and within the widest possible scope, after ranking requests for mutual legal assistance by priority, and with due regard to the principle of reciprocity and dual criminality, in all matters relating to investigations connected with corruption offences and the offences provided for in Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 318/2001 and its amendments, in particular Law No. 44/2015, in a manner that does not conflict with the international conventions concluded by Lebanon.

The details of the implementation of this Law shall be determined, where necessary, by decrees taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Finance and Justice following the submission of the National Anti-Corruption Commission upon its establishment.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Definitions:

Each of the expressions and terms mentioned below shall have the meaning corresponding thereto

1- Nursing: is the provision of nursing care based on sound medical or health assessment in order to enable individuals, families and groups to improve, promote and preserve their health, and nursing also includes the alleviation of pain and assistance in the prevention of disease and injuries in order to adapt to health problems and reach the best possible quality of life regardless of the type of disease or disability; and this is under the supervision of the attending physician and in coordination with the health team which comprises members from the various health professions.

2- The Health Team: the team which comprises members from the various health professions that work together and cooperate in order to provide health care and furnish health services to individuals, families and communities and work alongside patients.

All members of the health team must practise their profession on the basis of the utmost knowledge they have acquired through their education in order to provide high-quality care to patients at the appropriate time and in various circumstances.

3- The Medical Team: the physicians concerned with treating the patients.

Workers in the field of nursing shall be divided into four categories:

1- First Category: the Specialist Nurse.

2- Second Category: the Nurse.

3- Third Category: the Technical Nurse.

4- Fourth Category: the Assistant Nurse.

The Specialist Nurse is one who has pursued his academic attainment above the university Bachelor's degree in Nursing Sciences, and has subsequently obtained, at least, a Specialist Master's degree in these Nursing Sciences, issued by a university, faculty or university institute recognised by the Lebanese State or the equivalent of this degree, and has obtained a permit to practise the profession in the capacity of a specialist nurse from the Ministry of Public Health and possesses the competencies and skills to be determined in the implementing decrees of this Law.

A specialist nurse may play a planning and leadership role in the field of nursing, in cooperation and partnership with the medical, health and administrative team in the institution concerned.

In addition to the duties of a nurse, the duties of a specialist nurse shall include, within the scope of his specialisation,

the following:

a - Providing advanced and specialised nursing care, which consists of high-quality nursing care requiring advanced clinical competencies within the scope of his specialisation.

b - Contributing to the development of academic and professional curricula adopted in higher education institutions at their request, and to the implementation of the continuing education law in accordance with the programmes adopted by the Order of Nurses in this regard.

c - Conducting scientific studies and research within the framework of developing the profession and its practice, and in particular within the scope of the plans and programmes approved by the Order of Nurses.

d-  Rendering an opinion to the institution for which he works and at its request, or by way of proposal, on the rules and manner of providing nursing services.

A nurse is a person who has completed the study of the basic university programme in nursing sciences for a period of not less than three years, holds a university degree from a university, faculty, university institute or university technical institute recognised by the Lebanese State, or its equivalent, has obtained a licence to practise the profession as a nurse from the Ministry of Public Health, and possesses the competencies provided for in the implementation decrees of this Law.
A nurse shall provide nursing care in participation and coordination with the health team and the attending physician in order to meet the needs of individuals, families and groups.

An assistant nurse is a person who holds a Technical Baccalaureate diploma in nursing care issued by the Directorate General of Vocational and Technical Education, or its equivalent, and holds a licence to practise the profession of assistant nurse from the Ministry of Public Health. He shall possess the competencies and skills provided for in the implementing decrees.

The assistant nurse shall provide nursing care under the supervision of the specialist nurse, the nurse or the technical nurse, and within the nursing work team that ensures health care according to the needs of individuals, families and communities.

The duties of the assistant nurse shall include the following:

Carrying out the nursing activities assigned to him by the specialist nurse, the nurse or the technical nurse.

Contributing to the protection of individuals, families and communities from infection and health-related risks.

Communicating effectively within his field of work with individuals, families, communities and the health team.

Documenting information accurately, within the framework of his work.

Using modern technologies accurately and effectively in providing care, under the supervision of the specialist nurse, the nurse or the technical nurse.

The duties of the nurse cover:

Providing nursing care within the framework of the nursing work mechanism.

Securing the needs of the individuals, families and communities with whose care he is entrusted at the physical, psychological and social levels.

Providing guidance and health education to individuals, families and communities in accordance with their health needs.

Documenting information accurately, according to the laws in force.

Participating and contributing, in coordination with the members of the medical and health team, in formulating, developing and implementing public health programmes.

Using resources effectively.

Determining the nursing activities,

which may be assigned, when needed, to workers in the health team, and supervising their application.

Participating in nursing research aimed at developing the profession by collecting and publishing information and applying the results of scientific research in nursing care.

Enhancing means of communication with individuals, families and communities and with the health team.

Training and following up on new nurses, including students and trainees, within the scope of their duties.

The technical nurse is one who has completed a vocational education programme in the field of nursing with a study period of not less than three years after the General Secondary Certificate or the Technical Baccalaureate, and has obtained a vocational certificate (Technical Licence) issued by the Directorate General of Vocational and Technical Education or its equivalent.

And has obtained a permit to practise the profession in the capacity of technical nurse from the Ministry of Public Health, and enjoys the competencies provided for in the implementing decrees.
The technical nurse provides nursing care under the supervision of the physician and in coordination with the nurse and the health team.

The duties of the technical nurse cover:

Participating with the nurse and the health team in executing the nursing duties entrusted to the nursing team.

Providing nursing care within the framework of the nursing work mechanism.

Securing the needs of the individuals, families and communities with whose care he is entrusted at the physical, psychological and social levels.

Using appropriate communication skills with individuals, families and communities and with the health team.

Using resources effectively.

Documenting information accurately, according to the laws in force.

Assigning nursing activities to workers in the nursing team according to need.

1 - Technical Licence (LT): A duration of three academic years shall be adopted after the student in public or private institutes passes the official examination at the end of the study, in addition to a national examination (professional colloquium) for students of private institutes.

2 - Technical Baccalaureate (BT): A duration of three academic years shall be adopted after obtaining the official Intermediate Certificate or the Vocational Brevet, and passing the official examination conducted by the Directorate of Vocational and Technical Education.

3 - Vocational Brevet: A duration of nine academic months shall be adopted after obtaining the Lebanese Intermediate Certificate, and passing the official examination conducted by the Directorate of Vocational and Technical Education. Its holder shall obtain a permit to practise the profession in the capacity of a health auxiliary in accordance with the job description, provided that he is deemed as such from the effective date of this Law.

Permits previously granted by the Ministry of Public Health to practise the nursing profession with the title of assistant nurse on the basis of a certificate other than those specified in this Law shall remain valid, and the person concerned shall, with effect from its effective date, be deemed to be practising this profession in his capacity as a health auxiliary.

Students holding the Technical Licence certificate shall be entitled to pursue their university studies at various universities after completing a special programme determined by the Ministry of Education in cooperation with the Order of Nurses regarding the minimum subjects required to be acquired by them, with the holding of the colloquium examination after obtaining the university degree from private universities.

No person shall have the right to practise the nursing profession within Lebanese territory, nor to assume the title of specialist nurse, nurse, technical nurse, or assistant nurse except after obtaining a permit to practise the profession from the Ministry of Public Health, and registering compulsorily with the Order of Female and Male Nurses in Lebanon.

To obtain a permit to practise the profession, the following conditions must be fulfilled:

1 - That he be Lebanese and have attained the age of eighteen years.

2 - That he hold a certificate in nursing from Lebanon or from abroad after its equivalence has been granted in accordance with due process.

3 - That he not have been convicted of a felony or a dishonourable misdemeanour, and that he enjoy the health, mental, and moral qualities necessary to practise his profession.

4 - That the nurse have successfully passed the Colloquium examination.

5 - That the specialist nurse have been granted the title by the Nursing Specialities Committee after holding a permit to practise the profession of nurse.

The said Committee shall be formed of representatives of the universities that teach the nursing profession, of the Order of Nurses, and from among the employees of the Ministry of Health by a decision of the Minister of Health.

6 - That the technical nurse or the assistant nurse have successfully passed the official examination conducted by the Directorate General of Vocational and Technical Education, in addition to the vocational Colloquium examination for students of private institutes.

7 - That the assistant nurse have successfully passed the official examination conducted by the Directorate General of Vocational and Technical Education.

A non-Lebanese nurse who is licensed to practise the profession in his country may practise the profession in Lebanon in the following cases:

1 - That he be seconded by an international body, organisation, mission or institution licensed to operate in Lebanon and within the scope of the mission entrusted to him.

2 - That he be a member of the teaching bodies at nursing schools and universities and a signatory to a fixed-term employment contract.

3 - Non-Lebanese female and male nurses must obtain a permit to practise the profession from the Ministry of Public Health and register with the Order of Female and Male Nurses.

The Ministry of Health may authorise a Palestinian residing as a refugee in Lebanon according to the records of the UNRWA organisation, who meets the legally required conditions to practise the nursing profession, to work temporarily for a period of one year at a specified hospital institution after it produces proof of its need for nurses and that no Lebanese has applied to work in this profession despite its announcement of this need through the National Employment Office, provided that these very procedures are adopted each time this permit is renewed with it for a similar period.

The Ministry of Public Health shall suspend or withdraw the permit to practise the profession, on its own initiative or pursuant to a decision by the Disciplinary Council of the Order of Female and Male Nurses, from any specialist nurse, nurse, technical nurse or assistant nurse who loses one of the conditions that must be met for him to practise the profession or in the event of malpractice of the profession or breach of its ethics.

Anyone who practises the nursing profession, in all its categories, in an unlawful manner or bears the title of specialist nurse, nurse, technical nurse or assistant nurse in an unlawful manner shall be subject to the penalties provided for in Article 393 of the Penal Code.
Anyone who wears the nursing insignia determined by the Order in an unlawful manner shall be subject to the penalties provided for in Article 391 and of the Penal Code.

The classification set forth in the present Law for the categories of specialist nurse, nurse, technical nurse or assistant nurse shall take effect immediately upon its issuance, and the licences to practise the nursing profession granted prior to the issuance of this Law shall remain in force.

The details of implementation of this Law shall be determined by virtue of implementing decrees issued after the approval of the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Health.
All previous laws and decrees that conflict with the provisions of this Law are repealed.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Single Article:

- The proposed law relating to public procurement in Lebanon, as amended by the Joint Parliamentary Committees, has been approved.

- This law shall be published in the Official Gazette and shall come into force twelve months after the date of its publication.

Objective and general principles of the law:

This law determines the rules for conducting, executing, and monitoring public procurement, and it is based on the following principles:

1. Applying competitive procedures as a general rule.

2. Providing equal opportunities without discrimination for participating in public procurement.

3. Providing fair, equal, transparent, and accountable treatment to all bidders and contractors.

4. Publicity, integrity, and professionalism of procedures in a manner that activates oversight and accountability.

5. Encouraging local economic development, national employment, and national production on the basis of best value for spending public funds, without prejudice to effectiveness.

Procurement operations shall be subject to the rules of good governance and shall take into consideration the requirements of sustainable development.

The general principles contained in this Article shall be considered matters of public legal order.

Scope of Application:

1. All public procurement operations of supplies, works and services carried out by procuring entities shall be subject to the provisions of this Law, whether the contract is financed from budget or treasury funds, or from internal or external loans, or from grants not restricted by the donor's conditions, with due regard to the provisions of international treaties and agreements concluded with the Lebanese State. No procuring entity may, other than in the cases provided for in this Law, carry out any procurement operation except in accordance with its provisions.

2. A designated procuring entity may carry out procurement operations to meet common needs between itself and other procuring entities, and a designated procuring entity may also carry out procurement operations on behalf of other procuring entities.

3. Where the procurement is mixed, that is, where the procurement operation comprises two or more types of supplies, works and services, the procurement operation shall be subject to the special provisions governing the award of the type of procurement that predominates in the procurement operation.

4. Excluded from the provisions of this Law is procurement aimed at granting any concession or privilege for the exploitation of a resource of the country's natural wealth or a service of public utility or any monopoly, save in respect of the procedures preceding the granting of the privilege or monopoly, where such procedures shall be subject to the general principles provided for in Article One of this Law insofar as they do not conflict with any special provisions set forth in other laws.

5. The provisions of this Law shall apply to partnership contracts between the public and private sectors in all matters that do not conflict with the Law Regulating Partnership between the Public and Private Sectors No. 48 dated 7/9/2017 and its amendments.

6. The provisions of this Law shall apply to procurement operations conducted by the Bank of Lebanon, with the exception of the printing, issuance and transfers of currency.

7. In respect of the excluded cases above, the general principles set forth in the text of Article One of this Law shall apply.

Language:

The Arabic language shall be adopted in the procurement documents and in the decisions of the procuring entity. However, the English and/or French language may be adopted alongside Arabic for all correspondence and for drawing up the technical specifications or the terms of reference.

In the event of discrepancy between the Arabic and the foreign texts, the former shall prevail over the latter.

Currency:

The tender document shall specify the currency of the contract and the method of accounting in contracts in a foreign currency.

Confidentiality:

1. The procuring entity and all those concerned with the procurement process shall maintain the confidentiality of information relating to the protection of the essential security interests of the State, and of information the disclosure of which violates the law, impedes its enforcement, prejudices the legitimate commercial interests of bidders, or impedes fair competition, unless the competent judicial authorities order the disclosure of such information.

2. With the exception of cases where information is provided or published pursuant to the laws in force, the procuring entity shall refrain, in respect of applications for pre-qualification and submitted bids, from disclosing their contents and substance, including professional and technical secrets and those protected by intellectual property laws, the disclosure of which would cause unlawful harm to the bidders, to competing bidders, or to any other person not authorised to have access to this type of information.

3. Confidentiality shall be observed in any discussions, communications, negotiations or dialogues conducted between the procuring entity and any bidder in all matters that do not conflict with the laws in force. No party to any such discussions, communications, negotiations or dialogues may disclose to any other person any technical, financial or other information relating to these discussions, communications, negotiations or dialogues without the consent of the other party, unless the law so provides or the competent courts so order.

Exclusion of the bidder for offering benefits, or due to an unfair competitive advantage, or due to a conflict of interest:

1. The procuring entity shall exclude the bidder from the awarding procedures in either of the following two cases:

a- Where the bidder has committed any violation or act prohibited under the provisions of this Law, or any heinous crime, or one of the crimes covered by the Anti-Corruption Law, in particular the crimes of trading in influence and bribery, if it offers to any current or former official or employee of the procuring entity or of another governmental authority, or grants to him or agrees to grant to him, directly or indirectly, a benefit, employment, or any other thing of value, for the purpose of influencing an act or a decision on the part of the procuring entity or a procedure it follows in connection with the awarding procedures; or

b - If the bidder has an unfair competitive advantage or has a conflict of interest in violation of the provisions of this Law and the laws in force.

2. Every decision taken by the procuring entity to exclude the bidder from the awarding procedures pursuant to this Article, and the reasons for such exclusion, shall be included in the record of procurement proceedings, and the decision shall be communicated to the concerned bidder.

Rules of Conduct:

The Public Procurement Authority shall establish, pursuant to a regulatory decision, a charter of rules of conduct, professional ethics and good citizenship pertaining to public procurement operations, which shall apply to all staff working in procuring entities and to contractors therewith, provided that this charter includes, by way of example and not limitation, the standards stipulated in this Law, in particular the provisions on integrity, transparency and prevention of conflict of interest, in addition to the rules of good governance, impartiality, fairness, knowledge and competence. It must also provide for the regulatory measures applicable to staff and the procedures followed to verify competence, good conduct and the obligation to disclose violations.

Notice of Procurement:

1. The invitation to compete shall be made through the publication of a notice of procurement on the central electronic platform at the Public Procurement Authority and on the website of the procuring entity, if any. The procuring entity may also decide to publish the notice through any other additional means.

2. The duration of the notice shall be determined in accordance with the importance and complexity of the procurement project, provided that it shall in no case be less than twenty-one days prior to the deadline for the submission of bids. The duration of the notice may be reduced to fifteen days when it is practically impossible to apply the general rule, in exceptional circumstances, and after the procuring entity issues a reasoned decision specifying the nature of such circumstances, provided that the reasoning is recorded in the record of procurement proceedings in accordance with Article 9 of this Law.

3. The day of publication of the notice shall not be included in the calculation of the time limit, and if the last day for the submission of bids falls on an official holiday or a day of forced suspension of work, the time limit shall be extended automatically to the first working day following the suspension without the need for prior notice thereof.

Estimated value of the procurement project:

1. Every procuring entity shall update its estimates of the value of the procurement project prior to announcing it, except in exceptional cases where this is impracticable, provided that it sets forth the reasons in a reasoned and clear manner.

2. The procuring entity shall prepare the estimated value of the procurement project on the basis of realistic market prices and price inquiries with other administrations, and after taking into consideration any increase that may result from the application of the optional clauses provided for in the bidding documents (for example, an increase in quantities, incentives, etc...).

3. With respect to framework agreements, the maximum estimated value of the aggregate contracts expected throughout the duration of the agreement shall be taken into consideration.

4. When conducting procurement on the basis of lots, the estimated value of all the lots of which the contract consists shall be calculated.

5. The estimated value of the procurement project shall be determined by the procuring entity upon announcing it or upon commencing the awarding procedures.

6. The procuring entity is prohibited from calculating the estimated value of the procurement project at less or more than its actual value for the purpose of avoiding the application of the provisions of the Law.

7. When calculating the estimated value of the procurement project, all the elements necessary for its execution shall be taken into consideration.

8. The estimated value of the procurement project shall remain confidential before and after the awarding, unless the procuring entity deems otherwise for purposes relating to competition and ensuring the success of the awarding, or in transactions whose prices are manifestly and clearly known, in which case the estimated value shall be announced in due form. In all cases, confidentiality may not be invoked before the Court of Accounts and the oversight bodies.

Splitting of Procurement:

1. The procuring entity may split the procurement into separate lots in the following two cases only:

A - When the nature of the works, goods or services so requires, and where clear justifications exist, such as the diversity and multiplicity of sources of supply or the difference of the lots from one another in a manner that leads to a certain benefit from splitting, provided that the decision is justified and subject to oversight in accordance with the laws in force.

B - When implementing governmental development policies, such as encouraging the participation of small and medium-sized enterprises in public procurement.

2. Procurement may not be split into subdivisions in order to apply special provisions to each part thereof for the purpose of reducing the estimated value of the procurement project or with the intent of evading oversight or the application of the provisions of this Law or other laws and regulations.

Sustainability and Development Policies:

1. Procuring entities shall adopt, where possible, sustainable public procurement in order to direct the purchasing power of the State towards sustainable goods and services with the aim of reducing environmental impact and achieving the economic and social objectives provided for in international agreements and in accordance with national priority, while ensuring a balance between potential benefits and ensuring the achievement of best value for public money spent, and in a manner that allows granting incentives to small and medium-sized enterprises, local production, and national expertise.

2. Awarding shall, whenever possible, be carried out on the basis of lots or groups, provided that the special conditions of tender specify the number of such lots or groups, their nature, the conditions imposed for participating in a lot or group of the award, and the manner of awarding such contract, for the purpose of social and economic benefit. Rules and policies for sustainable public procurement shall be established by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the competent minister or ministers.

Preferential regimes:

1. Notwithstanding any other text, bids comprising goods or services of national origin may be granted a preference at a rate of //10// ten per cent over bids submitted for foreign goods or services. Preference shall be granted to the components of the bid that are of national origin. National goods and services and the conditions that must be met therein in order to benefit from this preference shall be determined in accordance with the rules of origin.

2. It is prohibited to include in bidding documents or prequalification documents provisions that lead to the exclusion of goods manufactured in Lebanon or Lebanese consultancy and intellectual services where they exist with a quality and standard that meet the requirements.

Description of the Subject Matter of the Procurement:

1. The procuring entity shall clearly specify the descriptions of the subject matter of the procurement in the bidding documents and shall set the criteria it will use in evaluating the submitted tenders, including the minimum requirements that the submitted tenders must meet in order to be considered responsive to the required requirements and specifications, and the manner in which those minimum requirements shall be applied.

2. The description of the subject matter of the procurement shall be objective and generic, and the relevant technical and functional characteristics and/or performance-related characteristics shall be specified in that description. The technical specifications and terms of reference shall be specified in accordance with the following standards:

a - In accordance with national or international standards issued by the competent authorities, and technical approvals or official technical specifications relating to the design, calculation, execution, and use of works and products,

and/or

b - On the basis of functional characteristics or performance requirements, where possible.

3. The description of the subject matter of the procurement may include specifications, plans, drawings, designs, requirements, tests and testing methods, packaging, conformity markings or certificates, and symbols and terminology.

4. The description of the subject matter of the procurement shall not refer to a specific trademark, trade name, patent, design, type, specific origin, or specific product, or include a reference to any of the same, except in the case where it is impossible to describe the subject matter of the procurement by another sufficiently precise and intelligible manner to describe the characteristics, provided that it is accompanied by the words "or equivalent".

5. Due regard shall be given to the use of standardised features, requirements, symbols, and terminology, where available, when formulating the description of the subject matter of the procurement to be included in the bidding documents or pre-qualification documents, if any, with respect to the technical and functional characteristics of the subject matter of the procurement and its performance-related characteristics.

6. Where contracting authorities adopt the method of referring to the specifications mentioned in Paragraph 2 (a) of this Article, they may not reject a tender on the grounds that the products and services that are the subject matter of the procurement do not comply with the said specifications where the bidder proves that the tender it submitted meets the requirements specified in the technical specifications by any means whatsoever. For this purpose, it may prepare and submit a technical report from the manufacturer or a certificate of conformity from an accredited body.

7. Where procuring entities adopt the option of setting the specifications on the basis of performance and functional characteristics, they may not reject a tender that conforms to international or national standards if the specifications meet the specified performance and functional characteristics, and the bidder shall have the right to prove to the procuring entities, by any means whatsoever and on the basis of the standards, that the works, products, or services conform to the required performance and the functional characteristics imposed by the procuring entities. For this purpose, it may prepare and submit a technical report from the manufacturer or a certificate of conformity from an accredited body.

8. Whenever possible, specified environmental characteristics shall be included by reference to a recognised eco-label that is accessible to all interested parties.

9. Specifications shall be proportionate to the required need and shall not be set or formulated in a manner that leads to the unlawful exclusion of bidders.

Requests for clarification:

First: Regarding the bidding documents and pre-qualification documents:

1. A bidder shall have the right to submit a written request for clarification regarding the bidding documents or pre-qualification documents within a time limit expiring ten days prior to the date of submission of bids or pre-qualification applications. The procuring entity shall respond within a time limit expiring six days prior to the deadline for the submission of bids or pre-qualification applications. The clarification shall be sent in writing, at the same time, without identifying the issuer of the request, to all bidders to whom the procuring entity has provided the bidding documents.

2. The procuring entity may, where necessary, set a specific appointment for potential bidders to inspect the site.

3. The procuring entity may, at any time prior to the deadline for the submission of bids or pre-qualification applications, and for any reason whatsoever, whether on its own initiative or as a result of a request for clarification submitted by a bidder, amend the bidding documents or pre-qualification documents by issuing an addendum thereto. The amendment shall be sent immediately to all bidders to whom the procuring entity has provided the bidding documents or pre-qualification documents,

and such amendment shall be binding on those bidders and shall be published on the central electronic platform at the Public Procurement Authority and on the website of the procuring entity, if any.

4. If the information published in the bidding documents or pre-qualification documents becomes materially different as a result of a clarification or amendment issued in accordance with this Article, the procuring entity shall ensure the publication of the amended information in the same manner in which the original information was published and in the same place, and shall extend the deadline for the submission of bids or pre-qualification applications as provided for in paragraph 4 of Article 20 of this Law.

5. If the procuring entity holds a meeting for bidders, it shall draw up minutes of that meeting containing the requests for clarification regarding the bidding documents submitted therein, and the responses provided by it to those requests, without identifying the sources of the requests. The minutes shall be notified to all bidders to whom the procuring entity has provided the bidding documents or pre-qualification documents, in order to enable them to prepare their applications for qualification or their bids in light of the information provided.

Second: Information relating to qualifications and bids:

1. The procuring entity may, at any stage of the procurement proceedings, request in writing from a bidder clarifications regarding the information relating to its qualifications or regarding its bids, in order to assist it in verifying the qualifications or examining and evaluating the submitted bids.

2. The procuring entity shall correct any purely arithmetical errors that it discovers during its examination of the submitted bids in accordance with the provisions of the tender specifications, and shall notify the corrections to the concerned bidder immediately.

3. No substantive change in the information relating to qualifications or in the submitted bid may be requested or permitted, including changes aimed at making an unqualified bidder qualified or making a non-responsive bid responsive to the requirements.

4. No negotiations may be conducted between the procuring entity and a bidder regarding the information relating to qualifications or regarding the submitted bids, nor may any change in price be made following a request for clarification from any bidder pursuant to this Article.

5. All correspondence conducted pursuant to this Article shall be included in the record of procurement proceedings in accordance with Article 9 of this Law.

Method and place of submitting prequalification applications and/or bids and the deadline for their submission:

1. The method and place of submitting prequalification applications and the deadline for their submission shall be specified in the invitation to prequalify and in the qualification documents. The envelopes containing the bids shall be sent by hand or by anonymous public or private mail to the authority authorised to receive them. The place of submitting bids and the deadline for their submission shall also be specified in the bidding documents.

2. The procuring entity shall preserve the security, integrity and confidentiality of the applications and bids, and shall ensure that their contents are not examined until after they have been opened in accordance with due process.

3. The time limits for submitting prequalification applications or submitting bids shall be expressed as a specific date and a specific hour, and such time limits must allow bidders sufficient time to prepare and submit their applications or bids, taking into account the needs of the procuring entity and the conditions of delivery.

4. If the procuring entity issues a clarification or an amendment to the prequalification documents or the bidding documents, it must proceed, prior to the deadline for submitting applications or bids, to extend that deadline if necessary or as required pursuant to paragraph 4 of First of Article 21 of this Law, in order to allow bidders sufficient time to take the clarification or amendment into account in their submitted applications or bids.

5. The extension of the deadline shall be notified to every bidder to whom the procuring entity has provided the prequalification documents or the bidding documents, and the extension shall also be published on the central electronic platform of the Public Procurement Authority.

Bid validity period:

1. The bidding documents shall specify the bid validity period provided that it is proportionate to the nature of the procurement, and provided that it is not less than thirty days from the final date for the submission of bids.

2. The procuring entity may request bidders, prior to the expiry of the validity period of their bids, to extend such period for an additional specified duration. A bidder may refuse such request without the forfeiture of its bid security.

3. Bidders who agree to extend the validity period of their bids shall extend the validity period of the bid securities, or submit new bid securities covering the extension period of the validity of the bids. A bidder who has not extended its bid security, or who has not submitted a new bid security, shall be deemed to have refused the request to extend the validity period of its bid.

4. A bidder may modify or withdraw its bid prior to the final deadline for the submission of bids without the forfeiture of its bid security. The modification or request for withdrawal of the bid shall be effective when received by the procuring entity prior to the final deadline for the submission of bids.

5. The validity of the bid shall be extended ipso jure in the event that the proceedings are suspended for a specified period by the Complaints Authority in accordance with the provisions of Chapter Seven of this Law, for a period of time equal to the period of suspension of the proceedings. The bidder shall extend the period of its bid security accordingly.

Joint bids:

Several suppliers, service providers or contractors who fulfil the technical and legal conditions of this Law may participate jointly in the execution of a single procurement project, provided that they appoint, pursuant to an official letter addressed to the contracting authority and included within the documents of the submitted bid, a lead partner who represents them jointly and severally, signs in their name, and whose acts are binding upon them.

All other conditions of participation provided for in this Article shall be specified in the bidding documents specific to each procurement project.

Rules for acceptance of the successful bid (or provisional award) and entry into force of the contract:

1. The procuring entity shall accept the submitted successful bid unless:

a - the bidder that submitted the successful bid is disqualified pursuant to Article 7 of this Law; or

b - the procurement is cancelled pursuant to paragraph 1 of Article 25 of this Law; or

c - the successful bid is rejected upon being deemed abnormally low pursuant to Article 27 of this Law; or

d - the bidder that submitted the successful bid is excluded from the awarding procedures for the reasons set forth in Article 8 of this Law.

2. After ascertaining the successful bid, the procuring entity shall notify the bidder that submitted that bid, and shall simultaneously publish its decision regarding the acceptance of the successful bid (the provisional award), which enters into force upon the expiry of the standstill period of ten working days commencing from the date of publication, which must include, at a minimum, the following information:

a - the name and address of the bidder that submitted the successful bid (the provisional contractor);

b - the value of the bid, and a summary of the other characteristics of the successful bid and its relative advantages may be added if the successful bid was confirmed on the basis of price and other criteria;

c - the duration of the standstill period in accordance with this paragraph.

3. The standstill period shall not apply in the following cases:

a - in subsequent contracts to framework agreements not involving second-stage competition concluded under such agreements;

b - in the case of procurement by invoice;

c - in the case of procurement by mutual agreement in application of paragraphs 2 and 4 of Article 46 of this Law.

4. Immediately upon the expiry of the standstill period, the procuring entity shall notify the provisional contractor of the obligation to sign the contract within a time limit not exceeding //15// fifteen days.

5. The competent authority at the procuring entity shall sign the contract within a time limit of //15// fifteen days from the date of signature of the contract by the provisional contractor. This time limit may be extended to //30// thirty days in certain cases determined by the competent authority.

6. The contract shall enter into force when the provisional contractor and the competent authority at the contracting authority sign it.

7. Neither the contracting authority nor the provisional contractor shall take any measure that conflicts with the entry into force of the contract or with the execution of the procurement during the time period between the notification of the concerned bidder of the provisional award and the date of entry into force of the contract.

8. In the event that the provisional contractor refrains from signing the contract, the procuring entity shall forfeit its bid security. In such case, the procuring entity may cancel the procurement or select the best bid from among the other successful bids in accordance with the criteria and procedures specified in this Law and in the bidding documents, the validity of which remains in effect. The provisions of this Article shall apply to such bid mutatis mutandis.

Cancellation of procurement and/or any of its procedures:

1. The procuring entity may cancel the procurement and/or any of its procedures at any time prior to notifying the provisional awardee of the conclusion of the contract, in the following cases:

a - When the procuring entity finds it necessary to introduce unforeseen substantive changes to the bidding documents after announcing the procurement;

b - When unforeseen changes occur to the budget of the procuring entity;

c - When the need for the subject matter of the procurement ceases to exist as a result of unforeseen and objective circumstances, in which case the bidding shall not be repeated during the same budget or financial year.

2. It may also cancel the procurement and/or any of its procedures if no bid is submitted and/or unacceptable bids are submitted.

3. The procuring entity may also cancel the procurement and/or any of its procedures after accepting the winning submitted bid in the case referred to in paragraph 8 of Article 24 of this Law.

4. The procuring entity shall cancel the procurement and/or any of its procedures in the case of a single acceptable bid; however, it shall be entitled to take a reasoned decision to contract with the submitter of the single acceptable bid if all of the following conditions are met jointly:

a - That the principles and provisions of this Law are applied and that the single bid does not result from exclusive conditions included in the special terms of reference for the procurement project;

b - That the need is essential and urgent and the price is consistent with the estimated value study;

c - That the publication of the procuring entity's decision to accept the winning bid (provisional award) includes an explicit text stating the submission by the single acceptable bidder and the intention to contract with them.

5. The procuring entity's decision to cancel the procurement and/or any of its procedures and the reasons for such decision shall be entered into the record of procurement proceedings, and shall be notified to all participating bidders within a period not exceeding five days from the date of the cancellation decision. In addition, the procuring entity shall publish a notice of cancellation of the procurement in the same manner in which the original information relating to the bidding procedures was published and in the same place, and shall return the bids and proposals that remained unopened up until the cancellation decision was taken to the bidders who submitted them, and shall proceed to release the submitted guarantees.

6. The procuring entity shall not bear, when applying paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Article, any liability towards the bidders.

7. The procuring entity shall not open any bids or proposals after taking a decision to cancel the procurement.

Rules on the Announcement of the Contract Award:

1. The procuring entity shall publish an announcement of the award of the contract or the framework agreement, when the contract enters into force or a framework agreement is concluded, specifying the name of the contractor and the value of the contract.

2. Paragraph 1 shall not apply to the award of contracts whose value is less than the financial ceiling specified in the conditions for using the method of procurement by invoice. However, the procuring entity shall publish, at least once a year, a cumulative announcement of all contracts of this kind that have been awarded. Paragraph 1 shall also not apply to the award of contracts characterized by secrecy and relating to national security and defence in accordance with Paragraph 4 of Article 46.

3. The information provided for in this Article shall be published on the website of the procuring entity, if any, and on the central electronic platform of the Public Procurement Authority.

Work Sites:

No procurement proceedings relating to the execution of works may be launched except after the completion by the procuring entity of all legal procedures relating to the preparation of the work sites, including the issuance of possession decisions.

Subcontracting:

1- The main contractor must personally undertake the performance of the contract and shall remain liable towards the contracting authority for the performance of all its clauses and conditions, and he shall be prohibited from assigning all of his contractual obligations to a third party.

2- In works and service contracts, and where the special specifications permit so, the contractor may entrust a subcontractor with the performance of a part of the contract within the permitted percentage stipulated in the special specifications, which must not exceed 50% of the contract value. The contractor must obtain prior approval for subcontracting from the contracting authority, which must take its decision of approval or reasoned rejection within a time limit specified in the conditions of the contract, and its silence upon the expiry of this time limit shall be deemed an implicit decision of acceptance.

3- The provisions of Clause "First" of Article Seven of this Law shall apply to the subcontractor.

Supervision of Execution and Statements of Account:

First: Supervision:

1- In works contracts, and in other contracts that so require such as service and manufacturing contracts for the benefit of the contracting authority, concurrent supervision shall be applied alongside the execution of the required works in a manner that ensures the continuity of the work and its achievement of the required specifications and desired results prior to the date of provisional acceptance.

2- Supervision shall be undertaken by a person assigned thereto by the contracting authority from among those possessing competence, experience, and the ability to follow up on the work, from within the contracting authority, or from outside it where necessary, in which case the supervisor shall be contracted in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

3- As a result of the supervision, periodic reports on the progress of the work and the description of the execution shall be drawn up, and the supervisor must notify the contracting authority of any violation or improper conduct carried out at the work sites.

4- The supervisor shall attend the work sites in a manner that ensures the soundness and continuity of the work, and shall audit the statements of account, attend the process of handing over the work sites and the provisional and final acceptance, express his opinion on the contractor's proposals and on the required modifications to the awarded works, propose what is appropriate for executing the work in a more suitable manner, and submit a report thereon to the contracting authority so that it may take the appropriate decision.

5- Whoever undertakes the supervision of the works shall bear personal liability for any default in the obligations incumbent upon him pursuant to this Article and shall be subject to the penalties provided for in Chapter Eight of this Law.

Second: Statements of Account:

The following must be specified in the terms of the contract:

1- The obligation of the contractor to submit statements of account for the goods, services, or works executed of various kinds, and the obligation that they be certified by the contracting authority;

2- The maximum time limit granted to the contractor to prepare these statements of account and the time limits for their approval or modification by the contracting authority;

3- The maximum time limit for issuing the payment order.

Contract Execution and Acceptance:

1- The supplies, works and services shall be received by the acceptance committee provided for in Article 101 of this Law, which shall submit its report within a maximum period of thirty days commencing from the date of submission of the request for acceptance by the contractor.

2- Consulting services shall be received by the entity supervising the execution of the contract, where one exists.

3- Where the nature and size of the project require a period exceeding thirty days, the committee shall justify the reasons therefor in writing and submit its proposals in this regard, provided that the period shall in no case exceed sixty days commencing from the date of submission of the request for acceptance by the contractor.

4- The acceptance period shall be stated in the conditions of the contract.

5- Acceptance shall be carried out in accordance with Article 101 of this Law.

Grounds for the Expiration of the Contract and its Consequences:

First: Default:

1- The contractor shall be deemed in default if he violates the terms of execution of the contract or the provisions of the bidding document, and after he has been officially served notice to comply with all his obligations by the contracting authority,

within a period ranging between five days at least and fifteen days at most, and the expiry of this period without the contractor performing what was requested of him.

2- The contractor may not be deemed in default except by virtue of a reasoned decision issued by the contracting authority upon the approval of the Public Procurement Authority.

3- If the contractor is deemed in default, the contract shall be rescinded ipso jure without the need for any notice, and the procedures stipulated in the first paragraph of the fourth item of this Article shall be applied.

Second: Termination

1- The contract shall expire ipso jure without the need for any notice in the following two cases:

a- Upon the death of the contractor if he is a natural person, unless the contracting authority approves a request to continue the execution by the heirs.

b- If the contractor becomes bankrupt or insolvent or the company is dissolved, in which case the procedures stipulated in the second paragraph of the fourth item of this Article shall be applied.

2- The contracting authority may terminate the contract if it becomes impossible for the contractor to perform any of his contractual obligations as a result of force majeure.

Third: Rescission:

1- The contract shall be rescinded ipso jure without the need for any notice in any of the following cases:

a- If a final judgment is issued against the contractor for committing any offence of corruption, collusion, fraud, deception, money laundering, financing of terrorism, conflict of interest, forgery, or fraudulent bankruptcy, in accordance with the laws in force;

b- If any of the cases mentioned in Article 8 of this Law materialises;

c- In the event of the loss of legal capacity of the contractor.

2- If the contract is rescinded for one of the reasons mentioned in the first paragraph of this item, the procedures stipulated in the first paragraph of the fourth item of this Article shall be applied.

Fourth: Consequences of the Expiration of the Contract:

1- In the event of the application of one of the cases of default or rescission specified in this Article, the contracting authority shall proceed to re-award the contract in accordance with the rules stipulated in this Law or execute it itself if it possesses the sufficient qualifications and capabilities for that without resorting to any type of contracting. If the new contract award or the execution results in a saving in costs, the saving shall accrue to the Treasury, and if it results in an increase in costs, the contracting authority shall have recourse against the defaulting contractor for the increase. In all cases, the performance bond shall be temporarily confiscated until the liquidation of the contract award.

2- In the event that the bankruptcy or insolvency of the contractor materialises, the following procedures shall immediately be followed, notwithstanding any other text:

a- The performance bond shall be temporarily confiscated for the account of the Treasury;

b- The contracting authority shall make an inventory of the executed works, supplies, or services or the stored materials prior to the date of the declaration of bankruptcy and shall draw up a statement thereof, the value of which it shall temporarily disburse on trust in the name of the Treasury;

c- The contracting authority shall proceed to re-award the contract in accordance with the rules stipulated in this Law or execute it itself if it possesses the sufficient qualifications and capabilities for that without resorting to any type of contracting. If the new contract award or the execution results in a saving in costs, the saving shall accrue to the Treasury, and the performance bond and the value of the statement set out in the preceding paragraph shall be paid to the bankruptcy trustee. If it results in an increase in costs, the increase shall be deducted from the bond and the value of the said statement, and the remainder shall be paid to the bankruptcy trustee. If that is not sufficient to cover the increase in its entirety, the value of the bond and the statement shall suffice.

3- In the event of the death of the contractor and the non-continuation of the execution by the heirs, the executed works or services or the supplied goods shall be received, and the value of his entitlements shall be disbursed in the name of the heirs.

4- No compensation shall be due for the services provided or the works executed by anyone who is proven to have committed any of the offences stipulated in sub-paragraph "a" of the first paragraph of "Third" of this Article.

5- The decision of the expiration of the contract and its reasons shall be published on the website of the contracting authority, if any, and on the central electronic platform at the Public Procurement Authority.

Bid Security:

1- The bid security shall be set at an amount that ensures the seriousness of the bidder and takes into account the value and importance of the procurement project without restricting competition, provided that it is a lump sum and does not exceed three percent of the estimated value of the procurement project.

2- The bid security shall not be mandatory for procurement projects whose estimated value does not exceed a financial ceiling set at /5/ billion Lebanese Pounds.

This financial ceiling shall be amended based on a recommendation from the Public Procurement Authority and by virtue of a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of its President, provided that the amendment does not lead to a violation of the objectives of this Article and the principles enshrined by this Law.

3- The bid security shall not be mandatory in the cases of contracting by mutual agreement provided for in Article 46 of this Law.

4- The validity of the bid security shall be set by adding //28// twenty-eight days to the validity of the bid.

5- The bid security shall be returned to the successful bidder upon submitting the performance security, and to the bidders to whom the contract was not awarded within a period not exceeding the entry into force of the contract.

Performance Security:

1- The amount of the performance security shall be set at a percentage not exceeding ten percent of the value of the contract.

2- Contracts concluded in accordance with the cases of contracting by mutual agreement provided for in Paragraph 5 of Article 46 of this Law and in the cases of purchase by invoice shall be exempted from the performance security.

3- The performance security must be submitted within the period specified in the conditions of the contract, provided that it does not exceed //15// fifteen days from the date of entry into force of the contract. In the event of failure to submit the performance security, the bid security shall be forfeited.

Method of Payment of Securities:

Both the bid security and the performance security shall be either in cash paid into the Treasury fund or into the fund of the contracting authority, or by virtue of an irrevocable bank letter of guarantee, issued by a bank accepted by the Bank of Lebanon, indicating that it is payable on demand.

Debarment:

1- A contractor who is deemed in default in accordance with Section "First" of Article 33 shall be debarred from participating in public procurement:

a- For a period of one full year when these procedures are applied to him for the first time, commencing from the date of publication of the first debarment decision.

b- For a period of two years when they are applied to him for a second time, commencing from the date of publication of the second decision ordering debarment.

c- For a period of five years when they are applied to him for the third time or more.

2- A contractor against whom a final judicial judgment is issued relating to one of the cases of termination specified in Article 33 of this Law shall be automatically debarred from participating in public procurement.

3- The contracting authority shall notify the debarment decision to the debarred contractor. The debarment decision shall also be published on the central electronic platform of the Public Procurement Authority and on the website of the contracting authority, if any.

4- The cessation of the impediment or rehabilitation shall restore to the bidders the right to participate.

5- The Public Procurement Authority shall update the debarment register on its central electronic platform and strike off the names of contractors whose conditions for participation in public procurement contracts have been restored, either on its own initiative or at their request.

6- Debarment decisions may be appealed before the State Council.

Procurement methods:

1- The procuring entity may carry out procurement by means of:

Public tender in accordance with the provisions of Article 42 and Section Two of this Chapter,

Two-stage tendering in accordance with the provisions of Articles 42 and 43 and Section Three of this Chapter,

Request for quotations in accordance with the provisions of Articles 42 and 44 and Section Four of this Chapter,

Request for proposals for consultancy services in accordance with the provisions of Articles 42 and 45 and Section Five of this Chapter,

Direct agreement in accordance with the provisions of Articles 42 and 46 and Section Seven of this Chapter,

Procurement by invoice in accordance with the provisions of Articles 42 and 47 and Section Six of this Chapter.

2- The procuring entity may also conduct framework agreement procedures in accordance with the provisions of Section Eight of this Chapter.

Payment of the contract price:

1- The contract price shall be paid after its performance in accordance with the provisions of Article 5 of this Law.

2-

a- The terms of the contract shall determine the method of payment according to the stages of performance or according to the deliverables, provided that the payments are commensurate with the deliverables, and provided that they do not exceed nine-tenths of the amount due, while one-tenth shall remain retained in the Treasury until final acceptance takes place.

b- These retentions shall be refunded upon final acceptance if the contract does not specify a warranty period for the supplies, works, or services. The contracting authority may cease deducting the one-tenth retentions when the guarantees provided cover the risks of the remainder of the performance of the contract. It shall also be entitled to replace the one-tenth retentions with an equivalent guarantee.

c- When making payments in accordance with the provisions of this paragraph, consideration must be given to deducting the amounts necessary to settle the payments on account referred to in paragraph 3 below.

3-

a- The contract may authorise the contracting authority to grant the contractor advances not exceeding //20// twenty percent of the contract price, provided that they do not in any case exceed a financial ceiling set at /15/ billion Lebanese pounds. This financial ceiling shall be amended upon the recommendation of the Public Procurement Authority and by virtue of a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of its President, provided that the amendment does not lead to a violation of the objectives of this Article and the principles enshrined by this Law. The contracting authority may, when exceeding the percentage specified in this paragraph, and where the terms of the contract so provide, grant the contractor advances against bank guarantees, after notifying the Public Procurement Authority.

b- The bank guarantee referred to in this paragraph shall be returned to the contractor upon the deduction of the full amounts of the advances.

Penalties:

The contractor must comply with the time limits specified in the contract under pain of paying the penalties specified therein.

Penalties shall be imposed ipso jure on the contractor merely by virtue of his violation of the provisions of the contract without the need to prove damage.

Deduction from the guarantee:

If an amount becomes due from the contractor in the course of performance, in application of the provisions and terms of the contract, the contracting authority shall be entitled to deduct this amount from the performance guarantee and call upon the contractor to replenish the amount within a specified period; if he fails to do so, he shall be deemed in default in accordance with the provisions of Item "First" of Article 33 of this Law.

General rules applicable to the selection of the procurement method:

1- Public procurement shall primarily be conducted by means of public tendering; however, in the cases provided for in Articles 43 to 48, other procurement methods may be adopted when their conditions are met.

2- Where it is not possible to adopt public tendering due to the non-fulfilment of its conditions and another method is selected, the procuring entity shall seek to maximise competition to the greatest extent possible.

3- Where the procuring entity uses a procurement method other than public tendering, it shall issue an explicit and reasoned decision to be entered in the register provided for in Article 9 of this Law, together with a statement of the reasons and circumstances upon which it relied to justify the use of that method.

Conditions for using two-stage tendering:

1- The procuring entity may conduct procurement by means of two-stage tendering in accordance with Section Three of this Chapter in the following two cases:

a- Where it is not possible for the procuring entity to describe and formulate the subject-matter of the procurement with the required precision in accordance with the requirements of the provisions of Article 17 of this Law, due to its complex nature. In this case, it may hold discussions with bidders with a view to determining the most satisfactory solution for its procurement needs;

b- Where the procuring entity has conducted a public tender twice consecutively and no bids were submitted, or where the said entity has cancelled the procurement proceedings in accordance with paragraph 3 or 4 of Article 25 of this Law, and it considers that entering into new public tendering proceedings, or using one of the procurement methods falling within the scope of Chapter Three of this Law, is unlikely to result in the conclusion of a procurement contract.

2- In all cases, the procuring entity shall obtain the prior approval of the Public Procurement Authority to use two-stage tendering. The Public Procurement Authority shall give its opinion on the request for approval sent by the procuring entity within //15// fifteen days, provided that the said Authority shall be deemed to have approved upon the expiry of this period without an opinion having been given.

Conditions for the use of the request for quotations:

The procuring entity may carry out procurement by means of a request for quotations, in accordance with the Fourth Clause of this Chapter, if the estimated value of the procurement project does not exceed a financial ceiling set at /15/ billion Lebanese Pounds. This financial ceiling shall be amended upon a recommendation of the Public Procurement Authority and pursuant to a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of its President, provided that the amendment does not lead to a violation of the objectives of this Article and the principles enshrined by this Law.

Conditions for the use of the request for proposals for consultancy services:

The procuring entity may carry out procurement by means of a request for proposals in accordance with the Fifth Clause of this Chapter, when it procures consultancy services the main subject of which is the provision of services of an intellectual or technical nature.

The scope of consultancy services shall include, by way of example and not limitation:

- Training, auditing, computer programming projects, and other specialised consultancy works;

- Preparing studies and designs, drawing up bidding documents, supervising the execution of works and projects, and supervising the provision of services.

In this case, the procuring entity shall examine the financial aspects of the proposals separately such that it shall only examine them after completing the examination and evaluation of the technical, functional, and performance-related characteristics of the proposal.

Conditions for procurement by invoice:

The procuring entity may procure by invoice in accordance with Section Six of this Chapter, if the estimated value of the procurement project, including consultancy services, does not exceed a financial ceiling set at one hundred //1.5// billion Lebanese pounds. This financial ceiling shall be amended upon a recommendation from the Public Procurement Authority and by virtue of a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of its President, provided that the amendment does not result in violating the objectives of this Article and the principles enshrined by this Law.

Conditions for the use of framework agreement procedures:
