1- The procuring entity may resort to framework agreement procedures, in accordance with the provisions of Section VIII of this Chapter, in either of the following two cases:

a- where the need is likely to arise on a recurrent basis and at an uncertain date;

b- where the need for the subject matter of the procurement, by virtue of its nature, arises on an urgent basis during a given period of time.

2- Framework agreements shall be concluded in cases of centralized procurement of goods, services, and simple works included in a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers for this purpose upon the recommendation of the Public Procurement Authority, in accordance with the provisions of Paragraph 2 of Article 3 of this Law. Otherwise, the procuring entity shall notify the Public Procurement Authority of its intention to use a framework agreement at least //10// ten days prior to the commencement of the procedures. The procuring entity shall not be entitled to use framework agreements to prevent or restrict competition.

3- The procuring entity shall include in the record provided for pursuant to Article 9 of this Law a statement of the reasons and circumstances upon which it relied to justify resorting to framework agreement procedures and the type of framework agreement it has selected.

Invitation to public tender:

Every procurement operation conducted by means of a public tender shall be preceded by the issuance of a notice to the public in accordance with the provisions of Article 12 of this Law, with the exception of procurement operations preceded by pre-qualification pursuant to Article 19 of this Law.

Provision of terms of reference (or bidding documents):

The procuring entity shall make the terms of reference or the bidding document available to bidders on its website, if any, and on the central electronic platform of the Public Procurement Authority concurrently with the announcement of the procurement. In the event that pre-qualification procedures are conducted, the procuring entity shall provide a set of bidding documents to each bidder that has been pre-qualified and pays the fee due for those documents, if there is a fee for them. The fee that the procuring entity may charge for the bidding documents must equal the cost of providing those documents to the bidders.

Submission of Bids

1- Bids shall be submitted in accordance with what the bidding documents stipulate as to the manner, place, and deadline of submission of the bid.

2- The bid shall be submitted in writing and signed in a sealed envelope. Bids may be submitted according to the two-envelope system or the single-envelope system in accordance with what the bidding documents stipulate.

3- The procuring entity shall provide the bidder with a receipt showing a serial number in addition to the date of receipt of the bid by hour, day, month, and year.

4- The procuring entity shall preserve the security, integrity, and confidentiality of the bid, and shall ensure that its contents are not accessed except after it has been duly opened.

5- No bid received by the procuring entity after the deadline for the submission of bids shall be opened; rather, it shall be returned sealed to the bidder who submitted it.

Opening of Bids:

1- The Tender Committee provided for in Article 100 of this Law shall open the bids in a public session in the presence of the persons authorised in the bidding document, at the time, place, and in accordance with the method specified in this document, provided that this session is held immediately upon the expiry of the time limit for the submission of bids.

2- All bidders participating in the procurement process or their duly authorised representatives, as well as the controller delegated by the Public Procurement Authority, shall have the right to attend the bid-opening session. The procuring entity may also invite the media to attend this session, provided that it provides for this in the bidding document.

3- Bids shall be opened according to the mechanism specified in the bidding document.

4- The proceedings of the opening of bids shall be recorded in writing in minutes signed by the chairperson and members of the Tender Committee, and an attendance list shall be drawn up and signed by the participants from among the representatives of the procuring entity and the Public Procurement Authority, and the bidders and their representatives, provided that this constitutes proof of their attendance. All information and documents relating to the proceedings of the session shall be entered into the record of procurement proceedings provided for in Article 9 of this Law.

Evaluation of bids:

1- The procuring entity shall examine the financial bids separately, such that it examines them after the completion of the verification and evaluation of the administrative and technical bids.

2- Subject to the provisions of Paragraph (3) of this Article, the procuring entity shall consider a bid to be substantially responsive to the requirements if it fulfills all the requirements set forth in the bidding documents in accordance with Article 17 of this Law.

3- Where the information or documents submitted in the bid are incomplete or erroneous, or in the absence of a specific document, the procuring entity may request in writing from the bidder concerned clarifications regarding its bid, or request the submission or completion of the relevant information or documents within a specified time period, provided that all correspondence is in writing and that the principles of transparency and equal treatment among bidders are respected in written requests for clarification or completion, and with due regard to the provisions of Paragraph 3 of the Second Clause of Article 21 of this Law.

4- The procuring entity shall reject a bid:

a- If the bidder is not qualified in view of the qualification conditions contained in the terms of reference and in application of the provisions of Article 7 of this Law;

b- If the bid is not substantially responsive to the requirements specified in the bidding file;

c- In the circumstantial cases referred to in Articles 8 or 25 of this Law.

5- The procuring entity shall evaluate the accepted bids with a view to determining the winning bid in accordance with the criteria and procedures contained in the bidding files. No criterion or procedure not contained in these files shall be used.

6- A bid shall be considered the winning bid in either of the following two cases:

a- The lowest-priced bid, where price is the sole criterion for awarding the contract;

b- The best bid based on the evaluation criteria and procedures specified in the bidding documents in accordance with Article 18 of this Law, where there are financial criteria and other criteria besides price.

7- The procuring entity shall evaluate the bids within a reasonable time limit commensurate with the validity period of the bids and with the nature of the procurement, and shall draw up a record thereof to be entered in the register of procurement proceedings provided for in Article 9 of this Law.

Prohibition of negotiations with bidders:

Negotiations between the procuring entity and any of the bidders regarding the bid submitted by that bidder shall be prohibited.

Two-stage tendering proceedings:

1- The provisions of Subdivision Two of this Chapter shall apply to two-stage tendering proceedings, to the extent that they do not conflict with the provisions of this Subdivision.

2- The procuring entity shall invite bidders to submit, in the first stage of two-stage tendering proceedings, initial bids containing their proposals without financial bids. The bidding documents may include a request for proposals regarding technical, functional or performance-related specifications, or regarding the contractual terms and conditions, as well as information and supporting documents concerning the professional, technical and financial qualifications of the bidders.

3- The procuring entity may, in the first stage, hold discussions with bidders whose initial bids have not been rejected, concerning any aspect of those bids. When the procuring entity holds discussions with any bidder, it shall afford all bidders an equal opportunity to participate in those discussions and shall strictly abide by the standards of transparency and equal treatment. The discussions shall be documented either by written or electronic correspondence or through bilateral online video sessions documented in minutes of meetings signed by the participants. Upon completion of the examination of the proposals and the discussions, the procuring entity shall prepare a detailed report on the proceedings of the first stage, upon which it shall rely in preparing the final technical requirements. The report, as well as the minutes of the discussions, shall be included in the record of procurement proceedings provided for in Article 9 of this Law.

4-

a- In the second stage of two-stage tendering proceedings, the procuring entity shall invite all bidders whose initial bids were not rejected in the first stage to submit final bids comprising technical and financial bids, in response to a revised set of terms and conditions for the procurement.

b- In revising the terms of reference and its relevant provisions, the procuring entity may not modify the subject matter of the procurement, but it may refine aspects of the description of the subject matter of the procurement by doing the following:

1) Deleting or modifying any aspect of the technical, functional or performance-related specifications set out in the first stage, and adding any new specifications that are consistent with the provisions of this Law;

2) Deleting or modifying any criterion for the evaluation of bids set out in the first stage, and adding any new criterion that is consistent with the provisions of this Law, provided that such deletion, modification or addition is limited to cases where such deletion, modification or addition is necessary as a result of changes made to the technical, functional or performance specifications.

5- Bidders shall be notified of the invitation to submit their final bids and shall be provided with the final bidding documents after their amendment pursuant to sub-paragraph (b) of paragraph 4 of this Article;

6- A bidder who does not wish to submit a final bid may withdraw from the tendering proceedings without forfeiting its right to recover the bid security that it may have submitted;

7- The final bids shall be evaluated in order to ascertain the winning bid in accordance with paragraph 5 of Article 55 of this Law.

Request for Quotations Procedures:

1- The provisions of Section Two of this Chapter shall apply to request for quotations procedures, with the exception of the provisions of Article 49 (Invitation to Public Tender).

2- The procuring entity shall determine the suppliers or contractors whom it wishes to invite to participate in the competition in accordance with Article 44 of this Law, and shall address the invitation to them directly and by a rapid and guaranteed means. Lists prepared by the procuring entity shall be adopted for this purpose, provided that the adopted list is entered in the record of procurement proceedings provided for in Article 9 of this Law. This list must be updated periodically in order to add new bidders to it on the basis of the guidelines issued by the Public Procurement Authority in this regard.

3- The number of invited bidders must not be less than three.

4- The publication period shall be set at a sufficient time that allows bidders to prepare their bids in keeping with the importance and complexity of the procurement project, provided that in all cases it is not less than //10// ten days prior to the deadline for the submission of bids. The publication period may be reduced to //5// five days by a reasoned decision in cases of justified urgency, provided that the reasoning is recorded in the record of procurement proceedings provided for in Article 9 of this Law.

Invitation to purchase by invoice:

1- When applying this method in accordance with the provisions of Article 47 of this Law, the procuring entity shall request price quotations from the largest number of suppliers or contractors as is practically possible, provided that they are not fewer than two quotations. Each supplier or contractor from whom a price quotation is requested shall be informed of whether any elements other than the costs of the subject matter of the procurement itself must be included in the price, such as any applicable transport and insurance expenses, customs duties, and taxes.

2- Each bidder shall be permitted to submit only one price quotation, and shall not be permitted to change its quotation. No negotiations shall take place between the procuring entity and any bidder regarding the price quotation submitted by it.

3 - A statement signed by the right holders detailing the services, supplies, or works shall suffice where it is impossible to submit an invoice, and an invoice alone may suffice where it is impossible to obtain two quotations.

The winning bid in purchase by invoice:

The winning price quotation shall be the lowest-priced quotation that meets the needs of the procuring entity as set out in the request for price quotations.

Procedures for Contracting by Mutual Agreement:

When the procuring entity carries out procurement from a single source in accordance with Article 46 of this Law:

1- The procuring entity shall notify the Public Procurement Authority of its intention to conclude a contract by mutual agreement and shall publish a notice of procurement by way of mutual agreement on the central electronic platform of the Public Procurement Authority and on its website, if any, at least //10// ten days prior to the date of conclusion of the contract. The notice shall include, as a minimum, the following information:

a- The name and address of the procuring entity;

b- A summary of the most important provisions and terms required in the procurement contract, including the nature and quantity of the goods to be supplied and the place of their delivery, or the nature and location of the works to be executed, or the nature of the services and the location where they are to be provided, as well as the time required for the supply of the goods, the completion of the works, or the provision of the services;

c- That the contract shall be concluded by way of mutual agreement.

2- The provisions of paragraph 1 of this Article shall not apply in the cases referred to in paragraphs 2 and 4 of Article 46 of this Law.

3- The procuring entity shall request a proposal or price quotations from a single bidder, and shall conduct negotiations with this bidder, unless such negotiations are impracticable in the circumstances surrounding the procurement process concerned.

4- The procuring entity may award the contract to the bidder without following competitive procedures.

Electronic Procurement System:

An electronic platform dedicated to electronic procurement shall be established at the Public Procurement Authority through the use of digital information means and technologies to secure the needs of procuring entities for supplies, works, and services.

This platform must include an electronic registration mechanism that enables suppliers, contractors, consultants, and service providers to register online in order to qualify to participate in electronic public procurement.

The platform shall allocate dedicated pages for the electronic submission and receipt of tenders, and these pages shall operate only from the date of issuance of the competition until the time of its closing, and the closing date and time for electronic awards shall be the same as the closing date and time for traditional awards.

The electronic procurement system shall cover the announcement of procurement, the submission and opening of tenders, and contracting electronically, as well as containing a virtual marketplace, and shall constitute a unified portal for traditional announcements and the use of standard documents.

Electronic Procurement Procedures:

Electronic procurement procedures shall be subject to the highest degrees of privacy, confidentiality, security, and transparency of information, and electronic exchanges shall enjoy evidentiary force, and the electronic procurement system shall ensure the confidentiality and integrity of transactions over an open information network without discrimination among transacting parties, and it shall be subject to the laws and regulations in force relating to electronic exchange.

Electronic signatures shall be applied in accordance with the requirements of the laws and regulations in force relating to electronic signatures.

Registration in the Electronic System:

Users must register in the electronic procurement system in order to be able to access it. This registration shall entitle each user to obtain a personal identifier

(username) enabling them to use the electronic procurement system.

Upon the electronic submission of registration applications and tenders, the system shall confirm the transmission and its date and time.

Electronic Submission of Tenders:

When the procuring entity uses the electronic procurement system, all tenders shall be submitted electronically, and where electronic submission is not possible, for technical or technological reasons, the tender or part thereof may be submitted by traditional methods within the time limits specified for accepting applications or tenders.

Electronic opening and evaluation of bids:

The opening and evaluation of bids shall be subject to the provisions set forth in this Law, and the session shall be public electronically via virtual means of communication, and the awarding, contracting and notice to proceed shall take place electronically.

Application of electronic procurement:

The Public Procurement Authority shall prepare the implementing details of electronic procurement, which shall be determined pursuant to a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers.

Training:

1- Those carrying out public procurement duties shall be subject to mandatory, continuous, specialized training implemented by the Ministry of Finance  Institut des Finances Basil Fuleihan.

2- Training shall be coordinated with the National Institute of Administration and the concerned entities while preserving the principle of synergy and complementarity of roles among the various institutes and training centers concerned with capacity building at the national level, and strengthening the collaborative approach with knowledge centers, including, by way of example and without limitation, universities, research centers and public policy centers, shall be encouraged.

3- Part of the training may be directed to the private sector.

4- Training programs shall be dedicated to enhancing the integrity of those concerned with procurement, from the public and private sectors, to raise the level of awareness of the risks of lack of integrity, such as corruption, fraud, collusion and discrimination, and the penalties associated therewith, and to develop knowledge of the means to confront these risks.

5- Periodic training shall include administrative and financial judges concerned with the implementation of this Law, subject to the approval of each of the President of the State Council and the President of the Court of Accounts.

6- Training shall include supporting the implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals.

Job Title:

1- Public procurement shall be included as a specific function within the job structure of the State. Implementation decrees shall determine the frameworks of cognitive competencies, skills, professional experience and behaviours, in addition to the job description and the conditions of recruitment and/or appointment and promotion specific to those working in procurement, to be prepared by the Public Procurement Authority in coordination with the Civil Service Board, in addition to providing motivating, competitive and merit-based career options.

2- A procurement unit shall be established in the organisational structure of the procuring entity, or this structure shall be amended, as required, and this unit shall be responsible for procurement operations in accordance with the provisions of this Law. This unit shall be formed of employees who have undergone training in accordance with Article 72 above, provided that the staffing of this unit and the competencies of its members are commensurate with the volume and nature of its procurement.

3- The cadre of the procurement unit at each procuring entity shall be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the competent authority.

4- The procurement unit may request technical advice, where required, from the Public Procurement Authority, or seek its opinion on a specific matter relating to procurement.

Establishment of the Public Procurement Authority:

1- An independent administrative authority called the "Public Procurement Authority" shall be established pursuant to this Law, exercising the powers and tasks set forth in its text, and its headquarters shall be in the city of Beirut.

2- The Authority shall enjoy legal personality and financial and administrative autonomy. It shall also have legal standing and interest to bring challenges against decisions related to the procurement process in accordance with the provisions of Chapter Seven of this Law.

3- The powers of the Authority shall cover all procuring entities in accordance with the definition determined for them pursuant to this Law.

4- The cadres and tasks of those working in the Public Procurement Authority shall be determined by a decree issued by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers following the recommendation of the Public Procurement Authority and consultation with the State Council, within a period of six months from the date of issuance of the decree forming the Authority.

5- The Authority shall not be subject to the provisions of Decree No. 4517 dated 13/12/1972 (General Regulations for Public Institutions), provided that it shall be subject to the provisions of this Law and to the ex-post audit of the Court of Accounts and to the oversight of the Central Inspection and the Civil Service Board.

Formation of the Authority:

1- The Authority shall be formed of a President and four members appointed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers in accordance with the conditions and mechanism of appointment detailed in Article 78. The term of office of each of the President and the four members shall be fixed at five years, renewable once only.

2- The Authority shall adopt its decisions by a majority of the members of which it is legally composed, and the Authority shall jointly assume the tasks and powers stipulated in this Law, pursuant to internal bylaws in which the distribution of tasks among the members and the methods and means of executing the decisions issued by the Authority are determined.

3- With the exception of the President, to whom the provisions of the first paragraph of Article 81 of this Law apply, every member of the Authority shall be deemed disciplinarily liable in the event that he intentionally or negligently breaches the duties imposed upon him by the applicable laws and regulations in force. Disciplinary prosecution in respect of the members or in respect of the President shall not preclude their prosecution, where applicable, before the competent civil or criminal courts.

Cases of Incompatibility and Full-Time Dedication:

1- The President and members of the Authority shall be bound, throughout the term of their mandate and even after its expiry, by professional secrecy in respect of all information of which they become aware on the occasion of or by reason of the performance of their duties, and they shall be prohibited from disclosing it except before the supervisory and judicial bodies. This obligation shall include information classified by the Authority as confidential in accordance with its regulations and decisions.

2- Each of the President and the members must be dedicated on a full-time basis.

3- The President and members of the Authority may not be appointed from among the following categories:

a- Any person who has any direct or indirect interest in any company or establishment participating in public procurement or with any procuring entity.

b- Any person who has declared cessation of payments or has been judicially declared bankrupt.

c- Any person against whom a disciplinary decision has been issued imposing a penalty other than a warning or a reprimand.

4- The President and members of the Authority shall be prohibited from practising any other public or private work, whether remunerated or unremunerated, during the assumption of their duties, including, by way of example, the presidency or membership of the Council of Ministers or the Chamber of Deputies, the chairmanship or membership of the board of directors of a public establishment, private company or bank, the presidency or membership of a public body, and the presidency or membership of a municipal council or a private company entrusted with the management of a public utility.

5- The President and members of the Authority shall be prohibited, during the term of their mandate and for a period of not less than two years after its expiry, from assuming, directly or indirectly, any position of responsibility in companies that participated in procurement proceedings within the framework of this Law during the period in which they exercised their powers.

6- Each of the President and members of the Public Procurement Authority shall be required to disclose in writing any developments likely to affect his membership in accordance with the provisions of this Law. In the event that any member breaches this obligation, the provisions in force shall apply to him.

7- Each of the President and the members shall take, before the President of the Republic and prior to assuming his duties, the following legal oath: "I swear by Almighty God to perform my duties with honesty, independence and loyalty, to be attentive to the enforcement of the laws and regulations, and to preserve the secrets and dignity of the office."

Conditions and mechanism for appointing the President and members of the Authority:

Subject to the conditions of appointment provided for in Article Four of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 dated 12/6/1959 (Civil Servants Regulations) and its amendments, with the exception of the conditions of age and competitive examination, the following conditions and mechanism shall be adopted for appointing the President and members of the Authority:

a- That they hold at least a Master's degree in public procurement, public administration, financial sciences, economics, law, engineering, political and administrative sciences, business administration, financial management, or information technology;

b- That they possess proven experience in the field of public procurement of not less than 10 years.

c- The Civil Service Board shall prepare the notice for filling the position of President and members of the Authority, containing the required qualifications and conditions in addition to the candidate evaluation criteria prepared by the committee referred to in Sub-paragraph "g", and shall publish it on the website of the Board, provided that the publication includes the time limit for submitting candidacy applications.

d- Candidacy applications shall be submitted by those who meet the qualifications and conditions within the specified time limit through a unified electronic form available on the website of the Civil Service Board, provided that candidacy applications submitted by hand or otherwise shall not be accepted.

e- The Civil Service Board shall undertake the acceptance of applications that fulfil the conditions and specifications in accordance with the first paragraph of this Article.

f- The Civil Service Board shall prepare a report containing the numerical lists of accepted candidacy applications, and nominal lists of unaccepted candidacy applications indicating the reasons for their non-acceptance, and they shall be deposited with the candidate selection committee referred to in Sub-paragraph "g" below of this paragraph.

g- Accepted candidacy applications shall be evaluated by a committee composed of:

- The President of the National Anti-Corruption Commission

- The President of the Court of Accounts

- The President of the Civil Service Board

- The President of the Central InspectionThe President of the Civil Service Board shall undertake the coordination and management of the work of this committee.

h- Accepted candidacy applications shall be evaluated in accordance with the criteria of specialization, qualifications, degrees, years of experience and its diversity, proficiency in foreign languages, and other criteria, and as a result thereof marks shall be assigned in accordance with a general average agreed upon, on the basis of which a list of the names of candidates accepted for the oral interview stage shall be drawn up, indicating the reasons for the non-acceptance of the other applications, provided that the committee prepares a report on the results of its work.

i- The names of the accepted candidates shall remain unannounced until the date for conducting the oral interviews is set. The oral interviews with the candidates whose applications have been accepted shall be conducted by the selection committee in a meeting scheduled for this purpose, provided that the interviews are conducted at the Civil Service Board.

j- The President of the Council of Ministers shall propose the names of those who passed the oral interview for each position in accordance with the order of marks, for submission to the Council of Ministers to select whom it appoints, after the submission of the documents proving the fulfilment of conditions and the verification of the candidate's possession thereof and of their authenticity.

Meetings of the Authority:

1- The Authority shall meet periodically, at least once every week, without the need to issue a convocation from its President, and shall take its decisions by a majority.

2- The date of the periodic meeting shall be determined in the first session it holds, and in the event that the meeting is not convened for any reason whatsoever, the meeting shall be convened on the following day.

3- The agenda of the said periodic sessions shall be dedicated to discussing the affairs of the Authority's work and any subjects raised by the President or any of the members.

4- The President shall prepare the agenda and notify it to the members at least two days prior to the date of the meeting.

5- The agenda shall be notified to the members by any appropriate means, including electronic mail.

6- In the event of the absence of the President, the eldest member shall preside over the meeting of the Authority.

7- If the President or any of the members is absent without a legitimate excuse from attending three consecutive meetings or from attending six meetings during the year, he shall be deemed to have resigned or to be relieved of his duties automatically.

Termination of Membership:

1- The term of office of the President and any of the four members shall end upon the expiry of the period specified in accordance with Article 75 of this Law, or by death, resignation, loss of capacity, or any of the conditions of appointment, incompatibility, or full-time dedication, or if his health or mental condition prevents him from performing his duties, or by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers upon their breach of their functional duties, after verification thereof by a panel composed of the President of the National Anti-Corruption Commission, the President of the Civil Service Board, and the President of the Court of Accounts, and by a decision taken by it by a majority based on a referral from the President of the Central Inspection in this regard.

2- In the event of a vacancy in the position of the President, the eldest member shall deputise for him. The Council of Ministers shall fill the vacancy within a period of one month at most and in accordance with the rules of appointment specified in this Law.

Allowances:

Each of the President of the Authority and the members shall receive lump-sum monthly allowances to be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers.

Finances of the Authority:

1- The Authority shall have an independent budget and its financial resources shall consist of the following:

a- A special annual financial contribution entered in a special chapter within the section of the Presidency of the Council of Ministers in the State General Budget Law, which shall be sufficient to cover the expenses and activities of the Authority;

b- Unconditional grants and donations from international donor institutions, subject to the observance of conflict of interest;

c- Any resources provided for in other laws and not provided for under this Article.

2- The funds of the Authority shall be deposited in a special account at the Bank of Lebanon, and the President of the Authority shall undertake the commitment of its expenditures in accordance with the rules provided for in the Public Accounting Law and the laws and regulations in force.

3- The Authority shall prepare an annual draft budget in accordance with the laws and regulations in force, and its financial bylaws shall determine the manner of preparing the budget, the expenditure mechanism, and all other financial matters related to the conduct of its work.

4- An additional appropriation shall be opened in the General Budget for the Authority for the first operational year following the issuance of this Law in accordance with the rules.

Publicity of Data:

1- The Authority shall make available to the public, by the available digital and/or paper means, all data, documents, records, and statements, subject to the observance of confidentiality with respect to public contracts related to national security and defense and the observance of the provisions of the sixth Article of this Law.

2- The Authority shall publish at the end of each financial year on its central electronic platform, at least, a statement on the status of its assets and holdings and a summary of its budget.

Decisions of the Authority:

1- The decisions of the Authority shall be subject to the principle of reasoning, and the Authority shall state in the recitals of the decision taken its reasons and objectives.

2- The decisions of the Authority shall not become effective except from the date of their notification or publication in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

Methods of Recourse against the Decisions of the Authority:

1- Every interested party shall have the right to challenge the decisions related to public procurement operations issued by the Authority in accordance with the provisions of Chapter Seven of this Law.

2- All other administrative decisions issued by the Authority or formed against it and not related to public procurement procedures shall be subject to recourse before the State Council where the legal conditions therefor are met.

Internal Regulations, Administrative Regulations and Staff Regulations:

The Authority shall draw up its internal regulations, administrative and financial regulations, and the regulations of its staff, after consulting the Civil Service Board and the State Council, within a maximum period of three months from the date of its establishment, provided that they are issued by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers, within a maximum period of two months from the date on which the draft decrees are referred to him by the Authority.

Transitional Provisions:

1- The Tenders Administration shall be abolished and its cadres and workers therein shall be transferred to the Public Procurement Authority without modification in rank and salary while retaining their right to seniority qualifying for step advancement, provided that they meet the conditions of appointment specified in Article Four of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 dated 12/6/1959 (Civil Servants Regulations) and its amendments, with the exception of the two conditions of age and competitive examination. The Director General of the Tenders Administration shall be the President of the Authority, and the current civil servants, contracted personnel and wage earners in the Tenders Administration shall be part of the administrative structure of the Public Procurement Authority.

2- Until the members of the Authority are appointed, the President of the Authority shall assume its functions.

Establishment of the Complaints Authority:

1- Pursuant to this Law, an independent authority called the "Administrative Complaints Authority" shall be established, which shall be concerned with adjudicating complaints submitted regarding explicit or implicit procedures or decisions issued by the procuring entity or any of the administrative entities concerned with the procurement process or formed against it, including tender documents.

2- The Authority alone and exclusively shall examine complaints regarding explicit or implicit decisions relating to procurement procedures submitted directly to it at the stage prior to the signing of the contract, notwithstanding any other text.

3- The Authority shall not be subject to the provisions of Decree No. 4517 dated 13/12/1972 (General Regulations of Public Institutions); however, it shall be subject to the provisions of this Law and to the ex-post audit of the Court of Accounts and to the oversight of the Central Inspection and the Civil Service Board.

Composition of the Authority:

1- The Authority shall be composed of a President and three members appointed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers in accordance with the conditions and mechanism of appointment detailed in Article 91 below. The term of office of each of the President and the three members shall be fixed at four years, renewable once only.

2- The Authority shall be assisted in its functions by a specialized administrative body.

Conditions and mechanism for appointing the President and members of the Objections Authority:

1- Subject to the conditions of appointment provided for in Article Four of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 dated 12/6/1959 (Civil Servants Regulations) and its amendments, with the exception of the two conditions of age and competitive examination, the following conditions shall be adopted for appointing the President and members of the Authority:

a- That they hold at least a Master's degree in law, public procurement, public administration, financial sciences, economics, jurisprudence, engineering, political and administrative sciences, business administration, financial management, information technology, or the equivalent thereof;

b- That they possess proven experience of not less than 10 years in fields related to public procurement.

2- Furthermore, the appointment mechanism provided for in Article 78 of this Law shall be adopted for appointing the President and members of the Authority.

3- The employees in the administrative corps shall be appointed in accordance with due process.

Cases of Incompatibility and Full-Time Service:

1- The President and members of the Authority shall be bound, throughout the term of their mandate and even after its expiry, by professional secrecy with respect to all information that has come to their knowledge on the occasion of the performance of their duties or by reason thereof, and they shall be prohibited from disclosing it except before the supervisory bodies and the judicial authority. This obligation shall include information classified by the Authority as confidential in accordance with its regulations and decisions.

2- Each of the President and the members must serve on a full-time basis.

3- The President and members of the Authority may not be appointed from among the following categories:

a- Any person who has any direct or indirect interest in any company or establishment participating in public procurement or with any procuring entity.

b- Any person who has declared cessation of payments or has been judicially declared bankrupt.

c- Any person against whom a disciplinary decision has been issued imposing a penalty other than reprimand, warning, or censure, with respect to members of the Authority from the public sector.

4- The President and members of the Authority shall be prohibited from engaging in any other public or private work, whether remunerated or unremunerated, during the performance of their duties, including, by way of example, the presidency or membership of the Council of Ministers or the Chamber of Deputies, the chairmanship or membership of the board of directors of a public institution, a private company, or a bank, the presidency or membership of a public authority, and the presidency or membership of a municipal council or a private company managing a public utility.

5- Each of the President and members of the Complaints Authority must disclose in writing any developments likely to affect his membership in accordance with the provisions of this Law. In the event that any member breaches this obligation, the provisions in force shall apply to him.

6- Each of the President and members of the Authority shall take, before the President of the Republic and prior to assuming his duties, the following legal oath: "I swear by Almighty God to perform my duties with honesty, independence, and loyalty, to be diligent in applying the laws and regulations, and to preserve the secrets and dignity of the office."

Termination of membership:

1- The term of office of the President and any of the three members shall terminate in either of the following two cases:

a- Upon the expiry of the term specified in accordance with Article 90 of this Law, or by death, resignation, loss of capacity, or loss of any of the conditions of appointment, incompatibility, or full-time dedication, or if his health or mental condition prevents him from performing his duties, which shall be established by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers,

b- Upon their breach of their functional duties, by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers, after verification thereof by a committee composed of the President of the National Anti-Corruption Commission, the President of the Civil Service Board, and the President of the Court of Audit, by a decision taken by it by majority upon a referral by the President of the Central Inspection in this regard.

2- In the event of a vacancy in the position of the President, the oldest member shall replace him. The Council of Ministers shall fill the vacancy within a period of one month at most and in accordance with the rules of appointment specified in this Law.

3- The President or any of the members shall be deemed to have resigned or been relieved of his duties ipso jure if he is absent without a legitimate excuse from attending three consecutive sessions or from attending six sessions during the year.

Remunerations:

Each of the President of the Authority and the members shall receive lump-sum monthly remunerations to be determined by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers.

Finances of the Complaints Authority:

1- The Complaints Authority shall have an independent budget, and its financial resources shall consist of the following:

a- An annual financial contribution entered in a special chapter within the section of the Presidency of the Council of Ministers in the State General Budget Law.

b- Fees collected pursuant to its internal regulations, in the event the collection of fees is adopted.

c- Any resources provided for in other laws and not provided for under this Article.

2- The Authority shall prepare its draft budget in accordance with the laws and regulations in force, and its financial regulations shall determine the manner of preparing the budget, the mechanism of expenditure, and all other financial matters related to the conduct of its work.

3- The funds of the Complaints Authority shall be deposited in a special account at the Bank of Lebanon, and the President of the Authority shall undertake the commitment of its expenditures in accordance with the procedures provided for in the Public Accounting Law and the laws in force.

4- An additional credit shall be opened in the General Budget for the Authority for the first operational year following the issuance of this Law in accordance with the applicable procedures.

Working mechanism of the Authority:

1- The President shall form for each objection file a sub-committee called the "Objections Committee", which he shall chair and which shall be composed of two of the three members of whom the Objections Authority is composed, according to specialization.

2- The Authority may seek the assistance of expertise from the private sector according to the type of objection file and the nature of the procurement process. The expert from the private sector shall be selected according to specialization and by lot from among the rosters of experts concerned with the subject-matter of the objected procurement, which are obtained according to the mechanism provided for in Paragraph 5 below, in the presence of the members of the Authority, provided that the same expert from the private sector is not used more than three consecutive times, and in compliance with the obligation of non-conflict of interest. In this case, the expert shall prepare his report according to the case and submit it to the Objections Committee.

3- The President shall chair the Objections Authority in addition to all committees and shall direct their meetings and deliberations.

4- The Objections Committees shall examine the complaints submitted before them and shall take their decisions by majority, and they must state the reasons for these decisions, detail their technical and factual elements, and set out the grounds upon which they relied, in accordance with the provisions of Chapter Seven of this Law. Where the assistance of an expert from the private sector is sought and his opinion is departed from by the Committee, it must then state the reasons that led it not to adopt his opinion.

5- The President of the Objections Authority shall obtain, before the month of October of each year, the nominal rosters of experts accompanied by curricula vitae from each of the Beirut Bar Association, the Tripoli Bar Association, the Orders of Engineers and Architects in Beirut and Tripoli, the Lebanese Orders of Physicians in Beirut and Tripoli, the Syndicate of Computer Sciences, the Association of Lebanese Industrialists, the Syndicate of Public Works and Building Contractors, the Order of Pharmacists of Lebanon, the Lebanese Association of Certified Public Accountants, the Federation of Chambers of Commerce, Industry and Agriculture in Lebanon, and other professional syndicates, provided that those persons hold university academic degrees and possess proven experience in their field of specialization, good reputation, and high professional ethics, and he shall select from among them by lot, where necessary, the expert from the private sector according to specialization and the subject-matter of the objection.

6- None of the experts or representatives of the private sector may be selected if it is established that they are being prosecuted or have been convicted of any misdemeanour, felony, or disciplinary penalty, or in the event of a conflict of interest, or if they have been declared bankrupt.

Internal Regulations, Administrative Regulations and Staff Regulations:

The Authority shall establish its internal regulations, its administrative and financial regulations, and the regulations of its staff, after consulting the Civil Service Board and the State Council, within a maximum period of three months from the date of its establishment, provided that they are issued pursuant to decrees adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers, within a maximum period of two months from the date on which the draft decrees are referred to him by the Authority.

Reports:

1- The Authority shall prepare an annual report setting out in its body the matters brought before it, the manner of addressing them, and the proposed recommendations, which shall be duly published, and it shall submit a copy thereof to the Chamber of Deputies, the President of the Court of Audit, the President of the Civil Service Board, the President of the Central Inspection, the President of the Procurement Authority, and the President of the Higher Disciplinary Board.

2- The Authority shall submit periodic reports to the oversight bodies according to the subject matter of the violations, whether financial or functional violations, accompanied by its recommendations.

Confidentiality:

The President and members of the Authority shall abide by maintaining the confidentiality of deliberations in a manner that does not conflict with the provisions of this Law.

First: Formation of Tendering Committees:

1- The tendering committee at the procuring entity shall consist of a chairperson and at least two principal members, and of an alternate chairperson and two alternate members who complete the committee in the absence of the chairperson or one of the members, provided that the number of its members is always odd. Neither the chairperson nor the members shall be in a state of conflict of interest with the participants in the procurement proceedings, and the committee shall act independently from the procuring entity in all its works and decisions.

Tendering committees at the procuring entities shall be formed from persons of experience and competence in accordance with bases established by the Public Procurement Authority, provided that priority in forming these committees is given to persons trained in public procurement.

Second: Functions of the Tendering Committee

1- Tendering committees shall exclusively undertake the examination of pre-qualification files and the opening and evaluation of tenders, and consequently the determination of the most suitable tender.

2- The chairperson of the committee and each of its members shall recuse himself from his duties in the aforementioned committee if he falls into any situation of conflict of interest or expects to fall therein, immediately upon becoming aware of this conflict.

3- The tendering committee may seek the assistance of experts from outside or inside the administration to assist in the technical and financial evaluation when necessary, by a decision of the competent authority at the procuring entity. The selection of experts from outside the administration shall be subject to the provisions of this Law.

Experts shall abide by confidentiality and impartiality in their work, and they shall not have the right to decide in the name of the committee, to participate in its deliberations, or to disclose them publicly, and they may be invited to be heard and to provide explanations by the concerned entities. Experts shall also submit a written report to the committee which shall be mandatorily annexed to the tendering minutes.

4- In the event of divergence of opinions among the members of the committee, decisions shall be taken by a majority of its members, and any dissenting member shall record the reasons for his dissent.

The Right to Object:

1- Every person having standing and interest, including the Public Procurement Authority, shall have the right to object to any measure or express or implied decision taken, adopted or applied by any of the entities concerned with procurement in the stage preceding the entry into force of the contract, which violates the provisions of this Law and the general principles relating to public procurement.

2- The objection shall be against the previously specified decisions, and every person fulfilling the conditions mentioned in the first paragraph of this Article shall be entitled to object in accordance with the following mandatory mechanism:

a- An application for reconsideration pursuant to Article 105 of this Law,

b- A complaint pursuant to Article 106 of this Law,

c- Review of the decisions of the Objections Authority before the State Council.

3- Until the formation of the Authority provided for in this Law, the objection procedures in force before the State Council shall be followed.

Acceptance committees at the procuring entities shall be composed of persons of experience and specialization in accordance with principles set by the Public Procurement Authority, provided that priority in forming these committees is given to persons trained in public procurement.

3- The acceptance committee shall be appointed by a decision of the Director General in public administrations and institutions, by a decision of the deliberative authority in municipalities and other bodies, and it shall differ in its composition and members from the awarding committee and shall not include the persons who participated in supervising the execution or who studied the market or set the estimated value of the procurement. Each committee shall consist of a chairperson and at least two members from within the administration if available, and where that is not possible, from the unified list held by the Public Procurement Authority or from the members of the municipal council in municipalities, provided that they are duly trained in accordance with the provisions of this Law. The inclusion of specialists shall be observed in its composition.

4- Acceptance shall take place in two stages, provisionally and finally, and it may take place at once or in stages, each stage of which covers a part of the contract award.

5- In the provisional acceptance, the committee shall indicate whether the works, supplies or services contracted for have been executed or provided in accordance with the conditions of the contract and the approved offer which has become part of the contract, and whether the contractor has fulfilled all the obligations incumbent upon him, and in the acceptance of supplies, it shall verify that the received items and their numbers conform to the technical conditions and specifications specified in the conditions of the contract and that they are fit and free from defects and their quantities conform to the delivery schedule. The date and hour at which the acceptance operation takes place shall be recorded in the minutes, which shall be signed by the chairperson and members of the committee regardless of how they voted (approval or disapproval), and the final acceptance shall take place after the expiry of the warranty period, pursuant to which the performance guarantee shall be returned to the contractor.

6- The committee shall refuse acceptance if it finds a breach of the conditions of the contract; however, if it deems that the contract has been executed in general in accordance with the provisions of the tender documents with the presence of some minor and non-material deficiencies or defects that do not prevent the use of the supplies, works or services in accordance with the purpose for which the contract was concluded, it may carry out the acceptance provided that it imposes on the contractor penalties proportionate to the deficiencies committed. The details of the application of this paragraph shall be determined in a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of its President and the recommendation of the Public Procurement Authority.

7- The committee may seek the assistance of expertise from outside the administration in the event that the expertise required for the validity of the acceptance is not available in at least one of its members, provided that the provisions of this Law are applied in selecting the expert from outside the administration.

8- The expert shall, in the event of seeking the assistance of external expertise, submit a written report to the acceptance committee.

9- The acceptance committee shall complete its work within the specified time and in accordance with the provisions of this Law and the conditions of the contract, and no legal effects shall arise from any acceptance operation conducted contrary thereto, and a member of the acceptance committee who abstains or fails without a legitimate excuse to perform the obligations incumbent upon him shall be deemed liable for his act and shall be prosecuted professionally and disciplinarily before the competent authorities. Moreover, tacit or de facto acceptance shall not be recognized without minutes duly drawn up showing the accrued rights and their value.

10- The competent authorities are prohibited from paying any amounts accrued as a result of any form of acceptance occurring contrary to this Law.

Effect of the Challenge:

1- The submission of the challenge shall entail a prohibition on signing the contract or framework agreement or putting it into execution before the issuance of final decisions thereon, administratively or judicially, or the expiry of the time-limits set for their issuance, and the procuring entity must comply with this prohibition immediately upon being notified of:

a- The request for reconsideration or the complaint from the Challenges Authority by the method of notification (electronically),

b- Or the petition before the State Council, by any of the methods of notification followed before the said Council.

2- The duration of the prohibition referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article shall end upon the lapse of //5// five working days from the date of notifying the complainant, the petitioner or the procuring entity, as the case may be, and all other participants in the challenge proceedings, of the decision of the procuring entity pursuant to Article 105 or the Challenges Authority pursuant to Article 106.

3- The Challenges Authority or the State Council shall have the right to decide to terminate the prohibition and allow the procuring entity, at its request or sua sponte, to resume the proceedings leading to the signing of the contract or the framework agreement, in exceptional cases justified by urgency and the requirements of the public interest and with the aim of avoiding certain damage that may befall it as a result of suspending the work or delaying the execution of the contract. The decision to lift the prohibition shall be entered in the record of procurement proceedings along with the reasons calling for its adoption, and shall be notified immediately to each of the procuring entity, the complainant and all other participants in the challenge proceedings and in the procurement proceedings.

4- Challenges submitted directly before the State Council regarding explicit or implicit decisions related to procurement proceedings in the pre-contractual stage shall not be admitted.

5- The decision prohibiting the signing of the contract shall remain in effect upon the submission of a petition before the State Council for a period of //7// seven working days from the date of submitting the petition, such that it shall be lifted ipso jure after this period unless the State Council decides to maintain it by an explicit decision.

6- Grounds relating to violations connected with the procurement process which the concerned parties, with the exception of the Public Procurement Authority, have not taken the initiative to raise within the time-limits set forth in the text of this Chapter shall be deemed unavailing, and consequently the said parties may not invoke them subsequently to submit a challenge pursuant to the provisions of this Chapter.

Submission of an application for reconsideration:

1- Any interested party may submit an application for reconsideration regarding a decision or measure taken by the procuring entity in the context of procurement proceedings. Notwithstanding any other provision, applications for reconsideration shall be submitted exclusively before the Complaints Authority provided for in Clause Two of Chapter Six of this Law.

2- The application for reconsideration shall be submitted in writing to the Complaints Authority within the following time periods:

a- Before the final deadline for the submission of tenders if they relate to the conditions of the invitation, pre-qualification, or the decisions or measures taken by the procuring entity in this context;

b- During the standstill period of //10// ten working days which starts from the date of notifying the winning bidder (known as the provisional awardee) in accordance with Paragraph 2 of Article 24 of this Law, if they relate to the other decisions or measures taken by the procuring entity within the framework of the procurement proceedings. In the event that no standstill period is applied, at any time prior to the entry into force of the procurement contract or the framework agreement.

3- The Complaints Authority shall electronically refer the application for reconsideration ipso jure to the procuring entity immediately upon its receipt of this application, and shall also publish a notice in this regard on the central electronic platform at the Public Procurement Authority containing a summary of the application and its grounds.

4- The procuring entity shall issue a decision regarding the application for reconsideration in accordance with Paragraph 5 of this Article within //5// five working days from the date of receiving the electronic referral from the Complaints Committee, and then immediately refer it electronically to the Complaints Authority, which in turn shall notify the decision to the applicant and to all other participants in the complaint proceedings and in the procurement proceedings, within one working day from its receipt of the procuring entity's decision.

5- The procuring entity may, when taking a decision regarding reconsideration, annul any decision or measure it took in the context of the procurement proceedings that are the subject of the application, or correct, amend, or confirm such decision or measure.

6- If the procuring entity does not refer its decision regarding reconsideration to the Complaints Authority in accordance with the requirements of Paragraph 4 of this Article and within the time limit specified therein, this shall be deemed an implicit decision of rejection on its part.

7- All decisions issued by the procuring entity pursuant to the Fifth Paragraph of this Article, with the exception of implicit decisions of rejection, shall be written decisions setting out the measures taken and the reasons calling for taking them. The procuring entity shall include in the record of procurement proceedings provided for in Article 9 of this Law the following:

a- The decisions issued by it;

b- The referral it received from the Complaints Authority pursuant to this Article.

Transparency:

1- Contracting authorities shall pursue a mandatory publication policy pursuant to which they announce their procurement plans and the details of the implementation thereof, including the progress of procurement operations, the procedures for the awarding and conclusion thereof, the result of the receipt and execution thereof, and the final value thereof, in accordance with the provisions of this Law and its implementing decrees.

2- Contracting authorities shall avail themselves, for announcing the aforementioned information, of all publication means available thereto, whether traditional such as the Official Gazette and newspapers, or modern means such as websites, and publication shall be mandatory on the central electronic platform at the Public Procurement Authority, and on the dedicated website of the procuring entity, if any.

3- Nothing shall limit publication except what is confidential by its nature pursuant to Article 6 of this Law.

4- Data relating to public procurement at all levels in accordance with the provisions of this Law shall be collected in a central database established for this purpose at the Public Procurement Authority as part of the central electronic platform. Access thereto shall be available free of charge to citizens and concerned parties, subject to the provisions of Article 6 of this Law.

5- Free access to information relating to public procurement shall be made available through the central electronic platform at the Public Procurement Authority and the dedicated websites of the procuring entities.

Rights of participants in the challenge:

1- Every person having standing and interest shall have the right to submit a challenge pursuant to Article 103 of this Law.

2- Any participant who is duly notified of the proceedings, including pre-qualification proceedings, but fails to participate therein, shall be barred from subsequently challenging, pursuant to Articles 105 and 106 of this Law, the decisions or measures taken by the Authority or by the procuring entity.

3- Subject to the provisions of Article 103 of this Law, the procuring entity shall have the right to participate in the challenge proceedings pursuant to Article 106 of this Law.

4- Participants in the challenge proceedings pursuant to this Law shall have the right to attend all hearings, to be represented therein, to be heard, to submit evidence and proofs by all means of proof, and to request the holding of any adversarial hearing, and they shall have the right of access to the record of the challenge proceedings, subject to the provisions of Article 108 of this Law.

Confidentiality in challenge proceedings:

No information shall be disclosed in the course of challenge proceedings if doing so would jeopardise the security interests of the State or if it would violate the law or impede its enforcement. However, in the event that the information affects the legitimate commercial interests of suppliers or contractors or impedes fair competition, the party requesting confidentiality must submit a request for the approval of the Public Procurement Authority.

Internal Audit:

1- Pursuant to a decision by the head of the administration, one or more employees of the procuring entity shall undertake the task of internal audit for the implementation of all the provisions of this Law and the regulatory decrees and decisions, in proportion to the size of this entity and the number and value of the contracts it concludes.

2- The employees mentioned in the first paragraph of this Article shall immediately notify both the Public Procurement Authority and the competent supervisory bodies of any violations or negligence resulting from the internal audit, and shall deposit a copy with the head of the administration.

3- The standards and procedures established by the Public Procurement Authority shall be followed in the internal audit.

4- The Public Procurement Authority and the procuring entities shall notify the competent supervisory bodies of the violations committed by public officials in order to take the necessary measures in accordance with the laws and regulations in force. Disciplinary and financial prosecutions shall not preclude criminal prosecution before the competent courts.

Integrity:

1- Subject to the provisions of Article 6 of this Law, the procuring entity shall bind all its personnel entrusted with procurement operations to the following:

a- Not to disclose any information or data relating to technical or commercial secrets and the confidential aspects of tenders, which came to their knowledge or which they obtained as a result of performing the tasks entrusted to them.

b- Not to provide information which came to their knowledge or which they obtained as a result of performing the tasks entrusted to them, that constitutes a benefit to third parties and in a manner that violates the principle of fair and equal treatment of all bidders provided for in the First Article of this Law.

2- The employees and personnel of the procuring entity shall abide by the code of conduct provided for in Article 10 of this Law and by ethical and professional standards, and shall refrain from corrupt practices, including by way of example and not limitation fraud, collusion, embezzlement, trading in influence and intimidation, as well as avoiding conflict of interest, as defined in the Second Article of this Law and other relevant laws.

3- The procuring entity shall exclude any of its employees or personnel responsible for evaluating or concluding a procurement contract or monitoring its execution who violated the provisions of this Law from participating in decisions relating to procurement, and shall refer him to the competent authorities to impose the penal and disciplinary sanctions provided for in the relevant laws in force.

4- The procuring entity shall bind its personnel to attend integrity training programmes,

to raise awareness of the risks of lack of integrity, such as corruption, fraud, collusion, and favouring or discriminating against one party over another, and the sanctions associated therewith, and to develop knowledge of the ways to confront these risks and promote a culture of integrity.

5- The procuring entity shall require those dealing with it to abide by the highest standards of professional ethics and good citizenship, especially during the period of procurement and contract execution, under pain of taking exclusion decisions against them in accordance with the provisions of Article 8 of this Law. To fulfil this obligation, bidders and contractors must refrain from the following practices:

a- "Corrupt practice", which means offering, receiving, delivering or soliciting anything of value, whether directly or indirectly, to influence the action of a public official in the procurement process or in contract execution;

b- "Fraudulent practice" leading to the misrepresentation or omission of facts in order to influence a procurement process or contract execution;

c- "Collusive practices" designed to establish any scheme or arrangement between two or more bidders with the aim of submitting prices at artificial and non-competitive levels;

d- "Coercive practices" leading to harming persons in themselves, their families or their property, or threatening to harm them, whether directly or indirectly, to influence their participation in a procurement process or the execution of a procurement contract;

e- Any practice leading to negatively influencing the procurement process and in a manner that violates the principles of this Law.

6- Neither the contractor nor his partners nor his personnel shall be entitled to receive any compensation, commissions, discounts or payments relating to the contract, other than the amounts due under the contract concluded with the procuring entity.

Ongoing files:

Ongoing procurement operations that were announced prior to the entry into force of this Law shall be governed by the laws in force on the date of the announcement of the procurement.

Repeal of conflicting articles:

1- Articles one hundred and twenty-one through one hundred and fifty-one inclusive, and Articles 220, 221 and 233 of the Public Accounting Law put into force by Decree 14969 dated 30/12/1963 and its amendments, are hereby repealed.

2- Article 157 of the Public Accounting Law put into force by Decree 14969 dated 30/12/1963 and its amendments is hereby repealed, in addition to the two decrees relating thereto, which are Decree No. 9333 dated 26/12/2002 relating to the classification of contractors and study offices for participation in the execution of public works contracts, and Decree No. 3688 dated 25/1/1966 relating to determining the conditions for participation in the execution of certain public contracts, and the pre-qualification provided for in Article 19 of this Law shall be adopted.

3- Notwithstanding the provisions of Articles 762 and 809 of the Code of Civil Procedure,

the contracting authority may include in the special conditions of the contract a clause providing that disputes arising from the execution of the contract shall be settled by way of arbitration. The arbitration clause shall not be valid unless authorised by a reasoned decision of the Council of Ministers.

The procedures provided for in the Code of Civil Procedure shall apply to the arbitration in all matters that do not conflict with the foregoing.

4- Articles 22, 23 and 24 of Decree No. 2460 dated 19/11/1959 and its amendments (Organisation of the Central Inspection), as well as Paragraph (c) of Schedule No. (1) annexed to the said Decree, are hereby repealed.

5- Every text contrary to the provisions of this Law or inconsistent with its content is also hereby repealed.

Details of implementation:

The details of implementation of this Law shall be determined, where necessary, by decrees taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the President of the Council of Ministers; however, the implementation of this Law may not be suspended pending the issuance of these decrees, and pending their issuance, the implementing regulations and decisions in force and issued in implementation of the Public Accounting Law shall be temporarily adopted and shall remain valid and in effect to the extent that they do not conflict with this Law and its implementing decrees.

Entry into force of the Law:

This Law shall be published in the Official Gazette and shall enter into force twelve months after the date of its publication.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The text of Article 66 (Sustainable Building) of Law No. 144/2019 (General Budget and Annexed Budgets for the year 2019) shall be repealed and replaced by the following text:

"New Article 66:

First: In zones where the number of storeys and height are specified

A - In unbuilt real properties, it is permitted to license an additional storey with a pitched roof not included in the general exploitation factor and the number of storeys and heights permitted in the zone, subject to the following conditions:

1- The clear height of the pitched-roof storey shall not exceed one metre and eighty centimetres (1.80m) at the edge of the storey and four metres and a half (4.5m) as the maximum clear height, provided that the roof pitch is not less than twenty-five degrees (25 degrees).

2- The roof of the pitched storey shall be completely covered with tiles or other materials to be specified by the Higher Council for Urban Planning, and shall include no less than fifteen per cent (15%) of the area of the pitched storey in solar panels for generating energy fully integrated with the cladding materials. The external building structure erected pursuant to this amendment shall be considered an integrated unit with respect to the cladding and facing materials used on the exterior, both in the vertical sections, if any, and the pitched sections.

3- The area allocated for common services shall not be less than fifteen per cent (15%) of the roof area with a minimum of thirty-five square metres (35m2), and shall be completely covered by the same cladding materials and/or solar panels, and independent access thereto shall be secured.

B - In built real properties subdivided into different rights, the following documents must be attached to the licensing file:

1- The approval of all owners of rights for the added construction and the area allocated for common services, executed before a notary public.

2- A duly issued certificate attesting to the load-bearing capacity of the existing building for the requested additions, in accordance with the conditions of the Public Safety Decree from the structural standpoint.

3- The clear height of the pitched-roof storey shall not exceed one metre and eighty centimetres (1.80 m) at the edge of the storey four metres and a half (4.5 m) as the maximum clear height, provided that the roof pitch is not less than twenty-five degrees (25 degrees).

4- The roof of the pitched storey shall be completely covered with tiles or other materials to be specified by the Higher Council for Urban Planning, and shall include no less than fifteen per cent (15%) of the area of the pitched storey in solar panels for generating energy fully integrated with the cladding materials. The external building structure erected pursuant to this amendment shall be considered an integrated unit with respect to the cladding and facing materials used on the exterior, both in the vertical sections, if any, and the pitched sections.

5- The area allocated for common services shall not be less than fifteen per cent (15%) of the roof area with a minimum of thirty-five square metres (35m2) and shall be completely covered by the same cladding materials and/or solar panels, and independent access thereto shall be secured.

Second: In zones where the number of storeys and height are not specified

A- An increase of (0.25) % may be added exclusively to the general exploitation factor.

B- In built real properties subdivided into different rights, only one storey may be added provided that the increase in the general exploitation factor does not exceed (0.25) %, and the following documents must be attached to the licensing file:

1- The approval of all owners of rights for the added construction and the area allocated for common services, executed before a notary public.

2- A duly issued certificate, attesting to the load-bearing capacity of the existing building for the requested additions, in accordance with the conditions of the Public Safety Decree from the structural standpoint.

C- The area allocated for common services must not be less than fifteen per cent (15%) of the roof area with a minimum of thirty-five square metres (35m2), and shall be completely covered by the same cladding materials and/or solar panels, and independent access thereto shall be secured.

D- The roof of the top storey shall be completely covered with materials to be specified by the Higher Council for Urban Planning, and the roof of the storey shall include no less than fifteen per cent (15%) of the area of the storey in solar panels for generating energy fully integrated with the cladding materials and the provision of a garden at a rate of no less than forty per cent (40%) of the area of the top roof. The external building structure erected pursuant to this amendment shall be considered an integrated unit with respect to the cladding and facing materials used on the exterior, both in the vertical sections, if any, and the pitched sections.

Third: In unbuilt real properties, license applicants wishing to benefit from the provisions of this Law must, in addition to what is set forth in paragraphs (First) and (Second), fulfil the following conditions:

A- Installing a wastewater treatment plant.

B- Securing tanks for collecting and treating water at a rate of at least five cubic metres (5 m3) for each residential apartment.

Fourth: The following zones shall be exempted from the provisions of this Article:

A- Zones where the building conditions impose special requirements for the shape of the tiled gable roof.

B- Zones designated for villas and private housing.
