C- Buildings that have been subject to laws on the settlement of building violations.

D- All buildings that have benefited from exceptional laws regarding heights or number of storeys.

E- Easement zones whose regulations include special detailed maps in which the building regulations are specified.

Fifth: Owners of the real property who wish to benefit from the provisions of this Article must pay a fee equivalent to:

- Thirty per cent (30%) of the value of the notional land required to secure the area of the storey mentioned above when the general exploitation factor does not exceed one (1) after the increase.

- Forty per cent (40%) when the general exploitation factor after the increase is higher than one (1) and does not exceed two (2).

- Fifty per cent (50%) when the general exploitation factor after the increase is higher than two (2).

The committees accredited to appraise the selling price per square metre for granting building permits shall appraise the price per square metre to determine the fees due.

Sixth: The revenues collected pursuant to this Article shall be distributed as follows:

- Thirty-five per cent (35 %) of the fees to the account of the Central Treasury Fund.

- Thirty per cent (30 %) of the fees to the account of the Public Corporation for Housing.

- Thirty-five per cent (35 %) of the fees to the account of the municipality concerned.

Seventh: The implementing decrees for this Law shall be issued where necessary, upon the proposal of the Minister of Public Works and Transport.

Exceptions:

1 - Exempted from the provisions of the First Article are Palestinians born on Lebanese territory and officially registered in the records of the Lebanese Ministry of Interior

and Municipalities, a foreign national whose mother is Lebanese or who is married to a Lebanese woman, and persons born in Lebanon who hold an unregistered status card, subject to compliance with the special conditions governing professions regulated by law.

2 - It pertains to the Minister to grant a work permit to a foreign worker of the Third Category, as an exception to the principle of restricting professions to Lebanese nationals, in the event that no Lebanese national is available, provided that the ratios of foreign workers to Lebanese nationals are observed, such that the general ratio in all establishments and businesses mentioned by way of example shall be three Lebanese nationals for every foreign national; exempted from this ratio are: restaurants, where the ratio shall be five Lebanese nationals for every foreign national, and establishments that employ cleaning workers or delivery workers, or washing and lubrication works and bakeries, where the ratio shall be one Lebanese national for every foreign national. As for establishments that undertake construction works, the ratio shall be one Lebanese national for every three foreign nationals.

3 - The Minister may also grant an exception to a company or establishment to bring in foreign nationals, provided that the justification of the application is based on serious and convincing grounds.

In implementation of Article 74 of Law No. 220 dated 29/5/2000 (concerning the rights of persons with disabilities), employers in the private sector where the number of employees is not less than thirty (30) and does not exceed sixty (60) are obliged to employ one employee from among persons with disabilities who possesses the required qualifications. Where the number of employees in the establishment exceeds sixty employees, the employer or the establishment is obliged to employ persons with disabilities at a rate of at least three per cent (3%) of its employees who possess the required qualifications. The National Social Security Fund shall verify the proper implementation of the employers' obligation to employ persons with disabilities, and it must refrain from issuing a clearance certificate to a violating employer.
Prior approval and renewal of a work permit may not be granted to foreign employers where this would lead to circumvention of this Decision.

The profession of the foreign national shall be specified in the application in a clear manner that does not admit of interpretation in more than one way, and any application containing the word expert, technician, coordinator, specialist consultant, specialist, and similar ambiguous terms shall be rejected, such that the type of expertise, coordination, technical or consultancy work, or specialization that is the subject of the work permit must be specified.

The following professions and occupations shall be deemed among the occupations and professions that the Ministry of Labour sees a necessity to restrict to Lebanese nationals only:

1 - All occupations, whatever their nature, at public administrations, public institutions, and municipalities.

2 - Professions regulated by law, the right to practise which is restricted to members affiliated with the syndicate of the profession and after obtaining a licence from the competent authority when required (such as: the legal profession, engineering, medicine, pharmacy, topography).

3 - All commercial occupations, import, export, and wholesale or retail sale of all types of goods and merchandise.

4 - Occupations connected to tourism professions of all types (establishments prepared for accommodation, establishments prepared for serving food and drink, establishments that exploit equipment and constructions of a touristic nature or for touristic purposes, bodies organizing touristic festivals, travel and tourism agencies and touristic transport) such that the practice of tourism professions is restricted to Lebanese nationals, particularly: manager of a touristic establishment, receptionist, room attendant, cook, chef, commis chef, chef and assistant chef specializing in Arabic cuisine, dining hall attendant, maintenance and equipment of touristic establishments, lifeguard, supervisor, and instructor of touristic activities (swimming, skiing)..., swimming pool attendant, tour guide, driver of touristic buses or cars, and other related professions.

5 - All occupations, whatever their nature, in the banking, financial, and accounting sector and the insurance sector.

6 - Administrative occupations in all their forms, whatever the establishment or company, including: Chairman of the Board of Directors, director, deputy director, head of the personnel department, treasurer, accountant, secretary, clerk, documentarian, archivist - commercial representative, marketing representative, works supervisor, operations supervisor, warehouse keeper, data entry clerk, clerk, inspector, purchasing officer, quality control, sales manager, public relations, archive.

7- Occupations connected to the health sector: all occupations in pharmacies and drug warehouses, laboratories, clinics, radiology centres, hospitals, medical eyewear shops, medical equipment, cosmetics centres, nutritional supplements, psychotherapy, and nursing work of all types.

8 - Occupations connected to educational professions in pre-university, vocational, and technical education, including: instructor or teacher, with the exception of teaching foreign languages when necessary, researcher, proctor, principal, library management, book coordination, nursery, and other occupations.

9 - Occupations related to media and advertising: advertisement design, promotion, publicity, public relations, broadcaster, journalist and media professional with the exception of a correspondent, programme presenter, producer, director, caricaturist, editor, programme preparer, screenwriter, writer, and similar occupations.

10 - In the construction and works sector: trade and manufacture of building materials, surveying, land measurement, mapping, and clearance of construction transactions, electrical installations and the industry of installing and maintaining electrical networks and lighting, installation of gypsum, aluminium, iron, wood, decoration, and sanitary ware, and all occupations related to construction works and the supervision, execution, follow-up, and management thereof, unless the employer is a company and the workers are registered in the name of the company and within the proportions prescribed in the regulations in force.

11 - Craft professions not regulated by law, whether a professional syndicate exists or does not exist, particularly and by way of example:

- Manufacture and sale of jewellery of all types, including precious stones.

- Tailoring, fashion design, darning and repairing clothes, knitting and embroidery, and the manufacture of and trade in clothes.

- Ironing and washing clothes.

- Women's and men's hairdressing salons, grooming, beautification, makeup, and all professions connected to grooming and beautification work.

- Printing, bookbinding, and publishing work.

- Butchery work and the manufacture, sale, and cooking of meats of all types.

- Sea fishing work and the manufacture of and trade in all marine products

- Manufacture of Oriental and Western sweets and the sale of and trade in the same.

- Manufacture, sale, and trading of vegetables and fruits and the cooking thereof, and all types of food including pastries, whether in the form of manakish, pizza, pies, sfiha, or otherwise.

- Manufacture of and trade in dairy products, cheeses, and all milk derivatives.

- Processing of nuts, dried fruits, coffee, and tea, and the sale of and trading in the same.

- Mechanics, bodywork, painting, electrical work, tyres, and oil change for cars and all mobile vehicles.

- At fuel stations, the work of filling petrol and diesel and changing oil.

- Wrought iron smithery work of all types and painting.

- Manufacture, upholstery, and trading of furniture and furniture painting.

- Photography or videography, design of photographs and films, and all occupations related to the photography sector and artistic production.

- Bookshop work, sale of stationery and books, and photocopying of books and documents.

- Electronic occupations: maintenance, repair, programming, sale, and trade of: cellular, electrical, and telephone devices of all types, air conditioners, machines of all types, and computers.

- Maintenance, repair, operation, programming, and installation of internet networks, and programming, including the programming and management of websites, working in internet distribution companies and internet service companies, and all occupations connected to this sector.

- Maintenance of electricity generators, collection of subscription bills, and electrical technicians.

12 - Service professions: usher, guard and private security, driver, delivery worker (Delivery), receptionist and customer service worker, watchman, bakery workers, salespersons in department stores and supermarkets, factory workers, and cleaning workers in universities, hospitals, schools, and hotels.

13 - In general, all occupations and professions for which Lebanese workers are available to fill.

The list of professions that foreigners are entitled to practise, posted on the electronic website of the Ministry and notified to General Security, is hereby repealed and shall be deemed null and void, and relying upon it or applying it is prohibited. The category to which the worker belongs shall be specified in the permit and the initial approval.

The decision licensing the practice of the profession for the permit applicant or for the establishment in which he works, in the event that the regulations require obtaining a licence to practise a profession, shall mandatorily be joined to the file of the application for a work permit or for an initial or prior approval, for example:

1 - For a tourism company or establishment (of all its classes): the decision licensing the establishment and operation of the tourism establishment from the Ministry of Tourism (pursuant to the provisions of Decree No. 15598 dated 21/9/1970 )determining the general conditions for the establishment and operation of tourism establishments and its amendments).

2 - For a massage centre: the licence granted pursuant to the urgent draft law promulgated by virtue of Decree No. 9827 dated 22/6/1962 (relating to medical massage and beauty care) and holding the approval of the Governor as to the centre's fulfilment of the conditions of health, public safety, and public morals.

3 - For associations and sports clubs: the notice or decision of incorporation of the association or club.

4 - For classified establishments: the decision licensing the practice of the profession issued by the Governor or the Qaemقام (District Commissioner).

5 - For factories: the decision licensing the establishment of a factory from the Ministry of Industry.

6 - Beauty centres and hairdressing and styling salons: presentation of a health certificate and an attestation of compliance with the condition of distance between salons specified in the internal regulations of the syndicate.
The initial or prior approval is personal such that it cannot be assigned to a third party.

Reconsideration must be reasoned and substantiated by documents, and shall be submitted to the Minister accompanied by the opinion of the competent department regarding the legality of the application, its fulfilment of the regulatory conditions, and the justifications for granting it.

The work permit and the prior approval are declaratory decisions the effect of which is limited to the conformity of the status of the holder thereof with the laws and regulations in force. The applicant shall bear responsibility for the accuracy of the declarations, and in the event of a violation, the permit or prior approval shall be withdrawn and the penalties prescribed in the regulations in force shall be applied to the violator and the applicant.
Every violation of the provisions of this Decision shall subject the violator to accountability.
Every text contrary to the provisions of this Decision is hereby repealed.
This Decision shall be published in the Official Gazette and shall enter into force from the date of its publication.

The figures of the General Budget for the financial year beginning on the first of January 2022 and ending on 31 December 2022 shall be determined in accordance with the provisions of the second and third Articles of this Law.

Appropriations:

In accordance with Schedule No. (1) annexed to this Law:

Revenues:

The revenues of the General Budget are estimated as follows:

In accordance with Schedule No. (2) annexed to this Law

Authorisation of collection:

It is authorised, in accordance with the provisions of this Law and the provisions of the laws in force, to collect the various taxes, duties, proceeds and revenues set forth in Schedule No. (2) annexed to this Law.

Authorisation to borrow:

1- The Government is authorised, within the framework of financing the maturities of the principal of debts and within the limits of the estimated deficit in the execution of the budget and in the expenditure of appropriations carried forward to the year 2022 and additional appropriations, to issue Treasury bonds in Lebanese currency for short, medium and long terms, pursuant to decisions issued by the Minister of Finance.

2- The Government shall inform the Chamber of Deputies quarterly of:

- The deficit realised in the execution of the budget and the Treasury,

- The expenditure of carried-forward and additional appropriations,

- The instalments of internal and external debts that have been settled,

- The result of issuing the Treasury bonds in Lebanese currency authorised to be issued pursuant to the first paragraph of this Article, as well as in foreign currencies authorised by special laws,

- Treasury advances.

Loan accounts:

1- Special Treasury accounts shall be opened for loans pursuant to decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance and the competent Minister, to which shall be credited the amounts received on account of these loans and to which shall be debited the amounts paid in settlement of due instalments and bonds.

2- Commitment and payment appropriations shall be opened in the General Budget for loans adopted by the State or contracted for its account.

Determining the procedures for spending grants and external loans:

1- In accordance with the provisions of Article 52 of the Public Accounting Law and its amendments or Article 52 of the Constitution, grants and external loans offered to each of the public administrations, public institutions, and autonomous services of all types, and to councils, bodies, and funds regardless of their designation, and to municipalities and unions of municipalities, and to all other institutions and bodies that manage public utilities shall be accepted, and expenditure from cash grants and from loans, whether from the local part or from the foreign part, shall be subject to the oversight of the Court of Accounts in accordance with the established procedures.

2- The provisions of the second paragraph of Article 27 of the draft law put into effect pursuant to Decree No. 14969 issued on 30/12/1963 shall not apply to supplementary appropriations related to cash grants, as these appropriations may be transferred from one item to another by a decision of the competent minister and the Minister of Finance after the endorsement of the Central Controller of Expenditure Commitment and after the concerned administration proves the desire of the donor entity to make this transfer.

3- The provisions of Article 104 of the draft law put into effect pursuant to Decree No. 14969 dated 30/12/1963 and its amendments, the Public Accounting Law, shall apply to emergency financial advances granted in payment of expenditures financed from cash grants.

Appropriations reserved for emergency financial advances related to grants given during a specific financial year to perform obligations the execution of which exceeds the year in payment of expenditures financed from these grants may be carried over, until the completion of the execution of the works related to the grant, to the budgets of subsequent financial years.

4- All balances of uncommitted appropriations financed from cash grants and loans shall be carried over to the budgets of subsequent years.

Opening exceptional appropriations:

In implementation of the provisions of Article 85 of the Constitution, the President of the Republic may, if emergency circumstances call for urgent expenditures, issue a decree based on a decision issued by the Council of Ministers to open exceptional or supplementary appropriations or to transfer appropriations in the budget of the year 2022, provided that these appropriations do not exceed three hundred billion Lebanese Pounds, and these measures must be submitted for the approval of the Chamber of Deputies at the first session in which it convenes thereafter.

Chapter Three

Tax Amendments.

Article Nineteen Payment of taxes and fees collected in foreign currencies

Wherever the phrase "fees and taxes collected in US Dollars or in any foreign currency" appears in this Law, they shall be deposited in the same currency in cash into the special account at the Bank of Lebanon.

Payment by instalments of taxes and fees due from public law persons with their exemption from the due assessment and collection fines

Notwithstanding any other text, exceptionally and for one time only, municipalities, union of municipalities, public institutions and all other public law persons upon whom obligations are due in favour of the Treasury resulting from violations relating to all taxes and fees assessed and collected by the Directorate of Public Finance and the fines resulting from their occupancy of public State property may pay these obligations and fines by instalments for a period of three years years without any interest, with their exemption from the due assessment and collection fines

Those persons wishing to benefit from this payment by instalments must submit a written application and pay the first instalment within a maximum time limit of. 31/12/2022

In the event of default in paying the instalment of two consecutive months on their due dates or failure to benefit from the provisions of this Article, interest shall be calculated on the due amounts at a rate equal to the interest of Treasury bonds for a period of one year, and the amounts shall be deducted as follows:

With respect to municipalities and unions of municipalities: from the habits of the Independent Municipal Fund that become due to them starting from 1/1/2023

With respect to public institutions and all other public law persons: from the contribution that that becomes due to them starting from 1/1/2023

The details of application of this Article shall be determined, where necessary, pursuant to a decision issued by the Ministers of Finance and of Interior and Municipalities.

Effecting a settlement on unpaid assessments relating to income tax and value added tax submitted before the Objection Committees.

Notwithstanding any text, and on an exceptional basis, unpaid assessments relating to income tax and value added tax for the operations of 2020 and prior years objected to before the Objection Committees and which have not been adjudicated up to 31/3/2008 shall be settled.

The value of the settlement shall be fixed at 50 per cent of the value of the objected taxes only, excluding the assessment and collection penalties that were due.

In order to benefit from this settlement, the taxpayer must submit a written application to the competent tax administration and pay the amount falling due on him as a result of the settlement in full within a period not exceeding three months from the date of publication of this Law.

The taxpayer may not choose to benefit from the settlement in respect of a part of a single assessment issued by the tax administration, such that the settlement shall cover all objected points and periods within the single assessment.

Related text: Determining the implementing details of the provisions of Article 21 of Law Put into Effect by Operation of Law No. 10 dated 15/11/2022 (the Public Budget Law for the Year 2022) regarding effecting a settlement on assessments relating to income tax and value added tax submitted before the Objection Committees

The Objection Committees notified by the tax administration of the taxpayer's application to effect the settlement shall cease to adjudicate the objection.

Taxpayers who paid the tax due on them in instalments prior to the date of publication of this Law without all instalments having been paid, and taxpayers who benefited from the provisions of Article 40 of Law No. 66 dated 3/11/2017 (the Public Budget and Annexed Budgets Law for the Year 2017) or the provisions of Article 29 of Law No. 79 dated 18/4/2018 (the Public Budget and Annexed Budgets Law for the Year 2018) or the provisions of Article 41 of Law No. 144 dated 31/7/2019 (the Public Budget and Annexed Budgets Law for the Year 2019) or the provisions of Article 28 of Law Put into Effect by Operation of Law No. 6 issued on 5/3/2020 (the Public Budget and Annexed Budgets Law for the Year 2020), may benefit from the provisions of this Article in accordance with the following:

"The value of the settlement shall be fixed at fifty per cent of the value of the objected taxes after deducting the paid part of the tax only".

Amendment of Law No. 662 dated 4/2/2005 (Determining the principles for the settlement of fines imposed pursuant to the tax laws).

Law No. 662 dated 4/2/2005 (Determining the principles for the settlement of fines imposed pursuant to the tax laws) is hereby amended to read as follows:

Article One:

1- Taxpayers liable for taxes and fees assessed and collected by the Directorate of Public Finance at the Ministry of Finance pursuant to the laws on direct and indirect taxes and fees shall be granted a period of six months from the date of publication of this Law to pay in full the taxes and fees, whether due by way of self-assessment or by way of assessments issued by the tax administration, on a date prior to its publication, with a reduction of:

- 100% of the fines resulting from violations committed during the period from 18/10/2019 until the publication of this Law.

- 90% in respect of the fines resulting from violations committed on a date prior to 18/10/2019.

2- In the event of failure to record those taxes and fees and the reduced fines due thereon within the period specified above, the taxpayers shall be obliged to pay them with the full fines, and no settlement may be conducted thereon.

3- The Minister of Finance may conduct a settlement on the fines assessed and collected by the Directorate of Public Finance at the Ministry of Finance, pursuant to the laws on direct and indirect taxes and fees,

due on the taxes and fees issued on a date subsequent to the publication of this Law, provided that the provisions of the settlement and the prescribed percentage for the reduction of each type of fine are determined pursuant to a regulatory decision issued by him within a maximum limit for the reduction not exceeding the following percentages:

- 85% of assessment fines.

- 75% of the collection fines.

- 60% of the fines set in lump-sum amounts.

In all cases, the reduced fine may not be less than two hundred thousand Lebanese pounds.

Article Two: Excluded from the settlement referred to in Item 3 of Article One of this Law are:

a- The fine resulting from the repetition of the violation.

b- The fine the settlement of which is subject to special legal provisions.

c- The fine the settlement of which the legal provisions have not authorised.

d- The fine the value of which is less than two hundred thousand Lebanese pounds.

Article Three: Without prejudice to the provisions of Article One of this Law, the authorisation for the settlement of any fine for which the reduction exceeds the amount of five billion Lebanese pounds shall be conditional upon the approval of the Council of Ministers

Article Four: Article 39 of Law No. 490 dated 15/2/1996, (the General Budget Law for the year 1996 amended pursuant to Article 33 of Law No. 622 dated 7/3/1997, is hereby repealed.

Article Five: This text shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

to read as follows:

In the event that the funds resulting from exportation are transferred to banks operating in Lebanon to invest them in Lebanon or in the event of proving their use in full for the purposes of the industrial activity practiced in Lebanon.

The following text is added to Article 16 of Legislative Decree 144 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Income Tax Law):

The deficit incurred during the year 2020 may be carried forward for an additional year.

Granting start-up companies (start up company). A tax deduction on the income tax on profits for a period of five years.

Notwithstanding any other text, start-up companies (start up company). that are established within five years from the date of publication of this Law shall benefit from a tax deduction equal to the full income tax on profits (Title One tax) for a period of five years starting from the date of their establishment, provided that at least 80% of their employees are Lebanese.

Granting awards to industrial and commercial companies and establishments established from the date of publication of this Law up to 31/12/2024 in regions that the Government wishes to develop.

Industrial and commercial companies and establishments established from the date of publication of this Law up to 31/12/2024 and carrying out their principal activity in the regions that the Government wishes to develop shall benefit from a tax deduction equivalent to the full tax on profits for a period of seven years starting from the date of carrying out their actual activity. The registration fees of their vehicles and the annual road traffic fees due on such vehicles shall also be reduced by 50% throughout the seven-year period. Furthermore, the buildings erected and used for carrying out their activity shall be exempted from the building fee.

In order to benefit from this tax deduction, it is required that the value of the invested capital be not less than one million US dollars transferred from abroad or paid in cash, and that they employ Lebanese labour of not less than fifty Lebanese nationals and at a rate of 60% of the total of their employees.

Amendment of Article 31 of the Income Tax Law (Legislative Decree No. 1959/144 and its amendments).

Article 31 of the Income Tax Law (Legislative Decree No. 1959/144 and its amendments) is amended to read as follows:

The tax is imposed on the actual or lump-sum determined profit after deducting therefrom, for each natural person among the taxpayers, an amount of /37.500.000/ L.L. thirty-seven million five hundred thousand Lebanese pounds, and to this deduction is added an amount of an amount of /12.500.000/ L.L. twelve million five hundred thousand Lebanese pounds for the married taxpayer and /2.500.000/ L.L. two million five hundred thousand Lebanese pounds for each legitimate child still dependent on him under the following conditions:

- For males if they have not exceeded the age of eighteen, or up to twenty-five at a maximum for those pursuing university studies.

- For males afflicted with a disabling infirmity and who do not perform remunerated work, provided that the disabling infirmity is proven pursuant to a certificate issued by the Ministry of Social Affairs proving special needs.

- For females prior to their marriage, or if they are widows or divorced, provided that the number of benefitting children does not exceed five.

- In the event that each of the spouses practices a profession or holds a post, each of them benefits from the deduction effected for a single person, and if the spouses have children dependent on them, the spouses benefit equally in halves between them and on an equal footing in accordance with the provisions of the first paragraph of this Article. In the case of legal separation (desertion, annulment of marriage, or divorce) between the spouses, the spouse obligated to pay maintenance benefits.

- If the father does not engage in remunerated work and his wife practices a profession or holds a post subject to the tax. The wife benefits, in addition to the deduction granted to a single person, from the full deduction for the spouse as well as from the full deduction for the children in accordance with the provisions of the first paragraph of this Article.

- If the child does not engage in remunerated work and his wife practices a profession or holds a post subject to the tax, the wife benefits, in addition to the deduction granted to a single person, from the full deduction for the spouse as well as from the full deduction for the children in accordance with the provisions of the first paragraph of this Article

The provisions of this Article apply with effect from 1/1/2022.

Conducting an exceptional revaluation of fixed assets for income tax taxpayers and of real properties covered by the provisions of Item (c) of Thirdly of Article 45 of the Income Tax Law as amended by Article 13 of Law No. 64 dated 30/12/2017.

1- An exceptional revaluation of fixed assets for income tax taxpayers and of real properties covered by the provisions of Item (c) of Thirdly of Article 45 of the Income Tax Law as amended by Article 13 of Law No. 64 dated 30/12/2017 may be conducted in accordance with the following:

a- Conducting an exceptional revaluation of fixed assets for income tax taxpayers:

Natural and legal persons obliged to keep regular accounting pursuant to legal or regulatory texts may, once only and within a time limit ending on 31/12/2022, conduct an exceptional revaluation of fixed asset items (including shares, debt securities, bonds, participation shares, real properties and other fixed assets) in order to correct the effects of monetary inflation resulting from the change in the values of those assets.

The revaluation operation shall cover all the assets referred to in the preceding paragraph and recorded in the entries of the enterprise on a date prior to the first of January 2020, provided that the value of the revalued assets does not exceed the market price on the date of conducting the revaluation operation.

The revaluation operation shall be conducted by one of the sworn appraisal experts in Lebanon with respect to real properties that constitute fixed assets, and by one of the experts affiliated with the Lebanese Association of Certified Public Accountants with respect to the remaining assets, chosen by the concerned party.

The positive differences resulting from the revaluation operation shall be subject to a new proportional tax at a rate of 5% (five percent) of the value of these differences

Taxpayers assessed on the basis of lump-sum or estimated profit shall benefit from the revaluation set forth in this Article if the existence of documents permitting the revaluation of fixed asset items is established

In all cases, with respect to banks, these provisions may not conflict with the Code of Money and Credit and all other regulatory and implementing texts issued by the Banque du Liban.

In the event of the disposal of any of the assets revalued in accordance with the provisions of this paragraph before the lapse of three years from the date of revaluation, the appraisal profit shall be calculated as the difference between the disposal value of the asset and its value prior to its revaluation.

b-. Conducting an exceptional revaluation of real properties covered by the provisions of Item (c) of Thirdly of Article 45 of the Income Tax Law as amended by Article 13 of Law No. 64 dated 30/12/2017.:

Natural and legal persons referred to in Item "c" of Article Thirteen of Law No. 64 dated 20/10/2017 may, once only within a time limit ending on 31/12/2020, conduct an exceptional revaluation of the real properties they own

The revaluation operation shall be conducted by one of the experts affiliated with the Syndicate of Appraisal Experts in Lebanon chosen by the concerned party

The positive differences resulting from the revaluation operation shall be subject to a new proportional tax at a rate of 3% 3(three percent) of the value of those differences

The tax on the positive differences resulting from the revaluation operation shall be paid in cash concurrently with the submission of the application for approval of the revaluation to the tax administration.

The competent financial unit shall decide on the revaluation operation, and if it refuses to approve its result or amends this result, it must notify the concerned parties of its decision of refusal or amendment, and they shall have the right to object before the competent Income Tax Objections Committee in accordance with the procedures provided for in the Tax Procedures Law.

2- The concerned parties referred to in Paragraphs "a" and "b" above shall pay the tax difference resulting from the introduction of an increase to the valuation result within a time limit of two months from their notification of the administration's decision, under penalty of the accrual of interest at a rate equivalent to the interest rate on five-year treasury bonds until payment; they may also recover the tax due to them in the event of a reduction of the valuation pursuant to a written application submitted by them to the competent financial unit.

3- The time limit granted for conducting a revaluation operation may be extended twice only, each time for a period of six months, pursuant to a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

4- Where necessary, the procedures for applying this Article shall be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

Clause 5 shall be added to Article 73 of Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Income Tax Law)

Clause 5 shall be added to Article 73 of Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Income Tax Law) so as to read as follows:

The gain from the assignment of shares realised by natural persons upon assigning their shares in any of the following joint-stock companies shall be subject to a tax equivalent to the real estate conveyance and transfer fee:

- Companies whose sole or main object is the ownership of built and unbuilt real estate.

- Companies that engage in the trade of built unbuilt real estate or in real estate development activity.

- Companies in which the value of their fixed assets consisting of real estate exceeds 50% of their total fixed assets.

The taxable gain shall be determined as the difference between the cost of acquiring the share and the actual price of its assignment.

The assignor shall benefit from a tax deduction at a rate of 50% when the assignment takes place among the shareholders themselves or between ascendants and descendants.

The gain realised by such persons upon assigning their shares in the remaining joint-stock companies shall be exempted from the tax.

Any shareholder may carry out an exceptional revaluation of his shares once and within a time limit ending on 30/6/2023.

The revaluation operation shall be carried out by one of the experts affiliated with the Lebanese Association of Certified Public Accountants.

The positive differences resulting from the revaluation operation shall be subject to a new proportional tax at a rate of 1% (one percent) of the value of these differences.

The assignor must, within a time limit of two months from the date of the assignment, declare the assignment operation and pay the tax due in accordance with special forms prepared by the Ministry of Finance for this purpose, and the assignor and the assignee shall be jointly and severally liable for the payment of the tax incurred on the assignment operation.

Where necessary, the details for the application of this Article shall be determined pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

Amendment of Article 20 of Legislative Decree No. 67 dated 5/8/1967 (Fiscal Stamp Duty Law)

Article 20 of Legislative Decree No. 67 dated 5/8/1967 (Fiscal Stamp Duty Law) is amended to read as follows:

Article 20: The fiscal stamp duty shall be paid by one of the following methods:

- By way of affixing fiscal stamps specially prepared for this purpose, provided that the value of the duty payable on the deed or writing does not exceed 500,000 L.L., and with the exception of cases in which the law explicitly provides for the adoption of another method for settling the duty.

- By means of stamping machines held by persons licensed to use them in accordance with the provisions of this Law, provided that the value of the duty does not exceed 500.000.000 L.L..

- In cash or pursuant to a banker's cheque before Notaries Public in respect of deeds and instruments that they draw up or authenticate, regardless of the value of the duty, provided that the value of the fiscal duty is included within the receipt issued by the Notary Public.

- In cash or pursuant to a banker's cheque at the public finance cash offices if the value of the duty exceeds 500,000 Lebanese Pounds, pursuant to collection orders issued by the competent finance departments in the governorates, or by the Real Estate Registries that heard the contract including the auxiliary real estate offices, or by the regional accountants in the districts, or by the Vehicles and Machinery Registration Service that heard the contract of sale including the offices affiliated with the Service, provided that the fiscal stamp duty is included within the collection order drawn up to levy registration fees, traffic fees, and work permit fees.

- Pursuant to payment notices adopted by the Ministry of Finance.

- Pursuant to an electronic fiscal stamp e-stamp in accordance with the methods and mechanisms adopted by the Ministry of Finance.

The detailed rules for the implementation of this Article shall be determined, where necessary, pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

Amendment of Article 36 of the Built Property Tax Law dated 17/6/1962 and its amendments.

Article /23/ of Law No. 44 dated 11/11/2008 and its amendments (Tax Procedures Law) is amended to read as follows:

New Article 23:

Cooperation between the Various Public and Private Administrations and the Concerned Entities

1- Every person, including government administrations, legal persons of a public character, public institutions, municipalities, and unions of municipalities, in addition to the various private sector bodies and syndicates, shall provide the tax administration with any information it requests, including information protected by banking secrecy, in order for it to perform its duties, including tax audit operations or measures aimed at enhancing tax compliance and detecting tax evasion.

2- The mechanism for requesting information from banks and the scope thereof shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

3- No one may invoke professional secrecy to prevent the employees of the tax administration from reviewing the accounting registers and documents that allow verifying the extent of taxpayers' compliance with their tax obligations, or that enable them to respond to requests for information received by the tax administration pursuant to double taxation avoidance agreements.

4- The employees of the tax administration shall be bound by professional secrecy with respect to the information they obtain in their aforementioned capacity. Such information may only be used for the purposes for which it was obtained, under penalty of administrative, civil, and criminal prosecution in accordance with the laws in force.

5 - The Public Prosecutions shall refer to the tax administration through the Ministry of Justice any information arising in lawsuits brought before the courts that involve suspicions that a taxpayer has defrauded or attempted to defraud the financial departments in relation to all taxes and fees, whether the lawsuit is civil, commercial, or criminal, with the exception of lawsuits or indictments that ended in a dismissal of proceedings.

First: Articles /1/, /2/, /7/ and /8/ of the Law issued on 3/9/1956 relating to Banking Secrecy are amended so as to read as follows:

New Article /1/:

Banks established in Lebanon in the form of joint-stock companies and banks that are branches of foreign companies shall be subject to professional secrecy.

The Agricultural, Industrial and Real Estate Credit Bank shall be exempted from the provisions of this Law.

New Article /2/:

a - The managers and employees of the banks referred to in Article One, and any person who, by virtue of his capacity or position, has access by any means whatsoever to bank book entries, transactions and correspondence, shall be bound by secrecy in the interest of the clients of these banks, and they may not disclose what they know regarding the clients' names, funds and matters relating to them to any person, whether an individual or an administrative, military or judicial public authority, except where authorised in writing to do so by the concerned party, his heirs or his legatees, or where he is declared bankrupt, or where a lawsuit arises relating to a banking transaction between the banks and their clients, or in accordance with the exceptions provided for in Article Seven of this Law.

b - The provisions of banking secrecy shall not apply with respect to:

1- A public official: any person obliged to submit the declaration of assets and liabilities provided for in Law No. 189/2020 and who performs a public function or a public service, whether appointed or elected, permanent or temporary, paid or unpaid, in any person of public law or private law, at the central and decentralised levels, and in general any person who performs work on behalf of public property, a public facility, a public utility, a public institution, a public service or public funds, whether owned, wholly or partially, by a person of public law, whether he assumed it de jure or de facto, including any position of the constitutional authorities or any legislative, judicial, executive, administrative, military, financial, security or advisory position, as well as spouses and minor children, and nominees, and/or trustees and/or guardians, and/or the beneficial owner.

2- Presidents of associations and administrative bodies that engage in political activity, and civil society organisations, as well as their spouses and minor children, and nominees, and/or trustees and/or guardians and/or the beneficial owner, and all candidates for parliamentary, municipal and mukhtar elections, through sequential holdings or other sequential indirect means of control or outside thereof pursuant to the laws in force.

3- Current and former chairmen and members of the boards of directors of banks, their executive managers and their auditors, and chairmen and members of the boards of directors of companies that manage or own audiovisual, print and electronic media outlets.

The effects of Paragraph (b) shall remain in force with respect to the persons mentioned therein even after the date of their resignation, the termination of their service or their retirement, for the entire period during which they held their aforementioned duties and for an additional period of five years thereafter. They shall also apply to anyone who previously held any of the responsibilities set out therein on 23 September 1988 and up to date, including those who have been retired or have left service, in accordance with the provisions of each of Law No. 44 dated 24/11/2015 and its amendments (Fighting Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing), Law No. 189 dated 16 October 2020 (Law on the Declaration of Assets and Liabilities and Interests and the Punishment of Illicit Enrichment), and Law No. 175 dated 8 May 2020 (Law on Combating Corruption in the Public Sector and Establishing the National Anti-Corruption Commission).

New Article /7/:

Subject to the provisions of Article Two of this Law, the banks referred to in Article One may not invoke professional secrecy or banking secrecy provided for in this Law, and they must provide all requested information immediately upon receiving a request from:

a - The competent judiciary in lawsuits relating to corruption offences and offences against property in accordance with the provisions of the Criminal Code, the offences provided for in Article 19 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the offences specified in Article One of Law No. 44 dated 24/11/2015 and its amendments (Fighting Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing), and lawsuits of illicit enrichment brought pursuant to Law No. 189 dated 16 October 2020 (Law on the Declaration of Assets and Liabilities and Interests and the Punishment of Illicit Enrichment).

b - The Special Investigation Commission pursuant to the aforementioned Law on Fighting Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing.

c - The National Anti-Corruption Commission pursuant to Law No. 175 dated 8 May 2020 (Law on Combating Corruption in the Public Sector and Establishing the National Anti-Corruption Commission), in particular Article Four thereof, and Article Thirteen of Law No. 189 dated 16/10/2020 (Law on the Declaration of Assets and Liabilities and Interests and the Punishment of Illicit Enrichment).

d - The tax administration for the purpose of combating tax evasion, tax compliance and auditing, in accordance with the provisions of Law No. 44 dated 11 November 2008 and its amendments (Tax Procedures Law).

e - Each of: the Banque du Liban established pursuant to the Law promulgated by Decree No. 13513 dated 1/8/1963 and its amendments (Code of Money and Credit), and the Banking Control Commission and the National Deposit Guarantee Institution established pursuant to Law No. 28/67 dated 9/5/1967 and its amendments (Amending and Completing the Legislation Relating to Banks and Establishing a Mixed Institution for the Guarantee of Bank Deposits), for the purpose of restructuring the banking sector and exercising their supervisory role over it. The bodies listed above may exchange information among themselves for this purpose.

f - For the purpose of restructuring the banking sector and carrying out supervisory work over it, the bodies referred to in Item (e) above may request information protected by banking secrecy without specifying a particular account or a particular client, including issuing a general request to provide information on all accounts and clients without their names. However, these requests shall remain subject to objection before the Judge of Urgent Matters by the natural and legal persons concerned thereby, and the objection shall in turn be subject to the procedures prescribed for orders on petitions.

g- The implementing criteria and controls relating to Paragraphs (e) and (f) above shall be determined by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

The objection shall stay the execution of the request until a judgment is issued thereon, unless the judge hearing the request decides otherwise within a period of fifteen days.

In the event that the decision of the Judge of Urgent Matters is appealed, the execution of the request shall be stayed for the aggrieved party to the exclusion of those included in the general request.

New Article /8/:

Any intentional violation of the provisions of this Law shall render its perpetrator punishable in accordance with the following:

a - Disclosure of information:

1- Anyone who discloses or attempts to disclose information protected by banking secrecy or data obtained in the course of applying this Law in violation of its provisions shall be punished by imprisonment from one month to three months, and by a fine of 150 times the minimum wage up to 300 times the minimum wage, and an attempt to commit the offence shall be punished by the same penalty.

2- The fine shall be doubled in the event of repetition or continuation of the violation.

b - Refusal to provide information:

1- Anyone who refrains from complying with the requests issued in accordance with Article Seven of this Law shall be subject to the penalty provided for in Item (1) of Article Three of Law No. 44 dated 24/11/2015 and its amendments (Fighting Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing).

The penalty shall be increased, as required by the provisions of Article 257 of the Criminal Code, in the event of failure to comply with any of these requests for a period exceeding thirty days from the date of its receipt, or in the event of repetition.

2- Prosecution shall not preclude obtaining the requested information in accordance with the procedures provided for in the Code of Criminal Procedure.

3- Any of the authorities provided for in Article Seven of this Law shall refer to the Higher Banking Commission established at the Banque du Liban the banks that intentionally refuse to provide the requested information within the period specified in the requests addressed to them in order to take legal measures against them, in particular those provided for in Article 208 of the Code of Money and Credit, within a time limit of two weeks from the date of referral.

c - Judicial prosecution shall not preclude the right of supervisory and regulatory bodies to impose disciplinary and administrative penalties in accordance with their regulations and the laws governing them.

d - A public prosecution shall be initiated only upon the complaint of the aggrieved party or the authorities competent to request information on bank accounts.

Amendment of the Designation of the Fourth Branch of the Social Security Branches:

The designation of the fourth branch of the social security branches provided for in Article (7) of the Social Security Law has been amended from "End-of-Service Indemnity Scheme" to "Pension Scheme".

Definitions:

1 - The Scheme: The Pension Scheme

2 - The Fund: The National Social Security Fund

3 - The Board of Directors: The Board of Directors of the National Social Security Fund

4 - Voluntary Participants: The persons who join voluntarily in accordance with Article (49-3).

5 - The Accumulated Notional Individual Account: The notional account in which the portion of contributions and the annual increase thereon are recorded for each individual separately, as defined in Article (50-6).

6 - The Conversion Factor: The formula that converts the accumulated notional individual account into an annual retirement pension as provided for in Article (50-1).

7 - Year of Contributions: The year for which contributions were paid or became due to be paid under the End-of-Service Indemnity Scheme or under the Pension Scheme.

8 - Qualified Actuary A recognized international association in Actuarial Sciences: Every expert holding a certificate "from a recognized international association in Actuarial Sciences".

9 - Children: Every person who has not completed the eighteenth year of his age.

10 - Indexation: The process of regular adjustment of the value of wages and pensions to reflect changes in the cost of living and salary levels, taking into account the funding policy mentioned in Article (54-4).

11 - Competencies Matrix (Competencies Matrix ): A list of the various special competencies required for each employee, expert, or official, comprising the knowledge, skills, experiences, and their durations, prepared in a detailed table.

Calculation of earnings:

Article (68), paragraph (1) of the Social Security Law has been amended as follows:

The earnings taken as a basis for the calculation of contributions shall comprise the total income paid to the worker in consideration of work or on the occasion of work, including all elements and accessories, in particular wages, gains, paid leave allowances, amounts deducted from the wage for workers' contributions, allowances, grants, bonuses, and all other benefits in cash or in kind, as well as amounts paid directly or by third parties by way of gratuities.

Limitation period for uncollected retirement, disability and death pensions:

The following text has been added to Article 56 of the Social Security Law as amended pursuant to Legislative Decree No. 116 dated 30/6/1977:

Subject to the provisions of Article (81) and notwithstanding the provisions of paragraph (5) of Article (48) of this Law, the limitation period for unreceived retirement, disability and death pensions shall be five (5) years, running from the date on which they fall due.

The limitation period for retirement, disability and death pensions, and for sickness and maternity insurance benefits and family and educational benefits, received without right, shall be five years running from the date of their payment.

Disputes:

The text of Article (84) of the Social Security Law is amended as follows:

1 - In the event of a dispute arising concerning sickness, fitness for work, state of health, date of recovery, or the healing of wounds resulting from a work accident or occupational disease, the dispute shall be examined jointly by the attending physician and the Fund's medical examiner. In the event of their disagreement, the Director General of the Fund shall appoint a committee composed of three experts from a list of specialist experts drawn up by the Board of Directors of the Fund and approved by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers, and their decision shall be final and not subject to any avenue of review.

2 - Without prejudice to the jurisdiction of the competent courts, disputes raised by the application of the provisions contained in Title Four of this Law shall be examined by:

a - With regard to disputes of a financial and administrative nature, the "Amicable Review Committee":

The Amicable Review Committee shall be formed by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour, and shall be chaired by a judge of the fifteenth grade and above designated by the Minister of Justice, with the membership of two delegates from the Board of Directors of the Fund representing the employers and the wage-earners therein, designated by the Board of Directors, and a Category One employee in the Secretariat of the Fund designated by the Director General, and each member thereof shall have an alternate member designated in the same manner.

b - This Committee shall adjudicate the disputes submitted to it by the Director General of the Fund, employers, or insured persons by a majority of votes, and in the event of a tie, the Chairman shall have a casting vote, within a period of one month, and the period may be extended for an additional month where necessary.

c - In the event that the Committee's decision is not issued within the period provided for above, the concerned parties may apply to the Arbitral Labour Council in Beirut to adjudicate the dispute, and its decisions may also be challenged, where necessary, before the aforementioned Arbitral Labour Council within a period of one month from the date the concerned party is notified of the decision.

d - The term of office of the Committee shall be four years, renewable, and the term of office of the delegates of the Board of Directors shall terminate ipso jure upon the expiry or forfeiture of their term of office on the Board of Directors.

e - The allowances of the Chairman and members of the Committee shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Labour.

f - A secretariat formed by a decision of the Director General shall be attached to the aforementioned Committee.

Organs of the Fund:

First: Paragraph (4) of Article 1 of the Social Security Law is amended as follows:

4 - a  The organs of the Fund consist of:

- A Board of Directors,

- A Technical Committee,

- An Investment Committee,

- A Director General of the Fund, to whom the Secretariat is subordinate.

4 - b - The designation "Financial Committee" wherever it appears in the Law is amended to "Investment Committee".

Second: Item a of paragraph (1) of Article (3) of the Social Security Law relating to (the organisation and appointment of the Financial Committee charged with carrying out investments of the Fund's moneys) is repealed.

Rules relating to the implementation of the Social Security Law and the computerisation of its operations:

Article 76 of the Social Security Law is amended as follows:

The Board of Directors shall determine, in accordance with the provisions of Article 3 of this Law, the rules relating to the registration of employers and insured persons, declarations of entry into and exit from employment, the methods of payment of contributions, allowances and advances, as well as all other measures necessary for the implementation of this Law.

For the purpose of implementing these rules, and within a period of twelve months from the date of publication of this Law "Establishing the Retirement and Social Protection System", the Fund shall:

1 - Establish a dedicated digital platform for electronic services relating to those rules, including the registration of subscribers and the payment of contributions and dues, in addition to digital/electronic channels for workers and employers to access information relating to contributions and entitlements.

2 - Develop computerised information systems capable of being linked with other relevant governmental information systems, including civil personal information and the Tax Authority, in line with current legislation relating to electronic governance and data privacy.

3- For the purpose of implementing the provisions of this Article, the Fund shall have the right to request from the "Administration", within the meaning of the definition specified in the amended Article 2 of Law No. 28 dated 10/2/2017 (the Right of Access to Information Law), to provide it with the necessary data and information and in accordance with the provisions of the said Law.

The Board of Directors:

Article Two of the Social Security Law shall be amended as follows:

1 - Composition of the Board of Directors of the Fund

The Board of Directors shall be composed of delegates, among whom are specialised experts, representing the State, employers and workers, in accordance with the following:

A - The Expert Delegates:

- Two experts (2) with an alternate expert, representing the State, who shall be selected from the schedule mentioned in Sub-paragraph (E) below.

- Four experts (4) with an alternate expert representing the "most representative professional bodies" of employers,

- Four experts (4) with an alternate expert representing the "most representative professional bodies" of wage-earners.

B - Within three months from the date of publication of this Law, and upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour, the "most representative bodies" referred to in Sub-paragraph (A) above, and the conditions and manner of electing the delegates representing these bodies, both ordinary and expert, shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, provided that the widest possible representation of existing sectors is observed therein.

C - Within three months from the date of publication of this Law, and at the request of the Minister of Labour, the Civil Service Board shall prepare:

-- A special list for the category of experts representing the State,

-- A special list for the experts representing each of the employers and the wage-earners,

each of which shall include university degrees, specialisations, the "matrix" of required skills and competencies, experience, and years of experience, in subjects related to social insurance, provided that the regular and alternate expert delegates representing the workers have experience of not less than seven (7) years.

D - The two lists mentioned in Sub-paragraph (C) above shall be issued by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour.

E - The Civil Service Board shall draw up a schedule for the category of experts representing the State that includes the names of the experts who meet the conditions and qualifications in accordance with the special list applicable to them above, for the State to select from among them its representatives referred to in Sub-paragraph (A) above, and shall notify it to the Minister of Labour.

F - The Civil Service Board shall, at the request of the Minister of Labour, undertake the review of these lists, the two lists mentioned in Sub-paragraph (C) and the schedule mentioned in Sub-paragraph (E) above, three months prior to the expiry of the term of office of each Board of Directors of the Fund.

2 - Mechanism for Appointing Delegates

A - The representatives of the State shall be appointed pursuant to a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour.

B - The election of the experts and delegates representing employers and wage-earners, who are elected in accordance with Sub-paragraph (1 B) of this Article, shall be ratified pursuant to a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour.

3 - Term of Office and Allowances

A - A delegate shall be appointed for a term of five years, renewable once.

B - New delegates shall be appointed or their election ratified at least two months prior to the expiry of the current term of office.

C - The Board of Directors shall, after the expiry of its term of office, continue to perform its duties until a new Board of Directors is appointed.

D - The Board of Directors shall elect, at its first meeting, a Chairman, a Vice-Chairman and a Secretary, and in the event of an equality of votes for each of them, the oldest by age shall be appointed.

E - All delegates, the Chairman, the Vice-Chairman and the Secretary shall receive a lump-sum allowance for actual attendance at each meeting of the Board,

-- The amount of this allowance and the maximum limit of the sums that may be received per month shall be determined by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour,

-- The Chairman of the Board, the Vice-Chairman, the Secretary and the other delegates may not receive any other wage or allowance in return for any work performed for the benefit of the Fund.

4 - Decision-Making and Voting:

Decisions in the Board shall be taken by an absolute majority, and each delegate shall have one vote, and in the event of an equality of votes, the Chairman shall have a casting vote. Provided that the majority that voted in the Board of Directors for the decision taken includes the absolute majority of each of the representatives of the State, the employers and the wage-earners; and if that is not met in a first sitting, the Board shall be convened to a second sitting to vote on the same decision by the absolute majority of the members of the Board without distinction, provided that the interval between the date of the first sitting and the convening of the second sitting is not less than a period of two weeks.

5 - Internal Regulations:

The Board shall lay down its internal regulations and determine the dates of its meetings, and it shall meet at the invitation of its Chairman once a month, and it may hold extraordinary meetings if requested to do so in writing by at least five delegates or at the request of the Minister of Labour, the Chairman of the Technical Committee, the Chairman of the Investment Committee, or the Director General.

6 - Recourse to Experts:

The Board of Directors may have recourse to specialised and qualified external experts and seek their opinion and expertise, according to their specialisations, in the various subjects submitted to it in order to study them and/or take decisions thereon.

The conditions and mechanisms for having recourse to experts and their allowances shall be determined in the internal regulations of the Board of Directors.

7 - Liability of Members of the Board for Their Acts:

A - The members of the Board of Directors shall be personally liable, even towards third parties, for acts of corruption that they may commit in the exercise of their duties. They shall be individually and jointly and severally liable for their acts on the Board and in the Bureau and for any damages incurred by injured parties, with the exception of anyone who dissented from the contested decision and recorded his dissent in the minutes of the meeting.

B - The action for liability shall lapse by prescription upon the expiry of five years from the date of the contested decision.

Vesting the powers of the "Bureau of the Board of Directors" in the Board of Directors:

The "Bureau of the Board of Directors" is hereby abolished from the provisions of the Social Security Law, and the Board of Directors of the Fund shall assume the tasks and powers delegated thereto.

Continuation of the enforcement of current texts:

The End-of-Service Indemnity Branch shall continue to operate with all its provisions stipulated in the Social Security Law until the completion of the enactment of all decrees and the putting of this system into actual implementation.

Detailed rules for the application of the provisions of this Law:

The detailed rules for the application of the provisions of this Law shall be determined in the internal regulations of the Fund.

Publication

This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette, and the provisions of Article Three thereof shall be put into implementation within the framework and time limits specified in Article 54-6 thereof (implementing and transitional provisions).

This Decision determines the tax treatment, in respect of income tax, transfer duty and fiscal stamp duty, of transactions transferring the economic right from its holder, as defined in Item 12 of Article 1 of Law No. 44 dated 11/11/2008 and its amendments (the Tax Procedures Law), to a third party by way of assignment or by way of inheritance.

Tax treatment of transactions transferring the economic right in respect of income tax:

A - In sole proprietorships, partnerships and liberal professions whose practitioners are not required to join a syndicate in order to practise the profession:

The profit resulting from the assignment of the economic right in a sole proprietorship, or in shares in commercial or civil partnerships, or in a liberal profession whose practitioners are not required to join a syndicate in order to practise it, shall be subject to the tax of Article 45 of the Income Tax Law.

The assignor shall declare the assignment transaction and pay the tax due within a period of two months from the date of assignment in accordance with the forms adopted by the Ministry of Finance.

The assignment transaction shall take place pursuant to a contract before a notary public, to which the documents proving the assigning person's ownership of that right shall be attached.

B - In capital companies:

The profit realised by the holder of the economic right in the capital of a limited liability company, the capital of a joint-stock company or the capital of a partnership limited by shares upon assigning his right shall be subject to the tax of Title III of the Income Tax Law.

The assignor shall submit the declaration of the assignment transaction and pay the tax within a period of two months from the date of assignment.

The assignment transaction shall take place pursuant to a contract before a notary public, to which the documents proving the assigning person's ownership of that right shall be attached.

The profit resulting from the assignment profit referred to in Items "A" and "B" of this Article shall be determined by the difference between the assignment value and the historical value of that right, whether equal to the purchase value of that right or equal to the cost of its creation.

Tax treatment of the transfer of the economic right in respect of the applicability of proportional fiscal stamp duty:

The transfer of the economic right from one person to another must take place pursuant to a contract drawn up before a notary public, including the specification of that right, the holder of the legal right therein and the specification of the price on the basis of which the change of the holder of the economic right therein was agreed upon, and this contract shall be subject to the proportional fiscal stamp duty.

Tax treatment of matters relating to the economic right with respect to the liability to transfer duty:

The obligation to declare the elements of the estate shall fall upon the heirs of the legal owner of those elements in respect of the elements which the law requires to be registered with the competent authority, or upon the heirs of the person who has in his possession any documents proving ownership of the elements which the law does not require to be registered with a competent authority.
This Decision shall be published in the Official Gazette and on the website of the Ministry of Finance.
