Authorisation of Collection:

It shall be authorised, in accordance with the provisions of this Law and the provisions of the laws in force, to collect the various taxes, fees, proceeds and revenues set forth in Schedule No. (2) annexed to this Law.

Authorisation to Borrow:

1 - The Government shall be authorised, within the framework of financing the maturities of the principal of debts, and in expending the appropriations carried over to the year 2024 and the additional appropriations, to issue Treasury bonds in the Lebanese currency for short, medium and long terms, pursuant to decisions issued by the Minister of Finance.

2 - The Government shall inform the Chamber of Deputies quarterly of:

- The deficit realised in the execution of the Budget and the Treasury,

- The expenditure of carried-over and additional appropriations,

- The instalments of internal and external debts that have been paid,

- The result of the issuance of Treasury bonds in the Lebanese currency authorised to be issued pursuant to the First Clause of this Article, as well as in foreign currencies authorised by special laws.

- Treasury advances.

Loan Accounts:

1 - Special Treasury accounts shall be opened for loans, to which the amounts received from the principal of these loans shall be credited and to which the amounts paid in settlement of due instalments and bonds shall be debited.

2 - Commitment and payment appropriations shall be opened in the General Budget for the loans contracted by the State, or contracted for its account, pursuant to decrees taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance and the competent Minister.

Determining the procedures for spending grants and external loans:

1 - With the exception of municipalities and federations of municipalities, grants and external loans offered to each of the public administrations, public institutions, and autonomous services of all kinds, to councils, bodies, and funds regardless of their designations, and to municipalities, federations of municipalities, and all other institutions and bodies that manage public utilities, shall be accepted in accordance with the provisions of Article 52 of the Public Accounting Law and its amendments, and Article 88 of the Constitution, and expenditure from cash grants and from loans, whether from the local component or from the foreign component, shall be subject to the oversight of the Court of Accounts in accordance with the rules.

2 - The provisions of the second paragraph of Article 27 of the draft law put into effect pursuant to Decree No. 14969 issued on 30/12/1963 shall not apply to supplementary appropriations relating to cash grants, as such appropriations may be transferred from one item to another by a decision of the competent minister and the Minister of Finance after the endorsement of the Central Controller for the Commitment of Expenditures, and after the concerned administration establishes the wish of the donor entity to make such transfer.

3 - All balances of uncommitted appropriations financed from cash grants and loans shall be carried forward to the budgets of subsequent years.

Opening exceptional appropriations:

In implementation of the provisions of Article 85 of the Constitution, the President of the Republic may, if emergency circumstances call for urgent expenditures, issue a decree pursuant to a decision issued by the Council of Ministers, opening exceptional or supplementary appropriations or transferring appropriations in the budget of the year 2024, provided that such appropriations do not exceed three hundred billion Lebanese pounds, and these measures must be submitted for the approval of the Chamber of Deputies at the first session in which it convenes thereafter.

Authorisation to transfer appropriations:

1 - Transfers in the General Budget reserve from one chapter to another and from one item to another within this reserve are authorised by a decision of the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

2 - The transfer of appropriations allocated for the salaries of surplus employees, contractors, wage earners and associates in public administrations and public institutions, coupled with the approval of the Civil Service Board, from the administration from which they are transferred to the administration to which they are transferred, is authorised. The transfer shall be effected by a decision of the Minister of Finance after the endorsement of the Central Controller of Expenditure Commitment.

3 - The transfer of appropriations provided for in the budget of the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities - Administrative Departments - allocated to the Traffic, Trucks and Vehicles Management Authority to the budget of the said Authority after the issuance of its own regulations, is authorised by a decision of the Minister of Finance, after the endorsement of the Central Controller of Expenditure Commitment.

4 - The transfer of appropriations provided for under the budget line "Liquid Fuels" in favour of the military bodies in the budget of the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities to the similar budget line in the other chapters is authorised by a decision of the Minister of Interior and Municipalities after the endorsement of the Central Controller of Expenditure Commitment.

Prohibition of granting Treasury advances contrary to the provisions of Articles 203 to 212 inclusive of the Public Accounting Law:

1 - The granting of Treasury advances contrary to the provisions of Articles 203 to 212 inclusive of the Public Accounting Law is prohibited.

2 - Anyone who violates these provisions shall bear out of their personal funds the repayment of the Treasury advances granted contrary to the rules and shall be prosecuted before the competent judiciary.

Healthcare appropriations:

Healthcare appropriations shall be distributed pursuant to a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, upon the joint proposal of the Minister of Public Health and the Minister of Finance, from the appropriations allocated as a lump sum under the Title of the Ministry of Public Health earmarked for treatment in public and private institutions, centres and hospitals, such that an advance of 60% of the total value of the monthly invoices submitted by public and private hospitals pending their audit by the Audit Committee is granted in advance to facilitate hospitalisation coverage, provided that the total value of the advances does not exceed the equivalent of one third of the hospital's annual financial ceiling approved under the hospitalisation contracts.

Deducting a share from the revenues collected in favour of municipalities for villages that do not have municipalities:

The Ministry of Finance shall deduct from the revenues collected in favour of municipalities, prior to their distribution, an amount of 150 billion LBP exclusively, which shall be allocated for lighting, works, and cleaning in the villages that do not have municipalities (energy, maintenance, equipment, and cleaning charges) through the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities. The revenues shall be distributed by decree upon the proposal of the Ministers of Finance and of Interior and Municipalities, provided that the decree includes all the villages that do not have municipalities.

Financial Autonomy of the Branches and Establishment of an Investment Committee:

Article 64 of the Social Security Law has been amended as follows:

Article 64-1: Financial Autonomy:

Each branch of the social security branches provided for in Article 7 of this Law shall enjoy financial autonomy and shall dispose of its own resources to cover its benefits. The revenues and property of the Fund may only be used for the purposes specified in this Law.

In all cases, the use of any resources from any branch for the account of another branch under any pretext and for any reason whatsoever is prohibited. Each branch shall have a specified and separate account.

Article 64-2: Investment Definitions:

The following definitions shall be adopted for investment terms:

They are the principles and orientations that define the long-term investment objectives and the development of the various investment policies and strategies, and which establish the basis for decisions relating to the Fund's moneys.

They consist in the long-term allocation of the Fund's moneys across the various asset classes,

in addition to several other matters relating to the investment of moneys, particularly including classes of investments and loans, return objectives, risk management and diversification, mandates entrusted to asset managers, liquidity of investments, valuation of investments, as well as performance measurement tools.

3 - Long-term Strategic Investment Plan.

Means the long-term action plan (of five years or more) which defines the strategies, policies, and operational programmes that must be selected in a manner that increases the possibility of achieving the specified objectives, in accordance with the "Investment Pillars" and "Investment Policies and Procedures".

4 - Yearly Investment Plan.

Describes the operational policies and programmes that will be implemented during the following year in a manner consistent with the Long-term Strategic Investment Plan, in accordance with the "Investment Pillars" and "Investment Policies and Procedures".

5 - Matrix of Authority for Approval of Investment Transactions: Schedule and Powers

(Matrix of Authority for Approval of Investment Transactions) The statement of the schedule and powers is that which describes for each class of asset classes the level and value of individual investment transactions that may be approved by any of the following bodies:

The Board of Directors, the Investment Committee, the Executive Investment Management, the Chief Investment Officer and the heads of the various operational investment units, and the external asset managers.

It is the annual report on investment operations prepared by the Investment Committee at the end of each financial year and submitted by it to the Board of Directors. The report shall include, at a minimum, a description of the investment strategies adopted for the past financial year, in addition to those planned for the subsequent year, with a statement of the performance results and yield for all asset classes and for the Fund as a whole, and shall also include the audited financial statements for the past financial year.

It is an investment management company, institution, or financial centre accredited by the Investment Committee and mandated by it with the external investment management of the Fund's assets, in accordance with the provisions of Article (64-14).

8 - Custodian

It is the financial institution or centre with which the assets, deeds, securities, and financial values belonging to the Fund and allocated for investment are kept, in accordance with the provisions of Paragraph (64-15) of this Law, and which is licensed in accordance with the laws in force.

The concept of conflict of interest includes any situation or conduct in which the Chairman or one of the members of the Investment Committee, the Chief Investment Officer, one of the heads of the executive units and the workers therein, or others who influence the business, contracts, calls for tenders, and awards relating to investment, has a private financial, economic, or moral interest, direct or indirect, that threatens the impartiality and independence of investment procedures, as detailed in Paragraph (64-7-III-5-a).

10 - Executive Investment Structure

It is the organisational and executive structure for investment within which the authority of powers, responsibilities, and mechanisms for all investment operations are distributed, under the supervision of the Investment Committee.

Article 64-3: Structure of the Investment Committee:

1 - The investment of the Fund's moneys shall be undertaken by a body headed by the "Investment Committee", which shall be linked to the Board of Directors of the Fund and enjoy administrative and financial autonomy.

2 - The Investment Committee shall bear the responsibility of laying down the policies for investing all the moneys of the Fund.

3 - Attached to this body shall be an "Executive Investment Structure", which shall be under the authority of the "Investment Committee" and shall undertake, through the "Executive Investment Management", the implementation of the investments of the moneys of the National Social Security Fund.

4 - The "Executive Investment Management" shall be composed of the "Chief Investment Officer", the "Heads of Executive Units", and executive employees, workers, and contractors, and shall be headed by the "Chief Investment Officer".

Article 64-4: Composition of the Investment Committee:

1 - The Investment Committee shall be composed of six (6) qualified independent experts, to whom shall be added ex officio the Director General of the Fund and the Chief Investment Officer, without either of them having the right to stand for election for the chairmanship of the Committee, or to elect and vote.

2 - The experts must fulfil the mandatory conditions imposed below:

a - Holding a university postgraduate degree in financial or economic sciences or in related fields, or a Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) certificate, with experience in the fields of investment of not less than twelve (12) years within investment institutions or funds of recognised standing.

b - Or holding a university degree and having experience and being seasoned in the fields of investment for a period of not less than fifteen (15) years within investment institutions or funds with a recognised reference.

c - Fulfilling at least one of the competencies and experiences specified and recorded in the table set out in Annex No. (1) to this Law.

These conditions, competencies, and experiences may be amended when necessary pursuant to a decree based on the proposal of the Minister of Labour and the Minister of Finance.

3 - Invitation of Experts to Apply

3-1 Invitation to Apply and List of Accepted Candidates

a - Within six (6) months from the date of publication of this Law, the Civil Service Board shall undertake the announcement of an invitation to experts who fulfil the conditions mentioned in Paragraph (2) above, including in the announcement the conditions imposed for appointment, and fixing a time limit for accepting applications.

b - Upon the expiry of the time limit for accepting applications, the Civil Service Board shall examine the applications and prepare a list of accepted candidates who fulfil the mandatory conditions, indicating the competencies and experiences they possess on the basis of Annex No. (1) to this Law.

c - The Civil Service Board shall invite the accepted candidates to personal interviews which it shall conduct for each of them, and it may seek the assistance of external experts possessing extensive experience in the fields of investment to involve them in these interviews.

d - Upon completion of this process, the President of the Civil Service Board shall send the list of accepted candidates, accompanied by the schedule of competencies and experiences contained in Annex No. (1) possessed by each of them, to the Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Fund.

e - The Civil Service Board shall be given a time limit of three (3) months to complete the above mission.

f - The Civil Service Board shall update this list at least every five (5) years, or whenever necessary, in accordance with the mechanism mentioned above, and communicate it to the Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Fund immediately upon its completion.

3-2 Mechanism for Selecting Experts

a - Upon the request of the Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Fund, the representatives of each of the Government, the employers, and the workers on the Board shall submit to him, within a time limit of one month, a list each containing four (4) names selected from the list received from the Civil Service Board.

b - The Chairman of the Board shall submit the lists prepared above, in addition to the list received from the Civil Service Board and its annexes, immediately upon receiving them, to the Minister of Labour.

c - The Minister of Labour shall submit the lists to the Council of Ministers, recommending three (3) names from each list, two to be appointed as regular members, and one name to be appointed as an alternate member.

d - The six experts, members of the Investment Committee, as well as the alternate experts, shall be appointed from among the names included in the lists submitted to it, and in accordance with the tripartite distribution of the Board of Directors of the Fund, by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers.

e - In all stages of the appointment, it shall be required to adhere to the diversity and distribution of the required competencies and experiences in accordance with the table set out in the aforementioned Annex No. (1) among the names proposed for appointment as regular members, as well as among the names of the alternate experts.

4 - Impediments to Appointment

No person may be appointed to the Investment Committee, nor may he complete his term of office on the Committee, who:

a - Has had a judgment rendered against him barring him from holding public office.

b - Has been declared in cessation of payments or has been judicially declared bankrupt.

c - Has been afflicted with a physical or mental infirmity and has become incapable of performing his duties for a period exceeding six months, such incapacity being verified by the Medical Committee provided for in Paragraph (5) of Article (6) of the Social Security Law.

d - Has failed to attend three consecutive ordinary meetings without a legitimate excuse.

e - Has intentionally or as a result of negligence committed, or allowed another person to commit, a violation of the provisions of the Social Security Law.

Where it is not permissible to complete the term of office due to any of the cases above, the Chairman of the Committee shall refer the matter to the Minister of Labour to present it to the Council of Ministers for determination, removal, or dismissal.

5 - Election of the Chairman of the Committee

Within a time limit of one month from the issuance of the decree forming the Investment Committee, the Minister of Labour shall invite the members of the Committee to a meeting held at the headquarters of the Fund to elect a Chairman of the Committee; if the votes are tied between the candidates, the oldest among them shall be the Chairman, and the Chief Investment Officer shall assume the duties of the secretariat of the Committee.

Article 64-5: Term of Office of the Committee, Liability for Performance, and Allowances:

1 - The term of office of the Chairman and members of the Investment Committee shall be fixed at five years, renewable once.

2 - The Chairman of the Investment Committee and its members shall be liable with their private property and criminally liable for acts of breach of trust and fraud committed by them in the exercise of their duties.

3 - Decisions taken by the Investment Committee that are subject to accountability shall be the responsibility of those who approved them, excluding anyone who dissented from the decision and recorded his dissent in the minutes of the meeting.

4 - Each of the Chairman and members of the Investment Committee shall receive a lump-sum allowance for actual attendance at each meeting in consideration of their performance of the duties and responsibilities entrusted to them pursuant to this Article.

The amount of these allowances, and the maximum limit of the amounts that each of them may receive in a single month, shall be fixed by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers based on the proposal of both the Minister of Labour and the Minister of Finance.

5 - The Chairman and members of the Investment Committee shall be bound, throughout their term of office and even after its expiry, by professional secrecy with respect to all information of which they became aware on the occasion of or by reason of the performance of their duties, and they shall be prohibited from disclosing it except before supervisory and judicial bodies.

This obligation shall include information classified by the Investment Committee as confidential in accordance with its regulations and decisions.

6 - Each of the Chairman and members of the Committee must recuse himself and abstain from participating in the discussions and deliberations of the Committee on subjects and draft investment contracts in which one of them has a personal interest, direct or indirect, and this shall be recorded in the minutes of the meeting.

The member having an interest may not participate in voting on the relevant draft decisions.

7 - In all events, the "Code of Conduct" mentioned in Item (III-a-5) of Article (64-7) below shall remain the reference for defining and detailing cases of "conflict of interest" that impede or affect the performance of the Chairman and members of the Committee, the Executive Investment Management, or other workers in the Executive Investment Structure on the occasion of their performance of their duties.

8 - Each of the Chairman and members of the Investment Committee must disclose in writing any new developments liable to affect his membership in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

Article 64-6: Internal Regulations of the Investment Committee:

1 - The Investment Committee shall meet upon the convocation of its Chairman at least once a month, and it may hold extraordinary meetings upon a written request signed by at least four members, or upon the request of the Minister of Labour or the Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Fund.

2 - Decisions in the Committee shall be taken by an absolute majority, and in the event of a tie, the Chairman shall have a casting vote.

3 - The Chairman of the Investment Committee shall communicate to the Board of Directors of the Fund a copy of the minutes of the Committee's meetings.

4 - Upon an invitation from the Chairman of the Board of Directors, both the Chairman of the Investment Committee and the Chief Investment Officer shall attend and participate in the meetings of the Board of Directors and the Bureau dedicated to subjects of placing and investing the Fund's moneys, without either of them having the right to vote.

5 - Upon the resignation, dismissal, or death of one of the six members, within a period exceeding six months prior to the expiry date of the term of office of the Investment Committee, the Minister of Labour shall invite the alternate member corresponding to him in terms of representation, who was previously appointed by the Council of Ministers, to join the Committee until the expiry of its term of office.

In the absence of an alternate member, or upon his refusal or excuse, the Council of Ministers shall appoint a replacement member to complete the term of office of the Investment Committee from the body represented by the resigned, dismissed, or deceased member.

Where the vacancy affects the position of Chairman of the Committee, the Minister of Labour shall invite the Committee, within a time limit of one month from the appointment of the alternate member, to elect the Chairman, and the election shall take place in accordance with the mechanism mentioned in Article (64-4) above.

Article 64-7: Duties and Responsibilities of the Investment Committee:

The Investment Committee shall undertake the following duties and responsibilities:

I. Organisational and Administrative Duties and the Operational Budget:

Duties and responsibilities that must be submitted to the Board of Directors for examination and due approval or for information:

1 - The first Investment Committee shall draw up the draft internal regulations of the Executive Investment Structure within a time limit of three months from the date of election of the Chairman, and shall include therein the operational establishment, its grades, the methods of appointing its personnel, and their salary scale, which shall be duly approved by the Board of Directors.

2 - Proposing names for the position of Chief Investment Officer in accordance with the provisions of Article (64-9) below.

3 - Preparing its draft annual budget, including appropriations for allowances, equipment, and the operational cost of the requirements and filled positions of the establishment of the Executive Investment Structure.

The Chairman of the Committee shall refer the draft budget to the Directorate General of the Fund, which shall automatically include these appropriations within the administrative budget of the Fund, which is approved by the Board of Directors in accordance with the adopted rules.

II. Investment Principles and Foundations: Principles, Procedures, Policies, and Guidelines

Duties and responsibilities that must be submitted to the Board of Directors for examination and due approval or for information:

1 - Preparing the "Investment Pillars" and submitting them to the Board of Directors for approval.

The Chairman of the Board of Directors shall submit this document to the Minister of Labour for endorsement after seeking the opinion of the Minister of Finance.

2 - Preparing the "Investment Policies and Procedures" for each branch of the Fund and submitting them to the Board of Directors for review and endorsement.

3 - Preparing other related policies, such as the risk policy, the conflict of interest policy, and the foreign investment policy, provided for in the "Investment Policies and Procedures".

4 - Reviewing the "Investment Policies and Procedures" annually, and whenever necessary, and submitting recommendations to the Board of Directors regarding changes occurring to these documents.

III. Duties Related to the Conduct of Business of the Executive Investment Structure and to Ethics

a. Duties of the Committee that must be approved by the Board of Directors

1 - Preparing the "Long-term Strategic Investment Plan".

2 - Adopting the "Matrix of Authority for Approval of Investment Transactions: Schedule and Powers", according to asset class and amounts, which are entrusted either to the Board of Directors, the Investment Committee, the Executive Management, the Investment Director, or the heads of executive units and external asset managers.

3 - Selecting the Custodian to be accredited as the entity for safekeeping and accounting for all securities held by asset managers, and preparing contracts with it and its remuneration.

4 - Adopting the annual report and the audited financial statements of the funds.

5 - Establishing a "Code of Conduct" to deal with actual and potential cases of conflict of interest that may affect the performance of the Chairman and members of the Committee, the Executive Investment Management, or other workers in the Committee on the occasion of their performance of their duties.

The "Code of Conduct" must include, in addition to the foregoing, the basic requirements and ethics that ensure integrity, transparency, and impartiality, provided that it is aligned with the codes of conduct adopted by highly rated international investment institutions.

b. Duties prepared, endorsed, and adopted by the Committee:

1 - Adopting the "Yearly Investment Plan" in accordance with the "Investment Policies and Procedures" and in accordance with the "Long-term Strategic Investment Plan" adopted by the Board, and laying down the necessary procedures for its implementation.

2 - Preparing the internal regulations necessary for the work of the investment units and for the management of investments in the Executive Investment Structure so as to ensure the achievement of investment objectives and priorities provided for in the "Long-term Strategic Investment Plan" and the "Investment Policies and Procedures".

3 - Approving the investment mandates to be given to internal investment units or to external asset managers.

4 - Approving the selection of external asset managers to be accredited for specific investment tasks and approving the contracts and fees of external service providers.

5 - Supervising all activities of the Executive Investment Management.

IV. Reports and Performance:

The Investment Committee must:

1 - Prepare the "Annual Investment Report" and submit it to the Board of Directors for approval.

After its approval, the Chairman of the Board of Directors shall submit this report to the Minister of Labour.

The Minister of Labour shall communicate a copy of the report to the Minister of Finance to seek his opinion thereon.

Each of the Minister of Labour and the Minister of Finance may express comments and request clarifications on the report, which shall be communicated to the Chairman of the Board of Directors within a time limit of one month.

After the expiry of the one-month time limit from the date the Ministry of Labour was notified of a copy of the report and/or after the date of expiry of the one-month time limit from the date of requesting clarifications, this report shall be published on the electronic platform of the Fund.

With respect to obtaining additional information thereon, the provisions of Law No. 28 dated 10/2/2017 and its amendments (Law on the Right of Access to Information) shall apply.

2 - Prepare quarterly reports covering the progress of investment operations and the extent of their compliance with investment policies, standards, and procedures, which the Chairman of the Committee shall submit to the Board of Directors.

3 - Upon the invitation of the Chairman of the Board of Directors, the Chairman of the Investment Committee, accompanied by the Chief Investment Officer, shall attend a meeting of the Board of Directors held every three months dedicated to discussing the quarterly reports and evaluating investment performance.

Article 64-8: The Chief Investment Officer:

1 - The Chief Investment Officer shall be appointed pursuant to a decree taken in the Council of Ministers, and his term of office shall be fixed at five years, renewable once.

2 - The Chief Investment Officer must fulfil the mandatory conditions imposed below:

a- Holding a university postgraduate degree in financial or economic sciences or in related fields, or a Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) certificate, with experience in the fields of investment of not less than fifteen years within investment institutions or funds of recognised standing.

b - Possessing in-depth experience in managing investments across various asset classes, including equity investments, fixed-income investments, and real assets such as real estate and infrastructure.

c - Having familiarity with the related subjects detailed in the table set out in Annex No. (2) to this Law.

3 - Mechanism for Appointing the Chief Investment Officer

a - Immediately upon the formation of the Investment Committee and the election of a Chairman thereof, the Chairman of the Committee shall announce an invitation to those who fulfil the mandatory conditions and some of the additional competencies and experiences mentioned in b above, for appointment to the position of Chief Investment Officer, and a time limit of one month for accepting applications running from the date of publication of the announcement shall be fixed in the announcement.

b - The Investment Committee shall meet within a period of two weeks from the date of expiry of the time limit for accepting applications in a meeting dedicated to examining the applications and preparing a list of accepted candidates, and shall invite them to personal interviews which it shall conduct for each of them, to evaluate the extent of fulfilment of the mandatory and additional conditions for appointment to this position, as detailed for each of them.

c - Each group of experts, the representatives of the Government, the employers, and the workers on the Investment Committee, shall, within one week from the date of preparing the list of accepted candidates, deliver to the Chairman of the Committee a list containing two names for the position of Chief Investment Officer from among the names included in the prepared list.

d - The Chairman of the Investment Committee shall submit the three lists within one week of receiving them, accompanied by a complete list of the pre-selected accepted candidates, to the Chairman of the Board of Directors for information and taking note, and he in turn shall submit these lists, within a time limit of one week from receiving them, to the Minister of Labour.

e - The Minister of Labour shall present the three lists to the Council of Ministers, recommending two names therefrom, and shall propose to the Council of Ministers the appointment of the Chief Investment Officer from among them.

4 - Impediments to Appointment

There shall be barred from appointment:

-- Anyone who is a member of the Board of Directors or of the Technical Committee.

-- Anyone who has been declared in cessation of payments or has been judicially declared bankrupt.

5 - Removal of the Chief Investment Officer

a - The Chief Investment Officer may be removed for one of the following reasons:

-- His commission of a felony or a dishonourable misdemeanour,

-- His commission of a gross fault in the exercise of his responsibilities and duties,

-- His incompetence or gross negligence in the exercise of his office.

b - The removal of the Chief Investment Officer shall take place based on a reasoned recommendation approved by the Investment Committee.

c - The Chairman of the Committee shall refer the recommendation for removal with its supporting documents to the Chairman of the Board of Directors for perusal and submission to the tutelage minister.

d - The tutelage minister shall submit the recommendation for removal, including his proposal, to the Council of Ministers for determination.

6 - In the event of the resignation of the Chief Investment Officer, he shall submit his request to the Chairman of the Investment Committee, who shall refer the request, accompanied by the opinion of the Committee, to the Chairman of the Board of Directors for perusal and submission to the tutelage minister, who in turn shall refer it to the Council of Ministers to decide on the resignation.

Article 64-9: Duties of the Chief Investment Officer:

I. Administrative Duties:

1 - Preparing the organisational structure of the Executive Investment Structure, defining the job duties, and submitting them to the Investment Committee for adoption.

2 - Managing and supervising the Executive Investment Structure and all its operational units.

3 - Preparing the draft annual budget pertaining to the investment body, including appropriations for allowances, equipment, and the operational cost of the filled positions of its establishment and its requirements.

4 - Committing the expenditures of the investment body, which shall be liquidated and paid in accordance with the rules specified in the financial regulations of the Fund.

5 - Preparing for the meetings of the Investment Committee, attending them, and participating in their discussions; he shall be entrusted with the secretariat of the Committee in recording and keeping its minutes, and he may reinforce it with human resources and secure for it the equipment necessary for its work.

6 - Preparing quarterly and annual reports and submitting them to the Investment Committee on the activity of the Executive Investment Structure, its financial statements relating to investment activities, and the final accounts for the end of the financial year.

Provided that these reports include the financial statements showing a detailed comparison of the funds during the reporting period, the closing balance, and the composition of the portfolios at the end of the period.

7 - Coordinating with any person delegated with duties relating to the Executive Investment Structure and its responsibilities in the other directorates of the Fund or with external parties.

8 - Coordinating with the Director General of the Fund to implement the orientations approved by the Board of Directors in transferring assets allocated for investment in accordance with Article (6416) below.

II. Duties Related to Investment:

The Chief Investment Officer, in cooperation and coordination with the heads of the investment units, shall undertake the following duties:

1 - Implementing the policies relating to investments approved by the Board of Directors and/or the Investment Committee.

2 - Implementing the decisions of the Investment Committee.

3 - Approving investment transactions that fall within the scope of its competence, according to the "Matrix of Authority for Approval of Investment Transactions: Schedule and Powers" adopted by the Board.

4 - Ensuring that the Investment Directorate adheres to the application of high standards of performance.

Article 64-10: The Executive Investment Management:

The Executive Investment Management shall be composed of the Chief Investment Officer and the heads of the investment units concerned with execution and operations management, control management, accounting, and risk management.

Article 64-11: Duties of the Executive Investment Management:

The Executive Investment Management shall undertake the following duties:

1 - Approving investment transactions that fall within the scope of its competence, according to the "Matrix of Authority for Approval of Investment Transactions: Schedule and Powers" adopted by the Board.

2 - Coordinating all the activities of the Executive Investment Structure.

3 - Developing various policies, procedures, rules, and guidelines for submission to the Investment Committee.

4 - Drawing up the "Yearly Investment Plan" in accordance with the "Investment Policies and Procedures" adopted by the Board and submitting it to the Investment Committee for adoption.

5 - Laying down the necessary procedures for implementing the Yearly Investment Plan adopted by the Investment Committee.

6 - Providing all necessary assistance to the Chief Investment Officer in any of the duties and responsibilities that fall under his responsibility in accordance with Article (649).

7 - Submitting a recommendation to the Investment Committee for the selection of the Custodian, external investment managers, and any relevant external supplier, for their accreditation, and preparing the relevant mandates and contracts.

8 - Submitting a monthly report to the Investment Committee on the investment activities and strategies and the performance of the various investment portfolios.

Article 64-12: Heads of Investment Units in the Executive Investment Management:

The internal regulations of the Investment Committee shall specify the conditions for each head of unit, his skills, his experience, the methods of their appointment, their responsibilities, and their duties within their units.

Article 64-13: Investment Mandates:

1 - The Investment Committee shall define the investment structure for the various branches of the Fund in accordance with the provisions of the statement of "Investment Policies and Procedures" and the "Strategic Investment Plan", and shall define the investment mandate for each class of asset classes.

2 - Investment mandates may be managed internally by the investment units under the supervision of the Chief Investment Officer or may be delegated to external investment managers.

3 - Each delegation of an investment mandate shall be approved by the Investment Committee, and the mandate shall include a general description thereof, a list of eligible investments, expected return objectives measured against market benchmarks and similar investments, the appropriate diversification measure for investments, the restrictions necessary to control risks, and the relevant conditions.

4 - Each investment transaction shall be approved in accordance with the "Matrix of Authority for Approval of Investment Transactions: Schedule and Powers".

Article 64-14: External Asset Managers:

I - On the Selection of the External Asset Manager

1 - The Investment Committee shall select an external investment manager for any investment mandate based on the recommendation of the Executive Investment Management.

2 - When drawing up its recommendation, the Executive Investment Management shall obtain from qualified institutions and companies licensed to provide the required investment management services proposals relating to investments, and shall analyse them thoroughly.

3 - To this end, the Investment Committee shall approve in advance a list of external investment managers who will be invited to submit their proposals in the fields of investing the Fund's moneys, and this shall take place prior to issuing the request for proposals to potential bidders.

4 - The request for proposals shall include a detailed description of the investment mandate, the qualitative and quantitative criteria to be used in the selection process, and a complete questionnaire to obtain all information deemed necessary in the selection process to ensure a thorough evaluation of the proposals.

5 - The Executive Investment Management must include in its recommendation a draft investment mandate contract between the external investment manager and the Fund, following the approval of the Investment Committee of the aforementioned recommendation.

II - On the Responsibilities of the External Asset Manager:

1 - The external asset manager, as well as the employees subordinate to this manager, mandated by the Fund, shall be deemed a fiduciary pursuant to this Law.

2 - Every external asset manager mandated with managing investments shall bear legal liability for damages that may result from his failure to perform his responsibility specified in this Law or in its regulations, or in any contract signed by him with the Fund. This liability may not be excluded or limited pursuant to a contract or agreement.

3 - The external asset manager may delegate his responsibilities or duties towards the Fund or the Fund's assets to any third party after the written approval of the Investment Committee, provided that such delegation shall not limit the legal liability of the external asset manager.

4 - The external asset manager and all those working for or with him who manage the investment must provide appropriate insurance contracts with a view to protecting the Fund against losses resulting from any forgery or any unlawful act committed by them directly or through a third party.

5 - The approval of the type of insurance, the extent of coverage, and the insurance company granting such coverage shall be subject to the approval of the Investment Committee, which shall lay down the appropriate regulations therefor, including what they contain regarding the nature of the amounts and the nature of the coverage.

6 - The assets of the Fund shall not be deemed the property of the external asset manager. They shall not be included in the execution of any judgment against him, nor shall they be counted among his assets if he is declared bankrupt.

7 - The external asset manager shall keep complete and accurate documents and records covering the investment operations for which he is responsible and the cost entailed thereby, and shall submit them when necessary to the Investment Committee for supervision and auditing.

8 - The Investment Committee reserves the right to rescind and terminate the mandate with the external investment manager in the following cases:

a - If the external investment manager ceases to be qualified and licensed to act in the management of investments in accordance with the laws and regulations in force.

b - If it is established by the Investment Committee that the performance of the manager has not achieved the desired objectives and return specified in his investment mandate contract.

c - In the event of his bankruptcy or the liquidation of his property.

9 - In the event of termination or non-renewal of the mandate contract, the external asset manager shall return all documents, records, and accounts to the Executive Investment Structure or to any new external asset manager appointed by the Investment Committee, upon its request, within the period agreed upon between the parties without delay and in a manner that ensures the continuous performance of the Fund's management activities.

Where, for one reason or another, a number of documents, records, and accounts remain in the possession of the asset manager after the termination of the contract with the knowledge and approval of the Fund, he shall keep them for a period of ten years from the date of expiry of the contract between the manager and the Fund. The external asset manager shall not destroy or dispose of the records and accounts before granting the Fund the opportunity to place them in its custody.

Article 64-15: The Custodian:

1- The Fund shall contract with a specialised financial institution or centre to act as the "Custodian".

2 - The "Custodian" must be authorised and licensed in accordance with the provisions of the laws in force, particularly the provisions of Law No. 161 dated 17/8/2011 (Capital Markets). The "Custodian" shall be responsible for the safe custody of all assets, deeds, values, and securities falling under its management.

3 - To this end, the "Custodian" must maintain a separate fund for each of the branch funds managed by the National Social Security Fund.

4 - The "Custodian" shall undertake the execution of all transactions requested by the Executive Investment Management in respect of investment business managed internally, whether through the executive investment units or through the external investment managers.

5 - The "Custodian" shall undertake to provide the Investment Committee with quarterly reports on the portfolio of assets, values, and securities, and monthly reports on the transactions executed during the period.

6 - As part of developing its proposal, the "Executive Investment Directorate" must obtain from the Capital Markets Authority established by Law No. 161 dated 17/8/2011 a list of licensed financial centres and institutions qualified to perform the duties of "Custodian".

To this end, the "Investment Committee" must approve in advance the list of financial centres and institutions that will be invited to submit bids to potential applicants for this mission and approve the content and details of the announcement of this invitation.

The invitation announcement must include a detailed description of all services and works that the "Custodian" must provide, as well as the criteria that will be used in the selection process and a comprehensive questionnaire to obtain all information deemed necessary in the selection process to ensure a thorough evaluation.

The "Executive Investment Directorate" must prepare and propose a draft agreement between the "Custodian" and the Fund, which must be adopted and approved by the Investment Committee prior to awarding the contract.

Article 64-16: Mechanisms for Transferring Assets Allocated for Investment:

1 - Within three (3) months from the appointment of the Chief Investment Officer, the latter, together with the Director General of the Fund, shall prepare a draft regulation to determine the following necessary criteria, mechanisms, and mandates:

a - Payment of accrued and accruing benefits, allowances, and pensions for each of the operating branches, in addition to the amounts necessary for executing the administrative budget and conducting the business and requirements of the Fund, subject to the provisions of Article (66) of the Social Security Law relating to the formation of a reserve fund for each branch.

b - Transfer of all financial balances in excess of the estimates mentioned above, from each of the operating branches, to the asset funds kept for each of these branches with the "Custodian".

c - Transfer of amounts, where necessary, from the balances of investment assets and returns for each branch kept with the "Custodian", to the Financial Directorate of the Fund to replenish the requirements of the branch.

d - The draft regulation must include the requirement to obtain the documented opinion, when preparing the periodic valuation, of both the Financial Directorate and the qualified actuary accredited to the Fund to determine the estimates detailed above.

2 - The Chief Investment Officer shall present the draft regulation to the Investment Committee for examination and adoption, and the Chairman of the Committee shall submit it to the Board of Directors for approval.

3 - Transfers of moneys shall take place every three (3) months at most, and at a shorter interval if possible, provided that the regulation mentioned above includes the mechanisms for coordination between the Executive Investment Directorate and the Financial Directorate, and specifies the documents necessary to regulate the transfer of moneys allocated for investment to the "Custodian".

Article 64-17: Enjoyment by the Fund of a Preferential Right:

The Fund shall enjoy a preferential right in acquiring shares of public companies privatised by the State or sukuk resulting from the securitisation of revenues and profits of public institutions. This preferential right shall amount to a maximum rate of fifteen per cent (15%) of the issued or offered shares or sukuk, provided that the Fund acquires them at the minimum fixed price or that resulting from a call for tenders, and the Investment Committee shall undertake the completion of the acquisition mechanism.

Article 64-18: Case of Dispute with the Board of Directors of the Fund:

Any dispute arising between the Board of Directors of the Fund and the Investment Committee shall be referred to the Minister of Labour, and if a settlement of the dispute is not reached, the Minister shall refer it to the Council of Ministers for determination.

Article 64-19: External Audit:

The Board of Directors of the Fund must contract with an auditing firm of recognised competence fulfilling international professional conditions, which shall undertake the auditing of its accounts and its risks, with respect to both liabilities and assets, provided that the detailed annual financial audit reports are published during the first half of the following year, and the management of the Fund shall publish quarterly reports periodically and regularly, which shall be placed at the disposal of the public.

Amendment of the text of Article 3 of Law No. 379 dated 14/12/2001 (Value Added Tax) and its amendments:

The text of Article 3 of Law No. 379 dated 14/12/2001 (Value Added Tax) and its amendments is amended to read as follows:

1 - Every natural or legal person who, through exercising an economic activity independently, performs operations of supplying goods or providing services that are subject to the tax or exempt from the tax with the right of deduction in accordance with the provisions of this Law, shall be subject to the tax, provided that the turnover pertaining to a period ranging between one quarter and four consecutive preceding quarters exceeds the amount of five billion Lebanese pounds.

Subject to Paragraph b of Article 60 of the Law, every natural or legal person who, through exercising an economic activity independently, performs operations of supplying goods or providing services that are subject to the tax or exempt from the tax with the right of deduction in accordance with the provisions of this Law, whose turnover pertaining to a period ranging between one quarter and four consecutive preceding quarters exceeded the amount of 100 million Lebanese pounds and did not exceed five billion Lebanese pounds during any period of the years 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2023, is exempted from the obligation of registration in the Value Added Tax and from all other obligations imposed in the Law.

Persons who registered in the Value Added Tax based on their mandatory turnover for subjection and did not exceed five billion Lebanese pounds for a period ranging between one quarter and four consecutive preceding quarters during any period of the years 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2023, have the right to submit a request to cancel their registration with the Value Added Tax Directorate.

The details of application of this Article shall be determined, where necessary, by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

2 - Every person who carries out an economic activity independently that is subject to the tax or exempt from the tax with the right of deduction in accordance with the provisions of this Law may request his optional registration in the tax provided that his turnover exceeds the amount of one billion Lebanese pounds during a period ranging between one quarter and four consecutive preceding quarters.

3 - Persons who do not meet the conditions of subjection set forth in Item 2 of this Article who sign contracts with public administrations, public institutions, municipalities, unions of municipalities, or other persons of public law relating to operations subject to or exempt from the tax with the right of deduction, the value of which, in addition to the value of their turnover, if any, pertaining to a period ranging between one quarter and four consecutive preceding quarters, exceeds the amount of five billion Lebanese pounds excluding the Value Added Tax, may submit a request for their registration with the Value Added Tax Directorate.

4 - The exporter and importer who, through exercising an economic activity independently, performs operations of supplying goods or providing services that are subject to the tax or exempt from the tax with the right of deduction in accordance with the provisions of this Law, shall be subject to the tax, regardless of the amount of his turnover.

The details of application of this Article shall be determined, where necessary, pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

Amendment of Article 87 of Law Enacted by Operation of Law No. 10 dated 15/11/2022 (the General Budget for the Year 2022):

Article 87 of Law Enacted by Operation of Law No. 10 dated 15/11/2022 (the General Budget for the Year 2022) shall be amended so as to read as follows:

A - The following shall be collected in Lebanese pounds:

Shares accruing to the Lebanese State.

Taxes and fees.

Charges for all kinds of services provided by the Lebanese State through various kinds of institutions owned, financed or managed, wholly or partially, by it; and if necessity requires equating the Lebanese pound to any foreign currency in respect of the charges for certain services, this shall mandatorily be in accordance with the actual exchange rate determined by the Banque du Liban in due form.

B - The following shall be exempted from the provisions of Paragraph "A" above:

First:

Shares and profits accruing to the Lebanese State denominated in foreign currencies, such as the share of the State from the oil and gas extraction sector, their derivatives and the sale thereof.

Second:

Taxes and fees due on revenues, yields and interest accruing to their beneficiaries in foreign currencies:

The tax due pursuant to the provisions of Article 51 of Law No. 497/2003 and its amendments (the General Budget and Annexed Budgets Law for the Year 2003) in respect of continuing to withhold the tax in accordance with the type of account.

The tax due on the revenues of foreign shares and debt bonds in accordance with the provisions of Title Three of the Income Tax Law.

Taxes and fees due on companies holding petroleum rights and operating companies holding petroleum rights.

Departure fees on passengers by sea and by air in United States dollars.

Consular fees collected by the departments of Lebanese diplomatic legations and consulates abroad, where they are collected in foreign currencies or in the local currency in which the diplomatic legation or consulate exercises its functions.

Airport fees.

All port fees in consideration for the use of the services of container terminals located in seaports, in addition to loading and unloading fees in public yards and warehouses and vessels (general cargo) and all other port fees, including the fees paid by shipping agents for foreign vessels, in cash United States dollars.

Third:

Charges due in favour of public administrations, public institutions and all other public law persons for services provided outside Lebanese territory.

C - With the exception of the taxes and fees set forth in Paragraph "B" above, the value of all other taxes, fees and fines due in foreign currency shall be imposed and calculated in Lebanese pounds in accordance with the actual exchange rate determined by the Banque du Liban in due form.

D - Where necessary, the details of application of this Article shall be determined pursuant to a decision by the Minister of Finance.

Amendment of Article 43 of Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Income Tax Law).

Article 43 of Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Income Tax Law) shall be amended to read as follows:

The detailed rules for the application of this Article shall be determined, where necessary, pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

Amendment of the first paragraph of Article 63 of Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Income Tax Law).

The first paragraph of Article 63 of Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Income Tax Law) shall be amended:

Article 154-1: (Added pursuant to Law 144 dated 31/7/2019)

And amended by Law Automatically in Force No. 6 dated 5/3/2020 and by Law in Force 10 dated 15/11/2022 and by Budget Law 324 dated 12/2/2024

Notwithstanding paragraph 8 of Article 154 of this Law, distinctive registration plate numbers of passenger vehicles shall be classified pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities, and all numbers falling outside this classification shall be deemed non-distinctive numbers". Furthermore, the code MP shall be used instead of AP for Members of Parliament.

Fees shall be imposed on the owners of vehicle registration plates bearing distinctive numbers across all codes, with the exception of the codes AP,AG,R,J,D,C, in accordance with the following:

First: On the annual fee allowance for distinctive passenger registration plate numbers placed into circulation:

Lump-sum annual fees shall be imposed on distinctive registration plate numbers pertaining to vehicles in accordance with the classification set forth in the attached Schedule.

These fees shall be paid annually together with the traffic fees, in accordance with the laws and decisions in force and the mechanisms designated therefor.

Failure by the owner of the registration plate to pay this fee shall result in its accumulation to the following year, together with the accrual of fines calculated by the same mechanism applicable to annual traffic fees.

On a one-time basis, these fees shall be paid directly for the year 2019 independently of the traffic fees within a time limit not exceeding 30/6/2020.

Second: On the allocation fee for a distinctive registration plate number:

1- A one-time allocation fee shall be paid by any person wishing to acquire ownership of a registration plate bearing a distinctive number, after the date of entry into force of this Law, in accordance with the following:

1.1 Categories: (3.1,4.1,5.1,6.1,7.1) set forth in the attached Schedule:

Distinctive numbers within these categories shall be offered to the public at public auction, provided that each is put up at the reserve price specified in the same Schedule for each category.

A special committee shall undertake the organisation of this auction; the members of this committee shall be appointed and its operating mechanism shall be determined pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities.

1.2 Remaining categories:

The allocation fee shall be paid in accordance with the amount specified in the attached Schedule corresponding to each category.

Upon payment of this fee, the registration plate number shall become his property, and an allocation deed shall be issued to him by the Traffic, Trucks and Vehicles Management Authority in consideration thereof.

Third: On the sale of a registration plate bearing a distinctive number to a third party:

Owners of registration plates bearing distinctive numbers prior to the date of entry into force of this Law may obtain from the Traffic, Trucks and Vehicles Management Authority an allocation deed for their respective numbers, in consideration of a fee equivalent to 5% of the allocation fee pertaining to the category of the number in accordance with the attached Schedule, after payment of the annual fees due by them.

Holders of deeds for distinctive numbers may sell their registration plates to a third party pursuant to a contract executed before a Notary Public; a transfer fee equivalent to 5% of the allocation fee pertaining to the number shall be imposed on such sale, and the Authority shall consequently issue a new deed in the name of the new owner.

A vehicle registered with a registration plate bearing a distinctive number may not be sold to a third party until after payment of the allocation fee and obtainment of the allocation deed. Excluded from this are cases of transfer of ownership between ascendants and descendants and between spouses. This fee shall not fall due upon the execution of a declaration of heirship

.

Fourth: On the surrender of a registration plate bearing a distinctive number to the Administration:

The owner of a registration plate bearing distinctive numbers, including a registration plate placed in salvage, may surrender their registration plates in favour of the Traffic, Trucks and Vehicles Management Authority, provided that his registration plate is replaced with a registration plate bearing a non-distinctive number without paying any fees, on a one-time basis only; this exemption shall cover more than one registration plate bearing a distinctive number owned by the same person.

The application for surrender shall be submitted to the Traffic, Vehicles and Trucks Management Authority, and this number shall be entered into the database of available distinctive numbers.

Fifth: On the allocation fee for a special non-distinctive number:

Any person wishing to register an available special non-distinctive number may register such number provided that he pays in consideration thereof, even on a one-time basis, an allocation fee equivalent to 800000 Lebanese Pounds.

Sixth: Exemption from the payment of the traffic fee, of whatever kind, shall not include exemption from the payment of the annual fee for a distinctive number, or the allocation fee for a distinctive number, or the allocation fee for a special non-distinctive number, provided for in this Article.

Seventh: The allocation fees set forth in the attached Schedule shall be exceptionally reduced by 20% for purchase transactions of registration plates bearing distinctive numbers until 30/6/2020.

The allocation deed fee shall be exceptionally reduced to 3% of the allocation fee as set forth in the attached Schedule, if the fee is paid within a time limit not exceeding 30/6/2020.

Eighth: Paragraph 4 of Article 154 of the New Traffic Law shall be amended to read as follows:

"4- The Latin letters Y-H-K-B-G--M-N-O-R-S-T-Z shall be used for private motor vehicle registration plates belonging to all citizens. Furthermore, the letter P shall be used for public motor vehicles, the letter D for the diplomatic corps, and the letter C for the consular corps".

Ninth: The details of implementation of this Article shall be determined pursuant to a joint decision issued by the Minister of Interior and Municipalities and the Minister of Finance.

Definitions:

The words and expressions set out in this Law shall have the meanings assigned to them below, unless the context of the text indicates otherwise:

1. The State: The Lebanese State.

2. The Public Accounting Law: The Law promulgated by Decree 14969 dated 30/12/1963 and its amendments.

3. Procuring Entity or Contracting Authority: The State and its administrations, its public institutions, independent administrative authorities, courts that have their own budgets, authorities, councils, funds, municipalities and their unions, security and military agencies (and the institutions, administrations and units affiliated therewith), diplomatic missions abroad, regulatory authorities, companies in which the State holds shares and which operate in a monopolistic environment, public utilities managed by private companies on behalf of the State, and any person under public law that expends public funds.

4. The Tenders Administration: The Tenders Administration established by Decree No. 2460 dated 9/11/1959 (Organisation of the Central Inspection).

5. The Competent Authority: The authority competent to commit expenditure in accordance with the laws in force.

6. Person: A natural or legal person.

7. Public Funds: That is, funds owned or disposed of by procuring entities or other persons under public law, or those to whom the provisions of this Law apply, as well as funds deposited in the Treasury, whether their source is budget revenues, loans or grants.

8. Procurement or Public Procurement: Means the acquisition by the procuring entity of supplies, works or services.

9. Supplies: Movable property of whatever kind and description, and the services related thereto if their value does not exceed the value of the supplies themselves.

10. Works: Works of public utility executed on Lebanese territory according to its legal definition for the account of a person under public law or by means of it or under its management, and they include, by way of example and without limitation, works related to building and construction, preparation of work sites, demolition, repair, maintenance or renewal of roads and bridges, establishment of infrastructure or superstructure, installation, or building works related to excavation, erection and maintenance of buildings and factories, as well as the installation of equipment, fixtures and materials, decoration, and services ancillary to the works if the value of these services does not exceed the value of the works themselves.

11. Consultancy Services: That is, services predominantly of an intellectual or advisory nature, including, by way of example and without limitation: engineering, professional, economic, financial, legal or environmental studies, and surveying works, including the tasks of design, preparation of specifications, supervision of execution, evaluation, reception, environmental impact assessment or economic feasibility studies.

12. Non-Consultancy Services: That is, services contracted for on the basis of performing physical work that can be described other than consultancy services, including: guarding, cleaning, transport services, insurance, maintenance and others.

13. Bidder: The submitter of a bid or the potential bidder to participate in the tendering or pre-qualification proceedings, or the person participating in these proceedings.

14. Tendering Proceedings or Procurement Proceedings: Means the proceedings related to procurement starting from the stage of announcement thereof or request for proposals until the conclusion of the contract.

15. Bid: The offer submitted by the bidder for the provision of supplies, works or services.

16. Framework Agreement: An agreement valid for a specified period, between one or more procuring entities and one or more suppliers, contractors, consultants or service providers, aimed at establishing the terms of the contract intended to be awarded within a specified time limit, in particular those relating to prices and, where appropriate, quantities.

17. Contract: A signed agreement between the procuring entity and the supplier, contractor, consultant or service provider resulting from the procurement proceedings.

18. Terms of Reference: The terms that define the objectives, purposes and scope of the consultancy assignment and provide information on the required service.

19. Supplier: The person who, pursuant to the contract concluded with the procuring entity, supplies goods or supplies and related services as a result of the procurement proceedings.

20. Contractor: The person who executes works pursuant to a contract concluded with the procuring entity as a result of the procurement proceedings.

21. Service Provider: The person who provides non-consultancy services pursuant to a contract concluded with the procuring entity as a result of the procurement proceedings.

22. Consultant: The person with whom a contract is concluded for the provision of consultancy services as a result of the procurement proceedings.

23. Awardee: The supplier, contractor, service provider or consultant with whom the procurement contract has been concluded.

24. Day: Means any day of the week.

25. Working Day: Means any day of the week excluding official holidays and days of official or compulsory suspension of work resulting from force majeure.

26. Book of Conditions or Tendering Documents: All documents related to the procurement issued to bidders and which they use for the purpose of preparing their bids, including the technical specifications and other requirements and the procedures to be followed for submitting bids, as well as the forms to be used and the general and special conditions of contract.

27. Electronic Means: The use of electronic equipment (including digital compression) for the processing and storage of information that is sent, transmitted and received by wired, radio, optical or any other electromagnetic means.

28. Pre-qualification: The procedure provided for in Article 19 of this Law, taken and announced by the procuring entity to verify the availability of technical capacities and financial, administrative, human and other capabilities of bidders to execute a contract with the required efficiency before inviting them to submit bids, in accordance with the qualification requirements and criteria specified in the pre-qualification request documents.

29. Collusion: An arrangement made between two or more parties before or after the submission of a bid, to achieve an unlawful purpose or to breach the principle of equal opportunity and the principle of freedom of competition, including directly or indirectly influencing the actions of another party, dividing contracts among bidders, or fixing or manipulating bid prices in a non-competitive manner.

30. Conflict of Interest: The concept of conflict of interest includes any situation in which a public official, one of the bidders, or others who influence the outcome of a procurement proceeding have a private interest, whether financial, economic or otherwise, direct or indirect, that threatens the impartiality and independence of the procurement proceedings. A conflict of interest also arises in the following cases:

a - If the bidder or one of its employees has, directly or indirectly, by itself or in participation with others, provided consultancy services for the preparation of the study, specifications or other documents specific to the procurement, as well as when they have worked during the preceding two years for an entity that provided these services, with the exception of the case where the procurement is conducted on the basis of an integrated project (Turnkey project)) in which the awardee executes multiple stages thereof partially or wholly and the procuring entity sees a public interest in awarding it in this manner, in which case prior disclosure thereof with the justifying reasons is required;

b - If the bidders are linked by certain ties, such as having a common partner who controls their business, or having the same legal representative in the bid;

c - If the bidder submits more than one bid during the procurement process, unless this is permitted in the tendering document specific to the procurement;

d - In any of the cases provided for in the Code of Conduct in accordance with Article 10 of this Law, which must include the obligation for officials to recuse themselves from the work they are performing if it is related to the procurement, in the event that they are linked by ties of kinship up to the fourth degree or clear common interests with the bidder, its employees, or the partners in the bidding company, with which it is feared that their work would not be characterised by impartiality or which clearly give rise to doubt as to such impartiality.

31. Emergency Situations: Situations of imminent danger and disasters declared in accordance with the law.

32. Relief: The urgent situation in which it is required to save lives and protect property following exposure to sudden danger or disasters, including by way of example and without limitation, searching for and evacuating victims, taking shelter and protection measures, and securing and preserving property.

33. Specifications: Means the technical, functional or performance specifications, which are all the technical or functional instructions or those related to performance contained in the tendering documents and which define the specifications and functions of the required goods, services or works.

34. Deliverables: The supplies provided or the services or works completed during the execution of the procurement contract.

35. Publication: Publication shall mandatorily take place on the central electronic platform of the Public Procurement Authority, and on the website of the procuring entity, if any. In addition thereto, publication may also take place through any other means deemed appropriate by the procuring entity, provided that the date of publication on the electronic platform shall be relied upon for all time limits provided for in this Law.

36. Notification: Notwithstanding any other text, general or special, no notification shall be relied upon except that which mandatorily takes place through the central electronic platform of the Public Procurement Authority.

37. Bracket/Tranche: A monetary amount ranging between a minimum and a maximum financial limit.

38. Decision-Making Authority: The body legally authorised to take decisions within the procuring entity.

39. The Public Procurement Authority: The authority concerned with regulating public procurement as defined in Chapter Six of this Law.

40. Persons Performing Procurement Functions: All officials and direct officers concerned with procurement operations in the procuring entities, in addition to the members of the tendering and reception committees.

41. Weighting: Assigning a score or percentage to the financial and technical grade of the submitted bid, which is used in the formula for calculating the final score obtained by each bidder.

42. Accredited Body: A reliable body constituting a third party whose certification of a specific matter is considered an official recognition of competence and conformity.

43. Subcontractor: Any natural or legal person with whom the awardee contracts to execute one or more parts of the works that are the subject of public procurement.

44. Notice: An official communication on a specific matter addressed to a specified party or parties, which mandatorily takes place on the central electronic platform of the Public Procurement Authority, and on the website of the procuring entity, if any.

45. Standstill Period: The period provided for in Article 24 of this Law.

46. Unfair Competitive Advantage: An advantage that gives the bidder a preferential position contrary to the principles of competition and equality among bidders, and legislation against monopoly and conflict of interest.

47. Compulsory Suspension of Work: An unavoidable and emergency suspension of work, not included among official holidays, which constitutes a general situation.
