Article 2 of Law No. 336 dated 24/5/1994 is repealed, and Article 10 of Law No. 60/1988 and its amendments (the Municipal Fees and Surtaxes Law is redrafted to read as follows:

Notwithstanding any other text, the rental values determined for the year 2022 on the basis of which the fee is imposed, except for those assessed on the basis of a new valuation during the year 2022, are multiplied in accordance with the following:

In respect of residential units 10 times

In respect of non-residential units:

* Located on a basement floor that can only be accessed via stairs 10 times

* Located on the ground floor 20 times

* On an upper floor 15 times

The fees shall be recalculated on this basis by the municipalities, and in the event that a fee exceeding the fee due according to the calculation referred to above has previously been paid, the difference paid in excess shall be deemed an advance payment on account of the fee due for subsequent years.

As of the effective date of this Law, and every time the minimum wage in the private sector is increased, the rental values adopted for imposing the fee shall be raised at a rate of half the percentage of the increase occurring to that minimum wage, whether or not they were covered by the amendment provided for in Clause A of this Article.

However, if an increase occurs to the rental value pursuant to the exceptional rent laws in the year in which the minimum wage in the private sector is increased, both increases shall not be applied, but rather the higher of the two.

Amendment of Article 99 of Law Executed Ipso Facto No. 10 dated 15/11/2022 (the General Budget Law for the Year 2022).

Article 99 of Law Executed Ipso Facto No. 10 dated 15/11/2022 (the General Budget Law for the Year 2022) is amended so as to read as follows:

1-The Judges' Mutual Fund shall levy a lump-sum fee of one hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds on every criminal complaint or direct action, payable upon submission of the complaint or direct action

2-On a writ of summons before all civil, administrative and military courts and before arbitral labour boards and judicial and administrative committees of a judicial character, in first instance, opposition, appeal, cassation, retrial, third-party opposition, and litigation against the State regarding liability arising from the acts of a judge.

3-An application for enforcement and a petition for attachment of all kinds.

4- Powers of attorney before all the courts mentioned above and before enforcement departments and at every degree of the courts.

The Fund shall also levy a lump-sum fee of one hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds on all lawsuits of separation, divorce and khul' (divorce by mutual consent for consideration), proof and annulment of marriage, denial and proof of filiation, interdiction, wills, proof of death, determination of heirs, designation of hereditary shares, and inventory of non-real estate estates, accounting and dismissal of a waqf administrator, accounting and dismissal of a guardian, and a certificate of celibacy, payable upon submission of the lawsuit or the certificate, and also upon submission of defences and the adjudication thereof, and on every report issued by an expert or forensic physician including marriage transactions, and on every legalisation transaction issued by the Supreme Sharia Court.

The affixing of the stamp shall be mandatory upon submission of the documents set out above to the courts and judicial departments, whether submitted by the lawyer or by his client.

Amendment of Article 3 of Law No. 273/2001 dated 5/1/2001 (the Mukhtar Stamp Law), as amended by Law No. 270/2014 dated 15/4/2014 and as amended by Law Automatically in Force No. 10 dated 15/11/2022 (the General Budget Law for the Year 2022)

Article 3 of Law No. 273/2001 (the Mukhtar Stamp Law) is amended to read as follows: The resources of the Fund shall consist of:

Amendment of Article 4 of Law No. 273/2001 dated 5/1/2001 (the Mukhtar Stamp Law), amended by Law No. 270/2014 dated 15/4/2014 and amended by Law Deemed in Force No. 10 dated 15/11/2022 (the General Budget Law for the Year 2022)

Special provisions relating to revenues subject to the provisions of Article 82 of the Income Tax Law.

Natural and legal persons resident in Lebanon who are subject to the provisions of Article 82 of the Income Tax Law shall be granted a period of six months from the date of publication of this Law to declare and pay the tax on revenues from movable capital of all kinds which they obtained from abroad, which have not lapsed by prescription and which they have not declared and paid the tax due thereon within the legal time limits, without any assessment or collection fine being imposed on them, provided that the provisions of Article 87 of Law Deemed in Force No. 10 dated 15/11/2022 (the General Budget Law for the Year 2022) are complied with as regards paying the taxes due in the same currency in which the revenues were realised for the year 2022.

The details of application of this Article shall be determined, where necessary, pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

Imposition of fines for violating the principle of access to beaches and violating the regulatory decrees governing this principle.

Notwithstanding any other text, any holder of a licence to occupy maritime public domain or beneficiary of the provisions of Article 11 of Law 64/2017, as well as any other person, who has violated or violates the following shall be punished by a fine of $10,000 to $35,000 or its equivalent in Lebanese pounds in accordance with the actual exchange rate determined by the Banque du Liban:

- The principle of access to the beach through the main and secondary roads leading to the seashore or the sea, by imposing a direct or indirect measure or by placing or constructing any physical barrier.

- The decrees issued by the Council of Ministers specifying the details of securing the continuity of the beach within the maritime public domain and specifying all the conditions that secure this right on the one hand and protect private property on the other hand, as well as specifying any measures that secure the right of citizens to access the beach.

Such violator shall be required to remove the violation immediately

In the event of repetition of the violation, double the previous fine shall be imposed on the violator, provided that it is not less than the maximum limit of $35,000, with the requirement to remove the violation, and the validity of the licence or temporary occupancy, where either exists, shall be suspended until the violation is removed, without the violator being entitled to any compensation or damages of any kind whatsoever.

Whoever fails to pay the fine due within a period of two months from the date of being notified of the assessment by the administration shall have the amount of the issued fine doubled, and the administration shall immediately issue a collection order for the amount of the doubled fine, and the procedures for collection orders shall be completed in accordance with the provisions of Law No. 147 dated 12/6/1959.

Article 32 of Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (the Income Tax Law), amended pursuant to Law Automatically in Force No. 10 dated 15/11/2022 (the General Budget Law for the Year 2022), is amended to read as follows:

The rate of tax on the profits of commercial, industrial and non-commercial professions is set as follows:

4% (four per cent) on the taxable portion not exceeding /540.000.000/ L.L. five hundred and forty million Lebanese pounds.

7% (seven per cent) on the taxable portion exceeding /540.000.000/ L.L. five hundred and forty million Lebanese pounds and not exceeding /1.440.000.000/ L.L. one billion and four hundred and forty Lebanese pounds.

12% (twelve per cent) on the taxable portion exceeding /1.440.000.000/ L.L. one billion and four hundred and forty Lebanese pounds and not exceeding /3.240.000.000/ L.L. three billion and two hundred and forty million Lebanese pounds.

16% (sixteen per cent) on the taxable portion exceeding /3.240.000.000/ L.L. three billion and two hundred and forty million Lebanese pounds and not exceeding /6.240.000.000/ L.L. six billion and two hundred and forty million Lebanese pounds.

21% (twenty-one per cent) on the taxable portion exceeding /6.240.000.000/ L.L. six billion and two hundred and forty million Lebanese pounds and not exceeding /13.500.000.000/ L.L. thirteen billion and five hundred million Lebanese pounds.

Amendment of Article 31 of Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (the Income Tax Law), as amended by Law automatically in force No. 10 dated 15/11/2022 (the 2022 Budget).

Article 31 of Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (the Income Tax Law), as amended by Law automatically in force No. 10 dated 15/11/2022 (the 2022 Budget), shall be amended to read as follows:

The tax shall be levied on actual or lump-sum profit after deducting therefrom, for each natural person among the taxpayers, an amount of LBP /450.000.000/ four hundred and fifty million Lebanese pounds, and there shall be added to this deduction an amount of /225.000.000/ two hundred and twenty-five million Lebanese pounds for a married taxpayer and LBP /45.000,000/ and forty-five million Lebanese pounds for each legitimate child still dependent on him, subject to the following conditions:

For males, if they have not exceeded the age of eighteen, or up to twenty-five as a maximum limit for those pursuing university studies.

For males afflicted with a disabling infirmity and who do not engage in paid work, subject to proving the disabling infirmity by virtue of a certificate issued by the Ministry of Social Affairs attesting to the special needs.

For females prior to their marriage or if they are widows or divorcees, provided that the number of benefiting children does not exceed five.

Where both spouses practise a profession or hold a position, each of them shall benefit from the deduction granted to a single person, and if the spouses have dependent children, the spouses shall benefit equally in halves between them and on an equal footing in accordance with the provisions of the first paragraph of this Article. In the case of legal separation (desertion, annulment of marriage, or divorce) between the spouses, the spouse obliged to pay maintenance shall benefit.

If the father does not engage in paid work and his wife practises a profession or holds a position subject to tax, the wife shall benefit, in addition to the deduction granted to a single person, from the full deduction for the spouse as well as the full deduction for the children in accordance with the provisions of the first paragraph of this Article.

Every Lebanese de facto partnership shall benefit from a single deduction.

As for the tax on taxpayers assessed on estimated profit, it shall be levied after an annual deduction equivalent to the deduction granted to a married person without children.

Amendment of Article 54 of the Built Property Tax Law dated 17/9/1962 and its amendments

Article 54 of the Built Property Tax Law dated 17/9/1962 and its amendments is hereby amended to read as follows:

A- The annual net revenues accruing to the taxpayer from each real property separately shall be subject to the built property tax, in accordance with the following rates:

- 4% for the bracket of revenues that does not exceed one billion and two hundred million pounds.

- 6% for the bracket of revenues that exceeds one billion and two hundred million pounds and does not exceed two billion and four hundred million pounds.

- 8% for the bracket of revenues that exceeds two billion and four hundred million pounds and does not exceed three billion and six hundred million pounds.

- 11% for the bracket of revenues that exceeds three billion and six hundred million pounds and does not exceed six billion million pounds.

- 14% for the bracket of revenues that exceeds six billion pounds.

No surcharge shall be added to this tax.

Amendment of Article 58 of the Built Property Tax Law dated 17/9/1962 and its amendments

Article 58 of the Built Property Tax Law dated 17/9/1962 and its amendments shall be amended to read as follows:

1 - Every taxpayer who owns or exploits a single built property or shares in a single built property and obtains as a result of his ownership or exploitation thereof net revenues exceeding one billion two hundred million pounds per year for each property, shall submit to the competent tax office a declaration before the first of April of each year indicating therein:

- The number of the property and its location

- The amount of his share in the property in shares

- The actual or estimated revenues of the property

- The tax due on the property

2 - The taxpayer shall pay the tax due on the property when he submits the declaration.

4- The details of the implementation of this Article shall be determined, where necessary, pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

Amendment of Article 52 of the Built Property Tax Law dated 17/9/1962 and its amendments.

Article 52 of the Built Property Tax Law dated 17/9/1962 and its amendments shall be amended to read as follows:

Starting from the revenues of the year 2024, an amount of 360.000.000 pounds shall be deducted from the taxable net revenues for each residential unit occupied by a natural person in the capacity of owner, or one of the co-owners, or a person deemed to be an owner.

The persons referred to in the first paragraph of this Article shall each benefit, in proportion to his share in the ownership, in respect of two residential units only, regardless of the number of residences they have occupied or occupy, and that in respect of the two units having the highest rental values.

The right of the persons referred to in the first paragraph of this Article to this deduction shall be preserved starting from the date of their occupancy, and the provisions of prescription shall not prevent them from benefiting from this deduction, provided that the taxes paid shall be considered a right of the Treasury and cannot be refunded.

The details of the implementation of this Article shall be determined, where necessary, by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

Amendment of Article 42 of Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Income Tax Law).

Article 42 of Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Income Tax Law) is amended to read as follows:

The net taxable amount received by a non-resident, based on the definition of a resident set forth in the Tax Procedures Law, shall be fixed on a lump-sum basis at twenty percent (20%) of the gross revenues referred to in the preceding Article, where they are in consideration for the delivery of property, and at fifty percent (50%) thereof where they have the nature of remuneration for a service, and the tax shall be withheld and collected at the rate of seventeen percent (17%), and no surtax shall be added to the principal of the tax.

This provision shall apply with effect from the quarter following the quarter in which this Law is published.

Amendment of Article 60 of Decision No. 275 issued on 25/1926 (Management and Sale of Private State Property).

Article 60 of Decision No. 275 issued on 25/1926 (Management and Sale of Private State Property) is hereby amended to read as follows:

Private property of the State and municipalities may be leased through a public auction organized in accordance with the Public Procurement Law and based on special terms of reference established by the Minister of Finance and the competent Minister.

Leasing shall take place and for periods not exceeding a maximum of four years, renewable once, with respect to built real properties and unbuilt real properties where the lease contract does not include the erection of constructions thereon and is limited to ordinary maintenance and exploitation, and nine years, renewable once, with respect to unbuilt real properties where the lease contract includes capital maintenance and exploitation works the value of which exceeds two years' rent.

Provided that a feasibility study for the project is submitted and approved by both the Minister of Finance and the competent Minister, and that the Directorate of Roads and Buildings at the Ministry of Public Works and Transport supervises the proper execution.

Ownership of these constructions shall pass to the Lebanese State upon the expiry of the lease term or the forfeiture of the lessee's right due to his breach of the leasing conditions, without any sum or compensation being due from the State in return for its acquisition of ownership of these constructions.

Except for cases in which real properties are leased to a person of public law, leasing shall take place exclusively by public open auction.

If the rent is not paid on its due dates or the other encumbrances and leasing conditions are not performed, the Minister of Finance may, upon the proposal of the competent Minister, rescind the contract if he does not deem it preferable to pursue the enforcement of the contract by all legal means.

Article One of Law No. 90 dated 10/9/1991, as amended pursuant to Law No. 280 dated 15/12/1993 (1993 Budget Law), Law No. 64 dated 20/10/2017, Law No. 144 dated 31/7/2019 (General Budget and Annexed Budgets Law for the Year 2019), and Law No. 303 dated 8/8/2022, is amended to read as follows:

Imposition of an exit fee on passengers travelling by air or sea and an entry fee on non-Lebanese nationals.

1- Notwithstanding any other provision, an exit fee shall be imposed on passengers travelling by air or sea in the amount of:

- $35 on each economy class passenger.

- $50 on each business class passenger.

- $65 on each first class passenger.

- $100 on each passenger aboard private aircraft or yachts.

A rate of 20 per cent shall be deducted from the amounts collected from the exit fees on each passenger specified in Article One, Paragraph (1) above, and these amounts from this fee shall be deposited in a special account opened in US dollars at the Bank of Lebanon in the name of the Lebanese State, the proceeds of which shall be allocated to expenditure on the equipment and maintenance of the airport and all technical, technological, and administrative services related to the civil aviation sector in accordance with the laws in force. The fees specified in US dollars shall be collected in cash.

2- An entry fee in the amount of 1.000.000 (one million Lebanese pounds), collected by means of a fiscal stamp, shall be imposed on non-Lebanese passengers travelling by land upon their entry into Lebanese territory.

The details of application of this paragraph shall be determined, where necessary, by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

Article Thirty-Three of Law No. 409 dated 7/2/ 1995 (the 1995 Budget) is repealed and replaced by the following text:

The proceeds of assessment fines imposed pursuant to the laws and regulations relating to direct taxes, indirect taxes, and similar fees assessed by the competent financial divisions affiliated with the Directorate General of Finance and finally collected, and the proceeds of late payment fines (collection fines) imposed pursuant to the provisions of Article 55 of Law No. 44/2008 (the Tax Procedures Law) and finally collected, shall be distributed in accordance with the following bases:

(60%) Sixty percent to the Treasury

11 shares (eleven shares) to: the Director General of Finance.

Cases Requiring the Imposition of the Fine under Article 110

1 - The fine under Article 110 shall be imposed on the additional tax resulting from the amendments made by the Tax Administration to the taxpayer's periodic or annual returns, where the Administration has relied for such amendments on the entries recorded in his registers.

2 - The fine under Article 110 shall not be imposed when no additional tax results from the amendments made by the Tax Administration to the taxpayer's periodic or annual returns.

This fine shall likewise not be imposed when the taxpayer amends his return without any additional tax resulting from such amendment, even if such amendment is made outside the time limits provided for in Article 40 of the Tax Procedures Law.

This fine shall likewise not be imposed if the taxpayer submits more than one amendment to his original return within the aforementioned time limits (Article 40-3) and the total of the amendments does not exceed 10% of the tax declared in that return.

Cases Requiring the Imposition of the Fine under Article 115:

The fine under Article 115, to the exclusion of the fine under Article 110, shall be imposed on the additional tax resulting from the amendments made by the Tax Administration to the taxpayer's periodic or annual returns where those amendments are accompanied by entries recorded in the registers contrary to accounting principles.

Where, however, there is an omission or error in recording the transactions in the accounting registers and that has no tax effect, the fine under Article 115 shall not be imposed in that case.

Cases Requiring the Imposition of the Fine under Articles 110 and 114 or the Fine under Articles 110 and 115 Together:

- The fine under Articles 110 and 114 shall be imposed together on the additional tax resulting from the amendments made by the Tax Administration to the taxpayer's periodic or annual returns where those amendments are accompanied by the failure to keep the accounting registers and documents substantiating those transactions.

- The fine under Articles 110 and 115 shall be imposed together on the additional tax resulting from the amendments made by the Tax Administration to the taxpayer's periodic or annual returns where those amendments are accompanied by the taxpayer's refusal to produce the accounting registers and documents substantiating those transactions or by the taxpayer's failure to include and record those transactions in his registers.

Fines on adjustments made by the Tax Administration to returns submitted after the deadline:

Any adjustment made by the Tax Administration to the taxpayer's periodic or annual returns submitted after the statutory deadline that results in an additional tax shall entail the imposition of the statutory fines as required by the provisions set forth in the Second, Third, Fourth and Fifth Articles of this Decree, and the fine of Article 109 or the fine of Article 116 shall be imposed on the entire tax due up to the date of submission of the return, provided that the assessment fine declared by the taxpayer is deducted therefrom.

Cases entailing the imposition of the fine of Article 111

The fine of Article 111 shall be imposed where the taxpayer omits to include any information in the returns and no additional tax results from such omission, and the accrual of this fine shall not preclude the imposition of the fine resulting from the adjustment to the taxpayer's returns.

Realising revenue from a concealed activity:

The fine of Article 109 shall be imposed on the additional tax assessed by the Tax Administration upon its discovery that the individual taxpayer carries on, alongside the declared activity, another activity at another place of business or carries on another activity that does not require a designated place of business, which requires him to declare the commencement of business for such other activity. The fines due in accordance with the provisions of this Decree shall also be imposed on the remaining violations, if any.

Delay by the taxpayer in notifying of the assignment of one of his establishments or of his cessation of work therein:

Where the taxpayer fails to notify the Tax Administration or delays in notifying it of his assignment of an establishment or of his cessation of work therein whilst continuing to work in another establishment or in the capacity of a partner in a partnership, the fine of Article 108 shall be imposed.

Adjustment to the annual return due to a deficiency other than that resulting from a deficiency in the periodic returns:

The fines due shall be imposed on the violations in the periodic returns, and no fine shall be imposed on the deficiency in the annual return resulting exclusively from the deficiency in the periodic returns for which the fine has been paid.

However, if an additional tax becomes due as a result of adjustments to the annual return other than those resulting from adjustments to the periodic returns, the fine shall be imposed on the entire difference of the tax due in the annual return.

Failure to submit the auditor's report or delay in submitting it:

The fine of Article 112 shall be imposed in the event of failure to submit the auditor's report or delay in submitting it, on the basis of the tax on profits (Title I) due from the company, including the tax of Article 45, and excluding the tax of Articles 41/42/43.

Cases warranting the fine of Article 150:

1 - The fine of Article 150 shall be imposed by the competent units in the Value Added Tax on the transactions subject to the invoice in the following two cases:

* Failure to include in the invoice or the document similar thereto a correct description of the transaction comprising the type of good, the unit price, the quantity the total value.

* Failure to include in the invoice or the document similar thereto the value of the Value Added Tax or including therein a tax less than what is due.

2 - The fine of Article 113 and the fine of Article 150 may not be imposed together on violations relating to the same invoices, such that the higher fine between them shall be imposed.

Application of the fine of Articles 109, 110, 112, 114 and 115, 116 and 125 to partnerships:

Subject to the obligation to impose fines on partners in partnerships, the fines of Articles 109, 110, 112, 114 and 115, 116 and 125 shall be imposed on those companies as follows:

- The fine of Article 109 at its minimum limit in the event of failure to submit or delay in submitting its annual declaration.

The fine of Article 109 shall also be imposed in the amount of five percent (5%) of the value of the tax due, in the event that the company is obligated to declare the share of the partners therein in accordance with the provisions of Article 35 of the Income Tax Law, including the tax of Article 45, provided that in all cases it shall not be less than the minimum limit.

- The fine of Article 112 in accordance with the two cases referred to in the paragraph above, in the event of failure to submit or delay in submitting the auditing commissioner's report, where required.

- The fine of Article 116 in the event of failure to submit or delay in submitting the annual declaration relating to salaries and wages. The fine of Article 125 shall be imposed thereon in the event of failure to submit or delay in submitting the periodic declaration relating to those salaries and wages.

- The fine of Article 109 or the fine of Article 116 in the event of failure to declare or delay in submitting the declaration for the amounts subject to Articles 41, 42 and 43 of the Income Tax Law or for the amounts subject to Article 45 thereof or for movable capital revenues or for Value Added Tax.

- The fine of Article 110 on the adjustments made by the tax administration to its annual declaration, when the company is obligated to declare the share of minor limited partners to whom the provisions of Article 66 of the Code of Commerce do not apply, and this fine shall be imposed on the adjustments made by the tax administration to the tax due on the share of these minor limited partners.

- The fine of Article 110 on the adjustments made by the tax administration to the periodic or annual declarations for the tax on salaries and wages or for the tax of Articles 41, 42 and 43 or the tax of Article 45 of the Income Tax Law or for the tax on movable capital revenues or for Value Added Tax.

- In the event of failure by the company to keep records or in the event of failure to produce them, the fine of Article 114 or the fine of Article 115 shall be calculated on the total tax due by the partners, provided that this fine shall not be less than 500,000 LBP.

Share Register:

Joint-stock companies and partnerships limited by shares shall be subject to the fine of Article 114 at its minimum in the event of failure to keep the share register and the special register for recording the names of shareholders present at general assemblies.

Violations Committed by Holding Companies and Offshore Companies:

The fine provided for in the regime of holding companies and in the regime of offshore companies shall be imposed when those companies commit a violation relating to the regime of each of them, whereas in the case where those companies have committed a violation relating to tax procedures, such as violating the obligation to keep registers or submitting a declaration outside the time limit or submitting an incorrect declaration, the fines provided for in the Tax Procedures Law shall be imposed. In the event that the companies commit two violations at the same time, the first relating to a violation of their regime and the second relating to a violation of tax procedures, the fines provided for in their regime and in the Tax Procedures Law shall be imposed.

Taxpayers on the Basis of Estimated Profit:

- Estimated profit taxpayers shall be subject to the fine of Article 114 at the rate of 50% of the tax due on their profits determined by the Tax Administration, provided that it is not less than the minimum at the rate of 100.000 L.L., if they do not keep one or both of the required registers (journal and fixed assets).

- Estimated profit taxpayers shall be subject to the fine of Article 115 at the rate of 50% of the tax due on their profits determined by the Tax Administration, provided that it is not less than the minimum fine, if they refrain from producing the two required registers (journal and fixed assets) or refrain from recording certain transactions therein in due form.

Institutions Exempt from Tax:

Institutions exempt from tax mentioned in the articles relating to fines in the Tax Procedures Law mean taxpayers exempt from income tax other than individuals and companies, such as associations and clubs.

Late payment fine:

The late payment fine shall be calculated on the total of the tax and the assessment fine when due, and shall take effect as from:

- The date of expiry of the basic payment time limit with respect to taxpayers subject to the self-assessment system, and in the event of extension of the time limit, the fine shall be calculated from the date of expiry of the extended time limit.

- After the lapse of two months from the date of publication of the basic rolls in the Official Gazette with respect to taxpayers whose tax due is issued pursuant to basic rolls.

- The date of expiry of the time limit for declaring the tax obligation in the absence of a payment time limit, such as the fine due for delay in declaring the commencement of work or delay in notifying the Administration of amendments relating to the taxpayer.

- After the lapse of two months from the date of issuance of the collection order for inheritance and transfer duty.

- The date of expiry of the payment time limit in the absence of a time limit for declaring the tax obligation.

Infractions that lapse by prescription:

No fine shall be imposed for non-compliance with a tax obligation arising from an event that occurred in a year that could not be assessed for tax due to its lapse by prescription, even if the time limit for declaring this event expires in a year for which the taxes and duties due have not lapsed by prescription.
This Decree shall be published in the Official Gazette and on the website of the Ministry of Finance.

This Decision determines the mechanism for calculating and paying the tax on salaries and wages, including amounts paid wholly or partially in foreign currency, and the method of calculating progressive tax rates.

Where salaries and wages are paid in a currency other than the national currency, and in order to determine the actual value in Lebanese Pounds of such amounts, whether paid wholly or partially in foreign currency, the following shall be complied with:

1 - Where salaries and wages are paid wholly in United States Dollars:

Such salaries and wages shall be converted into Lebanese Pounds in accordance with the following:

a - For the period extending from 1/1/2024 up to 31/3/2024:

* Where salaries and wages are paid in cash in United States Dollars:

On the basis of an exchange rate of 15.000 L.L. per United States Dollar.

* Where salaries and wages are paid by cheque or bank transfer within Lebanon:

On the basis of an exchange rate of 8.000 L.L. for the first three thousand and 1507.5 L.L. per one United States Dollar for the remainder of the amount.

b - For the period commencing with effect from 1/4/2024:

Taxable salaries and wages paid in United States Dollars shall be calculated on the basis of the exchange rate determined in Decision No. 302/1 dated 3/4/2024 (and its amendments), currently amounting to a value of 89.500 L.L. per one United States Dollar, whatever the method of payment.

2 - Where salaries and wages are paid partially in United States Dollars and the other part in Lebanese Pounds:

The part paid in United States Dollars shall be converted in accordance with what is stated above depending on the period concerned, and its value shall be added to the value of the part paid in Lebanese Pounds.

3 - Where salaries and wages are paid partially or wholly in a foreign currency other than in United States Dollars:

Such currency shall be converted into United States Dollars in accordance with the average conversion rate between foreign currencies against the United States Dollar, and thereafter such salaries and wages shall be converted into Lebanese Pounds in accordance with the provisions stated above.

On the rates and brackets to be applied to salaries and wages:

a - Income tax rates shall apply to salaries and wages as follows:

- 2% (two percent) on the portion of net taxable revenues not exceeding /360.000.000/ L.L. three hundred and sixty million Lebanese Pounds.

- 4% (four percent) on the portion of net taxable revenues exceeding /360.000.000/ L.L. three hundred and sixty million Lebanese Pounds and not exceeding /900.000.000/ L.L nine hundred million Lebanese Pounds.

- 7% (seven percent) on the portion of net taxable revenues exceeding /900.000.000/ L.L. nine hundred million Lebanese Pounds and not exceeding /1.800.000.000/ L.L one billion and eight hundred million Lebanese Pounds.

- 11% (eleven percent) on the portion of net taxable revenues exceeding /1.800.000.000/ L.L one billion and eight hundred million Lebanese Pounds and not exceeding /3.600.000.000/ L.L. three billion and six hundred million Lebanese Pounds.

- 15% (fifteen percent) on the portion of net taxable revenues exceeding /3.600.000.000/ L.L. three billion and six hundred million Lebanese Pounds and not exceeding /7.200.000.000/ L.L seven billion and two hundred million Lebanese Pounds.

- 20% (twenty percent) on the portion of net taxable revenues exceeding /7.200.000.000/ L.L seven billion and two hundred million Lebanese Pounds and not exceeding /13.500.000.000/ L.L thirteen billion and five hundred million Lebanese Pounds.

- 25% (twenty percent) on the portion of net taxable revenues exceeding /13.500.000.000/ L.L thirteen billion and five hundred million Lebanese Pounds.

b - There shall be deducted from the net revenues subject to tax on salaries and wages,

the family deduction as follows:

For each natural person 450.000.000 L.L., plus:

- for a married taxpayer whose wife does not work 225.000.000 L.L.,

- for each legitimate child still dependent on him within the same conditions mentioned in Article 31 of the Income Tax Law 45.000.000 L.L.,

The base deduction shall be calculated at an amount equivalent to 1.500.000 L.L. per day for hourly wage-earners who receive daily wages regardless of their family status.

These brackets and deductions shall apply effective from 1/1/2025.
