As from the date of entry into force of this Decree, electronic official instruments shall produce the same legal effects enjoyed by paper official instruments, provided that they satisfy the conditions stipulated in the Electronic Transactions Law and the provisions of this Decree.

In the absence of a provision in this Decree or in the Electronic Transactions Law, the rules and provisions governing paper official instruments shall apply to electronic official instruments, provided that their application shall only be to the extent of their compatibility with the electronic nature of electronic official instruments.

All official instruments classified as having a security or military specificity, or those characterised by secrecy or relating to State security, shall be excluded from this Decree.

This Decree aims to ensure that electronic official instruments enjoy the following attributes:

(1) That electronic official instruments have the same degree of reliability enjoyed by paper official instruments.

(2) That they be preserved in a secure and sustainable manner by means of mechanisms that observe the framework of the National Digital Transformation Strategy and the cybersecurity standards issued by the Council of Ministers.
This Decree regulates the procedures specific to electronic official instruments and the guarantees relating thereto with the aim of establishing unified regulatory rules for such instruments.

Public officials or persons charged with a public service may not draw up electronic official instruments or authenticate electronically until after the issuance of regulatory decisions by the head of the administration or official entity to which they report, comprising the following:

(1) The approval of the head of the administration or official entity for electronic dealing, and the determination of the scope of its application in each administration or official entity reporting to it.

(2) The determination of the regulatory particulars relating to each instrument among the electronic official instruments, in particular those relating to the form of the instrument, the manner of its issuance, preservation and transmission, and its required specifications for drawing it up and signing it electronically and for electronic authentication, and the mechanism for verifying approval of the content of the electronic official instrument where required, in accordance with the provisions of this Decree.

Definition of Terms

For the application of the provisions of this Decree, and with reference to those defined pursuant to Article 1 of Law No. 81 dated 10/10/2018 entitled "Electronic Transactions and Personal Data", each of the terms mentioned below shall have the meaning indicated next to each of them wherever they appear:

1 - Electronic Transactions Law: Law No. 81 issued on 10/10/2018 entitled "Electronic Transactions and Personal Data".

2 - Administration or Official Entity: Ministries, administrations, public institutions, courts, municipalities, official regulatory bodies, independent official administrative bodies, or other persons of public law or notaries public.

3 - Electronic Authentic Instrument: The authentic instrument provided for in Article 143 of the Code of Civil Procedure which is issued in electronic form in accordance with the provisions of the Electronic Transactions Law and the provisions of this Decree.

4 - Electronic Dealing: Any exchange, correspondence, contracting, or \any other procedure drawn up or executed wholly or partially by one or several electronic means.

5 - Electronic Signature: Data in electronic form attached to or logically associated with other data in electronic form, which is used by the signatory to sign.

6 - Electronic Seal: Data or an image of a seal in electronic form, which is attached to or logically associated with other data in electronic form to ensure the origin of the latter.

7 - Electronic Signature or Seal Creation Data: Means unique data used by the signatory to create an electronic signature or seal.

8 - European Regulation: European Regulation No. 910 issued on 23/7/2014 on electronic identification and authentication services for electronic transactions.

9 - Trusted Service Provider: Any natural or legal person who provides trust or authentication services accredited by the Lebanese Accreditation Council or by one of the international technical and technological bodies included in the list issued by the Lebanese Accreditation Council and its subsequent amendments.

10 - Electronic Signature or Seal Creation Means or Mechanism: A software or programmed device used to create an electronic signature, by means of information technology.

11 - Electronic Register: A set of records containing electronic data, created, established, or preserved by electronic means and capable of being retrieved or consulted in an intelligible form.

12 - Authentication Certificate: A certificate issued by a trust or authentication service provider attesting, at a minimum, to the confirmation of the identity of the person or entity holding a specific signature tool, and other data according to the type of certificate.

13 - Automatic Mechanism System: Or what is known as an Automated Process, which refers to a series of operations or tasks carried out automatically without the need for human intervention, in which technology and computer systems are used to execute specific steps or procedures.

14 - Electronic Copy: Any electronic copy conforming to the electronic instrument.

15 - Electronic Certification of a Copy: An electronic attestation stating that the electronic copy conforms to the original instrument.

16 - Electronic Certification of a Signature: An electronic attestation stating the validity of the signature.

Immediately upon the creation of the original electronic authentic instrument, the public official or the person entrusted with a public service shall verify its registration in the electronic registers of authentic instruments established in accordance with the provisions of this Decree, and shall also verify that the electronic authentic instrument registered in the electronic register is identical to the authentic instrument created by him.

After the registration process has been duly completed, and in the cases permitted by law, the public official or the person entrusted with a public service may:

(1) Issue, download, send and deliver electronic copies of the original electronic authentic instrument.

(2) Issue and deliver certified true paper copies of the original electronic authentic instrument.

The electronic authentic instrument registered in the electronic registers is the original instrument against which copies are compared.

In the event of a technical problem preventing the registration of the electronic authentic instrument immediately upon its creation, and if it is impossible to postpone the registration of the authentic instrument until this problem is resolved, the public official or the person entrusted with a public service may, exceptionally and notwithstanding the provisions of Article 9 of this Decree, issue electronic copies of the original electronic authentic instrument if he has previously issued a certified paper copy of the electronic authentic instrument and kept it in a safe place.

Immediately upon the resolution of the technical problem, the provisions of Article 9 of this Decree shall apply, and the conformity of the registered electronic authentic instrument with the content of the certified paper copy shall also be verified.

The administration or official body shall have recourse to providers of electronic signature and certification services who are reliable from a technical and technological standpoint by the Lebanese Council for Accreditation (COLIBAC) or by one of the international technical and technological bodies, included in the list issued by the Lebanese Council for Accreditation attached to this Decree and its subsequent amendments.

(As published in the Official Gazette No. 2 dated 9/1/2025 p. 77)

The administration or official body shall provide the minimum technical and administrative infrastructure and related resources to ensure the fulfilment of the conditions stipulated in this Decree, take the necessary precautions to avoid any unlawful use of the signature or electronic seal creation data or the personal equipment related to the signatory, and notify the accredited service provider of any unlawful use of any electronic signature or seal immediately upon becoming aware thereof.

Every administration or official body shall also, in any electronic transaction, observe the national strategies related to digital transformation and cybersecurity issued by the Council of Ministers and preserve digital sovereignty.

The public official or the person entrusted with a public service shall establish the electronic official instrument, after verifying its content, in accordance with the mechanism prescribed by the administration or official body to which he belongs, provided that this instrument includes the following elements:

(1) That it be signed electronically by the public official or the person entrusted with a public service in accordance with the conditions stipulated in this Decree.

(2) That it include the data proving that its signatory enjoys the capacity and competence on the date of its establishment and electronic signature.

(3) In cases where the consent of the concerned party to the content of the instrument is required, the public official or the person entrusted with a public service shall verify the consent and its inclusion on the electronic official instrument prior to signing it, and this condition shall in such case be deemed an additional condition to the two conditions mentioned above.

Every administration or official entity must organise and preserve its electronic official instruments in the form of entries in electronic registers belonging to it in accordance with the following conditions:

(1) The electronic register shall identify both the originator of the electronic official instrument and the originator of the entry.

(2) The electronic register shall include all data relating to the transaction or transactions connected to the electronic official instrument, provided that such data include the numbers of the transaction or transactions and their nature, the time and date of creation, sending, receipt and resending of the electronic official instrument, the date of its entry in the electronic register and the information relating to its cancellation or revocation, as well as acknowledgment of receipt messages where required by the administration or official entity.

(3) The electronic official instrument shall be preserved in the electronic register belonging to it in a manner through which it can be proven that its content matches the content in which it was created.

(4) The electronic register remains preserved in a manner that allows its subsequent use and reference.

Registers may be archived in any form of securely preserved electronic data that does not prejudice their content and existence, provided that the manner of inspecting them upon request by persons with standing is indicated.

Every administration or official entity shall be responsible for preserving its electronic registers in accordance with the provisions of the Electronic Transactions Law and the provisions of this Decree, and this responsibility is not negated in the event of engaging the services of other official or non-official entities to fulfil the conditions required for organising and preserving the electronic registers.

Every administration or official entity shall establish, within the limits of its competence, the list of administrative rules and procedures followed in preserving electronic registers and the administrative organisation of the electronic official instruments issued by it in a clear and comprehensible manner, particularly the manner of accessing them and making inquiries regarding them.

An electronically signed or sealed electronic instrument shall lose its authentic character if it is established that the identity data of its creator are not sound and consistent with the digital authentication certificate, or if the electronic signature or seal loses its close link with the data contained in the electronic instrument, or if it violates the provisions set forth in this Decree.

If the electronic instrument loses its authentic character for the reasons mentioned above, it shall be deemed to be an ordinary electronic instrument where the conditions for an ordinary electronic instrument set forth in the Electronic Transactions Law are met, and unless the authentic character is required for the validity of the legal act.

The electronic instrument shall not lose its authentic character if it is created by means of an electronic system that relies on an automated mechanism Automated Process operating on behalf of the public official or the person entrusted with a public service, provided that its use fulfils the conditions and soundness of automated creation and transmission.

A public official or a person entrusted with a public service may:

(1) Issue and deliver electronic copies of original paper authentic instruments.

(2) Issue and deliver certified true paper copies of original electronic authentic instruments.

(3) Electronically certify electronic copies of original paper instruments, electronic signatures or signatures on paper, and copies of electronic instruments.

Electronic copies of paper instruments and electronic certifications shall be subject to the conditions set forth in Article 8 of this Decree.

A paper or electronic copy of an original electronic authentic instrument shall be deemed to conform thereto unless contested by one of the parties, provided that the paper or electronic copy contains that through which the electronic original may be directly verified, and in case of doubt, the electronic or paper copy shall then be compared with the electronic original.

Save as otherwise provided by a contrary text, electronic authentic instruments, information, notices and other electronic documents may be sent to the concerned parties or users, and shall be deemed delivered and notified to the recipient entity if sent via an electronic medium, provided that the following conditions are met jointly:

(1) They must be issued and sent through an electronic system in accordance with the procedures established by the administration or official entity.

(2) They must be clear in terms of identifying the sending entity and the recipient entity, and the time and date during which they were sent.

The administration or official authority shall open an access point over electronic networks for the transmission and exchange of data, correspondence, electronic official deeds and other electronic documents, and shall place on its website the forms required to be completed and filled in and all downloading procedures, and secure the necessary means to enable the concerned parties to track the course of the transaction electronically, whilst taking into account the design of the systems to enable users with special needs and persons of determination to access and use them in accordance with the prescribed standards.

Priority shall be given to Lebanese companies registered in one of the commercial registers in Lebanon to provide the services of websites, access points, the exchange of data, correspondence, electronic official deeds and electronic documents, and electronic file management software.

Whilst complying with the applicable general interoperability framework, and in accordance with the prescribed encryption and protection technologies, the administration or official authority may secure a mechanism allowing the exchange of information and electronic register entries with any other administration or official authority, by embedding in the software adopted by it software elements comprising independent functions that enable other administrations or official authorities to communicate with it, in accordance with a set of clearly defined methods of communication between the various software components of the electronic software adopted by each administration or official authority.

All data relating to the electronic registers and the entries therein shall be preserved without the possibility of amendment thereof by any person who lacks standing, and in a manner whereby they may be accessed at any time for the purpose of their use by the employees assigned by the administration or the official entity, with the specification of the date, time, source, the sending and receiving entities, the entity or person that viewed or amended them, and the content of the amendment.

No electronic signature of a public official or a person entrusted with a public service on any electronic authentic instrument shall be recognised unless the following conditions are met cumulatively:

(1) That the electronic signature be directly and exclusively linked to the signatory.

(2) That the electronic signature be capable of identifying the signatory.

(3) That the electronic signature have been created by means of a signature-creation device that is beyond doubt under the sole control of the signatory, in accordance with the conditions provided for in Article 26 of this Decree.

(4) That the electronic signature be linked to the signed data in a manner that renders any amendment thereto, of whatever kind, directly detectable, even if the amendment does not alter the content or meaning of the signed data.

(5) That the electronic signature on any electronic authentic instrument be linked to a digital authentication certificate that is in force at the time the signature is effected and issued by a trusted service provider and in accordance with the provisions of Article 27 of this Decree.

When preserving electronic authentic instruments and the data relating thereto, the following conditions must be met:

(1) Following clear and documented rules and procedures for preserving the instruments.

(2) Preserving the electronic instruments and the data relating thereto in the format compatible with the regulations, laws and decisions in force at the entity that carried out the preservation process.

(3) Following clear and documented rules and standards to ensure the integrity of the preserved electronic instruments against unauthorised access and amendment, such that those rules include application, auditing and disaster recovery plans.

(4) If the preservation process requires determining the date and time, the date shall be determined according to the Gregorian calendar and the time by hour, minute and second according to Lebanese time, with the obligation to observe the official working hours adopted by the administration or official entity where applicable.

(5) Using appropriate technologies to ensure the preservation of each electronic instrument in the same form in which it was created, or to ensure that its content is identical to the content in which it was created.

(6) Every administration or official entity obliged to preserve electronic records must carry out "archiving" and backup operations periodically and automatically, in a manner that guarantees the rights of those who rely on these records.

Every administration or official entity that preserves electronic records and data shall be obliged to define the permissions for accessing and dealing with them in a manner consistent with the nature and type of these records and the operational need therefor, and shall also be obliged to comply with the standards relating to the protection of privacy provided for in the Electronic Transactions Law and the provisions of this Decree, and the information and data pertaining to the concerned parties may only be accessed by the competent employees and only when necessary.

The administration or official entity that provides services via electronic networks shall daily preserve a backup copy of the data, electronic authentic instruments and electronic records relating thereto on servers belonging to it, and shall secure a safe means for transmitting and preserving the documents and messages exchanged electronically, and shall take the necessary measures to prevent the amendment or alteration of such data without adopting the legal procedures, particularly personal data in accordance with the provisions of the Electronic Transactions Law.

The authentication certificate must include, at a minimum, the following:

(1) All the information that clearly identifies its issuing entity, the date of commencement of its effect, the duration of its validity, the manner of verifying it, and the verification data of the mechanism for creating the electronic signature or seal.

(2) Specifying the type of the signature or seal, the date and period of its validity, if it is linked to specific time periods, the scope of its operation, and its serial number if the administration or the concerned official entity requires serial numbers for electronic signatures and seals.

(3) The type of encryption algorithms used and the public encryption key, in accordance with the digital certificate policy and digital certification procedures.

(4) A set of data that identifies the accredited service provider and the state to which it belongs.

(5) The full three-part name of the signatory, his capacity, and the administration or official entity to which he belongs.

(6) Electronic signature verification data compatible with the signature creation data in accordance with a verification mechanism that ensures the validity and integrity of the electronic signature.

(7) The date and time of the commencement and expiry of the validity period of the certificate.

(8) The certificate identification code, which must be specific to the accredited service provider.

(9) The electronic signature or seal specific to the accredited service provider.

(10) The location of the certificate of the electronic signature or the electronic seal referred to in Paragraph (9) in a manner through which it can be accessed free of charge.

(11) The location of the services that can be used to inquire about the validity of the authentication certificate.

In the cases where the public official or the person entrusted with a public service is required to affix an electronic seal on any electronic official deed, the electronic seal shall not be recognised unless the conditions stipulated in Articles 25 to 27 of this Decree, which apply to the electronic seal, are fulfilled.

Every public official or person entrusted with a public service to whom an electronic official deed is presented must exercise the necessary care to verify the validity of the signature or seal appearing thereon and the electronic evidence which proves, on the date of the creation of the electronic official deed, that its signatory enjoys the capacity and competence to create this deed, by using the electronic signature or seal verification data associated therewith.

The electronic signature must be created through appropriate technical and procedural means in which the following conditions are met as a minimum:

(1) Ensuring the confidentiality of the electronic signature creation data used to create the electronic signature.

(2) Ensuring the use of the electronic signature creation data used to create the electronic signature once only.

(3) Ensuring the impossibility of deducing the electronic signature creation data used to create the electronic signature and that the electronic signature is protected, in a reliable manner, against forgery using the available technology.

(4) Ensuring the protection of the electronic signature creation data used to create the electronic signature by the signatory against their use by others.

(5) That the signature creation means does not alter the data to be signed or prevent the display of such data to the signatory prior to signing.

(6) That a trusted service provider issues or manages electronic signature creation data on behalf of the signatory.

The conditions mentioned in this Article shall be deemed fulfilled, if the electronic signature is created pursuant to a signature creation mechanism which the administration or the official entity has decided to make use of in accordance with the provisions of Article 6 of this Decree.

Where an electronic authentic instrument is issued in accordance with the conditions provided for in this Decree, the following shall be deemed established until the contrary is proved:

(1) That the electronic signature or seal is the signature or seal of the person or entity specified in the digital authentication certificate.

(2) That the electronic signature or seal was affixed by the person or entity specified in the digital authentication certificate, in accordance with the purpose specified therein.

(3) That the electronic authentic instrument has not undergone any alteration since the affixing of the electronic signature or seal thereon.

A plea of forgery of an electronic authentic instrument shall be subject to the same conditions and provisions as govern paper authentic instruments, in so far as is compatible with the electronic nature of the instrument,

In cases where an authentication service provider engaged by any official administration or entity loses any of the legal or technical conditions required for the issuance of an authentication certificate in accordance with the provisions of this Decree, the head of the official administration or entity shall be entitled to suspend the validity of the digital authentication certificate issued by the engaged authentication service provider, pursuant to a reasoned decision issued by him, without this measure affecting the electronic authentic instruments created or issued pursuant to such certificate prior to the issuance of the decision of suspension.

The authentication service provider shall suspend the certificate immediately upon being notified of the decision of suspension and shall notify whomsoever it may concern.
This Decree shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Subject to the provisions of special laws whereby the provisions suspending certain time limits were extended to terms exceeding the time limit set under this Law, the running of all statutory and contractual time limits granted to persons of public and private law for the purpose of exercising rights of all kinds shall be suspended ipso jure between 8 October 2023 and 31 March 2025 inclusive, whether such time limits are formal, procedural, customs-related, or their effect extends to the substance of the right.

The running of all judicial time limits before all Lebanese courts of their various kinds and degrees, granted to persons of public and private law for the purpose of exercising rights of all kinds, shall be suspended ipso jure between 31 March 2022 and 30 June 2024 inclusive, whether such time limits are formal, procedural, or their effect extends to the substance of the right.

The suspension of time limits shall cover administrative, civil, and commercial matters, and shall also cover the statutory time limits for the convening of the general assemblies of syndicates, associations, cooperatives, and all other bodies emanating therefrom.

In criminal matters, the time limits prescribed for the civil party, the defendant, or the accused to challenge formal defences and final judgments and decisions shall be suspended, and the civilly liable party and the guarantor shall benefit from this suspension in respect of decisions open to challenge by them.

The aforementioned time limits shall resume running anew upon the expiry of the suspension period.

The following shall be exempted from the provisions on suspension:

1 - Judicial time limits which the law leaves to the judge to assess.

2 - Time limits granted by the administration or set by it pursuant to its discretionary power.

3 - Time limits of forfeiture, prescription, discontinuance, and release in criminal cases, provided that the time limits set for exercising personal rights therein remain suspended.

4 - All statutory time limits and time limits relating to the convening of the general assemblies of syndicates and cooperatives that were held prior to the promulgation of this Law.

5 - Time limits relating to family matters, including alimony, guardianship, visitation, and others.

6 - Time limits set forth in the Rent Law promulgated on 9/5/2014 and its amendments.

Syndicates and cooperatives, with their general and executive bodies, shall continue their operations until the dates of the convening of ordinary assemblies in accordance with what is provided for in the laws and regulations pertaining to each of them, and shall remain standing with their president, councils, and bodies, and the acts carried out by them in accordance with the provisions set forth in their laws and regulations shall be deemed lawful.
The parties to agreements and contracts may waive the effect of the suspension, provided that the waiver is express and in writing.
Any final judgment in which the suspension of the time limits provided for in this Law was not observed shall be subject to retrial as from the date of entry into force of this Law.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Cases Requiring the Imposition of the Fine of Article 113:

1 - The fine of Clause 1 of Article 113 shall be imposed in the event of failure to issue an invoice, or a document similar to an invoice, whenever the issuance thereof is mandatory pursuant to the law.

This fine shall also be imposed when the invoice is deemed as if not issued due to the failure thereof, or the failure of the document similar thereto, to include the name of the supplier of goods or provider of services, and his tax identification number.

2 - The fine of Clause 2 of Article 113 shall be imposed upon issuing an invoice, or a document similar to an invoice, that contains one of the following violations:

* Failure to state the name of the supplier of goods or provider of services or his tax identification number.

* Failure to state the address of the supplier of goods or provider of services.

* Failure to state the name, address, or tax identification number of the person for whose benefit the invoice or the document similar thereto is issued, taking into consideration that there is no obligation to state the tax identification number of that person whenever he is a final consumer who is a natural person.

* Failure to state the rate of the Value Added Tax when it is due, even if the value thereof is stated.

* Failure to state the amount of the fee on food and beverage charges of various kinds determined pursuant to Article 22 of Law No. 671/1998 (the General Budget Law for the Year 1998), or failure to state the rate of the fee that was applied in the event it is due.

* Failure to state one of the elements of the transaction that is the subject of the invoice, without this leading to the inability to determine the full description of this transaction.

* Failure to state the serial number of the invoice and its date, and the imposition of the fine for this violation shall not preclude the Tax Administration from exercising its right to assess the revenues and profits of the offending taxpayer pursuant to the provisions of Article 42 of the Tax Procedures Law, when such violation constitutes an indicator of concealed revenues or profits.

3 - The fine provided for in Clause 2 of Article 113 shall not be imposed on taxpayers who do not include the tax identification number of their unregistered customers residing in Lebanon in their capacity as owners of commercial or industrial professions and establishments, or practitioners of liberal professions, or non-profit associations and institutions, if they provide the Tax Administration with information on the names of those customers and their detailed addresses quarterly within a period of 20 days from the end of the quarter.

4 - The fine of Clause 1 of Article 113 shall be imposed on money changers when they refrain from issuing invoices for the commercial transactions they carry out, such as transactions of exchanging various currencies, transactions of discounting cheques, or other transactions, at a rate of two percent (2%) on a proportion of one percent (1%) of the value of each transaction.

The fine of Clause 2 of Article 113 shall also be imposed on money changers when they issue invoices for the commercial transactions they carry out in which the required information pursuant to the legal and regulatory texts in this regard is not available, at a rate of half a percent (0.5%) on a proportion of one percent (1%) of the value of each transaction.

5 - The fine of Clause 1 of Article 113 shall be imposed on taxpayers who practice the activity of selling prepaid mobile phone cards when they refrain from issuing invoices for the commercial transactions they carry out, at a rate of two percent (2%) on a proportion of one and a half percent (1.5%) of the value of each transaction.

The fine of Clause 2 of Article 113 shall also be imposed on taxpayers who practice the activity of selling prepaid mobile phone cards when they issue invoices for the commercial transactions they carry out in which the required information pursuant to the legal and regulatory texts in this regard is not available, at a rate of half a percent (0.5%) on a proportion of one and a half percent (1.5%) of the value of each transaction.

6 - In all cases, the fine of Clause 1 and the fine of Clause 2 of Article 113 may not be imposed together for violations related to the same invoices.

7 - In the event that customs brokers fail to issue the invoices mandatorily imposed on them, or in the event that they commit a violation falling under the Second Clause of Article 113, their actual revenues from fees and endeavours shall be adopted, for the purpose of imposing the fine of either the First or Second Clause, as the value of the unissued invoice or of the offending invoice, and customs and port duties, fiscal stamps, and unloading, transport, and loading expenses shall not be calculated therein.

Conducting an exceptional revaluation of inventory and fixed assets for income tax taxpayers and conducting an exceptional treatment of positive and negative exchange differences

- Conducting an exceptional revaluation of inventory and fixed assets:

* Regarding the revaluation of inventory:

First: Natural and legal persons subject to income tax on the basis of real profit who are required to keep regular accounting entries pursuant to legal or regulatory provisions may, for the periods ending on 31/12/2026 for those who adopt the calendar fiscal year, and the end of the 2026 business year for those who adopt a special fiscal year, conduct an annual revaluation process of the balance of their inventory as at the end of the business year, starting from the 2022 business year and until the end of the business of the year 2026, in accordance with the following:

1 - The revaluation application must be submitted to the Tax Administration within a period of two months from the effective date of this Law in respect of the year 2023 and within the first month of each subsequent year, accompanied by an undertaking from the taxpayer to retain all the documents provided for in Clause Third.

2 - The inventory must be revalued in accordance with its historical cost in foreign currency on the basis of the actual exchange rate at the end of the relevant year.

3 - The difference between the cost of acquisition of the inventory (or the value acquired upon acquisition) and its actual value at the end of the year shall be recorded in the inventory account on the one hand, and in a separate account within the inventory revaluation differences account on the other hand.

4 - The positive differences resulting from the revaluation process recorded within the separate account referred to in Clause 3 above shall not be subject to the tax on profits.

4-2- The positive differences resulting from the revaluation process recorded within the separate account referred to in Clause 3 above shall not be subject to any kind of taxes.

5 - Taxpayers who recorded in their accounting entries the acquired inventory at a value other than its actual value and recorded the difference between that value and its actual value as exchange differences or under any other cost account in the profit and loss accounts, must re-correct those entries according to the actual value, and they must amend their declarations and pay the tax difference, if due, before submitting the inventory revaluation application.

6 - Taxpayers who have not declared the business of the years 2020, 2021 and 2022 shall not be permitted to benefit from the revaluation provisions, nor shall taxpayers who do not declare any subsequent year be permitted to benefit from the revaluation provisions for the inventory of that year.

7 - The revaluation process shall be conducted through one of the offices of certified public accountants chosen by the concerned party.

8 - Revaluation differences may be used:

- To cover losses that are still apparent and specified in the balance sheet.

- To increase capital in capital companies without the tax on distributions falling due.

- To distribute them to shareholders and quota-holders in capital companies, in which case they shall be subject to the tax on distributions if distributed before the lapse of five years from the revaluation process, and shall be exempted from that tax if distributed after the lapse of that period.

9 - Taxpayers who commence their business on a date subsequent to the date of publication of this Law shall have the right to benefit from the revaluation provisions for each year from the date they commence business and until the expiry of the validity of this Law.

10 - Taxpayers who benefit from tax exemptions may benefit from the provisions of this Article.

Taxpayers assessed on the basis of lump-sum profit or estimated profit may also conduct a revaluation process of their inventory in accordance with the provisions set forth above if they submit an application to the Tax Administration to convert their assessment to the basis of real profit prior to commencing the revaluation process.

Second: The applicant for revaluation shall have the right to amend the value of their inventory as it is at the end of the year starting from the date of submitting the application, and if the Tax Administration refuses to approve its result or amends this result, it must notify the concerned party of its reasoned decision of refusal or amendment, and the taxpayer must amend their entries and their declaration, which they had previously submitted, and they shall also have the right to object before the competent Income Tax Objections Committee in accordance with the procedures provided for in the Tax Procedures Law.

If the Tax Administration does not decide upon the revaluation application within a period of one year from the date of its submission, the application shall be deemed accepted by operation of law.

Third: The documents shown below must be ready with the taxpayer who wishes to conduct the revaluation upon submitting the revaluation application, under penalty of refusal of their application:

- The supporting documents for the warehouses and showrooms.

- A copy of the purchase invoices relating to the revalued inventory.

- The inventory list prepared by the taxpayer at the end of the business of each year (physical inventory) for all items.

- The computerised inventory list closed at the end of each year for all items, if any.

- The inventory register for all items at the end of the year.

- Detailed cards for all items at the end of the business of each year on an (Excel) file and on a compact disc (CD), provided that they include the following information: item code and name, purchase date, supplier name, purchase invoice number, quantity purchased, purchase cost in Lebanese Pounds, sale date, customer name, sales invoice number, quantity sold, exit cost in Lebanese Pounds, remaining quantity, cost of remaining inventory.

- The contracts pursuant to which the taxpayer's goods are placed on consignment with third parties.

Fourth: The taxpayer must retain, in paper or electronic form, a statement showing accurately the basic historical cost of the revalued goods and the differences that have been approved.

Fifth: If one of the persons who benefited from the revaluation of their inventory submits an application to destroy part of that inventory, the inventory whose destruction is approved by the Tax Administration shall then be removed from their accounts at its book value prior to the valuation and from the change in inventory account, and the revaluation value of the inventory approved to be destroyed shall be deducted from the inventory revaluation differences account.

* Conducting an exceptional revaluation of fixed assets:

Natural and legal persons subject to income tax on the basis of real profit who are required to keep regular accounting entries pursuant to legal or regulatory provisions, including those who have previously carried out a valuation process or an appraisal process in accordance with the provisions of Article 45 of the Income Tax Law, may, annually, and for the periods ending on 31/12/2026 for those who adopt the calendar fiscal year, and the end of the 2026 business year for those who adopt a special fiscal year, conduct an exceptional revaluation of all elements of fixed assets (including shares, debt securities, participation securities and shares, real estate, and other fixed assets) as at the end of the business year, to correct the effects of monetary inflation resulting from the change in the values of those assets, starting from the end of the 2022 business year and until the end of the 2026 business year.

The revaluation process shall cover all the assets referred to in the preceding paragraph that are entered in the enterprise's records at a date prior to the first of January of each year for those who adopt the calendar fiscal year and before the beginning of the first month of each fiscal year for those who adopt a special fiscal year, provided that the value of the revalued assets does not exceed the market price at the date of conducting the revaluation process.

The revaluation process shall be conducted through one of the sworn appraisal experts in Lebanon in respect of real estate that constitutes fixed assets, and through one of the experts affiliated with the Lebanese Association of Certified Public Accountants in respect of the remaining assets, chosen by the concerned party.

The positive differences resulting from the revaluation process shall not be subject to the tax on profits.

The depreciation of the revalued assets shall be calculated in accordance with the following:

- If they were wholly depreciated prior to the revaluation, no new depreciation may be made.

- If they were not wholly depreciated prior to the revaluation, depreciation for the remaining period of the life of the asset shall be calculated on the new value of the remaining balance.

Those differences may be used:

- To cover losses that are still apparent and specified in the balance sheet.

- To increase capital in capital companies without the tax on distributions falling due.

- To distribute them to shareholders and quota-holders in capital companies, in which case they shall be subject to the tax on distributions if distributed before the lapse of five years from the revaluation process, and shall be exempted from that tax if distributed after the lapse of that period.

Taxpayers assessed on the basis of lump-sum or estimated profit shall benefit from the revaluation if the existence of documents permitting the revaluation of the elements of fixed assets is proven.

In all cases, these provisions may not, in respect of banks, conflict with the Code of Money and Credit and all other regulatory and implementing texts issued by the Banque du Liban.

The competent financial unit shall decide upon the revaluation process, and if it refuses to approve its result or amends this result, it must notify the concerned parties of its reasoned decision of refusal or amendment.

If the Tax Administration does not decide upon the application for approval of the revaluation process within a period of one year from the date of its submission, the application shall be deemed accepted by operation of law.

Regarding the conduct of an exceptional treatment of positive and negative exchange differences

Notwithstanding any other text and for tax purposes, natural and legal persons required to keep regular accounting entries pursuant to legal or regulatory provisions must, for the periods ending on 31/12/2026 for those who adopt the calendar fiscal year, and the end of the 2026 business year for those who adopt a special fiscal year, conduct an exceptional treatment of positive and negative exchange differences relating to accounts of the Fourth and Fifth Classes as at the end of the business year, starting from the end of the 2022 business year and until the end of the business of the year 2026 for those who adopt a special fiscal year, as follows:

* The value of accounts of the Fourth and Fifth Classes recorded in foreign currency shall be calculated on the basis of the exchange rate adopted by the Banque du Liban at the end of each year.

* Exchange differences, whether positive or negative, relating to accounts of the Fourth and Fifth Classes closed at the end of the year shall not be included in the tax result except in the following case:

If the negative exchange differences resulting from the calculation of salaries and wages paid in foreign currency are at the legally specified exchange rate, they shall be excluded from the paragraph above and shall be included among the deductible charges.

The details of implementation of this Article shall be determined, where necessary, by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

This Decision determines the details of application of the provisions relating to the revaluation of inventory provided for by the second Article of Law No. 330 dated 4/12/2024 (Authorising income tax taxpayers to revalue their inventory).

Inventory means inventory as set out in the chart of accounts in Annex No. 2 of Decision No. 111 dated 2/2/1982, which includes the following accounts:

- Consumable raw materials.

- Work in progress (goods, works and services, including projects).

- Products (finished goods, intermediate products, production waste).

- Goods held for sale, whether tangible or intangible.

- Real estate and buildings subject to trading, including projects under completion.

The natural and legal persons who are permitted to carry out the revaluation operation of their inventory balance referred to in the first Article of this Decision are:

Income tax taxpayers on the basis of actual profit, including taxpayers who benefit from tax exemptions pursuant to the provisions of Article 5 bis of the Income Tax Law or pursuant to any other legal provisions.

Income tax taxpayers on the basis of lump-sum profit, with the exception of those who are compulsorily subject to assessment on the basis of lump-sum profit in accordance with the provisions of Article 44 of Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12/1/1959 and its amendments (the Income Tax Law), unless they carry on another activity assessed on the basis of actual profit, in which case they may carry out a revaluation operation of their inventory balance relating exclusively to that activity.

Income tax taxpayers on the basis of estimated profit.

Taxpayers who commence their business on a date subsequent to the date of 5/12/2024 are also entitled to benefit from the revaluation provisions for each year from the date of commencement of their business and until the end of the operations of the year 2026 in accordance with the provisions set out in Law No. 330/2024 and this Decision.

The authorisation for lump-sum profit taxpayers and estimated profit taxpayers to carry out a revaluation of their inventory is conditional upon their submitting applications to the competent financial unit within whose jurisdiction their place of assessment is located, to convert their assessment to the basis of actual profit.

These taxpayers may commence the revaluation operation immediately upon submitting those applications.

The running of all statutory and contractual time limits granted to persons under public and private law is suspended by operation of law between 8 October 2023 and 31 March 2025 inclusive, whether such time limits are formal or procedural or whether their effect extends to the substance of the right, and the suspension of time limits shall encompass administrative, civil and commercial matters.

These time limits are enumerated as follows:

1 - The time limits granted to non-Lebanese persons or to companies deemed to be non-Lebanese in respect of acquisition of ownership and the building annotation (Law on the Acquisition by Non-Lebanese of Real Property Rights).

2 - The time limit of six months for declaring new constructions before the head of the auxiliary office (Article 60 of Decision No. 189/1926).

3 - The time limit for priority of registration in the Real Property Register, whereby if the concerned party fails to pay the fees within three days, he loses the right of priority of registration (Article 68 of Decision No. 188/1926).

4 - The five-year time limit for an ordinary power of attorney relating to the registration of a right in rem (Article 50 of Decision No. 188/1926).

5 - The time limits prescribed for provisional entries registered in the real property folios which lapse by operation of law upon the expiry of those time limits in accordance with Articles 25, 26 and 29 of Decision No. 188/1926 as amended by Law 76 issued on 3/4/1999

6 - The time limits provided for in Article 26 of the Law of the Public Corporation for Housing (Subdivision of a Building under Construction) No. 539/1996 in respect of prohibiting the carrying out of any transaction on the subdivided unit if it is not completed and an occupancy permit therefor is not produced within three years from the date of subdivision.

7 - The time limit prescribed in Article 53 of the 2019 Budget, whereby the fee is doubled if contracts of sale and irrevocable powers of attorney are not registered within three years.

Time limits of whatever kind which expired prior to the date of the suspension of time limits on 8/10/2023 shall not benefit from the suspension of time limits; as for time limits which began to run prior to the suspension of time limits and have not been exhausted, the remaining time limit shall be suspended and shall resume running on 1 April 2025; as for a time limit which begins within the period of suspension, the entire time limit shall begin to run upon the expiry of the effect of the suspension law from the first of April 2025.

The time limit for submitting applications expressing the wish to carry out the revaluation operation for income tax taxpayers assessed on the basis of actual profit, which includes the undertaking to retain the required documents relating to the inventory or is accompanied by a separate letter containing such undertaking, and the time limit for submitting applications to convert the assessment to the basis of actual profit by taxpayers assessed on the basis of lump-sum profit or estimated profit, shall be determined as follows:

- Before 02/06/2025 in respect of the operations of the year 2023

- Before 01/05/2025 in respect of the operations of the year 2024

- Before 01/02/2026 in respect of the operations of the year 2025

- Before 01/02/2027 in respect of the operations of the year 2026

Taxpayers who do not submit the applications referred to above within the time limit specified in this Article shall forfeit their right to carry out the valuation operation.

The documents set out below must be ready in the possession of the taxpayer who wishes to carry out the revaluation upon submitting the revaluation application:

- Supporting documents for the warehouses and showrooms, where such warehouses and showrooms exist.

- A copy of the purchase invoices relating to the revalued inventory.

- The inventory count prepared by the taxpayer at the end of the operations of each year (physical inventory count) for all items.

- The computerised inventory count closed at the end of each year for all items, where it exists.

- The inventory register for all items at the end of the year.

- Detailed cards for all items at the end of the operations of each year in an (Excel) file and on a compact disc, provided that they include the following information: item code and name, purchase date, supplier name, purchase invoice number, quantity purchased, purchase cost in Lebanese Pounds, sale date, customer name, sales invoice number, quantity sold, withdrawal cost in Lebanese Pounds, remaining quantity, and cost of the remaining inventory, subject to compliance with the provisions relating to the adoption of the simplified system for issuing invoices in respect of taxpayers who have obtained approval to adopt that system.

- Contracts pursuant to which the taxpayer's goods are placed on consignment with third parties.

The taxpayer shall be required to retain, in paper or electronic form, a statement accurately showing the original historical cost of the revalued goods and the differences that have been approved,

Taxpayers who adopt, in closing their accounts with the approval of the competent financial departments, a special financial year must comply with the provisions of Decision No. 645/1 dated 4/6/2024 to the effect that their special financial year may not begin on a date other than the beginning of any of the second, third, or fourth quarters of the calendar year, effective from the operations of the year 2025; and in the event of failure by such taxpayers to comply voluntarily, the tax administration shall enforce the provisions set forth in the aforementioned Decision with respect to converting their year to the calendar year.

In respect of the inventory balance as it stands on 31/12/2022 or at the end of the 2022 operating year for those who adopt a special financial year in closing their accounts, the balance shall remain as it is and shall be recorded after its revaluation in the opening accounts of the 2023 operating year at the rate specified in Article Eleven of this Decision, and taxpayers shall record the revaluation variances in a separate account within the equity accounts pertaining to the 2023 operating year (Account No. 103 Revaluation Variances).

Taxpayers who recorded in their accounting entries the acquired inventory at a value other than its actual value and recorded the difference between that value and its actual value as exchange differences or under any other cost account in the profit and loss accounts, may not revalue the inventory balance of any year of the years for which they are legally authorised to revalue the inventory balance, unless they re-correct those entries, amend the return pertaining to each year, and pay the tax difference and fines in accordance with the provisions of Article 40 of the Tax Procedures Law, even if mission orders had been issued to audit their operations for the years 2021 and 2022

And they shall also submit the auditors' report pursuant to the amended return, if they are among the taxpayers obliged to submit that report.

Taxpayers who have not declared the operations of the years 2020, 2021 and 2022 prior to the publication of Law No. 330/2024 shall not be permitted to benefit from the revaluation provisions, nor shall taxpayers who do not declare for any subsequent year be permitted to benefit from the revaluation provisions for the inventory of that year.

The revaluation operation shall be carried out through one of the offices of certified public accountants chosen by the concerned party, and the application for approval of the revaluation must be submitted to the competent finance department within the jurisdiction of which their centre of assessment is located, accompanied by the report prepared by the accounting office within the time limit specified for submitting the annual return of the results of operations.

The historical cost in foreign currency of the inventory shall be determined on the basis of the value of the invoices or contracts, if issued in a foreign currency, or on the basis of the actual exchange rate as at the date of acquisition if the cost is recorded in Lebanese Pounds.

The revaluation report must include the new value in Lebanese Pounds and the value of the revalued real estate inventory must not exceed the market price as at the date of conducting the revaluation operation.

Taxpayers who have carried out the revaluation operation may use the positive differences resulting from that operation to cover audited losses eligible to be carried forward in accordance with the provisions of Article 16 of the Income Tax Law, provided that the provisions of Article 24 of Law automatically in force No. 10 dated 15/11/2022 (the General Budget Law for the year 2022), which permitted the carrying forward of the deficit incurred during the year 2020 for an additional year, are observed.

Capital companies may use the positive differences resulting from the revaluation of the inventory balance:

To increase the capital without the tax on distributions falling due; however, if they reduce their capital before the expiry of 5 years from its increase, the value of the reduction shall be subject to the tax on distributions.

To distribute them to shareholders and quota-holders without the tax on distributions falling due if the distribution takes place after the expiry of 5 years from the date of carrying out the revaluation operation.

However, if the distribution takes place before the expiry of that period, the tax on distributions shall fall due, even if the company that carried out the distribution benefits from a permanent or exceptional exemption from the tax on distributions pursuant to legal texts.

The positive differences resulting from the revaluation recorded in the equity account of foreign capital companies operating in Lebanon (branches of foreign companies) shall not be deemed automatically distributed.

Capital companies may not distribute revaluation differences to shareholders or quota-holders before covering losses, if any exist.

If a capital company increases its capital from the positive differences resulting from the revaluation of its inventory balance in any of the years in which the revaluation of its inventory is permitted, and then ceases operations before the expiry of five years from the revaluation operation, the differences that were used to increase the capital shall be deemed subject to the tax on distributions, unless such cessation is the result of bankruptcy.

If the taxpayers meet the conditions stipulated in Articles Eight and Nine of this Decision, namely with respect to correcting the entries for the inventory in the event that it was recorded at other than its actual value, and with respect to complying with the obligation to file a return for the years subject to assessment, they may choose the year in which they wish to carry out a revaluation of the inventory balance as it stands in the year preceding that year, provided that the revaluation operation for the years 2024 and thereafter is limited to the inventory acquired during the preceding year which still remains in the balance of that year, and the tax administration shall retain the right to audit with respect to the fulfilment of the conditions mentioned above.

Taxpayers who have carried out a revaluation operation of their inventory balance in any of the years covered by the revaluation must record the difference between the cost of acquisition of the inventory or its acquired value upon acquisition and its value after revaluation in the inventory account on the one hand, and in a separate account within the equity accounts on the other hand, (Account No. 103 Revaluation Differences).

The profit realised by taxpayers as a result of the sale of revalued inventory, represented by the difference between the sale value and the value after revaluation, shall be entered into the result account.

The negative difference realised as a result of the sale of revalued inventory, represented by the difference between the sale value and the value after revaluation, shall be deducted from the revaluation differences recorded in Account No. 103

The positive differences resulting from the revaluation operation recorded in the equity accounts shall not be subject to the tax on profits (Title I tax of the Income Tax Law).

Furthermore, no negative exchange differences resulting from inventory that was previously valued, which may subsequently arise due to any decline in the exchange rate of the dollar against the Lebanese pound, may be deducted from the revenues of the taxpayer, and they must be deducted from the revaluation differences account relating to the inventory, and if that account has been closed due to its use, whether to cover losses, to increase capital, or for distribution to shareholders, such differences shall be considered non-deductible.

Any taxpayer who has carried out a revaluation operation of the balance of his inventory in accordance with the provisions set forth in this Decision may rectify his accounting entries relating to that inventory in accordance with its revalued value, and where the Tax Administration rejects or amends the revaluation operation, it shall notify the concerned party of its reasoned decision of rejection or amendment, and he may object to the decision of the Administration in accordance with the procedures specified in the Tax Procedures Law.

Where the Tax Administration does not decide on the application for approval of the revaluation operation within a period of one year from the date on which it was notified of the application, the revaluation operation shall be deemed accepted by operation of law.

Inventory that is destroyed in accordance with the implementing texts specified in the relevant regulatory decisions following the approval of the Tax Administration, or donated in accordance with the legal texts, shall be removed from the accounts of the taxpayer at its book value prior to the valuation and from the change from inventory account, and the revaluation value of the donated inventory or of the inventory approved for destruction shall be deducted from the inventory revaluation differences account.

With respect to banks, the same rules specified in this Decision shall be adopted in the inventory revaluation operation, including real properties acquired in settlement of a debt, in so far as they do not conflict with the provisions of the Code of Money and Credit and all other regulatory and implementing texts issued by the Banque du Liban.
This Decision shall be published in the Official Gazette and on the website of the Ministry of Finance and shall enter into force immediately upon its publication.

The text of the First Article of the Labour Law promulgated on 23/9/1946 shall be repealed and replaced by the following text:

"First Article (New):

An employer is every natural or legal person who employs a wage-earner under a written or verbal employment contract, in consideration of a wage even if such wage is in kind or a share in the profits".

- The bill aiming to amend the provisions of Articles 1, 2, and 12 of the Labour Law promulgated on 23/9/1946 to include flexible work, as amended by the Committee on Public Health, Labour and Social Affairs, has been ratified.

- This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The text of Article 2 of the Labour Law promulgated on 23/9/1946 shall be repealed and replaced by the following text:

"Second Article (New):

A wage-earner is every man, woman or juvenile who works for a wage for an employer in the conditions set out in the First Article, on a full-time, part-time or seasonal basis, in person or remotely, and even if he uses his own equipment and tools to execute the work".

The text of Article 12 of the Labour Law promulgated on 23/9/1946 shall be repealed and replaced by the following text:

"Article 12 (New):

1 - An individual employment contract is an agreement whereby the wage-earner undertakes thereunder to willingly provide his work for the benefit of an employer and under his supervision and control in consideration of a wage regardless of the place of work.

2 - The written contract must be drawn up in the Arabic language and may be translated into a foreign language if the employer or the wage-earner is a foreigner who does not know the Arabic language".

The text of the following Article shall be added to the Labour Law promulgated on 23/9/1946:

"Article 12/1:

Where the nature of the work so permits, the employer and the wage-earner may agree to work in accordance with compressed working hours provided that the weekly working hours do not exceed 48 hours and without prejudice to the intermittent and continuous daily rest hours".

There shall be added to the Labour Law issued on 23/9/1946 the text of the following article:

"Article 12/2:

1 - Part-time work shall be considered work the working hours of which are not less than one-third of the working hours of comparable workers in the same establishment or company working full-time, or of employees working in the same branch of activity where there are no comparable workers working full-time in that establishment or company, and do not exceed two-thirds thereof.

2 - A part-time employment contract shall be in writing or oral, and agreement shall be reached therein on the nature of the employee's work, his working hours, the manner of their distribution over the week, month or year, and the amount of his remuneration with clarification of its components.

3 - Full-time employees affected by partial unemployment and by a collective and temporary reduction of their normal working hours, whether for economic, technical or structural reasons or exceptional circumstances in accordance with the provisions of this Law, shall not be considered employees working part-time."

There shall be added to the Labour Law issued on 23/9/1946 the text of the following article:

"Article 12/3:

The employer may, when the interest of the establishment so requires, ask the part-time employee to perform additional working hours, provided that agreement is reached on the possibility of working additional hours upon contracting, or with the express consent of the employee in the event of no prior agreement, provided that the employee is notified at least three days in advance of the additional working hours required of him, and that the additional working hours do not exceed ten per cent of the part-time working hours agreed upon between the two parties unless the employee agrees to such increase, the remuneration for the additional hour shall be paid with a fifty per cent increase over the remuneration for the working hour of the part-time employee."

There shall be added to the Labour Law issued on 23/9/1946 the text of the following article:

"Article 12/4:

Agreement may be reached in writing between the employee and the employer to transfer from full-time work to part-time work:

1 - For a maximum period of two years for an employee who wishes to pursue studies.

2 - For a maximum period of one year after the end of maternity leave for a working woman."

There shall be added to the Labour Law issued on 23/9/1946 the text of the following article:

"Article 12/5:

Employees working part-time shall enjoy priority to transfer to the full-time work regime, in the event that the required conditions are met, if the employer wishes to fill vacant or newly created full-time positions."

The text of the following Article shall be added to the Labour Law issued on 23/9/1946:

"Article 12/6: Seasonal work shall be deemed to be work which nature requires to be performed within a period of time not exceeding six months, and it shall be considered to be in the nature of fixed-term contracts".

The text of the following Article shall be added to the Labour Law issued on 23/9/1946:

"Article 12/7:

Remote work is work performed by the employee from any place of his choice other than the employer's workplace, on a full-time or part-time basis, in accordance with the directives and regulations of the employer."

The text of the following Article shall be added to the Labour Law issued on 23/9/1946:

"Article 12/8:

1 - Part-time, seasonal and remote employees shall benefit from the same protection as that enjoyed by comparable permanent and in-person employees in the establishment or company with respect to the right to:

- Organisation and the right to collective bargaining;

- Occupational safety and health;

- Non-discrimination in employment and occupation.

2 - Part-time or remote employees shall benefit from the rights pertaining to comparable full-time or in-person employees in the establishment or company in accordance with the provisions of the Labour and Social Security Laws, provided that the rule of proportionality based on the number of working hours is adopted in calculating and determining their entitlements and rights."

The text of the following Article shall be added to the Labour Law issued on 23/9/1946:

"Article 12/9:

The employer shall keep records showing the names of the employees, the type of their contracts, the number of their working hours, the types of their activity and the other conditions and terms of their work. The Labour, Prevention and Safety Inspection Service at the Ministry of Labour shall have the right to inspect them when necessary."

The text of the following Article shall be added to the Labour Law issued on 23/9/1946:

"Article 12/10:
