(Field of the Scope of Application of the Provisions of the Law)

All lease contracts of built real properties for non-residential premises concluded and whose original term expired before 23/7/1992 shall be subject to the provisions of this Law.

(Concept of Non-Residential Premises)

Considered as non-residential premises are those leased for the exercise of commerce, industry, any liberal profession regulated by a law, a craft profession, or any other non-residential activity.

(Extension)

A- The lease in non-residential premises shall be extended for a maximum period of four years from the date of entry into force of this Law in the event that the lessor claims the gradual increases on the rent specified in the Sixth Article of this Law, after which the lease shall become free and subject to the will of the contracting parties.

B- The lease shall be extended for a period of two years only from the date of entry into force of this Law in the event that the lessor waives his right to the gradual increases specified in the Sixth Article of this Law. Account shall be taken of the implicit waiver resulting from the failure of the lessor to submit any application to determine the fair rent during the two years following the issuance of this Law.

(Fair Rent)

The fair rent shall be calculated on the basis of a rate of 8% (eight per cent) of the sale value of the leased premises in its present condition as if it were vacant.

(Method of determining the fair rent)

The fair rent shall be determined in the following manner:

First - By mutual consent between the lessor and the lessee in accordance with the following procedures:

a. The lessor shall send a letter of invitation to negotiate to the lessee by means of a registered open postcard with acknowledgment of receipt or by means of a letter through a notary public.

b. The lessee shall reply to the invitation through a letter sent to the lessor within a period of 20 (twenty) days from the date of service or the date of establishing the impossibility of effecting the service procedure by the process server. In the event that he fails to reply within the period specified above, the provisions of paragraph Second of the present Article shall apply.

c. In the event that an amicable agreement is reached, a written contract shall be signed in this regard.

Second - In the event that an amicable agreement on the determination of the fair rent is not reached in accordance with what is set forth above, the lessor or the lessee shall follow the following procedures:

a. The lessor or the lessee shall apply to the Single Civil Judge hearing lease actions within whose jurisdiction the leased premises are located, by way of a statement of claim or a joint petition in order to have the fair rent determined judicially.

b. The Single Judge shall hear the action or the joint petition in accordance with the following rules of procedure:

1- Prior to taking any other measure and without being bound by the time limits for exchange of pleadings, the judge shall issue his decision in chambers appointing an expert within a period of one week from the date on which the action or the joint petition is filed before him.

2- The expertise shall be subject to the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, and the expert shall submit his report within a maximum period of two weeks from the date on which he is notified of the mission. This period shall be extendable for an equal duration and once only upon the request of the expert and for serious and substantive grounds by a reasoned decision, under penalty of his replacement by another expert by a decision issued in chambers.

3- Immediately upon receipt of the report, it shall be served upon the two parties through the court registry, and they shall have a period of one week to comment thereon. This period shall not be extendable except for an equal duration and once only by a reasoned decision of the judge and for serious grounds, provided that the exchange takes place at the registry, under penalty of inadmissibility of any pleading or comment outside thereof.

4- Following the closing of the proceedings, the judge shall issue his judgment within a maximum period of one month following the closing of the proceedings.

c. Subject to Article 50 of the Lease Law dated 9/5/2014, the decision of the judge determining the fair rent shall be subject to appeal within a period of eight days from the date of service, and the Court of Appeal shall hear the appeal brought before it in accordance with the rules of procedure specified above. The decision of the Court of Appeal shall be final and not subject to any ordinary or extraordinary means of recourse.

(Gradual Increases)

During the term of extension of the lease in accordance with the provisions of Article /3/ of this Law, the rent due on the date of entry into force of this Law shall be increased annually and successively in accordance with the following:

1- 25% twenty-five per cent of the value of the difference of the increase between the rent applicable prior to the entry into force of this Law and the fair market rent referred to above, for the first year of the extension years following the date of entry into force of this Law.

2- 50% fifty per cent of the value of the difference of the increase noted above, for the second year of the extension period.

3- The rent in the third and fourth years shall be equal to the value of the fair market rent referred to in Article 4 above.

At the end of the fourth extension year, the lease shall become free.

(Inadmissibility of Assignment of the Leased Premises and Subleasing)

The lessee may not assign the leased premises or sublease them wholly or partially save with the express and written consent of the lessor and under the conditions agreed upon.

If the original lessee assigns the leased premises and was expressly and in writing authorised to do so in the original lease contract or the contract extended by operation of law, the assignees shall benefit from the statutory extension and shall substitute the original lessee, and their relationship with the lessor shall become direct.

In the event of a total or partial sublease with the express and written consent of the owner in the original or extended contract, the lease relationship shall remain confined between the lessor and the original lessee, and the term of the sublease shall terminate upon the termination of the term of the original lease.

A sublease concluded as of 23/7/1992 shall be subject to freedom of contract in accordance with the provisions of Law No. 159/92.

The owner must request the joinder of the sublessee in every action brought against the original lessee, and the judgment rendered against the original lessee shall have the force of res judicata against the sublessee, provided that the sublessee shall be entitled to claim compensation from the original lessee in the event that bad faith, fault, or negligence on the part of the latter is established.

(Cases of Forfeiture of the Right to Statutory Extension)

The right to extension shall be forfeited, and the tenant and whoever replaces him shall be ordered to be evicted, in the following cases:

أ. If he fails to pay the rent that has fallen due from him within two months after being served with a formal notice by means of an unsealed registered postcard with acknowledgment of receipt, or by means of a letter through a notary public, or by means of a formal notice issued by the Execution Department in accordance with the provisions of Article /51/ of the Rent Law dated 9/5/2014 and its amendments. Service shall be effected in accordance with the procedures set forth in Chapter Four of the Code of Civil Procedure. The formal notice shall be exempt from any fee.

As for a legal person, it must, within a period of two months from the date of entry into force of this Law, elect a domicile, failing which the service procedures provided for in the Code of Civil Procedure shall apply to it.

In the event that it is impossible to effect the services referred to in the preceding paragraph, service shall be effected by publication in two local daily newspapers designated by the Judge of Urgent Matters after verifying the impossibility of service through the certificates issued by the process servers and without the need for any further investigation, upon a request by the lessor by way of a petition that is not subject to any fee or stamp duty of any kind whatsoever, and a copy of the formal notice shall be affixed to the door of the leased premises by a bailiff, and the two-month period shall run from the date of completion of the last formality of publication or affixation.

In the event that it is impossible to effect service of the formal notice issued by the Execution Department, service shall be effected by publication and affixation in accordance with the same procedures pursuant to a decision issued by the Head of the Execution Department.

The tenant shall bear the expenses of these formalities.

ب. If it is established that the tenant has refrained from paying the rents due from him on three consecutive occasions except after being served with a formal notice, in a manner that establishes bad faith on his part.

ج. If the tenant misuses the leased premises by causing damage thereto not resulting from normal use, or uses them or permits their use in a manner inconsistent with the terms of the contract without the express and written consent of the lessor.

Installations erected by the tenant at his own expense shall not be deemed a misuse of the leased premises, provided that they do not impair the structural soundness of the building. Works for installing an elevator and a water tank, or providing heating, cooling, or hot water, shall be deemed of this nature. Likewise, works relating to the rehabilitation of the leased premises or the entrances of the building that are necessary for the needs of a disabled person residing therein, in accordance with the minimum standards for buildings and facilities pursuant to Law No. 220/2000 relating to the Rights of Disabled Persons, shall not be deemed a misuse of the leased premises, provided that such works are technically feasible and do not impair the structural soundness of the building.

With the exception of simple superficial decoration and decor works and the installation of individual cooling and heating units, a tenant who wishes to benefit from the provisions of this Article must summon the lessor before the Judge of Urgent Matters to seek permission to carry out the works he wishes to undertake and which he must specify, in order to enable the court to assess their legality and appropriateness, provided that in all cases he obtains the administrative permits where such works so require.

The tenant must take out insurance, the costs of which he alone shall bear, against all risks that may result from the works he carries out, as well as the expenses of the aforementioned works and the expenses of restoring the parts of the building that may have been damaged on account of the works to their former condition, without having the right of recourse against the owner to claim the same or any part thereof, whether during his occupancy of the leased premises or on the date of termination of such occupancy.

The value of the improvements resulting from the works mentioned in this paragraph shall not be included in the calculation of the recovery compensation.

In all the cases mentioned above with respect to the misuse of the leased premises, it shall not be required that the works carried out impair the structural soundness of the building, as the decisive factor in abusive works is that they are inconsistent with the terms of the contract without the express and written consent of the lessor.

د. If he assigns the leased premises or sublets them in whole or in part without the express and written consent of the lessor, in which case the subtenant or assignee must be joined in the proceedings. The lessor may prove the fact of assignment or subletting by all means of proof, including the testimony of witnesses.

هـ. If he abandons the leased premises for an uninterrupted period of one year, even if he continues to pay the rent. Intermittent and circumstantial occupancy shall not be deemed to interrupt the one-year period. Non-serious occupancy shall fall within the concept of abandonment.

و. If he abandons the leased premises for an uninterrupted period of six months while owing any part of the rent, and has no residence known to the owner at which to be served with the formal notice to pay, or has not elected a domicile in Lebanon at which to be served with such formal notice and designated it to the lessor by means of a letter or an unsealed registered postcard with acknowledgment of receipt in accordance with the service procedures provided for in Paragraph «أ» of this Article.

ز. If a non-Lebanese tenant does not actually occupy the leased premises for an uninterrupted period of six months despite his payment of the rent.

ح. If his occupancy is simulated and lacks seriousness in accordance with what is stated in Paragraph «هـ» above, provided that the Civil Single Judge hearing rent actions shall have the discretion to assess this independently of verifying the fact of abandonment, and the dispute shall be subject to proof by all means, including the testimony of witnesses.

ط. If the tenant effects a change in the intended use of the leased premises as exclusively specified in the lease contract.

Upon the expiry of the period of statutory extension referred to in Article Three, in both of its paragraphs, of this Law, the tenant shall become an occupant of the leased premises without lawful justification and may be evicted from the leased premises by a decision of the Judge of Urgent Matters issued pursuant to an order on a petition submitted by the lessor, to which the necessary documents shall be attached.

(Cases of Recovery of Possession and Amount of Compensation)

(a) - The owner who is the proprietor of a hospital, an educational, instructional, or charitable institution, or an orphanage, who has leased a part of his property or his contiguous properties for residential use, may recover possession of this part, provided that it is added to the principal property and used for the purposes of the institution.

(b) - The owner may request the recovery of possession of the leased premises in order to demolish the building in which the leased premises are located and erect a new building in its place. In order to erect one or more storeys, he may request the recovery of possession of the structure standing on the roof if this structure occupies less than half of the area permitted by the Building Law.

In such a case, the owner shall bring a single action for recovery of possession against all the tenants, and he shall prove that the property on which a new building is intended to be constructed is buildable in accordance with the Building Law and the requirements of urban planning.

(c) - In the two cases mentioned above, the compensation shall be equivalent to 15% of the sale value of the leased premises.

(d) - The compensation due to the tenant shall decrease proportionally with the remaining duration of the extension period, that is, at the rate of one quarter (1/4) for each year that has elapsed of the extension period.

(e) - The owner shall pay the compensation to the tenant either directly from himself or by borrowing from any source he chooses, and the loan granted to the owner shall be deemed equivalent to a housing loan, in which case the owner shall benefit from the exemptions provided for in Law No. /543/ dated 24/07/1996.

(f) - In addition to the compensation specified in this Article, the owner shall be liable for further compensation for the loss incurred by the tenant as a result of the eviction (such as key money, loss of location and clientele, interruption of business, and others), provided that such compensation is determined either by agreement between the owner and the tenant or through the courts, in which case the tenant must prove such loss by means of official documents.

(g) - An owner who has recovered possession of his leased premises pursuant to the provisions of this Article shall be liable to pay to the tenant additional compensation equivalent to half the value of the compensation that he paid to the tenant, without the tenant being obliged to prove the damage he suffered, in the two cases set forth below:

1- If the leased premises were recovered pursuant to either of the two purposes provided for in paragraphs "(a)" and "(b)" of this Article and the owner, without legitimate justification, did not use them in accordance with the required purpose within a period of one year from the date of eviction, or did not continue, without legitimate justification, to use them in that manner for at least three years.

2- If the leased premises were recovered for demolition and reconstruction pursuant to the purpose provided for in paragraph "(b)" of this Article and the owner, without legitimate justification, did not commence construction within a period of eighteen months from the date of eviction of the last tenant and did not complete it within a period not exceeding five years from the date of commencement of the work without legitimate justification, or if he used the recovered leased premises for his residence or for his personal benefit or leased them to a third party during the one-year period set forth above.

(h) - The lessor may withdraw and discontinue the proceedings in actions for recovery of possession without the consent of the other party and at any stage of the proceedings.

(i) It may be agreed between the lessor and the tenant that the recovery of possession of the leased premises be by mutual consent, subject to following the procedures below:

1- The lessor shall notify the tenant in writing of his initial desire to recover possession of the leased premises within a period not exceeding two months from the date of determining the fair rent amicably or judicially with respect to the first extended year, and within the same period at the beginning of each of the remaining extended years, by means of a registered letter with acknowledgment of receipt or by means of a letter served through the notary public.

2- Obtaining the tenant's initial consent in writing to vacate the leased premises in return for compensation the value of which is agreed upon by the two parties in accordance with the same rules provided for in the preceding paragraph.

3- In all events, neither the owner nor the tenant may invoke the initial consent issued by either of them for any reason whatsoever and before any authority.

4- The owner shall pay the compensation to the tenant directly from himself or by borrowing from any source he chooses, and the loan granted to the owner shall be deemed equivalent to a housing loan, in which case the owner shall benefit from the exemptions provided for in Law No. /543/ dated 24/7/1996.

5- The owner shall tender and deposit with the notary public in the district in which the leased premises are located the value of the compensation agreed upon with the tenant.

6- In the event that the tenant agrees to the tender and deposit, he shall execute a declaration of consent and an undertaking to vacate the leased premises and hand them over vacant with the keys to the owner within the period agreed upon with the latter, during which the tenant shall continue to pay the rent due; the notary public shall then deliver to the tenant a proportion of 90% of the value of the tender and deposit in accordance with the rules, provided that he pays the remaining value upon completion of the actual vacation of the leased premises and the handing over of the keys by a written acknowledgment by both parties or by the tenant alone signed before the notary public.

7- If the tenant fails to vacate within the period referred to above for vacating the leased premises and handing them over vacant to the owner, the tenant shall thereafter become an occupant of the leased premises without legitimate justification and shall be subject, for each day of delay, to a non-reducible coercive fine payable to the lessor, equivalent to the rent of five days calculated on the basis of the fair rent, in which case the lessor shall be entitled to request directly from the Head of the Execution Department having jurisdiction over the leased premises to order the eviction by means of an application to which shall be attached: a copy of each of the agreement executed between him and the tenant on the eviction, the formal tender and deposit with the notary public referred to above, and the receipt for the collection of 90% of the value of the compensation, and this application shall be subject to the fixed fee.

8- The decisions of the Head of the Execution Department taken within the framework of the provisions of this paragraph shall not be subject to any avenue of appeal except opposition.

(j) - The provisions of this Law shall apply to pending actions for recovery of possession in which no final and binding decision has been issued prior to the date of its entry into force.

(Subjection of judicial proceedings to the fixed fee and exemptions from certain fees on transactions)

Judicial proceedings for the enforcement of eviction and all matters branching therefrom shall be subject to the fixed fee.

Transactions shall be exempted from any proportional fee and from stamp duty on all notary public procedures relating to valuations and the service thereof, or formal notices, or tender and deposit.

(Cases of doubling of rents)

Rents shall be doubled once in the following cases:

A - For premises leased to a natural or legal person who owns or comes to own buildings or undivided shares in premises where his share of the total actual rents thereof exceeds ten times the rent of the leased premises that he occupies.

For the purpose of calculating these rents, the husband, the wife, and the children residing with the tenant shall be deemed as a single person, and the landlord shall not be entitled to request this doubling from a single tenant or whoever replaces him by virtue of this Law more than once.

B - For leases deemed an element of a commercial establishment and which are the subject of an assignment contract or a free management contract in accordance with the provisions of Legislative Decree No. 11/1967, throughout the period of free management.

The rent shall be multiplied in accordance with the provisions of Paragraph "B" according to the following mechanism:

1- Where the annual rent is less than two hundred thousand Lebanese pounds, it shall be multiplied twentyfold.

2- Where the annual rent is between two hundred thousand Lebanese pounds and five hundred thousand Lebanese pounds, it shall be multiplied tenfold.

3- Where the annual rent is between five hundred thousand Lebanese pounds and one million Lebanese pounds, it shall be multiplied sevenfold.

4- Where the annual rent is between one million Lebanese pounds and five million Lebanese pounds, it shall be multiplied fivefold.

5- Where the annual rent is between five million Lebanese pounds and ten million Lebanese pounds, it shall be doubled once.

(Application of certain provisions of the New Rent Law of the year 2014 and its amendments to non-residential leases)

The common provisions for all lease contracts provided for in Title Four of the New Rent Law dated 9/5/2014 and its amendments, Articles /43/ to /55/, shall apply to non-residential premises.

(Certain Tax Exemptions)

Notwithstanding any other statutory or regulatory text, owners of leased buildings subject to the provisions of the Rent Law dated 9/5/2014 and its amendments and subject to this Law (for residential and non-residential purposes) shall be exempted from inheritance duty and estate settlement fees and from collection and delay fines thereon, and from built property taxes and the fines thereon for the period of ten years preceding the entry into force of this Law and until the year 2026. Transfer of ownership fees in the event of sale or gift between ascendants and descendants for the persons mentioned in Article One shall be reduced by 90% with effect from the date of entry into force of this Law.

(Repeal of Contrary Provisions)

All provisions contrary to this Law or inconsistent with the content thereof are hereby repealed.

(Publication and Entry into Force)

This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.
