(Benefit from the Right of Extension and Subrogation in Place of the Original Tenant)

The following shall benefit from the extension and be subrogated in place of the tenant in the event of his death:

First: With respect to premises leased for commercial or industrial purposes:

1- The tenant's spouse and his children, or one of them in the event of agreement among themselves, provided that the lessor is notified in all cases of the fate of the lease and the agreement on its continuation within a period of six months from the date of death by means of an unsealed postcard with acknowledgment of receipt or by means of a letter through a notary public, under pain of forfeiture of the right to the lease. All of this is subject to the condition of practising the same trade or industry.

2- The tenant's partners whose partnership is established at the date of the lease contract or at a date prior thereto.

3- The beneficiaries of the provisions of Article /5/ et seq. of Legislative Decree No. 11/1967 (relating to the business concern), provided that the concern was established at a date prior to the lease. In this case, the lease of the premises allocated for the operation of the business concern shall be extended and transferred to the person to whom that concern is transferred.

Premises leased for the purposes enumerated in Articles /6/, /7/ and /8/ of the Code of Land Commerce shall be deemed commercial or industrial.

4- It shall not be permissible for the tenant's spouse and his children to assign the leased premises to third parties, and any agreement to the contrary shall be deemed a ground for forfeiture of the right to the lease by both the assignor and the assignee.

Second: With respect to premises leased for the practice of a liberal profession regulated by law:

1- The tenant's spouse and his children, or one of them in the event of agreement among themselves, provided that the lessor is notified in all cases of the fate of the lease and the agreement on its continuation within a period of six months from the date of death by means of an unsealed postcard with acknowledgment of receipt or by means of a letter through a notary public, under pain of forfeiture of the right to the lease. All of this is subject to the condition of practising the same liberal profession.

2- If the leased premises are occupied by more than one person practising a liberal profession and one of them dies and there is no one among his wife or his children who practises his same profession, his partners shall be subrogated in his place in the lease under the same terms of the contract, in return for compensation to the heirs equivalent to ten times the deceased's share in the annual rent in force at the date of death.

3- However, in the event that the partner tenant vacates the leased premises for any reason whatsoever, his partners shall be subrogated in his place under the same terms of the contract.

4- It shall not be permissible for the tenant's spouse and his children to assign the leased premises to third parties, and any agreement to the contrary shall be deemed a ground for forfeiture of the right to the lease by both the assignor and the assignee.

Third: With respect to other premises:

1- The tenant's spouse and his children, or one of them in the event of agreement among themselves, provided that the lessor is notified in all cases of the fate of the lease and the agreement on its continuation within a period of six months from the date of death by means of an unsealed postcard with acknowledgment of receipt or by means of a letter through a notary public, under pain of forfeiture of the right to the lease. All of this is subject to the condition of practising the same profession or craft.

2- The tenant's partners whose partnership is established at the date of the lease contract or at a date prior thereto.

3- It shall not be permissible for the tenant's spouse and his children to assign the leased premises to third parties, and any agreement to the contrary shall be deemed a ground for forfeiture of the right to the lease by both the assignor and the assignee.

Fourth: On solidarity among the beneficiaries of the extension:

All persons benefiting from the extension pursuant to the provisions of this Article shall be deemed jointly and severally liable towards the lessor in the performance of their obligations.

In all the cases mentioned above, in the event that there is no person among the tenant's wife or his children who practises the same trade, industry, liberal profession, craft or vocation, the lease shall terminate.

Preliminary Provisions

Articles (1) to (36) determine the provisions upon which the process of reforming the situation of a bank and the liquidation process are based, and they shall be deemed in force upon the enactment of the Law on Financial Regularity and Recovery of Deposits.

Objectives of this Law

In compliance with the Code of Money and Credit, this Law aims to enhance the stability of the financial system, address cases of default, protect deposits in the liquidation and reform process, and limit the use of public funds in the process of reforming any defaulting bank.

Scope of Application of this Law

Foreign banks or branches of foreign banks operating in Lebanon, as well as Lebanese banks including their branches abroad, and financial institutions subject to the Code of Money and Credit, shall be subject to the provisions of this Law, unless the laws and regulations of the host countries provide otherwise.

For the purposes of applying the provisions of this Law, Article 10 of Law No. 28/1967 dated 9/5/1967 is amended to read as follows:

A body called the Higher Banking Authority shall be established at the Banque du Liban, composed of two Chambers as follows:

1- The First Chamber shall exercise the powers of the Higher Banking Authority provided for in Law No. 28/1967 dated 9/5/1967 and the laws in force, and shall be composed of:

- The Governor of the Banque du Liban - Chairman.

- The First Vice-Governor of the Banque du Liban.

- The Director General of Finance.

- A judge with no less than ten years of experience in financial and commercial affairs, appointed by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice, selected from a list of candidates prepared by the Supreme Judicial Council.

- The Chairman of the Banking Control Commission.

- The Chairman of the National Institute for the Guarantee of Deposits established pursuant to Law No. 28/1967.

The First Chamber of the Authority shall replace the Sanctions Committee provided for in Article 209 of the Code of Money and Credit, and shall apply, where necessary, the sanctions set forth in Article 208 of the same Law, and shall exercise the powers granted to it pursuant to Law No. 28/1967.

The Banking Control Commission must successively inform the Governor of the Banque du Liban of the conditions of the banks collectively and individually, and the First Chamber of the Authority has the right to request from the Commission any additional information regarding the cases brought before it.

The First Chamber of the Authority shall meet upon the convocation of its Chairman or at the request of two of its members, and its meetings shall not be legal unless attended by at least four members. It shall take its decisions by a majority of at least three votes, and in the event of a tie, the Chairman shall have a casting vote.

2- The Second Chamber shall be the competent authority for taking decisions regarding banks that must be subjected to resolution operations or liquidation operations in accordance with the laws in force, and shall be vested with the restructuring powers and tasks specified in the body of this Law, and shall be composed of:

- The Governor of the Banque du Liban - Chairman.

- Two Vice-Governors, provided that one of them is the First Vice-Governor of the Banque du Liban, and the second is chosen by the Central Council of the Banque du Liban.

- A financial expert with no less than ten years of experience in the fields of mergers and bank restructuring, appointed by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance, provided that he is independent of any governmental or banking entity.

- An economic expert with no less than ten years of experience in the fields of mergers and bank restructuring, appointed by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Economy and Trade, selected from a list of candidates prepared by the Federation of Economic Bodies.

- A judge with no less than ten years of experience in financial and commercial affairs, appointed by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice, selected from a list of candidates prepared by the Supreme Judicial Council.

- A representative of the National Institute for the Guarantee of Deposits, provided that he is from among the members of the Board of Directors of the Institute who do not represent commercial banks, and he shall exercise his duties in his personal capacity until an amendment is made to the bylaws whereby the Chairman of the Body ceases to be a representative of the banks.

- The Director General of Finance as a member of the Central Council of the Banque du Liban, provided that he exercises his duties in accordance with Article 28 of the Code of Money and Credit.

The Chairman of the Banking Control Commission shall attend the meetings of the Second Chamber of the Authority without the right to vote or be counted towards the quorum, and shall present an overview of the status of the bank under consideration and present the recommendations of the Control Commission, supported by a financial valuation report and an independent analysis prepared by an independent party appointed by the Banking Control Commission.

Each member of the Second Chamber of the Authority must submit to the General Secretariat of the Authority, two working days prior to the date of the meeting scheduled to discuss the conditions of a bank subject to the scope of the Law on Reforming the Status of Banks in Lebanon and their Reorganization, a declaration of any existing or previous relationship with the concerned bank during the two years preceding the date of the meeting.

In the event that any of the members of the Second Chamber of the Authority has any type of relationship that may expose him to a conflict of interest or affect in any way whatsoever his independence and decision during the performance of his work with respect to the bank subject to this Law, this member shall abstain from participating in any discussion or decision regarding the concerned bank and from exercising his voting rights in this regard. In this case, the decisions of the Second Chamber of the Authority shall be taken by a majority of the remaining members.

The Second Chamber of the Authority shall meet upon the convocation of its Chairman or at the request of three of its members, and its meetings shall not be legal unless attended by at least four members. It shall take its decisions by a majority of the votes of those present, and in the event of a tie, the Chairman shall have a casting vote. It shall be for its Chairman to set the agenda of its meetings. The deliberations of the Second Chamber of the Authority shall be confidential, and its decisions shall only be disclosed pursuant to reports or decisions signed by its Chairman.

The Banking Control Commission must successively inform the Governor of the Banque du Liban of the conditions of the banks and submit its report to the General Secretariat of the Higher Banking Authority, which shall refer each report to one of the two Chambers in accordance with the recommendation of the Banking Control

Commission based on the nature of the measures intended to be taken, whether with respect to imposing sanctions or with respect to addressing the status of the concerned bank.

Obligations of the members of the Higher Banking Commission for Reforming the Status of the Bankthe Banks to avoid conflict of interests

- Each of the members of the Higher Banking Commission shall submit the declaration provided for in Law No. 189 dated 16/10/2020 (Law on the Declaration of Assets and Interests and the Punishment of Illicit Enrichment). The time limit for submitting this declaration shall be one month from the date of publication of this Law in the Official Gazette with respect to current members, and two months from the date of appointment with respect to new members. Each member shall also be required, immediately, to submit an updated declaration in the event that any change occurs in his relationship with any bank. The General Secretariat of the Commission shall be entrusted with ensuring the proper implementation of this process.

- In the event that any of the members of the Higher Banking Commission has any kind of direct or indirect relationship that exposes him to a conflict of interests or affects in any manner whatsoever his independence when performing his work with respect to a bank subject to this Law, such member shall abstain from participating in any discussion or decision concerning the bank in question and from exercising his voting rights in this regard. In this case, the decisions of the Commission shall be taken by a majority of the remaining members.

- The following criteria shall be adopted in determining the independence of the member and the absence of a conflict of interests:

* That he has not been among the shareholders in the bank or the institutions affiliated therewith in the two years preceding his appointment.

* That he has not held in the five years preceding his appointment the position of member of the board of directors or senior management or adviser in the bank or the institutions affiliated therewith.

* That he is not a borrower from the bank or from the institutions affiliated therewith.

* That he is not a depositor of more than 100 thousand US dollars with the bank or the institutions affiliated therewith.

* That he does not have a relationship of kinship up to the fourth degree with a shareholder or a member of the board of directors or senior management at the bank or the institutions affiliated therewith.

* Any other criteria that may negatively affect his independence directly or indirectly.

Commencement of the Bank Resolution or Liquidation Process

- It shall rest with the Second Chamber of the Higher Banking Commission to take the decision regarding subjecting the bankbanks to one of the following two processes in accordance with the provisions of this Law:

a- The Resolution Process:

The Commission shall issue a decision to resolve the bank (the Resolution Decision) which includes, for each bank, the bank resolution tools to be applied, the measures to be complied with by the bank throughout its resolution process, and the time required to complete these measures.

b- The Liquidation Process:

The Commission shall issue a decision to strike the bank off the List of Banks of the Banque du Liban and a decision to liquidate the concerned bank.

The striking-off of the bank shall be followed by a decision appointing a Liquidation Committee.

- The Resolution Decision or the Striking-Off Decision shall be taken on the basis of a final valuation report sent by the Banking Control Commission, based on the report of an independent valuer, to the Higher Banking Commission regarding the necessity of liquidating the bank or rehabilitating it through resolution procedures, after stating the reasons that led to the taking of its decision.

- The bank resolution or liquidation process shall be based on a valuation the purpose of which is to determine the net value of the bank's assets and the size of the losses. The resolution process shall be based on a valuation prepared by the Banking Control Commission, which shall submit a recommendation to the Higher Banking Commission on the possibility of the bank's default and the necessity of taking corrective measures, provided that the valuation is duly completed at the request of the Higher Banking Commission by independent valuers as specified in Article 10 of this Law in order for the final decision to be taken by the Higher Banking Commission with respect to resolution or liquidation.

- The Higher Banking Commission shall state, in the minutes of its meetings, the justifying reasons for its decisions, including the justifying reasons for not adopting the recommendations of the Banking Control Commission, should that occur.

Financing of the Higher Banking Authority

The Banque du Liban shall bear the expenses of the Higher Banking Authority.

Title Three: The Independent Valuation Process

Article 10 Valuation Principles and Appointment of Independent Valuers

- The Banking Control Commission shall appoint independent valuers to conduct the valuation.

- The valuation shall be based on the International Valuation Standards and the International Financial Reporting Standards, taking into consideration the prudential requirements

and instructions issued by the Banque du Liban.

- The valuation shall be completed within the time limit specified by the Banking Control Commission.

- The following eligibility criteria shall be observed in the appointment of independent valuers:

▪ That they possess the required qualifications, specifically with respect to criteria of integrity, competence, and professional experience.

▪ That they enjoy independence and have no professional or personal relationship with the bank and its related institutions that may expose them to a conflict of interest.

- The independent valuers, their partners in the partnership agreement, and the external parties with whom they contract shall abide, throughout the duration of their mission and even after its termination, by the banking and professional secrecy regulations, in favour of the concerned bank and its clients, with respect to the information to which they gain access during the performance of their duties, under penalty of the laws in force.

- The Central Bank shall bear the cost of appointing the independent valuer / independent valuers.

- The independent valuers shall submit their reports to the Banking Control Commission with a copy thereof to the concerned bank, within the time limit specified by the Banking Control Commission.

- The Banque du Liban shall issue, upon the proposal of the Banking Control Commission, instructions and details of the characteristics, selection, and qualification of the valuer/ valuers together with the required valuation means, tools, and details.

Notification and Publication of the Decisions of the Higher Banking Commission

- With respect to the bank resolution process:

The Higher Banking Commission shall immediately notify the bank concerned of the resolution decision (including the bank resolution tools to be applied) and the decision shall be registered in the Commercial Register. The Higher Banking Commission shall publish a summary, and it shall be for the Commission to decide whether or not it includes any detail on the resolution tools of the bank concerned, together with a summary of the valuation results, in the Official Gazette, in a newspaper of wide circulation in Lebanon, and on the website of the Bank of Lebanon.

- With respect to the liquidation process:

The Higher Banking Commission shall immediately notify the bank concerned of the striking-off decision and the decision appointing a liquidator or a liquidation committee, and both decisions shall be registered in the Commercial Register. Both decisions, together with a summary of the valuation results, shall be published in the Official Gazette, in a newspaper of wide circulation in Lebanon, and on the website of the Bank of Lebanon.

- The Higher Banking Commission shall publish an annual report summarising the progress achieved towards fulfilling its objectives within the scope of this Law, and shall send a copy of this report to the Lebanese Parliament.

Acknowledgment of the Valuation Results

Failure by the bank to notify the Higher Banking Commission of any objection to the results of the valuation conducted by the independent valuers shall be deemed an acknowledgment of the valuation results. Where the bank objects to the valuation results on material grounds, it may notify the Higher Banking Commission, in writing with a copy to the Banking Control Commission, of the detailed grounds for its objection within a period not exceeding 30 working days from the date of issuance of the valuation report.

The Higher Banking Commission may, for legitimate reasons connected with the discovery of documentary errors as at the date of the valuation, after obtaining a report from the Banking Control Commission, decide to have the valuation conducted anew, in part or in whole, within a period not exceeding one month. In such case, the Higher Banking Commission shall decide whether new independent valuers shall be commissioned by the Control Commission, and the valuation results shall be final.

The Higher Banking Commission shall take its decision to reform the bank on the basis of the valuation report, and shall introduce any amendments it deems appropriate after reviewing the bank's letter, and in the case of liquidation, it shall take its decision in accordance with what is set forth in Article 23.

Criteria for Failure or Likelihood of Failure

- The Banking Control Commission shall assess whether the bank is in a state of failure or is likely to fail and whether any alternative measures such as a recovery plan or any other supervisory intervention could prevent the failure of the bank, on

the basis of one of the following criteria:

* Failure or likelihood of failure of the bank to comply with minimum own funds requirements in a timely manner.

* Failure or likelihood of failure of the bank to comply with minimum liquidity requirements in a timely manner.

* Failure or likelihood of failure of the bank to pay liabilities as they fall due.

* Failure or likelihood of failure of the bank to achieve and maintain profitability.

* Failure or likelihood of failure of the bank to comply with the conditions on the basis of which the licence was granted, including a material breach of applicable laws or regulations.

- Where the Banking Control Commission considers that the bank is failing or is likely to fail, it shall submit a recommendation to the Higher Banking Commission within a period not exceeding one week from the date of its assessment.

Tools for Addressing the Situation of the Bank

- The Higher Banking Commission may decide to apply any of the following tools for reforming the situation of the bank, individually or together with other tools, by way of example and not limitation:

* Internal rescue Bail-in

* Recapitalisation of the bank by the shareholders, by the parent bank, or through new investors.

* Transfer of some or all of the bank's assets, rights, and liabilities to another institution.

* Effecting a merger with another bank.

- The tools for reforming the situation of the bank shall be applied as specified in the decision on reforming the situation issued by the Higher Banking Commission regarding each bank in accordance with the provisions of Article 7 of this Law.

- The provisions of this Article shall apply after the enactment of the Law on Financial Regularisation and Deposit Recovery.

Exiting the "Under Resolution" Status

- The bank shall send an application to the Higher Banking Authority, with a copy thereof to the Banking Control Commission, requesting therein to exit the "Under Resolution" status and justifying therein its eligibility to exit therefrom.

- The Banking Control Commission shall assess the bank's eligibility to exit the "Under Resolution" status, including the status of

the bank, its viability, and its compliance with the laws, regulations, and the provisions mentioned in the decision for the resolution of its status within the specified time limits. The Banking Control Commission shall send its recommendation in this regard to the Higher Banking Authority within a reasonable period of time, provided that it does not exceed one month from the date of completion of the application.

- The Higher Banking Authority shall decide, on the basis of the recommendation of the Control Commission, whether the bank concerned may exit the "Under Resolution" status and shall notify this bank of its exit therefrom. This decision shall be registered in the Commercial Register, and published in the Official Gazette, in a newspaper of wide circulation in Lebanon, and on the website of the Banque du Liban.

General principles governing the bank resolution process

The following principles principles shall apply in the context of implementing the bank resolution process:

- The hierarchy of own funds and creditors set out in Annex No. 1 shall be observed.

- Own funds shall absorb all losses first, on a pro rata basis within the same rank of liabilities in accordance with the order set out in Annex No. 1.

- The creditors of the bank shall absorb losses on a pro rata basis within the same rank of liabilities in accordance with the order set out in Annex No. 1.

- Creditors within the same rank in accordance with Annex No. 1 shall be treated equally (the principle of equality).

- Shareholders within the same rank in accordance with Annex No. 1 shall be treated equally (the principle of equality).

- Depositors shall be protected in accordance with what shall be determined in the Law on Financial Regularity and Deposit Recovery, which allows for restoring balance to financial regularity in line with the objectives mentioned in Article 3 of this Law. Creditors within the same rank in accordance with Annex No. 1 shall not, as a result of applying the bank resolution tools, be in a financial position below their presumed position in the event of the liquidation of the bank. In circumstances where it becomes apparent to a creditor and/or shareholder that their financial position upon the resolution of the bank is below their presumed financial position had a liquidation decision been taken instead of a resolution decision in the context of this Law, creditors and/or shareholders may submit challenges to the Special Court mentioned in Article 29 of this Law within a maximum period of three months from the date of publication of the resolution decision. In cases where the entitlement of the creditor and/or shareholder is proven, the Special Court shall decide the amount of compensation and require the bank to pay it.

(Write-down and/or conversion of liabilities into capital instruments) Where Bail-in is used as one of the bank resolution tools, this tool shall apply to customer deposits.

- Bank resolution tools shall be used until the bank becomes compliant with the minimum own funds adequacy requirements.

- Certain liabilities shall be excluded from the mechanism of write-down or conversion into capital instruments as indicated in Annex No. 1 (Excluded Liabilities).

- The obligations of the bank linked to contingent liabilities, including those related to off-balance-sheet guarantees and credits, shall be cancelled where possible without additional risks and costs, and the cash collateral provided against them shall be released.

- Financial derivatives contracts shall be terminated and the remaining related liabilities, if any, shall be considered as unsecured liabilities, where possible without additional risks and costs.

- All suspense accounts shall be settled or cleared.

- Set-off shall take place between funded facilities (i.e. on-balance-sheet facilities) and cash collateral and/or cash margins and/or the fair value of financial instruments (bonds, shares, etc., if any) given as collateral against such facilities, within the limits of the utilised amount of such facilities and subject to the existence of a legally enforceable netting agreement and subject to the fulfilment of the offsetting criteria in accordance with International Accounting Standard No. 32. As for amounts exceeding the utilised amount of the facilities, they shall be subject to the bank resolution process.

The provisions of this Article shall apply after the issuance of the Law on Financial Regularity and Deposit Recovery.

Powers of the Banking Control Commission in the context of the bank resolution process

- A bank undergoing resolution shall remain under the supervision of the Banking Control Commission.

- In addition to the powers and responsibilities granted to the Banking Control Commission pursuant to other provisions of this Law and pursuant to other laws, the Banking Control Commission shall undertake the following:

* Preparing a provisional valuation of the bank and/or appointing an independent valuer to value the bank.

* Submitting a report to the Higher Banking Council on the results of the valuation.

* Submitting a recommendation to the Higher Banking Council on whether the bank should be liquidated or resolved and proposing the necessary measures, including the bank resolution tools to be adopted.

* Following up on the implementation of the bank resolution process and submitting periodic reports to the Higher Banking Council on compliance and non-compliance with the resolution decision.

* Conducting an assessment of the fitness and propriety of the new shareholders and the members appointed to the board of directors and/or the senior management of the bank undergoing resolution.

* Reviewing the reports of the provisional administrator and submitting any observations to the Higher Banking Council as needed.

* Preparing the resolution plan for each bank and submitting it to the Higher Banking Council.

- The Banking Control Commission shall issue, as needed, instructions and technical requirements for the purpose of ensuring the proper implementation of its powers and responsibilities in accordance with this Law.

- The Banking Control Commission shall be entitled to access all information necessary to implement the bank resolution process and exercise its powers and responsibilities in accordance with this Law.

- The Banking Control Commission shall submit a report on the foregoing to the Higher Banking Council.

Powers of the Higher Banking Commission

- The Higher Banking Commission shall have authority over the bank and shall exercise its powers in part or in whole, without need for the approval of the shareholders, creditors, Board of Directors, Senior Management, or any other counterparty of the bank under resolution, and in particular the decision of the Commission shall not be subject to the approval of any other authority.

- The powers of the Higher Banking Commission shall include the following:

* Appointing a temporary administrator, in cases where this is appropriate in accordance with the provisions of Title 8 of this Law.

* Dismissing or replacing members of the Board of Directors and/or Senior Management, or requesting the bank to do so.

* Appointing one or more independent non-executive members of the Board of Directors, or requesting the bank to do so.

* Objecting to the appointment of new members of the Board of Directors and/or Senior Management.

* Approving the periodically prepared/updated resolution plan of the bank for each bank.

* Imposing the measures necessary to remove impediments to the resolvability of the bank, including, without limitation:

- Requesting the bank to sell assets, including its assets abroad.

- Requesting the bank to limit or cease certain existing operations and business activities.

- Requesting the bank to change its legal or operational structure, including reorganising the ownership structure.

* Initiating the resolution process of the bank, and taking a decision regarding its duration where necessary.

* Imposing the application of resolution measures and tools on the bank.

* Amending the maturity of debt instruments and other liabilities of the bank (including deposits), or amending the amount of interest and/or principal payable under such instruments and other liabilities, or the due date of the interest and/or principal, where necessary.

* Suspending trading in listed capital instruments issued by the bank, where applicable, and/or postponing

market disclosure requirements after coordination with the competent authority.

* Imposing the principle of a temporary suspension (Moratorium) for a period of two months and staying the effects of existing and future legal proceedings for a maximum period of 8 months where necessary.

* Requiring third parties to continue providing essential services to the bank under resolution in accordance with the terms and conditions existing prior to the resolution of the bank.

* Imposing a suspension of early termination rights by prohibiting the enforcement of contractual clauses relating to financial lease, service, or licensing agreements, which allow the counterparty of the bank under resolution to exercise set-off, accelerate the payment of obligations, or terminate such contracts upon the initiation of the resolution process of the bank.

The suspension of early termination rights relating to financial contracts must not exceed a period of 3 days.

The early termination rights enjoyed by the counterparty against the bank under resolution shall be preserved in the event of any default unrelated to the initiation of the resolution process of the bank before or after the suspension period.

* Prohibiting the payment of any dividends to holders of capital instruments or the distribution of other capital profits to them, and any type of payments to members of the Board of Directors and senior managers, other than the basic remuneration paid to Senior Management.

* Imposing the clawback of funds paid to members of the Board of Directors or Senior Management in violation of the law, the circulars of the Banque du Liban, or the rules of sound governance, in respect of a preceding period of 10 years.

* Imposing the clawback of any funds transferred to other parties in a discriminatory or unfair manner, which prejudiced the rights of other depositors or creditors who were unable to make similar transfers after 17 October 2019.

*Striking off the concerned bank from the List of Banks of the Banque du Liban in accordance with the cases specified in this Law, and subsequently appointing a liquidator or a liquidation committee in accordance with Article 24 of this Law.

* Bringing an action in the name and on behalf of the bank, or requesting the bank or the temporary administrator to bring an action before the competent Lebanese courts and/or any competent foreign court in other countries, against major shareholders, members of the Board of Directors and Senior Management, authorised signatories, and auditors who held their positions at the concerned bank during the ten years preceding the date of issuance of the resolution decision, where there are reasonable grounds to suspect the involvement of any of those persons in a civil or criminal offence.

* Giving instructions to the liquidator / liquidation committee in the event of liquidation (as specified by Article 25 of this Law).

- The Higher Banking Commission may decide, after obtaining a report from the Banking Control Commission, for legitimate reasons linked to the discovery of factual errors as at the date of the valuation conducted by the independent valuer, to repeat the valuation process of the bank in part or in whole, through the same independent valuer or another independent valuer, within an expedited and reasonable time limit. The results of the second valuation shall be final and binding.

- The Higher Banking Commission may depart from the general principle requiring the equal treatment of creditors within the same rank, while specifying the cases in which this principle was not applied and providing a transparent explanation of the justifying reasons, only if it deems this necessary to contain the potential impact of the failure of a bank on the banking sector as a whole or to secure the maximum benefit for the creditors as a whole.

- The Higher Banking Commission may carry out a reversal process, in part or in whole, of any write-down in value and/or of other resolution tools, where necessary. In such case, the Higher Banking Commission may decide to write up the value of the claims of creditors and/or shareholders that ought not to have been subject to the write-down and/or to other resolution tools of the bank. The reversal process shall be carried out in accordance with Annex No. 1 (Hierarchy of Own Funds and Creditors).

Cooperation of Various Parties with the Higher Banking Commission

- Each of the Capital Markets Authority, the Insurance Control Commission, the Banque du Liban, the Banking Control Commission, the Commercial Register, the Real Estate Register, Midclear S.A.L., the National Deposit Guarantee Institution, and any other parties concerned with the application of the provisions of this Law must cooperate with the Higher Banking Commission, and coordination with the Ministry of Finance shall take place in all matters that the Commission deems necessary.

- Each of the above parties shall provide the Higher Banking Commission, within the time limit determined by the latter, with the necessary data, recommendations, and approvals.

- The Higher Banking Commission shall consult the Central Council of the Banque du Liban, in line with its tasks, regarding financial stability issues that may arise.

- The Central Council of the Banque du Liban shall send a recommendation to the Higher Banking Commission within a time limit determined by this Commission.

Appointment of the Provisional Administrator

- The Higher Banking Commission shall appoint, if it deems it appropriate, a provisional administrator for a pre-determined period of time renewable by this Commission, and it may delegate to him specific or broad powers, including the powers to manage the affairs of the bank whose situation is being resolved and the powers of the board of directors. The provisional administrator shall exercise any power related to resolving the bank's situation on the basis of a written decision from the Higher Banking Commission which determines, with respect to each bank, the powers of the provisional administrator, the scope of his work, his tasks, the duration of his appointment, and his duties towards the Higher Banking Commission.

- The decision appointing the provisional administrator issued by the Higher Banking Commission shall be registered in the Commercial Register, and published in the Official Gazette, in a widely circulated newspaper in Lebanon, and on the electronic website of the Banque du Liban.

- The Higher Banking Commission shall determine the remuneration of the provisional administrator, and the concerned bank shall bear the full expenses.

- The Higher Banking Commission may, if it deems it necessary, dismiss the provisional administrator at any time whatsoever, and it may appoint a replacement for him for the remaining period of his term.

- The same person may not be appointed as a provisional administrator for more than one bank.

Qualifications of the Interim Manager

The Interim Manager shall:

- Possess extensive professional experience of not less than twenty years in the banking and financial fields, along with administrative experience and in-depth knowledge of the financial and banking laws and regulations in force.

- Be independent from the bank whose situation is being reformed.

The independence criteria shall include the following:

* That he has not been, directly or indirectly, a shareholder in the bank or in its affiliated institutions during the five years preceding his appointment.

* That he has not held, directly or indirectly, during the two years preceding his appointment, the position of member of the Board of Directors or Senior Management, or advisor, in the bank or in its affiliated institutions.

* That he is not a borrower from the bank or from its affiliated institutions for more than 100 thousand US dollars.

* That he is not a depositor (for more than 100 thousand US dollars) with the bank or its affiliated institutions.

* That he has no kinship relation up to the fourth degree with a shareholder or a member of the Board of Directors or Senior Management at the bank or its affiliated institutions.

* Any other criteria that may negatively affect his independence, directly or indirectly.

- The bank may not participate in an operation if the Interim Manager has a fundamental interest in or a relation to it (directly or indirectly), and by way of exception, such operation may only be carried out after the prior written approval of the Higher Banking Commission.

- Disclose to the Higher Banking Commission the existence of an interest or relation that conflicts with the principle of independence and non-conflict of interest, and in the event that he refrains from making the disclosure as required, the Higher Banking Commission shall have the authority to dismiss him.

Delisting Decision Leading to Liquidation

The Higher Banking Commission shall have the authority to delist any bank in the following two cases:

1- Prior to the commencement of the bank resolution process: Upon receipt of an evaluation report from the Banking Control Commission recommending liquidation on the basis of the criteria of failure or likelihood of failure and the impossibility of rehabilitating the bank through bank resolution measures, provided that the bank is granted the right to submit any defences or demonstrate facts supported by evidentiary documents contradicting the submitted report, in person before the Higher Banking Commission within a period not exceeding 15 days.

2- At any time after the commencement of the bank resolution process:

a- Upon the Commission receiving an evaluation report from the Banking Control Commission concluding that the bank is failing or likely to fail despite the attempt to rehabilitate it through bank resolution measures.

b- Upon the Commission receiving an evaluation report from the Provisional Administrator highlighting the necessity of liquidating the bank concerned.

- The delisting decision shall be based on Articles 140, 208 and 209 of the Lebanese Code of Money and Credit. In such case, the provisions of Article 141 of the Code of Money and Credit shall apply, and the bank concerned shall be deemed under liquidation, provided that its liquidation is carried out in accordance with the liquidation provisions set forth in this Law.

- Following the delisting decision, the Higher Banking Commission shall appoint a liquidator or a liquidation committee, depending on the size of the bank under liquidation.

- All liquidation operations shall be referred to the Second Chamber for the application of the provisions of this Law, and the provisions of Title 9 of this Law shall apply exclusively to the liquidation process and shall supersede any other laws and regulations that conflict with their content.

- Once a bank is under liquidation, it must always use the phrase "Under Liquidation" alongside its name, particularly in its correspondence with third parties, until the conclusion of the liquidation process.

- After the date of issuance of the delisting decision and the commencement of the liquidation process, where there are serious grounds to suspect that any of the major shareholders, members of the Board of Directors, senior management, authorised signatories, and auditors who held

their positions at the bank under liquidation during the ten years preceding the date of issuance of the delisting decision has been involved in a civil or criminal offence, the liquidator / liquidation committee and/or the Higher Banking Commission shall:

* Notify the aforementioned persons of the obligation to refrain from disposing of all or part of their movable and immovable assets and their bank accounts, and place a restraint against disposal thereon, in addition to a decision prohibiting them from travelling, provided that the effects of such measures do not exceed six non-renewable months.

* Request the competent courts in Lebanon or abroad to levy a precautionary attachment on all or part of the movable and immovable assets belonging to the aforementioned persons in accordance with the applicable Lebanese and foreign laws.

* Prosecute such persons before the competent Lebanese courts and/or any competent foreign court for the civil and/or criminal liability incurred by them pursuant to the applicable laws and regulations.

Once either of the last two measures above is put into effect, the aforementioned persons shall be deemed to have waived the rights granted to them pursuant to the provisions of the Banking Secrecy Law, if any.

In the event that the provisional precautionary attachment is to be enforced, and upon the request of the liquidator / liquidation committee, the concerned major shareholders, members of the Board of Directors, senior management, authorised signatories, and auditors shall provide the liquidator / liquidation committee, within ten business days from the request of the liquidator / liquidation committee, with a complete and detailed list of all movable and immovable assets in Lebanon and abroad that they own, under pain of criminal prosecution and a penalty of imprisonment for a period of three months, together with the obligation to deliver what is required of them and holding them liable for the costs of obtaining the same through law firms appointed by the Higher Banking Commission.

Appointment of a Liquidator/ Liquidation Committee

The Higher Banking Commission shall appoint, within thirty days from the issuance of the striking-off decision, a liquidator or a liquidation committee of six members, according to the size of the concerned bank, provided that this committee includes:

* A member representing the creditors.

* A member representing the shareholders.

* A member representing the depositors.

* An expert in banking or financial affairs.

* A legal expert.

* The Chairman of the National Institute for the Guarantee of Deposits or a representative appointed by this Chairman.

The Higher Banking Commission shall appoint from among these members a Chairman for this committee and determine his powers. The Chairman shall exercise the daily business related to the liquidation process. Furthermore, the conclusion of any settlement agreement or any sale or liquidation operation of the bank's assets Regarding which a decision is taken by the liquidation committee shall not become effective except after obtaining a written approval

from the Higher Banking Commission.

The liquidation committee shall convene at the request of its Chairman or two (2) of its members. Its decisions shall be taken by a majority of its members. The Chairman shall represent the committee before third parties, when necessary.

In the event that a vacancy occurs in the composition of the committee (death, resignation, health conditions...) the Higher Banking Commission shall appoint a replacement within a reasonable period not exceeding 15 days.

- It is required of the liquidator/ any member of the liquidation committee:

* That he possesses the required qualifications in accordance with best practices, particularly with respect to the standards of integrity, competence, independence, and professional experience in his field of specialisation.

* That he has no affiliation or relationship of any kind, professional or personal, that may expose him to a conflict of interest, or affect in any way whatsoever his independence and his decision during the performance of the tasks entrusted to him.

* That he is not an assumed person or a depositor (of more than 100 thousand US dollars) with the bank or the institutions linked to it.

* That he is not a current or former member of the Board of Directors or senior management or an advisor to the concerned Board under liquidation or any of the institutions linked to it, during the five years preceding his appointment.

* That he has not conducted an audit of the accounts of the bank under liquidation, during the two years preceding the striking-off decision.

* That he does not have a relationship of kinship up to the fourth degree with any shareholder or member of the Board of Directors.

- The Higher Banking Commission shall determine the fees of the Chairman and members of the liquidation committee and the bank shall bear the costs.

- The decision appointing the liquidator/ liquidation committee shall be published in the Official Gazette and in at least one local newspaper and on the website of the Higher Banking Commission and/or the Banque du Liban and/or the Banking Control Commission.

Powers and responsibilities of the temporary administrator

- The temporary administrator exercises the powers granted to him by the Higher Banking Commission in the written decision determining the scope of his work, and his work shall be under the supervision of the Higher Banking Commission.

- The temporary administrator shall have unrestricted management over the properties, offices, assets, accounting books and other records of the bank concerned, and he shall also have the right of access to all information necessary for the exercise of his duties.

- It is within the power of the temporary administrator to dismiss any of the directors and/or responsible employees, and to appoint a replacement for them.

- The temporary administrator shall, at least quarterly and when needed, submit a report to the Higher Banking Commission, with a copy thereof to the Banking Control Commission, regarding the work accomplished, the evolution of the situation of the bank concerned and the action plan to be completed. In addition, and in the event that the bank's difficulties continue, he shall submit to the Higher Banking Commission a report determining the nature, source and significance of the obstacles, as well as the additional measures capable of improving the situation of the bank concerned.

- The temporary administrator must submit a report to the Higher Banking Commission, with a copy thereof to the Banking Control Commission, regarding any malpractice that becomes apparent to him as having occurred during the period of his appointment.

- All decisions issued by the temporary administrator are subject to appeal before the Higher Banking Commission.

Objectives of liquidation

The liquidation process shall be carried out with the objective of protecting financial stability and maximising the value of the benefit for the creditors as a whole.

The provisions of Article 17 of Law No. 110 dated 7/11/1991 and its amendments (Reform of the Banking Situation) relating to deciding the self-liquidation of any bank shall apply. In the event that the bank decides to carry out a self-liquidation, it must submit an application to the Higher Banking Commission showing therein that the assets cover all the liabilities.

Role and Powers of the Liquidator / Liquidation Committee

- The Liquidator / Liquidation Committee shall submit to the Higher Banking Commission for approval a liquidation plan comprising an organized timetable with a reasonable and specified timeframe for the steps necessary to sell the assets of the bank and distribute the proceeds thereof in accordance with the hierarchy of own funds and creditors referred to in Annex No. 1. The Higher Banking Commission shall approve this plan, monitor its implementation, and take the necessary measures in the event of any delay.

- The Liquidator / Liquidation Committee shall act in good faith and with the necessary prudence and due diligence in order to complete the liquidation process within the approved timeframe.

- It shall be required that:

* The Liquidator / Liquidation Committee exercise the powers vested in it by the Higher Banking Commission under the supervision of this Commission and refer to the Commission in advance in all matters relating to operations involving additional risks or the liquidation of assets

in large amounts or large losses.

* The Liquidator / Liquidation Committee assist the National Deposit Guarantee Institution in the payment process.

* The Liquidator / Liquidation Committee replace the Board of Directors of the concerned bank and its senior management in all decisions, following the written approval of the Higher Banking Commission.

* The Liquidator / Liquidation Committee conduct a valuation of the concerned bank or request independent valuers to conduct a valuation or update a previous valuation when needed.

* The Liquidator / Liquidation Committee submit periodic reports to the Higher Banking Commission on the progress of the liquidation process at the concerned bank and submit, within a timeframe specified by the Commission, any additional reports or information requested by this Commission.

* The Liquidator / Liquidation Committee have the right of access to all information necessary for the exercise of its duties.

Hierarchy in the Liquidation Process

- In cases of liquidation, the adopted international auditing standards shall apply while respecting the hierarchy of own funds and creditors and the protection of depositors.

This Article shall apply in accordance with the mechanisms determined by the Financial Regularity and Deposit Recovery Law.

Claims of Creditors and Depositors

- Creditors shall declare their debts and rights to the Liquidator / Liquidation Committee within three months from the publication of the decision appointing the Liquidator / Liquidation Committee in the Official Gazette, in at least one local newspaper, and on the website as stated in Article 24, under penalty of forfeiture of their right to claim them.

- The bank under liquidation shall preserve the right of depositors to access information relating to the nature and value of their deposits.

Role of the National Institute for the Guarantee of Deposits in the Liquidation Process

In the event of the liquidation of a bank in accordance with the provisions of this Law, deposits shall be covered in accordance with the criteria determined by the Law on Restoring Financial Regularity and Deposit Recovery.

The Special Court

- The provisions of Article 15 of Law No. 110 dated 7/11/1991 relating to the establishment of a Special Court in Beirut shall apply, and this Court shall have jurisdiction to adjudicate challenges submitted pursuant to the provisions of this Law and to resolve any dispute arising between a creditor or depositor, on the one hand, and the Liquidator/Liquidation Committee, on the other hand, concerning a debt or deposit held against the bank under liquidation.

- Any action pending before a Lebanese Court of First Instance relating to an existing dispute between a creditor or depositor and the bank concerned, in respect of which no final decision has been rendered, shall be referred administratively to the Special Court within one month of the appointment of the Liquidator/Liquidation Committee.

- The Special Court shall hear all cases relating to the temporary precautionary attachment referred to in this

Law.

- With the exception of an appeal before the competent Court of Appeal within a period of 60 days from the date of issuance of the final judgment, the decisions of the Special Court shall not be subject to any avenue of administrative or judicial review, whether ordinary or extraordinary.

Financing the Liquidation Process

The bank under liquidation shall bear all expenses relating to the liquidation process as determined or approved by the Higher Banking Commission.

Challenging the Decisions of the Higher Banking Commission

All decisions issued by the Higher Banking Commission shall be open to challenge before the Special Court established pursuant to Law No. 110 dated 11/7/1991, and the rules of civil procedure relating to the Court of First Instance shall be followed. A challenge before the competent court shall not stay the execution of the challenged decision and shall not annul decisions previously taken by the Higher Banking Commission - Second Chamber, and judgments issued by the Special Court in this regard shall be limited to determining financial compensation.

Non-Compliance with the Provisions of this Law or Obstruction of the Conduct of Work

Any party that fails to comply immediately with the provisions of this Law or otherwise obstructs the work of the Higher Banking Commission or the Provisional Administrator in the course of performing their duties shall be subject to a fine the amount of which shall be assessed by the Higher Banking Commission, provided that it is not less than 300 times the minimum wage in Lebanon. The Higher Banking Commission shall be the competent authority that decides whether there is a violation of its decisions or non-compliance with the provisions of this Law.

Requirements Imposed on Banks

All banks shall have fulfilled the following:

* The applicable minimum own funds requirements, provided that the banks' assets with the Banque du Liban are considered at book value prior to any provisions for potential losses on placements with the Banque du Liban, and investments in Eurobonds are considered on a net value basis after taking into account the expected loss ratio determined by the Banque du Liban.

* The minimum liquidity requirements, provided that the bank's assets with the Banque du Liban are considered within book maturities along with the rescheduling of deposit maturities by the bank.

These prudential requirements shall be amended in accordance with the Financial Regularity and Deposit Recovery Law which allows the restoration of balance to financial regularity in Lebanon provided for in Article 37 of this Law and immediately upon its promulgation.

- Banks identified by the Banking Control Commission as banks non-compliant with the requirements above shall remedy their violations through mechanisms including:

* Injecting own funds.

* Increasing their liquidity.

Entry into Force of the Law

This Law shall be published in the Official Gazette and its implementation shall be suspended until the enactment and publication of the Financial Regularity and Deposit Recovery Law.

a - Immediately upon the signing of the Partnership Contract by its parties, the Public Entity must appoint:

• Monitoring the operations carried out by the Project Company in terms of outputs and the required levels and quality of services with respect to the established standards and the allocation of risks.

Determination of the rules governing the expenditure of external grants and loans

1- With the exception of municipalities and federations of municipalities, external grants and loans offered to public administrations, public institutions and autonomous authorities of all kinds, to councils, bodies and funds regardless of their designations, and to all other institutions and bodies that manage public utilities, shall be accepted in accordance with the provisions of Article 52 of the Public Accounting Law and its amendments, and Article 88 of the Constitution, and expenditure from cash grants and from loans, whether from the local share or from the foreign share, shall be subject to the audit of the Court of Audit in due form.

2- The provisions of the second paragraph of Article 27 of the Law promulgated by Decree No. 14969 dated 30/12/1963 shall not apply to additional appropriations relating to cash grants, as such appropriations may be transferred from one item to another by a decision of the competent minister and the Minister of Finance after the endorsement of the Central Controller of Commitment of Expenditures, and after the administration concerned proves the desire of the donor entity to carry out this transfer.

3- The balances of all uncommitted appropriations financed from cash grants and loans shall be carried over to the budgets of subsequent years.

Opening of extraordinary appropriations

Pursuant to the provisions of Article 85 of the Constitution, the President of the Republic may, if emergency circumstances call for urgent expenditures, issue a decree based on a decision issued by the Council of Ministers, opening extraordinary or additional appropriations or transferring appropriations in the 2026 budget, provided that these appropriations do not exceed 1000 billion Lebanese pounds, and these measures must be submitted for the approval of the Chamber of Deputies at the first session in which it convenes thereafter.

Authorisation to transfer appropriations

1- Transfer within the general budget reserve from one chapter to another and from one item to another within this reserve is authorised by a decision of the Minister of Finance after the endorsement of the Central Controller of Expenditure Commitment.

2- The transfer of appropriations allocated for the salaries of surplus employees, contractors, wage earners and associates in public administrations and public institutions, accompanied by the approval of the Civil Service Board, from the administration from which the transfer is made to the administration to which the transfer is made, is authorised. The transfer shall be effected by a decision of the Minister of Finance after the endorsement of the Central Controller of Expenditure Commitment.

3- The transfer of appropriations provided for in the budget of the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities - Administrative Departments - allocated to the Traffic, Trucks and Vehicles Management Authority to the budget of the said Authority after the issuance of its own regulations, is authorised by a decision of the Minister of Finance, after the endorsement of the Central Controller of Expenditure Commitment. The transfer of appropriations provided for in the budget of the Central Inspection Administration allocated to the Public Procurement Authority to the budget of the Authority after the appointment of the members of the Public Procurement Authority and/or the implementation of the decision of the Council of Ministers is also authorised, by a decision of the Minister of Finance after the endorsement of the Central Controller of Expenditure Commitment.

4- The transfer of appropriations provided for in the allocation "Liquid Fuels" for the benefit of the military bodies in the budget of the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities to the similar allocation in the other chapters is authorised by a decision of the Minister of Interior and Municipalities after the endorsement of the Central Controller of Expenditure Commitment.

Carrying forward uncommitted appropriations allocated pursuant to Law No. 303 dated 8/8/2022 and its amendments

Notwithstanding any other provision, the carrying forward of the balances of all uncommitted appropriations allocated pursuant to Law No. 303 dated 8/8/2022 and its amendments and deducted at a rate of 20% from passenger departure fees deposited in US dollars to the budget of the following year is authorised.

Healthcare Treatment Appropriations

Healthcare treatment appropriations shall be distributed by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, upon the joint proposal of the Minister of Public Health and the Minister of Finance, from the appropriations allocated in a lump sum under the chapter of the Ministry of Public Health designated for treatment in public and private institutions, centres, and hospitals, whereby an advance in the amount of 60%60% of the total value of the monthly invoices submitted by public and private hospitals under audit by the Audit Committee shall be granted in advance in order to facilitate hospital coverage, provided that the total value of the advances does not exceed the equivalent of one-third of the hospital's annual financial ceiling approved under the hospitalisation contracts.

Deduction of a Share of the Revenues Collected in Favour of Municipalities for Villages Without Municipalities

The Ministry of Finance shall deduct from the revenues collected in favour of municipalities, prior to their distribution, an amount of 500 billion Lebanese pounds, to be allocated exclusively for lighting, works, and cleaning in villages without municipalities (energy charges, maintenance, equipment, and cleaning) through the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities. The revenues shall be distributed by a decree upon the proposal of the Ministers of Finance and of Interior and Municipalities, provided that the decree encompasses all villages without municipalities.

Inadmissibility of Transfer Within the Item in a Certain Case

Notwithstanding any other provision, it shall be prohibited to transfer appropriations provided for under the paragraph "Water, Electricity, and Wired and Wireless Telecommunications" to any other sub-paragraph that does not fall under this paragraph.

Transfer of Appropriation Within the Item

Notwithstanding any other general or special provision, and with the exception of the budget of the Chamber of Deputies, the transfer of appropriations within the same item in all budgets whose appropriations are listed in detail within the General Budget shall be subject to the endorsement of the Central Controller of Expenditure Commitment.

- Consuls General and Consuls accredited in Lebanon.

- International officials of the United Nations Organization and its specialized agencies residing in Lebanon, and members of their families holding passports issued by the United Nations Organization.

- International officials of the United Nations Organization and its specialized agencies delegated to Lebanon on an official mission and holding passports issued by the United Nations Organization.

- Children under two years of age.

- Drivers of transport trucks and drivers of public cars and public buses, upon the entry of the vehicles into Lebanese territory.

- Nationals of foreign States, subject to reciprocity.

Amendment of Article 15 of Law No. 324 dated 12/2/20242024/2/12 (the Public Budget for the Year 2024)

Article 15 of Law No. 324 dated 12/2/20242024/2/12 (the Public Budget for the Year 2024) is amended to read as follows:

A- The following shall be collected in Lebanese Pounds:

- Shares reverting to the Lebanese State.

- Taxes and fees.

- Charges for all types of services provided by the Lebanese State through the various types of institutions owned, funded or managed, wholly or partially, by it, and if necessity requires equating the Lebanese Pound with any foreign currency in respect of the charges for certain services, this shall be mandatory in accordance with the actual exchange rate determined by the Banque du Liban in accordance with due process.

B- The following shall be exempted from the provisions of this paragraph:

First: Shares and profits reverting to the Lebanese State denominated in foreign currencies.

Second: Taxes and fees due on revenues, proceeds and interest accruing to their beneficiaries in foreign currencies:

- The tax due pursuant to the provisions of Article 51 of Law No. 2003/497 and its amendments (the Public Budget and Annexed Budgets Law for the Year 2003) with regard to continuing to withhold the tax according to the type of account.

- The tax due on revenues from foreign shares and debt bonds in accordance with the provisions of Title Three of the Income Tax Law.

- Taxes and fees due from petroleum right holder companies and operator petroleum right holder companies.

- Departure fees on passengers by sea and by air in United States Dollars.

- Consular fees collected by the departments of Lebanese diplomatic missions and consulates abroad, where they are collected in foreign currencies or in the local currency in which the diplomatic mission or consulate exercises its functions.

- Airport fees.

- All port fees in consideration of the use of the services of container terminals located in seaports in addition to loading and unloading fees in public yards and warehouses and vessels (general cargo) and all other port fees, including the fees paid by shipping agents for foreign vessels, in cash United States Dollars.

- Entrance fees to archaeological, heritage and historical installations and monuments and national museums belonging to the Ministry of Culture payable by non-Lebanese.

- Taxes and fees that are imposed in foreign currencies.

C- Taxpayers liable for taxes, fees and fines due in Lebanese Pounds are authorised to settle them in foreign currency (the United States Dollar or the Euro), provided that the actual exchange rate determined by the Banque du Liban is adopted upon conversion.

D- Where necessary, the details for the implementation of this Article shall be determined by a decision of the Minister of Finance.

2- Fee 2- A goods transport permit fee on board foreign trucks to a third country "other than the country of registration of the truck" through border crossings, or a goods transport permit fee to their own country in respect of refrigerated trucks, in the amount of USD 50 (fifty United States dollars)

Amendment of Article 23 of Legislative Decree No. 67 dated 5/8/1967 (the Fiscal Stamp Duty Law)

Article 23 of Legislative Decree No. 67 dated 5/8/1967 (the Fiscal Stamp Duty Law) shall be amended so as to read as follows:

A- The licence to sell fiscal stamps shall be granted by the Director of the Treasury at the Ministry of Finance to natural persons, including mukhtars during their term of office, to municipalities and unions of municipalities, and to other legal persons after verifying the fulfilment of the conditions set out below:

First: With respect to mukhtars:

The value of the stamps that they are licensed to sell shall be determined in an amount equivalent to the value of the stamp duty due on the transactions, certificates and attestations issued by them, and in this case the commission that they receive shall not be subject to income tax.

The mukhtar shall sign a written undertaking in which he commits to respecting the laws and regulations, and to implementing the instructions relating to the sale of stamps, in particular not selling them for amounts exceeding their nominal value inscribed thereon.

Second: With respect to a natural person other than a mukhtar:

1- The applicant for the licence must be Lebanese and not less than twenty years of age.

2- He must not have been convicted of a felony or a dishonourable misdemeanour.

3- He must be registered with the Ministry of Finance in the event that he practises work independently and must have fixed premises for sale.

4- There must be a need to establish new premises for selling fiscal stamps in the area in which his premises are located.

5- He must sign a written undertaking in which he commits to respecting the laws and regulations, and to implementing the instructions relating to the sale of stamps, in particular not selling them for amounts exceeding their nominal value inscribed thereon, and in which he also commits to registering with the tax administration immediately upon obtaining the permit if he was not previously registered.

The permit shall be granted pursuant to an application submitted by the President of the Municipal Council with respect to the municipality and the President of the Union of Municipalities with respect to the union, and the undertaking shall include a commitment to respecting the laws and regulations, and to implementing the instructions relating to the sale of stamps, in particular not selling them for amounts exceeding their nominal value inscribed thereon.

The value of the stamps that they are licensed to sell shall be determined in an amount equivalent to the value of the stamp duty due on the transactions, certificates and attestations issued by them,

Fourth: With respect to a legal person other than municipalities and unions of municipalities

1- It must be registered with the Ministry of Finance.

2- There must be a necessity for the permit in order to alleviate the burdens of citizens.

3- It must sign a written undertaking in which it commits to respecting the laws and regulations, and to implementing the instructions relating to the sale of stamps, in particular not selling them for amounts exceeding their nominal value inscribed thereon.

B- Notwithstanding any other text, the Director of the Treasury shall verify, through the employees competent in stamp affairs:

- The existence of the stamp licence.

- The compliance by the holder of the licence with the conditions specified above and the continued fulfilment thereof by him.

These employees shall undertake to establish violations in this regard by virtue of seizure reports in accordance with the procedures specified in Article 64 of this Legislative Decree, and they shall enjoy in this respect the capacity of the judicial police and the provisions of Article 63 thereof shall apply to them.

The Director of the Treasury must, pursuant to the seizure reports establishing the violations provided for in Articles 71 and 72 of this Legislative Decree, impose the fines specified therein.

Authorising the Customs Administration to collect an amount at a specified rate of the value of each import transaction, as a deposit on account of tax

The Customs Administration shall collect an amount at a rate of 1.5% (one and a half per cent) of the value of each import transaction carried out by a taxpayer who has failed to comply with submitting the returns relating to the results of his operations or with submitting the Value Added Tax returns, during any period of the three years preceding the year during which the importation takes place, as a deposit on account of the tax due from the taxpayers from whom it is collected, provided that this amount is entered into the tax account of the taxpayer and is deducted and deducted from the annual tax due from him in accordance with the returns submitted by him, whilst preserving the fines incurred by the taxpayer pursuant to the Tax Procedures Law.

Where a surplus of the amount collected from the taxpayer referred to above is due to him upon submitting the return after making the deduction, and no other taxes are due from him, he may submit an application for the refund of the surplus amount, and the Tax Administration shall be required to refund that amount within a period not exceeding thirty days from the date of submission of the application, failing which interest shall be incurred by it in favour of the taxpayer at the rate of interest on Treasury bills for the period of delay.

The provisions of customs legislation shall be adopted to determine the import transactions, the value of each of them, and the cases relating thereto, and the details of the application of this Article shall be determined, where necessary, by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.
