Amendment of Item 7 of Article 7 of Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (the Income Tax Law)

Item 7 of Article 7 of Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (the Income Tax Law) is amended to read as follows:

Depreciation calculated on the basis of the original cost price of the items of tangible fixed assets of the enterprise.

The Minister of Finance shall issue, upon the proposal of the Director of Finance General, a decision determining the rates of such depreciation within maximum and minimum limits, and the taxpayer shall have the right to choose the rate or rates suited to the conditions of his enterprise, provided that he deposits the depreciation schedule in advance with the competent tax office, failing which he shall be deemed to have chosen the minimum depreciation rate.

The chosen rate or rates shall remain fixed and mandatory throughout the specified period until the depreciation value equals the original cost price.

As for passenger cars, the taxpayer shall be permitted to depreciate them provided that the original cost price of a single passenger car does not exceed 30,000 USD, and provided that passenger cars owned by enterprises engaged in the activity of car rental or the activity of providing paid passenger transport services, and hotels and tourist resorts classified as four stars and above, shall be exempted from this maximum limit.

If the cost of the car exceeds 30,000 USD, depreciation shall be calculated only up to 30,000 USD as a maximum cost limit.

As for intangible fixed assets, they may not be depreciated unless they are required to be relinquished without consideration upon the arrival of a fixed term, in which case they shall be depreciated in equal annual instalments throughout the period remaining until the arrival of that term.

The detailed rules for the application of this Article shall be determined, where necessary, pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

Amendment of Article 28 of Law No. 379 dated 14/12/200114/12/2001 (Value Added Tax)

Article 28 of Law No. 379 dated 14/12/200114/12/2001 (Value Added Tax) shall be amended to read as follows:

Deductible tax is the tax that has been charged on goods or services acquired by the taxable person from another taxable person and the goods and services that he has imported, including fixed assets, in order to carry out, within the framework of exercising his economic activity, one of the following operations:

1- The supply of goods and the provision of services subject to tax.

2- Operations related to exportation and similar operations and international transport operations exempted from tax pursuant to Articles 19, 20 and 21 of this Law.

Tax that has been charged on the stock of goods and raw materials held by the taxable person on the effective date of his registration for the tax, which he had acquired at a prior date, shall be deductible, provided that he allocates them to carry out taxable operations, in accordance with rules and procedures determined by a decision of the Minister of Finance.

Tax that has been charged on fixed assets acquired by a taxable person at a date prior to his becoming subject to tax and which he allocates to carry out taxable operations shall also be deductible.

Fixed assets within the meaning of this Article shall mean tangible property consisting of machinery and equipment intended for permanent use in the enterprise as a working tool or a means of investment.

As for the tax that has been charged on a passenger car, its deduction shall be accepted if the value of this car does not exceed the amount of 30,000 USD exclusive of Value Added Tax, and if the value of this car exceeds the amount of 30,000 USD exclusive of Value Added Tax, the deduction of the tax shall be accepted up to a maximum equivalent to the tax due upon purchasing a passenger car with a value of 30,000 USD exclusive of Value Added Tax, and the right to partial deduction, where it exists, shall be calculated on the basis of this maximum tax,

The maximum limit referred to above shall not apply if such car is used in passenger transport for hire service activities, or car rental activities, or the activities of hotels and tourist resorts classified as four stars and above.

Value Added Tax that has been charged on the following expenses shall be non-deductible:

a - Rental of passenger cars when the value of the passenger car exceeds 30,000 USD, with the exception of those used in passenger transport for hire service activities, or car rental activities, or the activities of hotels and tourist resorts classified as four stars and above.

b - Consumption of water, electricity, telecommunications, internet and petrol.

The rules and procedures for the application of this Article shall be determined by a decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

Amendment of Article 30 of Law No. 379 dated 2001/12/14 (Value Added Tax) and its amendments

Article 30 of Law No. 379 dated 2001/12/14 (Value Added Tax) and its amendments is amended to read as follows:

If the amount of deductible tax, at the end of a given tax period, exceeds the amount of tax due, the excess shall be carried forward to the subsequent period.

A taxable person shall have the right to submit, after the end of any calendar year and within a period of one month, an application for the refund of the balance of the excess deductible tax as at that date, provided that the amount claimed for refund is not less than two hundred million Lebanese Pounds.

Exporters shall have the right to submit, after the end of any tax calculation period and within a period of one month, an application for the refund of the balance of the excess deductible tax calculated for that period, provided that the amount claimed for refund is not less than two hundred million Lebanese Pounds.

Every person whose application for cancellation of registration has been approved by the Administration shall have the right to apply for the refund of the excess deductible tax, and within a period of one month from the date of expiry of the tax calculation period during which he was notified of the Tax Administration's approval of his application for cancellation of registration.

The Administration shall decide upon the refund application within a maximum period of three months from the date of expiry of the period specified for submitting refund applications.

The period shall be extended for an equal duration and once only if the Tax Administration finds it necessary to expand the examination of the taxpayer or to place the taxpayer's file on the tax audit programme for periods prior to the refund application.

If the Administration approves the refund application, wholly or partially, it shall return to the taxable person the amount due, failing which interest shall accrue on the unpaid amount at a rate equal to the average interest on Treasury bills for the category of six, provided that such rate does not exceed 9%9% per annum after the expiry of four months from the submission of the application or seven months in the event of extension of the period by the Tax Administration.

Amendment of Article 59 of Law No. 379 dated 14/12/2001 (Value Added Tax) and its amendments

Article 59 of Law No. 379 dated 14/12/2001 (Value Added Tax) and its amendments is amended to become to become as follows:

A refund may be requested for the full amount of the tax incurred on fixed assets that have been used in order to carry out the following tax-exempt activities in accordance with the provisions of Articles 16 and 17 of this Law:

- The manufacture of medicines.

- The manufacture of foodstuffs exempt from tax pursuant to the provisions of Paragraph (b) of Article 17 of this Law.

- Hospitalisation and medical laboratories.

- Education.

- The activities of bodies and associations having public utility status, and those concerned with the care of persons with special needs, the elderly, orphans, children, and persons suffering from mental illnesses, cancer, and other illnesses determined by a decision of the Council of Ministers.

- Collective transport of persons.

- The manufacture of books, newspapers and magazines.

- The manufacture of pharmaceutical products, including items for hygienic and pharmaceutical use (such as contraceptive sheaths, male condoms, sanitary pads and protectors, baby diapers and similar sanitary items).

- The manufacture of paper and paperboard of the kinds used for writing or printing, newsprint in rolls or sheets, printing ink.

- The manufacture of fodder.

Fixed assets, within the meaning of this Article, mean machinery and equipment intended for permanent use in the enterprise.

As for the tax incurred on a passenger vehicle, its refund shall be accepted if the value of such vehicle does not exceed the amount of USD 30,000 excluding Value Added Tax, and if the value of such vehicle exceeds the amount of USD 30,000 excluding Value Added Tax, a refund of the tax shall be accepted up to a maximum equivalent to the tax due upon the purchase of a passenger vehicle valued at USD 30,000 excluding Value Added Tax, and the refund shall be calculated on the basis of this maximum tax.

A refund may also be requested for 100% 100% of the tax incurred on current expenditure relating to the transactions referred to above.

Value Added Tax incurred on the following expenditure shall be non-refundable:

a- The rental of passenger vehicles where the value of the passenger vehicle exceeds USD 30,000.

b - The consumption of water, electricity, telecommunications, internet and petrol.

The taxpayer may submit, at the end of any calendar year and within a period of one month, a refund request in respect of the exempt transactions in accordance with the provisions of this Article, provided that the amount claimed for refund is not less than two hundred million Lebanese Pounds, and the amount that is less than two hundred million Lebanese Pounds shall be carried forward to the following year; however, where the taxpayer is no longer classified in accordance with the provisions of this Article, he may submit the said refund request regardless of the value of the request.

The details of the implementation of this Article shall be determined, where necessary, by a decree adopted upon the proposal of the Minister of Finance.

Extending the time limit specified in Law No. 330 dated 4/12/2024 for the revaluation of inventory and the revaluation of fixed assets and extending the time limit specified for the tax administration to decide on applications for revaluation, whether for inventory or for fixed assets

Notwithstanding the provisions of Clause 1 of First of Article Two of Law No. 330 dated 4/12/2024, taxpayers who are permitted to carry out a revaluation of their inventory in accordance with the provisions of Article Two of the Law shall be granted a time limit of three months from the date of publication of this Law to carry out the revaluation process of their inventory for the years 2023 and 2024, and 2024, provided that the undertaking relating to the retention by the taxpayer of the documents specific to the revaluation is attached to the application for revaluation, and taxpayers who are permitted to carry out an exceptional revaluation of their fixed assets in accordance with the provisions of the same Article Two shall also be granted a similar time limit to carry out the valuation process of those assets.

The time limit specified for the tax administration to decide on applications for revaluation, whether for inventory or for fixed assets, shall also be extended until 31/12/2030.

The details of the application of this Article shall be determined, where necessary, pursuant to a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

Granting an exceptional time limit to submit applications for refund in accordance with the provisions of Article 59 of Law No. 379 dated 14/12/2001 and its amendments (Value Added Tax) pertaining to the year 2024

Reduction of certain fines payable in favour of the State, municipalities, unions of municipalities, public institutions, or other persons of public law

With the exception of fines resulting from violations for the settlement of which their specific laws have laid down specific provisions, and fines resulting from the regularization of violations on maritime and riverine public property, fines payable to the State, municipalities, unions of municipalities, public institutions, or other persons of public law, regardless of the method of their collection (collection order, recovery order, collection receipt...), shall exceptionally be reduced by 85%, provided that the fine after reduction shall not be less than /200,000/ L.L. / two hundred thousand Lebanese Pounds for fines levied in Lebanese Pounds and /5$/ five United States Dollars for fines levied in United States Dollars, on condition that the full amounts payable together with the reduced fines are paid within a time limit of three months from the date of publication of this Law.

All fines paid prior to the publication of this Law shall be deemed an acquired right of the Treasury and may not be refunded.

Amendment of the First, Ninth (Clause 5), Tenth, Sixteenth, Eighteenth, Nineteenth, Twenty-First, Forty-First, and Forty-Third Articles of Legislative Decree No. 146 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Transfer Duty Law)

The First, Ninth (Clause 5), Tenth, Sixteenth, Eighteenth, Nineteenth, Twenty-First, Forty-First, and Forty-Third Articles of Legislative Decree No. 146 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Transfer Duty Law) shall be amended to read as follows:

First: Amendment of the First Article of Legislative Decree No. 146 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Transfer Duty Law):

The First Article of Legislative Decree No. 146 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Transfer Duty Law) shall be amended to read as follows:

A transfer duty shall be imposed on all rights and movable and immovable property that devolve to third parties, with the exception of the State, municipalities, and unions of municipalities, by way of inheritance, will, gift, or waqf, or by any other way without consideration equivalent to their true value, and events that occurred prior to 1/1/2007 shall be exempted from transfer duties, and the competent

judicial authorities shall be permitted to issue judgments of determination of heirs and execution of wills to the concerned parties without their presenting the licence required from the competent departments at the Ministry of Finance for deaths occurring prior to 1/1/2007.

Second: Amendment of the Fifth Clause of the Ninth Article of Legislative Decree No. 146/59 (Transfer Duty Law) amended pursuant to Article 56 of Law Effectively in Force No. 10 dated 15/11/2022 (General Budget Law for the Year 2022):

The Fifth Clause of the Ninth Article of Legislative Decree No. 146/59 (Transfer Duty Law) amended pursuant to Article 56 of Law Effectively in Force No. 10 dated 15/11/2022 (General Budget Law for the Year 2022) shall be amended to read as follows:

1- In respect of events occurring up to 15/11/2022 inclusive:

Shall be exempted from the duty, the portion of the net hereditary share that does not exceed:

a- For each of the descendants, spouses, and parents: one hundred and twenty million pounds.

b- For each of the ascendants other than the parents, and the brother and sister: forty-eight million pounds.

c- For each of the remaining heirs: twenty-four million pounds.

And there shall be added to the value of the exempted portion of the hereditary share of the children:

- Seventy-two million pounds when the child is afflicted with a permanent disability that prevents him from working.

- Four million and eight hundred thousand pounds for each year or fraction of a year separating the minor child from the eighteenth year of his age.

- Forty-eight million pounds when the heir has a dependent husband or wife, and twenty-four million pounds for each child who has not exceeded the age of eighteen provided that the total of these additions does not exceed the limit of one hundred and twenty million pounds.

2- In respect of events occurring with effect from the date of 16/11/2022 :

Shall be exempted from the duty the portion of the net hereditary share that does not exceed:

a- For each of the descendants, spouses, and parents: two billion and four hundredfour hundred million pounds.

b- For each of the ascendants other than the parents, and the brother and sister: nine hundrednine hundred and sixty million pounds.

c- For each of the remaining heirs: four hundredfour hundred and eighty million pounds.

And there shall be added to the value of the exempted portion of the hereditary share of the children:

- One billion and four hundredfour hundred and forty million pounds when the child is afflicted with a permanent disability that prevents him from working.

- Ninety-six million pounds for each year or fraction of a year separating the minor child from the eighteenth year of his age.

- Nine hundrednine hundred and sixty million pounds when the heir has a dependent husband or wife, and four hundredfour hundred and eighty million pounds for each child who has not exceeded the age of eighteen, provided that the total of these additions does not exceed the limit of two billion and four hundredfour hundred million pounds.

In order to benefit from the additions enumerated in this paragraph, it is required that the cause that gave rise to the right thereto be existing on the date of the decedent's death.

This amendment shall apply to uncompleted transactions or those whose duties have not been paid up to the date of issuance of this Law.

Third: Amendment of Article 10 of Legislative Decree No. 146 issued on 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Imposition of a Transfer Duty on Movable and Immovable Property):

Article 10 of Legislative Decree No. 146 issued on 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Imposition of a Transfer Duty on Movable and Immovable Property) shall be amended, to read as follows:

Shall be excluded permanently or temporarily from the estate:

1 - Debts owed to the decedent by bankrupt persons

2 - Bad debts or uncollectible debts.

3 - Disputed rights and the right of recourse against third parties

4 - Buildings that were demolished, or are demolished after the publication of this Law, due to the Israeli aggressions against Lebanon which fall within the elements of the estate of a deceaseddeceased person whose duties have not been liquidated, provided that the value of the land upon which those buildings were erected remains within the elements of the estate

Every heir in cases 1, 2 and 3 referred to above, must claim before the judiciary within a period of six months the rights and debts designated for him by the financial departments. If the designated time limit expires and the heir has not instituted the necessary lawsuits or has shown negligence in pursuing them, the said rights and debts shall be included in the valuation of his hereditary share.

Fourth: Amendment of Article 16 of Legislative Decree No. 146/59 (Transfer Duty Law):

Article 16 of Legislative Decree No. 146/59 (Transfer Duty Law) shall be amended to read as follows:

Shall be exempted from duties all assistance, subsidies, and grants paid from public funds, and every gift whose value does not exceed one million and six hundred thousand pounds shall also be exempted. . If it exceeds that, the duty shall be levied on the excess unless the donee is a charitable institution or a sports, cultural, artistic, charitable, or religious association, including religious waqfs, in which case the exemption shall cover an amount of one hundred million pounds in respect of events occurring up to the date of 15/11/2022 inclusive.

As for events occurring after 15/11/2022, all assistance, subsidies, and grants paid from public funds shall be exempted from duties, and every gift whose value does not exceed ninety-six million pounds shall also be exempted.

If it exceeds that, the duty shall be levied on the excess unless the donee is a charitable institution or a sports, cultural, artistic, charitable, or religious association, including religious waqfs, in which case the exemption shall cover an amount of six billion pounds.

This amendment shall apply to uncompleted transactions or those whose duties have not been paid up to the date of issuance of this Law.

Fifth: Amendment of Article 18 of Legislative Decree No. 146/59 (Transfer Duty Law):

Article 18 of Legislative Decree No. 146/59 (Transfer Duty Law) shall be amended to read as follows:

The duty shall be payable by the beneficiaries of the waqf with the exception of the founder of the waqf himself and shall be imposed on the value of the entitlement assessed in accordance with the third paragraph of Article 36 of this Legislative Decree after deducting an amount of one million and six hundred thousand Lebanese pounds from the value of the share

of each beneficiary in respect of events occurring up to 15/11/2022 inclusive and after deducting an amount of ninety-six million Lebanese pounds from the value of the share of each beneficiary in respect of events occurring after this date.

The duty shall be levied upon the death of the founder of the waqf and its assessment shall be renewed upon the renewal of the entitlement; the first time, the degree of kinship of the beneficiaries shall be determined in relation to the founder of the waqf, and thereafter in relation to the person whom they replaced.

This amendment shall apply to uncompleted transactions or those whose duties have not been paid up to the date of issuance of this Law.

Sixth: Amendment of Article 19 of Legislative Decree No. 146/59 (Transfer Duty Law):

Article 19 of Legislative Decree No. 146/59 (Transfer Duty Law) shall be amended to read as follows:

Upon the termination of the waqf, the duty shall be payable on two-thirds of the value of the property and shall be imposed on the value of the share of each right holder after deducting an amount of one million and six hundred thousand Lebanese pounds therefrom in respect of events occurring up to 15/11/2022 inclusive and after deducting an amount of ninety-six million Lebanese pounds therefrom in respect of events occurring after this date.

This amendment shall apply to uncompleted transactions or those whose duties have not been paid up to the date of issuance of this Law.

Seventh: Amendment of Article 21 of Legislative Decree No. 146 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Imposition of a Transfer Duty on All Rights and Movable and Immovable Property):

Article 21 of Legislative Decree No. 146 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (Imposition of a Transfer Duty on All Rights and Movable and Immovable Property) shall be amended to read as follows:

Heirs, donees, waqf beneficiaries, executors of wills, guardiansand waqfs, or their legal representatives must submit to the competent financial departments within 90 (ninety) days from the occurrence of the death, gift, execution of the will or waqf, or judgment of death of an absent person, a declaration containing the name of the decedent, donor, founder of the waqf, or testator, and the names

of the heirs, donees, legatees, waqf beneficiaries, and executors of the will or waqf, together with the place of residence of each of them and the particulars of the transferred property of all kinds in addition to its location and its true sale value.

The concerned parties shall attach to the declaration the documents substantiating it (the death certificate, family civil status extracts for the deceased and the heirs, title deeds or real estate certificates, the instrument of the will or the gift contract).

The concerned parties mentioned above must also submit all documents and evidence relating to their declaration within a period of six months at most from the date of occurrence of the event that gave rise to the duty (death, will, gift, waqf, termination of waqf) and submit a special declaration of the value of the duty and pay the duty due in accordance with the self-assessment method within the same period, pursuant to two forms prepared by the Ministry of Finance specifically for this purpose, while preserving the right of the heirs to benefit from the instalment provisions stipulated in this Law. In the event of a violation, the provisions of Article 55 and 63and 13 of Law No. 2008/4444/2008 and its amendments (Tax Procedures) shall apply.

. The supporting documents required to be submitted for each type of event giving rise to the duty shall be determined by decisions issued by the Minister of Finance.

The competent department must complete the estate file, make a supplementary assessment of the duty if due, and issue the payment order relating thereto within a maximum period of six months from the date of submission of the documents and evidence relating to the declaration and payment of the duty, and grant the licences for transferring ownership of the elements that were abstained from being declared.

In the event of failure to submit the declaration and documents and failure to pay the duty, the competent department shall resort to direct assessment as at the date of death, provided that it completes the estate file and issues the payment order for the duty and the fines incurred within a period of six months from the date of expiry of the period for submitting the documents and paying the duty.

Eighth: Amendment of Article 41 of Legislative Decree No. 59/146146/59 (Transfer Duty Law):

Article 41 of Legislative Decree No. 59/146146/59 (Transfer Duty Law) shall be amended to read as follows:

The transfer duty shall be imposed on the net hereditary share of estates and the net share bequeathed to an heir in accordance with the rates specified in Schedule (No. 1) annexed to this Legislative Decree after making the deductions stipulated in

the preceding Article 9 in respect of events occurring prior to 16/11/2022 and in accordance with the rates specified in Schedule (No. 3)(No. 2) annexed to this Legislative Decree after making the deductions stipulated in the preceding Article 9 in respect of events occurring or that may occur after this date.

Ninth: Amendment of Article 43 of Legislative Decree No. 146/59 (Transfer Duty Law):

Article 43 of Legislative Decree No. 146/59 (Transfer Duty Law) shall be amended to read as follows:

A flat transfer duty of five per thousand shall be imposed on all rights and movable and immovable property that devolve to third parties, with the exception of the State, municipalities, and unions of municipalities, by way of inheritance, will, gift, or waqf, or by any other way without consideration equivalent to their true value.

This flat additional duty shall be due on the portion of the gross total value of the transferred rights, property, and values that exceeds forty million Lebanese pounds, in respect of events occurring up to 15/11/2022 inclusive.

As for events occurring after 15/11/2022, this flat additional duty shall be due on the portion of the gross total value of the transferred rights, property, and values that exceeds two billion and four hundred million Lebanese pounds, and it shall be considered among the debts and liabilities incurred on the total of the said elements.

At the request of the concerned parties, this duty may be distributed in accordance with the proportions of the heirs' shares and without considering it among the burdens of the estate, notwithstanding the provisions of the preceding paragraph of this Article.

Extension of the periods provided for in Articles Three, Five, Seven and Nine of Law No. 139 dated 9/7/2019 (Settlement of building violations committed during the period from 13/9/1971 until 31/12/2018 inclusive)

Amendment of the time limit for submitting the periodic declaration set forth in Clause 4 of Article 35 of Law No. 379 dated 14/12/2001 (Value Added Tax) and its amendments and the time limit set forth in Article 39 thereof

Amendment of Article 93 of Law No. 324 dated 12/2/2024 (Public Budget Law for the Year 2024)

Article 93 of Law No. 324 dated 12/2/2024 (Public Budget Law for the Year 2024) shall be amended so as to read as follows:

"Notwithstanding any other provision, profits realised by natural and legal persons as a result of transactions executed by them on the Sayrafa platform pursuant to the circulars of the Banque du Liban issued in this regard and which exceed the amount of 100,000 US dollars (one hundred thousand US dollars) shall be subject to an additional exceptional tax at a rate of 17%17%, and nothing shall be exempted from this tax except differences related to salaries and wages".

This amendment shall take effect as of 15/2/2024 (the date of the Public Budget for the Year 2024).

The details of the application of this Article, particularly with regard to transactions declared prior to the publication of this amendment, shall be determined, where necessary, by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

Exemption from Duties for Non-Polluting Cars and Vehicles, Including Hybrid Ones (Mild Hybrid ,Hybrid, Hybrid plug-in) or Those Operating on Electricity full electric

(1) All new cars, vehicles, and machinery (such as electric bikes - e-scooter - e-bicycle) operating on electricity full electric, which are imported within five years as of the date of entry into force of this Law, shall be exempted from 100% of the customs duty and the internal consumption duty, and 70% of the registration fee and circulation fees (road tax / mécanique) upon registration for the first time only.

(2) As for new cars of all hybrid types, including (Mild Hybrid ,Hybrid, Hybrid plug-in) and others, which will be imported within five years as of the date of entry into force of this Law, they shall benefit from an exemption at a rate of 80% of the customs duty and the internal consumption duty, and 70% of the registration fee and circulation fees (road tax / mécanique) upon registration for the first time only.

Suspension of additional employment at the Ministry of Education and Higher Education at the expense of mutual funds, parents' funds, municipalities, and any other entity

Notwithstanding any other provision, contracting for the upcoming academic year with additional teachers at the Ministry of Education and Higher Education at the expense of mutual funds, school funds, parents' funds, municipalities, and any other entity shall be suspended, with the exception of mechanisation workers, employees, and teachers engaged for the morning shift at the expense of donor states whose services are proven to be of utmost necessity, provided that their employment is approved exclusively by the Minister of Education and Higher Education after verifying the Administration's need for them, and provided that the Ministry of Education and Higher Education takes the necessary measures to restrict contracting within the capacities of the funds and under specific conditions, and to stop burdening the Treasury with new charges that it did not previously bear, within a period of two months from the date of issuance of this Law.

Publication of the Law

This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Amendment of Article 52 of the draft law promulgated by Decree No. 14969 dated 30/12/1963 (the Public Accounting Law), as amended pursuant to Article 85 of Law No. 144/2019 (the General Budget and Annexed Budgets Law for the year 2019)

Article 52 of the draft law promulgated by Decree No. 14969 dated 30/12/1963 (the Public Accounting Law), as amended pursuant to Article 85 of Law No. 144/2019 (the General Budget and Annexed Budgets Law for the year 2019), shall be amended to read as follows:

1. Cash grants offered to the State by legal and natural persons shall be accepted by a decree issued upon the proposal of the competent minister and the Minister of Finance if their value does not exceed 11,500,000,000 Lebanese pounds.

2. Cash grants offered to the State by legal and natural persons shall be accepted by a decree adopted in the Council of Ministers if their value exceeds 11,500,000,000 Lebanese pounds.

4. Cash and in-kind grants received by the Lebanese Treasury shall be recorded in the revenues section of the budget, and if such grants have a specific expenditure purpose, appropriations equal to their value shall be opened for them in accordance with the established rules in the expenditures section.

The text of Article 2 of Law No. 305 dated 3/4/2001 has been amended to read as follows:

Article 2: The mission of the Order of Physiotherapists in Lebanon is a professional, health, scientific and administrative mission, the object of which is:

1 - To unite the ranks of physiotherapists, preserve their legitimate rights and interests, raise the standard of their profession, watch over the ethics and dignity of the physiotherapy profession, and observe the requirements of public order and public morals.

2 - To discipline physiotherapists who violate the law regulating the profession, its internal regulations, or the ethics of the profession.

3 - To express an opinion on draft laws and regulations relating to the physiotherapy profession at the request of the competent ministries.

4 - To express an opinion on the dispatch of delegations to attend physiotherapy conferences organised by local or international health or educational bodies.

5 - To cooperate with the Ministry of Public Health in inspecting for the licensing to open and operate physiotherapy centres, provided that a joint mechanism is established for this purpose.

6 - To endeavour with the Government to adopt the resolutions that the Order deems useful in matters relating to public health, prevention and rehabilitation.

7 - To endeavour to settle disputes that arise among physiotherapists, or between physiotherapists

and their patients, all arising out of the practice of the profession.

8 - To cooperate with the various workers in the health and medical fields and with all other local and international orders, associations, bodies and federations connected with physiotherapy, in order to raise the standard of the profession and exchange expertise and information.

9 - To represent the physiotherapy profession before all local authorities, whether governmental or private, and international authorities.

The text of Article 3 of Law No. 305 dated 3/4/2001 has been amended to read as follows:

Article 3: No physiotherapist shall be entitled to practise the physiotherapy profession across all Lebanese territory unless he is affiliated with the Order of Physiotherapists in Lebanon.

The text of Article 4 of Law No. 305 dated 3/4/2001 has been amended to read as follows:

Article 4:

"A - Subject to the provisions of Article Two of Law No. 96/99 dated 18/6/1999, anyone who submits an application for affiliation with the Order must fulfil the following conditions:

1 - Be Lebanese and enjoy their civil rights.

2 - The physical therapist must hold a university degree in physical therapy and/or a Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT) diploma from an official or private local university or from a foreign university recognised by the Lebanese State, provided that the duration of their study is not less than four years for the degree, and two years for the doctorate.

3 - Hold the Lebanese Baccalaureate Certificate Part Two or its official equivalent.

4 - Not be convicted of a dishonourable misdemeanour or a felony mentioned in their judicial record extract.

5 - Have passed the Colloquium examination conducted by the Ministry of Education and Higher Education.

6 - Hold a licence to practise the profession of physical therapy from the Ministry of Public Health.

7 - Have completed the age of twenty-one.

8 - Submit three passport-size photographs certified by the Mukhtar of the locality.

B - With regard to the affiliation of foreigners, the provisions of Article Four of Law 8/78 shall be observed in addition to the applicable legal procedures and the membership conditions mentioned above, and the licence to practise the profession of physical therapy shall be granted to the foreign therapist provided that they are a national of a country in which the Lebanese physical therapist is permitted to practise their profession on the basis of reciprocity. Foreign affiliates shall not have the right to be elected or to elect.

C - The application for affiliation shall be in writing and addressed to the Council of the Order and accompanied by the required documents together with a certificate of residence for the applicant for affiliation from the Mukhtar of the locality, and containing an undertaking to abide by the laws of the Order, its internal regulations, and the mandatory decisions of its Council."

The text of Article 5 of Law No. 305 dated 3/4/2001 has been amended to read as follows:

"Article 5: The Council of the Order shall examine the application for affiliation accompanied by the required mandatory documents in the first session it holds after the date of its submission or within a maximum period of two months, and shall decide to accept it if it fulfils the legal conditions, and no application fulfilling the conditions may be rejected except with clear reasoning for such rejection.

The physical therapist whose application for affiliation is rejected shall have the right to petition the Court of Appeal hearing syndical matters."

The text of Article 9 of Law No. 305 dated 3/4/2001 has been amended to read as follows:

"Article 9: None other than physical therapists registered on the roll of the Order who have paid in full the annual subscriptions due from them before the end of the last day of the month of June

of each year shall have the right to participate in the General Assembly, and none other than these shall have the right to stand as candidates and to vote (provided that they hold Lebanese nationality)."

The text of Article 10 of Law No. 305 dated 3/4/2001 has been amended to read as follows:

"Article 10:

1 - A physical therapist who is in arrears in the payment of the annual fee without a legitimate excuse for a period of two consecutive years shall have his name struck off the roll by a decision of the Council of the Order after being notified by means of a notice serving as a formal warning posted on the notice board at the headquarters of the Order or by registered mail with acknowledgment of receipt for a period of one month, and he shall not have the right to apply for the re-registration of his name until after he has paid the overdue fees and the prescribed fines incurred.

2 - A member who has been expelled and struck off the rolls of the Order shall have the right to submit a new application for membership upon the cessation of the causes that led to his expulsion.

3 - In all cases, namely in cases of expulsion, striking off, or temporary or permanent suspension from the practice of the profession by a decision of the Council of the Order or by final disciplinary judgments, or striking off for non-payment of the annual subscriptions for a period of two years without an acceptable excuse or for any other reason, the Order must immediately notify the competent authorities of the decision of striking off, expulsion, or prohibition from the practice of the profession, even if temporarily, and in particular the Ministry of Public Health in order to take the necessary legal action, and notify the National Social Security Fund with a view to taking the appropriate measures."

The text of Article 11 of Law No. 305 dated 3/4/2001 has been amended to read as follows:

"Article 11: The President of the Order shall preside over the General Assembly, and in the event of his absence or inability to attend, he shall be replaced successively by: the Vice President of the Order, then the Secretary of the Council, then the oldest member.

The President of the Order and the Secretary shall prepare the agenda of the ordinary and extraordinary General Assembly and submit it to

the Council of the Order for approval, and in all cases, the notice of convocation including the agenda shall be posted at the headquarters of the Order at least fifteen days prior to the date of the meeting, and the notice of convocation shall be published on the official website of the Order, stating the date and venue of the meeting."

Article Eight, the text of Article 12 of Law No. 305 dated 3/4/2001 has been amended to read as follows:

"Article 12: A meeting of the ordinary General Assembly shall not be deemed valid unless attended by more than half of the members of the Order who have paid their annual subscriptions before the end of the month of June of each year.

As for the convening of the extraordinary General Assembly, it shall not be deemed valid unless attended by two-thirds of the members who have paid their subscriptions up to the date of the notice of convocation to its meeting.

In both cases, if a quorum is not reached, the notice of convocation shall be repeated for a meeting to be held within fifteen days from the first notice of convocation, and such meeting shall be valid regardless of the number of attendees.

The ordinary General Assembly shall adopt its resolutions by voting and by an absolute majority of the members present.

As for the extraordinary General Assembly, it shall adopt its resolutions by voting and by a two-thirds majority of the members present."

The text of Article 13 of Law No. 305 dated 3/4/2001 was amended so as to read as follows:

"Article 13: The powers of the General Assembly shall encompass all matters capable of achieving the purpose and objectives of the Order, and shall encompass in particular the following matters:

1 - Electing the members of the Council of the Order and the President of the Order for a term of three years, and two members for the Disciplinary Council for a term of one year, and electing two members for the Retirement Fund Committee for a term of three years, and a Comptroller General for the Retirement Fund (from among the former Presidents of the Order) and two assistants, whose term of office shall be for one year (from among the former members of the Council of the Order or of the Disciplinary Council).

2 - Approving the resolutions proposed to it by the Council of the Order.

3 - Approving the financial report after examining and discussing it, as well as discussing the budget of the upcoming financial year proposed, where applicable, by the Council of the Order in order to adopt it.

4 - Determining the general orientations of the various activities, and examining the agenda and taking the appropriate decisions in respect thereof.

5 - Determining and amending the annual subscription fee and the registration fee imposed on physical therapists, and the candidacy fee for elections.

6 - Determining the monthly retirement pension in accordance with the prepared study, and amending the annual subscription fee for the Retirement Fund, which shall be paid annually in parallel with the annual fee of the Order.

7 - Auditing the accounts of the previous year and the closing of accounts and approving them.

8 - Granting discharge to the President of the Order and the members of the Council immediately upon the approval of the final account for the previous year."

The text of Article 18 of Law No. 305 dated 3/4/2001 was amended so as to read as follows:

"Article 18: Every Lebanese registered with the Order who has practised the profession for a period of at least ten years on Lebanese territory shall have the right to stand as a candidate for membership of the Council of the Order of Physical Therapists in Lebanon and/or for membership of the Disciplinary Council and/or for the Retirement Fund Committee. A physical therapist who has practised the profession for a period of at least fifteen years on Lebanese territory shall have the right to stand as a candidate for the post of President of the Order."

The text of Article 25 of Law No. 305 dated 3/4/2001 has been amended to read as follows:

"Article 25: If, for any reason whatsoever, one or two positions among the members of the Council of the Order fall vacant before the expiry of the term of office, the vacant position shall be filled by the candidate who obtained the highest number of votes in the previous elections.

However, if three or more positions fall vacant before the expiry of two thirds of the term of office of the Council, the Extraordinary General Assembly shall be convened to fill the vacant positions in an electoral session solely to complete the remainder of the term of office."

The text of Article 27 of Law No. 305 dated 3/4/2001 has been amended to read as follows:

"Article 27: The following matters shall fall within the functions of the Council of the Order:

1 - Laying down and amending the Internal Regulations of the Order and all other regulations relating to the Order, with the approval of the Minister of Public Health, and the date of such approval shall be deemed the entry into force for the implementation of the provisions of these regulations.

2 - Implementing the resolutions of the General Assembly.

3 - Preparing the annual budget and the annual financial report.

4 - Managing the general accounts of the Order, collecting the annual fee and the registration fee payable by Lebanese and foreign physical therapists, and proposing their amendment before the General Assembly for approval.

5 - Endeavouring to settle disputes between physical therapists and other members of the health and medical professions, or between physical therapists and their patients, arising out of the practice of the profession.

6 - Determining the value of the fees for paper and electronic services.

7 - Issuing an annual schedule of the minimum fee for a physical therapy session across all Lebanese territory. It shall be binding upon all physical therapists under penalty of disciplinary accountability, and this schedule shall be used for guidance by all insurance companies, funds, official and private guarantor bodies, hospital institutions, all licensed physical therapy centres, sports clubs and federations, primary health care centres, and dispensaries.

8 - Endeavouring to oblige all sports institutions, clubs, and federations to accredit at least one

physical therapist duly registered with the Order and entered on its general roll, who shall be present on the field and accompany the sports teams, with the mandatory licensing of physical therapy centres located inside sports clubs of all kinds, inside hospitals and joint medical centres, and in primary health care centres and dispensaries.

9 - Managing the business of the Order and organising work therein which do not fall within the functions of the competence of the General Assembly.

10 - Appointing and determining the wages of the administrative, financial, and professional staff of the Order, and dismissing them in accordance with due process.

11 - Determining the minimum wages of physical therapists who receive monthly salaries.

12 - Contracting with technical experts, legal advisers, and lawyers, determining their fees, terminating their services, and paying their indemnities.

13 - Contracting with insurance companies or others, and entrusting the President of the Order with drawing up the necessary powers of attorney as well as signing agreements and contracts with the Secretary.

14 - Mutual cooperation with ministerial and security authorities, bodies, and persons in relation to the interests of the Order and its members, and expressing an opinion on draft projects referred by the Ministry of Public Health or official authorities.

15 - Monitoring the compliance of all physical therapists within Lebanese territory with the laws and ethics of the profession and the duties of their profession, and full adherence to its regulations and the decisions of the Council of the Order and the circulars issued by it.

16 - Media appearances and publishing on social media platforms shall be subject to the approval of the Order in accordance with a mechanism determined by the Council of the Order in matters that do not prejudice the honour and dignity of the profession or detract from its value. In the event of non-compliance, offenders shall be subject to disciplinary accountability.

17 - The Order shall lay down therapeutic intervention protocols and the techniques permitted for use by the physical therapist in accordance with the tasks specified for them in the Law on the Practice of the Profession, and which do not conflict or overlap with other medical professions.

18 - Organising and managing scientific seminars and courses held at the Order for physical therapists and physical therapy students.

19 - Obliging the physical therapist to attend "Continuing Scientific Education" courses, the number of which and the number of credits required to be obtained by the therapist periodically or annually shall be determined by the Order, organised at the Order or within higher education institutions, universities, or scientific conferences, in cooperation between them and the Order and under its supervision, with the aim of enhancing and developing the scientific and professional capabilities of the physical therapist.

In the event that the physical therapist does not hold the credits required to be pursued and obtained annually, he shall be granted another opportunity within an additional one-year period, and in the event of non-compliance and failure to submit a legal excuse, the Order shall notify the Ministry of Health to suspend his licence to practise the profession until he attends the required courses.

20 - Approving the organisation and monitoring of scientific courses and educational training held by physical therapists, as well as refusing to recognise them or include them in the credit system for continuing training in the event that the Council of the Order does not approve their conduct. Anyone wishing to conduct such courses must submit an application to the Order accompanied by documents showing the identity, capacity, and academic qualifications of the lecturer, together with the substance, content, duration, and venue of the course, so that the application may be presented to the Council of the Order, after consulting the Scientific Committee, to take the appropriate decision within a period of fifteen days from the date of submission of the application.

21 - The Order shall work to sign annual cooperation protocols with guarantor companies and bodies, with the aim of unifying dealings between them and physical therapy centres to prevent speculation and monopoly, as well as the necessity of separating the physical therapist's fees from the total value of invoices, in order to collect them directly from them in accordance with the contracts signed between the physical therapist and the health and hospital institutions."

The following two committees shall be added to the committees provided for in Article 31 of Law No. 305 dated 3/4/2001:

"1 - The Physiotherapy Centres Affairs Committee.

2 - The Professional Investigations Committee."

A new article following Article 35 under number 35 bis 1 shall be added to Law No. 305 dated 3/4/2001, the text of which is as follows:

"Article 35 bis 1: The Physiotherapy Centres Affairs Committee

This Committee shall be chaired by one of the members of the Council of the Order, who shall be called the Head of Physiotherapy Centres Affairs, and it shall be vested with the following functions and powers:

a - Conducting a comprehensive and continuous survey of physiotherapy centres on Lebanese territory, to present it to the Council of the Order.

b - Inspecting physiotherapy centres intended to be opened and verifying their compliance with the required conditions and standards, as well as conducting periodic inspections to issue a certificate of accreditation of centres valid for a period of three years.

c - Pursuant to an assignment by the Council of the Order, the Committee shall, in cooperation with the Ministry of Public Health, inspect, where necessary, the licences for opening and operating physiotherapy centres and provide the Ministry with every violation or act contrary to the rules and laws of the profession in order to take the necessary legal action.

d - Cooperating with the Ministry of Public Health to conduct a census and enumeration of physiotherapy centres on Lebanese territory and update the information data relating thereto.

In the event that the position of the Chairman of the Committee becomes vacant, the Council of the Order shall meet immediately to appoint a successor to him."

A new article shall be added to Law No. 305 dated 3/4/2001 following Article 35 bis 1 under number 35 bis 2, reading as follows:

"Article 35 bis 2: The Professional Investigations Committee

The Professional Investigations Committee shall be composed of a Chairman and four members elected annually by the Council of the Order from among its members

for a full renewable year, and the members may be chosen from outside the Council of the Order.

The Committee shall examine matters and disputes arising between physiotherapists, or between them and their patients, referred to it by the President of the Order or by the Council following complaints relating to professional errors pertaining to the physiotherapist's practice of Direct Access, and it shall conduct the necessary investigations where required and submit its report to the Council of the Order. It may seek the assistance, when needed and by way of expertise, of physiotherapists, physicians, university professors, and the legal counsel of the Order.

A physiotherapist may not be prosecuted disciplinarily or remanded in custody for an offence arising from the practice of the profession prior to the closure of the Committee's report and the issuance of the decision of the Council of the Order. The Committee and the Council shall close the report and issue the decision thereon within a period not exceeding one month from the date of referral to the Committee; otherwise, disciplinary prosecution and remand in custody may be carried out independently thereof.

In the event of a vacancy in the position of Chairman of the Committee or of one of the members, the Council of the Order shall meet immediately to elect a successor to them."

The text of Article 37 of Law No. 305 dated 3/4/2001 has been amended to read as follows:

"Article 37: All physical therapists affiliated with the Order, whether Lebanese or non-Lebanese, if they breach the duties of their profession during or outside the practice thereof, expose their dignity and the dignity of the profession to anything that prejudices their honour, integrity or competence, and fail to observe the requirements of professional ethics, public order, public morals and ethical conduct, shall be subject to the following disciplinary penalties:

a - Caution.

b - Reprimand.

c - Temporary prohibition from practising the profession for a period not exceeding three years, and temporary striking off the rolls of the Order throughout the period of prohibition.

d - Permanent prohibition from practising the profession and striking off the rolls of the Order.

A physical therapist who is sentenced to temporary prohibition shall be prohibited from practising the profession throughout the period to which he is sentenced, and shall be temporarily struck off the roll, and all his duties towards the Order and his rights shall be suspended, including benefiting from retirement years, voting, running for office, and all other relevant periods for assuming functions and positions in the Order. These duties and rights shall resume upon the expiry of the period of prohibition and his re-registration after paying the affiliation fee anew.

The Council of the Order shall notify the relevant authorities of the decision of temporary or permanent prohibition from practising the profession, and of the decision of striking off consequent to this prohibition, and in particular the Ministry of Public Health to take the necessary legal action and to notify the National Social Security Fund to take the appropriate measures."
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The text of Article 38 of Law No. 305 dated 3/4/2001 has been amended to read as follows:

"Article 38: The Disciplinary Council shall be composed of the President of the Order or his Vice-President as Chairman, or whomever the President of the Order delegates as Chairman from among the members of the Disciplinary Council, of two members of the Council of the Order chosen by it by consensus or otherwise by election in the event of lack of consensus, and of two members from outside the Council elected by the General Assembly for a full term of one renewable year.

Anyone who nominates himself for membership of the Disciplinary Council from outside the Council of the Order must have practised the profession for a period of no less than ten years at least on Lebanese territory.

In the event of a vacancy in the seat or two seats of one of the members of the Disciplinary Council (from the two members delegated by the Council of the Order) for any reason whatsoever, it shall rest with the Council of the Order to choose the alternate member to fill the vacant seat to complete the term of the vacant seat.

However, if the vacant seat is that of the member elected by the General Assembly, the seat shall be filled by the candidate who obtained the highest number of votes. Where this is not possible, an election shall be held to complete the remaining period of the seat."

A new article shall be added to Law No. 8/78 issued on 20 February 1978 (Regulating the Profession of Physical Therapy) after Article No. 6, under the number 6 bis 1, the text of which is as follows:

"Article 6 bis 1:

1 - A physical therapist holding a Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT) degree shall have the right to perform assessment, examine areas of dysfunction, and initiate necessary treatment works in accordance with the principle of "direct intervention" "direct Access", outside hospitals and for outpatients only, and without prescribing medications.

2 - Prior to initiating treatment works, it shall be mandatory to conduct a comprehensive medical assessment of the patient in accordance with protocols determined by the Order in cooperation with the two Orders of Physicians and with the Ministry of Public Health, to comply with the items of the Checklist established by the Order prior to initiating treatment, and to verify the absence of any warning signs that require referral to a specialist physician.

3 - A physical therapist holding a Doctor of Physical Therapy degree shall bear direct responsibility for any therapeutic act under the direct intervention mechanism.

4 - Physical therapy sessions within the framework of the practice of Direct Access shall be covered directly by official and private insuring bodies within the approved coverage conditions.

5 - A physical therapist who practises "direct Access" shall be required to hold a professional liability insurance policy "Malpractice insurance".

B. The Protective Emblem: It is the Red Cross emblem used as a means of protection in armed

conflicts, which is:

The visible sign of protection in the largest possible size to facilitate its sighting and clear distinction, as provided for in the four Geneva Conventions, for the protection of medical and operational personnel, medical units and means of transport.

C. The Indicative Emblem: It is the emblem adopted in the country with text to refer to the National Society, used as a mark (Logo) to indicate that the persons, vehicles, buildings and other items used belong to the Lebanese Red Cross Society, and its size is small.

The indicative emblem, i.e., the mark (Logo), is the design adopted by the Society for use on everything connected with the Society to indicate a relationship therewith. It is the Red Cross emblem on a white background surrounded by a red circle in which two phrases are written in a circular manner in white, one in Arabic: "الصليب الأحمر اللبناني" and the second in French: "Croix-Rouge Libanaise", the drawing of which is attached hereto (Annex No. 2).

D - The Official Uniform: It is the uniform in its various forms and colours adopted by the Lebanese Red Cross Society, which includes the use of the protective and/or indicative emblems and/or the mark of the Society, to be worn by the members, volunteers and employees working in the Lebanese Red Cross Society.

E - The Emblems: It is the expression used in this Law as an abbreviation for all the emblems defined above (the Red Cross Emblem, the Protective Emblem, the Indicative Emblem and the mark of the Society).

Scope of Protection

This Law protects, in accordance with its provisions, in times of peace and war, the Emblems, the designation of the Lebanese Red Cross, and the Official Uniform.

The Lebanese Red Cross Society alone shall have the right to use the Indicative Emblem and the designation on all its buildings, centres, vehicles, equipment, crews and uniform.

Registration of Emblems

A - It is prohibited for legal persons and associations to register or use the emblems protected under this Law. It is also prohibited to register trade names, trademarks, industrial designs and models, and patents that use any of the emblems provided for in this Law or their designation, or any emblem name similar to any of them, or a logo similar to the logo of the Lebanese Red Cross Society, or any emblem that may create confusion with these emblems. The competent authorities shall prosecute violators and apply the measures and provisions provided for in this Law against them.

B - In the event that there are associations, bodies, or organizations using the emblem of the Red Cross or the emblem of any of the emblems of the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, or any designation, logo, or emblem specific to it prior to the date of issuance of this Law, the competent judicial and administrative authorities shall prosecute these associations or bodies and compel them to cease such use immediately and any other violation, and to change the adopted name or the used emblem under penalty of their dissolution, and apply all other resulting legal penalties and sanctions.

Use by the Medical Service of the Armed Forces

A. The medical services affiliated with all the armed forces in the Lebanese State are authorized to use the emblem of the Red Cross in times of peace and in armed conflicts alike; it shall be used by the personnel of the Lebanese Army in the Military Medical Service, in order to identify its medical personnel and the medical units and means of transport affiliated with it on land, at sea, and in the air.

B. Medical personnel are authorized to wear the uniform adopted by the security and military commands in the Lebanese Armed Forces as approved by their services by placing

the emblem of the Red Cross around the arm and carrying identity cards displaying the emblem, without resemblance to the uniform adopted by the National Society and the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement.

C. Religious personnel attached to the armed forces are entitled to use the protective emblem.

Prohibition of Using the Emblem for Private or Professional Purposes

A. Physicians, pharmacists, and any individual or body whatsoever are prohibited from bearing the emblems or anything suggestive of them, or using them on their clinics, pharmacies, vehicles, and other property belonging to them.

B. Anyone whatsoever is prohibited from using the emblems or anything suggestive of them, whether on private vehicles or otherwise.

Use by the Lebanese Red Cross Society and Partner National Societies

A - The Lebanese Red Cross Society shall have the right to use the emblems, in accordance with the requirements of the Geneva Conventions and the Protocols additional thereto, as follows:

1. As a protective device: for medical personnel, paramedics, units, means of transport, buildings, centres and ambulances belonging to the Lebanese Red Cross Society in times of armed conflict or disasters.

2. As an indicative device (indicative use): exclusively in order to show that buildings, individuals, vehicles and equipment belong to the Lebanese Red Cross Society. The dimensions of the emblem used as an indicative device shall be of a smaller size than the protective emblem with text, so as to avoid any confusion with the emblem used as a protective device.

B - Partner foreign National Societies belonging to the International Red Cross or Red Crescent Movement operating temporarily in Lebanon shall be permitted to use one of the two emblems (protective or indicative) within the conditions stipulated in Paragraph (A) and in accordance with the regulations in force. Such use shall be conditional upon obtaining prior written approval from the

Lebanese Red Cross Society.

Use of the Emblem by the Components of the International Movement

A. The components of the International Movement, namely the International Committee of the Red Cross and the International Federation, shall have the right to use and display the protective emblem for protective purposes at all times and for all their activities, in accordance with the First Geneva Convention.

B. The components of the International Movement, in particular the International Committee of the Red Cross and the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies and their duly accredited staff, shall also have the right to use, in cases of emergency and exceptional circumstances and to facilitate their work, another distinctive emblem recognised in the treaties of International Humanitarian Law to which the Lebanese State is a party (such as the Red Crescent).

Supervision Procedures

A. The Lebanese authorities shall, at all times, ensure the proper implementation of this Law, its provisions, and the rules governing the use of the emblems by accredited associations operating in Lebanese territory in coordination with the Lebanese Red Cross Society; this also includes the designations "Red Cross" and "Red Crescent" and other signs and designations protected under the treaties of international humanitarian law to which the Lebanese Republic is a party.

The Lebanese authorities shall also prosecute persons not authorised to use the emblems and designations, and shall exercise strict supervision over persons authorised to use such emblems and designations, to ensure their compliance with the provisions of this Law.

B. The competent authorities shall take all measures to disseminate and publish the rules provided for in this Law

widely among the armed forces, the police, and the civilian population;

C. The competent authorities shall take the appropriate measures to prevent any misuse, in particular by issuing instructions to civil and military authorities on how to use the distinctive emblems in accordance with the provisions of this Law, and in accordance with the Geneva Conventions and their Additional Protocols I and II.

Ensuring Respect for the Emblems and the Name

The Lebanese authorities are entrusted with the proper implementation of this Law, in particular ensuring respect for the emblems and the name of the Lebanese Red Cross Society. The judiciary shall act ex officio or upon a report regarding cases of misuse of the emblems and the name of the Society.

Penalties Resulting from Misuse of the Protective Emblem

A. Any person who intentionally commits or orders the commission of acts leading to the infliction of serious bodily or health injury through the misuse of the emblems shall be punished by temporary hard labour for a term of not less than seven years.

The penalty shall be increased to hard labour for a term of not less than ten years, if the act committed leads to death.

B. Whoever intentionally and without right uses any of the emblems and designations likely to cause confusion, whatever the purpose of such use, shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to three years or by a fine ranging between thirty and fifty times the value of the minimum wage, or by both penalties together.

C. If any of the offences specified above is committed by a legal person (such as: a declared or undeclared association, a syndicate, a commercial company, an organization, etc.) the penalty mentioned above shall be imposed on the legal representatives of these entities, and they shall be dissolved and their property confiscated.

Urgent Judicial Measures

The Judge of Urgent Matters shall have jurisdiction to take the appropriate urgent measures to prevent the occurrence of any violation or to stop any violation by means of orders on petition. He may also take all necessary urgent measures, including by way of example and not limitation: seizing the tools, equipment, documents, etc.. and materials marked with the emblems contrary to the provisions of this Law, and removing and destroying them at the expense of the perpetrator of the violation.

If any violation of the provisions of this Law is committed by any person under public law (including municipalities and their unions, public institutions, and their employees and civil servants), jurisdiction shall remain with the summary judiciary (civil or administrative) to take the necessary measures, being among the cases of trespass.

Standing and Interest

The Lebanese Red Cross Society and any of the components of the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement shall have the standing and interest to bring an action, file a complaint, or assume the capacity of a personal claimant (including claiming compensation) before all competent civil, criminal, and administrative authorities and courts.

Repeal of Contrary Texts

All legislative and regulatory texts and provisions contrary to this Law or inconsistent with its content are hereby repealed.

Entry into Force

This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Penalties Resulting from the Misuse of the Indicative Emblem

A. Shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to three years

or by a fine ranging between thirty to fifty times the value of the minimum wage, or by both penalties together, any natural or legal person who commits the following acts:

1) Whoever intentionally uses or exploits, in violation of the controls and conditions set forth in this Law, and without right, the emblems or designations imitating them or which may cause confusion, whatever the purpose of such use;

2) Whoever uses the emblems or designations on signs, posters, advertisements, publications, or commercial or non-commercial documents, or places them on goods or packaging, or sells, offers for sale, or markets goods stamped therewith;

B. If the offence is committed by a legal person (commercial company, organisation, etc.), the penalty shall apply to its legal representative, with the possibility of imposing an additional penalty ordering the dissolution of the legal person or prohibiting it from practising its activity for a period of not less than five years.

C. Shall be punished by imprisonment from one year to three years, and by a fine ranging between thirty to fifty times the value of the official minimum wage, whoever exploits any of the emblems, the name, or the uniform specific to the Society for all its activities, to create confusion among the public or for any cause not specified and approved in advance by the Lebanese Red Cross Society, with the aim of collecting donations or gifts or achieving financial gains and deceiving the donor into believing that they accrue to the benefit of the Lebanese Red Cross Society.

D. Any public official or person entrusted with performing a public service, who uses any of the emblems or the name and prevents the persons legally authorised from using them, or exploits his authority to impose unlawful restrictions on such use, shall be punished by the penalties provided for in this Law.

E. The penalties mentioned above shall be doubled in the event that they are committed in times of war, disasters, and crises.

Taking Provisional Measures

The competent authorities, administrative and judicial, shall take

the appropriate measures to stop the damage resulting from the violation of this Law and prevent its continuation, including the confiscation of materials involving the use of any of the emblems at the expense of the violator. They may also close the violating entities, temporarily or permanently, if their involvement in the violation of this Law is proven.
The death penalty is abolished wherever provided for in Lebanese laws.

Article /37/ of the Criminal Code (Legislative Decree No. 340 dated 1/3/1943 and its amendments) is amended to read as follows:

Article 37:

The ordinary felony penalties are:

Aggravated hard labour for life.

Hard labour for life

Detention for life.

Temporary hard labour.

Temporary detention.

The death penalty is replaced by the penalty of aggravated hard labour for life in respect of offences committed after the entry into force of this Law.

As for offences committed prior to the entry into force of this Law, the death penalty therein is replaced by the penalty immediately following it, which is the penalty of hard labour for life.

All procedures of investigation, prosecution, trial, all other rules of procedure, and the execution of penalties shall apply to offences that were punishable by the death penalty and replaced by aggravated hard labour for life.
Article 43 of the Criminal Code and Articles 420 inclusive to 424 inclusive of Law No. 328 dated 2/8/2001 (Code of Criminal Procedure) are repealed.

a - The abolition of the death penalty covers all judicial decisions previously rendered against persons sentenced thereto prior to the date of issuance of this Law whose death sentences have not been executed, and their penalty is replaced by the penalty of hard labour for life.

b - Persons sentenced to the death penalty whose penalty is replaced by the penalty of aggravated hard labour for life shall only benefit from the reduction provided for in the Execution of Penalties Law No. 463 dated 17/9/2002.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

The following expressions, wherever they appear in this Law, shall have the meanings set forth below:

Media: All works related to the publication and distribution of media materials, including monitoring, verifying, editing, and modifying them, and producing them if the media institution adopts that.

Media Outlets: The various technical types that allow the publication and distribution of media materials through print, radio, television, or the various electronic means regulated by this Law, and which are offered to the public or to specific categories thereof.

Media Materials: The media content that is produced, published, and distributed to the public through the various media outlets.

Media Institutions: Institutions that manage one of the regulated media outlets.

Owners of Media Institutions: Natural or legal persons holding the economic right to own media institutions.

The Minister: The Minister of Information.

The Authority: The National Media Authority established and regulated pursuant to the provisions of this Law.

Media Professional: A person who practices a media activity principally and regularly in return for a wage or remuneration, or for his own account, in one or more media institutions, and derives the greater part of his income from this work.

Responsible Director: The editorial director, programming director, or any media professional who legally and de facto assumes responsibility for supervising media materials in any of the media outlets provided for in this Law.

The Principle of Freedom

Freedom of opinion, expression, and media in its various forms and means is guaranteed in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution, and this freedom shall only be restricted by what is provided for in the relevant general laws in force and the provisions of this Law.

Various General Principles and Policies

The regulation of the media aims to achieve, protect, and promote the following objectives and policies:

1 - The provisions of the Constitution, human rights, democracy, and the rule of law.

2 - Freedom of expression and the promotion thereof in accordance with the Constitution and international conventions.

3 - Encouraging the Lebanese media and the pluralism thereof across the various

general and specialised fields.

4 - Supporting the qualitative production of Lebanese media outlets in order to enable them to compete in global markets.

5 - The right of society to science, knowledge, and access to reliable information.

6 - Pluralism and diversity in media outlets and in programmes in a manner that serves the public interest, including the promotion of programmes that are less profitable than others, particularly in the fields of health, culture, history, education, development, and children's programmes.

7 - Preventing monopolies in the ownership of media outlets and promoting free and fair competition in a manner commensurate with the size and needs of the market, particularly in the establishment of media outlets subject to licensing.

8 - Accuracy and balance in programmes.

9 - Clear separation between advertising, media, and other types of programmes.

10 - Encouraging the geographical and regional distribution of media outlets.

11 - Developing and promoting media content that reflects national culture and identity.

12 - Innovation and the use of technology in media production.

13 - Financial and competitive sustainability of media outlets.

Any natural or legal person residing in Lebanon, carrying out its activity therein, duly registered in accordance with its own constitutive regime, and fulfilling the additional conditions specified in this Law, such as companies of all kinds, associations, political parties, syndicates, municipalities, and religious and educational institutions, shall have the right to own any of the media outlets

provided for in this Law, provided that it carries out its media activity in accordance with the obligations provided for therein.

No person holding the nationality of an enemy State shall have the right to wholly or partially own, publish, operate, or finance, directly or indirectly, any media outlet whatsoever within the Lebanese territory.

A - Media outlets and their owners shall be prohibited from obtaining any benefit by unlawful means or performing any act deemed to constitute a conflict of interest.

B - Media institutions and their owners shall be strictly prohibited, whether directly or indirectly, from obtaining a concession right or public contracts or concluding any contracts with the State or with public institutions, municipalities and their unions, and with any body, sector or any entity dealing in public funds wholly or partially.

Audiovisual media companies shall be established in the form of a Lebanese joint-stock company, and they shall not have the right to own more than one television institution and one radio institution together as specified in this Law.

All shares of the company shall be registered shares, and the following conditions shall apply to the shareholders therein:

- A natural person must enjoy legal capacity and not have been convicted of a felony or an infamous misdemeanour or deprived of civil rights.
