- A legal person must be a Lebanese company.

- No single natural or legal person shall have the right to own, directly or indirectly, shares or stakes

in more than one media institution of the same category, and the husband or wife and their ascendants, descendants, their spouses and their in-laws shall be considered as a single person.

- Citizens of foreign nationalities may own registered shares in Lebanese joint-stock companies that own audiovisual media institutions of various categories, with the exception of media outlets that broadcast political programmes, in which the total ownership of foreign natural persons and legal persons the majority of whose shareholders are foreigners may not exceed a proportion of 20% of the capital.

- The Authority shall monitor the compliance of companies owning television and radio media institutions with the provisions of this Article, and shall require the companies concerned to provide the Authority with the official documents it requests regarding their capital and shareholders in order to take the necessary legal action in the event of a violation pursuant to the provisions of this Law, including the revocation of the relevant licences or notice and acknowledgement.

Owners of foreign media outlets shall carry out their media activity in Lebanon in accordance with the legal form they choose (for example, a branch, a subsidiary company, a commercial representative office, an accredited correspondent) and within the conditions of incorporation and registration specified in the relevant laws, provided that they comply in addition thereto with the following:

1 - To submit to the Authority notices of acknowledgment or licence applications relating to the media activity intended to be carried out in Lebanon, if such activity includes broadcasting, publishing and distribution therein, in accordance with the conditions and provisions stipulated in this Law, with the exception of production activity which is not subject to the provisions of this Law.

2 - To submit to the Authority a special notification in cases relating to local production and coverage activities (without broadcasting, publishing and distribution) in accordance with the following provisions specific to media representative offices.

3 - Owners of foreign media outlets operating in Lebanon shall be subject to all transparency and notification obligations stipulated in Title Three of this Law.

The media representative office shall operate under the name of the original media outlet with the addition of the phrase "Media Representative Office in Lebanon", and shall acquire legal personality in Lebanon upon the issuance of the acknowledgment decision by the Authority, without the need for any other formality or registration with any administration, including the Commercial Register.

The company owning the foreign media outlet must be registered abroad in accordance with the laws of its country, and the regulations of the media representative office with respect to the conduct and management of its activities shall be consistent with the provisions of this Law and all other relevant Lebanese laws.
Workers in the media representative office shall be subject to the Lebanese labour and social security laws and to the Lebanese tax laws.
The Authority shall lay down the details and particulars for the implementation of this Article by regulatory decisions issued by its Administrative Board.

Any violation of the provisions of this Chapter shall subject its perpetrator to a fine ranging between twenty times and one hundred times the official minimum wage, and the penalty shall be doubled in the event of recidivism.

A special register shall be established at the Authority for each type of media outlet regulated under this Law, divided into

two sections, in which shall be recorded the entries specified in Articles 16 and 17 below that serve to enhance transparency in media work with respect to the ownership and operation of media outlets, revenues and sources of funding.

The Authority shall provide access to all information recorded in the registers by publishing it mandatorily in full on a website managed by the Authority, making it available in paper form to any person who requests to inspect it, and issuing certificates in respect thereof without delay, which shall be exempt from fees. The provisions of the Law on the Right of Access to Information shall apply thereto.

a - The first section of the special register for each type of media outlet regulated under this Law shall contain the particulars relating to the owner or independent manager of the media outlet, as follows:

- The name of the owner or owners, their nationalities and their addresses.

- The legal form and place of registration.

- The addresses at which the owner of the media outlet and each of its affiliated media institutions are served with official transactions and correspondence, in particular the right of reply.

- The person or persons responsible for management, such as the names of the administrative body and its president and the names of the manager or managers.

- The capital, where it exists, and a list of the names of the partners who own more than 5% of the shares or stakes of the company, the percentage of their participation, and the names of the beneficial owners in respect of such ownerships.

b - The owner or manager of the media outlet shall notify the Authority, by any means determined by the Authority, of the basic information included in the first section of the special register provided for in this Chapter within one month of the establishment of the media institution or the transfer of its independent management, and shall likewise notify the Authority of every amendment occurring to the data mentioned above within one week of its occurrence.

a - The second section of the special register mentioned above shall contain the particulars relating to the revenues of the media outlets and their sources, as follows:

- The separate and consolidated financial statements and the property rights of the owners and managers connected with the media outlet's exercise of its activity,

- All detailed revenues connected with the activities of the media outlets, including those resulting from the exercise of media work itself such as advertisements, subscriptions, sales, and any loans and donations in kind and in cash, with the specification of the sources of such loans.

b - The proprietor or manager of the media outlet shall submit to the Authority, by any means it determines, in the first month of each financial year, the data provided for in paragraph (a) of this Article. He shall also notify the Authority of all revenues set forth in paragraph (a) of this Article within one week of their receipt during the period of election campaigns.

The Authority may verify the accuracy of the information contained in the declarations of media outlet owners in accordance with the provisions of the Articles above by all available means of verification, including commissioning auditors, in order to ascertain its accuracy and its non-violation of the provisions of this Law.

The competent courts shall punish the media institution or its owners for every violation of the provisions of Chapter One of Title Three relating to the obligation of declaration ranging from twenty times to one hundred times the official minimum wage, in addition to compelling the owners of the media outlets to fulfil their obligations accurately within a time limit not exceeding one month from the issuance of the judicial decision. In the event of recurrence or delay in execution, the

fine shall be doubled successively until full compliance with the obligations takes place.

Without prejudice to the special legal provisions relating to the criminalisation of the acts provided for in Article 5 above, the competent courts shall punish the media outlet or its owners for every violation of its provisions with a fine ranging from fifty times to one hundred times the official minimum wage, in addition to the immediate permanent closure of the offending media outlet and taking the decision to dissolve the institutions owning it.

The competent courts shall punish the media outlet or its owners for every violation of Article 6 above, in addition to the penalties provided for in the relevant offences, as follows:

a - With a fine ranging between fifty times and one hundred times the official minimum wage, in addition to the confiscation of the gain or benefit obtained in violation of the provisions of the Law.

b - In the event of recurrence within a period of one year, the court may double the penalty and issue a decision suspending the media outlet for a period ranging between one month and six months, or impose either of these two penalties.

c - The court may order permanent closure in the event of recurrence of the offence mentioned above for the third time within the same year from the date of commission of the first act.
Prosecution shall lapse if the media outlet fulfils the obligations incumbent upon it within a period of one week after the formal notice provided for in Article 98 of this Law.

The following terms shall mean as follows:

A - Publication: the means of publishing of all periodic and non-periodic kinds, based on the recording of words and shapes by letters, pictures and drawings, including, by way of example, newspapers, magazines, news press agencies, books and leaflets.

B - Periodic publication: the various kinds of publications that are issued continuously under a specific name and in successive parts and are prepared for distribution to the public, with the exception of periodic and non-periodic publications that are distributed within institutions, and the special supplements issued thereby shall be considered part of their periodic issues.

Any natural or legal person from among the persons specified in Article 4 above shall have the right to issue a periodic publication without prior licence and without depositing any guarantee or financial security and shall be subject to the obligation to deposit a statement of notification with the Authority in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

A - The "Statement of Notification" shall be submitted in writing to the Authority by any means proving the Authority's receipt thereof, signed by the responsible director, who shall immediately be given a written receipt therefor called the acknowledgment of receipt.

B - The "Statement of Notification" must contain the following information and supporting documents:

1 - The name of the owner of the publication, its legal form, its address in Lebanon and all the legal documents relating thereto.

2 - The name of the publication.

3 - The name of the person who undertakes the printing and his address.

4 - The language or languages in which it is issued.

5 - The name of the responsible director, his place of residence and his address.

C - The periodic publication shall be considered duly established as from the date of depositing with the Authority the "Statement of Notification" completed with all the information and documents specified in Paragraph (B)

above, and in the event that the Authority delays delivering the acknowledgment of receipt for any reason whatsoever, this shall not prevent the establishment process, and the date of depositing the "Statement of Notification" shall then be relied upon for the commencement of the validity of all rights and duties relating to the establishment of media outlets and the application of this Law in all its effects, including the commencement of media work in a normal manner.

D - The Authority shall notify the Press Syndicate of the statements of notification and the acknowledgments of receipt within a period of one week from its receipt and issuance thereof, to take note and express any observation of an advisory nature relating to literary and intellectual property.

A - Every periodical publication shall have a responsible director who fulfils the following conditions:

- To be a Lebanese media professional enjoying his civil and political rights, and not convicted of a felony or an infamous misdemeanour.

- To hold a university degree with no less than three years of experience in the field of media work.

- To be actually residing in Lebanon and working full-time for the periodical publication.

- Not to be a responsible director for more than one periodical publication.

- Not to be among the persons enjoying judicial immunity in accordance with the law.

B - The above-mentioned director shall remain civilly and criminally liable for publication acts until the Authority is notified in writing of his dismissal or resignation therefrom.

C - The owner of the publication shall have the right to be its responsible director whenever the above-mentioned conditions are fulfilled in him.
The owner of a periodical publication shall not have the right to use a name that enjoys legal protection for a publication in accordance with the provisions of the laws in force governing it.

Every issue of the periodical publication shall bear on

its cover or its first or last page, the name of the responsible director and the address where official transactions and correspondence are served, telephone, fax and electronic mail numbers, the registration number in the special register with the Authority, the name of its owner, its legal form and its address, its subscription fee, the price of a single copy thereof, and the date of issue.

Whoever violates the provisions of this Article shall be fined a fine of up to fifty times the official minimum wage.
The owner of the periodical publication shall submit to the Authority a statement of every replacement or amendment in the content of the notice of information within one week of its occurrence.

A - In the event of the cessation of the legal person owning the periodical publication by the fulfilment of one of the conditions of dissolution provided for in the law, or in the event of the death of the natural person owning the publication, the responsible director shall notify the Authority immediately and refrain from issuing the publication until the settlement of its legal status with respect to the legal person or the actual acceptance by one of the heirs of the natural person of the issuance of the periodical publication under his responsibility and declaring that to the Authority.

B - If the publication continues to be issued in violation of the provisions of paragraph (A) above, the person responsible for issuing it shall be criminally and civilly liable with his personal assets for any damage befalling third parties as a result of publication.

Non-periodical publications, in accordance with the provisions of this Law, mean the various types of books, works, studies, research papers, leaflets, articles and the like which are not published in periodical publications, and which are distributed to the public for a price or free of charge, whatever their subject matter or the methods, means and language used therein, and which are not issued periodically under a specific name and with sequential numbers and dates.

Non-periodical publications must include the name of the author, the publisher, the name of the printing press and the date of printing.

The addresses of the persons mentioned above and how to contact them shall be clearly specified in the non-periodical publication.

a - Anyone who wishes to issue a non-periodical publication must notify the Authority with a copy of the publication.

b- Notification of the Authority shall take place either directly or by any other means proving receipt prior to distribution and publication.

The following shall be exempted from the obligation of notification mentioned above:

- Books, works, studies and research papers.

- Postcards, announcement and invitation cards to attend public and private celebrations and occasions, official notices, leaflets, commercial advertisements and other similar papers.

The Authority shall keep a special register in which notification notices and acknowledgements of receipt are recorded, and shall retain a copy of the publication in the event of an inquiry by a judicial authority or by any party having an interest, and it shall rest with the Authority to destroy those documents after the lapse of three months from the date of notification.
The owners and directors of a periodical or non-periodical publication must deposit two copies of each issue or edition with the National Library and the National Archives Institution.

Subject to Article 29 of this Law, any violation of the provisions of this Chapter above shall be punishable for its perpetrator by a fine ranging between twenty times and one hundred times the official minimum wage.

The following expressions shall have the meanings set out below:

- Broadcasting service: the television or radio broadcasting service and/or the video on demand service.

- Television: the service that relies principally on simultaneous audio and visual broadcasting, which is provided to the public by any means of broadcasting, whether electromagnetic, electronic, or by any other means, capable of simultaneous reception of the broadcast at the time designated therefor, and composed of a defined programme schedule selected by the service provider such that news material or any current daily developments or current affairs are subject to editorial supervision.

- Radio: the service that relies principally on audio broadcasting, and is provided to the public by any means of broadcasting, whether electromagnetic, electronic or otherwise, capable of simultaneous reception of the broadcast at the time designated therefor, and composed of a defined programme schedule selected by the service provider such that news material and current daily developments or current affairs are subject to editorial supervision.

- Video and audio recording on demand: the provision of an audio and/or visual service to the public pursuant to an organised catalogue of programmes selected by the service provider which is left to the user to receive individually.

- Coded broadcasting: the television or radio broadcasting service that uses special coding or encryption technologies, which do not allow the public to access the media content except through the use of special technologies, whether for consideration or free of charge.

- Interactive broadcasting: the television or radio broadcasting service that allows the user to interact directly with the service in order to benefit from additional services such as voting and direct expression of opinion or defining and selecting the types of services.

- Pay broadcasting: the television and radio broadcasting service that cannot be accessed except for consideration.

- Networks:

Broadcasting network: the wired or wireless telecommunications network that transmits data, information, and visual and audio material directly to the public using electromagnetic waves, satellites, optical fibers, or any other technology. The equipment used by broadcasting stations shall be deemed telecommunications equipment.

Distribution network: any wired or wireless telecommunications network used to broadcast, distribute and publish data and visual and audio material directed to the public through the use of frequencies, electromagnetic waves, optical or electrical signals, satellites, optical fibers, or any other technology. The equipment used by distribution networks shall be deemed telecommunications equipment.

Link network: the wired or wireless telecommunications network used to transmit information and data between transmission centres, or transmission centres and studios, or between studios, using frequencies, electromagnetic waves, optical or electrical signals, satellites, optical fibers, or any other technology. The equipment used in interconnection networks shall be deemed telecommunications equipment.

- Channel: the series of frequencies used by a television broadcasting service for broadcasting over airwaves.

- Wave: the series of frequencies used by a radio broadcasting service for broadcasting over airwaves.

- Station: the trade name adopted to identify a television or radio service.

- Book of specifications: the regulatory document adopted by the Authority to determine the detailed technical, administrative and programming conditions and the specific specifications relating to television and radio media outlets.

- Programme: the visual or audio media material

that represents one of the elements of media work.

- Political programmes: the programmes that address public affairs issues linked to public policies and the performance of the constitutional, administrative and judicial authorities of the State and its agencies, and holders of public office or those bound by an interest therein or who engage in public affairs among politicians, parties and various political and social organisations, including news programmes and various talk and analytical programmes.

- Programme grid: the schedule or grid that defines the media material published by the television or radio.

Television and radio institutions shall be classified with respect to the regime of their establishment and the books of conditions applicable thereto as follows:

Type One: Institutions that rely on broadcasting and publication through internet media, satellites, and other unlimited technologies, whether owned and managed by the State or the private sector; they shall be established in accordance with the procedures of notice and acknowledgment issued by the Authority pursuant to the provisions of this Law.

Type Two: Institutions that rely on the terrestrial frequency television and radio broadcasting network of channels and waves owned by the Lebanese State, the distribution of which it controls in accordance with the licensing procedures under a prior permit regime issued by the Authority pursuant to the provisions of this Law.

This latter category and the legal articles related thereto shall be abolished upon the compliance of Lebanon and the television and radio media institutions with the obligations incumbent upon them pursuant to the provisions of the Regional Agreement for the European Broadcasting Area (Stockholm 1961), as revised during the Regional Radiocommunication Conference (Geneva 2006), to which Lebanon acceded in 2007 and which sets time limits for States for the transition of all media outlets to digital broadcasting instead of analogue broadcasting by around the year 2015.

Television and radio broadcasting institutions may not operate

in Lebanese territory without a licence or a notice and acknowledgment pursuant to the provisions of this Law.

a - Every television or radio media outlet must have a responsible director who fulfills the following conditions:

- To be a Lebanese media professional enjoying his civil and political rights, and not convicted of a felony or an infamous misdemeanour.

- To hold a university degree and have experience of not less than three years in the field of media work.

- To be an actual resident in Lebanon and working full-time for the media outlet.

- Not to be a responsible director for more than one media outlet.

- Not to be among the persons enjoying judicial immunity in accordance with the law.

b - The director mentioned above shall remain civilly and criminally liable for publication acts until the Authority is notified in writing of his dismissal or resignation from his duties as a responsible director.

c - The chairman of the board of directors of the company owning the television or radio media outlet shall have the right to be its responsible director whenever he fulfills the conditions mentioned above.

The Authority shall, after consulting the concerned parties, develop a licensing plan for the most developed media markets in Lebanon in respect of television or radio institutions subject to the licensing regime pursuant to Article 39 above, including the local market.

The licensing plan aims to:

- Set the general strategy of the licensing plan for the most developed local media markets.

- Determine the number of licences that must be granted to broadcasting service providers to operate in the media market.

- Determine the maximum specified time limit to increase or decrease the number of media broadcasting service providers

during the specified time limit to reach the targeted number.

- Determine the types and content of the relied-upon programmes that must be promoted in the media market.

- Appoint the general objectives through which broadcasting service providers in the media market must be distributed to consumers.

And the Authority shall be guided by the following considerations to develop the licensing plan in the media market:

- The commercial capacity of the said market to maintain media service providers capable of producing and distributing Lebanese content of a certain quality and purchasing suitable foreign content in a manner that meets the public interest in obtaining diverse programmes of a high-level quality.

- The current number of service providers operating in this market, the extent permitted to be increased to achieve the targeted number of licences, and the status of existing broadcasting service licences.

- Whether the existing broadcasting services meet the public interest in obtaining diverse programmes of quality and to what extent.

- Knowing how much the share of the viewing or listening audience represents of the existing broadcasting services, within the limits of the availability of this information.

- The need for modification in the manner in which broadcasting services are distributed in the market, including modifications resulting from the digital switchover.

Nothing in this Article shall prevent broadcasting distribution services from providing programmes on demand or upon request, in accordance with the regulations adopted by the Authority in this regard.

The entire licensing process shall take place on a competitive basis, pursuant to a call for tenders conducted in a public, fair, transparent and non-discretionary manner, and aiming to place the media sector within the context of the applicable licensing plan regardless of whether this would increase or reduce

the number of service providers.

The Authority shall have the power to establish special rules for competition in the licensing process, provided that it takes into consideration the following factors in making the decision to grant or refuse the licence to the applicant:

- The technical capability of the applicant to deliver a quality service, taking into consideration the nature of the proposed service.

- The nature and extent of the human and financial resources available to the applicant, and the financial feasibility and viability of the offer.

- The effect of licensing the proposed service in terms of concentration of ownership, cross-ownership or joint ownership, and fair, legitimate competition.

- The proposed method for distributing the broadcasting service.

- The promotion of the widest possible diversity of programmes, taking into consideration programme schedules, the demand and need for such service, the content-related needs derived from the licensing plan and the radio broadcasting services already available in this context, and any priorities for specific content for competition in licensing already established by the Authority.

- The need to promote locally produced programmes for the purposes of meeting the needs and interests of the Lebanese people.

a - The Authority may determine the regulations in advance for any licence offer in order to establish the process that must be followed in submitting the application, concurrently with establishing a description of the information that must be provided and a published schedule of annual licence fees.

b - When licence offers are launched, the Authority must publish widely an announcement in this regard containing the information provided for in the preceding paragraph.

c - All applicants for licences must provide the following information:

1 - The form of ownership and its distribution.

2 - The sources of funding and the financial plan proposed by them.

3 - The form of the administrative and organisational structure, including the working human staff and the expertise available to deliver the service,

the schedules of the proposed programmes, their types and the target audience.

4 - The technical facilities for delivering the service, including distribution arrangements for applicants for broadcasting service licences.

The procedures for evaluating competing licence applications must include the consideration of presenting the application in a public hearing during which written comments on the application are submitted by any concerned or interested party.

The Authority shall request the publication of the licence application in the Official Gazette at least thirty (30) days prior to the date of convening the public hearing referred to above, without this including any sensitive commercial information or other information submitted by the licence applicant.

When the Authority grants a licence pursuant to this Article, it shall publish its decision in the Official Gazette.

The licence is non-transferable from one owner to another without the prior approval of the Authority.

Compliance with all the conditions for submitting the licence application, including programme schedules, is one of the conditions for granting the licence.

Broadcasting services shall be obliged to preserve the master copy of broadcast programmes and advertisements for a period of at least two months from the date of broadcasting, and in the event that any of the broadcast materials is the subject of a dispute, the broadcasting service shall be obliged, upon a request from the Authority, to retain the master recording of the said material until the dispute is finally adjudicated.

The licence shall lapse in the event that broadcasting has not commenced or the activation of the broadcast distribution service has not commenced within six months from the date of granting the licence.

In the event that the media institution fails to comply with the conditions of the licence within two weeks of being served notice, the Authority shall refer the offending institution to the competent judiciary to request that the necessary measures be taken, including the revocation of the licence.

Every radio and television broadcasting institution shall appoint a director of programmes.

In addition to that, every television and radio institution of the first category that broadcasts news and political programmes shall appoint a responsible director for news and political programmes.
Media broadcasting institutions shall display the station's logo during television broadcasting and broadcast the name of the station and the frequency used during radio broadcasting.

Television and radio institutions shall be classified as follows:

First Category: Television and radio institutions that provide a broadcasting service to the public across all Lebanese territory, and they are divided into:

First Category A: Those that broadcast media material that includes all types of programmes, including political programmes and news.

First Category B: Those that broadcast media material that is restricted solely to news and political programmes.

Second Category: Television and radio institutions that do not include political programmes, and they are divided into:

Second Category A: Television and radio institutions that provide a broadcasting service to the public across all Lebanese territory and whose media material does not include political programmes or news.

Second Category B: Television and radio institutions that provide an encrypted (coded) one-way broadcasting service and an interactive broadcasting service using radio broadcasting networks or wired or wireless distribution networks through

the available and possible technologies, and whose media material does not include political programmes or news, and whose programmes can only be viewed by subscribers technically equipped for this purpose.

Radio institutions of the First and Second Categories may, within the broadcasting capacities granted to them, allocate in their general schedule a programme directed to a specific Lebanese region focusing on its affairs, provided that the duration of this broadcast does not exceed one hundred hours per week at most in the case of television and fifty hours per week in the case of radio.

Third Category: Local and international television and radio institutions that disseminate media material via satellites whose broadcasting coverage extends beyond Lebanese territory.

Fourth Category: Regional television and radio institutions that provide a radio broadcasting service in specific geographical areas. This category includes television institutions that provide interactive or one-way closed services through a radio broadcasting or distribution network confined to a specific geographical area, for special social or scientific purposes.

Article 51;

Licences granted prior to the entry into force of this Law shall remain valid until the end of their original term. Provided that the Authority grants previously licensed institutions a period of three months from the date of their notification to comply with the new books of specifications.

The validity terms of the licences granted pursuant to this Law are fixed as follows:

- Five years for a radio broadcasting licence.

- Seven years for a television broadcasting licence.

A - The Authority may, in accordance with the provisions of this Article, specify special criteria for a tender for a specific licence for the purpose of promoting the widest possible diversity of programmes, taking into consideration any anticipated need for certain content in the licensing plan after broadcasting services are already secured in

this field, and identifying the need for certain content covered in the tender.

The criteria may indicate the need for general programme areas of importance and interest or may specify percentages for programmes in specified areas.

The list of programme areas of special importance may include, on a non-exhaustive basis, the following areas:

- Educational programmes.

- Programmes dedicated to children.

- Programmes concerned with history or social programmes.

- Programmes that pertain to and support women.

- Programmes dedicated to marginalised categories or groups.

B - The broadcasting hours of local dramatic production, whether series or separate episodes, shall not be less than sixty hours annually for the visual media outlet, and it shall also broadcast at least one play every month.

Any violation of the provisions of this paragraph shall subject its perpetrator to a fine ranging between fifty times and one hundred times the official minimum wage.

With regard to the rules on the separation of services, no broadcasting service provider may exercise its authority over a digital multiplex service.

The Authority may lay down the standards relating to this technology in special books of specifications, provided that it always implicitly takes into consideration the following criteria:

- The technical capability of the applicant to secure a service of quality, taking into consideration the nature of the service provided.

- The nature and extent of the financial and human resources available to the applicant and the viability of the submitted offer to succeed from the financial standpoint (the financial feasibility thereof).

- The plans drawn up by the applicant with respect to the services

of broadcasting that it proposes to distribute.

- The effect of granting the notice and acknowledgement with respect to achieving a balance between promoting the transmission of the largest possible number of channels via digital transmission and securing high definition services in Lebanon.

Within the framework of laying down the standards of the books of specifications for the provision of a digital multiplex service, the Authority may lay down rules for the ratio of controls and high definition services to be provided.

Pursuant to the provisions of this Law, digital multiplex service providers are required to provide access to their distribution services to broadcasting service providers in a non-discretionary manner and based on fair grounds, and in the event that any dispute arises between a digital multiplex service provider and a broadcasting service provider regarding access to the service, it shall be for the Authority to adjudicate the dispute in the most appropriate manner.

Subject to literary and artistic intellectual property rights, when broadcasting distribution service providers undertake the distribution of a specific broadcast, this shall not necessarily be in return for consideration imposed by the distribution service provider on the broadcasting service provider, and likewise the broadcasting service provider shall not necessarily bind the broadcasting distribution service provider to consideration in return for the distribution of the broadcasting service, such that the distribution service provider retains the revenue.

In cases not covered by the provisions of the preceding paragraph above, the relationship between broadcasting distribution service providers and broadcasting service providers shall be subject to the principles and rules in force in the market and determined by the Authority to prevent monopoly, provided that negotiations always take place in a fair manner and without discrimination. In the event that a dispute arises between a broadcasting distribution service provider and a broadcasting service provider, the Authority shall have the power to adjudicate the dispute in the most appropriate manner.

The Authority may lay down technical conditions for licensed persons as it sees fit, whether applicable to all service providers, to a specific class thereof, or to a particular service provider.

Without prejudice to the generality of the provisions of the preceding paragraph and without limiting them, the technical conditions may be applied to the types of equipment used by service providers in the geographical distribution of broadcast distribution.

The Authority shall lay down as it sees fit, from time to time, through publication in the Official Gazette, regulations determining the general conditions for licences applicable to all licensees in general or to different types thereof.

Included among what these conditions comprise is the following:

- The minimum number of programmes entrusted to independent local producers.

- And/or the categories of information with which licensees must provide the Authority in their annual reports.

The Authority may attach to a broadcasting licence or a broadcast distribution service licence reasonable and specific conditions as it sees fit to promote the broadcasting policy provided for in the second Article.
Every violation of the provisions of this Chapter above shall punish its perpetrator with a fine ranging between fifty times and one hundred times the official minimum wage.

Shall be considered media agencies institutions that professionally collect, process, coordinate and provide all media materials that have undergone journalistic processing under their own responsibility, provided that at least half of their turnover derives from these materials.

Media agencies that publish their news shall be subject, in terms of their establishment, their management and all other obligations imposed upon them, to the provisions applicable to periodical publications and media

websites provided for in this Law.

Definitions

- Advertisements: means any public announcement aimed at promoting the sale, purchase or lease of a product or service, and at presenting an idea or cause or at producing certain other effects desired by the advertiser for which broadcasting time has been granted in return for a fee or similar consideration.

- Advertising Régie: means an advertising company that assumes the role of advertising agent for a media company and markets and manages the advertisements of television or radio media institutions.

- Advertising Department: means the department competent to market and manage advertisements within the media institution.

A - Every media company engaged in broadcasting may establish an advertising department or sign with an advertising régie company, to secure advertisements and manage their affairs.

B - In order to prevent monopolies, shareholders in broadcasting companies and in the advertising companies

contracted therewith (régie), as well as their husbands, wives, children, parents, in-laws and successors, shall not be entitled to hold shares in more than one company, and full-time employees in an advertising régie shall also be prohibited from working in more than one advertising company. Furthermore, the régie shall be prohibited from providing its services to more than one television company from among the five categories provided for in this Law.

C - All media outlets shall completely and clearly separate media content from advertising content in a manner that guarantees media integrity, editorial independence from advertisements, the public's right to know, and the non-exploitation of public trust in media content to pass disguised commercial or political messages.

A - The Authority shall be entrusted with verifying the validity of statistical studies relating to the distribution of viewers and listeners and with approving their results prior to placing them in circulation in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

B - The Authority shall be entrusted with verifying the compliance of media institutions with the obligations of advertising transparency provided for in the preceding Article above.
Any violation of the provisions of this Title shall subject its perpetrator to a fine ranging between fifty and one hundred times the official minimum wage.

The following expressions shall have the meanings set forth below:

A - Creators of professional electronic media websites: Providers of professional electronic media services are every natural or legal person who practises as a profession the broadcasting, publishing, aggregating, or rebroadcasting or republishing of non-radio and non-television media materials and programmes that are subject to the provisions of Chapter Two, by electronic means.

B - Creators of non-professional electronic media websites: Every natural or legal person who uses electronic means to express therein his personal opinions and ideas, such as personal blogs (Blogs), and to communicate with others.

C - Electronic media websites: The electronic website and digital media applications that provide to the public regularly updated media materials related to current developments and subject to editorial oversight.

Electronic media is free and the creation of electronic media platforms and websites shall not be subject to any prior approval or licence, with due regard to the provisions of the legal articles relating to literary and intellectual property rights.

A - Providers of professional electronic media services and creators of electronic media websites on the Internet in Lebanon must clearly specify on the electronic website the following:

The name of the owner of the website, its legal form, its address, and the registration number of the media outlet in the special register with the Authority.

The name of the responsible director, his address, and the address of the media outlet where official transactions and correspondence are served, and the telephone and fax numbers and electronic mail.

B - The responsible director must meet the following conditions:

- That he be a Lebanese media professional enjoying his civil and political rights and not convicted of a felony or a disgraceful misdemeanour.

- That he hold a university degree with experience of not less than three years in the field of specialisation of the media outlet.

- That he not be a responsible director for more than one electronic website.

- That he be an actual resident in Lebanon and devoted full-time to working for the electronic media outlet.

- That he not be one of the persons enjoying any type of immunity in accordance with the law.
Every violation of the provisions of this Chapter above shall be punishable for its perpetrator by a fine ranging between twenty times and one hundred times the official minimum wage.

The publication of an opinion poll is free, provided that the announcement, publication, broadcast or distribution of its result by any media outlet is accompanied by the clarification of the following matters at the least, on the responsibility of the institution that conducted the poll:

- The name of the entity that conducted the poll.

- The name of the entity that requested the poll and paid its cost.

- The dates on which the poll was conducted in the field and the time it took.

- The size of the sample whose opinion was polled, the method of its selection, its distribution and its nature.

- The technique followed in the poll.

- The limits of interpreting the results and the rate of the margin of error therein, where applicable.

The publication of opinion polls that do not conform with Article 69 above is prohibited unless they are accompanied by the following phrase:

"Attention is drawn to the fact that the results of this poll cannot necessarily be relied upon to express valid trends of public opinion." This means the polls conducted or published by media outlets without a precise definition of the selected polled sample by leaving the freedom of participation open without defined criteria, or by soliciting or urging the public to answer any question or subject with the word "yes" or "no", or by way of preference, or any other phrase or indication conveying the same.
Every violation of the provisions of this Title shall be punishable for its perpetrator by a fine ranging between fifty times and one hundred times the official minimum wage.

a - There shall be established pursuant to this Law the "National Media Authority", which shall enjoy moral personality and financial and administrative independence, and is referred to in this Law as the "Authority".

b - The members of the Authority, the employees and all other workers thereof shall exercise their functions in complete independence from any other authority, and shall not be bound by the decisions or directives of any reference or

authority, including the entities that nominated, appointed or elected them.

c - The executive authority shall not have the right to take a decision suspending or halting the work of the Authority under any circumstance whatsoever.

d - The Authority shall be subject to the provisions of the special articles pertaining to it that establish and regulate it in this Law, and no prior law applicable to public institutions and independent administrative authorities, including the Law on Public Institutions, shall apply to or govern it.

e - The Authority shall be subject to the subsequent audit of the Court of Audit.

Membership of the Authority may only be assumed by persons of attested integrity, competence and experience, provided that candidates for membership of the Authority satisfy the following conditions:

1 - That they have been Lebanese nationals for more than ten years.

2 - That the age of the member does not exceed 69 years upon appointment or election, with the exception of members who are judges, for whom the maximum limit shall be 74 years.

3 - That they satisfy the conditions for appointment to Grade One posts provided for in Article Four of Legislative Decree No. 112/59 dated 12/6/1959 (Civil Servants Regulations), with the exception of the two conditions of age and competitive examination.

4 - That they hold a university degree not lower than a university bachelor's degree in the specialisations specified in accordance with the categories provided for in Article 82 below, in addition to experience of not less than ten years.

5 - That they have not, at the time of candidacy and during the three preceding years, held any political office or any leadership position in any party or any association that engages in political activity.

6 - That they do not have, at the time of candidacy and during the three preceding years, a direct or indirect interest in any media institution or institution that provides a media service in Lebanon, or that supplies equipment used in the field of media in Lebanon. These conditions shall also apply with respect to spouses

and their ascendants, descendants and relatives by affinity, who are deemed to constitute a single person.

7 - That they are not in any of the states of incompatibility provided for in this Law or a candidate therefor.

8 - That they have not been declared to have ceased payment or been judicially declared bankrupt, or been convicted of felonies or disgraceful misdemeanours or any offence of corruption, domestic violence or sexual harassment.

A - The Authority shall be composed of ten members. Seven of them shall be elected directly to their positions in the Authority by the entities specified in this Article below; these entities shall also nominate a number of candidates for the appointment of three of them by a decision of the Council of Ministers to the membership of the Authority in accordance with the following procedures:

1 - A retired judge in an honorary position, who shall be elected by an absolute majority by the members of the Supreme Judicial Council, the Bureau of the State Council, and the Bureau of the Court of Accounts.

The convocation and supervision of the elections shall be carried out by the highest-ranking judge among the President of the Supreme Judicial Council, the President of the State Council, and the President of the Court of Accounts. After the announcement of the results, the Minister of Justice shall submit the name of the elected judge who obtained the largest number of votes to the Presidency of each of the Chamber of Deputies and the Council of Ministers for their information.

2 - A lawyer or jurist elected to the Authority directly by the Councils of the Bar Associations in Beirut and Tripoli by an absolute majority, in a joint meeting convened at the invitation of the President of the Beirut Bar Association, based on nominations received by them for the available position. The two Councils of the Bar Association shall also nominate, in accordance with the same procedures and conditions, two candidates to fill one of the three positions provided for in Paragraph (F) of this Article.

3 - A telecommunications or software engineer elected to the Authority directly by the Councils of the Orders of Engineers in Beirut and Tripoli by an absolute majority, in a joint meeting convened

at the invitation of the President of the Order of Engineers in Beirut, based on nominations received by them for the available position. The two Councils of the Order shall also nominate, in accordance with the same procedures and conditions, two candidates to fill one of the three positions provided for in Paragraph (F) of this Article.

4 - A media expert elected to the Authority directly by an absolute majority by each of the Dean and branch directors of the Faculty of Information at the Lebanese University and the syndicates and bureaus of the councils of media syndicates established by law or that may be established by law.

The Dean of the Faculty of Information at the Lebanese University shall invite the concerned parties in writing to a meeting within a period of two months from the date of entry into force of this Law or from the date of vacancy of any position belonging to this category, in order to hold the election based on nominations received by them for the available position. The entities mentioned in this item shall also nominate, in accordance with the same procedures and conditions, two candidates to fill one of the three positions provided for in Paragraph (F) of this Article.

5 - A university professor specialised in any of the subjects of philosophy, arts, sociology, or humanities, elected to the Authority directly by an absolute majority by the deans and directors of these faculties at universities in Lebanon that grant bachelor's degrees in philosophy, arts, and sociology.

The Dean of the Faculty of Fine Arts at the Lebanese University shall invite the remaining deans to a meeting within a period of two months from the date of entry into force of this Law or from the date of vacancy of any position belonging to this category, in order to hold the election based on nominations received by them for the available position. The deans and directors shall also nominate, in accordance with the same procedures and conditions, two candidates to fill one of the three positions provided for in Paragraph (F) of this Article.

6 - An expert in economics, business administration, or public administration, whom the National Anti-Corruption Commission elects by an absolute majority to the Authority directly based on nominations received by it for the available position. The Commission shall also nominate, in accordance with the same procedures and conditions, two candidates

to fill one of the three positions provided for in Paragraph (F) of this Article.

7 - An expert in public freedoms and human rights, whom it elects to the National Human Rights Commission directly by an absolute majority of the members of this Commission based on nominations received by it for the available position from associations and individuals specialised in defending and promoting the freedoms of opinion, expression, and media. The Commission shall also nominate, in accordance with the same procedures and conditions, two candidates to fill one of the three positions provided for in Paragraph (F) of this Article.

B - The entities specified in Paragraph (A) above shall announce broadly, publicly, and transparently the prescribed mechanism and the conditions of membership of the Authority the Authority as provided for by the Law, as well as determine a mechanism to receive the largest number of nominations that meet the conditions. They shall also verify the fulfilment of all the conditions specified in this Law through the various available means, including reviewing documented curricula vitae, and through meetings with the candidates which shall be recorded in minutes, so as to allow the formation of a complete file for each candidate to be presented to the entity competent for the election, which shall draw up official minutes of the election process and refer them to the President of the Supreme Judicial Council to take the necessary measures.

C - The entities specified in Paragraph (A) above shall submit their proposals or complete the election for the first time within a period of three months from the date of publication of this Law in the Official Gazette. This process must also be completed in subsequent times at least two months before the expiry of the term of office of the members of the Authority.

D - The President of the Supreme Judicial Council shall follow up on the proper implementation of all procedures specified in this Article, and shall draw up final minutes of all the minutes received by him from the competent entities specified in this Article, concluding therein with the announcement of the victory of the elected members, and shall draw up a list of the names of the candidates for the membership of the Authority who were nominated in accordance with the provisions of Paragraph (A) above. He shall refer these minutes accompanied by all the files

pertaining to each of them directly to the Council of Ministers through the Minister of Information to take the necessary measures specified in this Article below.

E - Within a period not exceeding two weeks from the receipt of the minutes provided for in Paragraph "D" above, the President of the Council of Ministers shall propose a list of twelve experienced candidates, to appoint the three members from among the proposed names, and shall place an item on the agenda of the Council to complete this appointment with the aim of completing the formation of the Authority.

F - The Council of Ministers shall discuss the twelve nomination files and appoint from among them, by a two-thirds majority, three members. Thereafter, a decree forming the Authority shall be issued including the elected members and the three members who were appointed by it, and it shall be published in the Official Gazette in accordance with the procedures.

a - The term of office of the members of the Authority shall be six non-renewable years, with the exception of the first founding council, where the membership of half of its members shall be terminated by lot or by voluntary withdrawal at the end of the first three years, and replacements for them shall be elected in accordance with the same mechanism specified in this Law for a term of six years.

b - The election process must be completed, for the first time after the entry into force of this Law, within a maximum period of one month following the three-month period provided for in Article (c) of Article 74 above. This process must also take place on subsequent occasions at least two months prior to the expiry of the term of office of the members of the Authority.

c - The members of the Authority shall continue to exercise their functions notwithstanding the expiry of their term of office until replacements for them are appointed and take the legal oath.

a - Members of the Authority shall be prohibited from practising any other public or private work in Lebanon and abroad, whether remunerated or unremunerated, with the exception of university teaching, including, by way of example, the presidency or membership of the Council of Ministers or the Chamber of Deputies,

assuming any political or partisan position, or membership in any association that practises political work, or membership in a party, or the presidency or membership of the board of directors of a public institution, a private company or a bank, or the presidency or membership of a public body, and the presidency or membership of a municipal council or a private company that undertakes the management of a public utility, and the presidency or membership of the councils of syndicates or the bodies nominating the members.

b - A member of the Authority may not have any direct or indirect interest in Lebanon and abroad in any of the media institutions concerned by this Law, or in any institution that provides a media service in Lebanon or to Lebanon, or that supplies equipment used in the field of media. These conditions shall also apply with respect to the spouse and their ascendants, descendants and in-laws, who are deemed to constitute a single person with the candidates.

c - A member of the Authority may not, prior to the lapse of one full year from the end of his membership, stand for parliamentary, municipal or mukhtar elections, or assume any political, administrative, security or syndical public position.

d - These cases of incompatibility must continue throughout the duration of the term of office of the members.

The members of the Authority shall take the following oath before the President of the Republic:

"I swear by Almighty God to perform my duties in the National Media Authority with honesty, loyalty, and independence, and to act in everything I do with integrity in a manner that enhances confidence in the Authority and consolidates the freedoms of opinion, expression, and publication, the right of citizens to access information, and the rule of law."

The Council of the Authority shall elect from among its members a President, a Vice-President, a Secretary, and a Treasurer every three years, without any customs or vested rights arising in respect of these positions, whether in terms of professional specialization or any other consideration.

a - The Authority shall establish internal bylaws containing the detailed rules and procedures governing its organization, the workflow therein, and its financial administration, including the powers of each of the President, the Vice-President, and other positions, within a period of three months from the date they take the legal oath, pursuant to a regulatory decision issued by the Authority by a two-thirds majority of the members entitled to vote and after consulting the State Council, provided that this opinion is returned to the Authority within a period of two months from the date of its receipt of the drafts, after which the Authority may approve them in accordance with the referred version.

b - The Authority may amend the internal bylaws in accordance with the same procedures.

c - The Authority shall establish, in accordance with the procedures specified above, a mandatory code of conduct to be applied in its work.

d - The Authority may establish committees to perform permanent or temporary missions in accordance with what is specified by the internal bylaws.

e - Until its internal bylaws are approved and duly issued, the Authority shall operate in accordance with the basic minimum provisions specified in Article 80.

A - The sources of income of the Authority shall be as follows:

1 - The allowances and fees allocated to it by this Law.

2 - Unconditional donations and grants provided by sources that have no direct or

indirect interest in the media sector. Such donations shall only be subject to the obligation of notifying the Council of Ministers thereof, notwithstanding any other text.

3 - Any contributions transferred from the Treasury account in favour of the Authority by the Minister of Finance in accordance with its budget established in the body of the general budget.

B - An additional appropriation shall be opened in the general budget for the Authority for the first operational year following the entry into force of this Law, upon the request of the Minister of Information based on the proposal of the Authority after its formation.

C - Any surplus in the income of the Authority exceeding ten per cent (10%)(10%) of its annual budget shall be transferred to the Treasury account.

The President and members of the Authority shall receive, during the term of their membership, a lump-sum monthly allowance equivalent to the salary of the President and members of the Constitutional Council, and they shall also benefit from social benefits defined by the internal regulations.

a - The Authority shall be assisted by a full-time administrative staff headed by a Secretary-General, who shall be appointed by the Authority following a competitive examination conducted transparently.

b - The procedures for appointing the Secretary-General and his duties, and the procedures for organising and appointing the administrative staff and its duties, shall be defined in the internal regulations and the staff regulations which determine the scale of wages and ranks specific to the Authority.

c - The Authority may, where necessary, seek the assistance of whomever it wishes from among experts from outside the Authority and its employees, whether Lebanese or non-Lebanese, to carry out a specific mission and for a specific period.

d - The Secretary-General and the employees in the administrative staff shall be subject to the Labour Law.
The Authority shall prepare an annual report on its work

a - The Authority shall have a special annual budget included in the special chapter for independent authorities within the general budget, which shall be sufficient to cover the Authority's expenses and activities.

b - The Authority shall prepare the draft budget and its President shall submit it, through the Minister of Information, to the Minister of Finance, who shall incorporate it into the draft general budget submitted to the Council of Ministers, which shall undertake to refer it to the competent authorities in accordance with the rules.

c - A special account shall be opened for the Authority at the Bank of Lebanon, and the President of the Authority shall undertake the commitment of its expenditures and the supervision of their commitment in accordance with the procedures provided for in the Public Accounting Law. At the end of the financial year, the President of the Authority shall send tables of the expended appropriations to the Ministry of Finance certified by him, and the provisions of the Authority's special financial regulations shall apply with respect to these tables.

d - In addition to the ex-post audit of the Court of Accounts, the accounts of the Authority shall be subject to the internal audit system and to independent auditing by auditing and accounting firms in accordance with the provisions of Article 73 of Law No. 326 dated 28/6/20012001/6/28 (the 2001 Budget Law), and the accounts and the audit reports pertaining thereto shall be published in the Official Gazette and on the official website of the Authority.

a - The Authority shall hold a meeting whenever necessary, provided that it meets at least once every month upon a convocation by the President, and in his absence by the Vice-President.

b - The President of the Authority, and in his/her absence the Vice-President, must mandatorily issue a convocation to hold a meeting of the Authority within seven days from the date of his receipt of a request to that effect submitted by three or more members.

c - The members shall be notified of the date and place of the meeting and the agenda at least seven days in advance. In the event of an urgent necessity, this time limit may be shortened.

d - The President shall preside over the sessions of the Authority, and in his/her absence the Vice-President, and otherwise the Secretary.

e - The quorum shall be legal in the presence of at least half of the members of the Authority plus one.

f - The Authority shall hold its sessions and take decisions by the absolute

majority of the members of whom the Authority is legally composed, and in the event of a tie, the vote of the president of the session shall be casting.

g - The Secretary, and in his absence any of the present members appointed in his place, shall work to record the session, draw up the minutes of a meeting, and keep all minutes of the meetings in the format agreed upon by the Authority.

h - The minutes shall be submitted to the Authority for approval and official adoption at the following meeting, provided that the person who presided over the session and the Secretary sign the approved minutes in the presence of the members of the Authority present at the meeting.

i - The same rules referred to in the three preceding clauses shall apply to the meetings of the committees of the Authority.

j - The decisions of the Authority shall be subject to the principle of reasoning, and it shall be required to specify the reasons for its decisions, in accordance with the provisions of the Right of Access to Information Law.

Article 81:

a - The members of the Authority shall draw up the declarations of assets and interests provided for in the Illicit Enrichment Law within a time limit of two weeks from the date of taking the oath.

b - Any member to whom the grounds for recusal and withdrawal of judges provided for in Article 77 of the Code of Criminal Procedure apply in a matter under discussion at a meeting of the Authority or at a meeting of a committee emanating from the Authority must disclose the fact in which he has an interest and its nature to the remaining members present at the session.

c - The disclosure of the fact referred to in the paragraph above shall be recorded in the minutes of the meeting of the session.

d - Following the disclosure of the fact in accordance with the first paragraph of this Article, the remaining members shall discuss it and determine the course of action to be followed in accordance with the following:

- Either they decide that the said member shall not participate in the discussion, deliberation, or decision with the Authority regarding the said matter.

- Or he continues to perform his role normally as a member during the discussion of this matter.

Article 82:

a - Except for flagrante delicto offences, no member of the Authority may be prosecuted for acts relating to their duties by way of a criminal action, nor may any criminal measure be taken against them, nor may they be arrested or detained throughout the term of their mandate except after obtaining permission from the Authority by at least the absolute majority of the members entitled to vote, excluding the member concerned, who shall be heard and shall not participate in the voting session.

b - The competence of the Authority in cases of prosecution shall be limited to determining whether the act for which prosecution is requested relates to work with it, and it may not refuse to grant permission unless it considers that the act is related to work with it and the prosecution thereof is malicious and not based on any serious ground.

c - In flagrante delicto offences, the offices of the Authority shall be searched by order of the Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation or by decision of the First Investigating Judge, provided that this takes place in the presence of the President of the Authority or whoever he delegates for this purpose.

Article 83:

a - The mandate of each of the President of the Authority and its members shall terminate upon its expiry, or by death, resignation, or termination of membership in accordance with the procedures and conditions specified in this Article.

b - The membership of the President or any member of the Authority may not be terminated except by a decision of the Council of Ministers by a two-thirds majority, upon a request from the President or any of the members of the Authority or upon a complaint received by the Council from a party having standing and interest, after a panel composed of the President of the Supreme Judicial Council, the President of the State Council, and the President of the Court of Accounts verifies that the conditions for termination are met, and after these two bodies hear the complained-against member, in the following cases only:

1 - If he loses legal capacity, or any of the conditions of appointment, incompatibility, or full-time dedication provided for in this Law.

2 - If his health or mental condition prevents him from performing his duties.

3 - If he commits a grave fault or breach in the performance of his duties.

4 - If a final judgment is rendered against the member for a felony or a dishonourable misdemeanour.

c - In the event of a vacancy in the position of the President or any of the members six months or more prior to the expiry of his mandate, the Authority shall ascertain the occurrence of this vacancy and notify the matter within one week to the authority concerned with electing a replacement for him for the remaining period within a time limit of one month at most and in accordance with the rules and conditions of election specified in this Law.

d - The Council of Ministers may not take a decision to suspend the work of the Authority, stop it, or dissolve it under any circumstances whatsoever, including states of emergency and wars.

A - The Authority shall guarantee freedom of expression, media and publication in accordance with the general principles stipulated by the Constitution, the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, the relevant international covenants and this Law, in particular Article 3 thereof. It shall also work towards the proper compliance of public and private media institutions with the provisions of this Law and other relevant laws, and their enjoyment of its benefits and guarantees.

B - The Authority shall have the standing and interest to prosecute all violators of the provisions of this Law and to bring legal action against them before all competent courts, and it shall have in this respect all the powers and rights associated with assuming the status of a civil claimant, with the exception of the right to claim compensation.

In particular, the Authority shall be entrusted with the following functions:

1 - Delivering acknowledgements of notification and granting licences to media institutions in accordance with what is delegated to it by this Law and other laws.

2 - Accrediting foreign correspondents in accordance with Legislative Decree 10493 dated 2 July 1968.

3 - Determining the capabilities, standards, and technical and artistic specifications for broadcasting and for transmission equipment.

4 - Establishing and managing the Public Register relating to media institutions and verifying the information published therein where necessary.

5 - Determining the particulars of the books of specifications relating to television and radio media outlets.

6 - Drafting and adopting codes of conduct in accordance with the procedures and conditions specified in Article 103 of this Law.

7 - Drafting and publishing general annual reports, and special reports when necessary, relating to the assessment of the state of the media in Lebanon and its quality, in particular with regard to freedoms of opinion, expression, media and publication, and to violations committed against the exercise of freedoms and violations of laws, and proposing means of developing the media and its quality.

8 - Expressing opinions of its own motion or at the request of public authorities and competent official bodies on legislation, decrees, decisions and drafts thereof, and on policies and strategies relating to the media.

9 - Guaranteeing respect for diversity and pluralism in the work of media institutions, in particular in political and social programmes and news bulletins, and the absence of systematic blocking or blackout of subjects and persons.

10 - Assisting aggrieved parties in exercising the right of reply in accordance with the provisions of this Law, in particular in cases of repetition of false or incorrect news relating to a single natural or legal person.

A. The Authority may take any of the following measures in the course of exercising its functions specified in the Law, progressively with respect to legal violations, violations of the books of specifications, and violations of the codes of conduct:

1. Request for clarification.

2. Caution.

3. Formal warning.

4. Drafting general or special reports on the subject of the violations and obligating the violating media institution to publish them at the timing and with the time and programme space parallel to the violation, in accordance with what is specified by the Authority.

5. Referring the violating media institution to the competent judicial authorities.

B. With respect to violations of the books of specifications, the Authority may impose financial fines that it specifies after addressing the appropriate formal warning and upon non-compliance therewith.

C. With respect to a violation of the codes of conduct, the Authority may refer the violating media institution to a committee emanating from the Authority specialised in media ethics, which shall be established and have its internal regulations determined by a decision of the Authority.

Every person may submit a complaint to the Authority in connection with this Law, provided that the Authority organises the complaints mechanism within its internal regulations, subject to publication obligations.

Every media institution that commits a violation of the provisions of this Part or the books of specifications issued by the Authority shall be liable to a fine ranging between fifty times and one hundred times the official minimum wage.
Subject to the rules and conditions for initiating a public prosecution, every injured party, as well as the Authority, may request prosecution for the violations specified in the Parts of this Law.

A. All decisions of the Authority shall be subject to appeal before the State Council by way of annulment or full jurisdiction appeal within the time limits and rules in force before this Council.

B. Disputes arising between the Authority and its employees and contractors shall fall within the jurisdiction of the ordinary judiciary, provided that arbitration clauses, where they exist, may be enforced in contracts

concluded with third parties.

C. Every party or injured person shall have the right to request a review of the decisions issued by the Authority within a period of two months from the date of their publication, notification, or receipt of notification. The Authority may decide of its own motion and within a period of two months from the date of issuing its decision, or within a period of two months from the date of submitting the request for review, to revoke its decision or suspend its execution, or to take provisional measures to preserve the status quo and avoid causing any harm until a final administrative or judicial decision is issued in this regard.

أ - The Authority shall launch the consultation process to establish media ethics codes of conduct in accordance with a consultative mechanism, which includes the criteria for selecting the individuals concerned, determined by the Authority and announced by it to the public through its website and all other available media outlets, and this through meetings and discussions bringing together the members of the Authority with the following entities:

١ - Representatives of media institutions holding a notice and receipt or licences.

٢ - Academics specialised in media ethics at faculties of media and communication in Lebanese universities.

٣ - Representatives of media syndicates established by law.

٤ - Representatives of civil society specialised in developing the media sector and supporting media freedom.

٥ - Lebanese and non-Lebanese experts.

٦ - Independent journalists enjoying extensive experience and a good reputation.

ب - Alongside the discussions, the Authority shall launch an open survey covering all categories working in the media field, including journalists, photographers, producers, and content creators.

ج - Upon the conclusion of the discussions, the Authority shall prepare the first

draft of each of the codes of conduct that it has completed, send copies thereof to all the entities that participated in the meetings, and publish it on its website to receive comments and proposals.

د - After completing this mechanism, the Authority shall meet to discuss and adopt the texts by a majority of two-thirds of the members who compose it, and they shall enter into force from the date of their adoption and be published in the Official Gazette directly at the request of the President of the Authority.

هـ - The codes of conduct shall be amended whenever the need arises by following the procedures specified above for their adoption.

Codes of conduct may include several subjects relating to media materials and the production thereof, including, at a minimum, the following subjects:

- Respecting the principles of the Constitution.

- Complying with the laws in force, including those relating to the boycott of the Israeli enemy.

- Respecting and protecting fundamental public freedoms and human rights, in particular freedom of belief, opinion and expression, including religious freedoms and the practices thereof, within the framework of the duties of individuals towards society and its values, including family values, in accordance with the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
