- Non-discrimination on the basis of belief, religion, sect, denomination, age, gender, region and political affiliation, and rejecting hate speech.

- Verifying information and exercising accuracy in the publication thereof.

- Adhering to balance, integrity and independence in media performance and observing the public interest.

- Not manipulating news, photographs and videos.

- Respecting and protecting sources of information and dealing with them professionally.

- Respecting the right of reply and adhering to the correction of false news.

- Not encroaching upon personal life and respecting the privacy of individuals.

- Respecting the privacy of children in media coverage.

- Respecting women's rights in media and advertising practice and seeking to achieve balance in media appearance.

The Authority shall prepare periodic annual reports, and special reports when necessary to document violations, regarding the extent of compliance by media institutions and media professionals with professional ethics. The Authority's internal regulations must include special provisions determining the methodology for documenting such violations, preparing reports, and announcing and publishing the same.

A - Every media institution and every media practitioner shall be prohibited from publishing, broadcasting or circulating any information, images or details concerning the private life of individuals, unless such information is accurate and directly and objectively connected to the public interest.

Media outlets, media websites, and media practitioners shall also be prohibited from addressing or circulating any case that is still under investigation before the judiciary, unless it is a case of public opinion or public interest. In all cases, it is forbidden to publish investigation minutes or parts thereof before the issuance of the indictment.

B - Publication shall be permissible for anything relating to the public interest in proven cases that relate to holding accountable persons entrusted with public affairs, or uncovering cases of corruption, or matters affecting public rights and freedoms, or public security or health.

C - Personal life or matters not related to a public function or to a social or

political responsibility shall not be considered as part of the public interest.

D - In the event of the publication of information, images or details that violate the provisions of this Article, the injured party shall have the right to resort to the competent judiciary and prosecute the perpetrators to demand the removal or correction of the published material, in addition to his right to take any protective measure decided by the judiciary to protect his private life and stop the harm inflicted upon him, including stopping the media campaign immediately and/or removing the material immediately or correcting it or any other measure the court deems appropriate, with the application of the principle of tortious liability and compensation for all material or moral damage resulting from the unlawful publication.

E - In everything relating to private life, and in the event of recidivism or in cases of abuse in the exercise of the media right, the penalty against the offender shall be increased pursuant to the laws in force.

Article 99;

When factual media material that is inaccurate is published by a media institution, any person shall have the right to request the latter to correct it or remove it from all media mediums owned by the media institution, including its website, its social media accounts, radio stations and television channels.

The request for correction, removal, or reply shall be served upon the media establishment at its address by any means of written notice, including notice via electronic mail.

The concerned media establishments shall make the requested correction or the requested removal and publish the reply free of charge and without any modification in the manner of displaying the reply, in a manner equivalent to the objected material in terms of the place of publication, its timing, and its volume in minutes or in the number of words, and which shall not be of lesser standing than the viewership rate of the objected media material and its impact or exceed the effect of the latter, within the period specified below in respect of each means

of media and publication:

1 - With respect to periodical publications, the reply must be published in the first issue released after receipt of the request for reply.

2 - With respect to electronic websites, the reply must be published at the earliest reasonable possible time after receipt thereof.

3 - With respect to television and radio stations, the reply must be published in the following manner:

- At the beginning of the same programme pursuant to which the original objected material was published and in the broadcast subsequent to that in which the objected material was broadcast.

- In the event that the original material was published as breaking news, the reply shall be published at the earliest possible time as breaking news.

The publication of the reply, the making of the correction, or the removal of the objected material shall take place across all media platforms owned by the media establishment, including its electronic website, its own social media pages, and its radio and television stations, immediately upon the appearance of the objected media material in any of these media platforms, if they and their news management are controlled by a single establishment.
In the event of the death of the person who submitted the request for correction, removal, or reply, this right shall devolve to any of his heirs.

The Responsible Director shall have the right to refuse to publish the reply or correction in the following cases:

- If the media institution has previously and completely corrected the concerned media material in accordance with the conditions stipulated in this Law.

- If the reply is signed with a pseudonym or is unclear:

- If the reply is written in a language other than the language used in the original material.

- If the reply is contrary to the law and contains statements the publication of which by the media institution exposes it to legal

accountability, or contains immoral and insulting statements towards others.

- If the request for reply or correction is received after the expiry of thirty days from the date of publication of the original material.

In the event that the media institution refuses to publish the reply or to make the correction or removal within the conditions and time limits specified above, the claimant shall have the right to submit an application before the judge of urgent matters in accordance with the procedures specified in this article to issue a decision for publication, provided that this application is exempt from any fees. The application submitted before the judge of urgent matters shall be notified to the media institution at its address, and it shall have the right to submit its observations in writing within a time limit not exceeding 24 hours from the date of its notification.

The judge of urgent matters must issue his decision within a time limit not exceeding 48 hours from the date of expiry of the time limit granted to the media institution to submit its observations. The decision issued shall be enforceable immediately and subject exclusively to opposition or appeal to the exclusion of any other ordinary and extraordinary means of recourse, and within the same conditions and time limits specified above.

In the event that the decision rules for mandatory publication, correction, or removal of the objected material, the concerned media institution must execute it in accordance with the provisions, procedures, and time limits specified in this Chapter, in addition to publishing a summary of the decision issued by the judge of urgent matters and its grounds within the same procedures.

In the event of abstaining from executing the decisions issued by the competent judiciary, the concerned media institution and the responsible director therein shall be punished, jointly and severally, with a coercive fine for each day of delay in publishing the reply pursuant to the decision of the competent judiciary.

The publication of the reply, the correction, or the removal of the objected media material does not exempt from liability in the event that its elements are met, and the injured party may have recourse to the competent judiciary to claim compensation for the damage

suffered by him as a result of the publication of the news or the delay in publishing the reply, correction, or removal.

The time limit for applying to the judge of urgent matters to compel the publication of the reply, correction, or removal shall expire after thirty days from the date of receipt of the request addressed to the media institution in accordance with the legal provisions stipulated above. The non-execution of the requested measures by the media outlet within the time limits specified therein shall be deemed an implicit refusal thereof.

Incitement to Hatred and Discrimination (and False News)

A - Whoever uses any means of publication, including any of the media outlets provided for in this Law, to incite sectarian conflict or violence against persons or a group by reason of their belonging or non-belonging in terms of race, religion, sect, colour, or sex. Shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to three years and by a fine set at five times the minimum wage and reaching up to fifteen times thereof, or by either of these two penalties, provided that the following elements are combined:

1 - The social and political context, whereby context means placing the speech act within the social and political context at the time the speech is issued and published.

2 - The standing of the perpetrator, meaning his standing in society, and in particular his individual position or the position of his organisation among the public to whom the speech is directed.

3 - The intent to incite the public against the targeted persons or group, and here what is meant is advocacy and incitement, not mere dissemination or circulation, and in this regard it is presumed that account shall be taken of the relationship between the purpose of the speech

and its subject matter, in addition to the audience of listeners, in order to measure the extent to which intent is present.

4 - The content and form of the speech, meaning here the extent to which this speech is provocative and direct, and the form, style, and nature of the arguments used in the speech.

5 - The extent of the dissemination of the speech, meaning whether it was circulated in a restricted environment or one open on a wide scale.

6 - The likelihood of harm, including harm certain to occur, meaning here whether there is a reasonable probability that the speech would succeed in inciting actual action against the targeted persons or group.

B - Whoever intentionally fabricates falsehoods and publishes false and harmful news shall be punished by imprisonment from three months to three years and by a fine set at five times the minimum wage and reaching up to fifteen times thereof, or by either of these two penalties.

C - The penalty shall be aggravated to hard labour if these acts lead to killing, injury, total or partial disruption, or major destruction of public and private property.

The provisions of the texts relating to slander and defamation provided for in Sub-section 5 of Chapter II of Title VIII of Book II and contempt provided for in Sub-section 3 of Chapter II of Title III of Book II of the Lebanese Penal Code (Legislative Decree No. 340/1943), as well as the publication of false news and offending religious or national sentiment provided for in the Lebanese Penal Code (Legislative Decree No. 340/1943), the Military Justice Law No. 24/1968, and Legislative Decree No. 104/1977 (amending the Publications Law issued on 14/9/1962), shall not apply to the provisions provided for in this Law.

Those texts shall remain in force in matters other than those relating to the special provisions governed by this Law, and they shall not be relied upon in interpreting or applying its provisions.

In the event of conflict, the provisions of this Law shall prevail as special texts that restrict general texts, and they shall take precedence over them in application.

Definitions

For the purposes of this Chapter of the Law, the following expressions shall have the meanings set out below:

- Public official: any person who performs a public function or a public service, whether appointed or elected, permanent or temporary, paid or unpaid, in any legal person of public law or private law, at the central and decentralised levels, and in general any person who performs work for the benefit of public property, a public facility, a public utility, a public institution, a public department, or public funds, whether wholly or partially owned by a legal person of public law, and whether he assumed it de jure or de facto, including any position of the constitutional authorities or any legislative, judicial, executive, administrative, military, financial, security, or advisory position.

- Public figures: public officials and persons who play influential roles in public life, whether political, economic, artistic, social, sports-related, or otherwise.

- Public place: a place accessible to all people or to a specific public upon the fulfilment of a number of special conditions for entering this place.

A - Every word of contempt or revilement, and every expression, drawing, or still or moving image that reveals

disparagement without containing defamation, shall be deemed vituperation.

B - The attribution of a matter to a natural or legal person, even in the form of doubt or interrogation, that impugns his honour, dignity or reputation, shall be deemed defamation.

C - Any natural or legal person who causes damage to any natural or legal person by means of the acts mentioned in Paragraphs (A) and (B) above, or any other public acts that harm the interest of others, may have an action brought against him by any injured party on the basis of Title Two, Illicit Acts: Delict or Quasi-Delict, of Book Two of the Code of Obligations and Contracts, and specifically Articles 121 to 128.

A - Criminal liability shall be precluded if the attribution of the matter by the defendant to a public official or a public figure was made in good faith and related to the office or the public interest, and the defendant who attributed the matter was able to submit evidence thereof, or prima facie evidence or presumptions as to the accuracy of the attributed information, provided that the court completes such evidence and presumptions with that which proves them, if possible, by compelling the competent administrations or authorities and the plaintiff to submit the information or documents in their possession.

B - The defendant may produce or provide to the court all elements of proof required by the necessities of defending himself as to the truth of the act of defamation directed at the public official or public figure, whether such disclosure leads to a breach of the confidentiality of the investigation or trial or any professional or official secrecy, and without this giving rise to any right to prosecute him judicially for offences connected with the possession of those elements of proof or the disclosure thereof, if such disclosure would prove the good faith of the defendant and the truth of the acts that he attributed to the public official.
It is prohibited to publish or broadcast anything that contravenes the laws in force.

The civil court that issued the judgment may compel the media outlet against which the judgment was issued to publish it free of charge, either in full or a summary thereof, in accordance with conditions determined by the court, under pain of imposing a coercive fine upon it.

A Civil Chamber of First Instance shall be established in each governorate having jurisdiction to hear quasi-delicts of opinion and media in accordance with the provisions of this Law, and the court within whose territorial jurisdiction the headquarters of the media institution or the defendant person is located shall be the court of competent jurisdiction.

The summary procedure rules provided for in the Code of Civil Procedure in Chapter Eleven bis: Summary Procedures shall apply at all stages of the trial, with the exception of Article 500 bis 1 regarding the acts provided for in Article One and Article 500 bis 3 bis 3 relating to the procedures and time limits for exchanging briefs, and the ordinary procedures provided for in Articles 451 and 454 and 454 of the Code of Civil Procedure shall apply.

Article 113,

The jurisdiction of the Military Court shall be excluded in respect of all offences relating to opinion and media provided for in this Law, as well as the offences provided for pursuant to Article 157 of the Code of Military Justice.
Pre-trial detention shall not be permissible in all offences committed through all media outlets and electronic means provided for in this Law, whatever the capacity or profession of the perpetrator.

a - Every journalist shall have the right to refuse to sign any article, programme, or contribution of any kind that has been modified in form or content without his knowledge or against his will.

b - Every journalist shall have the right to refrain from executing or participating in any work that conflicts with his professional conscience or codes of professional conduct, and he may not be compelled or penalised on this basis.

c - No form of material or moral pressure, interference, or threat may be exercised upon a journalist with the aim of influencing the content of his journalistic work. Every attempt of this kind shall be deemed an explicit violation of this Law.

d - Editorial independence shall be guaranteed in all media outlets. No owning, funding, or external entity may influence the editorial line or journalistic content, whether directly or indirectly.

e - Journalists shall enjoy, without discrimination, the right to freely establish or join syndicates. It shall be prohibited to take any administrative or professional measure against any journalist on account of his syndicate affiliation or his participation in lawful syndicate activities.

f - All journalists shall have the right to access information and to move freely to perform their work, and they may not be obstructed without a lawful legal justification. Official authorities shall be bound to cooperate with journalists and enable them to perform their duties within the limits of the law.

g - Journalists shall enjoy legal protection during the performance of their work. The criminal penalties provided for in the Penal Code shall be aggravated upon any harm, physical or verbal assault, incitement, or threat committed against them on account of their professional activity.

A media person has the right to maintain the confidentiality of

the sources of his information.

A - Neither a media person, nor any person to whom the information has reached in his capacity as a participant in the media production process, nor anyone in a similar position (such as a third party who becomes privy to the sources of information by virtue of his professional relationship with the media person) may be requested to disclose the identity of any person who supplied him with the information or to give specific information that would enable the identification of his source.

B - This protection shall apply against any administrative or judicial proceedings initiated against him, whether within the framework of a legal action relating to his journalistic work or within the framework of wiretapping and surveillance measures or search measures affecting the place of residence, workplaces, electronic devices, files and correspondence relating to the work of the media person.

C - All electronic devices and paper documents belonging to the persons enumerated in paragraph (A) above shall be deemed covered by this special protection, and shall not be subject to search or seizure except within the procedures and conditions specified in the paragraph below.

D - No authority, with the exception of the court conducting the investigation or the criminal or civil trial and by virtue of decisions supported by sufficient written reasoning, shall have the right to compel the persons covered by this protection to disclose the identity of the sources of their information or to order the search and seizure of electronic devices and paper documents for the purpose of disclosing them, if any of the following conditions is met:

- If the information would certainly prevent any crime of terrorism.

- If the information would prevent an imminent danger to the lives of persons.

All prosecutions, complaints and lawsuits that are still

before the Public Prosecutions on the date of entry into force of this Law shall be administratively referred to the competent court in accordance with the provisions of this Law, whereas prosecutions that are pending before other judicial authorities shall continue to be heard by those authorities, provided that the provisions of this Law shall apply to them.

All entries of judgments rendered pursuant to criminal articles that have been repealed pursuant to this Law shall be expunged, subject to the payment of personal damages, pursuant to a request submitted to the competent Appellate Public Prosecution at the place where the judgment was rendered.

All laws and legislative and regulatory provisions that contradict it or are incompatible with its provisions are repealed, in particular the following laws and provisions:

a - The Publications Law issued in the year 1962 is repealed with the exception of Title Four (the Lebanese Press Syndicate from Chapter One to Chapter Six inclusive), and Legislative Decree No. 104 issued on 30/6/1977 concerning publications offences is also repealed in full along with the regulatory texts issued in implementation thereof.

b - The provisions of Legislative Decree No. 74 issued on 13/4/1953, which fixed the number of political periodical publications, and the implementing texts issued in execution of its provisions are repealed.

c - Legislative Decree No. 55 issued on 5/8/1967, which prohibited the printing, issuance and publication of certain publications without obtaining a prior licence, is repealed.

d - Law No. 330/1994, which amended certain provisions of the Publications Law, is repealed.

e - The "Television and Radio Broadcasting" Law No. 382 issued on 11/6/1994 is repealed with the exception of the sixth paragraph of the seventh Article thereof.

f - The Publications Court provided for in Legislative Decree 104/1977 is abolished and competence

to hear all criminal offences related to opinion and media shall revert to the territorial and subject-matter jurisdiction provided for in the laws in force.

g - All provisions contrary to or inconsistent with the content of this Law are repealed, in particular those set forth in Legislative Decree No. 100 dated 30/6/1977 and Decree No. 770 dated 30/12/1977.
The details of implementation of this Law shall be determined, where necessary, by decrees adopted in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Information.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

A general amnesty is granted for offences committed prior to 1 March 2026, and all those who participated in committing them shall benefit therefrom, whether in their capacity as principals, accomplices, accessories, instigators or concealers, in accordance with the definitions set forth in the Penal Code.

The general amnesty shall result in the abatement of the public prosecution and the expungement of the principal penalties imposed, and all prosecutions, judgments and decisions, including administrative ones, issued against civil servants on charges other than financial corruption shall likewise lapse, whether rendered in presence, in absentia or deemed as rendered in presence.

The following offences shall be excluded from the general amnesty, whether judgments have been rendered or not:

1 - Offences that have been referred to the Judicial Council.

2 - Premeditated or intentional homicide and the offences set forth in the Terrorism Law issued on 11/1/1958 committed against civilians or military personnel and all members of the security forces.

3 - Military offences provided for in Title II, Book III, and disgraceful offences provided for in Article 105 of the Military Justice Law No. 24 dated 13/4/1968.

4 - Offences of treason, espionage, and offences relating to unlawful contact with the enemy, with the exception of those covered by Paragraph 2 of the Single Article of Law No. 194 dated 18/11/2011, who shall be deemed beneficiaries ipso jure of the present general amnesty law.

5 - Perpetrators of repeat drug felonies exceeding the second time, committed prior to the issuance of this Law, whether judicial judgments have been rendered therein or not, shall not benefit from the amnesty law.

- All drug offences committed by military personnel and members of security institutions.

- Offences of cultivating narcotic substances shall be deemed covered by this amnesty if committed prior to the issuance of this Law.

6 - Offences relating to all types of encroachment subject to prosecution which remain ongoing on the date of issuance of this Law and are committed against:

- Public property of the State of all types.

- Public property of municipalities.

- Municipal, communal, and state-owned (Amiri) commons.

- Public property belonging to public institutions.

- Private property and facilities of the State.

The amnesty shall not cover fines prescribed for contraventions prior to this Law.

7 - Offences committed against public funds.

8 - Offences of forgery, counterfeiting of national and foreign currency and circulating the same, undermining the financial standing of the State, offences of fraudulent bankruptcy, and offences provided for in the Code of Money and Credit, and all other laws and regulations relating to banks.

9 - Offences of illicit enrichment set forth in Law No. 189 dated 16/10/2020, relating to the embezzlement of public funds, breach of trust in respect thereof, or theft thereof, or to funds belonging to financial and banking institutions, and tax evasion.

10 - Offences provided for in the Law on Fighting Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing No. 44/2015, and offences in violation of the Code of Money and Credit whoever their perpetrators may be, in particular offences linked to depositors' funds and offences relating to banking offences of all types.

11 - Offences provided for in the laws relating to antiquities.

12 - Offences of rape, incest, human trafficking, domestic violence, sexual assault against minors, and the provisions of the Law on the Punishment of Torture and Other Cruel, Inhuman or Degrading Treatment or Punishment No. 65 / 20172017/65 and the Law on Missing and Forcibly Disappeared Persons No. 105 / 2018.2018/105.

13 - Offences of theft in accordance with the following:

• Felonies in the event of repetition of prosecutions or judgments more than twice

• Misdemeanours in the event of repetition of prosecutions or judgments more than three times

14 - Environmental offences provided for in the Law on the Protection of the Environment No. 444 dated 29/7/2002 and relevant texts.

Notwithstanding any other provision, in offences in which judgments have or have not been rendered and which occurred prior to the date of entry into force of this Law, and which are not covered by the amnesty, the term of penalties shall be commuted as follows:

1 - The penalty of death becomes 28 prison years.

2 - Hard labour for life becomes 17 prison years.

3 - All remaining penalties are reduced by one third.

And in offences of premeditated or intentional homicide coupled or accompanied by the following aggravating circumstances:

- Rape or sexual assault.

- Where committed by an ascendant or descendant or by a person having authority, guardianship or tutorship over the victim.

- Where coupled with torture, savagery, mutilation or kidnapping.

- Where committed within the framework of political assassination.

and the injured party had assumed the capacity of civil party prior to 1/3/2026, the convicted person shall not benefit from the reduction except after the dropping of the personal right.

The right to hear personal rights arising from an offence covered by the full amnesty, prescription, or the reduction of penalties shall remain within the jurisdiction of the criminal courts if the public action was brought directly before the criminal authorities or referred to them prior to the entry into force of this Law.

As for other personal right actions arising from a criminal offence covered by the full amnesty or prescription, they shall be adjudicated by the competent civil or administrative courts, and the laws on fees in force for civil actions before the criminal judiciary shall apply to them.

When enforcing a judgment for compensation rendered by the criminal or ordinary courts, the claimant is entitled to request the coercive imprisonment of the judgment debtor, in accordance with the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the Criminal Code.

Exceptionally, in all offences committed prior to the date of 1/3/2026 in which no judgment has been rendered, and where the period of detention has exceeded 12 prison years, the defendant shall be released ipso jure and his trial shall continue in accordance with the legal procedures.

In the event that a beneficiary of this Law commits a misdemeanour after the date of publication of the Law, his penalty for the new offence shall be aggravated in accordance with the provisions of Article 257 of the Criminal Code.

In the event that he commits a felony after the date of publication of this Law, the amnesty shall lapse in his regard and his penalty or his trial shall resume from the stage it was at prior to the issuance of this Law, in addition to his trial for the newly committed offence.

With respect to non-Lebanese nationals, any person who benefits from the provisions of this Law shall be handed over immediately upon his release from prison to the General Directorate of General Security to take the necessary measures in accordance with the legal procedures.
Fees, deposits and fines that have been collected, and items prohibited by law that have been confiscated or seized in all actions covered by the amnesty, shall not be returned.

Exceptionally, all convicted persons who have served the term of their penalty prior to the date of publication of this Law and who remain imprisoned for failure to pay the financial fines to which they were sentenced, shall be exempted from all fines and fees of whatever kind so that they may be released from prison.

For one time, exclusively and for the purposes of applying this Law, Article 205 of the Penal Code shall be amended to read

as follows:

With the exception of persons sentenced to the death penalty or life imprisonment, which are not subject to cumulation, if several felonies or misdemeanours are established, a penalty shall be pronounced for each offence and the most severe penalty alone shall be executed.

Provided that the penalties imposed may be cumulated such that the total of the temporary penalties does not exceed the maximum penalty prescribed for the most severe offence except by the amount of one quarter thereof.
This Law shall enter into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette.

Article 2 of Law No. 23 issued on 14/8/2025 (Law on the Reform and Reorganisation of the Status of Banks in Lebanon) is amended to read as follows:

Articles (1) to (36) determine the provisions on which the process of reforming the status of the bank and the liquidation process are based.

Article 3 of Law No. 23 issued on 14/8/2025 (Law on the Reform and Reorganisation of the Status of Banks in Lebanon) is amended to read as follows:

This Law aims to establish a modern legal framework aligned with followed international standards and what the Government and the Banque du Liban require in order to strengthen the stability of the financial system, address cases of distress of the bank while ensuring the continuity of critical functions and activities, protect deposits in the liquidation and reform process, and limit the use of public funds in the process of reforming any distressed bank.

The fifth Article of Law No. 23 issued on 14/8/2025 (the Law on the Resolution and Reorganization of Banks in Lebanon) is amended to read as follows:

For the purposes of applying the provisions of this Law, Article 10 of Law No. 28/1967 dated 9/5/1967 is amended to read as follows:

An authority called the Higher Banking Authority shall be established at the Banque du Liban, composed of two Chambers as follows:

1 - «The First Chamber exercises the powers of the Higher Banking Authority provided for in Law No. 28/1968 dated 9/5/1967 and the laws in force, and is composed of:

- The Governor of the Banque du Liban - Chairman.

- The First Vice-Governor of the Banque du Liban.

- The Director General of Finance.

- A judge with experience in financial and commercial affairs of not less than ten years, appointed by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice, selected from a list of candidates prepared by the Supreme Judicial Council.

- The Chairman of the Banking Control Commission.

- The Chairman of the National Deposit Guarantee Institution established pursuant to Law No. 28/1967.

The First Chamber of the Authority replaces the Sanctions Committee provided for in Article 209 of the Code of Money and Credit, applies, where necessary, the sanctions set out in Article 208 of the same Law, and exercises the powers vested in it pursuant to Law No. 28/1967.

In application of the administrative sanctions referred to in the paragraph above, where the First Chamber decides to appoint an interim manager, the provisions of the Articles of Title VIII of this Law shall apply. And where it is decided to strike the bank off the list of banks, the provisions of the Articles of Title IX of this Law shall apply.

The Banking Control Commission shall successively inform the Governor of the Banque du Liban of the conditions of the banks collectively and individually, and the First Chamber of the Authority has the right to request from the Commission any additional information on the cases brought before it.

The First Chamber of the Authority shall meet upon the convocation of its Chairman or at the request of two of its members, and its meetings shall not be legal unless at least four members attend. Its decisions shall be taken by a majority of at least three votes, and in the event of a tie, the Chairman shall have a casting vote.

2 - The Second Chamber shall be the competent authority for taking decisions regarding banks that must be subjected to resolution operations or liquidation operations in accordance with the laws in force, and is vested with the restructuring powers and functions

specified in the text of this Law, and is composed of:

- The Governor of the Banque du Liban - Chairman.

- Two of the Vice-Governors, provided that one of them is the First Vice-Governor of the Banque du Liban, and the second is selected by the Central Council of the Banque du Liban.

- A financial expert having experience of not less than ten years in the fields of bank mergers and restructuring, appointed by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers from a list of three candidates proposed by the Minister of Finance, provided that he is independent of any governmental or banking entity

- An economic expert having experience of not less than ten years in the fields of bank mergers and restructuring, appointed by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers from a list of three candidates proposed by the Minister of Economy and Trade, provided that he is independent of any governmental or banking entity.

- A judge with experience in financial and commercial affairs of not less than ten years, appointed by a decree taken in the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Justice, selected from a list of candidates prepared by the Supreme Judicial Council.

- The Director General of Finance as a member of the Central Council of the Banque du Liban, provided that he exercises his functions in accordance with Article 28 of the Code of Money and Credit.

The Chairman of the Banking Control Commission shall attend the meetings of the Second Chamber of the Authority without the right to vote or to be counted in the quorum, and shall present an overview of the status of the bank under consideration and present the recommendations of the Control Commission, supported by a financial valuation report and an independent analysis prepared by an independent party appointed by the Banking Control Commission.

Each member of the Second Chamber of the Authority shall submit to the General Secretariat of the Authority, two working days prior to the date of the meeting scheduled to discuss the conditions of a bank subject to the scope of the Law on the Resolution and Reorganization of Banks in Lebanon, a declaration of any existing or former relationship with the bank in accordance with the criteria specified in Article 6 of this Law.

In the event that any of the members of the Second Chamber of the Authority has any kind of relationship that may expose him to a conflict of interest or affect in any

manner whatsoever his independence and his decision during the performance of his work in respect of the bank subject to this Law, such member shall abstain from participating in any discussion or decision regarding the bank concerned and from exercising his voting rights in this regard. In such case, the decisions of the Second Chamber of the Authority shall be taken by a majority of the remaining members.

The Second Chamber of the Authority shall meet upon the convocation of its Chairman or at the request of three of its members, and its meetings shall not be legal unless at least four members attend. Its decisions shall be taken by a majority of the votes of those present, and in the event of a tie, the Chairman shall have a casting vote. It shall be for its Chairman to set the agenda of its meetings. The deliberations of the Second Chamber of the Authority shall be confidential and its decisions shall not be disclosed except by way of reports or decisions signed by its Chairman.

The Banking Control Commission shall successively inform the Governor of the Banque du Liban of the conditions of the banks and submit its report to the General Secretariat of the Higher Banking Authority, which shall refer each report to one of the two Chambers in accordance with the recommendation of the Banking Control Commission based on the nature of the measures intended to be taken, whether with respect to imposing sanctions or with respect to addressing the condition of the bank concerned.

Article 6 of Law No. 23 issued on 14/8/2025 (Law on the Reform of the Status of Banks in Lebanon and their Reorganisation) shall be amended to read as follows:

- Each member of the Higher Banking Commission shall submit the declaration provided for in Law No. 189 dated 16/10/2020 (Law on the Declaration of Assets and Interests and the Punishment of Illicit Enrichment). The time limit for submitting this declaration shall be one month from the date of publication of this Law in the Official Gazette for current members, and two months from the date of appointment for new members. Furthermore, each member must, immediately, submit an updated declaration in the event that any change occurs in his relationship with any bank. The General Secretariat of the Commission shall be tasked with ensuring the proper implementation of this process.

- In the event that any member of the Higher Banking Commission has any kind of direct or indirect relationship that exposes him to a conflict of interest or affects in any manner whatsoever his

independence when performing his work in relation to a bank subject to this Law, such member shall abstain from participating in any discussion or decision concerning the bank concerned and from exercising his voting rights in this regard. In this case, the decisions of the Commission shall be taken by the majority of the remaining members.

- The following criteria shall be adopted in determining the independence of a member and the absence of a conflict of interest:

* That he has not been a shareholder in the bank or its affiliated institutions in the preceding five years.

* That he has not held in the five years preceding his appointment the position of a member of the Board of Directors or Senior Management or an advisor in the bank or its affiliated institutions.

* That he is not a borrower or none of his family members is a borrower from the bank or from its affiliated institutions

* That he is not a depositor or none of his family members is a depositor of more than 100 thousand US dollars with the bank or its affiliated institutions

* That he has no kinship relation up to the fourth degree with a shareholder or a member of the Board of Directors or Senior Management at the bank or its affiliated institutions.

* Any other criteria that may negatively affect his independence directly or indirectly.

Article Seven of Law No. 23 issued on 14/8/2025 (Law on the Resolution and Reorganisation of Banks in Lebanon) is amended to read as follows:

- It shall pertain to the Second Chamber of the Higher Banking Authority to take the decision regarding subjecting banks to either of the following two processes in accordance with the provisions of this Law:

A - The Resolution Process:

The Authority shall issue a decision to resolve the bank (the Resolution Decision) containing, for each bank, the bank resolution tools that must be applied, the measures by which the bank must abide throughout its resolution process and the time necessary to complete these measures.

B - The Liquidation Process:

The Authority shall issue a decision to strike off the bank from the List of Banks of the Banque du Liban and a decision to liquidate the bank concerned.

The striking off of the bank shall be followed by a decision appointing a liquidation committee.

- The resolution decision or the striking-off decision shall be taken on the basis of a final valuation report sent by the Banking Control Commission, based on the report of an independent valuer, to the Higher Banking Authority regarding the necessity of liquidating the bank or rehabilitating it through resolution measures after stating the reasons that led to taking its decision.

- The bank resolution process or liquidation shall be based on a valuation the purpose of which is to determine the net value of the bank's assets and the size of the losses. The resolution process shall be based on a valuation prepared by the Banking Control Commission, which shall submit a recommendation to the Higher Banking Authority regarding the possibility of the bank's default and the necessity of taking resolution measures, provided that the valuation is duly completed by independent valuers appointed by the Banking Control Commission as specified in Article 10 and Article 11 of this Law for the taking of the final decision by the Higher Banking Authority with respect to resolution or liquidation. The Higher Banking Authority may also, on an exceptional basis, and in the event of the impossibility of preparing an urgent independent valuation, take the decision based solely on the report of the Control Commission in the event that the bank's situation requires urgency in order to preserve the assets of the bank and the depositors. Provided that an independent valuer is subsequently and urgently appointed by the Banking Control Commission to prepare a valuation to be submitted to the Higher Banking Authority, and the Authority may take additional measures or reconsider its decision based on the results of the valuation.

- The Higher Banking Authority shall state, in the minutes of its meetings, the justifying reasons for its decisions, including the justifying reasons for its non-adoption of the recommendations of the Banking Control Commission, should that occur.

Article Eight of Law No. 23 issued on 14/8/2025 (Law on the Reform of the Status of Banks in Lebanon and their Reorganisation) shall be amended so as to read as follows:

- With respect to the process of reforming the status of the bank:

- With respect to the liquidation process:

The Higher Banking Commission shall immediately notify the concerned bank of the decision of striking off and the decision of appointing a liquidator or a liquidation committee, and both decisions shall be registered in the Commercial Register. Both decisions shall be published, together with a summary of the valuation results, in the Official Gazette, in a newspaper of wide circulation in Lebanon, and on the website of the Banque du Liban.

- The Higher Banking Commission shall publish an annual report summarising the progress achieved towards the fulfilment of its objectives within the scope of this Law, and shall send a copy of this report to the Lebanese Parliament.

Article Ten of Law No. 23 issued on 2025/8/14 (Law on Reforming the Status of Banks in Lebanon and Reorganising Them) is amended to read as follows,

- The Banking Control Commission shall appoint independent valuers to conduct the valuation from among a list of international valuation institutions of professional standing.

- The valuation shall be based on International Valuation Standards and International Financial Reporting Standards, taking into consideration the prudential requirements and instructions issued by the Banque du Liban.

- The valuation shall be completed within the time limit set by the Banking Control Commission.

- The following eligibility criteria shall be observed in appointing the independent valuers:

* That they possess the required qualifications, specifically with regard to standards of integrity, competence, and professional experience.

* That they enjoy independence and have no professional or personal relationship with the bank and its related institutions that may expose them to a conflict of interest.

- The independent valuers, their partners in the partnership agreement, and the external parties with whom they contract shall abide, throughout the duration of their mission and even after its termination, by the banking and professional secrecy regulations, in favour of the concerned bank and its clients, with respect to the information to which they gain access during the performance of their duties, under penalty of the laws in force.

- The Central Bank shall bear the cost of appointing the independent valuer / independent valuers. The Banque du Liban shall recover the cost from the concerned bank.

- The independent valuers shall submit their reports to the Banking Control Commission with a copy thereof to the concerned bank, within the time limit set by the Banking Control Commission.

- The Banque du Liban shall issue, upon the proposal of the Banking Control Commission, instructions and details of the attributes, selection, and qualification of the valuer/ valuers along with the required valuation means, tools, and details.

Article Eleven of Law No. 23 issued on 2025/8/14 (Law on the Reform of the Status of Banks in Lebanon and Their Reorganization) shall be amended to read as follows:

The failure of the bank to notify the Higher Banking Commission of any objection to the results of the valuation conducted by the independent valuers shall be deemed an acknowledgment of the results of the valuation. In the event that the bank objects to the results of the valuation for material reasons and factual errors that substantially and materially affect the results of the valuation, it may notify the Higher Banking Commission, in writing with a copy to the Banking Control Commission, of the detailed reasons for its objection within a maximum period of 10 business days from the date the bank is notified of the valuation report.

The Higher Banking Commission may, upon the objection of the bank, for legitimate reasons related to the discovery of documentary and factual errors that substantially and materially affect the result of the valuation as at the date of the valuation, and after obtaining a report from the Banking Control Commission and the opinion of the independent valuer, decide to conduct the valuation anew, partially or wholly, within a maximum period of one month. In this case, the Higher Banking Commission shall decide whether the valuation shall be corrected

by the independent valuers or whether new independent valuers shall be commissioned by the Control Commission, and the results of the valuation shall be final.

The Higher Banking Commission shall take its decision to reform the bank on the basis of the valuation report, after reviewing the letter of the bank and the response of the Banking Control Commission and the independent valuer as well, and in the event of liquidation it shall take its decision in accordance with what is stated in Article 23.

Article Twelve of Law No. 23 issued on 14/8/2025 (Law on the Resolution and Reorganisation of Banks in Lebanon) is amended so as to read as follows

The Banking Control Commission shall assess whether the bank is failing or likely to fail and whether any alternative measures, such as a recovery plan or any other supervisory intervention, could prevent the failure of the bank, on the "basis of one of the following criteria:

* The failure or likely failure of the bank to comply with the minimum own funds requirements in due course.

* The failure or likely failure of the bank to comply with the minimum liquidity requirements in due course.

* The failure or likely failure of the bank to pay its liabilities as they fall due.

* The failure or likely failure of the bank to achieve and maintain profitability.

* The failure or likely failure of the bank to comply with the conditions on the basis of which the licence was granted, including a material breach of the laws or regulations in force.

Where the Banking Control Commission considers that the bank is failing or likely to fail, it shall submit the recommendation for resolution or liquidation and the statement of reasons therefor to the Higher Banking Commission within a period not exceeding one week from the date of its assessment. In the case of resolution, the recommendation shall include the resolution tool or tools that may be adopted to achieve the resolution objectives in accordance with the provisions of Article 3.

Article Fourteen of Law No. 23 issued on 14/8/2025 (Law on the Resolution and Reorganisation of Banks in Lebanon) is amended to read as follows:

The following principles shall apply in the course of implementing the bank resolution process:

- The hierarchy of own funds and creditors specified in Annex No. 1 shall be observed.

- Own funds shall absorb the entirety of the losses first, on

a pro rata basis within the same rank of liabilities in accordance with the order set out in Annex No. 1.

- The creditors of the bank shall absorb the losses on a pro rata basis within the same rank of liabilities in accordance with the order set out in Annex No. 1.

- Creditors within the same rank in accordance with Annex No. 1 shall be treated equally (principle of pari passu treatment).

- Shareholders within the same rank in accordance with Annex No. 1 shall be treated equally (principle of pari passu treatment).

Creditors within the same rank in accordance with Annex No. 1 shall not, as a result of the application of the bank resolution tools, be in a financial position below their presumed position in the event of the liquidation of the bank. In circumstances where it becomes apparent to a creditor and/or a shareholder that their financial position upon the resolution of the bank is below their presumed financial position had a liquidation decision been taken on the date the bank was placed under resolution, the creditors and/or shareholders may submit challenges to the Special Banking Court referred to in Article 29 of this Law within a maximum period of three months from the date of publication of the resolution decision. In cases where the entitlement of the creditor and/or shareholder is established, the Special Banking Court shall determine the value of the compensation representing the difference between what would have accrued to the creditor or shareholder as a result of the liquidation of the bank and what would accrue to them as a result of the resolution measures, and shall order the bank to pay it.

The Higher Banking Authority may reconsider the resolution measures such that the liabilities of the bank concerned include the differences determined by the Special Banking Court. In the event of using the internal rescue Bail-in as one of the rescue tools, this tool shall apply to customer deposits.

- The bank resolution tools shall be used until the bank becomes compliant with the minimum own funds adequacy requirements.

- Certain liabilities shall be excluded from the write-down or conversion into capital instruments mechanism as indicated in Annex No. 1 (Excluded Liabilities).

- The obligations of the bank linked to contingent

liabilities, including those relating to off-balance-sheet guarantees and credits, shall be cancelled where possible without additional risks and costs, and the cash collateral provided against them shall be released.

- Financial derivatives contracts shall be terminated and the remaining related liabilities, if any, shall be considered as unsecured liabilities, where possible without additional risks and costs.

- All suspense accounts shall be settled or netted.

- Set-off shall be carried out between funded facilities (i.e. on-balance-sheet facilities) and cash collateral and/or cash margins and/or the fair value of financial instruments (bonds, shares, etc., if any) given as collateral against these facilities, within the limit of the utilised amount of these facilities and subject to the existence of a legally enforceable set-off agreement and subject to the fulfilment of the offsetting criteria in accordance with International Accounting Standard No. 32. As for amounts exceeding the utilised amount of the facilities, they shall be subject to the bank resolution process.

The provisions of this Article shall apply following the enactment of the Law on Financial Regularisation and Recovery of Deposits.

Article Thirteen of Law No. 23 issued on 14/8/2025 (Law on the Reform of the Situation of Banks in Lebanon and their

Reorganisation) shall be amended to read as follows:

- It rests with the Higher Banking Commission to decide to apply any of the following tools for reforming the situation of the bank individually or together with other tools, by way of example and without limitation:

* Internal rescue Bail-in. Through writing down the value of own funds and liabilities and/or converting liabilities into capital instruments, the write-down mechanism consists in carrying out a partial or total reduction of the value of the elements of own funds and liabilities (including interest where applicable) in accordance with the hierarchy of liabilities and funds specified in Annex No. «1»

* Reconstituting the capital of the bank through the issuance of new shares to new investors with the possibility, and not the obligation, of accepting the participation of minority shareholders who are not major shareholders and do not hold control rights over the management of the bank in the stage prior to placing the bank under reform. All shareholders may exceptionally be involved in the recapitalisation only in the event of the enactment and application of the Law on Financial Regularisation and Recovery of Deposits.

* Transferring some or all of the assets, rights and liabilities of the bank to another institution.

* Carrying out a merger with another bank.

- The tools for reforming the situation of the bank shall be applied as specified in the decision to reform the situation issued by the Higher Banking Commission with respect to each bank in accordance with the provisions of Article 7 of this Law.

- The Higher Banking Commission may, with the approval of a two-thirds majority of its members, submit a recommendation to the Central Bank regarding all that is necessary to regulate the procedures for implementing this Law in accordance with due process.

Article Seventeen of Law No. 23 issued on 14/8/2025 (Law on the Resolution and Reorganisation of Banks in Lebanon) is amended so as to read as follows:

- A bank undergoing resolution shall remain under the supervision of the Banking Control Commission.

- In addition to the powers and responsibilities granted to the Banking Control Commission pursuant to other provisions in this Law and pursuant to other laws, the Banking Control Commission shall carry out the following:

* Preparing a provisional valuation of the bank and/or appointing an independent valuer in accordance with the provisions of Article 10 to value the bank.

* Sending a report to the Higher Banking Authority on the results of the valuation.

* Sending a recommendation to the Higher Banking Authority on whether the bank ought to be liquidated or resolved and proposing the necessary measures, including the bank resolution tools that must be adopted.

* Following up on the implementation of the bank resolution process and sending periodic reports to the Higher Banking Authority on compliance and non-compliance with the resolution decision.

* Conducting a fit and proper assessment of the new shareholders and the members appointed to the board of directors and/or senior management of the bank undergoing resolution.

* Reviewing the reports of the provisional administrator and sending any observations to the Higher Banking Authority when needed.

* Preparing the resolution plan for each bank and sending it to the Higher Banking Authority.

- The Banking Control Commission shall issue, as needed, instructions and technical requirements with a view to ensuring the proper implementation of its powers and responsibilities in accordance with this Law.

- The Banking Control Commission shall have the right to access all information necessary to implement the bank resolution process and to exercise its powers and responsibilities in accordance with this Law.

- The Banking Control Commission shall submit a report on the foregoing to the Higher Banking Authority.

Article Sixteen of Law No. 23 issued on 14/8/2025 (Law on the Resolution and Reorganisation of Banks in Lebanon) is amended to read as follows:

- The Higher Banking Commission shall have authority over the bank and the said Commission shall exercise its powers in part or in whole, without need for the consent of the shareholders of the bank under resolution, its creditors, its Board of Directors, its Senior Management, or any other counterparty, and in particular such that the Commission's decision shall not be contingent upon the consent of any other authority.

- The powers of the Higher Banking Commission shall include the following:

* Taking all decisions relating to the management of the bank and those vested in the General Assembly of Shareholders.

* Appointing a temporary administrator in accordance with the provisions of Title 8 of this Law.

* Dismissing and/or replacing and/or appointing one or more or all members of the Board of Directors, or requiring the bank to do so, whether the member or members are executive/non-executive or independent.

* Dismissing and/or replacing and/or appointing one or more or all members of the Senior Management, or requiring the bank to do so.

* Approving the bank resolution plan prepared/updated periodically for each bank. This plan shall not be binding on the Higher Banking Commission or a precondition for resolution in accordance with this Law.

* Amending the Articles of Association, including increasing or reducing the capital, issuing debt instruments, or taking any other measures required by the resolution process without being bound to follow the procedures provided for in other laws, in particular the Code of Commerce.

* Imposing the necessary measures to remove impediments to the resolvability of the bank, including, without limitation:

- Requiring the bank to sell assets, including its assets abroad.

- Requiring the bank to limit or cease certain existing operations and business activities.

- Requiring the bank to change its legal or operational structure, including reorganising the ownership structure.

- Initiating the bank resolution process and deciding on its duration where necessary.

* Imposing the application of resolution measures and tools on the bank.

* Amending the maturity date of debt instruments and other liabilities of the bank (including deposits), or amending the amount of interest and/or principal payable on such instruments and other liabilities, or the maturity date of the interest and/or principal where necessary.

* Suspending trading in listed capital instruments issued by the bank, where applicable, and/or deferring market disclosure requirements after coordination with the competent authority.

* Imposing the principle of temporary suspension (Moratorium) for a period of 3 months and staying the effects of existing and future legal proceedings for a maximum period of 8 months where necessary.

* Requiring third parties to continue providing essential services to the bank under resolution in accordance with the terms and conditions existing prior to the resolution of the bank.

* Imposing a suspension of early termination rights by prohibiting the enforcement of contractual clauses relating to financial lease, service, or licence agreements that allow the counterparty of the bank under resolution to exercise set-off, accelerate payment of obligations, or terminate such contracts upon the initiation of the bank resolution process.

The suspension of early termination rights relating to financial contracts must not exceed a period of 3 days.

Early termination rights enjoyed by the counterparty against the bank under resolution shall be preserved in the event of any default unrelated to the initiation of the bank resolution process before or after the suspension period.

* Prohibiting the payment of any dividends to holders of capital instruments or the distribution of other capital gains to them, and any kind of payments to members of the Board of Directors and senior managers, other than the basic remuneration paid to Senior Management.

* Imposing the clawback of funds paid to members of the Board of Directors or Senior Management in violation of the law, the circulars of the Banque du Liban, or the rules of good governance, for a preceding period of 10 years.

* Imposing the clawback of any funds transferred to other parties in a discriminatory or unfair manner that prejudiced the rights of other depositors or creditors who were unable to make similar transfers after 17 October 2019

* Striking the concerned bank off the list of banks of the Banque du Liban in accordance with the cases specified in this Law, and thereafter appointing a liquidator or a liquidation committee in accordance with Article 24 of this Law.

* Bringing an action in the name and on behalf of the bank, or requiring the bank or the temporary administrator to bring an action before the competent Lebanese courts and/or any competent foreign court in other countries, against major shareholders, members of the Board of Directors and Senior Management, authorised signatories, and auditors who held their positions at the concerned bank

in the ten years preceding the date of issuance of the resolution decision, where there are reasonable grounds to suspect the involvement of any of those persons in a civil wrong or criminal offence.

* Without prejudice to the application of the preceding paragraph of this Article with respect to auditing unlawful transactions, the Higher Banking Commission may require the temporary administrator to exercise the powers granted to the liquidator provided for in Article 25 of this Law relating to auditing transactions that generated unjustified profits and benefits in favour of third parties and/or related or close parties as defined in the circulars of the Banque du Liban, and to work to recover and collect such funds in favour of the bank.

Such transactions shall include, for example, those provided for in Article 25, and the look-back period for pursuing such transactions in the event of resolution may be applied in a manner similar to that provided for in Article 25 relating to liquidation proceedings, starting from the date the bank is placed under resolution.

* Giving instructions to the liquidator / liquidation committee in the event of liquidation (as defined by Article 25 of this Law).

- Without prejudice to the application of Article 14 of this Law relating to compensation in favour of the creditor/shareholder for the resulting difference determined by the Special Court, the Higher Banking Commission may depart from the general principle requiring equal treatment of creditors within the same class, only if the non-application of this principle is necessary for financial stability or if the non-application of this principle is in the interest of the creditors as a whole.

The Higher Banking Commission may also depart from this principle if it would bring about the following cases in particular:

a - Converting deposits into shares or writing down value for the purpose of bail-in within a short period so as to prevent the loss of resolution opportunities for the bank,

b - Securing the requirements for the continuity of the critical functions and activities of the bank under resolution,

c - Avoiding the occurrence of a systemic or sectoral crisis due to the failure to resolve the bank,

d - Preventing deterioration in value resulting from the measures taken which would cause the losses of other creditors resulting from the application of the principle of equality to exceed the losses resulting from the non-application of this principle.

The Higher Banking Commission may conduct a reversal operation, in part or in whole, of any write-down or write-up in value and/or of other resolution tools, where necessary. In such case, the Higher Banking Commission may decide to write up the value of the claims of creditors and/or shareholders that should not have been subjected to the write-down and/or other bank resolution tools. The reversal operation shall be carried out in accordance with Annex No. 1 (Hierarchy of Own Funds and Creditors).

Article nineteen of Law No. 23 issued on 14/8/2025 (Law on the Reform of the Status of Banks in Lebanon and their

Reorganisation) shall be amended so as to read as follows:

- The Higher Banking Commission shall appoint a temporary administrator for a pre-determined period of time renewable by this Commission and shall delegate to him the powers of managing the affairs of the bank whose status is being reformed and the powers of the Board of Directors. The temporary administrator shall exercise any power related to the reform of the status of the bank on the basis of a written decision from the Higher Banking Commission which defines, with respect to each bank, the powers of the temporary administrator, the scope of his work, his duties, the duration of his appointment, and his obligations towards the Higher Banking Commission.

The temporary administrator or the liquidator shall revert to the Higher Banking Commission in any decision requiring the approval of the General Assembly, and the Commission may grant approval or delegate the powers of the General Assembly to take the appropriate decision

- The decision appointing the temporary administrator issued by the Higher Banking Commission shall be registered in the Commercial Register, and shall be published in the Official Gazette, in a newspaper of wide circulation in Lebanon, and on the electronic website of the Bank of Lebanon.

- The Higher Banking Commission shall determine the remuneration of the temporary administrator, and the bank concerned shall bear the full expenses.

- The Higher Banking Commission may, if it deems it necessary, dismiss the temporary administrator at any time whatsoever, and it may appoint a replacement for him for the remainder of his term.

- The same person may not be appointed as a temporary administrator for more than one bank.

Article eighteen of Law No. 23 issued on 14/8/2025 (Law on the Reform of the Status of Banks in Lebanon and their Reorganization) shall be amended to read as follows:

- The Capital Markets Authority, the Insurance Control Commission, the Central Bank of Lebanon, the Banking Control Commission, the Commercial Register, the Real Estate Register, central deposit institutions, the National Deposit Guarantee Institution, and any other parties concerned with the application of the provisions of this Law must cooperate with the Higher Banking Authority, and coordination shall take place with the Ministry of Finance in all matters that the Authority deems necessary.

- Each of the above parties shall provide the Higher Banking Authority, within the time limit set by the latter, with the necessary data, recommendations, and approvals.

- The Higher Banking Authority shall consult the Central Council of the Central Bank of Lebanon, in line with its functions, regarding financial stability issues that may arise.

- The Central Council of the Central Bank of Lebanon shall send a recommendation to the Higher Banking Authority within a time limit set by this Authority.

- The Authority shall exercise all powers not assigned to any other authority and relating to the framework of implementation of this Law.

Article Twenty-One of Law No. 23 issued on 14/8/2025 (Law on the Reform of the Status of Banks in Lebanon and their Reorganization) is amended to read as follows:

- The provisional administrator shall exercise the powers vested in him by the Higher Banking Commission in the written decision defining the scope of his work, and his work shall be under the supervision of the Higher Banking Commission.

- The provisional administrator shall have unrestricted management over the properties, offices, assets, accounting books, and other records of the concerned bank, and he shall also have the right of access to all information necessary for the performance of his duties.

- It is within the power of the provisional administrator to dismiss any of the managers and/or responsible employees, and to appoint a replacement for them.

- The provisional administrator shall, at least quarterly and as needed, submit a report to the Higher Banking Commission, with a copy thereof to the Banking Control Commission, regarding the work accomplished, the development of the conditions of the concerned bank, and the action plan to be completed. In addition, and in the event that the difficulties of the bank persist, he shall submit to the Higher Banking Commission a report identifying the nature, source, and significance of the obstacles, as well as the additional measures that would improve the status of the concerned bank.

- The provisional administrator is required to submit a report to the Higher Banking Commission, with a copy thereof to the Banking Control Commission, regarding any malpractice that becomes apparent to him to have occurred during the term of his appointment.

- The Higher Banking Commission shall review the acts and decisions taken by the provisional administrator and shall have the absolute discretion as to the nature and seriousness of the transgression committed in the exercise of the powers of the administrator or the liquidator, and to take the measures it deems appropriate within 10 days from the date of its taking cognizance thereof, being notified thereof, or being petitioned by any party.

Article Twenty of Law No. 23 issued on 14/8/2025 (Law on the Reform of the Situation of Banks in Lebanon and their Reorganisation) is amended to read as follows:

The provisional administrator must:

- Possess extensive professional experience of not less than twenty years in the banking and financial fields, with administrative experience and in-depth knowledge of the financial and banking laws and regulations in force.

- Be independent from the bank whose situation is being reformed.

Possess a clean judicial record (no criminal conviction),

And not have been dismissed from any administrative position or subjected to sanctions by the Banque du Liban or by the Banking Control Commission.

The criteria of independence shall include the following:

* That he has not been, directly or indirectly, among the shareholders of the bank or its affiliated institutions in the five years preceding his appointment.

* That he has not, directly or indirectly, held in the five years preceding his appointment the position of member of the board of directors or senior management or adviser at the bank or its affiliated institutions

* That neither he nor any of his family members is a borrower from the bank or from its affiliated institutions for more than 100 thousand US dollars

* That neither he nor any of his family members is a depositor (for more than 100 thousand US dollars) with the bank or its affiliated institutions.

* That he has no relationship of kinship up to the fourth degree with a shareholder or a member of the board of directors or senior management at the bank or its affiliated institutions.

* Any other criteria that may negatively affect his independence directly or indirectly.

- The bank shall not be entitled to participate in a transaction if the provisional administrator has a fundamental interest in or relationship with it (directly or indirectly), and such transaction may exceptionally be conducted only after prior written approval from the Higher Banking Commission.

- Disclose to the Higher Banking Commission the existence of an interest or relationship that conflicts with the principle of independence and non-conflict of interest, and in the event that he refrains from disclosing as required, the Higher Banking Commission shall have the authority to dismiss him.

Article Twenty-Four of Law No. 23 issued on 14/8/2025 (Law on Reforming the Status of Banks in Lebanon and Their Reorganization) is amended so as to read as follows:

The Higher Banking Commission shall appoint, within thirty days from the issuance of the delisting decision, a liquidator or a liquidation committee of six

members, according to the size of the bank concerned, provided that this committee includes:

* A member representing the creditors.

* A member representing the shareholders.

* A member representing the depositors.

* An expert in banking or financial affairs.

* A legal expert.

* The Chairman of the National Institute for the Guarantee of Deposits or a representative appointed by this Chairman.

The Higher Banking Commission shall appoint from among these members a chairman for this committee and shall determine his powers. The chairman shall carry out the daily business related to the liquidation process. Furthermore, the conclusion of any settlement agreement or any sale or liquidation operation of the bank's assets Regarding which a decision is taken by the liquidation committee shall not become effective except after obtaining a written approval from the Higher Banking Commission.

The liquidation committee shall convene at the request of its chairman or two (2) of its members. It shall take its decisions by a majority of its members. The chairman shall represent the committee before third parties, when necessary.

In the event that a vacancy occurs in the composition of the committee (death, resignation, health conditions...), the Higher Banking Commission shall appoint a replacement within a reasonable period not exceeding 15 days.

- The liquidator/ any member of the liquidation committee is required:

* To possess the required qualifications in accordance with best practices, particularly with respect to the standards of integrity, competence, independence, and professional experience in his field of specialization.

* Not to have any connection or relationship of any kind, professional or personal, that may expose him to a conflict of interest, or affect in any manner whatsoever his independence and his decision during the performance of the tasks entrusted to him.

* That neither he nor any of his family members be a borrower or a depositor (more than 100 thousand US dollars) with the bank or the institutions linked to it.

* Not to be a current or former member of the board of directors or senior management or an advisor with the council concerned under liquidation or any of the institutions linked to it, during the five years preceding his appointment.

* Not to have conducted an audit of the accounts of the bank under liquidation, during the two years preceding the delisting decision.

* Not to have a relationship of kinship of the fourth degree with any shareholder or member of the board of directors.

- The Higher Banking Commission shall determine the fees of the chairman and members of the liquidation committee, and the bank shall bear the costs.

The decision appointing the liquidator/ liquidation committee shall be published in the Official Gazette and in at least one local newspaper and on the website of the Higher Banking Commission and/or the Banque du Liban and/or the Banking Control Commission.

Article Twenty-Three of Law No. 23 issued on 14/8/2025 (Law on the Reform of the Situation of Banks in Lebanon and their Reorganisation) is amended to read as follows:

The Higher Banking Authority may delist any bank in the following two cases:

1 - Prior to commencing the process of reforming the situation of the bank: following the receipt of an evaluation report from the Banking Control Commission recommending liquidation on the basis of the criteria of default or likelihood of default and the impossibility of rehabilitating the bank through measures for reforming the situation of the bank, provided that

the bank is given the right to submit any defences or demonstrate facts supported by evidentiary documents contradicting the submitted report, in person before the Higher Banking Authority within a maximum period of 15 days.

2 - At any time after commencing the process of reforming the situation of the bank:

a - Following the receipt by the Authority of an evaluation report from the Banking Control Commission concluding that the bank is in default or likely to default despite the attempt to rehabilitate it by means of measures for reforming the situation of the bank.

b - Following the receipt by the Authority of an evaluation report from the interim administrator highlighting the necessity of liquidating the concerned bank.

- The delisting decision shall be based on Articles 140, 208, 209, 208, and 209 of the Lebanese Code of Money and Credit. In this case, the provisions of Article 141 of the Code of Money and Credit shall apply, and the concerned bank shall be deemed under liquidation, provided that it is liquidated in accordance with the liquidation provisions set forth in this Law.
