- Following the delisting decision, the Higher Banking Authority shall appoint a liquidator or a liquidation committee, depending on the size of the bank under liquidation.

- All liquidation operations shall be referred to the Second Chamber for the application of the provisions of this Law, and the provisions of Title 9 of this Law shall apply exclusively to the liquidation process and shall supersede any other laws and regulations that conflict with their content.

- Once the bank comes under liquidation, it must always use the phrase "Under Liquidation" alongside its name, particularly in its correspondence with third parties, until the completion of the liquidation process.

- The principle of suspension (Moratorium) shall be imposed for a period of 3 months, and the effects of existing and future legal proceedings shall be stayed for a period of 8 months where necessary, with the exception of those relating to the proof of rights and the perfection of guarantees.

- After the date of issuance of the delisting decision and the commencement of the liquidation process, and in the event of serious grounds to suspect that any of the major shareholders, members of the board of directors, senior management, authorised signatories, and auditors who held their positions at the bank under liquidation during the ten years preceding the date of issuance of the delisting decision have been involved in

a civil or criminal offence, the liquidator / liquidation committee and/or the Higher Banking Authority must:

* Notify the persons mentioned above of the obligation to refrain from disposing of all or part of their movable and immovable property and their bank accounts, and place a restraint on disposal notation thereon in addition to a decision prohibiting them from travelling, provided that the effects of these measures do not exceed six non-renewable months.

- Request the competent courts in Lebanon or abroad to levy a precautionary attachment on all or part of the movable and immovable assets belonging to the aforementioned persons in accordance with the applicable Lebanese and foreign laws.

* Prosecute these persons before the competent Lebanese courts and/or any competent foreign court for the civil and/or criminal liability incurred by them pursuant to the applicable laws and regulations.

After either of the last two measures above is put into effect, the persons mentioned above shall be deemed to have waived the rights granted to them pursuant to the provisions of the Banking Secrecy Law, if any.

In the event that the temporary precautionary attachment is to be enforced, and upon the request of the liquidator / liquidation committee, the concerned major shareholders, members of the board of directors, senior management, authorised signatories, and auditors shall be required to provide the liquidator / liquidation committee, within ten working days from the request of the liquidator / liquidation committee, with a complete and detailed list of all movable and immovable assets in Lebanon and abroad that they own, under penalty of criminal prosecution and imprisonment for a period of three months, with the obligation to hand over what is required of them and holding them liable for the costs of obtaining the same through law firms appointed by the Higher Banking Authority.

Article Twenty-Six of Law No. 23 issued on 14/8/2025 (Law on Reforming the Status of Banks in Lebanon and Reorganising Them) is amended to read as follows:

Set-off by shareholders and creditors in the liquidation process shall be carried out in accordance with the rank specified in Annex No. «1» Hierarchy of Own Funds and Laws, provided that this is done on a pro rata basis within the same rank of own funds and within the same rank of liabilities in the bank subject to reform.

- Creditors within the same rank shall be treated equally in accordance with Annex No. 1 (principle of equality).

- Shareholders within the same rank shall be treated equally in accordance with Annex No. 1 (principle of equality)

- The single depositor concept shall apply to customer deposits in the concerned bank under reform or under liquidation and within the category specified in Table No. 1

- Set-off between debit accounts and credit accounts shall be carried out in accordance with the conditions referred to in Article 14 of this Law.

- The bank's obligations linked to contingent, existing or valid liabilities and contracts shall be cancelled where possible without risk and additional cost, and the guarantees provided against them shall be released.

- Financial derivatives contracts shall be terminated where possible without risk and additional cost, and the remaining related liabilities, if any, shall be considered as unsecured liabilities.

Article Twenty-Eight of Law No. 23 issued on 14/8/2025 (Law on Reforming the Status of Banks in Lebanon and Reorganising Them) is amended to read as follows:

In the event of the liquidation of a bank, deposits shall be covered in accordance with the criteria and provisions specified by this Law and the Law on Restoring Financial Regularity and Recovering Deposits, and the bylaws of the National Deposit Guarantee Institution with its amendments.

Article Twenty-Nine of Law No. 23 issued on 14/8/2025 (Law on Reforming the Situation of Banks in Lebanon and Reorganising Them) is amended so as to read as follows:

- The Special Court is established in accordance with Article 15 of Law No. 110 dated 7/11/1991, and this Court shall have jurisdiction to adjudicate applications for appeal submitted in execution of the provisions of this Law and to resolve any dispute arising between a creditor or a depositor on the one hand and the Liquidator/Liquidation Committee on the other concerning a debt or a deposit owed by the bank under liquidation.

- The Special Court shall hear all cases relating to the temporary precautionary attachment referred to in this Law.

- With the exception of an appeal before the competent Court of Appeal within a period of 20 days from the date of issuance of the final judgment, the decisions of the Special Court shall not be subject to any avenue of administrative or judicial recourse, whether ordinary or extraordinary.

Article Thirty-One of Law No. 23 issued on 14/8/2025 (Law on Reforming the Situation of Banks in Lebanon and Their Reorganization) shall be amended to read as follows:

All decisions issued by the Higher Banking Commission shall be subject to appeal before the Special Court established pursuant to Law No. 110 dated 11/7/1991 to examine the legality of the issued decisions, within a time limit of ten days:

- from the date of notifying the bank of the decision of the Higher Banking Commission,

- from the date the Commission publishes its decision on its electronic website, posts it at the bank's headquarters, or notifies the concerned parties thereof by registered mail, electronic mail, or any other means.

The rules of procedure before summary disposition courts provided for in the Code of Civil Procedure shall be followed before the Special Court.

An appeal before the competent court shall not stay the execution of the contested decision except by a decision of the court, in the event that there are manifest legal errors and that the immediate execution of the decision would cause serious losses and damages to the litigants.

The annulment of the contested decision shall not affect the validity of the measures taken to execute it, if the appeal would prejudice the rights legally acquired by a bona fide third party, in accordance with the provisions of the general laws in force.

The mere knowledge of the third party of the appeal shall not be deemed a sufficient reason in itself to consider the transactions carried out by such party as falling outside the scope of good faith.

The Commission must rectify the decision to conform with the law and in accordance with the judgments issued by the court. Litigants shall be compensated within the limits of the established losses incurred or estimated by the court, and the Commission may decide that the compensation be borne by the bank directly or through including the value in the category of senior liabilities of the harmed parties in the schedule of hierarchy of funds and creditors.

Article Twenty-Five of Law No. 23 issued on 14/8/2025 (Law on Reforming the Status of Banks in Lebanon and Their Reorganization) shall be amended so as to read as follows:

- Immediately upon the declaration of placing the bank under liquidation, the accrual of credit interest on deposit accounts, certificates of deposit, and debt instruments shall cease, with the exception of what is secured by guarantees and up to the value of such guarantees.

- The liquidator/liquidation committee shall submit to the Higher Banking Commission a liquidation plan for approval, comprising an organized timetable with a reasonable and specified time limit for the steps necessary to sell the bank's assets and distribute the proceeds thereof in accordance with the hierarchy of own funds and creditors referred to in Annex No. 1. The Higher Banking Commission shall approve this plan, monitor its implementation, and take the necessary measures in the event of any delay.

- The liquidator/liquidation committee shall act in good faith, with the necessary prudence and due diligence, in order to complete the liquidation process within the approved time limit.

- It shall be required that:

* The liquidator/liquidation committee exercise the powers granted thereto by the Higher Banking Commission under the supervision of this Commission, and refer to the Commission in advance in all matters relating to operations that involve additional risks, the liquidation of assets in large amounts, or large losses.

* The liquidator/liquidation committee assist the National Institute for the Guarantee of Deposits in the payment process.

* The liquidator/liquidation committee replace the board of directors of the concerned bank and its senior management in all decisions, following the written approval of the Higher Banking Commission.

* The liquidator/liquidation committee conduct a valuation of the concerned bank or request independent valuers to conduct a valuation or update a previous valuation when necessary.

* The liquidator/liquidation committee submit periodic reports to the Higher Banking Commission regarding the progress of the liquidation process at the concerned bank and submit, within a time limit specified by the Commission, any additional reports or information requested by this Commission.

* The liquidator/liquidation committee have the right of access to all information necessary for the exercise of his duties.

* The liquidator/the liquidated/liquidation committee have the following powers:

- Transferring some or all of the assets, rights, and liabilities of the bank to a third party, while observing the priority of liabilities in accordance with the hierarchy specified in Annex No. 1,

- Suspending or reducing interest on deposits, as well as increasing or reducing debts owed by the bank,

- Terminating, freezing, or amending contracts of dealing with suppliers and creditors if possible, in order to avoid the continuation of losses,

- Carrying out financial and/or forensic auditing works in order to preserve the interests and rights of the bank and execute liquidation operations,

- Undertaking prosecutions, instituting lawsuits, and exercising the right of action and the right of defense in preservation of the rights of the bank and in execution of the liquidation process,

- Negotiating in respect of compensations and obligations incurred by the bank as a result of the liquidation process, taking legal and administrative measures to preserve the funds of the bank, and relying on any legal provision contained in the laws in force in accordance with the provisions of Article 32 of this Law in order to complete the liquidation process under the supervision of the Higher Banking Commission.

- Terminating the services of certain employees or making recruitments required in order to complete the liquidation process, terminating or extending lease or service contracts, undertaking new measures that serve the liquidation process, and doing all that is required to regularize the status of the bank with official departments in accordance with the laws in force.

- Managing any incomplete sale or purchase transaction and completing it

in accordance with the interest of the bank and preventing any damages resulting therefrom.

- Assigning contracts concluded with third parties and taking whatever is necessary to prevent the continuation of additional expenses or losses within the laws governing such contracts.

- Without prejudice to the powers vested in the liquidator relating to unlawful operations or claims against any party pursuant to this Law, annulling/cancelling the following acts, which produced unjustified benefits at the expense of the interests of the creditors as a whole as at the date of placing the bank under liquidation or as at a prior date going back to 18 months before the date of placing the bank under liquidation, or for close or related parties in accordance with what is specified in the circulars of the Banque du Liban for a period of 36 months before the date of placing the bank under liquidation, and recovering and collecting the funds from the beneficiaries thereof or the equivalent of their value from the assets that were acquired by other parties in good faith, in particular:

• Donations, financial benefits without consideration, and gratuitous acts transferring funds, with the exception of what is within the limits of customary gifts or small presents.

• Establishing an endowment (waqf) and funds for charitable purposes

• Advance payments or settlements of unmatured debts, whatever their form

• Transferring ownership of real properties or assets in favor of specific creditors to the exclusion of others,

• Settlements of matured monetary debts by means other than money, transfers, or instruments, and in general any settlement by rendering a substitute,

• Establishing a consensual or judicial real property pledge/mortgage, a pledge of movables, or a pledge of exploitation over the assets of the bank to secure a prior debt,

• Structuring debts in a manner that leads to increasing the value of the funds that accrue to the creditor in the event of the liquidation of the bank

• Amending the interest rate or the yield on coupons during a period of 6 months before placing the bank under liquidation

• Operations in which the consideration provided by the bank far exceeds the consideration obtained by it

• Dividends and bonuses that were paid to shareholders and/or directors and that are not commensurate with the conditions of the bank as at the date of their approval and payment

The liquidator shall take urgent measures to annul these operations and within a time limit not exceeding one year from the date of placing the bank under liquidation, provided that the aforementioned operations and the preceding provisions shall not affect payments or transfers that took place in the ordinary course of business, or operations to the extent that they were part of a contemporaneous exchange for a reasonably equivalent value, or operations that were followed by the bank granting new credit facilities unsecured by the recipient, or operations that took place during the reform of the bank under the supervision of the interim director and the instructions of the Higher Banking Commission.

* The liquidator / liquidation committee abide by the instructions issued by the Higher Banking Commission and the circulars of the Banque du Liban that relate to the procedures for selling, liquidating, exchanging, using, or collecting the financial or in-kind assets of the bank. The liquidator/liquidation committee shall also abide by the procedures for distributing the proceeds to depositors and creditors in accordance with what is mentioned in Article 26 of this Law.

Article Thirty-Two of Law No. 23 issued on 14/8/2025 (Law on the Reform of the Status of Banks in Lebanon and their Reorganisation) is amended to read as follows:

- Notwithstanding any other provision, the provisions of this Law shall prevail over

all provisions conflicting with its provisions and inconsistent therewith.

- In all matters not specified by this Law, the Higher Banking Commission and the Special Court shall apply the mechanisms and procedures specified in general laws and special laws, particularly the Law of the Code of Land Commerce (Bankruptcy Chapter) and the Code of Obligations and Contracts or other laws relating to liquidation and merger in force, and in a manner commensurate with the objectives, nature and requirements of the implementation of the reform and liquidation tools.

- The provisions of Article 3 of Law 192/1993 shall apply with respect to the exchange of information from the parties in all matters relating to the implementation of the reform tools.

Any party that fails to comply immediately with the provisions of this Law or otherwise obstructs the work of the Higher Banking Commission or the Interim Administrator in the course of performing their duties shall be subject to a fine the value of which shall be assessed by the Higher Banking Commission, provided that it shall not be less than 300 times the minimum wage in Lebanon. The Higher Banking Commission shall be the competent authority that decides whether there is a violation of its decisions or non-compliance with the provisions of this Law

Article Thirty-Four of Law No. 23 issued on 14/8/2025 (Law on the Resolution and Reorganisation of Banks in Lebanon) is amended to read as follows:

In the performance of their duties or in respect of any act or omission occurring during the exercise of their powers and responsibilities provided for in this Law, the Higher Banking Authority, the Banking Control Commission, the Temporary Administrator, the Liquidator/Liquidation Committee, and any of the individuals or institutions contracted by the Control Commission or the Banque du Liban to perform the tasks required within the framework of resolution or liquidation shall incur no liability, unless a final and binding judgment is rendered proving that the act or omission was committed in bad faith or resulted from fraud, negligence, or gross fault on their part. The Higher Banking Authority shall bear the indemnification for the costs of legal actions brought against it or against any of its members, employees, or representatives, and the Banking Control Commission shall bear the indemnification for the costs of legal actions brought

against it or against any of its members, employees, or representatives, except in the case of the final and binding judgment referred to above.

No liability shall attach to the employees of the bank undergoing resolution as a result of their compliance with the decisions of the Higher Banking Authority. In such case, they shall be protected against any judicial proceeding or lawsuit brought against them.

Article Thirty-Six of Law No. 23 issued on 14/8/2025 (Law on the Reform of the Status of Banks in Lebanon and their Reorganisation) is amended to read as follows:

All banks must have met the following:

* The applicable minimum own funds requirements, provided that the banks' assets with the Banque du Liban are considered at book value prior to any provisions for potential losses on placements with the Banque du Liban, and investments in Eurobonds are considered on the basis of net value after taking into account the expected loss rate determined by the Banque du Liban.

* The minimum liquidity requirements, provided that the bank's assets with the Banque du Liban are considered within book maturities with the rescheduling of deposit maturities by the bank.

These prudential requirements shall be amended in accordance with the Financial Regularisation and Deposit Recovery Law that allows for the restoration of balance to financial regularity in Lebanon provided for in Article 37 of this Law and immediately upon its issuance. And in a manner commensurate with international standards for measuring capital adequacy and liquidity as determined by the monetary authority

- Banks identified by the Banking Control Commission as non-compliant with the above requirements must remedy their breaches through mechanisms including:

** Injecting own funds, and

* Increasing their liquidity

- This Article shall be repealed immediately upon the issuance of the Financial Regularisation and Deposit Recovery Law.

This Law shall be published in the Official Gazette and its implementation shall be suspended until the enactment and publication of the Financial Regularity and Deposit Recovery Law.

The annual school budget, imposed pursuant to Law No. 11/81 dated 13 May 1981, shall consist of two balanced chapters, one of which is for expenditures and the second for revenues. For the purpose of determining the school tuition fee, no account shall be taken of any expenditure that does not fall within the framework of the elements specified in the following Chapter of Expenditures.

First: In the Chapter of Expenditures:

This chapter shall comprise the following elements:

A - Salaries, wages, and their accessories:

1- Salaries due in accordance with the law and their legal accessories pertaining to members of the teaching staff in private schools, plus, and until the issuance of a new law determining the scale of ranks and salaries for members of the teaching staff in private schools, the additional wages and aid granted to members of the teaching staff as compensation for the collapse of the Lebanese currency.

2- Wages and their legal accessories, pertaining to members of the teaching staff not included in the permanent cadre and calculated on the basis of what is due to those included in the permanent cadre who hold the same certificate and provide the same working hours, with due regard to the provisions of Article 4 of the Law of 15 June 1956 and its amendments and with due regard to seniority, plus, and until the issuance of a new law determining the scale of ranks and salaries for members of the teaching staff in private schools, the additional wages and aid granted to members of the teaching staff as compensation for the collapse of the Lebanese currency.

3 - Wages provided for those included in the permanent cadre in consideration of educational teaching assignments exceeding their weekly working quota and calculated on the basis of what is due to them in accordance with the provisions of the preceding Paragraph <1>, provided that the total of their working hours in the school does not exceed the working schedule in force therein, within the limit of thirty-five teaching hours per week.

4 - Additions to salaries and wages, provided for rewarding members of the teaching staff in the school or assisting them, provided that their total does not exceed fifteen percent (15%) of the total of the preceding Paragraphs 1, 2, and 3.

5 - Wages pertaining to members of the administrative staff, employees, and all other persons connected with the progress of work in the school, who are subject to the Labour Law, or who are not covered by the provisions of the Law of 15 June 1956 and its amendments.

B - Charges other than salaries and wages, incurred by the school pursuant to laws and regulations in favour of the workers therein who were mentioned in Item (A), which are specifically the contribution of the school to the Compensation Fund for members of the teaching staff in private schools, the family allowance for them, the subscriptions of the school to the National Social Security Fund, and the transportation allowance.

C - All other expenditures and charges such as the expenditures and charges of insurance, medical supervision, and administrative expenses including water, electricity, telephone, fuel oil, rents, maintenance, and cleaning, and other general expenses, as well as depreciations, expenditures of renewal and development, compensations to the holder of the school licence, and aid to needy pupils.

The total of Items (A) and (B) must represent at least sixty-five percent (65%) of the total of Items (A), (B), and (C), and Item (C) must represent at most thirty-five percent (35%) of this total.

The total of Paragraphs 1, 2, 3, and 4 of Item (A), with the exception of the legal accessories, must correspond to the total of the schedule of salaries and wages submitted to the management of the Compensation Fund for members of the teaching staff in private schools, with due regard to the provisions of Item D- 1- with respect to what exceeds the maximum limits referred to in Paragraphs 3 and 4 of Item (A).

D-

1- Expenditures that exceed the maximum limits provided for in the two preceding paragraphs of Item (A) - 3 with respect to additional working hours and 4 with respect to the 15% ratio resulting from acquired rights, in which case the budget must be accompanied by a report of an auditor affiliated with the Lebanese Association of Certified Public Accountants.

2 - The municipal fee on the rental value.

3 - Education grants for members of the teaching staff not exempted by Article Six of this Law and education grants for all other persons connected with the progress of work in the school, including administrators, employees, and others, in accordance with the provisions of Decree No. 6263 dated 18/01/1995 with respect to this category.

4 - Notice compensation and an allocation for the reserve of dismissal compensation, and for the purpose of applying the provisions of this paragraph, dismissal compensation means the total wages of the members of the teaching staff not included in the permanent cadre for the last month of the school year that is the subject of the budget, with the required adjustments.

5 - What was paid in legal compensations for the preceding year to members of the teaching staff included in the permanent cadre and dismissed in accordance with the provisions of Articles 26 and 29 of the Law of 15 June 1956 and its amendments, and in compensations to them in consideration of the termination of their additional assignments.

6 - What was paid in settlement amounts for the preceding year to adjust the end-of-service indemnity of those subject to the Labour Law.

Second: In the Chapter of Revenues:

Revenues shall consist of the total school tuition fees parallel to the total elements of the Chapter of Expenditures specified in First of this Article.

46 - Outside the cadre - Affiliation to the Cooperative - Placement on non-active status (isti'da'): In the matter relating to the affiliation of an employee placed outside the cadre regarding the benefits of the Cooperative, the Civil Service Board replied by its Letter No. 3924 dated 19/2/2004 addressed to the State Employees' Cooperative as follows: Whereas the Civil Service Board, in Paragraph (2) of Item (First) of its Letter No. 2783 dated 23/9/2003, had previously considered that an employee placed outside the cadre does not lose his affiliation to the Cooperative, but rather his benefit from the effects of such affiliation, and consequently the benefit from all the benefits of the Cooperative, is suspended in accordance with the decisions issued in this regard by the Board of Directors of the State Employees' Cooperative. Consequently, the subject of the benefit of employees placed outside the cadre from these benefits does not require amending Article (3) of the Draft Law promulgated by Decree No. 14273/63, but rather reconsidering - where necessary - the decisions issued in this regard by the Board of Directors of the Cooperative. And whereas it appears that the Civil Service Board, by its Letter No. 2031 dated 14/6/2001, and in the course of stating its opinion regarding the possibility of employees placed outside the cadre or on non-active status benefiting from the benefits of the Cooperative, had previously expressed the following: 1 - That the position of this Board (relating to the refusal of the benefit of employees

placed on non-active status or outside the cadre from the benefits of the Cooperative) was based on the two decisions of the Board of Directors of the State Employees' Cooperative No. 790 dated 17/6/1972 (subsequently amended pursuant to Board of Directors Decision No. 208/2002 dated 5/8/ 2002) and No. 845 dated 14/10/1972, which provide that employees in the two aforementioned cases shall not benefit from the benefits of the Cooperative. 2 - That the State Employees' Cooperative is one of the public institutions that enjoy moral personality and financial and administrative autonomy, and consequently the competence to take a decision in this regard belongs to the Board of Directors of the said Cooperative pursuant to the general principles and rules governing public institutions, and consequently the Civil Service Board considered, by its Letter No. 3504 dated 5/7 /1999, that the subject of the benefit of employees (placed outside the cadre or on non-active status) from the benefits of the Cooperative requires

submission to the Board of Directors of the State Employees' Cooperative to take the appropriate decision thereon. Accordingly, the Civil Service Board concluded at the time that the competence to amend the two decisions of the Board of Directors of the Cooperative No. 790/72 and No. 845/72 belongs to the said Board of Directors in light of the data and statistics available to it, so that consideration may thereafter be given to the possibility of approving such amendment by the Civil Service Board in its capacity as the supervisory authority over the Cooperative, and subject to the following conditions: 1 - Affiliation to the Cooperative. 2 - Payment of the due deductions. 3 - Not benefiting from any similar assistance from any other official or private source. And whereas it appears that the Board of Directors of the Cooperative issued on 5/ 8/2002 Decision No. 208/2002, coupled with the approval of the supervisory authority by its Decision No. 3 dated 20/2/2003, providing that an employee placed on non-active status ex officio for health reasons, or upon his request due to suffering a grave accident or by reason of the illness of his spouse or one of his descendants, shall benefit from the benefits of the Cooperative subject to specific conditions in the aforementioned Decision No. 208/2002. Therefore, the Committee of the Civil Service Board saw fit to confirm the content of its Letter No. 2031 dated 14/6/2001 and that the Board of Directors of the Cooperative has the competence to take the decision on the issue of the benefit of employees placed outside the cadre or on non-active status from the benefits of the Cooperative subject to the following conditions: 1 - Affiliation to the Cooperative. 2 - Payment of the due deductions. 3 - Not benefiting from any similar assistance from any other official or private source. And this in light of the data and statistics available to it, provided that the said decision is submitted for the approval of this Board in accordance with the rules in its capacity as the supervisory authority over the Cooperative, so that it may take the appropriate decision thereon in light of the explanatory and justifying reasons.

Building Envelope:

Without the possibility of exceeding the maximum height specified in the regulations of the zone in which the plot is located, and in the absence of special provisions relating to the building envelope, the construction of a building shall be subject to the following conditions:

First - Building Envelope on Roads

A - The Building Envelope on Roads:

Buildings shall be erected within a maximum envelope line defined as follows:

A - 1 - By a vertical line erected on the boundary of the public road or on the boundary of the alignment, the height of which is equal to two and a half times the width of the road or the width prescribed for its approved alignment, with a minimum of 15 metres.

Where there is a setback easement imposed on one side or on both sides of the road or the alignment, the vertical line shall be erected at the setback limit on the side of the plot. The distance between the two lines of the imposed setback shall be deemed to be the width of the road for determining the height.

(Refer to Drawing No. 21)

The level of the pavement, or of the road in the absence of a pavement, or the level of the longitudinal section of the alignment at the middle of the facade, shall be taken as the starting point on the said vertical line.

On sloping roads, if the height between the two ends of the facade exceeds three and a half metres, the facade shall be divided into sections where the height between the two ends of each does not exceed three and a half metres, and a vertical line shall be taken at the middle of each section separately.

A - 2 - By an inclined line extending from the upper end of the vertical line towards the interior of the plot, inclined to the horizontal line at a ratio of 5/2 (two base to five height).

(Refer to Drawing No. 22)

A - 3 - Where the road is perpendicular to the facade of the plot, the road envelope shall apply only to the sections contiguous to and facing the road in accordance with Drawing 22 - B

(Drawing No. 22 - B in accordance with Decree 617 /2007 for insertion).

B - The Building Envelope on a Square:

If the plot has a facade on a square, the width of the widest road branching off from the square together with its imposed setbacks shall be adopted to determine the height of the vertical lines on this square and on the roads branching off from it to a depth of 30m from the limits of the setback from the square.

(Refer to Drawing No. 23)

C - Building Envelope of Rear Buildings:

If two or more buildings are erected within a single plot, including one or more buildings on the road and one or more rear buildings separated from the first by an internal courtyard and overlooking the road over the roof of the first building, such rear buildings may benefit from the road envelope line, provided that the separating distance between the two buildings is not less than 4.5 m and that the height of the buildings standing on the road does not exceed five times the distance separating them from the rear buildings (the width of the courtyard) within the maximum limits of the envelope.

This height shall be measured starting from the lowest point of the facades of the two buildings in contact with the final ground of the courtyard after levelling, provided that the courtyard is legal in accordance with Item "Second" of this Article.

(Refer to Drawing No. 24)

D - The Building Envelope on the Corner of Two or More Roads:

Where the plot is located on the corner of two or more roads, there shall be applied at each intersection, and for a length not exceeding thirty metres (30m) for a part of the building facade (including projections) located on the narrower road, (the choice of its positioning being left to the designer), the following envelope shall apply:

1 - A vertical line erected on the alignment of the public road equal to five times the prescribed width of the road.

Where there is a setback easement imposed on one side or both sides of the road, the vertical line shall be erected on the limits of the setback on the side of the plot, and the distance between the two lines of the imposed setback shall be deemed to be the width of the road for determining the height. The starting point of the height of this vertical line shall be taken as defined for the vertical line pertaining to Paragraph "A" of Item "First" of this Article.

2 - An inclined line extending from the upper end of the vertical line and inclined to the horizontal line at a ratio of 1/5 (one base to five height) towards the interior of the plot.

The maximum height of the building must not exceed the height resulting from the application of the envelope of the wider road, and the envelope line pertaining to the narrower road and defined in Paragraph "A" of Item "First" of this Article shall apply to the remaining parts of the facade overlooking this road.

(Refer to Drawings No. 25 and No. 26)

3 - In the event that the plot is located on two roads of the same width, the owner of the plot shall have the option of adopting the return on either of the two roads, provided that the larger setback is complied with at the corner of the two roads in accordance with Drawing 22 - C

(Drawing No. 22 - C in accordance with the Decree in force 617 /2007 for insertion)

Where the plot is surrounded by roads on three or more sides, no return of any road shall be adopted on a road that does not intersect with it; however, it is permitted to exempt the section of the building located within a depth of 30m from the limits of the setback from the widest road from the envelope pertaining to the road on the opposite side, provided that the envelope and the return referred to above on the side roads are complied with.

(Refer to Drawing No. 27)

E - Exceptional envelope cases not mentioned above shall be decided upon by the Higher Council for Urban Planning.

Second - Height of Buildings on Courtyards:

In the event that a line of sight is secured onto courtyards, the buildings or sections of buildings lit from these courtyards shall be erected within a maximum envelope line as follows:

1 - By a vertical line erected on the building facade without projections on the envelope line on the side of the courtyard, equal to five times the minimum distance of the actual line of sight secured in the building from the rooms ventilated and lit from the courtyard belonging to the plot or from the joint courtyards with the neighbouring plots. This distance shall be measured between the vertical line erected in contact with the facade at the axis of the opening that lights and ventilates the room and the vertical line prescribed on the boundaries of the plot or another vertical line (with due regard to the text of Article Nine), within the field of the line of sight and on the axis of the opening (window, glass door, or glass facade), from the most prominent point of the building structure opposite the opening.

The level of the final ground after levelling at the lowest point at its intersection with the facade in each independent courtyard shall be taken as the starting point for this vertical line, regardless of the level of the ramp pertaining to the garage.

(Refer to Drawings No. 28 and 29)

Where the line of sight is secured onto a joint courtyard with the neighbouring plots, the facade of the rooms, or the edge of the veranda, loggia, or balcony supported by it, for which the range of the line of sight is secured, must be at a distance of at least four and a half metres from the opposite boundaries of the joint courtyard.

(Refer to Drawing No. 30)

Underneath joint courtyards encumbered by an easement of non-building or of light and air, the construction of backfilled basements is permitted if this does not conflict with the special conditions that required their establishment and with the building regulations in the zone, subject to compliance with the provisions of Item 2 - D of Article Nine of this Decree.

A courtyard shall be deemed legal for taking the range of the line of sight onto it when its area is not less than 30 m2 (thirty square metres) and it accommodates a rectangle whose minimum dimensions are 4.50 * 5.50m. (four and a half metres x five and a half metres).

A courtyard shall be deemed independent as long as it does not connect with other courtyards, or if it connects with other courtyards by a width of less than 4.50m. (four and a half metres).

(Refer to Drawings No. 31 - A and 31 - B)

2 - By an inclined line of 1/5 (one base to five height) extending from the upper end of the vertical line.

(Refer to Drawings No. 28 and No. 29)

The width of watercourses, canals, or public domain contiguous to legal courtyards shall not be included in the calculation of the height of the envelope on these courtyards.

A - Subject to the provisions of Article 422 and the application of the penalty prescribed in Article 423, the following offences shall entail the seizure and confiscation of smuggled goods:

1- Provisions common to all goods

- No. 1- The importation or attempted importation of prohibited, monopolised, restricted or dutiable goods by way of smuggling or without a manifest or without a customs declaration.

- No. 2- A false declaration as to the description of the goods. The entry of prohibited or monopolised goods in the manifest or the documents taking its place under a designation that does not indicate their true description, kind and quality shall be deemed to be a false declaration as to description.

- No. 3 - A false declaration as to kind or quality that exposes duties to loss.

- No. 4 - A false declaration as to weight, number and measure (or any other specific unit) involving an excess of more than one-tenth (1/10) of the declared weight, number or measure (or any other specific unit), except with respect to products subject to high duties or to revenue duties designated by a decision of the Higher Council of Customs, to which the penalties provided for in this Article shall apply if the excess in weight, number or measure (or any other specific unit) exceeds one-twentieth (1/20).

- No. 5 - A false declaration as to value involving an increase equal to or exceeding one-tenth (1/10) of the declared value.

- No. 6 - A false declaration as to provenance or origin intended to obtain the benefit of a tariff lower than the tariff actually applicable.

- No. 7 - The drawing up or submission of false or forged documents or documents containing false indications, with the intent of obtaining the benefit either of an exemption from duties or of a tariff or duty lower than the tariff or duty actually applicable.

- No. 8 - The ascertainment of false indications as to number, weight, value and kind in invoices submitted as being original invoices.

- No. 9- The importation, by letter post, of closed dispatches and packets (ordinary and registered), dispatches with declared value, boxes with declared value, small packets (ordinary and registered), ordinary and registered printed matter, and ordinary and registered samples, devoid of the regulatory labels and proved to contain prohibited or dutiable goods, in accordance with the conditions provided for in the decisions in force.

- No. 10- The ascertainment, in any case whatsoever, of an unjustified shortage in packages sent in transit or in goods placed in packages sent in transit.

- No. 11- The substitution of goods declared as intended for transit, in whole or in part, by other goods, ascertained in any case whatsoever, without preventing, if the substituted goods are prohibited from exportation, the application of the penalties provided for in No. 28 of this Article.

- No. 12 - Failure to prove the passage abroad or arrival at destination of goods sent in transit or re-exported.

The repetition of this offence and of the two preceding offences may, moreover, lead to the deprivation of the perpetrator or his accomplices of the right to engage in transit operations, by a mere administrative measure.

- No. 13 - An unjustified shortage in the quantities of goods placed in private warehouses or in specialised warehouses.

This offence may lead to depriving the concerned parties of the benefit of the private warehouse or the specialised warehouse by a mere administrative measure.

- No. 14- Failure to return guaranteed bond notes relating to the transport of goods from one customs warehouse to another customs warehouse or their re-exportation from the customs warehouse, endorsed to certify the arrival of the goods.

- No. 15 - The discovery in the free zone of goods whose entry therein is prohibited. This offence shall be established against the owners of the goods or their depositors or their agents or their accomplices, and in general against all the persons mentioned in Article 417, or against the body entrusted with operating the free zone which may be liable pursuant to the provisions of Article 258.

- No. 16 - The introduction by way of smuggling into the customs territory of goods placed in the free zone. This offence shall be established against the owners of the goods or their depositors or their agents or their accomplices, and in general against the persons mentioned in Article 417.

- No. 17 - Failure to complete the formalities provided for in Articles 89, 251 and 259 concerning the free zone.

- No. 18- Failure to produce goods admitted under the temporary admission regime or under the industrial warehouse regime, upon every request of the Customs Administration,

either in the state in which they were upon entry or after their processing within the regulatory period.

- No. 19- Failure to re-export articles temporarily admitted free of duties and the articles resulting therefrom after their processing, or failure to place them in the public warehouse, within the regulatory time limit.

- No. 20- Failure to manufacture the goods admitted under the industrial warehouse regime or failure to discharge the said regime by re-exporting the compensating products or by placing them in a public warehouse or in a free zone or by releasing them for consumption.

Violation of these provisions or of the provisions of the two preceding paragraphs 18 and 19 may, moreover, lead to depriving the concerned parties of the benefit of the temporary admission regime or of the industrial warehouse regime by a mere administrative measure issued by the competent authority.

- No. 21 - The transhipment of goods from one means of transport to another means of transport or their re-exportation without a declaration or a regulatory authorisation.

- No. 22 - The loading or unloading of vessels, trucks, lorries or other means of transport, or the withdrawal of goods without authorisation from the Customs or in the absence of its representatives.

- No. 23- The entry of several closed packages, assembled in any manner whatsoever, in the manifest or in bills of lading or waybills or detailed declarations as a single unit.

- No. 24- An excess over the manifest or other documents taking its place, ascertained after the unloading of any means of transport whatsoever. This offence shall be established against the person in charge of operating the means of transport or the carrier or their duly authorised representative, and in general against all the persons mentioned in Article 417.

- No. 25 - The use of the articles mentioned below outside the places in which such use is permitted, or their use in ways other than the specific purposes for which they were imported, or their allocation to a purpose other than that for which they are intended, or their substitution, all of this in an irregular manner, or their sale without prior notice to the Customs and before the Customs has secured the collection of the ordinary duties or before the new purchaser has completely replaced the original importer and fulfilled all his obligations. These articles are:

a - Products admitted, in accordance with the customs tariff, free of duties or subject to reduced duties in view of the specific purpose for which they are intended.

b - Supplies, materials, tools or products delivered free of customs duties pursuant to Chapters 5, 8, 9 and 10 of Title Four of this Law.

c- Motor vehicles temporarily admitted free of duties.

These offences shall be recorded against the beneficiaries of the customs exemption or of the reduced duties or of the temporary admission, or against the customs clearing agents, intermediaries, contractors or concessionaires, and in general against all the persons mentioned in Article 417. These offences may also lead to the withdrawal of the privileged status from the offenders who benefit therefrom for a period that may reach five years.

- No. 26- The circulation or possession, in an irregular manner, within the customs zone, of goods subject to zone policing, and circulation that does not comply with the terms of the transport document.

- No. 27 - An unjustified excess or shortage in the open account specified in Article 344

- No. 28- The exportation or attempted exportation of goods whose exportation is prohibited, without a declaration or by way of smuggling, or false declarations upon exportation as to kind, description, quality or value intended to evade an export prohibition.

- No. 29 - Upon exportation, where the goods are subject to export duties, the exportation or attempted exportation without a declaration or by way of smuggling and the offences mentioned in Nos. 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8 of this Article.

- No. 30 - The evasion or attempted evasion of completing customs formalities on any item whatsoever, or of paying duties, by means of a false or incomplete declaration or by means of any fraudulent acts or means not provided for in this Article and in Articles 424 to 431, as well as all other offences not mentioned elsewhere.

2- Offences assimilated to offences of importing prohibited, restricted or monopolised goods without a declaration or by way of smuggling.

- No. 31- The possession of playing cards devoid of the legal stamp, or offering them for sale or transporting them within Lebanese territory. (No. 31 was repealed pursuant to Decree-Law Put into Force No. 480 dated 2/7/2007)

- No. 32 - The importation or re-exportation of the goods mentioned in Article 61 by means of vessels of a tonnage of less than 150 net register tons.

- No. 33 - The navigation within the maritime zone of vessels of a tonnage of less than 150 net register tons carrying goods of the kind mentioned in Article 61, or their stopping within twelve miles of the coasts or in any port other than in a proved case of force majeure.

- No. 34 - Failure to submit proof, within the time limits fixed in the guaranteed bond notes, of arrival at the intended foreign country, in respect of the goods mentioned in Article 61 and carried on vessels of a tonnage of less than 150 net register tons which had anchored within twelve miles of the coasts or in a Lebanese port following a situation resulting from a proved force majeure.

The designated places in the various curriculum years shall be filled after adhering to the order of preferences set out below, as follows:

1- In the First Intermediate Year:

a- By the failing pupils of the secondary school who are accepted to repeat their class, provided that their final total marks do not fall below 60% of the required passing average.

b- By the successful pupils of the Fifth Primary Year after sitting a written entrance examination in the following subjects:

Subject - Coefficient

Arabic Composition - 1

Foreign Language - 1

Arithmetic - 1

Every pupil who obtains at least 10/20 of the average of the total marks and does not obtain a zero in any subject of the examination shall be deemed successful, and the successful pupils shall be admitted according to the order of their total marks. The examining committee, chaired by the principal of the secondary school, may decide to grant a supplementary pass by no more than ten marks.

2- In the Second, Third, and Fourth Intermediate Years:

a- By the promoted pupils of the secondary school.

b- By the failing pupils of the secondary school to repeat their class, provided that their final total marks do not fall below 60% of the required passing average.

c- By new candidates from among the pupils of public secondary schools who succeeded in their schools.

d- By new candidates from among the pupils of other schools who succeeded in their schools, subject to their passing entrance examinations organized by the administration of the secondary school, comprising written tests in composition in the Arabic and foreign languages, and in mathematics and sciences. A candidate who obtains at least 10/20 of the average of the total marks and whose mark in any subject does not fall below 5/20 shall be deemed successful. The marks shall be assigned according to the coefficients of school examinations set out in Article 42 of these Regulations. The examining committee, chaired by the principal of the secondary school, may decide to grant a supplementary pass by no more than five marks.

3- In the First Secondary Year:

a- By the promoted pupils of the secondary school from the Fourth Intermediate Year who succeeded in their classes.

b- By the failing pupils of the secondary school who are accepted to repeat their class, provided that their final total marks do not fall below 60% of the required passing average.

c- By the promoted pupils of public secondary schools from the Fourth Intermediate Year who succeeded in their class.

d- By all other candidates in accordance with the following rules:

1- Holders of the Lebanese Higher Primary Studies Certificate or the Intermediate Certificate.

2- Holders of equivalencies to the Lebanese Higher Primary Studies Certificate, after the average of their official total marks has been determined.

3- Pupils of schools that do not nominate their pupils to the examinations of the Lebanese Higher Primary Studies Certificate, subject to their success:

- in the Fourth Intermediate Year in their previous schools;

- in an entrance examination in the subjects of composition (in the Arabic and foreign languages), mathematics, sciences, history, and geography, according to the coefficients prescribed in the official examinations.

A single list shall be drawn up of all candidates mentioned in this paragraph (d) who meet the conditions for admission.

e- By the failing pupils of public secondary schools who are accepted to repeat their class in their previous schools.

f- If the number of candidates in each of the categories provided for in paragraphs c, d, and e above exceeds the number of vacant places, the required number shall be admitted according to the order of total marks.

4- In the Second Secondary Year:

a- By the promoted pupils of the secondary school.

b- By the promoted pupils of public secondary schools.

c- By the promoted pupils of other schools, subject to their passing entrance examinations organized by the administration of the secondary school, comprising written tests in literature in the Arabic and foreign languages, and in mathematics and sciences.

A candidate who obtains at least 9 1/2 / 20 of the average of the total marks and whose mark in any subject does not fall below 5/20 shall be deemed successful. The marks shall be assigned according to the coefficients of school examinations set out in Article 43 of these Regulations.

d- In the event that vacant places remain in the secondary schools located outside the capitals of the governorates and not covered by the decision issued by the Director of Secondary Education pursuant to Article 2 of the Decision Regulating Repetition, the principal of the secondary school shall appoint another date for accepting applications for admission five days after the date of publication of the results of the second session of the examinations for each of the two branches of Part One of the Lebanese Baccalaureate, and the period for accepting applications shall be fixed at two working days.

These places shall be filled by repeating pupils of the secondary school and pupils of other public and private schools, provided that their total marks in the official examinations do not fall below 40% of the required passing average, according to the following preferences:

- Pupils of the secondary school

- Pupils of public secondary schools

- Pupils of other schools

e- If the number of candidates in each of the categories provided for in paragraphs c and d above exceeds the number of vacant places, the required number shall be admitted according to the order of total marks.

5- In the Third Secondary Year:

First - Philosophy Branch:

1- By the pupils who succeeded in the examinations of the Lebanese Baccalaureate, Part One, according to the following order:

a- Pupils of the secondary school

b- Pupils of public secondary schools

2- In the event that vacant places remain, the principal of the secondary school shall appoint another date for accepting applications for admission five days after the publication of the results of the second session for the last branch of the Lebanese Baccalaureate in both its parts, and the period for accepting applications shall be fixed at two working days.

These places shall be filled:

a- By the successful pupils of the secondary school.

b- By the candidates from among the successful pupils of public secondary schools.

c- By the candidates from among the successful pupils of other schools.

d- By the repeating pupils of the secondary school and the pupils of other public and private schools in the secondary schools located outside the capitals of the governorates and not covered by the decision issued by the Director of Secondary Education pursuant to Article 2 of the Decision Regulating Repetition - provided that their total marks in the official examinations do not fall below 40% of the required passing average, according to the following preferences:

- Pupils of the secondary school

- Pupils of public secondary schools

- Pupils of other schools

3- If the number of candidates in each of the categories provided for in 1 (b) and 2 (b, c, d) above exceeds the number of vacant places, the required number shall be admitted according to the order of total marks.

Second - Mathematics Branch:

1- By the pupils who succeeded in the Lebanese Baccalaureate - Part One - Scientific Branch, according to the following order:

a- By the pupils of the secondary school whose average of total marks in the two subjects of mathematics and sciences in the official examinations is not less than 25/40.

b- By the pupils of the secondary school who did not obtain the required average mentioned in the preceding paragraph and whom the administration of the secondary school decides to admit upon the recommendation of the teachers of the two subjects of mathematics and sciences, inspired by the school results.

c- By the candidates from among the pupils of the public secondary school whose average of total marks in the two subjects of mathematics and sciences in the official examinations is not less than 25/40.

d- By the candidates from among the pupils of other schools whose average of total marks in the two subjects of mathematics and sciences in the official examinations is not less than 25/40.

2- In the event that vacant places remain, the principal of the secondary school shall fix another date for accepting applications for admission five days after the date of publication of the results of the second session for the last branch of the Lebanese Baccalaureate in both its parts, and the period for accepting applications shall be fixed at two working days.

These places shall be filled:

a- By those who succeeded in the Lebanese Baccalaureate - Part One, Scientific Branch, provided that the average of their total marks in the two subjects of mathematics and sciences in the official examinations does not fall below 20/40. They shall be admitted according to the order of their total marks in these two subjects, according to the following preferences:

- Pupils of the secondary school

- Pupils of public secondary schools

- Pupils of other schools

b- By the repeating pupils of the secondary school and the pupils of other public and private schools in the secondary schools located outside the capitals of the governorates and not covered by the decision issued by the Director of Secondary Education pursuant to Article 3 of the Repetition Decision, provided that their total marks in the official examinations do not fall below 40% of the required passing average, according to the following preferences:

- Pupils of the secondary school

- Pupils of public secondary schools

- Pupils of other schools

3- If the number of candidates in each of the categories provided for in 1 (c, d) and 2 (a - excluding pupils of the secondary school - b) exceeds the number of vacant places, the required number shall be admitted according to the order of total marks.

Third - Experimental Sciences Branch:

1- By the pupils who succeeded in the Lebanese Baccalaureate - Part One - Scientific Branch, according to the following order:

a- Pupils of the secondary school

b- Pupils of public secondary schools

2- In the event that vacant places remain, the principal of the secondary school shall appoint another date for accepting applications for admission five days after the date of publication of the results of the second session for the last branch of the Lebanese Baccalaureate in both its parts, and the period for accepting applications shall be fixed at two working days.

These places shall be filled:

a- By the successful pupils of the secondary school.
