Remarks on the workflow in the Administration of Tenders It is necessary to point out the positive and negative aspects encountered by the Administration of Tenders in performing its tasks and exercising its powers during the year 2003 in comparison with the year 2002. Regarding the positive aspects: 1 - Adding the Director General of the Administration of Tenders, pursuant to Decree No. /11470/ dated 6/12/2003, to the Board for the Classification of Contractors and Consultants formed pursuant to Article Five of Decree No. /9333/ dated 26/12/2002 2 - Forming a committee to reconsider the organization of the Administration of Tenders. The said committee completed its mission and deposited the result of its work with the Presidency of the Council of Ministers in early June 1998, and the Commission for the Modernization of Laws examined the proposal, expressed remarks thereon, proposed additions thereto, and deposited it with the Parliamentary Committee on Administration and Justice. It is also worth noting that the Council of Ministers issued a decision under No. 7, Minutes 12, in the session of 3/3/1999, whereby it restricted the conduct of all tenders and requests for proposals to the Administration of Tenders based on the proposal of the Minister of State for Administrative Reform Affairs. Certain administrations abided by this decision to a large extent (Civil Aviation, Land and Maritime Transport...) and other administrations worked to evade it in several ways. This led to many objections, so the Court of Accounts annulled most of these tenders and requests for proposals. Here, it must be emphasized that adherence to the principle of the public tender is among the necessities that must be abided by, and not resorting to the exception under the pretext of an urgent case arising from emergency circumstances, in order to remove suspicions, preserve the principle of equality, and open the door to competition before all contractors. 2 - The negative aspects: Among the obstacles that limit the effectiveness of the Administration of Tenders: - The acute vacancy in the cadre of the Administration of Tenders. - The Administration of Tenders conducting certain public contracts the total value of which reached the following: /110425496601/ L.L. one hundred and ten billion, four hundred and twenty-five million, four hundred and ninety-six thousand, six hundred and one Lebanese pounds, which indicates the small value of the projects awarded at it when measured against the contract awards of other councils. - Despite the return of certain ministries to the procedures provided for in the Tenders Regulations, many contract awarding files remained noticeable for the smallness of their value and because the competent administrations did not adopt, for the most part, the percentage reduction method, which we consider the most correct in important public contracts, especially in the absence of operating with the secret estimated price. - The non-involvement of the Administration of Tenders in all stages of contract awarding starting from the submission of bids until execution. - The non-payment of compensation to the tender committees. - The non-publication of tender announcements in widely circulated newspapers. The Future Vision: We look forward to a day when the Administration of Tenders encompasses all public contracts for supplies, works, and services in the State, considering that it is the administrative body dedicated to this purpose. We also hold fast to maintaining a central administration that undertakes the conduct of public contracts, for the following reasons: - The danger of restricting all powers to a single administration that designs the project, sets the special conditions for contract awarding, appoints the contract awarding committees, the experts, and the reception committees, and assigns the tasks of setting the administrative, technical, and financial conditions to employees who are not qualified for that. - The conflict of opinions between one administration and another on how to conduct the contract awarding, so that there is no longer a single authority that observes the texts and applies them in order to reach sound solutions, causing chaos and contradiction to prevail. - That the Lebanese administration, at the present time, suffers from the increasing complaint of suspicious public contracts, which reinforces the position of maintaining a single central administration, activating it, expanding the scope of its jurisdiction, developing it, and computerizing it.

Powers and Duties of the Principal:

First - Powers:

1- The principal is the primary person responsible in the secondary school and is the direct

superior of all persons working therein, and they must execute his instructions

and respect his authority in accordance with the rules and laws in force

2- He presides over the councils and committees of the secondary school, directs their activities, and supervises

their work

3- He authorises the employees of the secondary school to be absent from their work in the case

provided for in paragraph 5 of Article 36 of these regulations

4- He distributes works and assignments among the employees of his school and organises

their working hours schedules in accordance with the rules in force and the principles of justice

Second - Duties - The principal of the secondary school must

1- Attend to the technical and educational organisation of the work and ensure

that the employees of the secondary school abide by the official working hours

2- Attend daily at the secondary school in the morning half an hour before the beginning of lessons

and sign the attendance register upon his arrival

3- Send a schedule of his working hours to each of the Directorate of Secondary Education

and the Educational Inspectorate at the beginning of the academic year

4- Attend lessons where required and review the special registers

or the card which the teachers are required to prepare and sign

them

5- Inform the competent authorities without delay of matters that occur

in the secondary school and that relate to all its work and to the affairs of

the employees working therein, and conduct preliminary investigations when

necessary, such as questioning the concerned parties in writing, and submit a report in this

regard to the competent authority in which the principal's observations

and proposals are recorded

6- Acquaint new teachers with the internal regulations and all

laws and regulations in force relating to their affairs

7- Organise school tests and the end-of-year examination or

assign administrative employees to perform this work

8- Assign certain teachers to perform the task of coordinating lessons, provided

that competence in teaching is observed in the selection

9- Submit his proposals to the Directorate of Secondary Education regarding

the books intended to be replaced on the basis of the studies of the teachers of

the subject and the lesson coordinators before the end of June of each

year, and if no reply is received from the Directorate before the fifteenth of the month of

September, the submitted proposals shall be deemed approved

10- Sign the payroll schedules of contracted employees and wage earners

working in the secondary school; he may not prepare the payroll schedule

or sign it for any employee, contractor, or wage earner who has discontinued his work

except in the special cases provided for by the law and regulations

in force (leave with full pay) suspension from work due to

disciplinary prosecution or remand in custody or

others...)

11- Study the needs of his secondary school for teaching hours and other works

and notify the Directorate of Secondary Education immediately of any shortage

or surplus that occurs, under penalty of liability

12- File with each of the Directorate of Annual Education and the Educational Inspectorate

a copy of:

a- The annual statement (before the end of the month of December), which includes:

1- A schedule of the working hours of the administrative and teaching staff

2- The weekly lesson distribution schedule

3- A schedule of the number of students who have not discontinued attending the secondary school

4- A list of the names of the prescribed books

5- A schedule of the number of students nominated for the official examinations

and the number of those who passed in the first and second sessions of the previous academic

year

6- The proposals and demands of the principal of the secondary school relating to the needs

of the secondary school for equipment and illustrative aids for the coming academic year

7- All other reports and statements that may be requested by the Directorate of

Secondary Education

b- The mid-year report (before the end of February), which relates to the trainee

teachers attached to the secondary school

c- The final report (before 15 July), which includes:

1- The status of contracted teachers

2- The status of tenured teachers and employees of the secondary school regarding whom necessity calls

for reporting

3- The needs of the secondary school for human resources

4- The final school results

5- The number of sections proposed for the coming academic year

6- An annual schedule of sick leaves pertaining to the employees of

the secondary school, with the exception of contractors, daily-paid workers, and physical education

teachers

7- All other reports and statements that may be requested by the Directorate of

Secondary Education

Definitions: Wherever they appear in this Law, the expressions shall be understood as follows:

- The Ministry: The Ministry of Energy and Water.

- The Minister: The Minister of Energy and Water.

- Public Water Investment Establishments: Beirut and Mount Lebanon Water Establishment, South Lebanon Water Establishment, North Lebanon Water Establishment, Bekaa Water Establishment, the Litani River National Authority.

- Groundwater Aquifer: One or several rocky or geological layers whose porous and permeable nature allows the flow of groundwater or the accumulation of large quantities of groundwater.

- Hydrographic Basin: Every area into which all waters seeping through a network of streams and rivers, and sometimes from lakes, flow towards the sea where they discharge through a single outlet.

- Sub-basin: Every area into which all waters seeping through a network of streams and rivers, and sometimes from lakes, flow at a specific point of a watercourse.

- Aquatic Environment: The ecological surroundings associated with the presence of water therein and its natural balances.

- Water Deficit: The noticeable decrease in the quantities of available freshwater in the entire country or in an area or an aquatic ecosystem which is unable to secure its own environmental balance or respond to the water needs that it usually met.

- Surface Water: Inland waters, moving and static, with the exception of groundwater and coastal waters save as relates to their chemical status, which also include territorial waters.

- Groundwater: All waters located beneath the surface of the earth in the accumulation zone directly connected to the surface of the earth or its subsoil.

- Lake: A body of inland water with a static surface whatever the source of its feeding.

- Body of Groundwater: A distinct volume of groundwater within a groundwater aquifer.

- Body of Surface Water: A significant part of surface water such as a lake, a reservoir, a stream, a river, or a canal, or part of a stream, a river, or a canal, or a section of coastal waters.

- Green Water: The water retained by the soil after rainfall.

- Water Pollution: The direct or indirect introduction, as a result of human activity, of substances or heat into the air, water, or land, which may cause harm to human health or to the quality of aquatic ecosystems or terrestrial ecosystems directly related to aquatic ecosystems, and which is also likely to lead to damage to material property or impairment of or obstruction to the enjoyment of a sound and stable environment and its other legitimate uses.

- Stream (River): A body of inland water flowing for the most part above the surface of the earth and which may flow beneath it in a section of its course.

- Non-conventional Water Resources: Include the treatment and reuse of treated water, the exploitation of submarine water springs, seawater desalination, greywater, and water resulting from cloud seeding.

- Conventional and Non-conventional Water: The quantity of conventional and non-conventional water that enters into the water balance of the Lebanese State.

- Water Diplomacy: Diplomacy applied to international basins pursuant to international agreements and United Nations conventions.

- Sustainable Water Management: The process of promoting the coordinated development and management of water, land, and related resources, in order to maximise economic and social benefits in an equitable manner without compromising the sustainability of vital ecosystems.

- Irrigation Water: Water allocated, from available water resources, for irrigating agricultural lands, and subject to the provisions of this Law.

- Transmission Network: The set of infrastructures previously established, or to be established subsequently, for use in conveying water from its source to one or more distribution networks. It consists of the primary network, which is composed of a main network for securing water whose ownership and management remain public, and of the secondary network which branches off from the main network.

- Distribution Network: The set of water structures fed from a specific feeding point of a transmission network, which may be used for distributing water, and is also known as the tertiary network.

- Water Supply Point: The intake or point that constitutes the source from which subscribers are supplied with water.

- Water Register: A non-probative administrative document prepared and periodically updated by the Ministry of Energy and Water.

- Basin Networks: Natural watercourses located within a specific hydrographic basin.

- Joint Project: Any project of public utility, as defined in Law No. 48 dated 7/9/2017 "Law Regulating Public-Private Partnership" and its amendments, to which the private sector contributes through financing and management and at least one of the following operations: design, establishment, construction, development, restoration, equipping, maintenance, rehabilitation, and operation.

- Traditional Rights to Water: Usufruct rights that were exercised in accordance with established customs, traditions, and usages.

- Licence: The permission granted by the competent authority for the usufruct of public waters.

- Delegated Management: A contract whereby a legal person of public law entrusts the management of a public utility to a public or private operator, whose remuneration is mostly linked to the results of operating the utility. The delegatee may also be charged with constructing facilities and acquiring the property necessary for the utility.

- Collective Sanitation: The discharge of wastewater into collection networks and the conveyance of such water to treatment plants where it is treated and then discharged or reused.

- Beneficiary: Anyone who benefits from water by way of subscription, use, usufruct, or any other means in accordance with laws, customs, and usages.

- Beneficiary of Irrigation Water: The subscriber and/or usufructuary of irrigation water.

- Water Usufruct Right: The right that entitles its holder to use specific quantities of water for specific purposes, pursuant to the provisions of this Law.

- Traditional Water Usufruct Rights: Water usufruct rights for a specific real property and for specific purposes, the continuity of which is recognised by law or custom or both together, and which are based on the right of individual or collective benefit from the waters of rivers, springs, wells, and water facilities. They are restricted within the limits provided for by this Law and the laws in force.

Allowing taxpayers to make a tax settlement

Settlement of the status of income tax taxpayers up to the year 2016 inclusive

First:

1- Notwithstanding any other text, and exceptionally, the status of income tax taxpayers shall be settled in the event that they opt for the settlement, in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

2- The phrase "the business results have not been examined" in this Law means the business results of the taxpayer the audit of which has not been commenced or the audit of which has not been completed.

The business of the taxpayer shall be deemed to have had its examination completed if the tax assessment notice resulting from the examination of the business has been issued in respect of the examination report.

Second:

The settlement shall cover:

1- The business of the years 2011 up to the year 2016 inclusive for concealed taxpayers.

2- The business of the years 2013 up to the year 2016 inclusive for registered taxpayers who:

- Declared their business and the declarations included a turnover.

- Declared their business at a nil value or submitted declarations of non-exercise of business

- Did not declare such business.

3- Taxpayers whose business was examined and who have not paid the taxes due from them as a result of the examination of such business for the years 2011 up to 2016 inclusive.

4- Taxpayers subject to the tax of Title II (salaries and wages) who belong to establishments enjoying exemptions from the tax of Title I (profits of industrial, commercial and non-commercial professions) in accordance with Article Five of Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12/06/1959 and its amendments (the Income Tax Law) and pursuant to special laws.

Third:

The profits of industrial, commercial and non-commercial professions, the amounts subject to Articles 41/42/43/45, and the tax of Title II shall be subject to the settlement, and it shall not apply to the tax of Title III of the Income Tax Law.

Fourth:

There shall be excluded from the provisions of the settlement:

1- Holding companies, companies whose activity is restricted outside Lebanon (offshore), and representative offices.

2- Natural and legal persons who enjoy temporary or exceptional exemptions from the aforementioned tax, for the years to which these exemptions pertain if they fall within the time period of the settlement provided for in this Law.

Fifth:

1- The value of the annual settlement for registered taxpayers subject to the tax on profits shall be calculated in accordance with the following bases:

a - Taxpayers who declared the business of the years covered by the settlement and whose declarations included a turnover:

- The value of the settlement shall be determined by multiplying the turnover declared before the issuance of this Law (non-financial operating revenues) for the business of each year covered by the settlement by 0.5% (one-half percent) for industrial establishments and by 1% (one percent) for commercial and service establishments and all other taxpayers.

- With respect to banks, financial institutions, and financial intermediation institutions, the value of the annual settlement shall be determined at a rate of 5 % (five percent) of the net proceeds (total declared revenues less interest paid). The same rate of the net proceeds (total declared revenues less returns paid) shall apply to Islamic banks.

- With respect to money changers, the value of the settlement shall be determined at a rate of 5% (five percent) of the foreign exchange revenues and realized commissions.

If the value of the settlement in a given year exceeds what the taxpayer paid on his industrial, commercial and non-commercial profits (Title I) for that year after deducting the tax of Article 51 of Law No. 497/2003 and its amendments, the taxpayer shall pay the difference, and in the opposite case, the difference shall be in favour of the Treasury.

b - Those who declared their business at a nil value or submitted declarations of non-exercise of business:

The value of the settlement for each year covered by the settlement shall be determined at the minimum set forth in paragraph 3 .

c - Those who did not declare for all the years covered by the settlement:

The value of the settlement for each year covered by the settlement shall be determined at the minimum set forth in paragraph 3 .

d - Taxpayers who did not declare the business of one or more of the years covered by the settlement:

If the taxpayer had not declared before the issuance of this Law the turnover of one or more given years of the years covered by the settlement, then for the purpose of determining the turnover of the undeclared year subject to the settlement in, the average turnover for the years covered by the settlement and declared shall be taken and multiplied by the rate determined according to the activity of the taxpayer.

e - Taxpayers whose business was examined for the years covered by the settlement:

The value of the settlement shall be determined by multiplying the turnover determined by the Administration for the business of each year covered by the settlement by 0.5% (one-half percent) for industrial establishments, by 1% (one percent) for commercial and service establishments, and by 5% for banks, financial institutions, financial intermediation institutions, and money changers.

f- Taxpayers assessed on the basis of estimated profit:

The value of the settlement shall be determined at a lump sum of 100,000 thousand pounds (one hundred thousand Lebanese pounds) for each year.

2 - There shall be deducted from the value of the settlement calculated on the basis of what has been set forth above, what was paid for each year of the declared tax and the instalments paid pertaining to that year, and the taxpayer shall pay the settlement calculated in accordance with the above.

3 - The minimum settlement for each year for registered taxpayers:

The value of the settlement pursuant to the provisions of the paragraphs set forth in Clause Fifth of this Article with respect to registered taxpayers shall in no case be less than:

- 2,000,000 pounds (two million Lebanese pounds) on joint-stock companies and partnerships limited by shares.

- 1,500,000 pounds (one million five hundred thousand Lebanese pounds) on limited liability companies, partnerships, sole proprietorships compulsorily subject to assessment on the basis of lump-sum profit, and real estate dealers.

- 400,000 pounds (four hundred thousand Lebanese pounds) for sole proprietorships assessed on the basis of real profit.

- 200,000 pounds (two hundred thousand Lebanese pounds) for professionals required to join a syndicate in order to practice the profession.

- 150,000 pounds (one hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese pounds) for professionals not required to join a syndicate in order to practice the profession and for the remaining taxpayers.

Sixth:

1- The value of the annual settlement for concealed taxpayers subject to the tax on profits shall be determined in accordance with the following:

- 4,000,000 pounds (four million Lebanese pounds) on joint-stock companies and partnerships limited by shares.

- 3,000,000 pounds (three million Lebanese pounds) on limited liability companies, partnerships, sole proprietorships compulsorily subject to assessment on the basis of lump-sum profit, and real estate dealers.

- 750,000 pounds (seven hundred and fifty thousand Lebanese pounds) for sole proprietorships compulsorily assessed on the basis of real profit.

- 300,000 pounds (three hundred thousand Lebanese pounds) for professionals required to join a syndicate in order to practice the profession.

- 200,000 pounds (two hundred thousand Lebanese pounds) for professionals not required to join a syndicate in order to practice the profession and for the remaining taxpayers.

2 - Applications for settlement with respect to concealed taxpayers shall be deemed equivalent to a declaration of commencement of business, and no fine shall be imposed on the taxpayer who opts to be subject to the provisions of the settlement due to the failure to submit the aforementioned declaration in due time, provided that he pays the lump sum due from him in accordance with the provisions of this Article within the specified time limit.

3 - With respect to concealed taxpayers who opt for it and practice multiple businesses, the settlement shall be made on the basis of the amounts specified above for each concealed activity separately.

Seventh:

The value of the annual settlement for taxpayers subject to the tax of Title II (salaries and wages) who belong to establishments enjoying exemptions from the tax of Title I (profits of industrial, commercial and non-commercial professions) in accordance with Article Five of Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12/06/1959 and its amendments (the Income Tax Law) and pursuant to their special laws shall be determined at 50,000 pounds (fifty thousand Lebanese pounds).

Eighth:

A taxpayer to whom the provisions of the settlement apply shall have the right to opt, within a time limit of six months from the date of entry into force of this Law, to be subject to these provisions, by virtue of a written letter submitted by him to the competent financial department in accordance with a form established by the Ministry of Finance in which he specifies the years that he wishes the settlement to cover, provided that they pay the taxes and fees due for the previous years and the years not covered by the settlement within the same time limit. The taxpayer may pay those taxes and fees in instalments over three years at the interest rate of treasury bonds of this category, provided that the first payment amounting to 10% is paid within a time limit of six months from the date of publication of this Law, and in the event of default in paying one of the instalments on the specified due date, an interest at the rate of 12% shall be imposed on the amounts paid in instalments.

As for the taxpayers who have not submitted any application within the specified time limit, as well as those who opted for a partial settlement out of the years legally covered by the settlement, the Tax Administration may examine their business for all the years that they did not opt for in accordance with the ordinary rules.

The taxpayer may opt for the settlement for the years from which he wishes to benefit, provided that they are among the years covered by this settlement, and provided that the years he opts for are consecutive.

Ninth:

Every taxpayer shall pay the amounts due from him for the settlement years in full by virtue of a prior payment notice specific to the settlement simultaneously with his submission of the settlement application.

Tenth:

Taxpayers who opt for the settlement shall be granted a time limit of six months from the date of entry into force of this Law:

1 - To declare the taxes relating to any of the settlement years but which are not subject to the provisions of this settlement (Title III of the Income Tax Law and its amendments).

2 - To duly submit a declaration of any concealed income for the period for which no settlement was requested and to pay the tax for this period with respect to the taxes subject to the settlement or not subject thereto.

3 - The taxpayers concerned by paragraphs 1 and 2 above of this Clause shall also benefit from this time limit in order to reorganize and correct their accounts and records and complete the statements relating thereto.

4 - The declarations, documents and statements mentioned in paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 of this Clause that are submitted before the expiry of the six-month time limit shall be deemed submitted within their original time limits, and those who submit them shall be exempted from the fines resulting from the failure to submit them within the original legal time limits.

5 - The taxes resulting from the reorganization and correction of the accounts must be paid upon submitting the declarations pertaining thereto and within the six-month time limit, and they shall be exempted from the late payment fines (collection fines).

Eleventh:

A taxpayer who has opted for the settlement shall not benefit from the provisions of Article 16 of Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (the Income Tax Law) for the years covered by the settlement. Consequently, the carry-forward of losses to subsequent years shall be cancelled, and if any tax becomes due as a result of this cancellation in the years subsequent to the years covered by the settlement, the taxpayer must declare and pay the tax thereon within six months from the date of making the settlement.

Twelfth:

The settlement for the years mentioned in this Article, after payment of its value, shall be deemed equivalent to a clearance for these years with respect to the types of taxes covered by the settlement pursuant to the provisions of this Article, and the business of the taxpayer for these years shall be deemed to have had its examination completed, and it shall not be permissible to return to auditing them with respect to the taxes covered by the settlement.

A taxpayer who opts for the settlement must retain the accounting records and documents pertaining to all the years not yet barred by prescription, including the settlement years, within the time limits specified in the Tax Procedures Law.

Thirteenth:

The competent financial unit shall decide upon the tax settlement applications within a time limit of six months from the end of the settlement time limit and shall recover any shortfall occurring in the paid settlement value plus a fine at the rate of 1% (one percent) per month starting from the date of expiry of the aforementioned time limit until the date of actual payment of this shortfall. A rate of 20% of the amounts paid pursuant to the settlement by concealed taxpayers and a rate of 15% of the amounts paid pursuant to the settlement by registered taxpayers shall be deemed an assessment fine.

Fourteenth:

The departments concerned with income tax shall cease tax audit operations up to 31/12/2018 except for cases of liquidation, cessation of business, periods not covered by the settlement, and cases requiring audit for the purpose of imposing taxes and fees other than income tax, and the time limit for recovering taxes due for the year 2013 with respect to registered taxpayers and for the year 2011 with respect to concealed taxpayers who did not opt to benefit from the settlement shall be extended up to 31/12/2019.

Fifteenth:

Immediately upon the expiry of the time limit specified for making the settlement, the Ministry of Finance shall conduct a field survey, in coordination with all the entities it deems appropriate, including municipalities, for all Lebanese regions to uncover concealed taxpayers and assess them for the taxes and fines due.

Sixteenth:

The details of implementation of this Article shall, where necessary, be determined by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.
