Article 45 of Legislative Decree No. 144 dated 12/6/1959 and its amendments (the Income Tax Law) is amended to read as follows:

First: Establishments subject to the assessment method on the basis of actual profit may revalue the items of fixed assets that they hold every five years in accordance with the procedures prescribed in the Code of Commerce for the valuation of contributions in kind in capital companies.

By way of exception, establishments, capital companies and partnerships assessed on the basis of lump-sum profit may, every year and for a period ending on 31/12/2026, revalue the items of fixed assets that they hold in accordance with the procedures prescribed for taxpayers under the actual profit method starting from the end of the year 2023.

The valuation report shall be notified to the competent finance department, which may object to it before the Income Tax Objections Committee within three months from the date of notification, and the said Committee shall issue its decision regarding the objection and determine the final valuation within a maximum period of six months from the date on which the establishment submits its observations on the rapporteur's report, failing which the valuation report shall be deemed enforceable.

Second: Where items of fixed assets are valued higher than their original cost price in the currency of their acquisition, or than the remaining balance thereof after depreciation, the increase shall be deemed a capital gain.

This gain shall not be subject to income tax in either of the following two cases:

- If it remains separate in a special account on both the assets and liabilities sides of the balance sheet.

- If it is used to cover losses that remain apparent and specified in the balance sheet, within the limits of what is used thereof to cover such losses.

This gain shall be subject to income tax at a rate of 15% in other cases. Depreciation may then be calculated on the new value appearing as a result of the revaluation.

Third:

A - The capital gain resulting from a total or partial disposal shall be subject to income tax at a rate of 15%; however, a taxpayer who reinvests this gain or part thereof before the expiry of two years following the year in which it was realised shall be entitled to request a deduction of the tax imposed to the extent of what he has reinvested thereof in constructing permanent dwellings to house the employees and wage-earners working in the establishment.

In this case, the provisions and conditions of Article 5 bis of the Income Tax Law shall apply.

The capital gain resulting from the disposal shall also be exempted to the extent of what is used thereof to write off losses incurred by the establishment.

B - Gains on the disposal of fixed assets, including real property, belonging to natural or legal persons subject to income tax on the basis of lump-sum or estimated profit shall be subject to tax at a rate of fifteen per cent (15%).

C - Gains on the disposal of real property belonging to natural or legal persons not subject to income tax, or who enjoyed permanent, special or exceptional exemptions from that tax, or belonging to natural persons subject to income tax where such real property does not constitute an asset of the practice of the profession, shall be subject to tax at a rate of fifteen per cent (15%).

By way of exception, and for a period ending on 31/12/2026, the tax rate referred to in this clause shall be reduced to 1%.

Gains on the disposal of the primary places of residence of a natural person shall be excluded from the tax mentioned above, provided that they do not exceed two dwellings.

For the purpose of calculating the taxable disposal gain, a rate of 8% of the value of the disposal gain shall be deducted for each full year separating the date of acquisition of the real property and the date of its disposal, and the gain on the disposal of the real property shall be exempted from tax if the transferor has continued to hold it for a period of 12 full years and above, provided that the difference is paid in the year during which the disposal takes place.

The persons referred to above shall, when carrying out a taxable disposal transaction, declare the disposal transaction and pay the tax due thereon within a period of two months from the date of the disposal.

In the event of a violation of the provisions of this Article, the fines provided for in Law No. 44 dated 11/11/2008 and its amendments (the Tax Procedures Law) shall be imposed.

The details of implementation of this Article shall be determined, where necessary, by a decision issued by the Minister of Finance.

Definitions

For the purpose of applying the provisions of this Law, the following definitions and terms shall be adopted:

- Banque du Liban: The Central Bank established pursuant to the Law put into force by Decree No. 13513 dated 1/8/1963 (the Code of Money and Credit and the Establishment of the Central Bank).

- The Higher Banking Commission: Article 10 of Law No. 28 dated 9/5/1967 and its amendments (Amending and Completing the Legislation Relating to Banks and Establishing a Mixed Institution for the Guarantee of Bank Deposits) shall be amended to read as follows:

"The Commission, in its two chambers, which is concerned with taking punitive decisions against violating financial institutions ( the First Chamber) and resolution and/or liquidation decisions and supervising their implementation (the Second Chamber), in accordance with the provisions of this Law and the relevant laws in force".

- The Banking Control Commission: The supervisory authority established pursuant to Law No. 28/67 dated 9/5/1967 and its amendments.

- Depositors:

Natural or legal persons (i.e. individuals or companies) who conclude a bank deposit contract with a licensed bank, whereby they deliver a sum of money to the bank for the purpose of safekeeping or investing it in accordance with agreed conditions, with the obligation of the bank to return this sum upon request or on a specified date, with or without interest.

- Creditor:

A creditor in accordance with the provisions of this Law is the holder of secured or unsecured liabilities not resulting from a deposit.

- Deposits:

A- Customer deposits: (including certificates of deposit issued by the bank and held by customers) belonging to natural

and legal persons, other than financial sector institutions, and which are not included within Excluded Liabilities in accordance with the definitions set out in the laws in force.

B- On-balance-sheet deposits belonging to financial sector institutions and arising from fiduciary contracts between those institutions in their capacity as financial intermediary and their customers.

C- Cash collateral and cash margins given as security against funded facilities (i.e. on-balance-sheet facilities) within the limits of the utilised amount of the facilities.

- Senior Management: The natural persons at banks who are responsible for setting policies and/or taking executive decisions with respect to placements, risks and compliance.

- Own Funds: Consist of:

* Common Equity Tier 1 rights, which include retained prior results, reserves, other comprehensive income items and other Common Equity Tier 1 items as defined in Annex No. 1 (Hierarchy of Own Funds and Creditors).

* Additional Tier 1 capital as defined in Annex No. 1 (Hierarchy of Own Funds and Creditors).

* Tier 2 capital as defined in Annex No. 1 (Hierarchy of Own Funds and Creditors).

- Hierarchy of Own Funds and Creditors: The rank of each of the elements of Own Funds and liabilities (as defined in Annex No. 1).

- Excluded Liabilities: The liabilities mentioned in Annex No. 1 which are not subject to a write-down in value or to conversion into capital instruments.

- Financial Sector Institutions: Include the following resident and non-resident institutions, whether related or unrelated to the bank:

* Central banks.

* International and regional development banks and financial institutions.

* Banks.

* Other institutions, comprising:

* Financial institutions as defined pursuant to Article 179 of the Code of Money and Credit, and the relevant circulars issued by Banque du Liban.

* Financial leasing companies.

* Credit counters regulated pursuant to Articles 183 and 184 of the Code of Money and Credit.

* Microfinance institutions.

* Clearing houses.

* Financial intermediation institutions.

* Exchange institutions.

* Companies concerned with the transfer of cash funds through electronic means.

* Investment funds.

* Investment companies, including holding companies and special purpose investment entities.

* Any other institution that provides financial services or carries out financial activities.

- Home Competent Authority or Supervisory Authority: The authority competent for the resolution of banks or the supervisory authority in the country where the head office of the foreign branch or of the foreign subsidiary bank operating in Lebanon is located.

- Host Competent Authority or Supervisory Authority: The authority competent for the resolution of banks or the supervisory authority in the country where the branch belonging to the head office in Lebanon or the subsidiary bank of the Lebanese parent bank operates.

- The Financial Regularity and Deposit Recovery Law: The law that allows the restoration of balance to financial regularity in Lebanon through addressing the financial gap by determining responsibilities. (Which the Government is obliged to refer to the Parliament in order to be enacted).

- Liquidation Process: A process that includes selling all the assets of the bank, settling its liabilities, distributing the balance of its net assets to the shareholders, closing it permanently and striking it off the List of Banks.

- Net Asset Value: The fair value of the assets of the bank (including off-balance-sheet items) minus the fair value of the liabilities of the bank (including off-balance-sheet items).

- Payments Due to Bank Employees: Fixed employee allocations and indemnities in accordance with the laws in force.

- Rank: The hierarchy in terms of loss absorption with respect to the various classes of Own Funds and liabilities upon the application of the bank resolution process or the liquidation process.

- Related Institutions:

Financial and non-financial sector institutions related to the bank through any of the following channels:

* The parent institution that exercises control over the bank in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS).

* Subsidiary institutions or institutions that are subject to the control of the bank in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards.

* Associate institutions in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards.

* Sister institutions defined as institutions subject to the control of the major shareholders of the bank.

- Bank Resolution Process: Consists in the exercise by the Competent Authority referred to in this Law in accordance with the powers defined in Articles 5 and 16, and 16, in order to achieve the objectives defined in Article 3 of this Law.

- Major Shareholder: The beneficial owner who ultimately owns, directly or indirectly, 5% or more of the shares or voting rights.

- New Deposits: Are deposits denominated in foreign currency originating from bank transfers from abroad or cash deposits after 30/10/2019.

- Unrelated Institutions: Financial and non-financial sector institutions that are not covered by the definition of "Related Institutions".

- Insured Deposits: Are deposits subject to the National Institute for the Guarantee of Deposits in accordance with the law in force and its amendments.

- Unsecured Liabilities: Consist of:

* Liabilities not legally secured by cash collateral, cash margins or financial instruments.

* The portion of legally secured liabilities that is not covered by cash collateral, cash margins or financial instruments. These liabilities include deposits of financial sector institutions (including certificates of deposit issued by the bank and held by financial sector institutions).

* On-balance-sheet deposits belonging to financial sector institutions and arising from fiduciary contracts between those institutions in their capacity as financial intermediary and their customers.

* Loans from financial sector institutions.

* Bonds issued by the bank and held by individuals and institutions from the financial and non-financial sector, related or unrelated to the bank.

* Other unsecured liabilities (excluding customer deposits) that are not excluded.

Amendment of the provisions of the Title on the End-of-Service Indemnity:

The provisions of Title Four (End-of-Service Indemnity) of Book Two (Benefits) of the Social Security Law are amended as follows:

New Title Four Retirement Scheme

Chapter One Establishment of the Retirement Scheme

Article 49-1: Establishment of a Retirement Scheme:

A retirement scheme is established to replace the end-of-service indemnity scheme in all its rights and obligations. Its organisation is determined in this Title and its resources in Chapter Six thereof.

This new scheme shall apply to the persons specified in Articles (49-2) and (49-3) set out below.

The provisions of the end-of-service indemnity scheme shall remain applicable, on a transitional basis, to the persons referred to in

paragraph (2) of Article (49-4).

Article 49-2: Persons Mandatorily Subject:

1 - Concerned categories:

Every person belonging to the categories set out below, whose age is not less than the minimum working age determined in the laws and regulations in force, regardless of the duration or form of the employment contract and whatever the nature of the wage, shall be mandatorily subject to the provisions of this scheme, provided that the work is performed within Lebanese territory:

a - Employees working under an employment contract, for the account of one or more employers, whether Lebanese or foreign.

b - Permanent employees working in an agricultural enterprise provided for in Law No. 8/74 dated 25/3/1974, and in Decree No. 7757 dated 7/5/1974.

c - Lebanese nationals working for the account of the State, municipalities, or any public administration, public institution, or autonomous service. Excluded from the provisions of this item is every sector governed by special legal provisions on retirement that differ from those provided for by the Social Security Law.

d - Members of the teaching staff at higher education institutions provided for in the Law Regulating Private Higher Education, issued on 26/12/1961, and at the technical institutes provided for in Article 12 of Regulatory Decree No. 7880 dated 25/7/1967, unless they have a mandatory special retirement scheme.

e - Employees contracted in Lebanon with an enterprise that has a head office or branch therein, who have commenced their work in Lebanon and been transferred to work abroad. In this case, the earnings or basic wage, excluding allowances paid to them during or on the occasion of working abroad, shall be taken as the basis for calculating contributions.

f - Employers, self-employed persons, and non-permanent employees in agriculture pursuant to a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the submission of the Board of Directors of the Fund and the proposal of the Minister of Labour.

2 - All other categories of persons not mentioned in this Article, for whom the necessity of subjecting them mandatorily to this scheme becomes apparent, shall be determined by decrees adopted by the Council of Ministers, upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour after the submission of the Board of Directors, and under the conditions specified therein.

3 - Foreign employees

a - Foreign employees working on Lebanese territory who are bound to one or more specific employers, and the employers who employ them, shall be subject to all the obligations provided for in the retirement scheme.

b- The foreign employees mentioned in accordance with paragraph "a" above shall not benefit from the benefits provided for in this scheme unless they hold a work permit in accordance with the laws and regulations in force, provided that the State to which they belong grants reciprocity to Lebanese nationals with respect to the retirement scheme.

c - The States that grant reciprocity to Lebanon shall be determined pursuant to decisions issued by the Board of Directors of the Fund, after consulting the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants.

d If a foreign national entitled to a retirement or invalidity pension leaves Lebanese territory permanently, his pension shall be commuted into a lump sum, unless a law provides otherwise through international agreements between Lebanon and other countries, and the Fund shall have the right to impose a deduction thereon, in accordance with rules determined in its regulations, particularly where the foreign insured person has benefited from the minimum guarantees subsidy.

e - In the event that a foreign national who is not eligible to receive the benefits of this scheme in accordance with items b and c of this Article suffers invalidity, dies, or leaves Lebanese territory indefinitely, the notional account of the insured person shall be liquidated and transferred as a lump sum, in accordance with the schedules determined by the Board of Directors of the Fund, without applying the minimum guarantees.

f - Foreign employees working in Lebanon pursuant to contracts concluded abroad with foreign enterprises shall not be subject to the provisions of this scheme if the employer proves that they benefit, in the country where the contract was concluded or the country to which they belong, from benefits similar to the benefits prescribed in this scheme.

Article 49-3: Voluntarily Participating Persons:

1 - In addition to the persons insured in accordance with Article 49-2, the following may participate in the retirement scheme on a voluntary basis:

a - Lebanese nationals residing in Lebanon who are self-employed, family workers, employers, and non-permanent employees in agriculture, pending the issuance of the decision set out in Article (49-2), paragraph (1), item (f).

b - Lebanese nationals working abroad, whether employees or non-employees, who are not mandatorily subject to this scheme.

c - Insured persons affiliated with the retirement scheme who, for any reason whatsoever, no longer fulfil the conditions for mandatory coverage.

2 - With respect to voluntary participants, the following provisions shall be observed:

a - The concerned party shall submit an application for affiliation to the Fund, accompanied by the documents determined by the regulations of the Fund.

b - The Fund must decide on the application and notify the concerned party of its decision within a period of two months from the date of registration of the application. Failure to reply within this period shall be deemed an approval of the application.

c - The effect of affiliation, whether approval is express or tacit, shall commence on the first day of the quarter following the quarter in which the application was registered.

d - Contributions shall be paid monthly or quarterly, and shall be assessed on the basis of a flat-rate income consisting of four or more brackets, from which the insured person chooses the bracket on the basis of which he wishes to contribute.

e - This income, as well as the brackets where necessary, shall be determined and amended by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and the submission of the Board of Directors of the National Social Security Fund. The highest bracket must not exceed four times the average wage, subject to any adjustment to the ceiling in accordance with Article (541), paragraph (3), item (a).

f - Voluntarily insured persons shall benefit from the benefits of this scheme under the conditions specified for mandatorily insured persons.

g - Where necessary, the detailed rules for the application of this Article, particularly with respect to the effects of early withdrawal from the scheme, shall be determined by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour after the submission of the Board of Directors of the Fund.

Article 49-4: Mandatory Coverage and Option:

1 - The following shall be mandatorily subject to the provisions of the retirement scheme:

a - Persons entering employment for the first time after the date on which the scheme is put into effect.

b - All other previously insured persons who have not reached the age of forty-nine on the date on which the scheme is put into effect.

All other previously insured persons who have reached the age of forty-nine and have not reached the age of fifty-eight shall be subject on an optional basis, provided that the duration of their affiliation with the end-of-service scheme, in addition to the period remaining until reaching the retirement age, is at least 15 years, thereby entitling them to obtain the retirement pension in accordance with Article (50-2), paragraph (1).

2 - Other insured persons shall have the option between one of the following two cases:

a - To remain subject to the end-of-service indemnity scheme.

b - To opt for affiliation with the retirement scheme prescribed in this Title, which option is irrevocable, within a period of one year as from the date on which it is put into effect.

3 - Upon acceptance of the subject and affiliated insured persons mentioned in paragraphs (1) and (2 b) of this Article, the previous years of work spent by the insured person under the end-of-service indemnity scheme shall be added to his subsequent period of work under the retirement scheme, and all his financial entitlements accrued under the previous scheme up to the date of his affiliation shall be transferred to his notional individual account, and their previous periods of work and their entitlements shall be calculated in accordance with the transitional provisions to be provided for by the decree referred to in Article (54-6) below.

4 - Without prejudice to the provisions of paragraph (2), item (b) above, voluntary affiliation with this scheme may be reopened pursuant to a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and the submission of the Board of Directors of the Fund.

Article 49-5: Benefits of the Scheme:

The scheme provides one of the following benefits:

1 - Retirement pension

2 - Invalidity pension

3- Survivors' pension of the insured person

Chapter Two Retirement Pension

Article 50-1: Elements of the Retirement Pension:

The scheme provides the insured person with a retirement pension that depends on all of the following elements combined:

1 - The accumulated notional (notional) individual account of the insured person, closed on the day preceding the date on which the entitlement arises, as specified in Article (506) of this Law.

2 - The age reached by the insured person.

3 - The number of years of contribution.

4 - The conversion factor (conversion factor) of the accumulated notional individual account into an annual retirement pension.

The conversion factor is based on the elements capable of affecting the constitution of the retirement pension, such as the age on the date of retirement, invalidity, or death, the future indexation (Indexation) of the retirement pension based on the expected evolution of the consumer price index, life expectancy, and the existence of survivors of the insured person upon retirement, based on a methodology included in the funding policy of the Fund mentioned in Article (54-4).

The conversion factor shall be determined and amended on the basis of the statistical and actuarial data prepared within the framework of the actuarial financial valuation in accordance with the provisions of Article (54-4).

Article 50-2: Entitlement to the Retirement Pension:

1 - The insured person shall be entitled to the retirement pension when the following two conditions are met together:

a - The insured person reaches the statutory retirement age set at 64 completed years.

b - The contribution period of the insured person reaches at least fifteen years.

2 - The insured person shall have the right to continue working after reaching the statutory retirement age and shall remain subject, together with the employer, to all the provisions of the Social Security Law.

3 - No amendment or correction to the date of birth of the insured person occurring after the date of his first affiliation with the National Social Security Fund shall be taken into account.

4 - If a pensioner returns to employment that subjects him to the provisions of this Law, the new period of employment shall be deemed an independent period, for which his entitlements shall be settled in accordance with its provisions, provided that he does not benefit from the value of the minimum guarantees subsidy throughout his new period of employment.

Article 50-3: Early Retirement:

1 - Within six (6) years prior to reaching the statutory retirement age, an insured person who is in a physical, mental, or psychological condition that renders him unable to perform his work without causing serious harm to his health, and whose incapacity for work has been medically established in accordance with the rules, may apply for the liquidation of his retirement pension in accordance with the provisions in force.

The rate of incapacity is set at fifty per cent (50%) of his general capacity.

The internal regulations of the Fund shall determine the procedures for submitting the application, the documents that must be attached thereto, and the competent authority to decide thereon.

The liquidation set out above shall preclude the arising of new retirement entitlements if the concerned party engages in a professional activity after the date of closure of the account.

2 - The insured person shall have the right, within four (4) years prior to reaching the statutory retirement age, to apply for the liquidation of his retirement entitlements, provided that his contribution period is not less than twenty (20) years, and that his notional individual account secures a retirement pension equal to or exceeding the maximum of the two guarantees calculated in paragraph (3) of Article (50-7).

Article 50-4: Categories of Employees with Special Status:

The contribution rates, age, and special conditions for benefiting from the pension for certain categories of employees who perform arduous work or whose nature of work does not allow for long service shall be determined by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour after the submission of the Board of Directors of the Fund, and based on actuarial studies conducted for this purpose by a qualified actuary in accordance with Article (54-4).

Article 50-5: Contribution Periods:

Years of contribution mean the periods for which retirement contributions have been paid or have fallen due.

For this purpose, a month of insurance shall be deemed to be a month during which the insured person became uninterruptedly subject to insurance, and for which contributions have been paid or have fallen due.

If the insured person was not uninterruptedly subject to insurance, the total periods equivalent to twenty-five (25) days, four (4) weeks, or two hundred (200) hours of work for which contributions have been paid or have fallen due shall be deemed to constitute a month of insurance.

For this purpose, a month shall be deemed to be 1/12 of a year, and a fraction of elapsed months shall be deemed a full month.

The Board of Directors of the Fund shall determine, in its internal regulations, the rules for calculating the contribution periods of part-time and/or seasonal or intermittent workers, and the rules for calculating the contributions due from them and from their employers, and shall also determine the rules for calculating the benefits provided by this scheme for them and for their survivors.

Article 50-6: Accumulated Notional Individual Account:

1 - The accumulated notional individual account of the insured person shall consist of:

a - The balance of the end-of-service indemnity transferred to this retirement scheme and liquidated pursuant to the provisions set out in Articles 51, 52, 53, and 54 of the Social Security Law and governed by the transitional provisions provided for in the implementing decree referred to in Article (54-6) below.

b Contributions paid or due, credited to the notional individual account, according to the rate determined in accordance with the provisions of Article (54-1), paragraph (3).

c - An annual increase in line with the increase in the average income of contributors.

On an identical specified date each year, the Fund shall announce the percentage increase in the index of the average income of contributors in the preceding year. On the same date, this percentage increase shall be applied for the indexation index of the notional account of each insured person, and this mechanism shall be adopted until the year preceding retirement.

The annual increase on the notional individual accounts may be adjusted upwards if the actuarial valuation of the scheme shows an exceptional surplus in the reserve specified in the funding policy approved by the Board of Directors, as detailed in Article (54-4).

2 - For the purpose of calculating retirement pensions, all amounts pertaining to the accumulated notional individual account of the insured person up to the date on which the pension falls due shall be taken into consideration.

Article 50-7: The Two Minimum Guarantees:

1 - When the conditions for retirement are met, the accumulated notional individual account shall be adopted and converted into a retirement pension for the contributor or the survivor, in accordance with the bases and rules specified therefor, pursuant to Article (50-1) (conversion factor).

2 - The Fund may pay to an insured person without survivors, upon his retirement and at his request, a lump sum from his notional individual account, provided that the total capital remaining in this account is sufficient to obtain a pension equivalent at least to the maximum of both guarantees provided for in paragraph 3 of this Article.

3 - This scheme guarantees that the retirement pension shall not be less than the better of the following two guarantees:

a - For an insured person who has contributed for fifteen (15) full years, a rate of fifty-five per cent (55%) of the official minimum wage adopted on the date of retirement, and this rate shall be increased by one point seventy-five per cent (1.75%) for each additional year of contribution, to reach a maximum of eighty per cent (80%) of the official minimum wage adopted on the date of retirement, of that limit.

b - A rate of one point thirty-three per cent (1.33%) of the average declared wages of the contributor throughout the period of his contribution to this scheme, revalued up to the date of retirement, for each year of contribution by the insured person.

The revaluation and indexation (Indexation) of the contributor's wages shall be carried out in accordance with the increase in the index of the average wages of contributors according to the mechanism provided for in paragraph (3) of Article (544) of this scheme.

4 - The rates mentioned in paragraphs (3a) and (3b) of this Article may be reviewed pursuant to a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Labour and Finance and the submission of the Board of Directors of the Fund, and in light of the recommendation of the qualified actuary referred to in Article (54-4).

5 - In the event of early retirement, in accordance with paragraph (2) of Article (50-3), the following two calculations shall be carried out:

a - The notional individual account of the insured person shall be converted into a retirement pension on the basis of the conversion factor corresponding to his age on the date of his early retirement.

b - The extent to which the insured person benefits from either of the two minimum pension guarantees provided for in paragraph (3) of Article (507) above shall be calculated after reducing them by half a per cent (0.5%) for each month preceding the statutory retirement age mentioned in paragraph (1a) of Article (50-2).

Article 50-8: Liquidation of the Accumulated Notional Individual Account for a Person Who Has Not Met the Condition of Years of Contribution:

If an affiliate reaches the statutory retirement age without meeting the condition of years of contribution, his accumulated notional individual account shall be liquidated, and the funds due to him shall be paid as a lump sum. At the request of the insured person, the said amounts may be paid in instalments or converted into a retirement pension, without the right to benefit from the two minimum pension guarantees provided for in paragraph (3) of the preceding Article (50-7).

Article 50-9: Date of Entitlement to the Pension:

The retirement pension shall fall due as from the beginning of the month following the date on which the conditions of entitlement are met.

Chapter Three Invalidity Pension

Article 51-1: The Invalid:

An invalid, within the meaning of this scheme, is a person afflicted with permanent and total invalidity, whether physical, mental, or psychological, that reduces his capacity for work by two thirds. The said invalidity shall not be taken into account if the insured person was afflicted with it before becoming subject to the scheme.

Article 51-2: Determination of the State of Invalidity:

The state of invalidity shall be assessed by the Medical Committee provided for in Article (6), paragraph (5) of the Social Security Law, according to the remaining capacity for work of the insured person, his general state of health, his age, and his physical, mental, and psychological faculties.

Article 51-3: Conditions of Entitlement:

-1 The retirement scheme provides an insured person afflicted with invalidity with a retirement pension in accordance with all of the following conditions together:

a - That he has been a contributor to the scheme for a period of at least three years prior to the date on which the state of invalidity is established.

b That the invalidity did not occur prior to the insured person's entry into the scheme, taking into consideration Law No. 220 dated 29/5/2000 relating to the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (persons with additional needs).

2 - If the invalidity results from a non-occupational accident or a medical emergency, the period of contribution to the scheme shall be reduced to twelve months.

Article 51-4: Method of Calculating the Pension:

1 - When the conditions of invalidity are met, the accumulated notional account, closed on the date of completion of the invalidity after its revaluation, shall be adopted, and this account shall be converted into an invalidity pension in accordance with the mechanism specified in Article (50-1).

2 - This scheme guarantees to an invalid who meets the conditions of invalidity an invalidity pension not less than the better of the following two guarantees:

a - For an insured person who has contributed for a period of fifteen full years, a rate of fifty-five per cent (55%) of the official minimum wage adopted on the date of retirement, and this rate shall be increased by one point seventy-five per cent (1.75%) for each additional year of contribution, to reach a maximum of eighty per cent

(80%) of the official minimum wage adopted on the date of invalidity. The guarantee shall be calculated in accordance with the years of contribution after adding a notional period extending from the day following the date of completion of the invalidity until the invalid insured person reaches the statutory retirement age.

b - A rate of one point thirty-three per cent (1.33%) of the average wages of the invalid, revalued up to the date of completion of the invalidity, for each year of his actual period of service extending from the date the insured person commenced work until the date of completion of the invalidity. The guarantee shall be calculated in accordance with the years of contribution after adding a notional period extending from the day following the date of completion of the invalidity until the invalid insured person reaches the statutory retirement age, provided that the total of the two periods does not exceed a maximum of thirty (30) years.

3 - The revaluation and indexation (Indexation) of the wages calculated for the invalid insured person shall be carried out in accordance with the increase in the index of the average wages of contributors according to the mechanism provided for in paragraph (3) of Article (54-4) of this scheme.

4- Where the condition of years of contribution provided for in paragraph (1) of Article (51-3) of this scheme is not met, the accumulated amounts of the invalid insured person credited to his notional individual account shall be liquidated and paid to him as a lump sum.

Article 51-5: Procedure for Applying for an Invalidity Pension:

The insured person or his official representative shall submit an application for an invalidity pension to the Fund within a period of twelve (12) months following, as the case may be, either the date of completion of the state of invalidity, or the date of medical confirmation of the invalidity if such invalidity results from premature bodily wear and tear in accordance with the medical and objective criteria established in the Medical Committee, or the date of stabilisation of the insured person's condition, or the date of expiry of the statutory period of entitlement to medical care benefits.

If the pension application is rejected, or if a previously granted pension is cancelled, the insured person may submit a new application within a period of twelve (12) months. In the event that the rate of invalidity reaches two thirds (2/3) only during the last twelve (12) months, the state of invalidity shall then be assessed as at the date of aggravation of the invalidity.

Article 51-6: Deciding on the Invalidity Pension Application:

The Fund shall decide on the invalidity pension application within a period of three (3) months from the date of its submission, based on the opinion of the Medical Committee provided for in paragraph (5) of Article (6) of the Social Security Law. The procedures for submitting and deciding on the application shall be determined in the internal regulations of the Fund.

Failure to decide within this period shall be deemed an approval of the application. The Fund shall notify the concerned party of its decision on the matter by means of an acknowledgement of receipt within the three-month period mentioned above.

Failure to notify within the period specified above shall entitle the insured person to seek recourse.

Article 51-7: Date of Entitlement to the Invalidity Pension:

The pension shall fall due as from the first of the month following the date on which the state of invalidity is established.

Article 51-8: Provisional Determination of the Invalidity Pension:

The invalidity pension shall be granted on a provisional basis and may be reviewed according to the evolution of the insured person's condition.

The Fund may request the Medical Committee to assess the remaining earning capacity of the concerned party. It may cancel, suspend, or amend the invalidity pension when the beneficiary's capacity exceeds 50% (fifty per cent), and the Fund shall determine the mechanism for amending the pension in the internal regulations.

Article 51-9: Method of Calculating the Retirement Pension if the Insured Person Returns to Work:

If the insured person returns to work covered by the provisions of this scheme after the cancellation of the invalidity pension, the period during which he received the pension shall be deemed a period of actual work taken into account for the application of the provisions of Article (16) of the Social Security Law and for entitlement to the retirement pension in accordance with the provisions of this scheme.

Chapter Four Survivors' Pension of the Insured Person

Article 52-1: Survivors of the Insured Person:

1 - The survivors of the insured person are:

a - The surviving husband or wife, provided that the marriage has been in existence for at least two years; the duration requirement shall be waived if there are children from this marriage.

b - Legitimate children, or those expected to be born within a period of nine (9) months, or those adopted at least two (2) years previously, who were dependent on the insured person at the time of his death.

Children shall benefit from their status as survivors until they reach the age of eighteen (18) completed years, or until the age of twenty-five (25) completed years for children devoted full-time to studies, and without age limit for unmarried children with additional needs whose condition renders them unable to earn their living.

Article 52-2: Entitlements of the Survivors of the Insured Person / Survivors' Pension:

1 - In the event of the death of the insured person before retirement:

a - The benefits received by the survivors shall be determined on the basis of the accumulated notional individual account of the deceased insured person, which, after its revaluation, shall be converted into a survivors' pension calculated in accordance with the same mechanisms provided for in Article (50-1).

b - This scheme guarantees a survivors' pension not less than the better of the following two guarantees:

1 - For an insured person who has contributed for a period of fifteen full years, a rate of fifty-five per cent (55%) of the official minimum wage adopted on the date of death, and this rate shall be increased by one point seventy-five per cent (1.75%) for each additional year of contribution, to reach a maximum of eighty per cent (80%) of the official minimum wage adopted on the date of death. To calculate the guarantee, the period of actual service shall be added to the period extending from the day following the date of death to the date of the retirement age.

2 - A rate of one point thirty-three per cent (1.33%) of the average wages of the deceased, revalued up to the date of death, for each year of his actual period of service extending from the date the insured person commenced work until the date of death, added to the period extending from the day following the date of his death until the date of the statutory retirement age, provided that the total of the two periods does not exceed a maximum of thirty years.

The revaluation and indexation (Indexation) of the wages calculated for the deceased insured person shall be carried out in accordance with the increase in the index of the average wages of contributors according to the mechanism provided for in paragraph 3 of Article 54-4 of this scheme.

2 - In the case of a deceased person who was receiving a retirement pension or an invalidity pension at the time of his death:

The survivors' benefits shall be distributed on the basis of eighty per cent (80%) of the retirement benefits of the insured person due upon retirement, as follows:

- 40% (forty per cent) to the surviving partner.

- 40% (forty per cent) to the children, distributed equally among them if there are more than one.

When the conditions for the children's entitlement lapse or in the absence of children, their share shall accrue to the partner, and vice versa.

3 - In the event that the deceased insured person had liquidated his entitlements in accordance with Article (50-8), the survivors shall not be entitled to receive a retirement pension, but shall be entitled to receive the value of the remaining instalments according to their due dates.

4 - The survivors' pension shall take effect:

a - On the first day of the month following the month in which the death occurred, if the application is submitted within a period of two (2) years from the date of death.

b - On the first day of the month following the date of submission of the application, if this application is submitted after the expiry of a period of two (2) years from the date of death, provided that the time limit shall remain open with respect to children.

Article 52-3: Cases of Cessation of the Pension for the Husband/Wife:

The pension shall cease for the beneficiary husband or beneficiary wife if he or she marries or dies, and his or her share shall be transferred to the beneficiary children.

Article 52-4: In the Absence of Survivors:

In the absence of any of the survivors mentioned in Article (52-1) at the time of the death of the insured person, his notional individual account shall be liquidated and paid as a lump sum to the rightful claimants (the mother or the father) specified in the draft law put into effect pursuant to Decree No. 8496 dated 2/8/1974.

Article 52-5: Upon Loss of Entitlement to the Invalidity Pension:

1 - If an insured person who holds a retirement pension or an invalidity pension, or who meets the conditions of entitlement to such pension, goes missing, his trace disappears, news of him ceases, and a judicial decision declaring him missing is issued, one of his survivors specified in Article (52-1) may, pursuant to a judicial authorisation, obtain a provisional liquidation of the entitlements that he would have received from the pension in the event of the death of the insured person.

2 - The provisional liquidation shall be reviewed upon the return of the missing person, or the provisional liquidation of entitlements shall become final upon the official declaration of death.

3 - Pensions shall be disbursed to the survivors of the insured person as from the first day of the month following the month in which the judicial decision declaring the insured person missing was pronounced.

Article 52-6: Entitlements of the Surviving Husband or Wife:

Notwithstanding any other text, the surviving husband or wife shall have the right to combine the survivors' pension of the insured person with the retirement pension or invalidity pension due to him or her personally, and the children shall also have the right to combine the pension received from both parents, provided that no benefit is drawn from the minimum pension subsidy where it exists.

Chapter Five Financing - Common Provisions - Transitional Provisions

Article 54-1: Sources of Financing:

1 - The sources of financing of the "Retirement Scheme" shall consist of:

a - Contributions.

b - Returns on the investment and placement of funds derived from these sources.

c - Amounts credited to the notional account of the insured person that are liquidated in accordance with the transitional provisions provided for in the implementing decree referred to in Article (54-6) below.

d - Late payment surcharges, interest, and additional fines incurred for non-compliance with the provisions of this Law.

e - The annual contribution of the State, which is determined as a percentage of the total earnings of the persons subject to this scheme, allocated, inter alia, to support the categories that do not have sufficient capacity to contribute to the scheme; these categories and the rate of contribution shall be determined by the implementing decree mentioned in Article (54-6), and may be amended, where necessary, pursuant to a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Labour and Finance and after the submission of the Board of Directors of the Fund, based on the recommendation of the qualified actuary and based on the funding policy referred to in Article (54-4).

This contribution shall be provided for annually in the General Budget Law.

f- Fees allocated to support the General Account, which are imposed pursuant to decrees adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Labour and Finance and after the submission of the Board of Directors of the National Social Security Fund.

2 -

a - The State is the ultimate guarantor of the financial sustainability of the scheme, and this should be clearly reflected in its general budget when needed.

b - Contributions shall be borne by employers and insured persons.

c - The employer shall pay the contributions due from him and from the insured persons working for him in full to the retirement scheme, and shall inform them of the balance of their contribution accounts annually.

3 -

a - Contributions shall be determined as a percentage of the total earnings of the employee provided for in paragraph (1) of Article (68) of the Social Security Law and within a ceiling limited to four (4) times the average declared wages.

b - On an identical specified date each year, the Fund shall announce the amount/level of the ceiling/limit after adjusting it based on the change in the average declared wages for the preceding year.

c - This ceiling shall be amended by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Finance and Labour and after the submission of the Board of Directors of the Fund, and based on the actuarial financial examination of the retirement scheme.

d - The rate of contributions incurred by each of the employer and the employee shall be determined and distributed pursuant to a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and the submission of the Board of Directors of the Fund,

In the text of this decree, the contribution rates above shall be determined and distributed in percentages to each of: the notional individual account, the account for supporting the minimum guarantees for retirement, invalidity, and death pensions, and the administrative expenses, based on the recommendation of the qualified actuary and based on the funding policy referred to in Article (544).

The Council of Ministers shall adopt the decree mentioned above in accordance with the provisions of Article (54-6) below on the basis of the schedule of contributions included in Annex No. 3.

4 - The contribution rates, the method of their distribution, and the earnings subject to contributions may be reviewed pursuant to decrees adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Ministers of Finance and Labour and the submission of the Board of Directors of the Fund, based on the recommendation of the qualified actuary and based on the funding policy referred to in Article (54-4).

5 - The General Account of the Retirement Scheme:

a - The General Account of the Fund means the account allocated to provide retirement, invalidity, and death pensions and to support and supplement these pensions.

b - The General Account of the Fund shall include:

- Balances of the end-of-service scheme transferred to this retirement scheme pursuant to the transitional provisions to be provided for by the decree referred to in Article (546) below.

- Contributions provided for in items (a) and (b) of paragraph (3) of this Article,

- Investment returns of the Fund,

- The annual contribution of the State specified in item (e) of paragraph (1) of this Article

- The allocated fees provided for in item (f) of paragraph (1) of this Article,

- The balance of late payment surcharges and fines incurred upon non-compliance with the provisions of this scheme.

Article 54-2: Fine for the Employer's Default in Paying Contributions:

In addition to the provisions of Articles (79) and (80) of this Law, and as from the due date specified in the regulations of the Fund, an additional fine at the rate of three per cent (3%) per month of the total contributions due shall be imposed on an employer who defaults in paying contributions within the time limits specified by the regulations, provided that this rate does not exceed fifteen per cent (15%) of this total.

Common Provisions

Article 54-3: Indexation (Indexation) and Payment of Retirement Pensions:

1 - Each year, on a specified date, the Fund shall revalue all pensions due and being paid in accordance with the provisions of this retirement scheme.

The revaluation shall be based on the increase in the index of the average income of contributors issued by the National Social Security Fund in accordance with paragraph (1 b) of Article (50-6) and pertaining to the year preceding the valuation year. The mechanism for the revaluation of pensions and the annual maximum rate of increase thereon shall be carried out in accordance with the funding policy adopted by the Board of Directors, and the revaluation process shall be subject to the mechanism mentioned in paragraph (3) of Article (54-4) below.

When appropriate economic conditions exist, the consumer price index issued by the Central Administration of Statistics may be adopted in the revaluation process instead of the wage increase index, pursuant to a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and after the submission of the Board of Directors of the Fund based on the recommendation of the qualified actuary.

2 - Pensions shall be paid on their due dates, in accordance with the procedures and dates determined by the internal regulations of the Fund.

Article 54-4: Examination and Valuation of the Financial Position Once Every Three Years:

1 - The Board of Directors of the Fund must issue a funding policy determining the criteria and bases for ensuring the long-term financial sustainability of the scheme within one year from the entry into force of this scheme.

The financial policy shall be approved by the Board of Directors of the Fund, based on the recommendation of the qualified actuary.

2 - The financial position of this scheme must be examined actuarially at most once every three years, in accordance with the criteria and bases provided for in the adopted funding policy.

The actuarial examination and valuation shall be carried out by an accredited actuarial firm or institution of recognised professional credibility in accordance with international standards, which may assign, under its responsibility and supervision, one of its actuaries.

The actuarial firm or institution shall be appointed and its tasks and duration determined by a decision issued by the Board of Directors of the Fund and approved by the Minister of Labour.

3 - Upon each actuarial examination and valuation, the actuary who conducted them must indicate in his report submitted to the Board of Directors of the Fund, based on the long-term funding policy duly adopted by the Board of Directors of the Fund, whether the position of the Fund permits the indexation (Indexation) of wages and pensions provided for in:

-- Item (b) of paragraph (3) of Article (50-7) and,

-- Paragraph (3) of Article (514) and,

-- Item (b2) of paragraph (1) of Article (52-2) and,

-- Paragraph (1) of Article (54-3),

for the period covered by the examination and valuation.

The indexation (Indexation) of wages and pensions shall be suspended if the valuation results are negative until the date of the subsequent examination and valuation, and the Board of Directors shall take the necessary measures for correction and rectification in accordance with the funding policy.

If the result of the subsequent examination and valuation proves positive, indexation (Indexation) may be applied to the wages and/or pensions mentioned above, even with retroactive effect, for the preceding years during which indexation (Indexation) of those wages and/or pensions was not permitted, and this shall be done in accordance with the rules specified for the funding policy approved by the Board of Directors.

4 - Every three (3) years, the valuation of the actuarial financial position shall be reviewed, and the actuarial firm or institution shall make recommendations to take the necessary measures and, where necessary, to amend the conversion factor conversion factor on the basis of the methodology for calculating conversion factors provided for in the funding policy.

5 - Where necessary, any amendments to the funding policy and its elements shall be reviewed in accordance with rules determined by a decree adopted by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and the submission of the Board of Directors of the Fund.

6 - In the event that the expert issues a qualified opinion or discovers any negligence, the administration shall immediately take the necessary measures to rectify the negligence.

Article 54-5: Method of Notifying Insured Persons of Their Account Statements:

The internal regulations of the Fund shall determine the method of notifying insured persons of their notional individual account statements and benefits, and the times of such notification.

Article 54-6: Implementing and Transitional Provisions:

1 - The decrees appointing the Board of Directors of the "National Social Security Fund" in accordance with the provisions of Article Nine of this Law shall be issued within six (6) months from the date of publication of this Law.

2 - The Council of Ministers shall adopt the decree appointing the "Investment Committee", in accordance with the provisions of Article (64-4) of this Law, within one year from the date of publication of this Law.

3 - The Council of Ministers shall adopt an implementing decree upon the proposal of the Minister of Labour and the submission of the Board of Directors of the Fund, determining therein the contribution rates and their distribution in accordance with the provisions of Article (54-1) based on the results of an updated actuarial valuation conducted by a qualified actuary assigned by the Board of Directors of the Fund, taking into account the prevailing economic conditions and circumstances in the short and medium terms, while taking inflation rates into consideration, within one year from the date of publication of this Law.

All transitional provisions relating to the treatment and liquidation of the acquired rights of employees under the end-of-service indemnity scheme, including the mechanisms for dealing with objections raised after the application of these transitional provisions, must be included in the implementing decree.

The decree must observe the following principles:

a - All provisions of this scheme shall apply to persons who transfer to the new scheme, and the period of contribution to the Fund shall be calculated from the day following the date on which their end-of-service indemnity fell due if they have previously received it, and otherwise from the date on which their coverage and contribution to social security commenced.

b - For those who transfer to the new scheme, the minimum guarantees shall be applied proportionally to the years of contribution, even for those who do not meet 15 years of contribution.

c - The value of the entitlements accumulated under the end-of-service indemnity scheme shall be credited to the notional individual account of each insured person affiliated with the new scheme.

d - If a surplus in the assets of the end-of-service indemnity scheme results at the end of the transitional period, such surplus shall be used to constitute a reserve fund for the benefit of the new scheme; during the transitional period, the first guarantee referred to in Article (50-7) may be linked to the average income of contributors instead of being linked to the minimum wage, in a manner that preserves the same value of the guarantee.

4 - After the lapse of one year from the date of issuance of the implementing decree mentioned in paragraph (3) above, the provisions of Article Three thereof shall be put into effect, subject to the time limits and provisions set out in Article (54-6).

The following definitions and terms of Article 1 of Law No. 23 issued on 14/8/2025 (Law on the Resolution and Reorganisation of Banks in Lebanon) are amended, and paragraph (d) is added to define deposits of financial sector institutions, so as to read as follows:

For the application of the provisions of this Law, the following definitions and terms shall be adopted:

- Banque du Liban: The Central Bank established pursuant to the Law put into force by Decree No. 13513 dated 1/8/1963 (Code of Money and Credit and Establishment of the Central Bank).

- The Higher Banking Commission: Article 10 of Law No. 28 dated 9/5/1967 and its amendments (Amending and Completing the Legislation Relating to Banks and Establishing a Mixed Institution for the Guarantee of Bank Deposits) is amended to read as follows:

"The Commission with its two Chambers, which is concerned with taking disciplinary decisions against offending financial institutions (the First Chamber) and resolution and/or liquidation decisions and supervising the implementation thereof (the Second Chamber), in accordance with the provisions of this Law and the relevant laws in force".

- The Banking Control Commission: The supervisory authority established pursuant to Law No. 28/67 dated 9/5/1967 and its amendments.

- Depositors: Natural or legal persons (i.e. individuals or companies) holding deposit accounts and certificates of deposit in accordance with the legal definition of a deposit and bank accounts set out in the laws in force and applicable in general, the provisions of which are determined primarily in the Code of Obligations and Contracts and the Code of Land

Commerce, in particular Article 307 thereof specifically.

- Creditor, a creditor in accordance with the provisions of this Law is the holder of secured or unsecured liabilities not arising from a deposit.

- Deposits:

a - Customer deposits: Customer deposits: (including certificates of deposit issued by the bank and held by customers) belonging to natural and legal persons, other than financial sector institutions, and which are not included among the excluded liabilities, in accordance with the definitions set out for deposits in the prevailing laws in force in general, the provisions of which are determined primarily in the Code of Obligations and Contracts and the Code of Land Commerce, in particular Article 307 thereof specifically.

b - On-balance-sheet fiduciary deposits of the financial sector:

Belonging to financial sector institutions and arising from fiduciary contracts between those institutions in their capacity as financial intermediary and their customers.

c - Cash collateral and cash margins:

Provided as security against funded facilities (i.e. on-balance-sheet facilities) up to the limit of the utilised amount of the facilities.

d - Deposits of financial sector institutions: Which include accounts existing between banks operating in Lebanon and accounts of financial institutions.

- Senior management: Natural persons at banks who are responsible for setting policies and/or taking executive decisions with respect to placements, risks and compliance.

- Own funds: Consist of:

• Common Equity Tier 1 capital, which includes retained prior results, reserves, other comprehensive income items and other Common Equity Tier 1 items as defined in Annex No. 1 (Hierarchy of Own Funds and Creditors).

• Additional Tier 1 capital as defined in Annex No. 1 (Hierarchy of Own Funds and Creditors).

* Tier 2 capital as defined in Annex No. 1 (Hierarchy of Own Funds and Creditors).

- Hierarchy of own funds and creditors: The rank of each of the items of own funds and liabilities (as defined in Annex No. 1).

- Excluded liabilities: The liabilities mentioned in Annex No. 1 which are not subject to a write-down in value or to conversion into capital instruments.

- Financial sector institutions: Include the following resident and non-resident institutions, whether related or unrelated to the bank:

* Central banks.

* International and regional development banks and financial institutions.

* Banks.

* Other institutions, comprising:

* Financial institutions as defined pursuant to Article 179 of the Code of Money and Credit, and the relevant circulars issued by Banque du Liban.

* Financial leasing companies.

* Credit counters regulated pursuant to Articles 183 and 184 of the Code of Money and Credit.

* Microfinance institutions.

* Clearing houses.

* Financial intermediation institutions.

* Exchange institutions.

* Companies concerned with the transfer of cash funds through electronic means.

* Investment funds.

* Investment companies, including holding companies and special purpose investment entities.

* Any other institution that provides financial services or carries out financial activities.

- Competent authority or supervisory authority in the home country: The authority competent for bank resolution or the supervisory authority in the country where the head office of the foreign branch or of the foreign subsidiary bank operating in Lebanon is located.

- Competent authority or supervisory authority in the host country: The authority competent for bank resolution or the supervisory authority in the country where the branch affiliated with the head office in Lebanon or the subsidiary bank of the Lebanese parent bank operates.

- The Financial Regularity and Deposit Recovery Law: The law that allows the restoration of balance to financial regularity in Lebanon through addressing the financial gap by determining responsibilities.

- Liquidation process: A process comprising the sale of all the assets of the bank, the settlement of its liabilities, the distribution of the balance of its net assets to the shareholders, its final closure and its striking off the list of banks.

- Net asset value: The fair value of the assets of the bank (including off-balance-sheet items) minus the fair value of the liabilities of the bank (including off-balance-sheet items).

- Payments due to bank employees; Fixed employee allocations and indemnities in accordance with the laws in force.

- Rank: The hierarchy in terms of loss absorption with respect to the various categories of own funds and liabilities upon the application of the bank resolution process or the liquidation process.

- Related institutions:

Financial and non-financial sector institutions related to the bank through any of the following channels:

* The parent institution that exercises control over the bank in accordance with the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS).

* Subsidiary institutions or institutions that are subject to the control of the bank in accordance with the International Financial Reporting Standards.

* Associate institutions in accordance with the International Financial Reporting Standards.

* Sister institutions defined as institutions subject to the control of the major shareholders of the bank.

- Bank resolution process: Consists in the exercise by the competent authority referred to in this Law in accordance with the powers defined in Articles 5 and 16, with a view to achieving

the objectives defined in Article 3 of this Law.

- Major shareholder: The beneficial owner who ultimately holds, directly or indirectly, 5% or more of the shares or voting rights.

- New deposits: Are deposits denominated in foreign currency originating from bank transfers from abroad or cash deposits after 17/10/2019.

- Unrelated institutions: Financial and non-financial sector institutions not covered by the definition of "related institutions".

- Insured deposits, are deposits subject to the National Institute for the Guarantee of Deposits in accordance with the law in force and its amendments.

- Unsecured liabilities: Consist of:

* Liabilities not legally secured by cash collateral, cash margins or financial instruments.

* The portion of legally secured liabilities that is not covered by cash collateral, cash margins or financial instruments; these liabilities include deposits of financial sector institutions (including certificates of deposit issued by the bank and held by financial sector institutions).

* Loans from financial sector institutions.

* Bonds issued by the bank and held by individuals and institutions from the financial and non-financial sector, related or unrelated to the bank.

* Other unsecured liabilities (excluding customer deposits) and non-excluded liabilities.

- Non-viability: Adoption of the criteria defined in Article 12 of Law No. 23/2025.

- Effective control over the bank: Effective control over the bank is established whenever a natural or legal person, or a group of persons acting in concert among themselves, has the ability to elect the majority of the members of the board of directors of the bank, who in turn appoint the members of the executive management of the bank and supervise its work.

- Single depositor: Every natural or legal person who holds deposits with the same bank, whereby all accounts belonging to him and his share of joint accounts in

that bank are aggregated and treated as a single deposit, regardless of the number or types of such accounts.

Both an estate account and a joint account shall be deemed equivalent to a single account regardless of the number of holders of each of them.

The balances of joint accounts shall be distributed among their holders in accordance with the terms of the agreement signed between them and the bank concerned, and in the absence of a provision determining the distribution ratios, they shall be distributed equally among them. Where the holder of joint accounts does not hold a personal account with the bank, the total of his shares in the various joint accounts shall then be deemed a single deposit.
